title: Umahi’s son denies recruiting 350 armed men ahead of 2027 polls

By Chioma Okoye

The allegation was raised by the a coalition that said its prel
content:
By Chioma Okoye

The Chairman of Ohaozara Local Government Area of Ebonyi State, Osborn Umahi, has denied allegations that he recruited and armed 350 men to intimidate opposition figures ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The allegation was raised by the a coalition that said its preliminary investigation indicated that at least 350 armed personnel had been equipped and deployed by the council chairman.

the Coalition said the group was formed last Friday and initially appeared to be a neighbourhood watch outfit or a reconstituted Ebubeagu security group.

However, in a statement, Umahi’s media directorate denied the allegation, insisting that the chairman had neither recruited nor armed anyone for electoral purposes.

It described the allegation as an attempt to damage his reputation, adding that Umahi was opposed to the use of violence as a means of securing electoral victory.

The directorate said the chairman would campaign across Ebonyi State to mobilise support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and Governor Francis Nwifuru, both of the All Progressives Congress (APC).

It added that Umahi remained committed to free and fair elections and opposed intimidation, harassment and violence in the political process.

title: 2027: Wike offers to lead Tinubu’s re-election campaigns in Imo, Kwara
description:
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has asked President Bola Tinubu and the leadership of the All Progressives Congress to assign him responsibility for mobilising political support for the President’s re-election in Imo and Kwara states ahead of the 2027 general elections.
W
content:
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has asked President Bola Tinubu and the leadership of the All Progressives Congress to assign him responsibility for mobilising political support for the President’s re-election in Imo and Kwara states ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Wike, who declared that he was done with Rivers State and the FCT, said he was ready to take on the political task in the two states and deliver them for the President.

The minister made the request on Wednesday at a Rainbow Coalition town hall meeting in Gokana Local Government Area of Rivers State, where he expressed confidence in his ability to expand the ruling party’s political influence beyond his immediate political base.

According to a statement issued by Wike’s Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media, Lere Olayinka, the FCT minister said he had already been assigned responsibility for coordinating political activities in Rivers State and the FCT.

“I was assigned to coordinate Rivers and the FCT. Frankly speaking, I am done with these states. All adequate political machineries have been set in motion to deliver Rivers State and the FCT for the President. So, I have no much work to do again,” he declared.

He appealed to the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’aziz Yari, and Tinubu to give him two additional states to oversee.

“As I am going now, I will plead with the DG and Mr President to add two more states for me to deliver,” he said.

Explaining his interest in Imo State, the former Rivers governor said he had received reports of political challenges in the state and was willing to intervene to strengthen support for Tinubu.

“From what I am told, they are having some problems in Imo State. So, I will love to go there and deliver the state for Mr President,” he stated.

On Kwara State, Wike said he had also read reports of divisions within the political structure, although he admitted that he had yet to independently verify the situation.

“Secondly, I have not confirmed, but what I read on social media is that there are some divisions in Kwara. So I plead with the DG of the APC Presidential Council, Senator Yari, and Mr President to allow me take over Imo and Kwara states, because I am done with Rivers and FCT,” Wike added.

The minister also used the Gokana meeting to canvass support for Tinubu’s second-term ambition, describing the President as a courageous leader willing to take difficult decisions in the country’s interest.

He cited the removal of the fuel subsidy, increased financial allocations to state and local governments, and the establishment of the Federal University of Environment and Technology in Ogoniland as some of the achievements that, according to him, justified continued support for the administration.

Wike also commended political stakeholders in Gokana for setting aside their differences and working together under the Rainbow Coalition, stressing that unity was essential to achieving their political objectives.

He urged the people to sustain their relationship with Tinubu, warning against abandoning an existing political alliance for an uncertain alternative.

Earlier, the former Secretary to the Rivers State Government and Coordinator of the Rainbow Coalition in Gokana, Chief Kenneth Kobani, described the gathering as unprecedented, saying it brought together different segments of the community.

Similarly, the APC South-South National Vice Chairman, Chief Victor Tombari Giadom, expressed confidence that the coalition would mobilise up to 90 per cent of the votes in Gokana in the 2027 elections.

Senator Magnus Abe also commended Wike for bringing previously divided political leaders together, saying the people of Gokana were united in their expectations from the coalition.

The meeting was attended by political leaders, traditional rulers, religious leaders, women, youths and other stakeholders from Gokana and neighbouring communities.

The post 2027: Wike offers to lead Tinubu’s re-election campaigns in Imo, Kwara appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Senegal Deny Contact With CAS In 2025 AFCON Row
description: The president of the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF), Abdoulaye Fall, on Wednesday denied Moroccan allegations that he had had “contact” with an arbitrator of the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) who ruled that Senegal were the rightful winners of the 2025 African Cup of Nations
content:
The president of the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF), Abdoulaye Fall, on Wednesday denied Moroccan allegations that he had had “contact” with an arbitrator of the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) who ruled that Senegal were the rightful winners of the 2025 African Cup of Nations.

The Moroccan federation (FRMF) asserted after Tuesday’s ruling there had been “contact” between Fall and German arbitrator Ulrich Haas, one of the three CAS panel members, 48 hours before they decided “unanimously” to award the trophy to Senegal.

“That is absolutely false. I have never had any exchange with any member of CAS,” said Fall on private television channel TFM.

“It surprised and astonished me that such accusations could even be made. I have never been in contact with anyone in connection with this procedure.”

In January, Senegal won a chaotic final 1-0 after extra time.

But two months later the Confederation of African Football (CAF) sensationally overturned the result, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title, after many Senegalese players walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty given to the hosts with the game still goalless.

The CAF Appeals Committee had justified its decision to overturn the result and declare Morocco champions based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations.

Those state that if a team “refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee, it shall be considered (loser) and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition”.

However, the Senegal players eventually returned to the pitch and the final carried on.

The three-person CAS panel therefore considered the referee’s decision to restart the final showed “the conditions for resuming the match had been met”, and that articles 82 and 84 were therefore “not applicable in this case”.

The Moroccan federation has the option of lodging an appeal with the Swiss Federal Supreme Court, which does not rule on the merits of the case but intervenes in procedural matters.

AFP

The post Senegal Deny Contact With CAS In 2025 AFCON Row appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Without Atiku, many Nigerians would have lost interest in democracy – Timi Frank
description:
By Omeiza Ajayi



ABUJA: A former Deputy National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress APC, Comrade Timi Frank, has said many Nigerians would have lost interest in democracy without former Vice President Atiku Abubakar’s consistent fight for due process.







Frank, a political ac
content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: A former Deputy National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress APC, Comrade Timi Frank, has said many Nigerians would have lost interest in democracy without former Vice President Atiku Abubakar’s consistent fight for due process.

Frank, a political activist, made the remark in a statement issued on Wednesday in Abuja to mark the 80th birthday of the Presidential Candidate of the African Democratic Congress ADC.

“Without you, many Nigerians would have totally lost interest in the democratic process but your courage energised not just a few Nigerians and I believe they (Nigerians across regions) will reward you with massive votes in 2027 general elections,” he said.

He described Atiku as an “enduring symbol of democratic resilience, national unity, educational advancement and entrepreneurial excellence.”

According to him, reaching the age of 80 is not merely a celebration of longevity but an opportunity for Nigerians to reflect on the former Vice President’s contributions to nation-building and democratic development.

Frank said Atiku’s consistent advocacy for democratic governance, political inclusion, constitutionalism, freedom of expression and the protection of democratic institutions had made him an influential figure in the country’s political history.

He said the former Vice President’s political journey showed an uncommon belief in healthy political competition, tolerance of divergent opinions and the need for an environment where every Nigerian, irrespective of background, could aspire to leadership.

The activist singled out Atiku’s passion for education, describing his investment in the educational development of young Nigerians as one of his most enduring legacies. In his view, Atiku recognised education as a powerful instrument for social transformation, human capital development and national prosperity.

Frank also applauded what he called Atiku’s detribalised disposition. “Atiku Abubakar represents a Nigeria where our differences should be sources of strength rather than instruments of division. His disposition towards people from different ethnic and religious backgrounds reinforces the belief that our common humanity and shared national aspirations must always take precedence over primordial considerations,” he said.

He praised the former Vice President’s business acumen, describing his journey in the private sector as evidence of entrepreneurial vision, courage and discipline. Frank said Atiku’s contributions to business and education showed that leadership extends beyond occupying public office to creating opportunities, empowering people and investing in institutions that can outlive individuals.

The former APC spokesman noted that in recent years Atiku had remained a prominent voice in national conversations on democratic governance, political accountability, economic reforms and the future of Nigeria. At 80, he added, the former Vice President’s experience, political maturity and understanding of the country’s complex socio-economic realities remained valuable assets in the quest for stability, unity and sustainable development.

“At a time when Nigeria needs greater tolerance, inclusive leadership, democratic maturity and a renewed commitment to nation-building, the values Atiku Abubakar represents deserve recognition and reflection,” Frank said.

The post Without Atiku, many Nigerians would have lost interest in democracy – Timi Frank appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: FG supports 3,520 flood-hit Kogi farmers with inputs
description:
The Federal Government has provided farm inputs to 3,520 farmers in Kogi State whose farmlands and agricultural activities were severely affected by flooding during the 2026 rainy season.
The intervention is aimed at helping the affected farmers recover their losses, restore their farmlands and resu
content:
The Federal Government has provided farm inputs to 3,520 farmers in Kogi State whose farmlands and agricultural activities were severely affected by flooding during the 2026 rainy season.

The intervention is aimed at helping the affected farmers recover their losses, restore their farmlands and resume agricultural production.

The Executive Secretary of the National Agricultural Development Fund, Mohammed Ibrahim, disclosed this on Wednesday while speaking on the Federal Government’s response to the flood disaster in the state.

Muhammad Gidado, who represented the NADF boss at a stakeholders’ meeting, said the extent of the damage necessitated urgent support for the affected farming communities.

According to him, the intervention was designed not only to help farmers recover from the destruction caused by the floods but also to strengthen food production and agricultural resilience in the state.

“Under the intervention programme, beneficiaries are expected to receive urea and NPK fertilisers, 15kg bags of rice seeds, pre-planting, pre-emergence and early post-emergence chemicals, as well as insecticides,” he said.

Gidado said the inputs would enable the affected farmers to resume cultivation and rebuild their agricultural activities after the flood-induced losses.

He stressed the need to ensure that the intervention reached the intended beneficiaries without delay, urging the Kogi State Government, community leaders and other stakeholders to ensure transparency in the distribution process.

He also appealed to the beneficiaries to make proper use of the inputs to achieve the programme’s objectives and contribute to food security.

Gidado said the initiative reflected the Federal Government’s commitment to protecting farmers, strengthening agricultural resilience and sustaining food production despite the impact of climate-related disasters.

In his response, the Kogi State Commissioner for Agriculture and Food Security, Timothy Ojomah, commended President Bola Tinubu, the Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Abubakar Kyari, and the leadership of the NADF for extending the intervention to farmers affected by flooding in the state.

He said the intervention would provide critical support to farmers whose livelihoods were disrupted by the 2026 floods and help accelerate the recovery of the agricultural sector in Kogi.

The post FG supports 3,520 flood-hit Kogi farmers with inputs appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Reps urge Tinubu to intervene in Delta political violence
description:
The House of Representatives has called on President Bola Tinubu to urgently intervene in the escalating political violence in Delta State, warning that the situation could warrant the consideration of constitutional emergency measures if it deteriorates further.
The House also urged the Inspector-G
content:
The House of Representatives has called on President Bola Tinubu to urgently intervene in the escalating political violence in Delta State, warning that the situation could warrant the consideration of constitutional emergency measures if it deteriorates further.

The House also urged the Inspector-General of Police to establish a special investigative team to probe successive attacks on political campaigns and rallies in the state, identify those responsible and prosecute the perpetrators and their sponsors.

The resolutions were contained in a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by the member representing Okpe/Sapele/Uvwie Federal Constituency of Delta State, Benedict Etanabene, during plenary on Wednesday.

The motion followed a series of violent incidents involving political gatherings across the state, including the November 23 attack on the campaign activities of former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, at Uduere community in Ughelli North Local Government Area, which left six people dead and several others injured.

Moving the motion, Etanabene expressed concern that the recurring attacks had created an atmosphere of fear among political parties, candidates, supporters and residents, threatening their constitutional right to participate in democratic activities.

He recalled that on November 7, “violence erupted during a political procession along Nnebisi Road, Asaba, resulting in the death of one person and injuries to five others, figures confirmed by the police.”

The lawmaker also cited an attack on a political party’s campaign team at Okpai, Ward 4, Ndokwa East Local Government Area, on November 11, which reportedly left five members injured.

He further recalled an earlier incident in September during a political mobilisation exercise in Effurun, Uvwie Local Government Area, where a participant reportedly sustained machete injuries and later died in hospital.

Etanabene said “the latest attack at Uduere, where at least six people were reportedly killed by suspected political thugs, underscored the urgency of decisive intervention by the Federal Government and security agencies.”

He warned that the growing frequency of attacks on political activities could trigger a wider breakdown of law and order, undermine peaceful coexistence and threaten the credibility of the 2027 general elections.

“The increasing frequency of attacks on political activities, if not urgently addressed, could escalate into a widespread breakdown of law and order, threaten peaceful coexistence and undermine the credibility of the democratic process ahead of the 2027 General Elections,” he said.

The motion further expressed concern that the recurrence of violence suggested that existing security arrangements might not be doing enough to deter perpetrators and protect political actors and innocent citizens.

It also warned that failure to identify, arrest and prosecute those responsible could encourage impunity and embolden further attacks.

Among its resolutions, the House urged Tinubu, in his capacity as Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, to direct relevant security agencies to take immediate measures to prevent further violence and loss of lives in Delta State.

It also called on the Inspector-General of Police to deploy adequate personnel, including tactical and intelligence units, to identified flashpoints across the state.

The lawmakers specifically demanded a comprehensive, impartial and independent investigation into all reported attacks on political campaigns, with a view to identifying not only the perpetrators but also their sponsors and financiers.

The motion further urged the police and other security agencies to provide adequate protection for all political rallies, campaigns, processions and other lawful political activities, irrespective of the political affiliation of the organisers.

Etanabene cautioned security operatives against standing by while political gatherings came under attack, insisting that their responsibility was to protect lives and maintain public order.

“The police, when present, should not act as bystanders, watching the unfolding chaos,” the lawmaker said.

In another significant resolution, the House urged the President to closely monitor the security situation in Delta State and consider invoking Section 305 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, if the situation reached the constitutionally prescribed threshold of an actual or imminent breakdown of public order and public safety.

The motion also called on the Federal Government to facilitate medical assistance and other necessary support for victims of the attacks and families of those killed.

It mandated the House Committees on Police Affairs, National Security and Intelligence, Electoral Matters, and Political Parties Matters to engage the Inspector-General of Police and other security agencies on the incidents and report back within two weeks with recommendations for immediate and long-term solutions.

The lawmakers further asked the Inspector-General of Police to invite all governorship candidates in the state for a meeting to remind them of the constitutional provisions and Electoral Act governing political campaigns and electioneering activities.

The latest attack has drawn national attention to the security of political activities in Delta State ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The Nigeria Police Force confirmed on November 24 that six people died and several others sustained injuries during the Uduere incident. The Inspector-General of Police subsequently ordered a thorough and impartial investigation into the attack, including an examination of the conduct of officers deployed to the scene.

The Delta State Government also imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area following the killings, while Governor Sheriff Oborevwori directed security agencies to track down and arrest those responsible.

The renewed calls for intervention come amid growing concerns about the safety of political candidates, party supporters and campaign volunteers as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 elections.

The post Reps urge Tinubu to intervene in Delta political violence appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: FCID decorates 14 promoted officers, demands professionalism
description:
By Matthew Johnson



The Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of the Force Criminal Investigation Department (FCID) Annex, Alagbon, Ikoyi, Lagos, Simeon Akpanudom, has decorated 14 newly promoted police officers, charging them to uphold discipline, professionalism and continuous learning
content:
By Matthew Johnson

The Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of the Force Criminal Investigation Department (FCID) Annex, Alagbon, Ikoyi, Lagos, Simeon Akpanudom, has decorated 14 newly promoted police officers, charging them to uphold discipline, professionalism and continuous learning.

Akpanudom gave the charge during the decoration ceremony held at the FCID Annex, Lagos, according to a statement issued on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, by the department’s Public Relations Officer, ASP Mayegun Aminat.

He said the new ranks came with greater responsibilities, higher expectations and increased accountability, urging the officers to justify their promotions through exemplary conduct and improved service delivery.

The promoted officers comprised one Assistant Commissioner of Police elevated to Deputy Commissioner of Police, two Superintendents of Police promoted to Chief Superintendents of Police, six Assistant Superintendents of Police elevated to Deputy Superintendents of Police, and five Police Constables promoted to Corporals.

Among those decorated were DCP Salami Janet, CSP Ayoleyi Ajayi, DSP Gbenga Omoniyi and Corporal Adewuyi Adetolase.

The AIG congratulated the officers, describing their promotions as recognition of their dedication, commitment and contributions to the Nigeria Police Force.

He also commended the Police Service Commission and the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Disu, for recognising the officers’ hard work and meritorious service.

Akpanudom urged the newly promoted personnel to demonstrate diligence, discipline and professionalism in the discharge of their duties.

He emphasised the importance of continuous learning and professional development, particularly in emerging areas of crime such as cybercrime, urging the officers to keep abreast of national developments and evolving security challenges.

The police chief also called on them to embrace community engagement, effective communication and people-oriented policing, noting that public confidence in the police depended largely on officers’ conduct and interactions with citizens.

He further charged the officers to exercise restraint, control their emotions and demonstrate maturity, fairness and respect for human dignity in their dealings with members of the public.

Akpanudom also urged Nigerians to continue supporting and cooperating with the police in the discharge of their constitutional responsibilities of protecting lives and property and maintaining law and order.

He said, “Promotion comes with greater responsibilities, higher expectations and increased accountability. You must justify your new ranks through discipline, professionalism, diligence and an unwavering commitment to duty.

“I advise the officers to familiarise themselves with their schedules of duty and understand the responsibilities attached to their respective offices.”

In her vote of thanks, DCP Salami Janet, who spoke on behalf of the newly promoted officers, appreciated Akpanudom and AIG Lennox Taylor for their presence and support.

She assured the police leadership that the officers would remain committed to professionalism, integrity, dignity and excellence in service.

Salami also pledged that they would uphold the core values of the Force and contribute to efforts to rebuild public confidence in the police.

The post FCID decorates 14 promoted officers, demands professionalism appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Katsina govt mandates official approval for Emirs hosting foreign visitors
description:
The Katsina State Government has introduced a new approval requirement for traditional rulers across the state, directing them to obtain official clearance before receiving foreign visitors in their palaces.
Under the directive, traditional rulers are expected to seek authorisation from the Departme
content:
The Katsina State Government has introduced a new approval requirement for traditional rulers across the state, directing them to obtain official clearance before receiving foreign visitors in their palaces.

Under the directive, traditional rulers are expected to seek authorisation from the Departments of Protocol and Cabinet/Security Matters, operating under the Office of the Secretary to the State Government.

The Commissioner for Information and Culture, Bala Zango, announced the development in a statement released on Wednesday, making it clear that traditional rulers must secure the required approval before hosting foreign guests.

According to the statement, the measure is intended to ensure proper coordination, security and adherence to official protocols during visits by foreign nationals to emirates’ palaces.

“The directive is intended to ensure proper coordination, security, and adherence to official protocols during visits to Emirs’ palace by foreign nationals, while also placing the traditional rulers under a formal regulatory framework regarding international relations.

“The measure is also intended to streamline interactions with foreign nationals and ensure that the government is fully aware of international engagements involving traditional institutions,” the statement read.

Zango said the directive was part of the administration’s broader strategy to strengthen security at the grassroots level.

He noted that “the state government partly relies on traditional rulers as key stakeholders in peace-building,”

“Furthermore, this clearance process is another strategy of the state government to ensure that all international visits to traditional domains are documented and vetted for safety,” the statement added.

The directive came a day after the state government announced the suspension of the Emir of Daura, Umar Faruk Umar, from official engagements and travels following a sexual assault allegation made against him by a Polish tourist, Mirka Czee.

The government also constituted a committee to investigate the allegation and advise it on the appropriate course of action.

Czee had released a video of her encounter with the Emir behind a closed door during a visit to his palace on November 14 and alleged that the monarch touched her breasts without her consent.

She said she recorded part of the encounter using Meta smart glasses and later shared the footage on social media.

The tourist, who was on a 30-day tour of Nigeria, said she waited until she had left the country before making the allegation public.

Following the circulation of the video and her account, Czee faced online harassment, including insults, victim-blaming and death threats.

She shared screenshots of some of the messages on Instagram, with some users demanding that she withdraw her allegation or delete the video.

Amnesty International Nigeria condemned the threats, saying the tourist had received hundreds of death threats, including warnings that she would be tracked down and killed or harmed.

The Daura Emirate Council had earlier said it was reviewing the footage to establish its authenticity and determine whether it had been manipulated.

The Katsina State Government said the Emir’s suspension would remain in place pending the outcome of the investigation and assured the public that the committee’s findings and recommendations would be implemented.

The post Katsina govt mandates official approval for Emirs hosting foreign visitors appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Tinubu pledges to secure release of abducted Borno schoolchildren
description:
President Bola Tinubu has pledged that his administration will do everything possible to secure the release of about 78 schoolchildren abducted from Mussa Primary School and Government Day Secondary School, Lassa, in Askira-Uba Local Government Area of Borno State.
Tinubu made the pledge on Wednesda
content:
President Bola Tinubu has pledged that his administration will do everything possible to secure the release of about 78 schoolchildren abducted from Mussa Primary School and Government Day Secondary School, Lassa, in Askira-Uba Local Government Area of Borno State.

Tinubu made the pledge on Wednesday in Maiduguri while addressing supporters at the All Progressives Congress North-East Zonal Rally held at the El-Kanemi Sports Centre.

The President said his administration remained committed to rescuing the children abducted by suspected Boko Haram terrorists and defeating insurgency in the North-East.

“We shall do everything possible to rescue the schoolchildren abducted in Mussa and Lassa communities,” he said.

“They are there with our prayers, with our armed forces and intelligence. We will rescue them, Insha Allah,” he added.

Tinubu also acknowledged the sacrifices of military personnel and other security operatives, particularly those serving on the frontline, assuring them of the government’s support in the fight against terrorism.

“The present administration under my leadership acknowledges the sacrifices of troops, especially those at the frontline. Therefore, the government would do its best to support our security operatives to defeat terrorism in this region,” he said.

He added, “We give respect to our men and women of the armed forces who have been in the bush, in the sun and in the rain, and who have put their lives on the line for us and for Borno, particularly Maiduguri, to have peace.

“We will achieve that peace. Terrorism will go. They have the opportunity now to lay down their arms, lay down all arms and surrender all weapons. Change from the character of terrorism and banditry.”

Earlier, Borno State Governor, Babagana Zulum, thanked the President for choosing Maiduguri as the venue for the zonal rally.

He expressed satisfaction with the large turnout and orderly conduct of APC supporters.

Zulum said Borno State had benefited significantly from the Federal Government’s Renewed Hope Agenda, citing the construction of the Gombe-Biu-Maiduguri Road and the establishment of the Federal Polytechnic, Monguno; Federal College of Education, Gwoza; and Federal University of Agriculture and Entrepreneurship, Bama.

The governor urged residents of Borno and other states in the North-East to vote for APC candidates at all levels in the 2027 general elections.

The post Tinubu pledges to secure release of abducted Borno schoolchildren appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Atiku should wait till 2031 to contest presidency, says Bode George
description:
Chief Olabode George, a former Deputy National Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), says he remains opposed to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s presidential ambition ahead of the 2027 general elections.



George said Atiku, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) candidate, continued
content:
Chief Olabode George, a former Deputy National Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), says he remains opposed to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s presidential ambition ahead of the 2027 general elections.

George said Atiku, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) candidate, continued to believe his continued ambition to succeed President Bola Tinubu was inconsistent with the power rotation arrangement designed to promote equity, fairness and national unity between the North and South.

George, who spoke at a news conference marking his 81st birthday, said the arrangement, which was part of the vision of the founding fathers of the current democratic dispensation, provided for the sharing of six strategic national positions among the country’s six geopolitical zones.

According to him, the arrangement requires power to rotate between the northern and southern regions after every eight years to ensure fairness and preserve national unity.

“It would have been an aberration if a southerner insisted on succeeding former President Olusegun Obasanjo in 2007.

“Later, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar disrupted this trajectory when he insisted on succeeding President Buhari, a fellow northerner, in 2023.

“This was why I kicked against his ambition. He went ahead and did everything possible but failed.

“And now, he is back, still seeking to be president when the South has not yet completed eight years. I am still against his presidential ambition,” he said.

George said Atiku was the only northerner currently pursuing the presidency in 2027, despite the South having the opportunity to complete its eight-year tenure.

“Is Atiku the only Northerner in Nigeria? Why is he contesting for this office every four years? Why is he inordinately ambitious? He is 80 years old already. I want to advise him to forget his presidential ambition next year.

“He should return in 2031 when the seat returns to the North. By then, he will be close to 85 years old, and Nigerians will decide if they want to vote for him or not,” he said.

George, a former military governor of Ondo State, said selfish political ambitions, disregard for democratic principles and the manipulation of national institutions were threatening Nigeria’s unity and democratic development.

He also expressed concern over what he described as inconsistencies in the judiciary, particularly conflicting judgments delivered by courts of coordinate jurisdiction on political disputes ahead of the 2027 elections.

George warned that the situation was creating uncertainty for political parties and candidates, with some still unsure of their eligibility to contest the forthcoming elections.

“Another contentious issue is the inconsistency of the judiciary as an independent arm of government in its interventions on political matters, with courts of the same competent jurisdiction delivering conflicting judgements on the same political disputes.

“If these cases are not resolved soon, the essence of the elections will be jeopardised and this could lead to political disturbances, the outcome of which no one can predict,” he said.

He questioned public confidence in the judiciary, urging judicial authorities to resolve outstanding political disputes promptly and uphold their constitutional responsibility as the last hope of the common man.

The PDP chieftain also condemned alleged persecution of political opponents, citing the continued detention of former Kaduna State Governor Nasir El-Rufai over multiple charges and what he described as stringent bail conditions.

He called on the judiciary to review the conditions and grant El-Rufai bail, insisting that the law should be applied fairly, without political considerations or intimidation.

“Bail is not a favour granted at the pleasure of authority; it is a constitutional right rooted in justice, fairness and the presumption of innocence.

“I want to plead with the judicial authorities to look into the El-Rufai issue. He should be allowed to go home and come to the court from there because two wrongs will never make a right,” he said.

On electoral violence, George expressed concern over alleged attacks on opposition gatherings and political rallies in some states, warning that such developments threatened democratic participation and peaceful elections.

He urged President Tinubu to caution members and supporters of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), as well as other political parties, against violence and intimidation.

“The right of opposition voices to organise, to speak, and to contest power is not a privilege granted by those in authority, but a constitutional necessity.

“To suppress dissent or undermine opposition structures is to erode the very framework that legitimises governance,” he said.

George also called on the National Peace Committee, led by former Head of State retired Gen. Abdulsalami Abubakar, to intensify efforts towards preventing political violence before, during and after the elections.

He said Nigeria’s democracy could not thrive where political opponents were intimidated, opposition parties weakened or public institutions manipulated for partisan interests.

The former PDP chieftain further urged the government to ensure a speedy process on the establishment of state police, describing it as a necessary measure to address kidnapping, banditry, terrorism and other security challenges.

He expressed delight that lawmakers across the 36 states had endorsed the proposed constitutional amendment for state police and forwarded it to the President for assent.

“I am filled with joy because during the Constitutional Conference set up by former President Goodluck Jonathan in 2014, of which I was a member, State Police was unanimously approved.

“That’s the only way to check kidnapping, banditry, terrorism and other vices in the country. The President should please sign the bill into law immediately and monitor its implementation by states,” he said.

George also called for deliberate efforts to eliminate tribalism and religious bigotry, which he described as major obstacles to national unity and development.

He urged political leaders to promote tolerance, national cohesion and equal opportunities, irrespective of ethnic, religious or political differences.

The retired naval commodore further advocated the establishment of skill acquisition centres across the country, saying investment in vocational training and human capacity development would accelerate national growth.

He maintained that respect for the rule of law, judicial independence, democratic accountability and protection of citizens’ rights were indispensable to building a stable nation.

George urged Nigerians to place national interest above personal and partisan ambitions.

He said his 81 years of life and service to the country had strengthened his resolve to continue speaking against injustice, political impunity and practices capable of undermining national unity.

“Nobody should keep quiet again. Greedy ambitions of a few individuals must be jettisoned in the collective interest of Nigerians. We may belong to various parties, but we have only one country: Nigeria,” he said.

George urged Nigerians to work together to restore the country’s standing in Africa and transform it from a mere geographical expression into a united and prosperous nation-state. (NAN)

title: BREAKING: Gunmen disrupt Peter Obi’s campaign in Edo, open fire on NDC members, destroy campaign materials
description:
Political thugs have allegedly attacked the campaign convoy and campaign office of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Benin City, Edo State, amid preparations for the visit of the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi.
Channels Television reported the incident on Wednesday, following an ea
content:
Political thugs have allegedly attacked the campaign convoy and campaign office of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Benin City, Edo State, amid preparations for the visit of the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi.

Channels Television reported the incident on Wednesday, following an earlier alert by the party that it had received intelligence about a possible attack on its town hall meeting in the state capital.

The Edo State Coordinator of the NDC Campaign Council, John Yakubu, had disclosed that the party was informed of plans to disrupt the event as supporters prepared to leave the campaign office to receive Obi at the airport.

Despite the warning, the party said it would proceed with its plans to welcome the presidential candidate, while calling for adequate security around the event.

Videos obtained by Channels Television reportedly showed bloodstains on the party’s campaign vehicles, while suspected bullet casings were seen on the floor of the campaign office.

One of the videos also showed an injured man lying in a pool of blood as supporters and hospital personnel attended to him at an unidentified medical facility. The footage was considered too graphic for broadcast.

The reported attack came barely 48 hours after the campaign convoy of former Deputy Senate President and NDC Delta Central senatorial candidate, Ovie Omo-Agege, was attacked during a campaign event in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, on Monday.

Preliminary police reports indicated that six people were killed in the Delta attack, while several others sustained injuries. Omo-Agege reportedly escaped unhurt.

Following the incident, the Delta State Police Command invited Omo-Agege and five other individuals for questioning as part of its investigation into the violence.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, Bright Edafe, said the individuals had been directed to report to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) at the police headquarters in Asaba on specified dates.

Omo-Agege was scheduled to appear on Thursday at 11 a.m., while Egbo was invited for 2 p.m. on the same day.

The other five invitees were identified as Gowon Egoide, a former chairman of Uduere Quarters; Onoriode Oneya, the incumbent youth chairman of Uduere Community; Edirin Wokode Ewhubare, an associate of Egoide; Erukaye Egoide, Egoide’s nephew; and Tony Gabon Mevowovo, another associate of Egoide.

The latest reported incident in Benin has raised fresh concerns over security at political campaign events, particularly as the NDC prepares for Obi’s engagement with supporters in Edo State.

title: FG begins N1.45tn ports upgrade, targets 20,000 jobs
description:
The Federal Government has commenced a £746m modernisation programme for the Lagos Port Complex, Apapa, and Tin Can Island Ports, with the project expected to improve cargo handling, reduce trade costs and generate at least 20,000 direct and indirect jobs.
The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Ad
content:
The Federal Government has commenced a £746m modernisation programme for the Lagos Port Complex, Apapa, and Tin Can Island Ports, with the project expected to improve cargo handling, reduce trade costs and generate at least 20,000 direct and indirect jobs.

The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, flagged off the project on Wednesday at a ceremony held at Tin Can Island Port, alongside the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, and other senior government officials.

Oyetola’s media aide, Dr Bolaji Akinola, disclosed this in a statement released on Wednesday.

The project, valued at approximately N1.45tn, is expected to tackle longstanding infrastructure deficiencies at the two ports, attract more international shipping lines and strengthen Nigeria’s position in regional and global trade.

Speaking at the ceremony, Oyetola said the initiative was a major step towards fulfilling President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda through infrastructure development, investment and job creation.

He said the country’s growing population and expanding trade had placed enormous pressure on port facilities that were no longer adequate for modern shipping operations.

According to the minister, Apapa Port was established in 1913, while Tin Can Island Port was commissioned in 1977, when Nigeria’s population was about 67.2 million, annual trade stood at $17bn and cargo throughput was 8.11 million metric tonnes.

He said the country’s population had since increased to about 240 million, merchandise trade had exceeded $100bn annually, while cargo throughput had risen to 129.3 million metric tonnes, almost 16 times the volume recorded when Tin Can Island Port opened.

Oyetola said the disparity between the growth in economic activity and the capacity of the ports had made their comprehensive upgrade imperative.

“The cost of inaction is far greater than the cost of modernisation,” he added, saying Nigeria would not surrender its competitive advantage.

He said the government was seeking to increase direct calls by international shipping lines, retain cargo destined for Nigeria and expand transhipment activities.

“Our ambition is to attract more direct calls by international shipping lines, retain Nigerian-bound cargo, expand transhipment opportunities and establish our ports as preferred gateways to trade across the African Continental Free Trade Area. We cannot achieve this ambition with infrastructure that falls behind the demands of modern shipping,” Oyetola said.

The minister lamented that cargo dwell time at Nigerian ports had historically ranged from 10 to 18 days, compared with three to five days at leading international ports.

He said the delays had resulted in congestion, demurrage and storage charges, with inefficiencies estimated to cost the Nigerian economy as much as $4bn annually.

Oyetola warned that Nigeria risked losing maritime business to neighbouring countries that had invested in deep-sea ports and modern cargo-handling facilities.

He said the project would cover the rehabilitation of quay walls and berths, dredging and navigation channels, access facilities, cargo-handling equipment and operational systems.

“The project will entail the comprehensive rehabilitation and upgrading of critical port infrastructure, including quay walls and berths, dredging and navigation channels, access facilities, cargo-handling equipment and operational systems. It will address longstanding physical constraints while advancing more integrated, efficient and digitally enabled port operations,” Oyetola said.

The minister said the construction and related activities would create jobs in engineering, dredging, logistics, transportation, port operations and other sectors.

“Our agricultural products, processed foods, solid minerals, manufactured goods, textiles and petrochemical products must compete effectively in regional and global markets. Efficient ports will help exporters meet delivery schedules, reduce costs, preserve product quality and secure international buyers’ confidence. They will equally create a more enabling environment for manufacturers, agro-processors and micro, small and medium-sized enterprises,” he said.

To minimise disruptions during construction, Oyetola said he had approved an Inter-Ministerial Committee comprising the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, the Nigerian Ports Authority and the Nigeria Ports Economic Regulatory Agency.

The committee, he said, would prepare a Port Business Continuity and Cargo Flow Management Plan to coordinate construction phases, vessel scheduling, cargo evacuation, truck movement and the use of alternative ports and transport systems.

Oyetola added that the Lagos ports upgrade was part of a wider maritime development programme that included the approved modernisation of Onne, Rivers, Delta and Calabar ports.

Also speaking, Oyedele said the project would help reduce the cost of doing business, improve the competitiveness of Nigerian products and support economic growth.

He described the financing arrangement as Nigeria’s largest sovereign export credit transaction since 2009 and the first project in the country for Poland’s Export Credit Insurance Corporation, KUKE.

Oyedele said the transaction reflected international confidence in Nigeria’s economic reforms and assured stakeholders of the government’s commitment to timely approvals, transparency and a stable operating environment.

The Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority, Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, described the groundbreaking as a landmark in the authority’s history.

He said the NPA would ensure that the project was executed in line with approved designs, engineering standards and contractual timelines, while maintaining technical supervision, quality assurance and coordination.

Dantsoho also pledged attention to safety, environmental standards and the uninterrupted operation of the ports during construction.

The ceremony was attended by Poland’s Deputy Foreign Minister, Marcin Bosacki; Polish Ambassador to Nigeria, Michal Cygan; and the British Deputy High Commissioner in Lagos, Jonny Baxter, as well as contractors, international financing partners and maritime industry stakeholders.

Apapa and Tin Can Island are among Nigeria’s principal maritime gateways, handling a substantial share of the country’s import and export cargo.

However, ageing infrastructure, congestion, lengthy cargo clearance and evacuation processes, and high logistics costs have frequently been cited as challenges affecting port efficiency.

The modernisation is intended to improve the capacity and operational performance of the Lagos ports at a time when African countries are seeking to expand trade under the African Continental Free Trade Area.

The post FG begins N1.45tn ports upgrade, targets 20,000 jobs appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Ekiti First Lady urges protection of women from gender-based violence
description:
Wife of Ekiti State Governor, Prof. Olayemi Oyebanji, has called for stronger measures to protect women and girls from gender-based violence, ensure justice for survivors and hold perpetrators accountable.
Oyebanji said that no woman or girl should be forced to endure violence in silence, adding tha
content:
Wife of Ekiti State Governor, Prof. Olayemi Oyebanji, has called for stronger measures to protect women and girls from gender-based violence, ensure justice for survivors and hold perpetrators accountable.

Oyebanji said that no woman or girl should be forced to endure violence in silence, adding that survivors must not be blamed, abandoned or subjected to further emotional trauma while seeking justice.

The governor’s wife spoke in Ado Ekiti on Wednesday in a message to mark the 2026 edition of the 16 Days of Activism Against GBV, with the theme, “Unite to End Violence Against Women and Girls: Ensure Justice, Protect Survivors, End Impunity,” running from November 25 to December 10.

She said that relevant government agencies, security institutions, civil society organisations and other stakeholders would continue to strengthen collaboration to expand advocacy, improve survivor support services and ensure access to justice across Ekiti State.

The First Lady said, “Eliminating GBV requires sustained commitment, collective action and a justice system that prioritises the protection of vulnerable people”.

Prof Oyebanji stressed that access to justice should not depend on an individual’s financial capacity, social status or personal connections, noting that every woman and girl deserved equal protection under the law.

The governor’s wife, who urged parents and guardians to create safe and supportive environments where children could report abuse without fear of intimidation or stigmatisation, also appealed to traditional rulers, religious leaders, teachers and community stakeholders “to challenge harmful cultural practices, promote gender equality and protect the fundamental rights of women and girls”.

She urged men and boys to become active partners in combating gender-based violence by promoting mutual respect, kindness and responsible behaviour, stressing that violence against women and girls must never be tolerated or excused.

The First Lady encouraged survivors of abuse to speak out and seek help, assuring them that the state government remained committed to supporting them.

She, however, maintained that efforts to combat GBV must extend beyond the 16-day campaign, requiring sustained commitment from individuals, families, institutions and communities.

Oyebanji urged residents to make the protection of women and girls a shared responsibility, saying that ending gender-based violence required deliberate action beyond declarations and awareness campaigns.

title: ‘Legends never truly die’ – May Edochie mourns father-in-law Pete
description:
By Adegboyega Adeleye







May Edochie, the estranged wife of Pete Edochie’s son Yul, has mourned the veteran actor, calling him “an institution” whose legacy will live on.







In a glowing tribute shared on Instagram on Wednesday, May recalled that false reports of the veteran actor’s death ha
content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

May Edochie, the estranged wife of Pete Edochie’s son Yul, has mourned the veteran actor, calling him “an institution” whose legacy will live on.

In a glowing tribute shared on Instagram on Wednesday, May recalled that false reports of the veteran actor’s death had circulated over the years, but he had continued working.

Pete’s family announced that he died in Enugu at 12:30 a.m. on Wednesday, aged 79, after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer.

“For so many years, every year, someone somewhere makes a false announcement of your death but you kept going with strength to continue working,” she wrote.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by May Yul-Edochie (@mayyuledochie)

Reflecting on his death, May said: “One moment, there is life; the next, eternity calls. Such is the fragility of human existence. We make plans, hold conversations, nurse expectations and believe there will always be another day, until life reminds us that tomorrow is never promised.”

Calling him the “Lion of Africa,” she said his passing reminded her that “beyond all, the opinions, the misunderstandings and the stories that life sometimes throws around, we are all humans, and death has a way of reminding us of what truly matters.”

May also said she would remember Pete as a veteran whose name, voice, presence and contributions to Nollywood would remain unforgettable.

“You were an institution, a father figure to many and a man whose legacy will outlive his earthly years,” she wrote.

“One thing is certain: legends never truly die; they live on through the memories they create and the impact they leave behind.”

She also prayed for Pete’s wife, Josephine, and other relatives, writing: “To mummy and the rest of us you have left behind, may the good Lord strengthen through Christ our Lord.”

She ended the tribute with prayers for the deceased: “God rest your soul Ononenyi!”

Vanguard News

title: ​We Cannot Stay in the House: How Gwagwalada families are surviving Nigeria’s rising heatwave
description:
By Oladosu Adebola Oluwaseun
In Gwagwalada, the relentless heat has pushed daily life past the point of discomfort. Speaking on the harsh, dry weather conditions gripping the area, local resident Aderemi Christiana described a community struggling to find relief both at home and in the workplace.
“T
content:
By Oladosu Adebola Oluwaseun

In Gwagwalada, the relentless heat has pushed daily life past the point of discomfort. Speaking on the harsh, dry weather conditions gripping the area, local resident Aderemi Christiana described a community struggling to find relief both at home and in the workplace.

“The weather is very harsh,” she said, explaining that inside houses, the trapped heat makes staying indoors nearly unbearable.

“Even to the children in the house, you cannot stay in the house. We have to go outside to look for fresh air because everywhere is hot.”

The youngest residents are bearing the brunt of the scorching temperatures, with Christiana noting that “their skin, they have started to have rashes due to the heat.”

​At workplaces across Gwagwalada, the story is much the same, as “many people, even at working place cannot stay outside. We have to rush because of heat in the office.”

Against the backdrop of grim national warnings predicting over 30,000 heatwave-related deaths across Nigeria, Christiana voiced an urgent plea for official intervention: “We need government to come to the rescue of Gwagwalada in particular… at least to do something, for the weather is not comfortable for us.”

​Yet, while waiting for official aid, she urged her neighbors to take immediate, practical steps to protect themselves and cool their surroundings.

Echoing the principle that “when you cut down a tree, you have to replace it with 10,” she emphasized that “each resident should at least try to plant a tree.”

She also advised residents to prioritize airflow when constructing homes rather than relying on a single window:

“Everybody should let there be open ventilation, cross-ventilation in the house when they are building. Don’t put just a window in the house.” Finally, she urged families not to lock up every entrance or stay trapped indoors, advising them to “open all the openings, all the entrances, the window, the doors, so that there’ll be fresh air,” while stepping outside in the cooler evenings to breathe.

Through Christiana’s eyes, surviving Gwagwalada’s extreme heat requires both urgent government backing and a community-wide commitment to greener, better-ventilated living spaces.

The post ​We Cannot Stay in the House: How Gwagwalada families are surviving Nigeria’s rising heatwave appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Katsina tightens security rules, requires Emirs to report foreign visitors
description:
The Katsina State Government has directed emirs and other traditional rulers across the state to obtain official approval before receiving foreign visitors in their palaces.
Under the directive, traditional rulers are required to secure clearance from the Departments of Protocol and Cabinet/Security
content:
The Katsina State Government has directed emirs and other traditional rulers across the state to obtain official approval before receiving foreign visitors in their palaces.

Under the directive, traditional rulers are required to secure clearance from the Departments of Protocol and Cabinet/Security Matters under the Office of the Secretary to the State Government (SSG) before hosting foreign nationals.

The government said the measure was aimed at strengthening security, improving coordination and preventing breaches of official protocol during visits by foreign nationals to traditional institutions.

The Commissioner for Information and Culture, Bala Salisu Zango, announced the directive in a statement issued on Wednesday.

According to the statement, the new arrangement would ensure that international engagements involving traditional institutions were properly documented, regulated and brought under government oversight.

It added that the clearance process would enable the government to maintain records of such engagements and screen foreign visitors for security purposes.

Zango said the directive formed part of the state government’s broader efforts to strengthen grassroots security, noting that traditional rulers remained important partners in peace-building across Katsina State.

He explained that documenting and vetting visits by foreign nationals to traditional domains was necessary for effective security coordination.

The announcement came a day after the state government suspended all official engagements and travels by the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Umar Farouk Umar, pending the outcome of an investigation into allegations of sexual assault levelled against him by a foreign female tourist.

title: My finances were better before Tinubu’s tenure – Seyi Law
description:
By Enitan Abdultawab







Nigerian comedian, Seyi Law, has admitted that his personal finances were in a better state before President Bola Tinubu assumed office, despite defending the administration’s economic policies and urging Nigerians to endure the hardship associated with them.







The c
content:
By Enitan Abdultawab

Nigerian comedian, Seyi Law, has admitted that his personal finances were in a better state before President Bola Tinubu assumed office, despite defending the administration’s economic policies and urging Nigerians to endure the hardship associated with them.

The comedian made the remarks during an appearance on the Charity Zone Podcast, where he argued that the benefits of some government policies might take years to become evident.

Seyi Law, a known supporter of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), said economic policies often come with immediate difficulties before producing long term gains.

Using China as an example, he said the country’s emergence as a major global economy involved significant sacrifices.

“For China to be where they are today, if they tell you the number of Chinese who died, you won’t believe,” he said.

When asked whether Nigerians must die before enjoying the benefits of the country’s economic policies, the comedian clarified that people would have to experience the hardship resulting from such decisions before the expected gains could materialise.

“No. You must feel the pain of the policy to reap the benefit of it. Every good policy that becomes good stabilises after 10 to 12 years,” he said.

Despite his defence of the government, Seyi Law acknowledged the economic difficulties facing many Nigerians, admitting that people were struggling to afford basic necessities.

“People are hungry. I will be a hypocrite, a bad person to say people are not hungry,” he said.

He also spoke about how the rising cost of living had affected his ability to support family members living in the United Kingdom.

According to him, an amount that previously covered their needs now requires a significantly higher sum, forcing him to increase his financial support.

“My finances were better before this government came in. My family are in the UK and then with N1.2 million they are okay, but now I have had to double that to like N4.5 million every other month,” he added.

title: Guardiola says next coaching job will be with national team
description:
By Adegboyega Adeleye



Pep Guardiola says he will manage a national team when he returns to coaching after turning down an offer to take charge of Italy because he felt he needed a break from football.



In an interview reported by Reuters, Guardiola told his former Barcelona teammate Romario tha
content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Pep Guardiola says he will manage a national team when he returns to coaching after turning down an offer to take charge of Italy because he felt he needed a break from football.

In an interview reported by Reuters, Guardiola told his former Barcelona teammate Romario that he had spoken with the Italian Football Federation but was not ready to take another job.

“It was one of the greatest honours I’ve had, that they thought of me to coach Italy. But it came at a time when I needed to stop,” he said. “If it had happened a year or two earlier, I probably would have accepted.”

The Spaniard said the approach came when Paolo Maldini and Leonardo, whom he described as people he loved dearly, reached out to him. He added that he did not know how long his break would last.

“Right now I feel very well,” Guardiola told former Brazil forward Romario. “But if I return to football one day, it will be when my stomach tells me it’s the right time.”

Guardiola left Manchester City at the end of last season after a decade in charge. He won six Premier League titles, including four in succession, three FA Cups, five League Cups and the Champions League.

In the same interview, Guardiola said Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo’s rivalry helped prolong both players’ careers. The pair won a combined 13 Ballon d’Or awards and dominated football for more than a decade, including during their spells at Barcelona and Real Madrid.

“If Messi hadn’t had Cristiano, or if Cristiano hadn’t had Messi, their careers would likely have been shorter,” Guardiola said. “They had each other in their rearview mirrors, watching what the other was doing made them think: ‘I want to be better than him, I want to win more than him,’”

Guardiola, who coached Messi for four seasons at Barcelona, credited the forward for much of his success there. He led the Spanish club to 14 trophies, including two Champions League titles and three La Liga crowns.

“Messi! When you have such good players, you become good yourself,” Guardiola said when asked what helped him win so many titles.

The post Guardiola says next coaching job will be with national team appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: 2027 Presidential Election: Allow Me Take Over Imo, Kwara, Wike Tells Tinubu
description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has appealed to President Bola Tinubu and the Director General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign council, Abdul’aziz Yari, to include Imo and Kwara as part of the states he is coordinating for the re-e
content:
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has appealed to President Bola Tinubu and the Director General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign council, Abdul’aziz Yari, to include Imo and Kwara as part of the states he is coordinating for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 elections.

Speaking during a town hall meeting with residents and members of the Rainbow Coalition in Gokana Local Government Area of Rivers State, Wike stated that he has tightened every loose end in Rivers and the FCT and would like to offer himself to head the campaigns in Kwara and Imo to ensure victory for President Tinubu in both states.

“You know I was given Rivers and FCT to coordinate, but frankly speaking, we are done with the two states, so there is no work to do again. As I am going now, I will plead with the DG and Mr President to add two more states for me to deliver,” the former Rivers State governor said.

“I hear from what I am told they are having problems in Imo. So I will like to go there and deliver Imo for Mr President.

Secondly, I hear there are some divisions in Kwara, so I will plead with the DG and Mr President to allow me to take over Imo and Kwara because I am done with Rivers and the FCT.”

“You know I was given Rivers and FCT to coordinate, but frankly speaking, we are done with the two states, so there is no work to do again. As I am going now, I will plead with the DG and Mr President to add two more states for me to deliver,” the former Rivers State governor said.

“I hear from what I am told they are having problems in Imo. So I will like to go there and deliver Imo for Mr President.

Secondly, I hear there are some divisions in Kwara, so I will plead with the DG and Mr President to allow me to take over Imo and Kwara because I am done with Rivers and the FCT.”

title: UK council approves 3am finish for Fury-Joshua fight
description:
Cardiff Council in Wales, United Kingdom has approved plans allowing the highly anticipated heavyweight boxing clash between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua to run into the early hours of the morning, with alcohol sales permitted until 3am.
The approval was granted by the council’s Licensing Sub Commi
content:
Cardiff Council in Wales, United Kingdom has approved plans allowing the highly anticipated heavyweight boxing clash between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua to run into the early hours of the morning, with alcohol sales permitted until 3am.

The approval was granted by the council’s Licensing Sub Committee ahead of the December 11 fight at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales.

As reported by the BBC, under the arrangement, hospitality boxes at the stadium will be allowed to serve alcohol until 3am, while the venue is expected to close at 3:30am to accommodate prime-time television coverage in the United States.

The fight’s ring walk is scheduled for 1am on December 12, with the opening bell expected at approximately 1:30am, according to stadium director Mark Williams.

Williams told councillors that the extended hours were necessary to accommodate the event’s schedule and confirmed that tickets were still available.

“We are expecting a capacity of 77,000, if everything sells,” he said.

To maintain security and public order, 130 police officers will be deployed, alongside twice the number of stewards normally provided for a regular sporting event.

Councillors were also informed that 450 of the 1,600 stewards would be assigned specifically to spectators seated on the stadium’s pitch area.

South Wales Police Chief Inspector Huw Thomas described the event as a major security operation, noting that the length of the programme meant officers were treating it as a “three-day event”.

Some residents had raised objections over concerns about noise, antisocial behaviour and public safety, although none attended the licensing meeting.

However, the council was assured that measures had been put in place to address the concerns, including additional early-morning train services and restrictions on external public address systems.

The meeting also heard that breathalysers would be used at stadium entrances for spectators who appeared intoxicated.

Chair of the Licensing Sub Committee, Grace Ferguson-Thorne, said the panel was reassured by the security and crowd-management arrangements, including the planned stewarding levels and closure of the stadium roof.

The approval marks another occasion when the Principality Stadium will host a major boxing event extending into the early hours.

In 2007, Joe Calzaghe’s victory over Mikkel Kessler began at approximately 2am to accommodate television audiences in the United States.

The 2018 heavyweight contest between Anthony Joshua and Joseph Parker also attracted more than 78,000 spectators, setting an attendance record for an event at the stadium.

The post UK council approves 3am finish for Fury-Joshua fight appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Most Nigerians support political violence when opponents are victims — Shehu Sani
description:
Former Kaduna Central Senator, Shehu Sani, has accused Nigerians of condoning political violence when it is directed at opponents, warning that the attitude is fuelling attacks on political supporters across the country.







Sani said many Nigerians encourage violence against people whose politic
content:
Former Kaduna Central Senator, Shehu Sani, has accused Nigerians of condoning political violence when it is directed at opponents, warning that the attitude is fuelling attacks on political supporters across the country.

Sani said many Nigerians encourage violence against people whose political choices or opinions differ from theirs, rather than condemn such acts irrespective of the victims’ affiliations.

He stated this on X on Wednesday following the campaign violence that reportedly left four persons dead in Delta State.

Condemning the killings, Sani said Nigerians were more likely to support or excuse political violence when those attacked belonged to opposing political camps.

“The political violence in Delta State has led to the death of four supporters of Senator Omo Agege of the NDC. A condemnable act. However, we are shying away from the truth that most Nigerians are fully in support of political violence as long as the victims are in the opposite camp,” he wrote.

He argued that people who support violence against political opponents often fail to recognise that such acts could eventually affect their own side.

“Most people encourage and support mob or thuggish acts against those they differ with in political choices or opinions. Those aiding and abetting political violence are feeding a Tiger with the thought that it will only consume their political adversaries,” Sani said.

The former senator also criticised the media’s handling of reports of political attacks, accusing some media organisations of using descriptions that downplay the severity of violence depending on the political affiliation of those involved.

He cited reports of attacks involving former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar in Kebbi and President Bola Tinubu in Abuja, saying some media outlets used different descriptions for incidents involving the two political figures.

“Some media Houses have even crafted a beautiful way of reporting political violence…POLITICAL THUGS attacked Atiku in Kebbi while ANGRY YOUTHS attacked Tinubu at Abuja Mosque,” he added.

Sani’s comments come amid growing concerns over political violence and intolerance ahead of the 2027 general elections, with incidents involving political supporters raising questions about the safety of campaign activities and the role of political parties in preventing attacks.

title: Tinubu breaks silence on 78 abducted Borno schoolchildren, promises rescue
description:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has assured families of 78 schoolchildren abducted in Borno State that the Federal Government will work to secure their release, breaking his public silence on the incidents during a visit to Maiduguri on Wednesday.
Tinubu gave the assurance while addressing supporters at
content:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has assured families of 78 schoolchildren abducted in Borno State that the Federal Government will work to secure their release, breaking his public silence on the incidents during a visit to Maiduguri on Wednesday.

Tinubu gave the assurance while addressing supporters at the Elkanemi Sports Centre, where he officially flagged off the North-East zonal rally of the All Progressives Congress (APC).

The President pledged to deploy the efforts of the military and intelligence agencies towards rescuing the children, while commending security personnel involved in operations against insurgents and other armed groups.

“With our armed forces and intelligence, we will rescue them, we will rescue them, Inshallah,” he told the crowd.

He also praised military personnel operating under difficult conditions, particularly in Borno State, for risking their lives to restore peace.

“We give respect to the men and women of the armed forces who are in the bush, in the sun and in the rain, who put their lives on the line for us and for Borno. Particularly, for Maiduguri to have peace. We will achieve that peace,” Tinubu said.

The President further urged terrorists to abandon violence and surrender, insisting that they still had an opportunity to lay down their arms.

The 78 children were reportedly abducted in two separate incidents in Borno State. According to reports, 42 were seized in Mussa on May 15, 2026, while another 36 were taken from Lassa on June 29, 2026. Some of the victims are reportedly toddlers below the age of two.

The Mussa abduction occurred on the same day that 44 pupils and teachers were reportedly kidnapped from a school in Oriire Local Government Area of Oyo State.

The Oyo victims were subsequently rescued on July 10, 2026, following a security operation, after spending 56 days in captivity.

However, the families of the abducted Borno children have continued to express frustration over the lack of information about their whereabouts and the progress of efforts to secure their release.

Some parents recently accused the Federal and Borno State governments of failing to provide adequate updates on the rescue operation, saying the prolonged uncertainty had taken a heavy emotional toll on their families.

One of the parents, Josephine Yohanna, whose three-year-old child was reportedly abducted in Mussa, described the suffering endured by families since the incident.

“For the past months, the pain of living without our child was acute. Some of us have fallen sick; we cannot eat or sleep,” she said.

Yohanna added that government officials had urged them to remain patient but questioned how long they would have to wait without receiving updates.

She said the families were prepared to make sacrifices to have their children returned home before Christmas.

Another parent, Sale Buba, lamented what he described as the silence of both the state and Federal Governments, claiming that families had not seen visible efforts by security agencies to rescue the children.

He appealed to the abductors to identify themselves and communicate their demands, saying the parents were exhausted by the uncertainty.

“We are tired of the suspense, tell us the reason for abducting the toddlers and present your demands,” he said.

A third parent, Mista Ali, expressed concern that the abductors might still be operating around the Sambisa Forest or Mandara Mountains.

He alleged that residents had yet to notice significant improvements in security or the deployment of a special rescue team in their area.

Ali said the prolonged absence of the children had left parents, particularly mothers, distressed and struggling with sleepless nights.

While acknowledging the government’s efforts, he appealed to security agencies to intensify operations and bring the children home safely.

Tinubu’s latest assurance has renewed hopes among the affected families, who are waiting for concrete action to secure the release of their children.

The post Tinubu breaks silence on 78 abducted Borno schoolchildren, promises rescue appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: 10 phones with the fastest charging speeds in 2026
description:
