From 120W ultra-fast charging systems to more moderate fast-charging options, several smartphones



now offer feat
content:
By Aniobi Angel

Smartphone manufacturers are continuously improving charging technology, introducing devices that can recharge their batteries in significantly less time.

From 120W ultra-fast charging systems to more moderate fast-charging options, several smartphones

now offer features designed to reduce the time users spend connected to power outlets.

In 2026, brands such as Xiaomi, Huawei, OnePlus, ASUS, Motorola, Samsung, Google and Apple continue to compete in the development of faster and more efficient charging technology.

Here are 10 smartphones with impressive charging capabilities.

  1. Xiaomi Redmi Note 14 Pro+ 5G – 120W

The Xiaomi Redmi Note 14 Pro+ 5G leads the list with its 120W HyperCharge technology.

The smartphone features a 5,110mAh battery and supports ultra-fast wired charging, allowing users to recharge their devices in approximately 20–30 minutes under suitable conditions.

  1. Xiaomi 11T Pro 5G – 120W

Another Xiaomi device making the list is the Xiaomi 11T Pro 5G, which features 120W Xiaomi HyperCharge technology.

Its 5,000mAh battery is designed to support rapid charging, with the manufacturer claiming that the device can reach a full charge in approximately 17 minutes under controlled conditions.

  1. OnePlus 15 – 100W

The OnePlus 15 features 100W fast-charging technology in markets where the higher-wattage version is available.

Its charging system is designed to provide quick battery replenishment, making it suitable for users who depend heavily on their smartphones throughout the day.

  1. Huawei Pura 80 Ultra – 100W

Huawei’s Pura 80 Ultra offers 100W wired SuperCharge technology and up to 80W wireless charging.

The device combines its fast-charging capabilities with a large battery, providing users with both wired and wireless charging options.

  1. OnePlus 11 5G Dual SIM – 100W

The OnePlus 11 5G supports 100W SUPERVOOC charging in compatible markets.

It features a 5,000mAh battery and is designed to recharge quickly, with OnePlus advertising a full charge in approximately 25 minutes under suitable conditions.

  1. ASUS ROG Phone 5s 5G Dual SIM – 65W

The ASUS ROG Phone 5s is equipped with 65W HyperCharge technology.

Designed primarily for mobile gaming, the smartphone combines its high-performance hardware with a 6,000mAh battery and fast-charging support.

  1. Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra – 45W

Samsung’s Galaxy S25 Ultra supports 45W wired fast charging.

The device features a 5,000mAh battery and can reach approximately 65 per cent charge in 30 minutes when used with a compatible 45W adapter.

  1. Motorola Razr 50 Ultra 5G – 45W

The Motorola Razr 50 Ultra 5G supports 45W TurboPower wired charging.

The foldable smartphone combines its distinctive design with a fast-charging system and wireless charging support, offering users additional convenience when powering their devices.

  1. Google Pixel 9 Pro XL – Up to 37W

Google’s Pixel 9 Pro XL supports fast wired charging using a compatible 45W USB-C charger.

The device can reach approximately 70 per cent battery capacity in 30 minutes under suitable conditions. It also supports wireless charging.

  1. Huawei P30 Pro Dual SIM – 40W

The Huawei P30 Pro Dual SIM completes the list with its 40W Huawei SuperCharge technology.

Despite being an older flagship smartphone, it remains notable for its charging capabilities. Its 4,200mAh battery supports fast charging, allowing users to replenish battery power more quickly than with standard charging technology.

title: Eight senatorial candidates withdraw, declare support for Yari in Zamfara
description:
Eight senatorial candidates from different political parties contesting the Zamfara West Senatorial District seat have withdrawn from the race and declared support for the incumbent senator, Abdulaziz Yari of the All Progressives Congress (APC), ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The candidates an
content:
Eight senatorial candidates from different political parties contesting the Zamfara West Senatorial District seat have withdrawn from the race and declared support for the incumbent senator, Abdulaziz Yari of the All Progressives Congress (APC), ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The candidates announced their decision during a visit to Yari’s constituency office in Talata Mafara, Zamfara State.

The development was disclosed in a statement issued on Wednesday in Gusau by the Coordinator of Yari’s Constituency Office, Sha’ayau’u Sarkinfawa.

The candidates include Sani Abdullahi of the Action Peoples Party (APP), Ibrahim Anka of the National Democratic Party (NDP), Sanusi Mohammed of the Young Progressive Party (YPP) and Yahaya Aliyu of the Labour Party (LP).

Others are Abdulmalik Adamu of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Murtala Abubakar of the Accord Party (AP), Anas Usman of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) and Aishat S-Pawa of the Action Democratic Party (ADP).

Speaking on behalf of the group, Abdullahi said their decision was taken in the interest of the people of Zamfara West.

He added that they had also pledged to support Yari, President Bola Tinubu and other APC candidates in the forthcoming 2027 general elections.

Abdullahi described Yari’s appointment as Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council as a significant honour, which he said deserved the backing of patriotic citizens of Zamfara State, regardless of their political affiliations.

“We will support to ensure the victory of Sen. Yari and the APC in the forthcoming general elections,” he said.

Responding through Sarkinfawa, Yari commended the candidates for their decision and assured them that they would not regret supporting him.

He said their move demonstrated their commitment to the interests of Zamfara West and pledged to involve them in the APC senatorial campaign committees and other activities of the district campaign office.

Yari also assured the candidates that they would receive equal consideration and recognition alongside existing APC members.

description:
By Ugochukwu Alaribe, Umuahia



Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Benjamin Kalu, has said that President Bola Tinubu has fulfilled the promise made to the Igbo after the civil war in 1970.



He noted that at the end of the civil war, the federal government had announced the poli
content:
By Ugochukwu Alaribe, Umuahia

Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Benjamin Kalu, has said that President Bola Tinubu has fulfilled the promise made to the Igbo after the civil war in 1970.

He noted that at the end of the civil war, the federal government had announced the policy of Reconciliation, Reconstruction and Rehabilitation to rebuild Igbo land, alleging that successive administrations failed to implement the policy.

The Deputy Speaker stated that Tinubu is the only president that has made meaningful efforts in implementing the policy by establishing the South East Development Commission (SEDC) and putting up infrastructural projects and political appointments across the South East zone.

Kalu, who stated this in Umuahia during the donation of 25 vehicles to the Abia State chapter of the Door to Door mobilisation by High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, urged the Igbo to re-elect the president to finish his job in the next four years.

“For over 50 years, nobody was able to fulfil the promise made to the Igbo after the civil war. Gone are the days of promise. Today, President Bola Tinubu has fulfilled the promise he has given the South East Development Commission (SEDC). He has also given the SEDC the permission to open what is known as the South East Investment Company. And he has funded the company with billions of Naira.

“Today, the company has started the project of piping gas across the Southeast. The companies in Lagos and Kano will start coming to build in the Southeast. This is the president that Tompolo wants us to support.

“Across the South East, more roads are springing up because our son is the Minister of Works, Engr Dave Umahi. I can’t remember the last time an Igbo man was the Minister of Works. Umahi has been making us proud. The President also appointed Ojukwu as the Minister of Foreign Affairs and another Igbo as the Chief of Naval Staff. The Minister of State for Finance is also an Igbo.

“The President has also invested money in securing our lives and properties. The Ministry of Defence budget has increased; employment in the military and police is increasing. The president has also supported state police. Salaries are not being owed because Tinubu removed the fuel subsidy and released more money for the sub-nations.

He urged the Igbo to reject anyone who is campaigning for the South East zone to serve for only a four-year term, stressing that when the time comes, the zone would take eight years, as others have done.

“Reject them when they come to you that they have signed an agreement for the Igbo to serve for only four years. The Igbo will not wait after 60 years to receive power for only four years. We didn’t wait for 60 years for the Igbo to take only half the bread. Other zones have done right years; when the time comes, the Igbo will take eight years, not four years.”

title: Tinubu celebrates Atiku at 80, says their shared democratic values remain important
description:
President Bola Tinubu has congratulated former Vice President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, on his 80th birthday, describing his contributions to Nigeria’s political and economic development as noteworthy.
Tinubu conveyed the message in a statement iss
content:
President Bola Tinubu has congratulated former Vice President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, on his 80th birthday, describing his contributions to Nigeria’s political and economic development as noteworthy.

Tinubu conveyed the message in a statement issued by the State House on Wednesday, November 25, 2026.

The President acknowledged his longstanding political relationship with Atiku, recalling that he supported the former Vice President’s 2007 presidential ambition under the defunct Action Congress platform.

According to Tinubu, his support for Atiku at the time was driven by his belief that democracy thrives when political actors are free to participate, present alternative ideas and contribute to discussions on leadership and governance.

He said his political philosophy had consistently emphasised the need to strengthen democratic institutions, respect opposing views and promote political competition in the interest of Nigerians.

Tinubu also reiterated his position that politics should be conducted without bitterness, with room for reconciliation after disagreements among political opponents.

The President noted that despite their different political affiliations and occasional disagreements, their shared commitment to Nigeria’s unity, democratic stability and the rule of law remained important.

He also acknowledged Atiku’s contributions to education, entrepreneurship and the private sector, particularly his investments in business development and job creation.

Tinubu specifically highlighted the establishment of the American University of Nigeria in Yola, Adamawa State, saying the institution had expanded access to higher education and contributed to human capital development.

While acknowledging that he and Atiku now belong to different political camps and hold contrasting positions on national issues, Tinubu said their common interest in Nigeria’s progress should remain paramount.

He wished the former Vice President good health, renewed strength and more years of service to the country and humanity as he marked his 80th birthday.

“Happy 80th birthday, Your Excellency,” the President stated.

title: Middle Belt Forum condemns renewed killings, abductions

…Urges governments to rescue abductees, protect communities and prosecute perpetrators



By Henry Umoru



ABUJA — The Middle Belt Forum (MBF) has condemned renewed attacks, killings, abductions and destruction of property in parts of Plateau, Niger, Benue, Kaduna and Borno states, calling on the F
content:
…Urges governments to rescue abductees, protect communities and prosecute perpetrators

By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The Middle Belt Forum (MBF) has condemned renewed attacks, killings, abductions and destruction of property in parts of Plateau, Niger, Benue, Kaduna and Borno states, calling on the Federal Government and security agencies to intensify efforts to protect vulnerable communities.

The forum also expressed concern over the prolonged captivity of schoolchildren abducted from Mussa and Lassa communities in Askira-Uba Local Government Area of Borno State, demanding their immediate rescue.

In a statement issued on Wednesday and signed by its National Spokesman, Luka Binniyat, the MBF said the children, abducted in May and June respectively, had remained with their captors for months.

It urged the Federal Government and security agencies to make their rescue an overriding national priority.

The forum expressed particular concern over reported attacks and destruction in Bong community, Doemak District of Qua’an Pan Local Government Area of Plateau State, as well as killings and abductions in Luman Ba’are community, Shagunu Ward, and Wawa community in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State.

It also condemned reported deadly attacks and reprisals in parts of Niger State, warning against collective punishment and retaliatory violence.

The statement read, “We condemn the killing of innocent people, regardless of their ethnic or religious identities, and caution against collective punishment and retaliatory violence.”

The forum said the incidents reflected a wider pattern of insecurity across the Middle Belt, noting that communities in Riyom, Barkin Ladi, Mangu and other parts of Plateau State had continued to experience attacks and loss of lives.

It added that communities in Logo, Ukum and other local government areas of Benue State had also suffered deadly attacks, displacement and destruction of livelihoods.

On Southern Kaduna, the MBF recalled the April attacks on Ariko community in Kachia Local Government Area, which reportedly resulted in killings and mass abductions.

It also cited subsequent attacks on Awon community and the November 4 attack on Akwando, both in Kachia LGA, where two people were reportedly killed and several others abducted.

The forum described the continued captivity of residents and reports of deaths among some abductees as unacceptable.

It further urged settlers and residents in Middle Belt communities to respect the cultures, traditions, values and established authorities of their host communities.

The MBF cautioned against the use of violence to intimidate host communities, displace residents or seize ancestral lands.

However, it also warned host communities and individuals against taking the law into their own hands, stressing that grievances or disagreements could not justify mob action, revenge killings or destruction of property.

“Anyone who breaks the law must be reported to the appropriate authorities and made to face justice,” the statement added.

The forum called on governments and security agencies to act swiftly, protect all communities, rescue people held in captivity and ensure that perpetrators of violence were brought to justice without discrimination.

“The Middle Belt must be a home where everyone lives in peace, respects one another and obeys the law,” it said.

The post Middle Belt Forum condemns renewed killings, abductions appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Reps seek funding for abandoned Ondo projects in 2027 budget
description:
TThe House of Representatives has called on the Federal Government to make adequate budgetary provisions in the 2027 Appropriation Bill for the completion of abandoned and uncompleted projects in Ilaje/Ese-Odo Federal Constituency of Ondo State.
The House also urged the Federal Government to dispatc
content:
TThe House of Representatives has called on the Federal Government to make adequate budgetary provisions in the 2027 Appropriation Bill for the completion of abandoned and uncompleted projects in Ilaje/Ese-Odo Federal Constituency of Ondo State.

The House also urged the Federal Government to dispatch a fact-finding delegation to Aiyetoro community to assess the extent of sea incursion threatening the coastal settlement and audit projects allegedly abandoned across the constituency.

The resolutions followed the unanimous adoption of a motion of urgent public importance moved at plenary on Wednesday by the member representing Ilaje/Ese-Odo Federal Constituency, Mr Donald Ojogo.

Moving the motion, Ojogo said the constituency remained the only oil-producing federal constituency in the South-West, contributing more than 60,000 barrels of crude oil daily to the nation’s production output.

He, however, lamented that despite its contribution to the national economy, the area had continued to suffer neglect, with several critical infrastructure projects either abandoned after commencement or left without adequate funding.

Among the affected projects, he listed the Aiyetoro shoreline protection project, Agadagba Obon/Arogbo bridge, Kiribo/Igbekebo bridge and Ukparama regional water project.

The lawmaker warned that the continued neglect of the projects had generated growing discontent among residents, particularly youths, with concerns that the situation could degenerate into protests and a possible disruption of oil production in the area.

He said the growing agitation over the plight of the communities required urgent intervention and assurances from the Federal Government to prevent a breakdown of law and order.

“The House notes with concern that the growing youthful elite convergence and conversation over and around the plight of the people of Ilaje/Ese-Odo has assumed a dimension that calls for immediate Federal Government assurances and action. The planned threat of shutdown of oil production in the area over the plight of the people, especially as it relates to Aiyetoro should be particularly disturbing,” he said.

Ojogo’s motion also drew attention to the environmental challenges confronting Aiyetoro, a coastal community in the Ilaje area that has faced persistent sea incursion and shoreline erosion, threatening homes, livelihoods and other critical infrastructure.

The community’s vulnerability to coastal erosion has remained a longstanding concern, with residents repeatedly calling for effective shoreline protection measures to prevent further destruction and displacement.

Following the adoption of the motion, the House urged the federal government to send “a fact-finding delegation to Aiyetoro community to confirm the extent of the tamable but overlooked sea incursion that has ravaged the oil-rich areas of Ilaje and as well take an audit of the highlighted abandoned projects.”

The lawmakers also urged the House Committee on Appropriation to ensure that adequate funds were provided in the 2027 budget for the completion of the identified projects and other interventions capable of improving the living conditions of residents.

By Egufe Yafugborhi



WARRI — The Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), Alfred Diete-Spiff Airport, Osubi, Delta State, has conducted its first simulated aircraft crash rescue exercise in about 20 years to assess its em
content:
…Drill identifies emergency response gaps, need for modern equipment

By Egufe Yafugborhi

WARRI — The Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), Alfred Diete-Spiff Airport, Osubi, Delta State, has conducted its first simulated aircraft crash rescue exercise in about 20 years to assess its emergency response capabilities and identify areas requiring improvement.

The exercise, conducted at about 1:30pm on the airport’s airside, simulated an aircraft crash involving passengers who sustained varying degrees of injuries.

Several emergency response agencies participated in the drill, including the Nigerian Navy Hospital and Air Station Fire Service, Nigeria Police Force, Delta State Fire Service, Nigerian Red Cross Society, Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB), Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Delta Procare Hospital, Nigerian Ports Authority Health Service and Renaissance Africa Energy Fire Service.

Speaking after the exercise, the Airport Manager, Winston Egwuatu, expressed satisfaction with the outcome, saying identified operational gaps would be addressed to strengthen the airport’s emergency response capacity.

He explained that the exercise was designed to test the preparedness of personnel, availability of equipment and effectiveness of established emergency procedures.

“No simulation exercise is perfect. It was actually meant to test the preparedness of both the officers who are going to be deployed, the materials and also the procedures.

“The purpose of this is to identify the gaps and close them, so that when it is deployed, we will deploy better,” he said.

Egwuatu, who spoke alongside departmental heads, said observers from the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) identified areas requiring improvement, particularly personnel training and retraining.

He noted that the airport had recorded operational improvements since its transition from an airstrip but stressed the need for additional operational vehicles and modern firefighting equipment.

“Within resources available to the management of the airport, we have done very well. This airport used to be an airstrip. Now it’s operating as an airport. That means there have been some level of upgrade.

“However, there is need for improvement in regards to operational vehicles and state-of-the-art fire tankers to meet the time that we find ourselves now,” he said.

The airport manager disclosed that observations from the exercise would be compiled into a comprehensive report to guide corrective measures and requests requiring intervention from higher authorities.

He also emphasised the importance of effective collaboration among emergency response agencies, noting that prompt intervention could determine survival during an aircraft accident.

“It is in the interest of everybody to deploy, all of us who have the wherewithal to not just respond, but respond timely. Because that timely response is critical. It can save the life of someone,” Egwuatu said.

He commended the participating organisations and other stakeholders for their cooperation, adding that FAAN planned to produce a video documentary of the exercise for educational purposes and to promote improved emergency preparedness.

Earlier, NCAA observers, Maureen Amewhule and Engr. Okrinade Ahmed, commended the airport management for organising the simulation, praising the alertness, professionalism and coordination demonstrated by personnel during the exercise.

They, however, called for more training, particularly for medical personnel, improved inter-agency collaboration and regular engagements among stakeholders.

The exercise, which is a regulatory requirement of the NCAA, was conducted without disrupting normal airport operations.

title: VIDEO: NDC alleges attack on supporters during Obi’s Edo visit
description:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress has alleged that suspected political thugs attacked its members and supporters in Benin City, Edo State, on Wednesday, leaving several people injured ahead of the arrival of its presidential candidate, Peter Obi.
The party made the allegation in a statement issued on
content:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress has alleged that suspected political thugs attacked its members and supporters in Benin City, Edo State, on Wednesday, leaving several people injured ahead of the arrival of its presidential candidate, Peter Obi.

The party made the allegation in a statement issued on Wednesday by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, saying the attack occurred along Airport Road as Obi arrived in the state for a town hall meeting and campaign activities.

The NDC alleged that the attackers opened fire, damaged campaign vehicles and buses, and injured several supporters.

The statement read, “As our presidential candidate, His Excellency Peter Obi, arrived in the state for a town hall meeting and campaign activities, suspected political thugs reportedly attacked NDC members and supporters along Airport Road.

“Reports indicate that the assailants opened fire, damaged campaign vehicles and buses, and left several people injured. Videos circulating online show the aftermath of this brazen assault.”

The party condemned the incident, describing it as a “vicious and unprovoked attack” on its members.

“This latest incident follows a disturbing pattern of violence, intimidation, and attacks against NDC members, candidates, and structures across Edo State and other parts of the country,” the statement said.

It added, “Politics is not war. No Nigerian should be attacked, shot at, or terrorised simply for supporting a political party or exercising their democratic rights.”

The statement was accompanied by viral videos showing the aftermath of the alleged attack.

The first video shows the scene on a busy roadside in daylight.

Campaign vehicles bearing NDC branding and images of Peter Obi were dented, and doors were removed.

Campaign posters and flyers lie scattered on the ground and pavement, some near what appear to be bloodstains close to one of the vehicles.

The second video shows multiple injured people lying on tables or stretchers, many with extensive blood covering their lower bodies, legs, and feet.

Some limbs appear heavily bandaged or severely wounded.

Medical staff in gloves and protective clothing attend to the victims amid significant amounts of blood on the tables, floor, and bodies.

NDC called on the Edo State Police Command, the Inspector-General of Police and other security agencies to secure the area, protect its supporters and candidates, and investigate the incident.

It also urged the authorities to identify, arrest and prosecute those responsible, including their alleged sponsors, regardless of political affiliation.

The NDC further called for guarantees of safety for political actors to enable campaigns and other lawful political activities to take place without fear of violence.

“The NDC remains committed to peaceful, issue-based politics. We will not be intimidated or driven out of any part of Nigeria. Our supporters are law-abiding citizens, and their safety is non-negotiable,” the statement added.

The party also urged Nigerians, civil society organisations, the media and the international community to take note of what it described as escalating political violence and hold the authorities accountable for protecting citizens’ rights to political participation.

The incident came a day after the NDC raised concerns over the withdrawal of approval for a venue it had booked for Obi’s town hall meeting in Benin City.

The party had alleged that the management of the event centre withdrew its approval after receiving payment.

However, the management denied political interference, saying the disagreement arose from a booking error after the party requested a change of date.

The latest incident also comes days after an attack on an NDC campaign gathering in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, where six people were killed, according to the police.

Delta campaign attack: Police confirm six dead, several injured

The Delta State Police Command has invited former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege and other political actors for questioning as investigations continue.

The post VIDEO: NDC alleges attack on supporters during Obi’s Edo visit appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NDLEA Dismantles Industrial-Scale Meth Lab In Enugu, Arrests Suspected Drug Baron, Five Mexicans
description: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said it has dismantled another industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratory in Enugu State.It also said that it arrested a 63-year-old drug baron it identified as one “Chuks Enoch Ezeike, popularly known as ‘Over Size’,” and fiv
content:
The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said it has dismantled another industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratory in Enugu State.

It also said that it arrested a 63-year-old drug baron it identified as one “Chuks Enoch Ezeike, popularly known as ‘Over Size’,” and five Mexican meth specialists whom he allegedly smuggled into the country with forged passports to produce the Class A drug on Nigerian soil.

The NDLEA disclosed that a total of 1,512 kilograms of methamphetamine, finished and in production, with an estimated value of US$226.8 million, equivalent to ₦303,913,000,000.00, was recovered from the clandestine factory, alongside 6.68 tons of 20 different types of precursor and essential chemicals and an array of industrial equipment for making the illicit substance.

“Ezeike, a businessman who holds the traditional title of Ebekuo Dike na Nanka in his community in Anambra State, had built the industrial complex behind San Savanna Oil Company Limited, at Kilometre 1/2 Abakaliki Expressway, Emene, Enugu, complete with living quarters for the Mexicans so they could live and produce in the same place without being seen in town,” Chairman/Chief Executive Officer of the agency, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Marwa (retd.) said at a press conference in Abuja on Wednesday.

Marwa described it as one of the most carefully planned, intelligence-led operations ever conducted by the agency, adding that the operation “began in faraway Mexico, ran through Colombia, France and the Republic of Benin, crossed into Lagos, and ended in an industrial complex in Enugu.”

He explained that the agency’s Special Operations Unit (SOU) began working on critical intelligence in April 2026, which identified Ezeike as a specialist in setting up clandestine methamphetamine laboratories with links to one Oscar Ramos-Cardenas, alleged to be a Mexican known for large-scale, industrial-grade methamphetamine production.

“From that moment, Ezeike was a marked man. Our officers opened a file on him, and we watched and waited,” the NDLEA chief was quoted as saying in a statement by the agency’s Director, Media and Advocacy, Femi Babafemi.

“On 25th August 2026, we received intelligence on the flight itineraries of five Mexican nationals, all identified as methamphetamine experts who were travelling from Mexico to Nigeria. Our analysis left no room for doubt: they were coming to set up an industrial-scale meth laboratory on Nigerian soil.

“Working closely with the Nigeria Immigration Service, we ensured that when they landed here in Abuja on 28th August 2026, they were denied entry. They were put on the next available flight back to Mexico.

“On that same day, our officers found out that Ezeike had travelled from Enugu to Abuja to receive the visiting Mexicans. His own bank records later confirmed the hotel payment in Abuja that day. The visitors he came to receive were the very men we had just sent back”, Marwa stated.

He further said that the suspect and his foreign collaborators worked out a new route.

The NDLEA chairman stated that the meth “experts” were flown from Bogotá, Colombia, through Paris, France, to the Republic of Benin, while Ezeike procured forged Argentine, Colombian and Chilean passports and sent them through a driver to Cotonou, where the Mexicans handed over their genuine passports and took on new identities.

“On 19th September 2026, the agency was alerted that five Mexicans had arrived in Cotonou, intending to slip into Nigeria through the land border. They are Gonzalez Numez Lucas (name on forged passport), Oscar Ramos-Cardenas (real name and leader/chief specialist), Lopez Salvador Vasquez Esperanza (name on forged passport), Juan Antonio Sarabia-Cabrera (real name), Hernandez Cortes Carlos Fuentes (Name on forged passport), Luis Enrique Garcia-Amador (real name), Fernandez Rio Mateo Jimenez (name on forged passport), Jose Alejandro Renteria-Reyes (Real name), Rodriguez Araya Andres Perez (name on forged passport), and Salomon Cabanillas-Torres (real name),” Marwa said.

He further said that, this time, Marwa said, the agency took a deliberate decision to let them in.

“We wanted the whole network: the meth specialist, the financier, the factory and the product. Sending them home a second time would only have postponed the problem,” he stated.

The chairman noted that three of the Mexicans crossed into Nigeria through the Seme Border Post on September 20, while the remaining two followed on September 21, on a road trip arranged by Ezeike.

“With NDLEA special operatives embedded in their every move, Ezeike received them in Lagos and lodged them in a hotel, where he was observed having breakfast with them on 22nd September, before moving them to Enugu.

“While the Mexicans lived and worked in the San Savanna complex, Ezeike stayed at Adig Suites, 2 Nwafor Orizu Street, Enugu, moving about in three vehicles: a blue Toyota Corolla, a red Toyota RAV4 and a Lexus RX 350. Providing further details,” Marwa said.

“Throughout September and October, our officers kept watch on both locations. In the course of surveillance, we watched the regular movement of Ezeike’s blue Corolla drive into San Savanna, stay a few minutes, and return to Adig Suites.

“Assisted by appropriate tools such as the deployment of a drone and other intelligence deductions, we were able to put all pieces together by 7th November 2026.

“Having got all this down, it was now time to strike. On 9th November, 2026, we assembled over 200 personnel of our Strike Force and Enugu State Command into a staging area. On 10th November, 2026, I gave the order to take down the lab. At about 5 a.m. on Wednesday, 11th November 2026, operatives of our Special Operations Unit, the Strike Force, the Forensic Directorate and the Enugu State Command carried out simultaneous raids on both locations. All personnel were appropriately deployed with clear tasks – those for outer cordon, inner cordon, search and arrest.”

Speaking further, he said, “At the San Savanna complex, our men stormed the laboratory and the adjoining guest house, which also served as a stash house. All five Mexicans were arrested at the scene, in the middle of production. At the same time, at Adig Suites, our operatives arrested Ezeike in Room 106. He was then taken to San Savanna to witness the search.

“There, in the presence of our officers, Ezeike admitted that he owns the laboratory and that he brought the Mexicans into Nigeria to manufacture methamphetamine. He told us that they had produced only a small batch so far. He also told us the Mexicans were due to leave Nigeria two days later, on Friday, 13th November 2026. In other words, we caught them with two days to spare.”

The NDLEA chairman disclosed that the 6.68 tons of precursor and essential chemicals recovered included 2,835kg of lead acetate, 1,050kg of tartaric acid, 450kg of mandelic acid, 160kg of P2P and 70kg of methylamine.

He said that the equipment seized included four industrial burners, two industrial distillation units, two boilers, two hydraulic presses, eleven gas cylinders, two freezers, two digital scales and four washing/drying machines, all of which forensic experts have confirmed are consistent with industrial methamphetamine manufacture.

“They were producing methamphetamine not by the kilogram, but by the ton. Had they succeeded, that poison would have flooded our streets, our schools and our communities, and exported to destroy lives abroad, with Nigeria’s name stamped on it,” the NDLEA boss declared.

According to Marwa, statements by the suspects since their arrest confirm that it was no first-time venture but an organised, recurring transnational operation with three layers: a cartel command in Mexico that recruits, deploys and pays the specialists.

He noted that Ezeike, as the local coordinator who built the laboratory, procured the chemicals and arranged travel, transport and false documents; and the Mexican production crew led by Ramos-Cardenas, whose supporting members change with each deployment.

He also said the cartel deliberately kept Nigerians out of the laboratory to reduce the risk of exposure, which was why the Mexicans lived where they worked and hid behind a company signboard.

According to him, the cooks were paid according to their production output.

Marwa noted that in the last four months alone, NDLEA has dismantled four industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratories in Enugu, the Ogun forest, the Oyo forest and the Ebonyi forest, with five Mexican nationals arrested in the earlier operations already in prison custody facing trial.

He also said that with the latest five, the number of Mexican meth specialists arrested in Nigeria in four months stands at 10.

Sending a strong message to foreign cartels, the NDLEA boss said, “Nigeria is not your laboratory. It is not your warehouse, and it is not your transit route. You may change your passports, your names, your flight routes and your entry points, but you cannot change the fact that we are watching.

“The next person you send will meet the same fate. Every one of your cooks who comes to Nigeria will leave in handcuffs, or not leave at all, except to serve his sentence.”

Describing Nigerian collaborators as “the greater traitors,” Marwa said, “You sell out your own country and your own people for profit. There is no hiding place for you. Not in a hotel suite, not behind a company signboard, and not in the deepest forest. We will find you, we will arrest you, we will prosecute you, and we will go after every naira, every property and every asset you gained from this trade.”

He urged landlords, property owners, and communities to know who lives in their property and what they do there, and to report anything suspicious to the nearest NDLEA office, assuring them that their identities would be protected.

The post NDLEA Dismantles Industrial-Scale Meth Lab In Enugu, Arrests Suspected Drug Baron, Five Mexicans appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Meet two Nigerian designers behind Cardi B’s Billboard cover outfits
description:
Two Nigerian fashion designers, Abelia Franklyn and Segun Aladejana, have gained international attention after American rapper Cardi B wore their creations for her Billboard Canada cover editorial.
The designers, whose labels are Weizdhurm Franklyn and Sevon Dejana, featured in the rapper’s fashion
content:
Two Nigerian fashion designers, Abelia Franklyn and Segun Aladejana, have gained international attention after American rapper Cardi B wore their creations for her Billboard Canada cover editorial.

The designers, whose labels are Weizdhurm Franklyn and Sevon Dejana, featured in the rapper’s fashion looks following her recognition as the inaugural Global Woman of the Year at the 2026 Billboard Canada Women in Music ceremony in Toronto on Tuesday.

Cardi B shared photographs of the outfits on her Instagram page on Tuesday, with the caption, “Global Woman of the Year 2026. Thank you so much @billboardca.”

One of the outfits was a sculptural blue mermaid gown designed by Franklyn and features exaggerated feather-like detailing at the neck and hem.

The piece is from the brand’s Spring/Summer collection “The Remembering (Ncheta),” inspired by Igbo-Ukwu bronze art.

Franklyn has built the label around sharp tailoring, clean construction and effortless sophistication.

While the brand is known for contemporary menswear that balances classic elegance with modern refinement, this high-profile womenswear moment underscores its growing reach.

Sharing the photographs on the brand’s Instagram page on Wednesday, the designer wrote, “Cardi B @iamcardib stuns in Weiz Dhurm Franklyn for Canada Billboard Women of the Year wearing a sculptural blue mermaid gown featuring an exaggerated feather-like detail on neck and hem from our Spring Summer 2027 Ready to Wear; The Remembering (Ncheta) – A collection inspired by Igbo-Ukwu Bronze Art.”

The second outfit was created by Aladejana’s Sevon Dejana.

Cardi B wore a structured jacket and matching skirt from the label’s Out of Body Haute Couture Spring/Summer 2027 collection.

The outfit featured gold, red and wine-coloured crystal embroidery.

Announcing the look on Instagram on Tuesday, the designer wrote, “CARDI B, Discover Global Superstar @iamcardib in our OUT OF BODY Haute Couture SS27 gold, red and wine crystal embroidered structured jacket and skirt for @billboardca @billboard cover.

“Styled by the amazing @kollincarter thank you so much.”

Aladejana’s interest in fashion is rooted in his family background.

His maternal grandparents ran a tailoring shop in Obalende, Lagos, where he was exposed to the craft.

He has developed a reputation for refined occasion wear that blends impeccable tailoring with modern femininity

The designer has since dressed several celebrities, including Nollywood actress Ini Edo and model Olandria.

The two designers’ appearance in Cardi B’s Billboard Canada editorial highlights the growing international visibility of Nigerian fashion designers and their work.

Meanwhile, Cardi B became Billboard Canada Women in Music’s first-ever Global Woman of the Year.

The post Meet two Nigerian designers behind Cardi B’s Billboard cover outfits appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: ‘Incoming President’, Titi celebrates Atiku, says ex-VP not tired at 80
description:
By Omeiza Ajayi



ABUJA: Wife of the former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar, has described her husband as the “incoming President of Nigeria” as he turned 80 on Wednesday, saying he is “not tired” and that his vision for the country is “even clearer.”







In a birthday tribute titled “Daddy at 80
content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: Wife of the former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar, has described her husband as the “incoming President of Nigeria” as he turned 80 on Wednesday, saying he is “not tired” and that his vision for the country is “even clearer.”

In a birthday tribute titled “Daddy at 80”, Chief Amina Titi Atiku Abubakar, the former Second Lady of Nigeria, said she was celebrating “the Incoming President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria come May 29th, 2027 by the Special Grace of God.”

“At 80, you are not tired. At 80, your vision for Nigeria is even clearer. I have walked with you through valleys and mountains, and I know what God has placed in you for Nigeria,” she wrote.

She said Nigeria needed his “experience,” his “capacity, and your compassionate heart now more than ever.” According to her, this is “reflecting in the enthusiastic and passionate ways Nigerians turned out to cheer you to victory as you articulate your policies and canvass support for your presidential aspiration come January 16, 2027.”

Titi said the milestone coincided with 57 years of marriage. “Eighty years of a life well-lived and Fifty-seven years of a love that has stood the test of time. When I first met you as a young lady, I saw a cute, handsome, principled, brilliant, focused Customs officer with big dreams. I did not know I was meeting a destiny.”

She credited her husband with the support that led her into the campaign against human trafficking. “Many men would have stopped their wife from confronting human trafficking. You did not. You not only gave me the wings to fly, but the inspiration, the courage, the confidence and the wherewithal to fight for humanity and the vulnerables. You told me, ‘Titi, go and save those girls.'”

She said the Women Trafficking and Child Labour Eradication Foundation (WOTCLEF) was born from that encouragement in 1999. “A law was made to criminalize human trafficking in Nigeria and NAPTIP was established to save millions.

“The woman I am today – the Lecturer, the Advocate, the Amazing Amazon, the Former Second Lady of Nigeria, the Grand Matron to several Organizations – I am because you allowed me to become,” she said.

Titi also paid tribute to Atiku’s record in public service. “Nigeria has known you as a diligent Customs Officer, a successful businessman, a two-term Vice President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria who chaired the National Economic Council that paid off the country’s foreign debt and a democrat who has kept faith with democracy even when it was costly. You don’t just make promises; you build systems. You don’t just talk about privatization and jobs; you did it.

“Only few people know how many school fees you pay silently; how many widows you feed daily; how many young people you gave jobs in and out of government, how many lives you have touched directly or indirectly and how many destinies you have transformed positively. Your philanthropy does not have a camera. It has a heart.”

As a father, she said, Atiku taught their children “that wealth without character is poverty” and “that education is the greatest inheritance. If in another world, I have the opportunity to pick a life partner, I will not hesitate to choose you again, again and again.”

The post ‘Incoming President’, Titi celebrates Atiku, says ex-VP not tired at 80 appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: ‘I got my first N1m after being slapped at a party,’ – Musiliu Ishola
description:
By Sekinat Osundiji







Apala singer Musiliu ‘Haruna’ Ishola has recounted how a performance at a family party ended with him being slapped by a female guest after a song he sang to entertain another wife offended her.







Ishola shared the experience while speaking to young artistes at a rece
content:
By Sekinat Osundiji

Apala singer Musiliu ‘Haruna’ Ishola has recounted how a performance at a family party ended with him being slapped by a female guest after a song he sang to entertain another wife offended her.

Ishola shared the experience while speaking to young artistes at a recent gathering, explaining how he became caught in a disagreement between two wives despite having no knowledge of the tension in the family.

According to him, the senior wife had specifically requested his performance at the party, but the junior wife initially objected to having Apala music at the event.

He said the husband eventually invited him because he did not want to disregard the senior wife’s preference.

However, when Ishola mounted the stage, the junior wife began enjoying his performance, dancing and spraying him money.

The singer said he was singing about enemies and their downfall while the junior wife danced, but the performance apparently offended the senior wife, who interpreted the lyrics as an indirect reference to her.

Recounting the incident, Ishola said: “I was singing about enemies while the second wife was dancing. Then the first wife came and slapped me.”

He described the impact of the slap, saying: “The slap was so heavy that I started seeing what looked like a thousand stars.”

Ishola said members of his team were ready to retaliate, but he instructed them to leave the woman alone to prevent the situation from escalating.

He subsequently left the stage and went backstage, where he reflected on the humiliation.

He said: “I went backstage and asked myself what kind of job I was doing that someone could just slap me.”

The singer said the husband later came to meet him and brought the senior wife, who knelt to apologise for her actions.

According to Ishola, she questioned why he had chosen a song that appeared to mock her while entertaining the junior wife, reminding him that she was responsible for inviting him to perform at the party.

He explained to her that he had no knowledge of the disagreement between the women and had only been doing his job as an entertainer.

Ishola said the couple later went into a room and returned with N1 million, which he described as the first time he received such an amount from a performance.

He attributed the unexpected reward to his patience and decision not to allow his team to retaliate, saying his response prevented the situation from escalating.

The singer added that the family has continued to invite him to perform at their events.

Vanguard News

title: ‘UTME not a do-or-die affair’, Osun commissioner tells candidates
description:
The Osun State Commissioner for Education, Professor Amare Omakasun, has urged candidates preparing for the 2027 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) to shun examination malpractice and embrace hard work, honesty and transparency.
Omakasun gave the advice while speaking in a message to
content:
The Osun State Commissioner for Education, Professor Amare Omakasun, has urged candidates preparing for the 2027 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) to shun examination malpractice and embrace hard work, honesty and transparency.

Omakasun gave the advice while speaking in a message to prospective candidates in a video posted on the Joint Admission and Matriculation Board’s (JAMB’s) X handle on Wednesday, warning that examination malpractice and attempts to cut corners could have serious consequences.

He stressed that candidates should approach the examination with the understanding that gaining admission into higher institutions was not a do-or-die affair.

“Examination is not a do-or-die affair. What we expect from you is complete transparency. If you cut corners, there are consequences,” he said.

The commissioner advised candidates to study diligently and remain focused on their preferred courses, noting that adequate preparation was the best way to secure admission.

“So the best thing is for you to study very hard, focus on the area of study you want to go and do, and then by the time you do well, JAMB will give you admission,” he stated.

Sharing his personal experience, Omakasun disclosed that he sat for his first UTME in 1988, describing the registration and examination process at the time as difficult.

He recalled that candidates had limited access to guidance during registration and had to complete their examination forms with little assistance.

According to him, candidates in those days also had to wait for their results to be delivered to their post office after writing the examination.

The commissioner disclosed that he scored 277 in his first UTME, using his experience to encourage prospective candidates to remain committed to their academic goals.

He reiterated the need for candidates to avoid examination malpractice and concentrate on legitimate efforts to achieve success in the 2027 UTME.

title: Lagos shuts four churches over noise pollution
description:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni



The Lagos State Government has shut down four churches across the state over alleged persistent noise pollution.







The enforcement exercise was carried out by the Lagos State Environmental Protection Agency (LASEPA) on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, as part of the governmen
content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

The Lagos State Government has shut down four churches across the state over alleged persistent noise pollution.

The enforcement exercise was carried out by the Lagos State Environmental Protection Agency (LASEPA) on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, as part of the government’s efforts to enforce environmental regulations and protect residents from excessive noise.

LASEPA disclosed this in a statement posted on its X handle on Wednesday.

The affected churches are Celestial Church of Christ (CCC), located at Chief Lawani Adeniyi Dosunmu Crescent, Lambada, Ajah; The Lord’s Chosen Charismatic Revival Movement, at 13, Sade Shobakin Street, Ona Ara Bus Stop, Ipaja-Ayobo; God’s Word Faith Ministries, at Olayemi Odukoya, Atan Kekere Bus Stop, off Ipaja-Ayobo; and His Presence Redemptions Ministry International, at 3, Olayemi Odukoya, Atan Kekere Bus Stop, off Ipaja-Ayobo.

The agency said the exercise was conducted in line with the state government’s directives to ensure compliance with environmental laws.

The statement read, “The Lagos State Environmental Protection Agency (LASEPA), on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, sealed four establishments across Lagos State for persistent noise pollution.

“The exercise was conducted in line with the directives of the Lagos State Government to ensure strict adherence to environmental laws, safeguard public health and promote a cleaner, healthier and safer environment for residents.”

LASEPA added that the enforcement was part of its ongoing efforts to ensure compliance with environmental regulations across the state.

The latest action comes weeks after the agency sealed All Christians Gathering Ministry in Surulere following repeated complaints by residents over late-night noise pollution.

The state government has also warned religious and entertainment centres against violating noise pollution regulations, saying establishments found culpable would face sanctions following investigations and warnings.

Under LASEPA’s noise pollution guidelines, permissible noise levels in residential areas must not exceed 55 decibels during the day and 45 decibels at night.

The agency also requires religious centres to operate in enclosed and soundproofed buildings, with the use of loudspeakers regulated to prevent disturbance to neighbouring residents.

title: Thugs Allegedly Attack NDC Convoy, Campaign Office In Benin
description: Political thugs have allegedly attacked the campaign convoy and campaign office of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Benin, Edo State, on Wednesday, Channels Television can report.The update came following an earlier uproar by the Party, saying it received an intelligence report on a possible
content:
Political thugs have allegedly attacked the campaign convoy and campaign office of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Benin, Edo State, on Wednesday, Channels Television can report.

The update came following an earlier uproar by the Party, saying it received an intelligence report on a possible attack at its town hall meeting in Benin, where its Presidential Candidate, Peter Obi, is expected to address supporters.

The Edo State Coordinator of the Party’s campaign council, John Yakubu, said the Party had been informed of plans to disrupt the event, as members prepared to leave their campaign office to receive Obi at the airport.

The Party, however, said it was moving ahead with plans to welcome Obi, while calling attention to the need for security around the event.

Videos obtained by our correspondent showed blood stains on the party convoys, including bullet exhibits seen on the floor of the Party’s campaign office.

Surrounded by other supporters and hospital personnel, a man was seen in the video to have been covered in a pool of his blood, and was seen being attended to at an unknown hospital. The video is too gory to be displayed here.

The development comes barely 48 hours after former deputy senate president, Ovie Omo-Agege’s campaign convoy was also attacked during an NDC campaign in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, in Delta State on Monday.

The attack on Omo-Agege, the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central, left six people dead, according to preliminary police reports, while several others sustained injuries.

Omo-Agege reportedly escaped unhurt.

The Delta State Police Command said it has invited Omo-Agege and five others for questioning over the deadly attack.

The police said the invitations were part of an ongoing investigation into the violence that occurred during an NDC campaign in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, on Monday.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, Bright Edafe, said the invited individuals had been asked to report to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) at the police headquarters in Asaba on specified dates.

Omo-Agege is expected to appear on Thursday at 11 a.m., while Egbo has been invited for 2 p.m. on the same day.

The five other invitees are Gowon Egoide, a former chairman of Uduere Quarters; Onoriode Oneya, the incumbent youth chairman of Uduere Community; Edirin Wokode Ewhubare, an associate of Egoide; Erukaye Egoide, Egoide’s nephew; and Tony Gabon Mevowovo, another associate of Egoide.

title: Army commander decorates 52 newly promoted soldiers in Edo
description:
The Commander, 4 Brigade Nigerian Army, Brigadier General Ahmed Balogun, has decorated 52 soldiers with their new ranks following their successful promotion in the Nigerian Army’s 2026 Promotion Exercise.
The decoration ceremony, held on November 24, 2026, at the Tiger 4 Mess Extension, Headquarters
content:
The Commander, 4 Brigade Nigerian Army, Brigadier General Ahmed Balogun, has decorated 52 soldiers with their new ranks following their successful promotion in the Nigerian Army’s 2026 Promotion Exercise.

The decoration ceremony, held on November 24, 2026, at the Tiger 4 Mess Extension, Headquarters 4 Brigade, Benin City, Edo State, recognised the soldiers’ dedication, commitment and contributions to the Nigerian Army.

According to a statement issued on Wednesday by the Assistant Director, Army Public Relations, 4 Brigade, Captain Kennedy Anyanwu, Balogun congratulated the beneficiaries and charged them to remain focused, diligent and loyal to constituted superior authorities.

The Brigade Commander reminded the soldiers that promotion came with increased responsibilities and higher expectations, urging them to justify the confidence reposed in them.

“Your promotion comes with increased responsibilities and higher expectations. You must therefore remain focused, diligent and loyal to constituted superior authorities,” Balogun charged.

He urged the newly promoted soldiers to demonstrate discipline, commitment and professionalism in the discharge of their duties.

The commander also encouraged them to take advantage of available military courses and training opportunities to improve their professional competence.

He further advised the soldiers to embrace continuous personal development through the study of relevant books and professional materials, particularly in regimentation and man management.

According to him, such knowledge would enhance their effectiveness both in the field and within their respective units.

Balogun described their promotion as recognition of their hard work, dedication and exemplary service to the Nigerian Army and the country.

He also emphasised the importance of discipline, integrity, loyalty, mutual respect and continuous self-development as essential qualities of effective soldiers.

The commander expressed appreciation to the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, for approving the promotions and reaffirmed 4 Brigade’s commitment to supporting the attainment of the COAS Command Philosophy.

In her remarks on behalf of the newly promoted soldiers, Master Warrant Officer Alice Yakubu expressed gratitude to the Nigerian Army leadership for finding them worthy of promotion.

“We sincerely appreciate the leadership of the Nigerian Army for the confidence reposed in us. We assure you that we will justify this trust through renewed commitment to discipline, professionalism and effective service,” Yakubu said.

She pledged that the beneficiaries would continue to contribute to the growth and operational effectiveness of 4 Brigade and the Nigerian Army.

The 52 promoted soldiers comprised six Master Warrant Officers, 10 Warrant Officers, 19 Staff Sergeants, five Sergeants, seven Corporals and five Lance Corporals.

Highlights of the ceremony included words of advice from dignitaries and the Chief of Staff, Headquarters 4 Brigade, Colonel US Agbo, decoration of the beneficiaries with their new ranks and group photographs.

title: Atiku embraces ‘Daddy Subsidy’ nickname, promises Nigerians relief at 80
description:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has embraced the nickname “Daddy Subsidy” as he marked his 80th birthday on Wednesday, promising Nigerians that relief would come and pledging to make the country affordable again.







Atiku, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, made t
content:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has embraced the nickname “Daddy Subsidy” as he marked his 80th birthday on Wednesday, promising Nigerians that relief would come and pledging to make the country affordable again.

Atiku, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, made the remark in a post on X while thanking Nigerians for their birthday wishes and prayers.

He said the nickname was among the names Nigerians had given him that he particularly enjoyed, adding that he remained committed to making life easier for citizens.

“Of all the names Nigerians have given me, ‘Daddy Subsidy’ may be the one I enjoy most on my birthday. Thank you for your kind wishes, and for the prayer that warmed my afternoon,” he wrote.

Addressing Nigerians across the country, the former vice-president promised that relief was coming, making an apparent reference to his position on petrol subsidy and the hardship associated with its removal.

“To the sons and daughters scattered across the country: relief is coming, and it will follow the barrel. I will make Nigeria affordable again,” Atiku added.

Atiku’s birthday message comes amid continued political debate over the Tinubu administration’s economic reforms, particularly the removal of petrol subsidy, which has contributed to increased living and transportation costs.

Meanwhile, President Bola Tinubu has congratulated Atiku on his 80th birthday, commending his contributions to Nigeria’s political development, democracy, education and the private sector.

In a statement issued by his spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, Tinubu said he shared with Atiku a commitment to democratic pluralism, political participation and allowing Nigerians to present alternative ideas on governance.

The president recalled supporting Atiku’s 2007 presidential ambition under the defunct Action Congress platform, saying the decision reflected his belief that democracy thrives when political actors are free to compete and contribute to national discourse.

Tinubu also praised Atiku’s investments in education and entrepreneurship, particularly the establishment of the American University of Nigeria, Yola, which he said had contributed to expanding access to higher education and developing human capital.

Despite their differences in political affiliation and views on national issues, Tinubu said their shared commitment to Nigeria’s unity and democratic stability remained important.

He wished the former vice-president good health, renewed strength and many more years of service to Nigeria and humanity as he joined the octogenarian club.

title: Police arrest man with pistol at APC rally in Benue
description:

The spokesperson for the state command, DSP Peter Aondongu, disclosed this in a statement issued and made available to journalists in Makurd
content:
The Benue State Police Command has arrested a man found in possession of a pistol during the All Progressives Congress campaign flag-off in Gboko, Benue State.

The spokesperson for the state command, DSP Peter Aondongu, disclosed this in a statement issued and made available to journalists in Makurdi on Wednesday.

According to the police spokesman, a Beretta pistol was recovered from the suspect, identified as Saalu Fidelis Teryange, during security screening at the venue of the campaign rally last Thursday.

He warned politicians in the state against instigating violence during the ongoing political activities, adding that the command would not tolerate any attempt by individuals or groups to use the electioneering period as an opportunity to foment trouble, engage in political thuggery, intimidate opponents or undermine the peace and security of the state.

The statement read in part, “The warning follows the arrest of a male suspect, identified as Saalu Fidelis Teryange, during security screening at a political campaign event held at J.S. Tarka Stadium, Gboko, on Thursday, 19th November 2026.

“A Beretta pistol was recovered from the suspect, who is currently in police custody undergoing investigation.

“Police personnel deployed to the venue maintained heightened security alertness on that day, much as the Commissioner of Police, CP Cletus C. N. Nwadiogbu, psc(+), mnips, PhD, alongside the Deputy Commissioner of Police in charge of Operations, were physically present to supervise the security arrangements which paid off with the arrest and recovery of the lethal weapon.”

The command spokesperson reaffirmed the command’s commitment to maintaining peace and security throughout the ongoing electioneering period.

According to him, the state Commissioner of Police had directed Area Commanders, Divisional Police Officers and Tactical Commanders to sustain heightened vigilance, strengthen intelligence-led policing and ensure adequate security coverage of political gatherings and other public events across the state.

The command assured residents of its readiness to discharge its constitutional responsibility of protecting lives and property before, during and after the electioneering period.

He charged members of the public to remain law-abiding and promptly report suspicious movements or activities to the nearest police station.

title: FG, Kogi warn farmers against hoarding, selling of inputs
description:
The Federal and Kogi State Governments have warned farmers against hoarding and selling of inputs distributed to them for free to boost food production.
The Kogi State government commended the National Agricultural Development Fund (NADF) and the Federal Government for extending the 2026 Flood Recov
content:
The Federal and Kogi State Governments have warned farmers against hoarding and selling of inputs distributed to them for free to boost food production.

The Kogi State government commended the National Agricultural Development Fund (NADF) and the Federal Government for extending the 2026 Flood Recovery Agricultural Inputs Intervention to 3,520 farmers affected by flooding across the state.

The intervention, flagged off in Lokoja, is aimed at restoring agricultural livelihoods and boosting food production among farmers whose farmlands and crops were destroyed by flooding.

The beneficiaries are expected to receive urea and NPK fertilisers, 15kg bags of rice seeds, pre-planting, pre-emergence and early post-emergence chemicals, as well as insecticides to support the resumption of farming activities.

Speaking on behalf of the Executive Secretary/Chief Executive Officer of NADF, Mohammed Ibrahim, the Fund’s Team Lead to Kogi State, Muhammad Gidado, described the intervention as a demonstration of the Federal Government’s commitment to agricultural resilience, farmers’ welfare and sustainable food production.

Gidado said the intervention would help affected farmers recover from the devastating effects of flooding, resume production and contribute to national food security.

“This intervention is more than the distribution of agricultural inputs, it is a demonstration of solidarity with our farmers and a collective commitment to restoring hope, protecting livelihoods and securing the future of agriculture in Nigeria,” he said.

He urged the Kogi State Government, community leaders and other stakeholders to ensure that the inputs were distributed transparently and promptly to the intended beneficiaries.

He also called on the farmers to make judicious use of the inputs to achieve the objectives of the intervention.

In his goodwill message, the Kogi State Commissioner for Agriculture and Food Security, Timothy Ojomah, expressed appreciation to President Bola Tinubu, the Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Senator Abubakar Kyari, and the NADF leadership for extending the intervention to the state.

Ojomah, who noted that Kogi was among six states benefiting from the Federal Government’s intervention, described the support as timely, given the state’s recurring experience of flooding.

“We sincerely thank NADF and its ES for providing this support to our farmers too,” he said.

He assured that the state government would ensure that the intervention achieved its intended purpose, warning beneficiaries against diverting or selling the agricultural inputs.

“Any inputs that are given to our farmers, they will make use of them judiciously. Our farmers need more. So there is no amount of inputs that are given to farmers that is enough to satisfy their farm. As such, selling is not an option here in Kogi,” he stated.

Similarly, the Managing Director of the Kogi State Agricultural Development Project (ADP), Dr. George Ogirima Bello, described the intervention as a timely lifeline for farmers struggling to recover from the impact of flooding.

Bello pledged that the ADP would complement the distribution of the inputs with extension services to guide beneficiaries on their proper application and utilisation.

He said the extension support would ensure that farmers derived maximum benefits from the intervention, while cautioning them against selling the inputs.

Also speaking, the Commissioner for Housing and Urban Development, Abanika Taiye, described the intervention as a welcome complement to the agricultural initiatives of Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo.

Taiye observed that flooding had left many farmers in difficult circumstances, adding that the Federal Government’s support had brought relief and renewed hope to affected farming communities.

“Farmers are in a disheartening situation. They are not happy. But with this now, this has brought them succour, and that is going to increase agricultural production in the state,” he said.

The State Chairman of the All Farmers Association of Nigeria (AFAN), Musa Raji, also commended the Federal Government and NADF for the intervention, assuring that the beneficiaries would make productive use of the inputs.

Raji said the support would reduce the cost of farming, improve agricultural production and enhance farmers’ productivity, ultimately contributing to food security.

He further acknowledged other Federal Government agricultural interventions, including the guaranteed minimum price initiative and plans to provide agro-processing and market infrastructure in the state.

The Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security, Mr. Moses Dare, was among dignitaries at the event, alongside other government officials, agricultural stakeholders and farmers.

The Commissioner for Agriculture and Food Security subsequently declared the intervention open and formally flagged off the distribution of the agricultural inputs to the 3,520 beneficiaries across the state.

The post FG, Kogi warn farmers against hoarding, selling of inputs appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: ‘Despite our differences, Nigeria comes first’ – Tinubu celebrates Atiku at 80
description:
By Enitan Abdultawab



President Bola Tinubu has congratulated former Vice President Atiku Abubakar on his 80th birthday, noting that despite their political differences and occasional disagreements, their shared commitment to Nigeria’s unity and democratic stability must remain paramount.







T
content:
By Enitan Abdultawab

President Bola Tinubu has congratulated former Vice President Atiku Abubakar on his 80th birthday, noting that despite their political differences and occasional disagreements, their shared commitment to Nigeria’s unity and democratic stability must remain paramount.

Tinubu, in a birthday message issued on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, commended Atiku’s contributions to Nigeria’s development, particularly his years of political engagement and commitment to democratic pluralism.

The message was shared by the President’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga.

Tinubu recalled that he supported Atiku’s 2007 presidential ambition, saying the decision reflected his belief that democracy thrives when political actors are free to participate, offer alternative visions and contribute to discussions on leadership and governance.

He said his political philosophy had consistently emphasised strengthening democratic institutions, respecting divergent opinions and ensuring that political competition served the interests of Nigerians.

The President also reiterated his advocacy for politics without bitterness, saying room should always be left for reconciliation after disagreements among political opponents.

“Despite our different political affiliations and occasional disagreements, Nigeria’s democracy must continue to benefit from citizens who remain committed to democratic engagement, national development, and the rule of law,” he said.

Tinubu also commended Atiku’s contributions to education, entrepreneurship and the private sector, particularly his establishment of the American University of Nigeria, Yola, which he said had expanded access to quality higher education and strengthened human capital development.

Although he acknowledged that he and Atiku now belonged to different political camps and held contrasting views on national issues, Tinubu said their shared commitment to Nigeria’s unity and democratic stability should remain paramount.

“Therefore, as the former vice president joins the Octogenarian Club, I wish him good health, renewed strength and many more years of service to the nation and humanity,” he said.

“Happy 80th birthday, Your Excellency,” the President added.

Atiku, who served as Nigeria’s vice president from 1999 to 2007, has contested the presidency several times and is the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate for the 2027 elections.

The post ‘Despite our differences, Nigeria comes first’ – Tinubu celebrates Atiku at 80 appeared first on Vanguard News.

description:

By Gift Chapi-Odekina, Abuja



ABUJA — The House of Representatives has urged the Federal Ministry of Works to direct Rock Result Nigeria Limited to return immediately to the site and rehabilitate or reconstruct damaged box culverts along t
content:
…Demand urgent repairs, four-week monitoring of project

By Gift Chapi-Odekina, Abuja

ABUJA — The House of Representatives has urged the Federal Ministry of Works to direct Rock Result Nigeria Limited to return immediately to the site and rehabilitate or reconstruct damaged box culverts along the East-West Road, particularly at Iheke in Ahoada East Local Government Area of Rivers State.

The resolution followed the adoption of a motion sponsored by Hon. Oboku Abonsizibe Oforji, who drew the attention of lawmakers to the reported deterioration of the culverts and the need for urgent intervention to prevent further damage and potential safety risks.

The House recalled that it had, on October 3, 2023, adopted a motion on the deplorable condition of the East-West Road, particularly the Iheke axis, following which the Federal Government undertook further interventions.

The interventions included the construction of box culverts, approval and release of funds for rehabilitation and flood mitigation works, payments to Rock Result Nigeria Limited and the re-award of the contract to Setraco Nigeria Limited for the continuation of the road dualisation project.

However, lawmakers expressed concern over reports that the constructed box culverts had deteriorated, despite the financial commitments made by the government.

They said the reported condition of the drainage infrastructure underscored the need for a technical assessment of the works, including the materials used, construction standards and supervision of the project.

The House noted that the East-West Road was a major economic and social corridor connecting Bayelsa, Rivers and Delta states to other parts of the country, serving communities and facilitating the movement of people, goods and services.

It warned that the deteriorating condition of the road could further disrupt transportation and expose motorists and other road users to safety risks.

Lawmakers also expressed concern that the dualisation of the East-West Road from Ahoada in Rivers State through the Bayelsa axis to Patani in Delta State remained incomplete, despite earlier completion targets of April 2025 and November 2025.

Consequently, the House urged the Ministry of Works to ensure that Rock Result Nigeria Limited returned to the site without delay to carry out the required rehabilitation or reconstruction of the damaged culverts in accordance with approved engineering standards.

It also called for adequate technical supervision, quality assurance and an independent engineering assessment of the remedial works to reduce the risk of further structural problems.

In addition, the lawmakers urged the ministry to ensure the completion of the dualisation of the Ahoada-Bayelsa and Patani sections of the road by Setraco Nigeria Limited.

The House mandated its Committee on Works and Legislative Compliance to monitor the implementation of the resolutions and report back within four weeks for further legislative action.
