title: Akpabio, NASENI to train 500 artisans, build science lab for secondary school in A/ Ibom
description: Senate President Godswill Akpabio in collaboration with the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure (NASENI) have concluded arrangements to train 500 artisans and provided starter packs to beneficiaries at Independence High School, Ukana, Essien Udim local government area, Akwa Ib
content:
Senate President Godswill Akpabio in collaboration with the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure (NASENI) have concluded arrangements to train 500 artisans and provided starter packs to beneficiaries at Independence High School, Ukana, Essien Udim local government area, Akwa Ibom state under Rebewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Tinubu .

Akpabio also laid a foundation for construction of Physics , Biology and Chemistry Laboratory for the Independence High School in Ukana, Essien Udim council area of the state .

Speaking at the ground breaking ceremony for the construction of science laboratory and sustainable empowerment programme at Independence High School in Ukana, Akpabio appreciated the Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure ( NASENI) and its leadership for demonstrating that government can lend a helping hand to citizens.

Akpabio acknowledged that there is a solemn covenant between a government and its people adding that the power from the people to enthrone government becomes the authority to advance welfare of the people .

” I commend the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure, NASENI, and its Executive Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Mr Khalil Suleiman Halilu, for demonstrating that government can be a helping hand to the struggling, a ladder to the aspiring and a bridge between the poverty of today and the prosperity of tomorrow

“It is vindicated when the farmer prospers, when the artisan earns an honest living, when the unemployed acquire productive skills and when the poorest child can look towards tomorrow with hope. That’s the social contract

“That is the duty of leadership and the work of government. And that is the noble work NASENI advances here today”.

Akpabio stared that only political independence of a nation is not enough but must be backed up with technological self reliant to build a nation where sovereignty can not be interrupted by foreigners through their technology.

“In 1960, Nigeria won political independence. But what is the worth of political independence if a nation remains dependent upon others for its technology, machinery, scientific knowledge and economic opportunities?

“Our fathers fought to free our country from colonial rule. Our generation must fight to free its productive capacities from dependence

“Our fathers raised the flag of political sovereignty. We must raise the standard of scientific and technological sovereignty

” The first independence gave us a nation. The next must give us the power to build a greater nation.
That is the significance of today’s groundbreaking for laboratories in Biology, Physics and Chemistry”

He charged the school management to turn the laboratories to become training ground for future scientists to fullfil the good intentions of the government agency .

He said the laboratories must be
be equipped, maintained and supported by teachers capable of turning scientific curiosity into practical competence.

“I am equally delighted that NASENI’s Sustainable Empowerment Programme will train 500 beneficiaries across 13 trades.

“This is an investment in human dignity, productive enterprise and economic independence

“A nation cannot build prosperity upon certificates alone. It needs skilled hands, disciplined minds and inventive spirits”

He tasked beneficiaries of the training programme to seize the opportunity to master their trades, uphold integrity and transform skills into livelihoods.

Akpabio further charge employers of labour to open their workshops, offer apprenticeships and give the emerging talents their chance.

“And to NASENI, I say: let success be measured not merely by the number trained, but by the lives transformed, businesses established and families lifted from poverty.”

He assured the public that the National Assembly, under his leadership, shall continue, through appropriation and oversight, to support public investments that deliver measurable benefits to Nigerians.

“My fellow Nigerians, when our forebears founded this school, they sowed the seeds of a glorious future. Today, we have come to nurture those seeds and secure a harvest of greatness for generations yet unborn

” Ours is the solemn duty to transform freedom into opportunity, knowledge into productive power, and political independence into enduring national prosperity”.

In his remarks, the Vice Chairman of NASENI Mr Khalil Suleiman Halilu commended senator Akpabio for his commitment to the well being of his people by
supporting investments in practical skills and science education.

” You are helping people to earn a living close to home and giving young people more opportunities to learn and succeed in their own communities

” I also thank the Government and people of Akwa Ibom State, the leadership of Essien Udim Local Government Area, our traditional and community leaders, and the management and staff of Independence High School for welcoming us” .

Halilu said 500 participants in the training would receive hands- on training in 13 engineering trades .

“Across Akwa Ibom, 500 participants will receive hands-on training in 13 engineering trades

” The trades range from solar installation and electronics repair to welding, refrigeration and CNG vehicle conversion”

Halilu explained that each participant who completes the training will receive a starter kit to advance their trades .

” Training equipment will also be handed over to trade cooperatives so that graduates can continue to access machinery that would be costly to buy individually

“I encourage local businesses, farmers and contractors to get to know these trainees and give them opportunities to put their skills to work

“The laboratories we are breaking ground for today will give students practical experience in Biology, Physics and Chemistry

A student should be able to build a circuit, examine a specimen under a microscope and test an idea through an experiment

” Those experiences can help young people see where science fits into their lives and what they might go on to do with it

“Under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, our responsibility at NASENI is to make science, engineering and technology useful in people’s everyday lives”.

The post Akpabio, NASENI to train 500 artisans, build science lab for secondary school in A/ Ibom appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

description:

By Adesina Wahab



Non-teaching staff of Yaba College of Technology (YABATECH), Lagos, on Wednesday protested the non-payment of several allowances owed them, threatening to embark on an indefinite strike from Thursday if their dema
content:
…Protest over unpaid allowances, give management until Thursday

By Adesina Wahab

Non-teaching staff of Yaba College of Technology (YABATECH), Lagos, on Wednesday protested the non-payment of several allowances owed them, threatening to embark on an indefinite strike from Thursday if their demands were not met.

The workers, under the umbrella of the Non-Teaching Staff Union of Polytechnics (NOTSUP), staged a protest march around the campus, led by the union’s Branch Chairman, Bayo Sanusi.

They marched to the Administrative Block, which houses the Rector’s office, the Bursary Department and the institution’s main gate, singing solidarity songs and displaying placards bearing various messages.

Addressing the protesters, Sanusi expressed displeasure over what he described as the exclusion of non-teaching staff from the payment of allowances, despite the reported payment of similar entitlements to teaching staff.

He said teaching and non-teaching employees played complementary roles in the administration of tertiary institutions and should be treated fairly.

“I don’t know whether our people have seen a bird flying with one wing. It is not possible. Tertiary institutions like ours have teaching and non-teaching staff and we complement one another. NOTSUP is made up of NASU and SSANIP members and we are united in calling for the payment of our dues. A labourer, they say, is worth his wages,” he said.

Sanusi said the union’s national leadership had engaged the Federal Government on the outstanding allowances and reached an agreement on their payment.

He added that the Minister of Education had directed the managements of federal polytechnics and colleges of education to source funds for the payments from available resources, including savings from capital expenditure and internally generated revenue, with a promise that the Federal Government would reimburse the institutions.

According to him, at least three federal polytechnics had complied with the directive and paid the allowances, while non-teaching staff at YABATECH were still awaiting payment.

He said the union had engaged the college management and was assured last Wednesday that the outstanding entitlements would be paid, but the promise had yet to be fulfilled.

“In line with the directive by the Minister, at least three federal Polytechnics have paid. Here at YABATECH, teaching staff have been paid leaving us in the lurch like orphans. We are not less human than teaching staff. We have contacted our management here and last Wednesday, they promised to pay. A week has passed and nothing has happened,” he said.

The union chairman questioned why the management had been able to pay teaching staff but had yet to settle the entitlements of non-teaching employees.

He said the rising cost of living had worsened the hardship faced by workers, citing the daily transport expenses incurred by some staff members who commute from areas such as Ikorodu to the college.

Sanusi also expressed concern over the personal challenges confronting members, including difficulties in meeting healthcare and other living expenses.

He clarified that the protest was not motivated by any personal disagreement with the Rector or Bursar, but was aimed at pressing the management to address the workers’ demands.

The union leader also rejected suggestions that the outstanding allowances could be paid next year, after the elections, insisting that members could no longer wait.

“We cannot take that. We cannot wait any longer as we have waited enough,” he said.

On the union’s next line of action, Sanusi said its branch leadership would consult the national leadership and await further directives, warning that an indefinite strike could commence from Thursday.

The demands include payment of 10 months’ arrears of the Consolidated Non-Teaching Tool Allowance (CONTTA), nine months’ Earned Allowance, 12 months’ arrears of the 25 and 35 per cent allowances, as well as outstanding promotion arrears.

content:
…Governor receives traditional Yoruba title, announces N50m donation as community pledges support for Tinubu, Fintiri and APC candidates

By Billy Abel, Yola

Adamawa State Governor, Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri, has declared support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, calling on residents of the state to rally behind the All Progressives Congress (APC) and its candidates across elective positions.

Fintiri made the declaration on Tuesday in Yola while addressing members of the Yoruba community in Adamawa State, who endorsed the President, the governor’s senatorial ambition and other APC candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The governor, who was conferred with the traditional Yoruba title of Atayese, described the economic reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration as necessary measures to reposition the country for sustainable growth.

He acknowledged the economic difficulties confronting Nigerians but maintained that the long-term benefits of the reforms would outweigh the immediate challenges.

Fintiri also commended the South-West for its contributions to Nigeria’s democratic development, urging Northerners to support Tinubu’s second-term ambition in the interest of national unity and the country’s progress.

He assured the Yoruba community of continued inclusion in his administration, particularly in appointments, education, scholarships, employment and economic opportunities.

The governor acknowledged the community’s contributions to Adamawa’s development and announced a donation of N50 million in support of the group.

Earlier, the Yoruba community, represented by leaders and members from the 21 local government areas of the state, declared what it described as 100 per cent support for Tinubu, Fintiri, the APC governorship candidate and other party aspirants.

Speaking on behalf of the community, its leader, Niyi Orionowa, said many Yoruba people had lived in Adamawa for several decades and regarded the state as their home.

He commended Fintiri for creating an environment that allows people from different ethnic backgrounds to participate in the state’s development.

Orionowa highlighted the contributions of Yoruba professionals and businesspeople in education, healthcare, commerce, infrastructure and public service.

He specifically cited the roles played by Yoruba judges, university academics, medical practitioners and other professionals, noting that many members of the community had spent the most productive years of their lives in Adamawa.

According to him, the governor’s policies on education, healthcare, infrastructure and road construction had contributed significantly to the state’s development.

He pledged that the community would reciprocate the administration’s support through political mobilisation for the APC in the 2027 elections.

The Yoruba traditional leader in Adamawa, Dr Adeyemi Alani, also reaffirmed the community’s commitment to Fintiri and the APC, promising that its members would support the party’s candidates at the polls.

Alani, speaking on behalf of the traditional council and the wider Yoruba community, described its members as peace-loving, hardworking and law-abiding citizens who were committed to the progress of Adamawa State.

He expressed support for the APC governorship candidate and Fintiri’s senatorial ambition, assuring the governor that the community would work towards the party’s electoral success.

In separate remarks, representatives of Yoruba youths and women appealed for greater inclusion in government appointments, empowerment programmes and other opportunities.

The youth representative, Abdulrazak Abdulhamid, commended the governor’s development initiatives but urged the state government to give qualified Yoruba youths greater opportunities to serve in government and participate in empowerment programmes.

Similarly, the Yoruba women leader called for sustained attention to women’s political participation, economic empowerment, appointments and educational opportunities.

She reiterated the community’s commitment to peaceful coexistence and equal opportunities for all residents, irrespective of ethnic background.

The APC governorship candidate, who also addressed the gathering, expressed appreciation for the community’s endorsement and pledged to sustain Fintiri’s development legacy if elected.

He said his administration would build on the governor’s achievements, particularly in education, healthcare, commerce and infrastructure, while maintaining an inclusive approach to governance.

He further assured the Yoruba community that people from different ethnic backgrounds would have opportunities to contribute to the administration, stressing that unity in diversity would remain a guiding principle.

The event attracted Yoruba traditional and community leaders, women, youths and other stakeholders from across Adamawa’s 21 local government areas, who pledged to mobilise support for the APC ahead of the 2027 general elections

content:
…Give NSCDC seven days to submit operational records

By Gift Cnapi-Odekina, Abuja

ABUJA — The House of Representatives Committee on Solid Minerals Development has asked the Commander of the Mining Marshals, ACC Attah John Onoja, to tender a written apology to the National Assembly over the contents of a letter concerning a member of the House, Hon. Abdulmalik Danga.

The committee also gave the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) seven days to submit outstanding operational records relating to petitions on the activities of the Mining Marshals, including complaints about arrests, detention of mining operators and the closure of mining sites.

The decisions followed an investigative hearing chaired by Hon. Jonathan Gaza, during which lawmakers sought clarification from Onoja over a July 24, 2026 letter addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas.

The letter concerned the intervention of Danga, who represents Adavi/Okehi Federal Constituency of Kogi State, in matters relating to the activities of the Mining Marshals.

In the correspondence, Onoja expressed reservations about the lawmaker’s intervention, linking it to concerns surrounding the enforcement of regulations against illegal mining.

Reading an excerpt from the letter, Gaza said the language used in the correspondence raised concerns about the manner in which a serving member of the National Assembly was addressed.

The letter stated: “While we respect the rules of lawmaking in shaping the society through oversight legislative functions, we strongly view the action of Abdulmalik Danga as anti-government and motivated by illegal mining cartels whose unlawful activities are being disrupted by the sanity being restored in the mining sector.”

The committee members questioned the basis for the assertions and whether the correspondence reflected an authorised institutional position of the NSCDC.

Responding, Onoja told the committee that he wrote the letter in his personal capacity as Commander of the Mining Marshals and did not intend to challenge the constitutional powers of the legislature.

He said: “Mr. Chairman, permit me to state clearly on record. My response, my letter, in my personal capacity as the Commander Mining Marshals, is not in any way looking into the legislative powers of the Committee. The letter is speaking to the motion as moved.”

Gaza, however, questioned the explanation, particularly because the correspondence was written on NSCDC letterhead and carried an official reference number.

The committee chairman consequently asked the NSCDC Commandant-General, Ahmed Abubakar Audi, to clarify whether the letter represented the official position of the Corps or was issued without institutional authorisation.

Audi said the Corps had administrative procedures requiring officers to obtain approval before issuing correspondence on behalf of the Commandant-General.

He explained that an officer authorised to communicate on behalf of the Commandant-General would sign such a letter in the latter’s name.

Audi said the letter under review did not follow that format, adding that Onoja had signed it in his personal capacity.

“According to our administrative procedure, if an officer is instructed to write a letter on behalf of the CG, the officer will sign that letter for the Commandant-General. But if you check the letter, you’ll see that there’s no… So he signed it on his own personal capacity,” Audi said.

The committee maintained that the use of official stationery and reference details required further clarification regarding the circumstances in which the correspondence was issued.

Reps demand outstanding operational records

In a separate development, the committee expressed concern over the non-submission of documents it had requested from the NSCDC concerning the operations of the Mining Marshals.

Gaza recalled that the committee, on October 20, 2026, issued a formal request for documentary records and a notice requiring the personal appearance of the Commandant-General.

The directive requested a comprehensive response verified on oath, alongside 10 properly bound and paginated hard copies and an identical electronic copy of the relevant primary documents.

The committee said the November 3 deadline passed without the requested documents and written response being submitted.

Gaza explained that the records were required to assist the committee in examining petitions and complaints concerning the enforcement activities of the Mining Marshals, including reported arrests, detention of mining operators and the handling of mining sites.

He said the Commandant-General’s appearance before the committee did not remove the Corps’ obligation to provide the requested documents.

“Let it be clear on the record that personal attendance does not cure or waive the statutory obligation to produce primary, certified, and unedited documentary records within the possession, custody, or control of the Corps,” he said.

The committee subsequently directed the Commandant-General, the Mining Marshals commander and all zonal, state and FCT commands to preserve records relating to their enforcement operations.

The requested records include mining site inspection reports, arrest and custody registers, operational logs, financial and banking records, vehicle registers, electronic metadata, official correspondence and CCTV recordings across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

Gaza cautioned against any alteration, concealment, removal or destruction of relevant records, as well as any action that could interfere with the committee’s investigation or intimidate officers and witnesses.

Citing Section 14 of the Legislative Houses (Powers and Privileges) Act, 2017, and Section 19 of the NSCDC Act, he said the committee would consider appropriate statutory measures where necessary.

At the end of the proceedings, the committee asked Onoja to issue a written apology to the National Assembly over the contents of his letter concerning Danga and directed the NSCDC to submit the outstanding records within seven days.

Mining operators present complaints

Meanwhile, some mining stakeholders who appeared before the committee raised concerns about the enforcement activities of the Mining Marshals.

The operators alleged that some mining businesses had been subjected to arrests, detention of personnel and closure of sites, including operations they said were covered by licences issued by the Ministry of Solid Minerals Development.

They also complained that enforcement actions had disrupted their businesses and resulted in financial losses, with some operators claiming that equipment and machinery had remained idle following the closure of their sites.

The stakeholders called on the committee to examine the complaints and establish whether the enforcement actions in question complied with applicable laws and regulatory procedures.

They urged the relevant authorities to ensure that disputes over mining licences and compliance were addressed through established regulatory and legal channels.

The operators further called for greater transparency in enforcement operations and safeguards for businesses operating with valid approvals.

They maintained that efforts to curb illegal mining should be accompanied by adherence to due process and respect for the rights of mining operators.

The complaints were presented as part of the issues before the committee and remain subject to its investigation.

title: NDLEA busts N303.9bn meth factory in Enugu, arrests kingpin, five Mexican “cooks”
description: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has dismantled an industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratory in Enugu, arresting a 63-year-old businessman, Chuks Enoch Ezeike, popularly called “Over Size”, and five Mexican nationals he allegedly smuggled into the country on forged passports to pro
content:
The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has dismantled an industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratory in Enugu, arresting a 63-year-old businessman, Chuks Enoch Ezeike, popularly called “Over Size”, and five Mexican nationals he allegedly smuggled into the country on forged passports to produce the drug.

Operatives recovered 1,512 kilograms of methamphetamine, finished and in production, valued at US$226.8 million (N303.913 billion). They also seized 6.68 tons of precursor chemicals and a range of industrial equipment.

NDLEA Chairman and CEO, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Marwa (Rtd), announced the breakthrough at a press conference at the Agency’s national headquarters in Abuja on Wednesday.

He described it as one of the most carefully planned, intelligence-led operations the Agency has ever conducted. According to him, it “began in faraway Mexico, ran through Colombia, France and the Republic of Benin, crossed into Lagos, and ended in an industrial complex in Enugu.”

Ezeike, who holds the traditional title of Ebekuo Dike na Nanka in his Anambra State community, built the plant behind San Savanna Oil Company Limited at Kilometre ½, Abakaliki Expressway, Emene, Enugu. The complex had living quarters, allowing the Mexicans to live and work in one place without being seen in town.

Marwa said the Agency’s Special Operations Unit (SOU) began working on intelligence in April 2026 that identified Ezeike as a specialist in setting up clandestine meth laboratories, with links to Oscar Ramos-Cardenas, a Mexican known for large-scale, industrial-grade production. “From that moment, Ezeike was a marked man,” he said.

On 25 August, the Agency received the flight itineraries of five Mexican meth experts bound for Nigeria. Working with the Nigeria Immigration Service, it had them denied entry when they landed in Abuja on 28 August and returned to Mexico. That same day, officers found that Ezeike had travelled from Enugu to Abuja to receive them. His bank records later confirmed his hotel payment.

The Mexicans were flown from Bogotá, Colombia, through Paris to the Republic of Benin. Ezeike allegedly procured forged Argentine, Colombian and Chilean passports and sent them by a driver to Cotonou, where the Mexicans swapped their genuine documents for false identities.

When the Agency learned on September 19 that the five had arrived in Cotonou, it made what Marwa called a deliberate decision to let them in. “We wanted the whole network: the meth specialist, the financier, the factory and the product. Sending them home a second time would only have postponed the problem,” he said.

Three of the Mexicans crossed through the Seme Border Post on 20 September and two followed on 21 September, on a road trip arranged by Ezeike. With NDLEA operatives embedded in their every move, Ezeike received them in Lagos and lodged them in a hotel, where he was observed having breakfast with them on 22 September, before moving them to Enugu.

While the Mexicans lived and worked at San Savanna, Ezeike stayed at Adig Suites, 2 Nwafor Orizu Street, Enugu, moving between locations in a blue Toyota Corolla, a red Toyota RAV4 and a Lexus RX 350. Officers watched both sites through September and October, using a drone and other intelligence tools, and had assembled the full picture by 7 November.

On November 9, over 200 personnel of the Strike Force and the Enugu State Command were assembled at a staging area. Marwa gave the order on 10 November, and at about 5 a.m. on 11 November, operatives of the SOU, the Strike Force, the Forensic Directorate and the Enugu State Command raided both locations simultaneously.

At San Savanna, officers stormed the laboratory and an adjoining guest house that doubled as a stash house, arresting all five Mexicans in the middle of production.

At Adig Suites, Ezeike was arrested in Room 106 and taken to San Savanna to witness the search. There, Marwa said, he admitted owning the laboratory and bringing in the Mexicans to manufacture methamphetamine. He claimed only a small batch had been produced, and said the Mexicans were due to leave on Friday, 13 November. “In other words, we caught them with two days to spare,” Marwa said.

The arrested Mexicans, listed with the names on their forged passports followed by their real names, are: Gonzalez Numez Lucas, whose real name is Oscar Ramos-Cardenas, the leader and chief specialist; Lopez Salvador Vasquez Esperanza, real name Juan Antonio Sarabia-Cabrera; Hernandez Cortes Carlos Fuentes, real name Luis Enrique Garcia-Amador; Fernandez Rio Mateo Jimenez, real name Jose Alejandro Renteria-Reyes; and Rodriguez Araya Andres Perez, real name Salomon Cabanillas-Torres.

The 6.68 tons of precursors, covering 20 types of chemicals, include 2,835kg of lead acetate, 1,050kg of tartaric acid, 450kg of mandelic acid, 160kg of P2P and 70kg of methylamine.

Equipment seized includes four industrial burners, two industrial distillation units, two boilers, two hydraulic presses, eleven gas cylinders, two freezers, two digital scales and four washing/drying machines. Forensic experts confirmed that all of it is consistent with industrial methamphetamine manufacture.

“They were producing methamphetamine not by the kilogram, but by the ton,” Marwa said. “Had they succeeded, that poison would have flooded our streets, our schools and our communities, and been exported to destroy lives abroad, with Nigeria’s name stamped on it.”

Marwa said statements by the suspects show this was an organised, recurring transnational operation with three layers. At the top is a cartel command in Mexico that recruits, deploys and pays the specialists. Ezeike served as the local coordinator who built the laboratory, procured chemicals and arranged travel, transport and false documents.

The third layer is the Mexican production crew, led by Ramos-Cardenas, whose supporting members change with each deployment.
He said the cartel deliberately kept Nigerians out of the laboratory to limit exposure, and paid the cooks according to their output.

In the last four months, the NDLEA has dismantled four industrial-scale meth laboratories, in Enugu, the Ogun forest, the Oyo forest and the Ebonyi forest.

Five Mexicans arrested in the earlier operations are in prison custody facing trial. With the latest arrests, ten Mexican meth specialists have been picked up in Nigeria in four months.

Warning to cartels and collaborators, Marwa said:
“Nigeria is not your laboratory. It is not your warehouse, and it is not your transit route,” Marwa warned foreign cartels. “You may change your passports, your names, your flight routes and your entry points, but you cannot change the fact that we are watching.”

To Nigerian collaborators, he said: “You are the greater traitors. You sell out your own country and your own people for profit.” He vowed to arrest and prosecute them and to go after “every naira, every property and every asset” gained from the trade.

He urged landlords, property owners and communities to know who lives in their premises and what they do there, and to report suspicious activity to the nearest NDLEA office, assuring them their identities would be protected.

Marwa commended the SOU, Strike Force, Forensic Directorate, DOGI, Intelligence Directorate and Enugu State Command for their patience and discipline over seven months of surveillance, “without once tipping them off.”

He also thanked the Nigeria Immigration Service, the Agency’s international partners and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for their support.

“The war against illicit drugs is a war for the soul of our nation,” he said. “We will not lose it.”

The post NDLEA busts N303.9bn meth factory in Enugu, arrests kingpin, five Mexican “cooks” appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

Tinubu, who mourned the reported death of the le
content:
• Recalls actor’s iconic portrayal of Okonkwo in ‘Things Fall Apart’

President Bola Tinubu has said veteran Nollywood actor, Chief Pete Edochie, lived well, played his part and left behind a body of work that would preserve his memory for generations.

Tinubu, who mourned the reported death of the legendary actor, said his enduring contributions to the film industry and Nigerian popular culture would continue to resonate long after his passing.

The President stated this in a condolence message he personally signed and issued by the State House on Wednesday.

Reflecting on Edochie’s life and legacy, Tinubu said the actor, popularly known as ‘Ebube Dike’, had earned an enduring place in the history of Nigerian cinema through decades of memorable performances.

“Pete Edochie lived well. He played his part and exited gracefully.

“In his works, he lives forever. Many generations will talk about the life and work of Chief Edochie in the arts industry and academia, in barbershops and marketplaces, and indeed wherever people gather,” he said.

The President recalled Edochie’s unforgettable portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s classic novel, Things Fall Apart, in the 1980s, describing him as an exceptional actor and one of the progenitors of Nollywood.

He also highlighted the actor’s performances in productions such as Igodo, Rituals and Lionheart, which he said helped shape the evolution and international visibility of Nigeria’s film industry.

According to Tinubu, Edochie’s portrayal of traditional institutions, family structures, African values and the complexities of human relationships helped project Nigeria’s cultural heritage and storytelling traditions to audiences worldwide.

Describing him as one of Africa’s most recognisable thespians, the President noted that Edochie was not only an actor but also an administrator, broadcaster and journalist.

“His place in the pantheon of those who shaped the film industry, our common norms, and popular culture remains indisputable,” Tinubu said.

The President, on behalf of his family and the Federal Government, extended condolences to the Edochie family, friends, associates and the entire Nigerian film industry.

He prayed that God Almighty would grant the veteran actor eternal rest.

title: 2027: Akpe, Lokpobiri mobilise Bayelsa West for Tinubu
description:
By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa



YENAGOA — The Deputy Governor of Bayelsa State, Dr Peter Akpe, Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Senator Heineken Lokpobiri, and other political leaders have called on residents of Bayelsa West Senatorial District to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-e
content:
By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa

YENAGOA — The Deputy Governor of Bayelsa State, Dr Peter Akpe, Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Senator Heineken Lokpobiri, and other political leaders have called on residents of Bayelsa West Senatorial District to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in the 2027 general elections.

The leaders made the call during the flag-off of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Bayelsa West sensitisation rally in Aghoro community and Ekeremor town, both in Ekeremor Local Government Area of the state.

Addressing supporters in Ijaw, Akpe said voting for Tinubu and other APC candidates would open new frontiers of development for Bayelsa State.

He commended Governor Douye Diri for defecting from the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) to the APC, describing the decision as timely and beneficial to the state.

The deputy governor urged residents of Ekeremor to vote for APC candidates at all levels, arguing that cooperation between the Federal Government and the state government had contributed to peace and development.

He described the party’s National and State Assembly candidates as qualified, adding that Bayelsa’s greatest economic potential lay in its Atlantic coastline and continental shelf.

Akpe said the Diri administration was committed to extending the Bayelsa West Senatorial Road project to Agge, while the Tinubu administration was executing projects aimed at opening up coastal communities and stimulating economic activities.

“Our biggest wealth, which God has blessed us with, actually lies in the ocean, and what we need to do to harness this wealth has not been done. But the President Tinubu administration is committed and is already doing projects in top gear that will open up our areas,” he said.

He attributed the relative peace in the state to cooperation between the Federal Government and the Bayelsa State Government, both controlled by the APC.

“Today, Bayelsa is one of the most peaceful states in this country because both the Federal Government and the Bayelsa State government are being controlled by the APC and are closely working together. So our primary agenda is to re-elect President Bola Tinubu in 2027,” he added.

Akpe expressed confidence that the senatorial road project would make significant progress before the end of the present administration in 2028.

He called on residents to support all APC candidates, from the presidential ticket to the State House of Assembly.

Also speaking, Lokpobiri urged the people of Bayelsa West to support Tinubu’s re-election, citing his appointment as minister and other federal appointments given to indigenes of the state.

The minister also recalled the zoning arrangement between Ekeremor and Sagbama for the rotation of the senatorial and House of Representatives seats, insisting that it was Ekeremor’s turn to produce the next senator.

Highlighting the achievements of the Tinubu administration, Lokpobiri claimed that Nigeria’s crude oil production had increased from less than one million barrels per day before the administration took office to more than 1.7 million barrels per day.

“Our President is coming back. I am your son. Today, President Tinubu has made your son a minister, and I am the only Ijaw man who is a minister in the Federal Executive Council under the Tinubu administration,” he said.

He urged the people to vote for the APC, citing the presence of Governor Diri and other political leaders from Bayelsa West in the party.

In his remarks, the Deputy Speaker of the Bayelsa State House of Assembly, Hon. Michael Ogbere, said Ekeremor residents had reasons to align politically with Governor Diri, particularly over the proposed extension of the Bayelsa West Senatorial Road project from Ekeremor to Ndoro and Aghoro.

He said the people would support their political leaders, who had expressed commitment to the APC and its candidates.

Other speakers at the rally included former Deputy Governor and Director-General of the APC Bayelsa West Campaign Council, Hon. Peremobowei Ebebi; the state APC Secretary, Mr Japan Udoji; former Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. Boyelayefa Debekeme; and Ekeremor Local Government Chairman, Mr Onniye Isaac.

Others were the Deputy Chief of Staff to the Deputy Governor, Comrade Gowon Toruyouyei; Elder Dimaro Deinyebofa; Hon. Benard Kenebai; Hon. Dein Benadoumene; Mr Orubebe Ogeibiri; Mrs Deme Pamosoo; and Dr Silbriks Obiriki, among other APC stakeholders.

The post 2027: Akpe, Lokpobiri mobilise Bayelsa West for Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Tinubu celebrates Atiku at 80, recalls backing his 2007 presidential bid
description:
President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday congratulated former Vice President and African Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, on his 80th birthday.
Tinubu recalled his support for Atiku’s 2007 presidential bid.

content:
President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday congratulated former Vice President and African Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, on his 80th birthday.

Tinubu recalled his support for Atiku’s 2007 presidential bid.

He said that despite their present political differences, Nigeria’s unity and democratic stability must remain paramount.

Tinubu conveyed his felicitations in a statement he signed Wednesday titled ‘President Tinubu Felicitates ADC Presidential Candidate Atiku Abubakar at 80.’

The President wrote, “I extend my warmest congratulations to former Vice President and African Democratic Congress Presidential Candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, on his 80th birthday today, November 25, 2026.”

He commended Atiku for his contributions to national progress and development over the years.

Tinubu said, “Of particular note are the many years of political engagement and undying commitment to democratic pluralism that I share with him, including my support for his 2007 presidential bid under the defunct Action Congress platform.”

According to him, the support reflected his conviction that democracy thrives when political actors can participate freely, present alternative visions, and contribute to the national conversation on leadership and governance.

The President said his political philosophy had consistently emphasised the need to deepen democracy, strengthen political institutions, respect divergent opinions and sustain an environment where political competition served the larger interests of Nigerians.

Tinubu said, “I have always advocated politics without bitterness and leaving room for reconciliation after differences or disagreements with political opponents.

“Despite our different political affiliations and occasional disagreements, Nigeria’s democracy must continue to benefit from citizens who remain committed to democratic engagement, national development, and the rule of law.”

Tinubu also praised Atiku’s role in business and education.

“Atiku’s contributions to education, entrepreneurship and the private sector are also remarkable. I note his involvement in business development and investments that have created economic opportunities and jobs for our people,” he said.

He described the establishment of the American University of Nigeria, Yola, as of particular significance, saying it had “expanded access to quality higher education and strengthened human capital development.”

Tinubu said, “Although the former number two citizen and I now travel different paths and hold contrasting views on national issues, our shared commitment to Nigeria’s unity and democratic stability must remain paramount.”

The President wished Atiku good health, renewed strength and many more years of service to the nation and humanity as he joins the Octogenarian Club.

“Happy 80th birthday, Your Excellency,” he said.

Atiku was born on November 25, 1946, in Jada, in present-day Adamawa State.

He worked in the Nigeria Customs Service for about two decades before retiring in 1989 to go into business and politics.

The former VP was elected Governor of Adamawa State in 1998 but was sworn in as Vice President in 1999 on the ticket of the Peoples Democratic Party, serving under President Olusegun Obasanjo until 2007.

However, he fell out with Obasanjo over the third-term agenda, left the PDP and ran for president in 2007 on the platform of the Action Congress, the party Tinubu helped lead.

He finished third in the election won by the PDP’s Umaru Yar’Adua.

Atiku is running for the presidency for the seventh time, including in 2019 against the late Muhammadu Buhari and in 2023 against Tinubu, who won the election.

He left the PDP in 2025 and joined the ADC, where he is now the presidential candidate in the 2027 election scheduled for January 16.

He founded the American University of Nigeria in Yola, Adamawa State, in 2003.

The post Tinubu celebrates Atiku at 80, recalls backing his 2007 presidential bid appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Ex-AfDB president proposes $50bn African space development fund
description:
Former President of the African Development Bank, Dr Akinwumi Adesina, has urged President Bola Tinubu and his counterparts in Rwanda and Egypt to provide political leadership for a proposed $50bn investment drive to develop Africa’s space economy.
He also proposed the establishment of an Africa Spa
content:
Former President of the African Development Bank, Dr Akinwumi Adesina, has urged President Bola Tinubu and his counterparts in Rwanda and Egypt to provide political leadership for a proposed $50bn investment drive to develop Africa’s space economy.

He also proposed the establishment of an Africa Space Future Fund to mobilise investments in the continent’s space industry over the next 10 to 15 years.

Adesina identified Tinubu, Rwandan President Paul Kagame and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi as potential founding political anchors of the initiative, citing their countries’ commitments to space development and technological innovation.

According to a statement on Wednesday, Adesina made the proposals at the Africa Space Economy, Innovation and Communication Conference 2026 in Abuja.

He said, “To provide the political leadership and continental standing this initiative deserves, I propose that three African Presidents provide its founding political anchor: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu of Nigeria, President Paul Kagame of Rwanda, and President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi of Egypt.

“Nigeria brings its ambition and growing commitment to space technology. Rwanda brings its experience in technology-driven development and innovation. Egypt brings its established space infrastructure and its role as host of the African Space Agency.”

The proposed fund, according to him, would have an initial capitalisation target of $5bn, with the ambition of mobilising up to $50bn in cumulative investments over the period.

Adesina clarified that the $50bn target was not a request for African governments to contribute the amount from their national budgets, but a long-term investment mobilisation plan.

He said, “To bridge this gap, I propose the establishment of a 5bn and progressively build the fund’s capacity to mobilise up to $`50bn in cumulative investments over 10 to 15 years.

“Let me emphasise that the `$50bn is a long-term investment mobilisation target. It is not a demand for African governments to provide that amount from their national budgets.”

He said the fund would bring together governments, sovereign wealth funds, development finance institutions, pension funds, insurance companies, private investors, international partners and the African diaspora.

The investments, he added, would support infrastructure, research, innovation, manufacturing and commercial space enterprises, with emphasis on African ownership and industrial development.

Adesina stressed the need for an independently governed fund with professional investment management, proper due diligence and transparent accountability.

He also proposed the Africa Link initiative as a flagship continental programme to expand satellite connectivity and strengthen Africa’s capacity to own and operate its digital infrastructure.

According to him, the initiative would begin by aggregating demand, developing shared ground infrastructure and establishing partnerships with satellite operators before progressing to African network operations, technology development, manufacturing and ownership.

Adesina urged African countries to move beyond being consumers of technologies developed elsewhere and position themselves as innovators, manufacturers and investors in the global space economy.

He said, “Africa must move beyond being a consumer of technologies developed elsewhere. We must become innovators, manufacturers, investors and active participants in the global space economy.”

He noted that the global space economy was valued at 1.8tn by 2035, saying Africa needed to increase its investments to benefit from the industry’s growth.

He said the continent should aspire to become one of the world’s leading space economies by 2050.

The former AfDB president maintained that Africa’s participation in the space economy should go beyond acquiring satellites to developing local capabilities, creating businesses and retaining value within the continent.

Africa’s space sector has expanded through the establishment of national space agencies and investments in satellite technology for telecommunications, weather forecasting, agriculture, environmental monitoring and security. However, the continent remains heavily dependent on foreign technology and funding, with limited local capacity in satellite manufacturing and space infrastructure.

title: 2027: ITUC-Africa raises alarm over political killings in Nigeria, INEC register scandal
description:
By Victor Ahiuma-Young



The African Regional Organisation of the International Trade Union Confederation, ITUC-Africa, has raised the alarm over escalating political violence, intimidation and attacks on opposition political parties and their campaigns ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 general elections.The
content:
By Victor Ahiuma-Young

The African Regional Organisation of the International Trade Union Confederation, ITUC-Africa, has raised the alarm over escalating political violence, intimidation and attacks on opposition political parties and their campaigns ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 general elections.
The organisation warned that the growing incidents of killings, assaults and disruption of lawful political gatherings pose a serious threat to Nigeria’s democratic development and could undermine public confidence in the electoral process.
It also expressed concern over fresh allegations of irregularities in the voters’ register in Edo State, calling on the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC,,to subject the register to an independent forensic audit and publicly disclose measures being taken to address identified anomalies.
In a statement by its General Secretary, Akhator Joel Odigie, ITUC-Africa said: “Reports of killings, assaults and disruptions of lawful political gatherings threaten Nigeria’s democratic gains. Global Rights’ October 2026 electoral violence monitoring report indicates that opposition parties constitute the majority of reported targets.

“Democracy cannot thrive where political participation becomes a life-threatening undertaking.

“ITUC-Africa calls on the Federal Government, security agencies, political parties, politicians, candidates, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and the Judiciary to take urgent, transparent and decisive measures to halt this political carnage.

“We acknowledge the assurances given by the Inspector-General of Police on 24 November concerning action against perpetrators of campaign violence. However, these commitments must translate into demonstrable action.

“Security agencies must intensify operations to protect all citizens, candidates and political parties without bias or favouritism. Perpetrators and sponsors of political violence must be investigated and prosecuted, irrespective of their political affiliations or influence.

“Equally disturbing are emerging questions about INEC’s preparedness, impartiality and the integrity of the electoral process.

“On 24 November, MundX Analytics reported that 192,908 voter records in Edo State shared only 9,818 distinct photographs, including blank placeholders. Although these findings require independent verification, they follow INEC’s own acknowledgement in October of irregularities in the preliminary voters’ register, including suspected AI-generated photographs and reported misconduct by registration officers.

“While INEC has undertaken to address identified irregularities before certifying the register on 15 December 2026, the latest findings warrant an independent forensic audit and full public disclosure of corrective measures.

“INEC must demonstrate its independence, ensure a level playing field and address allegations of partisanship. Unresolved electoral irregularities and perceptions of institutional bias risk deepening public distrust and fuelling unrest.

“Political leaders and candidates must renounce violence, restrain their supporters and commit to peaceful campaigns. The Judiciary must act independently, impartially and expeditiously in addressing electoral disputes and ensuring accountability.

“For African workers, democracy remains fundamental to freedom of association, collective bargaining, social justice and human dignity.

“The credibility of elections is not established on polling day alone; it is built through the fairness, transparency and security of the entire electoral process.

“Democracy must be a contest of ideas, not a contest of violence.”

title: ₦1.45trn Lagos ports upgrade targets 20,000 jobs
description:
…As FG flags off Apapa, Tin Can modernisation



By Efe Onodjae



The Federal Government on Wednesday flagged off a £746 million (about ₦1.45 trillion) modernisation of Apapa and Tin Can Island ports in Lagos, targeting 48-hour cargo clearance and the creation of 20,000 direct and indirect jobs.
content:
…As FG flags off Apapa, Tin Can modernisation

By Efe Onodjae

The Federal Government on Wednesday flagged off a £746 million (about ₦1.45 trillion) modernisation of Apapa and Tin Can Island ports in Lagos, targeting 48-hour cargo clearance and the creation of 20,000 direct and indirect jobs.

The project is expected to reduce cargo delays, lower logistics costs and improve Nigeria’s competitiveness in global trade.

Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Dr Adegboyega Oyetola, who performed the groundbreaking at Tin Can Island Port, said the upgrade had become urgent as cargo throughput had outgrown existing port infrastructure.

Oyetola said Nigeria’s cargo throughput had increased from 8.11 million metric tonnes in 1977 to 129.3 million metric tonnes, while merchandise trade had risen from $17 billion to over $100 billion annually.

He said the project would involve rehabilitation of quay walls and berths, dredging of navigation channels, improved access facilities and installation of modern cargo-handling equipment.

According to him, cargo dwell time at Nigerian ports had historically ranged between 10 and 18 days, compared with three to five days at leading international ports, costing the economy an estimated $4 billion annually.

He said the upgrade would attract international shipping lines, retain Nigerian-bound cargo and expand transshipment opportunities.

Also speaking, Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr Taiwo Oyedele, described the project as Nigeria’s largest sovereign export credit transaction since 2009.

He said the financing arrangement demonstrated international investor confidence in Nigeria’s economic reforms.

Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority, NPA, Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, assured that the project would be delivered in line with approved designs, engineering standards and contractual timelines.

title: Tinubu pledges to rescue abducted Borno schoolchildren
description:
By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri



MAIDUGURI — President Bola Tinubu has pledged that his administration will do everything possible to secure the release of about 70 schoolchildren abducted from Mussa Primary School and Government Technical School, Lassa, in Askira-Uba Local Government Area of Borno Sta
content:
By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri

MAIDUGURI — President Bola Tinubu has pledged that his administration will do everything possible to secure the release of about 70 schoolchildren abducted from Mussa Primary School and Government Technical School, Lassa, in Askira-Uba Local Government Area of Borno State.

Tinubu made the pledge on Wednesday in Maiduguri while addressing supporters at the All Progressives Congress (APC) North-East Zonal Rally held at the El-Kanemi Sports Centre.

The President said his administration remained committed to rescuing the children abducted by suspected Boko Haram terrorists and defeating insurgency in the North-East.

“We shall do everything possible to rescue the schoolchildren abducted in Mussa and Lassa communities,” he said.

The abductions, which occurred in the first quarter of 2026, involved more than 30 children, including toddlers, from Mussa and over 40 students from Lassa.

Tinubu also acknowledged the sacrifices of military personnel and other security operatives, particularly those serving on the frontline, assuring them of government support in the fight against terrorism.

“The present administration under my leadership acknowledges the sacrifices of troops, especially those at the frontline. Therefore, government would do its best to support our security operatives to defeat terrorism in this region,” he said.

On his second-term ambition, the President thanked the people of the North-East for their support for the APC-led administration, promising to consolidate on its achievements if re-elected in 2027.

He described Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who hails from Borno State, as a dependable ally and commended Governor Babagana Zulum for his administration’s development efforts.

Tinubu particularly cited the newly constructed International Conference Centre in Maiduguri and other projects he commissioned during his visit.

Earlier, Zulum thanked the President for choosing Maiduguri as the venue for the zonal rally, expressing satisfaction with the large turnout and orderly conduct of APC supporters.

He said Borno State had benefited significantly from the Federal Government’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

The governor disclosed that the Federal Government had commenced construction of the Gombe-Biu-Maiduguri road, while also highlighting the establishment of the Federal Polytechnic, Monguno; Federal College of Education, Gwoza; and Federal University of Agriculture and Entrepreneurship, Bama.

Zulum urged residents of Borno and other states in the North-East to vote for APC candidates at all levels in the 2027 general elections.

The rally attracted seven governors from the region, including Mai Mala Buni of Yobe State.

Also in attendance were the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu; wife of the Vice-President, Nana Shettima; former governors; ministers; members of the National Assembly and other APC stakeholders.

The post Tinubu pledges to rescue abducted Borno schoolchildren appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Raheem Sterling handed 12-month suspended prison sentence for dangerous driving
description:
Former England footballer Raheem Sterling was Wednesday given a 12-month suspended prison sentence for dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide after crashing his Lamborghini.



The 31-year-old was also ordered to complete 100 hours’ unpaid work and was banned from driving for 24 months du
content:
Former England footballer Raheem Sterling was Wednesday given a 12-month suspended prison sentence for dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide after crashing his Lamborghini.

The 31-year-old was also ordered to complete 100 hours’ unpaid work and was banned from driving for 24 months during the sentencing hearing at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court.

Sterling pleaded guilty in September to driving a Lamborghini Urus dangerously on May 28, 2026.

He also admitted possession of six nitrous oxide canisters for wrongful inhalation, a class C drug, and failing to provide a specimen.

Sterling’s sentence is suspended for 18 months.

The former Manchester City forward had been seen by other motorists inhaling from a balloon while driving his black sports car, swerving in and out of lanes, a court previously heard.

Dashcam footage released by the Crown Prosecution Service shows a black Lamborghini switching lanes multiple times before hitting a concrete barrier.

Sterling won 82 England caps, the last of which came at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

The winger, currently without a club, made his senior debut at Liverpool before joining City in 2015, winning four Premier League titles.

He left for Chelsea in 2022 but subsequently fell out of favour and spent the 2024/25 season on loan at Arsenal.

Sterling joined Feyenoord on a short-term deal in February, playing eight times in the Eredivisie, but left at the end of the season.

title: Igboho directive: You owe Nigerians explanation – Atiku’s camp tells Tinubu
description:
The camp of presidential candidate of African Democratic Congress (ADC), Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, has asked President Bola Tinubu to address Nigerians over Sunday Igboho’s claim that he directed him and his security network to sustain operations across the South-West.
Paul Ibe, media adviser to Atiku,
content:
The camp of presidential candidate of African Democratic Congress (ADC), Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, has asked President Bola Tinubu to address Nigerians over Sunday Igboho’s claim that he directed him and his security network to sustain operations across the South-West.

Paul Ibe, media adviser to Atiku, made the demand in a social media post on Wednesday.

The demand followed a statement issued on Monday by Igboho’s media office in Ibadan, Oyo State, claiming that Tinubu gave the charge during a brief meeting with the Iru Ekun Security Network founder inside his official car shortly after the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally at Mapo Hall in Ibadan on Saturday.

According to that statement, Tinubu instructed Igboho to continue working with security agencies to ensure peace and stability in the South-West, and to sustain operations in rural communities, urban centres and forests in Yorubaland against terrorists from neighbouring African countries.

Igboho was quoted as saying, “After the Ibadan Presidential Campaign Council rally on Saturday, President Bola Tinubu called me into his car and instructed me to continue working with security agencies to ensure peace and stability of the South-West.”

He also claimed the president directed the network to monitor terrains to prevent infiltration by terrorists from Lake Chad, Mali and other African countries, and to provide security to all Nigerians within its jurisdictions regardless of ethnic, religious and political divides, while informing security agencies ahead of its operations.

Reacting, Ibe said, “President Tinubu owes Nigerians an explanation over Sunday Igboho’s claim that he directed him and his security network to sustain operations across the South-West.”

He asked, “Did the President issue that directive? If so, under what legal framework? Who supervises this network, defines its operational limits and holds its members accountable?”

Ibe said community cooperation is essential to effective security, but providing intelligence to lawful authorities is different from receiving a personal presidential mandate to conduct security operations.

“Even accepting Igboho’s account that the President requested cooperation with established agencies and protection for all Nigerians, those assurances do not answer the fundamental questions of authority, training, command and accountability,” Atiku’s media aide added.

He warned that Nigeria’s security cannot rest on private understandings reached on the sidelines of a political rally, nor should presidential access become a substitute for transparent institutional responsibility.

Ibe urged the president to prioritise properly equipped, adequately funded and accountable police, military and other statutory security agencies, and to ensure that where community-based initiatives assist them, their responsibilities are clearly defined, lawful and subject to effective supervision.

He said an opaque arrangement with an organisation led by a Yoruba Nation campaigner risks blurring the distinction between community protection and ethnic mobilisation, a legitimate concern the presidency must address.

He said, “An opaque arrangement with an organisation led by a Yoruba nation campaigner risks blurring the distinction between community protection and ethnic mobilisation.

“If Igboho has misrepresented the discussion, the Presidency should correct the record. If his account is accurate, Nigerians deserve full disclosure of the arrangement and its safeguards.

“Every community deserves protection. Every security operation demands accountability. Mr President, strengthen the institutions entrusted with protecting Nigerians. Do not create uncertainty about who exercises coercive authority in their name.”

The post Igboho directive: You owe Nigerians explanation – Atiku’s camp tells Tinubu appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Adeleke presents ₦927bn 2027 budget to assembly
description:
Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has presented a proposed budget of ₦927.37 billion for the 2027 fiscal year to the State House of Assembly, describing it as the Budget of Advanced Commitment and Expansion.
In a post obtained from the state’s X handle, Adeleke presented the budget on Wednesday,
content:
Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has presented a proposed budget of ₦927.37 billion for the 2027 fiscal year to the State House of Assembly, describing it as the Budget of Advanced Commitment and Expansion.

In a post obtained from the state’s X handle, Adeleke presented the budget on Wednesday, outlining plans to prioritise infrastructure development, human capital growth, agriculture, security, workers’ welfare and job creation.

The governor said the proposed budget was designed in line with the reviewed Osun State Development Plans (2023–2050), with a focus on improving the state’s economy and expanding development across various sectors.

“The size of the proposed budget is ₦927,370,584,800 for the 2027 fiscal year. I tag it ‘Budget of Advanced Commitment and Expansion’,” he said.

Breaking down the revenue projections, Adeleke said the state expected ₦400.93 billion from its share of the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC), while internally generated revenue was projected at ₦250.17 billion.

He added that the government expected ₦230.65 billion in receipts from development partners.

On expenditure, the governor proposed ₦130.01 billion for personnel costs, including salaries, allowances, pensions and gratuities, while ₦238.05 billion was earmarked for overhead costs.

The sum of ₦559.31 billion was allocated to capital projects and developmental initiatives across the state.

Adeleke disclosed that the budget maintained a 40:60 ratio between recurrent and capital expenditure, with capital spending accounting for 60 per cent of the total proposal.

He said the budget was formulated to improve the ease of doing business, promote employment, enhance youth development, strengthen human capital and accelerate infrastructure expansion.

Highlighting the administration’s priorities for the 2027 fiscal year, the governor listed infrastructure, human capital development, revitalisation of agriculture, security, workers’ and pensioners’ welfare, and job creation.

Adeleke also commended the State House of Assembly for its cooperation with the executive arm, describing the relationship as instrumental to his administration’s achievements over the past four years.

“Our partnership was responsible for the tremendous progress and achievements of this administration in the last four years. We must further strengthen this relationship,” he said.

The governor assured residents that his administration would accelerate its development agenda, adding that the proposed budget was aimed at taking the state to greater heights.

He subsequently laid the ₦927.37 billion budget proposal before the House of Assembly for consideration and approval.Adeleke unveils ₦927bn budget for 2027

title: Ekiti varsity chancellor seeks increased investment in teacher education
description:
Business leader and Chancellor of Ekiti State University, Dr Tunji Olowolafe, has called for sustained investment in teacher education, saying Nigeria’s dual-mandate NCE-degree programme could help restore the prestige of the teaching profession and strengthen the country’s education system.
Olowola
content:
Business leader and Chancellor of Ekiti State University, Dr Tunji Olowolafe, has called for sustained investment in teacher education, saying Nigeria’s dual-mandate NCE-degree programme could help restore the prestige of the teaching profession and strengthen the country’s education system.

Olowolafe made the call while delivering the 2026 convocation lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology, Omu-Ajose, Ogun State, on Monday.

The lecture was themed, “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria.”

He described the reform, enabled by the Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 and operationalised in May 2025, as the most significant structural change in teacher education since the Ashby Commission of 1959.

The programme allows eligible colleges of education to award both the Nigeria Certificate in Education and bachelor’s degrees through a five-year pathway designed to combine practical teaching skills with academic training.

However, Olowolafe warned that granting institutions autonomy would not, on its own, guarantee the programme’s success, stressing the need for sustained funding, curriculum reform and the integration of technology.

He also highlighted Nigeria’s estimated one-million-teacher shortfall, warning that the country must prepare its teaching workforce for a growing population of school-age children.

“Nearly eight million babies will be born in Nigeria this year alone. In 2032, those children will walk into Primary One classrooms across this country,” he said.

The EKSU chancellor also identified the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 as an opportunity to strengthen education financing through the Tertiary Education Trust Fund and the Nigerian Education Loan Fund.

He said NELFUND had disbursed more than ₦372bn to over one million students for tuition and upkeep, urging the SACOETEC management to help eligible students access the loan scheme.

On curriculum development, Olowolafe advocated the early integration of vocational skills, coding and digital literacy into education.

He said artificial intelligence should complement rather than replace the human qualities required of teachers.

“AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said.

He added that honesty, fairness, empathy and civic responsibility remained essential values that teachers must impart to learners.

As part of efforts to support education infrastructure, the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation announced plans to establish a GOMTECH centre at SACOETEC.

The solar-powered information and communications technology centre will be equipped with high-speed internet facilities, with the foundation expected to fund, power and co-manage it with the college.

The initiative builds on the foundation’s existing digital education projects, including Project Digi-Teach at EKSU, which aims to certify all 650 lecturers in digital and AI-enabled teaching.

It also operates a GOMTECH centre in Are-Ekiti, where rural schoolchildren, university students and teachers receive training in artificial intelligence, coding, graphic design and Mandarin Chinese.

The foundation further pledged to recognise academic excellence at the college by honouring first-class degree graduates, NCE distinction holders and the overall best graduates in both categories.

Lecturers selected through student ratings will also receive recognition for their contributions to teaching.

Addressing the graduating students, Olowolafe urged them to embrace lifelong learning, drawing on his transition from medical training to entrepreneurship and academia.

He cited former Nigerian leaders Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa, Shehu Shagari and Chief Obafemi Awolowo, who had teaching backgrounds, as examples of the profession’s contribution to national leadership.

“Your training is a launchpad, not a ceiling,” he told the graduates, urging them to remain connected to their alma mater and contribute to the development of future generations.

title: New Abia CP seeks public cooperation to tackle crime
description:
The new Commissioner of Police in Abia State, Sylvester Edogbanya Adaji, has called for increased public cooperation and credible intelligence to tackle crime and strengthen security across the state.
Adaji made the call on Wednesday in Umuahia while officially taking over the leadership of the Abia
content:
The new Commissioner of Police in Abia State, Sylvester Edogbanya Adaji, has called for increased public cooperation and credible intelligence to tackle crime and strengthen security across the state.

Adaji made the call on Wednesday in Umuahia while officially taking over the leadership of the Abia State Police Command from his predecessor, now Assistant Inspector-General of Police, Wilfred Afolabi.

The new police commissioner said effective policing would be difficult without th
e support of residents, urging members of the public to bridge the trust gap between the police and communities by providing timely and actionable information.

“It is always difficult to police a lawless society. Nigerians, most of Nigerians, are very lawless. Lawless in the fact that the individual is quite rich and stronger than the institution that ought to control them,” he said.

Adaji, however, stressed that the police would remain committed to enforcing the law while respecting the fundamental rights of citizens.

He emphasised that information sharing was essential to effective policing, noting that the command would build on existing intelligence-gathering structures and strengthen public confidence in the police.

“Without information, organic and inorganic information from members of the public-spirited individuals of Abia, we cannot function very well,” he stated.

He added that rebuilding trust between police personnel and residents would encourage people to provide credible information capable of helping security agencies prevent and investigate crimes.

The commissioner also promised to strengthen collaboration with other security service commanders in the state, expressing confidence that cooperation and collective responsibility would improve security.

Commending Afolabi for his achievements during his tenure, Adaji assured residents that his administration would prioritise the fight against crime and criminality.

“For the health and safety of Abia and Abians, I have not come here to sleep only. I have not come here to do any other thing. I have come here to do police work,” he declared.

He further assured residents that the command remained committed to protecting lives and property, describing the responsibility as a fundamental duty under the Constitution, the Police Act and other relevant laws.

The new CP also promised increased police visibility during the festive season, announcing plans for heavy deployment to ensure that social and economic activities continued without interruption.

“You know, we are in the festive season. You are going to see heavy police deployment and visibility policing,” he said.

In his remarks, the outgoing commissioner, AIG Wilfred Afolabi, highlighted some of the strategies introduced during his administration to improve security in the state.

He listed divisional intelligence operations, intelligence-led policing, crime mapping, crime timing and crime prevention initiatives among the measures adopted by the command.

Afolabi also disclosed that personnel from various divisions had received training in intelligence gathering and crime analysis, while the command strengthened its cybercrime unit and introduced comparative crime analysis and statistics.

He, however, drew attention to some challenges confronting the command, including the poor condition of police vehicles, inadequate radio communication facilities and the lack of perimeter fencing at several police stations.

Other issues he highlighted included the need to fortify police facilities, train and retrain personnel and strengthen discipline within the force.

Sunday Nwakanma

The new Commissioner of Police in Abia State, Sylvester Edogbanya Adaji, has called for increased public cooperation and credible intelligence to tackle crime and strengthen security across the state.

Adaji made the call on Wednesday in Umuahia while officially taking over the leadership of the Abia State Police Command from his predecessor, now Assistant Inspector-General of Police, Wilfred Afolabi.

The new police commissioner said effective policing would be difficult without the support of residents, urging members of the public to bridge the trust gap between the police and communities by providing timely and actionable information.

“It is always difficult to police a lawless society. Nigerians, most of Nigerians, are very lawless. Lawless in the fact that the individual is quite rich and stronger than the institution that ought to control them,” he said.

Adaji, however, stressed that the police would remain committed to enforcing the law while respecting the fundamental rights of citizens.

He emphasised that information sharing was essential to effective policing, noting that the command would build on existing intelligence-gathering structures and strengthen public confidence in the police.

“Without information, organic and inorganic information from members of the public-spirited individuals of Abia, we cannot function very well,” he stated.

He added that rebuilding trust between police personnel and residents would encourage people to provide credible information capable of helping security agencies prevent and investigate crimes.

The commissioner also promised to strengthen collaboration with other security service commanders in the state, expressing confidence that cooperation and collective responsibility would improve security.

Commending Afolabi for his achievements during his tenure, Adaji assured residents that his administration would prioritise the fight against crime and criminality.

“For the health and safety of Abia and Abians, I have not come here to sleep only. I have not come here to do any other thing. I have come here to do police work,” he declared.

He further assured residents that the command remained committed to protecting lives and property, describing the responsibility as a fundamental duty under the Constitution, the Police Act and other relevant laws.

The new CP also promised increased police visibility during the festive season, announcing plans for heavy deployment to ensure that social and economic activities continued without interruption.

“You know, we are in the festive season. You are going to see heavy police deployment and visibility policing,” he said.

In his remarks, the outgoing commissioner, AIG Wilfred Afolabi, highlighted some of the strategies introduced during his administration to improve security in the state.

He listed divisional intelligence operations, intelligence-led policing, crime mapping, crime timing and crime prevention initiatives among the measures adopted by the command.

Afolabi also disclosed that personnel from various divisions had received training in intelligence gathering and crime analysis, while the command strengthened its cybercrime unit and introduced comparative crime analysis and statistics.

He, however, drew attention to some challenges confronting the command, including the poor condition of police vehicles, inadequate radio communication facilities and the lack of perimeter fencing at several police stations.

Other issues he highlighted included the need to fortify police facilities, train and retrain personnel and strengthen discipline within the force.

Adaji pledged to build on the existing strategies while working with officers, residents and other security agencies to improve safety across the state.
