title: 2027 election: NSCDC CG flags off 3-day training, says Corps committed to free, fair poll
description: Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Commandant General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Dr. Ahmed Abubakar Audi, mni, OFR, has declared open a three-day training workshop for senior management officers of the Corps drawn from across the country, with the theme: “Role of
content:
Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Commandant General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Dr. Ahmed Abubakar Audi, mni, OFR, has declared open a three-day training workshop for senior management officers of the Corps drawn from across the country, with the theme: “Role of Security Agencies in the Conduct of General Elections in Nigeria: Legal, Institutional and Strategic Command Perspective.”

The workshop, held today 25th of November 2026 at the General Abdulrahman Dambazau Hall, Nigerian Correctional Service Headquarters, Airport Road, Abuja, is aimed at ensuring the Corps is fully prepared for the task ahead and to guarantee a smooth electoral process in 2027.

Declaring the workshop open, CG Audi, who demonstrated discipline by taking attendance of participants, disclosed that the training was necessary to ensure the Corps and its officers are ready to deliver a credible 2027 general election and to align with global best practices. He noted that tactical commanders and junior officers had undergone a similar three-day training last month, hence the decision to train senior officers who would be in charge of giving instructions during the election.

“The responsibility of making the election free and fair lies within the security agencies and we are ready to play our part without prejudice. We must follow the three C’s; Coordination, Collaboration and Cooperation and we must adhere to them. We must respect the fundamental rights of citizens, as no room would be given for anybody who constitutionally violates anybody. Anybody who goes against the law guiding us would be shown the way out,” he said.

“We must ensure neutrality and remain non-partisan. We must strengthen our communication channels and ensure they align with national security guidelines. We must never lag in discharging our duties. We must avoid any misfortune and all operations must be reported to the National Headquarters. We must contribute meaningfully to the success of the election.”

The CG stressed that the training is essential to protecting electoral materials and engaging based on the rules of engagement. “We want to ensure the election is free and fair. This training will help increase capacity; it will help officers know how to handle situations and de-escalate issues so as to ensure everyone; including electoral staff from INEC and sensitive materials is protected, which is one of the core mandates of the agency.”

The Minister of Interior, Hon. Dr. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, who was ably represented by Alhaja Adaji Asman, Director of Joint Services, Ministry of Interior, declared the workshop open and charged personnel to be conversant with relevant laws, the code of conduct and rules of engagement. He emphasized that officers must respect the division of responsibility arrest and prosecution in line with electoral law and must ensure their statutory mandate to protect critical national assets and infrastructure, including INEC offices, INEC collation centres, INEC workers and power lines, among others.

“We must ensure synergy with other sister agencies; nobody should work in isolation. We must ensure cooperation with sister agencies to quench any possible threat to the electoral process. We demand a high standard of neutrality, remain non-partisan and remain loyal to the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria,” the Minister said.

The facilitator of the three-day training, Alnas Consulting Limited, represented by Prof. Nasirdeen Usman, said the training is based on practical classes that will help officers stay afloat and remain in tune with the rules of engagement, ensuring they are well trained to carry out their duties in tandem with global best practices. He disclosed that participants would be trained in crisis management, human management, de-escalation of issues, protection of materials and the use of force when required. “The training will further strengthen the agency on its core role,” he added.

In his remarks, Brigadier General Buba Marwa, represented by ACGN Abubakar Idris Ahmed, Director of Asset and Financial Investigations, disclosed that those who would distort the electoral process are likely to be drug users and he has instructed his men to raid all drug black spots across the country to ensure they are drug-free.

“This election is a very serious business and we must make it drug-free because those planning to disrupt it would want to be high on several substances. When we raid those drugs and prevent them from getting to the end users, election violence would be reduced drastically. We are very aware and we are on top of our game to ensure drugs are off the street and to keep Nigeria safe before and after the election,” he said.

Comptroller Dauda Ikharo, who represented the Comptroller General of Immigration, Kemi Nana Nandap, said the Nigerian Immigration Service is ready to share intelligence and provide support to ensure the election is free and fair. “We are ready for institutional synergy, to reduce cross-border migration that would disrupt the election. We are ready to engage in collaboration and also for joint patrol,” he said.

NSCDC DCG Intelligence & investigation, Dr Nnamdi Nwinyi, disclosed that the training is very essential and is coming at the best time. “The expectation of our personnel is to engage in strategy and operational readiness. We are following electoral law, strengthening our intelligence and also preparing for post-election crisis management. We must be professional enough to ensure every Nigerian performs their civic right without fear,” he said.

The Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), represented by Assistant Aliyu Bello of the Asset and Financial Investigation Department, disclosed that the workshop is very needed and that the DSS and its leadership are ready to synergize with all sister agencies in sharing intelligence to ensure a hitch-free election. He added that the agency is open to operational collaboration to ensure the election is free and that those who would vote are well protected.

The mission disclosed this in an announcement on its official Instagram account on Wedn
content:
By Enitan Abdultawab

The United States Mission in Nigeria has announced a two-day shutdown of its embassy in Abuja and consulate general in Lagos in observance of the country’s Thanksgiving holiday.

The mission disclosed this in an announcement on its official Instagram account on Wednesday, November 25, stating that both facilities would be closed on Thursday, November 26, and Friday, November 27, 2026.

The closure means that consular services and other official activities at the two diplomatic offices will be unavailable during the period.

Visa applicants, travellers and members of the public with appointments or enquiries scheduled for the affected dates will be unable to access services at the facilities.

The public is therefore advised to take note of the closure and plan visits accordingly, with normal operations expected to resume the following week.

Thanksgiving is a federal public holiday in the United States, observed annually on the fourth Thursday of November.

The holiday is traditionally marked by family gatherings and expressions of gratitude, while US diplomatic missions around the world typically suspend official operations in observance of it.

content:
By Adeola Badru

IBADAN — The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Oyo State has dismissed reports that its governorship candidate, Senator Sharafadeen Alli, plans to sack government workers or deny them salaries and other entitlements if elected governor in 2027.

The party described the reports as a campaign of calumny allegedly orchestrated by some elements within the ruling Allied Peoples Movement (APM) to mislead the public and discredit its candidate ahead of the governorship election.

Instead, the APC promised that an Alli administration would prioritise workers’ welfare through timely payment of salaries and allowances, regular promotions, improved working conditions and access to training opportunities.

The party’s position was contained in a statement issued on Wednesday by its Publicity Secretary, Olawale Sadare, and made available to journalists in Ibadan.

The statement followed media reports alleging that Alli would disengage a large number of government workers and deny others prompt payment of their salaries and wages if elected governor.

The APC questioned the credibility of the reports, noting that they did not identify their sources, and accused some APM members of sponsoring them to undermine Alli’s governorship ambition.

According to the party, the APC candidate has already outlined his plans for workers and other residents of the state in his campaign manifesto, unveiled in Ibadan a few weeks ago.

“For the avoidance of doubt, Sen. Alli has explained how he would better the lot of the people of Oyo State (including government workers) in the campaign manifesto which was released in Ibadan a few weeks ago,” the statement said.

The party argued that increased monthly allocations from the Federal Government had made it difficult to justify the non-payment of workers’ salaries and pensioners’ entitlements by state and local governments.

It promised that, if elected, Alli would establish a new relationship between government and workers, anchored on improved welfare and recognition of their contributions to the development of the state.

The APC said serving and retired civil and public servants would begin to enjoy improved conditions from May 29, 2027, when Alli is expected to assume office if elected.

It listed workers in ministries, departments and agencies, public school teachers, academic and non-academic staff of tertiary institutions, and local government employees among the beneficiaries of the proposed reforms.

The party also pledged workplace safety, a conducive working environment and greater involvement of workers in the formulation and implementation of policies affecting them.

It further promised to end what it described as the imposition of “shylock consultants” on government workers, while providing opportunities for periodic training and retraining programmes locally and overseas.

The APC also assured workers that promotions and financial entitlements would not be withheld.

“Apart from the guarantee of safety at workplace and conducive working environment, the APC government of Sen. Alli would break the yoke of alienation and deprivation which the Makinde administration has placed on government workers in the state as they would be carried along and allowed to do their job without forcing shylock consultants on them,” the statement said.

Beyond workers’ welfare, the party pledged prudent management of public funds and equitable distribution of infrastructure projects across the state’s 33 local government areas.

It also promised to respect local government autonomy, which it alleged had been undermined by the present administration of Governor Seyi Makinde.

The APC, however, urged the APM to desist from what it described as the spread of falsehoods and attacks against its leaders and other prominent personalities.

It specifically cautioned the party against sponsoring reports aimed at discrediting President Bola Tinubu, Alli and other APC leaders.

The statement warned that those allegedly responsible for the reports could face the consequences of their actions.

title: Nollywood Stars Joke Silva, Funke Akindele, Others Pay Tribute To Pete Edochie
description:

The actor’s death was announced by his son, Chief Leo Pete Edochie, who confirmed th
content:
Nollywood stars Joke Silva, Funke Akindele, Mercy Johnson and others have paid tributes to veteran actor Pete Edochie, who died Wednesday after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer at the age of 79.

The actor’s death was announced by his son, Chief Leo Pete Edochie, who confirmed that he died at 12:30 a.m. on November 25, 2026, in Enugu, Nigeria.

His death has sparked an outpouring of tributes from colleagues, public leaders and entertainers who have celebrated his remarkable career, influence and legacy.

Actress Joke Silva expressed sadness over his death, remembering his playful side.

“Uncle Pete…I will miss your teasing. Rest well Sir,” she wrote.

Filmmaker and actress Funke Akindele recalled growing up watching Edochie in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart, before eventually sharing the screen with him in the film Egg of Life.

She expressed gratitude for his encouragement and the impact he made on younger generations of actors.

“Thank you for paving the way for so many of us in Nollywood and for being an inspiration to us over the years. Your work lives on,” she wrote.

Similarly, actress Uche Jombo described Edochie as one of Nollywood’s greatest pillars, a master of his craft and a custodian of Nigerian culture.

She said the late actor “gave Nigerian storytelling a face, a voice and a legacy that will outlive generations.”

“His contribution to Nollywood cannot be measured by the number of films he appeared in, but by the impact he made, the standards he set and the generations of actors he inspired.”

Actress Omoni Oboli described his passing as the fall of an iroko tree, writing, “Hmmm 2026! It is well. The Iroko has fallen. Rest in power sir Pete Edochie.”

May Edochie, the estranged wife of the late actor’s son, Yul Edochie, also paid tribute, describing him as an institution and a father figure to many.

She reflected on the false reports of his death that had circulated over the years, noting that he had continued working despite the rumours.

Actor Charles Inojie paid tribute using several of the late actor’s traditional praise names, including Ebube Dike, Ntu Mara Igwe and King of the Forests, before praying for his peaceful rest.

While DJ Kaywise thanked him for his contributions to the industry, other entertainers who expressed their grief included comedian Sabinus, who described Edochie as an oracle and a legend.

Pete Edochie was born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State. His ancestral roots, however, trace back to Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, in Anambra State.

Edochie rose to prominence through his portrayal of Okonkwo in the 1987 Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart. His commanding screen presence, distinctive voice, and memorable delivery of traditional proverbs subsequently made him one of Nollywood’s most recognisable figures.

Beyond his acting career, Edochie was also celebrated for his contributions to broadcasting and his influence on generations of Nigerian actors.

He is survived by his wife, Barrister Josephine Edochie, with whom he had six children, including actors Yul and Linc Edochie.

title: Ebola Fight Runs Up Against Customs, Rites In Remote DR Congo
description: For health workers in the volatile eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), tackling local suspicions is as big a problem as combating the Ebola virus that has plagued it for six months.In the rural community of Bulambo-Isale, AFP saw a small crowd gather this week along a dirt track, determined
content:
For health workers in the volatile eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), tackling local suspicions is as big a problem as combating the Ebola virus that has plagued it for six months.

In the rural community of Bulambo-Isale, AFP saw a small crowd gather this week along a dirt track, determined to prevent an ambulance bringing the body of a local Ebola victim for burial.

Victims of the highly contagious haemorrhagic fever, which spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids, must be interred in sealed body bags to prevent infection spreading from the corpse.

Burial ceremonies are conducted by specially trained health workers, anonymous in protective hazmat suits, some of whom locals allege are brought in from outside the community and do not speak the local languages.

But custom dictates that the deceased be buried by their own family and their body be allowed to fuse with the earth of their ancestors.

“The authorities have imposed the Ebola response on locals without first making sure how they interpret it,” grumbled Patricien Kambale, who became a livestock farmer after university.

“The sick victim gets carted away in a vehicle and locals don’t know where they’re being taken. Then we learn later that the person has died so locals think the doctors are using poisoned medicine to kill people,” he said.

Suspicions of ‘profiteering’

Locals say they are distrustful of Congolese authorities, who have a reputation for corruption and nepotism.

Left to cope with the miseries inflicted by myriad armed groups that have stalked their mineral-rich region for more than three decades, they fear their customs and lives matter little to the powers that be.

Wilson Kasyani, chief doctor for the Vuhovi health district that includes Bulambo-Isale, a rural settlement in North Kivu province, was worried for the ambulance and its occupants.

“Weapons are everywhere” in the mountainous region, he said.

Medical workers face almost daily attacks due to locals’ hostility to efforts to respond to the Ebola outbreak, which has killed more than 5,000 people out of more than 11,000 cases since May.

“Today, people entered a nurse’s home and wounded her son,” Kasyani said wearily.

“And yesterday we had to stop someone who wanted to attack investigators with a machete.”

Roland Vivaya, head of the local youth council, said “most people” in Bulambo-Isale “don’t believe Ebola exists”.

He admitted he hadn’t “really” believed himself until he almost died of the virus.

Vivaya said the difficulty was not so much defiance but locals not understanding — despite memories of the last Ebola outbreak between 2018 and 2000.

The image at the time of “doctors protected by the military, scared the community”, Kambale said.

No vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, responsible for the current outbreak.

“How can you explain to locals — many of whom have never been to school — why there’s this sudden focus on this disease, when we’ve been dying for decades from the conflicts here,” Vivaya said.

“Personally, I only understood the virus when I had to go to the treatment centre, because they put on information sessions. But these meetings don’t get the message across to everyone,” he added ruefully.

Suspicions stem, in part, from health workers having not been trained in local customs or languages, leading to “resistance” among locals, he said.

“They think it might be some kind of profiteering,” Vivaya added.

Communicate with the dead

Bulambo-Isale is the cultural and religious heart of the Nande people, one of the eastern DRC’s largest ethnic groups.

From his palm-frond hut, blackened by wood smoke, traditional chief Pimbo Kakule watches, pipe clenched between his teeth, over one of Bulambo-Isale’s 12 sacred hills.

As in many rural communities affected by Ebola, the fight to staunch its spread runs up against ancient traditions.

“Our people believe there is life after death and our customs must be respected when a person is buried. Otherwise we think they’ve been sacrificed,” he said.

Nande custom dictates that a person should be buried by their family and their corpse enter the soil of their ancestors so the living can speak to them in the afterlife.

“A person who isn’t able to communicate with their dead can’t get into heaven,” Kakule said.

He said there were better ways to manage the issue than the current top-down approach.

“If we were to say: ‘Your brother’s died. We’re going to teach you how to bury him,’ we might reach an agreement and there wouldn’t be all this tension,” he said.

“We are fighting the disease, not the response teams.”

Top down or bottom up

The salaries that some locally recruited people are offered for joining the Ebola fight is also a source of mistrust.

Their wages, higher than the local average, feed jealousy and conspiracy theories.

When Kambale was vaccinated in 2020 against the Zaire strain of Ebola, responsible for the epidemic of the time, his neighbours accused him of taking a bribe in order to spread the virus and threatened to torch his house.

“Even protecting yourself has become a problem,” he said.

“Pressure groups” made up of members of youth organisations linked to local politicians, weaponise the tensions and sometimes prevent health workers reaching sick people.

In Vuhovi, such incidents are often the work of troublemakers who feel marginalised, said Salama Mwengesyali, who coordinates public Ebola information sessions.

“If we could bring all these individuals in, train them and get them involved in tackling Ebola, we could overcome this resistance,” the soft-spoken woman said.

“What we lack are the means to do that.”

Mwengesyali said her team lacked money to “motivate” locals in rural farming communities to attend lengthy Ebola information sessions, or pay health workers to ring them or travel to where they live.

“It’s come down to us having to go door to door to plead for body bags,” concurred Kasyani, the doctor.

Their Ebola treatment centre is cobbled together from planks of wood where patients “put up with intolerable conditions”, he said.

Two patients have run away in recent days.

“People tell themselves that if they go there, they’re going to die.”

The organisation also disclosed that 23.4 per cent of wo
content:
By Gabriel Ewepu

ABUJA — Oxfam Nigeria has raised the alarm over the prevalence of gender-based violence in the country, disclosing that more than one in five Nigerian women aged 15 to 49 have experienced physical or sexual violence.

The organisation also disclosed that 23.4 per cent of women in Nigeria had experienced intimate partner violence, while the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) recorded 84,187 complaints of domestic violence in 2024.

Oxfam’s Country Director in Nigeria, Tijani Ahmed Hamza, disclosed this on Wednesday in Abuja at a press conference to commemorate the 2026 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence and formally introduce its five-year FemFocus programme.

Hamza said the figures, drawn from the 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey and NHRC records, highlighted the urgent need for stronger institutional responses, improved survivor support services and better access to justice.

He expressed concern that despite progress in enacting laws to combat gender-based violence, implementation remained weak, with several states lacking essential facilities to support survivors.

According to him, 35 states and the Federal Capital Territory have domesticated the Violence Against Persons (Prohibition) Act or enacted equivalent legislation, but 14 states still lack Sexual Assault Referral Centres.

He added that only eight states maintained consistent forensic services, while six had neither referral centres nor shelters for survivors.

“Nigeria’s crisis is no longer primarily a gap in laws; it is a gap in implementation, financing and infrastructure,” he said.

The Oxfam director further noted that financial constraints continued to prevent many survivors from accessing justice, with some spending as much as N100,000 out of pocket in pursuit of justice.

He said the FemFocus programme was designed to address these challenges through improved survivor support services, stronger legal accountability and enhanced protection for Women Human Rights Defenders.

The five-year initiative, which will run from 2026 to 2030, is supported by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands, with €6.4 million allocated to Nigeria.

Hamza said the programme would focus on preventing violence against women and girls, expanding access to survivor-centred services, strengthening laws and institutional accountability, and protecting women human rights defenders.

He urged federal and state governments, law enforcement agencies, the judiciary, traditional institutions, the media and the private sector to support survivors, provide funding for grassroots feminist movements and ensure accountability.

Also speaking, the National Coordinator of Christian Women for Excellence, Empowerment and Development and Chairperson of the African Women Leaders Network, Prof. Fummilayo Para-Mallam, urged stakeholders to move beyond repeated awareness campaigns and adopt practical measures to address gender-based violence.

She called on Oxfam to collaborate with the Senator Oluremi Tinubu Gender Centre at the National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies and contribute to the ongoing review of the National Gender Policy.

Para-Mallam also emphasised the need for donor-funded programmes to invest in building the institutional capacity of local partners to ensure the sustainability of interventions beyond the funding period.

Similarly, the Executive Director of Kebekache Women Development and Research Centre, Dr. Emem Okon, advocated greater community participation in efforts to tackle violence against women and girls.

She urged stakeholders to engage traditional institutions, men, families and other influential groups in challenging harmful practices and changing attitudes that encourage violence.

Okon also called for measures to discourage families of survivors from accepting financial compensation from alleged perpetrators in exchange for withdrawing legal complaints.

In her remarks, the Chief Executive Officer of the Public and Private Development Centre, Lucy James Abagi, stressed the importance of sustainable funding for interventions addressing gender-based violence.

She urged governments, philanthropists and other stakeholders to establish sustainable funding mechanisms to ensure that projects and justice-sector interventions continued to deliver results beyond the lifespan of donor support.

content:
By Efe Onodjae

One of the victims killed in the alleged assassination attempt on former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, was a university student and the only son of his parents.

The deceased, identified as Festus Okoro Oghenenyore, was said to be driving his Spider car through Uduere when he stopped after learning that Omo-Agege, the Delta Central senatorial candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, was campaigning in the community.

According to information gathered by vanguard, he was said to have stopped by to witness the political activity when violence broke out, resulting in the death of four persons and injuries to several others.

Further investigation revealed that Oghenenyore’s was the only male child among the two children of his parents. He had only one sister. According to further findings, explained that his married and in his early 30s.

Vanguard gathered that his mother hails from Imodge community in Orogun, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, while his father is from Isoko in delta north.

title: ‘An iroko has fallen’: Nollywood stars mourn Pete Edochie
description:
By Rita Okoye

Nigerian celebrities have expressed grief over the unexpected passing of veteran Nollywood actor, Chief Pete Edochie, paying tribute to the screen icon whose towering presence, commanding voice and remarkable career helped shape the Nigerian film industry.
The tributes, shared on soci
content:
By Rita Okoye

Nigerian celebrities have expressed grief over the unexpected passing of veteran Nollywood actor, Chief Pete Edochie, paying tribute to the screen icon whose towering presence, commanding voice and remarkable career helped shape the Nigerian film industry.

The tributes, shared on social media, described the actor as a cultural icon, father figure, mentor and custodian of Igbo tradition, with many reflecting on his enduring influence on Nollywood and generations of actors.

Actress Rechael Okonkwo said the loss was deeply personal, describing Edochie as not only a screen legend but also a father figure who offered her love, wisdom and encouragement.

l“This one hurts deeply,” she wrote, lamenting the loss of a man whose name represented greatness, excellence and an unforgettable legacy.

She said the industry had lost a giant and an icon, while many had lost a father figure, adding that his contributions to Nollywood and the lives he touched would never be erased.

“Legends may leave this world, but their footprints never disappear. You will be deeply missed, Ebubedike,” she added.

May Yul-Edochie, the estranged daughter-in-law, described the news as heartbreaking, reflecting on the veteran’s life and the fragility of human existence.

She recalled how false death reports had circulated about the actor over the years, making the latest news particularly difficult to process.

In her tribute, she described him as a veteran whose name, voice, presence and contributions to the Nigerian film industry would remain unforgettable, adding that he was an institution and a father figure to many.

We “Legends never truly die; they live on through the memories they create and the impact they leave behind,” she wrote, praying for strength for his family and loved ones.

Actor Stan Nze also paid tribute to the deceased, describing him as a legend, a true custodian of Igbo culture and a celebrity in every sense.

Nze said Edochie’s legacy would never be eroded, noting that his footprints would remain for generations to emulate.

He recalled sharing the screen with the veteran actor, describing the experience as one he would cherish and recount to his children.

“You came, you saw, you won,” he wrote, bidding the actor farewell.

For Susan Peters, Edochie was an iroko tree that had fallen, lamenting the loss of a towering figure in African cinema.

She said the actor was more than a performer, noting that his voice, presence and portrayal of African traditions, kingship, wisdom and values left an indelible mark on generations.

According to her, Edochie gave African stories dignity and depth, with his influence extending beyond Nigeria’s borders.

“The curtains may fall, but the legend never dies,” Peters wrote, praying for eternal rest for the actor and strength for his family.

Actress Adaora Ukoh also expressed shock and sadness, describing the late actor as another giant and pillar of Nollywood whose voice, wisdom, talent and presence helped shape the industry.

She said words were inadequate to capture the pain of losing an actor whose work had touched generations, adding that his legacy and inspiration would endure.

“Nollywood has lost another giant, another pillar, another beautiful chapter of our history,” she wrote.
Similarly, actress Uche Jombo described Edochie as one of Nollywood’s greatest pillars, an institution, master of his craft and custodian of Nigerian culture.

She said his contribution to the industry went beyond the films he featured in, stressing that his impact, standards and inspiration to younger actors were immeasurable.

Jombo, who reflected on the giants whose shoulders younger actors stand on, said Edochie gave Nigerian storytelling a face, voice and legacy that would outlive generations.

She sympathised with his wife, children, family, friends and colleagues, adding that although the industry had lost a legend, it had not lost the legacy he left behind.

Actor Shawn Faqua equally mourned the veteran, describing his passing as heavy and profound.
He said Edochie paved the way for younger actors to thrive, adding that the industry was blessed to have witnessed his remarkable career.

“Words cannot fully capture the glory of your essence, but this industry is truly blessed to have experienced it; we saw your days and rejoiced,” he wrote, thanking the actor for his contributions and bidding him farewell.

The tributes underscored Edochie’s enduring impact, as his celebrated career, cultural influence, and distinctive screen presence made him one of Nollywood’s most revered figures.

The post ‘An iroko has fallen’: Nollywood stars mourn Pete Edochie appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Political Violence: Declare State Of Emergency In Delta If Necessary, Reps Urge Tinubu
description: The House of Representatives has urged President Bola Tinubu to closely monitor the security situation in Delta State and declare a state of emergency if necessary.This followed a motion by Representative Benedict Etanabene, who drew attention to a series of political violence in the state.The House
content:
The House of Representatives has urged President Bola Tinubu to closely monitor the security situation in Delta State and declare a state of emergency if necessary.

This followed a motion by Representative Benedict Etanabene, who drew attention to a series of political violence in the state.

The House said it feared that the deteriorating situation is creating an atmosphere of fear and is threatening peaceful coexistence in the state.

The House is also asking the Inspector General of Police, Tunji Disu, to identify flashpoints to prevent further attacks and establish a special investigative team to identify perpetrators and financiers of political violence in the state.

The development followed the deadly attack on a campaign convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the state.

The attack left six people dead, according to preliminary police reports, while several others sustained injuries.

Omo-Agege, a former deputy senate president and the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central, reportedly escaped unhurt.

The Delta State Police Command has since invited Omo-Agege, Ughelli North Local Government Chairman Jaro Egbo and five others for questioning over the deadly attack.

The police said the invitations were part of an ongoing investigation into the violence that occurred during an NDC campaign in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, on Monday.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, Bright Edafe, said the invited individuals had been asked to report to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) at the police headquarters in Asaba on specified dates.

Omo-Agege, the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central, is expected to appear on Thursday at 11 a.m., while Egbo has been invited for 2 p.m. on the same day.

The five other invitees are Gowon Egoide, a former chairman of Uduere Quarters; Onoriode Oneya, the incumbent youth chairman of Uduere Community; Edirin Wokode Ewhubare, an associate of Egoide; Erukaye Egoide, Egoide’s nephew; and Tony Gabon Mevowovo, another associate of Egoide.

The post Political Violence: Declare State Of Emergency In Delta If Necessary, Reps Urge Tinubu appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Barca, Real Madrid chief fail to reach agreement over ref scandal accusations
description:
Real Madrid and Barcelona failed to reach an agreement on Wednesday in a conciliation hearing over statements made by Los Blancos president Florentino Perez regarding the Negreira refereeing scandal, a source from the Catalan club confirmed to AFP.



The hearing followed a lawsuit filed by Barcelon
content:
Real Madrid and Barcelona failed to reach an agreement on Wednesday in a conciliation hearing over statements made by Los Blancos president Florentino Perez regarding the Negreira refereeing scandal, a source from the Catalan club confirmed to AFP.

The hearing followed a lawsuit filed by Barcelona on June 12 against Perez for his statements in May, in which he accused the Spanish champions of scheming to obtain favourable treatment from referees.

“The aim of this lawsuit is for Mr. Perez to retract certain statements he made, knowing they were false, which are defamatory and offensive to the club’s image and reputation,” Barcelona had declared when initiating legal action.

“In the event that this lawsuit is not duly addressed, Barcelona will proceed to file the corresponding criminal complaint for defamation,” Barca added in June.

“When someone makes statements and you might be mistaken or go too far with your words, a conciliation hearing gives you the chance to correct them,” Barca president Joan Laporta told reporters before the hearing on Wednesday.

“If that opportunity is not taken, it means we see malicious intent and we will have to continue with the proceedings.”

Barca could now file a criminal complaint against Perez over his remarks.

The main cause of the Catalan club’s anger was the press conference on May 12 in which Perez called elections for the Real Madrid presidency, which he later won.

In that appearance he reiterated his accusations against Barca regarding the matter known as the “Negreira case”.

Spanish courts are investigating alleged payments of around 7.5 million euros ($8.2m) made over almost two decades by Barcelona to companies belonging to Jose Maria Enriquez Negreira, the former number two in Spain’s refereeing hierarchy.

The investigation seeks to determine whether those payments may have been used to obtain any competitive advantages, something Barcelona deny, claiming they were solely for reports analysing referees.

title: Katsina govt orders emirs to seek clearance before hosting foreign guests
description:
By Adegboyega Adeleye







The Katsina State Government has directed emirs and other traditional rulers to obtain official clearance before receiving foreign visitors at their palaces.



Commissioner for Information and Culture Bala Salisu Zango announced the directive in a statement on Wednesday
content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

The Katsina State Government has directed emirs and other traditional rulers to obtain official clearance before receiving foreign visitors at their palaces.

Commissioner for Information and Culture Bala Salisu Zango announced the directive in a statement on Wednesday, saying rulers must obtain approval from the Departments of Protocol and Cabinet/Security Matters in the Office of the Secretary to the State Government before hosting foreign guests.

“The directive is intended to ensure proper coordination, security, and adherence to official protocols during visits to Emirs’ palace by foreign nationals, while also placing the traditional rulers under a formal regulatory framework regarding international relations,” the statement said.

It added that the measure was intended to “streamline interactions with foreign nationals and ensure that the government is fully aware of international engagements involving traditional institutions.” Zango said the policy was part of the state government’s broader security strategy, adding that “the state government partly relies on traditional rulers as key stakeholders in peace-building.”

The directive followed the government’s suspension of the Emir of Daura, Umar Faruk Umar, from official engagements and travel, pending an investigation into an allegation made by Polish tourist Mirka Czee. The government also set up a committee to investigate the allegation and advise it on the appropriate course of action.

Czee alleged that the Emir touched her breasts without her consent during a visit to his palace on November 14. She said she recorded part of the encounter using Meta smart glasses and released the video after leaving Nigeria.

The Daura Emirate Council said it was reviewing the footage to establish its authenticity and determine whether it had been manipulated. The Katsina State Government said the Emir’s suspension would remain in place pending the committee’s findings, which it said would be implemented.

Czee later shared screenshots of abusive messages and death threats she said she received after publishing the allegation. Amnesty International Nigeria condemned the threats, saying she had received hundreds.

title: INEC deploys AI unit to combat misinformation ahead of 2027 polls
description:
By Edwin Philip



ABUJA — The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has established a dedicated Artificial Intelligence (AI) division within its Information and Communication Technology department to tackle misinformation, disinformation and AI-driven manipulation ahead of the 2027 gener
content:
By Edwin Philip

ABUJA — The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has established a dedicated Artificial Intelligence (AI) division within its Information and Communication Technology department to tackle misinformation, disinformation and AI-driven manipulation ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The commission said the growing use of generative AI, synthetic voice cloning, deepfakes and coordinated online campaigns had made information management a critical part of election security.

INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Ojo Amupitan, SAN, stated this in a keynote address at the Nigeria Election Risk and Readiness Summit 2026 in Abuja on Wednesday.

Amupitan, who was represented by his Chief Press Secretary, Adedayo Oketola, said elections could be influenced by false information even before voting commenced.

The summit, convened by the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID) as part of its 2026 Media and Development Conference, had the theme, “Securing the Vote and Protecting the Frontliners.”

According to the INEC chairman, fabricated audio recordings, doctored videos and false election results could trigger panic, discourage voter participation and spark communal violence.

He cited an incident during the Federal Capital Territory election in which a viral video falsely claimed that members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) were being killed in parts of Abuja on election day.

Amupitan said INEC worked with the NYSC to verify and debunk the claim, preventing the misinformation from causing panic or disrupting the electoral process.

He said the commission was adopting a zero-tolerance approach to communication gaps but acknowledged that tackling false narratives in a highly connected society required collaboration.

INEC, therefore, called for an institutionalised partnership with independent fact-checking organisations, including Dubawa, media organisations, civil society groups and the National Orientation Agency.

The commission also pledged to provide verified journalists and fact-checkers with timely access to official information to enable them to counter false claims with accurate data.

Addressing journalists at the summit, INEC urged freelance and newsroom reporters to complete their accreditation before the portal closes, stressing that the registration deadlines are guided by the Electoral Act and cannot be extended arbitrarily.

On its preparations for the elections, the commission said it had procured about 57,000 new Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices, replaced batteries in serviceable units and established climate-controlled storage facilities across the states.

It also said it had reduced the voter-verification threshold per BVAS device from 1,250 to 850, with additional devices to be deployed to larger polling units to keep accreditation within an estimated one to two minutes.

INEC said it planned to deploy about 1.41 million ad hoc personnel for the 2027 general elections, comprising approximately 700,000 for the presidential and National Assembly elections and another 700,000 for the governorship and State Houses of Assembly polls.

The commission also disclosed that it had extended the registration period for ad hoc staff by between two and two-and-a-half weeks.

The 2027 presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections are slated for February 6.

Amupitan condemned political violence, attacks on campaign convoys and party offices, as well as threats against election workers and journalists, including incidents documented by CJID’s Press Attack Tracker.

He recalled an incident in London in which protesters waylaid him, saying neither he nor the commission would be intimidated in carrying out its responsibilities.

The INEC chairman also drew attention to tougher penalties under the Electoral Act 2026 for electoral offences, including fines of up to ₦5 million or imprisonment for up to 12 months for individuals, and an initial fine of ₦10 million for political parties under Sections 95 to 97.

He said INEC could prosecute offenders directly upon receiving police case files, as provided under Section 148, adding that the commission had held discussions with the Inspector-General of Police and political party leaders on election security.

The commission further highlighted the restructuring of the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security and the use of its Election Risk Management (EARM) tool to identify potential flashpoints and guide security deployments.

It said the tool informed targeted security deployments during the 2026 Osun governorship election.

Amupitan urged political parties, traditional and religious leaders, civil society organisations, the media and citizens to reject electoral violence and misinformation.

“No election or political ambition is worth the blood of a Nigerian,” he said, warning that Nigeria must protect democratic stability in the West African region.

Earlier, the European Union Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Ambassador Gautier Mignot, called on stakeholders to agree on practical measures to address electoral risks ahead of the 2027 elections.

Mignot said electoral integrity covered the entire process, including a fair pre-election environment, access to credible information, transparent results administration and timely resolution of disputes.

He noted that the conduct of Nigeria’s elections had implications for peace and democratic stability across West Africa.

Also speaking, the Norwegian Ambassador to Nigeria, Svein Baera, urged stakeholders to protect journalists, fact-checkers and electoral personnel ahead of the polls.

Baera commended CJID for its work in strengthening journalism, democratic accountability and public trust in Nigeria and West Africa, saying Norway was proud to partner with the organisation.

“We cannot secure the vote without protecting the people who make elections transparent and accountable. That includes election officials and observers, but also journalists, fact-checkers, editors, and other media outlets,” he said.

The post INEC deploys AI unit to combat misinformation ahead of 2027 polls appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: SGF calls for preventive policing to curb cultiism, others
description:
The Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume, has called on the Nigeria Police Force to strengthen preventive policing and community partnerships to tackle cultism, youth-related crimes and other social vices threatening national security.
Akume said tackling cultism required a co
content:
The Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume, has called on the Nigeria Police Force to strengthen preventive policing and community partnerships to tackle cultism, youth-related crimes and other social vices threatening national security.

Akume said tackling cultism required a coordinated approach involving security agencies, traditional rulers, religious leaders, parents, teachers and civil society organisations, rather than relying solely on law enforcement.

A statement released by his Media Assistant, Yomi Odunuga, said the SGF made the call on Wednesday in Abuja at the first national conference of the Police Campaign Against Cultism and Other Vices.

He said cultism and other social vices had continued to undermine community safety, disrupt educational activities, destroy promising lives and weaken the prospects of young Nigerians.

“These challenges demand a coordinated and proactive response that goes beyond law enforcement to address their underlying social and economic causes,” he said.

Akume described preventive policing as indispensable to addressing the menace, stressing the need for early identification of threats, intelligence-sharing and stronger trust between the police and communities.

“By identifying threats early, strengthening intelligence-sharing and building trust between the Police and communities, we can prevent crime before it occurs and create safer environments for all Nigerians,” he said.

He urged traditional rulers, religious leaders, parents, teachers, civil society organisations and community associations to work closely with security agencies in promoting vigilance, responsible citizenship and peaceful coexistence.

The SGF also called for increased investment in youth development, including education, mentorship, skills acquisition and entrepreneurship, to steer young people away from criminal activities.

He said, “We must also recognise that our youth are not merely beneficiaries of national development; they are its greatest resource.”

Akume added that providing young people with meaningful opportunities would help redirect vulnerable youths from destructive influences towards productive and responsible citizenship.

He said the Federal Government, under President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, remained committed to strengthening national security, empowering young Nigerians and creating a safer society.

The SGF assured that his office would continue to promote inter-agency coordination, policy coherence and collaboration among relevant institutions to address cultism and other social challenges.

He urged participants at the conference to come up with practical recommendations that would strengthen preventive policing and community engagement.

Cultism and youth-related crimes have remained security and social concerns in Nigeria, particularly in educational institutions and communities where clashes between rival groups have resulted in killings, injuries, intimidation and disruption of academic activities.

title: Adeleke presents ₦927bn 2027 budget proposal to Osun Assembly
description:
By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo



Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, on Wednesday presented a proposed budget of ₦927.37 billion for the 2027 fiscal year to the State House of Assembly for consideration.







The budget, tagged “Budget of Advanced Commitment and Expansion”, provides ₦559.31 billion
content:
By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo

Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, on Wednesday presented a proposed budget of ₦927.37 billion for the 2027 fiscal year to the State House of Assembly for consideration.

The budget, tagged “Budget of Advanced Commitment and Expansion”, provides ₦559.31 billion for capital expenditure and ₦368.06 billion for recurrent expenditure.

Presenting the estimates before the lawmakers, Adeleke said the proposed budget totalled ₦927,370,584,800, with a capital-to-recurrent expenditure ratio of 60:40.

He said the budget would be financed through the state’s share of the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC), estimated at ₦400.93 billion; internally generated revenue (IGR) of ₦250.17 billion; and other receipts amounting to ₦230.65 billion.

The governor said the 2027 budget was formulated in line with the reviewed Osun State Development Plans (2023–2050).

He explained that the proposal was designed to improve the ease of doing business, promote employment and youth development, strengthen human capital and accelerate infrastructure development.

“Our budgetary allocations emphasise the administration’s Five-Points Agenda. Therefore, our focus for the 2027 fiscal year are infrastructural development; human capital development; revitalised agriculture; security of our state; workers’ and pensioners’ welfare; and job creation,” he said.

Earlier, the Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. Adewale Egbedun, assured the governor that the lawmakers would work towards the timely consideration and passage of the appropriation bill.

He, however, stressed that the proposed estimates would undergo thorough legislative scrutiny to ensure that public funds were allocated according to the needs and priorities of residents.

“Pursuant to our constitutional responsibilities, this House is committed to ensuring the timely consideration and passage of the 2027 Appropriation Bill. However, this responsibility will be discharged with the utmost diligence, independence and commitment to the overall interest of the people of Osun State,” Egbedun said.

He said the Assembly’s examination of the proposals would be guided by fiscal prudence, equity, transparency, developmental impact and value for public expenditure.

The Speaker also congratulated Adeleke on his electoral victory and preparations for another term in office, pledging the Assembly’s continued partnership with the executive to promote development across the state.

title: Police arrest suspected cultist, recover pistol, ammunition in Ogun
description:
A 25-year-old suspected cultist, Yusuf Olasunkami, has been arrested by the Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) Unit of the Ogun State Police Command at Bode Olude, Ogun State.
In a Wednesday statement, command spokesman, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi said the intelligence-led operation also led to the recove
content:
A 25-year-old suspected cultist, Yusuf Olasunkami, has been arrested by the Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) Unit of the Ogun State Police Command at Bode Olude, Ogun State.

In a Wednesday statement, command spokesman, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi said the intelligence-led operation also led to the recovery of a locally-made pistol and ammunition.

Babaseyi further disclosed that the operation conducted on November 21 followed actionable intelligence gathered by the command on suspected criminal activities within the area.

The statement reads, “Acting on the information, SWAT operatives, led by the Officer-in-Charge, SP Obeh Eneye, conducted discreet surveillance, which led to the suspect’s arrest at his residence in Odo Eja, Bode Olude.

“A search conducted at the premises resulted in the recovery of one locally made pistol, two expended cartridges and one live cartridge.

“Preliminary investigation indicates the suspect’s alleged affiliation with the Aiye Confraternity.

“He is currently in police custody, while investigation continues to establish the full circumstances of the case and identify other persons who may be connected to it.”

The Commissioner of Police, Ogun State Command, CP Bode Ojajuni, reaffirmed the command’s commitment to proactive, intelligence-led policing and sustained efforts to prevent cult-related activities and other criminal conduct.

He urged residents to continue supporting the police with credible and timely information, assuring the public of the command’s unwavering commitment to protecting lives and property.

title: NDC faults Yusuf over allegation against Kwankwaso
description:
By Hadiza Yusuf



The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Kano State has faulted Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf over his allegation that he was pressured to facilitate discussions between the Presidency and Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso on a possible defection to the All Progressives Congress (APC).
content:
By Hadiza Yusuf

The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Kano State has faulted Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf over his allegation that he was pressured to facilitate discussions between the Presidency and Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso on a possible defection to the All Progressives Congress (APC).

The party described the allegation as contradictory and unfortunate, claiming that it contradicted the Kano State Government’s earlier position on alleged negotiations with the Presidency.

In a statement signed by its Chief Campaign Spokesperson, Hon. Hashimu Sulaiman Dungurawa, on Wednesday, the NDC said Yusuf’s recent interview with the BBC raised questions about his earlier comments on the matter.

Yusuf had reportedly alleged that he was persuaded and pressured to facilitate discussions on behalf of Kwankwaso with the Presidency over a possible move to the APC.

Reacting, the NDC recalled that the Kano State Government issued a statement on January 29, 2024, denying any deal, agreement or negotiation with the Presidency following the Supreme Court judgment on the governorship election.

The party argued that the governor’s latest comments, coming about 34 months after the earlier statement, were inconsistent with the government’s position at the time.

“The Governor’s 360-degree turnaround on the same subject after just 34 months, accusing Senator Kwankwaso, is to say the least contradictory, repulsive and unfortunate,” the statement said.

The NDC further maintained that Yusuf’s decision to join the APC was a personal political choice and was not influenced by Kwankwaso.

It also expressed concern that the allegation could embarrass the Presidency and undermine public confidence in the country’s political and judicial institutions.

The party called on the Kano State Government to withdraw the allegation, particularly the part relating to Kwankwaso’s character.

It added that statements allegedly made for political advantage or to attract public sympathy would not address the challenges confronting the governor’s administration.

“Deliberate statements made to muddle things up for political gains and attract undue sympathy would not save an already sinking ship,” the party said.

The post NDC faults Yusuf over allegation against Kwankwaso appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Lagos seals four churches over noise pollution
description:
The Lagos State Environmental Protection Agency has sealed four churches across the state over persistent noise pollution.
The agency disclosed this in a statement posted on its X handle on Wednesday, saying the enforcement exercise was carried out on Tuesday, November 24, 2026.
Sealed church. CREDI
content:
The Lagos State Environmental Protection Agency has sealed four churches across the state over persistent noise pollution.

The agency disclosed this in a statement posted on its X handle on Wednesday, saying the enforcement exercise was carried out on Tuesday, November 24, 2026.

The affected churches are “Celestial Church of Christ (CCC) at Chief Lawani Adeniyi Dosunmu Crescent, Lambada, Ajah; The Lord’s Chosen Charismatic Revival Movement at 13, Sade Shobakin Street, Ona Ara Bus Stop, Ipaja-Ayobo; God’s Word Faith Ministries at Olayemi Odukoya, Atan Kekere Bus Stop, off Ipaja-Ayobo; and His Presence Redemptions Ministry International at 3, Olayemi Odukoya, Atan Kekere Bus Stop, off Ipaja-Ayobo.”

“The Lagos State Environmental Protection Agency (LASEPA), on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, sealed four establishments across Lagos State for persistent noise pollution,” the statement read.

LASEPA said the exercise was conducted in line with the directives of the Lagos State Government to ensure strict adherence to environmental laws, safeguard public health and promote a cleaner, healthier and safer environment for residents.

It added that the enforcement was part of efforts to ensure compliance with environmental regulations across the state.

The latest action comes amid the Lagos State Government’s ongoing enforcement against religious centres and other establishments accused of violating noise pollution regulations.

In November, LASEPA sealed All Christians Gathering Ministry in Surulere following repeated complaints of late-night noise pollution from residents.

The state government has also said religious and entertainment centres found to be violating noise regulations would face sanctions after investigations and warnings.

Under LASEPA’s noise pollution guidelines, noise levels in residential areas must not exceed 55 decibels during the day and 45 decibels at night.

The agency also requires religious houses to operate in enclosed and soundproofed buildings, with regulated use of speakers to avoid disturbing neighbouring residents.

title: 2027: NSCDC pledges neutrality, vows to protect voters
description:
The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps has pledged to remain neutral and non-partisan during the 2027 general elections, assuring Nigerians of its readiness to protect voters, electoral officials and sensitive materials.
The Commandant General of the NSCDC, Prof. Ahmed Audi, gave the assurance
content:
The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps has pledged to remain neutral and non-partisan during the 2027 general elections, assuring Nigerians of its readiness to protect voters, electoral officials and sensitive materials.

The Commandant General of the NSCDC, Prof. Ahmed Audi, gave the assurance on Wednesday while declaring open a three-day training workshop for senior management officers of the corps in Abuja.

According to a statement issued by the Corps’ spokesperson, ACC Babawale Afolabi, the CG said the training was necessary to ensure that the corps was adequately prepared to contribute to credible elections and align its operations with global best practices.

He explained that tactical commanders and junior officers had undergone similar training the previous month, adding that senior officers needed to be equipped because they would be responsible for issuing operational instructions during the elections.

“The responsibility of making the election free and fair lies within the security agencies, and we are ready to play our part without prejudice. We must follow the three Cs: Coordination, Collaboration and Cooperation, and we must adhere to them.

“We must respect the fundamental rights of citizens, as no room would be given for anybody who constitutionally violates anybody. Anybody who goes against the law guiding us would be shown the way out,” he said.

The NSCDC boss urged officers to maintain neutrality, strengthen communication channels and ensure their operations complied with national security guidelines.

“We must ensure neutrality and remain non-partisan. We must strengthen our communication channels and ensure they align with national security guidelines. We must never lag in discharging our duties.

“We must avoid any misfortune and all operations must be reported to the National Headquarters. We must contribute meaningfully to the success of the election,” he added.

Audi said the training would also strengthen officers’ capacity to protect electoral materials, operate according to the rules of engagement and de-escalate tensions during the polls.

“We want to ensure the election is free and fair. This training will help increase capacity; it will help officers know how to handle situations and de-escalate issues so as to ensure everyone, including electoral staff from INEC and sensitive materials, is protected, which is one of the core mandates of the agency,” he said.

The Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, represented by the Director of Joint Services in the ministry, Adaji Asman, urged security personnel to familiarise themselves with relevant laws, codes of conduct and rules of engagement.

The minister also stressed the need for officers to respect the division of responsibilities relating to arrest and prosecution under electoral laws, while protecting critical national assets and infrastructure, including INEC offices, collation centres, workers and power lines.

He said, “We must ensure synergy with other sister agencies; nobody should work in isolation. We must ensure cooperation with sister agencies to quench any possible threat to the electoral process.

“We demand a high standard of neutrality, remain non-partisan and remain loyal to the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.”

The facilitator of the training, Alnas Consulting Limited, represented by Prof. Nasirdeen Usman, said the programme would combine practical sessions with instruction on the rules of engagement to prepare officers for election-related security challenges.

He said participants would receive training in crisis management, human management, de-escalation of tensions, protection of electoral materials and the appropriate use of force.

“The training will further strengthen the agency in its core role,” Usman added.

The Chairman of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, Brigadier General Buba Marwa (retd.), represented by the Director of Asset and Financial Investigations at the NDLEA, ACGN Ahmed, said drug abuse could contribute to violence and disruption during elections.

He disclosed that Marwa had directed NDLEA operatives to raid drug black spots across the country ahead of the polls.

“This election is a very serious business, and we must make it drug-free because those planning to disrupt it would want to be high on several substances.

“When we raid those drugs and prevent them from getting to the end users, election violence would be reduced drastically. We are very aware, and we are on top of our game to ensure drugs are off the street and to keep Nigeria safe before and after the election,” he said.

Similarly, Comptroller Dauda Ikharo, who represented the Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Immigration Service, Kemi Nandap, said the service was ready to support efforts to ensure peaceful elections through intelligence sharing and joint operations.

“We are ready for institutional synergy to reduce cross-border migration that would disrupt the election. We are ready to engage in collaboration and also for joint patrols,” he said.

The NSCDC Deputy Commandant General in charge of Intelligence and Investigation, Dr Nnamdi Nwinyi, described the training as timely, saying it would strengthen officers’ strategic and operational readiness.

“The expectation of our personnel is to engage in strategy and operational readiness. We are following electoral law, strengthening our intelligence and also preparing for post-election crisis management. We must be professional enough to ensure every Nigerian performs their civic right without fear,” he said.

The Director-General of the Department of State Services, represented by Assistant Director-General Aliyu Bello of the Asset and Financial Investigation Department, also pledged the agency’s support for inter-agency cooperation ahead of the elections.

Bello said the DSS was ready to share intelligence and collaborate operationally with other security agencies to ensure a hitch-free electoral process and protect voters.

description:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja
First Lady of Nigeria Oluremi Tinubu, has called for stronger action to dismantle systemic barriers that allow violence against women and girls to persist, insisting that survivors must be protected and perpetrators held accountable.
Mrs Tinubu made the call in a m
content:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

First Lady of Nigeria Oluremi Tinubu, has called for stronger action to dismantle systemic barriers that allow violence against women and girls to persist, insisting that survivors must be protected and perpetrators held accountable.

Mrs Tinubu made the call in a message marking the 2026 International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, observed on November 25.

Aligning with this year’s United Nations theme, “Ensure Justice. Protect Survivors. End Impunity,”the First Lady described gender-based violence as a profound violation of human dignity.

She said the global observance should serve as a renewed call for collective commitment to protecting women from all forms of violence and abuse.

According to her, achieving justice requires deliberate efforts to dismantle the systemic barriers that enable abuse to thrive, both in physical spaces and across the digital world.

“True justice means we must actively dismantle the systemic barriers that allow abuse to persist, both in physical spaces and across the digital world,” she said.

The First Lady stressed the need to build a society where every woman and girl could live free from fear, abuse and violence.

She urged Nigerians to renew their commitment to safeguarding the rights, dignity and security of women and girls.

title: 2027: Atiku postpones Kaduna campaign visit
description:
The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, Atiku Abubakar, has postponed his campaign visit to Kaduna State, initially scheduled for Wednesday, following a review of his campaign timetable.
The Kaduna State Chairman of the ADC, Dr Humble Katuka, disclosed this on Wednesday in a s
content:
The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, Atiku Abubakar, has postponed his campaign visit to Kaduna State, initially scheduled for Wednesday, following a review of his campaign timetable.

The Kaduna State Chairman of the ADC, Dr Humble Katuka, disclosed this on Wednesday in a statement posted on his Facebook page.

Katuka explained that the postponement followed a review of the presidential campaign timetable.

According to Katuka, the decision was taken by the Presidential Campaign Council to accommodate campaign activities in the southern part of the country before returning to the North.

He said a new date for the Kaduna visit would be announced in due course.

Katuka added that he and other party stakeholders had held discussions with the Chairman of the Presidential Campaign Council, Kashim Imam, and some members of the council over the development.

He explained that the postponement was also in response to the need to accommodate the growing expectations of party members and residents of Kaduna State, who had expressed enthusiasm about receiving the former vice-president.

The ADC chairman assured supporters that the visit would still take place, saying the party was working towards giving Atiku a grand reception whenever the new date was announced.

He said, “Myself and the state coordinator, alongside some critical stakeholders, have discussed extensively with the PCC Chairman, Sir Kashim Imam, and some of his key members.

“God willing, at the rescheduled date, the good people of Kaduna will receive the people’s president in a grand style.”

The planned visit is part of the ADC’s political activities ahead of the 2027 presidential election, as parties begin to intensify mobilisation and engagement with supporters across the country.

Kaduna, one of the major political centres in the North-West, is considered an important state in the region’s electoral calculations, making visits by presidential candidates significant for party mobilisation and outreach.

title: Ice hockey federation appeals Russia’s World Championship reinstatement
description:
The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) has announced plans to appeal a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) reinstating Russia for next year’s World Championship.
Russia has been barred from participating in IIHF competitions since February 2022 following its invasion of Ukrain
content:
The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) has announced plans to appeal a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) reinstating Russia for next year’s World Championship.

Russia has been barred from participating in IIHF competitions since February 2022 following its invasion of Ukraine, with the global governing body earlier this year deciding to extend the exclusion.

However, on October 30, CAS upheld appeals by the Russian Ice Hockey Federation against the ban, ruling that the IIHF’s arguments based on “safety, security and other concerns” were not supported by sufficient evidence.

The IIHF has now challenged the ruling before the Swiss Federal Tribunal, citing alleged undisclosed links between two of the three CAS panel members and Russia.

In a statement on Wednesday on X, the governing body said its decision to appeal was based on concerns about the independence and impartiality of the arbitrators.

“The decision is based on concerns around the independence and impartiality of two of the three arbitrators on the CAS Panel,” the IIHF said.

It added: “Especially following the information that has recently come to light regarding potential links between the two arbitrators and Russia.”

The federation maintained that the significance of the ruling and its implications for international ice hockey made further legal action necessary.

“Given the significance of the ruling and its implications for international ice hockey, the IIHF considers it definitively essential to pursue the matter before the Swiss Federal Tribunal,” the statement added.

Meanwhile, Ukraine’s ice hockey federation had expressed “deep outrage” following the overturning of the ban.

Austria, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, Latvia, Norway and Sweden have also indicated that they would refuse to face Russia in IIHF competitions.

Russia’s efforts to return to international sport also suffered a setback in November after Canada announced that Russian athletes and officials would be denied entry for the 2027 World Junior Championships.

title: Police arrest three over political violence in Kebbi
description:
The Kebbi State Police Command has arrested three persons over alleged political violence during a political gathering in Zauro, Makera and neighbouring communities in Birnin Kebbi Local Government Area.
The police alleged that the event was held in breach of an agreement requiring political parties
content:
The Kebbi State Police Command has arrested three persons over alleged political violence during a political gathering in Zauro, Makera and neighbouring communities in Birnin Kebbi Local Government Area.

The police alleged that the event was held in breach of an agreement requiring political parties to notify the command at least 48 hours before conducting political activities.

The command announced the arrests in a statement issued on Wednesday by its Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman.

According to the statement, preliminary findings showed that the gathering was presented as a distribution of relief materials and extended to Zauro, Makera, Gwadangwaji, Gawasu, Morida and Karyo.

The police said the organisers failed to inform the command of the activity, despite an understanding reached with political parties at a stakeholders’ meeting on September 7, 2026, and a subsequent meeting with the party’s caucus on November 2.

The command said the party had agreed to notify the Commissioner of Police ahead of its political engagements to enable the police to make necessary security arrangements.

However, it alleged that the agreement was disregarded during the gathering, with members of the convoy reportedly seen carrying weapons and some speakers making remarks capable of triggering unrest.

“Video evidence obtained by the command shows individuals in the convoy carrying sticks, machetes and swords, while some of the speakers made inciting statements capable of causing disturbances of public peace,” the statement said.

The police further alleged that some vehicles in the convoy were without registration numbers or displayed questionable number plates, while sirens were used in violation of traffic regulations.

Condemning the incident, the command warned political parties and their supporters against allowing political activities to be hijacked by violence and thuggery as preparations for the 2027 general elections gather momentum.

“The command will not tolerate conduct capable of undermining public peace or setting a dangerous precedent ahead of the 2027 general elections,” it warned.

The statement said the three suspects had been charged to court, while the party’s leadership was urged to honour its commitment to peaceful political engagement and cooperate with security agencies.

The police also called on relevant authorities to investigate reports that minors were involved in political activities, emphasising the need to protect children from exploitation and exposure to violence.

In a separate incident, the command said the Divisional Police Officer in Jega reported another political gathering organised by the same party without prior notification.

The organisers were subsequently directed to reschedule the rally and notify the police formally to allow adequate security arrangements, the statement added.

The command appealed to parents and guardians to discourage their children from being drawn into political violence.

“Any individual or political party found engaging in political violence, sponsoring thuggery or otherwise violating the law will be held accountable in accordance with the law,” the statement added.

Political activities have begun gathering momentum across the country ahead of the 2027 general elections, prompting security agencies to caution parties and their supporters against actions capable of disrupting public order.

Police commands have also been engaging political stakeholders to establish guidelines for rallies, campaigns and other gatherings, including advance notification to enable the deployment of adequate security personnel and prevent clashes.

The post Police arrest three over political violence in Kebbi appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
