title: Reps approve bill to convert Michael Okpara varsity to conventional institution
description:
From Ndubuisi Orji, Abuja
House of Representatives has approved the report of its Committee on University Education on a Bill to convert the Michael Okpara University of Agriculture Umudike to a conventional university.
Similarly, the House also approved another report of the committee for the conve
content:
From Ndubuisi Orji, Abuja

House of Representatives has approved the report of its Committee on University Education on a Bill to convert the Michael Okpara University of Agriculture Umudike to a conventional university.

Similarly, the House also approved another report of the committee for the conversion of the National Institute for Nigerian Languages (NINLAN), Aba, Abia State, to University of Nigerian Languages, as well as passed for third reading a Bill to establish a Federal College of Nursing Science, Umu-Imenyi Nkpa and well as a Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Bende, all in Abia State.

The Bills are sponsored by the Deputy Speaker and member representing Bende Federal Constituency of Abia at the National Assembly, Benjamin Kalu, and four others.

The parliament, while considering the report on the conversion of Michael Okpara University of Agriculture Umudike to a conventional university, at the Committee of the Whole, noted that being a specialized tertiary institution, it does not meet the growing educational need of the people of the State who are yearning to study other courses.

Therefore, the lawmakers agreed that making it a conventional university with a mandate to conduct teaching and research in all aspects of academic endeavour will be more beneficial to the people of the State and its environs.

Similarly, the conversion of NINLAN from an Institute of Nigerian languages to a University of Nigerian Languages, the House argued, will advance learning in Nigerian languages, develop academic programmes for diplomas, first degrees and postgraduate research, promoting indigenous culture and national unity, and train manpower for Nigerian languages and allied disciplines.

In the same vein, the proposed the Federal College of Nursing Science, Umu-Imenyi Nkpa when established, will train nurses, midwives and other frontline health workers through academic, clinical and practical programmes, conduct research in nursing and community health, and provide outreach, primary healthcare and health education services to surrounding communities.

Also, the Federal Medical Centre, Bende, is intended to provide specialised tertiary healthcare, emergency and referral services, maternal and child care, diagnostics and surgery to residents of Bende and neighbouring communities and also serve as a teaching and research centre for medical, nursing and allied health students, support training of health professionals, and complement existing primary and secondary health facilities in Abia State.

title: NDLEA busts ₦303.9bn meth lab in Enugu, arrests Nigerian, five Mexicans
description:
By Kingsley Omonobi



ABUJA — The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has dismantled an industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratory in Enugu State, arresting an alleged Nigerian drug baron and five Mexican nationals described as specialists in the production of the illicit drug.







The
content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

ABUJA — The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has dismantled an industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratory in Enugu State, arresting an alleged Nigerian drug baron and five Mexican nationals described as specialists in the production of the illicit drug.

The agency said it recovered 1,512 kilogrammes of methamphetamine, valued at about $226.8 million (approximately ₦303.9 billion), from the facility, alongside 6.68 tonnes of precursor and essential chemicals and industrial equipment used in manufacturing the drug.

The NDLEA identified the Nigerian suspect as 63-year-old Chuks Enoch Ezeike, popularly known as ‘Over Size’, while the five Mexican nationals were allegedly brought into the country to establish and operate the laboratory.

Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the agency, Brig.-Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), disclosed the breakthrough at a media briefing at the NDLEA headquarters on Wednesday.

Marwa described the operation as one of the agency’s most carefully planned intelligence-led operations, saying investigations traced the alleged drug network through Mexico, Colombia, France, the Republic of Benin, Lagos and Enugu.

According to him, the agency’s Special Operations Unit began working on intelligence in April 2026, which identified Ezeike as a suspected specialist in establishing clandestine methamphetamine laboratories with alleged links to Oscar Ramos-Cardenas, a Mexican identified as a major industrial-scale methamphetamine producer.

Marwa said the agency subsequently received intelligence on August 25, 2026, about five Mexican nationals identified as methamphetamine specialists travelling to Nigeria.

He said the NDLEA, working with the Nigeria Immigration Service, prevented the five men from entering Nigeria when they arrived in Abuja on August 28 and returned them to Mexico.

The NDLEA chairman said investigators later established that Ezeike had travelled from Enugu to Abuja to receive the visitors, with his bank records allegedly confirming payment for their hotel accommodation.

Marwa said the suspects subsequently devised another route through Bogotá, Colombia, Paris, France, and the Republic of Benin.

He alleged that Ezeike procured forged Argentine, Colombian and Chilean passports for the Mexican nationals, who surrendered their genuine travel documents and assumed new identities before entering Nigeria through the land border.

According to him, three of the Mexicans entered Nigeria through the Seme Border Post on September 20, while the remaining two arrived the following day.

The NDLEA boss said the agency deliberately allowed the suspects into the country to enable investigators to uncover the entire network, including the alleged financier, foreign specialists, laboratory and finished products.

“We wanted the whole network: the meth specialist, the financier, the factory and the product. Sending them home a second time would only have postponed the problem,” Marwa said.

He disclosed that Ezeike received the Mexicans in Lagos, lodged them in a hotel and subsequently moved them to Enugu, where they operated from an industrial complex behind San Savanna Oil Company Limited, along the Abakaliki Expressway, Emene.

The agency said the complex had living quarters for the foreign nationals, enabling them to live and work within the same premises.

Marwa said the Nigerian suspect lodged at Adig Suites, 2 Nwafor Orizu Street, Enugu, while NDLEA operatives monitored both locations throughout September and October.

He said surveillance operations, including drone deployment and intelligence analysis, helped investigators establish the activities of the suspects and prepare for the raids.

According to him, more than 200 personnel from the agency’s Strike Force and Enugu State Command were mobilised ahead of the operation.

He said simultaneous raids were conducted at the laboratory and Ezeike’s hotel accommodation in the early hours of November 11, 2026.

“At the San Savanna complex, our men stormed the laboratory and the adjoining guest house, which also served as a stash house. All five Mexicans were arrested at the scene, in the middle of production.

“At the same time, at Adig Suites, our operatives arrested Ezeike in Room 106,” he said.

Marwa alleged that Ezeike subsequently admitted ownership of the laboratory and acknowledged bringing the Mexican nationals into Nigeria to manufacture methamphetamine.

He said the suspect claimed that only a small batch of the drug had been produced and that the foreign nationals were scheduled to leave Nigeria on November 13, two days after their arrest.

The NDLEA chairman said the recovered chemicals included 2,835 kilogrammes of lead acetate, 1,050 kilogrammes of tartaric acid, 450 kilogrammes of mandelic acid, 160 kilogrammes of P2P and 70 kilogrammes of methylamine.

Other items seized included four industrial burners, two industrial distillation units, two boilers, two hydraulic presses, 11 gas cylinders, two freezers, two digital scales and four washing and drying machines.

Marwa said forensic experts confirmed that the equipment was consistent with industrial-scale methamphetamine production.

He alleged that preliminary statements obtained from the suspects pointed to an organised transnational operation involving three layers: a cartel command in Mexico responsible for recruiting and deploying specialists; Ezeike, who allegedly coordinated local operations and logistics; and Mexican production experts led by Ramos-Cardenas.

He further alleged that the cartel deliberately restricted the involvement of Nigerians in laboratory operations to minimise the risk of exposure, while the foreign specialists were paid according to their production output.

Marwa disclosed that the latest operation brought to four the number of industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratories dismantled by the NDLEA in the last four months.

He listed the locations of the previous operations as Enugu, Ogun, Oyo and Ebonyi forests, adding that five Mexican nationals arrested in earlier operations were already in custody facing trial.

With the latest arrests, he said the number of Mexican methamphetamine specialists arrested in Nigeria within four months had risen to 10.

Issuing a warning to international drug cartels, Marwa declared that Nigeria would not be allowed to become a production base, storage facility or transit route for illicit drugs.

” Nigeria is not your laboratory. It is not your warehouse, and it is not your transit route. You may change your passports, your names, your flight routes and your entry points, but you cannot change the fact that we are watching,” he said.

He also warned Nigerians involved in the illicit drug trade that the agency would pursue their arrests, prosecution and assets allegedly acquired through criminal activities.

The NDLEA chairman urged landlords, property owners and communities to monitor activities in their premises and report suspicious operations to the nearest agency office, assuring that the identities of informants would be protected.

Marwa commended personnel of the Special Operations Unit, Strike Force, Forensic Directorate, DOGI, Intelligence Directorate and Enugu State Command for their roles in the operation.

He also acknowledged the support of the Nigeria Immigration Service, international partners and President Bola Tinubu in the agency’s anti-drug operations.

“The war against illicit drugs is a war for the soul of our nation. We will not lose it,” he said.

title: FG proposes tougher scrap metal rules to curb infrastructure vandalism
description:
By Gabriel Ewepu



ABUJA — The Federal Government has proposed tougher regulations for Nigeria’s scrap metal industry, including mandatory traceability and environmental compliance measures, to curb the theft and vandalism of critical national infrastructure.







The proposed framework is also a
content:
By Gabriel Ewepu

ABUJA — The Federal Government has proposed tougher regulations for Nigeria’s scrap metal industry, including mandatory traceability and environmental compliance measures, to curb the theft and vandalism of critical national infrastructure.

The proposed framework is also aimed at sanitising the scrap metal value chain, protecting legitimate businesses, promoting responsible recycling and strengthening the country’s steel and metals manufacturing industry.

The Minister of Steel Development, Prince Shuaibu Abubakar Audu, disclosed this on Tuesday at the second-phase stakeholders’ engagement on the validation of the Draft Scrap Metal (Collection, Trading, Recycling and Regulation) Regulations Policy 2026 in Kano.

Audu, who was represented by the Director, Steel and Non-ferrous Metals Department, Alhaji Umar Tsoho, said Nigeria could not build a competitive steel industry without an organised scrap metal market where materials were lawfully sourced, safely handled, properly documented and supplied to legitimate industrial users.

Speaking on the theme, “Sustainable Scrap Metal Management through Effective Metallurgical Regulation: From Policy to Real Impact”, the minister described scrap metal as a critical resource for industrial development, noting that proper recovery and recycling could boost steel production, foundry operations, employment generation and the circular economy.

He, however, warned that an inadequately regulated industry could encourage the theft and vandalism of public and private infrastructure, unsafe dismantling practices, environmental degradation and significant economic losses.

According to him, the proposed regulations will establish a structured system for licensing and supervising operators, regulating collection and aggregation facilities, ensuring transaction traceability, promoting environmental and occupational safety, preventing illicit trade and strengthening monitoring and enforcement.

Audu clarified that the government’s intention was not to suppress legitimate commercial activities or undermine the livelihoods of Nigerians engaged in scrap metal collection and trading, but to create an orderly business environment where lawful operators could thrive while criminal activities were addressed.

He called for a regulatory framework that would accommodate small-scale operators through practical formalisation processes and requirements proportionate to the scale and risks of their operations, while ensuring that large-scale aggregation, processing and recycling facilities complied with prescribed standards.

On infrastructure vandalism, the minister expressed concern over the illegal acquisition and trading of metallic materials allegedly stolen from public infrastructure, industrial facilities and other protected assets.

He said the theft of electrical cables, railway components, manhole covers and other metallic installations went beyond the loss of materials, as it disrupted essential public services, compromised public safety, increased maintenance costs and undermined national infrastructure development.

The minister recalled that the first phase of the stakeholders’ engagement, held in Lagos from November 9 to 10, 2026, examined critical provisions of the draft regulations, including licensing, operator classification, traceability, collection and sorting facilities, environmental compliance, occupational safety, security and enforcement.

He said contributions from the Lagos engagement had provided valuable input into the ongoing review, adding that the Kano meeting was designed to broaden consultations and incorporate additional regional and operational perspectives, particularly from stakeholders in Northern Nigeria.

Audu urged participants to make specific and practical recommendations to clarify provisions, address implementation challenges and strengthen the effectiveness of the proposed regulations.

He assured that submissions from the Lagos and Kano engagements would be documented, reviewed and harmonised in refining the draft regulations, subject to the applicable legal framework and the initiative’s core objectives.

He also reaffirmed the ministry’s commitment to collaborating with relevant government institutions, industry operators, environmental agencies, security organisations and other stakeholders to ensure effective implementation of the proposed framework.

Meanwhile, the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Steel Development, Ambassador Nura Abba Rimi, represented by the Director, Metallurgical Inspectorate and Environmental Protection Department, Mr Christopher Wanje, said the Kano engagement was a continuation of efforts to ensure that the proposed regulations reflected the realities, expectations and legitimate concerns of industry operators across the country.

Rimi said the regulations would address challenges in the scrap metal value chain through appropriate licensing and compliance requirements, improved traceability, environmental and occupational safety standards, and stronger monitoring and enforcement.

He urged participants to build on the outcomes of the Lagos engagement by submitting practical recommendations on licensing arrangements, classification of operators, operational standards, security, environmental protection, inter-agency collaboration and enforcement.

He assured stakeholders that their contributions would be carefully considered and harmonised to produce a clear, legally sound, practical and implementable regulatory framework.

Also speaking, the Acting Executive Secretary, National Steel Council, Mr Aminu Shehu, represented by the Head of Planning, Research and Statistics, Dr Nana Firdausi Muhammad, reaffirmed the council’s support for the ministry’s efforts to establish a sustainable, transparent and well-regulated scrap metal industry.

He said the council was committed to ensuring effective implementation of the policy as a catalyst for national growth, economic development and employment generation.

Similarly, the Kano State Commandant of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Mohammed Hassan Agalama, who spoke on behalf of the Commandant-General, Prof. Ahmed Abubakar Audi, commended the ministry for initiating the regulatory framework.

Agalama said proper regulation of the scrap metal industry was essential to curbing the theft and vandalism of critical national assets, including electrical installations, pipelines, railway facilities and other government properties.

He reaffirmed the NSCDC’s commitment, in line with its statutory responsibilities, to working with the Ministry of Steel Development and other stakeholders to ensure effective implementation of the proposed regulations.

The post FG proposes tougher scrap metal rules to curb infrastructure vandalism appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: VIDEO: Tinubu arrives in Maiduguri for APC rally
description:
President Bola Tinubu touched down in Maiduguri, the capital of Borno State, on Wednesday for a presidential campaign rally organised by the All Progressives Congress.
A video shared on X by the Special Assistant to the President on Social Media, Dada Olusegun, captured the moment the presidential a
content:
President Bola Tinubu touched down in Maiduguri, the capital of Borno State, on Wednesday for a presidential campaign rally organised by the All Progressives Congress.

A video shared on X by the Special Assistant to the President on Social Media, Dada Olusegun, captured the moment the presidential aircraft landed and Tinubu disembarked onto a red carpet, where he was received by officials and security personnel.

The footage also shows crowds of supporters lining the streets, many of them women in colourful traditional APC plated attire.

They are dancing and waving campaign materials, while men wearing “Hope 2.0” T-shirts, and groups displaying flags and banners bearing messages such as “Tinubu Go Again” were also seen.

In a post accompanying the video, Olusegun wrote, “The moment President Tinubu touched down Maiduguri for the Presidential Campaign Rally in Maiduguri, Borno State. #RenewedHopeInBorno #RenewedHope2_0.”

The visit forms part of the APC’s mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Tinubu, the party’s presidential candidate, is seeking a second term with Vice-President Kashim Shettima, a native of Borno, as his running mate.

The rally is being held at the El-Kanemi Warriors Stadium and is expected to draw party supporters from across the North-East.

PUNCH Online had earlier reported that heavy security has been deployed across Maiduguri.

Major roads, including stretches of Airport Road, Kashim Ibrahim Road and routes leading to the International Conference Centre and Government House, were closed or restricted, with police, military, civil defence and Civilian Joint Task Force personnel manning key points.

Residents were advised to use alternative routes and avoid non-essential movement near the rally areas.

Presidential aides have framed the trip as both a campaign engagement and an opportunity to reinforce the Federal Government’s relationship with Borno.

The state has endured years of Boko Haram insurgency, and the administration has pointed to reconstruction efforts, infrastructure projects and the return of displaced persons as reasons for continued support.

title: PHOTOS: NDLEA busts N304bn meth lab in Enugu, arrests Nigerian, five Mexicans
description:
The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency has dismantled an industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratory in Enugu State, arresting a Nigerian drug baron, Enoch Ezeike, and five Mexican nationals allegedly brought into the country to manufacture the illicit substance.
The Chairman of the NDLEA, Brig. G
content:
The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency has dismantled an industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratory in Enugu State, arresting a Nigerian drug baron, Enoch Ezeike, and five Mexican nationals allegedly brought into the country to manufacture the illicit substance.

The Chairman of the NDLEA, Brig. Gen. Buba Marwa (retd.), disclosed this while addressing journalists in Abuja on Wednesday, saying the operation led to the seizure of 1,512 kilogrammes of methamphetamine and 6,680 kilogrammes of precursor chemicals.

Marwa said the production cycle initiated by the cartel was expected to yield methamphetamine worth $226.8m, equivalent to approximately N303.9bn.

He described the operation as a transnational investigation that began with intelligence on the Nigerian suspect in April 2026 and extended across Mexico, Colombia, France and the Republic of Benin before the suspects were arrested in Enugu.

According to him, the agency identified Ezeike as a specialist in establishing clandestine methamphetamine laboratories and linked him to a Mexican drug expert, Oscar Ramos-Cardenas, who allegedly specialises in large-scale industrial production of the substance.

Marwa said the NDLEA initially intercepted the five Mexican nationals when they arrived in Abuja on August 28, 2026, but they later returned to Nigeria through the Republic of Benin using forged passports.

He said the agency deliberately allowed them into the country to enable it to track the entire network and dismantle its operations.

“Rather than turn them back again, I allowed them to come in. We wanted the whole network: the meth specialists, the financier, the factory, and the products,” he said.

The NDLEA chairman said the agency was alerted on September 19, 2026, that five Mexicans had arrived in Cotonou, Benin Republic, intending to enter Nigeria through the land border.

The five suspects were identified by their names on the allegedly forged passports and their real names as follows: Gonzalez Numez Lucas, also known as Oscar Ramos-Cardenas, the alleged leader and chief specialist; Lopez Salvador Vasquez Esperanza, whose real name is Juan Antonio Sarabia-Cabrera; Hernandez Cortes Carlos Fuentes, whose real name is Luis Enrique Garcia-Amador; Fernandez Rio Mateo Jimenez, whose real name is Jose Alejandro Renteria-Reyes; and Rodriguez Araya Andres Perez, whose real name is Salomon Cabanillas-Torres.

He said three of them entered Nigeria through the Seme border post on September 20, while the remaining two arrived the following day.

According to him, NDLEA special operatives monitored their movements throughout the operation.

He said Ezeike received them in Lagos and lodged them in a hotel, where he was observed having breakfast with them on September 22 before moving them to Enugu.

“While the Mexicans lived and worked in the San Savanna complex, Ezeike stayed at Adig Suites, 2 Nwafor Orizu Street, Enugu, moving about in three vehicles: a blue Toyota Corolla, a red Toyota RAV4 and a Lexus RX 350.

“Throughout September and October, our officers kept watch on both locations. In the course of surveillance, we watched the regular movement of Ezeike’s blue Corolla drive into San Savanna, stay a few minutes, and return to Adig Suites. Assisted by appropriate tools such as the deployment of a drone and other intelligence deductions, we were able to put all pieces together by November 7, 2026,” he said.

The NDLEA chairman said operatives conducted surveillance on both locations throughout September and October before launching simultaneous raids on November 11, 2026.

“Having got all this down, it was now time to strike. On 9th November, 2026, we assembled over 200 personnel of our Strike Force and Enugu State Command into a staging area. On 10th November, 2026, I gave the order to take down the lab. At about 5:00 AM on Wednesday, 11th November 2026, operatives of our Special Operations Unit, Strike Force, Forensic Directorate, and Enugu State Command carried out simultaneous raids on both locations.

“Statements by the suspects since their arrest confirm that this was no first-time venture but an organised, recurring transnational operation with three layers: a cartel command in Mexico that recruits, deploys and pays the specialists; Ezeike as the local coordinator who built the laboratory, procured the chemicals and arranged travel, transport and false documents; and the Mexican production crew led by Ramos-Cardenas, whose supporting members change with each deployment,” he said.

Marwa disclosed that the five Mexican nationals were arrested at the laboratory while production was ongoing, while Ezeike was apprehended in Room 106 of Adig Suites.

He said the Nigerian suspect subsequently admitted ownership of the laboratory and bringing the Mexican nationals into the country to manufacture methamphetamine.

“He told us that they had produced only a small batch so far—actually 49 kilogrammes had been produced. He also told us that the Mexicans were due to leave Nigeria two days later, on Friday, 13th November 2026.

“In other words, ladies and gentlemen, we caught them in the nick of time—with two more days they would have left,” he added.

The agency recovered 1,512 kilogrammes of methamphetamine, comprising finished products and the substance still undergoing production, as well as 6.6 tonnes of precursor and essential chemicals in 20 different types.

The chemicals included 2,835 kilogrammes of lead acetate, 1,050 kilogrammes of tartaric acid, 450 kilogrammes of mandelic acid, 160 kilogrammes of P2P and 70 kilogrammes of methylamine.

Other items recovered included four industrial burners, two industrial distillation units, two boilers, two hydraulic presses, 11 gas cylinders, two freezers, two digital scales and four washing and drying machines.

Marwa said forensic experts had confirmed that the chemicals and equipment were consistent with industrial methamphetamine production.

He explained that investigations revealed a three-layer structure within the cartel, comprising a foreign-based command in Mexico responsible for recruiting and deploying specialists, Ezeike as the Nigerian facilitator responsible for establishing the laboratory and procuring materials, and the Mexican production team.

According to him, the cartel deliberately excluded Nigerians from the laboratory to minimise the possibility of its activities being exposed.

The NDLEA chairman further disclosed that the latest operation brought to 10 the number of Mexican methamphetamine specialists arrested in Nigeria within four months.

Marwa noted that the agency had dismantled four industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratories in the last four months, located in Enugu, the Ogun forest, the Oyo forest and the Ebonyi forest.

According to him, five Mexican nationals arrested during earlier operations were already in prison custody facing trial.

Marwa warned international drug cartels against using Nigeria as a production base, saying the agency would continue to track their operations and prosecute those involved.

“To foreign cartels, wherever they may be: Nigeria is not your laboratory. Nigeria is not your warehouse. It is not your transit route,” he said.

He also described Nigerian drug barons facilitating the activities of foreign cartels as traitors, warning that the agency would pursue their assets and properties.

“We will find you. We will arrest you. We will prosecute you. And we will go after every naira, every property, and every asset that you gained from this illicit trade,” Marwa said.

He urged landlords, property owners and communities to be vigilant about activities taking place in their neighbourhoods and report suspicious occupants to the nearest NDLEA office or other law enforcement agencies.

The NDLEA chairman commended the agency’s Special Operations Unit, Strike Force, Forensic Directorate, Intelligence Directorate and Enugu State Command for their roles in the operation.

He also acknowledged the cooperation of the Nigeria Immigration Service and other international partners, as well as the support of President Bola Tinubu for the agency’s anti-drug campaign.

The post PHOTOS: NDLEA busts N304bn meth lab in Enugu, arrests Nigerian, five Mexicans appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: ‘Fix Edo roads or I won’t return’ – Benny Hinn tells Okpebholo
description:
International evangelist, Pastor Benny Hinn, has urged Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, to urgently repair roads across the state, saying he would be reluctant to return if the poor road conditions persist.







Hinn made the remarks in a video circulating on social media after his recent vis
content:
International evangelist, Pastor Benny Hinn, has urged Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, to urgently repair roads across the state, saying he would be reluctant to return if the poor road conditions persist.

Hinn made the remarks in a video circulating on social media after his recent visit to Edo State, where he was hosted by Apostle Johnson Suleman, founder of Omega Fire Ministries International.

The US-based televangelist disclosed that he met with Okpebholo during the visit and appealed to him to address the condition of roads he travelled on.

“I went to Edo State and I met the governor. I just hope he fixes the roads. I don’t ever want to take that kind of bumpy road again,” Hinn said.

“If they ever want me back in Edo State, the governor has to fix those bad roads,” he added.

Hinn also expressed concern about a possible visit to Warri, Delta State, recalling the poor condition of roads he encountered during an earlier trip to the city.

His comments come amid complaints by residents and motorists about deteriorating road infrastructure in parts of Edo State, with some routes reportedly affected by potholes and failed sections.

One of the roads that has attracted complaints from commuters and transport operators is the Benin-Sapele-Warri highway, which links parts of Edo and Delta states.

In September, the Edo State Government acknowledged the poor condition of several roads across the state, blaming some of the deterioration on what it described as poor-quality construction carried out under the previous administration.

The government appealed to residents to be patient, promising extensive road rehabilitation during the dry season.

Okpebholo also inspected some road and drainage projects in November and pledged to address the state’s infrastructure challenges.

The post ‘Fix Edo roads or I won’t return’ – Benny Hinn tells Okpebholo appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Group alleges plot to blackmail Uzodimma, APC, says plan has failed
description: The Renewed Hope Ambassadors (South East) says it has uncovered a plot to tarnish the image of the Director-General of the Renewed Hope Ambassadors (RHA), Governor of Imo State, Chairman of the Progressive Governors’ Forum (PGF) and Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campa
content:
The Renewed Hope Ambassadors (South East) says it has uncovered a plot to tarnish the image of the Director-General of the Renewed Hope Ambassadors (RHA), Governor of Imo State, Chairman of the Progressive Governors’ Forum (PGF) and Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Hope Uzodinma.

Speaking in a statement signed by Chief Henry Ikoh (Abia State), Chief Okey Ezenwa (Anambra State), H.E. Barr. Kelechi Igwe (Ebonyi State), Hon. U.S.A. Igweshi (Enugu State), and Rt. Hon. Goodluck Opia (Imo State), the group disclosed that the perpetrators who are not from the Southeast “attribute fictitious quotes to Governor Uzodinma on social media, claiming that the Governor had asked the Southeast to support a Presidential Candidate of another political party from the region.”

“This unwarranted plot against Governor Uzodinma and the South East is deeply reprehensible, as he never made any such comments as claimed.

“It is rather clear that these merchants of falsehoods who are desperate to alienate Governor Uzodinma from the President so as to weaken the APC’s established strength in the Southeast region ahead of the critical 2027 general election.

“This plot is contrived basically to weaken the bargaining power of the entire Southeast after the victory of the President,” the statement said.

“It is a well-known fact that Governor Uzodinma is a frontline and highly respected leader who is working tirelessly in strengthening the APC both at the national and regional levels.

“He is a major propagator and promoter of President Tinubu’s achievements and re-election bid, which he further enhanced by the unity he has ensured among APC governors.

“It is on record that Governor Uzodinma defied the odds to strengthen the APC massively in the South East. Through dedicated effort, personal investment, and deep-rooted political networks and alliances, he successfully built the APC into a dominant political force in the region.

“Additionally, Governor Uzodinma’s effective coordination of the Renewed Hope Ambassadors—to promote President Tinubu’s achievements and re-election bid—continues to yield unprecedented results in educating Nigerians about the President’s vision and efforts for the nation.

“It is therefore obvious that the President, rather than Governor Uzodinma, is the target of this sinister plot by these unscrupulous elements, who know that alienating Governor Uzodinma and the South East from the President is a pathway to weakening his re-election in 2027.

“We therefore urge Governor Uzodinma not to be distracted, discouraged, or deterred by the activities of these mischievous elements. He should remain focused and discount their despicable acts, bearing in mind that these individuals are inconsequential minds who do not mean well for the nation.

“Governor Uzodinma is assured that the South East and the APC in the region and beyond are behind him in his wholehearted loyalty and support for the President and his re-election in 2027, and no amount of falsehood, propaganda, and lies can detract from this commitment,” the group added.

title: I never tapped Ribadu’s phone – El-Rufai
description:
Former Kaduna State governor, Nasir El-Rufai, has told a Federal High Court in Abuja that his claim about listening to the telephone conversation of National Security Adviser (NSA), Nuhu Ribadu, was an exaggeration made during a political exchange.
El-Rufai gave the explanation while testifying in h
content:
Former Kaduna State governor, Nasir El-Rufai, has told a Federal High Court in Abuja that his claim about listening to the telephone conversation of National Security Adviser (NSA), Nuhu Ribadu, was an exaggeration made during a political exchange.

El-Rufai gave the explanation while testifying in his ongoing phone-tapping case, insisting that he neither intercepted Ribadu’s calls nor possessed the equipment or technical expertise to do so.

Under questioning by his lawyer, Paul Erokoro, during Tuesday’s court session, the former governor said he never owned call interception equipment.

He also told the court that he lacked the technical knowledge to conduct telephone surveillance and had no access to Ribadu’s communication systems.

Explaining his choice of words during a February interview on Arise Television, El-Rufai said his use of “we” referred to opposition politicians and was not an admission of personal involvement in phone interception.

“I used ‘we’ to refer to opposition politicians. When I said ‘tapped’, it was an embellishment intended to make the government feel the pain we are feeling. It was rhetorical and exaggerated. My objective was to engage in political retort and linguistic flourish,” he said.

The former governor’s clarification came as he continued his testimony in the phone-tapping case before the Federal High Court in Abuja.

title: ‘Ebube Dike’, Tinubu Mourns, Pens Tribute To Late Actor Pete Edochie
description: President Bola Tinubu has mourned the death of veteran Nollywood actor Peter Edochie, who died on Wednesday at the age of 79 after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer.His death was announced on Wednesday by his son, Chief Leo Pete Edochie, in a statement shared on Instagram on behalf of the fami
content:
President Bola Tinubu has mourned the death of veteran Nollywood actor Peter Edochie, who died on Wednesday at the age of 79 after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer.

His death was announced on Wednesday by his son, Chief Leo Pete Edochie, in a statement shared on Instagram on behalf of the family.

According to the announcement, the actor died at 12:30 am on November 25, 2026, in Enugu, Nigeria.

Tinubu, while reacting to his death in a statement personally signed by him, noted that he received Edochie’s death news with “deep sorrow”.

He also paid tribute to the late actor, describing him as “exceptional”.

“It was with deep sorrow that I received the news of the passing of Chief Peter Uwadiegwu Ogugua Edochie, better known as Pete Edochie.

“Chief Edochie was an exceptional actor – one of the progenitors of our vibrant film industry, Nollywood. He was graceful and larger than life, both on the screen and in person.

“He was one of Africa’s most recognisable thespians. For decades, he plied his craft, bringing joy, laughter, and charm to many homes.

“I recall his unforgettable portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s evergreen novel, Things Fall Apart, in the 1980s, and his many brilliant performances afterwards.

“Through memorable performances in productions such as Igodo, Rituals and Lionheart, he helped shape the evolution and international visibility of Nollywood.

“His portrayal of traditional institutions, family structures, African values, and the complexities of human relationships helped project Nigeria’s cultural heritage and storytelling traditions to audiences worldwide.

“Pete Edochie was not only an actor; he was also an administrator, broadcaster, and journalist- truly one of our finest. His place in the pantheon of those who shaped the film industry, our common norms, and popular culture remains indisputable.

“As I mourn the passing of this legendary actor, I also reflect on his life. Pete Edochie lived well. He played his part and exited gracefully.

“In his works, he lives forever. Many generations will talk about the life and work of Chief Edochie in the arts industry and academia, in barbershops and marketplaces, and indeed wherever people gather.

“On behalf of my family and the Federal Government of Nigeria, I extend my condolences to the Edochie family, his friends, associates, and the entire Nigerian film industry.

“May God Almighty grant “Ebube Dike” eternal rest.”

Edochie hailed from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, Anambra State. He is survived by his wife, Josephine Edochie, his children, siblings and other relatives.

The late actor was born on March 7, 1947, and built a career spanning broadcasting and acting, becoming one of the most recognisable figures in Nigeria’s entertainment industry.

He began his professional career in broadcasting in 1967 with the Eastern Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation, where he worked for several years and rose to senior management positions, including Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director.

His transition into acting brought him national prominence in the 1980s when he portrayed Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s novel, Things Fall Apart.

The performance established him as a formidable screen presence and opened the door to a long career in Nigerian cinema.

Over the years, he became particularly associated with roles as traditional rulers, community leaders and family patriarchs, with his deep voice, commanding delivery and frequent use of proverbs becoming defining features of his performances.

His film credits include Igodo, Rituals and Lionheart, the 2018 film directed by Genevieve Nnaji.

In recognition of his contributions to the entertainment industry, he received the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003.

He also received the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards Industry Merit Award and other lifetime achievement honours.

The post ‘Ebube Dike’, Tinubu Mourns, Pens Tribute To Late Actor Pete Edochie appeared first on Channels Television.

title: APC Spokesman Morka questions NDC’s ‘Rig and Die’ slogan, challenges Peter Obi
description:
The National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Felix Morka, has challenged the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) to explain the legal basis for its “rig and die” slogan, questioning whether Nigerian law prescribes the death penalty for electoral offences.
Morka argued that
content:
The National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Felix Morka, has challenged the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) to explain the legal basis for its “rig and die” slogan, questioning whether Nigerian law prescribes the death penalty for electoral offences.

Morka argued that anyone suspected of manipulating election results should be arrested, investigated and prosecuted under the law instead of facing punishment determined by political parties or their supporters.

The APC spokesman made the remarks on Wednesday during an appearance on News Central, where he reacted to allegations that NDC supporters had engaged in violence against members of the ruling party.

His comments came after Peter Obi, the NDC presidential candidate, defended the party’s “rig and die” slogan during an interview with Channels Television.

Obi had spoken about the slogan following the party’s town hall meeting in Taraba State on Tuesday.

Obi had dismissed concerns over the message, insisting that the supporters were opposed to election rigging, not political campaigns.

“They said we said ‘rig and die.’ We didn’t say ‘campaign and die.’ What we, people said is that they don’t want rigging this time. They didn’t say they don’t want campaign this time. If anything, they want campaign this time,” Obi said.

However, reacting to the explanation, Morka said the slogan was inflammatory and questioned the implication of allowing individuals to determine who had rigged an election and should therefore die.

“Now, what does that mean? What message are you sending when you appoint yourself as custodians of elections, and therefore anyone you consider to have rigged an election — because that’s a subjective standard — should die,” he said.

Morka said he had watched a video in which Obi defended the statement, adding that the NDC candidate had acknowledged that the message was “rig and die” rather than “campaign and die”.

The APC spokesman then challenged Obi and the NDC to explain the legal justification for such a position.

“So, if somebody rigs an election, since when did Nigerian law prescribe the death penalty for rigging an election?” he asked.

Morka maintained that anyone suspected of electoral malpractice should be apprehended and made to face the consequences provided by law.

“I think as a lawyer and as a citizen, that anyone who rigs an election should be apprehended and be made to face the law as provided by the law, not as provided by Peter Obi or the NDC stalwarts who make this very incendiary comment,” he said.

Beyond the slogan, Morka also accused the NDC of making unsubstantiated allegations of violence against the APC without formally reporting the incidents to the police or seeking investigations by independent authorities.

“So when the NDC comes out and they make allegations, if you look at all the allegations they make, there’s not one that they have managed or even attempted to furnish any kind of substantiation,” he said.

He argued that the opposition party relied on social media to make accusations and expected the ruling party to respond without first seeking official investigations.

“They will never go to the police to make a proper complaint. So, they just make up stories and they come to you and they drop it on social media, and then we are supposed to respond because we’re the ruling party,” Morka said.

The APC spokesman also accused NDC supporters of displaying machetes at political gatherings, citing videos allegedly showing people carrying the weapons during campaign activities in Lagos and Delta states.

He said the NDC had not denied the videos circulating online, adding that such displays raised questions about the party’s own conduct amid its allegations of political violence.

The post APC Spokesman Morka questions NDC’s ‘Rig and Die’ slogan, challenges Peter Obi appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Ex-England star Sterling banned from driving for two years
description:
Former England international, Raheem Sterling, has been banned from driving for two years after being sentenced over dangerous driving, failing to provide a specimen for analysis and possession of nitrous oxide.
The 31-year-old footballer was handed a 12-month prison sentence, suspended for 18 month
content:
Former England international, Raheem Sterling, has been banned from driving for two years after being sentenced over dangerous driving, failing to provide a specimen for analysis and possession of nitrous oxide.

The 31-year-old footballer was handed a 12-month prison sentence, suspended for 18 months, and ordered to complete 100 hours of unpaid work.

Sterling was arrested in May following a crash involving his Lamborghini near the M3 motorway in Hampshire, United Kingdom.

He pleaded guilty to dangerous driving on the M3, M25, A327 and Minley Road, as well as possessing nitrous oxide, a Class C drug, and failing to provide a specimen for analysis.

According to the BBC on Wednesday, eyewitnesses told police they had seen the driver of the Lamborghini inhaling from a white balloon before the incident. One woman initially mistook the balloon for an inflated airbag.

During the court proceedings, Jason Bartfeld KC, representing Sterling, said the former Chelsea and Arsenal winger had recognised the unhealthy coping mechanisms that contributed to his situation.

Bartfeld said Sterling “recognised the various unhealthy coping mechanisms that brought him to this position.”

Police footage also showed the footballer’s arrest following the incident.

Sterling, who currently does not have a club, has earned 82 caps for England, with his last international appearance coming at the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar.

The former Manchester City and Liverpool forward remains one of England’s most experienced players of his generation.

The post Ex-England star Sterling banned from driving for two years appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

เมื่อพูดถึงเว็บแทงบอลที่คนไทยคุ้นเคย ชื่อของ UFABET มักเป็นหนึ่งในชื่อที่ถูกพูดถึงควบคู่กับการเดิมพันฟุตบอลออนไลน์ ภายในระบบมีทั้งฟุตบอลลีกใหญ่ ลีกย่อย การแข่งขันระดับทีมชาติ รวมถึงตลาดเดิมพันก่อนแข่งและระหว่างการแข่งขัน

แต่สำหรับคนที่เพิ่งรู้จักยูฟ่าเบท อาจยังไม่เข้าใจว่าหน้าเว็บแทงบอลมีส่วนประกอบ
content:
เมื่อพูดถึงเว็บแทงบอลที่คนไทยคุ้นเคย ชื่อของ UFABET มักเป็นหนึ่งในชื่อที่ถูกพูดถึงควบคู่กับการเดิมพันฟุตบอลออนไลน์ ภายในระบบมีทั้งฟุตบอลลีกใหญ่ ลีกย่อย การแข่งขันระดับทีมชาติ รวมถึงตลาดเดิมพันก่อนแข่งและระหว่างการแข่งขัน

แต่สำหรับคนที่เพิ่งรู้จักยูฟ่าเบท อาจยังไม่เข้าใจว่าหน้าเว็บแทงบอลมีส่วนประกอบอะไรบ้าง ราคาที่แสดงอยู่หมายถึงอะไร และการเดิมพันแต่ละรูปแบบแตกต่างกันอย่างไร บทความนี้จะพาไปทำความรู้จักกับระบบฟุตบอลของ UFABET และรายละเอียดที่เกี่ยวข้องกับการแทงบอลออนไลน์

ทำความรู้จัก UFABET กับระบบเว็บแทงบอลออนไลน์

UFABET เป็นชื่อแพลตฟอร์มเดิมพันออนไลน์ที่มีบริการหลายประเภท โดยฟุตบอลถือเป็นหนึ่งในหมวดหลักของระบบ Sportsbook ภายในหน้าเดิมพันจะมีตารางการแข่งขัน เวลาเริ่มแข่ง ราคาต่อรอง ค่าน้ำ และตลาดเดิมพันของแต่ละคู่แสดงอยู่ด้วยกัน

สิ่งที่แตกต่างจากเว็บไซต์รายงานผลฟุตบอลทั่วไปคือ ข้อมูลราคาบอลจะมีการเปลี่ยนแปลงตามช่วงเวลา โดยเฉพาะเมื่อใกล้เริ่มการแข่งขันหรือมีเหตุการณ์สำคัญเกิดขึ้นระหว่างเกม เช่น การทำประตู ใบแดง หรือการเปลี่ยนแปลงของสกอร์

นอกจากฟุตบอลแล้ว ระบบ Sportsbook ยังอาจครอบคลุมกีฬาอย่างบาสเกตบอล เทนนิส วอลเลย์บอล และอีสปอร์ต ขึ้นอยู่กับรายการที่เปิดให้บริการในแต่ละวัน

เว็บแทงบอล UFABET มีฟุตบอลลีกไหนบ้าง

ฟุตบอลที่ปรากฏในระบบเดิมพันไม่ได้จำกัดอยู่เพียงลีกดังของยุโรปเท่านั้น แต่ยังครอบคลุมการแข่งขันจากหลายภูมิภาค โดยสามารถแบ่งออกเป็นกลุ่มหลัก ๆ ได้ดังนี้

  • ฟุตบอลลีกอังกฤษ — พรีเมียร์ลีก แชมเปียนชิป ลีกวัน และลีกทู
  • ฟุตบอลลีกยุโรป — ลาลีกา เซเรียอา บุนเดสลีกา และลีกเอิง
  • ฟุตบอลถ้วยยุโรป — ยูฟ่าแชมเปียนส์ลีก ยูโรปาลีก และคอนเฟอเรนซ์ลีก
  • ฟุตบอลเอเชีย — ไทยลีก เจลีก เคลีก และการแข่งขันระดับสโมสรเอเชีย
  • ฟุตบอลอเมริกาใต้ — ลีกบราซิล ลีกอาร์เจนตินา และโคปาลิเบอร์ตาดอเรส
  • ฟุตบอลทีมชาติ — ฟุตบอลโลก ฟุตบอลยูโร เอเชียนคัพ และการแข่งขันรอบคัดเลือก

จำนวนคู่แข่งขันและตลาดที่เปิดในแต่ละลีกอาจไม่เท่ากัน โดยฟุตบอลรายการใหญ่มักมีตลาดย่อยมากกว่าการแข่งขันในลีกระดับรอง

หน้าเว็บแทงบอลของยูฟ่าเบทมีข้อมูลอะไรบ้าง

เมื่อเปิดหน้า Sportsbook ผู้เล่นจะพบตัวเลขและสัญลักษณ์หลายอย่างอยู่ในตารางเดียวกัน หากไม่คุ้นเคยกับหน้าตาของเว็บแทงบอล อาจแยกไม่ออกว่าตัวเลขไหนคือราคาต่อรองและตัวเลขไหนคือค่าน้ำ

ข้อมูลบนหน้าเว็บ ความหมาย
ชื่อทีมแข่งขัน ทีมเจ้าบ้านและทีมเยือน
เวลาแข่งขัน กำหนดเวลาเริ่มการแข่งขัน
Handicap ราคาต่อรองระหว่างสองทีม
Over/Under เส้นจำนวนประตูรวม
1X2 ราคาของผลชนะ เสมอ และแพ้
Odds อัตราจ่ายของแต่ละตลาด
Live Score สกอร์ปัจจุบันระหว่างการแข่งขัน
Bet Slip รายละเอียดรายการเดิมพัน

ข้อมูลเหล่านี้เป็นองค์ประกอบพื้นฐานที่พบได้ในเว็บแทงบอลทั่วไป ส่วนตำแหน่งและรูปแบบการแสดงผลอาจแตกต่างกันตามระบบ Sportsbook ของแต่ละเว็บไซต์

แทงบอลก่อนแข่งกับแทงบอลสด UFABET ต่างกันอย่างไร

การเดิมพันฟุตบอลแบ่งออกเป็นสองช่วงหลัก คือก่อนเริ่มการแข่งขันและระหว่างการแข่งขัน ซึ่งมีลักษณะของราคาและข้อมูลประกอบแตกต่างกัน

เดิมพันฟุตบอลก่อนแข่ง (Pre-match)

เป็นตลาดที่เปิดก่อนการแข่งขันเริ่มขึ้น ราคาบอลอาจเปลี่ยนแปลงตามข่าวนักเตะบาดเจ็บ รายชื่อผู้เล่นตัวจริง สภาพทีม และปัจจัยอื่นที่เกี่ยวข้องกับการแข่งขัน

เดิมพันฟุตบอลระหว่างแข่ง (Live Betting)

เป็นตลาดที่เปิดระหว่างการแข่งขัน ราคาจะเปลี่ยนตามเหตุการณ์ในสนาม เช่น เวลาที่เหลือ จำนวนประตู และจำนวนผู้เล่นของแต่ละทีม บางตลาดอาจถูกระงับชั่วคราวเมื่อเกิดเหตุการณ์สำคัญ

ความแตกต่างหลักของทั้งสองรูปแบบจึงอยู่ที่ช่วงเวลาและข้อมูลที่ใช้ประกอบการกำหนดราคา โดยตลาดบอลสดมีความผันผวนและเปลี่ยนแปลงรวดเร็วกว่าตลาดก่อนแข่ง

ทำไมราคาบอล UFABET ถึงเปลี่ยนระหว่างวัน

บางครั้งฟุตบอลคู่เดิมที่เปิดราคาไว้ในช่วงเช้า อาจมีราคาต่อรองและค่าน้ำเปลี่ยนไปเมื่อถึงช่วงเย็น ซึ่งเป็นเรื่องที่พบได้ทั่วไปในระบบเดิมพันกีฬา

ปัจจัยที่ส่งผลต่อการเปลี่ยนแปลงของราคา ได้แก่

  • ข่าวอาการบาดเจ็บหรือการติดโทษแบนของนักเตะ
  • การประกาศรายชื่อผู้เล่นตัวจริง
  • สภาพอากาศและความพร้อมของสนามแข่งขัน
  • การปรับราคาตามตลาดและการบริหารความเสี่ยงของผู้ให้บริการ
  • เหตุการณ์ที่เกิดขึ้นระหว่างการแข่งขันสำหรับตลาดบอลสด

อย่างไรก็ตาม การเปลี่ยนแปลงของราคาบอลไม่ได้เป็นเครื่องยืนยันว่าทีมใดจะชนะ เพราะราคาที่แสดงเป็นเพียงการประเมินของตลาดในช่วงเวลานั้น ไม่ใช่ผลการแข่งขันล่วงหน้า

เว็บแทงบอล UFABET มีจุดเด่นอะไรบ้าง

จุดเด่นของ UFABET อยู่ที่การรวบรวมการแข่งขันฟุตบอลและตลาดเดิมพันหลายรูปแบบไว้ในระบบเดียว ไม่ได้จำกัดเฉพาะการทายผลแพ้-ชนะ แต่ยังมีราคาต่อรอง จำนวนประตู และตลาดย่อยของแต่ละคู่แข่งขัน โดยมีองค์ประกอบหลักที่น่าสนใจดังนี้

  • ฟุตบอลหลากหลายลีก มีทั้งลีกชั้นนำของยุโรป ลีกเอเชีย ฟุตบอลถ้วย และการแข่งขันระดับทีมชาติ
  • ตลาดเดิมพันหลายรูปแบบ ทั้งบอลเต็ง บอลสเต็ป แฮนดิแคป สูง/ต่ำ และทายผลสกอร์
  • ระบบแทงบอลสด แสดงสกอร์ เวลาแข่งขัน และราคาที่เปลี่ยนแปลงตามเหตุการณ์ในสนาม
  • รวมกีฬาหลายประเภท นอกจากฟุตบอลยังมีกีฬาอย่างบาสเกตบอล เทนนิส วอลเลย์บอล และอีสปอร์ต
  • รองรับการใช้งานหลายอุปกรณ์ สามารถเข้าถึงระบบผ่านมือถือ แท็บเล็ต และคอมพิวเตอร์ได้

อย่างไรก็ตาม จำนวนลีก ตลาดเดิมพัน และฟังก์ชันต่าง ๆ อาจแตกต่างกันตามระบบของผู้ให้บริการและช่วงเวลาการแข่งขัน ส่วนเรื่องราคาบอลและอัตราจ่ายควรพิจารณาจากราคาที่แสดงจริงในแต่ละคู่

ทางเข้า UFABET และวิธีเข้าสู่ระบบเว็บแทงบอล

สำหรับผู้เล่นที่มีบัญชีสมาชิกอยู่แล้ว ทางเข้า UFABET เป็นหน้าที่ใช้เชื่อมไปยังระบบ Login ก่อนเข้าสู่หมวดแทงบอลออนไลน์ โดยสามารถเข้าผ่าน Browser ได้ทั้งบนมือถือและคอมพิวเตอร์

การเข้าสู่ระบบใช้เพียง Username และ Password ที่ลงทะเบียนไว้ เมื่อ Login สำเร็จ ผู้เล่นจะสามารถเข้าถึงหน้าสมาชิก ตารางการแข่งขัน ราคาบอล ประวัติการเดิมพัน และเมนูจัดการบัญชีได้ตามปกติ

กรณีที่เปิดทางเข้าเดิมไม่ได้หรือพบว่าหน้าเว็บไซต์เปลี่ยนไปจากที่เคยใช้ ควรเช็กชื่อโดเมนและแหล่งที่มาของลิงก์ก่อนกรอกข้อมูลบัญชี ไม่ควรเข้าสู่ระบบผ่านลิงก์ที่ไม่รู้จักหรือส่งรหัสผ่านให้บุคคลอื่น เพื่อป้องกันปัญหาบัญชีสมาชิกถูกนำไปใช้งานโดยไม่ได้รับอนุญาต

คำถามที่พบบ่อยเกี่ยวกับเว็บแทงบอล UFABET

UFABET มีเฉพาะการเดิมพันฟุตบอลหรือไม่?

นอกจากฟุตบอลแล้ว ชื่อ UFABET ยังเกี่ยวข้องกับบริการเดิมพันกีฬา คาสิโนสด บาคาร่า และเกมสล็อต โดยรายการที่เปิดให้บริการขึ้นอยู่กับแต่ละระบบ

ราคาบอลกับค่าน้ำต่างกันอย่างไร?

ราคาบอลหรือราคาต่อรองใช้กำหนดเงื่อนไขในการตัดสินผลเดิมพัน ส่วนค่าน้ำใช้คำนวณผลตอบแทนเมื่อเดิมพันชนะ

ฟุตบอลทุกลีกมีตลาดเดิมพันเหมือนกันไหม?

ไม่เหมือนกัน ฟุตบอลรายการใหญ่และการแข่งขันที่ได้รับความสนใจสูงมักมีตลาดย่อยมากกว่าลีกขนาดเล็ก

ราคาบอลที่เปลี่ยนไปหมายความว่าผลการแข่งขันจะเปลี่ยนหรือไม่?

ไม่เกี่ยวข้องโดยตรง ราคาบอลสะท้อนการประเมินและการปรับตัวของตลาด ไม่สามารถรับประกันผลการแข่งขันจริงได้

สรุปภาพรวมเว็บแทงบอล UFABET

UFABET เป็นชื่อที่เกี่ยวข้องกับระบบเดิมพันฟุตบอลออนไลน์ โดยมีองค์ประกอบสำคัญอย่างตารางการแข่งขัน ราคาต่อรอง ค่าน้ำ และตลาดเดิมพันหลายรูปแบบ ทั้งก่อนแข่งและระหว่างการแข่งขัน

การทำความเข้าใจข้อมูลเหล่านี้จะช่วยให้แยกความหมายของตัวเลขบนหน้า Sportsbook ได้ชัดเจนขึ้น รวมถึงเข้าใจว่าราคาบอลมีที่มาและเปลี่ยนแปลงได้อย่างไร ทั้งนี้ การพนันมีความเสี่ยงต่อการสูญเสียเงิน และการพนันออนไลน์ที่ไม่ได้รับอนุญาตถือเป็นสิ่งผิดกฎหมายในประเทศไทย

title: Ejiro Amos Tafiri to unveil SS27 collection in Abuja
description:

The Abuja showcase follows the collection’s unveiling at The Ci
content:
Nigerian fashion designer Ejiro Amos Tafiri will unveil her Spring/Summer 2027 (SS27) collection, tagged Reverie, in Abuja later this month, extending the presentation of her latest designs beyond Lagos to the Federal Capital Territory.

The Abuja showcase follows the collection’s unveiling at The Citadel, in Lagos, during the Lagos Fashion Week period. The presentation is expected to bring together fashion industry stakeholders, luxury consumers, government officials and other guests in the capital.

The move also comes as the fashion house seeks to strengthen its presence in Northern Nigeria, building on its existing Abuja flagship. The showcase provides an opportunity for the brand to reach more consumers in the region and expand its engagement with Nigeria’s luxury fashion market.

The Reverie collection explores themes of renewal, playfulness and reinvention, drawing inspiration from nature and the experience of walking through a forest. Its designs combine sculptural tailoring with more fluid pieces intended for everyday retail.

The collection features materials such as sheer organza, Chantilly lace, chiffon and hand-woven aso-oke, alongside nature-inspired embroidery. It also incorporates contemporary interpretations of traditional Nigerian clothing, including the iro, buba and danshiki, as well as eveningwear and menswear. The designs feature a range of colours, moving from neutral shades to lime green, fuchsia, pink and deep burgundy.

The Abuja presentation is part of activities marking 16 years of the fashion house’s operations. The Lagos unveiling was accompanied by the third edition of its industry symposium, Fashioning a Legacy: Leaving a Mark in Time, held at the British Council in Ikoyi.

The symposium brought together participants to discuss the fashion industry’s development and the role of industry practitioners in building a lasting fashion business.

The Abuja event will feature a runway presentation and private viewing of the SS27 collection. The fashion house said the event would bring together diplomats, government representatives, fashion editors and luxury consumers.

title: UPDATED: El-Rufai denies tapping Ribadu’s phone, says remarks exaggerated
description:
Former Kaduna State Governor, Nasir El-Rufai, has told the Federal High Court in Abuja that he neither intercepted telephone conversations involving the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, nor instructed anyone to do so.
El-Rufai made the clarification while testifying in his ongoing phone-tappi
content:
Former Kaduna State Governor, Nasir El-Rufai, has told the Federal High Court in Abuja that he neither intercepted telephone conversations involving the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, nor instructed anyone to do so.

El-Rufai made the clarification while testifying in his ongoing phone-tapping case on Wednesday, insisting that he neither possessed equipment for intercepting telephone calls nor had the technical skills required for such operations.

Led in evidence by his counsel, Paul Erokoro, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, the former governor also denied having access to Ribadu’s communication devices or the NSA’s communication networks.

He described his controversial remarks during an interview with Arise Television in February as political expressions rather than an admission that he had monitored Ribadu’s telephone conversations.

“I used ‘we’ to refer to opposition politicians. When I said ‘tapped’, it was an embellishment intended to make the government feel the pain we are feeling.

“It was rhetorical and exaggerated. My objective was to engage in political retort and linguistic flourish,” he told the court.

When reminded by Erokoro that his interviewer had pointed out that tapping another person’s phone was illegal, El-Rufai said his intention was to expose what he described as the government’s secret monitoring of opposition figures’ conversations without lawful court orders.

“I was referring to the government violating the law and not someone else doing it,” he said.

Asked who he meant by “we” when he claimed that “we are listening to their conversations”, the former governor said he was referring to himself and other leading opposition figures.

He, however, denied that they tapped Ribadu’s phone, saying they learnt of an alleged plan to arrest and detain him through a mutual friend.

El-Rufai declined to disclose the identity of the friend, saying he did not want to jeopardise the source’s interests.

He told the court that the friend visited him after the Arise Television interview and clarified that he had not tapped the NSA’s phone.

According to El-Rufai, he told the person that he already knew this but had made the claim to make those in government uncomfortable.

The case arose from an interview El-Rufai granted Arise Television’s Prime Time programme on February 13, 2026, a day after security operatives reportedly attempted to arrest him at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja.

The former governor had returned from Cairo, Egypt, when the operatives allegedly attempted to take him into custody. Although they seized his international passport, they did not arrest him.

During the interview, El-Rufai alleged that Ribadu ordered the attempted arrest, claiming he knew about the directive because he and others had listened to a telephone conversation in which the NSA instructed security operatives to arrest him.

Earlier in his testimony, El-Rufai said he had known Ribadu since 2003, when he, as the head of the Bureau of Public Enterprises, assisted him in establishing the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission by providing office space and funds.

He said their relationship deteriorated when Ribadu contested the presidency in 2011, adding that he believed former President Muhammadu Buhari was a better candidate.

The former governor also claimed that the NSA was against him because of his opposition to President Bola Tinubu’s re-election.

During cross-examination by the prosecuting counsel, Oluwole Aladedoye, SAN, El-Rufai, who said he had a law degree from the University of London, maintained that he would not disclose the identities of those he referred to as “we” in his claim that they listened to conversations involving government officials.

He also declined to name the person who allegedly informed him that Ribadu, Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, and the Chairman of the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission had met and agreed to ensure his arrest.

El-Rufai said he learnt of the alleged plan before returning from Cairo on February 12, 2026.

He added that he resisted the DSS operatives’ attempt to arrest him at the airport because they did not produce a valid arrest warrant.

The former governor also maintained that his claims during the television interview that he had never stolen public funds and knew nothing about the disappearance of activist Dadiyatta while he was governor of Kaduna State were factual.

He said all his other statements during the interview were true, except the claim relating to the tapping of Ribadu’s phone.

El-Rufai, who said he had filed fundamental rights suits over the search of his residence with what he described as a defective warrant, admitted that the cases had been dismissed by the High Court of the Federal Capital Territory and the Federal High Court.

At the close of the cross-examination, Aladedoye told the court that Erokoro had approached him before proceedings began to seek his assistance in the defence’s plan to invite Ribadu and the ICPC chairman as witnesses.

Aladedoye said he declined to assist because the matter was not within his control.

Erokoro, however, said he would make the necessary applications to secure their attendance.

Justice Joyce Abdulmalik subsequently adjourned the case until February 15 and 16 for the continuation of El-Rufai’s defence.

The post UPDATED: El-Rufai denies tapping Ribadu’s phone, says remarks exaggerated appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: Morka questions Obi, NDC over ‘Rig and die’ slogan
description:
The National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress, Felix Morka, has questioned the meaning and legal basis of the Nigeria Democratic Congress’ (NDC) ‘rig and die’ slogan, asking when election rigging became an offence punishable by death under Nigerian law.
Morka argued that anyone s
content:
The National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress, Felix Morka, has questioned the meaning and legal basis of the Nigeria Democratic Congress’ (NDC) ‘rig and die’ slogan, asking when election rigging became an offence punishable by death under Nigerian law.

Morka argued that anyone suspected of manipulating an election should be arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law rather than face punishment determined by a political party or its supporters.

He made the remarks during an appearance on News Central on Wednesday while reacting to allegations of political violence involving supporters of the NDC and the APC.

His comments followed an explanation by the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, who had defended the slogan during an interview with Channels Television after a town hall meeting in Taraba State on Tuesday.

Obi had clarified that the message was directed at preventing electoral malpractice, not discouraging political campaigns.

“They said we said ‘rig and die.’ We didn’t say ‘campaign and die.’ What we, people said is that they don’t want rigging this time. They didn’t say they don’t want campaign this time. If anything, they want campaign this time,” Obi said.

However, Morka questioned the implication of the slogan, particularly the suggestion that people accused of rigging elections should die.

“So, if somebody rigs an election, since when did Nigerian law prescribe the death penalty for rigging an election?” he asked.

The APC spokesman maintained that allegations of electoral offences should be handled through the established legal process.

He also accused the NDC of making unsubstantiated claims that the APC was responsible for political violence, arguing that the party had not reported the alleged incidents to the police or sought independent investigations.

Morka further alleged that some NDC supporters had displayed machetes at political gatherings, referring to videos he said were circulating online from Lagos and Delta states.

He questioned why the NDC had not denied the videos, although the allegations and his interpretation of the footage were his own claims.

title: Police Arrest Three Over Alleged Thug Attack On ADC Supporters In Kebbi
description: The Kebbi State Police Command has arrested three suspects in connection with an alleged violent political incident in Zauro, Makera, and surrounding communities in Birnin Kebbi Local Government Area, following reports of an attack involving suspected political thugs.The arrests come amid growing co
content:
The Kebbi State Police Command has arrested three suspects in connection with an alleged violent political incident in Zauro, Makera, and surrounding communities in Birnin Kebbi Local Government Area, following reports of an attack involving suspected political thugs.

The arrests come amid growing concerns over political violence and rising tensions ahead of the 2027 general elections.

According to the Police, preliminary investigations revealed that a political rally, reportedly organised by the wife of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate, was held across Zauro, Makera, Gwadangwaji, Gawasu, Morida and Karyo.

The Command said the organisers failed to notify the Police at least 48 hours before the event, in violation of an agreement reached with political parties during a stakeholders’ meeting on September 7, 2026, and a subsequent meeting with the party’s caucus on November 2, 2026.

The Police further alleged that some individuals in the convoy were seen carrying dangerous weapons, including sticks, machetes and swords, while some speakers made statements capable of inciting violence and disrupting public peace.

Video evidence obtained by the Command reportedly showed the individuals displaying the weapons during the political gathering.

The Police also raised concerns over vehicles allegedly operating without registration numbers or displaying questionable number plates, as well as the unauthorised use of sirens.

The Command condemned the development, warning political parties and their supporters against engaging in thuggery, violence and inflammatory statements capable of threatening public peace.

It stressed that any violation of the agreed security protocols or other applicable laws would attract appropriate legal action.

The Police confirmed that the three suspects had been charged to court for prosecution.

The Command also called on relevant authorities to investigate reports of minors being involved in political activities and take measures to protect them from exploitation and violence.

In a related development, the Divisional Police Officer in Jega reported another political activity organised by the same party without prior notification to the Police.

The organisers were subsequently directed to reschedule the rally and formally notify the Police to ensure adequate security arrangements.

The Command urged parents and guardians to discourage their children from being recruited into political violence, warning that individuals and political parties found sponsoring thuggery or violating the law would be held accountable.

title: NAHCON offers refund, rollover options to unsuccessful 2027 Hajj subscribers
description:
The National Hajj Commission of Nigeria has offered unsuccessful 2027 Hajj Savings Scheme subscribers the options of withdrawing their funds or retaining their savings in the scheme for the 2028 pilgrimage.
NAHCON management, in a statement released on Wednesday, also assured subscribers who fulfill
content:
The National Hajj Commission of Nigeria has offered unsuccessful 2027 Hajj Savings Scheme subscribers the options of withdrawing their funds or retaining their savings in the scheme for the 2028 pilgrimage.

NAHCON management, in a statement released on Wednesday, also assured subscribers who fulfilled the payment requirements for the 2027 Hajj but could not secure slots that they would be given priority for the 2028 exercise, subject to approved quotas and regulatory requirements.

The Commission explained that the failure to accommodate all intending pilgrims was due to the global reduction in Hajj slots imposed by Saudi Arabian authorities because of space constraints.

It stated, “National Hajj Commission of Nigeria acknowledges the disappointment of Hajj Savings Scheme subscribers and, indeed, many Nigerian Muslims who fulfilled the financial requirements for the 2027 Hajj but could not secure slots, and appreciates their patience, sacrifices and commitment towards fulfilling this important religious obligation.

“Nigeria, like other countries, is affected by the global reduction in Hajj slots imposed by the Saudi authorities due to space constraints.

“This has resulted in a backlog of intending pilgrims across the HSS, State Muslim Pilgrims’ Welfare Boards, Agencies and Commissions. NAHCON is required to operate within approved quotas, regulations and timelines.

“The Commission, however, welcomes the Saudi Government’s continued investment in Hajj infrastructure and remains hopeful that additional slots will become available in subsequent seasons.”

NAHCON explained that the Hajj Savings Scheme allows intending pilgrims to save gradually while earning investment returns, stressing that full payment does not automatically guarantee them a slot for a particular Hajj season.

It added, “Eligible subscribers and intending pilgrims who fulfilled the payment requirements for the 2027 Hajj but could not be accommodated will be accorded priority for the 2028 Hajj, subject to approved quotas and regulatory requirements.

“Intending pilgrims targeting the 2028 Hajj are advised to complete their required savings by the conclusion of the 2027 Hajj to facilitate timely reconciliation and registration.

“Affected subscribers may exercise either of the following options: approach their respective HSS partner banks to initiate withdrawals in accordance with established procedures, or retain their savings in the Scheme and continue to earn applicable investment returns, which may help offset future Hajj fares.

“To strengthen allocation management, address existing backlogs and improve planning, NAHCON is developing a National Hajj Database in collaboration with State Muslim Pilgrims’ Welfare Boards, Agencies and Commissions, HSS partner banks and other relevant stakeholders.”

NAHCON advised Hajj Savings Scheme subscribers and members of the public to seek information and guidance through its official channels and designated partner banks.

The Commission reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring equitable allocation of Hajj slots, transparency, compliance with regulations and the welfare of Nigerian pilgrims.

Saudi Arabia approved an additional 10,000 slots for Nigeria on October 1, increasing the country’s 2027 Hajj quota from 50,000 to 60,000 pilgrims.

However, despite the increase, some Nigerian intending pilgrims who made payments were unable to secure slots for the 2027 pilgrimage due to the limited allocation.

The post NAHCON offers refund, rollover options to unsuccessful 2027 Hajj subscribers appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: CAF announces finalists for 2026 Men’s Player of the Year Award
description:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has unveiled the five finalists for the 2026 Men’s Player of the Year award, with reigning winner Achraf Hakimi and Senegalese forward Sadio Mané among the nominees.
The shortlist was drawn from an initial list of 10 players based on their performances for
content:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has unveiled the five finalists for the 2026 Men’s Player of the Year award, with reigning winner Achraf Hakimi and Senegalese forward Sadio Mané among the nominees.

The shortlist was drawn from an initial list of 10 players based on their performances for their respective clubs and national teams during the assessment period.

Morocco has three representatives among the finalists, while Senegal accounts for two, highlighting the countries’ strong showing during the period under review.

Hakimi, who features for French champions Paris Saint-Germain, is seeking to retain the individual honour after playing a key role in the club’s UEFA Champions League and French Ligue 1 triumphs.

The Moroccan defender also captained his national team during its campaigns at the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Mané, a two-time winner of the award in 2019 and 2022, is also in contention for a third title after helping Senegal win the 2025 AFCON.

The Al-Nassr forward was named the tournament’s Best Player in recognition of his leadership and contributions to Senegal’s triumph.

Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz earned a place on the shortlist following his performances for Morocco, particularly at the 2025 AFCON, where he won the Golden Boot with five goals.

Villarreal midfielder Pape Gueye also made the list after scoring the winning goal in extra time as Senegal defeated Morocco 1-0 in the AFCON final in Rabat. His performances at the tournament also earned him a place in the Best XI.

Completing the shortlist is Morocco’s Ismael Saibari, who played an important role in his country’s run to the AFCON final, including scoring against Cameroon in the quarter-finals.

The winner will be announced at the 2026 CAF Awards ceremony scheduled for Wednesday, December 2, at the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts, popularly known as the National Theatre, in Lagos.

The ceremony is expected to begin at 7pm Nigerian time.

The CAF Awards will return to Lagos for the first time since the 2014 edition.

Full list of 2026 Men’s Player of the Year finalists

Achraf Hakimi (Morocco)

Sadio Mané (Senegal)

Brahim Diaz (Morocco)

Pape Gueye (Senegal)

Ismael Saibari (Morocco)

title: PHOTOS: Naval chief decorates eight promoted officers
description:
The Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS), Vice Admiral Idi Abbas, has decorated eight newly promoted officers of the Nigerian Navy with their new ranks, charging them to embrace greater responsibility, integrity and professionalism in the discharge of their duties.
The decoration ceremony, held at the Nav
content:
The Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS), Vice Admiral Idi Abbas, has decorated eight newly promoted officers of the Nigerian Navy with their new ranks, charging them to embrace greater responsibility, integrity and professionalism in the discharge of their duties.

The decoration ceremony, held at the Naval Headquarters, followed the promotion of the officers by the Navy Board from the rank of Commander to Captain.

In a post on the Nigerian Navy’s X on Wednesday, the newly promoted officers are Captains G Abe, EB Adeolu, BO Adebambo, TE Apanishile, D Joseph, AS Mustapha, DJ Shelpidi and Al Yalo.

Speaking at the ceremony, Abbas congratulated the officers on their elevation, urging them to see their promotion as a call to greater service rather than a mark of superiority over colleagues who were not promoted.

“Your elevation to the rank of Captain should be seen as a call to greater service and responsibility, not as a mark of superiority over colleagues who were not promoted,” the Naval Chief charged.

He emphasised the importance of upholding the Nigerian Navy’s core values of teamwork, integrity and professionalism, noting that higher ranks come with increased responsibilities and expectations.

According to him, “Promotion comes with greater expectations. You must therefore continue to demonstrate professionalism, integrity and commitment to duty while upholding the core values of the Nigerian Navy.”

The Naval Chief further urged the officers to justify the confidence reposed in them by maintaining high professional standards and contributing meaningfully to the service.

In his remarks on behalf of the newly promoted officers, Captain G Abe expressed appreciation to God and the Navy Board for finding them worthy of promotion.

“We are grateful to God and the Navy Board for finding us worthy of this elevation. We do not take this recognition for granted,” Abe said.

He also acknowledged the support and sacrifices of their spouses and family members throughout their careers, noting that their encouragement had contributed to their professional achievements.

Abe expressed appreciation to the families for standing by the officers throughout their years of service.

The ceremony was attended by Principal Staff Officers of the Naval Headquarters, family members and friends of the newly promoted officers.
