title: Daura Viral Video: Katsina Govt Orders Traditional Rulers To Obtain Clearance Before Hosting Foreign Visitors
description: The Katsina State Government has introduced a new protocol requiring all traditional rulers across the state to obtain official clearance before receiving foreign visitors, in a move aimed at strengthening security, improving coordination and regulating international engagements involving traditiona
content:
The Katsina State Government has introduced a new protocol requiring all traditional rulers across the state to obtain official clearance before receiving foreign visitors, in a move aimed at strengthening security, improving coordination and regulating international engagements involving traditional institutions.

Under the new directive, Emirs and other traditional rulers must secure approval from the Departments of Protocol and Cabinet/Security Matters in the Office of the Secretary to the State Government (SSG) before hosting any foreign guests at their palaces.

The directive was announced on Wednesday by the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Bala Salisu Zango, in a statement.

According to the commissioner, the policy is designed to ensure proper coordination, enhance security, and guarantee compliance with established government protocols during visits by foreign nationals to traditional institutions.

He explained that the measure will also enable the state government to effectively monitor and coordinate international engagements involving traditional rulers, ensuring that such visits are properly documented and subjected to necessary security vetting.

Zango said the initiative forms part of the administration’s broader strategy to reinforce the state’s security architecture, particularly at the grassroots, where traditional rulers play a critical role in maintaining peace, promoting stability and supporting government efforts in conflict prevention.

He noted that traditional institutions remain indispensable partners in community policing, intelligence gathering and peace-building, making it necessary for the government to maintain close oversight of their interactions with foreign visitors.

The commissioner added that the mandatory clearance process would provide an additional layer of security by ensuring that all international visits to traditional domains are officially vetted, coordinated and aligned with the state’s security objectives.

The Katsina State Government reaffirmed its commitment to safeguarding lives and property while promoting transparent and well-coordinated engagement between traditional institutions and the international community.

title: INEC Chairman Amupitan Briefs Commissioners, RECs On Strategies Ahead Of 2027 Polls
description: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, along with the national commissioners, is meeting with Resident Electoral Commissioners (RECs) and administrative secretaries from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). The meeting is happeni
content:
The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, along with the national commissioners, is meeting with Resident Electoral Commissioners (RECs) and administrative secretaries from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

The meeting is happening exactly 51 days to the 2027 general election, beginning with the presidential and National Assembly elections on January 16th.

The meeting, which is tagged “Strategic Meeting,” is also holding three days to the nationwide mock voter accreditation, slated for Saturday this weekend

The INEC chairman, in his opening remarks, emphasised the urgent need for RECS to now translate all the electoral policies and directives into reality in their various states.

He appealed to the RECS to consolidate on the various breakthroughs recorded in the office cycle elections held before now.

Amupitan also reminded the RECS to take seriously the decisions they took during the various zonal retreats he held with them.

He urged them to ensure that all lapses observed during the various off-cycle elections conducted must be permanently closed before the mock exercise on Saturday

The INEC chairman informed the gathering about six non-negotiable areas that RECS must be focused on, ahead of the general elections.

First, he explained that the target is a flawless execution of the November 28 Nationwide mock exercise, directing every REC to oversee the exercise and submit a report by Monday, 30th November 2026.

He clarified that the ballot paper must be a sampling ballot paper, without names of political parties

On the second area of focus, he urged RECS to pay attention to logistics ( Forward and reverse logistics), asking them to enforce strict tracking of voting materials.

The Commission has selected 17,676 polling units for the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) mock accreditation and result upload exercise slated for Saturday, 28 November 2026.

An update by the Commission via its X handle on Tuesday noted that the exercise will kick off from 8:30 AM to 2:PM in selected polling units across the country.

The total of 17,676 polling units was arrived at by multiplying the 8,838 Registration Areas by the two polling units selected in each area.

The mock exercise is intended to assess the readiness of the electoral technology and operational processes before the 2027 polls.

The post INEC Chairman Amupitan Briefs Commissioners, RECs On Strategies Ahead Of 2027 Polls appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Obidients urge IG to probe police conduct in Delta killings
description: The Obidient Movement has thrown its weight behind the Social Democratic Party’s demand for equal security protection for opposition parties, urging the Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, to investigate the conduct of policemen deployed during Monday’s deadly attack on the campaign entourage o
content:
The Obidient Movement has thrown its weight behind the Social Democratic Party’s demand for equal security protection for opposition parties, urging the Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, to investigate the conduct of policemen deployed during Monday’s deadly attack on the campaign entourage of former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, in Delta State.

Obidient Movement’s Director of Media and Communications, Onyeka Dike, made the appeal in a statement issued in Abuja on Wednesday.

The attack reportedly left six people dead and others injured, including an activist, Efemena Umukoro, and Omo-Agege’s aide, Moses Anuaghe.

Dike demanded an independent investigation into the security operatives’ conduct, including the identities of their commanders and the instructions they received before and during the incident.

He lamented that the presence of a large contingent of policemen at the venue, without preventing the violence, raised serious questions about the effectiveness and neutrality of the security arrangements.

The group spokesman also questioned the police response to previous confrontations involving supporters of the opposition NDC and the ruling All Progressives Congress, alleging that officers had been more forceful when opposition supporters retaliated against attacks.

He said, “If the Inspector-General, Tunji Disu, wants the Police Force that he leads to be taken seriously, he should immediately arrest and investigate everyone implicated in yesterday’s attack.

“Disu should also conduct an independent investigation into the conduct of the policemen at the scene, including the identities of their commanders and the instructions they received.”

The Obidient Movement further called for the arrest and investigation of Ughelli North Local Government Chairman, Jaro Egbo, whom the Omo-Agege campaign organisation had identified as the alleged leader of the attackers.

The movement’s position came hours after the National Chairman of the Social Democratic Party, Prof. Sadiq Gombe, called on the police to provide equal security protection for all political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Gombe made the appeal at a high-level security meeting coDisu convenedn Abuja to address political violence and security challenges during political activities.

He urged the police and other security agencies to remain professional, impartial and fair, insisting that opposition parties must be able to organise rallies, hold meetings and campaign without intimidation or fear of attacks.

The NDC had earlier announced its decision to boycott the meeting, citing alleged police bias and failure to protect its members from attacks by suspected political thugs.

The party alleged that security agencies failed to intervene during the killing of four of its members in Delta State and demanded investigations and prosecution of those responsible.

Meanwhile, Disu warned political actors against destroying campaign venues, attacking opponents and using dangerous weapons ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Speaking at the meeting, attended by representatives of the Independent National Electoral Commission, political parties, civil society organisations and other stakeholders, the police chief expressed concern over violent clashes among political supporters and attacks on campaign venues.

He said political competition must not be used as an excuse for violence, intimidation or actions capable of threatening public peace and national security.

The post Obidients urge IG to probe police conduct in Delta killings appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Bellingham at the heart of Real Madrid revival — Mourinho
description:
Even before Jude Bellingham’s wonder goal against PSV in the Champions League on Tuesday, there was little doubt the Englishman had become the crown jewel in Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid revival.
His importance was perhaps best illustrated by his absence, with Mourinho initially resting the midfielde
content:
Even before Jude Bellingham’s wonder goal against PSV in the Champions League on Tuesday, there was little doubt the Englishman had become the crown jewel in Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid revival.

His importance was perhaps best illustrated by his absence, with Mourinho initially resting the midfielder against the Dutch champions.

Los Blancos went in trailing 1-0 after a disjointed first-half display and Mourinho turned to Bellingham for emergency assistance.

The midfielder put on a masterclass to help Real Madrid produce perhaps the best half of football they have played in recent seasons, smashing in five goals to continue their 100 percent start in Europe.

Bellingham inspired the comeback, not just by scoring the second, a sensational sliced volley from the edge of the box after teeing himself up, but with his dynamism from the attacking midfield position invigorating his team-mates.

“After Jude came on, the players up front started functioning in a completely different way,” Mourinho told reporters.

The veteran coach said it had been a mistake to rest Bellingham, whom he said before the game had a minor fitness issue.

“Some players start to feel a little fatigued after games and can still play, but I thought, perhaps wrongly, that I could win without him,” Mourinho told Movistar afterwards.

“I tried to protect him as much as possible. But I knew I had an extraordinary bench, and having him there today was crucial.”

Bellingham has never been in better form in a Madrid shirt and has been instrumental in the team’s run of 10 consecutive victories across all competitions.

The Englishman made a spectacular start under Carlo Ancelotti after arriving in 2023, scoring a glut of goals as a makeshift centre-forward, but his overall influence on the team’s football under Mourinho is far greater.

Although Madrid won a Champions League and La Liga double in Bellingham’s first season, in the second half of the campaign his performances dipped.

The two seasons since were disappointing, both for the team, who failed to win a major trophy, and for Bellingham, who struggled to find consistent form.

There were brilliant moments scattered along the way, but he struggled to impose himself with any regularity, to the point where his position in the English national team even came into question.

A shoulder problem after a dislocation bugged him for well over a year and he underwent surgery on it in the summer of 2025.

‘Mourinho, full stop’

Asked about his superlative form after the game, with four goals in his last five Madrid matches, Bellingham had a simple answer. “Mourinho, full stop,” he said.

Mourinho modestly said Bellingham only had himself to thank and lavished praise on the 23-year-old, whom he said was the best midfielder on the planet.

“He’s an absolutely extraordinary player who has everything,” said the veteran Portuguese coach.

Bellingham took Real Madrid’s number five shirt upon arrival in what he said was homage to French great Zinedine Zidane, and some compared his goal against PSV to a Zidane-style strike.

Bellingham insisted the former French playmaker was “much better than me”, although the comparisons will keep coming.

“God save Bellingham” ran a headline in Spanish newspaper Marca.

Mourinho said it was a “scandal” Bellingham was not ranked in the Ballon d’Or top 10, while former Real Madrid coach Jorge Valdano said he could not believe the Englishman was so good at such a young age.

“You have to look twice at his age, he’s 23, it’s incredible how much he has ahead of him, because he has not even reached his peak. Your peak comes at 27, he’s only 23,” Valdano said on Movistar.

Bellingham even helped Vinicius Junior score his first Madrid goal since August, lofting a perfect ball over the top for the Brazilian to finish.

After two seasons dormant, both Bellingham and Mourinho’s revived Real Madrid look capable of hitting the heights once again.

AFP

The post Bellingham at the heart of Real Madrid revival — Mourinho appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: INEC fixes November 28 for Ekiti BVAS mock accreditation exercise
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has fixed Saturday, November 28, for a mock accreditation and result upload exercise in Ekiti State ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The exercise will be conducted using the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System to test the functionality of the devices
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has fixed Saturday, November 28, for a mock accreditation and result upload exercise in Ekiti State ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The exercise will be conducted using the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System to test the functionality of the devices and accreditation procedures under a simulated election environment.

INEC Resident Electoral Commissioner in Ekiti State, Dr Bunmi Omoseyindemi, disclosed this in a statement issued in Ado Ekiti on Wednesday.

Omoseyindemi said the exercise would hold between 8:30am and 2:30 pm, with two polling units selected in each ward across the state.

“The exercise will be conducted using the Bimodal Voters Accreditation System (BVAS) to test device functionality and accreditation procedure under a simulated election system,” he said.

According to the REC, the exercise is designed to identify possible operational and technical challenges ahead of the elections and enable the commission to address them before election day.

“The exercise will help the commission to identify possible operational and technical issues and address them before the general election,” he said.

He appealed to registered voters to turn out at the designated polling units and participate in the exercise.

The mock exercise is part of INEC’s preparations to ensure the smooth deployment of election technology during the 2027 general elections.

BVAS is used to verify voters’ identities through biometric accreditation and is also integrated into the commission’s election result management process.

Testing the devices and procedures before an election allows electoral officials to assess their readiness, identify technical faults and familiarise themselves with the system under simulated conditions.

The 2027 general elections are scheduled for January 16 and February 6, 2027. In Ekiti State, the elections will cover the presidential, National Assembly and State House of Assembly contests across the 16 local government areas.

The state governorship election was held on June 16, 2026.

The post INEC fixes November 28 for Ekiti BVAS mock accreditation exercise appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Anambra First Lady urges end to violence against women
description:
As the world marks the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, the Anambra State First Lady, Dr Nonye Soludo, has called on families, communities, institutions and leaders across the country to take a firm stand against all forms of violence and abuse.
Soludo, founder of the
content:
As the world marks the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, the Anambra State First Lady, Dr Nonye Soludo, has called on families, communities, institutions and leaders across the country to take a firm stand against all forms of violence and abuse.

Soludo, founder of the non-governmental organisation, Healthy Living with Nonye Soludo, said people must speak out against violence not only with compassion but also with total conviction.

She made the call in a press statement issued on Wednesday to commemorate the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, describing violence against women as an issue that must not be ignored, excused or concealed as a private matter.

She said, “Today, we must speak not just with compassion, but with total conviction. Violence against women is not a private matter to be ignored, excused or concealed.

“It is a violation of human dignity, a betrayal of humanity and an injustice that must never be tolerated by any society.

“Every woman deserves to live without fear, to walk with confidence, to speak without intimidation and to pursue her dreams without the threat of violence.

“No woman should have to endure abuse in silence, and no girl should grow up believing that violence is the price of being female.

“As we mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, I call on families, communities, institutions and leaders to stand firmly against every form of violence and abuse.

“Let us protect survivors, hold perpetrators accountable and raise a generation that understands that respect is not optional. A world where women are safe is not a favour to women; it is a responsibility we all share.”

The International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women is observed annually on November 25 to raise awareness and promote action against gender-based violence.

The day also marks the beginning of the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence, which runs until December 10, observed as International Human Rights Day.

The theme for 2026, ‘Ensure Justice, Protect Survivors, End Impunity’, focuses on strengthening justice systems, providing safe reporting channels and survivor-centred support services, enforcing laws, holding perpetrators and institutions accountable, and addressing online and AI-enabled abuse.

The post Anambra First Lady urges end to violence against women appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Tinubu’s anti-violence directive put into action in Kogi, says APC Chieftain
description:
A chieftain of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), Alhaji Mohammed Usman, has denied that the party had any involvement in reported campaign violence in Delta, Sokoto and Kebbi states.
Usman said the incidents should not be blamed on the APC, arguing that local political disputes and the act
content:
A chieftain of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), Alhaji Mohammed Usman, has denied that the party had any involvement in reported campaign violence in Delta, Sokoto and Kebbi states.

Usman said the incidents should not be blamed on the APC, arguing that local political disputes and the actions of individual actors were responsible. He added that the APC in Kogi State was guided by the same principles as the party elsewhere.

In a statement, the chieftain said the peaceful rally held in Kogi State by former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and his party offered evidence of the APC’s commitment to peaceful politics.

“Atiku can now testify to what happened in Kogi State, where he and his party held a peaceful rally,” Usman said. He praised Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo for ensuring the event proceeded peacefully, adding that the governor’s actions reflected President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s message of peace and unity.

Usman said Atiku should acknowledge the peaceful conduct of the rally and recognise the President’s efforts to promote unity. He added that President Tinubu had warned politicians and their supporters against violence ahead of the 2027 general elections and had pledged firm action against political thuggery and other anti-democratic activities.

According to Usman, the President has also directed security agencies to maintain public order and confront anyone seeking to disrupt it.

In a statement titled, “Let’s Shun Violence: Our Campaigns Must Be About Issues That Promote the Welfare of Our People,” Usman described the peaceful Kogi rally as a setback for what he called opposition propaganda and “name-calling and blame games.”

He also attributed the reported violence in Delta State to internal political disputes, citing a court ruling concerning the state’s Delta Central Senatorial District. Usman said the court ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to delist former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege, following a case instituted by Professor Alexander Akpodiete.

Usman further said the court found that the NDC had failed to submit its membership register to INEC 21 days before its primary and that Omo-Agege was not listed in the register. He also cited the court’s finding that Omo-Agege had participated in an APC primary on May 18, 2026. Usman argued that the dispute reflected internal party grievances rather than APC involvement.

He urged Atiku and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) to tell Nigerians that the Kogi rally was peaceful, crediting Governor Ododo’s conduct and the implementation of President Tinubu’s directive.

We are aware that some bad elements were hoping for violence so they could blame Mr. President. However, we thank God for Governor Usman Ododo, who—as the Chief Security Officer of the state—ensured that the President’s directive was implemented to the letter,” the APC chieftain said.

“Atiku came to Kogi State for a campaign, and our party did what was necessary to ensure peace,” Usman said. “The President’s directive was not just words; it was put into action.”

The post Tinubu’s anti-violence directive put into action in Kogi, says APC Chieftain appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Bayern Munich hold talks with Musiala’s management over his recovery
description:
Bayern Munich have held constructive discussions with the management of Germany international Jamal Musiala, reaffirming their commitment to supporting the midfielder’s recovery from injury.
The German Bundesliga champions disclosed that the meeting, held on Tuesday, focused on Musiala’s health and
content:
Bayern Munich have held constructive discussions with the management of Germany international Jamal Musiala, reaffirming their commitment to supporting the midfielder’s recovery from injury.

The German Bundesliga champions disclosed that the meeting, held on Tuesday, focused on Musiala’s health and rehabilitation, with both parties agreeing that his well-being remains the top priority.

In a statement on Wednesday on the club’s X handle, Bayern Munich and 11WINS, the agency representing the player, said the discussions were positive and aimed at ensuring a smooth recovery process.

“Both sides agree that the player’s health comes first. Jamal Musiala has their full support on his road to recovery,” the statement read.

The club also addressed recent speculation surrounding the midfielder’s medical condition, clarifying that he was first examined for absence-like symptoms on April 22, 2025.

According to Bayern, the examination was conducted in consultation with the club and its medical department immediately after the first neurological symptoms appeared.

“Given the many rumours in recent days, FC Bayern and 11WINS, the agency representing Jamal, would like to clarify: Jamal Musiala was first examined for absence-like symptoms on April 22, 2025,” the statement added.

Bayern and Musiala’s representatives also agreed to maintain their discussions in a spirit of partnership and confidentiality as the player continues his recovery.

The club reaffirmed its support for the midfielder, who remains an important member of its squad.

PUNCH Online reported that the International Federation of Professional Footballers (FIFPRO) condemned Bayern Munich over repeated public comments by the club’s leadership questioning the contract of midfielder Jamal Musiala as he continues his recovery from injury.

The post Bayern Munich hold talks with Musiala’s management over his recovery appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Daura: Katsina orders emirs to seek clearance before receiving foreign guests
description:
The Katsina State Government has directed traditional rulers across the state to obtain official clearance before receiving foreign guests at their palaces.
The directive requires the traditional rulers to seek approval from the Departments of Protocol and Cabinet/Security Matters under the Office o
content:
The Katsina State Government has directed traditional rulers across the state to obtain official clearance before receiving foreign guests at their palaces.

The directive requires the traditional rulers to seek approval from the Departments of Protocol and Cabinet/Security Matters under the Office of the Secretary to the State Government.

The state Commissioner for Information and Culture, Bala Zango, announced the directive in a statement issued on Wednesday.

According to the statement, the measure is intended to ensure proper coordination, security and adherence to official protocols during visits by foreign nationals to emirates’ palaces.

“The directive is intended to ensure proper coordination, security, and adherence to official protocols during visits to Emirs’ palace by foreign nationals, while also placing the traditional rulers under a formal regulatory framework regarding international relations.

“The measure is also intended to streamline interactions with foreign nationals and ensure that the government is fully aware of international engagements involving traditional institutions,” the statement read.

Zango said the directive was part of the administration’s broader strategy to strengthen security at the grassroots level.

He noted that “the state government partly relies on traditional rulers as key stakeholders in peace-building,”

“Furthermore, this clearance process is another strategy of the state government to ensure that all international visits to traditional domains are documented and vetted for safety,” the statement added.

The directive came a day after the state government announced the suspension of the Emir of Daura, Umar Faruk Umar, from official engagements and travels following a sexual assault allegation made against him by a Polish tourist, Mirka Czee.

The government also constituted a committee to investigate the allegation and advise it on the appropriate course of action.

Czee had released a video of her encounter with the Emir behind a closed door during a visit to his palace on November 14 and alleged that the monarch touched her breasts without her consent.

She said she recorded part of the encounter using Meta smart glasses and later shared the footage on social media.

The tourist, who was on a 30-day tour of Nigeria, said she waited until she had left the country before making the allegation public.

Following the circulation of the video and her account, Czee faced online harassment, including insults, victim-blaming and death threats.

She shared screenshots of some of the messages on Instagram, with some users demanding that she withdraw her allegation or delete the video.

Amnesty International Nigeria condemned the threats, saying the tourist had received hundreds of death threats, including warnings that she would be tracked down and killed or harmed.

The Daura Emirate Council had earlier said it was reviewing the footage to establish its authenticity and determine whether it had been manipulated.

The Katsina State Government said the Emir’s suspension would remain in place pending the outcome of the investigation and assured the public that the committee’s findings and recommendations would be implemented.

The post Daura: Katsina orders emirs to seek clearance before receiving foreign guests appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: El-Rufai Denies Tapping Ribadu’s Phone, Says ‘Tapped’ Remark Political Rhetoric
description: A Former Kaduna State Governor, Nasir El-Rufai, has denied intercepting telephone conversations or asking anyone to do so of the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu. Testifying in his ongoing phone-tapping case at the Federal High Court, Abuja, as evidence- in- chief, El-Rufai told the court that
content:
A Former Kaduna State Governor, Nasir El-Rufai, has denied intercepting telephone conversations or asking anyone to do so of the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu.

Testifying in his ongoing phone-tapping case at the Federal High Court, Abuja, as evidence- in- chief, El-Rufai told the court that he had never owned equipment used to intercept telephone calls and had no technical knowledge of how to do so.

Led in evidence by his lawyer, Paul Erokoro, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), the former governor also denied having access to the NSA’s communication networks or devices.

He maintained that his comments during an interview on a National Television in February were “political rhetoric” and not an admission that he had intercepted Mr Ribadu’s telephone.

“I used ‘we’ to refer to opposition politicians. When I said ‘tapped’, it was an embellishment intended to make the government feel the pain we are feeling. It was rhetorical and exaggerated. My objective was to engage in political retort and linguistic flourish,” he told the court.

The case followed an interview El-Rufai granted Arise Television’s Prime Time programme on 13 February 2026, a day after security operatives attempted to arrest him at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, on his return from Cairo, Egypt.

Although the operatives seized his international passport, they did not arrest him.

During the interview, El-Rufai accused Mr Ribadu of ordering the attempted arrest.

He said he knew about the directive because they had listened to a telephone conversation in which the NSA instructed security operatives to arrest him.

More details later.

title: Villarreal 0-6 Paris Saint-Germain and a Busy Mobile Betting Night
description:
Eight minutes. That’s how long Paris Saint-Germain needed in Villarreal on Tuesday night. Four goals went in between the 9th and 17th minutes, the game finished 6-0, and PSG became the first side in this season’s Champions League to win four out of four.
If you were flicking between a news feed and
content:
Eight minutes. That’s how long Paris Saint-Germain needed in Villarreal on Tuesday night. Four goals went in between the 9th and 17th minutes, the game finished 6-0, and PSG became the first side in this season’s Champions League to win four out of four.

If you were flicking between a news feed and the live markets on bizbet at the time, you might well have missed two of them. They came in the 12th and 13th minutes, about a minute apart.

Villarreal vs Paris Saint-Germain Goals Minute by Minute

Villarreal kept things level until the 9th minute. Here’s how the scoreboard changed after that.

  • 9th minute, 0-1
  • 12th minute, 0-2
  • 13th minute, 0-3
  • 17th minute, 0-4
  • 50th minute, 0-5
  • 78th minute, 0-6

For all practical purposes, the game was done by the 17th minute. The second half was mostly about the size of the margin.

Villarreal’s coach tried a change at half-time, then three more just after the hour. By then the fifth goal had already gone in, five minutes into the second half. PSG made two changes on the hour and three more at 74 minutes, and they still found a sixth at 78.

The foul count was just as uneven. Villarreal collected four yellow cards and gave away 19 fouls. PSG finished with no cards at all and only four fouls.

Villarreal vs Paris Saint-Germain Match Stats

Stat Villarreal Paris Saint-Germain
Possession 33% 67%
Total shots 13 22
Shots on target 2 12
Corners 4 8
Fouls 19 4
Yellow cards 4 0

Paris Saint-Germain Stay Perfect in the Champions League Table

PSG are halfway through with 12 points out of 12. That’s a strong platform for a top-eight finish, which would let them skip the play-off round.

Real Betis went into Wednesday’s game at Borussia Dortmund with three wins from three, the only other side still able to match that perfect record on matchday four.

Villarreal are going the other way. One win, three defeats and three points leave them in the bottom third of the league phase table.

How the 36-Team Champions League Phase Works

All 36 clubs share one table. Everyone plays eight games against eight different opponents, four at home and four away.

Finish in the top eight and you go straight to the round of 16. Ninth to 24th means a two-legged knockout play-off round first, with the clubs from 9th to 16th seeded, and anyone from 25th down is out.

Following Champions League Live Scores and In-Play Betting on Mobile

Tuesday was a night for the phone. Four goals in eight minutes means four goal alerts in eight minutes if you follow the club in an app, and live score centres update possession and shot counts while the game is still going. The numbers in the stats table above are the same ones those centres refresh minute by minute.

In-play betting moves just as quickly. Prices change the moment a goal goes in, and lots of live markets track the same numbers you see in the match centre, corners and shots on target included. Card markets had a busy night too, with all four bookings going to Villarreal, and totals markets had plenty to process after six goals in a game that sat at 0-0 for its first eight minutes.

Most of this now happens on mobile, in browser tabs or in apps installed through bizbet апп татах on the same phone, and a late-October market report from Mordor Intelligence puts phones and tablets at about 58.5% of online gambling in 2026. If you follow games this way, set your budget before kick-off and keep it part of the fun.

Champions League Matchday 4 Results From Tuesday Night

Matchday four was split across two nights, and the other half, including Real Madrid at AEK Athens and Liverpool at Fenerbahce, was played on Wednesday. Other Champions League results from Tuesday included these.

  • FC Barcelona 3-0 Aston Villa
  • Atletico Madrid 0-2 Bayern Munich
  • Feyenoord 0-3 Inter
  • Manchester United 3-2 AS Roma
  • Galatasaray 2-0 VfB Stuttgart
  • LASK 4-0 Slovan Bratislava
  • Bodø/Glimt 0-0 Lille

Champions League Standings After Tuesday’s Matchday 4 Games

PSG weren’t the only away side to keep a clean sheet and win by two or more. Bayern Munich did it at Atletico Madrid, which took them to eight points from two wins and two draws, and Inter did it in Rotterdam to move on to six.

Barcelona’s 3-0 against Aston Villa means both clubs now sit on nine points, three wins and a defeat apiece. Manchester United had to score three to see off Roma in a five-goal game, and that left them on six. Atletico Madrid and Roma, both beaten on Tuesday, are stuck on four points, while Feyenoord stay on three.

Galatasaray’s 2-0 against VfB Stuttgart lifted them to six, a point behind the visitors, while LASK’s 4-0 also put them on six. Slovan Bratislava still don’t have a point after four defeats, and Bodø/Glimt’s 0-0 draw with Lille means Lille are still waiting for a first win.

Next up is 24 November, with Galatasaray against Aston Villa and Arsenal against Borussia Dortmund among the first fixtures of matchday five.

title: Jigawa emirate bars unauthorised palace photos, video publications
description:
The Gumel Emirate Council in Jigawa State has banned the taking of photographs and videos, as well as the dissemination of information about the emirate, without its approval.
The development comes amid a controversy at the neighbouring Daura Emirate in Katsina State, where the Emir, Umar Faruk Umar
content:
The Gumel Emirate Council in Jigawa State has banned the taking of photographs and videos, as well as the dissemination of information about the emirate, without its approval.

The development comes amid a controversy at the neighbouring Daura Emirate in Katsina State, where the Emir, Umar Faruk Umar, was suspended from official engagements and travels by the state government following allegations of sexual assault made against him by a foreign tourist. The government has set up a committee to investigate the allegations.

In a statement made available to journalists on Wednesday and signed by the Secretary of the Gumel Emirate Council, Murtala Aliyu, the council said the new measures were introduced to regulate the emirate’s communication and public engagements.

“The Emirate has banned taking pictures and videos and spreading its information without its permission, to regulate communication and protect the Emirate’s information,” Aliyu said.

He said anyone who was not among the media officials approved by the palace had no right to take photographs, record videos or gather information on behalf of the emirate without its approval.

According to the statement, the palace had also prohibited the use of the emirate’s name to publish statements and reports without permission.

“The creation of social media pages bearing names linked to the Emirate without its approval has also been banned,” it added.

“The use of the Emirate’s name for publications without permission is prohibited, just as the creation of social media pages in its name without approval is prohibited,” Aliyu stated.

Furthermore, the secretary warned that anyone who violated the rules would face appropriate legal action.

“The Emirate will take appropriate legal steps against anyone who violates these rules,” he said.

Aliyu further disclosed that only statements confirmed to have originated from sources approved by the palace could be reshared.

“The measures were taken to ensure that only accurate and authorised information about the Emirate is released to the public,” he said.

The secretary stressed that the emirate remained committed to orderly communication and the protection of its image and official information.

The post Jigawa emirate bars unauthorised palace photos, video publications appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Murray-Bruce says Nigeria not dumping ground, demands five-year accountability for car, solar dealers
description:
Former Bayelsa East senator, Ben Murray-Bruce has called on the Federal Government to stop Nigeria from becoming a dumping ground for substandard vehicles, solar systems and other consumer products sold without warranty, spare parts or after-sales service.
In a post on X on Wednesday, Murray-Bruce s
content:
Former Bayelsa East senator, Ben Murray-Bruce has called on the Federal Government to stop Nigeria from becoming a dumping ground for substandard vehicles, solar systems and other consumer products sold without warranty, spare parts or after-sales service.

In a post on X on Wednesday, Murray-Bruce said Nigeria has become the world’s favourite dumping ground, and Nigerians are paying for it with their hard-earned money.

“Let me say this plainly: Nigeria has become the world’s favourite dumping ground, and we are paying for it with our hard-earned money,” he wrote.

He said every month, new car brands, many of them Chinese, open showrooms in Lagos and Abuja, sell vehicles with no real warranty, no spare parts and no after-sales service, and then close shop and vanish, leaving buyers stranded with vehicles nobody can repair.

Murray-Bruce cited his personal experience with a solar system installed in his home, saying the company went bankrupt and left Nigeria within a year, leaving the investment wasted because there is no one to service it.

“I know this pain. I invested in a solar system for my home. Within a year, the company that installed it went bankrupt and left Nigeria,” he said.

“Millions of Nigerians are buying inverters, batteries, and panels with the same broken promise: no warranty, no support, and no one to hold accountable when things fail.”

He described the practice as exploitation rather than trade, arguing that in serious countries, a company cannot sell a car or a power system and simply disappear, but must prove its capacity, keep spare parts, and stand behind its products for years.

“This is not trade; it is exploitation. In serious countries, a company cannot sell a car or a power system and simply disappear,” he said. “Why should Nigerians deserve anything less?”

Murray-Bruce called on the Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr. Jumoke Oduwole, and the Minister of State for Industry, Senator John Owan Enoh, to set the rules for who enters the Nigerian market.

He also urged the National Automotive Design and Development Council under Otunba Oluwemimo Osanipin to license only dealerships with real capacity, the Standards Organisation of Nigeria under Dr. Ifeanyi Okeke to stop substandard products at the borders, and the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission under Tunji Bello to protect buyers.

On solar and inverters, he called on the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, to insist on certified installers with lasting service obligations.

He proposed that any dealership that sells to Nigerians and shuts down within less than five years must be held accountable, with its directors pursued and its customers compensated.

“Every company must post a bond, guarantee spare parts and service for a minimum number of years, and register a local service centre before it sells a single product. Only reputable companies with a track record should be allowed in,” he said.

He stressed, “Nigeria is a market of more than 200 million people. We are not a dumping ground, and it is time we started acting like it.”

title: Tinubu mourns Pete Edochie, hails late actor’s contribution to Nollywood
description:
President Bola Tinubu has mourned veteran Nollywood actor, Pete Edochie, describing him as one of Nigeria’s greatest thespians and a pioneer of the country’s film industry.
Tinubu said Edochie, who was widely known as “Ebube Dike”, helped shape Nollywood and promote Nigerian culture through his memo
content:
President Bola Tinubu has mourned veteran Nollywood actor, Pete Edochie, describing him as one of Nigeria’s greatest thespians and a pioneer of the country’s film industry.

Tinubu said Edochie, who was widely known as “Ebube Dike”, helped shape Nollywood and promote Nigerian culture through his memorable performances.

The President made the remarks in a statement he personally issued on Wednesday, following news of the actor’s death by his family on Wednesday.

He described Edochie as an exceptional actor and one of the pioneers of Nollywood, noting that his influence extended beyond the screen.

“Chief Edochie was an exceptional actor – one of the progenitors of our vibrant film industry, Nollywood. He was graceful and larger than life, both on the screen and in person,” Tinubu said.

The President recalled Edochie’s portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s novel, Things Fall Apart, in the 1980s.

He also cited the actor’s performances in films such as Igodo, Rituals and Lionheart, saying they contributed to the growth and international recognition of Nollywood.

Tinubu said Edochie’s roles in productions depicting traditional institutions, family values and human relationships helped project Nigeria’s cultural heritage to audiences around the world.

He also acknowledged the late actor’s contributions to broadcasting, journalism and administration, describing him as one of the country’s finest talents.

“Pete Edochie was not only an actor; he was also an administrator, broadcaster, and journalist – truly one of our finest,” he said.

Reflecting on the actor’s legacy, Tinubu said his works would continue to inspire generations.

“In his works, he lives forever. Many generations will talk about the life and work of Chief Edochie in the arts industry and academia, in barbershops and marketplaces, and indeed wherever people gather,” he said.

The President extended his condolences to the Edochie family, friends, associates and members of the Nigerian film industry.

He prayed that God would grant the late actor eternal rest.

title: LASG includes ‘Lagos to London’ in SS1–SS3 literature curriculum
description:
By Chukwuma Umeorah
The Lagos State Government has included Lagos to London, a novel by Nigerian author Lola Aworanti-Ekugo, in the Literature-in-English curriculum for senior secondary school students, covering Senior Secondary School 1 to 3 (SS1–SS3).
The inclusion places the contemporary Nigerian
content:
By Chukwuma Umeorah

The Lagos State Government has included Lagos to London, a novel by Nigerian author Lola Aworanti-Ekugo, in the Literature-in-English curriculum for senior secondary school students, covering Senior Secondary School 1 to 3 (SS1–SS3).

The inclusion places the contemporary Nigerian novel among literary texts to be studied by students in public and private senior secondary schools across the state, providing an opportunity for young learners to engage with themes of migration, identity, ambition, societal expectations and the choices confronting Nigerians seeking opportunities abroad.

Published by Aworanti-Ekugo, Lagos to London “follows the experiences of two young Nigerians, Remi Coker and Nnamdi Okonkwo, who leave the country for the United Kingdom in search of better opportunities but approach migration from different backgrounds and perspectives. While Remi, who comes from the prominent Coker family, travels to London to pursue a law degree with the expectation of returning to Nigeria to eventually take over her family’s law firm, Nnamdi is driven by frustration with persistent strikes in federal universities and his determination to relocate permanently.”

The novel’s inclusion in the state curriculum brings the subject of migration, popularly described as ‘japa’ in Nigeria, into the classroom, offering students an opportunity to examine the motivations behind emigration, the expectations of life abroad and questions surrounding national development and the responsibilities of young Nigerians.

Commenting on the development, Aworanti-Ekugo said, “I wrote Lagos to London with the hope of telling real and relevant stories that resonate with young Africans today, encouraging them to think more deeply about identity, ambition, choices, opportunity and the world around them. Seeing the novel included in the Lagos State curriculum for senior secondary schools is particularly meaningful because it allows these important conversations to reach a wider audience of young people, inspiring them to broaden their horizons and engage with different perspectives through literature.”

The adoption also provides an avenue for students to study contemporary African fiction alongside the themes and literary techniques examined in their Literature-in-English lessons, while engaging with issues that reflect experiences within Nigerian society.

Beyond migration, the novel examines the influence of family expectations, educational challenges and individual aspirations on young people’s decisions, particularly as they navigate opportunities in an increasingly interconnected world.

title: CAF names five finalists for 2026 Men’s Player of the Year award
description:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has unveiled five finalists for the 2026 Men’s Player of the Year award, with reigning winner Achraf Hakimi, former recipient Sadio Mané, Brahim Diaz, Ismael Saibari and Pape Gueye making the shortlist.
In a post on CAF’s website on Wednesday, the final no
content:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has unveiled five finalists for the 2026 Men’s Player of the Year award, with reigning winner Achraf Hakimi, former recipient Sadio Mané, Brahim Diaz, Ismael Saibari and Pape Gueye making the shortlist.

In a post on CAF’s website on Wednesday, the final nominees were selected from an initial list of 10 players following their performances for club and country during the period under consideration.

Morocco and Senegal dominate the shortlist, with three Moroccan players and two Senegalese stars making the final five.

Hakimi, who plays for French giants Paris Saint-Germain, is seeking to retain the award following another impressive season with his club and the Moroccan national team.

The defender played a key role in PSG’s UEFA Champions League and French Ligue 1 successes, while captaining Morocco during its campaign at the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) and the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Senegal’s Mané, a two-time winner of the award in 2019 and 2022, is also in contention for a third title after helping the Lions of Teranga win the 2025 AFCON.

The Al-Nassr forward was named Best Player of the continental tournament in recognition of his leadership and contributions to Senegal’s triumph.

Real Madrid’s Brahim Diaz also made the shortlist following his impressive performances for Morocco, particularly at the 2025 AFCON, where he won the Puma Golden Boot with five goals.

Villarreal midfielder Pape Gueye earned his nomination after scoring the winning goal in extra time as Senegal defeated Morocco 1-0 in the AFCON final in Rabat.

Gueye’s performances throughout the competition also earned him a place in the tournament’s Best XI.

Completing the shortlist is Morocco’s Ismael Saibari, who played an important role in his country’s run to the AFCON final, including scoring against Cameroon in the quarter-finals.

The attacking midfielder also featured prominently in Morocco’s 2026 World Cup campaign.

The winner will be announced at the CAF Awards 2026 ceremony scheduled to hold on Wednesday, December 2, at the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts, popularly known as the National Theatre, in Lagos.

The ceremony is scheduled to begin at 7:00 p.m. Nigerian time (18:00 GMT).

The CAF Awards ceremony returns to Lagos for the first time since the 2014 edition.

title: Sokoto CP decorates 34 officers, urges renewed commitment to duty
description:
The Sokoto State Commissioner of Police, CP Hayatu Shaffa, has urged 34 newly promoted officers to demonstrate greater commitment, discipline and professionalism in the discharge of their duties.
The officers, who were promoted from the rank of Assistant Superintendent of Police to Deputy Superinten
content:
The Sokoto State Commissioner of Police, CP Hayatu Shaffa, has urged 34 newly promoted officers to demonstrate greater commitment, discipline and professionalism in the discharge of their duties.

The officers, who were promoted from the rank of Assistant Superintendent of Police to Deputy Superintendent of Police, were decorated at a ceremony held at the command headquarters.

Speaking at the event, Shaffa described the promotion as recognition of the officers’ hard work, dedication and commitment to duty, urging them to justify the confidence reposed in them by the police authorities.

“Your promotion should be seen as a call to greater service. It comes with increased responsibilities, and you must justify the confidence reposed in you through renewed vigour and professionalism,” he said.

The commissioner reminded the officers that their new ranks came with higher expectations, urging them to remain disciplined, loyal and steadfast in the fight against crime and criminality in the state.

He also commended the Inspector-General of Police for approving the promotions, noting that such recognition would boost the morale of personnel and encourage greater dedication to duty.

Responding on behalf of the beneficiaries, DSP Sulaiman Mada thanked the commissioner and the command’s management team for the honour.

“We are grateful for this recognition and promise not to disappoint the command. We will continue to uphold the ideals of the Nigeria Police Force and discharge our responsibilities with renewed dedication,” Mada said.

The ceremony was attended by members of the command’s management team, senior officers, colleagues and family members of the newly promoted officers.

The promotion comes amid ongoing efforts by the Nigeria Police Force to strengthen operational effectiveness and improve service delivery through the recognition and advancement of deserving personnel.

Promotions within the force are expected to encourage officers to maintain high standards of conduct, enhance their leadership capacity and take on greater responsibilities in policing their respective jurisdictions.

description: A US jury convicted Chinese tech giant Huawei of stealing trade secrets Tuesday, but acquitted it of a more serious racketeering allegation, according to the Department of Justice.The world’s leading telecom equipment manufacturer, Huawei, has been targeted by the Trump administration, which a
content:
A US jury convicted Chinese tech giant Huawei of stealing trade secrets Tuesday, but acquitted it of a more serious racketeering allegation, according to the Department of Justice.

The world’s leading telecom equipment manufacturer, Huawei, has been targeted by the Trump administration, which alleges a risk of it spying on behalf of the Chinese government.

The United States has previously urged countries not to use Huawei infrastructure for the rollout of new 5G mobile networks.

The verdict followed a three-month trial at a New York federal court, the US Department of Justice (DOJ) reported, with jurors finding Huawei guilty of 10 of the 12 criminal counts facing it — including bank fraud, conspiracy to steal trade secrets and conspiracy to defraud the United States.

“No person or company is above the law,” US Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a statement. “For decades, Huawei and three of its subsidiaries conducted their business in the United States on the basis of lies and theft.”

The equipment manufacturer was accused of attempting to recruit employees of US telecoms firms and obtaining technological information from them in the process.

That data allegedly enabled Huawei to develop products similar to those of its competitors, which it then sold at lower prices, according to the original indictment.

“The misappropriated intellectual property included trade secret information and copyrighted works, such as source code and user manuals for internet routers, antenna technology, and robot testing technology,” the DOJ said in a release.

Huawei even launched an internal program offering bonuses to employees who obtained industrial secrets from competitors, prosecutors claimed.

“Today’s verdict sends an unmistakable message: America will defend its businesses, protect its workers, and safeguard its national security against corrupt foreign corporations that lie, cheat, and steal to get ahead,” Assistant Attorney General Tysen A. Duva said in a statement.

The investigation also involved Huawei’s business dealings with the government of Iran.

“Huawei repeatedly lied about the nature of its business in Iran, falsely telling banks, journalists, and the US government that it did not assist Iran’s government, military, or intelligence community,” DOJ said.

The jury ultimately acquitted the company of a racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice.

AFP

title: I never refused doping test — French tennis player Rinderknech
description:
French tennis player Arthur Rinderknech has denied allegations that he refused to take a doping test, insisting that he expects to be cleared following an independent hearing.
According to French newspaper L’Équipe, on Wednesday, the world number 57 is under investigation by the International Tennis
content:
French tennis player Arthur Rinderknech has denied allegations that he refused to take a doping test, insisting that he expects to be cleared following an independent hearing.

According to French newspaper L’Équipe, on Wednesday, the world number 57 is under investigation by the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) over an alleged refusal to undergo a surprise doping test in June.

The report suggested that the incident may have resulted from a possible misunderstanding between Rinderknech and the sample collector.

Responding to the allegations in a statement posted on Instagram, the 31-year-old said he had already informed the ITIA that he denied the accusation and had requested an independent tribunal to hear and determine the matter.

Rinderknech expressed confidence that he would be exonerated, adding that he had never taken any banned substance.

“I am proud of my accomplishments in professional tennis, all of which have been achieved through hard work and with integrity always,” he said.

The allegations have drawn attention following the case of former Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova, who is currently serving a four-year suspension for refusing an out-of-competition doping test in December 2025. The Czech player has appealed the decision.

Rinderknech, who defeated Alexander Zverev in the first round at Wimbledon last year, maintains that he has done nothing wrong and is awaiting the independent tribunal’s determination.

No final decision has been announced in his case.

title: Tech innovators seek dedicated ICT ministry in Ogun
description:
The Ogun Tech Community has called for the establishment of a dedicated Ministry of Information and Communication Technology and Digital Economy, saying the ministry was necessary for the state to achieve its ambition of becoming Africa’s Silicon Valley.
The President of the community, Adekunle Duro
content:
The Ogun Tech Community has called for the establishment of a dedicated Ministry of Information and Communication Technology and Digital Economy, saying the ministry was necessary for the state to achieve its ambition of becoming Africa’s Silicon Valley.

The President of the community, Adekunle Durosinmi, said the proposed ministry would provide the policy direction and institutional framework needed to coordinate technology development, support innovation and attract investment.

Durosinmi, who made the call during a press conference on Tuesday in Abeokuta, said Ogun had the economic and human resources required to emerge as a major technology hub.

“Ogun needs a dedicated ICT ministry to harness its growing technology potential. A standalone ICT ministry will give technology development the attention and funding it deserves,” he said.

He cited Ogun’s proximity to Lagos, industrial base, concentration of higher institutions and growing population of young innovators as factors.

According to him, the state must move beyond fragmented technology initiatives and develop a coordinated strategy that would encourage local technology companies to develop solutions for local and international markets.

“Ogun State cannot afford to remain a consumer of technology when it has the human resources, educational institutions, entrepreneurial potential and emerging innovators required to become a producer and exporter of technology solutions,” he said.

Durosinmi said the community envisaged the development of specialised technology clusters in Abeokuta, Ota, Ijebu-Ode, Sagamu, Mowe, Ibafo and Ilaro to encourage innovation and expand economic opportunities across the state.

He added that a dedicated ministry would strengthen collaboration between universities, polytechnics, technology hubs, startups and investors while promoting digital skills in areas such as artificial intelligence, software development, cybersecurity, robotics and data science.

The OTC president said the community would also use its annual technology programme to showcase locally developed products and connect innovators with potential investors.

He disclosed that nine technology products developed by members of the community would be showcased during OTC Week 2026.

They include EduTAMS, a school management platform; IDS-Master, a community-sensitive surveillance system; Turnify, a digital queue and patient flow management platform; and SendEva, an artificial intelligence-powered sales and business management platform.

“Others are Konn3ct, a video conferencing platform; Golearn, a learning management system; CareMate, a personal health intelligence network; VnitPay, a digital voucher and payment platform; and ServeInOrder, a digital food ordering and service management platform,” he said.

Durosinmi cited EduTAMS, founded by an OTC board member, Ademola Adenubi, as an example of homegrown innovation gaining international recognition, saying it was recently named among the world’s top EdTech companies for 2026 by TIME and Statista.

He said the community was prepared to partner with the Ogun State Government, private sector organisations, academic institutions and development partners to achieve the state’s technology ambitions.

OTC Week 2026, which runs from November 23, would feature workshops and engagements on artificial intelligence in journalism, technology development, security and machine learning.

The programme will culminate in a dinner and awards night scheduled for December 26, 2026.

The push for a stronger digital economy comes as technology increasingly drives job creation, business growth and service delivery across sectors, including education, healthcare, agriculture and manufacturing.

For Ogun, which shares a border with Lagos and hosts a growing concentration of industries and educational institutions, expanding the technology sector could create opportunities for young people, support local businesses and diversify the state’s economy.

A coordinated digital development policy could also help bridge the gap between technology training and employment by connecting innovators with industry, investors and markets.

The post Tech innovators seek dedicated ICT ministry in Ogun appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Malaysia Sues Google For $146m Over YouTube Content
description: Malaysia said Wednesday it was suing Google for $146 million over the tech giant’s failure to remove “harmful” content posted on video-sharing platform YouTube.“The lawsuits concern two separate matters involving Google’s alleged failure to comply with its statutory obl
content:
Malaysia said Wednesday it was suing Google for $146 million over the tech giant’s failure to remove “harmful” content posted on video-sharing platform YouTube.

“The lawsuits concern two separate matters involving Google’s alleged failure to comply with its statutory obligations and applicable licence conditions,” the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission said.

The first suit related to the US firm’s alleged failure to take action against “thousands of online materials including gambling, scams and fraud”, the watchdog said in a statement.

The MCMC said it had submitted 73,703 reports to YouTube between January 1 and October 28 this year, the majority of which related to online gambling.

Of these gambling-related reports, some 4,950 cases received no response, while a further 35 cases took more than 90 days for a platform response or takedown, the MCMC added. A further 1,468 cases exceeded 30 days from the date of submission, it added.

“These figures demonstrate the scale of harmful content on the platform and the delays in addressing such content,” the watchdog said.

The second case related to YouTube’s failure to take down alleged defamatory and false content posted by a Malaysian blogger after the MCMC received a complaint.

Google could not immediately be reached for comment.

The lawsuits came three weeks after Google announced plans to invest $15 billion in Malaysia over the next two years to build data centres and other infrastructure, expanding on a $2 billion investment announced in 2024.

The country is Southeast Asia’s fastest-growing hub for new data centres crammed with servers that can train and run AI tools such as chatbots and image generators.

Malaysia had previously taken other major social media platforms, including TikTok, to task over allegations that they had failed to remove content deemed “grossly offensive”.

AFP

content:
There is a heavy security presence across Maiduguri, the capital of Borno State, with major routes currently blocked as residents await President Bola Tinubu’s visit for the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally.

Our correspondent reports that a combined team of security agencies, including the police, Army, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps and Civilian Joint Task Force, among others, has been deployed to man critical routes ahead of the President’s visit.

 The routes, according to a statement issued on Wednesday by the Public Relations Officer of the Borno State Police Command, ASP Nahum Daso, stretch from Airport Road, Kashim Ibrahim Road, Bulumkutu (Teachers’ Quarters Phase II/GSM Village), International Conference Centre, Mai Doki Roundabout, West End Roundabout, Shehu’s Palace, Dandal Roundabout and Bolori Roundabout to the Government House axis.

The statement warned residents to avoid non-essential movements in Maiduguri.

“Avoid the route/rally areas. Use alternative routes, allow extra time, keep a low profile, stay vigilant and follow directives from security personnel,” Daso said.

Meanwhile, our correspondent also observed a large crowd of supporters at the Elkanemi Warriors Centre and the deployment of police and military combat assets at strategic points across the city centre.

PUNCH Online had earlier reported that Tinubu was expected to arrive in Maiduguri, the Borno State capital, on Wednesday for the APC presidential campaign rally.

title: FG, Soludo, Nollywood stars mourn Pete Edochie
description:
The Federal Government, Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, and Nollywood stars have mourned veteran actor Pete Edochie, who died at the age of 79.
The Federal Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, in a tribute posted on its X handle on Wednesday, described Edochie’s
content:
The Federal Government, Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, and Nollywood stars have mourned veteran actor Pete Edochie, who died at the age of 79.

The Federal Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, in a tribute posted on its X handle on Wednesday, described Edochie’s contributions to Nigerian theatre and film as unforgettable.

The ministry said the actor dedicated decades to his craft, delivering memorable performances and mentoring generations of actors.

The statement read, “Forever in our hearts. For decades, Pete Edochie has dedicated his life to his craft, giving Nigerian theatre and film some of its most memorable performances. His contribution to Nollywood and the generations of actors he has mentored will not be forgotten.

“Thank you for the years, the stories and the legacy. May his soul rest in peace.”

Soludo also mourned the actor, describing him as an institution, a distinguished custodian of culture, a sage and a source of pride to the people of Anambra State.

The governor’s condolence message was contained in a statement issued on Wednesday by his Chief Press Secretary, Christian Aburime.

He described Edochie as a proud son of Anambra and a cultural giant whose work projected Igbo identity, wisdom and dignity to audiences across Nigeria, Africa and beyond.

The statement read, “Chief Pete Edochie was more than an actor. He was an institution, a distinguished custodian of our culture, a sage, and a source of immense pride to Ndi Anambra.

“Through his craft, he taught generations the value of dignity, courage, family and the wisdom of our elders. His passing leaves a void in our creative landscape and in the heart of our State, but his legacy will endure in the stories he told and the lives he touched.

“The Anambra State Government will ensure the late icon is honoured in a manner worthy of his stature and contribution to the State and the nation.”

Soludo extended his condolences to Edochie’s wife, Josephine, their children, the Edochie family, the people of Ifite Nteje, the Nigerian film community and his admirers.

He also prayed for the family to receive the strength to bear the loss and for the deceased to find eternal rest.

Meanwhile, Nollywood actors, entertainers and media personalities have continued to pay tribute to the late actor, highlighting his contributions to the film industry, influence on younger performers and memorable portrayal of Okonkwo in the 1987 Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart.

Actress Uche Jombo described Edochie as one of Nollywood’s greatest pillars, an institution, a master of his craft and a custodian of Nigerian culture.

In her tribute on X, she said, “He gave Nigerian storytelling a face, a voice and a legacy that will outlive generations.”

She added that although the industry had lost a legend, his work, wisdom and legacy would continue to speak for generations.

Comedian Sabinus also mourned the actor, describing him as an oracle and a legend, while disc jockey DJ Kaywise wrote, “Rest in paradise, Chief Pete Edochie. Thank you for everything. May your soul rest in peace.”

On Instagram, Neon Adejo expressed shock over the news, writing, “Omg.”

Actor Browny Igboegwu also paid tribute, saying, “Daddy you have done your part and we will miss you. Rest daddy rest in peace.”

Media personality Morayo Brown wrote, “May His Soul Rest in Peace.”

Edochie died at 12:30am on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, in Enugu, after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. His death was announced in a family statement signed by his son, Leo Pete Edochie.

He rose to prominence for his portrayal of Okonkwo in the 1987 NTA adaptation of Things Fall Apart, which brought him recognition beyond Nigeria.

Before becoming widely known as an actor, Edochie worked as a broadcaster, beginning his career in 1967. His acting career spanned several decades, during which he featured in numerous Nigerian films.

He was also a recipient of the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON).

The post FG, Soludo, Nollywood stars mourn Pete Edochie appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

May, the estranged wife of the actor’s son, Yul Edochie, expressed her grief in a tribute shared on her Ins
content:
Nollywood actress May Edochie has paid tribute to veteran actor Pete Edochie, whom she described as an institution whose contributions to the Nigerian film industry would remain unforgettable.

May, the estranged wife of the actor’s son, Yul Edochie, expressed her grief in a tribute shared on her Instagram page on Wednesday.

She recalled that false reports of the veteran actor’s death had circulated over the years, but he continued working despite the rumours.

“For so many years, every year, someone somewhere makes a false announcement of your death but you kept going with strength to continue working,” she wrote.

Reflecting on his death, May described it as a reminder of the fragility of human life, noting that people often make plans and assume there will always be another day.

She paid tribute to his legacy, describing him as a veteran whose name, voice and presence would remain memorable in the Nigerian film industry.

“Today, I choose to remember a veteran whose name, voice, presence and contribution to the Nigerian film industry will remain unforgettable. You were an institution, a father figure to many and a man whose legacy will outlive his earthly years,” she said.

May also offered prayers for the actor’s wife, Josephine, and other members of the family, asking God to give them strength to bear the loss.

“God rest your soul, Ononenyi!” she added.

Pete Edochie’s death was announced by his family on Wednesday, November 25, 2026. He died at 12:30am in Enugu, aged 79, after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer.

title: Kano distributes 484 tricycle ambulances to boost rural healthcare
description:
Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf launched the One Ward, One Ambulance initiative by distributing 484 specially designed tricycle ambulances to all 484 political wards across the state’s 44 local government areas.
The initiative, known as the Abba Gida-Gida Rural Ambulance Service, is designed to
content:
Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf launched the One Ward, One Ambulance initiative by distributing 484 specially designed tricycle ambulances to all 484 political wards across the state’s 44 local government areas.

The initiative, known as the Abba Gida-Gida Rural Ambulance Service, is designed to improve access to emergency medical transportation, particularly in rural communities.

The development was contained in a statement issued on Tuesday and signed by the Commissioner for Information and Internal Affairs, Sunusi Bature Dawakin Tofa.

Speaking during the official flag-off ceremony, the governor said the programme was introduced to address the challenges faced by pregnant women, children, accident victims and other vulnerable persons requiring urgent medical attention.

“Healthcare delivery goes beyond building hospitals and primary healthcare centres. An effective health system must also guarantee the timely transportation of patients to medical facilities,” Yusuf said.

He explained that the tricycle ambulances were specially designed to navigate rural roads and difficult terrains, ensuring that emergency medical services reach communities across the state.

“The success of this initiative will not be measured by the number of vehicles distributed, but by the number of lives saved,” the governor stated.

Yusuf called on traditional rulers, religious leaders, community leaders, councillors and healthcare workers to take ownership of the programme and protect the vehicles.

He directed local government chairmen and officials entrusted with the ambulances to ensure their proper maintenance, operation by trained personnel and strict use for their intended purpose.

“I formally declare the One Ward, One Ambulance initiative launched. This is another practical demonstration of our commitment to bringing governance closer to the people,” Yusuf said.

The initiative is expected to strengthen emergency response at the grassroots, particularly in rural communities where conventional ambulances may struggle to navigate narrow roads and difficult terrain.

Access to timely emergency transportation remains a major component of effective healthcare delivery, especially for pregnant women, children, and accident victims requiring urgent medical attention.

title: Adeleke pledges to prioritise welfare, infrastructure in second term
description:
Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has pledged to prioritise citizens’ welfare, infrastructure development, social services and economic growth as he prepares for his second-term inauguration.
Adeleke made the pledge in a state broadcast on Wednesday, ahead of activities marking his second-term i
content:
Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has pledged to prioritise citizens’ welfare, infrastructure development, social services and economic growth as he prepares for his second-term inauguration.

Adeleke made the pledge in a state broadcast on Wednesday, ahead of activities marking his second-term inauguration, while expressing gratitude to residents for their support during his re-election.

The governor assured the people that his administration would sustain a government of the people, by the people and for the people, with greater attention to their needs and aspirations.

“With a deep sense of responsibility, I have come back to you, residents and citizens of our dear state. I again place on record my gratitude for your unqualified support for my re-election,” he said.

Adeleke also paid tribute to those who lost their lives during the 2026 governorship election, acknowledging the sacrifices and challenges experienced by residents in the defence of democracy.

He disclosed that his administration had documented the events surrounding the election in a book titled _The 60 Days Siege_, stressing the need for democratic lessons to be learnt and assimilated.

“We won’t forget; history won’t overlook your travails, our afflictions. We have documented the Osun 2026 election in a book titled: ‘The 60 Days Siege’. Democratic lessons must be learnt and assimilated,” he stated.

The governor also expressed solidarity with families of those killed and other victims of the election, assuring them that their sacrifices would not be forgotten.

He said the best way to reciprocate the support of the people was to expand the delivery of good governance, improve infrastructure and strengthen the state’s economy.

“Our best response is to expand delivery of good governance, deliver more infrastructures, deepen social services and surge the state economy for job creation,” Adeleke said.

He further promised that his administration would remain listening, responsive and proactive in addressing the concerns of residents.

“As we have done in the last four years, we will pay more attention to your needs and aspirations. Our government will continue to be a listening, responsive and proactive one,” he added.

Adeleke maintained that the welfare of citizens remained the primary responsibility of government, pledging to intensify policy implementation to improve the lives of the people.

“The principal goal of a government is the welfare of the citizenry. We will redouble our policy delivery to take Osun and her people to greater heights,” he said.

He also assured residents that he would remain committed to his responsibilities and would not disappoint those who supported his re-election.

“As your governor, I won’t let you down. I will keep the flags flying; I will push ahead to make you proud,” the governor declared.

He concluded by wishing Osun State and the Federal Republic of Nigeria continued peace and progress.
