title: Soludo mourns veteran actor Pete Edochie
description:
By Vincent Ujumadu



Anambra State governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo has expressed deep sadness over the death of veteran Nollywood actor Pete Edochie, describing his passing as a profound loss to his community, Nteje, Igbo people, Nigeria and Africa.



In his condolence message, Soludo said he
content:
By Vincent Ujumadu

Anambra State governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo has expressed deep sadness over the death of veteran Nollywood actor Pete Edochie, describing his passing as a profound loss to his community, Nteje, Igbo people, Nigeria and Africa.

In his condolence message, Soludo said he received with deep grief the news of the death of the celebrated actor, cultural icon, and broadcaster, known to the world as Pete Edochie, who died peacefully in Enugu at the age of 79 years.

The governor described the late Edochie as a proud son of Anambra and a cultural giant whose work carried the Igbo voice, wisdom and dignity to audiences across Nigeria, Africa and the world.

Chief Press Secretary to the governor, Mr Christian Aburime, who signed Soludo’s message recalled that Edochie began his professional life in broadcasting in 1967 with the Eastern Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation, rising over the years to senior management positions, including Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director.

It reads: “His vivid portrayal of Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart in the 1980s brought him national acclaim and opened the door to a long and distinguished career in Nigerian cinema.

“Audiences came to know him through unforgettable portrayals of traditional rulers, community leaders and family patriarchs in films such as Igodo, Rituals and Lionheart. His deep voice, commanding presence, and masterful use of proverbs became the hallmark of his art and, for many, the very sound of Igbo tradition on screen.

“For his contributions to the entertainment industry in Nigeria, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003, and he also received the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards Industry Merit Award and several lifetime achievement honours.

According to the governor, “Chief Pete Edochie was more than an actor. He was an institution, a distinguished custodian of our culture, a sage, and a source of immense pride to Ndi Anambra. Through his craft, he taught generations the value of dignity, courage, family and the wisdom of our elders.

“His passing leaves a void in our creative landscape and in the heart of our state, but his legacy will endure in the stories he told and the lives he touched. The Anambra State Government will ensure the late icon is honoured in a manner worthy of his stature and contribution to the State and the nation.”

Governor Soludo extended condolences to the wife of the deceased, Mrs Josephine Edochie, and their children, the entire Edochie family, as well as the people of Ifite Nteje, the Nigerian film community, and all his admirers, and prayed that God grant the family the strength to bear the loss and grant the departed legend eternal rest.

The post Soludo mourns veteran actor Pete Edochie appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Puerto Rico’s Jennifer Barreto wins Miss Universe 2026
description:
Jennifer Barreto made history on Tuesday after becoming the first married woman and mother to win Miss Universe since the pageant lifted its restrictions on contestants who are married or have children.
The 27-year-old social worker from Puerto Rico was crowned winner of the 75th edition of the comp
content:
Jennifer Barreto made history on Tuesday after becoming the first married woman and mother to win Miss Universe since the pageant lifted its restrictions on contestants who are married or have children.

The 27-year-old social worker from Puerto Rico was crowned winner of the 75th edition of the competition, held in San Juan, the territory’s capital, beating 115 other contestants.

As reported by CNN, her victory marked a major moment for Puerto Rico, which has now won the global beauty competition six times, trailing only the United States and Venezuela in the number of Miss Universe titles.

Barreto secured the crown after impressing the judges during the final question-and-answer session, where contestants were asked about human values in an era of growing artificial intelligence.

Asked which human value should never be lost as AI advances, she said people must use the technology responsibly and remain committed to their principles.

“The best thing is to use it responsibly.

“If artificial intelligence puts our values at risk, then they were never values. Values are found in the consistency between what we say and what we do, especially when upholding those things becomes difficult,” she said in Spanish.

The final featured swimwear and evening gown presentations before the last five contestants faced questions from the judges.

Melissa Núñez of the Dominican Republic emerged as first runner-up, while Venezuela’s Clara Vegas finished second runner-up.

However, this year’s competition was overshadowed by controversies that affected the build-up to the grand finale.

Several contestants, including representatives from Nepal and five African countries, withdrew after encountering difficulties or delays in securing United States visas. The affected African countries included South Sudan and the Republic of Congo, which were participating in the competition for the first time.

Delegates from Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam were also absent following a contractual dispute between the Miss Universe Organisation and Thai businessman Nawat Itsaragrisil, who operates qualifying pageants in six Southeast Asian countries.

The controversy followed allegations of vote-rigging and favouritism at the 2025 edition, which was won by Mexico’s Fátima Bosch.

One of the judges, Omar Harfouch, resigned three days before last year’s finale, alleging that the results had been predetermined by an unofficial panel.

Harfouch also alleged that Bosch’s victory was linked to her father’s business relationship with Miss Universe co-owner Raúl Rocha Cantú. Both the businessman and the organisation denied the allegations.

The concerns over the judging process continued into this year’s competition, with the panel of judges announced only a day before the finale. Independent auditing firm Ernst & Young, which previously handled the verification of results, has not been involved for three years.

Itsaragrisil called for greater transparency in the selection of judges and the scoring process.

“I would like contestants to know who will judge them, how the judges are selected, how scores are verified and how conflicts of interest are handled,” he told CNN before the competition.

He also expressed hope that the six Southeast Asian delegates who missed this year’s contest would be able to participate in the next edition.

The Miss Universe Organisation did not respond to CNN’s request for comment on the judging process or its dispute with Itsaragrisil before the finale.

Despite the controversies, the competition attracted attention, particularly among Latino audiences. Spanish-language broadcaster Telemundo reported that its broadcast of the 2025 finale attracted 2.6 million viewers, compared with 2.1 million the previous year.

This year’s edition was the fourth time Puerto Rico hosted the Miss Universe finale, having previously staged the event in 1972, 2001 and 2002.

The organisation had earlier relaxed its eligibility rules, allowing married women, mothers and contestants who have previously been married to participate. It also removed its longstanding age limit of 28 in 2023.

The post Puerto Rico’s Jennifer Barreto wins Miss Universe 2026 appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
In Nollywood and Nigerian popular culture, few voices have resonated with the weight and wit of late Chief Pete Edochie.

The veteran actor, best known for his iconic portrayal of Okonkwo in the NTA adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart, became a cultural phenomenon not only for his commanding presence and deep baritone voice but for his masterful use of proverbs, adages, and sharp-tongued observations.

From traditional African wisdom adapted for the screen to lines delivered in interviews and public appearances, these sayings cemented his reputation as the “King of Proverbs”, or the wise elder of Nigerian cinema.

Fans, filmmakers, and everyday people continue to quote them for their humour, insight, and practical philosophy on life, relationships, power, caution, and human nature.

In memory of the legend who died on Wednesday at age 79, PUNCH Online curates some of the proverbs, quotes, and words of wisdom most widely attributed to or popularised by Edochie.

Some are traditional African proverbs, especially Igbo, which he made famous through performance, while others he said in character or in interviews.

On Caution, Humility and Wisdom

  1. A person who sells eggs should not start a fight in the market.
  2. Beware of the naked man who offers you clothes.
  3. The little opportunity given to a monkey to wear clothes does not guarantee it to join the dining table.
  4. If a man wants to grow a long tooth, he should have the lip to cover it.
  5. If you sell your father’s land to buy a trumpet, where will you stand to blow it?
  6. The frowning of a he-goat does not stop it from being priced in the market.
  7. Stupidity is what we all have in common as human beings, but some people insist that improving it is their entitlement.
  8. If a fool keeps shut in public, he will be counted as a wise man.
  9. A wise person knows that there is something to be learned from everyone.
  10. It requires wisdom to understand wisdom; the music is nothing if the audience is deaf.
  11. Those who had their nuts cracked by a benevolent spirit should not forget to be humble.
  12. Be careful who you trust! Salt and sugar are both white.
  13. The walls don’t only have ears; they now see.
  14. Never let negative and toxic people rent space in your head. Raise the rent and kick them out.

On Risk, Ambition and Life’s Realities

  1. Let the young man in his desperation go out and hunt. If he kills the elephant, his poverty ends. If the elephant kills him, his poverty ends.
  2. The cow in a hurry to go to America will come back as corned beef.
  3. The wolf on the hill is not as hungry as the wolf climbing the hill.
  4. The future belongs to the risk-takers, not the comfort seekers.
  5. If something that was going to chop off your head only knocks off your cap, you should be grateful.
  6. Whoever presents his own head to break coconut will not partake in the eating of it.
  7. A man who swallows a whole coconut has complete faith in his anus.
  8. Life goes on, even if you don’t want it to.
  9. No matter how rich you are, you cannot pay for your sins.
  10. People often say that motivation doesn’t last. Well, neither does bathing – that’s why we recommend it daily.

On Relationships, Women and Marriage

  1. A man who hangs around a beautiful girl without saying a word ends up fetching water for guests at her wedding.
  2. Girls are like mangoes. While you are waiting for them to ripen, others are eating them with salt.
  3. Having a female as a best friend is like having a chicken for a pet; you will eat it someday.
  4. A girl may never get married if she waits for the perfect man.
  5. When a girl has beauty without brains, the private parts suffer the most.
  6. The buttocks are like a married couple; though there is constant friction between them, they will still love and live together.
  7. A deaf husband and a blind wife are always a happy couple.
  8. No matter how often a man quarrels with his wife, he does not do so when bedtime is near.
  9. The strength of a woman is in her tongue; if a woman provokes you and you strike her, you are not qualified to be called a man.
  10. Any man who gets down on his knee to propose to a girl is not just an idiot but a bloody fool, a compound buffoon.
  11. No matter how dark a room is, a man can always find his way to a woman’s breast.
  12. A farmer who grows corn by the road and a man who has a beautiful woman have the same problem.
  13. He who will marry the daughter of the chief priest must be prepared to eat concoction all the time.
  14. However kind a man is, he will never give his wife as a gift to his friends.
  15. Party is not an option; a man who truly loves you would never think of sharing you with friends.

On Power, Status and Society

  1. The death of a lion cannot be announced by a goat.
  2. As powerful as a king is, he cannot command anyone to pass faeces for him.
  3. When a goat laughs upon hearing that a lion is around, one needs to find out what grass it has been eating.
  4. The lion may be the king of the jungle, but that same lion can be shot by the hunter’s gun.
  5. Those who are too smart to engage in politics are punished by being governed by those who are dumber.
  6. A diplomat is one who thinks twice before saying nothing.
  7. People respect the money and not the person.
  8. A rich man’s lie is trusted more than a poor man’s truth.
  9. When the house-rat starts calling itself bushmeat because it is getting fat, it has started passing its boundary.
  10. The household that pounds yam aloud thinks the silent ones don’t eat.
  11. A man who prevents his friend from becoming a king won’t be a friend to a king.
  12. When one’s goat gets missing, the aroma of a neighbour’s soup gets suspicious.
  13. No one goes to the native doctor to find out why he is doing well in life.

Everyday Observations and Humour

  1. Drinking garri doesn’t mean you are poor, but allowing it to swell before drinking is poverty.
  2. A man who counts his money after withdrawing from the ATM has trust issues.
  3. In this part of the world, it is bad manners for a child to eat the meat before the main food. The meat on the food is your reward; it should be slowly enjoyed.
  4. He who always thinks the soup is too much for the eba cannot handle greatness.
  5. No African girl will choose six packs over six cars. So my sons, stop the gym and work hard.
  6. Just because you met them at the church doesn’t mean they are the ones; demons go to church too.
  7. Never open the door for an armed robber; let them break it — it’s part of their job.
  8. When the cock is drunk, he forgets about the hawk.
  9. By the time the fool has learned the game, the players have dispersed.
  10. The plantain that refuses to ripen because it doesn’t want to be fried will be used for plantain chips.
  11. He who goes to an Owambe wearing shirt and jeans will encounter starvation.
  12. He who throws a party without jollof rice shall taste the bitter wrath of the gods.
  13. Be careful about the rumours you hear about a lady; it either comes from a man who can’t have her or a lady who can’t compete with her.
  14. Sometimes you have to play the role of a fool to fool the fools who think they are fooling you.
  15. Give them a chair if they can’t stand your success.
  16. No matter how bad a man is, he can always serve as a good example of how bad a man can be.
  17. No matter how careless a man is, he will never sit on his testicles.
  18. A child who asks questions does not become a fool.
  19. If you sell a drum in your own village, you get the money and keep the sound.

The post Pete Edochie’s most memorable proverbs, quotes appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Trump hails Infantino as USA to co-host 2031 Women’s World Cup
description:
President Donald Trump praised embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino on Tuesday while celebrating the United States being named a co-host of the 2031 Women’s World Cup.



Infantino, who gave Trump the first FIFA Peace Prize last December, is fighting to keep his job after causing outrage in Jul
content:
President Donald Trump praised embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino on Tuesday while celebrating the United States being named a co-host of the 2031 Women’s World Cup.

Infantino, who gave Trump the first FIFA Peace Prize last December, is fighting to keep his job after causing outrage in July with a shortlived plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

A FIFA election next March in Morocco will decide if Infantino keeps his job against rival contenders Philippe Diallo of France and Kozo Tashima of Japan.

“Thank you to Gianni Infantino, and his great staff, for working to bring the Tournament to the USA,” Trump posted on social media.

Trump and Infantino awarded Spain the trophy at this year’s final of the World Cup, which was co-hosted by Canada and Mexico.

FIFA confirmed Monday that the United States will co-host the 2031 Women’s World Cup with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica after Infantino noted it was the “sole candidacy” for the tournament.

“I am proud to announce that the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2031 will take place in the United States!” Trump posted.

“After hosting the Most Successful World Cup in History, no Country is better positioned than the United States to be home to the largest Women’s Sporting Event in History.”

The Women’s World Cup field will expand to a record 48 teams in 2031.

“The FIFA Women’s World Cup 2031 will bring Generational Economic Impact to the United States, grow the sport of Soccer throughout our Country and the World, and showcase America’s Exceptionalism,” Trump posted.

title: 2027: ‘No Political Ambition Is Worth The Life Of A Nigerian’, IGP Warns Politicians
description: The Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, on Tuesday warned politicians against turning the 2027 general elections into a theatre of violence.Speaking at a high-level security meeting in Abuja with the Independent National Electoral Commission, political party leaders, civil society organisations
content:
The Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, on Tuesday warned politicians against turning the 2027 general elections into a theatre of violence.

Speaking at a high-level security meeting in Abuja with the Independent National Electoral Commission, political party leaders, civil society organisations and other stakeholders, Disu described the growing incidents of political violence as a serious threat to public peace and democratic participation.

He warned politicians to desist from violence, which has led to growing cases of reported killings across the country.

“We are meeting at a particularly critical moment in our nation’s democratic journey. Recent incidents of violent clashes among political supporters, attacks on campaign venues and convoys, the use of dangerous weapons, intimidation of political opponents and the disruption of lawful political gatherings have become matters of serious concern.

“These developments threaten public peace, endanger innocent lives and undermine confidence in our democratic institutions. They are warning signs that must be addressed decisively before they escalate into a broader threat to national security.

“ Let me state categorically that political competition must never become a justification for violence. Democracy provides an opportunity for citizens to freely express their political preferences, support candidates of their choice and hold differing opinions without fear or intimidation.

“It must never become a contest of who can mobilise more thugs, deploy more weapons or inflict greater harm on political opponents. No political ambition is worth the life of a Nigerian, and no electoral victory is worth the destruction of our national peace.”

The IGP noted that the Force would not tolerate political violence, warning to take legal actions on those found guilty of employing thugs to intimidate and assault the public.

“The position of the Nigeria Police Force is clear: we have zero tolerance for political violence, irrespective of the political party, candidate, personality or interest involved. Our neutrality in the political process is non-negotiable.

“We owe allegiance to the Constitution, the law and the Nigerian people, not to any political party or individual. We will protect the rights of all lawful political actors to organise rallies, hold meetings and participate in the democratic process.

“However, we will not hesitate to take lawful and decisive action against anyone who engages in thuggery, intimidation, assault, the use of offensive weapons or any conduct capable of disrupting public peace.

“I wish to remind all political actors that the Constitution, the Electoral Act, the INEC Regulations and other applicable laws prescribe clear standards of conduct and consequences for electoral offences.

“Political office, party affiliation or personal influence does not place anyone above the law. The recruitment, financing or deployment of political thugs, threats of violence, attacks on electoral officials, destruction of electoral materials and other unlawful acts will attract appropriate law enforcement action, subject to due process.

“Those who sponsor, finance or direct such acts will be treated with the same seriousness as those who carry them out. The Police will investigate offences professionally and ensure that those found culpable are brought before the appropriate authorities.”

He assured of Police commitment to national peace, while also urging political leaders to cooperate with the police, and to issue clear directives to their followers and supporters against violence.

“The responsibility for peaceful political activities cannot be transferred entirely to the Police. Political party leaders must take ownership of the conduct of their candidates, officials, youth wings and supporters.

“National Chairmen must issue clear directives against violence and ensure that these directives are respected throughout their party structures. National Secretaries must facilitate effective communication and compliance with applicable notification requirements, while youth leaders must mobilise young people for constructive democratic participation rather than expose them to manipulation and political violence.

“Leadership must be demonstrated not only in the pursuit of electoral victories but also in the willingness to restrain supporters and condemn misconduct, even when it comes from within one’s own political camp.”

The IGP urged political parties to respect the rights of their opponents to lawful participation.

“Equally, political parties must respect the rights of their opponents to lawful political participation.

“The Police will facilitate adequate security for legitimate rallies and processions, while working with INEC and political parties to resolve conflicting schedules and prevent avoidable confrontations.

“We expect all parties to comply with the applicable advance notification requirements and cooperate with security agencies. Peaceful political engagement must be protected, just as unlawful conduct must be firmly addressed.”

The post 2027: ‘No Political Ambition Is Worth The Life Of A Nigerian’, IGP Warns Politicians appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Obi mourns Pete Edochie, says actor won’t witness ‘New Nigeria’
description:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has expressed sadness over the death of veteran Nollywood actor Pete Edochie, describing his passing as a significant loss to the Igbo people, Nigeria and Africa.
Obi said the late actor made notable contributions to the
content:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has expressed sadness over the death of veteran Nollywood actor Pete Edochie, describing his passing as a significant loss to the Igbo people, Nigeria and Africa.

Obi said the late actor made notable contributions to the promotion of African culture and traditions through his work in the entertainment industry.

In a condolence message shared on X on Wednesday, the former Anambra State governor praised Edochie’s talent, broadcasting experience and command of both English and Igbo languages.

He also highlighted the actor’s portrayal of Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s novel, Things Fall Apart, saying the performance helped introduce African cultural values to audiences around the world.

“Pete was a rare talent who seamlessly combined the experience of an accomplished broadcaster, a deep understanding of our culture and an exceptional command of both English and Igbo,” Obi said.

He added that Edochie’s performances, particularly his role in Things Fall Apart, helped project Nigerian and African traditions internationally.

Obi, who said he had met the actor several times, recalled that their conversations were always engaging and left him wishing he had spent more time with him.

He described Edochie as an important custodian of cultural heritage whose contributions would continue to influence Nigeria’s identity.

The NDC presidential candidate said he was particularly saddened that the actor would not live to witness the emergence of the Nigeria he had hoped for.

“I am particularly saddened that he would not live to witness the emergence of the New Nigeria he believed in and fought so passionately for,” Obi said.

Edochie’s death was announced by his family on Wednesday. He was 79.

Obi prayed for the repose of the actor’s soul, adding that his voice, artistic contributions and role in preserving cultural identity would remain memorable.

title: Two children, four others die in US plane crash
description:
Six people, including two children, have been confirmed dead after a small plane crashed into the Gulf of Mexico off the coast of Mississippi, the United States Coast Guard has said.
The Cessna 210 aircraft was travelling from New Orleans, Louisiana, to Fort Myers, Florida, when it crashed on Tuesda
content:
Six people, including two children, have been confirmed dead after a small plane crashed into the Gulf of Mexico off the coast of Mississippi, the United States Coast Guard has said.

The Cessna 210 aircraft was travelling from New Orleans, Louisiana, to Fort Myers, Florida, when it crashed on Tuesday.

According to the BBC on Wednesday, air traffic controllers lost contact with the aircraft at about 15:45 local time (21:45 GMT), before it went down in the Gulf of Mexico between Pascagoula and Horn Island.

Coast Guard spokesperson Juan Ros said divers recovered the bodies of four adults and two boys, aged eight and 10, inside the aircraft’s fuselage.

Rescue teams had spent several hours searching for the missing occupants after the crash.

Ros said initial findings at the scene included three life jackets, a life raft and the aircraft’s cabin floating on the water.

The Coast Guard later located the wreckage and recovered all six bodies from inside the fuselage.

Reacting to the tragedy, Cmdr Trevor Blount, the Coast Guard rescue mission coordinator, expressed sadness over the loss of lives while commending the agencies involved in the search and rescue operation.

“While this is not the outcome any of us had hoped for, we are grateful for the strong interagency co-ordination that enabled us to swiftly locate those aboard the aircraft and provide closure to their families,” Blount said.

The circumstances surrounding the crash were not immediately clear.

The post Two children, four others die in US plane crash appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: The Price Of Participation
content:
Deadly violence in Delta sharpens the question of campaign safety, while economic policy and electoral preparations face tests.

An election campaign should ask citizens for their votes. In Uduere, Delta State, families are now mourning people who went to a political gathering.

Police said on Tuesday that six people died in Monday’s violence at a campaign event in Ughelli North. That preliminary figure is higher than the four deaths initially reported by Ovie Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation. The circumstances and responsibility remain under investigation.

This is the most consequential political development since Friday.

Its significance extends beyond one party’s campaign. Every attack raises a question for the next person considering attending a meeting, volunteering or accompanying a candidate: is participation worth the risk?

When citizens begin making that calculation, electoral competition has already suffered.

Delta Needs Evidence And Accountability

The NDC has alleged official complicity. The Delta State Government has rejected attempts to link Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to the violence, condemned the killings and promised that those responsible will face justice. Those competing positions must remain distinct from investigative findings.

The state has imposed a daily 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. curfew across Ughelli North. Restoring calm is an immediate necessity. Establishing responsibility is the next obligation.

The investigation should establish the sequence of events, identify those who used weapons and examine allegations about the conduct of officials and security personnel. Witnesses need protection, and the public needs credible updates.

Political leaders also have an immediate responsibility to restrain inflammatory claims and prevent retaliation.

The standard is straightforward: lawful political activity must receive protection regardless of the party organising it.

A Separate Court Decision Changes The Delta Contest

On Tuesday, the Federal High Court in Warri nullified Omo-Agege’s nomination as the NDC’s Delta Central senatorial candidate and directed INEC to remove his name. Reporting attributes the decision to failures concerning the party’s membership register and nomination requirements. Responses from Omo-Agege and the NDC were unavailable in the initial reports.

The ruling and Monday’s violence are separate matters. Their proximity establishes no connection between them.

Electorally, however, the judgment creates fresh uncertainty around an influential politician and the organisation supporting him. Any subsequent appeal, interim order and INEC action will matter.

The wider lesson reaches across party lines: recruitment and defections must be supported by lawful nomination procedures. Political prominence cannot resolve defective paperwork.

Tinubu’s Lagos Outreach Meets An Economic Request

President Bola Tinubu’s meeting with Igbo stakeholders in Lagos on Monday continued his effort to broaden support through community and business networks.

According to the presidency, participants pledged support while Tinubu offered assurances of inclusive governance. Traders’ representative Tony Nwakeze also requested loans at five per cent interest to help businesses expand and move towards manufacturing. That was a request; the account did not announce an operational loan scheme.

The economic request gives the gathering significance beyond its endorsements.

Business owners want access to finance, reliable services and room to grow. Their electoral decisions may depend on whether political commitments produce practical improvements.

The gathering demonstrates outreach and organised support among those present. It cannot establish the preferences of an entire ethnic community. Voters retain their individual judgments, including when community leaders endorse a candidate.

The CBN Holds Its Position

The Central Bank’s Monetary Policy Committee retained the benchmark interest rate at 23 per cent today.

Set beside the traders’ request, the decision illustrates a central political tension: preserving economic stability while improving access to affordable finance.

The policy rate and the interest charged on a particular business loan are different measures. Even so, financing costs remain part of the environment in which enterprises decide whether to invest, employ and expand.

For the government, the campaign challenge is to show how stabilisation will translate into stronger livelihoods.

For the opposition, promising cheaper credit requires an explanation of funding, eligibility, repayment and protection against politically connected beneficiaries.

Voters deserve to see how those proposals would work.

Opposition Cooperation Still Awaits Its Decision Day

The opposition’s second summit remains scheduled for November 30, following its postponement from November 23. Organisers intend participating parties and candidates to endorse a framework for cooperation, democratic renewal and reform. A common presidential candidate has not been announced.

The distinction matters.

Parties can cooperate on election monitoring, campaign freedoms and policy priorities while continuing to compete for votes. Whether they intend to go further needs an explicit answer.

Monday’s summit should be assessed through its commitments: who signs, what each participant authorises and what work begins afterward.

The ADC, NDC, APM, SDP, PRP and participating PDP faction also have different local interests to reconcile. A national understanding becomes useful when constituency organisations know how to act on it.

Saturday Offers A Measurable Test

INEC has selected 17,676 polling units, covering two units in each registration area, for its nationwide mock accreditation and result-upload exercise on Saturday, November 28. The announced operating hours are 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Nigerian time.

This gives parties, observers and voters an opportunity to assess performance before the general election.

The useful evidence will include whether equipment works, eligible participants can be accredited, results upload correctly and failures receive a prompt, documented response.

INEC should publish findings and explain the corrective work required. A test earns public value when its results can be examined.

The position of the main camps is clearer in some respects, while important uncertainties remain:

•APC/Tinubu: outreach continues through party, community and business networks. The challenge is converting endorsements and the government’s record into individual votes.
•ADC/Atiku: the leadership appeal remains consequential. INEC’s latest reported position is that it will await the appellate decision before determining its next action; that does not establish that the ADC has won its appeal.
•NDC/Obi-Kwankwaso: the Delta violence creates immediate safety concerns, while the Omo-Agege judgment introduces a separate organisational uncertainty.
•APM/Makinde and other opposition partners: November 30 will test whether negotiations produce defined, implementable cooperation.

State and constituency developments deserve attention because presidential campaigns depend on local organisers, candidates and polling agents. Recent local and off-cycle results can inform that assessment when turnout, competitiveness and local circumstances are considered.

Election Watch assessment: campaign safety and legal uncertainty have become more consequential. The material reviewed does not support declaring a fresh national swing.

Can Young People Participate Without Paying With Their Safety?

The Delta deaths give this edition’s Youth Metre an immediate focus: the conditions under which people enter political life.

Campaigns depend on volunteers, organisers and supporters. Those participants need protection, clear responsibilities and leaders who reject intimidation consistently.

Young Nigerians should also have meaningful roles in examining proposals and holding campaigns accountable. Employment promises need funding and delivery plans. Enterprise support needs published access rules. Training needs a credible connection to work.

Saturday’s INEC exercise offers another practical point of engagement: eligible participants can help test the process, while accredited observers and journalists document performance and unresolved problems.

Youth Metre assessment: safety, economic opportunity and confidence in vote counting are the priorities to watch. No fresh, credible age-specific polling reviewed establishes a change in youth candidate preference.

What To Watch Before Friday

•Investigative findings and accountability following the Uduere killings.

•Any response, appeal or INEC action concerning Omo-Agege’s nomination.

•Any appellate order affecting the ADC leadership dispute.

•INEC’s arrangements for observing and reporting Saturday’s test.

•Final confirmation of the November 30 summit’s participants and commitments.

The Signal

Political party tracker

Party Latest verified position
APC No additional major defection or nomination change established today.

PDP Disagreement over participation in the proposed opposition coalition remains unresolved.

ADC Presidential nomination and national leadership litigation remain unresolved.

NDC Delta Central nomination nullified; party boycotts police security meeting.
Labour Party Disputed endorsement of Tinubu by the Abure faction has not changed the officially listed presidential ticket.

NNPP: No newly verified material organisational change.
APGA Existing presidential cooperation with APC remains in place.

APM, PRP and SDP Proposed November 30 opposition cooperation summit remains the next significant milestone.
Accord No additional qualifying electoral development established today.

The ADC leadership appeal and opposition coalition arrangements remain outstanding, with no newly verified resolution in today’s review.

Geopolitical-Zone Assessment

Geopolitical zone: Electoral development to monitor

South-South: Delta Central candidacy dispute and campaign security

South-East No newly verified material change

South-West: Election technology preparations in Lagos and Oyo

North-Central: Campaign access, security and existing party disputes

North-West: Existing political realignments, particularly in Kano

North-East: Outstanding candidate nomination disputes
Nationwide Election personnel recruitment and technology readiness

Countdown To 2027

Presidential & National Assembly
53 days
16 January 2027

Governorship & State Assembly
74 days
6 February 2027

Upcoming Milestones

28 Nov. INEC nationwide technology test

30 Nov. Proposed opposition coalition summit

2 Dec. Tinubu eligibility litigation resumes

3 Dec. INEC ad hoc personnel recruitment deadline

The Bottom Line

The Omo-Agege judgment represents a concrete change in the legal position of a National Assembly candidacy. The NDC’s security meeting boycott and INEC’s personnel shortage also raise substantive questions about the conditions under which the elections will be conducted.

With less than two months until the presidential election, electoral preparedness, campaign freedom and candidate eligibility deserve as much scrutiny as party alignments.

Electoral map: Delta Central requires a candidate-level adjustment, subject to appellate proceedings.

Presidential voter preferences: No newly verified evidence supports a change in the national assessment.

Campaigns are asking Nigerians to invest their hopes, time and resources in the coming election. The institutions and leaders involved owe them protection and a credible process.

The freedom to participate safely is the first promise every campaign must honour.

title: Imansuagbon woos Nigerians, says ADC candidate can end APC misrule
description: A stalwart of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and former Edo State governorship aspirant, Barrister Kenneth Imansuagbon, has called on Nigerians and lovers of democracy to rally behind former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, describing him as the most viable candidate capable of rescuing the cou
content:
A stalwart of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and former Edo State governorship aspirant, Barrister Kenneth Imansuagbon, has called on Nigerians and lovers of democracy to rally behind former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, describing him as the most viable candidate capable of rescuing the country from poverty, hunger, insecurity and what he termed the mismanagement of the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led administration.

Imansuagbon, who made the call on Wednesday while felicitating with Atiku on his birthday, urged Nigerians to translate their desire for a better country into electoral action by voting for the former Vice President.

He said the country required purposeful leadership, economic direction and a government committed to the welfare of the people, arguing that Atiku possessed the experience and political capacity to provide the needed change.

The popular Edo politician and educationist, in a statement signed and made available to journalists in Benin City, described Atiku as a statesman of uncommon courage and a steadfast defender of democracy whose contributions to Nigeria’s democratic development remained indelible.

He said the former Vice President had, over several decades, remained at the forefront of the struggle for participatory governance, the rule of law and the protection of citizens’ rights.

According to him, Atiku’s consistent advocacy for national unity, political inclusion, restructuring and institutional reforms has continued to shape conversations about Nigeria’s future.

Imansuagbon, popularly known as the ‘Rice Man’, said the ADC regarded Atiku as a father figure and a symbol of hope whose political ideals were in tandem with the party’s vision of building a just, prosperous and egalitarian society.

title: Germany book quarter-final place with five goals in Berlin
description: Germany reached the Nations League quarter-finals with a 5–0 victory over the Netherlands at Berlin’s Olympiastadion on 16 November 2026. Florian Wirtz scored twice as Jürgen Klopp’s side finished top of Group A2. The Netherlands also qualified, with both teams edging out Greece after all three ende
content:
Germany reached the Nations League quarter-finals with a 5–0 victory over the Netherlands at Berlin’s Olympiastadion on 16 November 2026. Florian Wirtz scored twice as Jürgen Klopp’s side finished top of Group A2. The Netherlands also qualified, with both teams edging out Greece after all three ended on 11 points. The match drew a sold-out crowd of 71,765 spectators.

Before kick-off, Germany had been quoted at decimal odds of 1.80 to win, against 3.60 for the Netherlands and 4.33 for a draw. Seeding also matters to quarter-final forecasts used in an affiliate campaign with Bizbet Partners, since Germany will play the return leg at home. The Dutch had arrived in Berlin following a 7–0 victory over Greece three days earlier.

Wirtz turns a narrow lead into a clear victory

Derry Scherhant broke the deadlock in the 41st minute. Receiving Joshua Kimmich’s pass, he cut inside and curled his finish into the top corner. It was his first senior international goal, scored in his home city, and gave Germany a 1–0 half-time lead.

Wirtz doubled the advantage after an hour with a shot from outside the penalty area. Nico Schlotterbeck then headed in a free-kick before Wirtz added his second in the 71st minute. Brajan Gruda completed the scoring after Scherhant struck the woodwork.

A pre-match goalscorer comparison, updated on 16 November, had listed Wirtz at 3.10, Scherhant at 3.50 and Gruda at 3.60 to score at any time. All three found the net, with Wirtz contributing twice during Germany’s decisive second-half spell.

Gruda’s contribution extended beyond the final goal. He supplied the free-kick for Schlotterbeck’s header and combined with Wirtz for Germany’s fourth, finishing with two assists. Scherhant had also struck the post before opening the scoring.

The four goals after the interval transformed a close contest. Germany recorded their biggest winning margin against the Netherlands since a 7–0 success in 1959, finishing the group with eight goals across their final two fixtures.

Eleven points produced three different finishes

Greece’s 1–0 win over Serbia meant the order could not be settled by points alone. The three-way head-to-head comparison placed Germany first, the Netherlands second and Greece third. Serbia finished without a point.

Position Team Points Goals scored Goals conceded
1 Germany 11 11 3
2 Netherlands 11 14 10
3 Greece 11 6 10
4 Serbia 0 4 12

Germany had entered the November window with five points from four matches. Their route to the top changed through two victories:

  • A 3–1 win away to Serbia on 13 November took them to eight points.
  • The five goals against the Netherlands secured qualification and first place on the final night.

The reverse fixture had finished 1–1 in September. Germany had also taken only one point from two meetings with Greece, leaving work to do in November.

Klopp’s team finished with three wins, two draws and one defeat. Their overall goal record was 11 scored and three conceded. The Netherlands scored more across the six fixtures, but Germany’s advantage in the direct comparison determined the final order.

A seeded position for the March tie

In the outright betting comparison available on 17 November, Germany’s tournament-winning odds ranged from 7.00 to 10.00. The Netherlands were quoted between 11.00 and 15.00. Germany therefore stood ahead of the opponents they had just beaten, while their next knockout matchup remained unconfirmed.

The quarter-final draw is scheduled for 20 November. Germany will face a runner-up from another group, with the two legs taking place during the 25–30 March 2027 window. Winning the group gives them the return fixture at home.

Germany end their November fixtures with four different scorers contributing against the Netherlands. In March, Klopp’s side will have to sustain their performance across two legs, with the second match on familiar ground. The prize beyond that tie is a place at the Nations League finals in June.

title: Pete Edochie’s death a loss to Nigeria, Africa – Obi
description:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, has described the death of veteran Nollywood actor, Pete Edochie, as a “profound loss” to Nteje, the Igbo people, Nigeria and Africa.
Obi, in a tribute posted on his X handle on Wednesday, said the late actor was a distinguish
content:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, has described the death of veteran Nollywood actor, Pete Edochie, as a “profound loss” to Nteje, the Igbo people, Nigeria and Africa.

Obi, in a tribute posted on his X handle on Wednesday, said the late actor was a distinguished son of Anambra State whose contributions to broadcasting, acting and the preservation of African cultural heritage would remain indelible.

“I am deeply saddened by the passing of Chief Pete Edochie, MON, a distinguished son of Anambra State and one of Africa’s most celebrated actors,” Obi wrote.

The former Anambra State governor described Edochie as a rare talent who combined his broadcasting experience with a deep understanding of African culture and an exceptional command of English and Igbo.

According to him, the actor’s memorable performances, particularly his portrayal of Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s classic novel, Things Fall Apart, helped project Nigerian culture and traditions to audiences across the world.

“Pete was a rare talent who seamlessly combined the experience of an accomplished broadcaster, a deep understanding of our culture and an exceptional command of both English and Igbo.

“Through his memorable performances, especially his portrayal of Okonkwo in ‘Things Fall Apart,’ he brought our culture and traditions to audiences across the world,” Obi said.

Obi, who said he had the privilege of meeting and listening to the actor on several occasions, recalled that their encounters were always engaging.

“I had the privilege of being with him and listening to him on several occasions. Each encounter was so engaging that I often wished I could remain longer in his company,” he said.

He further described Edochie as “a remarkable custodian of our cultural heritage,” noting that his influence extended beyond the entertainment industry.

He said the actor’s death was particularly painful because he would not live to witness the emergence of the “New Nigeria” he believed in and passionately advocated.

“His death is a profound loss to Nteje, Ndigbo, Nigeria and Africa.

“I am particularly saddened that he would not live to witness the emergence of the New Nigeria he believed in and fought so passionately for,” Obi stated.

He added that the late actor’s voice, artistry and contributions to Nigeria’s cultural identity would remain unforgettable.

“His voice, artistry and contribution to our cultural identity will remain indelible,” Obi said.

He prayed for the repose of the actor’s soul, adding, “May God grant his soul eternal repose. Amen.”

Edochie’s death was announced by his family on Wednesday.

He died at the age of 79 in Enugu after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer, according to reports quoting the family’s statement.

The veteran actor, who was born in Nteje, Anambra State, began his professional career in broadcasting before gaining widespread recognition for his portrayal of Okonkwo in the 1987 television adaptation of Achebe’s Things Fall Apart.

His performance established him as one of Nigeria’s most recognisable actors and earned him enduring acclaim across Africa.

Edochie was also known for his commanding screen presence and roles as traditional rulers, community leaders and family patriarchs.

He was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger in 2003 in recognition of his contributions to the entertainment industry.

The post Pete Edochie’s death a loss to Nigeria, Africa – Obi appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: My dad died from fake drugs — IMAN president
description:
……IMAN to introduce TIN for importers in 2027







By Efe Onodjae & Jacintha Ezugwu



The President of the Importers Association of Nigeria (IMAN), George Ndubuisi, has said his personal experience of losing his father to fake drugs has strengthened his resolve to fight the importation and distri
content:
……IMAN to introduce TIN for importers in 2027

By Efe Onodjae & Jacintha Ezugwu

The President of the Importers Association of Nigeria (IMAN), George Ndubuisi, has said his personal experience of losing his father to fake drugs has strengthened his resolve to fight the importation and distribution of counterfeit and adulterated products in Nigeria.

Ndubuisi, who disclosed that his father died in 2013 after taking drugs he described as fake, said the association would introduce an importer identification number in February 2027 to ensure that every imported container and its contents could be traced to a particular individual.

He said this during an end of the year party with the association at the Apapa office, Lagos.

According to him the initiative was designed to hold importers accountable for prohibited and substandard goods entering the country, while protecting clearing agents from bearing the consequences of import violations committed by their clients.

The IMAN president said the proposed system would ensure that every container brought into the country was linked to a specific importer through shipping documents and other relevant records.

He said, “In February 2027, IMAN is going to take a new position because the goalpost determines where you will put the goal.

“We are shifting the goalpost to ensure that every container or import that comes into the country is tagged to a particular person. That gives room for an IMAN identification number, through which every importer registered on our platform is a confirmed importer.

“If you are not on our platform, you are not an importer.”

Ndubuisi said the initiative became necessary because some importers allegedly bring prohibited goods, including arms and ammunition, into the country without proper identification.

He lamented that when such consignments are intercepted by the Nigeria Customs Service, clearing agents often bear the consequences while the importers disappear.

He said the proposed identification system would make it difficult for importers to evade responsibility, adding that their identities would be traceable through shipping documents.

“Even in the case of a breach, when Customs holds the goods, the people who suffer are the agents, while the importers go into hiding.

“With this measure, we want to bring the importer to book. Even if you try to hide, your identity on the shipping documents represents who you are,” he said.

The IMAN president explained that the identification number would be linked to the bank account of the importer, making it easier to establish ownership of imported goods and trace individuals responsible for bringing substandard products into the country.

He said the system would also help identify importers involved in the importation of fake and adulterated products, which he described as a major threat to public health and the economy.

Ndubuisi expressed optimism that the initiative would significantly reduce the circulation of counterfeit products, even if it achieved only a 20 per cent reduction.

“Anyone who brings in fake, adulterated products can easily be spotted with the identification number, which is why we are implementing it this February.

“I believe it is going to make a big change and reduce the nuisance we are facing in the country due to fake products.

“Even if we can take out 20 per cent of fake products, it is a good job. We need to save our community, our future, and that is the reason for the programme,” he said.

He added that the initiative was aimed at protecting consumers, importers and clearing agents, while safeguarding the Nigerian economy from the harmful effects of illicit imports.

Ndubuisi said the association was determined to ensure that importers could no longer hide behind shipping agents or other intermediaries when prohibited or substandard goods were discovered in their consignments.

title: ‘If you are not planning to rig, why are you afraid?’ – Ex-INEC director defends Omo-Agege
description: A former Director of the Political Party Monitoring and Liaison Department of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Dr Regina Omo-Agege, has defended her brother, former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege, over his controversial “Rig and Die” slogan ahead of the 2027 general elec
content:
A former Director of the Political Party Monitoring and Liaison Department of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Dr Regina Omo-Agege, has defended her brother, former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege, over his controversial “Rig and Die” slogan ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Regina argued that Nigerians should not be worried about the expression if they have no intention of manipulating election results.

She made the remarks during an interview on Arise News, where she questioned the criticism trailing her brother’s statement.

“My brother was quoted to have said, ‘Rig and die’. One begins to wonder: Do you want to rig? Why will anybody want to rig elections? So maybe out of fear, you see,” she said.

The former INEC director suggested that Omo-Agege might have made the statement out of concern over possible electoral manipulation, adding that other political figures had used similar expressions in the past.

She argued that the former Deputy Senate President was not the first person to make such a remark, claiming that individuals in government had previously issued similar warnings against election rigging.

“If you do your research well, you find that many people used it before him. People in government, they use this, and they even went as far as quoting the law that the only punishment for anybody that rigs is to die,” she stated.

Reacting to INEC’s concerns that the slogan could encourage violence against electoral officials, election materials and facilities, Regina acknowledged the commission’s position but questioned the possibility of such incidents.

She said INEC was a reputable institution that had no interest in electoral malpractice, but wondered why anyone who conducted themselves properly during an election should fear possible violence.

“INEC is a very standard organisation that would not want people to rig, and I appreciate their fear that whatever happens might lead to jungle justice, but if you don’t do anything that will lead to jungle justice, who will give you jungle justice?” she asked.

Regina further stressed the need for free, fair and credible elections, questioning why anyone would approach an election with the intention of manipulating the process.

“Why will you come out of your house thinking of rigging? Why? Let me understand free, fair, and credible election for this country. That’s all. That’s what all of us want,” she added.

Her comments come amid growing controversy over Omo-Agege’s repeated use of the “Rig and Die” slogan, which INEC has warned could heighten political tension and endanger the lives of electoral officials, voters and other stakeholders ahead of the 2027 elections.

Omo-Agege, who is seeking to represent Delta Central Senatorial District under the Nigeria Democratic Congress, has maintained that his statement was directed at election riggers and not ordinary voters or electoral officials.

However, INEC has urged political leaders to avoid inflammatory language and rely on lawful procedures to address suspected electoral malpractice.

The post ‘If you are not planning to rig, why are you afraid?’ – Ex-INEC director defends Omo-Agege appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: NSCDC arrests three over billboard vandalism in Anambra
description:
The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Anambra State Command, has arrested three suspects in connection with the vandalism of a billboard and other government symbols at Regina Junction, adjacent to Tracas Company, in Awka South Local Government Area of Anambra State.
The suspects, identified
content:
The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Anambra State Command, has arrested three suspects in connection with the vandalism of a billboard and other government symbols at Regina Junction, adjacent to Tracas Company, in Awka South Local Government Area of Anambra State.

The suspects, identified as Lateef Babalola, Mohammed Alhassan and Richard Peter, all male, were arrested on Monday at about 08:50 hours by operatives of the command who were on routine surveillance of critical national assets and infrastructure, while they were allegedly vandalising the billboard.

This was disclosed in a press statement issued on Wednesday by the Head of Media and Tactical Operations, NSCDC, Anambra State Command, CSC Edwin Okadigbo.

Okadigbo said the command viewed the act as a crime and a direct attack on public property, constituted authority and the relative peace currently being enjoyed in Anambra State.

The statement read, “The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Anambra State Command, has arrested three suspects in connection with the vandalism of a billboard and other government symbols situated at Regina Junction in Awka, Awka South Local Government Area of Anambra State.

“The suspects, identified as Lateef Babalola, Mohammed Alhassan and Richard Peter, all male, were arrested on Monday, at about 08:50 hours by operatives of the Command on routine surveillance of critical national assets and infrastructure, while vandalising the billboard.

“A preliminary investigation revealed that the suspects were engaged by an individual to dismantle the billboard.

“Further findings suggest that the suspects may be part of a larger criminal syndicate involved in the theft, destruction and sale of vandalised public infrastructure.

“Items recovered from the suspects included one big generator set, one welding machine, hand-held filling machine and one truck with Registration Number Bauchi KTG 02 XA.

“The suspects are currently in the custody of the Command for discreet investigation, after which they will be charged to court if found culpable.”

Reacting to the arrest, the State Commandant of the NSCDC, Anambra State Command, Olatunde Maku, reiterated the command’s commitment to protecting critical national assets and infrastructure across the state.

Maku warned vandals and criminal elements to desist from such acts, stressing that the command would not relent in its efforts to bring perpetrators to justice.

He further urged members of the public to join hands in preserving public infrastructure and continue to provide timely and credible information to the Corps to aid its operations.

The command assured residents that it would continue to intensify efforts to safeguard public infrastructure and bring offenders to justice.

Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Nigerian Police Force warned political parties, candidates and their supporters against destroying, removing or defacing opponents’ campaign materials.

The Force said such acts were unlawful and contrary to peaceful democratic engagement, adding that violators would face sanctions.

title: Bellingham dismisses Ballon d’Or ambition, prioritises Real Madrid trophies
description:
Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham has dismissed suggestions that winning the Ballon d’Or is his priority, insisting that team success and trophies matter more than individual recognition.
The England international made the remarks after an impressive performance in Real Madrid’s 5-1 comeback vi
content:
Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham has dismissed suggestions that winning the Ballon d’Or is his priority, insisting that team success and trophies matter more than individual recognition.

The England international made the remarks after an impressive performance in Real Madrid’s 5-1 comeback victory over PSV in the UEFA Champions League.

Bellingham started the encounter on the bench but was introduced in the second half after Madrid went into the break trailing 1-0 to the Dutch side.

His introduction helped turn the game around, with captain Federico Valverde equalising in the 50th minute before Bellingham put Madrid ahead 10 minutes later with a stunning volley.

The 23-year-old controlled the ball outside the penalty area before unleashing an exquisite effort with the outside of his right foot past PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar.

Kylian Mbappe added two goals, while Vinicius Junior completed the scoring to seal an emphatic victory for the Spanish giants.

Speaking after the match, Bellingham played down his chances of winning the Ballon d’Or, saying his ambition was to win major trophies with Real Madrid, including the Champions League and the league title.

“I don’t care about the Ballon d’Or, honestly. I want to win a lot of titles with the team, the Champions League, the League,” he said.

“The Ballon d’Or is something for you, journalists, to vote and create a bit of tension. But for me it’s more important that the team win.”

Madrid manager Jose Mourinho praised the midfielder, describing him as the best player in his position.

“He is an amazing player that has everything. He has physicality, he understands the game, he has absolutely everything. Today, he has changed how the game was evolving,” Mourinho said.

Bellingham’s stunning strike was his fourth goal in his last five appearances for Madrid, further highlighting his growing influence in the team.

However, the midfielder remained modest when asked to compare himself with former Real Madrid and France great Zinedine Zidane.

“I think Zidane is much better than me. He’s much more elegant and he’s my idol,” he said.

Bellingham also stressed the importance of consistency, saying his attention had already shifted to Madrid’s next fixture.

“I think you’re only as good as your next one. Your last one doesn’t really matter,” he added.

Despite the growing attention surrounding his performances, Bellingham maintained that collective achievements, rather than individual awards, remained his priority at the Santiago Bernabeu.

title: Police arrest suspected cultist, recover gun in Ogun
description:
The Ogun State Police Command has arrested a 25-year-old man, Yusuf Olasunkami, over alleged involvement in cult-related activities and recovered a locally made pistol and three cartridges during an intelligence-led operation in Bode Olude, Abeokuta.
The suspect was reportedly arrested by operatives
content:
The Ogun State Police Command has arrested a 25-year-old man, Yusuf Olasunkami, over alleged involvement in cult-related activities and recovered a locally made pistol and three cartridges during an intelligence-led operation in Bode Olude, Abeokuta.

The suspect was reportedly arrested by operatives of the Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) Unit on November 21, 2026, following actionable intelligence the command reportedly received about suspected criminal activities in the area.

According to a statement issued on Wednesday by the Police Public Relations Officer, Ogun State Command, DSP Oluseyi  Babaseyi, the operation was coordinated by the Officer-in-Charge of the SWAT Unit, SP Obeh Eneye.

Babaseyi explained that the operatives began discreet surveillance after receiving the intelligence, which led them to the suspect’s residence in Odo Eja, Bode Olude, where they arrested him.

The statement partly read, “The Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) Unit of the Ogun State Police Command has arrested one Yusuf Olasunkami, male, aged 25, suspected of cult-related activities, and recovered a locally made pistol and ammunition during an intelligence-led operation at Bode Olude, Ogun State.

“The operation, conducted on 21 November 2026, followed actionable intelligence gathered by the Command on suspected criminal activities within the area. Acting on the information, SWAT operatives, led by the Officer-in-Charge, SP Obeh Eneye, conducted discreet surveillance, which led to the suspect’s arrest at his residence in Odo Eja, Bode Olude.

“A search conducted at the premises resulted in the recovery of one locally made pistol, two expended cartridges and one live cartridge.

“Preliminary investigation indicates the suspect’s alleged affiliation with the Aiye Confraternity and he is currently in police custody, while investigation continues to establish the full circumstances of the case and identify other persons who may be connected to it.”

Reacting to the arrest, the state Commissioner of Police, CP Bode Ojajuni, reaffirmed the command’s commitment to proactive and intelligence-driven policing, particularly in tackling cultism and other forms of criminality across the state.

Ojajuni also appealed to residents to support security agencies by providing credible and timely information that could assist in preventing crime and apprehending suspected offenders.

The commissioner assured residents that the police would sustain efforts to protect lives and property, stressing the importance of public cooperation in maintaining security across Ogun State.

title: Guardiola urges Portugal to give Ronaldo dignified farewell
description:
Former Manchester City manager, Pep Guardiola, has urged the Portuguese Football Federation to give Cristiano Ronaldo a fitting farewell, saying the five-time Ballon d’Or winner deserves to end his international career on a dignified note.
Guardiola, speaking in an interview with former Brazil strik
content:
Former Manchester City manager, Pep Guardiola, has urged the Portuguese Football Federation to give Cristiano Ronaldo a fitting farewell, saying the five-time Ballon d’Or winner deserves to end his international career on a dignified note.

Guardiola, speaking in an interview with former Brazil striker Romário on Tuesday, said both the federation and Ronaldo needed to make efforts to ensure the football icon received a proper send-off after his 23-year stint with the national team.

“The Portuguese Football Federation must ensure a dignified end to Cristiano Ronaldo’s career.

“Both sides need to make an effort to guarantee a fitting farewell. Cristiano Ronaldo shouldn’t leave the Portuguese national team in this manner. They can’t let him go like this,” Guardiola said.

The former Manchester City manager described Ronaldo as “an incredibly important figure, not only for himself and Portugal, but for future generations of Portuguese players”, adding that the 41-year-old deserved to leave on his own terms.

“There are exceptional players, and Cristiano Ronaldo is one of them; therefore, this situation must be rectified,” Guardiola said.

“Whether they rectify it or not isn’t my concern, but they absolutely must. What he’s achieved in the world of football deserves a different ending.”

Guardiola called for a public celebration to allow Ronaldo feel the love and appreciation of Portuguese fans, while urging the player to move past recent disagreements.

“There should be a celebration where he feels the love of his countrymen, and he, in turn, must also take the initiative and say: Let’s turn the page on the past,” he said.

“An entire career shouldn’t be judged based on a month or two, or because of a disagreement or misunderstanding with one or two individuals.”

He added that great players deserved to leave through the front door, saying a fitting farewell would recognise their contributions and inspire young footballers who aspire to careers like those of Romário, Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Paolo Maldini.

Ronaldo formally retired from the Portugal national team on November 5, 2026, after 23 years, 234 appearances and a world-record 146 international goals.

His departure followed a dispute with coach Jorge Jesus in late September, when he reportedly left the national team camp without permission ahead of a Nations League match. He was subsequently disciplined by the federation.

Portugal organised tributes during the November international window, including having the squad wear Ronaldo’s No. 7 shirt, but the player was not present.

Guardiola’s comments, coming days after the tributes, have renewed calls for a more personal farewell involving the football star.

The post Guardiola urges Portugal to give Ronaldo dignified farewell appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Igwe Asadu mourns Pete Edochie, describes him as icon of African cinema
description:
From Felix Ikem, Nsukka
The Chairman of the Enugu State Traditional Rulers Council, HRM Igwe Samuel Ikechukwu Asadu (Igwe Ogadagidi), has mourned the death of veteran Nollywood actor, Chief Pete Edochie, describing him as an icon of African cinema and a custodian of African cultural heritage.
Igwe A
content:
From Felix Ikem, Nsukka

The Chairman of the Enugu State Traditional Rulers Council, HRM Igwe Samuel Ikechukwu Asadu (Igwe Ogadagidi), has mourned the death of veteran Nollywood actor, Chief Pete Edochie, describing him as an icon of African cinema and a custodian of African cultural heritage.

Igwe Asadu, in a condolence message in Enugu on Wednesday,
said the veteran broadcaster and actor’s death was a great loss to the Nigerian entertainment industry and the African continent, given his immense contributions to promoting African culture and tradition through his outstanding acting career.

He noted that the late actor was widely admired for his commanding screen presence, deep and authoritative voice, remarkable acting ability and mastery of traditional African roles.

According to the monarch, Edochie distinguished himself as one of the most celebrated actors in Africa, using his talent to showcase the richness of African values, customs, and heritage to audiences worldwide.

“Pete Edochie traversed the broadcasting and movie industries with remarkable distinction, integrity and an enviable sense of professionalism, leaving an indelible mark on both sectors.

“Throughout his illustrious career, he maintained an impeccable reputation, earning the admiration and respect of his colleagues, audiences and industry stakeholders alike, while promoting and preserving our great Igbo culture and heritage.

“Through his exceptional talent, discipline, dedication and mastery of his craft, Edochie rose from being a celebrated actor to an enduring symbol of excellence and a legend of African cinema. His remarkable contributions to the entertainment industry have not only enriched Nigerian filmmaking but have also elevated the status of African storytelling on the global stage,” Igwe Asadu said.

The Monarch, who is the immediate past Chairman, Southeast Traditional Rulers Council, and the Traditional Ruler of Edem-Ani Ogwugwu Ancient Kingdom in Nsukka Local Area, prayed for the repose of the actor’s soul and urged his family to sustain his legacy by preserving the values and principles that defined his life and career.

He also called on upcoming actors and actresses to emulate Edochie’s enduring legacies of professionalism, dedication, discipline and commitment to excellence, describing him as a worthy role model for generations of entertainers.

The monarch said the late actor’s contributions to Nollywood would remain indelible, adding that his name would continue to occupy a special place in the history of African cinema.

Here is a strengthened and professionally polished version, retaining the solemnity and traditional tone of the tribute:

“On behalf of the Enugu State Traditional Rulers Council, I extend my deepest and heartfelt condolences to the Edochie family, the government and people of Anambra State, the Nigerian nation, the African entertainment industry, as well as his friends, admirers and fans across the world over the painful loss of this extraordinary icon.

“Chief Pete Edochie may have departed this earthly realm, but his timeless works of art, profound teachings, remarkable contributions and enduring legacy will live on forever. His life and accomplishments will continue to inspire generations of actors, filmmakers and lovers of African culture, while his place in the history of Nigerian and African cinema remains indelible.

“His passing is a monumental loss to the entertainment industry and to all who cherished his immense talent, wisdom and cultural influence. However, we take solace in the fact that he lived a fulfilled life of service to humanity and made an enduring contribution to the preservation and promotion of our cultural heritage.

“Adieu, Ononenyi! Adieu, Ebubedike! Adieu, Chief Pete Edochie, MON, the Lion of Africa. Your footprints are indelible, and your legacy shall forever remain a source of pride and inspiration,” Igwe Asadu mourned.

The legendary actor was said to have passed away at about 12:30 a.m. on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, in Enugu, at the age of 79, following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer.

His death was announced in a statement titled ‘An Iroko Has Fallen’, signed by his son, Leo Pete Edochie, on behalf of the family.

title: Kwankwasiyya Supporters Carry Sticks But Harm Nobody, Obi Clarifies ‘Rig And Die’ Slogan
description: Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has clarified controversies surrounding the popular ‘rig and die’ slogan ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that it is a warning against electoral malpractice and not a threat to anyone.He spoke in an
content:
Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has clarified controversies surrounding the popular ‘rig and die’ slogan ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that it is a warning against electoral malpractice and not a threat to anyone.

He spoke in an interview with Channels Television on Tuesday evening in Jalingo, Taraba State, after an Obi-Kwankwaso town hall meeting.

Addressing concerns over the presence of weapons at political gatherings, Obi said the public had misunderstood the ‘rig and die’ calls against electoral malpractice as opposition to political campaigns.

This is as he defended supporters of his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, over allegations that they carry sticks to political campaigns, saying the items have not been used to “harm anyone”.

Obi insisted that he had not witnessed anyone being attacked with the stick-wielding Kwankwasiyya movement during political gatherings.

“They said we said ‘rig and die.’ We didn’t say ‘campaign and die.’ What we, people said is that they don’t want rigging this time. They didn’t say they don’t want campaign this time. If anything, they want campaign this time,” he said.

Obi explained that the Kwankwasiyya movement, led by Kwankwaso, had a longstanding tradition of supporters appearing at political gatherings with sticks and similar items.

He said, “Everybody who had followed the Kwankwansiyah group in Kano know that they come out with such sticks and everything, but they’ve never used it to harm anybody.

“I’ve been part of that family for a while, and I’ve never seen one day, maybe behind me, that anybody was harmed because they were carrying such items.”

The former Anambra State governor appealed to security agencies and other authorities to prevent violence during political activities, warning against the loss of lives over political ambitions.

“So we’re pleading with the authorities. Please, we cannot kill people, harm people, because we want to be political leaders,” he added.

His comments came amid growing concerns over attacks on opposition political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections.

On Monday, gunmen attacked a campaign gathering of the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central, Ovie Omo-Agege, in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, leaving several people dead and others injured.

Omo-Agege, a former Deputy President of the Senate, escaped the attack, while members of his campaign team and other supporters were among the casualties.
