title: ‘They only carry sticks but attack no one at rallies’- Obi defends Kwankwasiyya supporters
description:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has defended members of the Kwankwasiyya movement who attend political rallies with sticks, saying they have not used the items to attack anyone.
Obi maintained that carrying sticks at political gatherings was not a new
content:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has defended members of the Kwankwasiyya movement who attend political rallies with sticks, saying they have not used the items to attack anyone.

Obi maintained that carrying sticks at political gatherings was not a new practice among supporters of his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso. He also said he had never witnessed any incident in which members of the group used the sticks to harm anyone.

The former Anambra State governor made the remarks during an interview with Channels Television on Tuesday evening in Jalingo, Taraba State.

The interview followed an Obi-Kwankwaso town hall meeting held at The Crest Hall, where the NDC presidential candidate addressed questions about the political activities and conduct of the movement’s supporters.

Defending the supporters against concerns over the items they carry to political gatherings, Obi said their actions had been misunderstood, arguing that opposition to electoral rigging should not be confused with opposition to campaigning.

“They said we said ‘rig and die.’ We didn’t say ‘campaign and die.’ What we, people said is that they don’t want rigging this time. They didn’t say they don’t want campaign this time. If anything, they want campaign this time,” he said.

Obi said the Kwankwasiyya movement had a longstanding tradition of supporters carrying sticks during political outings but claimed the items had not been used to hurt others.

“Everybody who had followed the Kwankwansiyah group in Kano know that they come out with such sticks and everything, but they’ve never used it to harm anybody,” he said.

He added that despite his association with the group, he had not witnessed any incident in which anyone was attacked for carrying such items.

“I’ve been part of that family for a while, and I’ve never seen one day, maybe behind me, that anybody was harmed because they were carrying such items,” Obi said.

The NDC candidate appealed to security agencies to prevent violence at political gatherings, warning against people being injured or killed in the pursuit of political power.

“So we’re pleading with the authorities. Please, we cannot kill people, harm people, because we want to be political leaders,” he added.

His remarks come amid heightened concerns over political violence ahead of the 2027 elections, following attacks on political gatherings in Kano and Delta states, including the assault on the campaign entourage of NDC senatorial candidate Ovie Omo-Agege in Ughelli North, Delta State.

title: Man jailed for stealing microwave oven from home forfeited to FG
description:
Justice Alexander Owoeye of the Federal High Court, Ikoyi, Lagos, on Tuesday convicted and sentenced one Okpan Hassan to 11 months imprisonment for stealing a forfeited property.
Hassan was arraigned by the Lagos Zonal Directorate 1 of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) on a one-cou
content:
Justice Alexander Owoeye of the Federal High Court, Ikoyi, Lagos, on Tuesday convicted and sentenced one Okpan Hassan to 11 months imprisonment for stealing a forfeited property.

Hassan was arraigned by the Lagos Zonal Directorate 1 of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) on a one-count charge bordering on dealing with forfeited property.

The charge reads, “That you, Okpan Hassan, sometime in January, 2026, at Lagos, within the jurisdiction of this Honourable court, and without authorisation from the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, dealt with forfeited property, to wit: a microwave oven, which forms part of the appurtenances at Unit B3, Romax Atlantic View, forfeited to the Federal Government of Nigeria, and you thereby committed an offence contrary to and punishable under Section 32(1) of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (Establishment) Act, 2004.”

The defendant pleaded guilty when the charge was read to him.

Following his plea, prosecution counsel, E.S. Okongwu, reviewed the facts of the case and urged the court to convict and sentence him accordingly.

Justice Owoeye subsequently found Hassan guilty and sentenced him to 11 months imprisonment, without an option of fine.

The court also ordered the forfeiture of the microwave oven to the Correctional Facility, Ikoyi.

title: Buni presents N532bn 2027 budget to Yobe assembly
description:
Yobe State Governor, Mai Mala Buni, has presented a proposed budget of N532.27bn for the 2027 fiscal year, with recurrent expenditure taking the largest share of the estimates.
Buni presented the 2027 Appropriation and Finance Bills before the Yobe State House of Assembly in Damaturu on Tuesday, des
content:
Yobe State Governor, Mai Mala Buni, has presented a proposed budget of N532.27bn for the 2027 fiscal year, with recurrent expenditure taking the largest share of the estimates.

Buni presented the 2027 Appropriation and Finance Bills before the Yobe State House of Assembly in Damaturu on Tuesday, describing the proposal as the final budget of his administration.

Tagged the Budget of Consolidation, Sustainability and Inclusive Growth, the proposed budget represents an increase of N16.739bn, or 3.2 per cent, over the N515.532bn approved for the 2026 fiscal year.

A breakdown of the estimates shows that N288.426bn, representing 54.2 per cent, is allocated to recurrent expenditure, while N243.845bn, representing 45.8 per cent, is earmarked for capital projects.

Presenting the budget, Buni said it was designed to consolidate the achievements of his administration, complete ongoing projects and ensure the sustainability of existing investments.

He said, “Today, with a sense of humility and fulfilment, and in accordance with Section 121(1) of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (as amended), I once again stand before this Honourable House of Assembly to present the Eighth and last Finance and Appropriation Bills by this administration for your kind consideration and approval for the 2027 fiscal year.”

The governor said the administration would prioritise project completion, improved service delivery and prudent management of public resources.

“The 2027 budget is therefore designed to balance immediate service delivery with the long-term development interest of the state,” he said.

Buni disclosed that the education sector would receive N99.792bn, while N80.543bn was allocated to healthcare.

He said the education allocation would support the completion of ongoing school construction and rehabilitation projects, the provision of teaching materials, assistance to tertiary institutions and scholarship programmes.

On healthcare, the governor said the government would sustain investments in hospital upgrades, maternity and emergency services, medical equipment and healthcare training institutions.

He also identified the establishment of a modern kidney centre in Gashua as one of the administration’s priority projects.

“We are equally committed to advancing the ongoing establishment of a modern Kidney Centre in Gashua, with emphasis on a safe, accessible, patient-centred treatment environment, appropriate dialysis equipment and the clinical and operational arrangements required for sustainable service delivery,” Buni said.

The governor said infrastructure development would remain a major priority, with emphasis on completing ongoing road, drainage, electricity and commercial infrastructure projects.

He specifically mentioned the Gashua-Masaba, Balanguwa-Kumagannam and Dumbulwa-Lailai roads among the projects requiring attention.

Other priority areas include agricultural development, livestock production, water supply, environmental protection, peacebuilding and the rehabilitation of communities affected by insurgency.

Reviewing the performance of the 2026 budget as of September 30, Buni said the state recorded revenue receipts of N347.078bn, representing 67.3 per cent of the annual projection.

He said the approved 2026 budget stood at N515.532bn, comprising N291.904bn for capital expenditure and N223.628bn for recurrent expenditure.

According to him, recurrent expenditure during the first nine months amounted to N139.346bn, while capital expenditure stood at N94.280bn.

The governor said the administration remained committed to the payment of salaries, pensions and gratuities despite prevailing economic challenges and the demands of post-insurgency recovery.

Buni, who described the 2027 proposal as the final budget of his administration, said the government would ensure an orderly transition and preserve ongoing development projects.

“Development must not depend entirely on the presence of any individual in public office. It must be supported by strong institutions, competent public servants, credible planning frameworks and effective systems of accountability,” he said.

The governor assured residents that his administration would continue to discharge its responsibilities until the final day of its tenure.

“We shall continue to work, supervise, deliver and remain accountable until the final day of our mandate. There will be no abandonment of our responsibilities and projects,” he said.

He urged the House of Assembly to give the proposed budget timely consideration and passage.

In a political appeal towards the end of his address, Buni urged the people of Yobe to support President Bola Tinubu’s second-term ambition, arguing that the state’s membership of the ruling All Progressives Congress had created opportunities for it to benefit from the Federal Government.

He also commended Tinubu for approving the Federal Government’s takeover and reimbursement of the Muhammadu Buhari International Cargo Airport project in Damaturu, saying the intervention would free up resources for other development projects.

The post Buni presents N532bn 2027 budget to Yobe assembly appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Enugu gov mourns Pete Edochie, says Nigeria loses a titan
description:
The Governor of Enugu State, Peter Mbah, has expressed grief over the passing of veteran Nollywood actor, Pete Edochie, describing his death as the departure of a giant, an icon, and a patriot.
In a personal tribute issued in the early hours of Wednesday, after his son, Leo Edochie, announced the ac
content:
The Governor of Enugu State, Peter Mbah, has expressed grief over the passing of veteran Nollywood actor, Pete Edochie, describing his death as the departure of a giant, an icon, and a patriot.

In a personal tribute issued in the early hours of Wednesday, after his son, Leo Edochie, announced the actor’s death, the governor described the loss as personal to Enugu State.

Mbah noted that although the renowned thespian hailed from Nteje in Anambra State, he maintained lifelong ties with Enugu, which he frequently referred to as his birthplace, his “first port of call,” and a home away from home.

“I am deeply saddened by the passing of Chief Pete Edochie, one of Nigeria’s most iconic actors and titans, and one of the most recognisable faces of Nollywood and Africa’s creative industry across the world,” the governor said.

He added that the pain of the actor’s passing was deepened by its timing, coming while Enugu is hosting the National Festival of Arts and Culture.

“At a time when we are celebrating the richness of our cultural heritage and the creative talents that give it expression, we are confronted with the loss of one of its most distinguished ambassadors. It is a sobering reminder that while we celebrate the enduring power of our arts and culture, we must also mourn those who gave them life and brought them global recognition,” Mbah stated.

Describing Edochie as “more than an accomplished actor” and “an institution,” the governor praised his commanding screen presence, unmistakable voice, and mastery of dialogue, which helped shape Nigerian cinema globally.

Recalling the late actor’s breakthrough role in the screen adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s 1958 novel, ‘Things Fall Apart’, Mbah noted that Edochie wore his Igbo identity with pride, bringing its language, wisdom, and proverbs to life for international audiences.

“His performances transcended entertainment, preserving aspects of our cultural heritage and inspiring generations of actors and storytellers. His was a career defined not merely by longevity but by excellence, distinction, enduring influence, and uncommon social grace,” he added.

Mbah extended condolences on behalf of the government and people of Enugu State to the bereaved family, the Nollywood community, the Anambra State Government, and fans worldwide.

“Adieu, Chief Pete Edochie, MON. Adieu Ononenyi, Ebubedike, Gaga n’ ogwu, Ogadagidi, Nwoke ka Ibe Ya, Okara Mmadu Okara Mmuo, a legend, fine gentleman, veteran broadcaster and actor. Your voice may have gone silent, but your legacy will speak for generations,” the governor mourned.

The post Enugu gov mourns Pete Edochie, says Nigeria loses a titan appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: What I want to be remembered for – Pete Edochie
description:
By Benjamin Njoku







When Pete Edochie turned 76 in 2023, he revealed what he would want to be remembered for when he’s no more.







In a chat with Vanguard to mark his 76th birthday, Ebubedike, as he was fondly called by his friends and colleagues in the movie industry, said he would like to
content:
By Benjamin Njoku

When Pete Edochie turned 76 in 2023, he revealed what he would want to be remembered for when he’s no more.

In a chat with Vanguard to mark his 76th birthday, Ebubedike, as he was fondly called by his friends and colleagues in the movie industry, said he would like to be remembered as that man who brought happiness and joy to many homes in Africa and beyond with his craft.

Edochie became famous after the iconic role he played as Okonkwo in the NTA adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s best-selling novel, “Things Fall Apart”, in the 80s.

He is widely regarded as one of the most influential actors in the African film industry, having spent more than 50 years of his life bringing happiness to many homes in Africa and beyond.

The post What I want to be remembered for – Pete Edochie appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Ronaldo deserves fitting farewell from Portugal, says Guardiola
description:
Pep Guardiola has called on the Portuguese Football Federation to give Cristiano Ronaldo a fitting farewell from the national team, saying the forward deserves to end his international career with the recognition of his country.



The former Manchester City manager made the appeal during an intervi
content:
Pep Guardiola has called on the Portuguese Football Federation to give Cristiano Ronaldo a fitting farewell from the national team, saying the forward deserves to end his international career with the recognition of his country.

The former Manchester City manager made the appeal during an interview with former Brazilian footballer Romário on Tuesday, following Ronaldo’s announcement of his retirement from international football earlier this month.

“Cristiano Ronaldo shouldn’t leave the Portuguese national team in this manner. They can’t let him go like this,” Guardiola said.

“Both sides need to make an effort to guarantee a fitting farewell. He’s been an incredibly important figure, not only for himself and Portugal, but for future generations of Portuguese players.”

He added that Ronaldo’s achievements deserved to be celebrated rather than overshadowed by a disagreement with members of the national team.

“An entire career shouldn’t be judged based on a month or two, or because of a disagreement or misunderstanding with one or two individuals,” he said.

“There are exceptional players, and Cristiano Ronaldo is one of them; therefore, this situation must be rectified.”

Guardiola also called for a celebration in which Ronaldo would feel appreciated by Portuguese supporters, urging both parties to put their differences behind them.

“There should be a celebration where he feels the love of his countrymen, and he, in turn, must also take the initiative and say: Let’s turn the page on the past,” he added.

The disagreement between Ronaldo and Jesus came to public attention on September 30, when the forward left Portugal’s training camp in Copenhagen ahead of their Nations League fixture against Denmark.

Ronaldo had been an unused substitute in Portugal’s 2-1 victory over Norway on September 27, despite warming up for about 30 minutes during the match.

Jesus later admitted that Ronaldo was unhappy with his decision not to introduce him, while the forward subsequently accused the coach of breaking his word over an agreement concerning his playing time and the explanation of his omission.

Ronaldo also apologised for his conduct following the incident but said he remained available for Portugal after serving any punishment imposed by the football authorities.

However, on November 5, the five-time Ballon d’Or winner announced his retirement from international football, bringing an end to a 23-year career with the national team.

In his announcement, Ronaldo said it was time to hand back Portugal’s iconic No. 7 shirt, adding that the decision was not easy because it involved both his head and his heart.

He finished his international career with 234 appearances and 146 goals, making him the most-capped player and highest goalscorer in men’s international football.

Following his retirement, the Portuguese Football Federation redesigned the national team’s No. 7 shirt in tribute to the forward.

The post Ronaldo deserves fitting farewell from Portugal, says Guardiola appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Shettima unveils 10,330 NEDC electric vehicles, tricycles in Maiduguri
description:
From Timothy Olanrewaju, Maiduguri
Vice President Kashim Shettima has unveiled 10,330 electric vehicles procured by the North East Development Commission (NEDC) for the six states of the North-East, describing the intervention as an economic necessity.
The vehicles comprise 10,000 electric tricycles
content:
From Timothy Olanrewaju, Maiduguri

Vice President Kashim Shettima has unveiled 10,330 electric vehicles procured by the North East Development Commission (NEDC) for the six states of the North-East, describing the intervention as an economic necessity.

The vehicles comprise 10,000 electric tricycles, 300 electric taxis and 30 electric buses, unveiled under the NEDC’s e-mobility programme for the northeast.

Shettima, while unveiling the vehicles in Maiduguri on Tuesday, said the intervention would ease transportation challenges and reduce environmental pollution in the region.

“E-mobility is not only an environmental conversation but also an economic imperative. I commend the management and staff of NEDC for the intervention,” he said.

He said it was absolutely essential for the region to embrace alternative energy, noting that the North-East is endowed with abundant solar energy.

He said he was once accused of micro-managing the NEDC, adding: “I felt guilty, but I owe no one an apology.”

Shettima said the North-East is in the news for the wrong reasons of poverty, disease outbreaks and Boko Haram, and urged the people of the region to unite for good.

The Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of NEDC, Alhaji Mohammed Goni Alkali, commended the Federal Government for establishing the commission for the development of the region.

He said the 10,000 electric tricycles and 300 electric vehicles, were initiated by the commission to provide alternative power for users and increase access to transportation.

Alkali said the commission had also provided a 50 Megawatts solar power mini-grid project, distributed over 100,000 street lights and 1,100 solar-powered boreholes, and awarded scholarships worth N25 billion to indigent students in tertiary institutions in the region.

He lauded the governments of the Northeast states for their support.

Borno State Governor, Babagana Zulum, and his Gombe State counterpart, Alhaji Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, commended the NEDC for its interventions in the region.

The Minister of Regional Development, Engr. Abubakar Momoh, said the electric vehicles aligned with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda and would provide affordable transportation for women, youths, traders and farmers.

The Vice President also commissioned a road and bridge project executed by the NEDC, linking Maiduguri metropolis to one of its satellite communities.

title: CBN holds interest rate at 23%
description:

The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has retained its Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 23 per cent, maintaining its tight monetary policy stance amid the continued moderation in inflation.
However, the apex bank warned that the ongoing conf
content:
…warns Middle East conflict, election spending may fuel inflation

The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has retained its Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 23 per cent, maintaining its tight monetary policy stance amid the continued moderation in inflation.

However, the apex bank warned that the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and increased spending ahead of the festive season and elections could fuel inflationary pressures.

CBN Governor, Mr Olayemi Cardoso,
disclosed the decisions of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) at a briefing in Abuja on Tuesday.
He said the committee also retained the asymmetric corridor around the MPR at +50 and -300 basis points, while keeping the Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR) for deposit money banks at 45 per cent, merchant banks at 16 per cent and non-Treasury Single Account (TSA) public sector deposits at 75 per cent.

According to the CBN governor, the decision was informed by the need to consolidate the gains recorded in the disinflation process, despite lingering upside risks to the inflation outlook.

Cardoso disclosed that headline inflation declined to 14.06 per cent in October 2026 from 14.63 per cent in September, marking the fifth consecutive month of moderation.

He said core inflation also eased to 10.78 per cent from 12.95 per cent, while food inflation declined to 19.13 per cent from 19.59 per cent during the period.

The CBN governor attributed the moderation to sustained exchange rate stability, improved monetary policy transmission and increased food supply following the commencement of the harvest season.

He identified the ongoing Middle East conflict as a major risk to the inflation outlook, warning that disruptions could sustain pressure on global energy prices.

He added that increased spending associated with the end-of-year festive season and election-related activities could raise aggregate demand and exert further pressure on prices.

Cardoso said maintaining the current monetary policy stance would help anchor inflation expectations and sustain the disinflation process.

On the external sector, he disclosed that Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $54.02 billion as of November 17, 2026, sufficient to cover 10.26 months of imports of goods and services.

He also welcomed the Memorandum of Understanding between the CBN and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC), aimed at enhancing foreign exchange inflows, supporting energy project financing and improving macroeconomic stability.

According to him, effective implementation of the agreement would strengthen foreign exchange market liquidity, support external reserves and enhance investor confidence.

Cardoso further disclosed that the Composite Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) increased to 53.2 index points in October from 53 points in September, indicating sustained expansion in economic activities.

He attributed the improvement to increased activities in the industrial, agricultural and services sectors.

On the economic outlook, the CBN governor expressed optimism about growth prospects for the remainder of 2026 and into 2027, supported by improved crude oil production and sustained expansion in agriculture, industry and services.

He said: “Members noted the moderation in headline inflation for five consecutive months, reflecting the impact of sustained exchange rate stability and improved monetary policy transmission.”

“Given the prevailing headwinds which have slowed the pace of moderation in price pressures, members were of the view that maintaining the current policy stance would further anchor inflation expectations and support the disinflation process.”

“Members were mindful of lingering upside risks, particularly those arising from the ongoing Middle East conflict, which could sustain pressure on energy prices.”

“In addition, the MPC observed that the anticipated increase in spending from the end-of-year festive season and election-related activities could impact aggregate demand with likely upward pressure on prices.”

“Nevertheless, the committee judged that maintaining the current policy stance is appropriate to safeguard the gains of disinflation so far achieved, while remaining data-dependent and vigilant in taking further appropriate measures.”

“The outlook for the domestic economy remains positive for the rest of 2026 and into 2027, supported by improved crude oil production and sustained expansion in agriculture, services and industrial activity.”

The post CBN holds interest rate at 23% appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: ‘Kogi LG funds used to repay N2.1bn loan for Yahaya Bello’s children’s school fees’ – EFCC witness tells court
description:
An investigator with the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has told a court how Keyless Nature, a company, allegedly obtained a N2.1 billion loan which was later repaid with funds transferred from several accounts belonging to local government areas in Kogi State.
The investigator, Joh
content:
An investigator with the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has told a court how Keyless Nature, a company, allegedly obtained a N2.1 billion loan which was later repaid with funds transferred from several accounts belonging to local government areas in Kogi State.

The investigator, John Justice, who is the 20th prosecution witness in the ongoing trial of former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, and two other defendants, gave the testimony on Tuesday before the Federal Capital Territory High Court.

Details of his testimony were contained in a statement issued by the EFCC spokesperson, Dele Oyewale.

At an earlier court appearance in October, Justice had alleged that three companies used what he described as “in-and-out” transactions to move funds received from Kogi local governments without physically withdrawing the money.

His latest testimony centred on the alleged N2.1 billion loan obtained by Keyless Nature and how payments were subsequently made through inflows from multiple local government accounts.

He identified the companies as Hazyman Investment Limited, Bimas Ventures Limited and Fazad.

Bello is standing trial alongside Umar Shuaibu Oricha and Abdulsalami Hudu on 16 counts of criminal breach of trust over alleged diversion of N110.4 billion. The defendants have pleaded not guilty.

The EFCC alleged that the funds transferred to the companies were part of the N110.4 billion Bello allegedly diverted from the state treasury during his tenure as governor between January 2016 and January 2024.

The anti-graft agency also alleged that some of the funds were used to acquire properties in highbrow areas of Abuja and pay upfront school fees for Bello’s children.

THE TESTIMONY

Led in evidence by Kemi Pinheiro, prosecution counsel, the EFCC investigator told the court that the loan was obtained through Keyless Nature Limited, whose account is being operated by one Abba Adaudu.

Justice said the funds were subsequently disbursed through proxies, including bureau de change operators and one Jamilu Abdullahi’s personal account.

The witness said funds were paid from several local government areas in Kogi state into Keyless Nature’s account between 2021 and 2024.

According to him, the Kogi LGAs that made money transfers into the accounts are Ajaokuta, Ankpa, Ibaji, Omala, Ogori-Magongo, Ofu, Olamaboro, Okehi, Kogi, Kabba-Bunu, Ijumu and Igalamela-Odolu, among others.

“These inflows come monthly on a regular basis into the Keyless Nature account. When aggregated, the narration would be principal liquidation,” the EFCC witness said.

Asked what was the purpose of the loan, the witness said the facility was secured to make the transaction appear like a genuine business arrangement, while the LGAs bore the responsibility of repaying it.

The witness said the agency did not receive any response from the affected Kogi LGAs when it wrote to them to establish the basis for the payments.

He added that Adaudu could not provide documents showing the contracts allegedly executed by the companies benefitting from the funds.

The witness said the investigation could not establish any contracts awarded to Keyless Nature, Hayzma and Forza Oil and Gas by the local governments.

He said Hayzma claimed to be providing pharmaceutical services to the local governments but failed to provide the names and sources of its pharmaceutical suppliers.

The witness added that Hayzma could not provide evidence of its licensing by the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) or other relevant documentation.

The witness said the investigation established that Siyaka Adebenege, who was associated with the business, was an accountant and not a pharmacist.

According to him, part of the loan proceeds went to bureau de change operators, including Abdullahi, while some were transferred to other accounts.

The EFCC investigators said Kunfayakun Global Limited, E-traders International Limited and Abdullahi’s personal account were beneficiaries of the cash withdrawals.

He added that the investigation revealed that some of the withdrawals were subsequently treated as cash and redeposited into the accounts of the companies to conceal the identities of the ultimate recipients.

Earlier in his testimony, Justice had told the court how the investigation traced cash withdrawals and subsequent dollar transactions involving the companies and individuals allegedly used to facilitate payments to the American International School of Abuja for school fees.

HOW THE FUNDS MOVED

Speaking further, the EFCC witness told the court that searches conducted on the accounts and analysis of statements revealed that Abdullahi, a BDC operator, had interests in some of the companies.

Justice said the beneficiaries of Kunfayakun, E-traders and Jamilu Abdullahi claimed that the money was received for the purchase of US dollars, which were subsequently handed over to Abdullahi.

The witness said when Abdullahi was invited, he said he did not know Hayzma, Bibas and Forza Oil and Gas but knew one Adaudu.

The witness said Abdullahi told EFCC investigators that Adaudu provided instructions for payments to be made locally and internationally in dollars.

The EFCC investigator said Abdullahi brought in three companies, Whales, Forza Oil and Gas and Alyeshua, to facilitate the transactions, while Adaudu provided details of those who would receive the funds.

Justice said part of the payments went to the American International School of Abuja, while others were transferred to the school’s account domiciled with TD Bank outside Nigeria.

He said the payments were made for the school fees of four children of the first defendant, Yahaya Bello, and Zayyan Ali Bello, the son of his nephew, Ali Bello.

Making reference to exhibit AX7, a TD Bank statement of account, the EFCC witness highlighted several dollar transactions which he said corresponded with payments made to the American International School.

He pointed to entries of $49,575 and $45,675 in the November 2021 account records.

He also identified transactions of $78,125 and $42,145 recorded on January 25 and 26, 2021, respectively.

The witness mentioned four deposits recorded on September 7, 2021, and identified $74,920.71 in connection with the school’s acknowledgement of school fee payments.

He also identified payments of $44,675 and $10,975 made on November 12 and 15, 2021 and another deposit of $90,000 on February 15, 2022, into the school’s TD Bank account.

Speaking about an email correspondences between the school and Ali Bello, the witness said the correspondence formed part of the evidence obtained during the investigation.

He told the court that Abdullahi showed the companies he procured to facilitate the transactions, while the head of the school voluntarily provided a statement to the commission.

The witness identified an email from the school to Ali Bello confirming receipt of $44,675 for Na’ima Bello on November 12, 2022.

He also referred to an entry in Exhibit AX7 dated November 5, 2022, showing a transfer of $44,675 from Forza Oil and Gas.

The witness also identified another email from the school to Ali Bello confirming receipt of $78,131.

Hearing in the case was subsequently adjourned to December 2 and 14, 2026, January 26, and February 2 and 3, 2027.

The post ‘Kogi LG funds used to repay N2.1bn loan for Yahaya Bello’s children’s school fees’ – EFCC witness tells court appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: ‘Thanks for your kind encouragement’, Funke Akindele mourns Pete Edochie
description:
Nollywood actress and filmmaker, Funke Akindele, has paid tribute to veteran actor Pete Edochie, recalling his words of encouragement when they worked together on the film Egg of Life.
Akindele described the late actor as an inspiration to generations of Nollywood practitioners, saying his contribut
content:
Nollywood actress and filmmaker, Funke Akindele, has paid tribute to veteran actor Pete Edochie, recalling his words of encouragement when they worked together on the film Egg of Life.

Akindele described the late actor as an inspiration to generations of Nollywood practitioners, saying his contributions to the Nigerian film industry would continue to be remembered.

The actress made this known in a tribute posted on her X handle on Wednesday, following the announcement of Edochie’s death at the age of 79.

Recounting her experience of watching the veteran actor on television while growing up, Akindele said she later had the opportunity to work alongside him in the film industry.

She wrote, “Daddy Pete Edochie, I remember watching you in Things Fall Apart growing up. Many years later, I had the honour of working with you on Egg of Life. Your words of encouragement that day have stayed with me.

“Thank you for paving the way for so many of us in Nollywood and for being an inspiration to us over the years. Your work lives on.

“May God comfort the Edochie family and all of us in Nollywood. May your gentle soul rest in perfect peace, Daddy.”

Edochie died at 12:30am in Enugu after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer, according to a statement issued by his family and signed by his son, Leo Pete Edochie.

Born on March 7, 1947, the late actor began his career in broadcasting in 1967 with the Eastern Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation before rising to senior positions at the Anambra Broadcasting Service.

He became widely known for playing Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart. His commanding voice and portrayal of traditional rulers, fathers and community leaders subsequently made him one of Nollywood’s most recognisable actors.

He featured in several productions, including Igodo, Rituals and Lionheart, and received the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in recognition of his contributions to the entertainment industry.

His death has drawn tributes from colleagues and admirers, with many reflecting on his influence on the growth of Nollywood and the generations of actors who followed him.

The post ‘Thanks for your kind encouragement’, Funke Akindele mourns Pete Edochie appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Sarafa Isola: Happy 66th birthday to a brother and benefactor
description:
Dear Ambassador Sarafa Tunji Isola,
On the joyous occasion of your 66th birthday, I join your family, friends, associates and well-wishers to celebrate a remarkable personality whose life has been defined by service, generosity, humility and an unwavering commitment to the welfare of others.
Today,
content:
Dear Ambassador Sarafa Tunji Isola,

On the joyous occasion of your 66th birthday, I join your family, friends, associates and well-wishers to celebrate a remarkable personality whose life has been defined by service, generosity, humility and an unwavering commitment to the welfare of others.

Today, I celebrate not only an accomplished diplomat and distinguished public servant, but also a brother, a dependable friend and a benefactor whose kindness and support have touched many lives.

Your journey through public service and diplomacy has been a testament to your dedication to the advancement of our society. From your contributions to governance to your distinguished service as Nigeria’s Ambassador to the United Kingdom, you have consistently demonstrated that leadership is not merely about occupying positions of authority, but about making a meaningful and lasting impact.

Beyond your impressive public record, what endears you to many of us is your humane disposition, your accessibility and your willingness to stand by people in moments that matter. You have remained a source of encouragement, inspiration and support to many, irrespective of their status or background.

As a brother and benefactor, your generosity is deeply appreciated. Your commitment to the ideals of good governance, unity, peaceful coexistence and community development continues to inspire those who have the privilege of knowing you.

At 66, you have every reason to look back with gratitude on a life of accomplishments and forward with renewed hope for greater achievements. May this new chapter bring you abundant blessings, sound health, peace of mind and the fulfilment of your noble aspirations.

May Almighty Allah continue to guide your steps, strengthen you for greater responsibilities and reward you abundantly for your service to humanity. May He grant you many more years of life in good health, happiness and prosperity, surrounded by the love of family, friends and all those whose lives you have positively influenced.

Happy 66th birthday, dear brother and benefactor. May the years ahead be even more rewarding, impactful and fulfilling.

With warmest felicitations and best wishes.

Jimoh writes from Ogun State

title: Four Edo Security Operatives Arrested For Allegedly ‘Leaking Information’ To Cultists
description: The Edo State Police Command said it has arrested four members of the Edo State Security Corps for allegedly leaking information about police movements to suspected cultists, thereby frustrating an ongoing security operation in the state. The Police Public Relations Officer, speaking on behalf of th
content:
The Edo State Police Command said it has arrested four members of the Edo State Security Corps for allegedly leaking information about police movements to suspected cultists, thereby frustrating an ongoing security operation in the state.

The Police Public Relations Officer, speaking on behalf of the Commissioner of Police, CP Patrick Daaor, disclosed this during a press briefing in Benin City on Monday.

The Police said it also arrested 10 suspected cultists, four suspected kidnappers, one armed robbery suspect and one murder suspect in separate operations across the state.

The arrests, according to the Command, are part of intensified efforts to combat violent crimes and dismantle criminal networks in Edo State.

He said operatives arrested a suspected armed robber at Ugiokhuen Community, where a locally fabricated pistol, ammunition, and other exhibits were recovered.

In another operation, the police rescued two kidnapping victims, identified as Yakubu Ibrahim and Abdullahi Mohammed, unhurt, following a bush-combing operation at Ikakumoh/Ayaran Forest. Four suspected kidnappers were arrested in connection with the incident, which was reported on November 19.

In a separate anti-cultism operation at Osakpolor Street, off Adolor College Road, Benin City, 10 suspected members of the Aye Axe cult group were arrested during an alleged initiation exercise. A Mercedes-Benz GLK 350 was also recovered.

The police further confirmed the arrest of one John Bello, who allegedly murdered his father, Julius Bello, in Fugar before fleeing the scene. He was subsequently tracked down and apprehended by police operatives.

The Commissioner of Police, CP Patrick Daaor, reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to dismantling criminal networks and ensuring that perpetrators are brought to justice.

He commended the officers involved in the operations for their courage and professionalism, while appreciating members of the public for providing timely information and supporting the police.

The Command urged residents to remain vigilant and report suspicious activities, stressing that the security of the state remains a collective responsibility.

title: Men only want my body – Ivana seeks pastor’s prayers over failed relationships
description:
TikTok influencer, Ivana, has expressed frustration over what she described as a pattern of men showing interest in her only for physical intimacy rather than a committed relationship.
She also revealed that she recently sought prayers from a pastor over her repeated relationship disappointments.
Iv
content:
TikTok influencer, Ivana, has expressed frustration over what she described as a pattern of men showing interest in her only for physical intimacy rather than a committed relationship.

She also revealed that she recently sought prayers from a pastor over her repeated relationship disappointments.

Ivana made this known during a TikTok livestream, where she described her inability to sustain a lasting relationship as unusual, despite her efforts to make her previous relationships work.

According to her, the men often treat her well at the beginning of their relationships but later reveal their intentions, leaving her disappointed despite the sacrifices she makes to keep the relationships going.

“I went to meet a powerful pastor for prayer because I don’t know why relationship isn’t favouring me. I find it very strange when I can’t keep a man in my life at this age,” she said.

The influencer further claimed that the men she had dated were more interested in physical intimacy than committing to a future with her.

“It’s like everyone just wants only my body and not ready to stay. They all have this same pattern of being nice at first, then later they show their true colour,” she added.

Following her repeated disappointments, Ivana declared that she was no longer interested in pursuing romantic relationships but would rather focus on her music.

“I’m done with relationship! Let me go back to my music and vibes,” she said.

title: NGF disowns $100m Paris Club deal, says it never held disputed funds
description:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja
Nigeria Governors’ Forum (NGF) has distanced itself from the $100 million dispute arising from the Paris Club refunds, insisting that it neither participated in the transaction at the centre of the controversy nor held any of the disputed funds.
The Forum’s positio
content:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

Nigeria Governors’ Forum (NGF) has distanced itself from the $100 million dispute arising from the Paris Club refunds, insisting that it neither participated in the transaction at the centre of the controversy nor held any of the disputed funds.

The Forum’s position followed a November 19 interim order of the High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, restraining it and 29 commercial banks from dealing with funds up to $100 million, equivalent to about N135.5 billion, pending further proceedings in the case.

In a statement dated November 24 and signed by its Director of Media and Strategic Communications, Yunusa Tanko Abdullahi, the NGF said the dispute originated from alleged transactions between the claimant, Dr Ted Iseghohi-Edwards, and the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria (ALGON).

It maintained that it had no involvement in the transaction and did not engage any party to it.

“Please note that this issue emanated from allegations of transactions between the plaintiff and the Association of Local Government of Nigeria (ALGON). The Nigeria Governors Forum has no hand in that transaction and did not engage any party thereto, nor held any such monies in its custody at any time,” the statement said.

The Forum said its legal team was reviewing the court processes and would respond appropriately.

It, however, reaffirmed its commitment to the rule of law, transparency and accountability.

The NGF’s response comes against the backdrop of a suit filed by Iseghohi-Edwards, who is seeking to recover $100 million allegedly owed to him under an indemnity said to have been issued by the Forum on December 20, 2018.

The claimant, who operates under Edwards and Partners Law Firm, said ALGON retained him to represent the 774 local government councils regarding the London and Paris Club refunds.

He subsequently instituted suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/856/2016 against the Federal Government over outstanding legal and consultancy fees arising from the transactions.

According to his court filings, the Federal High Court, on February 16, 2018, established the Federal Government’s indebtedness of $318 million, following which the government made a part-payment of $159 million through promissory notes.

Iseghohi-Edwards argued that the judgment triggered the condition in the NGF’s alleged indemnity, under which the Forum reportedly undertook to pay him $100 million if the Federal Government was found liable for the outstanding professional fees.

He further alleged that the Forum failed to honour the undertaking despite a formal demand made in a letter dated October 8, 2026.

Consequently, he approached the FCT High Court, expressing fears that the disputed funds could be transferred or dissipated before the determination of his claim.

Justice O.C. Agbaza, in an interim Mareva injunction granted on November 19, restrained the Incorporated Trustees of the NGF from withdrawing, transferring, dissipating, concealing or otherwise dealing with funds up to $100 million or its naira equivalent.

The order also restrained 29 commercial banks from releasing, transferring, converting or otherwise dealing with funds standing to the credit of the NGF in their custody, up to the stipulated amount.

The banks were further directed to disclose within 48 hours of service of the order whether they held accounts belonging to the NGF containing the disputed funds, including the account details, currencies, available balances and amounts preserved.

The matter was adjourned until December 1, 2026, for the hearing of the claimant’s motion on notice for an interlocutory injunction.

The interim order does not constitute a final determination of the disputed funds’ ownership or establish the claimant’s entitlement to the $100 million.

The post NGF disowns $100m Paris Club deal, says it never held disputed funds appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Campaign violence: Kwankwasiyya supporters carry sticks but don’t harm anyone  -  Obi
description:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has defended supporters of the Kwankwasiyya movement who attend political rallies with sticks, insisting they have not used them to attack anyone.







Obi said the practice was not new among supporters of his running
content:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has defended supporters of the Kwankwasiyya movement who attend political rallies with sticks, insisting they have not used them to attack anyone.

Obi said the practice was not new among supporters of his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, and maintained that he had never witnessed anyone being harmed by members of the group carrying such items.

The former Anambra State governor spoke on Channels Television on Tuesday evening in Jalingo, Taraba State, after an Obi-Kwankwaso town hall meeting at The Crest Hall.

Defending the supporters against concerns over the items they carry to political gatherings, Obi said their actions had been misunderstood, arguing that opposition to electoral rigging should not be confused with opposition to campaigning.

“They said we said ‘rig and die.’ We didn’t say ‘campaign and die.’ What we, people said is that they don’t want rigging this time. They didn’t say they don’t want campaign this time. If anything, they want campaign this time,” he said.

Obi said the Kwankwasiyya movement had a longstanding tradition of supporters carrying sticks during political outings but claimed the items had not been used to hurt others.

“Everybody who had followed the Kwankwansiyah group in Kano know that they come out with such sticks and everything, but they’ve never used it to harm anybody,” he said.

He added that despite his association with the group, he had not witnessed any incident in which anyone was attacked for carrying such items.

“I’ve been part of that family for a while, and I’ve never seen one day, maybe behind me, that anybody was harmed because they were carrying such items,” Obi said.

The NDC candidate appealed to security agencies to prevent violence at political gatherings, warning against people being injured or killed in the pursuit of political power.

“So we’re pleading with the authorities. Please, we cannot kill people, harm people, because we want to be political leaders,” he added.

His remarks come amid heightened concerns over political violence ahead of the 2027 elections, following attacks on political gatherings in Kano and Delta states, including the assault on the campaign entourage of NDC senatorial candidate Ovie Omo-Agege in Ughelli North, Delta State.

title: THROWBACK VIDEO: Whenever it’s time for me to go, just take me — Pete Edochie
description:
A video of late Nollywood actor Pete Edochie speaking about his health and praying that God should take him when his time came, rather than allow him to become a burden to others, has resurfaced following his death at the age of 79 on Wednesday.
In the video, Edochie spoke about his difficulty walki
content:
A video of late Nollywood actor Pete Edochie speaking about his health and praying that God should take him when his time came, rather than allow him to become a burden to others, has resurfaced following his death at the age of 79 on Wednesday.

In the video, Edochie spoke about his difficulty walking and recurring swelling in parts of his body during a visit to ailing Ghanaian actor Emmanuel Armah at his home in Accra, Ghana, on September 30, 2026.

“Sitting down here, I am not very well myself. Walking is a problem for me now, but I still have hope that I will recover,” the late actor said.

“Sometimes, I get up, and parts of my body have swollen up. After some time, they go down again. My hand is swollen,” he added.

Reflecting on his health, Edochie said he had continued to pray to God, whom he described as the author of life, to determine when his time would come.

“I just keep asking God, you are the author of life. Whenever you feel it is time for me to go, just take me. Don’t let me bother the people who are around me,” he said.

He also offered words of encouragement to Armah, popularly known as Achuba, who has been battling health challenges for years.

“Emma, I believe that you will recover someday, by the grace of God,” Edochie said.

The footage was filmed and shared online by Ghana-based Nigerian comedian Parrot Mouth on September 30, during the actor’s visit to Armah in Accra. The clip has since resurfaced following news of Edochie’s death.

Edochie died at 12:30am on Wednesday, November 25, in Enugu, aged 79, after a protracted battle with prostate cancer, according to a family statement signed by his son, Leo Pete Edochie.

The family announced his death on Wednesday, describing him as a beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman.

Edochie was one of Nollywood’s most recognisable veteran actors, gaining prominence for his portrayal of Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s novel, Things Fall Apart.

title: Soun unveils N760m tech scholarship for 500 youths
description:
No fewer than 500 youths from Ogbomosoland are expected to benefit from a N760m technology scholarship initiative unveiled in honour of the Soun of Ogbomosoland, Oba Ghandi Olaoye.
The programme, known as the Oba Ghandi Indigent Fund for Technology and Skills, will provide tuition support to 100 stu
content:
No fewer than 500 youths from Ogbomosoland are expected to benefit from a N760m technology scholarship initiative unveiled in honour of the Soun of Ogbomosoland, Oba Ghandi Olaoye.

The programme, known as the Oba Ghandi Indigent Fund for Technology and Skills, will provide tuition support to 100 students annually for an initial period of five years.

Speaking during the virtual unveiling of the initiative on Tuesday, Oba Olaoye said the scholarship was designed to expand access to technology education, particularly for young people from financially disadvantaged backgrounds.

“The initiative was deliberately designed to give young people access to technology education, particularly those who might otherwise be unable to afford such opportunities,” the monarch said.

He explained that the programme would focus on computer-related disciplines, including Information Technology, Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, Forensic Technology, Data Science and Software Engineering.

The initiative is sponsored by the American College of Technology (ACTECH), an NBTE-accredited polytechnic, and its sister institution, American Open University Nigeria (A-Global), a private university licensed by the National Universities Commission.

The two institutions were founded by Prof David Akanbi, who is also the Chancellor of A-Global.

Oba Olaoye said equipping young people with relevant technological skills would prepare them for emerging opportunities in the global economy and enable them to contribute to decision-making at national and international levels.

He added that the scholarship was linked to his 25-year development plan for Ogbomosoland and urged individuals and organisations to support similar initiatives to widen educational opportunities for indigenes.

Under the programme, 70 scholarships will be awarded annually through ACTECH, while the remaining 30 will be offered through A-Global.

At ACTECH, 10 full scholarships covering 100 per cent of tuition fees will be awarded to candidates admitted into its National Diploma programmes in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence and Forensic Technology.

The full scholarships will be awarded strictly on merit, based on candidates’ Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board scores.

Another 60 students from Ogbomoso will receive 50 per cent tuition scholarships for the same programmes.

At A-Global, 20 undergraduate students will receive 75 per cent tuition support across its programmes, while 10 master’s degree students will benefit from 60 per cent tuition support.

The postgraduate component is expected to provide opportunities for graduates and working professionals seeking to acquire additional skills or transition into technology-related careers.

The sponsors said scholarship funds would be credited directly to beneficiaries’ accounts and sustained throughout their studies, provided they maintained satisfactory academic performance.

They, however, emphasised that the initiative would not compromise the admission requirements of either institution, adding that applicants must first secure admission before applying for the scholarship.

Secondary school principals and guidance counsellors in Ogbomoso North, Ogbomoso South, Oriire, Surulere and Ogo Oluwa local government areas were encouraged to inform eligible final-year students about the opportunity.

The sponsors also called on the Oyo State Government, local government councils, private sector operators, alumni associations and Ogbomoso indigenes in the diaspora to support the initiative.

The initiative comes amid growing efforts by governments, educational institutions and private organisations to expand access to technology education and equip young Nigerians with skills needed in the digital economy.

With increasing demand for professionals in fields such as artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and data science, scholarships and skills development programmes have become important avenues for addressing financial barriers to education and improving employment prospects among young people.

title: Protect Democracy, President Tinubu Urges Nigerians
description: President Bola Tinubu has called on Nigerians to protect democracy, stressing that it requires constant nurturing and commitment to flourish.President Tinubu spoke at the public presentation of ‘From AD to APC: The Evolution of Nigerian Political Parties and the Exploits of One Man (1998&ndash
content:
President Bola Tinubu has called on Nigerians to protect democracy, stressing that it requires constant nurturing and commitment to flourish.

President Tinubu spoke at the public presentation of ‘From AD to APC: The Evolution of Nigerian Political Parties and the Exploits of One Man (1998–2015)’, authored by Sam Omatseye, Chairman of the Editorial Board of The Nation newspaper, at the State House, Abuja.

According to a statement by the Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga on Wednesday in Abuja, Tinubu relived the long political journey of Nigeria’s Progressives from the Alliance for Democracy (AD) in 1999 to the All Progressives Congress (APC), describing it as a story of resilience, sacrifice and democratic conviction.

He paid glowing tributes to pro-democracy activists, saying their courage, sacrifices and unwavering commitment to popular sovereignty helped secure the democracy Nigerians enjoy today.

The President described the book as a masterpiece that captured events he had personally experienced and the struggles that shaped Nigeria’s democratic journey.

Tinubu recalled that Omatseye began the research about three years ago, engaging him through questions, interviews and requests to clarify events surrounding his political journey from 1999 to 2015, when the APC won the presidency by beating an incumbent.

President Tinubu traced their friendship to the June 12 pro-democracy struggle, recalling that he first met Omatseye in Abuja when the latter was Managing Editor of the Abuja Bureau of Concord Newspapers.

The President described the pro-democracy struggle as a defining test of courage and commitment, marked by loss of lives, livelihoods and separation from families.

“There was no price we would not pay for democracy. Some died along the way. Some were wounded for life. Some lost their livelihoods,” he said.

President Tinubu said the struggle was not merely about survival but about securing justice, popular sovereignty and democratic governance for future generations.

“Democracy is not an heirloom to be locked away in a drawer. It is a garden we must tend every day, so that it does not merely survive, but grows by leaps and bounds,” Tinubu said.

Former Ogun State Governor Chief Olusegun Osoba, who chaired the occasion, chronicled President Tinubu’s leadership of the progressive movement in Lagos amid opposition from the Federal Government under former President Olusegun Obasanjo.

Osoba recounted how the movement transformed from AD to AC and ACN, eventually merging with other opposition parties to form the APC.

He said the merger produced President Muhammadu Buhari as Nigeria’s first progressive president in 2015, marking a historic change in the country’s political landscape.

Senate President Godswill Akpabio praised Tinubu’s political vision and thanked Omatseye for documenting the evolution of Nigeria’s political parties.

Akpabio said Tinubu had consistently demonstrated progressive ideals, even as governor of Lagos State, adding that his positions on major policy decisions had often proved beneficial.

He cited the removal of petrol subsidy and tax reforms as examples of difficult but visionary decisions, noting that the reforms had improved revenue allocations to states.

Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani thanked President Tinubu for his tenacity and commitment to democracy, recalling that they had fought together during the pro-democracy struggle.

The Governor said President Tinubu’s leadership had continued to strengthen the progressive movement and advance democratic governance.

“Entrenching democratic ideals is much more difficult because we have been fighting anti-democratic elements, as well as military apologists in this country who today are masquerading as such.

“No one in Nigeria can boast of your democratic credentials. That is why we support you, and Nigerians will support you.” Uba Sani said.

Imo State Governor and Chairman of the Progressive Governors’ Forum, Hope Uzodimma, said governors remain committed to President Tinubu and his political ideals, stressing that governors benefited from the President’s political leadership.

Sen. Adams Oshiomhole spoke about the challenges President Tinubu faced under the Obasanjo administration, saying the former Lagos governor resisted political pressure and successfully sustained the progressive movement in the South-West before forging alliances across the country.

Tunji Bello, Executive Vice-Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC), also commended Tinubu for his doggedness and commitment to the progressive cause.

The reviewer of the book and Executive Commissioner (Operations) of the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) said the author definitely showed that there is truly only one undisputed master strategist in Nigerian politics, who is no other than President Tinubu – the only civilian Lagos State Governor who outsmarted five-star military generals in the political space.

The author, Sam Omatseye, said the book was developed through extensive research, primary source materials, and interviews with at least twenty-five individuals who participated in the political developments covered.

He thanked President Tinubu, Governor Uba Sani, the Senate President and other political leaders who contributed personal accounts and historical perspectives to the publication.

The presentation attracted governors, members of the National Assembly, ministers and other political leaders.

Among those present were Governors Ogun Dapo Abiodun, Ekiti Biodun Oyebanji, Benue Hyacinth Alia, Nasarawa Abdullahi Sule, Edo Monday Okpebholo, and Kogi Usman Ododo, as well as the APC Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda.

Others were Senate Leader Opeyemi Bamidele, Chief of Staff to the President Femi Gbajabiamila, National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu, Attorney General and Minister of Justice Lateef Fagbemi (SAN), Minister of Information and National Orientation Mohammed Idris, Minister of Budget and Economic Planning Atiku Bagudu, Minister of Science, Technology and Innovation Kingsley Udeh (SAN), and Chairman of the National Sports Commission Shehu Dikko.

The event also featured donations towards the book.

content:
Former Senate President, Dr Abubakar Bukola Saraki, has expressed sadness over the death of the Balogun Gambari of Ilorin and Balogun Agba of the Ilorin Emirate, Alhaji Aliyu Adebayo.

Saraki, in a condolence message shared on his Facebook page on Wednesday, described Adebayo’s death as a painful loss to the Ilorin Emirate and its traditional institution.

He noted that the late Adebayo, as Balogun Agba and the second most senior titleholder in the Ilorin Emirate Council, occupied a position of great responsibility and made significant contributions to the Emirate.

According to Saraki, the late traditional titleholder’s contributions would be remembered, while his absence would leave a vacuum in the traditional institution.

He extended his condolences to the Emir of Ilorin, Alhaji (Dr.) Ibrahim Sulu-Gambari, the Ilorin Emirate Council, the Gambari community and the deceased’s immediate family.

Saraki urged the bereaved family and the Emirate to take solace in the will of Almighty Allah and remain steadfast in prayers during the difficult period.

He prayed to Allah to forgive the deceased’s shortcomings and grant him Aljannah Firdaus, while giving his family and the entire Ilorin Emirate the strength to bear the loss. He also prayed for continued peace and unity in the Emirate.

title: Guardiola urges Portugal to give Ronaldo fitting farewell
description:
Pep Guardiola has urged the Portuguese Football Federation to ensure Cristiano Ronaldo receives a proper and respectful end to his international career, saying the five-time Ballon d’Or winner should not leave the national team under the current circumstances.
Speaking in an interview with former Br
content:
Pep Guardiola has urged the Portuguese Football Federation to ensure Cristiano Ronaldo receives a proper and respectful end to his international career, saying the five-time Ballon d’Or winner should not leave the national team under the current circumstances.

Speaking in an interview with former Brazil striker Romário on Tuesday, Guardiola said both the federation and the player need to make an effort to arrange a fitting send-off.

“The Portuguese Football Federation must ensure a dignified end to Cristiano Ronaldo’s career.

“Both sides need to make an effort to guarantee a fitting farewell. Cristiano Ronaldo shouldn’t leave the Portuguese national team in this manner. They can’t let him go like this, “ Guardiola said.

The ex-Manchester City manager described Ronaldo as “an incredibly important figure, not only for himself and Portugal, but for future generations of Portuguese players.” He added that the 41-year-old “deserves to leave on his own terms.”

“There are exceptional players, and Cristiano Ronaldo is one of them; therefore, this situation must be rectified,” Guardiola continued.

“Whether they rectify it or not isn’t my concern, but they absolutely must. What he’s achieved in the world of football deserves a different ending.”

Guardiola called for a public celebration in which Ronaldo could feel the support of Portuguese fans, while also encouraging the player to move past recent disagreements.

“There should be a celebration where he feels the love of his countrymen, and he, in turn, must also take the initiative and say: Let’s turn the page on the past,” he said.

“An entire career shouldn’t be judged based on a month or two, or because of a disagreement or misunderstanding with one or two individuals.”

He concluded that great players “deserve to leave through the front door,” both as recognition of their contributions and as an example for young players who aspire to end their careers like Romário, Ronaldo, Lionel Messi or Paolo Maldini.

Ronaldo formally retired from the Portugal national team on 5 November 2026 after 23 years, 234 appearances and a world-record 146 international goals.

His departure followed a dispute with coach Jorge Jesus in late September, when Ronaldo left the national team camp without permission ahead of a Nations League match.

He was later disciplined by the federation.
Portugal organised tributes during the November international window, including the squad wearing Ronaldo’s No. 7 shirt, but the player himself was not present.

Guardiola’s comments, made in the days after those tributes, have renewed discussion about whether a more personal farewell involving Ronaldo can still be arranged.
