title: Can We Prepare Children For Financial Success Before They Start Earning?
description:
Ufuoma Paula Onephrojire on the importance of childhood financial literacy, the inspiration behind her book, Operation Viper X7: A Money Adventure, and her mission to raise a financially conscious generation.







In a world where children are increasingly exposed to financial pressures, consumeri
content:
Ufuoma Paula Onephrojire on the importance of childhood financial literacy, the inspiration behind her book, Operation Viper X7: A Money Adventure, and her mission to raise a financially conscious generation.

In a world where children are increasingly exposed to financial pressures, consumerism and unrealistic portrayals of wealth, teaching them how to manage money has become more important than ever. Yet, financial education remains largely absent from many children’s formative learning experiences. Following the launch of her children’s book, Operation Viper X7: A Money Adventure, economist, financial literacy advocate and author, Ufuoma Paula Onephrojire, speaks about the personal experiences that inspired the book, why financial education must begin in childhood and her vision of making financial literacy accessible to children across Nigeria and Africa.

Why should financial education begin in childhood?

Interviewer: Financial literacy is increasingly becoming an important conversation among adults. Why are you making a case for introducing it to children?

Ufuoma Paula: I believe we have waited too long to introduce children to conversations about money. We spend years teaching them how to read, write, calculate and prepare for examinations, but how much attention do we give to preparing them to make sound financial decisions?

A child can graduate with excellent grades and still have no idea how to budget, save towards a goal, distinguish between needs and wants or manage money responsibly.

Financial literacy is not something people suddenly need when they get their first salary. It is a life skill that is best developed early.

Children already interact with money. They receive pocket money, make spending choices, compare what they own with what their friends have and develop attitudes towards money from what they observe at home and in society. Whether we deliberately teach them or not, they are learning something about money every day.

The question is whether what they are learning is preparing them for responsible financial decisions.

The lessons children learn about money today can influence the financial habits, values and decisions they carry into adulthood. Those decisions will affect not only their personal wellbeing, but also their families, businesses and communities. When we raise financially informed individuals, we are contributing to a society where people are better equipped to make responsible choices, recognise opportunities and manage resources wisely.

We should teach children not just how to make money someday, but how to manage resources, recognise opportunities, create value and understand that money is a tool, not a master.

The personal experiences behind the book

Interviewer: What inspired you to write Operation Viper X7: A Money Adventure? Was there a personal experience behind it?

Ufuoma Paula: My motivation comes from personal experiences, professional exposure and a deep desire to see the next generation develop a healthier relationship with money.

I studied Economics at Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology in Ghana and obtained an MBA from Aston University in the United Kingdom. I have worked in accounting and finance-related roles and experienced different dimensions of managing money, including the difficult lessons that come when things do not go as planned.

I know what it means to live from paycheck to paycheck, deal with debt and experience a business that did not turn out as expected. These experiences reinforced my conviction that financial knowledge must go beyond knowing how to earn money. We must understand how to keep it, manage it, protect it and grow it.

One childhood experience has also stayed with me. At about ten years old, I bought a fancy pen with money I had earned. My mother warned me that someone might steal it at school. Unfortunately, that was exactly what happened.

Looking back, I realise that even seemingly small childhood experiences can teach important lessons about money, value, ownership and decision-making.

I began asking myself: What if we could introduce children to these lessons deliberately, through stories and practical activities, before they encounter some of the more expensive mistakes adults make?

I did not want to write another book that simply tells children to save money. I wanted to create something that would help them understand money, develop good habits and make thoughtful financial decisions while they are still young.

That desire became Operation Viper X7: A Money Adventure.

Meet Efe and the electric-blue Viper X7

Interviewer: The title is quite intriguing. What is Operation Viper X7 about, and why did you choose an adventure rather than a conventional financial education textbook?

Ufuoma Paula: I wanted children to enjoy learning about money rather than feel as though they were attending another classroom lesson.

The book follows Onanefe Edeki, affectionately called Efe, a ten-year-old Nigerian boy who desperately wants an electric-blue Viper X7 bicycle worth ₦95,000 but does not have the money to buy it.

What begins as a simple desire for a bicycle becomes an adventure filled with money missions, discoveries, choices and challenges.

Through his interactions with family and friends, Efe learns that getting what you want involves more than simply asking for it. He discovers the importance of saving, spending wisely, managing what he has, earning, planning and exercising patience.

The story explores needs versus wants, goal-setting, responsible spending, delayed gratification, resisting peer pressure, discipline, integrity and creating value.

There is humour, adventure and a Nigerian setting children can identify with. I wanted them to see themselves in the characters and understand that these lessons are not abstract financial theories. They apply to everyday life.

One lesson I particularly want children to understand is that money can be earned by solving problems and using their abilities to create value. We should raise children who understand the dignity of honest work, not those who grow up believing that wealth is simply about acquiring money by any means.

Ultimately, Efe’s journey shows children that small, consistent and responsible decisions can move them closer to their goals.

More than a storybook: Building practical money habits

Interviewer: The project also includes an accompanying workbook. Why was it important to go beyond the storybook?

Ufuoma Paula: Because understanding a lesson and practising it are two different things.

The storybook introduces financial concepts in an enjoyable and relatable way, while the workbook provides practical activities and exercises that help children reflect on what they have read and apply those lessons.

I believe financial education should be practical. We cannot simply tell children to save and assume they understand what that means. We should help them set goals, track progress, make decisions and learn from the outcomes.

The storybook and workbook are designed to work together as a learning experience. The book is primarily targeted at children aged 8–14, although older children and teenagers can benefit from its lessons too.

My hope is that parents will use the materials to start meaningful conversations at home, while teachers incorporate them into reading and financial literacy activities.

The role of parents and schools

Interviewer: What role should parents and schools play in raising financially responsible children? Should financial literacy become part of school learning programmes?

Ufuoma Paula: Absolutely. Parents and schools have complementary roles to play.

Children learn from observing their parents. They notice how money is discussed at home, how spending decisions are made and how parents respond when they cannot afford something.

Sometimes, parents tell children to save but do not give them opportunities to practise. We need to move beyond simply giving children money and expecting them to figure things out. We must create opportunities for conversations and practical learning.

Schools can provide a structured environment for financial education through age-appropriate materials, practical exercises, savings activities and discussions about earning, spending, giving and investing.

I would love to see schools adopt Operation Viper X7 as part of their reading and financial literacy programmes, using the storybook and workbook to introduce these important conversations.

We cannot keep postponing financial education until adulthood and then wonder why so many people struggle with basic money management. By then, some attitudes and habits may already be deeply established.

Taking the mission beyond privileged communities

Interviewer: Beyond individual book sales, you have spoken about wanting this book to reach children across Nigeria and Africa, particularly those in underserved communities. Tell us more about that vision.

Ufuoma Paula: My vision is for Operation Viper X7 to be in the hands of as many African children as possible.

I do not want access to financial education to be determined by a child’s background, their parents’ income or the resources available in their school.

Children in underserved communities are just as intelligent, curious and full of potential as children in more privileged environments. They deserve access to resources that equip them with important life skills.

This is why I am inviting foundations, NGOs, banks, financial institutions, corporate organisations, government agencies and individuals who believe in children’s education and empowerment to support this mission.

I want organisations to sponsor copies of Operation Viper X7 for public and low-income schools, community libraries, orphanages and underserved communities.

Sponsorship can take different forms. An individual can sponsor a few copies, a company can sponsor a classroom or an entire school, while a foundation can support distribution across selected communities. Organisations can also partner with us to facilitate interactive financial literacy sessions alongside book distribution.

When an organisation sponsors these books, it is doing more than donating reading materials. It is helping introduce children to principles that can influence their financial decisions for years to come.

I want this to become a collaborative effort involving parents, educators, businesses, foundations and communities.

A mission bigger than a book

Interviewer: What is the bigger picture you hope to achieve through this initiative?

Ufuoma Paula: I want to contribute to raising a generation of children who understand money, recognise their abilities, create value, make responsible financial decisions and approach wealth creation with integrity.

Children today are exposed to so much information about money and success, particularly through social media. Unfortunately, not all the messages they encounter promote patience, discipline, honest work or responsible wealth creation.

I worry about a generation growing up admiring the appearance of wealth without understanding the principles behind building and sustaining it.

Financial success is not simply about having money or displaying material possessions. It involves making wise decisions, developing useful skills, creating value, managing resources and being responsible with what we have.

And the impact goes far beyond the individual. Imagine a generation that understands the consequences of its financial decisions, makes informed choices, approaches opportunities responsibly and uses its resources to create value. Such individuals are better positioned to build stable families, ethical businesses and stronger communities. Over time, these individual decisions contribute to a more financially responsible and productive society. That is the kind of long-term impact I believe financial literacy can create.

I want Operation Viper X7 to help nurture this understanding.

My ambition is to see the book reach homes, schools, libraries and communities across Nigeria and, ultimately, Africa. Every child deserves the opportunity to develop the knowledge and confidence to make better financial decisions.

How can parents, schools and organisations become part of the mission?

Interviewer: What is your message to parents, school administrators, foundations and organisations who would like to get involved?

Ufuoma Paula: My message is simple: let us be intentional about the financial future of our children.

To parents and guardians, I encourage you to get Operation Viper X7: A Money Adventure for your children. Do not wait until they start earning money before introducing them to financial responsibility. Allow them to develop healthy money habits while they are young and their habits are still forming.

To school proprietors, administrators and educators, I invite you to introduce the book and workbook into your classrooms, libraries, reading programmes and extracurricular activities. We are also open to school partnerships and interactive financial literacy sessions.

To foundations, NGOs, banks, financial institutions, and corporate organisations, as part of Corporate Social Responsibility programs, I invite you to sponsor copies for children and schools that may otherwise lack access to these resources. Together, we can make financial literacy more accessible and contribute meaningfully to the education and empowerment of the next generation.

I often think about a question parents ask after encouraging their children to save: “So your children have saved money. Now what?”

We need to teach them what comes next: how to make wise decisions, understand value, create opportunities, manage resources, and eventually grow what they have responsibly.

That is the thinking behind this book and the mission I want people to join.

I have planted a seed through Operation Viper X7. My invitation is for parents, schools, organisations and communities to help me water it.

Every child deserves the opportunity to grow up financially informed, confident and responsible. Let us not leave that future to chance.

ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Ufuoma Paula Onephrojire is an economist, financial educator, author and advocate for financial literacy and wealth creation. She holds a degree in Economics from Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Ghana, an MBA from Aston University, United Kingdom, and is a Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Economists of Nigeria.

She is the founder of Women and Wealth Initiative and is passionate about making financial education practical, accessible and relevant to everyday life. Through Operation Viper X7: A Money Adventure, she is extending her financial literacy advocacy to children, with a vision of nurturing a financially conscious generation across Africa.

title: AGN mourns Pete Edochie, describes him as ‘father figure’
description:
By Benjamin Njoku



The National President of the Actors Guild of Nigeria (AGN), Alhaji Abubakar Yakubu, has mourned veteran actor Pete Edochie, describing him as a father figure in the Nigerian entertainment industry whose legacy would endure for generations.







Edochie, 79, reportedly died in
content:
By Benjamin Njoku

The National President of the Actors Guild of Nigeria (AGN), Alhaji Abubakar Yakubu, has mourned veteran actor Pete Edochie, describing him as a father figure in the Nigerian entertainment industry whose legacy would endure for generations.

Edochie, 79, reportedly died in the early hours of Wednesday following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer.

His son, Leo Pete Edochie, announced his death in an Instagram post, describing him as “our beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman.”

In his tribute, Yakubu described the late actor as an all-rounder whose contributions extended beyond Nollywood to the broadcasting industry.

“Pete Edochie was a man of the people, a detribalised Nigerian who spoke different languages. He lived a noble life, a dedicated Christian and a disciplinarian,” he said.

He added that the actor’s death came at a time when the industry still needed his experience and contributions.

“He died when the industry needed him most. But as a thorough-bred actor, he left when the ovation was loudest,” Yakubu said.

Born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State, Edochie, fondly called Ebube Dike, hailed from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, Anambra State.

He began his career in broadcasting in 1967 with the Eastern Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation, where he rose to become Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director.

He gained national prominence in the 1980s through his portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s literary classic, Things Fall Apart.

The role earned him widespread recognition and helped launch a celebrated career in Nigerian cinema.

Known for his deep voice, commanding delivery and rich use of proverbs, Edochie became synonymous with portrayals of kings, community leaders and family patriarchs.

His notable film credits include Igodo, Rituals and Lionheart (2018), directed by Genevieve Nnaji.

In recognition of his contributions to the entertainment industry, he was honoured with the Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003, the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards Industry Merit Award and several lifetime achievement honours.

title: I don’t care about Ballon d’Or, says Bellingham
description:
Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham has insisted that winning the Ballon d’Or is not his priority, stressing that team success matters more than individual recognition.
The England international made the comments after producing an impressive performance in Real Madrid’s 5-1 comeback victory over
content:
Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham has insisted that winning the Ballon d’Or is not his priority, stressing that team success matters more than individual recognition.

The England international made the comments after producing an impressive performance in Real Madrid’s 5-1 comeback victory over PSV in the UEFA Champions League.

Bellingham started the match on the bench but was introduced in the second half after Madrid went into the break trailing 1-0 against the Dutch side.

His introduction changed the course of the game, with captain Federico Valverde equalising in the 50th minute before Bellingham put Madrid ahead 10 minutes later with a stunning volley.

The 23-year-old controlled the ball outside the penalty area before firing an exquisite effort with the outside of his right foot beyond PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar.

Kylian Mbappe added two more goals, while Vinicius Junior completed the scoring to seal an emphatic victory for the Spanish giants.

As reported by BBC Sport on Wednesday, speaking after the match, Bellingham played down suggestions that he was targeting the Ballon d’Or, insisting that winning trophies with Real Madrid remained his biggest ambition.

“I don’t care about the Ballon d’Or, honestly. I want to win a lot of titles with the team, the Champions League, the League,” he said.

“The Ballon d’Or is something for you, journalists, to vote and create a bit of tension. But for me it’s more important that the team win.”

Madrid manager Jose Mourinho was full of praise for the midfielder, describing him as the best player in his position.

“He is an amazing player that has everything. He has physicality, he understands the game, he has absolutely everything. Today, he has changed how the game was evolving,” Mourinho said.

Bellingham’s stunning strike was his fourth goal in his last five appearances for Madrid, further underlining his growing influence in the team.

However, the midfielder remained modest when asked whether he should be compared with former Real Madrid and France great Zinedine Zidane.

“I think Zidane is much better than me. He’s much more elegant and he’s my idol,” he said.

Bellingham also highlighted the importance of maintaining consistency, insisting that his attention had already shifted to Madrid’s next fixture.

“I think you’re only as good as your next one. Your last one doesn’t really matter,” he added.

Despite the growing attention surrounding his performances, Bellingham made it clear that collective achievements, rather than individual awards, would define his ambitions at the Santiago Bernabeu.

content:
By Femi Bolaji

JALINGO — Youths and supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Taraba State have assured President Bola Tinubu of a peaceful reception ahead of his anticipated campaign visit to the state for the 2027 general elections.

The youths, who also declared their readiness to mobilise support for the President and other APC candidates, made the pledge during a solidarity road walk in Tella Town, Wuryo Ward, Gassol Local Government Area.

They also expressed appreciation to Tinubu for appointing Taraba indigenes to strategic positions in his administration.

The convener of the road walk and Senior Special Assistant to Governor Agbu Kefas on Youth Mobilisation, Hon. Acho Righteous, described the turnout as evidence of growing support for the APC and its preparedness for the 2027 elections.

Righteous commended the APC National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, for strengthening the party’s national structure and advancing its unification agenda, particularly in Taraba, which recently transitioned from PDP to APC leadership.

“Our National Chairman, the erudite Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, has rebuilt the party and we are solidly behind his unification agenda.

“We are now on the field and mobilising our people to ensure President Bola Tinubu, Governor Agbu Kefas and all APC candidates at the state and national levels win convincingly at the polls,” he said.

He also praised the APC State Chairman, Abubakar Bawa, for promoting unity and strengthening the party’s structures across the state.

The Commissioner for Science and Technology, Hon. Muslim Aruwa, and an APC chieftain, Alhaji Adamu Musa, who also spoke at the event, said the road walk demonstrated the party’s determination to consolidate its grassroots support ahead of the 2027 general elections.

title: Pete Edochie: 8 interesting facts about Nollywood’s Fallen Iroko
description:
Chief Peter Uwadiegwu Ogugua Edochie, popularly known as Pete Edochie, was more than a celebrated Nollywood actor.
He was a broadcaster, accomplished storyteller and one of the influential figures whose performances helped shape Nigerian cinema.
Born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State, the vet
content:
Chief Peter Uwadiegwu Ogugua Edochie, popularly known as Pete Edochie, was more than a celebrated Nollywood actor.

He was a broadcaster, accomplished storyteller and one of the influential figures whose performances helped shape Nigerian cinema.

Born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State, the veteran entertainer died on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, in Enugu at the age of 79.

He became famous for his commanding screen presence, deep voice, memorable African proverbs and convincing portrayal of kings, traditional rulers and family patriarchs.

His performance as Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart remains one of the most recognised roles in Nigerian television history.

As the entertainment industry mourns his passing, here are eight remarkable facts about his life, career and legacy.

1. Kaduna was his birthplace, Anambra his ancestral home

Pete Edochie was born in Zaria, Kaduna State, but his ancestral roots traced back to Ifite Nteje in Anambra State. His full name was Peter Uwadiegwu Ogugua Edochie.

2. Shakespeare introduced him to the world of drama

His interest in acting began during his teenage years. In 1962, at just 15, he participated in a school drama presentation based on William Shakespeare’s The Merchant of Venice while attending St John’s College, Kaduna.

3. He climbed the broadcasting ladder before acting

Edochie’s professional journey started in 1967 when he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service as a junior programmes assistant.

Through years of experience, he rose to become Director of Programmes at the Anambra Broadcasting Service.

He also served as Deputy Managing Director and occasionally acted as Managing Director.

He furthered his professional education at the School of Journalism and Television in England.

4. Okonkwo became the role that defined his career

His portrayal of Okonkwo in the 1987 Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart brought him national and international recognition.

His impressive interpretation of the complex character attracted the attention of the British Broadcasting Corporation, which sent a delegation to interview him about his performance.

5. His professional journey extended beyond Nigeria

During the Nigerian Civil War, Edochie and his wife, Josephine, reportedly worked with the Voice of Biafra before returning to broadcasting after the war.

In 1980, he also received professional broadcasting training at the BBC. Years later, he became the pioneer director of ABS 3 FM Stereo in Enugu and named the station Sunrise ’96.

6. He built an impressive collection of film credits

Following his success in Things Fall Apart, Edochie featured in numerous Nigerian productions, including Igodo, Rituals, Lionheart, Idemili, Ebubedike, Unroyal, King Mabutu and Foreigner’s God.

He became particularly associated with roles portraying traditional rulers, wealthy businessmen and respected family heads.

7. His talent earned him national and international honours

In 2003, former President Olusegun Obasanjo conferred on him the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON).

Other recognitions included the Africa Magic Industry Merit Award, a Lifetime Achievement Award from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Legend Award, which he received in 2020.

8. Behind the Screen legend was a father of six

Edochie was married to Josephine Edochie, and their marriage produced six children, including popular Nollywood actors Yul and Linc Edochie.

In 2009, he survived a kidnapping incident and was later released unharmed. He was also a practising Catholic.

Pete Edochie’s passing marks the end of a remarkable chapter in Nigerian entertainment.

From his early broadcasting days to his unforgettable portrayal of Okonkwo, he established a legacy that extended beyond individual film productions.

His distinctive voice, memorable performances and contribution to African storytelling will remain part of Nollywood’s history.

The post Pete Edochie: 8 interesting facts about Nollywood’s Fallen Iroko appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: FG Seeks Polish Investment In Nigeria’s Fisheries, Aquaculture Sectors
description: The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Dr Adegboyega Oyetola, has called on Polish investors and businesses to take advantage of the vast investment opportunities in Nigeria’s fisheries and aquaculture sectors, saying strategic partnerships could boost local production, create jobs and stren
content:
The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Dr Adegboyega Oyetola, has called on Polish investors and businesses to take advantage of the vast investment opportunities in Nigeria’s fisheries and aquaculture sectors, saying strategic partnerships could boost local production, create jobs and strengthen the country’s food security.

Oyetola made the call in Lagos on Tuesday while delivering his goodwill message at the Polish-Nigerian Economic Forum held in Lagos State, according to a statement signed by Special Adviser to the Minister, Dr. Bolaji Akinola, in Abuja on Wednesday.

The minister described Nigeria’s marine and blue economy as a promising frontier for bilateral economic cooperation, urging Polish investors to bring in investment capital, modern technology, technical expertise and sustainable production systems to unlock the sector’s potential.

“I therefore wish to invite Polish investors, businesses, and technical partners to take a closer look at Nigeria’s fisheries and aquaculture sector,” he said.

He identified fish production, processing, storage, cold-chain logistics, aquaculture technology, feed production, equipment manufacturing and export development as key areas offering attractive investment opportunities.

According to him, investments in these areas would help increase domestic fish production, reduce dependence on imports, generate employment, empower coastal communities and create significant economic value.

“These investments can help boost local production, reduce fish import dependence, create employment, strengthen food security, empower coastal communities, and generate significant economic value,” Oyetola stated.

The minister also expressed appreciation to the Polish Government for its support for Nigeria’s Port Modernisation Programme, describing the gesture as a reflection of Poland’s confidence in Nigeria’s economic potential and commitment to strengthening bilateral relations.

He said the partnership would contribute to the development of efficient, modern and competitive maritime infrastructure, noting that the programme was scheduled for flag-off in Lagos on Wednesday, November 25.

Oyetola noted that the benefits of Nigeria-Poland cooperation should extend beyond port infrastructure to other critical areas of the marine and blue economy, including fisheries, aquaculture, marine technology and logistics.

“Our vision is to build a marine and blue economy that is productive, sustainable, resilient, and investment-driven,” he declared.

He expressed confidence that stronger collaboration between both countries would unlock new opportunities, promote technology transfer and accelerate sustainable economic development.

title: Pete Edochie: Nigeria has lost a voice that time will never silence — Pat Utomi
description:
Political economist, Pat Utomi, has paid tribute to veteran Nollywood actor, Pete Edochie, describing him as a cultural institution whose legacy will endure beyond his lifetime.







Utomi, in a tribute shared on his Facebook page on Wednesday, said Nigeria had lost a distinguished voice whose con
content:
Political economist, Pat Utomi, has paid tribute to veteran Nollywood actor, Pete Edochie, describing him as a cultural institution whose legacy will endure beyond his lifetime.

Utomi, in a tribute shared on his Facebook page on Wednesday, said Nigeria had lost a distinguished voice whose contributions to the country’s entertainment industry and cultural heritage would remain unforgettable.

Describing Edochie as an iroko tree that had fallen, Utomi said the veteran actor’s departure was a monumental loss not only to the entertainment industry but also to generations who grew up watching his performances.

“An iroko has fallen, Nigeria has lost a voice that time will never silence,” he wrote.

He described Edochie as a custodian of African storytelling and a cultural institution whose commanding presence and performances had become part of Nigeria’s collective memory.

Utomi particularly recalled the actor’s portrayal of Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s literary classic, Things Fall Apart, saying he brought the character to life and presented the depth and complexities of African civilisation to the world.

“When Chief Pete Edochie stood before the camera as Okonkwo in Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart, he did something extraordinary. He breathed life into a literary character and gave the world a glimpse into the depth, complexity, pride and contradictions of African civilisation,” he said.

According to Utomi, Edochie did not merely interpret the character but immortalised it through his performance.

He noted that the actor’s distinctive voice, commanding presence and dignified approach to his craft had earned him a special place in the hearts of audiences across generations.

Beyond acting, Utomi acknowledged Edochie’s contributions to Nigerian broadcasting and cinema, saying his influence extended beyond entertainment and helped shape the country’s cultural landscape.

He added that although the actor’s departure marked the end of a remarkable chapter, his legacy would continue through his films, the stories passed down to younger generations and the inspiration he provided to emerging actors.

Utomi also extended his condolences to Edochie’s wife, children, family, friends and colleagues, praying that God would grant them the strength to bear the loss.

“May your soul find eternal rest. Rest well, EBUBEDIKE!! Nigeria will never forget your legacy, Africa will speak your name till the end of time,” he added.

title: Delta campaign violence: I’m ready to face investigation - Jaro Egbo
description:
The Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, Jaro Egbo, says he is willing to face investigation over the violence that erupted during the campaign rally of former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, insisting he had no involvement in the incident.







Egbo, who has be
content:
The Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, Jaro Egbo, says he is willing to face investigation over the violence that erupted during the campaign rally of former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, insisting he had no involvement in the incident.

Egbo, who has been accused by Omo-Agege of masterminding an alleged assassination attempt on him, said he was not at the scene of the violence and was in his office meeting with a Department of State Services officer when the incident occurred.

Speaking on ARISE News on Tuesday, the council chairman said he learnt about the violence shortly after the meeting, denying claims that he mobilised armed men to attack the senator’s campaign entourage.

“I do believe that the IGP should go very deep and ensure that anybody that is culpable, including myself, should be subject to the law,” he said.

The violence reportedly claimed the lives of four members of Omo-Agege’s campaign team, while Egbo alleged that three members of his community were also killed during the confrontation.

He claimed the crisis started after disagreements over the use of a community hall, which had allegedly been booked for an annual prayer programme, and escalated following remarks made by Omo-Agege during the campaign.

Egbo further alleged that members of the senator’s entourage were armed and that a member of the team opened fire, hitting the community’s President-General and two other persons. He claimed the shooting triggered a reprisal by residents.

The chairman rejected claims that he acted on the orders of Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to disrupt the campaign, insisting the governor had consistently instructed local government chairmen to maintain peace.

He also dismissed calls for his resignation following the imposition of a curfew in Ughelli North, saying stepping down would amount to conceding to what he described as violent conduct.

“I am not to resign. If I resign my position, then Omo-Agege would have gotten his way as a violent one,” he said.

Egbo, however, acknowledged his responsibility as the local government’s chief security officer, saying residents had the constitutional right to assemble and carry out political activities freely.

He said the local security council had met and was engaging stakeholders to prevent further violence, adding that he welcomed a thorough investigation into the incident.

“I am a lawyer, so I rule by fact and law,” Egbo said, expressing sadness over the deaths and urging the police to ensure justice for all victims.

title: Tax administration: FG revenues jump to N33tn in 10 months
description:
The Federal Government generated a record N33tn in revenue between January and October 2026, with improvements in digital tax administration and electronic invoicing boosting collections.
Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, who said this recently, called for
content:
The Federal Government generated a record N33tn in revenue between January and October 2026, with improvements in digital tax administration and electronic invoicing boosting collections.

Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, who said this recently, called for greater investment in Nigeria’s digital infrastructure to strengthen economic competitiveness and government revenue mobilisation.

Oyedele said this in a lecture marking the 2026 convocation of the University of Uyo, AkwaIbom State, according to a statement by the minister’s Senior Special Assistant on Communications and Press Secretary, Maryann Duke.

Oyedele pointed to “improved digital systems, including electronic invoicing, as a key driver behind a record N33tn in government revenue collected between January and October 2026.”

The minister said the performance demonstrated the potential of technology to improve revenue administration, strengthen compliance and increase efficiency across government institutions.

Speaking on the theme, ‘Digital Sovereignty and Ethics: Guarding the Economy for the Next Generation,’ Oyedele warned that Nigeria risked losing substantial economic opportunities if it continued to depend heavily on foreign digital infrastructure.

Citing Nigerian Communications Commission figures, he disclosed that the country recorded more than 157 million active internet subscriptions as of May 2026.

He explained that these connections generated significant volumes of information through financial transactions, healthcare, education and taxation.

However, citing estimates from the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, Oyedele said as high as 90 per cent of the country’s data was hosted abroad.

According to him, the situation has implications for foreign exchange expenditure, employment opportunities, technological skills and Nigeria’s control over information generated by its citizens.

He compared the country’s reliance on foreign digital infrastructure with its historical dependence on imported refined petroleum products, warning against a situation where Nigerian data would be processed abroad and the resulting services sold back to domestic users.

The minister consequently advocated greater investment in local data infrastructure, technical expertise, cyber security and predictable regulations to enable Nigerian businesses to capture more value from the digital economy.

He clarified that digital sovereignty should not translate into technological isolation but should strengthen Nigeria’s capacity to participate competitively in international markets.

Addressing graduating students, Oyedele urged young Nigerians to become developers of technological solutions rather than remain primarily consumers of products created elsewhere.

He identified artificial intelligence as both a disruptive force and an opportunity for innovation, advising graduates to acquire relevant digital skills alongside critical thinking, creativity, sound judgement and integrity.

Tax Ombud seeks Tinubu’s nod for six regional offices

Office of the Tax Ombud has approached President Bola Tinubu for approval to establish six regional offices across Nigeria’s geopolitical zones as part of efforts to expand access to tax dispute resolution services and strengthen accountability in the country’s tax administration system

The office also disclosed that it had resolved approximately 82 percent of complaints received since its establishment, highlighting its efforts to address grievances between taxpayers and revenue authorities without recourse to prolonged litigation

The Tax Ombud and Chief Executive of the Office, John Nwabueze, disclosed these developments at the fourth-quarter 2026 breakfast meeting with members of the Finance Correspondents Association of Nigeria in Abuja recently

According to a statement by the Chief Press Secretary to the Tax Ombud, ChukwudiAchife, the proposed regional offices are expected to improve the accessibility of the institution’s services and bring its dispute resolution mechanisms closer to taxpayers across the country

Nwabueze said the offices were expected to become operational before the end of 2026, subject to approval by the President

He explained that the planned expansion formed part of the office’s broader strategy to improve taxpayer engagement, strengthen confidence in the tax system and ensure that individuals and businesses could access impartial channels for resolving disputes with revenue authorities.

“We are dedicated to building trust in the tax system and ensuring that all Nigerians have their voices heard. With the proposed launch of our regional offices and continued investment in public awareness and stakeholder engagement, we are confident in our ability to serve the nation better,” he said

The Tax Ombud said resolving about 82 percent of complaint reflected its commitment to addressing disagreements between taxpayers and tax authorities through alternative dispute resolution rather than allowing such matters to develop into lengthy court cases.
Nwabueze noted that establishing offices across the six geopolitical zones would particularly benefit taxpayers outside Abuja, who would otherwise have had to contend with geographical barriers in accessing the institution’s services

He added that the expansion would improve the speed and effectiveness of interventions by making it easier for affected individuals and businesses to submit complaints and engage with the office

As part of efforts to strengthen its presence at the state level, the Tax Ombud also plans to establish dedicated desks within tax authorities of all 36 states of the federation.
•              The Point

NRS preaches simpler tax rules for creative economy

Nigeria Revenue Service has called for simpler, clearer and business-friendly tax rules to unlock the investment potential of Nigeria’s creative economy, stressing that tax administration must facilitate enterprise growth, innovation and prosperity.

NRS said the emergence of digital business models, intellectual property-driven enterprises and cross-border transactions required tax system creators, entrepreneurs and investors could easily understand and navigate.

Executive Chairman of NRS, Dr. ZacchAdedeji, made the call at a high-level dialogue on taxation and investment in the creative economy at the Creative Africa Nexus event in Lagos, where he was represented by the Executive Director, People, Stakeholders and Communication, NRS, Mr. ObinnaIhedioha.

Adedeji described Nigeria’s creative economy as one of its most promising economic assets, noting that the country’s greatest resource was the minds and talents of its young people.

He said the sector had evolved beyond entertainment into a major economic enterprise capable of generating jobs, earning foreign exchange, attracting investment and expanding economic opportunities.

According to him, digital platforms and emerging business models have changed how value is created, with creative entrepreneurs building businesses around copyrights, designs, brands, digital products and audiences.

The NRS boss stated, “Government needs sustainable revenue to invest in education, security, technology and infrastructure.

But how we tax matters as much as what we collect. It shapes whether businesses start, whether investors come, and whether enterprises grow or stay small.”

Adedeji stressed that taxation should not be pursued at the expense of enterprise but should support the expansion of prosperity through a productive economy.

He added that growing businesses would ultimately strengthen government revenue and its capacity to deliver public services.

Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, Hannatu Musa Musawa, underscored the importance of the creative sector to Nigeria’s  economic diversification agenda, describing it as a major opportunity for job creation, wealth generation and youth empowerment.

description:
The Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria has reopened the Sam Mbakwe International Cargo Airport, Owerri, Imo State, for flight operations following the successful completion of runway rehabilitation works.
FAAN announced the reopening in a statement signed by its Director of Public Affairs and Con
content:
The Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria has reopened the Sam Mbakwe International Cargo Airport, Owerri, Imo State, for flight operations following the successful completion of runway rehabilitation works.

FAAN announced the reopening in a statement signed by its Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection, Henry Agbebire, and posted on its official X handle on Wednesday.

FAAN stated that the airport resumed operations on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, following approval by the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority after post-rehabilitation technical assessments and inspections.

The runway was temporarily closed on October 20, 2026, to allow for rehabilitation works aimed at improving its condition, enhancing operational efficiency and ensuring compliance with aviation safety standards.

FAAN said, “Following post-rehabilitation technical assessments and inspections, the NCAA approved the reopening of Runway 17, subject to specified operational conditions.”

The authority also acknowledged the contributions of Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma, and the state government, particularly in extending the runway from 2,700 metres to 3,200 metres.

According to FAAN, the intervention underscores the importance of federal-state collaboration in advancing aviation infrastructure, improving air connectivity and stimulating regional economic development.

However, the authority said the initial resumption of flight operations would be limited to daytime services under Visual Flight Rules.

It added that night operations and other applicable instrument flight operations would commence after the completion and verification of outstanding runway lighting installations.

“Appropriate safety measures will remain in place around areas where associated works are ongoing, in line with NCAA requirements,” the statement added.

FAAN also thanked airlines, passengers, host communities and other stakeholders for their patience and cooperation during the temporary closure.

The authority reaffirmed its commitment to providing safe, secure and efficient airport infrastructure in accordance with national and international aviation standards.

The post FAAN reopens Owerri airport for flight operations appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: I haven’t received any police invitation — Nduka Obaigbena
description:
Media mogul and Chairman of THISDAY and ARISE News, Nduka Obaigbena, has denied reports that he has been declared wanted by the Nigeria Police Force following a petition allegedly filed by the Chief Executive Officer of First Bank of Nigeria, Olusegun Alebiosu.







Obaigbena, in a statement issue
content:
Media mogul and Chairman of THISDAY and ARISE News, Nduka Obaigbena, has denied reports that he has been declared wanted by the Nigeria Police Force following a petition allegedly filed by the Chief Executive Officer of First Bank of Nigeria, Olusegun Alebiosu.

Obaigbena, in a statement issued by his office in Ikoyi, Lagos, described the reports as a “desperate smear campaign”, insisting that he had not received any police invitation or communication from any law enforcement agency.

He said his office had checked all its addresses and found no invitation concerning any investigation involving him.

The statement also disclosed that Obaigbena had been in communication with senior police authorities in recent weeks, including as recently as Thursday, November 19, when they discussed the proposed state police system and its implementation in Nigeria.

According to the statement, there was no indication during the engagements that the police required his attention over any matter.

Obaigbena’s office also linked the reports to an ongoing financial dispute involving First Bank, GHL, THISDAY Newspapers and ARISE Television, insisting that discussions were already underway to resolve outstanding issues amicably.

It recalled that the Supreme Court, in a unanimous 5-0 decision delivered on July 3, 2026, ruled in favour of GHL in its case against First Bank.

The statement said that following the judgment, First Bank and GHL had been exploring an out-of-court settlement.

It further disclosed that Obaigbena had met twice with First Bank Chairman, Femi Otedola, at the residences of businessman Aliko Dangote and at Hotel du Paris, Monaco, where discussions on possible settlement arrangements reportedly continued.

The statement also said Alebiosu had visited Obaigbena three times at his Ikoyi office, adding that both men had maintained dialogue on resolving the dispute.

It alleged that during one of the visits, Alebiosu presented Obaigbena with a bottle of whiskey.

According to the statement, efforts were also ongoing to settle debts allegedly owed by First Bank to THISDAY and ARISE Television without resorting to litigation.

“There is no basis for any police invitation on any matter affecting First Bank or Mr Obaigbena,” the statement said.

Obaigbena also denied threatening Alebiosu, stressing that the disagreement with First Bank was neither a personal dispute with the bank’s chief executive nor with Otedola.

He described himself as a law-abiding citizen and expressed respect for the Nigeria Police Force, noting that he was an elected member of the Constitutional Conference Committee in 1995, which worked on constitutional provisions relating to the police.

The statement further raised questions about whether other First Bank executives allegedly interested in succeeding Alebiosu had been interrogated by the police.

It said Obaigbena had no personal disagreement with Alebiosu, whose tenure as the bank’s chief executive, according to the statement, is expected to expire in April 2027.

The media mogul maintained that the dispute involving the bank and his media organisations was being addressed through dialogue and settlement efforts.

title: 10 Things to Know About Late Nollywood Veteran Pete Edochie
description:
The Nigerian entertainment industry has been thrown into mourning following the death of veteran Nollywood actor and broadcaster, Chief Pete Edochie, who died at the age of 79 on Wednesday, November 25, 2026.







Edochie, renowned for his commanding screen presence, distinctive voice and memorabl
content:
The Nigerian entertainment industry has been thrown into mourning following the death of veteran Nollywood actor and broadcaster, Chief Pete Edochie, who died at the age of 79 on Wednesday, November 25, 2026.

Edochie, renowned for his commanding screen presence, distinctive voice and memorable portrayal of traditional rulers and family patriarchs, was one of the most recognisable figures in Nigerian cinema.

Here are 10 things to know about the late actor.

1. He was born in Zaria, Kaduna State

Pete Edochie was born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State, although he hailed from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, in Anambra State.

He grew up in northern Nigeria before eventually establishing his roots in the southeastern part of the country.

2. He started his career as a broadcaster

Before becoming a household name in Nollywood, Edochie built a career in broadcasting.

He joined the Eastern Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation in 1967 as a junior programmes assistant and gradually rose through the ranks.

He later became Director of Programmes at the Anambra Broadcasting Service, where he also served as Deputy Managing Director and occasionally as Acting Managing Director.

3. He became famous for playing Okonkwo in Things Fall Apart

One of the defining moments of Edochie’s career was his portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s celebrated novel, Things Fall Apart.

His performance as the proud and uncompromising Igbo warrior earned him widespread recognition and established him as one of Nigeria’s leading television actors.

The role also attracted international attention, including coverage by the British Broadcasting Corporation.

4. He featured in over 200 screen productions

Edochie went on to feature in numerous Nigerian films and television productions throughout his career.

Some of his notable works include Rituals, Igodo, Billionaire’s Club, Egg of Life and Lionheart.

In Genevieve Nnaji’s 2018 film Lionheart, he played Chief Ernest Obiagu.

5. He was known for his deep voice and African proverbs

One of the qualities that distinguished Edochie from many actors was his commanding voice and measured delivery.

He became particularly associated with characters who portrayed traditional rulers, wealthy businessmen, fathers and authoritative family patriarchs.

His frequent use of African proverbs and traditional expressions also became a defining feature of his performances, earning him admiration among generations of movie lovers.

6. He received the national honour of MON

In recognition of his contributions to Nigerian entertainment, Edochie received the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003.

He also received the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards Industry Merit Award and a Lifetime Achievement Award at the Africa Film Academy.

In 2020, he was honoured with the African Film Legend Award at the African Film Festival.

7. He was married to Josephine Edochie and had six children

The late actor was married to Barrister Josephine Edochie, with whom he had six children.

Two of his children, Yul and Linc Edochie, followed in his footsteps and became actors in the Nigerian film industry.

His family occasionally attracted public attention, particularly following controversies surrounding Yul Edochie’s marriage to actress Judy Austin.

8. His death followed years of false death rumours

Edochie had repeatedly been the subject of false reports claiming that he had died.

In February 2026, his family dismissed another viral death rumour, with his eldest son, Leo Edochie, describing the reports as false and malicious.

The actor also previously spoke about how he had been declared dead several times on social media.

However, his family confirmed his death on November 25, 2026, in an official statement signed by Leo Edochie.

9. He died at 79 after a prolonged illness

The veteran actor died at 12:30 a.m. on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, in Enugu, according to the statement released by his family. He reportedly died following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer.

His family described him as a beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman, adding that funeral arrangements would be announced later.

10. He leaves behind a lasting legacy in Nollywood

Edochie’s death marks the loss of one of the influential figures in the history of Nigerian cinema.

From his early years in broadcasting to his celebrated portrayal of Okonkwo and subsequent appearances in hundreds of productions, he helped shape the representation of African culture, tradition and family life on screen.

His distinctive acting style, memorable dialogue and contribution to the growth of Nollywood have secured his place among the industry’s most celebrated veterans.

Vanguard News

title: [UPDATED] Enugu Has Lost An Icon, Mbah, Soludo Mourn Pete Edochie
description: Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah, has mourned veteran Nollywood actor, Chief Pete Edochie, describing his death as the loss of a giant, icon, and patriot.In a tribute issued early Wednesday, Mbah said Edochie’s death was a personal loss to Enugu State, recalling his strong ties with the state
content:
Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah, has mourned veteran Nollywood actor, Chief Pete Edochie, describing his death as the loss of a giant, icon, and patriot.

In a tribute issued early Wednesday, Mbah said Edochie’s death was a personal loss to Enugu State, recalling his strong ties with the state despite hailing from Nteje, Anambra State.

The governor said Edochie often described Enugu as his birthplace and “first port of call,” adding that he remained a great ambassador of the state.

“Pete Edochie was more than an accomplished actor; he was an institution,” Mbah said.

He noted that the actor’s commanding screen presence, distinctive voice and mastery of dialogue helped shape Nigerian cinema and project Igbo culture to the world.

Mbah also recalled Edochie’s portrayal of Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart, saying his performances preserved aspects of the region’s cultural heritage and inspired generations of actors.

The governor described the timing of the death as particularly painful, coming as Enugu hosts the National Festival of Arts and Culture (NAFEST).

“At a time when we are celebrating the richness of our cultural heritage and the creative talents that give it expression, we are confronted with the loss of one of its most distinguished ambassadors,” he said.

Mbah extended his condolences to Edochie’s family, the Nollywood community, the government and people of Anambra State, and his fans across the world.

“Your voice may have gone silent, but your legacy will speak for generations,” the governor added.

The veteran Nollywood actor and broadcaster died at the age of 79 after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer.

His death was announced on Wednesday by his son, Chief Leo Pete Edochie, in a statement shared on Instagram on behalf of the family.

According to the announcement, the actor died at 12:30 am on November 25, 2026, in Enugu, Nigeria.

title: US military base shooter seeks halt to firing squad execution
description:
Nidal Hasan, who is set to be executed by firing squad next month for his 2009 massacre at a US military base, asked a court on Tuesday to halt his execution, according to documents obtained by AFP.
The former US Army major and military psychiatrist asked a federal court to delay his execution, whic
content:
Nidal Hasan, who is set to be executed by firing squad next month for his 2009 massacre at a US military base, asked a court on Tuesday to halt his execution, according to documents obtained by AFP.

The former US Army major and military psychiatrist asked a federal court to delay his execution, which is set for December 3, while he prepares a case to challenge it on constitutional grounds.

If the execution goes ahead, Hasan will be the first person killed by a US military firing squad since 1945.

A furore over plans to livestream the killing erupted in early October.

US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth initially said the execution would be “public” before a Pentagon spokesperson added it would be available online.

Concerns mounted far and wide about making the execution into a spectacle and turning Hasan into a martyr.

After days of debate and condemnation, US President Donald Trump cancelled the plans to broadcast the killing, while allowing some witnesses to observe it in person.

Hasan killed 13 people, including 12 soldiers, and wounded 30 others in his November 2009 rampage.

He was shot by a civilian police officer and is paralysed from the waist down.

During his trial, Hasan chose to conduct his own defence, and court-appointed attorneys raised concerns that he was seeking to be executed.

Ultimately, he was sentenced to death by a military jury in 2013.

title: Morning Recap: Pete Edochie dies at 79, Omo-Agege rejects court ruling, other top stories
description:
From the death of veteran Nollywood actor Pete Edochie after a battle with prostate cancer to a court ruling nullifying Ovie Omo-Agege’s nomination for the 2027 Delta Central senatorial election, several major developments made the headlines.
The Inspector-General of Police has also warned politicia
content:
From the death of veteran Nollywood actor Pete Edochie after a battle with prostate cancer to a court ruling nullifying Ovie Omo-Agege’s nomination for the 2027 Delta Central senatorial election, several major developments made the headlines.

The Inspector-General of Police has also warned politicians against turning the 2027 elections into a theatre of violence following deadly attacks on political supporters in Delta State.

Meanwhile, President Bola Tinubu has proposed a N3.15tn reduction in the 2026 budget, while the Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Peter Obi, has defended Kwankwasiyya supporters over their practice of carrying sticks at political gatherings.

Here’s your complete morning roundup:

1. Pete Edochie dies at 79 after battle with prostate cancer

Veteran actor and broadcaster Pete Edochie died in Enugu at 12:30 am on Wednesday, November 25, aged 79, after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer.

His death was announced in a family statement signed by his son, Leo Pete Edochie, which described him as a “beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman.”

The statement said the actor hailed from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, Anambra State, and was survived by his wife, children, siblings and other relatives. Edochie rose to prominence for playing Okonkwo in the 1987 Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart.

He began his broadcasting career in 1967 before becoming one of Nollywood’s most recognisable actors.

READ MORE: https://punchng.com/veteran-actor-pete-edochie-dies-at-79/ 

2. Omo-Agege rejects court ruling voiding senatorial ticket

Former Deputy President of the Senate, Ovie Omo-Agege, has rejected a Federal High Court judgment nullifying his nomination as the Nigeria Democratic Congress candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 elections.

He said the ruling was “inconsistent with documentary evidence and applicable law” and directed his legal team to appeal.

The court ruled that the NDC failed to comply with provisions of the Electoral Act on submitting its membership register to the Independent National Electoral Commission before its primary.

It also ordered INEC to remove Omo-Agege’s name from its list of candidates. However, Omo-Agege insisted that “Senator Omo-Agege’s name appeared in the register submitted to INEC.”

READ MORE: https://punchng.com/omo-agege-kicks-as-court-voids-senatorial-ticket/ 

3. 2027 election: Delta killings heighten fears of poll violence

The Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, has warned politicians against turning the 2027 general elections into a theatre of violence, following attacks on political gatherings and the killing of six people in Uduere community, Delta State.

Disu said, “Political competition must never become justification for violence,” warning that those involved in attacks would be arrested and prosecuted.

INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, also cautioned that violence could undermine the credibility of the elections, saying, “When participants cannot assemble, campaign or organise themselves, express their views freely, the political process is compromised long before election day.”

The NDC, meanwhile, boycotted a security meeting with the police chief, saying it no longer felt safe or protected by the force.

READ MORE: https://punchng.com/2027-election-delta-killings-heighten-fears-of-poll-violence/ 

4. Tinubu cuts 2026 budget to N65.18tn, retains deficit

President Bola Tinubu has reduced the 2026 Federal Government budget from N68.323tn to N65.176tn while retaining the fiscal deficit at N31.457tn, representing 5.64 per cent of the country’s Gross Domestic Product.

The revised proposal was contained in a letter dated November 20 and read to the House of Representatives on Tuesday.

The revised budget provides for projected government revenue of N33.72tn and capital expenditure of N26.23tn.

Tinubu said the adjustments were intended to align spending with available resources and existing obligations, adding that they would “prioritise existing commitments and improve the credibility and execution of the capital budget while maintaining fiscal restraint.” The proposal also retains N29.22tn in new borrowing.

READ MORE: https://punchng.com/tinubu-cuts-2026-budget-to-n65-18tn-retains-deficit/ 

5. Kwankwasiyya supporters carry sticks but harm no one – Obi

Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, has defended supporters of the Kwankwasiyya movement over their practice of carrying sticks at political gatherings, saying he had never witnessed them being used to harm anyone.

Obi spoke during an interview with Channels Television in Jalingo, Taraba State, after a town hall meeting with his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso.

“Everybody who had followed the Kwankwansiyah group in Kano know that they come out with such sticks and everything, but they’ve never used it to harm anybody,” he said.

Obi also appealed to authorities to prevent violence during political activities, adding, “We cannot kill people, harm people, because we want to be political leaders.”

READ MORE: https://punchng.com/kwankwasiyya-supporters-carry-sticks-but-harm-no-one-obi/

title: After The Delta Killings, Nigeria Must Heed The Warning Signs
description: Six people were reported killed after gunfire broke out during a campaign visit in Uduere, in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, on Monday, 23 November. The police described the toll as preliminary and said several others were injured. The violence occurred during a visit by former
content:
Six people were reported killed after gunfire broke out during a campaign visit in Uduere, in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, on Monday, 23 November.

The police described the toll as preliminary and said several others were injured. The violence occurred during a visit by former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege, the Nigeria Democratic Congress candidate for Delta Central. The Inspector-General of Police has ordered an investigation that will also examine the conduct of officers at the venue.

For the bereaved families, the immediate demand is for answers and justice. For the country, the killings raise an urgent question. What are the authorities doing now to ensure that Nigerians can take part in the 2027 elections without fear?

Channels Television is deeply concerned by the violence we are seeing in this campaign. Every party has the right to campaign lawfully. Every journalist should be able to cover a political gathering safely. And every Nigerian should be able to attend a rally or cast a ballot without weighing the risk to their life. That is the standard by which we will judge the response to the killings in Delta and the preparations for the elections ahead.

The Warnings Were There Before Uduere

On 7 November, an attack on an NDC procession in Asaba killed one person and injured five, according to the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data project. That same week, the party’s presidential convoy came under attack in Calabar. On 12 November, armed men disrupted an NDC town hall in Oregun, Lagos, where a journalist was reportedly assaulted and his equipment seized. Each case warrants a separate investigation. Together, they show how quickly violence can deprive candidates of an audience, citizens of a chance to hear them and journalists of the ability to report.

The Centre for Democracy and Development in West Africa recorded 14 election-related incidents in September and 16 in October. Eleven of October’s incidents involved attacks on campaign gatherings or convoys. In a separate exercise, peace accord monitors recorded 33 incidents of political violence or thuggery between 19 August and 27 October. These figures predate the killings in Uduere.

The public is already making its own assessment. In an Afrobarometer survey released this month, 79 per cent of respondents said they thought it likely that party or candidate supporters would engage in violence on election day. Even so, 64 per cent said they were likely to vote. That willingness deserves a credible response. INEC has scheduled the presidential and National Assembly polls for 16 January 2027 and the governorship and state assembly elections for 6 February.

Where The Authorities Should Focus

Delta is an immediate priority. Two deadly campaign incidents in just over two weeks demand a response that reaches beyond the scene of Monday’s shooting. The recent attack in Calabar and the reported attack on a campaign convoy in Igueben, Edo, warrant close attention as well. In Rivers, three council secretariats were set ablaze after the October 2024 local government elections, a reminder that election security must extend beyond polling day.

Lagos, Enugu and Ebonyi show the importance of acting on recurring warnings. The attack in Oregun follows the intimidation documented in Lagos during the 2023 polls, when ethnic rhetoric intensified ahead of the state elections. CDD recorded fatal campaign attacks in Enugu and Ebonyi in October. EU observers had already identified both states, alongside Imo, as particularly volatile during the 2023 election period.

Kaduna, Kano and Katsina also merit close monitoring. Kaduna recorded the highest number of incidents among the locations highlighted by peace accord monitors. EU observers documented repeated attacks on campaigns in Kano in 2023, and CDD reported an attack on vehicles carrying party supporters in Malumfashi, Katsina, in October. In conflict-affected parts of Benue, Plateau, Taraba and the North East, armed violence and displacement pose an additional challenge. Even where campaigning is peaceful, people may struggle to check the register or reach a polling centre. These risks need to be assessed locally and updated as conditions change.

What Must Happen Before January

The police must account publicly for the Uduere investigation. Governor Sheriff Oborevwori has directed security agencies to apprehend those responsible, and the police have promised an impartial inquiry. The public should receive regular updates that protect witnesses and preserve the integrity of the case. Investigators should establish who fired, how officers responded and whether the evidence points to anyone who organised or financed the violence. The families deserve answers that will stand up in court.

INEC and the security agencies should explain how they will protect participation. In areas with repeated incidents, police commands should give campaigns, journalists and observers a clear way to report threats and explain how they respond. The same standards should apply to a governing party rally and an opposition town hall. INEC should also tell eligible displaced voters where they can vote, explain what happens if polling is disrupted by violence, and communicate changes quickly through local radio and other channels people use. Protection must continue through collation and the announcement of results.

Political parties must answer for how they conduct their campaigns. The National Peace Committee should publish verified breaches and intervene early when tensions rise. Party leaders should cooperate with investigators, discipline members where evidence establishes wrongdoing and condemn intimidation by their own supporters as promptly as they condemn attacks on their campaigns. Newsrooms have a duty too. We must verify footage before airing it, attribute allegations carefully and follow investigations after the first headlines have faded.

The first test is in Delta. The families in Uduere deserve to know what happened and who will answer for it. The rest of the country deserves to see, before January, what the authorities have done to prevent a recurrence. Nigerians should go to the polls thinking about whom to vote for, secure in the knowledge that they can get there, cast their ballot and come home safely.

The post After The Delta Killings, Nigeria Must Heed The Warning Signs appeared first on Channels Television.

content:
Veteran Nollywood actor and Nigerian film legend, Pete Edochie, has reportedly died at the age of 79 following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer.

The celebrated actor reportedly passed away at 12:30 a.m. on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, in Enugu, according to an announcement by his family.

The family confirmed his death in a statement shared on Instagram by his son, Leo Pete Edochie, who described the late actor as “our beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman”.

Accompanying the announcement was the emotional caption, “An Iroko Has Fallen.”

“With profound sadness and hearts bowed in total submission to the will of Almighty God, we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman, Chief Dr Pete EDOCHIE, MON (Ononenyi), a retired broadcaster and veteran Actor,” the statement read.

Edochie “departed this life on Wednesday, 25th November 2026 at 12.30a.m. after a protracted battle with prostate cancer in Enugu, Nigeria. He was aged 79 years.

“Chief Dr Pete EDOCHIE hailed from Akamnato Ifite Nteje and is survived by his beloved wife, Barrister Mrs Josephine Edochie, his children, siblings and numerous other relations.

“Funeral arrangements will be announced in due course.

“As we mourn this painful loss, we pray that Almighty God grants his gentle soul eternal rest and gives the entire family the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss.

“May God be with us all at this trying time,” added.

Biography

Pete Edochie was born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State. His hailed from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, in Anambra State.

He attended St Patrick’s and St James Primary Schools in Zaria; then St John’s College, Kaduna.

Late Edochie studied journalism and television at the School of Journalism and Television in England.

He joined the Eastern Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation in 1967 as a junior programmes assistant. He rose through the ranks. He became Director of Programmes at the Anambra Broadcasting Service, then served as Deputy Managing Director, while occasionally acting as Managing Director.

Things Fall Apart

When the Nigerian Television Authority, NTA, adapted Chinua Achebe’s “Things Fall Apart” into a movie in 1987, Edochie’s portrayal of the protagonist Okonkwo, made him a household name in entertainment and established him as one of Nigeria’s leading actors.

He has featured in many Nollywood movies, and won several awards.

content:
The Kebbi State Police Command has arrested a 30-year-old man, Tapro Tareza, for allegedly exhuming a corpse at Machika Cemetery in Ribah, Kebbi State.

The suspect was reportedly caught digging into a grave on November 10, shortly after the burial of a deceased person, following earlier reports of grave vandalism at the cemetery.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, the state Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman, said the police had mounted surveillance at the cemetery in collaboration with youths in the community to apprehend the suspected perpetrator.

“On 10th November 2026, at about 1915hrs, shortly after the burial of a newly deceased person, the suspect was caught digging into the grave.

“He was immediately apprehended by the vigilant youths, who promptly alerted the police,” the statement read.

The police said preliminary investigations revealed that the suspect allegedly removed items from the bodies of deceased persons.

The police said investigations were ongoing to establish the full circumstances surrounding the incidents and ensure that the suspect faced appropriate legal action.
