title: South-East governors working for my re-election — Tinubu
description:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru



ABUJA — AHEAD of the January 16 presidential election, President Bola Tinubu, on Monday, told the Igbo community and their leaders, in Lagos, that all the South-East governors are with him on the journey to make Nigeria a better place and are working for his re-election.
content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA — AHEAD of the January 16 presidential election, President Bola Tinubu, on Monday, told the Igbo community and their leaders, in Lagos, that all the South-East governors are with him on the journey to make Nigeria a better place and are working for his re-election.

The President said he was excited and that he would go home happy and eat because of their endorsement of his second term.

He thanked the Igbo communities and business leaders in Lagos for their resolve to support his re-election on January 16, 2027. He assured them of his administration’s commitment to inclusive governance, national unity and equity for all Nigerians.

President Tinubu gave the assurance while addressing youths, elders, and Ndigbo leaders during a town hall meeting organised by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiatives at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts, Iganmu, Lagos State.

He called on Ndigbo to strengthen their unity, deepen their participation in national politics, and work with other ethnic groups to build a peaceful, prosperous and united Nigeria.

To reaffirm his commitment to national unity, President Tinubu joined the gathering to sing the national anthem a second time.

“I didn’t believe you would turn out this many; I am very, very happy. May God bless you, and may God continue to guide and bless our country.

“It is a great honour for me to be here before you as your president. I can commit to one thing: the unity of Nigeria.

“Though tribes and tongues may differ, we stand in brotherhood. None of us told God where we would be born or what language we would speak when we were born.

“Whether you are Igbo or Hausa, you have no control over yourself. God created you and created that opportunity. We are all Nigerians.

“Let’s see ourselves as individuals living in the same house geographically called Nigeria,” the President told the gathering.

A statement by the presidential spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, said: “President Tinubu told the gathering that all the South-East governors are with him on the journey to make Nigeria a better place and are working for his re-election.”

He mentioned Chief Chidi Anyaegbu, owner of Chisco Motors; Dave Umahi; Doris Uzoka-Anite; and Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, who were at the gathering, as people with whom he has close connections.

On his part, the host Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, appealed to Ndigbo to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, assuring the President of massive votes from the state in the January 16, 2027, presidential election.

Sanwo-Olu described the turnout of Igbo leaders, traders and business owners as proof that Lagos residents were united behind the President, despite the meeting being held on a Monday, when many participants had to leave their businesses to attend.

In her remarks, the convener of the meeting and Minister of State for Budget and Economic Planning, Dr. Doris Uzoka-Anite, declared the Igbo community’s commitment in Lagos State to supporting President Tinubu’s re-election bid, saying the community had resolved to unite behind his leadership.

She said that Ndigbo had commenced grassroots mobilisation across Lagos State, with structures established at the polling-unit level ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

Also speaking, the former Minister of State for Labour and Employment, Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, assured President Bola Tinubu of Ndigbo’s support for his 2027 re-election bid, saying the gathering of Igbo leaders and stakeholders in Lagos demonstrated their unity and commitment to the President.

She said the community had recognised the importance of building political alliances with other geo-political zones to achieve its future presidential ambition.

The leader of the Ndigbo Traders Association in Lagos, Prince Tony Nwakeze, pledged the members’ support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, while appealing for access to loans at a 5 per cent interest rate to help traders transition from importation to local manufacturing.

Nwakeze said traders from Alaba, Trade Fair and Ladipo markets were seeking financial support to empower young people and expand their businesses.

He also assured the President that traders were prepared to organise themselves and adopt a cross-guarantee arrangement to ensure repayment of any loans granted to their members.

“We, the market people, will stand with you, support you and honour every agreement we enter into today,” he said.

title: The organic restructing  of Nigeria
description: The unity, social cohesion and structural stability of the Nigerian federation are conditions precedent for its economic growth and development. There has to be a Nigerian nation before any form of progress can be achieved. Nigeria is a country of a collection of micro ethno-geographic nationalities
content:
The unity, social cohesion and structural stability of the Nigerian federation are conditions precedent for its economic growth and development. There has to be a Nigerian nation before any form of progress can be achieved. Nigeria is a country of a collection of micro ethno-geographic nationalities whose localized interests are placed above that of the broad collective. The Nigerian populace are also more of ‘indigenes’ of these micro-ethnic nationalities than ‘citizens’ of Nigeria.

It has been argued that the diversity of the Nigerian people, which was compounded by the colonial experiment of forging a modern nation out of a critical mass of diverse indigenous peoples of uncommon history, tradition and culture is responsible for our disunity as a nation. This notion of Nigeria being an amalgam of cultural incompatibles that has become an entrenched narrative that justifies our disunity is a fallacy that is not supported by any shred of historical evidence and actually goes contrary to the logic of common sense.

Diversity is a measure of racial mix within a given geographic space and NOT the ethnic composition within a broad racial categorization. Therefore, a mono-racial [black] country such Nigeria does NOT qualify to be regarded as a diverse country on account of ethnic differences. Nigeria does not have much in common with racially diverse countries like the United States of America and the Republic of South Africa but has so much in common with less diverse mono-racial [Mongoloid] China and mono-racial [Caucasoid] United Kingdom of old. Like Nigeria, China has between 55 and 95 ethnic identifications within its broad Mongoloid mono-racial classification. They include the Uygur, Hui, Zhuang and the majority Han Chinese people. Mandarin, which is a language spoken by the majority Han Chinese people, originally evolved from closely related languages spoken by ‘diverse’ ethnic groups around the agricultural settlements of  the four cardinal points of China. Similarly, the multi-ethnic identification that characterises mono-racial Nigeria actually evolved from a common source as clearly discernable in the close similarities in culture, language and interwoven ancestral history of the various peoples of Nigeria from the four cardinal points of its current geographic space and beyond. In this circumstance, Nigeria is best described as a plural, but not a diverse, country.

Recall that the implosion of the Kwararafa confederacy several centuries ago ignited a wave of southward migrations from the fringes of old Kanem Borno Empire into the Benue valley. The Kwararafa is largely made up of groups who are regarded as “Banza bokwoi” who, nevertheless, shared a common patriarchy with the original seven Hausa states. One of such groups that migrated out of Kwararafa was the Igala. The Igala, who are closely related to the original Hausa states of Sahel Nigeria, migrated deep into the south of Nigeria and established a settlement on the banks of the great River Niger at a place called Idah. From their original base in Idah, a detachment of the Igala crossed the great River Niger and eventually joined a party of migrants out of the Benin Empire [a sub-group of the larger Yoruba of Western Nigeria] in a seamless form of cultural assimilation and integration. This party of Igala fused with the Bini migrants to establish the various Igbo-speaking communities of Isele-Uku, Agbor, Ogwashi-Uku and Asaba, in the Mid-West of Nigeria and Onitsha, Obosi, Ogbaru and Ugwuta in the eastern heartland of Nigeria, thus serving as a source of cultural linkage between the plural peoples of pre-colonial Nigeria. 

The British majority Caucasoid population, like the Chinese Mongoloid and Nigerian Negro populations, can similarly be classified into smaller ethnic groupings. Former British Prime ministers Benjamin Disraeli and Winston Churchill identified as Jewish [Middle Eastern origin] and Huguenot [French Protestant origin], respectively. Queen Elizabeth II of England was of Germanic ethnicity, while her successors are of Greek ancestry. The differences between Nigerians on one hand and the Chinese and British on the other hand is that they elevated their racial similarities and shared geographic reality [citizenship] above their petty man-made ethno-geographic differences in local origin [indigene ship] while we have put the latter ahead of the former in Nigeria. Like Queen Elizabeth II, Benjamin Disraeli and Winston Churchill that are broadly categorised as White and British, Ahmadu Bello, Nnamdi Azikiwe and Obafemi Awolowo are similarly Black and Nigerian. By putting our Nigerian citizenship above our individual ethno-geographic indigeneship, a pan-Nigerian consensus will be achieved that will allow time-tested economic models to work for us as a nation.   

To substitute the opium of sectionalism with the nourishment of nationalism, there will be a need for Nigeria’s political leadership to begin the process of mobilizing Nigerians to evolve the new political culture of aligning their individual economies with their democratic choices away from ethno-geographic and religious sentiments. As one people, shoemakers and garment workers of Aba, Sokoto and Ilesha will be mobilized to align their democratic choices with candidates whose economic policies hold prospects of higher productivity and increased individual prosperity, away from the culture of voting along ethnic and religious lines. 

Similarly, farmers in Jega, Agatu, Onitsha Ugbo and Owo will be mobilized to align their democratic choices with candidates whose policies hold bright prospects of higher yield of agro-produce with resultant increase in individual prosperity. If this process is successfully carried through all facets of Nigeria’s socio-economic polity, there will emerge from this political culture a people’s [proletarian] consensus to check the divisive tendencies of the existing elite [bourgeoisie] tactics of divide and rule. A proper aligning of individual business interests with democratic choices across board will birth the seamless convergence of politics and economy. This seamless convergence of politics and economics, emerging from a proper aligning of individual business interests with democratic choices by Nigerians will create a new democratic demography of competing pragmatic socio-economic ideas in contrast to the current democratic demography of ethno-geographic and religious struggle for supremacy. The competition of pragmatic economic ideas as the fundamentals of politics in Nigeria will birth the era of politics of ideology with political parties coalescing around clearly defined socio-economic ideological leanings. This process will throw up a democratic governance structure that is elected by a majority of people from plural backgrounds that are united by a set of socio-economic ideas, away from the existing majority of shared ethno-geographic and religious affiliation. 

Under this broad pan-Nigerian framework, the various federating units at the subnational level will transform from largely micro ethno-geographic and religious nationalities created with the sole political intention to partake in the sharing of Nigeria’s oil mineral revenues [National cake] into an all-inclusive geo- economic hub of wealth creation brought about by the freed energy of all Nigerians with additional prospects of increasing the national cake. Nigerians who were born in a particular ethno-geographic enclave will freely find their bearings by following their natural economic callings in line with their passions, talents and endowments and find affinity with like-mind Nigerians in any of the numerous economic hubs. For example, a young Nigerian who was born in Onitsha and identifies as Igbo may not necessary have trading as his natural economic calling. He may be drawn to cattle breeding as an occupation. His citizenship allows him to move to Sokoto or any other cattle-breeding hub to successfully pursue his economic goals in life. Similarly, a young Nigerian who was born in Kano and identifies as Fulani may not necessarily be inclined towards cattle breeding. If garment and shoemaking is his/her natural calling, then his/her Nigerian citizenship should allow an economic space in the industrial town of Aba. The same applies to a Kanuri from Borno who decides to pursue a career in marine transportation in the creeks of the Niger Delta or an Ijaw whose calling is not a fisherman in the waters of the delta but as cap weaver in Borno. 

If this process of systematic assimilation and integration of Nigerians from plural backgrounds into geo-economic zones becomes entrenched, the lon-term implication is that the Nigerian federation would have undergone a process of organic restructuring.

The commercial cities of Aba and Onitsha will no longer be enclaves of Igbo traders but that of Nigerian entrepreneurs. Cattle breeding will no longer be Fulani but Nigerian, the mastery of the creeks of the Niger Delta will no longer be an ‘Ijaw’ exclusive but inclusive of all Nigerians and the tanneries of Kano will become a Nigerian cultural economic heritage. Most importantly, the 13 per cent derivation from oil mineral resources payable to oil-rich Bayelsa State will no longer be considered an exclusive ‘Ijaw’ privilege but benefits to Nigerians [Kanuri, Fulani, Yoruba, etc.] for whom Bayelsa is home. Similarly, the 44 local governments areas of Kano State would no longer be considered as a structural advantage of the ‘Hausa/Fulani’ but structural benefits for Nigerians [Ijaw, Igbo, Bini etc] for whom Kano is home.

The post The organic restructing of Nigeria appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Bellingham beauty in Real Madrid win; Arsenal, Man City held in Champions League
description:
Jude Bellingham scored one of the goals of the season as Real Madrid hammered PSV Eindhoven 5-1 on Tuesday to maintain their perfect record in this season’s Champions League, while Arsenal and Manchester City were both held to draws at home.



Elsewhere, debutants Como and Real Betis continued thei
content:
Jude Bellingham scored one of the goals of the season as Real Madrid hammered PSV Eindhoven 5-1 on Tuesday to maintain their perfect record in this season’s Champions League, while Arsenal and Manchester City were both held to draws at home.

Elsewhere, debutants Como and Real Betis continued their excellent form since the start of the league phase, but Aston Villa slumped to another defeat on their travels.

Record 15-time European champions Real had to come from behind to beat PSV at the Bernabeu as they made it five wins from five in this season’s league phase to go clear at the top of the standings with 15 points.

Dutch champions PSV led at half-time courtesy of an Ivan Perisic penalty, but Federico Valverde equalised five minutes after the restart.

Bellingham then put Real ahead on the hour with a remarkable strike, as he controlled a Kylian Mbappe lay-off outside the box and then teed himself up for a sweet volley on the outside of his right boot which flew into the corner of the net.

Mbappe then scored twice to move to 19 goals in all competitions this season and 76 career Champions League goals. The France captain now has 105 Real Madrid goals, one more than the Brazilian Ronaldo managed for the club.

Vinicius Junior sealed the win for Jose Mourinho’s side, who have now claimed 10 consecutive victories in all competitions.

“That one was a nice one, it popped up for me nicely and then I just hit it. I thought I would go with the outside of the boot a little bit, stab it a little bit, I am not one for smashing the ball too hard. It was a nice moment,” England star Bellingham told British broadcaster TNT Sports about his goal.

Reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain can join Real at the top of the standings if they beat Roma on Wednesday, but Como and Betis are currently level with the French side on 12 points after they beat AEK Athens and Slovan Bratislava respectively.

Como and Betis flying

Luis Milla scored as Como beat AEK 1-0 in Italy after Lucas Da Cunha earlier squandered a penalty, while Cucho Hernandez grabbed both goals for Betis in their 2-0 victory in Slovakia.

Arsenal had to settle for a point after drawing 1-1 with Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium, as Viktor Gyokeres put the Gunners ahead but later missed a golden chance to win the game.

Gyokeres opened the scoring with a thunderous strike, but Maximilian Beier equalised for Dortmund and the Arsenal striker headed woefully wide from Martin Odegaard’s cross late on.

It is the second time Arsenal, last season’s beaten finalists, have dropped points to German opposition this season following a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich.

Manchester City are in the midst of a poor run of form in the Premier League and Enzo Maresca’s side had to come from behind twice in the second half to draw 2-2 against Napoli.

Rasmus Hojlund, formerly of Manchester United, gave the Italians the lead early in the second half only for Ayyoub Bouaddi to equalise.

Kevin De Bruyne was returning to face his former side and he saw his Napoli team retake the lead through Noa Lang in the 76th minute, but Rayan Cherki’s fine late goal earned City a point.

City won 10 of their first 11 games this season under Maresca. But the wheels have come off in the wake of the club being found guilty of widespread breaches of Premier League financial rules.

Aston Villa lose

“We don’t like these moments – we want to win games – but unfortunately this moment is like this,” said Maresca, ahead of a trip to Premier League champions Arsenal on Sunday.

None of the Premier League’s representatives in the competition won on Tuesday, with Villa losing 1-0 to Galatasaray in Istanbul as Deniz Gul scored the only goal of the game late on. The two clubs are now level on nine points in the standings.

Portuguese champions Porto won 1-0 at Feyenoord thanks to Oussama Targhalline’s early own-goal, while Antonio Nusa netted twice as RB Leipzig beat Lens 3-1 — that was a fourth straight Champions League loss for the French team.

A stoppage-time own-goal gave Bodo/Glimt a 1-0 victory against Austria’s LASK in Norway.

Vanguard News

title: We have a workable blueprint to take Zamfara to greater heights – Governor Lawal
description:
Governor Dauda Lawal said the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) has the blueprint to address all pending socio-economic and infrastructural issues in Zamfara State.



The governor disclosed this on Monday during the launch of the APC Presidential and Gubernatorial Campaign for the 2027 general
content:
Governor Dauda Lawal said the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) has the blueprint to address all pending socio-economic and infrastructural issues in Zamfara State.

The governor disclosed this on Monday during the launch of the APC Presidential and Gubernatorial Campaign for the 2027 general elections in Talata Mafara, Zamfara State.

“We have a workable blueprint, as you all can testify to, and I will continue to do more if re-elected as the governor of Zamfara State,” the governor said to a rousing applause of thousands of supporters at the rally.

In his remarks at the rally, Governor Lawal expressed satisfaction with the turnout and gratitude to the people of Talata Mafara for the grand reception.

He highlighted key projects implemented by his administration in the Talata Mafara Local Government Area.

He said, “I am here today to flag off the Presidential and Gubernatorial campaign of the APC, seeking your votes for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and for myself as your governor.

“I am also here to seek your support to vote for the APC from top to bottom. And from what we have seen today, I am sure that Mafara is for the APC.

“I have executed more than 40 projects in Talata Mafara LGA, which include the total rebuilding and equipping of the General Hospital, and many other projects in the State University.”

Governor Lawal assured supporters of his administration’s resolve to build infrastructure and address all other basic human and socio-economic challenges facing the state.

He also appealed to the youths, women and all other supporters to vote for the APC candidates from the president to the state house of assembly in the state

The Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, said he was overwhelmed by the unprecedented crowd of supporters who graced the event.

Senator Yari appealed to the APC supporters to vote for President Bola Tinubu, Governor Lawal and all other candidates of the party in the 2027 general elections.

The city of Mafara was agog during the campaign rally held at the main Eid Ground in the Talata Mafara Local Government Area.

The rally brought together major APC stakeholders in the state, including Mr Yari, and former governors Ahmad Sani Yarima and Mahmud Aliyu Shinkafi, among others.

The party’s stakeholders were welcomed by thousands of APC members and supporters, attesting to Governor Lawal’s popularity in the state.

title: Tinubu seeks reduction of 2026 budget to N65.176trn; Senate approves N10.79trn loan
description:
By Henry Umoru



ABUJA—THE Senate has begun a repeal and re-enactment of the 2026 budget, with President Bola Tinubu presenting a proposal to reduce government expenditure and realign the appropriation with available resources and existing obligations.



With the Senate fast-tracking the considera
content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA—THE Senate has begun a repeal and re-enactment of the 2026 budget, with President Bola Tinubu presenting a proposal to reduce government expenditure and realign the appropriation with available resources and existing obligations.

With the Senate fast-tracking the consideration of the President’s revised 2026 Appropriation Bill, it then scaled second reading in the Senate which approved an additional N10.79 trillion external borrowing to finance the budget deficit.

The revised appropriation proposal reduces the 2026 budget from the N68.3 trillion originally approved by the National Assembly to N66.1 trillion, while retaining the N31.4 trillion deficit and the N29.2 trillion borrowing plan.

The revised proposal, tagged “ Transmission of FGN 2026 Appropriation Repeal and Enactment bill and Revised 2026 Federal Government Fiscal Framework “ was presented by the President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio.

He said the proposal aligned with the 2026 budget in terms of existing obligations and available resources.

According to Tinubu, under the revised framework, aggregate expenditure is projected at N65.176 trillion, compared with N68.3 trillion in the approved budget.

Other highlights, as stated by the President in the request, include the fact that projected federal government revenue, including revenue from government-owned enterprises, stands at N33.7 trillion, while aggregate capital expenditure is N26.2 trillion.

Tinubu, who noted that the fiscal deficit remained unchanged at N31.4 trillion, equivalent to 5.6 per cent of GDP, said: These adjustments prioritise existing commitments and improve the credibility and execution of the capital budget while maintaining fiscal discipline.

“Planned new borrowing also remains at N29.2 trillion, comprising N18.4 trillion in domestic borrowing and N10.7 trillion in foreign borrowing.

“The proposed $7.7 billion in external borrowing, equivalent to approximately N10.3 trillion at an exchange rate of N1,346.5 to one US dollar, is intended to finance existing foreign borrowing provisions and does not increase the borrowing envelope.’’

He said the adjustments were intended to prioritise existing commitments, strengthen the credibility of the budget and improve capital budget implementation, while maintaining fiscal discipline.

The president’s request read: “The proposal aligns the 2026 budget with existing obligations and available resources. It regularises some NNPCL expenditures incurred on behalf of the federation, addresses under-provided debt service obligations, recognises issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments, and provides for reforms to ministries, departments and agencies and social accounts.’’

To quicken the process, the Upper Chamber temporarily suspended its rules, considered the presidential request and after scaling second reading, it was referred to the Committee on Appropriations, led by Senator Olamilekan Adeola, APC, Ogun West.

The Senate subsequently adjourned plenary until December 1 to enable the committee complete its work and present its report.

In his remarks, the Senate president, Godswill Akpabio, urged senators, particularly members of the appropriations committee, to suspend their campaign activities and concentrate on the urgent legislative assignment.

The decision was sequel to a motion by the Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, APC, Ekiti Central, who sought the cooperation of his colleagues for the accelerated consideration of the presidential request after a closed-door session lasting about 30 minutes.

Bamidele argued that the urgency of the revised budget required expeditious legislative action to enable the federal government address outstanding fiscal obligations and implement the appropriation before the expiration of the 2026 financial year on December 31.

In his lead debate on the revised budget, Bamidele said revision provided an opportunity to strengthen budget credibility by prioritising ongoing projects, setting legitimate outstanding obligations, and avoiding the proliferation of new projects at the expense of existing commitments.

“ I strongly believe that completing existing projects will provide greater economic value than continually commencing new ones without guaranteeing their completion,’’ he said.

Supporting the bill, Chairman of the Senate Committee on Appropriations, Solomon Adeola, said the proposed review was an effort to reposition the budget to make it more effective and efficient.

He assured the Senate that his committee would submit its report within one week, prompting Akpabio to consider suspending plenary to enable the 73-member committee concentrate on the assignment.

Senator Garba Maidoki, who supported the review, appealed for adequate funding of constituency projects and ongoing infrastructure interventions in rural communities.

title: Pete Edochie: Life, career and legacy of a Nollywood legend
description: Veteran Nigerian actor and broadcaster, Chief Pete Edochie, who died on Wednesday at the age of 79, was one of Nollywood’s most recognisable faces, celebrated for his commanding screen presence, distinctive voice, rich repertoire of African proverbs and portrayal of traditional rulers and family pat
content:
Veteran Nigerian actor and broadcaster, Chief Pete Edochie, who died on Wednesday at the age of 79, was one of Nollywood’s most recognisable faces, celebrated for his commanding screen presence, distinctive voice, rich repertoire of African proverbs and portrayal of traditional rulers and family patriarchs.

Edochie died at 12:30 am in Enugu following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer, according to a statement signed by his son, Leo Pete Edochie, on behalf of the family.

The actor’s death came on the same day an interview he granted Ugo Nwokolo TV was scheduled for release.

His last interview

An excerpt from the interview was shared on social media on Sunday, November 22.

The full episode was scheduled for release on Wednesday, November 25, according to a report published by PUNCH on Monday.

During the interview, the veteran actor spoke about the controversy surrounding his son, Yul Edochie’s decision to marry actress, Judy Austin, as his second wife.

Defending his son against public criticism, Edochie described him as a strong person who had remained undeterred by the backlash.

“Look at my son, Yul. Yul is a very tough guy. You can never subdue him, no matter how much you try,” he said.

He also praised Yul for not publicly speaking ill of his first wife, May Edochie, despite the controversy surrounding their marriage.

The interview attracted attention following the circulation of excerpts in which the actor discussed the impact of the controversy on his son’s career and public image.

Early life and education

Born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State, Edochie hailed from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, in Anambra State.

He attended St Patrick’s and St James Primary Schools in Zaria before proceeding to St John’s College, Kaduna. He also studied journalism and television at the School of Journalism and Television in England.

Career in broadcasting

Before becoming a household name in the Nigerian film industry, Edochie built a career in broadcasting.

He joined the Eastern Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation in 1967 as a junior programmes assistant and gradually rose through the ranks.

He eventually became Director of Programmes at the Anambra Broadcasting Service, where he also served as Deputy Managing Director and occasionally acted as Managing Director.

In a 2022 interview with Vanguard, Edochie recalled his years in broadcasting and spoke about presenting a classical music programme titled Music from the Masters.

Breakthrough with Things Fall Apart

Edochie’s breakthrough as an actor came through his portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s acclaimed novel, Things Fall Apart.

His performance as the respected but deeply troubled Igbo warrior earned him widespread recognition and established him as one of Nigeria’s leading television actors.

The role attracted international attention, with the British Broadcasting Corporation sending a delegation to interview him about his portrayal.

In a 2023 interview with The Nation, Edochie recalled that his performance had received international recognition even before the Nigerian movie industry became widely known as Nollywood.

Notable films and acting career

Following his success in Things Fall Apart, Edochie featured in numerous Nigerian films and television productions.

Some of his notable works include Igodo, Rituals, Billionaire’s Club and Genevieve Nnaji’s 2018 film Lionheart, in which he played Chief Ernest Obiagu.

He became particularly associated with roles as traditional rulers, wealthy businessmen and authoritative family patriarchs.

His deep voice, measured delivery and frequent use of traditional expressions and proverbs became distinctive features of his performances.

Awards and recognition

Edochie’s contributions to Nigerian entertainment earned him several honours during his career.

In 2003, he received the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) from former President Olusegun Obasanjo.

He also received the Industry Merit Award from Africa Magic and a Lifetime Achievement Award from the Africa Film Academy.

In 2020, he was honoured with the African Film Legend Award at the African Film Festival.

Marriage and family

Edochie was married to Barrister Josephine Edochie, with whom he had six children, including actors Yul and Linc Edochie.

His family life occasionally attracted public attention, particularly following controversies surrounding his son Yul’s marriage to actress Judy Austin and the resulting public disagreements involving his first wife, May Edochie.

Legacy

With a career spanning broadcasting, television and film, Edochie remained one of the most recognisable veteran actors in Nigeria.

His portrayal of Okonkwo in Things Fall Apart remains among his most memorable performances, while his subsequent roles helped establish him as a defining presence in Nollywood.

The post Pete Edochie: Life, career and legacy of a Nollywood legend appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: IGP reads riot act over political violence
description:
• Vows political office, influence won’t shield offenders    • INEC warns against turning campaigns into battlefield 
• NDC boycotts security meeting, seeks international intervention

From Molly Kilete and Adesuwa Tsan, Abuja
Alarmed by the escalating wave of political violence, killings, intimidat
content:
• Vows political office, influence won’t shield offenders    • INEC warns against turning campaigns into battlefield 

• NDC boycotts security meeting, seeks international intervention

From Molly Kilete and Adesuwa Tsan, Abuja

Alarmed by the escalating wave of political violence, killings, intimidation and attacks on opposition figures ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, yesterday read the riot act to the political class, vowing to investigate and prosecute politicians who recruit, finance and deploy thugs to unleash violence on their opponents, irrespective of their political offices, affiliations or influence.

Disu, who declared that the Force would no longer fold its arms and allow politicians and their supporters to take the law into their own hands, warned that no political ambition was worth the life of any Nigerian and no electoral victory justified the destruction of national peace.

The warning came as Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, raised the alarm over persistent violations of electoral laws by political actors, warning that growing incidents of violence, intimidation and attacks on citizens and members of political parties threatened the credibility of the forthcoming elections.

However, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) boycotted the high-level security meeting convened by the IGP, accusing the police and other security agencies of complicity in attacks on its members allegedly perpetrated by thugs loyal to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), and calling for international intervention to safeguard democratic participation in Nigeria.

Speaking at the security meeting held at the Force Headquarters, Abuja, which brought together national chairmen, secretaries and executives of registered political parties, representatives of security agencies, civil society organisations, INEC officials and other stakeholders, Disu expressed concern over the increasing incidents of violent clashes among political supporters, attacks on campaign venues, intimidation of political opponents, use of dangerous weapons and disruption of lawful political gatherings.

He warned that such developments endangered innocent lives, threatened public peace and undermined confidence in democratic institutions.

Declaring zero tolerance for political violence, irrespective of the parties, candidates or individuals involved, the IGP assured political parties and their supporters of adequate protection to exercise their democratic rights, including organising rallies, holding meetings and expressing their political preferences without fear or intimidation.

“Our neutrality in the political process is non-negotiable. We owe allegiance to the Constitution, the law and the Nigerian people, not any political party or individual,” he said.

Disu warned that the recruitment, financing and deployment of political thugs, threats of violence, attacks on electoral officials and destruction of electoral materials would attract appropriate law enforcement action, insisting that political office, party affiliation and personal influence would not place anyone above the law.He assured Nigerians that offenders would be professionally investigated and prosecuted in accordance with due process, while every political party and candidate would be accorded equal treatment under the law.

Beyond the responsibilities of security agencies, the IGP charged political party leaders to take responsibility for the conduct of their candidates, youth wings and supporters, urging national chairmen to issue clear directives against violence and ensure compliance across their party structures.

He also called on national secretaries to facilitate effective communication and ensure compliance with applicable electoral notification requirements, while urging youth leaders to mobilise young people for constructive democratic participation rather than expose them to manipulation and political violence.

Disu stressed that peaceful political competition remained essential to democratic development, urging stakeholders to place the lives of Nigerians and the stability of the country above partisan interests.

•INEC raises alarm over electoral law violations

Amupitan, who described the growing incidents of political violence and violations of electoral laws as worrisome, warned politicians against turning electioneering into a battlefield, urging them to concentrate on presenting their manifestos, policies and ideas to Nigerians rather than resorting to violence and intimidation in their quest for power.

The INEC chairman said strict compliance with electoral laws and procedures had become imperative as political activities intensified ahead of the 2027 general elections, stressing that the credibility of the polls depended not only on the integrity of the voting process but also on the political environment in which campaigns and other electoral activities were conducted.

Recalling his earlier engagement with political party leaders and members of the National Peace Committee on August 18, 2026, where he emphasised the need for peaceful political competition, Amupitan warned that when political actors could no longer freely assemble, organise campaigns or express their views without fear of intimidation, the democratic process was already being undermined before election day.

He noted that persistent attacks on political party members and other citizens could discourage voter participation and weaken public confidence in the electoral process, urging political stakeholders to operate within the boundaries established by the Constitution and electoral laws.

Amupitan reminded politicians and their supporters that the people whose votes they sought were the ultimate holders of sovereign power under the Constitution and that all stakeholders had a responsibility to protect their rights, security and welfare.

•NDC accuses police of partisanship

Despite Disu’s assurances of neutrality and equal protection for political parties, the NDC said its decision to boycott the security meeting followed repeated attacks on its members across the country and the alleged failure of security agencies to apprehend and prosecute those responsible.

In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, the party accused the police of abandoning their constitutional responsibility to protect all Nigerians, irrespective of their political affiliations.

“We no longer feel safe and protected by a Police Force that watches helplessly the slaughter of our members across the country by hired thugs of the ruling APC. We will not lend legitimacy to a process that has failed to protect us,” it said.

The party cited incidents in Benue, Edo, Cross River, Enugu and Delta states, alleging that its members had come under sustained attacks and that political campaigns were increasingly being characterised by violence and intimidation.

It particularly recalled the alleged prevention of its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, from entering Benue State by thugs loyal to the APC government and the reported killing of four of its members in Delta State.

“The killing of four members of the NDC in Delta State was done in the full glare of the Police and security forces who were supposed to protect all Nigerians,” the party alleged.

Accusing the police of partisan conduct, the NDC declared that the Nigeria Police Force had become an “APC Police sustained by taxpayers’ money”. It also faulted the police over what it described as their inability to conduct proper investigations into attacks on opposition politicians and ensure that perpetrators were brought to justice.

The party called on the international community to prevail on President Bola Tinubu and the APC-led government to uphold democratic standards, warning that democracy could not survive in an atmosphere where opposition members were attacked and killed with impunity.

“The NDC remains committed to peaceful, issue-based campaigns, but we will not be intimidated, silenced, or chased out of the democratic space,” it added.

The allegations have not been independently verified. Although Disu reaffirmed the neutrality of the police, his reported remarks at the security meeting did not specifically address the NDC’s wider accusations.

•Mounting concerns over political violence

The security meeting came against the backdrop of growing incidents of political violence across the country, with attacks on campaign rallies, political gatherings, candidates and their supporters heightening apprehension over the conduct of the forthcoming elections.

President Bola Tinubu had, on November 13, condemned the growing incidents of campaign violence and directed security agencies to deal firmly with perpetrators, irrespective of their political affiliations.

Similarly, the Senate, last week, called for investigations into attacks on political actors and urged INEC to enforce relevant provisions of the Electoral Act against perpetrators of political violence.

The upper legislative chamber also urged state governors to desist from denying opposition political parties access to public facilities for campaigns and other legitimate political activities.

The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) had also given INEC seven days to initiate the prosecution of suspected perpetrators of electoral violence against whom sufficient evidence existed or face legal action.

The post IGP reads riot act over political violence appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: 2027 Elections: NUC to shut varsities for 4 weeks, mobilises VCs for INEC
description:
By Joseph Erunke



ABUJA — The National Universities Commission, NUC, is considering a three-to-four-week adjustment of academic calendars across Nigerian universities to enable academics participate in the conduct of the 2027 general elections.



The move is part of a broader strategy by the comm
content:
By Joseph Erunke

ABUJA — The National Universities Commission, NUC, is considering a three-to-four-week adjustment of academic calendars across Nigerian universities to enable academics participate in the conduct of the 2027 general elections.

The move is part of a broader strategy by the commission to mobilise vice-chancellors and university authorities nationwide to provide credible, non-partisan academic personnel for the elections, particularly as Collation and Returning Officers.

NUC Executive Secretary, Prof. Abdullahi Yusufu Ribadu, disclosed this in Abuja when the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, led a delegation of national commissioners and senior officials on a courtesy visit to the commission Monday.

Ribadu said the NUC would engage vice-chancellors on the nomination of qualified academics for electoral assignments, adding that an online meeting would be convened to facilitate the process.

He also pledged to issue a formal circular to universities upon receiving an official request from INEC.

While stressing that the credibility of the 2027 elections would depend significantly on the integrity of personnel deployed to conduct them, Ribadu said: “Since we want to have credible elections, we also have to have credible personnel.’’

The NUC boss said the proposed adjustment of academic calendars would provide sufficient room for academics to discharge their electoral responsibilities without compromising students’ academic programmes.

According to him, the proposed break will not exceed four weeks, while the commission will consult university administrators to ensure that the arrangement does not disrupt academic activities or interfere with INEC’s electoral timetable.

“We will discuss with the vice-chancellors and have their calendars tweaked in such a way that it will not affect the elections, nor will it affect the studies of the students,” he sai

Ribadu further insisted that academics and other ad hoc officials engaged in the electoral process must demonstrate absolute neutrality, proposing that they be made to take an oath of neutrality before deployment.

Beyond providing election officials, the NUC executive secretary proposed a broader institutional partnership between universities and INEC, including student internship opportunities at the electoral commission, joint research initiatives and possible academic programmes in electoral studies.

Earlier in his remarks, INEC Chairman, Prof. Amupitan, said the visit was aimed at strengthening the existing partnership between the electoral commission and Nigerian universities, ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He acknowledged the critical role universities had played in previous elections, particularly through the deployment of vice-chancellors and other senior academics as Collation and Returning Officers.

Amupitan, however, said INEC was introducing far-reaching technological, operational and security reforms to strengthen the electoral process and guarantee the safety of academics and other personnel engaged in election duties.

On technological improvements, he disclosed that polling unit results recorded on Form EC8A would undergo automated arithmetic consistency and over-voting checks before transmission to INEC Result Viewing Portal, IReV.

He also announced the procurement of 57,000 additional Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS, machines, a development he said would reduce the voter-to-device ratio to 850 voters per machine.

On the security of electoral personnel, Amupitan disclosed that the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security, ICCES, had been decentralised to Local Government Areas and Registration Areas to strengthen security coordination at the grassroots.

He said dedicated security cordons and escort arrangements would also be provided around collation centres to protect election officials from intimidation and attacks.

The INEC chairman further cited provisions of the Electoral Act 2026 criminalising violence, abusive rhetoric and threats against electoral personnel, stressing that the commission had the powers to prosecute offenders.

“No Returning Officer or Collation Officer will be left to stand alone against lawlessness,” he assured.

title: Billboard controversy: Senator Kalu’s politics anchored in people, not billboards –Group
description: Reality Organisation has reacted to the removal of a billboard bearing the photographs of President Bola Tinubu, Senator Orji Uzor Kalu and Governor Alex Otti in Arochukwu Local Government Area of Abia State, dismissing suggestions of a political alliance among the three leaders and insisting that t
content:
Reality Organisation has reacted to the removal of a billboard bearing the photographs of President Bola Tinubu, Senator Orji Uzor Kalu and Governor Alex Otti in Arochukwu Local Government Area of Abia State, dismissing suggestions of a political alliance among the three leaders and insisting that the former Abia governor neither erected nor commissioned the billboard.

The organisation, which called on the Nigeria Police Force and the Department of State Services (DSS) to closely monitor actions and utterances capable of heightening political tension in the state ahead of the 2027 general elections, maintained that individuals had the democratic right to support candidates across political party lines without their preferences being interpreted as evidence of a formal political alliance.

In a statement signed by Dimgba Okereke yesterday, the organisation disclosed that the billboard was the independent initiative of an Arochukwu indigene identified as Emeka, who chose to publicly identify with the three political leaders.

“For the avoidance of doubt, Senator Orji Uzor Kalu neither erected nor commissioned the billboard. It was the independent initiative of Engr. Emeka, a well-known son of Arochukwu, who chose to express his support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Senator Orji Uzor Kalu and Governor Alex Otti.

“That is his personal choice and democratic right. His preference should not be misconstrued as evidence of a political alliance between the individuals or their respective political parties,” the organisation stated.

It maintained that Kalu’s political engagements over the decades had been anchored in grassroots mobilisation and direct interaction with the electorate rather than publicity materials.

“Senator Orji Uzor Kalu’s politics is anchored in the people, not billboards. For decades, he has maintained direct relationships with communities and ordinary citizens. His ongoing community-to-community engagements across Abia North are consistent with his longstanding approach to politics and representation.

“The OUK Movement and Reality Organisation have established grassroots structures built over several years through direct engagement with communities and voluntary participation by members and supporters.

“Senator Kalu cannot be held responsible for every independent expression of support by those who admire him. Neither can he be expected to stop individuals from expressing their political preferences within the confines of the law.”

While acknowledging the statutory responsibilities of advertising regulatory agencies, the organisation demanded fairness, transparency and political neutrality in the enforcement of advertising regulations, stressing that democracy thrived on freedom of choice, tolerance and respect for divergent political interests.

“Democracy is about the people and their freedom to make choices. A citizen’s decision to support candidates across political party lines does not necessarily amount to a formal political coalition.

“While we recognise the statutory responsibilities of advertising regulatory agencies, we expect such regulations to be applied fairly, transparently and without political discrimination.”

The organisation also urged its members and supporters to remain peaceful and resist any provocation while pursuing their legitimate political activities.

“We urge the Police and the DSS to pay careful attention to actions and utterances capable of creating unnecessary political tension in the state.

“We equally urge members of Reality Organisation to remain peaceful, disciplined and resolute in their lawful grassroots engagements without allowing themselves to be provoked by the actions of others.

“Ultimately, elections are determined by the electorate, not by billboards or their removal. The democratic right of the people to freely choose their representatives must remain paramount,” the statement concluded.

title: Katsina suspends Daura emir from official functions, probes sexual assault allegations
description:
From Agaju Madugba, Katsina
Katsina State Government has suspended all official engagements and travels of the Emir of Daura, Umar Farouk Umar, following allegations of sexual assault levelled against the traditional ruler by a Polish tourist who visited his palace on November 14, 2026.
Governor Dik
content:
From Agaju Madugba, Katsina

Katsina State Government has suspended all official engagements and travels of the Emir of Daura, Umar Farouk Umar, following allegations of sexual assault levelled against the traditional ruler by a Polish tourist who visited his palace on November 14, 2026.

Governor Dikko Umar Radda has also directed the establishment of a committee to investigate the allegations, which have generated widespread public outrage and attracted calls from human rights organisations and prominent Nigerians for an independent investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the alleged incident and ensure that justice is served.

Commissioner for Information and Culture, Bala Salisu Zango, who announced the government’s decision in a statement yesterday, said the administration was taking the allegations seriously and would ensure the full implementation of the recommendations of the investigative committee.

“The state government has taken the allegations seriously. His Excellency Malam Dikko Umar Radda, has therefore directed for the establishment of a committee to investigate the issue and advise the government accordingly.

“Meanwhile, the state government has also suspended all official engagements and travels of the monarch.

“The government wishes to assure the public that justice will be served and that the outcome of the committee’s findings and recommendations will be fully implemented.

“Therefore, government wishes to call on the general public to be calm, law-abiding and continue with their normal activities.”

The government’s directive, however, did not announce the removal of the monarch from the throne, but restricted his official engagements and travels pending investigation.

•Genesis of the controversy

The controversy erupted at the weekend after the foreign tourist, a travel blogger who identifies herself as Mirka, took to social media to recount her alleged ordeal during a visit to the Daura palace as part of a 30-day tour of Nigeria.

The tourist, who had documented her visits to several communities and traditional institutions across the country, alleged that the monarch touched her breasts without her consent during an audience with him at his palace on Saturday, November 14.

She claimed that what began as a cordial reception subsequently degenerated into an uncomfortable encounter during which the traditional ruler allegedly hugged, kissed and touched her inappropriately despite her objections.

The tourist subsequently released video footage which she said was recorded with smart glasses during the encounter, explaining that she had deliberately waited until she left Nigeria before making her allegations public.

Before her visit to Daura, she had visited the palace of the Oba of Benin on October 24 and attended activities marking the 10th coronation anniversary of Oba Ewuare II the following day.

The footage generated widespread reactions on social media, with human rights advocates and other Nigerians demanding an investigation.

Following the controversy, the Daura Emirate Council announced on Monday that it had commenced a review of the video to establish its authenticity and determine whether it had been manipulated.

The council’s spokesperson, Ibrahim Murtala, confirmed in an interview with Channels Television that the emirate was aware of the footage and was examining the allegations.

The council indicated that it would issue a formal statement upon conclusion of its review.

However, an unnamed palace source had earlier dismissed the allegations, acknowledging that the tourist visited the palace but denying that any inappropriate conduct took place.

The Katsina State Police Command was also reported on Monday to have said it had not received a formal complaint concerning the alleged incident.

Amnesty International Nigeria had on Sunday called on the Katsina State Government and the Nigeria Police Force to immediately investigate the allegations, insisting that the status of the traditional ruler should not prevent the authorities from establishing the facts and ensuring accountability through due process.

The organisation stressed that the allegations presented an opportunity for the authorities to demonstrate their commitment to protecting women against sexual violence, irrespective of the social standing of those accused.

In a further intervention yesterday, Amnesty International raised the alarm over hundreds of death threats allegedly directed at the tourist following her decision to make the allegations public.

The organisation said the woman had been subjected to sustained cyberbullying, intimidation and abusive messages, including threats to kill or harm her unless she withdrew her allegations.

It condemned the harassment and called for the protection of her rights and safety, amid concerns that intimidation of complainants could discourage other victims of sexual violence from reporting their experiences.

Before yesterday’s announcement by the Katsina State Government, former military governor of Kaduna State, Col. Abubakar Dangiwa Umar (retd.), had called on Radda to suspend the monarch pending the outcome of a comprehensive, impartial and transparent investigation into the allegations.

In an open letter to the governor dated November 23, Umar argued that the traditional institution occupied an important position in society and that its custodians were expected to demonstrate exemplary conduct.

He maintained that suspending the monarch pending investigation would not amount to a declaration of guilt but would safeguard the integrity of the traditional institution and protect the investigative process.

The former military governor also recommended the deposition of the monarch should the authenticity of the footage and the allegations against him be established.

Similarly, the Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) called on the Inspector-General of Police and the Katsina State Government to ensure an impartial investigation, warning against allowing the monarch’s age, status or influence to obstruct the pursuit of justice.

Islamic cleric, Sheikh Ahmad Gumi, also joined those demanding accountability, advocating the removal of any traditional ruler found guilty of immoral conduct.

Umar ascended the throne on February 28, 2007, following the death of his predecessor, Muhammadu Bashar Dan Umaru, who had occupied the throne for 41 years.

He is recognised as the 60th traditional ruler of Daura and has been on the throne for more than 19 years.

Daura occupies a significant position in the history of northern Nigeria as one of the seven original Hausa states, traditionally known as the Hausa Bakwai, and is also the hometown of former President Muhammadu Buhari.

The emirate’s historical and cultural significance has made its palace a destination for diplomats, political leaders, researchers and tourists seeking to explore the heritage of northern Nigeria.

The allegations against the monarch have yet to be established by an independent investigation, while the composition, terms of reference and reporting deadline of the committee constituted by the Katsina State Government were not disclosed in the statement announcing the suspension of his official engagements.

title: Air Peace launches London-Owerri flights December 15
description:
Air Peace says all is set to open a new international travel corridor between the United Kingdom and South-East Nigeria with the commencement of its London-Owerri flight operations effective 15 December.
The airline, in a statement on Monday, said the new service is expected to bring considerable re
content:
Air Peace says all is set to open a new international travel corridor between the United Kingdom and South-East Nigeria with the commencement of its London-Owerri flight operations effective 15 December.

The airline, in a statement on Monday, said the new service is expected to bring considerable relief to residents of Imo State and neighbouring states, particularly families, businesspeople and members of the Nigerian diaspora who have had to contend with the inconvenience of travelling through other airports before connecting to their destinations in the South-East.

The airline said the new connection would operate from London’s Gatwick and Heathrow airports, giving travellers greater flexibility when planning their journeys.

Air Peace attributed the development to a joint effort by the Imo State and Federal Governments, particularly the contributions of Governor Hope Uzodimma and the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo.

The airline noted that the minister played a key role in securing President Bola Tinubu’s approval for Owerri Airport to commence international operations.

The airline added that beyond passenger convenience, “the new route is expected to provide opportunities for stronger family connections, business exchanges and tourism between the United Kingdom and South-Eastern Nigeria.”

The carrier explained that passengers will be flown aboard Air Peace’s premium Boeing 777 wide-body aircraft, “which offers spacious cabins, comfortable seating and inflight meals featuring Nigerian and international cuisine.”

The airline also highlighted its baggage allowances as part of the benefits of the service. Economy Class passengers will be entitled to two checked bags weighing 23 kg each, while Business Class travellers will enjoy two bags weighing 32 kg each.

Air Peace said the new connection was part of its broader ambition to expand its international and domestic operations while making air travel more accessible to Nigerians.

title: Four Edo security operatives arrested for aiding cultists
description:
Four operatives of the Edo State Security Corps have been arrested for allegedly leaking information about police movements to suspected cultists in the Adolor area of Benin City.
The suspects, identified as Gideon Acher, Tony Oahiale and Culture Uzo, were arrested while police operatives were track
content:
Four operatives of the Edo State Security Corps have been arrested for allegedly leaking information about police movements to suspected cultists in the Adolor area of Benin City.

The suspects, identified as Gideon Acher, Tony Oahiale and Culture Uzo, were arrested while police operatives were tracking suspected cultists in the area.

The spokesman for the Edo State Police Command, Eno Ikoedem, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying the operatives were surprised to discover that information about their movements and activities had been leaked.

Ikoedem, who spoke during the parade of suspects arrested for various offences, said investigations into the leak led to the arrest of the four security personnel.

She added that a separate operation led to the arrest of 10 suspected members of the Aye cult group during an alleged initiation ceremony.

Other suspects paraded included four suspected kidnappers and an alleged armed robber arrested in the Ugiokhuen Community.

According to her, the four suspected kidnappers were arrested following the rescue of two victims, Yakubu Ibrahim and Abdullahi Mohammed, who were found unharmed during an intensive bush-combing operation in the Ikakumoh/Ayaran Forest.

She said, “Four personnel of the Edo State Security Corps were arrested for allegedly leaking information on police movements to suspected cultists in the Adolor area of Benin City.

“Others were also arrested for other crimes, which include kidnapping, cultism and armed robbery.

“These arrests underscore the Command’s determination to sustain pressure on criminal elements and ensure the safety of residents.

“The Commissioner of Police, Patrick Daaor, reiterates the Command’s resolve to dismantle criminal networks and bring perpetrators to justice. He commends the officers involved for their courage and professionalism and appreciates members of the public for their timely information and continued support.

“Residents are urged to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious activities, as the security of Edo State remains a collective responsibility.”

title: Dear Bunmi, should I tell him his wife is sleeping with my husband?
description:
Dear Bunmi, my husband of almost 25 years had been having an affair with a married woman. And he was reluctant to let go, even after years of pleading with him to.



In the end, I decided I’d had enough.



The kids had left home and I didn’t need him any more, as he was a sort of irritant.
content:
Dear Bunmi, my husband of almost 25 years had been having an affair with a married woman. And he was reluctant to let go, even after years of pleading with him to.

In the end, I decided I’d had enough.

The kids had left home and I didn’t need him any more, as he was a sort of irritant.

As you can imagine, I’m very angry at the other woman. I don’t know whether she’s still sleeping with my ex-husband, but I do know that her husband has no idea.

Dear Bunmi, I feel he should be made aware of what’s going on, as she’s taking her husband for a fool. Besides, why should mine be the only marriage to suffer?

Kemi, by e-mail

Dear Kemi,

What are you hoping to achieve by meddling in someone else’s relationship? Yes, perhaps her husband has a right to know, but if you were honest with yourself, that wouldn’t be why you would do such a thing. The truth is, you don’t want justice, you want revenge. If you really want to move on from the break-up of your marriage, forget about the past. If you truly want to move on from this, be the better person and move on.

content:
United States President Donald Trump is scheduled to meet NATO Secretary-General, Mark Rutte, today, amid growing concerns over European security and the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine.

The meeting, expected to take place in Palm Beach, Florida, comes as Washington and its European allies continue discussions over the future of Ukraine, military support and security guarantees for the war-torn country.

According to Reuters, the White House announced the planned meeting, while NATO also confirmed Rutte’s visit to the United States.

The discussions are expected to focus on transatlantic security relations, NATO’s defence commitments and efforts to find a diplomatic solution to the conflict between Moscow and Kyiv.

Trump has repeatedly called on European members of NATO to increase their defence spending and take greater responsibility for the security of the continent.

The meeting also comes amid disagreements among Western allies over the terms of a possible peace agreement and the extent of future military assistance to Ukraine.

Rutte has maintained that NATO’s support for Ukraine remains important to European security, as Russia’s invasion continues to shape diplomatic and military calculations across the region.

The outcome of Wednesday’s meeting could provide further indications of Washington’s position on NATO’s future role in the Ukraine conflict.

title: Omo-Agege kicks against disqualification, heads to A‘Court
description:
• Says judgment defies facts, law, logic
• Court orders INEC to delist ex-DSP, forecloses fresh primary

From Joe Obukata Ogbodu, Warri
Former deputy Senate president, Ovie Omo-Agege, has rejected the judgment of the Federal High Court sitting in Warri, Delta State, nullifying his nomination as the
content:
• Says judgment defies facts, law, logic

• Court orders INEC to delist ex-DSP, forecloses fresh primary

From Joe Obukata Ogbodu, Warri

Former deputy Senate president, Ovie Omo-Agege, has rejected the judgment of the Federal High Court sitting in Warri, Delta State, nullifying his nomination as the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections, describing the verdict as one that defies facts, law and logic and directing his legal team to immediately challenge it at the Court of Appeal.

Omo-Agege, who suffered the judicial setback a day after an attack on his campaign entourage left six persons dead, according to preliminary police reports, and several others injured, insisted that the findings of the court were inconsistent with the documentary evidence presented before it, particularly the NDC membership register which, he said, contained his name and was authenticated by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

Justice Hyeladzira Ajiya Nganjiwa had, in his judgment yesterday, ordered INEC to remove Omo-Agege’s name from its list of candidates and restrained him from parading himself as the NDC senatorial candidate, holding that his name was not contained in the party’s membership register submitted to the commission at least 21 days before its primary election.

In a further setback for the NDC, the court held that the party could no longer conduct a fresh primary to nominate another candidate for the senatorial seat, as the statutory window prescribed by the Electoral Act had elapsed.

However, Omo-Agege faulted the basis of the judgment, insisting that both the NDC and INEC presented documentary evidence establishing his membership of the party, while questioning the legal standing of the plaintiff, Prof. Alexander Osondu Akpodiete, to challenge the outcome of a primary election in which he allegedly neither sought the party’s nomination nor participated.

The former deputy senate president cautioned those celebrating the verdict as the end of his political journey against premature jubilation, declaring that the legal process had not run its course and that he would pursue every lawful avenue to overturn the judgment.

In a statement by his media aide, Sunny Areh, titled: “Warri judgment defies facts, law and logic; immediate appeal underway,” Omo-Agege expressed deep disappointment over the verdict but reaffirmed his commitment to the rule of law.

“While we respect the court, we strongly disagree with its decision. We believe that some of the findings do not reflect the documentary evidence presented before the court. Senator Omo-Agege has therefore directed his legal team to immediately challenge the judgment at the Court of Appeal.

“We are confident in the strength of our position and will pursue every lawful avenue to ensure that the issues raised by this judgment receive proper judicial consideration.”

Faulting the principal ground upon which the court invalidated his nomination, Omo-Agege maintained that the finding that his name was not contained in the NDC membership register was difficult to reconcile with the evidence presented before the court.

“Both the NDC and INEC produced documents showing that Senator Omo-Agege’s name was in the membership register submitted by the party. There was only one register. The NDC did not submit two different registers or maintain competing membership records for the same primary election. Senator Omo-Agege’s name appeared in the register submitted to INEC.

“Indeed, INEC acknowledged receipt of the register and issued Certified True Copies (CTCs) of that same document, bearing Senator Omo-Agege’s name, to several persons.

“The question that the Court of Appeal will be asked to examine is straightforward: if the register was before the trial court, and both the party and INEC presented evidence confirming that Senator Omo-Agege’s name appeared in it, what was the basis for the court’s contrary finding? This is a fundamental issue that deserves careful judicial scrutiny.”

Omo-Agege also questioned Akpodiete’s locus standi to institute the action, alleging that the plaintiff neither obtained the nomination forms required to participate in the party’s primary nor secured clearance from the NDC to contest the election.

According to him, Akpodiete’s name did not appear among the participants listed in INEC’s official monitoring report on the primary election.

“These circumstances raise serious questions about whether he established the legal standing required to challenge the outcome of a primary in which he did not participate. The issue is not whether a person can approach the courts for redress, but whether the plaintiff in this particular case demonstrated a sufficient legal interest to bring the action. We believe this issue warrants proper consideration on appeal.”

The statement further questioned the plaintiff’s decision to seek the invalidation of Omo-Agege’s nomination without asking the court to declare him the winner of the primary or award him the party’s ticket.

“It is also significant that the plaintiff did not ask the court to declare him the winner of the primary or award him the NDC ticket. Instead, he sought to invalidate the party’s nomination without seeking the ticket for himself. The implications of that position, including the legal interest behind the action, deserve close examination.”

Omo-Agege also alleged that attempts had been made before the judgment to persuade INEC to remove his name from its final list of candidates but that the commission declined, having confirmed that his name appeared in the membership register submitted by the NDC.

“These are official records, not political assertions. They formed part of the documentary evidence surrounding the case and must be examined in their proper context.”

•Why court nullified nomination

The judgment followed a suit instituted by Akpodiete, marked FHC/WR/CS/120/2026, challenging the validity of Omo-Agege’s nomination on grounds bordering on his resignation from the All Progressives Congress (APC), membership of the NDC and eligibility to participate in the party’s senatorial primary.

Delivering judgment, Justice Nganjiwa dismissed all five preliminary objections raised by Omo-Agege, the NDC and INEC challenging the competence of the suit before proceeding to determine the substantive issues raised by the plaintiff.

The court held that the NDC failed to comply with the mandatory provisions of the Electoral Act regarding the submission of its membership register to INEC ahead of its primary election, finding that Omo-Agege’s name was not contained in the register submitted to the commission within the prescribed period.

The judge further held that the party failed to provide credible evidence establishing that its membership register was subsequently updated to accommodate Omo-Agege and submitted to INEC within the statutory period preceding the primary.

Relying on INEC’s revised electoral timetable, the court also noted that Omo-Agege participated in the APC senatorial primary held on May 18, 2026, a development which, according to the court, established that he was still a member of the APC at the material time.

Justice Nganjiwa maintained that only persons whose names appeared in a political party’s membership register, in accordance with the requirements of the Electoral Act, were eligible to participate in its primary elections.

On the admissibility of a previously withdrawn affidavit, the court held that a party was entitled to withdraw an affidavit already filed in a proceeding, adding that once withdrawn, such an affidavit ceased to form part of the court’s records and could not be relied upon in determining the matter.

The judge maintained that a valid nomination could not be founded on a process that failed to satisfy statutory requirements, stressing that where a political party failed to comply with the Electoral Act in nominating its candidate, INEC was not permitted to include such a candidate on the ballot.

The court further held that the statutory window for conducting fresh primaries had closed, citing the provision of the Electoral Act prescribing a timeline of 180 days before the general elections.

Consequently, the court invalidated Omo-Agege’s nomination, directed INEC to delist him and restrained him from presenting himself as the NDC candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the forthcoming elections.

•My political journey not over – Omo-Agege

While reaffirming his respect for the judiciary, Omo-Agege maintained that exercising his right of appeal should not be construed as an attack on the court or rejection of the rule of law.

“Senator Omo-Agege has always maintained respect for the judiciary. That respect, however, does not require him to agree with every decision, particularly one he believes is inconsistent with the evidence and the applicable law. The right of appeal is an essential part of our judicial system. Exercising that right is neither an attack on the court nor a rejection of the rule of law.

“He has therefore directed his legal team to proceed immediately to the Court of Appeal. We intend to challenge the findings of the trial court and seek the correction of what we regard as serious errors in the judgment.”

The former deputy senate president insisted that the verdict would not diminish his commitment to the NDC and the people of Delta Central.

“Those already celebrating this decision as the end of Senator Omo-Agege’s political journey should exercise patience. This is a judgment of the trial court, and the opportunity for appellate review remains. The legal process has not run its course.

“Our commitment to the NDC and the people of Delta Central remains firm. Senator Omo-Agege will not abandon the democratic process because of a judgment he believes to be wrong. He will defend his rights through the courts and remain committed to the people whose support has brought him this far.

“We believe in the rule of law, but we also believe that justice must be anchored in facts and evidence. We will appeal this judgment and pursue that appeal with determination.”

•Double setback

The judgment came amid heightened tension over Monday’s deadly attack on Omo-Agege’s campaign entourage at Uduere community, which prompted the Delta State Government to impose an indefinite dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area.

The incident triggered a war of words between Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation and the state government, with the former accusing Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and the Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Area, Jaro Egbo, of complicity in the attack.

The state government dismissed the allegations and vowed to ensure that those responsible for the killings were brought to justice, irrespective of their political positions or status.

The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, has since ordered a thorough, impartial and evidence-based investigation into the attack, including the conduct of police personnel deployed to the venue.

As of press time, separate responses from the NDC and INEC to the judgment were not immediately available, while confirmation that Omo-Agege’s legal team had formally filed the appeal was still being awaited.
