title: Alumni illuminate UNN department with 36kVA solar power
description:
From Felix Ikem, Nsukka
The  Vice-Chancellor of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN), Prof Simon Ortuanya, has applauded the Class of 2006 alumni of the Department of Political Science and Diplomacy for installing a 36kVA solar power system in the department.
Ortuanya gave the commendation in Nsu
content:
From Felix Ikem, Nsukka

The  Vice-Chancellor of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN), Prof Simon Ortuanya, has applauded the Class of 2006 alumni of the Department of Political Science and Diplomacy for installing a 36kVA solar power system in the department.

Ortuanya gave the commendation in Nsukka, at the weekend, during the commissioning of the project at the Department of Political Science and Diplomacy. He said the decision of the Class of 2006 to remember and give back to the department that shaped their academic and professional careers was highly commendable.

“It is indisputable that a reliable and steady electricity supply is indispensable to effective teaching, learning, research, and administrative work in any department.

“By providing this reliable alternative source of energy, you have made a meaningful contribution towards improving the department’s learning environment and supporting the university’s commitment to renewable energy and sustainable development.

“Your gesture also sends a powerful message to current students and younger alumni that graduation should not mark the end of one’s relationship with the university, but rather the beginning of a lifelong partnership with one’s alma mater,” he said.

The Vice-Chancellor, who was represented by the Deputy Vice-Chancellor, Administration, Prof. Michael Onyia, urged other alumni to emulate the Class of 2006, stressing that the development of the university is a collective responsibility.

“I commend the Head of Department, Political Science, Prof. Peter Mbah; the Local Organising Committee (LOC) Chairman of the Class of 2006, Dr. Finnbar Emeogu; and others who contributed in one way or another to make this project a reality,” he said.

The Vice-Chancellor urged the Department of Political Science and Diplomacy to ensure proper utilisation and maintenance of the project to achieve the noble objective of the Class of 2006 in providing the facility.

“It is my honour and privilege to hereby commission this 36kVA solar power system provided by the Class of 2006 of Political Science and Diplomacy, UNN, to their alma mater,” the Vice-Chancellor said.

Speaking, the Head of Department of Political Science and Diplomacy, Prof. Peter Mbah, said November 20, 2026, would remain a milestone in the department, being the day that witnessed the unveiling and commissioning of the 36kVA solar power system provided by the Class of 2006.

Mbah said the department would now enjoy 24-hour uninterrupted electricity supply, courtesy of the Class of 2006 alumni.

“The Department of Political Science and Diplomacy will remain forever grateful for this immense contribution, which will aid teaching, learning, research, and administrative work. This 36kVA solar power system provides electricity to all classrooms and offices, as well as powering air conditioners, refrigerators, and other electrical gadgets in the department.

“The department will do everything within its capacity to ensure adequate utilisation, protection, and maintenance of the project,” the HOD pledged.

He said that, to ensure the protection of the project, the department had already installed solar-powered lights and CCTV cameras around the department to monitor the facilities and capture anyone attempting to vandalise the installations.

Earlier, in a remark, the Local Organising Chairman for the Class of 2006 project, Dr. Finnbar Emeogu, said the alumni provided the 36kVA solar power system to the Department of Political Science and Diplomacy because the department had contributed immensely to making them who they are today.

The LOC Chairman said the project was executed by the Class of 2006 and powered by Chief Obinna Iyiegbu, popularly known as Okpata Ozuora, who is also a member of the class. He disclosed that the decision to give back to their alma mater was conceived during the Class of 2006’s 20th graduation reunion held this year.

Emeogu, a staff member of the Department of Registry, UNN, and a former member of the university’s Governing Council, said his experience had made him understand the importance of a steady power supply to teaching, learning, research, and administrative work.

“The Class of 2006 is happy that the problem of public power supply has been addressed in the Department of Political Science and Diplomacy. The solar panels can last for over 30 years, the lithium batteries for over eight years, and the inverter for over 10 years, while the entire installed solar system has fire safety features to detect any fire outbreak,” he said.

On behalf of the Class of 2006, the LOC Chairman commended the HOD and other staff members of the Department of Political Science and Diplomacy for their maximum cooperation, which ensured that the project was commissioned as scheduled. He said the department had already put measures, including the installation of CCTV cameras, in place to ensure the protection of the facility against vandalism.

In a chat with Daily Sun, Prof. Chidi Nzeadibe, the immediate past Dean of the Faculty of Social Sciences, commended Prof. Peter Mbah, the Head of Department of Political Science and Diplomacy, for his numerous achievements since assuming office and wished him greater accomplishments.

Among the Class of 2006 alumni present at the commissioning were Dr. Finnbar Emeogu, the LOC Chairman; Dr. Isaac Ndubuisi; Dr. Ifeanyi Nzenweakil; and Dr. Ezeanya Emeka, among others.

The post Alumni illuminate UNN department with 36kVA solar power appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: IMG MD urges staff to drive efficiency, inclusion
description:
The Acting Managing Director of Industrial & Medical Gases Nigeria Plc, Abayomi Oke, has urged male employees of the company to embrace responsibility, innovation, discipline and accountability as critical values for driving corporate growth and sustaining organisational excellence.
Oke made the cal
content:
The Acting Managing Director of Industrial & Medical Gases Nigeria Plc, Abayomi Oke, has urged male employees of the company to embrace responsibility, innovation, discipline and accountability as critical values for driving corporate growth and sustaining organisational excellence.

Oke made the call while addressing employees during the celebration of the 2026 International Men’s Day, themed ‘The Future Is Everyone: Men Driving Progress.’

He said the theme underscored the collective responsibility of men to contribute meaningfully to organisational development, family stability and societal progress.

He noted that male employees at IMG have important responsibilities in enhancing operational efficiency, boosting the company’s competitiveness and improving its ability to deliver value to customers across key sectors of the economy.

He said that IMG occupied an important position in Nigeria’s industrial and healthcare value chains through the manufacture and supply of industrial and medical gases, including oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen and argon.

Oke explained that the company’s contributions extended beyond the production and distribution of gases, as its products supported healthcare delivery, manufacturing, food and beverage processing, energy and other essential economic activities.

“What we do goes beyond producing and selling gases. We support industries, contribute to healthcare delivery, enable businesses to operate and ultimately touch lives,” he said.

He acknowledged the contributions of employees across production, engineering, maintenance, logistics, sales, finance, administration and other departments, describing their individual efforts as essential to the company’s value chain and overall performance.

The IMG chief also emphasised the need for strict adherence to safety standards, noting that the company’s operations involved specialised equipment, high-pressure installations, cryogenic facilities, production plants and transportation systems that required constant vigilance.

He urged employees to take personal responsibility for workplace safety, comply with established procedures, promptly report unsafe conditions and look out for their colleagues.

“Let us never sacrifice safety for speed or operational convenience. A responsible man is not just one who delivers results; he is one who delivers results safely, ethically and professionally,” he stated.

On business competitiveness, Oke challenged employees to embrace continuous learning, technological advancement and innovative approaches to work, stressing that changing industry dynamics and rising customer expectations required a workforce committed to improvement.

He identified improved plant efficiency, reduced production losses, minimised equipment downtime, cost control, timely deliveries and stronger customer relationships as areas requiring collective attention.

He further called for a culture of ownership and accountability, urging employees to move beyond merely completing assigned tasks to actively identifying challenges and contributing practical solutions.

Oke said genuine strength among men should be reflected in integrity, humility, emotional intelligence, mutual respect and the ability to collaborate effectively with others, stressing the importance of positive workplace relationships and personal development.

He urged male employees to mentor younger colleagues, support women in the workplace and promote an inclusive culture that allows every employee to contribute meaningfully and achieve their potential.

He also highlighted their responsibilities outside the workplace as fathers, husbands, brothers, mentors and community members, encouraging them to prioritise their physical, emotional and mental well-being.

On the organisation’s future, the acting managing director noted that achieving improved performance, business expansion and a stronger competitive position in the industrial and medical gases market would require collective commitment across all departments.

He urged production teams to enhance efficiency and reliability, engineering personnel to maintain plants and equipment in optimal condition, logistics teams to ensure safe and timely deliveries, sales teams to strengthen customer relationships, and support departments to reinforce the operational systems necessary for business growth.

Oke commended the male workforce for their dedication, resilience and contributions to the company, urging them to sustain their commitment to professional development and excellence.

He maintained that building a stronger IMG would depend on men who embodied good character, purposeful leadership, innovation and an unwavering dedication to delivering value.

The post IMG MD urges staff to drive efficiency, inclusion appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Marseille coach hails Nnadi
description:
Marseille coach Bruno Genesio has praised Nigerian midfielder Tochukwu Nnadi for his work rate, commitment and continued improvement since joining the French club.
The 23-year-old has earned his coach’s admiration for his contributions beyond the obvious aspects of his game, particularly his ability
content:
Marseille coach Bruno Genesio has praised Nigerian midfielder Tochukwu Nnadi for his work rate, commitment and continued improvement since joining the French club.

The 23-year-old has earned his coach’s admiration for his contributions beyond the obvious aspects of his game, particularly his ability to cover ground and deny opponents space.

Genesio described Nnadi as a player whose efforts are vital to the team’s collective performance.

“He’s a fantastic player; he does so much for the team, he does things that others might not see. The distance he covers on the pitch… I’m sure he’s someone you don’t want to play against because he won’t leave any space,” he said.

The coach also praised the midfielder’s development and popularity among his teammates.

“He has a lot of qualities; he keeps improving. He’s an extraordinary guy; everyone on the team loves him. He’s a really great person,” Genesio added.

Nnadi joined Marseille from Belgian side Zulte Waregem in February 2026 and has continued to work towards establishing himself in the French side’s midfield.

He also provided an assist in Marseille’s 5-2 victory over Angers on October 18.

title: Nigerian Enamelware cuts half-year loss to N40.66m
description:
Nigerian Enamelware Plc has narrowed its loss for the period ended 31 October 2026, while recording higher six-month revenue in its unaudited second-quarter financial report for the 2026/2027 financial year.
According to the interim financial statements approved by the board of directors on 19 Novem
content:
Nigerian Enamelware Plc has narrowed its loss for the period ended 31 October 2026, while recording higher six-month revenue in its unaudited second-quarter financial report for the 2026/2027 financial year.

According to the interim financial statements approved by the board of directors on 19 November 2026, and signed off by Managing Director Taiwo Alli and Finance Manager Babatunde Adeoye, revenue for the six months from 1 May 2026, to 31 October 2026, increased to N478.79m from N451.12m in the equivalent period of 2025.

For the three-month period from 1 August 2026, to 31 October 2026, revenue came in at N247.08m compared with N404.51m a year earlier.

In the filing, the company stated, “Based on our knowledge, the financial statement and other financial information included in the report fairly present in all material respects the financial condition and results of operations of the Company as of, and for the periods presented in the report.”

Cost of sales for the six-month period eased to N433.26m from N497.57m in the prior-year period, pushing gross profit to N45.54m from a gross loss of N46.45m. For the three months ended 31 October 2026, gross profit rose to N15.45m from N4.81m in the corresponding period of 2025.

Loss for the three-month period ended 31 October 2026, narrowed to N3.14m from N5.63m in the same period of 2025, while loss for the six-month period improved to N40.66m from N86.15m. Basic loss per share stood at 4 kobo for the three-month period against seven kobo a year earlier, and 53 kobo for the six-month period compared with 113 kobo previously.

On the statement of financial position as of 31 October 2026, total assets stood at N2.97bn compared with N2.74bn as of 31 October 2025, and N2.89bn as of 30 April 2026. Total current liabilities stood at N3.82bn compared with N3.55bn a year earlier, leaving net liabilities at N849.54m.

Nigerian Enamelware Plc, listed on the Main Board of the Nigerian Exchange and active in manufacturing and marketing enamelware, plastic products and galvanised buckets, has its majority parent company in Hong Kong-incorporated I-Feng Limited, which owns 60 per cent of its equity.

title: Nigerian startups make Google’s Africa AI Lab
description:
Three Nigerian technology start-ups, Intron, Termii and Vendy, have been selected for the inaugural cohort of Google’s Africa Applied AI Lab, securing three of the 10 places in a programme designed to help businesses develop artificial intelligence products for the continent.
The companies were sele
content:
Three Nigerian technology start-ups, Intron, Termii and Vendy, have been selected for the inaugural cohort of Google’s Africa Applied AI Lab, securing three of the 10 places in a programme designed to help businesses develop artificial intelligence products for the continent.

The companies were selected from thousands of applications submitted from more than 45 African countries, reflecting the growing presence of Nigerian technology firms developing AI-powered solutions for businesses and consumers.

The three start-ups already operate products addressing practical challenges across different sectors. Intron develops speech recognition technology for hospitals, courtrooms and contact centres, with systems designed to recognise African accents and accommodate speakers switching between languages.

Termii provides messaging and customer verification services used by banks and fintech companies for one-time passwords, secure logins and transaction notifications, while Vendy enables businesses to operate online storefronts and receive payments through WhatsApp without requiring customers to download separate applications.

They will join seven other start-ups selected for the programme, including AethexAI, Agrails, Smile ID and Viamo, which operate across multiple African markets. The remaining participants are Crane AI Labs from Uganda, Satlyt from Kenya and Tolbi from Senegal.

The Africa Applied AI Lab Google is managed by the Google AI Futures Fund in collaboration with Google Research. It is intended to help founders translate advances in artificial intelligence research into products that can be deployed by businesses and consumers.

Over the coming weeks, the selected companies will work with Google’s engineers, research scientists, and product leaders. They will also receive early access to Google’s artificial intelligence models, including Gemini and Gemma, as they develop and improve their products.

Four African venture capital firms, 4DX Ventures, Norrsken22, Novastar Ventures and Ventures Platform, will guide financing and take the start-ups’ products to market.

The programme will culminate in a Demo Day in December at the Accra AI Community Centre in Ghana, where the companies will present their work to investors, industry leaders and members of the technology community.

In a blog post announcing the cohort, Head of Google Research Africa, Aisha Walcott-Bryant, and Country Manager and Research Lead for Google Ghana, Perry Nelson, said the start-ups were working on challenges with significance beyond the continent.

“The priorities these teams are addressing are crucial for Africa, and the breakthroughs they pioneer here will redefine possibilities globally,” they wrote.

Applications for the programme opened in July and closed on 31 August, with Google saying the final selection considered the quality of the start-ups’ products and the traction they had already achieved.

The selection places three Nigerian companies among the first group of African businesses to receive direct technical support and research access through the initiative.

The post Nigerian startups make Google’s Africa AI Lab appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Alimosho wins Lagos basic schools sports competition
description:
Alimosho Local Government Education Authority, Lagos State, has emerged winner of the 2026 Basic Education Schools Sports Competition in the state.
The competition finals were held at the YABATECH Sports Complex on Monday under the coordination of the Lagos State Universal Basic Education Board.
Ali
content:
Alimosho Local Government Education Authority, Lagos State, has emerged winner of the 2026 Basic Education Schools Sports Competition in the state.

The competition finals were held at the YABATECH Sports Complex on Monday under the coordination of the Lagos State Universal Basic Education Board.

Alimosho emerged winner after winning 11 medals, comprising five gold, two silver and four bronze, across various sporting events.

The competition saw athletes participate in various sporting events, including athletics, swimming, football, long jump, Ayo Olopon, table tennis, Scrabble and chess.

Alimosho’s feat included a double victory in male and female football, with both teams clinching gold medals.

The female team defeated Agege LGEA 2–0, while the male team secured a convincing 3–0 victory over Apapa LGEA in the final.

In male football, Alimosho also won individual honours as Azeez Samson emerged as the Most Valuable Player, while Ibrahim Babatunde received the Best Goalkeeper award.

In the female category, Falilat Olabamiji was named MVP, while Uwaoma Favour won the Best Goalkeeper award.

In the final medal standings, Ibeju-Lekki LGEA emerged second with four gold, seven silver and six bronze medals, while Lagos Island secured third position with four gold, two silver and three bronze medals.

Apapa LGEA came fourth with three gold and four silver medals, while Kosofe finished fifth with three gold and three silver medals.

A total of 83 medals, comprising 28 gold, 28 silver and 27 bronze medals, were won across the competition.

Speaking at the event, the Chairman of LASUBEB, Dr Hakeem Shittu, said the competition emphasised the importance of physical fitness, discipline, teamwork, confidence and healthy competition among pupils.

He said, “At LASUBEB, we recognise that education goes beyond academic excellence. While literacy and numeracy remain fundamental to basic education, we equally understand the importance of sports and other co-curricular activities in shaping well-rounded individuals.

“The competition provided an avenue for identifying and nurturing young sporting talents across public primary schools while promoting inclusive participation and creating opportunities for pupils to demonstrate their abilities beyond the classroom.”

He added that participation in sporting activities helped pupils develop confidence, resilience, determination and the ability to work collaboratively towards achieving common goals.

The chairman reaffirmed the board’s commitment to strengthening co-curricular activities in public primary schools and ensuring that every child had an opportunity to discover and maximise their potential.

In her goodwill message, the Executive Secretary of the Universal Basic Education Commission, Dr Aisha Garba, represented by the UBEC State Coordinator, Arema Sunday, commended LASUBEB for organising the competition and acknowledged the importance of sports in promoting the holistic development of children.

She reaffirmed the commission’s commitment to supporting initiatives that strengthen basic education and encouraged continued collaboration between federal and state education institutions to improve learning outcomes and the overall development of pupils.

Meanwhile, the Education Secretary of Alimosho LGEA, Dr Aminat Ige, expressed delight at the pupils’ outstanding performance.

She attributed the achievement to early preparation, continuous motivation, purposeful leadership and the collective efforts of the pupils, coaches, teachers, Desk Sports Officers and other stakeholders.

Ige reaffirmed her commitment to grassroots sports development, talent discovery and the nurturing of young athletes to sustain Alimosho’s leading position in school sports across Lagos State.

title: ‘State govts must drive grassroots sports’
description:
Sports philanthropist Yemi Idowu has called for a review of Nigeria’s sports development policies, advocating the transfer of grassroots sports administration and resources to state and local governments to strengthen talent development across the country.
Idowu, who has invested in grassroots sport
content:
Sports philanthropist Yemi Idowu has called for a review of Nigeria’s sports development policies, advocating the transfer of grassroots sports administration and resources to state and local governments to strengthen talent development across the country.

Idowu, who has invested in grassroots sports through his foundation and funded the Ajegunle Maracana Sports Centre in Lagos, made the call at the National Grassroots Sports Summit in Abuja. He argued that Nigeria’s sporting challenges stem largely from policy and implementation gaps rather than a shortage of talent.

The Ajegunle facility has 19 pitches, comprising 10 five-a-side pitches, eight seven-a-side pitches and one standard pitch.

“Nigerian sports does not have any problem; what we have is a policy problem. If there is anything we will come up with today, it is to develop policies that will make Nigerian sports work,” he said.

Idowu said returning grassroots sports responsibilities and resources to state governments, backed by effective policies and regular competitions, would improve local sports administration, attract private-sector investment and sponsorship, and create more opportunities for young athletes.

He proposed that the Federal Government limit its role to coordinating grassroots sports activities across the states, while state and local governments take greater responsibility for implementation.

He also called for greater recognition and support for grassroots sports administrators, local government officials and media practitioners, who he said contribute significantly to talent development despite often operating with limited resources.

On football, Idowu urged the Nigeria Football Federation to concentrate on managing the national teams and international competitions, while state governments take charge of grassroots development.

He advocated regular U-17 and other age-grade competitions across the 36 states to establish clear pathways for talented athletes to progress from schools and local communities to state and national teams.

Idowu commended the Senior Special Assistant on Grassroots Sports to President Bola Tinubu, Anthony Adeboye, for convening the summit and bringing stakeholders together to discuss practical solutions to the challenges facing sports development.

Describing the summit as the beginning of a wider reform process, he urged the organisers to hold a follow-up gathering to assess the implementation of recommendations reached at the event.

“The National Grassroots Sports Summit is the beginning of a process. The most important thing is that hopefully we can now have another event where we can review all the things we agreed on this year to see whether some of them have been implemented,” he said.

The post ‘State govts must drive grassroots sports’ appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Otti seeks China Harbour’s full partnership on Abia Sea Port project
description:
By Steve Oko



UMUAHIA – Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has expressed preference for a full-scale partnership with China Harbour Engineering Company Limited (CHEC) on the proposed Abia Sea Port City project, extending beyond feasibility studies to construction and eventual delivery.







Otti sa
content:
By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA – Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has expressed preference for a full-scale partnership with China Harbour Engineering Company Limited (CHEC) on the proposed Abia Sea Port City project, extending beyond feasibility studies to construction and eventual delivery.

Otti said his administration wanted the Chinese firm involved throughout the project’s lifecycle, rather than restricting its role to consultancy, as discussions on the proposed port gathered momentum.

The governor spoke in Umuahia while receiving a CHEC delegation led by its Managing Director, Wang Jason, who presented preliminary findings and proposals on the port project.

Otti said the state was interested in a long-term partnership but would rely on professional, independent assessments to determine the project’s viability, technical requirements and commercial framework.

“My preference would have been a partnership that takes off from the feasibility, to the construction and ultimately delivery,” the governor said.

He described the proposed arrangement as a public-private partnership, assuring CHEC of his administration’s commitment to transparency and mutually beneficial business dealings.

The governor, however, said further engagements were necessary to clarify the technical and commercial details of the proposal, stressing that the feasibility study would determine the appropriate direction of the project.

He disclosed that Abia had also attracted interest from other prospective investors, including Afreximbank, but said their participation would equally depend on the outcome of the feasibility assessment.

Otti said the proposed port would require strategic planning, technical expertise, patience and long-term commitment, expressing optimism that its integration with other infrastructure and economic activities could significantly expand Abia’s economic prospects.

He said his administration had enacted a 25-year development plan to provide continuity for strategic projects beyond successive governments.

Earlier, CHEC Managing Director, Wang Jason, described the proposed port project as viable, saying the feasibility study would determine the most suitable port design, depth and technical specifications for the location.

Jason said the company was interested in a long-term relationship with Abia beyond conducting feasibility studies, expressing confidence in Aba’s commercial strength and its capacity to support an integrated infrastructure development project.

He said CHEC was prepared to explore further cooperation with the state after the feasibility study, including discussions on the business and partnership models for the project’s implementation.

The proposed Abia Sea Port City to be cited around Obuaku/Azumini axis of Ukwa East Local Government Area, is expected to form part of the state’s broader infrastructure and economic development vision.

Otti has said his administration considered the project one of its key priorities.

title: Quadre braces for professional tennis career
description: Nigeria tennis star Oyinlomo Quadre is preparing to take the next step in her career as she transitions from college tennis to the professional circuit following an impressive campaign at the maiden Destiny Da-Silva Tennis Open Championship, where she claimed both the women’s singles and doubles tit
content:
Nigeria tennis star Oyinlomo Quadre is preparing to take the next step in her career as she transitions from college tennis to the professional circuit following an impressive campaign at the maiden Destiny Da-Silva Tennis Open Championship, where she claimed both the women’s singles and doubles titles.

Quadre underlined her dominance on Saturday, defeating Success Ogunjobi 6-1, 6-1 to win the singles crown.

She also partnered Ntoro Bassey to the women’s doubles title, recovering from a set down to overcome teenagers Aina Goodnews and Samuel Gloria 3-6, 6-2, 10-5.

The tournament marked another successful outing for the United States-based player, who is now looking forward to beginning her professional career after graduating from college.

“This would be the start of my pre-season. Next year would be my first year doing full professional because I just graduated from college. So basically, I will be going back to work,” Quadre said.

The 22-year-old has steadily built her reputation since moving to the United States for college tennis in 2022/23.

She joined Florida International University as Nigeria’s No. 1-ranked junior and a player ranked among the top 100 in the ITF World Junior Rankings before transferring to the University of Oklahoma.

Her collegiate career has yielded several honours, including First Team Singles All-Conference USA and First Team Doubles All-Conference USA selections in 2025.

Despite spending much of her career abroad, Quadre has continued to make her presence felt on the domestic circuit.

Representing Delta State at the last National Sports Festival, she defeated Ogun State’s Nene Yakubu 6-1, 6-0 to claim her third singles gold medal at the multi-sport competition.

The post Quadre braces for professional tennis career appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Tinubu cuts 2026 budget to N65.18tn, retains deficit
description:
President Bola Tinubu has transmitted a bill to the House of Representatives seeking to repeal and re-enact the 2026 Appropriation Act, reducing the approved budget from N68.32tn to N65.18tn while retaining the N31.46tn fiscal deficit.
The revised budget provides for projected Federal Government rev
content:
President Bola Tinubu has transmitted a bill to the House of Representatives seeking to repeal and re-enact the 2026 Appropriation Act, reducing the approved budget from N68.32tn to N65.18tn while retaining the N31.46tn fiscal deficit.

The revised budget provides for projected Federal Government revenue of N33.72tn, including earnings from Government-Owned Enterprises, and capital expenditure of N26.23tn.

Tinubu’s request was contained in a letter dated November 20, 2026, addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, and read during plenary on Tuesday.

The President also transmitted a revised 2026 Federal Government Fiscal Framework, explaining that the adjustments were intended to align the budget with existing obligations and available resources.

According to the letter, the revision seeks to regularise some expenditures incurred by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) on behalf of the Federation, address underprovided debt-service obligations, recognise issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments, and provide for refunds to Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) and special accounts.

Tinubu said capital provisions for MDAs consisted mainly of amounts already warranted, while a few new capital and overhead allocations were introduced to address priority national interventions.

He identified the completion of critical road projects, protection of agricultural production, reduction of production costs, improvement of farm yields, enhanced market access and measures to address water vulnerability as key priorities.

The President said the revised fiscal framework was designed to prioritise existing commitments, improve the credibility and execution of the capital budget, and maintain fiscal restraint.

Despite the reduction in the overall budget, the fiscal deficit, including project-tied loans, remains unchanged at N31.457tn, representing 5.64 per cent of the Gross Domestic Product.

Tinubu also retained the proposed new borrowing of N29.22tn, comprising N18.43tn in domestic borrowing and N10.79tn in foreign borrowing.

On the proposed external borrowing, the President said the planned $7.7bn loan, estimated at N10.37tn using an exchange rate of N1,346.50 to the dollar, was intended to finance the existing foreign borrowing provision without increasing the borrowing envelope.

The letter read: “The proposal aligns the 2026 budget with existing obligations and available resources. It regularises some NNPCL expenditures incurred on behalf of the Federation, addresses underprovided debt-service obligations, recognises issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments, and provides for refunds to Ministries, Departments and Agencies and Special Accounts.

“MDA capital provision consists mainly of amounts already warranted. A few new MDA capital and overhead provisions were included as priority national interventions, particularly to complete critical road projects, protect agricultural production, reduce production costs, improve farm yields, and enhance market access, while addressing water vulnerability.

“Under the revised framework, aggregate expenditure is N65.176tn, compared with N68.323tn in the approved budget, while projected FGN revenue, including Government-Owned Enterprises, is N33.720tn. Aggregate capital expenditure is N26.232tn.

“The fiscal deficit, including project-tied loans, remains unchanged at N31.457tn, equivalent to 5.64 per cent of GDP. These adjustments prioritise existing commitments and improve the credibility and execution of the capital budget while maintaining fiscal restraint.”

Seeking the cooperation of lawmakers for speedy passage, Tinubu said the revised appropriation was necessary to ensure orderly implementation of the budget and settlement of outstanding obligations.

“I, therefore, request the kind cooperation of the House of Representatives for expeditious consideration and passage of the Bill to facilitate orderly implementation of the revised budget and settlement of existing obligations,” he added.

The bill will be subjected to legislative scrutiny before the revised appropriation can take effect. Its passage would provide the legal basis for the Federal Government to implement the adjusted spending plan and meet the obligations outlined in the revised fiscal framework.

The post Tinubu cuts 2026 budget to N65.18tn, retains deficit appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Lawmakers scrutinise 664 laws, flag possible alterations
description:
The Senate has ordered a thorough examination of the revised and consolidated Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2025 before approving the document, warning that any alteration of laws passed by the National Assembly could undermine the country’s legal system.
The decision followed a letter from Pres
content:
The Senate has ordered a thorough examination of the revised and consolidated Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2025 before approving the document, warning that any alteration of laws passed by the National Assembly could undermine the country’s legal system.

The decision followed a letter from President Bola Tinubu seeking the National Assembly’s approval of the revised compendium, which contains updated federal laws and subsidiary legislation.

The Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, read the President’s letter, dated November 18, 2026, during plenary on Tuesday, while Senate President Godswill Akpabio also read the correspondence before the Senate.

In the letter, Tinubu disclosed that a technical committee constituted on October 24, 2024, under the supervision of the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, examined 932 federal enactments and 731 subsidiary legislations.

The committee, chaired by Olawale Fapohunda (SAN), validated 664 principal enactments for inclusion in the revised compendium and recommended the removal of 268 others identified as obsolete, spent or repealed.

Tinubu said the exercise was necessary to address the long gap since the last official consolidation of Nigeria’s federal laws in 2004, noting that the country had undergone significant legislative, constitutional, institutional and technological changes.

In his letter, titled ‘Transmission of the Revised and Consolidated Compendium of the Laws of the Federation of Nigeria (LFN 2025) for Consideration and Approval’, the President said, “I write to formally inform you of the conclusion of the review, update, and consolidation of the Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, and to forward herewith the proposed Revised Compendium of the Laws of the Federation of Nigeria (LFN 2025) for the kind consideration and approval of the House of Representatives of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

“You may wish to recall that the last official consolidation of the Laws of the Federation was undertaken in 2004. Over the past twenty (20) years, Nigeria has witnessed profound legislative, constitutional, institutional, and technological transformations.

“These developments have necessitated the enactment of numerous new statutes, substantial amendments to existing laws, and a significant accumulation of subsidiary legislation, making the consolidation of an updated, coherent, and accessible body of Federal laws an urgent national imperative.”

According to Tinubu, the committee was mandated to identify obsolete and spent enactments, resolve statutory inconsistencies and overlaps, and produce an authoritative modern edition of the country’s laws.

He said the updated compendium would provide a reliable legal reference for the judiciary, legal practitioners, government institutions, investors and the general public.

The President added, “In discharging this mandate, the Committee rigorously examined a total of 932 Federal enactments and 731 subsidiary legislations. Following extensive legal research, technical consultations, editorial scrutiny, and quality assurance, 664 principal enactments alongside their relevant subsidiary legislation were validated for inclusion in the LFN 2025, while 268 enactments were identified as obsolete, spent, or repealed.

“An updated, accurate, and easily accessible compendium of Federal laws is indispensable to our democratic and economic growth. Upon enactment, the LFN 2025 will serve as a reliable legal reference for the judiciary, legal practitioners, government institutions, domestic and foreign investors, and the general public, thereby enhancing legal certainty, institutional efficiency, and public confidence in our justice system.”

However, Akpabio said lawmakers must ensure that all amendments made by the National Assembly were accurately reflected in the revised document.

He said the exercise would involve comparing the consolidated laws with the original versions passed by both chambers to prevent errors or unauthorised changes.

Contributing to the debate, former Senate Leader, Senator Yahaya Abdullahi, described the exercise as important to the administration of justice and the country’s legal system.

The Kebbi North senator recalled that a similar exercise was undertaken after the return to democratic rule in 1999 to give legal backing to decrees enacted during military administrations.

He, however, warned against rushing the process, given its implications for the justice system, and urged the Senate Committee on Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters to work with legal experts to examine the volumes and submit a comprehensive report before approval.

Also speaking, Deputy Senate President Jibrin Barau supported the call for proper scrutiny, warning that even a single altered provision could make the revised document inconsistent with laws passed by the National Assembly.

The Kano North senator said the consolidated laws should be compared with the original versions passed by both chambers and those assented to by the President.

Akpabio agreed with the lawmakers, saying the National Assembly would involve consultants and legal experts in the verification process.

He said, “The Senate usually engages consultants and relevant experts to examine such documents before presenting a summarised report.

“I am directing that the leadership and management of the National Assembly be involved in the verification exercise to ensure accuracy.”

The Senate subsequently referred the document to its Committees on Rules and Business and Judiciary for further legislative consideration.

Earlier, Fagbemi had explained that the review involved extensive legal research, legislative analysis, technical coordination and editorial work. Fourteen thematic working groups were also established to harmonise the findings through retreats and other technical engagements.

The exercise received technical and development support from several institutions and organisations, including the Rule of Law and Anti-Corruption Programme, the Law Commission of England and Wales, LexisNexis South Africa, the Lagos State Law Reform Commission and Law Pavilion.

Tinubu described the exercise as a major deliverable of his administration’s Renewed Hope Agenda, particularly its commitment to justice sector reform, strengthening the rule of law and establishing a legal framework capable of supporting national development.

He urged lawmakers to expedite consideration and approval of the revised compendium, saying it would improve legal certainty, institutional efficiency and public confidence in the justice system.

The post Lawmakers scrutinise 664 laws, flag possible alterations appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: ESUT remains committed to quality academic standards, VC tells NUC accreditation teams
description: By Alumona UkwuezeENUGU—The Vice-Chancellor of the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT), Professor Aloysius-Michaels Okolie, on Tuesday , reaffirmed the university’s commitment to sustaining high academic standards, strengthening quality assurance and improving service delivery.
content:
By Alumona Ukwueze
ENUGU—The Vice-Chancellor of the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT), Professor Aloysius-Michaels Okolie, on Tuesday , reaffirmed the university’s commitment to sustaining high academic standards, strengthening quality assurance and improving service delivery.

Professor Okolie gave the assurance when accreditation teams from the National Universities Commission (NUC), responsible for Civil Engineering and Mechanical and Production Engineering programmes, visited the university to assess the programmes.

He commended the NUC for its efforts in upholding academic standards in Nigeria’s tertiary education system, noting that ESUT had prioritised practical training for staff and students to equip them with the skills needed to address challenges within their immediate environment and the country at large.

The Vice-Chancellor disclosed that the university had signed a partnership agreement with a Qatar-based Information and Communication Technology (ICT) firm, Vertex Labs, to establish a Centre of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence (AI).

He added that representatives of the company were expected to arrive soon to expand the scope of the partnership to include the fabrication of computer accessories.

According to him, the initiative builds on the selection of ESUT by the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) as a South-East Centre of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, Cybersecurity and other related fields.

Professor Okolie also disclosed that the university management had inaugurated an ICT Innovation Hub to provide staff and students with practical training and professional certification programmes that would enhance their employability and economic independence after graduation.

He emphasised the importance of engineering in driving the university’s innovation agenda, adding that the institution makes adequate preparations for accreditation exercises by setting aside special funds ahead of time.

The Vice-Chancellor further acknowledged TETFund’s contributions towards the procurement of equipment required for accreditation exercises and assured the visiting teams of the full support and cooperation of the university management.

Speaking at the ESUT Council Chamber, the leader of the Civil Engineering accreditation team, Professor Mohammed Saidu, said the exercise was not intended to witch-hunt the university but to objectively assess its compliance with established academic standards.

He assured the university that the teams would discharge their responsibilities with professionalism, objectivity and due diligence.

The accreditation team for Mechanical and Production Engineering was led by Professor Aje Tokan of the Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University, Bauchi State.

title: Abolish pipeline surveillance contracts
description: There is something insanely absurd in having to incentivise any group of persons to restrain them from destroying assets in which they have significant stakes. This is even more so when the environmental costs of such destruction are considered. That absurdity writ large in Nigeria at the dawn of th
content:
There is something insanely absurd in having to incentivise any group of persons to restrain them from destroying assets in which they have significant stakes. This is even more so when the environmental costs of such destruction are considered. That absurdity writ large in Nigeria at the dawn of the Fourth Republic, under the term “Pipelines surveillance contracts”. Before then, there had been reported random attacks on oil and gas infrastructure and abductions of expatriate staff of O&G companies by disgruntled elements, otherwise dubbed “militants” in the Niger Delta region. The military juntas of that era resorted to a carrot-and-stick approach to curb the nuisance. But, for all intents and purposes, that approach proved as ineffectual as water off a duck’s back.

The first democratically elected president of the Fourth Republic, Olusegun Obasanjo, a retired army general, took that carrot-and-stick approach to the next level, as it were. Billions of naira were paid to faceless third parties each month to secure Nigeria’s O&G infrastructure operations. However, Obasanjo’s successor, Umaru Musa Yar’Adua, saw the foolhardiness in the carrot and promptly stopped it, while intensifying the stick for a very limited period. He subsequently declared an Amnesty window during which militants were invited to surrender their arms. The militants responded in their numbers, and relative peace seemed to be returning to the Niger Delta when Yar’Adua succumbed to a protracted illness. His successor, Goodluck Jonathan, an indigene of the Niger Delta, was apparently too emotionally immersed in the regional crises to continue his predecessor’s initiative firmly.

Soon after, it was status quo ante, and that trajectory has continued to this day. In the interval, a number of novel measures were introduced by successive civilian governments to mitigate the worsening crises in the Niger Delta region. First, it was resolved that 13 per cent of hydrocarbon proceeds should be paid to O&G-bearing states. Next, a Federal Ministry of Niger Delta was created, with a well-funded development commission – NDDC, under its supervision. Expectedly, the O&G sub-nationals would subsequently quickly set up their own O&G development commissions. Furthermore, the Petroleum Industry Act of 2021 made ample provisions for O&G companies to set aside 3 per cent of their operating profits for infrastructural projects in hydrocarbon-bearing communities.

In spite of the foregoing, however, the deteriorating economic and environmental conditions of the Niger Delta perplexingly persisted. Reported national oil production continues to fall short of Nigeria’s OPEC quota of 2-odd million barrels per day, even as whole swathes of the Niger Delta region remain an ecological nightmare.

And, in an apparent end-of-wit clandestine move, the FG then resorted to awarding so-called “Pipelines surveillance contracts” to non-state actors in the Niger Delta. Even that desperate initiative did not yield any measurable impact, going by NUPRC/NEITI 2025 data, which aggregated Nigeria’s yearly crude oil losses to theft and vandalism at about 20 million barrels since 2000!

What then is the answer to the Niger Delta conundrum? To persuasively answer this question would require interrogating a number of other related questions. First, what set of circumstances compelled the Niger Delta militants to start attacking the nation’s O&G assets in the first instance? Second, why couldn’t Nigeria’s renowned sub-regional military might promptly nip the emerging Niger Delta nuisance in the bud? Third, why did the “militants’ contagion” instead quickly spread across the region, assuming something of a regional culture?

The answer to the first question has since become a refrain: the socioeconomics of the peoples of the Niger Delta are not being positively impacted by the exploration and exploitation of the region’s hydrocarbon endowments, and amid industry-scale environmental degradation. The military solution fell far short because it didn’t at all seek to solve the issues raised by the first question. Then, when the stick woefully failed, the FG threw in some carrots (read: O&G deals) to placate the militants and their allies. Little wonder the contagion quickly spread when it became evident that blackmailing the FG has become the fastest path to superlative wealth. The latter phenomenon became so overwhelming that the belated attempts by the FG to address the issue of neglected socio-economics of the Niger Delta amounted to nothing; rather, the Ministry of Niger Delta, the NDDC, and her sub-national equivalents are always making the Headlines for scandalous reasons.

We thus come full circle, and this is the crux of the conundrum: what stirred the angst of the militants in the first instance? That is the pertinent question, which the military solution utterly failed to address, and to which we had suggested an answer back in 2020, in an article in ThisDay newspaper, “The tragedy of NDDC”, from which we should like to quote in extenso. “Fledging nations should always regard pooling of funds for unproductive activities as a devastating plague. Furthermore, global bodies like the World Bank, the International Monetary Fund, and the European Union have since availed humanity of cost-effective and sustainable models for developing the infrastructure and socioeconomics of local communities. Those models postulate that the latter’s budgets be effectively captured into project costing, rather than setting aside ad hoc entities to redistribute pooled funds.”

In our considered opinion, therefore, anything short of the aforesaid prescription would fail to abate the agitations in the Niger Delta because, as borne out of various reports on the Niger Delta crises, the agitators want their living standards to be brought to parity with those of International Oil Companies (IOCs) personnel in the region. As anyone with even cursory knowledge of the region would attest, the living standards of the IOCs’ personnel compare favourably with those of the First World. If the IOCs could create First World conditions from the slums and chaos of the Niger Delta, then it is no-brainer that the people of the region would expect nothing less from the IOCs. The operative phrase is, “from the IOCs”. Money is not everything; the management of it is! Throwing trillions of naira at the Niger Delta conundrum without well-thought-through project management WILL NOT ABATE the decades-old menace. We believe the IOCs’ proven project-management capacity is the missing elixir; we strongly recommend it, much in the manner our existing Laws (Environmental Acts), in line with the World Bank’s directives, insist.

Indeed, a universal aphorism supports the above proposition: to effectively change a people’s mindset, change their environment. As a matter of utmost urgency, therefore, the FG should abolish pipeline surveillance contracts and enact Laws mandating entities engaging in massive extraction and processing of our natural resources to be directly responsible for the development and/or re-development of impacted local communities.

Godwin Nkemdiche, a consulting engineer, writes from Abuja

The post Abolish pipeline surveillance contracts appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: We will adhere to CAS decision – CAF president
description:
Confederation of African Football president Patrice Motsepe has assured that the continental governing body will respect and implement the Court of Arbitration for Sport’s ruling reinstating Senegal as winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations.
CAS on Tuesday upheld Senegal’s appeal against the CAF
content:
Confederation of African Football president Patrice Motsepe has assured that the continental governing body will respect and implement the Court of Arbitration for Sport’s ruling reinstating Senegal as winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations.

CAS on Tuesday upheld Senegal’s appeal against the CAF Appeals Board’s ruling, which had awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory after Senegal’s players temporarily walked off the pitch in protest during the January 18 final in Rabat.

The tribunal consequently set aside the Appeals Board’s decision and reinstated the ruling of CAF’s Disciplinary Board, confirming Senegal’s original 1-0 victory over the hosts after extra time.

Motsepe said CAF’s commitment to its 54 member associations and the integrity of the game required it to abide by the verdict of the Lausanne-based tribunal, which overturned the decision to strip Senegal of their title and award it to Morocco.

“My commitment and the commitment of CAF is to all the 54 member association countries, and whatever decision comes out of CAS, we will respect and adhere to it because it is very important, and the integrity of the game and the credibility of the game are not negotiable,” Motsepe said.

However, Morocco have renewed their protest against the outcome, insisting they will pursue all available legal avenues to challenge the ruling.

The Royal Moroccan Football Federation expressed its dissatisfaction with Tuesday’s decision, questioning the handling of the arbitration proceedings and the interpretation of the laws governing the controversial final.

“The Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest at the failure to consider its request to take into account the necessary legal consequences for practices that could compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration process, particularly the confirmed communication between German arbitrator Ulrich Haas and the President of the Senegalese Football Federation 48 hours before the decision was issued,” the statement read.

The Moroccan federation also confirmed its intention to challenge the verdict, stating, “Accordingly, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation confirms its intention to pursue all available legal avenues to appeal the Court of Arbitration for Sport’s decision.”

Senegal, however, swiftly dismissed the allegations, describing the Moroccan claims as “fake news”, according to French sports outlet RMC Sport.

The CAS ruling means Senegal have been officially restored as AFCON champions, securing their second continental title after their maiden triumph in Cameroon 2021.

title: Osimhen, Okoye, Ajayi lead Nigerian MOTM winners abroad
description:
Victor Osimhen, Maduka Okoye and Semi Ajayi are among at least nine Nigerian footballers to have been named Man of The Match for their clubs abroad this season, with Osimhen’s award coming from UEFA and Ajayi’s from the Premier League, PETER AKINBO writes

Osimhen (Galatasaray)
Osimhen received the
content:
Victor Osimhen, Maduka Okoye and Semi Ajayi are among at least nine Nigerian footballers to have been named Man of The Match for their clubs abroad this season, with Osimhen’s award coming from UEFA and Ajayi’s from the Premier League, PETER AKINBO writes

Osimhen (Galatasaray)

Osimhen received the official UEFA Man of The Match award after Galatasaray beat his former club Lille 4-2 in the Champions League on October 21. The result gave the Turkish champions their first points of the campaign.

The striker scored the fourth goal in the 61st minute, and he did not celebrate it out of respect for Lille, where he played during the 2019/20 season. The strike took his Champions League tally to 17 goals, extending his record as Nigeria’s highest-scoring player in the competition proper.

The award drew some debate. Galatasaray officials and players were reportedly surprised that he was picked ahead of Batrakov, while former Turkish referee Ahmet Çakar argued that at least three of his teammates were just as worthy.

The 27-year-old is no stranger to the honour. UEFA data showed he had the most Man of The Match awards in the 2025/26 Champions League at that stage of the season, with four.

Arokodare (Ajax)

Arokodare won Ajax’s Player of The Match award after scoring twice on his first start for the club in a 5-3 win over Sion at the Johan Cruijff Arena on August 27. Ajax announced the award on their official account.

One of his goals came in first-half stoppage time, to make it 3-2, from a cross by Abdellah Ouazane. He also hit the crossbar, and his 9.0 rating from FotMob was the highest of any Ajax player on the night.

The result sent Ajax through 9-5 on aggregate and into the Conference League league phase. He had also scored and provided an assist in the 4-2 first-leg win in Switzerland on August 20.

Okoye (Udinese)

Okoye was named Man of The Match after saving a penalty in Udinese’s 0-0 draw away to Parma in Serie A. The point ended a run of six straight league defeats for the Italian club.

Parma were awarded the spot-kick in the 68th minute after a lengthy VAR review, and Adrián Bernabé took it two minutes later. Okoye guessed correctly, dived low to his left and kept out the effort. The penalty followed his own fumble of a corner, with the ball striking James Abankwah’s arm.

Udinese had conceded 18 goals in their opening eight league games without keeping a clean sheet, so the result was a welcome change. SofaScore gave the goalkeeper a 7.3 rating, level with Jürgen Ekkelenkamp.

Speaking via Udinese’s official webpage, Okoye said, “The penalty save was pure instinct.” He also told reporters, “We always want to win, and we need points.”

Ajayi (Hull City)

Ajayi won both Man of The Match awards after Hull City drew 1-1 with Brentford at the MKM Stadium on October 25. He took the Premier League’s Player of the Match award and Hull’s fan poll.

He received 43.6 per cent of the vote in the club poll, ahead of Oli McBurnie, Tim Iroegbunam and Lewis Coyle. McBurnie scored for Hull, while Dango Ouattara equalised for Brentford.

Hull went into the game with nine points from their opening seven league matches. The newly promoted side were unbeaten in nothing but spirit, as Ajayi said after the match that a point at home is always positive.

The defender had earlier scored in the 17th minute of Hull’s 2-0 win over Manchester United on August 22. It was Hull’s first top-flight goal in nine years, and Ajayi’s first in the Premier League since the 2020/21 season with West Bromwich Albion.

Ilenikhena (Al-Ittihad)

George Ilenikhena was reported as the official Man of The Match after scoring and providing an assist in Al-Ittihad’s 4-1 win over Al-Ettifaq in the Saudi Pro League on October 20.

He opened the scoring in the 16th minute, and Youssef En-Nesyri added a brace late on, in the 80th and 85th minutes. The win ended a two-game losing run for Al-Ittihad, in which Ilenikhena had missed the defeat at Al-Hilal through fitness issues and returned from a minor injury in the loss to Shabab Al-Ahli.

Three days later, he opened the scoring in the 30th minute of the 2-0 win over Al-Diriyah. Foot Africa put his tally at nine goals and three assists in 14 matches.

The 20-year-old also scored twice in the first 22 minutes of Al-Ittihad’s 2-1 win over Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al-Nassr on September 5, which ended Al-Nassr’s unbeaten start to the season. He was called up to the Super Eagles in September for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers.

Chukwueze (AC Milan)

Samuel Chukwueze was named Man of The Match on his 2026/27 debut as AC Milan won 2-1 at Torino in their Serie A opener on August 23.

He played at right wing-back under Ruben Amorim, a position he has not regularly occupied, and created four chances, more than any other player in the game. He also set up Adrien Rabiot’s goal in the 66th minute, two minutes after Alphadjo Cisse’s Serie A debut goal. Che Adams pulled one back for Torino in stoppage time.

Chukwueze won three of his five ground duels, had the joint-most touches in the opposition box and earned an 8.3 rating from FotMob. Italian outlet Tuttomercatoweb said he was awarded the match MVP.

After the game, he said he was ready to operate as a wing-back for the full season. Milan’s own statistics showed he had been involved in three goals, all assists, in his last four Serie A matches, equalling his tally from his previous 25 appearances in the competition.

Bassey (Fulham)

Calvin Bassey was named Man of The Match after Fulham drew 1-1 at Aston Villa in the Premier League at Villa Park on October 31.

Villa went ahead through Nicolas Jackson in the 39th minute, before an own goal from goalkeeper Zion Suzuki in the 64th minute earned Fulham a point. Fulham, managed by Álvaro Arbeloa, had 55 per cent of possession and 14 shots, five of them on target.

The award is not new to the defender. Fulham’s supporters voted him their Man of The Match after the victories over Arsenal in January 2024 and Liverpool in April 2025, and after the narrow defeat to Manchester United in January 2025.

Nwabali (Chippa United)

Stanley Nwabali was named Man of The Match in Chippa United’s 0-0 draw with Golden Arrows in their South African Premier Soccer League opener. It was his first competitive game after an eight-month absence.

He made three saves in each half, and Golden Arrows were denied by the crossbar early in the second half. In added time, he kept the clean sheet with a point-blank save with his leg to deny Thokozani Khumalo. His six saves earned him a place in the league’s Team of The Week.

The 30-year-old has won the honour on a bigger stage before. He was the official CAF Man of the Match when Nigeria beat South Africa on penalties in the 2024 Africa Cup of Nations semi-final in Bouake, where he saved two spot-kicks.

Akinsola (Cercle Brugge)

Tunde Akinsola was named Man of The Match after scoring twice in Cercle Brugge’s 2-1 win over Royal Antwerp in the Belgian Pro League on November 1. They were his first goals for the club.

After a goalless first half, he broke the deadlock in the 48th minute and struck again in the 61st, with both goals set up by Steve Ngoura. Antwerp pulled one back in the 81st minute, but Cercle held on. Akinsola was replaced in the 71st minute.

He joined the club in September and had to wait until this match to open his account. Foot Africa described him as the driving force behind the victory.

Iheanacho (Bursaspor)

Iheanacho was not named Man of the Match, but beIN SPORTS named him the best player of the opening eight rounds of the Turkish 1. Lig.

The striker had scored 11 goals and provided two assists in his first eight league appearances after joining as a free agent from Celtic. He scored in every game, matching Fernandao’s Bursaspor record of eight consecutive league games with a goal. His last of those came in a brace in a 2-1 comeback win at Batman Petrolspor on September 19.

The post Osimhen, Okoye, Ajayi lead Nigerian MOTM winners abroad appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Zero-dose children: Lagos, Kano charged to sustain immunisation gains
description:
…As GSK-supported Save The Children BOOST project approaches 2027 close-outBy Sola Ogundipe



Lagos and Kano States have been urged to take full ownership of the Better Opportunities for Optimal Services and Targeted Immunisation for Zero-Dose and Under-Immunised Children (BOOST) programme towards
content:
…As GSK-supported Save The Children BOOST project approaches 2027 close-out
By Sola Ogundipe

Lagos and Kano States have been urged to take full ownership of the Better Opportunities for Optimal Services and Targeted Immunisation for Zero-Dose and Under-Immunised Children (BOOST) programme towards making adequate budgetary provisions to sustain its gains ahead of the project’s expected close-out in 2027.
The call came amid continuing efforts to bridge Nigeria’s zero-dose and under-immunisation gaps, with stakeholders warning that local ownership, sustainable financing and stronger primary healthcare delivery will be critical to ensuring that children are not left unprotected when donor-supported interventions end.
BOOST is a four-year initiative funded by GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) and implemented by Save the Children International (SCI) in Lagos and Kano States. It seeks to reduce the number of children who have never received routine vaccines or have missed important doses in their immunisation schedules.
The programme is built around the principle that no child should be left unprotected against vaccine-preventable diseases because of where they live, their family’s economic circumstances or weaknesses in the healthcare system.

Stakeholders who made the call in Abuja during the Lessons Learning and Transition Planning Workshop organised by SCI with support from GSK, urged government officials and civil society organisations from both states to review the project’s sustainability prospects, share best practices and develop strategies for transferring successful interventions to government-led interventions.

Participants said sustaining improvements in immunisation coverage and reducing the number of zero-dose and under-immunised children would depend on state governments adopting successful project innovations, strengthening partnerships with civil society organisations and maintaining community engagement beyond the programme’s lifespan.

The Policy and Advocacy Coordinator of the GSK-supported BOOST Project in Lagos State, Dr Itunu Dave-Agboola, said the programme had recorded significant improvements in immunisation coverage and acceptance across its intervention local government areas.

“I would say the project has been successful because, looking at data coming in from the intervention LGAs, there’s a significant improvement in immunisation coverage and acceptance. We have enjoyed effective collaboration from the governments of both states, both at the level of the Ministry of Health and Primary Health Care Board. They have been very supportive and collaborative. We supported them to implement a lot of their activities.

“The collaboration is a strong one such that we see sustainability even beyond the life of the BOOST project, because that is the most important thing, sustainability, so that the gains of this project will not be lost in transit,” she said.

She explained that the four-year intervention focused on three thematic areas: service delivery, social and behaviour change communication, and advocacy.

According to her, participants examined interventions under the three areas and identified approaches that could be replicated, adapted or sustained after the programme ends.

She added that for civil society organisations, sustaining the gains would require more than continued advocacy, stressing the need to build independent institutional structures and mobilise resources.

The Secretary of the Advocacy Subcommittee of LASAM, Revd Bola Nuga, said the workshop provided an opportunity to learn from Kano’s experiences and identify successful approaches that could be adapted to strengthen advocacy in Lagos.

He described the engagement as an eye-opener, particularly in understanding how the two states had implemented BOOST interventions and how their experiences could inform future advocacy strategies.

Nuga disclosed that Save the Children was considering further support for the advocacy subcommittees in Lagos and the Kano Community of Practice to enable them to become formally registered and institutionalised.

“Formal registration would strengthen capacity to access funding from local and international sources and sustain their activities beyond direct support from Save the Children. They plan to provide more support to the subcommittees of LASAM and the Kano Community of Practice to see how they can be institutionalised in terms of registration so that they can access funds, which is key,” he said.

He said the proposed institutionalisation was particularly important as the project approaches its conclusion, noting that civil society organisations would need the capacity to continue engaging governments and advocating policies and interventions that protect children still unreached by routine immunisation.

Also speaking, the Project Manager of the Community of Practice (CoP), Save the Children, Kano, Ablai Magama, said the workshop enabled stakeholders to conduct a comprehensive review of the programme, noting that senior government officials and other participants actively contributed to identifying challenges and proposing solutions.

He said eliminating zero-dose and under-immunisation would require collective responsibility involving government, traditional and religious institutions, caregivers, communities, the media and relevant ministries and agencies.

“The governments must ensure consistent vaccine availability while working with traditional and religious leaders to address myths and misconceptions that contribute to vaccine hesitancy. The experiences shared by Lagos and Kano demonstrated that sustained collaboration between government and civil society organisations could help reduce the number of children missing essential vaccines,” he said.

Magama said ministries responsible for economic planning and budgeting, youth and social development, women’s affairs and poverty alleviation also had important roles to play in sustaining immunisation efforts and closing existing gaps.

“A major gap in vaccine acceptance has to do with the caregivers, and we need to identify the issues that promote hesitancy. Once we can identify those barriers and overcome them, there will be greater acceptance. So we move closer to the eradication of zero-dose and under-immunisation,” he stated.

On his part, the Chairman of the Evidence Subcommittee of LASAM, Mr Basit Baruwa, said the partnership had helped Lagos identify and reach zero-dose children in underserved communities, particularly in local government areas where access to routine immunisation services had remained difficult.

He said the programme’s technical and financial support had been significant, contributing to improvements in maternal and child health outcomes, particularly immunisation coverage in areas such as Ikorodu and Alimosho.

“The BOOST programme in Lagos State has been a successful partnership. Through it, we have been able to identify and reach many zero-dose children in some of our local government areas and communities where reaching them would otherwise have been difficult.

“The improvements recorded over the past two to three years underscore the value of sustained collaboration between government and development partners, but the gains could be undermined if the state fails to establish a clear sustainability plan before the project winds down.

“Since the BOOST project is expected to end next year, we feel that the state government should take full ownership by ensuring that all the interventions and resources currently available through the project are sustained and captured in the state’s budget for 2027,” he said.

Beyond government funding, Baruwa called for broader local resource mobilisation, urging the state to engage more organisations and private-sector partners to support immunisation and other primary healthcare interventions.

He said expanding the pool of local partners would help reduce dependence on external funding and ensure continuity of services in communities currently benefiting from the programme.

Baruwa also described the peer-learning workshop as an opportunity for both states to exchange practical experiences and learn from each other’s approaches to reaching underserved populations.

He noted that despite their geographical differences, Lagos and Kano shared similarities in population dynamics and commercial activities, making the exchange particularly useful.

“There were several things we in Lagos had done that our colleagues could learn from, and we also gained valuable lessons from Kano. It was a mutually beneficial experience,” he said.

He advocated expanding the programme’s reach to more local government areas, stressing that government and development partners must work together to extend immunisation services beyond the communities currently covered.

The workshop recommended that state governments take full ownership of the programme’s interventions by ensuring that activities and resources currently supported by BOOST were sustained and reflected in their respective budgets.

Participants also called for expanded resource mobilisation to attract local organisations and private-sector partners, stressing that their involvement would be essential to sustaining immunisation services and protecting the gains recorded under the programme.

The post Zero-dose children: Lagos, Kano charged to sustain immunisation gains appeared first on Vanguard News.
