title: FG launches innovation hub to boost Borno’s digital economy
description:
The Federal Government, in partnership with IHS Nigeria and the Borno State Government, has inaugurated the Ambassador Babagana Kingibe Innovation Hub in Maiduguri to expand digital skills development, promote technological innovation and create economic opportunities for young people.
The facility,
content:
The Federal Government, in partnership with IHS Nigeria and the Borno State Government, has inaugurated the Ambassador Babagana Kingibe Innovation Hub in Maiduguri to expand digital skills development, promote technological innovation and create economic opportunities for young people.

The facility, commissioned on Monday by Vice-President Kashim Shettima, will also serve as a training and collaboration centre for participants in the Federal Government’s Three Million Technical Talent programme in Borno State.

According to a statement issued by the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy on Tuesday, the initiative forms part of efforts to extend digital opportunities beyond major urban centres and increase participation in Nigeria’s digital economy.

The statement read, “Vice President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Senator Kashim Shettima, today officially commissioned the Ambassador Babagana Kingibe Innovation Hub in Maiduguri, Borno State, reinforcing the Federal Government’s commitment to expanding digital opportunities, strengthening technical talent development and supporting innovation across the country.”

Speaking at the inauguration, Shettima commended the Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, Bosun Tijani, for expanding access to digital skills development across the country.

“His Ministry recognises that digital opportunities must reach Maiduguri and other communities within the state,” the Vice-President said.

Shettima described the 3MTT programme as an important intervention for equipping young Nigerians with the skills required to compete in the global digital economy.

He expressed optimism that the innovation hub would become a “playground of ideas”, providing young people in Borno with opportunities to demonstrate their capabilities and pursue careers in technology.

In his remarks, Tijani said the Federal Government was complementing investments in broadband infrastructure with technical skills development to ensure that Nigerians could benefit from improved connectivity.

“As we connect more communities, we are also helping more young people acquire the skills they need to make use of that connectivity,” the minister said.

Tijani disclosed that applications for the next cohort of the 3MTT programme were expected to open in December, adding that the Maiduguri facility would enable participants to collaborate on projects, develop professional portfolios and showcase their skills to prospective employers.

He urged young people in Borno to take ownership of the facility, noting that its long-term impact would depend on their participation and productive use of its resources.

The minister also highlighted other digital infrastructure interventions, including the National Digital Alphanumeric Postcode System, aimed at strengthening Nigeria’s digital ecosystem.

Borno State Governor, Babagana Zulum, welcomed the investments, describing improved internet connectivity as critical to economic development, employment generation and efforts to address security challenges.

Zulum disclosed that several local government areas in the state still lacked adequate connectivity, expressing his administration’s readiness to collaborate with the Federal Government to bridge the gap.

“I therefore express my political will and commitment to partner with the Ministry of Communications, Innovation & Digital Economy to ensure the sustainability of all the projects coming through the support of the Ministry,” the governor said.

The ministry added that the innovation hub complemented its broader digital development strategy, which includes Project BRIDGE, technical talent development and the establishment of community-based innovation centres.

It reaffirmed its commitment to working with state governments, development partners and private sector organisations to expand digital access and create opportunities for technology-driven businesses.

The PUNCH reports that Project BRIDGE is a $2bn public-private partnership initiative designed to deploy 90,000 kilometres of fibre-optic infrastructure across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, connecting all local government areas, with financing from the World Bank, African Development Bank and European Bank for Reconstruction and Development

The post FG launches innovation hub to boost Borno’s digital economy appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NGX market capitalisation sheds N515bn as equities dip
description:

Similarly, the All-Share Index dropped by 793.03 points to finish at 245,685.87 compared with 246,478.90 o
content:
Equities trading on the Nigerian Exchange Limited closed lower on Tuesday, as market capitalisation declined by N514.91bn to settle at N159.52tn from N160.04tn recorded in the previous session.

Similarly, the All-Share Index dropped by 793.03 points to finish at 245,685.87 compared with 246,478.90 on Monday.

Across equities trading, a total of 31,609 trades were executed on 489,436,237 volumes. On the Main Board, investors exchanged 421,644,103 shares across 19,650 deals.

Within the financial services space, Access Holdings Plc gained 5.06 per cent to close at N27.00 with 19,983,044 shares traded across 1,381 deals, while First HoldCo Plc rose 0.53 per cent to N103.55 on 9,232,721 volume.

Conversely, Zenith Bank Plc slipped 3.23 per cent to N105.00 on 12,758,063 shares, and United Bank for Africa Plc shed 2.56 per cent to N38.00 on 8,264,580 shares.

On the Main Board, Fidelity Bank Plc edged up 0.45 per cent to N22.20 on 15,706,299 shares, while Guaranty Trust Holding Company Plc lost 0.89 per cent to N111.00 and Sterling Financial Holdings Company Plc dipped 3.07 per cent to N74.90.

Insurance stocks recorded mixed price movements during the session, with Cornerstone Insurance Plc, NEM Insurance Plc, and Sunu Assurances Nigeria Plc each advancing 10.00 per cent to N6.05, N30.80, and N2.86, respectively. AIICO Insurance Plc rose 9.91 per cent to N4.77 on 72,092,356 shares, while Mutual Benefits Assurance Plc gained 7.77 per cent to N3.05 on 23,641,213 shares.

On the downside, Guinea Insurance Plc dropped 7.53 per cent to N0.86, Fortis Global Insurance Plc fell 7.41 per cent to N1.50, and International Energy Insurance Plc lost 5.00 per cent to N2.00.

On the Main Board, Unilever Nigeria Plc fell 9.98 per cent to N101.00, Legend Internet Plc declined 9.72 per cent to N3.25, and Omatek Ventures Plc lost 9.66 per cent to N1.31, while FCMB Group Plc rose 7.23 per cent to N12.60 on 54,054,267 shares.

Key sector gauges closed mixed to lower as the NGX Banking Index eased from 2,266.95 to 2,256.23 and the NGX Pension Index moved from 12,161.75 to 12,116.73, whereas the NGX Insurance Index rose from 1,129.35 to 1,185.90.

Trading in exchange-traded product securities recorded 567 deals involving 152,022 units, led by Meristem Value Exchange Traded Fund (+6.60 per centto N136.45), Vetiva S & P Nigeria Sovereign Bond ETF (+5.05 per cent to N197.90), and Lotus Halal Equity ETF (+4.00 per cent to N125.00), while The Siaml Pension ETF 40 dropped 6.94 per cent to N1,340.00.

Bonds trading accounted for 14 deals and 139,374 units overall, including 15 per cent TAJ SUKUK S1 rising 11.32 per cent to N99.85 on one deal of 10,140 units and 19.75 per cent FGN MAY 2032 easing 8.19 per cent to N110.17.

title: SUNU Assurances chairman, vice-chairman exit after nine years
description:
SUNU Assurances Nigeria Plc has announced the exit of its board chairman, Kyari Bukar, and vice-chairman, Taizir Ajala, following the expiration of their nine-year tenures as Independent Non-Executive Directors.
The company disclosed this in a notice filed with the Nigerian Exchange Limited on Tuesd
content:
SUNU Assurances Nigeria Plc has announced the exit of its board chairman, Kyari Bukar, and vice-chairman, Taizir Ajala, following the expiration of their nine-year tenures as Independent Non-Executive Directors.

The company disclosed this in a notice filed with the Nigerian Exchange Limited on Tuesday, saying the departures took effect on 23 October, 2026.

Bukar and Ajala completaed the maximum nine-year tenure allowed for Independent Non-Executive Directors under the National Insurance Commission’s Corporate Governance Guidelines for Insurance and Reinsurance Companies in Nigeria, 2021.

Bukar served as Chairman of the Board, while Ajala occupied the position of Vice-Chairman.

Their exits mark changes in the leadership of the insurer’s board, although the company did not announce replacements or disclose when new appointments would be made.

SUNU Assurances said the two directors contributed to its strategic direction, corporate governance and institutional development during their years on the board.

The insurer also credited them with strengthening board oversight and providing strategic guidance during important stages of its development.

The board and management thanked the outgoing directors for their services and contributions to the company’s growth.

The disclosure was signed by Company Secretary and Head of Legal, Taiwo Kuku, in compliance with the Nigerian Exchange’s post-listing disclosure requirements.

The post SUNU Assurances chairman, vice-chairman exit after nine years appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Man City’s struggles continue with 2-2 draw against Napoli in Champions League
description:
Manchester City’s struggles continued on Tuesday as they were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw against Napoli in their UEFA Champions League encounter at the Etihad Stadium.
The hosts twice fought back from a goal down to earn a point, but the result did little to ease concerns over their recent perf
content:
Manchester City’s struggles continued on Tuesday as they were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw against Napoli in their UEFA Champions League encounter at the Etihad Stadium.

The hosts twice fought back from a goal down to earn a point, but the result did little to ease concerns over their recent performances following a difficult run in domestic competition.

After a goalless first half, Napoli took the lead 10 minutes after the restart through Rasmus Højlund, who finished off a pass from Billy Gilmour.

City responded in the 67th minute when Ayyoub Bouaddi scored his first goal for the club, with substitute Jérémy Doku providing the assist.

Napoli, however, regained the lead nine minutes later as Noa Lang volleyed home a cross from Leonardo Spinazzola to put the visitors 2-1 ahead.

Manchester City refused to give up, and Rayan Cherki rescued a point for the home side five minutes from full time with a well-taken finish past the Napoli goalkeeper.

The encounter also marked Kevin De Bruyne’s return to the Etihad Stadium. The former City midfielder received a warm reception from the home supporters.

Despite enjoying large spells of possession, City struggled to convert their dominance into clear-cut scoring opportunities, while Napoli remained dangerous on the counterattack.

The draw followed a disappointing domestic run in which City had gone four consecutive Premier League matches without a victory. They suffered defeats to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest before playing out a 1-1 draw against Fulham at the weekend.

Tuesday’s result will therefore offer limited consolation to City as they continue their search for consistency.

The post Man City’s struggles continue with 2-2 draw against Napoli in Champions League appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Bayelsa boat accident: Ending the cycle of tragedies
description: It was Nigerian singer, Oritsefemi, who, in 2013, released “Double Wahala,” which became a hit across radio stations. The song, a tribute to the legendary Fela Anikulapo-Kuti, featured the memorable refrain, “Double wahala for dead body and the owner of dem body.” The line alludes to the multiple la
content:
It was Nigerian singer, Oritsefemi, who, in 2013, released “Double Wahala,” which became a hit across radio stations. The song, a tribute to the legendary Fela Anikulapo-Kuti, featured the memorable refrain, “Double wahala for dead body and the owner of dem body.” The line alludes to the multiple layers of trouble that can accompany an unfortunate situation.

Thirteen years after the release of that hit song, it rang loudly in my ears on Friday, November 20, when news filtered in that a boat accident had occurred in Bayelsa State, with many passengers feared dead. But rather than move my body to the rhythm of the song, this time, I was heartbroken.

What is the connection between the song and the accident? The passengers were reportedly mainly mourners travelling from Ayama to Ukubie for a burial ceremony when their boat capsized around the Oweikorogha–Otuan river junction in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area. They set out to attend a funeral, but their journey ended with their families, unfortunately, preparing for more burials.

As of Sunday, the death toll was put at 29. This is not just a number. These were 29 people who left home with plans, responsibilities and loved ones expecting their return. They were someone’s parents, children, siblings or relatives. Some may have been breadwinners. Whatever their individual circumstances, they deserved to arrive safely.

There is something we must understand: travelling by boat in many riverine communities is not optional. It is not about tourism or recreation. Unlike residents of cities with extensive road networks, many Nigerians living in coastal and riverine communities rely on boats to reach schools, hospitals, markets, workplaces, places of worship and neighbouring settlements.

For these people, there is often no practical alternative because their destinations are accessible mainly by water. When a mode of transportation is essential to daily life, government must make its safety a public service priority.

While the precise cause of this latest tragedy may not yet have been established, several recurring risk factors have been identified in previous boat accidents. These include overcrowding, inadequate life jackets, poorly maintained boats, inexperienced operators, unsafe night travel, adverse weather conditions, weak regulatory enforcement and limited emergency response capacity.

We should not still be debating the necessity of life jackets for passengers in 2026. A life jacket should be as fundamental to a commercial boat journey as a seat belt is to travelling by car.

Yet, the challenge is not merely making life jackets available. They must be serviceable, properly fitted and worn throughout the journey. A life jacket stored under a seat or tied to the roof of a boat is of little use to a passenger thrown into the water.

Another problem plaguing us as a nation is our limited capacity to rescue accident victims promptly. This is not even restricted to the waterways. I have previously discussed this problem on this page in relation to road crashes and emergency response.

Even with strong preventive measures, emergencies can occur. What often makes the difference between survival and death is how quickly help arrives.

In riverine communities, rescue operations may depend heavily on local fishermen, divers, boat operators and residents who rush to the scene before official emergency responders arrive.

When a boat capsizes, passengers struggling to stay afloat do not have the luxury of waiting for government officials to hold meetings before help arrives. Every minute matters.

The difference between a successful rescue and the recovery of bodies may depend on the availability of rescue equipment, trained personnel and effective communication. We must, therefore, ask whether our waterways have the emergency infrastructure required to protect those who depend on them.

Whenever tragedies like this occur, Nigeria is never short of condolence messages and, sometimes, donations. With the elections approaching, such messages are not restricted to government officials. Candidates of different political parties seeking various elective offices are usually quick to join in expressing sympathy.

Condolences and donations are good, but they are not enough. There is a clear difference between responding to a tragedy and preventing another. Government cannot continue to measure its response to disasters only by the amount of money donated to grieving families. We should also measure its commitment by the safety measures put in place to ensure that other families do not suffer similar losses.

The National Inland Waterways Authority has responsibilities relating to inland waterway regulation and safety. State governments, marine police units, emergency management agencies and local authorities also have relevant roles to play. With so many institutions having responsibilities for waterway safety, Nigerians should not be left wondering who is accountable when something goes wrong.

The Bayelsa tragedy is not an isolated incident. There have been similar tragedies in Niger, Kebbi and other states where water transportation is common, with varying degrees of human loss.

Each disaster generates public outrage, condolences and promises of stronger regulation. We have listened to explanations about safety violations, heard promises of tougher enforcement and watched government officials visit grieving communities. Yet, the tragedies continue.

At what point do we stop treating these disasters as isolated misfortunes and begin addressing the weaknesses that make them recur? What have we learnt from the lives already lost? Going forward, regulatory authorities must ensure that every commercial passenger boat carries sufficient approved, properly fitted life jackets and that passengers wear them throughout their journeys.

They should ensure regular boat inspections, enforce passenger capacity limits and establish effective maintenance standards. They should also ensure that commercial boat operators receive practical training in navigation, emergency procedures and passenger safety.

In the area of rescue operations, the relevant authorities should position trained marine rescue teams and appropriate equipment along busy routes and near high-risk locations.

Public safety campaigns should also be taken seriously. Radio programmes in local languages, notices at jetties and engagement with community associations can be used to educate passengers and boat operators on safety precautions and emergency procedures.

The findings of investigations into major boat accidents should also be made public, alongside the measures being taken to prevent a recurrence. Where negligence or violations of safety regulations are established, those responsible should be held accountable.

Preventing another tragedy does not require government to reinvent the wheel. Many of the necessary precautions are already known. What is missing, too often, is consistent implementation.

Safety enforcement should not be an occasional exercise conducted in the aftermath of a disaster. It must become a routine part of water transportation, just as vehicle roadworthiness checks and aviation safety inspections are expected to be.

Many people travelling by boat are ordinary Nigerians with limited financial resources. Safety regulations must not become another opportunity to extort operators and passengers or impose unaffordable costs without providing practical alternatives.

The government should consider supporting the provision of affordable life jackets, safer boats and improved jetties, particularly in underserved riverine communities.

Waterway safety must not become a privilege available only to passengers who can afford expensive boats. The life of a market woman crossing a river is as valuable as that of a wealthy Nigerian travelling in a private vessel.

The passengers who boarded that ill-fated boat in Bayelsa State on November 20 were undertaking what should have been a routine journey. They went to mourn the dead but ended up being mourned themselves.

Their families deserve sympathy, support and answers. But beyond these, other Nigerians who depend on water transportation deserve assurances, backed by concrete action, that their next journey will not be their last.

The greatest tribute we can pay the victims of the Bayelsa tragedy is to ensure that other Nigerians do not lose their lives simply because they boarded a boat.

The post Bayelsa boat accident: Ending the cycle of tragedies appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Men key to ending gender-based violence – Lawyer
description:
Renowned human rights lawyer and former United Nations Special Rapporteur, Prof. Joy Ezeilo, SAN, has said that men hold the key to ending gender-based violence in Nigeria, urging them to become champions of positive change rather than silent bystanders.
Ezeilo stated this in her welcome remarks at
content:
Renowned human rights lawyer and former United Nations Special Rapporteur, Prof. Joy Ezeilo, SAN, has said that men hold the key to ending gender-based violence in Nigeria, urging them to become champions of positive change rather than silent bystanders.

Ezeilo stated this in her welcome remarks at the Male Champions Workshop on Positive Masculinity, Healthy Relationships, and the Prevention of Gender-Based Violence, organised by the Women’s Aid Collective (WACOL) in Ebonyi State, with support from the Ford Foundation Office for West Africa on Monday.

The workshop, she said, was grounded in a simple but powerful conviction: that men and boys play a critical role in preventing violence, promoting respect, and advancing gender equality.

“Across our communities, gender-based violence continues to undermine the safety, well-being, and potential of countless women, girls, and families. While this challenge is complex, so too is the opportunity before us. When men choose to become allies, advocates, and champions of positive change, they help create safer homes, healthier relationships, and stronger communities,” she added.

Ezeilo, a life bencher, stressed that the workshop was designed not merely as a learning event, but as a platform for reflection, dialogue, and action.

She explained that participants would examine the meaning of positive masculinity, explore the impact of social norms and gender expectations, discuss practical strategies for preventing violence, and strengthen their capacity to serve as role models and change agents.

“Silence sustains violence, but courageous leadership can break the cycle,” she declared.

The WACOL founder challenged participants to leave the workshop with a clear commitment, that is, “to become active champions of positive masculinity; to speak out against gender-based violence wherever it occurs; to model respectful, equitable, and healthy relationships; and to mentor other men and boys to do the same.”

Ezeilo reminded the gathering that “real transformation starts with personal commitment,” warning that “the true measure of our success will not be the quality of our discussions, but the actions we take when we return to our homes, workplaces, communities, faith organisations, and institutions.”

She urged the men to redefine strength not as dominance, but as respect; not as control, but as partnership; not as silence, but as standing up for what is right.

In her address, Dr. Izeduwa Derex-Briggs, Programme Officer at the Ford Foundation Office for West Africa, challenged participants to confront the privileges they enjoy as men and dismantle the patriarchal mindset that enables gender-based violence.

“I don’t think there’s any man I have met whose daughter would be beaten up by anybody, including the husband who paid the bride price, and would tolerate it.

“I’m yet to see any man who tolerates his mother being beaten up. Even if we grew up in an abusive home and you saw your father beating up your mother, you consciously tell yourself that you are waiting for the day you can challenge your dad and actually beat him up because he was beating up your mother—but when it comes to your wife, the relationship is totally different. When it comes to your sister, the relationship is totally different.”

She explained that her decision to attend the workshop was driven by a desire to understand the mindset of those being targeted for change.

Derex-Briggs challenged participants to become agents of change in their religious institutions and communities.

“We want you in the room taking part in this workshop to be that agent of change. We want you to actually talk to your religious leader in the church where you worship and say, the interpretation of this is wrong,” she said.

She cited successful advocacy efforts that led to women being included in traditional councils previously considered taboo.

“There are cultures that state that a woman doesn’t sit on the traditional council. I can tell you the number of traditional councils where women have now been included, something that used to be taboo. Today, it is no longer so because of sustained advocacy and because certain gender-responsive men pushed back and supported the changes.

Derex-Briggs disclosed that a network of male feminists in Nigeria now boasts over 15,000 men actively speaking out against gender-based violence, with an additional 8,000 men seeking to join.

“Right now, we have a network of male feminists in Nigeria, and there are over 15,000 men in that network who are speaking up and saying, No, we can’t allow this to happen’—including traditional and community leaders who are members of this new network. We also have about 8,000 men who say they want to become members of the network, though they haven’t formally subscribed yet.

“So, things are happening, movements are being created, and things are changing because like-minded people are saying this is not right. Boys and girls are born equal, and as they grow up, we cannot segregate them into who should have rights and who should not,” she said.

She urged participants to keep an open mind, adding: “I’m hoping that even in a room of 40 men, if we can get 10 male champions, we will have achieved something.”

The post Men key to ending gender-based violence – Lawyer appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NDC campaign violence: Police summon Omo-Agege, Delta gov mourns six
description: Delta State Police Command has invited former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege among some key political actors, and other persons of interest connected with the recent political violence during the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) campaign at Uduere, Ughelli North Local Govern
content:
Delta State Police Command has invited former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege among some key political actors, and other persons of interest connected with the recent political violence during the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) campaign at Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area, to report to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Delta State Police Command Headquarters, Asaba, in furtherance of the ongoing investigation into the incident.

This is as the state governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, on Tuesday, ordered security agencies to track down and arrest those responsible for the deadly political violence.

The police invitation was contained in a statement issued on Tuesday by the state Police Public Relations Officer for the Command, SP Bright Edafe, copies of which were made available to journalists in Warri.

The statement noted that “the invitations form part of ongoing investigations aimed at establishing their level of involvement in the incident”.

Those being invited by the police command, and the dates specified against their respective names, according to the statement, are Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, NDC Senatorial Candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District (Thursday, 26th November 2026 at 1100hrs); Hon. Jaro Movudu Egbo, Chairman, Ughelli North Local Government Council, Delta State (Thursday, 26th November 2026 at 1400hrs); Gowon Egoide, Former Chairman of Uduere Quarters, Ughelli North LGA, Delta State (Friday, 27th November 2026, at 1200hrs).

Others are Onoriode Oneya, incumbent Youth Chairman of Uduere Community, Ughelli North LGA, Delta State (Friday, 27th November 2026, at 1200hrs); Edirin Wokode Ewhubare, an associate of Gowon Egoide from Otowvodo, Ughelli North LGA, Delta State (Friday, 27th November 2026, at 1200hrs);

Erukaye Egoide, Nephew of Gowon Egoide (Friday, 27th November 2026, at 1200hrs); and Tony Gabon Mevowovo, an associate of Gowon Egoide (Friday, 27th November 2026, at 1200hrs).

Meanwhile, the State Commissioner of Police, CP Samuel Erale, has “urged all invited persons to honour the invitations as scheduled and cooperate fully with the Police”.

The CP noted that “the invitations are to the mentioned individuals only as the Command will not accept the presence of supporters and other persons not explicitly invited”.

He assured members of the public of a thorough and impartial investigation, emphasising that anyone found culpable will be brought to justice, irrespective of political affiliation or status.

‎

‎The CP further appealed to residents to remain calm and law-abiding as the investigation progresses.

‎

Meanwhile, the governor gave the directive during a visit to the community to assess the situation and reassure residents.

The attack occurred during a campaign visit by Omo-Agege, the Nigeria Democratic Congress candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections. His campaign organisation had initially reported that four people, including two of his aides, were killed when gunmen allegedly opened fire on the gathering.

The Nigeria Police Force confirmed on Tuesday that preliminary reports indicated that six people had died, while several others sustained injuries.

Among those identified by Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation as victims were Moses Anaughe, a former member of the Delta State House of Assembly and aide to the former senator, and the Urhobo youth activist, Akima Efemena Umukoro.

The violence prompted the Delta State Government to impose a dusk-to-dawn curfew across the Ughelli North Local Government Area, restricting movement between 6pm and 6am daily until further notice.

The police have also commenced an investigation into the incident, with the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, directing a thorough and impartial probe to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack, identify those responsible and examine the conduct of officers deployed to the venue.

Oborevwori described the killings as unfortunate and unacceptable, insisting that those responsible would face the full weight of the law.

“No political disagreement or ambition is worth the loss of human lives,” the governor said, warning that his administration would not tolerate any attempt to undermine peace and security in the state.

Before proceeding to Uduere, Oborevwori had held a security meeting with heads of security agencies at the Area Command Office in Ughelli.

He was accompanied to the community by the State Commissioner of Police, Samuel Erale; Commander of the 63 Brigade of the Nigerian Army, Brigadier General Ibrahim Buhari; the State Director of the Department of State Services; and other security officials.

Addressing journalists during the visit, the governor condemned the invasion of communities under the guise of political activities, describing the killing of fellow Nigerians over political differences as unconscionable.

He expressed disappointment that political disagreements could degenerate into violence and the killing of innocent people, particularly when his administration had worked to maintain relative peace in the state since assuming office in 2023.

Oborevwori said his administration remained committed to peace and security, noting that the fourth pillar of his MORE Agenda was specifically designed to promote a peaceful and secure environment across Delta State.

He said, “Those who know me know that I am not a violent person. That is why, in my MORE Agenda, the fourth pillar is dedicated to enhancing peace and security.

“We have been preaching peace, and Delta State has enjoyed relative peace since 2023. The important thing is how to sustain that peace. I want to assure the people that this will not happen again.”

The governor insisted that the perpetrators must be identified, apprehended and prosecuted, declaring that the state would not allow political activities to become a source of insecurity.

“This must stop. It must stop. We cannot continue like this,” he warned.

Oborevwori also observed that sustained peace and security were critical to economic development, stressing that businesses and investments could not thrive in an atmosphere of violence, fear and uncertainty.

He appealed to political leaders, supporters and other stakeholders to exercise restraint, shun political thuggery and avoid actions capable of triggering further violence.

The governor further charged the police and other security agencies to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the incident, arrest everyone connected to the killings and ensure that those found culpable were brought to justice.

The attack has heightened concerns about the safety of political campaigns and supporters ahead of the 2027 general elections, with the police urging political actors and residents to remain calm, comply with the curfew and avoid spreading unverified information.

The post NDC campaign violence: Police summon Omo-Agege, Delta gov mourns six appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Cornerstone, AIICO plan N858bn merger to create largest listed insurer
description:
Cornerstone Plc and AIICO Insurance Plc have announced plans to merge their businesses in a transaction that will create an insurance group with combined assets of N858bn and shareholders’ funds of N194bn.
The proposed merger, approved in principle by the boards of both companies, will also involve
content:
Cornerstone Plc and AIICO Insurance Plc have announced plans to merge their businesses in a transaction that will create an insurance group with combined assets of N858bn and shareholders’ funds of N194bn.

The proposed merger, approved in principle by the boards of both companies, will also involve two insurance subsidiaries of AIICO Insurance, according to a joint notification to the Nigerian Exchange Limited on Monday.

The companies said the enlarged entity was expected to become Nigeria’s largest listed insurance company by gross written premium, insurance revenue and capital.

The merged company will retain its listing on the Nigerian Exchange after the transaction is completed.

The combination will bring together AIICO’s life insurance, annuity and retail distribution operations with Cornerstone’s general insurance business and growing takaful operations.

The companies said the merger would expand their product offerings across life, general, health and takaful insurance, while providing a wider distribution network and greater capacity to serve individuals and businesses.

They added that the combined capital base would allow the group to underwrite larger risks, retain more business and increase investment in technology and product development.

The transaction comes as insurance companies face higher capital requirements and a risk-based capital framework introduced under the Nigerian Insurance Industry Reform Act.

Cornerstone and AIICO said their combined shareholders’ funds of N194bn and assets of N858bn would provide a stronger financial base for underwriting larger risks and meeting the industry’s changing regulatory requirements.

They also pointed to Nigeria’s low insurance penetration as an opportunity for the enlarged company to expand its market reach and provide insurance products to more individuals and businesses.

The merger will be executed through a Scheme of Merger, with the scheme document expected to contain the full transaction terms, including the share exchange ratio.

The document will be presented to shareholders of both companies for consideration.

Completion is subject to approvals from the National Insurance Commission, Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission, Securities and Exchange Commission and Nigerian Exchange Limited.

Shareholders of both companies must also approve the transaction at separate court-ordered meetings, while the Federal High Court must sanction the scheme.

The companies said existing policies and claims would remain valid, adding that their relationships with brokers, agents, reinsurers and bancassurance partners would be maintained.

Cornerstone, incorporated in 1991, became a public limited liability company in 1997. It recently completed its restructuring into a holding company, with subsidiaries providing general, life and takaful insurance services.

The companies did not disclose the proposed share exchange ratio or a timeline for completing the merger.

The post Cornerstone, AIICO plan N858bn merger to create largest listed insurer appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Omo-Agege kicks as court voids senatorial ticket
description: Former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, has rejected a Federal High Court judgment nullifying his nomination as the Nigeria Democratic Congress candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections, describing the ruling as inconsistent with documentary
content:
Former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, has rejected a Federal High Court judgment nullifying his nomination as the Nigeria Democratic Congress candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections, describing the ruling as inconsistent with documentary evidence and applicable law.

Omo-Agege, in a statement on Tuesday signed by his Media Adviser, Sunday Areh, said he had directed his legal team to immediately appeal the judgment delivered by the Federal High Court sitting in Warri, Delta State.

“While we respect the court, we strongly disagree with its decision. We believe that some of the findings do not reflect the documentary evidence presented before the court. Senator Omo-Agege has therefore directed his legal team to immediately challenge the judgment at the Court of Appeal,” the statement said.

The court had on Tuesday nullified Omo-Agege’s nomination, citing non-compliance with the provisions of the Electoral Act.

The judgment followed a suit marked FHC/WR/CS/120/2026, instituted by Prof. Alexander Osondu Akpodiete, challenging the validity of Omo-Agege’s nomination on grounds bordering on his resignation from the All Progressives Congress, membership of the NDC and eligibility to participate in the party’s senatorial primary.

Delivering the judgment, Justice Hyeladzira Ajiya Nganjiwa ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission to remove forthwith Omo-Agege’s name from its list of candidates for the election and restrained the former Deputy President of the Senate from parading himself as the NDC senatorial candidate.

Justice Nganjiwa dismissed all five preliminary objections raised by Omo-Agege, the NDC and INEC challenging the competence of the suit before proceeding to determine the substantive issues raised by the plaintiff.

The court held that the NDC failed to comply with the Electoral Act’s mandatory provisions on submitting its membership register to INEC before its primary election.

It also found that Omo-Agege’s name was not contained in the NDC membership register submitted to INEC at least 21 days before the conduct of the party’s primary election.

In addition, the court held that the NDC failed to provide credible evidence establishing that its membership register was subsequently updated and submitted to INEC within the statutory period preceding the primary.

However, Omo-Agege faulted the court’s finding that his name was missing from the register, insisting that both the NDC and INEC presented documents showing that he was included in the membership register submitted by the party.

“Both the NDC and INEC produced documents showing that Senator Omo-Agege’s name was in the membership register submitted by the party.

“There was only one register. The NDC did not submit two different registers or maintain competing membership records for the same primary election. Senator Omo-Agege’s name appeared in the register submitted to INEC,” the statement said.

It further claimed that INEC acknowledged receipt of the register and issued Certified True Copies of the document to several persons, with Omo-Agege’s name appearing on it.

The statement said the legal team would ask the Court of Appeal to examine the basis for the trial court’s finding that his name was missing from the register despite the documents presented by the party and the electoral commission.

Omo-Agege also questioned the legal standing of Akpodiete to institute the suit, arguing that the plaintiff did not obtain nomination forms, was not cleared by the party to contest, and was not listed among the participants in INEC’s official monitoring report on the primary election.

“The evidence before the court was that Prof. Akpodiete did not obtain the Nomination Forms required to participate in the party’s primaries. He was also not cleared by the party to contest, and his name did not appear among the participants listed in INEC’s official monitoring report on the primaries exercise,” the statement said.

It added that the plaintiff did not ask the court to declare him winner of the primary or award him the party’s ticket, but instead sought to invalidate Omo-Agege’s nomination.

The former Deputy Senate President also alleged that there had been attempts before the judgment to persuade INEC to remove his name from its final list of candidates, but said the commission declined after confirming that his name appeared in the membership register submitted by the NDC.

Describing the documents as official records, the statement maintained that they should be examined in their proper context during the appeal.

Omo-Agege said his decision to challenge the judgment should not be interpreted as disrespect for the judiciary, insisting that seeking appellate review was part of the judicial process.

“Those already celebrating this decision as the end of Senator Omo-Agege’s political journey should exercise patience. This is a judgment of the trial court, and the opportunity for appellate review remains. The legal process has not run its course,” the statement said.

The former lawmaker also reaffirmed his commitment to the NDC and the people of Delta Central, saying he would defend his political rights through lawful means.

Meanwhile, Justice Nganjiwa, relying on INEC’s revised electoral timetable, noted that Omo-Agege participated in the APC senatorial primary held on May 18, 2026, a development which, according to the court, established that he was still a member of the APC at the material time.

The judge maintained that only persons whose names appeared in a political party’s membership register, in accordance with the requirements of the Electoral Act, were eligible to participate in its primary elections.

On the admissibility of a previously withdrawn affidavit, the court held that a party was entitled to withdraw an affidavit already filed in a proceeding, adding that once withdrawn, such an affidavit ceased to form part of the court’s records and could not be relied upon in determining the matter.

Justice Nganjiwa further held that a valid nomination could not be founded on a process that failed to satisfy statutory requirements, stressing that where a political party failed to comply with the Electoral Act in nominating its candidate, INEC was not permitted to include such a candidate on the ballot.

To further highlight the setback for the NDC, the court held that the statutory window for conducting fresh primaries to nominate another candidate had elapsed, as the Electoral Act prescribed a timeline of 180 days before the general elections.

Consequently, the court invalidated Omo-Agege’s nomination, directed INEC to delist him and restrained him from presenting himself as the NDC candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the forthcoming general elections.

The certified copy of the court’s judgment was not available as of the time of filing this report.

The post Omo-Agege kicks as court voids senatorial ticket appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: T-bill yield climbs to 17.82% on sell-off
description:
Yields on Nigerian Treasury bills rose to an average of 17.82 per cent last week as investors sold off fixed-income securities ahead of an additional N600bn government debt auction.
The increase reflected cautious positioning in the secondary market as investors assessed the impact of fresh T-bill s
content:
Yields on Nigerian Treasury bills rose to an average of 17.82 per cent last week as investors sold off fixed-income securities ahead of an additional N600bn government debt auction.

The increase reflected cautious positioning in the secondary market as investors assessed the impact of fresh T-bill supply on yields and adjusted their portfolios in anticipation of the auction.

Market activity was largely bearish, with selling pressure particularly pronounced in the Open Market Operations segment, although some investors returned to the market towards the end of the week to take advantage of higher yields.

The sell-off came despite easing inflation, which had improved the attractiveness of naira-denominated fixed-income instruments by supporting positive real returns.

Earlier in the week, buying interest was recorded in short- and medium-term T-bills, outweighing yield increases at the longer end of the curve.

Newly issued T-bills maturing on 11 November, 2027, opened trading at quoted yields of 16.00 per cent and 15.80 per cent.

However, offers increased as investors began reducing their holdings, with market sentiment further influenced by the Central Bank of Nigeria’s announcement of an additional N600bn T-bill auction across standard maturities.

The additional supply prompted investors to reassess their positions ahead of the auction, amid expectations that the increased volume of government securities could influence market yields.

Investment firm, Comercio Partners, reported that selling pressure was particularly strong in the OMO segment, where the 16 March instrument traded at 18.20 per cent.

Although selling activity moderated towards the end of the week as some investors sought to lock in higher returns, overall trading remained subdued.

The 11 November, 2027 T-bill closed at quoted yields of 15.90 per cent and 15.80 per cent, while the broader market maintained a bearish trend.

Consequently, the average benchmark T-bill yield settled at 17.82 per cent.

The post T-bill yield climbs to 17.82% on sell-off appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: FESTAC residents threaten lawsuit over alleged LG caretaker committee plan
description: The leadership of the FESTAC Town Residents Association has threatened legal action against the Chairman of Amuwo Odofin Local Government Area, Prince Lanre Sanusi, and the Lagos State Police Command over alleged moves to impose caretaker committees on communities and stop scheduled association elec
content:
The leadership of the FESTAC Town Residents Association has threatened legal action against the Chairman of Amuwo Odofin Local Government Area, Prince Lanre Sanusi, and the Lagos State Police Command over alleged moves to impose caretaker committees on communities and stop scheduled association elections.

The president of the FTRA, Mohammed Adegbenro, made the allegation while speaking with reporters in FESTAC Town, Lagos.

Adegbenro said the association’s constitution provided for a three-year tenure, after which elections would be conducted to usher in new executives.

He said that with the tenures of the community executives expiring in November and that of the central leadership ending in December, the association had constituted an electoral committee to conduct elections across the five communities and the central body.

The FTRA president alleged that a former president, Sola Fakorede, and an aspirant who previously contested the presidency unsuccessfully had sought an alternative route to leadership after allegedly concluding that their preferred candidate might not win a contested election.

He alleged that the local government chairman invited FTRA leaders to what was presented as a reconciliation meeting, but later insisted that caretaker committees should be constituted for the communities as their tenures expired.

“Of course, there is no room in our constitution for such things. The only thing we have is your time when the tenure ends, and we conduct elections and bring in the new people coming,” Adegbenro said.

He alleged that after the FTRA executives rejected the proposal, the council chairman constituted a committee, reportedly headed by an elderly resident, to select caretaker committees for the communities.

“They just used him because he’s an elder. The old man also came and said, ‘Yes, we’re going to have a caretaker committee,’ the FTRA president alleged.

Adegbenro further alleged that following the association’s refusal to accept the caretaker committees, the local government chairman directed the police to stop the elections.

He said the Divisional Police Officer subsequently wrote to the association, postponing the elections based on unspecified “security reports.”

The FTRA president also alleged that on November 7, 2026, while Community 1 was holding its routine monthly meeting, the Area Commander for Area E arrived with a detachment of policemen and declared the meeting banned.

Adegbenro said the meeting had been held monthly for about 35 years across FESTAC’s five communities and more than 80 zones.

He alleged that the Area Commander threatened to arrest him and tear-gas the attendees, including elderly residents in their 90s, before he appealed to the residents to disperse peacefully.

“Till today, he has not been able to tell me what my offences are. Who complained? The only thing we heard was that the chairman of the local government directed the local commander to come and arrest me, simply because we said we wanted to conduct an election,” he said.

According to Adegbenro, subsequent visits to the Area Commander, the DPO and the Lagos State Commissioner of Police failed to resolve the dispute, alleging that the FTRA officials were not allowed to present their side.

“So, the Commissioner of Police also just dismissed us and told us there must not be any election. He did not even entertain any comment or question. He did not even listen to what we had to say,” he said.

Adegbenro said the association had commenced legal action over alleged violations of its members’ rights and interference in the affairs of a voluntary association.

He also appealed to the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, to intervene in the dispute ahead of FESTAC Town’s 50th anniversary in 2027.

“We have also taken some legal actions against the chairman of the local government. Who thinks FTRA is an appendage or a department in the local government?” he asked.

The association’s central executive election is scheduled for December, while the community elections were expected to hold this month.

However, responding to the allegations, a former chairman of the FTRA, Sola Fakorede, told PUNCH Metro on Monday that the claims were false.

“It is totally false. They are just spreading falsehoods,” Fakorede said.

He alleged that the incumbent FTRA chairman had taken decisions that contravened the association’s constitution.

“The allegation is not true. Reconciliation has been ongoing. It started shortly after the incumbent president came on board. Many of us have pointed out that he seemed to be high-handed and did not want to comply with the dictates of the constitution,” he said.

Fakorede said the dispute was partly over an amended constitution which, according to him, had not been properly communicated to members.

“He came with another constitutional issue, and we asked him which constitution he was talking about. He said it was an amended constitution. If the constitution was amended, we should all know. We should all know the dictates and content of the constitution,” he said.

He said the former executives told Adegbenro that he could not conduct an election under a constitution whose contents were not known to members.

Fakorede also denied that the local government chairman was attempting to impose a leadership on the association, saying the council chairman had instead offered to assist with printing copies of the constitution.

“We got to the local government; the chairman offered to pay for the printing of the constitution. He asked for the cost of printing the constitution and promised to give the association N1m for the purpose.

“I told the chairman that they can’t print what we have not passed. He took the meeting of the association to his house. We have the minutes of the meeting that was held in his house. He can’t pick the electoral chairman of the association in your house and impose him on us. If I had done that, he wouldn’t have become president,” Fakorede said.

He added that several other respected individuals had intervened in the dispute, including the local government chairman.

Meanwhile, the spokesperson for the Lagos State Police Command, Superintendent of Police Abimbola Adebisi, said she was not aware of the incident, having been away at a conference.

She, however, said the presence of policemen at the meeting could have been based on a complaint received by the police.

“However, for the police to have gone to where they were having their meeting, it could be as a result of the complaint that has been laid to them.

“The police in Area E or the FESTAC Division do not belong to the local government chairman. They are for everybody in that area. Everybody has free access to them. So, for them to have gone to their meeting, it may be as a result of a complaint or permission they were working on. I wouldn’t know. I will get the DPO to ascertain what actually transpired,” Adebisi said.

Attempts to speak with the local government chairman, Prince Lanre Sanusi, were unsuccessful, as he did not answer calls from our correspondent or respond to a message sent to his WhatsApp.

The FTRA said it was also preparing to celebrate the 50th anniversary of FESTAC Town in 2027.

The post FESTAC residents threaten lawsuit over alleged LG caretaker committee plan appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NANS, UNIOSUN clash over arrest, arraignment of three students
description:
The national leadership of the National Association of Nigerian Students and the management of Osun State University on Tuesday differed over the arraignment of three officials of the Students’ Union of the Government of the institution in court for assault.
PUNCH Metro reports that the NANS Nationa
content:
The national leadership of the National Association of Nigerian Students and the management of Osun State University on Tuesday differed over the arraignment of three officials of the Students’ Union of the Government of the institution in court for assault.

PUNCH Metro reports that the NANS National President, Babatunde Akinteye, in a statement, expressed concern over reports that the Vice-Chancellor of Osun State University, Prof. Clement Adebooye, allegedly ordered the arrest of the Students’ Union Government President of the university.

Akinteye also said the SUG president, after his arrest, was charged to court and remanded in prison.

He said the development was unacceptable, describing it as a direct affront to the rights and dignity of the students.

The NANS President’s statement further reads, “I have received disturbing reports that the Vice-Chancellor of Osun State University allegedly ordered the arrest of the Students’ Union Government President, who was subsequently charged to court and remanded in prison.

“Consequently, I have directed the NANS Zonal Coordinator and the Osun State JCC Chairman to immediately mobilise students for a coordinated shutdown of the university and a peaceful occupation of the Osun State Government Secretariat to demand the immediate removal of the Vice-Chancellor.

“Furthermore, all structures of NANS nationwide have been activated to fully relocate to Osun State until justice is served and the matter is decisively addressed. No university administrator should mistake the patience of Nigerian students for weakness. We will not fold our arms while the rights of our elected student representatives are trampled upon.”

But the university management, in a statement signed by the Public Relations Officer, Ademola Adesoji, said it had temporarily suspended all Students’ Union activities following an “alleged assault involving three student union executives and a 100-level student of the institution.”

Adesoji further disclosed that the decision was taken by the management to allow an investigation into the incident reported at night on Friday, November 20.

He identified the student allegedly assaulted as Emmanuel Onifade, a 100-level software engineering student, while the three students accused of perpetrating the act were identified as Layonu Idowu Akintayo, a 500-level medicine and surgery student who is the UNIOSUN Students’ Union president; Adesanmi Tijesunimi, a 400-level computer science student and assistant general secretary of the union; and Oyedeji Samsideen, a 400-level information technology student and faculty chairman.

The statement further read, “Preliminary findings indicated that the incident followed allegations that Onifade had used the university’s logo and the Office of Student Affairs as the identity of a WhatsApp platform. He was also accused of threatening Oyebode Oluwatobi Jomiloju Barnabas, a 200-level computer science student, over a video the latter had posted on social media concerning the university’s students.

“Oyebode reported the matter to the Students’ Union executives, after which the union president contacted Onifade and asked him to meet at the downtown area of the main campus. Onifade was subsequently taken by the Students’ Union in the union vehicle to a mechanic workshop in Osogbo, where he was thoroughly assaulted, beaten and brutalised by the Assistant General Secretary and others present.

“It was further alleged that Onifade was taken to another location, where he met the Students’ Union president and was assaulted again by the Assistant General Secretary and Samsideen. He was later released with serious bodily injuries. The victim’s father subsequently reported the incident at the Oja-Oba Divisional Police Headquarters in Oke Baale, Osogbo. The three students were handed over to the police and later charged before a magistrate’s court in Oke-Fia, Osogbo.

“They have reportedly been granted administrative bail, while the case has been adjourned until December 23, 2026.”

Responding to the incident, Adesoji said the university had temporarily suspended all Students’ Union activities until the issues surrounding this ugly event were resolved.

He reaffirmed UNIOSUN management’s commitment to the safety and welfare of students and urged members of the university community to conduct themselves responsibly and in accordance with the law.

The university said the suspension would remain in force until further notice.

The post NANS, UNIOSUN clash over arrest, arraignment of three students appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Paris Club refunds: Court freezes N135.58bn NGF funds
description:
A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, has ordered the freezing of $100m (about N135.58bn) allegedly held by the Nigerian Governors’ Forum over a dispute arising from the Paris Club refunds and outstanding legal and consultancy fees.
Justice O.C. Agbaza granted the interim Mareva inju
content:
A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, has ordered the freezing of $100m (about N135.58bn) allegedly held by the Nigerian Governors’ Forum over a dispute arising from the Paris Club refunds and outstanding legal and consultancy fees.

Justice O.C. Agbaza granted the interim Mareva injunction on November 19, following an ex parte application by a lawyer, Dr Ted Iseghohi-Edwards, against the Incorporated Trustees of the Nigerian Governors’ Forum and 29 commercial banks.

In a copy of the Certified True Copy of the order sighted by PUNCH on Tuesday, the claimant is seeking to recover the money pursuant to an indemnity allegedly issued by the NGF on December 20, 2018, under an arrangement in which the Federal Government paid $100m to the forum as a stakeholder pending the determination of its liability for professional fees.

In the enrolled order, the judge restrained the NGF, its servants, agents, representatives and anyone acting on its behalf from withdrawing, transferring, dissipating, concealing, disposing of or otherwise dealing with the funds.

The order also restrained the 29 banks from releasing, transferring, converting, withdrawing, paying out or otherwise dealing with any funds standing to the credit of the NGF in their custody, up to the aggregate sum of $100m or its naira equivalent of N135,580,360,000.

The enrolled order stated, “An order of Interim Mareva Injunction restraining the 1st Defendant/Respondent, whether by themselves, their servants, agents, privies, representatives or any person acting on its instructions or behalf from withdrawing, transferring, dissipating, concealing, disposing of, encumbering or otherwise dealing with any funds up the sum of $100,000,000.00 or its Naira equivalent being the sum of N135,580,360,000.00, calculated at the prevailing exchange rate of the United States Dollars to the Nigerian Naira as published by the Central Bank of Nigeria on 17 November 2026, or any part thereof.

“Being funds representing the subject of the Claimant/Applicant’s claim upon the indemnity dated 20 December 2018 to the extent that those funds are held by or on behalf of the 1st Defendant/Respondent within the jurisdiction of this court pending the hearing and determination of the Motion on Notice for Interlocutory Injunction or further order of this Honourable Court.

“An order of interim Mareva Injunction restraining the 2nd – 30th Respondents, whether by themselves, their directors, officers, servants, agents, privies or representatives, upon service of the order and to the extent that any of them holds funds described in prayer 1 in an account from releasing, paying, transferring, withdrawing, converting, dissipating or otherwise dealing with any funds standing to the credit of the 1st Defendant in the name of the 1st Defendant/Respondent, from permitting any withdrawal, transfer, conversion, payment, disbursement, application, utilisation or other dealing with those funds, subject to the same duration and single aggregate limit”.

Justice Agbaza further directed the banks to disclose, within 48 hours of being served with the order, whether the NGF maintained accounts containing the disputed funds.

The banks are also required to identify such accounts, their currencies, available balances and the amounts preserved pursuant to the order.

The 29 banks joined in the suit as respondents include Access Bank, Alpha Morgan Bank, Ecobank Nigeria, Fidelity Bank, First Bank, Sterling Bank, United Bank for Africa, Unity Bank, Zenith Bank, Jaiz Bank, Guaranty Trust Bank, Keystone Bank, Stanbic IBTC, Standard Chartered Bank and Wema Bank.

Others are Union Bank, First City Monument Bank, Lotus Bank, Parallex Bank, Polaris Bank, Globus Bank, SunTrust Bank, Citibank Nigeria, Nova Bank, Optimus Bank, Premium Trust Bank, Signature Bank, Tatum Bank and Titan Trust Bank.

The judge directed the claimant to promptly serve the originating processes, supporting affidavit, written address, motion on notice and enrolled order on the respondents.

The claimant’s case is that the money belongs to him under the indemnity issued by the NGF, which reportedly undertook to pay him the $100m if the Federal Government was found liable for the outstanding professional fees.

Iseghohi-Edwards, who carries on business under the name and style of Edwards and Partners Law Firm, claimed to have been retained by the Incorporated Trustees of the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria to represent the 774 local government councils in matters relating to the London and Paris Club refunds.

He subsequently instituted suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/856/2016 against the Federal Government over outstanding legal and consultancy fees arising from the transactions.

According to his court filings, the Federal High Court delivered judgment on February 16, 2018, establishing the government’s indebtedness of $318m.

He said the Federal Government subsequently made a part-payment of $159m through Promissory Notes.

The claimant contended that the judgment satisfied the condition contained in the NGF’s indemnity, thereby making the $100m payable directly to him.

He further alleged that despite formally demanding payment from the NGF in a letter dated October 8, 2026, the forum failed to honour its undertaking.

Consequently, he approached the FCT High Court to preserve the disputed funds pending the determination of his substantive claim.

In seeking the interim injunction, Iseghohi-Edwards expressed apprehension that the NGF could transfer, disburse or dissipate the funds, thereby frustrating the enforcement of any eventual judgment in his favour.

He also told the court that he could not independently identify the specific bank accounts holding the money without judicial intervention.

The claimant argued that the injunction was necessary to preserve the subject matter of the dispute and prevent the proceedings from becoming futile.

He maintained that the restriction was limited to a single aggregate sum of $100m across the NGF and all participating banks.

The application was brought pursuant to Orders 30(3) and 32(1) of the High Court of the Federal Capital Territory Civil Procedure Rules and the court’s inherent jurisdiction.

In granting the application, Justice Agbaza ordered that the restrictions on the banks would remain in force pending the hearing and determination of the claimant’s motion on notice for an interlocutory injunction or further order of the court.

The judge also directed the banks to file affidavits disclosing whether they held accounts belonging to the NGF containing the disputed funds.

The order further required the banks to identify the accounts, the relevant currency, the balances at the time of service and the amounts preserved, subject to any confidentiality directions the court might make.

The case was adjourned until December 1, 2026, for the hearing of the motion on notice.

The post Paris Club refunds: Court freezes N135.58bn NGF funds appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Police declare Arise News owner Nduka Obaigbena, Nestoil MD, seven others wanted over threat to FirstBank MD
description:
The Nigeria Police Force has declared Arise News TV owner, Nduka Obaigbena; Nestoil Managing Director, Dr Ernest Azudialu-Obiejesi; and seven other corporate executives wanted over an alleged threat to the life of First Bank of Nigeria Managing Director, Olusegun Alebiosu.
The Assistant Inspector-Ge
content:
The Nigeria Police Force has declared Arise News TV owner, Nduka Obaigbena; Nestoil Managing Director, Dr Ernest Azudialu-Obiejesi; and seven other corporate executives wanted over an alleged threat to the life of First Bank of Nigeria Managing Director, Olusegun Alebiosu.

The Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of Zone 2, Olohundare Jimoh, announced the development on Tuesday during a briefing with journalists at the Zone 2 Police Command headquarters in Onikan, Lagos.

Jimoh said the declaration followed the failure of nine individuals to honour police invitations issued as part of an investigation into a parcel containing two rounds of 7.62mm live ammunition delivered to Alebiosu’s residence.

According to the police, 10 bank customers and other individuals considered relevant to the investigation were invited for questioning. The invitations were issued on November 5, with the individuals expected to report on November 12.

However, Jimoh said only one person honoured the invitation, while the remaining nine failed to appear, prompting the police to declare them wanted to facilitate the investigation.

The incident dates back to May 7, 2026, when a parcel containing two live rounds of ammunition was delivered to Alebiosu’s residence in Lagos. The package was reportedly opened the following morning.

The parcel, which was disguised as a fashion-design gift, was delivered by a dispatch rider whose identity remains unknown. It was received by security personnel at the residence before being handed over to the bank chief.

Upon opening it, Alebiosu reportedly discovered two live bullets concealed inside. The package contained no accompanying letter or message identifying the sender.

The Lagos State Commissioner of Police had confirmed the incident in June, saying investigations were underway to identify those responsible.

Jimoh described the ammunition as dangerous, noting that the 7.62mm rounds were designed for compatible firearms, including AK-47 rifles.

He said the discovery prompted the constitution of a joint investigative team comprising crime detectives, ballistic experts and forensic investigators.

According to the AIG, preliminary investigations revealed that First Bank had undertaken extensive loan recovery activities involving customers allegedly owing the bank several billions of naira.

He said some of the customers reportedly confronted bank representatives and issued threats against the managing director during the recovery process.

The police said the investigation was aimed at establishing the circumstances surrounding the delivery of the ammunition and identifying those responsible for the alleged threat against Alebiosu and his family.

The nine individuals declared wanted are Nduka Obaigbena of Arise News TV; Dr Ernest Azudialu-Obiejesi and Nnenna Azudialu-Obiejesi of Nestoil Plc; Tope Shonubi of Sahara Group Limited; Henry Kayode Ojogho of Broron Limited; Emmanuel Iheagwazi of Necit Nigeria Limited; Eze David of Energy Shield Petrochemical; and Emmanuel Orim and Victoria Orim of Luzen Plaza.

Jimoh urged anyone with useful information about their whereabouts to report to the nearest police station.

He assured the public that the investigation would be conducted professionally and discreetly, adding that anyone found culpable would face the full weight of the law.

The AIG also stressed that the rights of both the suspects and the complainant would be protected throughout the investigation.
