title: Political Signals: The Price Of Participation
content:
Deadly violence in Delta sharpens the question of campaign safety, while economic policy and electoral preparations face tests.

An election campaign should ask citizens for their votes. In Uduere, Delta State, families are now mourning people who went to a political gathering.

Police said on Tuesday that six people died in Monday’s violence at a campaign event in Ughelli North. That preliminary figure is higher than the four deaths initially reported by Ovie Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation. The circumstances and responsibility remain under investigation.

This is the most consequential political development since Friday.

Its significance extends beyond one party’s campaign. Every attack raises a question for the next person considering attending a meeting, volunteering or accompanying a candidate: is participation worth the risk?

When citizens begin making that calculation, electoral competition has already suffered.

Delta Needs Evidence And Accountability

The NDC has alleged official complicity. The Delta State Government has rejected attempts to link Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to the violence, condemned the killings and promised that those responsible will face justice. Those competing positions must remain distinct from investigative findings.

The state has imposed a daily 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. curfew across Ughelli North. Restoring calm is an immediate necessity. Establishing responsibility is the next obligation.

The investigation should establish the sequence of events, identify those who used weapons and examine allegations about the conduct of officials and security personnel. Witnesses need protection, and the public needs credible updates.

Political leaders also have an immediate responsibility to restrain inflammatory claims and prevent retaliation.

The standard is straightforward: lawful political activity must receive protection regardless of the party organising it.

A Separate Court Decision Changes The Delta Contest

On Tuesday, the Federal High Court in Warri nullified Omo-Agege’s nomination as the NDC’s Delta Central senatorial candidate and directed INEC to remove his name. Reporting attributes the decision to failures concerning the party’s membership register and nomination requirements. Responses from Omo-Agege and the NDC were unavailable in the initial reports.

The ruling and Monday’s violence are separate matters. Their proximity establishes no connection between them.

Electorally, however, the judgment creates fresh uncertainty around an influential politician and the organisation supporting him. Any subsequent appeal, interim order and INEC action will matter.

The wider lesson reaches across party lines: recruitment and defections must be supported by lawful nomination procedures. Political prominence cannot resolve defective paperwork.

Tinubu’s Lagos Outreach Meets An Economic Request

President Bola Tinubu’s meeting with Igbo stakeholders in Lagos on Monday continued his effort to broaden support through community and business networks.

According to the presidency, participants pledged support while Tinubu offered assurances of inclusive governance. Traders’ representative Tony Nwakeze also requested loans at five per cent interest to help businesses expand and move towards manufacturing. That was a request; the account did not announce an operational loan scheme.

The economic request gives the gathering significance beyond its endorsements.

Business owners want access to finance, reliable services and room to grow. Their electoral decisions may depend on whether political commitments produce practical improvements.

The gathering demonstrates outreach and organised support among those present. It cannot establish the preferences of an entire ethnic community. Voters retain their individual judgments, including when community leaders endorse a candidate.

The CBN Holds Its Position

The Central Bank’s Monetary Policy Committee retained the benchmark interest rate at 23 per cent today.

Set beside the traders’ request, the decision illustrates a central political tension: preserving economic stability while improving access to affordable finance.

The policy rate and the interest charged on a particular business loan are different measures. Even so, financing costs remain part of the environment in which enterprises decide whether to invest, employ and expand.

For the government, the campaign challenge is to show how stabilisation will translate into stronger livelihoods.

For the opposition, promising cheaper credit requires an explanation of funding, eligibility, repayment and protection against politically connected beneficiaries.

Voters deserve to see how those proposals would work.

Opposition Cooperation Still Awaits Its Decision Day

The opposition’s second summit remains scheduled for November 30, following its postponement from November 23. Organisers intend participating parties and candidates to endorse a framework for cooperation, democratic renewal and reform. A common presidential candidate has not been announced.

The distinction matters.

Parties can cooperate on election monitoring, campaign freedoms and policy priorities while continuing to compete for votes. Whether they intend to go further needs an explicit answer.

Monday’s summit should be assessed through its commitments: who signs, what each participant authorises and what work begins afterward.

The ADC, NDC, APM, SDP, PRP and participating PDP faction also have different local interests to reconcile. A national understanding becomes useful when constituency organisations know how to act on it.

Saturday Offers A Measurable Test

INEC has selected 17,676 polling units, covering two units in each registration area, for its nationwide mock accreditation and result-upload exercise on Saturday, November 28. The announced operating hours are 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Nigerian time.

This gives parties, observers and voters an opportunity to assess performance before the general election.

The useful evidence will include whether equipment works, eligible participants can be accredited, results upload correctly and failures receive a prompt, documented response.

INEC should publish findings and explain the corrective work required. A test earns public value when its results can be examined.

The position of the main camps is clearer in some respects, while important uncertainties remain:

•APC/Tinubu: outreach continues through party, community and business networks. The challenge is converting endorsements and the government’s record into individual votes.
•ADC/Atiku: the leadership appeal remains consequential. INEC’s latest reported position is that it will await the appellate decision before determining its next action; that does not establish that the ADC has won its appeal.
•NDC/Obi-Kwankwaso: the Delta violence creates immediate safety concerns, while the Omo-Agege judgment introduces a separate organisational uncertainty.
•APM/Makinde and other opposition partners: November 30 will test whether negotiations produce defined, implementable cooperation.

State and constituency developments deserve attention because presidential campaigns depend on local organisers, candidates and polling agents. Recent local and off-cycle results can inform that assessment when turnout, competitiveness and local circumstances are considered.

Election Watch assessment: campaign safety and legal uncertainty have become more consequential. The material reviewed does not support declaring a fresh national swing.

Can Young People Participate Without Paying With Their Safety?

The Delta deaths give this edition’s Youth Metre an immediate focus: the conditions under which people enter political life.

Campaigns depend on volunteers, organisers and supporters. Those participants need protection, clear responsibilities and leaders who reject intimidation consistently.

Young Nigerians should also have meaningful roles in examining proposals and holding campaigns accountable. Employment promises need funding and delivery plans. Enterprise support needs published access rules. Training needs a credible connection to work.

Saturday’s INEC exercise offers another practical point of engagement: eligible participants can help test the process, while accredited observers and journalists document performance and unresolved problems.

Youth Metre assessment: safety, economic opportunity and confidence in vote counting are the priorities to watch. No fresh, credible age-specific polling reviewed establishes a change in youth candidate preference.

What To Watch Before Friday

•Investigative findings and accountability following the Uduere killings.

•Any response, appeal or INEC action concerning Omo-Agege’s nomination.

•Any appellate order affecting the ADC leadership dispute.

•INEC’s arrangements for observing and reporting Saturday’s test.

•Final confirmation of the November 30 summit’s participants and commitments.

The Signal

Political party tracker

Party Latest verified position
APC No additional major defection or nomination change established today.

PDP Disagreement over participation in the proposed opposition coalition remains unresolved.

ADC Presidential nomination and national leadership litigation remain unresolved.

NDC Delta Central nomination nullified; party boycotts police security meeting.
Labour Party Disputed endorsement of Tinubu by the Abure faction has not changed the officially listed presidential ticket.

NNPP: No newly verified material organisational change.
APGA Existing presidential cooperation with APC remains in place.

APM, PRP and SDP Proposed November 30 opposition cooperation summit remains the next significant milestone.
Accord No additional qualifying electoral development established today.

The ADC leadership appeal and opposition coalition arrangements remain outstanding, with no newly verified resolution in today’s review.

Geopolitical-Zone Assessment

Geopolitical zone: Electoral development to monitor

South-South: Delta Central candidacy dispute and campaign security

South-East No newly verified material change

South-West: Election technology preparations in Lagos and Oyo

North-Central: Campaign access, security and existing party disputes

North-West: Existing political realignments, particularly in Kano

North-East: Outstanding candidate nomination disputes
Nationwide Election personnel recruitment and technology readiness

Countdown To 2027

Presidential & National Assembly
53 days
16 January 2027

Governorship & State Assembly
74 days
6 February 2027

Upcoming Milestones

28 Nov. INEC nationwide technology test

30 Nov. Proposed opposition coalition summit

2 Dec. Tinubu eligibility litigation resumes

3 Dec. INEC ad hoc personnel recruitment deadline

The Bottom Line

The Omo-Agege judgment represents a concrete change in the legal position of a National Assembly candidacy. The NDC’s security meeting boycott and INEC’s personnel shortage also raise substantive questions about the conditions under which the elections will be conducted.

With less than two months until the presidential election, electoral preparedness, campaign freedom and candidate eligibility deserve as much scrutiny as party alignments.

Electoral map: Delta Central requires a candidate-level adjustment, subject to appellate proceedings.

Presidential voter preferences: No newly verified evidence supports a change in the national assessment.

Campaigns are asking Nigerians to invest their hopes, time and resources in the coming election. The institutions and leaders involved owe them protection and a credible process.

The freedom to participate safely is the first promise every campaign must honour.

description:
Former Sokoto State Governor and African Democratic Congress chieftain, Aminu Tambuwal, has commended Kogi State Governor, Usman Ododo, for allowing the ADC to hold its rally at Muhammadu Buhari Square in the state.



Tambuwal described the gesture as an act of statesmanship, saying political diffe
content:
Former Sokoto State Governor and African Democratic Congress chieftain, Aminu Tambuwal, has commended Kogi State Governor, Usman Ododo, for allowing the ADC to hold its rally at Muhammadu Buhari Square in the state.

Tambuwal described the gesture as an act of statesmanship, saying political differences should not prevent leaders from respecting democratic rights and promoting peaceful coexistence.

In a post on X on Tuesday, he thanked Ododo for granting the opposition party access to the venue, noting that such actions strengthened democracy and encouraged political tolerance.

“I wish to express my sincere appreciation to the Governor of Kogi State, His Excellency, for his commendable show of statesmanship in granting the African Democratic Congress (ADC) the use of Muhammadu Buhari Square for its rally in Kogi State,” he said.

Tambuwal said the governor’s action demonstrated that disagreements over political affiliations should not undermine the right of citizens and parties to participate in the democratic process.

He said democracy was strengthened when political leaders respected the constitutional rights of others to assemble, associate and express their views regardless of party differences.

The former governor also praised Kogi residents for their conduct during the rally, commending them for maintaining peace and order throughout the event.

Tambuwal urged political leaders to promote tolerance and avoid treating political opponents as adversaries, stressing that disagreements should be settled through the exchange of ideas.

“Democracy is not a contest of enemies but a contest of ideas, and that our political differences must never overshadow our shared commitment to the peace, unity and progress of our country,” he said.

title: Nigeria Is Cutting The Budget, But Not The Deficit
description: The economic signal this week is that the Federal Government has acknowledged that its 2026 budget is larger than it can credibly implement.President Bola Tinubu has asked the National Assembly to repeal and re-enact the 2026 Appropriation Act, reducing total expenditure from ₦68.323 trillion to ₦65
content:
The economic signal this week is that the Federal Government has acknowledged that its 2026 budget is larger than it can credibly implement.

President Bola Tinubu has asked the National Assembly to repeal and re-enact the 2026 Appropriation Act, reducing total expenditure from ₦68.323 trillion to ₦65.176 trillion, a cut of approximately ₦3.15 trillion, or 4.6 per cent.

Budget revision is not inherently a sign of failure. Governments should adjust spending plans when revenue, financing conditions or obligations change. An unrealistic budget does not become credible merely because it has been signed into law.

The more important signal is what remains unchanged: a ₦31.457 trillion fiscal deficit and planned new borrowing of ₦29.218 trillion.

Nigeria is reducing expenditure, but it is not reducing the gap between what government earns and what it intends to spend.

What Is Being Revised

Under the proposed framework, projected federal revenue, including receipts from government-owned enterprises, stands at ₦33.720 trillion. Capital expenditure is estimated at ₦26.232 trillion, while the deficit remains equivalent to 5.64 per cent of GDP.

The borrowing plan comprises ₦18.428 trillion in domestic financing and ₦10.790 trillion from external sources. The government says its proposed $7.7 billion foreign loan will fund an existing external-borrowing provision rather than increase the approved envelope.

The administration says the revision will regularise expenditure incurred by NNPC Limited on behalf of the Federation, address debt-service obligations that were underprovided for, recognise already issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments, and refund ministries and special accounts.

Some new allocations are also proposed for critical roads, agriculture, farm productivity, market access and water security.

These may be legitimate obligations. But their late recognition exposes weaknesses in the original budget’s preparation.

The Credibility Problem

The 2026 budget began as an executive proposal of approximately ₦58.47 trillion. It was subsequently expanded and signed at ₦68.323 trillion in April. Seven months later, the executive is asking Parliament to reduce it.

The new figure remains ₦6.7 trillion above the original proposal.

This sequence matters because Nigeria’s budget has become less a binding financial plan than a collection of ambitions, negotiated additions and subsequent corrections. Ministries receive large appropriations but often wait months for releases. Projects are announced without complete financing. Unpaid obligations accumulate and eventually return as supplementary provisions.

A smaller, executable budget would be preferable to a larger one that exists chiefly on paper. But credibility requires more than reducing the headline figure. Government should publish exactly which programmes are being removed, reduced, deferred or reclassified.

Without that schedule, Nigerians cannot determine who bears the adjustment.

Why The Unchanged Deficit Matters

A ₦31.457 trillion deficit means that projected revenue will finance only slightly more than half of the revised spending plan.

The administration argues that much of the borrowing will support infrastructure and productive investment. That may be economically defensible where financing is affordable and projects generate measurable value.

But borrowing also exposes the budget to interest costs, refinancing pressures and exchange-rate risk. Domestic borrowing can crowd out private-sector credit, while external debt becomes more expensive in naira terms when the currency weakens.

The cut therefore raises a central question: if expenditure has been reduced to reflect available resources, why have the deficit and borrowing requirements not also fallen?

The answer may lie in the incorporation of previously underfunded debt service and other obligations. If so, the government should provide a clear reconciliation. Fiscal arithmetic should not require citizens to infer what has changed.

The Political Dimension

The revision comes weeks before the expected presentation of the 2027 budget and less than two months before the presidential election.

The government will describe the exercise as responsible adjustment evidence that it is prioritising existing commitments and improving capital budget execution. Opposition parties are likely to portray it as proof that the original budget was inflated or poorly planned.

Neither political conclusion should substitute for legislative scrutiny.

The National Assembly approved the expansion to ₦68.323 trillion. It should now explain the basis on which it evaluates the reduction, rather than treating the new request as an administrative formality.

What To Watch

Watch the detailed schedule of reductions. Are politically inserted projects being removed, or are essential capital programmes carrying the burden?

Watch actual revenue collections and capital releases. Appropriation is not implementation.

Finally, watch the 2027 budget. If it repeats optimistic revenue assumptions and large legislative additions, the current revision will have corrected a number without correcting the process.

Bottom Line

Reducing an unrealistic budget is fiscally sensible. Retaining an unchanged deficit and borrowing plan makes the adjustment less reassuring.

Nigeria does not merely need a smaller budget. It needs an honest one built on credible revenue, transparent obligations and projects that can actually be completed.

The true test of fiscal discipline is not how much government appropriates. It is how closely promises, resources and delivery finally align.

title: I have an incurable form of cancer  -  Farooq Oreagba opens up
description:
The Managing Director of NG Clearing Limited, Farooq Oreagba, has disclosed that he is living with an incurable form of cancer, saying his treatment is progressing well and he hopes to return to remission next year.



The 60-year-old investment banker said he was diagnosed on February 4 following a
content:
The Managing Director of NG Clearing Limited, Farooq Oreagba, has disclosed that he is living with an incurable form of cancer, saying his treatment is progressing well and he hopes to return to remission next year.

The 60-year-old investment banker said he was diagnosed on February 4 following a medical screening but had continued working and maintaining his lifestyle despite the condition.

In an interview with TheCable Lifestyle on Monday, Oreagba said he had learnt to manage the illness and remained optimistic about his recovery.

“I have an incurable form of cancer. It comes, I treat, and it goes. I was diagnosed in February, after which I rode at Ojude Oba, celebrated my 60th and continued as if nothing was wrong,” he said.

Oreagba said he was responding well to treatment and expected to return to remission around March or April 2027.

“I am very fine, working as usual and doing what I always do. My treatment is going well, and I expect to be back in remission by March/April next year,” he added.

Popularly known as the ‘King of Steeze’, Oreagba became an internet sensation in 2024 after his stylish appearance and horseback display at the Ojude Oba Festival in Ijebu-Ode, Ogun State, attracted widespread attention.

However, his battle with cancer dates back to 2014, when he was diagnosed with bone marrow and skin cancer. He underwent a transplant in August of that year and has since continued managing the condition, receiving treatment in Johannesburg, South Africa.

Oreagba urged Nigerians to prioritise routine medical examinations, saying his condition was detected early during a screening exercise.

He said he undergoes medical checks every three months, adding that people should not wait until they experience symptoms before seeking medical attention.

“Early detection saves lives, and I recommend regular checks. I do mine every three months, but even every six months would suffice,” he said.

He added, “It is important to know that a cancer diagnosis is not a death sentence. I am making great progress.”

description:
By Steve Oko







UMUAHIA — The legal team of detained Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) leader, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, says efforts are still being considered to secure an earlier hearing date for his appeal against conviction, insisting that the January 25, 2027 date is not sacrosanct.



Kanu’s Spe
content:
By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA — The legal team of detained Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) leader, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, says efforts are still being considered to secure an earlier hearing date for his appeal against conviction, insisting that the January 25, 2027 date is not sacrosanct.

Kanu’s Special Counsel, Aloy Ejimakor, disclosed this in a press release on Tuesday, clarifying that the legal team had contemplated moving the appeal forward almost two months ago when the January 25 date was initially communicated to Kanu and his lawyers.

Ejimakor said the decision to seek an earlier hearing had remained unchanged, dismissing any impression that the scheduled date was a settled matter.

He explained that the Rules of Court allow an appellant to formally apply for an abridgment of time, a procedural mechanism through which a court can be asked to fast-track an appeal and hear it earlier than originally scheduled.

According to him, the option remains under active consideration in view of the critical issues involved in the appeal and the urgency attached to it.

“Nothing is yet set in stone,” Ejimakor declared, assuring that legal avenues for expediting the hearing remained available and were being carefully weighed to prevent justice from being delayed.

The clarification comes amid expectations surrounding Kanu’s appeal, with his legal team signalling its intention to explore available judicial procedures to bring forward the hearing date.

Ejimakor, who signed the statement on behalf of Kanu, said the pursuit of an earlier date had been on the table since the original January 25, 2027, date was made known to the defendant and his lawyers.

The legal team, however, did not disclose whether an application for abridgment of time had already been formally filed or when such an application might be made.

Kanu was sentenced to life imprisonment since November, 2025, and his efforts to appeal the judgment have suffered unnecessary setbacks for one year.

title: 2027: Omo-Agege Not A Threat, Can’t Get 25% Of Votes For Obi – Delta Council Chairman
description: The Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Council in Delta State, Jaro Egbo, has dismissed former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege as a political threat ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that the former lawmaker lacks the support to secure significant votes for the Nigeria De
content:
The Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Council in Delta State, Jaro Egbo, has dismissed former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege as a political threat ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that the former lawmaker lacks the support to secure significant votes for the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the state.

Egbo said Omo-Agege would struggle to deliver even 25 per cent of the votes for the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, arguing that his political influence in Delta State was exaggerated.

The council chairman spoke on Tuesday as a guest on Channels Television’s ‘Politics Today’, where he was asked whether Omo-Agege’s claim that the APC could not win elections in Delta State was a source of concern, particularly given Obi’s victory in the state during the 2023 presidential election.

Responding, Egbo questioned Omo-Agege’s political strength, recalling that the former deputy senate president was a member of the All Progressives Congress during the 2023 elections but could not secure 25 per cent of the votes for President Bola Tinubu in Delta State.

“When Peter Obi contested and won in Delta in 2023, Omo-Agege was in APC. Omo-Agege couldn’t get 25 per cent of the vote for Mr President. If he was that popular, why was he unable to get 25 per cent for Mr President?” he asked.

Egbo, who said he belonged to the Peoples Democratic Party at the time, added that his party secured more than 25 per cent of the votes for its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar.

He argued that Omo-Agege’s defection to the NDC would not translate into electoral gains for Obi, insisting that the former deputy senate president lacked the political following to influence the outcome of the election.

“Now that he has gone to NDC, I am sure he won’t be able to also get 25 per cent for Peter Obi. So, he’s not a threat to anybody. He knows that he’s not a threat,” he said.

Egbo, who is also from Ughelli North, Omo-Agege’s hometown, urged Omo-Agege to face the electorate rather than make claims about his political strength, saying voters would determine his popularity at the polls.

Egbo also called on the former deputy senate president to tone down his political rhetoric.

Omo-Agege had, during an appearance on Politics Today on Monday, dismissed the APC’s chances of winning elections in Delta State in 2027, citing Obi’s popularity and the support base he claimed to command.

“Peter Obi remains very popular here in Delta State. There is no chance that APC will win anything,” he said.

Omo-Agege, who left the APC for the NDC in May 2026, also argued that a combination of his political support base and Obi’s popularity would make it difficult for the ruling party to win in the state.

However, the Federal High Court in Warri, Delta State, on Tuesday invalidated Omo-Agege’s nomination as the NDC candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 elections over alleged violations of the Electoral Act.

Omo-Agege has rejected the judgment nullifying his NDC nomination for Delta Central, describing it as inconsistent with the evidence and law, and announced plans to appeal the ruling.

The post 2027: Omo-Agege Not A Threat, Can’t Get 25% Of Votes For Obi – Delta Council Chairman appeared first on Channels Television.

title: How Tinubu saved Buhari from disqualification in 2015 election — Omatseye
description:
— No conspiracy will stop President’s re-election— Tinubu was kept at a distance in Buhari’s administration — Osoba



By Johnbosco Agbakwuru



ABUJA — Former President Muhammadu Buhari could have been disqualified from the 2015 presidential election had Bola Tinubu, then APC national leader, not u
content:
— No conspiracy will stop President’s re-election
— Tinubu was kept at a distance in Buhari’s administration — Osoba

By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA — Former President Muhammadu Buhari could have been disqualified from the 2015 presidential election had Bola Tinubu, then APC national leader, not urgently called eminent lawyer Wole Olanipekun.

This was disclosed by veteran journalist Sam Omatseye in Chapter 29, pages 483–485, of his book, From AD to APC: The Evolution of Nigerian Political Parties and the Exploits of One Man (1998–2015), which was launched yesterday by President Tinubu at the Banquet Hall, Presidential Villa, Abuja.

This is as former Governor of Ogun State and veteran journalist, Aremu Segun Osoba, stated that after helping to put in place the All Progressives Congress government led by the late Muhammadu Buhari, President Tinubu was kept at a distance by the administration.

An excerpt of Tinubu’s intervention to ensure that Buhari was on the ballot in 2015 was contained in the programme of events for the book’s public presentation, attended by several governors.

According to the book, days before the 2015 presidential election, Tinubu phoned Olanipekun, asking him to rush to the Federal High Court in Abuja or Buhari might not contest the poll.

Olanipekun was in Akure, Ondo State, on an official assignment on a Monday evening, a few days before the March 28, 2015 election, when Tinubu called him.

Olanipekun narrated in the book: “I was in Akure, Ondo State, on an official assignment on the fateful Monday evening when I got a call from Asiwaju.

“And as usual, I was trying to embark on the usual exchange of banter and pleasantries by hailing him as my Asiwaju of the universe.”

However, his humour was deflected due to the gravity of the challenge on the ground.

“He sharply replied that there is fire on the mountain and you’re shouting Asiwaju of the universe; there’s an emergency here, where are you?” Tinubu was quoted as saying.

Olanipekun said he told Tinubu that the assignment would last until the following day.

Tinubu then raised his voice and told him: “You have to leave that your Akure immediately as your attention and presence are imperative at the Federal High Court in Abuja tomorrow, otherwise Buhari might not contest the election coming up this Saturday.”

Although the excerpt did not state the case before the court, several suits before the Federal High Court in Abuja sought to disqualify Buhari from the March 28, 2015 presidential election, in what became known as the certificate saga.

The plaintiffs argued that Buhari did not submit his academic certificates with his Form CF001 to the Independent National Electoral Commission.

They said this breached Sections 131 and 318 of the 1999 Constitution and Section 31(3) of the Electoral Act, 2010.

One plaintiff, Chike Okafor, accused Buhari of perjury and asked the court to restrain INEC from allowing him to take part in the election.

The suits were heard before Justice Adeniyi Ademola, and Olanipekun was named as counsel to Buhari and the APC.

Some of the suits were struck out as duplicates. The judge, however, dismissed applications by two parties to be joined as defendants.

On March 25, three days before the election, he adjourned the remaining suits to April 22 and 23, keeping Buhari on the ballot.

“Your colleagues are here with me, led by Kola Awodein SAN, insisting that I must fetch you out to lead them in the matter,” Olanipekun recalled Tinubu saying in the book.

He said Awodein “seconded Asiwaju’s application with his own plea that I should try by all means to be in court the following day.”

According to the book, Tinubu took the phone back and said: “I’ll send an aircraft to pick you up at Akure tomorrow morning. The plane will leave Lagos early in the morning with Awodein and co, pick you up at Akure to Abuja, wait for you at the tarmac till you finish in court, and when you’re done in court, you can take it to Ikere, in case you already have an airport there!”

Omatseye wrote that the SAN “took it as a marching order,” describing the episode as “one ominous hour in Nigerian history.”

The book, which covers the period from 1998 to 2015, from Nigeria’s return to civilian rule through the collapse of the PDP’s 16-year grip on federal power, is Omatseye’s second major political work.

The book is to be reviewed by Louis Odion, with excerpts read by Ohi Alegbe, Stella Din Jacobs and Yomi Odunuga.

Tinubu, a former senator who had run on the Social Democratic Party platform in the 1992 senatorial elections, returned from exile and contested the Lagos governorship under the Alliance for Democracy, winning in 1999 and beginning the political journey that would eventually lead him to the presidency in 2023.

Chairman of the occasion and former Governor of Ogun State, Chief Segun Osoba, said President Tinubu’s emergence was the result of tenacity and hard work.

He said what made the APC successful in 2015 was that President Tinubu decided that Buhari should be adopted as the presidential candidate.

Osoba, who offered an insider’s account of the political realignments that produced the APC, said Tinubu’s courage, determination and sacrifices were instrumental to the survival of the progressive movement and its eventual electoral success.

“People do not know that the President is where he is today by dint of hard work, courage, ferocity and determination to get us to where we are today,” he said.

Recounting the political crisis that followed the 2003 general election, Osoba said the AD suffered devastating electoral losses, leaving Tinubu as the party’s only remaining governor.

He said Tinubu mobilised prominent Nigerians, including former Inspector-General of Police, Gambo Jimeta, and the late MD Yusuf, to resist what he described as an attempt to impose a one-party state.

“The first battle was against that attempt. I remember that when we were having meetings, people like Gambo Jimeta, former IGP, and MD Yusuf, who were not politicians, were assembled by the President to fight that battle. We fought it successfully,” he said.

Osoba recalled that Tinubu subsequently initiated efforts to bring Buhari into the opposition fold following the controversial 2003 presidential election.

“In 2003, the President called me and said I should lead a delegation to Kaduna to go and talk to General Muhammadu Buhari to come to us and let us work together,” he said.

He also credited Tinubu with facilitating the emergence of former Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) Chairman, Nuhu Ribadu, as the Action Congress’s presidential candidate in 2011.

According to him, Tinubu took opposition leaders to Dubai, United Arab Emirates, where they persuaded Ribadu, who was then living in exile in the United States, to return and participate in the political process.

Osoba said the negotiations and political realignments eventually culminated in the formation of the APC in 2013, identifying Tinubu’s insistence on Buhari as the party’s presidential candidate in 2015 as the defining decision behind its historic victory.

“What made APC successful? The President decided that we should adopt Buhari as the presidential candidate. That singular decision on who would be the presidential candidate made APC successful,” he declared.

The former governor further recalled Tinubu’s determination to support Buhari’s re-election in 2019 despite growing dissatisfaction with the administration and internal disagreements within the party.

He said he personally approached Tinubu in London on January 1, 2016, to express concern about Buhari’s performance and its possible political implications for the APC.

Osoba said he spent about two hours trying to persuade Tinubu to reconsider his position, but the former Lagos governor remained resolute.

“He listened to me for about two hours. I argued. He said I should come back and we should meet again. By the time we got to Lagos, he said, ‘Good or bad, the North must have a second term, and we must support Buhari’,” he recounted.

Drawing a parallel between Tinubu’s support for Buhari’s second term and his current political ambition, Osoba questioned why the same principle should not apply to the incumbent President.

“If he insisted, in spite of the fact that our party became unpopular, that the North must have a second term, what is wrong and what is new that we now say President Tinubu should have a second term? Is there anything wrong with this issue?” he asked.

Beyond party politics, Osoba cited Tinubu’s determination to implement economic reforms, particularly the legislation establishing the Nigerian Revenue Service, as evidence of his willingness to take difficult decisions despite opposition.

He disclosed that he had advised the President to withdraw the proposal and consult state governors when they initially opposed the reforms.

“I went to him and said, ‘Please, can you withdraw this thing and let’s consult with the governors?’ He said no,” Osoba recalled.

He also said he approached Tinubu on Christmas Day to request that the January 1 implementation date be postponed until April 1 to allow more time for public sensitisation.

However, he said the President subsequently rejected the proposal.

“He called me aside and said, ‘That you are trying to do, I am rejecting it. Come fire, come rain, I will do it January 1’,” Osoba quoted Tinubu as saying.

Although initially apprehensive, Osoba said he later commended the President for proceeding with the reform.

“Thank you for your courage. You did it, and now we are beneficiaries of that decision to go ahead on January 1,” he said.

He also praised Nigerian Revenue Service Chairman Zacch Adedeji for explaining the economic rationale behind the reforms, urging APC leaders to take the administration’s policies to the grassroots and communicate their benefits to Nigerians.

“The President decided that all of us should go back home and face the grassroots and convince them on the coming election. By the grace of God, we shall do so, and we shall deliver,” he said.

President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, said no conspiracy would stop President Tinubu from securing a second term.

He said: “And because God decided to give you a victory in 2023 for you to do two terms as President of Nigeria, nobody can stop you. God will give you good health and the enablement to conclude.”

Senator Akpabio also urged that the book be relaunched across the country to broaden public understanding of the political history behind the APC’s emergence.

“My suggestion, Mr President, would be that this kind of beautiful enterprise, this ingenuity, should be relaunched. I believe that we should go to different places and launch this book to a wider audience, so that more people will read and know how the APC finally evolved from the then AD,” he said.

The Senate President said his longstanding interactions with Tinubu had given him insight into the political calculations and experiences that shaped the party.

He recalled Tinubu cautioning him against mistaking political friendliness for genuine loyalty, saying the President once warned him that political associates could appear friendly before turning against one another.

“Do you know that that could be deception? They can dance with you like that, and the next moment they sting you like a bee,” Akpabio recalled Tinubu telling him.

The Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, who described Tinubu’s contributions to the pro-democracy struggle as significant, said the President provided financial and political support to activists during military rule, despite the risks to himself and his family.

The Kaduna governor said he attended the book presentation as a contributor, a former member of the National Democratic Coalition (NADECO) and a beneficiary of the democracy for which activists fought.

He recalled Tinubu’s support for the campaign under the leadership of the late Dr Beko Ransome-Kuti, noting that the President provided resources without attempting to dictate how the struggle should be conducted.

“I can remember vividly when he sponsored our struggling campaign for democracy under the leadership of our leader, Dr Beko Ransome-Kuti, of blessed memory. He gave us the resources, but Beko Ransome-Kuti insisted that he could only support us and would never tell us what to do. That shows that he is a true democrat,” Sani said.

He traced Tinubu’s political involvement from the AD through the Action Congress (AC) and Action Congress of Nigeria (ACN) to the formation of the APC, which he said brought together political leaders with diverse interests and delivered the party’s historic victory in 2015.

“I dare insist that President Bola Tinubu is the modern-day father of Nigerian democracy,” he declared.

Sani praised Tinubu’s ability to recognise talent, accommodate divergent interests and provide opportunities for capable Nigerians to serve, both as Lagos governor and President.

He also cited what he described as significant federal interventions in Kaduna State under the administration, including approval for four federal universities following the state’s request for two, and three ministerial appointments against its request for one.

The governor further listed proposed light rail investments valued at $865 million and the construction of roads linking Mando to Birnin Gwari and Zaria through Soba to Pambegua.

He said some of the road projects had remained the people’s demands for more than 45 years.

“The people of Kaduna State, and the North in particular, will repay you with our votes on January 16, 2027,” he said.

Sani added that the challenge of sustaining democracy was greater than the struggle to restore civilian rule.

“Fighting for democracy is one aspect of it. Entrenching democratic ideals is even more difficult because we have been fighting against anti-democratic elements as well as military apologists in this country,” he said.

Governor Hope Uzodimma reaffirmed the commitment of APC governors to Tinubu, describing them as beneficiaries of his progressive leadership.

He said the President’s policies had enabled states to stimulate economic activities, develop infrastructure and address development gaps.

“We are very happy that today we are the first-line beneficiaries of the progressive leadership you have demonstrated in Nigeria. We are stimulating our states, building infrastructure and closing the gaps. These are only possible because you are leading and we are following,” he said.

The Imo governor urged scholars to undertake further research into Tinubu’s political career, arguing that a single publication could not adequately capture his political experience.

He also pledged that APC governors would demonstrate their appreciation of the President’s leadership at the polls in 2027.

title: ‘I will restore fuel subsidy, revive Ajaokuta Steel mill’ – Atiku promises Kogi residents
description:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has promised to restore fuel subsidy, revive the Ajaokuta Steel Mill, dredge the Baro Port and complete the Kabba/Egbe Road if elected President.
Atiku made the promises while addressing supporters at the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential rally in Ko
content:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has promised to restore fuel subsidy, revive the Ajaokuta Steel Mill, dredge the Baro Port and complete the Kabba/Egbe Road if elected President.

Atiku made the promises while addressing supporters at the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential rally in Kogi State.

The former Vice President said his administration would prioritise the revival of critical national infrastructure and projects that have remained incomplete for years.

He specifically pledged to bring back fuel subsidy, restart operations at the Ajaokuta Steel Mill, which has remained largely inactive for decades, and undertake the dredging of Baro Port to improve its capacity and economic importance.

Atiku also promised to complete the Kabba/Egbe Road, a project of importance to residents and commuters in the area.

The commitments formed part of his campaign promises to Nigerians as he outlined his proposed priorities ahead of the 2027 general election.

His pledges are expected to feature prominently in discussions about economic policy, infrastructure development and the future of major national projects.

title: UK police arrest two men after break-in at William and Kate’s home
description:
Two men have been arrested on suspicion of burglary, police said on Tuesday, after a reported break-in at the countryside retreat of UK royals Prince William and his wife Catherine, who were not in residence at the time.



Police dogs, drones and a helicopter were deployed to the Sandringham estate
content:
Two men have been arrested on suspicion of burglary, police said on Tuesday, after a reported break-in at the countryside retreat of UK royals Prince William and his wife Catherine, who were not in residence at the time.

Police dogs, drones and a helicopter were deployed to the Sandringham estate in Norfolk, eastern England, after the local force received a call just before 6:00 pm (1800 GMT) on Monday of “suspicious activity”, Norfolk police said in a statement sent to AFP.

Anmer Hall where William, Kate and their three children occasionally live — especially during the school holidays — was broken into, according to UK media.

The 10-bedroom red-brick Georgian manor was gifted to the couple by the late Queen Elizabeth II after their marriage.

The men “were arrested on the estate on suspicion of burglary and trespass”, police said.

The sprawling Sandringham estate is owned by William’s father King Charles III.

Police said the property “was unoccupied” at the time and the men remained in custody.

William and Kate mainly live at their home on the Windsor estate, just west of London.

Kensington Palace, which handles the affairs of William, the heir to the throne, told AFP they would not comment on security matters.

Charles’s disgraced brother, the former prince Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, moved to Sandringham earlier this year and lives about a mile from Anmer Hall.

The king ousted Andrew from his home of two decades in Windsor and stripped him of his royal titles amid the fallout from his brother’s alleged dealings with the late US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

– Chat with the queen –

It is not the first time a royal residence has been broken into, despite the tight security surrounding the royal family.

In 2024, several intruders were caught on the Windsor estate after they broke into a farm building and tried to steal a pick-up truck and a quad bike.

Around Christmas 2021, a 21-year-old man with mental health issues was arrested after being caught near the queen’s apartments armed with a loaded crossbow.

He admitted in court to trying to kill Elizabeth and was handed a nine-year sentence, to be served initially in the high-security Broadmoor psychiatric hospital.

The most famous incident was in July 1982, when a man named Michael Fagan sneaked into Buckingham Palace and made his way to Queen Elizabeth II’s bedroom.

He sat on her four-poster bed and had a 10-minute chat with her before being taken away by security. He was initially charged but the accusations were later dropped.

News of Monday’s break-in came just as William made his first visit to Downing Street for talks with Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

The two men discussed their “shared commitment to tackling the earth’s greatest challenges,” a Downing Street spokesperson said.

“They turned to homelessness and their shared desire to find sustainable options for prevention, followed by defence and security issues and the Commonwealth,” the spokesperson added.

The meeting was seen as another step towards the heir to the throne’s future role as monarch.

title: Trump celebrates USA co-hosting 2031 Women’s World Cup, hails Infantino
description:
President Donald Trump praised embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino on Tuesday while celebrating the United States being named a co-host of the 2031 Women’s World Cup.
Infantino, who gave Trump the first FIFA Peace Prize last December, is fighting to keep his job after causing outrage in July w
content:
President Donald Trump praised embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino on Tuesday while celebrating the United States being named a co-host of the 2031 Women’s World Cup.

Infantino, who gave Trump the first FIFA Peace Prize last December, is fighting to keep his job after causing outrage in July with a short-lived plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

A FIFA election next March in Morocco will decide if Infantino keeps his job against rival contenders Philippe Diallo of France and Kozo Tashima of Japan.

“Thank you to Gianni Infantino, and his great staff, for working to bring the Tournament to the USA,” Trump posted on social media.

Trump and Infantino awarded Spain the trophy at this year’s final of the World Cup, which was co-hosted by Canada and Mexico.

FIFA confirmed Monday that the United States will co-host the 2031 Women’s World Cup with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica after Infantino noted it was the “sole candidacy” for the tournament.

“I am proud to announce that the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2031 will take place in the United States!” Trump posted.

“After hosting the Most Successful World Cup in History, no Country is better positioned than the United States to be home to the largest Women’s Sporting Event in History.”

The Women’s World Cup field will expand to a record 48 teams in 2031.

“The FIFA Women’s World Cup 2031 will bring Generational Economic Impact to the United States, grow the sport of Soccer throughout our Country and the World, and showcase America’s Exceptionalism,” Trump posted.

AFP

title: 17 die, 25 injured in Zamfara road crash — FRSC
description:
A road traffic crash has claimed 17 lives at Kisami village, along the Gummi-Daki Takwas-Anka Road in Zamfara, the Federal Road Safety Corps has confirmed.
The FRSC Zamfara Sector Command disclosed this in a statement released by the command’s Public Relations Officer, Isah Aliyu, in Gusau on Tuesda
content:
A road traffic crash has claimed 17 lives at Kisami village, along the Gummi-Daki Takwas-Anka Road in Zamfara, the Federal Road Safety Corps has confirmed.

The FRSC Zamfara Sector Command disclosed this in a statement released by the command’s Public Relations Officer, Isah Aliyu, in Gusau on Tuesday.

It said the crash, which occurred on Monday, involved a Toyota Camry (ash colour) and a Fuso Canter (white colour).

According to the statement, the incident was caused by wrongful overtaking and loss of control.

It added that “52 people were involved in the crash, with 17 persons, all male, dying instantly, 25 injured, while 10 escaped unhurt.”

“The FRSC rescue team responded within 10 minutes of the crash and evacuated the injured and the corpses to the General Hospital, Gummi,” the statement said.

content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of promoting political violence to intimidate opposition parties and Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general elections, following the killing of six people in an attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Delta State.

The organisation said the attack on the campaign entourage of former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, exposed the dangers of allowing political violence to flourish ahead of the elections, warning that it could undermine peaceful electoral competition.

In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, the MDPCO condemned the November 23 incident, alleging that APC agents were responsible for the attack in Delta State.

It warned that the incident could be part of a broader attempt to deploy armed thugs against opposition parties and frustrate the conduct of peaceful elections.

The organisation said, “This APC’s resort to killing before the 2027 general elections raises apprehension of a bigger design to use armed thugs to unleash mayhem on innocent citizens apparently with the aim to frustrate the smooth conduct of the elections.”

It recalled President Bola Tinubu’s remark to his supporters ahead of the 2023 elections that political power was not served in a restaurant and urged them to ‘at all cost, fight for it, grab it, snatch it and run with it.’

The campaign organisation also cited an alleged threat by Edo State APC Chairman, Jarret Tenebe, to invoke the power of AK-47 against anyone who opposed the party’s plan to secure Tinubu’s re-election, accusing the ruling party of failing to condemn the statement.

It further alleged that opposition parties had suffered attacks in Sokoto, Kebbi, Edo, Lagos, Cross River, Kaduna and Kano states, describing the latest incident in Delta as part of a disturbing pattern.

The MDPCO accused the APC leadership of failing to take decisive action against members allegedly involved in political violence, warning that its silence could further embolden those responsible.

“This deafening silence and apparent reluctance to demand accountability deepen public apprehension and clears every doubt that the APC is not ready for a free fair, credible and peaceful democratic competition,” it said.

The organisation warned that Nigerians would not accept the use of violence or insecurity as instruments of electoral conquest, insisting that political parties must respect citizens’ freedom to choose their leaders.

It declared that the resort to violence would not alter what it described as Nigerians’ determination to vote the APC out of power.

“The resort to violence will not save the President from obvious defeat in January,” the organisation said.

It demanded an immediate end to what it described as attempts to suppress democratic participation, while urging Nigerians to support its principal, Engr. Seyi Makinde, the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), whom it said would reset the country through a government committed to transparency, security and citizens’ welfare.

title: NNPC Dismisses Missing $2.04bn Duke Oil Crude Proceeds Reports
description: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) Limited has debunked reports alleging that $2.04 billion in crude oil proceeds from cargoes lifted by Duke Oil Company Incorporated, now NNPC Trading S.A., is missing or unaccounted for.The company said all crude cargoes lifted under the Direct Sale Dir
content:
The Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) Limited has debunked reports alleging that $2.04 billion in crude oil proceeds from cargoes lifted by Duke Oil Company Incorporated, now NNPC Trading S.A., is missing or unaccounted for.

The company said all crude cargoes lifted under the Direct Sale Direct Purchase (DSDP) programme had been fully accounted for, with proceeds reconciled against the cost of refined petroleum products supplied to the Nigerian market.

NNPC’s Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odeh, stated this in a statement issued on Tuesday in Abuja.

The company explained that reports suggesting a financial gap arose from the absence of separate dollar receipts for some DSDP cargoes, noting that the crude proceeds were offset against the cost of petroleum products supplied under the contractual arrangement.

According to NNPC, the $2.04 billion cited in the reports represents the gross value of 29 cargoes whose proceeds were reconciled through the arrangement, rather than missing funds.

It explained that under the DSDP programme, Duke Oil and other participating traders lifted crude oil and supplied refined petroleum products, including petrol, for the Nigerian market.

The company notes that while crude oil was priced in US dollars, the products supplied were sold in naira.

It said that the value of the products delivered was therefore reconciled against the corresponding value of crude lifted, with the transactions reflected in the audited financial statements of the relevant entities.

NNPC further said the reports acknowledged that all 59 cargoes under review were accounted for and reconciled with their respective beneficiaries.

It disclosed that 30 cargoes were paid for in US dollars, while proceeds from 28 cargoes, valued at approximately $1.96 billion, were remitted in naira to the NNPC Group Treasury or NNPC Upstream Investment Management Services (NUIMS) accounts.

The NNPC states that the remaining cargo, a February 2023 Bonga tax-oil lifting valued at approximately $75.9 million, was paid directly into the then-designated dollar account of the Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS).

The company also defended Duke Oil’s corporate structure, rejecting suggestions that the subsidiary was merely NNPC operating under another name.

It said Duke Oil was incorporated in 1989 as a wholly owned trading subsidiary of NNPC, adding that its ownership had been documented in the company’s corporate history, audited financial statements and the Nigeria Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (NEITI) 2023 industry report.

According to NNPC, using a dedicated trading subsidiary is standard practice in the global oil and gas industry, while transactions between related entities are disclosed in line with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).

title: EFCC to investigate Kwankwaso over 10 properties allegedly linked to him
description:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has pledged to review a petition seeking an investigation into 10 properties allegedly linked to Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) vice-presidential candidate.
The commission gave the assurance on Tuesday after receiving a
content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has pledged to review a petition seeking an investigation into 10 properties allegedly linked to Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) vice-presidential candidate.

The commission gave the assurance on Tuesday after receiving a petition from the Society for Anti-Corruption and Good Governance Initiative (SACGGI) at its headquarters in Abuja.

The petition followed a protest by members of the organisation, who urged the anti-graft agency to investigate the alleged property holdings and establish the sources of funds used to acquire them.

The group, led by its spokesperson, Muhammad Abdullahi, also called for an examination of Kwankwaso’s bank accounts, tax records and asset declarations.

Responding on behalf of the EFCC chairman, the commission’s Chief of Staff, Michael Nzekwe, said the petition would be considered on its merits and handled professionally.

“EFCC is apolitical. We are not partisan. We are just here to ensure that the mandate of the commission is fulfilled. We have seen what you have submitted, and the commission will look into it on its merits and handle it professionally,” Nzekwe said.

He added that the petition would be forwarded to the commission’s leadership for appropriate action, assuring the protesters that the necessary steps would be taken promptly.

Earlier, Abdullahi said the petition followed the organisation’s review of the lifestyles and alleged property holdings of political office seekers ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He described SACGGI as a non-governmental, non-partisan and non-profit organisation comprising young professionals, including lawyers, accountants, engineers, journalists and community leaders, committed to accountability and good governance.

“We are young professionals, lawyers, accountants, engineers, journalists and community leaders who believe public office is public trust and no one is above the law,” he said.

The petition listed 10 properties allegedly connected to Kwankwaso and asked the EFCC to independently verify their ownership and status.

Among the properties are Key Science Academy along the Abuja-Keffi Expressway in Masaka, Nasarawa State; the former headquarters of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) at No. 1 Mahatma Gandhi Street, Area 11, Abuja; and Plot 3060, CZ A06, Maitama District, Abuja.

Others include the former Clintonia Hotel in Apo, Abuja; Tidbe Plaza in the Central Business District; a building at No. 10 Port Harcourt Crescent, Area 11, Garki; and No. 28 Katsina Ala Crescent, Maitama.

The organisation also listed Nigeria-Egypt International School in Gwarinpa Estate, Abuja; Kano Mansion on Miller Road, Kano; and Hafsat Plaza on Constitution Avenue, Abuja.

SACGGI said it identified the properties through public reports but maintained that their ownership must be independently established by the EFCC.

It questioned whether the alleged acquisitions were consistent with Kwankwaso’s legitimate earnings and whether the properties were properly declared during his years in public office.

The group urged the commission to conduct a lifestyle audit of the former Kano State governor and examine his asset declarations filed with the Code of Conduct Bureau from 1999 to date.

It also called for forensic examinations of his bank accounts and tax records to establish the sources of funds allegedly used to acquire the properties.

Furthermore, the organisation asked the EFCC to verify the properties through the Abuja Geographic Information Systems, the Federal Capital Territory Administration, Kano State land authorities and the Corporate Affairs Commission.

It also urged the commission to invite Kwankwaso for questioning if necessary, while stressing that he should be given an opportunity to respond to the allegations in accordance with the principles of fair hearing and natural justice.

SACGGI further called for collaboration between the EFCC and other relevant agencies, including the Code of Conduct Bureau, the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission, the Federal Inland Revenue Service and the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit.

The organisation urged the commission to prosecute anyone found culpable and recover any public funds established to have been diverted or misappropriated. It also requested that the outcome of the investigation be made public before the 2027 elections.

In the petition, SACGGI said its action was not motivated by political considerations.

“This protest is not borne out of malice or political witch-hunt. It is borne out of the desire to ensure that as Nigeria heads towards 2027, only persons with proven integrity are allowed to seek the highest offices. Public office is public trust,” the group stated.

It added: “If these properties are legitimately acquired, the candidate should have no difficulty proving the source, and if otherwise, the law should take its full course irrespective of political status.”

Kwankwaso has held several public offices, including Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives between 1992 and 1993, governor of Kano State from 1999 to 2003 and 2011 to 2015, Minister of Defence from 2003 to 2007, and senator representing Kano Central from 2015 to 2019.

title: It was reprisal action – Ughelli LG chairman accuses Omo-Agege’s boys of firing first shot
description:
The Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, Jaro Movudu, has described the violence involving Senator Ovie Omo-Agege and his supporters as a reprisal, accusing the senator’s men of killing community members before the incident escalated.



Movudu, who had earlier been accuse
content:
The Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, Jaro Movudu, has described the violence involving Senator Ovie Omo-Agege and his supporters as a reprisal, accusing the senator’s men of killing community members before the incident escalated.

Movudu, who had earlier been accused by Omo-Agege of masterminding an alleged assassination attempt on the senator, denied the allegation, claiming that the violence was triggered by the killing of the community’s president-general and other residents.

Speaking on Channels Television on Tuesday, the council chairman alleged that Omo-Agege’s supporters fired the first shots, killing members of the community where the senator held his campaign rally.

He said the incident was a sad development, extending condolences to victims on both sides of the violence, regardless of their political affiliations.

“Let me express my sincere condolences to all those who lost their lives yesterday on both sides. Most of them know to me. They are my friends. Whether they are working for NDC or APC, nobody’s life is worth the ambition of anybody, and it was a sad day yesterday,” he said.

Movudu alleged that Omo-Agege had made provocative remarks against him during his campaign visit to the community, claiming that the senator allegedly incited his supporters before they opened fire.

He said he was not present at the venue when the campaign took place, as he was in his office, but alleged that Omo-Agege abused him while addressing residents and subsequently riled up his supporters.

“But when he was leaving, he riled up the people. He gave instructions to his boys, and then they gunned down the president-general of the community and then shut other people down. It was that death that brought that anger,” Movudu alleged.

The council chairman described the subsequent violence as a reprisal for the killing, claiming that the community was angered by the death of its leader and other innocent residents.

“What happened yesterday was a reprisal action to answer to the unjust killing of the president and two other onlookers who were innocent,” he said.

Reacting to Omo-Agege’s claim that he was targeted for assassination, Movudu questioned the presence of firearms at the senator’s campaign rally, alleging that his supporters were armed.

“At the end of it all, he came to TV and was saying that they wanted to kill him. You don’t go to campaign rallies with AK-47. You don’t go to campaign rallies with pump-action rifles. What are you going to use them for?” he asked.

Movudu further questioned why supporters attending a political rally would be carrying weapons, alleging that the firearms were used against members of the community.

“The people that are going to vote for you, you want to kill them?” he said.

His allegations come amid conflicting accounts of the violence, with Omo-Agege accusing Movudu of orchestrating an assassination attempt against him during his campaign visit to Delta community. The incident reportedly left four people dead and several others injured.

title: Morocco rejects CAS verdict, vows further legal action over Senegal’s AFCON title
description:
The Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) has rejected the Court of Arbitration for Sport’s (CAS) decision reinstating Senegal as the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) champions, vowing to pursue further legal action to challenge the ruling.
The Moroccan federation also renewed its allegation t
content:
The Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) has rejected the Court of Arbitration for Sport’s (CAS) decision reinstating Senegal as the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) champions, vowing to pursue further legal action to challenge the ruling.

The Moroccan federation also renewed its allegation that Senegalese Football Federation President Abdoulaye Fall had telephone contact with German arbitrator Ulrich Haas, one of the three members of the CAS panel, 48 hours before the verdict was delivered.

In a statement published on its official X account on Tuesday, November 24, the FRMF expressed surprise that CAS did not address its request for legal consequences over the alleged communication, which it argued could undermine the integrity and credibility of the arbitration proceedings.

The statement read: “The Royal Moroccan Football Federation has taken note of the decision issued by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, in Lausanne, Switzerland, concerning the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation against the decision of the Appeals Committee of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) relating to the final match of the Africa Cup of Nations.

“In this regard, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest over the failure to consider its request, which sought to ensure that the necessary legal consequences were applied to practices capable of undermining the integrity and credibility of the arbitration proceedings.

“In particular, this concerns the confirmed communication between German arbitrator Ulrich Haas and the President of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was issued.”

The Moroccan federation also criticised CAS for allegedly failing to consider the positions of the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and FIFA on players leaving the pitch without the referee’s permission.

“The Royal Moroccan Football Federation also notes that the decision did not take into account the position recently established by both the International Football Association Board (IFAB), the body responsible for the Laws of the Game, and FIFA regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and sanctions,” the statement added.

The federation said it remained determined to challenge the ruling through every available legal channel.

“Accordingly, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation reaffirms its determination to pursue all available legal avenues to challenge the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport,” it said.

The reaction followed Tuesday’s CAS verdict, which overturned CAF’s Appeals Committee decision awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory in the disputed final and restored Senegal’s original 1-0 win.

CAS upheld Senegal’s appeal, ruling that the AFCON regulations relied upon by CAF to declare the Teranga Lions losers by forfeiture were not applicable because the referee had allowed the match to resume after the Senegalese players returned to the pitch.

The controversy dates back to the final played at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat on January 18, 2026, when Senegal defeated hosts Morocco 1-0 after extra time to win their second continental title.

The match was disrupted during stoppage time after the referee awarded Morocco a penalty following a VAR review, shortly after Senegal had a goal disallowed.

Angered by the decision, Senegal coach Pape Thiaw instructed his players to leave the pitch in protest. They returned after approximately 14 minutes, but Morocco’s Brahim Diaz missed the resulting penalty before Pape Gueye scored Senegal’s winning goal in extra time.

Morocco subsequently lodged a complaint with CAF, arguing that Senegal’s walk-off had disrupted the normal course of the match.

CAF’s Disciplinary Board initially upheld the result while imposing sanctions on both teams. However, its Appeals Committee reversed that decision on March 17, ruling that Senegal had forfeited the final for breaching Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations. Morocco was consequently awarded a 3-0 victory.

Senegal rejected the decision and appealed to CAS on March 25, seeking the restoration of the original result.

The case was heard at CAS headquarters in Lausanne, Switzerland, on October 8, with representatives of Senegal, Morocco and CAF presenting their arguments behind closed doors.

Before the verdict, Morocco had also raised concerns over the alleged contact between Fall and one of the arbitrators handling the appeal.

Reuters, citing a source familiar with the matter, reported that the Moroccan federation had notified CAS about the alleged telephone conversation during the proceedings. The source claimed Fall spoke with one of the three arbitrators on a Sunday, 48 hours before the ruling.

Moroccan media outlet Hespress, citing French sports broadcaster RMC Sport, also reported that the federation’s legal adviser had written to CAS seeking clarification over the alleged conversation between Fall and a German legal expert on the panel.

The Senegalese federation denied the allegation. Its Secretary-General, Sow, dismissed the claim as “an imaginary appeal”.

“President Abdoulaye Fall doesn’t even know the judges involved in this case, because he wasn’t present on the day of the hearing,” he said.

The post Morocco rejects CAS verdict, vows further legal action over Senegal’s AFCON title appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: 2027: Akiolu urges politicians to shun violence, campaign on track records
description:
The Oba of Lagos, Rilwan Akiolu, has urged politicians to shun violence and allow their records and past performance to speak for them, warning that Nigerians do not want political rancour and bloodshed.
Akiolu said candidates should focus on presenting their programmes and achievements to Nigerians
content:
The Oba of Lagos, Rilwan Akiolu, has urged politicians to shun violence and allow their records and past performance to speak for them, warning that Nigerians do not want political rancour and bloodshed.

Akiolu said candidates should focus on presenting their programmes and achievements to Nigerians rather than resorting to hostility, adding that the country needed cooperation, patience and peaceful political engagement.

The monarch spoke after the installation of the new Kakawa of Lagos, High Chief Jamiu Kakawa, and Eletu of Iwashe, High Chief Teslim Oluwatosin, at his palace in Iduganran, Lagos Island, on Tuesday.

He said, “My pleading to all of us in this country is we should give peace a chance. See the programmes of all the aspirants, see what they have done, and pray for them and support them and all will be well with us.”

The traditional ruler, who urged politicians to be guided by their records rather than political hostility, said their past conduct and performance should determine how Nigerians assessed them.

“You see the performances of each of the presidential candidates, what some of them have done in the past will speak for them. In life, a man doesn’t get to position and you don’t know how he has behaved,” he said.

Akiolu, who noted that Lagosians were opposed to violence and rancour, urged those with resources to support the less privileged rather than accumulate excessive wealth.

“Lagosians don’t want rancour, violence. The one that has should give the one that does not have. Why amass so much riches?” he asked.

His appeal comes amid reported attacks and disruptions involving political activities in parts of the country, including the killing of supporters during a campaign visit by former Deputy President of the Senate, Ovie Omo-Agege, in Delta State, and the recent disruption of a meeting of the Nigeria Democratic Congress in Lagos.

Speaking further, the monarch appealed to Nigerians to give President Bola Tinubu more time to address the country’s challenges, saying the incumbent’s performance should be considered in assessing his administration.

“As far as I am concerned, the performance of the incumbent president speaks a lot for him. We have experienced many things around this area. With God on our side, and the cooperation of our people, all went well,” he said.

He added, “My special appeal to all Nigerians is to give more time to the incumbent president on this assignment and with the support and prayers of all of us, all will be well. We need patience.”

Akiolu called for cooperation, prayers and closeness to God, expressing optimism that the country would overcome its challenges.

“All we require in this country is cooperation, prayer and closeness to God,” he said.

On state police, the monarch commended the new State Police Law but stressed that its success would depend on impartial enforcement and implementation.

“Anybody can make a law but the application is what matters. If it is approached and enforced and implemented with the fear of God, everything will be in order,” he said.

The post 2027: Akiolu urges politicians to shun violence, campaign on track records appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
