title: Ogun ADC gov candidate hails Supreme Court judgment, calls for unity
description:
Dr Biodun Ogundipe has lauded the Supreme Court for affirming him as the governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress in Ogun State for the 2027 election.
Ogundipe, in a statement reacting to the judgment delivered by the apex court in Abuja on Tuesday, described the verdict as a landma
content:
Dr Biodun Ogundipe has lauded the Supreme Court for affirming him as the governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress in Ogun State for the 2027 election.

Ogundipe, in a statement reacting to the judgment delivered by the apex court in Abuja on Tuesday, described the verdict as a landmark decision that reaffirmed the principles of truth, due process and strict adherence to established rules governing political party primaries.

The Supreme Court had set aside the earlier decisions of the Federal High Court and the Court of Appeal, which had declared Otunba Jimi Lawal the ADC governorship candidate in Ogun State, thereby resolving the prolonged legal dispute in Ogundipe’s favour.

Expressing appreciation to the judiciary, Ogundipe said the judgment had brought clarity to the controversy surrounding the party’s governorship primary and established the appropriate party organ with the authority to collate and declare election results.

Ogundipe said, “I sincerely appreciate the Supreme Court of Nigeria for its landmark judgment affirming my candidacy as the duly recognised Gubernatorial Candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Ogun State.

“By setting aside the concurrent decisions of the Federal High Court and the Court of Appeal, which had declared Jimi Lawal as the party’s candidate, the apex court has reaffirmed the importance of truth, due process and strict adherence to the established rules governing political party primaries.

“This judgment brings clarity to the legal dispute and settles the question of the appropriate party organ vested with the authority to collate and declare results in ADC primary elections.”

The ADC candidate also commended the Supreme Court for recognising the party’s Three-Tier Primary Election Guidelines, established by its National Working Committee (NWC), as the organisational framework for conducting and determining the outcome of its primary elections.

According to him, the court’s recognition of the guidelines underscored the importance of respecting the constitutional and institutional structures through which political parties conduct their internal electoral processes.

Ogundipe said, “I particularly commend the Supreme Court for recognising the clarity and organisational framework of the ADC’s Three-Tier Primary Election Guidelines established by the National Working Committee (NWC), in determining the conduct and outcome of the party’s primary election.

“This decision is consistent with the Supreme Court’s established position on the constitutional and institutional powers of political parties in conducting their primary elections. I receive this judgment with humility, gratitude and a renewed sense of responsibility.”

He further thanked the ADC leadership, members, supporters and stakeholders for remaining steadfast throughout the legal contest, noting that their patience and confidence had sustained him during the period of uncertainty.

Ogundipe urged party members to regard the judgment as an opportunity to strengthen internal unity and concentrate on positioning the ADC for the 2027 governorship election.

He stressed that the time had come to move beyond the legal disagreement and work collectively towards the party’s political aspirations in Ogun State.

“I thank the leadership of our great party, our supporters, stakeholders and members for their steadfastness, patience and confidence throughout this process.

“The time has come to put the legal contest behind us, strengthen our party’s unity and focus collectively on the task ahead,” he said.

In a unanimous judgment delivered on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, in Abuja, a five-member panel of the Supreme Court set aside the earlier decisions of the Federal High Court and the Court of Appeal, which had recognised Otunba Jimi Lawal as the party’s governorship candidate.

The panel was presided over by Justice Emmanuel Akomaye Agim, while Justice Haruna Simon Tsammani read the lead judgment.

The dispute arose from conflicting claims over the outcome of the ADC governorship primary election in the state. The disagreement culminated in a Federal High Court judgment in Abeokuta in July 2026, which overturned Ogundipe’s claim to the party’s ticket and declared Lawal the candidate.

Dissatisfied with the ruling, Ogundipe challenged the decision, arguing that the party’s State Congress lacked the authority to collate and declare a result contrary to the outcome of the primary election conducted by the State Electoral Committee constituted by the party’s National Working Committee (NWC).

The Supreme Court’s decision effectively restores Ogundipe’s claim to the ADC governorship ticket and settles the legal controversy over the party organ authorised to collate and declare the results of its primary elections.

The session was presided over by a boa
content:
The Police Service Commission (PSC) has approved the appointment and posting of CP Usman Sheikh Adamu as the new Commissioner of Police for Zamfara State.

The approval followed an interview session held at the commission’s corporate headquarters in Jabi, Abuja.

The session was presided over by a board member, Justice Paul Adamu Galumje (JSC, rtd), on behalf of the PSC Chairman, DIG Hashimu Salihu Argungu (rtd).

In a statement issued by the commission’s spokesperson, Torty Njoku, the PSC said the newly appointed commissioner had been directed to uphold professionalism and neutrality in the discharge of his responsibilities.

The commission also stressed the importance of maintaining these standards, particularly as Nigeria prepares for the 2027 general elections.

According to the statement, Adamu was also tasked with addressing the security challenges confronting Zamfara State and prioritising public safety.

Before his new appointment, Adamu served as Area Commander, Jos Metro, Plateau State Command; Area Commander in Yobe State; Deputy Commissioner of Police, Criminal Investigation Department (CID), Plateau State; and Commissioner of Police, SERVICOM, at the Force Headquarters, Abuja.

An alumnus of the University of Maiduguri, where he obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Linguistics, Adamu joined the Nigeria Police Force on June 10, 1994, as a Cadet Assistant Superintendent of Police.

The commission said the approval had been communicated to the Inspector-General of Police through a letter signed by its Secretary, Chief Onyemuche Nnamani.

title: How I encountered the devil thrice, saw gates of hell – Pope Francis
description:
The late Pope Francis recounted three encounters with what he described as the devil and a terrifying vision of the entrance to hell in his private diaries published posthumously on Tuesday.
The diaries also reveal that the pontiff experienced a two-year spiritual crisis between 2021 and 2022, durin
content:
The late Pope Francis recounted three encounters with what he described as the devil and a terrifying vision of the entrance to hell in his private diaries published posthumously on Tuesday.

The diaries also reveal that the pontiff experienced a two-year spiritual crisis between 2021 and 2022, during which he struggled with temptations associated with power and the exercise of authority.

The revelations are contained in The Private Diary of Pope Francis, a 160-page book written by Cardinal Víctor Manuel Fernández, one of the late pope’s closest aides and a fellow Argentine.

According to CNN, which reported the revelations on Tuesday, the book contains entries from diaries Francis kept intermittently between 1992 and 2024, first as a bishop in Argentina and later as pope.

The volume reveals that Francis faced “frequent demonic attacks” and detailed three encounters with the devil—two while he was archbishop of Buenos Aires and a third in 2018 after his election as pope.

In an August 18, 2024 entry, Francis wrote of the devil’s “eyes of fire,” describing them as “menacing” and “seductive.”

“I can’t forget his eyes the first two times — from the car when I was returning to the house, and in the choir loft during Mass. However, he always reappears in different situations,” he noted.

The third encounter came shortly after a 2018 trip to Chile overshadowed by the clerical sexual abuse scandal.

In a January 24, 2021 entry, Francis recalled: “On one occasion, a few days after returning to Rome, I was in a meeting. I saw him and heard his voice [his underlining], triumphant, possessing everything: ‘Now I’ve gotten everything I wanted.’ Just as I can’t forget his eyes from the previous two, in this case, I can’t forget the powerful raspiness of his voice. The Lord granted me an opportunity to leave that meeting, and he thus freed me.”

Based on Catholic teaching, the devil is a fallen angel. Catholic tradition cautions that those who are serious about attaining holiness will often encounter strong spiritual opposition.

The diaries also describe a vision of “the entrance to hell” in 2018, which Francis characterized as a form of “pagan seduction in full force.”

“I peeked in to look a little and it terrified me. It was before going to sleep. I grabbed the rosary as a weapon. I thank the Lord for this help,” he wrote.

The book reveals that Francis experienced a spiritual crisis in 2021 and 2022, which Fernández linked to temptations associated with power, excessive activity and feelings of self-sufficiency.

The late pontiff reportedly described the crisis as involving “governance issues, pressure regarding decisions to make, and aridity and desolation.”

To overcome the temptation, Francis sought to practise greater humility and patience, including by retaining some officials in the Church’s central administration despite criticism of their conduct.

Fernández recalled an occasion when a bishop asked Francis why he had not dismissed an official in the Roman Curia who had publicly criticised him and pursued what the bishop considered a different agenda.

“After an interminable silence, he responded by explaining that he felt a strong sensation in his heart that God did not want him to become a puppeteer who uses and manipulates people according to his own convenience. He explained that, for this reason, he preferred to let that person remain in his position,” Fernández wrote.

In an entry dated December 30, 2022, Francis said he had resisted the temptation to treat “others like puppets”.

He also recalled that, in 2018, a sense of self-sufficiency and the belief that he could solve everything had brought him close to what he described as the gates of hell.

“This sense of self-sufficiency and I can solve everything brought me to the gates of hell. I can’t forget the day I saw it,” he wrote.

Fernández explained that the crisis was connected to Francis’ struggle with the temptation to discover what it meant to exercise personal power.

He added that the pope considered feeling “above the world” through power to be “the path of the worst spiritual worldliness imaginable”.

The diaries also contain Francis’ reflections on the clerical sexual abuse scandal in Chile in 2018, when he faced criticism for his handling of allegations against a bishop accused of witnessing and covering up abuse.

The pope later apologised for his handling of the case and summoned Chilean bishops to Rome, where they collectively offered their resignations.

“Devastated because of the situation in Chile and the dialogue with the journalists on the airplane. I fell off the cot then,” Francis wrote.

The book explains that the expression “fell off the cot” means suddenly waking up to something.

The diaries also reveal Francis’ assessment of Cardinal Robert Prevost, who succeeded him as Pope Leo XIV.

According to Fernández, Francis described Prevost as “a great pastor, a generous missionary, and an irreproachable man”.

He also praised other cardinals who had criticised him, describing Cardinal Robert Sarah as having “a refined spiritual sensitivity” and saying of Cardinal Gerhard Muller that he “seems aggressive but he’s a good man”.

The entries further show Francis’ frequent exhaustion and dedication to his ministry. In 2019, he described himself as “feeling exhausted, almost without spiritual support and without a point of reference”.

Francis, who became the first Latin American pope when he was elected on March 13, 2013, died on April 21, 2025, aged 88, after being hospitalised with double pneumonia.

His funeral was held on April 26, 2025, at St Peter’s Square in the Vatican.

Fernández said the diaries were intended to reveal the heart of Jorge Mario Bergoglio, the late pope’s birth name.

“His total dedication, coupled with frequently feeling completely exhausted, speaks of heroism in pastoral charity,” he said.

The diaries are being published by the Vatican Publishing House, while Image Books, an imprint of Penguin Random House Christian Publishing Group, is releasing the English-language edition in the United States and Canada.

The post How I encountered the devil thrice, saw gates of hell – Pope Francis appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: Yari urges Zamfara voters to back APC candidates
description:
By Idris Salisu, Gusau



The Director-General of President Bola Tinubu’s Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, has urged voters in Zamfara State to support All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates at all levels in the 2027 general elections.







Yari made the appeal on Monday at the flag-o
content:
By Idris Salisu, Gusau

The Director-General of President Bola Tinubu’s Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, has urged voters in Zamfara State to support All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates at all levels in the 2027 general elections.

Yari made the appeal on Monday at the flag-off of the re-election campaign of Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, in Talata Mafara, headquarters of Talata Mafara Local Government Area.

The event attracted supporters from the 14 local government areas of the state, including party faithful, women and youth groups, traditional leaders and other political stakeholders.

Addressing the gathering, Yari, a former governor of Zamfara State and senator representing Zamfara West, said voting for the APC at all levels, from the presidency to the state Houses of Assembly, would enable the state to benefit from federal government projects, appointments and other interventions.

He argued that Zamfara could not afford to remain in opposition in 2027, urging residents to align with the ruling party at the federal level.

“I urge you, the good people of Zamfara, to vote for APC from top to bottom in 2027. Vote for President Tinubu, vote for Governor Lawal, vote for our senators, House of Representatives members and State Assembly members. That is the only way Zamfara will move forward,” Yari said.

He also urged voters to support Tinubu’s re-election bid, describing the President as the candidate capable of driving development in the North-West and the country.

Yari said the Tinubu administration had demonstrated commitment to addressing insecurity, reviving the economy, improving infrastructure and repositioning the country for sustainable growth.

He noted that the North-West, which had experienced years of banditry, kidnapping and economic challenges, needed sustained investment in security and development.

“President Tinubu is the only candidate who, if given a second mandate, will develop the North-West and the country at large. He has the vision, the experience and the political will to take Nigeria to the next level. We must give him our full support,” he said.

Yari called on Zamfara residents to give Tinubu substantial electoral support in 2027, as they did in 2023, to enable him to complete his reform agenda.

He also canvassed support for Governor Lawal’s second-term ambition, saying the governor needed the backing of residents to consolidate his administration’s Rescue Zamfara Agenda.

According to him, cooperation between the Federal Government and the Zamfara State Government would accelerate development in security, job creation, education, healthcare and infrastructure.

The campaign launch was attended by APC stakeholders, government officials, members of the state executive council, federal and state lawmakers, local government chairmen, women and youth groups, and party supporters.

The post 2027: Yari urges Zamfara voters to back APC candidates appeared first on Vanguard News.

Kareem, who hails from Odenk Upogoro Ward in Okene Local Government Area of Kogi State, ann
content:
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Kogi Central has recorded a political gain following the resignation of a prominent All Progressives Congress (APC) chieftain, Hon. Umar Kareem, popularly known as Kasco.

Kareem, who hails from Odenk Upogoro Ward in Okene Local Government Area of Kogi State, announced his departure from the ruling APC in a resignation letter addressed to the party’s ward chairman.

The letter, which became public on Tuesday, stated that his resignation from the APC took immediate effect.

He explained that the decision followed extensive consultations, careful consideration and an assessment of his political journey, personal convictions and future aspirations.

Kareem said he had remained loyal and committed to the APC over the years, contributing his time, resources and efforts to the growth and development of the party.

However, he said his decision to leave was informed by his belief that political participation should be based on mutual respect, fairness, recognition, inclusiveness and a genuine sense of belonging.

“I firmly believe that political participation should be anchored on mutual respect, fairness, recognition, inclusiveness and a genuine sense of belonging,” he said.

He expressed appreciation to the APC for the relationships he built and experiences gained during his membership, while wishing the party’s leadership well.

Kareem’s defection to the PDP comes amid political realignments in Kogi Central ahead of future electoral contests.

title: Governments that listen only to praise risk losing touch with citizens – Shettima
description:
Vice-President Kashim Shettima on Tuesday called on Nigerian leaders to embrace constructive criticism and accountability, warning that a government which listens only to praise risks losing touch with the people it is elected to serve.
Shettima said the country must value the contributions of journ
content:
Vice-President Kashim Shettima on Tuesday called on Nigerian leaders to embrace constructive criticism and accountability, warning that a government which listens only to praise risks losing touch with the people it is elected to serve.

Shettima said the country must value the contributions of journalists and intellectuals who challenge those in authority, stressing that their criticisms, however uncomfortable, could help strengthen public institutions and deepen democratic accountability.

The VP made the call during his goodwill message delivered virtually at the public presentation of nine books drawn from the celebrated Monday Lines column of Saturday Tribune Editor, Lasisi Olagunju, at the International Conference Centre, University of Ibadan, Ibadan, the Oyo State capital.

The event brought together prominent political leaders, academics, journalists and other dignitaries to celebrate Olagunju’s 15 years of political commentary, which has examined Nigeria’s leadership, governance, institutions and national development.

Shettima, who congratulated the author on what he described as a remarkable contribution to Nigerian journalism and letters, said the preservation of the columns in book form would provide future generations with an important record of the country’s political and intellectual history.

He said, “There is a wisdom that says when an elder dies, a library burns. But there is a tragedy we seldom speak about. When a society refuses to listen to its writers, it allows its library to burn while its custodians are still alive.”

He described Olagunju as belonging to a distinguished tradition of journalists who understand that the responsibility of the pen is to awaken the conscience of society.

“His writings remind us that the newspaper is more than a record of yesterday’s events. It is a conversation between a nation and its conscience,” he said.

Shettima said one of the greatest dangers facing public officeholders was the temptation to listen only to opinions that affirmed their positions.

“Human nature draws us towards agreement and reassurance. Yet, the voices that challenge our assumptions may sometimes be the very voices we need most. A government that listens only to praise risks losing touch with the people it was elected to serve,” he said.

The VP maintained that journalists who asked difficult questions could render valuable services to the institutions they scrutinised, adding that disagreement should not be interpreted as disrespect.

He, however, emphasised that journalists also had a responsibility to uphold honesty, fairness and intellectual courage, just as public officials must demonstrate humility, accountability and a willingness to listen.

“There is also something remarkable about the decision to preserve 15 years of newspaper commentary in books. A newspaper may be read in the morning and discarded by evening. But the ideas it carries can outlive the events that inspired them,” he said.

He added that the books had preserved the anxieties, contradictions, hopes and arguments of a generation, expressing the hope that they would continue to provoke thought and encourage honest conversations, adding, “The greatness of a nation lies partly in its willingness to examine itself.”

In his remarks, Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde called for a socio-political reset of Nigeria, saying the country must return to the vision of its founding fathers, who envisaged a federal system that accommodates the country’s diverse nationalities.

Makinde, who is the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement, said the reset would ensure that governance worked for everyone, irrespective of ethnic background, gender or religious affiliation, adding that the proposal was aimed at rebuilding Nigeria’s socio-political space around inclusion, transparency and accountability.

The governor, who said he had been promoting the reset agenda across the country, maintained that Nigerians should consider a different course if the existing system was not delivering the desired results.

“We came out and said, Let us reset Nigeria. That is the message I have been carrying all over the country. If Nigeria is working for you, if you are okay with the state of things, then don’t change anything. But if it’s not, then let us take a different course. Let us reset our socio-political space.”

He said the journalist’s work had demonstrated that his Monday Lines column could not have been sustained over the years without him being regarded as a vocal critic of leadership.

Makinde said he identified with Olagunju’s experience as a beneficiary of opportunities provided by Nigeria, recalling that he enjoyed free education in Oyo State between 1980 and 1985 before proceeding to the University of Lagos, where he studied engineering without paying tuition fees.

The governor also recalled that he secured employment in Port Harcourt on the strength of his skills and knowledge, despite having no personal connections in the city, noting that Olagunju similarly secured employment at the Nigerian Tribune through his professional competence.

Earlier, the Chairman of the occasion, Prof. Toyin Falola, described Olagunju as a rare journalist-turned-public intellectual whose weekly column had become an archive of Nigeria’s political and intellectual history.

The Mother of the Day and Chairman of the Board of African Newspapers of Nigeria, PLC, publishers of the Tribune titles, Olatokunbo Awolowo-Dosunmu, described the nine books as an extraordinary harvest of intellectual labour, discipline and dedication.

She congratulated Olagunju on what she called a remarkable literary and journalistic achievement, commending the author for sustaining a column that had grown beyond its original newspaper platform.

Awolowo-Dosunmu said Monday Lines had become a running commentary on the Nigerian condition, capturing the country’s triumphs and disappointments, contradictions and aspirations, as well as the often bewildering turns in its national journey.

In his vote of thanks, Olagunju said the decision to publish nine volumes was informed by the need to preserve 15 years of newspaper commentary and provide a coherent record of his intellectual work.

He explained that the books contained selected and arranged columns from the Monday Lines series, which began in October 2011.

Dignitaries at the event were former Osun State Governors Olagunsoye Oyinlola and Adegboyega Oyetola; former Minister of Education, Prof. Tunde Adeniran; former Ambassador to the Philippines, Yemi Farounbi; Oyo State Deputy Governor, Bayo Lawal; among others.

The post Governments that listen only to praise risk losing touch with citizens – Shettima appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Northern govs dissolve NNDC board, order comprehensive audit
description:
The Governors of the 19 Northern states have dissolved the Board of Directors of the New Nigerian Development Company, jointly owned by the states, as part of efforts to reposition the company and strengthen its operations.
The decision was taken on Tuesday at a Special General Meeting in Kaduna by
content:
The Governors of the 19 Northern states have dissolved the Board of Directors of the New Nigerian Development Company, jointly owned by the states, as part of efforts to reposition the company and strengthen its operations.

The decision was taken on Tuesday at a Special General Meeting in Kaduna by the Secretaries to the Governments of the 19 Northern states, who represented their respective governments as shareholders.

The shareholders resolved that a new board would be constituted, subject to the adoption of the relevant ordinary resolutions at a duly convened general meeting and compliance with statutory requirements.

Addressing journalists after the meeting, the Secretary to the Gombe State Government, Prof. Ibrahim Abubakar Njodi, said the shareholders had agreed to undertake a comprehensive reorganisation of the company to improve its performance and restore confidence in its administration.

He said the exercise was aimed at strengthening the company’s institutional capacity, improving corporate governance, enhancing operational efficiency and repositioning it as a viable investment and development institution serving the collective economic interests of the 19 Northern states.

Njodi said, “The shareholders have resolved to undertake a comprehensive reorganisation and repositioning of NNDC to strengthen its institutional capacity, improve its corporate governance, enhance operational efficiency and reposition it as a viable investment and development institution.”

He explained that a new board would provide strategic leadership, effective supervision, policy direction and corporate oversight for the company.

According to him, the composition, nomination and appointment of the new directors would reflect the ownership interests of the participating states, the company’s Memorandum and Articles of Association, and the provisions of the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020.

“The shareholders shall subsequently approve the nominations and appointments of the new directors in accordance with the company’s constitutional documents and applicable law,” he said.

Njodi further disclosed that the incoming board would review the existing management structure, personnel, administrative arrangements, operational framework and overall performance of the company.

He said the exercise would enable the new board to strengthen the management structure and promote accountability, professionalism and improved corporate performance.

The incoming board would also conduct a comprehensive corporate governance, financial, administrative and operational audit of the company, he added.

According to Njodi, the audit would cover NNDC’s financial position, assets and liabilities, existing investments, subsidiaries, joint ventures and other commercial interests.

The post Northern govs dissolve NNDC board, order comprehensive audit appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: No alliance between Otti, Orji Kalu — LP
description:
By Ugochukwu Alaribe



UMUAHIA — The Labour Party (LP) in Abia State has denied any political alliance between Governor Alex Otti and Senator Orji Uzor Kalu, representing Abia North Senatorial District, ahead of the 2027 general elections.







The party also urged Kalu to desist from what it des
content:
By Ugochukwu Alaribe

UMUAHIA — The Labour Party (LP) in Abia State has denied any political alliance between Governor Alex Otti and Senator Orji Uzor Kalu, representing Abia North Senatorial District, ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The party also urged Kalu to desist from what it described as attempts to impose a political coalition on it, insisting that it was not interested in any alliance with the All Progressives Congress (APC) or any other party for the Abia North senatorial seat.

The state Publicity Secretary of the party, Emenike Iroegbu, stated this following the dismantling of a billboard bearing the portraits of Otti and Kalu in Arochukwu Local Government Area.

Iroegbu said the billboard, titled ‘Coalition of Choice’, was intended to create the impression of a political alliance between the governor and the senator, insisting that no such arrangement existed.

The billboard was reportedly dismantled over concerns that it could mislead the public and for allegedly failing to comply with statutory outdoor advertising regulations.

The party condemned its erection, describing it as an attempt to misinform voters in Abia North.

Iroegbu said, “We have made it categorically clear that the Labour Party in Abia State is neither in talks nor in any form of political coalition with the APC or any other political party.

“The Labour Party in Abia State has no coalition with any party as regards Abia North Senatorial Seat, and it is wrong for individuals or groups to erect billboards misinforming our people about a coalition when there is none.

“We call on Senator Orji Uzor Kalu to stop trying to force a coalition on the Labour Party. Our party is not interested in any coalition for the Abia North senatorial seat.”

He further alleged that Kalu was seeking to associate himself politically with Governor Otti ahead of the 2027 elections, adding that the Labour Party would not allow the public to be misled.

The party commended the Abia State Signages and Advertising Agency (ABSSAA) for removing the billboard, stressing that public communication materials must comply with relevant regulatory requirements.

Iroegbu also disclosed that the party had a substantive senatorial candidate for Abia North, Chief David Onuoha Bourdex.

He said the party would not allow what it described as misleading political narratives to confuse its supporters across Arochukwu, Bende, Isuikwuato, Ohafia and Umunneochi local government areas.

title: Delta killings: Police invite Omo-Agege, LG chairman, five others
description:
The Delta State Police Command has invited former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, the Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Area, Jaro Egbo, and five other individuals for questioning over the deadly violence in Uduere community, Delta State.
The invitations followed a shooting
content:
The Delta State Police Command has invited former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, the Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Area, Jaro Egbo, and five other individuals for questioning over the deadly violence in Uduere community, Delta State.

The invitations followed a shooting incident during a campaign visit by Omo-Agege, the Nigeria Democratic Congress candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections, on Monday.

The police also disclosed that Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, accompanied by the Commissioner of Police, CP Samuel Erale, and other heads of security agencies, visited the community on Tuesday for an on-the-spot assessment of the incident.

The Police Public Relations Officer in the state, Bright Edafe, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying the invitations were part of efforts to establish the involvement of those connected with the incident.

The statement listed Omo-Agege as the first person invited, directing him to report at the Delta State Police Command Headquarters, Asaba, on Thursday, November 26, at 11am.

Egbo is expected to appear at 2pm on the same day.

The five other individuals invited are Gowon Egoide, former Chairman of Uduere Quarters; Onoriode Oneya, the incumbent Youth Chairman of Uduere Community; Edirin Wokode Ewhubare, an associate of Egoide from Otowvodo; Erukaye Egoide, his nephew; and Tony Gabon Mevowovo, another associate.

They are scheduled to report at the police headquarters on Friday, November 27, at noon.

“The invitations form part of ongoing investigations aimed at establishing their level of involvement in the incident,” the statement said.

The command urged all those invited to honour their appointments and cooperate with investigators, warning that supporters and other persons not specifically invited would not be allowed to accompany them.

“The Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, CP Samuel E. Erale, psc, mnips, urges all invited persons to honour the invitations as scheduled and cooperate fully with the Police while noting that the invitations are to the mentioned individuals only as the Command will not accept the presence of supporters and other persons not explicitly invited,” the statement said.

The police assured residents that the investigation would be thorough and impartial, adding that anyone found culpable would be brought to justice irrespective of political affiliation or status.

“The CP further appeals to residents to remain calm and law-abiding as the investigation progresses,” the statement added.

PUNCH Online reported that gunfire erupted on Monday, during a campaign visit by Omo-Agege to Uduere community in Ughelli North Local Government Area, leaving several people dead and others injured.

The Nigeria Police Force’s preliminary report put the death toll at six.

Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation initially reported four deaths, including two of the senator’s aides, Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro, and described the incident as an assassination attempt on the former deputy senate president.

However, Egbo accused members of Omo-Agege’s entourage of opening fire on his supporters, claiming that three people were killed.

The conflicting accounts of the incident are expected to form part of the issues to be examined during the police investigation.

Following the violence, the Delta State Government imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area.

The post Delta killings: Police invite Omo-Agege, LG chairman, five others appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

description:
By John Alechenu, Abuja



The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Kogi Central has recorded a defection from the All Progressives Congress (APC) following the resignation of a prominent APC chieftain, Hon. Umar Kareem, popularly known as Kasco.







Kareem, from Odenk Upogoro Ward in Okene Local Go
content:
By John Alechenu, Abuja

The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Kogi Central has recorded a defection from the All Progressives Congress (APC) following the resignation of a prominent APC chieftain, Hon. Umar Kareem, popularly known as Kasco.

Kareem, from Odenk Upogoro Ward in Okene Local Government Area of Kogi State, announced his resignation from the ruling party in a letter addressed to the APC ward chairman.

In the letter, made public on Tuesday, he said his resignation took immediate effect.

He explained that the decision followed extensive consultations, careful consideration and an assessment of his political journey, personal convictions and future aspirations.

Kareem said he had remained loyal and committed to the APC over the years, contributing his time, resources and efforts to the growth and development of the party.

However, he said his decision to leave was informed by his belief that political participation should be based on mutual respect, fairness, recognition, inclusiveness and a genuine sense of belonging.

“I firmly believe that political participation should be anchored on mutual respect, fairness, recognition, inclusiveness and a genuine sense of belonging,” he said.

He expressed appreciation to the APC for the relationships he built and experiences gained during his membership, while wishing the party’s leadership well.

Kareem’s defection to the PDP comes amid political realignments in Kogi Central ahead of future electoral contests.

title: US confirmed as host of 2028 Copa America
description:
The Copa America will be staged in the United States for a second successive edition in 2028 just ahead of the Los Angeles Olympics, organizers announced on Tuesday.







CONMEBOL, the South American football confederation, and CONCACAF, the governing body for North America, agreed to conduct the
content:
The Copa America will be staged in the United States for a second successive edition in 2028 just ahead of the Los Angeles Olympics, organizers announced on Tuesday.

CONMEBOL, the South American football confederation, and CONCACAF, the governing body for North America, agreed to conduct the 49th edition of the event at US venues from June 9 to July 9, 2028.

The Los Angeles Olympics are scheduled for July 14-30 but the first pre-Olympic group-stage men’s soccer matches begin on July 10, only hours after the Copa final.

The tournament will feature 16 teams, the 10 nations from South America plus six countries from North America that will qualify through the 2027 CONCACAF Gold Cup.

The event was also played in the United States in 2016, the Copa America Centenario, and 2024 ahead of the USA co-hosting the World Cup earlier this year.

“The CONMEBOL Copa America is much more than a tournament: it is part of our identity, our history, and the greatness of South American football,” CONMEBOL president Alejandro Dominguez said.

“In 2028, we will once again bring that passion to the United States, reaffirming our historic partnership with CONCACAF and our shared commitment to continuing to drive the growth of football across the continent.”

The host cities and other details will be announced later.

“We’re pleased to join forces again to bring the CONMEBOL Copa America to our region in 2028,” said CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani.

“We look forward to working alongside CONMEBOL, the host venues, and other key parties to organize a first-class tournament.”

The post US confirmed as host of 2028 Copa America appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Nigeria records 46,909 online abuse cases in one year
description:
By John Alechenu



ABUJA — Nigeria accounted for 58 per cent of verified online gender-based violence cases recorded across Africa in the last 12 months, with 46,909 incidents documented in the country, according to data from the OGBV Evidence Tracker.







The figures were unveiled at a high-lev
content:
By John Alechenu

ABUJA — Nigeria accounted for 58 per cent of verified online gender-based violence cases recorded across Africa in the last 12 months, with 46,909 incidents documented in the country, according to data from the OGBV Evidence Tracker.

The figures were unveiled at a high-level consultative meeting on digital safety and online gender-based violence in schools, organised by the Centre for Redefining Alternative Civic Engagement for Africa (RACE Centre) under its Protect Secondary School Initiative in Abuja on Tuesday.

Data from the tracker, powered by the RACE Centre, showed that 46,909 approved incidents were recorded between November 23, 2025, and November 23, 2026.

The tracker monitors online abuse across Africa, with Nigeria recording the highest concentration of incidents with verified locations.

X, formerly Twitter, accounted for 89 per cent of the documented cases, while Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube were also monitored.

Harassment and general abuse topped the categories of violations, with 23,209 incidents, representing 56 per cent of the cases.

Body shaming accounted for 7,662 incidents, representing 18 per cent, while slut shaming recorded 7,332 cases, also representing 18 per cent.

Threats of violence accounted for 2,643 incidents, or six per cent.

Other forms of abuse recorded included doxxing and privacy violations with 1,940 cases, synthetic artificial intelligence image manipulation with 1,730, stalking with 1,590 and impersonation with 790 incidents.

The tracker had yet to publish a finalised report for November 2026 as the month was still ongoing, although its live dashboard indicated that the trend remained high.

Speaking at the meeting, the Executive Director of RACE Centre, Evelyn Ugbe, said the organisation worked with feminist online watchers to document reports of abuse and refer victims to relevant authorities for intervention.

“We have our feminist online watchers. When we get a report, we document and refer them to appropriate agencies such as NAPTIP, NSCDC and or the Police for immediate action,” she said.

Ugbe urged parents to take a keen interest in their children’s online activities and create an enabling environment for teenagers to confide in them about their experiences in cyberspace.

Stakeholders at the meeting said the figures highlighted the need for stronger accountability by digital platforms, improved digital safety education and faster responses to online abuse targeting women and girls.

The meeting was attended by representatives of the Federal Ministry of Education, the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP), the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC), civil society organisations and the media.

title: CAF vows to enforce CAS ruling restoring Senegal’s AFCON title
description:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has pledged to implement the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling that restored Senegal’s 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title following its dispute with Morocco.







CAF made its position known in a statement on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, saying it
content:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has pledged to implement the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling that restored Senegal’s 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title following its dispute with Morocco.

CAF made its position known in a statement on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, saying it respected the decision of the Lausanne based tribunal and would take the necessary steps to give effect to it.

“CAF respects the CAS Award and will take all the necessary measures to implement it,” the football governing body said.

The CAS ruling overturned the CAF Appeal Board’s decision of March 17, 2026, which stripped Senegal of the title and awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory after ruling that the Teranga Lions had forfeited the final.

Instead, the tribunal reinstated the decision of CAF’s Disciplinary Board, which had upheld Senegal’s 1-0 victory over Morocco in the final played in Rabat on January 18, 2026.

The dispute followed a controversial incident late in regulation time when Senegal’s players temporarily left the pitch after the referee awarded Morocco a penalty.

The Senegalese players returned after about 14 minutes, but Morocco captain Brahim Diaz failed to convert the spot kick. Senegal later secured victory through Pape Gueye’s goal in extra time.

Morocco subsequently challenged the result, arguing that Senegal had breached Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, which address situations where a team abandons or refuses to continue a match.

However, CAS ruled that the provisions did not apply because the referee had not permanently abandoned the match. The tribunal also held that the referee acted within his authority when he allowed play to resume.

The decision was unanimous, according to CAS Secretary General Matthieu Reeb, who said the panel found no legal error in the referee’s handling of the incident.

The tribunal’s ruling does not affect separate disciplinary sanctions imposed by CAF on Senegal coach Pape Thiaw and players Iliman Ndiaye and Ismaila Sarr over incidents during the final.

Although CAF has promised to comply with the decision, it has not yet provided details of the administrative steps or a timeline for implementing the ruling.

CAS confirmed that the full grounds for its decision had been communicated to the parties on Tuesday. The award is expected to be made public in due course, unless the parties request that it remain confidential.

The ruling brings an end to the dispute over the final and restores Senegal’s second AFCON title, following its first triumph in 2021.

The post CAF vows to enforce CAS ruling restoring Senegal’s AFCON title appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: ADC to Tinubu: Resign or face impeachment over Kano judgment
description:
By Luminous Jannamike



ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has asked President Bola Tinubu to resign or face impeachment over allegations that he interfered in the Supreme Court’s 2023 Kano governorship election judgment in exchange for Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf’s defection to the All Pr
content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has asked President Bola Tinubu to resign or face impeachment over allegations that he interfered in the Supreme Court’s 2023 Kano governorship election judgment in exchange for Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf’s defection to the All Progressives Congress (APC).

The party said Yusuf’s recent BBC Hausa interview had raised serious questions about the independence of the judiciary, alleging that the President may have used his office to influence a judicial outcome for political advantage.

In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC described the allegation as a grave breach of the President’s constitutional oath and urged the National Assembly to investigate the alleged arrangement.

“No conduct can be more heinous on the part of a democratically elected President than to make the administration of justice an instrument of political bargaining. No betrayal of the presidential oath can be more profound than to pervert the cause of justice in pursuit of personal political advantage,” the party said.

The ADC said Yusuf’s account suggested that the President had secured a favourable judgment from the Supreme Court in return for the governor’s defection to the APC.

“In plain language, what Governor Yusuf was has admitted to was that the President of Nigeria, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, got the highest court in the land to award him justice in exchange for him decamping to APC. This a very grave allegation that undermines every principle regarding the rule of law, independence of the judiciary, and, indeed, the fight against corruption,” it said.

The party called on the National Assembly to initiate impeachment proceedings against Tinubu and compel all parties to the alleged arrangement to provide evidence.

It warned that the alleged interference, if established, would undermine confidence in the Supreme Court and send a damaging signal to international investors about the state of the rule of law in Nigeria.

“The Supreme Court is not an extension of the APC national secretariat, and the President of Nigeria is not the proprietor of the Nigerian judiciary. With this revelation, the President has signalled to the rest of the world, including investors, that the rule of law is dead in Nigeria and that the Supreme Court of Nigeria is actually pliant to the political whims of the President. What a shame,” the ADC said.

The opposition party challenged the National Assembly to demonstrate whether its allegiance was to the President or the Constitution, saying its response would test its willingness to hold the President accountable.

title: GBV costs Nigeria $3bn annually – Minister
description:
…Over 27,000 cases of sexual, gender-based violence documented



...ActionAid calls for stronger law enforcement to end GBV



By Gabriel Ewepu



ABUJA — The Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Hajiya Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim, has said gender-based violence (GBV) costs Nigeria about $3
content:
…Over 27,000 cases of sexual, gender-based violence documented

...ActionAid calls for stronger law enforcement to end GBV

By Gabriel Ewepu

ABUJA — The Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Hajiya Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim, has said gender-based violence (GBV) costs Nigeria about $3 billion annually, representing approximately 1.5 per cent of the country’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

Sulaiman-Ibrahim disclosed this in Abuja on Monday during a press briefing to mark the commencement of the 2026 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence.

She said the economic and social consequences of GBV included loss of productivity, physical deformities, depression, healthcare challenges, family breakdown, school dropouts and job losses.

The minister also disclosed that more than 27,000 cases of sexual and gender-based violence were documented in the most recent reporting cycle, warning that millions of cases remained unreported.

She said one in three Nigerian women aged 15 to 49 had experienced physical or sexual violence.

According to her, the trauma suffered by survivors is often compounded by societal stigma, which leaves many battling low self-esteem and other psychological consequences.

She called for concerted efforts by government and non-state actors to provide support and assistance to survivors.

“We cannot afford to merely count these numbers. We must turn remembrance into rescue,” she said.

The minister said her ministry was collaborating with state governments to establish sexual assault referral centres in every local government area to improve access to support services at the grassroots.

She added that the government was also pursuing a vision of establishing sexual assault centres in every ward under the Union of Social Impact Intervention.

Sulaiman-Ibrahim commended development partners, including the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), UNICEF, World Bank, Spring Projects, Ideas International, WaterAid, ActionAid, Policy Innovation Centre, Save the Children, Women at Risk International Foundation and Safe Jobmas, for their contributions to efforts against GBV.

Meanwhile, the Country Director of ActionAid Nigeria, Andrew Mamedu, represented by the organisation’s Women’s Rights Specialist, Niri Goyit, described gender-based violence as a grave human rights violation that continues to undermine the dignity, safety and opportunities of millions of women and girls.

Citing findings from the 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey, Mamedu said 21 per cent of women aged 15 to 49 had experienced physical or sexual violence, while 23 per cent of ever-married or partnered women had experienced physical, sexual or emotional violence from their current or most recent partners.

He stressed that ending GBV required effective implementation of existing laws, adequately funded survivor-support services, accessible justice systems and accountability for perpetrators, regardless of their status or influence.

Speaking on the 2026 16 Days of Activism theme, ‘UNiTE to End Violence Against Women and Girls: Ensure Justice, Protect Survivors, End Impunity’, he called on federal and state governments, security agencies, justice institutions, civil society organisations, development partners, the media and community leaders to translate commitments into measurable action.

He urged governments and relevant institutions to strengthen enforcement of the Violence Against Persons (Prohibition) Act and other protective legal frameworks, close implementation gaps and invest in safe, accessible and survivor-centred services.

Mamedu also called for measures to ensure that every woman and girl could access justice, irrespective of her location or socioeconomic circumstances.

Also speaking, the UNFPA Resident Representative in Nigeria, Ms. Muriel Mafico, reaffirmed the agency’s commitment to ending sexual and gender-based violence, with the message: “Name it. Believe it. End it.”

She said violence that remained unnamed often went unaddressed, describing the identification of all forms of GBV as a critical first step towards justice and prevention.

“Violence against women and girls must never be normalised, excused or concealed. Whether it occurs in our homes, communities, institutions or digital spaces, every survivor deserves to be heard, protected, and supported to access justice,” Mafico said.

The post GBV costs Nigeria $3bn annually – Minister appeared first on Vanguard News.

By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri



The Borno State Police Command has warned motorists and residents of possible temporary closures of major roads in Maiduguri ahead of President Bola Tinubu’s visit to the state on Wednesday, November 25, 2026.







The visit is expected to coincide with the launch of
content:
By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri

The Borno State Police Command has warned motorists and residents of possible temporary closures of major roads in Maiduguri ahead of President Bola Tinubu’s visit to the state on Wednesday, November 25, 2026.

The visit is expected to coincide with the launch of the President’s 2027 re-election campaign.

The Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Kenneth Daso, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying the temporary restrictions would be part of security arrangements for the presidential visit and other Very Important Personalities expected in the state.

According to him, some major roads and adjoining routes within the metropolis may be temporarily closed to vehicular movement to facilitate security operations and ensure the smooth conduct of the visit.

“Motorists, commuters and other road users are advised to plan their journeys accordingly,” Daso said.

He added that alternative routes would be provided and communicated to the public to ease movement during the period.

The police spokesman also urged residents to comply with traffic regulations and directives from security personnel, while soliciting the understanding and cooperation of the public over any inconvenience caused by the restrictions.

Our correspondent reports that heightened security measures have often accompanied presidential visits to Borno State since the outbreak of the Boko Haram insurgency in 2009.

Such measures, including traffic restrictions and road closures, have sometimes attracted complaints from residents over the disruption of movement and daily economic activities.

The suspect, a resident of Changu Village, Gwazawa, under Kanya District, w
content:
By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi

The Kebbi State Police Command has arrested a 30-year-old man, Tapro Tareza, for allegedly exhuming a corpse at Machika Cemetery in the Danko/Wasagu Local Government Area of the state.

The suspect, a resident of Changu Village, Gwazawa, under Kanya District, was arrested following reports of repeated grave desecration at the cemetery.

The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying the arrest followed a surveillance operation mounted by the police in collaboration with concerned youths in the community.

According to him, on November 10, 2026, at about 7:15 p.m., shortly after the burial of a deceased person, the suspect was allegedly caught digging into the newly covered grave.

Usman said vigilant youths apprehended him while he was allegedly committing the act and immediately alerted the police.

He added that preliminary investigations indicated that the suspect allegedly removed items from the bodies of deceased persons.

The police spokesman further said the suspect reportedly admitted involvement in previous acts of grave desecration at the same cemetery, including an earlier incident in which he allegedly removed and took away the burial shroud of a deceased person.

Usman said investigations were ongoing to establish the full circumstances surrounding the incidents and ensure that the suspect faced appropriate legal action.

The command commended members of the community for their vigilance and cooperation, while cautioning residents against taking the law into their own hands.

It urged members of the public to promptly report suspicious activities to the police.

title: FG vows to crack down on fake seeds, protect food security
description:
The Federal Government has vowed to intensify enforcement against counterfeit, adulterated and substandard seeds, warning that their circulation threatens agricultural productivity, farmers’ livelihoods and efforts to achieve food security in Nigeria.
The government also unveiled the National Seed S
content:
The Federal Government has vowed to intensify enforcement against counterfeit, adulterated and substandard seeds, warning that their circulation threatens agricultural productivity, farmers’ livelihoods and efforts to achieve food security in Nigeria.

The government also unveiled the National Seed Sector Roadmap for 2026–2031 to attract investments, strengthen regulatory oversight and improve farmers’ access to quality planting materials.

The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Abubakar Kyari, disclosed this at the ninth SeedConnect Africa Conference and Exhibition in Abuja on Tuesday.

According to a statement issued by the ministry’s Head of Information, Ezeaja Ikemefuna, the minister, represented by the Permanent Secretary, Marcus Ogunbiyi, called for stronger regulatory enforcement alongside efforts to expand regional seed trade.

The statement read, “Kyari said that harmonised regulatory standards, improved certification systems, and effective cross-border cooperation can facilitate the movement of quality seeds across national boundaries, expand markets for domestic enterprises, and improve farmers’ access to suitable varieties.

“He stressed, however, that such integration cannot succeed while counterfeit, adulterated, and poor-quality seeds continue to threaten agricultural productivity, adding that the Federal Government will keep strengthening the National Agricultural Seeds Council to handle seed certification, quality assurance, market surveillance, and standards enforcement.”

Kyari advocated the adoption of digital traceability, electronic verification and reliable seed identification systems to enable farmers to verify the authenticity of planting materials and help regulators monitor compliance.

He explained that investments in fertiliser, irrigation, mechanisation and agricultural extension services would not achieve their full potential without access to quality seeds.

“Quality seed is the foundation of agricultural productivity and the principal means through which improved genetics and innovations move from laboratories to farmers’ fields,” the statement added.

The minister said the government would encourage the development, multiplication and commercialisation of improved seed varieties capable of withstanding drought, heat, flooding, pests and diseases.

He also advocated the production of nutrient-rich crops to improve nutrition, urging research institutions to strengthen collaboration with seed companies, agricultural processors and farmers.

On financing, Kyari identified limited access to affordable credit as a major constraint facing Africa’s seed industry, particularly small and medium enterprises.

He urged commercial banks, development finance institutions, insurance companies and private investors to explore blended financing, credit guarantees, agricultural insurance and risk-sharing arrangements.

“Government, he affirmed, recognises that public resources alone cannot finance the transformation required. Its responsibility is to create an enabling environment, strengthen institutions, reduce investment risks and mobilise private capital,” the statement noted.

Kyari further called for harmonised regulatory standards, improved certification systems and cross-border cooperation to expand market opportunities for Nigerian seed producers across Africa.

He reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to implementing the outcomes of the African Union’s inaugural continental Seed Summit, held in Eswatini between October 5 and 7, 2026, subject to formal endorsement by African leaders and alignment with national priorities.

The minister also cited the Plant Variety Protection Act, 2021, and Nigeria’s accession to the International Union for the Protection of New Varieties of Plants in March 2025 as measures to protect breeders’ rights and encourage investment in crop improvement.

He stressed the need to strengthen seed distribution networks, expand access to agro-dealer outlets and improve the availability of planting materials for crops such as cassava, yam and cocoa.

Kyari directed the council to collaborate with relevant institutions and private sector stakeholders to develop an implementation framework for the conference’s recommendations, with clearly defined responsibilities, timelines and measurable targets.

Earlier, the Director-General of the National Agricultural Seeds Council, Fatuhu Muhammed, identified inadequate financing, infrastructure gaps, limited adoption of improved varieties and weak linkages between research and commercial seed production as persistent challenges facing the industry.

Muhammed described the newly unveiled five-year roadmap as a framework for coordinating investments and interventions towards building a productive, resilient and commercially viable seed industry.

He encouraged seed companies to leverage the conference to establish partnerships, attract investments and strengthen business relationships.

The PUNCH reported in September 2025 that the NASC pledged tougher measures to eliminate fake seeds from circulation and ensure Nigeria’s agricultural produce meets global export standards.

In 2019, the council introduced SeedCodex, an electronic authentication technology that allows farmers to verify the authenticity of seeds through unique identification codes sent via text messages.

The National Agricultural Seeds Council Act, 2019, also criminalises unlicensed commercial seed production and marketing, misleading labelling and fraudulent practices in the sale of seeds.

title: 2027: NUC considers four-week break to mobilise university dons for polls
description:
From Fred Ezeh, Abuja
The National Universities Commission (NUC) has said it is considering a three-to-four-week break in university academic activities to enable lecturers and other university personnel to participate in the 2027 general elections.
The Commission also pledged to mobilise Vice-Chanc
content:
From Fred Ezeh, Abuja

The National Universities Commission (NUC) has said it is considering a three-to-four-week break in university academic activities to enable lecturers and other university personnel to participate in the 2027 general elections.

The Commission also pledged to mobilise Vice-Chancellors across the country to nominate credible and non-partisan academics to serve as Collation and Returning Officers during the elections.

The Executive Secretary of the NUC, Prof. Abdullahi Yusufu Ribadu, stated this in Abuja when the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, led a delegation of National Commissioners and senior officials on a courtesy visit to the Commission.

Ribadu said the NUC would engage Vice-Chancellors on the nomination of suitable academics, adding that an online meeting would be convened to facilitate the process.

He also promised to issue a circular to universities upon receiving a formal request from INEC.

On the proposed academic break, Ribadu said the Commission would consult Vice-Chancellors to determine how best to adjust academic calendars without disrupting the electoral timetable or adversely affecting students’ academic activities.

“We will discuss with the Vice-Chancellors and have their calendars tweaked in such a way that it will not affect the elections, nor will it affect the studies of the students,” he said.

Emphasising the importance of credible electoral personnel, the NUC boss insisted that academics and other ad hoc officials deployed for election duties must demonstrate neutrality and integrity. “Since we want to have credible elections, we also have to have credible personnel,” he stated.

Ribadu said that, beyond providing personnel, the NUC might propose a broader collaboration between the two institutions that might include internship opportunities for university students at INEC offices, the possible introduction of programmes in electoral studies and joint research in artificial intelligence, robotics and data analytics.

He also suggested that university students could support voter education through campus clubs and other platforms, particularly in tackling misinformation and disinformation ahead of the elections.

Ribadu congratulated Amupitan on his appointment, describing him as a lawyer and academic of international repute. He expressed confidence that INEC would deliver transparent, free and fair elections capable of serving as a model for other African countries.

Earlier, the INEC Chairman, Amupitan, described the visit as a strategic engagement aimed at strengthening the partnership between the two institutions ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He acknowledged the significant contributions of Nigerian universities to the electoral process over the years, particularly the deployment of Vice-Chancellors and other academics as Collation and Returning Officers.

Amupitan disclosed that INEC was introducing technological, operational and security reforms to improve election management and guarantee the safety of academics serving as electoral officials.

He said polling unit results recorded on Form EC8A would undergo automated arithmetic consistency and over-voting checks before transmission to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV).

The INEC chairman also announced the procurement of 57,000 additional Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) machines, a development expected to reduce the voter-to-device ratio to 850 per machine.

As part of its preparations, he said the commission would conduct a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise on Saturday, November 28, 2026, across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

On security, Amupitan disclosed that the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) had been decentralised to Local Government Areas and Registration Areas, with dedicated security cordons and escort arrangements around collation centres.

He further cited provisions of the Electoral Act 2026 criminalising violence, abusive rhetoric and threats against electoral personnel, noting that INEC had powers to prosecute offenders. “No Returning Officer or Collation Officer will be left to stand alone against lawlessness,” he assured.

Amupitan also requested the NUC’s support in four key areas, namely the timely nomination of qualified and non-partisan academics, adjustment of university calendars, collaboration on campus voter education and countering disinformation, as well as improved welfare and recognition for academics deployed for election duties.

The Presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027, while the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections will hold on February 6, 2027.

title: 2027: SDP demands equal police protection for all parties
description:
The Social Democratic Party has called on the Nigeria Police Force to provide equal security protection for all political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning against the use of security agencies to advance partisan interests.
The National Chairman of the SDP, Prof. Sadiq Gombe, made
content:
The Social Democratic Party has called on the Nigeria Police Force to provide equal security protection for all political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning against the use of security agencies to advance partisan interests.

The National Chairman of the SDP, Prof. Sadiq Gombe, made the call on Tuesday at a high-level security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, Olayunji Disu, to address political violence and security challenges during political activities.

Gombe urged the police and other security agencies to remain professional, impartial and fair, insisting that opposition parties must be able to organise rallies, hold meetings and campaign without intimidation or fear of attacks.

He said, “We call on the police and other security agencies to be professional, impartial, firm, and fair. Every party must be able to say, with confidence, that its candidates, supporters, offices and rallies will receive equal protection under the law. Not some parties. Not the powerful. Every party. Every electorate.”

The SDP chairman warned that any perception of police bias could undermine public confidence in the electoral process and weaken the country’s democracy.

“Security must never be perceived as a tool for political advantage. The moment citizens believe the uniform belongs to a political camp, trust is lost. And once trust is lost, it is very difficult to rebuild,” he said.

His remarks came hours after the Nigeria Democratic Congress announced its decision to boycott the meeting, citing alleged police bias and failure to protect its members from attacks by suspected political thugs.

The opposition party alleged that security agencies failed to intervene during the killing of four of its members in Delta State, while demanding investigations and prosecution of those responsible.

Against this backdrop, Gombe said security agencies must respond promptly to reported threats, investigate incidents of political violence thoroughly and ensure that perpetrators are brought to justice irrespective of their political affiliations.

“Where threats are reported, response must be prompt and swift. Where violence occurs, investigation must be thorough. And where offenders are identified, the law must take its course, whoever they are and whatever party they belong to,” he said.

The SDP chairman maintained that political opponents should be regarded as fellow citizens rather than enemies, urging parties to compete through ideas, policies and peaceful mobilisation.

He further disclosed that the SDP was committed to disciplining members found engaging in or inciting political violence, challenging other parties to adopt similar measures.

“Condemnation is easy when the offender belongs to someone else. The real test of leadership is what we do when the offender is one of our own. The SDP is committed to disciplining any member who engages in violence or incites it, and we challenge every other party here to do the same,” Gombe said.

He urged the Independent National Electoral Commission and political parties to work closely with security agencies to prevent disagreements over campaign venues, schedules, routes and permissions from escalating into violence.

To strengthen security ahead of the elections, Gombe proposed establishing a permanent communication channel between political parties and security agencies, with designated liaison officers to ensure prompt responses to threats.

He also called for an early-warning system to identify emerging tensions, adequate and impartial security for campaign activities, responsible political communication and the documentation, investigation and prosecution of reported cases of electoral violence.

The SDP chairman further advocated periodic meetings among stakeholders to review security arrangements and assess compliance with agreed commitments.

He expressed concern that previous engagements on electoral security had often produced resolutions without corresponding action.

“Nigerians are tired of words that do not become action. So this meeting must be different. It must produce measurable commitments,” he said.

The post 2027: SDP demands equal police protection for all parties appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
