title: Reps seek safer boats, life jackets after Bayelsa boat mishap
description:
By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja



The House of Representatives has called for the provision of safer boats, life jackets and other water safety equipment to riverine communities in Bayelsa State following a deadly boat mishap.







The House also urged relevant agencies to intensify rescue operations
content:
By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja

The House of Representatives has called for the provision of safer boats, life jackets and other water safety equipment to riverine communities in Bayelsa State following a deadly boat mishap.

The House also urged relevant agencies to intensify rescue operations, provide relief materials to affected communities and investigate the circumstances surrounding the tragedy.

The resolutions followed a motion of urgent public importance moved by Rep. Rodney Ebikebina Ambaiowei, representing Southern Ijaw Federal Constituency, during plenary on Tuesday.

Ambaiowei told the House that more than 150 people, mostly indigenes of Southern Ijaw, were involved in the accident on November 20, 2026, while travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a condolence visit.

He said the boat capsized at the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan, throwing its occupants into the water.

According to him, rescue efforts began immediately, with the Bayelsa State Government, security personnel and other relevant agencies responding to the incident.

He disclosed that, as of November 22, several people had been rescued alive with varying degrees of injuries and discomfort, while others had died.

The rescued victims, he said, were taken to medical facilities in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area and government hospitals in Yenagoa for treatment, while search and rescue operations continued for missing persons and possible survivors.

The lawmaker expressed concern that several victims were still missing, despite the efforts of the state government, and called for a broader search operation.

He said the tragedy had plunged families and residents of Southern Ijaw, particularly Ukubie and neighbouring communities, into mourning.

Ambaiowei attributed the vulnerability of riverine communities partly to the poor condition of boats used for transportation, noting that many were old, overworked and overloaded because of the scarcity of vessels.

He also lamented the absence of life jackets, floaters and other water safety equipment, as well as inadequate enforcement of their use, despite waterways being the major means of transportation in the largely riverine constituency.

The lawmaker said the communities had limited access to motorable roads, despite ongoing road construction efforts by the Bayelsa State Government, leaving residents heavily dependent on waterways.

He warned that failure by the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) and other relevant bodies to intensify rescue operations and provide relief materials could worsen the impact of the tragedy.

Ambaiowei added that the affected communities depended largely on fishing for food and income, stressing that the accident had disrupted their livelihoods and economic activities.

He commended President Bola Tinubu for sending Vice-President Kashim Shettima to the affected area to sympathise with families of the deceased.

The lawmaker also acknowledged the Federal Government’s donation of ₦250 million to victims of the tragedy.

Contributions to the motion centred on the need for safer water transportation, stricter enforcement of safety standards and accountability by government agencies and community-level authorities.

House Minority Leader, Rep. Fred Agbedi, said the accident had exposed the hardship faced by riverine communities, arguing that government transportation interventions had largely overlooked people who depended on waterways.

Agbedi advocated the provision of modern boats at subsidised rates, similar to the Federal Government’s introduction of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) buses to reduce the cost of road transportation.

“Mr Speaker, this happening brings to attention what the people of the riverine communities are suffering. And I think it’s a moment that we should use to also assuage the challenges.

“I’m aware that the federal government is providing CNG buses, you know, that are more economical. But each time we talk about mass transit and all that, there is no river craft provision.

“So in this century, you see people using a dugout boat, you know, with weak roofs, that will collapse from the roof on the people who are sitting at the bottom. If government has provided, as we do mass transit and do CNG buses and all that, if vessels are provided for transportation at subsidised rates, I’m sure that this incident will have been averted,” he said.

Agbedi described the motion as an opportunity to address the longstanding neglect of riverine communities, insisting that federal transportation policies should also cater for people with little or no access to roads.

He urged the Federal Government to make budgetary provisions for modern and affordable boats, alongside its planned interventions in road transportation.

Rep. Shina Oyedeji urged the government to stop paying lip service to safety standards, saying the tragedy should serve as a wake-up call for authorities to regulate transportation operations properly.

He questioned the training and certification of boat operators and the standards governing the use of boats and other transport facilities.

Oyedeji also called for a review of safety procedures and certification requirements, insisting that operators must be properly trained and qualified.

“We cannot continue to assume that they do it in America, they do it in the UK, they do it in Russia or Morocco, we want to do it here without having the right process. We must write a manner that can say this is how it must be done,” he said.

He urged the relevant committee of the House to examine the country’s safety standards and ensure that necessary regulations were enforced.

The Deputy Majority Whip, Rep. Isiaka Ibrahim, said responsibility for safety on inland waterways rested with both the Federal and state governments, noting that creeks and offshore waters were on the concurrent legislative list.

He urged the House to investigate the accident and examine the safety practices of operators, particularly in comparison with those of multinational companies operating offshore.

Ibrahim argued that adopting even a fraction of the safety measures observed by multinational companies could help prevent accidents in the creeks.

He also warned against disregarding life jackets on the assumption that swimming ability could guarantee survival in an accident.

“I know how to swim. I have been swimming for 40 years. No, you don’t even know the condition of the boat or the condition of the water or the depth or what may have happened to the boat.

“Life vests, life jackets, we ignore it. And then we are not talking about mishap. Definitely, it’s a hazard,” he said.

He urged the House to use the incident as a learning opportunity and address the circumstances that led to the tragedy.

House Leader, Rep. Julius Ihonvbere, however, stressed the need to hold grassroots authorities and community organisations accountable for safety failures.

He said footage from the accident showed people boarding boats without life jackets, describing the practice as unacceptable and calling for tougher penalties against those who violated safety regulations.

Ihonvbere argued that community associations, maritime associations, local government councils, state governments and relevant agencies all had responsibilities to ensure safety on waterways.

He insisted that familiarity with waterways or swimming experience should not be used as an excuse for ignoring safety requirements.

“The fact that I was born in the river side, I was thrown into the river, I was a baby, I have been swimming for 20, 35 years, is not an excuse to board a boat without the appropriate life vest,” he said.

He also questioned the inspection of watercraft and called for stronger enforcement of safety regulations at jetties and other boarding points.

Ihonvbere said recurring accidents would continue unless authorities at all levels took responsibility and imposed appropriate penalties for safety violations.

The House unanimously adopted the motion and mandated its Committee on Emergency and Disaster Management to work with NEMA and the Bayelsa State Government to investigate the immediate and remote causes of the accident and recommend measures to prevent future occurrences.

It also called on NEMA, the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), the National Inland Waterways Authority and the South-South Development Agency to provide additional relief materials to affected communities to cushion the impact of the tragedy and the loss of livelihoods.

The House further urged the agencies to urgently supply safer boats, life jackets, floaters and other water transport safety equipment to riverine communities, while ensuring their mandatory use.

The post Reps seek safer boats, life jackets after Bayelsa boat mishap appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Reps move to refocus social investment programme
description:
From Ndubuisi Orji, Abuja
The House of Representatives has passed through second reading a bill seeking to amend the National Social Investment Programme Agency (Establishment) Act, 2023, to reposition and refocus the agency for better performance, improved efficiency and more effective delivery of
content:
From Ndubuisi Orji, Abuja

The House of Representatives has passed through second reading a bill seeking to amend the National Social Investment Programme Agency (Establishment) Act, 2023, to reposition and refocus the agency for better performance, improved efficiency and more effective delivery of social investment programmes across the country.

The proposed legislation, which is sponsored by the Deputy Speaker, Benjamin Kalu, and six others, seeks to strengthen the institutional framework for the coordination, implementation and monitoring of social protection interventions in the country.

Essentially, the proposed legislation seeks the introduction of the Grant for Vulnerable Groups Programme and the National Social Safety-Net Coordinating Office as additional components of the Agency, as well as the establishment of the National Social Safety-Net Coordinating Office as the central coordinating and data-management office for national social safety-net programmes.

Kalu, in his lead debate, stated that the strength of a social investment programme should not be measured by the size of its budget or the number of programmes it carries, but by whether the vulnerable citizens it was designed to reach can actually feel its impact.

He explained that the proposed amendments recognise that effective social investment requires more than individual programmes operating independently, noting that it demands an integrated system in which beneficiary data is properly managed, programmes are coordinated, and state and local governments are effectively engaged.

According to him, “The strength of a social investment programme is ultimately measured not by the size of its budget, nor by the number of programmes it carries, but by whether the vulnerable citizen it was designed to reach can actually feel its impact. Social investment is, at its core, a promise of the Nigerian State to stand between vulnerability and destitution, and to ensure that temporary hardship does not become permanent exclusion.

“The National Social Investment Programme Agency was established to give institutional structure to that promise. However, as the scale and complexity of our social protection landscape continue to evolve, there is a compelling need to strengthen the architecture through which these programmes are coordinated, implemented and monitored.

“This Bill therefore seeks to reposition and refocus the Agency for better performance and improved efficiency, while establishing clearer institutional responsibilities and stronger coordination mechanisms.”

title: Benue APC crisis: Why Alia/Akume reconciliation ‘ll not work – Agada
description:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi



Factional Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, APC, in Benue State, Mr Austin Agada, has declared that there is currently no genuine reconciliation between the camps of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, Senator George Akume, and Governor Hyacinth
content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi

Factional Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, APC, in Benue State, Mr Austin Agada, has declared that there is currently no genuine reconciliation between the camps of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, Senator George Akume, and Governor Hyacinth Alia, insisting that any peace deal must go beyond preparations for the 2027 general elections.

Agada, an ally of Senator Akume, made the position known in a social media exchange with another APC stalwart and Akume loyalist, Mr Abua Yaji, where he explained why previous reconciliation efforts within the ruling party in the state had failed.

He maintained that reconciliation could only be meaningful if it addressed the broader concerns of the Benue people, stressing that it must not be reduced to an arrangement designed to secure political advantage ahead of the next elections.

According to him, “the truth remains that reconciliation cannot be done on the basis of electioneering alone. If there must be reconciliation in the first place, it has to be genuine, and it will not even be with us, it will be with the Benue people.”

Agada recalled the massive support the APC enjoyed from the electorate during the 2023 general elections, arguing that any reconciliation process must take into consideration the expectations and interests of the people who voted for the party.

“Reconciliation must be seen to be total in all spheres, considering the level the Benue people came out in the last election in 2023 to vote for our party under my leadership. So, when they are ready for reconciliation, we will know. But for now, there is no reconciliation; they are not ready for reconciliation,” he declared.

He, however, clarified that his position did not amount to a rejection of dialogue among party leaders, noting that there was nothing wrong with political stakeholders sitting together to resolve their differences.

“The Benue people have their resolve already, it does not matter what anybody thinks about it. But the truth about it is that there is nothing wrong for people to sit down and talk. We are not in a theatre of war. Even in a war situation, people sit down and talk,” he said.

Explaining further, Agada described the ongoing engagements among the party leaders as brotherly discussions, insisting that any eventual agreement must be transparent and acceptable to the people of the state.

“So, what is going on is that they are talking as brothers, and if it reaches the time for a genuine reconciliation, the entire Benue people will know. People will sit down and people will speak out,” he stated.

He stressed that the disagreement within the APC should not be viewed as a personal contest involving Akume or any other political leader, but as an issue concerning the entire party structure and the people of Benue state.

“So, it is not about Austin Agada or the SGF, George Akume. It is about the Benue people and the entire leadership of our party from the ward level to the state. We have not foreclosed reconciliation, but it cannot be tailored towards an election,” he added.

Agada also questioned the fulfilment of campaign promises made to the people during the 2023 elections, particularly commitments concerning the return of displaced communities in Sankera and the MINDA bloc, as well as alleged governance imbalance and persistent insecurity in Benue South.

He said, “Aside from the factionalisation of the party, which was purposefully done, what about the promises we made to the Benue people during the electioneering that I swore round the 23 Local Government Areas?” he queried.

Recalling the campaign commitments, he asked, “Like I always say, we promised to bring back home the people of Sankera. Have we done that till today? They contributed money for us, including people in the bush. What about the people of MINDA bloc that have lost their ancestral homes, and we promised them that in our first 100 days in office we will take them back home. What have we done about them? What about the people of Benue South, also known as Zone C (Idoma-speaking area), the imbalance in the system of governance, what about the attacjs and killings in Agatu, Otukpo, Apa, Ogbadibo and even Okpokwu Local Government Areas? These are some of the issues.”

title: CBN maintains interest rate at 23% as MPC unanimously rejects rate cut
description:
The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has retained the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 23 per cent.
CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, announced the decision on Tuesday during a press briefing following the 308th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC).
Cardoso said all members of the committee unanimo
content:
The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has retained the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 23 per cent.

CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, announced the decision on Tuesday during a press briefing following the 308th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC).

Cardoso said all members of the committee unanimously agreed to maintain the country’s benchmark interest rate at 23 per cent.

The committee also retained the asymmetric corridor around the MPR at +50/-300 basis points.

The committee maintained the Cash Reserve Ratio, CRR, for commercial banks at 45 per cent, retained the rate for merchant banks at 16 per cent, and kept the CRR on non-Treasury Single Account, TSA, public-sector deposits at 75 per cent for liquidity management purposes.

“The Monetary Policy Committee, MPC, at its 308th meeting, voted on policy parameters as follows:

Monetary Policy Rate (MPR): Retained at 23%.

“Standing Facilities Corridor: Retained at +50/-300 basis points around the MPR.

“Cash Reserve Requirement, CRR: Retained at 45% for Deposit Money Banks, 16% for Merchant Banks, and 75% for non-TSA public sector deposits”, CBN stated on X.

This comes amid the continued depreciation of the naira and a decline in the country’s foreign reserves, which stood at N1,394.01 per dollar and $54.58 billion, respectively, as of November 20, 2026.

The MPC’s latest decision comes despite a decline in Nigeria’s headline inflation rate to 14.06 per cent in October 2026.

Recall that at its 307th meeting, the MPC reduced the interest rate to 23 per cent from 26.5 per cent.

The post CBN maintains interest rate at 23% as MPC unanimously rejects rate cut appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Tinubu needs no presidential debate, policies are clear — Showunmi

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta



ABEOKUTA — Convener of the Alternative Movement and chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Otunba Segun Showunmi, has dismissed calls for President Bola Tinubu to p
content:
…PDP chieftain urges Ogun residents to mobilise votes, cautions against political violence

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

ABEOKUTA — Convener of the Alternative Movement and chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Otunba Segun Showunmi, has dismissed calls for President Bola Tinubu to participate in a presidential debate ahead of the 2027 general elections, arguing that the President has sufficiently communicated his policies, programmes and vision to Nigerians.

Showunmi, who is also a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, maintained that a presidential debate was unnecessary, insisting that Tinubu’s policy direction and philosophy of governance were already clear to the electorate.

He argued that the primary purpose of a presidential debate was to enable voters to understand candidates’ policies, programmes and development agendas, a responsibility he said Tinubu had already fulfilled through his engagements with Nigerians.

“When it comes to Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, his policy direction is very clear. We are now on the journey to prosperity. His guiding principles of governance are equally clear: an inclusive, united and indivisible Nigeria that works for everyone,” he said.

Describing Tinubu’s leadership style as accessible, relatable, pragmatic and intelligent, Showunmi said the President was under no obligation to participate in a debate merely to satisfy public expectations.

“Even if we were to bring the candidates together for a debate, who exactly would he be debating? Is it Peter Obi, who, when asked a question, will run to Malaysia, or the other man, whose name I would rather not mention?” he asked.

He added: “The debate has already conducted itself.”

Showunmi, however, acknowledged that the final decision on whether to participate in a presidential debate rested with Tinubu, saying the President could either engage his opponents or rely on his previous interactions with the electorate.

“If the President decides to participate in a debate, that is entirely up to him. If he decides that he has already engaged with the people at a level where they understand his message, that is also his prerogative,” he said.

He likened calls for Tinubu to debate opposition candidates to asking a headmaster to participate in a speaking contest with primary school pupils.

Turning to the party’s electoral preparations in Ogun State, Showunmi urged residents to prioritise grassroots mobilisation and voter participation rather than become distracted by political arguments.

He said the immediate challenge facing the campaign team was to ensure that Tinubu secured a substantial share of the votes in Ogun State.

“His victory is no longer in question; we are winning. What we are working towards now is ensuring that our numbers are also respectable,” he declared.

Showunmi questioned why Ogun State, with an estimated 3.5 million votes, should fail to record an impressive electoral performance compared with other states.

“When you look at the numbers from other states, some people will record one million votes, while others will record two million. Why should we behave like illiterates in Ogun State when we have 3.5 million votes?” he queried.

He called on residents to intensify mobilisation, encourage eligible voters to participate and ensure peaceful conduct on election day.

Showunmi also expressed optimism that the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) would conduct a credible election capable of strengthening Nigeria’s democratic image before the international community.

“The earlier we come out and motivate ourselves to participate on that one day, the better. That is all I am asking of them. By the grace of God Almighty, we will secure the maximum number of available votes in Ogun State,” he said.

On the political dynamics in Ogun State, Showunmi reaffirmed his commitment to following the political direction of Governor Dapo Abiodun while maintaining his support for Tinubu’s presidential ambition.

He said his loyalty to the President was unquestionable, citing his membership of two presidential campaign councils.

“What we know is that I have told my people that wherever Governor Dapo Abiodun goes, I will follow. I have also specifically told them that, when it comes to the presidential campaign, they do not even need to ask where I stand, considering that I am a member of two critical campaign councils of the President,” he said.

Showunmi explained that his immediate responsibility was to mobilise support for Tinubu while awaiting further political instructions from the Ogun State governor.

“Therefore, I have come here to mobilise them on behalf of the President while waiting for Governor Dapo Abiodun to tell me who else he wants me to support,” he stated.

Speaking on the Rainbow Coalition, a political platform reportedly comprising individuals from different political parties supporting Tinubu, Showunmi said the initiative had created an opportunity for broader political cooperation.

He noted, however, that the coalition’s political identity in Ogun State appeared closely associated with Governor Abiodun.

“As far as we are concerned, those who have created what they call the Rainbow Coalition have provided a platform for people from other political parties to come together and support the President,” he said.

“However, as far as Ogun State is concerned, I have a feeling that the Rainbow is the Rainbow of Dapo Abiodun.”

Showunmi also called for an end to political violence and the use of young people to perpetrate criminal activities, urging parents, families and community leaders to take responsibility for the conduct of their members.

He argued that those who instigated ordinary citizens to engage in violence should be held accountable, noting that perpetrators were often members of the same communities rather than outsiders.

“Angels do not kill people, and neither do the children of the Pope come here carrying sticks. More often than not, they are our own children and our own people, instigated by characters I describe as scallywags,” he said.

He added that anyone who instigated ordinary people to engage in criminal activities deserved to be condemned.

Showunmi urged politicians and their supporters not to allow electoral contests and political disagreements to destroy relationships or destabilise communities, reminding them that elections were temporary and political opponents would continue to coexist after the polls.

“At the end of the day, elections come once every four years. After we have conducted this election and Bola Ahmed Tinubu has won overwhelmingly, another election will still come,” he added.

He also cautioned APC supporters against complacency, saying his political engagements outside Ogun State had convinced him that Tinubu enjoyed substantial support in other parts of the country.

“I am even afraid that the President may secure more votes in the North than here, despite the reason I have been appealing to my people,” he said.

“I have been around, and the support for him out there is massive. I do not want a situation where the support at home, or the numbers we record here, become disappointingly low because of our attitude.”

He renewed his appeal to eligible voters across Ogun State to intensify grassroots mobilisation, shun violence and participate actively in the electoral process.

title: 2027: SDP urges police, security agencies to be impartial
description:
Party calls for accountability, says culture of impunity must be confronted



By Henry Umoru



ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Social Democratic Party (SDP) has urged the police and other security agencies to remain professional, impartial, firm and fair in handling electoral acti
content:
Party calls for accountability, says culture of impunity must be confronted

By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Social Democratic Party (SDP) has urged the police and other security agencies to remain professional, impartial, firm and fair in handling electoral activities, warning against the use of security institutions to advance partisan interests.

The party also called for an end to the culture of impunity, insisting that perpetrators of political violence must be held accountable irrespective of their political affiliations or status.

National Chairman of the SDP, Prof. Sadiq Gombe, made the call on Tuesday at a security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Disu, in Abuja.

Gombe said every political party must be assured that its candidates, supporters, offices and campaign rallies would receive equal protection under the law.

“Not some parties. Not the powerful. Every party. Every electorate,” he said.

He warned that security must never be perceived as a tool for political advantage, stressing that public confidence would be eroded if citizens believed security agencies were aligned with particular political interests.

According to him, threats reported to security agencies must attract prompt responses, incidents of violence must be thoroughly investigated, while identified offenders must face the law irrespective of their political affiliations.

The SDP chairman said the culture of impunity must also be confronted, warning that failure to punish perpetrators of political violence could encourage others to engage in similar acts.

“When perpetrators of political violence go unpunished, we send a dangerous message to the next person: that violence is acceptable, that it is cheap, and that it pays. Accountability is not vengeance. It is the foundation of deterrence,” he said.

Gombe reaffirmed the party’s commitment to peaceful political participation, respect for the rule of law and the protection of the democratic rights of every Nigerian.

He urged SDP members, candidates, supporters and campaign organisations to conduct themselves responsibly, saying the party would compete through ideas, persuasion, peaceful mobilisation and constructive dialogue.

“Let me be clear: peace must be built on fairness and justice.

“Every Nigerian must be free to support the party of their choice without intimidation. Every candidate must be able to campaign without fear. Every party must be able to organise within the law. And every citizen, the farmer in the village, the trader in the market, the young graduate searching for opportunity, must have confidence that their vote and their voice truly matter,” he said.

The SDP chairman condemned political thuggery, hate speech, mobilisation of armed groups, destruction of campaign materials, attacks on rallies and party offices, and attempts to disrupt lawful political activities.

He said political violence was often a consequence of the actions and decisions of political leaders, particularly their statements at rallies and their failure to caution supporters against misconduct.

“Political opponents are not enemies. They are fellow citizens. We may disagree on policy, on ideology, and on leadership, but we share one country and one destiny. We are Nigerians first, before we are politicians,” he said.

Gombe challenged political party leaders to take responsibility for the conduct of their members and supporters, insisting that condemnation of violence must extend to offenders within their own political organisations.

He said the SDP was committed to disciplining any member found engaging in or inciting violence and urged other political parties to adopt similar measures.

“Peace cannot merely be preached. It must be practised,” he added.

Addressing the police and other security agencies, Gombe said their conduct in the months leading to the elections would significantly influence public confidence in the electoral process.

He also urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and political parties to ensure compliance with the Electoral Act and other regulations governing political activities.

The SDP chairman said many confrontations during political campaigns could be avoided through timely communication, coordination and clarity over rally venues, schedules, routes and required permissions.

He called for improved cooperation among security agencies, INEC and political parties to ensure that disagreements over campaign arrangements were resolved before escalating into violence.

Gombe said the 2027 general elections would test not only the political preparedness of stakeholders but also their collective commitment to democracy.

He urged political actors to pursue their ambitions without endangering the lives, property and dignity of fellow Nigerians.

“Our duty is greater than our personal ambitions. It is greater than the interests of any party. It is a duty to this nation and to the generations who will inherit whatever we leave behind,” he said.

He expressed the SDP’s readiness to work with the police, INEC, other political parties and stakeholders to ensure that the 2027 electoral process was peaceful, credible, inclusive and reflective of the will of Nigerians.

The meeting was convened by the Inspector-General of Police amid concerns over political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, including attacks on campaign rallies, destruction of billboards and other campaign materials, and threats to public peace.

The post 2027: SDP urges police, security agencies to be impartial appeared first on Vanguard News.

content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has forwarded the nomination of Agboola Lukman Dabiri to the Senate for screening and confirmation as Commissioner representing the South-West at the National Assembly Service Commission (NASC).

Tinubu’s request was conveyed in a letter read on the floor of the Senate on Monday by the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio.

In the letter, the President said the nomination was made pursuant to subsection 4 of the National Assembly Service Commission Act 2014.

“I am pleased to forward for confirmation by the Senate the appointment of Agboola Lukman Dabiri as Commissioner representing South-West at the National Assembly Service Commission.

“While I hope that the Senate will consider and confirm the nominee in its usual expeditious manner, please accept, Distinguished Senate and Distinguished Senate President, the assurances of my highest consideration,” Tinubu said.

The President urged the Senate to consider and confirm Dabiri’s nomination.

Akpabio disclosed that the nominee’s curriculum vitae was attached to the letter for the lawmakers’ reference.

He subsequently referred the request to the Senate Committee on Establishment, which is expected to report back to the chamber within two weeks.

The Senate President said the timeframe was considered appropriate given the current campaign period.

Dabiri is expected to replace Taiwo Oluga, who resigned from the commission to contest in the 2027 general elections.

Adegoke, who described himself
content:
By Adeola Badru

The African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate in Oyo State, Adegboyega Adegoke, has dismissed rumours that he is planning to withdraw from the 2027 governorship race, declaring that he is determined to contest and win the election.

Adegoke, who described himself as a committed contender in the race, said he would not step down for any candidate under any circumstances, insisting that his ambition was driven by his determination to implement his policy agenda, tagged SOLUTIONS, for the benefit of residents of the state.

The ADC candidate made his position known in a statement issued by his media team on Tuesday, in which he described the reports of his planned withdrawal as unfounded, unfortunate and misleading.

He said he remained resolute in his ambition to become the next governor of Oyo State, adding that he was not in the race as a placeholder for any other candidate.

“Let me state unequivocally that I am not stepping down for anybody. I am in this race to win and become the next occupier of the Agodi Governor’s Office,” Adegoke said.

He added: “The rumour is unfounded, unfortunate and misleading. I have stated many times that I am not a placeholder. I am the Oyo State governorship candidate of our great party, the African Democratic Congress (ADC), the next Executive Governor of Oyo State, Insha Allah.”

Adegoke said his ambition was anchored on his determination to deliver the promises contained in his SOLUTIONS agenda, which he said was designed to address the needs of the people and improve their welfare.

He urged his supporters across the state to remain steadfast and not allow the rumours to distract them from the campaign, assuring them that he remained fully committed to the governorship contest.

The ADC candidate attributed the speculation to individuals who, according to him, were unsettled by his growing popularity and prospects of victory at the polls.

He further expressed confidence that his ambition would be realised, declaring that no individual or group could frustrate what he described as God’s plan for his emergence as the next governor of Oyo State.

“Nobody can stop the plan of God to make me the next Executive Governor of Oyo State,” he said.

title: Police Invite Omo-Agege, Delta Council Chairman, Five Others Over Attack In Ughelli
description: The Delta State Police Command has invited a former deputy senate president, Ovie Omo-Agege, Ughelli North Local Government Chairman Jaro Egbo and five others for questioning over the deadly attack on a campaign convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the state.The police said the invitat
content:
The Delta State Police Command has invited a former deputy senate president, Ovie Omo-Agege, Ughelli North Local Government Chairman Jaro Egbo and five others for questioning over the deadly attack on a campaign convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the state.

The police said the invitations were part of an ongoing investigation into the violence that occurred during an NDC campaign in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, on Monday.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, Bright Edafe, said the invited individuals had been asked to report to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) at the police headquarters in Asaba on specified dates.

Omo-Agege, the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central, is expected to appear on Thursday at 11 a.m., while Egbo has been invited for 2 p.m. on the same day.

The five other invitees are Gowon Egoide, a former chairman of Uduere Quarters; Onoriode Oneya, the incumbent youth chairman of Uduere Community; Edirin Wokode Ewhubare, an associate of Egoide; Erukaye Egoide, Egoide’s nephew; and Tony Gabon Mevowovo, another associate of Egoide.

They are expected to appear before the police on Friday, November 27, at noon.

The police said the invitations were intended to establish the individuals’ level of involvement in the incident.

The development comes as Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, accompanied by the Commissioner of Police, Samuel Erale, and other heads of security agencies, visited Uduere community for an on-the-spot assessment of the attack.

During the visit, the governor expressed confidence in the police command to ensure that everyone found culpable was brought to justice, irrespective of political affiliation or status.

The Commissioner of Police urged the invited individuals to honour the invitations and cooperate with investigators.

He also warned that the command would not accept the presence of supporters or other persons who had not been formally invited.

The police assured residents that the investigation would be thorough and impartial, adding that anyone found culpable would be brought to justice.

The command also appealed to residents to remain calm and law-abiding as investigations continue.

Meanwhile, Omo-Agege and Egbo have traded conflicting accusations over who orchestrated the attack.

The attack left six people dead, according to preliminary police reports, while several others sustained injuries.

Omo-Agege reportedly escaped unhurt.

content:
The introduction of the 11-point scoring system in table tennis in 2001 marked one of the most significant changes in the sport’s history. The 1xBet Sierra Leone betting website also has a fully-fledged section dedicated to table tennis too.

For decades, matches had been played using a 21-point system, which allowed players more time to:

  • develop strategies;
  • recover from mistakes;
  • and establish control over a game.

However, the International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF) decided to replace this traditional format. And regardless of the format, the betting website 1xBet Sierra Leone will always allow you to wager on table tennis too.

Some details about this change

The decision was approved at the ITTF Annual General Meeting in Osaka, Japan, on April 26, 2001, and came into effect on September 1 of that year. Under the new regulations, games would be played to 11 points, with players changing service after every 2 points instead of 5. It is very easy to get the 1xBet app download and start betting on table tennis on the go as well.

Matches would consist of an odd number of games, generally best-of-5 or best-of-7. A 2-point advantage would still be required when the score reached 10-10.

The main argument in favour of the change was the need to make table tennis more attractive to television audiences and spectators. If this game is attractive for you, you can download the 1xBet app so you can make all your bets on its matches as well.

The ITTF believed that shorter games would create more exciting moments, increase uncertainty and generate additional opportunities for broadcasters to show decisive points. Greater television exposure was also expected to attract sponsors and improve the sport’s international popularity.

Much more than just changing the number of points

Nevertheless, the reform generated controversy. Critics argued that the traditional 21-point system offered greater opportunities for tactical development and allowed experienced players to demonstrate their consistency. Under the shorter format, every point became extremely important, increasing psychological pressure and making unexpected results more likely. You can check the 1xBet bonus rules and see how easy it is to use them on table tennis wagers.

Chinese players and officials were particularly concerned about the consequences of the reforms. The new scoring system also forced players to abandon familiar serving routines and adapt their psychological and tactical approaches. title: Alleged cyberbullying: DSS asks court to foreclose Sowore’s defence for exceeding adjournments’ ceiling
description:
The Department of State Services (DSS) on Tuesday asked the Federal High Court in Abuja to make an order foreclosing the defence of African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore,, in his ongoing trial for alleged cyberbullying.
Counsel to the DSS, Akinlolu Kehinde, SAN, inform
content:
The Department of State Services (DSS) on Tuesday asked the Federal High Court in Abuja to make an order foreclosing the defence of African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore,, in his ongoing trial for alleged cyberbullying.

Counsel to the DSS, Akinlolu Kehinde, SAN, informed Justice Mohammed Umar shortly before adjournment, that an application has been filed to the effect.

Kehinde told the court that Sowore’s legal team had already been served with the application.

The senior lawyer, who submitted that Sowore exceeded the five adjournments he is entitled to in criminal trial by nine, said there must be an end to this.

“Before we finally draw the curtain to the proceedings, I want to bring to your lordship notice the application we filed and and served on the defendant.

“The application is that, there must be an end to all these. The defendant has since exceeded the number of adjournments as required by law,” he said.

He urged the court to allow the application to be taken.

In the motion on notice filed on November 23 by Kehinde, the DSS sought two orders.

The security agency sought an order of the court ordering the closure of the case for the defence.

It also sought an order directing the parties to file and exchange their final written addresses within such time as the court shall direct, and fix a date for the adoption of the said addresses.

Giving a nine-ground argument, the lawyer said Sowore was in the suit and was re-arraigned on a two-count charge on which he pleaded not guilty on Jan. 19, 2026, and thereafter the trial commenced.

He said the DSS called its witness and closed its case in March 2026, and the defendant’s no-case submission was overruled on 8th May, 2026 and he was called upon to enter his defence.

The lawyer said Sowore, as particularised in the affidavit in support of the motion, sought or procured an adjournment of the proceedings on at least 14 occasions.

He said eight of the adjournments were sought since he was called upon to enter his defence.

“This is far in excess of the five (5) adjournments to which a party is entitled under Section 396(4) of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act, 2015.

“Since the defendant/respondent opened his defence on 6th July 2026, the trial has not progressed beyond the evidence of two defence witnesses,” he said.

Kehinde said Sowore has repeatedly filed applications and processes which had the effect of stalling the trial, including the subpoena issued against him, the lead counsel to the complainant/applicant).

He said the court has on several occasions warned Sowore against further delay.

According to him, the right to fair hearing guaranteed by Section 36 of the Constitution is a right to an opportunity to be heard, not a right to an unlimited number of adjournments.

He argued that a defendant who has been afforded ample opportunity to present his defence and fails to use it cannot complain of a breach of that right.

‘Section 36(4) of the Constitution guarantees a fair hearing within a reasonable time, and the Administration of Criminal Justice Act, 2015 requires that criminal trials proceed from day to day or, where that is impracticable, within the strict limits on adjournments prescribed by Section 396 of the ACJA.”

Kehinde urged the court to grant the application in the interest of justice.

Responding, Reuben Adakole, who appeared for Sowore, acknowledged the receipt of the application seeking to foreclose their defence.

Adakole, however, said that before the prosecution’s application could be taken, the court needs to deliver its ruling on the objection raised by Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) Chairman, against their subpoena, including their preliminary objection and ex-parte motion.

“In as much as the application tends to foreclose us, there is our application which the court ought to pronounce on first. Until after the ruling, we can look at it. The application is unripe my lord,” he said.

Kehinde, however, corrected Adakole’s impression that the prosecution’s request was to get a date to hear the application seeking the foreclosure of Sowore’s case.l

title: Don’t turn 2027 elections into battlefield, INEC chairman warns politicians
description:
The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, Prof. Joash Amupitan, has warned political parties and their supporters against turning the 2027 general elections into a battlefield, urging them to embrace peaceful campaigns and respect the rights of other political actors.
Amupitan s
content:
The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, Prof. Joash Amupitan, has warned political parties and their supporters against turning the 2027 general elections into a battlefield, urging them to embrace peaceful campaigns and respect the rights of other political actors.

Amupitan said rising cases of political violence, attacks on party members and intimidation of citizens could undermine the credibility of the elections before voting begins.

He spoke on Tuesday in Abuja at a high-level security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, with leaders of political parties and other stakeholders ahead of the 2027 elections.

The INEC chairman, who disclosed that the commission suspended its meeting to attend the engagement, described the situation as worrying.

He said, “If I tell you that as Chair of INEC I’m not concerned, I’m worried about the state of violence and thuggery, attacks on Nigerian citizens, on political party members who we’re supposed to work with, then I’ll be deceiving everybody. It’s a worrying situation.”

Amupitan recalled that he had previously urged political leaders not to turn elections into a battlefield but an opportunity for parties to present their policies and ideas to voters.

“You will recall during my address to the leaders of the political parties and members of the National Peace Committee on the 18th of August 2026, I emphasised one very key point, that we should not turn our election into a battlefield, but as we proceed with campaigns, that we should look at the election as a competitive interviewing job,” he said.

He argued that political parties should appeal to Nigerians for their votes rather than engage in activities that threaten their safety.

According to him, the Constitution vests sovereignty in the people, adding that their security and welfare should remain the priority of government.

The INEC chairman said violence could discourage voters from participating in elections, thereby compromising the democratic process.

He said, “When participants cannot assemble, campaign or organise themselves, express their views freely, the political process is compromised long before election day.

“And that is what this violence is meant to be, to scare the people so that the people will not turn out our votes.”

Amupitan urged the police to arrest, investigate and ensure the prosecution of those involved in electoral violence, particularly perpetrators of inflammatory campaign statements and the deployment of armed groups.

He cited Sections 95, 96 and 97 of the Electoral Act 2026, which provide guidelines on political rallies, prohibited campaign practices and threats of violence.

He noted that Section 95 mandated state Commissioners of Police and the FCT Commissioner of Police to provide adequate security for political rallies and processions.

The INEC chairman also warned political parties against organising, equipping or retaining security groups and political vanguards for campaigns.

He said the police were obligated to protect lawful political activities rather than obstruct them, adding that parties and candidates must comply with notification requirements for rallies.

Amupitan further disclosed that INEC would convene a security conference on Thursday, November 26, with the police, service chiefs and other members of the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security to address emerging threats and finalise security protocols for the 2027 elections.

He also appealed to political parties to participate in the commission’s nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise scheduled for Saturday, November 28.

He said the exercise would test the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, accreditation procedures and results transmission ahead of the general elections.

The warning came amid growing concerns over political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The National Peace Committee recently disclosed that 26 states and the FCT recorded 109 breaches of the National Peace Accord between August 19 and October 27, 2026, with political violence and thuggery accounting for 33 incidents.

title: Olowolafe: Quality teachers key to Nigeria’s economic growth
description:
Dr Tunji Olowolafe, Chancellor of Ekiti State University (EKSU), has described teachers as critical drivers of Nigeria’s economic development, while commending President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the Minister of Education for advancing the Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme.
Olowolafe made this submissio
content:
Dr Tunji Olowolafe, Chancellor of Ekiti State University (EKSU), has described teachers as critical drivers of Nigeria’s economic development, while commending President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the Minister of Education for advancing the Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme.

Olowolafe made this submission while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State, on Monday, November 23, 2026.

Speaking on the theme, “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the reform as a landmark development that would restore the dignity of Colleges of Education, strengthen teacher preparation and expand opportunities for prospective educators.

He applauded President Tinubu for signing the Federal Colleges of Education Act in 2023 and the Federal Ministry of Education for operationalising the programme in May 2025. Under the five-year arrangement, students can obtain an NCE after three years and proceed to earn a Bachelor’s degree within the same institution after another two years.

According to him, the reform combines practical teaching skills with academic depth, making graduates better equipped to teach across basic and post-basic education levels, particularly at a time Nigeria faces an estimated shortage of one million teachers.

He also highlighted the contributions of TETFund and NELFUND to educational development, citing SACOETEC as a practical example of the impact of sustained intervention. He observed that approximately 80 per cent of the College’s buildings were funded through TETFund, while encouraging eligible students to take advantage of NELFUND’s financial support for tuition and upkeep.

A major thrust of the lecture was the relationship between quality teaching and economic prosperity. Olowolafe described what he called a virtuous circle in which excellent teachers produce knowledgeable, skilled and innovative citizens, who drive business productivity and economic growth, ultimately expanding the resources available for further investment in education.

He maintained that teachers are much more than classroom instructors, describing them as nation-builders who shape minds and character at the most formative stages of life. He stressed that Nigeria cannot aspire to greatness without investing in the quality, capacity and welfare of its teachers.

He consequently advocated curriculum reforms that prioritise vocational education, practical skills, technology and problem-solving, while urging educators to embrace artificial intelligence without losing the human qualities of empathy, patience and moral guidance that define effective teaching.

Demonstrating the importance of recognising excellence, the Chancellor announced annual incentives through the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation for outstanding students and lecturers at the College. The initiative will reward the best NCE and degree graduates, first-class degree holders, NCE distinction graduates and lecturers rated highest by students, as an encouragement for hard work and higher academic standards.

He also announced plans by the Foundation to establish a solar-powered GOMTECH ICT centre at SACOETEC, equipped with Starlink connectivity to promote digital learning, artificial intelligence and technology-driven education. The Foundation will fund, equip and co-manage the facility in partnership with the College.

Olowolafe urged the graduating students to see their qualifications as a foundation for lifelong learning and leadership, citing former Nigerian leaders and nation-builders, including Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa, Shehu Shagari and Chief Obafemi Awolowo, who all had teaching backgrounds.

He challenged the graduands to appreciate the responsibility of their chosen profession, insisting that the quality of teachers Nigeria produces today will significantly determine the quality of its future leaders, workforce and overall national development.

The convocation lecture was attended by members of the College’s Governing Council and Management, academics, students, graduands and other stakeholders in the education sector.

title: Why Tinubu returned from exile after Abacha’s death – Omatseye
description:
President Bola Tinubu risked his life and political future by returning to Nigeria shortly after the death of military dictator, General Sani Abacha, in 1998, overruling the caution of fellow pro-democracy exiles just to see his mother.
The disclosure is contained in Chapter 11, pages 185–187, of ‘F
content:
President Bola Tinubu risked his life and political future by returning to Nigeria shortly after the death of military dictator, General Sani Abacha, in 1998, overruling the caution of fellow pro-democracy exiles just to see his mother.

The disclosure is contained in Chapter 11, pages 185–187, of ‘From AD to APC: The Evolution of Nigerian Political Parties and the Exploits of One Man (1998–2015),’ a new book by veteran journalist Sam Omatseye.

The excerpt was included in the programme of events for the book’s public presentation on Tuesday at the State House Conference Centre, Abuja, which was to be attended by the President.

According to the book, Tinubu, who was in exile, expressed a desire to see his mother during an emergency meeting in London convened by NADECO Abroad following Abacha’s sudden death in June 1998.

“It was in a room in London, and members of the NADECO Abroad had convened.

“The meeting was tense. An earthquake had happened at home, and the consequence was one for the ages. The dictator Sani Abacha had died,” the excerpt read.

According to Omatseye, although the new military Head of State, General Abdulsalami Abubakar, had conveyed a conciliatory tone to civil society organisations, suspicions ran deep.

Those present at the London meeting included former Foreign Affairs Minister, Professor Bolaji Akinyemi; retired General Alani Akinrinade; and Prince Iludoyin, all of whom had endured exile and deprivation, with the constant fear of being captured by the regime.

He wrote, “Most did not want to return just yet. They still wanted to watch the direction of affairs. There was a sense in which caution made sense.

“The military from the times of Babangida had laid ambush against the political society.”

However, Tinubu, described in the book as the face of NADECO Abroad, argued for an immediate return.

He warned that a delay would hand the political space to those who had propped up military rule.

“If they delayed and stayed back, they would surrender the country to the apologists of the military.

“They were the members of the five leprous fingers, and they could execute a pirouette and style themselves as democrats.

“It would turn the work of all of them, who had lost lives and resources, into a waste. He did not want that,” it read.

Omatseye added, “Tinubu tried to persuade them to take the plunge, and that the death of Abacha meant the decapitation of an era.”

Nonetheless, his fellow exiles hesitated, arguing that it made sense to visit Nigeria first and assess the situation rather than commit to a full return.

Addressing his reluctant comrades, Tinubu revealed that his real reason for returning to the country was to see his mother again, Omatseye wrote.

“So, in order to provide an excuse, he brought in a sense of domestic humour to disarm his fellows. He burst out in Yoruba, ‘Mo fe lo ri maami.’ (I want to see my mother.) They were amused but they had no counterpoint to his cheerful alibi,” the book stated.

The 1998 meeting followed the death of Abacha, who seized power from the Ernest Shonekan-led Interim National Government several months after the annulment of the June 12, 1993, presidential election won by Chief MKO Abiola.

Abiola died in custody on July 7, 1998.

General Abdulsalami subsequently oversaw a transition programme that produced the 1999 Constitution and transferred power to civilian rule on May 29, 1999.

Tinubu, a former senator who contested the 1992 senatorial election on the Social Democratic Party platform, returned from exile and contested the Lagos governorship election under the Alliance for Democracy, winning in 1999 and beginning the political journey that would eventually take him to the presidency in 2023.

The book, which covers the period from 1998 to 2015, tracing Nigeria’s return to civilian rule through the collapse of the Peoples Democratic Party’s 16-year grip on federal power, is Omatseye’s second major political work.

His first, ‘Beating All Odds: How Bola Tinubu Became President,’ was published in 2024.

An award-winning journalist, author, poet and playwright, Omatseye is Chairman of the Editorial Board of The Nation newspaper, where his weekly column, In Touch, has run for two decades.

Born on June 15, 1961, he studied History at the University of Ife, now Obafemi Awolowo University, and began his career at Newswatch magazine before rising to deputy political editor at Concord Newspapers during the June 12 crisis.

He was beaten by soldiers while covering the 1992 Ejigbo air crash. He later won the Nigerian Media Merit Award for Reporter of the Year.

Omatseye has won three additional NMMAs as Columnist of the Year and four Diamond Awards for Media Excellence.

He is also a recipient of the Association of Black Journalists’ Features Prize and the Scripps Howard Award for deadline reporting. He was the inaugural recipient of the Gordon N. Fisher Commonwealth Fellowship for Journalists.

He was among 51 persons granted national honours by the President in his 2026 Democracy Day speech on June 12.

According to the programme of events, the gathering was scheduled to receive goodwill messages from the governors of Lagos, Delta and Kaduna states, as well as former Zamfara Governor Abdulaziz Yari, former APC National Chairman Adams Oshiomhole, Minister of Environment Tunji Bello, media executive Dapo Olorunyomi and Alex Kabba.

The book was scheduled to be reviewed by Louis Odion, with excerpts to be read by Ohi Alegbe, Stella Din Jacobs and Yomi Odunuga.

The post Why Tinubu returned from exile after Abacha’s death – Omatseye appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: JUST IN: Katsina govt suspends Daura Emir, launches probe over Polish tourist allegation
description:
The Katsina State Government has constituted a committee to investigate allegations of sexual assault involving the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Umar Faruk Umar, and a foreign tourist.
As part of the measures taken, the government has suspended all official engagements and travels involving the traditional
content:
The Katsina State Government has constituted a committee to investigate allegations of sexual assault involving the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Umar Faruk Umar, and a foreign tourist.

As part of the measures taken, the government has suspended all official engagements and travels involving the traditional ruler pending the conclusion of the investigation.

The state Commissioner for Information and Culture, Bala Salisu Zango, announced the development in a statement issued on Tuesday.

The committee is expected to investigate the allegations and establish the circumstances surrounding the reported incident.

According to the statement, Governor Dikko Umaru Radda directed the establishment of the committee to investigate the allegations and advise the government accordingly.

“The Katsina State Government, under the leadership of His Excellency Governor Malam Dikko Umaru Radda, has expressed significant displeasure and concern over the purported viral allegations of sexual assault involving the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Umar Faruk Umar, and a foreign tourist,” the statement said.

It added that the government had taken the allegations seriously and would ensure that the matter received appropriate attention.

The commissioner further stated that the government was committed to implementing the committee’s findings and recommendations.

“Government wishes to assure the public that justice will be served and that the outcome of the committee’s findings and recommendations will be fully implemented,” the statement added.

The government urged members of the public to remain calm, law-abiding and continue with their normal activities while the investigation is ongoing.

title: Billboard controversy: Senator Orji Kalu’s politics anchored in the people, not Billboards — Reality organisation
description: Reality Organisation has reacted to the removal of a billboard bearing the photographs of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Senator Orji Uzor Kalu and Governor Alex Otti in Arochukwu Local Government Area of Abia State, clarifying that the billboard was neither erected nor commissioned by the former Abia
content:
Reality Organisation has reacted to the removal of a billboard bearing the photographs of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Senator Orji Uzor Kalu and Governor Alex Otti in Arochukwu Local Government Area of Abia State, clarifying that the billboard was neither erected nor commissioned by the former Abia governor.

The organisation, in a statement signed by Dimgba Okereke on Tuesday, disclosed that the billboard was erected by Engr. Emeka, a prominent son of Arochukwu, who independently chose to identify with the three political leaders.

“For the avoidance of doubt, Senator Orji Uzor Kalu neither erected nor commissioned the billboard. It was the independent initiative of Engr. Emeka, a well-known son of Arochukwu, who chose to express his support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Senator Orji Uzor Kalu and Governor Alex Otti.

“That is his personal choice and democratic right. His preference should not be misconstrued as evidence of a political alliance between the individuals or their respective political parties,” the organisation stated.

Reality Organisation noted that Kalu’s political engagements over the decades had been anchored in grassroots relationships and direct interaction with the electorate rather than publicity materials.

“Senator Orji Uzor Kalu’s politics is anchored in the people, not billboards. For decades, he has maintained direct relationships with communities and ordinary citizens. His ongoing community-to-community engagements across Abia North are consistent with his longstanding approach to politics and representation.

“The OUK Movement and Reality Organisation have established grassroots structures built over several years through direct engagement with communities and voluntary participation by members and supporters.

“Senator Kalu cannot be held responsible for every independent expression of support by those who admire him. Neither can he be expected to stop individuals from expressing their political preferences within the confines of the law.”

The organisation stressed that democracy thrives on freedom of choice, tolerance and respect for divergent political interests, urging those behind the removal of the billboard to appreciate the fundamental principles of democratic participation.

“Democracy is about the people and their freedom to make choices. A citizen’s decision to support candidates across political party lines does not necessarily amount to a formal political coalition.

“While we recognise the statutory responsibilities of advertising regulatory agencies, we expect such regulations to be applied fairly, transparently and without political discrimination.”

The organisation also called on the Nigeria Police Force and the Department of State Services (DSS) to closely monitor developments capable of overheating the polity and undermining peaceful political participation in Abia State.

“We urge the Police and the DSS to pay careful attention to actions and utterances capable of creating unnecessary political tension in the state.

“We equally urge members of Reality Organisation to remain peaceful, disciplined and resolute in their lawful grassroots engagements without allowing themselves to be provoked by the actions of others.

“Ultimately, elections are determined by the electorate, not by billboards or their removal. The democratic right of the people to freely choose their representatives must remain paramount,” the statement concluded.

The post Billboard controversy: Senator Orji Kalu’s politics anchored in the people, not Billboards — Reality organisation appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: CAF pledges to implement verdict restoring Senegal’s AFCON title
description:
The Confederation of African Football has pledged to implement the Court of Arbitration for Sport’s ruling restoring Senegal as champions of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations.
CAF, in a statement published on its website on Tuesday, said it respected the verdict, which overturned its Appeals Board’s de
content:
The Confederation of African Football has pledged to implement the Court of Arbitration for Sport’s ruling restoring Senegal as champions of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations.

CAF, in a statement published on its website on Tuesday, said it respected the verdict, which overturned its Appeals Board’s decision to strip Senegal of the continental title and award it to Morocco.

It said the CAS panel had set aside the decision of CAF’s Appeals Board, which stripped Senegal of the title and awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory, while upholding the earlier decision of the CAF Disciplinary Board.

“The CAS Panel ruled as follows: The Decision of the CAF Appeal Board of 17 March 2026 is set aside.

“The Decision of the CAF Disciplinary Board of 11 February 2026 is confirmed.

“Senegal has therefore been declared by CAS as the Winner of the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025,” the statement read.

The football governing body added that it “respects the CAS Award and will take all the necessary measures to implement it.”

The ruling followed an appeal by Senegal against CAF’s Appeals Board decision of March 17, which declared the Teranga Lions to have forfeited the final for breaching Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations and awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory.

The dispute stemmed from the controversial final played on January 18 at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat, where Senegal initially defeated hosts Morocco 1-0 after extra time to win their second continental title.

The match descended into controversy in stoppage time after the referee awarded Morocco a penalty following a VAR review, shortly after Senegal had a goal disallowed.

Angered by the decision, Senegal coach Pape Thiaw instructed his players to leave the pitch in protest. They returned after about 14 minutes, allowing the match to continue.

Morocco’s Brahim Diaz subsequently missed the penalty, while Pape Gueye scored the decisive goal in extra time to secure Senegal’s victory.

Morocco later lodged a complaint with CAF, arguing that Senegal’s withdrawal had disrupted the normal course of the match.

CAF’s Disciplinary Board initially allowed the result to stand while imposing sanctions on both teams over incidents during the final. However, its Appeals Board overturned that decision on March 17 and awarded Morocco the title.

Senegal rejected the decision and appealed to CAS on March 25, seeking to have the original result restored.

In its ruling on Tuesday, CAS held that the AFCON regulations invoked by CAF were not applicable to the circumstances of the match because the referee had allowed play to resume after Senegal’s players returned to the pitch.

“AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently. They are therefore not applicable in this case,” the panel ruled, according to a statement shared by Sky Sports reporter Rob Harris.

The Royal Moroccan Football Federation has, however, rejected the CAS verdict and vowed to pursue further legal action.

In a statement published on its X handle on Tuesday, the Moroccan federation also renewed its allegation that Senegalese Football Federation President Abdoulaye Fall had contacted German arbitrator Ulrich Haas, one of the three members of the CAS panel, 48 hours before the ruling.

The Senegalese federation had denied the allegation, with its Secretary-General, Sow, describing it as “an imaginary appeal” and saying Fall did not know the judges and was not present at the hearing.

Morocco’s rejection of the ruling came after CAS restored Senegal’s original 1-0 victory, ending months of uncertainty over the winner of the 2025 continental tournament.

The post CAF pledges to implement verdict restoring Senegal’s AFCON title appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Two lovers arraigned over alleged N178.2m theft in Lagos
description:
Two lovers, Chukwu Amaka Goodness and Ajijie Ferdinand Eri, were on Tuesday arraigned before Justice D.I. Dipeolu of the Federal High Court sitting in Ikoyi, Lagos for an alleged N178.2m theft.
The Lagos Zonal Directorate 2 of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) arraigned the duo.
Th
content:
Two lovers, Chukwu Amaka Goodness and Ajijie Ferdinand Eri, were on Tuesday arraigned before Justice D.I. Dipeolu of the Federal High Court sitting in Ikoyi, Lagos for an alleged N178.2m theft.

The Lagos Zonal Directorate 2 of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) arraigned the duo.

The defendants are facing trial on a 13-count second amended charge bordering on stealing, conspiracy, fraudulent conversion and money laundering to the tune of N178,271,321.70.

Chukwu was a former employee of Nibel Enterprises owned by Bonnibel Ugochi, the petitioner.

One of the counts reads: “That you, Chukwu Amaka Goodness and Ajijie Ferdinand Eri, sometime in March 2025, in Lagos, within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court, conspired amongst yourselves to commit an offence to wit: retention of the total sum of N75,000,000.00 (Seventy-Five Million Naira) in an account nominated by you with account name ‘Ajijie Ferdinand’ and account number 6013401684, domiciled in Moniepoint Microfinance Bank, which sum you reasonably ought to have known forms part of the proceeds of your unlawful act, to wit: stealing, and you thereby committed an offence contrary to and punishable under Section 21(a) of the Money Laundering (Prohibition and Prevention) Act, 2022.”

Another count reads:”That you, CHUKWU AMAKA GOODNESS and AJIJIE FERDINAND ERI, sometime in March 2025, in Lagos, within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court, conspired amongst yourselves to commit an offence to wit: retention of the total sum of N38,364,921.70 (Thirty-Eight Million, Three Hundred and Sixty Four Thousand, Nine Hundred and Twenty One Naira, Seventy Kobo) in an account nominated by you with account name ‘Ferdinand Ajijie’ and account number 2729506481, domiciled in Zenith Bank Plc., which sum you reasonably ought to have known forms part of the proceeds of your unlawful act, to wit: stealing and you thereby committed an offence contrary to and punishable under Section 21(a) of the Money Laundering (Prohibition and Prevention Act), 2022.”

The defendants pleaded “guilty” to the charges when they were read to them in court.

Justice Dipeolu, thereafter, asked the defendants whether they pleaded guilty due to unfavourable conditions at the Correctional Centre or had been compelled to do so.

The defendants, however, denied being forced to enter the pleas, insisting that they voluntarily admitted committing the offences contained in the charges.

The prosecution counsel, Suleiman I. Suleiman, thereafter, urged the court to proceed with the review of facts in the case and called Ismail Saifullahi, an investigator with the EFCC, to testify.

Saifullahi, who was the sole witness, told the court that the defendants were arrested at the Force Criminal Investigation Department, Alagbon, Lagos, following their release from the police custody.

He also told the court that investigations traced the alleged diversion of proceeds from supermarket sales to accounts operated by the defendants.

According to him, Chukwu, who worked as a salesperson for the petitioner, Ugochi, connived with her boyfriend, Ajijie, to open a Moniepoint business account using his details, through which proceeds from the sales of goods at Nibel Enterprises were diverted.

“Goodness and Eri also received customers’ payments into their personal bank accounts and a Moniepoint account originally opened in the name of Eri and subsequently upgraded to a business account with the business name “Mibel Enterprises” mimicking “Nibel Enterprises” the business name of the petitioner, Bonnibel, while funds diverted from the sales of products and the stealing of goods belonging to the supermarket were traced to several bank accounts belonging to the defendants.”

Saifullahi also informed the court that a Camry car belonging to Ajijie, which is suspected to be proceeds of crime, was seized during investigation.

Consequently, Suleiman urged the court to convict the defendants and order the restitution of the sum of N79,835,950 to the petitioner, Ugochi.

During the proceedings, Justice Dipeolu reduced the charges from 13 to 12, noting that counts one and two were similar.

The judge held that “ Counts 1 and 2 are similar. Therefore, the counts are reduced from 13 to 12-count charge.”

The judge adjourned till December 1, 2026 for “ conviction and sentencing.”

The post Two lovers arraigned over alleged N178.2m theft in Lagos appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.
