title: CBN Retains Interest Rate At 23% As Inflation Drops To 14.06%
description: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has retained its Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 23 per cent, despite a further decline in the country’s inflation rate to 14.06 per cent in October 2026.The decision was taken at the 308th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), held on Monday and Tuesd
content:
The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has retained its Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 23 per cent, despite a further decline in the country’s inflation rate to 14.06 per cent in October 2026.

The decision was taken at the 308th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), held on Monday and Tuesday, November 23 and 24, 2026.

In a communiqué issued on Tuesday and signed by the CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, the committee also retained the Standing Facilities Corridor at +50/-300 basis points around the MPR.

It further maintained the Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR) for Deposit Money Banks at 45 per cent, Merchant Banks at 16 per cent and non-Treasury Single Account (TSA) public sector deposits at 75 per cent.

The committee said the decision was informed by the need to sustain the progress made in reducing inflation and keep inflation expectations under control.

It noted that headline inflation had moderated for five consecutive months, supported by exchange rate stability and improved transmission of monetary policy measures.

However, members expressed concern over prevailing economic headwinds that could slow the pace of the decline in price pressures, maintaining that the current monetary policy stance remained appropriate.

According to the CBN, headline inflation declined to 14.06 per cent in October from 14.63 per cent in September 2026.

Core inflation also dropped to 10.78 per cent from 12.95 per cent, while food inflation eased to 19.13 per cent from 19.59 per cent over the same period.

The committee attributed the moderation in food inflation to lower prices of processed food and farm produce following the commencement of the harvest season.

It also noted that the composite Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 53.2 points in October from 53.0 points in September, indicating sustained expansion in economic activities across the industrial, agricultural and services sectors.

The CBN said Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $54.02bn as of November 17, 2026, providing cover for 10.26 months of imports of goods and services.

Inflation Risks

Despite the improvement in key economic indicators, the MPC identified potential risks that could put renewed pressure on prices.

These include the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which could sustain elevated global energy prices, as well as increased spending associated with the end-of-year festive season and election-related activities.

The committee also expressed confidence that continued exchange rate stability and improved food supply would support the disinflation process.

It welcomed a Memorandum of Understanding between the CBN and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, aimed at boosting foreign exchange inflows, supporting energy project financing and improving macroeconomic stability.

According to the committee, effective implementation of the agreement would strengthen foreign exchange market liquidity, boost external reserves and improve investor confidence.

The MPC also noted the resilience of the banking sector, citing adequate capital buffers and improved risk management practices.

Looking ahead, the committee expressed optimism about Nigeria’s economic outlook for the remainder of 2026 and into 2027, citing improved crude oil production and sustained growth in the agricultural, industrial and services sectors.

It, however, warned that disruptions to global energy supplies and adverse weather conditions remained key risks to the inflation outlook.

The CBN said it would continue to monitor domestic and global economic developments to ensure that future monetary policy decisions remain data-driven and focused on maintaining price stability.

The next MPC meeting is scheduled for February 22 and 23, 2027.

The post CBN Retains Interest Rate At 23% As Inflation Drops To 14.06% appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Omo-Agege heads to Appeal Court over nullification of Delta central senate ticket
description:
Former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, has directed his legal team to appeal the Federal High Court judgment in Warri, Delta State, which nullified his nomination as the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District.
Omo-Agege’s decision wa
content:
Former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, has directed his legal team to appeal the Federal High Court judgment in Warri, Delta State, which nullified his nomination as the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District.

Omo-Agege’s decision was disclosed in a statement issued on Tuesday by his Media Adviser, Sunny Areh, following the judgment in a suit filed by Prof. Alexander Osondu Akpodiete, who challenged his nomination.

The former senator described the ruling as disappointing, arguing that some of the court’s findings did not align with the documentary evidence presented during the proceedings.

He, however, said he respected the court but disagreed with its decision, adding that he was confident in the strength of his case on appeal.

One of the major issues raised by Omo-Agege’s camp was the court’s finding that his name was not contained in the NDC membership register submitted to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) at least 21 days before the party’s primaries.

According to the statement, both the NDC and INEC produced documents showing that his name appeared in the membership register submitted by the party.

It maintained that the party submitted only one register and did not maintain competing membership records for the same primary election.

The statement further claimed that INEC acknowledged receipt of the register and issued Certified True Copies (CTCs) of the document, bearing Omo-Agege’s name, to several persons.

It questioned the basis for the trial court’s finding, arguing that the documentary evidence presented by both the party and INEC confirmed his inclusion in the register.

The senator’s camp also challenged the plaintiff’s legal standing to institute the suit, arguing that Akpodiete did not obtain nomination forms, was not cleared by the party to contest and was not listed among the participants in INEC’s official monitoring report on the primaries.

It argued that these circumstances raised questions about whether the plaintiff had established sufficient legal interest to challenge the outcome of a primary in which he did not participate.

The statement also noted that Akpodiete did not ask the court to declare him the winner of the primary or award him the party’s ticket but instead sought to invalidate Omo-Agege’s nomination.

It further alleged that attempts had been made before the judgment to persuade INEC to remove Omo-Agege’s name from its final list of candidates, but the commission declined, having confirmed his inclusion in the membership register submitted by the party.

Describing the documents as official records rather than political assertions, Omo-Agege’s camp said they should be examined in their proper context during the appeal.

It maintained that the senator’s decision to challenge the judgment should not be interpreted as an attack on the judiciary or a rejection of the rule of law.

The statement urged those celebrating the judgment as the end of Omo-Agege’s political ambition to exercise patience, noting that the decision remained subject to appellate review.

It added that Omo-Agege remained committed to the NDC and the people of Delta Central, insisting that he would continue to pursue his political rights through lawful means.

“We believe in the rule of law, but we also believe that justice must be anchored in facts and evidence. We will appeal this judgment and pursue that appeal with determination,” the statement said.

The post Omo-Agege heads to Appeal Court over nullification of Delta central senate ticket appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: 2027: PDP flags off Bauchi governorship campaign, promises jobs, rural development
description:
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has officially commenced its governorship campaign in Bauchi State, promising to prioritise education, rural development and employment opportunities for women if elected in the 2027 general elections.
The party launched its campaign on Tuesday in Bununu, Tafawa Ba
content:
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has officially commenced its governorship campaign in Bauchi State, promising to prioritise education, rural development and employment opportunities for women if elected in the 2027 general elections.

The party launched its campaign on Tuesday in Bununu, Tafawa Balewa Local Government Area, where its governorship candidate, Usman Suphi, dismissed suggestions that the PDP had lost its political relevance in the state.

Suphi insisted that the party remained a strong political force in Bauchi, expressing confidence in its political standing ahead of the 2027 elections.

He also outlined the party’s key priorities, highlighting education, development of rural communities and improved employment opportunities for women as major areas of focus if the PDP wins the governorship election.

He said, “Whoever said PDP is dead is lying. PDP has been a strong force here and is still maintaining its strength.

“We will campaign with our blueprint in education, rural development and women’s employment. If elected, we will ensure development in our dear state.”

Suphi urged residents to trust the PDP, promising to deliver impactful development and improve the living conditions of the people.

He also thanked party supporters and leaders for their presence and commitment, describing their turnout as a demonstration of confidence in the party’s leadership.

The candidate further expressed optimism about the party’s chances in the 2027 elections, saying he was confident of assuming office on May 29, 2027.

Earlier, the Bauchi State PDP Chairman, Ibrahim Kashim, described Suphi as the most qualified among the governorship contenders, expressing confidence in his capacity to lead the state.

Kashim said the candidate was an honest and modest individual with an unblemished record, adding that he possessed the qualities required to drive the state’s development.

He said, “Suphi is an honest and modest individual with no record of betrayal. He is capable and has all it takes to develop Bauchi State.”

title: 2027: IG vows to arrest, prosecute perpetrators of electoral violence
description:
The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, has vowed to arrest and prosecute perpetrators of electoral violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that political office, party affiliation and personal influence would not shield offenders from prosecution.
Disu gave the warning on Tues
content:
The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, has vowed to arrest and prosecute perpetrators of electoral violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that political office, party affiliation and personal influence would not shield offenders from prosecution.

Disu gave the warning on Tuesday in Abuja during a high-level security meeting involving the Independent National Electoral Commission, political party leaders, civil society organisations and other stakeholders.

He expressed concern over recent incidents of violent clashes among political supporters, attacks on campaign venues and the use of dangerous weapons during political activities.

He said, “Recent incidents of violent clashes among political supporters, attacks on campaign venues, the use of dangerous weapons, intimidation of political opponents and the destruction of lawful political gatherings have become matters of serious concern.”

He warned that the developments posed threats to innocent lives and public confidence in the democratic process.

The police chief said, “Let me state categorically that political competition must never become justification for violence.

“Democracy provides an opportunity for citizens to freely express their political preferences, support candidates of their choice and hold differing opinions without fear of intimidation. It must never become a contest of who can mobilise more thugs, deploy more weapons or inflict greater harm on political opponents.”

Disu said the police remained neutral in the political process, irrespective of political parties, candidates or individuals involved.

“The position of the Nigeria Police Force is clear. Our neutrality in the political process is non-negotiable.

“We owe allegiance to the Constitution, the law and the Nigerian people, not to any political party or individual,” he said.

He, however, warned that the police would not hesitate to take decisive action against anyone involved in intimidation, assault, the use of weapons or other criminal conduct capable of disrupting political activities.

The IG also warned that political office, party affiliation and personal influence would not shield offenders from prosecution.

He said the destruction of campaign venues, attacks on electoral officials and materials, and other acts of electoral violence would attract appropriate law enforcement action.

Disu urged political party leaders to take responsibility for the conduct of their candidates, officials and supporters, adding that they must issue clear directives against violence and ensure compliance across their structures.

He also called on political parties to respect the rights of their opponents to participate in lawful political activities and comply with notification requirements for rallies and processions.

The IG said the police would continue to strengthen intelligence gathering, operational preparedness and collaboration with INEC and other security agencies to provide adequate security for political activities.

He said, “The Nigeria Police Force will not take sides in political contests, but will take a firm stand against anyone who threatens the peace.

“We will not protect political interests; we will protect Nigerian people.”

Disu also condemned the killing of six persons during a political campaign incident in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, on Monday, describing the development as unacceptable.

He said the security meeting had been scheduled before the incident but urged political stakeholders to take the development as a warning against allowing political activities to degenerate into violence.

The warning by the Inspector-General of Police comes amid growing concerns over political violence, attacks on campaign activities and intimidation of political opponents ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The concerns have been heightened by the deadly attack on the campaign entourage of former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, on Monday, November 23, 2026.

The post 2027: IG vows to arrest, prosecute perpetrators of electoral violence appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Omo-Agege rejects judgment nullifying senatorial ticket, vows to appeal
description: Former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, has rejected the Federal High Court judgment nullifying his nomination as the Nigeria Democratic Congress candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections, saying he will challenge the decision at the Court of Appea
content:
Former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, has rejected the Federal High Court judgment nullifying his nomination as the Nigeria Democratic Congress candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections, saying he will challenge the decision at the Court of Appeal.

Omo-Agege, in a statement on Tuesday signed by his Media Adviser, Sunday Areh, described the judgment delivered by the court in Warri, Delta State, as inconsistent with the documentary evidence and applicable law.

He said he had directed his legal team to immediately appeal the ruling, which followed a suit filed by Prof. Alexander Akpodiete, challenging his nomination.

“While we respect the court, we strongly disagree with its decision. We believe that some of the findings do not reflect the documentary evidence presented before the court. Senator Omo-Agege has therefore directed his legal team to immediately challenge the judgment at the Court of Appeal,” the statement said.

The former lawmaker faulted the court’s finding that his name was not included in the NDC membership register submitted to the Independent National Electoral Commission at least 21 days before the party’s primary election.

According to him, both the NDC and INEC presented documents showing that his name was contained in the register submitted by the party.

“Both the NDC and INEC produced documents showing that Senator Omo-Agege’s name was in the membership register submitted by the party.

“There was only one register. The NDC did not submit two different registers or maintain competing membership records for the same primary election. Senator Omo-Agege’s name appeared in the register submitted to INEC,” the statement said.

It further claimed that INEC acknowledged receipt of the register and issued Certified True Copies of the document to several persons, with Omo-Agege’s name appearing on it.

The statement said the legal team would ask the Court of Appeal to examine the basis for the trial court’s finding that his name was missing from the register despite the documents presented by the party and the electoral commission.

Omo-Agege also questioned the legal standing of Akpodiete to institute the suit, arguing that the plaintiff did not obtain nomination forms, was not cleared by the party to contest and was not listed among the participants in INEC’s official monitoring report on the primary election.

“The evidence before the court was that Prof. Akpodiete did not obtain the Nomination Forms required to participate in the party’s primaries. He was also not cleared by the party to contest, and his name did not appear among the participants listed in INEC’s official monitoring report on the primaries exercise,” the statement said.

It added that the plaintiff did not ask the court to declare him winner of the primary or award him the party’s ticket, but instead sought to invalidate Omo-Agege’s nomination.

The former Deputy Senate President also alleged that there had been attempts before the judgment to persuade INEC to remove his name from its final list of candidates, but said the commission declined after confirming that his name appeared in the membership register submitted by the NDC.

Describing the documents as official records, the statement maintained that they should be examined in their proper context during the appeal.

Omo-Agege said his decision to challenge the judgment should not be interpreted as disrespect for the judiciary, insisting that seeking appellate review was part of the judicial process.

“Those already celebrating this decision as the end of Senator Omo-Agege’s political journey should exercise patience. This is a judgment of the trial court, and the opportunity for appellate review remains. The legal process has not run its course,” the statement said.

The former lawmaker also reaffirmed his commitment to the NDC and the people of Delta Central, saying he would defend his political rights through lawful means.

PUNCH Online had reported that the Federal High Court sitting in Warri, Delta State, on Tuesday nullified Omo-Agege’s nomination as the NDC candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections over alleged non-compliance with provisions of the Electoral Act.

The judgment followed a suit marked FHC/WR/CS/120/2026, instituted by Akpodiete, who challenged the validity of Omo-Agege’s nomination on grounds bordering on his resignation from the All Progressives Congress, membership of the NDC and eligibility to participate in the party’s senatorial primary.

Delivering the judgment, Justice Hyeladzira Nganjiwa dismissed all five preliminary objections raised by Omo-Agege, the NDC and INEC challenging the competence of the suit before determining the substantive issues.

The court held that the NDC failed to comply with the Electoral Act’s mandatory provisions on submitting its membership register to INEC before conducting its primary election.

It also found that Omo-Agege’s name was not contained in the register submitted to INEC at least 21 days before the primary.

The judge further held that the party failed to provide credible evidence establishing that its membership register was subsequently updated and submitted to INEC within the statutory period preceding the primary.

Relying on INEC’s revised electoral timetable, the court noted that Omo-Agege participated in the APC senatorial primary held on May 18, 2026, which it said established that he was still a member of the APC at the material time.

Justice Nganjiwa consequently invalidated his nomination, ordered INEC to remove his name from its list of candidates for the election and restrained him from parading himself as the NDC candidate for Delta Central.

The court also held that the statutory period for conducting fresh primaries to nominate another candidate had elapsed, citing the Electoral Act’s timeline of 180 days before the general elections.

title: NANS Lagos demands action against alleged fake, expired products
description: The National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS), Joint Campus Council, Lagos State Axis, has issued a seven-working-day ultimatum to the Federal Government and the Lagos State Government to take decisive action against the alleged production, distribution and repackaging of counterfeit and expi
content:
The National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS), Joint Campus Council, Lagos State Axis, has issued a seven-working-day ultimatum to the Federal Government and the Lagos State Government to take decisive action against the alleged production, distribution and repackaging of counterfeit and expired products at the Trade Fair Complex and other locations across Lagos State.

Speaking at a World Press Conference, the Chairman of NANS JCC Lagos State Axis, Comrade Quadri Ishola Odewunmi, described the situation as a public health emergency and an alleged attempt at mass murder, warning that the circulation of fake medicines, adulterated beverages and other unsafe consumables poses a serious threat to the lives of unsuspecting Nigerians, particularly students and vulnerable members of society.

Odewunmi expressed concern over the continued activities of suspected counterfeit product operators within the Trade Fair Complex despite previous enforcement operations by the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC).

He questioned the sustainability of existing enforcement efforts and called for stronger political will from both levels of government to bring the situation under control.

He further highlighted the potential health implications of consuming substandard and falsified medicines and contaminated products, noting that Nigerians should not have to fear that medications purchased to treat common illnesses could expose them to further health complications.

As part of its demands, NANS called for the immediate lawful sealing of the entire Trade Fair Complex, the establishment of a multi-agency Joint Task Force comprising NAFDAC, NDLEA, the Nigeria Police Force, Nigerian Army and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, as well as a comprehensive screening of every shop, warehouse, production facility and storage space within the complex.

The association also demanded the investigation and prosecution of all individuals found culpable, including the consideration of appropriate charges relating to deliberate endangerment of human lives where supported by evidence and applicable law.

It further insisted that the complex should only be reopened after a thorough screening exercise and the implementation of effective monitoring mechanisms.

Issuing a firm warning, the NANS chairman declared that should the two levels of government fail to demonstrate concrete action within seven working days, the association would consider relocating its Lagos State Secretariat to the Trade Fair Complex and mobilising students across Lagos and neighbouring states for a peaceful and sustained protest and occupation to demand accountability.

The association also condemned reported attacks on NAFDAC officials during enforcement operations, warning that Nigerian students would not be intimidated by threats or acts of violence.

It, however, emphasised that its proposed intervention would remain peaceful and directed against criminal activities rather than legitimate traders and business operators.

Reaffirming its position, NANS called on the Federal and Lagos State Governments to prioritise public health and human lives over commercial interests, insisting that the protection of consumers and the eradication of counterfeit and expired products must become an urgent government priority.

The association concluded with a strong declaration that the lives of ordinary Nigerians must not be sacrificed to commercial greed, demanding safe markets, effective regulation and accountability for all those involved in the production and circulation of dangerous products.

The post NANS Lagos demands action against alleged fake, expired products appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Katsina Suspends Emir Of Daura Over Sexual Harrassment Controversy
description: The Katsina State Government has suspended the Emir of Daura, Umar Umar, from all official engagements and travel following viral allegations of sexual assault levelled against him by a foreign tourist.The government also announced the establishment of a high-level committee to investigate the alleg
content:
The Katsina State Government has suspended the Emir of Daura, Umar Umar, from all official engagements and travel following viral allegations of sexual assault levelled against him by a foreign tourist.

The government also announced the establishment of a high-level committee to investigate the allegations and advise it on the appropriate action.

The decision, announced on Tuesday, comes amid widespread public reactions to the allegations, which have attracted attention within and outside Nigeria.

In a statement signed by the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Bala Zango, the state government said it viewed the allegations with utmost seriousness.

According to the statement, Governor Dikko Radda directed the immediate constitution of an investigative committee to examine the claims and advise the government accordingly.

“The Katsina State Government has taken the allegations seriously. His Excellency, Governor Malam Dikko Umaru Radda, has therefore directed the establishment of a committee to investigate the issue and advise the government accordingly,” the statement read.

As part of the measures announced, the government said the Emir had been suspended from all official engagements and travels pending the outcome of the investigation.

It assured residents that justice would be served, adding that the committee’s findings and recommendations would be fully implemented.

The government also appealed to members of the public to remain calm, law-abiding and continue with their normal activities while the investigation proceeds.

The development follows a viral video posted by a foreign tourist identified as Mirka, who is known on Instagram as @beduinqa.

She alleged that the incident occurred during a visit to the Emir’s palace in Daura on November 14, 2026.

The tourist claimed she was granted a private audience with the Emir, during which he allegedly held her hand despite her objections before hugging her, kissing her on the cheeks and touching her breast without her consent.

According to her account, she secretly recorded the encounter using Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses equipped with a built-in camera.

She later published the footage after completing a 30-day tour of Nigeria.

She described the alleged incident as the only experience of sexual harassment she encountered during her travels across the country, adding that it left her emotionally distressed.

Before the state government’s intervention, the Daura Emirate Council had confirmed that it was aware of the viral video and had commenced an internal review to establish the authenticity of the footage and determine whether it had been altered or manipulated.

The spokesman for the Emirate Council, Ibrahim Murtala, said an official position would be released after the review was concluded.

The allegations have generated widespread reactions on social media, with many calling for a thorough and impartial investigation to establish the facts, ensure justice for all parties involved and protect the integrity of Nigeria’s traditional institutions.

The post Katsina Suspends Emir Of Daura Over Sexual Harrassment Controversy appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Atiku: We won’t leave any part of Kogi behind
description:
From Ndubuisi Orji, Abuja
African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate and former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar, has said that every part of Kogi State will feel the impact of his administration if he is elected president in 2027.
Atiku, according to a statement by the ADC Director of S
content:
From Ndubuisi Orji, Abuja

African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate and former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar, has said that every part of Kogi State will feel the impact of his administration if he is elected president in 2027.

Atiku, according to a statement by the ADC Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, said this while speaking at a campaign rally in Lokoja, the Kogi State capital.

The ADC candidate promised to revive the Ajaokuta Steel Mill in Kogi Central, develop the Idah River Port and improve roads and water supply across Kogi East, and complete the Kabba to Egbe road in Kogi West. He noted that the promises were geared towards making life more affordable for citizens.

According to him, “To my brothers and sisters in Kogi East, I know what it means when a farmer cannot get produce to market because the road has failed, or when a family must struggle every day for clean water. We will improve your roads and water supply, and develop Idah River Port so that the region’s farmers and businesses can reach more customers.

“To the people of Kogi Central, Ajaokuta must finally become a working steel mill. I want its furnaces working, its gates open to skilled workers and its promise felt in the homes of the people who have waited so long. We will also support the roads and services that allow surrounding communities to benefit from that industry.

“To the people of Kogi West, the Kabba to Egbe road cannot remain an endless promise. We will complete it and make travel and trade easier for the communities along its route.”

The former Vice President, who stated that the strength of Kogi State lay in its people, also promised to pursue the dredging of Baro Port and to restore a targeted subsidy on fuel refined in Nigeria to ease transport and production costs.

“Kogi’s strength lies in its people. I have seen your welcome today, and I will remember it. You deserve a government that turns your state’s potential into jobs, working infrastructure and a life your families can afford,” he stated.

The post Atiku: We won’t leave any part of Kogi behind appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: 116 bag first-class degrees as Ajayi Crowther varsity graduates 4,104
description:
Ajayi Crowther University, Oyo State, will graduate 4,104 students at its 18th convocation ceremony scheduled for Wednesday and Thursday, November 25 and 26, with 116 graduands earning First Class Honours degrees.
This was disclosed in a statement made available to PUNCH Online on Tuesday, stating t
content:
Ajayi Crowther University, Oyo State, will graduate 4,104 students at its 18th convocation ceremony scheduled for Wednesday and Thursday, November 25 and 26, with 116 graduands earning First Class Honours degrees.

This was disclosed in a statement made available to PUNCH Online on Tuesday, stating that the university will also confer honorary doctorate degrees on renowned historian, Prof. Toyin Falola, and financier, Mr Kayode Falowo.

“Prof. Falola, one of Africa’s best-known historians, is a Professor of History at the University of Texas at Austin, United States. He has authored and edited numerous publications on African history and culture,” the statement said.

The honorary degrees will be conferred at the university chapel on the same day that 87 candidates will receive doctoral degrees in various disciplines.

“Giving a breakdown of the graduands, Oduwole said 116 students would receive First Class Honours degrees, 1,207 Second Class Upper degrees, 693 Second Class Lower degrees and 45 Third Class degrees.

“At the postgraduate level, 158 candidates will be awarded postgraduate diplomas, 1,798 will receive master’s degrees, while 87 will be awarded doctorate degrees.

“In all, the university will confer awards on 4,104 individuals across undergraduate and postgraduate categories in recognition of their achievements in learning and character,” the statement said.

The Vice-Chancellor also highlighted the institution’s achievements since she assumed office about a year ago, citing improvements in infrastructure and academic development, as well as the approval of new academic programmes by the National Universities Commission.

Among the newly approved programmes are Medicine and Surgery, Pharmacy and several other courses.

title: [VIDEO] 2027 Elections: Everybody Should Be Allowed To Campaign Freely, Says Obi
description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has called on the Federal Government and security agencies to ensure that all political parties and candidates are allowed to campaign freely ahead of the 2027 general elections, condemning the growing incidents of polit
content:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has called on the Federal Government and security agencies to ensure that all political parties and candidates are allowed to campaign freely ahead of the 2027 general elections, condemning the growing incidents of political violence across the country.

Speaking to Channels Television after interacting with residents during a town hall meeting in Taraba State, the former Anambra State governor described the situation as unhealthy for Nigeria’s democracy.

Obi was responding to questions about the reported attack on the campaign convoy of his party’s Delta Central senatorial candidate, Ovie Omo-Agege, and concerns over the safety of opposition politicians.

He said there was no justification for subjecting Nigerians to violence during political campaigns, stressing that the country should uphold peaceful democratic practices.

Obi also urged the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to allow a free, fair and credible electoral process, noting that the party already controls the government.

Beyond politics, Obi said his town hall engagements were aimed at listening to Nigerians and understanding their challenges, including unemployment, overtaxation of small businesses, lack of access to funding, strikes in schools and inadequate primary healthcare.

He described listening to citizens as an essential part of responsible and demand-driven leadership.

title: Grief as Bayelsa begins mass burial of boat accident victims
description:
The Bayelsa State Government on Tuesday commenced the mass burial of victims of the boat accident involving mourners travelling to Ukubie community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state.
The mass burial took place at the Azikoro Cemetery in Yenagoa, the state capital, amid tears and gr
content:
The Bayelsa State Government on Tuesday commenced the mass burial of victims of the boat accident involving mourners travelling to Ukubie community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state.

The mass burial took place at the Azikoro Cemetery in Yenagoa, the state capital, amid tears and grief as relatives, friends and sympathisers bade farewell to their loved ones.

The Secretary to the State Government, Prof. Nimibofa Ayawei, accompanied by the Commissioner for Environment, Mr Ebi Ben Ololo, supervised the burial.

A stench hung in the air as the corpses were conveyed into the cemetery, with some sympathisers wearing face masks to protect themselves from the offensive odour.

The remains, wrapped in black plastic bags, were transported to the cemetery in four commercial vehicles before an excavator was deployed to cover the mass grave.

Relatives and sympathisers broke down in tears as the bodies were lowered into the grave, while small groups of mourners were seen discussing the tragedy in hushed tones.

The incident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, when a passenger boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony in Ukubie capsized at the Oweikorogha/Otuan river junction in Southern Ijaw.

The accident triggered an extensive search-and-rescue operation involving security agencies, emergency responders, community volunteers and government officials.

Speaking during the burial exercise, the Chairman of the Ukubie Community Development Committee, Mr Ruben Kemelate, said the community had not planned any separate funeral ceremony for the victims because of the prevailing atmosphere of grief and the government’s decision to take charge of the burial arrangements.

He explained that the community leadership and affected families had met with the state government, adding that residents were awaiting further directives from the authorities.

Kemelate said, “Actually, the community has not planned any ceremony or anything because it is a sad mood. It is the government that is in charge now, and the community is looking up to the government for directives.”

Describing the devastating impact of the tragedy on Ukubie, the CDC chairman said virtually every family in the community had lost a relative in the accident.

He said the scale of the loss had left the entire community traumatised, adding that he personally lost his elder sister, who died in his hands at the Federal Medical Centre.

“In Ukubie community, we are in a very sad mood from the first day till now that we are burying them. Every family is affected. There is no family that is not affected.

“Like me, my elder sister died in my hands at FMC. So every family is in a sad mood. We are in a very sad mood as a community,” he added.

Meanwhile, Governor Douye Diri had ordered an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the fatal accident, particularly reports that the ill-fated boat was overloaded, had no passenger manifest and that most of the passengers were not wearing life jackets.

The governor, who cut short an official trip outside the state to visit the scene of the incident, directed the Commissioner of Police, the State Director of the Department of State Services and the Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy to commence an immediate investigation.

Diri had described the circumstances surrounding the accident as a serious breach of established marine transportation safety protocols, warning that anyone found to have acted negligently would face prosecution.

The tragedy has renewed concerns over the safety of water transportation in Bayelsa, where several riverine communities depend heavily on boats for movement and commercial activities.

The mass burial brought another painful chapter to the aftermath of the disaster, as the affected families and the Ukubie community continue to grapple with the loss of their loved ones.

The post Grief as Bayelsa begins mass burial of boat accident victims appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Imo Airport reopens tomorrow as Uzodimma extends runway
description:
‎After an upgrade of some of its facilities, including the extension of the runway, Sam Mbakwe International Airport will reopen tomorrow.
The Airport was temporarily shut down for infrastructural intervention aimed at restoring the structural integrity of the existing runway, extending its operatio
content:
‎After an upgrade of some of its facilities, including the extension of the runway, Sam Mbakwe International Airport will reopen tomorrow.

The Airport was temporarily shut down for infrastructural intervention aimed at restoring the structural integrity of the existing runway, extending its operational length and strengthening associated aircraft movement infrastructure.

‎Imo State Commissioner for Information, Public Orientation and Strategy, Hon Declan Emelumba announced the news of the reopening of the airport.

‎He disclosed that the Imo State government bore the entire cost of the infrastructural upgrade at the Sam Mbakwe International Airport.

‎He said the rehabilitation became necessary following the deterioration of sections of the existing 2.7 kilometres runway.

According to the commissioner, the runway has now been extended to 3.2 kilometres with ashphalt resurfacing and strengthening of the existing taxiways.

‎”The rehabilitation and expansion of the Sam Mbakwe International Airport represent a significant infrastructural investment by His Excellency, Governor Hope Uzodimma,” he declared.

‎Emelumba further explained that the governor undertook the project to enhance the smooth movement of aircrafts especially during this Christmas period, that Imo people and others would be home.

‎According to him, Uzodimma anticipated increased traffic at the airport and decided to ensure that the facilities were upgraded.

‎He said the upgrade of the airport was part of a broader policy initiative of the government to make it easier for would be investors to access the state through the air.

The post Imo Airport reopens tomorrow as Uzodimma extends runway appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: ‘This Is Payback Time’, Shettima Makes Case For Tinubu Re-Election In Borno
description: Vice President Kashim Shettima has urged voters in the North to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, describing it as an opportunity to reciprocate the president’s past political support for the region.Shettima made the appeal while speaking at the distribution and fl
content:
Vice President Kashim Shettima has urged voters in the North to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, describing it as an opportunity to reciprocate the president’s past political support for the region.

Shettima made the appeal while speaking at the distribution and flag-off of special intervention projects by the North-East Development Commission (NEDC) in Borno State.

He recalled that Tinubu played a significant role in securing the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential ticket for former President Muhammadu Buhari ahead of the 2015 general election.

According to the vice president, Tinubu deliberately moved the party’s presidential primary to Lagos and mobilised support for Buhari in the South-West, contributing to his emergence as the party’s candidate.

“Those of us that were active in the political scene can bear testimony to the fact that without the efforts of President Bola Tinubu, Muhammadu Buhari couldn’t have clinched the ticket of the APC in 2014 in Lagos.

“He deliberately shifted the base of the primaries to Lagos, and he worked assiduously to deliver the South-West. And one good turn always deserves another,” Shettima said.

The vice president urged the people of the North to reciprocate Tinubu’s political support by backing his re-election, declaring that the region had an opportunity to return the favour.

“And for us in the North, this is payback time. I urge you, I beseech all of us here, let us use our informed judgment and make decisions that are in the best interest of our nation,” he said.

Making a case for the administration’s economic policies, Shettima urged Nigerians to consider the government’s economic performance when deciding who to support in the 2027 elections.

He cited a decline in headline inflation and an increase in the country’s foreign reserves, which he said had reached their highest level in 17 years.

“The economy has turned the corner. Headline inflation has come down. Our foreign reserve is the highest in the past 17 years. It’s now hovering in the region of 55 billion dollars,” he said.

Defending the removal of the petrol subsidy, the vice president maintained that the decision was not intended to worsen the economic hardship faced by Nigerians but to prevent the country’s economy from collapsing.

“And the President has a great deal of human empathy for the Nigerian people. He withdrew the subsidy not to inflict pain on Nigerians, no. He removed the subsidy to save the Nigerian economy from collapse,” he said.

The post ‘This Is Payback Time’, Shettima Makes Case For Tinubu Re-Election In Borno appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Sexual assault allegation: Katsina suspends Daura emir, orders probe
description:
The Katsina State Government has constituted a committee to investigate the sexual assault allegation made by a Polish tourist, Mirka Czee, against the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Umar Farouk Umar.
The government also announced the suspension of all official engagements and travels by the monarch pending
content:
The Katsina State Government has constituted a committee to investigate the sexual assault allegation made by a Polish tourist, Mirka Czee, against the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Umar Farouk Umar.

The government also announced the suspension of all official engagements and travels by the monarch pending the outcome of the investigation.

The decision was contained in a press release issued on Tuesday by the state Commissioner for Information, Culture and Tourism, Dr Bala Zango.

According to the statement, Governor Dikko Radda directed the establishment of the committee to investigate the allegations and advise the government on the appropriate course of action.

“The Katsina State Government, under the leadership of His Excellency, Governor Malam Dikko Umaru Radda, has expressed significant displeasure and concern over the purported viral allegations of sexual assault involving the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Umar Farouk Umar, and a foreign tourist,” the statement said.

The government said it was taking the allegations seriously, adding that the committee would examine the matter and submit its findings and recommendations.

It further assured residents that the outcome of the investigation would be implemented.

“The government wishes to assure the public that justice will be served and that the outcome of the committee’s findings and recommendations will be fully implemented,” the statement added.

The state government, however, urged members of the public to remain calm, law-abiding and continue with their normal activities while the investigation was ongoing.

The development follows the circulation of a video in which Czee accused the traditional ruler of sexually assaulting her during a visit to his palace.

The Polish tourist, who was born in the Czech Republic, had said she was left alone with the Emir after being shown around the palace and its surroundings.

She alleged that he held her hand, hugged and kissed her on the cheek before touching her breasts without her consent.

Czee said she recorded part of the encounter using Meta smart glasses and later shared the footage on social media, explaining that she wanted to speak out about her experience and raise awareness about unwanted touching.

The Daura Emirate Council had earlier said it was reviewing the video to establish its authenticity and determine whether it had been manipulated or artificially generated.

The council, through its spokesperson, Ibrahim Daura, said it would examine the footage before making a formal pronouncement.

An unnamed source in the Emir’s palace had also denied the allegation, saying there was nothing of the sort during the tourist’s visit.

Meanwhile, Amnesty International Nigeria called on the Katsina State Government and the police to conduct a transparent and independent investigation into the allegation.

As of the time the government issued its statement, it had not disclosed the composition of the investigative committee or the timeline for submitting its report.

The post Sexual assault allegation: Katsina suspends Daura emir, orders probe appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: DSS asks court to foreclose Sowore’s defence over 14 adjournments
description:
The Department of State Services has asked the Federal High Court in Abuja to foreclose the defence of the presidential candidate of the African Action Congress, Omoyele Sowore, over alleged delays in his ongoing cyberbullying trial.
The DSS, through its counsel, Akinlolu Kehinde, SAN, on Tuesday, u
content:
The Department of State Services has asked the Federal High Court in Abuja to foreclose the defence of the presidential candidate of the African Action Congress, Omoyele Sowore, over alleged delays in his ongoing cyberbullying trial.

The DSS, through its counsel, Akinlolu Kehinde, SAN, on Tuesday, urged Justice Mohammed Umar to grant an application seeking to close the defendant’s case, alleging that he had exceeded the number of adjournments permitted under the law.

Kehinde told the court that the application, filed on November 23, had been served on Sowore’s legal team, adding that the defendant had sought or procured adjournments on at least 14 occasions since the commencement of the trial.

He argued that the number was far beyond the five adjournments permitted under Section 396(4) of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act, 2015.

“Before we finally draw the curtain on the proceedings, I want to bring to your Lordship’s notice the application we filed and served on the defendant.

“The application is that there must be an end to all this. The defendant has since exceeded the number of adjournments as required by law,” he said.

In the motion on notice, the DSS sought an order closing the defence’s case and directing parties to file and exchange their final written addresses within a period to be determined by the court, ahead of a date for their adoption.

Giving nine grounds in support of the application, Kehinde said Sowore was re-arraigned on a two-count charge on January 19, 2026, to which he pleaded not guilty, after which the trial commenced.

He said the prosecution called its witness and closed its case in March 2026, while the court dismissed Sowore’s no-case submission on May 8, 2026, and directed him to enter his defence.

According to the prosecution, Sowore subsequently sought or procured adjournments on at least 14 occasions, eight of which occurred after he was called upon to open his defence.

Kehinde said the trial had made little progress since Sowore opened his defence on July 6, 2026, with only two defence witnesses having testified.

“Since the defendant/respondent opened his defence on 6th July 2026, the trial has not progressed beyond the evidence of two defence witnesses,” he said.

The senior lawyer further accused Sowore of repeatedly filing applications and court processes that allegedly stalled the proceedings, including the subpoena issued against the lead counsel to the complainant.

He said the court had, on several occasions, cautioned the defendant against delaying the trial.

Kehinde argued that the constitutional right to fair hearing did not confer an unlimited right to adjournments, stressing that a defendant who had been given sufficient opportunity to present his case could not complain of a breach of that right.

“Section 36(4) of the Constitution guarantees a fair hearing within a reasonable time, and the Administration of Criminal Justice Act, 2015 requires that criminal trials proceed from day to day or, where that is impracticable, within the strict limits on adjournments prescribed by Section 396 of the ACJA.”

He urged the court to grant the application in the interest of justice.

However, Sowore’s counsel, Reuben Adakole, opposed the timing of the application, arguing that the court should first determine pending applications relating to the subpoena issued against the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN.

Adakole acknowledged receiving the DSS application but maintained that the court needed to deliver its ruling on Amupitan’s application to set aside the subpoena, as well as the defence’s preliminary objection and ex-parte motion, before considering the prosecution’s request.

“Inasmuch as the application tends to foreclose us, there is our application which the court ought to pronounce on first. Until after the ruling, we can look at it. The application is unripe, my lord,” he said.

Meanwhile, Alex Iziyon, SAN, who represented Amupitan, informed the court that the matter had previously been adjourned because the defence had yet to file its counter-affidavit.

He, however, confirmed that the defence had subsequently filed the process and that he had responded, urging the parties to adopt their respective processes.

Adakole confirmed that the processes had been exchanged but clarified that the subpoena issued to the INEC chairman was strictly a *subpoena duces tecum*, requiring him to produce documents rather than appear as a witness to give oral evidence.

“It is just strictly to come and tender the documents, and that was why we filed a motion to amend the application.

“We ask that we be allowed to move our motion ex parte, so that it will lay to rest all these issues.

“So the intent was just for INEC chairman to tender the documents and not to testify,” he said.

Iziyon disagreed, accusing the defence of attempting to circumvent the court’s earlier directive.

“The defendant cannot take this court for a ride. I submit with all sense of responsibility,” he said.

He reminded the court that it had directed the defence to file a formal application on notice to enable the opposing parties to respond.

In response, Justice Umar told Adakole that the defence was required to comply with the court’s directive since the parties had already joined issues on the matter.

“Before the last adjourned date, I told you that since you have issued that subpoena and they have been joined, anything you want to do now will be by motion on notice; serve them, and they will respond,” the judge said.

The court subsequently heard the applications, with Iziyon adopting three processes filed on behalf of Amupitan and urging the court to set aside the subpoena.

He relied on an earlier ruling by Justice Umar on the court’s power to set aside a subpoena and cited a previous case in which a subpoena was set aside because the person sought to be summoned had no connection with the subject matter of the proceedings.

Adakole, in his response, adopted the defence processes and urged the court to dismiss Amupitan’s application.

He also moved an ex parte application filed on November 11, seeking four reliefs, arguing that the documents requested were public records in the custody of a public officer and were necessary for Sowore’s defence.

He maintained that their relevance could only be determined by the court after they had been produced.

“It is not for the applicant to say so. That will be preemptive,” he said.

After listening to the parties, Justice Umar adjourned the case until December 7 for ruling on Amupitan’s application to set aside the subpoena.

The judge also fixed the date for the hearing of the DSS application seeking to foreclose Sowore’s defence and other pending applications.

The post DSS asks court to foreclose Sowore’s defence over 14 adjournments appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: AFCON: Morocco rejects verdict, alleges Senegal FA chief phoned CAS arbitrator
description:
The Royal Moroccan Football Federation has rejected the Court of Arbitration for Sport’s decision restoring Senegal as the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions, vowing to pursue further legal action against the ruling.
The Moroccan federation also renewed its allegation that Senegalese Football Fede
content:
The Royal Moroccan Football Federation has rejected the Court of Arbitration for Sport’s decision restoring Senegal as the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions, vowing to pursue further legal action against the ruling.

The Moroccan federation also renewed its allegation that Senegalese Football Federation President Abdoulaye Fall had telephone contact with German arbitrator Ulrich Haas, one of the three members of the CAS panel, 48 hours before the verdict was delivered.

Reacting to the verdict in a statement published on its X handle on Tuesday, the federation expressed surprise that the arbitration court did not consider its request for legal consequences over the alleged communication, which it said could undermine the integrity and credibility of the proceedings.

The statement read, “The Royal Moroccan Football Federation has taken note of the decision issued by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, in Lausanne, Switzerland, concerning the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation against the decision of the Appeals Committee of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) relating to the final match of the Africa Cup of Nations.

“In this regard, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest over the failure to consider its request, which sought to ensure that the necessary legal consequences were applied to practices capable of undermining the integrity and credibility of the arbitration proceedings.

“In particular, this concerns the confirmed communication between German arbitrator Ulrich Haas and the President of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was issued.”

The federation further faulted the CAS ruling for failing to consider the positions of the International Football Association Board and FIFA on players leaving the field without the referee’s permission.

It argued that the decision did not adequately address the disciplinary responsibilities and sanctions arising from such conduct.

“The Royal Moroccan Football Federation also notes that the decision did not take into account the position recently established by both the International Football Association Board (IFAB), the body responsible for the Laws of the Game, and FIFA regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and sanctions,” it added.

The Moroccan federation said it would explore further legal options to challenge the ruling.

“Accordingly, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation reaffirms its determination to pursue all available legal avenues to challenge the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport,” the statement said.

The development follows Tuesday’s ruling by CAS, which overturned the Confederation of African Football Appeals Board’s decision to award Morocco a 3-0 victory in the disputed final and restored Senegal’s original 1-0 win.

CAS upheld Senegal’s appeal against the CAF decision, ruling that the tournament regulations invoked to declare the Teranga Lions losers by forfeiture did not apply because the referee had allowed the match to resume after the players returned to the pitch.

The dispute dates back to the January 18 final at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat, where Senegal defeated hosts Morocco 1-0 after extra time.

The match was thrown into controversy in stoppage time after the referee awarded Morocco a penalty following a VAR review, shortly after Senegal had a goal ruled out.

Angered by the decision, Senegal coach Pape Thiaw instructed his players to leave the pitch in protest. They returned after about 14 minutes, but Morocco’s Brahim Diaz missed the resulting penalty before Pape Gueye scored Senegal’s winning goal in extra time.

Morocco subsequently lodged a complaint with CAF, arguing that Senegal’s withdrawal had disrupted the normal course of the match.

CAF’s Disciplinary Board initially allowed the result to stand while imposing sanctions on both teams. However, its Appeals Board, on March 17, overturned the decision, ruled that Senegal had forfeited the final for breaching Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, and awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory.

Senegal rejected the decision and appealed to CAS on March 25, seeking the restoration of the original result.

Before the CAS verdict, Morocco had also accused Fall of contacting one of the arbitrators handling the appeal.

The allegation was reported by Reuters and Moroccan media outlet Hespress, citing sources familiar with the matter.

The Senegalese federation denied the allegation. Its Secretary-General, Sow, described it as “an imaginary appeal”, saying Fall did not know the judges and was not present at the hearing.

Reuters had reported that it could not independently verify whether the alleged telephone conversation took place or establish what was discussed.

CAS had not immediately commented on the allegation at the time of that report.

The post AFCON: Morocco rejects verdict, alleges Senegal FA chief phoned CAS arbitrator appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Gov Sule Directs Security Agencies To Tackle Farmers-Herders Clashes, Kidnapping In Nasarawa
description: Governor Abdullahi Sule of Nasarawa State has urged security agencies to intensify efforts to address the farmer-herder clashes, kidnapping and rising cases of violent crime, particularly in Doma and Karu local government areas.The governor made the call on Tuesday while presiding over a security co
content:
Governor Abdullahi Sule of Nasarawa State has urged security agencies to intensify efforts to address the farmer-herder clashes, kidnapping and rising cases of violent crime, particularly in Doma and Karu local government areas.

The governor made the call on Tuesday while presiding over a security council meeting with heads of security agencies and selected traditional rulers at the Government House in Lafia.

He expressed concern over recurring disputes between farmers and herders in Doma, urging security agencies to work closely with traditional rulers and other stakeholders to prevent further clashes.

Sule also raised concerns over increasing cases of homicide in Karu, urging the Commissioner of Police to pay special attention to the area and take measures to curb the trend.

On emerging political security concerns, the governor said the activities of the Sowore-led movement in major towns, including Lafia, Keffi, Akwanga and Karu, would be discussed at the meeting.

He explained that the involvement of traditional rulers and local government officials was intended to strengthen collaboration and improve efforts to address potential security threats.

The governor commended security agencies for their cooperation, particularly the arrest of about 14 suspected drug dealers by the 4 Special Forces in Doma, in collaboration with the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA).

He also praised their joint efforts in arresting a suspected kidnapper in Angwan Farin Kasa village, who was subsequently handed over to the Department of State Services (DSS), as well as security operations in Kantsakuwa village, Lafia Local Government Area.

To strengthen security operations across the state, Sule distributed additional vehicles to security agencies shortly after the meeting.

The vehicles were presented on his behalf by the Deputy Governor, Emmanuel Akabe.

Welcoming the new Commissioner of Police and the State Commandant of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), the governor urged them to strengthen cooperation with other security agencies to tackle emerging threats.

He also expressed appreciation to the outgoing Commissioner of Police, and the outgoing NSCDC commandant for their services to the state, wishing them success in their new assignments.

title: 2027: IG pledges journalists’ safety, warns against misinformation
description:
The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, has assured journalists of the Nigeria Police Force’s protection during the 2027 general elections, warning that misinformation and information disorder pose threats to credible polls.
Disu said the police would support journalists in carrying out thei
content:
The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, has assured journalists of the Nigeria Police Force’s protection during the 2027 general elections, warning that misinformation and information disorder pose threats to credible polls.

Disu said the police would support journalists in carrying out their professional duties, pledging that the force would not be used as an instrument of political oppression.

He spoke on Tuesday while delivering the keynote address at the 2026 Media and Development Conference organised by the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development in Abuja.

Speaking on the theme, Policing, Public Trust and Accountability, the IG described journalism and policing as professions with similar demands, involving significant risks, rigorous responsibilities and service to the public.

He said, “Election security should not be seen as the sole responsibility of the police, noting that threats to credible elections extended beyond physical violence to misinformation, fake news and other forms of information disorder capable of discouraging voter participation.”

Disu stressed that accountability must go beyond rhetoric and be demonstrated through practical actions, assuring journalists that the police would not allow themselves to be used as instruments of political oppression.

“Police personnel were being trained to understand media expectations and their responsibilities towards journalists, commissioners of police have also been directed to organise practical training sessions and media parley as part of preparations for the 2027 general elections,” he said.

Meanwhile, the Deputy Ambassador of the Netherlands to Nigeria, Ronald Sonnemans, called for an end to the arrest, harassment and intimidation of journalists, stressing the need to protect press freedom and media independence.

Sonnemans expressed hope that the conference would equip journalists with the skills and practical tools to conduct independent investigations, deliver credible reports and provide citizens with information to make informed decisions.

He also urged journalists to take control of the use of artificial intelligence, advising them to deploy the technology for fact-checking and improving their stories without becoming overly dependent on it.

The envoy advocated independent newsrooms free from restrictive laws and policies capable of undermining their operations and threatening press freedom.

Earlier, the Chief Executive Officer of CJID, Dapo Olorunyomi, described technology as a tool for strengthening journalism rather than an enemy, particularly in the fight against misinformation.

Speaking at the opening of the three-day conference on Monday, Olorunyomi highlighted the contributions of data journalism to exposing misinformation, government misconduct and corruption, but warned that technology without accountability and proper oversight could also pose a threat.

He described technology as democratic infrastructure, stressing the need for accountability in the deployment of artificial intelligence and other digital tools.

Also, Kolly Amina Shettima, who represented the MacArthur Foundation, called for greater protection of journalists in their pursuit of truth, noting that the relationship between journalism and the state might not always be cordial because of the media’s accountability role.

The conference, themed Media, Technology and the Future of Democratic Societies, attracted media practitioners and stakeholders from Nigeria, Mali, Niger and other West African countries.

title: Yuletide: NAPTIP warns schoolchildren against antics of human traffickers
description: The National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons and the International Centre for Migration Policy Development have warned secondary school students in Ogun State against falling victim to human trafficking, particularly during the December festive season, when traffickers are said
content:
The National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons and the International Centre for Migration Policy Development have warned secondary school students in Ogun State against falling victim to human trafficking, particularly during the December festive season, when traffickers are said to intensify efforts to recruit vulnerable children and young people.

The Ogun State Commander of NAPTIP, Bose Jimoh, gave the warning on Tuesday during a sensitisation programme on human trafficking and the inauguration of an Anti-Trafficking and Violence Against Persons Vanguard at St John Anglican Grammar School, Ode Lemo, Ogun State.

The inauguration of the Anti-Trafficking and Violence Against Persons Vanguard across 50 secondary schools in the state is part of the School Anti-Trafficking Education and Advocacy Project of the International Centre for Migration Policy Development, funded by the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

Addressing the students, Jimoh described human trafficking as a serious crime that thrives on deception, exploitation and the vulnerability of unsuspecting victims, particularly school-age children.

She warned that traffickers often disguise their activities as legitimate employment opportunities, educational assistance and promises of better living conditions to lure young people away from their families.

She said the festive season presented an increased risk because unscrupulous individuals often exploited the movement of people and the financial expectations of families to recruit potential victims.

Jimoh cautioned students against accepting suspicious job offers in Lagos, other parts of Nigeria or foreign countries without proper verification.

She said, “This is the peak period. December time is already on ground. So many people will come in the form of friends to come and tell parents that, okay, since your daughter finished school, instead of her staying at home doing nothing, there is work in Lagos or there is work in Mali, so that she can go and work and make money for the family.

“It is deception. That is why human trafficking is defined as the recruitment, transportation, transfer, harbouring and receipt of persons for the purpose of exploitation. Prevention is better than cure.

“People capitalise on the situation in our communities, especially our students, to deceive them within Nigeria or take them from one place to another, from Ogun State to Lagos, Kano or Sokoto, and even from Nigeria to other countries such as Mali, Burkina Faso and Libya.”

The NAPTIP commander said the agency’s experience in Ogun State showed that school-age children, particularly adolescent girls, constituted a significant proportion of the trafficking victims received by the command.

Giving an account of the experiences of some victims, Jimoh said, “Since we came to Ogun State Command, since the command was set up, all the victims of human trafficking we’ve been receiving, the majority of them are school-age children, especially our girls.

“They were taken to Mali, Burkina Faso, Ghana for sexual exploitation. They were made to have sex with as many as 30 men on a daily basis.

“These are not lies. We have all the evidence in our office. Some of them came back with HIV. Some of the cases are already in court to show you the seriousness of the crime of human trafficking.”

She further disclosed that NAPTIP had recently rescued five girls, aged between 15 and 17, who were trafficked to Mali, describing the incident as further evidence that secondary school students were increasingly being targeted by traffickers.

Jimoh urged the newly inaugurated Vanguard members to become advocates of awareness in their schools, churches, communities and families.

Speaking with journalists, Rhoda Dia-Johnson, Project Manager of the School Anti-Trafficking Education and Advocacy Project at ICMPD, Abuja, explained that the decision to target schools was informed by statistics indicating that children of school age constituted a significant proportion of trafficking victims.

Dia-Johnson said NAPTIP records indicated that approximately 54 per cent of trafficking victims were children of school age, while a United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime report put the proportion of trafficking victims who were school-age children in West Africa at over 60 per cent.

According to her, educating students and equipping them with the knowledge to recognise trafficking activities would help prevent exploitation before it occurred.

She disclosed that STEAP was being implemented in five Nigerian states — Ogun, Delta, Benue, Enugu and Edo — with 50 schools selected in each state, bringing the total number of participating schools to 250.

Also speaking, the Ogun State Project Officer of ICMPD coordinating the implementation of STEAP, Samuel Okoroji, disclosed that the Vanguard inauguration at St John Anglican Grammar School was the 45th of the 50 schools selected for the programme in Ogun State.

He said 30 students had been identified and inducted as anti-trafficking champions in each participating school, bringing the total number of inducted students to 1,350.

Okoroji added that more than 60,000 students had so far received sensitisation on human trafficking through the programme.

He described the Vanguard initiative as a major component of STEAP, being implemented by ICMPD and funded by the Kingdom of the Netherlands. He said it was designed to establish a sustainable peer-to-peer advocacy system through which students could educate one another and extend anti-trafficking messages to their communities.

Okoroji particularly hailed the state government for institutionalising the fight against human trafficking across its schools, saying the move would help strengthen the fight against human trafficking in the state.

In her remarks, the Principal of St John Anglican Grammar School, Ode Lemo, Mrs Omonike Adepoju, commended NAPTIP, ICMPD and other stakeholders for extending the anti-trafficking campaign to the school.

She described the establishment of the Anti-Trafficking Vanguard Club as timely, saying it would equip students with the knowledge and skills to identify trafficking risks, resist deceptive offers and educate their peers.

The post Yuletide: NAPTIP warns schoolchildren against antics of human traffickers appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Katsina suspends Emir of Daura’s engagements over assault allegation, launches investigation

content:
By Fauziyya Lawal, Katsina

The Katsina State Government has constituted an investigative committee to probe allegations of sexual assault involving the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Umar Faruk Umar, and a foreign tourist.

The government also announced the suspension of the traditional ruler’s official engagements and travels pending the outcome of the investigation.

The decisions were contained in a statement issued on Tuesday by the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Dr Bala Salisu Zango, on behalf of the state government.

According to the statement, Governor Dikko Umaru Radda expressed serious concern over the allegations, describing the matter as one requiring careful attention and appropriate action.

The governor consequently directed the immediate constitution of an investigative committee to examine the allegations and advise the government on the appropriate course of action.

The statement said the decision was informed by the seriousness of the allegations and the need to establish the facts surrounding the reported incident.

The government assured the public that justice would be served, adding that the findings and recommendations of the committee would be fully implemented.

It said the suspension of the Emir’s official engagements and travels was among the measures taken by the government while the investigation lasted.

The government also appealed to residents and members of the public to remain calm, law-abiding and refrain from actions capable of disrupting public peace.

It urged residents to continue with their normal activities, reaffirming its commitment to handling the matter appropriately.

The outcome of the committee’s investigation is expected to guide further action by the state government.

title: Man Utd win appeal over Yoro red card
description:
Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension for the red card he was shown in Manchester United’s 4-0 mauling by Liverpool has been overturned, the Football Association announced on Tuesday.



The French defender was dismissed in the eighth minute at Anfield for bringing down Alexander Isak as he advanced towa
content:
Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension for the red card he was shown in Manchester United’s 4-0 mauling by Liverpool has been overturned, the Football Association announced on Tuesday.

The French defender was dismissed in the eighth minute at Anfield for bringing down Alexander Isak as he advanced towards goal, with referee Sam Barrott deciding Yoro had denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

United indicated on Monday that they intended to appeal for wrongful dismissal and a one-match suspension for the centre-back has now been lifted.

The FA said the written reasons for their decision would be published in due course.

Yoro, 21, will now be available for Saturday’s 1500 GMT kick-off against Brentford at Old Trafford.

Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool’s opening goal directly from the free-kick awarded for Yoro’s challenge and the home team cantered to an easy win.

One question raised over the Yoro incident was whether Isak had the ball sufficiently under control for it to count as denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

United captain Bruno Fernandes told the BBC after the match that it was “never a red card”, adding: “I think it’s too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR, seated, with such a long time to see and put it back, go forward, put it back, do it in slow motion, whatsoever.

“To make a mistake like this can change a game. But obviously, then, it’s not because of them that we concede the goal from the free-kick, but it changes completely the flow of the game.”

Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United tenure got off to the worst possible start at Anfield, with a defeat that keeps them in the Premier League relegation zone after just one top-flight win all season.
