title: NAFDAC faults Edo committee over drug seizures, business closures
description:
Seeks Okpebholo’s intervention over Arden Table Water



By Chioma Obinna



The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has faulted the Edo State Consumer Protection Committee (ESCPC) over the alleged seizure of pharmaceutical products, closure of business premises and
content:
Seeks Okpebholo’s intervention over Arden Table Water

By Chioma Obinna

The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has faulted the Edo State Consumer Protection Committee (ESCPC) over the alleged seizure of pharmaceutical products, closure of business premises and imposition of fines on operators without proper regulatory authorisation.

The agency also appealed to Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, to intervene in the reported shutdown of Chepfets Mega Investment Nigeria Limited, manufacturer of Arden Table Water, insisting that the product’s registration was undergoing renewal and that this did not establish that it was unsafe or substandard.

The Director-General of NAFDAC, Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye, raised the concerns while clarifying the agency’s position on the committee’s activities in the state.

She expressed concern over reports that the committee had been using NAFDAC’s product authentication platforms to verify regulated products and make public declarations about their authenticity and quality.

Adeyeye explained that access to the agency’s authentication platforms did not automatically confer regulatory authority on users or provide the technical basis for declaring products counterfeit, adulterated, injurious, safe or unsafe.

NAFDAC said it recognised the importance of consumer protection and welcomed collaboration with state governments and other stakeholders in the fight against counterfeit, falsified, adulterated and substandard products.

However, it stressed that such interventions must respect established regulatory boundaries and applicable laws.

The agency said it was particularly concerned by reports that the committee had seized regulated products, publicly labelled some products fake or adulterated, sealed business premises and imposed fines on operators under the guise of working for NAFDAC without its authorisation or guidance.

It also raised concerns over the reported deployment of NAFDAC’s Automated Product Administration and Monitoring System (NAPAMS), QR code scanner, Short Messaging Service (SMS) verification platform and other regulatory tools by the committee to assess products and make public pronouncements on their identity, authenticity, efficacy and effectiveness.

According to the agency, failed QR code scans, missing registration details or inconsistencies in product packaging do not, on their own, constitute sufficient evidence that a product is counterfeit or substandard.

It advised consumers and other stakeholders to report such irregularities to NAFDAC for investigation and possible laboratory analysis, urging the public to await the agency’s findings before making claims about products.

On the reported enforcement activities, NAFDAC condemned what it described as the unilateral seizure of pharmaceutical products, closure of establishments and imposition of fines by the committee.

It maintained that the regulation of drugs, medicines and pharmaceuticals falls under the exclusive legislative jurisdiction of the Federal Government.

The agency said details of seized products, including quantities, estimated value, storage conditions, documentation and circumstances of seizure, should be properly recorded, with impounded regulated products subsequently handed over to NAFDAC.

Arden Table Water registration

Clarifying the status of Arden Table Water, Adeyeye said the product, manufactured by Chepfets Mega Investment Nigeria Limited at 1, Afegbua Street, Ekenwan Road, Benin City, Edo State, was available in sachet and bottled forms.

She explained that the sachet water registration was valid, with registration number D1-3016L, while the bottled water registration, number D1-3065, was undergoing renewal in line with the agency’s NAPAMS procedures.

NAFDAC expressed serious concern that the committee reportedly shut down the company’s operations, imposed a fine and made an arrest without first seeking clarification from the agency on the product’s registration status.

Adeyeye said, “The absence of a status update on the NAPAMS portal provides no basis for concluding that the product is unsafe, ineffective or substandard.”

The agency consequently appealed to Okpebholo to review the reported actions and direct the committee to seek formal clarification from NAFDAC in similar circumstances.

NAFDAC said it had commenced investigations to establish the facts surrounding the developments, including the circumstances of the reported intervention by its Zonal Enforcement Team in Asaba, Delta State, and whether any formal working relationship or authorisation existed between the committee and the agency.

It added that it would engage relevant authorities to clarify the committee’s statutory mandate, particularly regarding products regulated under federal law.

The agency also urged manufacturers with active NAFDAC registration licences to begin renewal processes at least six months before expiration to allow sufficient time for processing.

Adeyeye advised traders, distributors, manufacturers, healthcare providers, pharmacists, doctors and members of the public to report suspected counterfeit, adulterated, fake, unregistered or substandard products through its official helplines: +234(0)700-1-623322 and +234(0)800-1-623322, or via email at reforms@nafdac.gov.ng.

She said complaints could also be submitted through the agency’s online complaints form or at its state offices, adding that the Edo office was located at the Federal Secretariat Complex, Benin-Auchi Road, Aduwawa, Benin City.

NAFDAC reaffirmed its commitment to protecting public health and ensuring that enforcement activities were conducted in accordance with the law and established technical procedures.

It stressed that while consumer protection was a shared responsibility, regulatory accountability must remain clearly defined.

title: 2027: PDP begins Bauchi gov campaign, promises rural development
description:
The Peoples Democratic Party has flagged off its governorship campaign in Bauchi State, unveiling plans to prioritise education, rural development and women’s employment if elected in the 2027 general elections.
Speaking at the campaign flag-off on Tuesday in Bununu, Tafawa Balewa Local Government A
content:
The Peoples Democratic Party has flagged off its governorship campaign in Bauchi State, unveiling plans to prioritise education, rural development and women’s employment if elected in the 2027 general elections.

Speaking at the campaign flag-off on Tuesday in Bununu, Tafawa Balewa Local Government Area, the party’s governorship candidate, Usman Suphi, dismissed claims that the PDP had lost its political relevance in the state, insisting that the party remained a strong political force.

He said, “Whoever said PDP is dead is lying. PDP has been a strong force here and is still maintaining its strength.

“We will campaign with our blueprint in education, rural development and women’s employment. If elected, we will ensure development in our dear state.”

Suphi urged residents to trust the PDP, promising to deliver impactful development and improve the living conditions of the people.

He also thanked party supporters and leaders for their presence and commitment, describing their turnout as a demonstration of confidence in the party’s leadership.

The candidate further expressed optimism about the party’s chances in the 2027 elections, saying he was confident of assuming office on May 29, 2027.

Earlier, the Bauchi State PDP Chairman, Ibrahim Kashim, described Suphi as the most qualified among the governorship contenders, expressing confidence in his capacity to lead the state.

Kashim said the candidate was an honest and modest individual with an unblemished record, adding that he possessed the qualities required to drive the state’s development.

He said, “Suphi is an honest and modest individual with no record of betrayal. He is capable and has all it takes to develop Bauchi State.”

title: NNPC dismisses claims of missing $2.04bn crude oil proceeds
description: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited has denied claims that $2.04bn in crude oil proceeds involving its trading subsidiary, Duke Oil Company Incorporated, now NNPC Trading S.A., is missing, insisting that all transactions under the Direct Sale Direct Purchase programme were fully accounte
content:
The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited has denied claims that $2.04bn in crude oil proceeds involving its trading subsidiary, Duke Oil Company Incorporated, now NNPC Trading S.A., is missing, insisting that all transactions under the Direct Sale Direct Purchase programme were fully accounted for.

The national oil company said the apparent gaps in dollar receipts cited in recent media reports arose from the settlement arrangement under the programme, through which the value of crude supplied was offset against the cost of refined petroleum products delivered to Nigeria.

In a statement issued on Tuesday by its Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odeh, titled ‘Duke Oil Cargoes Are Fully Accounted For’, the company said the $2.04bn represented the gross value of 29 crude cargoes and did not constitute missing or unpaid revenue.

NNPC said the absence of separate dollar payments for the cargoes was consistent with the contractual terms of the DSDP arrangement, under which crude oil was exchanged for refined products.

“NNPC Limited states categorically that no sum is missing, unaccounted for, or unpaid, in respect of crude cargoes lifted by Duke Oil Company Incorporated, now NNPC Trading S.A., under the Direct Sale Direct Purchase programme.

“No separate receipt appears because the crude sale proceeds were set off against the product purchase price, as the contracts provide,” the company stated.

It added that the reports in question acknowledged that the records pointed to reconciliation of transactions within the NNPC Group rather than any financial loss.

Under the DSDP programme, Duke Oil and other participating traders lifted Nigerian crude oil and supplied refined petroleum products, including petrol, for the domestic market.

While crude oil was priced in dollars, the petroleum products supplied were sold in naira. The value of the products delivered was subsequently reconciled against the corresponding crude oil value, with the transactions reflected in the audited financial statements of the relevant entities.

NNPC further argued that the reports had acknowledged that all 59 crude cargoes were accounted for and reconciled with their respective beneficiaries.

Providing a breakdown, the company said 30 cargoes were paid for in dollars, while proceeds from 28 cargoes, valued at approximately `$1.96bn, were remitted in naira into the NNPC Group Treasury or NNPC Upstream Investment Management Services accounts.

It said the remaining cargo, a February 2023 Bonga tax-oil lifting valued at approximately $75.9m, was paid directly into the then-designated dollar account of the Federal Inland Revenue Service.

The company maintained that the transactions were properly documented and that the absence of separate dollar receipts for some cargoes should not be interpreted as evidence of missing funds.

NNPC also defended the role of Duke Oil, following reports describing the company as NNPC operating under another name.

It said Duke Oil was incorporated in 1989 as a wholly owned trading subsidiary of NNPC, adding that its ownership had been disclosed in the national oil company’s corporate history, audited financial statements and the Nigeria Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative’s 2023 industry report.

“Characterising Duke Oil as ‘NNPC wearing another name’ frames a long-disclosed fact as a revelation,” the company said.

It argued that using a dedicated trading subsidiary was standard practice in the international oil industry and that transactions between related companies were disclosed in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards.

The latest clarification comes amid heightened public scrutiny of NNPC’s crude oil sales, domestic petroleum supply arrangements and financial remittances, particularly following the removal of petrol subsidy and the introduction of new arrangements for supplying crude to domestic refineries.

The DSDP programme was introduced to address Nigeria’s domestic fuel supply challenges by exchanging crude oil for refined petroleum products, reducing the immediate need for cash payments for imported petrol.

However, the structure has attracted questions over transparency, the accounting of crude allocations, the value of products supplied and the reconciliation of transactions involving NNPC and its trading partners.

NNPC said it remained committed to transparent financial reporting and accounting for crude oil liftings, product deliveries and payments to beneficiaries.

While acknowledging the importance of responsible journalism and public scrutiny, the company warned against what it described as false and misleading publications capable of damaging its reputation.

It said it reserved the right to pursue legal action against those responsible for such reports.

The post NNPC dismisses claims of missing $2.04bn crude oil proceeds appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Scrap metal regulation won’t hurt legitimate traders – FG
description:
The Federal Government has said its proposed regulation of the scrap metal industry is aimed at curbing the theft and vandalism of public infrastructure without undermining the livelihoods of legitimate collectors, traders and recyclers.
The Minister of Steel Development, Shuaibu Audu, gave the assu
content:
The Federal Government has said its proposed regulation of the scrap metal industry is aimed at curbing the theft and vandalism of public infrastructure without undermining the livelihoods of legitimate collectors, traders and recyclers.

The Minister of Steel Development, Shuaibu Audu, gave the assurance on Tuesday in Kano during a stakeholders’ engagement on the proposed scrap metal regulations.

Represented by the Director of Steel and Non-ferrous Metals Department, Umar Tsoho, the minister, according to a statement issued by the Head, Press and Public Relations Department, Tine-Iulun, M.A., said the government wanted to establish an orderly business environment where legitimate scrap metal collectors, traders and recyclers could operate without providing cover for criminal activities.

He said, “The Federal Government’s intention is not to suppress legitimate commercial activities or undermine the livelihoods of Nigerians engaged in scrap metal collection and trading, but to create an orderly business environment where lawful operators can thrive while criminal activities are effectively addressed.”

The government’s position comes amid persistent concerns over the theft of metallic components from electricity installations, railway facilities, pipelines, manhole covers and other public assets, with the stolen materials often finding their way into the scrap metal market.

The proposed regulations are expected to introduce licensing and supervision of operators, improve the tracking of scrap metal transactions and establish standards for collection centres, aggregation facilities and recycling plants.

Audu described scrap metal as an important resource for Nigeria’s industrial development, particularly the steel, foundry and manufacturing sectors, noting that effective recovery and recycling could create jobs and support a circular economy.

He said Nigeria’s ambition to develop a competitive steel industry depended partly on an organised scrap metal value chain capable of providing reliable supplies of raw materials to legitimate industrial users.

According to him, materials must be lawfully sourced, safely handled, properly documented and supplied through transparent channels to support sustainable industrial production.

The minister, however, warned that an inadequately regulated industry could encourage infrastructure vandalism, unsafe dismantling practices, environmental degradation and significant economic losses.

He said the theft of metallic components from public infrastructure went beyond the loss of materials, as it disrupted essential services, threatened public safety, increased maintenance costs and undermined national development.

“The theft of electrical cables, railway components, manhole covers and other metallic installations goes beyond the loss of materials,” he said, stressing the need to prevent the illicit acquisition and trading of metals belonging to public institutions and protected industrial facilities.

Audu said the proposed framework would also accommodate small-scale operators through practical formalisation arrangements, with requirements proportionate to the size and risks of their businesses.

He explained that while small collectors should not be subjected to unnecessarily burdensome requirements, large-scale aggregation, processing and recycling facilities would be expected to meet appropriate regulatory and operational standards.

The Kano meeting followed the first phase of consultations held in Lagos between November 9 and 10, 2026, where stakeholders examined provisions covering licensing, classification of operators, traceability, collection and sorting facilities, environmental compliance, occupational safety, security and enforcement.

Audu said the Kano engagement was designed to expand consultations and incorporate regional and operational perspectives, particularly the experiences of industry stakeholders in northern Nigeria.

He urged participants to offer practical recommendations that would make the proposed regulations effective and implementable, assuring them that submissions from both meetings would be documented, reviewed and harmonised in line with the applicable legal framework.

The minister reaffirmed the ministry’s readiness to work with government agencies, industry operators, environmental authorities and security organisations to ensure effective implementation of the regulations.

In his remarks, the Permanent Secretary of the ministry, Amb. Nura Abba Rimi, represented by the Director of Metallurgical Inspectorate and Environmental Protection Department, Christopher Wanje, said the consultations were intended to ensure that the proposed framework reflected the realities and legitimate concerns of operators across the country.

He said the regulations would address weaknesses in the scrap metal value chain through licensing, compliance requirements, improved traceability, environmental safeguards and stronger monitoring and enforcement.

Rimi urged stakeholders to make further submissions on licensing arrangements, operator classification, security, environmental protection and inter-agency collaboration.

He assured them that their contributions would be carefully considered to produce a legally sound and practical regulatory framework.

Also speaking, the Acting Executive Secretary of the National Steel Council, Aminu Shehu, represented by the Head of Planning, Research and Statistics, Nana Firdausi Muhammad, expressed the council’s support for the initiative.

He said effective regulation of the industry could promote transparency, create employment and contribute to national economic growth.

Similarly, the Kano State Commandant of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Mohammed Hassan Agalama, who spoke on behalf of the Commandant-General, Prof. Ahmed Abubakar Audi, supported the proposed regulations.

He said proper management of the scrap metal industry was necessary to curb the theft and vandalism of critical national assets, including electricity installations, pipelines, railway facilities and government properties.

Agalama reaffirmed the corps’ readiness to collaborate with the Ministry of Steel Development and other relevant agencies to enforce the proposed framework.

The post Scrap metal regulation won’t hurt legitimate traders – FG appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Omo-Agege rejects court judgment, heads to Appeal Court
description:
Senator Ovie Omo-Agege has directed his legal team to appeal the judgment of the Federal High Court in Warri, Delta State, which nullified his nomination as the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District.







Omo-Agege’s position was contained in a statement
content:
Senator Ovie Omo-Agege has directed his legal team to appeal the judgment of the Federal High Court in Warri, Delta State, which nullified his nomination as the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District.

Omo-Agege’s position was contained in a statement issued on Tuesday by his Media Adviser, Sunny Areh, in reaction to the judgment delivered in a suit filed by Prof. Alexander Osondu Akpodiete challenging his nomination.

The former Deputy President of the Senate described the judgment as disappointing, arguing that some of the court’s findings were inconsistent with the documentary evidence presented during the proceedings.

He, however, said he respected the court but disagreed with its decision, adding that he was confident in the strength of his case on appeal.

One of the major issues raised by Omo-Agege’s camp was the court’s finding that his name was not contained in the NDC membership register submitted to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) at least 21 days before the party’s primaries.

According to the statement, both the NDC and INEC produced documents showing that his name appeared in the membership register submitted by the party.

It maintained that the party submitted only one register and did not maintain competing membership records for the same primary election.

The statement further claimed that INEC acknowledged receipt of the register and issued Certified True Copies (CTCs) of the document, bearing Omo-Agege’s name, to several persons.

It questioned the basis for the trial court’s finding, arguing that the documentary evidence presented by both the party and INEC confirmed his inclusion in the register.

The senator’s camp also challenged the plaintiff’s legal standing to institute the suit, arguing that Akpodiete did not obtain nomination forms, was not cleared by the party to contest and was not listed among the participants in INEC’s official monitoring report on the primaries.

It argued that these circumstances raised questions about whether the plaintiff had established sufficient legal interest to challenge the outcome of a primary in which he did not participate.

The statement also noted that Akpodiete did not ask the court to declare him the winner of the primary or award him the party’s ticket but instead sought to invalidate Omo-Agege’s nomination.

It further alleged that attempts had been made before the judgment to persuade INEC to remove Omo-Agege’s name from its final list of candidates, but the commission declined, having confirmed his inclusion in the membership register submitted by the party.

Describing the documents as official records rather than political assertions, Omo-Agege’s camp said they should be examined in their proper context during the appeal.

It maintained that the senator’s decision to challenge the judgment should not be interpreted as an attack on the judiciary or a rejection of the rule of law.

The statement urged those celebrating the judgment as the end of Omo-Agege’s political ambition to exercise patience, noting that the decision remained subject to appellate review.

It added that Omo-Agege remained committed to the NDC and the people of Delta Central, insisting that he would continue to pursue his political rights through lawful means.

“We believe in the rule of law, but we also believe that justice must be anchored in facts and evidence. We will appeal this judgment and pursue that appeal with determination,” the statement said.

The post Omo-Agege rejects court judgment, heads to Appeal Court appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Court freezes Governors’ Forum account over $100m debt, restrains 29 banks
description:
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri



ABUJA –A Federal Capital Territory (FCT) High Court in Abuja has issued an interim order freezing all accounts operated by the Nigerian Governors’ Forum (NGF), following an alleged failure to release the sum of $100 million that was paid in by the Federal Government.
content:
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

ABUJA –A Federal Capital Territory (FCT) High Court in Abuja has issued an interim order freezing all accounts operated by the Nigerian Governors’ Forum (NGF), following an alleged failure to release the sum of $100 million that was paid in by the Federal Government.

In an ex-parte order, Justice Charles Agbaza granted an interim Mareva injunction restraining the Incorporated Trustees of the NGF from withdrawing, transferring or dissipating the funds.

It further restrained 29 commercial banks from releasing, transferring, converting or otherwise dealing with funds belonging to the NGF that are in their custody.

The ruling followed a legal action relating to the Paris Club refunds, which were payments for over-deductions made from the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) for external debt servicing between 1995 and 2002.

The court had affirmed that the claimant, Dr. Ted Iseghohi-Edwards, rendered legal services in connection with the London and Paris Club refunds owed to Nigeria’s 774 Local Government Areas.

He subsequently secured a judgment in respect of those services, which remains unsatisfied.

Justice Agbaza directed the listed banks to disclose, within 48 hours of being served with the order, whether the NGF maintains accounts containing the said funds.

The banks are required to identify such accounts, their currencies, available balances and the amounts preserved under the court’s order.

The amount represents $100 million, equivalent to N135.55 billion at an exchange rate of N1,355.80 to the dollar.

The orders, dated November 19, were made after the court heard an application moved by the claimant’s counsel, Emonye Adekwu, SAN, and Damilola Odesola.

The claimant approached the court seeking recovery of the judgment debt, pursuant to an indemnity he said was issued by the NGF on December 20, 2018.

The indemnity reportedly arose from an arrangement under which the Federal Government paid $100 million to the NGF as stakeholder.

The claimant had sued the FG over non-payment of his consultancy fees relating to the Paris Club refunds.

In suit number FHC/ABJ/CS/856/2016, the Federal High Court in Abuja, on February 16, 2018, delivered judgment establishing the government’s indebtedness of $318 million.

The claimant said the government subsequently made a part-payment of $159 million through promissory notes.

He contended that the judgment fulfilled the condition contained in the NGF’s indemnity, thereby making the $100 million payable directly to him.

Iseghohi-Edwards said he formally demanded payment from the NGF in a letter dated October 8, 2026, but the forum allegedly failed to honour the undertaking.

Consequently, he approached the FCT High Court, seeking to preserve the money pending the determination of his substantive claim.

In the application, he expressed apprehension that the NGF might transfer, disburse or dissipate the funds, thereby frustrating enforcement of any eventual judgment.

He also told the court that he could not identify the specific bank accounts holding the funds without judicial intervention.

The claimant argued that the injunction was necessary to preserve the subject matter of the dispute and prevent the proceedings from becoming futile.

He maintained that the restriction was limited to one aggregate sum of $100 million across the NGF and all participating banks.

The application was brought pursuant to Orders 30(3) and 32(1) of the FCT High Court Civil Procedure Rules and the court’s inherent jurisdiction.

The claimant also undertook to abide by any order for damages should the court subsequently determine that the interim injunction ought not to have been granted.

Justice Agbaza adjourned the matter until December 1 and ordered service of the order on all the respondents.

The Incorporated Trustees of the Nigerian Governors’ Forum is listed as the 1st respondent in the suit, while 29 banks are joined as co-respondents.

The post Court freezes Governors’ Forum account over $100m debt, restrains 29 banks appeared first on Vanguard News.

By Luminous Jannamike



ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has pledged to revive the Ajaokuta Steel Mill, develop Idah River Port and complete the Kabba-Egbe road, promising to address longstanding infrastructure challenges across Kogi State.



Speaking at his campaign rally in Lokoja, A
content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has pledged to revive the Ajaokuta Steel Mill, develop Idah River Port and complete the Kabba-Egbe road, promising to address longstanding infrastructure challenges across Kogi State.

Speaking at his campaign rally in Lokoja, Atiku outlined development projects for the state’s three senatorial districts, including improved roads and water supply in Kogi East. He said the plans were aimed at creating jobs, expanding economic opportunities and making life more affordable for residents.

According to the Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku said his proposed interventions would focus on turning the state’s economic potential into tangible benefits for its people.

Addressing residents of Kogi East, he pledged to improve rural infrastructure and develop Idah River Port to ease the movement of agricultural produce and expand business opportunities.

“To my brothers and sisters in Kogi East, I know what it means when a farmer cannot get produce to market because the road has failed, or when a family must struggle every day for clean water. We will improve your roads and water supply, and develop Idah River Port so that the region’s farmers and businesses can reach more customers,” he said.

For Kogi Central, Atiku promised to revive the Ajaokuta Steel Mill, with a focus on restoring industrial production and creating employment.

“Ajaokuta must finally become a working steel mill. I want its furnaces working, its gates open to skilled workers and its promise felt in the homes of the people who have waited so long. We will also support the roads and services that allow surrounding communities to benefit from that industry,” he said.

In Kogi West, he pledged to complete the Kabba-Egbe road, which he said should no longer remain an unfulfilled promise.

“The Kabba to Egbe road cannot remain an endless promise. We will complete it and make travel and trade easier for the communities along its route,” he stated.

At the national level, Atiku also pledged to pursue the dredging of Baro Port and restore a targeted subsidy on fuel refined in Nigeria, saying the measures would help reduce transportation and production costs.

The proposals formed part of his broader promise to translate infrastructure development and the state’s economic resources into employment and improved living conditions.

title: APC mourns 15 supporters killed in Zamfara road accident
description:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) has mourned 15 of its members and supporters killed in a road accident in Zamfara State on Monday, November 23.







The party also expressed sympathy with the families of the deceased and prayed for the recovery of 27 others who sustained injuries in the crash.
content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) has mourned 15 of its members and supporters killed in a road accident in Zamfara State on Monday, November 23.

The party also expressed sympathy with the families of the deceased and prayed for the recovery of 27 others who sustained injuries in the crash.

The victims were reportedly travelling from Gummi Local Government Area to Talata Mafara to attend the APC presidential and governorship campaign flag off when the accident occurred.

In a statement posted on its official X account on Tuesday and signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, the party described the incident as a tragic loss to the APC family.

The statement read, “The All Progressives Congress (APC) has received, with profound sadness, the news of the tragic road accident in Zamfara State, which reportedly claimed the lives of 15 members and supporters of our great Party, while several others sustained injuries.”

The party extended its condolences to Zamfara State Governor Dauda Lawal, the bereaved families, the state government and members of the party.

It also commended the decision to postpone the campaign rally scheduled for Tuesday in Maru Local Government Area in honour of those who died.

The accident occurred around 12:30pm near Kisami village along the Gummi-Daki-Takwas-Anka road.

According to a Federal Road Safety Corps report, the crash involved a Toyota Camry and a Mitsubishi Canter truck. A total of 52 people were involved, comprising 50 men and two women.

The FRSC recorded 15 deaths, all male, while 27 men sustained injuries. Eight men and two women escaped unhurt. The injured victims and bodies of the deceased were taken to General Hospital, Gummi.

The corps identified wrongful overtaking and loss of control as suspected causes of the accident.

The Zamfara State Government also expressed condolences to the affected families and suspended its scheduled campaign activities in Maru following the tragedy.

The state APC Presidential and Gubernatorial Campaign Council had earlier announced the postponement of the rally, saying a revised campaign timetable would be communicated later.

The accident occurred on the day the APC held its presidential and governorship campaign flag off in Talata Mafara, attended by Governor Lawal and other party leaders.

The post APC mourns 15 supporters killed in Zamfara road accident appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Atiku has youth support despite Tinubu’s control of Lagos, says Momodu
description:
By Adegboyega Adeleye



African Democratic Congress (ADC) chieftain Dele Momodu has defended former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s appeal to young voters, saying Atiku has never controlled a state while President Bola Tinubu exercises strong political influence in Lagos.



Momodu spoke in an inte
content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

African Democratic Congress (ADC) chieftain Dele Momodu has defended former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s appeal to young voters, saying Atiku has never controlled a state while President Bola Tinubu exercises strong political influence in Lagos.

Momodu spoke in an interview on Arise Television on Tuesday, discussing Atiku’s chances in the 2027 election, age dynamics, political influence and efforts by opposition parties to agree on a consensus candidate.

“If he’s not connecting to the youths, you won’t see people shouting ‘Bamayi’ all over Nigeria. I just watched your programme now in Kogi State. The people on the streets are not geriatrics; they are young people,” he said.

The ADC chieftain argued that age should not be used to judge a candidate’s ability to connect with voters. Citing his own presidential bid, he said: “I contested 15 years ago, at the age of 51 to be president of Nigeria. Why didn’t I win? It’s not about age.”

He said Atiku was surrounded by young supporters and described him as “a completely detribalised Nigerian” and “an employer of labour.” Comparing Atiku’s political influence with Tinubu’s, Momodu said, “He has never held on to any state. Tinubu controls Lagos, life and death. Tinubu controls Lagos and Atiku does not control anywhere.”

On talks to select a consensus opposition candidate, Momodu pointed to Atiku’s past willingness to step aside for another candidate.

“In 1993, I was 33 years old when Alhaji Atiku Abubakar first came out to run as a potential candidate of SDP, and at that time, he stepped down for MKO Abiola without making any trouble. After that, he was expected to be the running mate, he didn’t get it. He never fought anybody. He then contested in his state and became governor before they now made him running mate to President Olusegun Obasanjo. He has pursued his dreams with uncommon equanimity,” he said.

title: Why I criticise Atiku but don’t insult Obi, others – Shettima
description:
Vice President Kashim Shettima on Tuesday justified his persistent criticism of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar while insisting he refrains from insulting other opposition figures such as Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, Peter Obi and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso.
Shettima said he only res
content:
Vice President Kashim Shettima on Tuesday justified his persistent criticism of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar while insisting he refrains from insulting other opposition figures such as Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, Peter Obi and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso.

Shettima said he only responds when President Bola Tinubu is attacked.

He maintained that his relationship with Atiku, whom he described as an elder statesman, was different because they were both Fulani, adding that he had the right to criticise him.

The Vice-President spoke on Tuesday in Maiduguri, Borno State, at the presidential launch and inauguration of the North-East Development Commission’s multi-sectoral development interventions.

Speaking about Atiku, Shettima said, “He is an elder statesman whom we hold in very high esteem. But as a Fulani man, I have the right to throw stones at him, and he has to endure whatever stones I throw at him.

“So, some idiots without any sense of history will come out and say, ‘Oh, he was a Vice President.’ Keep your Fulani banter.”

He also cautioned against attempts to portray political disagreements as personal hostility, saying he was willing to maintain cordial relationships with opposition figures as long as they did not attack his principal.

“So long as they do not attack my boss, we will practise  politics of maturity, politics without bitterness, and politics of tolerance because what binds us together surpasses whatever that divides us,” he said.

He, however, said he had never insulted Obi, Makinde or Kwankwaso, describing them as friends.

“Peter Obi is my friend. We were governors together. I have never insulted the governor of Oyo State. He is my personal friend. The same goes for the former governor of Kano State, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso.

“Have you ever heard me, Hajiya Laba, insult Kwankwaso? I will not insult him. But whoever attacks our boss, we will attack him too,” he said.

Shettima also recalled that his disagreement with former President Goodluck Jonathan was partly connected to his support for former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi.

“Part of the problem I had with former President Goodluck Ebele Jonathan had to do with my support for Rotimi Amaechi during the race for the chairmanship of the Nigeria Governors’ Forum. Rotimi Amaechi is my friend,” he said.

He said he would continue to promote mature politics, tolerance and peaceful political engagement, provided those involved did not attack Tinubu.

“As long as they do not attack our boss, we will practise politics of maturity, politics without bitterness and politics of tolerance because what binds us together is greater than whatever divides us,” he said.

The Vice-President urged members of the All Progressives Congress to support the party’s candidates, while insisting that political leaders should work together rather than engage in rivalry.

He also called on Nigerians to support Tinubu, saying the President deserved another term in office.

“There has to be a president of Nigeria at any given time, and, by the grace of God and with the support of the Nigerian people, January 16, Nigerians will massively vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said.

Shettima added that social media activity should not be mistaken for electoral support, saying votes were cast at polling units, not online.

“Since we don’t have polling booths on the internet, there are no polling booths on Facebook or Instagram. These young ladies can go to Instagram and post beautiful pictures, but there are no polling units on Instagram,” he said.

On the NEDC interventions, Shettima described the promotion of electric mobility as both an environmental and economic necessity, noting that the North-East had significant solar energy potential.

“E-mobility is not only an environmental combination, but also an economic imperative. It’s absolutely essential that we support the usage of alternative sources of power and energy in the North-East. The North-East is one part of the country highly endowed with solar potentials,” he said.

He commended the commission for its projects, including 10,000 electric tricycles, 300 electric buses and taxis, and 50-megawatt mini-grids across the region.

“On behalf of President Bola, I want to commend the management and staff of NEDC for this far-reaching initiative. Beyond the 10,000 electric tricycles and 300 electric buses and taxis, they are also embarking on 50 megawatts mini-grids across the nooks and crannies of the North-East. They have built over 1,000 solar-powered boreholes, roads, bridges,” he said.

Shettima also identified poverty as a major factor behind insecurity and other challenges in the North, including ethno-religious crises, Boko Haram insurgency and armed banditry.

“In Nigeria, poverty wears a northern face. We are in the news for the wrong reasons. Ethno-religious crisis, Boko Haram, armed banditry, and behind all this insanity lies the real cause, which is extreme poverty,” he said.

He commended Borno Governor Babagana Zulum and other governors in the region for investing in education, describing it as the greatest driver of change.

The Vice-President also praised Gombe State Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for what he described as his development-oriented leadership.

He called for unity among political leaders, saying the Federal Government and state governments should work together to address the challenges facing the country.

Shettima further defended Tinubu’s economic policies, saying the President inherited a difficult economic situation but had avoided insulting his predecessor, late former President Muhammadu Buhari.

He said the President believed he had to inherit both the assets and liabilities of the previous administration, adding that insulting Buhari was one of the quickest ways to incur Tinubu’s displeasure.

The post Why I criticise Atiku but don’t insult Obi, others – Shettima appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Senate orders scrutiny of revised 2025 laws before approval
description:
The Senate has ordered a thorough examination of the revised and consolidated Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2025 before approving the document, warning that any alteration of laws passed by the National Assembly could undermine the country’s legal system.
The decision followed a letter from Pres
content:
The Senate has ordered a thorough examination of the revised and consolidated Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2025 before approving the document, warning that any alteration of laws passed by the National Assembly could undermine the country’s legal system.

The decision followed a letter from President Bola Tinubu seeking the National Assembly’s approval of the revised compendium, which contains updated federal laws and subsidiary legislation.

Reading the letter at Tuesday’s plenary, Senate President Godswill Akpabio said lawmakers must ensure that all amendments made by the National Assembly were accurately reflected in the revised document.

He said the exercise would involve comparing the consolidated laws with the original versions passed by both chambers to prevent errors or unauthorised changes.

In his letter, Tinubu disclosed that a committee constituted on October 24, 2024, examined 932 federal enactments and 731 subsidiary legislations.

He said 664 principal enactments were validated for inclusion in the revised compendium, while 268 were identified as obsolete, spent or repealed.

According to the President, the updated laws would provide a reliable legal reference for the judiciary, legal practitioners, government institutions, investors and the general public.

The Senate subsequently referred the document to its Committees on Rules and Business and Judiciary for further legislative consideration.

Contributing to the debate, former Senate Leader, Senator Yahaya Abdullahi, described the exercise as important to the administration of justice and the country’s legal system.

The Kebbi North senator recalled that a similar exercise was undertaken after the return to democratic rule in 1999 to give legal backing to decrees enacted during military administrations.

He said the last official consolidation of the laws was carried out in 2004, making the current review necessary after more than two decades.

Abdullahi, however, warned against rushing the process, given its implications for the justice system.

He urged the Senate Committee on Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters to work with legal experts to examine the volumes and submit a comprehensive report before approval.

Also speaking, Deputy Senate President, Jibrin Barau, supported the call for proper scrutiny, warning that even a single altered provision could make the revised document inconsistent with the laws passed by the National Assembly.

The Kano North senator said the consolidated laws should be compared with the original versions passed by both chambers and those assented to by the President.

Akpabio agreed with the lawmakers, saying the National Assembly would involve consultants and legal experts in the verification process.

He said, “The Senate usually engages consultants and relevant experts to examine such documents before presenting a summarised report.

“I am directing that the leadership and management of the National Assembly be involved in the verification exercise to ensure accuracy.”

The post Senate orders scrutiny of revised 2025 laws before approval appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NDC Boycotts IGP’s Meeting Over Alleged Attacks On Members
description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has announced its decision to boycott a security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, citing alleged attacks on its members and what it described as the police’s failure to protect opposition figures.The party said it no longer felt safe un
content:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has announced its decision to boycott a security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, citing alleged attacks on its members and what it described as the police’s failure to protect opposition figures.

The party said it no longer felt safe under the Nigeria Police Force, accusing security agencies of failing to prevent repeated attacks on its members allegedly carried out by thugs loyal to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

The NDC announced its position in a statement signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, on Monday.

It said it would not legitimise a security process that had failed to protect its members, adding that the alleged violence had become an intolerable pattern across the country.

The party cited incidents in Benue, Edo, Calabar, Enugu and Delta states, including an alleged attempt by APC loyalists to prevent its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, from entering Benue State.

It accused the APC-led government of turning political campaigns into battlefields, where the safety of opposition members could no longer be guaranteed.

The NDC also alleged that security personnel were complicit in the violence, particularly the alleged attack on the campaign team of its Delta Central senatorial candidate, Ovie Omo-Agege, in Delta State.

Gunmen reportedly attacked Omo-Agege’s campaign convoy in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area.

The former deputy senate president escaped unhurt, according to his media adviser, Sunny Areh.

The attack initially left four campaign members dead, according to the Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation.

However, the Nigeria Police Force said preliminary reports indicated that six people were killed, while several others sustained injuries.

Police Speak

The police, in a statement issued on Tuesday by its Force Public Relations Officer, said an investigation had been launched to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack and determine the verified casualty figure.

Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, directed the Delta State Commissioner of Police to conduct a thorough, impartial and evidence-based investigation.

The police said the investigation would examine the sequence of events, identify those responsible and establish the circumstances surrounding the shooting, including the deployment and conduct of officers at the scene.

It added that any officer found to have acted negligently or breached professional standards would face disciplinary action, while anyone found culpable of criminal offences would be prosecuted.

The NDC, however, accused the police of displaying bias and failing to investigate previous attacks on its members or bring those responsible to justice.

It called on the international community to prevail on President Bola Tinubu and the APC-led government to uphold internationally accepted democratic standards.

“Democracy cannot survive where opposition members are hunted, attacked, and killed with impunity while state institutions look the other way,” it said.

The NDC maintained that it remained committed to peaceful and issue-based campaigns but would not be intimidated or forced out of the democratic space.

Meanwhile, the Delta State Government has imposed a daily curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area from 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. until further notice following the attack.

The police also said security deployment, patrols and intelligence-led operations had also been intensified to prevent further violence and restore normalcy.

title: CAS explains decision to restore Senegal’s AFCON title
description:
By Ayobami Okerinde



The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has explained why it overturned the Confederation of African Football’s (CAF) decision to award Morocco the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title, ruling that Senegal’s 1-0 victory in the final must stand.



In a media release on Tuesday, t
content:
By Ayobami Okerinde

The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has explained why it overturned the Confederation of African Football’s (CAF) decision to award Morocco the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title, ruling that Senegal’s 1-0 victory in the final must stand.

In a media release on Tuesday, the court said both teams had returned to the pitch and expressed their willingness to continue before the referee, Jean-Jacques Ndala, blew his whistle to resume play in the 109th minute.

It explained that the referee’s decision to restart or stop the match fell within his authority, adding that the effects of his decision were limited to the pitch and therefore covered by the ‘field of play’ doctrine.

“After having examined the arguments raised by the Parties, the Arbitral Panel considered that the Referee’s decision to resume the match or to stop it fell definitively within his sole authority. By blowing his whistle to restart play, the Referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met – both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume,” the statement said.

CAS also ruled that Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, relied upon by Morocco in its challenge, did not apply to the circumstances of the final. According to the court, the provisions are intended to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to abandon the game permanently.

The court further rejected the description of the referee’s decision as ‘arbitrary’, acknowledging the extreme tension surrounding the match but stating that his judgment did not appear to have been influenced by external factors.

Consequently, CAS upheld the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF), set aside the CAF Appeal Board’s decision and reinstated the decision of CAF’s Disciplinary Board.

The ruling confirms Senegal’s 1-0 victory over Morocco in the January 18 final, restoring the West African nation as AFCON 2025 champions.

CAF had previously declared Senegal to have forfeited the final after the team temporarily left the pitch in protest during the match, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory.

The decision was unanimous among the three-member CAS panel.

The post CAS explains decision to restore Senegal’s AFCON title appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: How CAS Overturned CAF’s Decision And Restored Senegal’s AFCON Title
description: Gambiaj.com – (LAUSANNE, SWITZERLAND) – The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has overturned the Confederation of African Football (CAF) Appeals Board decision that stripped Senegal of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title and awarded it to Morocco, ruling that the referee’s decision to resume the
content:
Gambiaj.com – (LAUSANNE, SWITZERLAND) – The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has overturned the Confederation of African Football (CAF) Appeals Board decision that stripped Senegal of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title and awarded it to Morocco, ruling that the referee’s decision to resume the final was decisive in determining its outcome.

In a unanimous verdict, the Lausanne-based tribunal found that referee Jean-Jacques Ngambo Ndala had acted within his authority when he restarted the match after Senegal’s players temporarily left the pitch. It concluded that his decision fell under the “field of play doctrine” and could not subsequently be overturned by CAF on the basis of forfeiture provisions relating to permanently abandoned matches.

The ruling offers an important distinction between two issues that had become central to the dispute: Senegal’s responsibility for its players’ conduct during the final and the authority of the referee to determine whether the match should continue or be abandoned.

It was this distinction that ultimately shaped the tribunal’s reasoning and provided the legal basis for restoring Senegal’s title.

The Legal Battle: Referee’s Authority Versus Forfeiture Rules

The dispute originated from the controversial final, during which Senegal’s players temporarily walked off the pitch before returning to complete the match.

CAF initially accepted the sporting outcome of the final, but on 17 March 2026, its Appeals Board overturned that result, declared Senegal defeated by forfeit, and awarded the trophy to Morocco.

The Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) subsequently appealed to CAS, arguing that the referee’s decision to resume play in the 109th minute (90+19) was a sporting decision protected by the field of play doctrine.

This principle generally prevents judicial and disciplinary bodies from revisiting decisions made by referees in the course of a match, particularly where those decisions concern the application of the laws of the game.

Morocco’s Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) challenged that interpretation. It argued that the dispute was not simply about a refereeing decision but about the disciplinary consequences of Senegal’s conduct.

The Moroccan federation maintained that Senegal had breached Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations by leaving the pitch and that the referee should have abandoned the match. It further argued that allowing play to resume amounted to an error of law and an arbitrary exercise of authority.

The central question before CAS was therefore whether the referee’s decision to restart the final could be reviewed retrospectively by CAF’s Appeals Board.

Why The Referee’s Decision Became Decisive

CAS’s reasoning rested primarily on the circumstances surrounding the resumption of play.

After examining the arguments presented by both federations, the arbitration panel concluded that deciding whether to resume a match or stop it permanently fell within the referee’s discretion.

The tribunal attached particular importance to the fact that both teams had returned to the pitch and demonstrated their willingness to continue playing.

By signalling the resumption of the match, Ngambo Ndala had effectively determined that the conditions for continuing the game had been met.

For CAS, this was not a minor procedural decision. It was the exercise of the referee’s authority over the conduct of the match.

The panel consequently determined that the effects of his decision were confined to the field of play, bringing it within the protection of the field of play doctrine.

This finding undermined the foundation of CAF’s decision. If the referee’s decision to resume the match was protected from retrospective review, CAF could not subsequently treat the same incident as grounds for declaring that the match should have ended in a forfeit.

In effect, CAS placed the authority exercised by the referee during the match above the subsequent attempt by CAF’s Appeals Board to change its sporting outcome.

Why Articles 82 And 84 Did Not Apply

Another important element of the ruling concerned the interpretation of Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations.

Morocco had relied on these provisions to argue that Senegal’s conduct should have resulted in an automatic forfeiture.

However, CAS interpreted the articles as applying to situations in which the behaviour of a team leads the referee to establish that a match has been permanently abandoned.

That distinction was crucial.

The tribunal reasoned that the provisions were intended to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct causes the referee to stop it definitively. They were not applicable where the referee had decided to resume play and allow the contest to reach its sporting conclusion.

Since Ngambo Ndala had restarted the final, CAS found no legal basis for applying those forfeiture provisions retrospectively.

The tribunal therefore concluded that the referee had committed no error of law.

This was arguably the strongest element of Senegal’s case: the regulations invoked by Morocco could not be applied independently of what the referee had actually decided during the match.

CAS Rejects The Argument Of Arbitrary Refereeing

The panel also considered Morocco’s argument that the referee’s decision was arbitrary.

CAS acknowledged that Ngambo Ndala had been operating under extremely tense circumstances. However, it found that the difficult atmosphere surrounding the final did not, in itself, establish that his decision was arbitrary.

More importantly, the tribunal found no indication that his judgement had been influenced by factors external to the game.

This finding reinforced the application of the field of play doctrine. Had CAS established that the referee’s decision was arbitrary or influenced by external considerations, the argument for protecting it from review might have been more difficult to sustain.

Instead, the panel concluded that the referee had exercised his judgment in circumstances that did not invalidate his decision.

Disciplinary Responsibility Was Not the Same as Sporting Forfeiture

Perhaps the most significant distinction in the ruling was CAS’s treatment of the disciplinary consequences of Senegal’s walk-off.

The tribunal did not suggest that Senegal’s conduct was acceptable or that the players and officials were exempt from disciplinary responsibility.

Rather, it noted that the FSF, head coach Pape Thiaw and some players had already been sanctioned by CAF through separate disciplinary proceedings.

This allowed CAS to distinguish between punishing misconduct and changing the result of a completed match.

In the tribunal’s reasoning, disciplinary sanctions could address Senegal’s conduct without necessarily requiring the retrospective annulment of the sporting result.

This distinction was central to the outcome. Morocco’s argument sought to connect Senegal’s temporary departure from the pitch directly to forfeiture, while CAS considered that the disciplinary dimension had already been addressed separately.

The tribunal therefore found no justification for using the same incident to overturn the result of a match that the referee had allowed to continue.

A Defeat For CAF’s Interpretation Of Its Own Regulations

The ruling is also a significant setback for CAF’s Appeals Board, whose decision to award the title to Morocco was effectively overturned because the tribunal rejected its interpretation and application of the forfeiture provisions.

The case raises questions about the relationship between refereeing authority, competition regulations, and the powers of football governing bodies to intervene after a match has ended.

At the center of CAS’s reasoning was the principle that a governing body’s disciplinary authority does not automatically extend to reversing sporting decisions that fall within the referee’s jurisdiction.

Senegal’s victory, therefore, was not based on a finding that the walk-off did not happen or that the team had no disciplinary responsibility. It rested on the legal consequences of the referee’s decision to restart the game.

By unanimously admitting the FSF’s appeal, CAS overturned the CAF Appeals Board decision and restored the sporting outcome of the final in Senegal’s favor.

The broader significance of the ruling lies in the boundary it draws between disciplinary accountability and the integrity of decisions made on the field: a team may still face sanctions for misconduct, but that misconduct does not automatically entitle a governing body to rewrite a match result when the referee has exercised his authority to allow the game to continue.

title: Tinubu gets Reps’ approval to borrow $7.7bn for 2026 budget
description:

The approval was granted during Tuesday’s plenary after lawmakers considered a report presented by Sada Soli o
content:
The House of Representatives has approved President Bola Tinubu’s request for a supplementary external borrowing plan worth $20.52 billion and €1.04 billion for the 2026–2027 fiscal period.

The approval was granted during Tuesday’s plenary after lawmakers considered a report presented by Sada Soli on behalf of Abubakar Nalaraba, chairman of the House Committee on Aids, Loans and Debt Management.

As part of the resolution, the lawmakers approved Tinubu’s request to borrow N10.790 trillion, equivalent to approximately $7.707 billion at an exchange rate of N1,409 to the dollar.

The proposed borrowing is expected to help finance part of the Federal Government’s 2026 budget.

The house further authorised the federal government to raise the approved funds through one or more of the financing sources outlined in the president’s request, including concessional and commercial financing windows of multilateral and bilateral institutions, the International Monetary Fund (IMF), bridge financing facilities, loan syndication, and Eurobond issuance.

The lawmakers stipulated that the government must prioritise financing arrangements with the most favourable terms and conditions.

As part of measures to ensure accountability, the house directed the federal government, through the Debt Management Office (DMO), to submit periodic reports to the national assembly detailing concluded financing arrangements.

The reports are expected to include the amounts borrowed, sources of financing, interest rates, repayment periods, associated fees and other relevant loan conditions.

The lawmakers mandated the committee on local and foreign debts to maintain continuous oversight of the borrowing programme, including monitoring financing arrangements, actual drawdowns, utilisation of proceeds and compliance with the terms and conditions approved by the national assembly.

In a letter dated November 5, 2025, and addressed to Tajudeen Abbas, speaker of the house, Tinubu said the new external borrowings are required to implement the items, programmes, and projects in the 2026 Appropriation Act, which are designed to stabilise and strengthen the macroeconomic reforms and gains recorded by the administration in the past few years.

“The key projects in priority sectors, such as defence and security, transport, agriculture, power, education and health, in the budget will receive attention,” Tinubu said.

“It is also important to add that the proceeds will increase the accretions to the external reserves since they will be received by the Central Bank of Nigeria on behalf of the FGN and thereby support the naira exchange rate’.

Tinubu has also asked the national assembly to repeal and re-enact the 2026 Appropriation Act.

The president is proposing to reduce the total 2026 aggregate budget expenditure from N68.323 trillion to N65.176 trillion.

title: Senate approves Tinubu’s $20.5bn, €1.45bn external borrowing plan
description:
The Senate has approved President Bola Tinubu’s request for a supplementary external borrowing plan of $20.517 billion and €1.45 billion to finance government projects and other commitments in 2026 and 2027.
The approval was given at Tuesday’s plenary after the consideration of a report by the Senat
content:
The Senate has approved President Bola Tinubu’s request for a supplementary external borrowing plan of $20.517 billion and €1.45 billion to finance government projects and other commitments in 2026 and 2027.

The approval was given at Tuesday’s plenary after the consideration of a report by the Senate Committee on Local and Foreign Loans.

The House of Representatives had earlier approved the borrowing plan, paving the way for its endorsement by both chambers of the National Assembly.

The Senate’s approval came a few hours after Tinubu sought legislative approval for a revised 2026 budget, reducing the previously approved expenditure by more than N3tn.

The President’s letter, titled ‘Transmission of FGN 2026 Appropriation Repeal and Re-enactment Bill and Revised 2026 Federal Government Fiscal Framework,’ was read by Senate President Godswill Akpabio.

Akpabio subsequently referred it to the Senate Committee on Rules and Business for consideration.

Under the revised fiscal framework, total expenditure is projected at N65.176 trillion, down from the N68.323 trillion earlier approved by the National Assembly.

The Federal Government’s projected revenue, including earnings from government-owned enterprises, stands at N33.720tn, while capital expenditure is set at N26.232tn.

Despite the reduction in expenditure, the fiscal deficit remains unchanged at N31.457tn, representing 5.64 per cent of the country’s Gross Domestic Product.

The proposed borrowing of N29.218tn also remains unchanged, comprising N18.428tn in domestic loans and N10.790tn in external borrowing.

Tinubu said the proposed $7.7bn external loan, estimated at N10.368tn, would finance an existing foreign borrowing provision and would not increase the overall borrowing limit.

He said, “The adjustments are intended to prioritise existing commitments, strengthen the credibility of the budget and improve capital budget implementation while maintaining fiscal discipline.”

The President is expected to present the 2027 budget to the National Assembly before the end of December.

title: Osun father tortures son to death over N75,000, phone
description:
The Osun State Police Command on Tuesday said it had arrested a 48-year-old man, Kayode Ogunniran, in connection with the alleged murder of his son, identified as Raphael.
In a statement on Tuesday, the command’s Public Relations Officer, Abiodun Ojelabi, said the remains of the deceased were discov
content:
The Osun State Police Command on Tuesday said it had arrested a 48-year-old man, Kayode Ogunniran, in connection with the alleged murder of his son, identified as Raphael.

In a statement on Tuesday, the command’s Public Relations Officer, Abiodun Ojelabi, said the remains of the deceased were discovered in a shallow grave behind Ogunniran’s residence in Faji, Osun State.

The command said operatives from its Intelligence Department received information that the suspect had tortured Raphael, said to be about 21 years old, to death and buried his corpse in a shallow grave behind their residence.

It said that upon receipt of the information, detectives swung into action and the suspect was apprehended.

“During interrogation, he stated that his son stole a sum of N75,000 and absconded with an Android phone he bought for him on EasyBuy to an unknown place.

“As a member of Iru-Ekun Security Network, Ogunniran was able to get the son arrested through the help of his colleague. The case was transferred to the Homicide Section for further investigation.

“Upon receipt of the case, detectives from the Homicide Section visited the crime scene and the shallow grave where the body was buried. “During the course of investigation, pictorial and video evidence were retrieved, showing how the deceased was tied up on both legs and hands before he was later tortured to death by his father,” the statement read.

The police added that the suspect admitted killing the deceased.

Commenting on the case, the state Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Zungura, warned individuals and groups involved in criminal activities to desist or be prepared to face the full weight of the law.

Zungura, who declared that the police had a duty to protect lives and property, encouraged residents to continue providing timely and credible information to the command to support crime prevention and prompt response to security threats.

The incident comes days after the command disclosed the arrest of suspects over the alleged sale of a 16-day-old baby for N1.5m in the state.

title: Bayelsa tragedy: Senate demands nationwide audit of boats, ferries
description:
The Senate has called for an urgent nationwide audit of boats and ferries operating on Nigeria’s waterways following the death of 29 people in a boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.
The lawmakers blamed the November 20 disaster on overloading and poor safety standar
content:
The Senate has called for an urgent nationwide audit of boats and ferries operating on Nigeria’s waterways following the death of 29 people in a boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.

The lawmakers blamed the November 20 disaster on overloading and poor safety standards, urging the Nigerian Inland Waterways Authority and other regulatory agencies to strengthen inspections and enforce safety regulations to prevent further accidents.

The resolutions followed a motion moved on Tuesday by Senator Benson Konbowei, representing Bayelsa Central, who described the incident as shocking and unfortunate.

Leading the debate, Konbowei said the ill-fated boat was carrying more than 300 passengers, far above its capacity, before its weak structure reportedly broke apart and capsized.

He said, “The boat had more than 300 passengers on board, which was more than its old and weak frame could comfortably carry, and it broke apart, capsized and threw the passengers into the river.”

The lawmaker disclosed that 29 bodies had been recovered, while divers and other rescue workers were still searching for missing passengers.

“After recovering 29 dead bodies so far, divers and other rescue and recovery workers are still combing the river beds in search of corpses,” he said.

He added that several survivors had been taken to hospitals across the state for treatment.

Konbowei said the accident highlighted the dangers of relying on poorly regulated water transportation, particularly in Bayelsa, where inadequate road networks had made boats the major means of transportation for many communities.

He called on the Federal Government to support critical road projects, particularly the proposed Yenagoa-Oporoma Road, which he said was recommended in the 1958 Willink Commission Report.

The senator commended Governor Douye Diri for his response to the disaster and President Bola Tinubu for sending Vice-President Kashim Shettima to the state.

Shettima had announced a donation of N250m to support the state government’s disaster management efforts and affected families.

Seconding the motion, Senator Simon Lalong, representing Plateau South, commended the state and Federal Governments for their response.

“We watched him [Diri] on television. I also commend the response of the Federal Government and particularly the visit of the Vice President to Bayelsa State that gave a lot of relief to some of those people that were affected,” he said.

Lalong, however, urged Nigerians to take water transportation safety seriously, particularly in communities where travelling by boat was unavoidable.

“We are always lamenting. This is a natural gift from God, water, but we must be very, very careful,” Lalong stated.

Also contributing, the Deputy Senate President, Barau Jibrin, urged regulatory agencies to conduct routine inspections of boats and ferries to ensure compliance with safety standards.

He said the country must move beyond expressing condolences after accidents and take practical steps to prevent their recurrence.

“It’s really sad, really sad, but what can one do when God has decided on what should happen? And once it happens, the only thing we can do is to look at ways to prevent the occurrence of such a situation in the future,” he said.

Barau said regular inspections would help identify unserviceable vessels and prevent overloading.

“I think if that was the case, if there were routine checks, I’m sure this kind of calamity will not be occurring at the rate they are occurring in our country,” he said.

He added, “We are not indicting them, but the fact is that they should do more in ensuring that things are done the way they should be done in terms of ensuring that regulations that guide the waterway transportation system are really adhered to.”

Similarly, Senator Sunday Marshall Katung, representing Kaduna South, called for a comprehensive investigation into the accident, saying it exposed weaknesses in the country’s water transportation regulatory system.

He said, “There are gaps in the regulatory framework that have given rise to situations such as this, and I want to urge that the relevant committee of the Senate needs to step in and conduct investigations.”

Katung also demanded an audit of all vessels operating in the country’s territorial waters to establish their condition and suitability for carrying passengers.

“The relevant authorities should step in quickly and ensure that there is an audit of all vessels that are operating within our territorial waters to ensure that they are fit and worthy of operating, particularly as they carry passengers,” he stated.

In his remarks, the Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, commended Tinubu for his response to the tragedy, saying the President had demonstrated concern for the welfare of Nigerians.

“I just want to personally commend the President for swiftly empathising with the people, showing compassion and also showing that he cares for the well-being of Nigerians and not just the politics of the country,” he said.

Akpabio also disclosed that a political rally had been cut short following news of the accident because the country was mourning the victims.

“Since we were already at the rally, there was no point cancelling it. We just went in, greeted the people and walked away because, as far as we were concerned at that moment, the nation was in mourning. There was no point continuing with the rally,” he stated.

The Senate President urged rescue teams to continue searching for missing passengers, particularly in the difficult-to-access mangrove areas of Bayelsa.

“We pray for the safe recovery of those who probably are still in the waters because they could swim and they are trying to get to safer areas. I hope that the rescue operation should still continue because some may still be within the mangrove swamps of Bayelsa and are not dead and waiting to be rescued,” he said.

Akpabio also blamed the accident on overloading, insisting that boat operators must observe approved passenger limits.

“This clearly was as a result of overloading, and if we do not carry overload and we restrict to the capacity of the boat, this would never have happened,” he said.

The Senate unanimously adopted seven prayers contained in the motion, including observing a minute’s silence for the victims and commending the Federal and Bayelsa State Governments for their interventions.

The lawmakers also urged the Federal Government to support the construction of the Yenagoa-Oporoma Road and other critical roads in the state to provide safer alternatives to water transportation.

They further called on NIWA and other regulatory agencies to enforce safety standards, while the National Emergency Management Agency was urged to provide relief materials and other assistance to survivors and affected families.

The chamber subsequently observed a minute’s silence in honour of those who died in the accident.

The post Bayelsa tragedy: Senate demands nationwide audit of boats, ferries appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
