title: ASUP declares two-week strike in four states over unpaid allowances
description:
Accuses Enugu govt of neglecting lecturers’ welfare since 2014



By Chinedu Adonu



The Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics (ASUP), Zone D, has directed its chapters in Enugu, Imo, Edo and Cross River states to embark on a two-week warning strike over the failure of the respective state governmen
content:
Accuses Enugu govt of neglecting lecturers’ welfare since 2014

By Chinedu Adonu

The Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics (ASUP), Zone D, has directed its chapters in Enugu, Imo, Edo and Cross River states to embark on a two-week warning strike over the failure of the respective state governments to implement the 2026 renegotiated agreement between the union and the Federal Government.

The union also directed chapters that have yet to join the ongoing industrial action to commence the strike immediately, warning that failure to address its demands could result in an indefinite shutdown of academic activities in the affected institutions.

ASUP Zone D, which covers the South-East and South-South geopolitical zones, announced the directive at a press briefing in Enugu on Tuesday by its Zonal Coordinator, Comrade Dr Iloma U. Richard.

The union said the strike followed the failure of the affected state governments to implement the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance (CATA), Earned Academic Allowance (EAA) and other components of the ASUP/FGN 2026 renegotiated agreement.

It recalled that the Federal Government and ASUP signed the agreement on April 8, 2026, with implementation of the allowances taking effect from January 2026.

According to the union, while the Federal Government has commenced implementation of the agreement for lecturers in federal polytechnics, several state governments have failed to extend the benefits to academic staff in their institutions.

It said its national leadership had written to state governors on August 10 and September 21, 2026, appealing for the implementation of the allowances but received disappointing responses from some states.

The union said the National Executive Council, at its 118th regular meeting held on October 22 in Abuja, subsequently issued a 15-day ultimatum to the affected state governments, beginning October 27, to address the matter.

“Having exhaustively explored measures to persuade concerned states to comply, the national leadership was constrained to direct all chapters in the states that were yet to comply to proceed on strike with effect from November 12, 2026,” the union said.

ASUP, however, noted that some states had responded positively, listing Yobe, Kano, Ondo, Bayelsa, Niger, Abia, Taraba, Plateau, Nasarawa, Zamfara, Jigawa and Rivers as states that had approved the implementation of CATA and EAA.

It added that engagements with Delta, Akwa Ibom and Katsina states were also progressing positively.

Enugu lecturers’ welfare

Beyond the allowances, the union expressed particular concern over what it described as years of neglect of academic staff welfare in Enugu State-owned institutions, particularly the Institute of Management and Technology (IMT), Enugu, and Enugu State Polytechnic, Iwollo.

It alleged that lecturers in the two institutions were yet to benefit from the prevailing minimum wage, wage awards and the 35 per cent and 25 per cent salary reviews approved in 2023.

The union also complained about outstanding arrears arising from the CONTISS 15 migration since 2014, the non-establishment of a pension scheme at Enugu State Polytechnic, Iwollo, and the failure to harmonise pension benefits from CONTISS to COMPCASS at IMT, Enugu.

It further alleged that academic staff at Enugu State Polytechnic, Iwollo, had not been promoted since 2015.

“This development is pathetic as the compensation package for academic staff in these two institutions remains one of the worst in the entire country,” it said.

ASUP also accused successive administrations at IMT of victimising its officials, claiming that some members of the immediate past Chapter Executive Council had been denied certain benefits for more than eight years because of their positions on staff welfare.

The union’s demands include the implementation of CATA and EAA with effect from January 2026; payment of outstanding wage review and minimum wage benefits; appropriate placement arising from the CONTISS 15 migration; establishment of an acceptable pension scheme for lecturers at Enugu State Polytechnic; and reversal of what it described as anti-union policies in Enugu State-owned polytechnics.

The union said its National Executive Council would meet on December 2, 2026, to review the level of compliance by the affected states and determine further action.

It urged the concerned governments to commence meaningful negotiations and address the outstanding welfare issues to avert an indefinite shutdown of academic activities.

“We therefore urge the affected states to enter meaningful engagements with our union with a view to commencing the payment of appropriate compensation packages so as to avert an indefinite shutdown of academic activities in the concerned institutions,” the statement added.

The union ended its statement with its traditional slogan: “Aluta Continua; Victoria Acerta.”

title: Bayelsa boat accident: Reps demand safer boats, compulsory life jackets
description:
The House of Representatives has called for the provision of safer boats, compulsory use of life jackets and stricter enforcement of water transportation safety standards in riverine communities following a boat accident in Bayelsa State that claimed 29 lives, including two children.
The lawmakers a
content:
The House of Representatives has called for the provision of safer boats, compulsory use of life jackets and stricter enforcement of water transportation safety standards in riverine communities following a boat accident in Bayelsa State that claimed 29 lives, including two children.

The lawmakers also urged the Federal Government to intensify rescue operations, provide relief materials to affected communities and introduce subsidised modern boats to reduce the risks associated with water transportation.

The resolutions followed a motion of urgent public importance moved by Rodney Ambaiowei, representing Southern Ijaw Federal Constituency, during plenary on Tuesday.

Moving the motion, Ambaiowei said more than 150 people, mostly indigenes of Southern Ijaw, were involved in the accident on November 20, 2026, while travelling from Ayama community to Ukubie for a condolence visit.

He said the boat capsized at the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan, throwing all its occupants into the water.

According to the lawmaker, rescue operations began immediately, with the Bayelsa State Government, security personnel and other relevant agencies joining efforts to save the victims.

As of November 22, he said, 51 people had been rescued alive with varying degrees of injuries and discomfort, while 29 others, including two children, had been confirmed dead.

The rescued victims were taken to medical facilities in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area and government hospitals in Yenagoa for treatment, while search operations continued for missing persons and possible survivors.

Ambaiowei expressed concern over the number of people still unaccounted for, warning that the scale of the tragedy required a more extensive search and rescue operation.

He said the accident had plunged families and residents of Southern Ijaw, particularly Ukubie and neighbouring communities, into mourning.

The lawmaker attributed the vulnerability of riverine communities to the poor condition of boats used for transportation, noting that many vessels were old, overworked and frequently overloaded because of their scarcity.

He also lamented the widespread absence of life jackets, floaters and other water safety equipment, as well as the failure to enforce their use, despite waterways being the major means of transportation in the constituency.

Ambaiowei noted that many communities had limited access to motorable roads, leaving residents heavily dependent on waterways for their daily movement, despite ongoing road construction projects by the Bayelsa State Government.

He warned that failure by the National Emergency Management Agency and other relevant bodies to intensify rescue operations and provide relief materials could worsen the hardship facing affected families.

The lawmaker added that fishing, which provides food and income for many residents, had also been disrupted by the tragedy.

He commended President Bola Tinubu for sending Vice-President Kashim Shettima to the affected communities to sympathise with bereaved families, noting that the Federal Government had also donated ₦250m to the victims.

Contributing to the motion, lawmakers called for a broader review of water transportation in riverine communities, arguing that government interventions had largely focused on road transportation at the expense of people who depend on waterways.

The House Minority Leader, Fred Agbedi, said the tragedy had exposed the difficulties faced by riverine communities and called for the introduction of subsidised modern boats, similar to the Federal Government’s intervention in road transportation through Compressed Natural Gas buses.

“Mr Speaker, this incident brings to the fore what people in riverine communities are suffering. I think it is an opportunity for us to address these challenges.

“I am aware that the Federal Government is providing CNG buses, which are more economical. But whenever we talk about mass transit, there is no provision for river craft.

“In this century, people are still using dugout boats with weak roofs that could collapse on passengers. If the government provides modern vessels for transportation at subsidised rates, as it does with mass transit and CNG buses, I am sure incidents like this could be prevented,” he said.

Agbedi described the motion as an opportunity to address the longstanding neglect of riverine communities, insisting that federal transportation policies should also accommodate people living in areas with little or no access to roads.

He urged the Federal Government to include modern boats in its transportation interventions and future budgetary provisions to make travel to remote riverine communities safer and more affordable.

On his part, Shina Oyedeji urged the government to stop paying lip service to safety standards, describing the accident as a wake-up call for authorities to strengthen the regulation of transportation operations.

He questioned the training and certification of boat operators and called for proper inspection of vessels and other transport facilities.

“I think this is an opportunity for us as a nation to start doing things the right way.

“The time to stop playing games is now. The government meant well by introducing CNG buses to make transportation cheaper, but the implementation must be properly regulated to ensure safety.

“Many of these drivers and operators, I do not know who trained them or who certified them. When was the last time their certifications were reviewed?” he said.

Oyedeji warned against adopting practices from other countries without establishing and enforcing appropriate standards to reflect Nigeria’s circumstances.

He urged the House committee responsible for safety standards to examine the matter and ensure that relevant regulations were properly enforced.

“Safety standards must be taken seriously in Nigeria,” he added.

The Deputy Majority Whip, Isiaka Ibrahim, said responsibility for safety on inland waterways rested with both federal and state governments, noting that creeks and offshore waters were on the concurrent legislative list.

He called for an investigation into the accident and urged lawmakers to examine the safety standards observed by boat operators, particularly in comparison with multinational companies operating in Nigeria’s offshore waters.

Ibrahim said the safety measures adopted by multinational companies operating in offshore waters should serve as a reference for improving safety practices in the country’s creeks.

He cautioned against relying on swimming ability as a substitute for basic safety precautions, particularly the use of life jackets.

“I know how to swim. I have been swimming for 40 years. But you do not know the condition of the boat, the water, its depth or what may have happened to the boat.

“We ignore life vests and life jackets, and then we talk about accidents. This motion should provide an opportunity to learn from what has happened and address the causes,” he said.

However, the House Leader, Prof. Julius Ihonvbere, argued that while federal intervention was important, communities, maritime associations, local governments and state authorities must also be held accountable for safety failures.

He said television footage of the accident showed passengers boarding boats without life jackets, describing the practice as unacceptable and calling for tougher penalties against those who violated safety regulations.

“Mr Speaker, I think our aim should be to extend the leadership’s deep sympathies to the people of Bayelsa over this unfortunate incident.

“But this is not an issue for the Federal Government alone. We must look at the grassroots, including community associations, maritime associations, local government councils, state governments and the relevant agencies.

“Even as we watched reports on television, we saw people boarding boats and canoes without life vests. How does somebody get on a boat without a life vest?” he asked.

Ihonvbere insisted that familiarity with waterways or swimming experience should not be an excuse for disregarding safety requirements.

He also questioned the responsibility for inspecting watercraft, describing the condition of some boats operating in riverine communities as unacceptable.

The House Leader called for stronger enforcement at jetties and other boarding points, warning that recurring accidents would continue unless authorities and community-level institutions took responsibility.

He said penalties and enforcement were necessary to ensure compliance with safety regulations, adding that the responsibility for preventing such incidents should not rest solely on the Federal Government.

The House unanimously adopted the motion and mandated its Committee on Emergency and Disaster Management to work with NEMA and the Bayelsa State Government to investigate the immediate and remote causes of the accident and recommend measures to prevent future occurrences.

It also urged NEMA, the Niger Delta Development Commission, the Nigerian Inland Waterways Authority and the South-South Development Agency to provide additional relief materials to affected communities to cushion the impact of the tragedy and the loss of livelihoods.

The lawmakers further called for the urgent provision of safer boats, life jackets, floaters and other water transportation safety equipment to riverine communities, with measures to ensure their compulsory use.

title: Full List: 10 countries with most AFCON titles
description:
Egypt remain the most successful country in the history of the Africa Cup of Nations, AFCON with seven titles, followed by Cameroon and Ghana, who have won the continental competition five and four times respectively.







Nigeria are among five countries in the top four positions, having lifted t
content:
Egypt remain the most successful country in the history of the Africa Cup of Nations, AFCON with seven titles, followed by Cameroon and Ghana, who have won the continental competition five and four times respectively.

Nigeria are among five countries in the top four positions, having lifted the trophy three times since making their debut at the tournament.

The Super Eagles won their first AFCON title in 1980, when Nigeria hosted the competition and defeated Algeria 3-0 in the final. They secured their second crown in Tunisia in 1994, beating Zambia 2-1, before claiming their third title in South Africa in 2013 with a 1-0 victory over Burkina Faso.

Côte d’Ivoire are also three-time champions, having won the tournament in 1992, 2015 and 2023.

Egypt lead the all-time standings with seven titles, having dominated the competition in its early years and later enjoyed a remarkable run of three consecutive championships in 2006, 2008 and 2010.

Cameroon occupy second place with five titles, while Ghana are third with four. Ghana’s last triumph came in 1982, while Cameroon’s most recent success was in 2017.

Algeria and the Democratic Republic of the Congo have each won the competition twice. Algeria claimed their titles in 1990 and 2019, while DR Congo won in 1968 and 1974, when the country competed under the names Congo-Kinshasa and Zaire.

Morocco are also credited with two titles, following the Confederation of African Football’s March 2026 decision to award them the 2025 AFCON trophy. Senegal had initially won the final 1-0 after extra time, but CAF’s Appeal Board later ruled that the Senegalese team had forfeited the match and recorded a 3-0 victory for Morocco.

Senegal subsequently appealed the decision to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, which was expected to issue its ruling on November 24, 2026. The outcome of that appeal could affect the official title record.

Seven other countries have won the AFCON title once. They are Ethiopia, Sudan, Congo, South Africa, Tunisia, Zambia and Senegal.

Below is the ranking of countries by the number of AFCON titles won:

  1. Egypt – 7 titles: 1957, 1959, 1986, 1998, 2006, 2008 and 2010.
  2. Cameroon – 5 titles: 1984, 1988, 2000, 2002 and 2017.
  3. Ghana – 4 titles: 1963, 1965, 1978 and 1982.
  4. Nigeria – 3 titles: 1980, 1994 and 2013.
  5. Côte d’Ivoire – 3 titles: 1992, 2015 and 2023.
  6. Algeria – 2 titles: 1990 and 2019.
  7. DR Congo – 2 titles: 1968 and 1974
  8. Senegal – 2 titles: 2021, 2025
  9. Ethiopia – 1 title: 1962.
  10. Sudan – 1 title: 1970.
  11. Congo – 1 title: 1972.
  12. South Africa – 1 title: 1996.
  13. Tunisia – 1 title: 2004.
  14. Zambia – 1 title: 2012.
  15. Morocco – 1 title: 1976

title: Kwankwasiyya challenges Yusuf to prove alleged APC pact
description:
The Kwankwasiyya movement has challenged Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, to provide credible evidence of an alleged agreement with Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso to defect to the All Progressives Congress (APC).







Yusuf had claimed in an interview with the BBC Hausa Service that Kwankwaso, the vice-p
content:
The Kwankwasiyya movement has challenged Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, to provide credible evidence of an alleged agreement with Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso to defect to the All Progressives Congress (APC).

Yusuf had claimed in an interview with the BBC Hausa Service that Kwankwaso, the vice-presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), made him swear an oath on the Quran to join the APC if President Bola Tinubu did not interfere in the 2023 Kano governorship election tribunal case.

The governor also alleged that he and Kwankwaso had an understanding with Tinubu that they would return to the APC if the President did not interfere in the legal proceedings.

Yusuf said Kwankwaso reneged on the agreement despite having made him swear on the Quran.

The governor defected from the New Nigeria People’s Party (NNPP) to the APC in January 2026, citing what he described as deepening internal crises and prolonged leadership disputes within the party.

His defection reportedly strained his relationship with Kwankwaso, his former political leader, who played a prominent role in his emergence as governor.

Reacting in a statement on Monday, spokesperson of the Kwankwasiyya movement, Habibu Sale Mohammed, described the allegation of an oath-taking agreement as an attempt by Yusuf to shift responsibility for his political decisions to Kwankwaso.

Mohammed said the governor was entitled to explain his decision to defect but had no right to make sweeping allegations against another person without providing credible evidence.

He said the movement’s tradition was to consult widely with stakeholders, elected representatives and party leaders before taking major political decisions.

“If Governor Abba Yusuf insists that such an agreement existed, we challenge him to provide specific and verifiable details. When exactly was this agreement reached? Who were the participants?” the statement asked.

The spokesperson also sought clarification on the alleged discussions involving Tinubu and the 2023 election petition.

“The Governor also needs to explain the implications of his claim that President Tinubu was approached and asked not to interfere in the legal proceedings challenging the 2023 Kano governorship election.

“The Supreme Court eventually determined that dispute and affirmed his election. Nigerians deserve clarity on what precisely was discussed, without creating an impression that the judicial process was subject to a political bargain,” the statement said.

The movement also questioned why an alleged agreement dating back to 2023 was being presented as the principal justification for Yusuf’s defection in January 2026.

It asked why the governor had not publicly explained the alleged understanding when he left the NNPP, rather than presenting it as a retrospective justification.

“Let us make one thing clear: Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso is not responsible for Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf’s decision to defect to the APC,” Mohammed said.

He urged Yusuf to defend his decision on its own merits and explain the benefits the people of Kano State stood to gain from his defection, rather than transferring responsibility to another political leader.

title: 2027: Atiku promises cheaper fuel, stronger purchasing power
description:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress has vowed to restore fuel subsidy and improve the purchasing power of the Naira.
Atiku also promised to strengthen local production of goods within the country.

content:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress has vowed to restore fuel subsidy and improve the purchasing power of the Naira.

Atiku also promised to strengthen local production of goods within the country.

The ADC presidential candidate stated this on Tuesday during his campaign rally in Kogi State, according to a statement issued by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu.

The statement is titled ‘Atiku storms Kogi with Affordable Life message as mammoth crowd chants Tinubu Must Go.’

Atiku stated that his ‘Affordable Life campaign’ is targeted at families and people who can no longer afford to buy food items at costly prices and the high cost of transportation.

He said, “When we say we will make life affordable again, we are speaking to the parents counting the last notes in a purse and the worker calculating whether a salary will last until month’s end.

“They came here in their numbers because they want to be heard. Their hardship is real, and their hope deserves an answer.”

The statement noted that the former VP “said his Affordable Life campaign is a promise to those families: to bring down the cost of fuel, help Nigerians produce and sell their goods, and restore the value of what people earn.”

Atiku stated further that the people of Kogi can not “endure pain with no end in sight” as they chanted “Tinubu Must Go.”

“The people of Kogi are chanting ‘Tinubu Must Go’ because they are tired of being told to endure pain with no end in sight. I hear them. I see the faces in this crowd, and I know what is at stake. No family should have to beg for the chance to live with dignity in its own country.

“A mother should not have to choose between feeding her children and paying their school fees. A trader should not open a shop each morning wondering whether anyone can afford to buy. A young person should not work hard all day and still struggle to pay for the journey home. These are the lives behind the figures this government recites,’ the ADC presidential candidate said.

He thanked the people of the state for the welcome, as he urged supporters to keep maintaining peace.

“Let no one mistake your restraint for acceptance of hardship. Let your voices be heard, and let your votes decide Nigeria’s future,” he urged.

The 2027 campaign has been underway for some weeks now as presidential candidates continue to take their promises and manifestos to selected states nationwide.

Atiku is seeking the presidency for the fourth time as a candidate in a general election, having previously contested in 2007, 2019 and 2023.

His running mate is former Rivers State Governor, Rotimi Amaechi.

Another top opposition challenging President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress is Peter Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Cingress.

The post 2027: Atiku promises cheaper fuel, stronger purchasing power appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: CAS overturns CAF decision, declares Senegal 2025 AFCON champions
description:
The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has ruled in favour of Senegal in the dispute over the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) final, confirming the Teranga Lions as champions.
In its ruling on Tuesday, the Switzerland-based tribunal overturned the earlier decision by the Confederation of Africa
content:
The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has ruled in favour of Senegal in the dispute over the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) final, confirming the Teranga Lions as champions.

In its ruling on Tuesday, the Switzerland-based tribunal overturned the earlier decision by the Confederation of African Football (CAF), which had awarded the trophy to Morocco.

CAS upheld Senegal’s appeal through “a unanimous decision”, restoring the team’s original 1-0 victory over Morocco after extra time.

“After having examined the arguments raised by the Parties, the Arbitral Panel considered that the Referee’s decision to resume the match or to stop it fell definitively within his sole authority. By blowing his whistle to restart play, the Referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met – both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume,” the CAS ruling reads.

“In the Panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee’s decision were limited to the pitch. As such, the Panel considers that the Referee’s decision was covered by the ‘field of play’ doctrine. Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case. In conclusion, the Panel considers that in resuming the match, the Referee did not err in law.

“The Panel acknowledged that the Referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension. However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as “arbitrary”. On the contrary, the Referee’s judgment did not appear to have been affected by factors external to the game.”

The post CAS overturns CAF decision, declares Senegal 2025 AFCON champions appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Four Edo security personnel arrested for aiding cultists
description:
Four personnel of the Edo State Security Corps have been arrested for allegedly leaking information on police movements to suspected cultists in the Adolor area of Benin City.
The four suspects, Isaac Iruvwe, Gideon Acher, Tony Oahiale and Culture Uzo, were arrested while police operatives were on t
content:
Four personnel of the Edo State Security Corps have been arrested for allegedly leaking information on police movements to suspected cultists in the Adolor area of Benin City.

The four suspects, Isaac Iruvwe, Gideon Acher, Tony Oahiale and Culture Uzo, were arrested while police operatives were on the trail of some suspected cultists.

The spokesperson for the Edo Police Command, Eno Ikoedem, said in a statement on Tuesday that police operatives were surprised that their movements and actions had been leaked.

Ikoedem, who spoke at the parade of some suspects arrested for various crimes, said an investigation led to the arrest of the four security personnel.

She said a separate operation led to the arrest of 10 suspected members of the Aye cult group during an alleged initiation exercise.

Other suspects paraded were four suspected kidnappers and a suspected armed robber at Ugiokhuen Community.

She said the four suspected kidnappers were arrested after two victims, Yakubu Ibrahim and Abdullahi Mohammed, were rescued unhurt during an intensive bush-combing operation at Ikakumoh/Ayaran Forest.

According to her, “Four personnel of the Edo State Security Corps were arrested for allegedly leaking information on police movements to suspected cultists in the Adolor area of Benin City.

“Others were also arrested for other crimes which include kidnapping, cultism and armed robbery.

“These arrests underscore the command’s determination to sustain pressure on criminal elements and ensure the safety of residents.

“The Commissioner of Police, CP Patrick Daaor, reiterates the command’s resolve to dismantle criminal networks and bring perpetrators to justice. He commends the officers involved for their courage and professionalism, and appreciates members of the public for their timely information and continued support.

“Residents are urged to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious activities, as the security of Edo State remains a collective responsibility.”

The post Four Edo security personnel arrested for aiding cultists appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: I’ll continue to criticise Atiku for attacking Tinubu – Shettima
description:
By Ayobami Okerinde



Vice-President Kashim Shettima has defended his right to criticise African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, saying he would not hold back in defending President Bola Tinubu against political attacks.



Shettima, who described Atiku as an elder
content:
By Ayobami Okerinde

Vice-President Kashim Shettima has defended his right to criticise African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, saying he would not hold back in defending President Bola Tinubu against political attacks.

Shettima, who described Atiku as an elder statesman whom he holds in high regard, said their political differences would not prevent him from expressing his views about the former vice-president.

He spoke on Tuesday in Maiduguri, Borno State’s capital, during the inauguration of the North-East Development Commission’s multi-sectoral development interventions.

“We respect former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. He is an elder statesman we hold in very high esteem, but as a Fulani man, I have the right to throw stones at him. And he has to endure strictly whatever stones I throw at him,” he said.

The vice president also cautioned against attempts to portray political disagreements as personal hostility, saying he was willing to maintain cordial relationships with opposition figures as long as they did not attack his principal.

“So long as they do not attack my boss, we will practise politics of maturity, politics without bitterness, and politics of tolerance because what binds us together surpasses whatever that divides us,” he said.

Shettima also identified former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi and former Kano State Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso as his friends, while describing Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde as a personal friend.

He said he had never insulted Makinde, adding that political differences should not undermine relationships among leaders.

The vice-president urged Nigerians to make informed decisions ahead of the 2027 presidential election, arguing that the Tinubu administration’s economic policies were beginning to yield results.

Shettima also ruled out a return to petrol subsidy, saying its removal and the realignment of multiple exchange rates were necessary to prevent the economy from collapsing.

“The president has a great deal of human empathy for the Nigerian people. He withdrew the subsidy, not to inflict pain on Nigerians. No, he removed the subsidy to save the Nigerian economy from collapse,” he said.

He further accused some Nigerians who had benefited from the previous economic arrangements of sponsoring anti-government sentiments.

Calling for restraint among political actors, Shettima urged candidates to accept the outcome of the 2027 election rather than resort to threats and actions capable of creating tension.

He expressed confidence that Nigerians would vote massively for Tinubu on January 16, adding that there were no polling booths on Facebook, Instagram or other social media platforms.

title: UK police arrest two over break-in at Prince William’s home
description:
Two men have been arrested on suspicion of burglary, police said Tuesday, after a reported break-in at the rural country retreat of UK royals Prince William and his wife Catherine.
Police dogs, drones and a helicopter were deployed to the remote Sandringham estate in eastern England after receiving
content:
Two men have been arrested on suspicion of burglary, police said Tuesday, after a reported break-in at the rural country retreat of UK royals Prince William and his wife Catherine.

Police dogs, drones and a helicopter were deployed to the remote Sandringham estate in eastern England after receiving a call just before 6:00 pm (1800GMT) on Monday of suspicious activity, Norfolk police said in a statement sent to AFP.

Anmer Hall, where William and Kate, and their three children, occasionally live — especially during the school holidays — was broken into, according to UK media.

The men “were arrested on the estate on suspicion of burglary and trespass” at the estate owned by King Charles, police said.

The property involved “was unoccupied” at the time, they added.

William and Kate mainly live at their home on the Windsor Estate, just west of London.

Kensington Palace, which handles the affairs of William, the heir-to-throne, did not immediately reply to AFP’s request for comment.

This is not the first time a royal residence has been broken into.

In 2024, several intruders were caught on the Windsor estate after they broke into a farm building and tried to steal a pick-up truck and a quad bike.

The most famous incident was in July 1982 when a man, Michael Fagan, sneaked into Buckingham Palace and made his way to Queen Elizabeth II’s bedroom.

He sat on her four-poster bed and had a 10-minute chat with her before being taken away by security. He was initially charged, but then the charges were dropped.

News of Monday’s break-in broke just as William made his first visit to Downing Street on Tuesday, where he talked about “shared priorities” with Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

The meeting was seen as another step towards the heir to the throne’s future role as monarch.

AFP

title: Osun declares November 27 public holiday for Adeleke’s second-term inauguration
description:
The Osun State Government has declared Friday, November 27, a public holiday to allow residents to participate in the inauguration of Governor Ademola Adeleke for a second term in office.
The announcement was made in a circular issued by the state Ministry of Home Affairs and sighted by Very Nigeria
content:
The Osun State Government has declared Friday, November 27, a public holiday to allow residents to participate in the inauguration of Governor Ademola Adeleke for a second term in office.

The announcement was made in a circular issued by the state Ministry of Home Affairs and sighted by Very Nigerian on Tuesday.

The public holiday is intended to give residents the opportunity to attend and participate in activities marking the governor’s second-term inauguration.

“In view of the significance of this event, His Excellency has graciously approved that Friday, 27 November, 2026 be observed as a Public Holiday throughout the State to enable the good people of Osun State and well-wishers to participate in the Inauguration Ceremony,” the circular stated.

It directed all public offices, schools and other public institutions in the state to observe the holiday, except those providing essential services.

“All Public Offices, Schools and other public institutions in the state are hereby directed to observe the holiday except those on essential services who are to maintain their normal duties,” it added.

Very Nigerian had earlier reported that the inauguration would hold at the Osogbo Township Stadium, with President Bola Tinubu, governors in the South-West, diplomats and other dignitaries invited to the ceremony.
Adeleke was declared winner of the August 15, 2026, governorship election by the Independent National Electoral Commission, defeating the All Progressives Congress candidate, Bola Oyebamiji.

The governor, who contested under the Accord Party, polled 511,067 votes against Oyebamiji’s 444,815 votes to secure a second term.

Ahead of the inauguration, Adeleke assured residents that he would not disappoint them and promised to do more during his second term.

He gave the assurance in a statement issued by his spokesperson, Olawale Rasheed, after Jumu’at prayers at the Osogbo Central Mosque on November 20, where activities marking the inauguration began.

“I won’t disappoint Osun people. I will deliver even more than my first term. I am hopeful our financial situation will soon improve with the expected resolution of the local government crisis. We will take good care of workers and all segments of the society,” the governor said.

The post Osun declares November 27 public holiday for Adeleke’s second-term inauguration appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Northerners in South move to convert presence into economic power
description:
By Steve Oko











Northerners resident in the 17 states of Southern Nigeria have taken a major step to organise their economic activities, strengthen business networks and convert their widespread commercial presence into greater economic influence and development opportunities



This was dis
content:
By Steve Oko

Northerners resident in the 17 states of Southern Nigeria have taken a major step to organise their economic activities, strengthen business networks and convert their widespread commercial presence into greater economic influence and development opportunities

This was disclosed at a press conference during the unveiling of the Association of Northerners in Southern Nigeria (ANISON), on Tuesday in Umuahia, Abia State.

Speaking at the press conference, the Acting Chairman of the association, Alhaji Ibrahim Abdulkadir, said numerical strength alone could not change the fortunes of Northerners without organisation, enterprise, discipline and meaningful contributions to their host communities.

“Our numbers alone will not change our circumstances. Our organisation, our character, our enterprise and our contribution will,” he said.

Abdulkadir urged members to focus on what they were building in their places of residence rather than define themselves by the challenges they encountered.

He stressed that ANISON was committed to fostering cooperation rather than rivalry with host communities.

“We do not come to compete with you for belonging. We come to build with you,” he said, extending a hand of partnership to Southern communities.

He called on Northerners across the region to support the association with their ideas, businesses and commitment, urging them to remain united, productive and organised.

“Let 2027 find us organised, not scattered; productive, not passive; united in purpose, not divided by suspicion,” he said

Speaking also, convener of ANISON, Dr Ukpai Iro Ukpai, said the initiative was aimed at ending the scattered and poorly documented nature of Northerners’ economic activities across the South.

He said Northerners were heavily involved in trade, agriculture, transportation, food distribution, crafts and services, but their contributions remained largely unorganised and disconnected from institutions that could expand their economic opportunities.

“We cannot remain economically present but institutionally invisible,” he declared.

He said ANISON would promote business formalisation, proper record-keeping, market linkages, institutional engagement and documentation of members’ contributions to their host communities.

According to him Nigeria’s diversity can be explored for economic integration and collaboration instead of being exploited by politicians for their selfish interests.

Ukpai stressed that the association was neither a political party nor an ethnic pressure group, but a platform for economic participation, responsible citizenship and mutually beneficial relationships with host communities.

“We don’t just want you to count our presence, we want you to also measure our contribution,” he said.

He argued that economic coexistence should go beyond tolerance to joint investments, job creation, trade, skills transfer and community development, insisting that Northerners could preserve their ancestral identities while embracing responsibilities in their places of residence.

He said ANISON would pursue partnerships with host communities, governments, traditional institutions, businesses and development organisations, adding that the association did not seek dominance or privileges above other Nigerians.

Ukpai announced that ANISON would hold its first leadership training in Owerri, Imo State, on December 5, ahead of its inaugural summit in Uyo in mid-December, where Northerners from across the 17 Southern states would engage government, industry, institutions and host communities.

He said the association would be judged by measurable achievements rather than membership numbers, stressing that its ultimate goal was to turn collective potential into tangible economic and social value.

“Our greatest achievement will not be how many people we bring together, but what those people build together,” he said.

Some of the Northernes in attendance at the briefing included ANISON’s Enugu State Coordinator, Aliyu Abdulllahi; his Imo State counterpart, Rilwan Zubani; woman leader, Hannah Anyanwu; Ibrahim Mustapha; Mustapha Isa among others.

The post Northerners in South move to convert presence into economic power appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Senate orders scrutiny of revised 2025 laws
description:
By Henry Umoru



ABUJA — The Senate has called for a thorough scrutiny of the revised and consolidated Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2025, to ensure accuracy before granting legislative approval.



The President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, made the call on Tuesday while reading a
content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The Senate has called for a thorough scrutiny of the revised and consolidated Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2025, to ensure accuracy before granting legislative approval.

The President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, made the call on Tuesday while reading a letter from President Bola Tinubu seeking the National Assembly’s approval of the revised compendium.

Akpabio said the Senate must ensure that all amendments were accurately reflected and that no provisions had been altered from the original laws passed by the National Assembly.

He said it was necessary to compare the compiled laws with the versions passed by both chambers to prevent discrepancies that could undermine the country’s legal framework.

In the letter, Tinubu said the committee constituted on October 24, 2024, examined 932 federal enactments and 731 subsidiary legislations.

He disclosed that 664 principal enactments were validated for inclusion in the revised compendium, while 268 were identified as obsolete, spent or repealed.

According to the President, the updated compendium would provide a reliable legal reference for the judiciary, legal practitioners, government institutions, investors and the general public.

The Senate subsequently referred the revised compendium to the Committees on Rules and Business and Judiciary for further legislative action.

Contributing to the debate, former Senate Leader, Senator Yahaya Abdullahi (APC, Kebbi North), described the exercise as important to Nigeria’s legal system and the administration of justice.

He recalled that a similar exercise was conducted after the return to democratic governance in 1999 to give legitimacy to decrees enacted under military administrations.

Abdullahi, who noted that the last official consolidation of the laws was undertaken in 2004, said the current exercise had become necessary after more than two decades.

He, however, cautioned against rushing the process, given its implications for the country’s legal system and justice delivery.

He proposed that the compendium be thoroughly examined by the Senate Committee on Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters, with the support of competent legal experts.

According to him, the committee should analyse the volumes and present a comprehensive report to enable lawmakers to understand the proposed changes before approval.

Also contributing, Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Jibrin Barau (APC, Kano North), supported the call for scrutiny, warning that even a single altered clause could make the compilation inconsistent with the laws passed by the National Assembly.

Barau recommended that the consolidated provisions be compared with the original versions passed by both chambers and those assented to by the President.

Akpabio agreed with the submissions, saying the Senate usually engaged consultants and relevant experts to examine such documents before presenting a summarised report.

He also directed that the leadership and management of the National Assembly be involved in the verification exercise to ensure accuracy.

The post Senate orders scrutiny of revised 2025 laws appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Delta campaign killings: Oborevwori orders arrest of perpetrators
description:
Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, on Tuesday ordered security agencies to track down and arrest those responsible for the deadly political violence in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of the state.
The governor gave the directive during a visit to the community to assess
content:
Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, on Tuesday ordered security agencies to track down and arrest those responsible for the deadly political violence in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of the state.

The governor gave the directive during a visit to the community to assess the situation and reassure residents following Monday’s attack on the campaign entourage of former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, which left six people dead and several others injured.

The attack occurred during a campaign visit by Omo-Agege, the Nigeria Democratic Congress candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections. His campaign organisation had initially reported that four people, including two of his aides, were killed when gunmen allegedly opened fire on the gathering.

However, the Nigeria Police Force confirmed on Tuesday that preliminary reports indicated that six people had died, while several others sustained injuries.

Among those identified by Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation as victims were Moses Anaughe, a former member of the Delta State House of Assembly and aide to the former senator, and Urhobo youth activist, Akima Efemena Umukoro.

The violence prompted the Delta State Government to impose a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area, restricting movement between 6pm and 6am daily until further notice.

The police have also commenced an investigation into the incident, with the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, directing a thorough and impartial probe to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack, identify those responsible and examine the conduct of officers deployed to the venue.

Oborevwori described the killings as unfortunate and unacceptable, insisting that those responsible would face the full weight of the law.

“No political disagreement or ambition is worth the loss of human lives,” the governor said, warning that his administration would not tolerate any attempt to undermine peace and security in the state.

Before proceeding to Uduere, Oborevwori had held a security meeting with heads of security agencies at the Area Command Office in Ughelli.

He was accompanied to the community by the State Commissioner of Police, CP Samuel Etaifo Erale; Commander of the 63 Brigade of the Nigerian Army, Brigadier General Ibrahim Buhari; the State Director of the Department of State Services and other security officials.

Addressing journalists during the visit, the governor condemned the invasion of communities under the guise of political activities, describing the killing of fellow Nigerians over political differences as unconscionable.

He expressed disappointment that political disagreements could degenerate into violence and the killing of innocent people, particularly when his administration had worked to maintain relative peace in the state since assuming office in 2023.

Oborevwori said his administration remained committed to peace and security, noting that the fourth pillar of his MORE Agenda was specifically designed to promote a peaceful and secure environment across Delta State.

He said, “Those who know me know that I am not a violent person. That is why, in my MORE Agenda, the fourth pillar is dedicated to enhancing peace and security.

“We have been preaching peace, and Delta State has enjoyed relative peace since 2023. The important thing is how to sustain that peace. I want to assure the people that this will not happen again.”

The governor insisted that the perpetrators must be identified, apprehended and prosecuted, declaring that the state would not allow political activities to become a source of insecurity.

“This must stop. It must stop. We cannot continue like this,” he warned.

Oborevwori also observed that sustained peace and security were critical to economic development, stressing that businesses and investments could not thrive in an atmosphere of violence, fear and uncertainty.

He appealed to political leaders, supporters and other stakeholders to exercise restraint, shun political thuggery and avoid actions capable of triggering further violence.

The governor further charged the police and other security agencies to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the incident, arrest everyone connected to the killings and ensure that those found culpable were brought to justice.

The attack has heightened concerns about the safety of political campaigns and supporters ahead of the 2027 general elections, with the police urging political actors and residents to remain calm, comply with the curfew and avoid spreading unverified information.

description:
The Ado-Odo Progressive Forum in Ogun State says it will embark on door-to-door campaigns, market engagement and voter sensitisation to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress governorship candidate, Senator Olamilekan Adeola, ahead of the 2027 elections.
The gro
content:
The Ado-Odo Progressive Forum in Ogun State says it will embark on door-to-door campaigns, market engagement and voter sensitisation to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress governorship candidate, Senator Olamilekan Adeola, ahead of the 2027 elections.

The group, which is targeting 95 per cent votes for the candidates, said it would reach residents across streets, communities and villages in Ado-Odo to canvass support and encourage newly registered voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards.

One of the forum’s coordinators, Alhaji Sharafa Mustapha, disclosed this at a rally held on Monday at Methodist Primary School, Ado-Odo, where the group expressed support for Tinubu’s re-election and Adeola’s governorship ambition.

Mustapha said the mobilisation would include educating residents on voting procedures and encouraging them to participate in the elections.

“We are ready to mobilise all newly registered voters to collect their PVC, and we are going on a door-to-door campaign, market engagement, as well as a voter sensitisation exercise to educate voters on voting procedures,” he said.

Another member Tinubu was partly driven by the appointment of Kamorudeen Olawale Yusuf, an indigene of Ado-Odo, as the President’s Personal Assistant on Special Duties.

He said the appointment had brought pride to the community and encouraged residents to mobilise in support of the President’s re-election.

“We are mobilising for President Tinubu to show appreciation for appointing our son, Alhaji Kamorudeen Olawale Yusuf, into his cabinet as a Personal Assistant on Special Duties,” Olamilekan said.

He added that residents had benefited from federal appointments, employment opportunities and infrastructure projects under the Tinubu administration.

“Today, many of our children are now employed in the federal civil service,” he said.

Olamilekan also cited the ongoing Atan-Alapoti-Ado-Odo-Ikoga Road project as one of the developments the community appreciated.

At the rally, the forum honoured Yusuf for his contributions to the community. The award was received on his behalf by Yusuf Yakub and Edalere Nafiu.

The group said it would sustain its mobilisation activities across Ado-Odo and neighbouring communities to encourage voter participation and secure support for Tinubu and Adeola in the 2027 elections.

title: Reps advance bills to reform social investment agency, regulate eye care
description:
By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja



The House of Representatives has passed two bills seeking to reform Nigeria’s social investment programmes and strengthen the regulation of optometry and dispensing opticians through second reading.



The bills, sponsored by Deputy Speaker Benjamin Kalu and other law
content:
By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja

The House of Representatives has passed two bills seeking to reform Nigeria’s social investment programmes and strengthen the regulation of optometry and dispensing opticians through second reading.

The bills, sponsored by Deputy Speaker Benjamin Kalu and other lawmakers, are aimed at improving the delivery of social protection programmes and addressing regulatory gaps in the country’s eye care sector.

Leading the debate on the proposed amendment to the National Social Investment Programme Agency (Establishment) Act, 2023, Kalu said the success of social investment programmes should be measured not by the size of their budgets or the number of initiatives introduced, but by their actual impact on vulnerable Nigerians.

He described social investment as a commitment by the Nigerian state to prevent temporary hardship from becoming permanent exclusion.

The Deputy Speaker said the growing scale and complexity of Nigeria’s social protection system had made it necessary to strengthen the institutional framework for coordinating, implementing and monitoring interventions.

According to him, the proposed amendment would address administrative fragmentation, duplication of beneficiaries, unreliable data and inadequate coordination among the different levels of government.

Among its major provisions is the introduction of the Grant for Vulnerable Groups Programme and the National Social Safety-Net Coordinating Office as components of the agency.

The bill also seeks to establish the National Social Safety-Net Coordinating Office as the central institution for coordinating and managing data on national social safety nets, including maintaining, updating and verifying the National Social Register.

Kalu said the proposed legislation would also provide for the establishment of state offices to bring programme implementation closer to beneficiaries and introduce executive directors with clearly defined responsibilities for individual programmes.

He explained that the changes would strengthen accountability, improve coordination and ensure that government assistance reached intended beneficiaries.

He identified children requiring support to remain in school, unemployed youths seeking economic opportunities and vulnerable households needing temporary assistance as some of those expected to benefit from a more coordinated social investment system.

The 15-clause bill was subsequently subjected to a voice vote by the Speaker, Abbas Tajudeen, and received the support of lawmakers.

In a related development, the House also passed second reading a bill seeking to repeal the Optometrists and Dispensing Opticians (Registration, etc.) Act, Cap. 09, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004, and introduce a new regulatory framework for the profession.

The proposed legislation, sponsored by Kalu and eight other lawmakers, seeks to establish the Optometrists and Dispensing Opticians Registration Council of Nigeria to regulate professional training and practice.

Kalu said the proposed law would introduce mandatory continuing professional education, accredited internships and stiffer penalties for unregistered practitioners.

It would also strengthen professional disciplinary procedures while providing safeguards for fair hearing and opportunities for appeal to the Federal High Court.

The bill, comprising 30 clauses across six parts and three schedules, also provides for the establishment, powers and governance of the proposed council, registration and regulatory oversight, professional privileges, training and quality assurance.

Other provisions cover offences by unregistered practitioners, professional discipline, appellate safeguards, scope of practice and professional qualifications.

Kalu said the proposed legislation would help protect Nigerians against preventable blindness, improve primary eye care delivery and align professional regulation with contemporary standards.

He urged lawmakers to support the bill, noting that stronger regulation was necessary to guarantee higher professional standards in public and private healthcare facilities.

The Speaker, Abbas, subsequently subjected the bill to a voice vote, and it was overwhelmingly supported by members.

Both bills were referred for further legislative consideration, with the optometry bill specifically referred to the House Committee on Health Institutions.

title: Senegal Regain AFCON Title After Appeal
description: Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January.“The Court of Arbitration for Spor
content:
Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January.

“The Court of Arbitration for Sport has upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025,” CAS said in a statement.

The Swiss-based sports court said Senegal’s appeal had been upheld by “a unanimous decision”, and their original 1-0 victory after extra time is reinstated.

In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) sensationally overturned the result of the final, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title, after many Senegalese players walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty given to the hosts with the game still goalless.

Senegal and Morocco players line up prior the Africa Cup of Nations (CAN) final football match between Senegal and Morocco at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat on January 18, 2026. Photo by PAUL ELLIS / AFP

The CAF Appeals Committee had justified its decision to overturn the result and declare Morocco champions based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations.

Those state that if a team “refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee, it shall be considered (loser) and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition”.

However, the Senegal players eventually returned to the pitch and the final carried on.

The CAS panel therefore considered that the referee’s decision to restart the final showed that “the conditions for resuming the match had been met”, and that articles 82 and 84 were therefore “not applicable in this case”.

The National Universities Commission (NUC) is considering a three-to-four-week adjustment of academic calendars across Nigerian universities to enable academics to participate in the cond
content:
…Mobilises VCs to support INEC as commission plans 57,000 additional BVAS machines

By Joseph Erunke, Abuja

The National Universities Commission (NUC) is considering a three-to-four-week adjustment of academic calendars across Nigerian universities to enable academics to participate in the conduct of the 2027 general elections.

The proposed adjustment is part of efforts by the commission to mobilise Vice-Chancellors and university authorities nationwide to provide credible and non-partisan academic personnel, particularly as Collation and Returning Officers.

The NUC Executive Secretary, Prof. Abdullahi Yusufu Ribadu, disclosed this on Monday in Abuja when the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, led a delegation of National Commissioners and senior officials on a courtesy visit to the commission.

Ribadu said the NUC would engage Vice-Chancellors on the nomination of qualified academics for electoral assignments, adding that an online meeting would be convened to facilitate the process.

He also pledged to issue a formal circular to universities upon receiving an official request from INEC, stressing that the credibility of the 2027 elections would depend significantly on the integrity of personnel deployed to conduct them.

“Since we want to have credible elections, we also have to have credible personnel,” he said.

The NUC boss explained that the proposed adjustment of academic calendars would give academics sufficient time to discharge their electoral responsibilities without compromising students’ academic programmes.

According to him, the proposed break would not exceed four weeks, adding that the commission would consult university administrators to ensure that the arrangement neither disrupted academic activities nor interfered with INEC’s electoral timetable.

“We will discuss with the Vice-Chancellors and have their calendars tweaked in such a way that it will not affect the elections, nor will it affect the studies of the students,” he said.

Ribadu also stressed that academics and other ad hoc officials engaged in the electoral process must demonstrate absolute neutrality, proposing that they take an oath of neutrality before deployment.

Beyond providing election officials, the NUC Executive Secretary proposed a broader institutional partnership between universities and INEC, including student internship opportunities at the electoral commission, joint research initiatives and possible academic programmes in electoral studies.

He identified artificial intelligence, robotics and data analytics as areas where Nigerian universities could collaborate with INEC to strengthen electoral administration and improve the country’s democratic process.

The NUC also proposed leveraging student organisations, campus clubs and other university platforms to intensify voter education and combat misinformation and disinformation ahead of the elections.

Earlier, INEC Chairman, Amupitan, said the visit was aimed at strengthening the existing partnership between the electoral commission and Nigerian universities ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He acknowledged the critical role universities had played in previous elections, particularly through the deployment of Vice-Chancellors and other senior academics as Collation and Returning Officers.

Amupitan, however, said INEC was introducing technological, operational and security reforms to strengthen the electoral process and guarantee the safety of academics and other personnel engaged in election duties.

On technological improvements, he disclosed that polling unit results recorded on Form EC8A would undergo automated arithmetic consistency and over-voting checks before transmission to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV).

He also announced the procurement of 57,000 additional Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) machines, which he said would reduce the voter-to-device ratio to 850 voters per machine.

As part of its readiness assessment, the commission will conduct a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise on Saturday, November 28, 2026, across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

On the security of electoral personnel, Amupitan disclosed that the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) had been decentralised to Local Government Areas and Registration Areas to strengthen security coordination at the grassroots.

He said dedicated security cordons and escort arrangements would also be provided around collation centres to protect election officials from intimidation and attacks.

The INEC chairman further cited provisions of the Electoral Act 2026 criminalising violence, abusive rhetoric and threats against electoral personnel, stressing that the commission had the power to prosecute offenders.

“No Returning Officer or Collation Officer will be left to stand alone against lawlessness,” he assured.

Amupitan specifically sought the NUC’s intervention in four areas: timely nomination of qualified and non-partisan academics for election duties; adjustment of university academic calendars to accommodate the elections; collaboration on campus voter education and the fight against disinformation; and improved welfare and recognition for academics deployed for electoral assignments.

Ribadu congratulated Amupitan on his appointment, describing him as a lawyer and academic of international repute.

He expressed confidence that INEC would deliver transparent, free and fair elections capable of setting a positive democratic example for other African countries.

The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027, while governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections will hold on February 6, 2027.

ABUJA — The Kabiru Tanimu Turaki-led Interim National Working Committee (INWC) of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has blamed President Bola Tinubu’s past political statements for what it described as a growing climate of violence against opposition parties, following the
content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA — The Kabiru Tanimu Turaki-led Interim National Working Committee (INWC) of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has blamed President Bola Tinubu’s past political statements for what it described as a growing climate of violence against opposition parties, following the killing of at least four persons in an attack on a Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) campaign in Delta State.

The group said the attack in Uduere, Ughelli North, where gunmen opened fire while former Deputy Senate President and NDC Delta Central senatorial candidate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, was addressing supporters, exposed the dangers of inflammatory political rhetoric ahead of the 2027 general elections.

In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Comrade Ini Ememobong, on Tuesday, the INWC demanded that Tinubu publicly renounce his previous remarks, which it accused of encouraging hostility towards opposition parties.

The statement cited Tinubu’s 2022 declaration that political power must be “grabbed, snatched and run away with”, as well as his 2026 remark that “all is fair in politics”, as examples of what it described as dangerous political messaging.

“These two statements alone, coming from their leader, were the adrenaline that APC followers needed to unleash unmitigated mayhem on opposition parties,” it alleged.

It also cited alleged threats by some APC figures, including Senator Fadahunsi of Osun State, the Chairman of Kuje Area Council and the party’s Edo State chairman, against citizens unwilling to vote for the ruling party.

On Delta State, the group alleged that intimidation of opposition figures had become recurrent, claiming that at least two deadly attacks against opposition groups had occurred in November alone. It further alleged that the incidents were widely believed to have been sponsored by the APC.

“With this latest attack and the deaths and injuries it caused, the world can now clearly see the fruits of the evil seed planted by the APC through violent communication,” the statement said.

The INWC also demanded a thorough and transparent investigation into the attack, urging the police to make their findings public. It called on the Inspector-General of Police to ensure that the investigation he ordered was conducted professionally and that other political attacks across the country received similar attention.

It urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), the National Peace Committee and election observers to identify and publicly expose individuals responsible for political violence, including through international platforms.

The group also raised concerns over allegations that police personnel were present at the scene but failed to assist victims, calling on security agencies, particularly the police, to demonstrate neutrality and professionalism.

“Nigerians need responsible leadership that does not sacrifice the peace and unity of the country at the altar of political domination and elections,” it said.

The PDP bloc urged Nigerians to vote out the APC and its government, declaring that the ruling party must leave office by January next year.

The post Delta killings: Turaki-led PDP urges presidency to renounce ‘war rhetoric’ ahead of 2027 appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: NYSC warns Bayelsa corps members against night movements, politicians
description:
By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa



The National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) in Bayelsa State has warned corps members deployed to the state to avoid late-night movements, compromising situations and unnecessary exposure to security risks.







The State Coordinator, Mr Samuel Pepple, gave the warning
content:
By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa

The National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) in Bayelsa State has warned corps members deployed to the state to avoid late-night movements, compromising situations and unnecessary exposure to security risks.

The State Coordinator, Mr Samuel Pepple, gave the warning on Tuesday during the low-key closing ceremony of the 2026 Batch C Stream II orientation course at the NYSC Permanent Orientation Camp, Boro Town, Kolokuma-Opokuma Local Government Area.

Pepple urged the departing corps members to uphold discipline, remain security-conscious and demonstrate integrity as they proceed to their respective Places of Primary Assignment (PPAs).

He advised them to embrace their postings, particularly those assigned to rural and riverine communities, assuring them of adequate security arrangements, decent accommodation and necessary safety equipment, including life jackets for those deployed to riverine areas.

Emphasising personal safety, the coordinator urged the corps members to communicate their whereabouts to trusted persons and strictly adhere to security guidelines provided during the orientation course.

On electoral responsibilities, Pepple warned them against political interference, inducements and other actions capable of compromising their integrity.

He stressed that corps members must remain politically neutral and discharge any electoral responsibilities assigned to them with professionalism and patriotism.

The state coordinator also encouraged them to integrate into their host communities, respect local cultures and traditions, and contribute meaningfully to the development of their areas of deployment.

He noted that their services were particularly needed in rural and riverine communities, where access to essential services, especially education, remained limited.

Reminding them that the orientation course was only the first phase of their service year, Pepple directed the corps members to report promptly to their PPAs after completing the necessary documentation.

He also instructed them to obtain approval before embarking on any journey outside their places of primary assignment.

Pepple expressed confidence in their ability to contribute meaningfully to national development, urging them to serve with courage, commitment and selflessness.

He concluded by praying for their safety and a successful service year, wishing them journey mercies as they departed the camp for their respective places of primary assignment.

The post NYSC warns Bayelsa corps members against night movements, politicians appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: 2027: Again, Atiku vows to restore subsidy; revive Ajaokuta steel mill
description:
By Adegboyega Adeleye



Former Vice-President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar has renewed his pledge to restore fuel subsidy and promised to revive and complete the Ajaokuta Steel Mill if elected president in 2027.



Atiku made the pledge at the ADC pres
content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Former Vice-President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar has renewed his pledge to restore fuel subsidy and promised to revive and complete the Ajaokuta Steel Mill if elected president in 2027.

Atiku made the pledge at the ADC presidential campaign rally in Lokoja, Kogi State, on Tuesday, while restating his commitment to making life more affordable and creating jobs and prosperity through industrial investment.

“Our leadership in the previous years have not met the aspirations of the people of Kogi State. I have already promised Nigerians that I will return subsidy. I want to let you know that I mean it. I am serious about it, and I am sincere about it. This will bring about affordability of your life,” Atiku said.

He also pledged to revive and complete the Ajaokuta Steel Mill, saying foreign investment could fund the project without public spending.

“Secondly, for me in particular, I want to promise you here today that I will revive and complete the Ajaokuta steel mill. This is very doable because we can bring in foreign investment to complete that without putting any money there. It is business…” he said.

Atiku also promised to continue the Baro Port project by dredging the River Niger, saying the port could serve states beyond Kogi and create jobs and economic opportunities.

“Again, let me assure you, people of Kogi State, we shall continue the project of the Baro Port by dredging the River Niger, so that Baro Port can also serve other states of Nigeria. So you can imagine Baro Port being an equivalent of Apapa Port. It would bring about tremendous job opportunities and prosperity for the people of Kogi State and the entire Northern states.”

The former vice-president has previously described his subsidy plan as support for locally refined fuel to reduce production costs and make petrol more affordable, rather than a return to subsidising imported fuel. Vanguard reported that he said the policy was intended to reduce fuel and transport costs.

title: BREAKING: CAS restores Senegal as 2025 AFCON champions
description:
The Court of Arbitration for Sport has overturned the decision to strip Senegal of their 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title, declaring the Teranga Lions champions and restoring their 1-0 victory over Morocco in the controversial final, PUNCH Online reports.
CAS, in its ruling on Tuesday, upheld Senega
content:
The Court of Arbitration for Sport has overturned the decision to strip Senegal of their 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title, declaring the Teranga Lions champions and restoring their 1-0 victory over Morocco in the controversial final, PUNCH Online reports.

CAS, in its ruling on Tuesday, upheld Senegal’s appeal against the Confederation of African Football Appeals Board’s decision, which had awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory after Senegal’s players temporarily walked off the pitch in protest during the January 18 final in Rabat.

In its ruling, CAS held that the AFCON regulations invoked by CAF were not applicable to the circumstances of the match, arguing that the referee had not erred in law by allowing the game to resume.

“AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently. They are therefore not applicable in this case,” the panel ruled in a statement shared by Sky Sports reporter Rob Harris.

The panel added that the referee did not err in law by allowing the match to continue after Senegal’s players returned to the pitch.

The dispute followed the chaotic final at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat, where Senegal initially defeated hosts Morocco 1-0 after extra time to claim their second continental title.

The final descended into controversy in stoppage time when the referee awarded Morocco a penalty following a VAR review, shortly after Senegal had a goal ruled out.

Angered by the decision, Senegal coach Pape Thiaw instructed his players to leave the pitch in protest, with the team remaining off the field for about 14 minutes before returning to continue the match.

Morocco’s Brahim Diaz subsequently missed the penalty, while Pape Gueye scored the decisive goal in extra time to hand Senegal victory.

However, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation lodged a formal complaint with CAF and FIFA, arguing that Senegal’s withdrawal disrupted the normal course of the match.

CAF’s Disciplinary Board initially allowed the result to stand while imposing sanctions on both teams over incidents during the final.

Morocco, dissatisfied with the decision, subsequently appealed. On March 17, CAF’s Appeals Board overturned the earlier ruling, declared Senegal to have forfeited the final for breaching Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, and awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory.

The decision triggered widespread criticism, with Senegal’s football federation describing it as unfair and unacceptable before taking the matter to CAS on March 25.

Senegal had asked the Lausanne-based tribunal to overturn CAF’s decision, restore the original result and recognise the country as champions.

The post BREAKING: CAS restores Senegal as 2025 AFCON champions appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
