title: CAS Restores Senegal’s AFCON 2025 Title, Overturns CAF Decision
description: Gambiaj.com – (LAUSANNE, SWITZERLAND) – The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has officially declared Senegal the winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON), overturning a controversial decision by the Confederation of African Football (CAF) that had stripped the Teranga Lions of their tit
content:
Gambiaj.com – (LAUSANNE, SWITZERLAND) – The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has officially declared Senegal the winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON), overturning a controversial decision by the Confederation of African Football (CAF) that had stripped the Teranga Lions of their title and awarded it to Morocco.

In a ruling delivered unanimously on Tuesday, 24 November, in Lausanne, Switzerland, the sports tribunal upheld Senegal’s appeal against CAF and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF), confirming the original 1-0 victory secured by the Senegalese team on the pitch.

In a statement to the media, CAS said it had accepted the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF), annulled the decision of CAF’s Appeals Board and reinstated the earlier ruling of the CAF Disciplinary Board.

“ The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has upheld the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) concerning the final of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON). The decision of the CAF Appeals Board is set aside, and the decision of the CAF Disciplinary Board is reinstated. Consequently, the result of the 2025 AFCON final is confirmed, with Senegal winning 1-0,” the tribunal said in a statement to the media.

Consequently, the result of the final, which Senegal won 1-0 after extra time, was confirmed, restoring the continental title to the West African nation.

The verdict ends nearly ten months of uncertainty and escalating tensions between Senegal and Morocco following the controversial final played in Rabat on 18 January 2026.

Senegal had initially been crowned champions after a closely contested final that descended into controversy during stoppage time. Several Senegalese players left the pitch in protest after the referee awarded Morocco a penalty, returning nearly 15 minutes later.

Morocco’s Brahim Diaz subsequently missed the penalty, and the match proceeded into extra time, where Senegal secured a 1-0 victory to lift the trophy.

However, the celebrations were overshadowed when CAF’s Appeals Board, acting on a complaint from the Moroccan federation, ruled on 17 March 2026 that Senegal had forfeited the final.

Invoking Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, which prohibit teams from leaving the field before the end of a match without the referee’s authorization, CAF awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory by forfeit.

The decision triggered strong protests from the Senegalese federation, which described it as “the grossest administrative robbery in the history of our sport” and subsequently took the matter to CAS.

The tribunal held a closed-door hearing in Lausanne on 8 October, during which it heard arguments from the parties for more than five hours. It had subsequently indicated that its decision would be announced towards the end of November.

Morocco Reports Alleged Contact With CAS Arbitrator

The ruling comes amid fresh controversy surrounding an alleged incident involving FSF president Abdoulaye Fall.

The Moroccan federation had formally written to CAS reporting an alleged telephone conversation between Fall and one of the three arbitrators appointed to decide the case.

However, Fall firmly denied the allegation when contacted by RFI, saying he was “surprised” by the report and insisting that he had not had any telephone communication with any of the arbitrators.

The allegation added another layer of tension to an already contentious dispute between the two football federations.

Meanwhile, CAS’s official website experienced technical disruptions as news of the verdict emerged, reportedly due to an exceptional surge in visitors seeking access to the ruling.

The decision restores Senegal’s status as African champions and allows the country to officially add a second star to its national team’s jersey, following its first AFCON triumph in 2021.

title: Nigeria Urges UN To Clear 216 Outstanding Audit Queries
description: Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, has urged the UN management to urgently resolve 216 outstanding audit queries, stressing the need for greater accountability, transparency and compliance with established financial rules and procedures.Ibrahim
content:
Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, has urged the UN management to urgently resolve 216 outstanding audit queries, stressing the need for greater accountability, transparency and compliance with established financial rules and procedures.

Ibrahim made the call during deliberations of the UN General Assembly’s Fifth Committee on reports of the United Nations Board of Auditors, where he expressed concern over the number of unresolved audit issues and called for improved performance by the organisation’s management.

He acknowledged that 100 audit reports had been cleared but said the 216 outstanding reports remained a significant concern that required urgent attention.

Although he recognised that some of the cases might have been overtaken by events, the Nigerian diplomat urged the UN management to improve its clearance rate, which currently stands at 55 per cent.

Ibrahim also emphasised the importance of timely payment of assessed contributions by member states, insisting that payments should be made according to schedule and translated into tangible benefits.

On financial reporting, he stressed that the accuracy and integrity of data were fundamental to the credibility of reports presented before member states.

He said all stakeholders had a collective responsibility to safeguard the integrity of information underpinning the UN’s financial reporting.

The Nigerian envoy warned that continued explanations without corresponding compliance could leave the organisation trapped in an endless cycle of justifications.

He, therefore, urged UN management to prioritise adherence to established financial rules and procedures as the most effective way to address recurring audit concerns.

Ibrahim also commended the cooperation between information-gathering systems and audit teams, describing their coordination as essential to improving the quality and reliability of UN reports.

Meanwhile, the Fifth Committee considered the Secretary-General’s report on the estimated use of the commitment authority for 2026 and the proposed 2027 subvention to the Extraordinary Chambers in the Courts of Cambodia.

Speaking on behalf of the Group of 77 and China, Uruguay reaffirmed the group’s support for the proposed subvention, as well as its commitment to justice and national reconciliation.

The Committee subsequently concluded its general discussion, with Canada’s representative, Sophia, expected to lead informal consultations to consolidate the observations and contributions of delegations. The Committee is scheduled to reconvene on November 30, 2026.

The post Nigeria Urges UN To Clear 216 Outstanding Audit Queries appeared first on Channels Television.

content:
The Monetary Policy Committee of the Central Bank of Nigeria has retained the benchmark interest rate at 23 per cent amid a sustained decline in inflation.

The CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, announced the decision on Tuesday at the end of the committee’s 308th meeting in Abuja.

Cardoso said, “The Committee decided as follows: retain the monetary policy rate at 23 per cent.”

The decision follows the 350-basis-point reduction in the Monetary Policy Rate from 26.5 per cent to 23 per cent in September 2026.

The apex bank had earlier reduced the benchmark interest rate by 50 basis points in February before retaining it at subsequent meetings before the September cut.

The PUNCH had earlier reported that financial market analysts warned that renewed pressure on the naira, declining foreign exchange reserves and rising global interest rates could constrain the apex bank’s ability to further ease monetary policy despite moderating inflation.

The decision to retain the benchmark interest rate also comes amid five consecutive months of declining headline inflation in the country.

According to the most recent Consumer Price Index report released by the National Bureau of Statistics, Nigeria’s headline inflation rate eased to 14.06 per cent in October 2026 from 14.63 per cent in September, representing a decline of 0.57 percentage points.

title: UPDATED: CBN retains interest rate at 23%, warns of election spending risks
description:
The Monetary Policy Committee of the Central Bank of Nigeria has retained the benchmark interest rate at 23 per cent, citing inflationary risks arising from anticipated election-related spending, increased festive season expenditure and disruptions to global energy supplies.
The CBN Governor, Olayem
content:
The Monetary Policy Committee of the Central Bank of Nigeria has retained the benchmark interest rate at 23 per cent, citing inflationary risks arising from anticipated election-related spending, increased festive season expenditure and disruptions to global energy supplies.

The CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, announced the decision on Tuesday at the end of the committee’s 308th meeting, held on November 23 and 24, 2026, in Abuja, with 10 members in attendance.

Cardoso said, “The committee decided as follows: retain the Monetary Policy Rate at 23 per cent.”

The committee also retained the Standing Facilities Corridor at plus 50 and minus 300 basis points around the MPR, while maintaining the Cash Reserve Requirement for deposit money banks at 45 per cent, merchant banks at 16 per cent and non-Treasury Single Account public sector deposits at 75 per cent.

The decision follows the 350-basis-point reduction in the benchmark interest rate from 26.5 per cent to 23 per cent in September 2026.

Cardoso explained that although headline inflation had moderated for five consecutive months, prevailing economic risks necessitated maintaining the current monetary policy stance to consolidate the gains recorded in price stability.

He said, “The MPC observed that the anticipated increase in spending from the end-of-year festive season and election-related activities could impact aggregate demand with likely upward pressure on prices.”

The committee also expressed concern over the ongoing Middle East conflict, which could sustain pressure on energy prices, and adverse weather conditions that could undermine food supply.

Nigeria’s headline inflation declined to 14.06 per cent in October from 14.63 per cent in September, while core inflation fell to 10.78 per cent from 12.95 per cent.

Food inflation also moderated to 19.13 per cent from 19.59 per cent, reflecting easing price pressures on processed food and farm produce following the commencement of the harvest season.

Cardoso attributed the sustained moderation in inflation to exchange rate stability, improved monetary policy transmission and the restrictive monetary policy stance.

He added that the Composite Purchasing Managers’ Index rose from 53 points in September to 53.2 points in October, reflecting improved activities across the industrial, agricultural and services sectors.

Responding to questions from journalists, Cardoso disclosed that the September interest rate adjustment was yielding the intended results, with interbank lending rates moving closer to the lower band of the Standing Facilities Corridor.

“What we’re finding is that the interbank rates are moving closer to the lower band of the corridor, and that’s exactly where we want to be,” he said.

The governor added that rates on Open Market Operations instruments and Treasury bills had moderated, while the gap between the benchmark interest rate and prevailing market rates had narrowed considerably.

He also disclosed that credit to the private sector was gradually recovering, adding that the apex bank would continue to monitor borrowing costs.

“We are very pleased that, really, the amount of credit going out to the private sector has gradually begun to come up,” Cardoso said.

He maintained that the September adjustment was intended to align the benchmark rate with market realities rather than signal a departure from the restrictive monetary policy stance.

On recent pressure on the naira and declining external reserves, Cardoso dismissed concerns over the sustainability of exchange rate stability, describing the developments as temporary and largely seasonal.

Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $`54.02bn as of November 17, 2026, sufficient to cover 10.26 months of imports of goods and services.

The governor attributed the recent volatility to year-end portfolio adjustments by foreign investors, increased foreign exchange demand by domestic businesses seeking to hedge against future risks and rising election-related expenditure.

“These are all seasonal. And we believe very strongly that as we go into the next year, we will find a major moderation in the volatility that you have seen,” he said.

Cardoso also disclosed that diaspora remittances exceeded `$900m in the preceding month, adding that Nigeria’s current account surplus and sustained remittance inflows would strengthen external buffers.

He assured Nigerians that the apex bank would do everything possible to preserve exchange rate stability.

Speaking on the recently signed Memorandum of Understanding between the CBN and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, Cardoso said the agreement followed months of consultations between both institutions.

He explained that the partnership would improve transparency in the management of oil-related foreign exchange inflows, deepen the foreign exchange market, strengthen external reserves and support energy project financing.

The governor added that the CBN would deploy its advisory expertise and convening power to support the national oil company’s operations.

On the outlook for 2027, Cardoso promised policy consistency, stronger coordination between fiscal and monetary authorities, sustained banking sector stability and further improvements in monetary policy transmission.

“Our goal is single-digit inflation, and we will not stop until we get there. We will continue to ensure that we do everything possible to move inflation to single digits,” he said.

The committee projected a positive domestic economic outlook, supported by improved crude oil production and sustained expansion across agriculture, services and industry.

However, it warned that elevated global energy prices, trade policy uncertainty, supply chain disruptions, cyber threats and diminishing fiscal space remained risks to the global economy.

The PUNCH had earlier reported that financial market analysts warned that renewed pressure on the naira, declining external reserves and rising global interest rates could constrain further monetary policy easing despite moderating domestic inflation.

The post UPDATED: CBN retains interest rate at 23%, warns of election spending risks appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has retained the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 23 per cent, maintaining its benchmark interest rate amid prevailing economic conditions.

CBN Governor, Mr Olayemi Cardoso, disclosed this on Tuesday at the end of the 308th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) in Abuja.

Cardoso said the committee also retained the standing facilities corridor at +50 and -300 basis points around the MPR.

The bank equally maintained the Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR) for Deposit Money Banks at 45 per cent, merchant banks at 16 per cent and non-Treasury Single Account (TSA) public sector deposits at 75 per cent.

Fielding questions from journalists after the meeting, the CBN governor allayed concerns over the decline in the country’s foreign reserves by more than $300 million.

He said the movement in the reserves was normal, particularly towards the end of the year, and should not be a cause for concern.

According to him, fluctuations in the country’s external reserves are expected as the CBN manages its foreign exchange obligations and other transactions.

title: 2027: ‘Rig-And-Die’ Slogan Not A Threat But A Call For Free, Fair Elections — Omo-Agege
description: Former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege has defended his controversial ‘rig and die’ slogan ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that it is a warning against electoral malpractice and not a threat to anyone.Omo-Agege, who is seeking election to the Delta Central Senatoria
content:
Former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege has defended his controversial ‘rig and die’ slogan ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that it is a warning against electoral malpractice and not a threat to anyone.

Omo-Agege, who is seeking election to the Delta Central Senatorial District under the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), said only those planning to manipulate the elections should be concerned about the slogan.

He spoke on Monday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he was asked whether the rhetoric could be contributing to the political violence being witnessed ahead of the elections.

The former lawmaker dismissed the suggestion, arguing that his message was a call for free, fair and credible elections.

“No, because the ‘rig and die’ rhetoric that you just alluded to, you know, it says nobody is being threatened here. We didn’t threaten anybody. All we are saying is that we want free, fair and credible elections. We don’t want anybody rigging the elections.

“To the extent that people have no plans to rig the elections, they have nothing to worry about. It is only those who have plans to rig the elections that are the ones who ought to have sleepless nights,” he said.

Omo-Agege’s defence comes amid concerns over the use of inflammatory language by politicians as preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum.

The slogan has attracted criticism from electoral stakeholders, including officials of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), who have warned that such rhetoric could encourage violence against voters and election officials.

The controversy also follows an alleged attack on members of Omo-Agege’s campaign team in Delta State, in which four people were reportedly killed.

The former Deputy Senate President alleged that the attackers repeatedly called his name and declared that he was “their target,” suggesting that they intended to kill him.

title: Osun declares Friday public holiday for Adeleke’s inauguration
description:
The Osun State Government has declared Friday, November 27, a public holiday to enable residents to participate in the inauguration of Governor Ademola Adeleke for a second term in office.
The declaration was contained in a circular issued by the state Ministry of Home Affairs and sighted by PUNCH O
content:
The Osun State Government has declared Friday, November 27, a public holiday to enable residents to participate in the inauguration of Governor Ademola Adeleke for a second term in office.

The declaration was contained in a circular issued by the state Ministry of Home Affairs and sighted by PUNCH Online on Tuesday.

“In view of the significance of this event, His Excellency has graciously approved that Friday, 27 November, 2026 be observed as a Public Holiday throughout the State to enable the good people of Osun State and well-wishers to participate in the Inauguration Ceremony,” the circular stated.

It directed all public offices, schools and other public institutions in the state to observe the holiday, except those providing essential services.

“All Public Offices, Schools and other public institutions in the state are hereby directed to observe the holiday except those on essential services who are to maintain their normal duties,” it added.

PUNCH Online had earlier reported that the inauguration would hold at the Osogbo Township Stadium, with President Bola Tinubu, governors in the South-West, diplomats and other dignitaries invited to the ceremony.

Adeleke was declared winner of the August 15, 2026, governorship election by the Independent National Electoral Commission, defeating the All Progressives Congress candidate, Bola Oyebamiji.

The governor, who contested under the Accord Party, polled 511,067 votes against Oyebamiji’s 444,815 votes to secure a second term.

Ahead of the inauguration, Adeleke assured residents that he would not disappoint them and promised to do more during his second term.

He gave the assurance in a statement issued by his spokesperson, Olawale Rasheed, after Jumu’at prayers at the Osogbo Central Mosque on November 20, where activities marking the inauguration began.

“I won’t disappoint Osun people. I will deliver even more than my first term. I am hopeful our financial situation will soon improve with the expected resolution of the local government crisis. We will take good care of workers and all segments of the society,” the governor said.

The post Osun declares Friday public holiday for Adeleke’s inauguration appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: US names more Nigerians in ‘Worst of the Worst’ list [see list]
description:
The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has added more Nigerians to its “Worst of the Worst” list, bringing the number of Nigerians featured on the register to 157.







The newly listed individuals were linked to offences ranging from fraud, money laundering and drug-related crime
content:
The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has added more Nigerians to its “Worst of the Worst” list, bringing the number of Nigerians featured on the register to 157.

The newly listed individuals were linked to offences ranging from fraud, money laundering and drug-related crimes to identity theft, forgery, assault and child cruelty.

The names appeared on the DHS website, which features foreign nationals arrested by the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) over criminal activities and identified by the department as facing removal from the country.

Those listed include Emmanuel Omowaiye, arrested in Richmond, Texas, over mail fraud; Laurene Onwuka, arrested in Chantilly, Virginia, for fraud by impersonation; and Olusegun Shonekan, arrested in Newark, New Jersey, over wire fraud.

Others are Olusegun Olaseni, arrested in Greencastle, Indiana, over the sale of amphetamine; Peter Ude, arrested in Atlanta, Georgia, over wire fraud; and Newton Jemide, arrested in Fort Dix, New Jersey, over wire fraud, conspiracy and mail fraud.

The list also features Shedrack Umukoro, arrested in Yazoo City, Mississippi, over money laundering; Olasoji Akinbode, arrested in Kearny, New Jersey, over fraud by impersonation; and Oluwatosin Afolabi, arrested in Conroe, Texas, over fraud.

Other Nigerians identified by the department include Alameen Adetunji Tokosi, arrested in Chicago, Illinois, over heroin possession; Joshua Ipoade, arrested in Atlanta, Georgia, over wire fraud; and Michael Orji, arrested in Oxford, Wisconsin, over offences including weapons-related crimes, identity theft, fraud and money laundering.

The second group comprises Ahmadu Apooyin, arrested in Baltimore, Maryland, over a cocaine-related offence; Teslim Kiriji, arrested in Yazoo City, Mississippi, over money laundering; and Onomen Uduebor, arrested in Seattle, Washington, over identity theft.

Also listed are Charles Ochi and Daniel Eta, arrested in White Deer, Pennsylvania, over money laundering and wire fraud, respectively.

Others are Ifeanyi Ibennah, arrested in Tampa, Florida, over cruelty towards a child; Kazeem Runsewe, arrested in Thomson, Illinois, over wire fraud; and Fatiu Lawal, arrested in Lompoc, California, also over wire fraud.

The remaining names include Justin Akubueze, arrested in Orem, Utah, over money laundering; Moyinoluwaseun Okeowo, arrested in Orlando, Florida, over larceny, forgery and concealing stolen property; Babajide Oluwaseun Faseyi, arrested in Alden, New York, over assault; and Bright Eigbedion, arrested in Lompoc, California, over money laundering.

The DHS said the initiative was part of President Donald Trump’s administration’s efforts to remove foreign nationals involved in serious criminal activities from the United States.

In a statement on the website, the department said the platform highlights foreign nationals arrested by ICE who are being removed after engaging in serious criminal activities, including drug and weapons offences, violent crimes, fraud and the misuse or theft of public benefits.

The department launched the “Worst of the Worst” website on December 8, 2025, as a searchable database highlighting foreign nationals arrested by ICE across the United States.

However, the latest update does not specify when the 24 Nigerians would be deported or provide details of their individual immigration proceedings.

The inclusion of their names on the website also does not, by itself, establish that they have been convicted of the offences listed against them.

Vanguard News

title: 2027: Atiku storms Kogi, says Nigerians deserve to live with dignity
description:
By Luminous Jannamike



ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar on Tuesday took his campaign to Kogi State, declaring that Nigerians should be able to live with dignity in their own country.







At a rally, supporters reportedly chanted ‘Tinubu Must Go!’ as Atiku criticised the economic har
content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar on Tuesday took his campaign to Kogi State, declaring that Nigerians should be able to live with dignity in their own country.

At a rally, supporters reportedly chanted ‘Tinubu Must Go!’ as Atiku criticised the economic hardship facing households, traders and workers, and called for a change in the country’s economic direction.

In a statement by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said the reception in Kogi reflected the frustration of families struggling to cope with rising living costs.

“They came here in their numbers because they want to be heard. Their hardship is real, and their hope deserves an answer,” he said.

Atiku said his proposed economic approach would focus on reducing fuel costs, supporting local production and ensuring that Nigerians could get more value from their earnings.

“A mother should not have to choose between feeding her children and paying their school fees. A trader should not open a shop each morning wondering whether anyone can afford to buy. A young person should not work hard all day and still struggle to pay for the journey home. These are the lives behind the figures this government recites,” he said.

Explaining his campaign’s promise of affordable living, Atiku said the objective was to make it easier for ordinary Nigerians to meet their daily needs.

“When we say we will make life affordable again, we are speaking to the parent counting the last notes in a purse and the worker calculating whether a salary will last until month’s end,” he said.

Reacting to the chants against President Bola Tinubu, Atiku said they reflected the frustration of people who felt they had been asked to endure hardship without a clear end in sight.

“The people of Kogi are chanting ‘Tinubu Must Go’ because they are tired of being told to endure pain with no end in sight. I hear them. I see the faces in this crowd, and I know what is at stake. No family should have to beg for the chance to live with dignity in its own country,” he said.

He thanked the people of Kogi for their reception and urged his supporters to remain peaceful, while encouraging them to use their votes to determine the country’s political future.

“Let no one mistake your restraint for acceptance of hardship. Let your voices be heard, and let your votes decide Nigeria’s future,” he urged.

title: VIDEO: Woman gives birth to baby girl at Oshodi bus stop in Lagos
description:
A woman has given birth to a baby girl at the Oshodi underbridge bus stop in Lagos State after reportedly going into labour unexpectedly on Monday morning.
The incident, which occurred on November 23, 2026, attracted the attention of commuters and passers-by, with people at the scene reportedly rall
content:
A woman has given birth to a baby girl at the Oshodi underbridge bus stop in Lagos State after reportedly going into labour unexpectedly on Monday morning.

The incident, which occurred on November 23, 2026, attracted the attention of commuters and passers-by, with people at the scene reportedly rallying around the woman to assist her during the delivery.

The development was first reported on Facebook by Blessed N & M Enterprise, which shared the news alongside a congratulatory message.

“God is wonderful ooooo. Is a bouncing baby girl. A woman give birth at oshodi Lagos state this morning,” the page wrote.

In another post, the page celebrated the arrival of the baby girl, saying, “God is wonderful ooo. Is a baby girl oooo. A woman give birth at oshodi bustop just now.”

According to accounts shared on social media, the heavily pregnant woman went into labour at the bus stop after telling people around her that she could no longer move.

Commuters and women at the scene reportedly gathered around her, forming a protective circle to shield her from the crowd and provide some privacy as they helped her deliver the baby.

A Facebook user, Aduroja Foluke Olaoluwa, who also shared an account of the incident, said she was unable to look at the woman while passing because of the difficulty of the situation.

She, however, expressed concern over the behaviour of some boys who gathered around the woman, saying they were peeping instead of showing respect and giving her privacy.

“Where is our sense of humanity and respect? Not everything is for public entertainment,” she wrote.

Olaoluwa said a woman in labour deserved dignity, compassion and support, while praising the women who stood by the mother and helped her through the delivery.

“God bless the women who stood by her and helped her through that difficult moment. May God reward your kindness,” she added.

She also congratulated the woman on the birth of her daughter, wishing the baby good health and happiness for the family.

title: Soludo presents ₦893.4bn 2027 budget proposal to Anambra Assembly
description:
Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has presented a proposed budget of ₦893,435,059,830 for the 2027 fiscal year to the state House of Assembly.
The budget, themed “Solution 2.0: Unlocking New Axes for Sustainable Prosperity,” represents a 16.58 per cent increase over the 2026 fiscal esti
content:
Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has presented a proposed budget of ₦893,435,059,830 for the 2027 fiscal year to the state House of Assembly.

The budget, themed “Solution 2.0: Unlocking New Axes for Sustainable Prosperity,” represents a 16.58 per cent increase over the 2026 fiscal estimate.

Presenting the document to the lawmakers on Tuesday, Soludo said the theme reflected his administration’s commitment to expanding its development vision for the state.

The governor expressed gratitude to the people of the state for their support in the last election and acknowledged the partnership his administration had enjoyed with the legislature.

Reviewing his administration’s performance, Soludo cited achievements in security, healthcare delivery and sustainable infrastructure, among other sectors.

He said, “The success of the state’s free education policy, which currently benefits nearly 500,000 Anambra children, and plans to recruit 5,000 new teachers to build on the 8,115 teachers initially employed, are part of the achievements recorded under the previous budget.

“On fiscal discipline, the state has not borrowed from any commercial bank so far. We assure lawmakers and citizens that any future borrowing, if necessary, will be strictly guided and economically justified.”

In his remarks, the Speaker of the Anambra State House of Assembly, Somtochukwu Udeze, commended the governor for his developmental strides across various sectors of the state’s economy.

He also appreciated the upgrade of the Assembly complex, noting that the improvements had provided a more conducive environment for legislative business.

Highlighting the productivity of the current Assembly, Udeze said 44 bills had been passed, including 26 executive bills. He added that several of the laws could serve as legislative templates for other states.

While calling for the continuation of the productive relationship between the executive and legislative arms of government, the speaker stressed the need for both arms to respect their constitutional boundaries.

He expressed hope that the 2027 budget would address the pressing needs of the people and make a meaningful impact on their lives.

The post Soludo presents ₦893.4bn 2027 budget proposal to Anambra Assembly appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

Rhodes-Vivour, questioned whether Igbos were no
content:
By Enitan Abdultawab

The governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress in Lagos State, Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, has reacted to President Bola Tinubu’s appeal to Igbo residents in the state to support his re-election bid in 2027.

Rhodes-Vivour, questioned whether Igbos were now welcome to vote in Lagos after Tinubu met with Igbo leaders, traders and other stakeholders at a town hall meeting in the state.

“Wow!! Igbos are now welcome to vote in Lagos? Indeed, what God cannot do, doesn’t exist,” he wrote on X.

The meeting, organised by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiative, was held on Monday at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts, National Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos.

At the gathering, Tinubu appealed to the Igbo community to support his second term ambition, while acknowledging that some members of the community did not vote for him in the 2023 presidential election.

“Some of you did not vote for me in 2023; I vex o. Now, we have settled. Get your PVC, and you will vote for me this time. Come by January 16; you will vote. Agreement is agreement. Tinubu is APC,” the President said.

He also urged the Igbo residents to vote for Lagos Deputy Governor and APC governorship candidate, Obafemi Hamzat, as well as other candidates of the party in the 2027 elections.

The President described the Igbo as his brothers and sisters, saying his administration remained committed to inclusive governance, national unity and equity.

“I can commit to one thing: the unity of Nigeria. Though tribes and tongues may differ, in brotherhood we stand. None of us told God when we were born where we would be born or what language we would speak. Whether you are Igbo or Hausa, you have no control over yourself. God created you, created that opportunity. We are all Nigerians,” he said.

Tinubu further called on Nigerians to see themselves as people living together in one country, adding that no ethnic group or region would be left behind under his Renewed Hope Agenda.

He also acknowledged the contributions of Igbo communities to Nigeria’s economic growth and commended market leaders and business owners who left their businesses to attend the meeting.

title: NDC boycotts IGP’s security meeting over attacks on members
description:
… Condemns Escalating violence against its members



By Henry Umoru, Abuja



Disturbed by what it described as recurring cases of political thuggery and attacks against its members’ supporters, the national leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress: NDC has boycotted the security meeting calle
content:
… Condemns Escalating violence against its members

By Henry Umoru, Abuja

Disturbed by what it described as recurring cases of political thuggery and attacks against its members’ supporters, the national leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress: NDC has boycotted the security meeting called by the Inspector General of Police, IGP, Olatunji Disu.

The NDC, while condemning in the strongest terms the spate of violence orchestrated against its members across the country, said they no longer feel safe and protected by a police force that watches helplessly the slaughter of their members across the country by hired thugs of the ruling APC, adding that they will not lend legitimacy to a process that has failed to protect them.

Recall that amid growing concerns over political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, the IGP summoned chairmen and secretaries of all registered political parties to a meeting in Abuja to address attacks on campaign rallies, destruction of billboards and other campaign materials, as well as threats to public peace.

In a statement signed on Tuesday by NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, he said the violence against NDC members has become an intolerable pattern across the length and breadth of Nigeria.

The statement is titled “NDC boycotts IGP’s security meeting, condemns escalating violence against its members.”

The statement read, “The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) condemns in the strongest terms the spate of violence orchestrated against its members across the country.

“Therefore, the NDC has decided to boycott the security meeting called by the Inspector General of Police. We no longer feel safe and protected by a police force that watches helplessly the slaughter of our members across the country by hired thugs of the ruling APC. We will not lend legitimacy to a process that has failed to protect us.

“The violence against NDC members has become an intolerable pattern across the length and breadth of Nigeria.

“From Benue State, where our presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, was prevented from entering the state by thugs loyal to the APC government, to Edo, Calabar, Enugu and the incessant attacks on our members in Delta State, the political temperature is on the rise, with campaigns turned into a battlefield.

“Politics and campaigns are not supposed to be war. However, the APC government has turned the campaign into a battlefield, where lives have become nasty, brutish and uncertain.

“The situation is compounded by the complicity of the police and security forces. The killing of four members of the NDC in Delta State was done in the full glare of the police and security forces who were supposed to protect all Nigerians.

“Presently, the Nigeria Police has become an APC Police sustained by taxpayers’ money.

“The NDC and its members no longer feel safe and protected by the police and security agencies due to the manifest bias shown by their inability to carry out a proper investigation and make those responsible for the violence face the full wrath of the law.

“We call on the international community to compel President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the APC government to play by internationally accepted democratic standards.

“Democracy cannot survive where opposition members are hunted, attacked, and killed with impunity while state institutions look the other way.

“The NDC remains committed to peaceful, issue-based campaigns, but we will not be intimidated, silenced, or chased out of the democratic space.”

The post NDC boycotts IGP’s security meeting over attacks on members appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Uduere Killings: Oborevwori visits community, vows justice as Police confirm six dead
content:
Police probe possible security lapses;

women, youths protest killings;

Tributes pour in for slain activist Efemena Umukoro

Senator OmoAgege visits injured at the hospital

Senator Dafinone condemns killings

By Jimitota Onoyume

Governor Sheriff Oborevwori yesterday ( today) visited Uduere community in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State following the gruesome killing of six persons by suspected political thugs during a political rally, assuring residents that those responsible for the violence would be brought to justice.

Four of the deceased were reportedly members of the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC), who were in the community for the party’s Delta Central senatorial rally. The All Progressives Congress (APC) was also holding a meeting close to the venue of the NDC rally.

The governor, who appeared visibly disturbed by the killings, said his administration would work closely with security agencies to ensure that the perpetrators were identified, arrested and prosecuted.

He described the incident as particularly disturbing, coming just weeks before the general elections, and warned that his administration would no longer tolerate political violence in any part of the state.

“Those who know me know that I am not a violent person. That is why, in my MORE Agenda, the fourth pillar is dedicated to enhancing peace and security.

“We have been preaching peace, and Delta State has enjoyed relative peace since 2023. The important thing is how to sustain that peace. I want to assure the people that this will not happen again. This must stop. It must stop. We cannot continue like this,” he said.

Oborevwori was accompanied on the visit by the Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Area, Mr Jaro Egbo, and top security officers in the state.

Some community residents, particularly women, carried placards expressing outrage over the killings and demanding justice for the victims, especially the President-General of the community, who was among those killed.

Police confirm six deaths, probe security deployment

Meanwhile, the Nigeria Police Force has confirmed that six persons lost their lives during the violence that erupted at the NDC rally in Uduere, the hometown of the Ughelli North Council Chairman, Mr Jaro Egbo.

The confirmation was contained in a statement issued by the Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, who said the police had commenced a thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

The police also said the investigation would examine the deployment and conduct of officers assigned to provide security at the rally, including whether they discharged their responsibilities professionally.

The statement read: ” Preliminary Police reports indicate that six persons lost their lives, while several others sustained injuries. The Force is aware of varying casualty figures circulating in the public domain. An ongoing investigation will establish the verified number of casualties and determine the circumstances surrounding the incident.

“The Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, psc(+), NPM, has directed the Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, to immediately commence a thorough, impartial and evidence-based investigation into the incident.

“The investigation will establish the sequence of events, identify those responsible for the violence, and examine the circumstances surrounding the shooting, including the deployment and conduct of Police personnel at the venue.

“Any officer found to have acted negligently, unlawfully or in breach of professional standards will face appropriate disciplinary action, while all persons found culpable of criminal offences will be prosecuted in accordance with the law.”

Deltans question police neutrality –

Multiple sources claimed that about six police patrol vehicles were deployed to provide security during the rally, prompting concerns among residents and political observers over the effectiveness of the security arrangements.

“Why did the violence happen despite the presence of security operatives? Were the armed policemen unable to prevent the killings, or did they fail to discharge their responsibilities?” some Deltans queried.

The police have promised to examine the conduct of their personnel as part of the ongoing investigation.

Tributes pour in for slain activist Efemena Umukoro

Meanwhile, tributes have continued to pour in for Comrade Efemena Umukoro, popularly known as Akima, a prominent NDC member and one of those killed during the violence.

Umukoro was a renowned activist and former President of the youth wing of the Urhobo Progress Union (UPU), the apex socio-cultural organisation of the Urhobo nation.

The Board of Trustees of the Anti-Cult Volunteer Corps Nigeria has condemned his killing, describing him as a courageous member who was deeply committed to the struggle for justice, human rights and a peaceful Delta State.

In a statement, the Chairman of the Board, Comrade Amb. Eyefia Oliver, described his death as a devastating loss to the organisation, the human rights community and the many people whose lives he touched.

The statement said:

“Comrade Akima was a courageous human rights defender, a passionate advocate for the vulnerable and an active personality of great reputation whose dedication to humanity was evident in his everyday engagements.

“He was particularly known for his determination to seek justice for those who had been oppressed, victimised or denied their fundamental rights.

“He had a rare sense of responsibility towards the challenges of others, often handling people’s problems with the same urgency, compassion and determination as though they were his personal concerns.”

The organisation called on the Nigeria Police Force and other security agencies to conduct a thorough, professional and transparent investigation into his killing, identify all those connected with the crime and ensure they were prosecuted.

It warned that the circumstances surrounding his death must not be allowed to become another unresolved case.

The group also extended condolences to his aged parents, children, immediate family, friends and associates, insisting that his death was a painful blow to the struggle for justice and human rights.

“We demand justice for Akima. His killers must not go unpunished,” the statement added.

Oborevwori urged to make Delta politically safe

The killings have also triggered wider concerns over political security in Delta State, with residents urging Governor Oborevwori to take decisive steps to guarantee a level playing field for all political parties and candidates ahead of the general elections.

Some Deltans appealed to the governor to demonstrate, through concrete action, his commitment to peace, describing the protection of human lives as a responsibility that must transcend party affiliations.

One of the reactions drew attention to the governor’s recent appearance as an usher in a church ( which has earned him a nickname Chief Usher in the state) , urging him to reflect the values of Christianity in his approach to political governance.

“He should demonstrate the value for human life that Christianity is known for. The video of him performing the duties of an usher in a church recently went viral. We know him as a chief usher; let the Christ he professes be seen in his leadership,” the concerned resident said.

Others called on the governor to ensure that the blood of Urhobo youths was not continually shed because of political differences.

“Governor Sheriff should make sure the killing of Urhobo youths stops. We cannot continue to lose our young people because of party differences,” they said.

Orogun youths protest Efemena’s killing

Meanwhile, youths in Orogun community, the hometown of the late Efemena Umukoro, took to the streets to protest his gruesome killing.

The protesters condemned the violence and demanded justice, calling on the state government and security agencies to unravel the circumstances surrounding his death and bring those responsible to justice.

They insisted that his killing must not be swept under the carpet and urged security operatives to ensure that everyone connected with the crime was identified and prosecuted.

OmoAgege visits injured

Delta central candidate of the NDC Senator Ovie OmoAgege yesterday ( today) visited hospitalized members of his party receiving treatment at a hospital , urging them to be strong.

Senator Dafinone condemns the killing

Senator Ede Dafinone representing Delta central senatorial district and the senatorial candidate of the APC in the coming election has also condemned the killing , adding that the police should prosecute those behind the sad development.

“I received with profound shock and sadness the disturbing reports of violent clashes in Uduere Community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, which reportedly claimed several lives and left others injured. I unequivocally condemn this tragic loss of innocent lives and every act of violence, regardless of the circumstances or political affiliations of those involved. No political ambition, disagreement or grievance is worth the blood of any citizen.

“I call on the Nigeria Police Force and other relevant security agencies to conduct a thorough, impartial and transparent investigation into the circumstances surrounding this unfortunate incident, identify those responsible and ensure that justice is served in accordance with the law “, he said.

The post Uduere Killings: Oborevwori visits community, vows justice as Police confirm six dead appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: NASS Approves Tinubu’s $20.5bn, €1.45bn Supplementary External Borrowing Plan
description: The National Assembly has approved President Bola Tinubu’s request for a supplementary external borrowing plan of $20.517 billion and €1.45 billion for 2026 and 2027.The Senate approved the request on Tuesday following consideration of the recommendations of its Committee on Local and For
content:
The National Assembly has approved President Bola Tinubu’s request for a supplementary external borrowing plan of $20.517 billion and €1.45 billion for 2026 and 2027.

The Senate approved the request on Tuesday following consideration of the recommendations of its Committee on Local and Foreign Loans.

The approval came after the House of Representatives also endorsed the President’s borrowing plan.

The proposed borrowing was calculated at an exchange rate of ₦1,400 to the dollar.

Earlier on Tuesday, President Tinubu wrote to the Senate, seeking approval for a revised 2026 budget that reduces the previously approved expenditure by more than ₦3 trillion.

The proposal, titled ‘Transmission of FGN 2026 Appropriation Repeal and Re-enactment Bill and Revised 2026 Federal Government Fiscal Framework’, was presented during plenary by Senate President Godswill Akpabio.

Akpabio subsequently referred the correspondence to the Senate Committee on Rules and Business for legislative consideration.

Under the revised fiscal framework, aggregate expenditure is projected at ₦65.176 trillion, down from the ₦68.323 trillion earlier approved by the National Assembly.

Projected Federal Government revenue, including receipts from government-owned enterprises, stands at ₦33.720 trillion, while capital expenditure is pegged at ₦26.232 trillion.

Despite the reduction in overall expenditure, the fiscal deficit remains unchanged at ₦31.457 trillion, representing 5.64 per cent of the country’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

The proposed new borrowing of ₦29.218 trillion also remains unchanged. This comprises ₦18.428 trillion in domestic borrowing and ₦10.790 trillion in external borrowing.

Tinubu explained that the proposed $7.7 billion external loan, estimated at ₦10.368 trillion, would finance an existing foreign borrowing provision and would not increase the overall borrowing limit.

According to the President, the adjustments are intended to prioritise existing commitments, strengthen the credibility of the budget and improve capital budget implementation while maintaining fiscal discipline.

The development comes amid expectations that Tinubu will present the 2027 budget to the National Assembly before the end of December.

content:
The Federal Road Safety Corps, FRSC Zamfara state Command under the leadership of CC Aliyu Magaji has confirmed the sudden death of 15 people in a fatal car crash at Kisami Village, 67Km along Gummi-Daki Takwas-Anka Road.

This was contained in a statement signed by SRC Isah Aliyu Kankara on behalf of Sector Commander
RS10.3 Zamfara on Tuesday and made available to Journalists in Gusau.

According to the statement, the fatal road traffic crash occurred on 23rd November, 2026 at about 12:30hrs at Kisami Village, Km 67 along Gummi – Daki Takwas – Anka Road, where vehicles Involving Toyota Camry (Ash) and Fuso Canter (White) crashed.

Preliminary investigation revealed that, the Cause of the auto traffic crash was was a result of wrongful Overtaking and Loss of Control in the part of both drivers.

Casualties details include 52 people, 17killed (all male), 25 injured and 10 escaped unhurt

The FRSC Zamfara state Command’s rescue team responded within 10 minutes and evacuated the injured and corpses to General Hospital in Gummi.

The Sector Commander CC ALIYu Maaji sympathizes with The govt and people of Zamfara as well as the families of the deceased and warned motorists to avoid wrongful, overtaking overloading and over-speeding.

title: NDC boycotts IG’s security meeting over attacks on members
description:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress on Tuesday announced its decision to boycott a security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, citing alleged police bias and failure to protect its members from attacks by suspected political thugs.
The opposition party said it no longer had confidence
content:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress on Tuesday announced its decision to boycott a security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, citing alleged police bias and failure to protect its members from attacks by suspected political thugs.

The opposition party said it no longer had confidence in the Nigeria Police Force, accusing security operatives of failing to prevent violence against its members allegedly perpetrated by supporters of the ruling All Progressives Congress.

The decision followed a series of reported attacks on NDC members and campaign activities in different parts of the country, including Benue, Edo, Cross River, Enugu and Delta states.

In a statement signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, the party condemned what it described as a growing pattern of politically motivated violence against its members and accused the police of failing to investigate the incidents and prosecute those responsible.

He said, “The NDC has decided to boycott the security meeting called by the Inspector-General of Police. We no longer feel safe and protected by a Police Force that watches helplessly the slaughter of our members across the country by hired thugs of the ruling APC.

“We will not lend legitimacy to a process that has failed to protect us.”

Director specifically recalled an incident in Benue State, where he said their presidential candidate, Peter Obi, was prevented from entering the state by thugs loyal to the APC government.

The party spokesman also cited attacks in Edo, Calabar and Enugu, as well as repeated assaults on its members in Delta State, warning that the growing violence could undermine the conduct of peaceful campaigns ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He said, “Politics and campaigns are not supposed to be war. However, the APC government has turned the campaign into a battlefield, where lives have become nasty, brutish and uncertain.”

The NDC further raised concerns that the police and other security agencies failed to intervene during the killing of four of its members in Delta State, describing the incident as evidence of the alleged compromise of security institutions.

“The situation is compounded by the complicity of the Police and security forces. The killing of four members of the NDC in Delta State was done in the full glare of the Police and security forces who were supposed to protect all Nigerians,” it added.

Director said the party’s decision to shun the meeting was informed by what he described as the failure of security agencies to conduct credible investigations into attacks on its members and bring the perpetrators to justice.

The NDC called on the international community to prevail on President Bola Tinubu and the APC-led Federal Government to uphold democratic standards and guarantee the safety of opposition politicians.

“We call on the international community to compel President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the APC government to play by internationally accepted democratic standards.

“Democracy cannot survive where opposition members are hunted, attacked, and killed with impunity while state institutions look the other way,” the party said.

Despite its grievances, the NDC maintained that it remained committed to peaceful campaigns, insisting that the alleged attacks would not force it out of the political process.

The post NDC boycotts IG’s security meeting over attacks on members appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Mock Accreditation: INEC Urges Nigerians To Participate In Exercise Ahead Of 2027 Elections
description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has urged Nigerians to participate in its 2026 Mock Accreditation Exercise scheduled to hold nationwide on November 28, 2026, as part of efforts to assess the readiness and functionality of its electoral technology ahead of the 2027 general electi
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has urged Nigerians to participate in its 2026 Mock Accreditation Exercise scheduled to hold nationwide on November 28, 2026, as part of efforts to assess the readiness and functionality of its electoral technology ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The Director of Voter Education and Publicity at INEC, Victoria Meci, made the call during an appearance on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Tuesday.

Meci explained that the exercise would serve as a test run of the commission’s technological equipment, particularly the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS), noting that INEC would not wait until the 2027 general elections before testing the system’s effectiveness and reliability.

“We don’t want to wait till the elections before we test the ruggedness, readiness and functionality of the system,” she said.

She acknowledged the challenges experienced during the 2023 general elections, explaining that the commission was taking proactive steps to address previous shortcomings and improve the conduct of the 2027 elections.

She also disclosed that INEC had reduced the accreditation threshold to 850 voters per BVAS machine, adding that polling units with more than 850 registered voters would be provided with multiple BVAS devices to ensure a smoother and more efficient accreditation process.

On the electronic transmission and viewing of election results, Meci stated that Nigerians would be able to follow the performance of candidates as results are uploaded, subject to network availability.

“The commission has assured Nigerians that, if the network is in order, results will be uploaded to the IREV portal,” she said.

She added that the commission was committed to transparency and encouraged Nigerians to monitor the process and report any challenges encountered during the exercise.

Meci further disclosed that INEC would deploy trained personnel to the selected polling units, adding that adequate training would be provided ahead of the exercise to ensure the effective use of the technology.

According to her, 17,676 polling units have been selected for the nationwide exercise.

She urged eligible voters in the selected polling units to turn out and participate, noting that the list of designated polling units had been published on the commission’s official website.

On security arrangements, the director said INEC was working in collaboration with security agencies to ensure the safety of electoral personnel and voters at all designated polling units.

She added that the commission expects the mock exercise to provide an opportunity to identify and address possible technical challenges ahead of the 2027 general elections.

title: AFCON dispute: Morocco accuses Senegal FA chief of contacting CAS arbitrator
description:
The Royal Moroccan Football Federation has reportedly accused Senegalese Football Federation of speaking by phone with one of the three arbitrators handling Senegal’s appeal against the Confederation of African Football’s decision to award Morocco the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title.
The RMFF claim
content:
The Royal Moroccan Football Federation has reportedly accused Senegalese Football Federation of speaking by phone with one of the three arbitrators handling Senegal’s appeal against the Confederation of African Football’s decision to award Morocco the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title.

The RMFF claimed FSF President Abdoulaye Fall called the Court of Arbitration for Sport’s official while the case is ongoing, according to multiple reports, including Reuters and Moroccan media outlet Hespress.

Reuters, citing a source with direct knowledge of the matter, reported on Tuesday that Morocco’s federation had notified CAS of the alleged incident during the proceedings, ahead of its ruling on Senegal’s appeal.

The source, who declined to be named because they were not authorised to discuss the case, alleged that Fall spoke by phone with one of the three arbitrators on Sunday.

Hespress, citing French sports broadcaster RMC Sport, reported that the Moroccan federation’s legal adviser had sent an official letter to CAS seeking clarification over the alleged conversation between Fall and a German legal expert serving on the arbitration panel.

The Moroccan federation reportedly asked the court to clarify the circumstances surrounding the contact, citing concerns about the independence and impartiality of the proceedings.

PUNCH Online could not independently verify whether the alleged call took place or establish what was discussed. CAS had yet to comment on the report as of the time of publication.

The Senegalese Football Federation has denied the allegation.

According to Senegalese media outlet SeneNews, the federation’s Secretary-General, Sow, dismissed the claim, describing it as “an imaginary appeal”.

“President Abdoulaye Fall doesn’t even know the judges involved in this case, because he wasn’t present on the day of the hearing,” he said.

The development comes as CAS is expected to deliver its verdict on Tuesday afternoon in the appeal filed by the Senegalese federation against CAF and the Moroccan federation.

In a procedural update on Monday, CAS said both countries had been notified that its decision would be delivered on Tuesday, November 24, 2026.

The dispute followed the controversial AFCON final played at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat on January 18, 2026, where Senegal defeated hosts Morocco 1-0 after extra time to win their second continental title.

The final was disrupted in stoppage time after the referee awarded Morocco a penalty following a VAR review, shortly after Senegal had a goal ruled out.

Angered by the decision, Senegal coach Pape Thiaw instructed his players to leave the pitch in protest. They returned after about 14 minutes, and Morocco’s Brahim Diaz subsequently missed the penalty before Pape Gueye scored Senegal’s winning goal in extra time.

Morocco later lodged a complaint with CAF, arguing that Senegal’s withdrawal from the pitch disrupted the normal course of the match.

CAF’s Appeals Board, on March 17, overturned the earlier disciplinary ruling and declared Senegal to have forfeited the final for breaching Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations. It consequently awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory.

Senegal rejected the decision and filed an appeal at CAS on March 25, seeking to have CAF’s ruling overturned and the original 1-0 result restored.

The case was heard at CAS headquarters in Lausanne, Switzerland, on October 8, with representatives of Senegal, Morocco and CAF presenting their arguments behind closed doors.

The post AFCON dispute: Morocco accuses Senegal FA chief of contacting CAS arbitrator appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

description: President Bola Tinubu has forwarded a compilation of Nigeria’s revised and updated laws to the Senate for consideration.According to the President’s letter, which was read during plenary by the President of the Senate, Tinubu explained that the review exercise, which commenced in 2024 th
content:
President Bola Tinubu has forwarded a compilation of Nigeria’s revised and updated laws to the Senate for consideration.

According to the President’s letter, which was read during plenary by the President of the Senate, Tinubu explained that the review exercise, which commenced in 2024 through a committee established under the office of the Attorney-General of the Federation, is aimed at updating and consolidating the country’s laws to reflect current realities.

President Tinubu also noted in the correspondence that the last comprehensive review and updating of Nigeria’s laws took place in 2004, more than two decades ago.

Meanwhile, some lawmakers immediately demanded that a thorough examination of the document be conducted before deciding whether to accept or reject it.

Senator Yahaya Abdullahi described the exercise as a step in the right direction but underscored the need for closer scrutiny of the various volumes to ensure accuracy and completeness.

The Deputy Senate President, Barau Jibrin, corroborated this by stating that the need for the analysis is a process embedded within the Senate’s rules and established legislative procedures.

Further aligning with the submissions, Senate President Godswill Akpabio noted that the compilation comprises several volumes and would therefore require considerable time to review.

He said the National Assembly would compare the revised compilation with laws previously passed by the legislature and assented to by the President to identify discrepancies and establish their accuracy.

He added that a summarised report should subsequently be presented to the chamber for consideration.

The exercise is subsequently referred to the committees on judiciary, human rights and legal matters, and rules and business alongside the management of the National Assembly for further action.

title: 2027: Court voids Omo-Agege’s NDC ticket, orders INEC to delist him
description: The Federal High Court sitting in Warri, Delta State, on Tuesday nullified the nomination of former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, as the Nigeria Democratic Congress candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections, citing non-compliance with the provis
content:
The Federal High Court sitting in Warri, Delta State, on Tuesday nullified the nomination of former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, as the Nigeria Democratic Congress candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections, citing non-compliance with the provisions of the Electoral Act.

The nullification was contained in the court’s judgment following a suit marked FHC/WR/CS/120/2026, instituted by Prof. Alexander Osondu Akpodiete.

The suit is challenging the validity of Omo-Agege’s nomination on grounds bordering on his resignation from the All Progressives Congress, membership of the NDC and eligibility to participate in the party’s senatorial primary.

Delivering the judgment, Justice Hyeladzira Nganjiwa ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission to remove Omo-Agege’s name forthwith from its list of candidates for the election and restrained the former Deputy Senate President from parading himself as the NDC senatorial candidate.

Justice Nganjiwa dismissed all five preliminary objections raised by Omo-Agege, the NDC and INEC challenging the competence of the suit before proceeding to determine the substantive issues raised by the plaintiff.

In a further setback for the NDC, the court held that the statutory window for conducting fresh primaries to nominate another candidate had elapsed, as the Electoral Act prescribed a timeline of 180 days before the general elections.

Justice Nganjiwa held that the NDC failed to comply with the Electoral Act’s mandatory provisions on submitting its membership register to INEC before its primary election.

The court also found that Omo-Agege’s name was not contained in the NDC membership register submitted to INEC at least 21 days before the party’s primary election.

In addition, the court held that the NDC failed to provide credible evidence establishing that its membership register was subsequently updated and submitted to INEC within the statutory period preceding the primary.

Relying on INEC’s revised electoral timetable, the court noted that Omo-Agege participated in the APC senatorial primary held on May 18, 2026, a development which, according to the court, established that he was still a member of the APC at the material time.

Justice Nganjiwa maintained that only persons whose names appeared in a political party’s membership register, in accordance with the requirements of the Electoral Act, were eligible to participate in its primary elections.

On the admissibility of a previously withdrawn affidavit, the court held that a party was entitled to withdraw an affidavit already filed in a proceeding, adding that once withdrawn, such an affidavit ceased to form part of the court’s records and could not be relied upon in determining the matter.

The judge maintained that a valid nomination could not be founded on a process that failed to satisfy statutory requirements, stressing that where a political party failed to comply with the Electoral Act in nominating its candidate, INEC was not permitted to include such a candidate on the ballot.

Consequently, the court invalidated Omo-Agege’s nomination, directed INEC to delist him and restrained him from presenting himself as the NDC candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the forthcoming general elections.

Also, responses from Omo-Agege, the NDC and INEC to the judgment could not be immediately obtained by journalists.

title: ‘How I saw devil thrice; gates of hell’ – Pope Francis
description:
The late Pope Francis recounted seeing the devil three times and, on one occasion, the “gate of hell”, in excerpts from his personal diary published Tuesday in a new book.



“The Private Diary of Pope Francis,” by Argentine Cardinal Victor Manuel Fernandez, includes passages taken from a journal th
content:
The late Pope Francis recounted seeing the devil three times and, on one occasion, the “gate of hell”, in excerpts from his personal diary published Tuesday in a new book.

“The Private Diary of Pope Francis,” by Argentine Cardinal Victor Manuel Fernandez, includes passages taken from a journal the former Jorge Bergoglio kept between 1992 and 2024, a document that reveals his worries, regrets and self-critiques — as well as his enormous humanity and faith.

Fernandez, head of the Vatican’s Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith, said he was asked by Francis to help make known to the world the musings inside the black plastic journal.

Upon Francis’s death last year, Fernandez expressed concern to his successor, Leo XIV, that the book “might end up abandoned in a warehouse somewhere”. He was allowed to publish passages, noting that “the spiritual concerns present in his heart are very explicit and can be helpful to us”.

In one of the most intriguing revelations, Francis writes that while archbishop of Buenos Aires, he saw the devil three different times including “from the car when I was returning to the house, and in the choir loft during Mass” and once in Rome following a visit to Chile.

“I discovered that the devil had been brazenly lurking around cunningly,” wrote Francis in his journal on January 24, 2021, according to a copy of the English language version of the book published by Penguin Random House and viewed by AFP.

Francis wrote that he recalled three episodes “when I don’t doubt he was physically present”.

“More or less fifteen years ago. I saw him from the car window. I can’t forget his menacing and, at the same time, seductive eyes,” he wrote.

During the second episode inside a Carmelite chapel, Francis wrote: “He was watching me with eyes of fire”.

“I can’t forget that gaze, stronger than the previous. They were like flames of fire.”

The third episode occurred during a meeting in Rome, following a visit to Chile.

“I saw him and heard his voice, triumphant, possessing everything… I can’t forget the powerful raspiness of his voice,” he wrote, adding that “the Lord granted me an opportunity to leave that meeting, and he thus freed me”.

Francis also revealed, on June 7, 2018, that on the night before, while getting ready to go to sleep, he “saw the entrance to hell”.

“Pagan seduction in full force. I peeked in to look a little, and it terrified me,” he said, adding that he “grabbed the Rosary as a weapon”.

“It’s dangerous to approach the gate of hell because flames can leap out and burn,” he wrote.

Self critiques

Throughout the diary, Francis does not hesitate to criticise himself, for his occasional “feelings of disdain, envy, pride” or for having ignored a drunk man in the street who addressed him “because I wanted to have a serene walk”.

“The proud, self-sufficient, cynical, self-deceptive Jorge,” is how the former pope described himself on December 30, 2022.

On January 15, 2017, he confessed that for a few days he had been experiencing “a very bad spirit of anger and discontent”.

While charismatic, Pope Francis also had a strong personality and was sometimes criticised within the Curia, the Catholic Church’s governing body, for being authoritarian.

Mercy is a recurrent theme in the journal.

“I felt, looking back, all the evil I’ve done in life. I’m in such abundant need of the Lord’s mercy!” he wrote on January 5, 1997.

End of life

Pope Francis appeared to worry that his days on Earth would be short-lived, fretting over his ageing and the need to “bear it”.

In 1996, at age 60 – nearly three decades before his death – he wrote: “I want to do good during the little time I have left, desiring to be good.

“How much time I’ve used badly! How much badly done!”

In 2001, he wrote that “these 65 years make me think about the end. I’m already counting down”.

The worries continued even after becoming pope in 2013, with Francis writing on April 9, 2016 that “the attacks of the devil under different aspects have increased… Could it be a sign that my time is up and he doesn’t want to lose?”

The journal contains 86 pages written before his election as pope in 2013, and another 55 written afterwards.

One of the briefest – and most moving – passages in Francis’s diary comes on July 21, 2013: “On March 13, they elected me pope.”

Francis died on April 21, 2025.

Vanguard News

title: Trump gains possibly millions from Nvidia shares after Huang’s return – Report
description:
The spectacular rebound in Nvidia’s share price following Jensen Huang’s return as chief executive could have added as much as $15 million to US President Donald Trump’s holdings in the stock on Monday, according to calculations by the Financial Times.



Huang resigned on November 12 over extramari
content:
The spectacular rebound in Nvidia’s share price following Jensen Huang’s return as chief executive could have added as much as $15 million to US President Donald Trump’s holdings in the stock on Monday, according to calculations by the Financial Times.

Huang resigned on November 12 over extramarital affairs including one with a suspected Chinese spy, a departure that sent shares in the US chip giant tumbling.

News of his return sent Nvidia shares soaring more than 30 percent and added more than $900 billion to the company’s market value.

According to the Financial Times, Trump may have owned as many as 370,000 shares in Nvidia as of September 30.

The newspaper based its estimate on the president’s financial disclosures to the Office of Government Ethics, the most recent of which was filed on November 5.

The disclosures do not include precise figures for disposals and purchases of shares.

The maximum figure for his holdings was therefore calculated on the assumption of purchases at the upper limit of each range, and sales at the lower limit.

A report from ABC News, citing Trump’s annual financial disclosure report, did not specify the number of shares he owned but said their value reached at least $12 million by the end of 2025.

It added that his accounts have continued to trade Nvidia in recent months, citing separate filings.

Nvidia said Monday that it had reinstated Huang as chief executive after receiving information from the US government that he did not pose a national security risk.

Trump said Huang’s return followed his own direct contacts with Nvidia’s board.

“I’ve been speaking to the board directly and indirectly, and I felt very strongly about it,” he told US broadcaster CNBC.

Ruben Gallego, a Democratic senator for Arizona, called for scrutiny of Trump’s portfolio.

“We need to investigate what stock positions took place before the announcement,” he said in a post on X. “This White House is the most corrupt in history.”
