description:
The Federal High Court sitting in Warri, Delta State, has nullified the nomination of former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, as the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections.
The court, presided over by Justice Hyeladzira
content:
The Federal High Court sitting in Warri, Delta State, has nullified the nomination of former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, as the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections.

The court, presided over by Justice Hyeladzira Ajiya Nganjiwa, directed the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to remove Omo-Agege’s name from its list of candidates and restrained him from presenting himself as the party’s senatorial candidate.

Delivering judgment on Tuesday, the court ruled that the NDC failed to comply with mandatory provisions of the Electoral Act in the process leading to Omo-Agege’s nomination.

The judge also held that the statutory period for conducting fresh primaries to select another candidate had elapsed, noting that the law prescribed a 180-day window before the general election.

The judgment followed a suit filed by Prof. Alexander Osondu Akpodiete, marked FHC/WR/CS/120/2026, challenging the validity of Omo-Agege’s nomination.

The plaintiff’s case centred on issues surrounding Omo-Agege’s resignation from the All Progressives Congress (APC), his membership of the NDC and his eligibility to participate in the party’s senatorial primary.

Before determining the substantive issues, Justice Nganjiwa dismissed five preliminary objections raised by Omo-Agege, the NDC and INEC challenging the competence of the suit.

The court found that the NDC failed to submit a valid membership register to INEC in accordance with the Electoral Act before conducting its primary election.

It held that Omo-Agege’s name was absent from the party’s membership register submitted to the electoral commission at least 21 days before the primary.

The judge further noted that the NDC failed to provide credible evidence showing that the register was subsequently updated and submitted to INEC within the period prescribed by law.

On Omo-Agege’s political affiliation, the court relied on INEC’s revised electoral timetable, which showed that he participated in the APC senatorial primary conducted on May 18, 2026.

According to the judge, the development established that Omo-Agege was still a member of the APC at the material time.

Justice Nganjiwa emphasised that only individuals whose names appeared in a political party’s membership register, in compliance with the Electoral Act, were eligible to participate in its primary elections.

The court also addressed the admissibility of a previously withdrawn affidavit, ruling that a party could withdraw an affidavit already filed in a proceeding. It added that such a document ceased to form part of the court’s records once withdrawn and could no longer be relied upon.

The judge maintained that a political party’s nomination could not stand where the process failed to satisfy statutory requirements, stressing that INEC could not recognise a candidate produced through an unlawful process.

Consequently, the court invalidated Omo-Agege’s nomination, ordered INEC to delist him and barred him from parading himself as the NDC candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections.

title: Ex-DSS officer sentenced to two years in prison over recruitment fraud
description:
A magistrate court in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) has sentenced a former Department of State Services (DSS) officer, Salihu Mohammed, to two years in prison for recruitment fraud.
The presiding judge, Moriyike Osinbajo, convicted Mohammed on Monday after he pleaded guilty to a one-count char
content:
A magistrate court in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) has sentenced a former Department of State Services (DSS) officer, Salihu Mohammed, to two years in prison for recruitment fraud.

The presiding judge, Moriyike Osinbajo, convicted Mohammed on Monday after he pleaded guilty to a one-count charge of cheating by impersonation.

Mohammed, who had earlier been dismissed from the DSS, was subsequently sentenced to two years’ imprisonment.

Osinbajo sentenced the dismissed DSS official without an option of fine and ordered him to pay restitution of N2.5 million to the victim.

Mohammed was accused of conspiring with an accomplice to fraudulently obtain money from Abdulkadir Liman and Abdullahi Alhassan under the guise of facilitating their recruitment into the DSS.

Very Nigerian understands that after a report on the recruitment fraud, the DSS director-general ordered an immediate investigation into the matter.

A source said it was established that Mohammed violated the service’s extant rules and regulations.

Subsequently, Mohammed was dismissed from the DSS.

In November 2025, the DSS announced the dismissal of 115 personnel as part of ongoing reforms in the agency.

The secret police advised the public to desist from dealing with the dismissed personnel.

The agency also published the names and pictures of the 115 disengaged officers on its website.

title: NPA: Maritime Coalition urges Tinubu to strengthen leadership capacity, transparency, ongoing port reforms
description:
A Coalition of Maritime and Energy Consultants in Nigeria has called on President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to consider strengthening the leadership and administrative capacity of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) to accelerate reforms and improve efficiency in the nation’s maritime sector.
The Coalition,
content:
A Coalition of Maritime and Energy Consultants in Nigeria has called on President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to consider strengthening the leadership and administrative capacity of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) to accelerate reforms and improve efficiency in the nation’s maritime sector.

The Coalition, through its spokesperson, Engr. Danjuma Yakubu, said effective leadership, transparency and accountability were essential to achieving the President’s vision of transforming Nigeria into a leading maritime and logistics hub in Africa.

In a statement issued on behalf of the coalition and other maritime groups, Yakubu noted that the NPA, under the leadership of its Managing Director, Dr. Abubakar Dantsoho, had faced several governance, procurement and operational concerns since his appointment in July 2024, which, according to the group, required attention to strengthen institutional performance.

The coalition specifically highlighted the controversy surrounding the reported $25 million emergency dredging contract for the Warri-Escravos Channel in 2025, which generated public discussions about the procurement process, the justification for the emergency procedure and compliance with established procurement regulations.

Although the NPA had defended the contract, maintaining that due process was followed in line with the Public Procurement Act, the coalition said the issues surrounding the project underscored the importance of greater transparency and public disclosure in the management of public resources.

They also called for closer scrutiny of the Authority’s multi-billion-naira budgetary allocations, particularly expenditures relating to dredging, consultancy services, environmental sanitation, conferences and administrative activities.

According to the group, independent reviews and comprehensive disclosures would help establish value for money, strengthen public confidence and promote accountability in the management of the Authority’s finances.

Another issue raised by the coalition was the status of expired port concession agreements and terminal leases, with some reportedly dating back to 2016 and 2021.

The group said the absence of publicly available terminal-by-terminal performance audits and clear timelines for concluding concession reviews had created uncertainty within the maritime industry.

The coalition observed that addressing the outstanding concession issues would provide greater regulatory certainty, encourage fresh investments, promote competition, facilitate terminal modernisation and improve government revenue.

They also called for an independent assessment of reported procurement disputes and administrative concerns involving the Authority, noting that regular institutional reviews would help identify areas requiring improvement and strengthen confidence among contractors and other industry stakeholders.

On operational efficiency, the group expressed concern over persistent challenges at Nigerian ports, including congestion, high charges, prolonged cargo clearance and infrastructure limitations.
It cited industry reports which reportedly put cargo dwell time at Apapa and Tin Can Island ports at between 18 and 21 days, compared with a global benchmark of about four days, while port charges were said to be 30 to 40 per cent higher than those of competing regional ports.

The coalition said addressing these challenges would be important to reducing the cost of doing business, improving Nigeria’s competitiveness and attracting more foreign investment.

They also referenced concerns raised by the Presidential Enabling Business Environment Council regarding the economic implications of port inefficiencies, stressing the need for sustained collaboration among relevant government agencies and maritime stakeholders to improve service delivery.

The group maintained that resolving governance, concession and operational challenges at the NPA would be critical to ensuring that ongoing investments in the maritime sector translate into tangible economic benefits.

They acknowledged the Federal Government’s commitment to expanding Nigeria’s maritime infrastructure, citing initiatives such as the approval of the Ibom Deep Seaport in Akwa Ibom State, the proposed development of the Bakassi Deep Seaport in Cross River State and the full operationalisation of the Tsamiya Inland Dry Port in Kebbi State.

They also referenced plans to modernise the Onne, Rivers, Delta and Calabar ports, alongside the modernisation programmes for Apapa and Tin Can Island ports.

According to the coalition, these projects offer significant opportunities for economic diversification, employment generation, regional trade expansion and increased government revenue.

They, however, stressed that infrastructure development must be supported by effective institutional management, investor-friendly policies, efficient concession administration and improved port operations to achieve the desired outcomes.

The group therefore urged President Tinubu to assess the current leadership structure at the NPA and consider the appointment of a maritime professional with proven administrative experience, integrity and a strong understanding of contemporary port management.

They said such leadership would be expected to prioritise accountability, tackle operational bottlenecks, accelerate digital transformation and create an enabling environment for investors and other stakeholders.

The coalition further called for stronger institutional coordination to ensure that the NPA effectively supports the Federal Government’s Renewed Hope Agenda and broader efforts to reposition Nigeria’s maritime economy.

The group said sustained attention to leadership effectiveness, transparency and operational reforms would help translate the President’s maritime development plans into measurable results for the country.

title: Tinubu seeks National Assembly’s nod to reduce 2026 budget from N68.32tn to N65.18tn
description:
President Bola Tinubu has forwarded a bill to the House of Representatives seeking to repeal and re-enact the 2026 Appropriation Act, proposing a reduction in the national budget from N68.32 trillion to N65.18 trillion.
Despite the proposed reduction in total expenditure, the President maintained th
content:
President Bola Tinubu has forwarded a bill to the House of Representatives seeking to repeal and re-enact the 2026 Appropriation Act, proposing a reduction in the national budget from N68.32 trillion to N65.18 trillion.

Despite the proposed reduction in total expenditure, the President maintained the fiscal deficit at N31.46 trillion.

The revised budget estimates the Federal Government’s revenue at N33.72 trillion, including earnings expected from Government-Owned Enterprises (GOEs), while capital expenditure is projected at N26.23 trillion.

Tinubu’s request was contained in a letter dated November 20, 2026, addressed to the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas.

The letter was read to lawmakers during plenary on Tuesday as the President sought the National Assembly’s consideration and approval of the proposed changes to the 2026 budget.

The President also transmitted a revised 2026 Federal Government Fiscal Framework, explaining that the adjustments were intended to align the budget with existing obligations and available resources.

According to the letter, the revision seeks to regularise some expenditures incurred by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) on behalf of the Federation, address underprovided debt-service obligations, recognise issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments, and provide for refunds to Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) and special accounts.

Tinubu said capital provisions for MDAs consisted mainly of amounts already warranted, while a few new capital and overhead allocations were introduced to address priority national interventions.

He identified the completion of critical road projects, protection of agricultural production, reduction of production costs, improvement of farm yields, enhanced market access and measures to address water vulnerability as key priorities.

The President said the revised fiscal framework was designed to prioritise existing commitments, improve the credibility and execution of the capital budget, and maintain fiscal restraint.

Despite the reduction in the overall budget, the fiscal deficit, including project-tied loans, remains unchanged at N31.457tn, representing 5.64 per cent of the Gross Domestic Product.

Tinubu also retained the proposed new borrowing of N29.22tn, comprising N18.43tn in domestic borrowing and N10.79tn in foreign borrowing.

On the proposed external borrowing, the President said the planned $7.7bn loan, estimated at N10.37tn using an exchange rate of N1,346.50 to the dollar, was intended to finance the existing foreign borrowing provision without increasing the borrowing envelope.

The letter read: “The proposal aligns the 2026 budget with existing obligations and available resources. It regularises some NNPCL expenditures incurred on behalf of the Federation, addresses underprovided debt-service obligations, recognises issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments, and provides for refunds to Ministries, Departments and Agencies and Special Accounts.

“MDA capital provision consists mainly of amounts already warranted. A few new MDA capital and overhead provisions were included as priority national interventions, particularly to complete critical road projects, protect agricultural production, reduce production costs, improve farm yields, and enhance market access, while addressing water vulnerability.

“Under the revised framework, aggregate expenditure is N65.176tn, compared with N68.323tn in the approved budget, while projected FGN revenue, including Government-Owned Enterprises, is N33.720tn. Aggregate capital expenditure is N26.232tn.

“The fiscal deficit, including project-tied loans, remains unchanged at N31.457tn, equivalent to 5.64 per cent of GDP. These adjustments prioritise existing commitments and improve the credibility and execution of the capital budget while maintaining fiscal restraint.”

Seeking the cooperation of lawmakers for speedy passage, Tinubu said the revised appropriation was necessary to ensure the orderly implementation of the budget and settlement of outstanding obligations.

“I, therefore, request the kind cooperation of the House of Representatives for expeditious consideration and passage of the Bill to facilitate orderly implementation of the revised budget and settlement of existing obligations,” he added.

The bill will be subjected to legislative scrutiny before the revised appropriation can take effect. Its passage would provide the legal basis for the Federal Government to implement the adjusted spending plan and meet the obligations outlined in the revised fiscal framework.

title: Plateau govt to recruit 7,000 personnel for state police
description:
The Plateau State Government is considering the recruitment of between 5,000 and 7,000 personnel for its proposed state police service as part of measures to improve security and address growing insecurity across the state.
The proposal was made public on Tuesday by retired Deputy Inspector-General
content:
The Plateau State Government is considering the recruitment of between 5,000 and 7,000 personnel for its proposed state police service as part of measures to improve security and address growing insecurity across the state.

The proposal was made public on Tuesday by retired Deputy Inspector-General of Police, Habila Joshak, chairman of the 14-member Plateau State Advisory Committee on State Police.

Joshak disclosed the plan while presenting the committee’s interim report to the state government in Jos.

The proposed recruitment is expected to strengthen security operations across Plateau State and support efforts to tackle the rising security challenges affecting communities in the state.

“We propose an implementation roadmap for recruiting between 5,000 and 7,000 personnel, with pilot deployments in flashpoint areas before statewide coverage,” Joshak said.

He said, “The proposed recruitment and phased deployment are part of measures to ensure that the service is properly structured and positioned to respond to security challenges across the state.”

Joshak said, “Consultations with stakeholders in the Northern and Central zones recorded overwhelming support for the establishment of state police, provided adequate safeguards are put in place against political intimidation, ethnic and religious bias, and human rights abuses.”

He said the committee recommended seven major pillars, including a legal framework, zonal and divisional command structures, 24-hour operations, an independent Police Service Commission with a civilian majority, inter-agency collaboration and phased implementation.

“The committee’s work is not yet complete, and we stand ready to continue it, refining our proposals and the draft legislative instruments as the constitutional alteration process unfolds,” he said.

Earlier, the Secretary of the committee, Julie Sanda, said, “The committee has spent seven months undertaking research, reviewing security structures and consulting stakeholders across the three senatorial districts and the 17 local government areas of the state.”

She said, “We established seven subcommittees to examine different aspects of the proposed state police service and engaged the Plateau State House of Assembly, the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria, traditional and religious leaders, women and youth groups, civil society organisations, professional associations and transport unions.”

Sanda said, “Stakeholders expressed support for the establishment of state police but emphasised the need for adequate safeguards against political manipulation, ethnic bias and human rights abuses.”

She added that, “The committee is proposing a proactive, community-orientated and accountable police service that will be responsive to the security needs of the people.”

According to her, “An online consultation portal was also launched to enable members of the public to contribute to the process, while the interim report and draft legislative proposals reflect the concerns and aspirations expressed during the consultations.”

The Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Philemon Dafi, SAN, described the proposed state police service as a practical necessity in view of the security realities confronting Plateau State.

Dafi said, “Plateau State has become the first state in the country to make structured progress towards operationalising state police.”

He disclosed that the committee had prepared the draft Plateau State Police Service Establishment Law, 2026, and the Plateau State Police Service Regulation, 2026, to provide the legal foundation for the proposed service.

He said, “The assignment was to develop a comprehensive framework that would address the constitutional and legal requirements, security challenges, feasibility, recruitment, training, discipline and inter-agency coordination.”

Dafi said consultations were still ongoing across the 17 local government areas through the official online portal and regional stakeholder validation workshops.

He, however, noted that constitutional amendments by the National Assembly and the development of a national policing framework were necessary before further implementation could take place.

Representing Governor Caleb Mutfwang, the Deputy Governor, Ngo Josephine Piyo, said, “The security challenges confronting our state require thoughtful, innovative and sustainable solutions.”

She said, “The proposed state police service, if established within the provisions of the Constitution, will provide an additional layer of security and strengthen efforts to protect lives and property.”

Piyo added that “the proposed state police service must not merely be another institution. It must be one that commands public trust, respects human rights and upholds the highest standards of professionalism and accountability.”

She said the state government would study the committee’s interim report and continue consultations before taking further steps.

Piyo assured that “the safety and well-being of our people remain a priority of the Mutfwang administration.” ””

The 14-member committee was inaugurated by Governor Mutfwang on March 10, 2026, with a mandate to develop the legal, operational, financial and oversight frameworks for the proposed Plateau State Police Service in anticipation of the amendment of Sections 214 to 216 of the 1999 Constitution.

title: Senegal win AFCON title back as CAS overturns CAF ruling
description:
The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has declared the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) the official winner of the TotalEnergies Africa Cup of Nations 2025, overturning the Confederation of African Football (CAF) decision that handed the trophy to Morocco.
In an award dated Lausanne, 24 Novem
content:
The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has declared the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) the official winner of the TotalEnergies Africa Cup of Nations 2025, overturning the Confederation of African Football (CAF) decision that handed the trophy to Morocco.

In an award dated Lausanne, 24 November 2026, in case TAS 2025/AFC/0876, the CAS Panel said it examined the FSF’s appeal against CAF’s decision dated 30 April 2025, which awarded the tournament to the Kingdom of Morocco.

The Panel found that CAF’s decision was affected by procedural irregularities and a breach of the principles of natural justice. It ruled that the result of the final, played on 18 January 2026, must be upheld.

The CAS Panel therefore set aside the CAF decision and declared the FSF the official winner, with all associated rights and privileges.

CAF is instructed to implement the award immediately and make the necessary adjustments to its official records, including the trophy, medal distribution and rankings. No further costs were awarded.

The award was signed for the Court of Arbitration for Sport by Prof. Ulrich Haas, President of the CAS Panel. Copies went to CAF, the FSF and FIFA. The document is marked confidential.

title: AFCON dispute: Senegal’s walk-off was wrong, Hakimi insists
description:
Morocco captain Achraf Hakimi has spoken out on the long-running dispute over the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title, insisting that Senegal’s decision to leave the pitch during the final was unacceptable.
The Paris Saint-Germain defender made the comments as the Court of Arbitration for Sport prepare
content:
Morocco captain Achraf Hakimi has spoken out on the long-running dispute over the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title, insisting that Senegal’s decision to leave the pitch during the final was unacceptable.

The Paris Saint-Germain defender made the comments as the Court of Arbitration for Sport prepares to deliver its ruling on the disputed final on Tuesday.

Speaking in an interview on Tuesday, as reported by football journalist Fabrizio Romano, Hakimi expressed pride in his team’s performance, regardless of the CAS verdict.

“We wait for the verdict but in my view, you can’t leave the pitch in that way as Senegal did,” Hakimi said.

“I am proud of my team; and we will see what happens.

“For me, it will be a calm day. Train, go home, then someone will tell me the verdict and I will go to sleep ahead of tomorrow game,” he added.

The 2025 AFCON final between hosts Morocco and Senegal, played in Rabat in January 2026, descended into chaos in stoppage time.

After a disputed penalty was awarded to Morocco following a VAR review of a foul on Brahim Díaz, Senegal coach Pape Thiaw ordered his players off the pitch in protest.

The walk-off lasted roughly 15 minutes before captain Sadio Mané helped persuade his teammates to return.

Morocco’s subsequent penalty was missed, and Senegal went on to win 1-0 in extra time.

The Confederation of African Football later ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match.

Its Appeals Board awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory, overturning the on-pitch result. Senegal appealed the decision to CAS.

Hakimi and several others were sanctioned in the aftermath.

The right-back received a two-match ban, with one match suspended, following incidents of unsporting behaviour during the final.

Senegal’s coach was handed a longer suspension, while both federations faced substantial fines.

The dispute has remained unresolved for months, with the title’s legitimacy still contested ahead of the CAS decision.

title: Tinubu seeks ₦3.15tn cut in 2026 budget, retains ₦31.46tn deficit
description:
President Bola Tinubu has asked the National Assembly to approve a reduction of ₦3.15tn in the 2026 national budget, bringing the proposed expenditure down from ₦68.32tn to ₦65.18tn while retaining the ₦31.46tn fiscal deficit.
The President’s request is contained in a bill seeking to repeal and re-e
content:
President Bola Tinubu has asked the National Assembly to approve a reduction of ₦3.15tn in the 2026 national budget, bringing the proposed expenditure down from ₦68.32tn to ₦65.18tn while retaining the ₦31.46tn fiscal deficit.

The President’s request is contained in a bill seeking to repeal and re-enact the 2026 Appropriation Act, alongside a revised Federal Government Fiscal Framework.

In a letter dated November 20, 2026, addressed to the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, Tinubu said the adjustments were intended to align the budget with existing obligations and available resources.

The letter was read during plenary on Tuesday.

Under the revised proposal, projected Federal Government revenue, including earnings from Government-Owned Enterprises, stands at ₦33.72tn, while aggregate capital expenditure is put at ₦26.23tn.

Tinubu said the revision would regularise some expenditures incurred by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) on behalf of the Federation, address underprovided debt-service obligations, recognise issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments, and provide for refunds to Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) and special accounts.

He explained that most of the capital provisions for MDAs comprised funds already warranted, while a few new capital and overhead allocations were introduced to address priority national interventions.

According to the President, the priority areas include completing critical road projects, protecting agricultural production, reducing production costs, improving farm yields, enhancing market access and addressing water vulnerability.

He said the revised fiscal framework was designed to prioritise existing commitments, improve the credibility and execution of the capital budget, and maintain fiscal restraint.

Despite the proposed reduction in total expenditure, the fiscal deficit, including project-tied loans, remains unchanged at ₦31.457tn, representing 5.64 per cent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

Tinubu also retained the proposed new borrowing of ₦29.22tn, comprising ₦18.43tn in domestic borrowing and ₦10.79tn in foreign borrowing.

On external borrowing, the President said the planned $7.7bn loan, estimated at ₦10.37tn using an exchange rate of ₦1,346.50 to the dollar, would finance the existing foreign borrowing provision without increasing the borrowing envelope.

The letter partly read: “The proposal aligns the 2026 budget with existing obligations and available resources.

“It regularises some NNPCL expenditures incurred on behalf of the Federation, addresses underprovided debt-service obligations, recognises issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments, and provides for refunds to Ministries, Departments and Agencies and Special Accounts.

“Under the revised framework, aggregate expenditure is ₦65.176tn, compared with ₦68.323tn in the approved budget, while projected FGN revenue, including Government-Owned Enterprises, is ₦33.720tn. Aggregate capital expenditure is ₦26.232tn.

“The fiscal deficit, including project-tied loans, remains unchanged at ₦31.457tn, equivalent to 5.64 per cent of GDP.

“These adjustments prioritise existing commitments and improve the credibility and execution of the capital budget while maintaining fiscal restraint.”

Seeking the cooperation of lawmakers for speedy passage, Tinubu said the revised appropriation was necessary to ensure orderly implementation of the budget and settlement of outstanding obligations.

“I, therefore, request the kind cooperation of the House of Representatives for expeditious consideration and passage of the Bill to facilitate orderly implementation of the revised budget and settlement of existing obligations,” he added.

The bill will undergo legislative scrutiny before the revised appropriation can take effect. If passed, it will provide the legal basis for the Federal Government to implement the adjusted spending plan.

title: EU Explains Silence On Barrow’s Third-Term Bid, Citing Absence Of Constitutional Term Limits
description:
Gambiaj.com – (BANJUL, THE GAMBIA) – The European Union has explained why it has refrained from condemning President Adama Barrow’s controversial bid for a third term, saying The Gambia’s 1997 Constitution does not impose presidential term limits.

Stéphane Mondon, deputy chief observer of the EU El
content:
Gambiaj.com – (BANJUL, THE GAMBIA) – The European Union has explained why it has refrained from condemning President Adama Barrow’s controversial bid for a third term, saying The Gambia’s 1997 Constitution does not impose presidential term limits.
Stéphane Mondon, deputy chief observer of the EU Election Observation Mission (EU EOM) in The Gambia, said the EU’s longstanding position in support of presidential term limits in Africa remained unchanged, but that the principle did not apply to The Gambia because its current legal framework does not restrict the number of terms a president can serve.

In an exclusive interview with The Standard, Mondon said the mission would have raised concerns if Barrow’s candidacy involved an attempt to breach an existing constitutional or legal provision limiting presidential terms.

“In The Gambia, the constitution doesn’t set any term limit. That’s why we haven’t said anything because there’s no infringement of the law, or the legal framework,” he said.

Constitutional Gap Behind EU Position

The EU has previously spoken out against attempts by political leaders in countries such as Senegal, Guinea and Côte d’Ivoire to circumvent constitutional term limits, which it considers an important safeguard for democratic consolidation.

However, The Gambia’s 1997 Constitution, enacted during former president Yahya Jammeh’s rule, contains no provision restricting presidents to two terms.

Two attempts to introduce a new constitution containing presidential term limits have failed, leaving the existing constitutional framework unchanged and allowing Barrow to seek another mandate.

The issue remains politically contentious as opposition candidates, including United Democratic Party (UDP) leader Ousainou Darboe, have pledged to serve only one term if elected.

Mondon said the EU would not comment on candidates exercising rights permitted under the country’s laws, stressing that respect for national sovereignty and non-interference remained central to the mission’s approach.

“But it’s not the case as of now in the country. So if candidates respect the law of the country, we don’t comment. It’s the sovereign issue of the country to respect,” he explained.

EU Monitoring Campaign Conduct And Media Freedom

With 16 long-term observers deployed across the country, the EU mission is monitoring several aspects of the electoral process, including campaign violence, hate speech, media access and the use of state resources.

Mondon said the mission was particularly attentive to the advantages enjoyed by the incumbent and whether all presidential candidates had fair access to the media.

“We monitor to see if the media gives a level playing field to all candidates, and if the narrative is not inflammatory or targeting a specific ethnic group,” he said.

He also emphasized the importance of protecting journalists from intimidation and attacks while carrying out their professional responsibilities.

Mondon said journalists must be allowed to work freely and that individuals unhappy with their reporting should use the right of reply rather than resort to intimidation.

“If you disagree with a report, you have the right to reply. You don’t have the right to attack the journalist,” he said.

EU Cautious On IEC Preparedness

Responding to concerns raised by opposition parties about the credibility and preparedness of the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) to conduct a free and fair election, Mondon said it was too early for the mission to reach a definitive conclusion.

“It’s a bit early to say,” he said.

However, he praised the transparency demonstrated by the electoral commission during the nomination process for presidential candidates, describing it as a positive aspect of the preparations so far.

Mondon stressed that the EU mission was not in The Gambia to endorse or reject the eventual election outcome but to assess whether the process reflected the will of voters.

“We don’t come here to validate or invalidate the result of the election. We are not the arbiters of this process,” he said.

He added that the mission would speak out if it observed irregularities capable of undermining voters’ choices, including during the announcement of results.

“However, if we see something that could threaten the will of the voters, including in the announcement of the result, we will definitely say it,” he said.

Peace Pact Welcomed

Mondon also welcomed the peace pact signed by all presidential candidates, including Barrow, describing their collective commitment as a positive development ahead of the December 5 presidential election.

“The fact that all candidates, including the incumbent, signed, is definitely a positive step. An election is a fight of ideas. It is not a fight of people,” he said.

The EU Election Observation Mission is expected to release its preliminary statement on December 7, two days after polling.

Mondon said the statement would outline the mission’s initial findings and conclusions on the electoral process, alongside recommendations for improving future elections.

title: Complainant seeks AGF takeover of fraud, assault suit as court fixes December 10 for hearing
description:
Justice Hauwa Joseph Yilwa of the Federal High Court in Abuja on Monday adjourned the trial of Mrs Paula Mary Nnoruka and Muntari Yusuf over alleged fraud, assault and property damage to December 10, after the prosecution indicated they wanted the charge withdrawn.
The development prompted the compl
content:
Justice Hauwa Joseph Yilwa of the Federal High Court in Abuja on Monday adjourned the trial of Mrs Paula Mary Nnoruka and Muntari Yusuf over alleged fraud, assault and property damage to December 10, after the prosecution indicated they wanted the charge withdrawn.

The development prompted the complainant, Chief Chuma Nnoruka, to seek the court’s attention, while his solicitors have separately petitioned the Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF) to take over the prosecution.

At Monday’s proceedings, prosecution counsel, J. I. Kpandegh, told the court that he had been instructed to withdraw the charge.

He explained that he could not file a formal notice of withdrawal because the instruction came during the weekend.

The judge questioned why the notice had not been filed and said any oral application for withdrawal would require the other parties to respond.

Kpandegh opted to make a formal application and requested a short adjournment.

Chief Nnoruka subsequently sought to address the court, but the judge explained that the criminal case was instituted by the Inspector-General of Police and that the complainant was not the prosecuting authority.

The judge advised him to liaise with the police over his concerns, adding that counsel appearing for him was only holding a watching brief and could not make submissions on the prosecution.

The matter was adjourned to December 10 for to enable the prosecuting counsel bring a formal application for withdrawal

Meanwhile, solicitors to two of the complainant’s clients have asked the AGF to assume responsibility for the prosecution, expressing concern that the case could be discontinued for reasons unrelated to the allegations before the court.

In a petition dated November 22 and received by the Federal Ministry of Justice on November 23, Law Corridor said its clients, Kamsiyonna Samuel Nnoruka and Tobenna Kerry Nnoruka, were apprehensive about the possible termination of the proceedings.

The firm alleged that a police officer in the Department of Legal Services, had urged the parties to pursue alternative dispute resolution over the disputed property.

According to the petition, the officer allegedly warned that refusal to participate in settlement could lead to a recommendation that the prosecution be classified as malicious and discontinued.

The solicitors asked the AGF to investigate the allegations, protect the integrity of the proceedings and take over the prosecution to its conclusion.

The claims concerning the police officer are contained in the petition and have not been independently established.

The case, Charge No. FHC/ABJ/CR/272/2025, was filed by the Inspector-General of Police against Nnoruka, Yusuf and others said to be at large.

The amended charge contains 13 counts, including allegations of fraudulent alteration of company records, forgery, conspiracy, assault, intimidation and damage to property.

The prosecution alleges that Nnoruka unlawfully altered the directorship and shareholding structure of West Wood International Services Ltd in 2019 and submitted disputed documents to the Corporate Affairs Commission.

Other counts concern alleged assaults and threats against Mrs Racheal Futuk and her children, as well as the alleged demolition of part of a property at No. 11 Rudolf Street, Maitama, Abuja.

description:
From Enweliku Kent, Asaba
Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, has assured members of the 2026 Batch C Stream II of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) of adequate security and welfare support throughout their service year in the state.
Oborevwori, who was represented by the Commissioner fo
content:
From Enweliku Kent, Asaba

Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, has assured members of the 2026 Batch C Stream II of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) of adequate security and welfare support throughout their service year in the state.

Oborevwori, who was represented by the Commissioner for Youth Development, Hon. Barr. Brave Enodeh, gave the assurance during the closing ceremony of combined Delta and Lagos of the three-week orientation course held at the NYSC Permanent Orientation Camp, Issele-Uku, in Aniocha North Local Government Area.

The governor said his administration would sustain its collaboration with the NYSC management, security agencies, local government authorities and other stakeholders to ensure the safety and well-being of corps members.

He urged the corps members to remain security-conscious, law-abiding and vigilant, adhere to security advisories and promptly report any threats to their safety.

He also encouraged them to accept their postings in good faith, integrate into their host communities, respect local customs and contribute meaningfully to community development.

Oborevwori charged the corps members to demonstrate patriotism, professionalism and integrity, while initiating or participating in impactful Community Development Service (CDS) projects in such areas as education, healthcare, agriculture, environmental sanitation, digital literacy and skills development.

He further appealed to local government chairmen, traditional rulers and community leaders to provide corps members with the necessary hospitality, guidance and security.

Earlier, the NYSC State Coordinator Mr John Vandi Kwaghe commended the corps members for their discipline and conduct throughout the orientation exercise, noting that the programme had achieved its objectives through various activities, including drills, sporting events, lectures and social engagements.

The coordinator urged the corps members to sustain their participation in the Skill Acquisition and Entrepreneurship Development (SAED) programme by engaging in post-camp training to acquire skills that would promote self-reliance and wealth creation.

He also appealed to the state government to renovate some of the camp’s hostel facilities to accommodate the increasing population of corps members.

Kwaghe, however, expressed appreciation to Governor Oborevwori for completing the re-roofing and renovation of the camp’s multipurpose hall and providing a high-capacity mobile generating plant following a major fault in the existing generator.

title: Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval to remove 268 obsolete laws
description:
President Bola Tinubu has asked the House of Representatives to approve the revised and consolidated Laws of the Federation of Nigeria (LFN 2025), following a comprehensive review that recommended the removal of 268 obsolete, spent or repealed enactments and the retention of 664 principal laws.
The
content:
President Bola Tinubu has asked the House of Representatives to approve the revised and consolidated Laws of the Federation of Nigeria (LFN 2025), following a comprehensive review that recommended the removal of 268 obsolete, spent or repealed enactments and the retention of 664 principal laws.

The review covered 932 federal enactments and 731 subsidiary legislations, in what the President described as an effort to modernise Nigeria’s legal framework and make federal laws more coherent, accessible and relevant to contemporary realities.

The Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, read the President’s letter, dated November 18, 2026, during plenary on Tuesday.

The letter, titled ‘Transmission of the Revised and Consolidated Compendium of the Laws of the Federation of Nigeria (LFN 2025) for Consideration and Approval’, followed the recommendations of a technical committee constituted under the supervision of the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi.

Tinubu said the exercise was necessary to address the long gap since the last official consolidation of Nigeria’s federal laws in 2004, noting that the country had undergone significant legislative, constitutional, institutional and technological changes in the intervening years.

In the letter addressed to the Speaker, the President said: “I write to formally inform you of the conclusion of the review, update and consolidation of the Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, and to forward herewith the proposed Revised compendium of the Laws of the Federation of Nigeria (LFN 2025) for the kind consideration and approval of the House of Representatives of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

“You may wish to recall that the last official consolidation of the Laws of the Federation was undertaken in 2004. Over the past twenty (20) years, Nigeria has witnessed profound legislative, constitutional, institutional, and technological transformations.

“These developments have necessitated the enactment of numerous new statutes, substantial amendments to existing laws, and a significant accumulation of subsidiary legislation, making the consolidation of an updated, coherent, and accessible body of Federal laws an urgent national imperative.”

According to Tinubu, a specialised committee was established on October 24, 2024, to conduct a comprehensive review and update of federal laws, identify obsolete and spent enactments, resolve statutory inconsistencies and overlaps, and produce an authoritative modern edition of the country’s laws.

He said the committee examined 932 federal enactments and 731 subsidiary legislations before validating 664 principal enactments for inclusion in the LFN 2025, while recommending the removal of 268 others.

The President added: “In discharging this mandate, the Committee rigorously examined a total of 932 Federal enactments and 731 subsidiary legislations. Following extensive legal research, technical consultations, editorial scrutiny, and quality assurance, 664 principal enactments alongside their relevant subsidiary legislation were validated for inclusion in the LFN 2025, while 268 enactments were identified as obsolete, spent, or repealed.

“An updated, accurate, and easily accessible compendium of Federal laws is indispensable to our democratic and economic growth. Upon enactment, the LFN 2025 will serve as a reliable legal reference for the judiciary, legal practitioners, government institutions, domestic and foreign investors, and the general public, thereby enhancing legal certainty, institutional efficiency, and public confidence in our justice system.”

Tinubu described the exercise as a major deliverable of his administration’s Renewed Hope Agenda, particularly its commitment to justice sector reform, strengthening the rule of law and establishing a legal framework capable of supporting national development.

He urged the lawmakers to expedite consideration and approval of the revised compendium, emphasising its importance to governance and the administration of justice.

“This milestone represents a flagship deliverable of our administration’s Renewed Hope Agenda, particularly as it relates to reforming the justice sector, strengthening the rule of law, and establishing a responsive legal framework that supports sustainable national development.

“In view of the critical importance of this instrument to national governance and the administration of justice, I earnestly urge the Honourable Members of the House of Representatives to expeditiously consider and approve the Revised Edition of the Laws of the Federation of Nigeria (LFN 2025),” the President added.

The Attorney-General of the Federation had earlier disclosed details of the exercise at a media briefing on November 12, explaining that the review was undertaken by a committee chaired by Olawale Fap

title: Ex-LP presidential candidate backs Abure’s endorsement of Tinubu
description:
A former Labour Party presidential candidate, Kennedy Ahanotu, has welcomed the Julius Abure camp’s endorsement of President Bola Tinubu for re-election, describing it as a step toward political realignment and national unity.
Ahanotu, who emerged as the party’s National Youth Leader at the Nnewi Co
content:
A former Labour Party presidential candidate, Kennedy Ahanotu, has welcomed the Julius Abure camp’s endorsement of President Bola Tinubu for re-election, describing it as a step toward political realignment and national unity.

Ahanotu, who emerged as the party’s National Youth Leader at the Nnewi Convention and contested its presidential ticket, said he was particularly pleased with the decision, which he said reflected the need to prioritise national interests over partisan differences.

In a statement on Tuesday, the former presidential hopeful said the endorsement by Abure and some factional state chairmen was a positive development that could promote constructive political engagement and collaboration.

He urged other Nigerians, particularly youths, to support efforts towards national development under Tinubu’s administration.

“This decision reinforces my long-held belief that the future of our country must take precedence over partisan differences. At a time when Nigeria needs collective commitment, stability and sustained efforts towards national development, I commend this move and encourage other well-meaning Nigerians, particularly the youths, to embrace constructive political engagement and contribute meaningfully to the nation’s progress under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said.

Ahanotu, who is the convener of the Renewed Hope Alliance of Labour Party Youth Leaders, also pledged his support for what he described as genuine efforts to build a stronger and more prosperous Nigeria under the President’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

“I remain committed to supporting every genuine effort aimed at building a stronger, more prosperous, and inclusive Nigeria under the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he added.

The endorsement came as Abure and some factional leaders of the Labour Party announced their support for Tinubu’s re-election bid, pledging to mobilise six million votes for the President in 2027.

Abure announced the decision at a National Executive Council meeting attended by members of his National Working Committee, factional state chairmen and secretaries, as well as leaders of the Obidient Movement in the party’s Directorate of Mobilisation.

Those present included former South-West National Vice Chairman, Abayomi Arabambi; Chairman of the LP State Chairmen Forum, Ceekay Igara; Deputy National Chairman, Ayo Olufemi; and former National Legal Adviser, Kehinde Edun.

Abure said the faction would deploy a coordinated nationwide mobilisation strategy to deliver the promised votes for Tinubu in the next presidential election.

title: Tinubu seeks N3.15tn cut in 2026 budget, retains N31.46tn deficit
description:
President Bola Tinubu has transmitted a bill to the House of Representatives seeking to repeal and re-enact the 2026 Appropriation Act, reducing the approved budget from N68.32tn to N65.18tn while retaining the N31.46tn fiscal deficit.
The revised budget provides for projected Federal Government rev
content:
President Bola Tinubu has transmitted a bill to the House of Representatives seeking to repeal and re-enact the 2026 Appropriation Act, reducing the approved budget from N68.32tn to N65.18tn while retaining the N31.46tn fiscal deficit.

The revised budget provides for projected Federal Government revenue of N33.72tn, including earnings from Government-Owned Enterprises, and capital expenditure of N26.23tn.

Tinubu’s request was contained in a letter dated November 20, 2026, addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, and read during plenary on Tuesday.

The President also transmitted a revised 2026 Federal Government Fiscal Framework, explaining that the adjustments were intended to align the budget with existing obligations and available resources.

According to the letter, the revision seeks to regularise some expenditures incurred by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) on behalf of the Federation, address underprovided debt-service obligations, recognise issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments, and provide for refunds to Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) and special accounts.

Tinubu said capital provisions for MDAs consisted mainly of amounts already warranted, while a few new capital and overhead allocations were introduced to address priority national interventions.

He identified the completion of critical road projects, protection of agricultural production, reduction of production costs, improvement of farm yields, enhanced market access and measures to address water vulnerability as key priorities.

The President said the revised fiscal framework was designed to prioritise existing commitments, improve the credibility and execution of the capital budget, and maintain fiscal restraint.

Despite the reduction in the overall budget, the fiscal deficit, including project-tied loans, remains unchanged at N31.457tn, representing 5.64 per cent of the Gross Domestic Product.

Tinubu also retained the proposed new borrowing of N29.22tn, comprising N18.43tn in domestic borrowing and N10.79tn in foreign borrowing.

On the proposed external borrowing, the President said the planned $7.7bn loan, estimated at N10.37tn using an exchange rate of N1,346.50 to the dollar, was intended to finance the existing foreign borrowing provision without increasing the borrowing envelope.

The letter read: “The proposal aligns the 2026 budget with existing obligations and available resources. It regularises some NNPCL expenditures incurred on behalf of the Federation, addresses underprovided debt-service obligations, recognises issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments, and provides for refunds to Ministries, Departments and Agencies and Special Accounts.

“MDA capital provision consists mainly of amounts already warranted. A few new MDA capital and overhead provisions were included as priority national interventions, particularly to complete critical road projects, protect agricultural production, reduce production costs, improve farm yields, and enhance market access, while addressing water vulnerability.

“Under the revised framework, aggregate expenditure is N65.176tn, compared with N68.323tn in the approved budget, while projected FGN revenue, including Government-Owned Enterprises, is N33.720tn. Aggregate capital expenditure is N26.232tn.

“The fiscal deficit, including project-tied loans, remains unchanged at N31.457tn, equivalent to 5.64 per cent of GDP. These adjustments prioritise existing commitments and improve the credibility and execution of the capital budget while maintaining fiscal restraint.”

Seeking the cooperation of lawmakers for speedy passage, Tinubu said the revised appropriation was necessary to ensure the orderly implementation of the budget and settlement of outstanding obligations.

“I, therefore, request the kind cooperation of the House of Representatives for expeditious consideration and passage of the Bill to facilitate orderly implementation of the revised budget and settlement of existing obligations,” he added.

The bill will be subjected to legislative scrutiny before the revised appropriation can take effect. Its passage would provide the legal basis for the Federal Government to implement the adjusted spending plan and meet the obligations outlined in the revised fiscal framework.

The post Tinubu seeks N3.15tn cut in 2026 budget, retains N31.46tn deficit appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: State police will tackle Plateau insecurity, says Mutfwang
description:
Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, on Tuesday received the preliminary report of the 14-member Advisory Committee on State Police at the Rayfield Government House, Jos, expressing confidence that a well-structured state policing system would address the state’s security challenges.
The committe
content:
Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, on Tuesday received the preliminary report of the 14-member Advisory Committee on State Police at the Rayfield Government House, Jos, expressing confidence that a well-structured state policing system would address the state’s security challenges.

The committee was inaugurated by the governor in March 2026, under the chairmanship of retired Deputy Inspector-General of Police, DIG Habila Joshak, to undertake a comprehensive review of the legal, operational and institutional frameworks necessary for the establishment of a decentralised policing structure in Plateau State, in alignment with ongoing national security reforms.

Receiving the report, the governor, who was represented by his deputy, Josephine Piyo, expressed sincere appreciation to the chairman and members of the committee for the dedication, diligence and sense of responsibility demonstrated in undertaking the assignment.

“The presentation of this preliminary report marks a significant step in our collective determination to strengthen the security architecture of Plateau State.

“We recognise that the security challenges confronting our state require thoughtful, innovative, and sustainable solutions, anchored on effective collaboration between government, security institutions, and the communities we serve,” she said.

She said the decision to establish the committee was informed by the conviction that security must be responsive to local realities.

“We believe that a well-structured, professional, and accountable state policing system, operating within the framework of the constitution and the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, could provide an additional layer of security and improve our capacity to protect lives and property,” she said.

“I wish to emphasise that our interest is not merely in establishing another security institution, but in building a system that commands public trust, respects human rights, promotes professionalism, and remains accountable to the people,” she said.

She assured the committee that the preliminary report would receive the necessary attention and consideration.

“We will carefully examine its recommendations and pursue further consultations with relevant stakeholders to ensure that whatever framework eventually emerges is inclusive, practical, and sustainable,” she said.

She also appreciated traditional institutions, civil society organisations, security agencies and other stakeholders who contributed their perspectives to the process.

“As a government, our commitment to the safety and well-being of every resident of Plateau State remains unwavering. We will continue to explore every legitimate opportunity to strengthen our security institutions and restore lasting peace across our communities.

“Once again, I commend the committee for its work and formally acknowledge the receipt of this preliminary report,” she said.

Presenting the report, the chairman of the committee, DIG Habila Joshak (retd.), said the committee was inaugurated on March 10, 2026, and charged to design a comprehensive, actionable and sustainable framework for a Plateau State Police Service, in anticipation of the ongoing amendment of Sections 214 to 216 of the Constitution.

“On behalf of every member, it is my honour to report that we have discharged that mandate,” Joshak said.

He said the committee worked through seven sub-committees and took consultations to the people, convening town hall meetings in Shendam, Pankshin and Jos. It also consulted the State House of Assembly, all 17 local government chairmen, the Traditional Council, Federal security agencies and development partners.

“The verdict was clear. Stakeholders across the Northern and Central Zones recorded 100% support for a Plateau State Police Service, on the firm condition that it is never used for political intimidation, ethnic or religious bias, or human rights abuse,” he said.

Joshak said the report rests on seven pillars: a ready-to-enact legal framework; a zonal and divisional command structure supported by 24/7 operations; recruitment with a 30 to 40% gender quota; a politically insulated training system; an independent, civilian-majority Police Service Commission for accountability; synergy with the Nigeria Police Force and sister agencies; and a phased implementation roadmap.

“The roadmap proposes the recruitment of 5,000 to 7,000 personnel, with pilots in flashpoint areas before statewide rollout,” he said.

He added that the committee’s work was not yet complete and that it stood ready to continue refining its proposal and the draft legislative instrument as the constitutional amendment process unfolded, so that Plateau State would be prepared when it concluded.

“It is now my distinct honour to formally present the preliminary report and strategic proposal for the establishment of the Plateau State Police Service,” Joshak said.

Addressing journalists after the report presentation, the State Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Philemon Daffi, SAN, said the presentation of the report underscored the landmark significance of the exercise.

“For the government and people of Plateau State, the establishment of State Police is not a theoretical concept. It is a practical, urgent necessity, born out of our local security realities and the present demand for responsive, community-centred policing,” Daffi said.

He said the committee’s mandate included examining Nigeria’s constitutional and legal framework, reviewing national policy proposals, assessing Plateau State’s peculiar security challenges, conducting a feasibility study on the operational viability of a State Police Service, and recommending standards for recruitment, training, discipline and inter-agency coordination with Federal security institutions.

“Through this work, Plateau State stands as the first state in Nigeria to make concrete, structured progress towards operationalising State Police, having already produced preliminary sub-committee findings alongside drafts of the Plateau State Police Service Establishment Law 2026 and the Plateau State Police Service Regulation 2026,” Daffi said.

He said the milestone was anchored in an inclusive, wide-ranging consultative process involving traditional rulers, the Plateau State House of Assembly, existing security institutions and relevant Federal authorities, with grassroots consultation ongoing across all 17 Local Government Areas.

“This initiative is a core component of Governor Caleb Mutfwang’s vision for effective policing in Plateau State — one aimed at deepening community security, promoting professionalism and neutrality, and guaranteeing lasting peace for socio-economic growth,” he said.

Daffi, however, noted that the state government remained firmly committed to constitutional order and was awaiting the enactment of the enabling constitutional amendment by the National Assembly, as well as the overarching national policing framework, which would determine the exact next steps and rollout by the state.

He encouraged citizens, civil society organisations, traditional institutions and community leaders across the 17 Local Government Areas to continue participating constructively as the consultative process advanced.

The post State police will tackle Plateau insecurity, says Mutfwang appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Tinubu Seeks Senate Approval To Cut 2026 Budget Spending By ₦3.14trn
description: President Bola Tinubu has written to the Senate, seeking approval for a revised 2026 budget that reduces the approved expenditure by more than ₦3 trillion. The revised proposal, tagged ‘ TRANSMISSION OF FGN 2026 APPROPRIATION REPEAL AND REENACTMENT BILL AND REVISED 2026 FEDERAL GOVERNMENT FISC
content:
President Bola Tinubu has written to the Senate, seeking approval for a revised 2026 budget that reduces the approved expenditure by more than ₦3 trillion.

The revised proposal, tagged ‘ TRANSMISSION OF FGN 2026 APPROPRIATION REPEAL AND REENACTMENT BILL AND REVISED 2026 FEDERAL GOVERNMENT FISCAL FRAMEWORK ’, was presented during plenary by the President of the Senate, Sen. Godswill Akpabio, who subsequently referred the correspondence to the Senate Committee on Rules and Business for legislative action.

Under the revised fiscal framework, aggregate expenditure is pegged at 65.176 trillion naira, down from the 68.323 trillion naira earlier approved by the National Assembly.

Projected Federal Government revenue, including receipts from government-owned enterprises, stands at 33.720 trillion naira, while capital expenditure is put at 26.232 trillion naira.

Despite the reduction in overall expenditure, the fiscal deficit remains unchanged at 31.457 trillion naira, representing 5.64 per cent of the country’s GDP.

The President says the adjustments are intended to prioritise existing commitments, strengthen the credibility of the budget and improve capital budget implementation while maintaining fiscal discipline.

The proposed new borrowing of 29.218 trillion naira also remains unchanged, comprising 18.428 trillion naira in domestic borrowing and 10.790 trillion naira in external borrowing.

Tinubu further clarified that the proposed 7.7 billion dollar external loan, estimated at 10.368 trillion naira, is intended to finance an existing foreign borrowing provision and will not increase the overall borrowing limit.

The development comes amid expectations that President Tinubu will present the 2027 budget to the National Assembly before the end of December this year.

The post Tinubu Seeks Senate Approval To Cut 2026 Budget Spending By ₦3.14trn appeared first on Channels Television.

title: 2027: APC vows to take over Ideato North, opposition stronghold in Imo
description:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) has vowed to make a bold statement in Ideato North, one of the opposition’s strongest bases in Imo State, ahead of the 2027 general elections.

content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) has vowed to make a bold statement in Ideato North, one of the opposition’s strongest bases in Imo State, ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The member representing Ideato State Constituency in the Imo State House of Assembly, Hon. Okechukwu Udeze, popularly known as Okey Is Okay, made the declaration during the visit of the Imo State Working Committee of the APC, led by the State Chairman, Chief Austin Onyedebelu, to Ideato North.

The event, held at the council headquarters in Urualla, attracted thousands of party members, supporters, political leaders, stakeholders and members of the public.

Addressing the gathering, Udeze declared that Ideato North is firmly behind the APC and will record overwhelming victories in 2027.

He highlighted what he described as the remarkable achievements of Governor Hope Uzodimma in Ideato North, saying the visible impact of the government’s interventions had strengthened the people’s confidence in the party.

He said the people of Ideato North had become firmly identified with the ruling party and no longer considered any alternative political platform.

Udeze assured the party leadership that Ideato North would deliver massively for the APC. He specifically declared support for the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the election of Governor Hope Uzodimma into the Senate to represent Imo West Senatorial District, the replacement of the incumbent member representing Ideato Federal Constituency, Hon. Ikenga Imo Ugochinyere, with the APC candidate, Lady Nnanna Anyama, and his own return to the Imo State House of Assembly for a second term.

According to him, the people’s affection for the APC is neither recent nor accidental, pointing to previous electoral victories as evidence of the party’s longstanding grassroots acceptance in the constituency.

He expressed confidence that the same loyalty would translate into another decisive triumph.

Udeze’s declaration was greeted with enthusiastic solidarity chants from the crowd, as party faithful openly expressed support for the political direction he outlined.

The massive turnout and charged atmosphere underscored the significance of the visit, with the APC leadership receiving an emphatic show of support from the constituency.

The visit is being viewed as a major political statement in Ideato North, with the APC determined to consolidate its grassroots structure and make a decisive electoral inroad into the area ahead of 2027.

The post 2027: APC vows to take over Ideato North, opposition stronghold in Imo appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: We are making event planning easier for Nigerians, says Akoh
description:
Event-planning platform, Celedom, has recorded more than 1,500 sign-ups since the introduction of its second version in February, its Project Lead, Chris Akoh, has said.
Akoh said the platform was developed to address difficulties faced by people searching for vendors and service providers for weddi
content:
Event-planning platform, Celedom, has recorded more than 1,500 sign-ups since the introduction of its second version in February, its Project Lead, Chris Akoh, has said.

Akoh said the platform was developed to address difficulties faced by people searching for vendors and service providers for weddings, birthdays and other social events.

He noted that many event vendors use social media to advertise their services, making it difficult for prospective clients to verify their credibility, compare options and establish contact.

Speaking on the platform’s operations, Akoh said it provides separate applications for event organisers and service providers.

According to him, the vendor application allows service providers to create profiles and receive enquiries from prospective clients, while the celebrants’ application enables users to search for vendors, make enquiries and communicate with service providers.

“Celedom is a problem solver. It literally solves the service-provider-finding problem we have here,” he said.

Akoh added that the platform conducts verification checks on vendors, with businesses that meet its requirements receiving a verification badge.

The platform also has a feature that allows users to organise their event requirements and identify service providers based on their needs.

Its Marketing Lead, Alaezi Akpuru, said the platform caters to different categories of events, including small gatherings and large celebrations.

Akpuru said, “Whether it’s small get-togethers or big events like weddings, Celedom covers it all.”

The platform operates through separate applications for celebrants and vendors, with further information available on its website.

The post We are making event planning easier for Nigerians, says Akoh appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Indonesia Factory Fire Death Toll Rises To 26- Police
description: The death toll from a confectionery factory fire in Indonesia has risen to 26 after two more bodies were retrieved, police said on Tuesday.The Fonusa Agung Mulia factory, located in Banten province’s Serang district around 50 kilometres (30 miles) from the capital Jakarta, caught fire on Satur
content:
The death toll from a confectionery factory fire in Indonesia has risen to 26 after two more bodies were retrieved, police said on Tuesday.

The Fonusa Agung Mulia factory, located in Banten province’s Serang district around 50 kilometres (30 miles) from the capital Jakarta, caught fire on Saturday afternoon, trapping dozens of workers inside.

Rescuers retrieved two more bodies from the building, local police said in a statement on Tuesday, bringing the death toll to 26.

Another 28 people remain unaccounted for, police said, adding that they had launched a probe into the cause of the blaze.

“Based on the facts from the investigation and the evidence that has been secured, we found that there was an alleged crime related to negligence or carelessness that resulted in a fire and endangered others,” said Banten deputy police chief Zain Dwi Nugroho.

Rescue worker Jajuli — who, like many Indonesians, uses only one name — said on Monday that many of the victims found had been “burnt and reduced to dust”.

Deadly fires are not uncommon in the Southeast Asian nation.

A blaze that was likely caused by a drone battery explosion tore through a seven-storey building in Jakarta and killed at least 22 people in December.

And at least 13 people were killed in the country’s east in 2023 after an explosion at a nickel-processing plant.

AFP

title: 2027: Judge lawmakers by development records, LP candidate tells voters
description:
Labour Party candidate for Bende Federal Constituency in the 2027 general elections, Chima Anyaso, has urged voters to assess lawmakers seeking re-election based on their constituency development records and the impact of their representation on the people.
Anyaso made the call during an interview w
content:
Labour Party candidate for Bende Federal Constituency in the 2027 general elections, Chima Anyaso, has urged voters to assess lawmakers seeking re-election based on their constituency development records and the impact of their representation on the people.

Anyaso made the call during an interview with Vimbai Ekpenyong on ARISE News on Monday, where he discussed legislative performance, constituency development and voters’ expectations ahead of the 2027 elections.

He said constituents should demand clear accounts of how their representatives had used their positions to attract projects and improve living conditions in their communities.

“Political representation should be judged by tangible results rather than political visibility, public relations activities or the prominence of an officeholder’s position in the National Assembly,” he said.

Anyaso argued that effective representation should go beyond parliamentary participation to include attracting federal projects, improving infrastructure and supporting development in education, healthcare, agriculture and youth empowerment.

He urged voters to distinguish between projects announced by lawmakers, those captured in government budgets and those completed and delivered for public use.

According to him, constituents should be able to identify specific projects and interventions undertaken by their representatives without relying on political publicity.

He described projects announced or publicised without corresponding implementation or measurable benefits as “audio projects”.

The LP candidate cited Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, as an example of leadership whose performance, he said, could be assessed through measurable achievements.

He maintained that public officeholders seeking fresh mandates should present clear accounts of their stewardship and explain how their interventions had improved the lives of the people.

“Public office should not become an entitlement or a permanent occupation disconnected from the expectations of the electorate,” he said.

Anyaso also stressed that residents of Bende deserved transparent explanations of how constituency-related interventions and federal opportunities had been deployed over the years.

The comments come as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general elections, with constituency development and legislative accountability expected to feature in campaigns.

The post 2027: Judge lawmakers by development records, LP candidate tells voters appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Peter Obi Lacks Competence To Lead Nigeria, Tinubu 100% Better — Abure
description: Former National Chairman of the Labour Party, Julius Abure, has said the party’s former presidential candidate, Peter Obi, lacks the character and competence to lead Nigeria, insisting that President Bola Tinubu is “100 per cent better”.Abure said he would not support Obi’s p
content:
Former National Chairman of the Labour Party, Julius Abure, has said the party’s former presidential candidate, Peter Obi, lacks the character and competence to lead Nigeria, insisting that President Bola Tinubu is “100 per cent better”.

Abure said he would not support Obi’s presidential ambition in the 2027 general election, citing his experience working with the former Anambra State governor and the internal crisis that fractured the Labour Party.

He made the remarks during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he explained why he considered Tinubu a better choice among the leading contenders for the presidency.

Abure was a key ally of Obi during the 2023 presidential campaign and campaigned extensively for him. However, Obi subsequently left the Labour Party following a protracted leadership crisis.

He blamed Obi’s caretaker committee decision for deepening the Labour Party’s crisis, driving elected officials away and raising questions about his leadership.

“If indeed Obi was a good leader, why did they not follow Peter Obi? Peter Obi doesn’t have the character and competence to lead the country; we are sorry to say. Given my experience, I now know better,” he said.

Asked whether his decision to campaign extensively for Obi in 2023 had been a mistake, Abure admitted that it might have been.

“Yes, it may have been an error because I now know better. Experience, they say, is the best teacher. Now I have experienced working with Peter Obi and that he is unstable, unreliable, a pretender who cannot be trusted because of the way he treated the leadership of the party,” he said.

Asked whether he still considered Obi “a saint,” Abure declared his support for Tinubu, describing the president as a more suitable candidate.

“President Bola Tinubu is 100 per cent better. Today, we have the right to support whatever candidate we want. Obviously, Peter Obi is out of the question for us to support, given our experiences with him. We made a critical analysis of all the candidates: Tinubu, Atiku and Obi.

“We feel Tinubu is the best candidate for us to support, given his trajectory so far in office and his ability to resolve conflicts compared to Peter Obi. The stage we are in now requires someone who can bring people together because the country is more divided than ever before. We need a bridge-builder who can unite people, and I do not believe Peter Obi has that capacity at this critical time in our history,” he said.

He, however, dismissed allegations that he was responsible for Obi’s departure from the Labour Party, describing such claims as a “clear misconception”.

Obi has since joined the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and will fly the party’s flag for the 2027 presidential election.

Other prominent figures expected to feature in the election include Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Atiku of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and Omoyele Sowore of the African Action Congress (AAC). In the 2023 presidential election, Tinubu won with 8,794,726 votes, while Atiku secured 6,984,520 votes. Obi finished third with 6,101,533 votes.

The post Peter Obi Lacks Competence To Lead Nigeria, Tinubu 100% Better — Abure appeared first on Channels Television.
