title: Court Nullifies Omo-Agege’s NDC Senatorial Candidacy, Directs INEC To Remove Name From List
description: The Federal High Court in Warri, Delta State, has invalidated the nomination of former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, as the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections over alleged violations of the Elector
content:
The Federal High Court in Warri, Delta State, has invalidated the nomination of former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, as the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections over alleged violations of the Electoral Act.

In its ruling on Tuesday, Justice Hyeladzira Ajiya Nganjiwa directed the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to remove Omo-Agege’s name from its list of candidates for the election. The court also barred the former Deputy Senate President from presenting himself as the NDC candidate for the senatorial district.

The court further held that the statutory period for conducting fresh primaries to produce a replacement candidate had expired, referring to the Electoral Act provision requiring political parties to nominate candidates not later than 180 days before the general election.

The suit, marked FHC/WR/CS/120/2026, was filed by Prof. Alexander Osondu Akpodiete, who challenged the legality of Omo-Agege’s emergence as the NDC candidate. The plaintiff raised issues relating to his resignation from the All Progressives Congress (APC), membership of the NDC and eligibility to contest the party’s senatorial primary.

Before determining the substantive issues, Justice Nganjiwa dismissed five preliminary objections filed by Omo-Agege, the NDC and INEC, which challenged the competence of the suit.

On the merits of the case, the judge found that the NDC did not satisfy the Electoral Act’s requirements for submitting its membership register to INEC ahead of its primary election.

The court specifically observed that Omo-Agege’s name was absent from the party’s membership register submitted to the electoral commission at least 21 days before the primary. It also held that the NDC failed to produce sufficient evidence showing that the register was subsequently updated and submitted within the prescribed period.

The judge also relied on INEC’s revised electoral timetable, which showed that Omo-Agege participated in the APC senatorial primary conducted on May 18, 2026. According to the court, his participation indicated that he remained an APC member at the time.

Justice Nganjiwa stressed that only individuals whose names were duly captured in a political party’s membership register, in line with the Electoral Act, could lawfully participate in its primary elections.

The court also addressed the issue of a previously withdrawn affidavit, ruling that a party could withdraw an affidavit already filed in a case. It held that once withdrawn, the document ceased to form part of the court’s records and could no longer be relied upon in determining the dispute.

Emphasising the need for strict compliance with electoral laws, the judge held that a party’s candidate nomination must satisfy the statutory requirements, adding that INEC could not recognise or list a candidate whose emergence resulted from a process that breached the law.

Consequently, the court set aside Omo-Agege’s nomination, ordered INEC to delist him and restrained him from holding himself out as the NDC’s candidate for Delta Central in the 2027 elections.

The ruling introduces fresh uncertainty into the NDC’s quest to contest the Delta Central senatorial seat, particularly following the court’s position that the deadline for conducting replacement primaries has passed.

Neither the NDC nor Senator Ovie Omo Agege has reacted to this judgment.

The post Court Nullifies Omo-Agege’s NDC Senatorial Candidacy, Directs INEC To Remove Name From List appeared first on Channels Television.

title: CAS To Rule On Senegal-Morocco AFCON Final Dispute Amid Fresh Allegations
description: Gambiaj.com – (LAUSANNE, SWITZERLAND) – The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) is expected to deliver its ruling this afternoon in the dispute over the winner of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) final between Senegal and Morocco, as fresh allegations of an alleged contact involving a member
content:
Gambiaj.com – (LAUSANNE, SWITZERLAND) – The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) is expected to deliver its ruling this afternoon in the dispute over the winner of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) final between Senegal and Morocco, as fresh allegations of an alleged contact involving a member of the arbitration panel and Senegalese football officials emerge ahead of the decision.

The Moroccan Royal Football Federation (FRMF) has formally reported an alleged incident to CAS, claiming that Senegal Football Federation (FSF) president Abdoulaye Fall had a telephone conversation with one of the arbitrators handling the case shortly before the verdict was due.

The allegation, reportedly raised in a letter sent to CAS’s legal representatives on Tuesday, 24 November, has been strongly rejected by the Senegalese side.

FSF Secretary General Abdoulaye Seydou Sow dismissed the claim, describing it as an “imaginary call” and insisting that Fall does not even know the judges assigned to the case, according to statements reported by Senegalese media outlet SeneNews.

The latest development adds another layer of tension to an already contentious legal battle, with both countries awaiting a decision that will determine the official winner of the January final.

In its announcement, CAS said the parties had been informed that the ruling would be delivered during the afternoon on Tuesday.

“The parties have been notified that the CAS decision will be rendered in the course of the afternoon,” the court said, adding that only information communicated through its official channels should be considered authoritative.

Dispute Over the January Final

The legal battle stems from the final played on 18 January at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat, where Senegal defeated hosts Morocco 1-0 after extra time to claim their second Africa Cup of Nations title.

Senegal’s Pape Gueye scored the decisive goal in extra time after a controversial incident involving the referee’s decision to award Morocco a penalty.

Senegal’s players walked off the pitch in protest without the referee’s permission, forcing a suspension of nearly 15 minutes before they returned to continue the match.

Morocco had an opportunity to secure victory in regulation time when striker Brahim Diaz was awarded a penalty with virtually the final kick of the 90 minutes. However, he failed to convert, sending the match into extra time, where Senegal eventually scored the winner.

Following the final, the FRMF challenged the result, arguing that Senegal had effectively abandoned the match by leaving the pitch.

After an initial appeal was rejected by CAF’s disciplinary committee, Moroccan football authorities pursued the matter further within the continental governing body.

On 17 March 2026, CAF overturned the result, ruling that Senegal had forfeited the match and awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory, effectively transferring the continental title to the North African country.

Senegal’s football authorities subsequently appealed to CAS, challenging CAF’s decision.

Five-Hour Hearing in Lausanne

A three-member CAS panel heard arguments from lawyers representing the Senegalese and Moroccan football federations, as well as CAF, during a five-hour hearing in Lausanne, Switzerland, on 8 October.

The hearing was held behind closed doors as the independent sports tribunal considered the competing arguments over CAF’s decision and the circumstances surrounding the final.

Tuesday’s ruling will determine whether CAF’s decision stands or Senegal retains the title it won on the pitch in January.

The fresh allegations reported by Morocco have also raised questions about the circumstances surrounding the proceedings, although the Senegalese federation has categorically denied any inappropriate contact involving its president.

Both Teams Qualified for 2027 AFCON

The legal dispute has continued even as both countries have moved on to other international competitions.

At the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States, Mexico, Canada, and Senegal were eliminated in the round of 32, while Morocco reached the quarter-finals before losing to France.

Both nations have also secured qualification for the next Africa Cup of Nations, which will be jointly hosted by Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda in 2027.

Morocco qualified from Group A with four wins from four matches, while Senegal also secured their place from Group J under new head coach Patrick Vieira.

The 2027 AFCON finals will feature 24 teams and are scheduled to take place from 19 June to 17 July.

Tuesday’s CAS ruling is expected to settle one of the most contentious disputes in African football, determining which country will officially be recognized as the 2025 continental champion.

title: Attack on Omo-Agege’s campaign team dangerous for democracy – Ochei
description: The Delta North senatorial candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Hon. Victor Ochei, has strongly condemned the reported attack on the campaign team of his Delta Central counterpart, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area, describing it as a dangerous thre
content:
The Delta North senatorial candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Hon. Victor Ochei, has strongly condemned the reported attack on the campaign team of his Delta Central counterpart, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area, describing it as a dangerous threat to democratic participation in Delta State.

This was conveyed in a Tuesday statement issued by the Media and Publicity Unit, Victor Ochei Campaign Organisation.

Ochei expressed concern over reports that armed attackers opened fire on the campaign entourage, resulting in deaths and injuries.

He commiserated with the bereaved families, wished the injured speedy recovery and expressed solidarity with Omo-Agege and his supporters.

He noted that the incident adds to growing concerns over political violence in the state, recalling the reported disruption of the NDC mobilisation march in Asaba on November 7, which allegedly resulted in a death, injuries and destruction of campaign vehicles, as well as an attack on the party’s campaign team in Okpai, Ndokwa East.

Ochei warned that political competition must be based on ideas, policies and the support of voters, not intimidation, violence or thuggery.

He called on Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to publicly condemn the Uduere attack and demonstrate leadership by ensuring that all political parties and candidates can campaign freely and safely across the state.

He also urged the Inspector-General of Police, the Delta State Police Command and other security agencies to conduct a thorough and impartial investigation, identify the perpetrators and alleged sponsors, and bring them to justice.

He emphasised the need for adequate security protection for all candidates, campaign teams and supporters, irrespective of political affiliation.

Recalling his recent appearance on ARISE News, where he raised concerns about attacks on opposition parties, particularly the NDC, Ochei stressed that democracy cannot thrive where political opponents are denied the freedom to organise, mobilise and campaign without fear.

“An election should be a contest of ideas and a peaceful appeal to the electorate, not a season of bloodshed, intimidation and political vendetta. No political ambition is worth the life of any Nigerian,” he stated.

He appealed to political leaders, party supporters and youths across Delta to reject violence, while urging NDC members to remain calm, law-abiding and committed to peaceful democratic engagement.

Ochei maintained that Delta State belongs to all its citizens and that no political party should claim ownership or monopoly of the democratic space.

“The people deserve peace, security and the freedom to make their political choices without fear. Governor Oborevwori must act now to protect these fundamental democratic rights,” the senatorial candidate stated.

title: BREAKING: Court sacks Omo-Agege as NDC Senatorial candidate, orders INEC to delist him
description: The Federal High Court sitting in Warri, Delta State, on Tuesday, nullified the nomination of former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, as the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections, citing non-compliance w
content:
The Federal High Court sitting in Warri, Delta State, on Tuesday, nullified the nomination of former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, as the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections, citing non-compliance with the provisions of the Electoral Act.

The court, presided over by Justice Hyeladzira Ajiya Nganjiwa, ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to remove Omo-Agege’s name from its list of candidates for the election and restrained the former Deputy Senate President from parading himself as the NDC senatorial candidate.

In a further setback for the NDC, the court held that the statutory window for conducting fresh primaries to nominate another candidate had elapsed, noting that the Electoral Act prescribed a 180-day timeline before the general elections.

The judgment followed a suit instituted by Prof. Alexander Osondu Akpodiete, marked FHC/WR/CS/120/2026, challenging the validity of Omo-Agege’s nomination on grounds bordering on his resignation from the All Progressives Congress (APC), membership of the NDC and eligibility to participate in the party’s senatorial primary.

Delivering judgment, Justice Nganjiwa dismissed all five preliminary objections raised by Omo-Agege, the NDC and INEC challenging the competence of the suit, before proceeding to determine the substantive issues raised by the plaintiff.

The court held that the NDC failed to comply with the mandatory provisions of the Electoral Act requiring it to submit its membership register to INEC ahead of its primary election.

Justice Nganjiwa found that Omo-Agege’s name was not contained in the NDC membership register submitted to INEC at least 21 days before the conduct of the party’s primary election.

The judge further held that the NDC failed to provide credible evidence establishing that its membership register was subsequently updated and submitted to INEC within the statutory period preceding the primary.

Relying on INEC’s revised electoral timetable, the court also noted that Omo-Agege participated in the APC senatorial primary held on May 18, 2026, a development which, according to the court, established that he was still a member of the APC at the material time.

Justice Nganjiwa maintained that only persons whose names appeared in a political party’s membership register, in accordance with the requirements of the Electoral Act, were eligible to participate in its primary elections.

On the admissibility of a previously withdrawn affidavit, the court held that a party was entitled to withdraw an affidavit already filed in a proceeding, adding that once withdrawn, such an affidavit ceased to form part of the court’s records and could not be relied upon in determining the matter.

The judge maintained that a valid nomination could not be founded on a process that failed to satisfy statutory requirements, stressing that where a political party failed to comply with the Electoral Act in nominating its candidate, INEC was not permitted to include such a candidate on the ballot.

Consequently, the court invalidated Omo-Agege’s nomination, directed INEC to delist him and restrained him from presenting himself as the NDC candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the forthcoming general elections.

The judgment represents a significant development in the race for the Delta Central senatorial seat, raising questions over the NDC’s participation in the election, particularly in view of the court’s pronouncement that the statutory deadline for nominating candidates had elapsed.

The full certified judgment and any response from Omo-Agege, the NDC or INEC were not available in the initial account of the ruling.

He said the officers intercepted a gang s
content:
The Benue State Police Command has arrested two suspected robbers linked to a robbery incident in Abuja.

The spokesperson for the state command, DSP Peter Aondongu, disclosed this in a statement issued on Tuesday and made available to journalists in Makurdi.

He said the officers intercepted a gang suspected of specialising in interstate robbery operations along the Agatu-Keffi Road.

The statement read in part, “On 22nd November 2026, at about 0818 hours, a segment of the command’s Operation Anyam Nyor Police Tactical Team deployed along the Agatu-Keffi Road in Agatu Local Government Area intercepted a red-coloured Toyota Camry with two occupants who were reasonably suspected not to be the owners of the car.

“During a search of the car and the occupants, as well as preliminary investigations, the team recovered documents and other items linking the red Toyota Camry to a robbery incident in Abuja, as the owner was contacted and confirmed the robbery attack.”

Aondongu said that while the suspects were being conveyed to the station, one of them, who was driving the vehicle, jumped out and fled into the bush.

He, however, said the police successfully rearrested the fleeing suspect, who was immediately rushed to the Comprehensive Health Centre in Agatu for medical attention.

“But later died while receiving treatment. His remains have been deposited at the hospital mortuary for post-mortem examination and other investigative processes,” the statement added.

Aondongu listed the items recovered in connection with the incident to include a red Toyota Camry, a jackknife, a live cartridge, two small Tecno button phones, a Lenovo laptop, a walking stick, three National Identity Cards, five ATM cards, a long black beaded necklace, N5,000 cash, two phone chargers, a wristwatch, two brown bags, vehicle particulars and other documents.

The police spokesperson said the command had commenced a thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the robbery, determine the extent of the suspects’ involvement and uncover other possible criminal activities.

He added that efforts were ongoing to identify and arrest other members of the syndicate.

The Commissioner of Police, Cletus Nwadiogbu, reassured residents of the command’s commitment to protecting lives and property.

He urged members of the public to remain vigilant and provide timely and credible information to assist the police.

title: NDC: Oborevwori visits Uduere attack scene, orders arrest of perpetrators
description:
Delta State Governor, Rt. Hon. Sheriff Oborevwori on Tuesday visited the scene of attack in Uduere Community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, expressing deep sadness over the outbreak of political violence , which claimed several lives in the state.
The Governor, who visited Uduere community to
content:
Delta State Governor, Rt. Hon. Sheriff Oborevwori on Tuesday visited the scene of attack in Uduere Community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, expressing deep sadness over the outbreak of political violence , which claimed several lives in the state.

The Governor, who visited Uduere community to assess the situation and reassure residents, described the incident as totally unacceptable and a grave threat to the peace and security of the state.

The Governor called on security agencies to intensify efforts to apprehend all those involved in the violence and ensure thatthey are brought to justice.

Oborevwori, who first met with heads of security agencies in the state at the Area Command Office, Ughelli, was accompanied by the Commissioner of Police, CP Samuel Etaifo Erale, Commander, 63 Brigade of the Nigerian Army, Brigadier General Ibrahim Buhari, State Director of the Department of State Services (DSS) and other security officials.

Addressing journalists at the community, the Governor lamented that it was unfortunate that political differences could degenerate into violence and the loss of human lives, particularly when the state had worked hard to sustain an atmosphere of peace since 2023.

Expressing concern over the killings, Oborevwori said it was unconscionable for anyone to invade a community under the guise of political activity and resort to killing fellow Nigerians.

“Those who know me know that I am not a violent person. That is why, in my MORE Agenda, the fourth pillar is dedicated to enhancing peace and security.

“We have been preaching peace, and Delta State has enjoyed relative peace since 2023. The important thing is how to sustain that peace. I want to assure the people that this will not happen again,” he said.

The Governor condemned the actions of those responsible for the violence, insisting that political ambition or disagreement could never justify the destruction of lives and property.

He declared that the perpetrators must be identified, arrested and made to face the full consequences of their actions, stressing that the state could not afford to allow political activities to become a breeding ground for violence and insecurity.

“This must stop. It must stop. We cannot continue like this,” he warned.

Oborevwori further noted that peace and security remained indispensable to economic growth, explaining that no meaningful business activity or investment could thrive in an atmosphere of violence and uncertainty.

Speaking further, the Governor urged all political actors to shun violence, maintain peace and refrain from actions capable of escalating tensions.

The Governor urged security agencies, particularly the police to conduct a thorough investigation, arrest all those involved and ensure that justice is served.

The Governor reiterated that his administration would remain resolute in its commitment to protecting lives and property, sustain the prevailing peace and strengthen security across the state, in line with the fourth pillar of his MORE Agenda.

The post NDC: Oborevwori visits Uduere attack scene, orders arrest of perpetrators appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: 2027: Ex-CJN warns against repeat of 2011 post-election killings
description: Former Chief Justice of Nigeria and Chairman of the Council of the Wise of the Savannah Centre for Diplomacy, Democracy and Development, Justice Olukayode Ariwoola (retd.), has warned against a repeat of the violence that followed the 2011 general elections, urging political actors and other stakeho
content:
Former Chief Justice of Nigeria and Chairman of the Council of the Wise of the Savannah Centre for Diplomacy, Democracy and Development, Justice Olukayode Ariwoola (retd.), has warned against a repeat of the violence that followed the 2011 general elections, urging political actors and other stakeholders to take urgent steps to safeguard the 2027 polls.

Speaking at a press conference in Abuja on Tuesday, Ariwoola raised concerns over increasing incidents of political violence, intimidation and destruction of property associated with political activities across the country.

Political violence involving candidates and supporters of major political parties appears to be escalating ahead of the 2027 general elections, with growing reports of attacks across the country.

The incidents have resulted in the destruction of property, loss of life, and injuries to several people.

In an exclusive report published by The PUNCH on November 11, the National Peace Committee revealed that 26 states and the Federal Capital Territory recorded 109 violations of the National Peace Accord during a 10-week monitoring exercise, raising concerns over the safety of political campaigns and the conduct of the 2027 elections.

The report, which covered the period between August 19 and October 27 and was obtained by The PUNCH, identified political violence and thuggery as the most frequent violations, with 33 incidents, followed by misinformation and disinformation, which accounted for 29 cases.

Reacting, the former CJN urged security agencies to ensure adequate protection at campaign venues and arrest and prosecute perpetrators of electoral violence. He also called on the Independent National Electoral Commission to enforce electoral laws without fear or favour.

The Savannah Centre’s Council of the Wise expressed deep concern over the wave of political violence and intimidation, which it said had led to loss of lives and destruction of property during ongoing political campaigns across Nigeria ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Ariwoola noted that, “Recent media reports indicated that in the past five weeks, Nigeria has witnessed a disturbing recurrence of politically motivated violence and attacks in many states of the federation, thereby dangerously threatening the safety of candidates, electorates, journalists and the general public.

“Since the commencement of political campaigns, reported attacks and disturbances thus far have affected political convoys of some candidates, rallies and gatherings of political parties in Kano, Katsina, Lagos, Edo, Delta, Enugu, Cross River, Sokoto, Enugu, Bayelsa and Rivers states as well as the Federal Capital Territory.”

The Council of the Wise also expressed concern over rising political violence ahead of the 2027 elections, citing deaths, injuries, destruction of property and alleged threats by political leaders against their opponents.

Ariwoola added, “The Council of the Wise therefore wishes to remind all Nigerians, particularly politicians and their supporters, that democracy thrives on the peaceful contestation of ideas and visions, not on bloodshed or coercion.

“Every Nigerian has a constitutional right to participate in the electoral process freely and safely, regardless of party affiliation. It is important to note that if this dangerous trend of political violence is not effectively checked, it will lead to more unpleasant consequences.

“The Council stresses that abiding by the governing laws is indispensable to electoral peace, protection of lives and the credibility of the democratic process. Political parties, candidates, supporters, public officials, security agencies and the citizens must respect the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended), the Electoral Act, 2026 and applicable INEC regulations and guidelines. Compliance must be consistent and impartial, as political ambition cannot justify unlawful conduct.”

The Council urged political parties and their supporters to ensure peaceful and responsible campaigns in line with the Constitution, warning that failure to address the situation could trigger a national crisis.

Ariwoola said, “The Nigeria Police Force, the Department of State Security Service, the Nigerian Security and Civil Defense Corps, the National Intelligence Agency, the Defense Intelligence Agency, as well as the Nigerian Armed Forces must deploy adequate personnel to secure all major campaign venues and political rallies across the Country. Perpetrators of political violence must be swiftly arrested and prosecuted without fear or favor. Ban and confiscate dangerous weapons such as knives, sticks, cutlasses, and guns at political gatherings nationwide.

“Leaders of all political parties, candidates, and their respective campaign councils must take full responsibility for the conduct of their supporters in accordance with the Electoral Act and the Law. Party leaders must publicly and continually denounce violence and call their irate followers to order, to strictly adhere to the Peace Accord they signed and abide by the electoral guidelines issued by INEC.

“They should desist from inflammatory, hateful, and insulting rhetoric in their utterances. They should promptly take disciplinary action against any of their members who engage in electoral violence, or threaten the use of violence. Members of their respective campaign committees should be trained in conducting peaceful campaigns in accordance with parties’ codes of conduct and the electoral laws.”

The Council urged governments at all levels to provide a level playing field for political parties by ensuring that opposition groups were not denied access to public or private facilities for peaceful campaigns.

Ariwoola continued, “The Independent National Electoral Commission should take steps to enforce the electoral laws without fear or favour. It should coordinate with the Nigeria Police on investigation and speedy prosecution of electoral offenders by its legal team in accordance with section 148 of the Electoral Act.

“The National Assembly should strengthen its oversight duty over the Security Agencies, INEC and other public institutions involved in the election process to ensure peaceful conduct of the elections.

“The judiciary should ensure speedy trials of electoral cases in order to end the culture of impunity.”

The Council urged citizens, particularly youths, to shun political thuggery and violence, stressing that elections should be peaceful and voters must respect the rights of others to participate in the electoral process.

Ariwoola continued, “Political competition should be a contest of ideas, not a justification for intimidation and violence. The Council of the Wise urges all Nigerians to choose peace over violence; dialogue over threats; and democracy over anarchy.

“It will be an unfortunate national shame if Nigerians collectively allow a repeat of what happened after the 2011 elections, where, according to Human Rights Watch, over 800 people were killed in the election-related violence. The 2027 elections must be won at the ballot boxes, not on the streets through intimidation and bloodshed.”

The post 2027: Ex-CJN warns against repeat of 2011 post-election killings appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Hamanteh Project Launched to Preserve Gambia’s Oral History Through AI
description:
Gambiaj.com – (BANJUL, THE GAMBIA) – A new initiative seeking to preserve The Gambia’s family histories, cultural heritage, and ancestral connections through artificial intelligence (AI) was launched on Saturday at the National Library in Banjul.
Known as the Hamanteh Project, the initiative aims to
content:
Gambiaj.com – (BANJUL, THE GAMBIA) – A new initiative seeking to preserve The Gambia’s family histories, cultural heritage, and ancestral connections through artificial intelligence (AI) was launched on Saturday at the National Library in Banjul.

Known as the Hamanteh Project, the initiative aims to build a national oral history network by bringing together family histories from across the country and connecting them through a digital platform developed by Banjul-born Gambian IT expert Amran Gaye.

The project draws its initial foundation from an extensive community-led documentation exercise in Half Die, Banjul, where residents recorded their histories house by house and elder by elder. The exercise was spearheaded by members of the Half Die community, whose recordings have now become part of the data used to develop the Hamanteh AI platform.

At the heart of the initiative was the Half Die Mansa Musa WhatsApp group, administered by Bai-Mass Taal. Acting on their own initiative, members of the group had already collected more than 500 audio recordings of family histories, with elders narrating their personal experiences and ancestral accounts.

Recognizing the historical value of these recordings, Gaye retrieved the material and began working with it alongside a team of volunteers, including Tijan Baabu Jow, Fatoumatta L. Sisay, and Mar Yaam Njie, to develop the digital platform.

Reconnecting Families Through Technology

Speaking at the launch, Bai-Mass Taal thanked participants and members of the community for attending the ceremony, particularly those who had contributed to the initiative.

He said the project was inspired by the traditional networks of family relationships, friendships, and community connections that historically brought Gambians together, regardless of ethnic background or political affiliation.

In her intervention, Juka Jabang said these relationships played an important role in maintaining social cohesion, mutual support, and security within communities.

She said the gradual disappearance of these connections, particularly as elderly people pass away without their knowledge and experiences being documented, makes it increasingly important to preserve family histories for future generations.

Amran Gaye, the brain behind the project highlighted the relevance of the initiative during the current election period, which he described as a challenging time for democratic societies because of political disagreements and divisions.

“I found this event especially relevant as we go through this election period: a difficult period in any democracy, with much disagreement and division,” he said.

“But the ancestors left us with a tool to hold our people together: a network linking us by surname to surname, family to family, and friend to friend. Every Gambian connected to every other Gambian in some way. Ties beyond tribe or political affiliation, a common bond that has always held us together as a people.”

He warned that this traditional network was gradually fading, particularly as elders died without passing on or recording the knowledge they carried.

“But with the digital tools we have now, we can be the generation that revives it, adding all our histories from across the land. For us, now, to become reconnected, and for our children and all the Gambians yet to come,” Gaye said.

A National Effort To Document Family Histories

The Hamanteh platform is designed to allow Gambians at home and abroad to contribute their family histories and genealogical information, creating an interconnected repository of the country’s collective memory.

Gaye said the launch was only the beginning of a much broader effort that would require active participation from communities across the country.

He called on Gambians to upload their family histories and family trees, help transcribe oral recordings into English for the AI system, and encourage relatives and other community members to contribute.

He also appealed for volunteers to become community champions who could coordinate documentation exercises in their respective towns, neighborhoods, and streets, recording histories house by house.

Gaye said families could also organize their own projects to document their complete histories and preserve the experiences of older generations.

The project plans to expand its public engagement through a Facebook group where members will share family histories, lineages, and photographs for identification. A radio program is also being developed to invite elders from different parts of the country to share their stories.

Gambians interested in contributing or exploring the platform can visit https://hamanteh.dundalai.com/join.

Gaye stressed that the initiative would only achieve its objectives if people across the country actively participated in documenting and sharing their histories.

Half Die Community Recognized for Leading Initiative

Saturday’s ceremony brought together several personalities and community representatives, including Bai-Mass Taal and other members of the Half Die Mansa Musa group, whose grassroots initiative provided the foundation for the project.

The launch was also attended by Juka Jabang Njie, Tunde Jones, Bakary Sanyang, who hosted the ceremony at the National Library, Sirra Ndow, head of the African Network Against Extrajudicial Killings and Enforced Disappearances, and UNDP Country Representative Mandisa Mashologu.

Gambian Talents Promotion provided live coverage of the event.

Gaye acknowledged the Half Die community for taking the initiative to document its own history, expressing hope that other communities would follow its example.

The project ultimately seeks to give Gambians greater ownership of how their histories, identities, and cultural heritage are documented and passed on.

Its underlying message is that the responsibility for preserving the country’s collective memory should rest with Gambians themselves, rather than leaving future generations to depend entirely on accounts produced by outsiders.

As the initiative seeks to expand beyond Half Die to communities across the country, its appeal is straightforward: Gambians should document their own histories, connect their family lineages, and ensure that the stories of their ancestors are not lost.

title: How Gaming Platforms Protect Personal Data and Player Accounts
description: A game account holds more than a username and high scores: it can include an email address, a saved card, a friends list and chat logs, so gaming sites collect a lot of private data. Protecting it matters, because a breach can lead to account takeover, fraud and bullying, and many players are minors
content:
A game account holds more than a username and high scores: it can include an email address, a saved card, a friends list and chat logs, so gaming sites collect a lot of private data. Protecting it matters, because a breach can lead to account takeover, fraud and bullying, and many players are minors.

On real-money sites, which are for adults only, the stakes are higher still, since payment and ID details are stored too. Slotozilla’s list of UK casino deposit 1 get 20 offers is a useful way to compare low-entry sites, but it is worth checking how each one protects card details before signing up. The same check applies to any platform that keeps your information on file.

pixabay

What Personal Data Do Gaming Platforms Collect?

Platforms gather data to run accounts, take payments, match players, and keep services safe. Each type carries its own risk if it leaks. The main categories are:

  • Account and personal information, including name, email, date of birth, and username.
  • Payment and transaction information, including credit card information and transaction history.
  • Play data, such as progress, session length and in-game activity.
  • Device and IP information, which can be used to determine approximate location and device.
  • Chat, voice, and social media information, such as chat messages and friends.

Since these categories can combine to paint a full picture of one individual, they deserve multi-layered protection. The technologies below aim to solve various aspects of the problem.

What Technologies Protect Player Data?

No single tool protects everything, so platforms combine several. The table gives a quick comparison before we look at each in more detail:

Technology What it helps protect Example
Encryption Data stored and transmitted HTTPS for connections and encryption of stored records
Multi-factor authentication Accounts Codes from an app or SMS
Access controls Stored data Limits on staff and systems
Privacy defaults Children’s data Voice chat off by default
Monitoring Accounts and systems Alerts for unusual logins

Each row represents a common pattern, and each organisation may adopt a different configuration. Some platforms use all of these layers, while others rely on just a few.

Encryption and Secure Data Storage

Encryption converts readable data into a protected form that cannot normally be understood without the appropriate decryption key. The ICO, the UK’s data regulator, states that encryption is a key technical control. It applies to both stored and transmitted data. HTTPS is a good example for securing an entire website.

The card data is subject to more restrictions. Organisations that store, process or transmit payment card data are expected to comply with applicable PCI DSS requirements. Several additional PCI DSS v4.x requirements became effective on 31 March 2025.

Authentication and Access Controls

Authentication confirms who the user is before granting access to the account. Multi-factor authentication is an additional process after the password. For instance, in PlayStation, the verification code can be sent via SMS or using an authentication app, with backup codes in case of lost devices. Access controls ensure that sensitive data is accessible only to authorised personnel.

Monitoring and Threat Detection

Detection systems identify suspicious patterns, such as repeated failed logins, sign-ins from an unrecognised device or unusual access to stored data. Upon detecting such a pattern, a platform may request additional authentication, lock an account, or notify the security team.

Additional steps may be included in routine activities, such as logging in. For instance, upon the activation of 2-step verification on PlayStation, the player must enter the verification code on their first sign-in, and upon manually logging out and resetting the password. Monitoring cannot prevent every security breach, but it helps security teams detect suspicious activity and respond more quickly.

Privacy by Design and Default Settings

Privacy by design means building protections into a product from the start. The ICO’s children’s code covers video games and expects high-privacy settings by default. Its tips for game designers suggest voice chat for children should be off by default, and friend requests set to “nobody”.

pixabay

How Can Players Improve Their Own Data Security?

Platform measures work best alongside careful habits. A few minutes of setup makes accounts much harder to take over. These steps are worth taking:

  • Set up multi-factor authentication with an authenticator app, and save the backup codes.
  • Have separate passwords for each gaming account, ideally using a password manager.
  • Inspect the privacy settings, especially concerning chat, friends’ requests, and profile visibility.
  • Review apps and accounts linked to your gaming profile, and remove any you no longer use.
  • Never click on unknown links, and never give out your verification code to anyone.

Nothing makes an account completely safe, but these habits reduce the risk. Check your settings periodically, because platforms add features and defaults can change.

The post How Gaming Platforms Protect Personal Data and Player Accounts appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Kano court reschedules suit challenging NDC governorship candidacy to December 7
description:
The Federal High Court in Kano has postponed proceedings in a case questioning the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidacy in the state ahead of the 2027 election to December 7.
The decision came after the plaintiffs requested more time to file their response to a preliminary object
content:
The Federal High Court in Kano has postponed proceedings in a case questioning the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidacy in the state ahead of the 2027 election to December 7.

The decision came after the plaintiffs requested more time to file their response to a preliminary objection submitted by the party’s lawyer, Barrister Magaji Mato, who is asking the court to dismiss the suit.

Speaking to journalists after the court session on Monday, Mato explained that the plaintiffs were unable to proceed because they had not responded to the objection and other legal documents served on them the previous week.

He said the request for an adjournment followed the plaintiffs’ failure to complete the necessary responses to the court processes filed by the party.

The case is expected to resume on December 7.

“Unfortunately, the other side that brought us to court said they were not ready because we had filed some processes, including a notice of preliminary objection, asking the court to dismiss the matter at this stage because there is no case for us to answer,” he said.

He said his clients did not oppose the request for an adjournment.

“The court graciously adjourned the matter to December 7 for definite hearing. We are ready, and if they serve us with their processes, we will also respond to them. By December 7, we will be fully ready to hear the matter, by the grace of God,” Mato added.

Explaining the grounds of the preliminary objection, the lawyer argued that the suit did not qualify as a pre-election matter because the three plaintiffs were not members of the NDC.

He also contended that even if they were members, they did not participate in the party’s governorship primary organised by its National Working Committee on May 29, 2026.

“Our grounds are simple. First of all, it is not a pre-election matter because the three persons who brought us to court are not even members of our political party,” he said.

Mato further argued that the plaintiffs had not attached documents showing that they purchased nomination forms or were registered members of the party.

He described them as “mercenaries being presented for the purpose of causing confusion among the good people of Kano State”.

The lawyer also challenged the timing of the suit, arguing that it was filed outside the 14-day period stipulated under Section 285(9) of the 1999 Constitution.

He said the NDC submitted its list of candidates on June 10, while the plaintiffs instituted the suit on October 17.

“In this case, the party submitted its list of candidates on June 10, while the suit was instituted on October 17. If you calculate from June 10 to October 17, you will realise that it is far beyond the statutory 14 days,” he said.

Mato argued that the court consequently lacked jurisdiction to entertain the suit.

He said his clients were asking the court to dismiss the case and award costs against the plaintiffs and their lawyers.

“We are asking the court to dismiss their matter because it is a waste of time, energy and resources. Secondly, we are asking the court to impose costs not only on the parties who went to court but also on their counsel,” he stated.

The suit was filed by three NDC members in Kano, Garba Umar Isa, Yau Abubakar and another party member, who are seeking to stop the party from fielding a governorship candidate in the state for the 2027 election.

They are also asking the court to restrain the Independent National Electoral Commission from publishing the name of the party’s governorship candidate, citing a Supreme Court judgment in the Zenith Labour Party case.

In an earlier proceeding, the court, presided over by Justice Simon Amobeda, joined the party’s governorship candidate, Aminu Gwarzo, as a defendant following an application by his counsel, Sagir Gezawa (SAN).

Gwarzo, who secured the NDC ticket with Mustapha Rabiu Kwankwaso as his running mate, was joined as a necessary party to the suit.

title: Iranian currency falls sharply after fresh US sanctions
description:
Iran’s currency plunged on the black market on Tuesday after Washington announced fresh sanctions, which the central bank governor said targeted a regular platform for registering transactions.
The US Treasury announced sanctions on Monday against more than two dozen Iranian exchange houses, alleged
content:
Iran’s currency plunged on the black market on Tuesday after Washington announced fresh sanctions, which the central bank governor said targeted a regular platform for registering transactions.

The US Treasury announced sanctions on Monday against more than two dozen Iranian exchange houses, alleged front companies and individuals said to be part of the country’s “shadow banking” network. It said the network was “overseen” by the central bank.

By Tuesday afternoon, the US dollar was trading at around 2.82 million rials, up about five percent from around 2.68 million the day before, according to websites monitoring black market rates.

The euro also rose to around 3.07 million rials, up from 2.94 million on Monday, the websites said. Iranians use black market rates as the central bank rate is usually much lower.

Central Bank governor Abdolnaser Hemmati dismissed the sanctions, saying the US appeared to have “run out of targets” and had resorted to targeting a legitimate platform.

The sanctioned Iran Currency and Gold Exchange centre “is merely a platform for registering transactions” and “is there for everyone to see,” said Hemmati, according to Tasnim news agency.

The US Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) said it connects exporters earning foreign currency from overseas sales with importers seeking foreign currency to buy goods, facilitating tens of billions of dollars in trade annually.

“While Iran’s shadow banking system moves the funds generated by Iran’s international trade, the Iran Center for Exchange plays matchmaker and guides these funds to their ultimate destination inside Iran,” OFAC said.

The latest sanctions were announced nearly nine months into the Middle East war, which broke out on February 28 when US-Israeli strikes killed Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

The conflict expanded after Iran retaliated with missile and drone strikes across the region, while militant groups it backs in Lebanon, Yemen and Iraq also entered the fray.

Washington has ramped up sanctions since August as part of an “economic asphyxiation” campaign, and launched a task force to disrupt land routes into Iran.

It has also maintained a naval blockade on Iranian ports to choke off the country’s oil revenue in retaliation for Iran’s effective blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy conduit.

title: Bayelsa boat tragedy: Diri appeals for FG’s support to complete roads
description:
Bayelsa State Governor, Senator Douye Diri, has made a fresh appeal to the Federal Government to deepen its collaboration with the state in the construction and completion of the three senatorial district road projects.
The ongoing projects include the Ekeremor-Agge road in Bayelsa West, Yenagoa-Opo
content:
Bayelsa State Governor, Senator Douye Diri, has made a fresh appeal to the Federal Government to deepen its collaboration with the state in the construction and completion of the three senatorial district road projects.

The ongoing projects include the Ekeremor-Agge road in Bayelsa West, Yenagoa-Oporoma-Ukubie road in Bayelsa Central, and the Nembe-Brass road in the eastern district.

While the state had undertaken the construction of phase one of the Nembe-Brass road, with the project nearing completion, the Federal Government has awarded the contract for the second phase.

The other two senatorial roads are being constructed solely by the state government.

Diri renewed his appeal in a statement issued by his Chief Press Secretary, Mr Daniel Alabrah, on Tuesday, following the tragic boat incident of November 20, 2026, in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state, which claimed no fewer than 29 lives.

During Vice-President Kashim Shettima’s condolence visit to the state on Sunday, the Bayelsa governor lamented the slow pace of work on the second phase of the Nembe-Brass project.

He also noted that tragic boat incidents in the riverine state would be reduced or averted if the road projects were completed.

He added that completing the roads would unlock economic benefits for the state and the country, considering the huge natural resources in Bayelsa’s maritime domain.

“Work on the second phase of the Nembe-Brass road is too slow. We believe that if that road is completed, Brass Island will be one of the best in Nigeria,” he said.

On the Yenagoa-Ukubie road, Diri explained that his administration continued its construction from where previous governments stopped around Igeibiri community and completed one of the longest bridges in the state at Angiama, which was commissioned by President Bola Tinubu on April 10 this year.

“Today we drive to Oporoma, the headquarters of Southern Ijaw Local Government Area. This road continues to Ukubie, where these victims were heading as their final destination.

“I have less than two years to go. Because of the cost of construction, I plead and again bring to attention the necessity of a federal government collaboration with the state to take this road from Oporoma to Ukubie. I am very sure that if there was a road to Ukubie, this accident might not have happened.”

On the West Senatorial Road, Diri said Agge in Ekeremor Local Government Area has a natural deep seaport and that the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy was collaborating with the state to develop the Agge Deep Seaport into another economic hub, not only for Bayelsa but for the country.

“Agge has a natural deep seaport and ships are already berthing there. So it is an economically viable area. We have gone very far in making sure that it becomes another economic hub, not only for our state but for our country,” Diri said.

He further stated that the Ekeremor-Agge road serves as the critical land link connecting Bayelsa’s riverine communities to the Atlantic Ocean, unlocking maritime trade, lowering transport costs and spurring industrial growth, which would in turn contribute to the nation’s GDP.

According to him, the state government was actively constructing the key access route to the proposed $3bn seaport at Agge.

The Bayelsa governor urged the Federal Government to sustain its support for the state, noting that the completion of the senatorial roads would improve connectivity and open up more communities for economic activities.

“Your Excellency, Mr President, if you collaborate with our state government on these roads, you would have written your name in gold in Bayelsa State,” he said.

The post Bayelsa boat tragedy: Diri appeals for FG’s support to complete roads appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Army decorates 32 newly promoted soldiers
description:
The General Officer Commanding, 10 Division of the Nigerian Army, Major General Chinedu Nnebeife, has urged 32 newly promoted soldiers to demonstrate greater dedication, discipline and professionalism in their duties.
Nnebeife gave the charge during the decoration ceremony of the soldiers, who were
content:
The General Officer Commanding, 10 Division of the Nigerian Army, Major General Chinedu Nnebeife, has urged 32 newly promoted soldiers to demonstrate greater dedication, discipline and professionalism in their duties.

Nnebeife gave the charge during the decoration ceremony of the soldiers, who were promoted in the Nigerian Army’s 2026 promotion exercise, with their new ranks ranging from Lance Corporal to Army Warrant Officer.

The Army disclosed this in a statement posted on its X handle on Tuesday and signed by the Acting Deputy Director, Army Public Relations, 10 Division, Aliyu Danja.

The GOC urged the beneficiaries to justify the confidence reposed in them by the Army, noting that promotion came with greater responsibilities and higher expectations.

He noted that “while promotion ultimately comes from God Almighty, their elevation was equally a recognition of their hard work, commitment and contributions to the Service.”

He reminded them to uphold the Nigerian Army’s core values of courage, discipline, selfless service, respect for humanity and dedication to duty.

Nnebeife said their elevation was not only a recognition of their hard work, commitment and contributions to the service but also a call to greater responsibility.

He congratulated the soldiers and urged them to regard their new ranks as an opportunity to demonstrate greater professionalism and loyalty to the Nigerian Army.

The GOC also acknowledged the sacrifices of the beneficiaries’ families, particularly their spouses, who often shoulder additional responsibilities while the soldiers are away from home on operational assignments and other military duties.

He commended them for their patience, resilience and continued support, describing their contributions as invaluable to the effectiveness and success of military personnel.

Speaking on behalf of the beneficiaries, Army Warrant Officer Emeka Ukandu thanked the Chief of Army Staff for approving their promotions and finding them worthy of elevation.

He assured the Army leadership of their renewed commitment to duty and determination to justify the confidence reposed in them.

Ukandu also appreciated the GOC for his leadership and encouragement, while acknowledging the sacrifices and support of their families.

He prayed for personnel awaiting promotion, expressing hope that they would be successful in subsequent exercises.

The 32 promoted soldiers comprised one Army Warrant Officer, two Master Warrant Officers, three Staff Sergeants, one Sergeant, eight Corporals and 17 Lance Corporals.

The ceremony was attended by commanders, staff officers, serving and retired military personnel, family members and well-wishers.

Highlights included the reading of the beneficiaries’ citations, decoration with their new ranks, words of advice, a vote of thanks and group photographs.

title: China sentences official to death for spying, leaking state secrets
description:
The Chinese government has sentenced an official identified as Ma to death for spying for a foreign country.
The official reportedly signed an agreement on “confidentiality” and “loyalty”, handed over 35 pieces of information classified as state secrets, and received payments worth more than 1 milli
content:
The Chinese government has sentenced an official identified as Ma to death for spying for a foreign country.

The official reportedly signed an agreement on “confidentiality” and “loyalty”, handed over 35 pieces of information classified as state secrets, and received payments worth more than 1 million yuan ($150,000), The Guardian reported on Tuesday.

According to Gold Wall Press, a publishing company associated with China’s national administration of state secrets protection, Ma was approached and recruited by an unnamed foreign intelligence service while working abroad.

The report stated that an intelligence operative identified as Kailin “frequently arranged to meet with Ma, hoping to engage with him more,” citing an interest in learning Chinese.

It added that Kailin later introduced Ma to a colleague who threatened to report his earlier disclosures to Chinese authorities if he refused to cooperate.

After returning to China, Ma continued to gather intelligence for the foreign agency, which provided him with a laptop, the statement said. He used his position to collect material from classified documents during the day and transmitted it overseas at night via an espionage website.

The statement did not disclose the countries involved, when or where Ma was sentenced, or whether he had already been executed.

The report further stated that recently, the Ministry of State Security and Gold Wall Press have increasingly publicised arrests, as well as using social media, movies and comics to promote warnings about espionage.

Chinese courts typically do not publish information about state security cases, it added.

Gold Wall Press said “this shocking case serves as yet another wake-up call,” as it warned that foreign intelligence agencies were “cunning” and used emotional ties, financial interests and threats to recruit people in key positions.

The statement also urged officials to remain vigilant, strengthen their loyalty to the Communist Party, protect state secrets and guard against foreign recruitment.

The Guardian reported that the case followed publications by US intelligence of its efforts to recruit sources in China.

It referenced the YouTube channel of the Central Intelligence Agency, saying its five most-viewed videos on the channel are recruiting advertisements in Mandarin.

A check on the CIA’s YouTube channel by PUNCH Online on Tuesday revealed that the five most-viewed videos had a total of 135.7 million views.

The oldest of the five videos, titled ‘Safely Contacting the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency (CIA),’ was uploaded on October 2, 2024, with over 17m views.

Screenshots taken from the video and translated to English urged anyone willing to contact the CIA to take some precautions, including the type of computer, internet network, and browser to use.

Some of the instructions read, “The preferred way to contact us is to use a trusted non-local VPN service or the Tor network to strengthen your security. If you don’t take these steps, any website you visit may be monitored by security or intelligence agencies or other third parties. Although the content of our website is encrypted, if you don’t take these steps, others may be able to see which websites you have visited.

“If you choose to contact us through https://cia.gov, you must use a VPN. Please consider the following: Use a VPN provider whose headquarters are not in Russia, Iran, China, or any other country considered unfriendly to the United States. Choose a VPN server (country/region of origin) that is not in Russia, Iran, China, or a country considered unfriendly to the United States.”

It added that if an individual wants to be contacted by the CIA via email, they must “provide an email address whose domain host is not in China, Iran, Russia, or any other country considered unfriendly to the United States.

“This email address must not include any personally identifying information, and must not be linked to any account or device you use personally,” among other instructions.

The Guardian reported that in June 2023, China expanded the definition of espionage and strengthened the investigative powers of state security authorities.

The Guardian reported that under the revised law, “relying on espionage organisations and their agents” as well as the unauthorised obtaining of “documents, data, materials, and items related to national security and interests” can constitute a spying offence.

The post China sentences official to death for spying, leaking state secrets appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
The Federal High Court in Kano has adjourned until December 7 a suit challenging the Nigeria Democratic Congress’s governorship candidacy in the state ahead of the 2027 election.

“Unfortunately, the other side that brought us to court said they were not ready because we had filed some processes, including a notice of preliminary objection, asking the court to dismiss the matter at this stage because there is no case for us to answer,” he said.

He said his clients did not oppose the request for an adjournment.

“The court graciously adjourned the matter to December 7 for definite hearing. We are ready, and if they serve us with their processes, we will also respond to them. By December 7, we will be fully ready to hear the matter, by the grace of God,” Mato added.

Explaining the grounds of the preliminary objection, the lawyer argued that the suit did not qualify as a pre-election matter because the three plaintiffs were not members of the NDC.

He also contended that even if they were members, they did not participate in the party’s governorship primary organised by its National Working Committee on May 29, 2026.

“Our grounds are simple. First of all, it is not a pre-election matter because the three persons who brought us to court are not even members of our political party,” he said.

Mato further argued that the plaintiffs had not attached documents showing that they purchased nomination forms or were registered members of the party.

He described them as “mercenaries being presented for the purpose of causing confusion among the good people of Kano State”.

The lawyer also challenged the timing of the suit, arguing that it was filed outside the 14-day period stipulated under Section 285(9) of the 1999 Constitution.

He said the NDC submitted its list of candidates on June 10, while the plaintiffs instituted the suit on October 17.

“In this case, the party submitted its list of candidates on June 10, while the suit was instituted on October 17. If you calculate from June 10 to October 17, you will realise that it is far beyond the statutory 14 days,” he said.

Mato argued that the court consequently lacked jurisdiction to entertain the suit.

He said his clients were asking the court to dismiss the case and award costs against the plaintiffs and their lawyers.

“We are asking the court to dismiss their matter because it is a waste of time, energy and resources. Secondly, we are asking the court to impose costs not only on the parties who went to court but also on their counsel,” he stated.

The suit was filed by three NDC members in Kano, Garba Umar Isa, Yau Abubakar and another party member, who are seeking to stop the party from fielding a governorship candidate in the state for the 2027 election.

They are also asking the court to restrain the Independent National Electoral Commission from publishing the name of the party’s governorship candidate, citing a Supreme Court judgment in the Zenith Labour Party case.

In an earlier proceeding, the court, presided over by Justice Simon Amobeda, joined the party’s governorship candidate, Aminu Gwarzo, as a defendant following an application by his counsel, Sagir Gezawa (SAN).

Gwarzo, who secured the NDC ticket with Mustapha Rabiu Kwankwaso as his running mate, was joined as a necessary party to the suit.

title: NYSC urges corps members to respect culture of host communities
description:
The Benue State Coordinator of the National Youth Service Corps, Veronica Garba, has charged corps members to respect the traditions and cultures of their host communities.
Garba gave the charge on Tuesday during the closing ceremony of the 2026 Batch ‘C’ Stream II Orientation Course for corps membe
content:
The Benue State Coordinator of the National Youth Service Corps, Veronica Garba, has charged corps members to respect the traditions and cultures of their host communities.

Garba gave the charge on Tuesday during the closing ceremony of the 2026 Batch ‘C’ Stream II Orientation Course for corps members deployed to the state, including those dislodged from the Federal Capital Territory.

The ceremony was held at the NYSC Permanent Orientation Camp, Wannune, Tarka Local Government Area of the state.

A total of 1,608 corps members were posted to the state for the 2026 Batch ‘C’ Stream II.

The state coordinator further charged them to integrate positively into their new environments and make meaningful contributions that would leave lasting and positive impressions.

She said, “As you are going to your area of primary assignment, endeavour to respect the culture and traditions of your host communities. Do not constitute a nuisance but make positive contributions that will impact positively on your host communities.”

Garba also used the opportunity to appreciate Governor Hyacinth Alia for his unwavering support and commitment to the security and welfare of the scheme in the state.

She said, “Let me use this opportunity to appreciate the Executive Governor of Benue State, Rev. Fr. Hyacinth Alia, for consistently providing an enabling environment for the successful conduct of orientation courses and other NYSC activities in the state since the inception of his administration.”

She further urged the corps members to put into practice the values, lessons and training acquired during the orientation course, particularly the skills acquired through the Skills Acquisition and Entrepreneurship Development programme.

“As you go to your primary assignment, ensure you put into practice the values and lessons learnt during the orientation camp.

“I encourage you to also put into practice the Skills Acquisition and Entrepreneurship Development programme, which can enhance your self-development, employability and income generation,” she stated.

title: Abuja Court orders freeze on N135.5bn NGF funds over Paris Club refund dispute
description:
An Abuja High Court has ordered the interim freezing of $100 million, equivalent to approximately N135.55 billion, paid to the Nigerian Governors’ Forum (NGF) as a stakeholder in the disputed London and Paris Club refunds.
Justice O. C. Agbaza granted the interim Mareva injunction on November 19, fo
content:
An Abuja High Court has ordered the interim freezing of $100 million, equivalent to approximately N135.55 billion, paid to the Nigerian Governors’ Forum (NGF) as a stakeholder in the disputed London and Paris Club refunds.

Justice O. C. Agbaza granted the interim Mareva injunction on November 19, following an ex-parte application filed by Dr Ted Iseghohi-Edwards.

The order restrains the Incorporated Trustees of the NGF from withdrawing, transferring, dissipating or otherwise dealing with the disputed funds.

The judge also directed 29 commercial banks joined in the suit to refrain from releasing, transferring, converting or otherwise dealing with any NGF funds in their custody.

In addition, the banks were ordered to disclose within 48 hours of receiving the order whether the NGF maintains accounts with them containing the disputed money.

They are also required to identify the accounts, state their currencies and available balances, and disclose the amounts preserved in compliance with the court order.

The $100 million was valued at N135.55 billion using an exchange rate of N1,355.80 to the dollar.

A certified true copy of the enrolled order was obtained by the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Tuesday in Abuja.

Iseghohi-Edwards, who operates Edwards and Partners Law Firm, is seeking to recover the money based on an indemnity allegedly issued by the NGF on December 20, 2018.

According to his claim, the indemnity arose from an arrangement under which the Federal Government paid $100 million to the NGF to hold as a stakeholder pending the determination of the government’s liability for his legal and consultancy fees.

The fees reportedly arose from services he rendered in connection with the London and Paris Club loan transactions.

The claimant said he was engaged by the Incorporated Trustees of the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria (ALGON) to represent the 774 local government councils in matters relating to the London and Paris Club refunds.

He subsequently instituted Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/856/2016 against the Federal Government over outstanding professional fees.

In his court filings, Iseghohi-Edwards claimed that the Federal High Court, on February 16, 2018, delivered judgment establishing the government’s indebtedness to him in the sum of $318 million.

He further stated that the government later made a part-payment of $159 million through promissory notes.

The claimant argued that the judgment satisfied the condition stipulated in the NGF’s indemnity, thereby making the $100 million payable to him.

Under the alleged indemnity, the NGF had undertaken to release the money to him if the Federal Government was found liable.

Iseghohi-Edwards said he formally demanded payment from the forum in a letter dated October 8, 2026, but the NGF allegedly failed to honour its undertaking.

He consequently approached the FCT High Court to secure the funds pending the determination of his substantive claim.

In his application, he expressed fears that the NGF might transfer, disburse or dissipate the money, potentially frustrating the enforcement of any eventual judgment in his favour.

He also told the court that he could not identify the specific bank accounts holding the funds without judicial intervention.

The claimant maintained that the injunction was necessary to preserve the subject matter of the dispute and prevent the proceedings from being rendered ineffective.

He further argued that the restriction covered only one aggregate sum of $100 million across the NGF and all the participating banks.

The application was brought under Orders 30(3) and 32(1) of the FCT High Court Civil Procedure Rules, as well as the court’s inherent jurisdiction.

He also undertook to abide by any order for damages should the court later determine that the interim injunction ought not to have been granted.

Justice Agbaza adjourned the matter until December 1 for the hearing of the motion on notice and directed the claimant to serve the order on all respondents.

The first respondent in the suit is the Incorporated Trustees of the Nigerian Governors’ Forum, while 29 commercial banks were joined as co-respondents.

The banks include Access Bank Plc, Alpha Morgan Bank Limited, Ecobank Nigeria Plc, Fidelity Bank Plc, First Bank of Nigeria Plc, Sterling Bank Plc, United Bank for Africa Plc, Unity Bank Plc, Zenith Bank Plc and Jaiz Bank Plc.

Others are Guaranty Trust Bank Plc, Keystone Bank Plc, Stanbic IBTC Bank Limited, Standard Chartered Bank Limited, Wema Bank Plc, Union Bank of Nigeria Plc, First City Monument Bank Plc, Lotus Bank Plc, Parallex Bank Limited and Polaris Bank Limited.

The remaining respondents are Globus Bank Limited, SunTrust Bank Limited, Citibank Nigeria Limited, Nova Bank Limited, Optimus Bank Limited, Premium Trust Bank Limited, Signature Bank Limited, Tatum Bank Limited and Titan Trust Bank Limited.

The post Abuja Court orders freeze on N135.5bn NGF funds over Paris Club refund dispute appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Lagos opens channels to report poor artisan services
description:
The Lagos State Government has urged residents to report artisans and other skilled service providers who delay jobs, fail to deliver agreed services or abandon projects after collecting payment.
The Lagos State Consumer Protection Agency said residents experiencing disputes with tailors, plumbers,
content:
The Lagos State Government has urged residents to report artisans and other skilled service providers who delay jobs, fail to deliver agreed services or abandon projects after collecting payment.

The Lagos State Consumer Protection Agency said residents experiencing disputes with tailors, plumbers, electricians, mechanics, air-conditioner and refrigerator repairers, carpenters, painters and other skilled professionals could seek redress through its complaint channels.

It also advised consumers to use its mediation services to resolve such disputes rather than resorting to confrontation or involving the police in matters that could be addressed through consumer protection mechanisms.

LASCOPA General Manager and Chief Executive Officer, Afolabi Solebo, disclosed this in a statement posted on the Lagos State Government’s Facebook page on Tuesday.

Solebo said engaging an artisan or skilled professional established a consumer-service provider relationship, entitling customers to fair treatment, satisfactory service delivery and redress when agreed terms were breached.

He said the agency had received several complaints from residents who struggled to resolve disputes with service providers, particularly where artisans failed to complete agreed jobs, delayed delivery or abandoned projects without satisfactory explanations.

He cited cases involving tailors who failed to deliver clothes as agreed and other service providers who abandoned customers after collecting payment.

“We have handled cases where consumers submitted clothes to tailors for sewing, only for the artisans to fail to deliver as agreed. In some instances, consumers were left frustrated and without any clear means of resolving the situation until they were referred to LASCOPA for intervention,” he said.

The LASCOPA chief urged residents facing such challenges to lodge formal complaints with the agency, irrespective of their language, tribe, religion, political affiliation or social status, assuring them of fair and impartial attention.

He also advised consumers to preserve evidence of transactions, including receipts, invoices, payment records, bank debit alerts, transfer confirmations, written agreements and correspondence with service providers, to facilitate the investigation and resolution of complaints.

Solebo called on artisans and other skilled service providers to uphold professionalism, transparency and accountability by delivering services according to agreed specifications, maintaining effective communication with customers and avoiding unnecessary delays or abandonment of jobs.

LASCOPA reaffirmed its commitment to facilitating amicable dispute resolution under the Lagos State Consumer Protection Law 2025 (as amended) and the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act 2018.

The agency said it operated annex offices in Ikorodu, Badagry, Bariga, Ikoyi-Obalende, Ojo, Epe, Agege and Isolo to make its services accessible to residents.

Consumers can also contact the agency through its complaint lines, 081 2499 3895 and 091 5389 4878, or its toll-free helpline, 080 0005 2726, available on weekdays.

Complaints may also be sent by email to lasgcopa@gmail.com or lascopa@lagosstate.gov.ng, or through the agency’s Facebook page, LASCOPA, and Instagram account, @lasgcopa.

The post Lagos opens channels to report poor artisan services appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
