title: VIDEO: ‘I’ll be a better CEO,’ reinstated Nvidia boss tells cheering staff
description:
The President and Chief Executive Officer of US technology giant Nvidia, Jensen Huang, has promised to become a “better CEO” following his reinstatement after an 11-day absence from the position.
Huang resigned on November 12, 2026, amid a controversy involving allegations of extramarital relationsh
content:
The President and Chief Executive Officer of US technology giant Nvidia, Jensen Huang, has promised to become a “better CEO” following his reinstatement after an 11-day absence from the position.

Huang resigned on November 12, 2026, amid a controversy involving allegations of extramarital relationships, including one with Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed International, whom US authorities reportedly suspected of having links to Chinese intelligence.

Huang admitted being unfaithful to his wife and apologised to his family and colleagues, but did not publicly confirm the specific allegations involving Alice.

In light of this, the company appointed board member Harvey Jones, a former chief executive of technology company Synopsys, as its first-ever board chairman.

However, on Monday, November 23, 2026, Nvidia’s board unanimously reinstated Huang as chief executive.

The decision came after a series of discussions and meetings with Huang, the board said, adding that it was satisfied with his candour and ability to lead the company.

However, in a video posted by NBC News on its Facebook page on Monday, Huang was seen addressing employees, as he apologised for putting them through the controversy.

During his address, a woman whose identity could not immediately be verified ran towards him and embraced him, while employees in the packed lobby chanted, “Jensen! Jensen! Jensen!”

He said, “Thank you all for the second chance. I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around.

“I’m terribly sorry for putting all of you through all of this. I’ve made some very terrible mistakes, and I’m going to work on coming back.”

On Monday, US President Donald Trump praised Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Huang as chief executive, as Democratic leaders vowed investigations and prominent Republicans questioned whether his return posed a national security risk.

Trump also posted a doctored version of the famous photograph of him raising his fist after surviving a 2024 assassination attempt, replacing himself with Huang, who brandished a red bra beneath an Nvidia flag.

The image appeared to allude to the scandal that forced Huang to resign less than two weeks earlier.

According to a CNN report, the company’s shares recorded their third-best day on record on Monday following Huang’s return, climbing by more than 30 per cent.

title: Court freezes $100m linked to governors over Paris Club refund
description:
A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, has ordered the freezing of $100 million (about N135.58 billion) allegedly held by the Nigerian Governors’ Forum over a dispute arising from the Paris Club refunds and outstanding legal and consultancy fees.
Justice O.C. Agbaza granted the interi
content:
A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, has ordered the freezing of $100 million (about N135.58 billion) allegedly held by the Nigerian Governors’ Forum over a dispute arising from the Paris Club refunds and outstanding legal and consultancy fees.

Justice O.C. Agbaza granted the interim Mareva injunction on November 19, following an ex parte application by a lawyer, Dr Ted Iseghohi-Edwards, against the Incorporated Trustees of the NGF and 29 commercial banks.

In the copy of the CTC order sighted by The PUNCH on Tuesday, the claimant is seeking to recover the money pursuant to an indemnity allegedly issued by the NGF on December 20, 2018, under an arrangement in which the Federal Government paid $100m to the forum as a stakeholder pending the determination of its liability for professional fees.

The 29 banks joined in the suit as respondents include Access Bank, Alpha Morgan Bank, Ecobank Nigeria, Fidelity Bank, First Bank, Sterling Bank, United Bank for Africa, Unity Bank, Zenith Bank, Jaiz Bank, Guaranty Trust Bank, Keystone Bank, Stanbic IBTC, Standard Chartered Bank and Wema Bank.

Others are Union Bank, First City Monument Bank, Lotus Bank, Parallex Bank, Polaris Bank, Globus Bank, SunTrust Bank, Citibank Nigeria, Nova Bank, Optimus Bank, Premium Trust Bank, Signature Bank, Tatum Bank and Titan Trust Bank.

In the enrolled order, the judge restrained the NGF, its servants, agents, representatives and anyone acting on its behalf from withdrawing, transferring, dissipating, concealing, disposing of or otherwise dealing with the funds.

The order also restrained the 29 banks from releasing, transferring, converting, withdrawing, paying out or otherwise dealing with any funds standing to the credit of the NGF in their custody, up to the aggregate sum of $100m or its naira equivalent of N135,580,360,000.

The enrolled order stated, “An order of Interim Mareva Injunction restraining the 1st Defendant/Respondent, whether by themselves, their servants, agents, privies, representatives or any person acting on its instructions or behalf from withdrawing, transferring, dissipating, concealing, disposing of, encumbering or otherwise dealing with any funds up the sum of US$100,000,000.00 (One Hundred Million United State Dollars) or its Naira equivalent being the sum of ₦135,580,360,000.00 (One Hundred and Thirty-Five Billion, Five Hundred and Eighty Million, Three Hundred and Sixty Thousand Naira), calculated at the prevailing exchange rate of the United States Dollars to the Nigerian Naira as published by the Central Bank of Nigeria on 17 November 2026, or any part thereof.

“Being funds representing the subject of the Claimant/Applicant’s claim upon the indemnity dated 20 December 2018 to the extent that those funds are held by or on behalf of the 1st Defendant/Respondent within the jurisdiction of this court pending the hearing and determination of the Motion on Notice for Interlocutory Injunction or further order of this Honourable Court.

“An order of interim Mareva Injunction restraining the 2nd – 30th Respondents, whether by themselves, their directors, officers, servants, agents, privies or representatives, upon service of the order and to the extent that any of them holds funds described in prayer 1 in an account from releasing, paying, transferring, withdrawing, converting, dissipating or otherwise dealing with any funds standing to the credit of the 1st Defendant in the name of the 1st Defendant/Respondent, from permitting any withdrawal, transfer, conversion, payment, disbursement, application, utilisation or other dealing with those funds, subject to the same duration and single aggregate limit.”

Justice Agbaza further directed the banks to disclose, within 48 hours of being served with the order, whether the NGF maintained accounts containing the disputed funds.

The banks are also required to identify such accounts, their currencies, available balances and the amounts preserved pursuant to the order.

The judge directed the claimant to promptly serve the originating process, supporting affidavit, written address, motion on notice and enrolled order on the respondents.

The claimant’s case is that the money belongs to him under the indemnity issued by the NGF, which reportedly undertook to pay him the $100m if the FG was found liable for the outstanding professional fees.

Iseghohi-Edwards, who carries on business under the name and style of Edwards and Partners Law Firm, claimed to have been retained by the Incorporated Trustees of the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria to represent the 774 Local Government councils in matters relating to the London and Paris Club refunds.

He subsequently instituted suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/856/2016 against the FG over outstanding legal and consultancy fees arising from the transactions.

According to his court filings, the Federal High Court delivered judgment on February 16, 2018, establishing the government’s indebtedness of $318m.

He said the FG subsequently made a part-payment of $159m through Promissory Notes.

The claimant contended that the judgment satisfied the condition contained in the NGF’s indemnity, thereby making the $100m payable directly to him.

He further alleged that despite formally demanding payment from the NGF in a letter dated October 8, 2026, the forum failed to honour its undertaking.

Consequently, he approached the FCT High Court to preserve the disputed funds pending the determination of his substantive claim.

In seeking the interim injunction, Iseghohi-Edwards expressed apprehension that the NGF could transfer, disburse or dissipate the funds, thereby frustrating the enforcement of any eventual judgment in his favour.

He also told the court that he could not independently identify the specific bank accounts holding the money without judicial intervention.

The claimant argued that the injunction was necessary to preserve the subject matter of the dispute and prevent the proceedings from becoming futile.

He maintained that the restriction was limited to a single aggregate sum of $100m across the NGF and all participating banks.

The application was brought pursuant to Orders 30(3) and 32(1) of the High Court of the Federal Capital Territory Civil Procedure Rules and the court’s inherent jurisdiction.

In granting the application, Justice Agbaza ordered that the restrictions on the banks would remain in force pending the hearing and determination of the claimant’s motion on notice for an interlocutory injunction or further order of the court.

The judge also directed the banks to file affidavits disclosing whether they held accounts belonging to the NGF containing the disputed funds.

The order further required the banks to identify the accounts, the relevant currency, the balances at the time of service and the amounts preserved, subject to any confidentiality directions the court might make.

The case was adjourned until December 1, 2026, for the hearing of the motion on notice.

title: Delta campaign attack fifth attempt on my life — Omo-Agege
description:
Former Deputy Senate President and Nigeria Democratic Congress candidate for Delta Central, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, has described Monday’s deadly attack on his campaign event in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, as the fifth attempt on his life.
Omo-Agege, who said the gunm
content:
Former Deputy Senate President and Nigeria Democratic Congress candidate for Delta Central, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, has described Monday’s deadly attack on his campaign event in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, as the fifth attempt on his life.

Omo-Agege, who said the gunmen opened fire only after he began addressing supporters, also accused police officers deployed to the campaign venue of failing to intervene as fire was opened on his entourage.

The NDC senatorial candidate made the allegations on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily.

Recounting the attack, which reportedly left several people dead and others injured, Omo-Agege said, “This is the fifth attempt on my life.”

He recalled that the first attempt occurred at a consultation event in Usiefurun, Ughelli South.

“The first attempt on my life was at a community called Usiefurun in Ughelli South. We were supposed to have had the same consultation event at a Catholic school there because usually here in Delta State, we are not allowed to use government venues, including government schools, weekend or otherwise.

“We’re not allowed to use even private hotels that we normally use. They threaten the hotel owners to revoke their permissions,” he said.

The former Deputy President of the Senate alleged that police officers at the scene did not protect him or attempt to stop the attackers.

He said the officers watched as the assailants initially fired shots into the air before turning their guns towards him and his entourage.

“The police officers were there, but in the course of this shooting, they didn’t even lift a finger. Not a gunshot, they didn’t protect me. They were just—it was like they were there to supervise my execution, for want of a better expression,” he said.

Omo-Agege added that he expected the officers to stop the shooting, seize the weapons and arrest the attackers, but they allegedly failed to act.

“I expected the police officers, you know, to shut down what they were doing, maybe seize the guns and arrest them, but they didn’t do that,” he said.

He further alleged that the shooting began shortly after other political representatives had addressed the gathering and he stood up to speak.

“They waited for me to get on my feet before the gunshots began to ring out. I’m so bitter. I’m so disappointed. We don’t expect any justice,” he added.

The attack occurred on Monday while Omo-Agege was addressing supporters in Uduere.

In an earlier interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today, he said the gunmen repeatedly shouted his name. “Right there at the venue, while they were shooting, we could hear them say, ‘It is Omo-Agege we want to kill. We must kill Omo-Agege.’”

He credited his Department of State Services (DSS) escorts with saving his life, describing the assault as premeditated and timed for less than five minutes after he began speaking.

His campaign organisation initially reported that four people were killed, including aides Moses Anaughe (a former member of the Delta State House of Assembly) and Akima Efemena Umukoro, with about 15 others injured, some critically.

The Nigeria Police Force later confirmed that preliminary reports indicated six people died and several others were injured.

The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, said the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, has ordered a thorough, impartial investigation that will also examine the deployment and conduct of police personnel at the venue.

Any officer found negligent or in breach of standards faces disciplinary action or prosecution.

The Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew (6 pm to 6 am) across Ughelli North until further notice.

NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi condemned the killings, identified some of the victims, offered condolences, and demanded that security agencies identify and prosecute those responsible, including any sponsors.

He stressed that political differences must be resolved through persuasion and the ballot, not violence.

Omo-Agege’s campaign has called for an independent probe by the Inspector-General of Police and urged supporters to remain calm while continuing its activities.

The post Delta campaign attack fifth attempt on my life — Omo-Agege appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Bauchi targets 1.5 million children for vitamin A supplementation
description:
The Bauchi State Government has targeted 1,557,500 children aged between six and 59 months for vitamin A supplementation in the second round of the 2026 Maternal, Newborn and Child Health Week campaign.
The exercise, flagged off on Monday by the State Primary Health Care Development Board, will also
content:
The Bauchi State Government has targeted 1,557,500 children aged between six and 59 months for vitamin A supplementation in the second round of the 2026 Maternal, Newborn and Child Health Week campaign.

The exercise, flagged off on Monday by the State Primary Health Care Development Board, will also target pregnant women with the distribution of 36,000 bottles of multiple micronutrient supplements.

Speaking at the flag-off ceremony, the Executive Chairman of the board, Dr Rilwanu Mohammed, said the state recorded 99 per cent coverage in vitamin A supplementation during the first round of the 2026 campaign.

He described the achievement as encouraging and commended health workers, community mobilisers and development partners for their contributions.

“During the first round of the 2026 MNCHW, our results were encouraging. The state attained 99 per cent coverage in vitamin A supplementation, demonstrating the commitment of our health workers, community mobilisers and partners.

“I commend everyone who contributed to this achievement and urge us to sustain this momentum,” he said.

Mohammed explained that the interventions were designed to address micronutrient deficiencies, strengthen immunity, support healthy child development and improve maternal nutrition.

He, however, expressed concern over some maternal and child health indicators in the state, noting that antenatal care coverage by skilled providers stood at 61 per cent, facility delivery at 42.1 per cent and skilled birth attendance at 40.9 per cent.

He added that Penta 3 immunisation coverage had declined to 44.1 per cent, stressing the need for increased efforts to improve access to essential maternal and child healthcare services.

The chairman also commended Helen Keller International, UNICEF, the World Health Organisation and other development partners for supporting the state’s healthcare interventions.

He further disclosed that Bauchi State recorded 68 per cent coverage during the recent Human Papillomavirus vaccination intensification exercise, ranking second nationally after Lagos State.

Mohammed urged health workers, traditional and religious leaders, community mobilisers, civil society organisations and the media to intensify awareness and mobilisation to ensure that eligible children and pregnant women benefited from the campaign.

In her remarks, the Bauchi State First Lady, Aisha Mohammed, said preventable maternal and childhood illnesses and deaths remained major public health challenges requiring sustained interventions.

She said the campaign provided an opportunity to deliver essential healthcare services to women and children, particularly those in underserved and hard-to-reach communities.

The First Lady urged mothers and caregivers to take advantage of the exercise by ensuring that eligible children received routine immunisation, vitamin A supplementation, deworming and other nutritional interventions.

She also advised pregnant women to attend antenatal clinics regularly, deliver under the care of skilled birth attendants and seek medical attention whenever necessary.

“As the First Lady of Bauchi State, I remain committed to promoting women’s health, child protection, family welfare and the well-being of vulnerable members of our society.

“We must work together to ensure that no mother is left behind, no child is denied essential healthcare, and no community is excluded from these life-saving interventions,” she said.

She subsequently declared the second round of the 2026 Maternal, Newborn and Child Health Week campaign open.

In her goodwill message, the UNICEF Chief of Bauchi Field Office, Nuzhat Rafique, commended the state government for its continued commitment to improving maternal and child health through the timely implementation of the programme.

Rafique, who was represented by the Health Specialist, Dr David Audu, described the campaign as one of the most effective platforms for delivering integrated, life-saving interventions to vulnerable populations.

She disclosed that UNICEF had provided more than 1.5 million doses of vitamin A supplements, alongside additional implementation support, to strengthen service delivery and improve coverage across the state.

According to her, children aged between six and 59 months would benefit from vitamin A supplementation, deworming, nutritional screening and referral services, while pregnant women would receive multiple micronutrient supplements and other essential maternal health interventions.

She explained that vitamin A played a critical role in children’s growth and immunity, warning that its deficiency could cause preventable childhood blindness and increase the risk of severe infections and death from diseases such as diarrhoea and measles.

“Evidence shows that periodic high-dose vitamin A supplementation is a cost-effective intervention capable of reducing child mortality by between 12 and 24 per cent, making it a critical investment in child survival,” she said.

The UNICEF representative called on parents, caregivers, community and religious leaders, as well as the media, to support mobilisation efforts and ensure that every eligible child and pregnant woman accessed the services.

title: Nollywood mourns as actress Anike Sinleke dies
description:
Nollywood has been thrown into mourning following the death of Yoruba actress Adenike Babajide, popularly known as Anike Sinleke, after reportedly battling ovarian cancer.
Fellow actress Bukky Fagbuyi announced her death on Sunday in a post shared on Instagram.
Sinleke is the latest in a string of Y
content:
Nollywood has been thrown into mourning following the death of Yoruba actress Adenike Babajide, popularly known as Anike Sinleke, after reportedly battling ovarian cancer.

Fellow actress Bukky Fagbuyi announced her death on Sunday in a post shared on Instagram.

Sinleke is the latest in a string of Yoruba film industry figures to have died of cancer in recent months.

Recall that actress and filmmaker Temitope Osoba died in early August at the age of 40 after a prolonged battle with breast cancer, which she had spoken about publicly. She began acting in 2005 and featured in films including Ogun Mi and Gucci Girls.

Later that month, on August 23, veteran actor Taiwo Hassan, popularly known as Ogogo, also died after reportedly battling stage-four cancer.

Barely two weeks later, actress Atinuke Remilekun Kareemalso died of breast cancer. Her death was announced by the Ogun State chapter of the Theatre Arts and Motion Pictures Practitioners Association of Nigeria.

Fagbuyi, who hosts the Instagram Live programme Rubbin Minds With Bukky, disclosed that the late actress had been scheduled to appear as a guest on the programme on the day her death was announced.

“Unfortunately, Nollywood Actress Adenike Abike Babajide A.K.A Anike Sinleke, who was supposed to join us today on our Instagram Live programme RUBBIN MINDS WITH BUKKY, has passed after a battle with Ovarian Cancer.

“May her soul rest in Peace,” she wrote.

The announcement attracted condolence messages from colleagues, including actresses Mistura Asunramu and Omoborty.

Asunramu expressed shock over the news, writing, “Omg, so sorry about this, may her soul rest in peace o.”

Omoborty also reacted, saying, “Oh No!!!”

Actresses Regina Chukwu and Seliat also expressed their sadness with crying emojis.

A Nollywood fan, Bakky Adeoye, wrote, “My condolences, babe. May her soul rest in peace with her ancestors. Aku ara fe’ra ku though I don’t know her.”

Adore by Ayeesha also recalled one of the actress’s popular roles, writing, “Wa sinleke fun mi. Anike Sinleke” before adding, “OMG. RIP beautiful Queen.”

Sinleke began her acting career under the guidance of veteran actor Remmy Shitta and worked with filmmaker Deji Adenuga on movie productions.

She also ventured into film production in the Yoruba movie industry before taking a break from acting to pursue her Higher National Diploma.
Beyond acting, she helped promote Lagos culture and empower women through the Sisi Eko beauty pageant, which she founded around 2011.

The initiative, reportedly supported by the Lagos State Ministry of Information and Strategy, provided a platform for young women to showcase their knowledge of culture, tourism, and education alongside the traditional beauty competition.

Her death has drawn tributes from colleagues and admirers, particularly within the Yoruba movie industry.

The post Nollywood mourns as actress Anike Sinleke dies appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Oyo varsity urges FG to extend NELFUND to private institutions
description:
The Vice-Chancellor of Ajayi Crowther University in Oyo State, Prof Ebunoluwa Oduwole, has urged the Federal Government to extend the Nigerian Education Loan Fund scheme to students of accredited private universities in Nigeria.
She made the appeal during a press conference to herald the institution
content:
The Vice-Chancellor of Ajayi Crowther University in Oyo State, Prof Ebunoluwa Oduwole, has urged the Federal Government to extend the Nigerian Education Loan Fund scheme to students of accredited private universities in Nigeria.

She made the appeal during a press conference to herald the institution’s 18th Convocation Ceremony, held on the school premises in Oyo town on Monday.

Oduwole argued that the exclusion of students in private higher institutions from the scheme defeats its fundamental purpose, which is to make higher education accessible to qualified Nigerians irrespective of their financial circumstances.

The VC said, “Federal Government support for education should be about the Nigerian student, not about the ownership of institutions. If a student is a Nigerian, is admitted through the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board, and is studying in an accredited university in Nigeria, that student deserves support.

“I want to urge the Federal Government and NELFUND management to review the existing legal framework and establish a mechanism through which accredited private universities could participate in the student loan scheme.

“Students in private institutions in Nigeria are still waiting for the full outcome of this initiative,” she added.

PUNCH Online reports that NELFUND, established under the Student Loans (Access to Higher Education) Act, 2024, currently covers students in public universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, leaving out thousands of Nigerian students enrolled in private institutions.

Oduwole explained that the university’s contribution to the nation’s higher education system, as reflected in the number of graduands it would produce this year, demonstrated why private institutions should not be ignored in national funding policies.

Speaking on the convocation, the varsity don added, “A total of 4,104 graduands would be awarded degrees and other qualifications at the university’s 18th convocation. About 116 graduands would receive First Class degrees, 1,207 Second Class Upper degrees, 693 Second Class Lower degrees and 45 Third Class degrees at undergraduate level.

“At postgraduate level, 158 graduands would be awarded postgraduate diplomas, 1,798 master’s degrees and 87 doctoral degrees.”

Oduwole added that the figures demonstrated that private universities were shouldering a significant proportion of Nigeria’s higher education responsibilities and deserved corresponding recognition in the country’s educational funding framework.

She dismissed concerns about academic standards in private universities as an insufficient justification for excluding their students from NELFUND, insisting that institutions such as ACU were subject to the same regulatory standards as their public counterparts.

“If there are objections, if there are issues, there is a formal process we follow. When we talk about quality assurance, it means there is something you are assuring. We ensure that quality is not compromised. So when we say First Class, we mean First Class,” she said.

She stressed that the institution was fully accredited by the JAMB and deployed information and communications technology not only in teaching and learning but also in conducting credible examinations.

According to her, the university had adopted a blend of face-to-face and virtual learning to enhance its academic delivery and improve access to educational resources.

The VC said the National Universities Commission had approved new academic programmes for the university for the 2026/2027 academic session.

“The programmes include Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS), Pharmacy, B.Sc. Anatomy, B.Sc. Physiology, B.Sc. Pharmacology, B.Sc. Public Health, and B.Sc. Artificial Intelligence.

“These are not just numbers. They are a resounding vote of confidence in our academic and infrastructural standards. At Ajayi Crowther University, we don’t just raise scholars; we raise Godly Intellectuals,” Oduwole said.

The post Oyo varsity urges FG to extend NELFUND to private institutions appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: Akpabio, Eno rally support for Tinubu, APC candidates
description:
The President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, and the Akwa Ibom State Governor, Pastor Umo Eno, have urged residents of Ika and Etim Ekpo Local Government Areas to vote for President Bola Tinubu and all candidates of the All Progressives Congress in the 2027 general elections.
Akpabio and Eno made
content:
The President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, and the Akwa Ibom State Governor, Pastor Umo Eno, have urged residents of Ika and Etim Ekpo Local Government Areas to vote for President Bola Tinubu and all candidates of the All Progressives Congress in the 2027 general elections.

Akpabio and Eno made the call on Monday during the flag-off of the APC campaign in the Akwa Ibom North-West Senatorial District, held in Ika and Etim Ekpo LGAs.

Akpabio, who expressed delight at the turnout of APC stakeholders and supporters, urged them to translate their support for him into votes for other candidates of the party.

He called on the people to vote for all APC candidates in the 2027 general elections, assuring them that he would continue to attract development projects to the area with their support.

Akpabio recalled the infrastructure projects he facilitated in the areas while serving as governor and during his tenure as President of the Senate, promising to attract more projects.

“I am not coming to campaign in Ika and Etim Ekpo. I am coming to thank you for your support over the years and to urge you to extend this support to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Governor Umo Eno, and indeed all candidates of our great party,” he said.

Akpabio described Eno as God’s gift to Akwa Ibom State, citing his administration’s developmental strides, and pledged to continue supporting the governor.

“Ikot Ekpene Senatorial District will give the highest number of votes for President Bola Tinubu and all candidates of the All Progressives Congress,” he said.

In his remarks, Eno said the various development projects in the area had been made possible by increased allocations to states and local governments under the Tinubu administration.

He urged residents to turn out en masse to vote for the President and other APC candidates in the 2027 elections.

“We must use our votes to return President Bola Ahmed Tinubu as our President, Distinguished Senator Godswill Akpabio as your senator and myself as the governor, as well as all other candidates of our party, the APC.

“In Akwa Ibom, there is clear zoning of the governorship, and with your support, I will complete my second term and hand over to someone from Ikot Ekpene Senatorial District. This zoning, which has kept our state united, must not be distorted,” Eno said.

Also speaking, the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Ekperikpe Ekpo, an indigene of the area, assured Eno and Akpabio of the people’s commitment to supporting APC candidates in the elections.

“I assure you of our support and commitment to return all the candidates of our party in the general elections come 2027,” he said.

The post 2027: Akpabio, Eno rally support for Tinubu, APC candidates appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Kwankwaso denies sending Yusuf to negotiate APC return
description:
The Vice-Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, has denied sending Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, to President Bola Tinubu to negotiate an arrangement for their return to the All Progressives Congress.
The denial was contained in a statement issued on M
content:
The Vice-Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, has denied sending Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, to President Bola Tinubu to negotiate an arrangement for their return to the All Progressives Congress.

The denial was contained in a statement issued on Monday by the spokesperson for the Kwankwasiyya Movement, Dr Habibu Mohammed, a copy of which was made available to The PUNCH.

“Our attention has been drawn to the interview granted by Kano State Governor, Alhaji Abba Kabir Yusuf, to BBC Hausa, in which he alleged that Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso personally sent him to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to negotiate an arrangement for their return to the All Progressives Congress (APC), allegedly asking him to swear on the Holy Qur’an as evidence of their commitment.

“We consider this allegation another unfortunate attempt by the Governor to shift responsibility for his political decisions to Senator Kwankwaso, rather than demonstrate the courage and maturity expected of a leader entrusted with the mandate of millions of Kano citizens,” it said.

According to the statement, “The Governor is entitled to explain his political decisions and defend his defection. However, he must not confuse the right to offer an explanation with the right to make sweeping allegations against another person without providing credible evidence.”

It explained that Kwankwaso was a nationally recognised political leader whose political decisions and public positions should be judged by his record, publicly expressed convictions and verifiable facts, not by allegations introduced to justify another politician’s changing political affiliations.

“Let it be clearly understood that political consultations, meetings and discussions do not automatically constitute a binding commitment by an entire political movement or its leader to abandon its political convictions. No individual should unilaterally claim to have secured the political consent of Senator Kwankwaso or the Kwankwasiyya Movement without credible evidence,” it further said.

“Let us make one thing clear: Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso is not responsible for Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf’s decision to defect to the APC. If the governor believes that joining the APC is in the best interest of Kano State, he should defend that decision on its own merits and explain the benefits the people of Kano are expected to derive from it, rather than attempting to transfer responsibility to another political leader.

“The statement reminded Governor Yusuf that the political history of their movement demonstrated a consistent tradition of consultation, collective deliberation and engagement with relevant stakeholders. From our political engagements during the days of the PDP, through the formation and development of the APC, the developments around NNPP, and subsequent political engagements involving the ADC and NDC, major decisions have always required consultation with Kwankwasiyya stakeholders, elected representatives, party leaders and relevant organs of the movement.

“These are not decisions that can be made by one individual through private conversations or informal arrangements. No individual can legitimately claim to have secured the consent of an entire political movement simply because of an alleged personal understanding.

“Kwankwaso challenged Governor Yusuf to provide specific and verifiable details if such an arrangement existed.

“If Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf insists that such an agreement existed, we challenge him to provide specific and verifiable details. When exactly was this agreement reached? Who were the participants? Which delegations were involved? What were the terms? Are there documentary records or independent witnesses who can corroborate his account?

“The Governor also needs to explain the implications of his claim that President Tinubu was approached and asked not to interfere in the legal proceedings challenging the 2023 Kano governorship election. The Supreme Court eventually determined that dispute and affirmed his election. Nigerians deserve clarity on what precisely was discussed, without creating an impression that the judicial process was subject to a political bargain.”

“We must also ask why an alleged understanding dating back to 2023 is being presented as the principal justification for a defection that took place in January 2026,” the statement added.

The post Kwankwaso denies sending Yusuf to negotiate APC return appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Political violence: Sowore rejects peace accord, questions peace committee’s relevance
description: The Presidential Candidate of the African Action Congress, Omoyele Sowore, has questioned the relevance of the Kukah Centre, led by the Catholic Bishop of Sokoto Diocese, Matthew Kukah, and the National Peace Committee over their “radio silence” on the recurring political violence that has marred ca
content:
The Presidential Candidate of the African Action Congress, Omoyele Sowore, has questioned the relevance of the Kukah Centre, led by the Catholic Bishop of Sokoto Diocese, Matthew Kukah, and the National Peace Committee over their “radio silence” on the recurring political violence that has marred campaigns ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Sowore announced his party’s withdrawal from the National Peace Accord signing, an agreement by politicians to avoid violence and ensure that their supporters do not undermine the electoral process.

The statement, titled ‘It is time to shut down Archbishop Matthew Hassan Kukah’s National Peace Committee,’ was issued by Sowore on Tuesday, a copy of which was obtained by PUNCH Online.

The AAC presidential candidate demanded the relevance of the peace accords, lamenting that political violence has claimed lives, while citizens are intimidated for exercising their democratic rights.

He also called for the National Peace Committee to be shut down.

“It is time to ask Bishop Matthew Hassan Kukah, founder of the Kukah Centre, and the leadership of the National Peace Committee to explain what purpose their so-called peace accords serve when political violence continues to claim lives, opposition candidates are attacked, and citizens are intimidated for exercising their democratic rights while the committee maintains radio silence.

“Nigeria cannot continue to celebrate ceremonial peace accords while political violence becomes an increasingly dangerous feature of our electoral process,” he stated.

The development comes amid growing concerns over political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections.

In an editorial published on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, The PUNCH urged the police to demonstrate their commitment to tackling electoral violence by arresting and prosecuting politicians threatening citizens with death, expulsion and suppression.

The newspaper also called on the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, to strengthen intelligence gathering to identify and prosecute politicians and their associates involved in vote-buying.

Sowore cited instances of political violence from the August 15, 2026 Osun State governorship election, the October 30 attack on his team in Ekiti State, and recently, the gunmen attack on the campaign organisation of former Deputy President of the Senate, Ovie Omo-Agege, during a campaign tour in Delta State.

Sowore lamented that over 70 lives were lost in the Osun election, which he tied to the “struggle” between the All Progressives Congress and the Accord Party in the state.

On the Ekiti attack, Sowore questioned the actionable steps taken by the peace committee, despite describing the attack as an “assassination attempt” and having identified individuals believed should be “investigated for their alleged roles in its planning and execution.”

In an August 2026 report, The PUNCH reported that an election observer organisation, Kimpact Development Initiative, said 17 election-related violence incidents were recorded across 10 Local Government Areas of Osun State during the August governorship election, with more than 44 victims recorded.

KDI stated that the incidents, which included gunshots, physical assaults, intimidation and harassment, were documented through its Election Day Data Room, established to coordinate and analyse reports from accredited observers deployed across the state.

“Consider what happened in Osun State during the last gubernatorial election. The struggle between the APC and ACCORD party over the gubernatorial election in the state descended into deadly violence. Over 70 people were confirmed killed, several others injured, and communities thrown into fear.

“These were not imaginary casualties. They were Nigerians whose lives were lost in a political confrontation.

“What practical intervention did the National Peace Committee make to prevent such violence, demand accountability, or ensure that those responsible faced justice?” Sowore queried.

On November 16, 2026, Sowore petitioned the Ekiti State Police Command, demanding the immediate arrest, interrogation, and prosecution of an alleged participant in the October 30 attack on him and members of his campaign team in Ado-Ekiti, the state capital.

The petition alleged that Sowore and his team were attacked shortly after he concluded a radio interview at MIDAS FM 90.5 by “a group of more than twenty armed men” who allegedly used “guns, machetes and bottles”.

On this, Sowore stated on Tuesday, “Then consider what happened to us in Ado-Ekiti on October 30, 2026. Armed attackers descended on members of our campaign team after a radio interview.

“We have publicly described the attack as an assassination attempt and identified individuals we believe should be investigated for their alleged roles in its planning and execution. Yet the central questions about accountability remain unanswered.

“Where was the National Peace Committee when our lives were endangered? Did anyone from the committee publicly demand an independent investigation?

“Did anyone insist that political candidates must be able to travel, campaign, speak, and organise without facing violence?” he asked further.

Meanwhile, in an updated report on Tuesday morning, The PUNCH reports that the Nigeria Police Force confirmed that six people were killed and several others were injured during violence at a political campaign event in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.

The police confirmation came a day after Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation alleged that gunmen attacked his entourage during a campaign tour, killing four people and critically injuring four others.

The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, disclosed the casualty figure in a statement released on Tuesday, saying preliminary police reports indicated that six people died in the violence.

Sowore stated further, “Now look at Delta State. On November 23, 2026, political violence erupted in the Uduere community of Ughelli North Local Government Area during a campaign visit by former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege. Four people were reportedly killed and others injured.

“Omo-Agege’s campaign described the incident as an assassination attempt, while local political actors have offered conflicting accounts of who initiated the violence.

“Whatever the outcome of an independent investigation, four human lives have reportedly been lost in circumstances connected to political activities. That alone should be sufficient to provoke national outrage and urgent action.

“Not a single statement from the “National Peace Committee” to shut down the cottage peace committee. As for the AAC, we will never participate any further in the charade known as the “Peace Accord” Signing.”

The post Political violence: Sowore rejects peace accord, questions peace committee’s relevance appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: Barau urges Kano clerics to back Tinubu
description:
The Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin, has urged more than 2,000 Islamic clerics in Kano State to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, citing the Federal Government’s development projects in the state and the North.
Barau made the appeal on Monday duri
content:
The Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin, has urged more than 2,000 Islamic clerics in Kano State to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, citing the Federal Government’s development projects in the state and the North.

Barau made the appeal on Monday during a meeting with Islamic clerics from the 13 local government areas of Kano North Senatorial District, where he urged them to support Tinubu and other All Progressives Congress candidates.

In a statement issued on Monday by his Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Ismail Mudashir, the senator said the President was committed to the development of Kano, the North-West and the country.

He acknowledged the contributions of religious leaders to peace and stability in the state, urging them to sustain their prayers and support for political leaders.

“This is a gathering of our fathers, our leaders, our sheikhs and our imams. You are our leaders. I warmly welcome you all to this gathering and sincerely appreciate your prayers and support,” Barau said.

Highlighting some of the Federal Government’s interventions in Kano, the Deputy President of the Senate said he had personally approached Tinubu to seek the conversion of the Federal Polytechnic, Kabo, into a university, which was subsequently approved.

He also cited the approval for the conversion of the Federal College of Education, Kano, into a university, as well as the establishment of a Police Training School, Civil Defence Training School and Immigration Training School in the state.

Barau said the establishment of the North-West Development Commission was another intervention by the Tinubu administration to address the developmental challenges facing the region.

He also said that, following Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf’s return to the APC, projects worth about N2tn had been attracted to Kano State.

On the economic challenges facing Nigerians, Barau acknowledged the hardship but argued that the situation had a global dimension.

“The economic hardship that some people are using to campaign against us is not peculiar to Nigeria. It has a global dimension,” he said.

The senator urged the clerics to pray for Tinubu, the APC, political leaders and the country, saying their supplications should extend beyond individual officeholders.

As part of the meeting, Barau announced a motorcycle empowerment programme for Islamic clerics across the 13 local government areas of Kano North.

He said 15 motorcycles would be distributed in each local government area in the first phase, bringing the initial allocation to 195, while another 195 would be distributed after three months.

He added that the programme would continue in subsequent phases until all targeted beneficiaries were covered.

“In addition, each of you will receive N50,000. We recognise your contributions to society, and we have a responsibility to support you,” he said.

Barau also commended Governor Yusuf for his development projects and interventions across the state.

In his remarks, the Chairman of the Kano North APC Campaign Council and Managing Director of the Hadejia-Jama’are River Basin Development Authority, Engineer Rabiu Sulaiman Bichi, said the meeting was organised to appreciate the clerics for their contributions to society and their role in promoting peace.

Bichi cited the ongoing railway projects linking Kano to Lagos and Kano to Maradi, as well as road infrastructure and other initiatives, as evidence of the Federal Government’s development efforts in the state.

The Chairman of the Kano North Council of Imams and Chief Imam of Bichi Local Government Area, Malam Lawal Imam, commended Barau for his interventions, including the construction of mosques.

“We will continue to pray for him, the APC and the entire country. The clerics have a wide network of influence. Each of us has family members, students, pupils and followers who look up to us. Our collective reach within the communities is significant,” he said.

Also speaking, the Kano State Commissioner for Information, Sunusi Bature Dawakin Tofa, said he had never witnessed such a gathering of religious leaders at a political meeting.

He commended Barau for bringing the clerics together and praised the governor’s efforts to promote unity among religious leaders in the state.

The post 2027: Barau urges Kano clerics to back Tinubu appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Canada PM brings Trump impersonator on stage during press gala
description:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney invited a Donald Trump impersonator on stage during a weekend press gala, a move one critic said risks provoking a president known to bristle at being mocked.



Carney was making a lighthearted speech at the Canadian equivalent of the White House Correspondents’
content:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney invited a Donald Trump impersonator on stage during a weekend press gala, a move one critic said risks provoking a president known to bristle at being mocked.

Carney was making a lighthearted speech at the Canadian equivalent of the White House Correspondents’ Dinner when he announced he was pressing an “emergency comedy button.”

Comedian Mark McKinney, who impersonates Carney, came out first, followed by Trump impersonator Mark Critch, who appears on the long-running Canadian sketch comedy show “This Hour Has 22 Minutes.”

“We’ve got two Carneys here, it’s a disaster,” Critch joked as Trump, before taking shots at Washington’s controversial ambassador to Canada and the White House press secretary vacancy, after Katie Zacharia left the role in just five days.

With the United States and Canada still locked in a trade war, Critch offered some comic assurances about an impending pact.

“Mark, we’re gonna have an incredible deal,” he said, mimicking Trump. “There’s only one thing standing in the way — me, because I’m crazy.”

The bit appeared to go down well with reporters in Ottawa, but one of Carney’s political rivals was unimpressed.

“I think provoking President Trump is arrogant, stupid and not funny,” said Yves-Francois Blanchet, the leader of the separatist Bloc Quebecois.

He noted that Trump’s tariffs, including those affecting an aluminum industry central to Quebec’s economy, are causing real economic pain.

“Quebec is paying the highest price for these tariffs…which should not be inflamed with bad jokes,” Blanchet said.

Trump and Carney have both offered optimism that trade talks are progressing, but there were similarly positive comments in the days before negotiations collapsed in August.

Canada wants relief from tariffs on key sectors, notably autos, but Ottawa has warned that completely removing the levies is unlikely and the Canadian economy needs to adjust to a permanently altered trading relationship with the United States.

title: Six killed, several injured in Delta political campaign clash – Police
description:
The Nigeria Police Force has confirmed that six people died and several others sustained injuries during a violent incident at a political campaign event in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.



The Force also said the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, ha
content:
The Nigeria Police Force has confirmed that six people died and several others sustained injuries during a violent incident at a political campaign event in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.

The Force also said the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, had ordered a comprehensive investigation into the incident, including the actions of police officers deployed to the venue.

CSP Ani Iniedu, the Force Public Relations Officer, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, adding that preliminary police findings indicated that six people were killed.

“Preliminary Police reports indicate that six persons lost their lives, while several others sustained injuries.

“The Force is aware of varying casualty figures circulating in the public domain. An ongoing investigation will establish the verified number of casualties and determine the circumstances surrounding the incident,” the statement read.

Iniedu said the IGP had instructed the Delta State Commissioner of Police to conduct a thorough, impartial and evidence-based investigation.

He added that the probe would examine the sequence of events, establish the identities of those involved and determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting, including the actions and deployment of police personnel at the scene.

The Force also confirmed that the Delta State Government had imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area, running from 6pm to 6am daily until further notice.

“In response to the security situation, the Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area, from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. daily, until further notice. The Delta State Police Command is enforcing the directive and has intensified security measures to prevent further breakdown of law and order,” the statement read.

The police urged residents, community leaders, political stakeholders and campaign groups to remain peaceful, obey the curfew and refrain from circulating unverified reports that could worsen tensions.

It also called on anyone with useful information, photographs, video footage or other evidence to assist the investigation by submitting them through established police channels, assuring that the identity of informants would be protected.

The police confirmation followed an earlier allegation by the campaign organisation of former Deputy President of the Senate, Ovie Omo-Agege, that gunmen attacked his entourage during a campaign tour of the area.

The organisation had put the death toll at four, including two of its aides, identified as Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro, while claiming that four other people sustained critical injuries.

title: What to know about Efemena Umukoro, Urhobo youth leader killed in Delta attack
description: Urhobo youth leader, Efemena Umukoro, popularly known as General Akima, was among four people reportedly killed when gunmen attacked the campaign team of former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, on Monday, November 23, 2
content:
Urhobo youth leader, Efemena Umukoro, popularly known as General Akima, was among four people reportedly killed when gunmen attacked the campaign team of former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, on Monday, November 23, 2026.

Omo-Agege, the Nigeria Democratic Congress candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 elections, reportedly escaped unhurt.

The late Umukoro’s death has drawn attention to his public profile as a youth leader and activist, as well as to a September interview in which he spoke about surviving an earlier attack.

Here are some things to know about him.

1. He was an Urhobo youth leader

Umukoro was a prominent figure in the Urhobo youth community and served as President of the Urhobo Progress Union Youth Wing Worldwide.

He emerged as president in January 2020, having previously served as the youth body’s Secretary-General and Publicity Secretary.

His emergence was celebrated by members of the Orogun community, where he hailed from, during a reception organised in his honour in February 2020.

2. He was a human rights activist

Umukoro was also known for his involvement in youth advocacy, community affairs and human rights activities.

In 2020, the National Association of Nigerian Students Joint Campus Committee, Delta Axis, honoured him with its Icon of Hope and Inspiration Award in recognition of his advocacy for the welfare of young people, particularly students.

He also received a Pragmatic Leadership Award from Citizens Focus News in December 2022 for his advocacy for good governance and the protection of young people’s rights.

In May 2024, he called for a crackdown on armed youth groups in parts of Delta State, warning that criminal activities by youths could bring traditional institutions into disrepute.

He also cautioned against the establishment of unauthorised community security groups, saying youth leaders should not recruit people into security outfits that were not backed by law.

3. He was involved in community policing

Umukoro was also associated with community security initiatives in Delta State.

He was reportedly appointed to the Delta State Community Policing Committee as a representative of the National Youth Council of Nigeria.

His public activities included speaking on insecurity, youth welfare, and disputes affecting communities in the Niger Delta.

4. He went viral for saying knives could not penetrate him

A video of Umukoro speaking during an interview with News Central TV in September 2026 resurfaced after news of his death.

In the viral interview, he recounted an earlier attack on members of the NDC during a political mobilisation exercise in Delta State.

He said some attackers had blocked their road and that he was struck from behind with a weapon during the incident.

Speaking confidently about surviving the attack, he said: “I be youth leader na, how knife go enter me? I am an Orogun man. Knives cannot get into me. It is as simple as that.”

The clip, dated September 24, circulated widely on social media following reports of his death by gunfire.

5. He was involved in the NDC’s political activities

Umukoro was associated with the Nigeria Democratic Congress and was among the supporters involved in Omo-Agege’s political activities ahead of the 2027 elections.

He was identified as one of the aides of the former deputy Senate president in the statement issued by Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation following Monday’s attack.

6. He was killed during an attack on Omo-Agege’s campaign team

Umukoro was among four people reportedly killed when gunmen opened fire on Omo-Agege and members of his entourage during a campaign visit to Uduere community in Ughelli North Local Government Area on November 23.

In a statement issued by his media adviser, Sunny Areh, the campaign organisation identified Umukoro and Moses Anaughe as two of those killed.

It also said four other people sustained critical gunshot injuries during the incident.

The organisation described the attack as an assassination attempt on Omo-Agege, alleging that the attackers opened fire at close range while he was addressing supporters.

The Delta State Police Command said it had deployed operatives to the area, while the state government imposed a curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area following the incident.

7. He became a father in May 2026

Umukoro also shared a personal milestone earlier in the year when he became a father for the first time.

Reports said he announced the birth of his son on May 15, 2026, about six months before his death.

The post What to know about Efemena Umukoro, Urhobo youth leader killed in Delta attack appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: ‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍⁠⁠​​‌⁠‌INEC to conduct mock accreditation in 490 Lagos polling units
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it will conduct a mock accreditation and result upload exercise in 490 polling units across Lagos State on Saturday.



Prof. Ayobami Salami, the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Lagos State, disclosed this in an interview with the Ne
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) says it will conduct a mock accreditation and result upload exercise in 490 polling units across Lagos State on Saturday.

Prof. Ayobami Salami, the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Lagos State, disclosed this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Tuesday in Lagos.

Salami said the exercise would take place between 8:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m. in selected polling units across the state.

He said it was designed to assess the performance of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and identify possible gaps or challenges that would be addressed before the 2027 general elections.

According to him, the exercise will cover the 245 Registration Areas (RAs) across the state’s 20 Local Government Areas (LGAs), with two polling units selected in each Registration Area.

He urged residents, particularly eligible voters in the selected polling units, to participate in the exercise to enable the commission to assess the effectiveness of its equipment and electoral processes.

The REC said the list of selected polling units would be displayed at the respective local government area offices to enable residents to identify the designated locations.

Salami said he had directed all electoral officers in the state to convene stakeholder meetings in their respective LGAs ahead of the exercise.

He said the meetings would provide an opportunity to engage political parties and other stakeholders on the importance of participating in the mock accreditation exercise.

The REC said the engagements would also help mobilise eligible voters in the selected polling units to participate in the exercise.

He outlined the activities preceding the exercise, saying BVAS configuration would take place on Nov. 25, followed by the training of nominated personnel on Nov. 26.

According to him, personnel and devices would be deployed to the selected polling units on Friday, ahead of the exercise.

Salami reiterated that the exercise formed part of INEC’s preparations to ensure a smooth and efficient electoral process during the 2027 general elections. (NAN)

title: ITUC-Africa demands justice for survivors of gender violence
description:
By Victor Ahiuma-Young



The African Regional Organisation of the International Trade Union Confederation (ITUC-Africa) has called on African governments and employers to intensify efforts to end violence against women and girls, ensure justice for survivors and hold perpetrators accountable.
content:
By Victor Ahiuma-Young

The African Regional Organisation of the International Trade Union Confederation (ITUC-Africa) has called on African governments and employers to intensify efforts to end violence against women and girls, ensure justice for survivors and hold perpetrators accountable.

The organisation, in a statement ahead of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women on November 25, 2026, described gender-based violence as a serious human rights violation that undermines equality, decent work, democracy and sustainable development.

ITUC-Africa General Secretary, Akhator Joel Odigie, called for an end to the culture of silence, weak law enforcement and impunity that allows perpetrators to escape accountability.

The organisation said violence against women and girls occurred in homes, public spaces, online platforms and workplaces, including factories, farms, markets, offices, schools, hospitals and during work-related travels.

It noted that women in the informal economy, migrant and domestic workers, young women and women with disabilities faced heightened risks and often had limited access to justice.

According to the statement, survivors frequently encounter stigma, delays, retaliation and even job losses when they report cases of violence.

“Silence, weak enforcement and power imbalances can protect perpetrators. Without accountability, violence is normalised,” it said.

The organisation also highlighted the importance of the International Labour Organisation’s Violence and Harassment Convention, 2019 (No. 190), and Recommendation No. 206, which establish protections against violence and harassment, including gender-based violence, in the world of work.

It said the instruments covered workers regardless of their contractual status, including those in the informal economy, and addressed violence in workplaces, work-related travel, communications, employer-provided accommodation and digital spaces.

The convention and recommendation also recognise the impact of domestic violence on workers and their employment, it added.

ITUC-Africa urged African governments to ratify and fully implement Convention 190 and Recommendation 206, align national laws with their provisions and establish effective complaint and redress mechanisms.

It also called for protection against retaliation, improved access to justice and adequate funding for labour inspectorates and courts.

Employers, it said, should develop and enforce workplace policies against violence and harassment in consultation with trade unions.

The organisation pledged to continue supporting campaigns by its affiliates for the ratification and implementation of Convention 190, while strengthening the capacity of women and young trade unionists and amplifying the voices of survivors.

It said the commitment would build on the outcomes of its Biennial Women’s Conference held in Lomé earlier in 2026, with emphasis on women’s leadership and participation in trade union activities.

As part of the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence, scheduled for November 25 to December 10, ITUC-Africa urged its affiliates, partners and allies to organise campaigns, mobilise communities and speak out against violence.

“Violence against women and girls can be prevented, and it must end,” the organisation declared.

The post ITUC-Africa demands justice for survivors of gender violence appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Nvidia shares soar 30% as Jensen Huang returns as CEO
description:
Shares in American chipmaker Nvidia rose by more than 30 per cent after its board reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as chief executive, following pressure from US President Donald Trump.
CNN reported on Tuesday that the company’s shares recorded their third-best day on record on Monday after the bo
content:
Shares in American chipmaker Nvidia rose by more than 30 per cent after its board reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as chief executive, following pressure from US President Donald Trump.

CNN reported on Tuesday that the company’s shares recorded their third-best day on record on Monday after the board announced Huang’s immediate return as chief executive and president.

The decision reversed the board’s earlier position that it did not intend to reinstate Huang, who stepped down on November 12 following revelations about his relationships with two women, including one suspected by US officials of having links to Chinese intelligence.

Trump said he had spoken directly to Nvidia’s board about bringing Huang back, arguing that the technology executive had done nothing wrong.

The president also defended his intervention, saying the United States risked losing Huang’s expertise to China amid competition between the two countries in artificial intelligence development.

“The bigger threat would be losing the brain power of somebody like Jensen. That would be a threat — to me that would be a far bigger threat,” Trump told CNBC.

Trump’s financial portfolio has also had millions of dollars invested in Nvidia shares, although the White House has consistently denied that he influences investment decisions in his accounts.

Nvidia’s board said it received input from senior US government officials before reaching its decision and was confident that Huang’s reinstatement posed no national security risk.

However, the move has drawn criticism from lawmakers across party lines, with some questioning the board’s decision and the potential security implications.

The Republican chairmen of the House Intelligence and Foreign Affairs committees and the China select committee said the company’s “brief internal investigation” and Huang’s reinstatement did not remove the national security concerns surrounding the case.

Other Republican lawmakers also criticised the decision, while Democratic members of Congress raised questions about who in the government advised Nvidia’s board.

Huang is expected to testify before the House and Senate next month.

The controversy followed reports that Huang had an affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman whose possible links to Chinese intelligence had raised concerns among US officials. Beijing has rejected the allegation, describing it as an attempt to smear China.

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia more than three decades ago, acknowledged making serious mistakes in his personal life before stepping down. The company’s board initially ruled out bringing him back, but later reversed its position following pressure from Trump and senior administration officials.

The post Nvidia shares soar 30% as Jensen Huang returns as CEO appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Tinubu has earned Ndigbo’s support, says Kalu
description:
The Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, has called on voters in Abia State to re-elect President Bola Tinubu in the January 16, 2027, presidential election, declaring that the President has earned the support of Ndigbo through key appointments and developmental projects.
K
content:
The Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, has called on voters in Abia State to re-elect President Bola Tinubu in the January 16, 2027, presidential election, declaring that the President has earned the support of Ndigbo through key appointments and developmental projects.

Kalu made the call on Monday during the inauguration of the Abia State chapter of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, which featured the donation of 25 campaign vehicles and mobilisation materials by the Grand Patron of the movement, Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo.

According to a statement issued by the PBAT Door-to-Door Media Unit and sent to PUNCH Online on Monday, the Deputy Speaker noted that President Tinubu had fulfilled the long-held aspiration of the South-East geopolitical zone by establishing the South-East Development Commission to spearhead regional development.

He also cited strategic Federal appointments granted to indigenes of the zone, including ministerial positions, heads of Federal agencies, the former Chief of Naval Staff, Vice Admiral Emmanuel Ogalla (retd.), and the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Aneke, as compelling reasons for Ndigbo to back Tinubu’s second-term bid.

“The President Tompolo wants us to support and gave us Minister of Works, and today roads are coming up. (Senator Dave) Umahi is making us proud with the kind of job he’s doing. This president is the president that gave us the Minister of Foreign Affairs. The wife of the late (Dim Chukwuemeka) Ojukwu is in charge of Foreign Affairs. She is our image-maker around the world,” Kalu said.

“We are talking about a game changer. This game changer was the one who gave us the former Chief of Naval Staff to monitor all the waterways where our oil and gas pass. He gave it to us. This same president gave us the person in charge of the Air Force, the Chief of the Air Force. That is the same president we are talking about. The president gave us Minister of State Finance, who is now Minister of State Budget and Economic Planning,” he added.

Kalu rejected proposals for a single-term Igbo presidency and urged members of the All Progressives Congress and supporters of the administration to counter narratives claiming that the South-East had been sidelined.

“When people ask you, what has he done for us, this is the list I’m giving to you. And the man standing here is his own son, Benjamin Okezie Kalu. This man is the same president. Before he became president, he supported me to remain in the House of Representatives. When he became president, he supported me to be the Deputy Speaker. Today, your brother is the Deputy Speaker,” he stated.

The Deputy Speaker commended Tompolo for taking the campaign for Tinubu’s re-election across the country, describing the Niger Delta leader’s mobilisation strategy as impactful.

Earlier in his remarks, Tompolo’s representative and Managing Director of Tantita Security Services Limited, Kestin Pondi, announced the donation of the 25 campaign vehicles to mobilise voters for Tinubu’s second term and all APC candidates in the state.

Pondi urged the people of Abia State to vote for the APC at all levels, noting that the state stood to gain greater federal benefits by aligning with the ruling party at the centre.

“The PBAT Door-to-Door Movement has visited 31 states. And in every one of these states, we have done one thing. We inaugurated the state chapter of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement and also give them the resources to carry out our mission, which is to carry the message of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to everybody from door to door. Because in an election, the most important doors are the doors of the voters, and we acknowledge that.

“Today, we are in your state to inaugurate the Abia State Chapter of the Movement and also provide, like we have done in other states, 25 campaign vehicles that are mounted with speakers, amplifiers, and generators, microphones to carry our messages to every nook and cranny of Abia State,” Pondi said.

In his welcome address, the National Coordinator of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Sunday Asuku, described Tinubu as a courageous leader whose far-reaching economic reforms had increased Federal allocations to state governments for the payment of salaries and pensions and the execution of infrastructure projects.

Asuku maintained that the policies implemented during the administration’s first term had placed the economy on a recovery path, urging members of the movement to vigorously engage voters across cities and villages in the state.

The post Tinubu has earned Ndigbo’s support, says Kalu appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Three suspects nabbed for armed robbery, kidnapping in Kano
description:
The Kano State Police Command has arrested three suspects, Nafi’u Lawal alias Gamji, Auwalu Shafi’u alias Bakin Tuwo, and Yunusa Sale, alias Bammi, in connection with cases of house trespass, armed robbery, kidnapping and criminal intimidation in Rogo Local Government Area of the state.
Police Publi
content:
The Kano State Police Command has arrested three suspects, Nafi’u Lawal alias Gamji, Auwalu Shafi’u alias Bakin Tuwo, and Yunusa Sale, alias Bammi, in connection with cases of house trespass, armed robbery, kidnapping and criminal intimidation in Rogo Local Government Area of the state.

Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO) of the command, CSP Abdullahi Kiyawa disclosed this in a Monday statement.

Kiyawa said the arrest followed a report received at about 2:00 p.m on November 3, from a resident of Aleko Village, Rogo LGA, that unknown armed men stormed and unlawfully entered his dwelling house armed with sophisticated weapons.

The suspects allegedly attacked members of the household, assaulted a female in the house, and robbed the complainant of a red Boxer motorcycle valued at N1.15 million and twenty-five bags of dry pepper valued at N850,000.

The complainant further stated that he recognised one of the suspects as Nafi’u Lawal, alias Gamji.

The police spokesman said that upon receipt of the report, the Commissioner of Police, Kano State Police Command, CP Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, directed a team of operatives attached to the Anti-Kidnapping Squad to ensure the arrest of the culprits.

Kiyawa said sustained intelligence-led follow-up coupled with coordinated operations led to the arrest of the recognised suspect and two others, identified as Nafi’u Lawal, alias Gamji, aged 21 years, of Aleko Village, Rogo LGA; Auwalu Shafi’u, alias Bakin Tuwo, aged 26 years, of the same address, who was traced and arrested at Doguwa LGA; and Yunusa Sale, alias Bammi, aged 26 years, of Jajaye Village, Rogo LGA.

According to Kiyawa, the suspects confessed to the crime during interrogation, and further confessed to their involvement in other cases of kidnapping involving two victims, Ibrahim Iro, alias Dangi, of Aleko Village, and Shadari, alias Ardo.

The suspects further disclosed that the victims were abducted and taken to an unknown destination until the sums of N900,000 and N1 million respectively were paid as ransom for their release.

The command spokesman said investigation is ongoing with a view to trace and arrest the remaining members of the syndicate and recover the stolen items.

He added that the case would be charged to court upon completion of investigation.

The Kano CP commended the operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Squad for their swift response, professionalism and dedication to duty which led to the arrest.

The command reiterated its commitment to the protection of lives and property, and the fight against kidnapping, armed robbery and all forms of crime in the state.

The command also called on members of the public to continue to support the police with timely and credible information, and to report any suspicious persons or movements to the nearest police station or through the command’s emergency lines.

The post Three suspects nabbed for armed robbery, kidnapping in Kano appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Woman attacks police inspector, tears uniform during arrest
description:
By Steve Oko



A woman, identified as Ettoh Barkerk, has been arrested by the Abia State Police Command for allegedly assaulting a police inspector and tearing his uniform during a confrontation in Aba.



The suspect was also accused of attacking worshippers with fireworks at Christ the King Churc
content:
By Steve Oko

A woman, identified as Ettoh Barkerk, has been arrested by the Abia State Police Command for allegedly assaulting a police inspector and tearing his uniform during a confrontation in Aba.

The suspect was also accused of attacking worshippers with fireworks at Christ the King Church (CKC), Aba, triggering panic within the church premises.

The police said Barkerk was arrested on Sunday, November 22, after a distress call alerted the Ndiegoro Divisional Police Headquarters to an attack on church members by hoodlums throwing explosive fireworks indiscriminately.

According to the Command, a patrol team deployed to the scene to restore order apprehended the suspect with fireworks in her possession.

However, she allegedly turned violent, assaulted an inspector attached to the patrol team, tore his uniform and attempted to forcefully retrieve the recovered exhibits.

The police said she was subsequently subdued and arrested, while the fireworks and other relevant exhibits were secured for investigation.

The Command’s spokesperson, DSP Maureen Chinaka, disclosed this in a statement Monday, condemning the assault as reprehensible and warning against attacks on officers performing lawful duties.

She said the suspect would be charged in court after investigation.

Chinaka added that normalcy had been restored at the church and its environs, while police monitoring continued to prevent further breakdown of law and order.

The Command warned that it would not tolerate assault, obstruction or interference with police officers in the discharge of their duties, urging residents to maintain peace and respect lawful authority.
