title: Tourist shares death threats, abusive messages, reveals $50,000 offer to take down video of Daura Emir
description:
A foreign tourist who accused the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Faruk Umar Faruk, of inappropriate sexual conduct has released screenshots of threatening and abusive messages she allegedly received following the circulation of a video of their encounter.
The tourist, who identifies herself on Instagram as @
content:
A foreign tourist who accused the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Faruk Umar Faruk, of inappropriate sexual conduct has released screenshots of threatening and abusive messages she allegedly received following the circulation of a video of their encounter.

The tourist, who identifies herself on Instagram as @beduinqa, also disclosed that an individual offered her $50,000 to delete the video, which has generated widespread controversy on social media.

In screenshots shared online, several individuals reportedly accused her of disrespecting the traditional institution, embarrassing the Hausa community and deliberately damaging the Emir’s reputation.

One of the messages contained an offer of $50,000 in exchange for removing the footage.

“I will give you 50k$ if you can remove the video of emir of daura please,” the sender reportedly wrote.

Other messages contained insults and threats, with some individuals warning the tourist against returning to Africa.

One sender allegedly threatened her, saying she would regret her decision if she failed to remove the video.

Another message accused her of encouraging the Emir’s alleged advances during their meeting before subsequently taking the matter to social media.

Some of the reactions also blamed her for publishing the footage, claiming it had damaged the reputation of the Hausa community, its culture and traditions.

The controversy followed a video shared by the tourist after her visit to the Emir’s palace in Daura, Katsina State, on November 14, 2026.

In her account, she alleged that the traditional ruler held her hand, hugged her, kissed her on the cheek and touched her breast without her consent.

She claimed she repeatedly asked him to stop, but he laughed at her objections.

The tourist said she recorded the encounter using Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses and decided to publish the footage after leaving Nigeria.

The development has attracted further reactions, with Amnesty International Nigeria condemning the threats and calling on the Nigeria Police Force to protect the tourist and conduct an impartial investigation into her allegation.

The human rights organisation said the woman had received hundreds of death threats and warned that intimidation and victim-blaming could discourage survivors of sexual violence from speaking out.

Amnesty also urged the Katsina State Government to ensure that the matter was properly investigated.

Meanwhile, the Daura Emirate Council had earlier confirmed that it was reviewing the viral footage to establish its authenticity and determine whether it had been manipulated.

The allegations against the Emir remain unproven, and no official findings have been announced. The reported threats and financial offer are based on screenshots shared by the tourist.

description:
The Nigeria Police Force has confirmed that six people were killed and several others injured during violence at a political campaign event in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.
The police confirmation came a day after the campaign organisation of former Deputy Pre
content:
The Nigeria Police Force has confirmed that six people were killed and several others injured during violence at a political campaign event in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.

The police confirmation came a day after the campaign organisation of former Deputy President of the Senate, Ovie Omo-Agege, alleged that gunmen attacked his entourage during a campaign tour, killing four people and critically injuring four others.

The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, disclosed the casualty figure in a statement released on Tuesday, saying preliminary police reports indicated that six people died in the violence.

“Preliminary Police reports indicate that six persons lost their lives, while several others sustained injuries.

“The Force is aware of varying casualty figures circulating in the public domain. An ongoing investigation will establish the verified number of casualties and determine the circumstances surrounding the incident,” the statement added.

The FPRO stated that the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, had directed the Delta State Commissioner of Police to commence a “thorough, impartial and evidence-based investigation” into the incident.

According to him, the investigation would establish the sequence of events, identify those responsible and examine the circumstances surrounding the shooting, including the deployment and conduct of police personnel at the venue.

He added that any officer found to have acted negligently, unlawfully or in breach of professional standards would face disciplinary action, while those found culpable of criminal offences would be prosecuted.

The Force also confirmed that the Delta State Government had imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North, from 6 pm to 6 am daily, until further notice.

“The Delta State Police Command is enforcing the directive and has intensified security measures to prevent further breakdown of law and order,” Iniedu stated.

He noted that the IGP had also ordered enhanced security deployment, intelligence-led operations, sustained patrols and rapid-response measures to protect lives and property and restore normalcy to the affected communities.

The FPRO urged residents, community leaders, political actors and campaign organisations to remain calm, comply with the curfew and avoid spreading unverified information capable of escalating tensions.

The statement further urged anyone with credible information, photographs, video recordings or other evidence that could assist the investigation to report through established police channels.

Iniedu added that measures would be taken to protect the confidentiality of information provided.

Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation had earlier alleged that four people, including two of its aides, Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro, were killed in the attack.

The campaign organisation also named four others as critically injured and accused the Delta State Police Command of failing to prevent the violence despite the presence of its officers at the venue.

The organisation had called on the Inspector-General of Police to take over the investigation, saying it had lost confidence in the state command.

However, the police statement said the investigation would also examine the conduct of officers deployed to the campaign venue.

The incident comes ahead of the 2027 general elections, amid concerns over violence during political activities.

The post Delta campaign attack: Police confirm six dead, several injured appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Morning Recap: 157 Nigerians face US deportation, police bust Ogun ‘Yahoo academy’, other top stories
description:
In Ogun State, police arrested 11 suspected internet fraudsters during a raid on an alleged internet fraud training centre, popularly called a “Yahoo academy”, where suspected human remains and other items were recovered.
Meanwhile, a Lagos State High Court has ordered Pastor Jimmy Odukoya to appear
content:
In Ogun State, police arrested 11 suspected internet fraudsters during a raid on an alleged internet fraud training centre, popularly called a “Yahoo academy”, where suspected human remains and other items were recovered.

Meanwhile, a Lagos State High Court has ordered Pastor Jimmy Odukoya to appear on November 26 in connection with the leadership dispute at the Fountain of Life Church.

Ahead of the 2027 general elections, opposition parties have accused authorities in several states of restricting access to campaign venues, while political leaders and other dignitaries attended the traditional wedding of the daughter of the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, in Lagos.

Here are five top stories this morning:

1. US adds 24 Nigerians to deportation list, total now 157

The United States Department of Homeland Security has added 24 Nigerians to its list of foreign nationals facing removal from the country, bringing the total number to 157. The individuals were listed over alleged offences including fraud, money laundering, drug-related crimes, identity theft and child cruelty, although the department did not disclose when they would be deported or their immigration status. Being named on the list does not, on its own, establish that they have been convicted of the offences.

Read Here: https://punchng.com/us-names-157-nigerians-for-deportation/

2. Police bust Ogun ‘Yahoo academy’, uncover suspected human remains

The Police Special Fraud Unit has arrested 11 suspected internet fraudsters during a raid on an alleged fraud training centre in Abeokuta, Ogun State. Police said they recovered suspected human remains, charms, blood-stained fetish items, 11 iPhones, three Samsung phones and eight laptops, while the alleged leader of the operation, Goriola Oluwaseun Olanrewaju, also known as Update, remains at large.

Read Here: https://punchng.com/police-bust-ogun-yahoo-academy-uncover-human-remains/

3. Court orders Jimmy Odukoya to appear November 26 over church dispute

The Lagos State High Court has ordered Pastor Jimmy Odukoya to appear before it on November 26 to show cause in the ongoing leadership dispute at the Fountain of Life Church. The order followed an application by the church’s trustees to serve him with court processes through substituted means, including newspaper publication and electronic channels, after an earlier ruling restrained him from presenting himself as the church’s senior pastor and spiritual head.

Read Here: https://punchng.com/court-orders-jimmy-odukoya-to-appear-november-26-over-church-dispute/

4. Campaign venue disputes deepen APC-opposition tensions ahead of 2027

The African Democratic Congress and the Nigeria Democratic Congress have accused authorities in Kaduna, Kano, Jigawa, Sokoto, Gombe and Ekiti states of restricting their access to public campaign venues and advertising spaces ahead of the 2027 elections. The APC and some state governments have denied the allegations, while former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has also accused the Federal Government of intimidating ADC members following reported arrests in Kaduna.

Read Here: https://punchng.com/2027-campaign-venue-rows-fuel-apc-opposition-tensions/

5. Dele Alake’s daughter weds in Lagos

Wuraola Alake, daughter of the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, has married her partner, Wasem Yaji, at a traditional wedding ceremony in Lagos. The Sunday event at the Eko Convention Centre attracted several dignitaries, including Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun and the President’s Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila.

Read Here: https://punchng.com/photos-dele-alakes-daughter-weds-in-lagos/

title: YouTube star Ms Rachel protests US child immigration hearings
description:
Ms Rachel, the American creator of hit sing-songy educational videos for toddlers, attacked the use of immigration hearings for children following a courthouse visit on Monday.



“I’ve seen children who are just missing the light in their eyes and they’re begging to go to the spelling bee or to jus
content:
Ms Rachel, the American creator of hit sing-songy educational videos for toddlers, attacked the use of immigration hearings for children following a courthouse visit on Monday.

“I’ve seen children who are just missing the light in their eyes and they’re begging to go to the spelling bee or to just, you know, be with their younger siblings,” said Ms Rachel, who is known offline as Rachel Accurso.

“They’re just so scared and praying to God, that they, please change the hearts of ICE (Immigration and Customs Enforcement) and let us out,” added the 43-year-old after observing legal procedures of juveniles being processed through the immigration courts.

Her appearance at the New York youth immigration court was part of an effort to shine light on the Trump administration’s immigration policy that was supported by newly elected US lawmaker Brad Lander.

Lander criticized a “travesty of justice” as cases are sped up while funding for legal representation is cut.

In videos uploaded to her 22 million subscribers on YouTube, Ms Rachel, known for her signature pink headband and denim overalls, teaches infants to identify animals, colors, and numbers.

On her other social media platforms, she is taking an increasingly vocal stand for children’s rights.

She has notably led a fundraiser for the organization Save the Children in support of Palestinian children in Gaza and has backed campaigns critical of US migrant detention centers where children are kept, decrying poor conditions and calling for their closure.

Targeted by a smear campaign for her pro-Gaza stance, Ms Rachel said previously that it would be more controversial to say nothing.

“I think it’s sad to take someone’s dedication and love for all children and try and make that wrong,” she told PBS last year.

The post YouTube star Ms Rachel protests US child immigration hearings appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Paris Club Refunds: Court freezes N135.5bn linked to Governors’ Forum
description:

By Taiye Agbaje



An Abuja High Court has ordered an interim freeze on N135.5 billion paid to the Nigerian Governors’ Forum (NGF) as a stakeholder in the Paris Club refunds dispute.



Justice O. C. Agbaza granted the interim Mareva injunction following an ex-parte applicatio
content:
…restrains 29 banks

By Taiye Agbaje

An Abuja High Court has ordered an interim freeze on N135.5 billion paid to the Nigerian Governors’ Forum (NGF) as a stakeholder in the Paris Club refunds dispute.

Justice O. C. Agbaza granted the interim Mareva injunction following an ex-parte application brought by Dr Ted Iseghohi-Edwards.

The order restrained the Incorporated Trustees of the NGF from withdrawing, transferring, dissipating or otherwise dealing with the funds.

The order also restrained 29 commercial banks from releasing, transferring, converting or otherwise dealing with funds belonging to the NGF within their custody.

The judge further directed the banks to disclose, within 48 hours of service, whether the NGF maintains accounts containing the disputed funds.

The banks are required to identify such accounts, their currencies, available balances and amounts preserved under the court’s order.

The amount represents 100 million dollars, equivalent to the N135.55 billion, calculated at the exchange rate of N1,355.80 to the dollar.

Justice Agbaza made the orders on Nov. 19, following the ex parte application and submissions by the claimant’s counsel, Emonye Adekwu, SAN, alongside Damilola Odesola, from Ade Okeaya-Inneh & Co. Law Firm.

A certified true copy of the enrolled order by the court was obtained by the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Tuesday in Abuja.

Iseghohi-Edwards, who carries on business as Edwards and Partners Law Firm, is seeking recovery of the money pursuant to an indemnity issued by the NGF.

The claimant’s case is that the money belongs to him under an indemnity dated Dec. 20, 2018, issued by the NGF.

The indemnity reportedly arose from an arrangement under which the Federal Government paid 100 million dollars to the NGF as a stakeholder.

The money was to be held pending the determination of the Federal Government’s liability to Iseghohi-Edwards over legal and consultancy fees.

The fees arose from services allegedly rendered in connection with the London and Paris Club loan transaction.

Iseghohi-Edwards claimed he was retained by the Incorporated Trustees of the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria (ALGON) to represent the 774 local government councils in the London and Paris Clubs’ refund matters.

He had instituted Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/856/2016 against the Federal Government over the outstanding professional fees.

According to his court filings, the Federal High Court, on Feb. 16, 2018, delivered judgment establishing the government’s indebtedness of 318 million dollars.

The claimant said the government subsequently made a part-payment of 159 million dollars through promissory notes.

He contended that the judgment fulfilled the condition contained in the NGF’s indemnity, thereby making the 100 million dollars payable directly to him.

Under the indemnity, the NGF had undertaken to pay the claimant the money if the federal government was found liable.

Iseghohi-Edwards said he formally demanded payment from the NGF through a letter dated Oct. 8, 2026, but the forum allegedly failed to honour the undertaking.

Consequently, he approached the FCT High Court, seeking to preserve the money pending the determination of his substantive claim.

In the application, he expressed apprehension that the NGF might transfer, disburse or dissipate the funds, thereby frustrating enforcement of any eventual judgment.

He also told the court that he could not identify the specific bank accounts holding the funds without judicial intervention.

The claimant argued that the injunction was necessary to preserve the subject matter of the dispute and prevent the proceedings from becoming futile.

He maintained that the restriction was limited to one aggregate sum of 100 million dollars across the NGF and all participating banks.

The application was brought pursuant to Orders 30(3) and 32(1) of the FCT High Court Civil Procedure Rules and the court’s inherent jurisdiction.

The claimant also undertook to abide by any order for damages should the court subsequently determine that the interim injunction ought not to have been granted.

Justice Agbaza adjourned the matter until Dec. 1, for hearing of the motion on notice, and directed the claimant to serve the order on all respondents.

The first respondent in the suit is the Incorporated Trustees of the Nigerian Governors’ Forum.

The 29 banks that joined as co-respondents are Access Bank Plc, Alpha Morgan Bank Limited, Ecobank Nigeria Plc, Fidelity Bank Plc and First Bank of Nigeria Plc.

Others are Sterling Bank Plc, United Bank for Africa Plc, Unity Bank Plc, Zenith Bank Plc and Jaiz Bank Plc.

Also joined in the suit are Guarantee Trust Bank Plc, Keystone Bank Plc, Stanbic IBTC Bank Limited, Standard Chartered Bank Limited and Wema Bank Plc.

The list further includes Union Bank of Nigeria Plc, First City Monument Bank Plc, Lotus Bank Plc, Parallex Bank Limited and Polaris Bank Limited.

Other respondents are Globus Bank Limited, SunTrust Bank Limited, Citibank Nigeria Limited, Nova Bank Limited and Optimus Bank Limited.

The remaining banks joined in the suit are Premium Trust Bank Limited, Signature Bank Limited, Tatum Bank Limited and Titan Trust Bank Limited. (NAN)

The post Paris Club Refunds: Court freezes N135.5bn linked to Governors’ Forum appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Five women killed hourly by partners, relatives in 2025 – UN
description:
More than 47,000 women and girls, or around five per hour, were killed by relatives around the world in 2025, a figure broadly unchanged from previous years, according to a UN report published Tuesday.
The number of women and girls killed by an intimate partner or a family member has fluctuated betw
content:
More than 47,000 women and girls, or around five per hour, were killed by relatives around the world in 2025, a figure broadly unchanged from previous years, according to a UN report published Tuesday.

The number of women and girls killed by an intimate partner or a family member has fluctuated between 45,000 and 51,000 over the past several years, according to estimates by UN Women and the UN Office on Drugs and Crime.

Of the 78,000 women and girls who were victims of intentional homicide last year, around 60 percent were killed by an intimate partner or family member, the report said ahead of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.

The estimated 47,000 victims represent 129 women and girls killed every day. The figure was calculated using an analysis of statistics from 122 countries and territories.

While women accounted for 19 percent of homicide victims worldwide in 2025, 60 percent of them were killed in the private sphere. By contrast, 11 percent of male homicide victims were killed in such circumstances.

The UN stressed the “urgency of ensuring that the prevention of domestic violence addresses intimate relationships, as well as relationships in wider family structures.”

No region was completely safe but Africa once again recorded the highest number of women and girls killed by intimate partners or family members, at 22,100.

Asia followed with 15,100 victims, ahead of the Americas with 7,400, Europe with 2,100 and Oceania with 300.

The report also noted that while homicide rates have fallen globally, rates of femicide have declined more slowly, particularly in the Americas and Europe.

This suggests, according to the UN, “that these crimes are deeply rooted in social norms and gender stereotypes,” adding that it points to barriers in accessing the justice system.

Femicide refers to the gender-related killing of women and girls. Beyond murders committed by intimate partners or family members, the term can also encompass certain killings linked to organized crime, forced labor or human trafficking.

However, data on femicides committed outside the private sphere remain very limited, the report said, making it impossible to measure the scale of the phenomenon at regional or global level.

AFP

title: 2027: Massive support for Orji Kalu as Ihechiowa traditional rulers, community leaders pledge unalloyed backing
description: The Senator representing Abia North Senatorial District, Orji Uzor Kalu, has received massive expressions of support from traditional rulers, community leaders, political stakeholders and residents of Ihechiowa Clan in Arochukwu Local Government Area of Abia State during his ongoing ward-to-ward con
content:
The Senator representing Abia North Senatorial District, Orji Uzor Kalu, has received massive expressions of support from traditional rulers, community leaders, political stakeholders and residents of Ihechiowa Clan in Arochukwu Local Government Area of Abia State during his ongoing ward-to-ward consultation tour ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The former Abia State governor received overwhelming goodwill and renewed declarations of support as he visited various communities across Ihechiowa, where traditional rulers and other stakeholders acknowledged his constituency interventions and expressed confidence in his continued representation of Abia North.

The Monday engagements provided an opportunity for community leaders to appreciate his contributions to grassroots development while presenting additional demands for roads, educational facilities, potable water and other essential infrastructure.

Kalu began the tour with courtesy visits to Chief Eze Okali of Okpo Ihechiowa and Chief Otigba Kalu Chukwu, Eze Ogo of Achara Ihechiowa. Discussions during the visits focused on community development, rural infrastructure, education and the need for sustained government attention to rural communities.

The traditional rulers acknowledged the senator’s interventions, including the construction of rural roads and classroom blocks, provision of school desks and educational support programmes, including overseas scholarship opportunities.

At the various community gatherings, Kalu received warm receptions from constituents who commended his engagement with the grassroots and expressed support for his continued representation.

His engagements covered Okpor Village Square, Eleoha Ward 4; Achara Market Square, Eleoha Ward 3; Amafia Etitii Village Square, Eleoha Ward 2; and Umuchi Market, Eleoha Ward 1.

At Amafia/Amaetiti, he met with Chief Kalu O. Kalu of Amafia Ihechiowa and Chief Eke Torty, Eze Amaetiti, who highlighted the infrastructural challenges confronting their communities, particularly poor road networks, inadequate electricity and lack of potable water.

Responding to their concerns, the senator assured the communities that he would work towards incorporating their priority needs into the forthcoming budget, with particular attention to rural roads and educational infrastructure.

He also pledged to facilitate additional school projects, stressing the importance of education and accessible roads to rural economic development.

One of the notable endorsements came from Pastor Innocent Okoro, who commended Kalu’s activities at the National Assembly and his constituency development initiatives.

Describing the senator as one of the country’s performing legislators, Okoro declared the community’s readiness to support his continued representation.

“Senator Orji Uzor Kalu is among the best in the country. If others have performed like him, Abia North would be a paradise. We are going to give him our total support,” he declared.

The senator also visited Prince Abel Uche, Eze Umuakuma, and held further engagements with community stakeholders across Ikwun Wards 1 and 2, including Chief Okorie Amannukwu of Ama Mmiri.

During the meetings, community leaders acknowledged his interventions and pledged their support for his continued representation, while presenting additional development priorities for his consideration.

Addressing the people, Kalu called for support for his re-election bid, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and other candidates of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general elections.

He also introduced Chief Ikenna Nicholas Ukwa, the APC candidate for Arochukwu/Ohafia Federal Constituency, and Prince Ike Okorafor, the party’s candidate for Arochukwu State Constituency.

Beyond the political and developmental engagements, the senator demonstrated solidarity with bereaved families in Ihechiowa.

He paid a condolence visit to Hon. High Chief Offor Okorie following the death of his mother, Mrs. Mercy Boniface Okorie, aged 67.

He also visited Austine Emeka Bonny, popularly known as Delazz Inc., of Ndi Okpo, Ihechiowa, to commiserate with him over his bereavement.

Kalu expressed his heartfelt condolences to both families and prayed for God’s comfort and strength for them during their respective periods of mourning.

Among the dignitaries accompanying the senator were Chief Ikenna Nicholas Ukwa, Prince Ike Okorafor, APC Chairman of Arochukwu LGA, Mazi Sunday Torty, Chief Smart Ukoha, Hon. Paul Uche and other party chieftains and community stakeholders.

The tour concluded at Ikwun Ward 1, where Kalu expressed appreciation to the people of Ihechiowa for their hospitality, goodwill and expressions of support.

He reiterated that his ward-to-ward engagements were designed to strengthen direct communication with constituents, assess ongoing projects and identify areas requiring further government intervention.

The widespread expressions of support from traditional rulers, community leaders and political stakeholders formed a major highlight of the visit, as communities used the opportunity to reaffirm their relationship with the senator while seeking further development interventions.

Kalu assured the people that their concerns would receive attention, pledging to sustain engagement with the communities and pursue projects aimed at improving infrastructure, education and the general welfare of residents.

title: NDC attack: Police confirm six people killed in Delta
description:
The Nigeria Police Force has stated that six persons lost their lives in Monday’s deadly attack at a Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) campaign event at Uduere Community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.
Force Public Relations Officer (FPRO), CSP Ani Iniedu confirmed this in a Tue
content:
The Nigeria Police Force has stated that six persons lost their lives in Monday’s deadly attack at a Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) campaign event at Uduere Community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.

Force Public Relations Officer (FPRO), CSP Ani Iniedu confirmed this in a Tuesday statement.

The statement reads, “The Nigeria Police Force strongly condemns the deadly violence that occurred on Monday, 23 November 2026, at Uduere Community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, during a political campaign event.

“The Force deeply regrets the loss of lives and injuries recorded and extends its heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families, while wishing the injured a speedy recovery.

“Preliminary Police reports indicate that six persons lost their lives, while several others sustained injuries. The Force is aware of varying casualty figures circulating in the public domain.

“An ongoing investigation will establish the verified number of casualties and determine the circumstances surrounding the incident.”

The confirmation comes a day after the Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation reported that four people were killed during the attack on the campaign team of Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, a former Deputy Senate President and Delta Central senatorial candidate of NDC, in Uduere.

Meanwhile, the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Disu, has directed the Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, to immediately commence a thorough, impartial and evidence-based investigation into the incident.

According to the force, the investigation will establish the sequence of events, identify those responsible for the violence, and examine the circumstances surrounding the shooting, including the deployment and conduct of police personnel at the venue.

The Omo-Agege campaign had earlier alleged that police officers were present with six trucks but did nothing to prevent the attack and killings, and had called on the IGP to personally take over the investigation.

“Any officer found to have acted negligently, unlawfully or in breach of professional standards will face appropriate disciplinary action, while all persons found culpable of criminal offences will be prosecuted in accordance with the law,” the force statement reads in part.

The police reiterated that political differences, campaign rivalries or partisan interests must never be allowed to result in violence, intimidation, destruction of property or the loss of innocent lives.

In response to the security situation, the Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area, from 6:00 pm to 6:00 am daily, until further notice.

The Delta State Police Command is enforcing the directive and has intensified security measures to prevent further breakdown of law and order.

The IGP has further ordered enhanced security deployment, intelligence-led operations, sustained patrols and rapid-response measures to protect lives and property, prevent further violence and restore normalcy to the affected communities.

Residents, community leaders, political actors, campaign organisations and their supporters were urged to remain calm, comply strictly with the curfew and all lawful security directives, and refrain from spreading unverified information or inflammatory content capable of escalating tensions.

Members of the public were also encouraged to cooperate with security agencies, while anyone with credible information, photographs, video recordings or other evidence that could assist the investigation was urged to report through established police channels.

“The Nigeria Police Force remains committed to protecting lives and property, maintaining public order, safeguarding the democratic process and ensuring that all those found responsible for this violence are brought to justice,” the statement further reads.

title: ‎2027: Northern leaders should appeal to Atiku to step down, wait for North’s turn — Smart Adeyemi
description: The Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council in Kogi State, Senator Smart Adeyemi,has appealed on the Northern Leaders to prevail on the Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, Atiku Abubakar to step down out of the presidential race sa
content:
The Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council in Kogi State, Senator Smart Adeyemi,has appealed on the Northern Leaders to prevail on the Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, Atiku Abubakar to step down out of the presidential race saying it is not yet the Northern turn.

Senator Adeyemi who insisted that Southern Nigeria must be allowed to complete its eight-year presidential tenure in 2027, stressed that the unity of the country was more paramount than the ambition of an Individual saying anything that will heat up the polity and derail the smooth running of the current democracy must not be allowed .

‎Adeyemi, a three-term former lawmaker who represented Kogi West Senatorial District, made the remarks on Sunday evening while appearing as a guest on TVC News’ current affairs programme, Politics Today, monitored by newsmen.
‎
‎Speaking during the televised interview, the Kogi APC campaign chief argued that equity, fairness, and national stability demand that the South concludes its full two-term cycle before power rotates back to the North.
‎
‎He further stressed that when power eventually returns to Northern Nigeria, leadership opportunities must be thrown open to a wider pool of competent men and women rather than remaining the exclusive preserve of the former Vice President every election cycle.
‎
‎“In the spirit of fairness and national unity, the South must be allowed to complete its eight years in office. Beyond that, Northern Nigeria has many capable men and women who can aspire to lead this country when power returns to the region. Atiku cannot continue to contest every four years as though the North has no other credible leaders,” Adeyemi stated during the broadcast.
‎
‎The former NUJ National President also criticised the former Vice President’s political antecedents, describing him as a politician encumbered by unresolved controversies and heavy political baggage that render his candidacy unattractive to Nigerians.
‎

title: Again, Africa Tops UN Report On Intentional Homicide Against Women, Girls In 2025
description: Although no region was completely safe, Africa once again recorded the highest number of women and girls killed by intimate partners or family members, at 22,100, according to a UN report published Tuesday.Asia followed with 15,100 victims, ahead of the Americas with 7,400, Europe with 2,100 and Oce
content:
Although no region was completely safe, Africa once again recorded the highest number of women and girls killed by intimate partners or family members, at 22,100, according to a UN report published Tuesday.

Asia followed with 15,100 victims, ahead of the Americas with 7,400, Europe with 2,100 and Oceania with 300.

The report published ahead of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women noted that more than 47,000 women and girls, or around five per hour, were killed by relatives around the world in 2025, a figure broadly unchanged from previous years.

The estimated 47,000 victims represent 129 women and girls killed every day. The figure was calculated using an analysis of statistics from 122 countries and territories.

The number of women and girls killed by an intimate partner or a family member has fluctuated between 45,000 and 51,000 over the past several years, according to estimates by UN Women and the UN Office on Drugs and Crime.

Of the 78,000 women and girls who were victims of intentional homicide last year, around 60 percent were killed by an intimate partner or family member.

While women accounted for 19 percent of homicide victims worldwide in 2025, 60 percent of them were killed in the private sphere. By contrast, 11 percent of male homicide victims were killed in such circumstances.

The UN stressed the “urgency of ensuring that the prevention of domestic violence addresses intimate relationships, as well as relationships in wider family structures.”

The report also noted that while homicide rates have fallen globally, rates of femicide have declined more slowly, particularly in the Americas and Europe.

This suggests, according to the UN, “that these crimes are deeply rooted in social norms and gender stereotypes,” adding that it points to barriers in accessing the justice system.

Femicide refers to the gender-related killing of women and girls. Beyond murders committed by intimate partners or family members, the term can also encompass certain killings linked to organized crime, forced labor or human trafficking.

However, data on femicides committed outside the private sphere remain very limited, the report said, making it impossible to measure the scale of the phenomenon at regional or global level.

AFP

title: Pack of dogs mauls US Army veteran to death
description:
A 36-year-old United States Army veteran and mother of three, Allison Lynn Anderson, has died after being attacked by a pack of dogs in Cartersville, Georgia.
Anderson was found with fatal injuries on November 16 after police responded to reports of an unresponsive woman near an abandoned property,
content:
A 36-year-old United States Army veteran and mother of three, Allison Lynn Anderson, has died after being attacked by a pack of dogs in Cartersville, Georgia.

Anderson was found with fatal injuries on November 16 after police responded to reports of an unresponsive woman near an abandoned property, according to a report by the New York Post on Monday.

The Georgia Bureau of Investigation disclosed the circumstances surrounding her death, citing preliminary autopsy findings, but did not reveal the exact number of dogs involved.

Several of the dogs have been taken into the custody of Bartow County Animal Control, while investigators continue to probe the incident.

Anderson, a mother of three, joined the US Army in 2007. She was also unknowingly about to become a grandmother, as her 20-year-old daughter, Miley Garner, is expecting her first child.

Garner, who is expecting the baby with her fiancé, Jesse Jarrett, said her mother would have been excited to learn about the pregnancy.

“If my mom knew that I was carrying her first grandchild, she would be over the moon and full of excitement,” she told WAFB, a Louisiana-based television station in the US.

Expressing anger over the incident, Garner said the owners of the dogs should have kept them under control.

“I am so disgusted and absolutely heartbroken that the owners of these dogs did not have control over them. What my mom went through was torture,” she said.

She added that her mother deserved justice but would have forgiven those responsible.

Anderson’s family described her as a woman with a lively personality who was always willing to help others.

“She was outgoing, full of personality, and never met a stranger. If someone needed help, Allison was there, whether she knew them or not,” the family said in an obituary announcing her death.

The family also said she enjoyed spending time outdoors, swimming, fishing, listening to music and singing.

Meanwhile, investigators are reviewing surveillance footage from the area as part of their probe.

No arrests had been made as of Monday, according to the report.

The post Pack of dogs mauls US Army veteran to death appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: He got it wrong – Gerrard criticises Pochettino over Man Utd star
description:
Former Liverpool captain, Steven Gerrard, has criticised Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino for leaving Harry Maguire out of his starting lineup during Sunday’s 4-0 defeat to Liverpool.
Gerrard described the decision as disrespectful, arguing that Maguire should have started ahead of Matt
content:
Former Liverpool captain, Steven Gerrard, has criticised Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino for leaving Harry Maguire out of his starting lineup during Sunday’s 4-0 defeat to Liverpool.

Gerrard described the decision as disrespectful, arguing that Maguire should have started ahead of Matthijs de Ligt, who had only recently returned from a lengthy injury absence.

Speaking on The Overlap, Gerrard said Pochettino made the wrong defensive selection for a match of such importance.

“I thought he got it wrong. I thought he got it wrong in the back line,” the former England midfielder said.

He questioned the decision to start De Ligt, who had not played since November 2025, in such a high-profile encounter.

Gerrard acknowledged that Pochettino might have wanted to introduce changes following his appointment as United manager but insisted that Maguire deserved to retain his place.

“Harry Maguire is their best defender at the moment. He should have started the game, and he made a difference when he came on,” he added.

The former Liverpool midfielder also praised Maguire’s contribution after coming off the bench, particularly his defensive commitment and a crucial block that prevented a potential Liverpool goal.

Gerrard further described the decision to favour De Ligt over Maguire as “a bit disrespectful”, noting that although the England defender had not been perfect, he had shown commitment to the team.

Manchester United suffered a 4-0 defeat at Anfield after Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute, with Liverpool taking advantage of their numerical superiority to secure a convincing victory.

Gerrard also warned that United could face difficulties strengthening their defence during the January transfer window, arguing that clubs would be reluctant to release top centre-backs midway through the season.

He said United would have to pay substantial sums if they were determined to sign established defenders in January.

title: Backing Obi in 2023 was a mistake – Abure
description:
Factional National Chairman of the Labour Party, Julius Abure, has said supporting Peter Obi in the 2023 presidential election may have been a mistake, declaring his backing for President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 polls.
Abure made the remarks on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday ni
content:
Factional National Chairman of the Labour Party, Julius Abure, has said supporting Peter Obi in the 2023 presidential election may have been a mistake, declaring his backing for President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 polls.

Abure made the remarks on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday night, accusing Obi of lacking the character and competence to lead Nigeria.

“President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is 100 per cent better,” he said, adding that his experience working with Obi had changed his assessment of the former Anambra State governor.

Asked by the interviewer whether Obi was a bad leader, Abure said the former Anambra State governor lacked the character and competence to lead the country.

“Peter Obi cannot… doesn’t have the character and competence to lead the country. Well, sorry to say, given my experiences, I now know better,” he said.

When reminded that he had previously sold Obi to Nigerians as the Labour Party’s presidential candidate, Abure replied, “Yes, and that may have been an error because I now know better. I now know better.”

He said his experience working with Obi had changed his opinion of him.

“Where are the 34, 35 House of Representatives members that we got in 2023? Where are the senators? If indeed Peter Obi was a good leader, why did they not follow Peter Obi?” he asked.

The Labour Party chieftain, who said the party leadership had supported Obi during the 2023 campaign without receiving financial assistance or vehicles from him, compared the former governor with Tinubu.

“President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is 100 per cent better,” Abure said, adding that a comparative assessment of both politicians had been made at a party meeting.

Asked directly whether he had declared support for Tinubu, Abure responded, “Obviously, we are supporting him.”

He also said members of the Labour Party had the right to support any presidential candidate of their choice, insisting that Obi was no longer an option for his political camp.

Obi contested the 2023 presidential election on the Labour Party platform, finishing third behind Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress and Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party. He is now the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress for the 2027 election.

Abure’s remarks come amid the prolonged leadership crisis within the Labour Party, which has been the subject of legal disputes and competing claims over the party’s leadership.

Abure and Obi’s relationship deteriorated following the 2023 general election, amid disagreements over the leadership and control of the Labour Party. In September 2024, Obi and Abia State Governor Alex Otti backed the formation of a caretaker committee led by Senator Nenadi Usman, a move Abure opposed, accusing the two politicians of destabilising the party.

Although Abure initially described the disagreements as a “family affair” and expressed willingness to reconcile, he later became increasingly critical of Obi.

In June 2026, he accused the former governor of failing to unite the party after the election and said Obi should have put the party’s house in order.

The post Backing Obi in 2023 was a mistake – Abure appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Tyson Fury reveals schizophrenia, bipolar disorder
description:
Former world heavyweight boxing champion, Tyson Fury, has disclosed that he was diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder in a forthcoming Netflix documentary about his life and career.



According to Deadline, Fury made the revelation in the feature-length documentary titled Tyson Fury, wh
content:
Former world heavyweight boxing champion, Tyson Fury, has disclosed that he was diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder in a forthcoming Netflix documentary about his life and career.

According to Deadline, Fury made the revelation in the feature-length documentary titled Tyson Fury, which is scheduled for release later this month.

The boxer said he was diagnosed with schizophrenia shortly after defeating Wladimir Klitschko in 2015 to become the world heavyweight champion.

He also disclosed that he received a bipolar disorder diagnosis in 2017.

Reflecting on his mental health struggles in the documentary, Fury described experiencing periods of severe psychological distress.

“Words can’t explain the darkness I was in. I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100% thought at times I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much,” he reportedly said.

Fury also recounted experiencing intense anxiety that frequently woke him in the middle of the night.

He said he eventually sought professional help from a psychiatrist in London, who assessed him through a series of questions and identified depression, anxiety and bipolar disorder.

The documentary also features contributions from his wife, Paris Fury, and father, John Fury, who discuss his mental health challenges.

The post Tyson Fury reveals schizophrenia, bipolar disorder appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Kwara begins payment of outstanding gratuities to LG retirees
description:
The Kwara State Government has commenced the payment of outstanding gratuities to retired local government and Local Government Education Authority workers who left service between 2018 and 2019, with more than N2bn released for the exercise.
The Chairman of the Kwara State Local Government Staff Pe
content:
The Kwara State Government has commenced the payment of outstanding gratuities to retired local government and Local Government Education Authority workers who left service between 2018 and 2019, with more than N2bn released for the exercise.

The Chairman of the Kwara State Local Government Staff Pension Board and Executive Chairman of the Local Government Service Commission, Umar Danladi Shero, disclosed this on Monday while briefing journalists in Ilorin on recent developments in the commission and efforts to settle outstanding pension obligations.

Shero said beneficiaries who retired within the 2018–2019 period had started receiving their payments following the completion of the necessary verification and screening exercises.

He described the development as another step in the state government’s efforts to settle inherited gratuity liabilities and improve the welfare of retired local government and LG workers.

“The payment exercise is part of the ongoing efforts to clear inherited gratuity liabilities from the past administration,” he said.

The pension board chairman also disclosed that the state government had spent more than N7bn on gratuity payments to local government and LG retirees who left service between 2011 and 2017.

According to him, the amount was expended between July and October, while the latest disbursement of more than N2bn extended the payment exercise to retirees from 2018 and 2019.

Shero commended Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq for his support in addressing pension obligations and improving the welfare of retired workers.

“The Governor’s continued support and intervention have provided the necessary enabling environment for sustained pension administration, regular pension payments and the gradual settlement of outstanding gratuity obligations inherited from previous administrations,” he stated.

He assured retirees that the board had put arrangements in place to ensure a seamless and transparent payment process.

“Payments will be made directly into beneficiaries’ designated bank accounts,” he added.

Shero reaffirmed the board’s commitment to ensuring that all verified and eligible retirees received their entitlements as the government continued efforts to settle outstanding gratuity obligations.

He urged beneficiaries to remain patient and cooperate with the board where necessary, assuring them that the payment exercise would continue in an orderly and transparent manner.

He added that the government’s resolve was to ensure that no eligible pensioner was left behind as it worked towards clearing outstanding gratuity liabilities.

The latest disbursement comes amid the state government’s ongoing efforts to clear years of accumulated gratuity arrears owed to retired local government workers.

In October 2025, the state Commissioner for Finance, Dr Hauwa Nuhu, disclosed that the government had inherited more than N19bn in local government gratuity liabilities dating back to 2009, out of which N12bn had been paid.

She also said gratuities for local government workers had been cleared up to 2011, while N2.5bn had been earmarked for arrears covering 2012 to 2014.

The government had earlier said it increased monthly releases for gratuity payments from N20m to N100m after assuming office in 2019, as part of efforts to gradually settle the inherited backlog.

The post Kwara begins payment of outstanding gratuities to LG retirees appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: US adds 24 Nigerians to deportation list, total hits 157
description:
The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has added 24 Nigerians to its list of foreign nationals facing deportation over alleged criminal activities, bringing the total number of Nigerians featured on the register to 157.
The latest names were published on the department’s “Worst of t
content:
The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has added 24 Nigerians to its list of foreign nationals facing deportation over alleged criminal activities, bringing the total number of Nigerians featured on the register to 157.

The latest names were published on the department’s “Worst of the Worst” webpage, which identifies foreign nationals arrested by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) over serious criminal offences and facing removal from the country.

According to the DHS website, the Nigerians were arrested for offences ranging from fraud, money laundering and drug-related crimes to identity theft, assault, forgery and child cruelty.

Among those listed are Emmanuel Omowaiye, arrested in Richmond, Texas, over mail fraud; Laurene Onwuka, arrested in Chantilly, Virginia, over fraud by impersonation; and Olusegun Shonekan, arrested in Newark, New Jersey, over wire fraud.

Others include Olusegun Olaseni, arrested in Greencastle, Indiana, over the sale of amphetamine; Peter Ude, arrested in Atlanta, Georgia, over wire fraud; and Newton Jemide, arrested in Fort Dix, New Jersey, over wire fraud, conspiracy and mail fraud.

The list also features Shedrack Umukoro, arrested in Yazoo City, Mississippi, over money laundering; Olasoji Akinbode, arrested in Kearny, New Jersey, over fraud by impersonation; and Oluwatosin Afolabi, arrested in Conroe, Texas, over fraud.

Also named are Alameen Adetunji Tokosi, arrested in Chicago, Illinois, over heroin possession, and Joshua Ipoade, arrested in Atlanta, Georgia, over wire fraud.

Michael Orji, arrested in Oxford, Wisconsin, was listed over weapons-related offences, fraud, identity theft, wire fraud, false citizenship and money laundering.

Other Nigerians on the list include Ahmadu Apooyin, arrested in Baltimore, Maryland, over a cocaine-related offence; Teslim Kiriji, arrested in Yazoo City, Mississippi, over money laundering; and Onomen Uduebor, arrested in Seattle, Washington, over identity theft.

Charles Ochi and Daniel Eta were arrested in White Deer, Pennsylvania, over money laundering and wire fraud, respectively.

Ifeanyi Ibennah, arrested in Tampa, Florida, was listed over child cruelty, while Kazeem Runsewe, arrested in Thomson, Illinois, and Fatiu Lawal, arrested in Lompoc, California, were listed over wire fraud.

The remaining names include Justin Akubueze, arrested in Orem, Utah, over money laundering; Moyinoluwaseun Okeowo, arrested in Orlando, Florida, over larceny, forgery and concealing stolen property; Babajide Oluwaseun Faseyi, arrested in Alden, New York, over assault; and Bright Eigbedion, arrested in Lompoc, California, over money laundering.

The DHS said the initiative was part of President Donald Trump’s administration’s efforts to remove foreign nationals involved in serious criminal activities from the United States.

The department stated: “The U.S. Department of Homeland Security is fulfilling President Trump’s promise to remove the worst of the worst criminal aliens from the United States.

“This page highlights criminal aliens arrested by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement who are being removed after engaging in serious criminal activity, including drug and weapons offences, violent crimes including rape and murder, fraud, and the misuse or theft of public benefits.”

However, the department did not specify when the listed Nigerians would be deported or their immigration status as of the time of filing this report.

The publication of their names on the webpage does not, on its own, establish that they have been convicted of the offences listed against them.

The post US adds 24 Nigerians to deportation list, total hits 157 appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: NDA 2027 admission: How to apply, fees, requirements
description:
The Nigerian Defence Academy has opened applications for admission into its 79th Regular Course for the 2027/2028 academic session, with eligible male and female Nigerians required to pay ₦7,100 for the application.
The academy announced on Monday that the application portal would remain open from N
content:
The Nigerian Defence Academy has opened applications for admission into its 79th Regular Course for the 2027/2028 academic session, with eligible male and female Nigerians required to pay ₦7,100 for the application.

The academy announced on Monday that the application portal would remain open from November 23, 2026, to April 30, 2027.

Prospective applicants are expected to meet the admission requirements, participate in the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board examination and pass the academy’s screening exercises.

Here is what candidates need to know about the admission process.

When does the NDA 2027 admission application close?

The application portal opened on Monday, November 23, 2026, and will close on April 30, 2027.

According to the admission announcement, “Online application for admission into the 79 Regular Course (RC) of the Nigerian Defence Academy (NDA), Kaduna will be available from Monday 23 November 2026 to 30 April 2027.”

It added that admission was open to “both male and female Nigerians.”

How much is the NDA application form?

The application fee is ₦7,100.

Candidates are required to visit the academy’s admission portal, select the purchase access code option and complete their details before making payment through Remita.

The announcement stated, “Candidates should log on to the application portal rc.nda.edu.ng, select ‘Purchase Access Code’ and fill in their details to pay for their application via REMITA in the sum of ₦7,100.00 only.”

It warned that “only payment against RRR Codes generated via the application portal would be accepted.”

How can candidates apply?

Interested candidates are required to complete their applications online through the NDA admission portal.

The academy advised applicants to download and carefully read the instructions provided on the website before proceeding with their applications.

“Interested candidates are advised to go online and complete the application on the website indicated above. Please download and read carefully, the instructions provided on the website,” the announcement stated.

Candidates are also required to submit their applications alongside scanned copies of their Senior Secondary Certificate Examination, National Examinations Council or equivalent results and their National Identification Number details.

The academy said, “All NIN details must be in tandem with details on other credentials.”

After submitting their applications, candidates are expected to download an acknowledgement form.

Is JAMB required for NDA admission?

Yes. Applicants must register for the 2027 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination organised by JAMB and select the Nigerian Defence Academy as their first-choice institution.

The academy made this requirement clear in its announcement, stating, “Applicants seeking admission into the NDA must also apply to the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) and must select NDA as first choice institution.”

It added that such applicants were “expected to sit for the JAMB Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME).”

What is the required UTME score?

Candidates seeking admission into Engineering programmes must score at least 210 in the UTME, while those applying for other faculties must obtain a minimum of 180.

The academy stated that only candidates who satisfied the admission requirements and obtained the required UTME scores would be able to print their screening test admission cards and participate in the screening exercise.

What are the other admission requirements?

The specific requirements for the various undergraduate degree programmes are available on the NDA website and application portal.

However, the academy stated that candidates must have SSCE, NECO or equivalent results not more than five years old at the time of admission.

It also identified knowledge of French or Arabic as an added advantage, stating, “Knowledge of French or Arabic will be an added advantage to applicants.”

The announcement further emphasised that results from SSCE, NECO or equivalent examinations “must also not be more than 5 years as of the time of admission.”

When will the NDA screening test hold?

The NDA announced Saturday, June 8, 2027, as the date for the first phase of its screening test, which will serve as the post-UTME exercise.

The announcement stated, “The NDA Screening Test will be conducted as Phase One of the Post-UTME screening and is scheduled to hold on Saturday 8 June 2027.”

Candidates who qualify are required to present their acknowledgement forms, screening test admission cards, JAMB result slips and two postcard-sized photographs measuring 3.5 by five inches.

According to the academy, the photographs must show candidates from the chest upwards and contain their names, examination numbers, states, examination centres, courses of study and signatures at the back.

What happens after the first screening test?

Candidates who successfully pass the first phase will be invited for the Armed Forces Selection Board exercise, which constitutes the second phase of the screening process.

The academy stated that “only successful candidates at the NDA Screening Test will subsequently be invited for the Armed Forces Selection Board (Phase 2 of the NDA Screening Test).”

It added that the list of admitted candidates would be published after the exercise.

How long is the NDA training?

Candidates admitted into the 79th Regular Course will undergo five years of military and academic training as officer cadets.

The academy stated that “candidates admitted into the NDA for Regular Course will undergo military and academic training as officer cadets for a duration of 5 years.”

Upon successful completion of the programme, graduates will receive honours degrees in their respective disciplines, including Bachelor of Science, Bachelor of Engineering and Bachelor of Arts degrees.

The academy added that graduates would “equally earn a Presidential Commission into the Armed Forces of Nigeria.”

Who pays for the training?

The Federal Government will bear the cost of administration and logistics for all Regular Course cadets throughout their training.

The academy stated, “All Regular Course cadets will train in NDA and the cost of their administration and logistics will be borne by the Federal Government of Nigeria.”

Where can applicants get more information?

Prospective applicants can obtain further information about the admission process, available courses, eligibility requirements and screening centres through the following channels:

• NDA website: www.nda.edu.ng
• Application portal: rc.nda.edu.ng
• Enquiries/support: info@ndaapplications.net

The academy also announced that a compendium of past questions and answers was available for interested candidates.

According to the notice, “The Academy offers a Compendium of Past Questions & Answers at a taken fee to interested candidates. This can be purchased from the Registry, NDA.”

The post NDA 2027 admission: How to apply, fees, requirements appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Nigerians Firmly Behind APC Despite Criticism And Insults — Yari
description: The Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’azeez Yari Abubakar, has said the massive turnout at the party’s governorship campaign flag-off in Zamfara State demonstrates the people’s acceptance of the party despite what h
content:
The Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’azeez Yari Abubakar, has said the massive turnout at the party’s governorship campaign flag-off in Zamfara State demonstrates the people’s acceptance of the party despite what he described as campaigns of calumny and insults against it.

Yari said the APC was consolidating its support base to secure victory at all levels in the 2027 general elections, attributing the party’s growing acceptance to its closeness to the masses.

He stated this on Monday during the APC campaign flag-off held in Talata-Mafara, which attracted party faithful, support groups and members of the public.

Crowds of party supporters welcomed Governor Dauda Lawal’s motorcade to Talata-Mafara town before proceeding to the town’s Eid ground, venue of the rally.

Speaking at the event, Senator Yari said the large turnout reflected the enthusiasm and commitment of party members and supporters towards the party’s preparations for the 2027 elections.

“Make sure this message gets to the public: we are determined to deliver victory for the APC, from President Tinubu down to members of the State House of Assembly.

“The overwhelming response to our call demonstrates that, despite the insults and campaigns against the APC, the people of Zamfara have understood our message and are firmly behind the party,” he said.

Also speaking, Governor Dauda Lawal expressed gratitude to party supporters for their show of solidarity, while commending the people for their resilience and commitment to peaceful coexistence.

He reaffirmed his administration’s resolve to promote inclusive governance, equitable development and sustained engagement with communities across the state.

“This crowd speaks for itself; there is very little to say other than to thank Almighty God. Whenever I turn around and see this mammoth crowd of supporters, I am filled with gratitude.

“At this point, I will simply say, let us wait for election day and, ultimately, the swearing-in day,” Lawal said.

The APC campaign train is expected to move to other local government areas of Zamfara State as the party intensifies its mobilisation and grassroots engagement ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The post Nigerians Firmly Behind APC Despite Criticism And Insults — Yari appeared first on Channels Television.

By Olasunkanmi Akoni

The Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA) has launched a nighttime waste evacuation operation across the state to tackle mounting refuse heaps and restore environmental sanitation ahead of the Christmas and New Year festivities.

The exercise, which commenced on Monday night, began along the Isheri–Igando–LASU–Iba corridor, with sanitation teams and heavy-duty equipment deployed to clear identified waste black spots.

LAWMA’s Acting Managing Director, Olajuwon Akinyemi, led the operation at Igando Bus Stop alongside the Acting Executive Director of Operations, Olorunwa Tijani, and the Executive Director of Finance, Kunle Adebiyi.

Speaking during the exercise, Akinyemi said the nighttime evacuation would be extended to other major entry routes and high-traffic corridors, including Ojota–Ikorodu Road, Mushin–Moshalashi axis and Lekki–Ajah corridor.

He said the operation was aimed at restoring Lagos’s environmental appeal and providing a cleaner and healthier atmosphere for residents and visitors expected in the state during the busy December holiday season.

To prevent cleared locations from becoming refuse dumps again, the agency said it was partnering with traditional institutions across the state to strengthen community monitoring and enforcement.

Beyond the immediate clean-up exercise, Akinyemi announced plans to establish more than 10 regional offices across Lagos as part of efforts to decentralise the authority’s operations.

He described the restructuring as non-negotiable, saying the regional offices would improve operational coordination, bring waste management services closer to communities, strengthen accountability and ensure faster responses to sanitation challenges.

The LAWMA boss appealed to residents to remain patient with the state government as it works to address waste management challenges across the metropolis.

He also urged residents to promptly report service failures by Private Sector Participation (PSP) waste operators through the authority’s official communication channels to enable it to enforce compliance.

title: How Ruben Amorim Is Rebuilding His Reputation At AC Milan
description:
It was meant to be a dream job for Ruben Amorim when he took over at Manchester United in November 2024. His successor Michael Carrick has also now departed, at the same time Amorim has built his reputation once again.  
The Portuguese came from Sporting highly recommended following their dominance
content:
It was meant to be a dream job for Ruben Amorim when he took over at Manchester United in November 2024. His successor Michael Carrick has also now departed, at the same time Amorim has built his reputation once again.  

The Portuguese came from Sporting highly recommended following their dominance an exceptional run under his stewardship. Five major trophies across just four years in charge was a very impressive return, while a winning percentage of 71.43% in 231 games with 165 wins tells its own story.

With Manchester United still searching for solidity and success following the removal of a fifth permanent manager along with four caretaker or interim managers since Sir Alex Ferguson in 2013, Amorim looked like the perfect tonic for United’s woes.

However, after a total of just 63 games, he was sacked. Just 24 wins, 18 draws and 21 defeats saw him oversee wins in just 38.1% of his matches. For a side like United, a win in just over one in three games is not good enough.

January 2026 saw Amorim leave his position as manager, with his dream turning into a nightmare that was beamed across the world.  

However, away from the intense scrutiny of the Premier League, Amorim has been able to slowly but steadily rebuild his reputation and leading sports analysts Bets.co.za have looked at how it happened.

AC Milan, a side that like United had been hugely successful but have departed Europe’s elite level, came calling. Installed as manager in June of 2026, Amorim’s nearly half a year out of football management was brought to an end by the Serie A club.

This announcement came with some serious scrutiny. While the Premier League is one of the most intensely competitive leagues in the game, thus seeing managers critiqued for every result, performance, substitution and statement, signing with AC Milan would not provide much leeway.

Indeed, over the last 10 years since 2016, Amorim comes in as the 10th manager. Clearly, Milan are looking for the right way forward, but have they found it?

For Amorim, this switch is both a major challenge and a chance at a shared rebirth.

Milan were once one of the great Italian sides, feared in their own league and across Europe. To give some perspective, they currently play in Europe’s secondary competition (the Europa League) and have won one of their four outings.

With the likes of Barcelona, Real Madrid and Bayern Munich still dominating the competition, AC Milan have slipped someway short of the summit of the European game.

For Amorim, two league titles, two league cups and a Portuguese Super Cup during his time with Sporting was a hugely impressive return, and he will be desperate to get back to guiding his side to big trophies.

The one overriding concern for Amorim was his over-reliance on his system. Indeed, it was not only an over-reliance, but it was also Amorim being unwilling or unable to change, and this cost him at United.

With the English side, Amorim stuck rigidly to his formation, which generally featured three defenders. With the ball, he wanted his team to be structured in their play as they utilised wingbacks to keep the width of the pitch. Without the ball, the wingbacks would drop into a five-man defence.

Playing in the Premier League brought real issues for Amorim as flaws in his formation were exposed and he failed to solve these problems.

A two-man midfield saw United continually overrun by opponents choosing to play with three in that area. If Bruno Fernandes was then to drop deep to try to even up this mismatch, it deprived United of their most creative player further up the field.

His refusal to allow players to float around the pitch also saw United become incredibly predictable. While many of the most creative players look to pop up in space across the pitch, designated zones for players meant that it was easy for the opposition to mark United’s players and take them out of the game.

The wrong personnel also hurt Amorim as he tried to make do with a squad that he had not created and therefore did not suit his style of play. This was particularly obvious in their wingbacks struggling to deal with the demands of proving an attacking threat when going forward along with dropping in to make up a back five. They were either missing when United were going forward or leaving huge holes at the back which were exploited.

For the fans, his refusal to change became a reason to want him sacked. Ultimately, he would not change his style regardless of the teams he played against, while he would not tweak his formation or plans even if United were losing and needed a spark to get back into a match, with like-for-like substitutions and uninspiring changes bringing the ire of the fans.  

At AC Milan, Amorim seems to have learnt his lesson.

Flexibility with his formation has been a particular feature of this new Amorim. Indeed, he has employed a back four when needed, with this switching into a back three when in possession and a back five when defending.

There is still the reliance on overloading forward areas of the field with wide men, but if the wingbacks can stretch the pitch and provide more shape in the middle, then this leads to Milan’s creative players having more time and freedom to pick passes.

Of course, having a player like Luka Modric is also key. Modric does not have the legs he once had, but he is still a maestro in possession. His ability to control the tempo of the game or receive the ball under pressure and move it on intelligently is something he did not have at United.

Amorim has also shown an aptitude for change in the middle. As the game evolves, Amorim often brings on players that will look to press and hustle the opposition, which is particularly effective later in the game as players tire.  

This feels like a far cry from the coach that was so married to his system that it cost him his role with Manchester United. Gone is the manager that only made like-for-like substitutions and refused to make decisions based on the game situation.

Sat in fourth in Serie A with 24 points from 11 games, Milan are showing signs that Amorim’s system is working. However, as they are currently sat in 28th in the Europa League, it is not all perfect for Amorim.

While he seems to be cracking the code in Serie A as his side look to compete once again, sides from other European leagues have proved that they can still bypass his tactics and take the points.

Of course, the project is still in its early stages. Time and patience are needed to turn a club around, which is something he did not get at Old Trafford. While he will likely get more leeway with AC Milan, 10 managers in 10 years allude to the fact that while the clock is ticking down slower, it is still ticking nonetheless.

title: Omo Agege attack: ‘Enough is enough’, arrest, prosecute perpetrators – Keyamo tells police
description:

Keyamo, in a statement issued on Monday, d
content:
The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has condemned the killing of four persons in Ughelli, Delta State, following an outbreak of political violence, calling on security agencies to arrest and prosecute those responsible.

Keyamo, in a statement issued on Monday, described the incident in his hometown as disturbing and said several other persons sustained injuries and were receiving treatment.

He expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and wished those injured a speedy recovery.

The minister also condemned the killing of a tricycle operator allegedly by supporters of a political party in Asaba on November 7, 2026, urging law enforcement agencies to investigate both incidents and bring the perpetrators to justice.

“I have been in touch with the top hierarchy of law enforcement agencies in the last one month over the rising wave of political violence and violent rhetoric in Delta State,” he said.

Keyamo lamented that Delta, which had enjoyed relative political peace since 1999, was witnessing a disturbing rise in violence, insisting that political disagreements should not degenerate into killings.

“Since 1999, Delta State has been a relatively peaceful state, politically. Our disagreements have never led to violence and killings. We are all brothers and sisters who went to the same primary, secondary and tertiary institutions, and we all know ourselves and our families so well. There is ABSOLUTELY NO NEED for a descent into violence,” he said.

He also criticised the slogan, “Rig and Die”, allegedly promoted by some political actors in Delta State and elsewhere, describing it as capable of escalating political tension and encouraging violence.

The minister urged those promoting the slogan to reconsider their position, publicly withdraw it and apologise for overheating the political atmosphere.

“Those who have promoted the mantra of ‘Rig and Die’ in Delta State and elsewhere should have a rethink, publicly withdraw it, and apologise for overheating the political temperature in the State and country. As can be seen, anyone can be a victim,” he said.

Keyamo maintained that only law enforcement agencies had the authority to deal with offenders, warning political leaders against encouraging their supporters to attack other citizens.

He described such conduct as a sign of desperation and called on the Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, to urgently address residents and warn those threatening violence.

“I call on our leader and my elder brother, the Governor of Delta State and the Chief Security Officer of the State, Rt. Hon. Elder Sheriff Oborevwori, to urgently address Deltans and read the Riot Act against those who are threatening fire and brimstone.

“Enough is enough,” he said.
