title: 5 Managers Facing The English Premier League Sack
description:
The revolving door for Premier League managers is almost as entertaining and unpredictable as the football itself – and it seems a sacking is around the corner.
Despite all 20 remaining in their position heading into November, there are a number of managers that look to be teetering on the edge.
Lea
content:
The revolving door for Premier League managers is almost as entertaining and unpredictable as the football itself – and it seems a sacking is around the corner.

Despite all 20 remaining in their position heading into November, there are a number of managers that look to be teetering on the edge.

Leading sports betting website Bets.ng have taken a look at the five most likely candidates to be the next Premier League manager to lose their job.

Matthias Jaissle (Newcastle)

Matthias Jaissle is the first name on the chopping blocking list, and it is no wonder why he is one of the favourites to go first.

Nine matches have culminated in three wins, two draws and four defeats. With 11 points in the bank, the Magpies may only be four points short of the European places, but the dull and uninspiring brand of football they are playing is not currently worth the entry fee.

Eddie Howe may not have been the flashiest name, but he was solid. Howe had a clear idea of how he wanted to play.

Making Newcastle tough to beat may not bring them the same sort of press as an all-action plan in which goals come freely would, it did bring them the 2024/25 EFL Cup after a brilliant run in which they beat Liverpool in the final at Wembley.

Fast forward to today, and the Magpies languish in the bottom half of the league after a poor start that has seen them lose to the likes of Leeds, Coventry and Everton.

The Magpies have been toothless across the start of the season, and if there are no major improvement quickly, then Jaissle will likely be looking for work very soon.

Oliver Glasner (Nottingham Forest)

Oliver Glasner left Crystal Palace following a superb run of results that saw him guide his side to the FA Cup at the end of 2025 and the Conference League in 2026.

A run like this tends to see a manager looking for a change after they have seriously overachieved with their side.

However, Glasner’s switch to Nottingham Forest is yet to ignite. One win, three draws and five defeats in nine matches sees Nottingham Forest spared propping up the table by Sunderland’s worse start.

Worrying for Glasner will be Forest’s track record of sacking managers of late. Since Nuno Espirito Santo was dismissed in September of 2025, four managers have come and gone as Forest have failed to find the remedy for their woes.

Finishing five points clear of the relegation zone in the 2025/26 season felt like a very close call, and it seems unlikely that this sort of close call will go down well with the Forest hierarchy once again.

Regis Le Bris (Sunderland)

The 2025/26 Premier League season was one that completely defied expectations for a number of sides, but none more so than Sunderland. A total of 14 wins, 12 draws and 12 defeats saw the Black Cats amass 54 points and qualify for the UEFA Europa League.

However, exceptional results lead to higher expectations.

This season, Sunderland prop up the Premier League table after nine matches. A single win, two draws and six defeats, coupled with just seven goals and 17 conceded has been a recipe for disaster. While the season is still incredibly young, fans will worry that the bubble may have burst.

Their European exploits have included wins over AZ Alkmaar and Torreense preceded a draw with Lech Poznan.

Is Europe to blame for their stuttering start to the season? Sunderland are not blessed with the sort of resources that Manchester City, Arsenal or Liverpool can call upon to compete across fronts, so it is likely a factor.

However, Regis Le Bris is starting to feel the pressure of a poor run of results. While Sunderland’s fans still have faith in him to turn the fortunes of the club around, how long will those in power hold off before pressing the panic button?

Pierre Sage (Crystal Palace)

Pierre Sage’s success at Ligue 1 side Lens saw him come in as the replacement for Oliver Glasner when Crystal Palace’s manager departed for Nottingham Forest.

However, arriving following success in France means little when the start to a new managerial venture comes with as much scrutiny as Sage’s has at Palace.

After nine matches, Palace have won twice, drawn once and lost six times. With nine goals scored and 21 conceded, Palace have one of the lowest returns up front while they have the worst defensive record.

While Palace have lost to Everton and Manchester City in games they were expected to lose, they have also lost to Ipswich, Newcastle and Tottenham, with each of the three teams they could have beaten considering their disappointing records.

The big humiliation came as they were completely played off the pitch by arch-rivals Brighton in a stunning 5-0 loss. While Brighton are enjoying a stunning start to their season, Palace and their fans will not accept a humiliation on this sort of scale from their biggest rivals.

Throw in the fact that Glasner was able to guide Palace to an FA Cup triumph in 2025 and the Conference League crown in 2026, and you have all of the ingredients for a Premier League side that have changed their manager and with this switch, suddenly their exploits on the field have changed drastically.

Michael Carrick (Manchester United)

A single win does not save a manager their job and Michael Carrick will know that he is still very much up against it if he is to still be the man leading Manchester United when the November international break comes to an end.

The bookmakers make Carrick the outright favourite to be the next Premier League manager to go, and there are no prizes for guessing why.

Since their 4-0 win over minnows Sabah in the Champions League on September 10, United have lost to Manchester City, Brighton, Atletico Madrid, Como, Bournemouth and Chelsea. They have also drawn with Fulham, Tottenham and Leeds.

Sat in 17th in the Premier League and 17th in the Champions League, trophies in either of them two biggest competitions in United’s sights seems unlikely.

Does securing a Champions League berth save Carrick’s job? Will winning the FA Cup be enough if United’s league season ends in an underwhelming campaign? Time will tell whether United are looking for their 13th new manager or caretaker manager since Sir Alex Ferguson in 2013, with this weekend’s match against Aston Villa potentially crucial.

The post 5 Managers Facing The English Premier League Sack appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Fani-Kayode denies recall, meets Enikanolaiye
description:
Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has denied reports that he was recalled from his diplomatic posting, saying his visit to Abuja was to brief the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on his activities and consult with officials.







Fani-Kayode spoke on Monday after meeting wi
content:
Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has denied reports that he was recalled from his diplomatic posting, saying his visit to Abuja was to brief the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on his activities and consult with officials.

Fani-Kayode spoke on Monday after meeting with the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Sola Enikanolaiye, at the ministry’s headquarters in Abuja.

He said the meeting was part of his official responsibilities and had nothing to do with reports circulating on social media that he had been recalled.

“There have been reports on social media suggesting that I have been recalled. Those claims are simply untrue.

“If I had been recalled, I doubt I would be standing here smiling after a cordial and productive meeting with the minister,” he said.

The envoy explained that his visit was to submit official reports, consult with ministry officials, spend time with his family and prepare for their possible relocation to South Africa.

He said he had initially planned to spend only a few days in South Africa following his posting but had extended his stay to complete necessary diplomatic procedures.

Fani-Kayode also dismissed reports that his meeting with South Africa’s Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) over the controversy surrounding the omission of his speech during the presentation of his letters of credence to President Cyril Ramaphosa amounted to a reprimand.

He described the engagement as cordial and constructive, saying concerns were addressed professionally by both sides.

“Our engagements with South African authorities have been cordial and constructive. Concerns have been raised on both sides in a professional diplomatic manner, and no reprimand of any kind occurred,” he said.

The high commissioner reaffirmed his commitment to strengthening diplomatic relations between Nigeria and South Africa, particularly in trade, investment and other areas of mutual interest.

“I believe strongly that if South Africa and Nigeria do not come together, it would affect the destiny of the whole African continent. We will do our best to build that bridge, and that bridge must never be broken,” he said.

He, however, stressed that efforts to improve bilateral relations must not come at the expense of Nigeria’s national interests or the dignity, rights and welfare of Nigerians living in South Africa.

Fani-Kayode expressed concern over persistent xenophobic attacks, killings and discriminatory rhetoric targeting Nigerians in the country.

He also condemned attempts to portray Nigerians collectively as criminals and drug dealers, insisting that the actions of a few individuals should not be used to stigmatise an entire community.

“As ambassador, I would be failing in my responsibility if I did not raise concerns about the treatment of Nigerians in South Africa.

“Thousands of Nigerians in South Africa are law-abiding professionals, including doctors, lawyers, academics and entrepreneurs. A small minority engaged in wrongdoing should not be used to define an entire community,” he said.

The envoy pledged to continue raising concerns whenever Nigeria’s dignity and the rights of its citizens abroad were threatened.

title: Tinubu to Lagos Igbo: ‘Vote for me in 2027, I was angry you didn’t vote for me in 2023’
description:
President Bola Tinubu has urged Igbo residents in Lagos to vote for him in the 2027 presidential election, admitting that he was angry with those who did not support his candidacy in the 2023 polls.







Tinubu made the appeal on Monday during a town hall meeting with Igbo youths, elders and commu
content:
President Bola Tinubu has urged Igbo residents in Lagos to vote for him in the 2027 presidential election, admitting that he was angry with those who did not support his candidacy in the 2023 polls.

Tinubu made the appeal on Monday during a town hall meeting with Igbo youths, elders and community leaders at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, National Theatre, Lagos.

The meeting was organised by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiative.

The president, who described the Igbo as his brothers and sisters, said his administration remained committed to inclusive governance, national unity and equity, assuring that no section of the country would be left behind under his Renewed Hope Agenda.

He urged the Igbo community to strengthen its unity, deepen its participation in national politics and collaborate with other ethnic groups to build a peaceful and prosperous Nigeria.

Tinubu also acknowledged the contributions of Igbo communities to the country’s economic growth, while commending the stakeholders for attending the meeting.

Expressing appreciation for their presence, he said: “To all of you, I am grateful for one thing: that you are here this afternoon. You left your businesses, left money-making to come and listen to the president, and I must say thank you.”

He stressed that national development required collective commitment, mutual understanding and cooperation, urging the Igbo community to embrace dialogue and constructive engagement in addressing its challenges and advancing its interests within the Nigerian federation.

Explaining some of his administration’s policies, Tinubu said his government was working to ensure stability in tertiary institutions, improve infrastructure and expand access to education for disadvantaged Nigerians.

“To eliminate the crisis in the universities and to build good roads and the engineers that will maintain our cars, our children must be in school. Just because they are poor doesn’t mean they must not go to university or develop,” he said.

The president said the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) was helping to improve access to higher education, while the government was also providing financial support for agriculture and businesses through relevant intervention programmes.

“We are doing that with NELFUND. The university is stable today because we are doing well. We are putting money into agriculture and trading, and anyone in the trade business can apply to the Bank of Industry and get a loan; anyone in agriculture can take a small farmers’ loan,” he said.

Tinubu, who confirmed his intention to seek re-election, said the Constitution permitted him to serve a second term.

“We have to maintain this country for the sake of every one of us. The critical line in our national anthem is what I’m standing here for. I begged for it, and I am ready to serve.

“And I served the first term. The constitution says I can ask for a second term. I want a second term. As you are here today, you make me happy, you make me excited, and I will go home happy and eat akpu,” he added.

He subsequently appealed to Igbo residents in Lagos to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and support him, Lagos State Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat, the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate, and other party candidates in the 2027 elections.

“I am here to listen to you. I am here to work with you. Igbos are my brothers and sisters.

“Some of you did not vote for me in 2023; I vex o. Now, we have settled. Get your PVC, and you will vote for me this time. Come by January 16; you will vote. Agreement is agreement. Tinubu is APC,” he said.

According to the Independent National Electoral Commission’s election timetable, the presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027.

Tinubu contested the 2023 presidential election on the platform of the APC alongside Peter Obi of the Labour Party and Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party.

However, he lost Lagos State, his political stronghold since 1999, to Obi in the election.

title: US lists 157 Nigerians for deportation over various criminal offences
description:
The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has added 24 more Nigerians to its deportation list, bringing the total number of Nigerians featured on the list to 157.
Very Nigerian gathered from the US DHS website on Monday that the latest additions were arrested over alleged offences incl
content:
The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has added 24 more Nigerians to its deportation list, bringing the total number of Nigerians featured on the list to 157.

Very Nigerian gathered from the US DHS website on Monday that the latest additions were arrested over alleged offences including fraud, money laundering, drug-related crimes, identity theft and child cruelty.

The Nigerians were listed on the department’s *Worst of the Worst* webpage, which features foreign nationals arrested by the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) over serious criminal offences and facing deportation from the country.

The list identifies the individuals by their Nigerian origin and includes offences such as mail fraud, wire fraud, impersonation, forgery, assault and weapons-related crimes.

Those listed include Emmanuel Omowaiye, arrested in Richmond, Texas, over mail fraud; Laurene Onwuka, arrested in Chantilly, Virginia, over fraud by impersonation; and Olusegun Shonekan, arrested in Newark, New Jersey, over wire fraud.

Others are Olusegun Olaseni, arrested in Greencastle, Indiana, over the sale of amphetamine; Peter Ude, arrested in Atlanta, Georgia, over wire fraud; and Newton Jemide, arrested in Fort Dix, New Jersey, over wire fraud, conspiracy and mail fraud.

Also on the list are Shedrack Umukoro, arrested in Yazoo City, Mississippi, over money laundering; Olasoji Akinbode, arrested in Kearny, New Jersey, over fraud by impersonation; and Oluwatosin Afolabi, arrested in Conroe, Texas, over fraud.

The department also listed Alameen Adetunji Tokosi, arrested in Chicago, Illinois, over heroin possession, and Joshua Ipoadе, arrested in Atlanta, Georgia, over wire fraud.

Another Nigerian, Michael Orji, arrested in Oxford, Wisconsin, was listed for weapons-related offences, fraud, identity theft, wire fraud, false citizenship and money laundering.

The second batch of names included Ahmadu Apooyin, arrested in Baltimore, Maryland, over a cocaine-related offence; Teslim Kiriji, arrested in Yazoo City, Mississippi, over money laundering; and Onomen Uduebоr, arrested in Seattle, Washington, over identity theft.

Others were Charles Ochi and Daniel Eta, arrested in White Deer, Pennsylvania, over money laundering and wire fraud, respectively.

Ifeanyi Ibennah, arrested in Tampa, Florida, was listed over cruelty towards a child, while Kazeem Runsewe, arrested in Thomson, Illinois, and Fatiu Lawal, arrested in Lompoc, California, were listed over wire fraud.

The list further included Justin Akubueze, arrested in Orem, Utah, over money laundering; Moyinoluwaseun Okeowo, arrested in Orlando, Florida, over larceny, forgery and concealing stolen property; Babajide Oluwaseun Faseyi, arrested in Alden, New York, over assault; and Bright Eigbedion, arrested in Lompoc, California, over money laundering.

The DHS said the initiative was part of the administration of President Donald Trump’s efforts to remove foreign nationals involved in serious criminal activities from the United States.

The accompanying text read, “The U.S. Department of Homeland Security is fulfilling President Trump’s promise to remove the worst of the worst criminal aliens from the United States.

“This page highlights criminal aliens arrested by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement who are being removed after engaging in serious criminal activity, including drug and weapons offences, violent crimes including rape and murder, fraud, and the misuse or theft of public benefits.”

Meanwhile, the DHS did not state when the listed persons would be deported or their immigration status at the time of filing this report.

Similarly, the publication of the names on the webpage does not, on its own, establish that the individuals have been convicted of the listed offences.

Very Nigerian had reported in September that 134 Nigerians were on the deportation lists, as fraud-related offences and money laundering featured prominently among their offences.

The Nigerians were among foreign nationals identified by the United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement and listed by the Department of Homeland Security in its “Worst of the Worst” register.

The report noted that 10 names were added in August, taking the number of Nigerians on the register to 134, following an earlier list of 124 Nigerians published in July.

content:
President Bola Tinubu has admitted that he was angry that many Igbo residents in Lagos State did not vote for him during the 2023 presidential election.

The President made the disclosure on Monday while addressing youths, elders and leaders of Ndigbo at a town hall meeting held at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, National Theatre, Lagos.

The meeting was organised by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiative.

Tinubu, however, reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to inclusive governance, national unity and fairness, stressing the importance of ensuring that all Nigerians are carried along regardless of their ethnic background.

He urged the Ndigbo to strengthen their unity, deepen their participation in national politics and work with other ethnic groups to build a peaceful, prosperous, and united Nigeria.

Tinubu said his administration recognised the significant contributions of Igbo communities to the country’s economic growth.

He assured them that no section of the country would be left behind under the renewed hope agenda.

He also applauded the stakeholders for attending the meeting.

“To all of you, I am grateful for one thing: that you are here this afternoon. You left your businesses, left money-making to come and listen to the president, and I must say thank you,” Tinubu said.

He noted that national development requires collective commitment, mutual understanding, and cooperation.

He said the Igbo community should embrace dialogue and constructive engagement to address challenges and advance their interests within the Nigerian federation.

Tinubu explained some of the reasons behind his policies, such as ensuring the tertiary schools are no longer paralysed by union strikes.

“To eliminate the crisis in the universities and to build good roads and the engineers that will maintain our cars, our children must be in school. Just because they are poor doesn’t mean they must not go to university or develop,” the president said.

“We are doing that with NELFUND. The university is stable today because we are doing well. We are putting money into agriculture and trading, and anyone in the trade business can apply to the Bank of Industry and get a loan; anyone in agriculture can take a small farmers’ loan.

“We have to maintain this country for the sake of every one of us. The critical line in our national anthem is what I’m standing here for. I begged for it, and I am ready to serve.

“And I served the first term. The constitution says I can ask for a second term. I want a second term. As you are here today, you make me happy, you make me excited, and I will go home happy and eat akpu.”

He also urged Ndigbo residents in Lagos to participate actively and vote for him, Obafemi Hamzat, the APC governorship candidate, and other candidates of the party.

“I am here to listen to you. I am here to work with you. Igbos are my brothers and sisters,” Tinubu said.

“Some of you did not vote for me in 2023; I vex o. Now, we have settled. Get your PVC, and you will vote for me this time. Come by January 16; you will vote. Agreement is agreement. Tinubu is APC.”

According to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) election calendar, the 2027 presidential and national assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027.

BACK STORY

In 2023, Tinubu contested the presidential election as the candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), alongside Peter Obi and Atiku Abubakar, the standard-bearers of the Labour Party (LP) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), respectively.

Tinubu lost Lagos, his home state and political stronghold since 1999, to Obi in the election.

Tinubu also polled just one percent of his total votes in the south-east, Obi’s home region. He secured a total of 127,605 votes across the five states but failed to score 25 percent in any of them.

Tinubu recorded his lowest votes nationwide in Enugu state (4,772), followed by Anambra (5,111), Abia (8,914), Ebonyi (42,402), Bayelsa (42,572) and Imo (66,406).

He won only one zone in the south — the south-west — but came second in the south-south and south-east. He polled 799,957 votes in the south-south, accounting for nine percent of his total votes.

title: Fani-Kayode meets foreign affairs minister, denies recall rumours
description:
Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has briefed the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Sola Enikanolaiye, on his activities since assuming his diplomatic appointment.
Fani-Kayode met with Enikanolaiye at the Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs headquarters in Abuja on
content:
Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has briefed the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Sola Enikanolaiye, on his activities since assuming his diplomatic appointment.

Fani-Kayode met with Enikanolaiye at the Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs headquarters in Abuja on Monday.

During the meeting, the former Minister of Aviation dismissed reports suggesting that his visit to the ministry was connected to a possible recall from his diplomatic posting in South Africa.

“There have been reports on social media suggesting that I have been recalled. Those claims are simply untrue,” he said.

“If I had been recalled, I doubt I would be standing here smiling after a cordial and productive meeting with the minister,” he added.

Fani-Kayode said the purpose of his visit was to submit official reports, consult with ministry officials, spend time with his family and prepare for their possible relocation to South Africa.

He said he had initially planned to spend a few days in South Africa after his posting but noted that his stay had been extended to allow for the completion of official diplomatic procedures.

The high commissioner also said his meeting with South Africa’s department of international relations and cooperation (DIRCO) over the row triggered by the omission of his speech during the presentation of his letters of credence to President Cyril Ramaphosa was not a reprimand, contrary to reports on social media.

“Our engagements with South African authorities have been cordial and constructive. Concerns have been raised on both sides in a professional diplomatic manner, and no reprimand of any kind occurred,” he said.

Fani-Kayode said he was committed to strengthening diplomatic relations, promoting mutually beneficial trade and investment opportunities, and deepening cooperation between Nigeria and South Africa.

“I believe strongly that if South Africa and Nigeria do not come together, it would affect the destiny of the whole African continent. We will do our best to build that bridge, and that bridge must never be broken,” he said.

Fani-Kayode, however, noted that strengthening bilateral relations must go hand in hand with the protecting Nigeria’s national interests and the dignity, rights and welfare of Nigerians living in South Africa.

He expressed concern over persistent xenophobic attacks, killings and discriminatory rhetoric against Nigerians in South Africa.

He also condemned attempts to collectively label Nigerians as criminals and drug dealers.

“As ambassador, I would be failing in my responsibility if I did not raise concerns about the treatment of Nigerians in South Africa,” he said.

“Thousands of Nigerians in South Africa are law-abiding professionals, including doctors, lawyers, academics and entrepreneurs. A small minority engaged in wrongdoing should not be used to define an entire community.”

The envoy said he would continue to speak out whenever the country’s dignity and the rights of its citizens are threatened.

content:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Presidential Campaign Council has denied reports of a disagreement between its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and the party over campaign funding.

In a statement issued on Monday, the spokesperson for the NDC Campaign Council, Constance Ikokwu, said reports suggesting a disagreement between the party and its candidate were false

The party insisted that both sides remained united ahead of the 2027 general election, describing winning the election as an already done deal.

According to the statement, the party said Obi had neither complained about inadequate campaign funds nor expressed dissatisfaction with how it handled campaign finances.

It described reports of a rift as an attempt to divide the opposition camp.

She said, “Let me state categorically that Peter Obi has not complained about a lack of campaign funds or expressed any dissatisfaction with the party over funding.”

Ikokwu maintained that Obi remained committed to the campaign, adding that his nationwide engagements demonstrated his determination to secure victory in the 2027 election.

“Let’s be clear – no presidential candidate in this race is campaigning with the energy, consistency and intensity that Obi is bringing to this election. His commitment to reaching Nigerians across the country is there for all to see, and he’s doing that superbly. The campaign so far is a resounding success,” she said.

She urged Nigerians to disregard what she described as manufactured controversies, insisting that the party and its candidate were focused on winning the election.

“The relationship between the party and its presidential candidate remains focused on one overriding objective: winning the 2027 presidential election and offering Nigerians a credible alternative. Those attempting to engineer a needless quarrel should not mistake their wishful thinking for reality. We are united, focused and determined,” Ikokwu added.

The clarification comes amid growing concerns over the control and management of campaign donations following a fundraising initiative launched by activist Aisha Yesufu for Obi’s presidential bid.

title: Obi breaks silence, demands justice after attack kills four NDC supporters in Delta
description:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has called for a thorough investigation into the killing of four party supporters during a political gathering in Delta State.
Obi condemned the attack, describing it as a senseless act of violence, and urged security ag
content:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has called for a thorough investigation into the killing of four party supporters during a political gathering in Delta State.

Obi condemned the attack, describing it as a senseless act of violence, and urged security agencies to identify and prosecute everyone involved, including those who may have sponsored the incident.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, the former Anambra State governor disclosed that 15 other NDC supporters sustained serious injuries during the attack in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.

He called on the relevant authorities to ensure that those responsible are brought to justice.

He identified the deceased as Moses Anaughe, a former Federal Commissioner of the Federal Character Commission; Akima Efenena Umukoro, a former President of the Urhobo Progress Union Youth Wing; and Nyoren Okoro, an NDC chieftain.

He said the identity of the fourth victim had yet to be established.

Among those injured were Evance Ivwurie, Chairman of Senator Ovie Omo-Agege’s Campaign Organisation, and Chuks Erhire, its Director-General.

Obi, who expressed condolences to the families of the deceased, said, “I offer my deepest condolences to the families of those who died and pray for a swift recovery for the injured.”

He urged security agencies to “conduct a comprehensive investigation, identify those responsible and their sponsors, and ensure they face justice.”

The former governor also called on the authorities to take immediate steps to protect Nigerians participating in political activities.

He said, “Every Nigerian has a constitutional right to support any political party or candidate without fear of intimidation or violence.”

Expressing concern over the escalation of political hostility, Obi said it was no longer enough for those behind attacks on opposition supporters to spread false claims against them.

“It is no longer sufficient for those responsible to fund the dissemination of false claims against the opposition. They have now escalated to the appalling practice of murdering innocent Nigerians solely because of their political affiliations. This is completely unacceptable,” he said.

He added that political disagreements should not result in violence, insisting that elections and persuasion remained the legitimate ways to resolve political differences.

“Political differences must be resolved through persuasion and the ballot, never through the use of bullets. No political ambition is worth the life of even one Nigerian,” Obi said.

The attack occurred in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, during a political gathering involving Omo-Agege, the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central.

Omo-Agege had alleged that the attackers repeatedly called his name and threatened to kill him during the incident. He said he escaped through the intervention of his security escorts.

Following the violence, the Delta State Government imposed a 12-hour curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area to prevent further breakdown of law and order.

The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, also condemned the political violence, warning that the “Rig and Die” slogan was contributing to tension in the state.

He called on those promoting the slogan to publicly withdraw it and apologise.

title: It was an attempt on my life — Omo-Agege
description:
Senator Omo-Agege, has alleged that the attack on his campaign train in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State was “premeditated”, saying it was part of an ongoing attempt to eliminate him.







Speaking on Channels TV via Zoom, Omo-Agege said four members of his campaign organisation
content:
Senator Omo-Agege, has alleged that the attack on his campaign train in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State was “premeditated”, saying it was part of an ongoing attempt to eliminate him.

Speaking on Channels TV via Zoom, Omo-Agege said four members of his campaign organisation were killed, while about 15 others were critically injured when gunmen opened fire during his campaign event in Udu-Ere, Ughelli North.

He said he was addressing supporters when the gunmen opened fire, adding that he heard them repeatedly shouting that they wanted to kill him.

He said he survived the attack through the intervention of his Department of State Services, DSS, security details.
He said the attack occurred less than five minutes after he began his remarks at the campaign venue.


His words: “This is premeditated. It is not something that just happened today. I just gave you the buildup. This thing has been going on.

“As I was speaking, I just moved over to the side of a vehicle to be able to make eye contact with those I was speaking with. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started. The former Deputy Senate President said four members of his campaign organisation were killed in the attack, including former Federal Character Commissioner, and the immediate past president of the Urhobo Progress Union youth wing.

The former senator said he heard the attackers shouting in English, “Omo-Agege, we want to kill,” while the shooting was ongoing.

Omo-Agege called on the Inspector-General of Police to take over the investigation, saying he did not expect the Delta State Police Command to deliver justice.

“We are appealing to the IGP to step in immediately and directly handle this investigation. We need justice,” he said.


We need justice. We need justice for these four people who have been killed. We need justice for the 15 people who are critically injured and hospitalised right now,” he said.

He also appealed to his supporters not to retaliate, saying the attack would not deter him from continuing his campaign.


“If the idea is that this is supposed to deter me from going forward with the campaigns, it’s a very, very big mistake and a big lie. It ain’t going to happen,” Omo-Agege said.

The post It was an attempt on my life — Omo-Agege appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Police arrest eight suspected drug dealers in Jigawa
description:
By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse



The Jigawa State Police Command has arrested eight suspected drug dealers and consumers, including two women aged 18 and 20, during operations targeting illicit drug trafficking and substance abuse across the state.







The arrests were disclosed in a statement issued
content:
By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse

The Jigawa State Police Command has arrested eight suspected drug dealers and consumers, including two women aged 18 and 20, during operations targeting illicit drug trafficking and substance abuse across the state.

The arrests were disclosed in a statement issued to newsmen by the Police Public Relations Officer, SP Shiisu Lawan Adam.

Adam identified the suspects as Garba Sabo, 20; Kamal Ibrahim, 20; Muhammad Ibrahim, 25; Muhammad Nura, 25; Muhammad Bako, 25; Habu Usman, 23, also known as Makwa; Firdausi Sani, 20; and Nusaiba Ibrahim, 18.

According to the statement, the suspects, aged between 18 and 25, were arrested at different locations, including Gadama, Bulangu, Sara, Gumel and Kazaure towns. One of the female suspects was identified as a resident of Sandamu Daura in Katsina State.

During the operations, the police recovered 8,739 assorted illicit drug-related substances, including suspected Indian hemp, tramadol, pregabalin, diazepam and other intoxicating substances.

The recovered exhibits included 4,035 pieces of Exol, 1,384 pieces of D5, 634 pregabalin capsules, 896 tramadol capsules, 248 diazepam tablets and 1,199 wraps of marijuana, alongside three and a half blocks of the substance.

Other items recovered included rubber solution, whisky, shisha, syrups, snuff and other intoxicating substances.

The Commissioner of Police, CP Tijjani Murtala, said the command would sustain its operations against drug trafficking and substance abuse, warning those involved in the illicit trade to desist or face prosecution.

He said the police would continue to deploy intelligence-led policing, surveillance and targeted operations to dismantle drug distribution networks and tackle criminal activities associated with substance abuse.

The commissioner also called on parents, guardians, community leaders and religious institutions to intensify efforts to discourage drug abuse, particularly among young people.

He urged members of the public to support the police in the fight against drug-related activities across the state.

title: Mastercard and SMEDAN convene MSME Growth Forum and sign MoU to advance SME digitization in Nigeria
description:
Government leaders, financial institutions and entrepreneurs gather to explore payments, credit and digital capabilities for Nigerian SMEs as Mastercard and SMEDAN sign an MoU to explore opportunities to support MSME digitization and growth.

Mastercard and the Small and Medium Enterprises Developme
content:
• Government leaders, financial institutions and entrepreneurs gather to explore payments, credit and digital capabilities for Nigerian SMEs as Mastercard and SMEDAN sign an MoU to explore opportunities to support MSME digitization and growth.

Mastercard and the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria (SMEDAN) convened entrepreneurs, financial institutions, policymakers and ecosystem partners at the SMEDAN MSME Growth Forum to explore the practical tools, collaborations and capabilities Nigerian small businesses need to grow in the digital age.

The collaboration builds on the Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment’s support for the design and piloting of a national MSME Digitization Programme, which aligns with the Government’s priorities for advancing Nigeria’s digital economy and supporting SME development.

Through the MoU, Mastercard and SMEDAN will explore opportunities to collaborate on initiatives that support MSME digitization and growth. Together, the organizations aim to support Nigerian SMEs adopt digital tools, improve operational efficiency and participate more fully in the formal economy.

Tara Nathan, executive vice president, Growth Segments, Mastercard, said: “Small businesses are the engine of economic growth, job creation and innovation, but many entrepreneurs continue to face barriers to digitization, skills development and access to finance. Through the framework established by this MoU, Mastercard and SMEDAN will explore opportunities to support Nigerian entrepreneurs as they build stronger and more resilient businesses. By equipping SMEs with the tools, capabilities and connections they need to participate in the digital economy, we are unlocking new opportunities for growth, productivity and long-term success”

Charles Odii, director general, SMEDAN, said: “Nigerian entrepreneurs need more than encouragement to digitize. They need practical tools, skills and support that fit the realities of running a small business. Our collaboration with Mastercard creates a framework for bringing these capabilities closer to the businesses that need them, while coordinating engagement with government and ecosystem partners.”

Kari Tukur, country manager, West Africa, Mastercard, said: “SMEs are central to Nigeria’s economic future, and supporting their growth requires more than access to funding alone. Business owners increasingly need digital payment capabilities, practical skills, market access and trusted partners to help them grow sustainably. The MSME Growth Forum was designed to bring these conversations and solutions together, while our collaboration with SMEDAN reinforces our long-term commitment to helping Nigerian entrepreneurs participate and succeed in an increasingly digital economy.”

The forum featured a keynote address from Nathan, who also joined Aisha Rimi, Executive Secretary and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Investment Promotion Commission (NIPC) for a fireside discussion titled “Informal to Inclusive: Payments, Policy and the Path for Nigeria’s Small Businesses.”

This was followed by a panel discussion titled “Beyond Credit: The Solutions Nigerian SMEs Need to Grow and Scale” featuring representatives from Access Bank, Wema Bank, AFEX and SMEDAN, moderated by Kari Tukur, country manager, West Africa, Mastercard.

The two engagements explored how public-private collaboration, digital payments and enabling policy frameworks can help informal businesses transition into the formal economy, improve resilience and access new growth opportunities; while also examining the practical barriers facing Nigerian entrepreneurs, highlighting the need for a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond access to credit.

Small business attendees also took part in practical masterclasses designed to build business and digital capabilities. Sessions covered digital marketing strategies to help SMEs attract and retain customers online, as well as solutions supporting entrepreneurs across key sectors, including agriculture, enabling them to improve productivity, expand market access and build more sustainable businesses.

The collaboration comes as Nigerian entrepreneurs increasingly identify digital capabilities, skills and finance as essential to growth. According to Mastercard’s 2026 SME Confidence Index, 100% of Nigerian SMEs surveyed consider digital and online payments vital to growing their businesses, while 78% identify digitizing their business as a key priority, 79% prioritize training and upskilling staff, and 69% are seeking credit to expand.

The forum reflects Mastercard and SMEDAN’s shared interest in exploring opportunities to support the competitiveness of Nigerian SMEs through innovation, capability building and collaboration. By aiming to bring together policymakers, financial institutions, business leaders and entrepreneurs, the initiative seeks to create practical pathways for small businesses to participate more fully in Nigeria’s digital economy.

                                                                             

About Mastercard

Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re building a resilient economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential.

www.mastercard.com

 

About SMEDAN

The Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria (SMEDAN) is the Federal Government agency that drives the growth of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) across the country. SMEDAN works as a one-stop shop for MSME development and gives business owners access to knowledge, finance, tools and markets. Its work spans policy formulation and advocacy, capacity building, specialised funding schemes, market linkages, research, and the promotion of entrepreneurship. It works alongside government agencies, development partners and private sector stakeholders to build an ecosystem in which Nigerian entrepreneurs can prosper. Led by Director General/CEO Charles Odii, SMEDAN has its headquarters in Abuja and offices in all six geopolitical zones. For more information, visit www.smedan.gov.ng.

 

The post Mastercard and SMEDAN convene MSME Growth Forum and sign MoU to advance SME digitization in Nigeria appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

The ceremony was held on Sunday at the Eko Convention Centre, with political leaders, family members and other prominent personalities in atte
content:
Wuraola, daughter of the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, has married her partner, Wasem Yaji, at a traditional wedding ceremony in Lagos.

The ceremony was held on Sunday at the Eko Convention Centre, with political leaders, family members and other prominent personalities in attendance.

Photographs from the event showed the couple dressed in traditional outfits, posing together and with guests, while Alake was seen receiving and greeting attendees.

Among the dignitaries at the wedding were the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila; Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu; his deputy, Obafemi Hamzat; and Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun.

Other governors present included Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo State, Biodun Oyebanji of Ekiti State, Babagana Zulum of Borno State, Uba Sani of Kaduna State and Hope Uzodimma of Imo State.

Former Ogun State Governor, Gbenga Daniel; former Ekiti State Governor, Niyi Adebayo; and Deputy President of the Senate, Barau Jibrin, also attended.

Others included former Minister of Defence and ex-Governor of Jigawa State, Abubakar Badaru; Executive Chairman of the Nigeria Revenue Service, Zacch Adedeji; Lagos State Commissioner for the Environment, Tokunbo Wahab; and Chairman of the Nigerians in Diaspora Commission, Abike Dabiri-Erewa.

Wasem Yaji is the son of the late Nigerian engineer, Aloysius Ahile Yaji.

title: The Blood of Four Nigerians: Who will answer for the attack on Omo-Agege, NDC supporters in Ughelli?
description: At least four persons have been feared dead after gunmen opened fire on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) campaign team accompanying former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, during a campaign visit to Uduere Community in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta Stat
content:
At least four persons have been feared dead after gunmen opened fire on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) campaign team accompanying former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, during a campaign visit to Uduere Community in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.

The incident, which occurred during a political campaign ahead of the 2027 general elections, also left several people injured, including a former member of the Delta State House of Assembly, Chief Evans Ivwurie, who was reportedly battling for his life alongside other victims receiving medical attention.

Among those reportedly killed was Moses Anaughe, a former Commissioner of the Federal Character Commission and aide to Omo-Agege.

Another victim, identified as Akima Umukoro, popularly known as Akhima, was also reported dead.

Omo-Agege, who is contesting the Delta Central Senatorial District seat under the NDC in the 2027 National Assembly elections, described the incident as a premeditated assassination attempt against him.

However, the Ughelli North Local Government Chairman, Olorogun Jaro Egbo, rejected the allegation, accusing members of Omo-Agege’s entourage of opening fire on his supporters.

The two camps have continued to trade accusations over the circumstances surrounding the violence, while the Delta State Police Command says investigations have commenced to establish what happened and identify those responsible.

Omo-Agege’s Camp Alleges Assassination Attempt

In a statement issued by his Media Adviser, Sunny Areh, Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation condemned the attack, alleging that armed men opened fire on the senator and members of his entourage at close range during what it described as a peaceful campaign visit.

The organisation claimed that Omo-Agege narrowly escaped death when bullets reportedly passed close to his head while he was addressing supporters.

It identified four people, including two of its aides, Moses Anaughe and Akima Umukoro, as among those killed in the incident.

The campaign organisation also listed Chief Evans Ivwurie, Chuks Erhire, Tobore Agba and Ayodo Wanogho among those who sustained gunshot injuries.

According to the statement, the victims were shot at close range and were receiving medical attention.

The organisation further alleged that eyewitnesses identified Egbo as the person leading the attackers.

It described the incident as a targeted attempt to assassinate Omo-Agege, insisting that it was neither a misunderstanding nor a clash between rival groups.

The campaign organisation called on Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, to condemn the attack and ensure that those allegedly responsible were arrested and investigated.

It also appealed to the Inspector-General of Police to take over the investigation, expressing concerns about the handling of the incident by the Delta State Police Command.

The group, however, urged its supporters not to retaliate or take the law into their hands, insisting that the attack would not prevent it from participating in the 2027 elections.

Egbo Denies Allegations, Accuses Omo-Agege’s Supporters

But Egbo dismissed the allegations against him, offering a different account of how the confrontation started.

According to the council chairman, his supporters had visited the community ahead of an event he was scheduled to host when they learnt that Omo-Agege’s team intended to use the same community hall.

He claimed that his group had already booked the facility and that disagreements arose after members of the NDC entourage allegedly refused to use another location.

Egbo further alleged that his supporters had received intelligence that armed men, including individuals allegedly carrying AK-47 rifles, had been brought into the area from Sapele and Ughelli.

He said he contacted the Area Commander, the Divisional Police Officer and the military to ensure that security was maintained.

The council chairman claimed that despite efforts to prevent a confrontation, members of Omo-Agege’s entourage opened fire on his supporters as the senator was leaving the community.

He alleged that three of his supporters were killed, while others sustained critical injuries.

Egbo also accused Omo-Agege of being responsible for the violence, referencing the senator’s reported political slogan, “Rig & Die”.

However, these allegations have not been independently established, and the police say investigations are ongoing.

Omo-Agege Says Attack Was Premeditated

Speaking during an interview on Channels Television via Zoom, Omo-Agege described the incident as a premeditated attempt on his life, claiming that it was part of an ongoing plot to eliminate him.

The former Deputy Senate President said four members of his campaign organisation were killed, while about 15 others sustained serious injuries.

He explained that he was addressing supporters when gunmen suddenly opened fire, adding that he heard some of the attackers shouting that they wanted to kill him.

According to him, he survived because of the intervention of his Department of State Services (DSS) security personnel.

Omo-Agege said the shooting started less than five minutes after he began speaking at the campaign venue.

He said: “This is premeditated. It is not something that just happened today. I just gave you the buildup. This thing has been going on.

“As I was speaking, I just moved over to the side of a vehicle to be able to make eye contact with those I was speaking with. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started.”

He appealed to the Inspector-General of Police to take over the investigation, saying he had concerns about whether the state police command could deliver justice.

The senator also appealed to his supporters not to retaliate, insisting that the attack would not stop him from continuing his campaign.

“If the idea is that this is supposed to deter me from going forward with the campaigns, it’s a very, very big mistake and a big lie. It ain’t going to happen,” he said.

Delta Government Imposes Curfew

Following the incident, the Delta State Government imposed a curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area to prevent further violence and restore calm.

The restriction, which took effect on the day of the incident, runs from 6pm to 6am daily until further notice.

The Secretary to the State Government, Dr Kingsley Emu, announced the directive in a statement, urging residents to comply with the restriction.

The government said the measure was necessary to bring the security situation under control following reports of gunshots and deaths in parts of the local government area.

Police Begin Investigation, Warn Political Actors

The Delta State Police Command condemned the violence and said it had commenced investigations to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident.

The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bright Edafe, said Commissioner of Police Samuel Erale had directed intensified security operations in the affected area to prevent further violence and maintain law and order.

The police also urged residents to remain calm, cooperate with security personnel and comply with the curfew.

The Commissioner of Police reportedly ordered a full-scale investigation, assuring residents that anyone found culpable would face the law, irrespective of political affiliation or status.

He also warned politicians and their supporters against thuggery, intimidation and the unlawful use of firearms, stressing that political differences should not result in loss of lives.

However, in a separate account contained in the report, Edafe was also quoted as saying that the command was yet to receive an official report of the incident, despite claims that the Ughelli Area Commander was at the hospital where some of the victims were taken.

NDC Accuses APC of Attacking Its Members

The national leadership of the NDC also condemned the attack, accusing suspected agents of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of being responsible.

In a statement issued by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, the party alleged that the attack was part of repeated attempts to intimidate its members and supporters in Delta State.

The party claimed that four people had been killed, including a close aide to Omo-Agege, while several others sustained injuries.

It described the incident as an attempt to silence opposition voices and discourage its members from participating in the democratic process.

The NDC called on the Nigeria Police Force and other security agencies to investigate the incident, arrest those responsible and identify anyone who may have sponsored the attack.

It also expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and wished the injured a speedy recovery.

The APC, however, rejected the accusations and accused the NDC of instigating the violence, claiming that three of its members were among those killed.

Third Major Political Violence Incident in Delta

The Uduere attack is the latest in a series of violent incidents linked to political activities in Delta State ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The first major incident occurred during a political procession in the Warri-Effurun axis on September 18, when supporters of rival political interests clashed. The incident reportedly involved allegations of armed violence, with an AK-47 rifle said to have been recovered afterwards.

Another violent confrontation occurred during a political procession in Asaba on November 7, involving supporters of the NDC and the Obedient Movement. The incident left one person dead and several others injured.

The police had said they received intelligence about the planned procession and advised against a road march. Political actors subsequently traded accusations over responsibility for the violence.

With the latest incident in Ughelli North, concerns have continued to grow over the safety of political campaigns and the possibility of further confrontations as the 2027 elections approach.

The conflicting accounts from the NDC and the APC, the disputed casualty figures and the allegations of an assassination attempt have placed pressure on security agencies to establish what actually happened.

For now, the police investigation, the identities of those responsible and the circumstances that led to the deadly shooting remain central to the search for justice.

As political activities intensify, the latest bloodshed serves as another reminder that electoral competition must not become a justification for violence, intimidation or the loss of innocent lives.

The post The Blood of Four Nigerians: Who will answer for the attack on Omo-Agege, NDC supporters in Ughelli? appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Troops Kill Two Bandits, Recover AK-47 Riffles In Kogi Forest
description: Troops of the Nigerian Army said they have killed two bandits and recovered weapons and other items during an operation in Asungwe Forest, Okehi Local Government Area of Kogi State.A statement by the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Appolonia Anele, released on Tuesday, noted that the ambush
content:
Troops of the Nigerian Army said they have killed two bandits and recovered weapons and other items during an operation in Asungwe Forest, Okehi Local Government Area of Kogi State.

A statement by the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Appolonia Anele, released on Tuesday, noted that the ambush conducted on Monday by troops of 12 Brigade under Operation BEM HEMBE, in conjunction with Other Hybrid Forces, followed credible intelligence obtained from previously arrested bandits.

“The intelligence provided actionable leads on the movement of criminal elements operating within Asungwe Forest and adjoining communities along the Kogi, Edo and Ondo states’ boundaries.

“Acting swiftly on the intelligence, troops deployed from Patrol Base Kabba and strategically positioned themselves along a suspected bandits’ crossing route within the forest.

“The troops made contact with the criminals and engaged them with superior firepower, neutralising two bandits while others fled in disarray”, the statement read in part.

During exploitation of the area, troops said they recovered two AK-47 rifles, three magazines, 27 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition, two Android phones, three Tecno keypad phones, assorted drugs and bags suspected to belong to the fleeing criminals.

“The successful operation further demonstrates the Nigerian Army’s sustained resolve to dismantle criminal networks, disrupt bandits’ movements and deny terrorists and kidnappers freedom of action across vulnerable communities.”

The Nigerian Army said it remained committed to intensifying intelligence-driven operations and sustaining pressure on criminal elements to enhance the security of lives and property.

Members of the public were also encouraged to continue providing credible and timely information to security agencies to support ongoing operations against criminality.

title: INEC not anticipating technical glitches in 2027 — Abia REC
description:
…Says commission building ICT facility, procuring equipment to prevent glitches



…Gives Abia’s total registered voters as 2.62m



…Explains why INEC relies on federal university VCs for collation, returning officers



…Rules out owing ad-hoc staff allowances



By Steve Oko



The Independent Na
content:
…Says commission building ICT facility, procuring equipment to prevent glitches

…Gives Abia’s total registered voters as 2.62m

…Explains why INEC relies on federal university VCs for collation, returning officers

…Rules out owing ad-hoc staff allowances

By Steve Oko

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has assured voters in Abia State that their votes will count in the 2027 general elections, declaring that the commission is putting necessary measures in place to deliver a free, fair, credible and seamless exercise.

The Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Abia State, Professor Sylvia Uchenna Agu, gave the assurance in an exclusive interview with Vanguard, disclosing that the commission had commenced the receipt of non-sensitive election materials, including generators and brand-new Hilux vans, from its headquarters in Abuja.

Agu, who assumed office in April, also spoke on the commission’s efforts to address infrastructural deficiencies at its Abia office, prevent a recurrence of the electronic transmission controversy, popularly known as the ‘technical glitch’, during the 2023 presidential election, ensure credible recruitment of ad-hoc personnel and improve election logistics.

She disclosed that Abia’s voter register had increased from 2,180,140 in 2023 to 2,620,151, following the registration of 460,011 additional voters in the last Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise.

The REC also explained why INEC relies heavily on federal universities in recruiting collation and returning officers, defended the commission’s use of other categories of ad-hoc personnel and urged eligible voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs).

Excerpts:

The 2027 general elections are approaching. How prepared is INEC in Abia State for the exercise?

We are very much prepared. By the grace of God, we are still receiving our non-sensitive election materials. We have received generators, vehicles and other materials. For the first time, we have received brand-new Hilux vans, and more vehicles are expected in the coming days.

Preparations are on top gear. On a weekly basis, we receive materials from Abuja, and the commission is making every effort to ensure that we deliver a seamless election. I can assure you that we are working towards a very successful election in 2027.

You mentioned receiving new vehicles and other materials. But what is the state of your operational facilities in Abia, particularly your ICT infrastructure, which is critical to election management?

When I assumed office in April, I was not impressed with what I saw. The condition of the facility was not encouraging. Sensitive materials, including result sheets for the local government areas, were packed in Ghana-Must-Go bags. There were no proper cabinets for storing them.

I was equally concerned that there was no dedicated ICT building. The ICT Department was sharing an office with the Operations Department, which was not conducive to the effective handling of our Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) machines. The BVAS machines occupied the strong room meant for the Operations Department, while the Operations materials were squeezed into a corner.

I immediately travelled to Abuja and met the National Chairman of INEC, Professor Joash Amupitan. I explained what I had seen, but he initially found it difficult to believe.

However, what he did afterwards was quite remarkable. He immediately dispatched a fact-finding team to Abia to verify my claims. He wanted to establish whether we truly had no dedicated ICT building, whether our result sheets were stored in Ghana-Must-Go bags and whether the ICT and Operations Departments were sharing the same office.

The next day, he sent the Estate and Works Department to inspect the facility. I was still in Abuja when I received a call that the officials had arrived. I instructed my staff to show them everything without hiding anything because I was in Abuja to address the same problems.

What has changed since then?

Following the inspection, plans were drawn for an ICT building, and construction is ongoing. Work is progressing day and night, and we hope to commission the facility in the first week of December.

We have also received 17 cabinets meant for the 17 local government areas to ensure proper storage of sensitive election materials.

The cabinets are already in our stores. We are waiting for the ICT building to be completed so that we can move the relevant materials there and allow the Operations Department to reclaim its office.

So, significant improvements are taking place, and I appreciate the National Chairman for responding promptly to our concerns.

Electronic transmission of election results remains a major issue of public concern, particularly following the technical glitch that marred the uploading of presidential election results in 2023. What has INEC done to prevent a recurrence in 2027?

In 2023, the BVAS worked, but unfortunately, we experienced a technical glitch that affected the uploading of the presidential election results.

We were supposed to upload the results to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), but we could not do so because of the glitch. It was unfortunate.

What assurances can you give Nigerians that there will be no such technical problem in 2027?

We are not anticipating any glitch in 2027. We have held several meetings to ensure that whatever caused the problem is addressed and nipped in the bud. By the grace of God, I trust that there will not be a recurrence.

Some Nigerians have lost confidence in INEC following the controversies surrounding previous elections. Some have even vowed never to vote again because they believe their votes will not count. Has the commission done enough to restore public confidence?

I would be surprised if Abia voters expressed such sentiments because, in 2023, votes counted in Abia, and in 2027, they will count again. We are determined to ensure that the electoral process is credible and that the will of the people prevails.

The Labour Party’s presidential candidate in 2023, Peter Obi, has consistently maintained that he won the presidential election but that his mandate was stolen. Has INEC addressed the issues he raised, particularly concerning the electronic transmission of results?

By the grace of God, we have addressed the problem that resulted in the technical glitch. We are working to ensure that such a situation does not arise again.

There have been persistent allegations of compromise against some ad-hoc election personnel, particularly university-based collation and returning officers. What measures has INEC put in place to ensure that only credible persons are recruited for the 2027 elections?

You know that INEC usually recruits university personnel, and we believe they are people of integrity. We normally approach the vice-chancellors of federal universities in the relevant environments and ask them to nominate men and women of substance who will not compromise when deployed for election duties.

We rely on the integrity of the vice-chancellors to give us credible personnel.

So, INEC actually involves vice-chancellors in the recruitment of ad-hoc staff?

Yes. We engage the vice-chancellors, who send the names directly to our headquarters in Abuja. Our responsibility thereafter is to train those selected.

We normally use federal universities rather than state universities.

Why does INEC prefer federal universities?

Because it is a Federal Government arrangement.

Why not also involve university-based associations such as the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) and the Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU) in the recruitment process?

I know the vice-chancellor is the figurehead of the university. However, I can also speak from personal experience.

Before my present assignment, when I was a lecturer in the university, I was selected to work for INEC during the 2019 elections. In my case, it was ASUU that selected me, not the vice-chancellor.

So, different arrangements may apply, but INEC works with the university authorities.

Given the criticisms and allegations against some university personnel used as ad-hoc staff, should INEC not consider involving other professional bodies, such as the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Nigerian Medical Association (NMA) and Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), to nominate credible members for election duties?

It is important to understand how INEC’s ad-hoc staffing arrangement works. It is not only university lecturers who work for the commission during elections.

We recruit different categories of personnel, including corps members and civil servants.

We have Assistant Presiding Officers (APOs), Supervisory Presiding Officers (SPOs), collation officers and returning officers, among others.

The APOs are usually corps members, penultimate-year university students or recent graduates. The supervisory personnel are also drawn from various government establishments and other eligible applicants.

The university personnel we primarily rely on are those serving as collation and returning officers.

Remember that the results are generated at the polling units by the personnel in the field before being taken to the collation officers. So, if there is any error or compromise, we must also examine what happens at the polling unit level.

I am not trying to exonerate university lecturers, but it is important to understand that collation officers work with the results brought to them from the field.

We have mechanisms to check possible compromise. One of them is the IReV portal, which allows members of the public to access uploaded polling unit results and monitor the process.

Once we conclude the process at the polling units, the results are uploaded. Anybody can access the IReV portal and follow the uploads.

That is one of the mechanisms designed to check electoral malpractice and enhance transparency.

Can Nigerians, therefore, trust INEC to deliver a credible election in 2027?

Emphatically, yes!

There have also been complaints in previous elections about delayed payment of allowances to ad-hoc personnel, sometimes resulting in protests. What is INEC doing to prevent such incidents in 2027?

Where I worked before, in Imo State, I am sure you did not hear such complaints. I can speak confidently about my experience there.

You will not hear such complaints in Abia because we have never owed our ad-hoc personnel.

How much do we pay them that we would want to owe them? Immediately after the election, we transfer their allowances directly to their bank accounts.

The only challenge we may encounter is where an Electoral Officer (EO) recruits somebody who subsequently provides bank account details different from the ones submitted during registration.

Remember that the EOs recruit personnel from their respective local government areas. Applicants indicate their local governments and states during registration, and they are generally deployed within those areas.

But as far as payment of allowances is concerned, we do not owe our workers.

Are you anticipating any major challenges in the 2027 elections in Abia?

At the moment, I am not anticipating any major challenge. By the grace of God, I am looking forward to a seamless election.

Are you carrying political parties and other critical stakeholders along in your preparations?

Yes, we are.

Have you held meetings with the political parties?

Yes. I have held a meeting with the Inter-Party Advisory Council (IPAC).

I also directed the leadership to invite all the political parties because we need to engage them collectively and ensure that everybody is carried along.

We are also engaging security agencies. I just had a meeting with the police, and we are discussing security arrangements and the peace accord.

We will continue to meet with the relevant stakeholders to ensure a peaceful electoral environment.

What assurances have the security agencies given you?

We have had discussions with them, and they have assured us of their cooperation.

We are working towards a peace accord involving all the political parties. Whoever wins should be allowed to win, and whoever loses should accept the outcome peacefully.

Our desire is to have a free, fair, credible and seamless election.

What is INEC doing to sensitise voters and encourage greater participation in the 2027 elections?

We have what we call INEC Half Hour, which we use for voter education every week on radio stations. We have also been on air, engaging the public on electoral matters.

PVC collection is ongoing, and we have been distributing the cards to registered voters. We have also been using online jingles and other communication channels to create awareness.

We will intensify the sensitisation campaign when we receive the full complement of the PVCs for distribution.

How many new voters were registered in Abia during the last Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise?

We registered 460,011 new voters.

How many PVCs have arrived for collection, and what has been the response of voters?

We have received the first batch of 21,528 PVCs as of October 22, 2026. Collection is still ongoing, and we expect more batches because the cards are arriving in phases.

What is your assessment of the attitude of Abia voters towards PVC collection?

I think Abia is ready. The people have really tried this time around. They have shown interest, and they are coming out to collect their PVCs.

The turnout has been quite impressive. We expect more people to come forward as additional batches of cards arrive.

What is the current total number of registered voters in Abia State?

Abia has 2,620,151 registered voters.

In 2023, we had 2,180,140 registered voters. The additional 460,011 voters recorded during the last Continuous Voter Registration exercise have brought the total to 2,620,151.

What is your general advice to Abia voters, and what assurances can you give them that INEC is ready to deliver a credible election in 2027?

My general advice is that eligible voters should go and collect their PVCs. Your vote is your voice, and your vote will count.

Abia voters will decide. INEC will not decide for them.

Our responsibility on election day is to go to the field early enough, ensure that materials and personnel are deployed promptly and provide the necessary environment for voters to exercise their franchise.

We are going to activate our Registration Area Centres (RACs) to facilitate early deployment of personnel and materials.

I promise the people of Abia that, by the grace of God, their votes will count. Abia decides, not INEC.

Late commencement of voting has often been attributed to logistical challenges, particularly delays in the deployment of election materials and personnel. What measures are you taking to ensure that voting starts early in 2027?

We have been engaging security agencies and other relevant stakeholders. We just had a meeting with them, and we agreed that such meetings would hold every two weeks.

The essence is to identify and address potential challenges ahead of the election.

By the first week of December, we intend to visit and activate the Registration Area Centres (RACs). We want to ensure that the centres have conducive environments and the necessary facilities for election personnel to operate from.

How will RACs activation improve election logistics?

They are strategic locations from which election materials and personnel can be deployed to several polling units within an area.

The idea is to move our personnel and materials closer to the polling units ahead of election day rather than having them travel long distances from our local government offices.

Once the RACs are activated, personnel will stay close to their polling units. So, when it is time for deployment, they can leave early and get to their respective polling units without unnecessary delays.

If we can properly activate the RACs and position our personnel and materials there, it will significantly improve early deployment.

That is part of our strategy to ensure that voting commences on time and that Abia voters have a seamless electoral experience.

The post INEC not anticipating technical glitches in 2027 — Abia REC appeared first on Vanguard News.
