title: Police bust ‘Yahoo academy’ in Ogun, uncover human remains
description:
The Police Special Fraud Unit (PSFU) has arrested 11 suspected internet fraudsters during a raid on an alleged Yahoo academy in Abeokuta, Ogun State, recovering mobile phones, laptops, fetish items and suspected human remains.
The suspects were arrested at House 10, Second Hill Estate, Oloke-Meji, O
content:
The Police Special Fraud Unit (PSFU) has arrested 11 suspected internet fraudsters during a raid on an alleged Yahoo academy in Abeokuta, Ogun State, recovering mobile phones, laptops, fetish items and suspected human remains.

The suspects were arrested at House 10, Second Hill Estate, Oloke-Meji, Onikolobo, Abeokuta, following intelligence-led investigations by detectives of the unit.

Items recovered during the operation included 11 iPhones, three Samsung mobile phones, eight laptops and a 2014 Lexus RX 350. The police also said they recovered charms, blood-stained fetish materials and suspected human remains.

According to the police, the suspects were allegedly involved in an organised internet fraud network known as “Hustle Kingdom”, which operated from the apartment.

In a statement issued on Monday, the PSFU Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Ovie Ewhubare, said the suspects admitted to using the identities and personal information of foreign nationals to defraud unsuspecting victims online.

The statement identified the arrested suspects as Adedolapo Samuel, 25; Timothy Babatunde, 27; Ibrahim Sholete, 30; Torioza Oluwatosin, 30; Yusuf Alabi, 30; Adeyemi Seyi, 32; Tobiloba Oguntoyinbo, 32; Taiwo Mathew, 23; Shoyombo Ayomide, 24; Abayomi Rahmon, 32; and Abolaji Tunji, 28.

The police, however, said the alleged leader of the operation, Goriola Oluwaseun Olanrewaju, also known as Update, remained at large.

According to the statement, Olanrewaju allegedly rented the apartment in 2021 and subsequently recruited young men into the fraud network.

The statement read, “Investigations revealed that one Goriola Oluwaseun Olanrewaju ‘M’, also known as Update, currently at large, rented the apartment in 2021 and subsequently recruited young men into an organised internet fraud operation, commonly known as a ‘Hustle Kingdom’, where they use the facility as a base for cyber-related fraud and other criminal activities.

“The suspects admitted that they exploit the identities and personal details of foreign nationals to defraud unsuspecting victims online.”

The Commissioner of Police, Eloho Okpoziakpo, said the operation highlighted the importance of credible information, intelligence-led policing and professional investigative skills in tackling organised financial and cyber-enabled crimes.

He added that investigations were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the occupation of the property and determine whether the owners fulfilled their responsibilities in verifying and monitoring their tenants.

The commissioner also said the police were working to trace and recover proceeds allegedly generated from the criminal activities.

The latest operation comes less than two weeks after the same police unit uncovered an alleged counterfeit footwear production facility in Makun, Sagamu, Ogun State.

The police said that discovery followed an investigation into the activities of Meibalun International Nigeria Limited, which was accused of producing and marketing footwear bearing the trademarks of international brands without authorisation.

content:
The National Agricultural Development Fund has distributed agricultural inputs to 8,000 rice and maize farmers in Ogun State whose crops were destroyed by flooding during the 2026 rainy season.

The intervention, flagged off in Abeokuta, the state capital, on Monday in collaboration with the state government, is part of the NADF’s emergency agricultural recovery programme aimed at helping affected farmers resume production and recover their livelihoods.

The beneficiaries comprise 4,000 rice farmers and 4,000 maize farmers, who are expected to receive improved seeds, fertilisers, herbicides, pesticides and other farm inputs.

Speaking at the event, the Executive Secretary and Chief Executive Officer of NADF, Mohammed Ibrahim, represented by Olakunle Dabiri, said the programme was designed to prevent farmers from losing an entire planting season because of the floods.

He said the intervention was being implemented in six states across the South-South, South-West and North-Central regions, with rice farmers in Bayelsa, Akwa Ibom, Benue and Kogi also expected to benefit.

Ibrahim said the flood damage extended beyond crops to farm infrastructure, productive land and household incomes, warning that failure to provide timely assistance could affect farmers beyond the current production cycle.

He said the programme would be implemented within seven weeks, with beneficiaries verified to ensure transparency in the distribution of the inputs.

The NADF chief added that the intervention would also promote climate-smart agricultural practices, early-warning systems and agricultural insurance to reduce farmers’ vulnerability to future disasters.

The Ogun State Commissioner for Agriculture and Food Security, Bolu Owotomo, said the state government had earlier distributed 25 bags of fertiliser to farmers free of charge, while the latest intervention would further support those whose farms were affected by flooding.

Owotomo recalled that the NADF had supplied more than 20,000 bags of fertiliser to farmers in the state during the planting season earlier in the year.

He appealed to the fund to extend its support to cotton farmers in Ogun, saying the state was seeking to increase production ahead of the commencement of operations at a proposed cotton processing facility in its industrial zone.

“Ogun actually produces the best cotton as far as Nigeria is concerned. We will be looking for support in that regard,” he said.

He added that cotton farmers needed assistance to boost production before the facility commenced operations, urging the NADF to partner with the state government in supporting them.

According to a statement by Col. Appolonia Anele, the
content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

Troops of the Nigerian Army have neutralised two armed bandits and recovered two AK-47 rifles and other items during an intelligence-led ambush operation in Asungwe Forest, Okehi Local Government Area of Kogi State.

According to a statement by Col. Appolonia Anele, the operation followed sustained offensives against banditry and kidnapping gangs in the state.

The statement said the operation was conducted on Monday, November 23, 2026, by troops of the 12 Brigade under Operation Bem Hembe, in conjunction with other hybrid forces.

It added that the operation was launched following credible intelligence obtained from previously arrested bandits, which provided actionable leads on the movement of criminal elements operating in Asungwe Forest and adjoining communities along the boundaries of Kogi, Edo and Ondo states.

Acting on the intelligence, troops deployed from Patrol Base Kabba and positioned themselves along a suspected bandits’ crossing route within the forest.

The troops subsequently made contact with the criminals and engaged them with superior firepower, neutralising two bandits, while others fled.

Items recovered during the operation included two AK-47 rifles, three magazines, 27 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition, two Android phones, three Tecno keypad phones, assorted drugs and bags suspected to belong to the fleeing criminals.

The statement said the operation demonstrated the Nigerian Army’s resolve to dismantle criminal networks, disrupt bandits’ movements and deny terrorists and kidnappers freedom of action across vulnerable communities.

It added that the Army remained committed to intensifying intelligence-driven operations and sustaining pressure on criminal elements to enhance the security of lives and property.

The Army also urged members of the public to continue providing credible and timely information to security agencies to support ongoing operations against criminal activities.

title: The last thing we heard was “Shoot Omo-Agege”’ – Witness
description:
…My three men were killed — LG chairman



By Efe Onodjae



A witness to the alleged attack on former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, during a campaign rally at Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, has narrated how gunshots erupted at the venue, alleging that
content:
…My three men were killed — LG chairman

By Efe Onodjae

A witness to the alleged attack on former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, during a campaign rally at Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, has narrated how gunshots erupted at the venue, alleging that the last words they heard from a rival group were: “Shoot Omo-Agege.”

The witness, Pius Eguono, alleged that the incident followed a series of confrontations between Omo-Agege’s supporters and some youths in the community ahead of the campaign rally.

According to Eguono, Omo-Agege had been conducting consultations ahead of his campaign and had paid for the use of the community town hall for his official campaign rally scheduled for the following day.

He alleged that the town crier engaged to announce the campaign in the community was beaten up.

Eguono further claimed that on the morning of the rally, the Divisional Police Officer (DPO) of Ufuoma arrived at the venue alongside some youths allegedly linked to Otovwodo community and insisted that the organisers could not use the town hall.

He said the organisers accepted the decision and made alternative arrangements by erecting canopies nearby.

Recounting the events, Eguono said: “Ovie Omo-Agege had been conducting consultations ahead of his campaign. Yesterday, he sent money to pay for the town hall for his official campaign, which was scheduled to kick off today at Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.

“The town crier, who was also paid to make announcements about Ovie Omo-Agege’s campaign, was allegedly beaten to a stupor.

“This morning, the Ufuoma DPO came in the company of Otovwodo youths and insisted that we should not use the community town hall, which we obliged. We then arranged canopies nearby.

“As the rally was ongoing, they brought a cow to roast, apparently to suffocate us with smoke, but we did not mind.

“Meanwhile, the president of Otovwodo Motor Park, Gueke, and his boys started shooting while the police were there. We drew the attention of the most senior officer, the Ufuoma Divisional Police Officer, and he stylishly said he would talk to them.

“If you watch the video clearly, you would hear the sound of gunshots while Ovie Omo-Agege was speaking. But because they were shooting up, we just decided to carry on.

“So, in order to keep us alert, some of the security men with us also fired shots up. Immediately, it was as if they were waiting for our gunshots. The next thing we heard from the Otovwodo youth leader, named Gueke, who was shooting with his boys, was: ‘Shoot Ovie Omo-Agege.’”

On his part, the Ughelli North Local Government Chairman, Olorogun Jaro Egbo, has claimed that three of his supporters were killed during the incident.

Egbo, a chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), said the disagreement began over the use of a community hall, which he claimed had already been booked for an event he was organising for residents of Uduere.

According to him: “Yesterday (Sunday), at the village, we went there to set up our canopy for today’s and tomorrow’s events because I am hosting the entire village.

“When we got there, some people said Omo-Agege was coming and that they wanted to use the hall. So, my president told them that the hall had been booked and that they could take their event elsewhere. They refused.”

Egbo said the NDC campaign subsequently proceeded with its activities close to where his supporters had gathered, despite the disagreement.

He added that security personnel had been alerted ahead of the incident, insisting that he had taken steps to prevent violence.

“In the morning, we had received intelligence that they had brought AK-47 rifles and armed men from Sapele and Ughelli. So, I called the Area Commander and the DPO to go there and maintain peace. We even called the Army.

“When the DPO got there, he called me to say that he was appealing to them not to fight.

“So, I told my people not to talk to anybody but to enjoy themselves. They should drink, eat and be merry. They had their own event, and that was when he (Omo-Agege) was saying that I was his PA, I was this, I was that.”

Egbo, however, accused members of Omo-Agege’s entourage of opening fire on his supporters, claiming that three of his men were killed.

He specifically accused one Akima, whom he described as an anti-cult operative, of shooting at his supporters at close range with a pump-action rifle.

He said: “Thereafter, as he was going, one of his boys, one Akima, who calls himself Anti-Cult, brought out a pump-action gun and opened fire on innocent citizens. He shot three of my people at close range.

“As they fired, two died. The other one we rushed to the hospital has just died. Three others are in critical condition.”

The post The last thing we heard was “Shoot Omo-Agege”’ – Witness appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Court orders Jimmy Odukoya to appear Thursday over church dispute
description:
The Lagos State High Court has directed the Senior Pastor of the Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, to appear before it on Thursday, November 26, over the ongoing leadership crisis in the church.
Justice O. O. Adewunmi-Oshin gave the directive on Monday after hearing an application by the churc
content:
The Lagos State High Court has directed the Senior Pastor of the Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, to appear before it on Thursday, November 26, over the ongoing leadership crisis in the church.

Justice O. O. Adewunmi-Oshin gave the directive on Monday after hearing an application by the church’s counsel, Ibitayo Reju, seeking permission to serve Odukoya with court processes through substituted means.

The court granted the application by the Incorporated Trustees of the Fountain of Life Church, allowing the service of Form 48, the originating court processes, orders and notices through newspaper publication, pasting at Odukoya’s last known address in Ilupeju, Lagos, and electronic means.

The enrolled order stated: “Leave is hereby granted to the Applicant to serve Form 48, the originating court process to be filed in this suit, Orders made, Notices issued, and all other processes to be issued and filed in this suit on the Respondent through substituted means by newspaper publication in several newspaper that is in wide circulation within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court and by pasting at a conspicuous part of the Respondent’s last known address at No. 12 Industrial Estate Road, off Town Planning Way, Ilupeju, Lagos State and also through any Electronical means.”

The judge also directed Odukoya to be present in court on the adjourned date to show cause.

“The Respondent is required to be present in Court on the said date,” the order stated.

The case was subsequently adjourned until November 26, 2026.

The latest development is part of the dispute over the church’s leadership following the purported removal of Odukoya as its Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees.

Odukoya had earlier instituted a separate suit at the Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging decisions taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees, including his purported removal from office.

The leadership crisis also led to an earlier order by the Lagos State High Court on November 18, restraining him from presenting himself as the church’s Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head.

However, during Sunday’s service at the church in Ilupeju, Lagos, Odukoya told the congregation that although he had heard about the injunction, he had not been formally served with the court order.

“I heard that there was an injunction against me. I heard. I’ve not seen it. But I heard. But I’ve not been served. So, legally, I’ve not been served,” he said.

His comments followed a visit by the founder of The Redeemed Evangelical Mission, Bishop Mike Okonkwo, who urged church members not to take sides in the leadership dispute involving Odukoya and his sister, Tolu.

The post Court orders Jimmy Odukoya to appear Thursday over church dispute appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Season’s sweat up in flames as fire ravages Yobe farms
description:
By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman



For four farmers in Gadana, months of labour and the promise of a rewarding harvest ended in ashes when fire swept through their farmlands, destroying approximately 147 bags of mature sorghum just weeks before the end of the year.



In neighbouring communities, the dev
content:
By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman

For four farmers in Gadana, months of labour and the promise of a rewarding harvest ended in ashes when fire swept through their farmlands, destroying approximately 147 bags of mature sorghum just weeks before the end of the year.

In neighbouring communities, the devastation has taken different forms: two households in Godowoli have lost agricultural produce reserved to feed their families, while a tailor in Old Nangere has watched his sewing machines, fabrics, customers’ clothes and other tools of trade disappear in a fire that has crippled his business.

The three incidents, recorded across Nangere and Fika Local Government Areas of Yobe State within five days, have left affected residents counting their losses, with 27 people in Nangere alone facing food insecurity, loss of income and economic hardship.

The incidents were reported in two separate statements published on the official Facebook page of the Yobe State Emergency Management Agency (YOSEMA), both signed by its Director of Search and Rescue Operations, Dr M. I. Jalo.

According to the agency, the first incident occurred at about 4pm on November 14 in Godowoli community, Nangere Ward, where fire destroyed harvested agricultural produce stored by two households as food reserves for the year.

Four days later, another fire outbreak engulfed a tailoring shop in Old Nangere, destroying two electric sewing machines, electric irons, fabrics, customers’ clothes and other tailoring equipment.

Beyond the immediate financial loss, the destruction has left the tailor without essential tools for his trade, while the loss of customers’ clothing could expose him to additional financial obligations.

Midnight fire

In Gadana farmland area of Fika Local Government Area, the fire outbreak occurred at about 1am on November 15, destroying mature sorghum crops belonging to four farmers.

A joint assessment team comprising officials of the Local Emergency Management Committee, Community Development Officers and the affected farmers visited the farmlands to establish the extent of the damage.

The assessment confirmed that approximately 147 bags of sorghum were lost, with the agency describing the destroyed crops as the major source of food, income and household sustenance for the affected farmers and their dependants.

The agency said a detailed assessment documenting the affected farmers, farm sizes, estimated crop losses and corresponding financial implications had been compiled for consideration.

For the affected households, the losses come with concerns about how to meet basic needs and sustain their livelihoods, particularly as the year draws to a close.

YOSEMA said the affected farming community had appealed for urgent intervention to cushion the impact of the disaster, while expressing appreciation for the agency’s commitment to disaster risk management and emergency response.

The agency also urged farmers and residents to exercise caution during the dry season, warning against indiscriminate bush burning, unattended open flames and other activities capable of triggering fire outbreaks.

It advised farmers to establish firebreaks around their farms and homes, keep flammable materials away from ignition sources and promptly report potential fire hazards.

The agency further cautioned residents against entering burning or smouldering areas, stressing that trained emergency responders should be allowed to manage fire incidents to prevent further loss of lives and property.

title: Police arrest 10 suspected cultists, four kidnappers, others in Edo

The arrests were disclosed by the Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), ASP Eno Ikoedem,
content:
The Edo State Police Command has arrested ten suspected cultists, one armed robbery suspect, four suspected kidnappers and one murder suspect in intensified operations against violent crimes across the state.

The arrests were disclosed by the Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), ASP Eno Ikoedem, on behalf of the Commissioner of Police, during a Monday press briefing in Benin City.

According to the command, the arrests underscore its determination to sustain pressure on criminal elements and ensure the safety of residents.

In one operation, the police arrested a suspected armed robber at Ugiokhuen Community, recovering a locally fabricated pistol, ammunition and other exhibits.

The command also recorded a major breakthrough in a kidnapping incident reported on November 19, with the rescue of two victims, Yakubu Ibrahim and Abdullahi Mohammed, unhurt, and the arrest of four suspected kidnappers during an intensive bush-combing operation at Ikakumoh/Ayaran Forest.

Furthermore, four members of the Edo State Security Corps were arrested for allegedly leaking information on police movements to suspected cultists, thereby frustrating an ongoing operation.

In a separate anti-cultism operation at Osakpolor Street, off Adolor College Road, Benin City, ten suspected members of the Aye Axe cult group were arrested during an alleged initiation exercise, while a Mercedes-Benz GLK 350 was recovered.

The command also arrested one John Bello, who allegedly murdered his father, Julius Bello, in Fugar and fled, before he was subsequently tracked down and apprehended.

The Commissioner of Police, CP Patrick Daaor, reiterated the command’s resolve to dismantle criminal networks and bring perpetrators to justice.

He commended the officers involved for their courage and professionalism, and appreciated members of the public for their timely information and continued support.

Residents were urged to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious activities, as the security of Edo State remains a collective responsibility.

title: NUPRC seeks UNIBEN partnership to boost oil production
description:
The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission has offered to partner with the University of Benin on oil and gas research, particularly in gas development and heavy oil extraction, as Nigeria targets crude oil production of three million barrels per day by 2030.
The Commission Chief Executiv
content:
The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission has offered to partner with the University of Benin on oil and gas research, particularly in gas development and heavy oil extraction, as Nigeria targets crude oil production of three million barrels per day by 2030.

The Commission Chief Executive, Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, announced the proposed collaboration on Monday while delivering the 56th Founders’ Day Lecture of the University of Benin in Benin, Edo State.

Eyesan said Nigeria would need to invest in education, skills acquisition and research to meet its oil and gas production targets, stressing that the country’s petroleum resources alone would not guarantee the desired output.

In a statement issued by the commission’s Head of Corporate Communications and Media, Eniola Akinkuotu, the NUPRC chief executive said the Federal Government had also set a target of producing 12 trillion cubic feet of gas by 2030.

“The task before us is enormous. The Federal Government, under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, has set ambitious targets of three million barrels of oil and 12 trillion cubic feet of gas by 2030.

“Achieving these ambitions will require more than the development of our petroleum resources; it will demand a corresponding investment in the knowledge, skills and capabilities of the people who will drive the industry forward. This is why the meeting of minds between town and gown is essential,” she said.

She said the commission would support researchers at the university working on innovative approaches to petroleum exploration, development and extraction, with particular attention to gas and heavy oil.

“To strengthen research and development at the University, the Commission will provide support for researchers pursuing innovative approaches to the development and extraction of our petroleum resources, with particular emphasis on gas and heavy oil,” Eyesan said.

She added that research outcomes from the proposed partnership would be jointly owned by the commission and the university.

Eyesan said stronger collaboration between regulatory institutions and universities was necessary to turn academic research into practical solutions for the petroleum industry.

She also urged students to explore opportunities beyond their immediate academic disciplines, saying broader knowledge would help them develop their potential and contribute to national development.

The Vice-Chancellor of the University of Benin, Edoba Bright Omoregie, thanked Eyesan for her support for the institution and presented her with a medallion on behalf of the university’s management.

Omoregie said Eyesan, the NUPRC Executive Commissioner for Development and Production, Enorense Amadasu, and other prominent figures in the oil and gas industry were products of the university.

title: Otti woos Chinese firm for Abia seaport development
description:
Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has sought a comprehensive partnership with China Harbour Engineering Company Limited for the development of the proposed Abia Seaport City.
Otti said the state preferred an arrangement that would involve the Chinese firm in the project’s feasibility studies, construc
content:
Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has sought a comprehensive partnership with China Harbour Engineering Company Limited for the development of the proposed Abia Seaport City.

Otti said the state preferred an arrangement that would involve the Chinese firm in the project’s feasibility studies, construction and eventual delivery rather than limiting its participation to consultancy services.

The governor spoke on Monday while receiving a delegation led by CHEC’s Managing Director, Wang Jason, who presented preliminary findings and proposals for the project.

He stressed that the state was interested in receiving honest and professional advice based on the company’s findings, noting that the feasibility study would determine the project’s viability and appropriate technical direction.

“I am sure that my people will be engaging with you. But I know they need some clarifications.

“So, my preference would have been a partnership that takes off from the feasibility, to the construction and ultimately delivery,” Otti said.

The governor described the proposed arrangement as a genuine public-private partnership, assuring the Chinese firm that his administration was committed to transparency, integrity and mutually beneficial business relationships.

“So in that case, it’s a real public-private partnership transaction. The major things you have said are also what we believe in. We don’t play games, we don’t cheat people.

“So, if you are in partnership with us, you can be sure that you can go to bed and sleep,” he added.

Otti said he was encouraged by the company’s preliminary presentation but emphasised the need for further discussions to clarify the technical and commercial details of the proposed partnership.

He disclosed that the state had also attracted interest from other prospective investors, including Afreximbank, whose participation would equally depend on the outcome of the feasibility study.

The governor said his administration was prepared to support the project and work with the company to ensure its successful implementation. He, however, noted that the development would require patience, strategic planning, technical capacity and long-term commitment.

He expressed optimism that the project, when integrated with other infrastructure and economic activities, could significantly transform Abia’s economic landscape.

Otti further said his administration’s development agenda was anchored on a long-term framework, noting that the state had enacted a 25-year development plan into law to ensure continuity in governance and development projects beyond successive administrations.

Earlier, Jason described the proposed seaport project as viable and capable of contributing significantly to the development of the state.

He said the proposal was an integrated infrastructure development master plan, explaining that the feasibility study would determine the most suitable port design, technical specifications and depth requirements for the proposed location.

“I want to say that, for this project or this concept, it is an integrated infrastructure development master plan.

“As you said, from this presentation, it’s viable. The only thing we need to verify is what kind of port or what depth will be more viable. That doesn’t mean we don’t have an available option.

“We need to use a feasibility study to find out the most viable, most suitable solution for this area. So, that’s the reason. Generally, if I don’t believe this one is possible anyway, I won’t want to be involved,” he said.

Jason said CHEC had considerable expertise in feasibility studies and port infrastructure development but was more interested in establishing a long-term relationship with Abia State than undertaking consultancy work alone.

“Certainly, for China Harbour, this feasibility study, we are good at it; it is our major business, and we have to do a good job. But we are not focused on this, on the consultancy work. We wish to have a long-term cooperation with Abia State for the future development and delivery.

“But for the detailed cooperation model, the business model, I think after the feasibility study, we can continue the discussion. I think it will be more serious for me to express our position,” Jason stated.

He said he was impressed by Aba’s economic significance, describing the commercial city as an important hub in Nigeria and expressing confidence in its potential to support the proposed integrated infrastructure development.

The proposed seaport is part of Abia State’s plan to improve maritime access for the South-East and strengthen the region’s trade and logistics capacity.

The project, identified as the Azumini–Obeaku Seaport and Inland Waterways Corridor, is located in the Azumini area of Ukwa East Local Government Area.

The proposed port is expected to provide a maritime gateway for Aba’s industrial and commercial activities and potentially reduce the cost of transporting goods for manufacturers in the region. It could also create a logistics corridor linking the South-East to international markets.

Otti had earlier approved a feasibility study for the project in May 2026, directing CHEC to accelerate the process.

The study is expected to establish the technical, economic and environmental requirements, including the dredging needed to make the proposed waterway navigable.

Its findings will help determine whether the project is viable and the appropriate investment and construction model.

The governor was accompanied at Monday’s meeting by the Secretary to the State Government, Dr Emmanuel Meribeole, and other members of the State Executive Council.

The post Otti woos Chinese firm for Abia seaport development appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Omo Agege attack: Slain supporter was father of 6-month-old baby
description:
By Efe Onodjae



One of the supporters killed in the alleged assassination attempt on former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, was a father of just six months, having welcomed his first child on May 15, 2026.







The deceased, identified as Efemena Umukoro, had taken to Facebook o
content:
By Efe Onodjae

One of the supporters killed in the alleged assassination attempt on former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, was a father of just six months, having welcomed his first child on May 15, 2026.

The deceased, identified as Efemena Umukoro, had taken to Facebook on May 15 to announce the birth of his baby boy, celebrating the safe delivery of his wife and child.

In the emotional post, Umukoro narrated his experience during his wife’s labour, describing women as heroes for enduring the pains of childbirth.

Sadly, six months after celebrating the arrival of his newborn son, Umukoro was found dead in his Toyota Highlander SUV following the alleged assassination attempt during a campaign tour by Omo-Agege in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.

In a video seen by Vanguard, Umukoro was found lying lifeless in the vehicle, dressed in a white shirt and black shorts.

Four persons were confirmed dead in the attack, which occurred during a political campaign activity in the community.

In his May 15 Facebook post announcing the birth of his son, Umukoro wrote: “My Prince is here, mother and child in good health. Women are the heroes and keepers of life.

“From 1cm to 10cm dilation, I stood firmly beside her through every painful minute that almost felt like a whole year suspended in time between hope and fear.

“Indeed, women are heroes. They carry the deepest pains of this world in silence and strength.

“I watched my beautiful wife grumble and tremble in agony, entering a realm where shame no longer existed. She tore off her clothes, choosing nakedness as though, in that vulnerable state, she found the strength to fight a battle nature designed only for mothers.

“Every single minute mattered to us. I kept staring at my phone, counting contractions, wishing with all my heart that I could take the pain away from her. But each time I thought the worst had passed, the pain returned even harder. And there I was… helpless, watching the woman I love fight a war I could not fight for her.

“How does one endure pain without knowing its limits? “How does a human body survive waves of agony with no certainty of when relief will finally come?

The post Omo Agege attack: Slain supporter was father of 6-month-old baby appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: ‘We must see ourselves as one – Tinubu tells Igbo community in Lagos
description:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni



President Bola Tinubu and Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, have urged Nigerians to rise above ethnic and regional divisions, emphasising the need for national cohesion, mutual understanding and inclusive economic development.



The leaders made the call on Monday at
content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

President Bola Tinubu and Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, have urged Nigerians to rise above ethnic and regional divisions, emphasising the need for national cohesion, mutual understanding and inclusive economic development.

The leaders made the call on Monday at the Ndigbo Lagos State Town Hall, organised by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiative (NNDDI) at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly the National Arts Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos.

The engagement, attended by Igbo community leaders, business stakeholders and government officials, provided an opportunity to strengthen relations between the Igbo community and the Lagos and Federal Governments ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Addressing participants, Tinubu urged Nigerians to embrace a shared national identity, irrespective of their ethnic, religious or regional backgrounds, saying the country’s development depended on the collective contributions of all citizens.

He also stressed the importance of creating broad-based economic opportunities to enable Nigerians to contribute meaningfully to nation-building.

“We must see ourselves as one people with a shared future.

“Nigeria must rise above its divisions, because our true development depends on the active participation and commitment of every single citizen, regardless of background,” the President said.

Earlier, Sanwo-Olu commended Tinubu for attending the gathering, describing his presence as an affirmation of the important role played by the Igbo community in the socioeconomic development of Lagos State.

He acknowledged the contributions of Igbo political leaders, entrepreneurs, business associates and other stakeholders to the growth of the state.

“The President’s presence here today is a significant gesture of recognition for Ndigbo and their rightful place in Lagos.

“We deeply value the enduring contributions and longstanding partnerships of the political leaders, business associates, and stakeholders who continue to build this state alongside us,” the governor said.

Reflecting on Nigeria’s democratic journey, particularly the political developments of 1999, 2003 and 2007, Sanwo-Olu also paid tribute to past and present leaders whose contributions helped shape the country’s political evolution.

The town hall was designed to deepen engagement, address concerns affecting the Igbo community in Lagos and strengthen collaboration between community representatives and the two tiers of government.

title: Delta killings: Keyamo condemns attack on Omo-Agege’s campaign team
description:
The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has condemned the attack on the campaign team of former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, in Delta State, which reportedly left four people dead and four others critically injured.
Keyamo described the incident as disturbing a
content:
The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has condemned the attack on the campaign team of former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, in Delta State, which reportedly left four people dead and four others critically injured.

Keyamo described the incident as disturbing and called on security agencies to identify and arrest those responsible for the killings.

The attack occurred on Monday in the Uduere area of Ughelli North Local Government Area while Omo-Agege, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Delta Central, was on a campaign tour of the community.

Sunny Areh, the former senator’s media adviser, said armed men opened fire on Omo-Agege’s entourage at close range as he addressed supporters. He added that Omo-Agege escaped unhurt.

Those reportedly killed in the attack were identified as Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro, while the injured included Evance Ivwurie, Chuks Erhire, Tobore Agba and Ayodo Wanogho.

In a statement issued on Monday, Keyamo linked the incident to what he described as an increasingly hostile political atmosphere in the state.

He also recalled the killing of a tricycle operator in a daylight attack in Asaba on November 7, urging law enforcement agencies to investigate both incidents.

“I call on the law enforcement agencies to fish out the perpetrators of these killings, both in Asaba and Ughelli, and bring them to book,” he said.

The minister said he had been engaging senior security officials over the rising incidents of political violence and inflammatory statements in Delta State.

He noted that political disagreements in the state had largely remained peaceful since 1999, expressing concern that political competition was now being accompanied by threats and violence.

“We are all brothers and sisters who went to the same primary, secondary and tertiary institutions, and we all know ourselves and our families so well. There is absolutely no need for a descent into violence,” Keyamo said.

He specifically criticised the use of the phrase “Rig and Die”, which he said had contributed to tensions in the state and elsewhere.

“Those who have promoted the mantra of ‘Rig and Die’ in Delta State and elsewhere should have a rethink, publicly withdraw it, and apologise for overheating the political temperature in the State and country,” he said.

Keyamo also warned political leaders against encouraging supporters to attack opponents or other citizens, insisting that the responsibility for dealing with offenders rested with law enforcement agencies.

“It is wrong to tell your supporters to kill other citizens under whatever guise. It smacks of desperation,” he added.

The minister appealed to Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to address residents and caution individuals making threats of violence.

He said the governor, as the state’s chief security officer, should urgently speak to the people and warn those threatening to cause violence.

The statement comes weeks after Omo-Agege made remarks about the 2027 general election, warning that anyone caught rigging the poll could be killed.

Speaking in October, the former deputy senate president said, “Anybody who rigs the election on that day, we will kill him! If you don’t value your life, come and rig the election.”

He also declared, “It is rig and die. We’re going to give them aura for aura. There’s no court this time. We’re going to fight.”

title: Delta killings: Impunity fuelling political violence – Falana
description:
Human rights lawyer and Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Femi Falana, has blamed the rising wave of political violence in the country on the failure to prosecute electoral offenders, warning that continued impunity could threaten the 2027 general elections.
Falana spoke on Channels Television’s Politics
content:
Human rights lawyer and Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Femi Falana, has blamed the rising wave of political violence in the country on the failure to prosecute electoral offenders, warning that continued impunity could threaten the 2027 general elections.

Falana spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday while reacting to the deadly violence at a political rally in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.

He urged the Nigerian Bar Association, civil society organisations and security agencies to ensure that those responsible for electoral violence were brought to justice.

His comment came following a deadly incident at a campaign rally in Delta State.

The attack occurred during a campaign rally in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, on Monday.

Former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, who is seeking election to the Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general election on the platform of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, said gunmen opened fire shortly after he began addressing supporters.

He said four members of his campaign team were killed, while 15 others sustained critical injuries.

The former Deputy Senate President also credited his Department of State Services security detail with helping him escape unharmed.

The incident prompted the Delta State Government to impose a 12-hour curfew on Ughelli North and order an investigation into the violence.

The police also announced a probe into the incident.

Reacting, Falana described the incident as avoidable but unsurprising, citing previous attacks involving prominent political figures.

He recalled previous incidents, including an attack on the convoy of former presidential candidate Peter Obi, in Calabar, Cross River State, in which a person reportedly died, as well as the stoning of President Bola Tinubu’s convoy in Akwa Ibom State.

“Well, it is very sad. What happened today is extremely sad, avoidable, but not surprising.

“We’ve had attacks on politicians. I think Omoyele Sowore was lucky in Ekiti. I think somebody died in Calabar when Mr Peter Obi’s convoy was attacked. The president’s convoy was stoned in Akwa Ibom about two weeks ago. So the stakes are for the members of the political class. Impunity is already institutionalised,” he said.

Falana argued that the absence of effective prosecution had emboldened perpetrators of political violence, warning that the country could face a serious crisis if politicians were left to determine the course of public affairs without accountability.

He added, “From this unfortunate incident, nothing may come out of it. Yesterday, we lost scores of people in Bayelsa State in a boat accident. Nothing will happen.

“Now, electoral offences are taking place. Nobody is being prosecuted.”

The senior lawyer challenged the Nigerian Bar Association, human rights organisations and other stakeholders to take a more active role in ensuring that electoral offenders were brought to justice.

“I am challenging the Nigerian Bar Association, the human rights community and other stakeholders to intervene very decisively because if we leave the affairs of our country in the hands of politicians, we may run into a very serious crisis. And the earlier, the better,” he said.

Falana proposed that the NBA should mobilise lawyers across the country to assist the Independent National Electoral Commission in prosecuting electoral offenders.

He said the arrangement had been adopted during previous elections and could help address the commission’s limited capacity to handle prosecutions alongside its other responsibilities.

“I have suggested, as we have done in the past. Go and sit down with INEC and mobilise lawyers to assist INEC to prosecute electoral offenders. And that has to be done,” he said.

“We did it in 2011, 2015, 2020, 2023. So that all those who have been arrested for committing electoral offences can be nabbed and prosecuted because impunity is the order of the day,” he said.

He maintained that perpetrators would think twice before engaging in violence if they knew they would face the consequences of their actions.

“Nobody would have thought we were going to kill people in a rally if they knew that the law would catch up with them,” he said.

Falana also criticised the National Assembly for failing to establish an Electoral Offences Commission, despite recommendations by successive electoral reform panels dating back to 2009 and 2010.

He said the absence of a dedicated body had left INEC with the responsibility of prosecuting electoral offenders, despite the commission’s existing workload.

According to him, the electoral body was already handling hundreds of pre-election cases and would have more post-election disputes to contend with after the polls.

He urged security agencies, particularly the police and the Department of State Services, to ensure that political violence was investigated and that those responsible were prosecuted, irrespective of their political affiliations.

He stated, “The security forces in our country, particularly the police and the State Security Service, must actualise the wishes of Nigerians, i.e. to have a peaceful election.

“Let the people decide. Give the people the opportunity to choose among their oppressors. It’s their right. But the way we are going, we are going to lose more lives unnecessarily.”

title: 2027: Falana warns politicians against violence ahead of elections
description:
Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) and human rights activist, Femi Falana, has warned that political violence and killings ahead of the 2027 general elections will continue unless perpetrators are swiftly arrested and prosecuted.
Falana said the failure to hold those responsible for previous election-
content:
Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) and human rights activist, Femi Falana, has warned that political violence and killings ahead of the 2027 general elections will continue unless perpetrators are swiftly arrested and prosecuted.

Falana said the failure to hold those responsible for previous election-related violence accountable had encouraged impunity and emboldened political actors to resort to violence.

He spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday while reacting to recent election-related incidents, including the killing of four supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Delta State.

The human rights lawyer described the deaths as tragic and preventable, arguing that people would think twice before engaging in violence if they knew they would face the full weight of the law.

“The stakes are high for the political class, but in this unfortunate incident, nothing may come of it. Yesterday, we lost scores of people in Bayelsa State in what was a boat accident. What would happen? Donations have already started; who is the owner of the boat?

“Nobody would have thought they were going to kill people in a rally if they know that the law will catch up with them,” Falana said.

He urged the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), civil society organisations and human rights groups to take a more active role in addressing the country’s political challenges rather than leaving the responsibility entirely to politicians.

“Arrests may be made in Delta State, but I am challenging the Nigerian Bar Association and the human rights community to intervene very decisively because if we leave the affairs of our country in the hands of politicians, we will run into a serious crisis,” he said.

Falana also called on the NBA to mobilise lawyers to assist the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in prosecuting electoral offenders.

He argued that the commission was already burdened with pre-election and post-election litigation and needed support to ensure that electoral offences did not go unpunished.

Beyond political violence, the senior lawyer called for greater public scrutiny of the electoral process, including the cleaning up of the voters’ register, accountability by electoral officials and transparent transmission of election results.

He also urged political parties and candidates to focus their campaigns on governance and issues affecting Nigerians rather than relying on ethnic and religious divisions.

Falana identified unspent funds allocated to basic education by state governments, compulsory health insurance, implementation of child rights laws, fuel subsidy controversies, crude oil-backed loans and stalled refinery rehabilitation projects as issues that should feature prominently in political debates.

Despite his concerns about the country’s political climate, he said Nigeria was not beyond redemption, insisting that existing laws could bring about meaningful change if citizens, the media and civil society organisations demanded accountability.

“So for me it’s not a hopeless situation. It is about promoting debates and that’s what I miss,” he said, urging Nigerians to engage political leaders on substantive national issues rather than focus only on political campaigns and spectacles.

title: Delta killings: Obi demands justice for four NDC supporters
description:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, has demanded a thorough investigation into the killing of four party supporters during a political gathering in Delta State.
Obi, who condemned the attack as a senseless act of violence, called on security agencies to identify
content:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, has demanded a thorough investigation into the killing of four party supporters during a political gathering in Delta State.

Obi, who condemned the attack as a senseless act of violence, called on security agencies to identify and prosecute those responsible, including any sponsors.

In a statement on Tuesday, the former Anambra State governor said 15 other supporters sustained serious injuries in the attack in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area.

He identified the deceased as Moses Anaughe, a former Federal Commissioner of the Federal Character Commission; Akima Efenena Umukoro, a former President of the Urhobo Progress Union Youth Wing; and Nyoren Okoro, an NDC chieftain.

He said the identity of the fourth victim had yet to be established.

Among those injured were Evance Ivwurie, Chairman of Senator Ovie Omo-Agege’s Campaign Organisation, and Chuks Erhire, its Director-General.

Obi, who expressed condolences to the families of the deceased, said, “I offer my deepest condolences to the families of those who died and pray for a swift recovery for the injured.”

He urged security agencies to “conduct a comprehensive investigation, identify those responsible and their sponsors, and ensure they face justice.”

The former governor also called on the authorities to take immediate steps to protect Nigerians participating in political activities.

He said, “Every Nigerian has a constitutional right to support any political party or candidate without fear of intimidation or violence.”

Expressing concern over the escalation of political hostility, Obi said it was no longer enough for those behind attacks on opposition supporters to spread false claims against them.

“It is no longer sufficient for those responsible to fund the dissemination of false claims against the opposition. They have now escalated to the appalling practice of murdering innocent Nigerians solely because of their political affiliations. This is completely unacceptable,” he said.

He added that political disagreements should not result in violence, insisting that elections and persuasion remained the legitimate ways to resolve political differences.

“Political differences must be resolved through persuasion and the ballot, never through the use of bullets. No political ambition is worth the life of even one Nigerian,” Obi said.

The attack occurred in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, during a political gathering involving Omo-Agege, the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central.

Omo-Agege had alleged that the attackers repeatedly called his name and threatened to kill him during the incident. He said he escaped through the intervention of his security escorts.

Following the violence, the Delta State Government imposed a 12-hour curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area to prevent further breakdown of law and order.

The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, also condemned the political violence, warning that the “Rig and Die” slogan was contributing to tension in the state.

He called on those promoting the slogan to publicly withdraw it and apologise.

title: Amnesty International condemns death threats against tourist over Daura Emir video
description:
A Polish tourist, Mirka Czee, has shared screenshots of threats and abusive messages she received following her allegation of sexual assault against the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Faruk Umar Faruk.
Amnesty International Nigeria on Tuesday condemned the threats against the tourist, saying she had received
content:
A Polish tourist, Mirka Czee, has shared screenshots of threats and abusive messages she received following her allegation of sexual assault against the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Faruk Umar Faruk.

Amnesty International Nigeria on Tuesday condemned the threats against the tourist, saying she had received hundreds of death threats, including warnings that she would be tracked down and killed or harmed.

The organisation said Czee had been subjected to round-the-clock attacks and cyberbullying since speaking out about the alleged incident at the Emir’s palace in Daura, Katsina State, on November 14.

In a statement shared on its social media platforms, Amnesty said the messages warned the tourist to either withdraw her allegation or face death.

“It is appalling that the foreign tourist that was allegedly sexually assaulted by the 92-year-old Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, has been receiving hundreds of death threats, including threats to track her wherever she is to kill or harm her,” the organisation said.

Czee shared screenshots of some of the messages in an Instagram post on Monday, showing threats, insults and demands for her to delete the viral video of her encounter with the traditional ruler.

Some of the messages accused her of deliberately trying to damage the Emir’s reputation, while others threatened her safety and warned her against returning to Nigeria.

In one of the private messages, a user identified as Handel Benny accused the tourist of encouraging the alleged advances before publishing the video.

“You went to visit a man, you sat close to him as per his queen, he held ur hand, you were laughing, no caution. You enjoyed everything. You gave him the green light to continue after he continued, you rushed to social media to lament,” the message read.

Other messages contained threats of violence, with one user warning Czee not to return to Africa, while another threatened harm against her and people from her country.

The screenshots also showed several comments blaming the tourist for the alleged incident, accusing her of disrespecting Islam and Hausa traditions and questioning her reasons for publishing the recording.

One private message also offered her $50,000 to remove the video, saying, “I will give you 50k$ if you can remove the video of Emir of Daura please.”

Amnesty said the attacks demonstrated why many rape cases went unreported in Nigeria, citing corruption, stigma and victim-blaming.

It called on the Nigeria Police Force to provide necessary support to Czee and conduct an impartial and effective investigation into the allegation.

“The Nigeria police must provide all necessary support to the survivor and act in line with their code of conduct, by carrying out impartial and effective investigation,” the organisation said.

It also criticised what it described as the silence of the Katsina State Government, saying the response highlighted concerns about the prevalence of sexual abuse and the safety of women and girls.

The development comes amid growing reactions to the allegation, which followed the circulation of a video appearing to show the Emir interacting with Czee during her visit to his palace.

The tourist had alleged that the monarch held her hand, hugged her and kissed her cheek before touching her breasts without her consent.

She said she repeatedly told him not to touch her, adding that she activated the recording function on her Meta smart glasses after becoming uncomfortable when he held her hand.

Czee, who was born in the Czech Republic, said the incident happened on November 14, during a 30-day tour of Nigeria, but she waited until she had left the country before making the allegation public.

The Daura Emirate Council said it was reviewing the viral footage to establish its authenticity and determine whether it had been manipulated or artificially generated.

Its spokesperson, Ibrahim Daura, said the council would issue an official statement after concluding the review.

PUNCH Online could not independently confirm the allegation, while the Emir had yet to personally respond to it as of the time of filing this report.

title: AFCON final: CAS delivers ruling today on Senegal’s appeal
description:
The Court of Arbitration for Sport, CAS, has confirmed that it will issue its ruling on the disputed 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final between Morocco and Senegal today, bringing months of legal proceedings closer to a conclusion.



According to Morocco World News, in an official statement released
content:
The Court of Arbitration for Sport, CAS, has confirmed that it will issue its ruling on the disputed 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final between Morocco and Senegal today, bringing months of legal proceedings closer to a conclusion.

According to Morocco World News, in an official statement released yesterday, CAS said it had notified the Senegalese Football Federation, FSF, the Confederation of African Football, CAF, and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation, FRMF, that the decision would arrive in the afternoon.

The court did not specify an exact time and stressed that only announcements published through its official channels would carry legal authority.

The dispute concerns CAF’s March 17 decision to declare Senegal’s national team to have forfeited the January 18 final in Rabat, awarding Morocco a 3–0 victory under Articles 82 and 84 of the competition regulations.

CAF’s Appeal Board reached that decision after Senegal’s players temporarily walked off the pitch in protest against a late penalty awarded to Morocco.

The players eventually returned, and Senegal secured a 1–0 victory after extra time. However, the Moroccan Federation challenged the circumstances surrounding the interruption, prompting CAF’s Appeal Board to overturn the result.

Senegal subsequently appealed the ruling to CAS, seeking to reverse CAF’s decision.

Morocco’s position rests on the competition’s written regulations. Article 82 states that a team leaving the pitch before the end of a match without the referee’s authorization faces forfeiture, while Article 84 provides for a 3–0 defeat.

CAF’s Appeal Board explicitly found that Senegal had breached Article 82, accepting Morocco’s argument that the team’s conduct warranted consequences regardless of the eventual score.

The Senegalese player’s departure interrupted the final for approximately 14 minutes, leaving Brahim Diaz to take Morocco’s stoppage-time penalty only after the lengthy disruption.

Although Senegal returned and completed the match, the resumption did not erase the incident from CAF’s disciplinary assessment. Senegal now argues that the completed match and the referee’s decision to resume play should preserve its victory, while Morocco maintains that the regulations apply to the unauthorized departure itself.

title: Nigeria’s electricity crisis to persist as FG shifts debt payment to 2027
description:
•Poor teamwork, illiquidity, others undermine efficiency – Tegbe •Power crisis requires structural overhaul – Iledare



By Ediri Ejoh



Nigeria’s electricity crisis is unlikely to be resolved in 2026, as the Federal Government has shifted the settlement of its N3.3 trillion debt to power generatio
content:
•Poor teamwork, illiquidity, others undermine efficiency – Tegbe •Power crisis requires structural overhaul – Iledare

By Ediri Ejoh

Nigeria’s electricity crisis is unlikely to be resolved in 2026, as the Federal Government has shifted the settlement of its N3.3 trillion debt to power generation companies to 2027, while major interventions in metering and transmission infrastructure are also expected to extend beyond this year.

The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, disclosed this during an interview with Arise News yesterday, adding that the government had paid N1.23 trillion of the debt, negotiated down from an initial N6 trillion, and was exploring options to clear the outstanding balance.

These include offsetting obligations against royalties and corporate income tax, as well as engaging the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, NNPC, to reduce gas costs for power generation companies.

“We’re on track to finish paying the rest next year. Because we are looking at different ways to settle it,” Tegbe said.

On the proposed debt offsets, he said: “You can’t take money with one hand and give it with the other hand. So, let’s net it off.”

Tegbe attributed 80 per cent of the sector’s challenges to human and institutional factors, with technical issues accounting for the remaining 20 per cent.

“I said the problem in power sector is 20 per cent technical, 80 per cent human,” he said, identifying poor teamwork, lack of coordination among operators, liquidity constraints and governance issues as major obstacles to efficiency.

He also criticised past investment decisions, saying some projects were driven by political considerations rather than proper planning.

“From a technical point of view, I will tell you the biggest issue: it is that we’ve been throwing money at wrong things,” he said.

The minister said his ministry was reviewing ongoing projects to prioritise investments capable of improving electricity access.

Tegbe recently projected that stable electricity supply could take another three to five years. He also announced plans for a $2 billion East-West Super Grid project to expand transmission capacity from about 4,000MW to 19,000MW.

The proposed network would link Funtua, Gwagwalada, Ikot Ekpene, Benin, Epe and Ilorin. Procurement is under way, with completion expected within two years, according to the minister.

Reacting, Professor Emeritus of Petroleum Economics, Wumi Iledare, called for a structural overhaul, warning that replacing individuals would not resolve the sector’s deep-rooted problems.

“Darkness arising from persistent electricity failures in Nigeria is not fundamentally a consequence of individual ineptitude; it is a manifestation of institutional failure,” he said.

Iledare argued that decentralisation could encourage competition, investment and subnational participation, but stressed that it must be backed by effective regulation, institutional capacity and accountability.

“Ultimately, Nigeria needs institutional reform, not merely a change of individuals. The real test of decentralisation must be measurable improvements in electricity availability, affordability, reliability and accessibility,” he said.

Checks by Energy Vanguard showed that many homes and businesses in several parts of the country had endured weeks of irregular electricity supply.

Industry data also showed that more than 3,000MW was available for distribution nationwide, underscoring the gap between available supply and consumers’ electricity needs.

Vanguard News

The post Nigeria’s electricity crisis to persist as FG shifts debt payment to 2027 appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Asaba children turn to begging, exposing gaps in Delta’s education enforcement
description:
By Egufe Yafugborhi

content:
By Egufe Yafugborhi

ASABA — The contrast is disturbing, almost cruel in its simplicity. At GRA Junction on Okpanam Road, neatly dressed students of Model Secondary School, GRA, Asaba, walk briskly towards their classrooms, ready to begin another week of learning.

On the DBS Junction side, children of their age stand by the traffic lights, stretching out their hands to motorists, begging for money under the guise of cleaning windscreens, directing traffic or simply signaling hunger.

It is one junction, one Monday morning, but two sharply different childhood experiences. One group is headed for lessons; the other is already at work, struggling to secure its next meal. The disturbing spectacle exposes a troubling contradiction in Delta State, where laws and government programmes have been established to guarantee children’s access to education, yet vulnerable children remain visibly engaged in street begging during school hours.

Virtually all of these children, predominantly from disadvantaged backgrounds, spend their days around busy roads, approaching motorists for handouts. When the day’s activities end, they retire to makeshift shelters in open shops, uncompleted buildings and other available spaces, exposed to untold vulnerabilities.

Their circumstances raise fundamental questions about parental responsibility, child protection, migration, poverty and, particularly, the enforcement of compulsory basic education.

For most of them, how they ended up on the streets is similar. They claim to have migrated from neighbouring states after relatives or acquaintances brought them to Asaba with promises of domestic employment, shop assistance or apprenticeship. Having allegedly become stranded after falling out with those who brought them, they turn to street begging to survive, unable to return home.

These accounts could not be independently verified, as the children were unwilling to divulge details of their backgrounds. Only the youngest among them, a girl who claimed to be five but appeared about three years older, told NDV: “My Auntie brought me from Enugu. She said I should be coming here to beg.”

Another older female soon joined the group and dragged her away from the conversation, truncating the opportunity to establish whether she was the aunt who brought the girl from Enugu to Asaba. The common narrative, however, points to possible cases of child neglect, exploitation and abandonment requiring investigation.

Laws guarantee free education, enforcement fails

What makes the situation troubling is that Delta State already has laws to address the problem of out-of-school children. The Delta State Universal Basic Education Law, 2006, guarantees free, compulsory and universal basic education for every child of primary and junior secondary school age. It places responsibility on parents to ensure school attendance and prescribes sanctions for defaulting parents, including reprimand, fines and imprisonment.

It also makes education in public primary and junior secondary schools free and mandates Local Government Education Authorities and the State Universal Basic Education Board to ensure full enrolment and attendance.

Beyond that, the Delta State Child Rights Law, 2008, amended in 2024, prohibits subjecting children to exploitative labour, using them as domestic help outside their family environment, and deploying them for begging and hawking in ways that deprive them of schooling. On paper, therefore, the state has a comprehensive framework: free education, compulsory attendance, parental obligations and institutions empowered to enforce compliance.

Previous promises, same streets

The problem is not new to the authorities. In December 2021, the Chairman of the Child Rights Implementation Committee, Mrs Kevwe Agas, announced plans to raid streets and apprehend persons involved in street begging and child hawking during school hours after completing sensitisation campaigns.

In February 2022, the government said 28 alleged street beggars, six women and 22 girls were taken into custody in an operation involving FIDA, for allegedly using children to solicit alms instead of sending them to school. That showed the government recognised the problem and could act. But the renewed visibility of children begging around Asaba raises questions about the sustainability of such interventions, monitoring and enforcement.

Laws for optics, no will to enforce

Coordinator of Journalists for Just Development, Austin Aghomi, described the situation as evidence of a gap between legislation and implementation, saying: “Their sight is a reminder of a Delta State that makes laws for optics with no will to enforce. Like the idle anti-open grazing law and ‘anti-deve’ law that have existed on paper without meaningful enforcement against alarming infractions, Delta has existing statutes outlawing out-of-school children.

“I remember the late former Governor Emmanuel Uduaghan established Edu-Marshals in 2013 to enforce the law, including punishing parents who neglect or deny their wards basic education considered free. Edu-Marshals were to, ordinarily, identify out-of-school children, trace families and ensure return to classrooms. I doubt if Edu-Marshals still exist.”

Under Uduaghan’s successor, Senator Ifeanyi Okowa, the state government terminated the programme as a stand-alone initiative around 2017–2018. The administration had its reasons. To it, Edu-Marshals represented institutional duplication and an indictment or vote of no confidence in the monitoring and inspectorate arm of the Education ministry.

Rather than maintain an independent enforcement corps, the government unbundled the programme and absorbed its monitoring duties into the regular institutional schedules of the Delta State Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education. Although concerned citizens have occasionally called on the state government to restore Edu-Marshals to combat street roaming during school hours, no official reintroduction has occurred.

Under Governor Sheriff Oborevwori’s administration, school attendance and truancy monitoring remain the responsibility of school administrators, principals and the state Education ministry.

But enforcement cannot end with occasional patrols. It requires identification, family tracing, rehabilitation, enrolment and sustained monitoring. Child rights advocates note that children found begging are not offenders but victims of poverty, abandonment, trafficking or family breakdown. The response should target adults exploiting them, investigate how they ended up on the streets, and provide shelter, counselling and educational support. Where children have been brought from other states, authorities should work with their states of origin to establish their identities and facilitate safe reunification.

Test of commitment

For the students walking towards Model Secondary School, Monday morning represents an opportunity to learn and prepare for the future. For their contemporaries begging on the opposite side, the same morning presents a struggle for survival. That contrast should trouble every stakeholder in Delta’s education and child protection system.

The Oborevwori administration must demonstrate that its commitment to child welfare extends beyond policy pronouncements to measurable enforcement, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration. Until then, DBS Junction will remain a disturbing picture of two childhoods side by side: one moving towards the classroom, the other begging for survival.

The question Delta must answer is simple: What becomes of free and compulsory education when children who should be in classrooms are left to beg motorists for food?
