title: 20th Coronation: Governors, traditional rulers, Amuka, others honour Orodje of Okpe
description:
By Jimitota Onoyume



For 10 memorable days, the ancient Okpe Kingdom in Delta State was agog with celebrations as the Orodje of Okpe, His Royal Majesty, Major General Felix Mujakperuo (Rtd.), CFR, Orhue I, marked his 20th coronation anniversary with pomp, pageantry and an impressive display of cul
content:
By Jimitota Onoyume

For 10 memorable days, the ancient Okpe Kingdom in Delta State was agog with celebrations as the Orodje of Okpe, His Royal Majesty, Major General Felix Mujakperuo (Rtd.), CFR, Orhue I, marked his 20th coronation anniversary with pomp, pageantry and an impressive display of culture and tradition. One of the most captivating moments at the grand finale last Saturday in his palace was when the retired army General used his ceremonial military sword, a gift from the Nigerian Army in recognition of his distinguished service, to cut his anniversary cake.

The visibly elated monarch, who was flanked by the Queen Consort, Governor Oborevwori , Bayelsa State Governor, Senator Douye Diri; Kogi State Governor, Alhaji Ahmed Usman Ododo; and Taraba State Governor, Dr Agbu Kefas took time to explain the significance of the sword, particularly its curved shape, which distinguished it from those of officers of lower ranks.

“I was allowed to retire with my sword as a Major General. You will observe that my sword is curved because Major Generals get the curved sword, while those of officers below the rank of Major General are straight. The understanding is that we have used the sword to secure several combat victories as Major Generals,” he explained.

Amid applause and excitement, the monarch, assisted by some of the dignitaries around him, ceremoniously cut the anniversary cake with the sword. Beautiful musical performances subsequently filled the atmosphere, adding colour to the historic moment.

In his address, the Orodje expressed gratitude to Almighty God for sustaining him in the last 20-year reign. He also used the occasion to raise concerns over the declining use of the Okpe language, appealing to parents to take deliberate steps to preserve the kingdom’s linguistic heritage by ensuring that their children learn and speak it.

The monarch said he was pained by reports that the language was gradually going into extinction, stressing that the preservation of the Okpe identity must begin within individual homes and families.

Governor Douye Diri of Bayelsa State, who chaired the occasion, commended the Orodje for providing purposeful leadership and sustaining peace in Okpe Kingdom, noting that a peaceful environment was essential for meaningful development. He congratulated the monarch on the milestone, describing 20 years on the throne as a remarkable achievement.

Delta State Governor, Rt. Hon. Sheriff Oborevwori, in his remarks, also congratulated the monarch, recalling his distinguished career in the Nigerian Army and commending his contributions to the development of Okpe Kingdom and Delta State.

For ten days, the anniversary celebration was felt across Okpe Kingdom. From Orerokpe, the traditional headquarters of the kingdom, to Sapele, Osubi and other communities, the atmosphere reflected the significance of the historic milestone. Several streets were beautifully decorated in vibrant colours, while residents and visitors joined in the festivities.

Governors, former governors, traditional rulers, business moguls, sports personalities, golfers and other prominent Nigerians turned out to celebrate the monarch, who is also Chairman of the Delta State Traditional Rulers Council. His colleagues from different kingdoms in Delta State and beyond were equally on hand to share in his moment of glory.

The impressive list of dignitaries included Bayelsa State Governor, Senator Douye Diri; Kogi State Governor, Alhaji Ahmed Usman Ododo; Taraba State Governor, Dr Agbu Kefas; former Delta State governors, Chief James Ibori and Senator Ifeanyi Okowa; and Delta State Deputy Governor, Sir Monday Onyeme.

Also present were the Olu of Warri, Ogiame Atuwatse III; the Ovie of Uvwie Kingdom; the Pere of Gbaramatu Kingdom; the Asagba of Asaba; the Ovie of Idjerhe Kingdom; several other prominent traditional leaders from the north , as well as representatives of the Chief of Army Staff.

Other notable personalities included the Chairman of Vanguard newspaper , Mr Sam Amuka, alongside prominent business leaders, political figures and other well-wishers who came to identify with the revered monarch.

The ten-day programme featured a variety of activities reflecting the monarch’s interests and the cultural heritage of the kingdom. The celebration began with a prayer session in Orerokpe, after which the monarch embarked on visits to major communities across Okpe Kingdom.

He also flagged off a golf tournament at the Athletic Club, Sapele, and a football competition at the Sapele Township Stadium, attracting sports enthusiasts and other participants to this part of his kingdom.

Speaking on the significance of the anniversary, the Unu Okpe (Traditional Prime Minister of Okpe Kingdom), Chief Michael Affe, said the monarch ascended the throne of his ancestors in 2006 following the demise of his predecessor, HRM Orhorho I.

According to him, the past 20 years have witnessed remarkable progress in peace, unity, urban development and educational advancement across the kingdom.

“Today, 20 years after, we look in retrospect with much pride at a reign that has brought exceptional harmony, urban development and educational advancement to Okpe Kingdom. Without a doubt, His Royal Majesty’s kingship has brought unity to Okpe people and positioned the kingdom as a beacon of progress.

“We make bold to say that Okpe Kingdom is more peaceful, more united and more respected across Delta State and Nigeria as a result of HRM’s purposeful leadership,” he said.

Chief Affe explained that the monarch, recognising the vast geographical spread of the kingdom and its estimated 200 communities, introduced administrative reforms by dividing it into districts to strengthen traditional administration and bring governance closer to the people.

He said the kingdom initially had 13 districts, with a 14th district, Ugolo II, recently created by the monarch, adding that district heads were appointed to oversee their respective areas.

Before ascending the throne, the Orodje had an illustrious career in the Nigerian Army, where he retired with the rank of Major General. He occupied several strategic positions, including Director of Army Legal Services, Provost Marshal of the Nigerian Army, General Officer Commanding (GOC), 2 Division, Ibadan, and GOC, 82 Division, Enugu.

He also served as ECOMOG Force Commander in Sierra Leone and Liberia, as well as Commander, Training and Doctrine Command, Nigerian Army, Minna.

In addition to his military career, the monarch studied law and was called to the Nigerian Bar. He also attended the Judge Advocate General’s School in the United States and was awarded an honorary Doctor of Laws (LL.D.)

The Orodje currently serves as Chancellor of the Nigerian Army University, Biu; Chairman of the Delta State Traditional Rulers Council; a member of the National Council of Traditional Rulers of Nigeria; and Chairman of the Association of Traditional Rulers of Mineral-Producing Communities of Nigeria (TROMPCON).

He was also Chancellor of Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu University, Anambra State, from November 24, 2012, to July 2021.

He has several honours and awards to his credit.

The memories of the 20th coronation anniversary will linger for long. The event added additional glamour and beauty to the kingdom and its rich cultural values.

Vanguard News

content:
• Agwarive urges Oborevwori to press NDDC or take over project

 By Ochuko Akuopha

AGBARHA-OTOR—For the people of Eriemu oil field, Agbarha-Otor, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, the road to a better life was supposed to be paved with asphalt. Instead, it is a treacherous, marshy track of broken dreams.

In a region that pumps the black gold that fuels the nation, the communities of Owevwe, Otokutu, Opherin, Saniko, Gana, Agbaide, and Ughere are drowning in a sea of neglect. They are the hosts of two Oil Mining Leases (OMLs 26 and 30), home to over 30 oil wells, a flow station, a Nigerian Gas Company plant, and the biggest manifold in West Africa.

Yet, for over a decade, the residents have been held hostage by a single, glaring failure: an 11-kilometre stretch of road that was supposed to connect them to the world, but which now only connects them to frustration.

A promise turned mirage

The year was 2010. After years of agitation, the Niger-Delta Development Commission, NDDC finally awarded a contract to construct the road. The residents were overjoyed. Here, finally, was the promise of relief, a smooth drive to the Ughelli-Asaba expressway, a lifeline for their businesses, and a path for their children to get to school safely. But that hope was a mirage.

No sooner had the contractor mobilised to the site than the equipment was withdrawn. The reason, allegedly, was a familiar one: a lack of funds from the interventionist agency. Sixteen years later, the road remains an abandoned scar on the landscape.

The stretch that was meant to connect Otokutu community to the expressway, and Saniko to Emevor-Agbarha Road, is now a daily obstacle course of potholes and despair.

“You wake up every day and see the same abandoned road,” laments Comrade Pender Agwarive, a man whose title, Chairman, Board of Trustees, PIA OML 30 Uherevie Host Community Development Trust, belies the powerlessness he feels.

“The road was expected to bring relief and improve our socio-economic lives. Instead, it has left our people disappointed and frustrated.”

Agwarive, who is also the HOSTCOM Chairman for the Urhobo Ethnic Nationality in Delta Central, has been a firsthand witness to the saga, recalling the initial excitement, the contractor’s arrival, and then the slow, painful demobilisation.

“The community noticed the contractor was gradually leaving.We tried to persuade him to return. We held peaceful protests at the NDDC headquarters in Port Harcourt.

“We were told the contract was re-awarded to a new company. Their representatives even came to introduce themselves. They never returned. The road has remained abandoned up till now,” he lamented.

A matter of life and death

For the people, the consequences are not just an inconvenience; they are a matter of life and death. The Owevwe-Otokutu axis has become a notorious hunting ground for kidnappers and armed robbers, preying on travellers forced to navigate the crumbling, isolated road.

“The abandonment has caused us a lot of pain and hardship. It has exposed our people to serious security threats.

“We host the oil facilities that generate Nigeria’s wealth, yet we cannot boast of a motorable road. It is a painful irony,” Mr. Newworld Ehwre, President- General of Owevwe Community,” told NDV.

“The story of this road is a microcosm of the broken promise of the Niger-Delta, a region where immense wealth coexists with abject poverty, and where communities are expected to swallow the bitter pill of neglect while their resources are carted away,” a resident who pleaded anonymity said.

Appeal to Gov Oborevwori

Now, the community leaders are making a desperate plea to the Delta State Governor, Rt. Hon. Sheriff Oborevwori. They are asking him to intervene, to prevail on the NDDC, or, in a last-ditch effort, to have the state government take over the project.

“We are appealing to the Governor to come to our rescue. We want to see a road. We want to see progress,” Agwarive said.

title: Delta attack: Nobody will kill at rallies if law catches up with them  —  Falana
description:
Senior Advocate of Nigeria and human rights activist Femi Falana has warned that recurring pre-election violence and political killings will persist unless perpetrators face swift prosecution and legal accountability ahead of the 2027 polls.







Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on
content:
Senior Advocate of Nigeria and human rights activist Femi Falana has warned that recurring pre-election violence and political killings will persist unless perpetrators face swift prosecution and legal accountability ahead of the 2027 polls.

Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, Falana described recent election-related fatalities — including killings reported in Delta State — as tragic and preventable, blaming entrenched impunity across past tragedies and political clashes.

He noted that attacks on political figures and convoys are often met with little or no consequence, creating a climate where violent tactics are normalized.

“The stakes are high for the political class, but in this unfortunate incident, nothing may come of it. Yesterday, we lost scores of people in Bayelsa State in what was a boat accident. What would happen? Donations have already started; who is the owner of the boat?

“Nobody would have thought they were going to kill people in a rally if they know that the law will catch up with them,” Falana said.

Falana urged the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), civil society, and other stakeholders to step up rather than leaving political affairs solely to politicians.

“Arrests may be made in Delta State, but I am challenging the Nigerian Bar Association and the human rights community to intervene very decisively because if we leave the affairs of our country in the hands of politicians, we will run into a serious crisis,” he said.

He further called on the NBA to mobilize lawyers to help the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) prosecute electoral offenders, arguing that INEC is already stretched by pre-election and post-election litigation and lacks the bandwidth to handle prosecutions alone.

Beyond electoral violence and credibility concerns — such as voter register cleanup, official accountability, and result transmission — Falana pressed political parties and candidates to campaign on concrete governance issues rather than ethnicity or religion.

He pointed to unspent basic education funds at the state level, compulsory health insurance and child rights laws, fuel subsidy controversies, crude-for-loans commitments, and stalled refinery rehabilitations as areas requiring public debate and enforcement.

Despite mounting frustrations, Falana rejected the idea that Nigeria is beyond hope, arguing that existing laws can drive change if citizens, the media, and civil society enforce accountability.

“So for me it’s not a hopeless situation. It is about promoting debates and that’s what I miss,” he said, adding that Nigerians must discuss issues and hold leaders accountable rather than merely watching political spectacles

The vessel, operated by the Senegalese Consorti
content:
Gambiaj.com – (DAKAR, SENEGAL) – The planned maritime route between Senegal and The Gambia has moved closer to reality after the Senegalese vessel Aguène successfully completed a return trial voyage between Dakar and Banjul on November 17 and 18, 2026.

The vessel, operated by the Senegalese Consortium of Maritime Activities (COSAMA), completed the test journey as part of preparations for the proposed Dakar-Banjul-Dakar maritime service.

The trial was conducted in the presence of Senegal’s Minister of Fisheries and Maritime Economy, Amy Mara Dieye, Gambian maritime and port authorities, and a COSAMA delegation led by its Director General, Dr Baba Tall.

The participation of officials from both countries underscored the importance attached to the initiative as part of efforts to strengthen bilateral maritime cooperation.

Beyond establishing a direct sea connection between the two capitals, the project is expected to facilitate the movement of people and goods, boost commercial exchanges and improve transport links between the neighboring countries.

It also forms part of Senegal’s broader ambition to strengthen maritime connectivity among coastal cities and countries, in line with the Senegal 2050 National Transformation Agenda championed by President Bassirou Diomaye Faye.

With the trial voyage successfully completed, the commercial launch of the Dakar-Banjul-Dakar service is expected in the coming weeks. However, the authorities have yet to announce the operational arrangements, including schedules, fares and passenger access conditions.

The new service could provide an alternative transport corridor between the two countries, whose populations share longstanding economic, social and family ties.

title: Intrigues, factors shaping battle for 7 North-West states
description:
By  Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo, Haruna Aliyu, Musa Ubandawaki, Idris Salisu, Fauziyya Lawal, Hadiza Yusuf & Muhammad Inuwa



THE battle for the seven North-West state government houses of Kaduna, Jigawa, Sokoto, Kano, Kebbi, Katsina and Zamfara is gathering momentum ahead of the February 6, 2027 governors
content:
By  Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo, Haruna Aliyu, Musa Ubandawaki, Idris Salisu, Fauziyya Lawal, Hadiza Yusuf & Muhammad Inuwa

THE battle for the seven North-West state government houses of Kaduna, Jigawa, Sokoto, Kano, Kebbi, Katsina and Zamfara is gathering momentum ahead of the February 6, 2027 governorship elections, with incumbent governors seeking fresh mandates amid growing opposition activities, political defections and shifting alliances.

Although the All Progressives Congress, APC, controls all the states and enjoys the advantage of incumbency, the emerging political landscape suggests that none of the contests can be taken for granted. The African Democratic Congress, ADC, is positioning itself as a rallying platform for politicians dissatisfied with the ruling party, while the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, is banking on its traditional grassroots structures and political networks.

In Kaduna, Governor Uba Sani faces a familiar challenger, Isa Ashiru of the ADC. In Jigawa, Governor Umar Namadi confronts Mustapha Sule Lamido of the PDP and Senator Sabo Muhammad Nakudu of the ADC. Sokoto presents a potentially bruising contest between Governor Ahmed Aliyu and former Deputy Governor Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, while Kano Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf faces opposition candidates and the political consequences of his separation from former political benefactor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso.

In Kebbi, Governor Nasir Idris faces former Attorney-General of the Federation, Abubakar Malami, who is seeking to capitalise on public dissatisfaction. Katsina Governor Dikko Umaru Radda is challenged by Senators Yakubu Lado Danmarke and Ahmad Babba Kaita of the PDP and ADC respectively. In Zamfara, Governor Dauda Lawal, who defected from the PDP to the APC, faces Senator Kabiru Marafa of the National Democratic Congress, NDC, and other opposition candidates.

Across the seven states, insecurity, particularly banditry, kidnapping, attacks on rural communities and displacement, is emerging as a defining electoral issue. Economic hardship, unemployment, poverty and the rising cost of living will also influence voters’ assessment of the incumbents.

The governors must contend with internal party rivalries and the challenge of translating government projects and political appointments into votes. The opposition, on its part, must convert public dissatisfaction, endorsements and growing political visibility into effective grassroots mobilisation.

ZAMFARA: Lawal, Marafa in security-driven battle Zamfara

Governor banks on APC and federal backing, development projects as banditry and opposition realignments shape contest

The battle for Zamfara Government House is gathering momentum ahead of the February 2027 governorship election, with incumbent Governor Dauda Lawal seeking re-election on the APC platform after defecting from the PDP, the party on which he won in 2023.

His major challenger is Senator Kabiru Marafa of the NDC, while Bulyaminu Yusuf Shinkafi of the ADC and Hamza Musa Maibulawis of the SDP are also in the race.

Lawal banks on projects, federal backing

Lawal is expected to campaign on his administration’s performance in infrastructure, education, healthcare and other sectors across Zamfara’s 14 local government areas.

His supporters argue that the administration has made significant progress in transforming the state within a relatively short period.

Former Deputy Speaker Namadi Isah Kasuwar Daji has expressed confidence in the governor’s performance, declaring that there is “no vacancy” in Zamfara Government House in 2027.

Lawal is also expected to benefit from the political advantages associated with the APC and its federal connections.

Pro-President Bola Tinubu mobilisation has been active in Gusau, including the presentation of campaign vehicles for the Tinubu Door-to-Door Movement at the Government House. Defence Minister Bello Mohammed Matawalle has also pledged to boost highway security while rallying support for the APC.

However, insecurity remains the biggest obstacle to Lawal’s re-election bid. Banditry, attacks on communities and disruption of livelihoods have continued to affect parts of the state.

The opposition is expected to make the security situation a major campaign issue, questioning the administration’s ability to protect lives and property.

The governor’s development projects may strengthen his appeal, but voters will also assess progress in restoring peace, securing rural communities and enabling farmers to return to their fields.

Marafa seeks to exploit security concerns

Senator Kabiru Marafa of the NDC is seeking to capitalise on dissatisfaction with insecurity and the political realignment following Lawal’s defection to the APC.

Marafa, who comes from Zamfara Central, is regarded by his supporters as a politician with a substantial following.

A political group backing his ambition, Marafa Ambassadors for Change, has declared its intention to challenge Lawal’s administration and mobilise support for the senator.

The group’s state coordinator, Comrade Mukhtar Yahuza General, described it as a movement comprising graduates, young people, professionals and businesspeople united by their support for Marafa.

The group accused Lawal’s administration of failing to address insecurity and protect lives and property.

It praised Marafa, declaring: “He cannot lie, he cannot cheat, and he cannot betray his people, while countless politicians do not have these qualities.”

The endorsement reflects the group’s confidence in Marafa, although the extent to which its support can translate into votes remains to be seen.

His major challenge will be building a statewide political structure capable of competing with the incumbent’s government machinery and the APC’s federal connections.

ADC, SDP candidates seek regional support

ADC candidate Bulyaminu Yusuf Shinkafi comes from Zamfara North and is expected to draw support from his home zone.

The district comprises Shinkafi, Zurmi, Birnin Magaji and Kaura-Namoda local government areas, which have experienced serious bandit attacks.

The security challenges could create an opening for Shinkafi among residents seeking stronger representation and a different approach to tackling insecurity.

However, his lack of broad popularity across Zamfara could limit his chances. He must extend his appeal beyond the North and attract support across the state’s 14 local government areas.

The SDP candidate, Hamza Musa Maibulawis, could draw support from Gusau and other parts of the Central zone because of his geographical connection to the area. Nevertheless, his statewide political visibility and organisational strength appear limited.

Incumbency, El-Rufai’s influence, opposition realignment, Southern Kaduna’s expectations shape contest in Kaduna

The battle for Sir Kashim Ibrahim House is taking shape ahead of the February 6, 2027 election, with Governor Uba Sani of the APC seeking a second term against Isa Ashiru of the ADC, who is making another attempt to govern Kaduna State.

Although 16 political parties have candidates in the race, attention is increasingly focused on the two leading contenders and the ability of the opposition to consolidate around a common alternative.

Other candidates include Adamu Alhaji Ahamed of the Action Alliance, AA; Solomon John Yayock of the Action Democratic Party, ADP; Tukur Rabiu of APGA; Haruna Yunusa Saeed of the Allied Peoples Movement, APM; Rilwanu Muhammad Lawal of the Labour Party, LP; Bawa Shehu Usman of the PDP; Abdulfattah Muhammad Aminu of the PRP; Idris Adamu Abubakar of the SDP and candidates of other parties.

Uba Sani banks on incumbency, expanding coalition

Uba Sani enters the contest with the advantages of incumbency, control of government machinery and the backing of the APC establishment. His political network extends across the state’s 23 local government areas.

His coalition has expanded beyond traditional APC supporters. Former governor Ramalan Yero, former senator Shehu Sani, former senator Suleiman Hunkuyi, Senator Sunday Marshall Katung and other influential politicians have become associated with his camp.

The governor has also attracted politicians previously associated with his predecessor, Nasir El-Rufai. The October defection of former Finance Commissioner Muhammad Bashir Sa’idu, former Education Commissioner Jafaru Sani and former senator Suleiman Abdu Kwari from the ADC to the APC was significant.

Sa’idu claimed that his political organisation brought more than 200,000 supporters into the APC. Uba Sani subsequently announced that the party was targeting three million votes in Kaduna.

The governor’s calculation is that the expanding coalition, combined with his administration’s record and the APC’s organisational strength, will improve his re-election prospects. The real test, however, is whether the alliances will translate into votes.

Ashiru makes another attempt

For Ashiru, 2027 represents another opportunity to realise his governorship ambition. He contested against El-Rufai in 2019 and Uba Sani in 2023, finishing second on both occasions.

In 2023, he secured 719,196 votes against Uba Sani’s 730,002, demonstrating his substantial electoral following.

His emergence as the ADC candidate has placed him in a new political arrangement involving some former associates of El-Rufai. Ashiru secured the party’s ticket in May 2026 with 86,113 votes, defeating several aspirants, including Jafaru Sani.

He has appointed John Ayuba, a former commissioner under the administrations of Patrick Yakowa and Ramalan Yero, as Director-General of his campaign organisation.

His challenge is to consolidate his political base, retain the El-Rufai network’s support and prevent internal disagreements from weakening his campaign.

El-Rufai and Southern Kaduna factors

The relationship between Uba Sani and his former political benefactor, El-Rufai, remains a major factor. Their differences have reshaped alliances within the APC and opposition.

El-Rufai’s association with the ADC initially raised expectations that his political network would provide Ashiru with substantial organisational support. However, defections by some former associates to the APC have complicated that calculation.

The November 12 defection of members of the Nasiriyya Youth and other former ADC supporters to Uba Sani’s camp further illustrates the fluidity of the political alignment.

Southern Kaduna will also be a critical battleground. Expectations concerning representation, security, development and inclusion in government will influence voting decisions.

While Uba Sani must demonstrate that his administration has addressed longstanding concerns, Ashiru must convince voters across the three senatorial districts that he offers a credible statewide alternative.

Ultimately, security, unemployment, agriculture, infrastructure, education and healthcare will shape the electorate’s assessment. Uba Sani has incumbency and an expanding coalition on his side, but Ashiru’s previous electoral performance and opposition realignment make the contest worth watching.

Namadi, Lamido, Nakudu in three-way race in Jigawa

Jigawa State is heading towards a potentially competitive governorship election, with Governor Umar Namadi of the APC facing Mustapha Sule Lamido of the PDP and Senator Sabo Muhammad Nakudu of the ADC.

The state has 27 local government areas, 4,522 polling units and 2,867,787 registered voters. Its three senatorial districts—North-East, South-West and North-West—will be central to the candidates’ calculations.

Lamido banks on political legacy, PDP structures

Mustapha Sule Lamido enters the race with considerable goodwill, particularly among young people, and the advantage of belonging to a party with established electoral structures in Jigawa.

His origin from Jigawa South-West, traditionally a PDP stronghold, gives him an important starting point. The zone has seven local government areas and was the only senatorial district where the PDP won the Senate, House of Representatives and State House of Assembly seats during the 2023 elections.

His political standing is also associated with the influence and legacy of his father, former Governor Sule Lamido. Projects and political activities undertaken during his father’s administration remain important reference points for some voters.

The movement of two former APC Speakers of the Jigawa State House of Assembly into the PDP could further improve his prospects through their political connections and grassroots influence.

However, defections from the PDP, particularly to the ADC, threaten to weaken its structure and fragment its traditional support base.

Vice President Kashim Shettima’s recent assertion that former Jigawa governors, including Sule Lamido, were supporting the APC has also generated controversy. Although the former governor rejected the claim, it introduced another dimension into the political debate.

Nakudu seeks to establish ADC as a force

Senator Sabo Muhammad Nakudu is banking on the ADC’s growing national visibility to establish the party as a serious contender.

Dissatisfaction with Federal Government policies could create an opening for the ADC to attract voters seeking an alternative to the established parties. Internal divisions within the APC may also provide opportunities for the opposition.

Nakudu’s choice of Aminu Ibrahim Ringim as running mate is another factor in the party’s calculations. Ringim’s political relationships and local connections could help the ADC extend its influence.

However, Nakudu faces a significant challenge because he and Lamido come from the same senatorial district. Their rivalry could divide the opposition’s traditional support base and benefit the APC.

Disagreements within the ADC at state and national levels could also undermine its mobilisation efforts. Nakudu must convert the party’s growing visibility and political alliances into an effective structure across all 27 local government areas.

Namadi relies on performance, APC machinery

Namadi enters the election with the advantages of incumbency and the ruling party’s political machinery.

His administration’s record in infrastructure, agriculture, youth empowerment and other development programmes is expected to form a major part of his campaign.

Coming from Jigawa North-East, which has eight local government areas, the governor has an opportunity to build his electoral strength around his home zone. However, he will need substantial support in the South-West and North-West.

The defection of influential opposition politicians into the APC, including a PDP member of the State House of Assembly representing Birnin Kudu and an NNPP member of the House of Representatives representing Gwaram, could improve the party’s mobilisation network.

Despite these advantages, economic hardship associated with Federal Government policies, including fuel subsidy removal and tax reforms, could generate dissatisfaction that affects APC candidates.

Internal disagreements among APC stakeholders also represent a potential threat.

Ultimately, Lamido must retain the PDP’s South-West stronghold and expand into other zones. Nakudu must transform the ADC’s national visibility into grassroots strength, while Namadi must defend his record and prevent opposition fragmentation from becoming a serious threat.

SOKOTO: Aliyu, Dan’iya brace for showdown as APC, ADC jostle for power

Wamakko’s political machinery backs incumbent as Tambuwal’s influence, insecurity and economic hardship fuel opposition hopes

The 2027 Sokoto governorship election is shaping up as a contest between the ruling APC, led by Governor Ahmed Aliyu, and the ADC, whose candidate, former Deputy Governor Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, is emerging as a formidable challenger.

The Labour Party’s Haliru Dikko and the NDC candidate, Shamsuddeen Aliyu Haido, are also in the race, although their prospects appear more difficult.

Aliyu banks on Wamakko’s political machinery

Aliyu enters the contest with considerable political advantages. His strongest asset is the support of former Governor and APC leader in Sokoto, Senator Aliyu Magatakarda Wamakko, whose political influence and grassroots network remain critical to the state’s political calculations.

The governor also enjoys the backing of serving political officeholders, the 23 local government council chairmen, senior government officials and other influential stakeholders.

As incumbent, Aliyu has the opportunity to showcase his administration’s achievements in infrastructure, security, public services and other sectors.

However, political endorsements and government structures do not automatically guarantee victory. He must convince voters that his administration has adequately addressed their economic difficulties and insecurity.

Dan’iya rides on opposition sentiment, Tambuwal’s influence

For Dan’iya, the election offers an opportunity to transform his political experience and growing opposition support into an electoral breakthrough.

A former deputy governor, Commissioner for Local Government Affairs and local government chairman, he is familiar with Sokoto’s political and administrative structures.

His potential advantage is the support he enjoys among communities affected by persistent banditry and criminal activities. Residents displaced by insecurity are looking towards political alternatives capable of restoring peace and rebuilding their communities.

Economic hardship, rising living costs, unemployment and poverty have also created dissatisfaction with the ruling establishment.

The ADC hopes to capitalise on this sentiment. Its presidential candidate, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, used his campaign flag-off in Sokoto to promise to address insecurity, restore petroleum subsidy arrangements and improve citizens’ welfare if elected in 2027.

The large crowd reportedly witnessed at the rally further energised the party’s supporters, although rally attendance does not necessarily translate into votes.

Dan’iya also enjoys the backing of former Sokoto Governor and former Speaker of the House of Representatives, Aminu Waziri Tambuwal, whose political network remains influential across the state.

His challenge is to translate this support into effective election-day organisation, including polling agents, mobilisation structures and resources to compete against an incumbent government.

LP, NDC face uphill task

Labour Party candidate Haliru Dikko, a retired Permanent Secretary in the Sokoto State Civil Service, brings administrative experience to the contest. However, his emergence following the withdrawal of the initial candidate, Aminu Umar, popularly known as Maxia, raises questions about the party’s preparedness and internal cohesion.

Haido, on the other hand, is a relatively new face in Sokoto politics. He spent much of his political and professional life in Kaduna before emerging as a governorship contender in his home state.

His visibility increased during the visit of former presidential candidate Peter Obi and former Kano State Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso to Sokoto for stakeholders’ and youth engagement meetings and their visit to the internally displaced persons’ camp at Ramen Kura.

On July 2, 2026, Haido hosted a unity meeting at the NDC state secretariat, bringing together members of the State Executive Committee, chairmen of the 23 local government areas, party aspirants and members of the OK Movement. The meeting focused on party unity and grassroots mobilisation.

Nevertheless, both the LP and NDC face organisational and financial limitations compared with the APC and ADC.

The Sokoto contest could ultimately become a referendum on the incumbent’s performance and the opposition’s promise of change. Aliyu has Wamakko’s political machinery behind him, while Dan’iya has Tambuwal’s influence and the ADC’s growing appeal.

APC crisis, Kwankwasiyya factor test Yusuf’s second-term bid in Kano

Governor faces ADC and NDC challengers as political realignments, court battles and internal divisions shape contest

With 78 days to the February 6, 2027 governorship election, the battle for Kano is taking shape, although political activities among the major parties have remained relatively low-key.

Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, seeking re-election on the APC platform, faces challenges arising from divisions within his party and the political consequences of his separation from former political benefactor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso.

His major challengers are Ibrahim Ali Amin, popularly known as Little, of the ADC and Aminu Abdussalam Gwarzo, a former deputy governor, of the NDC.

Yusuf enjoys the advantage of incumbency and the backing of influential APC figures, including former governors Abdullahi Ganduje and Ibrahim Shekarau, Deputy Senate President Barau Jibrin and other stakeholders.

However, his biggest challenge may come from within the APC. Disagreements among stakeholders, including interests associated with Barau Jibrin and Deputy Governor Murtala Sule Garo, could affect the party’s unity.

Although Garo is Yusuf’s running mate, reconciling competing interests will be crucial to the governor’s re-election chances.

Another development with possible political implications is Yusuf’s marital crisis involving his second wife, Zainab Musa Kwankwaso, a relative of his former political ally. The governor confirmed that he had initiated steps to dissolve the marriage, while the divorce case was adjourned to December 15.

Although personal, the matter could have political implications given Yusuf’s separation from Kwankwaso and defection from the NNPP to the APC. It could affect his relationship with some supporters loyal to the Kwankwasiyya movement.

ADC, NDC seek opening

ADC candidate Little is positioning himself as an alternative to the ruling party. His running mate, Shehu Abdulkadir Bari, is an ICT and artificial intelligence specialist from Rogo Local Government Area.

The party’s agenda focuses on industrialisation, education, healthcare, agriculture, infrastructure and youth and women’s empowerment.

Little has constituted an 18-member campaign council and secured a favourable court ruling in a legal challenge brought by Sheikh Ibrahim Khalil. The November 18 ruling dismissed the challenge as statute-barred, removing a major legal obstacle to his candidacy.

The NDC is also hoping to challenge the APC through Gwarzo, who has Mustapha Kwankwaso, son of the former governor, as running mate.

However, the party faces a legal battle over recognition of its candidates by INEC. Their names were omitted from the commission’s initial final candidate list following a suit by three aggrieved party members challenging their emergence.

On October 27, the Federal High Court in Kano issued an interim order restraining INEC from publishing the NDC candidates pending the hearing of the substantive case. The commission subsequently retained the party on its updated list with the notation, “Court Order”, instead of the candidates’ names.

The NDC accused the APC of being behind efforts to prevent its candidates from appearing on the ballot, alleging that the ruling party fears the Kwankwasiyya movement. The APC denied the allegation and challenged the NDC to provide evidence linking it or Governor Yusuf to the lawsuit.

The NDC has yet to commence its campaign in Kano. Its prospects could improve if the legal dispute is resolved in its favour. Gwarzo’s experience as a former deputy governor and Mustapha Kwankwaso’s political connection could provide an important platform.

For Yusuf, the priority is to manage APC divisions, defend his record and prevent the Kwankwasiyya factor from becoming an electoral liability. The opposition must overcome its legal and organisational challenges.

KEBBI: Idris, Malami in high-stakes battle

Rider: Governor banks on infrastructure and APC heavyweights as former AGF exploits insecurity and public discontent

The contest for Kebbi Government House is increasingly taking shape between incumbent Governor Nasir Idris of the APC and former Attorney-General of the Federation, Abubakar Chika Malami, who is seeking the governorship on the ADC platform.

Idris is expected to make infrastructure development and interventions in critical sectors the centrepiece of his re-election campaign.

Before he assumed office, successive administrations were accused of neglecting Birnin Kebbi, with the state capital lacking adequate road networks and other urban infrastructure.

His administration has undertaken road construction and rehabilitation in the state capital, alongside improvements to roundabouts and township roads.

Another advantage is his political strategy of reaching out to different segments of the population through appointments. His administration has appointed more than 5,000 aides in different categories, a strategy intended to bring government closer to the people and expand its political network.

Idris also enjoys the backing of influential politicians, including Senator Adamu Aliero, Senator Yahaya Abdullahi, former governors Saidu Nasamu Dakingari and Atiku Bagudu, as well as grassroots political figures.

Their influence could strengthen APC mobilisation across the state. However, the governor must demonstrate that the projects and appointments have translated into tangible improvements in people’s lives.

Malami banks on ADC momentum, insecurity concerns

Malami hopes to draw strength from the growing national visibility of the ADC and its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar.

He is also banking on public dissatisfaction with the APC, particularly over insecurity and the disruption of farming activities in parts of the North.

Persistent attacks by armed bandits have affected rural communities, undermined agricultural activities and heightened concerns about government’s ability to protect lives and property.

Malami’s calculation is that a strong ADC performance at the presidential level could improve the chances of its candidates in the states.

He has also made attractive pledges to civil servants, traditional rulers and traders in Kebbi, seeking to appeal to groups that may feel the incumbent administration has not done enough for them.

His arrests and detention by anti-graft agencies have generated public attention and sympathy among some sections of the electorate, which his supporters could seek to translate into votes.

Nevertheless, Malami must demonstrate that the ADC has the organisational strength to challenge the APC’s established structures.

For Idris, the challenge is to defend his development record and address security concerns. For Malami, it is to convert public dissatisfaction and the ADC’s growing profile into a credible electoral coalition.

KATSINA: Lado, Babba Kaita challenge APC, Radda’s dominance

Development record and APC machinery give incumbent an edge, but insecurity and economic hardship threaten ruling party’s dominance

The battle for Katsina Government House is taking shape, with incumbent Governor Dikko Umaru Radda of the APC facing Senator Yakubu Lado Danmarke of the PDP and Senator Ahmad Babba Kaita of the ADC.

Although Radda has the advantage of incumbency and the ruling party’s political machinery, the opposition is seeking to make the contest competitive.

Radda banks on development record, APC structure

Radda’s strongest selling point is his administration’s development record. Since assuming office, his government has embarked on road construction and rehabilitation, as well as the upgrading of schools and healthcare facilities.

His administration has also introduced programmes in agriculture, education, healthcare, women empowerment and youth development.

The APC’s structures across the state’s 34 local government areas and 361 wards, alongside the support of party stakeholders, elected officials and political appointees, strengthen his position.

However, insecurity remains a major concern in several communities, while economic hardship, unemployment and rising living costs continue to shape public opinion.

How convincingly Radda addresses these challenges and communicates his achievements will determine whether his development record translates into votes.

Lado relies on grassroots appeal

For the PDP, Senator Yakubu Lado Danmarke presents a formidable challenge, particularly because of his grassroots connections and reputation for humanitarian interventions and empowerment programmes.

His supporters point to his assistance to students, empowerment initiatives and support for less privileged residents, including people facing serious health challenges.

His November 18 campaign flag-off, which attracted an impressive gathering, demonstrated the PDP’s determination to challenge the ruling party.

Lado’s experience in the House of Representatives and Senate also gives him an established political platform.

However, his association with FCT Minister Nyesom Wike has generated mixed perceptions among some voters. Critics portray him as a political ally of the former Rivers State governor.

Whether this becomes an electoral liability will depend on his ability to establish an independent political identity and convince voters that his ambition is driven by Katsina’s interests.

He must also maintain PDP unity and attract voters beyond the party’s traditional supporters.

Babba Kaita banks on experience

Senator Ahmad Babba Kaita of the ADC brings political experience and a record of constituency representation to the contest.

During his tenure in the Senate, he attracted attention through empowerment initiatives and interventions aimed at improving constituents’ welfare.

However, questions have been raised about his temperament and whether his perceived hot temper aligns with the patience, restraint and tolerance expected of a governor.

Convincing voters that he possesses the necessary leadership qualities will be important to his ambition.

He must also build an effective statewide structure rather than rely mainly on support around his former senatorial constituency.

On balance, Radda appears to have an advantage because of incumbency, APC structures and his administration’s development projects. But insecurity and economic difficulties could undermine his chances.

Lado could benefit from his humanitarian appeal and grassroots connections, while Babba Kaita’s political experience gives him a platform to compete. Both must demonstrate wider statewide acceptance.

The deciding factors

Across the seven states, the 2027 governorship elections will be shaped by incumbency, political alliances, party structures, security, economic conditions and candidates’ records.

The APC governors enjoy government machinery, political appointments and established networks. However, these advantages could be undermined by internal disagreements, public dissatisfaction and failure to address pressing challenges.

The ADC’s emergence as a major opposition platform has altered political calculations in several states. Its ability to attract influential politicians and dissatisfied members of other parties could make it a significant force. The PDP, meanwhile, retains grassroots structures and political legacies that could prove decisive in states such as Jigawa and Katsina.

Ultimately, the elections will be determined not by defections, campaign vehicles, endorsements or rally crowds alone, but by candidates’ capacity to mobilise voters, maintain party unity, protect their votes and convince the electorate that they deserve another mandate.

For the incumbents, the question is whether their records justify another term. For the opposition, it is whether its promise of change can be translated into an organised and winning electoral movement.

title: Darboe’s Tough Talk Meets Reality as UDP Convoy Gives Way to Barrow
description: Gambiaj.com – (JANJANBUREH, THE GAMBIA) – UDP leader and opposition presidential candidate Ousainou Darboe’s warning that his campaign convoy would not be stopped by the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC), police or army ultimately ended without confrontation on Monday, as his supporters stopped
content:
Gambiaj.com – (JANJANBUREH, THE GAMBIA) – UDP leader and opposition presidential candidate Ousainou Darboe’s warning that his campaign convoy would not be stopped by the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC), police or army ultimately ended without confrontation on Monday, as his supporters stopped at YBK Junction to allow President Adama Barrow’s National People’s Party (NPP) convoy to pass.

Darboe had earlier issued a strong warning to the electoral commission and security forces while addressing supporters at Bantanto in Upper Fulladu West District, insisting that his campaign would proceed unhindered up to Koina.

Speaking before the gathering, Darboe placed the planned engagement in Boyeram at the center of his message, framing the visit as a test of peaceful political coexistence in the Central River Region as the UDP-led coalition intensifies its campaign ahead of the December 5 presidential election.

“If anyone wants to stop us from holding a meeting in Boyeram village, you don’t want peace. It means you want fitna,” he told supporters.

He insisted that the UDP would proceed peacefully but would not be intimidated, arguing that the right to campaign freely belonged to every Gambian.

Darboe also cautioned the IEC against attempting to stop his convoy and warned the police and army that his campaign was determined to move unhindered up to Koina.

He called on President Barrow and his ministers to recognize their responsibilities as the country’s highest authorities and set an example by avoiding actions that could create unnecessary tensions around his campaign activities.

The remarks came as both campaign delegations were operating in the same general area. The UDP was holding meetings along its route, while the NPP delegation was also moving between Janjanbureh and Brikama Ba, with plans to hold a rally in Janjanbureh and spend the night there.

However, despite Darboe’s combative rhetoric and warnings to the authorities, the anticipated confrontation did not materialize. Reports indicated that the UDP convoy stopped at YBK Junction to allow Barrow and his NPP campaign team to pass.

The development marked a notably calmer outcome than Darboe’s earlier statements had suggested, with neither the IEC nor the security forces reportedly having to intervene.

Earlier Encounter Passed Without Incident

The encounter at YBK Junction was not the first time the two rival campaign teams had crossed paths on Monday.

Earlier in the day, the UDP-led alliance convoy passed through Taifa, where President Barrow was holding a campaign meeting. Supporters of both camps cheered as the opposition convoy went through, with no incident reported.

The competing campaign activities have brought the two political camps into close proximity as they seek to consolidate support ahead of the December 5 presidential election.

While Darboe’s warning had raised the prospect of tensions over the movement of campaign convoys, the decision to allow Barrow’s delegation to pass suggested that, at least on this occasion, political rivalry did not translate into a confrontation on the road.

title: N4.11trn dividend: How 65 firms beat economic crunch
description:
*81 companies fail to pay *As earnings hit N9.29trn *MTN, Dangote Cement, BUA Foods, GTBank, Zenith, others dominate payout *Shareholders get cash, companies retain N5.18trn for growth *Analysts warn: High dividend payout could constrain expansion if earnings weaken



By Peter Egwuatu



For thousa
content:
*81 companies fail to pay *As earnings hit N9.29trn *MTN, Dangote Cement, BUA Foods, GTBank, Zenith, others dominate payout *Shareholders get cash, companies retain N5.18trn for growth *Analysts warn: High dividend payout could constrain expansion if earnings weaken

By Peter Egwuatu

For thousands of investors who put their money into the Nigerian stock market, the real reward from owning shares is often not the daily movement in stock prices, but the cash that eventually lands in their accounts.

That reward amounted to a staggering N4.11 trillion for shareholders of 65companies quoted on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX), as the companies paid out the sum as dividends from combined net income of N9.29 trillion in the financial year 2025, amid the ongoing economic reforms of the Federal Government.

The dividend payout comes against the backdrop of wide-ranging economic reforms by the Federal Government, including the removal of the petrol subsidy, exchange-rate reforms and measures aimed at improving government revenue, investment and the business environment.

Against this backdrop, dividend payments have become particularly significant for investors seeking to preserve returns and generate income amid persistent economic pressures.

The dividend declared means that the companies distributed about 44.2 per cent of their combined earnings to shareholders, leaving approximately N5.18 trillion, or 55.8 per cent, within the businesses.

For shareholders, the numbers represent a major income stream at a time when investors are increasingly looking for reliable returns from the capital market.

Vanguard’s latest findings show that, out of the 146 listed companies, 81 companies did not declare dividends to their shareholders.

But behind the dividend bonanza lies a bigger concern for the companies and the Nigerian economy: how much should businesses distribute today and how much should they retain to finance tomorrow’s growth?

MTN, Dangote Cemen, BUA Foods lead N4.11trn payout

The dividend distribution was heavily driven by some of the country’s biggest and most profitable listed companies.

MTN Nigeria topped the table with N860.83 billion in dividend payments, followed by Dangote Cement with N753.80 billion.

BUA Foods paid N504 billion, while Guaranty Trust Bank (GTBank) and Zenith Bank paid N429.83 billion and N410.69 billion, respectively.

BUA Cement distributed N338.64 billion, while HBM Nigeria paid N257.70 billion.

The other three companies that made the top 10 were Aradel Holdings, N99.0 billion; Stanbic IBTC Holdings, N63.61 billion; and Ecobank Transnational Incorporated, N52.80 billion.

The scale of the payouts shows the growing importance of large listed companies to investors who depend on dividend income.

For a retail investor holding shares directly, the dividend represents cash income. For pension funds and other institutional investors, dividends form part of the returns generated for millions of beneficiaries and clients.

Top 10 low-paying dividend companies

Vanguard’s analysis of the top 10 low-paying dividend companies shows that Industrial & Medical Gases Nigeria led the pack, recording N365.5 million, followed by Learn Africa with N303.758 million.

Chams Holding Company occupied the third position, posting N270.0 million. Meyer Plc recorded N223.977 million, followed by UPDC Plc with N185.671 million.

ABC Transport occupied the sixth position, while Academy Press followed, recording N90.7 million.

Other companies with low dividend payments included McNichols, recording N78.24 million; University Press, posting N77.65 million; and Multiverse Mining Exploration, recording N63.92 million.

Investors: Cash today versus value tomorrow

Analysts said the N4.11 trillion dividend payout could strengthen confidence in stocks because it demonstrates that listed companies are not merely vehicles for capital appreciation but also sources of regular income.

An investment analyst said: “Dividends provide tangible returns to shareholders. Investors can use the income for consumption, reinvest it in other securities or add it to their existing holdings.”

However, the analyst cautioned investors against judging companies simply by the size of their dividend.

“What matters is whether the dividend is supported by recurring earnings and adequate cash flow. A very high dividend from a company whose earnings are weakening may not be sustainable,” the analyst said.

This is particularly important because shareholders ultimately benefit from both current income and the future value of their investments.

Where a company retains adequate earnings and invests them profitably, shareholders could benefit from higher future earnings and potentially larger dividends. Conversely, excessive retention without productive deployment of funds could limit shareholder returns.

Companies retain N5.18trn for expansion

The other side of the dividend is the N5.18 trillion retained by the companies.

Analysts said the money could provide an important source of internally generated capital for businesses seeking to expand production, acquire technology, strengthen working capital, reduce debt or finance new projects.

The advantage is that companies can undertake such investments without relying entirely on bank loans or fresh equity injections.

The analyst said: “Retained earnings are one of the cheapest sources of corporate funding. If management can deploy them into projects that generate returns above the cost of capital, shareholders ultimately benefit.”

High payouts raise sustainability concerns

The data also show significant differences in the proportion of earnings distributed by the companies.

For instance, BUA Foods paid dividends equivalent to about 93.1 per cent of its net income, while Dangote Cement and BUA Cement paid about 66.7 per cent and 67.7 per cent, respectively.

MTN Nigeria’s dividend payout was about 61.1 per cent, while GTBank’s stood at approximately 52.4 per cent.

Analysts said a high payout ratio is not necessarily a weakness because mature companies with strong cash flows may have fewer immediate investment needs.

But for companies operating in capital-intensive sectors or those with significant expansion plans, retaining a larger proportion of earnings could provide greater financial flexibility.

However, the analyst warned that retaining money simply for the sake of retaining it does not necessarily create value.

“Investors will want to know what management is doing with retained earnings. If the company has profitable investment opportunities, retention makes sense. But if there are no attractive projects, shareholders may prefer a greater portion of the earnings to be distributed,” the analyst added.

Analysts’ comments

Commenting on the implications of dividend payouts and retained earnings, David Adonri, Managing Director of High Cap Securities Plc, said: “ Beyond individual investors and companies, the N4. 11 trillion dividend payment has implications for the wider Nigerian economy.

Dividends can stimulate economic activity when shareholders spend the income or reinvest it in other assets.

Institutional investors can also deploy dividend proceeds into other companies, government securities and other investments, thereby creating another channel through which corporate earnings circulate within the financial system.

He further said: “Money paid out as dividends is money that companies cannot simultaneously deploy to build new factories, increase production capacity, purchase machinery, develop technology or expand their workforce.

“Nigeria needs companies that are profitable enough to pay dividends and strong enough to continue investing. The objective should not be dividend maximisation alone, but sustainable corporate growth.

In fact, the overall figures underscore the growing role of the NGX in wealth distribution while highlighting the need for companies to strike a sustainable balance between dividend payments, retained earnings, capital investment and long-term growth.”

Speaking as well, Clifford Egbomeade, economic and communications expert, said: “ Stronger corporate investment could generate wider economic benefits through employment creation, increased production, tax revenues and development of local supply chains.

Another feature of the data is the concentration of dividend payments among a relatively small number of companies.

MTN Nigeria, Dangote Cement, BUA Foods, GTBank, Zenith Bank, BUA Cement and HBM Nigeria account for a substantial share of the total N4.11trillion distributed.

This means that a significant proportion of dividend income available to investors is being generated by a relatively small group of large and profitable companies.

The development underscores the importance of broadening the pool of profitable listed companies on the NGX.

A wider base of dividend-paying companies would give investors more choices and reduce dependence on a relatively small number of large corporations for equity income.”

On the N4.11 trillion dividend payout, he said: “It represents money flowing from corporate balance sheets into the hands of shareholders, while the N5.18 trillion retained represents potential funding for the next phase of corporate expansion.

“For investors, the immediate attraction is the cash return. For companies, the challenge is ensuring that retained earnings generate sufficient returns to justify keeping them within the business.

“For the Nigerian economy, the balance is equally important: dividends can deepen household and institutional income, while corporate reinvestment can create jobs, expand production and strengthen economic capacity.

“The performance of the 65 companies therefore highlights a fundamental capital-market equation reward shareholders today, but retain enough earnings to build the businesses that will generate tomorrow’s dividends.”

title: Gambian Teachers Warn Of Sit-Down Strike Over Three Months Of Unpaid Allowances
description:
Gambiaj.com – (BANJUL, THE GAMBIA) – Teachers across The Gambia are threatening a sit-down strike over three months of unpaid hardship and double-shift allowances, as the Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education (MoBSE) says it is working to settle the outstanding payments by 30 November.
The threa
content:
Gambiaj.com – (BANJUL, THE GAMBIA) – Teachers across The Gambia are threatening a sit-down strike over three months of unpaid hardship and double-shift allowances, as the Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education (MoBSE) says it is working to settle the outstanding payments by 30 November.

The threatened industrial action follows growing frustration among teachers who say they have continued to work under additional responsibilities without receiving the allowances attached to their duties.

Several affected teachers have called on the Gambia Teachers’ Union (GTU) to intervene, arguing that the delays have become unacceptable and that the union should consider industrial action if the government fails to meet its payment obligations.

One teacher described it as unfair that educators could work for nearly two months under double-shift arrangements without receiving the corresponding allowances.

The teacher urged the GTU to stand with its members and consider calling a sit-down strike if the outstanding payments are not settled.

Another teacher questioned why salaries had reportedly been paid while allowances and arrears remained outstanding. The teacher also raised concerns about the September school reopening date, which was initially scheduled for 14 September before being moved to 16 September.

“September has passed. October has passed. November is practically coming to an end,” the teacher said.

Teachers Question Government’s Commitment

Other teachers expressed frustration over what they described as a lack of consideration for their welfare, arguing that the education system continues to demand commitment and sacrifice from educators while delaying payments they are entitled to receive.

“Teachers are not slaves,” one teacher said, insisting that educators should not have to beg for allowances attached to work they have already performed.

The concerns also extend to the Foundation Learning Program (FLP), with one teacher questioning how millions of dalasis could be invested in the initiative while those responsible for implementing it continued to wait for their allowances.

The teacher argued that the success of education programs also depends on the welfare and motivation of the people delivering them.

Ministry Promises Payment By November 30

Meanwhile, MoBSE has acknowledged the delays, saying it is engaging relevant government institutions to facilitate payment.

The ministry’s Communications Officer, Saidou Jallow, confirmed that the allowances remained unpaid but said arrangements were underway to resolve the situation.

“About the delay of allowances, yes it is true,” Jallow said. “So the ministry has noted, the management in particular have noted the concerns. And already efforts are in place to engage with relevant government institutions to ensure that the allowances are paid effective next week, not later than the 30th of November.”

Jallow said the ministry had received assurances from the institutions responsible for processing the payments that the outstanding allowances would be settled by the stated deadline.

However, the ministry has not provided a detailed explanation for the delays, the number of teachers affected or the total amount owed.

With the 30 November deadline approaching, attention is now turning to whether the government will fulfill its commitment and avert the threatened industrial action.

For the affected teachers, the dispute goes beyond delayed payments. They say it is also about recognizing the additional responsibilities they have continued to shoulder without receiving the compensation attached to their work.

title: Delta attack: Obi calls for probe, protection of opposition supporters
description:
Peter Obi has condemned the killing of four supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Delta State, calling on security agencies to investigate the attack and bring the perpetrators and their sponsors to justice.







The former Anambra State governor also urged authorities to take urg
content:
Peter Obi has condemned the killing of four supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Delta State, calling on security agencies to investigate the attack and bring the perpetrators and their sponsors to justice.

The former Anambra State governor also urged authorities to take urgent steps to protect Nigerians participating in political activities, warning against the growing violence targeting opposition supporters.

Obi made the call in a statement posted on his X handle following an attack involving former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, and his supporters in Delta State.

He described the killing of the four people as a senseless act of violence, expressing concern over what he called repeated attacks on opposition supporters across the country.

“It is no longer sufficient for those responsible to fund the dissemination of false claims against the opposition. They have now escalated to the appalling practice of murdering innocent Nigerians solely because of their political affiliations,” he said.

The deceased, according to Obi, include Hon. Moses Anaughe, immediate past Federal Commissioner of the Federal Character Commission; Comrade Akima Efenena Umukoro, former President of the Urhobo Progress Union Youth Wing; Nyoren Okoro, an NDC chieftain; and another victim whose identity had yet to be established.

He said 15 other people sustained critical injuries and were hospitalised, including Hon. Evance Ivwurie, chairman of Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation, and Comrade Chuks Erhire, its director-general.

Obi expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and prayed for the recovery of the injured, while urging security agencies to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the incident.

“I urge the security agencies to conduct a comprehensive investigation, identify those responsible and their sponsors, and ensure they face justice,” he said.

He stressed that Nigerians had the constitutional right to support political parties and candidates of their choice without fear of intimidation or violence.

“Political differences must be resolved through persuasion and the ballot, never through the use of bullets. No political ambition is worth the life of even one Nigerian,” Obi added.

By Samuel Oyadongha & Henry Umoru



The death toll in last Friday’s boat mishap in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 32, as the state government deploy
content:
•As Bayelsa deploys crane to lift wreckage of capsized boat •PANDEF mourns victims •Police AIG visits Ayama-Ijaw

By Samuel Oyadongha & Henry Umoru

The death toll in last Friday’s boat mishap in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 32, as the state government deployed a heavy-duty crane to the scene to lift the wreckage of the capsized vessel and facilitate a thorough search for persons who may still be trapped beneath or within it.

This came as Pan Niger Delta Forum, PANDEF, the apex socio-political body of the South-South geopolitical zone, mourned victims of the recent boat accident that claimed several lives.

Also, the Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of Zone 16, Regina Udoette, has visited the Ayama-Ijaw waterside in Southern Ijaw to interact with marine workers and the Red Cross rescue team over the fatal boat mishap.

The operation, involving the Bayelsa State Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, the Bayelsa State Emergency Management Agency, BYSEMA, the National Inland Waterways Authority, NIWA, security agencies, divers and other relevant responders, is continuing as the government intensifies efforts to account for all persons affected by the tragic incident.

It was learned that the deployment of the crane was aimed at removing the submerged wreckage and enabling divers and rescue personnel to properly examine the site, while extending the search to areas that may not have been accessible during the initial operations.

The state government had sustained the search and recovery effort since the mishap, with relevant agencies working to ensure that every part of the affected waterway and the wreckage was thoroughly examined.

The latest deployment signals an escalation of the multi-agency operation, as authorities move to conclusively determine the fate of passengers who remain unaccounted for since the vessel went down.

The boat tragedy, which occurred on the state’s inland waterways, around Oweikorogha and Otuan junction in the council, has once again brought to the fore concerns over water transportation safety in Bayelsa, a riverine state where boats serve as a primary means of movement for many communities.

PANDEF mourns victims 

In a statement by PANDEF National Chairman, Amb. Godknows Igali, said: “PANDEF particularly commiserates with the affected families, the government and people of Bayelsa State, the people of Southern Ijaw council, and the affected communities, who have been impacted by this tragedy. We stand in full solidarity with them, share in their sorrow and extend the heartfelt condolences of the peoples of the entire South-South geopolitical zone.

“While mourning this tragic loss, PANDEF calls on the relevant emergency relief agencies, security agencies and regulatory authorities to work closely with the Bayelsa State government to ensure that all necessary measures are taken to assuage the impact on survivors and bereaved families. “More importantly to take all necessary measures to prevent a recurrence of such tragedies. In particular, we call for strict enforcement of water transportation safety regulations, including compliance with passenger safety protocols, the use of appropriate safety equipment, and the operation of only seaworthy vessels that meet prescribed safety standards.

“PANDEF also reiterates that this tragic incident reinforces its longstanding call on the Federal Government and the governments of the affected states to prioritise the construction of roads and bridges to open up the coastal communities of the country. The continued isolation of many of these communities, resulting from inadequate road connections leaves their people with little or no alternative than cheap water transportation.

“In the interim, the Federal Government should support the states to acquire adequate sea worthy vessels to meet the needs of these fellow Nigerians. May the Almighty God grant eternal rest to the departed and comfort to all those affected by this terrible mishap.”

Police AIG visits Ayama-Ijaw 

The AIG, while responding to the incident, commiserated with the Bayelsa State government and the people of the state over the sad development, and commended President Bola Tinubu for his quick response and show of empathy over the incident.

She said: “I am here with my management team and the Bayelsa CP on behalf of the Inspector General of Police to sympathise with the people that died in the incident. I register our condolences and wish the injured quick recovery.”

“Besides, the maritime personnel told us of the refusal of passengers to obey safety rules, and the boat captain loaded over 500 persons for a boat with a 200-person capacity. That was a suicide mission and a disaster waiting to happen.”

“Some of these deaths are avoidable. Many of the passengers refuse to obey safety rules. My Bible tells me obedience is better than sacrifice. There are rules and regulations on life jackets and overloading, but they refused.

“For the living, this is a big lesson to everyone that wants to use a boat for their journey. They should listen to the rules. People should use common sense. This disaster is avoidable.”

description:
By Efe Onodjae







The freight forwarding industry generates between N2 trillion and N3 trillion annually, underscoring its potential to contribute significantly to Nigeria’s $1 trillion economy target by 2030, the Council for the Regulation of Freight Forwarding in Nigeria (CRFFN) has said.



R
content:
By Efe Onodjae

The freight forwarding industry generates between N2 trillion and N3 trillion annually, underscoring its potential to contribute significantly to Nigeria’s $1 trillion economy target by 2030, the Council for the Regulation of Freight Forwarding in Nigeria (CRFFN) has said.

Registrar and Chief Executive Officer of CRFFN, Mr Kingsley Igwe, disclosed this in Lagos during the council’s nationwide staff capacity-building programme.

Igwe said freight forwarding remained critical to international trade, noting that sea transport accounts for about 90 per cent of global cargo movement.

“Freight forwarding is critical to the movement of cargo from exporting countries to importers. The industry plays a vital role through professional handling, documentation and compliance with international trade regulations,” he said.

He said the industry’s estimated annual contribution of between N2 trillion and N3 trillion positioned it as a significant contributor to Nigeria’s economic growth and the Federal Government’s ambition of building a $1 trillion economy by 2030.

Igwe disclosed that CRFFN currently had close to 10,000 registered freight forwarders, while over 1,000 applications were being processed under its new licensing scheme.

“We are targeting between 20,000 and 25,000 corporate entities and over 40,000 individual practitioners to be certified within the next five years. The licensing exercise is also projected to generate over N30 billion annually,” he said.

On complaints about multiple charges at Nigerian ports, the CRFFN boss said the council had issued a circular prohibiting illegal charges on cargo entering or leaving the country.

“Anybody collecting unauthorised charges at port terminals or along the roads will face sanctions. Only payments that are statutorily approved are permitted,” he warned.

He said the licensing programme would help identify unregistered operators, improve accountability and strengthen regulatory compliance across the freight forwarding industry.

Igwe explained that the staff capacity-building programme was designed to enhance the council’s regulatory effectiveness, adding that the training, which commenced in Lagos, would extend to Port Harcourt, Abuja and Kano.
