title: Curfew in Delta: How gunmen killed 4 in Omo-Agege’s  convoy
description:
By Henry Umoru



No fewer than four persons were killed, yesterday, as gunmen opened fire on members of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, who were on the campaign train of former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, in Uduere Community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State
content:
By Henry Umoru

No fewer than four persons were killed, yesterday, as gunmen opened fire on members of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, who were on the campaign train of former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, in Uduere Community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.

Omo-Agege is the Delta Central Senatorial candidate of the NDC in 2027 National Assembly polls.

While the NDC claimed the All Progressives Congress, APC, was responsible for the attack, the ruling party accused the NDC of stoking the attack, which, it alleged, claimed three of its members.

But the state police command said it was investigating the attack.

Among NDC members killed was Moses Anaughe, a former Commissioner, Federal Character Commission and aide to Omo-Agege. A former member of the Delta State House of Assembly, Chief Evans Ivwurie, was among those shot and currently battling for his life alongside other victims receiving medical attention.

Videos circulating on social media showed Umukoro, popularly known as Akhima, lying motionless at a hospital where efforts were being made to revive him. Another video showed Iwurie being assisted into a hospital, with blood stains visible around his chest.

This came as the Delta State government imposed a curfew on Ughelli North, following the gunshots and attendant deaths in parts of the council.

Meanwhile, Ughelli North Council Chairman, Olorogun Jaro Egbo, claimed that three of his supporters were killed, with both sides accusing the each other of instigating the violence.

The State Police condemned the killings, and commenced investigations to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible.

The latest bloodshed was the third major violent incident linked to political activities involving rival camps in the state, following earlier clashes in the Warri-Effurun axis and Asaba, where one person was killed.

While Omo-Agege’s camp put the Uduere death toll at four, Egbo claimed three of his supporters were killed, with both sides accusing each other of instigating the violence.

The recurrence of deadly confrontations, with the 2027 general elections still months away, has heightened concerns over the safety of political campaigns and the possibility of Delta becoming increasingly engulfed in political violence.

Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation alleged that armed men opened fire on the senator and his entourage at close range during a peaceful campaign visit, describing the incident as an assassination attempt.

Assasination attempt

In a statement by his Media Adviser, Sunny Areh, the campaign organisation said: “We condemn in the strongest possible terms the murderous attack on the campaign team of Senator Omo-Agege, Delta Central senatorial candidate of the NDC, in Uduere, Ughelli North.

“According to eyewitness reports received from the scene, armed men opened fire at close range on Senator Omo-Agege and his entourage during a peaceful campaign tour to Uduere.

“Senator Omo-Agege was saved by a divine distraction, when bullets wheezed past his head as he was addressing the crowd that gathered to receive him.

“We are pained to report that four people including two of our aides, Moses Anaughe and Akima Umukoro were shot dead.

“Four others, Chief Iwuvrie, Chuks Erhire, Tobore Agba (who was shot in the neck) and Ayodo Wanogho were shot at very close range and wounded critically. They are currently receiving medical attention.

“This was not a clash. This was not a misunderstanding. This was, according to witnesses, a targeted attempt to assassinate Senator Omo-Agege.”

It further alleged that witnesses identified Egbo as leading the attackers.

Egbo kicks

However, Egbo rejected the allegations, offering a completely different account of how the confrontation erupted.

According to him: “Yesterday (Sunday) at the village, we went there to set up our canopy for today’s and tomorrow’s event because I’m hosting the whole village people.

“When we got there, some people said that Omo-Agege was coming and they want to use the hall. So, my president told them that this hall had been booked, so, you can take it to elsewhere. They refused.

“In the morning, we had got intelligence that they brought in AK47 and armed men from Sapele and Ughelli. So, I called the Area Commander and the DPO to go there and maintain peace. We even called the Army.

“So, when the DPO got there, he called me to say that he’s preaching to them that they shouldn’t fight.

“So, I told my people, don’t talk to anybody. Just enjoy yourself there. Drink and eat and merry. They had their own and that was when he (Omo-Agege) was saying that I was his PA, I was this, I was that.”

Egbo accused members of Omo-Agege’s entourage of opening fire on his supporters, claiming that three of his men died.

“And thereafter, as he was going, that was when one of his boys, one Akima, who calls himself Anti-Cult, brought out a pump action and opened fire at innocent citizens.Three of them at close range, on my people.

“As they fired, two died. The other one we rushed to the hospital, he just died now. And then three others are in critical condition.

“So, it’s Omo-Agege that ordered them to shoot innocent people, since he declared ‘Rig & Die’. So, they came with arms, fully armed, to cause disruption,” he alleged.

Egbo further said casualties were being treated at the Central Hospital, Ughelli, adding that the Area Commander was at the facility.

The NDC campaign organisation, meanwhile, called on Governor Oborevwori to condemn the attack and ensure the arrest and investigation of those allegedly responsible, including Egbo.

“We call on the Inspector-General of Police to personally take over the investigation as we no longer have confidence in the Delta State Police Command whose officers were present with six trucks but did nothing to prevent the attack and killings.”

The organisation urged its supporters, “Do not retaliate. Do not take the law into your own hands. We refuse to be intimidated. We refuse to be silenced.”

Delta govt imposes curfew

The curfew, which takes effect from yesterday, will run from 6p.m to 6a.m, daily until further notice.

The Secretary to the State Government, SSG, Dr. Kingsley Emu, announced the restriction in a statement, saying it was aimed at bringing the situation under control.

According to the statement, the curfew covers the entire Ughelli North.

The government urged residents to comply strictly with the directive.

Condemns killings, warns against political thuggery

Contacted, Delta State Police Command’s Spokesman, Bright Edafe, said: “Following the reported violence during a campaign rally of the NDC at Uduere Community, Ughelli North, which allegedly resulted in loss of lives and injuries to several persons, the Delta State government has imposed a curfew in Ughelli North from 6p.m., to 6a.m., daily until further notice.

“The command has commenced investigations to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible.

“The command, therefore, urges residents of Ughelli North to comply strictly with the curfew imposed by the Delta State Government, restricting movement between 1800hrs to 0600hrs until further notice. Residents are advised to remain calm and cooperate with security personnel in the interest of public safety.

“The Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, CP Samuel. Erale, has directed intensified security operations in the affected area to prevent further violence and maintain law and order.

“The CP has ordered a full-scale investigation and assures residents of the state that anyone found culpable will face the full weight of the law, irrespective of political affiliation or status, and urges members of the public to provide credible information to assist ongoing investigations.

“CP Samuel Erale, extends his condolences to the bereaved families and wishes the injured a speedy recovery. He assures residents of the Command’s commitment to protecting lives and property and ensuring a peaceful environment for lawful political activities.

“The CP warns political actors and their supporters against thuggery, intimidation and the unlawful use of firearms, stressing that political differences must never be allowed to degenerate into violence or loss of lives.” .

NDC calls on Police, security agencies to investigate attack on Omo-Agege

Also, the national leadership of NDC condemned the attack on the campaign train of Senator Omo-Agege, saying enough was enough.

In a statement, yesterday, by NDC’s National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, the party said: “We strongly condemns the spate of violence and attacks orchestrated against its members, which reached its peak today in Ughelli, Delta State.

“The campaign train of the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central and former Deputy Senate President, DSP, Omo-Agege, was attacked by hoodlums suspected to be agents of the ruling party, the APC.

“Sadly, as at press time, four persons have been feared dead, including a close aide of Omo-Agege, while several others sustained varying degrees of injuries. Indeed, Omo-Agege narrowly escaped assassination.

“This is an attack against the NDC for the umpteenth time in Delta State. It is a clear, calculated, and cowardly attempt to silence opposition voices and scare our members and supporters away from the democratic process.

“We call on the Nigeria Police Force and all relevant security agencies to immediately investigate this dastardly attack, bring the perpetrators and their sponsors to book, and take urgent steps to checkmate the descent of the campaign into a battlefield.

“Election is not war. No life should be lost in the contest for power. The NDC will not be intimidated. We will not be cowed. We will continue to exercise our constitutional right to participate fully in the forthcoming general elections, and no amount of violence will deter us from rescuing Delta State and Nigeria.

“We commiserate with the families of the deceased, and pray for the speedy recovery of the injured.”

It was an attempt on my life — Omo-Agege

Senator Omo-Agege, yesterday, alleged that the attack on his campaign train in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State was “premeditated”, saying it was part of an ongoing attempt to eliminate him.

Speaking on Channels TV via Zoom, Omo-Agege said four members of his campaign organisation were killed, while about 15 others were critically injured when gunmen opened fire during his campaign event in Udu-Ere, Ughelli North.

He said he was addressing supporters when the gunmen opened fire, adding that he heard them repeatedly shouting that they wanted to kill him.

He said he survived the attack through the intervention of his Department of State Services, DSS, security details.

He said the attack occurred less than five minutes after he began his remarks at the campaign venue.

His words: “This is premeditated. It is not something that just happened today. I just gave you the buildup. This thing has been going on.

“As I was speaking, I just moved over to the side of a vehicle to be able to make eye contact with those I was speaking with. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started.’The former Deputy Senate President said four members of his campaign organisation were killed in the attack, including former Federal Character Commissioner, and the immediate past president of the Urhobo Progress Union youth wing.

The former senator said he heard the attackers shouting in English, “Omo-Agege, we want to kill,” while the shooting was ongoing.

Omo-Agege called on the Inspector-General of Police to take over the investigation, saying he did not expect the Delta State Police Command to deliver justice.

“We are appealing to the IGP to step in immediately and directly handle this investigation. We need justice,” he said.

We need justice. We need justice for these four people who have been killed. We need justice for the 15 people who are critically injured and hospitalised right now,” he said.

He also appealed to his supporters not to retaliate, saying the attack would not deter him from continuing his campaign.

“If the idea is that this is supposed to deter me from going forward with the campaigns, it’s a very, very big mistake and a big lie. It ain’t going to happen,” Omo-Agege said.

From Warri-Effurun to Asaba

The Uduere violence comes against the backdrop of previous confrontations involving political supporters in the state, raising questions about the effectiveness of earlier security interventions and assurances of peaceful political activities.

The first major incident occurred during a political procession in the Warri-Effurun axis on September 18, when supporters of rival political interests clashed, with allegations of armed involvement and an AK-47 rifle reportedly recovered in the aftermath.

The incident prompted condemnation and calls for investigation, amid conflicting accounts by political actors and security authorities over how the violence started and who was responsibl

Barely two months later, on November 7, another political procession in Asaba, involving supporters of the NDC and the Obedient Movement, ended in bloodshed, leaving one person dead and several others injured.

The police had said they received intelligence about the planned procession and advised against a road march, while political actors subsequently traded accusations over responsibility for the violence.

The Asaba incident also attracted concern from traditional and political stakeholders, who warned against allowing partisan rivalry to threaten the peace of the stat

With Uduere now added to the list, the succession of violent incidents has raised troubling questions about whether political actors and security agencies have learnt any lessons from the earlier bloodshed.

The rival accounts surrounding the latest shooting, the actual casualty figure, the identities of those responsible and the circumstances leading to the violence now require urgent and impartial investigation.

When contacted, Delta State Police Command’s Spokesman, SP Bright Edafe, said the Command was yet to receive official report despite Egbo affirming that the Ughelli Area Commander was in the know and at the Ughelli Central Hospital where some casualties were rushed to the Accident and Emergency Unit.

Jimitota Onoyume, Egufe Yafugborhi, Akpokona Omafuaire, Efe Onodjae, Ochuko Akuopha & Cynthia Alo.

Vanguard News

The African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) is to finance export-oriented Nigerian Small and Medium -sized Enterprises (SMEs) through the Nigerian Export-Import Bank (NEXIM).



“The facility will finance working capital and capital expenditure for export an
content:
By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

The African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) is to finance export-oriented Nigerian Small and Medium -sized Enterprises (SMEs) through the Nigerian Export-Import Bank (NEXIM).

“The facility will finance working capital and capital expenditure for export and intra-African trade activities, with eligible businesses in fashion, film, music, design and the wider creative industries among the intended beneficiaries,” Afreximbank said in a statement.

The facility reinforces Afreximbank’s broader commitment to expanding access to finance for African SMEs and exporters, including eligible businesses in the creative economy, the institution said.

It said the agreement was signed on behalf of Afreximbank by Mrs. Kanayo Awani, Executive Vice President, Intra-African Trade and Export Development, and on behalf of NEXIM by Mr. Abba Bello, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer , at the recent CANEX event in Lagos.

“Nigeria’s SMEs and export-oriented businesses need access to finance to expand production, invest in productive capacity and compete in new markets.

This $30 million facility will enable NEXIM to provide the working capital and investment financing required to support their growth and increase Nigeria’s exports across Africa and beyond,” Mrs. Awani was quoted as saying.

“By combining NEXIM’s export-finance capabilities with Afreximbank’s trade and development mandate, we can help more Nigerian enterprises build the capacity required to participate in regional and global value chains. Eligible creative businesses will also be able to benefit from the facility, supporting CANEX’s broader objective of connecting African talent and enterprise with appropriate finance and market opportunities,” she added.

Welcoming the partnership, Mr. Abba Bello, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NEXIM said, “We are delighted to partner with Afreximbank to expand financing opportunities for Nigerian exporters. This $30 million facility marks an important step in our efforts to help more businesses add value locally, fulfil export orders and reach new markets across Africa and beyond. SMEs operating across the export value chain, including eligible businesses in the creative industries, will also be able to access financing through this facility. We are particularly pleased that this partnership will help more Nigerian businesses strengthen their capacity to compete in regional and global markets, supporting our country’s economic diversification.”

content:
Gambiaj.com – (KAUR, THE GAMBIA) – United Democratic Party (UDP) leader and Gambia First Coalition flagbearer ANM Ousainou Darboe has pledged to revive Kaur Wharf Town, popularly known as Dande Mayoo, if elected president in the December 5 presidential election.

Darboe made the pledge while addressing residents during his campaign tour of Kaur, where he urged voters to support the UDP-led coalition, arguing that the town and the wider Saloum area have remained largely neglected in terms of development.

Reflecting on his first visit to the area in 1996, Darboe questioned how little the town had changed over the past three decades, lamenting what he described as a lack of progress in Kaur and the wider Saloum region.

“When I came here in 1996, and today, there are no changes in Kaur. In Saloum, it continues to be the same. There is no development,” he said.

Darboe challenged residents to assess what successive administrations, from former President Yahya Jammeh’s government to the current administration of President Adama Barrow, had delivered to the town.

“Since the time of Jammeh up to President Barrow’s government, what meaningful development have they brought to Kaur Wharf Town?” he asked.

The UDP leader said his coalition would make the revival of Kaur Wharf Town a priority if elected, presenting the town’s restoration as part of his development promise to the area.

“We can only revive Kaur Wharf Town, ‘Dande Mayoo’, if you vote for the UDP,” he said.

The pledge forms part of Darboe’s campaign message as the Gambia First Coalition seeks to consolidate support across the country ahead of the December 5 presidential election.

title: Peter Obi lacks capacity to manage people properly — Abure
description:
By Adegboyega Adeleye







Factional National Chairman of the Labour Party (LP), Julius Abure has accused Peter Obi of lacking the capacity to unite and manage people, citing the departure of several figures who worked with the party’s 2023 presidential candidate.







Abure made the allegation
content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Factional National Chairman of the Labour Party (LP), Julius Abure has accused Peter Obi of lacking the capacity to unite and manage people, citing the departure of several figures who worked with the party’s 2023 presidential candidate.

Abure made the allegation on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, while explaining his fallout with Obi and his decision to support President Bola Tinubu.

“Peter Obi doesn’t have capacity to manage people properly. I ask you, the structure we built around him in the 2023 general election. Where are the people? Where is Yunusa Tanko? He is in another party. You are looking at me because I’m saying I’m supporting Bola Tinubu. Yunusa Tanko is no longer with Peter,” Abure said.

“Ask yourself what happened to Yunusa Tanko. Ask yourself where is Sarah Ibrahim? Where is his vice-presidential candidate in the 2023 general election? Where are a lot of others? Where is people like Valentine Ozigbo? There are many others.

The man simply does not have the capacity, the character, and competence to put people together and galvanise them towards achieving a set goal.”

Abure denied ever frustrating Obi out of the Labour party, saying the party had given him substantial control after the 2023 election. He argued that Obi’s experience with political parties and the Obidient movement showed, in his view, that he had struggled to keep people together.

“There was no frustration, we gave him everything. We practically handed over the leadership of the party to him, and that was the truth of the matter. If you go and find out, you are journalists. I’m sure a lot of your people were with us during the campaign.

“After the campaign, I practically almost handed over the party for him to run, and the result is what you have seen,” he said.

“Peter Obi himself will tell you: Look at people’s past. Look at Obi’s past. Look at APGA, look at PDP, look at Labour now, and look at the people that are with him, even in the Obidient movement, how they have all abandoned him and left him because he doesn’t have that capacity to put people together and manage them for effective performance.”

Abure also said his experience working with Obi, who is now contesting the 2027 election under the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), had convinced him that the former Anambra governor was “unstable” and “unreliable.”

He said he chose to support Tinubu ahead of the 2027 elections because he believed the president was better suited to lead.

“You see, experience they say is the best teacher. Now I have experience working with Peter Obi, and I have seen him in and out that he is unstable, unreliable, a pretender cannot be trusted because of the way he treated the leadership of the party,” Abure added.

“President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is 100% better. And I give you the analysis today. Today, we gave a comparative analysis of the personality of Peter Obi and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, giving our experiences now, and all the party members that were there were very clear. It was clear. Obviously, we are supporting him (Tinubu).”

title: 970m Africans lack access to clean cooking — Energy expert
description:
By Ediri Ejoh & Henry Obetta







About 970 million Africans lack access to clean cooking, while over 560 million people in sub-Saharan Africa are without electricity, energy experts have said, calling for greater continental collaboration to tackle the crisis.







Regional Chair for Africa of
content:
By Ediri Ejoh & Henry Obetta

About 970 million Africans lack access to clean cooking, while over 560 million people in sub-Saharan Africa are without electricity, energy experts have said, calling for greater continental collaboration to tackle the crisis.

Regional Chair for Africa of the World Energy Council, Mr Omar Farouk, disclosed this at the 14th anniversary lecture and investiture into the Realnews Hall of Fame, organised by Realnews Magazine, with the theme: “Geopolitical Turbulence and Energy Security: Forging Strategic Opportunities for Africa.”

Citing the 2026 Tracking SDG 7 Report, based on 2024 data, Farouk lamented Africa’s energy poverty despite its abundant oil, gas and renewable resources.

“How can a continent so richly endowed with energy resources remain so energy poor? Why do petroleum-producing countries sometimes struggle to supply affordable fuels to their own citizens? Why do countries with natural gas resources suffer from electricity shortages?” he asked.

He attributed the crisis largely to inadequate finance, technology and infrastructure, rather than resource scarcity.

“We cannot, as a continent, be able to get out of where we have found ourselves today if we continue to operate in silos. Our solution lies in cooperation and collaboration,” he said.

Farouk stressed that finance, technology and infrastructure must work together to drive energy development, adding: “You can have a lot of money without the technology, you can’t make any progress. You can bring scientists, technologists, without the money, they can’t make progress. And you can have both of these without the energy infrastructure, you can’t move energy from one point to the other.”

He said Africa was projected to attract only $110 billion, or 3.3 per cent of the estimated $3.4 trillion global energy investment in 2026, while universal clean cooking access would require about $4 billion annually.

Managing Director of Frazimex Engineering Limited, a subsidiary of Oilserv Group, Engr. Chuka Eze, urged African countries to leverage global geopolitical disruptions to strengthen energy sovereignty and industrial capacity.

He said Africa captures less than one per cent of the value generated from clean-energy technology manufacturing, despite its rich mineral resources.

“Africa’s opportunity is to move from being a supplier of strategic resources to becoming a shaper of the global energy system,” Eze said.

He called for stronger local-content policies, technology transfer, skills development and regional cooperation to promote domestic processing, manufacturing and industrial growth.

content:
A former Military Governor of Kaduna State, Col. Abubakar Dangiwa Umar (retd.), has called on the Katsina State Governor, Dikko Radda, to suspend the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Faruk Umar Faruk, over allegations of sexual assault levelled against him by a Polish tourist.

Umar, in an open letter to the governor, urged the state government to suspend the traditional ruler pending a thorough, impartial and transparent investigation into the allegation.

ArewaPUNCH reports that the call came amid growing controversy over a viral video reportedly showing the Emir in an encounter with the female tourist, Mirka Czee, who accused him of touching her breasts without her consent during a visit to his palace.

The tourist, who uses the Instagram handle @beduinqa, has maintained that she was sexually assaulted during the encounter, while the Daura Emirate Council says it is examining the footage to establish its authenticity and determine whether it has been manipulated or artificially generated.

In the letter dated Novemeber 22, 2026, a copy made available to ArewaPUNCH on Monday, Umar described the allegation as disturbing, saying that if the video was authentic, the conduct would amount to an abuse of the dignity, authority and responsibilities attached to the traditional institution.

He said the Emir’s position was not merely ceremonial but carried enormous moral, cultural and historical responsibilities.

According to him, occupants of revered traditional offices are expected to demonstrate dignity, restraint and exemplary conduct.

“Any behaviour such as this that brings the institution into disrepute inevitably diminishes public confidence in traditional leadership generally,” he said.

Umar expressed concern that previous reports of alleged misuse of power by the Emir had reportedly caused embarrassment and anxiety among traditional rulers and members of the public.

He urged Radda to exercise his constitutional and statutory powers to suspend Faruk immediately, adding that if the allegations were established, the Emir should be deposed without delay.

The former military governor, however, stressed that suspension pending investigation should not be interpreted as a declaration of guilt.

Rather, he said, it would demonstrate that nobody, irrespective of age, status or traditional authority, was above accountability.

Meanwhile, Czee has given a detailed account of her alleged experience at the palace, explaining why she decided to make the incident public.

The Polish tourist, who was born in the Czech Republic, said she had travelled across several parts of Nigeria, including Oron, Calabar, Ibadan, Benin City, Lagos, Abeokuta, Osogbo, Ilorin, Abuja, Jos, Bauchi, Dutse, Kano, Zaria, Katsina and Daura.

She said she travelled by public transport and interacted with residents as part of her efforts to experience Nigeria’s culture and diversity, adding that she had mostly encountered kind, helpful and hospitable people.

Recounting her visit to the Daura palace, Czee said she was introduced to the Emir, who instructed his dignitaries to take her for a meal and show her around the palace and its surroundings.

She said she learnt about Daura’s history, including its place in Hausa history, stories about female rulers and the account of a prince from Baghdad who killed a snake at a well.

She also visited different rooms and the palace stables, where she rode a horse.

According to her, she was later taken back to the Emir but was surprised when she was left alone with him in a large room.

She alleged that the Emir asked her to sit close to him on a couch, held her hand and began playing with it, making her uncomfortable.

Czee said she lowered the Meta glasses on her head and activated their recording function while trying to maintain their conversation.

“I felt we sat too close, I felt uncomfortable that he grabbed my hand and started to play with it,” she wrote.

She further alleged that the Emir later hugged and kissed her on the cheek as they stood up before touching her breasts without her consent.

“I just couldn’t believe he did it. I reacted with lots of ‘no, no, no, no Emir’ and he repeated after me ‘no, no, no’ with laughter. I said, ‘you cannot be touching’,” she alleged.

Explaining why she decided to publish the recording, the tourist said she believed other women might have experienced similar unwanted advances without having the opportunity or means to speak out.

She said, “Because it happened to me. Because I had a chance and a tool to record it, and because I believe it happens to so many other women who don’t have a chance to speak up.”

Czee stressed that her concern was not simply about an alleged incident in a public space but that it happened inside the palace of a traditional ruler.

“I wasn’t grabbed by boobs on streets of Nigeria, even in crowded places, but in a palace of traditional leader who should be showing exemplary ways of behaviour. And he did not. I was a guest in his country, in his region, in his city, in his palace. And I was assaulted,” she wrote.

She also said the incident had affected her emotionally and that she needed time and space to recover.

The post Ex-Kaduna gov demands Daura emir’s suspension over sexual assault allegation appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Police bust Ogun ‘Yahoo academy’, uncover human remains
description:
The Police Special Fraud Unit has arrested 11 suspected internet fraudsters during a raid on an alleged Yahoo academy in Abeokuta, Ogun State, recovering charms, blood-stained fetish items and suspected human remains.
PUNCH Metro learnt that the suspects were arrested at House 10, Second Hill Estate
content:
The Police Special Fraud Unit has arrested 11 suspected internet fraudsters during a raid on an alleged Yahoo academy in Abeokuta, Ogun State, recovering charms, blood-stained fetish items and suspected human remains.

PUNCH Metro learnt that the suspects were arrested at House 10, Second Hill Estate, Oloke-Meji, Onikolobo, Abeokuta, following intelligence-led investigations by detectives of the unit.

The operation also led to the recovery of 11 iPhones, three Samsung mobile phones, eight laptops and a 2014 Lexus RX 350, 2014 model.

The police said the suspects were allegedly involved in an organised internet fraud operation known as “Hustle Kingdom,” where they used the apartment as a base for cyber-related fraud and other criminal activities.

According to a statement issued on Monday by the Police Public Relations Officer of the PSFU, DSP Ovie Ewhubare, the suspects admitted to exploiting the identities and personal details of foreign nationals to defraud unsuspecting victims online.

The statement identified the suspects as Adedolapo Samuel, 25; Timothy Babatunde, 27; Ibrahim Sholete, 30; Torioza Oluwatosin, 30; Yusuf Alabi, 30; Adeyemi Seyi, 32; Tobiloba Oguntoyinbo, 32; Taiwo Mathew, 23; Shoyombo Ayomide, 24; Abayomi Rahmon, 32; and Abolaji Tunji, 28.

It added that the alleged leader of the operation, identified as Goriola Oluwaseun Olanrewaju, aka Update, was still at large.

The police said Olanrewaju rented the apartment in 2021 and subsequently recruited young men into the alleged fraud network.

The statement partly read, “Investigations revealed that one Goriola Oluwaseun Olanrewaju ‘M ’, also known as Update, currently at large, rented the apartment in 2021 and subsequently recruited young men into an organised internet fraud operation, commonly known as a ‘Hustle Kingdom’, where they use the facility as a base for cyber-related fraud and other criminal activities.

“The suspects admitted that they exploit the identities and personal details of foreign nationals to defraud unsuspecting victims online.”

The Commissioner of Police, Eloho Okpoziakpo, said the operation demonstrated the importance of credible information, intelligence-led policing and professional investigative skills in tackling organised financial and cyber-enabled crimes.

He added that investigations were ongoing into the circumstances surrounding the occupation of the property and whether the owners had fulfilled their responsibilities to verify and monitor their occupants.

The police commissioner said efforts were also being made to trace and recover the proceeds of the alleged crimes.

This came less than two weeks after the same police unit uncovered a counterfeit footwear production operation at a factory in Makun, Sagamu, Ogun State.

The command said the discovery followed an investigation into the activities of Meibalun International Nigeria Limited, which allegedly produced and marketed footwear bearing the trademarks of international brands without authorisation.

The post Police bust Ogun ‘Yahoo academy’, uncover human remains appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Fountain board drags Jimmy Odukoya to court for contempt
description:
The Incorporated Trustees of the Fountain of Life Church have initiated contempt enforcement proceedings against Olujimmy Odukoya over his alleged failure to comply with a court order restraining him from parading himself as the church’s Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head.
The church, through its coun
content:
The Incorporated Trustees of the Fountain of Life Church have initiated contempt enforcement proceedings against Olujimmy Odukoya over his alleged failure to comply with a court order restraining him from parading himself as the church’s Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head.

The church, through its counsel, Ibitayo Reju, on Monday obtained an order of substituted service from the Lagos State High Court, authorising it to serve Odukoya with Form 48, a notice warning of the consequences of disobeying an order of court.

Justice O. O. Adewunmi-Oshin, sitting at the Lagos High Court, granted the application in suit number LD/0126PRA/2026, permitting service through newspaper publications, pasting at Odukoya’s last known address at No. 12 Industrial Estate Road, off Town Planning Way, Ilupeju, Lagos, and electronic means.

The judge also directed Odukoya to appear before the court on November 26, 2026, to show cause.

Form 48, issued on November 23 pursuant to Section 72 of the Sheriffs and Civil Processes Act and Order IX Rule 13 of the Judgment (Enforcement) Rules of Court, warned Odukoya that failure to comply with the order made on November 18 would amount to contempt of court and expose him to committal to prison.

The notice, addressed to Odukoya at his last known address in Ilupeju, stated: “Take notice that unless you obey the Order of this Honourable Court (annexed to this process) made on 18 November 2026, you will be guilty of contempt of Court and will be liable to be committed to prison.”

The contempt proceedings followed an ex-parte order made by Justice Adewunmi-Oshin on November 18, restraining Odukoya, whether acting personally or through proxies, from holding himself out as the Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of the church.

The court also restrained him from interfering with, disrupting, meddling with or obstructing the activities, governance, and other affairs of the church.

The church had argued in its application that Odukoya had ceased to occupy the position following the appointment of a successor by its late founder and Senior Pastor, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, in accordance with the church’s constitution.

While granting the application, the judge also gave the church leave to commence the action under the pre-action protocol provisions of the Lagos State High Court (Expeditious Disposal of Civil Cases) Practice Direction No. 2 of 2019.

The court directed that the originating processes and accompanying documents be served on the respondent and that he file his response within the timelines prescribed by the Practice Direction.

The judge, however, expressly stated that the November 18 order was made ex parte and without prejudice to Odukoya’s right to apply to set it aside or respond fully to the substantive claims upon being served.

At Monday’s proceedings, Reju appeared for the applicant, while Odukoya was unrepresented. Both parties were absent.

The matter was adjourned to November 26 for Odukoya to show cause,the matter was initially adjourned to December 1, 2026, for mention before  Monday’s proceedings.

The post Fountain board drags Jimmy Odukoya to court for contempt appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NDC denies rift with Obi over campaign funding
description:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council on Monday dismissed reports of a disagreement between its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and the party over campaign funding, insisting that both sides remained united ahead of the 2027 general election.
The party said Obi had neither
content:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council on Monday dismissed reports of a disagreement between its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and the party over campaign funding, insisting that both sides remained united ahead of the 2027 general election.

The party said Obi had neither complained about inadequate campaign funds nor expressed dissatisfaction with how it handled campaign finances, describing reports of a rift as an attempt to divide the opposition camp.

The clarification comes amid growing concerns over the control and management of campaign donations following a fundraising initiative launched by activist Aisha Yesufu for Obi’s presidential bid.

In a statement issued on Monday, the spokesperson for the NDC Campaign Council, Constance Ikokwu, said reports suggesting a disagreement between the party and its candidate were false.

She said, “Let me state categorically that Peter Obi has not complained about a lack of campaign funds or expressed any dissatisfaction with the party over funding.”

Ikokwu maintained that Obi remained committed to the campaign, adding that his nationwide engagements demonstrated his determination to secure victory in the 2027 election.

“Let’s be clear – no presidential candidate in this race is campaigning with the energy, consistency and intensity that Obi is bringing to this election. His commitment to reaching Nigerians across the country is there for all to see, and he’s doing that superbly. The campaign so far is a resounding success,” she said.

She urged Nigerians to disregard what she described as manufactured controversies, insisting that the party and its candidate were focused on winning the election.

“The relationship between the party and its presidential candidate remains focused on one overriding objective: winning the 2027 presidential election and offering Nigerians a credible alternative. Those attempting to engineer a needless quarrel should not mistake their wishful thinking for reality. We are united, focused and determined,” Ikokwu added.

The rebuttal comes about two weeks after a fresh dispute over the control and management of campaign donations emerged in the opposition camp.

Former Labour Party National Chairman, Julius Abure, had warned the NDC against allowing Yesufu and other loyalists of Obi to operate parallel fundraising structures without the party’s approval.

The warning followed Yesufu’s launch of a public fundraising drive, during which she urged Nigerians to contribute towards financing Obi’s 2027 presidential campaign.

Yesufu had argued that Obi should not be left to shoulder the financial burden of the campaign alone, urging supporters to take ownership of the political project through individual contributions, irrespective of the amounts involved.

The initiative, however, raised questions about compliance with the NDC’s earlier directive that all campaign donations should be channelled through designated party accounts.

While the NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, expressed confidence that Yesufu had the blessing of the party leadership, Abure, in an exclusive interview with The PUNCH, cautioned that allowing individuals to control campaign funds outside the party’s supervision could reproduce the crisis that rocked the Labour Party after the 2023 general elections.

The post NDC denies rift with Obi over campaign funding appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NRS urges investigative reporting to curb illicit financial flows
description:
By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief







The Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) has urged the media to strengthen investigative reporting to expose illicit financial flows (IFFs) and revenue leakages undermining Nigeria’s economic development.







The call was made at a media workshop in Abuja, where a
content:
By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

The Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) has urged the media to strengthen investigative reporting to expose illicit financial flows (IFFs) and revenue leakages undermining Nigeria’s economic development.

The call was made at a media workshop in Abuja, where an NRS official, Idris Abdullahi, said illicit financial flows were depriving government of resources needed to fund infrastructure, healthcare, education and other development programmes.

He stressed the importance of media engagement in exposing financial vulnerabilities and promoting accountability in the management of public resources.

An illicit financial flows investigation expert, Adebayo Kayode, said journalists needed specialised training to uncover suspicious financial activities and trace how funds were diverted.

He said: “There is a fundamental difference between reporting that money has disappeared and investigating how, why, through whose arrangements and under what institutional circumstances it disappeared.”

Kayode urged journalists to scrutinise customs declarations, corporate ownership structures, extractive-sector export records, government budgets, procurement processes and tax policies to identify inconsistencies and revenue losses.

He, however, cautioned that collaboration with government agencies must not compromise press independence, stressing that journalists must remain free to investigate wrongdoing and hold public institutions accountable.

Kayode identified the National Action Plan for 2027–2030 as an important framework for strengthening Nigeria’s response to illicit financial flows, saying its success would require effective public scrutiny and media engagement.

He urged journalists to focus on emerging vulnerabilities, including cryptocurrency transactions, beneficial ownership disclosures, trade misinvoicing, public procurement, extractive-sector activities and unexplained wealth.

He said journalists could expose institutional weaknesses and financial irregularities, stimulate public demand for accountability and help translate policy declarations into measurable results.

“The fight against illicit financial flows is ultimately a fight for the future of Nigeria. It is about protecting the integrity of our economy, safeguarding public revenue, strengthening our institutions and ensuring that the nation’s resources serve the people,” he said.

title: Ajaokuta: NES blames collapse of long-term planning for 40-year stalemate
description:
By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief







The President, Nigerian Economic Society (NES), Dr. Baba Musa, has blamed the collapse of long-term economic planning for the failure of the Ajaokuta Steel Company to become operational more than four decades after its establishment.







Musa, who spoke at
content:
By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

The President, Nigerian Economic Society (NES), Dr. Baba Musa, has blamed the collapse of long-term economic planning for the failure of the Ajaokuta Steel Company to become operational more than four decades after its establishment.

Musa, who spoke at the National Growth & Development Forum (NGDF) 2026 in Abuja, said Nigeria lost the link between economic planning and execution, resulting in the abandonment or underperformance of strategic national projects.

“History demands candour. Somewhere along the way, we lost vital links between plan and performance. We built, but did not always maintain,” he said.

According to him, the oil windfall of the 1970s diverted the country from agriculture and non-oil exports which had previously sustained the economy.

“The oil windfall of the 1970s drew us away from the agriculture and non-oil exports that had sustained us. Strategic projects such as the Ajaokuta Steel Complex, begun with great promise, have yet to fulfil it four decades on. “And when formal planning gave way in the mid-1980s, long-term strategy too often yielded to visions that changed with administrations,” Musa said.

He said Nigeria must learn from its past policy failures to avoid repeating mistakes that have undermined economic development.

“The Nigeria we want must be built upon the Nigeria we have, and the Nigeria we have,” he added. The NES president also expressed concern that economic reforms had yet to translate into shared prosperity, noting that about 63 per cent of Nigerians, estimated at 140 million people, lived below the poverty line in 2025, according to the World Bank.

“Macroeconomic stability is necessary, but it is not yet shared prosperity. A stable exchange rate is not yet a full dinner table. Stability is the foundation; it is not the building,” he said.

Musa called for an economy that generates jobs, supports the poor, boosts domestic production, invests in human capital and promotes disciplined public finance and credible institutions.

Similarly, President, Capital Market Academics of Nigeria, Prof. Uche Uwaleke, said economic reforms must be measured by their impact on citizens’ welfare, job creation, purchasing power and poverty reduction.

title: Nigeria’s monthly trade surplus falls 31% to $2.03bn
description:
By Elizabeth Adegbesan







Nigeria’s trade surplus fell by 31.44 percent, month-on-month, MoM to $2.03  billion in July from $2.96 billion in June, as decline in  exports aggravated the impact of sharp rise in imports.







The Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, disclosed this in its Monthly Economi
content:
By Elizabeth Adegbesan

Nigeria’s trade surplus fell by 31.44 percent, month-on-month, MoM to $2.03 billion in July from $2.96 billion in June, as decline in exports aggravated the impact of sharp rise in imports.

The Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, disclosed this in its Monthly Economic Report for July, which showed that the aggregate export fell by 6.85 per cent MoM to $6.31 billion in July, from $6.77 billion in June, while total import rose by 12.25 per cent, MoM to $4.28 billion, up from $3.81 billion in June.

Oil exports maintained dominance in the country’s external trade profile, accounting for 93.11 per cent of total export proceeds, while non-oil exports made up the remaining 6.89 per cent.

Despite the overall drop in aggregate exports, earnings from the oil sector edged up marginally by 1.66 per cent to $5.31 billion, from $5.22 billion in June.

This resilience was driven by a surge in refined petroleum products and gas receipts, which cushioned a notable slump in crude oil sales.

“Specifically, receipts from refined petroleum products rose by 22.56 per cent to $1.31 billion, from $1.07 billion, following the restoration of refinery after the reduction in the operating rate of the residue fluid catalytic cracking (RFCC) unit in the preceding months,” CBN said.

Gas export earnings also posted positive growth, rising by 4.75 per cent to $1.21 billion from $1.15 billion. Conversely, crude oil receipts fell by 6.97 per cent to $2.79 billion, down from $3 billion in June 2026, due to lower terminal outturns.

Within the oil export basket, crude oil still held the largest share at 52.57 per cent, followed by refined petroleum products at 24.65 per cent, and gas products at 22.78 per cent.

On the non-oil front, export performance weakened during the review period. Earnings fell by 7.70 per cent to $0.43 billion in July, compared to $0.46 billion recorded in June.

“Non-oil export earnings declined in July 2026, driven mainly by lower exports of agricultural and mineral products,” CBN noted.

A breakdown of the non-oil sector showed that agricultural products remained the top contributor, accounting for 43.03 per cent of total non-oil proceeds.

Other products followed at 22.46 per cent, semi-manufactured products at 18.28 per cent, minerals at 8.43 per cent, and manufactured products at 7.8 per cent.

The post Nigeria’s monthly trade surplus falls 31% to $2.03bn appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: 2027 Elections: IGP to meet with party chairmen, secretaries over political violence, others
description:
From Molly Kilete, Abuja
Ahead of the 2027, general elections, the Inspector General of Police(IGP), Olatunji Disu, will on Tuesday, meet with chairmen and secretaries of all the political parties in the country.
The meeting/interactive session is schedule to take place at the Goodluck Ebele Jonatha
content:
From Molly Kilete, Abuja

Ahead of the 2027, general elections, the Inspector General of Police(IGP), Olatunji Disu, will on Tuesday, meet with chairmen and secretaries of all the political parties in the country.

The meeting/interactive session is schedule to take place at the Goodluck Ebele Jonathan Peacekeeping Hall, Force Headquarters, Abuja.

Top on the agenda of the meeting schedule for 11;o’clock in the morning according to a letter of invitation by the force public relations officer Ani Iniedu, will focus on “political violence, campaign-related violence, destruction of campaign banners and other campaign materials, as well as the disruption of political campaigns and rallies by political thugs”.

The meeting with the leaders of the political parties it was gathered had become necessary following attack on innocent persons during campaigns.

Aside the concerns listed for deliberations, the meeting it was gathered will also focus on hate speech which has become the other of the day by some politicians.

A security source who does not want to be mentioned in print, told Daily Sun, that security reports at the disposal of the security agencies revealed that the elections may be marred with severe violence that may overwhelm the security agencies to curtail if nothing is done at this early stage to address some of the ugly incidences that could trigger a breakdown of law and order before, during and after the ejections.

Already most of the chairmen, secretaries and other leaders of all the political parties have arrived Abuja for the meeting.

Some of the leaders who spoke to Daily Sun, described the meeting as timely and commendable and expressed the hope that the outcome of decisions reached would end the violence and unnecessary attacks especially on the opposition parties at the end of the day.

title: FG declares war on oil thieves, drug barons, arraigns oil boss, 7 others
description:
The Federal Government has stepped up its war against economic and drug-related crimes, arraigning an oil entrepreneur and seven others over alleged illegal dealings in petroleum products while unveiling measures to fast-track drug trafficking trials and confiscate proceeds of illicit activities.
Th
content:
The Federal Government has stepped up its war against economic and drug-related crimes, arraigning an oil entrepreneur and seven others over alleged illegal dealings in petroleum products while unveiling measures to fast-track drug trafficking trials and confiscate proceeds of illicit activities.

The two developments in Abuja yesterday signalled the government’s renewed push to dismantle criminal networks through speedy prosecution, asset recovery and stronger collaboration among law enforcement agencies, prosecutors, the judiciary and international partners.

Chairman of Ebenco Group Limited, Ebenezer Oluwagbemiga, was arraigned alongside seven other defendants before Justice Binta Nyako of the Federal High Court, Abuja, on a five-count charge bordering on alleged dealings in petroleum products without lawful authority or the requisite licence.

The other defendants are Elliot Boukoru, Peter Nzekwo, MV Ebenco Grace IMO-7239759, Ebenco Global Link Limited, MT ROSE IMO-8106795, Florence Marine and Shipping Limited, and Ganiyu Basit Olatunbosun.

All the defendants pleaded not guilty to the charges.

Director of Public Prosecutions of the Federation, Rotimi Oyedepo, who led the prosecution, told the court that the five-count charge was filed on November 3 and urged it to take the defendants’ pleas.

“There is a charge of five counts filed on Nov. 3. We prayed that my lord accept the charge and cause the plea of the defendants to be taken,” he said.

Following their pleas, Oyedepo urged the court to grant an accelerated hearing, citing the economic implications of the alleged offences.

“Considering the sensitivity of the matter and the implications on the economy, we urge the honourable court to grant an accelerated hearing,” he said.

The prosecution also sought an order remanding the defendants in custody pending the determination of the case or as the court might deem appropriate.

However, counsel to the first, second, third, fourth, fifth and eighth defendants, Femi Falana, informed the court that bail applications had been filed for the first, second, third and eighth defendants.

He added that the defence had responded to the prosecution’s counter-affidavits through replies on points of law.

Olalekan Ojo appeared for the sixth and seventh defendants.

Justice Nyako adjourned the matter until November 24 at 1 p.m. for hearing of the bail applications and ordered that the defendants remain in the custody of the arresting agency pending the hearing.

The prosecution said the alleged offences contravened provisions of the Miscellaneous Offences Act, Cap. M17, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004, including Section 3(6), and are punishable under Section 1(17) of the Act.

Meanwhile, Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, has announced plans to strengthen the prosecution of drug-related offences through speedy trials, confiscation of criminal assets and increased international cooperation.

Speaking at the inauguration of the National Drug Control Master Plan (NDCMP) 2026–2030 in Abuja, Fagbemi said the Federal Ministry of Justice would work with the judiciary to ensure the speedy disposal of drug-related cases in line with the Administration of Criminal Justice Act.

He said the government would also intensify efforts to strip convicted traffickers of the proceeds of their crimes, warning that criminal networks must not be allowed to enjoy the financial benefits of their illegal activities.

“The government will intensify mutual legal assistance, extradition processes and cross-border asset recovery to disrupt the financial networks sustaining organised drug trafficking.

“These measures are necessary to strengthen Nigeria’s criminal justice response and ensure that drug traffickers did not continue to benefit from the proceeds of their illegal activities,” he said.

The minister said prosecution and asset recovery remained critical to dismantling organised criminal enterprises, particularly those operating across international borders.

He commended the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) for strengthening cooperation between investigators and prosecutors from the early stages of criminal investigations, noting that the approach had improved evidence gathering, reduced procedural errors and enhanced the prosecution of drug cases.

Fagbemi described the agency as central to Nigeria’s drug control efforts, commending its Chairman, Buba Marwa, for his contributions to the fight against drug trafficking and substance abuse.

“The agency remains the bedrock of our national drug control architecture, delivering vital results across intelligence operations, interdiction, investigation, prosecution and public sensitisation.

“I specifically commend Buba Marwa, who has been a silent achiever and has consistently made this administration and country proud,” he said.

The Attorney-General, however, stressed that the government’s tougher prosecution strategy would distinguish between major drug traffickers and persons suffering from substance use disorders.

He said drug kingpins should face the full weight of the law, while persons struggling with drug dependence should receive medical treatment, psychological support and rehabilitation.

According to him, an effective national drug control policy must combine law enforcement with prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and social reintegration.

Fagbemi said the NDCMP 2026–2030 was designed to strengthen cooperation among law enforcement agencies, public health institutions, educational authorities, social development agencies, financial investigators and community organisations.

He also praised the NDLEA’s alternative development initiatives aimed at encouraging communities involved in illicit drug cultivation to embrace legitimate agricultural activities.

He said the initiative, which promotes the cultivation of lawful cash crops in place of illicit drugs, was consistent with President Bola Tinubu’s agenda of turning challenges into opportunities for progress.

The minister urged relevant institutions to translate the provisions of the master plan into measurable programmes, insisting that it must guide their daily operations rather than remain a policy document without practical impact.

The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) Commission has pledged support for Nigeria’s new drug control strategy, describing it as a significant contribution to regional efforts against drug trafficking and substance abuse.

ECOWAS Commissioner for Human Development and Social Affairs, Nassirou Bako-Arifari, said the success of the master plan would depend on sustained political commitment, adequate funding and cooperation among governments, civil society organisations, communities and international partners.

He noted that the cross-border nature of drug trafficking made coordinated action among West African countries imperative.

“Nigeria’s progress in implementing the master plan will contribute significantly to strengthening regional cooperation against illicit drug trafficking and its associated consequences.

“The ECOWAS Commission will stand with Nigeria at every step, sharing experience, mobilising support and linking this national effort to the work of other member states.

“Nigeria’s progress will guide the region because no country can win this fight alone,” he said.

title: INEC chairman, Sowore clash over subpoena as trial stalls
description:
The failure of the African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, to file court documents within the stipulated time stalled proceedings yesterday his ongoing trial over alleged cybercrime offences before the Federal High Court, Abuja.
Sowore’s lawyer, Reuben Adakole, who repr
content:
The failure of the African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, to file court documents within the stipulated time stalled proceedings yesterday his ongoing trial over alleged cybercrime offences before the Federal High Court, Abuja.

Sowore’s lawyer, Reuben Adakole, who represented him when the case was last heard on November 17, had undertaken to file his client’s response before the next adjourned date.

The response was to address an application filed by the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan (SAN), seeking to set aside a subpoena issued on him at the instance of the defendant.

The politician is being prosecuted by the Department of State Services (DSS) over social media posts he allegedly published on X (formerly Twitter) and Facebook in August 2025, in which he described President Bola Tinubu as a “criminal” and accused him of lying about the level of corruption in the country.

When the matter was called on Monday, Sowore’s lawyer, Adeyinka Olumide-Fusika (SAN), told the court that his colleagues were experiencing difficulties filing the defendant’s counter-affidavit at the court registry.

Olumide-Fusika explained that he was informed that officials responsible for generating Remita payment details at the registry were experiencing technical difficulties.

He consequently sought a short stand-down to enable his colleagues to complete the filing process.

However, Amupitan’s lawyer, Alex Izinyon (SAN), expressed disappointment over the defence team’s decision to wait until Monday to file its response, insisting that the documents ought to have been filed earlier.

Izinyon recalled that at the previous sitting on November 17, Adakole had undertaken to file the defendant’s response before the next hearing date, questioning why the defence waited until the day of the hearing.

He further disclosed that rather than file the expected response, the defendant opted to file a notice of preliminary objection, which was served on him last Friday.

According to him, the development forced him to work throughout the weekend to prepare a reply, which he filed before the court commenced sitting on Monday and subsequently served on the defence.

While the lawyers were still deliberating on how to proceed, Justice Mohammed Umar suggested that the matter be adjourned until Tuesday.

However, shortly after the suggestion, one of Olumide-Fusika’s colleagues rushed into the courtroom with the newly filed documents, prompting the defence lawyer to hand a copy to Izinyon.

After examining the documents, Izinyon confirmed that they contained a counter-affidavit and a written address.

He, however, told the court that he would need time to study the processes and file a response, either before the court registry closed on Monday or early Tuesday before the commencement of proceedings.

Following the absence of any objection from the prosecuting counsel, Akinlolu Kehinde (SAN), Justice Umar adjourned the matter until Tuesday for hearing.

The counter-affidavit and preliminary objection filed by Sowore are responses to Amupitan’s application seeking to set aside the subpoena issued at the defendant’s instance.

Sowore wants the INEC chairman to appear in court as his witness and produce certain documents, including the academic credentials President Tinubu submitted to the electoral commission.

At the last sitting, Izinyon had argued that the subpoena should be set aside on the grounds of alleged irregularities.

He also faulted the claim by Sowore’s lawyer, Adakole, that his client had filed an application seeking to amend the subpoena.

Izinyon argued that the defence could not introduce another application to amend the subpoena without first addressing the alleged irregularities surrounding the original process.

He further maintained that Adakole needed to clarify whether Sowore intended to withdraw the original subpoena or proceed with the application to amend it.

The INEC chairman’s lawyer insisted that the subpoena could not be altered at Sowore’s instance without a proper order of the court.

title: Drug control plan: Shettima demands action, NDLEA  seeks funding
description:
From Godwin Tsa, Abuja
Vice President Kashim Shettima has called for urgent implementation of the National Drug Control Master Plan (NDCMP) 2026–2030, directing that its priorities be incorporated into institutional work plans, budget proposals and implementation schedules.
Shettima, who spoke at th
content:
From Godwin Tsa, Abuja

Vice President Kashim Shettima has called for urgent implementation of the National Drug Control Master Plan (NDCMP) 2026–2030, directing that its priorities be incorporated into institutional work plans, budget proposals and implementation schedules.

Shettima, who spoke at the launch of the plan in Abuja on Monday, warned that inadequate financing could undermine its objectives, as the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) sought sustained funding from government and support from the private sector.

“A national plan without a credible financing pathway risks becoming a declaration of good intentions,” the Vice President said.

Represented by the Special Adviser to the President on Special Duties, Office of the Vice President, Modibbo Aliyu Umar, Shettima urged federal agencies, state and local governments, the National Assembly, businesses, traditional and religious institutions, and international partners to implement the plan with urgency, discipline and accountability.

He described the drug problem as a public health concern, security threat, development challenge and economic issue, warning that enforcement alone would not succeed without prevention, treatment and action against the illicit financial flows sustaining drug markets.

“A nation cannot secure its future if it fails to protect the people who must build that future,” he said.

The plan rests on six pillars: supply reduction; drug demand reduction; access to controlled medicines for scientific and medical purposes; alternative development and sustainable livelihoods; disruption of the illicit drug economy; and governance, financing and coordination.

Shettima commended the NDLEA, under its Chairman, Mohamed Marwa, for what he described as its pioneering alternative development programme in Africa. He said the pilot was already transforming three communities in Ondo State and urged state and local governments to take ownership of the initiative.

In his welcome address, Marwa said the new plan drew on the achievements and shortcomings of its predecessor and was designed “to keep what worked, fix what did not, and confront what is emerging.”

He disclosed that an evaluation of the 2021–2025 plan recorded 77,736 arrests, seizures of more than 14.8 million kilograms of drugs and over 14,200 convictions, while more than 32,400 people received treatment, counselling and rehabilitation.

However, the evaluation identified gaps in coordination, financing, service delivery, data, monitoring and accountability, alongside weak capacity at state and local government levels.

Marwa said the new framework would address those weaknesses and strengthen the response to trafficking networks, synthetic drugs, new psychoactive substances and syndicates exploiting encrypted communications and cryptocurrency.

Describing sustainable financing as “perhaps the single most important condition” for success, he urged federal budget authorities to reflect the plan’s priorities in annual budgets and the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework.

He also asked states and local governments to provide dedicated funding for their drug control committees, while inviting banks, telecommunications companies, technology firms, agribusinesses and philanthropists to support prevention, treatment and livelihood programmes.

“A policy priority without resources is merely an aspiration,” he said.

Highlighting the international reach of trafficking networks, Marwa cited a joint operation conducted on April 28, 2026, with the United States Drug Enforcement Administration and law enforcement partners in Switzerland, France and Greece.

He said the operation led to the arrest of an alleged drug baron, Amadi Simon, in Switzerland, as well as Jecinta Amara Ikechi in Anambra State and Blessing Ngozi Amadi in Delta State.

According to him, several bank accounts and cryptocurrency wallets were blocked, while the agency secured interim forfeiture of properties linked to Simon, including two hotels in Delta State and an apartment building in Mabushi, Abuja.

Marwa also recalled the dismantling of a Nigerian-Mexican methamphetamine network and a clandestine laboratory in Ogun State, involving drugs and chemicals valued at about $362.9 million.

He said four additional Mexican-linked laboratories were subsequently uncovered in Oyo, Ebonyi and Enugu states, leading to the arrest of 10 Mexicans and 14 local collaborators who were facing criminal charges.

The NDLEA chairman welcomed President Bola Tinubu’s transmission of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency Bill, 2026, to the National Assembly, where he said it had passed second reading, and assured that enforcement would remain guided by the rule of law, due process and respect for human rights.

Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, described the NDLEA as “the bedrock of our national drug response,” saying the plan linked law enforcement with public health, education, social development and financial investigation.

He said the Ministry of Justice would work with the Judiciary to accelerate the disposal of drug cases under the Administration of Criminal Justice Act, pursue confiscation of illicit assets alongside convictions and strengthen mutual legal assistance, extradition and cross-border asset recovery.

Fagbemi stressed the distinction between trafficking and drug dependence.

“While traffickers must face the full weight of the law, those experiencing drug use disorders require evidence-based care, counseling, treatment, and community reintegration,” he said.

The ECOWAS Commissioner for Human Development and Social Affairs, Nassirou Bako-Arifari, said the plan aligned with regional commitments and pledged the commission’s support.

ECOWAS would “stand with Nigeria at every step,” he said, adding that “no country can win this fight alone.”

Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Drugs and Narcotics, Abass Adigun, represented by Dominic Okafor, pledged legislative support and oversight, stressing the need for adequate funding and coordination among agencies. Yobe State First Lady, Hafsat Kollere Buni, also pledged support.

Marwa acknowledged the European Union’s sponsorship of the previous plan and the support of the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime and ECOWAS.

The launch, themed “Strategic Action for a Drug-Free Nation,” brought together government officials, lawmakers, diplomats, traditional and religious leaders, civil society organisations, businesses and youth groups.

“Five years from now, the significance of today’s launch will not be judged by the ceremony,” Shettima said. “Let this be the moment Nigeria moves from policy to action.”

title: Syndicate fakes baby’s death, sells 16-day-old for N1.5m
description:
From Lateef Dada, Osogbo
The Osun State Police Command has rescued a 16-day-old baby boy allegedly sold for N1.5 million to a buyer in Akure, Ondo State, by a child trafficking syndicate that staged the infant’s death to deceive his teenage mother.
The police also arrested several suspects allegedly
content:
From Lateef Dada, Osogbo

The Osun State Police Command has rescued a 16-day-old baby boy allegedly sold for N1.5 million to a buyer in Akure, Ondo State, by a child trafficking syndicate that staged the infant’s death to deceive his teenage mother.

The police also arrested several suspects allegedly involved in the trafficking network.

The Police Public Relations Officer, Abiodun Ojelabi, who disclosed this in a statement on Monday, said the operation followed intelligence that exposed the syndicate’s activities.

According to the police, 18-year-old Victoria Michael was admitted to a private hospital in Kajola on November 1, where she gave birth to a baby boy the following day. She was discharged on November 3.

The biological father of the child, identified only as Tayo, reportedly refused to accept responsibility for the pregnancy or the baby.

Before the delivery, a 30-year-old friend of the teenage mother, identified as Comfort Olayinka, had allegedly contacted a woman, Eri-Ife, in Abeokuta, Ogun State, claiming that Victoria could not cater for the baby and was looking for someone to take over his care.

Eri-Ife subsequently linked Comfort to 46-year-old Oladipo Olamide, who allegedly claimed to operate a non-governmental organisation dedicated to caring for underprivileged children. The police, however, later established that the claim was false.

On November 5, Comfort and Victoria reportedly travelled to Ogun State, where they handed the newborn to Oladipo.

In a bid to conceal the transaction, Comfort allegedly deceived the teenage mother into believing that her baby had died.

She reportedly handed Victoria a folded, baby-shaped object inside a bag and instructed her to throw it into the Lafenwa River, making her believe she was disposing of her dead child’s remains.

The police said Comfort had already collected N450,000 from Oladipo under the guise of providing care for the teenage mother.

Acting on intelligence, police operatives stormed Abeokuta on November 17 and arrested Oladipo.

During interrogation, he reportedly confessed to selling the infant to a woman identified as Mrs Bolanle Ruth.

The following day, Oladipo led detectives to Akure, Ondo State, where the baby was recovered and Mrs Ruth arrested.

She reportedly confessed to paying Oladipo N1.5 million to facilitate the purchase of the child.

Oladipo was also said to have promised to process official adoption documents through the relevant government agencies, but failed to do so.

The police said all the suspects had confessed to their respective roles in the crime and would be charged to court upon the conclusion of investigations.

The Commissioner of Police, Osun State Command, CP Ibrahim Zungura, warned individuals and criminal groups involved in child trafficking to desist from the criminal act or face the full weight of the law.

He reiterated the command’s commitment to protecting lives and property and ensuring that perpetrators of criminal activities were brought to justice.

title: Troops foil planned attacks, neutralise 37 terrorists in Borno
description:
Troops of the Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), have neutralised 37 terrorists and destroyed four terrorist vehicles in a series of intelligence-led precision air strikes across Borno State.
The operations, conducted by the Air Component of OPHK between November 16 and 23, 2
content:
Troops of the Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), have neutralised 37 terrorists and destroyed four terrorist vehicles in a series of intelligence-led precision air strikes across Borno State.

The operations, conducted by the Air Component of OPHK between November 16 and 23, 2026, also led to the destruction of a terrorist staging facility and disrupted suspected Improvised Explosive Device (IED) activities along troops’ operational routes.

In a statement issued on Monday in Maiduguri, the Acting Media Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI, Captain Mohammed Goni, said six precision air strikes were conducted across five locations within the theatre of operations.

He said the strikes resulted in the neutralisation of 37 terrorists, as confirmed by Battle Damage Assessment (BDA), and the destruction of four terrorist vehicles.

According to him, the operations were carried out based on credible intelligence and sustained Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR), targeting terrorist movements, hideouts and logistics assets across Monguno Local Government Area, Kerenoa and Fage in Marte LGA, and the Tumbuma Baba general area of Kukawa LGA.

Giving details of the operations, Goni said on November 16, troops launched a pre-emptive strike following verified intelligence that about 40 terrorists were moving north-east of Monguno to attack troops.

He said the subsequent BDA confirmed that 10 terrorists were neutralised, while several others sustained injuries.

On November 17, an ISR asset conducting surveillance over Arina Chiki identified a terrorist staging facility where insurgents were reportedly planning an attack on troops’ defensive positions.

The location was subsequently engaged with precision fire, destroying the targeted building, with no further movement observed within the structure.

Goni said that on November 20, an Intelligence, Surveillance, Target Acquisition and Reconnaissance (ISTAR) asset monitoring Kerenoa spotted two terrorist vehicles parked near a tree.

The vehicles were engaged in a precision strike and subsequently confirmed destroyed.

Similarly, an ISTAR asset operating over the Fage general area on the same day identified a terrorist vehicle at an IED assembly location, where preparations were reportedly underway to plant explosives along a troop movement route.

He said the vehicle was immediately engaged and destroyed, disrupting the terrorists’ suspected IED operations in the area.

The military spokesman further disclosed that on November 23, an ISTAR asset monitoring the Tumbuma Baba general area identified another terrorist vehicle following intelligence reports of terrorist activities in the location.

The vehicle was subsequently destroyed in a precision air strike, as confirmed by BDA.

He added that surveillance later tracked two suspected terrorists moving from a nearby structure to join six others taking cover under a tree.

After additional terrorists joined the gathering, the military launched another precision air strike, which, according to the BDA, neutralised all eight terrorists at the location.

Operation HADIN KAI commended the professionalism of its air and intelligence components, reaffirming its commitment to sustained offensive operations in collaboration with ground forces to defeat terrorism and restore lasting peace in the North-East.

The post Troops foil planned attacks, neutralise 37 terrorists in Borno appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.
