title: N582m fraud: Ex-NNPCL cooperative president given Dec 15 deadline for arraignment
description:
Justice Leslie Wike of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, High Court in Gwarinpa, Abuja, yesterday ordered the former President of the NNPC Staff Multi-Purpose Cooperative Society, Olalekan Ogunbayo, to appear in court on December 15, 2026, for his arraignment over an alleged N582 Million fraud.
Th
content:
Justice Leslie Wike of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, High Court in Gwarinpa, Abuja, yesterday ordered the former President of the NNPC Staff Multi-Purpose Cooperative Society, Olalekan Ogunbayo, to appear in court on December 15, 2026, for his arraignment over an alleged N582 Million fraud.

The judge warned that Ogunbayo risked a warrant of arrest if he failed to appear on the next adjourned date.

Ogunbayo and Abolade Nurudeen are being prosecuted by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC on an eight-count charge bordering on criminal misappropriation, conspiracy and corruption in connection with the alleged diversion of N582  realised from the sale of a property belonging to the NNPC Staff Multi-Purpose Cooperative Society.

At Monday’s proceedings, prosecution counsel, R.U. Adagba, informed the court that the matter was scheduled for arraignment but the first defendant was again absent in court.

Adagba recalled that Ogunbayo was also absent at the previous sitting on October 26, 2026, despite an undertaking by his counsel to produce him in court.

She urged the court to issue a warrant of arrest against him pursuant to Sections 35, 114 and 115 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act, 2015, citing his repeated failure to appear, lack of  explanation for his non-attendance and the prosecution’s inability to establish his whereabouts.

The prosecution counsel further told the court that several efforts had been made to secure Ogunbayo’s appearance, including written invitations and attempts to reach his surety, who stood for him when he was granted administrative bail.

She also argued that the defendant was aware of the charge pending against him, having personally deposed to an affidavit in support of a bail application before the court on October 13, 2026.

However, counsel to the first defendant, Innocent Adoo, acknowledged that he had undertaken to produce his client but explained that the prosecution had not served him with a copy of the charge.

Adoo informed the court that Ogunbayo had contacted his head of Chambers earlier in the day, claiming that he had been invited by the Inspector-General of Police and the Code of Conduct Bureau over the same subject matter.

He said obtaining a copy of the charge would enable his client to establish that the matter was already before the court when responding to the invitations.

In her response, Adagba described the defence counsel’s position on service as a misrepresentation, insisting that the court had not made any order authorising service of the charge on him on behalf of the first defendant.

She explained that the prosecution had taken additional steps to secure Ogunbayo’s appearance, including writing to his office on October 22, 2026, and making efforts to reach his surety.

Adagba also maintained that the defendant was fully aware of the pending criminal proceedings, having personally filed an affidavit in support of his bail application before the court.

On the alleged invitations by the police and the Code of Conduct Bureau, she clarified that the EFCC was prosecuting the charge before the court and was not a party to any separate proceedings involving the other agencies.

In her ruling, Justice Wike directed that the charge against Ogunbayo be served on him through his counsel, Adoo.

The judge further warned that the defendant would risk a warrant of arrest if he failed to appear in court on the next adjourned date.

The matter was adjourned until December 15, 2026, for arraignment.

Ogarabe gave the assurance at the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) Combined Stakeholders’ Meeting held at the Commission’s
content:
The Commissioner of Police, Enugu State Command, Fidelis Ogarabe, has assured residents of adequate security before, during and after the 2027 General Elections.

Ogarabe gave the assurance at the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) Combined Stakeholders’ Meeting held at the Commission’s State Headquarters, Independence Layout, Enugu.

Speaking at the interactive meeting in his capacity as Co-Chairman of the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES), the CP reaffirmed the readiness of the Nigeria Police Force and other security agencies to provide adequate security and ensure a peaceful electoral process.

He urged citizens, particularly eligible voters, to remain law-abiding, shun acts capable of undermining the electoral process and support security agencies with credible and timely information to ensure peaceful, secure and credible elections.

In a statement, the Police Public Relations Officer of the command, SP Daniel Ndukwe, said the INEC Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC), Dr Chukwu Chukwuemeka, had earlier outlined the Commission’s ongoing preparations for the elections.

According to the statement, the REC highlighted activities including the collection of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and the nationwide Mock Accreditation Exercise scheduled for Saturday, November 28, 2026.

Chukwuemeka also responded to questions and concerns raised by participants during the meeting.

The meeting was attended by heads of security agencies, political party leaders, the Chairman of the Enugu State Traditional Rulers Council, Igwe Samuel Asadu; the State Coordinator of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC); leaders of town unions and Presidents-General of communities across the state.

Other participants included members of the media, INEC field officers and other critical stakeholders.

title: EFCC arraigns 2 over $6.52m forgery
description:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has arraigned two defendants, Olasubomi Osinusi and Emenike Mgbemena, over an alleged $6.52 million forgery before Justice Mojisola Dada of the Special Offences Court sitting in Ikeja, Lagos.
The defendants were arraigned yesterday on an amended ei
content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has arraigned two defendants, Olasubomi Osinusi and Emenike Mgbemena, over an alleged $6.52 million forgery before Justice Mojisola Dada of the Special Offences Court sitting in Ikeja, Lagos.

The defendants were arraigned yesterday on an amended eight-count charge bordering on conspiracy, possession of fraudulent documents and the alleged use of fabricated evidence to procure a judgment of $6,520,190 against the Federal Government of Nigeria.

They were accused of conspiring to fabricate and use written statements on oath purportedly made by one Dan Mohammed Jafaru to mislead the High Court of Justice of England and Wales in proceedings involving Louis Emovbira Williams (at large), the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and the Federal Government.

Count one of the charge alleged that Osinusi, Mgbemena and Williams, on or about March 25, 2013, in Lagos, conspired to fabricate and use a written statement on oath purportedly made by Jafaru as evidence in a claim before the High Court of Justice of England and Wales involving Williams and the CBN.

The alleged offence was said to be contrary to Sections 409 and 88(1) of the Criminal Law of Lagos State, 2011, and punishable under Section 88(1) of the same law.

Count three similarly accused the defendants of conspiring to fabricate and use the purported statement on oath to procure a judgment sum of $6,520,190 against the Federal Government of Nigeria in a case involving Williams, the Federal Government and the Attorney-General of the Federation.

The defendants, however, pleaded not guilty to all the charges.

Following their pleas, prosecution counsel, Muhammed Abbah, SAN, urged the court to remand them in a correctional centre pending the continuation of trial.

Abbah, however, said the prosecution had no objection to the first defendant, Osinusi, who was initially arraigned on February 25, 2026, on a two-count charge bordering on forgery, continuing to enjoy the bail earlier granted to him.

He explained that Osinusi had consistently attended court since the commencement of proceedings.

On the second defendant, Mgbemena, the prosecution counsel told the court that he was a dual citizen of Nigeria and the United Kingdom and had allegedly failed to honour several invitations extended to him by the EFCC since 2024 and subsequently in 2025.

Abbah said the Commission had evidence that an invitation letter was dispatched to Mgbemena’s UK address, adding that the defendant also responded electronically to an email from one of the EFCC investigators.

According to him, the invitation was also scanned and forwarded to Mgbemena through email and WhatsApp, but he failed to honour it at the time.

The prosecution counsel said Mgbemena was eventually traced to a location in Nigeria following his return to the country, after which he reported to the EFCC and was granted administrative bail.

He, however, left the decision on whether the second defendant should be remanded in EFCC custody or a correctional centre to the discretion of the court.

Earlier, counsel to Mgbemena, Obinna S. Nwosu, told the court that his client was served with the amended charges on the afternoon of Friday, November 20, 2026.

He explained that he could not file a bail application immediately because he was in Abuja at the time.

Nwosu said the defence would file a formal bail application for his client, whom he described as a senior member of the Bar.

He also informed the court that Mgbemena had earlier been granted administrative bail by the EFCC and that his Nigerian and British passports were still in the custody of the Commission.

In her remarks, Justice Dada observed that the submissions before the court showed that Mgbemena had been invited by the EFCC but failed to honour the invitation at the time.

In her ruling, the judge ordered that Mgbemena be remanded in a correctional centre pending the determination of his bail application.

She, however, allowed Osinusi to continue enjoying the bail earlier granted to him.

Justice Dada adjourned the hearing of Mgbemena’s bail application to December 7, 2026, while February 8 and 9, 2027, were fixed for the commencement of trial.

content:
Delta State Police Command has curfew on Uduere Community, Ughelli North Local Government .

The curfew  from 6 pm to 6 am  was imposed by the command following the reported violence during a campaign rally of the NDC at Uduere Community, which allegedly resulted in loss of lives and injuries to several persons.

It was gathered that an unspecified number of persons lost their lives while many others were injured. 

In a statement,  The Police Public Relations Officer in the state,  SP Bright Edafe, said,” the Delta State Government has imposed a curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area, from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. daily until further notice. The Command has commenced investigations to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible.

“The Command therefore urges residents of Ughelli LG  to comply strictly with the curfew imposed by the Delta State Government, restricting movement between 1800hrs to 0600hrs until further notice. Residents are advised to remain calm and cooperate with security personnel in the interest of public safety.

“ Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, CP Samuel  Erale, has directed intensified security operations in the affected area to prevent further violence and maintain law and order. The CP has ordered a full-scale investigation and assures residents of the state that anyone found culpable will face the full weight of the law, irrespective of political affiliation or status, and urges members of the public to provide credible information to assist ongoing investigations.

“CP Erale, extends his condolences to the bereaved families and wishes the injured a speedy recovery. He assures residents of the Command’s commitment to protecting lives and property and ensuring a peaceful environment for lawful political activities. The CP warns political actors and their supporters against thuggery, intimidation and the unlawful use of firearms, stressing that political differences must never be allowed to degenerate into violence or loss of lives. “

content:
…….Honours Enerst Ndukwe, ABC Orjiakor, Francis Fatona on Convocation

By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

No fewer than 59 students of Alex Ekwueme Federal University of Ndufu-Alike Ikwo (AE-FUNAI), Ebonyi State have bagged first class for the four sets of 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026 academic years for first degrees.

The Vice Chancellor of the University Professor Daniel Nwachukwu who disclosed this during Pre-Covocation press conferenc for 9th, 10th, 11th and 12th combined convocation, said that a total of 8,649 students would be graduating.

He noted that the 1, 867 students obtained Second Class Upper Division while 5,040 students got Second Class Lower Division and 1, 675 students received Thrid Class also 8 students obtained Pass.

The VC said that a total of 552 postgraduate students would be graduating across various disciplines as follows PhD (44), M.Sc. (348) and PGD (160)

Professor Nwachukwu who is organizing his first convocation ceremony on November 28, 2026 having been appointed the fourth Vice Chancellor of the University ten months ago said he had brought many innovation to the institution within the short period in office.

“According to the programme of activities: “Wednesday, 25th November, 2026: Research and Innovation Faire  We will showcase the research and groundbreaking innovations of our academics to the public. This underscores the contributions of our university to the betterment of society and the body of knowledge.

“Thursday, 26th November, 2026: Alumni Dinner & Price Giving Day: We will host the alumni, who are critical partners to the development of our university to a dinner. At the event, prices will also be given to graduating students that distinguished themselves in their various fields/discipline, and other aspects of human endeavours.

“Friday, 27th November, 2026: Chancellor’s Ball: We will host our highly-revered Chancellor, the Alake and Paramount Ruler of Egbaland, HRM Oba (Dr.) Michael Aremu Adedotun Gbadebo CFR. It will be an evening of songs and cultural display to celebrate the Chancellor.

“On Saturday, 28th November, 2026, Convocation Lecture: To be delivered by Dr. ABC Orjiakor, Pioneer Chairman, Seplat Energies Ltd, with topic: ‘Who Will Build the Nigeria We Want? Character, Competence and Opportunities in a Difficult Economy’ he stated.

The VC said that the university will confer Honorary Doctorate Degrees (Honoris Causa) to three eminent Nigerians for their unparallel contributions to the development of Nigeria in various areas.

“The nominees are; Dr. Ernest Ndukwe, Chairman, MTN, Nigeria to be awarded with Doctor of Telecommunications Engineering (honoris causa); Dr. ABC Orjiakor, Pioneer Chairman, Seplat Energies Ltd, to be awarded with Doctor of Business Administration (honoris causa), and Dr. Olayiwola Francis Fatona, Founder Renaissance Energy to be awarded Doctor of Business Administration (honoris causa).

“I assumed office as the 4th substantive Vice-Chancellor of the University on February 11, 2026 with the vision of making AE-FUNAI a hub of academic and intellectual excellence. In the last 10 months, we have hit the ground running. We have consolidated the gains of the past, while also making some sweeping changes geared towards repositioning the university. Some of the gains include:

“We have instituted democratic governance in the Faculties and College of Medical Sciences, while also decentralizing administration to the Faculties. We have granted semi autonomous status to the College of Medical Sciences

“We have established 14 new programmes across 5 Faculties to meet 21st century demands. These include Hotel Management and Tourism; Zoology, Environmental Biology, and Plant Science and Biotechnology; Urban and Regional Planning, Estate Management, Surveying and Geoinformatics, and Quantity Surveying; as well as Physiotherapy, Optometry, and Medical Radiography. Others are Marketing, Social Work, and Library and Information Science.

“To expand access to university education and offer academic degrees to willing students, we have established academic affiliations with Marist Polytechnic, Enugu, AE-FUTHA College of Nursing, Abakaliki, Royal College of Nursing Ezzangbo, Mater Misericordia College Afikpo, and CSMT School of Biblical Studies Abakaliki, and partnership with Shandong University, Jianzhu, China, on staff and students exchange programme.

“We have renovated the University Staff School, VCs office and Conference room, senate chambers, among others

“About 150 solar street lights have been installed from the Main Gate to the Senate Building and College of Medical Sciences through the support of Hon. Nkemkanma Kama. We have also procured additional 200 solar street light which are been mounted across the campus.

“A MoU was signed with AG-Zara for new student hostels. Senator Onyekachi Nwebonyi pledged a N250M Faculty of Law Auditorium, while Hon. Iduma Igariwey pledged a massive building project. Hon. Chinedu Ogah has also pledged a CBT Centre for the University. Further, a Renewed Hope Hostel is also been constructed in the University.

“The University is at an advanced stage of discussion with a private investor for the building of a water processing industrial plant to provide portable water within and outside the campus. The plant will also provide hands-on research activities for staff and students.

” We have a proposal from a private investor for the establishment of a 21st century self-funded inter and intra campus transportation scheme using electric vehicles at no cost to the university.

“Collaborations with INNOSON Motors and Zobis Wires & Cables for research, internships, and technology transfer has been consummated.

“We signed a partnership with Laudable Insurance Brokers Ltd for a Students Personal Accident Insurance and Combined Risk Insurance Policy to protect our students and the university physical infrastructure.

“We secured funding from TETFund and renovated the auditoriums of Faculty of Physical Sciences and Faculty of Biological Sciences. It is over 80% completed. We are revisiting the long abandoned Central Administrative building and the main library by TETFund” Prof Nwachukwu stated.

title: FG’s oil revenue tumbles N1.44tn despite price boom
description:
The Federal Government recorded a N1.44tn decline in gross oil revenue in the first half of 2026 despite a 41.23 per cent increase in international crude oil prices in the second quarter of the year, according to the Budget Office of the Federation.
An analysis of the Second Quarter and Half-Year 20
content:
The Federal Government recorded a N1.44tn decline in gross oil revenue in the first half of 2026 despite a 41.23 per cent increase in international crude oil prices in the second quarter of the year, according to the Budget Office of the Federation.

An analysis of the Second Quarter and Half-Year 2026 Budget Implementation Report showed that gross oil revenue fell to N7.88tn between January and June 2026, compared with approximately N9.32tn recorded during the corresponding period of 2025.

The decline represented a 15.45 per cent year-on-year contraction, highlighting Nigeria’s continued difficulty in translating favourable international oil prices into higher government revenue.

The report, prepared by the Budget Office under the Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning, disclosed that the N7.88tn collected during the first six months of 2026 was also N10.78tn below the government’s half-year revenue target of N18.65tn.

This translated into a budget performance rate of just 42.22 per cent, leaving a substantial gap in the revenue expected to finance government expenditure.

The development occurred despite international crude oil prices averaging $104.52 per barrel in the Q2 of 2026, compared with $74 per barrel in the corresponding period of 2025.

The increase of $30.52 per barrel represented a 41.23 per cent rise, while the average price was also $39.67, or 61.17 per cent, above the 2026 budget benchmark of $64.85 per barrel.

However, the government was unable to fully benefit from the price increase because of persistent production challenges, weak oil sales receipts, lower-than-expected petroleum taxes and deductions from oil revenue.

Explaining the situation, the Budget Office said, “The low Net oil revenue performance in the second quarter of 2026 compared with the quarterly budget projection could be attributed to the decrease in oil production and lifting, which was also due to low sector investment and legacy oil production constraint issues.”

It added, “The performance could also be ascribed to high fiscal deduction as provided in the PIA.”

The Petroleum Industry Act provides the framework for fiscal obligations, deductions and revenue administration in Nigeria’s petroleum industry.

The report identified crude oil theft, pipeline vandalism, security challenges, inadequate investment in modern infrastructure, corruption and regulatory uncertainty among the difficulties confronting the sector.

Although average crude oil production increased to 1.72 million barrels per day in the Q2 of 2026 from 1.68 million barrels per day in the corresponding period of 2025, output remained below the government’s budget target of 1.84 million barrels per day.

This represented a production gap of approximately 120,000 barrels per day, equivalent to 6.52 per cent of the budget benchmark.

Production nevertheless improved from the 1.55 million barrels per day recorded in the first quarter, suggesting a gradual recovery in output that had yet to translate into the expected fiscal gains.

The Budget Office observed that the improvement in oil prices was insufficient to overcome the structural challenges affecting production and government receipts.

It said, “Despite the favourable international crude oil price environment during the quarter, average production remained below the budget benchmark, limiting the revenue gains available to the Federation.”

The agency consequently recommended stronger security around petroleum infrastructure, improved operational efficiency, greater investment and stricter enforcement of royalty and other statutory payment obligations.

A breakdown of the half-year performance showed that petroleum profit and gas taxes recorded the largest shortfall, generating N2.92tn against a projected N11.96tn.

The N9.05tn deficit represented 75.62 per cent of the expected receipts from this revenue category, making it the biggest contributor to the overall oil revenue gap.

Similarly, gross profit oil from crude oil and gas sales generated only N285.64bn, compared with a half-year target of N1.17tn. This represented a shortfall of N884.81bn, or 75.60 per cent.

Oil and gas royalties performed relatively better, generating N4.07tn against a projected N5.42tn, although the government still missed its target by N1.35tn, equivalent to 24.87 per cent.

Royalties consequently accounted for approximately 51.65 per cent of total gross oil revenue collected during the first six months of 2026, compared with 37.04 per cent contributed by petroleum profit and gas taxes.

The figures showed that royalties had become the largest component of reported gross oil receipts, even as direct crude oil and gas sales contributed just 3.63 per cent.

Other revenue categories recorded mixed performances.

Concessional rentals generated N25.02bn against a half-year target of N19.43bn, exceeding projections by N5.59bn, or 28.74 per cent.

Miscellaneous oil receipts, including pipeline fees, reached N444.73bn, compared with a target of N3.08bn, representing an increase of N441.65bn above the projection.

Incidental oil revenue, comprising royalty recoveries and marginal field licences, generated N113.31bn against a target of N82.01bn, exceeding expectations by N31.30bn.

Gas-flaring penalties, for which no budgetary provision was made, contributed N324.56bn during the first half of the year.

The post FG’s oil revenue tumbles N1.44tn despite price boom appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Lekki Tech Academy targets next  generation of African tech professionals
description:
As demand for technology professionals continues to grow globally, Lekki Tech Academy has announced the commencement of its technology training programmes, offering professional courses across several high-demand areas of the digital economy.
The academy, established to contribute to technology skil
content:
As demand for technology professionals continues to grow globally, Lekki Tech Academy has announced the commencement of its technology training programmes, offering professional courses across several high-demand areas of the digital economy.

The academy, established to contribute to technology skills development and workforce capacity building, is providing training opportunities in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, software engineering, web development, data science, cloud computing, robotics, digital product management and other emerging technology disciplines.

The institution is targeting young graduates, students, working professionals, entrepreneurs and individuals seeking to acquire relevant technology skills or transition into the rapidly expanding technology industry.

Speaking on the vision behind the academy, Head of Corporate Communications, Jessica Izuora, said management established the Academy to close the gap between classroom learning and industry needs.

“Technology is reshaping every sector. Our goal is to equip learners with skills they can actually use in the workplace,” she said.

According to the academy, its programmes are designed to combine structured learning with practical assignments, industry-relevant projects and professional development.

In a move aimed at strengthening the connection between classroom learning and workplace experience, Lekki Tech Academy is also introducing a six-month internship placement opportunity for every professional certificate enrolment.

Miss Izuora said the internship is central to the academy’s approach.

“We don’t want our students to graduate with theory alone. The internship gives them real exposure, mentorship and confidence,” she said.

The initiative is expected to provide learners with opportunities for practical exposure, professional mentorship and portfolio development.

The academy further explained that its programmes accommodate both beginners and individuals with existing technology knowledge who wish to upgrade their professional competencies.

With Africa’s youthful population and growing digital economy, the institution believes that developing a skilled technology workforce will remain essential to economic competitiveness, innovation and employment generation.

“Africa has the talent. What we are building is the pathway for that talent to compete globally,” Mrs Izuora added.

Lekki Tech Academy says it intends to grow into a recognised centre for technology education, innovation and professional development, contributing to the development of globally competitive African technology talent.

The post Lekki Tech Academy targets next generation of African tech professionals appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NEC approves additional N130bn for police training institutions
description:
The National Economic Council on Monday approved an additional N130bn for the rehabilitation of Nigeria’s police training institutions.
This brings the total funding to N230bn as the country prepares for the establishment of state police and the recruitment of 50,000 new officers.
The Council also e
content:
The National Economic Council on Monday approved an additional N130bn for the rehabilitation of Nigeria’s police training institutions.

This brings the total funding to N230bn as the country prepares for the establishment of state police and the recruitment of 50,000 new officers.

The Council also endorsed two major development projects backed by proposed World Bank financing of $850m, covering disaster preparedness and early childhood development, and received an economic update showing that inflation had fallen for the fifth consecutive month to its lowest level since September 2020.

These were among the decisions taken at the Council’s 162nd meeting, chaired by Vice President Kashim Shettima, according to a statement signed on Monday by the Vice President’s Senior Special Assistant on Media and Communications, Stanley Nkwocha.

“With state police on the horizon, the National Economic Council has committed an extra N130bn to overhaul Nigeria’s police training institutions, bringing the total funding to N230bn,” the statement read.

Presenting an update on the rehabilitation of police training institutions, the NEC Ad-Hoc Committee, chaired by Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah, disclosed that interventions were currently underway in 13 locations across the country, with 30 per cent of the rehabilitation work completed.

The committee said the additional N130bn would accelerate rehabilitation works, upgrade training facilities and strengthen the capacity of police institutions to accommodate increased recruitment and training requirements.

The Council had earlier approved N100bn for the rehabilitation programme following the establishment of the committee in October 2025, on the recommendation of President Bola Tinubu.

The intervention is also expected to support preparations for the recruitment of 50,000 police personnel and improve the country’s security training infrastructure ahead of the rollout of state policing.

On the state of the economy, Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, informed the Council that Nigeria’s real Gross Domestic Product grew by 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, compared with 4.23 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025.

Oyedele disclosed that headline inflation declined for the fifth consecutive month to 14.06 per cent in October 2026, its lowest level since September 2020, while external reserves stood at $54.87bn as of November 12, 2026.

He added that Nigeria’s trade surplus doubled from N10.2tn in the first half of 2025 to N20.1tn in the corresponding period of 2026, while net revenue distributed through the Federation Account Allocation Committee rose by 44 per cent, from N15.2tn in 2024 to N21.9tn in 2025.

Oyedele, however, cautioned that the improving macroeconomic indicators had yet to translate sufficiently into relief for households and businesses, particularly in the areas of food prices, electricity costs, access to affordable credit and employment. He noted that food inflation remained elevated at 19.13 per cent in October, while high lending rates and energy costs continued to place pressure on businesses and household incomes.

The Council also approved two memoranda presented through the Federal Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning, headed by Senator Atiku Bagudu.

The first memorandum concerned the proposed $350m Accelerating Resilience through Investment Systems and Engagement, ARISE-Nigeria, project, a six-year World Bank-supported programme designed to strengthen the country’s capacity to anticipate, prepare for and respond to floods, droughts, fires and other natural disasters.

The programme will improve emergency operations centres, early warning systems, weather monitoring and disaster response financing at federal and state levels.

Nkwocha revealed that between five and 10 states were expected to participate in the initial phase, with selection based on disaster risk exposure, institutional readiness and commitment to emergency preparedness.

The second memorandum concerned Nigeria’s State-Led Early Childhood Development Programme, designed to improve children’s access to healthcare, nutrition, early learning and protection services across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

The initiative is expected to receive support from a proposed $500m World Bank financing arrangement, with the Global Financing Facility indicating potential additional grant support of $30m.

Under the programme, early childhood development hubs will connect primary healthcare facilities with childcare, preschool education and other essential social services, particularly in underserved communities. State governors are expected to provide leadership for implementation, resource mobilisation and accountability, while existing institutions will coordinate service delivery.

On the proposed NIMC Act 2026, the Council called for stronger collaboration between the National Identity Management Commission and state governments to accelerate the registration of Nigerians and improve the integration of the National Identification Number into public services.

The Council urged state governments to fast-track identity registration and data capture to ensure that all Nigerians are covered by the national identity system, saying the initiative would strengthen public service delivery, improve tax administration, eliminate duplicate records and reduce fraud in government payrolls, pensions and social intervention programmes.

On pension reforms, the Director-General of the National Pension Commission, Omolola Oloworaran, presented a proposal titled ‘Securing the Retirement of Nigerian Workers While Strengthening State Finances,’ calling for the full implementation of the Contributory Pension Scheme across the federation.

The Council approved the proposal and urged state governors to formally adopt implementation timelines for the scheme, while directing their administrative and finance teams to work with PenCom on the necessary arrangements.

In his opening remarks, Vice President Shettima said Nigeria’s economic future and the lasting success of President Tinubu’s reforms depended on building strong institutions capable of outlasting any single administration.

“While His Excellency, President Bola Tinubu, GCFR, makes the difficult reforms to stabilise the economy, we must all participate in establishing institutions capable of sustaining the benefits of those reforms. This requires ministries and states to settle practical responsibilities without losing sight of the people affected. To achieve this, we must cooperate,” he said.

Shettima urged Council members to consider the Nigerian who would depend on the decisions they made years from now. He said sound practice in one jurisdiction should inform decisions elsewhere while respecting differences in capacity and circumstance across the country.

“The quality of our cooperation will shape the inheritance we leave,” he said.

On the ARISE disaster resilience project, the Vice President said the fundamental obligation was “to reduce the damage that disruption can do to incomes, enterprises and public services,” noting that resilience begins with decisions made before a shock rather than after it.

“This matters especially where a family or business has little room to absorb another loss. The capacity to recover should never depend entirely on the resources a person already possesses.

“People affected by an intervention must also have a place in shaping it. Their experience can reveal what a proposal overlooks. The strength of a project rests partly on the institutions and citizens that will carry it,” Shettima said.

The post NEC approves additional N130bn for police training institutions appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: Ebonyi PDP candidate Odii promises 180,000 jobs
description:
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki



The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Ebonyi State, Chief Ifeanyi Chukwuma Odii, has promised to create more than 180,000 jobs and introduce free public primary and secondary education if elected governor in 2027.







Odii made the pledge
content:
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Ebonyi State, Chief Ifeanyi Chukwuma Odii, has promised to create more than 180,000 jobs and introduce free public primary and secondary education if elected governor in 2027.

Odii made the pledges while unveiling his 2027 governorship manifesto, titled “ANYI G’EMEYA”: A Promise of Possibility, which outlines his proposed development agenda for the state.

The manifesto contains plans to transform the state’s economy through industrialisation, agricultural development and private-sector investment, while reducing its dependence on federal allocations.

It identifies economic development and industrialisation, infrastructure, youth and human capital development, institutional reforms and security as key pillars of the proposed administration.

On economic development, Odii said his administration would prioritise agriculture, manufacturing, trade and commerce, mining and quarrying, and tourism to create employment and expand the state’s revenue base.

He proposed moving agriculture from subsistence production to commercial and technology-driven farming through mechanisation, improved farming inputs, irrigation, affordable financing and stronger market linkages.

The manifesto also proposes the establishment of special agro-industrial processing zones and clusters in strategic locations to encourage large-scale processing, reduce post-harvest losses and increase the value of agricultural produce.

It further identifies an initial 400 to 500 hectares of suitable land for commercial farming and agro-industrial investments, subject to feasibility assessments and consultations with host communities.

Smallholder farmers, according to the document, would be integrated into the proposed investments through outgrower schemes.

In the manufacturing sector, the PDP candidate promised to establish industrial clusters and manufacturing hubs equipped with electricity, access roads and water supply to attract small, medium and large-scale businesses.

He also proposed simplifying business registration and permit processes, eliminating multiple and arbitrary levies within the state’s jurisdiction and improving the regulatory environment to attract domestic and foreign investors.

On electricity, Odii said his administration would leverage the opportunities provided by the Electricity Act 2023 to attract private investment into power generation and distribution.

He listed solar mini-grids, biomass, gas-based power solutions and other renewable energy sources as options for improving electricity supply to industrial clusters, commercial centres and underserved communities.

On infrastructure, he promised investments in roads, housing, water supply and digital connectivity, with particular emphasis on linking agricultural production areas to industrial clusters, storage facilities and markets.

For the education sector, Odii pledged free public primary and secondary education, improved school infrastructure, better teaching quality and expanded access to practical and technical education.

He also proposed partnerships with educational institutions, manufacturers and industry associations to strengthen vocational training and equip young people with skills required by emerging industries.

In healthcare, the manifesto promises improvements in medical infrastructure, staffing, access to essential medicines and the quality of healthcare delivery, particularly in underserved communities.

On security, Odii advocated a coordinated, intelligence-led and community-based approach to tackling kidnapping, communal conflicts, cultism, drug abuse and other criminal activities.

He specifically identified the longstanding communal disputes involving Abaomege and Ishinkwo, Ezza and Ezilo, Ezza and Effium, as well as Ngbo and Agila, as conflicts requiring sustained intervention and peaceful resolution.

The proposed approach includes stronger collaboration among security agencies, traditional rulers, local governments and community organisations, alongside improved intelligence gathering, surveillance and emergency response mechanisms.

The PDP candidate also promised institutional reforms covering land administration, right-of-way permits, the civil service and judicial administration.

On funding, he said his administration would conduct a comprehensive assessment of the state’s financial position, existing obligations and development priorities while strengthening internally generated revenue without imposing unnecessary burdens on residents and businesses.

He proposed public-private partnerships, development financing, community development partnerships and infrastructure tax incentives as alternative funding mechanisms.

The manifesto also promises transparent procurement processes, digital budgeting, expenditure tracking and regular publication of reports on government revenue and expenditure.

On implementation, Odii pledged to develop a detailed execution plan for the proposed initiatives and pursue visible results within his first 200 days in office if elected.

He also promised to establish a delivery unit to monitor government commitments and ensure accountability for measurable outcomes.

The manifesto presents his vision of making Ebonyi a preferred investment destination through inclusive economic growth, sustainable wealth creation and improved living standards.

The post 2027: Ebonyi PDP candidate Odii promises 180,000 jobs appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Church advocates good governance ahead of elections
description:
The Eternal Sacred Order of the Cherubim and Seraphim has urged Nigerians to seek divine guidance before voting in the February 2027 general elections.
The Vice Baba Aladura of the church, Elder John Oladapo, stated this recently during the international press conference and flag-off of the centenar
content:
The Eternal Sacred Order of the Cherubim and Seraphim has urged Nigerians to seek divine guidance before voting in the February 2027 general elections.

The Vice Baba Aladura of the church, Elder John Oladapo, stated this recently during the international press conference and flag-off of the centenary celebrations of the United Fogo Olorun Han Band at the church’s international headquarters, Ojokoro, Lagos State.

Oladapo said the church was committed to promoting peace, praying for the country, and encouraging those in government to embrace good governance and do what was right for Nigerians.

He said, “We keep on praying for this nation and the world at large because whatever affects one nation affects the other. We are preaching peace because we cannot live in a country where things are not going the way they should. We talk to people in government. We encourage them to be nice, to do the right thing and to make peace available in the country.

“To our members, we tell them that we are not partisans. We permit everybody to go and get their PVC and vote for the candidate of their choice. In doing that, ask God for direction. Don’t use your human decision alone; God will always direct His people to do the right thing.”

The cleric expressed optimism that the February 2027 elections would be successful, adding that the church would continue to pray for divine intervention in Nigeria and other parts of the world.

The press conference was held as part of activities marking the 100th anniversary of the United Fogo Olorun Han Band, established in 1926 by the founder of the Cherubim and Seraphim Church, Saint Moses Orimolade Tunolase.

In his keynote address, titled “The United Fogo Olorun Han Band at 100: Preserving the Legacy of Our Founding Father Through Service and Righteousness in Worship,” Oladapo said the centenary was an opportunity to reflect on the band’s history, spiritual responsibilities and future.

He explained that the band was among four groups established by Orimolade in 1926 to support critical areas of the church’s ministry as its membership increased.

According to him, the establishment of the bands was guided by the Holy Spirit and reflected the founding father’s application of the principle of delegation in managing the growing church.

Describing the centenary as a celebration of faith, dedication and service, Oladapo said successive generations had sustained the vision despite changing social circumstances.

He said, “Our centenary is therefore a celebration of God’s faithfulness across generations. We stand on the shoulders of men whose commitment made this milestone possible, and we owe it to them and to future generations to preserve and strengthen this inheritance.”

Speaking on the theme of the celebration, ‘Righteousness in Worship,’ drawn from Isaiah 60:21, the cleric urged members to demonstrate godly character and integrity in their worship and service.

Oladapo also urged the band’s leadership to prepare younger members to sustain its legacy, stressing that its 100-year history should inspire renewed commitment rather than complacency.

He said the next century should be marked by stronger spirituality, effective organisation, unity, accountability and deliberate mentoring of younger generations.

“Our relevance will not be determined by how many years we have existed but by the quality of our contribution to the Kingdom of God,” he said.

He added that the band’s first 100 years testified to God’s faithfulness, while its next century should demonstrate the members’ faithfulness to God.

The Chairman of the Centenary Committee, Elder Niyi Afolabi, said the band had proudly carried the torch of the Cherubim and Seraphim Church relentlessly over the last 100 years.

“Composed mostly of individuals who are elders and leaders across our churches, the band has served at the forefront of preserving the heritage and legacy of Saint Moses Orimolade Tunolase – contributing to church development and developing a new generation of leaders for the future,” he added.

The post Church advocates good governance ahead of elections appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NEDC links isolated Yobe communities with bridges
description: The North-East Development Commission has commenced the construction of bridges to connect isolated communities in Potiskum Local Government Area of Yobe State, while a civil society coalition has criticised the North-West Development Commission over alleged delays in staff recruitment and distribut
content:
The North-East Development Commission has commenced the construction of bridges to connect isolated communities in Potiskum Local Government Area of Yobe State, while a civil society coalition has criticised the North-West Development Commission over alleged delays in staff recruitment and distribution of intervention materials.

Residents of Lai-Lai, Masaka and neighbouring communities in Potiskum have endured years of transportation difficulties due to a river separating them from other parts of the area, making access to hospitals, schools, markets and other essential facilities challenging.

The ongoing bridge projects are expected to ease movement, reduce travel time and improve socioeconomic activities in the affected communities.

The Yobe State Coordinator of NEDC, Prof. Ali Ibrahim Abbas, disclosed this during an inspection of the commission’s ongoing projects in Potiskum.

Abbas said the projects were part of the Federal Government’s efforts to improve infrastructure and connectivity across the North-East.

He said, “We are here in Potiskum to inspect NEDC projects. These are among the bridges currently under construction in Potiskum Local Government Area.

“One of them is the construction of a two-span, 40-metre bridge with a 2.6-kilometre asphalt road at Kara–Masaka–Mazaga Road.

“This is part of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s efforts to link these adjoining communities in the Potiskum area.”

The coordinator, who was accompanied by the commission’s consultants and contractors, said the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NEDC, Mohammed Goni Alkali, was keen on ensuring that the projects were completed before the end of 2026.

He said the contractor had assured the commission that the projects would be delivered soon.

Abbas explained that the bridges would address longstanding transportation challenges caused by the river separating the communities.

“Because of this river, many members of the communities find it difficult to go about their daily routines. Building these bridges is paramount to linking the town and making movement easier for the people.

“These projects will open up the communities, improve access to essential services and bring more opportunities to the people,” he said.

He added that the infrastructure would also boost commercial activities by enabling residents to transport their goods more easily and access markets in neighbouring communities.

A resident of Lai-Lai, Musa Ibrahim, said the bridge would end years of difficulties experienced by residents travelling to hospitals and schools.

He said, “Before now, one had to travel extra miles to access hospitals and schools. It has not been easy for us, particularly when someone needs urgent medical attention.

“We thank the NEDC for this project because it will make movement easier and save people from the difficulties they have been experiencing over the years.”

Another resident, Mato Muhammad, said the absence of a bridge had made accessing healthcare facilities particularly difficult whenever a family member fell ill.

He expressed optimism that the bridge linking Lai-Lai to Tandari, Misau Road, Race House and other neighbouring areas would improve the situation.

The residents said the completed projects would particularly benefit pregnant women, sick persons, schoolchildren and traders who frequently travel between the communities.

Meanwhile, the Coalition of Civil Society for Good Governance and Accountability has raised concerns over alleged delays by the North-West Development Commission in recruiting staff and distributing intervention materials procured for its 2026 programmes.

The coalition’s National Chairman, Dr Abdussalam Muhammad Kani, made the complaints at a press conference held at the Nigeria Union of Journalists Press Centre in Kano on Saturday.

Kani said the Federal Character Commission and other relevant regulatory agencies had approved the commission’s recruitment exercise but alleged that the process had yet to commence months after the approval.

He demanded that the NWDC management immediately advertise the vacancies and publish the application procedures, recruitment timetable and selection criteria.

“The CCSGGA is aware that the Federal Character Commission (FCC) and other relevant regulatory agencies have granted approval for employment into the commission.

“We therefore demand that the NWDC Board and Management should immediately commence the recruitment process in line with the approvals already granted,” he said.

The coalition chairman lamented that the commission had yet to publish a recruitment advertisement, open an application portal or provide an official explanation for the delay.

He warned that the silence could create suspicion of favouritism and backdoor recruitment while denying qualified young people in the North-West equal employment opportunities.

“A commission created to serve the people cannot remain understaffed, inactive and unaccountable while approvals already granted gather dust,” Kani said.

The coalition also expressed concern over what it described as delays in distributing intervention materials procured by the commission for farmers, internally displaced persons and vulnerable households across the region.

Kani listed the items as Hilux vehicles, solar-powered irrigation water pumps, fertilisers, food supplies, including rice, beans, groundnut oil, seasoning and salt, as well as streetlights and tractors.

He alleged that the materials were lying unused despite their potential to improve livelihoods and address the needs of vulnerable communities.

“These interventions have the potential to make a meaningful difference in the lives of farmers, vulnerable households and communities. However, their value can only be realised when they are distributed transparently, fairly and without unnecessary delay,” he said.

Efforts to obtain a response from the Commission’s management were unsuccessful, as several phone calls and text messages sent to its Managing Director, Prof. Shehu Abdullahi Ma’aji, were not answered.

When our correspondent visited the commission’s headquarters on Monday, he was informed that Ma’aji had travelled to Jos, Plateau State, for an official engagement, while other staff members had yet to arrive as of 10.30am.

The NWDC, established under the NWDC Act, 2024, received N15.17bn in statutory allocations between January and May 2026.

title: JIBWIS defends NERDC boss’ appointment
description: The Jama’atu Izalatil Bid’ah Wa Iqamatus Sunnah has defended the appointment of Prof. Salisu Shehu as the Executive Secretary of the Nigerian Educational Research and Development Council, describing it as well deserved and urging critics not to allow religious sentiments to influence their assessmen
content:
The Jama’atu Izalatil Bid’ah Wa Iqamatus Sunnah has defended the appointment of Prof. Salisu Shehu as the Executive Secretary of the Nigerian Educational Research and Development Council, describing it as well deserved and urging critics not to allow religious sentiments to influence their assessment.

The Islamic organisation said Shehu possessed the academic qualifications, professional experience and intellectual capacity required to lead the national education institution.

The National Chairman of JIBWIS, Sheikh Abdullah Bala Lau, stated this in a statement made available to Arewa PUNCH on Monday, congratulating the professor on his appointment.

Lau said Shehu had devoted his career to studying, teaching, research and contributing to educational development in Nigeria and beyond.

He commended the Federal Government and the Federal Ministry of Education for the appointment, expressing confidence in the ability of the new NERDC chief to discharge his responsibilities effectively.

The organisation, however, expressed concern over criticisms of the appointment linked to Shehu’s previous academic contributions to the debate on the Islamisation of Knowledge.

It cautioned individuals and groups against portraying the professor’s scholarly engagement with the subject as a reason he was unsuitable to head a national educational institution.

According to JIBWIS, such criticisms were based on misconceptions and unfounded fears that could undermine objective assessment of qualified professionals appointed to public offices.

The statement said, “Islamisation of Knowledge simply refers to a scholarly exploration of knowledge from a Muslim perspective.”

The organisation stressed the need for critics to distinguish between Islamisation of Knowledge and Islamisation of Education, insisting that the two concepts should not be confused.

It said it would not engage in the broader academic arguments surrounding the subject, noting that other scholars had already addressed what it described as the shortcomings of the criticisms.

JIBWIS further explained that Islamic values placed strong emphasis on fairness and justice to all people, irrespective of their religious or social backgrounds.

It said these principles guided Muslims in their public and private dealings and should not be misconstrued as grounds for questioning the suitability of a scholar for public service.

The organisation urged Shehu to deploy his academic experience and professional expertise in advancing the mandate of NERDC and justifying the confidence reposed in him by the Federal Government.

It also charged him to discharge his responsibilities without fear or favour and strictly adhere to the rules, regulations, goals and objectives guiding the council.

“At JIBWIS, we do not entertain any doubt that Prof. Salisu Shehu will stand firm and abide by the rules and regulations governing the institution he is appointed to supervise,” the statement added.

The organisation also appealed to individuals and groups opposed to the appointment to embrace objective assessments of public office holders rather than resorting to what it described as sentimental judgments based on identity or name.

It maintained that professionals appointed to public institutions should be assessed based on their qualifications, experience and contributions rather than subjected to criticism that undermined scholarship and constructive intellectual engagement.

The post JIBWIS defends NERDC boss’ appointment appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: INEC queries 54 officials over voter registration breaches
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission said it had issued queries to 54 of its personnel allegedly involved in voter registration irregularities across 10 states, as it begins disciplinary procedures against the affected officials.
INEC National Commissioner, Mohammed Haruna, disclosed this i
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission said it had issued queries to 54 of its personnel allegedly involved in voter registration irregularities across 10 states, as it begins disciplinary procedures against the affected officials.

INEC National Commissioner, Mohammed Haruna, disclosed this in an exclusive chat with The PUNCH on Monday in Abuja, explaining that the commission had commenced the process of investigating the officials but would not rush to disciplinary decisions without observing due process.

Haruna said the affected personnel had been issued queries and were expected to respond, after which they would be invited for further investigation.

He stressed that the commission was committed to ensuring fairness and allowing the officials to defend themselves before any decision was taken.

“There is a due process. They have to be queried. They’ve been queried. When they respond, they are invited, and the whole matter is investigated. You have to give people a fair hearing. You can’t just take a decision within a year.

“When did this happen? It’s less than two weeks. These disciplinary procedures, they take weeks. You have to query them.

“They have to give you an answer within 72 hours. After that, then you invite them. These persons involved are from the far places. They come; you interview them. So the process is elaborate. We have to follow every step of the way, and you know they are in other states. So across 10 states. So it will take a while for their reply to reach us,” he said.

The national commissioner explained that investigations would begin at the state level through committees to be constituted by the respective Resident Electoral Commissioners before a panel would be established at the commission’s headquarters to review the findings.

He said the geographical spread of the affected personnel across 10 states and the administrative procedures involved meant that the investigation would take time.

“The investigation will start from their own place because, of course, there is a Resident Electoral Commission there. They will set up a committee to look into it, before a panel will be set up in headquarters to look into the matter. So there are steps that we have to take.

“Every step of the way, we have to follow those processes,” Haruna added.

INEC had earlier disclosed that it had identified 54 personnel across 10 states allegedly involved in the manipulation of the voter registration exercise.

On November 9, the INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, while addressing journalists in Abuja on the outcome of the commission’s review of the Preliminary Register of Voters ahead of the 2027 general elections, warned that those found culpable would face administrative disciplinary measures and possible prosecution.

The queries issued to the INEC officials followed public complaints about irregularities in the preliminary register of voters displayed at registration areas between October 9 and 15, 2026.

After the register was published online on October 26, there was an outcry among Nigerians over the inclusion of suspicious profiles, including those suspected to be AI-generated, in the voters’ register.

The complaints included allegations of multiple registrations, unusual names, artificial or manipulated photographs, and deceased persons remaining on the register.

The commission, however, clarified that it had deleted over 1,608,660 confirmed invalid registrations from the preliminary register generated from the 2025/2026 Continuous Voter Registration exercise.

The clean-up comes amid the commission’s efforts to sanitise the voters’ register and prevent irregularities that could undermine the credibility of the 2027 general elections.

The post INEC queries 54 officials over voter registration breaches appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Sani, Abbas rally Zaria religious leaders for Tinubu’s re-election
description:
Kaduna State Governor, Senator Uba Sani, and the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, have urged religious leaders in Zaria to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in the 2027 general elections.
The duo made the appeal during an engagement with Christian and M
content:
Kaduna State Governor, Senator Uba Sani, and the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, have urged religious leaders in Zaria to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in the 2027 general elections.

The duo made the appeal during an engagement with Christian and Muslim leaders in Zaria, where they highlighted the achievements of the Tinubu administration and appealed for prayers and support for the All Progressives Congress.

Sani, who was represented by the Secretary to the State Government, Dr Abdulkadir Meyere, said the meeting was part of efforts to strengthen the relationship between the government and religious institutions.

He said, “We are here to strengthen our partnership with religious institutions and seek your prayers for peaceful elections and successful governance. Religious leaders have important roles to play in promoting peace, unity and development in our society.”

Meyere urged the clerics to sustain their support for the APC-led government at all levels, assuring them that the governor remained committed to delivering on his promises.

He also assured the district heads that the state government would sustain the payment of their additional allowances, while appealing to the religious leaders to continue praying for peaceful elections and the success of the administration.

Abbas, in his remarks, called on residents of Zaria and Kaduna State to support Tinubu’s re-election, saying the President deserved another term because of his contributions to national development.

The Speaker listed several interventions he had facilitated for traditional institutions, including the provision of utility vehicles for traditional rulers and the construction and renovation of district heads’ residences.

He said, “Through my interventions, district heads are now receiving monthly salaries. We have also facilitated the provision of vehicles for traditional rulers and the construction and renovation of their residences.”

Abbas disclosed that more than 7,000 students would benefit from a scholarship programme facilitated by him, while an empowerment programme was scheduled to hold the following week.

He also announced plans for the groundbreaking of an international grains market at Dambo, Zaria, attributing the interventions to the support of the Tinubu administration.

He urged the people to reciprocate the President’s support for the constituency by voting for him in the 2027 elections.

Responding, a leader of the Fityanul Islam, Darika Sufaye group, Malam Rabiu Sufi, commended Sani for maintaining cordial relations with religious organisations.

Sufi said, “We appreciate the governor for the relationship he has maintained with religious organisations. We have forgiven the government wherever it may have made mistakes, and we assure it of our continued support.”

He, however, urged the government to intensify efforts to publicise its achievements at the grassroots, saying many residents needed to be better informed about government policies and programmes.

“We will continue to mobilise our followers and communicate the achievements of the government to our people,” he added.

Similarly, a Kaduna State leader of the Izala group, Sheikh Aliyu Abdullah Telex, assured the government that religious leaders were prepared to pass its messages to their followers.

He pledged continued prayers for the country but urged political leaders to address the challenges confronting Nigerians.

The Secretary of the Christian Association of Nigeria, Zone One, Pastor Titus Yohana, also commended the government for what he described as its inclusive approach to governance.

Yohana said, “We appreciate the government for carrying Christians along in its engagements. We will continue to pray for the success of the administration and urge it to sustain this inclusive approach.”

Meanwhile, the Director-General of the First Aid Group of Jama’atu Izalatil Bid’ah Wa Iqamatis Sunnah, Engr. Imam Sitti, urged religious leaders to promote peaceful coexistence and avoid sentiments capable of dividing their followers.

Sitti advised the clerics to reflect on past mistakes, correct their shortcomings and ensure that their messages strengthened unity and peaceful coexistence.

Another religious leader, Malam Tanimu Mai Rawani, pledged support for Tinubu, citing the interventions Abbas had facilitated for traditional institutions.

He, however, appealed for the release of Sheikh Khalifa, whom he said was in custody.

In a related development, former Kaduna State Governor, Mukhtar Ramalan Yero, has urged APC members to embrace patience and unity, warning against allowing personal interests to undermine the party’s collective success.

Yero said political positions were temporary and called on party stakeholders to support whoever emerged as the party’s candidate at all levels.

“Political positions are temporary. What is important is the success of the party. We must learn to put our personal interests aside and support whoever emerges as our candidate,” he said.

The post Sani, Abbas rally Zaria religious leaders for Tinubu’s re-election appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Army commander tasks newly promoted senior officers on greater responsibilities
description:
The Commander of the Nigerian Army 39 Artillery Brigade, Niger State, Brigadier General Kabir Rabiu, has charged a newly promoted Colonel, Labilwa Madugu, to justify his elevation by demonstrating greater commitment, discipline and professionalism in the discharge of his duties.
Rabiu gave the charg
content:
The Commander of the Nigerian Army 39 Artillery Brigade, Niger State, Brigadier General Kabir Rabiu, has charged a newly promoted Colonel, Labilwa Madugu, to justify his elevation by demonstrating greater commitment, discipline and professionalism in the discharge of his duties.

Rabiu gave the charge during the decoration of Madugu with his new rank of Colonel, following his promotion from Lieutenant Colonel, at the brigade’s conference hall in Niger State.

The commander described promotion in the Nigerian Army as an earned privilege that came with increased responsibilities, warning that the new rank should not be seen merely as an opportunity for celebration.

He said, “Promotion in the Nigerian Army is not given; it is earned. For you to be promoted, you must be found competent, professional, disciplined and worthy of being shouldered with heavier responsibilities.”

Rabiu explained that the promotion was both recognition of Madugu’s contributions to the Army and an opportunity to prepare him for greater responsibilities.

“Promotion comes with dual reasons. One, appreciating you for all the good works and consistent service you have given to Niger State and the country at large, and secondly, to prepare you to shoulder heavier responsibilities,” he said.

Illustrating the demands associated with the rank of Colonel, the brigade commander recalled an experience following his own promotion in 2017.

He said the then Chief of Army Staff, upon seeing him wearing his new rank insignia, made a remark about the weight of responsibilities that came with the elevation.

Rabiu recalled that the senior officer had told him, “What, young man, so you have started wearing red neck? Once you start bleeding from the neck, you know there is a problem.”

He added, “So, I’m telling you, there is a problem now because you are already bleeding from the neck.”

The commander used the anecdote to remind Madugu that his new rank came with expectations and challenges that required greater sacrifice and dedication.

He also acknowledged the contributions of Madugu’s wife and family, saying they had made sacrifices to support his military career.

According to him, the promotion was not only a personal achievement for the celebrant but also a recognition of the sacrifices made by his immediate and extended family.

“This promotion is not just for you, Col Madugu; it is also for Mrs Madugu and all the members of his immediate and extended family. They must have endured his absence, his unavailability and his lack of attention, all of which were given to the service,” Rabiu said.

In his response, Madugu expressed appreciation to the Nigerian Army and his superior officers for recognising his dedication and promoting him to the rank of Colonel.

He pledged to remain committed to the service and continue contributing to the attainment of the Army’s objectives.

The post Army commander tasks newly promoted senior officers on greater responsibilities appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Retirement: BPSR urges FG agencies to prepare workers early
description:
The Bureau of Public Service Reforms has urged federal government agencies to institutionalise pre-retirement training programmes to prepare workers for life after service and ensure they retire with dignity, financial security and peace of mind.
The Director-General of BPSR, Dr Dasuki Arabi, made t
content:
The Bureau of Public Service Reforms has urged federal government agencies to institutionalise pre-retirement training programmes to prepare workers for life after service and ensure they retire with dignity, financial security and peace of mind.

The Director-General of BPSR, Dr Dasuki Arabi, made the call at the opening of the 2026 Pre-Retirement Training Programme for Retiring Officers of Federal Parastatals.

Arewa PUNCH reports that the five-day programme is designed to equip retiring public servants with the knowledge and practical skills required to navigate life after active service.

Arabi said retirement preparation should be an integral part of responsible human resource management rather than an intervention introduced only when workers were about to leave service.

He described retirement as a transition to a new phase of life, stressing that it should not be seen as the end of an individual’s relevance or productivity.

“Retirement is a natural stage in every career, but it should not be regarded as the end of relevance or productivity. It is the beginning of a new phase, offering opportunities for personal development, family engagement, entrepreneurship, mentorship and other meaningful pursuits,” he said.

The BPSR boss noted that the knowledge, experience, discipline and institutional memory acquired by public servants during their years of service remained valuable assets that could benefit society after retirement.

He said the Federal Government’s commitment to public service reforms and workers’ welfare should extend beyond active employment to adequate preparation for retirement.

“A responsive public service should support its workforce at every stage of the employment cycle, including retirement. Accordingly, BPSR regards the preparation of retiring officers as an important component of public service reform,” he added.

According to him, the training will address critical issues, including personal financial planning, savings, investment decisions, wealth preservation, entrepreneurship, alternative sources of income, healthcare and psychological adjustment.

Other areas include pension administration, retirement documentation, verification processes, entitlements and procedures for resolving pension-related challenges.

Arabi stressed that successful retirement required more than the payment of gratuity and pension, noting that workers needed adequate preparation, informed financial decisions and responsible management of available resources.

“Do not regard the training as a mere formality; see it as an investment in your future. Use the opportunity to develop a realistic retirement plan that reflects your aspirations, financial circumstances, family responsibilities and long-term interests,” he advised participants.

He also urged participating federal parastatals to maintain accurate personnel and pension records, process retirement documents promptly and provide necessary administrative support to outgoing employees.

Such measures, he said, would improve retirees’ welfare, strengthen institutional credibility and boost public confidence in government institutions.

“A public servant who has served the nation faithfully deserves to retire with dignity and peace of mind. This requires accurate information, efficient pension administration, appropriate guidance and responsive institutional support,” he stated.

The BPSR director-general acknowledged the importance of collaboration with relevant institutions, particularly the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation and federal parastatals, in ensuring that retiring officers received adequate information and support.

He further described retired public servants as important contributors to national development, saying their professional expertise and institutional experience could be deployed through mentorship, consultancy, community development and other productive engagements.

“Retirement is therefore not a withdrawal from life, but an opportunity to redefine purpose, explore new possibilities and enjoy the rewards of dedicated service,” he said.

He urged participants to actively engage facilitators, ask questions and share experiences throughout the five-day programme to maximise its benefits.

Arabi subsequently declared the 2026 Pre-Retirement Training Programme open, appreciating the collaborating institutions, participating parastatals and facilitators for their support.

The post Retirement: BPSR urges FG agencies to prepare workers early appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Kebbi trains health workers to cater for displaced communities
description:
The Kebbi State Government has trained healthcare workers to provide essential medical services to communities displaced by insecurity across the state, in collaboration with the United Nations Children’s Fund.
The two-day capacity-building exercise, held between November 19 and 20, 2026, was organi
content:
The Kebbi State Government has trained healthcare workers to provide essential medical services to communities displaced by insecurity across the state, in collaboration with the United Nations Children’s Fund.

The two-day capacity-building exercise, held between November 19 and 20, 2026, was organised for members of the Integrated Mobile Health Brigade Teams and local government and state health officials from six local government areas benefiting from an intervention supported by the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency.

Speaking during the training, the State Director of Public Health, Alhaji Usman Magaji, commended UNICEF and SIDA for their continued support towards strengthening healthcare delivery and addressing the needs of vulnerable populations.

He urged the participants to demonstrate commitment, dedication and selflessness in delivering healthcare services to displaced communities, particularly those affected by insecurity.

“I urge you to take this training seriously and demonstrate commitment, dedication and selflessness in discharging your responsibilities,” Magaji said.

He explained that the mobile health teams would provide basic treatment for minor illnesses, routine immunisation, health education and other essential healthcare services to displaced persons.

Magaji said the intervention was aimed at ensuring that people forced to flee their homes because of insecurity were not deprived of access to basic medical care.

“The essence of this intervention is to ensure that people displaced by insecurity are not denied access to essential healthcare services because of their circumstances,” he said.

He identified the benefiting local government areas as Zuru, Danko-Wasagu, Sakaba, Arewa, Aliero and Jega.

The public health director charged the participants to apply the knowledge acquired during the training to improve service delivery and ensure that displaced persons received timely and quality medical attention.

The intervention is expected to improve access to healthcare and reduce preventable illnesses and deaths among displaced populations, particularly women, children and other vulnerable groups.

The training is part of efforts by the Kebbi State Government and its development partners to strengthen healthcare services in communities affected by insecurity.

The post Kebbi trains health workers to cater for displaced communities appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
