title: Developers urged to prioritise SMEs in AI deployment
description:
Developers have been urged to deploy artificial intelligence to boost small and medium-sized enterprises rather than focusing only on big businesses and government.
Special Assistant on Communication to the Governor of Oyo State, Mr Dayo Ogunbowale, made the call while delivering the keynote address
content:
Developers have been urged to deploy artificial intelligence to boost small and medium-sized enterprises rather than focusing only on big businesses and government.

Special Assistant on Communication to the Governor of Oyo State, Mr Dayo Ogunbowale, made the call while delivering the keynote address on the theme ‘Building the Future: How AI and Digital Innovation Can Transform Governance and Society’ at the seventh annual Google Developer Groups event in Ibadan, the Oyo State capital.

Organised by the Ibadan Google Developer Groups, in collaboration with Kakanfo Inn and Conference Centre, the programme took place at the facility in Ibadan at the weekend, attracting about 3,000 young people from across Nigeria and beyond.

Addressing the theme, Ogunbowale identified small and medium-sized enterprises as the bedrock of Oyo State’s economy, stressing that digital transformation would remain incomplete if SMEs were excluded from the benefits of technological advancement.

“Small and Medium Enterprise are the backbone of Oyo State’s economy. If AI serves only big business and government while SMEs are left on the far side of the digital divide, then our “digital transformation” is a half-finised product,” he said.

Ogunbowale stated that this year’s DevFest theme, ‘Building Safe, Secure, and Scalable Solutions with AI and Cloud’ aptly captured the technical pulse of the moment with precision. He noted that Nigeria must move from being a consumer to a creator of technology, saying, “We must become creators of intelligence rooted in our reality and responsive to our aspirations.”

“If we rely only on foreign AI models, they will not understand our nuances, our culture, and our people. We need an AI that understands the meaning of ‘akwa,’ ‘ekaabo,’ ‘sannu’ and not just translates them,” he added.

In his remarks, the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Kakanfo Inn and Conference Centre, Mr Adedamola Are, expressed delight at being a co-host of DevFEST 2026: “We were very pleased to host the 2026 edition of DevFEST on 21 November 2026 here at Kakanfo Inn & Conference Centre.”

Their emphasis was on AI/ML and agentic AI, Google Cloud, Flutter, Web3, distributed systems, product design, data privacy, and tech community/mental health discussions.

According to Are, the primary goal of DevFest is to educate developers, builders, and tech enthusiasts on Google’s latest technologies while fostering community-driven learning and local networking.

Speaking with newsmen on the sidelines of the event, Developer Ecosystem Programme Manager, Google, Sodiq Akinjobi, disclosed that developers, engineers, programme managers and product managers are currently building for Nigeria’s markets.

“They are building their apps in Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo, not just in English, so that they can cover everyone. So the information, the instruction and technology can reach everyone whether you are learned or not. And with user research, it is now getting easier to apply these technologies in your day to day activities,” he said.

Akinjobi commended the government for implementing initiatives right from secondary schools, aimed at utilising new technologies and taking advantage of AI opportunities.

“And if you walk into the conference hall, you will see many participants are within 22 and 25 age bracket. And you will also see that everybody here is young and upwardly mobile. And I believe they are taking the acquired skills back to their younger ones, so we are getting youths on the map.There are lots of emerging innovations. I have just spoken to a lady who is building in robotics, and she is already building prototypes in robotics for healthcare,” he added.

Responding to questions from journalists at the event, the Lead Organiser of GDG Ibadan, software engineer and founder of Abit Technologies Hub Limited, Abidemi Tiamiyu, said the team volunteers with Google Developer Group Ibadan, which organises DevFEST Ibadan, to equip young people with the skills needed to remain relevant in an increasingly technology-driven world.

“We are volunteering for Google Developer Groups Ibadan, the organiser of DevFEST Ibadan. We are driven by the inspiration to impact our community with the technical know-how, mentorship and to show them the pathway to success,” he said.

He added, “Many of the participants are already showing interest in how to use AI to drive products and services. So, I believe that taking that away from here is 100 per cent valuable for anyone.”

According to Abidemi, speakers at this year’s event came from Accra, Ghana; Lagos; Ado-Ekiti; and other parts of the world. “We have speakers that came from Accra Ghana, Lagos, Ado-Ekiti, and other parts of the world,” he said, adding that DevFEST has a presence in Accra, Nairobi, Lagos, Ibadan and Ogbomoso.

He asserted that training programmes provided by DevFEST for over a decade have immensely aided several youths with valuable skills to earn a living, saying that DevFEST recorded 2,500 participants in 2025 and about 3,000 participants in attendance at the 2026 DevFEST.

“In 2025, we recorded 2,500 participants. But as I speak with you, I believe we already have about 3,000 participants right in the hall because the crowd is far larger than what we had in 2025. That’s what we have been doing to groom young people in the past 10 years and many have benefited from it.”

The Co-Lead Organiser of GDG Ibadan and software engineer at Resilience17, Joshua Odejide, underscored DevFEST’s impact on young people, noting that the programme had equipped many participants with website development capabilities and other digital skills to become self-reliant.

He said, “One of the major takeaways from this programme is that everybody will actually become a builder. Before now, if you want to build a website, you will have to go to someone who would do it for charges. But if the charges are too much, one might drop the idea. But DevFEST equips you with skills to build it a website yourself.”

Highlighting the numerous benefits of artificial intelligence, Odejide noted that tasks such as designing graphic flyers could now be completed within seconds using AI tools. He stressed the need for professionals across various fields to adapt to emerging technologies and keep pace with rapid innovations.

The event featured panellists, including the Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of Zeeh Africa, David Adeleke; Investor and Community Builder, Michael Toyinbo; Director of Expansion, Strategy and Operations at Chowdeck; Founder of Prine, Gbolahan Alli; and Developer Relations Lead at ALATPay, Haastrup Adegoke, among other dignitaries.

The post Developers urged to prioritise SMEs in AI deployment appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Nigeria’s growing population offers businesses market opportunities – KukuBima
description:
The Country Manager of KukuBima Energy Drink, Mr John Abah, has said that Nigeria’s growing population offers an advantage to businesses in the country.
Abah disclosed this over the weekend in Lagos while speaking during a gala night organised by KukuBima Energy Drink to celebrate its distributors a
content:
The Country Manager of KukuBima Energy Drink, Mr John Abah, has said that Nigeria’s growing population offers an advantage to businesses in the country.

Abah disclosed this over the weekend in Lagos while speaking during a gala night organised by KukuBima Energy Drink to celebrate its distributors and customers in Nigeria.

The gathering brought together representatives of Sido Muncul, Muncul Nigeria, its Nigerian distributor, and the Indonesia Trade Promotion Center in Lagos, reflecting their shared commitment to strengthening business partnerships and supporting KukuBima’s continued growth in Nigeria.

Abah said that Nigeria has a very large population of young people who can buy into its products at a very affordable price.

“I want to dwell more on the potential in Nigeria. The population of Nigeria is growing and despite the challenges, the market opportunity is also there. So we are looking more at the opportunities and less on our challenges. I wouldn’t say we do not face challenges, but we are looking at possible solutions and opportunities in the Nigerian market. We have a very large population of youngpeople. We think we can buy into it and our product is very affordable,” Abah said.

While highlighting that the energy drink market in Nigeria was big, Abah reiterated that, given the large population of young people in the country, there was potential for the sector.

“As we speak, the population of Nigeria is over 200 million. And in the future, I think by the year 2050, it is projected that the population of Nigeria will be 350 million. This being said, the opportunity for our product would keep growing,” he said.

Speaking on the company’s plans for the coming year, he announced that the company was expecting products that would address environmental challenges.

“Like we all know, we have global warming and there would be that taste, that dryness in your throat. So we are bringing products that will address some of the environmental challenges with regards to that. Also, we are bringing in a ready-to-drink energy drink in cans and bottles as well,” Abah said.

title: TikTok deploys AI tools to curb election misinformation
description: TikTok is deploying artificial intelligence tools, specialist moderation teams and independent fact-checking partnerships to monitor election-related content in Nigeria ahead of the 2027 general elections, as the social media platform steps up efforts to address misinformation and coordinated attemp
content:
TikTok is deploying artificial intelligence tools, specialist moderation teams and independent fact-checking partnerships to monitor election-related content in Nigeria ahead of the 2027 general elections, as the social media platform steps up efforts to address misinformation and coordinated attempts to manipulate public debate.

The measures include an election task force comprising specialists in platform integrity, cybersecurity, deceptive behaviour, misinformation and election integrity, supported by automated moderation systems and local language moderators.

The platform disclosed that its preparations also include collaborations with the Independent National Electoral Commission, the Nigeria Union of Journalists and fact-checking organisations such as Code for Africa and DUBAWA to enhance access to credible electoral information and strengthen the verification of content shared online.

TikTok revealed this in a statement to The PUNCH detailing its election integrity framework for Nigeria, noting that the measures draw on its experience in managing platform-related risks during more than 300 elections worldwide.

The Global Integrity Programmes Lead at TikTok, Lorenzo Andreozzi, said the company was working with electoral authorities, independent fact-checkers, and civil society organisations to address information challenges during the election period.

“As important civic events such as Nigeria’s elections unfold, upholding platform integrity is at the heart of our mission. We recognise that no platform can tackle modern information challenges alone; that is why we actively deepen our partnerships with independent fact-checkers, the Independent National Electoral Commission, and civil society experts such as DUBAWA, ensuring that we lean into local context and understanding of the realities on the ground,” he said.

As part of the initiative, TikTok has introduced an in-app Election Centre in partnership with INEC and DUBAWA, providing users with information on voting procedures, important electoral dates and other details about the election process.

The centre also connects users to an artificial intelligence media literacy hub designed to help them identify AI-generated content, understand responsible AI use, and recognise the platform’s measures for promoting transparency around synthetic media.

The Director of Voter Education and Publicity at INEC, Victoria-Eta Messie, said access to credible electoral information was important for improving voter awareness and understanding of the electoral process.

She said the initiative could help counter misinformation and disinformation, particularly among young people, who constitute a significant segment of the voting population.

TikTok is also working with the NUJ and Code for Africa to train more than 300 media professionals across Lagos, Abuja, Ogun and Oyo states on digital platforms, information verification and responsible online journalism.

The Vice Chairman of the NUJ Lagos State Council, Philip Nwosu, said the training would strengthen journalists’ capacity to provide accurate and credible election coverage.

The platform said it removes content that violates its election misinformation policies, including false claims about voting procedures and accounts impersonating politicians or news organisations.

Where election-related claims cannot immediately be verified, TikTok said it could attach labels identifying the information as unverified, warn users before they share it, and restrict its recommendation on the For You feed.

It also works with more than 20 International Fact-Checking Network-accredited organisations globally, while Code for Africa supports its fact-checking efforts in Nigeria. The organisations assess claims circulating on the platform and provide feedback to inform content moderation decisions.

Between April and June 2026, TikTok said it removed more than 210,000 videos for violating its policies on civic and election integrity, misinformation and harmful misleading AI-generated content. More than 99 per cent of the content was removed before users reported it.

In Nigeria, the platform removed more than four million videos for violating its community guidelines during the second quarter of 2026. It said 98 per cent of the videos were taken down before they were reported, while 91.7 per cent were removed within 24 hours.

The company is also strengthening safeguards around AI-generated content, requiring creators to label such material and deploying tools including Content Credentials, developed under the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity standard, and invisible watermarking technology.

TikTok said more than five billion videos had been labelled through its AI-generated content tools and technologies since the introduction of the labelling feature.

Political advertising is also prohibited on the platform, including paid promotions by creators for politicians and political parties. Accounts belonging to political figures and parties are restricted from advertising and accessing monetisation features, while government and political accounts are subject to additional security requirements, including mandatory two-step verification.

Official election management bodies are, however, permitted to advertise essential voter information, such as voter registration guidance, polling details and participation requirements.

TikTok said it would continue investing in platform security, content moderation and partnerships with local institutions to address emerging threats and provide users with access to reliable information during Nigeria’s electoral process.

The post TikTok deploys AI tools to curb election misinformation appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

The organisation w
content:
The Women in Leadership Advancement Network is using a national television platform to bring women seeking elective offices ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 general elections before voters, with discussions expected to cover leadership priorities and issues affecting the country’s economy.

The organisation will host a live edition of ‘The Leading Woman Show, titled Women on the Ballot’, on 25 November, featuring female candidates from Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones.

The two-hour programme will hold in Lagos, and will be broadcast on Channels Television, the Nigerian Television Authority, African Independent Television and News Central Television. It will also stream on WILAN Global’s YouTube platform.

The programme comes as economic policy issues, including access to finance, employment, business ownership and investment, remain important considerations for Nigerians ahead of the next general elections.

Women seeking subnational offices will feature in the first half of the programme, while the second half will focus on six women contesting federal elective positions. Each candidate will participate in an individual moderated interview covering her political experience, reasons for seeking office, community priorities and plans for public leadership.

For businesses and investors, the policy direction of candidates seeking public office is relevant because decisions on taxation, infrastructure, access to credit, education and employment can influence the operating environment for companies and entrepreneurs.

Founder and Executive Director of WILAN, Abosede George-Ogan, said the programme would give voters an opportunity to assess candidates beyond their political affiliations and campaign materials.

She said the platform would allow women contesting elections to present their ideas, priorities and vision directly to citizens.

WILAN said its broader work focuses on improving women’s access to leadership opportunities through advocacy, research, leadership programmes and media engagement.

Established in 2018, the nonprofit organisation operates ‘The Leading Woman Show’ as its flagship media platform. The programme has completed four seasons featuring discussions on leadership, governance, representation and women’s participation in shaping Nigeria’s future.

The post WILAN puts women candidates’ economic agenda in focus appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: MTN, Audiomack deepen partnership with festive music campaign
description:
MTN Nigeria and global music streaming platform Audiomack are extending their partnership with a festive campaign offering subscribers backstage access to performances by Nigerian artistes Victony and Seyi Vibez in Lagos.
The initiative will give six Audiomack+ subscribers the opportunity to win bac
content:
MTN Nigeria and global music streaming platform Audiomack are extending their partnership with a festive campaign offering subscribers backstage access to performances by Nigerian artistes Victony and Seyi Vibez in Lagos.

The initiative will give six Audiomack+ subscribers the opportunity to win backstage passes to two December concerts, with three passes available for each show, the streaming giant said in a release.

The selected subscribers will attend Victony’s The Bonfire Experience on 26 December and Seyi Vibez’s SWAGUU Live in Concert at Tafawa Balewa Square on 29 December.

The winners will have the opportunity to meet the artistes, watch performances from the side of the stage and receive merchandise, according to a statement by Audiomack.

The campaign, which runs from 20 November to 2 January, requires participants to maintain an active Audiomack+ subscription during the promotional period, stream the official Bonfire x SWAGUU playlist on the platform and share a video of themselves enjoying the music.

The company said subscribers could participate through any of its plans, including the N100 daily pass and N900 monthly subscription. Winners will be announced weekly on Audiomack’s Instagram and X accounts and contacted directly.

The latest initiative follows a similar activation at Felabration in October, where Audiomack+ members received VIP seating, as the streaming platform expands the benefits attached to its paid subscription service.

The partnership also builds on the companies’ airtime payment arrangement, introduced in 2024, which allows MTN subscribers to pay for Audiomack+ through their airtime balances, either within the Audiomack application or by sending an SMS to 3134.

The arrangement provides an alternative to debit card payments, allowing subscribers with an MTN line and sufficient airtime to access the platform’s premium service.

Speaking on the campaign, the Vice-President of Marketing for Africa, Europe, the Middle East and North Africa at Audiomack, Charlotte Bwana, said the company wanted subscribers to enjoy benefits beyond music streaming.

“December is when Nigerians spend the most on music: tickets, data, airtime, everything. We want Audiomack+ members to feel their subscription takes them somewhere real, and there is no better place than backstage with Victony and Seyi Vibez, two artists our listeners play on repeat,” she said.

Bwana added that the airtime payment option was intended to make the subscription accessible to more Nigerians who might not have debit cards.

Beyond concert-related benefits, Audiomack+ offers an ad-free listening experience and offline downloads, allowing subscribers to listen to music without an active internet connection.

Nigeria remains Audiomack’s largest single market, with 15.3 million monthly users, according to the company, which said it planned to introduce more benefits for subscribers during the festive season.

The post MTN, Audiomack deepen partnership with festive music campaign appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: ‘CBN data rule requires local cloud infrastructure’
description:
Nigerian banks, fintech companies and payment service providers will need reliable domestic cloud infrastructure to meet the Central Bank of Nigeria’s data localisation requirements, the Managing Director of CloudVantage Limited, Muhideen Ashiru, has said.
The warning comes as CloudVantage establish
content:
Nigerian banks, fintech companies and payment service providers will need reliable domestic cloud infrastructure to meet the Central Bank of Nigeria’s data localisation requirements, the Managing Director of CloudVantage Limited, Muhideen Ashiru, has said.

The warning comes as CloudVantage establishes cloud availability regions in Lagos and Abuja, providing local computing, storage and networking infrastructure for Nigerian businesses seeking to host critical workloads within the country and reduce their reliance on foreign cloud services.

Ashiru said in a news release on Monday that requiring financial institutions to keep payment transaction data within Nigeria without sufficient domestic technology infrastructure could create significant operational challenges for businesses preparing to comply with the new requirements.

His comments come ahead of the CBN’s 1 January 2027 compliance deadline, which requires financial institutions and payment service providers to ensure that payment transaction data generated within Nigeria is stored and managed locally.

The development is drawing attention to the capacity of Nigeria’s domestic digital infrastructure to support financial institutions as they review their existing hosting arrangements and consider alternatives to international cloud providers.

Speaking at the Nigeria Cloud Independence Day Summit, a virtual event organised by CloudVantage under the theme ‘Securing Nigeria’s Data, Enabling Innovation and Building a Resilient Digital Economy’, Ashiru said local infrastructure needed to deliver practical business benefits alongside regulatory compliance.

“The CBN’s new rule is a major step towards taking control of Nigeria’s digital future. But requiring businesses to keep data local without providing reliable domestic technology would create significant challenges,” he said.

“Through our partnership with Rack Centre, CloudVantage is building a local cloud platform that helps businesses strengthen data control, improve resilience and manage their infrastructure costs. We want local cloud adoption to be a smart business decision, not just a compliance exercise.”

The Lagos region was initially announced at the summit, which brought together technology leaders, risk managers and industry stakeholders to discuss data sovereignty, infrastructure readiness and the future of Nigeria’s digital economy. The company has now established availability regions in both Lagos and Abuja.

However, moving workloads from international cloud providers to domestic infrastructure could present technical challenges for businesses, particularly those operating complex databases, legacy applications, interconnected systems and sensitive transaction records.

Such migrations require organisations to protect data integrity and maintain service availability while transferring critical workloads. Ashiru said regulatory compliance involved more than securing physical space in a domestic data centre, noting that businesses also needed to address data protection during migration, system configuration, backup and recovery.

“True regulatory compliance goes beyond securing physical rack space in a data centre. Businesses must also consider data protection during migration, system configuration, backup and recovery. Our automation tools help organisations manage these operational requirements while their teams focus on their core business,” he said.

CloudVantage said its platform combines cloud automation, workload management, data replication and backup capabilities to simplify migration and ongoing infrastructure management. The services are designed to reduce manual intervention, support recovery planning and help organisations maintain business continuity.

Both availability regions are backed by a 99.99 per cent availability service-level agreement, according to the company.

Beyond regulatory compliance, the shift towards local cloud hosting could give businesses an opportunity to review their technology expenditure, particularly where international cloud contracts expose them to foreign exchange fluctuations.

CloudVantage said its pricing was tailored to the markets in which its customers operate, with naira payment options intended to reduce exposure to foreign currency-denominated cloud charges.

Depending on their workloads and existing contracts, businesses could also reduce cross-border data transfers and improve response times for local users by hosting infrastructure closer to their customers.

The company said its infrastructure was supported by security and business continuity standards, including ISO 27001, ISO 22301 and PCI DSS compliance credentials.

Speaking at the summit, Kelechukwu Nsofor, Head of Business Development at Digital Realty, encouraged Nigerian organisations using international hyperscale cloud providers to explore domestic alternatives and communicate their infrastructure challenges to local providers.

“This is the perfect opportunity for organisations using foreign hyperscalers to look inward and share their pain points with Nigerian providers like CloudVantage,” Nsofor said.

He also highlighted the importance of developing clear migration plans as organisations prepare for the CBN’s data localisation requirements.

CloudVantage said its Lagos and Abuja regions would give banks, fintech companies, payment service providers and other businesses additional options for hosting and managing critical workloads locally while maintaining control over where their data is stored.

The company added that its services were designed to support secure operations, simplify migration and strengthen infrastructure resilience through automation-backed management and technical support.

The post ‘CBN data rule requires local cloud infrastructure’ appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Tech firms dominate list of companies creating billionaires
description:
Technology organisations are emerging as major engines of billionaire wealth, from the artificial intelligence firms reshaping the industry to social media platforms and software businesses whose founders and early employees have built fortunes through company ownership.
A study by trading firm Atmo
content:
Technology organisations are emerging as major engines of billionaire wealth, from the artificial intelligence firms reshaping the industry to social media platforms and software businesses whose founders and early employees have built fortunes through company ownership.

A study by trading firm Atmos found that seven of the 12 companies with at least five billionaire founders and employees were technology or technology-related businesses. The list was led by Anthropic, the Claude AI maker, which had seven billionaires, all co-founders, with a combined estimated fortune of $95.4bn.

The findings created a picture of how wealth is being created in businesses whose valuations can rise significantly as their products attract users, customers and investment. The report also drew attention to the role of company ownership in building fortunes, as founders and early employees benefit from shares and stock options when businesses expand.

The ranking suggests that technology’s contribution to billionaire wealth extends beyond the founders of household-name platforms. It includes employees who joined businesses, acquired equity and benefited as those companies grew. In the case of Meta, for example, three of the six billionaires identified by the study were employees rather than founders. At Alphabet, the parent company of Google, three of the five were also non-founders.

The distinction matters because it shows that the wealth generated by a successful technology company can spread beyond the people who started it. Employees who receive shares or stock options can build substantial fortunes if the company’s value rises, although the size of those gains depends on the equity they hold and the terms attached to it.

Anthropic illustrates the founder-led side of the trend. Established in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers, the artificial intelligence company develops Claude, a family of AI models and products. Its seven billionaire founders had an estimated combined fortune of $95.4bn, according to the Atmos study.

“Billionaires are rarely made with paychecks. Anthropic’s CEO earned about $18M in total pay in 2025, and only $654K of that was salary,” Nick Cooke, CEO of Atmos, commented on the study.

Meta, Facebook’s parent company, provides another example of how wealth can extend to employees. Founded in 2004 by Mark Zuckerberg and his co-founders, the US social media company has since expanded through acquisitions and the development of platforms, including Instagram and WhatsApp. The study identified six billionaires linked to the company, with a combined estimated fortune of $262.9bn. Three were founders, while the other three were former employees, including former Chief Operating Officer Sheryl Sandberg and former President Sean Parker.

Alphabet, the parent company of Google, had five billionaires with a combined estimated fortune of $553bn, the largest total among the businesses in the ranking. They included Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin, as well as former Chief Executive Officer Eric Schmidt, Alphabet Chief Executive Sundar Pichai and former Google executive Marissa Mayer.

Google was founded in 1998 by Page and Brin as an internet search engine before expanding into advertising, mobile operating systems, cloud computing, video and other digital services. Alphabet was established in 2015 as its parent holding company. The fortunes attributed to the group demonstrate how the growth of a technology business can create substantial wealth for founders and senior employees over time.

Chinese smartphone maker Xiaomi had five billionaires, all founders, with a combined fortune of $36bn. Its chairman and chief executive, Lei Jun, accounted for an estimated $20.9bn.

Contemporary Amperex Technology Company Limited, known as CATL, also had five billionaires, with a combined estimated wealth of $63bn. The Chinese company, established in 2011, manufactures batteries for electric vehicles and energy storage systems, placing it at the intersection of technology and the global transition towards electric mobility.

India’s Infosys, an information technology services and consulting company, had five billionaire founders with a combined estimated fortune of $13.3bn. Founded in 1981, the company is the only Indian business among the 12 firms highlighted in the study.

Snowflake, an American cloud data platform company, also had five billionaires, comprising two founders and three other employees. Their combined estimated fortune was $11.3bn. The company’s inclusion points to the wealth created not only by consumer-facing technology brands but also by businesses providing the data infrastructure used by other organisations.

Beyond technology founders

Although technology companies accounted for seven of the 12 businesses, the study found that other sectors have also produced billionaires through company ownership and employment.

Alfa Group, a Russian banking and investment group, had six billionaires, split equally between founders and other employees, with a combined estimated fortune of $44.4bn. Glencore, the Switzerland-based commodities trading and mining company, also had six, all of whom were employees rather than founders. Their combined wealth was estimated at $29bn.

Private equity firms Thoma Bravo and EQT each had five billionaires, while Chinese food manufacturer Foshan Haitian Flavouring and Food also recorded five. The figures show that the accumulation of substantial wealth through company ownership is not exclusive to technology, even if technology businesses feature prominently in the ranking.

Value of equity

The study’s central argument is that company ownership, rather than salary alone, is a major route through which founders and employees build billionaire fortunes.

“Many founders and early employees accept lower pay in the early years in exchange for stock or options, then wait. Even after a company lists, a 180-day lockup usually keeps insiders from selling right away, so most of the wealth stays on paper for a while longer,” Cooke added.

The explanation is particularly relevant to technology businesses, where founders and early employees may receive equity as part of their compensation. As a company attracts investment, expands its operations or lists on a stock exchange, the value of those holdings can increase. However, the wealth represented by shares is not necessarily cash available to the individuals, particularly where shares are subject to restrictions on sale.

The methodology also sets boundaries on what the ranking measures. Atmos examined nearly 100 companies and identified self-made billionaires on Forbes’ real-time list whose wealth was primarily linked to a company they founded or worked for. It excluded investors, board members and heirs, and counted each individual against only one company. The 12 businesses highlighted had at least five qualifying billionaires, although the wider study included companies with at least three.

The combined fortunes are estimates of the individuals’ net worth, not the market value of the companies or the value of their holdings alone. They are also tied to the date on which the estimates were compiled and may change as share prices and private-company valuations move.

The post Tech firms dominate list of companies creating billionaires appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Multi-Trex posts N1.03bn pre-tax loss despite revenue surge
description:
Multi-Trex Integrated Foods Plc recorded a 79 per cent rise in pre-tax loss to N1.03bn for the financial year ended 30 April 2026, compared with a restated N577.97m in 2025, as higher direct cocoa trading costs and administrative expenses offset a significant recovery in turnover.
According to the c
content:
Multi-Trex Integrated Foods Plc recorded a 79 per cent rise in pre-tax loss to N1.03bn for the financial year ended 30 April 2026, compared with a restated N577.97m in 2025, as higher direct cocoa trading costs and administrative expenses offset a significant recovery in turnover.

According to the company’s audited financial statements filed on the Nigerian Exchange and audited by Baker Tilly Nigeria, revenue surged 6,392 per cent year-on-year to N3.11bn from N47.90m in the corresponding period of 2025.

In the report, the directors noted that while the firm’s principal activities span cocoa bean trading, industrial cocoa processing and consumer product manufacturing, only cocoa bean trading took place during the year under review, with all N3.11bn generated from export sales compared with N9.48m in export revenue and N38.42m in local sales in 2025.

However, the top-line expansion was largely offset by cost of sales, which jumped from N6.82m in 2025 to N3.10bn in 2026 due to N3.09bn spent on direct materials. As a result, gross profit declined 79.1 per cent to N8.58m from N41.08m a year earlier.

Other operating income also fell 48.4 per cent to N198.13m from N384.31m in 2025, reflecting the absence of the N281.35m unrealised foreign exchange gain recorded in the prior year, even as scrap sales proceeds rose to N195.38m from N100.64m.

Administrative expenses climbed 28.3 per cent to N1.17bn from N911.36m in the preceding year, driven largely by N734.01m in depreciation and amortisation charges on idle productive assets, N90.25m in realised foreign exchange losses, N88.37m in staff costs and N60.34m in repairs and maintenance. Consequently, the company’s operating loss widened 98.2 per cent to N962.96m from N485.96m in 2025.

Although interest expenses on borrowings declined  23.3 per cent to N70.60m from N92.01m, pre-tax loss deepened to N1.03bn. Following a deferred tax credit of N136.50m, loss after taxation rose by 55 per cent to N897.06m from N578.62m in 2025, pushing basic and diluted loss per share to 14 kobo from nine kobo.

Given the accumulated losses sustained over the years, the Board of Directors did not recommend a dividend for the 2026 financial year.

On the balance sheet, total assets contracted 4.5 per cent to N13.79bn as of 30 April 2026, compared with N14.44bn in 2025.

While property, plant and equipment increased 15 per cent to N13.20bn from N11.48bn following N3.01bn in capital additions aimed at plant refurbishment, current assets plunged 82.9 per cent to N490.18m from N2.87bn as cash and cash equivalents dropped to N297.97m from N2.04bn and trade and other receivables fell to N132.96m from N830.60m.

Total liabilities rose 4.4 per cent to N6.21bn from N5.95bn in 2025, driven by a 33.7 per cent rise in trade and other payables to N1.71bn from N1.28bn, including N760.19m owed to related party N-Foods Universal Concept Limited.

Shareholders’ equity fell 10.7 per cent to N7.58bn from N8.49bn as retained deficit widened to N5.56bn from N4.69bn, leaving the company with a negative working capital of N2.37bn compared with a positive working capital of N411.73m in 2025.

In its disclosures on events after the reporting period, the company revealed that on 10 July 2026, it reached a final settlement with the Nigerian Export-Import Bank over its defaulted 14 per cent term loan facility. Under the agreement, Multi-Trex paid off the outstanding principal of N470.04m in full, while NEXIM Bank granted a full waiver of N595.90m in accumulated interest, discharging the company from all indebtedness under the facility.

The company also disclosed retrospective restatements to its 2025 financial statements in line with International Accounting Standard 8 to correct under-depreciation of property, plant and equipment between 2022 and 2025, alongside reclassifications of deferred building repairs and share issue costs.

Meanwhile, the management maintained that ongoing plant refurbishment and backing from strategic investors position the company to sustain operations and achieve full operational recovery.

The post Multi-Trex posts N1.03bn pre-tax loss despite revenue surge appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: FGN bond yield climbs to 16.57%
description:
Yields on Federal Government of Nigeria bonds rose by nine basis points to 16.57 per cent last week as investors reduced their exposure to government securities following another undersubscribed bond auction by the Debt Management Office.
The increase came despite the DMO offering N2tn in its 16 Nov
content:
Yields on Federal Government of Nigeria bonds rose by nine basis points to 16.57 per cent last week as investors reduced their exposure to government securities following another undersubscribed bond auction by the Debt Management Office.

The increase came despite the DMO offering N2tn in its 16 November bond auction, which attracted subscriptions of N1.81tn. The debt office eventually allotted N1.42tn, representing 71 per cent of the amount offered.

According to investment firm Comercio Limited, the auction marked the fifth consecutive time the DMO fell short of its offer, reflecting investors’ reluctance to commit funds at the prevailing market rates.

Cowry Asset Limited also noted that although investors maintained interest in government securities, aggregate demand remained below the government’s borrowing target.

The auction results showed that demand was concentrated in the 19.89 per cent FGN May 2033 bond, which attracted subscriptions of N766.40bn against an offer of N300bn.

The DMO allotted N676.58bn to the instrument, exceeding its initial offer by 125.5 per cent, with a bid-to-cover ratio of 2.55 times.

The 19.30 per cent FGN April 2029 bond also recorded relatively strong demand, attracting subscriptions of N350.78bn against an offer of N250bn. However, the DMO allotted N241.03bn, representing 96.4 per cent of the amount offered.

Demand was weaker for the 21 per cent FGN March 2028 and 17.945 per cent FGN August 2030 bonds, which attracted subscriptions of N276.98bn and N415.99bn against respective offers of N700bn and N750bn.

The auction outcome indicated investors’ preference for the longer-dated 2033 instrument over shorter and medium-term securities, suggesting differences in appetite across maturities at the prevailing yields.

Meanwhile, trading in the secondary bond market remained bearish, with investors selling existing holdings despite the DMO’s failure to raise its targeted amount.

Market analysts attributed the pressure to profit-taking and portfolio repositioning as investors sought better returns in other fixed-income instruments, particularly Open Market Operations bills and Treasury bills.

Comercio Limited said the naira’s depreciation also contributed to selling pressure, encouraging investors to reduce their bond positions and pushing yields higher across the medium-term segment.

Although buying interest returned towards the end of the week, particularly across short- and medium-dated securities, it was insufficient to reverse the broader bearish sentiment.

The 2031 and 2033 maturities closed the week at bid and offer yields of 17.00/16.80 per cent and 17.15/17.05 per cent, respectively.

The post FGN bond yield climbs to 16.57% appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Cornerstone, Diuto clash over N21m employee death benefit claim
description:
Cornerstone Insurance Plc has urged the Federal High Court in Abuja to dismiss a N21m death benefit claim brought by Diuto Nigeria Limited and another plaintiff, alleging that the documents supporting the claim contained inconsistencies.
The insurer made the submission in its final written address,
content:
Cornerstone Insurance Plc has urged the Federal High Court in Abuja to dismiss a N21m death benefit claim brought by Diuto Nigeria Limited and another plaintiff, alleging that the documents supporting the claim contained inconsistencies.

The insurer made the submission in its final written address, adopted by its counsel, Nkem Egbuta, before Justice R. N. Ofili-Ajumogobia on Monday, 23 November, 2026.

The dispute centres on a Group Life Assurance policy covering Diuto employees between 2 November, 2021, and 1 November, 2022.

Diuto claimed that two employees, Nura Adamu and Muhammad Tasiu, died in a road accident along Keffi Road on 30 March, 2022, while on official duty. It subsequently sought payment of their death benefits under the policy.

However, Cornerstone argued that its investigation uncovered discrepancies in the documents submitted to support the claim, prompting it to challenge the plaintiffs’ case.

In its address, the insurer said an investigation at the Federal Medical Centre, Keffi, found no records showing that either employee had been admitted, treated or deposited at the hospital’s mortuary or Accident and Emergency Unit on the reported date or at any other time.

The insurer also questioned the medical death certificates submitted by the plaintiffs, arguing that the hospital issued them based solely on a police report without physically verifying or treating the deceased.

Cornerstone further alleged that the plaintiffs claimed the employees were buried at Keffi Cemetery but submitted a burial certificate from Gudu Cemetery in Abuja.

It urged the court to dismiss the suit, citing what it described as identity discrepancies, conflicting accounts of the deaths, hearsay evidence and unpleaded claims.

Diuto, however, maintained that the two employees died while the insurance policy was valid and that Cornerstone had been notified of the deaths.

In its final written address, the company argued that it supplied the documents requested by the insurer through the next of kin of the deceased employees but Cornerstone failed to settle the claims despite repeated correspondence and demands.

The plaintiffs also maintained that the accident was reported to the police and that the police report was admitted as evidence during the trial.

They argued that Cornerstone did not dispute the existence of a valid Group Life Assurance policy when the employees died and should therefore pay the benefits to their next of kin.

The plaintiffs asked the court to order the insurer to pay the death benefits, alongside interest and legal costs.

Both parties adopted their final written addresses before the court on Monday, bringing the proceedings to the stage of judgment.

Justice Ofili-Ajumogobia adjourned the matter until 3 December, 2026, for judgment.

Under Section 7.1 of the Revised Guidelines on Group Life Insurance Policy for Employees, issued jointly by the National Insurance Commission and the National Pension Commission, employers are required to notify insurers of employees’ deaths and commence processing death benefit claims.

The post Cornerstone, Diuto clash over N21m employee death benefit claim appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: LeapFrog agrees to sell 30.53% AIICO stake
description:
Cornerstone Plc has announced that Insur Investments Limited, an investment vehicle sponsored by the company, has agreed to acquire 30.53 per cent of the issued share capital of AIICO Insurance Plc from LeapFrog III Nigeria Insurance Holdings Limited.
The proposed transaction involves the acquisitio
content:
Cornerstone Plc has announced that Insur Investments Limited, an investment vehicle sponsored by the company, has agreed to acquire 30.53 per cent of the issued share capital of AIICO Insurance Plc from LeapFrog III Nigeria Insurance Holdings Limited.

The proposed transaction involves the acquisition of 11.17 billion ordinary shares of 50 kobo each in AIICO Insurance, according to a notice filed with the Nigerian Exchange Limited on Monday.

The shares represent 30.53 per cent of AIICO’s issued share capital, making the proposed acquisition a significant ownership transaction in the insurance company.

Cornerstone said completion of the deal remained subject to the fulfillment of agreed conditions and receipt of the necessary regulatory approvals.

The company said it would continue to update the NGX, its shareholders and the investing public on material developments, including the completion of the transaction.

The notice was signed by Cornerstone’s Company Secretary, Aramide Oyeneyin.

The proposed acquisition comes as the ownership structure of AIICO Insurance faces a major change, with Insur Investments seeking to take over the stake currently held by LeapFrog III Nigeria Insurance Holdings Limited.

However, the transaction has not been completed, and its outcome will depend on the satisfaction of the outstanding conditions and regulatory approvals.

title: Foreign investors increase appetite for Nigerian Eurobonds as yields fall
description:
Foreign investors increased their exposure to Nigerian dollar-denominated bonds amid renewed buying interest in emerging and African debt markets, pushing the average yield on the country’s Eurobonds down by 18 basis points to 7.07 per cent.
The decline reflected broad-based price gains across Niger
content:
Foreign investors increased their exposure to Nigerian dollar-denominated bonds amid renewed buying interest in emerging and African debt markets, pushing the average yield on the country’s Eurobonds down by 18 basis points to 7.07 per cent.

The decline reflected broad-based price gains across Nigeria’s external debt securities, with investors showing particular interest in bonds maturing in February 2028, February 2030 and September 2033.

Trading activities in the international debt market were largely positive last week, as investors increased their positions in African sovereign bonds amid changing global market conditions.

Nigeria attracted renewed attention as the Federal Government sought parliamentary approval for plans to raise more than $20bn from external markets.

Other African sovereign issuers also recorded improved investor demand, with Angola’s dollar-denominated bonds attracting buying interest, while yields on Ghanaian and Egyptian Eurobonds also moderated.

Market sentiment was supported by expectations of easing inflationary pressures and further monetary policy adjustments, which improved foreign asset managers’ appetite for emerging-market debt.

However, developments in the United States continued to influence global fixed-income markets, as investors assessed stronger-than-expected employment data and its implications for the Federal Reserve’s interest rate decisions.

US Treasury yields rose on Friday following the release of October employment figures, strengthening expectations that the Federal Reserve could maintain a tighter monetary policy stance.

The benchmark 10-year Treasury note yield increased by more than two basis points to 4.864 per cent, while the 30-year bond yield climbed by more than one basis point to 5.263 per cent.

Similarly, the two-year Treasury yield advanced by more than four basis points to 4.522 per cent.

The contrasting movements in Nigerian Eurobond and US Treasury yields highlight the influence of changing global risk appetite and country-specific demand on sovereign borrowing costs.

For Nigeria, stronger foreign demand could support Eurobond prices, ease external borrowing costs and improve the government’s access to international debt markets.

The post Foreign investors increase appetite for Nigerian Eurobonds as yields fall appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Police deploy across Ibadan as NURTW threatens park takeover
description:
Men of the Nigeria Police Force and the Nigerian Army on Monday embarked on patrols across parts of Ibadan, the Oyo State capital, in a show of force amid threats by members of the National Union of Road Transport Workers to take over motor parks across the state.
The PUNCH sighted the patrol vehicl
content:
Men of the Nigeria Police Force and the Nigerian Army on Monday embarked on patrols across parts of Ibadan, the Oyo State capital, in a show of force amid threats by members of the National Union of Road Transport Workers to take over motor parks across the state.

The PUNCH sighted the patrol vehicles, with sirens blaring, moving from Challenge through Iwo Road to the Ojoo area of the state capital.

Combined teams of the police, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps and volunteer policemen were also stationed at bus terminals in Challenge, Iwo Road, Ojoo, the Iwo Road underbridge and the area before World Oil motor park.

The security teams had arrived at the parks early on Monday morning. One of the stationed policemen was heard daring NURTW members to show up, adding that security agencies were on the ground.

There was palpable fear on Monday morning as traders at the parks made calls to ascertain the situation before leaving their homes.

A woman who spoke with The PUNCH at the Iwo Road bus terminal, a POS operator, said, “I had to call before coming out as we have been told that the NURTW members are coming to take over the parks. But so far, it is still the PMS members that are in charge.”

The tension was fuelled by a viral notice circulated on Sunday, asking residents of the state capital to avoid the Iwo Road, Ojoo and Challenge areas and warning of a possible clash between NURTW members and park managers over control of motor parks on Monday.

The notice, sighted by The PUNCH, added, “If possible, stay indoors throughout the day.”

The Oyo State Police Public Relations Officer, Ayanlade Olayinka, had in a statement allayed fears, saying the command had deployed adequate personnel and enhanced surveillance and intelligence-gathering mechanisms across strategic locations in the state.

The police urged the two parties to embrace dialogue and explore legitimate and appropriate legal channels for resolving their differences.

“No individual or group should resort to self-help, violence, intimidation or any action capable of threatening public peace,” the police urged.

The command, however, vowed to deal decisively with anyone found engaging in conduct capable of disturbing public peace.

The NURTW had threatened to take over motor parks across Oyo State on Monday, accusing Governor Seyi Makinde’s administration of repeatedly disobeying court judgments recognising its right to manage the parks.

The union said it would begin enforcing the judgments if the state government failed to withdraw its Park Management System from motor parks in the state’s 33 local government areas.

It described its exclusion from managing the parks as seven and a half years of unlawful exclusion, hardship and humiliation under the state government’s management arrangement.

In a joint statement signed by its state leaders, Abideen Olajide and Lekan Alesinloye, the union accused the Makinde administration of disregarding the rule of law by continuing to operate through the PMS despite several court rulings in its favour.

The NURTW said it had repeatedly appealed to the government to comply with the judgments recognising its status as a constitutionally registered labour union and its rights over the management of motor parks and the activities of its members across the state.

It alleged that PMS officials remained in control of the parks despite the judicial pronouncements.

The union said it had notified the Federal Government, the General Officer Commanding, 2 Division of the Nigerian Army, the Department of State Services, the Oyo State Commissioner of Police and the Nigeria Labour Congress of its intention to enforce the judgments without waiting any longer for the state government.

“We are alerting the Federal Government, GOC, Director of DSS and the Commissioner of Police that we will implement the court judgment by ourselves because the governor has failed us,” the union leaders said.

The NURTW also alleged that its prolonged exclusion from managing the parks had resulted in hunger, humiliation and the deaths of several members, warning that it could no longer tolerate the situation.

The Makinde government replaced the NURTW system with the Park Management System upon assuming office in 2019.

The Oyo State chapter of the NURTW is relying on the unanimous judgment of the Court of Appeal, Ibadan Division, delivered on September 26, 2025, in Appeal No. CA/IB/263/2022.

The lead judgment was delivered by Justice Kenneth Ikechukwu Amadi in an appeal brought by the NURTW against the Governor of Oyo State, the Attorney General of Oyo State, the Commissioner for Public Works, Infrastructure and Transportation, and the Commissioner of Police, Oyo State.

The appellate court overturned an earlier National Industrial Court decision, ruled that the state government had failed to justify the union’s suspension and set aside Governor Seyi Makinde’s May 31, 2019, proscription and suspension of NURTW operations in Oyo State.

The union leadership, led by Chairman Alhaji Abideen Olajide and Secretary Lekan Alesinloye, contends that setting aside the 2019 suspension restores its right to operate in motor parks across the state. It is relying on the judgment as the basis for its ultimatum to displace Park Management System officials.

However, the state government disputes that interpretation, maintaining that the judgment merely affirmed freedom of association and did not order the handover of public motor parks or grant ownership, control or management rights over local government-owned facilities to the NURTW.

Meanwhile, the Oyo State Government said security agencies across the state had been placed on red alert to bring the full weight of the law against troublemakers and anyone who might attempt to disrupt the peace and harmony of the state.

In a statement on Monday made available to The PUNCH, the Special Adviser on Security to the Oyo State Governor, Abayomi Fagbenro, advised the NURTW leadership to immediately withdraw its threats of unleashing mayhem on the state.

Fagbenro urged NURTW members to embrace dialogue, amicability, moral suasion, sacrifice, and give-and-take to settle the dispute.

The statement read, “The reported decision of the NURTW leaders to resort to self-help in their vaunted ambition for the control of the motor parks and garages will bode ill for them and those backing them.

“The government is not unmindful of the unseen hand behind the sudden boldness of the NURTW issuing threats of mayhem in the thick of electioneering ahead of the forthcoming crucial elections.

“Let me state unequivocally that no individual, group, or union has the right to take the law into its own hands, and any such attempt will be resisted.”

Fagbenro argued that the management of motor parks in Oyo State was regulated by law and government policy, stressing that any change in leadership or administration must follow due process.

He added, “Any attempt to cause a breakdown of law and order, foment crisis, or unleash violence on innocent citizens and park users under the guise of union rivalry will not be tolerated by this government.

“I am by this statement warning all those involved in this plot to desist forthwith, because the state has put behind it the past spectre of thuggery and brigandage synonymous with drivers’ union activities.

“Anyone caught with dangerous weapons, inciting violence, or leading thugs to attack any park will be arrested and prosecuted to the full extent of the law. There will be no sacred cows.”

While urging all law-abiding drivers and park managers to go about their lawful duties without fear, Fagbenro also urged residents of the state to remain vigilant.

“All grievances should be channelled through legitimate and lawful means and any action considered an affront to the constituted authorities will have lawful and legal consequences,” Fagbenro added.

title: $4.67bn FX turnover fails to halt naira’s decline
description:
Nigeria’s foreign exchange market recorded $4.67bn in transactions last week, but the increased trading activity failed to halt the naira’s depreciation, exposing persistent pressure on dollar supply.
The turnover, the second-highest weekly level recorded in 2026, increased by 36.59 per cent from $3
content:
Nigeria’s foreign exchange market recorded $4.67bn in transactions last week, but the increased trading activity failed to halt the naira’s depreciation, exposing persistent pressure on dollar supply.

The turnover, the second-highest weekly level recorded in 2026, increased by 36.59 per cent from $3.42bn in the preceding week, according to FMDQ data.

However, the naira depreciated by 2.50 per cent to close at N1,394 per dollar, its weakest level in eight months, suggesting that higher transaction volumes were not translating into sufficient dollar supply to stabilise the currency.

Cordros Securities said foreign portfolio investor demand outweighed the CBN’s reported $1.30bn intervention during the week, indicating the extent of demand pressure in the FX market.

Spot transactions accounted for $4.64bn, or 99.40 per cent, of total turnover, representing an increase of 43.08 per cent from the preceding week.

Forward transactions, meanwhile, fell by 83.88 per cent to $28.19m, leaving them with just 0.60 per cent of total turnover.

The sharp increase in spot transactions pushed average daily turnover to $934.50m from $684.18m a week earlier.

Despite the increase in market activity, the naira weakened from N1,360 per dollar on Monday to N1,394 on Friday, while the parallel market rate depreciated by 2.33 per cent to N1,458 per dollar.

The one-month forward rate also weakened by 2.7 per cent to N1,414.99, while the three-month contract depreciated by 2.7 per cent to N1,451.81.

The six-month forward rate fell by 2.1 per cent to N1,495.98, while the one-year contract weakened by 2.0 per cent to N1,597.57 per dollar.

The figures suggest that increased trading activity alone may not be sufficient to ease pressure on the naira, particularly as FX demand continues to outpace available supply.

However, FMDQ’s turnover data do not establish whether the increase in transactions was driven by additional dollar supply or stronger demand, making it difficult to determine the extent to which market liquidity improved.

Daily interbank turnover at the CBN’s Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market window rose from $68.66m on Monday to $815.57m on Friday, while calculations based on daily CBN figures showed approximately $2.55bn in turnover during the week.

The figures differ from FMDQ’s $4.67bn because they reflect different reporting scopes and should not be combined.

Cordros Securities expects FX demand pressures to persist through the remainder of the year, citing weaker net foreign inflows and investor caution ahead of the 2027 general elections.

the Chief Executive Officer of the Centre for Promotion of Private Enterprise, Dr Muda Yusuf, said domestic factors could be contributing to the successive decline of the naira against the dollar.

The economist identified political spending, capital flight and policy uncertainty as possible factors behind the weakening currency and declining foreign reserves.

He said political spending could inject liquidity into the economy and put pressure on the naira, noting that the Central Bank of Nigeria had previously raised concerns about the impact of political activities on exchange rate stability.

“The political spending liquidity may be already putting pressure on the naira. The CBN had expressed that fear before during the latest Monetary Policy Committee meeting,” Yusuf said.

He argued that foreign exchange demand associated with political activities could be channelled through the parallel market because such transactions might not be formally documented or conducted through official channels.

Yusuf also warned that political uncertainty and statements by some politicians about reversing the economic reforms of the President Bola Tinubu administration could trigger capital flight.

An emerging markets expert and economist, Ike Ibeabuchi, attributed the weakening naira and declining reserves to reduced dollar supply and rising demand for foreign exchange.

He said lower inflows from exporters, investors and other sources might be reducing dollar availability in the market, while demand for foreign currency to finance imports and international transactions continued to exert pressure on the naira.

“Lower foreign exchange inflows from exporters, investors and other sources reduce dollar supply in the market, while demand for foreign currency for imports, international payments and other transactions continues to exert pressure on the naira,” Ibeabuchi said.

He said the festive season typically increases demand for foreign exchange, while the influence of election-related spending on the currency could be greater than initially anticipated.

The post $4.67bn FX turnover fails to halt naira’s decline appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: FG unveils five-year drug control plan, seeks emergency response
description:
The Federal Government has called for drug abuse and illicit drug trafficking to be treated as a national emergency, warning that the menace poses serious threats to public health, national security and economic development.
Vice-President Kashim Shettima made the call on Monday during the official
content:
The Federal Government has called for drug abuse and illicit drug trafficking to be treated as a national emergency, warning that the menace poses serious threats to public health, national security and economic development.

Vice-President Kashim Shettima made the call on Monday during the official launch of the National Drug Control Master Plan 2026–2030.

Shettima, who was represented by the Special Adviser to the President on Special Duties, Office of the Vice-President, Modibbo Umar, said drug control must remain a national priority, stressing that the challenge extends beyond drug seizures and arrests of suspected traffickers.

He said, “That is why drug control must remain a national priority. As a matter of fact, it should be treated as a national emergency.

“The challenge before us goes beyond the consignments intercepted by our agencies or the criminal networks brought before our courts. It reaches into our homes, our schools, our workplaces, and our communities.”

Shettima noted that drug abuse affects families, workforce productivity, and the future of young Nigerians, adding that the country must confront the problem with determination and compassion.

According to him, the drug problem should be understood as a public health concern, security threat, development challenge and economic issue.

He said the response must go beyond enforcement to include prevention, early intervention, treatment, rehabilitation and recovery, while security agencies must intensify intelligence-led operations to dismantle trafficking networks.

“These dimensions are bound together. We cannot rely on enforcement alone and neglect prevention. We cannot promote treatment without improving access to appropriate services.

“We cannot disrupt trafficking networks while ignoring the financial structures that sustain them. And we cannot expect lasting results when institutions work in isolation or lack the resources to discharge their responsibilities,” he said.

The Vice-President said the new master plan builds on the experience of the 2021–2025 framework, urging relevant institutions to consolidate previous achievements, address implementation gaps and respond to emerging threats.

He stressed that the success of the plan would depend on effective implementation rather than the unveiling of the policy document.

“The worth of a national plan lies not merely in the priorities it sets, but in the change it produces—in how institutions conduct themselves, how resources are allocated, and how people’s lives are improved,” he added.

Shettima called on federal ministries, departments and agencies, state and local governments to take responsibility for implementing the plan, noting that the National Assembly, judiciary, health and education institutions also had critical roles to play.

He further identified traditional rulers, religious leaders, civil society organisations, the private sector, parents, teachers and young Nigerians as essential partners in tackling the menace.

“No single institution, however capable, can overcome this challenge alone,” he said.

He said the impact of the master plan would ultimately be measured by improved access to treatment, effective prevention, stronger institutional cooperation, disruption of criminal networks and better living conditions for Nigerians.

“Let this be the moment Nigeria moves from policy to action, from fragmented efforts to coordinated national impact, and from commitment on paper to measurable improvements in the lives of our people,” he said.

Speaking earlier, the Chairman of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), said the new master plan was designed to build on previous achievements while addressing identified gaps and emerging threats.

Marwa said the summative evaluation of the 2021–2025 National Drug Control Master Plan recorded 77,736 arrests, the seizure of more than 14.8 million kilogrammes of drugs and over 14,200 convictions.

He added that more than 32,400 people also benefited from treatment, counselling and rehabilitation services during the period.

According to him, the evaluation identified gaps in coordination, financing, service delivery, data management, monitoring and accountability, as well as weak institutional capacity at state and local government levels.

He said the new plan was designed “to keep what worked, fix what did not, and confront what is emerging.”

Marwa explained that the framework would better integrate drug supply and demand reduction while targeting the financial and technological systems sustaining illicit drug markets.

He said the approach would strengthen the agency’s capacity to confront sophisticated trafficking networks, synthetic drugs, new psychoactive substances and criminal syndicates exploiting encrypted communications and cryptocurrency.

Also speaking, the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, described the NDLEA as “the bedrock of our national drug response.”

He said the new master plan would consolidate the agency’s achievements into a whole-of-government framework integrating law enforcement with public health, education, social development, financial investigation and community participation.

Fagbemi commended the leadership and personnel of the agency under Marwa, assuring that the Federal Ministry of Justice would collaborate with the judiciary to facilitate the speedy determination of drug-related cases in line with the Administration of Criminal Justice Act.

He said the ministry would also ensure that convictions were accompanied by the confiscation of illicit assets and strengthen mutual legal assistance, extradition and cross-border asset recovery.

The AGF further praised the NDLEA’s practice of involving prosecutors early in investigations, noting that the approach helped preserve evidence and prevent procedural errors.

He stressed the need to distinguish between drug traffickers and people struggling with drug dependence, saying the latter required treatment rather than punishment alone.

“While traffickers must face the full weight of the law, those experiencing drug use disorders require evidence-based care, counselling, treatment, and community reintegration,” he said.

Fagbemi urged stakeholders to make the master plan their operational guide, adding that the NDLEA’s efforts to replace illicit drug cultivation with legitimate cash crops and other agricultural activities aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s development agenda.

In a goodwill message, the ECOWAS Commissioner for Human Development and Social Affairs, Professor Nassirou Bako-Arifari, commended Nigeria for the initiative, describing the master plan as consistent with regional commitments towards a safer and healthier West Africa.

He, however, said its success would depend on sustained political will, adequate funding and cooperation among governments, civil society organisations, communities, the private sector and international partners.

“The ECOWAS Commission will stand with Nigeria at every step, sharing experience, mobilising support and linking this national effort to the work of other Member States.

“Nigeria’s progress will guide the region, because no country can win this fight alone,” he said.

title: Fani-Kayode denies recall, faults treatment of Nigerians in S’Africa
description:
Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has dismissed reports alleging that he was recalled or reprimanded by the Federal Government over his diplomatic engagements, describing the claims circulating on social media as “completely unfounded.”
The envoy, however, raised concern
content:
Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has dismissed reports alleging that he was recalled or reprimanded by the Federal Government over his diplomatic engagements, describing the claims circulating on social media as “completely unfounded.”

The envoy, however, raised concerns over unresolved deaths of Nigerians, alleged misconduct by some South African security personnel and recurring anti-Nigerian sentiments, insisting that protecting Nigerians abroad must remain a priority of his diplomatic mission and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Fani-Kayode spoke during a visit to Abuja, where he said his presence was part of routine diplomatic consultations with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and should not be interpreted as a disciplinary measure.

He said he briefed ministry officials on developments in South Africa and received policy guidance on Nigeria’s diplomatic engagements. His consultations included meetings with officials responsible for African affairs and the country’s diplomatic missions across the continent.

“There have been reports on social media suggesting that I have been recalled. Those claims are simply untrue,” he said.

The ambassador maintained that his visit to Nigeria was for official consultations, submission of reports, family engagements and preparations for the relocation of his family to South Africa.

He said the trip should not be mistaken for a recall, stressing that his engagements with the ministry had been cordial and productive. “If I had been recalled, I doubt I would be standing here smiling after a cordial and productive meeting with the minister.”

Fani-Kayode also disclosed that what was initially expected to be a short assignment in South Africa had been extended to allow for the completion of official diplomatic procedures.

Addressing speculation that he had been reprimanded over his recent engagements in the country, the envoy insisted that diplomatic relations between Abuja and Pretoria remained cordial.

“Our engagements with South African authorities have been cordial and constructive. Concerns have been raised on both sides in a professional diplomatic manner, and no reprimand of any kind occurred.”

In a statement issued on Monday, Fani-Kayode called for stronger bilateral cooperation between Nigeria and South Africa, describing relations between the two countries as critical to Africa’s economic integration, political stability and development.

He said that while the Nigerian government remained committed to strengthening diplomatic and economic relations with South Africa, it would not overlook issues affecting the safety, dignity and welfare of Nigerians living in the country.

“The future of Africa is closely tied to the relationship between Nigeria and South Africa. If these two countries fail to work together, it could have significant implications for the continent’s progress,” he said.

He noted that since assuming office, he had consistently advocated dialogue, mutual respect and stronger bilateral ties between both countries.

However, he said the cordial relationship between the two governments should not prevent Nigeria from raising concerns over the treatment of its citizens. “As ambassador, I would be failing in my responsibility if I did not raise concerns about the treatment of Nigerians in South Africa,” he said.

Among the issues he identified were unresolved cases involving the deaths of Nigerians, reports of misconduct by some security personnel and recurring anti-Nigerian rhetoric by certain groups.

Meanwhile, no fewer than 12 Nigerians have been killed in South Africa in 2026 as a result of anti-migrant protests, alleged police brutality and Afrophobia attacks.

The envoy also faulted attempts to portray Nigerians living in South Africa as criminals, arguing that such generalisations unfairly undermined the contributions of thousands of law-abiding citizens.

“Thousands of Nigerians in South Africa are law-abiding professionals, including doctors, lawyers, academics and entrepreneurs. A small minority engaged in wrongdoing should not be used to define an entire community,” he said.

Fani-Kayode maintained that the anti-Nigerian sentiments expressed by some organisations should not be interpreted as representing the position of the majority of South Africans.

He nevertheless described such rhetoric as troubling, urging both countries to address tensions through sustained engagement, dialogue and mutual understanding.

The ambassador also commended Nigerian community organisations in South Africa for their contributions to protecting the interests and welfare of citizens living in the country.

He said their engagement had helped ensure that the concerns of Nigerians received greater attention and representation.

“Many Nigerians believe that their concerns are finally being heard and represented. I remain committed to speaking on their behalf and standing up for their interests,” he said.

Fani-Kayode further encouraged Nigerian investors and business owners operating in South Africa to sustain their investments and expand their enterprises, while supporting fellow Nigerians facing difficulties.

Reaffirming his commitment to defending Nigeria’s interests, he said: “Wherever Nigeria’s dignity is challenged or undermined, I will not hesitate to speak out and defend the green-white-green.”

He criticised what he described as the growing spread of misinformation on social media, arguing that unverified claims were often amplified by individuals seeking to undermine Nigeria’s interests.

The ambassador reaffirmed his commitment to protecting Nigeria’s diplomatic interests in South Africa, adding that he remained fully aligned with the foreign policy objectives of President Bola Tinubu’s administration.

He reiterated that strengthening Nigeria-South Africa relations, promoting economic cooperation and safeguarding the welfare of Nigerians abroad would remain central to his diplomatic mission.

The post Fani-Kayode denies recall, faults treatment of Nigerians in S’Africa appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
