title: Cross River opposition leaders unite under Rainbow Coalition
description:
Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Rainbow Coalition has been inaugurated in Cross River State, with its leaders vowing to reclaim the state from years of mismanagement and poor leadership.
The inauguration, held on Monday in Calabar, drew leaders of the Peoples Democratic Party, coalition par
content:
Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Rainbow Coalition has been inaugurated in Cross River State, with its leaders vowing to reclaim the state from years of mismanagement and poor leadership.

The inauguration, held on Monday in Calabar, drew leaders of the Peoples Democratic Party, coalition partners, community leaders, youth movements and supporters from across the 18 local government areas of the state.

The coalition, promoted nationally by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, is a cross-party platform to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu in 2027, while allowing candidates from different parties to contest governorship, National Assembly and State Assembly seats.

Speaking at the event, the State Chairman of PDP in Cross River, Dr. Frank Bullem, said the launch was built not on confidence but on the conviction to reclaim the state from poor leadership and mismanagement.

He said, “The launch of the Rainbow Coalition seeks a partnership with our committed volunteers to reclaim our state from gross mismanagement and ineptitude in leadership.

“We gather here not just to launch a coalition and campaign; we gather to declare that the challenges before us are too great for any single party, any single leader, or any single organisation to confront.”

Bullem said the state was grappling with a weakened economy, decayed infrastructure in public schools and hospitals, insecurity in communities, mismanagement of collective resources, and eroded confidence in public institutions.

He said the coalition was anchored on four pillars: unity over division, ideas over insults, service over self-interest, and mobilisation of every citizen.

“Under this platform, we reject politics of polarisation. Our strength lies in our diversity of region, of religion, of generations, of professionals, and we will harness that strength and not fear it.

“We will present to the public a clear, consistent and credible plan in key policy areas: jobs, education, healthcare and infrastructure”, he said.

He urged supporters to become ambassadors, organisers and champions of the cause, and to take the message to every ward, village and street.

Also speaking, the Deputy National Chairman (South), Aaron Chukwuemeka, described the coalition’s candidate for the state as a formidable candidate who had stood with the helpless Nigerians.

“The candidate that I have here today is a formidable candidate. He is a terrific candidate. I believe in the truth, and the truth is that the candidate you are choosing to run for this state is a candidate you must vote for,” Chukwuemeka said.

In his remarks, the State Coordinator of the Rainbow Coalition, Hon. Jones Ojong, expressed confidence that the coalition would produce a new government with a new pathway for the state.

“And we believe that with this coalition, we will have a new government in this state that will have a new pathway in this state. So we are 100 per cent in support of this coalition, and by the grace of God, we are going to deliver.

“The vision for a new state is possible. For the first time, this kind of vision is coming to play. When you see parties coming together to chant this cause of a change, a total turnaround.”

Ojong thanked coalition partners for their courage and trust, and pledged a partnership built on respect, shared responsibility and mutual accountability.

He called on market women, students, farmers, teachers, workers and entrepreneurs to take ownership of the movement, saying the 2027 election would be decided at the grassroots.

The post Cross River opposition leaders unite under Rainbow Coalition appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Hashim tasks Tinubu on 2027 general elections
description:
The presidential candidate of the Accord Party, Dr Olawepo Hashim, has warned that any attempt to rig the 2027 general election could push Nigeria into a full-blown civil war.
Hashim gave the warning on Symfoni Podcast with Olawale Oluwade on Saturday, where he spoke on the state of the nation, inse
content:
The presidential candidate of the Accord Party, Dr Olawepo Hashim, has warned that any attempt to rig the 2027 general election could push Nigeria into a full-blown civil war.

Hashim gave the warning on Symfoni Podcast with Olawale Oluwade on Saturday, where he spoke on the state of the nation, insecurity and the credibility of the electoral process.

He claimed that the Independent National Electoral Commission was showing a lack of preparedness, as he condemned the postponement of the voters’ register clean-up exercise until after the election.

INEC Chairman, Prof Joash Amupitan, had on Friday cited constraints and public opposition to its earlier plan to revalidate the register as reasons for the postponement of the planned comprehensive clean-up of the voter register.

Amupitan said the commission had initially proposed a six-month exercise to remove deceased persons, underage voters, incomplete registrations and duplicate entries from the register but shelved the plan after facing opposition.

Amupitan, however, said INEC was addressing cases of multiple registrations following public complaints.

Speaking, Hashim warned that any form of election rigging could trigger confusion that could give insurgents an opportunity to advance towards state capitals, potentially triggering a wider conflict that could degenerate into civil war.

Hashim said, “The moment there’s a slight political crisis, the militia and terrorist groups, who are well organised, may take advantage of the political instability to expand and declare control in some states in the North and press towards Abuja.

“Don’t plunge Nigeria into another civil war.”

He claimed that Nigeria was sitting on a dangerous edge, citing “insecurity, political mistrust and a failing electoral system.”

“With the current insecurity, political violence, and adding election rigging in 2027 will delegitimise government completely, and this could open space for non-state actors, insurgents, etc., already operating in 17 out of the 19 northern states to take advantage of the situation,” he warned.

According to Hashim, President Bola Tinubu had not shown the ability to tackle the nation’s challenges head-on.

“And, President Tinubu will do the usual thing he does best, which is to run away. He is always away, he cannot stay to solve any problem; he will run away, he will take a flight out of the country,” he said.

title: FG seeks stronger food policies to curb malnutrition, NCDs
description:
By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja



The Federal Government has called for stronger implementation of healthy food policies to address malnutrition, micronutrient deficiencies and the rising burden of diet-related non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in the country.







The Minister of State for Health and S
content:
By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja

The Federal Government has called for stronger implementation of healthy food policies to address malnutrition, micronutrient deficiencies and the rising burden of diet-related non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in the country.

The Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Dr. Iziaq Adekunle Salako, made the call on Monday while delivering the keynote address at the maiden National Healthy Food Week and Learning Conference 2026 in Abuja.

The conference, themed, “Our Food, Our Health, Our Future,” was organised to promote healthier food systems and strengthen efforts to address nutrition-related health challenges.

Represented by the ministry’s Permanent Secretary, Ms. Daju Kachollom, Salako said tackling the country’s nutrition and health challenges required stronger collaboration among government institutions, regulatory agencies, food manufacturers, health professionals, researchers, development partners, the media and consumers.

He noted that food choices and the quality of food available in markets, schools, hospitals, workplaces and homes had significant implications for public health, workforce productivity, child development and national prosperity.

The minister said the Federal Government had introduced several policies and regulatory measures to improve food safety and nutritional standards, including the Revised National Policy on Food Safety and Quality and its Implementation Plan (2023).

He said the policy framework promoted food safety, food fortification, sodium reduction, elimination of industrially produced trans fats and healthier food procurement practices in public institutions.

Salako also highlighted the National Guidelines for Sodium Reduction, the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control’s (NAFDAC) Read the Label Campaign and the development of front-of-pack nutrition labelling as measures to help consumers make informed food choices and encourage manufacturers to improve the nutritional quality of their products.

On public food procurement, he said government institutions provided millions of meals annually through schools, hospitals, correctional centres, emergency shelters and National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) camps, making public procurement an important instrument for improving the country’s food environment.

He urged relevant authorities to ensure effective implementation of the Bureau of Public Procurement’s National Guidelines for Public Procurement of Food and Related Services through adequate monitoring, accountability and capacity building.

The minister also identified fiscal measures, including the sugar-sweetened beverage tax, as important tools for discouraging excessive consumption of sugary drinks and generating revenue for public health interventions.

He advocated transparent allocation of part of the revenue to nutrition education, healthier food environments and the prevention of diet-related diseases.

On micronutrient deficiencies, Salako emphasised the need to strengthen large-scale food fortification, noting that its effectiveness depended on regulatory compliance, quality assurance, adequate laboratory capacity and market surveillance.

He also encouraged Nigerians to consume more locally available nutritious foods, including legumes, fruits, vegetables, nuts, whole grains and traditional nutrient-rich foods.

While acknowledging progress in developing healthy food policies and regulatory frameworks, the minister said the priority should now be to ensure their effective implementation on a wider scale.

He identified state and local governments, primary healthcare facilities, community organisations, traditional and religious institutions, women’s groups, youth networks and the media as critical partners in translating policies into measurable health outcomes.

Salako warned that unhealthy food environments could worsen the burden of hypertension, diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular diseases, stroke and kidney disease, with serious implications for healthcare costs and national productivity.

He called for the National Healthy Food Week and Learning Conference to become a sustainable platform for accountability, partnership, innovation and continuous improvement of Nigeria’s food systems.

He stressed that every Nigerian should have access to safe, nutritious, affordable and health-promoting food.

In a goodwill message, the Interim Country Director of Resolve to Save Lives (RTSL), Dr. Jenom Danjuma, reaffirmed the organisation’s commitment to supporting government efforts to promote healthy diets and strengthen food policies to reduce the burden of NCDs.

Danjuma identified excessive sodium, industrially produced trans fats and added sugars, particularly from sugar-sweetened beverages, as major dietary risk factors contributing to premature deaths from hypertension, cardiovascular diseases and type 2 diabetes.

He called for evidence-based policies and sustained collaboration among stakeholders to promote healthier food environments and make nutritious food more accessible to Nigerians.

He said the four-day conference would provide an opportunity for stakeholders to assess progress in implementing healthy food policies, share experiences, identify challenges and develop practical strategies to accelerate action.

Similarly, the Executive Director of the Network for Health Equity and Development (NHED), Dr. Jerome Mafeni, said access to safe, nutritious and affordable food should be treated as a public health priority rather than solely an individual responsibility.

Mafeni said food choices were influenced not only by personal preferences but also by availability, production standards, affordability and access to reliable consumer information.

He argued that the effectiveness of healthy food policies should be measured by their impact on what was produced, marketed and made available to consumers rather than by the mere adoption of policy documents.

He urged stakeholders to move beyond discussions and agree on practical commitments, stronger institutional coordination and sustained accountability, adding that the conference’s success would depend on the actions taken and their impact on Nigerians.

Also speaking, the World Health Organisation (WHO) Representative, Dr. Pavel Ursu, represented by Pindar Wakawa, called for stronger measures to promote healthy diets and address the growing burden of diet-related NCDs in Nigeria.

Ursu described the conference as a timely national platform for advancing healthy food policies, noting that healthy diets were among the most effective investments countries could make to prevent diseases, improve productivity, strengthen human capital and accelerate socioeconomic development.

He expressed concern that diet-related NCDs accounted for approximately 27 per cent of all deaths in Nigeria, identifying cardiovascular diseases, hypertension, diabetes and chronic respiratory diseases as major public health concerns partly driven by excessive consumption of salt, sugar and unhealthy fats.

The WHO representative also disclosed that nearly one in three Nigerian adults was living with hypertension, a major risk factor for heart disease, stroke and kidney failure.

He called for sustained collaboration among government institutions, development partners, civil society organisations and the private sector to ensure that healthy food was accessible, affordable and available to all Nigerians.

The post FG seeks stronger food policies to curb malnutrition, NCDs appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Yuletide: Why pregnant women should avoid long trips – Gynaecologists

content:
As the festive season approaches with its usual visits and travels, maternal health experts have advised pregnant women, most importantly those close to their expected dates of delivery, to avoid long-distance journeys.

They clarified that although travelling itself would not trigger labour, pregnant women should consider the length of the journey, the prolonged sitting it may involve, the condition of the means of transportation, and the availability of skilled medical personnel at their destination.

The gynaecologists warned that going into labour while travelling, especially on a long-distance journey or aboard an aircraft, could create medical challenges because appropriate care might not be readily available.

Away from the festive season, they also advised women who intend to travel to their parents’ or relatives’ homes for support during childbirth and after delivery to make the journey early, preferably before 35 weeks of gestation, and arrange to continue their antenatal care at a health facility at their destination.

Yuletide in Nigeria comes with a lot of visits and travels to the homes of loved ones, as well as trips to exciting places and for religious activities.

Also, for many expectant mothers in Nigeria, travelling to their parents’ or relatives’ homes ahead of delivery is a way of securing family support during childbirth and the demanding early weeks of caring for a newborn.

Some rely on their mothers or mothers-in-law for assistance with the baby and other household responsibilities, especially where they have other young children.

PUNCH Healthwise had earlier reported that maternal health experts advised pregnant women to register for antenatal care at health facilities close to their homes and avoid long-distance journeys as their EDD approached.

The experts warned that labour could progress rapidly, while traffic congestion, transport difficulties and delays in accessing emergency care could leave women delivering on the road or in other places without appropriate medical assistance.

Providing expert insight into the matter, a Professor of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Oluwarotimi Akinola, said there was no evidence to suggest that travelling alone triggered labour, but cautioned pregnant women against taking unnecessary risks when they were approaching their delivery dates.

The gynaecologist said the concern was the possibility of labour beginning during a journey, particularly when the woman was travelling for several hours without easy access to medical care.

He said, “I honestly cannot say travel on its own will trigger labour. Nobody can absolutely say that because you are travelling, it will trigger labour. But what we know is that at some gestational age, labour might start.”

The professor said pregnant women planning to travel by air should be cautious, noting that a long flight could become difficult if labour began while they were on board.

“For example, if you are taking a plane and you are going to spend six to eight hours on that plane, I would want to be sure that you are not close to labour.

“Because when you go into labour on the plane, it has territorial political implications and all that. Apart from the medical challenges, it constitutes a risk for the people on the plane,” he said.

He, however, maintained that the journey itself was not necessarily responsible for the onset of labour, adding that the concern was the possibility of labour beginning when appropriate medical care might not be readily available.

For women travelling within the country, especially those going to stay with their parents or in-laws ahead of delivery, Akinola advised that the journey should be made early enough to allow them to transfer their antenatal care appropriately so that the health workers at their destination could understand their medical history and know how to manage them if complications arose.

“The advice is that they do so in good time, so that they can transfer their care appropriately. So that the people who are going to take care of them will know them and know what to do when anything happens,” he added.

Akinola, a former President of the Society of Gynaecology and Obstetrics of Nigeria, advised women not to wait until the final weeks of pregnancy before making such journeys, stressing the importance of following the guidance of their antenatal care providers.

“Don’t wait until the last minute and start travelling,” he said.

Akinola advised pregnant women to take antenatal care seriously because it provides guidance on preparing for childbirth and recognising situations that require medical attention.

Also, a Professor of Obstetrics and Gynaecology at the Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife, Osun State, Ernest Orji, advised pregnant women against travelling late in pregnancy, especially over long distances by road.

He added that prolonged sitting during long journeys, bad roads and the possibility of witnessing or being involved in accidents were concerns for heavily pregnant women.

He said, “What I normally tell people is that you should not travel after 35 weeks. If you want to travel, travel early. Many commercial bus drivers are careless, and some of the roads are bad. The trauma of seeing or having an accident is not good for a woman who is heavily pregnant.

“Also, a pregnant woman is not supposed to be sitting down for long; it’s not good for the baby too.”

Orji said women travelling to another town to deliver should also ensure that the health workers at their destination have access to their antenatal records and previous test results.

He said this would help the receiving medical team understand the woman’s condition, the care she had received and any precautions that might be necessary during delivery.

“We advise them to get their records and results from the hospital where they are coming from so that the new hospital knows what their state is, what has been done for them, and precautions they need to take,” he said.

Orji also urged pregnant women and their families to make practical arrangements for delivery before labour began, rather than waiting until an emergency arose.

He advised them to identify a suitable health facility, preferably one with qualified medical personnel, and ensure that they had the necessary supplies for delivery.

The obstetrician further urged families to arrange reliable transportation that would be available at any time of the day or night, including ensuring that vehicles had enough fuel.

The post Yuletide: Why pregnant women should avoid long trips – Gynaecologists appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Abia woman docked for assaulting cop, tearing uniform
description:
The Abia State Police Command has arrested and charged to court a woman accused of assaulting a police officer and tearing his uniform during an operation at a church in Aba.
The woman, identified as Ettoh Barkerk, was arrested after she allegedly became violent and attacked an inspector attached to
content:
The Abia State Police Command has arrested and charged to court a woman accused of assaulting a police officer and tearing his uniform during an operation at a church in Aba.

The woman, identified as Ettoh Barkerk, was arrested after she allegedly became violent and attacked an inspector attached to a patrol team responding to a distress call at the CKC Church, Aba.

The Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Maureen Chinaka, disclosed this in a statement on Monday, following a viral video showing the woman assaulting the officer.

Chinaka said the command strongly condemned the incident, describing it as “reprehensible and unacceptable” and contrary to the standards of civility and respect for the law.

According to the statement, the Ndiegoro Divisional Police Headquarters received a distress call on Sunday that some hoodlums were attacking members of the church congregation by indiscriminately throwing fireworks within the premises, causing panic and threatening public peace.

“Upon receipt of the report, a patrol team from the Division swiftly mobilised to the scene to contain the situation, prevent further escalation and restore public order,” the statement said.

The police said Barkerk was apprehended at the scene with fireworks in her possession.

“However, the suspect became violent and physically assaulted an inspector attached to the patrol team, tore his uniform and attempted to forcibly retrieve the recovered exhibits,” the statement added.

The command said the suspect was subsequently subdued and arrested, while the recovered fireworks and other relevant exhibits were secured for investigation.

It said the suspect had been charged to court following the conclusion of the investigation.

The police said normalcy had since returned to the church premises and its environs, adding that monitoring of the area was ongoing to prevent any further breach of peace.

The command reiterated its commitment to carrying out its constitutional responsibilities and warned that it would not tolerate assault, obstruction or interference with police officers performing their lawful duties.

It urged members of the public to remain law-abiding, exercise restraint and respect law enforcement officers carrying out their legitimate responsibilities of protecting lives and property.

The post Abia woman docked for assaulting cop, tearing uniform appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Four killed as gunmen attack Omo-Agege’s campaign convoy
description: The Delta State Government has imposed a curfew on Ughelli North Local Government Area following a violent attack on the campaign entourage of former Deputy President of the Senate and Nigeria Democratic Congress senatorial candidate for Delta Central, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, which reportedly left a
content:
The Delta State Government has imposed a curfew on Ughelli North Local Government Area following a violent attack on the campaign entourage of former Deputy President of the Senate and Nigeria Democratic Congress senatorial candidate for Delta Central, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, which reportedly left at least four persons dead and several others injured.

The violence occurred on Monday during a campaign visit by Omo-Agege to Uduere community, where gunmen allegedly opened fire on his supporters, throwing the area into panic.

Omo-Agege reportedly escaped unhurt after bullets allegedly flew past his head while he was addressing a crowd gathered to receive him.

Among those killed was Moses Anaughe, a former member of the Delta State House of Assembly representing Ughelli North II and Personal Assistant to Omo-Agege. Anaughe was also a former Commissioner representing Delta State at the Federal Character Commission.

He reportedly died at the Ughelli Central Hospital, where he was taken for medical attention after sustaining gunshot injuries during the attack.

Another victim was an Urhobo youth activist, Comrade Akima Efemena Umukoro, popularly known as Efe Umukoro.

In a statement issued on Monday by his Media Adviser, Sunny Areh, the Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation confirmed that Anaughe and Umukoro were among four persons killed in the attack.

The statement partly read, “Senator Ovie Omo-Agege was saved by a divine distraction, when bullets whizzed past his head as he was addressing the crowd that gathered to receive him.

“We are pained to report that FOUR PEOPLE, including two of our aides — Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro — were shot dead.

“Four others — Chief Evans Iwuvrie, Chuks Erhire, Tobore Agba (who was shot in the neck) and Ayodo Wanogho — were shot at very close range and wounded critically. They are currently receiving medical attention. We pray for their speedy recovery, and we stand with their families at this dark hour.

“Witnesses allege that the attackers were shouting, “It’s Omo-Agege we want to kill! It’s Omo-Agege we want to kill!”

The campaign organisation alleged that armed men opened fire on Omo-Agege and his entourage at close range while the former deputy Senate president was addressing the crowd.

It also described the incident as an assassination attempt, alleging that the Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Area, Jaro Egbo, led the attackers and acted on the orders of Governor Sheriff Oborevwori.

However, the allegations against the council chairman and the governor had not been independently established.

Earlier accounts of the incident said no fewer than eight other persons were in critical condition following the confrontation. One account identified Evans Ekurie, a former member of the Delta State House of Assembly, and Mr Tobore Agbah among those who sustained gunshot wounds. The campaign organisation, however, identified Chief Evans Iwuvrie, Chuks Erhire, Tobore Agba and Ayodo Wanogho as the four persons critically injured.

The Delta State Police Command, in a statement, said the state government had imposed a curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area from 6:00 pm to 6:00 am daily until further notice.

The command said it had commenced investigations to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible.

It urged residents to comply strictly with the curfew, remain calm, and cooperate with security personnel in the interest of public safety.

The Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, CP Samuel Erale, directed intensified security operations in the affected area to prevent further violence and maintain law and order.

The police said the commissioner had ordered a full-scale investigation and assured residents that anyone found culpable would face the full weight of the law, irrespective of political affiliation or status.

He also urged members of the public to provide credible information to assist the ongoing investigations.

Erale extended his condolences to the bereaved families and wished the injured a speedy recovery. He assured residents of the command’s commitment to protecting lives and property and ensuring a peaceful environment for lawful political activities.

The commissioner warned political actors and their supporters against thuggery, intimidation and the unlawful use of firearms, stressing that political differences must never be allowed to degenerate into violence or loss of life.

The Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation called on the Inspector-General of Police, the Director-General of the Department of State Services and the Delta State Commissioner of Police to investigate the incident.

It also accused police officers deployed to the area of failing to prevent the attack despite their alleged presence with six patrol vehicles.

The organisation urged its supporters not to retaliate, saying its ward-to-ward campaign across Delta Central would continue.

“Delta State is not a war zone. Campaigning is not a crime. Seeking the votes of the people should not be a death sentence,” the statement said.

The post Four killed as gunmen attack Omo-Agege’s campaign convoy appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: BOMBSHELL!: Infantino: Why Nigeria can’t host World Cup
description: Gianni Infantino, President of FIFA, has confirmed that, with Nigeria’s current sports infrastructure, it cannot host the FIFA World Cup, but shared optimism that the 3-time AFCON champions have the resources and the will to get there, pointing to stadiums, airports and transport as the work still t
content:
Gianni Infantino, President of FIFA, has confirmed that, with Nigeria’s current sports infrastructure, it cannot host the FIFA World Cup, but shared optimism that the 3-time AFCON champions have the resources and the will to get there, pointing to stadiums, airports and transport as the work still to be done.

Infantino gave his assessment in an interview with ARISE News in Abuja on Monday, days after attending the 48th CAF Ordinary General Assembly and inspecting the NFF’s technical centre and a renovated stadium in Warri.

Asked whether Nigeria could stage a tournament of that size, he was direct, before turning to what he had seen on his trip.

“Today, no. But tomorrow, why not?”

“The key to hosting a World Cup is obviously the infrastructure, the stadiums, the airports, transportation, and this is where best practice is needed,” he said.

“I think Nigeria has the resources, has the passion, has the will as well to move ahead with the projects that are planned in terms of stadiums,” he added.

The FIFA president also singled out the facilities he inspected. “For example, I visited a national training centre in Abuja, in Warri as well. A very nice stadium. Very nice,” he said.

The post BOMBSHELL!: Infantino: Why Nigeria can’t host World Cup appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: ‎Court orders Jimmy Odukoya to appear November 26 over church dispute
description:

‎
‎Justice O. O. Adewunmi-Oshin gave the direc
content:
‎The Lagos State High Court has directed Pastor Jimmy Odukoya to appear before it on Thursday, November 26, following an application by the Incorporated Trustees of the Fountain of Life Church to serve him with court processes through substituted means.
‎
‎Justice O. O. Adewunmi-Oshin gave the directive on Monday, after hearing an application moved by the church’s counsel, Ibitayo Reju.

PUNCH Online sighted a Certified True Copy of the enrolled order on Monday.
‎
‎In the enrolment of order, the court granted the church permission to serve Odukoya with Form 48, the originating court process, orders and notices through newspaper publication, pasting at his last known address in Ilupeju, Lagos, and electronic means.
‎
‎The court stated, “Leave is hereby granted to the Applicant to serve Form 48, the originating court process to be filed in this suit, Orders made, Notices issued, and all other processes to be issued and filed in this suit on the Respondent through substituted means by newspaper publication in several newspaper that is in wide circulation within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court and by pasting at a conspicuous part of the Respondent’s last known address at No. 12 Industrial Estate Road, off Town Planning Way, Ilupeju, Lagos State and also through any Electronical means.”
‎
‎The judge further directed that Odukoya appear before the court on the adjourned date.
‎
‎“The Respondent is required to be present in Court on the said date,” the order stated.
‎
‎The court subsequently adjourned the case until November 26, 2026, for Odukoya to show cause.
‎
‎The latest development is part of the dispute over the leadership of the church following the purported removal of Odukoya as its Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees.
‎
‎PUNCH Online had reported that Odukoya instituted a separate suit at the Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging the decisions of some members of the church’s Board of Trustees, including his purported removal from office.
‎
‎The dispute also led to an earlier order by the Lagos State High Court on November 18, restraining Odukoya from presenting himself as the church’s Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head.
‎
‎On Sunday, during the service at the church in Ilupeju, Lagos, Odukoya addressed the congregation.
‎
‎He told worshippers that he had heard about the injunction but had not been formally served with it.
‎
‎“I heard that there was an injunction against me. I heard. I’ve not seen it. But I heard. But I’ve not been served. So, legally, I’ve not been served,” he said.
‎
‎His remarks came after Bishop Mike Okonkwo, founder of The Redeemed Evangelical Mission, visited the church and urged members not to take sides in the leadership dispute involving Odukoya and his sister, Tolu.
‎

The post ‎Court orders Jimmy Odukoya to appear November 26 over church dispute appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Abbas urges states to commit N1bn for SMEs
description:
The Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, has challenged state governments to set aside at least N1bn monthly for small and medium-scale enterprises, accusing them of failing to support businesses despite increased federal allocations.
Abbas, who spoke through the House Majority L
content:
The Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, has challenged state governments to set aside at least N1bn monthly for small and medium-scale enterprises, accusing them of failing to support businesses despite increased federal allocations.

Abbas, who spoke through the House Majority Leader, Prof Julius Ihonvbere, at a stakeholders’ engagement organised by the House Committee on Small and Medium Enterprises in Abuja on Monday, said state governments had the financial capacity to establish dedicated intervention funds for entrepreneurs.

He also criticised local governments for failing to provide the institutional and financial support needed to stimulate grassroots businesses, insisting that the responsibility for improving the economy should not be left to the Federal Government alone.

“There is no governor in this country that cannot put one billion naira a month in a special fund for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises in his state. There is no state that cannot do it,” he said.

The Speaker’s position came amid growing concerns over the difficulties confronting MSMEs, including high lending rates, cumbersome access to intervention funds, regulatory bottlenecks and inadequate government support.

Abbas lamented that despite the establishment of several government agencies and the injection of substantial funds into the sector, many small businesses continued to struggle to survive, largely through the determination of their owners rather than institutional assistance.

“Those that are surviving are surviving not because of government and agencies, but in spite of government and agencies,” he said.

He particularly faulted the bureaucratic procedures associated with accessing government-backed intervention funds, arguing that excessive documentation and administrative requirements had undermined the purpose of such programmes.

“I’m a systems man, but I know this system is not working. And it will not work when you bureaucratise a procedure. A lot of red tape,” Abbas said.

He also cautioned small business owners against borrowing at double-digit interest rates, noting that the cost of credit could cripple enterprises before they became sufficiently established to meet repayment obligations.

According to him, government interventions must focus not only on making funds available but also on ensuring that financing is affordable and accessible under conditions that reflect the realities of small businesses.

The Speaker further faulted state and local governments for failing to translate increased federal allocations into tangible economic benefits for their residents.

“All the complaints you are hearing in this country today is not because of Tinubu. Not because of the federal government. It’s because of state and local governments that are not performing,” he added.

He urged Nigerians to hold elected officials at all levels accountable, stressing that subnational governments had important responsibilities in promoting employment, entrepreneurship and economic development.

Earlier, the Chairman of the House Committee on Small and Medium Enterprises, Pascal Agbodike, said the engagement was organised to identify practical solutions to the challenges confronting MSMEs and examine why existing government interventions had failed to produce the desired results.

Agbodike said the committee had invited relevant government agencies and financial institutions to explain their intervention programmes, identify implementation gaps and account for the extent to which funds appropriated by the National Assembly had reached intended beneficiaries.

“We are lawmakers. Ours is simple: to appropriate the necessary funds. But when we appropriate those funds, how is it being trickled down to the common man in the street?” he asked.

He disclosed that the committee would examine the activities of institutions, including the Central Bank of Nigeria and the Bank of Industry, to establish the gaps between policy formulation, funding approvals and actual disbursement to entrepreneurs.

The lawmaker expressed optimism that the engagement would produce concrete recommendations and measurable improvements in the delivery of MSME support programmes within 100 days.

Also speaking, the Director-General of the Presidential Enabling Business Environment Council, Princess Zahrah Audu, identified affordable financing, regulatory reforms and stronger collaboration with state governments as critical to the growth of small businesses.

Audu said PEBEC monitored 69 ministries, departments and agencies, adding that the council had introduced the ReportGov digital platform to enable businesses to report difficulties encountered in their dealings with government institutions.

She explained that complaints submitted through the platform were automatically referred to the relevant agencies, which were expected to address them within 72 hours, with PEBEC intervening where necessary.

However, she stressed that improving the business environment required coordinated action beyond the Federal Government.

Audu advocated partnerships between state governments and development finance institutions, including the Bank of Industry, Bank of Agriculture and Nigerian Export-Import Bank, to expand access to credit.

She explained that state governments could provide counterpart funding to reduce lending risks, ease collateral requirements and enable entrepreneurs with viable business proposals to secure loans.

According to her, PEBEC had facilitated similar arrangements in about 15 states, providing opportunities for business associations to participate in financing partnerships with development finance institutions.

She also called for patient capital, arguing that small businesses needed financing arrangements that allowed sufficient time for their operations to stabilise and generate returns before repayment commenced.

“For me, the solution for SMEs is patient capital,” she said, urging the Central Bank of Nigeria to review prevailing interest rates to make borrowing more affordable.

In his contribution, a former member of the Anambra State House of Assembly and consultant, Charles Ezeani, identified excessive documentation and cumbersome lending procedures as major obstacles preventing rural entrepreneurs from accessing government-backed credit facilities.

Ezeani said many small business owners lacked the technical capacity and resources to satisfy the requirements imposed by commercial banks, even after obtaining preliminary approvals from development finance institutions.

He particularly criticised the lengthy process of obtaining letters of intent from commercial banks under intervention financing arrangements, arguing that the additional requirements often discouraged applicants.

He called for legislation establishing government-backed credit guarantee institutions to reduce the risks faced by banks lending to small businesses, particularly those without conventional collateral.

“Government institutions should have the capacity to give guarantees of almost zero collateral to the downtrodden,” he said.

Ezeani maintained that effective credit guarantee mechanisms, alongside simplified lending procedures, would encourage financial institutions to extend more credit to micro and small enterprises rather than concentrate largely on established businesses and corporate organisations.

The post Abbas urges states to commit N1bn for SMEs appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: …NFF to get $25m yearly from FIFA
description:
Gianni Infantino, FIFA President, says the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) will get $25m yearly from its purse.
According to Infantino: “Investing $25 million in every African country – plus additional funding for CAF – will amount to about $1.5 billion in just four years. That will transform Afri
content:
Gianni Infantino, FIFA President, says the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) will get $25m yearly from its purse.

According to Infantino: “Investing $25 million in every African country – plus additional funding for CAF – will amount to about $1.5 billion in just four years. That will transform African football: better technical centres, better stadiums, better competitions, better youth programmes. With this investment, we can give every African country the chance to compete.”

Infantino spoke on the 2026 World Cup being a major success: “I am friends with world leaders. We organised the World Cup in Russia in 2018, in Qatar in 2022, and in 2026 across three countries. To organise a World Cup today is a very complex venture. It is not something a private organisation can do on its own. You need to collaborate with governments and cultivate relationships with heads of state. The 2026 World Cup was so successful. We always say we want full stadiums and no incidents — and that is exactly what happened.

“I feel vindicated in expanding the World Cup to 48 teams. There is so much potential for football at the top level.

Going to 48 teams, there were critical voices. But look at countries like Cape Verde – many had never heard of them before the World Cup. They came and played very good football.

On going to 64 teams, people are split. I myself am not convinced what is better or worse. We are discussing it with the members. There’s no bad idea.”

The post …NFF to get $25m yearly from FIFA appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: FirstBank donates golf proceeds to Hearts of Gold Children’s Hospice
description:
FirstBank of Nigeria Limited has reaffirmed its commitment to social impact by donating the proceeds raised from its Corporate Golf Challenge for Charity, held at the prestigious Ikoyi Club 1938, to Hearts of Gold Children’s Hospice, a non-governmental organisation.
The tournament, which forms a key
content:
FirstBank of Nigeria Limited has reaffirmed its commitment to social impact by donating the proceeds raised from its Corporate Golf Challenge for Charity, held at the prestigious Ikoyi Club 1938, to Hearts of Gold Children’s Hospice, a non-governmental organisation.

The tournament, which forms a key highlight of the historic 65th FirstBank Lagos Amateur Open Golf Championship, brought together top corporate teams to compete on the greens while driving vital financial support for underserved communities across Nigeria.

Established by Laja Adedoyin, the NGO provides palliative, respite, and emotional care for abandoned children with severe disabilities or life-limiting conditions.

Meanwhile, Enugu-based Michael Isife has claimed the amateur crown of the 65th Lagos Amateur Open Golf Championship, while reigning champion in the professional category, Monday Eze, delivered a composed performance to defend his professional title.

Waking from a slow start, Isife fired from all cylinders for a closing 73 to overcome a 3-shot deficit going to the finals, winning the competition by four shots over hard-fighting Olalere Olakunle, who closed with 80 to duck in the second position.

Lucky Onjefu was further down on the leaderboard, playing 231-gross over 54 holes. Onjefu completed the top three in the gross category.

Eze, who competed alongside other professional golfers, gathered a total of 39 stableford points to top the category, while Kenyan Sam Njoroge, with a score of 35 stableford points, came second. Ikoyi-based Tajudeen Ajayi, with a score of 34-stableponits came third.

The week-long 65th anniversary celebration, held from November 16 to 22 under FirstBank’s First@Sports initiative, featured more than just championship golf. Alongside the main event, the tournament hosted the Search4Stars Caddies Tournament, the Championship Kitty, youth development clinics, and the Corporate Golf Challenge for Charity.

At the closing ceremony, the Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of FirstBank, Olusegun Alebiosu, represented by Nnaemeka Ejeh, Group Executive, Commercial Banking, South of FirstBank, Alebiosu commended the players for their discipline and sportsmanship, reaffirming the bank’s commitment to growing golf and nurturing emerging talent across Nigeria.

The post FirstBank donates golf proceeds to Hearts of Gold Children’s Hospice appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Soname, Ibitoye, others to speak at Oyo Sports Summit 2026
description:
Olanrewaju Agiri, Ibadan
The Oyo State Sports Summit 2026 is set to bring together leading voices across sports administration, athlete development, business, media and investment to explore practical solutions for building a stronger, more sustainable sporting ecosystem in the state.
With the theme
content:
Olanrewaju Agiri, Ibadan

The Oyo State Sports Summit 2026 is set to bring together leading voices across sports administration, athlete development, business, media and investment to explore practical solutions for building a stronger, more sustainable sporting ecosystem in the state.

With the theme “Beyond the Podium: People. Performance. Progress. Legacy”, the summit reflects the organisers’ vision of repositioning sports beyond competition and medals, towards an industry driven by people, opportunity, infrastructure, investment, professional development and long-term impact.

Scheduled to be held on December 2, 2026, at Mauve 21, Ring Road, Ibadan, the summit will feature three major panel discussions addressing some of the critical issues shaping the future of sports: athlete welfare and performance pathways; facilities, grassroots development and access; and financing and growing the sports economy.

The organisers believe that unlocking Oyo State’s sporting potential requires a deliberate approach that connects talent development with the right support systems, investment, infrastructure, access and professional opportunities.

The first panel session, “Athlete Welfare and the Performance Pathway,” will feature Dr. Yusuf Alli, Segun Ajose, Dr. Falade Babatunde and Bayo Adigun.

The session will examine the athlete’s journey beyond the field of play, with discussions focusing on welfare, career development, professional opportunities, talent identification, performance support and the transition from active sports to life after competition.

At the heart of this conversation is the need to create a sporting environment where athletes are not only discovered and developed but adequately supported to achieve their potential and build sustainable careers.

Athlete welfare remains a crucial component of sporting success, encompassing access to appropriate support systems, career guidance, development opportunities and planning for life beyond active competition. The panel is expected to explore how stakeholders can contribute to a more structured performance pathway that prioritises the athlete as a person while pursuing excellence in competition.

The second panel, “Facilities, Grassroots Development & Access,” will feature Hon. Kunle Soname, Prof. Oladipupo Oladele, Dr. Adesoji Taiwo and Barr. Damola Awosika.

The discussion will focus on sports infrastructure, grassroots talent development, access to sporting facilities, community participation and sustainable pathways for emerging athletes.

Grassroots sports remain the foundation of talent discovery and the development of a sporting culture. However, the ability of young people to participate, develop and progress is often shaped by access to quality facilities, organised programmes, coaching, competitions and supportive communities.

The panel will explore how infrastructure and grassroots systems can be strengthened to create more opportunities for participation and talent development, while addressing the need for sustainable access to sporting facilities beyond major urban centres and elite sporting environments.

The broader objective is to stimulate conversations on building accessible, functional and sustainable sports structures that allow young talents to emerge and progress through clearly defined pathways.

The third panel discussion, “Financing and Growing the Sports Ecoomy,” will feature Toyin Ibitoye, Kehinde Ssports, Femi Abegunde and Sulaimon Adebayo (POOJA).

The session will address sports investment, private-sector participation, sponsorship, sports business, commercialisation, revenue generation and the development of a sustainable sports economy.

As sports continues to evolve into a major economic and commercial sector globally, the panel will explore how Oyo State can better position itself to attract investment, develop commercially viable sports properties, create business opportunities and unlock value across different areas of the industry.

Discussions are expected to examine the role of businesses, brands, investors, promoters, sports organisations and other stakeholders in creating a more financially sustainable ecosystem capable of supporting athletes, competitions, facilities and sports-related enterprises.

The focus is on exploring ways sports can become not only a platform for recreation and competition but also a viable contributor to economic development, employment, tourism and enterprise.

The organisers’ vision for the summit is anchored on the belief that meaningful sports development requires collaboration across sectors. Government, private investors, sports administrators, athletes, media, community organisations and technical professionals all have roles to play in shaping the future of sports.

The summit is therefore designed not merely as a gathering of stakeholders but as a platform for exchanging ideas, identifying opportunities, challenging existing approaches and encouraging conversations that can translate into action.

As part of the event, an Award of Recognition will also be presented to celebrate individuals making outstanding contributions to sports and inspiring the next generation.

The recognition is intended to acknowledge the dedication, commitment and impact of people contributing to sports development, including those whose work in nurturing talent, creating opportunities and strengthening the sporting community deserves to be celebrated.

While the award provides an opportunity to honour excellence, the central focus of the summit remains on conversations, collaboration and the future of sports development in Oyo State.

The Oyo State Sports Summit 2026 is supported by DNIpay, Tripdey, iFitness, Item7go, the Oyo State Government, LS Foundation, Badig and Blaze Lighting and Effects.

Event collaborators and creative partners include Nexora Events and Production, Design Loft, TimiAkindele Photography and AI Creavis, whose contributions support the execution, creative direction, production and visibility of the summit.

Their involvement reflects the importance of partnerships and collective support in bringing stakeholders together and advancing conversations around sports development.

title: Fury reveals schizophrenia diagnosis ahead of Joshua clash
description:
Tyson Fury has said he was diagnosed with schizophrenia soon after his world title win over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015.
“Words can’t explain the darkness I was in,” said the heavyweight boxer. “It was like a living version of the pits of hell.
“I thought I would end up in a padded room with the door
content:
Tyson Fury has said he was diagnosed with schizophrenia soon after his world title win over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015.

“Words can’t explain the darkness I was in,” said the heavyweight boxer. “It was like a living version of the pits of hell.

“I thought I would end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.

“The anxiety was crippling me. I just could not overcome it and that’s when I went and saw the psychiatrist down in London.”

Fury has made the revelations about his mental health in a documentary which will be released by Netflix on Friday.

The 38-year-old is preparing for the long-awaited all-British heavyweight fight against Anthony Joshua, a fellow former world champion, in Cardiff on December 11 — a bout that will be broadcast live on Netflix.

Fury recalled hearing the radio talking to him, and begging wife Paris to get him out of the hospital because “the Illuminati” wanted him.

Following his victory over Klitschko, Fury gained weight and struggled with alcohol and drug addiction.

“It got that bad I was hearing voices in my mind,” he said. “I wouldn’t be able to sit and have a conversation because I’d be hearing stuff in my mind.

“I didn’t know where to turn and no-one knew what to do. I really needed help, or check into rehab or something. I never got a break from it for years. I wanted to be what I thought was normal again.”

After Fury was released from hospital, a diagnosis of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder was confirmed.

Fury said a turning point in his life came when he was on a night out for Halloween in 2017.

“I looked around and could see all the young people and I thought, ‘I had the world in my hands and I threw it all away, and now I’m a fat mess addicted to alcohol’,” he said.

But Fury added he channelled his disgust into a comeback which led him to return to training, focus more on his family and claim another world title when he beat Deontay Wilder in 2020.

title: Dangote wins Awolowo leadership prize
description:
The Obafemi Awolowo Foundation has named Africa’s richest industrialist, Aliko Dangote, as the recipient of its 2026 Obafemi Awolowo Prize for Leadership, recognising his contributions to industrialisation, entrepreneurship and economic development across the continent.
The Foundation also announced
content:
The Obafemi Awolowo Foundation has named Africa’s richest industrialist, Aliko Dangote, as the recipient of its 2026 Obafemi Awolowo Prize for Leadership, recognising his contributions to industrialisation, entrepreneurship and economic development across the continent.

The Foundation also announced technology entrepreneur and Future Africa founder, Iyinoluwa Aboyeji, as the inaugural recipient of its Obafemi Awolowo Sectoral Leadership Award in Corporate Governance and Social Responsibility.

In a statement signed by its Executive Director, Ambassador Olatokunbo Awolowo Dosumu, and obtained by The PUNCH on Monday, the Foundation said Dangote was selected following a rigorous process involving public nominations, screening, verification and evaluation by a committee chaired by former Commonwealth Secretary-General, Chief Emeka Anyaoku.

It said the committee recognised Dangote’s decades of investments in manufacturing, cement production, fertiliser, petroleum refining and other strategic sectors, noting that his business activities had helped expand Africa’s productive capacity and advance economic self-reliance.

The Foundation said the committee also considered his philanthropic interventions through the Aliko Dangote Foundation, particularly in education, healthcare and social welfare.

It singled out his educational initiative launched in 2026, which is designed to support 45,000 students initially, with an ambition to extend the programme to 1.3 million students by 2035.

The initiative focuses on science, technology, engineering and mathematics, narrowing the gender gap in literacy, teacher development and improving the transition from education to employment.

Quoting Dangote’s description of the intervention as a “strategic investment”, the Foundation said his commitment to education aligned with the philosophy of the late Chief Obafemi Awolowo, who regarded human capital development as fundamental to national progress.

It also cited his declaration that, “Every child we keep in school strengthens our economy. Every student we support reduces inequality.”

According to the Foundation, the selection committee considered Dangote’s combination of enterprise, industrial transformation and commitment to human development a demonstration of leadership whose impact transcended individual achievement.

The award, established in 2012, is conferred biennially in honour of the late Awolowo, the first Premier of the Western Region, whose administration was associated with landmark investments in education, healthcare and rural development.

The Foundation said the prize was designed to recognise individuals whose leadership reflected the late statesman’s values of integrity, vision, courage, discipline, accountability and people-centred governance.

Dangote will receive the award on March 6, 2027, at a ceremony marking the anniversary of Awoloww’s birth. He is also expected to deliver the Obafemi Awolowo Prize for Leadership Lecture, in keeping with the award’s tradition.

Meanwhile, the Foundation said the newly introduced Sectoral Leadership Awards would complement its flagship prize by recognising outstanding contributions in specific areas of national development.

The awards cover four broad categories: Politics and Governance; Corporate Governance and Social Responsibility; Educational Transformation; and People-Centred Advocacy and Support for the Underprivileged.

Aboyeji was named the inaugural recipient in the Corporate Governance and Social Responsibility category for his contributions to entrepreneurship, innovation and economic empowerment.

title: NFF President: Sadi, Oyekanmi, other Kaduna legends want Akwuegbu
description:
Oladunni Oyekanmi and Dahiru Sadi are the latest ex-Nigeria internationals who have thrown their weight behind Benedict Akwuegbu to become the next president of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF).
Oyekanmi and Sadi, on behalf of Kaduna football legends, declared the former RC Lens and AZ Alkmaar
content:
Oladunni Oyekanmi and Dahiru Sadi are the latest ex-Nigeria internationals who have thrown their weight behind Benedict Akwuegbu to become the next president of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF).

Oyekanmi and Sadi, on behalf of Kaduna football legends, declared the former RC Lens and AZ Alkmaar record goal scorer, Akwuegbu, as the most qualified ex-footballer to head the NFF. Both veterans and other Kaduna-based legends, including Abubakar Balarabe, Abubakar Aliu, Gidi Mohammed, Tunde Abdulraman, Alhaji Aminu, Jamilu Uje, and Kabiru Aso, among several others, last Sunday formally endorsed Akwuegbu for the NFF top seat.

Oyekanmi said Kaduna Legends see Akwuegbu as the right man to lead Nigerian football out of the wilderness.

“He (Akwuegbu) is the choice of all of us, and Kaduna Legends will seek the support of other stakeholders across the country to ensure that he emerges as the next NFF president. Akwuegbu is tested and trusted, besides being a successful player.

“Akwuegbu is sound, trustworthy, and disciplined. He is well educated, apart from being a successful club owner. He knows where the shoe pinches. We believe it’s time for ex-players to take over the administration of Nigerian football, hence our endorsement of the Austrian Bomber”.

Dahiru Sadi added that Kaduna Legends endorsed Akwuegbu because he has the pedigree. He said the former Super Eagles’ attacker, who played at the Africa Cup of Nations and FIFA World Cup, needs the support of those who want proper repositioning of Nigerian football.

“Kaduna Legends believe in him, and he will take us to the promised land. He is not an ordinary Nigerian but one who whole-heartedlly served the country. He is still ready to serve; hence we are giving him our total support. It’s our chance to bring out the very best to run Nigerian football,” said the former midfield maestro.

Estevao, 19, has played a bit-part role for Chelsea so far this season, following the summer appointment of Xabi Alonso, and he has been heavily linked with an exit over the past few weeks.

The Blues hierarchy have no interest in selling Estevao next year, and with his current contract not due to expire until 2033, they remain in a strong negotiating position to rebuff any offers from PSG.

description:

The 33-year-old Congolese fighter replaces Australian Jai Opetaia, who withdrew after aggravating a hand injury in training.
Scotland-based B
content:
Heavyweight Martin Bakole will face former world champion Deontay Wilder on the undercard of Tyson Fury’s fight with Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on 11 December.

The 33-year-old Congolese fighter replaces Australian Jai Opetaia, who withdrew after aggravating a hand injury in training.

Scotland-based Bakole had been scheduled to fight unbeaten Nigerian Solomon Adebayo on the bill, but will instead face 41-year-old Wilder in the co-main event.

Bakole suffered a second-round knockout defeat by Joseph Parker in February 2025, having accepted the fight on just two days’ notice.

He then fought to a majority draw with Nigerian Efe Ajagba in May 2025 and has not competed since.

Former WBC heavyweight champion Wilder, who has 43 knockouts in 45 victories, is looking to build on his split-decision win over Britain’s Derek Chisora in April.

Unbeaten cruiserweight Opetaia, 31, was set to make his heavyweight debut against Wilder but pulled out of the contest last week.

Several British heavyweights, including Chisora, Richard Riakporhe, Frazer Clarke and Johnny Fisher had expressed an interest in facing Wilder following Opetaia’s withdrawal.

content:
Nigeria-born Ghanaian Ubiedi Stanley topped the Masters category with 16 wins and a +426 spread at the maiden Festus Osifo Foundation National Scrabble Classics in Benin City.

The two-day tournament, held November 21–22, 2026, in partnership with the Nigeria Scrabble Federation, drew nearly 300 players and enthusiasts. Participants came from the United Kingdom, the United States, Ghana and other countries, and the event is now billed as the biggest Scrabble tournament in Nigeria.

Other champions were Kelvin Ekeh (Intermediate), Ukpe Victor (Opens) and Humble Isaac (Youth U16).

The prize package was among the tournament’s biggest draws. The Masters winner took home $3,000, the Intermediate champion $2,000 and the Opens winner $1,000. The Youth champion received ₦500,000 and a laptop, while about ₦14 million in extra prizes was shared among other winners.

Off the board, the Gala Night kept guests entertained with comedy, live music and a magic show.

With its large turnout, international field and rich prizes, the first edition has raised the bar for Scrabble events in Nigeria and set the stage for future editions.

title: Alcaraz rakes €4,7m at 2026 ATP Finals

content:
Carlos Alcaraz left Turin with the entire prize money thanks to his undefeated record. This means taking home the largest cash prize in tennis history, amounting to $5,171,000 (€4,714,282), in addition to 1,500 ranking points that put him in a good position to overtake Jannik Sinner during the upcoming Australian Open and potentially surpass Alexander Zverev at the Masters 1000 tournaments in Indian Wells and Miami in March.

The largest sum Alcaraz had earned to date was the €4,291,770 he received as the winner of the 2015 US Open . Throughout his career, he has accumulated €66,766,671, placing him fifth on the all-time earnings list. Ahead of him are  Novak Djokovic, Rafael Nadal, Roger Federer, and Alexander Zverev . His ATP Finals title allows him to climb one position and surpass Sinner in total earnings.

Zverev, the loser in the Turin final, takes home  $2,759,000 (€2,513,893) and 1,000 points, further cementing his position at the top of the rankings.

title: INEC selects 17,676 polling units for mock BVAS exercise
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has selected 17,676 polling units across the country for its nationwide mock accreditation and electronic result upload exercise scheduled for Saturday, November 28, ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The commission said the exercise would cover two po
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has selected 17,676 polling units across the country for its nationwide mock accreditation and electronic result upload exercise scheduled for Saturday, November 28, ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The commission said the exercise would cover two polling units in each of the 8,838 Registration Areas nationwide and run from 8:30 am to 2:30 pm.

INEC announced this in a post on its X handle on Monday, directing political parties, stakeholders and members of the public to its website to access the list of selected polling units.

The exercise is aimed at testing the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, assessing accreditation procedures and identifying possible technical challenges before the 2027 general elections.

In its announcement, the commission said, “INEC will conduct a nationwide Mock Accreditation and Result Upload Exercise using the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) on Saturday, 28 November 2026, from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m.

“The exercise is designed to test BVAS functionality, assess accreditation procedures and identify possible technical issues ahead of the 2027 General Elections.

“It will take place in two Polling Units in each of the 8,838 Registration Areas nationwide.”

INEC also provided a link to the list of selected polling units, urging stakeholders and interested members of the public to consult its website for details.

The total of 17,676 polling units was arrived at by multiplying the 8,838 Registration Areas by the two polling units selected in each area.

The announcement comes amid concerns among political stakeholders over the time available to prepare for the exercise.

The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council had, on November 18, called on INEC to postpone the exercise, arguing that the short notice given to political parties could undermine their participation.

The council described the preparation timeline as inadequate and urged the commission to reschedule the exercise to enable political parties to make the necessary arrangements and participate meaningfully.

However, INEC’s latest announcement indicates that preparations for the mock exercise are proceeding towards the November 28 date.

The exercise is expected to provide an opportunity for the commission to assess the performance of its BVAS technology and electronic result transmission procedures ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Meanwhile, in a separate development, INEC disclosed that between 75 and 80 per cent of its BVAS devices, representing 186,277 machines, had been deployed to states ahead of the 2027 elections.

title: Dangote IPO: SEC approves share allocation after 300% subscription
description:
The Securities and Exchange Commission has approved the share allocation plan for Dangote Petroleum Refinery’s heavily oversubscribed initial public offering, clearing a major hurdle for the $20bn facility’s anticipated stock market debut later this month.
The approval, granted on Monday, followed w
content:
The Securities and Exchange Commission has approved the share allocation plan for Dangote Petroleum Refinery’s heavily oversubscribed initial public offering, clearing a major hurdle for the $20bn facility’s anticipated stock market debut later this month.

The approval, granted on Monday, followed weeks of waiting by investors who participated in the offer, which attracted subscriptions estimated at three times its original size.

A Reuters report on Monday, quoting three people familiar with the matter, said the regulatory clearance would allow Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE to proceed with the allocation of shares and final preparations for its listing on the Nigerian Exchange.

The report read, “The Nigeria’s Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday approved Dangote Refinery’s plan for allocating shares in its heavily oversubscribed initial public offering that closed last month, three ‌people familiar with the matter said.”

The report added that the refinery is also seeking the commission’s approval to increase the size of the offer by up to 30 per cent to accommodate the overwhelming demand from investors.

The proposed expansion would enable the company to accommodate more investors and raise additional capital from the public, although the regulator’s approval of the share allocation does not necessarily mean the proposed increase has also been cleared.

The Dangote Group spokesperson declined to comment on the development, while the SEC could not immediately be reached for a response.

The IPO represents a significant step in the refinery’s ownership structure, as Africa’s richest man, Aliko Dangote, seeks to broaden public participation in the business and allow ordinary Nigerians to own stakes in one of the country’s biggest industrial investments.

Dangote has repeatedly described the share offer as a “people’s IPO”, arguing that it would give Nigerians an opportunity to participate in the refinery’s growth and financial success.

The offer was structured to accommodate small investors, with individuals able to purchase as few as 10 shares through fintech companies and other digital investment platforms. The minimum investment was put at about $4, making the offer accessible to retail investors who might otherwise be unable to participate in a major industrial investment.

The strong demand for the shares underscores investor interest in the refinery, which has become a major player in Nigeria’s petroleum products market since commencing operations in 2024.

Built at an estimated cost of $20bn on the outskirts of Lagos, the 700,000-barrel-per-day facility was designed to reduce Nigeria’s dependence on imported refined petroleum products, strengthen domestic supply and position the country as a regional energy hub.

Its operations have increasingly attracted international attention, particularly amid supply disruptions associated with the Iran war, which have affected global petroleum markets and created opportunities for the refinery to expand its exports.

The facility has benefited from increased demand for its products, including jet fuel, which it has supplied to markets in Western Europe as disruptions to international supplies intensified.

The refinery is also pursuing an ambitious expansion programme that could double its processing capacity to 1.4 million barrels per day by 2029.

Beyond its proposed Nigerian listing, Dangote has indicated that the refinery business could pursue a secondary listing in the United States within the next three to four years, potentially widening its access to international investors and capital markets.

title: Two Nigerians qualify for African mountain biking championships
description:
Mary Samuel and Fanen Rumun have secured Nigeria’s places in the women’s and men’s events at the 2027 African Mountain Bike Championships after emerging winners at the Abuja Chaingang Mountain Bike Festival.
The duo claimed the Cross-Country Olympic (XCO) titles at the competition held on Sunday at
content:
Mary Samuel and Fanen Rumun have secured Nigeria’s places in the women’s and men’s events at the 2027 African Mountain Bike Championships after emerging winners at the Abuja Chaingang Mountain Bike Festival.

The duo claimed the Cross-Country Olympic (XCO) titles at the competition held on Sunday at Sunrise Hills, behind Sunrise Waterpark, Asokoro, Abuja.

Samuel won the women’s race after completing four laps in one hour and one minute, finishing ahead of Comfort Inyang, who clocked one hour and 11 minutes. Suzy Angmun placed third in one hour and 24 minutes.

In the men’s category, Rumun emerged victorious after covering seven laps in one hour, 26 minutes and 43 seconds.

Ateba Ndi finished second in one hour, 31 minutes and 20 seconds, while Berry Monday took third place in one hour, 36 minutes and 17 seconds.

The victories earned Samuel and Rumun qualification for the continental championship scheduled to hold in Lusaka, Zambia, in April 2027.

The women’s race featured three cyclists, while 18 riders competed in the men’s event.

Samuel described the course as challenging, citing its hills, descents and narrow sections, but said determination helped her secure the victory.

“The race was tough because of the hills, descents and narrow roads, but you just have to keep pushing and give thanks to God,” she said.

She also urged aspiring cyclists to remain committed to the sport despite the challenges involved.

The two-day festival, organised by Abuja Chaingang Cycling Club in collaboration with the Cycling Federation of Nigeria, also featured the Cross-Country Short Circuit race, trail running, hiking and other outdoor activities.
