title: APC disowns fake letter asking INEC to guarantee Tinubu’s victory
description:
The All Progressives Congress has disowned a purported letter allegedly written by its National Chairman, Prof Nentawe Yilwatda, to the Independent National Electoral Commission, urging the electoral body to ensure President Bola Tinubu’s victory in the 2027 presidential election.
In a statement on
content:
The All Progressives Congress has disowned a purported letter allegedly written by its National Chairman, Prof Nentawe Yilwatda, to the Independent National Electoral Commission, urging the electoral body to ensure President Bola Tinubu’s victory in the 2027 presidential election.

In a statement on Monday, the APC National Chairman’s Special Adviser on Media and Information Strategy, Abimbola Tooki, described the letter, which circulated on social media, as fake, malicious and a desperate attempt to tarnish the image of the party’s leadership and undermine democratic institutions.

A purported letter dated November 22, 2026, and addressed to INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, allegedly by APC National Chairman, Prof. Yilwatda, sought the electoral commission’s cooperation ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

The unsigned document claimed that the APC leadership expected INEC to deploy its administrative and operational mechanisms to ensure President Bola Tinubu’s declaration as the winner of the 2027 presidential election.

Reacting, the APC said the document was neither authored by Yilwatda nor issued by his office, insisting that it was inconsistent with the party’s established communication procedures.

The statement read in part, “The All Progressives Congress has condemned in the strongest possible terms a purported letter circulating on social media, allegedly written by the National Chairman of the party, Professor Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda, to the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, titled ‘Preparations for the 2027 Presidential Election and Ensuring the Victory of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.’

“The unsigned letter, dated November 22, 2026, contains an outrageous and entirely fabricated claim that the APC leadership expects INEC to deploy its institutional mechanisms, administrative frameworks and operational capacities to ensure the declaration of President Bola Tinubu as the winner of the 2027 presidential election.

“The party categorically states that the purported letter did not emanate from Professor Yilwatda, was not authored by him, and has absolutely nothing to do with the National Chairman or his office. It is a fraudulent document, a malicious fabrication and a reckless attempt to impugn the integrity of the National Chairman, the APC and the democratic process.”

The APC said the absence of a signature or authentication on the purported letter exposed its fraudulent nature, alleging that it was deliberately circulated to mislead the public and tarnish the image of its National Chairman.

The party also faulted the document for violating its established communication procedures, insisting that a letter of such significance could not have been issued outside its official channels.

It added, “The APC will not allow faceless individuals, political mischief-makers and purveyors of fabricated information to drag its leadership into disrepute through the circulation of fictitious documents.

“We condemn the author of this despicable letter in the strongest possible terms and challenge those responsible to come out of hiding, take ownership of their actions and provide verifiable evidence for their claims, rather than hiding behind anonymity to spread falsehoods and create distrust in democratic institutions.

“For the avoidance of doubt, the APC remains firmly committed to a peaceful, transparent, free and fair electoral process in the forthcoming 2027 general elections. Our party believes in the sanctity of the ballot, the independence of INEC and the right of Nigerians to freely choose their leaders without intimidation, manipulation or interference.

“President Bola Ahmed Tinubu himself has consistently demonstrated his commitment to democratic principles. At campaign rallies and public engagements across the country, the President has repeatedly urged Nigerians, particularly eligible voters, to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards and exercise their civic responsibility.

“This is a clear demonstration of his confidence in the democratic process and his belief that electoral legitimacy must come from the will of the people, freely expressed through the ballot.”

The APC National Chairman urged Nigerians and the media to disregard the purported letter, insisting that the party remained committed to democratic values, peaceful elections and respect for electoral institutions.

The party said it would approach the 2027 elections with confidence and discipline, stressing that electoral victory must be earned through the support and mandate of Nigerians.

The post APC disowns fake letter asking INEC to guarantee Tinubu’s victory appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: Police must be fair, neutral
description:
WITH assurances from Inspector-General of Police Olatunji Disu that the Force is ready to deliver a successful 2027 general election, Nigerians should join efforts to make the country’s polls safer, better, and more credible.
The police remain the most critical stakeholder in the electoral ecosystem
content:
WITH assurances from Inspector-General of Police Olatunji Disu that the Force is ready to deliver a successful 2027 general election, Nigerians should join efforts to make the country’s polls safer, better, and more credible.

The police remain the most critical stakeholder in the electoral ecosystem of a developing democracy where election management is hugely manual, and institutions are weak.

Consequently, a lot depends on the police for the country to achieve electoral propriety.

Indeed, police weakness has plagued elections throughout Nigeria’s political trajectory. This institutional deficiency has deepened human, procedural, and operational issues in the pre- and post-election altercations.

The forthcoming 2027 general elections are no different. Apprehension is in the air, as the polity is already tainted by threats and mutual suspicion.

Therefore, all eyes are on the Nigeria Police Force to turn over a new leaf.

“So far so good, we are not afraid. We are confident that even if the elections start tomorrow, the Nigerian Police Force is ready to do what is expected of the Force,” Disu told a delegation led by the Head of the United Nations Office for West Africa and the Sahel.

“We are ever ready to go, and we want to assure you that Nigerians will not be disappointed with the activities of the Nigerian Police Force in the election.”

By rhetoric and administration, Disu may be right. But prosecuting a peaceful election that has carried the usual violent undertones goes beyond that. It involves radical courage, sincerity, and transparency.

The IG’s predecessors had promised Nigerians free, fair, credible and peaceful elections since 1999 but delivered little.

Under IG Mohammed Adamu, 323 offenders were arrested during the 2019 general elections, but only a few were prosecuted.

In the 2023 elections overseen by IG Usman Baba, 781 offenders were apprehended, without meaningful prosecution.

During the Osun governorship election held under Disu on August 15, 293 of the 295 arrests made were released on bail after screening. The election consumed 30 lives.

In the build-up to the Osun governorship election and the 2027 polls, the police were lackadaisical about the politicians’ threats of killings, cutting off fingers, expulsion of the people from their communities, violence and suppression in Osun, Borno, and Abuja.

Five days after the Osun governorship election, the convoy of the state governor, Ademola Adeleke, was shot at Osogbo after a visit to the Ataoja, the paramount ruler in the state capital. Two people were killed on August 24 at Ikire in Irewole LGA of the state. Two police officers sustained injuries while a patrol vehicle belonging to the Ikire Police Division and an AK-47 service rifle was snatched from the police.

In past elections, the police practically looked helpless as politicians engaged in vote-buying, rigging, abetting and other fraudulent acts.

During the November 11, 2023 off-cycle governorship elections in Imo State, YIAGA reported, “In many instances, security agencies were complicit, as observed in several viral videos, while compromising their duties of ensuring credible elections. By that, they aided and abetted the massive rigging as witnessed in the Imo election.”

Over 800 people were killed in the 2011 post-election violence in the North.

This is the police Disu inherited.

Disu therefore requires a large dose of courage and a change of tactics.

The ball is in IGP Disu’s court.

The IG should read the riot act to his officers and lead the vanguard from the front.

One of the ways for the police to demonstrate that they mean business is to arrest and prosecute the politicians threatening the people with death, expulsion, and suppression.

The Force should deepen its intelligence network to arrest and prosecute politicians engaging in vote-buying. Indeed, the IG must come up with a strong strategy for unearthing and arresting politicians and their cronies engaging in vote-buying at the polls.

All the electoral offenders in police custody must be prosecuted forthwith to serve as a deterrent to the others.

The final word: The 2027 general elections are as good as the police make them.

The post 2027: Police must be fair, neutral appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Joshua talks retirement ahead Fury fight
description:
Anthony Joshua has admitted that retirement is close, with barely three weeks left before his fight against Tyson Fury.

content:
Anthony Joshua has admitted that retirement is close, with barely three weeks left before his fight against Tyson Fury.

“When am I going to retire? Pretty soon,” Joshua told The Sun.

“I am getting old now. From an athlete’s point of view, I am getting old. Maybe that will be our next sit-down when we talk about plans for after boxing, because that will be coming around pretty soon. I have not got many years ahead of me.”

The 37-year-old turned professional in 2013 after a successful amateur career that included Olympic gold, and later became a unified world champion.

His career has, however, been through a difficult period since 2019, with two losses to Oleksandr Usyk and a knockout defeat by Daniel Dubois after he had regained his titles from Andy Ruiz Jr.

In July, Joshua stopped Albania’s Kristian Prenga in the second round in Jeddah, but he was dropped twice in the first round by the 35-year-old.

Joshua also lost two close friends and team members, Sina Ghami and Latif Ayodele, in a road accident in Nigeria in December last year. His uncle, Adedamola Joshua, told PUNCH Sports Extra that the family was happy about the retirement talk.

“Each time he is knocked down, it is just like the heart is coming out of our chest,” the uncle said.

“Now that he has said that he is leaving while the ovation is highest, we are happy.”

Joshua is reportedly set to earn nearly $100m for the Fury fight. His promoter, Eddie Hearn, has said, “Probably 2026 will be his last year in the sport.”

Joshua has dropped similar hints before, though, and Fury himself returned five times after announcing his retirement.

title: Why many Nigerians relocate: My baptism of fire in Canada
description: My baptism of fire as President of the Association of Nigerians in Nova Scotia, Canada, came in April 2024, the same week I assumed office. Some Nigerian students at Cape Breton University in Sydney, Nova Scotia, were travelling from Halifax to Sydney when their vehicle was involved in a serious acc
content:
My baptism of fire as President of the Association of Nigerians in Nova Scotia, Canada, came in April 2024, the same week I assumed office. Some Nigerian students at Cape Breton University in Sydney, Nova Scotia, were travelling from Halifax to Sydney when their vehicle was involved in a serious accident. The journey takes over four hours by road. Some students live in Halifax because it offers more employment opportunities, and they arrange group transportation to attend classes and examinations in Sydney.

It was examination time. Their vehicle was 15 minutes away from Sydney, and daybreak was still a while away. Then their vehicle collided with an oncoming vehicle. Some of the occupants sustained minor injuries, but one Nigerian student was critically injured. Within a short time, an air ambulance had arrived to evacuate him for urgent medical attention.

As officials of the Nigerian association, we swung into action to provide whatever assistance we could. His church was making efforts to help, while his university was also involved. I was particularly worried. Having just assumed office, I was praying that our tenure would not begin with bereavement within our community.

As healthcare professionals battled to save his life, Cape Breton University facilitated arrangements to bring his wife and children from Nigeria to be with him. When they arrived in Halifax, we went to the airport to receive them at about 2am and drive them to their accommodation, thanks to the commitment of our fantastic brother, Oloruntoyin Balogun.

Eventually, our compatriot was removed from the danger list. We heaved a sigh of relief and thanked God for his survival and the swift emergency response in Nova Scotia.

Why am I telling this story? None of the students involved was a Canadian citizen. The critically injured student was neither a permanent resident nor someone with political connections in Canada. He was an international student carrying a Nigerian passport. Yet, when his life was threatened, the emergency services responded without making his nationality or immigration status the issue.

That experience has remained with me. That is not to say that emergency services in Canada don’t have shortcomings, which include ambulance delays and overstretched hospitals. But there is an established system in charge of responding to people in danger, regardless of their nationality. The student did not need to know a governor, senator or minister before an air ambulance came to his rescue.

Whenever I remember that incident and compare it with what happens in Nigeria, I feel sad. Recall what happened to Nollywood actor Junior Pope Odonwodo on April 10, 2024, the same period as this case. He and four others died after a boat accident during a film production on the River Niger. The subsequent investigation by the Nigeria Safety Investigation Bureau revealed that the boat operator was uncertified, the vessel was unregistered, and the rescue operation was not timely because trained divers were unavailable. Junior Pope’s story was actually the incident that made me draft this piece in April 2024 and keep it in the cooler since then.

Junior Pope was a popular actor, yet that could not protect him from a system in which basic safety precautions were neglected. Imagine the chances of an ordinary Nigerian whose name nobody recognises. We may never know whether faster intervention would have saved him or any of the other victims. What we know is that the arrangements that should have reduced the risk and improved their chances of survival were inadequate.

Then came the December 29, 2025 accident involving former world heavyweight boxing champion Anthony Joshua on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. Joshua survived with minor injuries, but two of his close friends and team members, Sina Ghami and Latif Ayodele, died when their vehicle collided with a stationary truck. Joshua received medical attention and was discharged two days later. The accident again exposed the dangers on Nigerian roads, where stationary heavy vehicles, reckless driving and weak enforcement continue to claim lives.

In 2024 alone, the Federal Road Safety Corps recorded 5,421 deaths in 9,570 road crashes across Nigeria. These were not merely figures for an annual report. They represented fathers, mothers, children and breadwinners whose absence changed families permanently. Yet, how many of our major highways have emergency medical services capable of reaching critically injured passengers quickly and transporting them to properly equipped trauma centres?

The same disregard for human life is evident in our response to insecurity. On Christmas Eve in 2023, armed attackers descended on communities in Bokkos and Barkin Ladi local government areas of Plateau State. According to Amnesty International, more than 190 people were killed, while the attackers moved between villages for over 48 hours. Amnesty questioned the failure of security agencies to halt the killings even after the attacks had continued for hours.

Imagine that. Human beings were being slaughtered, houses were burning, and families were fleeing for their lives while the violence continued from one community to another. Similar questions have followed attacks by Boko Haram, bandits and other armed groups across northern Nigeria. In some communities, residents have learnt that surviving an attack may depend more on their ability to escape than on the timely arrival of security personnel.

We cannot claim that Nigeria lacks courageous doctors, nurses, emergency workers or security officers. Many work under appalling conditions and risk their lives to save others. The problem is that individual courage cannot compensate for an unreliable system. An ambulance without equipment, a hospital without essential supplies, or a security post without the means to respond quickly offers little reassurance to someone facing death.

Life abroad is not all rosy. No sane person who enjoys the warmth, familiar food, communal relationships and sunshine of Nigeria would ordinarily be eager to exchange them for the freezing winters and often lonely lifestyle of Canada, the United States, Britain or Australia. The decision is even more painful for someone who has built a successful career and strong relationships in Nigeria.

Yet many Nigerians make that decision because they want assurance that their lives and their families’ lives will matter in an emergency. They want to know that when they dial an emergency number, somebody will respond. They want their children to attend school without the fear of abduction and their relatives to travel without wondering whether help will arrive if disaster strikes.

Nigeria has the resources and human talent to build such a society. What has been missing is political commitment, reinforced by a culture in which public office is treated as an opportunity for personal enrichment. Worse still, many citizens defend the politicians responsible for these failures because they share the same ethnic identity, religion or political party. Ironically, many of such defenders live in countries where politicians perform much better than their Nigerian counterparts but are still vilified for issues that will be considered inconsequential in Nigeria.

I will always remember that Nigerian student whose life was saved in Nova Scotia. He had no Canadian passport, no permanent residence and no political influence. Yet, when his life hung in the balance, the system responded. Until Nigeria learns to treat the life of an unknown citizen with the same urgency it accords the security and comfort of its political leaders, Nigerians will continue to seek safety and dignity elsewhere.

— X: @BrandAzuka

The post Why many Nigerians relocate: My baptism of fire in Canada appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: eTranzact boosts shareholder returns with 50k dividend
description:
eTranzact International Plc has recommended a dividend of 50 kobo per share for the 2025 financial year.
The dividend recommendation reflects the company’s commitment to delivering value to shareholders while sustaining growth and improving profitability.
The payment solutions company recorded a pro
content:
eTranzact International Plc has recommended a dividend of 50 kobo per share for the 2025 financial year.

The dividend recommendation reflects the company’s commitment to delivering value to shareholders while sustaining growth and improving profitability.

The payment solutions company recorded a profit before tax of N4.2bn. Its revenue rose by 2.39 per cent to N30.61bn in 2025, compared with N29.89bn recorded in 2024, while profit after tax stood at N2.47bn.

The Chairman, eTranzact, Mr. Wole Abegunde, disclosed the financial performance and dividend recommendation at the company’s Annual General Meeting in Lagos on Thursday.

He assured shareholders that improving profitability would remain a major priority, adding that the company would continue to explore revenue expansion opportunities, strengthen operational efficiency and control costs to maximise shareholder value.

Speaking on the company’s strategic positioning, Abegunde said eTranzact recognised the benefits of strategic alliances and the business opportunities they could create.

He said, “As a company, we fully understand the benefits of strategic alliances and the potential business opportunities these can create. We have fostered new relationships, enhanced and deepened existing ones and explored newer opportunities within our ongoing associations with existing partners. We are positive that our alliances will lead to improved performance in the years ahead.”

According to the 2025 annual report presented at the meeting, a major development during the year was the acquisition of a 56.18 per cent stake in eTranzact by Trademarks Global Concepts Limited.

The shares were transferred by Access Bank Nigeria Plc, Acelerex Holdings and eTranzact Global Limited.

Abegunde expressed optimism that the change in ownership would further strengthen the company’s position in Nigeria’s financial technology sector.

The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of eTranzact, Mr. Olaniyi Toluwalope, said the company expanded its customer and merchant base in 2025 across its switching, card and payment gateway businesses.

He explained that its switching services, which include airtime top-up, funds transfer and bills payment, recorded growth in customer and merchant numbers, including financial institutions, microfinance institutions and other fintech companies.

Toluwalope added that the card switching business gained traction during the year, with infrastructure upgrades opening access to new markets.

The company’s merchant acquiring business also expanded, with more businesses onboarded on the Credo Payment Gateway.

In the public sector, he said Federal Government payments, including salaries for ministries, departments and agencies, contributed significantly to the company’s business performance in 2025.

He added that the deployment of Payoutlet 2.0 to more commercial banks boosted internally generated revenue collections for states using eTranzact’s platform.

Toluwalope said the company onboarded more agents across Nigeria and enhanced its terminal management system to support smoother agency banking transactions.

It also issued more point-of-sale terminals to new merchants, strengthening its merchant transaction business.

He further disclosed that the company revamped and repositioned PocketMoni, its digital banking product, to reach a wider market.

According to him, the platform recorded increases in active users and transactions, with expectations of a more significant contribution to the company’s performance in subsequent years.

The post eTranzact boosts shareholder returns with 50k dividend appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: UBEC official hosts empowerment programme in Lagos
description: The Deputy Executive Secretary of the Universal Basic Education Commission, Olajuwon Akinyemi, has hosted a community empowerment initiative in Agbado-Oke-Odo Local Council Development Area of Lagos State, featuring a football competition, free medical outreach and the distribution of household and
content:
The Deputy Executive Secretary of the Universal Basic Education Commission, Olajuwon Akinyemi, has hosted a community empowerment initiative in Agbado-Oke-Odo Local Council Development Area of Lagos State, featuring a football competition, free medical outreach and the distribution of household and business-support items to residents.

The programme, organised under the theme, “Giving Back to the Community”, brought together sporting activities, healthcare services and an empowerment exercise aimed at supporting residents and promoting grassroots development.

The activities were held at Lemmy Field, Akinola, Aboru, Yana-Ipaja, with the concluding empowerment event taking place on Sunday, November 22.

The sporting activities featured a 2km fitness walk and football competition. The fitness walk and semi-final matches were held on November 14, while the third-place match and final took place on November 20.

A medical outreach followed on November 21, offering residents health and eye examinations as part of efforts to improve access to basic healthcare and encourage early detection of health conditions.

The programme climaxed on Sunday with the empowerment exercise, during which beneficiaries received items including sewing machines, generators, grinding machines, clippers, foodstuffs, chest freezers and other day-to-day items to support their livelihoods and improve their living conditions. In what was described as a super empowerment initiative, a member of the community was gifted a minibus to kick-start a transportation business.

One of the beneficiaries, Adijat Abimbola, who received a sewing machine, said the equipment would directly support her tailoring business.

“This sewing machine will help me a lot in my handwork and I am really grateful to the honourable for this gesture,” she said.

Abimbola commended the organisers for combining the empowerment exercise with sporting and medical activities, noting that residents of different age groups, particularly older people, had benefited from the health and eye examinations.

Another beneficiary, Sumani Olatunji, who received a generator, said he intended to use it at home to improve access to electricity. “I will be using it at home. I am really thankful that they gave me this,” he said.

A third beneficiary, who identified himself simply as Ibrahim, said the chest freezer would support his wife’s frozen-food business by helping to preserve unsold stock and reduce losses.

He explained that his wife often bought frozen food for resale, but leftovers sometimes went bad before they could be sold.

“My wife goes out in the morning to buy frozen foods and sells for hours till evening. Sometimes, we have leftovers which go to waste and reduce profit or even at times leave her at a loss. I believe we can use the freezer in this regard. It will boost our business,” he said.

The PUNCH also spoke with guests at the event, including the Chairman of Onigbongbo Local Council Development Area, Moyo Adebanjo; Tunde Akamo; Remi Durojaiye; Sewanu Amosu; Mosun Shefau; Tijani Olorunwa; and Isiaka Aminu. Traditional rulers were also among those present.

The guests commended the initiative, describing community-based interventions as important contributions to grassroots development. They noted that although the impact of such programmes might take time to become evident, sustained efforts could complement broader government policies and reforms by delivering practical benefits to households and small businesses.

They also encouraged more individuals and organisations with the capacity to support community development to undertake similar initiatives.

The programme’s combination of sports, medical services and material support reflected an approach to community engagement that extended beyond one-off donations, bringing together interventions focused on health, recreation and economic welfare.

Akinyemi hosted the initiative as part of his community engagement activities in Agbado-Oke-Odo.

The post UBEC official hosts empowerment programme in Lagos appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Presidency: Empire-building as enemy of consensus candidate
description: As a young secondary school boy of Ansar-Ud-Deen High School, Ikole Ekiti, Ekiti State (1978-1983), I loved History as a subject, a love the West African Examination Council justified in its exam in 1983. Did I hear you say, “E don tay?” You are right. At the Anglican Grammar School, Ilaro, Ogun Sta
content:
As a young secondary school boy of Ansar-Ud-Deen High School, Ikole Ekiti, Ekiti State (1978-1983), I loved History as a subject, a love the West African Examination Council justified in its exam in 1983. Did I hear you say, “E don tay?” You are right. At the Anglican Grammar School, Ilaro, Ogun State, in 1985, WAEC confirmed that my love for History, along with other art subjects, wasn’t misplaced at all.

I was wildly fascinated by the factors responsible for the rise and fall of old kingdoms and empires in Africa and the incursion of fraudulent European exploiters and missionaries, nicely referred to as explorers. The alternate subject I could have registered for at the time was Government.

I felt Government was too simple. It didn’t offer me the stories of wars and suspense that usually excite young minds; no powerful names like Mansa Kankan Musa of the Mali Empire (reigned 1312—1337); the emergence of a powerful leader like Usman Dan Fodiyo, founder of the Sokoto Caliphate, whose great-great-grandparents migrated from Futa Toro along the Senegal River in the present-day Senegal and settled around Degel in the Gobir emirate in the North; and the Ekiti Parapo wars.

My beloved History equally taught me the origin and growth of the Yoruba Kingdom and the dispersal of the Oduduwa princes to far-flung places, including the Benin Kingdom and Dahomey (Republic of Benin). It brought to light how the Old Oyo Empire and Ilorin fell to the Fulani jihadists and warmongers in the 1830s (no be today) and the incursion of Islam to the fringes of present-day southern Nigeria.

Despite my love for History, I trailed a stubbornly-good Joseph Omolade, a classmate at AUD, to the finish line (the mock exam), where he led yours truly by half a mark (85 vs 85.5 percent). If it’s not painful, I won’t be telling you 43 years later.

Omolade’s sit-tight domination was not the only painful part in my final year at the AUD in 1983, a particularly troublesome set, hated by seniors, feared by juniors and troubled by teachers. I wasn’t really a person of particular concern in a set where you had students like Oscar Lee, who almost beat up the vice principal; Ballo, a leader of a partying gang who would normally play music while reading; and Kurry, who always chewed bitter kola to suppress other substances in his system which I don’t need to mention here.

As troublesome as he was, Oscar Lee still remembered my fine handwriting (a few actually referred to it as a printing press) over 40 years after our exit from AUD, Only the Best. What’s your own school’s motto jare?

Among our wonderful teachers, one particularly stood out, the English teacher, one Mr Ogunsan. If this man taught you English for two years and you still fumbled in WASCE, you need to consider a career in yam or akara frying, which had yet to be modernised by Senator Oluremi Tinubu then. Ogunsan’s one hour English class started at 6am with the aid of a gas lamp, after which you would need to endure the serially-monotonous threats of the vice principal on the assembly ground.

A few months before our WASCE, Ogunsan suddenly transformed into a villain, a traducer of a sort, who worked with a particularly acidic gusto to ensure the failure of about 200 young boys and girls in our set.

Some of us, the gentle ones, didn’t know our offence until it became known that our English teacher had equally been coaching one of our female classmates behind closed doors. Remember, there were no small girls in schools in those days like there are these days.

A testimony predictably came out of the private lecherous lessons as our mate became pregnant. Then the set became ostracised not just by Ogunsan but by other compromised teachers, many of whom stopped coming to class to perform their statutory duties so the innocent students could fail their final exams.

Of course, they knew we had been talking in hushed and open tones about the amorous secret affair that the Lord had brought into the open. That’s our unpardonable offence. Today, the AUD ’83 set remembers all of you as the weapons temporarily fashioned against the set’s success like yesterday. I’m happy to tell all the colluding teachers (dead and alive) that your weapons failed to prosper.

Let’s leave aside my great school and the negative legacies of some teachers who unfortunately are many in different institutions in our modern society, but it’s equally important to tell their own history as well before we return to the history of the past kingdoms.

One thing that remained constant in all these empires and their rise and fall was the inseparable link between the kingdoms and their all-powerful emperors. The kings were as powerful as their kingdoms, if not more powerful, except in the old Oyo Empire, where there was a clearly-defined governmental structure that may shame modern-day political set-up in the land.

Among the contemporary political strategies in our clime is the never-ending plan of the opposition parties to field a consensus presidential candidate to battle the All Progressives Congress flag bearer, President Bola Tinubu, in the January 16, 2027election. In my past commentary on this novel plan, I alluded to the fact that the presidential contest in any nation cannot be compared to a primary school’s inter-house sport. It appears, however, that as the reported plot by the opposition elements gathers momentum daily, the more flippant and impracticable the plan looks.

You may wish to recall that in April this year, shortly before the political parties picked their presidential candidates, the opposition camps gathered at the Government House, Ibadan, for the National Summit of All Opposition Parties and came up with the famous (really?) Ibadan Declaration meant to produce a consensus presidential candidate to battle the APC in January.

Among the over a dozen parties at this Ibadan Summit were the African Democratic Congress, Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peoples Democratic Party, Allied Peoples Movement, Social Democratic Party, Labour Party, Accord, New Nigeria People’s Party, and People’s Redemption Party. Attended by top chiefs of the parties, great speeches were equally delivered on the woes of the country and the serial offences of Tinubu at the expense of planning how a consensus presidential candidate would emerge.

The futility of the Ibadan talk show expectedly manifested just about a month after the jamboree as the various opposition parties separately went about picking their presidential candidates against the seemingly gentleman’s agreement reached in Ibadan.

I must admit that at the moment, the opposition parties have serious cause to worry about their fortunes in the January election. On the current template, I can tell you for free that none of the major parties can match the strength of the Bola Tinubu-led APC in the presidential contest if the opposition parties run separately. Serious challengers like the ADC and the NDC lack the spread, depth, financial capacity and structure to unseat the incumbent president in any national electoral contest.

I’m not asking you to agree with my amateurish postulations, but that does not stop me from telling you. The NDC presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, whose candidacy resonates well with the younger population, the biggest demographic sector in Nigeria, is at best a regional champion. Obi will top the chart in the five states of the South-East; he will do very well in the South-South. After the landslide victory in the South, fuel go dry.

No candidate can win the presidential election in Nigeria on regional votes. Muhammadu Buhari’s efforts in 2003, 2007 and 2011 were based on northern votes,which couldn’t get him the Presidency. You can check Obi’s votes in the last election when he ran for the same office in 2023 on the platform of the Labour Party, largely in the South-East.

While Obi has every right to contest the presidency, the ADC presidential candidate, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, if he has any regard for the thin thread holding this nation together, shouldn’t have ventured to contest the presidential election either in 2023 or in 2027.

In the Nigerian political calendar, the Presidency is zoned into two regions – the North and the South – not six geo-political zones. After the eight years of Buhari, a Fulani man from the North, it is inconceivable that another Fulani man from the North, regardless of political affiliation, would nurse the ambition of succeeding the retired general. As how now? Military regimes ended in Nigeria in 1999.

Are we saying this man is sensitive to the political temperature of this country? Atiku’s ambition smacks of political arrogance; it is unreasonable; it is reckless; it is dangerous; it is unjustifiable, and actually a threat to the unity of Nigeria.

In case you have forgotten, Atiku’s unjustifiable presidential ambition tore apart the PDP after the 2023 general elections. I laughed most of the time whenever some political commentators attribute the collapse of the once-ruling party to the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Mr Nyesom Wike’s unending fight with another faction loyal to Atiku.

Against the party agreement zoning the PDP presidential ticket to the South, Atiku insisted on contesting the ticket, which he won. Wike, along with the Oyo State governor, Seyi Makinde, and three other governors who opposed Atiku’s bid, vowed to ensure the victory of a southern presidential candidate, a pledge they accomplished. Having realised that his unbridled ambition would never be achieved on the platform of a fragmented PDP, Atiku sought refuge in the ADC, where he is currently battling to realise his lifetime ambition.

One can’t, however, dismiss Atiku’s ambition and electoral value essentially based on desperation rather than equity. In spite of the ex-Vice President’s war chest and the serial intrigues he has continued to instigate in the United States (as if the US will conduct Nigeria’s elections), Atiku remains a regional champion. He will do well in about 15 states in the North but will struggle in the South-West, the South-East and the South-South.

The opposition parties, faced with the above reality, have realised the need to ‘forge a common front’ by presenting a single presidential candidate. Despite his political separation from Wike, Makinde has maintained that the South must complete its eight years of Presidency. So, Atiku’s candidacy is out of his consideration as a consensus pick. Unfortunately, the Oyo State governor, who is running in the presidential race for a personal, misdirected motive, can’t clinch the opposition’s ticket.

Obi, who is in a more stable political environment than the former vice president at the moment, won’t step down for Atiku in order not to destroy his political investments, in spite of his shortcomings and the controversies surrounding his performance as the two-term governor of Anambra State.

I can tell you with all the confidence in me that Atiku won’t step down for anyone as the presidential flag bearer on the opposition’s consensus platform. To the former number two man during Olusegun Obasanjo’s Presidency, occupying Aso Villa as President is a lifetime project which he can’t defer until 2031 when he might be adjudged to be ‘too old’.

You may not agree with my proposition that the black man is essentially an empire builder, not a nation builder, who first of all ensures that his interests are protected in every step to be taken, regardless of how such actions affect others. You may check your street, where you have mansions owned by the high and mighty, and where you have very deplorable roads leading to the community. Does that tell you anything?

It is strange that the opposition thinks it can adopt the APC-styled template in its plans to field a consensus presidential candidate about 53 days to the contest. The APC started its groundwork for a merger among different political parties, featuring many sitting governors, two years before the 2015 polls. Does this template look like the one that can be adopted by the current stock of opposition parties? I doubt this.

It appears the opposition parties may need a miracle worker not just to find a consensus presidential candidate within a month but to win the presidential election in January 2027 against an incumbent President and a party which currently parades 34 governors as supporters. At the moment, only the governors of Oyo and Bauchi states, who are both in the APM, are not supporting Tinubu’s re-election.

The post Presidency: Empire-building as enemy of consensus candidate appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

Nigeria’s financial markets recorded mixed performances in the week ended 20
content:
Nigeria’s financial markets recorded mixed performances in the week ended 20 November 2026, as equities declined while foreign exchange turnover rose sharply, driven by increased spot dollar transactions, JIDE AJIA reports

Nigeria’s financial markets recorded mixed performances in the week ended 20 November 2026, as equities declined while foreign exchange turnover rose sharply, driven by increased spot dollar transactions, JIDE AJIA reports

The NGX All-Share Index dipped 1.83 per cent to 247,660.74 points, with equity turnover falling over 42 per cent in value, and over 70 per cent in volume, to N106.36bn, whereas FMDQ FX turnover jumped 36.59 per cent to $4.67bn on the back of a 43.08 per cent rise in spot dollar trades.

Trading activity on the Nigerian Exchange recorded a notable downturn during the week as investors exchanged a total turnover of 2.366 billion shares valued at N106.363bn across 159,759 deals, marking a steep contraction from the 8.029 billion shares worth N185.358bn traded in 160,836 deals during the preceding week.

Daily trading volumes steadily declined throughout the five-day session, starting at 673.59 million shares valued at N26.10bn in 38,218 deals on Monday, 16 November, before tapering to 564.04 million shares on Tuesday, 451.10 million shares on Wednesday, and 372.01 million shares on Thursday. It closed the week on Friday with 305.62 million shares worth N16.55bn across 29,586 deals.

Sectoral performance, measured by volume, remained heavily concentrated in the Financial Services Industry, which dominated the activity chart with 1.717 billion shares valued at N67.579bn across 74,214 deals. The sector single-handedly accounted for 72.57 per cent of the total equity turnover volume and 63.54 per cent of the total turnover value.

The Consumer Goods Industry followed in second place with 174.538 million shares worth N9.052bn traded in 20,668 deals, while the Services Industry ranked third with a turnover of 158.306 million shares valued at N1.378bn across 8,975 deals.

Activity in the top three equities by volume, including Access Holdings Plc, FCMB Group Plc and NEM Insurance Plc, generated a combined turnover of 613.658 million shares, reported as 613.658 million in the exchange summary, worth N12.994bn across 8,726 deals, representing 25.93 per cent and 12.22 per cent of total equity volume and value, respectively.

In the Exchange Traded Products segment, investors transacted a total of 1.107 million units valued at N410.452m across 3,848 deals, reflecting a slight dip in unit volume but a substantial jump in transaction value compared to the 1.212 million units worth N278.965m traded in 3,351 deals the previous week.

VETBANK led the ETP board by volume with 286,081 units valued at N7.43m across 247 deals, while STANBICETF30 dominated by value and deal count, recording 229,738 units worth N210.75m in 1,644 deals.

Other active funds included VETGRIF30 with 197,247 units valued at N18.08m, VETGOODS with 108,885 units worth N4.49m, LOTUSHAL15 with 94,284 units valued at N12.03m, and SIAMLETF40 with 90,696 units worth N132.23m. Smaller volumes were recorded across VETINDETF, MERGROWTH, VSPBONDETF, MERVALUE, GREENWETF and NEWGOLD, with NEWGOLD generating N9.65m from just 128 units.

Fixed income market

Activity in the secondary debt market saw a contraction in volume and value despite an increase in deal count, with a total of 116,356 bond units valued at N122.704m changing hands across 49 deals, compared to 156,612 units worth N177.879m traded in 41 deals the prior week.

Trading was anchored by FG202034S2, which recorded 37,848 units worth N43.43m in four deals, closely followed by FGSUK2033S6 with 37,289 units valued at N37.99m across nine deals, and TAJSUKS2 with 22,090 units worth N22.09m in 11 deals.

Additional notable transactions occurred in FG142037S2 with 10,000 units valued at N10.09m, alongside lighter trades in FG202029S5, FGS202776, TAJSUKS1, FGSUK2031S4, FGS202770, FGSUK2032S5, FGSUK2027S3 and FGS202888.

Index, sectoral movements

Broad market sentiment turned bearish during the period under review, pushing the NGX All-Share Index and total market capitalisation down by 1.83 per cent to close at 247,660.74 points and N160.804tn, respectively, down from the previous week’s ASI close of 252,269.16 points.

While the ASI retains a strong year-to-date gain of 59.15 per cent, it now reflects a month-to-date decline of 2.61 per cent and a quarter-to-date dip of 1.41 per cent.

Almost all sectoral and thematic indices ended in negative territory, led downward by the NGX Industrial Goods Index, which fell 5.29 per cent to 11,726.62; the NGX MERI Value Index, which dropped 4.62 per cent to 22,991.14; and the NGX-AFR Bank Value Index, which lost 4.28 per cent to close at 4,559.13.

Other notable declines included the NGX Premium Index (-3.77 per cent), NGX Oil/Gas Index (-3.75 per cent), NGX AFR Div Yield Index (-3.70 per cent), NGX Banking Index (-2.75 per cent), NGX Lotus II (-2.66 per cent), NGX Commodity Index (-2.54 per cent), NGX Pension Index (-2.36 per cent), NGX Pension Broad Index (-2.07 per cent), NGX 30 Index (-1.95 per cent), NGX CG Index (-1.95 per cent), NGX MERI Growth Index (-0.37 per cent), NGX-Main Board Index (-0.36 per cent) and the NGX Sovereign Bond Index (-0.24 per cent).

Bucking the broader downward trend, only three indices closed higher: the NGX Insurance Index advanced 2.47 per cent to 1,098.77, the NGX Consumer Goods Index gained 2.35 per cent to reach 4,028.05, and the NGX Growth Index rose 1.10 per cent to 26,752.31.

Breadth, movers, listings

Market breadth weakened compared to the previous week, as 39 equities appreciated, down from 43 the prior week, while 43 equities depreciated, up from 39 previously, and 64 equities remained unchanged.

LivingTrust Mortgage Bank Plc topped the gainers’ chart with a 28.76 per cent surge from N2.33 to N3.00, followed by Chellarams Plc, which rose 20.62 per cent from N9.70 to N11.70, and International Breweries Plc, which climbed 20.24 per cent from N8.40 to N10.10.

Regency Alliance Insurance Plc gained 18.75 per cent to close at N0.76, Critical Minerals Financing Corp Plc added 17.33 per cent to reach N3.52, Sovereign Trust Insurance Plc rose 16.89 per cent to N2.56, and Legend Internet Plc advanced 16.13 per cent to N3.60.

Rounding out the top 10 gainers were International Energy Insurance Plc (+14.29 per cent to N2.00), Cornerstone Insurance Plc (+13.64 per cent to N5.00) and Omatek Ventures Plc (+11.54 per cent to N1.45).

On the decliners’ side, Meyer Plc suffered the steepest percentage loss, shedding 17.43 per cent to fall from N17.50 to N14.45, followed closely by R. T. Briscoe (Nigeria) Plc, which dropped 16.94 per cent from N9.15 to N7.60.

Lasaco Assurance Plc and Aradel Holdings Plc both declined 10.00 per cent, closing at N1.71 and N1,166.40, respectively, while heavyweight Dangote Cement Plc slipped 9.99 per cent from N1,469.90 to N1,323.00, exerting significant downward pressure on the benchmark index.

Other top decliners included Haldane McCall Plc (-9.91 per cent to N3.00), FTN Cocoa Processors Plc (-9.72 per cent to N6.50), John Holt Plc (-9.71 per cent to N7.90), Red Star Express Plc (-9.60 per cent to N11.30) and Learn Africa Plc (-9.41 per cent to N7.70).

Finally, on the corporate listings front, Nigerian Exchange Limited admitted an additional 323,805 units of the Chapel Hill Denham Nigeria Infrastructure Debt Fund to its Daily Official List on Monday, 16 November 2026. These supplementary units were issued pursuant to the Fund’s Q3 2026 scrip dividend distribution, increasing the total listed units of NIDF on the Exchange from 1,197,308,007 to 1,197,631,812 units.

FX market performance

In contrast to the downturn in equities, turnover in the Foreign Exchange Spot and Derivatives markets between FMDQ Dealing Member (Banks)/Authorised Dealers and their clients surged  36.59 per cent ($1,251.63m) week-on-week to reach a total of $4,672.49m for the week ended 20 November 2026, up from $3,420.86m in the preceding week.

Daily average turnover rose accordingly from $684.18m to $934.50m.

According to the FMDQ weekly market report, “The week-on-week increase in total turnover was solely driven by the 43.08 per cent ($1,398.37m) increase in FX Spot transactions, which recorded a total value of $4,644.30m compared to $3,245.93m in the week-ended November 13, 2026, offsetting the 83.88 per cent ($146.74m) decrease in FX Derivatives transactions (comprising FX Forward) for the week-ended 20 November 2026.”

FX Spot transactions accounted for 99.40 per cent of total market turnover with a daily average of $928.86m, increasing its share from 94.89 per cent in the prior week.

Conversely, FX Derivatives, representing FX Forwards turnover, contracted sharply from $174.93m (a daily average of $34.99m and a 5.11 per cent market share) to $28.19m (a daily average of $5.64m), narrowing its share of total weekly FX turnover to just 0.60 per cent.

title: Rewane projects N519.75tn capital market growth by 2028
description: The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Financial Derivatives Company Limited, Bismarck Rewane, has projected that Nigeria’s capital market could expand 2.25-fold to N519.75tn by 2028, driven by price effects, stronger domestic participation, ongoing reforms, new listings and wider inve
content:
The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Financial Derivatives Company Limited, Bismarck Rewane, has projected that Nigeria’s capital market could expand 2.25-fold to N519.75tn by 2028, driven by price effects, stronger domestic participation, ongoing reforms, new listings and wider investor engagement.

Rewane made the projection while delivering the 2027 macroeconomic outlook at the 2026 Parthian Economic Discourse in Lagos, where financial and industry leaders stressed that Nigeria’s next phase of reform must move beyond macroeconomic stabilisation towards building strong institutions, trusted markets and productive capital for sustainable business competitiveness.

He also projected that headline inflation could moderate to 13 per cent by 2028 as productivity and economic efficiency improve. He, however, cautioned that policy pronouncements alone would not deliver the projected outcomes without institutional overhaul.

He said, “There is a difference between policy reform and institutional reform.

“Nigeria has been changing policies over the years but has not been able to reform the institution that delivers them.”

Convened to examine Nigeria’s 2027 macroeconomic outlook and the structural conditions required for long-term competitiveness, the annual discourse brought together executives from finance, industry, development finance institutions and the digital economy.

Earlier in his welcome address, the Group Managing Director of Parthian Financial Services Limited, Oluseye Olusoga, stated that national competitiveness must be measured by the capacity of Nigerian enterprises to deliver quality goods at prices capable of competing in regional and global markets.

“A competitive economy is one that does two things very well: it produces at competitive prices and gets more out of every resource, every Naira and every hour,” Olusoga said.

He continued, “Competitiveness is when a Nigerian product wins in Accra, Nairobi and Rotterdam on price and quality without any extraordinary help.

“A weak Naira can make our goods cheap for a while, and protection can make our goods the only option for a while, but neither makes us competitive.”

Olusoga noted that declining operating costs, higher productivity, deeper domestic capital markets and predictable regulation were critical if economic reforms were to translate into higher household incomes and improved living standards.

“What Nigeria needs in 2027 is policy stability, strong institutions and staying the course,” he said.

During a panel session themed ‘Building a Competitive Economy: The Next Frontier of Nigeria’s Reform Agenda,’ speakers examined structural bottlenecks limiting the expansion of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, including digital infrastructure gaps, payment systems, credit access, alternative collateral frameworks and regulatory coordination.

The Managing Director-Designate of Parthian Financial, Foluso Ayo-Olaiya, urged commercial lenders to transition from collateral-led lending to structuring transactions around the cash flows and operational realities of viable businesses.

“To build a competitive economy, financial institutions must shift from collateral lending to structuring deals for businesses while mitigating risks through collaboration with development finance institutions and export credit agencies,” Ayo-Olaiya said.

Also speaking, a general manager at the Bank of Industry, Dr Isa Omagu, underscored the centrality of human capital development to sustainable economic transformation, noting, “If you fix the people, the country will be fixed.”

In a fireside chat titled Financing Nigeria’s Next Growth Phase, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority, Aminu Umar-Sadiq, emphasised the need for deliberate risk-mitigation mechanisms to unlock long-term institutional capital for critical infrastructure.

“Bankability is a necessary but insufficient condition for mobilising long-term capital into the power sector,” Umar-Sadiq said.

“Other important considerations include the opportunity cost of capital, the regulatory framework, risk mitigation and credit enhancement”, he added.

The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of First Bank of Nigeria Limited, Olusegun Alebiosu, identified institutional trust and a functional legal framework as prerequisites for private sector-led growth and MSME expansion.

“The private sector should be richer than the public sector if we are to grow as a country,” Alebiosu said.

“The biggest problem we have in Nigeria today is trust”, he added.

The discourse concluded with a consensus on combining policy consistency with institutional reforms, reliable infrastructure, deeper capital markets and a culture of trust to enable Nigerian businesses to compete on merit rather than protectionism.

The post Rewane projects N519.75tn capital market growth by 2028 appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Trump backs Nvidia CEO’s return as backlash grows
description:
US President Donald Trump praised Nvidia’s decision Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, as Democratic leaders vowed investigations and prominent Republicans questioned whether his return posed a national security risk.
Trump also posted a doctored version of the famous photograph of
content:
US President Donald Trump praised Nvidia’s decision Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, as Democratic leaders vowed investigations and prominent Republicans questioned whether his return posed a national security risk.

Trump also posted a doctored version of the famous photograph of him raising his fist after surviving a 2024 assassination attempt, replacing himself with Huang, who brandished a red bra beneath an Nvidia flag.

The image appeared to allude to the scandal that forced Huang, co-founder of the AI chip giant, to resign less than two weeks earlier following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

“The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, adding that the government had no reason to believe his return posed a national security risk.

In a telephone interview with CNBC, Trump suggested the scandal could prove to be “a net positive” by highlighting Nvidia’s technological advances.

“I don’t think he’s going to be diminished at all,” he said, predicting Huang would return at “an almost higher level.”

He said the attorney general had confirmed that US authorities possessed no evidence Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct, but urged Nvidia to continue investigating its compliance with restrictions on advanced chip sales to China.

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer and House speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries vowed sweeping investigations into Nvidia, Trump and his senior officials, with Jeffries singling out Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

“We will not allow America’s national security to be sold out by the Trump administration for personal financial gain,” Jeffries said.

• ‘What changed?’ –

Huang is already scheduled to face questioning behind closed doors by three House committees on December 1 over his relationship with the suspected Chinese intelligence operative and concerns about Nvidia’s chip exports.

And the Republican-led Senate Banking Committee has announced that his appearance scheduled for December 3 will be livestreamed.

“We still don’t know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him,” said House Intelligence Committee Democrat Raja Krishnamoorthi, demanding a full public congressional hearing.

Senator Elizabeth Warren called the decision “reckless” and demanded details of what input senior administration officials had provided in support of Huang’s return.

Republican Senator John Curtis raised similar questions, noting that Nvidia’s board had reversed its opposition to reinstating Huang while an independent investigation remained unfinished.

“Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board?” he wrote on X. “I’d like to know what changed.”

Senator Pete Ricketts, also a Republican, said Huang’s behavior did not warrant reinstatement and insisted the move did not excuse him from testifying before Congress.

Former Republican House speaker Newt Gingrich called for scrutiny of what he described as a national security issue “of enormous proportions.”

Outgoing Republican congressman Don Bacon alleged Huang had been “compromised and exploited by a Chinese spy,” demanding answers about who had authorized advanced chip sales to China.

And Republican Senator John Cornyn offered a terse response to Trump’s assurances.

“No national security risk? Based on what?” he wrote on X.

Trump declined earlier Monday to comment on a New York Times report that the woman at the center of the scandal had been in contact with an official from China’s principal intelligence agency during her affair with Huang.

AFP

The post Trump backs Nvidia CEO’s return as backlash grows appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 15 APC supporters killed in Zamfara road crash, party postpones rally
description:
The Zamfara State All Progressives Congress Presidential and Gubernatorial Campaign Council has postponed its rally scheduled for Tuesday in Maru Local Government Area following the death of 15 supporters in a road accident.
The supporters were reportedly travelling from Gummi to Talata Mafara to at
content:
The Zamfara State All Progressives Congress Presidential and Gubernatorial Campaign Council has postponed its rally scheduled for Tuesday in Maru Local Government Area following the death of 15 supporters in a road accident.

The supporters were reportedly travelling from Gummi to Talata Mafara to attend the campaign flag-off when the accident occurred.

The council announced the postponement in a statement dated Monday and signed by its Secretary-General, Abubakar Nakwada.

It said 15 supporters lost their lives in the accident, while others sustained injuries and were receiving medical attention.

The council also mourned the death of a former Secretary to the Zamfara State Government, Alhaji Kabiru Balarabe, who died after a brief illness.

“In honour of the departed and in solidarity with the grieving families, the council has postponed the rally scheduled for Tuesday, 24 November 2026, in Maru Local Government Area. A revised campaign timetable will be announced in due course,” the statement said.

The council extended its condolences to the bereaved families, the people of Gummi and residents of Zamfara State.

It also said it was monitoring the condition of the injured and would provide appropriate support to them and the families of those who died.

The statement added, “May Almighty Allah forgive the shortcomings of the departed and admit them into Jannatul Firdaus. May He grant the injured a swift and full recovery and give the bereaved families the strength to bear their losses.”

The postponement came after the APC in Zamfara State flagged off its presidential and governorship campaigns in Talata Mafara Local Government Area on Monday.

The rally was attended by Governor Dauda Lawal, former governors Abdul’aziz Yari, Ahmed Sani Yarima and Mahmud Shinkafi, as well as other party leaders and supporters.

Lawal used the occasion to seek support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and his own second term in office.

title: 2027: NUC proposes 4-week break for universities
description:
By Omeiza Ajayi







The National Universities Commission NUC has proposed that universities adopt a three-to-four-week break to accommodate the 2027 general election, saying the entire election cycle will last no more than four weeks.







Executive Secretary of the NUC, Prof. Abdullahi Yusufu
content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

The National Universities Commission NUC has proposed that universities adopt a three-to-four-week break to accommodate the 2027 general election, saying the entire election cycle will last no more than four weeks.

Executive Secretary of the NUC, Prof. Abdullahi Yusufu Ribadu, made the proposal on Monday in Abuja during a courtesy visit by the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN.

According to a statement from INEC on Monday night, Amupitan was accompanied by National Commissioners and senior officials of the commission.

The Presidential and National Assembly elections hold on Saturday, 16 January 2027. The Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections follow on Saturday, 6 February 2027.

He noted that the academic community had for over a decade served as the backbone of collation and declaration of results, with Vice-Chancellors serving as Collation and Returning Officers across the Federation.

The INEC Chairman said the commission had introduced operational, technological and security reforms to make the work of its university partners safer and less contentious.

He said polling unit results on Form EC8A would undergo automated arithmetic consistency and over-voting checks before transmission to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV).

According to him, the commission has procured 57,000 new Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices and lowered the voter-to-device ratio to 850 per machine.

Amupitan added that INEC would conduct a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on Saturday, 28 November 2026.

On security, he said the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) had been decentralised to every Local Government Area and Registration Area, with dedicated security cordons and escort protocols around collation centres.

He drew attention to Sections 96 and 97 of the Electoral Act 2026, which criminalise violence, abusive rhetoric and threats against electoral personnel, and Section 148, which empowers the commission to prosecute offenders directly.

“No Returning Officer or Collation Officer will be left to stand alone against lawlessness,” Amupitan said.

He then asked the NUC for support in four areas: the timely nomination of academic staff of verified non-partisan standing, the alignment of academic calendars with the election dates, collaboration on voter education and counter-disinformation on campuses, and the welfare and recognition of academics deployed for election duty.

Responding, Ribadu congratulated Amupitan on his appointment, describing him as a lawyer and academic of international repute and “a round peg in a round hole.”
,

The NUC Executive Secretary said the commission would engage Vice-Chancellors on the nomination of academic staff, including through an online meeting. He said it would also transmit a circular to the universities once INEC forwards a formal letter on the matter.

“Since we want to have credible elections, we also have to have credible personnel,” Ribadu said. He added that all ad hoc personnel should take an oath of neutrality.

On the academic calendar, he said the entire election cycle would last no more than four weeks, and suggested that universities could adopt a three-to-four-week break to accommodate it.

“We will discuss with the Vice-Chancellors and have their calendars tweaked in such a way that it will not affect the elections, nor will it affect the studies of the students,” Ribadu said.

He said students could also support voter education through campus clubs.
Ribadu expressed confidence that INEC would deliver a transparent, free and fair election that would serve as an example to other African countries.

He proposed expanded collaboration between the two institutions, including student internships at INEC offices, a possible programme in electoral studies, and joint research on artificial intelligence, robotics and data analytics.

The post 2027: NUC proposes 4-week break for universities appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Delta imposes 12-hour curfew in Ughelli north after rally violence
description:
The Delta State Government has imposed a curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area following reported violence at a campaign rally of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Uduere community, which allegedly left some people dead and others injured.
The Delta State Police Command disclosed thi
content:
The Delta State Government has imposed a curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area following reported violence at a campaign rally of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Uduere community, which allegedly left some people dead and others injured.

The Delta State Police Command disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Public Relations Officer, SP Bright Edafe.

According to the statement, the curfew will run from 6pm to 6am daily until further notice.

The police said investigations had commenced to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible.

The statement read, “Following the reported violence during a campaign rally of the NDC at Uduere Community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, which allegedly resulted in loss of lives and injuries to several persons, the Delta State Government has imposed a curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area, from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. daily until further notice.

“The command has commenced investigations to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible.

“The command therefore urges residents of Ughelli North Local Government Area to comply strictly with the curfew imposed by the Delta State Government, restricting movement between 1800hrs to 0600hrs until further notice.”

The police urged residents to remain calm and cooperate with security personnel.

The Commissioner of Police, Samuel Erale, was said to have directed intensified security operations in the affected area to prevent further violence and maintain law and order.

Erale also ordered a full-scale investigation, assuring residents that anyone found culpable would face the law, irrespective of political affiliation or status.

He extended condolences to the families of those who died and wished the injured a speedy recovery.

Erale warned political actors and their supporters against thuggery, intimidation and the unlawful use of firearms, stressing that political differences should not degenerate into violence or loss of lives.

content:
Over 10 members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) have reportedly lost their lives in a road accident shortly after the party’s governorship campaign flag-off in Talata-Mafara, Zamfara State.

The victims were reportedly returning to their hometown in Gummi Local Government Area after attending the campaign rally when the accident occurred, which also left several others injured.

Confirming the incident in a press statement issued on Monday, the Zamfara State Commissioner for Information and Culture, Mahmud Muhammad Dantawasa, said the state government had expressed condolences to the bereaved families and the APC family over the tragic loss.

According to the statement, the government has also suspended the APC campaign rally scheduled to be held in Maru Local Government Area on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, in honour of the victims.

The statement added that the government sympathised with those who sustained injuries and prayed for their speedy recovery.

It also urged residents of the state to remain calm and offer prayers for the deceased and injured persons.

The government further prayed for Almighty Allah to forgive the souls of the departed, grant them Aljannatul Firdaus, and give their families the strength to bear the loss.

content:
A former Minister of State for Niger Delta Affairs and chieftain of the All Progressives Congress, Senator Tayo Alasoadura, has said the party has achieved over 70 per cent of its nationwide mobilisation and coordination efforts ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Alasoadura expressed confidence that the APC would secure victory for President Bola Tinubu if party leaders and stakeholders sustained their commitment to the mobilisation exercise.

In a statement personally signed by him on Monday, the former minister described nationwide political mobilisation as an extensive and demanding task but said the party had made considerable progress.

According to him, the party had achieved well over 70 per cent of the required coordination nationwide.

“The task of organising and sustaining a nationwide political mobilisation structure is extensive and demanding. Considerable progress has already been made.The APC has achieved well over 70 per cent of its required coordination nationwide. Maintaining the current momentum would translate into electoral success,” he said.

He described the prospect of victory as “sacrosanct and well assured”, urging party leaders and stakeholders to sustain the momentum.

Speaking on regional mobilisation, Alasoadura said political leaders across the South-West were working to consolidate support for Tinubu, particularly to ensure a decisive victory for the President in Ondo State.

He stressed the need for unity, effective coordination and sustained engagement among party members, noting that the success of the mobilisation exercise depended on the collective commitment of leaders and members at all levels.

He expressed optimism that the party’s ongoing efforts would translate into electoral success in the 2027 general elections.

He commended the APC National Chairman, members of the National Working Committee, the leadership of the Presidential Campaign Council and other party stakeholders for their efforts in coordinating the party’s activities.

The APC is intensifying efforts to strengthen its nationwide political structures and mobilise support for the 2027 general elections, in which President Bola Tinubu is expected to seek re-election.

The party has continued to engage its leaders and stakeholders across the six geopolitical zones to consolidate its support base, with the South-West, Tinubu’s home region, expected to play a significant role in its re-election bid.

title: DSS arraigns seven over terrorism, kidnapping in Kebbi
description:
The Department of State Services has arraigned seven persons before a Federal High Court in Birnin Kebbi over alleged involvement in terrorism-related activities, kidnapping and illegal possession of firearms.
The defendants were brought before Justice Emmanuel Gakko on Monday in three separate case
content:
The Department of State Services has arraigned seven persons before a Federal High Court in Birnin Kebbi over alleged involvement in terrorism-related activities, kidnapping and illegal possession of firearms.

The defendants were brought before Justice Emmanuel Gakko on Monday in three separate cases filed by the DSS in Kebbi State.

In the first case, marked FHC/KB/CR/58/2026, five defendants, Garba Safiyanu, Lawali Adamu, Abubakar Murtala, Kabiru Sani and Salah Muhammad, are facing three counts bordering on conspiracy, providing support to a terrorist group and withholding information about terrorist activities.

The prosecution alleged, “The defendants bought and sold cattle rustled by members of the Islamic State in Sahel Province, also known as Lakurawa, operating in parts of Argungu and Augie Local Government Areas of Kebbi State.”

It said the alleged transactions amounted to providing material support to the group and concealing information about its operations.

The offences were allegedly committed on May 20, 2026, in Argungu Local Government Area.

In the second case, marked FHC/KB/CR/59/2026, Bello Abdullahi, also known as Riskuwa, was charged with concealing information about terrorism, supporting terrorists and aiding their activities.

According to the prosecution, Abdullahi allegedly withheld information about the activities of a suspected terrorist leader identified as Abdullahi, said to be his cousin, and members of his gang following an attack on Cikanwa village in Danko-Wasagu Local Government Area.

He was also accused of communicating with the suspected leader by telephone and providing information about the gang’s activities.

The prosecution further alleged that their conversations included discussions about the killing of Nadajo Bakumi during an earlier attack on the community.

Abdullahi was also accused of expressing willingness to contact relatives of other victims abducted by the gang to negotiate ransom payments.

The alleged offences occurred on January 4, 2026, in Maga town, Danko-Wasagu Local Government Area.

The third case involved Kyale Ayuba, popularly known as Jikan Dole, who was charged with unlawful possession of firearms.

The prosecution alleged that Ayuba was found with a locally made revolver pistol, a magazine and five rounds of live 9mm ammunition, contrary to Section 27(1)(a) of the Firearms Act.

Director of Legal Services at the DSS, Abdullahi Shehu, prosecuted the cases on behalf of the Federal Government.

Hamza Nagari represented four of the defendants in the first case, while Sadiq Shehu appeared for the fifth defendant. S. M. Danyaro represented Bello Abdullahi in the second case.

All seven defendants pleaded not guilty to the charges after they were read to them.

Justice Gakko adjourned the three cases until December 3, 2026, for hearing.

Lakurawa has emerged as a major security concern in Kebbi and neighbouring Sokoto State, with the armed group linked to attacks on rural communities, cattle rustling and abductions for ransom.

The group reportedly became more active in north-western Nigeria in 2024, with its activities spreading across border communities.

The European Union Agency for Asylum, in a security assessment of Kebbi, documented attacks and abductions attributed to armed groups, including Lakurawa, as well as incidents of cattle rustling and killings.

The Institute for Security Studies has also described Lakurawa as a cross-border group combining jihadist activities with organised criminality, including kidnapping for ransom and the seizure of livestock and farm produce.
