title: ‘Rig and die’ rhetoric fuelling Delta tension – Keyamo
description:
The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has called on those promoting the ‘Rig and Die’ slogan in Delta State to withdraw it publicly and apologise, warning that the rhetoric is overheating the political atmosphere in the state.
Keyamo said the growing wave of political vi
content:
The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has called on those promoting the ‘Rig and Die’ slogan in Delta State to withdraw it publicly and apologise, warning that the rhetoric is overheating the political atmosphere in the state.

Keyamo said the growing wave of political violence could make anyone a victim, following the killing of four members of the campaign organisation of former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, in Ughelli, Delta State.

The former lawmaker had alleged that gunmen attacked his campaign team in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area, repeatedly shouting his name and threatening to kill him.

Omo-Agege said he escaped because of the intervention of his Department of State Services escorts.

According to him, the attackers opened fire less than five minutes after he began addressing supporters at the campaign venue.

Reacting to the incident in a statement on Monday, Keyamo, who described Ughelli as his town of birth, said he received disturbing reports of the attack, which left four persons dead and several others injured.

“Those who have promoted the mantra of ‘Rig and Die’ in Delta State and elsewhere should have a rethink, publicly withdraw it, and apologise for overheating the political temperature in the state and country. As can be seen, anyone can be a victim,” he said.

He expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and wished those injured a quick recovery.

The minister condemned the killings and called on security agencies to identify and arrest those responsible, including perpetrators of an earlier killing in Asaba.

He said, “I condemn in the strongest possible terms the killing of these persons, just as I also condemned the killing of a tricycle operator in broad daylight by identified supporters of a political party in Asaba on November 7, 2026.

“I call on the law enforcement agencies to fish out the perpetrators of these killings, both in Asaba and Ughelli, and bring them to book.”

Keyamo disclosed that he had been engaging security officials over the rising political tension in the state.

“I have been in touch with the top hierarchy of law enforcement agencies in the last one month over the rising wave of political violence and violent rhetoric in Delta State,” he said.

He noted that Delta had maintained relative political peace since the return to democracy in 1999, arguing that political disagreements among residents had never previously degenerated into killings.

“Since 1999, Delta State has been a relatively peaceful state, politically. Our disagreements have never led to violence and killings. We are all brothers and sisters who went to the same primary, secondary and tertiary institutions, and we all know ourselves and our families so well. There is absolutely no need for a descent into violence,” he said.

The minister also cautioned political actors against encouraging supporters to resort to violence, insisting that only security agencies had the authority to deal with offenders.

“It is wrong to tell your supporters to kill other citizens under whatever guise. It smacks of desperation,” he added.

He appealed to Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to address residents of the state and warn individuals threatening violence.

“I call on our leader and my elder brother, the Governor of Delta State and the Chief Security Officer of the State, Rt. Hon. Elder Sheriff Oborevwori, to urgently address Deltans and read the Riot Act against those who are threatening fire and brimstone,” Keyamo said.

He ended the statement with the words, “Enough is enough.”

In a statement issued through his media adviser, Sunny Areh, Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation described the incident as an assassination attempt on the former deputy senate president during his campaign tour.

It called on the Nigeria Police Force to conduct an independent and thorough investigation into the attack and appealed to the Inspector-General of Police, the Department of State Services and the Independent National Electoral Commission to ensure the safety of political candidates and their supporters.

The organisation also urged supporters to remain calm and avoid retaliation, saying its ward-to-ward campaign activities across Delta Central would continue.

Omo-Agege, who is seeking election to represent Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general election, said four members of his campaign organisation were killed, while about 15 others sustained injuries, some of them critically.

Among those reportedly killed were Moses Anaughe, a former member of the Delta State House of Assembly and personal assistant to Omo-Agege, and Akima Efemena Umukoro.

The controversy surrounding the slogan dates back to October 23, when Omo-Agege used it during the flag-off of his campaign for the Delta Central Senatorial District seat in Uvwie Local Government Area.

“Anybody who rigs the election on that day, we will kill him! If you don’t value your life, come and rig the election. They’re rigging your future. They’re rigging the future of your children. We’re waiting for them. Let them try it. It is rig and die,” he said.

Following the backlash, his Special Adviser on Strategy and Communications, Godwin Anaughe, defended the remarks, saying they were directed at electoral offenders who manipulate results and steal electoral materials, not voters or innocent citizens.

Keyamo had also reacted to the slogan on November 5 in a post on X, sarcastically arguing that its promoters would have to explain how many alleged riggers they killed if they lost an election conducted freely and fairly.

The slogan has featured amid political rivalry in Delta Central, where Omo-Agege is challenging incumbent Senator Ede Dafinone of the All Progressives Congress for the senatorial seat in the 2027 elections.

The post ‘Rig and die’ rhetoric fuelling Delta tension – Keyamo appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Govt Condemns Delta Killings, Says No One Will Be Shielded From Justice
description: The Delta State Government has condemned the killing of people during a violent incident in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, assuring that those responsible for the dastardly act will not escape justice.Arising from the reported gunshots and attendant deaths in some parts of th
content:
The Delta State Government has condemned the killing of people during a violent incident in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, assuring that those responsible for the dastardly act will not escape justice.

Arising from the reported gunshots and attendant deaths in some parts of the area, the state government has declared an immediate curfew from 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. every day starting from November 23, 2026, until further notice.

This, it said, was to bring the situation under control.

According to a statement signed by the Secretary to the Delta State Government (SSG), Kingsley Emu, the curfew covers the entire Ughelli North Local Government Area.

Emu said Governor Sheriff Oborevwori was deeply disturbed by the killings and had directed security agencies to immediately investigate the incident, identify those responsible, and ensure that they are brought to justice.

He described the loss of life as tragic and unacceptable, stressing that no political ambition or disagreement should result in the taking of innocent lives.

The state government commiserated with the families of the deceased and all those affected by the incident, and also wished the injured victims a speedy recovery.

While acknowledging the seriousness of the allegations raised by a former deputy senate president, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, Emu said it was important to allow security agencies to conduct a thorough, impartial and professional investigation rather than rush to conclusions or assign blame without facts.

He specifically dismissed the attempt to link Governor Oborevwori to the violence, describing such allegations as grave matters that must be substantiated and investigated rather than presented as facts.

“The governor has nothing to gain from violence or the loss of innocent lives. His administration remains committed to peace, security and the protection of every resident of Delta State, irrespective of political affiliation.

“Governor Oborevwori has made it clear that anyone found to have participated in, sponsored, or facilitated this criminal act must face the full weight of the law. Nobody will be protected on account of political position, status or affiliation,” he said.

The SSG emphasised that Delta State must not be allowed to degenerate into an atmosphere of political violence, adding that the right to campaign, canvass for votes and participate in the democratic process must be respected and protected.

He urged political leaders, party supporters and their followers to exercise restraint, avoid inflammatory statements and refrain from actions capable of escalating tensions in the state.

He further appealed to residents of Uduere and neighbouring communities to remain calm, cooperate with security agencies and provide useful information that could assist in the investigation.

He assured that the Oborevwori administration would continue to work with relevant security agencies to maintain peace and protect lives and property across the state.

Emu reiterated that the government would not condone political violence under any guise, insisting that the perpetrators of the Uduere killings must be identified and brought to justice.

Four people were reportedly killed and four others injured following a gun attack on the campaign entourage of Omo-Agege in Uduere community.

The incident occurred on Monday during a campaign tour by the former lawmaker, who is the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for the Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections.

Initial reports indicated that suspected political thugs invaded the campaign venue, leaving three people with gunshot injuries, while the senator was reportedly whisked away from the scene.

Omo-Agege alleged that the gunmen who attacked his campaign team in Delta State, killing four people, repeatedly shouted his name and declared their intention to kill him.

The post Govt Condemns Delta Killings, Says No One Will Be Shielded From Justice appeared first on Channels Television.

title: British Council awards grants to seven Nigerians for community projects
description:
The British Council has awarded grants of up to £5,000 each to seven Nigerians to implement community projects addressing flooding, electronic waste management, girls’ education, unemployment and social inclusion.
The projects, which will run for five months, include training young women to collect
content:
The British Council has awarded grants of up to £5,000 each to seven Nigerians to implement community projects addressing flooding, electronic waste management, girls’ education, unemployment and social inclusion.

The projects, which will run for five months, include training young women to collect flood-related data in Bayelsa State, equipping solar technicians in Rivers State to safely manage discarded solar batteries and providing learning support to disadvantaged girls in Lagos and Imo states.

According to a statement by the British Council on Monday, the grants were announced in Lagos on Thursday November 19, under the 2026–27 Alumni UK Grant Programme.

The awards were presented by its Deputy Country Director in Nigeria, Chilufya Besa, who said the funding was tied to specific projects and measurable outcomes.

“These are not personal awards. The money is tied to a project, an agreed budget and clear results,” the statement quoted Besa as saying.

It added that the beneficiaries would be required to report on what they delivered, the people reached and the lessons learnt from implementing their projects.

“We are not simply recognising seven people for what they have already achieved. We are backing them to do something practical,” he said.

Four of the projects focus on climate action and environmental sustainability, while three address inclusion, reducing inequality and empowerment.

In Bayelsa State, May Tamara Stow will train 40 young women aged 16 to 24 in Otuoke to collect, analyse and present flood-related data from more than 200 households.

The project, which will be implemented in partnership with the Federal University Otuoke and community leaders, will also produce community flood-preparedness stories and a practical toolkit to help households prepare for flooding.

In Rivers State, Peter Abiye Banigo’s Solar Second Life Project will train 30 informal-sector solar technicians, including women and young people, to repair, restore and safely manage discarded solar equipment and lithium batteries.

The initiative will also develop open-access training materials and establish a community recovery network in partnership with a licensed electronic waste recycler.

Another beneficiary, Adelopo Abdulganiyu Omobolaji, will implement CircuRise in Lagos, targeting 100 informal waste workers at selected dumpsites and waste-picker communities.

The project will equip participants with digital and carbon literacy skills while testing multilingual learning tools, artificial intelligence-assisted waste identification and mobile reporting systems.

In Abuja, Bethel Ikenna Okeke’s Green Cycle Initiative will support 100 adolescent girls and young women aged 15 to 24 in the Durumi and Lugbe camps for internally displaced persons.

The initiative will provide menstrual health education and training in reusable sanitary pad production, entrepreneurship and financial literacy, alongside mentorship and business support to help participants establish small enterprises.

Under the inclusion theme, Charity K. Usifoh-Chenge will expand The Next Hundred Public Health Stewards programme to Gombe and Nasarawa states, supporting between 40 and 50 young people and early-career professionals through training and mentorship.

The project will focus on women and underserved groups, drawing on the programme’s 2025 evaluation to guide possible expansion across the country.

David Chukwuma Izuogu’s Exam Equity for Girls will support 150 girls from low-income families in two underserved secondary schools in Lagos and Imo states.

Led by Africa of Our Dream Education Initiative in partnership with Aspiralane, the project will combine offline-accessible digital learning, artificial intelligence-supported tutoring, female mentorship in science, technology, engineering and mathematics, and scholarship guidance.

It will also provide teachers with support to sustain digital learning beyond the project period.

The seventh initiative, Bridging Digital Divide for Equal Disability Employment, led by Opeolu Stephen Akinola, will equip 50 undergraduates and graduates with visual, hearing and physical disabilities with digital and employment skills.

Implemented by Accesstech Innovation and Research Centre in partnership with six organisations of persons with disabilities, the project will provide training in digital literacy, assistive technologies, CV preparation and interview skills.

Training materials will be available in Braille, large print and screen-reader-compatible formats, with sign language interpretation also provided.

Speaking on the rationale for the grants, Besa acknowledged that the funding would not independently resolve the challenges being addressed but could help beneficiaries test their ideas and attract further support.

“A grant of up to £5,000 will not solve a national problem. It can, however, test an idea,” the statement quoted him as saying.

He added that climate change affected several aspects of people’s lives beyond the environment, including employment, healthcare, energy, transportation and the ability of communities to withstand economic pressure.

“Climate change is not only about the environment. It affects jobs, health, energy, transport and the ability of communities to cope with economic pressure,” he said.

On social inclusion, Besa said it was important to ensure that people could access education, technology, employment and healthcare and participate fully in society.

“Inclusion is about whether people can enter a classroom, use technology, find work, access healthcare and participate properly in society,” he added.

The seven Nigerian projects are part of a wider British Council initiative supporting 61 alumni-led projects across 15 countries. Of these, 35 focus on climate action and sustainability, while 26 address inclusion, inequality and empowerment.

The statement said applicants in Nigeria were required to be Nigerian nationals living in the country, have studied at a UK institution for at least one term and be independent of political affiliations.

It added that the seven beneficiaries emerged through a competitive selection process.

Explaining the importance of the programme to Nigeria-UK relations, Besa cited British Council research involving more than 4,000 international alumni of UK institutions.

According to him, the research found that nearly three-quarters of the alumni had maintained contact with people they met while studying in the UK, while more than half of the alumni entrepreneurs surveyed were collaborating or trading with the UK.

“A UK education, therefore, does not end at graduation,” he said.

The British Council said it would work with the beneficiaries throughout the five-month implementation period, with a global showcase of the projects scheduled for April 2027.

It also said the recipients would be expected to provide honest accounts of their achievements and challenges during implementation.

“Honest evidence is more useful than a success story that leaves out the difficult parts,” Besa said.

He urged organisations to support the initiatives through technical advice, access to communities, equipment, data and other forms of collaboration.

“Not every partnership begins with a large cheque. Sometimes, the right connection is what allows a good idea to move forward,” he said.

title: ‘Obi lacks character, competence to lead Nigeria, Tinubu 100% better’ – Abure

Factional National Chairman of the Labour Party, Julius Abure, has criticised former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi, questioning his character and competence to lead Nigeria.
Abure, who said his experience working with Obi had changed his perception of the former presidential candidate, described
content:
Factional National Chairman of the Labour Party, Julius Abure, has criticised former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi, questioning his character and competence to lead Nigeria.

Abure, who said his experience working with Obi had changed his perception of the former presidential candidate, described him as unstable, unreliable and untrustworthy.

According to the Labour Party factional leader, his dealings with Obi had given him what he called a better understanding of the politician’s character.

“Peter Obi doesn’t have the character and competence to lead the country. Given my experiences, I now know better. Experience, they say, is the best teacher.

“I have experience working with Obi and have seen him in and out, and he is unstable, unreliable, a pretender, and cannot be trusted. President Tinubu is 100% better,” Abure said.

His remarks amount to a strong criticism of Obi and an expression of preference for President Bola Tinubu, amid political realignments and discussions ahead of the 2027 general election.

The allegations and assessment of both political figures reflect Abure’s personal views.

title: Trump backs Nvidia CEO’s return amid US lawmakers’ spy allegations, security concerns
description:
US President Donald Trump praised Nvidia’s decision Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, as Democratic leaders vowed investigations and prominent Republicans questioned whether his return posed a national security risk.



Trump also posted a doctored version of the famous photograph
content:
US President Donald Trump praised Nvidia’s decision Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, as Democratic leaders vowed investigations and prominent Republicans questioned whether his return posed a national security risk.

Trump also posted a doctored version of the famous photograph of him raising his fist after surviving a 2024 assassination attempt, replacing himself with Huang, who brandished a red bra beneath an Nvidia flag.

The image appeared to allude to the scandal that forced Huang, co-founder of the AI chip giant, to resign less than two weeks earlier following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

“The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, adding that the government had no reason to believe his return posed a national security risk.

In a telephone interview with CNBC, Trump suggested the scandal could prove to be “a net positive” by highlighting Nvidia’s technological advances.

“I don’t think he’s going to be diminished at all,” he said, predicting Huang would return at “an almost higher level.”

He said the attorney general had confirmed that US authorities possessed no evidence Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct, but urged Nvidia to continue investigating its compliance with restrictions on advanced chip sales to China.

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer and House speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries vowed sweeping investigations into Nvidia, Trump and his senior officials, with Jeffries singling out Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

“We will not allow America’s national security to be sold out by the Trump administration for personal financial gain,” Jeffries said.

– ‘What changed?’ –

Huang is already scheduled to face questioning behind closed doors by three House committees on December 1 over his relationship with the suspected Chinese intelligence operative and concerns about Nvidia’s chip exports.

And the Republican-led Senate Banking Committee has announced that his appearance scheduled for December 3 will be livestreamed.

“We still don’t know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him,” said House Intelligence Committee Democrat Raja Krishnamoorthi, demanding a full public congressional hearing.

Senator Elizabeth Warren called the decision “reckless” and demanded details of what input senior administration officials had provided in support of Huang’s return.

Republican Senator John Curtis raised similar questions, noting that Nvidia’s board had reversed its opposition to reinstating Huang while an independent investigation remained unfinished.

“Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board?” he wrote on X. “I’d like to know what changed.”

Senator Pete Ricketts, also a Republican, said Huang’s behavior did not warrant reinstatement and insisted the move did not excuse him from testifying before Congress.

Former Republican House speaker Newt Gingrich called for scrutiny of what he described as a national security issue “of enormous proportions.”

Outgoing Republican congressman Don Bacon alleged Huang had been “compromised and exploited by a Chinese spy,” demanding answers about who had authorized advanced chip sales to China.

And Republican Senator John Cornyn offered a terse response to Trump’s assurances.

“No national security risk? Based on what?” he wrote on X.

Trump declined earlier Monday to comment on a New York Times report that the woman at the center of the scandal had been in contact with an official from China’s principal intelligence agency during her affair with Huang.

title: Nigeria’s rice revolution collapses as 90 mills shutdown
description:
*Paddy production volume crashes *From 75% self-sufficiency country goes into massive imports *Farmers abandon rice, move to other crops *Operators blame policy reversals, others *Why rice value chain now struggling —FG







By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief, Jeff Agbodo (Abakiliki), Aliyu Usman (B
content:
*Paddy production volume crashes *From 75% self-sufficiency country goes into massive imports *Farmers abandon rice, move to other crops *Operators blame policy reversals, others *Why rice value chain now struggling —FG

By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief, Jeff Agbodo (Abakiliki), Aliyu Usman (Birnin Kebbi) and Sukanmi Akanni (Lagos)

Nigeria’s much-celebrated rice revolution is facing a major reversal, with more than 90 out of the country’s 260 integrated rice mills shutting down completely over acute paddy scarcity, rising production costs and the influx of cheaper imported rice.

This comes as the National Rice Development Strategy II, launched in 2021 to accelerate investments and self sufficiency in rice production expires next month.

The programme was part of the Buhari administration’s agricultural transformation agenda, which sought to reduce dependence on food imports and conserve foreign exchange.

Nigeria had announced 75 per cent self-sufficiency in rice production in February 2023 and projected to become a net exporter of the commodity by 2026.

The progress was showcased in January 2023 when the Federal Government, the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, and Rice Farmers Association of Nigeria, RIFAN, unveiled what they described as the world’s largest rice pyramids in Abuja.

The pyramids, comprising one million bags of paddy, were presented as evidence of Nigeria’s growing capacity to produce enough rice for domestic consumption and eventually export the commodity.

Nigeria’s annual rice import bill, estimated at about $1 billion in 2015, was said to have fallen to approximately $18.5 million by 2021.

But the year 2025 marked the beginning of the reversal of fortune with Paddy production, which had risen to 8.5 million tonnes in 2021, recording a sharp decline to about 4.8 million tonnes, while mill capacity utilisation dropped below 30 per cent.

Industry operators told Financial Vanguard that leading integrated mills, including Umza in Kano and Stallion in Lagos, are operating below 50 per cent of their installed capacity.

Speaking to the unfolding crisis the National Chairman of the Rice Millers Association of Nigeria, RIMAN, and Chairman, Board of Trustees of the Competitive African Rice Forum for Sustainable Development, CARF-FSD, Nigeria Chapter, Mr. Peter Dama, noted the rice policy inconsistency especially the suspension of the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme (ABP), which drove the country’s rice production surge between 2015 and 2023.

The industry operators listed inadequate agricultural financing, insecurity, escalating input costs and weak supply chains as key in the derailing of the growth over the past three years.

More recently they said that 2026 has witnessed a deliberate opening of the country’s borders allowing massive importation of cheaper foreign rice especially through Seme border with Benin Republic.

They lamented that Nigerians have invested heavily in building rice mills but the government has failed to sustain the agricultural production policy needed to keep them running.

Paradox of idle capacity, imports

Perhaps the most disturbing aspect of the current crisis is the contradiction between Nigeria’s enormous milling capacity and the shortage of locally produced paddy.

According to Dama, the country has installed rice milling capacity of approximately 7.5 million tonnes annually but currently produces only 4.1 million tonnes of paddy.

This leaves a huge gap between the capacity of the industry and the raw materials available to sustain its operations.

The operators noted cost over-run as the main factor stoking the crises as a tonne of paddy that sold for about N180,000 in 2021 now costs between N600,000 and N650,000.

Fertiliser prices, according to them, have increased from about N8,000 to N45,000, while petrol has risen from N250 to N1,400 per litre.

The input cost, according to them, has made the local rice now uncompetitive against the imported brands.

Dama said, ‘‘locally milled rice at current paddy prices costs higher than imported finished rice through Lagos ports.

‘‘This is a fundamental competitiveness problem that cannot be resolved merely by announcing restrictions on rice imports’’.

Consequently, some farmers are abandoning rice for alternative crops such as sesame and sorghum, further worsening the shortage of paddy.

The crises, according to the operators, goes beyond the fortunes of rice mill owners to include farmers, transporters, distributors, workers and millions of households that depend on rice as a staple food.

Why rice value chain now struggling — FG

A top official of the Federal Ministry of Agriculture, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said that the main challenge facing the rice value chain is policy inconsistency.

He said three other factors combined to create the current gap in rice production and the consumption needs of the Nigerian society.

According to him the growing population, rural-urban migration and the changing eating pattern of Nigerians combined to put pressure on rice, which is a staple food in almost every part of the country.

He said Nigeria remains the largest producer but also the largest importer of rice due to the inability of production to meet demand.

He revealed that the nation’s current self-sufficiency in rice production has dropped to 69 percent.

He however lamented that the cost of inputs such as fertilisers, seeds and agro-chemicals have challenged farmers lately, especially since the end of the Presidential Fertiliser Initiative (PFI) initiative when Urea was imported from Morocco and sold to fertilizer blenders at subsidized rate, who in turn sold fertilisers to farmers at subsidised rates.

According to him, fertiliser blenders now buy urea at market prices and that combined with the geopolitical crisis in the Middle East, especially the blockade of the Strait of Homuz, where 30 percent of fertiliser raw material pass, the fertiliser market has become more challenged, making the products more expensive and out of reach for many small-holder farmers.

He added that with very expensive inputs, paddy produced is sold to millers at high prices.

He confessed that millers who also face high operational costs due largely to dependence on diesel, rather than electricity come up with milled rice that cannot compete with the imported rice.

According to him, governments of the countries of origin of imported rice subsidise rice production for export and that as such, locally milled rice is struggling to compete with the imported rice.

He suggested that if rice production is to significantly increase in the country, the government must consider a way of subsidizing agricultural inputs, as is the case with other countries of the world.

Collapse of ABP

At the heart of the crisis, according to the operators, is the collapse of the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme, ABP, introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria under former Governor Godwin Emefiele.

The programme was one of the most ambitious attempts to address Nigeria’s food import dependence by linking smallholder farmers with processors and providing them with affordable agricultural financing.

Between 2015 and 2021, it reportedly helped increase paddy production from 2.5 million tonnes to 8.5 million tonnes.

Official rice imports, according to figures supplied by industry stakeholders, fell from 2.4 million tonnes to less than 400,000 tonnes during the period.

The programme’s strength was its integrated approach to agricultural production.

Rather than simply giving farmers cash, it provided seeds, fertiliser and herbicides on credit, with repayment made in paddy after harvest.

It also linked farmers to rice millers who guaranteed markets for their produce.

Interest rates were pegged at nine per cent, significantly below the commercial lending rates of about 28 per cent cited by industry stakeholders.

This arrangement addressed two major constraints confronting farmers: access to inputs and guaranteed markets.

It also provided millers with a more predictable supply of paddy.

However, the programme became controversial over allegations of politicisation, poor loan recovery and the inclusion of beneficiaries who were not genuine farmers.

Although more than N1.1 trillion was reportedly disbursed, loan recovery was said to have fallen below 30 per cent.

Consequently, a new CBN leadership discontinued the programme in 2023 without an effective replacement arrangement.

That decision created a financing vacuum in the rice value chain.

Dama estimates that more than 40 per cent of smallholder farmers who participated in the programme have since moved into other crops.

The Ministry of Agriculture’s dry-season wheat and rice initiatives, according to him, have not been sufficient to reach the majority of genuine farmers, while the Bank of Agriculture lacks the resources to provide financing on the scale required.

Dama further argued that ‘‘it is not necessarily that the ABP should be restored in its original form. Its weaknesses, particularly poor loan recovery and political interference, must be addressed.

‘‘But dismantling a programme without putting a functional alternative in place has exposed the industry to precisely the production challenges it was designed to overcome’’.

Cotonou smuggling challenge

Commenting on the influx of cheaper imported rice, which local millers say is undermining their ability to compete, Dama described the situation as an open secret, alleging that more than 2.5 million tonnes of foreign rice entered Nigeria through the Benin Republic’s Cotonou port and porous land borders so far in 2026.

He claimed that imported rice sells for between N52,000 and N60,000 per 50kg bag, compared with N75,000 to N80,000 for locally produced rice.

The price difference makes foreign rice attractive to consumers, particularly households struggling with the rising cost of living.

More troubling, according to him, is his allegation that some lower quality imported rice is repackaged and sold as Nigerian rice in major markets across Lagos, Abuja, Kano and Ibadan.

If the allegation is established, it points to a serious enforcement failure, with implications for consumer confidence, local investment and government revenue.

The tariff differential between Nigeria and Benin Republic is also contributing to the problem.

According to Dama, Nigeria imposes a 70 per cent duty, compared with 35 per cent in Benin, creating an incentive for traders to route rice imports through the neighbouring country.

He therefore called for the implementation of the ECOWAS Rice Roadmap 2025-2035, which provides for a common external tariff of 35 per cent for paddy and 50 per cent for milled rice across the 15 member states.

‘‘A harmonised regional tariff, combined with technology-driven border surveillance, could reduce the incentive for smuggling’’, Dama said.

Lagos Lake Rice disappears

The disappearance of Lake Rice from Lagos markets offers another illustration of the difficulty of sustaining agricultural partnerships beyond their initial political appeal.

In 2016, Lagos and Kebbi states entered into a Memorandum of Understanding to promote rice production in Kebbi and processing and distribution in Lagos.

The arrangement was designed to transport paddy from Kebbi to Lagos, where it would be milled, packaged and sold to consumers.

The initiative was intended to connect farmers in the North with a major consumer market in the South. But the arrangement eventually collapsed.

Investigations by Vanguard indicated that personal interests undermined the original agreement.

Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu’s Special Adviser on Agriculture and Food Systems, Dr Oluwarotimi Fashola, said the initiative was discontinued because the original understanding between the two states was not followed. According to him, the agreement was for Kebbi to supply paddy to Lagos for milling and packaging, rather than for finished rice supplied by a private consulting firm to be repackaged and distributed as Lake Rice.

The industry stakeholders said the collapse of the arrangement underscores the importance of transparency, accountability and strict adherence to agreed terms in public-private agricultural partnerships.

They also said it illustrates how potentially beneficial agricultural arrangements can fail when institutional interests and implementation shortcomings undermine their original objectives.

Women farmers and the financing gap

The consequences of the collapse of agricultural financing are also being felt by women farmers, particularly in Kebbi State.

The Chairperson of Kebbi State Female Farmers Associations, Hajia Hadiza Kola, identified inadequate funding as a major obstacle to expanding agricultural production following the end of the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme.

She said women faced additional social challenges because farming was traditionally regarded in parts of the state as an occupation largely reserved for men.

Some women also struggle to obtain the support of their husbands to participate in commercial farming.

Nevertheless, advocacy activities across towns and villages have encouraged hundreds of women to register with female farmers’ associations and take up farming, including through home gardening.

Their experience highlights the importance of making agricultural financing accessible to women and other groups that may be excluded from conventional farming arrangements.

Without affordable credit, the potential contribution of women to Nigeria’s food production drive will remain constrained.

Other failed rice project

Amidst the failures recorded in rice projects across Northern parts there are other fortune reversals of the Nigerian rice value-chain in other regions that grow the commodity.

The government of Chief Martin Elechi in Ebonyi State established modern rice cluster mills in three senatorial districts, located at Izzi, Ikwo and Oso Edda around 2013.

The mills started with very big expectation to complement the existing Abakaliki rice mill with morden machines. The mill started simultaneously churning out foreign-like polished rice and with good packaging with the brand name EbonyRice. But the mills have turned to ghosts of themselves as at 2025.

A former worker at the mill Mr. Onyeka Ndukwe Nkama, told Vanguard that Governor Elechi’s administration handed over the mills to Chief David Umahi who handed over a dying project to the present administration.

The modern mills started closing down one after the other starting from the mill at Oso Edda to Ikwo and now the Izzi mill has finally shutdown.

Nkama stated: “The managers had complained of lack of enough Paddy to feed the mills, they said that Ebonyi Rice farmers could not produce enough rice to run three mills. At some time, they were sourcing rice Paddy from the northern part of the country to feed the mills but to no avail.

“So, after some time some parts of the machines started rusting and could not perform effectively. So, gradually the mills started packing up. I learnt that the mill at Izzi that worked last but I’m not sure whether it still processing rice. For some time now all the workers at the mills had left to look for other jobs.” Chief Charles Ugwu established a private rice mill at Ikwo which produced high quality rice branded as Ebony Gold and Ebony Silver. The mill has also shut down due to similar Paddy problems.

Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief, Jeff Agbodo (Abakiliki), Aliyu Usman (Birnin Kebbi) & Sukanmi Akanni (Lagos) contributed to this report.

Vanguard News

title: ‘I would love to speak with Azikiwe’, Makinde names preferred leader
description:
Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has named Nigeria’s first President, the late Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, as the Nigerian leader he would most like to seek advice from, dead or alive.
Makinde made the remark during a special rooftop conversation with Channels Television’s Kayode Okikiolu in a video shared
content:
Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has named Nigeria’s first President, the late Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, as the Nigerian leader he would most like to seek advice from, dead or alive.

Makinde made the remark during a special rooftop conversation with Channels Television’s Kayode Okikiolu in a video shared on X on Monday, where he was asked which Nigerian leader he would like to speak with.

“The Nigerian leader, dead or alive, I would like to speak to is Baba Nnamdi Azikiwe,” he said.

The governor explained that although he held the late Chief Obafemi Awolowo in high regard, he was particularly interested in understanding the decisions Azikiwe made at a critical point in Nigeria’s history.

He said Azikiwe was at the centre of a crucial moment in the country’s history and that he wanted to understand the thinking behind a decision he believed Nigeria was still grappling with 66 years later.

Makinde said, “Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe was there, just at the centre, and he took a decision that we’re battling with sixty-six years after. I would love to really have an insight and ask him, ‘Papa, how did you get here?’”

The conversation comes as Makinde pursues his presidential ambition on the platform of the Allied Peoples Movement ahead of the 2027 general election.

He is expected to run with former Director-General of the Department of State Services, Lawal Daura, as his running mate.

Makinde’s admiration for Azikiwe is not new.

At the 12th Annual Zik Lecture Series in Awka, Anambra State, on November 16, 2023, he praised the late nationalist’s commitment to Nigerian unity and argued that the country needed restructuring to promote fairness and strengthen its federal system.

He had described Azikiwe as a dynamic leader who was willing to adapt to changing political realities, adding that Nigeria should focus on building a structure that works for all its federating units.

title: 2027: ‘As You Do For Me, I Do For You,’ Tinubu Seeks Igbo Support In Lagos
description: President Bola Tinubu has appealed to Igbo residents in Lagos State to support his re-election bid in the 2027 general elections.President Tinubu made the call while addressing Igbo stakeholders at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, Iganmu, Lagos, on Monday.﻿President Tinubu said
content:
President Bola Tinubu has appealed to Igbo residents in Lagos State to support his re-election bid in the 2027 general elections.

President Tinubu made the call while addressing Igbo stakeholders at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, Iganmu, Lagos, on Monday.

President Tinubu said that though he was displeased when he lost the 2023 election in the state, which is considered a stronghold of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), the matter had been settled.

“Some of you didn’t vote for me in 2023; I vex o. We don settle. Get your PVC,” he urged the crowd.

Tinubu also asked if they would vote for him, to which they replied with a resounding “Yes.”

After receiving assurance from the stakeholders to back his re-election bid, the president said, “Come January 16, get your PVC; you come vote. Agreement na agreement o, na Bola Tinubu be APC o. As you do for me, I do for you.”

‘Follow Who Know Road’

President Tinubu called for national unity and collective responsibility, urging Nigerians to see themselves as one people with a shared future, in the interest of the country.

“You must follow who know road. I have to work hard to make sure the economy improves, to ensure that your children are in school, to eliminate crises in the universities, to build good roads that will maintain our cars.

“The future is in our hands. For every one of us, our children must be in school. Because we are poor doesn’t mean they shouldn’t attend the universities,” he added.

Tinubu further said the country must rise above its divisions, noting that its development depended on the participation and commitment of all its people.

Also speaking, the Governor of Lagos State, Mr Babajide Sanwo-Olu, urged Igbo residents to support Tinubu’s re-election and vote for all candidates of the APC in the 2027 general elections.

The governor also implored them to work for the emergence of the Deputy Governor and APC governorship candidate, Obafemi Hamzat, as the next Governor of Lagos State.

During the meeting, the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi; the Minister of State for Budget and Planning, Doris Uzoka-Anite; and the former Minister of Labour and Employment, Nkiruka Onyejeocha, as well as other Igbo leaders and stakeholders, assured President Tinubu of their support.

The Independent National Electoral Commission said Peter Obi, who was the candidate of the Labour Party, polled 582,454 votes in Lagos, higher than the 572,606 votes polled by Tinubu in the February 25, 2023 presidential election.

Lagos, Nigeria’s commercial hub, has one of the highest numbers of registered voters for the 2027 general elections.

Emphasising the electoral importance of Lagos, Tinubu described it as a big deal to him.

”To me, Lagos is the big deal. How can you have seven million registered voters and produce 100,000-200,000 votes? That’s failure.

“Even if you win, and say, ‘A win is a win,’ no. You have to generate the maximum,” he said during a prayer session at the hall of the Yoruba Tennis Club in Lagos, where he urged party leaders to generate the maximum win for the APC.

The post 2027: ‘As You Do For Me, I Do For You,’ Tinubu Seeks Igbo Support In Lagos appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Delta attack: Gunmen wanted to kill me – Omo-Agege
description:
Former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, has alleged that gunmen who attacked his campaign team in Delta State repeatedly shouted his name and declared that they wanted to kill him.
PUNCH Online reports that four members of Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation were reportedly killed.
Omo-Agege,
content:
Former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, has alleged that gunmen who attacked his campaign team in Delta State repeatedly shouted his name and declared that they wanted to kill him.

PUNCH Online reports that four members of Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation were reportedly killed.

Omo-Agege, who is seeking election to the Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general election on the platform of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, said he escaped because of the intervention of his Department of State Services escorts.

He made the allegation on Monday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today, while recounting the attack on his campaign team in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.

“Right there at the venue, while they were shooting, we could hear them say, ‘It is Omo-Agege we want to kill. We must kill Omo-Agege.’

“But I was lucky because my DSS details were very professional. In fact, after God, the only reason I am alive today is because of the DSS operatives who were with me,” he said.

The former lawmaker described the incident as a premeditated attack, alleging that there had been a build-up to the violence.

He questioned why he would be singled out for attack when several other politicians were also contesting elective positions.

Omo-Agege said the gunmen opened fire less than five minutes after he began addressing supporters at the campaign venue.

According to him, he had moved towards the side of his vehicle to make eye contact with members of the audience when the shooting started.

“It was by divine intervention. As I was speaking, I just moved over to the side of the vehicle to be able to make eye contact with those I was speaking with. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started,” he said.

He said four members of his campaign organisation were killed in the attack, while about 15 others sustained injuries, some of them critically.

PUNCH Online had reported that Moses Anaughe, a former member of the Delta State House of Assembly and a personal assistant to Omo-Agege, died at the Ughelli Central Hospital after he was reportedly shot during the attack.

The campaign organisation had also said that four people were killed and four others injured in the incident. It identified another aide, Akima Efemena Umukoro, among the dead.

In a statement issued on Monday by his media adviser, Sunny Areh, the campaign organisation described the incident as an assassination attempt on Omo-Agege during a campaign tour in Uduere.

It alleged that armed men opened fire on the former deputy senate president and his entourage while he was addressing supporters.

The organisation called on the Nigeria Police Force to conduct an independent and thorough investigation into the incident.

It also appealed to the Inspector-General of Police, the DSS, the Independent National Electoral Commission, civil society organisations and the international community to ensure the safety of political candidates and their supporters.

The campaign organisation urged supporters to remain calm and avoid retaliation, adding that its ward-to-ward campaign activities across Delta Central would continue.

The post Delta attack: Gunmen wanted to kill me – Omo-Agege appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Gov. Mutfwang loses brother
description:
By Golok Nanmwa







Plateau State Governor, Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang, has lost his elder brother, Arc. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang, who died Sunday night following a protracted illness, family sources have disclosed.







The Plateau State Government confirmed the death on Monday, as the State Exec
content:
By Golok Nanmwa

Plateau State Governor, Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang, has lost his elder brother, Arc. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang, who died Sunday night following a protracted illness, family sources have disclosed.

The Plateau State Government confirmed the death on Monday, as the State Executive Council and the Plateau State Inter-Religious Council paid separate condolence visits to the Governor’s family at the Government House, Jos.

The Deputy Governor, Ngo Josephine Piyo, who led members of the State Executive Council on a condolence visit to the Governor’s Residence at the Old Government House, Jos, described the deceased as “a distinguished personality, a devoted family man, a lover of peace and a patriotic Nigerian who made meaningful contributions to public service.”

She said the Council received the news of his passing “with profound shock and sadness,” noting that his death was “not only a painful loss to the Mutfwang family but also a significant loss to Plateau State and the nation, given his contributions to society and his exemplary life.”

Piyo prayed for the peaceful repose of his soul and asked Almighty God to grant the Governor, the bereaved family and all those mourning his demise “the strength, grace and fortitude to bear the tragic loss.”

In a separate visit, the Plateau State Inter-Religious Council also condoled with the Governor and his family over the death of Arc. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang.

The delegation, led by the Emir of Wase, Alhaji (Dr.) Muhammadu Sambo Haruna, who spoke on behalf of the Council’s Co-Chairman, Rev. Prof. Pandam Yamsat, described the deceased’s passing as “a painful loss to the family and the state.”

Haruna acknowledged the inevitability of death as part of the human experience, urging the bereaved family to “find solace in the sovereignty and wisdom of Almighty God.”

He also prayed that God would grant the family “the comfort, strength and resilience needed to navigate this difficult period.”

Responding on behalf of the family during the separate condolence visits, Mr. Jonathan Mutfwang expressed “profound appreciation to both delegations for their thoughtful gesture, solidarity and prayers.”

He noted that their presence had brought “considerable comfort and encouragement to the bereaved family at this difficult time.”

Jonathan also prayed for God’s continued protection, blessings and preservation upon members of the delegations.

The family disclosed that the burial of the late Arc. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang has been scheduled for Thursday, November 26, 2026.

The condolence visits were disclosed in a statement signed by the Director of Press and Public Affairs to the Governor, Gyang Bere, PhD, and made available to newsmen in Jos on Monday.

The post Gov. Mutfwang loses brother appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: N582m fraud: Court threatens ex-NNPC cooperative president with arrest
description:
The Federal Capital Territory High Court in Gwarinpa, Abuja, on Monday threatened to issue a warrant of arrest against a former President of the NNPC Staff Multi-Purpose Cooperative Society, Olalekan Ogunbayo, over his repeated failure to appear for arraignment in an alleged N582m fraud case.
Justic
content:
The Federal Capital Territory High Court in Gwarinpa, Abuja, on Monday threatened to issue a warrant of arrest against a former President of the NNPC Staff Multi-Purpose Cooperative Society, Olalekan Ogunbayo, over his repeated failure to appear for arraignment in an alleged N582m fraud case.

Justice Leslie Wike gave the warning while adjourning the case until December 15, 2026, for the arraignment of Ogunbayo and his co-defendant, Abolade Nurudeen.

This was contained in a statement on the anti-graft agency’s social media handle on Monday.

“Justice Leslie Wike of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, High Court in Gwarinpa, Abuja, on Monday, November 23, 2026, ordered the former President of the NNPC Staff Multi-Purpose Cooperative Society, Olalekan Ogunbayo, to appear in court on December 15, 2026, for his arraignment over an alleged N582m.

“The judge warned that Ogunbayo risked a warrant of arrest if he failed to appear on the next adjourned date,” the statement partly read.

At Monday’s proceedings, prosecution counsel, R.U. Adagba, informed the court that the matter was scheduled for arraignment but Ogunbayo was absent.

Adagba said the defendant was also absent at the previous sitting on October 26, despite an undertaking by his counsel to produce him in court.

She urged the court to issue a warrant of arrest against Ogunbayo pursuant to Sections 35, 114 and 115 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act, 2015, citing his repeated failure to attend proceedings without explanation.

The prosecution counsel said efforts to secure his appearance, including written invitations and attempts to reach his surety, had proved unsuccessful.

She further argued that Ogunbayo was aware of the criminal proceedings, having personally deposed to an affidavit in support of a bail application before the court on October 13.

However, counsel to the first defendant, Innocent Adoo, acknowledged that he had undertaken to produce his client but explained that the prosecution had yet to serve him with a copy of the charge.

Adoo told the court that Ogunbayo contacted his head of chambers earlier on Monday, claiming he had received invitations from the Inspector-General of Police and the Code of Conduct Bureau over the same subject matter.

He said a copy of the charge would enable his client to establish that the matter was already before the court when responding to the invitations.

In her response, Adagba described the defence counsel’s position on service as a misrepresentation, insisting that the court had not made any order authorising service of the charge on him on behalf of the first defendant.

She said the prosecution had written to Ogunbayo’s office on October 22 and made efforts to reach his surety to ensure his appearance.

Adagba also clarified that the EFCC was prosecuting the charge before the court and was not a party to any separate proceedings involving the police or the Code of Conduct Bureau.

In her ruling, Justice Wike directed that the charge be served on Ogunbayo through his counsel, Adoo.

The judge warned that the defendant risked a warrant of arrest if he failed to appear at the next sitting.

The matter was subsequently adjourned until December 15, 2026 for arraignment.

The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission is prosecuting the defendants on an eight-count charge bordering on criminal misappropriation, conspiracy and corruption over the alleged diversion of N582m realised from the sale of a property belonging to the cooperative society.

The post N582m fraud: Court threatens ex-NNPC cooperative president with arrest appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: South-East governors are with me, working for my re-election — Tinubu
description:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru







Ahead of the January 16 presidential election, President Bola Tinubu on Monday told the Igbo community in Lagos and their leaders that all the South-East governors are with him on the journey to make Nigeria a better place and are working for his re-election.







The
content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

Ahead of the January 16 presidential election, President Bola Tinubu on Monday told the Igbo community in Lagos and their leaders that all the South-East governors are with him on the journey to make Nigeria a better place and are working for his re-election.

The President said he was excited and that he would go home happy and eat because of their endorsement of his second term.

He thanked the Igbo communities and business leaders in Lagos for their resolve to support his re-election on January 16, 2027.

He assured them of his administration’s commitment to inclusive governance, national unity and equity for all Nigerians.

President Tinubu gave the assurance while addressing youths, elders and leaders of Ndigbo during a town hall meeting organised

by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiatives at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts, Iganmu, Lagos State.

He called on Ndigbo to strengthen their unity, deepen their participation in national politics, and work with other ethnic groups to build a peaceful, prosperous and united Nigeria.

To reaffirm his commitment to national unity, President Tinubu joined the gathering to sing the national anthem a second time.

“I didn’t believe you would turn out this many; I am very, very happy. May God bless you, and may God continue to guide and bless our country. It is a great honour for me to be here before you as your president.

“I can commit to one thing: the unity of Nigeria. Though tribes and tongues may differ, in brotherhood we stand. None of us told God where we would be born or what language we would speak when we were born. Whether you are Igbo or Hausa, you have no

control over yourself. God created you and created that opportunity. We are all Nigerians.

“Let’s see ourselves as individuals living in the same house, geographically called Nigeria,” the President told the gathering.

The President said his administration recognises the significant contributions of the Igbo communities to Nigeria’s economic growth, assuring them that no section of the country would be left behind under the Renewed Hope Agenda.

President Tinubu appreciated the leadership of all the market leaders in Lagos for leaving their businesses to be at the gathering.

“To all of you, I am grateful for one thing: that you are here this afternoon. You left your businesses and money-making opportunities to come and listen to the president, and I must say thank you,” he said.

The President expressed his determination to consolidate his administration’s economic gains.

He said national development requires collective commitment, mutual understanding and cooperation, urging the Igbo community to embrace dialogue and constructive engagement to address challenges and advance their interests within the Nigerian federation.

A statement by the presidential spokesman, Bayo Onanuga said: “President Tinubu told the gathering that all the South-East

governors are with him on the journey to make Nigeria a better place and are working for his re-election.”

He mentioned Chief Chidi Anyeagbu, owner of Chisco Motors; Dave Umahi; Doris Uzoka-Anite; and Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, who were at the gathering, as people with whom he has close connections.

President Tinubu explained some of the reasons behind his policies, such as ensuring that tertiary institutions are no longer paralysed by union strikes.

“To eliminate the crisis in the universities, to build good roads and train the engineers who will maintain our cars, our children must be in school. Just because they are poor doesn’t mean they must not go to university or develop.

“We are doing that with NELFUND. The university is stable today because we are doing well. We are putting money into agriculture and trading, and anyone in the trade business can apply to the Bank of Industry and get a loan; anyone in agriculture can take a small farmers’ loan.

“We have to maintain this country for the sake of every one of us. The critical line in our national anthem is what I’m standing here for. I begged for it, and I am ready to serve.

“And I served the first term. The constitution says I can ask for a second term. I want a second term. As you are here today, you make me happy, you make me excited, and I will go home happy and eat akpu,” he said.

President Tinubu also called on Ndigbo residents in Lagos to participate actively and vote for him, APC governorship candidate Obafemi Hamzat, and other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections.

He commended the organisers of the town hall meeting for providing a platform for constructive engagement between the Federal Government and the Igbo community.

On his part, the host governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, rallied members of the Ndigbo to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, assuring the President of massive votes from the state in the January 16, 2027, presidential election.

Sanwo-Olu described the turnout of Igbo leaders, traders and business owners as proof that Lagos residents were united behind the President, despite the meeting being held on a Monday, when many participants had to leave their businesses to attend.

The governor urged the community to sustain the unity and support, saying Lagos would deliver an unprecedented number of votes for Tinubu.

He also praised Tinubu as a detribalised Nigerian and nationalist, saying his administration had promoted development across the six geopolitical zones and strengthened national unity.

Sanwo-Olu further commended the President for what he described as economic stability, increased investment and opportunities for young people, while thanking him for his contributions to Lagos State.

Describing the gathering as a reflection of the “One Lagos” spirit, the governor said the presence of people from different ethnic backgrounds demonstrated that residents could work together in support of a common political cause.

In her remarks, the convener of the meeting and Minister of State for Budget and Economic Planning, Dr Doris Uzoka-Anite, declared the Igbo community’s commitment in Lagos State to supporting President Tinubu’s re-election bid, saying the community had resolved to unite behind his leadership.

She said the Ndigbo had commenced grassroots mobilisation across Lagos State, with structures established at the polling-unit level ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

Also speaking, the former Minister of State for Labour and Employment, Hon. Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, assured President Bola Tinubu of the Ndigbo’s support for his 2027 re-election bid, saying the gathering of Igbo leaders and stakeholders in Lagos demonstrated their unity and commitment to the President.

She said the community had recognised the importance of building political alliances with other geopolitical zones to achieve its future presidential ambition.

The leader of the Ndigbo Traders Association in Lagos, Prince Tony Nwakeze, pledged the members’ support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, while appealing for access to loans at a 5 per cent interest rate to help traders transition from importation to local manufacturing.

Nwakeze said traders from Alaba, Trade Fair and Ladipo markets were seeking financial support to empower young people and expand their businesses.

He also assured the President that traders were prepared to organise themselves and adopt a cross-guarantee arrangement to ensure repayment of any loans granted to their members.

He also pledged that the market leadership would honour agreements reached with the government, stressing that traders had learnt from previous misunderstandings and were committed to sustaining a cordial relationship with the Lagos State Government.

He thanked the President for attending the meeting and promised that traders across Lagos markets would support him and honour every agreement reached with the government.

“We, the market people, will stand with you, support you and honour every agreement we enter into today,” he said.

The post South-East governors are with me, working for my re-election — Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Ogun poly to graduate 4,817 students at 50th anniversary
description:
Ogun State Polytechnic of Health and Allied Sciences, Ilese-Ijebu, is set to graduate 4,817 students on Thursday at its 4th Combined Convocation Ceremony as the institution marks its 50th anniversary.
The polytechnic has also received N339.5m from the Nigerian Education Loan Fund for about 1,300 stu
content:
Ogun State Polytechnic of Health and Allied Sciences, Ilese-Ijebu, is set to graduate 4,817 students on Thursday at its 4th Combined Convocation Ceremony as the institution marks its 50th anniversary.

The polytechnic has also received N339.5m from the Nigerian Education Loan Fund for about 1,300 students across three academic sessions: 2023/2024, 2024/2025 and 2025/2026.

The development comes as the institution commended Governor Dapo Abiodun for increasing its monthly subvention from N5m to N30m.

The Rector of the polytechnic, Dr Rasaki Yinka Akinbo, disclosed this on Monday at a briefing ahead of the institution’s 4th combined convocation and 50th anniversary celebrations.

Akinbo used the occasion to highlight the institution’s major academic, infrastructural and administrative achievements while appealing to the state government for increased funding and inclusion in the Tertiary Education Trust Fund intervention programme.

The rector said the graduating students comprised 2,191 from the 2024/2025 academic session and 2,626 from the 2025/2026 session, with a combined total of 291 students graduating with distinctions.

He explained that 191 students from the 2024/2025 session earned distinctions, while another 100 achieved the same academic feat in the 2025/2026 session.

Giving a breakdown of the graduating students, Akinbo said, “The 2024/2025 session produced 377 Higher National Diploma graduates, 56 of whom earned distinctions; 606 National Diploma graduates, with 25 distinctions; 1,109 Diploma graduates, including 35 distinctions; and 99 certificate graduates, of whom three earned distinctions.

“For the 2025/2026 session, 395 students graduated with HND qualifications, including 33 with distinctions, while 1,146 obtained National Diplomas, with 26 earning distinctions.”

He added that 980 students graduated from the Diploma programme, including 39 with distinctions, while 105 completed certificate programmes, with two earning distinctions.

The rector identified Saliu Fatimah Abisola of the Health Information Management Department as the overall best graduating student of the combined convocation, having recorded a cumulative grade point average of 3.88 in the 2024/2025 academic session.

He said Monsurat Onifade, also of the Health Information Management Department, emerged as the best graduating student for the 2025/2026 academic session with a CGPA of 3.85.

Akinbo also disclosed that the institution had recorded a significant increase in students’ participation in the Federal Government’s student loan scheme, NELFUND, with beneficiaries rising from 40 in the 2023/2024 academic session to more than 1,000 in subsequent sessions.

He explained that “Initially, our students did not want to embrace NELFUND, but after a lot of enlightenment, they have embraced it because it remains a very wonderful initiative that the Federal Government has introduced to ensure that no one is deprived of tertiary education because of lack of funding.

“In the 2023/2024 academic session, we had 40 applications processed, and that amounted to N5,413,000. Then, for 2024/2025, we had another 109 beneficiaries, and that amounted to N28,141,000.

“In 2025/2026, about 1,149 students benefited, and that amounted to N211,122,000. And then we also had another one for 2025/2026, which amounted to N94,824,000. The total amount received from NELFUND so far is N339,500,000.”

Reflecting on the institution’s five-decade journey, Akinbo recalled that the polytechnic was established on September 28, 1976, as Ogun State School of Health Technology, initially operating from a temporary site at Itamogiri under its pioneer principal, Dr V.B. Odunlami.

The rector disclosed that the management had secured resource accreditation for 15 new programmes and accreditation for five existing programmes, describing the development as part of efforts to strengthen the institution’s academic standing and meet the standards of the National Board for Technical Education.

He also said the institution had improved its entrance and internal examination processes, while its admission procedures had been upgraded to align with Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board requirements.

Despite the progress recorded, Akinbo identified inadequate funding, the need for additional facilities and infrastructural expansion as some of the major challenges confronting the institution.

He appealed to the Ogun State Government to increase its financial support, particularly for programme accreditation, noting that the process required substantial resources.

Among the institution’s pressing needs, he listed the construction of a 1,000-seat ICT centre, a 2,000-capacity auditorium, a teaching hospital and entrance and adjoining roads within the campus.

He also appealed to the state government to facilitate the institution’s inclusion as a beneficiary of TETFund interventions.

Akinbo, however, commended Abiodun for increasing the polytechnic’s monthly subvention from N5m to N30m, saying the gesture would help offset some of the backlog of allowances that forced lecturers at the institution to embark on a recent strike.

title: Gombe community seeks justice for three killed by Air Force personnel
description:
The Lawanti Community Development Foundation has demanded an independent investigation and prosecution of Nigerian Air Force personnel over the alleged killing of three residents and shooting of 11 others in Lawanti, Akko North Local Council Development Area of Gombe State.
The foundation, which acc
content:
The Lawanti Community Development Foundation has demanded an independent investigation and prosecution of Nigerian Air Force personnel over the alleged killing of three residents and shooting of 11 others in Lawanti, Akko North Local Council Development Area of Gombe State.

The foundation, which accused personnel of the 109 Combat Reconnaissance Base of opening fire on residents on November 20, also demanded compensation for the families of the deceased and injured victims.

In a statement issued on Monday and signed by its Executive Director and Programme Manager, the foundation condemned what it described as an act of brutality and indiscriminate shooting, insisting that the community would pursue justice through lawful means.

According to the foundation, “the incident began following an allegation by Air Force personnel that an electrical cable connected to a transformer within their facility near the Gombe Airport had been stolen.”

It said the personnel reported the matter to the District Head of Lawanti, who reportedly assured them of the community’s cooperation in identifying those responsible.

However, the foundation alleged that military personnel later invaded the community around 7pm, assaulting residents, intimidating traders and forcing businesses to close.

The development reportedly triggered protests along the Gombe-Bauchi Highway, where residents barricaded sections of the road with burning tyres.

The foundation said calm was eventually restored following the intervention of the Emir of Gona, the Chairman of Akko North LCDA and other community stakeholders.

It, however, alleged that the personnel returned shortly after the situation had been brought under control and opened fire on residents, leaving 14 people with gunshot wounds, three of whom later died.

The deceased have since been buried in accordance with Islamic rites, while the 11 survivors are receiving treatment for varying degrees of injuries, the statement added.

Expressing outrage over the incident, the foundation said, “No stolen cable, regardless of its value, can ever be worth the life of a single innocent Nigerian.”

It added, “Even where a crime has been committed, the responsibility of security personnel is to investigate, identify suspects and ensure that justice takes its lawful course, not to subject an entire community to collective punishment.”

The foundation stressed that its condemnation of the alleged shootings should not be mistaken for hostility towards the military, noting that residents respected the sacrifices of the armed forces in defending the country.

“The uniform of the Nigerian Air Force is a symbol of honour, discipline and national service. It must never become an instrument of oppression against the very citizens it is meant to protect,” it said.

It also warned against a situation in which civilians could allegedly be assaulted or killed without accountability because those involved wore military uniforms.

The community commended Governor Muhammadu Yahaya for condemning the incident, ordering an investigation and dispatching a government delegation led by the Secretary to the State Government, Professor Ibrahim Abubakar Njodi, to engage with affected residents.

It also acknowledged the governor’s pledge to provide medical and humanitarian assistance to the injured and bereaved families but urged him to ensure that the investigation resulted in concrete action.

Among its demands, the foundation called for an independent commission of inquiry, with civilian representation, to investigate the incident and make its findings public.

It also urged the Chief of the Air Staff and the Minister of Defence to identify personnel involved in the alleged operation and ensure that those found culpable were prosecuted.

The foundation further called on the National Human Rights Commission to investigate the alleged extrajudicial killings, indiscriminate shootings and other human rights violations.

It demanded adequate compensation for the families of the three deceased residents and the survivors, as well as comprehensive medical treatment and rehabilitation for the injured at no personal cost.

The community also sought guarantees against intimidation or reprisals targeting victims, eyewitnesses and community leaders.

Reiterating its commitment to peace, the foundation urged youths in Lawanti to remain calm and avoid actions capable of escalating tensions.

“We will pursue every lawful and constitutional avenue available to ensure that the deaths of our three community members are not swept under the carpet and that the injured receive the justice and support they deserve,” the statement added.

It called on civil society organisations, human rights groups and the media to support its demand for justice, declaring that the lives of Lawanti residents must not be treated as expendable.

title: UK, 13 nations acknowledge ICJ ruling on Rohingya genocide
description:
The UK and 13 other countries on Monday “acknowledged” the top UN court’s ruling that Myanmar perpetrated genocide against its Rohingya minority as London announced new sanctions.
The foreign ministers of Australia, Belgium, Canada, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Estonia, Iceland, Latvia, Luxembourg, New Z
content:
The UK and 13 other countries on Monday “acknowledged” the top UN court’s ruling that Myanmar perpetrated genocide against its Rohingya minority as London announced new sanctions.

The foreign ministers of Australia, Belgium, Canada, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Estonia, Iceland, Latvia, Luxembourg, New Zealand, Portugal, Spain, The Gambia and the United Kingdom said Myanmar had “violated its obligations under the Genocide Convention”.

“We underscore that the Court’s judgment is binding upon Myanmar and call on Myanmar to comply fully with its obligations under international law, including the Court’s decision,” they said in a joint statement.

The UK separately said it “formally recognises” genocide against the Rohingya and announced sanctions on five senior military figures.

“The horrific violence and persecution inflicted on the Rohingya cannot go unanswered,” UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said.

The sanctions include asset freezes and travel bans, a Foreign Office statement said, adding that London “also intends to introduce legislation targeting the export and supply of aviation fuel to Myanmar”.

“The UK is providing an additional £5m in new funding to support Rohingya and other communities with essential lifesaving and life-affirming services to approximately 350,000 people who need it most in Rakhine state, where humanitarian need is most acute,” the statement added.

It said a further £3 million would “go towards strengthening accountability and justice for survivors of human rights abuses across Myanmar.”

On November 19 in a historic verdict, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruled Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority during a 2017 crackdown in the western Rakhine state.

The ruling was the first time in the ICJ’s 80-year history that it has determined that a state committed genocide.

Myanmar’s government called the ruling unfair and a “great disappointment”.

Shortly after the verdict, Britain announced it would expel Myanmar’s defence attaché.

AFP
