title: Delta govt imposes curfew in Ughelli North after campaign rally violence
description:
The Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area following reported violence at a campaign rally of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Uduere Community, which allegedly left some people dead and several others injured.







The curfew, whic
content:
The Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area following reported violence at a campaign rally of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Uduere Community, which allegedly left some people dead and several others injured.

The curfew, which takes effect from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. daily, will remain in force until further notice.

The Delta State Police Command disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bright Edafe.

According to the statement, the police have commenced investigations to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible.

The Command urged residents to comply strictly with the curfew and cooperate with security personnel to maintain peace and public safety.

The statement reads, “The Command therefore urges residents of Ughelli North Local Government Area to comply strictly with the curfew imposed by the Delta State Government, restricting movement between 1800hrs to 0600hrs until further notice. Residents are advised to remain calm and cooperate with security personnel in the interest of public safety.

“The Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, CP Samuel E. Erale, psc, mnips, has directed intensified security operations in the affected area to prevent further violence and maintain law and order. The CP has ordered a full-scale investigation and assures residents of the state that anyone found culpable will face the full weight of the law, irrespective of political affiliation or status, and urges members of the public to provide credible information to assist ongoing investigations.”

Erale also extended his condolences to the families of those who died and wished the injured a speedy recovery.

He reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to protecting lives and property while ensuring a peaceful environment for lawful

political activities.

The police commissioner further warned political actors and their supporters against thuggery, intimidation and the unlawful use of firearms.

He stressed that political differences must never be allowed to degenerate into violence or loss of lives.

title: NEC approves additional N130bn for Police training, raises funding to N230bn
description:
The National Economic Council (NEC) has approved an additional N130 billion for the rehabilitation of police training institutions across Nigeria, bringing the total funding for the programme to N230 billion.
The additional allocation is expected to speed up rehabilitation work, upgrade training fac
content:
The National Economic Council (NEC) has approved an additional N130 billion for the rehabilitation of police training institutions across Nigeria, bringing the total funding for the programme to N230 billion.

The additional allocation is expected to speed up rehabilitation work, upgrade training facilities and prepare police institutions for the proposed recruitment of 50,000 personnel.

The approval followed a presentation by the NEC Ad-Hoc Committee on the rehabilitation of police training institutions, chaired by Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah.

The committee informed the council that rehabilitation work was ongoing at 13 locations nationwide, with about 30 per cent of the projects completed.

NEC had earlier approved N100 billion for the programme after the committee was established in October 2025 on the recommendation of President Bola Tinubu.

According to a statement issued on Monday by Stanley Nkwocha, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Media and Communications in the Office of the Vice-President, the new funding would strengthen the capacity of the institutions to handle increased recruitment and training demands.

The statement said the intervention would also support preparations for the recruitment of 50,000 police personnel and improve the country’s security training infrastructure.

The approval was among the major decisions reached at the council’s 162nd meeting on Monday, where members also endorsed two development projects expected to receive a combined $850 million in proposed World Bank financing.

The projects are the $350 million Accelerating Resilience through Investment Systems and Engagement (ARISE-Nigeria) Project and the $500 million State-Led Early Childhood Development Programme.

The ARISE-Nigeria Project is a six-year initiative designed to strengthen Nigeria’s capacity to prepare for and respond to natural disasters, including floods, droughts and fires.

According to the statement, the programme will support the development of emergency operations centres, early warning systems, weather monitoring and disaster response financing at federal and state levels.

Between five and 10 states are expected to participate in the initial phase, with selection based on their exposure to disaster risks, institutional readiness and commitment to emergency preparedness.

The second project is designed to improve access to healthcare, nutrition, early learning and protection services for children across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

It will establish early childhood development hubs to connect primary healthcare facilities with childcare, preschool education and other essential social services, particularly in underserved communities.

The proposed $500 million World Bank financing for the programme is expected to be complemented by a potential $30 million grant from the Global Financing Facility.

On the economy, the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, presented an update showing that Nigeria’s real Gross Domestic Product grew by 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, compared with 4.23 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025.

The report also indicated that headline inflation declined for the fifth consecutive month to 14.06 per cent in October, while the country’s external reserves stood at $54.87 billion as of November 12, 2026.

Nigeria’s trade surplus also increased from N10.2 trillion in the first half of 2025 to N20.1 trillion in the corresponding period of 2026.

Similarly, net revenue distributed through the Federation Account Allocation Committee rose by 44 per cent, from N15.2 trillion in 2024 to N21.9 trillion in 2025.

Despite the improvements in key economic indicators, Oyedele noted that households and businesses were yet to experience sufficient relief, particularly in food prices, electricity costs, access to affordable credit and employment.

The statement added that food inflation stood at 19.13 per cent in October, while high lending rates and energy costs continued to place pressure on businesses and household incomes.

The council also called for stronger cooperation between the National Identity Management Commission and state governments to accelerate national identity registration and the integration of the National Identification Number into public services.

On pension reforms, NEC approved a proposal presented by the Director-General of the National Pension Commission, Omolola Oloworaran, titled “Securing the Retirement of Nigerian Workers While Strengthening State Finances.”

The council urged state governors to establish timelines for implementing the Contributory Pension Scheme and directed their administrative and finance teams to work with PenCom on the necessary arrangements.

Earlier, Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who chairs the council, said the success of the Tinubu administration’s economic reforms would depend on the development of strong institutions capable of sustaining their benefits.

Shettima called on federal ministries and state governments to work together in addressing practical challenges, while ensuring that the impact of government policies on citizens remained a priority.

He also urged states to learn from successful practices in other jurisdictions while taking into account differences in their capacities and circumstances.

Speaking about the ARISE-Nigeria Project, the Vice-President said the initiative was intended to reduce the economic and social damage caused by disasters, particularly to families, businesses and public services.

He stressed that communities affected by development interventions should also have opportunities to contribute to the planning and implementation of such projects.

title: 2027: INEC selects 17,656 polling units for nationwide mock accreditation exercise
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has selected 17,656 polling units across Nigeria’s 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) for a nationwide mock accreditation and result upload exercise ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The exercise, which will test the commission’s
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has selected 17,656 polling units across Nigeria’s 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) for a nationwide mock accreditation and result upload exercise ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The exercise, which will test the commission’s Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and result transmission process, is scheduled for Saturday, November 28, 2026, between 8:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m.

INEC published the list of selected polling units on its website, indicating the state, local government area, registration area or ward, polling unit and delimitation code for each location.

The list covers all 36 states, arranged alphabetically from Abia to Zamfara, with the FCT included at the end.

Abia State has 368 selected polling units, while Adamawa has 452. In the FCT, 124 polling units were selected across the six area councils.

Abaji, Bwari, Gwagwalada, Kuje and Kwali Area Councils each have 20 selected polling units, while the Abuja Municipal Area Council has 24.

INEC National Commissioner and Chairman of its Information and Voter Education Committee (IVEC), Mohammed Kudu Haruna, announced details of the exercise on Monday at a forum for media executives in Abuja.

Haruna said the exercise would take place in two polling units in each registration area across the 36 states and the FCT.

He explained that the process would simulate a presidential election, with polling units opening at 8:30 a.m. and voter accreditation continuing until 2:30 p.m.

According to him, the exercise would assess the performance of BVAS and the uploading of election results to the INEC Result Viewing (IReV) portal.

The commissioner stressed that the exercise was strictly a technical test and should not be mistaken for an actual election.

“It is a test, not an election, and no winners or losers will be declared,” he said.

Haruna explained that the exercise was intended to identify technical problems ahead of the general elections, giving the commission sufficient time to address any shortcomings.

“Its value lies in finding faults while there is still time to fix them, so a fault recorded on Saturday is the exercise doing its job,” he added.

He urged journalists to report the exercise accurately and avoid presenting it as an election.

“I ask you to report it as a test,” he said.

The INEC commissioner also appealed to voters in the selected polling units to participate in the exercise by coming out with their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs).

The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for Saturday, January 16, 2027.

title: 89 fall ill after unknown substance released at UK Arena concert
description:
Thousands of concertgoers were evacuated from the UK’s largest indoor arena after the release of an “unknown substance”, with dozens reporting suffering side effects, police said Monday.



Some 12,000 people were attending the Sunday night show by US rapper Don Toliver at the Co-op Live arena in Ma
content:
Thousands of concertgoers were evacuated from the UK’s largest indoor arena after the release of an “unknown substance”, with dozens reporting suffering side effects, police said Monday.

Some 12,000 people were attending the Sunday night show by US rapper Don Toliver at the Co-op Live arena in Manchester, northwest England.

“A total of 89 people displayed symptoms believed to be linked to exposure,” Manchester police said, adding one woman was taken to hospital for treatment.

“Enquiries remain ongoing to establish the nature of the substance, where it came from and any associated risk,” Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said in a statement.

Toliver said he had postponed his Monday night London show following the incident, which led to one person being taken to hospital.

Emergency services were called after “reports of people in the crowd suffering effects from an unknown substance”, Manchester police said, declaring a major incident at the scene.

The venue, which bills itself as the country’s largest live entertainment arena, said it was working with police to “identify the cause of the incident”.

The regional ambulance service said it assessed more than 50 people, including some reporting “eye and respiratory symptoms”.

Toliver, who was nominated for five Grammy Awards last week, is currently on the second leg of his “Nitrous” world tour.

He announced he was rescheduling his show at London’s O2 arena due to an “unfortunate incident last night (in) Manchester”.

“My heart and prayers are with everyone that was injured last night,” Toliver said on Instagram, without providing more details.

Concertgoers told the BBC that people were “choking” and coughing, recalling “distressing scenes” of people leaving the venue in a panic.

Some criticised the lack of security checks at the venue, especially in a city still scarred by the 2017 Manchester Arena bombing, which killed 22 people at an Ariana Grande concert.

Okpebholo made t
content:
Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has promised to begin construction of a third flyover bridge in Benin City if President Bola Tinubu wins the 2027 presidential election.

The proposed bridge will link Agbor Road to Sakponba Road in Ikpoba-Okha Local Government Area of the state.

Okpebholo made the pledge during the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Ikpoba-Okha, following the party’s campaign activities in Orhionmwon Local Government Area.

He said the project would improve movement and provide better access for residents and businesses in the area but explained that its execution would depend on financial support from the Federal Government.

“I promise to start a flyover bridge from the back of Guinness to Sakpoba Road in Ikpoba-Okha. I need money to do this, and I can only do it with the support of President Tinubu,” the governor said.

He urged residents to vote for Tinubu and other APC candidates in the 2027 general election, arguing that their support would help sustain development in the state.

The governor also called on voters to support APC candidates, whom he described as competent and credible, saying they would work with his administration to advance development.

Deputy Governor Dennis Idahosa thanked residents of Orhionmwon and Ikpoba-Okha for their support and appealed to them to back Tinubu and other party candidates.

Former Edo State governor and senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, urged voters to consider competence and credibility rather than ethnic affiliations when choosing their leaders. He also claimed that the APC had performed well at the state and federal levels.

Former Deputy Governor Pius Odubu expressed confidence in continued development under Okpebholo, while APC leader in Edo South, Osagie Ize-Iyamu, praised the governor for starting electricity projects in Orhionmwon, which he said had experienced poor electricity supply for about 20 years.

The Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Matthew Urhoghide, commended Okpebholo over what he described as improved security in the state. He also urged residents to help secure 2.5 million votes for Tinubu.

APC State Chairman, Jarrett Tenebe, said the party had attracted new members in Orhionmwon and remained united. He attributed the party’s cohesion to Okpebholo’s leadership and claimed that cultism, kidnapping and other criminal activities had reduced across the state.

The party’s Deputy State Chairman, Sylvester Aigboboh, said Orhionmwon and Ikpoba-Okha had benefited from more than 50 development projects. He urged residents to vote for Tinubu and other APC candidates to sustain the projects.

title: Senate intervenes in 50-year Ogun communities, Army land dispute
description: The Chairman of the Senate Committee on Ethics, Privileges and Public Petitions, Senator Neda Imasuen, has assured residents of at least 16 communities bordering Ijebu North-East and Ijebu East Local Government Areas of Ogun State of the Federal Government’s commitment to resolving their 50-year-old
content:
The Chairman of the Senate Committee on Ethics, Privileges and Public Petitions, Senator Neda Imasuen, has assured residents of at least 16 communities bordering Ijebu North-East and Ijebu East Local Government Areas of Ogun State of the Federal Government’s commitment to resolving their 50-year-old land dispute with the Nigerian Army.

The Army had reportedly given the communities one week to vacate their ancestral land earlier this year, claiming that the expanse of land, said to measure more than 500 hectares, had been acquired over the last 50 years.

The action of the Army was said to have caused confusion and anxiety, with thousands of residents wondering where else to call home.

However, during the committee’s visit to Apunren-Ijebu and Ijebu Imushin on Monday, Imasuen said the Senate was working round the clock to ensure that the conflict was resolved in a way that would be acceptable to all parties involved.

He attributed the committee’s visit largely to the determination and sustained efforts of Senator Gbenga Daniel, who represents Ogun East Senatorial District, commending him for his commitment to bringing the matter before the Senate and ensuring that the concerns of the affected communities received the necessary attention.

The committee chairman acknowledged that the dispute had persisted for more than 50 years, describing the visit as an important step towards resolving an issue that had remained a source of concern to successive generations.

“We are here today largely because of the doggedness of our leader, Senator Gbenga Daniel. I am sure you are aware that members of the Committee have had to contend with several engagements across their respective states and senatorial districts. Despite these commitments, he worked tirelessly to ensure that we could come here at this time.

“I am glad that the people appreciate what he has done in this regard. This matter has been on for over 50 years, and Senator Gbenga Daniel appears to be bringing a special 50th-anniversary gift to the people through this intervention,” Imasuen said.

“We have come with a genuine commitment to see things for ourselves. We want to inspect the boundaries, the affected houses, the schools and other facilities so that we can properly appreciate the situation on the ground.

“Interestingly, as I alighted from the bus, I was informed that even this palace was, so to speak, is on Army land. I immediately asked: if the palace is on Army land, then who owns the land?” he queried.

While acknowledging the concerns raised by the communities, Imasuen commended the Nigerian Army for its cooperation and willingness to engage with the committee and other stakeholders in addressing the matter.

He said the Army’s approach had helped facilitate the committee’s work, noting that its leadership had demonstrated an understanding of the human and communal dimensions of the dispute.

“I must also express our appreciation to the Nigerian Army for its cooperation. They have been very helpful and have made our work easier. We appreciate the leadership of the Army for the way it has handled this engagement and for its efforts to give the matter a human face.

“We are all Nigerians, and we live together as one people. It is important that issues of this nature are approached with understanding, cooperation and a genuine commitment to finding solutions,” he stated.

Imasuen further assured the communities that the committee would make every effort to prepare its report promptly upon returning to Abuja, so that the document could be presented to the Senate for consideration and the necessary legislative action.

He expressed optimism that the committee’s intervention, coupled with Daniel’s sustained efforts, would bring the prolonged dispute closer to a satisfactory conclusion.

The senator, however, urged Apunren-Ijebu and other affected communities to maintain unity, cooperation and mutual understanding throughout the resolution process.

He cautioned that the interests of the various communities involved must be carefully harmonised to avoid resolving one dispute while inadvertently creating another.

Speaking during the committee’s visit, Daniel said he was deeply concerned by what he personally witnessed during the inspection of the affected areas.

“I came here to see things for myself, and I must confess that I was not particularly happy with what I saw. Many people’s houses have been marked by the Nigerian Army.

“From the information available to me, this land was acquired over 50 years ago, yet the matter has remained unresolved for so long,” he said.

He disclosed that he had successfully moved a motion on the floor of the Senate, drawing attention to the prolonged situation and the need for the National Assembly to intervene.

Daniel explained that the Senate subsequently authorised the appropriate committee to undertake an on-the-spot assessment of the affected communities and investigate the issues surrounding the land dispute.

“With the support you have given me as your senator, I was able to successfully present a motion on the floor of the Senate, drawing attention to what has been happening in our community.

“The National Assembly could no longer simply look away while this situation continued. Consequently, the appropriate committee was mandated to come here, see things for themselves and examine the circumstances surrounding the matter,” he stated.

Daniel expressed satisfaction that those engagements had begun to yield some positive developments, including the Army’s commencement of certain activities towards addressing the situation.

The senator thanked President Bola Tinubu, the Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, and the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Ethics, Privileges and Public Petitions, Senator Imasuen, among others, for their support and cooperation towards resolving the conflict.

Daniel urged the residents to remain calm and patient, assuring them that the committee had now personally inspected the affected areas, listened to the communities’ concerns and received relevant explanations from the military authorities.

“All the efforts we have made would amount to very little if we do not take this opportunity to move the matter forward. That is why we are here today.

“We have gone round the affected areas. You should therefore remain calm and patient. The members of the Committee have seen what is happening with their own eyes, and we have also listened to the explanations provided by the Army,” he said.

title: 2027: Armed Men Who Killed Four NDC Campaign Members Said I Was Their Target, Omo-Agege
description: Former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege has alleged that the gunmen who attacked his campaign team in Delta State, killing four people, repeatedly shouted his name and declared their intention to kill him.Omo-Agege, who is seeking election to the Delta Central Senatorial District on the platfo
content:
Former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege has alleged that the gunmen who attacked his campaign team in Delta State, killing four people, repeatedly shouted his name and declared their intention to kill him.

Omo-Agege, who is seeking election to the Delta Central Senatorial District on the platform of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 general elections, said he escaped the attack through the intervention of his Department of State Services (DSS) escorts.

He spoke on Monday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today.

Recounting the incident, the former deputy senate president said he heard the attackers repeatedly shouting that they wanted to kill him while opening fire at the campaign venue.

“Right there at the venue, while they were shooting, we could hear them say, ‘It is Omo-Agege we want to kill. We must kill Omo-Agege.’

“But I was lucky because my DSS details were very professional. In fact, after God, the only reason I am alive today is because of the DSS operatives who were with me,” he said.

Omo-Agege described the incident as a premeditated attack, alleging that there had been a build-up to the violence.

He questioned why he would be singled out for elimination when several other politicians were also contesting elective positions.

The former lawmaker said the attackers struck less than five minutes after he began addressing supporters at the campaign venue.

According to him, he had moved towards the side of his vehicle to make eye contact with members of the audience when the gunshots rang out.

“It was by divine intervention. As I was speaking, I just moved over to the side of the vehicle to be able to make eye contact with those I was speaking with. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started,” he said.

The former deputy senate president said four members of his campaign organisation were killed, while about 15 others sustained injuries, with some in critical condition.

In a statement issued earlier on Monday by his media adviser, Sunny Areh, Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation said he survived an assassination attempt during a campaign tour in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State.

Areh alleged that armed men opened fire on the senator and his entourage while he was addressing supporters during a campaign visit.

The organisation called for an independent and thorough investigation by the Nigeria Police Force, while appealing to the Inspector-General of Police, the DSS, INEC, civil society organisations and the international community to ensure the safety of political candidates and their supporters.

It also urged supporters to remain calm and avoid retaliation, adding that its ward-to-ward campaign activities across Delta Central would continue.

title: Caregiver Salami shot dead in US weeks before starting Nursing school
description:
By Adegboyega Adeleye







A 24-year-old Togolese caregiver in Chicago, Bintou Salami, has been shot dead while returning home from work, weeks before she was due to begin nursing school.







According to ABC7 Chicago, Salami was found with a gunshot wound in the 1400 block of West Chase Avenue
content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

A 24-year-old Togolese caregiver in Chicago, Bintou Salami, has been shot dead while returning home from work, weeks before she was due to begin nursing school.

According to ABC7 Chicago, Salami was found with a gunshot wound in the 1400 block of West Chase Avenue at about 11:15 p.m. on Wednesday.

She had just finished her shift at Misericordia, where she cared for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

Ms Salami relocated from France to the U.S. in 2024 following her marriage and planned to begin nursing school in January; she is survived by her husband and son.

Her killing was one of three shootings on Chicago’s North Side that night as Police said the incidents were connected. A 35-year-old man was critically wounded near the bike path by Belmont Harbor, while a 25-year-old man was later found dead at the Morse Red Line station and a gun was recovered at the station. The Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office said the man died by suicide.

Salami’s coworkers described her as caring and devoted. Ashley Hespen, assistant vice president of residential services at Misericordia, said residents loved spending time with her.

Friends, relatives and members of Chicago’s Togolese community gathered at a vigil to honour Salami and demand answers. As they sang the Togolese national anthem, supporters stood with her brother at the place where she was killed.

“I can’t stop looking at the picture. I don’t know, like — it’s not fair,” said Nanipo Damyete, Salami’s former roommate.

Amevi Avouglah, the USA country delegate for the High Council of Togolese Abroad, said Salami’s future had been cut short.

“All the dreams that Bintou is carrying vanished like that in one minute! She was coming from work,” Avouglah said.

Salami’s brother, Raoufou, questioned the suggestion that she was killed during a robbery, saying nothing appeared to have been taken.

“The police telling me, like, somebody tried to rob her or something. What I can’t understand is how are you trying to rob somebody and you don’t take her phone, nothing?” he said.

Salami moved to the United States from France in 2024 after completing college and following her marriage. She is survived by her husband and their 4-year-old son, who lives with her mother in Togo.

Chicago police have not publicly explained how the shootings were connected and no suspects have been identified.

The fatal shooting has sparked calls for justice from her family, friends and members of the Togolese community in the U.S.

title: Mock accreditation: INEC publishes 17,656 selected PUs across 36 states, FCT
description:
By Omeiza Ajayi







The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has published the list of polling units selected for its nationwide mock accreditation exercise, naming 17,656 locations across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory FCT.







The commission said the exercise is a
content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has published the list of polling units selected for its nationwide mock accreditation exercise, naming 17,656 locations across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory FCT.

The commission said the exercise is a “Mock Accreditation and Result Upload Exercise” using the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS). It will hold on Saturday, 28 November 2026, from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m.

The list, posted on INEC’s website, gives the state, local government area, ward, polling unit and delimitation code of each selected location. It runs alphabetically from Abia State to Zamfara State, with the FCT last.

Abia has 368 entries, while Adamawa follows with 452. In the FCT, 124 polling units were selected across the six area councils. Abaji, Bwari, Gwagwalada, Kuje and Kwali have 20 each, while the Municipal Area Council has 24.

INEC’s National Commissioner and Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee (IVEC), Mohammed Kudu Haruna, spoke about the exercise on Monday at a forum for media executives in Abuja.

Haruna said it would run “across all 36 states and the FCT, in two polling units per Registration Area.”

According to him, it will simulate the Presidential election, with polling units opening by 8:30 a.m. and accreditation running from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m.

He said it will test the BVAS, the upload of results to the IReV portal. The commissioner stressed that the exercise is not a real poll. “It is a test, not an election, and no winners or losers will be declared,” he said.

He said the value of the exercise lies in the faults it finds. “Its value lies in finding faults while there is still time to fix them, so a fault recorded on Saturday is the exercise doing its job,” Haruna said.

He asked journalists to describe it accurately. “I ask you to report it as a test,” he said.

Haruna also appealed to residents of the affected areas to take part. “I also appeal to voters in the selected polling units to come out with their PVCs and take part,” he said.

The presidential and National Assembly elections hold on Saturday, 16 January 2027.

The post Mock accreditation: INEC publishes 17,656 selected PUs across 36 states, FCT appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Plateau gov loses elder brother
description:
Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has lost his elder brother, Morris Mutfwang, following a protracted illness.
The Plateau State Deputy Governor, Ngo Piyo, on Monday led members of the State Executive Council on a condolence visit to the governor’s residence at the Old Government House, Jos.
I
content:
Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has lost his elder brother, Morris Mutfwang, following a protracted illness.

The Plateau State Deputy Governor, Ngo Piyo, on Monday led members of the State Executive Council on a condolence visit to the governor’s residence at the Old Government House, Jos.

In a statement issued after the visit by the governor’s Director of Press and Public Affairs, Dr Gyang Bere, Piyo described the deceased as “a distinguished personality, a devoted family man, a lover of peace and a patriotic Nigerian” who made meaningful contributions to public service.

She said the council received news of his death with shock and sadness, adding that his passing was a painful loss to the Mutfwang family, Plateau State and the country.

“The deputy governor prayed for the peaceful repose of his soul and asked Almighty God to grant the Governor, the bereaved family and all those mourning his demise the strength, grace and fortitude to bear the tragic loss,” the statement said.

The Plateau State Inter-Religious Council also paid a condolence visit to the family.

The delegation, led by the Emir of Wase, Alhaji Muhammadu Sambo Haruna, who spoke on behalf of the council’s Co-Chairman, Rev. Prof. Pandam Yamsat, described the death as a painful loss to the family and the state.

Haruna urged the family to find comfort in the sovereignty and wisdom of God and prayed for strength to cope with the loss.

Responding on behalf of the family, Jonathan Mutfwang thanked both delegations for their visits, prayers and show of solidarity, saying their presence had brought comfort to the bereaved family.

He disclosed that the deceased would be buried on Thursday, November 26, 2026.

content:
The Osun State Police Command has arrested a man who allegedly posed as the operator of a non-governmental organisation and other suspects over the sale of a newborn baby for N1.5m.

Police said the baby’s mother was deceived into believing that her child had died after handing him over to a woman who promised to arrange care for him.

The command’s spokesperson, Abiodun Ojelabi, disclosed in a statement on Monday that the baby had been recovered in Akure, Ondo State, following investigations spanning three states.

According to the police, the baby’s 18-year-old mother, Victoria Michael, was allegedly deceived by her 30-year-old friend, Comfort Olayinka, who took the newborn from her shortly after delivery and handed him over to Oladipo in Abeokuta, Ogun State.

The police said Oladipo, 46, had presented himself as the operator of an NGO responsible for caring for less privileged people and had promised to help the young mother find someone to take care of her baby.

The statement explained that Olayinka had contacted an individual identified as Eri-Ife in Abeokuta even before the baby’s delivery, informing him that her pregnant friend could not afford to take care of the child.

Eri-Ife subsequently linked her with Oladipo, who allegedly agreed to facilitate the arrangement.

The statement read, “On 13/11/2026, information was received that, on 1/11/2026, one Victoria Michael, ‘f’, aged 18 years, who was pregnant, was taken to a private hospital in Kajola for delivery. Consequently, she gave birth to a baby boy on 2/11/2026 and was discharged on the second day, being 3/11/2026.

“The man, one Tayo, other name unknown, responsible for the pregnancy, according to the victim, refused to accept responsibility for the pregnancy. During the course of investigation, it was discovered that Comfort Olayinka, ‘f’, aged 30 years, was a friend of the mother of the baby (Victoria Michael) and, based on discussion, Comfort contacted one Eri-Ife in Abeokuta, Ogun State, even before the time of delivery and informed Eri-Ife that her friend, Victoria Michael, is pregnant and cannot take care of the baby, and that she needs someone who can take care of the baby when delivered.

“Eri-Ife then linked Comfort to one Oladipo Olamide, ‘m’, aged 46 years, who claimed to run/operate a Non-Governmental Organisation (NGO) that takes care of the less privileged, which was discovered to be false, and promised to take care of her request.”

The police said investigations revealed that the mother and Olayinka took the baby to Ogun State on November 5 and handed him over to Oladipo.

However, Olayinka allegedly returned to deceive the mother that the baby had died, giving her a bag purportedly containing the remains of the child.

The distraught mother reportedly threw the bag into the Lafenwa River, unaware that her baby was still alive and had allegedly been sold.

The police further alleged that Olayinka collected N450,000 from Oladipo, purportedly to take care of the baby’s mother.

According to the statement, Oladipo was arrested in Abeokuta on November 17 and allegedly confessed to selling the baby to a woman identified as Mrs Ruth Bolanle in Akure, Ondo State.

He subsequently led police operatives to Akure on November 18, where the child was recovered and Bolanle arrested.

The police said Bolanle confessed to paying N1.5m to Oladipo for the baby, adding that he had promised to obtain the necessary documentation from the appropriate government agency but failed to do so.

The statement added, “All the suspects have explained their roles and will be charged to court when investigation is concluded.”

Reacting to the development, the Osun State Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Zungura, warned individuals and groups involved in child trafficking to desist from the criminal act or face the full weight of the law.

He assured residents that the command would not relent in its efforts to protect lives and property across the state.

The incident comes amid concerns over child trafficking and the unlawful transfer of children, with the police urging members of the public to remain vigilant and report suspicious activities to security agencies.

The post Police arrest fake NGO operator, others over N1.5m baby sale appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: PSG suffer major injury blow as Doue, Kvaratskhelia face long layoffs
description:
The sight of the unfortunate Desire Doue going down holding his knee in agony was distressing for anyone connected to Paris Saint-Germain, but encouraging for those hoping to stop the French club from winning a third consecutive Champions League this season.



PSG have been European champions in ea
content:
The sight of the unfortunate Desire Doue going down holding his knee in agony was distressing for anyone connected to Paris Saint-Germain, but encouraging for those hoping to stop the French club from winning a third consecutive Champions League this season.

PSG have been European champions in each of the last two years and their quest to retain the crown this season has started superbly, with four straight wins leaving them top of the 36-team standings halfway through the league phase.

However, they have now lost the outstanding Doue, exactly a month after Khvicha Kvaratskhelia succumbed to the same injury, casting serious doubt over the chances of Luis Enrique’s team going all the way again.

Doue was stretchered off in tears after twisting his knee awkwardly during PSG’s 3-2 win at Nice in Ligue 1 on Saturday, with the club later confirming the 21-year-old had ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee and needed surgery.

Doue’s season is likely now over, while Kvaratskhelia is beginning the process of rehabilitation after rupturing the same ACL in last month’s win over Barcelona.

The explosive Georgian winger was the best player in last season’s Champions League knockout rounds and came sixth in this year’s Ballon d’Or ranking.

Meanwhile Doue was the man of the match when Paris demolished Inter Milan 5-0 in the 2025 Champions League final and had been their star performer in recent weeks.

“He will come back twice as strong. I am not worried,” insisted Luis Enrique, but he will know that the injuries to two of his best attacking players seriously damage the club’s prospects of more European glory.

So what do they do now, as they prepare to host Roma on Wednesday and with the January transfer window approaching?

“We are always open to possibilities in the transfer window, but not just because we have players injured,” said the Spaniard.

“We have players who can come in and we will overcome this as a team. It is not a problem.”

He could be forgiven for now regretting the decision to allow Bradley Barcola — scorer of 34 goals across the last two campaigns — to leave for Liverpool.

Suddenly the pressure on the injury-prone Ousmane Dembele to stay fit is enormous.

– Bayern in bother –

As for who appears the best-placed to take advantage of PSG’s misfortune, it may not be Bayern Munich, as the German champions deal with problems of their own.

Twenty-four hours before Doue went down for PSG, newly-crowned Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane was substituted with an ankle injury playing for Bayern against Cologne.

He is now expected to be sidelined for up to four months, although that will at least mean he has a chance of being fresh by March, in time for the Champions League knockout rounds.

“I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season,” Kane said in a social media post.

The loss of a player who scored 61 goals last season and had 10 so far in this campaign is still a massive setback for the Bavarians.

They also saw the brilliant Michael Olise come off in that match, while coach Vincent Kompany has been struggling too.

He was back in the dugout at the weekend, but with his arm in a sling, having dislocated his shoulder when he collapsed on the training pitch before being hospitalised with meningeal irritation in October.

On top of that, Bayern have also come in for criticism from global players’ union FIFPro for putting pressure on star midfielder Jamal Musiala to renegotiate his contract as he recovers from injury.

Senior club bosses had questioned whether Musiala, who missed several matches with a neurological condition earlier in the season and has recently returned from a hamstring injury, should continue to receive his contracted salary.

FIFPro called it “a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala” and said “a club of Bayern’s standing should know better”.

Barcelona, Real Madrid and last season’s runners-up Arsenal are among the teams who must now be smelling an opportunity amid the troubles of their chief continental rivals.

title: 2027: Tinubu woos Igbo, recalls 2023 defeat in Lagos
description:
President Bola Tinubu has appealed to Igbo stakeholders in Lagos State to support his re-election bid in the 2027 general election.
Tinubu stated this on Monday during the Lagos Central PBAT-KOH Campaign Rally, held at the Mobolaji Johnson Arena, Onikan Stadium, Lagos.
The President arrived in Lagos
content:
President Bola Tinubu has appealed to Igbo stakeholders in Lagos State to support his re-election bid in the 2027 general election.

Tinubu stated this on Monday during the Lagos Central PBAT-KOH Campaign Rally, held at the Mobolaji Johnson Arena, Onikan Stadium, Lagos.

The President arrived in Lagos on Saturday after attending the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State.

The Lagos rally was a move to promote Tinubu’s candidacy for a second term in office, and also canvass votes for the APC governorship candidate and current Lagos deputy governor, Obafemi Hamzat.

While addressing the Igbo stakeholders, Tinubu recalled losing the 2023 election in the state, which is considered a stronghold of the APC.

The PUNCH reported in February 2023 that the then presidential candidate of the Labour Party, Peter Obi, defeated Tinubu to win the presidential election in the state.

In the 20 Local Government Areas in the state, Obi won in some LGAs that many had considered major strongholds for the APC in previous elections.

Polling 582,454 votes in total, Obi cleared votes in Ajeromi-Ifelodun, Amuwo-Odofin, Eti-Osa, Ikeja, Kosofe, Oshodi-Isolo, Somolu, Ojo and Alimosho

While Tinubu garnered 572,606 votes from Agege, Apapa, Badagry, Epe, Ibeju-Lekki, Ifako-Ijaiye, Ikorodu, Mushin, Lagos Island, Lagos Mainland, and Surulere.

The report added that despite winning two more LGs in the state than the LP candidate, Tinubu still lost the election to Obi on the number of votes won by 9,848 votes.

In his remarks, according to a video shared by an APC member, Imran Muhammed, via his X handle on Monday, Tinubu jokingly told the Igbo stakeholders that he was disappointed over the 2023 voting result in Lagos.

“Some of you didn’t vote for me in 2023; I vex o. We don settle. Get your PVC,” he urged the crowd.

Tinubu also asked if they would vote for him, to which they replied with a resounding “Yes.”

Tinubu said, “Come January 16, get your PVC; you come vote. Agreement na agreement o, na Bola Tinubu be APC o. As you do for me, I do for you.

“You must follow who know road. I have to work hard to make sure the economy improves, to ensure that your children are in school, to eliminate crises in the universities, to build good roads that will maintain our cars.

“The future is in our hands. For every one of us, our children must be in school. Because we are poor doesn’t mean they shouldn’t attend the universities.

“We are doing that. The university is stable today because we are doing well.”

The President, who served as a two-term Lagos governor, noted that he was ready to go for a second term in Aso Villa.

“The critical line in our National Anthem is what I am standing here for. I begged for it; I am ready to serve you.

“I have served the first term. The Constitution said I must ask for a second term. I want a second term.

“As you are here today, you make me happy; you make me excited. I will go home happy and eat akpu,” Tinubu added.

The post 2027: Tinubu woos Igbo, recalls 2023 defeat in Lagos appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Police dismantle internet fraud camp in Abeokuta, arrest 11 suspects, recover vehicles, charms, others
description:
The Police Special Fraud Unit (SFU), Ikoyi, Lagos, has dismantled an internet fraud camp in Abeokuta, Ogun State, and secured the remand of eleven suspects arrested at the location.
Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), SFU, DSP Ovie Kenneth Ewhubare disclosed this in a Monday statement issued on
content:
The Police Special Fraud Unit (SFU), Ikoyi, Lagos, has dismantled an internet fraud camp in Abeokuta, Ogun State, and secured the remand of eleven suspects arrested at the location.

Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), SFU, DSP Ovie Kenneth Ewhubare disclosed this in a Monday statement issued on behalf of the Commissioner of Police of the unit.

According to the statement, the operation followed credible intelligence and coordinated investigative efforts which led detectives to House 10, Second Hill Estate, Oloke-Meji, Onikolobo, Abeokuta, where the suspects had been using the apartment as their operational base.

During the operation, detectives recovered eleven iPhones, three Samsung mobile phones, eight laptops, a Lexus RX 350 of 2014 model, charms, multiple blood-stained fetish items and suspected human remains.

Ewhubare said investigations revealed that one Goriola Oluwaseun Olanrewaju, also known as Update, who is currently at large, rented the apartment in 2021 and subsequently recruited young men into an organised internet fraud operation commonly known as a Hustle Kingdom, where they used the facility as a base for cyber-related fraud and other criminal activities.

The police image-maker disclosed that the suspects admitted that they exploit the identities and personal details of foreign nationals to defraud unsuspecting victims online.

The statement quoted the CP, SFU, CP Eloho Edwin Okpoziakpo, as saying that the discovery underscored the importance of credible information, intelligence-led policing and professional investigative skills in combating organised financial and cyber-enabled crimes.

He added that investigations were ongoing into the circumstances surrounding the occupation of the premises and the extent to which the property owner complied with the responsibility to properly verify and monitor occupants, particularly in view of the prolonged use of the apartment for criminal activities.

Ewhubare said efforts were also being made to trace and recover all the proceeds of crime in a bid to pursue justice in its restorative form.

The Italian tennis star could be sidelined for between three and four months followin
content:
By Enitan Abdultawab

Former world number one Jannik Sinner is set to undergo knee surgery in Finland, a development that could rule him out of the 2027 Australian Open, according to Sky Sports Italia.

The Italian tennis star could be sidelined for between three and four months following the procedure, which is expected to be performed by Lasse Lempainen, a specialist in tendon and muscle injuries.

Sinner, 25, has been struggling with persistent inflammation in his right knee, which forced him to end his 2026 season prematurely.

His last competitive appearance was at Wimbledon in July, where he defeated Alexander Zverev in the final to win his fifth Grand Slam title. He subsequently missed the North American hard-court tournaments, including the US Open, because of the injury.

The former world number one had earlier expressed hope of returning to action at the Australian Open in January, following a planned appearance at the Six Kings Slam in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, in late December.

“The goal is to go to Australia; I hope to get there, and perhaps play a few tournaments beforehand,” Sinner told reporters in Milan earlier this month.

However, the reported surgery and expected recovery period have cast serious doubt over his participation in the season’s first Grand Slam.

Despite competing in only nine tournaments during the 2026 season, Sinner recorded 44 wins in 47 matches, won six titles and reclaimed the world number one ranking during a 30-match winning streak.

He also won his maiden titles at Indian Wells, Monte Carlo and Madrid, becoming the second man after Novak Djokovic to win all nine ATP Masters 1000 tournaments.

Sinner ended his season in October and recently announced his separation from coach Darren Cahill after a successful five-year partnership. Magnus Norman has been tipped to replace the Australian.

title: 2027: 4 dead, 4 wounded as Omo-Agege camp alleges assassination attempt in Uduere
description:
At least four people have reported and four others were wounded after gunmen allegedly opened fire on the campaign team of Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, Delta Central Senatorial Candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area.
The incident occurred on Mon
content:
At least four people have reported and four others were wounded after gunmen allegedly opened fire on the campaign team of Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, Delta Central Senatorial Candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area.

The incident occurred on Monday, 23rd November 2026, during a campaign tour to Uduere.

In a press statement signed by his Media Adviser, Sunny Areh, the Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation said armed men opened fire at close range on Senator Omo-Agege and his entourage while he was addressing the crowd.

The campaign claimed the attack was a targeted attempt to assassinate the Senator.

According to the campaign, two of its aides namely, Moses Anaughe and a popular human rights activist,
Akima Efemena Umukoro were among those killed.

Two others were also killed, bringing the death toll to four.

Four others were wounded including Chief Evans Iwuvrie, Chuks Erhire, Tobore Agba who was shot in the neck and Ayodo Wanogho.

The wounded are currently receiving medical attention.

The campaign alleged that witnesses heard the attackers shouting, _”It’s Omo-Agege we want to kill! It’s Omo-Agege we want to kill!”

It further alleged that the attack was led by the Chairman of Ughelli North LGA, Barr. Jaro Egbo, acting on orders from Governor Sheriff Oborevwori.

The Delta State Police Command and the Delta State Government have not yet issued a response as at the time of filing this report to the allegations.

The campaign also alleged that police officers present at the scene with six trucks did nothing to prevent the attack.

The Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation demanded that Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, as Chief Security Officer of the state, should publicly condemn the attack in Uduere, order the immediate arrest and investigation of all persons alleged to have participated in, financed, or directed the attack, including Barr. Jaro Egbo, guarantee the safety of Senator Omo-Agege, NDC leadership and all opposition candidates in Delta State

It also called on the Inspector-General of Police to personally take over the investigation, saying it no longer has confidence in the Delta State Police Command.

It further called on the DSS, INEC, civil society organisations and the international community to take note.

The campaign urged its supporters not to retaliate, saying its ward-to-ward tour of Delta Central will continue.

“Delta State is not a war zone. Campaigning is not a crime. Seeking the votes of the people should not be a death sentence,” the statement said.

title: London promoter fulfils late brother’s dream with K1
description:
Bolanle Olatise turns grief into a mission as Alexis Promotions brings Fuji legend to UK stage


A United Kingdom-based music promoter, Bolanle Olatise, has revealed that her journey into entertainment was inspired by a promise she made to her late elder brother — to promote Fuji music icon, King Wa
content:
• Bolanle Olatise turns grief into a mission as Alexis Promotions brings Fuji legend to UK stage

A United Kingdom-based music promoter, Bolanle Olatise, has revealed that her journey into entertainment was inspired by a promise she made to her late elder brother — to promote Fuji music icon, King Wasiu Ayinde Marshal, popularly known as K1 De Ultimate.

Olatise, who promotes under the aegis of Alexis Promotions Limited, disclosed this in an exclusive interview, where she spoke about passion, resilience and determination.

According to her, she is the last-born of three children, and her elder brother was a devoted lover of Fuji music, particularly the music of K1.

“My elder brother was deeply passionate about Fuji music, particularly K1. He loved the music and was a strong admirer of him,” she said.

She explained that her brother’s greatest dream was to one day promote K1, but he passed away before he could achieve it.

“Unfortunately, my brother passed away, but one of his greatest dreams was to promote K1. I promised him that I would make that dream a reality. That promise was the major reason I ventured into entertainment and music promotion,” Olatise said.

The London-based promoter admitted that at the time she made the promise, she did not have the financial capacity to undertake a project of such magnitude.

“At the time, I couldn’t afford to undertake such a huge project. However, I am someone who loves challenges,” she said.

“Whenever I set my mind on something, I work hard and do everything possible to achieve it. So, I started saving towards fulfilling my brother’s dream.”

Olatise said her entry into music promotion was therefore not driven by fame or profit, but by commitment to family, legacy and a love for Fuji music.

Through Alexis Promotions Limited, she has continued to work towards bringing K1’s music to a wider audience in the United Kingdom, turning what began as a personal promise into a growing professional brand.

Olatise maintained that she remains committed to sustaining her brother’s legacy through quality entertainment and promotion of African music in the diaspora.

The post London promoter fulfils late brother’s dream with K1 appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: EXPLAINER: Why Nigerians are pushing back against ‘lazy youths’ narrative
description:
When Enioluwa Adeoluwa stood before a crowd of young Nigerians at the Emergence of Stars Youth Conference in Port Harcourt on April 1, 2025, he probably thought he was delivering a motivational speech.
Instead, his words would return more than a year later to trigger a heated debate about hard work,
content:
When Enioluwa Adeoluwa stood before a crowd of young Nigerians at the Emergence of Stars Youth Conference in Port Harcourt on April 1, 2025, he probably thought he was delivering a motivational speech.

Instead, his words would return more than a year later to trigger a heated debate about hard work, privilege, and the struggles of Nigerian youths.

Enioluwa passionately said, “Young people, we do not like to work anymore because we think that things should come easily for us. We need to understand that we must work; we cannot give up easily. You are 20, and you are already saying you are tired of life. Have you even seen life? What has life shown you?”

He added, “You have to have mentors. For example, Tyler Perry is my mentor. If you read every night, you are going to finish with a first-class. It is very easy. Life is not difficult; we overcomplicate it. You need to put in the work that will bring you a certain result.”

Although the speech was delivered in 2025, a clip from the event resurfaced on social media on November 17, 2026. Within hours, many Nigerians were criticising the influencer, arguing that his comments overlooked the economic realities facing young people.

Why Nigerians are angry about the label?

To understand the anger, it is important to look beyond Enioluwa’s comments.

For many Nigerians, being called lazy is particularly insulting because they believe they are already working harder than their circumstances allow.

Across the country, graduates are taking jobs unrelated to their qualifications, running side businesses, learning new skills and combining multiple jobs just to make ends meet. Yet, even with these efforts, many struggle to afford food, rent, transportation and other basic needs.

Low salaries are another problem. A young person can work full-time and still depend on side hustles to survive. Others work long hours, sometimes in jobs that have little connection to their professional training, because waiting for an opportunity in their chosen fields is not financially possible.
An X user, @MkpoikankeF, shared his experience of working two jobs at 26 but earning a combined ₦170,000 monthly. He explained that his mother’s medication cost ₦90,000, leaving him with little after transportation and feeding expenses.

Another user, @favwunmi, questioned what was left for a worker earning ₦60,000 monthly after waking up at 4am to go to work, paying bills and borrowing against the next salary.

A pharmacist, @ClemsAndy, also wrote that despite working at least eight hours a day, six days a week, since his induction in February 2024, he could not boast of owning a car.

These experiences raise an important question: how can a generation that is constantly finding ways to survive be described as unwilling to work?

There is also the frustration with bad leadership and poor public infrastructure. Nigerians have continued to contend with unreliable electricity, poor roads, rising food prices, limited job opportunities and an economy that makes it difficult for many businesses to grow.

When government fails to create an environment where hard work can translate into a decent standard of living, young people are left to find their own ways to survive.

For many, the problem is not a lack of willingness to work but the limited rewards for their efforts.

title: ‘Three of my supporters were killed’ –  LG chair reacts to Omo-Agege’s assassination claim
description:
By Egufe Yafugborhi, Ochuko Akuopha, Akpokona Omafuaire & Efe Onodjae



UGHELLI – Olorogun Jaro Egbo, the local government chairman of Ughelli North, Delta State, were Senator Ovie Omo-Agege said an assassination attempt was made on his life, has said three of his (Egbo) supporters were killed.
content:
By Egufe Yafugborhi, Ochuko Akuopha, Akpokona Omafuaire & Efe Onodjae

UGHELLI – Olorogun Jaro Egbo, the local government chairman of Ughelli North, Delta State, were Senator Ovie Omo-Agege said an assassination attempt was made on his life, has said three of his (Egbo) supporters were killed.

Read Also: Four die as Omo-Agege survives alleged assassination attempt in Delta

Recall that a campaign tour by Senator Omo-Agege, Delta Central senatorial candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, turned bloody in Uduere community, Ughelli North, today, with four persons in his entourage reportedly killed and several others critically wounded in a fresh political violence involving supporters of the NDC and All Progressives Congress, APC.

Among those reportedly killed was Moses Anaughe, a former Commissioner, Federal Character Commission and aide to Omo-Agege.

Also, former member of the Delta State House of Assembly, Chief Evans Ivwurie, was among those shot and reportedly battling for his life alongside other victims receiving medical attention.

The latest bloodshed, which has triggered a fierce exchange of accusations between Omo-Agege’s camp and Olorogun Egbo, is the third major violent incident linked to political activities involving rival camps in the state.

Clashes had erupted in the Warri-Effurun axis and Asaba, where one person was also killed.

While Omo-Agege’s camp put the Uduere death toll at four, Egbo claimed three of his supporters were killed, with both sides accusing the other of instigating the violence.

The recurrence of deadly confrontations, with the 2027 general elections still months away, has heightened concerns over the safety of political campaigns and the possibility of Delta becoming increasingly engulfed in political violence.

Omo-Agege

Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation alleged that armed men opened fire on the senator and his entourage at close range during a peaceful campaign visit, describing the incident as an assassination attempt.

In a statement signed by his Media Adviser, Sunny Areh, the campaign organisation said: “We condemn in the strongest possible terms the murderous attack on the campaign team of Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, Delta Central Senatorial Candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area.

“According to eyewitness reports received from the scene, armed men opened fire at close range on Senator Omo-Agege and his entourage during a peaceful campaign tour to Uduere.

“Senator Ovie Omo-Agege was saved by a divine distraction, when bullets wheezed past his head as he was addressing the crowd that gathered to receive him.”

The organisation put the death toll at four, identifying two of the deceased as its aides, Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro.

It also named Chief Evans Ivwurie, Chuks Erhire, Tobore Agba and Ayodo Wanogho as among those shot, with four victims initially reported wounded.

“We are pained to report that four people including two of our aides — Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro — were shot dead.

“Four others — Chief Evans Iwuvrie, Chuks Erhire, Tobore Agba (who was shot in the neck) and Ayodo Wanogho — were shot at very close range and wounded critically. They are currently receiving medical attention,” the statement said.

The NDC camp maintained that the incident was not an ordinary political disagreement.

“This was not a clash. This was not a misunderstanding. This was, according to witnesses, a targeted attempt to assassinate Senator Ovie Omo-Agege.”

It further alleged that witnesses identified Egbo as leading the attackers on the orders of Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, demanding an immediate and transparent investigation.

Egbo, LG chair’s account

However, Egbo rejected the allegations, offering a completely different account of how the confrontation erupted.

The APC chieftain said the disagreement began over the use of a community hall, which he claimed had already been booked for an event he was organising for Uduere residents.

According to him: “Yesterday (Sunday) at the village, we went there to set up our canopy for today’s and tomorrow’s event because I’m hosting the whole village people.

“When we got there, some people said that Omo-Agege is coming and they want to use the hall. So my president told them that this hall has been booked, so you can take it to elsewhere. They refused.”

Egbo said the NDC campaign subsequently proceeded with its activities close to where his supporters had gathered, despite the disagreement.

He added that security personnel had been alerted before the incident, insisting that he took steps to prevent violence.

“In the morning, we had got intelligence that they brought in AK-47 and armed men from Sapele and Ughelli. So I called the Area Commander and the DPO to go there and maintain peace. We even called the Army.

“So when the DPO got there, he called me to say that he’s preaching to them that they shouldn’t fight.

“So I told my people, don’t talk to anybody. Just enjoy yourself there. Drink and eat and merry. They had their own and that was when he (Omo-Agege) was saying that I was his PA, I was this, I was that.”

Egbo, however, accused members of Omo-Agege’s entourage of opening fire on his supporters, claiming that three of his men died.

He specifically accused one Akima, whom he described as an anti-cult operative, of firing a pump-action gun at close range.

“And thereafter, as he was going, that was when one of his boys, one Akima, who calls himself Anti-Cult, brought out a pump action and opened fire at innocent citizens. Three of them at close range, on my people.

“As they fired, two died. The other one we rushed to the hospital, he just died now. And then three other ones are in critical condition.”

‘Omo-Agege ordered the shooting’

The council chairman also alleged that Omo-Agege ordered the shooting, a claim not independently established.

“So it’s Omo-Agege ordered them to shoot innocent people, since he declared ‘Rig & Die’. So they came with arms, fully armed, to cause disruption,” he alleged.

Egbo further said casualties were being treated at the Central Hospital, Ughelli, adding that the Area Commander was at the facility.

The NDC campaign organisation, meanwhile, called on Governor Oborevwori to condemn the attack and ensure the arrest and investigation of those allegedly responsible, including Egbo.

It also demanded that the Inspector-General of Police, IGP, the Director-General of the Department of State Services, DSS, and the Delta State Commissioner of Police take over the investigation.

“We call on the Inspector-General of Police to personally take over the investigation as we no longer have confidence in the Delta State Police Command whose officers were present with six trucks but did nothing to prevent the attack and killings,” the statement added.

The organisation urged its supporters not to retaliate, declaring that its ward-to-ward campaign across Delta Central would continue.

“Do not retaliate. Do not take the law into your own hands. We refuse to be intimidated. We refuse to be silenced.”

Political violence in Warri, Effurun to Asaba

The Uduere violence comes against the backdrop of previous confrontations involving political supporters in the state, raising questions about the effectiveness of earlier security interventions and assurances of peaceful political activities.

The first major incident occurred during a political procession in the Warri-Effurun axis on September 18, when supporters of rival political interests clashed, with allegations of armed involvement and an AK-47 rifle reportedly recovered in the aftermath.

The incident prompted condemnation and calls for investigation, amid conflicting accounts by political actors and security authorities over how the violence started and who was responsible.

Barely two months later, on November 7, another political procession in Asaba, involving supporters of the NDC and the Obedient Movement, ended in bloodshed, leaving one person dead and several others injured.

The police had said they received intelligence about the planned procession and advised against a road march, while political actors subsequently traded accusations over responsibility for the violence.

The Asaba incident also attracted concern from traditional and political stakeholders, who warned against allowing partisan rivalry to threaten the peace of the state.

Udumere

With Uduere now added to the list, the succession of violent incidents has raised troubling questions about whether political actors and security agencies have learnt any lessons from the earlier bloodshed.

The rival accounts surrounding the latest shooting, the actual casualty figure, the identities of those responsible and the circumstances leading to the violence now require urgent and impartial investigation.

For residents of Delta, the growing concern is that political competition, rather than being settled through persuasion and the ballot, could increasingly expose innocent citizens and party supporters to deadly confrontations.

When contacted, Delta State Police Command’s Spokesman, SP Bright Edafe, said the Command was yet to receive official report despite Egbo affirming that the Ughelli Area Commander was in the know and at the Ughelli Central Hospital where some casualties were rushed to the Accident and Emergency Unit.

Vanguard News

title: Alleged assassination: We want IG to investigate, not Delta police — Omo-Agege
description:
Former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, has called on the Inspector-General of Police to take over the investigation into the alleged assassination attempt on him in Delta State, saying he has no confidence in the state police command to deliver justice.







Omo-Agege, the Nigeria Democra
content:
Former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, has called on the Inspector-General of Police to take over the investigation into the alleged assassination attempt on him in Delta State, saying he has no confidence in the state police command to deliver justice.

Omo-Agege, the Nigeria Democratic Congress senatorial candidate for Delta Central, made the appeal on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, following an attack on his campaign entourage in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area.

He alleged that police officers present during the incident failed to intervene as gunmen opened fire on his team, adding that the attack had heightened fears among opposition politicians in the state.

“What we have learned is this: we are not safe here in Delta State. In fact, all members of the opposition party, NDC, most especially, we are all endangered,” he said.

Omo-Agege claimed that six truckloads of policemen were deployed to the campaign venue but did not act when the shooting occurred.

He accused the state police command of being unlikely to conduct an impartial investigation and urged the IGP to handle the case directly.

“We do not expect any justice to come from the police here in Delta State. Neither do we expect any justice to come from the police on this very one,” he said.

“We are appealing to the IG to take this matter over directly. We tried to reach him this evening. We couldn’t reach him.”

The former lawmaker said he wanted the federal police leadership to investigate the incident, insisting that the state command should not be involved in the probe.

He also called for justice for those affected by the attack, saying lives had been lost and several others were receiving treatment in hospitals.

“We need justice. We need justice. We need justice for these four people who have been killed. We need justice for the 15 people who are critically injured and hospitalised right now,” Omo-Agege said.

Despite the incident, he vowed not to abandon his campaign, dismissing suggestions that the attack could intimidate him into withdrawing from the race.

“If the idea is that this is supposed to deter me from going forward with the campaigns, it’s a very big mistake and a big lie. Ain’t going to happen,” he said.

He, however, appealed to his supporters to remain calm and avoid reprisals, warning that tensions remained high following the attack.

The Executive Governor of Zamfara state, Dr. Dauda lawal has flagged off the All Progressive Congress, APC Campaign, consultation and mobilization exercise, the target is to gather more than three million votes for President Bola Ahmad Tinubu and ensure the success of all can
content:
From John Bassey, Gusau

The Executive Governor of Zamfara state, Dr. Dauda lawal has flagged off the All Progressive Congress, APC Campaign, consultation and mobilization exercise, the target is to gather more than three million votes for President Bola Ahmad Tinubu and ensure the success of all candidates under the party.

The exercise which commenced at the prayer grounds of Talata Mafara aimed at honouring the son of Zamfara state, Dr. Abdullaziz Yari the Director General of APC Presidential Campaign Council as his home town sets the pace for the remaining 13 Local Government Areas, Governor Lawal vowed inclusive governance and assured the citizens of Zamfara state of a conducive state of peace where everyone experience prosperity, joy and togetherness during his second tenure.

Governor Lawal pledged to intensify war against insurgency, build more infrastructure, concentrate on Rural Access Roads construction, focus on human capital development and fullfil his proposed plans under rescue Agenda if elected come 2027.

He encouraged the people of Zamfara state, members, supporters and stakeholders of APC to have more confidence on the administration of President Bola Tinubu and his administration as the only leadership that have the capacity to satisfy their imaginations and enhance their comfort in the next four years.

He called on the people to vote for APC both in the state, local government and wards level in order to secure their freedom.

The Director General, APC Presidential Campaign Council, Sen. Abdullaziz Yari Abubakar expressed gratitude to the people of Zamfara state, supporters, members and stakeholders of APC for coming out in mass for the flag-off exercise in Talata Mafara amidst the long distance and poor condition of the roads.

He assured the people of his continued support in all areas and urged them never to be distracted by some people who are telling lies just to be in the position of power.

He echoed to the people if they were satisfied with the administration of Governor Dauda lawal and they all replied Yes. He again asked if they were satisfied with the administration of President Bola Ahmad Tinubu and they unanimously agreed, Yes.

He concluded by urging everyone to stand up for APC and ensure that all the candidates are voted into power come 2027 general elections.

Presence at the flag-off exercise were the former governors of Zamfara state, House of Assembly members, serving Senators, House of Representative members and other dignitaries to celebrate the commencement of the exercise.
