title: 2027: Tinubu woos Ndigbo in Lagos, seeks support for second term, APC candidates
description:
President Bola Tinubu has appealed to members of the Igbo community in Lagos State, market leaders and traders to support his re-election bid in 2027, urging them to vote for the All Progressives Congress (APC) and its candidates across the country.
Tinubu made the appeal on Monday while addressing
content:
President Bola Tinubu has appealed to members of the Igbo community in Lagos State, market leaders and traders to support his re-election bid in 2027, urging them to vote for the All Progressives Congress (APC) and its candidates across the country.

Tinubu made the appeal on Monday while addressing the Ndigbo Lagos State Town Hall, organised by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiative (NNDDI) at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly National Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos.

The President, who adopted a conciliatory tone in his engagement with the Igbo community, acknowledged that a significant number of Ndigbo in Lagos did not support his presidential ambition in the 2023 election.

He, however, urged them to reconsider their political position, obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and support his administration for another four years, citing ongoing infrastructure development and economic opportunities across the country, particularly in the Southeast.

Addressing a large gathering of traders and socio-cultural leaders drawn from major commercial centres, including Alaba International Market, Radio Market and ASPAMDA, Tinubu said another term would enable him to consolidate his administration’s achievements and continue serving Nigerians.

“The critical aspect in our national anthem is what I came here for. I appeal for the job and I am ready to serve; to serve you as I did in my first term. The Constitution allows me to serve for another term, so I want a second term,” he declared.

The President urged Nigerians to rise above ethnic and religious differences, insisting that the country should be regarded as a common home where everyone could pursue legitimate aspirations and prosper.

“Let’s see ourselves as one people living in the same house geographically called Nigeria. So, if you are in Nnewi, Onitsha or anywhere, grow up there and you come to Lagos, you are just answering the call of business and opportunity that God-given country, Nigeria, has given to you,” he said.

Tinubu cautioned against individuals and groups seeking to exploit ethnic differences for political advantage, stressing that national development depended on unity, mutual understanding and collective responsibility.

“Don’t let anyone come to divide us. In brotherhood we stand,” he added.

The President also made references to his family’s multi-ethnic connections, including his wife, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, who is of Itsekiri heritage, as an illustration of the cultural diversity and interconnectedness that define Nigeria.

He maintained that Nigerians, irrespective of their ethnic backgrounds or places of origin, should be able to live, work and conduct business anywhere in the country without discrimination.

Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, who attended the town hall alongside his deputy, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, described Tinubu’s presence as a significant recognition of the Igbo community and its contributions to Lagos State.

Sanwo-Olu expressed appreciation to the President for honouring the gathering, noting that the engagement provided an opportunity to strengthen relationships between the government and the Ndigbo community.

He also acknowledged political leaders, business associates and other stakeholders at the event, recognising their contributions to the political and economic development of Lagos and Nigeria.

The governor made references to Nigeria’s political journey, particularly the elections of 1999, 2003 and 2007, while acknowledging the roles played by various political leaders in shaping the country’s democratic development.

The town hall brought together Igbo community leaders, traders, business owners, political stakeholders and government representatives to discuss issues affecting Ndigbo in Lagos and explore ways of strengthening their relationship with the state and Federal Government.

It also provided a platform to promote dialogue, inclusion and peaceful coexistence, with participants underscoring the importance of mutual respect and cooperation in sustaining the unity and development of Lagos State and Nigeria.

The post 2027: Tinubu woos Ndigbo in Lagos, seeks support for second term, APC candidates appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Benue PDP inaugurates campaign council, says over 15 pol parties have endorsed Aondoakaa
description:
Ahead of the general elections in 2027, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Benue State has inaugurated the Aondoakaa/Ogbenjuwa 2027 Campaign Council in Makurdi, the state capital.
The PDP, during the inauguration on Monday said more than 15 political parties have endorsed its governorship candida
content:
Ahead of the general elections in 2027, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Benue State has inaugurated the Aondoakaa/Ogbenjuwa 2027 Campaign Council in Makurdi, the state capital.

The PDP, during the inauguration on Monday said more than 15 political parties have endorsed its governorship candidate, Chief Mike Aondoakaa, and are working hard to ensure his victory come at the polls.

The chairman of the party, Ezekiel Adaji, who disclosed this while addressing party members at the event said the endorsements were evidence of growing support for Aondoakaa and the party’s determination to reclaim power in the state.

Adaji urged party members to intensify mobilisation across the 23 local government areas, expressing confidence that the Aondoakaa-led administration would restore peace and address insecurity, particularly the difficulties confronting farmers.

The PDP candidate Mike Aondoakaa, SAN, in his address, pledged to promote fairness, protect businesses and ensure that farmers, investors and other residents could pursue legitimate economic activities without intimidation or discrimination.

Aondoakaa also called for independent public institutions, effective leadership and improved access to basic amenities, including clean water.

Aondoakaa pledged to develop rural communities and step up the fight against insecurity to enable people return to their ancestral homes to continue their farming activities.

He said Benue, an agrarian state, has majority of its people living in rural areas, arguing that concentrating development in Makurdi and a few other towns is completely unacceptable and selective.

The PDP governorship candidate promised to prioritize local government autonomy to allow council chairmen have a free hand to operate, so that people living in rural communities can have sustained security, access to clean water and good rural roads.

He announced that his blueprint has mapped out programmes including enhanced security, pointing out that an attack during his administration on one local government would be considered an attack on all 23 local government areas to ensure that the people are defended.

Aondoakaa condemned what he described as gagging of the opposition by the present administration, arguing that whenever PDP is in power, the rule of law is practised and true democracy is observed.

He recalled that during the immediate past administration, the then Governor Samuel Ortom always allowed opposition to use public facilities such as the IBB Square and the Aper Aku Stadium, stating that what is happening currently is not democratic.

Also, the Senate Minority Leader, Senator Abba Moro, congratulated members inaugurated into the Aondoakaa/Ogbenjuwa Campaign Council, led by Chief Laha Dzever, and pledged to mobilise support for the candidates across Benue South Senatorial District (Zone C).

He urged the campaign council to work assiduously for the victory of the party and expressed optimism that Aondoakaa would be a listening governor and not an emperor.

Responding on behalf of the campaign team, the Director-General of the council, Dr. Laha Dzever, promised that he and his team would do everything possible to lead the party to victory.

He urged the Benue people to support their candidates pledging that a PDP government would promote unity, fairness and inclusive development.

The post Benue PDP inaugurates campaign council, says over 15 pol parties have endorsed Aondoakaa appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Osun police rescue 16-day-old baby sold for N1.5m, arrest trafficking syndicate
description:
The Osun State Police Command has rescued a 16-day-old baby boy after he was sold to a buyer in Akure, Ondo State, following a fake death plot orchestrated by a child trafficking syndicate.
In a statement released on Monday, the Police Public Relations Officer, Abiodun Ojelabi, confirmed the rescue
content:
The Osun State Police Command has rescued a 16-day-old baby boy after he was sold to a buyer in Akure, Ondo State, following a fake death plot orchestrated by a child trafficking syndicate.

In a statement released on Monday, the Police Public Relations Officer, Abiodun Ojelabi, confirmed the rescue and disclosed that several suspects involved in the trafficking ring had been arrested.

According to the police, 18-year-old Victoria Michael was admitted to a private hospital in Kajola on November 1, where she gave birth to a baby boy the following day and she was discharged on November 3.

The biological father, identified only as Tayo, had reportedly refused to take responsibility for the pregnancy or the child.

Prior to the birth, 30-year-old Comfort Olayinka, a friend of the mother, was said to have contacted a woman named Eri-Ife in Abeokuta, Ogun State, claiming the young mother could not care for the baby and was looking for someone to take over parental responsibilities.

Eri-Ife subsequently connected Comfort to 46-year-old Oladipo Olamide, who claimed to run a non-governmental organization caring for the underprivileged—a claim police later confirmed was false.

On November 5, Comfort and Victoria reportedly traveled to Ogun State and handed the infant over to Oladipo.

Comfort then deceived the teenage mother into believing her newborn had died and she handed Victoria a folded, baby-shaped object inside a bag to throw into the Lafenwa River, concealing the fact that she had already collected N450,000 from Oladipo under the guise of funding the mother’s care.

Acting on intelligence, police operatives stormed Abeokuta on November 17 and arrested Oladipo. Under interrogation, he confessed to selling the infant to a buyer named Mrs. Bolanle Ruth.

The following day, Oladipo led detectives to Akure, Ondo State, where the baby was recovered and Mrs. Ruth was arrested.

She confessed to paying Oladipo N1.5 million to facilitate the purchase.

Oladipo had promised to process official adoption documents through relevant government agencies, which he failed to do.

Police confirmed that all suspects have confessed to their roles in the crime and will be charged to court upon the conclusion of investigations.

Osun State Commissioner of Police, CP Ibrahim Zungura, warned individuals and criminal groups involved in child trafficking to desist or face the full weight of the law, reiterating the command’s unwavering commitment to protecting lives and property.

‎Eno, who spoke on Monday at the inauguration ceremony in Ik
content:
‎Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno has inaugurated the newly constructed Ika Local Government Secretariat, built by the Chairman of the Council, Utibe Nwoko, commending him for the initiative and his commitment to grassroots development.
‎
‎Eno, who spoke on Monday at the inauguration ceremony in Ika LGA of the state, reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to equitable development across Akwa Ibom State, noting the importance of effective local government administration in delivering development to the people.
‎
‎He also announced that the 2027 budget would provide for the construction of 10 kilometres of roads in each of the 31 Local Government Areas of the state.
‎
‎He said, “With what I am seeing in Ika today, Ika will become a model town. For us, the 2027 budget will provide for the construction of 10 kilometres of roads in each of the 31 Local Government Areas of the state.”
‎
‎With the respective local governments’ needs assessments, which have identified priority roads for intervention, the governor said he would actualise projects rather than make promises if re-elected, adding that the government would continue to invest in roads, schools, hospitals, electricity and other critical infrastructure.
‎
‎“We are here to serve. We will continue to serve, and we will continue to bring development. We have a record of service. You can verify it,” he said.
‎
‎The governor acknowledged the contributions of President Bola Tinubu to development in Akwa Ibom, noting that the financial autonomy granted to local governments had created opportunities for council administrations to execute projects at the grassroots.
‎
‎He commended the Chairman of Ika Local Government Area for his performance and appreciated him for naming the council secretariat after him, disclosing that work had commenced on the road leading to the Paramount Ruler’s residence.
‎
‎ Eno urged the people of Ika to support Tinubu and all APC candidates, including Senate President Godswill Akpabio, Clement Jimbo and Boniface Ebehwo, describing continued support for the party as important to sustaining development.

title: FG plans sexual assault centres in 774 LGAs to tackle gender-based violence
description:
• Only 52 centres currently serve over 240m Nigerians – Minister
• Says GBV costs Nigeria $3bn annually, vows stronger survivor protection
Federal Government has unveiled plans to establish at least one Sexual Assault Referral Centre in each of Nigeria’s 774 Local Government Areas as part of efforts
content:
• Only 52 centres currently serve over 240m Nigerians – Minister

• Says GBV costs Nigeria $3bn annually, vows stronger survivor protection

Federal Government has unveiled plans to establish at least one Sexual Assault Referral Centre in each of Nigeria’s 774 Local Government Areas as part of efforts to strengthen the fight against gender-based violence and improve access to justice for survivors.

The Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim, disclosed this in Abuja on Monday at a press conference to flag off the 2026 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence.

She lamented that Nigeria currently has only 52 Sexual Assault Referral Centres providing medical, psychosocial and referral services to survivors, describing the number as grossly inadequate for a country with a population of more than 240 million.

According to her, the Federal Government is working with state governments to ensure that at least one centre is established in every local government area, with the possibility of extending the facilities to every ward.

The minister explained that the centres would provide comprehensive support beyond responses to sexual abuse, including psychosocial assistance and protection mechanisms for survivors.

She said: “For a nation of over 240 million people, 52 centres are grossly inadequate. We are actively working with state governments to ensure that at least one Sexual Assault Referral Centre is established in every local government area across the country.

“Indeed, nothing stops us from eventual establishment of a sexual assault centre in every ward.”

Sulaiman-Ibrahim also disclosed that gender-based violence costs Nigeria an estimated 1.5 per cent of its Gross Domestic Product, amounting to approximately $3 billion annually through lost productivity, healthcare burdens and disrupted livelihoods.

She further cited national data indicating that nearly one in three Nigerian women aged 18 to 49 had experienced physical or sexual violence, while more than 27,000 sexual and gender-based violence cases were documented in a recent reporting cycle, alongside millions of unreported incidents.

Describing the figures as a national emergency, the minister said the country must move beyond annual commemorations and translate awareness campaigns into measurable protection, justice and accountability.

“This is not just another global slogan or call. It is a clear demand to move beyond empty awareness and deliver real justice, real protection for survivors and an absolute end to impunity across our beloved country,” she said.

The 2026 campaign, themed, “Unite to End Violence Against Women and Girls: Ensure Justice, Protect Survivors and End Impunity,” runs from November 25 to December 10.

The minister said the Federal Government was adopting a coordinated national approach through the Renewed Hope Social Impact Intervention 774, a nine-pillar framework targeting 50 million women, children and vulnerable Nigerians across the country’s 774 local government areas.

She listed the intervention areas to include economic inclusion, clean energy, digital literacy, agriculture, healthcare, social protection, affirmative procurement, leadership and family development.

Under the initiative, she said the government was targeting the empowerment of five million women through the Nigerian for Women Programme scale-up, while the Happy Women Platform and App would onboard 10 million women to improve financial literacy, savings and enterprise support.

She added that the Digital Harmony initiative would train five million women in essential digital skills, while the Women Rise, Innovate and Create initiative would empower three million women in the creative economy.

The minister also highlighted the Power of 10 Million initiative, designed to organise women into grassroots groups for savings, access to credit, cooperative enterprises, mutual protection and civic participation.

On legal protection, Sulaiman-Ibrahim said the Child Rights Act had been domesticated in all 36 states, while the Violence Against Persons (Prohibition) Act had been domesticated in 35 states.

She said the Ministry was working to strengthen the implementation of both laws and close existing gaps, while reviewing the National Gender Policy, which expires this year.

She also announced the commencement of efforts to strengthen the National Boy Child Policy, arguing that protecting boys alongside girls was necessary to break the cycle of intergenerational violence.

“For decades, social interventions have largely focused on the girl child. Yet, we can no longer ignore the rising school dropout rates, substance abuse, street vulnerabilities and social neglect confronting our boys.

“By intentionally mentoring, protecting and empowering the boy child alongside the girl child, we are breaking the cycle of intergenerational violence at its roots and raising responsible men who will become true partners in building peaceful homes and a secure nation,” she said.

The minister further disclosed that the Federal Executive Council had approved the National Strategy and Costed Action Plan on Ending Child Marriage in Nigeria, 2025–2030, as well as the National Policy on Menstrual Health and Hygiene Management, 2026–2030, and the National Care Policy and Implementation Plan, 2026–2030.

She said the menstrual health policy and incentives approved by President Bola Tinubu for local manufacturers of sanitary products would help reduce the country’s dependence on imported menstrual hygiene products.

Sulaiman-Ibrahim also announced that the national Gender-Based Violence Electronic Dashboard and Situation Room was now operational to strengthen real-time data management, evidence-based interventions, coordination and accountability.

She called for greater collaboration among government institutions, development partners, civil society organisations, traditional and religious leaders, and the media, stressing that the fight against gender-based violence required sustained commitment beyond the 16-day campaign.

The Minister urged all stakeholders to sustain their commitment beyond the campaign, insisting that the 16 Days of Activism must translate into 365 days of action.

“The time for silence is over. The time for collective action is now. Let us unite to end violence against women and girls, ensure justice, protect survivors and end impunity,” she said.

In their goodwill messages, representatives of United Nations agencies and development partners called for stronger enforcement of existing laws, improved survivor-centred services, adequate funding and accountability to end violence against women and girls.

The UN Women Country Representative to Nigeria (and ECOWAS) Beatrice Eyong, reaffirmed the organisation’s commitment to supporting the Federal Government, noting that approximately 840 million women globally, representing one in three, had experienced physical or sexual violence in their lifetime.

Eyong who was represented, identified intimate partner violence, rape, sexual assault, child marriage, female genital mutilation, trafficking, sexual harassment, harmful traditional practices and technology-facilitated violence as major manifestations of abuse in Nigeria.

She urged the government to strengthen laws, close implementation gaps, invest in survivor-centred services and ensure predictable funding for interventions.

The International IDEA representative, who delivered a message on behalf of the organisation’s Head of Programmes in Nigeria, Danladi Plang, said the fight against gender-based violence must go beyond the annual 16-day commemoration.

She lamented that girls who suffered rape were often blamed for their dressing, women beaten in their homes were told to endure the abuse, while some children were forced into marriage before they understood the meaning of childhood.

She called for effective implementation of the Violence Against Persons (Prohibition) Act, stronger protection systems, accessible survivor-centred services and accountable institutions.

According to her, justice should not depend on a survivor’s social status or economic circumstances.

The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) representative commended the Minister for efforts to raise awareness about existing laws and encourage their domestication across states.

She emphasised prevention, believing survivors and ensuring that every form of violence was properly identified and addressed.

She also disclosed that UNFPA had worked with universities to institutionalise training on gender-based violence in emergencies, with 28 graduates completing the programme in the previous week.

She called for stronger implementation of existing laws, investment in essential services and sustained efforts to address the root causes of gender-based violence.

The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) representative, Wafaa Abdelatef, said violence against children and adolescent girls required urgent intervention, stressing that survivors must be heard, believed, protected and supported.

Abdelatef, who was represented urged the media to report cases responsibly, protect survivors’ identities and dignity, challenge the normalisation of violence and hold institutions and decision-makers accountable.

“To every child listening today, our message is simple: violence is never your fault. You deserve to be safe. You deserve to be heard. You deserve justice,” he said.

The team leader of the SPRiNG Programme also called for stronger community-level interventions, noting that conflict, displacement and climate pressures continued to expose women and girls to violence by disrupting livelihoods and weakening community protection systems.

He disclosed that the programme was working with community leaders, legal experts and the Nigeria Police Force to strengthen referrals, provide pro bono legal services to survivors and improve forensic evidence gathering for stronger investigations and prosecutions.

He urged stakeholders to integrate prevention into institutional plans and budgets and ensure that survivors had access to timely, confidential and accessible services.

Similarly, the Daisy Hope Foundation’s Programme Director, Dr Kiema Ogunlana, called for sustained coordination and improved referral services to ensure that women and girls in underserved communities, including persons with disabilities, were not left behind.

She urged the media to protect survivors’ privacy and follow up on commitments made by government and development partners.

The Director-General of the Maryam Babangida National Centre for Women Development, Adedayo Benjamins-Laniyi, highlighted the importance of translating existing laws into practical community-level action.

She cited the Centre’s collaboration with UN Women on a 220-hour Guinness World Record attempt involving the reading of African laws against sexual and gender-based violence, describing the initiative as an effort to give voice to the law and strengthen its implementation at the grassroots.

title: ACPN accuses Edo agency of illegal drug enforcement
description:
By Doris Obinna
The Association of Community Pharmacists of Nigeria (ACPN) has accused the Edo State Consumer Protection Committee of regulatory overreach, misinformation and unlawful enforcement in the pharmaceutical sector.
It warned that the committee’s actions could undermine patient safety and
content:
By Doris Obinna

The Association of Community Pharmacists of Nigeria (ACPN) has accused the Edo State Consumer Protection Committee of regulatory overreach, misinformation and unlawful enforcement in the pharmaceutical sector.

It warned that the committee’s actions could undermine patient safety and violate federal laws.
The association, in a petition to the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, called for an end to pharmaceutical enforcement activities by agencies operating outside their statutory mandates.

The petition, signed by ACPN National Chairman, Ambrose Ezeh, and National Secretary, Mrs. Obiageri Ikwu, specifically faulted the committee for allegedly declaring Camosunate a banned medicinal product in Nigeria without statutory authority or verifiable regulatory evidence.

ACPN maintained that the regulation, registration, suspension and prohibition of medicines fall within the statutory mandate of the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC), stressing that state agencies must not assume powers not expressly conferred on them by law.

Citing NAFDAC’s official Green Book, the association said Camosunate Children Powder, with registration number 04-7908, manufactured by Front Pharmaceuticals PLC and marketed by Geneith Pharmaceuticals Limited, remains an active registered medicine in Nigeria.

It said the product’s registration was approved on November 26, 2025, and remains valid until November 25, 2030.
According to ACPN, there is no official NAFDAC declaration establishing that the specific formulation described as banned by the Edo committee has been prohibited, suspended, withdrawn or deregistered.

The association described the committee’s reported declaration as misleading and a violation of established regulatory procedures, insisting that public claims about the safety or registration status of medicines must be backed by credible evidence.

It also questioned the reported enforcement action against ALSO CARE Pharmacy in Evbuodia community, along Airport Road, Benin City, demanding transparent disclosure of the products seized and their registration details.
The association also called for the release of independent regulatory evidence supporting allegations that the pharmacy stocked counterfeit or prohibited medicines.

ACPN warned against publicly condemning pharmaceutical establishments on the basis of unverified allegations, insisting that enforcement actions must be evidence-based and conducted in accordance with the law.

On the jurisdiction of state agencies, the association cited the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) Establishment Act 2022, particularly Sections 4, 22, 31 and 32, which provide the framework for the regulation, inspection, registration and licensing of pharmaceutical premises.

It argued that the Act vests the PCN with responsibility for regulating pharmaceutical premises in both the public and private sectors, through designated Pharmaceutical Inspection Officers.

The association also cited Sections 7 and 8 of the Counterfeit and Fake Drugs and Unwholesome Processed Foods (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, Cap C34, Laws of the Federation 2004, which provide for the constitution and powers of State Task Forces.

It, however, maintained that such statutory provisions do not automatically empower state consumer protection committees to exercise specialised pharmaceutical regulatory functions.

ACPN further argued that a general consumer protection mandate does not confer the authority to regulate medicines or inspect and control pharmaceutical premises outside the powers established by relevant federal laws.

Consequently, the association called for an end to pharmaceutical enforcement activities carried out without appropriate statutory authority, particularly in Edo State.

It urged the Federal Ministry of Justice to work with the Attorneys-General and Commissioners for Justice across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory to sensitise government agencies on their constitutional and statutory limits.

The association said respect for the respective mandates of NAFDAC and PCN was essential to protecting public health and preventing regulatory confusion.

ACPN reaffirmed its commitment to combating fake, counterfeit and falsified medicines, warning that consumer protection must not become a cover for misinformation, administrative arbitrariness or regulatory intimidation.
It insisted that public officials must be held accountable for claims made in the course of enforcement.

The post ACPN accuses Edo agency of illegal drug enforcement appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Osun police bust child trafficking syndicate, rescue 16-day-old baby
description:
By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo



The Osun State Police Command has dismantled a suspected child trafficking syndicate and rescued a 16-day-old baby boy allegedly sold for N1.5 million in a transaction involving two suspects.







The command’s Public Relations Officer, DSP Abiodun Ojelabi, disclosed t
content:
By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo

The Osun State Police Command has dismantled a suspected child trafficking syndicate and rescued a 16-day-old baby boy allegedly sold for N1.5 million in a transaction involving two suspects.

The command’s Public Relations Officer, DSP Abiodun Ojelabi, disclosed this in a statement on Monday, saying two suspects had been arrested in connection with the alleged trafficking.

According to the police, the baby’s mother, Victoria Michael, 18, gave birth at a private hospital in Kajola on November 2 but was unable to cater for the child after the father, identified as Tayo, allegedly denied responsibility.

Ojelabi said one of the mother’s friends, Comfort Olayinka, offered to help her find assistance through a contact in Abeokuta, Ogun State.

He said Olayinka subsequently linked up with Oladipo Olamide, 46, who allegedly claimed to operate a non-governmental organisation providing care for less-privileged persons and offered to take the baby into its care.

The police spokesman said the baby’s mother and Olayinka travelled to Abeokuta on November 5 and handed the child over to Olamide.

However, Olayinka later allegedly told the mother that the baby had died and gave her a folded object resembling a baby, packed in a bag, which she was instructed to throw into Lafenwa River.

Unknown to the mother, Olayinka had allegedly collected N450,000 from Olamide, purportedly for her upkeep.

Ojelabi said police operatives, acting on intelligence, arrested Olamide in Abeokuta on November 17.

During interrogation, the suspect allegedly confessed to selling the baby to one Mrs Bolanle Ruth for N1.5 million.

He said Olamide subsequently led the operatives to Akure, Ondo State, where Ruth was arrested on November 18.

According to the police, Ruth admitted paying N1.5 million for the baby and claimed she was promised that the necessary documents would be provided by an agency, but had yet to receive them.

The police did not disclose the whereabouts or status of the other suspect, Olayinka, in the statement.

Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police in Osun State, Ibrahim Zungura, warned individuals and groups against child trafficking, assuring residents that the command would not tolerate the crime.

He urged members of the public to provide useful information to security agencies to help prevent child trafficking and protect vulnerable children.

content:
By Efe Onodjae

The Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew on Ughelli North Local Government Area following reports of deadly violence and gunshots in parts of the council.

The curfew, which takes effect on Monday, November 23, 2026, will run daily from 6pm to 6am until further notice.

The Secretary to the State Government, Dr Kingsley Emu, announced the restriction in a statement, saying the measure was aimed at restoring calm and bringing the security situation under control.

According to the statement, the curfew covers the entire Ughelli North Local Government Area.

The government urged residents to comply strictly with the directive.

The development follows reports of deadly violence in the area, including an attack on the campaign team of former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, during a campaign tour of Uduere.

The attack reportedly left four persons dead and four others critically injured.

title: Greece reopens Acropolis museum after $11m renovation
description:
Greek authorities on Monday reopened a historic museum on the ancient Acropolis of Athens, prompting the country’s leader to repeat a demand for Britain to return prized classical sculptures it says were looted from the site.
Built from the late 19th century, the Old Acropolis Museum, a few metres (
content:
Greek authorities on Monday reopened a historic museum on the ancient Acropolis of Athens, prompting the country’s leader to repeat a demand for Britain to return prized classical sculptures it says were looted from the site.

Built from the late 19th century, the Old Acropolis Museum, a few metres (yards) away from the Parthenon temple, closed in 2007 and the site’s main treasures were transferred to a bigger site nearby.

That museum, opened in 2009, symbolically included a space for the Parthenon sculptures, which Greece maintains were looted in 1802 by a British diplomat.

The earlier site, the Old Acropolis Museum, reopened its doors on Monday after a 10-million-euro ($11 million) renovation, displaying precious works that have been brought out of storage.

Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis used a visit to the refurbished museum to make a pointed new demand for the return of the ancient sculptures.

“As we reopen the gates of the Old Acropolis Museum, just a few metres from the iconic Parthenon, our thoughts inevitably turn to what is missing,” he said.

“The return and reunification of the Parthenon sculptures remains firmly our great and non-negotiable national goal.”

Athens has for decades been demanding the return of the sculptures — sometimes known in Britain as the “Elgin marbles”, after the lord who Greece accuses of looting them.

Mitsotakis has said they could be an issue in any talks on Britain renewing its ties to the European Union.

• ‘New chapter’ –
The Old Acropolis Museum was the first museum to house antiquities from the iconic site of western civilisation dating back to the 5th century BC.

“A new chapter is opening for the Acropolis of Athens with the reopening of the Old Acropolis Museum,” Culture Minister Lina Mendoni said at the inauguration.

The “historic museum”, she added, was “inextricably linked to the history of Greek archaeology and excavations on the Sacred Rock”.

She said it would now have a new role as “a space for archaeological knowledge and contemporary cultural dialogue”.

The first part of the museum features a permanent exhibition of sculptures which had been kept in storage and are presented to the public for the first time.

The second part has 750 restored archaeological objects from the city of Athens.

A third section houses a three-dimensional digital presentation of 100 Acropolis monuments, created with the help of artificial intelligence.

A fourth part is dedicated to contemporary art, with an installation by the American-Iraqi artist Michael Rakowitz.

It shows “contemporary artworks interacting with ancient artefacts of the Middle East and southeastern Mediterranean regions”, according to the NEON art group.

Some 4.6 million people visited the Acropolis in 2025, according to official figures.

Visitors who pay 30 euros to get into the Parthenon will have to pay 15 euros to see the refurbished museum, according to organisers.

AFP

title: Adamawa court jails man 10 years for N7.48m fraud
description:
By Henry Obetta







An Adamawa State High Court sitting in Yola has sentenced a man, Shuaibu Usman, to 10 years’ imprisonment without an option of fine for defrauding Hamza Abba Ishaka of N7.48 million under the guise of investing in a digital mining business.







The court, presided over by J
content:
By Henry Obetta

An Adamawa State High Court sitting in Yola has sentenced a man, Shuaibu Usman, to 10 years’ imprisonment without an option of fine for defrauding Hamza Abba Ishaka of N7.48 million under the guise of investing in a digital mining business.

The court, presided over by Justice Benjamin Manji, also ordered Usman to refund the sum of N7,483,950 to the victim.

The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) disclosed this in a statement posted on its X account on Monday, saying the convict was prosecuted by its Gombe Zonal Directorate on a one-count charge of cheating.

According to the charge, Usman sometime in September 2022 in Yola, Adamawa State, dishonestly induced Ishaka to part with N7,483,950 under the pretext of investing in a digital mining business.

The offence was said to contravene Section 312 and punishable under Section 313 of the Adamawa State Penal Code Law, 2018.

The EFCC said Usman was arraigned on February 17, 2025, but pleaded not guilty, leading to a full trial.

During the trial, prosecution counsel, A.M. Labaran, called two witnesses and tendered documentary evidence to establish the case against the defendant.

The defence counsel, A.Y. Mohammed, on his part, presented four witnesses and tendered four exhibits.

In his judgment delivered on November 17, 2026, Justice Manji found Usman guilty and sentenced him to 10 years in prison without an option of fine.

The judge also ordered him to make full restitution of the defrauded sum to Ishaka.

The commission said the case followed a petition by Ishaka, who alleged that Usman collected the money from him on the promise of investing it in a digital mining business.

However, the purported investment turned out to be fraudulent, and efforts by the petitioner to recover his money from Usman were unsuccessful, prompting him to petition the EFCC.

title: Navy intercepts 89,000 litres of stolen crude, illegal diesel in Rivers
description:
By Kingsley Omonobi



The Nigerian Navy has intercepted about 35,000 litres of suspected stolen crude oil and uncovered an illegal refining site containing an additional 54,000 litres of suspected illegally refined Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) in Rivers State.



The operation, conducted on November 22
content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

The Nigerian Navy has intercepted about 35,000 litres of suspected stolen crude oil and uncovered an illegal refining site containing an additional 54,000 litres of suspected illegally refined Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) in Rivers State.

The operation, conducted on November 22 by personnel of Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Pathfinder around Okarki Creek and Okarki Community in Ahoada West Local Government Area, followed credible intelligence.

In a statement on Monday, the Director of Naval Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, said the naval personnel intercepted a wooden boat conveying about 150 sacks containing suspected stolen crude oil.

He said a subsequent operation in the adjoining area led to the discovery of an illegal refining site containing approximately 10 dugout pits, 180 sacks and a storage container holding an estimated 54,000 litres of suspected illegally refined AGO.

According to him, the combined volume of petroleum products recovered or identified during the operation was approximately 89,000 litres.

“The boat, its contents and the refining site, including the stored products, were handled in accordance with established anti-crude oil theft procedures,” the statement said.

The Navy described the operation as part of its sustained campaign to disrupt the supply networks supporting crude oil theft and illegal refining activities in the Niger Delta.

It said intercepting the suspected stolen crude oil and dismantling associated refining infrastructure would help deny oil thieves access to petroleum resources while addressing environmental degradation and revenue losses.

The Service reaffirmed its commitment to intelligence-driven operations to protect critical oil and gas infrastructure, support national crude oil production and safeguard Nigeria’s economic interests.

It added that operations would continue across the Niger Delta creeks to combat crude oil theft and illegal refining.

title: NEC approves additional N130bn for rehabilitation of police colleges
description:
The National Economic Council (NEC) has approved an additional N130 billion for the ongoing rehabilitation of police training institutions across the country.







The council also endorsed two major development projects involving proposed World Bank financing of 850 million dollars.







The pr
content:
The National Economic Council (NEC) has approved an additional N130 billion for the ongoing rehabilitation of police training institutions across the country.

The council also endorsed two major development projects involving proposed World Bank financing of 850 million dollars.

The projects are aimed at strengthening disaster preparedness, climate resilience and early childhood development across the country.

Gov. Peter Mbah of Enugu, Chairman of the NEC Ad-Hoc Committee on Rehabilitation of Police Training Institutions, disclosed this while briefing newsmen.

Mbah briefed newsmen on the outcome of the 162nd NEC meeting, held virtually and chaired by Vice-President Kashim Shettima.

NAN recalls that NEC, on Dec. 3, 2025, approved N100 billion for rehabilitating training institutions for the police and other security agencies.

The additional N130 billion brings the total approved funding to N230 billion.

Mbah disclosed that rehabilitation work was ongoing at 13 locations nationwide, with about 30 per cent of the work completed.

He explained that the additional N130 billion would accelerate the rehabilitation, upgrade training facilities and strengthen the capacity of police institutions.

According to him, the intervention would enable the institutions to accommodate increased recruitment and training requirements.

The governor said the intervention would also support preparations for recruiting 50,000 police personnel.

“It will also improve the country’s security training infrastructure,” Mbah said.

On the economy, the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr Taiwo Oyedele, informed the council that Nigeria’s economic indicators had continued to improve.

He said the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew by 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, compared with 4.23 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025.

He disclosed that headline inflation declined for the fifth consecutive month to 14.06 per cent in October 2026, its lowest level since September 2020.

“External reserves stood at 54.87 billion dollars as of November 12, 2026,” he said.

The minister said Nigeria’s trade surplus increased from N10.2 trillion in the first half of 2025 to N20.1 trillion in the corresponding period of 2026.

“Net revenue distributed through the Federation Account Allocation Committee rose by 44 per cent, from N15.2 trillion in 2024 to N21.9 trillion in 2025,” he said.

Oyedele, however, observed that the improving economic indicators had yet to translate sufficiently into relief for households and businesses.

“This is particularly in the areas of food prices, electricity costs, access to affordable credit and employment,” he said.

He noted that food inflation remained elevated at 19.13 per cent in October, while high lending rates and energy costs continued to pressure businesses and household incomes.

Meanwhile, the council approved two memoranda presented through the Federal Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning, headed by Sen. Atiku Bagudu.

Bagudu explained that the first concerned the proposed 350 million dollars Accelerating Resilience through Investment Systems and Engagement (ARISE-Nigeria) Project.

He said the six-year, World Bank-supported programme was designed to strengthen Nigeria’s capacity to anticipate, prepare for and respond to floods, droughts, fires and other natural disasters.

The minister said the programme would improve emergency operations centres, early warning systems, weather monitoring and disaster response financing at federal and state levels.

“Between five and 10 states are expected to participate in the initial phase.

“Selection will be based on disaster risk exposure, institutional readiness and commitment to emergency preparedness,” he said.

The minister said the second memorandum concerned Nigeria’s State-Led Early Childhood Development Programme.

“It is designed to improve children’s access to healthcare, nutrition, early learning and protection services across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory,” he said.

Bagudu said the initiative was expected to receive support through a proposed 500 million dollars World Bank financing arrangement.

He added that the Global Financing Facility had indicated potential additional grant support of 30 million dollars.

“Under the programme, early childhood development hubs will connect primary healthcare facilities with childcare, preschool education and other essential social services.

“This will particularly benefit underserved communities,” he said.

Bagudu said state governors were expected to provide leadership in implementation, resource mobilisation and accountability.

On the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) Act, 2026, Gov. Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta said the council called for stronger collaboration between the commission and state governments.

Oborevwori said the collaboration would accelerate the registration of Nigerians and improve the integration of the National Identification Number into public services.

He urged state governments to fast-track identity registration and data capture to ensure that all Nigerians were covered by the national identity system.

On pension reforms, Gov. Abdullahi Sule of Nasarawa said the council urged state governors to formally adopt implementation timelines for the Contributory Pension Scheme.

He said governors were also advised to direct their administrative and finance teams to work with the National Pension Commission (PenCom) on the necessary arrangements

title: Okpebholo promises third Benin flyover if Tinubu wins re-election
description:
Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has pledged to begin the construction of a third flyover bridge in Benin City if President Bola Tinubu wins the 2027 presidential election.
The proposed flyover, which would link Agbor Road to Sakpoba Road in Ikpoba-Okha Local Government Area, is expected to ope
content:
Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has pledged to begin the construction of a third flyover bridge in Benin City if President Bola Tinubu wins the 2027 presidential election.

The proposed flyover, which would link Agbor Road to Sakpoba Road in Ikpoba-Okha Local Government Area, is expected to open up the area to residents and businesses.

Okpebholo made the pledge while leading the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign through Ikpoba-Okha Local Government Area on Monday.

He had earlier led the campaign in Orhionmwon Local Government Area.

“I promise to start a flyover bridge from the back of Guinness to Sakpoba Road in Ikpoba-Okha. I need money to do this, and I can only do it with the support of President Tinubu,” he said.

The governor urged residents to turn out in large numbers and vote for Tinubu, adding that the proposed project would improve connectivity in the area.

He also called on residents to vote for APC candidates, whom he described as intelligent, credible and competent, saying they would work with his administration to sustain the state’s development drive.

This was contained in a Monday statement titled “Governor Okpebholo Pledges Third Flyover Bridge in Benin City with Tinubu as President come 2027”, signed by the governor’s Chief Press Secretary, Dr Patrick Akhere Ebojele.

Deputy Governor Dennis Idahosa thanked residents of Orhionmwon and Ikpoba-Okha for their continued support for the administration and assured them of more development projects.

He urged them to support Tinubu and all APC candidates in the general election to sustain the achievements recorded at the state and federal levels.

The senator representing Edo North and former governor of the state, Adams Oshiomhole, urged residents to vote based on intelligence, credibility and competence rather than ethnicity or sentiment.

“I urge you to vote for APC candidates who are intelligent, credible and competent, to deliver the dividends of democracy to the people they represent at the Senate, the House of Representatives and the Edo State House of Assembly,” he said.

Oshiomhole added that the APC had performed well at both the state and federal levels, saying Tinubu needed more than four years to complete his administration’s transformation agenda.

Former Deputy Governor Pius Odubu, who is also the APC senatorial leader in Edo South, assured residents of Orhionmwon and Ikpoba-Okha that Okpebholo would continue to improve living conditions across the state.

He thanked the governor for appointing indigenes of Orhionmwon to public offices and said Ikpoba-Okha had also benefited from development projects under his administration.

Odubu appealed to residents to vote for all APC candidates, including Tinubu, in the 2027 general election.

The APC leader in Edo South Senatorial District, Pastor Osagie Ize-Iyamu, commended the governor for flagging off electricity projects in Orhionmwon on Friday, November 20, 2026.

He said the area had been without reliable electricity for about 20 years before the intervention.

“We will support you for bringing us out of darkness. We will work with the other six local government areas in the senatorial district to ensure that we win Edo South for President Tinubu and all other APC candidates in the forthcoming general election,” he said.

The Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Mathew Urhoghide, commended Okpebholo for what he described as improved security across the state.

He urged residents of Ikpoba-Okha and Orhionmwon to help deliver 2.5 million votes for Tinubu, saying the President’s reforms had placed Nigeria on the path to growth and development.

The Edo State APC Chairman, Jarrett Tenebe, said the party had recorded a large influx of new members in Orhionmwon and that it remained united across the state.

He also said the security situation had improved, with cultism, kidnapping and other criminal activities drastically reduced.

“Gov Okpebholo met a divided state, but came in and brought unity into the party. Today we can boast of our unity, which is needed for our victory. This is not a time for fighting anybody, but with unity and cooperation we will continue to transform Edo State and Nigeria, making life better for the people,” he said.

The party’s Deputy State Chairman, Sylvester Aigboboh, said Orhionmwon and Ikpoba-Okha local government areas had benefited from more than 50 development projects.

He urged residents to vote in large numbers for Tinubu and other APC candidates to ensure the continuation of growth and development across the country.

title: 2027: NOA mobilises Benue communities against voter apathy, vote buying, electoral violence
description:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi



The National Orientation Agency (NOA) in Benue State has unveiled plans to intensify grassroots mobilisation across the 23 local government areas of the state ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning voters against apathy, vote buying, electoral violence and the spread
content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi

The National Orientation Agency (NOA) in Benue State has unveiled plans to intensify grassroots mobilisation across the 23 local government areas of the state ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning voters against apathy, vote buying, electoral violence and the spread of fake news.

The State Director of NOA, Comrade Mark Dewua, disclosed this in Makurdi while addressing journalists on the flag-off of the agency’s 2027 General Elections Grassroots Mobilisation Campaign in Benue state.

The campaign, which has the theme, “Your Vote, Your Voice, Our Future: Say No to Apathy, Vote Buying and Violence. Let’s Build a United Nigeria in 2027,” is aimed at encouraging citizens to take greater responsibility for the democratic process and promote peaceful, credible and inclusive elections.

Dewua explained that the nationwide campaign was launched in Abuja on October 15, 2026, by the Director-General of NOA, Mallam Lanre Issa-Onilu, stressing that the credibility of elections depended not only on the institutions conducting them but also on the attitude and participation of citizens.

He said: “Elections are an important part of our democracy, but their credibility and value depend not only on the institutions that conduct them but also on the attitude and participation of citizens. When people stay away from elections, they give up an important opportunity to influence decisions about their future.

“We therefore encourage all eligible voters to take an interest in the process, obtain relevant information from the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, ensure that they have their Permanent Voter Cards, PVCs, and participate in accordance with the Commission’s guidelines. Every vote represents a citizen’s voice, and that voice deserves to be heard.”

On vote buying, the NOA Director cautioned voters against exchanging their electoral choices for inducements, saying “we must make it clear that votes are not commodities for sale. We understand the economic challenges facing many Nigerians, but temporary financial benefits should not determine decisions with consequences that may last for years. We appeal to voters to reject inducements and to political actors to seek public support through their ideas, programmes and policies.”

Dewua also warned political actors and their supporters against resorting to violence, intimidation and destruction of property in pursuit of political ambitions, particularly cautioning young people against allowing themselves to be recruited as instruments of electoral violence.

“Our message, particularly to young people, is that no political ambition is worth a human life. Do not allow yourselves to be recruited or manipulated into acts of violence. Our communities must remain peaceful before, during and after the elections,” he said.

He further expressed concern over the spread of fake news, fabricated election results and inflammatory messages, particularly on social media, urging residents to verify information before sharing it and rely on credible sources, especially official communications from INEC.

According to him, the agency would also prioritise inclusive participation by women, young people, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups, ensuring that they have equal opportunities to participate in the democratic process through targeted community engagements and partnerships.

On its grassroots mobilisation strategy, Dewua said the agency would adopt community-driven approaches, taking electoral education directly to residents in their respective communities and communicating in languages they understand, including Tiv, Idoma and Igede.

He said: “The Agency will therefore intensify its engagement with traditional rulers, religious leaders, community associations, market groups, transport unions, youth and women organisations, schools, civil society organisations and other stakeholders. We will utilise town hall meetings, community dialogues, radio programmes, interpersonal communication, public sensitisation activities and digital platforms to expand the reach of the campaign.”

He added that NOA officers across the 23 Local Government Areas, LGA, would sustain engagements, identify information gaps and work with community stakeholders to promote responsible electoral conduct, stressing that the campaign would be a continuous enlightenment exercise leading to the 2027 elections.

The NOA director also solicited the cooperation of INEC, security agencies, political parties, traditional and religious institutions, civil society organisations and the media, emphasising that the agency remained non-partisan and was not established to promote any political party or candidate.

He appealed to journalists to give prominence to voter education, peaceful participation and the fight against misinformation, adding: “We also encourage you to help amplify the message that elections should be decided by the free choice of voters, not by money, intimidation or violence. Our democracy belongs to all of us, and its future depends on the choices we make and the responsibilities we accept.”

The post 2027: NOA mobilises Benue communities against voter apathy, vote buying, electoral violence appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Bayelsa boat tragedy death toll rises to 32, police warn operators
description:
The death toll from last Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 32, with the police warning boat operators and passengers against violating marine transportation safety regulations.
The Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of Zone 16, R
content:
The death toll from last Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 32, with the police warning boat operators and passengers against violating marine transportation safety regulations.

The Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of Zone 16, Regina Udoette, disclosed this on Monday during a visit to the Ayama-Ijaw waterside, where she assessed the ongoing search and rescue operation.

Udoette, accompanied by the Bayelsa State Commissioner of Police, Saka Ajao Adewale, interacted with marine transport workers and Red Cross personnel involved in the search for missing passengers.

She said reports from the rescue team indicated that more bodies had been recovered, raising the death toll from the previously reported 26 to 32.

The AIG condemned the reported overloading of the boat, which was said to have carried more than 500 passengers despite having a capacity of 200.

“The maritime personnel told us about the refusal of passengers to obey safety rules and how the boat captain loaded over 500 persons into a boat with a capacity for 200 passengers. That was a suicide mission and a disaster waiting to happen,” she said.

Udoette said the tragedy could have been avoided if the boat operator and passengers had complied with established safety regulations, particularly those requiring the use of life jackets and prohibiting overloading.

“Some of these deaths are avoidable deaths. Many of the passengers refused to obey safety rules. My Bible tells me that obedience is better than sacrifice. There are rules and regulations on the use of life jackets and overloading, but they refused to obey them,” she stated.

She urged the Bayelsa State Ministry of Transport and relevant marine transport unions to strengthen enforcement of passenger limits and compulsory life-jacket use.

The police chief also called for the arrest and prosecution of marine transport workers who violate safety regulations, saying such action would serve as a deterrent to others.

She said the delegation visited the area on behalf of the Inspector-General of Police to sympathise with the bereaved families and obtain first-hand information from marine operators and rescue personnel.

“I am here with my management team and the Bayelsa Commissioner of Police, on behalf of the Inspector-General of Police, to sympathise with the people who died in the incident. I register our condolences and wish the injured a quick recovery,” she said.

Udoette urged residents who rely on waterways for transportation to take safety precautions seriously and insist on basic protective measures before boarding boats.

“For the living, this is a big lesson to everyone who wants to use a boat for their journey. They should listen to the rules. People should use common sense. This disaster was avoidable,” she added.

The accident occurred last Friday along the Oweikorogha-Otuan waterway in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area when a passenger boat carrying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized.

The post Bayelsa boat tragedy death toll rises to 32, police warn operators appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Electoral Act not responsible for rising campaign violence — Adegbonmire
description:
By Cynthia Alo &  Kafayat Kokumo







Chairman of the Senate Ad Hoc Committee on Electoral Reforms,  Adeniyi Adegbonmire, has said the Electoral Act is not responsible for rising cases of campaign violence across the country, insisting that the problem lies in the failure of relevant institutions
content:
By Cynthia Alo & Kafayat Kokumo

Chairman of the Senate Ad Hoc Committee on Electoral Reforms, Adeniyi Adegbonmire, has said the Electoral Act is not responsible for rising cases of campaign violence across the country, insisting that the problem lies in the failure of relevant institutions to enforce its provisions.

Adegbonmire, who is also the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Judiciary, Human Rights, and Legal Matters, said the National Assembly had made adequate provisions for electoral offences in the Electoral Act and empowered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to prosecute offenders.

Speaking during an interview on Arise Television on Monday , he said the responsibility for addressing electoral violence rested on INEC, the police and other security agencies, which must ensure strict enforcement of the law.

He said: “The National Assembly passed an Electoral Act, the intention being to set out everything that relates to electoral matters, and in that Electoral Act there are electoral offences and it gives INEC the powers to prosecute.

“So, for me, when it comes to the Act itself, it’s made provisions for what you refer to, and so when it comes to all of these reports that we hear, electoral skirmishes here and there, I don’t think it’s a function of the Act. It’s a function of how to ensure whoever, INEC, police, security agents take advantage of the provisions of the Act.”

The senator also faulted what he described as inconsistent media reports on political violence, urging journalists to condemn attacks regardless of the political party involved or the identity of those responsible.

According to him, describing attacks against the ruling party as public protests while reporting similar incidents involving opposition parties as attacks by thugs could encourage a biased perception of political violence.

He said: “It is the collective responsibility of all of us to ensure that acts of violence in whatever form or fashion are condemned regardless of who is the victim or who are the perpetrators.”

On the Senate’s recent call for investigations into reported campaign violence, Adegbonmire clarified that the resolution was not an indictment of security agencies but an effort to draw attention to the growing threat and urge relevant institutions to act.

He disclosed that security agencies were investigating some incidents but cautioned against making arrests without proper investigations, noting that not everyone present at a violent rally necessarily participated in the violence.

“If we are going to follow the law, let’s follow it strictly regardless of what advantage or disadvantage it may visit upon us. Let everybody follow the rule of law,” he said.

On concerns about voter safety ahead of the 2027 general elections, the senator expressed confidence in the ability of security agencies to protect voters.

He cited the governorship elections in Anambra and Osun states, where Governors Chukwuma Soludo and Ademola Adeleke emerged winners, arguing that the outcomes reflected the choices of the electorate despite pockets of violence.

He said there was no empirical basis for predicting that the 2027 elections would not reflect the people’s choice.

The senator also defended INEC’s planned nationwide mock accreditation exercise scheduled for November 28, saying the exercise should be seen as an opportunity to identify and correct operational challenges before the presidential and National Assembly elections on January 16, 2027.

He said Nigerians should not condemn the commission if technical challenges emerged during the mock exercise, as identifying such problems ahead of the actual polls was its primary purpose.

On the proposed deployment of artificial intelligence, AI, in the electoral process, Adegbonmire said the Senate would wait for INEC to publish its guidelines before scrutinising the proposed framework.

He said the commission had indicated that it was developing guidelines for the deployment of the technology, adding that lawmakers would examine the document and seek necessary clarifications or corrections once it was released.

“I would prefer to wait for INEC to publish their guidelines and then we start to interrogate it if we feel that there’s a need to have certain corrections or clarifications done,” he said.

The post Electoral Act not responsible for rising campaign violence — Adegbonmire appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Instagram removes Polish tourist’s video accusing Daura Emir of sexual assault
description:
Instagram has removed a video shared by Polish tourist Mirka Cze, in which she accused the Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, of grabbing her breast during a visit to his palace in Katsina State.







Cze disclosed the removal in a post on her Instagram page on Monday, saying she believed the video
content:
Instagram has removed a video shared by Polish tourist Mirka Cze, in which she accused the Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, of grabbing her breast during a visit to his palace in Katsina State.

Cze disclosed the removal in a post on her Instagram page on Monday, saying she believed the video was taken down after several users reported it.

“It seems that because too many people were clicking on the ‘report’ button, the Instagram algorithm has removed the video. I didn’t,” she wrote.

The tourist said she had asked Meta, Instagram’s parent company, to review the decision and restore the video. She added that she was relieved other bloggers had reposted the footage, allowing it to remain in circulation.

Cze said she decided to speak publicly about the alleged incident because she had recorded evidence and wanted to draw attention to the experiences of women who might have suffered sexual abuse but had no opportunity to speak out.

“When this bad experience happened to me at the palace of the Emir of Daura, I felt I needed to share it. Because it happened to me. Because I had a chance and a tool to record it, and because I believe it happens to so many other women who don’t have a chance to speak up,” she said in the Instagram post.

She explained that her visit to the palace had initially been welcoming, with the emir offering her local food while palace guards showed her around the premises, including the stables, where she rode a horse.

However, she said she became uncomfortable when she was left alone with the traditional ruler, unlike her previous visits to other palaces where guards were present during her interactions with monarchs.

The Polish tourist also said she had visited 18 other locations and palaces across Nigeria without experiencing sexual assault before the alleged incident in Daura.

Reflecting on the reactions to her earlier post, Cze said most people had shown her kindness and support, although some questioned her account.

She added that she needed time away from the controversy to recover emotionally and move on from the experience.

“I’m writing this with tears coming down, and I really feel that for the healing and for getting in better mental space, I need to start thinking about other things and places to leave Nigeria and what happened there behind,” she wrote.

“I’ve seen the comments and messages, and would say that 90 per cent were supportive and kind, but I need my space now.”

Meta had yet to publicly explain why the video was removed as of Monday.

The post Instagram removes Polish tourist’s video accusing Daura Emir of sexual assault appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: FG moves to fast-track drug trials, seize traffickers’ assets
description:
The Federal Government has pledged to strengthen the prosecution of drug-related offences through the speedy disposal of cases, confiscation of illicit assets and enhanced international cooperation against drug trafficking networks.
The Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lat
content:
The Federal Government has pledged to strengthen the prosecution of drug-related offences through the speedy disposal of cases, confiscation of illicit assets and enhanced international cooperation against drug trafficking networks.

The Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi (SAN), disclosed this on Monday in Abuja at the inauguration of the National Drug Control Master Plan (NDCMP) 2026–2030.

Fagbemi said the Federal Ministry of Justice would collaborate with the judiciary to facilitate the speedy disposal of drug cases in accordance with the Administration of the Criminal Justice Act.

He said the ministry would also strengthen efforts to ensure that convictions for drug-related offences were accompanied by the confiscation of assets acquired through illicit activities.

“The government will intensify mutual legal assistance, extradition processes and cross-border asset recovery to disrupt the financial networks sustaining organised drug trafficking.

“These measures are necessary to strengthen Nigeria’s criminal justice response and ensure that drug traffickers did not continue to benefit from the proceeds of their illegal activities,” he said.

Fagbemi stressed that effective prosecution and asset recovery were critical to dismantling criminal enterprises and discouraging the financing of illicit drug markets.

He also commended the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) for promoting early collaboration between investigators and prosecutors.

He said the approach had helped strengthen evidence gathering, prevent procedural errors and improve the effectiveness of criminal proceedings.

The Attorney-General described the NDLEA as the bedrock of Nigeria’s national drug control architecture, citing its contributions to intelligence gathering, interdiction, investigation, prosecution and public sensitisation.

He particularly commended the NDLEA Chairman, retired Brig.-Gen. Buba Marwa, for his leadership and commitment to strengthening the country’s drug control efforts.

“The agency remains the bedrock of our national drug control architecture, delivering vital results across intelligence operations, interdiction, investigation, prosecution and public sensitisation.

“I specifically commend Brig.-Gen Buba Marwa, who has been a silent achiever and has consistently made this administration and country proud,” he said.

Fagbemi said the NDCMP 2026–2030 would consolidate the agency’s achievements within a broader whole-of-government framework.

He explained that the framework was designed to strengthen collaboration among law enforcement agencies, public health institutions, educational authorities, social development agencies, financial investigators and community stakeholders.

According to him, the multidimensional nature of drug-related challenges required an integrated approach that addressed both criminal activities and the social and health consequences of substance abuse.

The minister stressed that Nigeria’s legal and policy response must distinguish between major drug traffickers and persons experiencing substance use disorders.

He said while criminal kingpins must face the full weight of the law, individuals struggling with drug dependence should have access to appropriate medical and psychological support.

Fagbemi emphasised that effective drug control must combine firm law enforcement with prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and social reintegration.

He said such an approach would help ensure that the criminal justice system addressed organised trafficking without neglecting the health and welfare needs of persons affected by substance dependence.

The Attorney-General also commended the NDLEA’s alternative development initiatives aimed at replacing the cultivation of illicit drugs with legitimate agricultural activities.

He said the agency’s efforts to encourage the cultivation of lawful cash crops and other agricultural enterprises demonstrated the importance of addressing the economic factors associated with illicit drug production.

“As we saw in the documentary earlier, the NDLEA is delivering in that regard through successful efforts at replacing the planting and cultivation of illicit drugs with that of licit cash crops, in addition to other legitimate agricultural activities.

“This is a commendable move, in line with the agenda and philosophy of President Bola Tinubu to turn adversity into opportunities for progress,” he said.

Fagbemi said the initiative reflected the importance of providing sustainable economic alternatives to communities vulnerable to involvement in illicit drug cultivation.

He described the new master plan as an important instrument for strengthening institutional coordination and ensuring that drug control interventions were implemented consistently across relevant sectors.

The minister urged stakeholders to translate the provisions of the document into practical programmes and measurable outcomes.

He stressed that the plan should not be regarded merely as a policy statement but as a guide for the daily operations of institutions responsible for its implementation.

Fagbemi reiterated the commitment of the Federal Ministry of Justice to strengthening legal cooperation and supporting measures aimed at improving the effectiveness of Nigeria’s drug control system.

In a goodwill message, the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) Commission commended Nigeria for developing the NDCMP 2026–2030, describing it as an important contribution to regional drug control efforts.

The commission’s representative, Prof. Nassirou Bako-Arifari, Commissioner for Human Development and Social Affairs, said the master plan aligned with regional commitments towards a safer, healthier and more resilient West Africa.

Bako-Arifari said the success of the policy would depend on sustained political commitment, adequate funding and cooperation among governments, civil society organisations, communities, the private sector and international partners.

He stressed that drug trafficking and substance abuse were transnational challenges requiring coordinated responses across West African countries.

“Nigeria’s progress in implementing the master plan will contribute significantly to strengthening regional cooperation against illicit drug trafficking and its associated consequences.

“The ECOWAS Commission will stand with Nigeria at every step, sharing experience, mobilising support and linking this national effort to the work of other member states.

“Nigeria’s progress will guide the region because no country can win this fight alone,” he said. (NAN)

The post FG moves to fast-track drug trials, seize traffickers’ assets appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Fubara mourns victims of Bayelsa boat accident
description:
Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, has commiserated with his Bayelsa State counterpart, Senator Douye Diri, the government and people of Bayelsa State over the tragic boat accident that occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state.
The ill-fat
content:
Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, has commiserated with his Bayelsa State counterpart, Senator Douye Diri, the government and people of Bayelsa State over the tragic boat accident that occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state.

The ill-fated boat, which was conveying passengers from Ayama to Ukubie for a burial, reportedly capsized at the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities, leading to the loss of lives.

Authorities said on Sunday that the death toll from the boat mishap had risen to 29.

President Bola Tinubu, through Vice President Kashim Shettima, announced a donation of N250m in support of the families of the deceased.

Fubara, in a condolence message to Diri, said he received the news of the accident with deep shock and profound sadness.

Fubara’s condolences were contained in a statement issued in Port Harcourt on Monday by his Chief Press Secretary, Onwuka Nzeshi.

The governor described the tragedy as even more painful because the victims were on a journey of solidarity to honour and bury a loved one, only to meet this unfortunate fate.

The statement partly read, “On behalf of my family, the government and the good people of Rivers State, I extend our heartfelt condolences to you, the government and people of Bayelsa State, and particularly to the bereaved families and the affected communities”.

Fubara noted that, as neighbours bound by shared history, culture and brotherhood, the pain of the people of Bayelsa State was equally the pain of the people of Rivers State.

The governor commended the swift response of the Bayelsa State Government, security agencies, local divers and emergency responders in the search, rescue and recovery efforts, and prayed for the quick and full recovery of the survivors receiving medical attention.

He prayed that Almighty God would grant eternal rest to the souls of the departed, comfort the bereaved families, and give Governor Diri and the entire people of Bayelsa State the strength and fortitude to bear the irreparable loss.

The post Fubara mourns victims of Bayelsa boat accident appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
