title: Omo-Agege’s camp alleges four killed in Delta attack
description:
The campaign organisation of former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege has alleged that four people were killed and four others critically injured when gunmen attacked his entourage during a political gathering in Delta State.
The organisation, in a statement issued on Monday by Omo-Agege’s Medi
content:
The campaign organisation of former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege has alleged that four people were killed and four others critically injured when gunmen attacked his entourage during a political gathering in Delta State.

The organisation, in a statement issued on Monday by Omo-Agege’s Media Adviser, Sunny Areh, said the former lawmaker, who is the Nigeria Democratic Congress senatorial candidate for Delta Central, escaped unhurt during the incident at Uduere in Ughelli North Local Government Area.

It described the incident as an assassination attempt, although the circumstances and casualty figures had yet to be independently verified.

The organisation said, “We are pained to report that four people, including two of our aides — Moses Anaughe and Akima Efemena Umukoro — were shot dead.”

It also named four others who were reportedly shot and critically injured as Chief Evans Iwuvrie, Chuks Erhire, Tobore Agba, who was allegedly shot in the neck, and Ayodo Wanogho.

“They are currently receiving medical attention. We pray for their speedy recovery and we stand with their families at this dark hour,” the statement added.

According to the organisation, armed men opened fire at close range on Omo-Agege and his entourage during what it described as a peaceful campaign tour.

The organisation described the incident as a targeted attempt to assassinate the former deputy senate president.

The campaign organisation also accused the Delta State Police Command of failing to prevent the attack, despite the alleged presence of its officers at the scene.

It called on the Inspector-General of Police to personally take over the investigation, saying it had lost confidence in the state command.

“We in fact, call on the Inspector-General of Police to personally take over the investigation as we no longer have confidence in the Delta State Police Command whose officers were present with Six trucks but did nothing to prevent the attack and killings,” it stated.

The organisation also called on the Director-General of the Department of State Services and the Delta State Commissioner of Police to intervene.

It urged Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, to publicly condemn the attack, ensure the arrest and investigation of those accused of participating in or directing it, and guarantee the safety of opposition candidates in the state.

“Delta State is not a war zone. Campaigning is not a crime. Seeking the votes of the people should not be a death sentence,” the statement added.

The organisation urged its supporters not to retaliate or take the law into their hands, saying its ward-to-ward campaign tour of Delta Central would continue.

The Delta State Police Command had yet to comment on the reported attack as of the time of filing this report.

The casualty figures and allegations made by the campaign organisation had not been independently verified.

The post Omo-Agege’s camp alleges four killed in Delta attack appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Plateau blames dam repairs for water shortage in Jos
description:
The Plateau State Government has blamed the ongoing rehabilitation of major water treatment plants for the water shortage being experienced by residents of Jos and Bukuru.
The General Manager of the Jos Water Services Corporation, Apollos Samchi, stated this on Monday while leading journalists on an
content:
The Plateau State Government has blamed the ongoing rehabilitation of major water treatment plants for the water shortage being experienced by residents of Jos and Bukuru.

The General Manager of the Jos Water Services Corporation, Apollos Samchi, stated this on Monday while leading journalists on an inspection tour of the ongoing rehabilitation work at the Yakubu Gowon Dam and Liberty Dam and their treatment plants.

The tour came amid concerns raised by residents over the water shortage in Jos and Bukuru.

Samchi said the ongoing repairs at the Yakubu Gowon Dam were responsible for the low water supply being experienced by residents.

“The repairs ongoing at the Yakubu Gowon Dam are responsible for the low water supply being experienced by residents within Jos and Bukuru metropolis,” he said.

He added that rehabilitation work was also ongoing at the Lamingo Treatment Plant.

“Rehabilitation work at the Lamingo Treatment Plant is also ongoing. We have less power consumption at the plant so that production can continue,” he said.

Samchi explained that production was being affected because some production lines had to be shut down to enable the contractor to carry out the work.

“Product is also being affected because you have to shut down some production lines to enable the contractor to do his work. We want people to know that water must continue. We must make sure that,” he said.

According to the Jos Water Services Corporation, the Yakubu Gowon Water Treatment Plant, which supplies about 80 per cent of the water consumed in Jos and its environs, has not been rehabilitated in the last 50 years.

The state government recently signed a contract worth over N13.5bn with the China Geo-Engineering Corporation for the rehabilitation of the two plants.

On the project timeline, Samchi said the rehabilitation was time-bound and would be completed as scheduled.

“We have an 18-month timeline to finish work on the two projects. By then, they will have been completed and handed over to us,” he said.

“It started in February. The work has gone halfway into the project. Some of the equipment is being procured from China and shipped to Nigeria. I’m happy to announce to you that some of them have started arriving in Jos for installation. After that, we will be able to increase our water production to serve the increasing demands,” he added.

Samchi also spoke about the problem of frequent pipe bursts whenever water was supplied across the metropolis.

“Each time we supply water, there will be leakages of water all over the town. Some are a result of vandalism or inability of our customers to take care of their pipes,” he said.

“Most of the reasons for water bursts are because most of the pipes are rusted, some over fifty years old, and they usually give way when pressurised water passes through them,” he said.

He said the government had, therefore, decided that the pipes needed to be replaced.

“Based on this, the government decided that these pipes have to be replaced. We are going to do almost 400km of pipe laying between Jos and Bukuru metropolis,” Samchi said.

He disclosed that the pipe-laying work had been divided into 17 zones, with work ongoing in eight of them.

“We have zoned the work into 17 zones. We start with eight now; work is ongoing,” he said.
Samchi added that the project also included household metering to ensure transparency in water supply.

“Connected to the pipeline is household metering. We will also make the metering very transparent to be on par with modern water supply. All water consumers will be metered,” he said.

“If you want to tamper with it, it is very sensitive and will just cut you off,” he added.

On measures to cushion the effects of the shortage, Samchi said the corporation had provided alternative sources of water to affected communities.

“Water supply has drastically reduced because of ongoing rehabilitation work at the dams. We have provided three tankers. Organised communities to take water to them for free. Constructed five water kiosks. Presently designing ten more,” he said.

He said the corporation was targeting vulnerable locations for water supply, including Tudun Wada, Bauchi Road, Utan and Jenta Adamu.

“We are targeting very vulnerable locations for water supply, including Tudun Wada, Bauchi Road, Utan and Jenta Adamu. We also have a water scheme to take care of Tudun,” he said.

Samchi also disclosed plans to extend water supply from the Lamingo plant to other parts of the metropolis.

“We also want to start pumping water from Lamingo treatment plant to other parts of Jos metropolis,” he said.

He appealed to residents to be patient, assuring them that efforts were being made to address the water challenge comprehensively.

He said the water project reflected the commitment of the administration of Governor Caleb Mutfwang to ensuring a steady supply of potable water to residents within the Greater Jos Master Plan.

He urged residents of Jos and Bukuru to bear with the temporary disruption, assuring them that the rehabilitation, when completed, would guarantee an improved and sustainable water supply to the metropolis.

The post Plateau blames dam repairs for water shortage in Jos appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Obi Meets Niger State Residents, Urges Nigerians To Turn Out For 2027 Elections
description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged Nigerians to turn out en masse for the 2027 general elections and remain at their polling units until their votes are counted and transmitted.Obi made the call during a campaign visit to Suleja, Niger State, wh
content:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged Nigerians to turn out en masse for the 2027 general elections and remain at their polling units until their votes are counted and transmitted.

Obi made the call during a campaign visit to Suleja, Niger State, where he urged voters to resist attempts to manipulate the outcome of the elections by ensuring that their votes were properly accounted for.

He also criticised President Bola Tinubu, claiming that the president lacked the physical strength required to govern the country and was more interested in retaining power for personal gains than serving Nigerians.

Obi, who is seeking the presidency for the second time, also promised to address Nigeria’s electricity challenges, pledging that his administration would generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000 megawatts of electricity if elected.

He said Niger State would play a role in achieving the target, citing the state’s resources as part of the potential support for his proposed power-sector plan.

The former Anambra State governor has been holding town hall meetings and engaging residents in different states ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Obi contested the 2023 presidential election under the Labour Party, finishing third with 6,101,533 votes, behind Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, who polled 8,794,726 votes, and Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, who received 6,984,520 votes.

Tinubu is seeking re-election in 2027, while Obi is contesting under the NDC.

Ahead of the election, major contenders include Tinubu under the APC, Atiku of the ADC, and Obi of the NDC.

Other parties include the AAC, PDP, APM, SDP, PRP, Labour Party, and YPP.

The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections are slated for February 6, 2027.

title: Okpebholo Promises Third Benin Flyover If Tinubu Wins 2027 Election
description: Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has pledged to commence the construction of a third flyover bridge in Benin City linking Agbor Road to Sakponba Road in Ikpoba-Okha Local Government Area, if President Bola Tinubu wins the 2027 presidential election.Okpebholo made the promise during the All Prog
content:
Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has pledged to commence the construction of a third flyover bridge in Benin City linking Agbor Road to Sakponba Road in Ikpoba-Okha Local Government Area, if President Bola Tinubu wins the 2027 presidential election.

Okpebholo made the promise during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Ikpoba-Okha, after leading the party’s campaign in Orhionmwon Local Government Area.

He said the proposed flyover would improve access to the area for residents and businesses but noted that its construction would depend on financial support from the Federal Government.

“I promise to start a flyover bridge from the back of Guinness to Sakpoba Road in Ikpoba-Okha. I need money to do this, and I can only do it with the support of President Tinubu,” the governor said, urging residents to vote for Tinubu and other APC candidates in the 2027 general election.

The governor also urged residents to support APC candidates, whom he described as intelligent, credible and competent, saying they would work with his administration to sustain development in the state.

Deputy Governor Dennis Idahosa thanked residents of Orhionmwon and Ikpoba-Okha for their support and urged them to vote for Tinubu and other APC candidates to sustain development.

Former Edo governor and Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, also urged voters to prioritise competence and credibility over ethnic considerations, saying the APC had performed well at both state and federal levels.

Former deputy governor Pius Odubu assured residents of continued development under Okpebholo, while APC leader in Edo South, Osagie Ize-Iyamu, commended the governor for the commencement of electricity projects in Orhionmwon, which he said had been without reliable electricity for about 20 years.

Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Matthew Urhoghide, praised the governor for what he described as improved security and called on residents to help deliver 2.5 million votes for Tinubu.

He also described the President’s reforms as a pathway to national growth.

APC State Chairman Jarrett Tenebe said the party had gained new members in Orhionmwon and remained united.

He added that cultism, kidnapping and other criminal activities had reduced across the state.

Tenebe attributed the party’s unity to Okpebholo’s leadership and urged members to work together to secure victory in the 2027 elections.

Deputy State Chairman Sylvester Aigboboh said Orhionmwon and Ikpoba-Okha had benefited from more than 50 development projects, urging residents to vote for Tinubu and other APC candidates to sustain the development.

The Ramat Park Flyover at Ikpoba Hill is the state’s first flyover.

It links the Benin-Auchi and Benin-Asaba highways.

The project also includes road expansion, improved drainage, and the redevelopment of a recreational park.

The second project, the Adesuwa Junction Flyover along Sapele Road, is designed to ease traffic congestion at the busy intersection connecting the Benin-Sapele-Warri corridor.

Approved in April 2025 and subsequently flagged off, construction is ongoing alongside the wider reconstruction of Sapele Road.

The post Okpebholo Promises Third Benin Flyover If Tinubu Wins 2027 Election appeared first on Channels Television.

content:
Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Yahaya, has promised to construct a N3.6bn general hospital in Billiri Local Government Area as part of efforts to expand healthcare access in the state.

Yahaya disclosed this during a visit to the palace of the Mai Tangle, Malam Danladi Sanusi-Maiyamba, on Monday, while leading the All Progressives Congress Campaign Council on a political tour of the area.

The governor said the proposed hospital was in response to a longstanding demand by residents, assuring them that construction would commence soon.

He said, “The proposed N3.6bn general hospital is part of our commitment to improving healthcare delivery and responding to the needs of our people in Billiri.”

Yahaya explained that the facility would complement existing investments in primary healthcare centres across the wards of the local government, as well as the Federal Orthopaedic Hospital approved by President Bola Tinubu for Billiri.

According to him, the federal institution would improve access to specialised medical services and address complex healthcare needs in the area.

The governor also urged residents to support Tinubu and other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections, promising that his successor would sustain the development programmes of his administration.

He acknowledged the economic difficulties associated with the Tinubu administration’s reforms but described them as “necessary decisions that previous governments had avoided for decades”.

Yahaya expressed optimism that the reforms would eventually produce positive results, urging Nigerians to remain patient and support the process.

He attributed the development recorded in Gombe State to the relative peace and security enjoyed across the state, noting that stability remained essential to implementing government projects.

Responding, the Mai Tangle, Sanusi-Maiyamba, commended the governor for his administration’s interventions, particularly efforts to sustain peace and security in Billiri.

The traditional ruler also prayed for continued peace and stability in the local government and Gombe State before, during and after the 2027 general elections.

title: FCT upgrades 20 PHCs, expands free maternal healthcare to pregnant women
description:
The Federal Capital Territory Administration has upgraded 20 primary healthcare centres across the six area councils and expanded free maternal healthcare services to reduce maternal deaths and improve access to healthcare.
The Mandate Secretary of the FCT Health Services and Environment Secretariat
content:
The Federal Capital Territory Administration has upgraded 20 primary healthcare centres across the six area councils and expanded free maternal healthcare services to reduce maternal deaths and improve access to healthcare.

The Mandate Secretary of the FCT Health Services and Environment Secretariat, Dr Dolapo Fasawe, disclosed this on Monday during a community engagement at the Owner Occupier Primary Healthcare Centre, Kubwa, Abuja.

Fasawe said the upgraded facilities had been equipped with electricity, water, staff accommodation, medical equipment and essential medicines to enable round-the-clock services.

She said the centres provided maternal and child healthcare, immunisation, nutrition services, breastfeeding education, malaria testing and treatment, as well as emergency referrals.

According to her, the administration was also providing free maternal healthcare and one-year health insurance coverage to eligible residents, with at least 1,000 women already enrolled in the programme.

“We are addressing the three delays that contribute to maternal deaths: the delay in deciding to seek care, the delay in reaching a health facility and the delay in receiving appropriate treatment,” she said.

To address transportation challenges, Fasawe said the FCTA had introduced emergency transportation arrangements involving commercial drivers and transport workers to ensure that pregnant women and other patients could reach health facilities when they needed care.

She said the arrangement complemented the FCT Emergency Medical Services and Ambulance System, which was linked to the national emergency response system.

The mandate secretary also disclosed that women who delivered in recognised FCT health facilities received baby-care kits, while delivery kits containing essential medical supplies were provided to reduce the financial burden on expectant mothers and encourage institutional childbirth.

She attributed the decline in malaria incidence in the territory from 18.7 per cent in 2023 to 7.4 per cent to free testing, treatment, immunisation and other interventions.

Fasawe further said health insurance enrolment in the FCT had “increased by nearly 70 per cent”, adding that the administration was strengthening healthcare workers’ welfare and facility-level funding through the Basic Health Care Provision Fund.

She urged community leaders and residents to monitor health facilities and report any that demanded payment for services designated as free.

A World Bank Senior Health Specialist and Task Team Leader of the Immunisation Plus and Malaria Progress by Accelerating Coverage and Transforming Services project, Dr Onoriode Ezire, said the initiative was being integrated into government programmes to ensure its sustainability beyond the project’s lifespan.

Ezire said the FCT had demonstrated ownership of the interventions by committing government resources to emergency services and other healthcare programmes, while the World Bank continued to provide technical support.

Also speaking, the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement (North-Central), Dr Abiodun Essiet, said more than 16 million Nigerians had been enrolled in health coverage since 2023, while over N235bn had been invested in primary healthcare upgrades.

She said the Basic Health Care Provision Fund was supporting the upgrade of at least one primary healthcare centre in each ward across the 774 local government areas.

Essiet added that about 48,000 women had benefited from free maternal and child healthcare packages, while 14 million girls had received human papillomavirus vaccinations.

She said the Federal Government was targeting 90 per cent primary healthcare coverage by 2027, alongside the expansion of free emergency childbirth services.

Meanwhile, a deaf beneficiary of the free Caesarean section intervention commended the programme but called for sign-language interpreters in health facilities to help persons with hearing impairments access antenatal information and other healthcare services.

The FCT APC Woman Leader, Farida Suleiman, also commended the facility’s upgrade and called for similar interventions across the six area councils and 62 wards.

The post FCT upgrades 20 PHCs, expands free maternal healthcare to pregnant women appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NEC Approves Fresh ₦130bn For Police Colleges, Endorses $850m World Bank Projects
description: ​The National Economic Council (NEC) has approved an additional ₦130 billion for the overhaul of police training institutions nationwide and endorsed two major World Bank-backed development projects valued at $850 million.​The resolutions were reached on Monday during the council’s 162nd meeti
content:
​The National Economic Council (NEC) has approved an additional ₦130 billion for the overhaul of police training institutions nationwide and endorsed two major World Bank-backed development projects valued at $850 million.

​The resolutions were reached on Monday during the council’s 162nd meeting held virtually and presided over by Vice President Kashim Shettima.

The fresh allocation raises total committed funding for the police training rehabilitation programme to ₦230 billion, coming alongside discussions on Nigeria’s macroeconomic outlook, pension reforms, and national identity integration.

​The ₦130 billion approval follows an initial ₦100 billion tranche authorised after President Bola Tinubu recommended the establishment of an ad hoc intervention committee in October 2025.

Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah, who chairs the NEC Ad-Hoc Committee on the Rehabilitation of Police Training Institutions, briefed the council that construction was currently underway across 13 locations nationwide, with 30 percent of the work completed.

According to the committee, the additional funds will accelerate infrastructure upgrades to support the planned recruitment and training of 50,000 new police personnel ahead of the anticipated rollout of state policing.

World Bank $850m Financing

​In a separate resolution, council approved two memoranda presented by the Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Senator Atiku Bagudu, involving $850 million in proposed World Bank financing.

​The first is the $350 million Accelerating Resilience through Investment Systems and Engagement (ARISE-Nigeria) Project, a six-year programme designed to bolster federal and state capacities to manage floods, droughts, fires, and other natural disasters.

Five to 10 states will participate in the initial phase based on disaster risk exposure and institutional readiness.

The second memorandum covers the State-Led Early Childhood Development Programme, backed by $500 million in proposed World Bank financing and a potential $30 million grant from the Global Financing Facility, aimed at linking primary healthcare with childcare and preschool services across all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

​Briefing the council on the state of the economy, the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, reported improvements across major macroeconomic indicators.

Real Gross Domestic Product grew by 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, up from 4.23 per cent in the same period of 2025.

Headline inflation declined for the fifth consecutive month to 14.06 per cent in October 2026—its lowest level since September 2020, while external reserves stood at $54.87 billion as of November 12.

​Oyedele added that Nigeria’s trade surplus nearly doubled from ₦10.2 trillion in the first half of 2025 to ₦20.1 trillion in the first half of 2026, while net revenue distributed through the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) rose by 44 per cent from ₦15.2 trillion in 2024 to ₦21.9 trillion in 2025.

However, the minister cautioned that the gains had yet to provide sufficient relief to households and businesses, citing elevated food inflation at 19.13 per cent in October, alongside high lending rates and energy costs.

​Council also deliberated on identity management and pension administration.

Members urged state governments to collaborate with the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) under the proposed NIMC Act 2026 to fast-track citizen registration and integrate the National Identification Number (NIN) into public services to curb payroll and pension fraud.

Additionally, following a presentation by National Pension Commission (PenCom) Director-General Omolola Oloworaran, the council urged state governors to adopt formal timelines for the full implementation of the Contributory Pension Scheme.

​Earlier in his opening remarks, Vice President Kashim Shettima charged ministries and state governors to build durable institutions capable of sustaining President Tinubu’s economic reforms.

Emphasising intergovernmental cooperation and citizen inclusion, Shettima noted that proactive investments like the ARISE-Nigeria project were vital to protecting vulnerable households and enterprises from economic shocks.

​”The capacity to recover should never depend entirely on the resources a person already possesses,” the Vice President said. “People affected by an intervention must also have a place in shaping it. Their experience can reveal what a proposal overlooks, and the strength of a project rests partly on the institutions and citizens that will carry it.”

The post NEC Approves Fresh ₦130bn For Police Colleges, Endorses $850m World Bank Projects appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Re-electing Tinubu is the best way to appreciate him — Sanwo-Olu
description:
Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has urged Nigerians to re-elect President Bola Tinubu in 2027, saying voting for him and other All Progressives Congress candidates is the only way to appreciate the administration’s efforts.
This was disclosed in a statement released on Monday by the Govern
content:
Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has urged Nigerians to re-elect President Bola Tinubu in 2027, saying voting for him and other All Progressives Congress candidates is the only way to appreciate the administration’s efforts.

This was disclosed in a statement released on Monday by the Governor’s Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Gboyega Akosile.

Sanwo-Olu also called on Lagos residents to support the state’s Deputy Governor and APC governorship candidate, Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, in the 2027 governorship election.

The governor made the appeal during the APC Lagos Central Senatorial District rally held at the Mobolaji Johnson Arena, Onikan, Lagos, where he highlighted what he described as the achievements of the Tinubu administration.

He said the President had made significant progress in transforming the country through investments in road construction, rail transportation, aviation and other critical sectors.

“The only way to show appreciation to the President is by coming out to vote massively for him and all APC candidates. That is the only way we can continue to enjoy the development he has started,” Sanwo-Olu said.

The governor also expressed confidence in Hamzat’s ability to lead Lagos State, urging residents to support his candidacy and allow him to build on the achievements of the current administration.

“K.O.H. has served you well, and he will serve you even better. He will serve you with greater commitment and dedication. I urge you all to support him and give him the opportunity to continue the good work and build on the achievements already recorded.

“Let us come out in our numbers, mobilise our families, friends and neighbours, and ensure his overwhelming victory in the 2027 election,” he said.

Hamzat, in his remarks, urged APC members and supporters to intensify mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election, saying no nation could make meaningful progress with a manifesto of grievances.

He called on party faithful to turn out in large numbers on January 16 to vote for Tinubu and other APC candidates in the National Assembly elections, while urging them to support him and all House of Assembly candidates on February 6.

The deputy governor said continued electoral support for the APC would enable Lagos to sustain its development trajectory and consolidate the gains recorded, rather than reverse the progress made.

Also speaking, the Senator representing Lagos Central Senatorial District, Wasiu Eshilokun-Sanni, urged residents to vote for APC candidates, describing them as credible leaders committed to infrastructure development and national progress.

He highlighted the achievements of APC-led administrations in improving citizens’ welfare through empowerment programmes, infrastructure development and other people-oriented initiatives.

In his welcome address, the Lagos State APC Chairman, Cornelius Ojelabi, urged registered voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards to enable them to participate in the forthcoming elections.

He stressed that the PVC remained the only instrument through which citizens could exercise their right to vote and elect their preferred candidates.

“Let us go out and collect our PVCs because they are the only means through which we can participate and exercise our civic rights in the coming election. Let us encourage our family members, friends and neighbours to vote for PBAT/KOH in the 2027 general election. By doing so, we can ensure continuity in infrastructure development and the progress of our nation,” he said.

The Director-General of the PBAT/KOH Campaign Council, Musiliu Obanikoro, described Tinubu as a committed and steadfast APC member whose leadership and resilience exemplified the qualities of a true leader.

Obanikoro also described Tinubu and Hamzat as knowledgeable leaders interested in the development of the country, particularly in children’s education, which he identified as the bedrock of every developed society.

The post Re-electing Tinubu is the best way to appreciate him — Sanwo-Olu appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Humanitarian group appoints Anambra health commissioner as state director
description:
The Anambra State Commissioner for Health, Dr Afam Obidike, has been appointed the state director of BATMEDICS, a Nigerian medical support and humanitarian outreach organisation.
The appointment was announced in a statement issued on Monday by the organisation’s National Director of Research, Media,
content:
The Anambra State Commissioner for Health, Dr Afam Obidike, has been appointed the state director of BATMEDICS, a Nigerian medical support and humanitarian outreach organisation.

The appointment was announced in a statement issued on Monday by the organisation’s National Director of Research, Media, Publicity and Strategic Communications, Petra Onyegbule.

BATMEDICS, formed in 2022, mobilises medical professionals to provide free healthcare services and support to underserved communities across Nigeria.

Onyegbule said Obidike’s appointment was expected to strengthen the organisation’s coordination of health services and deepen its engagement with communities across Anambra State.

The statement read, “BATMEDICS is pleased to announce the appointment of Dr Afam Ben Obidike as Anambra State Director of BATMEDICS.

“Obidike is a public health physician, service-delivery-oriented consultant anaesthetist, and Critical Care Specialist who collaborates across multidisciplinary teams to deliver high-standard emergency and critical care services.

“He has made major contributions to public health policy, emergency care systems, and healthcare human resource management and is currently concluding an MSc in International Public Health at the University of Liverpool, England.

“His appointment comes in handy in strengthening BATMEDICS’ leadership coordination on health services and deepening engagement in communities across Anambra State.

“Join us in congratulating Dr Afam Ben Obidike as we wish him success in the discharge of this critical responsibility.”

The post Humanitarian group appoints Anambra health commissioner as state director appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Lagos Assembly Adopts Report On Tenancy Bill
description: The Lagos State House of Assembly has adopted the report of the House Committee on Housing titled ‘Lagos State Tenancy Bill, 2025,’ marking another significant step towards establishing a comprehensive legal framework for regulating landlord-tenant relationships and the recovery of premi
content:
The Lagos State House of Assembly has adopted the report of the House Committee on Housing titled ‘Lagos State Tenancy Bill, 2025,’ marking another significant step towards establishing a comprehensive legal framework for regulating landlord-tenant relationships and the recovery of premises across the State.

The proposed legislation, titled ‘A Bill for a Law to Regulate the Relationship Between Landlords and Tenants Including the Procedure for the Recovery of Premises in Lagos State and for Other Connected Matters,’ seeks to provide a more structured and transparent framework for tenancy arrangements in the State.

It will be recalled that the bill had earlier undergone a public hearing on Wednesday, August 13, 2025, where stakeholders in the housing sector, legal profession, real estate industry, government institutions and civil society organisations made submissions and recommendations towards strengthening the proposed legislation.

Presenting the report, the Chairman, Committee on Housing, Olusegun Ege, stated that the bill was aimed at addressing prevailing challenges in the rental sector, while clearly defining the rights, responsibilities and obligations of landlords and tenants and providing appropriate procedures for the recovery of premises.

The proposed law is expected to promote a more orderly rental market, strengthen the administration of tenancy agreements and provide a clearer legal framework for resolving disputes arising from landlord-tenant relationships.

Following the presentation of the report, the sitting, which was presided over by the Speaker of the House, Mudashiru Obasa, subsequently adopted the recommendations of the Committee as the resolution of the House.

The initiative represents a further step in the legislative process towards reforming tenancy regulation in Lagos State, with particular attention to the need for fairness, accountability and protection of the interests of both property owners and tenants.

The post Lagos Assembly Adopts Report On Tenancy Bill appeared first on Channels Television.

title: 2027: APC will win three South-East states, Obi may take Abia, Anambra – Bwala
description: The Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, has projected that the All Progressives Congress (APC) will win three of the five South-East states in the 2027 general elections, while acknowledging that former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi could retain strong
content:
The Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, has projected that the All Progressives Congress (APC) will win three of the five South-East states in the 2027 general elections, while acknowledging that former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi could retain strong political support in Abia and Anambra states.

Bwala made the projection on Monday during an interview on Channels Television’s Morning Brief, where he discussed the ruling party’s chances of making electoral gains in the South-East.

According to him, Obi’s political influence in Abia and Anambra could make it difficult for the APC to secure victories in the two states.

He, however, expressed confidence that the ruling party would win the remaining three states in the region.

“We will struggle in Abia. You see, in Abia and Anambra, Peter has a very convincing presence. Even in these two states, I am assuming that if we lose, we still come second, which is not a bad thing. Apart from these two states, the remainder of the states, we are winning,” Bwala said.

The presidential aide clarified that his assessment was a projection rather than a definite prediction, noting that political actors could arrive at different conclusions based on their interpretation of available information.

He said the APC was willing to acknowledge areas where it might face electoral challenges instead of claiming it would win every state.

Bwala added that admitting the party’s potential difficulties in Abia and Anambra did not amount to conceding defeat in the two states.

The presidential aide also expressed confidence in the APC’s overall chances ahead of the 2027 elections, questioning the preparedness of opposition parties to challenge the ruling party.

“I do not think the opposition is ready. Those who understand the political trajectory can see that they are already facing defeat,” he added.

Bwala’s comments come amid growing political activities and realignments by parties and political groups ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The post 2027: APC will win three South-East states, Obi may take Abia, Anambra – Bwala appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Alliance With Tinubu Has Benefited Rivers, Must Continue Beyond 2027 — Wike
description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has urged the people of Rivers State to sustain their political alliance with President Bola Tinubu beyond 2027, saying the partnership has attracted critical infrastructure and development projects to the state.Wike said residents sh
content:
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has urged the people of Rivers State to sustain their political alliance with President Bola Tinubu beyond 2027, saying the partnership has attracted critical infrastructure and development projects to the state.

Wike said residents should assess political leaders based on their records in office rather than ethnic ties or claims of brotherhood, arguing that strategic alliances were necessary to secure development for their communities.

He spoke on Monday during a town hall meeting with political leaders, traditional rulers, youths, women and other stakeholders in Khana Local Government Area of Rivers State.

The meeting, according to the minister, was aimed at explaining the political situation ahead of the 2027 general election and seeking continued support for Tinubu’s re-election.

Recalling his political relationship with the people of Khana, Wike said they had supported him during his tenure as governor and in the 2023 elections when he mobilised support for the emergence of the incumbent governor.

He described the turnout at the meeting as evidence of their continued commitment to the relationship.

Wike emphasised the importance of political alliances, saying no individual or community could achieve its objectives without building relationships with influential political actors.

He explained that the Rainbow Coalition was formed specifically to mobilise support for Tinubu’s re-election and was not an arrangement to determine who would become governor, senator or member of the House of Representatives.

“The coalition we are doing is to support Mr President. It is to vote for Mr President. I am not doing an alliance with anybody to go back as governor somewhere,” he said.

He added that the arrangement was designed to accommodate different political interests, including members of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and the All Progressives Congress (APC).

Amaechi’s Record

The minister also criticised former Rivers State governor and former Minister of Transportation, Rotimi Amaechi, questioning his contributions to the Ogoni people despite spending 16 years in influential public positions.

Wike alleged that the major projects associated with Amaechi’s administration in the area included a proposed prison and banana plantation.

He contrasted these with the establishment of the University of Environment by the Tinubu administration and the completion of the Bori-Bonny Road.

“Within just three and a half years, see what he has given to us. But our brother was governor for eight years and minister for eight years. The only thing he promised was prison and a banana plantation,” he alleged.

Wike also questioned the execution of projects under Amaechi, alleging that $10 million was spent on a proposed statewide mosquito fumigation programme without achieving its intended results.

He further alleged that $39 million was paid to a company identified as Trinotech for a proposed 1,000-bed Caribbean White Specialist Hospital, which he claimed never progressed to the foundation stage.

He also criticised the monorail project, alleging that ₦68 billion was spent without its completion.

The minister urged residents to demand accountability from political leaders, insisting that public office holders should be judged by their achievements and the impact of their policies.

He also referenced ADC presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar’s ambitions, questioning the records of political leaders who had occupied influential positions.

Wike urged the people of Khana to mobilise support for Tinubu ahead of the 2027 elections, particularly by ensuring that previous supporters returned to vote.

Earlier, the Paramount Ruler of Bori Nortem Community, Lenu Saro Igbara, commended Wike for establishing the Rainbow Coalition, describing it as an unexpected political strategy that had attracted national attention.

The post Alliance With Tinubu Has Benefited Rivers, Must Continue Beyond 2027 — Wike appeared first on Channels Television.

Vice-President Kashim Shettima made the call on Monday in Abuja during the
content:
The Federal Government has called for drug abuse and illicit drug trafficking to be treated as a national emergency, warning that the menace poses serious threats to public health, national security and economic development.

Vice-President Kashim Shettima made the call on Monday in Abuja during the official launch of the National Drug Control Master Plan 2026–2030.

Shettima, who was represented by the Special Adviser to the President on Special Duties, Office of the Vice President,  Modibbo  Umar, said drug control must remain a national priority, stressing that the challenge extends beyond drug seizures and arrests of suspected traffickers.

He said, “That is why drug control must remain a national priority. As a matter of fact, it should be treated as a national emergency.

“The challenge before us goes beyond the consignments intercepted by our agencies or the criminal networks brought before our courts. It reaches into our homes, our schools, our workplaces, and our communities.”

Shettima noted that drug abuse affects families, workforce productivity and the future of young Nigerians, adding that the country must confront the problem with determination and compassion.

According to him, the drug problem should be understood as a public health concern, security threat, development challenge and economic issue.

He said the response must go beyond enforcement to include prevention, early intervention, treatment, rehabilitation and recovery, while security agencies must intensify intelligence-led operations to dismantle trafficking networks.

“These dimensions are bound together. We cannot rely on enforcement alone and neglect prevention. We cannot promote treatment without improving access to appropriate services.

“We cannot disrupt trafficking networks while ignoring the financial structures that sustain them. And we cannot expect lasting results when institutions work in isolation or lack the resources to discharge their responsibilities,” he said.

The VP said the new master plan builds on the experience of the 2021–2025 framework, urging relevant institutions to consolidate previous achievements, address implementation gaps and respond to emerging threats, as he stressed that the success of the plan would depend on effective implementation rather than the unveiling of the policy document.

“The worth of a national plan lies not merely in the priorities it sets, but in the change it produces—in how institutions conduct themselves, how resources are allocated, and how people’s lives are improved,” he added.

Shettima called on federal ministries, departments and agencies, state and local governments to take responsibility for implementing the plan, noting that the National Assembly, judiciary, health and education institutions also had critical roles to play.

He further identified traditional rulers, religious leaders, civil society organisations, the private sector, parents, teachers and young Nigerians as essential partners in tackling the menace.

“No single institution, however capable, can overcome this challenge alone,” he said.

He said the impact of the master plan would ultimately be measured by improved access to treatment, effective prevention, stronger institutional cooperation, disruption of criminal networks and better living conditions for Nigerians.

“Let this be the moment Nigeria moves from policy to action, from fragmented efforts to coordinated national impact, and from commitment on paper to measurable improvements in the lives of our people,” he said.

Speaking earlier, the Chairman of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, Brig-Gen. Mohamed Marwa (retd.), said the new master plan was designed to build on previous achievements while addressing identified gaps and emerging threats.

Marwa said the summative evaluation of the 2021–2025 National Drug Control Master Plan recorded 77,736 arrests, the seizure of more than 14.8 million kilogrammes of drugs and over 14,200 convictions.

He added that more than 32,400 people also benefited from treatment, counselling and rehabilitation services during the period.

According to him, the evaluation identified gaps in coordination, financing, service delivery, data management, monitoring and accountability, as well as weak institutional capacity at state and local government levels.

He said the new plan was designed “to keep what worked, fix what did not, and confront what is emerging.”

Marwa explained that the framework would better integrate drug supply and demand reduction while targeting the financial and technological systems sustaining illicit drug markets.

He said the approach would strengthen the agency’s capacity to confront sophisticated trafficking networks, synthetic drugs, new psychoactive substances and criminal syndicates exploiting encrypted communications and cryptocurrency.

Also speaking, the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, described the NDLEA as “the bedrock of our national drug response.”

He said the new master plan would consolidate the agency’s achievements into a whole-of-government framework integrating law enforcement with public health, education, social development, financial investigation and community participation.

Fagbemi commended the leadership and personnel of the agency under Marwa, assuring that the Federal Ministry of Justice would collaborate with the judiciary to facilitate the speedy determination of drug-related cases in line with the Administration of Criminal Justice Act.

He said the ministry would also ensure that convictions were accompanied by the confiscation of illicit assets and strengthen mutual legal assistance, extradition and cross-border asset recovery.

The AGF further praised the NDLEA’s practice of involving prosecutors early in investigations, noting that the approach helped preserve evidence and prevent procedural errors.

He stressed the need to distinguish between drug traffickers and people struggling with drug dependence, saying the latter required treatment rather than punishment alone.

In a goodwill message, the ECOWAS Commissioner for Human Development and Social Affairs, Prof. Nassirou Bako-Arifari, commended Nigeria for the initiative, describing the master plan as consistent with regional commitments towards a safer and healthier West Africa.

He, however, said its success would depend on sustained political will, adequate funding and cooperation among governments, civil society organisations, communities, the private sector and international partners.

content:
The Kogi State chapter of the African Democratic Congress has announced preparations for the presidential campaign rally of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar scheduled to be held in Lokoja, the state capital, on Tuesday, November 24, 2026.

The party said mobilisation had intensified across the state ahead of the rally, expressing confidence that the event would attract a large gathering of supporters.

The State Director of the Strategic Communications Directorate, Usman Okai, disclosed this in a statement on Monday issued in Lokoja.

Okai described the planned visit as a significant moment for the party in Kogi, adding that Atiku would present party flags to its National Assembly candidates across the three senatorial districts.

He said the state leadership, alongside members of the Presidential Campaign Council, had intensified efforts to ensure a successful event.

According to him, prominent party figures coordinating the preparations include the North-Central leader, Senator Dino Melaye; former Senator Tunde Ogbeha; media strategist, Kola Ologbondiyan; Director of Contact and Mobilisation, Musa Wada; and the state’s party chairman, Tom Zekeri.

On the venue, Okai confirmed that Buhari Square in Lokoja had been secured for the rally, expressing optimism that the facility would accommodate a large number of party supporters.

He said, “The political atmosphere in Kogi State is already charged, and grassroots mobilisation has reached an advanced stage ahead of the visit.

“This will be a defining moment for the ADC in Kogi State, as our presidential candidate is expected to officially present party flags to all our National Assembly candidates across the three senatorial zones.”

The party spokesman also urged security agencies deployed for the rally to maintain professionalism and ensure a peaceful atmosphere throughout the event.

He wished party members, delegates and supporters travelling from different parts of the state safe journeys to Lokoja, expressing confidence in a successful rally.

title: Gombe regulator visits 200 hospitals to improve healthcare
description:
The Gombe State Private Hospitals Registration and Regulation Authority on Monday called for stronger collaboration with private healthcare providers to improve patient safety, strengthen service delivery and promote sustainable growth in the state’s health sector.
The authority said it was shifting
content:
The Gombe State Private Hospitals Registration and Regulation Authority on Monday called for stronger collaboration with private healthcare providers to improve patient safety, strengthen service delivery and promote sustainable growth in the state’s health sector.

The authority said it was shifting from what it described as a one-sided regulatory approach towards a partnership-driven system that combines enforcement with mentorship, professional guidance and institutional support.

The Chairman of the authority and Chairman of the summit’s Local Organising Committee, Dr Peter Ubong, stated this during a one-day summit organised in collaboration with the Gombe State Ministry of Health.

The summit, themed ‘Effective Regulation for Patient Safety and Sustainable Growth in the Private Health Sector,’ brought together private healthcare providers and other stakeholders to discuss challenges confronting the sector and strategies for improving healthcare delivery.

Ubong said the summit was informed by his observations after assuming office, particularly the strained relationship between regulators and operators of private health facilities.

“When I was appointed as the Chairman, I discovered that the regulation of private facilities had been one-sided. Regulators would simply go to these facilities and start oppressing them, without necessarily understanding their challenges,” he said.

Ubong explained that the approach had created fear and apprehension among private healthcare providers whenever they encountered regulatory officials.

According to him, the authority decided to change the narrative by engaging operators, listening to their concerns and understanding the difficulties affecting their operations.

He disclosed that the authority had visited more than 200 of the 237 registered private hospitals in the state to obtain firsthand information about their operations and challenges.

“We needed to do this because we wanted to have a firsthand view and overview of the issues. We interacted with some of them and discovered that they had a lot of challenges,” he said.

He added that the summit was designed not only to educate private hospital operators on regulatory requirements but also to provide an opportunity for them to communicate their concerns and make recommendations.

“The major crux of this summit, apart from what we are going to tell them, is what they are going to tell us. What are their issues? Let them feel carried along. Let them be brought from the periphery into the mainstream.

“Let it not be a master-servant relationship. Let it be a partnership. They will help us, and we will help them,” he stated.

He said experienced medical professionals in the state could assist private practitioners in improving their clinical skills, facility standards and service delivery.

“We can mentor them, show them how to do things better, teach them and correct them. We can advise them and draw the red line where necessary. We can also link them with other facilities, experts and people who can provide the assistance they need,” Ubong said.

Also speaking, the state Commissioner for Health, Prof. Adamu Danladi, described the summit as timely, noting that it was the first of its kind aimed at bringing private healthcare operators together with government regulators to address challenges in the sector.

He said the state government had made significant investments in public healthcare infrastructure under Governor Muhammadu Yahaya, including the revitalisation of primary healthcare centres, upgrading of general hospitals and strengthening of healthcare management institutions.

Danladi disclosed that the state now had more than 300 primary healthcare facilities, while several general hospitals had been upgraded to specialist hospital standards.

He listed the facilities at Kaltungo, Bajoga and Kumo among those that had benefited from the government’s interventions, adding that the improved status of Kumo General Hospital contributed to its selection for conversion into a Federal Medical Centre.

The commissioner also cited the establishment of the Gombe State Contributory Healthcare Scheme, GO-HEALTH, as one of the initiatives strengthening access to healthcare services in the state, among others.

title: Tinubu donates ₦250m to families of Bayelsa boat accident victims
description:
President Bola Tinubu has approved ₦250 million in financial assistance for families of victims of the deadly boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.
Vice-President Kashim Shettima announced the intervention on Sunday during a condolence visit to the state, following t
content:
President Bola Tinubu has approved ₦250 million in financial assistance for families of victims of the deadly boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.

Vice-President Kashim Shettima announced the intervention on Sunday during a condolence visit to the state, following the accident which occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026.

The boat was conveying passengers from Ayama community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony when it capsized around the Oweikorogha/Otuan River Junction.

The death toll had risen to 29, while more than 51 survivors had been recorded, according to Governor Douye Diri.

Shettima, who represented the President, said Tinubu had directed relevant federal agencies to support the Bayelsa State Government in providing assistance to affected families and survivors.

He also disclosed that the President had ordered the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) to provide necessary support to those affected by the tragedy.

The Vice-President further revealed that Tinubu had directed the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy to strengthen safety measures on the country’s inland waterways.

He added that the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) had been directed to procure boats to improve transportation in riverine communities.

Tinubu also called for a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident, insisting that stronger safety standards, vessel inspections and enforcement were necessary to prevent similar tragedies.

He described the incident as a national tragedy, stressing that Nigerians who travel by water deserve the same level of protection as those using road and air transportation.

During the visit, Shettima also inspected survivors receiving treatment at the Bayelsa Medical University Teaching Hospital in Yenagoa and assured them of continued support.

Earlier, Governor Diri said preliminary findings suggested that the accident could have been avoided if established safety regulations had been followed.

He alleged that the boat was not fit for river transportation and had operated from an unauthorised loading point.

The governor disclosed that the state government had taken responsibility for the medical bills and treatment of survivors.

He also said a commission of inquiry had been established to investigate the incident and recommend measures to prevent future occurrences.

The tragedy has renewed concerns over safety standards on Nigeria’s inland waterways, particularly in riverine communities where residents depend heavily on boats for transportation.

title: APC disowns letter asking INEC to ensure Tinubu’s 2027 victory
description:
The All Progressives Congress has disowned a letter purportedly written by its National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, to the Independent National Electoral Commission, urging the electoral body to ensure President Bola Tinubu’s victory in the 2027 presidential election.
In a statement on Monday,
content:
The All Progressives Congress has disowned a letter purportedly written by its National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, to the Independent National Electoral Commission, urging the electoral body to ensure President Bola Tinubu’s victory in the 2027 presidential election.

In a statement on Monday, the APC National Chairman’s Special Adviser on Media and Information Strategy, Abimbola Tooki, described the letter, which circulated on social media, as fake, malicious and a desperate attempt to tarnish the image of its leadership and undermine democratic institutions.

A purported letter dated November 22, 2026, and addressed to INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, allegedly by APC National Chairman,, sought the electoral commission’s cooperation ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

The unsigned document claimed the APC leadership expected INEC to deploy its administrative and operational mechanisms to ensure Tinubu’s declaration as the winner of the 2027 presidential election.

Reacting, APC said the document was neither authored by Yilwatda nor issued by his office, insisting that it was inconsistent with the party’s established communication procedures.

The statement read in part, “The All Progressives Congress has condemned in the strongest possible terms a purported letter circulating on social media, allegedly written by the National Chairman of the party, Professor Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda, to the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, titled ‘Preparations for the 2027 Presidential Election and Ensuring the Victory of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.’

“The unsigned letter, dated November 22, 2026, contains an outrageous and entirely fabricated claim that the APC leadership expects INEC to deploy its institutional mechanisms, administrative frameworks and operational capacities to ensure the declaration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu as the winner of the 2027 presidential election.

“The party categorically states that the purported letter did not emanate from Professor Yilwatda, was not authored by him and has absolutely nothing to do with the National Chairman or his office. It is a fraudulent document, a malicious fabrication and a reckless attempt to impugn the integrity of the National Chairman, the APC and the democratic process.”

APC said the absence of a signature or authentication on the purported letter exposed its fraudulent nature, alleging that it was deliberately circulated to mislead the public and tarnish the image of its National Chairman.

The party also faulted the document for violating its established communication procedures, insisting that a letter of such significance could not have been issued outside its official channels.

It added, “The APC will not allow faceless individuals, political mischief-makers and purveyors of fabricated information to drag its leadership into disrepute through the circulation of fictitious documents.

“We condemn the author of this despicable letter in the strongest possible terms and challenge those responsible to come out of hiding, take ownership of their actions and provide verifiable evidence for their claims, rather than hiding behind anonymity to spread falsehoods and create distrust in democratic institutions.

“For the avoidance of doubt, the APC remains firmly committed to a peaceful, transparent, free and fair electoral process in the forthcoming 2027 general elections. Our party believes in the sanctity of the ballot, the independence of INEC and the right of Nigerians to freely choose their leaders without intimidation, manipulation or interference.

“President Bola Ahmed Tinubu himself has consistently demonstrated his commitment to democratic principles. At campaign rallies and public engagements across the country, the President has repeatedly urged Nigerians, particularly eligible voters, to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards and exercise their civic responsibility.

“This is a clear demonstration of his confidence in the democratic process and his belief that electoral legitimacy must come from the will of the people, freely expressed through the ballot.”

APC National Chairman urged Nigerians and the media to disregard the purported letter, insisting that it remained committed to democratic values, peaceful elections and respect for electoral institutions.

The party said it would approach the 2027 elections with confidence and discipline, stressing that electoral victory must be earned through the support and mandate of Nigerians.

The post APC disowns letter asking INEC to ensure Tinubu’s 2027 victory appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Trump Hails Nvidia CEO’s Return As US Lawmakers Raise Security Alarm
description: US President Donald Trump praised Nvidia’s decision Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, predicting he would emerge stronger from a scandal that sparked outrage among Democrats and skepticism from some Republicans over national security concerns.Huang, who co-founded the AI chi
content:
US President Donald Trump praised Nvidia’s decision Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, predicting he would emerge stronger from a scandal that sparked outrage among Democrats and skepticism from some Republicans over national security concerns.

Huang, who co-founded the AI chip giant, returned less than two weeks after resigning following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

“The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.

In a subsequent telephone interview with CNBC, Trump suggested the scandal could prove to be “a net positive” for Nvidia by drawing attention to the sophistication of its technology.

“I don’t think he’s going to be diminished at all,” he said, predicting Huang would return at “an almost higher level.”

“He’s apologized for his indiscretion, which was unfortunate,” Trump added.

On Truth Social, Trump called Huang “a Great Patriot” and said the US government had no reason to believe his return posed a national security risk.

He said the attorney general had confirmed that the government possessed no evidence Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct, but urged Nvidia to continue investigating its compliance with restrictions on advanced chip sales to China.

Democratic lawmakers denounced the reinstatement, arguing that questions about Huang’s relationship with the suspected Chinese intelligence operative and Nvidia’s business dealings remained unanswered.

“Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang is outrageous,” said Democratic Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi, a member of the House Intelligence Committee.

“We still don’t know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him, and neither the government nor Nvidia’s own board has completed its investigation.”

Krishnamoorthi demanded that Huang testify publicly before Congress.

Senator Elizabeth Warren called the decision “reckless” and demanded an explanation of what input senior administration officials had provided in support of the reinstatement.

Democratic Representative Debbie Dingell called Nvidia’s decision “irresponsible,” while Illinois Governor JB Pritzker, a potential 2028 presidential contender, accused the company and administration of showing “greed and lack of accountability.”

Some Republicans also questioned the move.

“Jensen Huang was compromised and exploited by a Chinese spy,” outgoing Republican congressman Don Bacon alleged on X, saying Nvidia should have ignored the administration’s calls for his reinstatement.

Bacon demanded an investigation into who had authorized sales of advanced chips to China.

Outgoing Republican Senator John Cornyn challenged Trump’s assertion that Huang posed no security threat.

“No national security risk? Based on what?” he wrote on X.

Trump declined Monday to comment on a New York Times report that the woman at the center of the scandal had been in contact with an official from China’s principal intelligence agency during her relationship with Huang.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Sunday that the administration needed more information about Nvidia’s advanced chip sales abroad.

AFP

The post Trump Hails Nvidia CEO’s Return As US Lawmakers Raise Security Alarm appeared first on Channels Television.

title: My best is yet to come – Bruno Guimaraes
description:
Arsenal midfielder Bruno Guimaraes says he is yet to reach his best despite making a successful start to life at the Premier League club.
The Brazilian stated this on Monday ahead of Arsenal’s UEFA Champions League clash against Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday.
This was contained in a release posted on
content:
Arsenal midfielder Bruno Guimaraes says he is yet to reach his best despite making a successful start to life at the Premier League club.

The Brazilian stated this on Monday ahead of Arsenal’s UEFA Champions League clash against Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday.

This was contained in a release posted on the club’s website.

Guimaraes, who joined Arsenal from Newcastle United in the summer, said he was still adapting to the demands of manager Mikel Arteta and believed he could improve his performances.

“Definitely I’m building up,” he told the media on Monday. “Of course because I scored two goals, I think some fans want me to score every game, but it’s not like this, I’m definitely adapting myself.

“I’ve been here three or four months, and there’s still a lot to go. But now I definitely understand my role in the team, the way Mikel wants me to play in the team, so I think I still can play much, much better.

“The welcome has been amazing, I think [our supporters] have been so good with me, I want to thank them for their support.”

The midfielder said Arsenal’s system required him to operate in different positions, adding that he was gradually becoming accustomed to the tactical demands.

Guimaraes declared, “It’s very different, here is a little bit more free. You play as a six, an eight, and a nine sometimes, so we have to move a lot, and of course I was not used to it.

“Now I understand a little bit more what [Mikel Arteta] wants from the midfield. I understand Declan because it’s a little hard, but yeah, I think now I’m getting there. I’m still not at the level that I want, but I feel I can play much more and help the team.”

Guimaraes also highlighted the competition for places in Arsenal’s midfield, saying it pushed players to maintain high standards.

“We push each other to always be playing well, because if you don’t play well, other players will come and play well; I think that’s very important for Arsenal. We want to make a dynasty here, we want to win everything possible,” he said.

He added that Arteta had made the ambition clear to him when he joined the club.

The Brazilian stated, “I think since I came to the club, the first thing Mikel said to me was create a dynasty for the club, so we want to win everything that’s possible.”

Ahead of the Dortmund encounter, the midfielder acknowledged the quality of the German side and the importance of the fixture.

“I know how much the Champions League means for the fans, and for us here. Tomorrow we have a big test with a top team, they have been unbelievable this season, so tomorrow we have to play a very good game because it’s going to be against a top side,” he said.

The Brazilian also praised his midfield teammates Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard, saying he was learning from both players.

He said, “They’re both amazing players. I think Declan is a monster, he can run 15 kilometres in a game, and Martin Odegaard, he always can find space to penetrate the opposite side.

“I’m learning a lot with the guys, they’re trying to help me where I have to position myself when we don’t have the ball, when we do have the ball, and like I said, it’s about adaptation.”

Guimaraes said he had been impressed by the team’s mentality and its determination to compete for victories.

“But I think so far it has been good. The mentality is unbelievable, we don’t play for a draw here, we play for a win every game, that’s the level,” he said.

“It’s what Mikel demands for us and his staff every day, so the mentality is very good. I think we are creating something big here, and I hope at the end of the season we can celebrate together,” he concluded.

title: Ghana win first Amputee Football World Cup title
description:
Ghana’s national amputee football team, the Black Challenge, have won their first-ever Amputee Football World Cup title after beating Morocco 1-0 in Sunday’s final in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico.
Ghana’s Mubarik is the top goal scorer of the WAFF tournament
Captain Richard Opentil scored the decis
content:
Ghana’s national amputee football team, the Black Challenge, have won their first-ever Amputee Football World Cup title after beating Morocco 1-0 in Sunday’s final in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico.

Captain Richard Opentil scored the decisive goal in the 32nd minute to secure the historic victory.

The Ghana Football Association disclosed this in a statement published on its website on Monday.

In its report titled, “Ghana make history as Black Challenge beat Morocco to win 2026 Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico”, the association said the team had “etched their names into football history” after being crowned champions.

It said, “In a fiercely contested encounter between two of Africa’s finest sides, the Black Challenge demonstrated remarkable determination, resilience and defensive discipline to protect their slender advantage and hold off Morocco until the final whistle.”

The association added that the encounter was a rematch of the 2024 African Amputee Cup of Nations final and the 2023 African Para Games final.

Ghana’s victory made the country the second African nation to win the competition after Angola, who lifted the trophy in 2018.

The team’s achievement was also highlighted by forward Mubarik Mohammed, who claimed the tournament’s Golden Boot after finishing as the leading scorer with seven goals.

The GFA said the Black Challenge’s journey to the championship was built on “a series of impressive performances against formidable opposition”.

Ghana began their knockout campaign with a 3-1 victory over the United States in the round of 16 before defeating Egypt 2-0 in the quarter-finals to reach the last four.

The team then faced defending champions Türkiye in the semi-finals. After the encounter ended 1-1 following extra time, Ghana won 4-3 on penalties to book their place in the final.

They carried that momentum into Sunday’s showdown against Morocco, where “Opentil’s first-half strike proved decisive in delivering the title.”

title: Raya ruled out of Arsenal’s Champions League clash with Dortmund
description:
Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya will miss Tuesday’s UEFA Champions League clash against Borussia Dortmund after sustaining an injury during Saturday’s Premier League draw with Newcastle United.
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta disclosed this in an update published on the club’s website on Monday, saying t
content:
Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya will miss Tuesday’s UEFA Champions League clash against Borussia Dortmund after sustaining an injury during Saturday’s Premier League draw with Newcastle United.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta disclosed this in an update published on the club’s website on Monday, saying the goalkeeper appeared to have avoided a serious injury.

“He’s not fit for tomorrow unfortunately,” Arteta told reporters at the Sobha Realty Training Centre. “But it doesn’t look too serious. We need some more tests tomorrow, but it’s quite encouraging.”

The manager said the extent of the pain Raya experienced immediately after the incident had initially raised concerns.

“With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action, we were all quite worried, but he seems to be better than we expected. When you look at the action, it doesn’t seem to be much on it, but the extent of the pain that he had and how he was struggling, it was quite worrying,” he said.

Arteta added that the initial tests had provided more encouraging indications, although further examinations would determine how long the Spain international would be unavailable.

“Yes, as I mentioned, we expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain that he had. The first test that we’ve done showed something that is much more encouraging,” he said.

He added, “There’s no need for surgery, which was the main fear, especially because that would rule him out for months, so let’s see. Tomorrow, we’ll have more tests, and we will know.”

With Raya unavailable for the Dortmund encounter, Arteta expressed confidence in the goalkeeping options available to him, naming Kepa and Illan Meslier.

“We know, and I think we’ve seen what David brings to the team, but as well that’s why we are very protective with Kepa and Illan,” he said.

“Everybody needs to be ready because these things unfortunately happen, and now we need to show how well we are protected and the good keepers we have with Kepa and Illan.

“We always assess every situation to make the right call, and it’s quite clear what we’re going to do,” Arteta concluded.

The post Raya ruled out of Arsenal’s Champions League clash with Dortmund appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
