title: FIFA President Infantino lists stadiums, airports, transport as obstacles to Nigeria hosting World Cup
description:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino has said Nigeria is not currently equipped to host the men’s FIFA World Cup, citing inadequate infrastructure, including stadiums, airports and transportation networks.
Infantino made the assessment on Monday during an interview with ARISE News in Abuja, where he was
content:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino has said Nigeria is not currently equipped to host the men’s FIFA World Cup, citing inadequate infrastructure, including stadiums, airports and transportation networks.

Infantino made the assessment on Monday during an interview with ARISE News in Abuja, where he was asked whether Nigeria could host a tournament of the World Cup’s magnitude.

“Today, no. But tomorrow, why not?” he replied.

The FIFA president, however, expressed optimism that Nigeria could become a host nation in the future, pointing to the country’s resources, passion for football and determination to develop the necessary facilities.

According to him, hosting the competition requires world-class infrastructure, particularly stadiums, airports and efficient transportation systems.

“The key to hosting a World Cup is obviously the infrastructure, the stadiums, the airports, transportation, and this is where best practice is needed,” Infantino said.

He added that Nigeria had the resources and commitment to pursue the projects required to meet FIFA’s hosting standards.

“I think Nigeria has the resources, has the passion, has the will as well to move ahead with the projects that are planned in terms of stadiums,” he said.

Infantino also spoke about his visits to football facilities in Abuja and Warri, describing the stadiums he inspected as impressive.

“For example, I visited a national training centre in Abuja, in Warri as well. A very nice stadium. Very nice,” he said.

His remarks followed his inspection of the ongoing FIFA Forward Technical Centre project at the Moshood Abiola National Stadium in Abuja and the renovated Warri City Stadium in Delta State.

The Abuja technical centre, being developed in partnership with the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF), received $4.88 million in funding from FIFA under its Forward 3.0 programme.

The project includes a 68-room players’ hostel, two training pitches and other facilities intended to support the development of Nigeria’s national teams.

Meanwhile, the Warri City Stadium, which has a capacity of 15,000 spectators, is undergoing extensive remodelling alongside other sporting facilities in Delta State.

Africa has hosted the men’s FIFA World Cup only once, when South Africa staged the tournament in 2010.

Morocco is expected to become the second African country to host the competition when it co-hosts the 2030 edition with Spain and Portugal. Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay are also scheduled to host one centenary celebration match each.

title: NEC approves additional N130bn for police training facilities
description:
The National Economic Council has approved an additional N130bn for the rehabilitation of police training institutions across the country, bringing the total funding for the programme to N230bn, as preparations continue for the proposed recruitment of 50,000 police personnel.
The additional allocati
content:
The National Economic Council has approved an additional N130bn for the rehabilitation of police training institutions across the country, bringing the total funding for the programme to N230bn, as preparations continue for the proposed recruitment of 50,000 police personnel.

The additional allocation is expected to accelerate the ongoing rehabilitation, upgrade training facilities and strengthen the capacity of police institutions to accommodate increased recruitment and training requirements.

The decision followed an update by the NEC Ad-Hoc Committee on the rehabilitation of police training institutions, chaired by Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah, which disclosed that work was ongoing at 13 locations nationwide, with 30 per cent of the rehabilitation completed.

The council had earlier approved N100bn for the programme following the establishment of the committee in October 2025, on the recommendation of President Bola Tinubu.

According to a statement signed by Stanley Nkwocha, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Media and Communications, Office of the Vice President, on Monday, the additional funding would “accelerate rehabilitation works, upgrade training facilities and strengthen the capacity of police institutions to accommodate increased recruitment and training requirements.”

The statement added that the intervention was expected to “support preparations for the recruitment of 50,000 police personnel and improve the country’s security training infrastructure.”

The approval was among the key decisions reached at the council’s 162nd meeting on Monday, where members also endorsed two development projects involving proposed World Bank financing of $`850m.

The projects comprise the $350m Accelerating Resilience through Investment Systems and Engagement (ARISE-Nigeria) Project and the State-Led Early Childhood Development Programme, with proposed World Bank financing of $500m.

The ARISE-Nigeria Project is a six-year programme designed to strengthen the country’s capacity to prepare for and respond to floods, droughts, fires and other natural disasters.

The statement said the programme would improve “emergency operations centres, early warning systems, weather monitoring and disaster response financing at federal and state levels.”

Between five and 10 states are expected to participate in the initial phase, with selection based on disaster risk exposure, institutional readiness and commitment to emergency preparedness.

The second project is designed to improve children’s access to healthcare, nutrition, early learning and protection services across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

The statement said the initiative would establish early childhood development hubs to “connect primary healthcare facilities with childcare, preschool education and other essential social services, particularly in underserved communities.”

The proposed $500m World Bank financing is expected to be complemented by potential additional grant support of $30m from the Global Financing Facility.

On the economy, the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, reported that Nigeria’s real Gross Domestic Product grew by 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, compared with 4.23 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025.

The statement said headline inflation declined for the fifth consecutive month to 14.06 per cent in October, its lowest level since September 2020, while external reserves stood at `$54.87bn as of November 12, 2026.

It also reported that the country’s trade surplus increased from N10.2tn in the first half of 2025 to N20.1tn in the corresponding period of 2026, while net revenue distributed through the Federation Account Allocation Committee rose by 44 per cent, from N15.2tn in 2024 to N21.9tn in 2025.

However, Oyedele noted that the improving economic indicators had yet to translate sufficiently into relief for households and businesses, particularly in food prices, electricity costs, access to affordable credit and employment.

The statement added that food inflation remained at 19.13 per cent in October, while high lending rates and energy costs continued to put pressure on businesses and household incomes.

The council also called for stronger collaboration between the National Identity Management Commission and state governments to accelerate national identity registration and the integration of the National Identification Number into public services.

On pension reforms, the council approved a proposal presented by the Director-General of the National Pension Commission, Omolola Oloworaran, titled “Securing the Retirement of Nigerian Workers While Strengthening State Finances.”

It urged state governors to adopt implementation timelines for the Contributory Pension Scheme and directed their administrative and finance teams to work with PenCom on the necessary arrangements.

Earlier, Vice President Kashim Shettima, who chairs the council, said the success of President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms depended on building institutions capable of sustaining their benefits.

“While His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, makes the difficult reforms to stabilise the economy, we must all participate in establishing institutions capable of sustaining the benefits of those reforms. This requires ministries and States to settle practical responsibilities without losing sight of the people affected. To achieve this, we must cooperate,” he said.

He added, “We must allow a sound practice in one jurisdiction to inform decisions elsewhere, while respecting the differences in capacity and circumstance across the country. The quality of our cooperation will shape the inheritance we leave.”

Speaking on the ARISE-Nigeria Project, Shettima said it was intended “to reduce the damage that disruption can do to incomes, enterprises and public services.”

He stressed the importance of protecting families and businesses from the effects of disasters, saying, “This matters especially where a family or business has little room to absorb another loss. The capacity to recover should never depend entirely on the resources a person already possesses.”

The Vice President further said, “People affected by an intervention must also have a place in shaping it. Their experience can reveal what a proposal overlooks. The strength of a project rests partly on the institutions and citizens that will carry it.”

The post NEC approves additional N130bn for police training facilities appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Yahaya unveils 30 buses as Gombe Line purchases hit 110
description:
Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Yahaya, on Monday unveiled 30 newly acquired buses for the state-owned transport company, Gombe Line, bringing the number of vehicles procured by his administration to 110 since 2019.
The governor, who inaugurated the buses at the Government House, Gombe, commended th
content:
Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Yahaya, on Monday unveiled 30 newly acquired buses for the state-owned transport company, Gombe Line, bringing the number of vehicles procured by his administration to 110 since 2019.

The governor, who inaugurated the buses at the Government House, Gombe, commended the management of the transport company for improving service delivery, strengthening its financial position and settling more than 98 per cent of inherited liabilities.

Yahaya described the acquisition as part of his administration’s commitment to revitalising public transportation, expanding access to affordable mobility and creating employment opportunities.

He praised the Director-General of Gombe Line, Sani Sabo, and his management team for their efforts in repositioning the company, particularly in addressing its inherited financial challenges and improving operational efficiency.

The governor reaffirmed his administration’s determination to sustain investments in the transport sector to ensure residents enjoy safe, affordable and reliable transportation services.

Speaking at the ceremony, Sabo said the latest acquisition reflected the governor’s continued commitment to strengthening public transportation in the state.

He recalled that the administration procured 50 Toyota buses in 2019 and another 30 in 2022, with the latest 30 bringing the total number of buses acquired under Yahaya’s administration to 110.

Reviewing his three years in office since September 2, 2023, the Director-General said he inherited an organisation burdened by huge financial liabilities, grounded vehicles and inefficient manual operations.

He said, “When I assumed office, Gombe Line was confronted with huge inherited liabilities, grounded vehicles and operational challenges. However, through deliberate reforms and the support of the state government, we have been able to settle over 98 per cent of the inherited liabilities.”

Sabo listed the introduction of an online ticketing system, the revival and maintenance of grounded vehicles, and the expansion of operational routes to Dei-Dei in Abuja, Biu and Damaturu among the achievements recorded under his leadership.

Other interventions, according to him, include the establishment of a registered courier service, the construction of an NSCDC outpost at the Mega Park, the ongoing construction of a company workshop and improvements to existing park facilities.

He added that the management had prioritised staff welfare through improved working conditions and prompt payment of salaries, while a mosque was also constructed through voluntary contributions.

On the newly commissioned buses, Sabo assured residents that the management would ensure proper maintenance and effective utilisation of the vehicles.

He said, “We will ensure that these buses are properly maintained and efficiently managed to guarantee their sustainability and maximise the benefits of the government’s investment.”

The Director-General reiterated the company’s commitment to providing safe, affordable and reliable transportation for residents of Gombe State and passengers travelling to other parts of the country.

The post Yahaya unveils 30 buses as Gombe Line purchases hit 110 appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NVIDIA board reverses decision, reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
description:
NVIDIA’s board of directors has reinstated Jensen Huang as the company’s president and Chief Executive Officer (CEO), less than two weeks after he stepped down from the positions.
The technology company announced the decision on Monday, stating that its board members unanimously approved Huang’s ret
content:
NVIDIA’s board of directors has reinstated Jensen Huang as the company’s president and Chief Executive Officer (CEO), less than two weeks after he stepped down from the positions.

The technology company announced the decision on Monday, stating that its board members unanimously approved Huang’s return with immediate effect.

“The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk,” NVIDIA said.

Harvey C. Jones, chairman of NVIDIA’s board, said the directors believe Huang is the right person to lead the company and that his return is in the best interests of shareholders, employees, partners and customers.

“We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer,” the chairman said.

Jones will retain his position as board chairman.

Huang said he was honoured to return to lead the company, describing NVIDIA as one of the most consequential technology companies in the world “at the beginning of a new industrial revolution”.

“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work,” Huang said.

‘NVIDIA SETS UP COMMITTEE TO CONTINUE PROBE INTO FOREIGN INTELLIGENCE ALLEGATIONS’

NVIDIA said the board had established a committee comprising independent directors to investigate the matter, with the support of independent legal counsel.

“The Board reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it,” NVIDIA said.

The board said it has established a national security and export control committee, made up entirely of independent directors, to oversee trade compliance and national security risks.

The committee is engaging legal counsel with expertise in national security matters, who will also retain specialist advisers.

NVIDIA said it was beginning a search for a chief compliance officer to oversee compliance across the company and report to the board’s nominating and corporate governance committee.

The company added that it would continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries.

Huang resigned as NVIDIA’s president and CEO on November 12, ending his 33-year leadership of the technology company.

His resignation followed an investigation into his relationship with a woman suspected of working for Chinese intelligence.

On November 17, Huang said he would return if the board determined that his reinstatement was in the best interests of the company, its shareholders and employees.

In a post on his X account, Huang said he had received calls from NVIDIA employees, investors, business partners and customers urging him to resume leadership.

The tech expert also acknowledged making serious mistakes in his personal life and creating problems for the board, pledging to cooperate with its independent investigation.

The post NVIDIA board reverses decision, reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Fani-Kayode raises the alarm over attacks on Nigerians in South Africa
description: Nigeria’s Ambassador to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has raised concerns over unresolved deaths of Nigerians, alleged misconduct by some South African security personnel and recurring anti-Nigerian sentiments, insisting that protecting Nigerians abroad must remain a priority of his diplomatic mis
content:
Nigeria’s Ambassador to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has raised concerns over unresolved deaths of Nigerians, alleged misconduct by some South African security personnel and recurring anti-Nigerian sentiments, insisting that protecting Nigerians abroad must remain a priority of his diplomatic mission and Foreign Ministry.

Fani-Kayode expressed the concern in a statement issued on Monday, where he called for stronger bilateral cooperation between Nigeria and South Africa, describing relations between the two countries as critical to Africa’s economic integration, political stability and development.

Meanwhile, no less than 12 Nigerians have been killed in South Africa in 2026, as a result of Anti-Migrant protests, alleged police brutality and Afrophobia attacks.

Fani-Kayode in the statement, said while the Nigerian government remained committed to strengthening diplomatic and economic relations with South Africa, it would not overlook issues affecting the safety, dignity and welfare of Nigerians living in the country.

“The future of Africa is closely tied to the relationship between Nigeria and South Africa. If these two countries fail to work together, it could have significant implications for the continent’s progress,” he said.

He noted that since assuming office, he had consistently advocated dialogue, mutual respect and stronger bilateral ties between both countries.

However, he said the cordial relationship between the two governments should not prevent Nigeria from raising concerns over the treatment of its citizens.

“As ambassador, I would be failing in my responsibility if I did not raise concerns about the treatment of Nigerians in South Africa,” he said.

Among the issues he identified were unresolved cases involving the deaths of Nigerians, reports of misconduct by some security personnel and recurring anti-Nigerian rhetoric by certain groups.

The envoy also faulted attempts to portray Nigerians living in South Africa as criminals, arguing that such generalisations unfairly undermine the contributions of thousands of law-abiding citizens.

“Thousands of Nigerians in South Africa are law-abiding professionals, including doctors, lawyers, academics and entrepreneurs. A small minority engaged in wrongdoing should not be used to define an entire community,” he said.

Fani-Kayode maintained that the anti-Nigerian sentiments expressed by some organisations should not be interpreted as representing the position of the majority of South Africans.

He nevertheless described such rhetoric as troubling, urging both countries to address tensions through sustained engagement, dialogue and mutual understanding.

The ambassador also commended Nigerian community organisations in South Africa for their contributions to protecting the interests and welfare of citizens living in the country.

He said their engagement had helped ensure that the concerns of Nigerians received greater attention and representation.

“Many Nigerians believe that their concerns are finally being heard and represented. I remain committed to speaking on their behalf and standing up for their interests,” he said.

Fani-Kayode further encouraged Nigerian investors and business owners operating in South Africa to sustain their investments and expand their enterprises, while supporting fellow Nigerians facing difficulties.

Reaffirming his commitment to defending Nigeria’s interests, he said: “Wherever Nigeria’s dignity is challenged or undermined, I will not hesitate to speak out and defend the green-white-green.”

He reiterated that strengthening Nigeria-South Africa relations, promoting economic cooperation and safeguarding the welfare of Nigerians abroad would remain central to his diplomatic mission.

The post Fani-Kayode raises the alarm over attacks on Nigerians in South Africa appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Nvidia reinstates Huang as CEO amid foreign intelligence probe
description:
US tech giant NVIDIA has reinstated Jensen Huang as its President and Chief Executive Officer, as well as a member of its board, following a unanimous decision by its board of directors.
The company announced this in a statement published on its newsroom on Monday, November 23, 2026, saying the rein
content:
US tech giant NVIDIA has reinstated Jensen Huang as its President and Chief Executive Officer, as well as a member of its board, following a unanimous decision by its board of directors.

The company announced this in a statement published on its newsroom on Monday, November 23, 2026, saying the reinstatement took effect immediately.

According to the statement, the board voted unanimously after a series of discussions and meetings with Huang, adding that it was satisfied with his candour and ability to lead the company.

It also disclosed that the board received input from senior levels of the United States government before reaching its decision and was confident that Huang’s return posed no national security risk.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” the company’s board chair, Harvey C. Jones, said.

Jones said the board had confidence in Huang and looked forward to working with him as he resumed leadership of the company.

He also thanked Colette Kress for her service as interim chief executive officer, alongside her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.

Huang, in his remarks, said he was honoured to return and lead the technology company, describing the period as the beginning of a new industrial revolution.

“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” he said, thanking the board, Jones, Kress, the company’s executive staff, employees, shareholders, industry leaders and partners for their support.

Investigation continues

Despite the reinstatement, NVIDIA said an independent committee established by the board would continue investigating reports that Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.

The committee, made up solely of independent directors, has retained independent counsel to assist with the investigation.

The company said Huang fully supported the investigation and was committed to cooperating with it.

NVIDIA also announced the formation of a National Security and Export Control Committee, comprising independent directors, to oversee trade compliance and national security risks.

The committee is engaging legal counsel experienced in national security matters, who will also retain advisers with relevant expertise.

The company further disclosed that it had begun searching for a Chief Compliance Officer to oversee compliance across NVIDIA and report to the board’s Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee.

It added that it would continue cooperating with ongoing government investigations and inquiries.

The controversy

The development follows a controversy that led to Huang’s resignation on November 12, barely days after NVIDIA’s board opened an independent investigation into reports that he had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.

PUNCH reported that the controversy involved allegations of extramarital relationships, including one with Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed International, whom US authorities reportedly suspected of having links to Chinese intelligence.

Huang admitted being unfaithful to his wife and apologised to his family and colleagues, but did not publicly confirm the specific allegations concerning Alice Huang.

The post Nvidia reinstates Huang as CEO amid foreign intelligence probe appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Ekiti court sentences 23-year-old man to death for killing toddler
description:
An Ekiti State High Court sitting in Ado Ekiti has sentenced a 23-year-old man, Kayode Ademilolu, to death by hanging for murdering a 30-month-old boy, Heritage Taiwo.
Ademilolu was convicted on Monday by Justice Adekunle Adeleye after the court found him guilty of killing the toddler on September 1
content:
An Ekiti State High Court sitting in Ado Ekiti has sentenced a 23-year-old man, Kayode Ademilolu, to death by hanging for murdering a 30-month-old boy, Heritage Taiwo.

Ademilolu was convicted on Monday by Justice Adekunle Adeleye after the court found him guilty of killing the toddler on September 14, 2025, at Odo-Emure Street, Agbado-Ekiti.

The charge stated that the defendant murdered the child, contrary to Section 234 of the Criminal Law of Ekiti State, 2021.

Testifying before the court, the deceased’s father, Abiodun Taiwo, said he was asleep when the incident occurred but woke up at about 6.30pm after hearing a crowd shouting outside his house.

“I woke up at about 6.30pm due to shouts of a crowd in front of my house. When I enquired, I was told somebody had killed my son,” he said.

He told the court that he rushed to the scene and found his son’s lifeless body, with his head smashed and blood around him.

“On getting to the scene, I saw the lifeless body of the boy. I could not recognise the dead body initially because the head had been pressed and the body was in the pool of his own blood.

“Everybody at the scene identified Kayode as the one who smashed the boy’s head with a stone,” he said.

Taiwo added that the police later took the child’s remains to the mortuary of the General Hospital, Ode-Ekiti.

The prosecutor, Dr Surajudeen Ajibola, called three witnesses and tendered the defendant’s statements to the police and photographs of the deceased as exhibits.

In his statement, Ademilolu confessed to killing the child with a stone, saying he did not know what came over him.

He said he had visited the deceased’s father at his home on the day of the incident and that the boy had asked for a biscuit.

“The late boy demanded for biscuit. We went together to buy it. I asked the boy to go in front of me, I later carried a big stone and smashed it on his head from the back. Neither the father nor the boy earlier offended me, but I did not know what came over me,” he stated.

The defendant did not call any witness in his defence.

Delivering judgment Justice Adeleye said the prosecution had established the essential elements of murder beyond reasonable doubt.

“My finding is that Taiwo Heritage is dead, and his death is instantaneous.

“The defendant also admitted that he hit the two and half years old deceased with a stone on the head. His confession is unequivocal and cogent. The admitted facts require no further proof,” the judge said.

He added that the evidence of the prosecution witnesses established the offence and found Ademilolu guilty as charged.

“I find the defendant guilty as charged, consequently, he is hereby sentenced to death by hanging,” the judge pronounced.

The post Ekiti court sentences 23-year-old man to death for killing toddler appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: FG targets 2027 to clear N3.3tn power debt
description:
The Federal Government is targeting the settlement of its outstanding N3.3tn debt to power generation companies by 2027, while promising significant improvements in electricity supply within the next three to five years.
The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, disclosed this during an exclusive intervi
content:
The Federal Government is targeting the settlement of its outstanding N3.3tn debt to power generation companies by 2027, while promising significant improvements in electricity supply within the next three to five years.

The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, disclosed this during an exclusive interview on ARISE News on Monday, where he outlined the government’s plans to address longstanding infrastructure deficiencies, outstanding obligations to power generation companies and other challenges affecting the electricity sector.

Tegbe said the government had negotiated the debt down from N6tn to N3.3tn and had already paid N1.23tn, adding that it was exploring different arrangements to settle the outstanding balance by 2027.

“Today, we have paid 1.23 trillion. We’re speaking 1.23 trillion in this economy in a speed of about one and a half years.

“And we’re on track to finish paying the rest next year. Because we are looking at different ways to settle it,” he said.

The minister explained that the government was considering offsetting some of its outstanding obligations against royalties and corporate income tax as part of efforts to meet its financial commitments to generation companies.

“We want a net of royalties against the debts we have. You can’t take money with one hand and give it with the other hand. So let’s net it off.

“Corporate income tax, we can net it off. We’re negotiating with them. They are in agreement that we can take that out as long as we go down,” he said.

He also disclosed that the government was engaging the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited to explore ways of reducing the cost of gas supplied to power generation companies.

“We’re also sitting down with NNPC to say, gas for power. And we look at how we can cut down the cost to Gencos, to the gas suppliers. Because we own this gas.

“It’s a comparative advantage. And if we want to give power to Nigerians, let’s use what we have to get what we want,” Tegbe said.

On electricity supply, the minister said Nigerians should expect massive improvements within the next three to five years, acknowledging that infrastructure deficiencies in the sector were more extensive than initially estimated.

He attributed the challenges partly to decades of neglect and poor investment priorities, arguing that successive administrations had spent money on projects without adequately considering how they connected to the wider electricity network.

“The bulk of the challenges is not in generation.

“I’ll tell you that, look, infrastructure decay is enormous. These things have happened over 50 years. Don’t expect us to fix it in two years,” he said.

Tegbe also identified poor planning and politically motivated investment decisions as factors affecting electricity delivery, saying his ministry was reviewing ongoing projects to identify priority investments.

He said the government was examining the relationship between projects and their potential contributions to improved electricity supply to ensure that available resources were spent on the right infrastructure.

The post FG targets 2027 to clear N3.3tn power debt appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Military airstrikes kill 37 terrorists, destroy four vehicles in Borno
description:
The military has killed 37 terrorists and destroyed four vehicles in six air strikes conducted across five locations in Borno State between November 16 and 23.
The operations also destroyed a terrorist staging facility, disrupted suspected improvised explosive device activities and left several othe
content:
The military has killed 37 terrorists and destroyed four vehicles in six air strikes conducted across five locations in Borno State between November 16 and 23.

The operations also destroyed a terrorist staging facility, disrupted suspected improvised explosive device activities and left several other fighters injured, according to the military.

The figures were confirmed in a statement signed by the Acting Media Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force (North East), Operation Hadin Kai, Captain Mohammed Goni, on Monday.

The statement read, “Between 16 and 23 November 2026, OPHK air assets conducted 6 precision air strikes across 5 locations, neutralising 37 terrorists confirmed by Battle Damage Assessment and destroying 4 terrorist vehicles.”

It added that the operations also “disrupted suspected IED activities and inflicted further disruption on terrorist elements, including reported injuries and flight from targeted locations.”

The military said the air strikes were conducted following credible intelligence and persistent Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance operations targeting terrorist movements, hideouts and logistics assets.

The affected locations included Monguno Local Government Area, Kerenoa and Fage in Marte LGA, and the Tumbuma Baba general area of Kukawa LGA.

According to the statement, the first operation was conducted on November 16 after intelligence reports indicated that about 40 terrorists were moving northeast of Monguno towards troops’ positions.

“Following verified intelligence sighted approximately 40 terrorists moving northeast of the Monguno to attack own troops, a pre-emptive strike was executed,” the statement said.

It added that battle damage assessment confirmed that 10 terrorists were killed, while several others sustained injuries.

In another operation on November 17, surveillance assets identified a terrorist staging area at Arina Chiki, where fighters were reportedly planning an attack on troops’ defensive positions.

The military said a precision air strike was launched against the target, adding that subsequent assessment confirmed the destruction of the building.

“Subsequent BDA confirmed the destruction of the targeted building, with no further movement observed within the structure,” it stated.

On November 20, an Intelligence, Surveillance, Target Acquisition and Reconnaissance asset spotted two terrorist vehicles parked close to a tree in Kerenoa.

The vehicles were engaged in a precision strike, with the military confirming their destruction through subsequent battle damage assessment.

In a separate operation on the same day, an air surveillance asset spotted a terrorist vehicle at an identified IED assembly location in the Fage general area.

The military said the vehicle was preparing to lay explosives along troops’ route when it was targeted.

“The vehicle was immediately engaged in a precision strike and successfully destroyed, thereby disrupting the terrorist IED-related activity in the area,” the statement said.

The latest operation was conducted on November 23 in the Tumbuma Baba general area, where surveillance assets identified and destroyed a terrorist vehicle following intelligence reports of activities in the location.

The military said two suspected terrorists were subsequently observed emerging from a nearby life-support structure and were tracked to a gathering of six other fighters taking cover under a tree.

It said additional terrorists later joined the gathering before a precision strike was launched against the group.

“BDA confirmed the neutralisation of all eight terrorists, with no further movement observed at the location,” the statement added.

Assessing the operations, the task force said the successes demonstrated “the effectiveness of intelligence-led air operations and sustained ISR in degrading terrorist capabilities and disrupting their movements and logistics across the theatre.”

Operation Hadin Kai also commended the professionalism of its air and intelligence components, reaffirming its commitment to sustained offensive operations in collaboration with ground forces.

The task force urged members of the public to continue providing “credible and timely information” to support ongoing military operations and efforts to restore lasting peace in the North-East.

The post Military airstrikes kill 37 terrorists, destroy four vehicles in Borno appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 31 bag first class as Ogun college graduates 4,944
description:
The Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology, Omu-Ajose, in Odogbolu Local Government Area of Ogun State, is set to graduate 4,944 students at its second combined convocation ceremony scheduled for Wednesday, with 31 graduates earning first-class honours.
The Provost of the Colleg
content:
The Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology, Omu-Ajose, in Odogbolu Local Government Area of Ogun State, is set to graduate 4,944 students at its second combined convocation ceremony scheduled for Wednesday, with 31 graduates earning first-class honours.

The Provost of the College, Dr Modupe Oba-Adenuga, disclosed this on Monday during a press conference held as part of activities marking the institution’s second combined convocation ceremony.

According to the Provost, the graduating students comprise 1,932 full-time Nigeria Certificate in Education graduates, 1,816 part-time NCE graduates, 967 first-degree graduates and 229 recipients of the Professional Diploma in Education.

She explained that the NCE category accounts for 3,748 graduates, while the overall figure of 4,944 includes graduates across the College’s various academic programmes.

The first-degree graduates are affiliated with Olabisi Onabanjo University, Ago-Iwoye, while the convocation will cover NCE graduates from the 2019/2020 to 2025/2026 academic sessions, PDE graduates and degree recipients from the 2021/2022 to 2024/2025 academic sessions.

Describing the ceremony as a significant milestone in the institution’s development, Oba-Adenuga said the convocation would celebrate not only the academic accomplishments of the graduating students but also the collective contributions of parents, guardians, lecturers, administrative personnel and other stakeholders.

She explained that “For NCE full-time, we have 1,932 graduands; for NCE part-time, the figure is 1,816; and for our first degree, we have 967. For PDE, that’s Professional Diploma in Education, we have 229. So, the total for NCE is 3,748, and the grand total of all graduating students is 4,944. We have 31 first-class students.

“This 2nd combined ceremony represents an important milestone in the history of our College. It is an occasion to celebrate the academic accomplishments, perseverance and determination of our graduating students, while recognising the contributions of parents, guardians, lecturers, administrative personnel and other stakeholders who have supported their educational journeys.

“Beyond the presentation of certificates and degrees, this convocation is a celebration of the College’s enduring commitment to the production of competent, knowledgeable and professionally equipped graduates who can contribute meaningfully to society.”

The Provost emphasised that the institution remained committed to producing graduates with the requisite knowledge, professional competence and practical skills to contribute to national development.

A major highlight of the convocation activities is the College’s focus on the Federal Government’s NCE-Degree Dual-Mandate Programme, which is expected to expand the academic opportunities available to Colleges of Education across the country.

The Provost also acknowledged the support of the Ogun State Government, particularly the administration of Governor Dapo Abiodun, whom she commended for interventions aimed at strengthening the institution and supporting the implementation of the NCE-Degree Dual-Mandate Programme.

She disclosed that the state government had recently provided financial intervention to the College to support the implementation of the dual-mandate initiative and staff welfare.

She further revealed that the government had increased the College’s monthly subvention in the week preceding the press conference.

As part of activities marking the convocation, the College will confer its prestigious College Fellowship Award on three distinguished Nigerians in recognition of their contributions to education, professional development, leadership and societal advancement.

The recipients are Chief Chris Olufunmilola Okunowo, an accomplished legal practitioner, businessman and community leader; Emeritus Professor Peter Okebukola, an internationally recognised scholar and authority in education; and Dr Angela Ajala, Executive Secretary of the National Commission for Colleges of Education (NCCE).

The College particularly recognises Dr Ajala’s leadership during a period that witnessed the implementation of the NCE-Degree Dual-Mandate Programme.

The institution will also honour its immediate past Provost, Dr Adeola Kiadese Lukmon, who currently serves as Special Adviser to the Ogun State Governor on Education, with an Award of Excellence in recognition of his meritorious service and contributions to the College.

She added that the convocation lecture, themed “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria”, would be delivered by Dr Tunji Olowolafe, Chancellor of Ekiti State University and Chairman of Deux Project Limited. She said the lecture was timely, given the ongoing transformation of teacher education and the changing role of Colleges of Education in Nigeria’s tertiary education system.

title: 2027: Rainbow coalition inaugurated in Cross River
description:
Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Rainbow Coalition was inaugurated in Cross River State, with its leaders vowing to reclaim the state from years of mismanagement and poor leadership.
‎
‎The inauguration held at the PDP State Secretariat on Monday in Calabar, the state capital, drew leaders o
content:
Ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Rainbow Coalition was inaugurated in Cross River State, with its leaders vowing to reclaim the state from years of mismanagement and poor leadership.
‎
‎The inauguration held at the PDP State Secretariat on Monday in Calabar, the state capital, drew leaders of the Peoples Democratic Party, coalition partners, community leaders, youth movements and supporters from across the 18 Local Government Areas of the state.

‎‎The coalition, promoted nationally by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, is a cross-party platform to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu in 2027, while allowing candidates from different parties to contest governorship, National Assembly and state assembly seats.
‎
‎Speaking at the event, the state’s PDP Chairman, Dr Frank Bullem, said the launch was built not on confidence, but on conviction to reclaim the state from poor leadership and mismanagement.
‎
‎He said, “The launch of the Rainbow Coalition seeks a partnership with our committed volunteers to reclaim our state from gross mismanagement and ineptitude in leadership.
‎
‎“We gather here not just to launch a coalition and campaign; we gather to declare that the challenges before us are too great for any single party, any single leader, or any single organisation to confront.”
‎
‎Bullem said the state was grappling with a weakened economy, decayed infrastructure in public schools and hospitals, insecurity in communities, mismanagement of collective resources, and eroded confidence in public institutions.
‎
‎He said the coalition was anchored on four pillars: unity over division, ideas over insults, service over self-interest, and mobilisation of every citizen.
‎
‎“Under this platform, we reject politics of polarisation. Our strength lies in our diversity of region, of religion, of generations, of professionals, and we will harness that strength and not fear it.
‎
‎“We will present to the public a clear, consistent and credible plan in key policy areas: jobs, education, healthcare and infrastructure”, he said.‎
‎He urged supporters to become ambassadors, organisers and champions of the cause, and to take the message to every ward, village and street.
‎
‎Also speaking, the Deputy National Chairman (South), Aaron Chukwuemeka, described the coalition’s governorship candidate for the state, Arthur-Javis Archibong, as formidable, saying he had stood with the helpless Nigerians.

‎“The candidate that I have here today is a formidable candidate. He is a terrific candidate. I believe in the truth, and the truth is that the candidate you are choosing to run for this state is a candidate you must vote for,” Chukwuemeka said.
‎
‎In his remarks, State Coordinator of the Rainbow Coalition, Jones Ojong, expressed confidence that the coalition would produce a new government with a new pathway for the state.
‎
‎“And we believe that with this coalition, we will have a new government in this state that will have a new pathway in this state. So we are 100 per cent in support of this coalition, and by the grace of God, we are going to deliver.
‎
‎“The vision for a new state is possible. For the first time, this kind of vision is coming to play. When you see parties coming together to chant this cause of change, a total turnaround,” Ojong stated.
‎
‎He thanked coalition partners for their courage and trust, and pledged a partnership built on respect, shared responsibility and mutual accountability.
‎
‎He called on market women, students, farmers, teachers, workers and entrepreneurs to take ownership of the movement, saying the 2027 election would be decided at the grassroots.

The post 2027: Rainbow coalition inaugurated in Cross River appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Gambia Decides 2026: From Dry Ports To Constitutional Reform, Candidates Pitch Competing Cases To Gambian Voters
description:
Gambiaj.com – (BANJUL, THE GAMBIA) – With the December 5 presidential election approaching, candidates are intensifying their campaigns across the country, presenting competing visions on development, governance, constitutional reform, and national leadership. 
From promises of major infrastructure
content:
Gambiaj.com – (BANJUL, THE GAMBIA) – With the December 5 presidential election approaching, candidates are intensifying their campaigns across the country, presenting competing visions on development, governance, constitutional reform, and national leadership.

From promises of major infrastructure investments to calls for institutional change and political renewal, the campaign trail is increasingly becoming a platform for candidates to make their case to voters.

Barrow Promises Basse Dry Port as He Seeks Third Term

President Adama Barrow has pledged to establish a dry port in Basse, Upper River Region, as part of plans to transform the town into a major commercial hub if re-elected for a third term.

Addressing supporters during a campaign meeting in Basse, the National People’s Party (NPP)-led alliance candidate said a contract had already been signed for the proposed facility, which he believes would attract goods from neighboring countries, including Mali, Guinea-Bissau, and Guinea-Conakry.

Barrow said the project, alongside the new port under construction in Sanyang, forms part of his government’s broader infrastructure and development agenda.

He challenged opposition candidates to explain what they would offer Gambians, arguing that his administration had already made progress in road construction, water supply, education, healthcare, and electricity.

Describing opposition candidates as his “apprentices,” Barrow urged voters to support continuity, presenting the December 5 election as a choice between maintaining ongoing development projects and reversing the progress achieved under his administration.

He also interpreted the turnout in Basse as evidence of strong support for his re-election bid, naming several constituencies in the Upper River Region that he said were ready for the polls.

Bensouda Presents Business and Municipal Experience as Leadership Credentials

Coalition 2026 candidate Talib Ahmed Bensouda is making his experience in the private sector and local government a central part of his presidential campaign, arguing that his professional background has prepared him to address the country’s economic and governance challenges.

Speaking to journalists, the former Kanifing Municipal Council mayor said his years as an employee in the private sector, entrepreneur, and local government leader had exposed him to the difficulties confronting businesses, workers, and public institutions.

He cited foreign exchange constraints, high energy costs, and market instability as challenges he had experienced firsthand in business, while his time at the municipal council had given him practical knowledge of public administration and service delivery.

During campaign meetings in Sare Sofie, Dobong, and Galleh Manda, Bensouda also criticized the government’s development record, questioning the quality of roads, healthcare, and electricity provision.

“What President Barrow cannot do in 10 years, he cannot do in 15 years,” he told supporters.

In Sare Sofie, he questioned why residents had continued to experience poor road conditions despite previous development promises, including Barrow’s pledge to transform the area into a Dubai-like community.

Bensouda argued that development should not be measured solely by infrastructure projects but also by improvements in people’s daily lives, including access to functioning healthcare facilities, qualified medical personnel, essential medicines, and reliable electricity.

He pledged to replicate and expand initiatives introduced during his tenure as KMC mayor across the country’s regions if elected president.

Darboe Calls for National Healing and Accountability

United Democratic Party (UDP) leader and Gambia First Coalition presidential candidate Ousainou Darboe has urged Gambians to use the December 5 election to address what he described as a longstanding national wound dating back to 1996.

Addressing supporters in Diabugu Batapa, Upper River Region, Darboe framed the election as an opportunity for national recovery, encouraging voters to carefully assess the sincerity, experience, and competence of those seeking the presidency.

He drew comparisons between his background and that of incumbent President Adama Barrow, arguing that effective leadership requires education, administrative experience, and the ability to honor campaign commitments.

The opposition leader attributed the country’s economic difficulties to what he described as shortcomings in the current administration’s leadership, accusing Barrow of failing to fulfill promises made over the past decade.

Darboe also raised concerns about the management of natural resources in the Upper River Region, alleging that foreign involvement in the fishing sector had contributed to declining fish stocks and reduced access for Gambian fishermen.

He further criticized previous market clearances in the Greater Banjul Area, arguing that the deployment of security personnel to remove trading stalls had negatively affected women vendors and places of worship without delivering the promised development projects.

He urged voters to prioritize compassion for vulnerable communities and accountability when choosing their next president.

Lamin J. Darboe Promises One-Term Presidency And Constitutional Limits

Team Gambia Grand Coalition presidential candidate Lamin J. Darboe has made presidential term limits a central feature of his campaign, pledging that his coalition would serve only one five-year term if elected.

Addressing supporters in Wuli Welingara Yareh, he said his administration would use its time in office to introduce legislation limiting presidents to a maximum of two five-year terms.

“We will serve only five years when we win. In those five years, we will make laws, and that law is that Gambia’s president will no more exceed ten years,” he said.

Darboe argued that prolonged presidential rule had contributed to the country’s governance challenges, criticizing what he described as a tendency among political leaders to remain in power for extended periods.

He said The Gambia had had only three presidents in 61 years, with previous leaders spending more than two decades in office.

The candidate also criticized Barrow’s decade in power, arguing that constitutional safeguards were necessary to prevent excessive concentration of political authority.

He presented the proposed reforms as part of a broader commitment to good governance, insisting that national development depends on the quality of leadership and the strength of democratic institutions.

Isatou Touray Makes New Constitution A Campaign Priority

Independent presidential candidate and former Vice President Isatou Touray has pledged to prioritize the adoption of a new constitution if elected in December.

Speaking to supporters in Jattaba and Kiang Jiffarong, Touray argued that The Gambia cannot fully enter a new democratic era without replacing the existing constitutional framework.

“We are only talking, but there is no democracy because democracy requires us to ensure that we have a constitution that guides the governance and development of a country,” she said.

The former Vice President maintained that constitutional and political reforms would be central to her administration, arguing that a strong constitutional framework is essential for democratic governance and national development.

Touray also presented her candidacy as a peaceful route to political change, urging Gambians to exercise their democratic rights through the ballot box rather than resorting to violence.

“I am coming here to seek power, to seek your votes, and to tell you that, to address the problems that we have, we have to work hard to do it in a non-violent way,” she told supporters.

She said she had consistently advocated peaceful democratic change since 2016 and called on voters to protect the country’s integrity and democratic future.

Almameh Gibba’s Campaign Gets An Unexpected Newborn Namesake

For No To Alliance Movement presidential candidate Almameh Gibba, a campaign stop in Niamina Pacharr produced an unexpected moment of public affection when a couple named their newborn baby after him.

According to Sadibou Bajakarr Badjie, the movement’s Media Director, the couple stopped Gibba’s campaign convoy to welcome the presidential aspirant and introduce their newborn, whom they had named in his honor.

Gibba was reportedly surprised and delighted by the gesture, as villagers expressed their admiration and pledged support for his presidential bid ahead of the December 5 election.

The episode offered a personal moment during the campaign tour, illustrating how political support can sometimes be expressed through gestures that extend beyond speeches and rallies.

The movement described the encounter as a demonstration of affection and solidarity, while its campaign caravan continued its tour of the country.

title: Extreme heat is rewriting the farming calendar in Gwagwalada
description:
By Oladosu Adebola Oluwaseun
In the sweltering heat of Gwagwalada Area Council, where the rising temperatures of the Federal Capital Territory are already testing daily life, a sobering prediction hangs over Nigeria: by 2027, extreme heatwaves could claim over 30,000 additional lives. Sitting down t
content:
By Oladosu Adebola Oluwaseun

In the sweltering heat of Gwagwalada Area Council, where the rising temperatures of the Federal Capital Territory are already testing daily life, a sobering prediction hangs over Nigeria: by 2027, extreme heatwaves could claim over 30,000 additional lives. Sitting down to address what this looming crisis means for local food security and rural livelihoods is Audu Hassan, the Director of Agriculture for Gwagwalada Area Council.

​With a calm, pragmatic demeanor, Hassan acknowledged that the relationship between government support and local farming has shifted.

In previous years, top-down directives often stalled before reaching the fields. Today, the responsibility falls squarely on the direct partnership between the Department of Agriculture and the farmers working the soil.
​For Hassan, survival in an era of relentless heat comes down to one non-negotiable strategy: climate-smart farming.
​”There are seeds that can produce for this heat,” Hassan explained, noting that traditional farming calendars are no longer reliable. Historically, local growers waited patiently for predictable rains before planting. Now, with erratic weather patterns and scorching heatwaves, waiting means risking total crop failure.

​Through ongoing agricultural research and field demonstrations, his department is actively introducing fast-maturing, heat-resilient crop varieties specifically highlighting improved rice options suited for the current harsh conditions. However, convincing longtime farmers to abandon familiar traditional seeds for newly developed, scientifically resilient varieties remains an uphill battle. Many are initially skeptical, clinging to what they have always planted.

​To break through that hesitation, the department isn’t just giving advice from behind desks; they are planting alongside the farmers in the fields. “When they try, they say, ‘Ah, this one is fast, oh,'” Hassan noted with a knowing smile. “Before the rain stops, we have harvested.”

​As the threat of extreme heat intensifies ahead of 2027, Hassan emphasized that sustained advocacy and institutional backing are essential. With the Area Council Chairman turning attention toward the Department of Agriculture, the mission moving forward is clear: bridge the gap between agricultural research and the grassroots farmer, replace outdated planting habits with climate-resilient seeds, and ensure Gwagwalada’s residents can harvest their crops before the heat takes its toll.

title: Troops clear suspected IPOB/ESN camp, neutralise IEDs in Imo
description:
By Kingsley Omonobi



Troops of the Nigerian Army, working alongside other security agencies, have cleared additional sections of a suspected Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) and Eastern Security Network (ESN) camp in Imo State, uncovering and neutralising improvised explosive devices (IEDs).
content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

Troops of the Nigerian Army, working alongside other security agencies, have cleared additional sections of a suspected Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) and Eastern Security Network (ESN) camp in Imo State, uncovering and neutralising improvised explosive devices (IEDs).

The operation, conducted on November 21 around Awomama in Oru East Local Government Area, was part of ongoing security offensives launched on November 16 and 17, according to the Army.

The joint operation involved troops of the 34 Artillery Brigade and personnel of the Nigerian Navy, Nigerian Air Force, Nigeria Police Force, Department of State Services (DSS) and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC).

Security sources said the joint team advanced into the Tango 2 and Tango 3 sections of the suspected camp at about 6:30 a.m., where they discovered that the locations had been heavily fortified with explosives.

With the support of Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) personnel, the troops located and successfully neutralised the improvised explosive devices.

The operation also led to the recovery of two battery components suspected to have been used to trigger the explosives.

The clearance operation is part of sustained efforts by security agencies to dismantle suspected criminal hideouts and prevent attacks in the area.

The socio-political organisation a
content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF) has mourned victims of the boat accident around Oweikorogha Community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, which reportedly claimed several lives, including youths and children.

The socio-political organisation also renewed its call on the Federal Government and governments of oil-producing states to prioritise the construction of roads and bridges to connect isolated coastal communities and reduce their dependence on water transportation.

PANDEF, in a statement signed by its National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, said it received the news of the accident, which occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, with shock and sadness.

The organisation described the incident as heartbreaking and commiserated with the affected families, the Bayelsa State Government, residents of Southern Ijaw and the affected communities.

It said the tragedy reinforced its longstanding position that inadequate road infrastructure had left many coastal communities with limited transportation options, making water travel a necessity for their residents.

According to PANDEF, the Federal Government should, as an interim measure, support state governments in acquiring adequate seaworthy vessels to meet the transportation needs of coastal communities.

The organisation also called on emergency relief agencies, security agencies and regulatory authorities to work with the Bayelsa State Government to provide assistance to survivors and bereaved families.

It urged the relevant authorities to strengthen enforcement of water transportation safety regulations, including compliance with passenger safety protocols, the use of appropriate safety equipment and the operation of vessels that meet prescribed seaworthiness standards.

PANDEF said measures must be taken to prevent a recurrence of such tragedies, stressing the need for improved transportation infrastructure and stricter safety standards across the coastal areas.

The statement read in part: “While mourning this tragic loss, PANDEF calls on the relevant emergency relief agencies, security agencies and regulatory authorities to work closely with the Bayelsa State Government to ensure that all necessary measures are taken to assuage the impact on survivors and bereaved families.

“More importantly, [they should] take all necessary measures to prevent a recurrence of such tragedies.”

The organisation expressed solidarity with the victims’ families and the people of Bayelsa State, praying for the repose of the souls of the deceased and comfort for those affected by the tragedy.

title: CAS Sets Tuesday For Verdict On Senegal AFCON Title Appeal
description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) announced that a verdict on Senegal’s appeal of the decision to strip them of the Africa Cup of Nations title in favour of Morocco will come on Tuesday.CAS’s ruling comes after a hearing of the case, over a chaotic AFCON final in January, which to
content:
The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) announced that a verdict on Senegal’s appeal of the decision to strip them of the Africa Cup of Nations title in favour of Morocco will come on Tuesday.

CAS’s ruling comes after a hearing of the case, over a chaotic AFCON final in January, which took place behind closed doors at its headquarters in Lausanne on October 8.

“The parties have been notified that the CAS decision will be rendered Tuesday 24 November 2026 in the course of the afternoon (GMT),” CAS said in a short statement on Monday.

At the January 18 final in Rabat, Senegal won 1-0 thanks to Pape Gueye’s extra-time goal, but the occasion was marred near the end of normal time when many Senegal players walked off the pitch in protest at the decision to award Morocco a penalty with the match still goalless.

Some Senegalese supporters also attempted a pitch invasion, and the game was held up for almost 20 minutes before the Senegal players returned.

In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) overturned that result, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory and the title.

In response, the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) denounced the ruling as the “most blatant administrative robbery in the history of our sport”.

The Senegal team even paraded the trophy to their supporters in Paris at the end of March.

AFP

title: Simeone sets La Liga record with 345 wins for Atletico Madrid
description:
Diego Pablo Simeone has become the manager with the most victories in La Liga history after guiding Atletico Madrid to a 3-0 win over Getafe on Sunday.
Simeone reached 345 La Liga victories in 567 matches, surpassing Atletico Madrid legend Luis Aragonés, who previously held the record.
Atletico Madr
content:
Diego Pablo Simeone has become the manager with the most victories in La Liga history after guiding Atletico Madrid to a 3-0 win over Getafe on Sunday.

Simeone reached 345 La Liga victories in 567 matches, surpassing Atletico Madrid legend Luis Aragonés, who previously held the record.

Atletico Madrid announced the milestone in a statement on Sunday, saying, “With Sunday’s victory, our manager, Diego Pablo Simeone, became the manager with the most wins in the history of the league (345), surpassing club legend Luis Aragonés.”

The club said Simeone achieved the feat after taking charge of 567 league matches, winning 60 per cent of them.

“Simeone has achieved this feat after taking charge of 567 league matches, a remarkable record in Spanish football’s top flight.

“This means he has won 60% of all the league matches he has managed,” the statement added.

The Argentine manager has also won eight trophies during his time at Atletico Madrid, including two La Liga titles, one Copa del Rey, one Spanish Super Cup, two UEFA Super Cups and two Europa League titles.

The club noted that Simeone had won two more trophies than Aragonés, who claimed six during his time at Atletico Madrid.

“Diego Pablo Simeone has won eight trophies during his time at our club (two league titles, one Copa del Rey, one Spanish Super Cup, two UEFA Super Cups and two Europa League titles), two more than the six won by Luis,” Atlético said.

It added, “With this milestone, the Argentine manager further cements his legacy in the history of LaLiga and Atlético de Madrid. You’re one of a kind, boss!”

Defensive football label rejected – Simeone

Reflecting on the milestone after the match, Simeone admitted the achievement meant a great deal: “It makes me happy. I don’t usually find many things to be happy about, but there is an incredible amount of work behind this.”

Despite evolving Atletico’s style considerably since arriving in 2011, the coach still faces familiar jibes about his tactics. Addressing the scrutiny on Spanish television channel Movistar, he added: “Then there’s the constant criticism we face. I don’t place much value on it, but I do take note of it.

“This narrative that we’re a defensive team, as if we’re always playing solely to defend. You don’t win 345 matches just by defending. Is that even possible?”

The post Simeone sets La Liga record with 345 wins for Atletico Madrid appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Aliko Dangote Emerges Recipient Of 2026 Awolowo Prize For Leadership
description: Billionaire businessman and entrepreneur Aliko Dangote has emerged as the preferred recipient of the 2026 Obafemi Awolowo Prize for Leadership, instituted in honour of one of Africa’s foremost statesmen and advocates of visionary, people-centred governance.Awolọwọ, first Premier of the Western
content:
Billionaire businessman and entrepreneur Aliko Dangote has emerged as the preferred recipient of the 2026 Obafemi Awolowo Prize for Leadership, instituted in honour of one of Africa’s foremost statesmen and advocates of visionary, people-centred governance.

Awolọwọ, first Premier of the Western Region of Nigeria, was widely acclaimed for his visionary leadership, integrity, discipline and commitment to social and economic transformation for the citizens.

His pioneering programmes in education, healthcare and rural development, together with his advocacy of federalism and economic self-reliance, remain enduring landmarks in Nigeria’s developmental history.

Established in 2012, following a special dialogue organised by the Foundation on Transformational Leadership and Good Governance: Lessons from the Awolọwọ Example, the biennial Prize seeks to recognise, reward and celebrate individuals whose leadership exemplifies the values and ideals for which Chief Awolọwọ was renowned.

A statement released by The Obafemi Awolowo Foundation on Monday, and signed by its Executive Director, Dr Ọlatokunbọ Dosumu, noted that the selection process involved public nominations, rigorous screening, verification and careful evaluation against established criteria, including integrity, vision, courage, discipline, accountability, people-centred leadership and demonstrable contributions to societal advancement.

“The process is overseen by a distinguished Selection Committee chaired by former Commonwealth Secretary-General, Chief Emeka Anyaoku, GCON, GCVO, CFR.

“Following the conclusion of the selection process, the Foundation is pleased to announce Alhaji Aliko Dangote, GCON, President of the Dangote Group, as the recipient of the 2026 Ọbafẹmi Awolọwọ Prize for Leadership.

“In arriving at its decision, the Selection Committee recognised Dangote’s extraordinary contributions to entrepreneurship, industrialisation and economic development in Nigeria and across Africa.

“Through decades of sustained investment in manufacturing, cement production, fertiliser, petroleum refining and other strategic sectors, he has demonstrated remarkable vision, courage, resilience and tenacity of 2 purpose, while helping to expand Africa’s productive capacity and advance the prospects of economic self-reliance.

“The Committee also placed considerable emphasis on his commitment to philanthropy and human development through the Aliko Dangote Foundation, established in 1994. Its interventions in education, healthcare and social welfare reflect a recognition that economic growth must be accompanied by meaningful improvements in people’s lives.

“Of particular significance is the Foundation’s ambitious educational initiative launched in 2026, designed to support 45,000 students initially, with plans to extend its reach to 1.3 million students by 2035”, the statement read in part.

The Foundation noted that the initiative places special emphasis on science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM), closing the literacy gender gap, teacher development and improving the transition from education to employment.

“Dangote’s description of this commitment as a “strategic investment” resonates strongly with Chief Awolọwọ’s conviction that education and human-capital development are fundamental to national progress.

“His declaration that “Every child we keep in school strengthens our economy. Every student we support reduces inequality” is particularly significant in this regard.

“The Committee considers Dangote’s combination of visionary enterprise, industrial transformation and commitment to human development a compelling demonstration of leadership whose impact extends beyond individual achievement to the wider society.”

The Prize will be formally presented to Dangote on Saturday, March 6, 2027, the anniversary of Chief Awolọwọ’s birth, at a ceremony which will also feature the Ọbafẹmi Awolọwọ Prize for Leadership Lecture, to be delivered by the laureate, in keeping with the tradition of the Award.

The post Aliko Dangote Emerges Recipient Of 2026 Awolowo Prize For Leadership appeared first on Channels Television.

title: 2027: Tinubu directs APC leaders to reconcile aggrieved members
description:
President Bola Tinubu has urged leaders and members of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to resolve internal disagreements, reconcile aggrieved members and strengthen political mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Tinubu gave the directive on Sunday at a special family prayer s
content:
President Bola Tinubu has urged leaders and members of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to resolve internal disagreements, reconcile aggrieved members and strengthen political mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Tinubu gave the directive on Sunday at a special family prayer session organised in his honour at the Yoruba Tennis Club in Lagos State.

At the gathering, the President specifically directed his Special Adviser on Political Matters, Ibrahim Masari, to reconcile with Katsina State Governor, Dikko Radda, and extend the reconciliation efforts to Jigawa State and other parts of the country.

He also called on residents and political supporters in Lagos to intensify voter mobilisation, describing the state’s low voter turnout in previous elections, despite its large number of registered voters, as unacceptable.

Tinubu urged APC members to put aside personal grievances and work together to secure sufficient votes for the party in 2027. He said the party needed to mobilise enough voters to defeat its political opponents.

Reflecting on the challenges surrounding the 2023 presidential election, the President attributed his emergence to divine intervention and the support of loyal party members.

He also acknowledged persistent electricity and water supply challenges in the country, promising that his administration would continue working to address the infrastructure deficit.

Meanwhile, a 94-year-old elder statesman, Lateef Okunnu, pledged to mobilise support for Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The prayer session attracted several governors, religious leaders, political figures and members of the President’s family.

title: Alice Huang had contact with China spy agency during Nvidia boss affair – Report
description:
Alice Huang, the alleged spy at the center of the Nvidia scandal, was in touch with an official from China’s top spy agency during an affair with the chip giant’s former chief executive Jensen Huang, the New York Times reported on Sunday.



Alice Huang was this month outed as a suspected Chinese sp
content:
Alice Huang, the alleged spy at the center of the Nvidia scandal, was in touch with an official from China’s top spy agency during an affair with the chip giant’s former chief executive Jensen Huang, the New York Times reported on Sunday.

Alice Huang was this month outed as a suspected Chinese spy, accused of having an affair with Jensen Huang while digging up company secrets for Beijing.

She was in contact with an officer of China’s Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the Times reported, citing people with knowledge of the intelligence.

Alice Huang, who is no relation to Jensen, previously led Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based tech group under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese firms gain access to Nvidia chips, possibly in violation of US export controls.

According to the Times, Alice Huang’s contacts with the Chinese spy agency correspond to the affair as well as a period when Megaspeed was acquiring large amounts of advanced Nvidia chips.

The Times also reported that US intelligence agencies have gathered evidence that Alice Huang’s business partner Kang Wei — who the newspaper said was often introduced as her husband — worked with the same Chinese spy agency.

Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia’s chief executive earlier this month, following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang.

He is to be questioned by US lawmakers on December 1 over national security concerns.

The upheaval has battered shares of Nvidia which is at the center of an AI boom that has helped propel markets to record highs and boosted economic growth around the globe.

description:

The NYSC Director-General, Brigadier General Olakunle Nafiu, disclosed this while ad
content:
The National Youth Service Corps and the Independent National Electoral Commission have agreed on additional insurance coverage for corps members who will serve as ad hoc personnel during the 2027 general elections.

The NYSC Director-General, Brigadier General Olakunle Nafiu, disclosed this while addressing corps members at the scheme’s orientation camp in Kogi State.

This was according to a Monday update shared by the NYSC on its official X account.

He said the “arrangement was part of the scheme’s efforts to strengthen the safety, protection and welfare of corps members deployed for electoral duties.”

Nafiu “encouraged the corps members to register for participation in the 2027 elections,” “assuring them that the NYSC was collaborating with relevant security agencies to ensure their safety throughout the electoral process.”

He also urged them to activate the “NYSC emergency response application,” noting that the platform had enhanced security agencies’ capacity to respond promptly to emergencies involving corps members and had helped save lives.

The director-general charged them to “demonstrate responsible citizenship by discharging their electoral duties in strict compliance with INEC’s rules and guidelines.”

He described participation in the conduct of free, fair and credible elections as one of the ways corps members could contribute to national development and reciprocate the nation’s investment in subsidising their tertiary education.

Nafiu also cautioned them against the “misuse of social media, urging them to verify information before sharing it and to contribute meaningfully to public discourse rather than spread misinformation and disinformation.”

The NYSC State Coordinator in Kogi, Mrs Chika Chris-Moneke, disclosed that the Asaya Orientation Camp hosted corps members deployed to Kogi State and the Federal Capital Territory for the 2026 Batch ‘C’ Stream II Orientation Exercise.

She said 2,540 corps members, comprising 1,166 males and 1,374 females, registered at the camp.

Chris-Moneke “commended the corps members for their discipline and cooperation, noting that the orientation activities had progressed smoothly.”
