title: If you register with ADC, we can offer you presidential campaign DG – Nafiu tells Atiku
description:
The Nafiu Bala-led faction of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) has insisted that former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar must formally register as a member of the party before enjoying the rights and privileges of membership.
The factional National Chairman, Nafiu Bala Gombe, made the position kno
content:
The Nafiu Bala-led faction of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) has insisted that former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar must formally register as a member of the party before enjoying the rights and privileges of membership.

The factional National Chairman, Nafiu Bala Gombe, made the position known in Kaduna State during the group’s strategic meeting with its candidates ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Bala urged Atiku to return to his ward and complete the party’s membership registration process, saying the former vice-president must comply with the ADC constitution like every other member.

He explained that formal registration would grant Atiku the full rights, benefits and privileges of party membership.

Bala also disclosed that he would consider appointing Atiku as chairman of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council for the 2027 elections if he completed the registration process.

According to him, Atiku’s political experience, national influence and understanding of governance could be valuable to the faction’s efforts to challenge the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

The factional chairman said the group remained committed to building a united party structure and coordinating its campaign activities across the country.

The meeting was attended by the faction’s presidential candidate, Professor Chris Uba, its vice-presidential candidate, Dr Shamsuddeen Modibbo Barkindo, as well as governorship and National Assembly candidates.

The development comes amid the leadership crisis within the ADC, following a Federal High Court judgment that nullified the David Mark-led party leadership and Atiku’s emergence as the faction’s presidential candidate.

The David Mark-led camp has challenged the judgment, while the dispute continues to generate uncertainty over the party’s leadership and preparations for the 2027 elections.

Bala’s latest position further highlights the disagreement between the two camps over party membership, leadership and the procedures for participating in the ADC’s activities.

title: Fury opens up on mental health struggles after 2015 Klitschko victory
description:
British heavyweight boxer Tyson Fury has disclosed that he was diagnosed with schizophrenia following his world title victory over Ukrainian boxer Wladimir Klitschko in 2015.
The 38-year-old ‘Gypsy King’ won Klitschko’s WBA, IBF and WBO heavyweight titles by unanimous decision after 12 rounds.
In a
content:
British heavyweight boxer Tyson Fury has disclosed that he was diagnosed with schizophrenia following his world title victory over Ukrainian boxer Wladimir Klitschko in 2015.

The 38-year-old ‘Gypsy King’ won Klitschko’s WBA, IBF and WBO heavyweight titles by unanimous decision after 12 rounds.

In a BBC Sport report on Monday, the British boxer made the revelation in a Netflix documentary titled Tyson Fury.’

According to Netflix, the film goes into Fury’s loss of a child, complex family relationships, and struggles with mental health and addiction. It will be streamed on November 27, which is exactly two weeks before his bout with Anthony Joshua.

Fury recalled that at the height of his mental health struggle, he visited a psychiatrist in London, after which he was diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.

“Words can’t explain the darkness I was in. It was like a living version of the pits of hell. I thought I would end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.

“The anxiety was crippling me. I just could not overcome it, and that’s when I went and saw the psychiatrist down in London.

“She asked me a gazillion questions, and I ticked all the boxes. Depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder,” Fury recalled.

He stated that he suffered from the ordeal for years, saying it was tough for him to engage in conversations.

Fury said, “It got that bad I was hearing voices in my mind. I wouldn’t be able to sit and have a conversation because I’d be hearing stuff in my mind.

“I didn’t know where to turn, and no one knew what to do. I really needed help, or to check into rehab or something.

“I never got a break from it for years. I wanted to be what I thought was normal again.”

Fury recalls hearing the radio talking to him, and begging Paris to get him out of the hospital because “the Illuminati” wanted him, the report added.

The Gypsy King also recounted that he struggled with drug and alcohol addiction.

He said further that a turning point came in 2017 when he was on a night out for Halloween.

“I went out, and I was embarrassed by how I looked.

“I was a fat mess, and I had a glow-in-the-dark skeleton suit with a full face mask on.

“I looked around and could see all the young people, and I thought, ‘I had the world in my hands, and I threw it all away, and now I’m a fat mess addicted to alcohol,'” Fury lamented.

In 2020, Fury won another world title when he beat American boxer Deontay Wilder.

Netflix said the documentary charts Fury’s rise and fall, and road to redemption.

The World Health Organisation said that people with schizophrenia often experience persistent difficulties with their cognitive or thinking skills, such as memory, attention and problem-solving.

The post Fury opens up on mental health struggles after 2015 Klitschko victory appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Tinubu urges Igboho to work with security agencies to protect South-West
description:
President Bola Tinubu has tasked Yoruba nation activist and founder of the Iru Ekun Security Network, Chief Sunday Adeyemo, popularly known as Sunday Igboho, with helping to ensure security in the South-West against threats to residents’ peace and safety.
He also stressed the need for healthy synerg
content:
President Bola Tinubu has tasked Yoruba nation activist and founder of the Iru Ekun Security Network, Chief Sunday Adeyemo, popularly known as Sunday Igboho, with helping to ensure security in the South-West against threats to residents’ peace and safety.

He also stressed the need for healthy synergy between Iru Ekun, a home-grown security initiative, and the police, Nigerian Army, Department of State Services and other relevant stakeholders to further stem the tide of insecurity in Yoruba states ahead of the January 2027 general elections.

According to a statement issued by Igboho’s media office in Ibadan, Oyo State, on Monday, Tinubu gave the charge during a brief meeting with Igboho inside his official car shortly after the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally held at the popular Mapo Hall in Ibadan on Saturday.

The statement said Tinubu held a brief session with Igboho, which focused on the activities of Iru Ekun and the critical need for its operatives to work effectively with all security agencies to improve security in rural communities and urban centres.

The statement quoted Igboho as saying, “After the Ibadan Presidential Campaign Council rally on Saturday, President Bola Tinubu called me into his car and instructed me to continue working with security agencies to ensure peace and stability of the South-West.

“I was honoured by our President on Saturday when I had a brief discussion with him inside his official car before the presidential convoy moved out of the ancient Mapo Hall premises, Ibadan, on Saturday. It vividly shows that Mr President values our selfless efforts to galvanise and improve the security and safety of our people.

“Our discussion lasted for about five minutes. Mr President directed that we must sustain our operations by securing rural communities, urban centres and our forests in Yorubaland against terrorists from neighbouring African countries.

“Mr President emphasised that Iru Ekun cooperation with all security agencies is germane to tackling criminality in Yorubaland, including our agrarian settlements and forest reserves. He said we should monitor all terrains with a view to preventing infiltration by terrorists from Lake Chad, Mali and other African countries.

“We were also instructed to provide security to all Nigerians within our jurisdictions regardless of ethnic, religious, and political divides. The president stressed that our security duties must be carried out by informing security agencies ahead such that positive results and impacts can be achieved in restoring the confidence of the people in government’s responsibility of providing security for the citizenry,” the statement concluded.

title: Kwankwaso Asked Me To Swear By Qur’an Over APC Deal With Tinubu, Abba Yusuf Alleges
description: Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, has revealed how his former political mentor, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, allegedly instructed him to swear by the Holy Qur’an over an agreement to return to the All Progressives Congress (APC) after the 2023 governorship election.The governor made the revelation
content:
Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, has revealed how his former political mentor, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, allegedly instructed him to swear by the Holy Qur’an over an agreement to return to the All Progressives Congress (APC) after the 2023 governorship election.

The governor made the revelation during an interview with BBC Hausa presenter, Aminu Kutama, while explaining the circumstances surrounding his defection from the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) to the APC in January 2026.

According to Yusuf, Kwankwaso personally sent him to meet President Bola Tinubu shortly after the 2023 governorship election, when his victory was being challenged by the APC candidate, Nasiru Yusuf Gawuna.

He alleged that Kwankwaso asked him to assure the President that they would return to the APC if Tinubu allowed the legal proceedings challenging his election victory to run without interference.

“He himself sent me to Tinubu. He begged me to go and tell him that we had made this promise, and that if necessary, I should swear with the Qur’an right there that if we won, he wanted us to come together,” Yusuf said.

The governor further claimed that Kwankwaso held several meetings with Tinubu and sent delegations to discuss the proposed political arrangement.

He added that lawmakers and local government chairmen were also involved in the discussions, insisting that Kwankwaso was aware of the negotiations.

“Everything that was done was done with the knowledge of the leader. We reached an agreement, but Kwankwaso did not fulfil it,” he stated.

Yusuf explained that the arrangement eventually collapsed after Kwankwaso allegedly made statements opposing the proposed political deal, days after he had communicated their commitment to the President.

He said the remarks were conveyed to Tinubu and affected the understanding reached between the parties.

The governor rejected suggestions that his defection to the APC amounted to a betrayal of his former political mentor, insisting that he was only fulfilling an agreement initiated by Kwankwaso.

Despite their political differences, Yusuf disclosed that communication between them had not completely ended, saying he recently sent greetings to his former leader.

The governor’s comments have reopened debate over the political relationship between Kwankwaso and Tinubu following the 2023 Kano governorship election and the subsequent breakdown of the alliance between the two Kano political figures.

Kwankwaso had previously denied reaching any agreement with Tinubu over the Supreme Court case, maintaining that the court decided the election dispute on its merits.

Yusuf’s latest account presents a different version of the political negotiations surrounding the case.

The Supreme Court upheld Yusuf’s election victory in January 2024 after overturning earlier judgments that had favoured Gawuna.

Yusuf formally defected from the NNPP to the APC on January 26, 2026, ending his longstanding political association with Kwankwaso, who played a major role in his emergence as Kano governor.

The post Kwankwaso Asked Me To Swear By Qur’an Over APC Deal With Tinubu, Abba Yusuf Alleges appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Polish tourist should have set boundaries with Daura Emir — Delta gov’s aide
description:
A media aide to Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, Ossai Ovie Success, has said Polish tourist Mirka Czee should have set boundaries during her encounter with the Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, following her allegation of sexual assault against the monarch.
Ossai expressed his position in a
content:
A media aide to Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, Ossai Ovie Success, has said Polish tourist Mirka Czee should have set boundaries during her encounter with the Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, following her allegation of sexual assault against the monarch.

Ossai expressed his position in a Facebook post on Monday, saying the tourist should not blame the traditional ruler alone, but also examine her conduct during the visit to the Daura palace in Katsina State.

“Before we blame the Emir of Daura alone, let’s be honest about what happened,” he wrote.

He questioned why Czee sat close to the Emir during their first meeting instead of taking the other end of the couch, describing it as a matter of “common sense and basic boundaries”.

The aide also faulted her for remaining in the room after the Emir allegedly held and rubbed her hand, arguing that she should have withdrawn from the interaction.

“The moment her hand was held and rubbed inappropriately, that was her cue to draw a firm line, pull back and end the meeting immediately,” he said.

Ossai, however, said he was not defending the Emir, adding that the traditional ruler should have known better.

“Nobody is excusing bad behaviour from anyone. A leader should know better and protect his dignity,” he wrote.

He added, “Leaders must respect boundaries. Visitors must set boundaries. I am disappointed.”

The comments followed a viral video recorded by Czee during her visit to the Emir’s palace, in which she accused the monarch of sexually assaulting her.

The Polish tourist, who was born in the Czech Republic, alleged that the Emir held her hand and began playing with it after asking her to sit close to him.

She further alleged that he hugged and kissed her on the cheek before touching her breasts without her consent.

In subsequent Instagram posts, Czee said she repeatedly told the Emir not to touch her and explained that her laughter during the encounter was a reaction to her discomfort.

She also said she activated the recording function on her Meta glasses after becoming uncomfortable when the Emir allegedly held her hand.

The Daura Emirate Council, through its spokesperson, Ibrahim Daura, said it was examining the footage to establish its authenticity and determine whether it had been manipulated or artificially generated.

The council said it would issue an official statement after concluding its review.

Meanwhile, Amnesty International Nigeria has called on the Katsina State Government and the police to conduct a transparent and independent investigation into the allegation.

PUNCH Online could not independently confirm the allegation, while the Emir had yet to personally respond to the claims as of the time of filing this report.

The post Polish tourist should have set boundaries with Daura Emir — Delta gov’s aide appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: FG considers electricity tariff model review, rules out hike
description:
The Federal Government is reviewing assumptions underpinning Nigeria’s electricity tariff model and considering changes to the framework, while ruling out an increase in electricity tariffs in 2027.
The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, disclosed this during an interview on ARISE News on Monday, amid
content:
The Federal Government is reviewing assumptions underpinning Nigeria’s electricity tariff model and considering changes to the framework, while ruling out an increase in electricity tariffs in 2027.

The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, disclosed this during an interview on ARISE News on Monday, amid concerns over mounting debts in the electricity sector and the government’s plans to address the financial challenges affecting power generation and distribution.

Tegbe said the government was exploring alternative measures to address the sector’s financial difficulties without placing additional financial burdens on electricity consumers.

“Let me make it categorically clear to Nigerians. And I’ll say it again. There’s no plan to increase tariff,” the minister said.

He explained that his priority was to improve electricity access, adding that the government was considering a concessionary gas pricing arrangement for power generation companies.

“I even have, to be honest with you, the most important thing for me, is how do I get electricity to Nigeria? And I’ll tell you, Mr President is saying, we own the gas. People need to give Jenko’s gas at a particular concessionary rate that is not going to make gas suppliers go out of business. Let’s look at the model,” he said.

The minister also disclosed that the government was reviewing assumptions built into the electricity tariff model, suggesting that some could be revised.

“Also, we’re looking at assumptions that have been built into the tariff model. There’s a possibility that some of those assumptions may need to be revised. But rule out tariff increase,” Tegbe said.

He maintained that the government would reconsider existing policies and arrangements in the power sector to improve electricity supply.

“I’m re-evaluating many things. And I have no boundary. The only boundary and guiding principle I have is re-evaluate everything, re-jig whatever you can re-jig, as long as you can give Nigeria electricity access.

“I will tell you, tariff increase is not on the plates. Tell Nigerians for me,” he added.

The assurance comes as the Federal Government continues to grapple with outstanding obligations to power generation companies and other financial challenges across the electricity value chain.

Recall that in September, the minister ruled out any increase in electricity tariffs, noting that the government was focused on improving electricity supply and strengthening the financial and physical foundations of the power sector rather than imposing additional costs on consumers.

The post FG considers electricity tariff model review, rules out hike appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Senegal to know fate of AFCON title appeal Tuesday – CAS
description:
The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) announced that a verdict on Senegal’s appeal of the decision to strip them of the Africa Cup of Nations title in favour of Morocco will come on Tuesday.



CAS’s ruling comes after a hearing of the case, over a chaotic AFCON final in January, which took place
content:
The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) announced that a verdict on Senegal’s appeal of the decision to strip them of the Africa Cup of Nations title in favour of Morocco will come on Tuesday.

CAS’s ruling comes after a hearing of the case, over a chaotic AFCON final in January, which took place behind closed doors at its headquarters in Lausanne on October 8.

“The parties have been notified that the CAS decision will be rendered Tuesday 24 November 2026 in the course of the afternoon (GMT),” CAS said in a short statement on Monday.

At the January 18 final in Rabat, Senegal won 1-0 thanks to Pape Gueye’s extra-time goal, but the occasion was marred near the end of normal time when many Senegal players walked off the pitch in protest at the decision to award Morocco a penalty with the match still goalless.

Some Senegalese supporters also attempted a pitch invasion, and the game was held up for almost 20 minutes before the Senegal players returned.

In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) overturned that result, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title.

In response, the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) denounced the ruling as the “most blatant administrative robbery in the history of our sport”.

The Senegal team even paraded the trophy to their supporters in Paris at the end of March.

title: Tinubu directed me to secure Yorubaland against terrorists – Igboho
description:
…says President called for collaboration with security agencies to protect rural communities, urban centres, forests



By Adeola Badru



Yoruba nation activist and founder of the Iru Ekun Security Network, Chief Sunday Adeyemo, popularly known as Sunday Igboho, has disclosed that President Bola Ti
content:
…says President called for collaboration with security agencies to protect rural communities, urban centres, forests

By Adeola Badru

Yoruba nation activist and founder of the Iru Ekun Security Network, Chief Sunday Adeyemo, popularly known as Sunday Igboho, has disclosed that President Bola Tinubu directed him to sustain security operations across Yorubaland, with particular emphasis on protecting rural communities, urban centres and forests against terrorists from neighbouring African countries.

Igboho said the president gave the directive during a brief discussion lasting about five minutes inside his official car shortly after the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally held at Mapo Hall, Ibadan, the Oyo State capital, on Saturday.

According to him, Tinubu also emphasised the need for the Iru Ekun Security Network to maintain effective collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigerian Army, the Department of State Services (DSS) and other relevant security agencies to prevent the infiltration of terrorists and other criminal elements into the South-West.

Igboho disclosed this in a statement issued by his media office on Monday, which quoted him as saying that the President’s directive was aimed at strengthening security across the region, particularly in rural settlements, urban centres and forest reserves.

He said, “After the Ibadan Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) rally on Saturday, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu called me into his car and instructed me to continue working with security agencies to ensure peace and stability in the South-West.”

“I was honoured by our President on Saturday when I had a brief discussion with him inside his official car before the presidential convoy moved out of the ancient Mapo Hall premises, Ibadan.”

“It vividly shows that Mr. President values our selfless efforts to galvanise and improve security and safety of our people.”

The Yoruba activist said the discussion, although brief, highlighted the importance the president attached to the security of the Southwest and the continued activities of the homegrown security initiative.

“Our discussion lasted for about five minutes. Mr President directed that we must sustain our operations by securing rural communities, urban centres and our forests in Yorubaland against terrorists from neighbouring African countries,” he said.

Igboho added that Tinubu specifically stressed the importance of cooperation between the Iru Ekun Security Network and established security agencies in tackling criminal activities across the region.

He said the president also directed the operatives to pay particular attention to agrarian communities and forest reserves, which could be vulnerable to infiltration by terrorists and other criminal groups.

“Mr President emphasised that Iru Ekun cooperation with all security agencies is germane to tackle criminalities in Yorubaland, including our agrarian settlements and forest reserves.”

“He said we should monitor all terrains with a view to preventing infiltration by terrorists from Lake Chad, Mali and other African countries,” he stated.

Igboho further disclosed that the President instructed the security network to provide protection for all Nigerians within its areas of operation, irrespective of their ethnic, religious or political affiliations.

According to him, Tinubu also stressed the need for the network to notify the relevant security agencies before carrying out its operations in order to ensure effective coordination and achieve the desired results.

“We were also instructed to provide security to all Nigerians within our jurisdictions, regardless of ethnic, religion and political divides.

“He stressed that our security duties must be carried out by informing security agencies ahead such that positive results and impacts can be achieved in restoring the confidence of the people in government’s responsibility of providing security for the citizenry,” the statement quoted Igboho as saying.”

Igboho said the brief encounter with Tinubu demonstrated the president’s recognition of the efforts of local security initiatives in supporting the protection of lives and property, while stressing that such efforts must remain coordinated with established security agencies.

He added that the directive was not limited to any particular community or group but covered all Nigerians within the operational areas of the Iru Ekun Security Network, regardless of their ethnic, religious or political differences.

Igboho reiterated the importance of collaboration between the network and conventional security agencies, particularly in securing vulnerable communities and preventing the infiltration of terrorists from neighbouring African countries.

He added that the security network would continue to work towards restoring public confidence in the government’s responsibility to protect citizens and maintain peace across Yorubaland.

The post Tinubu directed me to secure Yorubaland against terrorists – Igboho appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Fire Destroys Over 100 Shops At Kano Fish Market, Traders Count Losses
description: A fire outbreak at Kano Fish Market along Zaria Road has destroyed more than 100 shops, leaving traders counting losses estimated to run into billions of naira.The fire reportedly broke out at about 9:00 p.m. on Sunday, near Kano Line Motor Park, spreading across sections of the market and destroyin
content:
A fire outbreak at Kano Fish Market along Zaria Road has destroyed more than 100 shops, leaving traders counting losses estimated to run into billions of naira.

The fire reportedly broke out at about 9:00 p.m. on Sunday, near Kano Line Motor Park, spreading across sections of the market and destroying shops, containers and goods.

Reports indicate that approximately 150 shops and 200 containers were affected by the inferno, with some traders reportedly losing goods valued at millions of naira.

One of the affected traders, Usman Sani, recounted how the fire spread through the market, destroying shops and goods before traders could salvage their belongings.

“We received the news of the fire and rushed to the market, but by the time we got here, the flames had already spread. Many shops were affected, and traders lost goods worth millions of naira. The situation is heartbreaking,” he said.

Another trader, Musa Inuwa, described the incident as a major setback for those who depend on the market for their livelihood.

“Many of us depend entirely on this business to feed our families. We have lost our goods and capital, and we do not know where to start from. We are appealing to the government to come to our assistance,” he said.

The affected traders are appealing to the Kano State Government and relevant authorities for urgent intervention to support those who lost their businesses.

The Kano State Fire Service reportedly received a distress call at about 9:58 p.m. and deployed personnel to the scene, arriving four minutes later.

Meanwhile, the cause of the fire remains unknown, as investigations continue.

title: UK Digging New Reservoirs To Fight Persistent Droughts
description: Britain has long had a reputation for rain. But as it adapts to a warmer, drier climate, the UK is racing to complete a huge new reservoir, its first in over three decades.Bulldozers have been digging up the ground for the vast £800-million ($1 billion) Havant Thicket project near the southern
content:
Britain has long had a reputation for rain. But as it adapts to a warmer, drier climate, the UK is racing to complete a huge new reservoir, its first in over three decades.

Bulldozers have been digging up the ground for the vast £800-million ($1 billion) Havant Thicket project near the southern coastal port of Portsmouth.

Like much of Europe, Britain endured record-breaking heat this summer and, despite the return of rains as the country moves into winter, parts are still grappling with drought conditions.

“We’ve got increasing problems with our water security in the UK,” climate scientist Hannah Cloke from Reading University told AFP.

“We need to really think about how we’re storing that water because this problem is only going to get worse.”

Scientists have warned extreme weather events are likely to become more frequent and more intense as the global climate changes.

By mid-November, almost all of England remained in drought, with some areas classified as suffering severe drought, according to the Environment Agency.

Potentially exacerbating matters, existing reservoirs were only 60 percent full, 19 percentage points below the seasonal average.

For policymakers, the situation poses a longer-term challenge as the thirst for water increases with a rising population and the growth of heavy water-using industries such as data centres.

Under England’s National Framework for Water Resources published in 2025, the country could face a daily water supply shortfall of five billion litres (1.3 billion gallons) by 2055, with resources under pressure.

At the sprawling Havant Thicket site, Portsmouth Water chief executive Bob Taylor said the industry was waking up to the scale of the challenge after successive droughts and hot summers.

The issue, he stressed, was not necessarily how much rain falls over the course of a year, but when it falls. Winters are becoming wetter, while summers are increasingly dry.

“Without reservoirs you can’t store that intense rainfall and put it somewhere where it can be used at another time,” Taylor said.

The new reservoir will eventually hold up to 8.7 billion litres of water, helping secure supplies for hundreds of thousands of people.

Fed in part by winter surpluses from a major spring already tapped by Portsmouth Water, it has become one of the flagship projects in a broader shift in Britain’s water strategy.

The government has approved the construction of nine major reservoirs by 2050, and last year relaxed planning rules to speed up projects after decades of under-investment in water infrastructure.

Together, the future reservoirs could deliver an additional 670 million litres of water per day.

‘Not a silver bullet’

Havant Thicket Reservoir, the only reservoir currently under construction, will be the first to enter service in England since 1992. According to Taylor, it is expected to become operational by 2032 or 2033.

Combined with a planned wastewater recycling plant being developed by Southern Water which still needs approval, it is expected to supply up to 111 million litres a day.

The recycling facility has, however, sparked strong local opposition.

Residents and elected officials argue the reservoir should be supplied exclusively by spring water, reflecting broader public mistrust of the water industry following a series of scandals involving illegal sewage discharges.

Taylor insists the project will deliver major environmental benefits by reducing Southern Water’s reliance on southern England’s iconic chalk streams – fragile ecosystems that have been damaged by over-extraction.

“The reservoirs that we’re thinking about building here in the UK won’t be online for decades,” said Cloke. Construction, therefore, she warned, is “not a silver bullet”.

She argued for a broader approach that combines rainwater harvesting and recycling with lower consumption and modernisation of creaking networks.

“The UK is not keeping up. I think with many other countries in Europe people do think about how they look after water better,” she said.

The Environment Agency agrees that there is a gap to be closed. It estimated that around 60 percent of the future water shortfall must be bridged through lower consumption, reduced leakage and more efficient use of supplies.

Beyond reservoirs, the remainder would have to come from inter-regional water transfers, recycling schemes and desalination projects, several of which are already under development.

The post UK Digging New Reservoirs To Fight Persistent Droughts appeared first on Channels Television.

title: 2027: Tinubu’s admission on power, water supply shows administration’s failure – Kenneth Okonkwo
description:
A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Kenneth Okonkwo, has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his admission that electricity and water supply remain unreliable at the Presidential Villa.
Okonkwo described the development as evidence of the failure of the Tinubu administration, ques
content:
A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Kenneth Okonkwo, has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his admission that electricity and water supply remain unreliable at the Presidential Villa.

Okonkwo described the development as evidence of the failure of the Tinubu administration, questioning how the government could address the country’s infrastructure challenges when basic amenities were reportedly lacking at the seat of power.

He made the remarks in a statement posted on his X page on Monday.

According to him, the absence of steady electricity supply undermines industrialisation, while access to water is essential for human survival.

“The confession of President Tinubu that there is no steady water and electricity supply even at the Villa almost after four years of his election is the greatest testimony of the failure of his administration,” he wrote.

Okonkwo added, “Without electricity, there is no industrialisation. Without water, there is no life. If Tinubu could not give himself light and life, are you expecting him to give you what he doesn’t have?”

He further declared that anyone voting for Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general election would be voting for darkness and death.

“Anyone voting for APC and Tinubu in 2027 is voting for darkness and death,” he stated.

Okonkwo urged Nigerians to support former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar in the 2027 presidential election, describing him as an alternative for improved electricity and water supply.

“An opportunity to rescue Nigeria has come. Vote HE Atiku Abubakar for light and life, electricity and water for all Nigerians,” he added.

title: My life changed after I stopped following politicians around – Deji Adeyanju
description:
Human rights lawyer, Deji Adeyanju has again enjoined youths, especially those serving as political praise-singers, errand boys and social media attack dogs for politicians, to invest in education, skills and personal enterprise instead of depending on handouts from office holders.
Adeyanju gave the
content:
Human rights lawyer, Deji Adeyanju has again enjoined youths, especially those serving as political praise-singers, errand boys and social media attack dogs for politicians, to invest in education, skills and personal enterprise instead of depending on handouts from office holders.

Adeyanju gave the fresh charge in a Facebook post on Monday.

Citing a personal example, the lawyer said the decision he took 11 years ago to take his life seriously and stop hanging around politicians laid the foundation for the academic and professional turnaround he now enjoys.

He said, “PhD in Law in view! Looking back at my decision to start afresh and take my life seriously, I’m deeply grateful to God. You can achieve anything—just take the first step. People only take you seriously when you take yourself seriously. I beg everyone following useless Nigerian politicians around: after this upcoming election, abandon that life and take your future seriously. I made that choice 11 years ago, and my life has never been the same.”

The Abuja-based lawyer has often taken to his page to discourage young Nigerians from depending on politicians for survival, emphasising the value of education and skills for personal upliftment.

Adeyanju, who previously served as Head of New Media for the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), left partisan politics to pursue full-time activism in 2017.

He later returned to school, bagging a Bachelor of Laws with First Class Honours from Baze University, Abuja in 2022, and was called to the Nigerian Bar shortly after. He went on to obtain an LL.M from the same university and is now pursuing a PhD in Law.

He has said in previous interviews that multiple arrests and trumped-up charges during his years of activism motivated him to study law, so he could defend himself and others.

Since his call to Bar, Adeyanju has co-founded the Abuja-based law firm, Deji Adeyanju & Partners, and has become one of the most visible human rights lawyers in the country, representing protesters, journalists and detained activists, including during the #EndBadGovernance protests in August 2024.

title: Alleged Sexual Assault: Daura Emirate Probes Viral Video As Tourist Accuses Emir of Inappropriate Conduct
description: Tension has gripped Daura in Katsina State following the emergence of a viral video in which a foreign female tourist accused the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Dr. Faruk Umar Faruk, of inappropriate sexual conduct during a visit to his palace.The allegations, which have generated widespread reactions on soc
content:
Tension has gripped Daura in Katsina State following the emergence of a viral video in which a foreign female tourist accused the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Dr. Faruk Umar Faruk, of inappropriate sexual conduct during a visit to his palace.

The allegations, which have generated widespread reactions on social media, are currently under review by the Daura Emirate Council, which says it is investigating the authenticity of the video and the claims made by the tourist.

The woman, identified as Mirka and known on Instagram by the handle @beduinqa, posted the video after completing a 30-day tour of different parts of Nigeria.

In a statement accompanying the footage, she alleged that the incident occurred on Saturday, November 14, 2026, when she visited the Emir’s palace in Daura.

According to her account, she was ushered into a large room where she met privately with the Emir.

She alleged that during their conversation, the Emir held her hand and began playing with it despite her objections.

Mirka claimed she repeatedly asked him to stop, writing: “I told him, ‘Your Highness, no, no, no. You should not be touching me like that.’ But he just laughed.”

She further alleged that as the meeting ended, the Emir hugged her, kissed her on the cheeks and touched her breast without her consent.

The tourist said the encounter left her shocked, disgusted and emotionally distressed, adding that it was the only alleged incident of sexual harassment she experienced throughout her month-long tour of Nigeria.

She also claimed she was able to capture the encounter using a pair of Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses equipped with a built-in camera, and alleged that she may not have been the first woman to experience such conduct but might have been the first to record it.

Reacting to the development, the spokesman of the Daura Emirate Council, Ibrahim Usman Murtala, confirmed in a telephone interview with our correspondent on Monday that the Emirate was aware of the viral video.

He said the Emirate had commenced a review of the footage to determine its authenticity and ascertain whether it had been altered or manipulated using any form of technology.

According to him, the Emirate will issue an official statement after concluding its internal review of the matter.

As of the time of filing this report, neither the Emir of Daura nor the Daura Emirate Council had issued a substantive response to the specific allegations made by the tourist.

Meanwhile, residents of Daura described the development as disturbing, saying allegations of such magnitude should be thoroughly investigated to establish the facts while safeguarding the integrity of Nigeria’s traditional institutions and ensuring justice for all parties involved.

The allegations remain unproven, and no authority has announced any formal findings. The Daura Emirate has stated that it is reviewing the matter before issuing its official position.

The post Alleged Sexual Assault: Daura Emirate Probes Viral Video As Tourist Accuses Emir of Inappropriate Conduct appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Kebbi commissioner petitions DSS over alleged kidnap plot
description:
The Kebbi State Commissioner for Information and Culture, Yakubu Ahmed-BK, has petitioned the Department of State Services over alleged attempts by unidentified persons to abduct him and members of his family in Birnin Kebbi, the state capital.
In a petition dated November 15, 2026, and addressed to
content:
The Kebbi State Commissioner for Information and Culture, Yakubu Ahmed-BK, has petitioned the Department of State Services over alleged attempts by unidentified persons to abduct him and members of his family in Birnin Kebbi, the state capital.

In a petition dated November 15, 2026, and addressed to the Director-General of the DSS through the Deputy Director-General, Operations, Ahmed-BK alleged that the suspects were operating a white, fully tinted Hilux or Innoson van with a red Agege registration number.

The copy of the petition, which was made available to our correspondent on Monday, said the first incident occurred on Tuesday, November 10, while he was taking his usual early-morning walk with his wife along the Sani Abacha Bypass in Birnin Kebbi.

According to him, the occupants of the vehicle slowed down when they approached the couple and attempted to open one of its doors close to them.

He said he also noticed what appeared to be the nozzle of a rifle inside the vehicle, although he could not see its occupants clearly because of the tinted windows.

“Immediately we connected with the Sani Abacha Bypass, we noticed a white vehicle, either a Hilux or the Innoson type of van, fully tinted with a red Agege plate number, driving against traffic.

“It slowed down when it reached us, and attempts were made to open one of the doors on our side. It looked to me that, although I couldn’t see inside, I saw something like a nozzle of a rifle,” he stated.

Ahmed-BK said the vehicle drove past them but later turned back and began approaching them slowly, prompting him and his wife to seek refuge inside Amina Rabo Plaza along the bypass.

He explained that after hiding for about five minutes, he cautiously checked outside and discovered that the vehicle was still parked nearby with its headlights on and engine running.

The commissioner said he subsequently contacted a security officer attached to the Kebbi State Government House, identified as Alhaji Chika, who regularly encountered him during his morning exercise.

He said the officer immediately drove to the scene after receiving his distress call, adding that the suspicious vehicle sped away upon his arrival.

The commissioner, however, said he initially considered the incident an isolated occurrence until Sunday, November 15, when the same vehicle was reportedly sighted around his second residence in the Oando area of the state capital.

He said residents who spotted the vehicle around 6:30 am and 7 am alerted a fellow commissioner, who also lives in the neighbourhood.

According to him, the vehicle reportedly remained close to his residence for about five minutes before driving away.

“Since the first incident of November 10, I have passed word about the matter to some neighbours and friends in the neighbourhood. I must also state that since the first incident, I stopped going out for the trekking exercise altogether,” he said.

Ahmed-BK expressed concern that the suspects might have been monitoring his movements and could have changed their approach after he stopped his regular morning walks.

He urged the DSS to investigate the incidents and deploy plain-clothes security personnel around his Bayan Oando residence to protect him and members of his family.

The commissioner also requested surveillance operations to identify and track down the occupants of the vehicle.

He further appealed for permission, if legally permissible, to carry arms temporarily for personal protection until after the general elections.

“I suggest that the road from ZBCC junction near Azbir Hotel up to Bayan Kara junction, all on Sani Abacha Bypass, be put under surveillance, especially between the hours of 6 am and 7 am when they seem to be active,” he added.

The commissioner urged the DSS to respond promptly to his petition, expressing concern over the safety of his family.

The petition did not indicate whether the commissioner had received a response from the DSS as of the time of filing this report.

title: CAF adopts Kiswahili as fifth official language
description:
The Confederation of African Football has adopted Kiswahili as its fifth official language, joining English, French, Arabic and Portuguese in the governing body’s official languages.
Our correspondent learned this on Monday from a statement published on the football body’s website. CAF described the
content:
The Confederation of African Football has adopted Kiswahili as its fifth official language, joining English, French, Arabic and Portuguese in the governing body’s official languages.

Our correspondent learned this on Monday from a statement published on the football body’s website. CAF described the adoption as a historic decision, saying it reflected the body’s commitment to embracing Africa’s linguistic and cultural diversity.

The decision was among the resolutions reached at CAF’s 48th Ordinary General Assembly held in Abuja, Nigeria, on Saturday, November 21, 2026.

It said, “Kiswahili joins French, English, Arabic and Portuguese as an official language recognised under the CAF Statutes.

“This decision reflects CAF’s commitment to embracing Africa’s linguistic and cultural diversity and strengthening the representation of African languages in football administration across the continent.”

The assembly brought together representatives of CAF’s 54 member associations, members of its Executive Committee, vice-presidents, sponsors, partners, international football stakeholders and African football legends.

The meeting also reaffirmed the unanimous support of the 54 member associations and CAF Executive Committee for FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s re-election.

Infantino, who has led FIFA since February 2016, is seeking another term at the 77th FIFA Congress, scheduled for March 18, 2027, in Rabat, Morocco.

CAF President Patrice Motsepe also thanked President Bola Tinubu, the Nigerian government, the Nigeria Football Federation and the people of Nigeria for their hospitality and continued support for African football.

The 48th Ordinary General Assembly was held in Abuja as part of CAF’s engagements with its member associations and stakeholders across the continent.

Its adoption makes it the first indigenous African language to be recognised among the continental body’s official languages.

Kiswahili, a Bantu language that originated along the East African coast, is widely spoken across East, Central and parts of Southern Africa, particularly in Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Rwanda and Burundi. It serves as a common language among communities with different mother tongues and has more than 200 million speakers worldwide, according to UNESCO.

Kiswahili is one of several indigenous African languages with a significant cross-border presence, alongside Hausa and Fulfulde (Fula) in West and Central Africa, and Yoruba, which is spoken in Nigeria, Benin, and Togo.

title: Pete Edochie commends son Yul’s restraint amid marital controversy
description:
Veteran Nollywood actor Pete Edochie has praised his son, Yul Edochie, for refraining from public outburst towards his wife, May, amid controversy surrounding his second marriage.



Edochie gave the commendation  when he featured  on Unfiltered with Ugo and Precious, an online interview series feat
content:
Veteran Nollywood actor Pete Edochie has praised his son, Yul Edochie, for refraining from public outburst towards his wife, May, amid controversy surrounding his second marriage.

Edochie gave the commendation when he featured on Unfiltered with Ugo and Precious, an online interview series featuring candid conversations on relationships, public opinion, lifestyle and personal experiences.

Describing Yul as strong-willed, the veteran actor said his son had remained undeterred despite insults directed at him over his marital decisions.

“Yul is a very tough guy. You can never subdue him, no matter how much you try.

“He took a second wife; people have been insulting him, saying all sorts of things, and he has been living his life,” he said.

Explaining why he held his son in high regard, Pete said Yul had never publicly insulted May or accused her of wrongdoing.

“He has never insulted his wife for one day. Go and check everything that has been happening.

“He has never come out to say this woman is this or that. It shows somebody responsible,” he said.

Edochie also said May had equally refrained from making negative public comments about Yul.

“The wife too, on her own part, has not said anything against him,” he added.

He further alleged that award organisers had repeatedly excluded Yul from industry recognitions but said his son had continued to thrive.

“Each time awards are organised, they don’t include him. He hasn’t bothered. He’s doing very well. I can tell you that he’s my son.

“Yul has the best voice in the industry,” he said.

The embattled actor publicly introduced actress Judy Austin as his second wife in April 2022, while announcing the birth of their son.

The development has continued to attract public criticism on social media platforms, especially from supporters of May, with whom he has four children. (NAN)

title: World Cup: Nigeria not ready to host event – Infantino
description:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino has said Nigeria is not currently prepared to host the FIFA World Cup, citing inadequate infrastructure, including stadiums, hotels, airports and transportation networks.
Infantino made this known in an interview with Arise News aired on Monday, while responding to a
content:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino has said Nigeria is not currently prepared to host the FIFA World Cup, citing inadequate infrastructure, including stadiums, hotels, airports and transportation networks.

Infantino made this known in an interview with Arise News aired on Monday, while responding to a question on what Nigeria would need to do to host football’s biggest tournament.

He, however, expressed optimism that the country could host the competition in the future, noting that Nigeria had the resources, passion and determination required.

“The key for hosting a World Cup is the infrastructure: the stadiums, hotels, airports, and transportation. This is where the investment is really necessary.

“A country like Nigeria has the resources, the passion, and the will as well,” he said.

Asked directly whether Nigeria was ready to host the tournament, Infantino replied: “Today, no, but tomorrow, why not?”

Nigeria last hosted a FIFA tournament in 2009, when it staged the FIFA U-17 World Cup. Switzerland defeated the country’s Golden Eaglets 1-0 in the final played in Abuja.

Speaking on his 10-year tenure as FIFA president, Infantino said the organisation’s growth and expansion of its competitions reflected the achievements recorded under his leadership.

He cited the expansion of the men’s and women’s World Cups, the increase in the number of participating teams and improved competitive balance among the competitions.

“I think the facts really speak quite loudly here. Speak for themselves. The organisation of the World Cups, both for men and women, increasing the number of teams, increasing the competitive balance of these competitions, and the revenue.

“Of course, we moved from a bit more than 5 billion before I arrived to 16 billion in this last cycle,” he said.

Infantino added that the growth of football and FIFA required hard work and strict adherence to established standards.

“Football is growing. FIFA is growing. This is not possible if you don’t work hard, but also if you don’t work in compliance with the highest possible standard,” he said.

The FIFA president was in Nigeria over the weekend. On Friday, he inspected the remodelled Warri City Stadium alongside FIFA Secretary-General Mattias Grafström.

During the visit, he praised Nigeria’s football heritage and its contribution to the global game, noting that some of the world’s finest players came from the country, particularly Delta State.

“This stadium is fantastic. It has everything you can dream of. I just would love to wear some shorts and kick the ball. So as soon as it’s completely finished, we’d come and play games with all these great Nigerian legends who come from this region.

“Not just in Nigeria, but some of the best players in the world come from Nigeria, come from Delta State,” he said.

At the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football in Abuja on Saturday, Infantino also praised President Bola Tinubu for investments in sports facilities, saying they demonstrated the country’s commitment to its young population.

“He is doing, together with all of you, fantastic job here in Nigeria, showing that you are a country projected into the future,” he said.

He added: “The investments done in sports facilities, infrastructure, show that you believe in your youth, in the young girls and the young boys of Nigeria.”

Infantino is seeking re-election as FIFA president in 2027. France’s Philippe Diallo and Japan’s Kozo Tashima have emerged as potential challengers, while Nigeria has endorsed his bid for another term.

title: NDC begins Kano campaign, promises LG autonomy
description:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress on Sunday officially kicked off its 2027 general election campaign in Kano, promising to grant full autonomy to local governments across the state if voted into power.
The campaign, launched in Gezawa Local Government Area on Sunday, drew a large crowd of supporters,
content:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress on Sunday officially kicked off its 2027 general election campaign in Kano, promising to grant full autonomy to local governments across the state if voted into power.

The campaign, launched in Gezawa Local Government Area on Sunday, drew a large crowd of supporters, party leaders and stakeholders from across Kano State, setting the tone for what the party described as a new era of grassroots governance and accountability.

Speaking at the event, the governorship candidate of the party, Aminu Abdussalam Gwarzo, said local governments had been crippled for too long by excessive control from state governments, blaming the situation for poor service delivery, abandoned projects and a lack of development at the grassroots.

He said that under an NDC government, local government funds would go directly to the councils, elected chairmen would be allowed to function independently, and rural communities would witness development in roads, health, education and water supply.

Gwarzo alleged that despite the N12bn monthly allocation meant for the local governments and collected by the state government during the last three years of Governor Yusuf’s administration, there had been no commensurate development in the area.

“There are many uncompleted projects here, including that of a health institution promised to be completed by the governor. People are still battling with health services, potable drinking water, and the backwardness of our education system.

“If elected as the next governor of Kano State in 2027, I promise all our 44 local governments will be autonomous by collecting their monthly allocation from the federation account, so that all our LGAs will be financially stable,” he said.

Gwarzo condemned what he described as Tinubu’s harsh policies, which he said had brought about the financial hardship being experienced by Nigerians and the current wave of insecurity, especially in the North-West. He urged Nigerians to reject the APC in the upcoming elections.

He called on Nigerians, especially the electorate, to vote for the Obi/Kwankwaso ticket, which he described as the only alternative to the hardship and insecurity he attributed to APC maladministration.

title: Drone Strikes Hit Homes, UN Building In Sudan’s Capital
description: Drones struck Sudan’s capital, Khartoum, ripping through homes and damaging a United Nations building on Sunday, witnesses and the world organisation said.Explosions rang out in the area around Khartoum airport and other parts of the city from around 2:00 am (0000 GMT) until approximately 4:30
content:
Drones struck Sudan’s capital, Khartoum, ripping through homes and damaging a United Nations building on Sunday, witnesses and the world organisation said.

Explosions rang out in the area around Khartoum airport and other parts of the city from around 2:00 am (0000 GMT) until approximately 4:30 am.

A drone strike destroyed a house, a witness said, while a Sudanese army source said the drones had been launched from Ethiopia.

“The drone attack at dawn today is a continuation of Ethiopian aggression against Sudanese territory, as the drones were launched from Ethiopia’s Bahir Dar airport,” the source told AFP.

Sudan’s military has repeatedly accused Ethiopia of aiding the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), against which it has been fighting since April 2023, including through drone attacks launched from Ethiopian territory.

Ethiopia denies the accusations.

AFP footage showed a house reduced to rubble, with a security perimeter around the site. Pieces of furniture, household items and clothing were scattered among the debris.

Al-Nour Adam, who lives in the area, told AFP that upon entering the house after the strike, “we found a person lying on a bed, wounded in his left arm, chest and head”.

‘Where Are We Supposed To Go?’

“The strikes are indiscriminate,” Adam said.

“A strike could hit while you are asleep. You might wake up to find your children gone… It is truly tragic. You cannot be certain of anything.”

Yasser Hassan, another resident, said that the occupants of the house “had only just moved in, after searching for shelter for a long time”.

“Then the drone struck them. Where are we supposed to go?”

Another witness reported that a drone hit the home of a mosque’s muezzin, the person who calls Muslims to prayer, in Jebel Aulia, around 45 kilometres (28 miles) south of Khartoum.

“People were trying to rescue family members trapped under the rubble,” the witness said.

The United Nations, meanwhile, said that “a UN premises with UN colleagues in the building was damaged”.

“This occurred in a civilian neighbourhood,” the UN’s humanitarian office (OCHA) said in a statement posted on X.

OCHA condemned the risk posed to humanitarian workers, saying it was “unacceptable” that UN personnel were being exposed to such danger.

Saudi Arabia, which has provided support to the Sudanese regular army in the country’s war, said on X that it “categorically rejects these brutal attacks”.

Egypt, which also backs Sudan’s military, said in a foreign ministry statement it “strongly condemns” the attacks.

Drone Warfare

Authorities did not immediately report on casualties.

The conflict between the RSF and the Sudanese army has killed more than 200,000 people, aid workers estimate, and triggered the world’s largest hunger and displacement crises.

The United Nations has repeatedly criticised both sides’ rampant use of drones, which killed more than 1,100 people in the first half of 2026.

Of the hundreds of child casualties this year, two-thirds were killed or injured by drone strikes, the UN said.

A Sudanese army drone strike killed 15 people, including four children, in a West Kordofan village days ago, as the army pushed through the state, recapturing territory from the RSF.

The rival forces have, for the last year, wrestled for control of the resource-rich southern Kordofan region, which connects the army-held centre and east to RSF-controlled Darfur.

In recent months, both the army and the RSF have increasingly relied on drones capable of striking targets hundreds of kilometres away without risking their fighters.

AFP

title: Ukraine Claims Strikes On Two Russian Boats Off Libya
description: President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday said Ukraine was behind strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya, adding that one of them sank in the latest spillover from Moscow’s war with Kyiv.The attacks on Sunday near the Libyan port of Benghazi come at a time when Ukraine has stepped up its strike
content:
President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday said Ukraine was behind strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya, adding that one of them sank in the latest spillover from Moscow’s war with Kyiv.

The attacks on Sunday near the Libyan port of Benghazi come at a time when Ukraine has stepped up its strikes against Russia far from the frontlines.

But the United Nations condemned the strikes, warning against the prospect of a country still divided after the Libyan civil war becoming “a battleground for foreign conflicts”.

“It all took place off the coast of Libya. Our warriors deployed seven Ukrainian-made naval drones. Despite all the enemy’s efforts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk,” Zelensky wrote on X.

The Ukrainian leader claimed the Merkury was “one of their newest ships, commissioned in 2023, during the full-scale war”.

“Our second target was the Russian dry cargo vessel MV ANGARA, which the enemy used to transport weapons. Result: target hit,” he added.

A Ka-27 combat helicopter was also destroyed in the strike on the Merkury, Zelensky said.

Sunday’s strikes came after a drone hit a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea on Saturday, close to the waters of Finland, whose border guard said the strike was Ukrainian.

The UN mission in Libya expressed “serious concern” over the attacks, calling for “an immediate, independent and transparent investigation”.

“Libya cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts,” the UNSMIL wrote on X.

title: I thought I would lose my leg after shooting – Broda Shaggi
description:
Popular comedian and skit maker, Samuel Perry, popularly known as Broda Shaggi, has revealed that he feared losing the use of his leg after he was hit by a stray bullet in March 2026.
The entertainer also credited the Senior Pastor of Harvesters International Christian Centre, Bolaji Idowu, with hel
content:
Popular comedian and skit maker, Samuel Perry, popularly known as Broda Shaggi, has revealed that he feared losing the use of his leg after he was hit by a stray bullet in March 2026.

The entertainer also credited the Senior Pastor of Harvesters International Christian Centre, Bolaji Idowu, with helping him secure further medical treatment in Dubai after months of delays in Nigeria.

Shaggi recounted his ordeal on Sunday during a thanksgiving service at the church, where he expressed gratitude to the pastor for intervening when his recovery was uncertain.

He said he initially resisted travelling abroad for another surgery, despite being unable to walk for months after the shooting.

According to him, Idowu insisted that he seek treatment outside Nigeria and helped connect his team with a specialist, Dr Lushola.

Shaggi’s manager, Olufemi Oguntamu, popularly known as Penza, who also spoke at the service, said the comedian spent about a month in hospital before he was discharged and asked to return for weekly check-ups.

He said they initially expected another surgery to take place within two or three weeks, but the process was delayed for about four months.

The delay prompted discussions about seeking treatment abroad, although Shaggi was initially unwilling to travel.

Oguntamu said Idowu eventually intervened and insisted that the comedian needed further medical attention outside the country.

He explained that they considered treatment options in Dubai and the United Kingdom before settling for Dubai, with the pastor helping to connect them with the specialist and arrange support.

He added that Idowu remained involved throughout the process, regularly calling to check on them and praying for Shaggi’s recovery.

“At a point, Pastor Balaji would call me in the midnight. And I’d be like, ‘Ah, shit, this man no get wife?’ Every time, like, he would call me and pray for me. And he’d be like, ‘Samuel, don’t worry. You’ll be fine,’” Oguntamu said.

He also disclosed that the pastor travelled from London to Dubai to support Shaggi during the surgery.

Oguntamu recalled that Idowu had promised to mobilise church members to support the comedian wherever he eventually underwent the procedure.

“He was even saying that, ‘Oh, Shaggy, what’s the problem? Is it people that are going to take care of you?’ Because for those that don’t know, he’s a very private person.

“So, he didn’t want a lot of people into, you know, his matter. But Pastor Balaji would say, ‘Don’t worry. Anywhere you want the surgery, I’m going to ensure that I get members there that will support you and all of that,’” he said.

Responding to the testimony, Idowu disclosed that doctors in Dubai told them Shaggi’s injured leg was already shrinking when he eventually arrived for treatment.

“When they eventually got to Dubai, the doctor said if they had come late, the leg they shot was already shrinking. I’m telling you. And that’s the glory of God,” the pastor said.

Shaggi, who repeatedly thanked Idowu for his intervention, said he had feared he might never regain the use of his leg after the shooting.

Recounting the incident, he said it happened on March 19, 2026, while he and his team were returning from a brand activation assignment.

He said they were caught in traffic when a crowd gathered around his vehicle, cheering and calling his name. Suddenly, he heard a loud bang.

Shaggi said he initially thought policemen in the area were shooting but later realised he had been hit when he touched his hip and noticed blood.

“There was traffic, the policemen were in front, my team were at the back, my car was in the middle, then these area boys just gathered. They were all happy and shouting, ‘Shaggy!’ like they always do. And all of a sudden, all I heard was a loud bang.

“I thought maybe the policemen were shooting outside or something was happening outside. So I looked to the right. I saw people moving, I saw people talking, but I couldn’t hear a thing. It was just total silence. Then, when I touched my hip, I started seeing blood,” he said.

The comedian said the incident made him afraid of dying, despite previously believing he was prepared for death.

“Like, I don’t know, I’ve always said, when death comes, I’m ready. Like, I’m ready. But we got to that point, and the next thing I was just saying is, ‘Jesus, I don’t want to die. Jesus, I don’t want to die. Jesus, I don’t want to die,’” he added.

He said he was first taken to a hospital where the required treatment could not be provided before being transferred to another facility in Ikeja, where he received first aid and was stabilised.

Shaggi said the injury also raised fears about the future of his entertainment career, particularly because dancing and physical performances were important parts of his work.

He disclosed that he initially expected to spend only a few days in hospital and instructed his manager not to inform his mother about the incident.

However, as his hospitalisation continued, he eventually called her and told her he was receiving treatment. He said he did not initially disclose that he had been shot because he feared she would become distressed.

“I just had to call her. I didn’t even tell her I was shot. I just said I was in the hospital so that she wouldn’t shout wherever she was,” he said.

He described seeing his mother at the hospital as an emotional experience, saying it was the first time she had seen him in such a condition.

“She came, she saw me, she felt really bad. I felt so bad, too, because it was the first time she would see me in that position. It was the first time I would see myself in that position. I’m not going to lie, I thought I was going to lose it,” he added.

The comedian said he could not walk for months and depended on crutches and assistance from others for basic activities, including bathing.

“After four months, I couldn’t walk. It was just me on my crutches and this leg up like this. I was in the hospital. They bathed me. There was this very small girl. She would bathe me,” he said.

He added that he had prepared himself for the possibility of using crutches permanently but was grateful that his recovery took a different turn.

“For my fans, for those who follow me, for those who watch my videos, I love you too. I already made up my mind that whatever happens, I’m going to use that crutch as brother. But thank God, it didn’t go that way,” he said.

The comedian had earlier narrated his experience in a YouTube video, saying the injury kept him away from work for months and left him uncertain about his future in the entertainment industry.

He also spoke about his fear that audiences might forget him while he was unable to create content and perform.

In that account, Shaggi said he underwent an initial surgery in Nigeria before travelling to Dubai for further treatment and physiotherapy.

He said his condition improved after the procedure in Dubai, disclosing that he was able to stand with support on the second day and walk with crutches on the third day.

At Sunday’s thanksgiving service, Shaggi also led the congregation in praise songs, accompanied by the church choir, as he celebrated his recovery and thanked those who supported him through the difficult period.

title: Daura emirate probes viral video as tourist insists on assault claim
description:
The Daura Emirate Council in Katsina State has commenced a review of a viral video in which a Polish tourist, Mirka Czee, accused the Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, of sexually assaulting her during a visit to his palace.
The council, through its spokesperson, Ibrahim Daura, said it was examining
content:
The Daura Emirate Council in Katsina State has commenced a review of a viral video in which a Polish tourist, Mirka Czee, accused the Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, of sexually assaulting her during a visit to his palace.

The council, through its spokesperson, Ibrahim Daura, said it was examining the footage to establish its authenticity and determine whether it had been manipulated or artificially generated.

The development comes as Czee, who uses the Instagram handle @beduinqa, has reiterated her allegation in a series of posts, explaining why she decided to make the incident public and describing its emotional effect on her.

The Polish citizen, who was born in the Czech Republic, said she had travelled across several parts of Nigeria, including Oron, Calabar, Ibadan, Benin City, Lagos, Abeokuta, Osogbo, Ilorin, Abuja, Jos, Bauchi, Dutse, Kano, Zaria, Katsina and Daura.

She said she travelled by public transport and interacted with residents as part of her effort to experience Nigeria’s culture and diversity, adding that she had mostly encountered kind, helpful and hospitable people.

Czee said she had also met other traditional rulers in Nigeria and described those encounters as respectful.

Recounting her visit to the Daura palace, she said she was introduced to the Emir, who instructed his dignitaries to take her for a meal and show her around the palace and its surroundings.

She said she learnt about Daura’s history, including its place in Hausa history, stories about female rulers and the account of a prince from Baghdad who killed a snake at a well. She also visited different rooms and the palace stables, where she rode a horse.

According to her, she was later taken back to the Emir but was surprised when she was left alone with him in a large room.

She alleged that he asked her to sit close to him on a couch, held her hand and began playing with it, making her uncomfortable.

Czee said she lowered the Meta glasses on her head and activated their recording function while trying to maintain their conversation.

She wrote, “I felt we sat too close, I felt uncomfortable that he grabbed my hand & started to play with it, so | lowered sunglasses (meta glasses) that were on top of my head down & clicked to turn them up.”

She alleged that the Emir later hugged and kissed her on the cheek as they stood up, before touching her breasts without her consent.

The tourist said she was shocked by the alleged action and repeatedly told him not to touch her.

“I just couldn’t believe he did it, l reacted with lots of “no no no no Emir” & he repeated after me “no no no” with laughter. I said “you cannot be touching”,” she wrote.

She added that her laughter during the encounter was a reflection of her discomfort.

“I believe my “giggling” was sign of how uncomfortable I felt,” she said.

Explaining why she decided to publish the recording, Czee said she believed the Emir was too comfortable with the alleged behaviour and that other women might have experienced unwanted touching without having the opportunity or means to speak about it.

She wrote, “But when this bad experience happened to me at the Palace of Emir of Daura, I felt I needed to share it. Because it happened to me. Because I had a chance & a tool to record it, & because I believe it happens to so many other women who don’t have a chance to speak up.”

She said she initially expected the video to be seen by only a few thousand people but was surprised by how widely it circulated.

Czee also stressed that her concern was that the alleged incident happened inside the palace of a traditional ruler, rather than in a public space.

“What’s important for me, & I already wrote it in short description when uploading the video: I wasn’t grabbed by boobs on streets of Nigeria, even in crowded places, but in a palace of traditional leader who should be showing exemplary ways of behaviour. And he did not. I was a guest in his country, in his region, in his city, in his palace. And I was assaulted,” she wrote.

The tourist also addressed reports about the video’s availability on Instagram, saying she believed it had been removed after many users reported it.

She, however, said she did not request its removal but had asked the platform for a human review of the decision.

“It seems that because too many people were clicking on “report” button the Instagram algorithm has removed the video. I didn’t. I clicked for human revision of that decision, but I don’t know how much time it takes,” she wrote.

She added that several copies of the recording were already circulating online.

Czee said the incident had affected her emotionally and that she needed space to recover and move on from her experience in Nigeria.

“I’m writing this with tears coming down, & I really feel that for the healing & for getting in better mental space, I need to start thinking about other things & places to leave Nigeria & what happened there behind,” she wrote.

She said about 90 per cent of the comments and messages she received were supportive but maintained that she needed time away from the discussion.

The tourist added that she still enjoyed her visit to Nigeria and wished Nigerians well.

According to Guardian Nigeria, the Sarkin Labaran Daura, Ibrahim Murtala Daura, confirmed on Sunday that the Emirate Council was aware of the video circulating on social media. He added that the Emirate Council would issue an official statement after concluding its review of the matter.

“We are examining the video to ascertain its authenticity and establish that it has not been created or altered using technology,” he said.
Alfijir Radio also stated in its report in Hausa on Sunday that the council was examining the footage to establish its authenticity and determine whether it had been manipulated or artificially generated.

PUNCH Online also contacted the Daura Emirate Council through an official telephone number listed on its social media page.

However, a man who answered the call identified himself as a page handler and said he was unaware of the allegation.

“I am the one handling the page. I do not know anything about it,” he said before ending the call.

The response came after an unnamed source in the Emir’s palace had earlier denied the allegation, saying there was nothing of the sort during the tourist’s visit.

“There was nothing like that. She visited the palace, but how she got that information cooked up still amused us in the palace,” the source told PUNCH Online by telephone on Sunday.

The source, who spoke on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to speak to the press, said an official statement would be released.

When contacted, the Katsina State Commissioner for Information, Culture and Tourism, Dr Bala Zango, said he had not seen the video and would watch it before responding.

Meanwhile, Amnesty International Nigeria has called on the Katsina State Government and the police to conduct a transparent and independent investigation into the allegation.

The human rights organisation described the allegation as deeply disturbing and urged the authorities to ensure accountability.

As of the time of filing this report, the Emirate Council had not released a detailed statement on the allegation, while the Emir had not personally responded to the claims.

PUNCH Online could not independently confirm the allegation.
