title: ‘No turning back on Lagos-Calabar coastal highway’ –  Umahi insists
description:
Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, has reaffirmed President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to completing the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, insisting that nothing will prevent the project from being delivered.
Umahi made the declaration during an inspection of bridge construction works
content:
Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, has reaffirmed President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to completing the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, insisting that nothing will prevent the project from being delivered.

Umahi made the declaration during an inspection of bridge construction works along Sections 1 and 2 of the coastal highway.

The minister reiterated the Federal Government’s determination to ensure the completion of the major road project, which is expected to connect Lagos with Calabar across several coastal states.

The development was disclosed in a statement issued in Abuja on Monday by Francis Nwaze, Senior Special Assistant to the Minister of Works.

He quoted the minister as saying, “Nothing will happen to the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, which passes through the nine coastal states. The President has directed that the project must be completed as envisaged.”

Umahi described the highway as a profitable national investment capable of generating revenue, attracting private investors and unlocking tourism and industrial opportunities.

“We are using concrete, and so we are entitled to carbon credits claim. We are also using solar instead of conventional electricity; we are entitled to carbon credits,” he said.

He added that the superhighway would accommodate tourism facilities, factories, CCTV surveillance and other commercial infrastructure, with private investors already showing interest in recovering costs through investment arrangements.

The minister disclosed that President Tinubu is expected to commission Section 1 this month or early December.

He also clarified that the reconstruction of the East-West Road is an additional commitment by the President and does not replace or affect the Coastal Highway.

He described the ongoing 1,068-kilometre Sokoto-Badagry Road as another major infrastructure undertaking of the administration, stressing that Tinubu is pursuing multiple major projects simultaneously.

Umahi commended the President for the scale of infrastructure development and economic reforms, citing declining inflation, improved foreign exchange access for businesses and the absence of ASUU strikes.

He urged Nigerians, particularly South-East residents in Lagos, to support the President, noting that the administration has delivered significant infrastructure projects to the region.

Meanwhile, Umahi has ordered a three-week nationwide emergency rehabilitation of major federal highways ahead of the festive season and the January 2027 elections.

He directed Zonal Directors, Controllers, Resident Engineers and contractors to return to the field immediately to ensure critical roads are made motorable across all six geopolitical zones.

“I feel so sad that a contractor will be on site doing permanent work, yet some sections of the roads remain impassable. This practice must stop,” he said.

He warned that contractors must not allow motorists to suffer on failed sections while permanent construction continues, directing that damaged portions be excavated and rehabilitated using appropriate materials and asphalt where necessary.

Umahi directed officials to document the exercise, engage contractors, report challenges promptly and restore roads to acceptable motorable conditions within three weeks.

The Minister said the intervention is aimed at easing movement during the festive season, facilitating transportation of goods and services, supporting movement of election materials and strengthening security operations ahead of the 2027 elections.

title: Osanipin, FRSC boss to headline 19th NAJA auto awards
description:
By Moses Akaigwe
The Director-General of the National Automotive Design and Development Council (NADDC), Chief Joseph Oluwemimo Osanipin, and the Corps Marshal of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Shehu Mohammed, have confirmed their attendance at the 19th Nigeria Auto Journalists Association (N
content:
By Moses Akaigwe

The Director-General of the National Automotive Design and Development Council (NADDC), Chief Joseph Oluwemimo Osanipin, and the Corps Marshal of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Shehu Mohammed, have confirmed their attendance at the 19th Nigeria Auto Journalists Association (NAJA) International Auto Awards, scheduled for Thursday, December 3, 2026, in Lagos.

The two prominent government officials are expected to join leading automobile manufacturers, distributors, policymakers, industry captains and other stakeholders at the prestigious ceremony, which will hold at the Civic Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos.

Osanipin’s confirmation is particularly significant, given NADDC’s strategic role in driving the Federal Government’s automotive industrialisation agenda, including local vehicle assembly, technology development, capacity building and the transition towards cleaner mobility.

Under his leadership, the Council has continued to engage industry stakeholders on initiatives aimed at strengthening Nigeria’s automotive value chain, promoting local manufacturing and encouraging investments in alternative-energy vehicles.

Similarly, the presence of the FRSC Corps Marshal as a Special Guest underscores the importance of road safety in the development of Nigeria’s automotive and transportation sectors.

The FRSC remains a critical stakeholder in vehicle regulation, road safety enforcement, driver education and the promotion of safer motoring practices across the country.

Chairman of the 2026 NAJA Awards Planning Committee, Frank Kintum, said the committee was encouraged by the confirmation of the two senior government officials, noting that their participation would further enhance the significance of the annual industry gathering.

He said preparations were in top gear to deliver a memorable ceremony that would recognise outstanding achievements, innovation and professionalism across Nigeria’s automotive industry.

The NAJA International Auto Awards, now in its 19th edition, has evolved into a major platform for celebrating excellence among automobile manufacturers, vehicle assemblers, distributors, after-sales service providers and other players in the automotive value chain.

Chairman of NAJA, Theodore Opara, said the awards remained committed to recognising organisations and individuals making measurable contributions to the growth and transformation of the Nigerian automotive industry.

The 2026 edition is expected to attract major players across the sector, with awards covering vehicle manufacturing and assembly, automotive distribution, alternative-energy mobility, after-sales services, commercial vehicles and individual industry contributions.

A major attraction at this year’s ceremony is expected to be the Car of the Year category, which is likely to generate keen competition among established automotive brands and emerging manufacturers.

Other categories include Bus of the Year, Pickup of the Year, SUV of the Year, among others.

title: Nigerian Sinotrucks, Sterling Bank partner to expand vehicle ownership, advance mobility solutions
description:
By Moses Akaigwe
Nigerian Sinotrucks Limited has entered into a strategic partnership with Sterling Bank Limited to widen access to vehicle ownership and advance integrated mobility and financial solutions in Nigeria, in a collaboration both organisations say will create new opportunities for indivi
content:
By Moses Akaigwe

Nigerian Sinotrucks Limited has entered into a strategic partnership with Sterling Bank Limited to widen access to vehicle ownership and advance integrated mobility and financial solutions in Nigeria, in a collaboration both organisations say will create new opportunities for individuals, entrepreneurs and businesses.

Collaboration seeks to bridge vehicle acquisition financing gaps, strengthen commercial mobility and unlock new opportunities for businesses and individuals.

The agreement, formalised through the signing of a Memorandum of Agreement (MoA), underscores a shared ambition to address one of the major constraints in the mobility market: access to appropriate financing for vehicle acquisition.

Anchored on the theme, “From Partnership to Progress: Advancing Integrated Mobility and Financial Solutions”, the collaboration brings together Nigerian Sinotrucks Limited’s commercial vehicle expertise and market presence with Sterling Bank’s financial capabilities to create a more accessible vehicle ownership proposition.

For Nigerian Sinotrucks Limited, the partnership represents another significant step in its broader ambition to deepen its footprint in Nigeria’s automotive and transportation ecosystem, while making its vehicle solutions more accessible to a wider customer base.

Speaking on the significance of the agreement, the Managing Director of Nigerian Sinotrucks Limited, Alfred Okugbeni, said the collaboration was driven by the company’s determination to go beyond vehicle supply and provide solutions that respond to the broader needs of customers.

“At Nigerian Sinotrucks, we understand that access to reliable vehicles is only one part of the mobility equation. Access to appropriate financing is equally important. Our partnership with Sterling Bank is a deliberate effort to bridge that gap and create greater opportunities for individuals and businesses to acquire the vehicles they need to grow.

“We believe that when mobility and finance work together, the benefits extend beyond vehicle ownership. They translate into stronger businesses, improved logistics, greater productivity and wider economic opportunities,” he said.

For Sterling Bank, the agreement reinforces its commitment to using strategic partnerships to deliver financial solutions that address real economic needs, with transportation and mobility forming an important part of that agenda.

Speaking at the signing, Akporee Idenedo, Divisional Head, Commercial Banking at Sterling Bank, said the partnership reflects the Bank’s conviction that financial institutions and mobility providers have to work together to unlock growth.

“Transportation is the backbone of commerce. Every truck on the road is a supply chain moving, a business expanding, jobs being created and sustained. Yet for many entrepreneurs and businesses, the cost of acquiring the right vehicle remains a major barrier. Through this partnership with Nigerian Sinotrucks, we are bringing financing directly to the point of need, so customers can access quality vehicles on terms that are practical and fit their realities.

“At Sterling Bank, we believe the most meaningful financial solutions are the ones that solve real problems. This collaboration lets us support individuals and businesses who want to own their vehicles, while helping to build a more efficient and productive transportation ecosystem for the country,” he said.

The agreement also builds on Nigerian Sinotrucks Limited’s broader customer-support proposition, which extends beyond vehicle sales to include after-sales services, maintenance, genuine spare parts and technical training for drivers and mechanics.

These capabilities are particularly important in commercial transportation, where vehicle reliability, maintenance support and operational efficiency have direct implications for business performance. 

The company, which is wholly Nigerian-owned and was incorporated in 2012, is a Federal Government-recognised vehicle manufacturer and assembler, as well as an authorised distributor of Sinotruk products in Nigeria. It received Federal Government recognition as a vehicle assembler in January 2015. 

Its portfolio spans heavy-duty commercial vehicles, including HOWO tractor heads, dump trucks, tippers, cargo trucks, tankers and other specialised vehicles. The company has also expanded its alternative-energy offerings, with CNG and LNG-powered trucks, alongside its recent introduction of Sitrak electric commercial trucks into the Nigerian market. 

This evolving product offering reflects the company’s determination to respond to changing demands in the transportation industry, particularly as businesses seek more efficient, cost-effective and sustainable ways to move goods and manage logistics operations.

The partnership with Sterling Bank is expected to complement this ambition by bringing financing more directly into the vehicle acquisition process, helping to address the capital constraints that can prevent individuals and businesses from investing in the vehicles they need.

Industry observers have increasingly pointed to the need for stronger collaboration between vehicle distributors, financial institutions and other mobility stakeholders to address the high cost of vehicle acquisition and improve access to transportation assets.

Against this backdrop, the Nigerian Sinotrucks-Sterling Bank partnership represents a practical approach to connecting vehicle solutions with financial accessibility, with the potential to support businesses across logistics, manufacturing, distribution, construction and other sectors dependent on transportation.

The signing ceremony was marked by the exchange of duly executed copies of the agreement, followed by a handshake between representatives of both organisations and a brief celebratory moment, symbolising the formal commencement of the collaboration.

More than a ceremonial milestone, the occasion represented a shared commitment to building a stronger mobility ecosystem in which financial access and reliable vehicle solutions work together to unlock progress.

For Nigerian Sinotrucks Limited, the partnership reinforces its position as a mobility solutions provider with ambitions that extend beyond the supply of commercial vehicles to supporting the wider transportation and automotive value chain.

As the collaboration takes shape, both organisations will be looking to translate the agreement into tangible customer benefits, expanded access to vehicle ownership and greater opportunities for businesses to move, grow and compete.

From partnership to progress, the message is clear: when mobility meets finance, progress moves forward.

According to the Managing Director, Nigerian Sinotrucks Limited, Alfred Okugbeni, ‘Nigerian Sinotrucks is not simply putting more vehicles on Nigerian roads; it is helping create the financial and mobility partnerships that make progress possible.’’

The post Nigerian Sinotrucks, Sterling Bank partner to expand vehicle ownership, advance mobility solutions appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Kwankwaso asked me to swear on Qur’an over APC return deal — Kano gov
description:
Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, has claimed that his former political mentor, Rabiu Kwankwaso, asked him to swear on the Qur’an to confirm their agreement to return to the All Progressives Congress after his victory at the Supreme Court.
Yusuf said Kwankwaso personally sent him to meet President Bo
content:
Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, has claimed that his former political mentor, Rabiu Kwankwaso, asked him to swear on the Qur’an to confirm their agreement to return to the All Progressives Congress after his victory at the Supreme Court.

Yusuf said Kwankwaso personally sent him to meet President Bola Tinubu and communicate the proposed agreement, which also required the President to exercise restraint and not interfere in the legal proceedings.

The governor disclosed this in an interview with BBC Hausa, where he gave his account of the events leading to the breakdown of his relationship with Kwankwaso and his eventual defection from the New Nigeria Peoples Party to the APC.

“He himself sent me to Tinubu. He begged me to go and tell him that we had made this promise, and that if necessary I should swear with the Qur’an right there that if we won, he wanted us to come together,” Yusuf said.

Asked whether there was an understanding that they would join the APC if he won the court case, the governor replied, “That existed. There was an agreement.”

He said Tinubu was approached several times and asked to be patient and avoid interfering in the case, while Kwankwaso, Yusuf and their supporters were expected to move to the APC if the Supreme Court ruled in his favour.

“The President was approached not once, not twice, not three times,” he said.

Yusuf added that he personally met Tinubu to communicate the pledge and later returned to inform Kwankwaso about their discussion.

He said the arrangement was based on the relationship between Tinubu and Kwankwaso at the time, adding that the objective was to ensure political unity after the court judgment.

The governor rejected accusations that he betrayed his former mentor, insisting that Kwankwaso was aware of the discussions and had sent people to follow up on them.

“Everything that was done was done with the knowledge of the leader…We reached an agreement, but Kwankwaso did not fulfil it,” he added.

Yusuf also said the proposed meeting between Tinubu and Kwankwaso was arranged through him after the President agreed to receive the former Kano governor.

He added that things did not go well after Kwankwaso visited Kano, claiming that the former governor made comments against the President.

Explaining some of the reasons behind his decision to leave the NNPP, Yusuf said the party’s limited nationwide presence affected his administration’s ability to secure cooperation from the Federal Government.

“We came into this party doing what ought to be done, yet we weren’t getting cooperation. Why? Because we weren’t in the party that is nationwide—that is, the Federal Government,” he said.

He added that politics was not permanent, noting that politicians could move between parties depending on prevailing circumstances.

“Politics, as the public knows, is something that has no permanence in it. Today you can be in this party, tomorrow you find yourself in another,” he said.

Yusuf was elected Kano State governor in 2023 on the NNPP platform with the backing of Kwankwaso, who had endorsed his candidacy. The Supreme Court affirmed his election in January 2024 after the APC candidate, Nasiru Yusuf Gawuna, challenged the result.

Yusuf formally defected to the APC on January 26, 2026, a move Kwankwaso described as “the worst betrayal I have witnessed in my life”. The governor has, however, said his former mentor knew about the discussions that preceded the proposed move to the ruling party.

title: Versat Automobile signs exclusive distribution agreement with EXEED
description:
By Moses Akaigwe
Versat Automobile Limited has signed an exclusive Distribution Agreement with Chery Group, formally securing its appointment as the authorised General Distributor of EXEED in Nigeria. 
The agreement marks a significant milestone in the company’s expansion within the Nigerian automot
content:
By Moses Akaigwe

Versat Automobile Limited has signed an exclusive Distribution Agreement with Chery Group, formally securing its appointment as the authorised General Distributor of EXEED in Nigeria. 

The agreement marks a significant milestone in the company’s expansion within the Nigerian automotive industry and lays the foundation for introducing the premium brand to the Nigerian market in 2027.

The signing ceremony took place in Wuhu, Anhui Province, China. Alhaji Francis TntñtjlOgboro, Non-Executive Director of Versat Automobile Limited, signed on behalf of Versat, and Mr. Heaven Hai, Regional Director of Chery Group, signed on behalf of Chery Group. Mr. Umoh Ekanem, Head of Commercial Vehicles at Versat Automobile Limited, and Mr. Shane Ni, National Director at Chery Group, were also in attendance. 

Under the agreement, Versat Automobile will be responsible for the distribution and representation of EXEED in Nigeria. The mandate covers passenger cars (electric vehicles, hybrid vehicles, internal combustion engine vehicles l) and after-sales support. 

This framework establishes the brand’s local operations and reflects a shared vision to introduce a premium automotive offering that responds to the changing expectations of Nigerian consumers, with better access to quality vehicles, innovative mobility solutions, and dependable ownership support.

Speaking on the significance of the agreement, Alhaji Francis Ogboro said: “This partnership represents an important development in our commitment īto bringing quality automotive brands and innovative mobility solutions to Nigeria. 

Securing the exclusive distribution rights for EXEED is a responsibility we take seriously, and we are committed to establishing the brand on a strong foundation. We recognise the opportunities within the Nigerian automotive market and look forward to building a lasting partnership that delivers value to customers while contributing positively to the industry’s development.”

Nigeria remains an important market for automotive distribution, supported by a large population, growing urban centres, expanding business activity and evolving consumer expectations. As mobility needs change, vehicle quality, technological advancement, reliability, efficiency and dependable After-Sales services matter more than ever. Against this backdrop, EXEED broadens the range of premium choices available to Nigerian consumers and contributes to the development of the country’s automotive distribution landscape.

For Versat Automobile, the agreement is more than an addition to its portfolio. It is a strategic commitment to building a recognised automotive brand in Nigeria through structured distribution, market development and sustained customer engagement. As General Distributor, Versat will lead EXEED’s market representation and distribution activities, working closely with Chery Group to put the necessary commercial and operational framework in place. A key feature of the agreement is that it goes beyond vehicle distribution to include After-Sales (Services and Genuine Parts). A successful brand introduction takes more than making  vehicles available for purchase. It also needs the infrastructure, technical capability and service standards to support ownership throughout the vehicle’s lifecycle. Versat will develop an after-sales framework for EXEED customers, including genuine parts, technical support and service arrangements designed to maintain performance, reliability and customer confidence.

The inclusion of Electric and Hybrid Vehicles also reflects the changing direction of the industry. As alternative powertrains gain attention, the Nigerian market will need distributors able to support different vehicle technologies and their ownership requirements. Versat will work with Chery Group to align its local operations with the brand’s standards while accounting for the needs of Nigerian customers and the realities of the local market.

Mr. Umoh Ekanem said: “The agreement gives us a clear mandate to develop EXEED’s presence in Nigeria across vehicle distribution and After-Sales. Our focus is on putting the right structures, resources and support systems in place to ensure that customers receive a complete ownership experience. We are working towards building a distribution and service framework that reflects the standards of the brand and provides the level of support Nigerian customers expect.”

Speaking on the partnership, Mr. Shane Ni commented: “We believe that EXEED’s collaboration with the Versat team will bring more opportunities to the region and better embody our philosophy of ‘in somewhere, be somewhere, for somewhere.”

The signing took place during the 2026 EXEED International User Summit, which brought together 120 user representatives from 26 countries and regions. During the summit, EXEED unveiled its “Future Luxury” design language, rooted in its Perpetua philosophy, and held its 12th track experience event at a professional circuit. 

Versat Automobile and Chery Group will continue preparing for the official introduction of EXEED in Nigeria in 2027. The launch will be the next major milestone, giving the brand a formal introduction to Nigerian  consumers, automotive stakeholders, business leaders and the media. 

Until then, Versat will continue work on distribution planning, customer engagement, after-sales readiness and other operational requirements. 

Further details on the launch, product availability, distribution arrangements and customer-facing activities will be shared through the company’s official channels in due course.

Alhaji Ogboro added: “We see significant potential for EXEED in Nigeria, and we intend to build a brand presence that is both commercially sustainable and responsive to the needs of the market. We are approaching this partnership with a long-term perspective, recognising that establishing customer confidence requires consistency, quality and dependable support. 

We look forward to introducing EXEED to Nigerians and building a relationship with customers that extends well beyond the point of purchase.”

The signing marks an important new chapter for Versat Automobile. With both organisations committed to 2the partnership, the focus now shifts to turning the agreement into a structured market presence supported by effective distribution, reliable after-sales services and a strong customer-focused approach.

title: Man With Alzheimer’s Found Alive After 11 Days In Brazilian Amazon Rainforest
description: A 74-year-old man with Alzheimer’s disease was found alive after 11 days lost in Brazil’s Amazon rainforest, where he ate wild fruit and slept on beds of leaves, rescuers and local media reports said.Nine days later, his granddaughter Sara Montes urged firefighters to keep looking for hi
content:
A 74-year-old man with Alzheimer’s disease was found alive after 11 days lost in Brazil’s Amazon rainforest, where he ate wild fruit and slept on beds of leaves, rescuers and local media reports said.

Nine days later, his granddaughter Sara Montes urged firefighters to keep looking for him. In a video posted on Instagram, she said they planned to suspend the search on Sunday, November 22.

“Don’t forget about us. Don’t forget about Grandpa,” she pleaded.

Rescuers found him Friday about 10 kilometers (six miles) from where he disappeared, according to social media posts by a group of park rangers and one of the rescuers.

Images from the rescue show him sitting in his underwear, looking disoriented.

A video posted on the g1 news site shows several men carrying him through the forest on a makeshift stretcher.

Local media reported Sunday that Ferreira dos Santos, a former informal miner who knew the rainforest well, survived by eating fruit from the buriti, an Amazonian palm, and drank water from natural sources.

Park ranger Nerivan da Silva told g1 that searchers found beds Ferreira dos Santos had made from acai palm leaves and footprints showing he had been walking in circles.

In dense rainforest like the area where rescuers searched, thick vegetation can limit visibility to a few meters.

Ferreira dos Santos remained in the hospital as of Sunday morning, according to g1.

title: Beyond the showroom: Why car buyers in Nigeria must demand more than 4 wheels
description:
By Moses Akaigwe
For many Nigerians, buying a brand-new vehicle represents a major financial commitment, often involving years of savings, bank loans or carefully planned investments. Yet, the excitement of driving a new car home can quickly turn into frustration when the vehicle develops a fault an
content:
By Moses Akaigwe

For many Nigerians, buying a brand-new vehicle represents a major financial commitment, often involving years of savings, bank loans or carefully planned investments. Yet, the excitement of driving a new car home can quickly turn into frustration when the vehicle develops a fault and the dealer suddenly becomes difficult to reach.

This growing disconnect between the promises made at the point of sale and the support customers receive afterwards has brought the issue of after-sales service into sharper focus in Nigeria’s automotive industry.

Consumer rights advocate, Akonte Ekine, knows this experience firsthand. He recalled purchasing a brand-new vehicle through a bank only for it to develop a problem barely two weeks after delivery. His attempts to obtain assistance from the seller and insurance company, he said, yielded little response.

“I once spent my good money to buy a brand-new car through a bank and just two weeks after, the car developed a problem. I complained to the seller and to my insurance but they didn’t even show interest in the situation,” Ekine told BusinessDay.

His experience raises an important question for automobile manufacturers, distributors and dealers: What happens to the customer after the money has changed hands?
For Ekine, the answer should be straightforward. Businesses must deliver the quality of service promised to customers, regardless of the market in which they operate.

“The consumer is the same everywhere. What he or she wants is simple quality service based on the brand promise,” he said.

The concern goes beyond individual experiences. In Nigeria, where vehicle ownership involves considerable financial sacrifice, access to genuine spare parts, qualified technicians, warranty services and timely repairs can significantly influence the overall ownership experience.
Importantly, consumers are not without legal protection.

The Executive Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC), Mr Tunji Bello, has reinforced this position, insisting that businesses cannot evade their statutory obligations through restrictive company policies.

Speaking at a stakeholders’ engagement organised by the FCCPC and Lagos State Consumer Protection Agency (LASCOPA) in Lagos on July 29, 2026, Bello said consumers were entitled to appropriate remedies when goods failed to meet legally required standards.

“They must also know that where the law gives them the right to a refund, replacement, or repair, that right will be respected,” he stated.

He further emphasised that: “Every transaction also carries an implied warranty that goods supplied will be of acceptable quality and fit for the purpose for which they were purchased.”

The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act 2018 provides for consumers’ entitlement to goods of acceptable quality, while Section 132 establishes an implied warranty of quality and provides remedies for qualifying defective products.

For the automotive industry, this should serve as more than a regulatory reminder. It is a call to rethink customer relationships and recognise that a vehicle purchase is the beginning, not the end, of a business relationship.

Automobile brands that invest in responsive customer care, transparent warranty arrangements, accessible service centres and reliable spare-parts networks stand a better chance of earning consumer confidence and securing repeat patronage.

Ultimately, the real test of an automobile brand is not simply how attractive its vehicles look in the showroom or how aggressively they are marketed. It is how the company treats customers when the excitement of a new purchase gives way to the realities of vehicle ownership.

For Nigerian buyers, the lesson is equally important: before collecting the keys, ask what happens when something goes wrong. A good vehicle should come with the assurance that the people who sold it will not disappear when their customers need them most.

title: India To Give $1.6b Aid Package To Flood-Hit Nepal
description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi offered a $1.6 billion “development cooperation” package to neighbouring Nepal on Monday in the wake of devastating Himalayan floods.“We express our deep condolences for the loss of lives caused by the devastating floods in Nepal in August,&rdquo
content:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi offered a $1.6 billion “development cooperation” package to neighbouring Nepal on Monday in the wake of devastating Himalayan floods.

“We express our deep condolences for the loss of lives caused by the devastating floods in Nepal in August,” Modi said, standing alongside his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah in New Delhi.

“To support Nepal’s reconstruction, and give fresh momentum to its long-term development, we announce a development cooperation package worth 240 billion Nepali rupees ($1.6 billion),” he said.

India did not immediately give specific details of what the development package included.

Shah was given a military honour guard parade at the presidential palace in New Delhi, on his first trip to a neighbouring country since taking office in March.

The rapper-turned-politician came to power following a wave of youth-led anti-corruption protests in September 2025.

Shah, 36, wearing his trademark sunglasses and dressed in black, was given a bear hug by Modi, 76, dressed all in white.

Unlike his predecessors, Shah had initially refrained from foreign visits since becoming prime minister.

His first overseas trip was to New York in September, where he addressed the United Nations General Assembly as Nepal reeled from a deadly tsunami-like flood, triggered by a high-altitude glacial mountain collapse, that killed more than 1,400 people and left 5,000 missing.

‘Deal with future disasters’

Nepal, a largely rural country that contributes little to global greenhouse gas emissions, estimates reconstruction will cost $4.78 billion.

Shah said it showed the “imperative to address the challenges of climate change through collective action”.

In October, the United Nations’ climate loss and damage fund agreed the modest sum of $20 million in aid to Nepal — the maximum amount countries can request in a single application — and the first time it has set aside money for any country.

Nepal, a landlocked Himalayan nation of 30 million people, has long had to balance its relations with its two giant neighbours, India and China.

“Our commitment will be to help affected families rebuild their lives, create new opportunities and further strengthen Nepal’s capacity to deal with future disasters,” Modi said.

India is Nepal’s largest trading partner, accounting for more than 60 percent of its imports, worth $8.6 billion, while China accounts for 13 percent, or $1.8 billion, according to World Bank figures.

Modi said the two countries’ relationship was rooted in “shared history, culture and deep people-to-people ties”, as he unveiled a joint vision document for cooperation.

The two leaders also launched projects including a cross-border railway, a 669-megawatt hydropower plant, an expanded petroleum pipeline and a new oil storage terminal.

“May the friendship between Nepal and India be one where trust stands as tall as the Himalayas, cooperation flows as continuously as a river, and the prosperity of both nations flourishes beneath our shared sky,” Shah added.

The post India To Give $1.6b Aid Package To Flood-Hit Nepal appeared first on Channels Television.

title: One hospitalised, 12,000 evacuated from Manchester concert
description:
More than 12, 000 people were evacuated during US rapper Don Toliver’s concert at Co-op Live Arena in Manchester, United Kingdom, on Sunday, following reports of people in the crowd suffering effects from an unknown substance.
The incident prompted a major emergency response, with some concertgoers
content:
More than 12, 000 people were evacuated during US rapper Don Toliver’s concert at Co-op Live Arena in Manchester, United Kingdom, on Sunday, following reports of people in the crowd suffering effects from an unknown substance.

The incident prompted a major emergency response, with some concertgoers medically assessed at the scene.

Greater Manchester Police said in an updated statement on Monday, the officers were first notified of the incident by venue staff shortly after 10 pm on Sunday, November 22, 2026.

Assistant Chief Constable Steph Parker, who was Gold Commander for the incident, said one person had been taken to hospital, adding that emergency services worked with partner agencies to coordinate the response.

He noted that investigations have begun to unravel the nature of the substance.

The police chief also advised other attendees to seek medical assistance if they felt unwell.

Parker said, “Our priority was to ensure the safety of every person who was attending the concert. Several people were treated on site, and one has been taken to hospital at this time. Anyone who has left the event and since become unwell is advised to attend their local hospital.

“We understand the concern that this incident will have raised – particularly those with loved ones at the venue last night – and we’d like to thank everyone for their patience as we dealt with it.

“There were over 12,000 people in attendance during this concert who were safely escorted from the arena so they could make their way home.

“Our declaration of a major incident has allowed us to ensure emergency services and partner agencies can work together quickly and effectively to coordinate a safe response. We will now begin to fully understand what this substance was and how this incident came about.”

North West Ambulance Service on Sunday stated that the incident occurred at 10.25 pm, saying it deployed several emergency crews, including the Hazardous Area Response Team, to support the safe assessment and treatment of people at the scene.

The ambulance service said more than 50 people were assessed by clinicians, with some “reporting eye and respiratory symptoms.”

It noted, however, that decontamination is being carried out as a precaution and one patient has been taken to Manchester Royal Infirmary for further assessment.

“The incident remains ongoing, and our teams remain at the scene assessing and caring for patients. We continue to work closely with emergency service partners while enquiries are carried out to establish what the substance was.

“Anyone at tonight’s event who has since noticed side effects or become ill should seek medical advice,” it advised.

The Standard quoted Co-op Live as saying, “Following an incident in the crowd at last night’s show, we are working closely with Greater Manchester Police to identify the cause and act appropriately.

“Our priority remains the safety and security of all visitors to Co-op Live, and we will provide more information once we have an update from GMP.”

Toliver, whose real name is Caleb Zackery Toliver, was performing in Manchester as part of his Nitrous tour. He is scheduled to perform at London’s O2 Arena on Monday and OVO Arena Wembley on Tuesday.

The Co-op Live Arena is scheduled to host US singer Phoebe Bridgers on Thursday.

title: Amnesty condemns killing of village head, six others in Niger village
description:
Amnesty International has condemned the killing of seven people in an attack on Lumma Ba’are village in the Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State, calling on the authorities to do more to end escalating bloody attacks on villages and communities across parts of the state.
This is contained in a
content:
Amnesty International has condemned the killing of seven people in an attack on Lumma Ba’are village in the Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State, calling on the authorities to do more to end escalating bloody attacks on villages and communities across parts of the state.

This is contained in a Monday statement shared by the rights group on X.

Amnesty said the brutal attack carried by gunmen widely referred to as bandits, which occurred around 5:00pm on Saturday, also resulted in many homes and shops getting burnt to ashes.

“The Nigerian authorities must do more to end escalating bloody attacks on villages and communities across some parts of Niger state,” Amnesty said.

The organisation stated, “The gunmen particularly targeted a mosque in which people were performing dawn prayers and killed the village head and other worshippers.

“This attack had torn the community apart, with many people still missing. The gunmen also kidnapped unspecified number of people.”

It added, “Clearly, the spate and scale of these attacks are indication that the Nigerian authorities have left rural communities in the north at the mercy of rampaging gunmen who have been killing people and burning down entire villages.”

Amnesty said terrifying attacks on rural communities in the north of Nigeria have been going on for years, describing the ongoing failure of security forces to take sufficient steps to protect villagers from these predictable attacks as utterly shameful.

“Gunmen and other armed groups have been intensifying bloody attacks on Borgu. The majority of the people in these communities depend on farming for their livelihoods, but they are now too afraid to go to the fields.

“The government has an obligation to protect its population. The rising death toll in the north of Nigeria shows just how badly the authorities are failing in this responsibility,” it further stated.

The post Amnesty condemns killing of village head, six others in Niger village appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Eisenkot, Netanyahu parties to meet again for Israel coalition talks
description:
The parties of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot, who is tasked with forming the next Israeli government, are due to resume coalition talks on Monday after negotiations a day earlier delivered no agreement.



The third round of talks comes as Eisenkot’s wide-ranging camp
content:
The parties of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot, who is tasked with forming the next Israeli government, are due to resume coalition talks on Monday after negotiations a day earlier delivered no agreement.

The third round of talks comes as Eisenkot’s wide-ranging camp faces divisions on whether to forge alliances with the ultra-Orthodox parties, or the Arab-majority lists, or whether to form a national unity government with Netanyahu’s Likud.

Former military chief Eisenkot has until December 6 — a deadline which can be extended by 14 days — to form a government to replace Netanyahu after the October election failed to deliver a clear majority for either bloc.

Delegations from Eisenkot’s centrist Yashar party and Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud are due to meet on Monday evening for a third round of negotiations, a spokesperson for Likud told AFP.

Representatives from each party met for nearly four hours on Sunday and laid out their positions “on a range of substantive issues,” with no sign of a breakthrough.

– Political ‘boycotts’ –

On Saturday, Yashar presented the talks as “a genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government”, saying that Eisenkot had asked his representatives to explore all options.

Likud immediately laid down several conditions for its participation in a unity government, including an end to “all personal attacks” and political “boycotts” targeting Netanyahu and his government.

Eisenkot’s 48-member bloc needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority and remains divided over how to build a coalition.

Short of 61 lawmakers, Eisenkot’s bloc could form a minority government.

The head of the left-leaning Democrats party, Yair Golan, on Monday called for an end to the “sham talks with Likud”.

Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel.

Such an arrangement could allow Netanyahu to keep his political leverage against the corruption charges he faces, as well as continue to oppose the creation of an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023.

But that prospect runs up against Eisenkot’s refusal to serve in a cabinet led by Netanyahu, against whom he centred his campaign.

Last week, Eisenkot said that he would be prepared to put forward a minority national emergency government for a parliamentary vote should efforts to create a broad-based government fail.

The post Eisenkot, Netanyahu parties to meet again for Israel coalition talks appeared first on Vanguard News.

content:
By Faheem Lawal

CANEX Creations Inc., a subsidiary of Afreximbank’s Fund for Export Development in Africa (FEDA), has completed a strategic equity investment in C.R.E.A.M. Platform Limited, the Nigerian digital platform founded by Afrobeats star D’Banj.

The completion was announced at a ceremony during CANEX WKND 2026 in Lagos on 6 November. CANEX Creations, set up to invest in, develop and commercialise African intellectual property, was represented by its Chief Executive Officer, Osahon Akpata. D’Banj, whose full name is Oladapo Daniel Oyebanjo, represented C.R.E.A.M., which he founded.

The investment closes out a deal first announced at the Afreximbank Annual Meetings in 2025, when the two sides signed a term sheet setting out the framework for the transaction.

The funds are expected to support the platform’s scaling, including the rollout of CREAM 3.0, expansion of services and content, and targeted marketing to grow users and revenue. C.R.E.A.M. says it will also gain institutional backing as it works to support African creative talent.

D’Banj cast the deal as bigger than a signing. “As I have always said, content is the new crude,” he said. “This is beyond a deal signing. It is history being made: Africa’s creativity becomes Africa’s capital. African creatives now have access to the financial infrastructure to compete globally, while owning and retaining our IP in Africa.”

C.R.E.A.M. gives independent creatives tools to showcase their skills, distribute content, connect with industry opportunities and earn income. Its monetisation channels include content distribution, caller ring back tunes, streaming platforms, copyright protection, royalty collection and intellectual property management.

Akpata said the investment reflects C.R.E.A.M.’s position as “an African-owned platform that discovers talent, distributes and monetises their creative content”, and fits CANEX Creations’ mandate to back commercially viable, high-impact projects in Africa’s creative and cultural industries. He said it also supports Afreximbank’s wider creative-economy strategy of building the infrastructure, platforms and market links that African creative businesses need to scale, and the Bank Group’s aim of turning creative potential into enterprises, jobs and income.

Akpata added that C.R.E.A.M.’s mobile-first, USSD-enabled model suits African market realities and reaches emerging and grassroots talent that international distribution platforms may underserve. He expressed confidence that the investment would strengthen the platform’s ability to connect creatives with discovery, distribution, audience engagement, monetisation and future financing, and support its expansion beyond Nigeria.

The post Afreximbank unit completes equity investment in D’Banj’s C.R.E.A.M. Platform appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Artisanal miners seek inclusion in Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda
description:
No fewer than 1.6 million artisanal miners under the National Artisanal and Small Scale Mining Cooperative Society have appealed for inclusion in the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Tinubu’s administration.
The miners who work in Nasarawa, Zamfara, Niger, Plateau, Kaduna, Taraba, Bauchi and ot
content:
No fewer than 1.6 million artisanal miners under the National Artisanal and Small Scale Mining Cooperative Society have appealed for inclusion in the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Tinubu’s administration.

The miners who work in Nasarawa, Zamfara, Niger, Plateau, Kaduna, Taraba, Bauchi and other mineral-producing states noted that they work without modern equipment, protective clothing, technical training, affordable financing or access to legitimate mineral markets.

Speaking on their behalf in a press statement made available to journalists in the Keffi Local Government Area of Nasarawa State on Sunday, the group’s National President, Abdullah Dantansidi, noted that such a situation exposes them to health risks, accidents and poverty, in spite of the mineral wealth in their communities.

Dantansidi said, “Beneath our soil lie mineral resources capable of transforming our economy, creating jobs, and reducing our dependence on oil. Yet the men and women whose hands uncover this wealth are often among the poorest and most vulnerable Nigerians.

“Across Nasarawa, Zamfara, Niger, Plateau, Kaduna, Taraba, Bauchi and other mineral-producing states, our miners go into pits daily with little more than hoes, shovels, and determination.

“Many work without modern equipment, protective clothing, technical training, affordable financing, or access to legitimate mineral markets. They risk their health and their lives.”

He, therefore, urged the President to include artisanal miners in the Renewed Hope Agenda through a dedicated empowerment and safety programme.

Meanwhile, Dantansidi commended the Federal Government for its efforts to formalise artisanal mining through registered cooperatives, as he advocated that the ongoing reforms should reach ordinary miners in remote communities.

According to him, about 1.6 million Nigerians are directly engaged in artisanal and small-scale mining, with millions of family members depending on the sector.

He added, “We are not asking the government to overlook mining regulations. We are asking for the practical support that will enable ordinary miners to comply with those regulations and earn a decent living.

“Behind every mineral is a human being. A father struggling to provide for his family. A mother working to educate her children. A young Nigerian seeking an honest livelihood.

“Let the Renewed Hope Agenda reach the mining pits, the rural communities and the hardworking Nigerians whose contributions often go unrecognised.

“We do not ask for charity. We ask for opportunity, protection, recognition, and a fair chance to contribute to the greatness of our country. When you empower Nigeria’s 1.6 million artisanal miners, you improve millions of livelihoods, strengthen rural communities, and give real meaning to Renewed Hope.”

Dantansidi appealed to Tinubu to establish a Renewed Hope Artisanal Miners Empowerment and Safety Programme, which should be built on existing initiatives of the Federal Ministry of Solid Minerals Development.

He listed six priority areas for the programme, which include: recognition, registration and licensing; modern equipment and shared mining facilities; safety training and protection; affordable financing and cooperative development; fair mineral markets and local value addition; and community development and family welfare.

He urged the President to direct the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, to engage representatives of artisanal mining cooperatives nationwide, and also proposed that the engagement should begin within 90 days.

Dantansidi said the miners were ready to organise themselves, meet appropriate standards and work with government institutions.

The post Artisanal miners seek inclusion in Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: FG, UN disappointed as COP31 climate talks collapse
description: The Federal Government has expressed disappointment over the collapse of climate negotiations in Antalya, Türkiye, where nearly 200The Federal Government has expressed disappointment over the collapse of climate negotiations in Antalya, Türkiye, where nearly 200 countries failed to agree on an overa
content:
The Federal Government has expressed disappointment over the collapse of climate negotiations in Antalya, Türkiye, where nearly 200The Federal Government has expressed disappointment over the collapse of climate negotiations in Antalya, Türkiye, where nearly 200 countries failed to agree on an overarching political deal after almost 50 hours of overtime talks at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference.

The FG maintained that despite the lack of a finalised deal, Nigeria would not stop its domestic climate programmes.

In a statement released on Sunday after the fallout, the Director-General, National Council on Climate Change, Omotenioye Majekodunmi, said Nigeria would continue implementing its climate commitments under its Nationally Determined Contribution 3.0, strengthening climate governance and attracting investment into the energy transition.

She said, “COP31’s inability to reach consensus on an overarching political outcome is disappointing and underscores the continuing challenges facing international climate cooperation. However, the absence of a new political agreement does not diminish the urgency of climate action, nor does it invalidate the commitments already undertaken under the Paris Agreement.”

She added, “For Nigeria, our focus remains firmly on implementation. We will continue advancing our NDC 3.0, strengthening climate governance, mobilising investment and pursuing an orderly, just and nationally determined energy transition.”

Majekodunmi said the negotiations had reinforced the need to match climate ambition with adequate financing and practical implementation plans, particularly for developing countries with different economic circumstances.

She said Nigeria’s climate progress would ultimately be measured by its impact on employment, businesses, energy access and livelihoods.

This year’s climate conference, tagged COP31, is the second time in the history of global climate talks that a summit has ended without an agreement and the first in 17 years, The PUNCH reports.

The summit, which opened on November 9, 2026, and was scheduled to close on November 20, 2026, ended on Sunday without adopting a final decision, exposing deep divisions over fossil fuel phase-out, climate finance, adaptation funding and a just energy transition.

The conference became the longest United Nations climate summit on record, surpassing the previous record held by COP25 in Madrid, Spain, in 2019, which ran about 44 hours past its scheduled closing time.

COP31 President Murat Kurum confirmed during the closing plenary on Sunday that the final draft agreement would not be adopted after countries failed to bridge their differences over the proposed text.

The breakdown followed disagreements over the inclusion of language on transitioning away from fossil fuels, adaptation finance and the role of carbon capture technologies in tackling climate change.

He said, “As the Presidency, we have worked with a focus on results from day one. Getting hung up on a single word and stalling the process means dashing the hopes of people expecting good news from us. A system that cannot make decisions benefits no one.

“If we are talking about sincerity, we must all act accordingly and work together towards our shared goals.”

COP31 negotiations chair Chris Bowen, who unsuccessfully sought to broker consensus among nearly 200 nations, conceded he could not overcome what he called “unbridgeable red lines.”

“Unfortunately, we were unable to reach agreement on a cover decision… And that’s disappointing, very disappointing,” Bowen, who is Australia’s climate minister, said.

The breakdown followed nearly two weeks of negotiations and disagreements over the language of the proposed agreement, particularly the demand for a clear commitment memories of the failed Copenhagen summit of 2009 and raised fresh doubts about the effectiveness of climate diplomacy.

The failure also attracted criticism from the UN Secretary-General, António Guterres, who expressed deep disappointment over the inability of governments to agree on a common political outcome.

In a statement following the conclusion of the summit, Guterres said, “I am deeply disappointed that COP31 has ended without consensus on an overarching outcome. I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands.”

He warned that the failure to reach an agreement would not change the urgency of the climate crisis, noting that global temperatures continued to break records while emissions remained dangerously high.

“There may be no consensus in the negotiating room. There is no ambiguity in the science. Temperatures keep shattering records. Climate extremes keep intensifying. Emissions remain far too high. And every delay makes our task harder and more costly,” he said.

The UN chief also criticised the continued dependence on fossil fuels, saying, “Fossil fuels are driving the climate crisis. The continued addiction to coal, oil and gas is fueling climate chaos, exposing economies to price shocks, and undermining energy security. We can’t put out the fire while pouring fuel on it.”

“It certainly fell short today,” said UN climate chief Simon Stiell, describing progress over the marathon fortnight of negotiations in Antalya as “limited. The world cannot afford a repeat.”

The disagreements also involved the proposed adaptation finance target of $120bn, which disappeared from the final draft, while countries failed to agree on a concrete plan to mobilise the resources needed by vulnerable economies.

The breakdown has shifted attention to COP32, scheduled to take place in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, next year, where countries are expected to continue discussions on unresolved climate commitments.

The failure comes after COP28 in Dubai in 2023, when countries agreed to transition away from fossil fuels in a just, orderly and equitable manner. COP30 in Belém, Brazil, also provided a mandate for developing a just transition mechanism, which campaigners had hoped would receive concrete institutional backing in Antalya.

However, the Climate Action Network maintained that the fight for climate justice would continue, insisting that the next summit must deliver financing, adaptation support and a fair transition for developing countries.

The post FG, UN disappointed as COP31 climate talks collapse appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: My son faced rejection over marriage controversy – Pete Edochie
description:
Veteran Nollywood actor, Pete Edochie, has said his son, Yul Edochie, faced public and professional rejection following the controversy surrounding his second marriage, claiming that there was a time people avoided anything associated with the actor.
File: Actor Yul Edochie and his estranged wife, M
content:
Veteran Nollywood actor, Pete Edochie, has said his son, Yul Edochie, faced public and professional rejection following the controversy surrounding his second marriage, claiming that there was a time people avoided anything associated with the actor.

Pete made this known in an interview with Ugo Nwokolo TV, an excerpt of which was shared on Sunday.

The full episode is expected to be released on Wednesday.

Speaking about the criticism Yul has faced since announcing his relationship with actress Judy Austin, Pete described his son as a strong person who had remained composed despite the backlash.

“Look at my son, Yul. Yul is a very tough guy. You can never subdue him, no matter how much you try,” he said.

The veteran actor said he respected Yul for not publicly speaking ill of his first wife, May, despite the controversy surrounding their marriage.

“He has never insulted his wife for one day. Go and check everything that has been happening. He has never come out to say, this woman did this, she did this. He has never done that,” Pete said.

He also claimed that the controversy had affected how some people in the entertainment industry received his son, alleging that award organisers repeatedly left him out.

“There was a time that anything he touched, people felt it was all poison. Nobody wanted to go close to it. Social media talks about him and his wife every day,” he said.

“Each time awards are organised, they don’t include him. He hasn’t bothered. He is doing very, very, very, very well.”

Yul’s marital controversy became public in April 2022 when he announced that he had welcomed a son with actress Judy Austin and introduced her as his second wife.

At the time, he was married to May, with whom he has four children. May subsequently made it clear that she did not accept a polygamous marriage, saying it was against her beliefs, faith and values.

In December 2022, Yul publicly apologised to May over his decision to marry another woman, acknowledging that he had hurt her and taking responsibility for his actions.

However, the disagreement between the couple continued to play out publicly. In January 2024, Yul cautioned May against what he described as attempts to manipulate public opinion against him, accusing her of encouraging people to hate him. He also claimed that he had remained silent for a long time to protect her image.

May later filed for divorce in August 2023, following the breakdown of their marriage. The dispute has remained a subject of public discussion, with the actor’s personal life frequently attracting reactions on social media.

Pete’s comments offer his perspective on the public and professional consequences Yul has faced, while also drawing attention to his claim that his son has refrained from publicly attacking May.

The post My son faced rejection over marriage controversy – Pete Edochie appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
UPDATE ON STATE OF AFFAIRS/STATEMENT OF FACTS OF THE COMPANY AND DEVELOPMENTS RELATED THERETO — BY THE RECEIVER AND LIQUIDATOR

 It will be recalled that the undersigned did a publication on July 17, 2026, briefing all stakeholders of Niger Insurance, Plc. on state of affairs of the company, following a judgment of 5th June, 2026 in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/887/2025, obtained in the name of the Company, without authority, by individuals who have no stake or shareholding in the company, but claiming to be Board Members of the company under Receivership/Liquidation.

For the purpose of those who must have missed the said publication, we shall restate in brief some salient facts contained therein, and thereafter state developments in respect of the company, vis-à-vis, position of the cases in the Appellate Courts, as at date:

  1. The operating license of Niger Insurance Plc. was cancelled by the official Regulatory Agency (National Insurance Commission), otherwise known as NAICOM, in June, 2022 for gross infraction against the prevailing Insurance Act and also for inability of the company to fulfill her core statutory obligations, i.e., payment of verified claims of its policy holders, since 2013 and inability to pay its staff salaries for well over a period of time, preceding 30 calendar months; after the company admitted those infractions in writing.
  2. In reaction to the license cancellation, the company immediately afterwards instituted an action at the Federal High Court Abuja, challenging the license cancellation and appointment of a Receiver/Liquidator for the company, by the Commission.
  3. The Federal High Court, Abuja, struck out the Suit for being incompetent and for lack of jurisdiction. The company immediately challenged that decision in an appeal to the Court of Appeal.
  4. The said Appeal was eventually dismissed by the Court of Appeal in 2024, following the filing of Notice of Withdrawal of the Appeal by the company.
  5. The company subsequently made a volve face and, engaged the services of another counsel (also a SAN) to file an application at the Court of Appeal to relist the dismissed Appeal, but the application was unanimously rejected and dismissed by the Court of Appeal sitting in Abuja, on the 27th of February, 2025.
  6. Dissatisfied with the decision of the Court of Appeal refusing to relist the dismissed appeal, the company went on further appeal to the Supreme Court; all the briefs of Argument have been duly filed and exchanged by the parties, but no hearing date has yet being given by the Apex Court.
  7. It was while the appeal on the subject matter of cancellation of the company license and appointment of a Receiver/Liquidator by the Commission was pending at the Supreme Court that the individuals who claimed to be Board members of the company in Receiver/Liquidation, initiated an action before the same Federal High Court, presided over, this time, by Hon. Justice J.K. Omotosho, vide an Amended Originating Summons dated 30th April, 2025 but filed on the 11th July, 2025; which action birthed the referenced judgment of 5th June, 2026 despite bringing to the attention of that Court the glaring issue of abuse of Court process involved.
  8. As mentioned above, despite the fact that attention of Justice Omotosho, via a Notice of Preliminary Objection, was pointedly drawn to the facts that the principal claims, issues and subject matters of the fresh case before him had been ruled upon by his fellow Judge of the same status ( Coram: Ekwo, J.) in January,  2023, and that the matter is now on appeal at the Supreme Court, awaiting determination on whether the Court of Appeal was right to dismiss the appeal of the company over the decision of Ekwo, J.,  the learned Justice Omotosho proceeded to hear the matter expeditiously, and gave judgment to the Plaintiffs on 5thJune 2026.
  9. The National Insurance Commission and the Receiver promptly filed their Notices of appeal against the judgement, of Omotosho, J. raising grounds of abuse of court process and also lack of jurisdiction/competence of the Presiding Judge, the fresh action having been barred by Statute of Limitation, having not been filed within the mandatory 3 months of occurrence of the alleged injurious actions of NAICOM, and their having to wait for over 2 calendar years after the said acts, before instituting the said fresh case in 2026, brought before Justice Omotosho.
  10. It should also be noted that both the Commission, (NAICOM) and the Receiver also filed along with their respective Notices of Appeal, Motions for Stay of Execution, by their Counsel, i.e., office of Prof Osipitan, SAN & Co, and Tochukwu, SAN & CO, at the Court of Appeal and the appeal, inclusive of the applications, are pending.
  11. It is also pertinent to note that the briefs of Argument had been filed by the parties Counsel, inclusive of Reply brief, and all being awaited now is hearing date from the Appeal Court Registry. Same goes with the earlier Appeal at the Apex Court in respect of the Court of Appeal dismissal of the challenge to the 2023 Ekwo, J’s judgment. The above stated scenario represents the undisputable development in the 3 cases cited above, all relating to Niger Insurance Plc, vis, a vis, efforts that had been made to circumvent due process of law, abuse of judicial process and the rule of law, by some known characters in this matter.
  12. It is pertinent to state that following the cancellation of the company’s operating license in June 2022 by the Commission/NAICOM and appointment of the Receiver, no shareholder of the company had opposed the actions taken by the Commission till date, albeit, gone to Court to challenge same, neither has any duly constituted Board of the company met to take any decision concerning the subject matter, or the company in general.
  13. The instituting of the case challenging the action of the Commission in June, 2022, was actually instigated and carried out on the instruction of a minority shareholder, without consultation with any of the company’s other shareholders.

The shareholder in question is merely one of the shareholders of the Plc company, and has only about 25% of Niger Insurance, Plc Shareholding, going by the last approved audited statement of the Company, and certainly not its majority shareholder. The authenticity of this fact can also be confirmed from the Commission, by any stakeholder.

  1. The very minority shareholder in question, after January 2023, i.e., following the striking out of Niger Insurance suit by Justice Ekwo of the Federal High Court, had approached the NAICOM and the Receiver, (verbally and in writing) requesting to not only buy but to be given the right of first refusal in the purchase of the 2 choicest properties of the company, i.e., its 10-storey building known as River Plaza and Mall, Abuja, as well as the Ikoyi property, popularly known as Polo House. The said deal could not go through following the ridiculous amount the minority shareholder of the company offered for purchase of the Rivers Plaza property, which of course, was vehemently rejected by the Receiver and the Commission (NAICOM).
  2. The advice by the then supervising Minister of the National Insurance Commission to the said shareholder at a meeting he conveyed in his office, to wit: not to short-change the company by buying its choicest property in Abuja, at an unreasonable price, was promptly turned down by the CEO of the said minority shareholder company.
  3. Niger Insurance, is a Plc, i.e., a Public Company duly registered under the CAC with 100% paid up share-capital, before its license was duly cancelled following its inability to meet up with its statutory responsibility for close to 10 calendar years, and having been serially given opportunities by the Commission to raise funds and recapitalise, and its failure to take advantage of the indulgence at the various times, up till June, 2022, when its license was eventually revoked.
  4. The last time the company paid claims of its policyholders was sometimes in 2016, and was then owing staff salaries for over 30 calendar months, prior to cancellation of its operating license by the National Insurance Commission (NAICOM).
  5. The last Actuary Valuation of the company showed it was owing close to 8,000 (Eight Thousand) policyholders, including Federal Government Agencies, in sum in the region of 2 digit billions of naira, aside its financial commitments to its numerous shareholders and other stakeholders.
  6. It should be noted by all stakeholders of the company, that Niger Insurance, being a public company, and assuming its licence had not been revoked by the Regulatory body, can only be recapitalised and come back to life, if the decision is supported by majority of its shareholders, at a meeting duly conveyed, pursuant to the mandatory procedure set out in CAMA, but certainly not at the instance of a company which does not hold majority of the shareholding of the company. We further state that even at that, the recapitalization exercise must be monitored by the Regulatory body, i.e., NAICOM and the SEC. The resolution of a simple majority of attendees will thereafter be tabled at the company’s Board meeting for further administrative process towards actual recapitalisation of the company.
  7. The last time Niger Insurance Plc. had a duly constituted Board meeting was in 2018. Since then, it did not have any recognised Board up to the time its operating license was cancelled. Before then, some of its Board members had resigned in writing and left the company in the hit of their challenges earlier mentioned herein, and had not been duly replaced before the company’s licence was revoked in June 2022.
  8. Indeed, some of such previous members of the Board whose names were used as Plaintiffs in the referenced Suit before Omotosho, J. have already gone to Court to ventilate their grievances over unauthorized use of their names in that Suit.
  9. EFFECT OF THE COURT CASES ON THE WORKS OF THE RECEIVER:It must be said that the pending cases, especially, the Omotosho, J. judgment of 5th June, 2026 have indeed constituted a bitter distraction to the Receiver/Liquidator, especially the unlawful resort to illegalities and unlawful operation at the instance of some faceless characters in in sealing off some of the company’s properties in Abuja and Lagos, thereby preventing its sales, and by extension, access of the Receiver to funds which he would have deployed into continued payments to policyholders, after verification of their claims.
  10. It should further be noted that the said illegal actions, purportedly on strength of the judgment delivered by Omotosho J, was carried out without any Order of the affected court, albeit, involvement of office of the Deputy Sheriff of the Federal High Court who ordinarily, is statutorily empowered and expected to carry out execution of any court judgment or Order, if any.

ON CURRENT LEGAL STATUS OF THE RECEIVER:

The undersigned states in unmistaken terms that his appointment remains valid and lawful, vis-à-vis, the statutorily activities and responsibility attached to the office, on the strength of justice I. E. Ekwo’s judgment, which is of the same hierarchy with that of justice Omotosho, and again, our having appealed against the latter’s judgment and filed a pending application for its execution.

It should also be noted that the Receiver since the January 2023 judgment in his favour by the Federal High Court (presided over by Hon. Justice Ekwo) which was upheld by dismissal of the Appellant’s Appeal against it, by the Court of Appeal Abuja, had continued in performance of his functions till date in the management of the company, and had indeed, since commenced payment to Individual Life Policyholders, whose claims had been duly verified and has also continued to attend to cases and claims against the company, among other assignments expected of him as the Receiver.

The undersigned wishes all stakeholders of the company to note that he has been ably strengthened and encouraged to continue in his statutory responsibility, having been guided by the extant Laws of the country and can therefore not be said to be in disobedience of any Court order or judgment, in any way, especially following the relevant judicial precedents laid down by our appellate courts in plethora of cases, for instances, the below captured cases:

(i)      BASIL OKOMA V. SUNDAY SAMUEL UDOH (2002) 1 NWLR 748 PG 438 (CA), where the Appellate court held thus: 

“Once an appeal is filed with a Motion for Stay, the applicant is not obliged to obey the judgment. Execution is suspended until hearing of Motion at least…This is because a party cannot be held to be in disobedience of the order he is appealing against and which he wants to be stayed. Nor can a party be stopped from exercising his constitutional right to appeal.”

(ii)      A.G. ANAMBRA STATE V. OKAFOR (1992) 2 NWLR (PT.224) 396 (P. 425, PARAS. G-H) (SC), where another appellate court also held as follows:

“It is an abuse of process for a respondent who knows that an appeal has been filed against a judgment in his favour and that a motion for stay of execution thereof is pending, to go ahead and execute the judgment until the motion for a stay of execution has been disposed of.”

Suffice to say that in this case, there was no Order of any court issued against the Receiver, whatsoever, till date.

IN CONCLUSION:

The Receiver urges all stakeholders of Niger Insurance, Plc, (Under Receivership) to exercise more patience with him and that he is committed to fulfilling his statutory obligations to them notwithstanding the aforesaid distractions he is confronted with, and shall in due course, continue with payment of claims to the policyholders after due verification, subject to availability of funds from sale of company’s assets, which he is vigorously pursuing.

Signed:

Otunba Sanya Ogunkuade, Esq.

(LL.B Hons, B.L, LL.D Hons)

Receiver & Liquidator,

Niger Insurance Plc

(Under Receivership)
