title: Katsina CDP Transforms 361 Wards, Secures ₦7.61bn For Grassroots Development
description: The Katsina State Community Development Programme (CDP) says it has established a comprehensive grassroots development framework across all 361 political wards in the state’s 34 Local Government Areas, with over ₦7.61 billion committed to community-driven projects to improve the lives of resid
content:
The Katsina State Community Development Programme (CDP) says it has established a comprehensive grassroots development framework across all 361 political wards in the state’s 34 Local Government Areas, with over ₦7.61 billion committed to community-driven projects to improve the lives of residents.

Speaking during a press conference and strategic stakeholders’ engagement held on Sunday in Daura to commemorate the programme’s second anniversary, the Programme Coordinator, Associate Professor Kamaluddeen Kabir, said the initiative has redefined development by placing communities at the centre of decision-making and project implementation.

The event, themed “Two Years of Impact, A Future of Possibilities: Celebrating Achievements, Inspiring Communities, Transforming Lives,” reviewed the programme’s achievements, acknowledged the contributions of communities and development partners, and outlined priorities for its next phase.

Kabir explained that the CDP provides communities with a platform to identify and prioritise projects in critical sectors including water supply, healthcare, education, agriculture, drainage, livelihoods and other essential services, leading to the implementation of thousands of community-driven interventions across the state.

He disclosed that the Katsina State Government invested ₦3.61 billion in the programme’s first phase, allocating ₦10 million to each of the 361 wards, while Governor Dikko Umaru Radda has approved an additional ₦4 billion for the second phase, reaffirming the administration’s commitment to inclusive grassroots development.

According to him, the programme has shifted communities from being passive beneficiaries to active partners involved in identifying needs, setting priorities, implementing projects, monitoring progress and safeguarding public investments.

“The CDP strengthens the relationship between government and citizens by ensuring that community priorities shape development decisions and public resource allocation,” he said.

Kabir noted that the programme is anchored on six key pillars: community development, infrastructure improvement, livelihoods and economic empowerment, water and sanitation, social inclusion, and sustainability through community ownership.

He revealed that more than 3,900 public facilities, including schools, healthcare centres, water schemes, drainage systems and solar-powered streetlights, have been renovated, rehabilitated or upgraded under the initiative.

On agriculture, the coordinator said the programme has supported over 18,000 farmers, while more than 36,100 farmers received fertiliser assistance, including the distribution of 400,000 bags of fertiliser, 4,000 hand power tillers, 4,000 solar-powered water pumps, 4,000 petrol-powered water pumps, and 4,000 knapsack sprayers to enhance productivity.

Kabir further stated that 32,490 small ruminants were distributed to 3,610 women and 361 large-scale farmers to strengthen livelihoods and improve household resilience.

He added that the programme has empowered 10,830 women through various interventions, supported 7,220 widows during Ramadan, and previously provided financial assistance of ₦50,000 each to more than 300 widows, underscoring its commitment to social inclusion and support for vulnerable groups.

While celebrating the achievements recorded within two years, Kabir stressed that the sustainability of the projects would depend largely on community participation, proper maintenance and protection of public assets against vandalism and neglect.

He called on traditional rulers, community leaders, local governments, development partners, civil society organisations, the private sector and the media to sustain collaboration in strengthening accountability, transparency and effective project monitoring.

The coordinator also urged residents to take ownership of public infrastructure by actively participating in project monitoring, reporting misuse and ensuring that facilities continue to serve future generations.

Kabir credited Governor Dikko Umaru Radda’s leadership for the programme’s success, describing the statewide coverage, the initial ₦3.61 billion investment and the approval of an additional ₦4 billion as clear demonstrations of the administration’s determination to bring governance closer to the people.

He said the next phase of the programme would focus on deepening community participation, improving monitoring and transparency, strengthening inclusion for women, youths, persons with disabilities and vulnerable households, while expanding agricultural productivity and enterprise development.

According to him, the programme has so far reached more than 900,000 people, laying what he described as a solid foundation for sustainable, community-driven development across Katsina State.

“Our message is clear: development becomes truly sustainable when communities participate in delivery, take ownership of outcomes and protect the public assets created for their benefit. That is the philosophy of the Katsina State Community Development Programme and the future we are committed to building together,” Kabir stated.

title: I feared losing my leg after shooting – Broda Shaggi
description:
Comedian and skit maker, Samuel Perry, popularly known as Broda Shaggi, has revealed how his injured leg was at risk of further damage after he was shot by a stray bullet in March 2026.
He credited the Senior Pastor of Harvesters International Christian Centre, Bolaji Idowu, with helping him secure
content:
Comedian and skit maker, Samuel Perry, popularly known as Broda Shaggi, has revealed how his injured leg was at risk of further damage after he was shot by a stray bullet in March 2026.

He credited the Senior Pastor of Harvesters International Christian Centre, Bolaji Idowu, with helping him secure treatment in Dubai.

Shaggi disclosed this on Sunday during a thanksgiving service at the church, where he recounted how Idowu intervened after months of delays in securing further treatment for the injury.

According to the comedian, he initially resisted travelling abroad for another surgery, despite being unable to walk for months after the shooting.

He said the pastor, however, insisted that he seek treatment outside Nigeria and helped connect his team with a specialist, Dr Lushola.

Shaggi’s manager, Olufemi Oguntamu, popularly known as Penza, who also spoke during the service, said the comedian had spent about a month in hospital before being discharged and instructed to return for weekly check-ups.

He said they initially expected that another surgery would be performed within two or three weeks, but the process dragged on for about four months.

Oguntamu said the delay prompted discussions about seeking treatment abroad, although Shaggi was initially unwilling to travel.

He added that Idowu intervened, insisting that the comedian needed to travel for further medical attention.

According to him, they considered treatment options in Dubai and the United Kingdom before eventually settling for Dubai, with the pastor helping to connect them with the specialist and arrange support.

Oguntamu said Idowu remained actively involved throughout the process, regularly calling to check on them and praying for the comedian’s recovery.

“At a point, Pastor Balaji would call me in the midnight. And I’d be like, ‘Ah, shit, this man no get wife?’ Every time, like, he would call me and pray for me. And he’d be like, ‘Samuel, don’t worry. You’ll be fine,’” he said.

He added that the pastor travelled from London to Dubai to support Shaggi during the surgery.

Oguntamu also recalled that Idowu had assured them that he would arrange support from church members wherever they eventually chose to have the surgery.

He said, “He was even saying that, ‘Oh, Shaggy, what’s the problem? Is it people that are going to take care of you?’ Because for those that don’t know, he’s a very private person.

“So, he didn’t want a lot of people into, you know, his matter. But Pastor Balaji would say, ‘Don’t worry. Anywhere you want the surgery, I’m going to ensure that I get members there that will support you and all of that.’”

Responding to the testimony, Idowu disclosed that doctors in Dubai told them the comedian’s injured leg was already shrinking when he eventually arrived for treatment.

“When they eventually got to Dubai, the doctor said if they had come late, the leg they shot was already shrinking. I’m telling you. And that’s the glory of God,” he said.

Shaggi, who repeatedly thanked the pastor for his intervention, said he had feared he might never regain the use of his leg after the shooting.

Recounting the incident, he said it happened on March 19, 2026, while he and his team were returning from a brand activation assignment.

He said they were caught in traffic when a crowd gathered around his vehicle, cheering and calling his name, before he suddenly heard a loud bang.

Shaggi said he initially thought policemen around the area were shooting but later discovered he had been hit when he touched his hip and noticed blood.

“There was traffic, the policemen were in front, my team were at the back, my car was in the middle, then these area boys just gathered. They were all happy and shouting, ‘Shaggy!’ like they always do. And all of a sudden, all I heard was a loud bang.

“I thought maybe the policemen were shooting outside or something was happening outside. So I looked to the right. I saw people moving, I saw people talking, but I couldn’t hear a thing. It was just total silence. Then, when I touched my hip, I started seeing blood,” he said.

The comedian said he became afraid of dying despite previously believing he was prepared for death.

“Like, I don’t know, I’ve always said, when death comes, I’m ready. Like, I’m ready. But we got to that point, and the next thing I was just saying is, ‘Jesus, I don’t want to die. Jesus, I don’t want to die. Jesus, I don’t want to die,’” he added.

He said he was initially taken to a hospital where the necessary treatment could not be provided before being transferred to another facility in Ikeja, where he received first aid and was stabilised.

Shaggi said the experience also made him worry about the future of his entertainment career, particularly because dancing and physical performances were important parts of his work.

He disclosed that he initially expected to spend only a few days in hospital and even instructed his manager not to inform his mother about the incident.

However, as his hospitalisation continued, he eventually contacted her and told her he was receiving treatment.

He said he did not initially tell her that he had been shot because he was afraid she would become distressed.

“I just had to call her. I didn’t even tell her I was shot. I just said I was in the hospital so that she wouldn’t shout wherever she was,” he said.

Shaggi said seeing his mother after she arrived at the hospital was particularly emotional because it was the first time she had seen him in such a condition.

“She came, she saw me, she felt really bad. I felt so bad, too, because it was the first time she would see me in that position. It was the first time I would see myself in that position. I’m not going to lie, I thought I was going to lose it,” he added.

The comedian said he could not walk for months and depended on crutches and assistance from others for basic activities, including bathing.

“After four months, I couldn’t walk. It was just me on my crutches and this leg up like this. I was in the hospital. They bathed me. There was this very small girl. She would bathe me,” he said.

He added that he had prepared himself for the possibility of using crutches permanently but remained grateful that his recovery took a different turn.

“For my fans, for those who follow me, for those who watch my videos, I love you too. I already made up my mind that whatever happens, I’m going to use that crutch as brother. But thank God, it didn’t go that way,” he said.

The comedian had earlier recounted his ordeal in a YouTube video, saying the injury kept him away from work for months and left him uncertain about his future in the entertainment industry.

He had also spoken about his fears that audiences might forget him while he was unable to create content and perform.

In that account, Shaggi said he underwent an initial surgery in Nigeria before eventually travelling to Dubai for further treatment and physiotherapy.

He disclosed that his recovery improved after the procedure in Dubai, saying he was able to stand with support on the second day and walk with crutches on the third day.

At Sunday’s thanksgiving service, Shaggi also led the congregation in praise songs, accompanied by the church choir, as he celebrated his recovery and expressed gratitude for the support he received during the difficult period.

title: Ondo community protests alleged planned imposition of monarch
description: Residents and community leaders in Bamikemo community in Ile-Oluji/Oke-Igbo Local Government Area of Ondo State have protested against the alleged imposition of a monarch on the ancient town, calling on Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa to intervene and ensure due process in the selection of their tradition
content:
Residents and community leaders in Bamikemo community in Ile-Oluji/Oke-Igbo Local Government Area of Ondo State have protested against the alleged imposition of a monarch on the ancient town, calling on Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa to intervene and ensure due process in the selection of their traditional ruler.

The protesters accused some people in power of planning to impose a candidate they described as a stranger on the community against the wishes of the people and kingmakers.

They carried placards with inscriptions such as “Governor Aiyedatiwa, save Bamikemo from imposition”; “The Akemo throne belongs to the royal blood”; “Don’t impose a stranger on us”; “We need due process for our king”; and “Don’t impose an unpopular person on Bamikemo.”

Speaking after the protest on Sunday, a community leader, Oluwaseun Adewolu, alleged that some traditional rulers in Ile Oluji were attempting to impose a candidate who had no ancestral or property tied to Bamikemo.

He said, “Our protest is against the imposition of somebody who doesn’t have land here; he doesn’t have a farm, doesn’t belong here, doesn’t have a house here.

“Bamikemo is a very autonomous town. Somebody whose grandfather doesn’t belong here, whose father doesn’t belong here, and he himself doesn’t belong here, I don’t know why they are trying to impose such a person on us.”

Adewolu described the alleged planned imposition as a violation of the community’s fundamental rights, insisting that the people should be allowed to determine who becomes their traditional ruler.

He identified one Prince Adelakun Bajewolu as the preferred candidate of the town, saying his family had ancestral connections and property in the community.

He added that the community had previously approached the Lisa of Ile-Iluji to express its displeasure but alleged that their concerns had not been addressed.

Also speaking, the Chairman of the Civil Liberty Protection Agency in Ondo State, Comrade Dayo Akingbola, urged the state government to prevail on the traditional authorities to respect the customary and native laws governing the selection of the monarch.

Akingbola alleged that that the development could undermine the rights and interests of Bamikemo residents if not addressed on time.

“We are pleading with the Governor of Ondo State, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, to listen to us and tell the imposers to respect the customary law, likewise the native law, and respect the lives and property of Bamikemo people,” he urged.

He also identified Prince Bajewolu as the rightful candidate, alleging that excessive manipulation from Ile-Iluji had affected the community’s efforts to select its preferred monarch.

Another community elder, Abdulahi Balogun, said the protesters were not seeking confrontation but wanted the government to prevent what he described as an injustice against the community.

He said, “The person they want to impose on us is someone we have no connection with. I have not even seen him before in Bamikemo. He is from another town entirely, and they want him to be king over us. We wouldn’t accept that.”

‎In a reaction, the state Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Amidu Takuro, said the government had received a petition from the community on the issue, but it would not interfere in it because it was a family matter.
‎
‎
‎” As far as Ondo State Government is concerned, every chieftaincy matter is addressed with due process in line with the law. We don’t interfere in such matters. We received a petition from the community over the matter, but we can’t interfere because it is a family affair. That is not our responsibility.

“It is the responsibility of the family to identify their son, whom they know is qualified to represent the family and the community at large. So when it comes to chieftaincy selection, we don’t interfere.”
‎
‎

title: Bad COP, Worse COP: What’s Next After Climate Talks Fail?
description: The collapse of marathon climate talks in Turkey has renewed questions about reform of their consensus requirement, and galvanised calls for legal action and ambitious side agreements between like-minded countries.The “conference of the parties” talks, better known as COP31, ended withou
content:
The collapse of marathon climate talks in Turkey has renewed questions about reform of their consensus requirement, and galvanised calls for legal action and ambitious side agreements between like-minded countries.

The “conference of the parties” talks, better known as COP31, ended without agreement and two days over schedule on Sunday, as countries deadlocked on fossil fuels, finance, science and carbon-removing technologies.

It was an ignominious end for an unusual dual-presidency shared by Australia and Turkey, and negotiations chair Chris Bowen, who is Australia’s climate minister, said it was “very disappointing”.

For many observers, the outcome was the inevitable result of a process that has regularly been hamstrung by its insistence on consensus.

“Decision-making that requires every country to agree on every comma is not fit for a climate emergency,” said Nikki Reisch, director of the Center of International Environmental Law’s climate and energy programme.

Bowen identified the same issue.

“The fundamental root of the problem is that when COP was created, for reasons I understand, it was made consensus only,” he said. “That’s a very tough ask.”

‘Significant reform’

Sunday’s collapse has renewed calls for a reform to that consensus-based process, in which any one country, or a small minority, can nix progress.

“It has been clear for years that the COP process is in need of significant reform,” wrote former US vice president Al Gore on X.

He urged a “reinvigorated multilateral process that reflects the latest science and represents the will of the majority of the world.”

But as Bowen noted, “you also need consensus to change consensus” — in other words, all countries would have to agree those reforms.

He described that as a “particular challenge,” although others might characterise it as simply impossible.

The COP31 talks deadlocked over multiple issues, notably whether the so-called cover decision would mention phasing out planet-warming fossil fuels.

Several countries refused a deal without that mention, while others including Saudi Arabia were vehemently opposed to its inclusion.

There were other serious faultlines, including the timing of scientific work from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, and language on carbon capture, a technology championed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised by some as costly and ineffective.

Crucially for developing countries, there was also no progress on finance — the money badly needed to help countries transition energy systems and adapt to the natural disasters climate change is already worsening.

“The fundamental problem for globally agreed climate policy is more starkly obvious than ever: fossil fuel powers will not agree to have their resource wealth devalued, and rich countries won’t provide enough climate finance to the developing world,” said Frank Jotzo, professor of environmental and climate change economics at the Australian National University.

‘Doesn’t replace COP’

Other COPs have ended in failure before, including most recently in 2009.

But for all the forum’s failings, most agree that the COP process remains important for its unique format, bringing together virtually every country in the world and offering equal billing to all.

As a result, few suggest the process should be abandoned, but there are growing calls for alternatives to advance climate change action, including legal suits.

That route is already being pursued, most notably with an International Court of Justice advisory opinion that confirmed states have a binding legal obligation to combat climate change.

“If the negotiations are not delivering what individual states need, then they’ll certainly consider turning to the ICJ and other international courts,” said Harj Narulla, an international lawyer who advised the Solomon Islands at COP31.

Others expect growing interest in agreements made outside the COP process, like the Santa Marta initiative, bringing together countries committed to phasing out fossil fuels.

The process grew out of the COP30 meeting in Brazil, where interested nations sought to bypass a lack of consensus on the issue.

Members held talks earlier this year and agreed some first steps, including an expert scientific panel to advise on pathways.

These “plurilateral processes are growing,” said Jotzo, and more are needed, including on carbon removal technologies and finance for adaptation.

Bowen, too, said he sees the Santa Marta process becoming “increasingly important.”

“Doesn’t replace COP. It’s just another way of doing it,” he added.

The post Bad COP, Worse COP: What’s Next After Climate Talks Fail? appeared first on Channels Television.

title: 2027: Tinubu orders APC leaders to reconcile, mobilise for victory
description:
President Bola Tinubu has directed leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to resolve internal disputes, reconcile aggrieved members and mobilise voters ahead of the 2027 general election.
He also urged party members and supporters to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and work towards
content:
President Bola Tinubu has directed leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to resolve internal disputes, reconcile aggrieved members and mobilise voters ahead of the 2027 general election.

He also urged party members and supporters to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and work towards securing overwhelming votes for the ruling party, warning against complacency.

Tinubu gave the directives on Sunday at a prayer session organised by his extended family at the Yoruba Tennis Club, Onikan, Lagos.

Acknowledging divisions within the party, the president urged its leaders to put aside personal differences, embrace forgiveness and strengthen internal cohesion to consolidate the gains of his administration ahead of the election.

“We must generate enough votes to overwhelm the opponents,” he said, reaffirming his commitment to providing purposeful leadership, strengthening national unity and justice, and building a prosperous country for Nigerians.

He called on party members to return to door-to-door mobilisation, urging them to visit their neighbours and encourage eligible voters to collect their PVCs.

“The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday, but we cannot take it for granted. You must knock on your neighbour’s door, tell them to collect their PVC.

“If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16th and February 6th, and that’s what I want to ask you to exercise,” he said.

Tinubu specifically directed his Special Adviser on Political Matters, Alhaji Ibrahim Kabiru Masari, and former Minister of Defence, Alhaji Abubakar Badaru, who were among those present, to help resolve disagreements within the party.

Apparently reacting to reports of a disagreement between Katsina State Governor Dikko Umar Radda and Masari, the president ordered his aide to return home and reconcile with the governor.

“Alhaji Kabiru Masari, go back home and reconcile with everybody. That is the president’s order. When you finish that, you move to Jigawa.

“You move to other places and reconcile them, beg them because we have to reconcile and every anger must dissipate and evaporate,” Tinubu said.

He gave a similar directive to Badaru, a former governor of Jigawa State, urging him to work towards resolving differences among party leaders.

The president cited his own experience of overcoming political disagreements in 2021 and 2022, recalling his relationship with the late former President Muhammadu Buhari as an example of the importance of forgiveness and political accommodation.

“I had my own anger in 2021-22. I can invoke the memory of Muhammadu Buhari. When he called me, I said, okay, he said you are the coordinator, co-chairman of the campaign. I said, oh yeah. I had my own anger full of hurt feeling, but I let go,” he said.

Tinubu also drew lessons from his recent visit to the Holy Ka’aba, emphasising faith, gratitude and forgiveness. He urged supporters to extend to others the forgiveness they seek from Almighty Allah.

He warned that political disagreements should not undermine the party’s collective objectives, calling on members to replace resentment with reconciliation and renewed commitment to its electoral ambition.

On voter participation, the president expressed concern about low turnout in Lagos State, questioning why an electorate of about seven million registered voters would produce only between 100,000 and 200,000 votes.

“Even if you win, and you say a win is a win. No. You have to generate the maximum. And to all of you, it’s not anger. Anger will not do it,” he said.

He urged party supporters to encourage eligible Nigerians to register and collect their PVCs, stressing that electoral victory should be backed by substantial voter participation.

Recalling his use of the Emilokan slogan during the 2022 presidential campaign, Tinubu told supporters that the responsibility of securing his re-election now rested with them.

“It is now your turn (Eyinlokan) to make the re-election possible,” he said, appealing to Lagos residents to turn out in large numbers on election day.

The president also recalled the economic difficulties and cash shortages that preceded the 2023 general election, attributing his eventual victory to divine intervention and the determination of his supporters.

“We invoked the spirit of Almighty Allah and said, ‘Kun faya kun (Be, and it becomes). It got us there, and we have the presidency. Allah gives power to whom he wants, and he takes it from whoever he wants,” he said.

Tinubu thanked members of his family for their longstanding prayers and support throughout his political career. He also urged young Nigerians to embrace leadership responsibilities and contribute to national development.

Reaffirming his administration’s commitment to infrastructure and development, he expressed confidence in the country’s ability to overcome its challenges through collective effort.

“We can do it in this country. There’s nothing we cannot do. Nothing. Go to Abuja, we’ve moved mountains. In Lagos, we’ve tamed the Atlantic. In Abuja, we’ve moved mountains to give way to development. Nothing we cannot do if we put our heart at it,” he added.

The president thanked the organisers and clerics who prayed for him, his administration and the country.

The session was attended by Muslim and Christian clerics, as well as the governors of Lagos, Kaduna, Kwara, Ogun and Imo states.

Other dignitaries included the National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu; Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila; Lagos Deputy Governor, Kadiri Obafemi Hamzat; Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa; and Speaker of the Lagos State House of Assembly, Mudashiru Obasa.

Also present were the Grand Chief Imam of Lagos, Sheikh Sulaimon Oluwatoyin Abou-Nolla; Chairman of the Board of Trustees of the Coalition of Northern Groups, Dr Nasturah Ashir Sharriff; members of the Tinubu family and party faithful.

Earlier, Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu described the president as an epitome of justice, fairness, equity and inclusive governance, saying the virtues were essential to building a united, peaceful and prosperous Nigeria.

Badaru said Northerners appreciated Tinubu’s support for Buhari’s victories in the 2015 and 2019 presidential elections. He urged voters in the region to reciprocate the gesture and support Tinubu’s re-election bid.

The chairman of the occasion, 94-year-old elder statesman Alhaji Lateef Femi Okunnu, pledged to canvass votes for the president and vote for him on January 16, 2027, saying Tinubu had done enough to merit another term.

Okunnu also stressed the need for justice and praised the administration’s focus on the economy and infrastructure, particularly the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, as well as efforts to strengthen the naira and foreign reserves.

In their vote of thanks, representatives of the Tinubu family, Alhaji Rafiu Tinubu and Alhaja Iyalode Bintu Tinubu, thanked God for the family’s blessings and urged Nigerians to support the president’s efforts to deliver the dividends of democracy.

Chairman of the Lagos State Government House Chapel, Rev. Honsu Oluremi, referenced the Bible and urged Nigerians to pray for the success of their leaders.

The coordinator of the prayer session, Abou-Nolla, also read from the Qur’an and prayed for Allah to grant the president success and good health.

The post 2027: Tinubu orders APC leaders to reconcile, mobilise for victory appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

content:
By Ayobami Okerinde

FIFA President Gianni Infantino has said Nigeria is not currently ready to host the FIFA World Cup, citing the need for investment in stadiums, hotels, airports and transportation infrastructure.

Infantino made this known in an interview with Arise News, aired on Monday, while responding to a question on what it would take for a country like Nigeria to host the global football tournament.

“The key for hosting a World Cup is the infrastructure: the stadiums, hotels, airports, and transportation. This is where the investment is really necessary.

“A country like Nigeria has the resources, the passion, and the will as well,” he said.

Asked directly whether Nigeria was ready to host the World Cup, Infantino replied, “Today, no, but tomorrow, why not?”

Nigeria last hosted a FIFA tournament in 2009, when it staged the FIFA U-17 World Cup, with Switzerland defeating Nigeria’s Golden Eaglets 1-0 in the final in Abuja.

On his 10-year tenure as FIFA president, Infantino said the organisation’s growth and the expansion of its competitions reflected the work done under his leadership.

“I think the facts really speak quite loudly here. Speak for themselves. The organisation of the World Cups, both for men and women, increasing the number of teams, increasing the competitive balance of these competitions, and the revenue news.

“Of course, we moved from a bit more than 5 billion before I arrived to 16 billion in this last cycle,” he said.

He added that football and FIFA had continued to grow, saying such progress required hard work and strict compliance with established standards.

“Football is growing. FIFA is growing. This is not possible if you don’t work hard, but also if you don’t work in compliance with the highest possible standard,” he said.

Infantino was in Nigeria over the weekend, where on Friday, he inspected the remodelled Warri City Stadium alongside FIFA Secretary-General Mattias Grafström.

During the visit, he praised Nigeria’s football heritage and the country’s contribution to the global game, noting that some of the world’s finest players came from Nigeria, particularly Delta State.
“This stadium is fantastic. It has everything you can dream of. I just would love to wear some shorts and kick the ball. So as soon as it’s completely finished, we’d come and play games with all these great Nigerian legends who come from this region.

“Not just in Nigeria, but some of the best players in the world come from Nigeria, come from Delta State,” he said.

At the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football in Abuja, on Saturday, Infantino also commended President Bola Tinubu for investments in sports facilities, saying they demonstrated the country’s commitment to its young population.

“He is doing, together with all of you, fantastic job here in Nigeria, showing that you are a country projected into the future,” he said.

He added, “The investments done in sports facilities, infrastructure, show that you believe in your youth, in the young girls and the young boys of Nigeria.”

Infantino is seeking re-election as FIFA president in 2027, with France’s Philippe Diallo and Japan’s Kozo Tashima emerging as potential challengers, while Nigeria has endorsed his bid for another term.

title: 2027: INEC selects 17,676 polling units for BVAS mock exercise
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has released the list of polling units selected for its nationwide mock accreditation and result upload exercise scheduled for Saturday, November 28, ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The commission said the exercise would take place in only two polli
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has released the list of polling units selected for its nationwide mock accreditation and result upload exercise scheduled for Saturday, November 28, ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The commission said the exercise would take place in only two polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 Registration Areas, with the selected locations published on its website for stakeholders and members of the public.

INEC announced the development in a post on its X handle on Monday, disclosing that the exercise would run from 8:30am to 2:30pm.

PUNCH had earlier reported that the commission fixed November 28 for the nationwide mock accreditation and voting exercise as part of its preparations for the 2027 general elections.

In its latest announcement, INEC said, “INEC will conduct a nationwide Mock Accreditation and Result Upload Exercise using the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) on Saturday, 28 November 2026, from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m.

“The exercise is designed to test BVAS functionality, assess accreditation procedures and identify possible technical issues ahead of the 2027 General Elections.

“It will take place in two Polling Units in each of the 8,838 Registration Areas nationwide.”

The commission also directed the public to its website to access the selected polling units, adding, “Find the selected Polling Units here. https://x.com/inecnigeria/status/2124790206897193069?”

PUNCH Online reports that the figure is arrived at by multiplying the 8,838 Registration Areas nationwide by the two polling units selected in each area, bringing the total to 17,676 polling units.

The announcement comes amid concerns raised by political stakeholders over the preparation time for the exercise.

The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council had, on November 18, asked INEC to postpone the exercise, alleging that the short notice given to political parties would undermine their participation.

It described the timeline as inadequate and demanded that the commission postpone the exercise to allow political parties to prepare and participate meaningfully.

INEC’s mock exercise is expected to test the performance of BVAS and the commission’s electronic result upload procedures ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Meanwhile, in a separate report, INEC said that about 75 to 80 per cent of its Bimodal Voter Accreditation Systems, which amounts to 186,277 devices, has already been deployed to states ahead of the 2027 general elections.

title: 2027: Lagos APC declares ‘Awa lo kan’ movement for Tinubu
description:
The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has declared that President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027 has evolved from a personal political ambition into a collective national movement, describing the emerging slogan as “Awa lo kan” (It is our turn).
The party said the pol
content:
The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has declared that President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027 has evolved from a personal political ambition into a collective national movement, describing the emerging slogan as “Awa lo kan” (It is our turn).

The party said the political movement that began with Tinubu’s “Emi lo kan” declaration ahead of the 2023 presidential election had grown into a shared determination among Nigerians to consolidate the administration’s reforms and sustain the country’s progress.

Lagos APC spokesman, Seye Oladejo, stated this on Monday, saying the shift reflected a defining moment in the country’s political evolution, where an individual aspiration had become a collective conviction.

According to him, the emerging “Awa lo kan” sentiment represents Nigerians’ desire to protect the gains of the Tinubu administration, expand opportunities and sustain the country’s journey towards prosperity.

The party said the movement was about ordinary Nigerians, including traders seeking a more predictable business environment, farmers demanding improved productivity, graduates looking for jobs, entrepreneurs seeking affordable credit and families hoping for a better standard of living.

“It is about a nation that cannot afford the luxury of abandoning its reform trajectory halfway through the journey,” the party stated.

The Lagos APC maintained that Tinubu had demonstrated the political will to confront structural challenges that previous administrations either postponed or approached with hesitation.

It cited the removal of the fuel subsidy, unification of the foreign exchange markets and investments in infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture and economic diversification as some of the administration’s major interventions.

However, the party acknowledged the difficulties associated with the reforms, saying responsible leadership required recognising both the present challenges and the opportunities being created for the future.

“The answer to transitional difficulties cannot be a reckless return to the policies and practices that contributed to the problems being collectively overcome,” it said.

On national unity, the APC said Tinubu’s administration had demonstrated commitment to inclusivity and representation across geopolitical zones, ethnic groups, religious affiliations, gender and social backgrounds.

It argued that the administration’s appointments, policies and development priorities reflected an understanding that Nigeria’s strength lay in its diversity and that national progress must benefit all sections of the country.

The party also pointed to efforts to strengthen the nation’s security architecture, saying interventions, operational improvements and increased investments in security capabilities represented steps in the right direction, despite continuing challenges in some parts of the country.

It accused the opposition of dismissing every improvement and amplifying setbacks for political purposes, insisting that national security should not be reduced to partisan propaganda.

The Lagos APC said the growing “Awa lo kan” campaign was not a call for complacency but an appeal for collective responsibility and commitment to sustaining the administration’s policies.

It added that the benefits of governance should be consolidated and expanded rather than sacrificed through what it described as political experimentation.

The party also criticised opposition groups, accusing them of being preoccupied with internal disagreements, ideological differences, leadership disputes and struggles for political relevance.

“Their inability to present a coherent, credible and sustainable alternative to the Renewed Hope Agenda makes their promises of an imaginary national rescue increasingly unconvincing,” it said.

The APC argued that Nigerians deserved more than political rhetoric and criticism, insisting that opposition parties should explain what they intended to do differently, how they planned to achieve it and why their proposals should be trusted over the current administration’s reforms.

It described the 2027 presidential election as a contest that would go beyond political parties and personalities, saying it would be a choice between continuity and uncertainty, consolidation and disruption, as well as sustained reforms and a return to what it called unsustainable policies.

“For the Lagos APC, the message is unmistakable: the Tinubu presidency has laid important foundations, and the responsibility before Nigerians is to ensure that these foundations translate into enduring national prosperity,” the statement said.

The party said the transition from “Emi lo kan” to “Awa lo kan” captured the evolution of Tinubu’s political project from an individual declaration into a collective aspiration centred on continuity, opportunity and shared destiny.

“In 2027, it is not simply about giving President Bola Ahmed Tinubu another term. It is about giving Nigeria the opportunity to complete the transformation that has begun.

“It is about our collective future. It is about our shared prosperity. It is about our common destiny. Awa lo kan! Nigeria’s turn to consolidate, progress and prosper,” the Lagos APC stated.

The post 2027: Lagos APC declares ‘Awa lo kan’ movement for Tinubu appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Nothing will stop 750km Coastal Highway – Umahi
description:
By John Alechenu, Abuja



The Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, has reaffirmed President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to completing the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, declaring that nothing will stop the project.



Umahi spoke during an inspection of bridges on Sections 1 and 2 of
content:
By John Alechenu, Abuja

The Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, has reaffirmed President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to completing the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, declaring that nothing will stop the project.

Umahi spoke during an inspection of bridges on Sections 1 and 2 of the highway.

The disclosure was made in a statement by Francis Nwaze, Senior Special Assistant to the Minister, in Abuja on Monday.

He quoted the minister as saying, “Nothing will happen to the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, which passes through the nine coastal states. The President has directed that the project must be completed as envisaged.”

Umahi described the highway as a profitable national investment capable of generating revenue, attracting private investors and unlocking tourism and industrial opportunities.

“We are using concrete, and so we are entitled to carbon credits claim. We are also using solar instead of conventional electricity; we are entitled to carbon credits,” he said.

He added that the superhighway would accommodate tourism facilities, factories, CCTV surveillance and other commercial infrastructure, with private investors already showing interest in recovering costs through investment arrangements.

The minister disclosed that President Tinubu is expected to commission Section 1 this month or early December.

He also clarified that the reconstruction of the East-West Road is an additional commitment by the President and does not replace or affect the Coastal Highway.

He described the ongoing 1,068-kilometre Sokoto-Badagry Road as another major infrastructure undertaking of the administration, stressing that Tinubu is pursuing multiple major projects simultaneously.

Umahi commended the President for the scale of infrastructure development and economic reforms, citing declining inflation, improved foreign exchange access for businesses and the absence of ASUU strikes.

He urged Nigerians, particularly South-East residents in Lagos, to support the President, noting that the administration has delivered significant infrastructure projects to the region.

Meanwhile, Umahi has ordered a three-week nationwide emergency rehabilitation of major federal highways ahead of the festive season and the January 2027 elections.

He directed Zonal Directors, Controllers, Resident Engineers and contractors to return to the field immediately to ensure critical roads are made motorable across all six geopolitical zones.

“I feel so sad that a contractor will be on site doing permanent work, yet some sections of the roads remain impassable. This practice must stop,” he said.

He warned that contractors must not allow motorists to suffer on failed sections while permanent construction continues, directing that damaged portions be excavated and rehabilitated using appropriate materials and asphalt where necessary.

Umahi directed officials to document the exercise, engage contractors, report challenges promptly and restore roads to acceptable motorable conditions within three weeks.

The Minister said the intervention is aimed at easing movement during the festive season, facilitating transportation of goods and services, supporting movement of election materials and strengthening security operations ahead of the 2027 elections.

The post Nothing will stop 750km Coastal Highway – Umahi appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Democrats Win Largest US House Majority In 34 Years — Report
description: Democrats have won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives in more than three decades, after Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina, US media projected on Sunday.The party won full control of both the House and Senate in a sweeping midterm ro
content:
Democrats have won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives in more than three decades, after Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina, US media projected on Sunday.

The party won full control of both the House and Senate in a sweeping midterm rout with a landslide of upsets that delivered a crushing rebuke of President Donald Trump and his Republican Party.

CBS News and NBC News projected Hubbard’s win on Sunday, securing the Democrats a 258th seat in Congress’ 435-member House.

The majority is the largest won by either party since 1992, when Bill Clinton won the presidency, and Democrats won a total of 258 seats.

“House Democrats have just secured the largest majority any party in Congress has held this century. BOOM,” House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said in a post on X.

Sunday’s result came after Foxx requested a recount.

Hubbard said Sunday that he had spoken with Foxx, who “graciously conceded following the results of the recount process.”

“Let me be the first to thank Congresswoman Foxx for her decades of service and countless sacrifices,” he added on X.

The Democratic victory hands the party the power to block Trump’s agenda and investigate alleged corruption for the last two years of his presidency.

The midterm results reflected deep anger over living costs, tariffs and Trump’s war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president.

title: Beyond Performance: Building Organisations That Endure
description: The Executive Director of Black Pelican Group, Adetola Owolabi, has shared her perspective on the relationship between business performance and organizational excellence, noting that the true strength of a business lies not only in the financial results it achieves, but in its ability to sustain hig
content:
The Executive Director of Black Pelican Group, Adetola Owolabi, has shared her perspective on the relationship between business performance and organizational excellence, noting that the true strength of a business lies not only in the financial results it achieves, but in its ability to sustain high standards as its operations, ambitions and responsibilities evolve.

As businesses reflect on the year’s achievements and prepare for new opportunities, consider a question beyond revenue, market share, and growth targets: What truly makes an organisation successful?

The answer lies not only in what a business achieves today, but in its ability to continue delivering results tomorrow, next year, and long into the future.

Many organisations achieve impressive results, yet remain heavily dependent on a few individuals, vulnerable to operational weaknesses or unprepared for the demands of future growth. Financial performance may reveal what a business has accomplished, but it does not always reveal the strength of the institution behind it.

The more important question, therefore, is not whether an organisation is performing well, but whether it is building the capacity to keep performing well.

There is an important distinction between success and organisational strength. Strong performance can be driven by favourable market conditions, exceptional talent or a unique opportunity. Enduring organisations go further. They develop the systems, discipline and shared knowledge that enable success to be repeated, challenges to be overcome and progress to continue regardless of changing circumstances.

As Mrs. Owolabi explains:

“An organisation must look beyond the results it has achieved and consider what they reveal about its underlying capabilities. The objective is not simply to succeed, but to build an institution that understands what makes it successful and has the discipline to sustain it.”

Achieving this requires more than ambition. It demands intentional leadership. Excellence must be reflected in the way decisions are made, resources are allocated, people are developed and performance is measured. It becomes part of an organisation’s culture, influencing not only what it does, but also what it refuses to do.

Every business faces moments when commercial opportunities, operational convenience and professional standards pull in different directions. A shortcut may appear attractive. A project may offer immediate financial rewards while creating long-term risks. A profitable opportunity may conflict with the reputation a company hopes to build.

In those moments, character becomes visible.True excellence is not only demonstrated by what an organisation pursues, but also by what it is willing to walk away from. The willingness to decline opportunities that compromise quality, integrity or long-term value often reveals more about an institution than its most celebrated achievements.

According to Mrs. Owolabi:

“The difficult decisions are often the ones that reveal what an organisation truly stands for. It is relatively easy to uphold a standard when doing so comes at little or no cost. The real test is whether that standard remains important when protecting it requires a difficult decision or the willingness to forgo an immediate opportunity.”

Such choices may carry short-term consequences, but they shape something far more valuable: trust. Customers, partners and employees develop expectations based on what an organisation consistently does. Over time, integrity and consistency become part of its identity, while repeated compromises gradually redefine what people expect from it.

This does not mean businesses should pursue perfection or resist change. Adaptability remains essential in a competitive environment. Strategies, products and processes must evolve. What should remain constant, however, is the commitment to delivering quality and creating value.

Equally important is the behind-the-scenes investment. Developing people, strengthening systems, preserving institutional knowledge and addressing recurring weaknesses may not generate immediate headlines, but they create the foundation for long-term success. Organisations that neglect these areas often find themselves repeating avoidable mistakes, relying excessively on key individuals or spending resources fixing problems that could have been prevented.

Viewed this way, excellence is not a luxury. It is a practical business advantage. It enables organisations to use their people, knowledge and resources more effectively, creating better outcomes for customers and stronger results over time.

Ultimately, the goal is not simply growth, nor success measured only by immediate rewards. The goal is to build institutions whose ambitions match their capabilities, whose decisions reflect their values, and whose achievements are sustainable because they rest on strong foundations.

For leaders looking to build lasting organisations, the lesson is clear: invest in the people, systems and principles that make great work repeatable. When excellence becomes a habit rather than an occasional achievement, success stops being an event and becomes a legacy.

The post Beyond Performance: Building Organisations That Endure appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: ‘Tinubu won’t be part of my government’ – Makinde
description:
The presidential candidate of the Action Peoples Movement, Seyi Makinde, has said President Bola Tinubu will not be part of his proposed government of national unity if he wins the 2027 election, citing an agreement he claimed the President failed to honour before the 2023 polls.
Makinde, however, s
content:
The presidential candidate of the Action Peoples Movement, Seyi Makinde, has said President Bola Tinubu will not be part of his proposed government of national unity if he wins the 2027 election, citing an agreement he claimed the President failed to honour before the 2023 polls.

Makinde, however, said his government would be open to appointing qualified Nigerians from the ruling All Progressives Congress, stressing that political affiliation would not prevent capable individuals from serving.

He made the remarks during an interview on The Rooftop Podcast, where he was asked whether he would accommodate political figures such as former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi and Tinubu in his proposed administration.

“Perhaps not President Tinubu, but there are still decent people in APC as well. I’ll tap them and they are Nigerians,” Makinde said.

When asked why he would exclude Tinubu, the governor referred to his political relationship with the President ahead of the 2023 general election.

Makinde said he had supported Tinubu at the time based on an understanding that an inclusive government would be formed after the election, but alleged that the agreement was not honoured.

“Well, not in that context. I mean, I worked for him in 2023. We agreed on a government of national unity. He did not fulfil it,” he said.

The governor explained that the arrangement was among the issues raised by the PDP G5 governors, who broke ranks with the party’s leadership before the 2023 presidential election.

According to him, the group wanted an administration that would bring together competent people from different parts of Nigeria rather than limit appointments to members of the ruling party.

“We came from the PDP as G5 and we said, ‘Look, this is not going to be a government of APC. It should be a government where you tap people from all across the country. Go to every corner of the country, pick and choose people that can help you know to sort some of this out,’” he said.

To explain his position, Makinde recalled how former military Head of State, General Sani Abacha, brought prominent Nigerians into his government after the annulment of the June 12, 1993 presidential election.

He mentioned former Lagos State Governor Lateef Jakande and businessman Alex Ibru among those appointed, arguing that their inclusion was intended to ease political tensions and accommodate aggrieved groups.

Makinde said he wanted to adopt a similar approach by bringing people with the right skills and experience into government, irrespective of their political backgrounds.

He faulted Tinubu’s approach to appointments, alleging that the President had largely favoured individuals from his political circle.

“Tinubu didn’t do that at all. All his appointees are from Bourdillon,” he said.

The APM candidate maintained that his proposed government of national unity would prioritise competence and national inclusion in selecting people to help address the country’s challenges.

The post 2027: ‘Tinubu won’t be part of my government’ – Makinde appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Thousands Evacuated After ‘Unknown Substance’ Released At UK Concert
description: Thousands were evacuated from a concert at the UK’s largest indoor arena after an “unknown substance” was released and several people reported suffering side effects, police said Monday.Some 12,000 people were attending the Sunday night show by US rapper Don Toliver at the Co-op Li
content:
Thousands were evacuated from a concert at the UK’s largest indoor arena after an “unknown substance” was released and several people reported suffering side effects, police said Monday.

Some 12,000 people were attending the Sunday night show by US rapper Don Toliver at the Co-op Live arena in Manchester, northwest England.

Emergency services were called after “reports of people in the crowd suffering effects from an unknown substance”, said Manchester police, which declared a major incident at the scene.

“Several people were treated on site, and one has been taken to hospital at this time,” Greater Manchester Police’s Steph Parker said, adding that the force was trying to “understand what this substance was”.

The venue, which bills itself as the country’s largest live entertainment arena, said it was working with police to “identify the cause of the incident”.

The regional ambulance service said it assessed more than 50 people at the scene, including some reporting “eye and respiratory symptoms”, with “decontamination” being carried out at the venue.

Toliver, an American singer who has collaborated with musicians Travis Scott and Justin Bieber, is currently on the second leg of his “Nitrous” world tour and scheduled to play in London on Monday.

title: 2027: Tinubu’s ‘Emi lo kan’ becomes ‘Awa lo kan’, says Lagos APC
description:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni



The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress, APC, said the political movement around President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027 has transcended personal ambition to become a collective national mission.



Lagos APC’s spokesman, Seye Oladejo, who made the remark
content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress, APC, said the political movement around President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027 has transcended personal ambition to become a collective national mission.

Lagos APC’s spokesman, Seye Oladejo, who made the remark on Monday, said there has come a defining moment in the political evolution of the nation when an individual’s aspiration becomes a collective conviction, and a personal declaration evolves into a shared national determination.

According to the party, the Tinubu political project has evolved from the “Emi lo kan” declaration that preceded the 2023 presidential election to the emerging “Awa lo kan” sentiment ahead of 2027.

It said the shift reflects a move from an individual ambition to a collective movement of Nigerians committed to consolidating ongoing reforms, protecting the gains made and sustaining the country’s journey towards prosperity.

“It is about the trader who wants a more predictable business environment, the farmer who desires greater productivity, the young graduate looking for meaningful opportunities, the entrepreneur seeking access to affordable credit, the student benefiting from expanded educational financing and the working family yearning for a better quality of life.

“It is about a nation that cannot afford the luxury of abandoning its reform trajectory halfway through the journey,” the party stated.

The Lagos APC also stated that Tinubu’s administration has demonstrated the courage to confront structural challenges that successive governments either postponed or approached with considerable hesitation. From the removal of the fuel subsidy and the unification of foreign exchange markets to ongoing investments in infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture and economic diversification, the administration has embarked on difficult but necessary interventions to reposition Nigeria.

However, it said responsible leadership demands that both the difficulties of the present and the opportunities being created for the future be acknowledged.

“The answer to transitional difficulties cannot be a reckless return to the policies and practices that contributed to the problems being collectively overcome.

“Beyond economics, the Tinubu administration has demonstrated an appreciable commitment to inclusivity and national representation.

“Its governing philosophy cuts across geopolitical zones, ethnic identities, religious affiliations, gender and social backgrounds.

“The administration’s appointments, policy interventions and development priorities reflect an understanding that Nigeria’s strength lies in its diversity and that national progress must be broad-based.

“Equally significant, is the ongoing effort to strengthen the nation’s security architecture. While security challenges remain in certain parts of the country, the interventions, operational improvements and renewed investments in security capabilities represent measurable steps in the right direction.

“The opposition’s determined efforts to dismiss every improvement or amplify every setback cannot erase the importance of the progress being made. National security is too serious an issue to be reduced to partisan propaganda.

“The growing national conversation around “Awa lo kan” is therefore not an invitation to complacency. It is a call for collective ownership, shared responsibility and sustained commitment.

“It is an acknowledgement that the dividends of governance must be consolidated and expanded rather than sacrificed on the altar of political experimentation.”

The Lagos APC, however, said those who once presented themselves as credible alternatives were increasingly consumed by internal disagreements, ideological differences, leadership disputes and what it described as a continuous struggle for political relevance.

“Their inability to present a coherent, credible and sustainable alternative to the Renewed Hope Agenda makes their promises of an imaginary national rescue increasingly unconvincing.

“Nigerians deserve more than recycled political rhetoric, emotional grandstanding and opportunistic criticism, the party added.

“They deserve a clear understanding of what the opposition intends to do differently, how it intends to achieve it and why its proposed alternatives should be trusted over an administration already undertaking difficult but consequential reforms.

“The 2027 presidential election will consequently be more than a contest between political parties and personalities, the statement said.

“It will be a referendum on continuity versus uncertainty, consolidation versus disruption, and the courage to pursue necessary reforms versus the temptation to retreat into familiar but unsustainable comfort zones.

“For the Lagos APC, the message is unmistakable: the Tinubu presidency has laid important foundations, and the responsibility before Nigerians is to ensure that these foundations translate into enduring national prosperity.

“The transition from “Emi lo kan” to “Awa lo kan” captures this political evolution perfectly, the party said. What began as one man’s declaration has become a collective aspiration. What was once a personal ambition has evolved into a national conversation about continuity, opportunity and shared destiny.

“In 2027, it is not simply about giving President Bola Ahmed Tinubu another term, the party concluded. It is about giving Nigeria the opportunity to complete the transformation that has begun.

“It is about our collective future. It is about our shared prosperity. It is about our common destiny. Awa lo kan! Nigeria’s turn to consolidate, progress and prosper,!” Lagos APC stated.

The post 2027: Tinubu’s ‘Emi lo kan’ becomes ‘Awa lo kan’, says Lagos APC appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: I oppose politicians’ children working around govt offices – Makinde
description:
Oyo State Governor and Allied Peoples Movement presidential candidate, Seyi Makinde, has said he is opposed to children of political office holders occupying positions around their parents in government offices, insisting that his own children should pursue independent paths.
Makinde stated this in
content:
Oyo State Governor and Allied Peoples Movement presidential candidate, Seyi Makinde, has said he is opposed to children of political office holders occupying positions around their parents in government offices, insisting that his own children should pursue independent paths.

Makinde stated this in an 87-second video clip from an interview on The Rooftop, which he shared on his X account on Monday.

In the interview, the governor said his children preferred to live private lives and make their own contributions to society rather than associate themselves with government offices.

“Of course I am. That’s why you can’t see any of my children, you know, around the government offices,” he said.

Asked whether he considered it inappropriate for children of people in power to work around government offices, Makinde replied, “No, I am totally, totally opposed to it.”

He said he would want anyone who could identify his children in Oyo State to come forward, maintaining that they were pursuing their own paths in life.

“For my children, they are on their own trajectory in life. My own job is to advise them, give them necessary support, and with the way they have been brought up, we know that they will go on to make their own mark in life,” he said.

However, Makinde said he would support his children if they independently decided to venture into politics, although he would not encourage them to do so.

“No, I won’t advise them to go into politics, but if they choose politics, I will support them,” he added.

His comments come amid renewed attention on the participation of children of prominent Nigerian politicians in elective offices ahead of the 2027 general elections.

A September report by The PUNCH, based on an International Centre for Investigative Reporting compilation drawn from Independent National Electoral Commission data, identified several children of former presidents, governors and other influential political figures among those contesting or seeking to retain National Assembly seats in 2027.

Those identified include Iyabo Obasanjo, daughter of former President Olusegun Obasanjo; Yusuf Buhari, son of the late former President Muhammadu Buhari; Bello El-Rufai, son of former Kaduna State Governor Nasir El-Rufai; and Erhiatake Ibori-Suenu, daughter of former Delta State Governor James Ibori.

Children of ex-presidents, governors in 2027 National Assembly race

The trend has also featured in previous PUNCH reports on political dynasties, which documented the presence of children and relatives of influential politicians in the National Assembly and other political offices.

In another part of the interview, Makinde was asked which Nigerian leader, dead or alive, he would want to receive advice from.

He named Nigeria’s first President, Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, saying he would like to understand how the late nationalist navigated the country’s political history and made some of the decisions that continue to affect Nigeria.

“Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe. Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe was there, just at the centre, and he took a decision that we’re battling with six years after,” he said.

Makinde added that he would like to ask Azikiwe how he arrived at such decisions and what informed his actions.

The post I oppose politicians’ children working around govt offices – Makinde appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NDC begins 2027 campaign in Kano, vows LG autonomy
description:
From Desmond Mgboh, Kano
The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has officially kicked off its 2027 election campaign in Kano State, pledging to grant full autonomy to local government councils across the state if elected.
The flag-off, held in Gezawa Local Government Area of the state, drew a large c
content:
From Desmond Mgboh, Kano

The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has officially kicked off its 2027 election campaign in Kano State, pledging to grant full autonomy to local government councils across the state if elected.

The flag-off, held in Gezawa Local Government Area of the state, drew a large crowd of supporters, party leaders and stakeholders from across the state.

Speaking at the event, the party’s governorship candidate, Aminu Abdulsalam Gwarzo, said local government areas had been crippled for too long by excessive control from the state government.

He blamed the state government for poor service delivery, abandoned projects and a lack of development at the grassroots.

He vowed that under an NDC government, local government funds would go directly to the councils, elected chairmen would be allowed to function independently, and rural communities would witness real development in roads, health, education and water supply.

Gwarzo alleged that, despite the N12 billion monthly allocation meant for local governments and collected by the state government in the last three years of the present administration, there was no commensurate development to show for the money.

He said: ‘There are many uncompleted projects here, including a health institution promised to be completed by the governor. People are still battling with poor health services, lack of potable drinking water, and backwardness in our education system.’

‘If elected as the next governor of Kano State in 2027, I promise all our 44 local governments will be autonomous by collecting their monthly allocation directly from the federation account, so that all our LGAs will be financially stable,’ he said.

Gwarzo also condemned President Tinubu’s policies, which he said had brought about the financial hardship being experienced by Nigerians and the current wave of insecurity, especially in the North-West. He urged Nigerians to reject the APC in the upcoming elections.

He called on Nigerians, especially the electorate, to vote for the Obi/Kwankwaso ticket, which he described as the only alternative to the hardship and insecurity brought by APC maladministration.

title: Blue economy: Coastal communities cry for attention, development
description:
From Tony John, Port Harcourt
Creek communities across Nigeria have risen with one voice, demanding special development planning, massive investment in the blue economy and a new spirit of unity summed up in the slogan: “Creek to Creek, We First.”
The demand came in a 30-point communique issued at t
content:
From Tony John, Port Harcourt

Creek communities across Nigeria have risen with one voice, demanding special development planning, massive investment in the blue economy and a new spirit of unity summed up in the slogan: “Creek to Creek, We First.”

The demand came in a 30-point communique issued at the end of the 2026 Creek to Creek Movement Summit, held at the Obi Wali Cultural Centre, Port Harcourt, Rivers State.

Signed by the Founder/Director-General of the Movement, Chief Mike Ebi Ayapaye, and the Deputy Director-General, Engr. Okiemute Onovughakpo, the communique declared that coastal communities are not just remote settlements scattered along the Atlantic coastline, creeks, estuaries and waterways.

They are, it said, the foundation of Nigeria’s economic survival.

Under the Exclusive Economic Zone Act, the communique noted, the creeks connect directly to the Atlantic economy and remain central to the country’s blue-economy ambitions.

The summit, themed “Unity, Prosperity & Renewed Hope Across the Creeks”, was convened to unite creek communities, empower youths and women, attract sustainable development and drive total transformation in the creeks.

In its resolutions, the summit commended governors for building safer water transportation infrastructure and hailed the Federal Government for the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, insisting that it must be delivered as originally planned, alongside the 415-kilometre East-West Road.

On the blue economy, stakeholders said the Niger Delta must no longer watch from the sidelines while others harvest the wealth of its waters. They listed commercial fisheries, aquaculture, fish processing, marine transportation, port services, shipbuilding and repairs, coastal tourism, renewable energy and marine research as areas from which the region must benefit.

They called for a decisive shift from subsistence fishing to modern deep-sea commercial fisheries, backed by technology, cold storage, processing facilities, financing and market access.

They also urged investment in maritime logistics, boat and ship repair, coastal hospitality and eco-tourism.

On the environment, the summit warned that restoration must be treated as an economic priority, not just an environmental duty. It demanded stronger pollution prevention, effective remediation, mangrove restoration, improved waste management, coastal protection and climate adaptation.

It challenged the private sector to recognise that its long-term interest lies in peaceful and prosperous host communities, and called for deliberate policies to attract wealthy sons and daughters of the creeks to invest back home.

The Movement said the future of the creeks must go beyond oil and gas to include modular refineries and gas-based industries such as power generation, mini-LNG facilities, LPG, CNG, petrochemicals and fertiliser production.

The communique recalled that the Willink Commission of 1957 had recommended special treatment for the Niger Delta, lamenting that, nearly seven decades later, the issues raised then remained unresolved.

“Nigeria cannot fully realise its economic potential while neglecting the creeks which help to sustain it,” it stated.

The Movement resolved that “Creek to Creek” must be more than a geographical description. It must stand for inclusion, connectivity and shared prosperity, where waterways are seen not as barriers separating communities, but as natural corridors connecting people, markets, businesses and opportunities.

On education, it demanded stronger links between schools and economic opportunities, with more technical, scientific and vocational training in oil and gas, maritime studies, engineering, fisheries, environmental management, IT, manufacturing and entrepreneurship.

The summit also resolved to establish a Niger Delta Investment and Development Fund to save and invest a substantial portion of collective resources for the future.

The Fund, according to the communique, must pull resources from government, the private sector, communities, corporate organisations and development partners, and operate within a structured capital market framework under the regulatory oversight of the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), in collaboration with the Nigerian Stock Exchange and other relevant financial institutions.

In his welcome address, Ayapaye said the Movement was built on the belief that every creek community deserves to be seen, heard and included in the nation’s progress.

“Creek to Creek means that when one creek rises, all creeks must rise too. When one child succeeds, it becomes a victory for all of us,” he declared.

Delivering the keynote address on “Regional Development, Coastal Development and Sustainable Unity and Peace in the Niger Delta”, Ambassador Godknows Igali said the gathering was a chance to look beyond the daily talk about oil, gas, security and resource control.
