title: Police probe officers over viral pregnant woman video in Abia
description:
The Abia State Police Command has stated that it is aware of and is investigating a viral video circulating on social media depicting an encounter between police officers and a man conveying his pregnant wife, whom he claimed was experiencing contractions and was about to give birth.
In a statement
content:
The Abia State Police Command has stated that it is aware of and is investigating a viral video circulating on social media depicting an encounter between police officers and a man conveying his pregnant wife, whom he claimed was experiencing contractions and was about to give birth.

In a statement issued on Sunday, the command’s Police Public Relations Officer, Maureen Chinaka, said on behalf of the Commissioner of Police that the video shows officers insisting the man be taken to the police station for allegedly driving a vehicle without a registration number plate.

“The command wishes to inform the public that the officers involved have been identified as officers of the Surveillance Patrol and Guard Team attached to Ubakala Divisional Police Station.

“An investigation into the incident has commenced to establish the circumstances surrounding the encounter and determine the extent of responsibility of the officers involved,” the statement read.

Chinaka further stated that preliminary findings indicate the man was driving a vehicle without a displayed registration number plate, contrary to applicable road traffic regulations 39(9) of the National Road Traffic Regulations, which require vehicles to display prescribed identification number plates.

The regulation of vehicle identification, she pointed out, is particularly important in view of prevailing security challenges, including vehicle theft and the use of unidentified vehicles for criminal activities.

The command, however, emphasises that the enforcement of traffic regulations must be carried out with sound judgement and consideration for human welfare.

According to the statement regarding the man’s claim that his wife was experiencing labour contractions and was about to give birth, “preliminary information indicates that she is fine and has not given birth as at the time of this release at 7.47 pm on Sunday.

“Furthermore, no medical evidence or documentation has so far been presented to substantiate the claim of imminent delivery. Nevertheless, the command maintains that the circumstances required the officers to exercise appropriate judgement, empathy and consideration for the welfare of the pregnant woman.”

The command regretted that while the officers were carrying out their official duties, “their apparent failure to demonstrate sufficient empathy towards the pregnant woman is strongly frowned upon by the command.”

The outgoing Commissioner of Police, AIG Wilfred Afolabi, reiterated that the Nigeria Police Force, in line with Section 4 of the Nigeria Police Act, is statutorily mandated to prevent and detect crime, protect lives and property, maintain law and order, uphold the rights of citizens and provide necessary assistance to persons in distress.

He further emphasised that the discharge of police duties must be guided by professionalism, empathy, restraint and respect for human dignity.

The CP, therefore, warned that while the command will not relent in enforcing extant laws and taking appropriate action against offenders, such responsibilities must be discharged with humanity, consideration and professionalism.

He advised members of the public to remain law-abiding and ensure compliance with vehicle registration and other applicable traffic regulations, as he also assured the public that the investigation will be thorough while appropriate disciplinary measures will be taken where misconduct is established.

The post Police probe officers over viral pregnant woman video in Abia appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: African players in Europe: Mixed fortunes for Nigerian Awoniyi
description:
Nigerian Taiwo Awoniyi scored for Coventry City and later had to be substituted after collapsing in a Premier League victory over Crystal Palace at the weekend.



AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues:



ENGLAND



TAIWO AWONIYI (Coventry City)



The striker s
content:
Nigerian Taiwo Awoniyi scored for Coventry City and later had to be substituted after collapsing in a Premier League victory over Crystal Palace at the weekend.

AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues:

ENGLAND

TAIWO AWONIYI (Coventry City)

The striker scored his third goal for Coventry in a 3-2 win against bottom club Palace, but his afternoon came to a bizarre premature end. Awoniyi netted in the fifth minute with a close-range finish into the far corner from Jack Rudoni’s pass to put Coventry 1-0 up at the CBS Arena. But the 29-year-old, signed from Nottingham Forest in the close season, was forced to miss the last 45 minutes after going down clutching his leg in pain while the players were lining up to start the second half. Awoniyi had to be helped up off the ground by two Palace players and limped off, forcing bemused Coventry boss Frank Lampard to make an unexpected substitution. Lampard admitted afterwards that Awoniyi felt a slight problem with his ankle from the first half.

SPAIN

YASSIR ZABIRI (Racing Santander)

Moroccan forward Zabiri struck twice in the opening stages to help Santander beat Real Sociedad 3-2 in La Liga. The 21-year-old, on loan from Rennes, climbed to 11 league goals and trails only Raphinha and Kylian Mbappe in the Spanish scoring charts. Zabiri smashed home in the sixth minute for the opener and two minutes later was alert to pinch the ball from Real Sociedad’s goalkeeper and roll it into the empty net for his second.

GERMANY

JUMA BAH (Augsburg)

Sierra Leone and Augsburg centre-back Bah netted his first goal since arriving on a season-long loan from Manchester City in his side’s 3-1 home romp over Mainz in the Bundesliga. With Augsburg 1-0 up, Bah was on the spot to prod a loose ball across the line from a corner to give the hosts their second.

FRANCE

PATRICK ZABI (Paris FC)

Ivorian Zabi opened the scoring just after half-time as second-placed Paris FC hammered lowly visitors Angers 4-0 to lie second in Ligue 1 after 11 rounds, three points behind European champions Paris Saint-Germain. A cross was nodded into the path of the 20-year-old, and he slammed the ball into the net.

BOULAYE DIA (Lorient)

Dia, a 2022 Africa Cup of Nations champion with Senegal, put Lorient ahead away to Rennes in a 1-1 draw between mid-table clubs. Tunisian Montassar Talbi equalised in the final minute of the first half.

title: Borno ADC Alleges Unlawful Arrest, Detention Of Member, Demands Release
description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Borno State has expressed concern over what it described as “unlawful arrest and detention” of its member, Alhaji Muktar, on 21st November, 2026, by non-official security operatives in Gubio Local Government Area of the State.In a Press statement
content:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Borno State has expressed concern over what it described as “unlawful arrest and detention” of its member, Alhaji Muktar, on 21st November, 2026, by non-official security operatives in Gubio Local Government Area of the State.

In a Press statement made available to Channels Television by Bukar Bukar-Petrol, the Director of Communications, ADC Campaign Council in the State, accused the Gubio local government chairman, Mali Bulama-Mali, of allegedly directing repentant Boko Haram members used as security operatives to arrest its member.

“ADC in Borno State Chapter, wishes to draw the attention of the general public and relevant security authorities to disturbing developments involving Hon. Mali Bulama Mali Gubio, Executive Chairman of Gubio Local Government Area, Borno State”

“The party reports that Alhaji Mukhtar, an ADC member and supporter in Gubio Local Government Area, was arrested on 21 November 2026 at approximately 10:00 p.m. by individuals described as repentant Boko Haram members, allegedly acting on the instructions of the Local Government Chairman,” the statement reads in part.

According to Bukar Petrol, “The circumstances surrounding the arrest are particularly disturbing. Alhaji Mukhtar is reportedly still being held, while his exact whereabouts remain unknown to the party and his associates. His wife witnessed the incident and can provide an account of the circumstances surrounding his arrest”

“More seriously, the arrest and continued detention reportedly took place outside recognized police procedures, with no confirmation that he was taken to a police station or formally processed by the appropriate law enforcement authorities.”

The Party demanded the immediate and unconditional release of Alhaji Mukhtar, urgent and independent investigation into the alleged involvement of Mali Bulama Mali Gubio in his arrest and detention.

It also requested the immediate cessation of the alleged use of repentant Boko Haram members as security operatives for intimidation, arrests and detention of citizens, as well as asked for appropriate legal and administrative action against anyone found responsible for the violations.

“We wish to state unequivocally that Hon. Mali Bulama Mali Gubio has no constitutional or statutory authority to establish a personal security outfit, delegate police powers to unofficial individuals or authorize the arrest and detention of citizens outside the law”

The ADC Chapter further reiterated it would not accept the use of public office as an instrument of political intimidation, coercion or unlawful detention, calling on the relevant security authorities to urgently intervene, establish Alhaji Mukhtar’s whereabouts, secure his release and investigate the conduct of everyone involved.

The post Borno ADC Alleges Unlawful Arrest, Detention Of Member, Demands Release appeared first on Channels Television.

title: 2027: Tinubu won’t be included in my national unity govt — Makinde
description:
The presidential candidate of the Action Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has ruled out including President Bola Tinubu in his proposed government of national unity if elected in 2027, accusing the president of failing to honour an agreement they reached ahead of the 2023 election.



Makinde,
content:
The presidential candidate of the Action Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has ruled out including President Bola Tinubu in his proposed government of national unity if elected in 2027, accusing the president of failing to honour an agreement they reached ahead of the 2023 election.

Makinde, however, said he would consider appointing capable members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) into his government, insisting that there were decent people in the ruling party who could contribute to governance.

He stated this during an interview on The Rooftop Podcast, where he was asked whether he would bring former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi and Tinubu into his government if elected.

“Perhaps not President Tinubu, but there are still decent people in APC as well. I’ll tap them and they are Nigerians,” Makinde said.

Asked whether he did not consider Tinubu decent, the governor said his position was informed by his experience working with the president during the 2023 election, when an agreement on a government of national unity was allegedly reached but not fulfilled.

“Well, not in that context. I mean, I worked for him in 2023. We agreed on a government of national unity. He did not fulfil it,” he said.

Makinde explained that the agreement was part of the position taken by the PDP G5 governors, who broke ranks with the party’s leadership ahead of the 2023 presidential election, saying they wanted an inclusive government that would draw competent Nigerians from across the country, irrespective of political affiliation.

“We came from the PDP as G5 and we said, ‘Look, this is not going to be a government of APC. It should be a government where you tap people from all across the country. Go to every corner of the country, pick and choose people that can help you know to sort some of this out,’” he said.

The APM candidate said the idea of a government of national unity was not new, citing the administration of the late military Head of State, General Sani Abacha, as an example of efforts to bring prominent Nigerians into government to ease political tensions.

He recalled that following the annulment of the June 12, 1993 presidential election, Abacha appointed prominent figures, including former Lagos State governor Lateef Jakande and businessman Alex Ibru, to his government.

Makinde said the appointments were intended to calm tensions and pacify aggrieved Nigerians.

“And it’s been done before. After the annulment of the June 12, 1993 elections, and General Abacha came into government, they went and tapped Alhaji Jakande, Alex Ibru, all of those were geared towards bringing down the temperature in the country and ensuring that where there are angry people, they are being pacified,” he said.

He accused Tinubu of failing to replicate such an inclusive approach, alleging that the president’s appointments were largely drawn from his political circle.

“Tinubu didn’t do that at all. All his appointees are from Bourdillon,” Makinde said.

He said his proposed government would instead seek out individuals from different parts of the country who could contribute to addressing Nigeria’s challenges, regardless of their party affiliations.

title: Motorpark takeover: Makinde directs security agencies to be vigilant
description:
Gov. Seyi Makinde of Oyo State has directed security agencies to stay vigilant and protect lives and property ahead of threats of a motorpark takeover by the National Union of Road Transport Workers (NURTW) members on Monday.



This is contained in a statement issued in Ibadan on Sunday by the Spec
content:
Gov. Seyi Makinde of Oyo State has directed security agencies to stay vigilant and protect lives and property ahead of threats of a motorpark takeover by the National Union of Road Transport Workers (NURTW) members on Monday.

This is contained in a statement issued in Ibadan on Sunday by the Special Adviser to the Governor on Media, Dr Suleimon Olanrewaju.

The government said it will not tolerate violence, intimidation, self-help or unlawful takeover of public facilities by any individual or group.

It urged transport stakeholders, including members of the NURTW, to act peacefully and in accordance with the law.

It maintained that no group would be allowed to disrupt public order or threaten the peace of the state.

The state government assured residents, commuters and investors that the state remains peaceful and secure.

The government further clarified that the Court of Appeal judgment only reaffirmed citizens’ constitutional right to freedom of association.

It said the judgment did not confer ownership, control or management of public motor parks on the NURTW.

“Any attempt to use the judgment to demand or effect takeover of parks is a misinterpretation with no basis in law.

“Security agencies have been directed to act decisively against anyone threatening public peace or disrupting economic activities,” it added.

It urged all residents to ignore rumours and unverified social media messages and rely only on official channels, stressing that the state remains safe, secure and open for business.

NAN reports that the union had threatened to take over motor parks across the state in seven days, accusing Makinde’s administration of repeatedly disobeying court judgments recognising its right to manage the parks.

The union said it would begin enforcing the judgments if the state government failed to withdraw its Park Management System from motor parks in the state’s 33 Local Government Areas. (NAN)

title: Real estate experts task Nigerian govts on housing crisis
description:
…demand active market intervention
By Bianca Iboma-Emefu
Real estate professionals have called on federal and state governments to move beyond passive regulation and take deliberate steps to address Nigeria’s widening housing deficit, rising rents and declining public confidence in the property mark
content:
…demand active market intervention

By Bianca Iboma-Emefu

Real estate professionals have called on federal and state governments to move beyond passive regulation and take deliberate steps to address Nigeria’s widening housing deficit, rising rents and declining public confidence in the property market.

The experts, who spoke at the third edition of the CWA Real Estate Academy in Lagos, argued that government must deploy its control over land allocation, title processing, planning approvals, infrastructure and housing incentives to influence market outcomes and make accommodation more affordable.

Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of West Norwood Realty, Alfred Osagie, said the housing crisis required governments to adopt a proactive approach rather than merely react to market developments.

Osagie, a senior real estate surveyor and facility manager, maintained that rising rents were symptoms of deeper structural problems that required a proper understanding of market behaviour, supply gaps and emerging trends.

“Rent is only a symptom. Value is a symptom of the behavioural pattern in the market,” he said, stressing that real estate professionals must understand the factors driving the market and identify gaps that government intervention could address.

He proposed that governments designate specific portions of land exclusively for social housing and provide developers operating in the segment with reduced entry costs, tax incentives and access to cheaper building materials.

He also recommended linking cement manufacturers’ corporate social responsibility programmes to discounted supplies for social housing projects, arguing that such incentives could reduce construction costs and improve affordability for low-income earners.

To prevent abuse, Osagie called for strict residency requirements to ensure that beneficiaries of subsidised housing were genuinely low-income households rather than property investors or individuals who already owned homes.

He further urged Lagos and Ogun state governments to strengthen collaboration on infrastructure development, particularly along their shared boundaries, where growing populations face inadequate transport links and limited access to essential institutions and commercial facilities.

According to him, improved road and rail connectivity would enable more workers to live in relatively affordable communities outside Lagos while maintaining access to employment opportunities in the state.

Also speaking, Akinropo Abraham, a registered estate surveyor and fellow, said neither government nor private developers could independently resolve Nigeria’s housing challenges.

He advocated a coordinated approach that would combine increased housing supply with affordability measures, including the release of properly titled government land, mandatory social housing components in private developments and faster processing of land titles.

Abraham also called on major employers to invest in staff housing, noting that such developments could contribute to the country’s overall housing stock.

Similarly, Akin Opatola identified insecure land titles, inadequate infrastructure and low purchasing power among working Nigerians as major obstacles to housing delivery.

He observed that much of the country’s land remained without secure title documentation, limiting its use as collateral and restricting access to development finance.

Opatola also criticised the practice of selling land before providing essential infrastructure, warning that the disconnect between property development and infrastructure delivery continued to undermine the sector.

He cautioned that without deliberate measures to address these structural weaknesses, housing demand would continue to outstrip supply, putting further pressure on rents and property prices.

Beyond government intervention, the experts identified poor professional standards and inadequate understanding of the real estate value chain as factors contributing to public mistrust.

Senior Operations Administration and Project Lead at CWA, Aramide Olopo, said the industry needed to address the misconception that advertising properties on social media automatically qualified individuals to operate as real estate professionals.

She explained that the academy was designed to expose participants to the different disciplines involved in property transactions and development, including quantity surveying, architecture, town planning, law and project management.

According to Olopo, the programme brings together emerging practitioners and experienced professionals to deepen their understanding of ethics, market intelligence, negotiation, risk management and the legal dimensions of real estate transactions.

She added that technology and artificial intelligence should strengthen professional judgement and operational efficiency rather than replace the expertise required to deliver credible services.

Osagie also called for mandatory periodic ethics training and assessments for members of regulatory institutions, including the Lagos State Real Estate Regulatory Authority (LASRERA), to strengthen accountability and restore public confidence.

He argued that continuous professional development should form an essential part of regulatory oversight, citing the standards maintained by the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors as a model.

The third edition of the CWA Real Estate Academy, held from November 18 to 20, 2026, at the CW Real Estate headquarters in Ikoyi, Lagos, was themed “The Modern Real Estate Playbook.”

The three-day programme brought together professionals from the real estate, investment, legal, construction, technology and business sectors to examine the challenges and opportunities shaping the industry.

Discussions on the first day focused on market realities, property valuation, identifying investment opportunities, deal fundamentals, sales and negotiation.

The second day examined transaction security, legal due diligence, property documentation, professional responsibility and risk management, alongside the growing application of artificial intelligence and digital tools in real estate operations.

The final day addressed business structures, financing, operational systems, customer experience and sustainable growth, including how real estate companies could build organisations capable of expanding beyond their founders.

The programme also featured an interactive session, “Ask Delani,” with CW Real Estate Founder and Director, Delani Adewuyi, who shared insights on leadership, career development, professional reputation and building businesses for long-term value.

Other speakers included Adeniji Adele, Munachi Ejinkeonye, Yemi Stephens, Tope Adekoya, Adekunle Osude, Olamiju Olayemi, Ijeoma Odunukwe, Mehrez Boutros, Oladapo Runsewe, Tola Akinhanmi, Olamide Oshikoya, Ife Bakare, Jonathan Millard, TPL Rasheed Osinowo and QS John Agbezin.

The discussions underscored the need for stronger collaboration between government and private sector operators, improved land administration, infrastructure investment and stricter professional standards.

The experts maintained that addressing Nigeria’s housing crisis would require more than increasing property transactions, insisting that deliberate public policies and responsible industry practices were necessary to expand access to decent and affordable housing.

title: Nigerians need solutions, not presidential pity party, Atiku’s aide tells Tinubu
description:
Phrank Shaibu, media aide to ADC presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, has criticised President Bola Tinubu over remarks that the Presidential Villa in Abuja suffers the same electricity and water shortages faced by ordinary Nigerians.
Tinubu made the remarks on Sunday during a special pray
content:
Phrank Shaibu, media aide to ADC presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, has criticised President Bola Tinubu over remarks that the Presidential Villa in Abuja suffers the same electricity and water shortages faced by ordinary Nigerians.

Tinubu made the remarks on Sunday during a special prayer session organised by members of his family at the Yoruba Tennis Club in Onikan, Lagos.

The event followed his attendance at an All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, the previous day as part of his 2027 re-election efforts.

Tinubu said the Presidential Villa experiences the same infrastructure failures that affect many Nigerians and vowed to address the country’s deficits in power and water supply.

Recounting a recent incident, the president said, “On the Wednesday of last week, I was shaving, and the water went off. And the villa, you won’t know punishment there too. The water went off. So we will correct all this. No light, no water, no electricity, no development. We have just started. We can do it, and we will do it for Nigeria.”

The comments have drawn criticism from opposition figures.

In a post on X on Monday, Shaibu questioned whether the comments amounted to a confession of failure more than three and a half years into Tinubu’s presidency.

He argued that Nigerians did not elect the president to join the ranks of those affected by poor governance, but to fix the problems.

“You cannot preside over a crisis and then seek sympathy from those bearing its consequences.

“Nigerians need solutions, not a presidential pity party. If even Aso Rock is suffering, what exactly is working?” Shaibu said.

He added that Tinubu should stop “mocking” Nigerians and instead own the failures of his administration, describing the president as “the President for now, not a fellow spectator.”

title: ‘Monies Borrowed Are Being Used For Investments, Infrastructure’, Umahi Inspects Coastal Road Bridges
description: The Minister for Works and Infrastructure, David Umahi, has defended the external borrowings of President Bola Tinubu, saying the monies are being invested in the building of infrastructure across the country.Umahi revealed this as he inspected the Coastal Road Bridges on Sunday.According to him, th
content:
The Minister for Works and Infrastructure, David Umahi, has defended the external borrowings of President Bola Tinubu, saying the monies are being invested in the building of infrastructure across the country.

Umahi revealed this as he inspected the Coastal Road Bridges on Sunday.

According to him, the road projects are not the only investments President Tinubu is spending the borrowed monies on, as the Federal Government also has the vision of investing in housing for rentals.

“As far back as six months, section one was already fully completed. Section two, which is about 53 kilometers, is also already completed. It has road architecture such as solar lights, underground drainage, and the walkway.

“So, it’s something that is out of this world in terms of performance, where you have over 200 kilometres plus being done within two and a half years. It’s a performance that no other contractor in Africa has been able to achieve.

“I have bragging rights as the Minister of Works over these projects because I am very proud of them. I have bragging rights for the President because when you are on this coastal way, it is quite relieving.

“Imagine if we can go all the way from Lagos to Calabar on this kind of road. All these roads are investments of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. And when you ask about the monies which are being borrowed. They are being used for infrastructure. They are being used for investment in infrastructure.

“And investors are asking how they can return the investments on this road. But we are still considering their request because we want to install CCTV, we want to rent houses. We want to buy land where we can have a lot of facilities for tourism, factories, and others.

“And these projects are profit-driven for the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

This is as President Tinubu has asked the House of Representatives to authorise FG to access $7.71bn (N10.79 trillion) in external loans already captured in the 2026 Appropriation Act, with Eurobond issuance expected to be a major funding option.

The request was contained in a letter to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, and was read during last Wednesday’s plenary.

Tinubu said the proposed borrowing would help finance part of the Federal Government’s budget deficit and fund projects across critical sectors, including defence, transportation, agriculture, power, education and health.

title: EPL: Chelsea striker Emegha robbed after scoring first goal in Leeds defeat
description:
Chelsea forward Emmanuel Emegha has revealed that he was robbed after the club’s humiliating 4-1 defeat to Leeds United at Stamford Bridge on Saturday.
The 23-year-old Dutch international disclosed the incident in a social media post on Sunday, assuring supporters that he was safe and nobody was inj
content:
Chelsea forward Emmanuel Emegha has revealed that he was robbed after the club’s humiliating 4-1 defeat to Leeds United at Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

The 23-year-old Dutch international disclosed the incident in a social media post on Sunday, assuring supporters that he was safe and nobody was injured.

Emegha endured a day of mixed fortunes, scoring his first goal for Chelsea before the hosts suffered a heavy defeat to Leeds.

The striker gave Chelsea an early lead with a left-footed effort that went in off the post, but Noah Okafor equalised for the visitors shortly afterwards.

Leeds took control in the second half, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin converting a penalty before Okafor and Brenden Aaronson added further goals to seal an emphatic victory.

The result handed Leeds their first win at Stamford Bridge since 1999.

Despite the disappointing outcome, Emegha celebrated opening his Chelsea account, only to reveal that he was robbed after the match.

“First goal, disappointing result, we’ll be back stronger on Friday,” he wrote on Instagram.

He added: “Unfortunately after the game I was robbed. I am okay and thankfully no one was hurt. Thanks for the messages of support.”

Details of the robbery remain unclear, as the player did not disclose where the incident occurred, what was stolen or the circumstances surrounding it.

Emegha joined Chelsea from sister club Strasbourg in the summer, following a transfer agreement reached a year earlier.

Before moving to Strasbourg, the forward featured for Sparta Rotterdam, Royal Antwerp and Austrian side Sturm Graz.

A hamstring injury delayed his Chelsea debut this season, limiting his involvement to three appearances, including two in the Premier League.

His maiden goal for the London club had provided a rare bright moment in Saturday’s disappointing outing, but the robbery added to his unfortunate experience after the match.

The post EPL: Chelsea striker Emegha robbed after scoring first goal in Leeds defeat appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: 2027: Why Nigerians should prefer me to Obi-Kwankwaso – Makinde
description:
By Bayo Wahab







Oyo State Governor and Allied Peoples Movement (APM) presidential candidate, Seyi Makinde, has explained why Nigerians should choose his ticket with former Kano State governor, Ibrahim Shekarau’s associate Daura, over the Peter Obi-Rabiu Kwankwaso ticket in the 2027 presidential
content:
By Bayo Wahab

Oyo State Governor and Allied Peoples Movement (APM) presidential candidate, Seyi Makinde, has explained why Nigerians should choose his ticket with former Kano State governor, Ibrahim Shekarau’s associate Daura, over the Peter Obi-Rabiu Kwankwaso ticket in the 2027 presidential election.

Makinde cited the historic alliance between the Southwest and North, his experience in governance, youthful energy and plans for national unity as key advantages of his candidacy.

Speaking on The Rooftop Podcast, the governor said the relationship between the two regions had helped Nigeria maintain stability during difficult periods, arguing that his ticket was positioned to sustain that tradition.

“Apart from the traditional Southwest-North alliance, because that alliance has always provided stability for Nigeria in time of crisis in the past,” Makinde said.

He recalled Nigeria’s first military coup, arguing that the Southwest and North had historically played significant roles in efforts to preserve the country’s stability.

“If you even go back to the first military coup in Nigeria, the people that were wasted were basically the north and southwest, because we’re always in the forefront of stability for the country, and that is what we have brought to the table,” he said.

Makinde also pointed to his performance in Oyo State and what he described as the youthful energy of his ticket, saying his administration’s achievements and commitments could be measured against documented promises.

He said his political agenda was designed to allow Nigerians hold him accountable for his promises, rather than rely solely on campaign rhetoric.

The APM candidate also outlined his proposed transitional government of national unity, saying it would address Nigeria’s political and security challenges through a broader national consensus.

Makinde said he was willing to lead such a transition but would not remain in office to benefit from its eventual outcome, arguing that doing so could compromise his decisions.

“I can lead it, but I will not be a beneficiary of the outcome because if I’m looking at myself benefiting from that outcome, it may cloud my judgment and also block how I will take that decision,” he said.

He said the proposed arrangement was necessary because insecurity and other problems affecting Nigeria were not confined to any particular region.

“And a government of national unity, because, you know, you look at insecurity and things fueling it all around the country. It’s not limited to any area,” Makinde said.

title: Kwankwaso broke APC defection pact with Tinubu — Abba
description:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo



Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, has accused his former political mentor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, of reneging on an agreement to defect to the All Progressives Congress (APC) after the 2023 governorship election.







Yusuf, who made the allegation in an inter
content:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo

Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, has accused his former political mentor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, of reneging on an agreement to defect to the All Progressives Congress (APC) after the 2023 governorship election.

Yusuf, who made the allegation in an interview with BBC Hausa, said Kwankwaso personally asked him to approach President Bola Tinubu and assure him that they would join the APC if the President did not interfere in the legal battle over the Kano governorship election.

The governor said the agreement was reached after the 2023 election, when his victory over the APC candidate, Nasiru Yusuf Gawuna, was being challenged in court.

According to Yusuf, Kwankwaso initiated the arrangement and asked him to swear by the Holy Qur’an that they would return to the APC if the judicial process was allowed to run its course without interference.

“Kwankwaso himself sent me to Tinubu and asked me to tell him that we had made that promise. He even wanted me to swear by the Holy Qur’an that if God granted us victory, we would all come together,” Yusuf told the BBC.

He said he honoured the agreement and subsequently assured Tinubu of their intention to defect.

Yusuf added that Kwankwaso also held several meetings with the President and sent delegations to discuss the proposed political realignment.

The governor, who formally defected from the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) to the APC on January 26, 2026, insisted that he did not betray his former political benefactor but fulfilled an agreement that Kwankwaso later abandoned.

He also dismissed suggestions that his defection was a political arrangement aimed at weakening the opposition or distracting the public, maintaining that Kwankwaso was aware of the discussions and arrangements leading to the move.

Yusuf, however, said some remarks allegedly made by Kwankwaso shortly after he had assured Tinubu of their planned defection undermined the arrangement.

He said the comments were communicated to the President and reportedly did not go down well with him.

On his relationship with Kwankwaso since their political separation, Yusuf said they had occasionally communicated, adding that he sometimes sent messages to greet his former mentor.

He declined to discuss publicly allegations that Kwankwaso had exerted undue influence over his administration or prevented him from exercising his responsibilities as governor, saying such matters were better left outside the media.

Marital crisis

The governor also spoke about the reported marital crisis between him and his wife, Zainab Musa Kwankwaso, a niece of the former Kano governor.

Yusuf said their marriage, which began about 20 years ago, produced children, but difficulties eventually emerged in their relationship.

He alleged that his wife’s belongings were removed from his residence and that she was taken away without his knowledge.

According to him, he had remained silent about the development and even assured their children that their mother would return home, only to learn later that she had instituted divorce proceedings against him at a court in Abuja.

The governor expressed disappointment over the development, alleging that his wife was taken from his residence without his consent before he was served with court documents.

He said he had evidence and detailed information about what transpired but would not disclose everything publicly, expressing hope that the matter could still be resolved amicably.

Security challenges

Speaking on the challenges of governing Kano State, Yusuf identified insecurity, particularly street gang activities, phone snatching and armed attacks on residential buildings, as his biggest headache.

He also claimed that his previous position as governor of an opposition party made it difficult for him to secure the cooperation of security agencies.

“I suffered considerably because I could not get the cooperation of security agencies,” he said.

Yusuf, however, maintained that his defection to the ruling APC had improved cooperation with the Federal Government and security agencies.

He further identified the legal battle over the 2023 governorship election, which eventually reached the Supreme Court, as one of the most difficult experiences of his first year in office.

The governor, however, said his administration had also recorded achievements in governance.

The post Kwankwaso broke APC defection pact with Tinubu — Abba appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Australian music icon Molly Meldrum passes away at 83
description:
Australian music icon Molly Meldrum has died at the age of 83 following a prolonged illness.
The veteran music promoter and broadcaster, whose real name was Ian Alexander Meldrum, died peacefully at a hospital in Melbourne in the early hours of Monday, according to a statement released by his family
content:
Australian music icon Molly Meldrum has died at the age of 83 following a prolonged illness.

The veteran music promoter and broadcaster, whose real name was Ian Alexander Meldrum, died peacefully at a hospital in Melbourne in the early hours of Monday, according to a statement released by his family.

Meldrum was widely recognised for his major contributions to the growth of Australia’s music industry over several decades.

He played an important role in promoting local music talents, including INXS and Kylie Minogue, while also helping to bring international music stars such as ABBA to Australian audiences.

Affectionately known as ‘the Guru’, he became a household name through his energetic personality, distinctive Stetson hat and remarkable contribution to music broadcasting.

title: US midterms: Democrats secure biggest House majority in 34 years
description:
Democrats have won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives in more than three decades, after Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina, US media projected on Sunday.
The party won full control of both the House and Senate in a sweeping midterm r
content:
Democrats have won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives in more than three decades, after Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina, US media projected on Sunday.

The party won full control of both the House and Senate in a sweeping midterm rout with a landslide of upsets that delivered a crushing rebuke of President Donald Trump and his Republican Party.

CBS News and NBC News projected Hubbard’s win on Sunday, securing the Democrats a 258th seat in Congress’ 435-member House.

The majority is the largest won by either party since 1992, when Bill Clinton won the presidency and Democrats won a total of 258 seats.

“House Democrats have just secured the largest majority any party in Congress has held this century. BOOM,” House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said in a post on X.

Sunday’s result came after Foxx requested a recount.

Hubbard said Sunday that he had spoken with Foxx, who “graciously conceded following the results of the recount process.”

“Let me be the first to thank Congresswoman Foxx for her decades of service and countless sacrifices,” he added on X.

The Democratic victory hands the party the power to block Trump’s agenda and investigate alleged corruption for the last two years of his presidency.

The midterm results reflected deep anger over living costs, tariffs and Trump’s war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president.

AFP

content:
Chelsea forward Emmanuel Emegha has disclosed that he was robbed following the club’s disappointing 4-1 defeat to Leeds United at Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

The 23-year-old revealed the incident in a social media post on Sunday, assuring fans that he was safe and that nobody was injured during the robbery.

Emegha had a mixed experience during the match, despite Chelsea’s heavy defeat, as he scored his first goal for the club.

The forward gave Chelsea an early lead with a left-footed effort that went into the net after hitting the post, but the hosts eventually suffered a 4-1 loss to Leeds United.

However, Noah Okafor quickly equalised for Leeds before the visitors took control in the second half.

A Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty and further goals from Okafor and Brenden Aaronson completed a convincing victory for Leeds, securing their first win at Stamford Bridge since 1999.

Despite the heavy defeat, Emegha had a personal milestone to celebrate after opening his Chelsea account.

Unfortunately, the forward later revealed that he had been robbed after the match.

“First goal, disappointing result, we’ll be back stronger on Friday,” he wrote on Instagram.
“Unfortunately after the game I was robbed. I am okay and thankfully no one was hurt. Thanks for the messages of support.”

Details of the robbery remain unclear, with no information provided about where the incident occurred, when it happened or what was stolen.

Emegha joined Chelsea from sister club Strasbourg in the summer, with the transfer agreement having been arranged a year earlier.

The Dutch international previously played for Sparta Rotterdam, Royal Antwerp and Austrian side Sturm Graz before moving to Strasbourg.

However, a hamstring injury delayed his Chelsea debut this season, limiting him to just three appearances for the club, including two in the Premier League.

His first goal against Leeds had offered a rare bright spot in a difficult afternoon for Chelsea, but the robbery added another unfortunate incident to an already disappointing day.

title: 26.3m People living with HIV in Africa — WHO
description:
By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja



The World Health Organisation (WHO) has estimated that 26.3 million people are living with HIV in Africa in 2026, with 21.7 million currently receiving antiretroviral therapy.







The WHO Regional Director for Africa, Dr Mohamed Janabi, disclosed this on Monday in a m
content:
By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja

The World Health Organisation (WHO) has estimated that 26.3 million people are living with HIV in Africa in 2026, with 21.7 million currently receiving antiretroviral therapy.

The WHO Regional Director for Africa, Dr Mohamed Janabi, disclosed this on Monday in a message to mark the 2026 World AIDS Day, observed annually on December 1.

Janabi said that despite significant progress in the fight against HIV, including declining new infections in several countries and improved access to treatment, millions of people across the continent still faced barriers to essential prevention and healthcare services.

He said the African Region continued to bear the greatest burden of the HIV epidemic, stressing the need to accelerate equitable access to prevention, testing, treatment and care to end AIDS as a public health threat.

This year’s World AIDS Day theme, “Ending AIDS starts with access”, highlights the importance of ensuring that scientific breakthroughs and available medical interventions reach everyone who needs them.

According to Janabi, access to HIV prevention empowers individuals to protect themselves and their loved ones, while testing enables people to know their status and seek treatment promptly.

He added that access to treatment allows people living with HIV to lead long and healthy lives, while confidential healthcare services free from stigma and discrimination ensure that patients receive care with dignity.

However, he identified distance, transportation costs, medicine stock-outs, stigma, punitive laws and gender inequalities as major obstacles preventing many people from accessing HIV services.

He warned that these barriers could result in undetected infections, delayed treatment and missed opportunities to prevent further transmission.

Janabi noted that countries across the African Region had introduced ambitious HIV programmes, including differentiated service delivery, integration of HIV services into primary healthcare and stronger community-based health systems.

He said countries were also preparing to introduce new HIV prevention tools, but emphasised that such interventions must be affordable and accessible to all.

Looking ahead to 2030, the WHO regional director called on governments to sustain investments in HIV prevention, testing, treatment and care while addressing the structural and social barriers preventing people from accessing essential services.

He also urged development partners to support countries in making new HIV prevention tools widely available, particularly in underserved communities.

“People living with HIV have helped lead this response from the beginning. Their experience must continue to guide the decisions we make about how and where care is provided,” he said.

Janabi said the progress recorded over the years demonstrated what could be achieved when access to lifesaving healthcare was prioritised.

“On this World AIDS Day, let us remember how much has changed because people insisted that lifesaving care should be within everyone’s reach. We owe it to those we have lost, and to those living with HIV today, to carry that work forward,” he said.

He urged stakeholders to ensure that people could protect their health, receive timely diagnoses and obtain the medicines they needed, saying this would bring the continent closer to ending AIDS as a public health threat.

The post 26.3m People living with HIV in Africa — WHO appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Kipit Asset Management Appoints Mr. Luke Ofojebe, CFA, as Acting Managing Director
description: As part of its strategic positioning, Kipit Asset Management Limited (formerly Fortuna Capital Limited), a Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) licensed Fund & Portfolio Management Company, has appointed Mr. Luke Ofojebe, CFA, as its Acting Managing Director, with effect from 20 November 2026. T
content:
As part of its strategic positioning, Kipit Asset Management Limited (formerly Fortuna Capital Limited), a Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) licensed Fund & Portfolio Management Company, has appointed Mr. Luke Ofojebe, CFA, as its Acting Managing Director, with effect from 20 November 2026. The appointment is subject to the approval and confirmation of the SEC.

Luke joins Kipit from Zedcrest Group, where he most recently served as Chief Investment Officer (CIO), capping nearly a decade in investment research and portfolio management. His appointment reflects the seriousness with which Kipit is pursuing its strategy: building an asset management firm anchored on deep research, disciplined portfolio management and experienced leadership.

A Research-Led Portfolio Manager

Before becoming CIO at Zedcrest Group, Luke was Head of Research and Portfolio Management at Zedcrest Wealth, the Group’s Asset Management arm, where he led the team that designed and executed the strategies that significantly grew the firm’s assets under management. He managed money market, equity and proprietary portfolios during that time.

Earlier in his career, Luke headed equity research at Vetiva Capital Management and worked as an equity analyst at CardinalStone Partners. Those years gave him a deep, ground-up understanding of Nigerian companies, sectors and capital markets, and they still shape how he invests today.

In the market, Luke is known for a disciplined, evidence-driven approach to portfolio management, a sharp read of macroeconomic and market trends, and the ability to turn that insight into sound decisions for investors. He is a CFA charterholder.

A Statement of Intent

Kipit was built on a simple belief: managing wealth in Nigeria should be simple, transparent and worthy of trust. Attracting a leader of Luke’s calibre is a statement of how seriously the company takes that belief. As Acting Managing Director, Luke will lead Kipit’s engagement with regulators, clients, partners and the wider market, and will work closely with the Board and management to sharpen the firm’s investment offering and widen its reach.

Commenting on his appointment, Luke Ofojebe said:

“Kipit is one of the most exciting stories in Nigerian asset management right now. The ambition is real, and so is the commitment to doing right by investors. I joined because I believe Kipit can set a new standard for how Nigerians build wealth, and I look forward to working with the team, our regulators and our investors to make that happen.”

The Board of Kipit Asset Management welcomes Luke and looks forward to the value he will bring to the company and its investors.

About Kipit Asset Management

Kipit Asset Management Limited is built to make wealth creation simple, transparent and trustworthy. Licensed by the SEC, the company offers both discretionary and non-discretionary portfolio management services and financial advisory services to individuals, businesses and institutions, to enhance their wealth for today and the future. Kipit prides itself on the security of its clients’ investments, combined with its expertise in delivering competitive returns, and treats every client as a partner in their wealth creation journey, guided by its mission: Build wealth, deliberately.

Phone: +(234) 707 198 5171

Sowore questioned the President’s ability to manage the country’s affairs, arguing that the failure to ma
content:
The 2027 presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, has criticised President Bola Tinubu over the disruption of water supply at the Presidential Villa in Abuja.

Sowore questioned the President’s ability to manage the country’s affairs, arguing that the failure to maintain a basic infrastructure service within the seat of government raised concerns about his administration.

The human rights activist made the remarks in a post on his official X handle on Sunday night.

He said those around Tinubu should have advised him to resign if he could not guarantee a steady supply of water at the Presidential Villa.

He wrote, “You can’t even keep the water running at Aso Rock Villa, and the goons clapping for you must really hate Nigeria.

“They should have told you to your face that if you can’t manage the water supply at Aso Rock, you should resign. Shameless people.”

The criticism followed Tinubu’s disclosure that water supply was interrupted at the Presidential Villa while he was shaving last Wednesday.

The President made the revelation on Sunday during a special prayer session organised by members of his family at the Yoruba Tennis Club, Onikan, Lagos.

Recounting the experience, Tinubu said, “On the Wednesday of last week, I was shaving, and the water went off. And the Villa, you won’t know punishment there too.

“The water went off. So we will correct all this. No light, no water, no electricity, no development.

“We have just started. We can do it, and we will do it for Nigeria.”

The President, however, expressed confidence that his administration would address the challenges, insisting that Nigeria had the capacity to overcome its infrastructure deficits.

Tinubu’s remarks highlighted the infrastructure challenges facing the country, including unreliable electricity and water supply, which he acknowledged also affected the Presidential Villa.

title: NAJA names Weststar Chairman, Benson Uwatse, Nigeria Auto Legend
description:
By Moses Akaigwe
The automotive industry is set to celebrate another distinguished industry leader as the Nigeria Auto Journalists Association (NAJA) has nominated Chief Benson Uwatse, Chairman of Weststar Associates Limited, for the prestigious Nigeria Auto Legend Award at the 19th Nigeria Auto Ind
content:
By Moses Akaigwe

The automotive industry is set to celebrate another distinguished industry leader as the Nigeria Auto Journalists Association (NAJA) has nominated Chief Benson Uwatse, Chairman of Weststar Associates Limited, for the prestigious Nigeria Auto Legend Award at the 19th Nigeria Auto Industry Awards.

The honour places Uwatse in an exclusive league of leading personalities whose contributions have helped shape the growth and development of Nigeria’s automotive industry over several decades.

He becomes the third frontline industry leader to receive the prestigious recognition, following Chief Michael Ade.Ojo, Chairman of Toyota Nigeria Limited, and Dr Cosmas Maduka, President and Chief Executive Officer of Coscharis Group.

The recognition underscores Uwatse’s longstanding involvement in the Nigerian automotive sector and his contributions to the development and representation of the globally renowned Mercedes-Benz brand in the country.

As Chairman of Weststar Associates Limited, the authorised general distributor of Mercedes-Benz in Nigeria, Uwatse occupies a strategic position in the country’s premium and luxury automobile market.

Weststar is responsible for coordinating Mercedes-Benz’s business activities in Nigeria, covering passenger cars, commercial vehicles, trucks and buses, alongside dealer support, marketing, training, genuine spare parts supply, warranties and after-sales services.

The company officially commenced operations in February 2008, assuming responsibility for Mercedes-Benz sales and after-sales operations in Nigeria. Its distribution network and authorised dealerships provide sales and servicing support across different parts of the country.

Uwatse’s association with the Mercedes-Benz brand spans more than three decades, giving him considerable experience in the Nigerian automotive business, particularly in premium vehicle distribution, customer relations and brand development.

His involvement in the business has also included leadership responsibilities in the Mercedes-Benz dealership network, specifically as Managing Director of MB Automobile Services Limited, one of the authorised Mercedes-Benz dealers in Nigeria.

The Nigeria Auto Legend Award is particularly significant because it recognises individuals whose contributions extend beyond routine business operations to the development, growth and advancement of the nation’s automotive industry.

Chief Ade.Ojo, the founder of Elizade Nigeria Limited and Chairman of Toyota Nigeria Limited, was the first recipient of the special industry recognition in 2017, in acknowledgement of his decades of investment, enterprise and contributions to Nigeria’s automobile business.

Dr Maduka, who transformed Coscharis from a modest automobile trading venture into one of Nigeria’s leading indigenous conglomerates, also earned recognition for his remarkable contributions to the automotive sector. Under his leadership, Coscharis Motors secured distribution franchises for several globally recognised automobile brands, including BMW, MINI, Rolls-Royce and Ford.

Uwatse’s emergence as the third recipient further reinforces NAJA’s commitment to celebrating individuals whose leadership, enterprise and industry experience have contributed significantly to the evolution of Nigeria’s automotive landscape.

The 19th edition of the Nigeria Auto Industry Awards, organised by NAJA, is scheduled to hold on Thursday, December 3, 2026, at the Civic Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos.

The annual awards bring together automobile manufacturers, distributors, dealers, policymakers, regulators, industry professionals and other stakeholders to celebrate outstanding achievements and recognise excellence across Nigeria’s automotive and transportation sectors.

The post NAJA names Weststar Chairman, Benson Uwatse, Nigeria Auto Legend appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Daura: Gumi calls for removal of Emirs found guilty of misconduct
description:
Islamic cleric Ahmad Gumi has called for the immediate removal of any Emir found guilty of immoral conduct, saying such action is necessary to preserve the dignity and credibility of traditional institutions.
Gumi made the call in a Facebook post on Sunday amid allegations of sexual assault against
content:
Islamic cleric Ahmad Gumi has called for the immediate removal of any Emir found guilty of immoral conduct, saying such action is necessary to preserve the dignity and credibility of traditional institutions.

Gumi made the call in a Facebook post on Sunday amid allegations of sexual assault against the 92-year-old Emir of Daura, Umar Faruk Umar, by a female foreign tourist who visited his palace in Katsina State.

“Any Emir found guilty of immoral conduct should be removed and replaced immediately to safeguard the integrity, dignity and credibility of the traditional institution,” the cleric wrote.

The controversy followed a video shared by the tourist on Instagram on Saturday, in which she alleged that the monarch sexually assaulted her during a visit to the palace on November 14.

According to her account, she was taken to a room where she and the Emir sat together and began a conversation.

She alleged that the monarch initially held her hand and played with it before hugging and kissing her cheek. She further claimed that he touched her breasts despite her objections.

In the video, the woman could be heard repeatedly telling the Emir not to touch her.

She also expressed shock over the alleged incident, saying she had not experienced sexual assault while walking on Nigerian streets, including in crowded areas.

Meanwhile, Amnesty International Nigeria has urged the Katsina State Government and the Nigeria Police Force to investigate the allegation.

In a statement published on its X account on Sunday, the organisation described the reported incident as disturbing and called for an independent and transparent investigation.

It specifically appealed to Governor Dikko Radda and the police to ensure that the allegation was properly examined and that accountability followed if the claims were established.

Amnesty International also stressed that any proceedings involving the Emir should be conducted fairly and without recourse to the death penalty.

The allegation against the Emir has not been established, while Gumi’s call for removal was expressly directed at traditional rulers found guilty of misconduct.

content:
By Moses Akaigwe

The 30th Anniversary of On The Highway Africa, founded by Julie Chi-Nwoha, took a defining turn recently with a legacy lecture on the theme: “Improving Public Transportation Infrastructure for Road Safety, Security and Sustainability.”

The guest lecturer was Dr. Femi Eguaikhide, Chairman of the Auto and Automotive Components Sectoral Group and Deputy Managing Director of RT Briscoe Nigeria Plc.

Delivering the lecture before chairmen of organisations, captains of industry, executive automotive players, media practitioners, regulators and other stakeholders, Dr. Eguaikhide declared: “Nigeria does not have a road problem. Nigeria has a public transportation infrastructure problem.”

He noted that 30 years ago, when Julie started reporting on the automotive sector, Nigeria was importing fairly used buses and patching potholes. Thirty years later, he said, the country was still doing the same thing, only with more traffic.

“We have celebrated the construction of roads. But we have not celebrated the construction of Transport Systems” he said.

From roads to integrated Transit Infrastructure

Dr. Eguaikhide said Nigeria must stop building roads in silos and start building integrated transport systems, where a Lagos resident can leave Ikorodu, board a CNG-powered BRT bus at the Ikorodu Terminal, connect to the Blue Line at Marina and then connect to last-mile transport, all using one Cowry card, within a terminal that is well-lit, clean and safe.

He noted that dedicated BRT lanes reduce accidents by 30 to 35 per cent globally, a fact he said Lagos had already demonstrated.

He called for a 10-year Dedicated Public Transit Infrastructure Plan involving the development of 1,000 kilometres of dedicated transit lanes and 50 modern interchange hubs across Lagos, Abuja, Kano, Port Harcourt and Enugu, with private-sector participation.

Security is Infrastructure, Not Just Policing

Dr. Eguaikhide said manufacturers, transporters and logistics companies lose over ₦15 trillion annually to insecurity, cargo diversion and unsafe transport corridors.

“You cannot have sustainable transport where a driver is afraid to drive at night, or a woman is afraid to wait at a bus stop at 7pm,” he said.

He argued that security in the next decade would not be about having more checkpoints, which hamper trade, but about providing smart terminals equipped with CCTV cameras and proper lighting, GPS tracking and panic buttons in all commercial buses, cashless fare systems, and a National Secure Corridor Command linking the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), the Police and private fleet owners.

He called for GPS tracking systems and speed limiters to be made mandatory for all public transport vehicles with seating capacities above 18 passengers. He also advocated incentives, including tax rebates for transport operators, to encourage the adoption of cashless ticketing systems.

Sustainability is economics, not environmental Grammar

On sustainability, Dr. Eguaikhide was emphatic that the future of public transportation lay in Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) and electric mobility, not because Paris had said so, but because of the economic benefits.

He explained that while a diesel-powered BRT bus consumes about ₦18 million worth of fuel annually, a comparable CNG-powered bus consumes about ₦6 million, representing an annual saving of ₦12 million per bus. 

For a fleet of 10,000 buses, he said, this would translate into ₦120 billion in savings, with additional benefits in foreign exchange conservation and job creation through gas conversion and local vehicle assembly.

While commending the Presidential CNG Initiative, he called for increased investment in supporting infrastructure, including mother stations, daughter stations and conversion centres, and, most importantly, locally assembled buses.

He proposed a five-year National Public Fleet Renewal Programme involving the assembly of 10,000 CNG and electric buses in Nigeria, supported by a five-year import duty waiver on Completely Knocked Down (CKD) kits and single-digit financing for transport operators.

“Let us build the buses here. Let us build the jobs here,” he said.

In his closing remarks, Dr. Eguaikhide congratulated Julie and On The Highway on their 30th anniversary, noting that the publication had demonstrated that journalism could sustain and contribute meaningfully to the growth of an industry.

“For the next 30 years, let us move from reporting accidents to preventing them,” he said. “If we build Systems, we will improve Safety. If we build Secure Corridors, we will improve Security. If we build CNG/electric fleets, we will achieve Sustainability.”

He added: “The Road to Nigeria’s $1 trillion economy will not be built on more cars. It will be built on better public transport.”

Eguaikhide honoured as Automotive Man of the Year

In a fitting climax to the lecture, Dr. Olorunfemi Eguaikhide was also presented with the Automotive Man of the Year Award at the anniversary celebration.

The award was in recognition of his positive contributions and unwavering commitment to the development of Nigeria’s automotive industry, as well as his transformational leadership in growing the automotive value chain.

Nneji honoured with Legacy Leadership Award

The Chairman of the event, Frank Nneji, OON, was also presented with the Legacy Leadership Award at the anniversary celebration in recognition of his outstanding leadership, enduring legacy and immense contributions to the growth of Nigeria’s transport and automotive industries.

He was honoured alongside other award recipients at the event.

The event also featured the presentation of the Road Safety Champion of the Year Award to Cedric Masters, alongside goodwill messages from industry stakeholders.

The post Nigeria has transport system problem, not road problem – Eguaikhide at On The Highway @ 30 appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Mikano Motors launches Deepal, unveils flagship S09,  advances vision for future of mobility
description:
By Moses Akaigwe
Mikano Motors has officially launched Deepal to the Nigerian automotive market, unveiling the brand’s flagship S09 SUV at a launch event held on recently at its showroom in Victoria Island, Lagos. 
The introduction marks a significant milestone in the company’s automotive journey, b
content:
By Moses Akaigwe

Mikano Motors has officially launched Deepal to the Nigerian automotive market, unveiling the brand’s flagship S09 SUV at a launch event held on recently at its showroom in Victoria Island, Lagos. 

The introduction marks a significant milestone in the company’s automotive journey, bringing a new generation of intelligent mobility technology, contemporary design and advanced vehicle engineering to Nigerian consumers.

Deepal is an intelligent electric vehicle brand within the portfolio of Changan Automobile, one of China’s established automotive manufacturers, while Mikano Motors serves as its authorised distributor in Nigeria.

Through this partnership, Mikano Motors is introducing four models to the market: the flagship S09, alongside the G318, S07 and S05.

Leading the introduction is the Deepal S09, a six-seater, full-sized SUV designed around premium comfort, space and intelligent technology. The vehicle features a dual-motor electric all-wheel-drive system, 485 horsepower and a combined driving range of over 1,100 kilometres.

Its Range Extended Electric Vehicle (REEV) technology uses electric motors as the primary source of propulsion, while an onboard petrol engine functions as a generator to support extended driving range. The S09 also features second-row zero-gravity seating, a 360-degree camera system and advanced driver-assistance technology.

Beyond introducing new vehicles, Mikano Motors is focused on building a comprehensive mobility proposition for Nigerian consumers. Its approach combines access to advanced automotive technology with a strong ownership support structure, including a six-year or 200,000-kilometre vehicle warranty and an eight-year battery warranty for the S09, alongside authorised after-sales servicing, maintenance and technical support. 

This reflects the company’s wider ambition to make contemporary mobility more accessible while giving customers confidence throughout their ownership journey.

The launch also reflected the lifestyle dimension of the Deepal brand, bringing together automotive design, Nigerian fashion and contemporary culture through showcases by local designers, creative installations and a live painting inspired by a Deepal vehicle. Guests also enjoyed an orchestra performance, dance presentations and other live entertainment.

The event, held on Friday, November 13, 2026, brought together leadership from Mikano International, Mikano Motors and Changan, including Mr Mofid Karameh, Chairman of Mikano International; Joelle Haykal, Group Executive Director of Mikano International; Mr Syam Abdulkadir, Head of Operations, Mikano Motors; and Stephanie Warl, Sales Director for African Sales (LHD), Middle East and Africa Region, Changan. Their remarks highlighted the significance of the partnership and the introduction of Deepal to Nigeria.

The evening also featured a raffle draw, announced by Joelle Haykal, which saw Mrs Bidemi Oyewo emerge as the winner of a brand-new Deepal S07, while Mrs Funmi Nwama won an exclusive trip to China with Kunle Remi, Mikano Motors’ Changan ambassador.

The introduction of Deepal represents a new chapter in Mikano Motors’ automotive journey, strengthening its relationship with Changan while expanding the mobility options available to Nigerian consumers. Through advanced vehicle technology, local distribution and a comprehensive ownership proposition, Mikano Motors is positioning Deepal as an important addition to Nigeria’s evolving automotive landscape.

The post Mikano Motors launches Deepal, unveils flagship S09,  advances vision for future of mobility appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Senate committee hails Air Peace over ₦80,000 military fare
description:
By Henry Umoru



ABUJA — The Senate Committee on Army has commended Air Peace and its Chairman, Dr Allen Onyema, for introducing a discounted one-way domestic air fare of ₦80,000 for serving and retired personnel of the Nigerian Armed Forces.







The committee also urged other airlines and corpo
content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The Senate Committee on Army has commended Air Peace and its Chairman, Dr Allen Onyema, for introducing a discounted one-way domestic air fare of ₦80,000 for serving and retired personnel of the Nigerian Armed Forces.

The committee also urged other airlines and corporate organisations in the country to emulate the gesture as part of efforts to improve the welfare of military personnel and veterans.

The commendation was contained in a statement issued on Sunday by the Chairman of the committee, Senator Abdulaziz Musa Yar’Adua, representing Katsina Central Senatorial District.

According to the statement, the initiative was unveiled on November 16, 2026, during the 2026 Chief of Defence Intelligence Annual Conference in Abuja.

The committee said the discounted fare was available to eligible military personnel who had served in the Nigerian Armed Forces since 1960, across all domestic routes.

It added that Air Peace would also bear the cost of tickets for regional and international flights, with beneficiaries required to pay only applicable taxes and charges.

Describing the initiative as a patriotic gesture, the committee said it was a practical demonstration of appreciation for the sacrifices made by serving and retired military personnel in defending the country’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

It noted that members of the Armed Forces had continued to make enormous sacrifices, often at great personal cost, and deserved tangible support that would improve their welfare and that of their families.

“By reducing the burden of air travel, Air Peace has demonstrated that patriotism is not only spoken in times of ceremony, but shown in practical action that touches the lives of those who serve,” the statement said.

The committee particularly praised Onyema for what it described as his consistent commitment to humanitarian causes, national development and support for the Nigerian military.

It also endorsed the airline chairman’s call for the military leadership to establish a robust verification system to ensure that only genuine beneficiaries access the concession.

According to the committee, such a mechanism would help make the initiative sustainable, transparent and free from abuse.

It appealed to other airlines and corporate organisations to support the Armed Forces, describing the welfare of serving personnel and veterans as a collective national responsibility.

“The private sector has a critical role to play in complementing the efforts of the Federal Government in improving the welfare and morale of our troops and veterans,” it said.

The Senate committee assured Air Peace of its support and readiness to work with the airline, the Ministry of Defence and the Service Chiefs to ensure the smooth implementation of the initiative.

It reiterated its appreciation to the airline’s management for the gesture, describing it as a meaningful tribute to Nigeria’s military personnel.

The post Senate committee hails Air Peace over ₦80,000 military fare appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Ajadi pledges greater harvest, launches hymn book at Ibadan church thanksgiving
description: Ambassador Olufemi Ajadi Oguntoyinbo, the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) senatorial candidate for Oyo Central Senatorial District, has attended the 2026 Annual Harvest Thanksgiving and launching of the hymn book of The Apostles of Christ Pentecostal Church in Ibadan, where he pledged continued suppor
content:
Ambassador Olufemi Ajadi Oguntoyinbo, the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) senatorial candidate for Oyo Central Senatorial District, has attended the 2026 Annual Harvest Thanksgiving and launching of the hymn book of The Apostles of Christ Pentecostal Church in Ibadan, where he pledged continued support for the church and its members.

The event, held on Saturday, November 22, 2026, at the church auditorium in Temidire Estate, Sooko, Elega Ojuirin, Akobo, Ibadan, was hosted by Apostle Seye Olajide, with Pastor Yinka Olajide serving as the Minister in Charge.

Ajadi, who was accompanied by the Executive Chairman of Ogo-Oluwa Local Government Area, Hon. Oluwaseun Ojo Adesoye, and other members of his entourage, described Apostle Olajide as a longstanding friend whose commitment to the propagation of the gospel dated back to their childhood.

Speaking at the gathering, the APM senatorial candidate said his relationship with the cleric had been built on years of friendship and shared experiences, noting that he had witnessed Apostle Olajide’s consistency in serving God from an early age.

Following the formal launching of the church’s hymn book, Ajadi expressed his appreciation to the congregation for the invitation and support, promising that the church’s 2027 Annual Harvest Thanksgiving would be celebrated on a greater scale after the 2027 general elections.

He encouraged the congregation to remain steadfast in their faith, while reaffirming his commitment to supporting religious institutions and initiatives that promote spiritual growth and community development.

Also addressing the congregation, Adesoye described Ajadi as a God-fearing individual whose philanthropic activities and commitment to human development had distinguished him.

The council chairman noted that although Ajadi was not currently holding public office, he had continued to empower individuals and support communities through his personal resources.

“Ambassador Ajadi is not in government, yet he has been empowering people with his personal money. I urge everyone of us to vote for him and other APM candidates in the 2027 general elections because he will ensure that the dividends of democracy reach the grassroots,” Adesoye said.

He further expressed confidence in Ajadi’s capacity to provide effective representation for Oyo Central Senatorial District, stressing the importance of having a representative who would champion motions, sponsor bills and pursue legislative interventions capable of advancing the interests of the district and Nigeria at large.

In his remarks, Apostle Seye Olajide called on members of the congregation to support all APM candidates in the 2027 general elections, particularly Ajadi’s senatorial ambition.

The cleric, who clarified that he was not a politician, said he considered it important to speak in support of Ajadi because of his reputation for philanthropy and commitment to helping people.

He urged the congregation to recognise the importance of supporting credible individuals whose contributions to society, in his view, demonstrated a genuine concern for the welfare of others.

The harvest thanksgiving and hymn book launch provided an opportunity for worship, thanksgiving and fellowship, bringing together church members, invited guests and political stakeholders to celebrate the church’s spiritual activities.

The post Ajadi pledges greater harvest, launches hymn book at Ibadan church thanksgiving appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.
