title: FG partners world’s largest pivot irrigation maker
description:
By Favour Ulebor



The Federal Government has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Valmont Industries Inc., the world’s largest manufacturer of pivot irrigation systems, to accelerate the implementation of its flagship Irrigate Nigeria Programme.







The agreement also provides for th
content:
By Favour Ulebor

The Federal Government has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Valmont Industries Inc., the world’s largest manufacturer of pivot irrigation systems, to accelerate the implementation of its flagship Irrigate Nigeria Programme.

The agreement also provides for the establishment of an irrigation equipment production plant in Nigeria in partnership with the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure (NASENI), as part of efforts to boost local manufacturing and reduce dependence on imported irrigation technology.

The Presidential Implementation Committee on Technology Transfer (PICTT) signed the agreement with Valmont at the weekend.

In a statement issued by NASENI on Sunday, the Chairman of PICTT, Dr Dahiru Muhammed, who is also coordinating the implementation of the Irrigate Nigeria Programme, said the agreement formally brought Valmont, through its Valley Irrigation brand, on board as a major partner in developing irrigation infrastructure across the country.

Muhammed, who signed the agreement alongside Valmont’s Regional Vice President for the Middle East and Africa, Mr Kalle Autto, described the partnership as a significant step towards expanding mechanised irrigation in Nigeria.

He said: “This MoU officially brings the biggest pivot irrigation manufacturer in the world on board as a major partner in building irrigation infrastructure across Nigeria under the Irrigate Nigeria Programme, the flagship irrigation programme of this administration.”

He explained that beyond developing irrigation infrastructure, Valmont had agreed to work with NASENI to establish a local production facility for irrigation equipment.

“Just as importantly, this partnership comes with the transfer of know-how and capacity building for Nigerians, which is precisely what technology transfer is all about,” he added.

The agreement also provides for a pilot irrigation programme covering 40,000 hectares in Adamawa State.

The project will be implemented in collaboration with the Nigeria Incentive-Based Risk Sharing System for Agricultural Lending (NIRSAL) and the National Agricultural Development Fund (NADF).

While PICTT will lead the overall implementation of the programme, NASENI will drive the adoption and domestication of the technology.

The partnership is also expected to create opportunities for collaboration with the University of Nebraska and the Robert B. Daugherty Water for Food Global Institute on sustainable irrigation systems and water resource management.

Muhammed said key stakeholders had already expressed interest in expanding irrigation infrastructure through the partnership, describing the development as a vote of confidence in the programme.

Officials said the agreement would help improve agricultural productivity, strengthen national food security and promote the sustainable management of water resources in line with the Federal Government’s agricultural transformation agenda.

title: Troops rescue 18 abducted children, hunt for four others in Kaduna
description:
By Kingsley Omonobi



Troops of the Nigerian Army under Operation Fansan Yamma have rescued 18 children abducted by suspected terrorists in Kaduna State, while intensifying efforts to secure the release of four others still held by the fleeing kidnappers.







The children, members of the Boys’ a
content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

Troops of the Nigerian Army under Operation Fansan Yamma have rescued 18 children abducted by suspected terrorists in Kaduna State, while intensifying efforts to secure the release of four others still held by the fleeing kidnappers.

The children, members of the Boys’ and Girls’ Brigade, were reportedly abducted early Sunday, November 22, 2026, while participating in a morning group road walk at Mother-Cat Community in the Kachia/Kajuru general area of the state.

Confirming the rescue in a statement on Sunday night, the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, said troops of the 1 Division Nigerian Army, operating under Sector 1 of Operation Fansan Yamma, launched a rescue operation shortly after receiving a distress call.

Anele said troops of Sub-Sector 5 immediately mobilised and pursued the abductors through surrounding bushes, advancing towards Rehina Riverside, where some of the children were found abandoned by the fleeing criminals.

She said the troops sustained the pursuit along the river line, rescuing additional victims and bringing the number of recovered children to 18.

According to the Army, sustained military pressure forced the abductors to abandon the children as they fled deeper into the surrounding forest.

The statement added that troops had extended their search operations along the Ankwa–Kabode–Pachi link road and towards the Awon and Akwondo general areas to locate the remaining four children and apprehend those responsible for the abduction.

The Army assured the families of the victims and the general public of its commitment to rescuing all the abducted children.

It also said troops would sustain offensive operations and intelligence-led patrols to protect vulnerable communities and prevent further attacks.

The military urged residents to remain vigilant and provide timely and credible information to security agencies to support the ongoing search-and-rescue operations and facilitate the arrest of the perpetrators.

Pochettino made the demand after Manchester United suffered a heavy loss to their arch-rivals at Anfield on S
content:
Manchester United manager, Mauricio Pochettino, has urged his players to improve their focus, concentration and decision-making following their 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in the Premier League.

Pochettino made the demand after Manchester United suffered a heavy loss to their arch-rivals at Anfield on Sunday.

The defeat leaves the Red Devils 19th on the Premier League table after 11 matches, intensifying pressure on the new manager.

Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Pochettino said the team must accept its current situation and take responsibility for improving their performances.

“We need to accept that reality. We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field,” he said.

He added that the players must also critically assess their performances, although he expressed dissatisfaction with some decisions made during the encounter.

Manchester United will hope to return to winning ways when they face Sporting CP in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday.

title: Sowore faults Tinubu over water disruption at Aso Rock
description:
The 2027 presidential candidate of the African Action Congress, Omoyele Sowore, has criticised President Bola Tinubu over the disruption of water supply at the Presidential Villa, Abuja.
Sowore accused the President of failing to address a basic infrastructure need within the seat of government, say
content:
The 2027 presidential candidate of the African Action Congress, Omoyele Sowore, has criticised President Bola Tinubu over the disruption of water supply at the Presidential Villa, Abuja.

Sowore accused the President of failing to address a basic infrastructure need within the seat of government, saying the situation raised questions about his administration’s ability to manage the country’s affairs.

In a post on his official X handle on Sunday night, the human rights activist said those around Tinubu should have advised him to resign if he could not guarantee a steady water supply at the Presidential Villa.

He wrote, “You can’t even keep the water running at Aso Rock Villa, and the goons clapping for you must really hate Nigeria.

“They should have told you to your face that if you can’t manage the water supply at Aso Rock, you should resign. Shameless people.”

The criticism followed Tinubu’s disclosure that water supply was interrupted at the Presidential Villa while he was shaving last Wednesday.

The President made the revelation on Sunday during a special prayer session organised by members of his family at the Yoruba Tennis Club, Onikan, Lagos.

Recounting the experience, Tinubu said, “On the Wednesday of last week, I was shaving, and the water went off. And the Villa, you won’t know punishment there too.

“The water went off. So we will correct all this. No light, no water, no electricity, no development.

“We have just started. We can do it, and we will do it for Nigeria.”

The President, however, expressed confidence that his administration would address the challenges, insisting that Nigeria had the capacity to overcome its infrastructure deficits.

Tinubu’s remarks highlighted the infrastructure challenges facing the country, including unreliable electricity and water supply, which he acknowledged also affected the Presidential Villa.

The post Sowore faults Tinubu over water disruption at Aso Rock appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority has urged motorists to obey traffic rules and regulations, maintain their vehicles and observe stipulated speed limits to ensure safety on Lagos roads.

The authority gave the advice in a post on its official X handle on Monday, noting that Monday mornings were usually characterised by heavy traffic due to the movement of workers and other commuters to their various destinations.

It said, “Monday morning in Lagos is usually a very busy and hectic period for workers commuting to their various places of work.

“The road is usually congested due to the mass movement of pedestrians and vehicles.”

LASTMA said its personnel had been strategically deployed across road networks to monitor vehicular movement, maintain orderliness and ensure smooth traffic flow.

“For orderliness and seamless movement across the road networks, LASTMA personnel are well positioned and strategically deployed to monitor vehicular movement and ensure that traffic remains unhindered,” it stated.

The authority also advised motorists to conduct daily checks on their vehicles before embarking on journeys, obey traffic regulations and show respect to traffic officials.

It further cautioned drivers against exceeding stipulated speed limits, stressing the importance of responsible driving in preventing road crashes and ensuring the safety of other road users.

LASTMA urged members of the public to report road incidents and unusual traffic situations through its toll-free line, 3367.

“In case of any road incidents or unusual traffic, you can reach us via the LASTMA toll-free line 3367,” the authority added.

title: Pepe’s eye surgery unrelated to solar eclipse – Villarreal
description:
Villarreal have dismissed reports linking Nicolas Pepe’s eye surgery to watching a solar eclipse, insisting that the procedure had nothing to do with the astronomical event.
The Spanish club described the reports as “completely false” following speculation that the former Arsenal forward damaged his
content:
Villarreal have dismissed reports linking Nicolas Pepe’s eye surgery to watching a solar eclipse, insisting that the procedure had nothing to do with the astronomical event.

The Spanish club described the reports as “completely false” following speculation that the former Arsenal forward damaged his eyes after staring directly at the sun during the solar eclipse on August 12.

The 31-year-old underwent eye surgery in October, which forced him to miss six matches, sparking rumours on social media that the injury resulted from watching the eclipse without proper protection.

A video also circulated online, purportedly from one of Pepe’s social media accounts, showing the Ivory Coast international watching the solar eclipse in Spain.

However, Villarreal clarified that the operation had been planned in advance and was entirely unrelated to the event.

In a post on its X handle on Sunday, the club said, “Villarreal CF, in response to reports published in various media outlets recently, clarifies that it is completely false that Nicolas Pepe’s eye surgery has any connection to viewing the solar eclipse,” the club said in a statement.

“The surgery had been scheduled in advance for reasons entirely unrelated to this event.

“The club urges accuracy and responsibility when reporting on matters related to its players’ health.”

Meanwhile, experts have warned that looking directly at a solar eclipse without appropriate eye protection can cause serious damage to the retina, particularly the cells responsible for central vision.

They have also stressed that ordinary sunglasses are not sufficient protection when viewing a solar eclipse, recommending specially designed eclipse glasses.

Pepe joined Villarreal from Turkish side Trabzonspor in 2024 and has scored 14 goals in 86 appearances across all competitions for the Spanish club.

The forward previously played for Arsenal, who signed him from Lille in 2019 for a then-club record fee of £72 million.

He scored 27 goals in 112 appearances for the Gunners before spending time on loan at Nice and subsequently joining Trabzonspor on a free transfer.

Villarreal’s statement has sought to put an end to speculation surrounding the cause of Pepe’s eye surgery, while urging the media to exercise responsibility when reporting on players’ medical conditions.

The post Pepe’s eye surgery unrelated to solar eclipse – Villarreal appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Umo Eno appoints chapel cleaner as Personal Assistant after four years of service
description:
Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, has appointed Edwin James, a volunteer who spent nearly four years cleaning the Latter House Chapel at the Government House in Uyo, as his Personal Assistant.
Eno announced the appointment during the monthly Government House prayer service on Sunday, directing the
content:
Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, has appointed Edwin James, a volunteer who spent nearly four years cleaning the Latter House Chapel at the Government House in Uyo, as his Personal Assistant.

Eno announced the appointment during the monthly Government House prayer service on Sunday, directing the Secretary to the State Government to make it effective from June 1, 2023, when James began his voluntary service.

Explaining the decision, the governor said the state had failed to recognise James’ contribution despite his years of dedication.

“We have been owing him,” Eno said, instructing the SSG to confirm the appointment and ensure that James received the benefits due to him from the effective date.

The governor said it would have been unfortunate for his administration to leave office without acknowledging the volunteer’s commitment to maintaining the chapel.

He questioned why James had worked for almost four years without receiving an official appointment, adding that his service should not have gone unnoticed.

A video shared on the Akwa Ibom State Government’s Facebook page showed James approaching the governor during the service. He appeared emotional as Eno publicly announced the appointment.

Members of the congregation subsequently congratulated him, with cheers and applause following the announcement.

In a separate statement on his LinkedIn account, Eno said the appointment reflected his administration’s position that dedication and service deserved recognition, regardless of an individual’s social standing.

“His story reminds us that dedication, humility and faithful service deserve recognition, regardless of one’s position in society,” the governor wrote.

During the prayer service, Eno also gave an update on his administration’s payment of inherited gratuities, saying approximately ₦102bn had been paid out of the ₦111bn backlog.

He further announced plans to increase student bursaries from June 2027.

Under the proposed arrangement, students studying general courses will receive ₦200,000 each, while those enrolled in professional programmes such as Medicine, Law, Architecture, Information and Communication Technology and Pharmacy will get ₦250,000 each.

The governor said the new rates were part of his administration’s efforts to improve access to education and support students across the state.

He noted that the bursary scheme had previously been increased from ₦10,000 to ₦20,000 and later to ₦50,000.

Eno added that his government would continue to prioritise the welfare of retired public servants and investment in education.

He also urged residents to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards and mobilise support in their respective wards ahead of the 2027 general elections.

title: 2027: Why Nigerians should choose me over Peter Obi – Makinde

Makinde made the claim during an interview on the ‘Roof Top’ podcast on Sunday, citing h
content:
The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has declared himself a better candidate than Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Makinde made the claim during an interview on the ‘Roof Top’ podcast on Sunday, citing his South-West origin as one of the reasons he believes he is better suited for the presidency.

According to him, the South-West and the North have maintained a longstanding political alliance, which he described as a stabilising factor in Nigeria.

“I am a better candidate than Peter Obi because as someone from the South-West, we and North have always been in alliance. We are the stabilising factor for Nigeria,” he said.

The Oyo State governor also made reference to the military coup of 1966, where he said mostly people from the South-West and the North were killed.

According to him, the South-West and the North paid the price together in 1966, and that shared sacrifice is why their alliance is the one that holds Nigeria together.

Makinde’s running mate, Lawal Daura, is from Katsina State in the North.

content:
Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai has been ranked the best free-kick taker in world football in 2026, finishing ahead of Lionel Messi and Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes.

According to Planet Football’s latest ranking on Sunday, the Hungarian international takes the top spot following his impressive performances from dead-ball situations, including his stunning free-kick against Manchester United.

Messi, widely regarded as one of the greatest free-kick specialists in football history, occupies second place. The Argentine has scored 76 career free-kick goals, putting him just two behind Brazilian Marcelinho Carioca’s record of 78.

Fernandes completes the top three, with the Manchester United playmaker continuing to demonstrate his quality from set-piece situations.

Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice also features prominently at sixth, while Real Madrid youngster Arda Güler is ranked seventh.

Former Liverpool defender Trent Alexander-Arnold, now at Real Madrid, occupies eighth place, while Cristiano Ronaldo and Hakan Calhanoglu complete the top 10.

The ranking also recognises Leeds United’s Anton Stach, who sits fifth, and Brazilian veteran Hulk, who takes fourth place after continuing to score free-kicks in domestic football.

Full ranking of the world’s 10 best free-kick takers in 2026

Dominik Szoboszlai (Liverpool)

Lionel Messi (Inter Miami)

Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United)

Hulk (Atlético Mineiro)

Anton Stach (Leeds United)

Declan Rice (Arsenal)

Arda Güler (Real Madrid)

Trent Alexander-Arnold (Real Madrid)

Cristiano Ronaldo (Al-Nassr)

Hakan Calhanoglu (Inter Milan)

Szoboszlai’s position at the summit highlights his growing reputation as one of football’s most dangerous dead-ball specialists.

Meanwhile, Messi’s continued presence near the top underlines his remarkable consistency, despite playing in Major League Soccer.

The ranking also shows that free-kick excellence is not limited to established superstars, with emerging talents such as Szoboszlai and Güler making their mark among the game’s elite specialists.

title: FCCPC shuts Lagos estate firm over property breach
description:
The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission has shut the business premises of Meridian Park Real Estate Company in Lagos over its alleged failure to deliver a five-bedroom duplex bought by a customer in 2020.
 Speaking during Thursday’s enforcement exercise, the FCCPC’s Deputy Directo
content:
The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission has shut the business premises of Meridian Park Real Estate Company in Lagos over its alleged failure to deliver a five-bedroom duplex bought by a customer in 2020.

 Speaking during Thursday’s enforcement exercise, the FCCPC’s Deputy Director of Surveillance and Investigation, Marvin Nadah, said the action followed the company’s failure to honour the Commission’s directive to hand over the property to the complainant within one month.

 According to him, the customer had fully paid for the property but was yet to take possession, prompting her to approach the Commission for intervention.

 Nadah said the FCCPC had continued to pursue the matter to secure redress for the complainant, “culminating in the issuance of a compliance notice in August 2026, directing the company to deliver the property within a month.”

 “In 2020, a complainant had made a full payment for a property to the company, and that property was not delivered. The complainant came to the Commission, and between last year and this year, the process had been on to provide redress to the issue to the point where a compliance notice was issued by the Commission directing that the property be handed over to the complainant within a one-month period in August of this year, 2026,” he said.

 He said the company failed to comply with the directive, “leading to the sealing of its premises in accordance with Section 150(4)(a) of the FCCPC Act.”

 “Failure of compliance with that directive by the Commission, is what, in line with the orders conferred on the FCCPC by Section 150, Subsection 4A, has led to our sealing the business premises,” he added.

 He said the enforcement was necessary to ensure the company complied with the Commission’s order, adding that the premises would remain sealed until the directive was fulfilled.

 The South-West Zonal Coordinator of the FCCPC, Dr Olubunmi Otti, also shared his thoughts on the exercise, saying, “It’s an enforcement exercise because there is a violation of the provision of the Act. And then when there’s a violation, the law says we should enforce, and we have enforced. And so we progress from there.”

 Otti urged consumers to exercise due diligence when buying anything.

 “But there’s something I want to tell consumers. Consumers should exercise due diligence when buying anything. Before you sign any terms and agreement, know the component of the terms and agreement before you sign. It’s very important. And then before you part with your money, collect the product,” Otti said.

 Earlier, the Director of Operations at Meridian Park Real Estate Company, Mr Uchenna Eze, said the matter had been amicably resolved, adding that the subscriber had been invited to collect the keys to the property.

 Eze said the company had collected the subscriber’s handover fees and fixed a date for the handover, noting that the customer had indicated her intention to send a representative to receive the keys.

 He expressed surprise at the sealing of the premises, maintaining that the company had fulfilled the terms of the complaint resolution.

 The company’s official said it was prepared to provide copies of correspondence received from the Commission to substantiate its position.

 “Yes, we have just witnessed the enforcement by the FCCPC. It’s regarding a subscriber of our project. The client wrote a petition at FCCPC, the matter was resolved, it was regarding the delivery of her subscribed property. We amicably resolved the matter, and we invited the subscriber to come and collect her keys. In line with our invitation, the subscriber has paid the handover fees, and we have already scheduled her for handover, either she comes in person or she sends a proxy. And she informed us that she’s going to send a proxy. What we witnessed today is a surprise to the organisation,” Eze said.

The post FCCPC shuts Lagos estate firm over property breach appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: GAS: Domestic market gets 41.3% as Nigeria’s supply averages 4.95bcf/d in 10 months
description:
•LPG retail price rises 12.5% to N1,800 per kg •Make domestic market attractive to secure adequate supply — NALPGAM



By Udeme Akpan



Despite Nigeria’s 215.19 trillion cubic feet (Tcf) of proven natural gas reserves, the domestic market received an average of 2.04 billion cubic feet per day (bcf/
content:
•LPG retail price rises 12.5% to N1,800 per kg •Make domestic market attractive to secure adequate supply — NALPGAM

By Udeme Akpan

Despite Nigeria’s 215.19 trillion cubic feet (Tcf) of proven natural gas reserves, the domestic market received an average of 2.04 billion cubic feet per day (bcf/d), representing 41.3 per cent of the country’s total supply of 4.95 bcf/d in the first 10 months of 2026.

The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, NMDPRA, disclosed this in its latest report obtained by Vanguard.

The report showed that the Nigeria LNG Limited, NLNG, received the remaining 58.7 per cent, averaging 2.91 bcf/d.

In October, total average daily gas supply rose by 2.7 per cent to 4.951 bcf/d, from 4.822 bcf/d in September.

Domestic supply increased by 2.3 per cent to 2.113 bcf/d, while deliveries to NLNG grew by three per cent to 2.838 bcf/d.

April recorded the highest average daily supply during the 10-month period at 5.141 bcf/d, comprising 2.01 bcf/d for domestic market and 3.13 bcf/d for NLNG.

Gas supply to power plants increased by 10 per cent to 0.571 bcf/d in October. Deliveries to gas-based industries also rose, while supplies to commercial users declined. Supply to the Escravos Gas-to-Liquids facility fell by two per cent.

Gas exports also strengthened. Average daily LNG exports increased by seven per cent to 52,721 metric tonnes per day, from 49,198 metric tonnes per day in September, while pipeline exports through the West African Gas Pipeline (WAGP) rose by 11 per cent to 0.149 bcf/d, from 0.134 bcf/d.

LPG retail price rises 12.5% to ₦1,800 per kg

Meanwhile, the average retail price of liquefied petroleum gas, LPG, also known as cooking gas, rose by 12.5 per cent to ₦1,800 per kilogramme in November 2026, from ₦1,600 in October.

Checks by Vanguard attributed the increase largely to limited supply.

The average depot price of LPG stood at ₦1,274 in the Daily Depot Price Intelligence Report for Friday, November 20, 2026. The report covered Lagos, Warri, Calabar and Port Harcourt but did not provide a regional breakdown of LPG prices.

Make domestic market attractive to secure adequate supply — NALPGAM

The Executive Secretary/Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Association of Liquefied Petroleum Gas Marketers, NALPGAM, Bassey Essien, told Vanguard in an interview that Nigeria must make its domestic gas market commercially attractive to secure adequate supplies.

He said: “Gas exports generate foreign exchange, but the domestic market must also be commercially attractive enough to secure adequate supply.

‘’The solution is not to stop exports but to make the domestic market competitive enough to attract supply while preserving export earnings.”

On Domestic Gas Delivery Obligation, DGDO, Essien noted that regulation alone could not guarantee physical deliveries without adequate infrastructure and effective payment systems.

“The Domestic Gas Delivery Obligation, DGDO, requires producers to supply the local market, but regulation alone cannot guarantee physical delivery where gathering, processing, transportation and payment systems are inadequate,” he said.

He identified the proposed Gas Swap Framework as a way to address infrastructure and supply gaps by connecting producers with available gas but limited evacuation capacity to operators with infrastructure but insufficient supply.

Essien added: “Gas is also essential to fertiliser, cement, petrochemicals, steel, methanol, glass, ceramics, food processing and other industries.

‘’Greater domestic utilisation can, therefore, create wider economic value through electricity, manufacturing, employment, taxation and investment.”

Similarly, the Lead Consultant for Industry and Private Sector Development at the ECOWAS Commission, Prof. Ken Ife, said Nigeria must focus on converting its vast reserves into reliable supplies for the domestic economy, while sustaining export earnings.

He said: “Nigeria’s gas challenge is no longer simply about how much gas the country has in the ground, it is about how quickly it can turn those reserves into reliable, commercially viable supplies for the domestic economy while sustaining the export revenues needed to finance further investment.”

title: President Tinubu does not need this falsehood
description:
By Dele Sobowale







Each time President Tinubu mentions $1 trillion economy by 2030, he reveals more than the politicians’ penchant for making promises they cannot keep. He brings into question his proclaimed economic qualification as an accounting graduate for a Chicago university. There is abu
content:
By Dele Sobowale

Each time President Tinubu mentions $1 trillion economy by 2030, he reveals more than the politicians’ penchant for making promises they cannot keep. He brings into question his proclaimed economic qualification as an accounting graduate for a Chicago university. There is abundant evidence, provided by Tinubu himself, to call that assertion a deliberate lie. I have touched on some of them before; but, Tinubu, despite expert advice continues to campaign on a promise which can never be redeemed. Here again, the facts which Tinubu stubbornly ignores; because they don’t fit into the narratives of a desperate politician running for elections, will once more be presented. This time fresh evidence will be added from Tinubu’s campaign organization.

POLITICS AND FALSEHOOD ARE INSEPRABLE

“The great masses of the people ..will fall victims to a great lie than to a small one.”

Adolf Hitler, 1899-1945, VANGUARD BOOK OF QUOTATIONS, VBQ p 130.

Politicians, under the best of circumstances, would repeat the same falsehood in the hope that saying it long enough will make it true. And, when they fail, they never apologise to the people; they blame others. President Tinubu’s assertion that Nigeria’s economy can grow to $1 trillion by 2030 is the sort of thing Hitler was talking about. I have given Tinubu the benefit of doubt that he read accounting in an American university as an undergraduate. But, his insistence that the Nigerian economy, whose Gross Domestic Product, GDP, is estimated to reach $386.67 billion at the end of the year 2026 could reach $1 trillion in just four years, would have had first year students of any university wondering if that was a joke or something else not hilarious. The figures don’t add up.

LIARS CAN FIGURE; FIGURES DON’T LIE

“Every government is run by liars and nothing they say should be believed.

I.F Stone, 1907-1989. US Journalist and Publisher.

Stone was one of my favourite columnists during my ten years in the US. I read his articles as if preparing for an examination on the subject discussed. He always led with evidence. So, let us start with the Federal Governments own figures. President Tinubu has been going round the country telling Nigerians the Nigerian economy is set to grow by 4.5 per cent this year. That will be the best performance since 2014. It is admittedly very commendable but worse than Jonathan’s worst year. The FG is also promising 6 percent growth in 2027. Highly praise-worthy if achieved. For some reason, not too difficult to understand, Tinubu, a self-proclaimed accountant, as well as his mob of supporters, cannot seem to understand that you cannot grow $386.67 billion to $1 trillion at 6 per cent in four years. This is primary school arithmetic called compound interest calculations. It is repeated at freshman level in American universities. Has Tinubu forgotten it or is he just peddling the big lie for political gain?

QUANTUM LEAPS OF OTHER VARIABLES NEEDED

“Economics is not magic; at its best, it is quantitative.” Nobel Prize Winner

For Nigeria’s economy to grow from $386.67bn to $1 trillion in four years, so many variables would have to change in quantum leaps at the same time. A course in economic planning based on input-output table would reveal, for instance, how much more power generation would be required to support a $1tr economy. None of the national economies currently in the $1tr class generates less than 50,000MW per day. Certainly, even the most optimistic of Tinubu supporters and the President himself cannot state categorically that Nigeria will generate and distribute 50,000MW in 2030. Yet, power supply is the most basic of all the inputs required to create a $1tr economy. Here is another.

“Nigeria needs 920 vessels to achieve $1tr economy.” Report, November 15, 2026

Dr Emeka Akabogu, a maritime lawyer, delivered a paper which effectively debunked Tinubu’s favourite fantasy. In the paper titled “Can Nigeria’s Seaports Carry a One-Trillion-Dollar Economy by 2030?” It was a damning indictment of the big lie being sold to Nigerians. According to Akabogu: ”under the country’s present fleet growth pattern, the number may only increase to approximately 348 by 2030. This means that even by 2030 , Nigeria could still be short of about 572 ships against the estimated 920 vessels required to support a $1tn economy.”

Ships are not assets you can go to the market and procure as you like. Research indicates that the time lag from order to delivery ranges fom five to seven years depending on the tonnage and type of vessel. Obviously, even if Nigerians place orders today, the first will not be delivered until after 2030. At any rate, nobody seriously expects Nigeria to have 920 vessels for at least twelve years; and the seaports might not even be capable of handling so many ships arriving suddenly. Another port congestion, reminiscent of the disastrous port congestion of 1976-7, will inevitably occur.

SOLUDO’S UNPROFESSIONAL FENCE-SITTING

“You cannot adopt politics as a profession and remain honest.”

Louis M Howe, 1871-1936.

“$1tr economy: Nigeria needs double-digit growth, massive investments – SOLUDO”

VANGUARD, November 13, 2026.

Every profession, except law and politics, expects its practitioners to be honest in their transactions and utterances. Soludo, like every economist, is expected to be as truthful as he can when the subject is the nation’s economy. His new role as a politician has thrown him into an ethical dilemma. He is a member of President Tinubu’s campaign committee. In that capacity, he is expected to echo the candidates’ positions on every issue. Suddenly, he found himself delivering the keynote address at the presentation of a book: Economic Diversification and Structural Transformation in Nigeria: The Past, The Present, The Future” written by a member of the House of Representatives. Suddenly forced to speak as an economics professor and professional, Soludo revealed the unvarnished truth. Here it is.

“Four per cent growth rate for the economy so far is an improvement over the recent past, but, very modest growth for the requirement for poverty reduction or accelerated transformation. Such growth that will be required to have a $1 trillion economy in the next few years and it would require this economy growing at a minimum of double digit.

“And to grow at double digit, you require huge investments in excess of 30 per cent of GDP. Currently, we are doing about 17- point something per cent.”

This is simply incredible. A professor of economics, a State Governor, aware of the great credibility gap between reality and President Tunubu’s falsehood is still going round urging Nigerians to vote for a candidate who is certainly deceiving them. What happened to professional ethics? Soludo needs to be reminded that Emilokan promised 10 per cent annual growth for 2024, 2025, 2026 in the RENEWED HOPE document. He failed every year; and will fail again.

Follow me on Facebook @ J Israel Biola.

title: How Oyibo, BEDC worker was murdered 4 months into marriage
description:
•Disco, Delta community mourn •Family shattered, seeks justice



By Egufe Yafugborhi & Cynthia Alo



Oscar Eze, popularly known as Oyibo or NEPA Man, left home on Monday, November 16, 2026, for another routine assignment as an operations personnel of the Benin Electricity Distribution Company, BED
content:
•Disco, Delta community mourn •Family shattered, seeks justice

By Egufe Yafugborhi & Cynthia Alo

Oscar Eze, popularly known as Oyibo or NEPA Man, left home on Monday, November 16, 2026, for another routine assignment as an operations personnel of the Benin Electricity Distribution Company, BEDC, Agbor Business Unit.

The 38-year-old had no reason to suspect that the day’s work in Umunede, Ika North-East Local Government Area of Delta State, would be his last.

Four months after remarrying following the death of his first wife, Eze was brutally murdered in circumstances that have left his pregnant wife, young son and elderly mother devastated, while colleagues and residents mourn a man widely remembered for his cheerful disposition.

His last assignment took him to a relatively isolated suburb of Idumu-Oba, with sparsely distributed buildings. While working alongside other workmen at a property apparently undergoing finishing, he was ambushed by a gang of youths.

A CCTV camera at the premises captured the horrifying encounter. The assailants accosted him around the small entrance gate, dragged him into the compound and repeatedly stabbed him with daggers as other workmen watched in fear.

He sustained multiple injuries to his upper body and died shortly afterwards. He was rushed to hospital, where he was confirmed dead.

The police subsequently confirmed that Eze was attacked on November 16, at about 1.15 p.m., during a power disconnection exercise at Ileje Quarters, Umunede.

According to BEDC management, the property he had disconnected owed the company almost N300,000 in electricity bills. His attackers allegedly trailed him after the disconnection.

A legitimate assignment to earn a living ended in a gruesome killing, leaving a community asking how a familiar electricity worker could have become the target of such violence.

A young marriage shattered

Beyond the circumstances of his death lies the tragedy of a family whose hopes have been abruptly shattered.

Eze’s first wife died about two years ago, leaving him with a son. He subsequently remarried barely four months before his death. His new wife was reportedly pregnant.

A neighbour close to the BEDC office affirmed: “His first wife, who had a child for him, died about two years ago. Then he remarried four months ago.

“I don’t know where the new wife is from. His former wife was from here (Umunede). Oyibo lived at Idumu-Oba.”

At the compound where Eze lived, a neighbour said his wife was taken away on the day news of the killing reached them.

“We don’t know anything about it. We were here when they sent the information to us, and even on the same day, they took her (Oyibo’s pregnant wife) away.

“Personally, I was surprised when I heard the news. I never had any complaints from anybody that he had a problem with them. To be sincere, he was outgoing.”

Describing his relationship with the deceased, the neighbour added: “For us here, we never had any misunderstanding with him ever since. He was very humble to us -very, very humble.”

For a man who had apparently begun rebuilding his family life after losing his first wife, his violent death has left a particularly painful void.

A jolly good fellow

An intelligence officer with the community’s Anti-Cultism Unit, which collaborates with the police, Emmanuel Nathaniel, said he was personally angered by the killing.

He described Eze as a friend and familiar personality in Umunede.

“The victim’s my good friend. He’s a jolly good fellow and we all know him as Oyibo, some call him NEPA Man. People call him Oyibo because of his fair skin colour.

“Personally, I’m so annoyed. I don’t like such criminal acts. That’s why I’m fighting against intimidation and oppression.”

Nathaniel said the community vigilante responded after receiving information about the attack, working with the police to recover the corpse and assist investigations.

“When we were alerted with calls, we were there. The camera (CCTV on the house) captured some things. And we went there with the DPO and we recovered everything.

“We investigated this and submitted it (report) to the police station because we are working under the police. We recovered the corpse and through the camera, the operation was made easier.

“Some people are saying it was a planned work. Some people are saying it was a cult-perpetrated violence. But me personally, Emmanuel Nathaniel, I know that he’s a NEPA (BEDC) man.”

Seven suspects arrested

The Delta State Police Command has announced the arrest of seven suspects in connection with the murder.

In a November 19 statement, the Police Public Relations Officer, Bright Edafe, said detectives were mobilised after the Umunede Division received information that BEDC personnel had been attacked by youths suspected to be cultists, armed with cutlasses, battle axes and daggers.

The first five suspects arrested were Emmanuel Chinonso, 30; Gift Francis, 24; Jerry Nusi, 20; Kelvin Ifeanyi, 19; and Emmanuel Chinaza, 24.

Two additional suspects, Michael Moses, 26, and Moses Egwuye, 35, were arrested on November 18. The police described them as suspected members of the Aiye Confraternity.

The Command said a manhunt for other suspects was ongoing.

The Commissioner of Police, CP Samuel E. Erale, condemned the killing, extended condolences to the bereaved family and BEDC, and warned against attacks on people discharging lawful duties.

He assured that everyone found culpable would be prosecuted, stressing that grievances must be addressed through lawful channels.

He was killed for doing his job — BEDC

The company’s Acting Managing Director, Jonathan Lawani, said Eze was murdered for carrying out an approved disconnection exercise.

Speaking at BEDC headquarters in Benin, Lawani disclosed that the disconnected property had an outstanding electricity bill of almost N300,000.

“The only instrument approved by NERC, the Nigeria Electricity Regulatory Commission, to ask for payment or to demand payment for those who refuse to pay us for our monthly electricity is disconnection.

“I want to put it straight that what the late Oscar did was an approved and official assignment.

“The house in question owes us almost three hundred thousand naira and he disconnected them for non-payment and left the place quietly.”

Lawani alleged that the attackers subsequently traced Eze to another property, where they stabbed him repeatedly.

He said the CCTV footage had helped expose the attack, which the perpetrators allegedly intended to conceal.

“What they planned did not work. These people had planned to kill him without any evidence. And what they did was to push him into a compound, a very isolated place where he went to carry out another assignment. Unfortunately for them, that house has a CCTV camera and they were all captured directly.

“We cannot bring him back but we must ensure that justice is served. We will do everything in line with the law to see that justice is served.”

Lawani disclosed that Eze left behind a son, his new wife and an elderly mother, calling on the Delta State Government to provide adequate security for electricity workers.

“We believe the government should provide an enabling environment for people to work, and for a critical sector like electricity, we should be protected.”

Abel Enechaziam, BEDC’s Head of Maximum Demand Customer and Acting Chief Commercial Officer, urged electricity consumers to use established complaint channels and regulatory authorities to resolve disputes.

Monarch, activist demand justice

The traditional ruler of Umunede Kingdom, HRM Dr Ezeagwu Ezenwali I, JP, condemned the murder, describing it as wicked, barbaric and alien to the peaceful disposition of the community.

The monarch, who expressed shock over the incident, assured BEDC and security agencies of the community’s cooperation in providing useful information.

He also commended the Umunede DPO, Brisibe Golus, and the Anti-Cultism group for their efforts in the arrests, urging parents to discourage their children from cultism and violence.

Austine Aghomi, Coordinator of Jesse Heights Development Association, chided Governor Sheriff Oborevwori over what he described as the government’s silence and lack of compassion towards the bereaved family.

Aghomi argued that electricity distribution workers required government protection because their duties frequently exposed them to hostility from consumers.

“So any responsible government committed to duty should champion the protection of assets or personnel of discos from the increasing vulnerabilities in the operating space.

“Now, it’s been over one week since a young man was ensnared in some isolated Umunede neighbourhood and gruesomely murdered. Where is the compassion, empathy from government? No official statement, no contact with the bereaved family.”

He specifically faulted the governor for allegedly failing to visit the community or publicly demand justice.

“If Oborevwori had as much taken a day off his extravagant re-election campaigns to visit Umunede, empathise with the bereaved family and issued an official statement over the murder of the innocent man, it could only be to his favour.”

Umunede in darkness

The killing has also triggered a blackout in Umunede, as BEDC suspended operations in the community following the death of its worker.

For residents, the suspension underscores the consequences of violence against personnel providing essential services. But for Eze’s family, the darkness is far more personal.

A commercial motorcyclist, John Agho, blamed growing unemployment and drug abuse among youths for the community’s security challenges.

“Too many youths are jobless in Umunede. Many want to live large without lawful means. So also is drug addiction.

“In the absence of meaningful jobs, the tendency to survive on criminality is so high here. No normal person would hack a fellow dead the way they killed Oyibo just to express anger over disconnection.”

With seven suspects in custody and a manhunt ongoing, the immediate demand from the family, BEDC and community stakeholders is that the investigation must not end with arrests.

Eze went out to perform his lawful duty and earn a living. He returned home a corpse.

Four months into a new marriage, his life was cut short, leaving a pregnant wife, a young son and an elderly mother to confront a future without him.

For Umunede, the challenge is not only to restore electricity but to ensure that those responsible for Oyibo’s last assignment ending in death are brought to justice.

Vanguard News

content:
The Nigerian Army Armoured Corps has formally pulled out 10 retired senior officers from service at a colourful ceremony held at the Brigadier General Y. Abubakar Parade Ground, Headquarters Nigerian Army Armoured Corps, Obienu Barracks, Bauchi.

The ceremony, which took place on Saturday, was the climax of the week-long 2026 Nigerian Army Armoured Corps Biennial Conference and Reunion.

The event brought together serving and retired officers of the Corps from across the country to celebrate the distinguished careers and contributions of the retired generals.

According to a statement issued on Sunday by the Acting Deputy Director, Army Public Relations, Headquarters Nigerian Army Armoured Corps, Major Adekunle Akinleye, the officers honoured were Lieutenant General Abdulsalami Ibrahim, Major Generals Benjamin Sawyerr, Ibrahim Ali, Sani Mohammed and Ibrahim Jallo, as well as Brigadier Generals Victor Ita, Tuni Isa, Aminu Usman, Ezra Barkins and Suleiman Adamu.

Speaking at the ceremony as Special Guest of Honour and Reviewing Officer, retired Lieutenant General Abdulsalami Ibrahim described the Armoured Corps as more than just a military formation, saying it had become a way of life for him and other officers who served in the Corps for decades.

“Armour is not only a branch of the Corps, but it is a way of life,” he declared.

He urged serving officers, particularly the younger generation, to uphold the values of courage, discipline and professionalism in the discharge of their responsibilities, stressing that they represented the future of the Corps.

The retired general also expressed appreciation to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, and the Nigerian Army authorities for the confidence reposed in him and his colleagues throughout their military careers.

He further commended everyone who contributed to the successful organisation of the ceremony.

The event was attended by the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, who was represented by the Commander Infantry Corps, Major General Godwin Mutkut.

Other senior officers present included the Commander Armoured Corps, Major General Umar Abubakar; General Officer Commanding 3 Division and Commander Operation Enduring Peace, Major General Maxwell Dangana; Corps Commander Ordnance, Major General Abdullahi Ibrahim; Chief of Personnel Management, Major General Adewale Adekeye; Chief of Special Services and Projects, Major General Aminu Garba; and Commandant Nigerian Army Armour School, Major General Sunday Makolo.

Serving officers, soldiers, family members, friends, well-wishers and members of the barracks community also attended the ceremony to celebrate the retired generals.

Highlights of the event included a ceremonial march past, the traditional pulling-out parade, presentation of souvenirs and group photographs, marking the formal end of the officers’ active military service.

title: 2027: Tinubu can’t save Alli, Yayi, Hamzat – Opposition
description:
Leaders of the All Progressives Congress in Lagos, Ogun and Oyo states are regrouping and intensifying mobilisation to secure victory for the party’s governorship candidates following President Bola Tinubu’s endorsement at Saturday’s campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State.
The renewed push by the rulin
content:
Leaders of the All Progressives Congress in Lagos, Ogun and Oyo states are regrouping and intensifying mobilisation to secure victory for the party’s governorship candidates following President Bola Tinubu’s endorsement at Saturday’s campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State.

The renewed push by the ruling party comes as seven opposition parties, including the Peoples Democratic Party, African Democratic Congress, Labour Party, Nigeria Democratic Congress, Social Democratic Party, Allied Peoples Movement and Young Progressives Party, also move to strengthen their electoral prospects in the three South-West states ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The development has set the stage for a fierce political contest, with APC leaders seeking to consolidate support for their candidates and translate the President’s endorsements into electoral victories, while opposition parties insist they are determined to defeat the ruling party at the polls.

The APC is particularly keen to retain control of Lagos and Ogun states while wresting Oyo State from the opposition, with party leaders stepping up efforts to rally members and supporters behind the three governorship candidates.

At Saturday’s rally held at Mapo Hall, Ibadan, Tinubu publicly endorsed Senator Sharafadeen Alli, Senator Solomon Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, and Obafemi Hamzat as the APC governorship candidates in Oyo, Ogun and Lagos states, respectively.

The President raised the candidates’ hands in a symbolic show of support, telling the gathering, “The governor you will vote for, I will show you,” before presenting Alli to the crowd.

He also endorsed Remi Oseni, the APC senatorial candidate for Oyo South.

The endorsements have given fresh impetus to the ruling party’s campaign efforts in the three states, with the APC seeking to capitalise on the President’s political influence and mobilise support for its candidates.

However, opposition parties have dismissed the endorsements as insufficient to guarantee electoral victories, insisting that the ruling party would face stiff resistance in Lagos, Ogun and Oyo.

In separate exclusive interviews with The PUNCH on Sunday, representatives of the seven opposition parties argued that Tinubu’s backing would not automatically translate into votes, maintaining that the electorate would ultimately determine the outcome of the governorship elections.

Some of the parties described the endorsements as a potential electoral liability, arguing that dissatisfaction with the APC’s performance could undermine the chances of its candidates.

The SDP National Publicity Secretary, Rufus Aiyenigba, said Tinubu’s endorsement posed no threat to the electoral prospects of his party’s candidates.

He said, “The President’s endorsements are not in any way a threat to the chances of the candidates of the SDP. The Nigerian people will surely make their choices and rightly at the polls.”

Similarly, the NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, said the APC had lost the confidence of Nigerians, arguing that no number of endorsements could reverse the ruling party’s declining popularity.

He said, “APC has lost the trust and confidence of the people. No matter the number of endorsements, they have been massively rejected by the majority of Nigerians for their woeful failure and poor performance.

“The NDC is the preferred party by the people, and we shall win by a landslide in most of the states in the coming general elections.”

The Labour Party National Publicity Secretary, Ken Asogwa, went further, describing Tinubu’s endorsement as potentially counterproductive, given what he called the President’s poor performance in office.

Asogwa said although the President had the right to support candidates of his party, the electorate retained the power to decide their political fate.

He said, “The President has the right to endorse the candidates of his party, while the electorate has the ultimate right to decide on election day. How can the Labour Party be bothered by the endorsement made by a President whose record of performance is abysmally poor? Such an endorsement is counterproductive and an own goal against the endorsees.

“We all saw what happened in America recently, where several Republican candidates endorsed by Donald Trump lost elections in the midterms. The few who managed to win were those who were wise enough to extricate themselves from the failures of the Trump presidency.

“So, I am sure the candidates would secretly be cursing the President for bringing misfortune to their campaigns and chances of winning. Meanwhile, in Lagos, where we have Hamzat, who jointly supervised the pillaging of the state’s resources for the past eight years, what is he coming to tell Lagosians?

“The Labour Party candidate in Lagos, Rotimi Odunaike, is speaking to Lagosians, and the preponderance of opinion on the streets of Lagos is that he should be given a chance to come in and turn his dreams into reality.”

In Ogun State, the PDP also dismissed the significance of Tinubu’s endorsement of Yayi, insisting that residents had already made up their minds to vote for the party’s governorship candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu.

The Media Aide to Adebutu, Afolabi Orekoya, told our correspondent on Sunday that the President’s endorsement would not alter the political calculations in the state.

He said, “The endorsement of governorship candidates of Ogun, Oyo and Lagos by President Bola Tinubu during his campaign at Ibadan on Saturday has nothing to do with the chances of the PDP governorship candidate for Ogun State in person of Hon Oladipupo Adebutu.

“It has absolutely nothing to do with our candidate because it is not the President who will come around to vote in the state. The duty of voting in the next governor for the state is purely the prerogative of the residents of Ogun State, and the people are already talking daily that they are pitching their tent with the PDP.

“It is the people that will decide; they are the ones to determine the chances of everyone, and we are happy with the position that the people of the state are taking every day. They are confident that with the PDP back in power, all of this anguish and hardship foisted on them by the APC will become a thing of the past.

“Our campaign watchword is Itura De, meaning that relief is here. So, let the President endorse anybody; it is none of our business because we know that the people have taken their destiny into their hands to ensure that the next party in power in the state is PDP.

“By the special grace of God, the PDP is winning all 26 State House of Assembly members; we are winning all the House of Representatives and the three Senate seats.

“And for the governorship, PDP will clear all six local governments in Ogun Central; we shall clear all nine local governments in Ogun East and in Ogun West we are confident of winning three local governments. So Hon Oladipupo Adebutu will emerge victoriously as the next governor of the state come February 2027.”

The PDP State Publicity Secretary, Kayode Adebayo, also dismissed the endorsement, saying it would not give the APC any electoral advantage in the state.

He said, “Endorsement means nothing and cannot have any political advantage in the 2027 elections, particularly in Ogun State. The people of Ogun State will decide who becomes their governor in 2027, and they are already saying that it is Hon Oladipupo Adebutu and other candidates of our great party that they want.”

Also reacting, the Ogun State Chairman of the African Democratic Party, Otunba Olufemi Soluade, said although Tinubu had the right to endorse candidates of his choice, such backing did not guarantee electoral victory.

 “I can assure you that for our gubernatorial candidate, Otunba Adebisi Jimi Lawal and our other candidates, such endorsement doesn’t pose any threat to their popularity and victory at the polls.

 “The most important thing is the underground works, consultations and other strategies we employed and our continuous efforts and strategies different from the conventional one by other political parties.

“We are already harvesting defectors across the state, and in the coming days, major defectors from NNPP and other political, professional and cultural groups will speak to the popularity of our party, the ADC in the state.”

The Allied Peoples Movement also predicted keen contests for the APC candidates in the three states, arguing that growing opposition support, voter dissatisfaction and changing political alignments could work against the ruling party despite Tinubu’s endorsement.

The APM National Publicity Secretary, Abubakar Yusuf, told The PUNCH that voters in Lagos were increasingly yearning for a change, while the APC candidate in Ogun could face a difficult contest following the court clearance of the PDP candidate, Adebutu.

He said, “It will be keenly contested, particularly in the three states. First, in Lagos State, the consciousness among non-indigenes, particularly the Igbos, to vote for opposition parties, including the APM, NDC and ADC, is rising.

“Secondly, with the new movement and political orientation and reorientation going on in the states, no matter the backing and endorsement, they may lose. In Lagos, people are already tired of Hamzat’s years in government, so they will yearn for a change.

The post 2027: Tinubu can’t save Alli, Yayi, Hamzat – Opposition appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Only 5.3m Nigerians covered by microinsurance – Report
description:
Only 5.3 million Nigerians are covered by microinsurance, despite the country’s exposure to climate-related disasters, health risks and other financial shocks, provisional industry findings for 2026 have shown.
The findings, presented by Edwin Sikaitwa of the Microinsurance Network at the fourth ann
content:
Only 5.3 million Nigerians are covered by microinsurance, despite the country’s exposure to climate-related disasters, health risks and other financial shocks, provisional industry findings for 2026 have shown.

The findings, presented by Edwin Sikaitwa of the Microinsurance Network at the fourth annual GOXI Microinsurance Conference in Lagos, showed that Nigeria had 97 microinsurance products covering approximately 5.3 million people.

The figures highlight the limited reach of microinsurance in a country where millions of households and small businesses remain exposed to financial losses without adequate insurance protection.

The findings also raised concerns about the effectiveness of existing products, showing that many microinsurance schemes spent more on distribution and administrative expenses than they paid out in claims.

The development comes as insurance industry stakeholders push for a decade-long expansion of coverage, with a target of extending affordable protection to more households and businesses by 2036.

Speaking at the conference, the Chairman of GOXI, Godwin Ehigiamusoe, said the need to expand insurance coverage had become more urgent amid growing climate-related risks and inadequate health insurance protection.

He noted that flood threats affected 33 states, while more than 130 million Nigerians lacked health insurance coverage.

Although the Nigerian Insurance Industry Reform Act 2025 had strengthened the capital base of insurance companies, Ehigiamusoe said the industry needed to translate the reforms into meaningful protection for more Nigerians.

He argued that the success of insurance companies should be measured by the number of families that recover financially after suffering losses.

Similarly, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of GOXI, Shina Gbadegesin, said the industry’s priority over the next decade should be expanding coverage through innovation and products designed around customers’ needs.

He disclosed that GOXI had paid more than N821m in claims over six years, stressing that prompt claims settlement was essential to building public confidence in insurance.

“Trust is built one paid claim at a time,” he said.

The Commissioner for Insurance, Olusegun Omosehin, represented by the Deputy Commissioner for Finance and Administration, Ekerete Gam-Ikon, said the success of NIIRA 2025 would depend on whether more Nigerians obtained meaningful insurance protection.

He reaffirmed the National Insurance Commission’s support for digital, embedded and parametric insurance products, while identifying prompt and fair claims settlement as important measures of industry performance.

Presenting the industry’s 2036 outlook, the Managing Consultant and Chief Executive Officer of SOEYA Consult, Yeside Abiodun Oyetayo, urged insurers to move beyond credit-life products and develop comprehensive coverage for underserved populations.

She also called for greater insurance penetration in the North-West and North-East, where adoption remains lowest.

Oyetayo said the industry should focus on the actual protection delivered to policyholders rather than the number of policies sold.

Paul Ehiagbonare of Miva Open University and the uLesson Group identified poor product design as another factor limiting insurance adoption.

He argued that insurance companies needed to develop products around customers’ financial circumstances and risks, rather than relying on conventional offerings that might not meet their needs.

He advocated customer-centred product development, artificial intelligence and data-triggered payouts to simplify insurance services and accelerate claims settlement.

title: ECOWAS Monetary Union: Cardoso advocates equity, fairness in governance structure
description:
By Babajide KomolafeThe Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Mr. Olayemi Cardoso, has called for equity, fairness and proportional representation in the governance structure of the proposed ECOWAS Monetary Union.







He stressed that while regional solidarity and respect for the soverei
content:
By Babajide Komolafe
The Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Mr. Olayemi Cardoso, has called for equity, fairness and proportional representation in the governance structure of the proposed ECOWAS Monetary Union.

He stressed that while regional solidarity and respect for the sovereign equality of member states must remain fundamental principles of the Union, these should be appropriately balanced with the relative financial commitments, responsibilities and risks borne by individual member states, particularly in determining participation in decision-making and governance.


Cardoso made the call on Friday, November 20, 2026, in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, on behalf of Nigeria at the Ministerial Session of the 6th Presidential Task Force Meeting on the ECOWAS Single Currency Programme in Abidjan, Cote d’ Ivoire.
The Ministerial Committee of the ECOWAS Presidential Task Force comprises Ministers of Finance and Governors of central banks of PTF member states.


He described the meeting as a defining milestone in the ECOWAS monetary integration process, noting that deliberations had recently focused on critical considerations regarding the institutional architecture of the proposed Monetary Union, including the location of its institutions, leadership appointments, and the allocation of authority and responsibilities.
“The decisions we take today will shape the future of the Union for decades to come,” Cardoso told delegates. “They will influence its credibility in the eyes of investors and development partners, its legitimacy in the eyes of our citizens, and the confidence of Member States that their commitments are being matched by a meaningful voice within the institutions they are helping to build.”
He restated Nigeria’s commitment to the ECOWAS Monetary Cooperation Programme and to establishing the ECO, describing it as “longstanding and unwavering” and citing substantial financial contributions, sustained technical support, and compromises made “in the broader interest of regional consensus”.
“Nigeria has and will continue to demonstrate solidarity and fairness, respecting the sovereignty of other member states. We remain fully committed to the successful establishment of the ECO and to a Monetary Union that is credible, sustainable and beneficial to all Member States,” Cardoso declared.
He, however, maintained that solidarity must be accompanied by equity, arguing that countries with larger economies and greater financial responsibilities should be given fair consideration in the governance of the institutions they support.
“While bigger economies continue to take up the burden, they should also be considered to play a significant role because of the risk and systemic importance they have in the sub-region. Above all, such economies need to defend the huge contribution they make before their respective parliaments and the civil society. Where obligations are shared but influence is not, arrangements may be agreed, but their long-term sustainability may be difficult to guarantee,” he added.
Reiterating Nigeria’s position, Governor Cardoso emphasised that the country’s stance was not driven by dominance or entitlement but by a sense of responsibility stemming from its status as the region’s largest economy and one of the principal contributors to the proposed Union.
He noted that Nigeria “will commit substantial financial resources, reserves and institutional capital to the success of the Monetary Union”, adding that it is therefore reasonable that responsibility, accountability and participation in governance should be appropriately aligned with the scale of those commitments.

title: Emmanuel, Quadre sweep  Da-Silva tennis championship titles
description:
Nigeria’s Michael Emmanuel and Oyinlomo Quadre completed a memorable campaign at the maiden Destiny Da-Silva Tennis Open Championship, winning the men’s and women’s singles titles respectively on Saturday at the National Stadium, Surulere, Lagos.
Emmanuel, who entered the tournament as Nigeria’s thi
content:
Nigeria’s Michael Emmanuel and Oyinlomo Quadre completed a memorable campaign at the maiden Destiny Da-Silva Tennis Open Championship, winning the men’s and women’s singles titles respectively on Saturday at the National Stadium, Surulere, Lagos.

Emmanuel, who entered the tournament as Nigeria’s third-ranked player, defeated Yusuf Abubakar 6-2, 6-3 to claim the men’s singles crown, while Quadre overcame Success Ogujobi 6-1, 6-1 to win the women’s title.

The victories completed a successful outing for both players, who had earlier won their respective doubles events on Friday.

Emmanuel partnered Matthew Abamu to the men’s doubles title, with the pair defeating Ikechukwu Iloputa and Chima Michael 6-1, 3-6, 10-7.

Quadre also claimed the women’s doubles crown alongside Ntoro Bassey. They recovered from losing the first set to beat teenagers Aina Goodnews and Samuel Gloria 3-6, 6-2, 10-5.

Speaking after her singles victory, Quadre said winning the title had been her target from the start of the competition.

“That was my goal coming into this tournament and I’m very happy to achieve that.

“It wasn’t exactly easy. The points were going pretty fast, but I had to stay locked in because she’s a really good player,” she said.

Tournament organiser Destiny Da-Silva praised the quality of tennis on display, saying the championship had provided an opportunity to discover emerging talents.

“I have witnessed tennis tournaments in several countries, and Nigeria most especially, but I have never seen the kinds of talents that have been on display. We have discovered some new talents and they have been excellent on the court, and they behave well off the court too,” he said.

Da-Silva also disclosed plans to expand the championship next year, with an international edition and a separate competition for Nigerian players.

“Come next year, this tournament will become international. We will not only have the international edition; we will also have a local version for Nigerian players,” he said.

In the wheelchair women’s category, Andrea Usoh and Chitturu Nwaozuzu won the doubles title after defeating Chika Enwerem and Bisoye Bankole 6-1, 6-2.

Nwaozuzu subsequently completed a singles and doubles double, beating Usoh 6-4, 6-4 in the wheelchair women’s singles final.

In the men’s wheelchair category, top seed Alex Adewale defeated Razaki Bankole to win the singles title and also partnered Pelumi Odunuga to claim the doubles crown.

Edet Akpaso emerged victorious in the veterans’ men’s singles category, defeating Samuel Obadofin 6-4, 4-6, 10-6.

The men’s and women’s singles champions received N1.5m each, while the runners-up earned N885,000 apiece.

Doubles winners in the men’s and women’s categories received N500,000, with the runners-up taking home N295,000.

In the wheelchair events, the singles champions received N500,000 each, while the runners-up earned N295,000. The wheelchair doubles winners received N300,000, with the runners-up getting N177,000.

The veterans’ men’s singles champion also received N300,000, while the runner-up went home with N177,000.

The post Emmanuel, Quadre sweep Da-Silva tennis championship titles appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Hutchison hails Awoniyi’s ‘cultured’ finish against Palace
description:
Former Liverpool midfielder Don Hutchison has praised Taiwo Awoniyi’s finishing after the Nigerian striker scored in Coventry City’s 3-2 victory over Crystal Palace on Saturday.
Awoniyi opened the scoring in the fifth minute at the Coventry Building Society Arena, connecting with Jack Rudoni’s deliv
content:
Former Liverpool midfielder Don Hutchison has praised Taiwo Awoniyi’s finishing after the Nigerian striker scored in Coventry City’s 3-2 victory over Crystal Palace on Saturday.

Awoniyi opened the scoring in the fifth minute at the Coventry Building Society Arena, connecting with Jack Rudoni’s delivery with a first-time effort into the bottom corner.

Reacting to the goal on the Premier League’s official website, Hutchison described it as a “cultured finish”, applauding the striker’s composure and technique.

“What a well-worked team goal this is, and what a cultured finish from Awoniyi,” he said.

“He opens up his right foot, opens up the angle and guides the ball away from the goalkeeper and into the bottom corner.”

The strike was Awoniyi’s second Premier League goal this season, following his effort in Coventry’s 3-1 victory over Sunderland on October 31.

The 29-year-old, who joined Coventry in the summer, was substituted at half-time after reporting an ankle problem. Manager Frank Lampard subsequently confirmed that the striker had wanted to continue but was unable to do so.

Coventry eventually secured all three points through a late own goal by Dwight McNeil, having earlier seen Awoniyi give them the advantage.

Hutchison’s praise comes as Awoniyi continues his return to regular football following an injury-disrupted spell at Nottingham Forest.
