title: Seven levels to mastering your finances
description:
Financial independence depends less on earnings than on effective money management, disciplined savings, multiple income sources and strategic investments that build wealth, strengthen financial security and secure the future, writes GODWIN AIKIGBE
Level 1: Surviving on salary
The first level is whe
content:
Financial independence depends less on earnings than on effective money management, disciplined savings, multiple income sources and strategic investments that build wealth, strengthen financial security and secure the future, writes GODWIN AIKIGBE

Level 1: Surviving on salary

The first level is where many salary earners find themselves: depending entirely on their monthly paychecks to meet their financial obligations.

At this stage, an individual’s income comes primarily from employment, and virtually every naira earned is committed to expenses before the next payday. Rent, transportation, food, school fees, utility bills, family responsibilities, loan repayments and other recurring expenses consume most, if not all, of the monthly earnings.

Some workers begin each month with the hope of saving but discover that their salaries have disappeared before they can put anything aside. Others depend on salary advances, overdrafts or loans to survive towards the end of the month.

This situation can create a cycle in which an individual works primarily to meet immediate financial obligations without making meaningful progress towards long-term financial security.

The danger of living exclusively on a paycheck is that it leaves little room for unexpected events. A medical bill, vehicle breakdown, sudden job loss or urgent family responsibility can destabilise the individual’s finances.

However, being at this level does not necessarily mean someone is financially irresponsible. In an economy characterised by rising living costs and competing demands, some workers genuinely struggle to make their earnings cover essential needs.

The first step towards improvement is to understand the difference between earning money and making financial progress. Earning a salary is important, but the ability to retain part of that income, however small, is what begins the journey towards financial stability.

Level 2: Start budgeting

The second level is learning how to budget.

A budget is a spending plan based on an individual’s income and expenses. It provides a clear picture of how much money comes in, how much goes out and what remains after financial obligations have been met.

Without a budget, many people spend money based on immediate needs, emotions and convenience. They may know their monthly salaries but have little understanding of how much they spend on food, transportation, entertainment, subscriptions, shopping and other activities.

Budgeting introduces discipline and accountability into personal finances. It requires individuals to assign specific purposes to their income rather than spending without a clear plan.

One major advantage of budgeting is that it prepares people for unpredictable life events. Although a budget cannot prevent emergencies, it can help individuals anticipate financial demands and make provisions for unexpected expenses.

It also makes it easier to plan for major purchases. Whether someone intends to buy a car, acquire a property, pay school fees, renovate a home or finance further education, a budget provides a framework for gradually setting aside the required funds.

Another benefit is that budgeting reveals an individual’s financial position and spending patterns. By reviewing income and expenses, people can identify areas where money is being wasted and redirect those resources towards more important priorities.

The importance of monitoring seemingly insignificant expenses was captured by Benjamin Franklin, who warned that “a small leak will sink a great ship”. This observation is particularly relevant to personal finance because small, seemingly harmless expenses can accumulate into substantial amounts over time.

For instance, someone who spends a considerable amount on frequent restaurant visits, impulse purchases or unnecessary subscriptions may discover that reducing such expenses could free up money for savings and investments.

There are different budgeting methods, including zero-based budgeting, the 50/30/20 rule and the envelope system. The most appropriate method depends on an individual’s income, responsibilities and financial goals.

The 50/30/20 rule, for example, recommends allocating 50 per cent of income to needs, 30 per cent to wants and 20 per cent to savings and debt repayment. However, people facing high living costs may need to adjust these proportions.

The important thing is to establish a realistic spending plan, review it regularly and ensure that savings and financial goals are treated as priorities rather than afterthoughts.

Level 3: Debt repayment

The third level is tackling debt, particularly expensive debt that consumes a significant portion of income.

For many people, debt is one of the biggest obstacles to financial progress. Credit card balances, payday loans, high-interest personal loans and other expensive borrowing arrangements can gradually undermine an individual’s ability to save and invest.

Debt becomes particularly dangerous when borrowers repeatedly take new loans to repay existing obligations. This creates a cycle in which a growing portion of future income is committed to servicing past spending.

The consequences of excessive borrowing were highlighted by Benjamin Franklin, who observed that “he that goes a borrowing goes a sorrowing”. Although borrowing can sometimes be useful, particularly when it finances productive activities, excessive debt can become a serious financial burden.

Budgeting helps expose this problem because it shows precisely where money is going. Once individuals understand their spending patterns, they can identify how much of their income is being consumed by loan repayments and interest charges.

The next step is to develop a repayment strategy.

One approach is the debt avalanche method, which involves prioritising debts with the highest interest rates while making minimum payments on other obligations. This can reduce the total interest paid over time.

Another is the debt snowball method, which involves paying off the smallest debts first while maintaining minimum payments on others. Clearing smaller obligations can provide psychological motivation to continue tackling larger debts.

Whichever approach is adopted, the objective should be to reduce expensive borrowing and avoid accumulating new unnecessary obligations.

However, it is important to distinguish between productive borrowing and harmful debt. Not all debt is necessarily bad. A carefully structured loan used to finance a viable business, acquire an income-generating asset or fund an investment with reasonable prospects may serve a useful purpose.

Nevertheless, borrowing should be approached cautiously. Individuals must consider interest rates, repayment periods, associated charges and their ability to meet obligations even when income falls.

Paying off expensive debt frees up money that would otherwise have gone towards interest payments. It also improves financial flexibility and creates room for savings and investment.

Level 4: Saving more

Once expensive debt has been brought under control, the next level is increasing savings.

Saving is one of the most important habits in personal finance because it creates the financial resources needed to meet future obligations without depending entirely on borrowed money.

At this stage, individuals should have a clearer understanding of their income and expenses, established a budget and made progress towards reducing their debt burden.

The money previously used to service expensive loans can now be redirected towards savings.

However, saving requires consistency. It should not depend on whether an individual has money left at the end of the month. Instead, it should be incorporated into the monthly financial plan.

Benjamin Franklin’s advice on wealth creation remains relevant: “If you would be wealthy, think of saving as well as of getting.” The message is simple: earning money is only one part of building wealth; retaining some of it is equally important.

One practical approach is to save immediately after receiving a salary or other income. This is commonly described as paying yourself first.

For example, someone earning N300,000 monthly could decide to save N30,000 before attending to discretionary expenses. Maintaining this habit for a year would produce N360,000, excluding any interest or investment returns.

The amount saved will depend on income, household responsibilities and other financial commitments. People with limited earnings may begin with smaller amounts and increase their contributions as their circumstances improve.

It is also important to distinguish between short-term savings and money intended for long-term investment. Funds needed within a few months should generally be kept in accessible, relatively low-risk accounts or instruments rather than exposed to significant market fluctuations.

The objective at this level is to build a savings culture and develop the discipline to retain part of every income received.

Ov time, consistent savings can provide the foundation for emergency funds, major purchases, business opportunities and investments.

Level 5: Build emergency fund

The fifth level is establishing an emergency fund.

While ordinary savings may be intended for planned purchases and future goals, an emergency fund is specifically designed to provide financial protection when unexpected events occur.

Life is unpredictable. People can lose their jobs, experience medical emergencies, face urgent home repairs or encounter unexpected family responsibilities. Without financial reserves, such situations may force them to borrow money, sell valuable assets or abandon important financial plans.

An emergency fund serves as a financial cushion against these uncertainties.

Financial experts commonly recommend keeping between three and six months of essential living expenses in an emergency fund. However, individuals with irregular incomes, dependants or less secure employment may need to consider a larger reserve.

For instance, if someone’s essential monthly expenses amount to N200,000, a six-month emergency fund would require N1.2m.

The fund should be kept somewhere safe and accessible, such as an appropriate savings account or other suitable low-risk, liquid financial instrument.

It should not be confused with money intended for holidays, shopping, entertainment or speculative investments. Its purpose is to provide support during genuine emergencies.

Having an emergency fund reduces dependence on family members, friends, employers and financial institutions when unexpected expenses arise.

It also provides peace of mind. Individuals who know they have money available to handle temporary financial difficulties are generally better positioned to make rational decisions without the pressure of immediate financial distress.

Building such a reserve may take time, particularly for people with modest incomes. The important thing is to start, contribute regularly and avoid using the money for non-emergency purposes.

Level 6: Increase income streams

The sixth level involves moving beyond dependence on a single source of income.

For many workers, salaries provide financial stability, but relying exclusively on employment income can limit opportunities to build wealth. Job losses, salary delays, economic downturns and unexpected changes in the workplace can expose the vulnerability of depending on one income source.

Developing additional income streams can provide greater financial flexibility and accelerate progress towards financial independence.

One way to achieve this is through a side hustle. Individuals can use their professional skills, experience, interests or available time to provide services outside their regular employment.

For example, a journalist could undertake writing, editing, research or communication consultancy. An accountant could offer bookkeeping services, while a teacher could provide private lessons or develop educational materials.

Other opportunities include catering, fashion design, photography, digital marketing, graphic design, content creation, agricultural ventures, online retail and professional consultancy.

The opportunities are numerous, but individuals must carefully assess the time, resources, skills and capital required before committing to any venture.

A side business should not be started simply because someone else appears to be making money from it. Researching the market, understanding customer needs, calculating costs and identifying potential risks are essential.

It is equally important to manage additional income responsibly. Rather than immediately increasing personal consumption, individuals should consider using part of the proceeds to strengthen savings, expand the business and invest.

Some side hustles may eventually grow into full-time businesses. Others may remain supplementary sources of income. Either outcome can be valuable if the venture is profitable and sustainable.

However, people in paid employment should also consider their employment contracts, workplace policies and the need to maintain a healthy balance between their jobs and additional activities.

The ultimate objective is to develop income sources that reduce financial vulnerability and create more opportunities for wealth accumulation.

Level 7: Start investing

The seventh level is where individuals begin using money as a tool to generate more money.

Saving is essential for financial security, but keeping all one’s money in cash or ordinary savings accounts may not be sufficient to achieve long-term wealth creation. Inflation can gradually reduce the purchasing power of money, making it important to consider appropriate investment opportunities.

Investing involves committing money to assets or financial instruments with the expectation of generating income, capital appreciation or both.

Unlike saving, investing generally involves some degree of risk. The value of investments can rise or fall, and returns are not guaranteed. Therefore, individuals must understand what they are investing in before committing their money.

The importance of looking beyond the price of an investment was captured by renowned investor Warren Buffett, who said, “Price is what you pay; value is what you get.” The observation, which Buffett credited to his mentor Benjamin Graham, highlights the importance of understanding the underlying value of an investment rather than being carried away by its market price.

There are several investment options available, depending on an individual’s financial goals, risk tolerance, investment horizon and available capital.

In Nigeria, these include Federal Government bonds, Treasury bills, commercial papers, mutual funds, equities, exchange-traded funds, real estate and carefully evaluated business investments.

Government securities may appeal to investors seeking relatively predictable returns, while equities offer opportunities to participate in the growth and profitability of listed companies. However, stock prices fluctuate, and investors can lose money.

Mutual funds and exchange-traded funds provide opportunities to invest in diversified portfolios without having to select every individual security.

Real estate can generate rental income and potential capital appreciation, although it requires substantial capital and involves expenses relating to maintenance, taxes, documentation and property management.

Investors must also consider liquidity, transaction costs, taxation and the credibility of investment providers.

One important principle is diversification. Rather than committing all available funds to one asset or investment opportunity, investors can spread their money across different asset classes to reduce exposure to a single risk.

It is also important to establish clear investment objectives. Some people invest to generate regular income, others seek long-term capital growth, while some prioritise preserving their capital against inflation.

The investment strategy should reflect these objectives.

Before investing, individuals should ensure that they have adequate emergency savings, manageable debt and sufficient understanding of the risks involved. They should also avoid schemes promising unrealistic or guaranteed returns, particularly those that depend on recruiting new participants.

Professional financial advice may be useful when making significant investment decisions.

Ultimately, investing is about allowing money to work alongside personal effort. Instead of depending entirely on wages or business profits, individuals can gradually build assets capable of generating income and appreciating in value.

Conclusion

The seven levels illustrate that financial independence is a gradual process rather than an achievement that happens overnight.

An individual cannot realistically expect to move from living paycheck to paycheck to becoming a successful investor without first developing the habits and financial discipline required to manage money.

Budgeting creates awareness. Debt repayment reduces financial pressure. Saving builds discipline, while an emergency fund provides protection against uncertainty. Additional income streams create opportunities to accumulate more money, and investing provides a pathway towards long-term wealth creation.

However, these levels should not be treated as rigid rules. People can work on several of them simultaneously, depending on their circumstances. Someone may begin investing small amounts while still repaying manageable debt, provided essential expenses and emergency needs are adequately addressed.

The most important lesson is that financial progress requires intentional decisions. Increasing income without controlling expenditure may not improve one’s financial position. Saving without investing may limit long-term growth, while investing without adequate knowledge can expose hard-earned money to unnecessary risks.

Money is a tool, and how effectively it serves an individual depends largely on the decisions made about earning, spending, saving, borrowing and investing.

The objective should not be to accumulate money merely for the sake of having it. Rather, it should be to achieve a level of financial security that provides choices, reduces dependence on others and creates opportunities to pursue meaningful goals.

The post Seven levels to mastering your finances appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: LAWMA rolls out 60-day operational efficiency plan
description:
The Acting Managing Director of the Lagos Waste Management Authority, Olajuwon Akinyemi, has unveiled a 60-day action plan focused on rapid waste evacuation, improved operational efficiency and institutional repositioning, as part of efforts to restore the Authority’s past glory.
 Akinyemi unveiled
content:
The Acting Managing Director of the Lagos Waste Management Authority, Olajuwon Akinyemi, has unveiled a 60-day action plan focused on rapid waste evacuation, improved operational efficiency and institutional repositioning, as part of efforts to restore the Authority’s past glory.

 Akinyemi unveiled the plan while addressing the  management and staff at a workers’ forum held at LAWMA’s headquarters in Ijora-Olopa on Friday. He was accompanied by the Acting Executive Director, Operations, Dr Olorunwa Tijani, and the Executive Director, Finance, Mr Kunle Adebiyi.

 LAWMA disclosed this in a statement over the weekend.

 Akinyemi explained that the immediate focus of the new management was to boost the Authority’s operational capacity, “particularly in waste evacuation, field monitoring and regulatory enforcement, while introducing strategic changes to improve service delivery across Lagos State.”

 Reflecting on his earlier years of service at LAWMA and other government institutions, Akinyemi urged employees to foster teamwork, adopt constructive attitudes and renew their dedication to their duties. He noted that repositioning the Authority would depend on the collective efforts and full participation of all staff members.

 “We are bringing in resilience and a new paradigm shift. It is a new wave in handling waste in Lagos. We already have the template to transform LAWMA positively. All we need to do is recreate, modernise and do better than in the past,” he stated.

 Under the 60-day action plan, Akinyemi revealed that staff would be strategically redeployed across the state’s three operational districts, with consideration given to their knowledge of various terrains and communities. He said the move was aimed at strengthening field monitoring, improving operational response and raising service delivery standards.

 He also disclosed plans to establish regional operational centres across the state to decentralise waste management activities, enhance supervision and ensure that interventions reached communities more promptly, particularly areas requiring urgent attention.

 Akinyemi further outlined plans to intensify community engagement and public enlightenment on proper waste sorting at source and responsible waste disposal, noting that traditional rulers, Community Development Association leaders, market associations, artisans and other community stakeholders would be mobilised to support efforts to curb indiscriminate dumping.

 He emphasised the need for stronger engagement with Private Sector Participation operators and greater public compliance with approved waste collection tariffs, describing collaboration among the Authority, service providers and residents as essential to achieving a cleaner Lagos.

 On staff welfare, Akinyemi assured employees of management’s commitment to their well-being, disclosing efforts to facilitate the procurement of Compressed Natural Gas-powered staff buses to ease transport challenges.

 Earlier, the Acting Executive Director, Operations, Dr Olorunwa Tijani, expressed delight at reuniting with the LAWMA family, assuring staff that the Authority’s operational framework would receive urgent attention and revitalisation to improve performance.

 He stressed the need for a more effective operational structure and pledged his support for the new management’s drive to reposition the Authority and strengthen service delivery.

 Also speaking, the Executive Director, Finance, Mr Kunle Adebiyi, expressed confidence in the capacity of the new leadership to reposition the Authority, pledging his support and commitment to teamwork.

 Adebiyi emphasised the importance of prudent financial management, accountability and effective resource utilisation, noting that successful implementation of the 60-day action plan would require synergy among all staff, directorates, departments and units.

 He urged employees to demonstrate professionalism, commitment and a shared sense of responsibility.

 The Acting Managing Director later toured various departments within the Authority, accompanied by the Acting Executive Director, Operations, and other management officials. During the visit, he engaged with staff to obtain first-hand knowledge of their responsibilities and the operational challenges they face.

The post LAWMA rolls out 60-day operational efficiency plan appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Sanwo-Olu advocates flexible mortgages to boost homeownership
description:
The Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has called for mortgage options where buyers can demonstrate long-term repayment capacity.
 Sanwo-Olu stated this over the weekend during the inauguration of Treasure Estate in the Ajah area of Lagos, according to a statement.
 He stressed that the gover
content:
The Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has called for mortgage options where buyers can demonstrate long-term repayment capacity.

 Sanwo-Olu stated this over the weekend during the inauguration of Treasure Estate in the Ajah area of Lagos, according to a statement.

 He stressed that the government uses both public and private financing to expand access to decent housing, while assuring residents that external road access and estate drainage infrastructure would be properly addressed.

 “Developers should explore mortgage options where buyers can demonstrate long-term repayment capacity. The government uses both public and private financing to expand access to decent housing while assuring residents that external road access and estate drainage infrastructure would be properly addressed,” Sanwo-Olu said.

 Sanwo-Olu acknowledged the long-standing land challenges that trailed the property for years before its eventual delivery.

 He disclosed that the state was preparing to inaugurate two housing estates in the Ajah area, assuring that political campaign periods would not disrupt governance or delay the handover of completed projects.

 “We know we are in a season, but the campaigning season we have must not stop the work that we do. The delivery remains a core pillar of the mandate given to his administration,” he assured.

 Sanwo-Olu explained that Treasure Estate was not designed exclusively for high-end buyers but to accommodate ordinary residents, including young professionals purchasing their first homes and growing families looking for adequate space and a secure living environment.

 “This is an estate that is not high-end. It has one-bedroom, two-bedroom and three-bedroom units. So, as a young person, you can afford a one-bedroom flat; you can do a two-bedroom as a young family, or a three-bedroom flat or three-bedroom terrace,” Sanwo-Olu explained.

 He also called on new homeowners and surrounding neighbours to foster a peaceful, welcoming community.

 Speaking on the economic realities surrounding the project, the Chief Executive Officer of AKF Properties Limited, Mr Ayodeji Fadoju, drew attention to the significant increase in construction costs between the commencement of the project around 2024–2025 and its completion.

 “A bag of cement, which cost about N5,000 when work began, rose to over N12,000 by delivery, alongside broader increases across building materials,” Fadoju said.

 He highlighted that, despite those pressures, determination and collaboration between LSDPC and AKF Properties enabled delivery to specification.

 “Gone are the days when you needed to pay 100 per cent for your houses,” the CEO said.

 He urged Nigerians and labour unions to take advantage of single-digit mortgage options when they meet documentation and repayment requirements.

 The Managing Director of LSDPC, Mr Ayodeji Joseph, described Treasure Estate as proof of how public land assets and private-sector expertise can combine to deliver housing and economic value.

 He also announced that Dogo Court in Apapa had been completed and was awaiting formal inauguration by the governor, while four additional housing estates were slated for unveiling between January and June 2027.

 Treasure Estate was developed under a joint venture agreement signed in 2023 between the Lagos State Development and Property Corporation and AKF Properties Limited. The estate occupies about 28,674 square metres of land covered by a Certificate of Occupancy issued by the state government to LSDPC.

The post Sanwo-Olu advocates flexible mortgages to boost homeownership appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Tinubu has approved N450bn for farmers – APC-PCC
description:

By Omeiza Ajayi



ABUJA — The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, APC-PCC, said, yesterday, President Bola Tinubu has approved a N1.5 trillion recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture, BoA, and committed N450 billion to agricultura
content:
•Commits N1.5tr recapitalisation to BoA 

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA — The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, APC-PCC, said, yesterday, President Bola Tinubu has approved a N1.5 trillion recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture, BoA, and committed N450 billion to agricultural financing programmes.

The council said the commitment was meant “to strengthen food security, expand domestic production, and improve the productivity of smallholder farmers across the country, especially in Northern Nigeria.”

In a statement issued by the spokesperson, Dele Alake, the council said the bank had reached “over 500,000 smallholder farmers.”

It added that the President “also approved a N1.5 trillion recapitalisation to expand agricultural financing and support the cultivation of 500,000 hectares under the Renewed Hope Agenda.”

According to the statement, the federal government “went beyond providing farmers with loans; it also addressed access to quality seeds, fertiliser, mechanisation, irrigation, storage facilities, commodity markets, and other essential components of the agricultural value chain.”

On the recapitalisation, the council, which noted that it was a major campaign promise of the President in 2023, said the move was designed “to enhance the bank’s financial capacity and ability to provide more affordable and accessible funding to farmers, agricultural cooperatives, processors, aggregators, and other businesses operating across the agricultural value chain.”

The statement added: “Under President Tinubu, a stronger Bank of Agriculture would be better positioned to support large-scale agricultural investments, expand its reach to underserved farming communities, and mobilise additional resources for domestic food production.”

The council disclosed that the Renewed Hope Smallholder Support and Value Chain Fund, which had a programme value of N250 billion, financed farmers through Farmer Aggregation Companies.

These companies, it said, “coordinate farmer registration, input distribution, extension services, and market linkages.”

The programme, according to the statement, has reached more than 500,000 smallholder farmers across 16 states, including over 70,000 women.

It has also supported the distribution of approximately 2.5 million bags of fertiliser and 300,000 bags of certified seeds. The council said the programme targets two million farmers and the distribution of more than 10 million bags of fertiliser. It named Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Niger, Borno, Gombe, Taraba, Adamawa, Yobe and Bauchi among the states receiving attention under the scheme.

To shield farmers from price shocks, the statement said, the bank is implementing a N200 billion Guaranteed Minimum Price Programme. Under it, the bank “has procured approximately 170,000 metric tonnes of maize, rice, sorghum, and cassava to strengthen commodity markets and protect farmers against distress sales.”

The council also said the bank created an Onion Financing Programme in partnership with the National Onion Producers, Processors and Marketers Association of Nigeria, NOPPMAN, which “represents over 11,800 onion farmers.”

The scheme, it noted, provided onion farmers with improved seeds and fertiliser, supported processors with commodity purchase funds, and helped develop storage and solar-powered cooling facilities to cut post-harvest losses.

“Under the arrangement, cooperatives will contribute 30 per cent of their input costs, while BOA will finance the remaining 70 per cent,” the statement said.

On dry-season farming, it said the bank is working with the All-Farmers Association of Nigeria “to develop a pipeline targeting 400,000 farmers for the 2026 farming cycle.” The initiative covers financing for 120,000 hectares of wheat and another 300,000 hectares for crops including rice, maize, sorghum, millet, cassava and soybeans.

The council added that the Nigeria Ginger Recovery Programme has supported 3,200 farmers in Kachia, Kaduna State, with blight-free seeds. It said more than 9,000 bags have been recovered for multiplication, with an expansion planned across 20,000 hectares in 16 states.

For women, the bank is “targeting at least 50,000 women nationwide through insured cooperative production financing at nine per cent, in partnership with the Federal Ministries of Women Affairs and Agriculture.”

On mechanisation, the statement said 1,571 tractors have been deployed to 23 states under the Renewed Hope National Agricultural Mechanisation Programme. They are expected to mechanise 1.2 million hectares of farmland.

It also cited a ₦385 billion productive-use-of-electricity programme, which “provides 44,000 electric cargo tricycles and 100,000 solar irrigation pumps, targeting 500,000 farming families.”

“The interventions demonstrated President Tinubu’s commitment to transforming agriculture into a major driver of economic growth, food security, and job creation,” the council added.

title: Ogunbote rues missed chances after Plateau draw
description:
Plateau United coach Gbenga Ogunbote has blamed his side’s poor finishing for their failure to secure victory against Ranchers Bees after settling for a 1-1 draw in Saturday’s Nigeria Premier Football League encounter in Minna.
The Peace Boys took an early lead through Vangsou Tchadienne in the fift
content:
Plateau United coach Gbenga Ogunbote has blamed his side’s poor finishing for their failure to secure victory against Ranchers Bees after settling for a 1-1 draw in Saturday’s Nigeria Premier Football League encounter in Minna.

The Peace Boys took an early lead through Vangsou Tchadienne in the fifth minute at the Bako Kontagora Stadium, but Jamilu Yusuf restored parity for the hosts seven minutes later.

Plateau created further opportunities to regain the lead but failed to convert them, leaving Ogunbote disappointed with his players’ wastefulness in front of goal.

“It wasn’t a bad outing, but no matter what, we were a bit wasteful. We didn’t take our chances. Had we converted them, it would have been a comfortable victory for us,” Ogunbote told the club’s media.

The former Shooting Stars coach, however, took consolation in securing a point away from home, insisting that his team would continue working towards ending their wait for a first away victory.

“All the same, one point on the road isn’t a bad one. We will keep hunting until we get the victory on the road,” he added.

The draw leaves Plateau United fourth on the table with 20 points from 14 matches, while the Jos-based side will return home to face Ikorodu City in their next league fixture.

Ranchers Bees, meanwhile, will take encouragement from recovering from the early setback to earn a point on home soil, while Plateau will be left to rue another missed opportunity to secure maximum points away from home.

The post Ogunbote rues missed chances after Plateau draw appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Okoko claims third straight title at Alpha Bravo Classic
description:
Nineteen-year-old Godwin Okoko has extended his remarkable winning run to three consecutive titles in less than four weeks, claiming the maiden Alpha Bravo Classic at Lakowe Lakes Golf Club, Lagos, after overturning a two-shot deficit to Ghana’s Vincent Torgah during the weekend.
The Nigerian teenag
content:
Nineteen-year-old Godwin Okoko has extended his remarkable winning run to three consecutive titles in less than four weeks, claiming the maiden Alpha Bravo Classic at Lakowe Lakes Golf Club, Lagos, after overturning a two-shot deficit to Ghana’s Vincent Torgah during the weekend.

The Nigerian teenager’s latest triumph follows victories at the Rift Valley Championship in Nakuru, Kenya, on October 27, and the seventh CIO Classic in Port Harcourt two weeks ago, where he set a new course record with a 22-under-par total of 266.

His only non-winning finish in his last four tournaments came at the 26th Ivory Coast Open, where he placed third behind Torgah and compatriot Sunday Olapade.

Okoko sealed the Alpha Bravo title with a four-under-par 68 to finish on eight-under-par 208, following rounds of 72, 68 and 68. His final-round charge displaced Torgah, who had led after the opening two rounds with identical scores of 69 but eventually settled for second place on six-under-par 210.

Uganda’s Ronald Rugumayo finished third on 213, while Nigeria’s Kamalu Bako and Kenya’s Samuel Njoroge tied for fourth on 216.

The maiden championship attracted professionals from five African countries — Nigeria, Ghana, Uganda, Kenya and Rwanda — with the $25,000 event co-sanctioned by the Sunshine Development Tour (SDT) and Safari Tour.

The tournament offered Official World Golf Ranking points and Safari Tour ranking points, providing participants with an opportunity to strengthen their prospects of qualifying for the 2027 Magical Kenya Open.

Alpha Bravo Chief Executive Officer, Tonbara Okoria, said the company’s investment in golf was aimed at providing emerging talents with opportunities to compete on the global stage.

“Our investment in golf is targeted at giving talents like Godwin Okoko the opportunity to showcase their abilities on a global platform. Africa has tremendous golfing talent, but these players need the right platforms, exposure and competitive opportunities to reach their full potential,” Okoria said.

He added that the championship reflected the company’s commitment to strengthening African golf by providing professionals across the continent with opportunities to compete, improve their rankings and advance their careers.

For Okoko, the victory in Lagos caps an impressive four-week stretch in which he has won three titles across Nigeria and Kenya, further establishing the teenager as one of the emerging talents in African professional golf.

The post Okoko claims third straight title at Alpha Bravo Classic appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Attacks On Shipping In Strait Of Hormuz Reach Highest Levels Since Iran War Began
description: Gambiaj.com – (WASHINGTON, UNITED STATES) – Reported attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz have reached their highest levels since the Iran war began in late February, according to maritime data, as Tehran steps up efforts to reassert control over the strategic waterway a
content:
Gambiaj.com – (WASHINGTON, UNITED STATES) – Reported attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz have reached their highest levels since the Iran war began in late February, according to maritime data, as Tehran steps up efforts to reassert control over the strategic waterway amid falling oil prices and mounting pressure on its oil revenues.

More than 30 attacks were reported to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Center (UKMTO), which is affiliated with the Royal Navy, in October, marking the highest monthly figure since the conflict began.

At least 22 attacks had also been reported in November as of Sunday, making it the second-highest monthly total since the outbreak of the war, according to an analysis of UKMTO data by CNN. The reporting area covers the Strait of Hormuz, the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.

Before October, reported attacks in the region averaged around 10 per month. Data from the International Maritime Organization (IMO) also identifies October as the month with the highest number of confirmed maritime incidents so far this year.

Rising Threat To Global Shipping

The Strait of Hormuz has become a major flashpoint in the conflict, with repeated attacks disrupting commercial shipping and threatening global oil and gas supplies.

Iran began attempting to halt maritime traffic through the strait following US-Israeli attacks that triggered the war. Washington subsequently imposed a blockade on Iranian ports, while Gulf oil producers have sought alternative ways to maintain shipments through the waterway.

Before the conflict, approximately one-fifth of the world’s oil supply passed through the strait. Although some commercial traffic has resumed, shipping volumes remain significantly below their 2025 levels.

Analysts say Iran’s renewed attacks could reflect growing concern in Tehran that it is losing its influence over the strategic passage, particularly as falling oil prices and restrictions on its exports put additional pressure on its economy.

The International Energy Agency has attributed the recent decline in global oil prices partly to the recovery of Gulf exports. Prices also fell following the US midterm election results, as concerns about renewed American military action in the Middle East eased.

Hamidreza Azizi, a senior Iran analyst at the International Crisis Group, told CNN that markets increasingly appeared to believe a return to full-scale war was unlikely and that oil supplies would gradually recover.

However, he warned that the situation could change quickly if Tehran decided to intensify the confrontation.

Iran’s Oil Revenues Under Pressure

The escalation comes as Iran faces growing financial pressure from the continued US blockade of its ports, which has restricted the country’s ability to transport crude oil to international markets.

Maritime data tracking company Kpler reported in late October that Iranian oil shipments outside the US blockade zone had effectively dried up after the last cargoes were discharged in China earlier that month.

The company warned that Iran’s oil revenues could fall to zero by mid-December if the situation continued.

The financial pressure has added to concerns that Tehran could increasingly use its influence over the Strait of Hormuz to pressure Washington into making concessions.

US President Donald Trump has, meanwhile, signaled little interest in reaching a new agreement with Iran.

Earlier this month, Trump said Washington did not need a deal with Tehran and directed Vice President JD Vance to focus on other matters.

In a post on his Truth Social platform, Trump declared: “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed!”

He also claimed that the United States had secured control over Iran’s financial resources and the Strait of Hormuz, while subsequently indicating that he would not rule out renewed military strikes against Iran if necessary.

Three Tankers Hit In Latest Attacks

The latest escalation was illustrated by attacks on three oil tankers attempting to leave the Strait of Hormuz on Friday and Saturday, according to maritime risk management company Marisks.

Although the company did not conclusively identify those responsible, it assessed Iranian involvement as likely.

The first incident involved the Captain Leon, a Marshall Islands-flagged chemical and oil tanker, which was struck at the bow at approximately 3 p.m. UTC on Friday. A fire broke out aboard the vessel, but all crew members were reported safe.

On Saturday, the Torkel, a Hong Kong-flagged crude oil tanker, caught fire after being hit in the stern at approximately 5 a.m. UTC.

Less than an hour later, another Hong Kong-flagged tanker, the Arina, was struck by a missile in its engine room.

Marisks said the incidents demonstrated the “continued critical threat” facing commercial shipping in the region, particularly along the southern corridor near Oman’s coastline.

The company noted that Iran strongly opposes the use of this route, underscoring the continuing risks to vessels attempting to navigate the strategically important waterway.

With oil markets showing signs of recovery and Iran facing mounting pressure on its export revenues, the latest attacks raise concerns that the Strait of Hormuz could remain a major source of instability for global energy supplies and international maritime trade.

title: Adeleke backs grassroots sports as Osun marathon awards N2.55m
description:
The Osun State Government has reiterated its commitment to grassroots sports development and youth engagement following the successful hosting of the 2026 10-kilometre Imole Marathon.
In a statement made available to journalists in Osogbo on Sunday, the race facilitator, Joseph Adeyemi, Special Assi
content:
The Osun State Government has reiterated its commitment to grassroots sports development and youth engagement following the successful hosting of the 2026 10-kilometre Imole Marathon.

In a statement made available to journalists in Osogbo on Sunday, the race facilitator, Joseph Adeyemi, Special Assistant on Youth and Sports to Governor Ademola Adeleke, said the event, which attracted participants from different backgrounds, started at Abere Roundabout and ended at Freedom Park, Osogbo.

“The race, held on Saturday, featured male and female categories, with six outstanding runners sharing N2.55m in cash prizes.

“In the male category, Odelana James emerged winner and received N750,000, while Adeyemi Segun came second with N500,000. Adebayo  Michael finished third and received N300,000.

“In the female category, Arinde Boluwatife emerged first and received N500,000. Idowu Adesewa came second with N300,000, while Popoola Omar finished third and received N200,000,” the statement read.

Speaking at the event, Governor Adeleke, who was represented by the Commissioner for Political Affairs and Inter-Governmental Relations, Dr Biyi Odunlade, reiterated his administration’s commitment to creating opportunities for young people through sports and other productive engagements.

“Sports remain an important avenue for youth development, talent discovery and community engagement.

“The Governor believes in creating opportunities for young people to demonstrate their abilities, and initiatives such as the Imole Marathon provide a platform to achieve this,” Odunlade said on behalf of the governor.

The Deputy Governor, who also serves as Commissioner for Sports, Kola Adewusi, reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to sports development and supporting talented athletes.

Adeyemi said the initiative was conceived to encourage more residents, particularly young people, to embrace sporting activities.

“The Imole Marathon is about taking sports closer to the people and encouraging participation beyond professional athletes. We want to make sporting activities accessible, discover new talents and promote a culture of fitness and healthy competition in Osun State,” he said.

Consolation prizes were also presented to other participants in recognition of their participation.

title: COP31 Ends In Deadlock As Fossil Fuel Dispute Derails Climate Agreement
description: Gambiaj.com – (ANTALYA, TÜRKIYE) – The COP31 climate summit ended in diplomatic deadlock on November 22 after the European Union and several other countries rejected a proposed agreement backed by the Turkish presidency for failing to explicitly mention fossil fuels, leaving negotiations without an
content:
Gambiaj.com – (ANTALYA, TÜRKIYE) – The COP31 climate summit ended in diplomatic deadlock on November 22 after the European Union and several other countries rejected a proposed agreement backed by the Turkish presidency for failing to explicitly mention fossil fuels, leaving negotiations without an overarching deal despite two weeks of discussions.

The collapse exposed deep divisions between countries pushing for a clear commitment to phase out fossil fuels and those resisting language that could threaten their economic interests. The disagreement also highlighted persistent tensions over climate financing, particularly between wealthy industrialized nations and developing countries bearing the brunt of climate change.

A European representative accused oil-producing states of having “taken COP31 hostage” following the rejection of the proposed text. Saudi Arabia had opposed any explicit reference to fossil fuels, while European countries were unwilling to reopen discussions on climate financing.

“Countries were not ready to take a step towards each other and think collectively about the solutions that could be found,” said Céline Kauffmann, director of programs at the Institute for Sustainable Development and International Relations (IDDRI).

African Countries Express Frustration

The failure to reach an agreement was particularly disappointing for African countries, whose demands on climate financing and adaptation remained largely unaddressed by the proposed text.

Mohamed Adow, director of the African climate advocacy organization PowerShift Africa, described the summit as the worst COP, arguing that its collapse should serve as a wake-up call for wealthy countries and major polluters.

“The rich countries and polluting governments must stop arriving empty-handed,” he said.

Adow also criticised the prospect of Africa having to take responsibility for resolving the diplomatic divisions left behind by the Turkish-hosted summit, with Ethiopia scheduled to host the next climate conference.

“COP31 was a ghost COP. The next one will take place in Ethiopia, in Africa, and it is a disgrace that the disorder left here must be untangled by Africa,” he said.

He argued that developing countries needed concrete commitments rather than repeated promises, particularly on who would provide climate financing and when vulnerable communities would benefit.

Countries struggling with debt, he added, needed adequate resources to protect themselves against a climate crisis they had done little to cause, without being pushed further into poverty.

Despite Failure, Some Progress Recorded

Although the summit failed to adopt its overarching decision, climate advocates said the negotiations were not entirely without progress.

Céline Kauffmann pointed to several initiatives, partnerships and coalitions launched during the conference, many of which focused on practical solutions outside the formal United Nations negotiating framework.

These included efforts to accelerate the transition away from fossil fuels, with around 20 countries having now presented roadmaps outlining how they intend to achieve that objective.

Gaïa Febvre, head of international policy at the Climate Action Network, said several other texts had nevertheless been adopted during the summit, although they would need to be strengthened at COP32.

She also welcomed Ethiopia’s selection as the next host, saying the African setting would provide an opportunity to maintain pressure on climate adaptation, a major priority for the continent.

Ethiopia and the African negotiating bloc are expected to play a central role in shaping the agenda for next year’s conference, while also attempting to rebuild consensus after the breakdown in Turkey.

Saudi Arabia’s Contradictory Climate Position

Saudi Arabia emerged as one of the most prominent opponents of efforts to explicitly address fossil fuels in the final agreement.

The kingdom, one of the world’s leading oil producers, is pursuing an economic diversification strategy under Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman through its Vision 2030 program, which seeks to reduce the country’s dependence on oil revenues.

However, its resistance to stronger international commitments on fossil fuels has raised questions about the apparent contradiction between its domestic economic ambitions and its position in global climate negotiations.

David Rigoulet-Roze, a researcher at the French Institute for Strategic Analysis, said the kingdom’s position reflected the complex challenge facing oil-producing countries as they contemplate a post-oil future.

Vision 2030 represents an acknowledgement that moving beyond oil dependence is ultimately necessary, he explained, but Saudi Arabia still needs oil revenues to finance that transition.

This creates an inherent contradiction, as the kingdom seeks to protect the economic interests that continue to underpin its development while facing growing international pressure to accelerate the energy transition.

Saudi Arabia and other Gulf oil monarchies are also confronting wider regional instability and economic uncertainty, including tensions surrounding the Strait of Hormuz, a critical route for global energy supplies.

Meanwhile, the urgency of climate action continues to grow. 2026 is expected to rank among the hottest years ever recorded, while scientists warn that 2027 could potentially surpass existing temperature records.

With COP31 ending without a comprehensive agreement, the responsibility now shifts to Ethiopia to revive negotiations and place the concerns of vulnerable countries, particularly those in Africa, more firmly at the centre of the global climate agenda.

title: Lagos summit to tackle growing business cybersecurity threats
description:
Businesses across Africa are facing growing pressure to strengthen cybersecurity and technology risk management as the adoption of artificial intelligence and digital services exposes organisations to new security and governance challenges.
Organisers said in a statement that the risks will be among
content:
Businesses across Africa are facing growing pressure to strengthen cybersecurity and technology risk management as the adoption of artificial intelligence and digital services exposes organisations to new security and governance challenges.

Organisers said in a statement that the risks will be among the issues examined at the 18th anniversary conference of Digital Jewels Africa, an IT governance, risk and compliance consulting and capacity-building firm, scheduled for 25 November in Lagos.

The conference, themed ‘The Trust Imperative: Securing Africa’s Digital Future’, will bring together business executives, policymakers and technology professionals from the financial services, telecommunications, insurance, energy and technology sectors to discuss ways of strengthening digital security and public confidence in technology-driven services.

As organisations increasingly depend on digital platforms to deliver services, manage information and engage customers, weaknesses in cybersecurity and technology governance could undermine business operations and expose sensitive information to security threats.

The conference will examine how businesses can manage these risks while adopting emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence, and strengthening their internal controls and corporate governance frameworks.

The event will be chaired by the Chair of Digital Jewels Africa, Ibukun Awosika, while the Managing Director of the Nigerian Economic Summit Group, Tayo Aduloju, will deliver the keynote address. The Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Digital Jewels Africa, Adedoyin Odunfa, will host the conference.

Participants will include the Chairman of Prudential Life Insurance, Ghana, Karen-Akiwumi Tanoh; Managing Director of Union Bank, Yetunde Oni; Managing Director of Midwestern Oil & Gas Company, Elozino Olaniyan; and Managing Director of Rex Insurance, Ebelechukwu Nwachukwu.

Other speakers include the Chief Executive Officer of eTranzact International, Niyi Toluwalope; Managing Director of Leadway Assurance, Gboyega Lesi; Director of Shared Services at the Central Bank of Nigeria, Usman Usman; and Chief Marketing Officer of MTN Nigeria, Onyinye Ikenna-Emeka.

The cybersecurity discussions will feature the Group Chief Information Security Officer of GTCO, Dr Bharat Soni; the Group Chief Information Security Officer of Access Bank, Dr Favour Femi-Oyewole; the Chief Internal Auditor of Interswitch Group, Adebayo Adebeshin; and the Chief Information Security Officer of MTN Nigeria, Jude Anietie.

The discussions will also examine the responsibilities of businesses, regulators and technology professionals in protecting sensitive information, managing technology-related risks and preparing organisations for the governance, risk and compliance demands associated with digital expansion.

Speaking ahead of the conference, Odunfa said the growing dependence of organisations on digital systems has made security and responsible technology adoption essential for Africa’s digital future.

“The trust imperative is at the heart of Africa’s digital future. As organisations rely more on digital systems, the question is no longer how fast we can innovate, but how securely and responsibly we can do so. We believe this conversation is critical, and our 18th anniversary conference provides an opportunity to bring the right voices together to address it,” she said.

Digital Jewels Africa said it had spent 18 years supporting organisations in areas including cybersecurity, information assurance, IT governance, project management, e-business and professional capacity development.

The anniversary conference is expected to provide a platform for business leaders and technology professionals to exchange experiences and discuss practical approaches to strengthening digital trust and security across Africa.

The post Lagos summit to tackle growing business cybersecurity threats appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

Gambiaj.com – (BANJUL, THE GAMBIA) – The No To Alliance Movement’s presidential aspirant, Almameh Gibba, has dismissed rumors of a possible political alliance with Talib Ahmed Bensouda’s UNITE, insisting that his movement will contest the December 5 presidential election independently.
Addressing su
content:
Gambiaj.com – (BANJUL, THE GAMBIA) – The No To Alliance Movement’s presidential aspirant, Almameh Gibba, has dismissed rumors of a possible political alliance with Talib Ahmed Bensouda’s UNITE, insisting that his movement will contest the December 5 presidential election independently.

Addressing supporters in Mamud Fana village, Gibba said the movement had neither reached nor signed any formal or informal agreement with UNITE, dismissing reports of a possible deal as false and unfounded.

He also reassured supporters that his name would appear on the ballot paper for the December 5 election, reaffirming the movement’s determination to participate in the presidential race.

The clarification comes amid growing speculation about political alliances and negotiations between opposition groups ahead of the election.

Earlier on Sunday, Alpha Bah, popularly known as Alpha Photo, also ruled out the possibility of the No To Alliance Movement joining another political party, saying the position was based on instructions from former President Yahya Jammeh.

Speaking during a livestream program, Bah said he was aware of calls from supporters of different political parties urging the movement to join their respective camps.

However, he maintained that the movement would remain independent, claiming that Jammeh had personally communicated the position to Gibba.

“Jammeh said it with his own mouth, and I, Alpaha, also heard it with my own ears. We will stand on our own, but our doors remain open to any political party that wishes to join us,” Bah revealed.

His remarks suggest that while the movement is not considering joining another party, it remains open to other political formations joining its ranks.

The statements from Gibba and Bah come as political parties and coalitions intensify their efforts to consolidate support ahead of the December 5 presidential election, with speculation continuing over possible alliances and last-minute political realignments.

title: Atiku Dismisses Claims He Has Withdrawn From 2027 Presidential Race
description:
Gambiaj.com – (LAGOS, NIGERIA) – Former Nigerian Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has dismissed reports that he has withdrawn from the 2027 presidential race, describing the claims as a “brazen, malicious and desperate falsehood“.
In a statement issued by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank
content:
Gambiaj.com – (LAGOS, NIGERIA) – Former Nigerian Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has dismissed reports that he has withdrawn from the 2027 presidential race, describing the claims as a “brazen, malicious and desperate falsehood“.

In a statement issued by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said no group claiming to support him had the authority to announce his withdrawal from the election or speak on his behalf.

“Putting my name on a placard does not make someone my supporter. Putting a lie in that person’s mouth does not make it my decision,” he said.

The former vice-president accused those behind the reports of attempting to create confusion within the opposition, suggesting that the claims were part of a political strategy to weaken his challenge to President Bola Tinubu.

He alleged that any party promoting the withdrawal story was indirectly advancing the interests of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

“Any party promoting the lie that I have stepped down is doing Tinubu’s work. Every false withdrawal story tries to clear his strongest opponent from the field,” Atiku said.

He insisted that he remained firmly in the contest and was determined to challenge Tinubu at the ballot box.

“But I am in this race to win, and Nigerians will have their choice,” he added.

Atiku also said his “Affordable Life” campaign was continuing across Nigeria, with a focus on the economic difficulties confronting households, particularly hunger, poverty and the rising cost of living.

He said the campaign was engaging communities across the country to address issues affecting ordinary Nigerians, arguing that the hardship facing families could not be understood solely through social media discussions.

“Hunger and poverty are not on social media. They are in our markets, our homes and every community where families struggle to afford food and transport,” he said.

Atiku further criticized opposition groups that he accused of relying on misinformation and fabricated declarations rather than competing for voters’ support.

He argued that attempts to manufacture political endorsements or circulate false reports of withdrawals would ultimately benefit the ruling party rather than strengthen the opposition’s chances of defeating Tinubu.

The former vice-president urged his supporters to remain mobilized ahead of the election, calling on them to prepare their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and intensify grassroots mobilization.

“No fabricated headline can withdraw me from an election I intend to win,” he said.

Atiku concluded by reiterating his determination to challenge Tinubu in the January 16, 2027 presidential election, declaring: “We will meet and beat Bola Tinubu at the ballot box.”

title: 2027 politics, Christmas spending squeeze naira
description:
The approaching 2027 general elections and the Christmas season are adding pressure to the naira, with the currency depreciating to N1,394/$ at the official market on Friday and N1,460/$ at the parallel market on Sunday.
The naira lost N6 at the official market on Friday, extending its depreciation
content:
The approaching 2027 general elections and the Christmas season are adding pressure to the naira, with the currency depreciating to N1,394/$ at the official market on Friday and N1,460/$ at the parallel market on Sunday.

The naira lost N6 at the official market on Friday, extending its depreciation streak after weakening by N8.01 on Thursday to N1,388/$ from N1,379.99/$ recorded on Wednesday.

On Wednesday, the currency had depreciated by N16.99 to N1,379.99/$ from N1,363/$ on Tuesday, highlighting renewed pressure in the official foreign exchange market.

At the parallel market, the naira traded at N1,440/$ on Thursday, compared with N1,375/$ a month earlier, while some currency traders said they were willing to offer lower rates to buyers purchasing large volumes.

However, currency demand has intensified in recent weeks, with traders attributing part of the pressure to political spending ahead of the 2027 elections and increased foreign exchange needs during the festive season.

A parallel market trader in Abuja, Haruna Ibrahim, said some customers were purchasing dollars on behalf of politicians preparing for the elections.

“There are people we see here who say they are politicians. They come here to buy dollars, claiming that they were sent by their bosses. I do not know which parties they belong, but they come here regularly,” he said.

Another Bureau de change trader in Lagos, who identified himself simply as Ahmed, said traders in Zone 5 believed political activities were contributing to increased demand for dollars, as politicians sought to accumulate foreign currency ahead of the elections.

Speaking in a phone interview with The PUNCH, the Chief Executive Officer of the Centre for Promotion of Private Enterprise, Dr Muda Yusuf, said domestic factors could be contributing to the successive decline of the naira against the dollar.

The economist identified political spending, capital flight and policy uncertainty as possible factors behind the weakening currency and declining foreign reserves.

He said political spending could inject liquidity into the economy and put pressure on the naira, noting that the Central Bank of Nigeria had previously raised concerns about the impact of political activities on exchange rate stability.

“The political spending liquidity may be already putting pressure on the naira. The CBN had expressed that fear before during the latest Monetary Policy Committee meeting,” Yusuf said.

He argued that foreign exchange demand associated with political activities could be channelled through the parallel market because such transactions might not be formally documented or conducted through official channels.

Yusuf also warned that political uncertainty and statements by some politicians about reversing the economic reforms of the President Bola Tinubu administration could trigger capital flight.

An emerging markets expert and economist, Ike Ibeabuchi, attributed the weakening naira and declining reserves to reduced dollar supply and rising demand for foreign exchange.

He said lower inflows from exporters, investors and other sources might be reducing dollar availability in the market, while demand for foreign currency to finance imports and international transactions continued to exert pressure on the naira.

“Lower foreign exchange inflows from exporters, investors and other sources reduce dollar supply in the market, while demand for foreign currency for imports, international payments and other transactions continues to exert pressure on the naira,” Ibeabuchi said.

He said the festive season typically increases demand for foreign exchange, while the influence of election-related spending on the currency could be greater than initially anticipated.

The combination of higher seasonal demand, political spending and weaker dollar inflows could further test the naira’s stability as the country approaches the 2027 elections.

Meanwhile, the reserves stood at $54.65bn on Friday, shedding $60.630m from Thursday’s $54.713bn.

The post 2027 politics, Christmas spending squeeze naira appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Nigeria, South Africa open reconciliation talks amid Fani-Kayode diplomatic row
description:
• Top officials hold closed-door meetings to ease tensions  •Tinubu reportedly intervenes   •Compensation for victims of xenophobic attacks remains uncertain

From Fred Itua and Aidoghie Paulinus, Abuja
Nigeria and South Africa have opened reconciliatory talks to strengthen diplomatic relations foll
content:
• Top officials hold closed-door meetings to ease tensions  •Tinubu reportedly intervenes   •Compensation for victims of xenophobic attacks remains uncertain

From Fred Itua and Aidoghie Paulinus, Abuja

Nigeria and South Africa have opened reconciliatory talks to strengthen diplomatic relations following the controversy involving Nigeria’s High Commissioner to Pretoria, Femi Fani-Kayode, amid concerns over recurring xenophobic attacks on Nigerians .

Daily Sun gathered that senior diplomatic officials from both countries have begun holding closed-door consultations to resolve outstanding differences and prevent the latest disagreement from undermining relations between Africa’s two major economies.

A diplomatic source, who spoke on condition of anonymity, confirmed that the two governments were already discussing ways to move beyond the controversy and strengthen bilateral cooperation.

“Yes, there are reconciliatory moves already. Both countries are already talking on ways that we can forge ahead,” the source said.

The renewed engagement comes against the backdrop of longstanding concerns over attacks on Nigerians and other foreign nationals in South Africa, which have resulted in loss of lives and property and heightened diplomatic tensions between Abuja and Pretoria.

According to information obtained by Daily Sun, more than 2,000 Nigerians have been evacuated from South Africa since June 10, 2026, through interventions involving the Federal Government and private organisations, including the Redeemed Christian Church of God.

However, it remains unclear whether the ongoing diplomatic discussions include compensation for Nigerians who lost relatives or property during the attacks.

Asked whether the issue had featured in the talks, the source said: “I can’t say if there will be any compensation.”

The reconciliatory moves also follow reports that President Bola Tinubu has initiated consultations with his South African counterpart, Cyril Ramaphosa, to ease tensions arising from Fani-Kayode’s recent confrontation with officials of the South African government.

Sources within the Presidential Villa and the Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs claimed that Tinubu had reached out to Ramaphosa to reassure Pretoria of Nigeria’s commitment to maintaining cordial relations, although neither government has publicly confirmed such presidential communication.

The reported intervention came as consultations continued in Abuja over Fani-Kayode’s future following his formal reprimand by South Africa’s Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) on November 17, four days after he presented his letters of credence to Ramaphosa.

Minister of Foreign Affairs was also said to have briefed the President on developments surrounding the dispute, while the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, reportedly maintained contact with ministry officials as consultations continued.

The controversy began on November 13 when Fani-Kayode joined 14 other newly accredited ambassadors and high commissioners to present their credentials to Ramaphosa at the Sefako Makgatho Presidential Guest House in Pretoria.

Shortly after the ceremony, the Nigerian envoy alleged that his introduction and address had been deliberately excluded from the livestream of the event, unlike those of other diplomatic representatives.

He also claimed that he raised the matter with Ramaphosa during a photo session and that the South African President directed him to relevant officials.

The allegation drew a response from Ramaphosa’s spokesperson, Vincent Magwenya, who disputed Fani-Kayode’s account of the President’s involvement.

Magwenya maintained that Ramaphosa had neither directed the broadcaster nor interfered with its editorial operations but had merely referred the Nigerian envoy to an appropriate official to address his complaint.

Although the South African Presidency subsequently made footage of Fani-Kayode’s address available, the disagreement escalated into a public exchange involving the Nigerian High Commission and South African officials.

On November 17, DIRCO Director-General Zane Dangor summoned Fani-Kayode and formally conveyed Pretoria’s displeasure over his public comments and handling of the matter.

Dangor drew the envoy’s attention to Article 41 of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, which requires diplomats to respect the laws and regulations of receiving states, refrain from interfering in their internal affairs and conduct official business through established diplomatic channels.

The South African government emphasised that official communications should pass through DIRCO, while reaffirming its commitment to maintaining constructive relations with Nigeria.

South Africa’s Minister of International Relations and Cooperation, Ronald Lamola, subsequently described the reprimand as a closed matter, indicating that Pretoria was prepared to move beyond the immediate disagreement while continuing to monitor developments.

Diplomatic sources told Daily Sun that the controversy could have been addressed through established diplomatic procedures without the public exchanges that followed.

They explained that complaints involving a host government were ordinarily handled through formal representations, diplomatic notes and other recognised channels rather than public statements capable of embarrassing either country.

A source familiar with the consultations said the manner in which the dispute unfolded had placed Nigeria in an uncomfortable diplomatic position.

“Whatever the merits of his complaint, the manner in which he handled it has put Nigeria in an awkward position with one of Africa’s biggest economies. A final decision on the recall is expected soon,” the source said.

Fani-Kayode, who was initially designated for Germany before his redeployment to South Africa, is also concurrently accredited to Lesotho and Eswatini.

His appointment came at a sensitive period in bilateral relations, following recurring tensions over xenophobic attacks, the treatment of Nigerian nationals and allegations of criminal activities involving some migrants.

In July, Lamola visited Abuja as Ramaphosa’s special envoy for discussions aimed at reducing tensions and strengthening diplomatic engagement.

Both governments subsequently emphasised the need to discourage inflammatory rhetoric, protect foreign nationals and address criminal conduct through lawful processes rather than collective blame or vigilante action.

At his November 13 accreditation ceremony, Fani-Kayode recalled Nigeria’s support for South Africa during the struggle against apartheid and pledged to strengthen cooperation between the countries.

Despite the subsequent controversy, the envoy and the Nigerian High Commission defended their position, while Fani-Kayode later described his meeting with Dangor as cordial and constructive.

Spokesperson of the Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Femi Adeniyi, also declined to comment directly on the matter , maintaining that Fani-Kayode had been accredited and was performing his diplomatic responsibilities.

“Ambassador Femi Fani-Kayode has been accredited as Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa. Therefore, he has since commenced the discharge of his diplomatic and representational duties, engaging with relevant South African authorities and key stakeholders on matters of mutual concern and shared interest to Nigeria and South Africa,” Adeniyi said.

title: 2027: South East APC leaders back Tinubu, Uzodimma
description:
Leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the South East geopolitical zone have backed President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027 and expressed support for the party’s leadership in the region under the watch of Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma.
The APC zonal leaders said that President
content:
Leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the South East geopolitical zone have backed President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027 and expressed support for the party’s leadership in the region under the watch of Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma.

The APC zonal leaders said that President Tinubu had done a lot for the zone to deserve re-election in the forthcoming presidential election, describing recent attacks on Governor Uzodimma as mischievous and aimed at frustrating Tinubu’s second tenure in office.

In a communiqué issued at the end of their zonal meeting, on Saturday, and signed by the Deputy National Chairman (South), Dr Benjamin Nwoye; National Treasurer, Chief Uguru Ofoke; and National Welfare Officer, Hon Donatus Nwankpa, among others, the APC stalwarts vowed to queue behind Uzodimma’s leadership of the party to actualise Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027.

The communiqué read, “The South East Zonal Executives of the All Progressives Congress (APC), having thoroughly deliberated on matters of urgent political and organisational importance affecting the party in the zone, hereby issue this communiqué in firm and unambiguous response to the deliberate circulation of AI-generated images, fabricated statements, and other forms of fake news targeted at His Excellency, Distinguished Senator Hope Uzodimma, Executive Governor of Imo State and the Leader of the APC in the South East Zone.

“We note, with deep concern, the growing trend of digital mischief, character assassination, and coordinated misinformation campaigns designed to undermine the hard-earned political progress of the APC in the South East. These reckless publications seek not only to impugn the integrity of our Leader, but also to create artificial tension, sow seeds of distrust, and distract the party from its core mandate of delivering good governance and consolidating the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Tinubu, GCFR.

“We reaffirm, without any reservation, whatsoever, our total, unalloyed, and unwavering support for, and absolute confidence in His Excellency, Distinguished Senator Hope Uzodimma, Executive Governor of Imo State and Leader of the All Progressives Congress in the South East Zone.

“We publicly acknowledge and deeply appreciate the consistent, substantial, and sacrificial support he has continued to extend to the party across the entire South East. This support has included significant financial contributions, logistical facilitation, strategic guidance, and personal mobilisation of party members and supporters, particularly during the recent Anambra Presidential Campaign Rally and other critical party programmes and activities throughout the zone. His leadership has remained a stabilising force and a major source of encouragement for APC structures in Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu, and Imo States.”

It added, “We state categorically, emphatically, and for the avoidance of all doubt, that the publications currently in circulation, including AI-generated images, purported statements, insinuations, and related fake news materials, are entirely false, fabricated, and malicious. No such information, statements, opinions, or insinuations emanated from Senator Hope Uzodimma, nor can they be linked in any remote or indirect manner to his person, office, or authorised representatives. These materials are deliberate fabrications manufactured by faceless individuals and groups whose sole intention is to mislead the public, create unnecessary controversy, and manufacture political tension where none exists.

“We are fully aware, and we place it on record, that these publications are ill-conceived, carefully orchestrated, and deliberately intended to sow discord, generate artificial discontent, and create a false impression of friction between our major benefactor in the South East Zone and the Federal Government. This mischievous campaign is particularly reprehensible when viewed against the clear and consistent record of unwavering support that Senator Hope Uzodimma continues to give to the All Progressives Congress, the policies of the Federal Government, and the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Tinubu in the South East. The authors of these materials seek to undermine the growing political harmony and progress that the APC is recording in the zone.”

The post 2027: South East APC leaders back Tinubu, Uzodimma appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.
