content:
From Uchenna Inya, Abakaliki

The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Ebonyi State has condemned the reported establishment and inauguration of a 200-member local security codenamed Neighbourhood Watch outfit by the Chairman, Ohaozara Local Government Area, Osborn Nweze Umahi.

Umahi inaugurated the 200-man vigilante at the weekend in Obiozara, headquarters of the local government.

NDC wondered why the action occurred at the critical period when the state was  approaching another electoral season.

In a statement signed by the state Chairman of the party, Alum Enyinnaya Udensi and the state Secretary, Okereke Nnanna, the party said that while it  recognises the legitimate responsibility of government to protect life and property, the party is deeply concerned about the timing, circumstances, composition, and possible implications of establishing such a large security outfit barely months before a general election.

“We find it particularly disturbing that a party that has had the opportunity to serve the people for the past 11 years, yet has failed to substantially improve the living conditions, economic fortunes and general welfare of the citizens, is suddenly demonstrating such urgency in establishing a 200-man security structure at a politically sensitive period.

“The question that begs for an answer is: What is the real intention behind this sudden mobilisation of 200 security personnel, and whose interests are they expected to protect?”, the party queried.

The party stated that if the initiative was genuinely intended to strengthen community security, the government must demonstrate transparency by making public the legal framework guiding its operations, the nature of equipment to be deployed, its chain of command, training arrangements, and the mechanisms for ensuring accountability.

It  noted that the party was  particularly concerned by any possibility that an ostensibly community-based security arrangement could be transformed into an instrument of political intimidation, harassment, voter suppression, or electoral violence.

“Let it be clearly understood that the security of our communities must never be converted into a political project or a weapon for intimidating political opponents and innocent citizens.

“Our warning is unequivocal: Whoever stokes violence, promotes intimidation or attempts to manipulate the electoral process through coercion will ultimately be consumed by the consequences of such actions.

“No individual, political office holder, or group should mistake the peaceful disposition of the people for weakness. We wish to remind those in positions of authority that the mandate given to them is an opportunity to improve the lives of ordinary Ebonyi people, provide employment, strengthen infrastructure, improve healthcare, support education, and create an environment where citizens can live with dignity and security.

“Unfortunately, the people are still confronted with enormous developmental challenges”.

The party maintained that it is unacceptable that the urgency now being demonstrated in establishing a massive security structure is not matched by the same level of commitment to addressing unemployment, poverty, insecurity, and the numerous hardships confronting our people.

“The NDC further wishes to remind the authorities of an important African proverb: “Whosoever harvests an ant-infested firewood has invited the lizards to a feast.”

“Those who create conditions for political tension, intimidation, and insecurity should not be surprised when the consequences become difficult to contain. Those who sow violence must understand that its consequences may extend far beyond their immediate expectations.

The party called on the Nigeria Police Force and other relevant security institutions to urgently investigate the development.

“Specifically, we demand that the security agencies establish the legality of the newly inaugurated 200-member outfit and ascertain the legal authority for possessing and deploying such arms.

“Investigate the recruitment process, training, operational guidelines, and actual mandate of the outfit. Ensure that no member of the outfit is deployed to intimidate political opponents, interfere with political activities or influence the choices of voters.

The party also urged the security agencies to put adequate safeguards in place to prevent the misuse of public resources and security structures during the forthcoming elections.

“We emphasise that the responsibility for maintaining law and order rests with constitutionally recognised security institutions. Community-based security arrangements must operate strictly within the law and under appropriate supervision”, the party said.

The party noted that it will not fold its arms while any development capable of undermining the peace, safety, and democratic rights of our people goes unquestioned. The party also called on the people of Ohaozara and, indeed, all Ebonyi citizens to remain calm, vigilant, and law-abiding, and also urge their supporters and members to resist provocation and conduct themselves peacefully while exercising their democratic rights.

“Finally, we remind the security agencies that their constitutional responsibility is to protect the lives and properties of all citizens, irrespective of political affiliation. They must live up to their expectations before, during, and after the elections.

“Ebonyi State belongs to all of us, and its security must never be sacrificed on the altar of political ambition. Our democracy must be protected, our people must be free, and the will of the electorate must prevail.

The post NDC condemns 200-man vigilante in Ebonyi LG, urges investigation appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Enugu massacre: NDC chieftain faults FG’s appeal against £420m compensation ruling
description: An Enugu-based senior lawyer and chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Okenna Peter Agubuzu, has criticised the Federal Government’s reported appeal against a court judgment ordering the British Government to pay £420 million in compensation to the families of 21 coal miners killed by
content:
An Enugu-based senior lawyer and chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Okenna Peter Agubuzu, has criticised the Federal Government’s reported appeal against a court judgment ordering the British Government to pay £420 million in compensation to the families of 21 coal miners killed by colonial police during the 1949 Iva Valley massacre in Enugu.

Agubuzu described the decision to challenge the judgment as regrettable, questioning why the Nigerian Government would seek to overturn a ruling in favour of citizens whose relatives were killed while protesting poor working conditions and racial discrimination under British colonial rule.

The judgment, delivered by Justice Anthony Onovo of the Enugu High Court on February 5, 2026, reportedly ordered the United Kingdom to pay £20 million to each of the 21 affected families and issue a formal apology for the killings.

The ruling followed suit E/909/2024, instituted by an activist, Greg Onoh, against the British Government, represented by the Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs, and other respondents, including the Federal Government and the Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF).

The court also held that the Federal Government had a constitutional responsibility to pursue justice and diplomatic engagement on behalf of the victims’ families.

Reacting to the reported appeal, Agubuzu accused the Tinubu administration of failing to demonstrate sufficient concern for the suffering endured by generations of families who lost their breadwinners in the massacre nearly eight decades ago.

“The appeal filed by the AGF is quite curious and regrettable. Whose interest is the AGF protecting? Is he protecting the interest of Nigerians or the United Kingdom? Is it the duty of the Nigerian Government to appeal against a judgment awarded in favour of Nigerians against ill-mannered colonialists?” he asked.

He maintained that the Federal Government should have supported efforts to secure compensation rather than challenge the ruling, arguing that the decision raised questions about its commitment to protecting the interests of Nigerian citizens.

“It is unfortunate and regrettable that the Tinubu government chose to protect the interest of the United Kingdom, rather than allow them to honour the judgment or appeal,” he said.

Agubuzu urged the government to reconsider its position, citing Kenya’s handling of compensation claims arising from abuses committed by British colonial authorities during the Mau Mau uprising in the 1950s. He recalled that the Kenyan government publicly supported the victims’ legal claims in British courts in 2010, while maintaining that independent Kenya could not be held responsible for abuses committed by the colonial administration.

He said the Kenyan government subsequently intensified diplomatic efforts to secure redress, including an October 2012 intervention by then Prime Minister Raila Odinga, who wrote to British Prime Minister, David Cameron, seeking a resolution.

The efforts culminated in a June 2013 settlement under which the British Government agreed to pay £19.9 million to 5,228 Kenyan claimants, expressed sincere regret over the torture and mistreatment they suffered, and pledged support for a memorial in Nairobi.

Agubuzu argued that Nigeria should adopt a similar approach by supporting the families of the slain miners in their pursuit of compensation and an official acknowledgment of the colonial-era killings. He consequently called on the Federal Government to withdraw its reported appeal and pursue diplomatic engagement with the British authorities to secure justice for the affected families.

The Iva Valley massacre occurred on November 18, 1949, when British colonial police opened fire on striking coal miners in Enugu, killing 21 workers and injuring 51 others.

The killings provoked widespread condemnation across Nigeria, galvanised organised labour and nationalist movements, and became a defining episode in the struggle against British colonial rule that culminated in Nigeria’s independence in 1960.

The controversy has acquired wider significance following similar demands by human rights lawyer, Femi Falana, and protests by descendants of the slain miners, who have called on Britain to comply with the judgment.

Falana, in a statement on November 18, urged the Federal Government to withdraw its appeal and, instead, intensify diplomatic efforts to secure the compensation, arguing that Britain had not challenged the ruling.

On November 19, relatives of the victims protested at the British High Commission, demanding payment of the compensation and a formal apology, 77 years after the massacre. Their counsel, Yemi Akinseye-George, confirmed that the Federal Government had appealed the judgment, while the British Government had neither appealed nor obtained a stay of execution.

The post Enugu massacre: NDC chieftain faults FG’s appeal against £420m compensation ruling appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Tinubu pledges 50,000 new hostel beds by 2027
description:
President Bola Tinubu has pledged to provide 50,000 additional hostel bed spaces across federal tertiary institutions by the end of 2027 to address accommodation shortages in Nigerian universities.
He made the pledge during the commissioning of Block E of the College of Medicine Students’ Hostel, Un
content:
President Bola Tinubu has pledged to provide 50,000 additional hostel bed spaces across federal tertiary institutions by the end of 2027 to address accommodation shortages in Nigerian universities.

He made the pledge during the commissioning of Block E of the College of Medicine Students’ Hostel, University of Ibadan, Oyo State, on Saturday.

The president, who was represented by the Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, said the project was part of the N400bn Student Hostels Programme, to be implemented through the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) and private-sector partnerships.

Tinubu said, “My administration will deliver 50,000 new bed spaces across federal tertiary institutions by the end of 2027, through our N400bn Student Hostels Programme. Our purpose is to give more students safe, decent accommodation that supports their education.”

He said the newly commissioned facility would accommodate 192 medical and dental students in 48 rooms across four floors, with each room designed for four occupants.

 The rooms have private toilets, showers and kitchenettes, alongside four reading rooms.

The president stressed that the college previously faced a shortage of 490 beds, representing 44.5 per cent of its accommodation requirement, following a 2020 directive by the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria requiring clinical students to reside within the premises of the University College Hospital (UCH).

He noted that the shortage exposed students to security challenges and affected the institution’s ability to fully utilise its admission quota.

Tinubu also said more than 36 universities had benefited from the Renewed Hope Energising Education Programme, with power installations ranging from 2.5 to 12 megawatts.

The president added that 20 compressed natural gas conversion centres had been completed, while another 40 were expected by the end of 2028.

“Reliable power supports laboratories, libraries, hostels and the clinical facilities on which medical education depends,” he said.

Earlier, the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ibadan, Peter Olapegba, described the commissioning as another milestone in efforts to improve accommodation for medical students.

He recalled that Blocks C and D, named after Philip Ozuah and TY Danjuma respectively, had also been commissioned as part of the initiative.

Olapegba thanked the Chagoury brothers for their contribution, saying, “Our expectation is that the improved learning environment will contribute to producing healthcare professionals distinguished by competence, integrity and a strong sense of national responsibility.”

In his address, the Provost of the College of Medicine, Temidayo Ogundiran, said the college accounted for about one-third of the university’s institutional footprint, while its researchers generated approximately 80 per cent of the institution’s grant income.

The provost commended the Federal Government’s N110bn Special High Impact Intervention Project, launched in April 2025 to rehabilitate 18 medical schools across the six geopolitical zones through TETFund.

Ogundiran appealed for government support to construct a 1,000-seat student auditorium, expand the college’s administrative building and complete hostel Blocks A and B.

The varsity don also disclosed that the college spent about N18m monthly on diesel and electricity bills.

He said, “The College currently spends about N18m monthly on diesel and as payment to IBEDC for electric power supply. This expenditure is unsustainable and is placing severe pressure on our operations.”

Ogundiran urged the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, to facilitate the implementation of an approved solar hybrid mini-grid project for the university and UCH, as well as the installation of four 5MVA transformers.

“The ultimate measure of these investments will not be the number of buildings commissioned, but the quality of healthcare professionals, researchers and leaders whose lives they help shape,” the provost said.

The hostel, named the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu GCFR Block, was donated by the Chairman of Chagoury Group, Gilbert Chagoury, and his brother, Ronald Chagoury.

The post Tinubu pledges 50,000 new hostel beds by 2027 appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Presidential Villa also suffers power, water shortages – Tinubu
description:
President Bola Tinubu on Sunday revealed that the Presidential Villa in Abuja suffers from the same electricity and water supply failures that plague ordinary Nigerians.
He revealed that the water supply went off while he was shaving earlier in the week, vowing to fix the country’s infrastructure de
content:
President Bola Tinubu on Sunday revealed that the Presidential Villa in Abuja suffers from the same electricity and water supply failures that plague ordinary Nigerians.

He revealed that the water supply went off while he was shaving earlier in the week, vowing to fix the country’s infrastructure deficit.

Tinubu made the disclosure on Sunday at a special prayer session organised in his honour by members of his family in Lagos.

The meeting followed his attendance at the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, on Saturday.

He explained, “On the Wednesday of last week, I was shaving, and the water went off. And the villa, you won’t know punishment there too.

“The water went off. So we will correct all this. No light, no water, no electricity, no development. We have just started. We can do it, and we will do it for Nigeria.”

The President also rallied supporters ahead of the 2027 general elections, charging them to maximise voter turnout in Lagos and urging warring factions within his political camp to reconcile.

“To me, Lagos is the big deal. How can you have seven million registered voters and produce 100,000, 200,000? That’s failure. Even if you win, I say a win is a win. No. You have to generate the maximum,” he said.

He directed supporters to canvass their neighbours for Permanent Voter Cards and to channel their grievances into electoral participation rather than internal conflict.

According to him, “It’s not anger. Anger will not do it. You are angry with Sylva, or you’re angry with Mulika, call Mulika and let her go vote. We finish the anger that day; you go back. We must generate enough votes to overwhelm them.”

Tinubu also ordered one of his associates in attendance, described as his “confidant and bulldozer”, to return home and broker reconciliation within the party’s ranks before moving on to other states.

He ordered, “Go back home and reconcile with everybody. That is the order of the president. Go back home and reconcile with everybody. And when you finish that, you move to Jigawa, you move to other places and reconcile them. Beg them.”

Drawing on his own experience, the President said he had set aside deep personal grievances during the 2023 campaign to pursue a broader goal.

“I had my own anger in 2021–22. When he called me, I said, okay, you are co-chairman of the campaign. I had my own anger, full of hot feelings, but I let go. Today, that is free,” he said, adding that the spirit of forgiveness was inseparable from seeking it.

Tinubu noted that, “If you cannot give it, why are you asking Allah to give you forgiveness? What you want from him, you must be able to give to humanity.”

The President credited divine support and family loyalty for his journey from governorship to the presidency, tracing a line of prayer and perseverance through each contest.

“First time, prayer. Second time, prayer. We did that. We won. After that, presidency, prayer, vision, mission, everything,” he said.

To the younger generation at the meeting, President Tinubu said the 2027 election was theirs to win or lose. “The challenge is yours now. It’s in your hands to knock on doors, get all the PVCs out, and do what is right.

“You are the leaders that we take over. We paved the way for you. But it’s left in your hands to do the great things that Nigeria expects,” he said.

Several governors attended the prayer session, including the Lagos, Kwara, Imo, Gombe and Kaduna state governors.

The post Presidential Villa also suffers power, water shortages – Tinubu appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: ADC faults Tinubu’s call to forget fuel subsidy
description:
The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council has accused President Bola Tinubu of insensitivity to the plight of Nigerians following his insistence that the country must move on from fuel subsidy removal.
The Council said the President’s position showed a lack of empathy for million
content:
The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council has accused President Bola Tinubu of insensitivity to the plight of Nigerians following his insistence that the country must move on from fuel subsidy removal.

The Council said the President’s position showed a lack of empathy for millions of Nigerians grappling with rising food prices, transportation costs, poverty and the worsening cost of living.

Tinubu had, at a rally at Mapo Hall in Ibadan, Oyo State, urged Nigerians to forget about fuel subsidy, declaring that the policy belonged to the past.

But reacting to the President’s remarks during an interaction with youths in Lokoja, Kogi State, ahead of the ADC presidential campaign rally scheduled for Tuesday, the ADC-PCC Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, said the President was disconnected from the economic realities facing ordinary Nigerians.

Ologbondiyan accused Tinubu of being more concerned about his presidential status than addressing the hardship confronting citizens.

“The President appears more interested in being addressed as Mr President than in tackling the crushing realities confronting the people. He has demonstrated little or no concern for the suffering of ordinary Nigerians.

“That explains his brash insistence that Nigerians should forget about fuel subsidy removal simply because, in his estimation, it belongs to the past,” he said.

The ADC-PCC questioned how the consequences of a policy that continues to shape the daily experiences of millions of Nigerians could be dismissed as a thing of the past.

It argued that the removal of fuel subsidy was implemented without adequate preparation, effective social safety nets, or sufficient measures to cushion its impact on vulnerable households.

According to the Council, the policy has contributed to soaring transportation costs, rising food prices, difficulties confronting small businesses and the further impoverishment of millions of households.

“To ask Nigerians to forget a policy whose consequences they confront every waking moment is not only insensitive; it is an insult to their intelligence and a mockery of their suffering,” Ologbondiyan added.

The opposition campaign council maintained that responsible leadership required the willingness to listen to citizens, acknowledge policy shortcomings and make necessary adjustments to ease their economic difficulties.

It also accused the Tinubu administration of defending its economic policies despite the hardship it has imposed on Nigerians.

Beyond the economic situation, the ADC-PCC raised concerns over what it described as the weakening and manipulation of critical democratic institutions, including the judiciary, security agencies, anti-corruption bodies and financial institutions, allegedly in pursuit of the President’s second-term ambition.

It warned that public institutions established to protect democracy and serve the national interest must not be subordinated to the political ambitions of any individual.

“Nigeria cannot afford a second term built on the ruins of its democratic institutions and the continued impoverishment of its citizens,” the Council declared.

The ADC-PCC said the country’s economic difficulties were not inevitable but could be addressed through better policy choices, adequate planning and leadership that prioritised citizens’ welfare.

It consequently presented the ADC presidential candidate, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, as the alternative capable of restoring economic confidence, strengthening democratic institutions and improving living conditions.

The Council promised that an Atiku-led administration would pursue economic policies backed by proper planning, effective social protection programmes and a people-centred approach to governance.

It urged Nigerians to use lawful and constitutional means to reject Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, insisting that the next general election would provide an opportunity to change the country’s direction.

deserve a government that feels their pain, understands their struggles and takes deliberate steps to ease their burden, not one that dismisses their suffering or asks them to forget the circumstances that have made life increasingly unbearable,” it added.

title: Adelabu group to launch Tinubu-Shettima rally in Ekiti
description:
The Modupe Adelabu Political Family, a group led by former Ekiti State Deputy Governor, Prof Modupe Adelabu, has expressed readiness to mobilise across the 16 local government areas of the state for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima.
The group, in a statemen
content:
The Modupe Adelabu Political Family, a group led by former Ekiti State Deputy Governor, Prof Modupe Adelabu, has expressed readiness to mobilise across the 16 local government areas of the state for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima.

The group, in a statement made available to PUNCH on Sunday, stated that it would flag off the Tinubu-Shettima re-election rally on Thursday at a grand event billed for the Mini Pavilion, Fajuyi, Ado-Ekiti, the Ekiti State capital.

It said the event, which would be hosted by Adelabu, who is the Governing Board Chairman of the National Examinations Council, “is aimed at demonstrating political unity, grassroots mobilisation and commitment to the Tinubu-Shettima re-election project ahead of the 2027 general election.

“It will have in attendance Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, as chief host and former Governor Segun Oni as the special guest of honour. The Deputy Governor, Mrs Monisade Afuye, will serve as the Mother of the Day, while Otunba Ladi Owolabi is Chairman of the Planning Committee.

“The flag-off ceremony is expected to bring together political stakeholders, party loyalists and supporters of the President and Vice-President in Ekiti State,” the group stated.

According to the organisers, the gathering will provide a platform for members and supporters of the political family to reaffirm their support for the Renewed Hope Agenda and strengthen their mobilisation efforts towards the 2027 elections.

They described the ceremony as “a significant step in consolidating the political structure of the Adelabu family across the state, with representatives from the 16 local government areas expected to participate.”

The political family, while declaring its readiness to rally behind the Tinubu-Shettima re-election bid, said, “The gathering is a demonstration of unity and commitment to the administration’s political aspirations”.

title: Independent judiciary check govt’s excesses –Nwifuru
description:
From Uchenna Inya, Abakaliki 
Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru, has stressed the importance of an independent judiciary in sustaining constitutional democracy, saying it checks the government and its excesses.
He also advocated adoption of technology-driven processes in the administration of t
content:
From Uchenna Inya, Abakaliki

Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru, has stressed the importance of an independent judiciary in sustaining constitutional democracy, saying it checks the government and its excesses.

He also advocated adoption of technology-driven processes in the administration of the justice system. He noted that the judiciary serves as a critical institutional safeguard against possible excesses of government.

Nwifuru stated this at the weekend, at the state High Court, Abakaliki, during the Special Court session marking the commencement of the 2026/2027 Legal Year in Ebonyi State. He said an efficient justice system must be capable of resolving disputes promptly and minimising unnecessary expenditure of resources.

“A justice system that cannot resolve disputes timely wastes resources. Technology offers us the opportunity to resolve some of these things. Digital filings and digital transcriptions help.

“The significance goes beyond governance. It helps to transact with various registries without recourse to location. An independent judiciary checks the government as well as its excesses. As a governor, I recognise that the independence of the judiciary must be respected and allowed to perform its constitutional and professional mandate,” he stated.

He explained that the deployment of digital technology in judicial administration would reduce the challenges associated with physical processes, improve efficiency, and enable legal practitioners and litigants to interact with relevant court registries more conveniently.

The governor noted that his People’s Charter of Needs Agenda is committed to the ongoing reforms in the justice sector, pointing to several initiatives introduced to strengthen the administration of justice and improve the delivery of judicial services in the state.

He said the ongoing adoption of electronic filing, establishment of the Moot Court, creation of the Office of the Public Defender and adoption of the Sexual Assault Bill as evidence of his government’s commitment to justice sector reforms.

He maintained that the reforms were designed to strengthen institutional capacity, promote access to justice and ensure that the justice system remains responsive to the needs and expectations of the people.

Earlier, the Chief Judge of Ebonyi State, Hon. Justice Elvis Ngene, informed the governor that the state judiciary had recorded progress in several areas of judicial administration under his leadership.

Justice Ngene identified the modernisation of the machinery of justice through the deployment of technology, protection of judicial integrity, improvement of access to justice, and the appointment of  deserving judicial officers as some of the areas receiving attention.

Justice Ngene stated that official visits to correctional centres, regular human capital development, professional capacity building, infrastructural development, and improvement of court facilities are significant components of the judiciary’s activities within the last one year.

The Chief Judge emphasised that judicial integrity remained fundamental to the credibility and effectiveness of the justice system, stressing the need for all judicial officers and personnel to uphold the highest ethical standards. He assured that the judiciary would continue to invest in professional development and institutional reforms despite the financial constraints confronting the institution.

“As part of our efforts to promote this, we shall, notwithstanding the leanness of our resources, continue to encourage continuous legal education and professional learning, strengthen administrative competence, promote responsible use of technology, and insist upon the highest ethical standards from every person entrusted with judicial responsibilities,” he said.

He said the judiciary would continue to recognise the dedication of its workforce and prioritise measures that promote professionalism, institutional discipline, and effective service delivery.

The post Independent judiciary check govt’s excesses –Nwifuru appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Tinubu’s reforms may be difficult to sustain without re-election — Wike
description:
Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said it would be difficult to sustain and stabilise President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms if he fails to secure re-election in 2027.







Wike said the initial challenges associated with the removal of petrol subsidy were tempora
content:
Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said it would be difficult to sustain and stabilise President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms if he fails to secure re-election in 2027.

Wike said the initial challenges associated with the removal of petrol subsidy were temporary, arguing that Tinubu should be allowed to complete the foundation he had laid for Nigeria’s economic recovery and prosperity.

The minister spoke on Sunday during a thanksgiving service at St Peter’s Anglican Church, Rumueprikom, in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State.

He said Nigeria had been facing the threat of economic collapse before Tinubu assumed office, describing the president as courageous for taking difficult decisions.

“This country was on the verge of collapse. But by the grace of God, He gave us somebody who is courageous,” Wike said.

“And that is why they say these disadvantages will be temporarily seen. He has laid his foundation; now it’s time for prosperity. If we don’t re-elect him, then it will be difficult to stabilise what he has done.”

Wike cited what he described as improved stability in the university system, noting that strikes by lecturers over unpaid entitlements, which frequently disrupted academic calendars in the past, were no longer a recurring feature under the Tinubu administration.

He also recalled the difficulties pensioners previously encountered in accessing their entitlements, arguing that decisions taken by the president had helped address some of the country’s longstanding challenges.

The FCT minister urged Nigerians across religious divides to support Tinubu’s re-election bid, insisting that the president’s campaign would accommodate Christians, Muslims and traditional worshippers.

“I am not a native doctor, but I need their votes now. I need everybody’s votes because I know they are registered voters. The Muslims, I need their votes too. The Christians like you, we need your votes,” he said.

Wike also dismissed claims of religious imbalance in appointments under the Tinubu administration, insisting that Christians had enjoyed greater representation in the current government than in previous administrations.

“Since Nigeria was created, we have never had the kind of appointments that are going on in this country now,” he said.

The minister, during the service, announced a donation of N100 million to the church on behalf of the Rainbow Coalition, his friends and associates.

The post Tinubu’s reforms may be difficult to sustain without re-election — Wike appeared first on Vanguard News.

Some police officers, who raised concerns over the promotions, alleged that the current board
content:
Allegations have emerged that the Police Service Commission promoted some retired Commissioners of Police to the rank of Assistant Inspectors-General of Police after they had left the Nigeria Police Force.

Some police officers, who raised concerns over the promotions, alleged that the current board of the commission illegally elevated the retired officers, with four of them reportedly serving as aides to members of the board.

The officers questioned the propriety of promoting individuals who had already retired from the police, particularly when some of them were allegedly working closely with members of the commission responsible for approving promotions.

A source familiar with the allegations said, “The current board illegally promoted some retired CPs to AIGs’ rank after retirement from the police. Four of them are currently serving as aides to board members.”

Another source said the promotions differ from the usual practice of elevating officers on the eve of retirement.

According to the source, the beneficiaries had long left the service before they were promoted.

The source said, “This is not that they were promoted and proceeded on retirement like we are used to. These ones had long been retired for one reason or the other, only for them to be promoted. One who was dismissed during Goodluck Jonathan tenure was last year promoted to DIG.”

When contacted on Sunday, the Police Service Commission spokesman, Torty Kalu, defended the commission’s actions, saying officers who believed they were unfairly denied promotion while in service had the right to appeal.

He explained that the commission could review such appeals, investigate the circumstances surrounding delayed promotions and approve them where there was sufficient justification.

“Before a decision is taken on any matter, there is always an investigation carried out on it. An investigation is carried out, due diligence, and they find out that you were not given justice,” Kalu said.

He added that officers who obtained favourable court judgments directing their promotion could also benefit from backdated promotions, stressing that the commission was bound to obey such orders.

On concerns that some beneficiaries were serving as aides to board members, Kalu argued that working with the commission did not disqualify anyone from enjoying rights available to other Nigerians.

“For the fact that you are serving in the commission, you are a board member of the commission, doesn’t deprive you of your rights. You’re just like every other Nigerian who can benefit from where you deserve to be benefited,” he said.

Kalu maintained that promotions were granted based on merit, adding that officers outside the commission had also benefited from successful appeals.

“If somebody working with a board member of the commission benefited in view of maybe an appeal made and promotion given to the person, the fact that he’s working with the commission doesn’t stop him from enjoying that if he merits it. And if he doesn’t merit it, it wouldn’t be given,” he added.

The post PSC denies wrongdoing over promotion of retired CPs appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: CJN urges senior lawyers to document experience
description:
The Chief Justice of Nigeria, Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, has urged senior lawyers to document their professional experiences to preserve valuable knowledge and guide younger generations in the legal profession.
Kekere-Ekun spoke on Friday in Lagos while chairing the public presentation of six books author
content:
The Chief Justice of Nigeria, Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, has urged senior lawyers to document their professional experiences to preserve valuable knowledge and guide younger generations in the legal profession.

Kekere-Ekun spoke on Friday in Lagos while chairing the public presentation of six books authored by and in honour of Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Kemi Pinheiro, at the Civic Centre, Victoria Island.

The publications cover arbitration, insolvency, criminal litigation, legal practice and contemporary jurisprudence, with the CJN describing them as a significant contribution to legal scholarship because they combine doctrinal analysis with practical experience.

She said, “One of the most valuable legacies a senior member of the profession can leave behind is something from which the next generation can learn and grow.

“Experience that is not shared may remain a personal achievement. Experience that is documented and transmitted becomes part of the profession’s collective inheritance.”

The six publications comprise four books authored by Pinheiro – Defining Moments: Chronicles of a Silk; Strategies in Criminal Trial – A Practitioner’s Guide; Insolvency Law in Nigeria: Practice and Procedure; and Arbitration Law and Practice in Nigeria – and two tribute volumes, The Compendium in My Honour and Trending Issues of Law and Faith: Essays in Honour of Kemi Pinheiro.

Also present at the unveiling of the six books were the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila; a Justice of the Supreme Court, Habeeb Abiru; the Presiding Justice, Lagos Division of the Court of Appeal, Yargata Nimpar; and other Justices of the Court of Appeal. The Chief Judge of Lagos State, Kazeem Alogba; other judges of the Lagos State High Court; and the Attorney General and Commissioner of Justice, Lagos State, Lawal Pedro, SAN, were also in attendance.

Kekere-Ekun said the books addressed significant areas of legal practice, engaged with contemporary developments in jurisprudence and sought to make legal knowledge more accessible to practitioners and others involved in the administration of justice.

She particularly highlighted Defining Moments: Chronicles of a Silk, describing it as a personal account of the experiences, encounters, challenges and defining moments that had shaped Pinheiro’s career spanning close to four decades at the Bar.

According to her, memoirs of that nature preserve aspects of professional life that might never find their way into law reports or formal institutional records. They also help younger practitioners understand the uncertainties, disappointments and perseverance that often accompany successful legal careers.

On Arbitration Law and Practice in Nigeria, the CJN said the book examined the framework established by the Arbitration and Mediation Act 2023 and the developing jurisprudence of Nigerian courts.

She noted that its practical treatment of arbitration agreements, recognition and enforcement of awards made it a useful resource for practitioners involved in commercial dispute resolution.

She also commended Insolvency Law in Nigeria: Practice and Procedure, saying its examination of corporate rescue, restructuring and administration was particularly relevant under the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020.

The CJN said preserving viable businesses, where appropriate, could serve the interests of creditors, employees, investors and the wider economy better than immediate liquidation.

On Strategies in Criminal Trial – A Practitioner’s Guide, she said its coverage of arraignment, bail, confessional statements, electronic evidence, no-case submissions and written addresses would benefit experienced practitioners and younger lawyers.

She described its consideration of emerging issues, including electronic evidence in the age of artificial intelligence, as particularly timely.

The two tribute publications, she said, brought together contributions on issues including arbitration, taxation, maritime law, judicial precedent, technology in dispute resolution, evidence, criminal law and contemporary jurisprudence.

Addressing younger lawyers, Kekere-Ekun said, “I hope that younger lawyers will see these works not simply as additions to their libraries, but as encouragement to read more deeply, think more critically and take their own professional development seriously.”

She added that a book presentation was an invitation to dialogue, in which authors offered their thoughts and experiences for readers to engage with, question and learn from.

Congratulating Pinheiro, the CJN said the opportunity to translate professional experiences into literature that could educate and inspire others was a legacy of lasting value.

In his remarks, Pinheiro said the four books he authored were drawn from nearly four decades of legal practice and were intended to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge acquired in law school and the realities of legal practice.

“These books are the curated end products of the differences between the theory of the law schools and the reality of legal practice,” he said.

The lawyer, who will mark 40 years at the Bar in October 2027, said the publications contained lessons gathered from his work as an insolvency practitioner, criminal prosecutor and arbitrator.

Reflecting on his professional journey, he recalled that his elevation to the rank of SAN in 2006 came after an unsuccessful attempt the previous year, an experience that informed some of the reflections in Defining Moments.

He also recounted how a distant uncle, Rasaq Shonibare, helped set him on the path to becoming a lawyer by giving him money to purchase his Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board form, which enabled him to secure admission to study Law at the University of Benin.

Pinheiro said he later represented the same uncle pro bono in a dispute in which his assets were at risk of being taken over by a bank.

“At the time he gave me the Naira notes on Bamgbose Street, Lagos Island, neither of us knew that the money he gave me was the professional fee for the legal services I would be rendering for him later in life,” he said.

He also recalled the financial difficulties he faced during his early years in practice, including his inability to afford a wig and gown.

He said a senior lawyer once came to his rescue after the person who rented him his professional attire attempted to retrieve it while court proceedings were still ongoing. The senior lawyer lent him his gown and waited outside the courtroom until he completed his appearance.

Pinheiro said the experience and other acts of kindness inspired him to establish a free wig and gown project for indigent graduates of the Nigerian Law School, through which more than 800 young lawyers had benefited.

He recalled one young lawyer who travelled from Lafia, Nasarawa State, to Lagos in a truck conveying tomatoes because he could not afford transportation. After arriving, the young man trekked from Oyingbo to Pinheiro’s law firm in Ilupeju to collect a free wig and gown.

On his criminal trial book, Pinheiro said it was motivated by the consequences of errors in criminal proceedings, which could result in the loss of life or liberty.

“If there is one area of law where a counsel cannot afford to make a mistake, it is Criminal Law,” he said.

He said the publication examined procedural, evidential and strategic issues in criminal trials, including the admissibility of electronic evidence.

On insolvency law, he said his experience in the field informed the need to produce practical reference material for lawyers and other stakeholders dealing with financially distressed businesses.

He acknowledged the Managing Director of the Asset Management Corporation of Nigeria, Gbenga Alade, who wrote the foreword to the book.

Pinheiro said his arbitration book focused on the Arbitration and Mediation Act 2023 and addressed issues including anti-suit injunctions, post-award litigation and appeals, drawing on comparative experiences from leading arbitration jurisdictions.

He also commended Kekere-Ekun for reforms in the judiciary, citing improvements in court infrastructure, digital access to court information and efforts to address delays in the administration of justice.

Recalling an appeal that had been pending for 13 years, Pinheiro said a younger lawyer recently informed him that the Supreme Court had contacted him to schedule the matter for hearing.

He praised the CJN for making the Supreme Court’s diary accessible online, describing her as a “silent revolutionary”.

“You abhor accolades. You are a silent revolutionary. History and posterity will certainly be kind to you, My Noble Lord,” he said.

Pinheiro also acknowledged his mentors, particularly the late Abiola Oshodi and his uncle, Toyin Pinheiro, SAN, whom he credited with shaping his career.

Describing legal practice as a relay race, he said senior practitioners had a responsibility to pass their knowledge and experience to younger lawyers.

“Law practice is a continuum. The legal profession is not a sprint of one hundred metres. It is a relay race where each runner collects the baton and passes it on to the succeeding runner. Our primary task is therefore not to drop the baton,” he said.

He also paid tribute to his wife, Yetunde Pinheiro, for standing by him after his unsuccessful SAN application in 2005.

He recalled that she comforted him as they returned to Lagos from the Supreme Court and assured him that he would eventually attain the rank, which he achieved the following year.

“She wiped my tears as we came back to Lagos alone, with the rank of SAN disappearing into the distance. She assured me prophetically that I would still wear the Silk. She believed in me,” he said.

He added, “If there is one single decision I have never regretted making, it is the choice of Yetunde as my spouse and life partner.”

Reviewing Strategies in Criminal Trial, the President of the Nigerian Bar Association, Oyinkansola Badejo-Okunsanya, SAN, said the book would help lawyers improve their courtroom skills and understand the reasoning behind effective advocacy.

She said the publication encouraged practitioners to reflect on their decisions during court proceedings, particularly in cross-examination and the handling of witnesses.

Badejo-Okunsanya said lawyers were often willing to recount what happened in court but did not always explain why they made particular decisions.

The post CJN urges senior lawyers to document experience appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Tinubu approves N1.5tn recapitalisation of BOA
description:
President Bola Tinubu has approved a N1.5tn recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture as part of efforts to expand agricultural financing and improve access to affordable loans for farmers and businesses across the agricultural value chain.
The APC Presidential Campaign Council, in a statement by
content:
President Bola Tinubu has approved a N1.5tn recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture as part of efforts to expand agricultural financing and improve access to affordable loans for farmers and businesses across the agricultural value chain.

The APC Presidential Campaign Council, in a statement by its spokesperson and Minister of Solid Minerals, Dele Alake, on Sunday, said the recapitalisation would strengthen the bank’s financial capacity to support farmers, agricultural cooperatives, processors and aggregators.

The APC PCC stated, “President Bola Tinubu’s administration has committed N450bn to agricultural financing programmes to strengthen food security, expand domestic production, and improve the productivity of smallholder farmers across the country, especially in Northern Nigeria.

“Through the Bank of Agriculture, the administration has reached over 500,000 smallholder farmers, and the President has also approved a N1.5tn recapitalisation to expand agricultural financing and support the cultivation of 500,000 hectares under the Renewed Hope Agenda.

“The Federal Government, under President Tinubu, went beyond providing farmers with loans; it also addressed access to quality seeds, fertiliser, mechanisation, irrigation, storage facilities, commodity markets, and other essential components of the agricultural value chain.

“The interventions demonstrated President Tinubu’s commitment to transforming agriculture into a major driver of economic growth, food security, and job creation.”

It added that the initiative was aimed at expanding the bank’s reach to underserved farming communities and mobilising more resources for domestic food production.

The ruling party’s Campaign Council stated, “The ₦450bn agricultural financing intervention, support for more than 500,000 smallholder farmers, and the planned ₦1.5tn recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture represent a significant commitment to building a more productive and resilient agricultural sector.

“Through the Renewed Hope Smallholder Support and Value Chain Fund, with a programme value of ₦250bn, the Bank of Agriculture is financing farmers through Farmer Aggregation Companies that coordinate farmer registration, input distribution, extension services, and market linkages.

“The programme has already reached more than 500,000 smallholder farmers across 16 states, including over 70,000 women. It has also supported the distribution of approximately 2.5 million bags of fertiliser and 300,000 bags of certified seeds.

“The initiative aims to reach two million farmers and distribute more than 10 million bags of fertiliser.

“The intervention was particularly significant in Northern Nigeria, where agriculture remains a major source of livelihood and economic activity.

“States including Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Niger, Borno, Gombe, Taraba, Adamawa, Yobe, and Bauchi are among the areas receiving attention under the programme.”

The APC Presidential Campaign Council said the Bank of Agriculture had procured about 170,000 metric tonnes of maize, rice, sorghum and cassava under its N200bn Guaranteed Minimum Price Programme to stabilise commodity markets and protect farmers from distress sales.

The APC Presidential Campaign Council said the Bank of Agriculture had introduced an Onion Financing Programme in partnership with NOPPMAN, which represents over 11,800 farmers, to boost production and market access.

The council said the scheme would provide farmers with improved seeds and fertiliser, while supporting processors with funds and solar-powered storage facilities to reduce post-harvest losses.

It added that the bank would cover 70 per cent of farmers’ input costs, while cooperatives would contribute the remaining 30 per cent.

The APC PCC stated, “Other agricultural initiatives the bank is implementing include dry-season farming financing, mechanisation, ginger recovery, women’s cooperative financing, youth participation, and commercial poultry production.

“Under the dry-season agricultural financing programme, the bank is working with the All-Farmers Association of Nigeria to develop a pipeline targeting 400,000 farmers for the 2026 farming cycle.

“The initiative includes financing for 120,000 hectares of wheat cultivation and another 300,000 hectares for crops including rice, maize, sorghum, millet, cassava, and soybeans.

“The Nigeria Ginger Recovery Programme has also supported 3,200 farmers in Kachia, Kaduna State, with blight-free seeds, recovered more than 9,000 bags for multiplication, and is planning an expansion across 20,000 hectares in 16 states.”

The APC PCC said the Bank of Agriculture was targeting 50,000 women nationwide with insured cooperative loans at nine per cent interest.

It continued, “Under the Renewed Hope National Agricultural Mechanisation Programme, 1,571 tractors have been deployed to 23 states.

“The tractors are expected to mechanise 1.2 million hectares of farmland, with access provided to farming communities through qualified Mechanisation Service Providers.

“Other interventions include a ₦385 billion productive-use-of-electricity programme, which provides 44,000 electric cargo tricycles and 100,000 solar irrigation pumps, targeting 500,000 farming families.”

Ahead of the January 16, 2027, presidential election, President Bola Tinubu is seeking re-election on the platform of the APC.

In preparation for the poll, the APC Presidential Campaign Council has continued to highlight the achievements of the Tinubu administration across various sectors.

The post Tinubu approves N1.5tn recapitalisation of BOA appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Daura emir faces sexual assault allegation, Amnesty seeks probe
description:
Nigerians have reacted with mixed feelings after a female tourist accused the Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, of touching her inappropriately during a visit to his palace in Katsina State.
The allegation, which has sparked debate on social media, followed the circulation of a video appearing to sho
content:
Nigerians have reacted with mixed feelings after a female tourist accused the Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, of touching her inappropriately during a visit to his palace in Katsina State.

The allegation, which has sparked debate on social media, followed the circulation of a video appearing to show the traditional ruler interacting with the tourist during her visit.

The woman, who identifies herself as @beduinqa, made the allegation in a post on Instagram on Saturday after completing a 30-day tour of Nigeria.

She said she waited until she left Nigeria before making the claim public.

According to a series of posts on her Instagram, the tourist was on a world tour with Nigeria as her 184th of 197 destinations.

She announced her arrival on October 19, 2026 and documented visits across the country, including a trip to the Oba of Benin’s palace on October 24.

She had also posted a video of her attendance at the 10th coronation anniversary celebration of Oba Ewuare II on October 25, her time at the Kala Kuta shrine and Makoko in Lagos, as well as stops in Kano, Katsina and Bauchi, where she met the Emir of Bauchi at his palace.

Recounting her experience at the Daura palace, the tourist said she was taken into an elegant room where she sat with the Emir and had a conversation with him.

She alleged that the traditional ruler held her hand and began playing with it before hugging and kissing her on the cheek.

She further alleged that he touched her breasts, an action she said shocked and disturbed her.

In her Instagram post, she wrote, “That was a shock for me. I told him, ‘Emir, no, no, no, no, Emir, you cannot be touching’, but he was just laughing about it.”

She said she had travelled through different parts of Nigeria without experiencing sexual assault in public spaces, making the alleged incident at the palace particularly disturbing.

“I wasn’t sexually assaulted at any moment when walking through streets of Nigeria, even in busy crowded places, but to my shock, I was assaulted in a palace by a traditional leader who should be behaving in an exemplary and dignified way,” she wrote.

The tourist described the experience as disgusting, adding that she had continued to relive it in her thoughts.

She said the incident happened on Saturday, November 14, but she waited until she had left Nigeria before making the allegation public.

She also suggested that other women might have experienced similar treatment from the Emir, although she did not provide evidence to support the claim.

“I suspect I wasn’t the first woman he assaulted but probably the first one with proof recorded. I have Meta glasses and quickly turned them on,” she added.

The allegation has generated reactions on X, with several users expressing outrage and calling for accountability.

Amnesty International Nigeria called on the authorities to investigate the allegation, describing it as deeply disturbing.

In a post on its X account, the human rights organisation said the Katsina State Government and the police should conduct a transparent and independent investigation to ensure accountability.

It said, “The Nigerian authorities must immediately and effectively investigate strong allegations of sexual assault on a female foreign tourist by the Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk.”

Amnesty added that the incident presented an opportunity for the government to demonstrate that nobody was above the law.

Another X user, identified as @mairowashere, described the alleged incident as appalling and expressed relief that the tourist had recorded the encounter.

“What a shame. Truly appalling. I’m really glad the woman managed to get it on video because, had she simply come forward to say she was assaulted, people would have demanded proof, questioned her account or dismissed her altogether,” the user wrote.

Similarly, @Bashir_GS called on the Katsina State Government to consider removing the Emir, describing him as unfit to occupy the throne.

Another user, @Nawas_masood, said the allegation had damaged the reputation of the traditional institution.

“It is really painful to watch this. The Emir of Daura has done serious damage to the dignity and standing of the Northern Emirates. What hurts most is that the damage goes beyond one emirate. It affects the image of our traditional institutions and the respect they have earned over the years,” the user wrote.

As of the time of filing this report, neither the Daura Emirate Council nor the Katsina State Government had issued an official response to the allegation.

PUNCH Online could not independently confirm the claim.

Meanwhile, a source in the emir’s palace has denied the allegation

“There was nothing like that. She visited the palace, but how she got that information cooked up still amused us in the palace.

“Meanwhile, an official statement will be released, while I advise you should not write the story or wait for the official statement,” the source, who spoke on condition anonymity because he was not authorised to speak to the press, told our correspondent by telephone on Sunday.

title: Ex-NDC spokesman Abdulsalami defects to Atiku’s ADC
description: Former Deputy National Publicity Secretary of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Abdulmumin Abdulsalami, has defected to the African Democratic Congress, the political platform of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, days after resigning from the NDC over alleged injustice, exclusion and internal pow
content:
Former Deputy National Publicity Secretary of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Abdulmumin Abdulsalami, has defected to the African Democratic Congress, the political platform of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, days after resigning from the NDC over alleged injustice, exclusion and internal power struggles.

Abdulsalami confirmed his defection in an exclusive interview with The PUNCH, saying he had been warmly received by the ADC and was ready to contribute to the party.

 Asked whether he had decided on his next political destination after quitting the NDC, the former spokesman said he had already joined the ADC.

 “No, there is no going back to the NDC. I have joined the ADC, where I have been welcomed with open arms. Now, I feel at home, and I am willing to put in my best, knowing that my efforts will be appreciated,” he said.

 When asked if he had been assigned a new responsibility, particularly in the ADC Campaign Council ahead of the 2027 general elections, Abdulsalami confirmed that he had taken up a new role but declined to disclose details.

 “Yes, I have a new role now. But I have not been cleared to release it for media consumption,” he said.

 His defection comes days after he announced his resignation from the NDC, accusing some influential party officials of frustrating his contributions and sidelining him despite his role in building the party.

 Abdulsalami, a foundation member and pioneer spokesperson of the NDC, announced his departure in a letter addressed to the National Chairman, Senator Moses Cleopas, through his former ward chairman in Nagazi Ward, Adavi Local Government Area of Kogi State.

 In the letter, titled Letter of Resignation from the Nigeria Democratic Congress: Withdrawal from All Partisan Commitments to the Party, he said his decision followed a growing disagreement between his contributions to the party and the interests of some powerful officials.

 “As a foundation member of the NDC, and a critical formative leader in the party, I am compelled to voluntarily take the exit having realised that my sincere and positive contributions to the meteoric rise and success of the party are at odds with the vested interests of a few powerful officers who call the shots.

 “More so, this painstaking decision serves my best interest as I prioritise my peace of mind rather than recurrent complaints at the sight of a series of injustices meted out to me,” he stated.

 Abdulsalami served as the NDC Protem Chairman in Kogi State before becoming Deputy National Publicity Secretary and later Deputy National Director for Labour and Civil Society.

 He also thanked the party’s National Leader, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, for the opportunities given to him, while acknowledging the support of colleagues, civil society activists and media practitioners who worked with him during the party’s formative period.

 Before confirming his defection to the ADC, Abdulsalami had indicated that he was withdrawing from partisan politics, saying he was no longer willing to remain in a party where he felt excluded.

 “I am calling it quits and heading back home to avoid orchestrated melodrama of exclusion from party affairs. I love you all, but I love myself and my mental sanity most,” he said.

 He, however, declined to identify the party officials he accused of frustrating his contributions.

 An NDC source, who spoke on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity of the matter, described his resignation as the culmination of a troubled relationship with the party’s leadership.

 “Abdul’s case is really a sad one. He has survived what I can call a toxic relationship. Despite all his efforts since the start of this NDC, he has never been paid a dime as salary or in the working budgets.

 “Secondly, he was subtly eased out of the National Working Committee despite being a foundational member by high-ranking leaders of the party. His leaving the party, to many of us, is the only choice.

 “He has been trying to do that since October. But the national leader of our party (Senator Seriake Dickson) kept urging him to stay back,” the source said.

 However, the NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, dismissed suggestions that Abdulsalami’s exit reflected a deeper crisis within the party.

 He told our correspondent, “There is no internal wrangling in the party. The exit of one person is not enough to conclude, especially as we also witness an influx of a lot of people into the party every day.”

 Abdulsalami’s defection comes amid a series of disagreements and political realignments involving the NDC and opposition figures ahead of the 2027 general elections.

 The party has faced disagreements over the relationship between its structures and the Obi-Kwankwaso Movement, a political platform supporting its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his prospective running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso.

 Barely two months ago, the Director-General of the OK Movement, John Ughulu, rejected suggestions that the group should surrender its national, state, local government and ward structures to the NDC.

 Dickson had argued that support groups should complement political parties rather than compete with them or operate parallel structures. He also described the movement’s decision to establish a presidential campaign council as “unheard of” and “nonsensical”.

 Ughulu, however, maintained that the movement was an independent political organisation and not merely a conventional support group.

The post Ex-NDC spokesman Abdulsalami defects to Atiku’s ADC appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: MTN deploys 106 new sites, upgrades 97 nationwide
description:
MTN Nigeria has deployed 106 new network sites and upgraded 97 existing ones across the country to improve connectivity and address growing demand for mobile services.
The latest rollout brings the number of new and upgraded sites to 203, covering selected locations across Nigeria’s six geopolitical
content:
MTN Nigeria has deployed 106 new network sites and upgraded 97 existing ones across the country to improve connectivity and address growing demand for mobile services.

The latest rollout brings the number of new and upgraded sites to 203, covering selected locations across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones and the Federal Capital Territory, according to a statement on Sunday.

The investment spans 2G, 3G and 4G technologies as the telecommunications operator seeks to strengthen network capacity and improve service delivery amid increasing data consumption and reliance on digital services.

In the South-West, the deployment includes four new sites and 16 upgrades in Lagos, two new sites and three upgrades in Ogun, alongside additional upgrades in Ondo, Ekiti, Osun and Oyo states.

In the South-East, Anambra received one new site and one upgrade, while Abia got two new sites and Imo one upgrade. Ebonyi recorded six new sites and four upgrades.

In the South-South, the rollout covers three new sites and two upgrades in Edo, two new sites in Akwa Ibom, three new sites and nine upgrades in Cross River, four new sites and two upgrades in Rivers, and three upgrades in Bayelsa.

Across the North-Central, seven new sites and four upgrades were deployed in Benue, eight new sites and four upgrades in Kogi, and one new site in Kwara. The Federal Capital Territory also received nine new sites.

In the North-East, the programme includes six new sites and two upgrades in Bauchi, two new sites and four upgrades in Borno, five new sites in Gombe, one new site and two upgrades in Taraba, five new sites in Yobe, and two upgrades in Adamawa.

The North-West also recorded network expansion, with five new sites and four upgrades in Kaduna, nine new sites in Kano, one new site and two upgrades in Kebbi, three new sites and six upgrades in Sokoto, seven new sites and three upgrades in Jigawa, seven new sites and seven upgrades in Katsina, and one upgrade in Zamfara.

The company said the expansion was aimed at addressing increasing network usage, improving service quality and meeting the changing connectivity needs of customers.

While the new sites are expected to extend network infrastructure into selected locations, upgrades to existing facilities will strengthen capacity in areas experiencing increased usage.

Commenting on the investment, Karl Toriola, Chief Executive Officer of MTN Nigeria, said, “Reliable connectivity is central to how Nigerians live, work and do business. Our continued network investment reflects our commitment to keeping pace with growing demand, addressing congestion and delivering a dependable experience for our customers.

“Through this 203-site rollout, we are strengthening capacity in busy commercial centres and university communities while extending coverage to underserved areas. This goes beyond infrastructure alone; it includes connecting people to opportunities and enabling them to participate more fully in the digital economy. Through our ‘Live It 100’ promise, we remain committed to making connectivity accessible to more Nigerians.”

The post MTN deploys 106 new sites, upgrades 97 nationwide appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: ADC crisis: Gombe mocks Atiku as feud deepens
description:
The factional National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress, Nafiu Bala Gombe, has urged former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar to return to his ward and formally register as a member of the party, promising to consider appointing him chairman of its 2027 Presidential Campaign Council.
Bala mad
content:
The factional National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress, Nafiu Bala Gombe, has urged former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar to return to his ward and formally register as a member of the party, promising to consider appointing him chairman of its 2027 Presidential Campaign Council.

Bala made the appeal in a statement sent to our correspondent on Sunday, while responding to a question on the faction’s next move after the Independent National Electoral Commission’s decision to await the outcome of the Court of Appeal proceedings before taking further action on the ADC leadership dispute.

Rather than announce a fresh legal or political step in response to INEC’s position, the factional chairman disclosed that the party had held a strategic engagement with its presidential, governorship and National Assembly candidates to harmonise campaign plans ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The meeting, held at the NCI International Conference Centre, Kaduna, was attended by the faction’s presidential candidate, Prof. Chris Uba; vice-presidential candidate, Dr Shamsuddeen Modibbo Barkindo; and other candidates from across the country.

In the statement signed by the faction’s Director of Media and Public Affairs, Christopher Okechukwu, Bala called on Atiku to “sheathe his sword” and return to his ward to register as a bona fide member of the ADC.

He said formal registration would accord the former vice-president all the rights, benefits and privileges of full membership of the party. Bala added that he would consider appointing Atiku as chairman of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council upon his registration.

The statement quoted him as saying that Atiku’s “wealth of political experience, national reach and deep understanding of governance would be a major asset to the party” in its bid to dislodge the All Progressives Congress-led Federal Government and provide Nigerians with an alternative.

The factional chairman also urged its candidates to return to their constituencies, mobilise support at the grassroots and work in unity with party structures at all levels.

He said the engagement reaffirmed the faction’s commitment to internal cohesion, inclusive leadership and a coordinated nationwide campaign ahead of the 2027 elections.

Attempts by our correspondent to reach Atiku’s ADC National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, for his reaction to the call by Nafiu Bala’s faction asking former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar to register afresh with the party to qualify for appointment as its campaign chairman were unsuccessful.

Calls and text messages sent to Abdullahi had not been responded to as of the time of filing this report.

The post ADC crisis: Gombe mocks Atiku as feud deepens appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
