content:
The Allied Peoples’ Movement in Oyo State on Sunday slammed President Bola Tinubu for attacking the APM during the All Progressives Congress rally held at Mapo Hall in Ibadan, saying, “what the people of the country need is better living conditions and not grandstanding.”

 The party also described the President’s remark as a desperate distraction from the mounting realities confronting Nigerians and the glaring failures of governance.

 This was contained in a statement issued by the APM State Director of Communication/Spokesperson, Campaign Council, Yinka Oladoyinbo, in Ibadan, the state capital.

 The PUNCH reports that President Tinubu had, on Saturday, in Ibadan, taken a swipe at the APM, whose presidential candidate for 2027 is Governor Seyi Makinde, deploying the Yoruba expression “Egbé Palemo” in what appeared to be an attempt to mock or discredit the political platform.

 APM, in a statement on Sunday, said, “We consider the expression a curious choice of words from a President whose administration has become synonymous with economic hardship, public frustration, political manoeuvring and an increasingly desperate search for electoral validation.”

 The statement read, “In Yoruba political parlance, ‘palemo’ evokes the hurried gathering, packing or clearing away of belongings, sometimes suggestive of preparing to leave or carrying away what one can before departure.

 “Mr President may wish to explain why such vocabulary comes so readily to him. As the saying goes, it takes a master of a craft to recognise the language of fellow practitioners. And when an accuser points one finger at another, the remaining four are invariably directed at himself.

 “The APM will not be distracted by presidential name-calling. Nigerians are far more concerned about the cost of living, the purchasing power of their incomes, insecurity, unemployment, collapsing economic confidence and the daily struggle to survive than the linguistic theatrics of a campaign podium.

 “A President seeking another mandate should be explaining what he has done with the first, not trading taunts with political opponents.

 “Instead of unnecessary distractions like the one at the Mapo Hall jamboree, President Tinubu should have apologised to the people of the state for the unprecedented hardship and suffering that he and his party (APC) have unleashed on them since his assumption of office in 2023.

 “We are equally alarmed by the apparent attempt to draw revered traditional institutions into the APC’s partisan electoral machinery in the state. The presence and engagement of the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, and the Soun of Ogbomoso, Oba Ghandi Afolabi Olaoye, must not be misconstrued as political endorsements or electoral commitments by their communities.

 “Our traditional rulers are custodians of culture, history, peace and communal identity. They are fathers to all, irrespective of political affiliation. Their palaces must remain places where the ruling party, the opposition, the undecided and the politically disenchanted can find counsel, mediation and a sense of belonging. They are not campaign surrogates, electoral assets or instruments for manufacturing political legitimacy.

 “The APC should therefore abandon the illusion that palace visits, royal courtesies, ceremonial appearances or photographs with traditional rulers can substitute for public approval. A royal handshake does not constitute a ballot. A palace audience does not confer electoral authority. Political choreography cannot manufacture the consent of the people.

 “The electorate in Oyo State is politically conscious, discerning and increasingly intolerant of empty promises. Voters will judge political parties and candidates by performance, competence, credibility, economic relief, security and the quality of leadership they have experienced, not by the spectacle of campaign rallies or the proximity of politicians to royal stools.

 “The APM is, therefore, unimpressed by the President’s grandstanding at Mapo Hall. Political arrogance, verbal assaults and carefully staged displays of influence will not erase the hardship Nigerians endure. Neither will the attempted appropriation of revered institutions conceal the fundamental question confronting this administration: what tangible improvement has it delivered to the lives of ordinary citizens that justifies another four years?

 “The answer will not be supplied by campaign slogans, presidential taunts or palace endorsements. It will be supplied by Nigerians themselves at the ballot box.

 “As the Yoruba proverb reminds us, Bí ikún lọ́ ní oko, bí pàkúté, ìpàdé d’ọjọ́ ìbò. However boldly the squirrel roams the farm, the trap awaits on voting day. Political swagger may dominate the rally ground, but the ballot box is where pretensions meet reality.”

 Oladoyinbo noted that the people would have their say on January 16, 2027, adding that no amount of presidential bravado, royal proximity or political intimidation could substitute for the sovereign will of the electorate.

 “The APM remains confident that Oyo voters will distinguish between political noise and credible leadership, between borrowed prestige and earned trust, and between the spectacle of power and the substance of governance,” the statement said.

title: CAF frowns at poor treatment of away teams
description:
The Confederation of African Football has threatened severe sanctions against countries that subject visiting national teams and clubs to poor treatment, warning that it will not tolerate acts of disrespect during continental competitions.
CAF president, Patrice Motsepe, issued the warning on Saturd
content:
The Confederation of African Football has threatened severe sanctions against countries that subject visiting national teams and clubs to poor treatment, warning that it will not tolerate acts of disrespect during continental competitions.

CAF president, Patrice Motsepe, issued the warning on Saturday during a press conference following the 48th Ordinary General Assembly in Abuja, insisting that host countries must guarantee visiting teams the dignity and respect they deserve.

He said the continental governing body would not hesitate to punish countries found responsible for mistreating participating teams, adding that the consequences could be severe.

“There will be consequences for those who treat visiting national teams or football clubs poorly. There will be consequences. And at times, there have to be severe consequences for that,” he said.

“That behaviour doesn’t happen. There’s zero tolerance for that kind of disrespectful behaviour,” the CAF president added.

Motsepe’s warning comes amid recurring concerns over the treatment of visiting teams in African football, particularly issues relating to security, accommodation and the conduct of host officials and supporters.

Nigeria have also experienced such challenges, notably when the Super Eagles were left stranded at Libya’s Al Abraq Airport for several hours ahead of their 2025 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier in October 2024.

Nigerian clubs have also raised concerns over the treatment of visiting teams in continental competitions, highlighting the need for stricter enforcement of CAF’s regulations on hosting arrangements.

The protection and fair treatment of visiting teams remain important to the organisation of CAF competitions, with host countries expected to provide an environment that guarantees the safety and dignity of players and officials.

Motsepe also reiterated CAF’s commitment to strengthening the integrity of African football, particularly through improvements in refereeing standards and the welfare of match officials.

He said the organisation was placing considerable emphasis on ensuring that referees command respect and receive competitive remuneration.

“The issue of referees is critical. Huge focus will make sure that the integrity and the respect of our referees is maintained. But we have to pay referees well, and pay them competitively,” he said.

The CAF president said the organisation would continue working with its 54 member associations to improve the standard and global reputation of African football.

description:

Alex Baena and Johnny Cardoso’
content:
Atletico Madrid stayed on the tail of Spain’s top two with a comfortable 3-0 derby win over Getafe in La Liga on Sunday.

Diego Simeone’s side, third, are five points behind leaders Barcelona and two off second-place Real Madrid, who both won earlier this weekend.

Alex Baena and Johnny Cardoso’s first-half goals, both set up by Julian Alvarez, got the job done away at the Coliseum stadium in the suburbs south of the Spanish capital.

Alex Grimaldo wrapped up the victory in stoppage time with a penalty, after Getafe’s Djene Dakonam was sent off for fouling Alexander Sorloth.

“I think the team had a very good, serious game, in defence and attack,” Atletico playmaker Baena told Movistar.

“We are focused on our own work, not looking at what Barcelona and Madrid are doing, and that suits us best.”

The Rojiblancos moved ahead after 10 minutes, with Alvarez teeing up Baena on the edge of the box to drill home low and hard at the near post.

Getafe goalkeeper David Soria saved well from Alvarez and David Hancko but was at fault for Atletico’s second goal.

Soria missed his punch from Alvarez’s corner and United States international Cardoso turned home with his knee from point-blank range.

Baena smashed over a fine chance for the third after Pablo Barrios played him in behind.

Soria denied Baena in the second half and Lee Kang-in fired over as Atletico continued to control the game and defended solidly to keep Getafe, 17th, at bay.

Atletico substitute Sorloth should have scored with a few minutes remaining but powered an effort straight at Soria.

The Norwegian striker won a penalty when Djene pushed him over as he ran through on goal and Grimaldo dispatched it with the minimum of fuss to close things ou

title: ‘Water went off while I was shaving, no light, no water’ — Tinubu speaks on challenges in Aso Rock
description:
President Bola Tinubu has disclosed that the Presidential Villa in Abuja also experiences electricity and water supply disruptions, similar to the challenges faced by many Nigerians.
The President said water supply was interrupted while he was shaving at the Villa last week, using the experience to
content:
President Bola Tinubu has disclosed that the Presidential Villa in Abuja also experiences electricity and water supply disruptions, similar to the challenges faced by many Nigerians.

The President said water supply was interrupted while he was shaving at the Villa last week, using the experience to highlight the country’s infrastructure challenges and pledge to address them.

Tinubu made the disclosure on Sunday during a special prayer session organised by members of his family in Lagos.

The event came a day after he attended the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State.

Recounting his experience, the President said: “On the Wednesday of last week, I was shaving, and the water went off. And the Villa, you won’t know punishment there too.

“The water went off. So we will correct all this. No light, no water, no electricity, no development.

“We have just started. We can do it, and we will do it for Nigeria.”

Tinubu also used the gathering to mobilise support ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging his supporters in Lagos State to improve voter turnout.

He questioned the low number of votes recorded in Lagos despite the state having about seven million registered voters.

“To me, Lagos is the big deal. How can you have seven million registered voters and produce 100,000, 200,000? That’s failure. Even if you win, I say a win is a win. No. You have to generate the maximum,” he said.

The President urged party supporters to encourage eligible voters to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and participate in the elections, rather than allow internal disagreements to weaken the party.

He specifically called on those aggrieved with other party members to resolve their differences and channel their energy into mobilising voters.

“It’s not anger. Anger will not do it. You are angry with Sylva, or you’re angry with Mulika, call Mulika and let her go vote. We finish the anger that day; you go back. We must generate enough votes to overwhelm them,” Tinubu said.

The President also directed an associate described as his confidant and “bulldozer” to return home and reconcile aggrieved members of the party before extending the peace effort to other states.

“Go back home and reconcile with everybody. That is the order of the president. Go back home and reconcile with everybody. And when you finish that, you move to Jigawa, you move to other places and reconcile them. Beg them,” he said.

Reflecting on his political experience, Tinubu said he had also put aside personal grievances during the build-up to the 2023 general election to pursue a broader political objective.

He recalled that he accepted a campaign role despite harbouring anger at the time, adding that he eventually moved past the disagreement.

The President also linked forgiveness to his religious beliefs, saying people who seek forgiveness from Allah should be willing to extend the same to others.

“If you cannot give it, why are you asking Allah to give you forgiveness? What you want from him, you must be able to give to humanity,” he said.

Tinubu attributed his political journey, from his time as governor to his emergence as President, to prayers, perseverance and support from his family.

He also challenged young people at the gathering to take responsibility for mobilising support ahead of the 2027 election, saying the next generation would determine the country’s political future.

“The challenge is yours now. It’s in your hands to knock on doors, get all the PVC out, and do what is right,” he said.

Several governors attended the prayer session, including those of Lagos, Kwara, Imo, Gombe and Kaduna states.

title: Climate Talks Collapse In Chaotic End To COP31
description: The COP31 climate talks failed Sunday as a contentious deal collapsed over fossil fuels and the summit in Turkey stretched into record overtime.The final agreement was rejected in a chaotic finale to a UN climate summit that ran two days over schedule, underscoring the strains on diplomacy in an inc
content:
The COP31 climate talks failed Sunday as a contentious deal collapsed over fossil fuels and the summit in Turkey stretched into record overtime.

The final agreement was rejected in a chaotic finale to a UN climate summit that ran two days over schedule, underscoring the strains on diplomacy in an increasingly fractured world.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who urged nations to send fossil fuels “the way of the dinosaurs” during a fiery appearance at the talks, expressed deep dismay.

“I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands,” the outgoing UN chief said in a statement.

COP31 negotiations chair Chris Bowen, who unsuccessfully sought to broker consensus among nearly 200 nations, conceded he could not overcome what he called “unbridgeable red lines”.

“Unfortunately, we were unable to reach agreement on a cover decision… And that’s disappointing. Very disappointing,” Bowen, who is Australia’s climate minister, told a throng of reporters.

More than 49 hours after the summit was supposed to end, COP31 President and Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum banged the gavel to conclude the marathon talks.

Calls For Reform

Bowen said the summit backdrop was “the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory”, as soaring energy prices and fallout from the Middle East war complicated the search for unity.

Under pressure to show progress in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal, Bowen sought an overarching “cover decision” to prove countries were still united in tackling the crisis.

But his plan unravelled as familiar fault lines emerged over fossil fuels, with the EU and Saudi Arabia locking horns over the pace of the shift away from coal, oil and gas.

The negotiations stalled as oil-producing states blocked any mention of phasing out fossil fuels in the final deal.

“We will not endorse a cover decision… that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change,” said Ireland’s climate minister, Darragh O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency.

“And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuels.”

Panama, Vanuatu and the Marshall Islands also objected, and as the deal imploded, COP31 became the longest climate summit on record.

Former US vice president and climate advocate Al Gore said it was “outrageous that a handful of petrostates have veto power over any mention of fossil fuels”.

The COP process is “in need of significant reform”, Gore said on X, as most countries sought “to move forward in good faith.”

Falling Short

The outcome revived memories of the failed Copenhagen summit of 2009 and raised fresh doubts about the effectiveness of climate diplomacy.

“It certainly fell short today,” said UN climate chief Simon Stiell, describing progress over the marathon fortnight of negotiations in Antalya as “limited”.

“The world cannot afford a repeat,” he said.

Frustrated by the inertia, countries are pushing ahead outside the COP process.

Around 60 countries joined a first-of-its-kind conference in April on phasing out fossil fuels while several nations at COP31 unveiled their own plans to exit coal, oil and gas.

In a last-ditch bid for compromise, COP31 co-hosts Turkey and Australia could only muster a veiled reference to fossil fuels in the final text.

But the pact also took fire for retaining a call to expand carbon capture — a costly technology championed by the fossil fuel industry.

“We believe that climate change requires all solutions on the table,” said Mohammad Ayoub, a climate negotiator for oil giant Saudi Arabia.

Facing blowback over the fossil fuels omission, the co-host nations tried to rally support behind a global goal to electrify the world economy.

They said “electrification” could cut heat-trapping emissions and bolster energy security, but the target was ultimately torpedoed, along with the rest of the doomed Antalya Pact.

‘Profound Disappointment’

Countries lamented a missed opportunity to reinforce the Paris Agreement’s 1.5C target, which scientists expect the world to overshoot in a few years as carbon-cutting goals fall short.

The summit also widened fault lines over science, with a fight over the work of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) spilling into the negotiations.

“We are profoundly disappointed by the substance of the cover decision,” said UK climate negotiator Kate Hughes.

“It moves us backwards on the science… It is a lowest common denominator where it should have been, instead, presenting bold collective ambition on climate action.”

As always, the summit laid bare the divide between major polluters driving climate change and smaller nations bearing the brunt of its impact.

Developing nations pushed for a $120 billion climate target that disappeared from the failed deal.

AFP

title: Alcaraz downs Zverev to win ATP Finals for first time
description:
Carlos Alcaraz won the ATP Finals with a 6-2, 7-6 (9/7) victory over world number one Alexander Zverev in the title match in Turin on Sunday.



After becoming the youngest man to complete a career Grand Slam at the start of the season with victory in the Australian Open, the 23-year-old has bookend
content:
Carlos Alcaraz won the ATP Finals with a 6-2, 7-6 (9/7) victory over world number one Alexander Zverev in the title match in Turin on Sunday.

After becoming the youngest man to complete a career Grand Slam at the start of the season with victory in the Australian Open, the 23-year-old has bookended an up-and-down year with a first title at the season-ending showpiece tournament.

Alongside Roger Federer, Andre Agassi and Novak Djokovic, Alcaraz now forms part of an exclusive list of men to have won all four majors and the ATP Finals.

With his illustrious compatriot Rafael Nadal never managing to win the season-ending tournament, Alcaraz became the first Spanish champion since Alex Corretja in 1998.

“It’s been an amazing week. I couldn’t finish the week in a better way, so I’m really proud,” Alcaraz said after capturing his sixth title of the year.

“I’ve been through really difficult moments with myself, with my team, and we could go through everything. I’m playing great tennis, so for me, lifting this trophy is something that I’ve been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me,” he added of the hamstring issue he suffered earlier in the tournament.

A wrist injury had caused Alcaraz to miss a good chunk of the middle of the season and following that victory in Melbourne he failed to add to his seven major titles.

But since returning in August, he has enjoyed a blistering end to the year, winning his last 14 matches to capture trophies at the Vienna Open, the Paris Masters for the first time and now the elusive ATP Finals.

He lost in the season-ender’s final to Jannik Sinner last year, but with the injured Italian having curtailed his season, Alcaraz found himself again in the Turin title match against a world number one.

Zverev, a two-time ATP Finals champion, broke his Grand Slam duck this season by claiming the French and US Opens, catapulting him above Alcaraz and Sinner to the top of the rankings.

– Topsy-turvy –

The top two seeds in Italy, Alcaraz and Zverev were a cut above the rest all throughout the tournament, both topping their respective pools with three wins from three.

The first set of Alcaraz’s semi-final win over Ben Shelton was the only frame either player had dropped all week.

Indeed Zverev had marched into the final without dropping a service game, but he was mightily tested straight out of the traps by Alcaraz as the world number three forced three break points in the very first game before the German dug in to hold.

Alcaraz was not so wasteful two games later, however, as he broke Zverev to love when the 29-year-old overcooked a mid-court forehand.

Zverev forced break-back points in the next game but, after failing to convert, he was left to rue his luck even further as the Spaniard broke to 30 to grow his lead to 4-1.

Zverev wiped out one break but Alcaraz was nonetheless firmly in the ascendancy and pounced for a third time on the Hamburg native’s serve in an entertaining seventh game which saw Zverev dejectedly chuck his racquet to the floor after netting a smash from an Alcaraz tweener lob.

A netted backhand by Zverev — his 19th unforced error of the match — on Alcaraz’s first set point then brought an end to a surprisingly sloppy opening frame.

Both players exchanged breaks in the second set as it went the distance.

The Murcian took a 3-0 lead in the tie-break before Zverev won the next six points to bring up three set points.

But the Spaniard struck back to wipe them out before getting a mini-break to bring up championship point on his own serve.

The first went begging when he whipped a forehand into the tramlines but he brought up a second with a drop-shot and sealed the title with a backhand.

title: 2027: If I’m not on the ballot, Tinubu is waiting for a coronation – Atiku
description:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has dismissed reports that he has withdrawn from the 2027 presidential race, insisting that he remains in the contest and has no intention of stepping aside for any aspirant.
Atiku described the reports as false, malicious and deliberately circulated to undermine
content:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has dismissed reports that he has withdrawn from the 2027 presidential race, insisting that he remains in the contest and has no intention of stepping aside for any aspirant.

Atiku described the reports as false, malicious and deliberately circulated to undermine his presidential ambition and strengthen President Bola Tinubu’s chances of securing re-election.

In a statement issued on Sunday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the former vice-president said nobody claiming to be his supporter had the authority to announce his withdrawal from the race.

He maintained that displaying his name on campaign materials or identifying with his political movement did not automatically make anyone his representative.

“Putting my name on a placard does not make someone my supporter. Putting a lie in that person’s mouth does not make it my decision,” Atiku said.

He accused those promoting the withdrawal reports of attempting to eliminate him from the contest in order to give Tinubu an easier path to victory.

“Any party promoting the lie that I have stepped down is doing Tinubu’s work. Every false withdrawal story tries to clear his strongest opponent from the field.

“If I am not on the ballot, Bola Tinubu might as well wait for a coronation. But I am in this race to win, and Nigerians will have their choice,” he stated.

Atiku also criticised opposition politicians who, according to him, were circulating false declarations of support instead of concentrating on persuading Nigerians to vote for their candidates.

He urged those seeking to defeat the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to take their campaigns directly to the electorate.

The former vice-president further said his campaign’s Affordable Life agenda remained focused on addressing the economic difficulties facing Nigerians, particularly the rising cost of food and transportation.

“Hunger and poverty are not on social media. They are in our markets, our homes and every community where families struggle to afford food and transport,” he said.

Atiku insisted that he did not need any candidate to withdraw for him and would not step aside for anyone.

“I do not need anyone to step down for me, and I am stepping down for no one,” he declared.

He urged his supporters to remain committed to the campaign, keep their Permanent Voter Cards ready and intensify grassroots mobilisation ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election.

The statement comes amid political discussions and calls for opposition cooperation ahead of the 2027 general election, including moves by some groups associated with Atiku to endorse other opposition figures.

title: 2027 Elections: Lagos Is The Big Deal To Me, Says Tinubu
description: President Bola Tinubu has described Lagos State as crucial ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to mobilise voters and ensure a higher turnout in the state.Tinubu spoke on Sunday during a prayer session at the hall of the Yoruba Tennis Club in
content:
President Bola Tinubu has described Lagos State as crucial ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to mobilise voters and ensure a higher turnout in the state.

Tinubu spoke on Sunday during a prayer session at the hall of the Yoruba Tennis Club in Lagos, where he urged them not to generate the maximum win.

“The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday. But we cannot take it for granted. You must knock on your neighbour’s door.

“Tell them to get, collect their PVC,” he said.

The President also urged the attendees at the prayer session that collecting the Permanent Voter Card (PVC) was essential to exercising their democratic rights.

“If you are here and you don’t have PVC, you are just here for amala and ewedu,” he told those present jokingly.

“If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16th and February 6. And that’s what I want to ask you to exercise.

”To me, Lagos is the big deal. How can you have seven million registered voters and produce 100,000-200,000 votes? That’s failure.

“Even if you win, and say, ‘A win is a win,’ no. You have to generate the maximum,” he added.

Tinubu lost the state to Peter Obi, who was then the presidential candidate of the Labour Party, despite the President’s longstanding political influence in the commercial capital where he served as governor from 1999 to 2007.

According to results announced by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Obi polled 582,454 votes to defeat Tinubu, who secured 572,606 votes in the February 25, 2023 presidential election.

The Peoples Democratic Party’s candidate in the election, Atiku Abubakar, came third with 75,750 votes, while Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party scored 8,442 votes.

The results showed that although Tinubu won 11 of Lagos State’s 20 local government areas, Obi secured the overall victory, winning nine local government areas, including Alimosho, Ojo and Oshodi-Isolo.

Lagos had 6,214,970 PVCs collected ahead of the 2023 election, the highest number recorded by any state in the country.

However, only 1,335,729 votes were cast in the state, comprising 1,271,451 valid votes and 64,278 rejected ballots.

Tinubu is seeking to consolidate his political support in the state as he prepares for another presidential contest in 2027, with opposition candidates, including Obi and Atiku, also in the race.

title: Leadership crisis: Odukoya says Fountain of Life church remains strong, ‘unshakable’
description:
The Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, has declared that the church remains strong and unshakable amid its lingering leadership crisis, which has now resulted in legal battles.
Odukoya made the declaration in a post on his X handle on Sunday night, alongside a highlight vid
content:
The Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, has declared that the church remains strong and unshakable amid its lingering leadership crisis, which has now resulted in legal battles.

Odukoya made the declaration in a post on his X handle on Sunday night, alongside a highlight video of the church’s service.

“We are strong… We are unshakable… We are unbreakable… We are @TFOLC!” he wrote, adding the hashtags #TFOLC and #GodNoGoShameUs.

His post came amid an escalating dispute between him and some members of the church’s Board of Trustees over his position as senior pastor and the succession arrangement following the death of the church’s founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya.

The crisis took a legal turn on November 18, when the Lagos State High Court restrained Jimmy from presenting himself as the church’s Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head.

The order, granted by Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin in Suit No. LD/0126PRA/2026, followed an application by the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church.

The court also restrained him from interfering with the church’s governance, administration and activities, either personally or through proxies.

The order was made ex parte, meaning it was granted without first hearing the other party. The court, however, preserved Jimmy’s right to apply to have it set aside or respond to the substantive claims after being served with the court processes. The matter was adjourned until December 1 for mention.

Addressing worshippers during Sunday’s service, Jimmy said he had heard about the injunction but had not received the court processes.

“I heard there was an injunction against me. I heard, but I have not seen it, and I have not been served. They said that there was no substituted service. Legally, I have not been served,” he said.

In a separate legal action, Jimmy and the Incorporated Trustees of the church approached the Federal High Court in Lagos to challenge the decisions taken by eight members of the Board of Trustees.

The suit, marked FHC/LAG/CS/1568/2026, was filed on November 20 against his sister, Pastor Tolu Odukoya, and seven other trustees, including Biodun Balogun, Biodun Awosika, Rotimi Okpaise, Tobi Enuha, Gbenga Onabanjo, Fred Ohiani and Akin Osinbajo.

The plaintiffs are asking the court to determine whether meetings held by some trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, and the resolutions reached at the meetings, complied with the church’s constitution.

In his supporting affidavit, Jimmy maintained that he was appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees at an emergency board meeting on September 14, 2023, and subsequently installed that month.

He alleged that the meetings convened by the defendants and the decisions taken at them violated the church’s constitution. He also asked the court to restrain the defendants from interfering with his functions and the management of the church pending the determination of the dispute.

The Federal High Court had yet to determine the issues raised in the suit as of the time of filing this report.

The leadership crisis became public on November 17, when a faction of the church’s trustees announced that it had withdrawn recognition of Jimmy as senior pastor and named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader.

The trustees reportedly based their decision on a December 2021 video in which the late founder allegedly identified Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor, with Jimmy assigned an administrative support role and leadership of the youth ministry.

They also raised objections to Jimmy’s remarriage.

However, Jimmy and the church rejected the purported removal, insisting that his appointment in September 2023 was valid and that the trustees’ action was unconstitutional.

The church had also maintained that the trustees behind the removal announcement were asked to resign in March 2026 over alleged violations of its constitution.

The dispute has since generated uncertainty over the church’s leadership structure, with both sides advancing opposing interpretations of the constitution and the late founder’s succession instructions.

title: Alcaraz beats Zverev to claim first ATP finals title
description:
Carlos Alcaraz defeated world number one Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6 (9-7) to win his first ATP Finals title, capping a remarkable comeback season following a lengthy injury absence.
As reported by BBC Sport on Sunday, the Spaniard produced an impressive performance to overcome Zverev in a dramatic fi
content:
Carlos Alcaraz defeated world number one Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6 (9-7) to win his first ATP Finals title, capping a remarkable comeback season following a lengthy injury absence.

As reported by BBC Sport on Sunday, the Spaniard produced an impressive performance to overcome Zverev in a dramatic final, sealing victory in the second-set tie-break after two hours of intense competition.

Alcaraz, who was still wearing heavy strapping around his upper-left leg following an injury scare earlier in the week, fell to the ground in celebration after securing the biggest title of his season.

The victory marked his 14th consecutive win and third successive tournament triumph, further underlining his return to top form after spending more than four months on the sidelines with a wrist injury.

The 23-year-old began the season by becoming the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam but was subsequently forced out of action by the injury.

However, since returning at the US Open in August, Alcaraz has won 21 of his 22 matches and claimed titles at four of the five tournaments he has entered.

His latest success also made him the youngest player to win all four Grand Slam titles and the season-ending ATP Finals, joining an exclusive group of just four players to achieve the feat.

Speaking after his victory, Alcaraz described the triumph as a special moment after enduring difficult times during his recovery.

“Lifting this trophy is something I have been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me,” he said.

“I have been through really difficult moments with myself, with my team. For me, it’s been an amazing week. I couldn’t finish the week in a better way.”

Meanwhile, Zverev ended the 2026 season with an ATP Tour-leading 69 match victories after reaching the final without dropping a set in his previous four matches.

However, the German struggled to contain Alcaraz, whose aggressive play and quality from the baseline disrupted his opponent’s rhythm.

Alcaraz made the stronger start, taking advantage of Zverev’s early struggles to establish a 4-1 lead with two breaks of serve before comfortably closing out the opening set.

Zverev fought harder in the second set, but Alcaraz maintained his composure in the tie-break to secure the title and complete a memorable return to the top of men’s tennis.

title: WHO chief pleads for peace in Ebola-hit DR Congo area
description:
The head of the World Health Organisation on Sunday pleaded for peace in the epicentre of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ebola outbreak that has killed nearly 5,700 people.
Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the frequency of attacks across the country’s east had increased since the end of October,
content:
The head of the World Health Organisation on Sunday pleaded for peace in the epicentre of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ebola outbreak that has killed nearly 5,700 people.

Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the frequency of attacks across the country’s east had increased since the end of October, seriously affecting the Ebola response.

“Heavy fighting has been ongoing since yesterday in the vicinity of a hospital in Ituri — in an area close to where the Ebola outbreak first emerged,” the UN health agency chief said on X.

He said medical staff had been sheltering for their lives in a maternity ward in the facility for more than 24 hours.

“The situation has disrupted the work of the hospital and the wider Ebola response, putting patients, families and health workers at grave risk,” said Tedros.

He said the WHO was trying to arrange a safe exit for the team and “for the hospital facilities, staff and patients to be protected.”

“The best medicine is peace,” said Tedros.

A total of 5,678 deaths out of 11,613 cases have been confirmed in the vast central African country’s worst-ever Ebola outbreak, according to the WHO.

The virus has spread across swathes of the DRC’s east and northeast, which have been plagued by violence for more than 30 years.

In an update on Saturday, the WHO said that while some areas had seen a slight decline in cases, “sustained, high-level transmission continues overall in the country”.

Ituri and Nord Kivu remain the most affected provinces.

The high proportion of deaths occurring in communities, meaning outside of dedicated treatment centres, especially among young children, “continues to highlight challenges in early case detection and timely access to appropriate care”, the WHO said.

Tedros has determined that the outbreak remains a public health emergency of international concern.

AFP

title: 2027: Tinubu orders Masari, Badaru to reconcile APC leaders
description:
President Bola Tinubu has urged leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to set aside personal differences, forgive one another and embrace reconciliation as the party prepares for the 2027 general elections.
According to his spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, Tinubu gave the charge on Sunday during a s
content:
President Bola Tinubu has urged leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to set aside personal differences, forgive one another and embrace reconciliation as the party prepares for the 2027 general elections.

According to his spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, Tinubu gave the charge on Sunday during a special prayer session organised in his honour by members of his extended family at the Yoruba Tennis Club in Lagos.

The President specifically directed his Special Adviser on Political Matters, Alhaji Ibrahim Masari, and former Minister of Defence, Alhaji Abubakar Badaru, to spearhead reconciliation efforts among aggrieved party leaders across the country.

Addressing reports of a disagreement between Katsina State Governor, Dikko Radda, and Masari, Tinubu instructed his political adviser to return home and resolve the differences.

“Alhaji Kabiru Masari, go back home and reconcile with everybody. That is the President’s order. When you finish that, you move to Jigawa. You move to other places and reconcile them, beg them because we have to reconcile and every anger must dissipate and evaporate,” he said.

He gave a similar assignment to Badaru, a former governor of Jigawa State, stressing the need for peace and cooperation among party members.

Tinubu maintained that personal grievances should not be allowed to undermine the collective interest of the APC, particularly as the party looks towards retaining power in 2027.

Reflecting on his emergence as President in the 2023 general elections, Tinubu acknowledged the difficulties Nigerians experienced during the cash scarcity and fuel shortages that characterised the period.

He recalled that despite the challenges, he secured victory, attributing his emergence to divine intervention.

“People cried. People suffered. People died. People had no five naira in their pockets because their money was in the bank and they couldn’t get it out. There was also no fuel. We invoked the spirit of Almighty Allah and said, ‘Kun faya kun’. It got us there, and we have the presidency. Allah gives power to whom he wants, and he takes it from whoever he wants,” the President said.

Revisiting his famous 2022 political declaration, “Emilokan”, meaning “It is my turn”, Tinubu told supporters that the time had come for them to reciprocate by working towards his re-election.

He described the moment as “Eyinlokan”, urging Lagos residents and other supporters to intensify grassroots mobilisation, encourage eligible voters to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and participate actively in the forthcoming elections.

“The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday, but we cannot take it for granted. You must knock on your neighbour’s door, tell them to collect their PVC. If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16th and February 6th… We must generate enough votes to overwhelm the opponents,” he said.

The prayer session attracted several political leaders and government officials, including Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu; Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani; Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq; Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun; and Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma.

Others present were National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu, Chief of Staff to the President Femi Gbajabiamila, Lagos State Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat, Minister of Education Tunji Alausa and Speaker of the Lagos State House of Assembly, Mudashiru Obasa.

In his remarks, Sanwo-Olu described Tinubu as an epitome of justice, fairness, equity and inclusive governance.

Badaru, who spoke on behalf of northern leaders, recalled Tinubu’s support for former President Muhammadu Buhari during the 2015 and 2019 presidential elections, urging voters in the North to reciprocate by supporting the current administration.

Also speaking, elder statesman Alhaji Lateef Femi Okunnu, 94, who chaired the occasion, pledged to campaign and vote for Tinubu in 2027.

title: Tinubu Urges APC Leaders To Unite Ahead Of 2027 Elections
description: President Bola Tinubu has called on leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to reconcile their differences ahead of the 2027 general elections, underscoring the virtue of forgiveness.He made the call on Sunday at a prayer session organised in his honour by his extended family in Lagos State,
content:
President Bola Tinubu has called on leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to reconcile their differences ahead of the 2027 general elections, underscoring the virtue of forgiveness.

He made the call on Sunday at a prayer session organised in his honour by his extended family in Lagos State, urging APC leaders to forgive one another and seek reconciliation.

His message was specifically directed at his Special Adviser on Political Matters, Ibrahim Masari, and former defence minister, Abubakar Badaru, both of whom were in the audience at the hall of the Yoruba Tennis Club, where the President spoke.

While reacting to reports of a misunderstanding between Governor Dikko Radda and Masari in Katsina State, Tinubu, in a statement by his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, urged Masari to go back home to reconcile with his governor.

“Alhaji Kabiru Masari, go back home and reconcile with everybody. That is the President’s order. When you finish that, you move to Jigawa. You move to other places and reconcile with them, beg them because we have to reconcile and every anger must dissipate and evaporate,” the President said.

He also gave the same order to Badaru, the former governor of Jigawa State.

President Tinubu appealed to all APC leaders to set aside personal differences, strengthen internal cohesion, and work collectively to consolidate his administration’s gains ahead of the 2027 elections.

He thanked the organisers of the Islamic prayer session and clerics who prayed for him, his administration, and Nigeria.

‘Obstacles Were On Our Way’

He also thanked God for his victory in the 2023 presidential election, despite formidable obstacles which he said “were on our way”.

“People cried. People suffered. People died. People had no ₦5 in their pockets because their money was in the bank and they couldn’t get it out. There was also no fuel.

“We invoked the spirit of Almighty Allah and said, ‘Kun faya kun (‘Be, and it becomes’). It got us there, and we have the presidency. Allah gives power to whom he wants, and he takes it from whoever he wants,” the President said.

The President recalled that he invoked “Emilokan’s spirit (it is my turn) in 2022.

“It is now your turn (Eyinlokan) to make the re-election possible,” he was quoted as saying.

He appealed to Lagosians to come out en masse on Election Day to exercise their right to vote.

“The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday, but we cannot take it for granted. You must knock on your neighbour’s door, tell them to collect their PVC. If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16th and February 6th, and that’s what I want to ask you to exercise,” the President said.

“We must generate enough votes to overwhelm the opponents,” he emphasised.

He reaffirmed his commitment to providing purposeful leadership, strengthening national unity and justice, and building a prosperous country for all Nigerians.

Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu of Lagos State described the President as an epitome of justice, fairness, equity, and inclusive governance, calling these virtues essential pillars for building a united, peaceful, and prosperous Nigeria.

Former Governor of Jigawa, Badaru Abubakar, said northerners appreciated President Tinubu’s support for the late former President Muhammadu Buhari in his 2015 and 2019 election victories.

Badaru urged Northern voters to reciprocate the gesture and help the President consolidate the administration’s achievements so far.

The chairman of the occasion and elder statesman, 94-year-old Lateef Okunnu, promised to canvass and vote for the President on January 16, 2027.

He said the President has done a lot to be re-elected.

The elder statesman also emphasised the need to uphold justice, saying that the Tinubu administration is focusing on the economy and infrastructure, especially the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, as well as strengthening the naira and foreign reserves.

In their vote of thanks, representatives of the Tinubu family, Rafiu Tinubu and Iyalode Bintu Tinubu, thanked God for the family’s blessings and urged Nigerians to support the President in his determination to deliver the dividends of democracy to the people.

Chairman of Lagos State Government House Chapel, Honsu Oluremi, referenced the Bible and urged the people to always pray for leaders’ success.

The coordinator of the prayer session and the Grand Chief Imam of Lagos, Sheikh Sulaimon Oluwatoyin Abou-Nolla, while reading from the holy Qur’an, asked Allah to grant the President success in his affairs and good health.

The prayer session was attended by Muslim and Christian clerics as well as the governors of Kaduna, Kwara, Ogun, and Imo states.

Other in attendance included National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu, Chief of Staff to the President Femi Gbajabiamila, and Lagos Deputy Governor Kadiri Obafemi Hamzat.

Also present were the Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa; Speaker of the Lagos State House of Assembly, Mudashiru Obasa; the Chairman, Board of Trustees of the Coalition of Northern Groups (CNG), Nasturah Sharriff; the Tinubu family members and party faithful.

title: Tinubu’s reforms will be difficult to stabilise if he’s not re-elected - Wike
description:
Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has warned that President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms could be difficult to sustain if he fails to secure re-election in 2027.



Wike said the president needed another term to consolidate the policies introduced by his administration, argui
content:
Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has warned that President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms could be difficult to sustain if he fails to secure re-election in 2027.

Wike said the president needed another term to consolidate the policies introduced by his administration, arguing that Nigeria was beginning to move towards economic recovery and prosperity despite the initial hardship caused by the reforms.

The minister spoke on Sunday during a thanksgiving service at St Peter’s Anglican Church in Rumueprikom, Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State.

He said Tinubu had taken courageous decisions to address the country’s economic challenges, particularly the removal of petrol subsidy, which he acknowledged came with difficulties for Nigerians.

According to Wike, abandoning the president’s policies before their benefits fully materialise could undermine the progress made so far.

“This country was on the verge of collapse. But by the grace of God, He gave us somebody who is courageous,” he said.

Wike argued that the country was entering a phase where the foundations laid by the administration could begin yielding positive results, stressing the importance of continuity.

“He has laid his foundation; now it’s time for prosperity. If we don’t re-elect him, then it will be difficult to stabilise what he has done,” the minister said.

He also cited improvements in the university system, claiming that strikes over unpaid entitlements, which previously disrupted academic activities, had become less frequent under Tinubu.

The minister further recalled the difficulties pensioners faced in receiving their payments, saying the president’s decisions had helped address some of the challenges confronting the country.

Wike called on Nigerians across religious divides to support Tinubu’s re-election, insisting that the president needed votes from Christians, Muslims and traditional worshippers.

“I am not a native doctor, but I need their votes now. I need everybody’s votes because I know they are registered voters. The Muslims, I need their votes too. The Christians like you, we need your votes,” he said.

He also dismissed claims of religious imbalance in the administration’s appointments, arguing that Christians had received better representation under Tinubu than in previous governments.

“Since Nigeria was created, we have never had the kind of appointments that are going on in this country now,” Wike said.

title: ‘We need to turn that anger into energy’ – Pochettino reacts to Man Utd’s 4-0 loss
description:
Mauricio Pochettino said Manchester United must harness the pain from a 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool on Sunday into positive change despite feeling aggrieved by Leny Yoro’s eighth-minute red card.



Pochettino’s reign got off to a nightmare start when Yoro was controversially sent off for bringing do
content:
Mauricio Pochettino said Manchester United must harness the pain from a 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool on Sunday into positive change despite feeling aggrieved by Leny Yoro’s eighth-minute red card.

Pochettino’s reign got off to a nightmare start when Yoro was controversially sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak.

United never recovered as Liverpool instantly took advantage when Dominik Szoboszlai smashed home the resulting free-kick.

Defeat leaves United still second bottom of the Premier League and at risk of relegation from the English top flight for the first time since 1974.

“It’s so painful, we feel pain for that defeat, but we need to keep the head up and translate that anger to an energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game,” said Pochettino.

“We need to accept the reality and we need to be responsible. We need to be united, we need to be all together and I think we feel disappointed because it’s clear that after eight minutes, I think, the plan was in the bin.”

Isak had taken a heavy touch and the ball appeared to be running through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens before contact was made by Yoro.

“I’m not going to change what happened and being respectful is always important,” added Pochettino.

“At the same time I need to defend my club and say what I feel. I feel like that was an action that everyone who plays football can see was clearly not a red card.”

– ‘Changes the game completely’ –

A repeat of United’s 7-0 thrashing at Anfield three years ago appeared on the cards when Florian Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s lead inside 13 minutes.

However, Pochettino’s introduction of Harry Maguire and switch to a back five helped stem the bleeding until teenager Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz rounded off the rout in the second half.

“It hurts a lot. It’s a difficult moment for us but we are the only ones who can get out of that situation,” said United captain Bruno Fernandes, who raged against the decision to dismiss Yoro.

“There are too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR taking so long to see to make a mistake like this that can change the game,” added the Portuguese international.

“It’s not because of them we conceded the goal from the free-kick, but it changes the game completely.”

Victory lifts Liverpool up to fourth in the table and within seven points of leaders Arsenal.

Andoni Iraola savoured the adulation coming his way at full-time and believes his side should have run up an even bigger margin of victory.

Isak and Bradley Barcola were guilty of wasting a number of big chances either side of half-time.

“It’s difficult to enjoy in the Premier League, normally you suffer even if you win, but I think we could celebrate at half-time and enjoy it a little bit,” said Iraola.

“We have missed some clear chances today. In other games you will remember those chances, but today we’ve controlled the game and everything was happening around the (United) box.”

Vanguard News

Gumi made the call in a Facebook post on Sunday, stressing that traditiona
content:
Islamic cleric, Sheikh Ahmad Gumi, has called for the immediate removal of any Emir found guilty of immoral conduct, saying such action is necessary to protect the integrity and credibility of traditional institutions.

Gumi made the call in a Facebook post on Sunday, stressing that traditional rulers must uphold high standards of conduct befitting the positions they occupy.

He said any Emir found culpable of immoral behaviour should be removed and replaced without delay to preserve the dignity of the traditional institution.

“Any Emir found guilty of immoral conduct should be removed and replaced immediately to safeguard the integrity, dignity and credibility of the traditional institution,” he said.

The cleric’s position underscores the need for accountability among traditional rulers, whose authority and influence in their communities depend significantly on public trust, moral standing and respect for established customs.

Traditional institutions remain important in community leadership, conflict resolution and the preservation of cultural and religious values, making the conduct of their occupants a matter of public concern.

title: Yoruba group laments Alaafin’s cancelled Benin visit
description:
A Yoruba socio-cultural association in the Republic of Benin, Isokan Omo Yoruba Benin, has expressed disappointment over the cancellation of the Alaafin of Oyo, Oba Abimbola Akeem Owoade’s planned visit to the country.
Oba Owoade I had been scheduled to arrive by road through the Seme border on Thur
content:
A Yoruba socio-cultural association in the Republic of Benin, Isokan Omo Yoruba Benin, has expressed disappointment over the cancellation of the Alaafin of Oyo, Oba Abimbola Akeem Owoade’s planned visit to the country.

Oba Owoade I had been scheduled to arrive by road through the Seme border on Thursday, November 12, 2026.

He was expected to serve as the guest of honour when members of the Yoruba community gathered for the association’s fifth General Assembly in Ouidah on Saturday, November 14.

Instead, the visit was called off on Friday, November 13, leaving organisers and community members disappointed despite extensive preparations made by Yoruba communities and kingdoms across Benin.

The group noted that substantial financial and logistical commitments had already been made ahead of the monarch’s planned arrival.

According to the association’s president, Professor John Igue, in a statement made available on Sunday, “Isokan Omo Yoruba Benin had budgeted 23,134,000 FCFA to receive the monarch, and millions had already been spent in preparation for his arrival.”

Igue said the visit was meant to promote unity within the Yoruba community, strengthen ties between Benin and Nigeria, and celebrate the Yoruba language and culture.

He noted that the monarch’s presence was also intended to support discussions on establishing a global Yoruba organisation dedicated to promoting Yoruba culture and language.

The association’s president said the decision to cancel the visit stemmed from tensions over the representation of the Yoruba community and the roles of individuals and groups involved in receiving the monarch.

He also addressed the role of an emissary linked to preparations for the trip, disputing his mandate.

“The role of the emissary presented as mandated by the Oyo Palace is strongly contested,” he said.

“This emissary in question is not on a mission for the Alaafin of Oyo, nor for the association Isokan Omo Yoruba Benin over which I preside,” Prof. Igue added.

The statement noted that discussions surrounding the visit touched on competing interests over representation and who stood to gain institutional and symbolic benefits before Beninese authorities from the Alaafin’s presence.

Following the gathering in Ouidah on November 14 without the announced guest of honour, the statement added that the monarch’s absence, after his visit had been officially announced, left numerous questions for the Oyo Palace to answer.

title: Any Emir guilty of immorality should be dethroned — Gumi
description:
Islamic cleric, Sheikh Ahmad Gumi, has called for the removal of any traditional ruler found guilty of immoral conduct, saying such action is necessary to protect the integrity of the traditional institution.
Gumi made the call in a Facebook post on Sunday amid the sexual harassment allegation again
content:
Islamic cleric, Sheikh Ahmad Gumi, has called for the removal of any traditional ruler found guilty of immoral conduct, saying such action is necessary to protect the integrity of the traditional institution.

Gumi made the call in a Facebook post on Sunday amid the sexual harassment allegation against the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Faruk Umar Faruk, by a female foreign tourist.

The cleric said any emir found culpable of immoral conduct should be dethroned and immediately replaced.

“Any Emir found guilty of immoral conduct should be removed and replaced immediately to safeguard the integrity, dignity and credibility of the traditional institution,” he wrote.

The statement comes after a female tourist, identified on Instagram as @beduinqa, accused the Daura monarch of touching her inappropriately during a visit to his palace in Katsina State on November 14.

The tourist alleged that the monarch held her hand, hugged her and kissed her on the cheek before touching her breasts without her consent.

She said she objected to the alleged conduct but that the Emir laughed at her reaction. She later shared her account on Instagram after leaving Nigeria.

Posting the video of her encounter with the king, she wrote, “Recently I finished a 30-day journey exploring all around #Nigeria. I had amazing time, saw beautiful places, met great people. Unfortunately I had also a bad experience when visiting #daura in Northern Nigeria.

“During visit to the #emirofdaura palace I was taken to an elegant room where we sat on a couch and started talking. It was strange for me that he grabbed my hand and started playing with it.

“Then when we stood up, he hugged me, kissed my cheek (which was also surprising for me), and then he grabbed my boobs. That was a shock for me. I told him ’emir no, no, no, no’ ’emir you cannot be touching’, but he was just laughing about it.

“I wasn’t sexually assaulted at any moment when walking through streets of Nigeria, even in busy crowded places, but to my shock I was assaulted in a palace by a traditional leader who should be behaving in exemplary and dignified way.

“I felt disgusted by this experience, and have been reliving it in my thoughts. It happened exactly one week ago, on Saturday 14th November, but I waited until after leaving Nigeria to post it.

“I suspect I wasn’t first woman he assaulted but probably first one with a proof recorded. I have meta glasses and quickly turned them on.”

The allegation sparked reactions on social media, with some Nigerians calling for accountability.

Amnesty International Nigeria also called on the Katsina State Government and the police to conduct a transparent and independent investigation into the allegation, stressing that the Emir should be held accountable if found culpable.

However, a source in the Emir’s palace denied the allegation, saying there was nothing improper during the tourist’s visit.

The Katsina State Commissioner for Information, Culture and Tourism, Dr Bala Zango, told PUNCH Online on Sunday that he had not seen the video and would watch it before responding.

As of the time of filing this report, the Daura Emirate Council and the Katsina State Government had not issued an official statement on the allegation.

title: PSG’s Doué set for surgery after ACL injury
description:
Paris Saint-Germain forward Désiré Doué is set to undergo surgery later this month after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in his right knee, according to BBC Sport on Sunday.
The 21-year-old suffered the injury during PSG’s 3-2 victory over Nice in Ligue 1 on Saturday night, leaving th
content:
Paris Saint-Germain forward Désiré Doué is set to undergo surgery later this month after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in his right knee, according to BBC Sport on Sunday.

The 21-year-old suffered the injury during PSG’s 3-2 victory over Nice in Ligue 1 on Saturday night, leaving the pitch in tears after being stretchered off towards the end of the first half.

Doué twisted his knee awkwardly without any contact and immediately went down in visible pain.

Play was halted for five minutes as medical staff attended to the France international before he received applause from supporters at the Allianz Riviera Stadium.

The injury represents a major setback for both the player and PSG, with Doué arguably among the club’s best performers this season.

The forward had already missed 13 matches during the 2025-26 campaign due to calf and hamstring problems, making his latest injury another frustrating chapter in an injury-hit season.l

PSG have also been dealing with several fitness concerns, including the absence of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who suffered an ACL injury against Barcelona in October.

Doué’s absence is expected to leave a significant gap in PSG’s attacking options as they continue their pursuit of domestic and European honours.

The European champions are scheduled to return to action on Wednesday when they host Roma in the Champions League, with the team facing another difficult test amid their growing injury concerns.

The post PSG’s Doué set for surgery after ACL injury appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Borno ADC demands whereabouts of detained supporter
description:
…Gubio chairman says he ordered his release, denies ADC’s allegations



By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri



MAIDUGURI — The African Democratic Congress (ADC) Campaign Council in Borno State has demanded the immediate disclosure of the whereabouts of one of its supporters, Alhaji Muktari, whom it alleged
content:
…Gubio chairman says he ordered his release, denies ADC’s allegations

By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri

MAIDUGURI — The African Democratic Congress (ADC) Campaign Council in Borno State has demanded the immediate disclosure of the whereabouts of one of its supporters, Alhaji Muktari, whom it alleged was arrested and detained in Gubio Local Government Area.

However, the Executive Chairman of Gubio Local Government Area, Mali Bulama Mali, has dismissed the allegations, insisting that Muktari had been released and had regained his freedom.

The Director of Communications of the ADC Campaign Council in Borno State, Bukar Bukar Petrol, alleged that Muktari was arrested by security operatives following a directive from the local government chairman over his involvement in grassroots mobilisation for the opposition party ahead of the 2027 general elections.

In a statement issued on Sunday, Petrol alleged that Muktari was arrested on November 21, 2026, at about 10pm by individuals described as repentant Boko Haram members allegedly acting on the instructions of the council chairman.

The party expressed concern that Muktari’s whereabouts were unknown to his family and associates, adding that his wife witnessed the incident.

It also alleged that the arrest and detention were carried out outside recognised police procedures, with no confirmation that he was taken to a police station or formally processed by law enforcement authorities.

The ADC further accused Mali of allegedly empowering repentant Boko Haram members to operate as unofficial security operatives and political foot soldiers in the council.

“The circumstances surrounding the arrest are particularly disturbing. Alhaji Mukhtar is reportedly still being held, while his exact whereabouts remain unknown to the party and his associates. His wife witnessed the incident and can provide an account of the circumstances surrounding his arrest,” the statement said.

The party described the alleged development as an abuse of public office and raised concerns about the possible creation of parallel security structures and unlawful deprivation of citizens’ liberty.

Consequently, the ADC demanded the immediate and unconditional release of Muktari, disclosure of his whereabouts and an independent investigation into the alleged involvement of the council chairman.

It also called for an end to the alleged use of repentant Boko Haram members as unofficial security operatives for intimidation, arrests and detention of citizens.

The party maintained that a local government chairman had no constitutional or statutory authority to establish a personal security outfit or delegate police powers to unofficial individuals.

“The ADC will not accept the use of public office as an instrument of political intimidation, coercion or unlawful detention,” Petrol said.

The party warned that it would escalate the matter to national security, human rights and judicial institutions if the authorities failed to address its concerns.

However, reacting to the allegations on Sunday, Mali denied ordering Muktari’s arrest, insisting that the ADC supporter had been released on his intervention.

The chairman alleged that Muktari, whom he described as a non-indigene of Gubio from Guzamala Local Government Area, was arrested by security authorities over an incident that allegedly caused trouble in the council, and not by repentant Boko Haram members as claimed by the ADC.

He said: “Actually, I was the one who ordered for his release and he, Muktari, has regained his freedom, but I cannot guarantee his safety.”

Mali’s response contradicted the ADC’s claim that its supporter remained in detention and that his whereabouts were unknown.

title: Daura Emirate council probes alleged sexual misconduct involving 92-year-old Emir
description:
The Daura Emirate Council in Katsina State has launched an investigation into a viral video featuring a foreign female tourist who accused the Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, of allegedly touching her inappropriately during a visit to his palace.
The woman, identified as Mirka, who operates the Ins
content:
The Daura Emirate Council in Katsina State has launched an investigation into a viral video featuring a foreign female tourist who accused the Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, of allegedly touching her inappropriately during a visit to his palace.

The woman, identified as Mirka, who operates the Instagram account @beduinqa, shared the video after completing a 30-day tour of different parts of Nigeria.

In her post accompanying the video, Mirka said she had a pleasant experience visiting several locations across the country and interacting with different people. However, she alleged that her visit to Daura in Katsina State was unpleasant due to her encounter at the Emir’s palace.

The Emirate Council said it was investigating the allegations contained in the viral video.

She claimed that during her visit to the emir’s palace, she was taken to a large room where they sat and engaged in a conversation.

According to her, the emir initially held her hand, later hugged her and kissed her on the cheek before allegedly touching her breast without her consent.

Reacting to the allegations, the Sarkin Labaran Daura, Ibrahim Murtala Daura, confirmed that the emirate was aware of the video circulating on social media.

In a telephone interview with Alfijir Radio, he said the emirate was examining the footage to establish its authenticity and determine whether it had been manipulated or artificially generated.

He said, “We are examining the video to ascertain its authenticity and establish that it has not been created or altered using technology.”

He added that the emirate would issue an official statement after concluding its review of the matter.

As of the time of filing this report, the Daura Emirate Council had not issued a detailed statement addressing the allegations, while the Emir of Daura had not personally responded to the claims.

title: 2027: Lagos is a big deal to me  -  Tinubu urges Lagosians to get PVC
description:
President Bola Tinubu has urged Lagos residents to mobilise voters and ensure they collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) ahead of the 2027 elections, declaring that the state remains central to his political ambition.



Tinubu spoke on Sunday at the Yoruba Tennis Club in Onikan, Lagos, during
content:
President Bola Tinubu has urged Lagos residents to mobilise voters and ensure they collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) ahead of the 2027 elections, declaring that the state remains central to his political ambition.

Tinubu spoke on Sunday at the Yoruba Tennis Club in Onikan, Lagos, during a prayer gathering organised by his family ahead of the general elections.

He urged his supporters to reach out to eligible voters in their neighbourhoods and persuade them to participate in the electoral process, warning against complacency.

“The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday. But we cannot take it for granted. You must knock your neighbour’s door. Tell them to go and collect their PVCs,” the President said.

He jokingly told those without voter cards at the gathering that they had come for the food, drawing laughter from attendees.

Tinubu also urged voters to turn out on the scheduled election days, saying their PVCs would give them the opportunity to determine the country’s political direction.

“If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16 and February 6. And that’s what I want to ask you to exercise,” he said.

Describing Lagos as particularly important to his political ambition, the President said the state’s voting strength should translate into greater participation at the polls.

“To me, Lagos is the big deal,” he declared.

Tinubu expressed dissatisfaction with the turnout recorded in previous elections, questioning how a state with millions of registered voters could produce relatively low numbers of votes.

“How can you have seven million registered voters and produce 100,000, 200,000? No. That’s failure. Even if you win and say you win, is it a win? No!” he said.

He further urged residents not to allow disagreements with political leaders to discourage them from voting, saying they could exercise their franchise and still express their grievances afterwards.

Tinubu lost Lagos to Peter Obi of the Labour Party in the 2023 presidential election. Obi secured 575,735 votes against Tinubu’s 573,001, despite Tinubu having governed the state from 1999 to 2007.

title: PHOTOS: Army pulls out 10 retired generals in Bauchi
description:
The Nigerian Army Armoured Corps has formally pulled out 10 retired senior officers from service at a colourful ceremony held at the Brigadier General Y. Abubakar Parade Ground, Headquarters Nigerian Army Armoured Corps, Obienu Barracks, Bauchi.
The ceremony, which took place on Saturday, was the cl
content:
The Nigerian Army Armoured Corps has formally pulled out 10 retired senior officers from service at a colourful ceremony held at the Brigadier General Y. Abubakar Parade Ground, Headquarters Nigerian Army Armoured Corps, Obienu Barracks, Bauchi.

The ceremony, which took place on Saturday, was the climax of the week-long 2026 Nigerian Army Armoured Corps Biennial Conference and Reunion.

The event brought together serving and retired officers of the Corps from across the country to celebrate the distinguished careers and contributions of the retired generals.

According to a statement issued on Sunday by the Acting Deputy Director, Army Public Relations, Headquarters Nigerian Army Armoured Corps, Major Adekunle Akinleye, the officers honoured were Lieutenant General Abdulsalami Ibrahim, Major Generals Benjamin Sawyerr, Ibrahim Ali, Sani Mohammed and Ibrahim Jallo, as well as Brigadier Generals Victor Ita, Tuni Isa, Aminu Usman, Ezra Barkins and Suleiman Adamu.

Speaking at the ceremony as Special Guest of Honour and Reviewing Officer, retired Lieutenant General Abdulsalami Ibrahim described the Armoured Corps as more than just a military formation, saying it had become a way of life for him and other officers who served in the Corps for decades.

“Armour is not only a branch of the Corps, but it is a way of life,” he declared.

He urged serving officers, particularly the younger generation, to uphold the values of courage, discipline and professionalism in the discharge of their responsibilities, stressing that they represented the future of the Corps.

The retired general also expressed appreciation to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, and the Nigerian Army authorities for the confidence reposed in him and his colleagues throughout their military careers.

He further commended everyone who contributed to the successful organisation of the ceremony.

The event was attended by the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, who was represented by the Commander Infantry Corps, Major General Godwin Mutkut.

Other senior officers present included the Commander Armoured Corps, Major General Umar Abubakar; General Officer Commanding 3 Division and Commander Operation Enduring Peace, Major General Maxwell Dangana; Corps Commander Ordnance, Major General Abdullahi Ibrahim; Chief of Personnel Management, Major General Adewale Adekeye; Chief of Special Services and Projects, Major General Aminu Garba; and Commandant Nigerian Army Armour School, Major General Sunday Makolo.

Serving officers, soldiers, family members, friends, well-wishers and members of the barracks community also attended the ceremony to celebrate the retired generals.

Highlights of the event included a ceremonial march past, the traditional pulling-out parade, presentation of souvenirs and group photographs, marking the formal end of the officers’ active military service.

The post PHOTOS: Army pulls out 10 retired generals in Bauchi appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
