title: CJN tasks lawyers to embrace scholarship
description:
…Commends Pinheiro’s 6 law booksBy Innocent Anaba



LAGOS—THE Chief Justice of Nigeria, CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, has commended the contributions of Kemi Pinheiro, SAN, to legal scholarship and professional development, describing six publications presented in his honour as valuable resourc
content:
…Commends Pinheiro’s 6 law books
By Innocent Anaba

LAGOS—THE Chief Justice of Nigeria, CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, has commended the contributions of Kemi Pinheiro, SAN, to legal scholarship and professional development, describing six publications presented in his honour as valuable resources that will enrich Nigerian jurisprudence and strengthen the intellectual foundation of the legal profession.


Kekere-Ekun, who spoke, weekend, while chairing the public presentation of the books in Lagos, said the publications reflected an impressive combination of legal scholarship, practical experience and engagement with contemporary developments in the administration of justice.


She noted that the collection, comprising four books authored by Pinheiro and two compilations produced in his honour, addressed significant areas of legal practice, including litigation, arbitration, insolvency, criminal law, technology and contemporary jurisprudence.


According to her, the publications were not merely a collection of books assembled to commemorate an accomplished legal practitioner but works that sought to make legal knowledge more accessible and useful to those responsible for applying, interpreting and developing the law.


The CJN said: “Taken together, the works reflect an engagement with important areas of legal practice and scholarship, as well as an attempt to preserve the experiences and contributions of a distinguished member of our profession.”


Kekere-Ekun described ‘Defining Moments: Chronicles of a Silk’ as particularly significant because it offered a personal account of the experiences, encounters, challenges and defining moments that had shaped Pinheiro’s career spanning close to four decades at the Bar.
She observed that memoirs of this nature were valuable because they preserved aspects of professional life that might never find their way into law reports or formal institutional records.
Such accounts, she said, enabled younger practitioners to appreciate the human experiences behind professional milestones, including the uncertainties, disappointments and perseverance that often accompanied a successful legal career.
The CJN also highlighted the importance of the two publications on arbitration and insolvency, particularly against the background of Nigeria’s increasingly sophisticated business environment
and the need for effective legal responses to commercial transactions.
, financial distress and dispute resolution.
Similarly, she described Insolvency Law in Nigeria: Practice and Procedure as an important contribution to an increasingly relevant area of law under the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020.
According to her, its examination of corporate rescue, restructuring, administration and other mechanisms for addressing financial distress reflected the growing recognition that preserving viable businesses could, in appropriate circumstances, better serve creditors, employees, investors and the wider economy than immediate liquidation.
On Strategies in Criminal Trials: A Practitioner’s Guide, Kekere-Ekun said the publication would be useful to both experienced practitioners and younger lawyers seeking to strengthen their competence in criminal advocacy.
She noted that criminal litigation required not only sound knowledge of substantive law but also a firm grasp of procedure, evidence and the strategic decisions that arose at different stages of a trial.
She said: “Experience that is not shared may remain a personal achievement. Experience that is documented and transmitted becomes part of the profession’s collective inheritance.”
Earlier, Pinheiro praised the CJN for reforms in the judiciary, particularly the digitisation of the Supreme Court’s operations and the refurbishment of federal courts.
Pinheiro said the four books he authored were products of his practical experiences as an insolvency practitioner, criminal prosecutor and arbitrator, rather than theoretical exercises.
The SAN, who said he would mark 40 years at the Bar in October 2027, explained that the publications represented lessons accumulated over nearly four decades of legal practice and 20 years as a member of the Inner Bar.

The post CJN tasks lawyers to embrace scholarship appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Tinubu approves N1.5tn recapitalisation of Bank of Agriculture
description:
President Bola Tinubu has approved a N1.5tn recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture as part of efforts to expand agricultural financing and improve access to affordable loans for farmers and businesses across the agricultural value chain.
The APC Presidential Campaign Council, in a statement iss
content:
President Bola Tinubu has approved a N1.5tn recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture as part of efforts to expand agricultural financing and improve access to affordable loans for farmers and businesses across the agricultural value chain.

The APC Presidential Campaign Council, in a statement issued on Sunday by its spokesperson and Minister of Solid Minerals, Dele Alake, said the recapitalisation would strengthen the bank’s financial capacity to support farmers, agricultural cooperatives, processors and aggregators.

The APC PCC stated, “President Bola Tinubu’s administration has committed ₦450 billion to agricultural financing programmes to strengthen food security, expand domestic production, and improve the productivity of smallholder farmers across the country, especially in Northern Nigeria.

“Through the Bank of Agriculture, the administration has reached over 500,000 smallholder farmers, and the President has also approved a ₦1.5 trillion recapitalisation to expand agricultural financing and support the cultivation of 500,000 hectares under the Renewed Hope Agenda.

“The Federal Government, under President Tinubu, went beyond providing farmers with loans; it also addressed access to quality seeds, fertiliser, mechanisation, irrigation, storage facilities, commodity markets, and other essential components of the agricultural value chain.

“The interventions demonstrated President Tinubu’s commitment to transforming agriculture into a major driver of economic growth, food security, and job creation.”

It added that the initiative was aimed at expanding the bank’s reach to underserved farming communities and mobilising more resources for domestic food production.

The campaign council further stated, “The ₦450 billion agricultural financing intervention, support for more than 500,000 smallholder farmers, and the planned ₦1.5 trillion recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture represent a significant commitment to building a more productive and resilient agricultural sector.

“Through the Renewed Hope Smallholder Support and Value Chain Fund, with a programme value of ₦250 billion, the Bank of Agriculture is financing farmers through Farmer Aggregation Companies that coordinate farmer registration, input distribution, extension services, and market linkages.

“The programme has already reached more than 500,000 smallholder farmers across 16 states, including over 70,000 women. It has also supported the distribution of approximately 2.5 million bags of fertiliser and 300,000 bags of certified seeds.

“The initiative aims to reach two million farmers and distribute more than 10 million bags of fertiliser.

“The intervention was particularly significant in Northern Nigeria, where agriculture remains a major source of livelihood and economic activity.

“States including Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Niger, Borno, Gombe, Taraba, Adamawa, Yobe, and Bauchi are among the areas receiving attention under the programme.”

The APC Presidential Campaign Council said the Bank of Agriculture had procured about 170,000 metric tonnes of maize, rice, sorghum and cassava under its N200bn Guaranteed Minimum Price Programme to stabilise commodity markets and protect farmers from distress sales.

The council also said the Bank of Agriculture had introduced an Onion Financing Programme in partnership with the National Onion Producers, Processors and Marketers Association of Nigeria, which represents over 11,800 farmers, to boost production and market access.

It said the scheme would provide farmers with improved seeds and fertiliser while supporting processors with funds and solar-powered storage facilities to reduce post-harvest losses.

It added that the bank would cover 70 per cent of farmers’ input costs, while cooperatives would contribute the remaining 30 per cent.

The APC PCC stated, “Other agricultural initiatives the bank is implementing include dry-season farming financing, mechanisation, ginger recovery, women’s cooperative financing, youth participation, and commercial poultry production.

“Under the dry-season agricultural financing programme, the bank is working with the All-Farmers Association of Nigeria to develop a pipeline targeting 400,000 farmers for the 2026 farming cycle.

“The initiative includes financing for 120,000 hectares of wheat cultivation and another 300,000 hectares for crops including rice, maize, sorghum, millet, cassava, and soybeans.

“The Nigeria Ginger Recovery Programme has also supported 3,200 farmers in Kachia, Kaduna State, with blight-free seeds, recovered more than 9,000 bags for multiplication, and is planning an expansion across 20,000 hectares in 16 states.”

The APC PCC said the Bank of Agriculture was targeting 50,000 women nationwide with insured cooperative loans at nine per cent interest.

It added:

“Under the Renewed Hope National Agricultural Mechanisation Programme, 1,571 tractors have been deployed to 23 states.

“The tractors are expected to mechanise 1.2 million hectares of farmland, with access provided to farming communities through qualified Mechanisation Service Providers.

“Other interventions include a ₦385 billion productive-use-of-electricity programme, which provides 44,000 electric cargo tricycles and 100,000 solar irrigation pumps, targeting 500,000 farming families.”

Ahead of the January 16, 2027, presidential election, President Bola Tinubu is seeking re-election on the platform of the APC.

In preparation for the poll, the APC Presidential Campaign Council has continued to highlight the achievements of the Tinubu administration across various sectors.

The post Tinubu approves N1.5tn recapitalisation of Bank of Agriculture appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Five children killed, one injured in Syria landmine blast
description:
A landmine explosion killed five children and wounded one other in northwest Syria, state media reported on Sunday.
State TV said the blast was caused by a mine “left behind” during the rule of toppled president Bashar al-Assad’s government and occurred in the village of Um Khuzaym in the countrysid
content:
A landmine explosion killed five children and wounded one other in northwest Syria, state media reported on Sunday.

State TV said the blast was caused by a mine “left behind” during the rule of toppled president Bashar al-Assad’s government and occurred in the village of Um Khuzaym in the countryside of Idlib province.

Landmines and unexploded ordnance remain scattered across Syria after more than 13 years of civil war, during which different sides planted mines in parts of the country.

Between the fall of Assad in December 2024 and early September this year, a Syria-wide coordination mechanism led by the UN Mine Action Service recorded 1,337 explosive ordnance incidents, which killed or injured 2,375 people, including more than 850 children.

Simon Jackson, Syria programme manager for NGO HALO Trust, told AFP in September that landmines and unexploded war remnants were causing around one death or injury every six hours.

Syria recorded the world’s highest number of mine and explosive-remnant casualties last year, with 1,600 people killed or wounded, according to a preliminary report published in June by the Landmine and Cluster Munition Monitor.

title: Oyo APM to Tinubu: Nigerians need better living conditions, not name-calling
description:
IBADAN—THE Allied Peoples’ Movement, APM, in Oyo State, yesterday, tackled President Bola Tinubu for purportedly attacking the party during the All Progressives Congress rally held at Mapo Hall, in Ibadan.



Tinubu, who was in Ibadan on Saturday, took a swipe at the APM and Governor Seyi Makinde.
content:
IBADAN—THE Allied Peoples’ Movement, APM, in Oyo State, yesterday, tackled President Bola Tinubu for purportedly attacking the party during the All Progressives Congress rally held at Mapo Hall, in Ibadan.


Tinubu, who was in Ibadan on Saturday, took a swipe at the APM and Governor Seyi Makinde.


He said: “We heard there is a certain group/faction called the ‘palẹmọ’ (Pack up) group. Don’t mind them; they are only waiting in vain; there is nowhere they are going.”


However, the APM described the president’s remark as desperate distractions from the mounting realities confronting Nigerians and the glaring failures of governance.
The party, in a statement by its Director of Communication/Spokesperson Campaign Council, Yinka Oladoyinbo, said: “We consider the expression a curious choice of words from a President whose administration has become synonymous with economic hardship, public frustration, political manoeuvring and an increasingly desperate search for electoral validation.
“In Yoruba political parlance, ‘palẹmọ’ evokes the hurried gathering, packing or clearing away of belongings, sometimes suggestive of preparing to leave or carrying away what one can before departure.
“Mr President may wish to explain why such vocabulary comes so readily to him. As the saying goes, it takes a master of a craft to recognise the language of fellow practitioners. And when an accuser points one finger at another, the remaining four are invariably directed at himself.
“The APM will not be distracted by presidential name-calling. Nigerians are far more concerned about the cost of living, the purchasing power of their incomes, insecurity, unemployment, collapsing economic confidence and the daily struggle to survive than the linguistic theatrics of a campaign podium.”
The party also warned that traditional rulers, irrespective of their political affiliations, remain ”fathers to all.”
“The APM remains confident that Oyo voters will distinguish between political noise and credible leadership, between borrowed prestige and earned trust, and between the spectacle of power and the substance of governance,” the statement said.

The post Oyo APM to Tinubu: Nigerians need better living conditions, not name-calling appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: VIDEO: A’Ibom gov appoints volunteer cleaner as PA
description:
Akwa Ibom State Governor Umo Eno has appointed a long-serving volunteer at the Government House in Uyo, Edwin James, as his Personal Assistant, after voluntarily cleaning the Latter House Chapel for nearly four years
The governor also directed the Secretary to the State Government to make James’ app
content:
Akwa Ibom State Governor Umo Eno has appointed a long-serving volunteer at the Government House in Uyo, Edwin James, as his Personal Assistant, after voluntarily cleaning the Latter House Chapel for nearly four years

The governor also directed the Secretary to the State Government to make James’ appointment effective from June 1, 2023, as recognition of his years of dedicated and selfless service, saying, “We have been owing him.”

Eno disclosed this while addressing worshippers during the monthly Government House prayer service held at the chapel on Sunday.

Eno also stated that his administration has paid approximately ₦102 billion of the inherited ₦111 billion gratuity backlog, while pensions and educational bursaries continue to receive attention.

In a video shared on the Akwa Ibom State Government’s Facebook page, James was seen approaching the governor before he received the news of his appointment.

While the governor was giving his speech, lauding James for his dedication and selfless service to the chapel and the state, James could be seen feeling emotional as his eyes became teary.

“This man, unfortunately, to this day, he has not been given an appointment. He has been doing this work voluntarily, cleaning this place. How come we have not remembered him? How come he has not been given an appointment? For almost four years?

“These are things to remind somebody about. It would have been bad if this government could finish, and this man has been serving God here, serving the state, cleaning and keeping, and we forget him; even God won’t be happy, but it’s not deliberate; honestly, these things have to be brought.

“So, please, SSG, on Monday morning, confirm his appointment as my PA, but backdate it to 1st of June 2023; that’s when he started working. So the state government has been owing him; let us pay.”

Eno prayed for the progress of the state, saying, “We will never go backwards. God will keep bringing leaders that will keep taking us forward.”

After the announcement, some members of the congregation congratulated James on his new appointment amid cheers and joyful screams from the crowd.

In a post on his LinkedIn account, the governor revealed that, beginning in June 2027, his administration would pay ₦200,000 each as bursaries to students studying general courses, while those pursuing professional courses such as Medicine, Law, Architecture, ICT and Pharmacy will receive ₦250,000 each.

He wrote, “Building a better Akwa Ibom State requires consistent investment in people, education and the welfare of those who have served our State. Today, at our monthly Government House Prayer Service in Uyo, I reflected on our administration’s progress, our commitment to the wellbeing of our people and our political priorities ahead of the 2027 general elections.

“Our administration has so far paid ₦102 billion out of the ₦111 billion inherited gratuities backlog, demonstrating our commitment to honouring the contributions of our retired public servants. In education, we have progressively increased student bursaries from ₦10,000 to ₦20,000 and subsequently to ₦50,000.

“Beginning in June 2027, students studying general courses will receive ₦200,000 each, while those pursuing professional courses such as Medicine, Law, Architecture, ICT and Pharmacy will receive ₦250,000 each.

“These investments reflect our conviction that no Akwa Ibom child should be denied access to education and the skills needed to succeed because of the circumstances of their birth.”

He also announced James’s appointment, saying, “I also announced the appointment of Mr Edwin James, who has faithfully served as a cleaner at the Latter House Chapel for several years, as my Personal Assistant, with effect from June 2023.

“His story reminds us that dedication, humility and faithful service deserve recognition, regardless of one’s position in society.

“As we continue implementing the ARISE Agenda, our focus remains on building an inclusive State where opportunities are accessible, service is valued, and every citizen has a chance to succeed.”

The governor encouraged residents to obtain their permanent voter cards and campaign in their wards ahead of the forthcoming 2027 general elections.

title: PDP urges FG to tackle recurring boat accidents
description:
The Peoples Democratic Party has called on the Federal Government to take urgent steps to address the recurring boat accidents across the country, following the tragic incident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, which claimed at least 24 lives.
The party condemned what it descr
content:
The Peoples Democratic Party has called on the Federal Government to take urgent steps to address the recurring boat accidents across the country, following the tragic incident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, which claimed at least 24 lives.

The party condemned what it described as the government’s failure to address the persistent safety challenges on Nigeria’s waterways, including overloading of passenger boats, poor maintenance, lack of life jackets and weak enforcement of maritime safety regulations.

In a press statement issued on Sunday and signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Ini Ememobong, the PDP said Nigerians needed decisive action rather than routine condolence messages from the All Progressives Congress-led Federal Government.

It described the recurring boat accidents as evidence of government neglect of the maritime transportation sector.

The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, when a passenger boat conveying mourners from Ayama to a burial ceremony in Ukubie capsized near the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities in Bayelsa State.

According to the statement, the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) confirmed at least 24 fatalities, while search-and-rescue operations continued for those still missing.

Eyewitness accounts reportedly put the number of passengers on board at approximately 300.

Expressing sympathy with the bereaved families, the PDP said, “We extend our heartfelt condolences to the families who lost loved ones on a journey meant to honour the dead. We pray for the quick recovery of the survivors receiving treatment in Ayama and Yenagoa.”

The party also commended divers, marine police officers and community members involved in the rescue operations, noting that they had risked their lives in efforts to save victims.

However, the PDP argued that the tragedy was not an isolated incident but part of a disturbing pattern of boat accidents across Nigeria, insisting that the Federal Government must move beyond issuing condolence messages and address the underlying causes.

“For a country with 853 km of coastline and a vast network of inland waterways, maritime transport deserves far more attention than this government is giving it,” the statement said.

The opposition party maintained that Nigeria needed effective maritime safety laws and properly equipped enforcement agencies to prevent further loss of lives.

It specifically urged the Federal Government to accelerate the passage of a coast guard law, beginning with the reconsideration of the Nigeria Coast Guard (Establishment) Bill, 2026 (SB. 575), which the Senate stepped down on July 22, 2026, for wider consultations.

The PDP argued that the government should demonstrate the same urgency it showed in the passage of the state police bill in addressing maritime security and safety concerns.

It further called for adequate funding of the Marine Police and the Nigerian Navy to enable them to deploy personnel, boats and other necessary equipment for effective enforcement of safety regulations on the waterways.

The party also urged the government to direct the National Inland Waterways Authority (NIWA) to collaborate with relevant agencies in enforcing passenger limits, conducting regular boat inspections and ensuring compulsory use of life jackets.

Additionally, it demanded a transparent investigation into the Bayelsa boat accident, insisting that the findings should be made public.

” Nigerians deserve a more responsive and responsible government than the one they have now,” the statement declared.

The PDP concluded by calling on Nigerians to make their voices count in the political process, noting that January 16, 2027, would provide an opportunity for citizens to make a choice about the kind of leadership they want.

The post PDP urges FG to tackle recurring boat accidents appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Subsidy Removal: You can’t wish away Nigerians’ hardship, ADC-PCC tells Tinubu
description:
By Luminous Jannamike



ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has tackled President Bola Tinubu over his insistence that Nigerians should forget fuel subsidy, accusing him of being insensitive to the economic hardship confronting millions of citizens.



Th
content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has tackled President Bola Tinubu over his insistence that Nigerians should forget fuel subsidy, accusing him of being insensitive to the economic hardship confronting millions of citizens.

The Council said the President’s remarks exposed his disconnect from Nigerians struggling with rising food prices, soaring transportation costs, poverty and an increasingly unbearable cost of living.

In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC was reacting to Tinubu’s declaration at a rally at Mapo Hall, Ibadan, Oyo State, that fuel subsidy belonged to the country’s past. Ologbondiyan spoke during an interaction with youths in Lokoja, ahead of the Council’s presidential campaign rally in Kogi State.

“The President appears more interested in being addressed as Mr President than in tackling the crushing realities confronting the people. He has demonstrated little or no concern for the suffering of ordinary Nigerians.

“That explains his brash insistence that Nigerians should forget about fuel subsidy removal simply because, in his estimation, it belongs to the past,” he said.

Questioning how the consequences of the policy could be dismissed when Nigerians continued to bear its effects, Ologbondiyan asked: “How can hardship, hunger and widespread poverty, which are direct consequences of the hurriedly imposed economic policies of the Tinubu administration, suddenly become things of the past when Nigerians continue to bear their devastating consequences every day?”

The Council argued that subsidy removal was announced without adequate preparation, effective safety nets or meaningful measures to cushion its impact on vulnerable citizens.

It said the policy had contributed to soaring transportation costs, unaffordable food prices, struggling small businesses and worsening poverty among households.

“To ask Nigerians to forget a policy whose consequences they confront every waking moment is not only insensitive; it is an insult to their intelligence and a mockery of their suffering,” Ologbondiyan added.

The ADC-PCC maintained that responsible leadership required acknowledging policy failures and making necessary adjustments to ease citizens’ hardship, rather than defending policies despite their consequences.

Beyond the economic crisis, the Council accused the Tinubu administration of weakening critical democratic institutions, including the judiciary, security agencies, anti-corruption bodies and financial institutions, allegedly to advance the President’s second-term ambition.

It warned that institutions established to safeguard democracy and protect the public interest must not be subordinated to the political ambitions of any individual.

“Nigeria cannot afford a second term built on the ruins of its democratic institutions and the continued impoverishment of its citizens,” the Council declared.

Describing the country’s economic difficulties as the consequence of poor policy choices, inadequate planning and a failure to prioritise citizens’ welfare, the ADC-PCC insisted that the situation was neither inevitable nor beyond remedy.

It endorsed its presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, as the leader capable of reversing the economic decline, restoring investor confidence and rebuilding democratic institutions.

The Council said an Atiku-led administration would pursue properly planned economic policies, effective social protection mechanisms and a more humane approach to governance.

It urged Nigerians to use lawful and democratic means to reject Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, arguing that the coming election offered an opportunity to change the country’s direction.

“Nigerians deserve a government that feels their pain, understands their struggles and takes deliberate steps to ease their burden, not one that dismisses their suffering or asks them to forget the circumstances that have made life increasingly unbearable.

“In 2027, Nigerians will have the opportunity to change this narrative. The power to rescue the country and restore hope rests firmly in their hands,” the ADC-PCC said.

The post Subsidy Removal: You can’t wish away Nigerians’ hardship, ADC-PCC tells Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Borno mourns eight soldiers, 13 workers killed during reconstruction
description:
The Borno State Government has mourned eight soldiers, including a major, and 13 construction workers killed while working in Mayanti, a displaced community in Bama Local Government Area of the state.
Speaking on Saturday at the inauguration of 500 housing units, 2,000 semi-permanent shelters and a
content:
The Borno State Government has mourned eight soldiers, including a major, and 13 construction workers killed while working in Mayanti, a displaced community in Bama Local Government Area of the state.

Speaking on Saturday at the inauguration of 500 housing units, 2,000 semi-permanent shelters and a school building for the Mayanti community, whose residents were displaced years ago, the state Commissioner for Education, Science, Technology and Innovation, Abba Wakilbe, who also chairs the community’s resettlement committee, said a total of 21 people were killed during construction work at the site over the past year.

The commissioner said construction of the project began in August 2025 and was completed in October 2026.

“This project commenced exactly in August 2025 and it was completed in October, 2026. Before inviting you (Governor Zulum) to commission this project, let me pay a special tribute to those who have fallen in the cause of this work, starting with Major Mairiga and seven soldiers with thirteen construction workers who lost their lives in the cause of the one year of this project. We pray that Allah grant them Jannah,” Wakilbe said.

Also speaking, the Borno State Governor, Babagana Zulum, commended the community’s resettlement committee for its resilience, saying the construction process had witnessed four to five attacks by insurgents.

“For those that have participated fully in this exercise, beginning from the Chairman, Engineer Abba Wakilbe and other very important members of the committee, from the button of my heart, I want to convey my sincere appreciation for all of you.”

“It is not easy to work here, I can recall that Mayanti was attacked several times during the construction exercise, at least, not fewer than four, five times. Despite those threats, they were resilience and today, we have seen the completion of the project. It is my singular honour to commission this 500 houses with 2,000 permanent semi-shelter here in Mayanti community, Borno state to the glory of God,” Zulum said.

Zulum also commended residents for returning to the community and assured them of continued security and support to rebuild their livelihoods.

“Reconstruction, resettlement and rehabilitation are the fulcrum of this administration. So far, we have resettled many communities, and I am happy that Mayanti is back on track,” he said.

Meanwhile, shortly after the inauguration, the governor proceeded to Bama town, where he participated in a campaign rally and urged residents of the local government area to re-elect President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to sustain security gains and keep development projects on track.

The post Borno mourns eight soldiers, 13 workers killed during reconstruction appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Water stopped while I was shaving in Aso Rock – Tinubu
description:
President Bola Tinubu on Sunday revealed that the Presidential Villa in Abuja suffers from the same electricity and water supply failures that plague ordinary Nigerians.
He revealed that the water went off while he was shaving earlier in the week and vowed to fix the country’s infrastructure deficit
content:
President Bola Tinubu on Sunday revealed that the Presidential Villa in Abuja suffers from the same electricity and water supply failures that plague ordinary Nigerians.

He revealed that the water went off while he was shaving earlier in the week and vowed to fix the country’s infrastructure deficit.

Tinubu made the disclosure on Sunday at a special prayer session organised in his honour by members of his family in Lagos.

The meeting followed his attendance at the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, on Saturday.

He explained, “On the Wednesday of last week, I was shaving, and the water went off. And the villa, you won’t know punishment there too.

“The water went off. So we will correct all this. No light, no water, no electricity, no development.

“We have just started. We can do it, and we will do it for Nigeria.”

The President also rallied supporters ahead of the 2027 general elections, charging them to maximise voter turnout in Lagos and urging warring factions within his political camp to reconcile.

“To me, Lagos is the big deal. How can you have seven million registered voters and produce 100,000, 200,000? That’s failure. Even if you win, I say a win is a win. No. You have to generate the maximum,” he said.

He directed supporters to canvass their neighbours for Permanent Voter Cards and to channel grievances into electoral participation rather than internal conflict.

According to him, “It’s not anger. Anger will not do it. You are angry with Sylva, or you’re angry with Mulika, call Mulika and let her go vote. We finish the anger that day; you go back. We must generate enough votes to overwhelm them.”

Tinubu also ordered one of his associates in attendance, described as his “confidant and bulldozer”, to return home and broker reconciliation within the party’s ranks before moving on to other states.

He ordered, “Go back home and reconcile with everybody. That is the order of the president. Go back home and reconcile with everybody. And when you finish that, you move to Jigawa, you move to other places and reconcile them. Beg them.”

Drawing on his own experience, the President said he had set aside deep personal grievances during the 2023 campaign in order to pursue a broader goal.

“I had my own anger in 2021–22. When he called me, I said, okay, you are co-chairman of the campaign. I had my own anger, full of hot feelings, but I let go. Today, that is free,” he said, adding that the spirit of forgiveness was inseparable from seeking it.

Tinubu noted that “If you cannot give it, why are you asking Allah to give you forgiveness? What you want from him, you must be able to give to humanity.”

The President credited divine support and family loyalty for his journey from governorship to the presidency, tracing a line of prayer and perseverance through each contest.

“First time, prayer. Second time, prayer. We did that. We won. After that, presidency, prayer, vision, mission, everything,” he said.

To the younger generation at the meeting, President Tinubu said the 2027 election was theirs to win or lose.

“The challenge is yours now. It’s in your hands to knock on doors, get all the PVC out, and do what is right.

“You are the leaders that we take over. We paved the way for you. But it’s left in your hands to do the great things that Nigeria expects,” he said.

Several governors attended the prayer session, including the Lagos, Kwara, Imo, Gombe and Kaduna state governors.

The post Water stopped while I was shaving in Aso Rock – Tinubu appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
By Esther Onyegbula

THE Lagos State Police Command has arrested a 34-year-old man, Adams Victor, over alleged vehicle theft and recovered two suspected stolen vehicles in Ibadan, Oyo State.

The arrest followed an investigation into a vehicle theft case reported in May 2026, which led police operatives to Ibadan, where the suspect was apprehended and the vehicles recovered.

The vehicles are a 2008 Toyota Corolla with registration number EPE 594 KR and a 1999 Toyota Sienna with registration number AGL 632 KU.

The Command said preliminary investigations revealed that the suspect had previously been convicted of offences relating to criminal activities.

In a statement on Sunday, November 22, 2026, the Police Public Relations Officer, SP Abimbola Adebisi, said the operation demonstrated the Command’s commitment to tracking down criminals and recovering stolen property, even beyond Lagos State.

The Commissioner of Police, CP Tijani Fatai, commended the operatives for their diligence and determination, assuring residents that the Command would sustain efforts to dismantle criminal networks and bring perpetrators to justice.
He urged members of the public to report suspicious activities and provide useful information to the police.
The Command provided the following emergency lines for reporting suspicious activities: 07061019374, 08065154338, 08063299264, 08039344870, 08080193432 (Marine) and 09168630929.

title: INEC under Amupitan has worst voter data, compromised register could jeopardise 2027 election – Rep Dasuki
description:
Says shrinking political space, rising violence are dangerous implications of tinubu’s ‘all is fair in politics’


Deputy Minority Leader of the House of Representatives, Rep. Abdussamad Dasuki, has raised the alarm over what he described as the poor state of the Independent National Electoral Commi
content:
• Says shrinking political space, rising violence are dangerous implications of tinubu’s ‘all is fair in politics’

Deputy Minority Leader of the House of Representatives, Rep. Abdussamad Dasuki, has raised the alarm over what he described as the poor state of the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) voter data under its chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, warning that a compromised voters’ register could jeopardise the electoral process and put the credibility of the 2027 general elections in peril.

Dasuki also noted that the shrinking political space and rising violence against opposition parties, could jeopardise the credibility of the 2027 general elections.

The lawmaker warned that a compromised voters’ register could undermine the electoral process and erode public confidence in the outcome of the next general elections.

Rep Dasuki spoke while addressing supporters of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar in Lagos at the weekend.

“INEC has not provided the assurance to Nigerians that the final register that would be used for next year’s election would be credible. This should worry all Nigerians,” he said.

He warned that the credibility of the 2027 elections could be seriously undermined if the commission failed to address concerns surrounding the integrity of its voter database before the final register is certified.

His concerns come against the backdrop of recent revelations by INEC that some of its registration officials abused their official access to create fraudulent voter records, including profiles containing fake photographs and manipulated biometric details.

Concern over the integrity of the database, however, intensified after INEC announced that it had removed 1,609,553 records from the voters’ register following a technical assessment.

The development has raised fresh questions about the effectiveness of the commission’s voter registration safeguards, the reliability of its database and whether adequate measures are being taken to prevent fraudulent records from finding their way into the final register.

INEC has, however, maintained that it remains committed to completing the necessary verification, adjudication and data-cleanup processes ahead of the scheduled certification of the final register of voters on December 15, 2026.

Dasuki disclosed that Amupitan would appear before the House committee this week, where he would be questioned on the growing concerns among Nigerians over the credibility of INEC’s voter data.

According to him, the INEC chairman would be expected to provide explanations on the circumstances surrounding the discovery of fraudulent voter records, the removal of over 1.6 million entries and the safeguards being put in place to ensure that the final register is reliable.

Beyond the concerns over voter data, Dasuki also warned that the shrinking political space and increasing violence against opposition parties and their supporters were dangerous implications of President Bola Tinubu’s “All is fair in politics” remark ahead of the 2027 elections.

He called on the President to retract the statement and publicly condemn actions threatening democratic participation, warning that the growing atmosphere of political intolerance could undermine the country’s democratic institutions and electoral process.

The lawmaker expressed concern over what he described as increasing attempts to restrict opposition parties’ access to public facilities, impose prohibitive fees on campaign billboards, instigate internal crises within opposition parties and intimidate political candidates and their supporters.

He said the political environment was becoming increasingly tense as the country approached the 2027 elections, adding that the President’s remark risked emboldening political actors who might interpret it as a justification for actions inconsistent with democratic principles.

“Although the President may have intended his remarks as an expression of determination to defend his political position, such language, coming from the nation’s highest political office, risks sending the wrong signal to political actors, particularly those who may interpret it as an endorsement of a politics without restraint,” he said.

Dasuki maintained that political competition must be guided by constitutional provisions, respect for human rights and the rule of law.

“In a democracy, not everything is fair in politics. Political competition must operate within the boundaries of the Constitution, the rule of law, respect for human rights and the fundamental principles of democratic engagement,” he stated.

Citing developments across the country, the lawmaker pointed to the controversy surrounding the African Democratic Congress’ presidential campaign flag-off in Sokoto State, where the opposition party accused the state government of denying it access to public facilities traditionally used for political activities.

He also referenced the attack on Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters during a town hall meeting at the Classique Event Centre in Oregun, Lagos State, where suspected political thugs invaded the venue in an attempt to disrupt the gathering.

The lawmaker further cited the reported attack on the Benin City residence of former Edo State Governor, Chief John Odigie-Oyegun, during a political meeting attended by prominent opposition figures, including Peter Obi and Olumide Akpata.

On the financial restrictions facing opposition campaigns, Dasuki expressed concern over reports of exorbitant billboard permit fees in some states, arguing that such charges could create barriers to equal political participation.

He said the combination of restrictions on political activities, attacks on supporters and administrative measures that make campaigning difficult could weaken opposition parties and undermine the electorate’s ability to freely make political choices.

The lawmaker also expressed concern over the use of conflicting judicial pronouncements and prolonged legal disputes in ways that could leave opposition parties distracted and weakened, stressing that the independence of the judiciary must be protected from political interference.

The post INEC under Amupitan has worst voter data, compromised register could jeopardise 2027 election – Rep Dasuki appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: A phone call in Ojuelegba took his art to America
description: Some people trace their big break to a mentor, a lucky meeting or a relative abroad. In this case, Dr. Bolaji Ogunwo traces his to a phone number, written and handed to him in Ojuelegba. That single call set the young graduate teacher on a road that has taken his paintings to California, Houston and
content:
Some people trace their big break to a mentor, a lucky meeting or a relative abroad. In this case, Dr. Bolaji Ogunwo traces his to a phone number, written and handed to him in Ojuelegba. That single call set the young graduate teacher on a road that has taken his paintings to California, Houston and Chicago, he revealed on The Morayo Show

The story started during his National Youth Service at the Federal College of Education, Akoka, where he taught. One of his students came back from an outing in Ojuelegba with interesting news: he had met a collector “someone who buys art,” as Dr. Bolaji explained and had brought back the man’s number, telling his teacher, “if you don’t mind, you can call him.” He called, went to see the man, and left with something even better than he had hoped for, an introduction to a second collector, a bigger one.

There is a detail in the story that still makes him smile every time, he said. The collector’s number began with 0803, the same way his wife’s number began on the evening she gave it to him. “Today, by God’s grace, I do shows in California, in Houston, Chicago,” he said, while also crediting MTN with powering that journey through numerous opportunities.

And the journey has not slowed down. He spent six months, from January to July this year, as a visiting professor at Missouri State University in Springfield, Missouri. Even then, he said, he and his wife, Mrs Funmilayo who runs a drinks and cocktail events company back in Nigeria, spoke every single day.

Three decades of studio practice, more than 60 exhibitions at home and abroad have followed that first meeting with a collector. And through it all, the phone has never been far from his hand

title: EPL: Pochettino’s Man Utd suffer heavy 4-0 defeat to Liverpool
description:
Mauricio Pochettino endured a disastrous start to life as Manchester United manager after Liverpool thrashed the Red Devils 4-0 at Anfield.
Liverpool took control of the encounter within the opening 13 minutes, scoring twice against a 10-man United side to secure a convincing victory.
United’s hopes
content:
Mauricio Pochettino endured a disastrous start to life as Manchester United manager after Liverpool thrashed the Red Devils 4-0 at Anfield.

Liverpool took control of the encounter within the opening 13 minutes, scoring twice against a 10-man United side to secure a convincing victory.

United’s hopes of getting a positive result suffered a major setback after Leny Yoro was controversially sent off just eight minutes into the match. Liverpool quickly capitalised on their numerical advantage, with Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz finding the back of the net.

The visitors struggled to recover from the early setback as Liverpool continued to dominate proceedings.

Teenager Rio Ngumoha produced a stunning individual effort to score the hosts’ third goal, before Victor Munoz added another to complete the 4-0 demolition of Manchester United.

Defeat leaves United still rooted second bottom of the Premier League and gave Pochettino an early indication of the huge job he has ahead to restore the 20-time English champions to their former glories.

Liverpool climb into the top four and within seven points of leaders Arsenal to rekindle faint hopes of challenging for the title.

Pochettino answered United’s call after Michael Carrick was sacked last week after winning just one of the Red Devils’ first 10 league games in charge.

The Argentine has been linked with a move to Old Trafford for a decade, but failed to make a strong first impression on the United fans.

Pochettino’s bold team selection backfired with the centre-back pairing of Matthijs de Ligt and Yoro at fault for the game’s decisive moment.

De Ligt, on his first Premier League start for nearly a year, let a long ball down the middle and go and allowed Alexander Isak to bear down on goal.

The Swedish striker took a heavy touch before he was clipped by Yoro, but referee Sam Barrott still deemed the French defender had denied a clear goalscoring opportunity and produced a red card.

Szoboszlai rubbed salt into United wounds by drilling home the resulting free-kick from the edge of the box.

Moments later Ngumoha skipped past Diogo Dalot and crossed for Wirtz to hook a shot in off the underside of the bar.

Having relegated Harry Maguire to the bench, Pochettino was forced to turn to the veteran centre-back just 22 minutes in to try and stem the bleeding.

United lost 7-0 at Anfield three years ago and a switch to a back five helped avoid similar damage, albeit with the help of some wayward Liverpool finishing.

Maguire made a brilliant block to deny Isak a third goal just before half-time.

Bradley Barcola and Isak were guilty of wasting huge chances early in the second half.

But Barcola’s blistering pace created Liverpool’s third just after the hour mark.

The French international destroyed Lisandro Martinez for pace before picking out Ngumoha to slot home.

Wirtz rounded off one of his best Liverpool displays since a £100 million move from Bayer Leverkusen last year with the assist for Munoz to crash home the fourth goal eight minutes from time.

Liverpool fans rejoiced in their rivals’ pain with chants of “you are going down”.

United have not been relegated since 1974 but find themselves in a battle for survival despite still enjoying one of the biggest revenues in world football.

The 34 goals they have conceded in all competitions is the worst defensive record of any team in Europe’s top five leagues this season.

The post EPL: Pochettino’s Man Utd suffer heavy 4-0 defeat to Liverpool appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Horror in Calabar: Driver runs over Nursing student twice, flees
description:
By Emma Una



CALABAR—A nursing student of the School of Nursing, Mary Slessor Avenue, Calabar, identified as Cynthia Eni, has been killed after a speeding driver reportedly knocked her down and reversed to run over her a second time before fleeing the scene.



The incident, which occurred at the
content:
By Emma Una

CALABAR—A nursing student of the School of Nursing, Mary Slessor Avenue, Calabar, identified as Cynthia Eni, has been killed after a speeding driver reportedly knocked her down and reversed to run over her a second time before fleeing the scene.

The incident, which occurred at the weekend, happened as Cynthia was crossing the road into the school compound after going out with two colleagues to buy some items.

A friend of the deceased, Mercy, who witnessed the incident, said the driver first knocked Cynthia down before reversing and running over her again as people attempted to come to her rescue.

“It was a bewildering scene. When the car knocked her down, we were shouting for help and before some boys could rush down, the same car returned and climbed her again. When the car was approaching we thought the driver had come to help but was surprised when the car ran over her again.”

Mercy said the driver took advantage of the fading light and the fact that people were focused on the victim to escape, adding that the vehicle’s registration number was not visible.

She said Cynthia, who was about 30, had completed her Community Health studies at the College of Health Technology and enrolled at the School of Nursing to obtain an additional qualification.

“We don’t know what was in the driver’s mind. Even if he was drunk or had some issues with Cynthia, he should have had some sense of humanity and not come back to crush her the way he did.”
Mercy said she could not recall any misunderstanding between the deceased and fellow students or outsiders.
“We leave everything to God,” she said, breaking down in tears.
There was no official at the Provost’s Office available to comment on the incident as it occurred at the weekend.

title: Suspected gunmen set govt secondary school ablaze in Plateau
description:
Suspected gunmen have reportedly set fire to Government Secondary School, Masharkut, in Butura District of Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State.
The incident, which occurred on Sunday afternoon, caused panic among residents after smoke was seen rising from the school premises shortly after
content:
Suspected gunmen have reportedly set fire to Government Secondary School, Masharkut, in Butura District of Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State.

The incident, which occurred on Sunday afternoon, caused panic among residents after smoke was seen rising from the school premises shortly after church service.

A community member, Daniel Bwehfa Makodeng, who brought the incident to the attention of journalists, disclosed that the school was set ablaze at about 1pm.

“Suspected bandits set the school on fire around 1pm,” he said.

He explained that residents initially noticed smoke coming from the school before discovering about 30 minutes later that the building was on fire.

The Chairman of Bokkos Local Government Area, Hon. Amalau Amalau, also confirmed the incident, saying the council had received reports that the school was engulfed in flames.

Speaking in a telephone interview, Amalau said the circumstances surrounding the fire and the identities of those responsible had yet to be established.

“We only saw the school in flames. We cannot ascertain at the moment who was responsible or whether it was carried out by terrorists,” he said.

The chairman confirmed that the incident occurred on Sunday, adding that the immediate concern was the destruction of the school building.

Efforts to reach security operatives for confirmation and comments were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report.

title: 2027: Lagos is a big deal to me – Tinubu
description:
President Bola Tinubu has urged Lagos residents to mobilise voters and collect their Permanent Voter Cards ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring that the state is a “big deal” to him.
Tinubu made the call on Sunday while addressing guests at the Yoruba Tennis Club in Onikan, Lagos, during a
content:
President Bola Tinubu has urged Lagos residents to mobilise voters and collect their Permanent Voter Cards ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring that the state is a “big deal” to him.

Tinubu made the call on Sunday while addressing guests at the Yoruba Tennis Club in Onikan, Lagos, during a special prayer session organised by members of his family ahead of the elections.

The President urged residents to encourage their neighbours to collect their PVCs, stressing that voter turnout in Lagos should reflect the state’s large number of registered voters.

“The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday. But we cannot take it for granted. You must knock your neighbour’s door. Tell them to go and collect their PVCs,” he said.

He added jokingly, “If you are here and you don’t have PVC, you are here for Amala.”

Tinubu urged eligible voters to exercise their franchise on the scheduled election dates, saying, “If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16 and February 6. And that’s what I want to ask you to exercise.”

Emphasising the importance of Lagos to his political ambition, he declared, “To me, Lagos is the big deal.”

He questioned the low voter turnout recorded in the state during previous elections, despite its large voter population.

“How can you have seven million registered voters and produce 100,000, 200,000? No. That’s failure. Even if you win and say you win, is it a win? No!” he said.

The President also urged residents to set aside anger and political disagreements and participate in the elections.

“You are angry with Silifa or you are angry with Mulika, Call Mulika and go vote. If you finish voting and still angry, you go back,” he said, drawing laughter from the audience.

In the 2023 presidential election, Tinubu lost Lagos to the Labour Party’s Peter Obi, despite having governed the state from 1999 to 2007.

Obi polled 575,735 votes to defeat Tinubu, who secured 573,001 votes.

The presidential candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party, Atiku Abubakar, had a total of 75,750 votes, while the presidential candidate of the New Nigeria People’s Party, Rabiu Kwankwaso, had a total of 8,8442 votes.

Although Tinubu won 11 of Lagos’s 20 local government areas, Obi secured victory in nine, giving him the overall state result.

Lagos had 7,060,195 registered voters at the time, but only 1,357,152 voters were accredited for the election.

The prayer session was organised by Tinubu’s family ahead of the 2027 general elections, with the master of ceremonies announcing that it was for the President’s re-election.

The Independent National Electoral Commission has fixed January 16, 2027, for the presidential and National Assembly elections, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections are scheduled for February 6, 2027.

title: New Manager, Same Problems, Liverpool Thrash 10-Man Man Utd In Pochettino’s First Match
description: Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare start as Manchester United manager after Liverpool struck twice inside the first 13 minutes against 10 men to set up a 4-0 win at Anfield.United never recovered from Leny Yoro’s controversial red card after just eight minutes as Dominik Szoboszlai and Fl
content:
Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare start as Manchester United manager after Liverpool struck twice inside the first 13 minutes against 10 men to set up a 4-0 win at Anfield.

United never recovered from Leny Yoro’s controversial red card after just eight minutes as Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz quickly made Liverpool’s man advantage count.

Teenager Rio Ngumoha rounded off a stunning individual with Liverpool’s third before Victor Munoz completed the rout.

Defeat leaves United still rooted second bottom of the Premier League and gave Pochettino an early indication of the huge job he has ahead to restore the 20-time English champions to their former glories.

Liverpool climb into the top four and within seven points of leaders Arsenal to rekindle faint hopes of challenging for the title.

Pochettino answered United’s call after Michael Carrick was sacked last week after winning just one of the Red Devils’ first 10 league games in charge.

The Argentine has been linked with a move to Old Trafford for a decade, but failed to make a strong first impression on the United fans.

Pochettino’s bold team selection backfired with the centre-back pairing of Matthijs de Ligt and Yoro at fault for the game’s decisive moment.

De Ligt, on his first Premier League start for nearly a year, let a long ball down the middle and go and allowed Alexander Isak to bear down on goal.

The Swedish striker took a heavy touch before he was clipped by Yoro, but referee Sam Barrott still deemed the French defender had denied a clear goalscoring opportunity and produced a red card.

Szoboszlai rubbed salt into United wounds by drilling home the resulting free-kick from the edge of the box.

Moments later Ngumoha skipped past Diogo Dalot and crossed for Wirtz to hook a shot in off the underside of the bar.

Having relegated Harry Maguire to the bench, Pochettino was forced to turn to the veteran centre-back just 22 minutes in to try and stem the bleeding.

United lost 7-0 at Anfield three years ago and a switch to a back five helped avoid similar damage, albeit with the help of some wayward Liverpool finishing.

Maguire made a brilliant block to deny Isak a third goal just before half-time.

Bradley Barcola and Isak were guilty of wasting huge chances early in the second half.

But Barcola’s blistering pace created Liverpool’s third just after the hour mark.

The French international destroyed Lisandro Martinez for pace before picking out Ngumoha to slot home.

Wirtz rounded off one of his best Liverpool displays since a £100 million move from Bayer Leverkusen last year with the assist for Munoz to crash home the fourth goal eight minutes from time.

Liverpool fans rejoiced in their rivals’ pain with chants of “you are going down”.

United have not been relegated since 1974 but find themselves in a battle for survival despite still enjoying one of the biggest revenues in world football.

The 34 goals they have conceded in all competitions is the worst defensive record of any team in Europe’s top five leagues this season.

title: Watford sack Dionisi after just 18 games
description:
Watford have sacked head coach Alessio Dionisi after 18 games in charge, following Saturday’s 4-0 defeat to Sheffield United, with the club now searching for another manager.
The Championship club confirmed the Italian’s departure in a statement on Sunday, a day after the heavy loss at Bramall Lane.
content:
Watford have sacked head coach Alessio Dionisi after 18 games in charge, following Saturday’s 4-0 defeat to Sheffield United, with the club now searching for another manager.

The Championship club confirmed the Italian’s departure in a statement on Sunday, a day after the heavy loss at Bramall Lane.

Dionisi, 46, was appointed in June following the departure of Ed Still, who had spent only three months at Vicarage Road.

The dismissal comes after a disappointing run of results that has left Watford 21st in the Championship table, with only four league victories under the Italian.

In a statement on the club’s website, sporting director Luke Dowling thanked Dionisi and his staff for their work.

“We thank Alessio and his staff for his professionalism and their efforts,” Dowling said.

“As I’m sure the supporters have seen, Alessio is a really good guy and we wish him the best for the future.

“The process has started for a replacement and we hope to be in a position to announce that shortly.”

Dionisi’s spell at Watford began positively, with his side beating Southampton in their opening league game. However, they won only two of their next 12 matches in all competitions.

Although they defeated Charlton on October 17, subsequent losses to Wolves and Norwich, followed by the heavy defeat to Sheffield United, increased pressure on the Italian.

Before joining Watford, Dionisi was in charge of Italian Serie B side Empoli, where he was sacked in March after five months following a run of five wins in 22 matches.

His appointment at Watford was his first managerial job outside Italy.

The latest departure adds to the club’s recent managerial instability. Since Tom Cleverley left at the end of the 2024-25 season, Watford have appointed Ed Still, Javi Gracia, Paulo Pezzolano and Dionisi as permanent head coaches, while Charlie Daniels also had a two-match spell as interim boss.

Dionisi was Watford’s 12th head coach, excluding interim appointments, since the end of the 2020-21 season.

The club are now searching for their 25th manager since the Pozzo family took over in 2012. Watford have had 57 permanent managers in their 145-year history.

The club’s managerial changes have continued despite previous acknowledgements of the need for greater stability. On the morning of their final-day defeat to Coventry last season, chief executive Scott Duxbury admitted that the club had made mistakes, describing the end to the campaign as “unacceptable” and “truly disappointing in the extreme”.

title: ELP: Liverpool thrash 10-man Man Utd 4-0 in Pochettino’s debut
description:
Liverpool handed Manchester United a humiliating 4-0 defeat at Anfield on Sunday, leaving the visitors in the Premier League relegation zone in Mauricio Pochettino’s first match as manager.
United’s afternoon quickly unravelled after defender Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute, leaving the
content:
Liverpool handed Manchester United a humiliating 4-0 defeat at Anfield on Sunday, leaving the visitors in the Premier League relegation zone in Mauricio Pochettino’s first match as manager.

United’s afternoon quickly unravelled after defender Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute, leaving the visitors to play most of the encounter with 10 men.

Liverpool capitalised on their numerical advantage, scoring twice in three minutes through Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz to take a commanding 2-0 lead into half-time.

Szoboszlai opened the scoring in the 10th minute before Wirtz doubled the advantage three minutes later, putting Liverpool firmly in control.

United struggled to contain the hosts after the break, with Liverpool continuing to create chances and dominate proceedings.

Teenage forward Rio Ngumoha extended the lead in the 66th minute, finishing off an assist from Bradley Barcola to make it 3-0.

Substitute Victor Muñoz completed the rout eight minutes from time, firing home after being set up by Wirtz.

The defeat marked a disastrous start to Pochettino’s reign, with United unable to recover from Yoro’s early dismissal and Liverpool’s relentless attacking pressure.

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson also denied United captain Bruno Fernandes on three occasions, preventing the visitors from finding a consolation goal.

The result lifted Liverpool to fourth place on the table, seven points behind leaders Arsenal, while United remained in the bottom three.

United have now conceded 34 goals in all competitions this season, the highest tally among clubs in Europe’s five major leagues, according to BBC Sport.

Liverpool had lost both league meetings with United last season but produced a dominant display to claim a convincing victory at Anfield.

title: Bayelsa Boat Mishap: Death toll rises to 29
description:
…Tinubu approves N250m for victims’ families, directs NDDC to procure boats



…FG backs probe of incident



…Diri makes case for senatorial roads



By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa



The death toll from last Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to
content:
…Tinubu approves N250m for victims’ families, directs NDDC to procure boats

…FG backs probe of incident

…Diri makes case for senatorial roads

By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa

The death toll from last Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 29, with more than 51 survivors recorded, as search and recovery operations continue.

President Bola Tinubu has also approved N250 million to support families of the victims and directed the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) to procure boats to improve water transportation in the riverine communities.

Vice President Kashim Shettima announced the presidential intervention on Sunday during a condolence visit to Bayelsa State on the President’s directive.

The boat, which was conveying passengers to Ukubie community for a burial ceremony, capsized near Oweikorogha community, leaving several persons dead and others rescued.

Speaking at the Government House, Yenagoa, after visiting hospitalised survivors at the Bayelsa Medical University Teaching Hospital (BMUTH), Shettima said the President had directed relevant federal agencies to collaborate with the state government in the search and rescue operations and provide support for those affected.

He described the incident as a national tragedy, noting that behind the casualty figures were individuals with families, relationships and responsibilities to their communities and society.

“Each person involved has a name, an identity, a history, relationships and responsibilities. Family members cannot come to terms with the fact that someone who left home for a funeral will never return,” he said.

The Vice President acknowledged the peculiar geographical challenges of Bayelsa, where waterways serve as major transportation routes connecting communities to schools, hospitals, markets and other essential services.

“Geography can determine how people travel, but it will never determine the worth of the lives involved,” Shettima stated.

He disclosed that Tinubu had directed the NDDC to procure boats to improve transportation in the riverine areas of the state.

Shettima also commended Governor Douye Diri for his response to the tragedy and the establishment of a commission of inquiry to investigate the incident.

He stressed the need for the recommendations of the panel to be implemented to prevent a recurrence.

In his remarks, Diri thanked Tinubu and the Vice President for their intervention and for identifying with the people of Bayelsa at a difficult time.

The governor recalled that Shettima was among the first senior government officials to contact him following the incident, alongside the President’s Chief of Staff and the Minister of Marine and Blue Economy.

He said the Federal Government’s response demonstrated its commitment to the welfare of Bayelsans, contrasting it with what he described as the inadequate attention the state received during the 2022 flood disaster.

“On behalf of the government and people of Bayelsa State, I acknowledge the very sound leadership of Mr President, your humble self and your team for the human face. We cannot thank you enough,” Diri said.

Describing the incident as a painful loss, the governor said many of the victims were young people whose futures held great promise.

However, he said preliminary findings suggested that the accident might have been avoided if established safety regulations had been observed.

“From what we have gathered so far, the boat was not seaworthy or river-worthy. The loading point was not an approved government loading point, and that is why all the necessary government requirements were not found in this incident,” he said.

Diri explained that the state government had taken charge of the rescue operation in collaboration with federal agencies, security services and other relevant authorities.

He added that the government was also taking responsibility for the medical bills and feeding of survivors receiving treatment in various hospitals across the state.

Providing an update on the incident, the governor said 29 persons had been confirmed dead, while more than 51 survivors had been recorded.

He said search and recovery operations were ongoing, adding that authorities were yet to retrieve the capsized boat.

According to him, the exact casualty figure could only be established after the recovery of the boat, as some bodies might still be trapped inside it.

Meanwhile, the governor appealed to the Federal Government to intervene in the slow pace of work on the second phase of the Nembe-Brass Road project, despite its approval by President Tinubu.

He explained that Bayelsa’s riverine and deltaic terrain made road construction particularly challenging and expensive, requiring sustained collaboration between the federal and state governments.

Diri urged the Vice President to convey the state’s concerns to the President and support efforts to accelerate work on the project, as well as collaborate with the state government on the completion of the three senatorial roads.

Shettima also met with families of the victims and presented cash assistance to them.

Those present during the visit included the governor’s wife, Dr Gloria Diri; Minority Leader of the House of Representatives, Fred Agbedi; Senators Konbowei Benson and Benson Agadaga; and the member representing Southern Ijaw Federal Constituency, Rodney Ambaiowei.

Others were the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Senator Heineken Lokpobiri; Deputy Speaker of the Bayelsa State House of Assembly, Michael Ogbere; former deputy governors Peremobowei Ebebi and Rear Admiral Gboribiogha John-Jonah; and NDDC Managing Director, Dr Samuel Ogbuku.

Also present were the Managing Director of the Niger Delta Basin Development Authority, Prince Ebitimi Amgbare; former NDDC Managing Director, Chief Ndutimi Alaibe; Chief David Lyon; and PANDEF National Chairman, Dr Boladei Igali.

The Director-General of the National Emergency Management Agency, Mrs Zubaida Abubakar Umar, was also part of the Vice President’s entourage.

title: UI undergraduate set to attempt 168-hour Guinness World Record teaching marathon
description:
A 200-level Education and Physics student at the University of Ibadan, Bello Oluwapelumi Ayomide, is set to attempt a 168-hour Guinness World Record teaching marathon, during which he plans to teach Physics continuously for seven days.







The attempt, scheduled to hold from November 27 to Decemb
content:
A 200-level Education and Physics student at the University of Ibadan, Bello Oluwapelumi Ayomide, is set to attempt a 168-hour Guinness World Record teaching marathon, during which he plans to teach Physics continuously for seven days.

The attempt, scheduled to hold from November 27 to December 4, 2026, will take place at the New Faculty Lecture Theatre, Faculty of Science, University of Ibadan.

Ayomide, popularly known as Tutor Bello, said the attempt, initially planned for the previous semester vacation, was postponed because of the university’s academic calendar.

Tutor Bello, who spoke in an interview aherad of the attempt at the University of Ibadan, explained that the short interval between his last examination and the commencement of the new semester made it difficult to organise the exercise as planned.

He said preparations had since resumed, with different teams established to coordinate the event, including welfare, attendance, meals and media units.

Ayomide also disclosed plans to hold a publicity rally within the University of Ibadan on Monday, November 23, at 4pm to create more awareness about the proposed marathon and encourage students to support the initiative.

Expressing confidence that the attempt would hold as scheduled, the student said considerable resources and efforts had already gone into the preparations.

“We cannot invest this much money and effort into the preparations without seeing the event through,” he said.

He explained that the approval of his application had a one-year validity period, making the forthcoming attempt particularly important, as his academic commitments might make it difficult to pursue the record the following year.

The proposed 168-hour marathon will focus on Mechanics, a component of Physics 101, a course taken by first-year students.

Ayomide said the choice of subject was deliberate, as he hoped to make a course many students find difficult to understand through sustained and detailed teaching.

He explained that the exercise was not solely intended to secure a Guinness World Record but also to create an educational resource that students could continue to access long after the event.

“The record itself isn’t even just for recognition,” he said, explaining that the planned online livestream would enable students to revisit the lessons whenever they needed them.

He added that recordings of the sessions could serve as learning materials for successive generations of first-year students who might encounter difficulties with the course.

On the requirements for the attempt, Ayomide said he had received guidelines from Guinness World Records detailing the conditions for the exercise, including stipulated rest periods, continuous video recording and the presence of witnesses.

According to him, the guidelines permit five minutes of rest for every hour of teaching, with the accumulated time allowing longer teaching sessions followed by corresponding breaks.

He explained that the recording would continue during breaks, while a timekeeping device would also be captured on camera to document the duration of the attempt.

The evidence would subsequently be submitted through the Guinness World Records evidence portal for assessment.

Meanwhile, Ayomide said he was still seeking financial support and sponsorship to strengthen the organisation of the marathon, appealing to individuals, organisations and corporate bodies interested in supporting education and youth development to partner with him.

Beyond the record attempt, Ayomide said he hoped to draw attention to the challenges students face in accessing quality education in Nigeria, particularly when they lack adequate learning support and educational resources.

He said he intended to use the publicity surrounding the exercise to promote technology-driven learning through platforms such as Belloxdydx and LockInPoint, which provide students with learning materials, past questions and other educational resources.

According to him, the attention generated by the attempt could also help him establish partnerships, attract support and expand access to affordable learning materials, particularly for students who cannot afford private tutoring.

“The record is not the destination; it is a platform to amplify my impact in education,” he said.

“With God, it is very possible, and for me, it is very achievable. The only major thing on the way is just finances,” he said.

The proposed attempt is expected to combine an endurance challenge with an educational initiative aimed at making learning resources more accessible to students.
