By Chioma Obinna

The Association of Community Pharmacists of Nigeria (ACPN) on Sunday petitioned the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, over alleged regulatory overreach and unlawful pharmaceutical enforcement by the Edo State Consumer Protection Committee.


The association urged the Federal Government to intervene, warning that state agencies must not assume regulatory powers vested in federal institutions under existing laws.


In a petition titled “Exercising Regulatory Control within the Constitutional Framework in Nigeria”, and jointly signed by ACPN National Chairman, Pharm. Ambrose Igwekamma Ezeh, and National Secretary, Pharm. Obiageri Ikwu, ACPN said it supported efforts to rid the country of counterfeit, adulterated, substandard and expired medicines but insisted that such interventions must be evidence-based, follow due process and comply with the relevant laws.


The association specifically faulted the Edo State Consumer Protection Committee for reportedly declaring Camosunate a banned medicinal product in Nigeria, arguing that the committee lacked the statutory authority to make such a pronouncement.


According to ACPN, “The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) is empowered by law to register, ban or deregister drugs and food products in the country. A verification of NAFDAC’s official Green Book showed that Camosunate Children Powder, with registration number 04-7908, manufactured by Front Pharmaceuticals PLC and marketed by Geneith Pharmaceuticals Limited, remained an active registered medicinal product.”


The association said the product’s registration was approved on November 26, 2025, and would remain valid until November 25, 2030.


“This is an official regulatory record, not an opinion or an industry rumour. There was no official NAFDAC declaration, suspension, withdrawal or cancellation notice establishing that the specific Camosunate formulation pronounced banned by the Edo committee was prohibited in Nigeria.”


The association also raised concerns over a reported enforcement operation involving ALSO CARE Pharmacy in Evbuodia community, along Airport Road, Benin City, and the public allegations made against the establishment.
It called for the disclosure of the products seized, their registration particulars and the independent regulatory evidence supporting any allegation of counterfeit or prohibited medicines.
“No pharmacy should be publicly condemned on the basis of unverified assertions,” the association said.
Citing the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (Establishment) Act 2022, ACPN maintained that the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) had statutory responsibility for the registration, inspection, licensing and regulation of pharmaceutical premises across the country.
It specifically referenced Sections 4, 22, 31 and 32 of the Act, arguing that pharmaceutical premises regulation must be undertaken by legally designated authorities.
The association also cited Sections 7 and 8 of the Counterfeit and Fake Drugs and Unwholesome Processed Foods (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, Cap C34 LFN 2004, which provide for the constitution and powers of state task forces.
It, however, argued that such provisions did not automatically empower state consumer protection committees to assume specialised pharmaceutical regulatory functions.
“Such powers cannot automatically be appropriated by State Consumer Protection Committee, as it is not recognised to carry out such functions in all the relevant existing federal laws,” it said.
ACPN further cited Section 5 of the NAFDAC Act, Cap N1 LFN 2004, as the statutory basis for NAFDAC’s responsibility for regulating medicinal products.

The association urged Fagbemi to liaise with Attorneys-General and Commissioners for Justice in the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory to sensitise government agencies on their constitutional and statutory responsibilities.
It also called for an end to pharmaceutical enforcement activities conducted without appropriate legal authority and urged all relevant agencies to respect the mandates of NAFDAC and PCN.
While reaffirming its commitment to protecting Nigerians from fake and falsified medicines, the association warned against the misuse of consumer protection powers.
“Consumer protection must never become a licence for misinformation, administrative arbitrariness, or regulatory intimidation. Public officials must be accountable for their claims.”

The post ACPN petitions AGF over Edo drug enforcement, alleges regulatory overreach appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Emir of Daura: Lawyer demands police probe
description:
By John Alechenu



ABUJA — Abuja-based legal practitioner, Pelumi Olajengbesi, has called on the Nigeria Police Force to immediately commence an independent investigation into the allegation of sexual assault levelled against the Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, by a foreign tourist.







Olajeng
content:
By John Alechenu

ABUJA — Abuja-based legal practitioner, Pelumi Olajengbesi, has called on the Nigeria Police Force to immediately commence an independent investigation into the allegation of sexual assault levelled against the Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, by a foreign tourist.

Olajengbesi described the allegation as disturbing, stressing that it should not be treated lightly and that all parties must be accorded fairness and due process.

He urged the police to investigate the matter thoroughly and independently to establish the facts and ensure that justice was served in accordance with the law.

“We must be able to show to the entire world that Nigeria doesn’t condone sexual harassment. Therefore, all parties must be accorded fairness and due process in the interest of justice,” he said.

“Sexual harassment has no place in our society. This is a no, no, no for Nigeria!” he declared.

The lawyer’s call follows allegations made by a foreign tourist, identified as Mirka on Instagram, where she uses the handle @beduinqa, who accused the Emir of sexually assaulting her during a visit to his palace on November 14.

The tourist, who said she was on a 30-day tour of Nigeria, alleged that the traditional ruler held her hand, hugged and kissed her on the cheek before touching her breasts despite her repeated objections.

“I told him ‘emir no, no, no, no’ ‘emir you cannot be touching’, but he was just laughing about it,” she wrote.

She claimed to have recorded the encounter with Meta smart glasses but waited until she had left Nigeria before making the allegation public.

The tourist said the alleged incident was particularly distressing because she had not experienced sexual assault while visiting other parts of the country.

“I wasn’t sexually assaulted at any moment when walking through streets of Nigeria, even in busy crowded places, but to my shock, I was assaulted in a palace by a traditional leader who should be behaving in exemplary and dignified way,” she said.

The video and her account have since circulated widely on social media platforms, including X, Instagram and Facebook, triggering discussions about consent, the conduct of traditional institutions and accountability.

Amnesty International Nigeria has also called on the Katsina State Government and the police to conduct a transparent and independent investigation into the allegation and ensure accountability if it is established.

As of Sunday, neither the Daura Emirate Council nor the Katsina State Government had issued an official response to the allegation.

The allegation remains unverified, and no finding of wrongdoing has been established against the Emir.

content:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

President Bola Tinubu hascelebrated Sir Davis Elaiho, father of the President/Group Chief Executive Officer of Transcorp Group, Owen Omogiafo, on his 80th birthday, praising his contributions to business, community development and philanthropy.

Tinubu described the octogenarian as a man whose life has been shaped by hard work, discipline and integrity, noting his contributions to the social and economic development of Edo State and Nigeria.

The President, in a birthday message issued on Sunday by his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, said Elaiho had inspired many through his decades of service as a businessman and community leader in Benin City.

He particularly commended his contributions through Jubilee Investments Limited, where he currently serves as Chairman following his retirement from active service.

Tinubu also acknowledged his commitment to human development and philanthropy, as well as his positive impact on lives through community leadership and membership of St. Matthew’s Cathedral, Benin City.

“On this memorable occasion of his 80th birthday anniversary, I rejoice with Sir Davis Elaiho, family, associates and friends for the grace to attain this important milestone.

“As a business and community leader in Benin, Sir Elaiho has made important contributions to society and inspired many people.

“I wish him a great celebration and God’s grace to see more years in good health,” the President said.

Elaiho is a businessman, community leader and a pillar of faith. He is also a Justice of the Peace (JP) and a Knight of St. Mulumba (KSM).

title: Bayelsa boat mishap: Tinubu donates N250m to victims’ families, as Shettima visits survivors
description:
…orders stiffer waterway safety measures



…Says Nigerians travelling by water deserve same protection as road, air passengers‎‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru‎‎ABUJA — PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has called for stricter enforcement of safety standards on Nigeria’s inland waterways following the tragic boat misha
content:
…orders stiffer waterway safety measures

…Says Nigerians travelling by water deserve same protection as road, air passengers
‎
‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
‎
‎ABUJA — PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has called for stricter enforcement of safety standards on Nigeria’s inland waterways following the tragic boat mishap in Bayelsa State, announcing a N250 million Federal Government donation to support the bereaved families.
‎
‎He also demanded a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident, vowing that the Federal Government would work with relevant authorities and state governments to strengthen vessel inspections, safety compliance and enforcement to prevent further loss of lives.
‎
‎Vice President Kashim Shettima conveyed the President’s position on Sunday during a condolence visit to Yenagoa, the Bayelsa State capital, following Friday’s boat accident at the Oweikorogha/Otuan River Junction in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area.
‎
‎Speaking at Government House, Yenagoa, the Vice President said the tragedy had exposed the urgent need to improve safety on inland waterways, particularly in riverine communities where water transportation remains essential to everyday life.
‎
‎”We cannot accept a situation in which citizens must gamble with their lives simply to move between communities. Geography may determine how people travel, but it must never determine how much protection their lives deserve. A Nigerian travelling by boat is entitled to the same concern for safety as one travelling by road or air,” he said.
‎
‎Senator Shettima said preliminary reports suggesting that the boat developed a mechanical fault must be thoroughly investigated to establish the circumstances of the accident and identify possible failures in safety procedures.
‎
‎”We have received preliminary reports concerning the circumstances of this accident, including indications of a possible mechanical failure. These reports must be thoroughly investigated by the appropriate authorities. We must establish what happened, identify any failures in safety procedures and take the necessary steps to prevent a recurrence.
‎
‎”President Tinubu’s administration will continue working with the relevant authorities and state governments to strengthen safety standards, vessel inspections and enforcement on our inland waterways. The lives of our people are too precious for safety to remain an afterthought,” the Vice President stated.
‎
‎Expressing grief over the tragedy, VP Shettima described the loss as particularly painful because the victims were travelling to attend a burial ceremony when the accident occurred.
‎
‎”There is a particular cruelty in the tragedy that has brought us here today. Our brothers and sisters set out on a journey to mourn the dead, only for death to claim some of them along the way,” he lamented.
‎
‎The Vice President recalled that President Tinubu had, upon receiving news of the disaster, directed relevant federal agencies to commence rescue and recovery operations and ordered that Saturday’s APC presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, be conducted without the usual celebrations in honour of the victims.
‎
‎He stressed that the victims must not be reduced to casualty figures, noting that each had a family, personal history and responsibilities.
‎
‎”Each person lost in those waters had a name, a history, relationships and responsibilities. Somewhere, a family is struggling to understand how someone who left home for a funeral will never walk through that door again,” VP Shettima added.
‎
‎He commended Governor Douye Diri for visiting the accident scene and coordinating the state’s response, while acknowledging the efforts of the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), Bayelsa State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA), Nigerian Red Cross Society, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), local divers and community volunteers.
‎
‎Assuring the bereaved families of the Federal Government’s continued support, the Vice President said, “To the families who have lost their loved ones, I will not pretend that time alone will make this pain disappear. Our responsibility is to stand with you beyond this visit, beyond these condolences and beyond the days when this tragedy dominates the news.”
‎
‎Before proceeding to the Government House, Vice President Shettima visited survivors receiving treatment at the Bayelsa Medical University Teaching Hospital, where he consoled them and assured them of adequate medical care and attention.
‎
‎The Vice President also met with members of the bereaved families and some survivors at the Government House, conveying President Tinubu’s condolences and the Federal Government’s solidarity with those affected.
‎
‎Earlier, Governor Diri, while briefing the Vice President and other government officials at the Government House, disclosed that the death toll had risen to 29, while more than 50 passengers survived the accident as of Sunday afternoon.
‎
‎The Governor attributed the tragedy to an alleged failure by the boat operators to observe established safety protocols, describing the incident as avoidable.
‎
‎He disclosed that the Bayelsa State Government had constituted a committee to investigate the immediate and remote causes of the accident and recommend measures to prevent similar incidents.
‎
‎Governor Diri further announced that the state government had taken responsibility for the medical bills and treatment of survivors, assuring the bereaved families that they would not be abandoned.
‎
‎He thanked the military, paramilitary agencies, emergency responders, local divers and other stakeholders who mobilised to assist the victims and support ongoing rescue and recovery operations.
‎
‎On arrival in Yenagoa, the Vice President was received by Governor Douye Diri; Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Senator Heineken Lokpobiri; Managing Director of the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), Dr. Samuel Ogbuku; Bayelsa State APC Chairman, Dr. Dennis Otiotio; and Managing Director of the Niger Delta River Basin Development Authority, Prince Ebitimi Amgbare.
‎
‎Others present included members of the National Assembly, members of the Bayelsa State House of Assembly and members of the State Executive Council.
‎
‎The Vice President was accompanied by the Director-General of NEMA and other senior Federal Government officials.
‎

The post Bayelsa boat mishap: Tinubu donates N250m to victims’ families, as Shettima visits survivors appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: ‘We Must Get To Root Of This Tragedy,’ Oyetola Orders Probe Into Bayelsa Boat Accident
description: The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, has ordered an immediate investigation into the remote and direct causes of the fatal boat mishap that occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha Community, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, clai
content:
The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, has ordered an immediate investigation into the remote and direct causes of the fatal boat mishap that occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha Community, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, claiming scores of lives.

Oyetola directed the National Inland Waterways Authority (NIWA) to conduct a thorough investigation into the incident and submit its report to him.

He further directed NIWA to work in collaboration with relevant government agencies and the Bayelsa State Government to ensure a comprehensive, transparent and credible investigation.

Describing the loss of lives as worrisome and unacceptable, Oyetola said the Federal Government would no longer tolerate avoidable safety lapses on the nation’s waterways.

The minister expressed concerns that passengers involved in the tragedy reportedly did not wear life jackets, recalling that he personally visited Bayelsa State on May 2, 2025, to distribute 3,500 life jackets to water transport users as part of efforts to promote safety and protect lives.

He also raised concerns over the alleged absence of a passenger manifest, stressing that proper passenger documentation was a critical safety requirement that must be strictly enforced.

“Safety lapses on our waterways are no longer acceptable. The Federal Government will not fold its arms and watch its citizens perish on the waterways. We must get to the root of this tragedy and ensure that those responsible for enforcing safety regulations do their jobs,” the minister was quoted as saying in a statement by Special Adviser to the minister, Bolaji Akinola.

Oyetola reiterated his call for the gradual phasing out of wooden boats by State Governments and their replacement with safer, more durable and better-equipped fiberglass or fiber-reinforced plastic vessels, particularly for passenger transportation.

“I have consistently advocated for state governments to begin gradually phasing out wooden boats and replace them with safer, more durable and better-equipped fiberglass or fiber-reinforced plastic vessels, particularly for passenger transportation,” he said.

The minister disclosed that he had called the Governor of Bayelsa State, Senator Douye Diri, to commiserate with him, the state government and families of the victims over the tragic incident.

Expressing sympathy to the bereaved families, the minister said the loss of lives in such circumstances was deeply painful and that the grief of families who had lost loved ones was beyond words.

“Our thoughts and prayers are with the affected families at this difficult time. We also sympathise with all those who have been affected by this tragedy and pray for strength, comfort and the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss,” he said.

He prayed for the repose of the souls of the departed and for divine comfort for their families, urging all stakeholders to work together to ensure that such a tragedy never happens again.

The accident left at least 29 people dead.

The post ‘We Must Get To Root Of This Tragedy,’ Oyetola Orders Probe Into Bayelsa Boat Accident appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Hypo Partners With NCDC In Support Of Efforts Against Ebola Virus Disease
description: Hypo Homecare Products Limited, makers of Hypo household hygiene products, has extended significant product support to the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention in support of national efforts to strengthen preparedness and response against Ebola Virus Disease in Nigeria. The contribution
content:
Hypo Homecare Products Limited, makers of Hypo household hygiene products, has extended significant product support to the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention in support of national efforts to strengthen preparedness and response against Ebola Virus Disease in Nigeria. The contribution of Hypo Bleach is aimed at supporting critical infection prevention and control efforts, particularly within healthcare facilities, and reinforcing the collective effort to safeguard public health and protect communities across the country.

The donation, which was formally presented to the NCDC, was received on behalf of the Centre by Tajudeen Arowolo, Head of Department, Health Emergency Preparedness and Response. The gesture reflects Hypo’s commitment to supporting public health efforts and promoting better hygiene and sanitation practices across Nigerian communities. The NCDC welcomed the contribution as Hypo reaffirmed its commitment to playing a role in the collective effort to protect public health.

As a household hygiene brand with a longstanding commitment to keeping homes and shared spaces clean and hygienic, Hypo recognises the importance of proper hygiene and environmental sanitation in supporting public health. Through its range of cleaning and disinfection products, the brand continues to encourage consumers to maintain cleaner and more hygienic environments.

Speaking on the donation, Ifeoluwa Adeyemo, Senior Brand Manager, Hypo, said:

“At Hypo, we believe that protecting public health is a collective responsibility. As a brand committed to providing effective cleaning and disinfection solutions, we recognise the importance of supporting efforts that promote healthier and safer communities. This donation is our way of contributing to the ongoing efforts against Ebola Virus Disease and demonstrating our commitment to the well-being of Nigerians.”

Acknowledging the contribution, Dr. Odianosen Ehiakhamen, Incident Manager for Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) in Nigeria, said:

“We’re grateful for the support we have just received from Hypo, providing us with IPC commodities to strengthen IPC practices, especially in health facilities. These cartons of hypochlorite solution will go a long way in supporting health facilities in the states, particularly through the state preparedness and response systems for Ebola Virus Disease and other outbreak diseases. Thank you so much, Hypo, for the support.”

Beyond the product donation, Hypo is also committed to supporting broader public awareness efforts through hygiene education. The brand recognises that access to effective hygiene solutions must go hand in hand with the knowledge and adoption of appropriate hygiene practices.

Through planned public awareness and hygiene education initiatives, Hypo aims to encourage better hygiene habits, promote responsible sanitation practices and reinforce the importance of maintaining clean and hygienic environments in homes and communities.

The donation underscores Hypo’s continued commitment to making a positive contribution to society, extending its role beyond providing household cleaning and disinfection products to supporting initiatives that promote healthier living.

About Hypo

Hypo is a household hygiene brand offering cleaning and disinfection solutions that help consumers maintain clean and hygienic homes and shared spaces. Through its products (Hypo Multi-Purpose Bleach and Hypo Toilet Cleaner) and consumer education initiatives, Hypo remains committed to promoting better hygiene practices and healthier communities.

The post Hypo Partners With NCDC In Support Of Efforts Against Ebola Virus Disease appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: 2027: Any plot against Tinubu will fail – Akpabio
description:
Senate President Godswill Akpabio on Sunday described President Bola Tinubu as a “child of covenant,” warning that any conspiracy against him ahead of the 2027 general elections will fail.
Akpabio spoke on Sunday at the Akwa Ibom State inauguration of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Uyo, where he
content:
Senate President Godswill Akpabio on Sunday described President Bola Tinubu as a “child of covenant,” warning that any conspiracy against him ahead of the 2027 general elections will fail.

Akpabio spoke on Sunday at the Akwa Ibom State inauguration of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Uyo, where he called on his supporters to reject attempts to undermine the President’s re-election bid.

“We are saying today that President Bola Tinubu is a child of covenant. And therefore, any conspiracy against him, and all conspirators against him, shall be consumed by fire. Holy Ghost, Fire! Holy Ghost, Fire! Holy Ghost, Fire!” he said.

The Senate President also described Vice-President Kashim Shettima as a child of covenant, warning that any conspiracy against him would not stand.

Akpabio said the National Assembly was fully behind Tinubu.

He said the legislature was supporting the administration’s efforts to address the country’s economic challenges.

“The National Assembly is behind the President 100 per cent. And we are doing this with a lot of personal sacrifice and patience,” he said.

He listed some of the administration’s initiatives, including the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, the Consumer Credit Scheme, the Presidential Compressed Natural Gas Initiative and agricultural interventions, as programmes aimed at improving the lives of Nigerians.

Akpabio also defended the removal of the petrol subsidy, describing those advocating its reversal as confused.

“No government can remedy what it does not understand. If you don’t understand that subsidy was killing Nigeria, can you remedy it? That is why they said they want to go back to subsidy. We wish them luck, because it is not in Nigeria. We have left them behind,” he said.

The former Akwa Ibom governor further claimed that political parties and support groups in the state had united behind Tinubu’s re-election bid.

“When we say here, A, B and C, and we say Akwa Ibom United, it means that all political parties have collapsed into one to vote for the President in 2027. It means that all political parties and all support groups have joined door to door to canvass support for the President come 2027,” he said.

Akpabio also said opposition parties had little political presence in the state, claiming that those who attempted to campaign there had struggled to attract supporters.

He commended the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement for taking its campaign to Akwa Ibom, saying the initiative recognised the importance of engaging voters in their homes and communities.

The movement, convened by Niger Delta leader Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, is mobilising grassroots support for Tinubu’s re-election in 2027 through state, local government, ward and polling unit structures.

The post 2027: Any plot against Tinubu will fail – Akpabio appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Tinubu needs second term to consolidate reforms – Wike
description:
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has urged Nigerians to re-elect President Bola Tinubu in 2027, warning that denying him a second term could undermine the gains of his administration’s economic reforms and efforts to stabilise the country.
Wike said although the removal of
content:
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has urged Nigerians to re-elect President Bola Tinubu in 2027, warning that denying him a second term could undermine the gains of his administration’s economic reforms and efforts to stabilise the country.

Wike said although the removal of the fuel subsidy had initially imposed difficulties on Nigerians, the policy and other reforms required time to yield the desired benefits.

He insisted that Tinubu should be allowed to consolidate the foundation he had laid for economic recovery and prosperity.

He spoke on Sunday during a thanksgiving and dedication service at St Peter’s Anglican Church, Rumueprikom, his hometown in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State, where the Rainbow Coalition Campaign Council was dedicated ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The minister, who disclosed that the coalition’s campaigns would commence on November 23, described Tinubu as a courageous leader whose decisions, though difficult, were necessary to prevent the country from collapsing.

He said, “This country was on the verge of collapse. On the verge of collapse. But by the grace of God, He gave us somebody who is courageous.”

Wike cited improvements in the university system, particularly the relative reduction in industrial disputes over unpaid entitlements, as evidence of the administration’s interventions.

He also recalled the difficulties pensioners previously experienced in accessing their payments, arguing that the President had taken necessary decisions to address longstanding challenges.

On the removal of the fuel subsidy, the minister acknowledged that the policy had brought some disadvantages but maintained that the difficulties were temporary and that the country needed continuity to consolidate the reforms.

He said, “Now, in doing that, there must be some disadvantages.

“And that’s why they say these disadvantages will be temporarily seen. As he has laid his foundation, now it’s time for prosperity.

“If we don’t re-elect him, then it will be difficult to stabilise what he has done,” he said.

The former Rivers State governor called on Nigerians across religious divides to support Tinubu’s re-election, saying the campaign would seek votes from Christians, Muslims and traditional worshippers.

He said, “I am not a native doctor but I need their votes now. I need everybody’s votes because I know they are registered voters.”

Wike added, “The Muslims, I need their votes too. The Christians like you, we need your votes.”

He also defended the Tinubu administration against allegations of religious imbalance in political appointments, claiming that Christians had received significant opportunities under the current government.

He said, “Since Nigeria was created, we have never had the kind of appointments that are going on in this country now.”

The minister urged Nigerians to participate actively in the 2027 elections, warning that abstaining from voting would not shield citizens from the consequences of electoral outcomes.

He said, “If you don’t participate, and you have a bad leader, it will also affect you.”

Turning to the Rivers State governorship election, Wike urged residents to support the All Progressives Congress candidate, Ogundu Kingsley Chinda, describing him as a son of the soil.

He said the dedication of the Rainbow Coalition Campaign Council was consistent with the group’s tradition of committing its political activities to God before commencing campaigns.

Expressing confidence that the forthcoming campaign would be peaceful, the minister said, “Just as we have never had crisis before, I believe we will also not have crisis in this period.”

Wike also pledged continued support for the church, announcing a donation of N100m on behalf of the Rainbow Coalition, his friends and associates.

He described the contribution as a demonstration of their commitment to supporting the church and called on religious leaders to reciprocate through prayers, while urging members of the congregation to support the coalition at the polls.

Among the political leaders present at the service were the APC governorship candidate, Ogundu Kingsley Chinda; Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party Board of Trustees, Senator Mao Ohuabunwa; Speaker of the Rivers State House of Assembly, Martin Amaewhule; and other members of the Rainbow Coalition.

title: Borno youths unveil local food to fight malnutrition
description:
From Timothy Olanrewaju, Maiduguri
Some youths in Borno State have unveiled locally produced ready-to-use foods to tackle malnutrition among children in the state.
The innovation, described by health experts as nutritious and affordable, was unveiled at a youth nutrition challenge organised by UNICE
content:
From Timothy Olanrewaju, Maiduguri

Some youths in Borno State have unveiled locally produced ready-to-use foods to tackle malnutrition among children in the state.

The innovation, described by health experts as nutritious and affordable, was unveiled at a youth nutrition challenge organised by UNICEF in Maiduguri at the weekend to mark the 2026 World Children’s Day.

UNICEF Chief of Maiduguri Field Office, Mr. Francis Butichi, said the youth-led nutrition challenge was more than a competition against malnutrition, but a platform for young people to be part of the solution.

“The youth-led nutrition challenge is more than an effort to address acute malnutrition. It is a platform for young people to collaborate and create local solutions to a global problem,” he said.

He said the youths sourced local but nutritious ingredients to produce affordable and accessible foods for children suffering from malnutrition.

Butichi said this year’s World Children’s Day was to celebrate children and renew commitment to their rights, hopes and wellbeing.

He said this year’s theme was a reminder that every child has a right to life, to grow up healthy and free from preventable illnesses, including acute malnutrition, and to fulfil their potential.

“We urge our young people to keep going. The world is waiting for your creative ideas for the nutrition of children right here in Borno. UNICEF will continue to support you,” he said.

Director of Community and Family Health at the Borno State Primary Health Care Development Board, Dr. Abdulwahab Mala, who represented the state at the event, appreciated UNICEF for its support to children in Borno, Adamawa and Yobe states.

He said the Borno State Government recognised the progress made from prevention to management of malnutrition.

“Malnutrition is a scourge and it is possible to deal with it. This collective initiative is a reflection of our bold commitment to child health,” he said.

He commended the governor for creating access to healthcare in many local government areas of the state.

The post Borno youths unveil local food to fight malnutrition appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Abiodun pledges to preserve Ogun’s cultural heritage
description:
Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to promoting cultural tourism, preserving historical heritage and supporting initiatives that would always showcase the state’s tourism potential.
He stated this at the 2026 Oronna Ilaro Festival, according to a stat
content:
Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to promoting cultural tourism, preserving historical heritage and supporting initiatives that would always showcase the state’s tourism potential.

He stated this at the 2026 Oronna Ilaro Festival, according to a statement made available to PUNCH Online on Sunday.

The event was themed ‘Festival of Dawn of New Glory.’

Represented by the Commissioner for Culture and Tourism, Sesan Fagbayi, the governor stated that the event’s theme is a call for collective responsibility, purposeful leadership and renewed commitment to preserving the values and traditions that define the people.

Abiodun said that the theme underscored the need to “translate shared history and cultural pride into meaningful actions that promote unity, economic advancement, youth empowerment and sustainable community development.”

He said his administration is committed to promoting cultural tourism, preserving historical heritage and creating opportunities for the “state’s rich cultural heritage to contribute meaningfully to economic growth, employment generation and overall development of the state.”

The governor also commended the Olu of Ilaro and Paramount Ruler of Yewaland, Oba Kehinde Olugbenle, the Council of Chiefs, festival organisers and other stakeholders for sustaining the important cultural celebration.

He urged the sons and daughters of Yewaland to “embrace the spirit of the festival by promoting culture, tourism, unity, peace, mutual understanding and collective action towards projecting the heritage of Yewaland for the benefit of present and future generations.

“He also called on the people to continue supporting initiatives that preserve historical heritage and create opportunities for cultural traditions to drive economic growth, generate employment and contribute to the overall development of the state.”

In his welcome address, the Chairman of the 2026 Oronna Ilaro Festival Committee, Lekan Asunni, said this year’s theme captured the aspirations of the Ilaro people for renewed hope, cultural renaissance, unity and sustainable development.

“He emphasised the importance of youth engagement in sustaining cultural identity and promoting community development, noting that greater involvement of young people was critical to preventing the gradual extinction of customs and traditions handed down by previous generations.

“In his address, the Olu of Ilaro and Paramount Ruler of Yewaland, Oba (Dr.) Olugbenle, welcomed guests and appreciated the Abiodun-led administration for its unwavering commitment to promoting and preserving the state’s cultural heritage.

“The monarch stressed the importance of intergenerational collaboration in cultural preservation, urging the older generation to continually involve young people in traditional practices and customs to prevent them from going extinct,” the statement read.

The post Abiodun pledges to preserve Ogun’s cultural heritage appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Bayelsa boat tragedy: Tinubu donates N250m as death toll hits 29
description:
President Bola Tinubu on Sunday donated  N250 million to families of victims of Friday’s boat accident in Bayelsa State.
He ordered stricter enforcement of safety standards on inland waterways, as the death toll from the accident rose to 29, with more than 50 survivors.
The accident occurred on Frid
content:
President Bola Tinubu on Sunday donated  N250 million to families of victims of Friday’s boat accident in Bayelsa State.

He ordered stricter enforcement of safety standards on inland waterways, as the death toll from the accident rose to 29, with more than 50 survivors.

The accident occurred on Friday at the Oweikorogha/Otuan River Junction in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area, when a boat carrying scores of mourners travelling to a funeral capsized.

Vice President Kashim Shettima conveyed the President’s position and the donation on Sunday during a condolence visit to Government House, Yenagoa, the state capital.

This is according to a statement signed Sunday by Senior Special Assistant to the Vice President on Media and Communications, Stanley Nkwocha, titled ‘Bayelsa Boat Mishap: President Tinubu Orders Stiffer Waterway Safety Measures.’

Governor Douye Diri, who briefed the Vice President at Government House, attributed the tragedy to an alleged failure by boat operators to observe established safety protocols, describing it as avoidable.

He said the state government had constituted a committee to investigate the immediate and remote causes of the accident.

Shettima said Tinubu had also demanded a thorough investigation into the circumstances of the mishap, including preliminary reports of a possible mechanical fault.

He stated, “We have received preliminary reports concerning the circumstances of this accident, including indications of a possible mechanical failure.

“These reports must be thoroughly investigated by the appropriate authorities.

“We must establish what happened, identify any failures in safety procedures and take the necessary steps to prevent a recurrence.”

The VP described the disaster as an equity issue, arguing that Nigerians who travel by water were entitled to the same standard of protection as those who travel by road or air.

“We cannot accept a situation in which citizens must gamble with their lives simply to move between communities. Geography may determine how people travel, but it must never determine how much protection their lives deserve.

“A Nigerian travelling by boat is entitled to the same concern for safety as one travelling by road or air,” he said.

The VP described the tragedy as carrying “a particular cruelty,” noting that the victims had set out to mourn the dead before death claimed them along the way.

Shettima stated, “Each person lost in those waters had a name, a history, relationships and responsibilities. Somewhere, a family is struggling to understand how someone who left home for a funeral will never walk through that door again.”

He assured the bereaved families that they would receive lasting support from the Federal Government.

“To the families who have lost their loved ones, I will not pretend that time alone will make this pain disappear.

“Our responsibility is to stand with you beyond this visit, beyond these condolences and beyond the days when this tragedy dominates the news,” he said.

Before proceeding to Government House, the VP visited survivors receiving treatment at the Bayelsa Medical University Teaching Hospital, where he consoled patients and assured them of adequate medical care.

Shettima commended the governor for visiting the accident scene and coordinating the state’s response.

He acknowledged the efforts of the National Emergency Management Agency, the Bayelsa State Emergency Management Agency, the Nigerian Red Cross Society, the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, local divers and community volunteers.

Diri announced that the state government had taken responsibility for the medical bills of all survivors and assured bereaved families they would not be abandoned.

On arrival in Yenagoa, Shettima was received by the governor, the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources, Senator Heineken Lokpobiri; the Managing Director of the Niger Delta Development Commission, Dr Samuel Ogbuku; Bayelsa State APC Chairman, Dr Dennis Otiotio; and the Managing Director, Niger Delta River Basin Development Authority, Ebitimi Amgbare, among others.

On Saturday, Tinubu called for a minute of silence in honour of victims of the boat accident during the All Progressives Congress campaign rally in Oyo State.

The President made the announcement while addressing supporters at the rally, where he called for prayers for the repose of the victims’ souls and an end to similar incidents.

The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, also called for an immediate investigation into the remote and direct causes of the fatal boat mishap

Oyetola, in a statement released on Sunday through his media aide, Dr Bolaji Akinola, directed the National Inland Waterways Authority to “conduct a thorough investigation into the incident and submit its report to him.”

Also, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has called on the Federal and Bayelsa State governments to investigate the boat mishap that claimed several lives in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State recently.

He also called for improved safety regulations across the nation’s waterways.

The post Bayelsa boat tragedy: Tinubu donates N250m as death toll hits 29 appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Iran unveils new missile launcher as commanders issue warning to US
description:
Iran has unveiled a new missile launcher as senior military commanders touted the Islamic republic’s capabilities in defiant messages to the United States.



“A launcher capable of firing two liquid-propellant missiles simultaneously was unveiled for the first time,” Iranian state television report
content:
Iran has unveiled a new missile launcher as senior military commanders touted the Islamic republic’s capabilities in defiant messages to the United States.

“A launcher capable of firing two liquid-propellant missiles simultaneously was unveiled for the first time,” Iranian state television reported on Saturday.

State television broadcast footage of Revolutionary Guards chief Ahmad Vahidi and the head of the Guards’ aerospace forces, Majid Mousavi, touring an underground missile base.

The two commanders were shown riding atop a vehicle through long tunnels lined with missiles, launchers and other military equipment.

“The damage suffered by our enemy is only the beginning. We shall witness their humiliation,” said Vahidi, whose Revolutionary Guards form the ideological arm of Iran’s military.

“Our capabilities have grown during the last two conflicts, and our high-performance weaponry can intimidate the enemy,” said Mousavi.

The unveiling comes months into the Middle East war, which broke out on February 28 when US-Israeli strikes killed Iran’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

Iran responded by launching missiles and drones at countries across the region, while militant groups it backs in Lebanon, Yemen and Iraq also entered the conflict.

During the war’s most intense phase, US-Israeli strikes targeted Iran’s missile capabilities and again hit its nuclear sites, though the extent of the damage remains unclear.

Earlier this month, Iran unveiled a new underground missile base housing ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as launchers.

title: Aliyu: ‘No government can function without the media’
description:
By Bianca Iboma-Emefu
Ambassador Dr. Dahiru Aliyu, President of the Nigeria Law Society, has described the media as indispensable to effective governance and nation-building, declaring that no government can function meaningfully without a strong and independent press.
Aliyu made the assertion while
content:
By Bianca Iboma-Emefu

Ambassador Dr. Dahiru Aliyu, President of the Nigeria Law Society, has described the media as indispensable to effective governance and nation-building, declaring that no government can function meaningfully without a strong and independent press.

Aliyu made the assertion while receiving an Award of Excellence in Legal Leadership and Professional Development at the 2026 Global Affairs Magazine Awards (GAMA 2026), held on Friday, November 20, at Eko Hotels and Suites, Victoria Island, Lagos.

Emphasising the media’s critical role in holding institutions accountable and disseminating information, the senior lawyer said journalists make significant sacrifices to ensure that citizens remain informed and society benefits from access to knowledge.

“If you remove the media, to me, that’s no government,” he declared, insisting that the media must be adequately empowered to discharge its responsibilities to society.

Aliyu, who travelled from Abuja to attend the ceremony, said he considered the recognition bigger than his individual achievements, dedicating the award to the Nigerian legal community, members of the Nigeria Law Society and the country at large.

“The award is for the institution, the members, the governing council. It’s for Nigerian lawyers. Because the recognition given to me is not for me alone,” he said.

He added that the honour should be seen as recognition of the collective contributions of legal practitioners to the development of the profession and the nation.

The lawyer also stressed that awards should reflect genuine service, commitment and contributions to society rather than being treated as entitlements.

His remarks brought the relationship between the media, the legal profession and democratic governance into focus, particularly the responsibility of both institutions to promote accountability, protect citizens’ rights and strengthen national development.

The 2026 GAMA awards brought together personalities from different professional fields to recognise contributions to their respective sectors.

Aliyu’s recognition in legal leadership and professional development also highlighted the importance of institutional leadership and the role of the legal profession in strengthening Nigeria’s democratic and professional institutions.

Meanwhile, a Lawyer and philanthropist, Dr. Valentine Mbamalu, was honoured for his humanitarian deeds. He builds homes for widows, award scholarship to their children and equally empower young entrepreneurs.

He recently built two houses for widows and provided ₦20 million in business support to 20 young entrepreneurs as part of his humanitarian interventions aimed at improving livelihoods and addressing economic vulnerabilities.

The interventions, carried out through the Touch of Valentine Foundation, also include the construction of another house for a widow, which is currently ongoing.

Under the youth empowerment programme, each of the 20 beneficiaries received ₦1 million last year to establish or expand their businesses, bringing the total financial support to ₦20 million.

Mbamalu, who was recently honoured with an Award of Excellence by the Global Affairs Magazine Awards (GAMA) for his humanitarian deeds, highlighted some of his interventions while speaking after receiving the recognition.

He said his philanthropic activities were driven by the desire to improve lives rather than the expectation of public recognition or rewards from beneficiaries.

According to him, some beneficiaries have voluntarily returned to share accounts of how the support has improved their circumstances, although the foundation does not compel them to provide feedback.

“There is nothing you do that is not seen. No matter how you think nobody is seeing you, they see what we do in society and the job that we have done, how we have impacted lives,” he said.

Mbamalu, who heads TOV Chambers and chairs TOV Group of Companies, said he was encouraged by the recognition of his humanitarian efforts.

His interventions underscore the importance of targeted private philanthropy in tackling housing insecurity and youth unemployment, particularly through practical support that enables vulnerable women to secure shelter and young people to build sustainable livelihoods.

The post Aliyu: ‘No government can function without the media’ appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Climate deal collapses in chaotic end to COP31
description:
The COP31 climate talks ended in failure Sunday as a contentious deal collapsed over fossil fuels and the summit stretched into record overtime in Turkey.



The final agreement was dramatically rejected in a chaotic finale to a UN climate summit which ran two days over schedule, underscoring the st
content:
The COP31 climate talks ended in failure Sunday as a contentious deal collapsed over fossil fuels and the summit stretched into record overtime in Turkey.

The final agreement was dramatically rejected in a chaotic finale to a UN climate summit which ran two days over schedule, underscoring the strains on diplomacy in an increasingly fractured world.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who urged nations to send fossil fuels “the way of the dinosaurs” during a fiery appearance at COP31, expressed deep dismay as the talks broke down.

“I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands,” the outgoing UN chief said in a statement.

COP31 negotiations chair Chris Bowen, who unsuccessfully sought to broker consensus among nearly 200 nations, conceded he could not overcome what he called “unbridgeable red lines”.

“Unfortunately, we were unable to reach agreement on a cover decision… And that’s disappointing. Very disappointing,” Bowen, who is Australia’s climate minister, told a throng of reporters.

More than 49 hours after the summit was supposed to end, COP31 President and Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum banged the gavel to conclude the marathon talks.

– ‘Greenwash’ –

Bowen said the summit backdrop was “the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory” as soaring energy prices and fallout from the Middle East war complicated the search for unity.

Under pressure to show progress in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal, Bowen sought an overarching “cover decision” to prove countries were still united in tackling the crisis.

But his plan unravelled as familiar fault lines emerged over fossil fuels, with the EU and Saudi Arabia locking horns over the pace of the shift away from coal, oil and gas.

The negotiations stalled as oil-producing states blocked any mention of phasing out fossil fuels in the final deal.

“We will not endorse a cover decision… that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change,” said Ireland’s climate minister, Darragh O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency.

“And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel.”

Panama, Vanuatu and the Marshall Islands also objected and as the deal imploded, COP31 became the longest climate summit on record.

– Falling short –

The outcome revived memories of the failed Copenhagen summit of 2009 and raised fresh doubts about the effectiveness of climate diplomacy.

“It certainly fell short today,” said UN climate chief Simon Stiell, describing progress over the marathon fortnight of negotiations in Antalya as “limited”.

“The world cannot afford a repeat.”

Frustrated by the inertia, countries are pushing ahead outside the COP process.

Around 60 countries joined a first-of-its-kind conference in April on phasing out fossil fuels while several nations at COP31 unveiled their own plans to exit coal, oil and gas.

In a last-ditch bid for compromise, COP31 hosts Turkey and Australia could only muster a veiled reference to fossil fuels in the final text.

But the pact also took fire for retaining a call to expand carbon capture — a costly technology championed by the fossil fuel industry.

“We believe that climate change requires all solutions on the table,” said Mohammad Ayoub, a climate negotiator for oil giant Saudi Arabia.

Facing blowback over the fossil fuels omission, Turkey and Australia tried to rally support behind a global goal to electrify the world economy.

They said “electrification” could cut heat-trapping emissions and bolster energy security but the target was ultimately torpedoed, along with the rest of the doomed Antalya Pact.

– ‘Profound disappointment’ –

Countries lamented a missed opportunity to reinforce the Paris agreement’s 1.5C target, which scientists expect the world to overshoot in a few years as carbon-cutting goals fall short.

The summit also widened fault lines over science, with a fight over the work of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) spilling into the negotiations.

“We are profoundly disappointed by the substance of the cover decision,” said UK climate negotiator Kate Hughes.

“It moves us backwards on the science… It is a lowest common denominator where it should have been, instead, presenting bold collective ambition on climate action.”

As always, the summit laid bare the divide between major polluters driving climate change and smaller nations bearing the brunt of its impact.

Developing nations pushed for a $120 billion target climate goal which disappeared from the failed deal.

The post Climate deal collapses in chaotic end to COP31 appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: La Liga: Barcelona rally from two goals down to beat Villarreal 3-2
description:
Spanish champions Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 on Sunday and restore their three point lead at the top of La Liga.
Barca edged clear of Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, who had pulled level with them on Saturday after beating Celta Vigo.
Two goals inside seven minutes
content:
Spanish champions Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 on Sunday and restore their three point lead at the top of La Liga.

Barca edged clear of Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, who had pulled level with them on Saturday after beating Celta Vigo.

Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou and Barca winger Lamine Yamal missed a first-half penalty.

However, the Catalan giants struck three times in an 11-minute spell in the second half to claim victory.

Gerard Martin and Fermin Lopez pulled Barca level before Pau Navarro’s own goal gave them the three points.

Barca have now won four consecutive matches across all competitions since their Clasico defeat by Real Madrid in October.

“We suffered because we started the game badly, we let in two goals very early. I’ll remember how the team reacted but we have to work to ensure this doesn’t happen again,” Barca midfielder Pedri told DAZN.

“Against a team like this you can’t always turn things around from two down.”

Barcelona coach Hansi Flick hailed his team’s comeback, something they have made a habit of during his reign.

“We made two mistakes and they scored two times… but the reaction that we had was unbelievable,” Flick told reporters.

The hosts were caught snoozing in the early afternoon sunlight and Buchanan fired Villarreal ahead in the fifth minute.

Lopez gave the ball away with a careless pass and Canada international Buchanan produced a perfect sliced effort from distance to send the visitors ahead.

Two minutes later Villarreal doubled their advantage when Oluwaseyi, another Canadian, broke in down the left flank and smashed an effort over Joan Garcia into the roof of the net.

Flick’s side should have pulled one back when Oluwaseyi felled Yamal in the area and a penalty was given after a VAR review.

Yamal took it himself but dragged his effort against the post and wide.

The winger tried to make amends with a burst inside from the wing before half-time but Peter Gulacsi palmed away his cross-shot and the goalkeeper and his defence combined to thwart Eric Garcia on the follow-up.

Quickfire treble –

Barcelona came out invigorated in the second half and quickly dragged themselves back into the match.

Pedri shot wide and Gulacsi saved from Lopez’s low effort before Martin found the net in the 57th minute.

Pedri crossed the ball in from the left for the defender to head home.

Four minutes later Lopez slammed home the second after being teed up by Yamal, and the third was quick to follow.

A clever backheel pass by Yamal fed Eric Garcia, whose cross was bundled into the back of his own net by Navarro.

Substitute Anthony Gordon was denied by Gulacsi and then appealed for a penalty after a bump from Santi Comesana but went down too easily.

Barcelona’s protests on the sidelines were vehement and referee Alejandro Hernandez Hernandez’s report revealed Lopez, who had already been substituted off, was sent off for dissent, but had already walked down the tunnel before he could be shown a red card.

Flick said although he was happy with refereeing in Spain generally, he disliked Hernandez Hernandez.

“We saw which referee was there and we expect it,” said Flick.

“I’m really happy with the referees but with this referee — not.”

Navarro was sent off for a second yellow card in stoppage time as Villarreal, ninth, left frustrated.

“The (first Barca) goal psychologically killed us, they gained confidence, a couple of minutes later they equalised and from there it’s a lot more difficult,” Comesana told DAZN.

Later Sunday, Atletico Madrid, third, visit Getafe among other fixtures.

AFP

title: UBA, police, telcos seek stronger intelligence sharing to tackle digital fraud
description:
Banks, telecommunications operators, regulators and law enforcement agencies have called for stronger intelligence sharing and investment in technology to tackle the growing threat of digital fraud in Nigeria.
They made the call at a panel session organised by United Bank for Africa (UBA) Plc as par
content:
Banks, telecommunications operators, regulators and law enforcement agencies have called for stronger intelligence sharing and investment in technology to tackle the growing threat of digital fraud in Nigeria.

They made the call at a panel session organised by United Bank for Africa (UBA) Plc as part of its 2026 Fraud Awareness Week, themed, “Fraud Dynamics: Staying One Step Ahead.”

The hybrid event, held at UBA’s head office in Lagos on Friday, November 20, brought together industry experts, security agencies, regulators, telecommunications operators, bank executives and other stakeholders to discuss emerging digital fraud threats.

UBA’s Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Oliver Alawuba, represented by the Group Deputy Managing Director, Chukwuma Nweke, said timely intelligence sharing among stakeholders was critical to detecting fraud and protecting customers.

He noted that the growing use of digital platforms for financial transactions had created more opportunities for criminals to exploit weaknesses in banking systems and customer information.

According to him, fraud schemes now range from phishing emails and fake text messages to account takeovers, SIM-related fraud and the abuse of digital banking channels.

“Consider a suspicious SIM change followed by an unusual transfer. The telecommunications provider will see the first warning sign while the bank sees the second. Sharing intelligence promptly can help us effectively act in time to protect customers,” he said.

UBA’s Group Chief Internal Auditor, Eugene Inotu, who hosted the event, said preventing fraud was the responsibility of everyone, urging bank employees to move beyond awareness and take active steps to stop fraudulent activities.

“The best fraud incident is the one we prevent, and not the ones we successfully investigate,” he stated.

He also warned customers against responding to suspicious calls and messages or visiting fake websites designed to impersonate banks.

“We also appeal to customers to always be circumspect when they get calls or suspicious messages from scammers or spoofed websites pretending to represent us or any bank. Kindly ignore and reach us immediately on our verified channels to report such,” he said.

Delivering the keynote address, Managing Director of WSC Technologies Limited, Wemimo Oluwalade, said digital fraud had moved beyond individual transactions to become a wider threat to the survival and operations of businesses.

He explained that a single fraud incident could involve stolen identities, tricking customers into revealing confidential information, compromised devices, accounts used to move stolen money, insider assistance and weak controls by service providers.

“The question we should ask ourselves is: how do we verify what is real? The fraudsters see the entire chain, and they build their design across the blind spots,” he said.

During the panel discussion, moderated by the Manager, Industry Fraud Desk at the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS), Oluwatosin Obadimu, the experts identified human error, insider involvement and SIM swap fraud as major threats to digital banking.

The panel included ACP Ty Mahmud of the Nigeria Police Special Fraud Unit; Revenue Assurance and Fraud Management Manager at Globacom, Sunday Alani; and Chairperson of the Association of Chief Audit Executives of Banks in Nigeria, Aina Amah.

Mahmud said criminals were increasingly exploiting human trust to gain access to financial accounts, adding that internal compromise accounted for about 70 per cent of cases handled by the police’s specialised fraud units.

“In every situation, fraudsters first attack the people, not the system,” he said.

Alani identified SIM swap fraud as a major weakness in digital banking because one-time passwords (OTPs), used to approve transactions, are often sent to customers through their SIM cards.

“If I can swap your SIM, then truly I’m in charge. The OTP that the bank sends to authorise the transaction comes to me,” he explained.

Amah urged financial institutions to invest more in fraud prevention technology, stronger audit systems and skilled security teams, warning against treating such investments as unnecessary costs.

“If you think you are saving cost by not improving your technology, not enhancing your technology team, your audit team, your CISO, you are doing yourself an injustice,” she said.

The panellists commended UBA for sustaining discussions on fraud prevention and agreed that banks, telecommunications operators, regulators and security agencies must work together, share information and strengthen their technology to keep pace with increasingly sophisticated fraudsters.

UBA operates in 20 African countries and several international markets, including the United Kingdom, the United States, France and the United Arab Emirates. The bank says it serves more than 45 million customers globally.

title: Army Intensifies Offensive In Katsina, Kills Terrorists, Recovers Motorcycles
description: Troops of the 17 Brigade, Nigerian Army, Joint Task Force (North West), Operation FANSAN YANMA, have intensified the offensive against terrorist groups in Katsina State, neutralising suspected terrorists, recovering motorcycles and dismantling criminal hideouts during coordinated clearance and fight
content:
Troops of the 17 Brigade, Nigerian Army, Joint Task Force (North West), Operation FANSAN YANMA, have intensified the offensive against terrorist groups in Katsina State, neutralising suspected terrorists, recovering motorcycles and dismantling criminal hideouts during coordinated clearance and fighting patrol operations across Sabuwa, Musawa and Malumfashi Local Government Areas.

The operations, conducted between November 18 and 19, 2026, formed part of the military’s ongoing efforts to deny terrorists freedom of movement and restore security in communities affected by banditry and other criminal activities.

According to the Nigerian Army, troops of Combat Team 3, supported by the 17 Brigade Strike Force, launched a clearance operation on November 19 against terrorist enclaves on the outskirts of Madachi Village in Sabuwa Local Government Area.

The troops reportedly came under fire from the terrorists shortly after making contact but responded with superior firepower, killing three suspected terrorists and recovering motorcycles abandoned during the encounter.

No casualties were recorded among the troops.

In a separate operation the same day, troops of the 83 Battalion, working alongside personnel from various Forward Operating Bases, the Administrative Company in Malumfashi and local hunters, carried out fighting patrols to Tsabe Village in Musawa Local Government Area and Tsamiyan Maigoro in Malumfashi Local Government Area following intelligence on the activities of a notorious terrorist kingpin, Rabe Rajaja.

During the operation, the troops engaged the terrorists at a deserted settlement, forcing them to flee with gunshot wounds while abandoning a motorcycle, which was recovered.

Troops also recovered farm produce allegedly exploited by the terrorists and have continued pursuit operations to track down the fleeing suspects.

The Army said the offensive had since been expanded, with troops of the 17 Brigade Strike Force and Combat Team 3 sustaining clearance operations around Madachi, Dungun Muazu and Dankolo forests in Sabuwa Local Government Area.

The operations featured coordinated dawn assaults, artillery bombardments on identified terrorist camps and the deployment of blocking forces along likely escape routes to intercept fleeing criminals.

Meanwhile, Commander of the 17 Brigade, Brigadier General Ishaya Ibrahim, undertook operational assessment visits to Forward Operating Bases in Mabai and Faskari on November 20 and 21 to evaluate troops’ combat readiness, operational effectiveness and welfare.

During the visits, the brigade commander received operational briefings, inspected military equipment and interacted with personnel, urging them to maintain discipline, professionalism and a high level of operational preparedness while addressing issues relating to promotion, uniforms and military kitting.

At FOB Faskari, Brigadier General Ibrahim also met with local hunters and vigilante groups, encouraging them to sustain the supply of credible intelligence and deepen collaboration with security agencies, while cautioning them against acts of hostility towards law-abiding citizens.

The commander also visited troops deployed at Machika to assess their operational posture as part of ongoing efforts to strengthen the Brigade’s capacity to confront emerging security threats across its area of responsibility.

In a statement issued on Sunday, the Acting Assistant Director, Army Public Relations, 17 Brigade, Nigerian Army, Captain Abayomi Adisa, reaffirmed the commitment of troops under Operation FANSAN YANMA to sustaining aggressive operations against terrorists and other criminal elements through enhanced collaboration with local security stakeholders.

He said the military remains resolute in its determination to restore lasting peace and security across Katsina State.

title: Climate talks collapse as COP31 ends without agreement
description:
The COP31 climate talks ended in failure on Sunday as a contentious deal collapsed over fossil fuels and the summit stretched into record overtime in Turkey.
The final agreement was dramatically rejected in a chaotic finale to a UN climate summit which ran two days over schedule, underscoring the st
content:
The COP31 climate talks ended in failure on Sunday as a contentious deal collapsed over fossil fuels and the summit stretched into record overtime in Turkey.

The final agreement was dramatically rejected in a chaotic finale to a UN climate summit which ran two days over schedule, underscoring the strains on diplomacy in an increasingly fractured world.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who urged nations to send fossil fuels “the way of the dinosaurs” during a fiery appearance at COP31, expressed deep dismay as the talks broke down.

“I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands,” the outgoing UN chief said in a statement.

COP31 negotiations chair Chris Bowen, who unsuccessfully sought to broker consensus among nearly 200 nations, conceded he could not overcome what he called “unbridgeable red lines”.

“Unfortunately, we were unable to reach agreement on a cover decision… And that’s disappointing. Very disappointing,” Bowen, who is Australia’s climate minister, told a throng of reporters.

More than 49 hours after the summit was supposed to end, COP31 President and Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum banged the gavel to conclude the marathon talks.

‘Greenwash’

Bowen said the summit backdrop was “the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory” as soaring energy prices and fallout from the Middle East war complicated the search for unity.

Under pressure to show progress in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal, Bowen sought an overarching “cover decision” to prove countries were still united in tackling the crisis.

But his plan unravelled as familiar fault lines emerged over fossil fuels, with the EU and Saudi Arabia locking horns over the pace of the shift away from coal, oil and gas.

The negotiations stalled as oil-producing states blocked any mention of phasing out fossil fuels in the final deal.

“We will not endorse a cover decision… that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change,” said Ireland’s climate minister, Darragh O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency.

“And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel.”

Panama, Vanuatu and the Marshall Islands also objected and as the deal imploded, COP31 became the longest climate summit on record.

Falling short –

The outcome revived memories of the failed Copenhagen summit of 2009 and raised fresh doubts about the effectiveness of climate diplomacy.

“It certainly fell short today,” said UN climate chief Simon Stiell, describing progress over the marathon fortnight of negotiations in Antalya as “limited”.

“The world cannot afford a repeat.”

Frustrated by the inertia, countries are pushing ahead outside the COP process.

Around 60 countries joined a first-of-its-kind conference in April on phasing out fossil fuels while several nations at COP31 unveiled their own plans to exit coal, oil and gas.

In a last-ditch bid for compromise, COP31 hosts Turkey and Australia could only muster a veiled reference to fossil fuels in the final text.

But the pact also took fire for retaining a call to expand carbon capture — a costly technology championed by the fossil fuel industry.

“We believe that climate change requires all solutions on the table,” said Mohammad Ayoub, a climate negotiator for oil giant Saudi Arabia.

Facing blowback over the fossil fuels omission, Turkey and Australia tried to rally support behind a global goal to electrify the world economy.

They said “electrification” could cut heat-trapping emissions and bolster energy security but the target was ultimately torpedoed, along with the rest of the doomed Antalya Pact.

‘Profound disappointment’ –

Countries lamented a missed opportunity to reinforce the Paris agreement’s 1.5C target, which scientists expect the world to overshoot in a few years as carbon-cutting goals fall short.

The summit also widened fault lines over science, with a fight over the work of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) spilling into the negotiations.

“We are profoundly disappointed by the substance of the cover decision,” said UK climate negotiator Kate Hughes.

“It moves us backwards on the science… It is a lowest common denominator where it should have been, instead, presenting bold collective ambition on climate action.”

As always, the summit laid bare the divide between major polluters driving climate change and smaller nations bearing the brunt of its impact.

Developing nations pushed for a $120 billion target climate goal which disappeared from the failed deal.

AFP

The post Climate talks collapse as COP31 ends without agreement appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Nigeria Backs Infantino For Re-Election As CAF Announces Major Financial Boost, New U-17 Women’s Tourney
description: Nigeria has officially thrown its weight behind FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election ahead of the upcoming March 2027 polls.President Bola Tinubu announced the country’s endorsement during the 48th CAF Ordinary General Assembly hosted in Abuja.The crucial endorsement pos
content:
Nigeria has officially thrown its weight behind FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election ahead of the upcoming March 2027 polls.

President Bola Tinubu announced the country’s endorsement during the 48th CAF Ordinary General Assembly hosted in Abuja.

The crucial endorsement positions Nigeria firmly behind Infantino as he heads toward the vote scheduled for March 18, 2027, in Rabat, Morocco, during the 77th FIFA Congress.

Infantino faces challenges from French Football Federation President Philippe Diallo and Japan Football Association honorary president Kohzo Tashima for the 2027–2031 term.

Represented at the assembly by the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, President Tinubu reaffirmed Nigeria’s strong confidence in the Swiss administrator’s leadership.

Echoing this stance, National Sports Commission Chairman Shehu Dikko formally conveyed the Federal Government’s resolution to the assembly, calling on fellow African member associations to rally behind Infantino’s candidacy in the collective interest of the continent’s football development.

In a separate landmark development at the assembly, Confederation of African Football (CAF) President Patrice Motsepe announced a significant 33 per cent increase in annual financial support for all 54 Member Associations.

Under the revised framework, yearly grants to each national association will jump from $525,000 to $700,000, injecting an extra $175,000 into local development.

Additionally, the six CAF zonal unions will see a 20 per cent funding increase, with allocations rising from $750,000 to $900,000 each to bolster administrative structures and grassroots competitions.

Adding to the wave of progressive updates, CAF officially approved the introduction of the CAF U-17 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations.

According to CAF, the newly minted tournament is designed to expand the international pathway for young female footballers, offering them vital competitive exposure and nurturing the next generation of global talent across the continent.
