title: Ekiti farmers hail FG over flood relief intervention
description:
The All Farmers Association of Nigeria has praised the Federal Government for coming to the aid of 4,000 members whose farms were recently destroyed by flooding.
The AFAN Chairman in Ekiti State, Mr Sunday Adekogbon, thanked the FG, the National Agricultural Development Fund and the state government
content:
The All Farmers Association of Nigeria has praised the Federal Government for coming to the aid of 4,000 members whose farms were recently destroyed by flooding.

The AFAN Chairman in Ekiti State, Mr Sunday Adekogbon, thanked the FG, the National Agricultural Development Fund and the state government for supporting the affected farmers with farm inputs to enable them to pick up after the disaster.

The FG had, through the agency, at an event tagged ‘NADF intervention for flood-affected farmers in Ekiti State’ on Saturday, distributed emergency farm inputs to 4,000 smallholder farmers affected by flooding in the state to help restore their farms and improve food production.

Items distributed to the affected farmers include 4,000 bags of NPK fertiliser, 4,000 bags of urea, 2,800 bags of rice seeds, 1,200 bags of maize seeds, 4,000 bottles of pre-plant chemicals, 4,000 bottles of pre-emergence herbicides, 4,000 bottles of early post-emergence herbicides and 4,000 bottles of insecticide.

The AFAN chairman urged beneficiaries not to sell the inputs, but to use them for their intended agricultural purposes.

Adekogbon, while appreciating NADF for the gesture, said, “The support will enable farmers to contribute more effectively to food security.”

The affected farmers, represented by Mr Ojo Falana, expressed appreciation for the intervention.

Falana said, “We appreciate the NADF for this gesture, and we promise to use the agricultural inputs judiciously to improve our farming activities and achieve the programme’s objectives.”

Speaking earlier, NADF Executive Secretary and Chief Executive Officer, Mr Muhammed Ibrahim, represented by the Head of Strategy, Planning, Evaluation, Monitoring and Learning, Mrs Adebanke Fajana, urged the beneficiaries to “use the materials for the purpose meant to justify government’s investment,” saying the gesture was to ensure recovery.

Speaking on the essence of the intervention, Ibrahim said, “For many farmers, this loss is threatening not only the current production cycle, but also the ability to prepare for the next production cycle.

“Without timely intervention, this disaster can easily become a crisis that lasts for seasons. We are here to ensure that recovery is done.”

Ibrahim added, “We want you to see renewed opportunity. We encourage you to see farms being restored to productivity. We encourage you to see families regaining their livelihood, and we see communities strengthened against failure shocks. Above all, we see a pathway towards more resilient and food-secure Nigeria. ”

The NADF boss said the intervention aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s vision “to protect livelihoods, strengthen food security and build a resilient agricultural economy under the Renewed Hope Agenda.”

The Special Adviser to Ekiti State Governor Biodun Oyebanji on Agriculture, Boluwade Ebenezer, said the intervention would restore the affected farmers’ confidence, boost agricultural production and strengthen food security in Ekiti State and Nigeria.

The post Ekiti farmers hail FG over flood relief intervention appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: Nigeria needs reset, Makinde insists
description:
Allied Peoples Movement ( APM) presidential candidate, Governor Seyi Makinde, has insisted that Nigeria needs a reset, so that the citizens can feel the impact of government.
Makinde, while speaking to journalists, after he attended  Sunday service at the Headquarters of Dunamis International Gospel
content:
Allied Peoples Movement ( APM) presidential candidate, Governor Seyi Makinde, has insisted that Nigeria needs a reset, so that the citizens can feel the impact of government.

Makinde, while speaking to journalists, after he attended  Sunday service at the Headquarters of Dunamis International Gospel Centre in Abuja, said he was in the 2027 presidential contest so as to return the country to its glorious era.

According to him,  the spate of insecurity, poverty, hunger and  poor infrastructure are evidence that Nigeria is not working and requires a redirection.

He charged as many Nigerians, who believed that the country is not working to embrace his Reset Nigeria Agenda, noting that “my message still is if Nigeria is not working for you then join me to press the reset button.

“If it is working for you okay, keep doing what you are doing but I know Nigeria is not working.”

Makinde also called on Nigerians to continue to pray for the country, ahead of the 2027 general election, stating that “when I came out to declare to run for president, what I have asked people to do is pray; one, that God should show mercy onto this country.

“If things are not working well, you know, you can’t take this spiritual aspect away from physical …Christian brothers and sisters. don’t even pray for me to be president of Nigeria, but pray that God’s will and God’s will alone be done.”

Makinde, who also also attended service at the Nongo u Kristu u i Ser u sha Tar (NKST), a Tiv phrase for “The Universal Reformed Christian Church” at Mabushi, on Sunday, recalled how Nigeria ‘happened’ to him in a positive way through his sojourn as a young man from Oyo State to Rivers state in the 1990s, before eventually returning home to work and  becoming the governor in 2019.

The Resident Pastor, NKST, Reverend Basil Orkpe, while receiving the APM candidate,   told him that he was on a mission to fulfill God’s purpose for Nigeria.

According to him, “without a shadow of a doubt, this great movement that God Himself has orchestrated has a purpose.

“Many people may have said, ‘Stop this, concentrate on something else’, but your heart’s desire and your cry to Jesus Christ have been that you would be able to serve this nation and, by extension, the rest of the world, and bring relief to the suffering of the people of this great land”.

The cleric implored  Makinde not to listen to voices discouraging him from fulfilling the purpose of God, noting “Sir, never to listen to or heed the cries of the crowd. Rather, keep your mind focused on one goal, the goal of salvaging this nation.”

Ladoja, in a statement issued by his media aide, Chief Adeola Oloko, in Ibadan, Oyo State, on Sunday, appreciat
content:
The Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, has commended President Bola Tinubu over his promise to reopen the defunct Leyland factory and other moribund facilities across the country.

Ladoja, in a statement issued by his media aide, Chief Adeola Oloko, in Ibadan, Oyo State, on Sunday, appreciated the President for infrastructure development projects across the country, particularly in the South-West.

Ladoja said, “The projects in question are works in progress. It is when they are completed that you can begin to make fresh requests for new ones.

“Let me express gratitude to the President over his promise to reopen the defunct Leyland Motor Assembly, Ibadan; Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode Road and Ibadan-Oyo Road, among others. Many of the roads had fallen into a terrible state of disrepair and exposed commuters to untold suffering.”

The PUNCH reports that Tinubu, during his visit to Ibadan for a political rally on Saturday, promised to reopen the Leyland factory following the signing of a memorandum of understanding with a Chinese firm.

He said, “For Oyo State, we have just signed a Memorandum of Understanding with a Chinese firm to reopen Leyland factory in Ibadan.

“We are re-opening it to produce public transport and automobile assembly plant to them. We will continue to bring industry. You will see it and I guarantee you an improvement in electricity supply. Joseph Tegbe is really working hard with his team.”

It will also be recalled that the Leyland assembly plant was established in the 1970s in Ibadan as a joint venture between the Nigerian government and British Leyland to assemble commercial vehicles and build local technical capacity.

Built on a 125-acre site, with approximately 55,000 square metres of buildings, the £37m plant was officially opened in March 1979 by British Leyland President, Lord Stokes.

As Nigeria’s economy faced severe headwinds and assembly operations struggled, the original Leyland Nigeria firm eventually ceased production and went into receivership.

Speaking further, the Olubadan said in the statement, “The President, Asiwaju Tinubu, arrived to a warm reception from members of the state Council of Obas and Chiefs before proceeding to Mapo for the campaign rally.

“The scores of monarchs, drawn from Ibadan, Ibarapa, Oyo, Ogbomoso, and Oke-Ogun zones one and two, received the President at the Ladoke Akintola Airport, Ibadan, at about 1:30 pm to reaffirm the position of the South-West’s leading monarchs at their recent meeting in Ibadan on his re-election.”

He contended that just as a man’s gifts make room for him, so do the works of his hands.

According to the statement, “Apart from the Olubadan, many monarchs in attendance were the Soun of Ogbomoso, Eleruwa of Eruwa, Aseyin of Iseyin, Okere of Saki, Onpetu of Ijeru, Olugbon of Orile-Igbon, members of the Olubadan-in-Council, Onigboho of Igboho, Alagere of Ago-Are, Olokaka of Okaka, Ona Onibode of Igboho, Akibio of Ilora, Olu of Fiditi, Alajawa of Ajaawa and a host of other prominent traditional rulers in the state.”

title: 2027: Akwa Ibom opposition to vote Tinubu – Akpabio
description:
As Tompolo donates 31 campaign vehicles


President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, has revealed that the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the state and other opposition political parties have formed a coalition that will vote massively to reelect President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in the 2027 president
content:
• As Tompolo donates 31 campaign vehicles

President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, has revealed that the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the state and other opposition political parties have formed a coalition that will vote massively to reelect President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election.

This is just as the High Chief Government Ekpemupolo-led PBAT Door-to-Door Movement inaugurated its Akwa Ibom State chapter and executives with a donation of 31 campaign vehicles, speakers and other campaign materials.

Speaking at the event held at the Ibom Hall Ground in Uyo, on Sunday, the Senate President declared that the entire state was for Tinubu and the APC because the people of the state were already enjoying the Tinubu Presidency through programmes like NELFUND, CreditCorp, presidential CNG initiative, coastal roads, payment of salaries and other economic policies which were stabilising the economy.

Likening the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement to the Peanut Brigade of the United States of America, through which a largely unpopular Jimmy Carter became president, he said history had taught that the destiny of nations is not only determined in the corridors of power, which underscores the importance of the work the Movement was doing.

“Thank you to the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement for recognising that true democracy must get to the homes of the people, that less magnificent doors like doors of farmer, widows, students, those who were struggling but whose hopes have been renewed, matter,” Akpabio said.

Continuing, he noted that the story of the 2027 election would be told by families who open their doors to the movement, students that have benefitted from initiatives like NELFUND, bursaries paid by the state government as a result of increased federal allocation, and workers who are no longer owed salaries, among others, emphasising that democracy must not become so fascinated by the great doors that it forgets the humble doors of the masses.

Akpabio reiterated the support of the National Assembly for President Tinubu, saying he requires such support to stay focused on the job he is doing.

Earlier, Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, who was represented by the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services, Chief Kestin Pondi, said the donation of the vehicles was to support the state organs of the APC in the campaign for Tinubu.

He reeled out some of the policies and reforms of the Tinubu administration and pointed out that such reforms often come with hardship but added that the pains abate once the reforms begin to yield result, which was already happening in the case of Nigeria.

Tompolo noted that reforms in other countries which many Nigerians admire, did not happen within a four-year tenure but the outcome of years of continuity by various governments, emphasising the need for Tinubu to be reelected to complete his two terms and consolidate on the ongoing reforms.

Also in a remark, the National Coordinator of the Movement, Sunday Asuku, urged the people to vote massively for Tinubu and other APC candidates, emphasising that the opposition does not mean well for the country and it shows in the antecedents of some of those contesting elections.

He pointed out that with the support of a cooperative National Assembly, led by Akpabio, President Tinubu had been able to give assent to bills such as the NELFUND Act and other bills like local government autonomy and state police which will soon be signed into law.

“We must follow a visionary leader working to change the face of Nigeria,” he stated.

title: Soldiers repel bandits’ attacks on Benue communities
description:
Suspected armed bandits have attacked Mbatian community in Dyom, as well as Atuluku, Tse Kasua and Amachigh villages in Ukum Local Government Area of Benue State.
The military reportedly responded swiftly, rescuing two abducted women.
According to a community source, the attacks occurred between Fri
content:
Suspected armed bandits have attacked Mbatian community in Dyom, as well as Atuluku, Tse Kasua and Amachigh villages in Ukum Local Government Area of Benue State.

The military reportedly responded swiftly, rescuing two abducted women.

According to a community source, the attacks occurred between Friday night and Saturday morning.

The resident said, “The attack occurred Friday night and Saturday morning. They also attacked military personnel at their duty posts, but luckily, the military repelled them.

“The two women were kidnapped by the armed men in Mbatian community but were eventually rescued by the military, who intervened quickly to avert a major disaster in the affected communities,” the source said.

Confirming the incident, the Chairman of Ukum LGA, Jonathan Modi, commended officers and men of the Nigerian Army operating in the area for their gallantry, swift response and commitment to protecting lives and property.

The chairman, in a statement released by his Special Assistant on Media and Public Communications, Samuel Atsua, said the commendation followed the successful repulsion of the attempted attack on Mbatian community in Dyom and subsequent attacks on other villages.

The statement read in part, “The prompt intervention of the Nigerian Army was instrumental in preventing what could have resulted in a devastating loss of lives and destruction of property. Particularly commendable was the rescue of two women reportedly abducted by the suspected attackers from the affected communities.”

The chairman described the military’s intervention as a demonstration of courage, professionalism and dedication to national service, adding that the presence and operational commitment of security personnel remained critical to restoring confidence among residents and protecting vulnerable communities.

In the statement, Modi said he visited the military base at Dyom, where he met with the Commander of the newly established 11 Brigade, Gboko, Brigadier General Akinkunmi Odubiyi, and other personnel.

He said, “I assure the Nigerian Army that the Ukum Local Government administration remains committed to providing the necessary support and cooperation to strengthen security operations and ensure the protection of lives, property and territorial integrity of the area.”

The chairman urged the military and other security agencies not to relent in their efforts, “particularly in sustaining their presence and responding promptly to security threats across vulnerable communities.”

Efforts to get a reaction from the spokesperson for the state police command, DSP Peter Aondongu, were unsuccessful as of the time of filling this report.

title: CBN seeks greater Nigerian role in ECOWAS monetary union
description: The Central Bank of Nigeria has called for greater Nigerian representation in the governance of the proposed Economic Community of West African States Monetary Union, insisting that countries making substantial financial contributions should have corresponding influence over decisions affecting the
content:
The Central Bank of Nigeria has called for greater Nigerian representation in the governance of the proposed Economic Community of West African States Monetary Union, insisting that countries making substantial financial contributions should have corresponding influence over decisions affecting the regional currency.

The CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, made the call on Friday at the ministerial session of the sixth Presidential Task Force Meeting on the ECOWAS Single Currency Programme in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire.

His position comes as West African countries intensify preparations for the phased introduction of the ECO single currency in 2027.

A statement issued by the CBN on Sunday read, “The Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, Mr Olayemi Cardoso, has called for equity, fairness and proportional representation in the governance structure of the proposed ECOWAS Monetary Union.

“He stressed that while regional solidarity and respect for the sovereign equality of member states must remain fundamental principles of the Union, these should be appropriately balanced with the relative financial commitments, responsibilities and risks borne by individual member states, particularly in determining participation in decision-making and governance.”

Cardoso argued that the governance structure must reflect the economic importance, financial commitments and risks borne by participating countries.

“While bigger economies continue to take up the burden, they should also be considered to play a significant role because of the risk and systemic importance they have in the sub-region,” Cardoso said.

“Above all, such economies need to defend the huge contribution they make before their respective parliaments and the civil society. Where obligations are shared but influence is not, arrangements may be agreed, but their long-term sustainability may be difficult to guarantee,” he added.

The governor maintained that regional solidarity and the sovereign equality of member states should remain fundamental principles of the proposed union but must be balanced against their financial responsibilities.

He explained that Nigeria’s position was not motivated by a desire to dominate other countries but by its responsibilities as the region’s largest economy and a major contributor to the monetary integration project.

According to him, Nigeria would commit substantial financial resources, foreign reserves and institutional capital to the proposed union, making it necessary to align governance participation with financial exposure.

Cardoso warned that decisions on the location of monetary institutions, leadership appointments and the allocation of authority would have long-term implications for the credibility and sustainability of the ECO.

“The decisions we take today will shape the future of the Union for decades to come,” he told delegates.

“They will influence its credibility in the eyes of investors and development partners, its legitimacy in the eyes of our citizens, and the confidence of Member States that their commitments are being matched by a meaningful voice within the institutions they are helping to build.”

He reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to the ECOWAS Monetary Cooperation Programme, citing its financial contributions, technical support and compromises made to promote regional consensus.

“Nigeria has and will continue to demonstrate solidarity and fairness, respecting the sovereignty of other member states. We remain fully committed to the successful establishment of the ECO and to a Monetary Union that is credible, sustainable and beneficial to all Member States,” Cardoso said.

He urged participating countries to negotiate with openness and mutual respect, warning against arrangements that impose substantial obligations on countries without giving them meaningful participation in governance.

The latest discussions follow years of delays in the proposed common currency, which is intended to deepen regional economic integration, facilitate cross-border transactions and reduce monetary fragmentation.

In July 2026, ECOWAS leaders reaffirmed their commitment to introducing the ECO in 2027, agreeing that implementation would begin with countries meeting the required macroeconomic convergence criteria.

The phased approach means that not every member state will necessarily adopt the currency at the same time. Countries that are not initially ready are expected to receive support to participate later.

The convergence requirements include conditions on inflation, fiscal deficits and monetary stability, intended to ensure that participating economies can operate under a common monetary framework.

Cardoso maintained that a sustainable monetary union must give every participating country a meaningful stake in its success while ensuring that financial responsibilities and decision-making powers are fairly distributed.

The post CBN seeks greater Nigerian role in ECOWAS monetary union appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Fire razes Plateau school, residents suspect bandits
description:
The Government Secondary School, Masharkut, in Butura District of Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State, has been burnt down following a fire outbreak on Sunday afternoon.
The Chairman of Bokkos Local Government Area, Amalau Samuel Amalau, confirmed the incident to PUNCH Online in Jos, the s
content:
The Government Secondary School, Masharkut, in Butura District of Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State, has been burnt down following a fire outbreak on Sunday afternoon.

The Chairman of Bokkos Local Government Area, Amalau Samuel Amalau, confirmed the incident to PUNCH Online in Jos, the state capital, when contacted on Sunday.

“It’s true that the school building was set ablaze. It happened today,” the chairman said.

Asked whether it was terrorists who set the building ablaze, Amalau said the cause of the fire and those responsible could not yet be ascertained.

“How will I know? We only saw the school on fire. We cannot ascertain for now what it is and who is responsible. It happened today,” he said.

The incident reportedly caused panic among residents of the community after smoke was sighted rising from the school premises shortly after church service.

Some members of the community have, however, blamed the fire incident on bandits who they said have been operating in the area.

A resident, Daniel Bwehfa, said residents initially noticed smoke coming from the school before discovering, about 30 minutes later, that the building was on fire.

According to him, the incident raised concerns among residents, who reportedly suspected that the school premises had been used as a temporary shelter by some individuals.

Bwehfa alleged that some suspected bandits had been using the school premises as a sleeping place, claiming that people were often seen gathering within the compound in the evenings.

He, however, did not provide further details about the identities of those allegedly seen around the school or establish whether they were responsible for the fire.

“Some strangers whom we suspect to be bandits have been coming to that school. We don’t know their mission. This has been a source of concern to community members. If they are not the people who set the school on fire, who else might have done that ?” Bwelfa wondered.

The latest incident has heightened concerns over the safety of public institutions and educational facilities in communities affected by insecurity in parts of Bokkos LGA.

Efforts to reach security operatives for confirmation, including the Spokesperson for the Plateau State Police Command, Alabo Alfred, were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report.

title: 2027: Obi endorses tech platform for election monitoring
description:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress for the 2027 election, Peter Obi, has endorsed SmartBallot, a technology platform designed to support grassroots mobilisation, civic engagement and election monitoring.
Obi urged supporters and candidates of the party to register on the p
content:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress for the 2027 election, Peter Obi, has endorsed SmartBallot, a technology platform designed to support grassroots mobilisation, civic engagement and election monitoring.

Obi urged supporters and candidates of the party to register on the platform and explore its tools for organising communities, coordinating voters and polling unit agents, and monitoring elections.

The former Anambra State governor made the call in a statement posted on his X handle on Sunday.

“I am pleased to endorse SmartBallot (http://smartballotapp.com), a platform developed to facilitate grassroots mobilisation, civic engagement, and election monitoring.

“I urge our supporters and NDC candidates to register on SmartBallot and examine how its tools can assist them in organizing their communities, coordinating voters and polling unit agents, expanding grassroots engagement, and supporting transparent election monitoring,” he wrote.

He said, “Through the effective use of technology and collective action, we can reinforce our democratic institutions and help ensure that every vote is counted.”

The NDC candidate added that credible elections required preparation, active participation and peaceful vigilance.

“Let us make full use of every available resource to create a more organised, engaged, and empowered electorate,” he said.

SmartBallot is a civic technology platform that groups users by polling unit, ward, local government area and state.

It enables communication, voter coordination and observation activities. On election day, agents can upload result sheets from polling units, allowing users to track reported figures alongside official processes.

The platform stresses that it is not an official electoral body and does not replace the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Its public-election features are limited to lawful civic engagement, voter education, voluntary mobilisation, community organisation and election observation.

Obi, who contested the 2023 presidential election on the Labour Party platform, is the NDC’s standard-bearer for the 2027 general elections.

The endorsement comes as political parties and civic groups intensify preparations for the polls, with renewed focus on technology-driven tools to improve transparency and participation.

title: ‎Universities must measure success by capability, not certificates – Prof. Okonkwo
description:
‎…pledges scholarships at AUN
‎By Faheem Lawal
‎The Executive Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Prof. Obiora Okonkwo, has said that a tertiary institution should measure its success by the capabilities it builds in students, not by the certificates it hands out.
‎Prof. Okonkwo, who presented a pa
content:
‎…pledges scholarships at AUN

‎By Faheem Lawal

‎The Executive Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Prof. Obiora Okonkwo, has said that a tertiary institution should measure its success by the capabilities it builds in students, not by the certificates it hands out.

‎Prof. Okonkwo, who presented a paper as the guest lecturer at the American University of Nigeria’s (AUN) 2026 Founder’s Day Lecture in Yola on Saturday, with theme: “Purposeful Education and the 21st-Century University: Leadership, Innovation and Social Responsibility,” said that beyond certificates, a degree is only a starting point.

‎In his paper, he said that education is not an end in itself but a transformative process, and warned that paper qualifications can be mistaken for competence.

“A certificate may confirm the completion of a programme, but it cannot, by itself, guarantee the capacity to diagnose a problem, communicate a solution, collaborate effectively, learn independently or exercise sound judgment under uncertainty. It is about gaining the knowledge that will take you to a higher place.

‎“Students must come to understand that education is not about getting certificates. What you earn from this school should not only be enough for you to succeed as an individual, but should also be useful to society. The goal should be to produce a complete education and a good citizen who can contribute to the development of the economy and of Nigeria as a whole,” he said.

‎He called on students to be employers as well as job seekers, saying: “The measure of your education will not ultimately be determined by the prestige of your certificates or the positions you occupy, but by the value you create, the problems you solve, the opportunities you generate, and the lives you improve. The world does not merely need graduates who understand its problems; it needs graduates who can imagine, design, and implement solutions to them.”

‎Okonkwo acknowledged that AUN is an international school offering an international curriculum, but said that status should be put to local use. He said he had not expected the institution to be so far along in the practices he was about to describe.

“We should be able to adapt its presence to northeastern Nigeria. The opposition between ‘international’ and ‘local’ is ultimately false, as global excellence without local relevance can become institutional display,” he said.

He also addressed the region’s reputation, saying he had heard that many people held the wrong impression of the institution because of its location, and he rejected that view. Okonkwo praised the university’s practices and said he would back them with action.

“I am happy to be here. I can see that this is a place many people have a wrong impression of because of its location. I am very glad to see that all of these things are already in practice here, so I commend them. I can tell you and everyone listening that next year I will send some students here on scholarship,” he said.

Okonkwo commended AUN’s founder, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, whom he described as a visionary and an outstanding institution builder. He noted that the former Vice President’s role in the institution transcends those of an ordinary founder. Okonkwo also marked the founder’s recent milestone and prayed that he would live many more years, and in great vitality and vibrancy.

‎He ended his lecture by stating that the university’s future depends on whether it can carry its founding idea forward. “Yola is not peripheral to the world of knowledge. It is a site from which knowledge can be created, tested, shared and transformed.”

The post ‎Universities must measure success by capability, not certificates – Prof. Okonkwo appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Amnesty International demands probe of Emir of Daura over sexual assault allegations
description:
Amnesty International Nigeria has called on the authorities to immediately investigate allegations of sexual assault against the 92-year-old Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, following an incident involving a female foreign tourist at his palace in Katsina State.







The human rights organisation
content:
Amnesty International Nigeria has called on the authorities to immediately investigate allegations of sexual assault against the 92-year-old Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, following an incident involving a female foreign tourist at his palace in Katsina State.

The human rights organisation made the call in a statement published on its X platform on Sunday.

Amnesty International said viral videos shared by the alleged survivor showed what it described as attempts by the emir to sexually violate the visitor despite her resistance.

The organisation said the tourist alleged that the emir touched her inappropriately during her visit to the Daura Emir’s Palace.

Condemning the alleged conduct, Amnesty International urged the Katsina State Government and the Nigeria Police Force to immediately commence a transparent and independent investigation into the incident.

It specifically called on Governor Dikko Radda and the police to ensure that the emir is held accountable for the alleged attempted rape through a fair trial, while ruling out the death penalty.

“The Nigerian authorities must immediately and effectively investigate strong allegations of sexual assault on a female foreign tourist by the 92-year-old Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk,” the organisation said.

Amnesty International said the incident presented an opportunity for the authorities to demonstrate that nobody was above the law in Nigeria.

It also expressed concern over what it described as the normalisation of rape and sexual violence in the country, alleging that such offences were frequently committed with impunity.

The organisation urged relevant authorities to ensure that the allegations were thoroughly investigated and that appropriate legal action followed.

title: Oyo, police warn NURTW against violence
description: The Oyo State Government and the state police command, on Sunday, warned the National Union of Road Transport Workers against violence over the Court of Appeal judgment, saying any attempt to take over public motor parks on Monday represents a clear misinterpretation of the court’s decision and has
content:
The Oyo State Government and the state police command, on Sunday, warned the National Union of Road Transport Workers against violence over the Court of Appeal judgment, saying any attempt to take over public motor parks on Monday represents a clear misinterpretation of the court’s decision and has no basis in law.

While assuring all residents, commuters, visitors, investors and travellers that the state remains peaceful and secure, the government and the police further warned against any act of violence, intimidation, self-help or unlawful takeover of public facilities by any individual or group, regardless of affiliation.

This warning followed a possible clash between the NURTW and park managers over the control of motor parks in parts of the state, particularly Ibadan.

The PUNCH reported that the union had threatened to take over motor parks across the state in seven days, accusing Governor Seyi Makinde’s administration of repeatedly disobeying court judgments recognising its right to manage the parks.

The union said it would begin enforcing the judgments if the state government failed to withdraw its Park Management System from motor parks in the state’s 33 Local Government Areas by November 23.

The warnings were contained in separate statements issued by the governor’s Special Adviser on media, Sulaimon Olarenwaju, and the command’s Police Public Relations Officer, Olayinka Ayanlade, in Ibadan, the state capital.

The government said it had taken note of speculations regarding a possible breakdown of law and order arising from issues surrounding the management of motor parks in parts of the state.

The statement read, “The state government wishes to categorically assure all residents, commuters, visitors, investors, and travellers that Oyo State remains peaceful and secure. There is no cause for alarm. Governor Seyi Makinde has directed all relevant security agencies to maintain vigilance and ensure the protection of lives and property across the state.

“Security personnel have been strategically deployed where necessary, and appropriate measures have been put in place to prevent any breach of the peace.

“The Makinde administration remains firmly committed to preserving the peace, stability and economic progress that Oyo State has enjoyed over the years. Consequently, the government will not tolerate any act of violence, intimidation, self-help or unlawful takeover of public facilities by any individual or group, regardless of affiliation.

“The government urges all transport stakeholders, including members of the NURTW, to conduct themselves peacefully and in accordance with the law. No group or individual will be permitted to take actions capable of disrupting public order or threatening the peace of the state.”

The government also reiterated its earlier position on the judgment of the Court of Appeal, saying the judgment merely reaffirmed the constitutional right of citizens to freedom of association.

The statement explained that the judgment neither conferred ownership, control, nor management of public motor parks on the NURTW, nor did it authorise the union to take over facilities built, maintained, and regulated by the government.

It added, “Accordingly, any attempt to rely on the judgment as a basis for demanding, threatening, or effecting the takeover of public motor parks represents a clear misinterpretation of the court’s decision and has no basis in law.

“The government remains committed to upholding the rule of law and ensuring that all disputes, regardless of their nature, are resolved through lawful and peaceful means.

“Security agencies have been directed to act decisively against anyone found threatening public peace or disrupting economic and social activities in any part of the state.”

The government, therefore, advised the residents to disregard rumours, alarmist messages, and unverified information circulating on social media, urging them to rely only on official channels of communication for accurate and timely information.

It insisted that Oyo remained safe, secure, and open for business, urging all the residents to continue their lawful activities without fear, confident in the knowledge that the government has taken all necessary steps to guarantee their safety and security.

In a statement issued by the PPRO, the state police command said, “The attention of the Oyo State Police command has been drawn to a purported security advisory allegedly issued by some members of the NURTW, warning of a possible clash between NURTW members and Park Managers over the control of motor parks in parts of Oyo, particularly Ibadan, on Monday, November 23, 2026.

“The notice, which has since been circulating across various social media platforms, advises members of the public to avoid certain locations, including Iwo Road, Ojoo and Challenge areas, while urging residents to remain indoors throughout the day.

“Given the apprehension such information may generate, the command considers it necessary to address the situation and reassure the public. In this regard, the command wishes to assure the good people of Oyo State, particularly residents of Ibadan and its environs, that there is no cause for panic.

“Residents are advised to go about their lawful businesses and daily activities without fear or intimidation, as the police have taken proactive steps to prevent any threat to public peace and security. Consequently, the command has strengthened its security architecture through the deployment of adequate personnel, enhanced surveillance and intelligence-gathering mechanisms across strategic locations in the state.”

The police added that the measures are “aimed at identifying and promptly addressing any potential security threat, while ensuring that no individual or group is allowed to disrupt the peace and safety of residents.

“While the command remains committed to preventing any breakdown of law and order, it also recognises the importance of peaceful dispute resolution.”

The police, therefore, urged all parties involved to embrace dialogue and explore legitimate and appropriate legal channels for resolving their differences, saying that “no individual or group should resort to self-help, violence, intimidation or any action capable of threatening public peace.”

The command further warned that it would not allow any individual or group to undermine the security gains recorded in the state or take the state backwards through acts of lawlessness.

It insisted that all necessary measures would be taken to deal decisively with anyone found engaging in conduct capable of disturbing public peace.

The state Commissioner of Police, Olugbenga Abimbola, reassured residents of the command’s unwavering commitment to the protection of lives and property and the maintenance of law and order across the state.

title: FG orders probe into deadly Bayelsa boat accident
description:
By Folarin Kehinde



The Federal Government has ordered an immediate investigation into the boat accident that claimed several lives in Bayelsa State, warning that it would no longer tolerate avoidable safety violations on the nation’s waterways.







The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adeg
content:
By Folarin Kehinde

The Federal Government has ordered an immediate investigation into the boat accident that claimed several lives in Bayelsa State, warning that it would no longer tolerate avoidable safety violations on the nation’s waterways.

The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, gave the directive to the National Inland Waterways Authority (NIWA), asking it to investigate the immediate and remote causes of the accident and submit its findings to him.

The mishap occurred on Friday, November 20, in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha Community, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.

In a statement issued on Sunday by his Special Adviser, Dr Bolaji Akinola, Oyetola also directed NIWA to work with relevant government agencies and the Bayelsa State Government to ensure a transparent and comprehensive investigation.

The minister described the loss of lives as worrisome and unacceptable, expressing concern over reports that passengers involved in the accident were not wearing life jackets.

He also raised concerns over the alleged absence of a passenger manifest, stressing that proper documentation of passengers was a critical safety requirement that must be strictly enforced.

“Safety lapses on our waterways are no longer acceptable. The Federal Government will not fold its arms and watch its citizens perish on the waterways. We must get to the root of this tragedy and ensure that those responsible for enforcing safety regulations do their jobs,” he said.

Oyetola recalled that he visited Bayelsa State on May 2, 2025, where he distributed 3,500 life jackets to water transport users as part of efforts to improve safety on the waterways.

He also renewed his call on state governments to gradually phase out wooden boats and replace them with safer and more durable fibreglass or fibre-reinforced plastic vessels, particularly for passenger transportation.

The minister disclosed that he had contacted Bayelsa State Governor, Douye Diri, to commiserate with him, the state government and families of the victims.

He sympathised with the bereaved families and prayed for the repose of the souls of those who died in the accident, while urging stakeholders to work together to prevent a recurrence.

title: Otti begins construction of new Umuahia traffic corridor
description:
By Steve Oko



Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has commenced construction of a new road linking Bende Road through the Umuahia Post Office Tower and railway crossing to First Bank/Akanu Ibiam Road, with completion targeted before Christmas.







The project, being executed by the Umuahia Capit
content:
By Steve Oko

Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has commenced construction of a new road linking Bende Road through the Umuahia Post Office Tower and railway crossing to First Bank/Akanu Ibiam Road, with completion targeted before Christmas.

The project, being executed by the Umuahia Capital Development Authority (UCDA), is designed to provide an alternative traffic corridor, ease congestion around Government House and Isigate, and improve connectivity within the state capital.

The General Manager of UCDA, Engr. Kingsley Agomoh, who conducted journalists round the project site, said the road would allow motorists coming from Bende and Ikot Ekpene roads to connect to Abia Line, Aguiyi Ironsi Boulevard, Abia Express Tower and Onuimo Road without passing through the Government House axis.

He said the project would significantly reduce traffic pressure on major roads, stimulate economic activities and improve the aesthetics of Umuahia.

” If you are coming from Bende Road, you pass through the Post Office Tower, cross the railway station and connect to First Bank, Ridge Club and Abia Line without going through the Government House axis,” Agomoh said.

He explained that the project was part of Otti’s broader urban renewal programme, adding that the governor had also directed the relocation of Umuahia Railway Station to the Nnennaya Oti Bus Terminal.

According to him, the state government has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Nigerian Railway Corporation to facilitate the construction of the access road across the railway corridor.

Agomoh also disclosed that another road linking First Bank to the Keystone, Sterling and FCMB bank areas would be reopened and reconstructed to provide motorists, particularly those coming from the Federal Medical Centre, Umuahia, with a shorter alternative route.

He said the road, which had been encroached upon by adjoining property owners, was being reclaimed to restore access and ease movement within the commercial district.

Describing the railway-crossing road as a signature project of the Otti administration, Agomoh said the governor’s urban renewal drive was repositioning Umuahia for increased economic activities and orderly development.

He urged Abians to support Otti and other Labour Party candidates in the 2027 elections, arguing that continuity would ensure the completion of ongoing infrastructure projects across the state.

title: APC challenges NDC over candidates’ eligibility
description:
By Hadiza Yusuf



The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kano State has challenged the New Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) to address questions surrounding the eligibility of its governorship candidate, Aminu Abdussalam Gwarzo, and running mate, Mustapha Rabiu Kwankwaso, before accusing the Indep
content:
By Hadiza Yusuf

The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kano State has challenged the New Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) to address questions surrounding the eligibility of its governorship candidate, Aminu Abdussalam Gwarzo, and running mate, Mustapha Rabiu Kwankwaso, before accusing the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) of electoral irregularities.

The APC said political parties should ensure that their candidates meet the legal requirements for contesting elections before raising concerns about the electoral process.

The NDC, led by the Kwankwasiyya Movement, had on Saturday accused INEC and the ruling APC of plotting to manipulate the electoral process ahead of next year’s election.

At a press conference, Director-General of the NDC Governorship Campaign Council, Shehu Wada Sagagi, alleged that the APC was mounting pressure to interfere with the process through the Coalition Supports and Results Verification System (CSRVS).

But the APC Chairman in Kano, Umar Haruna Doguwa, dismissed the allegations and challenged Sagagi to provide evidence to substantiate his claims.

Doguwa described the accusations as false, alleging that the opposition was attempting to divert attention from its own challenges.

He said the APC was prepared for the election and would not allow any party or individual to interfere with the electoral process under the guise of protecting its credibility.

“Instead of dissipating energy on matters of little concern, the NDC should concentrate on issues surrounding the eligibility and qualifications of its candidates,” Doguwa said.

He added that a party yet to meet the electoral requirements for its candidates to appear on the ballot should not be preoccupied with accusing INEC and the APC of wrongdoing.

“Such conduct is not only reckless but also a clear attempt to play the victim card,” he said.

The APC chairman also faulted what he described as premature allegations against the electoral commission and the ruling party over an election yet to be conducted.

He urged the NDC to address the questions surrounding its candidates and allow INEC and other relevant institutions to discharge their constitutional responsibilities.

The APC said it remained confident ahead of the forthcoming election and urged political parties to respect electoral laws.

The meeting, held on Saturday, November 21, 2026, was convened b
content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi

Governor Hyacinth Alia of Benue State has reiterated his commitment to reconciliation and unity within the All Progressives Congress (APC) following a meeting with prominent party stakeholders in Abuja.

The meeting, held on Saturday, November 21, 2026, was convened by the North Central Presidential Reconciliation Committee, chaired by former Katsina State Governor, Senator Ibrahim Shema, as part of efforts to resolve disagreements among party leaders in Benue.

Those in attendance included the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume; former Benue State Governor, Senator Gabriel Suswam; Senator Barnabas Gemade; Senator Jack Gyado; and Elder Simon Shango.

Alia disclosed the meeting in a post on his verified social media handle, saying the engagement lasted about two hours and provided an opportunity for the stakeholders to discuss the future of the party in the state.

He said: “Today, (Saturday, November 21, 2026) I joined fellow Benue APC stakeholders in Abuja for a reconciliation meeting convened by the North Central Presidential Reconciliation Committee, chaired by Sen. Ibrahim Shehu Shema, former Governor of Katsina State.

“The meeting, which lasted about two hours, brought together the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Sen. George Akume, former Benue State Governor, Sen. Gabriel Suswam, Sen. Barnabas Gemade, Sen. Jack Gyado and Elder Simon Shango.

“I thank Sen. Shema and his committee for bringing us together. Reconciliation takes a willingness to listen, to speak frankly and to keep working together even where differences remain.

“My commitment is clear. I will continue to engage with our leaders and stakeholders in the interest of a united APC, while keeping the peace, security and development of Benue State at the centre of my work.

“The people of Benue entrusted us with the responsibility to serve, and that responsibility must continue to guide us.”

description:
….Commits ₦450b to farm financing







By Omeiza Ajayi



ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC on Sunday said President Bola Tinubu has approved a ₦1.5 trillion recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture BoA and committed ₦450 billion to agricultural financin
content:
….Commits ₦450b to farm financing

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC on Sunday said President Bola Tinubu has approved a ₦1.5 trillion recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture BoA and committed ₦450 billion to agricultural financing programmes.

The council said the commitment is meant “to strengthen food security, expand domestic production, and improve the productivity of smallholder farmers across the country, especially in Northern Nigeria.”

In a statement issued by its Spokesperson, Dele Alake, the council said the bank had reached “over 500,000 smallholder farmers.”

It added that the President “also approved a ₦1.5 trillion recapitalisation to expand agricultural financing and support the cultivation of 500,000 hectares under the Renewed Hope Agenda.”

According to the statement, the Federal Government “went beyond providing farmers with loans; it also addressed access to quality seeds, fertiliser, mechanisation, irrigation, storage facilities, commodity markets, and other essential components of the agricultural value chain.”

On the recapitalisation, the council said it was “a major campaign promise of the President in 2023.” It said the move was designed “to enhance the bank’s financial capacity and ability to provide more affordable and accessible funding to farmers, agricultural cooperatives, processors, aggregators, and other businesses operating across the agricultural value chain.”

The statement added: “Under President Tinubu, a stronger Bank of Agriculture would be better positioned to support large-scale agricultural investments, expand its reach to underserved farming communities, and mobilise additional resources for domestic food production.”

The council disclosed that the Renewed Hope Smallholder Support and Value Chain Fund, which has a programme value of ₦250 billion, finances farmers through Farmer Aggregation Companies.

These companies, it said, “coordinate farmer registration, input distribution, extension services, and market linkages.” The programme, according to the statement, has reached more than 500,000 smallholder farmers across 16 states, including over 70,000 women.

It has also supported the distribution of approximately 2.5 million bags of fertiliser and 300,000 bags of certified seeds. The council said the programme targets two million farmers and the distribution of more than 10 million bags of fertiliser. It named Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Niger, Borno, Gombe, Taraba, Adamawa, Yobe and Bauchi among the states receiving attention under the scheme.

To shield farmers from price shocks, the statement said, the bank is implementing a ₦200 billion Guaranteed Minimum Price Programme. Under it, the bank “has procured approximately 170,000 metric tonnes of maize, rice, sorghum, and cassava to strengthen commodity markets and protect farmers against distress sales.”

The council also said the bank created an Onion Financing Programme in partnership with the National Onion Producers, Processors and Marketers Association of Nigeria (NOPPMAN), which “represents over 11,800 onion farmers.”

The scheme provides onion farmers with improved seeds and fertiliser, supports processors with commodity purchase funds, and helps develop storage and solar-powered cooling facilities to cut post-harvest losses.

“Under the arrangement, cooperatives will contribute 30 per cent of their input costs, while BOA will finance the remaining 70 per cent,” the statement said.

On dry-season farming, it said the bank is working with the All-Farmers Association of Nigeria “to develop a pipeline targeting 400,000 farmers for the 2026 farming cycle.” The initiative covers financing for 120,000 hectares of wheat and another 300,000 hectares for crops including rice, maize, sorghum, millet, cassava and soybeans.

The council added that the Nigeria Ginger Recovery Programme has supported 3,200 farmers in Kachia, Kaduna State, with blight-free seeds. It said more than 9,000 bags have been recovered for multiplication, with an expansion planned across 20,000 hectares in 16 states.

For women, the bank is “targeting at least 50,000 women nationwide through insured cooperative production financing at nine per cent, in partnership with the Federal Ministries of Women Affairs and Agriculture.”

On mechanisation, the statement said 1,571 tractors have been deployed to 23 states under the Renewed Hope National Agricultural Mechanisation Programme. They are expected to mechanise 1.2 million hectares of farmland.

It also cited a ₦385 billion productive-use-of-electricity programme, which “provides 44,000 electric cargo tricycles and 100,000 solar irrigation pumps, targeting 500,000 farming families.”

“The interventions demonstrated President Tinubu’s commitment to transforming agriculture into a major driver of economic growth, food security, and job creation”, the council added.

title: NDC dismisses allegations of hoarding ₦6bn campaign funds
description:
Party says money is reserved for operations, accuses critics of seeking access to development fund



By Henry Umoru



ABUJA – The national leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has dismissed allegations that it is withholding more than ₦6 billion meant for its presidential campaign,
content:
Party says money is reserved for operations, accuses critics of seeking access to development fund

By Henry Umoru

ABUJA – The national leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has dismissed allegations that it is withholding more than ₦6 billion meant for its presidential campaign, describing the claims as false and misleading.

The party said the allegations reflected a lack of understanding of party administration and the funding requirements of political campaigns.

Some members of the NDC National Campaign Council (NCC) had reportedly accused the party’s national leadership of failing to release adequate funds for campaign activities, including grassroots mobilisation, billboard advertisements and the printing of posters.

The aggrieved members alleged that more than ₦6 billion realised from the sale of nomination forms and contributions by aspirants had been kept in a fixed deposit account while the campaign council struggled to finance basic activities.

They also claimed that 75 per cent of the money came from the South-East, following the entry of aspirants who joined the party alongside its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and expressed concern that the alleged funding constraints could affect his electoral prospects.

However, speaking with Vanguard, the party’s National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, dismissed the allegations as rumours allegedly being promoted by individuals seeking to create divisions within the party.

He said the claims were intended to create friction between Obi and the party’s national leadership.

“These are rumours and machinations of mischief makers who don’t wish the party well, and want to create problems where there is none between our presidential candidate and the national leader of our party.

“Also, it shows acute ignorance on the part of those peddling the rumours about party administration and how presidential campaigns are funded,” he said.

Director advised those making the allegations to familiarise themselves with party administration and the provisions of the Electoral Act on campaign financing.

However, a senior party source, who spoke on condition of anonymity, confirmed that the campaign council had yet to receive substantial funding from the national leadership, despite the revenue reportedly generated from the sale of nomination forms.

The source expressed concern that the funding situation could hamper publicity, grassroots mobilisation and other campaign activities.

According to the source, the party disclosed at its third National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting that it had generated about ₦8 billion, spent approximately ₦2 billion and retained about ₦6 billion in a fixed deposit account.

The source said the funds were generated through the sale of nomination forms and development levies.

“Let me also inform you that more than 80 per cent of the candidates could not pay for the nomination and expression of interest forms. They were given forms free. Many states still do not have offices, and the party is assisting them. The national leadership recently got its office.

“The Obidient Movement is coming out crying about money. Where are the funds for senatorial, governorship and other positions?” the source queried.

The source further disclosed that the party had proposed the establishment of a National Campaign Fund involving its presidential candidate, his running mate, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, and the national leadership.

According to the source, the arrangement proposed the allocation of ₦1 billion to the South-South, another ₦1 billion to the South-East, while the remaining ₦3 billion would be managed by the Campaign Council.

The source claimed that Obi was asked to contribute ₦5 billion towards establishing the fund but provided only ₦220 million, out of which ₦200 million was subsequently transferred to the National Campaign Council.

“The party is not holding any campaign money,” the source insisted.

The source further alleged that those demanding access to the money were seeking the release of funds contributed for the party’s development.

“They want the development fund money people paid to be given to them. The ₦6 billion is to run the party. Only Aisha Yusuf has helped to open an account to assist the party. The party has not raised funds, Obi has not raised funds.

“The party will be going to Edo State on Wednesday. The party has no money; the people of Edo State will finance the visit.

“If we give them the money we saved to run the election, we will not have money to run the party,” the source said.

The source also lamented the absence of adequate funding for campaign publicity, including posters, billboards and youth mobilisation, as well as activities involving various support groups.

Vanguard’s efforts to obtain the reaction of the National Campaign Council spokesperson, Dr Constance Ikokwu, were unsuccessful, as she did not respond to a WhatsApp message sent to her over a period of more than five hours.

Recall that the NDC, at its third NEC meeting held on October 24 at JD Event Centre, Abuja, announced that it had generated ₦8,529,632,438.77 in revenue since its establishment seven months earlier.

The party attributed the revenue to the sale of nomination forms, contributions from supporters, membership dues and levies.

Presenting the financial statement, the National Treasurer, Dr Peter Onigah, said the party had spent approximately ₦2.40 billion and retained a balance of about ₦6.13 billion.

He said the expenditure covered party activities, including primaries, publicity, salaries and other administrative expenses.

Onigah said the party had maintained financial discipline and ensured that resources entrusted to its leadership were managed prudently.

He explained that its financial management was guided by the experience of party officials, advice from national leaders and the National Working Committee (NWC).

According to him, the party would provide a detailed breakdown of its financial transactions as it approached the end of its first accounting year.

“We have been very prudent. Our chief is made up of technocrats, people who are experienced and people who have different capacities,” he said.

Onigah also appealed to Nigerians and party members to support the party financially, noting that it was still developing its structures and had yet to control government at any level.

“As a new party, we don’t have people in government yet. All of us are outside the government. So we need to contribute together and ensure that our party will prevail and achieve the desired objectives,” he said.

The post NDC dismisses allegations of hoarding ₦6bn campaign funds appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: I didn’t politicise it — Gov Yusuf narrates how wife left Kano Govt House
description:
Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, has broken his silence on his marital crisis with wife, Zainab, recounting how she allegedly left the Government House and later initiated divorce proceedings against him in Abuja.



The governor, in an interview with BBC Hausa aired on Sunday, said he had remained
content:
Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, has broken his silence on his marital crisis with wife, Zainab, recounting how she allegedly left the Government House and later initiated divorce proceedings against him in Abuja.

The governor, in an interview with BBC Hausa aired on Sunday, said he had remained quiet despite developments in the marriage, which he said had lasted about two decades and produced children.

Yusuf said Zainab, a niece of his former political ally, Rabiu Kwankwaso, was previously married before they got together.

He recalled that their relationship eventually deteriorated, leading to her departure from the Government House, an experience he said he endured without publicly discussing the matter.

“Many things happened, to the point where her belongings were packed and she was taken away from my house, and through it all, I remained patient and did not speak out,” Yusuf said.

He said he had tried to reassure their children that their mother would return, but was subsequently taken aback when the matter ended up in court.

The governor said he was particularly surprised that the divorce suit was filed in Abuja rather than Kano.

“Suddenly, she dragged me to court, a court in Abuja, not even in Kano,” he said.

Yusuf described the development as distressing, adding that he had information about the circumstances surrounding his wife’s departure but would not publicly disclose the details.

Asked whether he was using the family dispute for political purposes, the governor denied bringing politics into the matter, questioning how anyone in a similar situation would react.

“I am not the one who politicised it. If this was done to you, how would you feel?” he asked.

He further lamented that his wife’s belongings were removed and she was taken to another residence without his knowledge, before he learnt that she had instituted legal proceedings against him.

The marital dispute is before the Upper Area Court in the Gudu District of Abuja, where the divorce case, marked CV/97/26, was adjourned until December 15.

The adjournment followed a request by Kano Commissioner for Information, Sanusi Bature, who represented Yusuf, for more time to brief the governor on the court proceedings.

The crisis has drawn political attention because of Yusuf’s relationship with Kwankwaso, who played a significant role in his political rise. Their relationship reportedly deteriorated after Yusuf defected from the New Nigeria Peoples Party to the All Progressives Congress in January 2026, while Kwankwaso later joined the New Nigeria Democratic Congress.

title: Amnesty demands probe as tourist accuses Daura emir of sexual assault
description:
Nigerians have reacted with mixed feelings after a female tourist accused the Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, of touching her inappropriately during a visit to his palace in Katsina State.
The allegation, which has sparked debate on social media, followed the circulation of a video appearing to sho
content:
Nigerians have reacted with mixed feelings after a female tourist accused the Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, of touching her inappropriately during a visit to his palace in Katsina State.

The allegation, which has sparked debate on social media, followed the circulation of a video appearing to show the traditional ruler interacting with the tourist during her visit.

The woman, who identifies herself as @beduinqa, made the allegation in a post on Instagram on Saturday after completing a 30-day tour of Nigeria.

She said she waited until she left Nigeria before making the claim public.

According to a series of posts on her Instagram, the tourist was on a world tour with Nigeria as her 184th of 197 destinations.

She announced her arrival on October 19, 2026 and documented visits across the country, including a trip to the Oba of Benin’s palace on October 24.

She had also posted a video of her attendance at the 10th coronation anniversary celebration of Oba Ewuare II on October 25, time at the Kala Kuta shrine and Makoko in Lagos, as well as stops in Kano, Katsina and Bauchi, where she met the Emir of Bauchi at his palace.

Recounting her experience at the Daura palace, the tourist said she was taken into an elegant room where she sat with the Emir and had a conversation with him.

She alleged that the traditional ruler held her hand and began playing with it before hugging and kissing her on the cheek.

She further alleged that he touched her breasts, an action she said shocked and disturbed her.

In her Instagram post, she wrote, “That was a shock for me. I told him ‘emir no, no, no, no’ ‘emir you cannot be touching’, but he was just laughing about it.”

She said she had travelled through different parts of Nigeria without experiencing sexual assault in public spaces, making the alleged incident at the palace particularly disturbing.

“I wasn’t sexually assaulted at any moment when walking through streets of Nigeria, even in busy crowded places, but to my shock, I was assaulted in a palace by a traditional leader who should be behaving in exemplary and dignified way,” she wrote.

The tourist described the experience as disgusting, adding that she had continued to relive it in her thoughts.

She said the incident happened on Saturday, November 14, but she waited until she had left Nigeria before making the allegation public.

She also suggested that other women might have experienced similar treatment from the Emir, although she did not provide evidence to support the claim.

“I suspect I wasn’t first woman he assaulted but probably first one with a proof recorded. I have meta glasses and quickly turned them on,” she added.

The allegation has generated reactions on X, with several users expressing outrage and calling for accountability.

Amnesty International Nigeria called on the authorities to investigate the allegation, describing it as deeply disturbing.

In a post on its X account, the human rights organisation said the Katsina State Government and the police should conduct a transparent and independent investigation to ensure accountability.

It said, “The Nigerian authorities must immediately and effectively investigate strong allegations of sexual assault on a female foreign tourist by the Emir of Daura Faruk Umar Faruk.”

Amnesty added that the incident presented an opportunity for the government to demonstrate that nobody was above the law.

Another X user, identified as @mairowashere, described the alleged incident as appalling and expressed relief that the tourist had recorded the encounter.

“What a shame. Truly appalling. I’m really glad the woman managed to get it on video because, had she simply come forward to say she was assaulted, people would have demanded proof, questioned her account or dismissed her altogether,” the user wrote.

Similarly, @Bashir_GS called on the Katsina State Government to consider removing the Emir, describing him as unfit to occupy the throne.

Another user, @Nawas_masood, said the allegation had damaged the reputation of the traditional institution.

“It is really painful to watch this. The Emir of Daura has done serious damage to the dignity and standing of the Northern Emirates. What hurts most is that the damage goes beyond one emirate. It affects the image of our traditional institutions and the respect they have earned over the years,” the user wrote.

As of the time of filing this report, neither the Daura Emirate Council nor the Katsina State Government had issued an official response to the allegation.

PUNCH Online could not independently confirm the claim.

Meanwhile, a source in the emir’s palace has denied the allegation

“There was nothing like that. She visited the palace, but how she got that information cooked up still amused us in the palace.

“Meanwhile, an official statement will be released, while I advise you should not write the story or wait for the official statement,” the source, who spoke on condition anonymity because he was not authorised to speak to the press, told our correspondent by telephone on Sunday.

When contacted, the Katsina State Commissioner for Information, Culture and Tourism, Dr Bala Zango, said he had not seen the video and would watch it before responding.

“I have not seen the video. But, let me watch the video and call you back,” he said.

The post Amnesty demands probe as tourist accuses Daura emir of sexual assault appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
By Golok Nanmwa

JOS – Suspected gunmen have reportedly set fire to Government Secondary School, Masharkut, in Butura District of Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State.

The incident, which occurred on Sunday afternoon, triggered panic in the community after residents noticed smoke billowing from the school premises shortly after church service.

A community member, Daniel Bwehfa Makodeng, who reported the incident to journalists, said the school was set ablaze at about 1pm.

“Suspected bandits set the school on fire around 1pm,” he said.

He explained that residents initially noticed smoke coming from the school before discovering about 30 minutes later that the building was on fire.

The Chairman of Bokkos Local Government Area, Hon. Amalau Amalau, also confirmed the incident, saying the council had received reports that the school was engulfed in flames.

Speaking in a telephone interview, Amalau said the circumstances surrounding the fire and the identities of those responsible had yet to be established.

“We only saw the school in flames. We cannot ascertain at the moment who was responsible or whether it was carried out by terrorists,” he said.

The chairman confirmed that the incident occurred on Sunday, adding that the immediate concern was the destruction of the school building.

Efforts to reach security operatives for confirmation and comments were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report.
