title: COP31 collapses as nations disagree over fossil fuel transition
description:
The 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) has ended without a comprehensive political agreement after participating countries failed to resolve disagreements over fossil fuels, climate financing and measures to tackle global warming.







The failure to adopt a final cover decision
content:
The 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) has ended without a comprehensive political agreement after participating countries failed to resolve disagreements over fossil fuels, climate financing and measures to tackle global warming.

The failure to adopt a final cover decision followed almost 48 hours of extended negotiations beyond the summit’s scheduled closing date of November 20, making the conference, held in Antalya, Turkey, the longest in the history of UN climate negotiations.

The 12-day summit opened on November 9, with countries struggling to reconcile competing positions on the future of fossil fuels and financial support for developing nations.

COP31 President, Murat Kurum, announced at Sunday’s closing plenary that delegates had been unable to reach the consensus required to adopt the final draft agreement.

At the centre of the disagreement was whether the outcome document should contain an explicit commitment to move away from fossil fuels, alongside provisions on adaptation financing and carbon capture technologies.

EU rejects final proposal

The European Union and several other countries opposed the final proposal, arguing that its failure to directly address fossil fuels weakened the global response to climate change.

Ireland’s Environment Minister, Darragh O’Brien, who represented the EU, maintained that the bloc could not support an agreement that failed to identify fossil fuels as a major driver of the climate crisis.

Norway, Panama, the Marshall Islands and other vulnerable nations also raised objections to the proposed text.

Ghana, speaking on behalf of the African Group of Negotiators, expressed dissatisfaction with aspects of the negotiation process, particularly the handling of issues affecting Africa and demands for climate financing.

Despite its reservations, the African group indicated that it was prepared to accept the proposed text to preserve the multilateral negotiation process.

Fossil fuel commitment dropped from successive drafts

The controversy intensified as successive versions of the proposed agreement emerged during the negotiations.

The initial draft, published on November 16, called for accelerated efforts to phase out fossil fuels and an immediate transition away from their use in energy systems.

However, subsequent versions removed the explicit fossil fuel provisions, alongside a proposed annual adaptation finance target of $120 billion for developing countries.

The final version, released in the early hours of Sunday, November 22, equally omitted a direct commitment to move away from fossil fuels.

Instead, it referred to the agreement reached at COP28 in Dubai in 2023, which called for a just, orderly and equitable transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems.

But countries seeking a stronger commitment argued that referring to an earlier agreement without spelling out concrete action was inadequate.

The disagreement revived tensions surrounding COP28, which produced the first explicit reference to transitioning away from fossil fuels in a UN climate conference agreement after decades of negotiations.

At COP31, however, governments failed to agree on how that commitment should be strengthened and translated into practical action.

Guterres expresses disappointment

United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres expressed disappointment over the absence of a comprehensive agreement, warning that the scientific evidence of climate change remained clear despite political divisions.

“There may be no consensus in the negotiating room. There is no ambiguity in the science,” he said.

Guterres noted that global temperatures continued to reach record levels, extreme weather events were becoming more intense and greenhouse gas emissions remained dangerously high.

He warned that the world was heading towards breaching the 1.5-degree Celsius warming threshold established under the Paris Agreement.

The UN chief urged governments to intensify efforts to reduce dependence on fossil fuels, increase climate financing and strengthen measures to protect communities most exposed to climate impacts.

Former Executive Secretary of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, Christiana Figueres, also described the outcome as disappointing.

She, however, noted that more than 130 countries had refused to endorse an agreement they considered inadequate in addressing the severity of the climate crisis.

Figueres argued that developments outside the formal negotiations offered some grounds for optimism, particularly through the COP31 Action Agenda, which encourages governments, businesses and other non-state actors to advance climate initiatives.

She also highlighted commitments and signals from economies representing about half of the global economy to raise electricity’s share of global final energy consumption to 35 per cent by 2035.

African climate advocate condemns outcome

The collapse of the negotiations also attracted criticism from Mohamed Adow, Director of Power Shift Africa, who described the outcome as a warning about the failure of international climate diplomacy to address the needs of vulnerable countries.

Adow accused wealthy nations of failing to provide the financial resources developing countries require to implement climate action.

He also criticised the European Union’s rejection of the proposed agreement, alleging that the bloc had contributed to setbacks in negotiations on adaptation financing and a just transition.

“COP31 was a ghost COP, and its lack of progress will haunt climate-vulnerable communities in Africa and around the world,” he said.

Adow further lamented the failure to establish a just transition mechanism, which he said was among the key expectations carried over from the previous climate summit in Brazil.

Although countries could not agree on the overarching political document, negotiations on some individual issues recorded progress, while activities under the COP31 Action Agenda continued.

The unresolved disagreements will now remain on the international climate negotiation agenda ahead of COP32, scheduled to hold in Ethiopia in November 2027.

title: Barcelona fight back from two goals down to beat Villarreal, extend La Liga lead
description:
Spanish champions Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 on Sunday and restore their three point lead at the top of La Liga.



Barca edged clear of Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, who had pulled level with them on Saturday after beating Celta Vigo.



Two goals inside seven m
content:
Spanish champions Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 on Sunday and restore their three point lead at the top of La Liga.

Barca edged clear of Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, who had pulled level with them on Saturday after beating Celta Vigo.

Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou and Barca winger Lamine Yamal missed a first half penalty.

However the Catalan giants struck three times in an 11-minute spell in the second half to claim victory.

Gerard Martin and Fermin Lopez pulled Barca level before Pau Navarro’s own goal gave them the three points.

Barca have now won four consecutive matches across all competitions since their Clasico defeat by Real Madrid in October.

“We suffered because we started the game badly, we let in two goals very early. I’ll remember how the team reacted but we have to work to ensure this doesn’t happen again,” Barca midfielder Pedri told DAZN.

“Against a team like this you can’t always turn things around from two down.”

The hosts were caught snoozing in the early afternoon sunlight and Buchanan fired Villarreal ahead in the fifth minute.

Fermin Lopez gave the ball away with a careless pass and Canada international Buchanan produced a perfect sliced effort from distance to send the visitors ahead.

Two minutes later Villarreal doubled their advantage when Tani Oluwaseyi, another Canadian, broke in down the left flank and smashed an effort over Joan Garcia into the roof of the net.

Hansi Flick’s side should have pulled one back when Oluwaseyi felled Yamal in the area and a penalty was given after a VAR review.

Yamal took it himself but dragged his effort against the post and wide.

The winger tried to make amends with a burst inside from the wing before half-time but Peter Gulacsi palmed away his cross-shot and the goalkeeper and his defence combined to thwart Eric Garcia on the follow up.

– Quickfire treble –

Barcelona came out invigorated in the second half and quickly dragged themselves back into the match.

Pedri shot wide and Gulacsi saved from Lopez’s low effort before Martin found the net in the 57th minute.

Pedri crossed the ball in from the left for the defender to head home.

Four minutes later Lopez slammed home the second after being teed up by Yamal, and the third was quick to follow.

A clever backheel pass by Yamal fed Eric Garcia, whose cross was bundled into the back of his own net by Navarro.

Substitute Anthony Gordon was denied by Gulacsi and then appealed for a penalty after a bump from Santi Comesana but went down too easily.

Navarro was sent off for a second yellow card in stoppage time as Villarreal, ninth, left frustrated.

“The (first Barca) goal psychologically killed us, they gained confidence, a couple of minutes later they equalised and from there it’s a lot more difficult,” Comesana told DAZN.

Later Sunday Atletico Madrid, third, visit Getafe among other fixtures.

title: ‘I’m stepping down for no one’ – Atiku insists on 2027 ambition
description:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has ruled out withdrawing from the 2027 presidential race, insisting that he remains in the contest to challenge President Bola Tinubu.
Atiku made his position known in a statement issued on Sunday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, in res
content:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has ruled out withdrawing from the 2027 presidential race, insisting that he remains in the contest to challenge President Bola Tinubu.

Atiku made his position known in a statement issued on Sunday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, in response to reports claiming that he had stepped down from the race.

He accused political parties promoting the reports of working in favour of Tinubu, describing the claims as an attempt to remove a strong opposition candidate from the contest.

“Any party promoting the lie that I have stepped down is doing Tinubu’s work. Every false withdrawal story tries to clear his strongest opponent from the field,” he said.

The former vice-president also dismissed declarations allegedly made by individuals claiming to represent his supporters, maintaining that nobody could announce his withdrawal on his behalf.

“Putting my name on a placard does not make someone my supporter. Putting a lie in that person’s mouth does not make it my decision,” Atiku said.

He warned that keeping him off the ballot would undermine Nigerians’ opportunity to choose their preferred candidate.

“If I am not on the ballot, Bola Tinubu might as well wait for a coronation. But I am in this race to win, and Nigerians will have their choice,” he added.

Atiku further accused those circulating the withdrawal reports of using misinformation to weaken opposition parties and give the ruling All Progressives Congress an advantage ahead of the election.

He urged opposition groups seeking to defeat Tinubu to concentrate on persuading voters rather than spreading claims about other candidates.

“Anyone serious about defeating the APC should take their case to voters. Manufacturing supporters and circulating false declarations will not defeat Tinubu. It only serves him,” he said.

Addressing his campaign agenda, Atiku said his Affordable Life programme was designed to tackle the economic challenges facing Nigerian households, particularly the rising costs of food and transportation.

“Hunger and poverty are not on social media. They are in our markets, our homes and every community where families struggle to afford food and transport,” he said.

He also called on his supporters to remain active ahead of the election and ensure they obtained their Permanent Voter Cards.

Reaffirming his position, Atiku said he was neither seeking another candidate to withdraw for him nor willing to leave the race for anyone.

“I do not need anyone to step down for me, and I am stepping down for no one,” he declared.

The former vice-president expressed confidence that he would defeat Tinubu in the presidential election scheduled for January 16, 2027.

title: Katsina ADC Gov Candidate Kaita Launches 2027 Campaign
description: The governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Katsina State, Senator Ahmed Kaita, has officially launched his 2027 campaign in the Funtua senatorial zone, drawing a crowd of supporters as residents of Funtua Local Government pledged to back ADC candidates in all elective pos
content:
The governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Katsina State, Senator Ahmed Kaita, has officially launched his 2027 campaign in the Funtua senatorial zone, drawing a crowd of supporters as residents of Funtua Local Government pledged to back ADC candidates in all elective positions during the forthcoming general elections.

The campaign rally, held on Sunday at Aya Primary School in Funtua, attracted scores of supporters from across Funtua and neighbouring communities, signalling the party’s determination to mount a strong challenge in the state.

Addressing the crowd, Senator Kaita expressed gratitude for what he described as the overwhelming voluntary turnout of supporters, insisting that those in attendance were driven by a genuine desire for change and good governance rather than political inducement.

He said the campaign would unveil its comprehensive policy agenda during the next rally scheduled for Faskari Local Government Area on Tuesday, explaining that the decision was deliberate to distinguish the ADC’s approach from that of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

“Today marks the beginning of the change that Katsina people have been yearning for. Everyone you see here came willingly because they desire good governance. I sincerely appreciate our supporters for the warm reception. By the grace of God, we will unveil our agenda in Faskari on Tuesday. We want to show the difference between our campaign and that of the APC-led government,” Kaita declared.

Before proceeding to the rally venue, the ADC governorship candidate paid a courtesy visit to the Sarkin Maskan Katsina and District Head of Funtua, where he sought royal blessings, prayers, guidance and support ahead of the elections.

The event also featured the ADC senatorial candidate for Funtua zone, Hon. Jamilu Muhammad Lion, whose appearance drew loud cheers from the large gathering of party faithful.

The Funtua rally marks the first major campaign outing by Senator Kaita in the 2027 election season and sets the stage for the ADC’s statewide mobilisation as political activities gather momentum across Katsina State.

title: Lagos firefighters rescue 70-year-old woman from 60-foot well
description:
The Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service has rescued a 70-year-old woman who accidentally fell into a 60-foot-deep well in Oworonshoki, Kosofe Local Government Area of the state.
The incident occurred at 37, Abiola Street, where firefighters from the Oworonshoki Fire Station responded to a distress c
content:
The Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service has rescued a 70-year-old woman who accidentally fell into a 60-foot-deep well in Oworonshoki, Kosofe Local Government Area of the state.

The incident occurred at 37, Abiola Street, where firefighters from the Oworonshoki Fire Station responded to a distress call in the early hours of Sunday.

The Controller-General of the service, Margaret Adeseye, disclosed this in a statement issued on Sunday, saying the firefighters successfully rescued the woman alive.

She said the rescue operation was concluded, “after the septuagenarian was stabilised and handed over to family.”

The circumstances surrounding the woman’s fall into the well were not immediately disclosed.

Falls into open or poorly covered wells remain a recurring hazard in parts of Lagos, where many residential compounds still rely on traditional water sources.

Similar incidents have been recorded in recent years, including the successful rescue of a younger woman from a 60-foot well in the Ikorodu area in October 2025 by the same service.

The Lagos State Government lists 112 and 767 as toll-free emergency lines for residents to report emergencies.

title: Oyetola orders probe into Bayelsa fatal boat mishap, raises safety concerns
description:
From Idu Jude, Abuja
The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, has ordered an immediate investigation into the remote and direct causes of the fatal boat mishap that occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha Community, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area o
content:
From Idu Jude, Abuja

The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, has ordered an immediate investigation into the remote and direct causes of the fatal boat mishap that occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha Community, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, claiming scores of lives.

Oyetola directed the National Inland Waterways Authority (NIWA) to conduct a thorough investigation into the incident and submit its report to him.

He further directed NIWA to work in collaboration with relevant government agencies and the Bayelsa State Government to ensure a comprehensive, transparent and credible investigation.

Describing the loss of lives as worrisome and unacceptable, Oyetola said the Federal Government would no longer tolerate avoidable safety lapses on the nation’s waterways.

The minister expressed concern that the passengers involved in the tragedy reportedly did not wear life jackets, recalling that he had personally visited Bayelsa State on May 2, 2025, to distribute 3,500 life jackets to water transport users as part of efforts to promote safety and protect lives.

He also raised concerns over the alleged absence of a passenger manifest, stressing that proper passenger documentation was a critical safety requirement that must be strictly enforced.

“Safety lapses on our waterways are no longer acceptable. The Federal Government will not fold its arms and watch its citizens perish on the waterways. We must get to the root of this tragedy and ensure that those responsible for enforcing safety regulations do their jobs,” the minister said.

Oyetola reiterated his call for the gradual phasing out of wooden boats by state governments and their replacement with safer, more durable and better-equipped fibreglass or fibre-reinforced plastic vessels, particularly for passenger transportation.

“I have consistently advocated for State Governments to begin gradual phasing out of wooden boats and replace them with safer, more durable and better-equipped fiberglass or fiber-reinforced plastic vessels, particularly for passenger transportation,” he said.

The minister disclosed that he had called the Governor of Bayelsa State, Senator Douye Diri, to commiserate with him, the state government and the families of the victims over the tragic incident.

Expressing sympathy to the bereaved families, the minister said the loss of lives in such circumstances was deeply painful and that the grief of families who had lost loved ones was beyond words.

“Our thoughts and prayers are with the affected families at this difficult time. We also sympathise with all those who have been affected by this tragedy and pray for strength, comfort and the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss,” he said.

He prayed for the repose of the souls of the departed and for divine comfort for their families, urging all stakeholders to work together to ensure that such a tragedy never happens again.

title: Bayelsa boat tragedy: Atiku demands probe, stricter safety measures
description:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has called on the Federal and Bayelsa State governments to investigate the boat mishap that claimed several lives in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State recently.
He also called for improved safety regulations across the nation’s waterways.
A
content:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has called on the Federal and Bayelsa State governments to investigate the boat mishap that claimed several lives in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State recently.

He also called for improved safety regulations across the nation’s waterways.

Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, urged the authorities to enforce existing regulations against boat overloading, the use of unseaworthy vessels and other unsafe practices responsible for avoidable accidents on waterways.

The boat mishap, which occurred on Friday, reportedly claimed several lives, leaving the affected communities of Ayama and Ukubie in mourning.

In a statement issued on Sunday in Lokoja, Kogi State, on behalf of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, described the incident as a heartbreaking tragedy that had plunged entire communities into grief.

He said the victims were ordinary Nigerians who had embarked on a journey to honour a departed loved one but lost their lives in the process.

“What makes this tragedy even more painful is that these were ordinary Nigerians who set out in love and solidarity to honour a departed loved one, only to meet their own untimely deaths on the waters.

“Bayelsa has lost fathers, mothers, children and breadwinners. No words can adequately capture the depth of grief now hanging over the affected communities,” the statement read in part.

Atiku extended his condolences to the bereaved families, the affected communities, the state government and the people of the state, as he prayed for the repose of the souls of the deceased and the speedy recovery of those injured in the accident.

The ADC-PCC commended local divers, the Marine Police, the National Emergency Management Agency and other emergency responders for their efforts in the search and rescue operations.

Meanwhile, the council insisted that beyond the immediate rescue efforts, governments must take concrete steps to address the safety challenges confronting water transportation, particularly in riverine communities.

Ologbondiyan said both governments must demonstrate the political will to prevent a recurrence by investing in safer transportation facilities and enforcing existing regulations.

“The Federal and State governments must prioritise the provision of standard and well-maintained boats, adequate life jackets, functional jetties and properly trained boat operators across riverine communities,” he stated.

He added that water transportation remained an essential means of movement for millions of Nigerians living in the Niger Delta and other riverine areas, warning that their safety should not be treated as an afterthought.

The council also called for immediate support to the affected families and survivors, adding that such intervention should cover medical treatment, psychosocial support and financial assistance for the burial of victims, arguing that families already devastated by the tragedy should not be left to bear the additional financial burden.

The incident has again drawn attention to the safety of water transportation in riverine communities, where boats serve as a major means of connecting settlements and accessing essential services.

The ADC-PCC urged the relevant authorities to conduct a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident and ensure that appropriate measures were taken to prevent similar tragedies.

The state governor, Senator Douye Diri, on Saturday, ordered an investigation into the boat mishap, as he also directed that anyone found culpable in the incident be prosecuted.

He said preliminary findings indicated that the boat was overloaded, had no passenger manifest and that most of those on board were not wearing life jackets.

Likewise, on Saturday, President Bola Tinubu called for a minute of silence in honour of victims of the boat accident during the All Progressives Congress campaign rally in Oyo State.

Tinubu, who expressed sympathy with the bereaved families and the people of Bayelsa, also announced that Vice-President Kashim Shettima would visit the state to commiserate with those affected by the tragedy.

The President made the announcement while addressing supporters at the rally, where he called for prayers for the repose of the victims’ souls and an end to similar incidents.

The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, also called for an immediate investigation into the remote and direct causes of the fatal boat mishap

Oyetola, in a statement released on Sunday through his media aide, Dr Bolaji Akinola, directed the National Inland Waterways Authority to “conduct a thorough investigation into the incident and submit its report to him.”

The post Bayelsa boat tragedy: Atiku demands probe, stricter safety measures appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

description:
Her Regal Majesty, Olori Ambassador Dr. Temitope Morenike Enitan-Ogunwusi, Southwest Malaria Advocate under Nigeria’s National Malaria Elimination Programme (NMEP), participated in the High-Level Dialogue on Malaria Elimination held in Gaborone, Botswana, from 4–5 November 2026.
The dialogue, conven
content:
Her Regal Majesty, Olori Ambassador Dr. Temitope Morenike Enitan-Ogunwusi, Southwest Malaria Advocate under Nigeria’s National Malaria Elimination Programme (NMEP), participated in the High-Level Dialogue on Malaria Elimination held in Gaborone, Botswana, from 4–5 November 2026.

The dialogue, convened by the United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS) and the RBM Partnership to End Malaria alongside the 36th RBM Partnership Board Meeting, brought together global health leaders, advocates and stakeholders to strengthen collective efforts towards malaria elimination.

Her Regal Majesty expressed appreciation to Dr. Michael Adekunle Charles, Chief Executive Officer of the RBM Partnership to End Malaria, and the RBM team for the invitation and for convening this important dialogue. She noted that such platforms are vital in strengthening partnerships, amplifying community voices and sustaining collective commitment towards a malaria-free Africa.

HRM’s participation provided an opportunity to contribute perspectives on community ownership, grassroots accountability, cultural leadership, gender inclusion and public trust in health interventions. She emphasised the importance of engaging communities as active partners in malaria prevention and control, noting that traditional institutions, women, young people and grassroots stakeholders have critical roles to play in achieving sustainable health outcomes.

During her visit, HRM was also warmly received and hosted by the President of the Republic of Botswana, His Excellency, Duma Boko, and the
First Lady, Kaone Tumalano Boko.

The engagement provided an opportunity for meaningful conversations around humanitarian development, women’s wellbeing, maternal and newborn health, and potential areas of collaboration between Botswana and Nigeria.

Olori Temitope Enitan-Ogunwusi expressed profound appreciation for the exceptional hospitality extended to her, describing the experience as memorable and reflective of the warmth, friendship and spirit of African solidarity.

The visit also opened conversations around possible collaboration with Hopesalive Initiative for Africa (HAI), under the leadership of His Imperial Majesty, the Ooni of Ife, particularly in advancing humanitarian initiatives focused on mothers, newborns and vulnerable communities.

Her Regal Majesty’s Botswana engagement reinforces her commitment to malaria advocacy, community-led development and building partnerships that translate shared African aspirations into meaningful impact.

title: Natasha provides patrol van, computers for Ihima police
description:
From Adesuwa Tsan, Abuja
The senator representing Kogi Central, Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, has facilitated the provision of another patrol van and donated two computers to the Ihima Police Station in Okehi Local Government Area of Kogi State to strengthen security operations and improve police respons
content:
From Adesuwa Tsan, Abuja

The senator representing Kogi Central, Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, has facilitated the provision of another patrol van and donated two computers to the Ihima Police Station in Okehi Local Government Area of Kogi State to strengthen security operations and improve police response to emergencies.

According to a statement issued by her media office on Sunday, the latest intervention is aimed at improving police mobility, surveillance and administrative capacity, particularly in rural communities where difficult terrain and long distances often hamper security patrols and emergency response.

The senator noted that security agencies needed practical support and adequate equipment to discharge their responsibilities effectively, stressing that protecting lives and property required sustained investment in their operational capacity.

Speaking further, she emphasised the importance of grassroots security interventions and stronger collaboration between security agencies and communities, noting that effective policing required adequate logistics and modern operational tools.

“Security is not something we should leave entirely to the men and women in uniform without providing them with the necessary tools to do their jobs. Our police officers need functional equipment, reliable transportation and the right working environment to respond effectively to the security needs of our communities.”

She expressed hope that the patrol van would enable officers to respond promptly to distress calls and strengthen police presence across their areas of responsibility, while the two computers would support administrative and operational activities, including record-keeping, documentation of complaints, crime reporting, digital case management and retrieval of information required for investigations.

“This additional patrol van will strengthen their mobility and enable them to reach more communities, while the computers will support proper documentation, record management and other essential police operations,” she stated.

The senator explained that her commitment to security was driven by the need to ensure that communities were adequately protected, while security personnel had the tools required to carry out their duties.

“My commitment is to continue supporting initiatives that improve the safety and wellbeing of our people. Every community deserves to feel protected, and our security agencies deserve the necessary support to deliver on their responsibilities,” she said.

title: Two years in office: Okpebholo thanks God at Winners’ Chapel
description:
From Tony Osauzo, Benin
Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, yesterday led members of his administration and the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to give thanks to God for the second anniversary of his government at the Living Faith Church, also known as Winners’ Chapel, Benin City.
S
content:
From Tony Osauzo, Benin

Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, yesterday led members of his administration and the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to give thanks to God for the second anniversary of his government at the Living Faith Church, also known as Winners’ Chapel, Benin City.

Speaking on the theme “Unlocking the Supernatural”, drawn from Isaiah 8:18, the officiating minister, Pastor Emmanuel Ibiwoye, described the achievements of the Okpebholo administration in two years as evidence of God’s hand at work.

He said that holding the anniversary celebration in the house of God showed that the governor respected the supremacy of God, as he urged him to stay focused and not grow weary in pursuing his SHINE agenda for the development of Edo State.

Pastor Ibiwoye assured the government of the church’s continued prayers and called on residents of the state to continue to pray for the administration from their homes.

“This governor is a believer. This governor has time for God. He loves his people, especially the masses, and he cares about their wellbeing,” the pastor said.

“Governor Okpebholo is interested in making life comfortable and convenient for his people. He has helped and empowered many of them.

“As a church, we will join His Excellency to sing and dance and give God thanks for what He has done in the first two years of the Okpebholo administration in Edo State,” he added.

The Special Adviser to the Governor on Religious Matters, Apostle Sule Faraday, said the prayers of the saints had strengthened the governor to remain upright and do the right thing for the people of Edo State.

He noted that some who had criticised the governor before the 2024 governorship election had changed their views and were now supporting him, having seen the impact of his projects across the state.

“Before the election that brought Governor Okpebholo to office, he was criticised. But those critics have no choice but to join in supporting him because of the developmental achievements of the last two years,” Faraday said.

The governor was accompanied by his deputy, Dennis Idahosa; the Deputy State Chairman of the APC, Sylvester Aigboboh; and other senior government officials and party leaders.

Governor Okpebholo, his deputy and the party leaders danced to the altar in a joyful procession, thanking God for the progress recorded in the past two years and renewing the administration’s commitment to projects that improve the lives of Edo people.

content:
From Uchenna Inya, Abakaliki

Ebonyi State Governor Francis Nwifuru has stressed the importance of an independent judiciary in sustaining constitutional democracy, saying it checkmates the government and its excesses.

He also advocated the adoption of technology-driven processes in the administration of justice.

He noted that the judiciary serves as a critical institutional safeguard against possible excesses of government.

Nwifuru stated this at the weekend at the State High Court, Abakaliki, during the Special Court Session marking the commencement of the 2026/2027 Legal Year in Ebonyi State.

He said an efficient justice system must be capable of resolving disputes promptly and minimising unnecessary expenditure of resources.

“A justice system that cannot resolve disputes timely wastes resources. Technology offers us the opportunity to resolve some of these things. Digital filings and digital transcriptions help.

“The significance goes beyond governance. It helps to transact with various registries without recourse to location.

“An independent judiciary checkmates the government as well as its excesses. As a Governor, I recognise that the independence of the judiciary must be respected and allowed to perform its constitutional and professional mandate,” he stated.

He explained that the deployment of digital technology in judicial administration would reduce the challenges associated with physical processes, improve efficiency and enable legal practitioners and litigants to interact with relevant court registries more conveniently.

The Governor noted that his People’s Charter of Needs Agenda was committed to the ongoing reforms in the justice sector, pointing to several initiatives introduced to strengthen the administration of justice and improve the delivery of judicial services in the state.

According to him, the ongoing adoption of electronic filing, the establishment of the Moot Court, the creation of the Office of the Public Defender and the adoption of the Sexual Assault Bill are evidence of his government’s commitment to justice sector reforms.

He maintained that the reforms were designed to strengthen institutional capacity, promote access to justice and ensure that the justice system remained responsive to the needs and expectations of the people.

Earlier, the Chief Judge of Ebonyi State, Hon. Justice Elvis Ngene, informed the Governor that the state judiciary had recorded progress in several areas of judicial administration under his leadership.

Justice Ngene identified the modernisation of the machinery of justice through the deployment of technology, the protection of judicial integrity, the improvement of access to justice and the appointment of deserving judicial officers as some of the areas receiving attention.

Justice Ngene stated that official visits to correctional centres, regular human capital development, professional capacity building, infrastructural development and the improvement of court facilities were significant components of the judiciary’s activities within the last one year.

The Chief Judge emphasised that judicial integrity remained fundamental to the credibility and effectiveness of the justice system, stressing the need for all judicial officers and personnel to uphold the highest ethical standards.

He assured that the judiciary would continue to invest in professional development and institutional reforms despite the financial constraints confronting the institution.

“As part of our efforts to promote this, we shall, notwithstanding the leanness of our resources, continue to encourage continuous legal education and professional learning, strengthen administrative competence, promote responsible use of technology and insist upon the highest ethical standards from every person entrusted with judicial responsibilities,” he said.

He said the judiciary would continue to recognise the dedication of its workforce and prioritise measures that promote professionalism, institutional discipline and effective service delivery.

The post Independent judiciary checkmates government, excesses – Nwifuru appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

content:
A foreign tourist has accused the Emir of Daura in Katsina State, Umar Faruk Umar, of sexual assault during a visit to the monarch’s palace.

The tourist made the allegation in a post shared on Instagram by @beduinqa on Saturday, where she recounted what she described as a disturbing experience during her visit to Daura.

According to her account, the incident allegedly occurred on November 14 when she visited the emir’s palace. She claimed she was taken to an “elegant” room, where she and the monarch sat together on a couch and began a conversation.

The tourist said the Emir grabbed her hand and started playing with it.

“It was strange for me that he grabbed my hand and started playing with it. Then when we stood up, he hugged me, kissed my cheek (which was also surprising for me), and then he grabbed my boobs,” the tourist wrote on Instagram.

“That was a shock for me. I told him ’emir no, no, no, no; emir you cannot be touching’, but he was just laughing about it.”

The tourist said she was shocked by the behaviour of the emir, adding that she was not sexually assaulted while walking through the streets of Nigeria, even in crowded places.

In the video published by the tourist, the emir appears to be holding the hands of a woman, while they were sitting on a couch.

In the video, the emir could be seen caressing the hand of the woman.

After some seconds, it appeared that the emir hugged the woman and touched a part of her body.

Immediately the woman responded: “Emir, no, no, no, why are you touching? Emir, you can’t be touching…”

The tourist said she recorded the video through meta glasses, an eyewear that has the capacity to take video and pictures.

A review of her Instagram page shows that she arrived Nigeria on October 19.

During her stay in Nigeria, she also visited the palace of the Oba of Benin in Benin city, Edo State, Makoko in Lagos, Bauchi, and Kano

title: Oyetola orders probe into Bayelsa boat accident
description:
The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, has ordered an immediate investigation into the remote and direct causes of the fatal boat mishap that occurred on Friday in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha Community, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, claiming many lives.
Oye
content:
The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, has ordered an immediate investigation into the remote and direct causes of the fatal boat mishap that occurred on Friday in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha Community, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, claiming many lives.

Oyetola, in a statement released on Sunday through his media aide, Dr Bolaji Akinola, directed the National Inland Waterways Authority to “conduct a thorough investigation into the incident and submit its report to him.”

He further directed NIWA to work in collaboration with relevant government agencies and the Bayelsa State Government to ensure a comprehensive, transparent and credible investigation.

Describing the loss of life as worrisome and unacceptable, Oyetola said the Federal Government would no longer tolerate avoidable safety lapses on the nation’s waterways.

The minister expressed concern that passengers involved in the tragedy reportedly did not wear life jackets, recalling that he personally visited Bayelsa on May 2, 2025, to distribute 3,500 life jackets to water transport users as part of efforts to promote safety and protect lives.

He also raised concerns over the alleged absence of a passenger manifest, stressing that proper passenger documentation was a critical safety requirement that must be strictly enforced.

“Safety lapses on our waterways are no longer acceptable. The Federal Government will not fold its arms and watch its citizens perish on the waterways. We must get to the root of this tragedy and ensure that those responsible for enforcing safety regulations do their jobs,” Oyetola vowed.

Oyetola reiterated his call for the gradual phasing out of wooden boats by state governments and their replacement with safer, more durable and better-equipped fibreglass or fibre-reinforced plastic vessels, particularly for passenger transportation.

“I have consistently advocated for state governments to begin gradually phasing out wooden boats and replace them with safer, more durable and better-equipped fibreglass or fibre-reinforced plastic vessels, particularly for passenger transportation,” he said.

The minister disclosed that he had called the Bayelsa State Governor, Senator Douye Diri, to commiserate with him, the state government and families of the victims over the tragic incident.

Expressing sympathy to the bereaved families, Oyetola said the loss of life in such circumstances was deeply painful and that the grief of families who had lost loved ones was beyond words.

“Our thoughts and prayers are with the affected families at this difficult time. We also sympathise with all those who have been affected by this tragedy and pray for strength, comfort and the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss,” he said.

He prayed for the repose of the souls of the departed and for divine comfort for their families, urging all stakeholders to work together to ensure that such a tragedy never happens again.

On Saturday, The PUNCH reported that four mourners, including two children, died after a passenger boat conveying people to a burial ceremony capsized in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa, as 24 other passengers were rescued from the incident, which occurred at about 11 am on Friday near the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities.

The Bayelsa State Police Command said the boat was travelling from Ayama to Ukubie community when it reportedly developed a mechanical fault and capsized.

The post Oyetola orders probe into Bayelsa boat accident appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
Suspected political thugs have reportedly attacked members of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Elele, Ikwerre Local Government Area of Rivers State.

The party’s Publicity Secretary, Chizy Enyi, disclosed the incident in a post on his official Facebook page on Sunday, stating that the attack occurred on Saturday night.

Enyi alleged that the suspected attackers had recently returned from Kogi State, where they were allegedly spiritually fortified ahead of the 2027 general elections.

However, details surrounding the attack, including the number of victims and the extent of injuries or damage recorded, were not provided in his statement.

Sharing a video of the alleged attack, the ADC chieftain claimed the suspected thugs destroyed a house belonging to Hon. Emeka Woke.

He wrote, “These are the thugs in Ikwerre LGA who recently came back from Kogi State after spiritual fortification, attacking ADC members in Elele, Ikwerre LGA of Rivers State.

“They destroyed the house of Hon. Woke last night, and this morning they destroyed and burnt the canopies. This was made a reality after the threat by Samuel Nwanosike.

“The worst is that the police are aiding this useless act, as the DPO of Elele Police Station has ordered the arrest of ADC members, claiming there is a court order.”

Efforts by Very Nigerian to reach the Rivers State Police Command for comments were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report.

title: National security: GOC 5 Division, Gara, charges newly promoted colonels on professionalism, value addition
description:
From Scholastica Hir, Makurdi
The General Officer Commanding (GOC), 5 Division, Nigerian Army, Major General Moses Gara, has charged the newly promoted colonels to ensure greater professionalism, commitment and value addition in the discharge of their responsibilities.
Gara, who is also the Force Co
content:
From Scholastica Hir, Makurdi

The General Officer Commanding (GOC), 5 Division, Nigerian Army, Major General Moses Gara, has charged the newly promoted colonels to ensure greater professionalism, commitment and value addition in the discharge of their responsibilities.

Gara, who is also the Force Commander, Operation Whirl Stroke (OPWS), gave the charge during the pipping and decoration of five officers who were promoted from the rank of Lieutenant Colonel to Colonel.

He described the promotion as recognition of the officers’ hard work, dedication and exemplary service, saying it would serve as a morale booster for the division’s operational activities.

The GOC said the promotion came with greater responsibilities and higher expectations, urging them not to disappoint the Nigerian Army and the nation.

Gara said: “As you have already observed, we have just finished the decoration of our newly promoted officers, as approved by the Army Council under the guidance of the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu.

“This promotion is a testament of the hard work of the officers who were considered for the promotion and for the division, it’s going to be a very big morale booster for us. If you have seen the faces of the officers that were decorated, you can see that they were rejoicing, they were highly motivated.

“But I must also add that it comes with a lot of responsibility, which we have reminded them not to fail the army authorities on the confidence that has been imposed on them to discharge the responsibilities of their new ranks.

“But by and large, it also motivates those who are aspiring to be promoted. We also have Colonels who are aspiring to be practitioners in the DIV and by the special grace of God, I am confident that they will pass the benchmark that has been set and it will be a very big plus for the division in the discharge of our operational activities.

“I have told them that once they add value to the army in all that they are called to do that the army will always add value to them and so that must be their watchword to ensure that in all that they do they bring value on board,” he said.

Also speaking, the 5 Division Mess President, Brigadier General Murtala Abdulsalam, urged the newly promoted officers to see their promotion as a reflection of their hard work and the confidence the Nigerian Army had in them.

Abdullahi urged them to regard the promotion not only as an achievement but as a call to greater service and sacrifice to the nation, and charged them to be worthy ambassadors of the Nigerian Army, particularly in discipline, courage and selfless service.

He appreciated the wives of the officers for their unwavering support in sustaining the family while their husbands carried out military assignments.

The Logistics Component Commander, Operation Whirl Stroke, Brigadier-General Charles Akpuogwu, congratulated the newly promoted officers, urging them to deploy their knowledge, expertise and emotional intelligence and to demonstrate greater commitment.

Akpuogwu said their promotion went beyond personal achievement but was an invitation for them to move beyond tactical considerations and prepare for higher operational and command assignments.

He urged them to be more professional and firm in their leadership, guiding their subordinates and supporting them.

Speaking on behalf of the newly promoted officers, Colonel John Ajiya appreciated God, the Chief of Army Staff, the GOC 5 Division, colleagues and families for their contributions to their training and service, assuring that they were committed to carrying out their duties with a full sense of responsibility and professionalism, and to adding value to the Nigerian Army and the security of the nation.

The post National security: GOC 5 Division, Gara, charges newly promoted colonels on professionalism, value addition appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Trade ministry cracks down on cheating measures in Ogun
description: The Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment, through its Weights and Measures Department, has intensified regulatory enforcement in Ogun State as part of its ongoing 2026 National Surveillance Exercise aimed at promoting transparency, measurement accuracy, and consumer protection across c
content:
The Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment, through its Weights and Measures Department, has intensified regulatory enforcement in Ogun State as part of its ongoing 2026 National Surveillance Exercise aimed at promoting transparency, measurement accuracy, and consumer protection across commercial transactions.

The ministry noted that the move reflects the Federal Government’s commitment to safeguarding the financial interests of consumers, businesses and the government by ensuring that all weighing and measuring instruments meet strict legal and technical standards.

This is contained in a statement made available to PUNCH Online on Sunday.

The Director of the ministry’s Weights and Measures Department, Dr Salim Mohammed, stated that the initiative is a joint effort between its national, zonal and state officials to cover key economic establishments across both the oil and gas and non-oil sectors.

He stated the significance of effective surveillance and compliance in preventing short measurements, eliminating unfair commercial advantages and building public confidence in the Nigerian marketplace,

“This is a coordinated effort between national, zonal, and state officials in Ogun State to cover key economic establishments across both the oil and gas and non-oil sectors, including manufacturing plants, petroleum depots, retail outlets, and industrial facilities.

“We visited some major manufacturing firms in the state such as Golden Terra Soya Oil, African GB Food Manufacturing Nigeria Limited and CWAY Nigeria Limited, to confirm that the actual quantities of products match the declarations printed on their packaging and ensure fair trade,” Mohammed said.

In the oil and gas sector, the surveillance team will focus on petroleum dispensing, storage, distribution and custody transfer equipment, while in the non-oil sector will focus on food processing, wholesale and retail operations.

On the former, the director noted that “minor calibration errors can trigger massive financial losses due to high transaction volumes, noting that inspections in the non-oil sector are to target food processing, wholesale, and retail operations to maintain a level playing field for legitimate businesses.”

In his remarks, the Zonal Coordinator, Awalu Uba, said that the department was “reinforcing the principle that manufacturers and distributors have a responsibility to ensure that the quantity of products supplied to consumers corresponds with the declarations made on their packaging and complies with applicable legal requirements.”

On his part, the State Coordinator, Bala Panti, said that through the coordinated effort, the department aims to “contribute to a more transparent business environment and ensure that Nigerians receive the exact value and quantity of goods for which they pay.”

title: 2027: Any party saying I’ve stepped down is working for Tinubu  -  Atiku
description:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has accused political parties spreading claims that he has withdrawn from the 2027 presidential race of working in favour of President Bola Tinubu.



Atiku described the reports as false and insisted that he remained in the contest to win the election.



In a s
content:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has accused political parties spreading claims that he has withdrawn from the 2027 presidential race of working in favour of President Bola Tinubu.

Atiku described the reports as false and insisted that he remained in the contest to win the election.

In a statement issued on Sunday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the former vice-president said no group claiming to be his supporters had the authority to announce his withdrawal.

“Any party promoting the lie that I have stepped down is doing Tinubu’s work. Every false withdrawal story tries to clear his strongest opponent from the field,” he said.

Atiku added that he had not made any decision to leave the race, dismissing claims attributed to individuals presenting themselves as his supporters.

“Putting my name on a placard does not make someone my supporter. Putting a lie in that person’s mouth does not make it my decision,” he said.

He warned that any attempt to remove him from the contest through fabricated declarations would deny Nigerians the opportunity to choose their preferred candidate.

“If I am not on the ballot, Bola Tinubu might as well wait for a coronation. But I am in this race to win, and Nigerians will have their choice,” he said.

The former vice-president also accused those behind the reports of using misinformation to weaken the opposition, alleging that the tactic was intended to benefit the ruling All Progressives Congress.

He urged opposition parties seeking to defeat Tinubu to focus on persuading voters rather than circulating claims about rival candidates.

“Anyone serious about defeating the APC should take their case to voters. Manufacturing supporters and circulating false declarations will not defeat Tinubu. It only serves him,” Atiku said.

On his campaign activities, Atiku said his Affordable Life agenda remained focused on addressing the economic difficulties confronting Nigerian households.

He cited the rising cost of food and transportation as issues his campaign intended to address, saying the campaign was reaching communities across the country.

“Hunger and poverty are not on social media. They are in our markets, our homes and every community where families struggle to afford food and transport,” he said.

Atiku urged his supporters to remain mobilised ahead of the election and ensure they had their Permanent Voter Cards.

He reiterated that he would not withdraw in favour of any other candidate, declaring that the contest would be decided by voters.

“I do not need anyone to step down for me, and I am stepping down for no one,” he said.

The statement concluded with Atiku expressing confidence that he would defeat Tinubu at the ballot box on January 16, 2027.

title: Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29
description: The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 29, with over 50 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals.Governor Douye Diri disclosed this during a condolence visit by Vice President Kashim Shettima.Diri explained that the fin
content:
The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 29, with over 50 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals.

Governor Douye Diri disclosed this during a condolence visit by Vice President Kashim Shettima.

Diri explained that the final casualty figure had yet to be established as efforts were still ongoing to recover the affected vessel.

He, however, said some passengers might still be trapped inside the boat.

The governor described the incident as avoidable, alleging that the boat was not fit for river travel and had operated from an unauthorised loading point.

He said the state government had taken responsibility for the medical bills and feeding of the survivors.

Diri thanked President Tinubu for the concern shown by the Presidency since the incident occurred, particularly the Vice President’s visit to the state.

He used the occasion to appeal for Federal Government support for the construction of more roads across Bayelsa, noting that improved road access would reduce the dependence of some communities on water transportation.

The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, when a boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw.

The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, adding that the boat was travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony on Friday, when it capsized at about 11 a.m.

The boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways, according to a preliminary police report.

Following the incident, rescue operations were launched, with several passengers rescued while others were initially reported missing.

A survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger boat, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings.

President Bola Tinubu expressed condolences to the families of the victims, describing the incident as tragic and directing relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery efforts.

He also approved ₦250 million in support for the families of the victims.

The post Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29 appeared first on Channels Television.

content:
From Ndubuisi Orji, Abuja

The House of Representatives Committee on the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) has congratulated its chairman, Muktar Betara, on the occasion of his 60th birthday.

The members of the committee, in a statement by the deputy chairman, Emeka Chinedu, and 150 others, lauded Betara for his contribution to nation-building and his commitment to legislative excellence.

The FCT Committee chairman, who was recently honoured as The Sun Newspaper’s House of Representatives Member of the Year, 2026, represents Biu, Bayo, Kwaya-Kusar and Shani Federal Constituency of Borno State in the Green Chamber.

According to the lawmakers, Betara, a five-time member of the House, has over the years demonstrated courage in leadership, as well as commitment to public service.

“As Chairman of our Committee, you have demonstrated exemplary leadership, uncommon dedication and an impressive capacity to build consensus, inspire confidence and deliver results.

“Your commitment to the work of the Committee and the development of the Federal Capital Territory reflects your deep understanding of public service and the responsibility entrusted to you.

“Your contributions to nation-building and your enduring commitment to the people of Biu, Bayo, Kwaya-Kusar and Shani Federal Constituency of Borno State have further distinguished your record of service.

“We are equally delighted to celebrate your well-deserved recognition as The Sun Newspaper’s House of Representatives Member of the Year, 2026.

“This prestigious honour is a fitting recognition of your legislative contributions, outstanding leadership and the positive impact of your service. At 60, you stand as an inspiring example of purposeful leadership, resilience and service with distinction.

“We are proud to be associated with your leadership and privileged to serve alongside you,” they stated.

description:
Juventus moved into the top six in Serie A on Sunday with a thumping 4-0 victory over Venezia as their recent upturn in form continued in Turin.
Goals from Nick Woltemade, Teun Koopmeiners, Juan Cabal and Randal Kolo Muani moved Juve up to sixth place on 21 points, 11 behind leaders Lazio, as the Bi
content:
Juventus moved into the top six in Serie A on Sunday with a thumping 4-0 victory over Venezia as their recent upturn in form continued in Turin.

Goals from Nick Woltemade, Teun Koopmeiners, Juan Cabal and Randal Kolo Muani moved Juve up to sixth place on 21 points, 11 behind leaders Lazio, as the Bianconeri extended their unbeaten run to four matches in all competitions.

Juventus coach Luciano Spalletti faced scrutiny after an underwhelming start to the season, with Antonio Conte linked with a return to his former club during the international break.

But Spalletti celebrated his 600th Serie A match as a coach, making him just the sixth manager to reach the milestone, with a resounding victory at the Allianz Stadium.

A dull first half ended with boos from the home crowd, but Woltemade’s introduction after the break sparked the game into life as he pounced on a loose ball to smash home his second league goal in two games before turning provider for Koopmeiners’ whipped finish.

Cabal headed home Juve’s third before Kolo Muani won and converted a penalty to complete the rout, with all four goals coming between the 53rd and 71st minute.

Champions Inter visit Atalanta and AC Milan host Frosinone in the evening kick-offs on Sunday, while Bologna face Udinese and Sassuolo host Genoa in the afternoon.

AFP

title: Ododo’s approval of ADC campaign venue exonerates Tinubu — Rights Group
description:
The Foundation for Democracy in Africa (FDA) has commended the Kogi State Government for approving campaign venues for opposition parties, including the African Democratic Congress (ADC), without bureaucratic obstruction.
In a statement signed by Mallam Bala Nasir, the civil rights group said Govern
content:
The Foundation for Democracy in Africa (FDA) has commended the Kogi State Government for approving campaign venues for opposition parties, including the African Democratic Congress (ADC), without bureaucratic obstruction.

In a statement signed by Mallam Bala Nasir, the civil rights group said Governor Usman Ododo’s action has punctured allegations that the ruling party instructed its governors to deny opposition parties access to public facilities for rallies.

The group maintained that the development clears President Bola Ahmed Tinubu of opposition claims that he masterminded a plot to stifle political opposition.

“Governor Usman Ododo is one of the governors closest to the President and would have been the first to implement such an order if it existed,” the statement noted. “By this singular action of the Kogi State Governor, President Tinubu is hereby exonerated from the claims by the opposition that the ruling APC and the President directed governors to deny the opposition venues for their rallies.”

Describing Governor Ododo as an asset to the All Progressives Congress (APC), the FDA urged other governors to emulate his approach, noting that granting venues to opponents does not translate to losing an election, but rather strengthens democratic norms.

The foundation also charged the opposition to reciprocate the governor’s political tolerance by ensuring peaceful campaigns and reining in supporters to prevent lawlessness.

Lauding Ododo as a patriotic leader, the FDA warned politicians against making inflammatory remarks capable of disrupting the peaceful coexistence of Kogi residents. It noted that the governor’s leadership has changed the state’s public image for the better since he assumed office.

Furthermore, the group praised Ododo for his proactive stance on security, acknowledging Kogi’s strategic geographic location and the necessity of sustained investments in public safety. It urged the governor to remain focused on maintaining peace across the state.

title: I’ve Not Been Served With Court Injunction, Jimmy Odukoya Tells Fountain Of Life Members
description: The Senior Pastor of the Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, has said he has not been formally served with the injunction reportedly restraining him from presenting himself as the church’s Senior Pastor.Odukoya made this known on Sunday while addressing members of the church during a servi
content:
The Senior Pastor of the Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, has said he has not been formally served with the injunction reportedly restraining him from presenting himself as the church’s Senior Pastor.

Odukoya made this known on Sunday while addressing members of the church during a service, amid an escalating leadership dispute between him and members of the church’s Board of Trustees.

The pastor said although he had heard about the court order, he had neither seen it nor received formal service of the court process.

“I heard there was an injunction against me. I heard, but I have not seen it, and I have not been served. They said that there was no substituted service. Legally, I have not been served,” he said.

Addressing the worshippers, he acknowledged their continued support amid the controversy and emphasised their importance to the church.

“You know there is no Fountain without you. You are Fountain of Life, and as long as you would have me, I will continue to speak for you. I will continue to stand for you,” he said.

Osukoya was at the centre of a leadership crisis at the church following an interim order reportedly granted by the Lagos State High Court on November 18, following an application by the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church.

The court, presided over by Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin, granted the trustees permission to commence legal proceedings against Odukoya under the pre-action protocol of the High Court of Lagos State.

The application also sought to restrain him from presenting himself as the church’s Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head, as well as interfering with its administration, governance and activities.

The order further restrained him from disrupting the church’s affairs, either personally or through representatives, pending compliance with the court’s pre-action requirements.

The court also directed that the originating processes and accompanying documents be served on Odukoya, while preserving his right to challenge the order.

Leadership Tussle

The dispute followed the November 17 announcement by a faction of the church’s Board of Trustees withdrawing recognition of Odukoya as Senior Pastor and appointing Pastor Rotimi Okpaise to oversee its interim spiritual and administrative leadership.

The trustees cited a December 2021 video recording in which the church’s late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, reportedly identified Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor.

They also raised concerns about the circumstances surrounding Jimmy Odukoya’s appointment in September 2023, alleging that relevant information about the succession arrangement was not disclosed to the board at the time.

However, Odukoya rejected the purported removal, describing it as unconstitutional and insisting that his appointment remained valid.

In a counter-statement, his camp argued that the trustees behind the decision had themselves been asked to resign in March 2026 over alleged violations of the church’s constitution.

Despite the legal dispute, Odukoya reaffirmed his commitment to the congregation, assuring members that he would continue to stand with them and speak on their behalf.

title: Awoyaya explosion: Doherty accuses Lagos APM guber candidate of plagiarising his statement
description:
The Lagos State governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Funso Doherty, has accused his Action Peoples Movement counterpart, Laja Laoye, of plagiarising his statement on the Awoyaya filling station explosion.



Doherty made the allegation in a post on X on Sunday, after accusing L
content:
The Lagos State governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Funso Doherty, has accused his Action Peoples Movement counterpart, Laja Laoye, of plagiarising his statement on the Awoyaya filling station explosion.

Doherty made the allegation in a post on X on Sunday, after accusing Laoye of reproducing almost identical wording in his reaction to the incident, which occurred on Saturday, November 21.

One person was reportedly killed after fire engulfed Sunbeth filling station at Awoyaya bus stop in the Ibeju-Lekki area of Lagos.

Videos circulating on social media showed a tanker catching fire within the filling station before an explosion, while people and vehicles were seen close to the scene.

Doherty had earlier reacted to the incident in a post on X at 10:09 am on Sunday, expressing sympathy for those affected and calling for measures to prevent a recurrence.

“I was saddened to learn of the explosion and fire in the Awoyaya area of Lagos this weekend. As more details emerge about this unfortunate incident, our thoughts and prayers are with those who were injured and those who have suffered devastating loss,” he wrote.

He added that authorities should investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident, learn from it and take corrective action.

“As we lend a hand of solidarity, sympathy and assistance to all those affected, we must also quickly work to understand why this occurred, learn from it, take remedial steps and institute punitive measures where appropriate to prevent future occurrences,” Doherty said.

About an hour later, at 11:01 am, Laoye published his own statement on the explosion, also expressing sympathy for victims and calling for an investigation into its cause.

In his post, the APM candidate wrote: “I was deeply saddened to learn of the explosion and fire that occurred in the Awoyaya area of Lagos this weekend. As more details emerge about this unfortunate incident, my thoughts and prayers are with the injured and with all those who have suffered devastating losses.”

He also called for remedial measures and appropriate sanctions where negligence or wrongdoing was established.

“It is equally important that we urgently establish the root causes of this tragedy. We must learn the necessary lessons, implement immediate remedial measures, and apply appropriate sanctions where negligence or wrongdoing is established, so that such incidents are prevented in the future,” Laoye said.

Doherty subsequently returned to X at about 1:49 pm to accuse his opponent of copying his statement.

“Imitation, they say, is the sincerest form of flattery. But this should not extend to plagiarism, especially when presented as an authentic, heartfelt message in tragic circumstances,” he wrote.

He said Laoye had posted a “near-identical message” approximately one hour after his own statement and urged social media users to compare the two posts.

“The APM Lagos Governorship candidate posted this near-identical message on X approximately one hour after I posted mine on the same subject. You be the judge,” Doherty added.

Laoye had not publicly responded to the accusation as of the time of filing this report.

The post Awoyaya explosion: Doherty accuses Lagos APM guber candidate of plagiarising his statement appeared first on Vanguard News.
