title: NDLEA arrests South African golfer, Kenyan chef at Lagos airport over 50kg cannabis shipment
description:
Intercepts 160 explosives bound for Zamfara
______________________________________________________________________
From Godwin Tsa, Abuja
A 37-year-old South African professional golfer, Grobler Henlo, and a 25-year-old Kenyan chef, Abubakar Faiza Njambi, have been arrested by the National Drug Law
content:
Intercepts 160 explosives bound for Zamfara

______________________________________________________________________

From Godwin Tsa, Abuja

A 37-year-old South African professional golfer, Grobler Henlo, and a 25-year-old Kenyan chef, Abubakar Faiza Njambi, have been arrested by the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Ikeja, Lagos, for their alleged roles in a syndicate’s attempt to smuggle 50.40 kilogrammes of Loud, a potent strain of cannabis, into Nigeria.

The agency’s Director of Media and Advocacy, Femi Babafemi, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday.

According to Babafemi, Grobler was arrested on Sunday, October 11, 2026, exactly one month before an American professional basketballer, Greene Da’monte Khiree, was intercepted at the same airport on Wednesday, November 11, with 33.95kg of the same substance.

Grobler arrived from South Africa on a South African Airways flight and was intercepted at the Terminal 2 arrival hall.

A search of the two boxes in his possession revealed 46 parcels of Loud with a gross weight of 50.40kg.

Investigators found that although the boxes were with him, they bore the luggage tags of his fellow courier, Njambi, who had collected two other boxes bearing his tags from the conveyor belt and left the airport.

The statement described the tag swap as a deliberate ploy by the syndicate to frustrate identification of ownership, allowing each courier to deny boxes bearing their name if intercepted.

In a preliminary interview, the golfer, who travelled in business class while Njambi flew economy, said he was recruited by a South African associate, Shanel, who linked him with other syndicate members he never met.

He said a driver picked him up from his home, handed him four boxes and took him to the airport, where he was told to meet the Kenyan woman and swap luggage tags. He claimed he was promised 5,000 South African rand on successful delivery.

Babafemi said tracking devices were found on the boxes and on the golfer’s mobile phone. Similar devices were found in the bags abandoned by the American basketballer a month later, which he said showed how closely the cartels monitor their couriers and consignments.

Njambi’s passport biodata page, recovered from the golfer’s phone, was profiled and she was placed on the NDLEA watchlist.

She was arrested at the departure boarding gate of the Lagos airport on Thursday, October 15, as she tried to board a South African Airways flight back to Kenya.

The private chef told operatives she was recruited by a man, and that a friend in Kenya persuaded her to accept an offer of US$8,000 on successful delivery.

She said she left Kenya for South Africa on October 4, stayed in a hotel for about a week, and met the golfer at the airport on October 11, where he handed her two of the four boxes before they checked them in under their respective tags.

She claimed that on arrival in Lagos she collected the two boxes bearing the golfer’s tags, after which a driver took her to a hotel in the Lekki area.

The claim tag for the two boxes bearing her name, which she abandoned at the airport, was recovered from her hand luggage. Both suspects identified each other during an identification parade.

At the import shed of the Lagos airport on Friday, November 13, operatives intercepted a consolidated consignment from the United Kingdom aboard an Allied Air flight. A freight agent, Sobowale Oladayo, was arrested when he presented himself for clearance.

Examination of the shipment led to the recovery of 10 parcels of synthetic cannabinoid (10.10kg); 27 packs of marshmallow (318.80kg); and precursor chemicals comprising 11 containers of N,N-Dimethylformamide (DMF) (18.90kg), 10 containers of 5-Bromo-1-Pentane (8.05kg) and seven containers of Potassium Carbonate (7.60kg). The total gross weight was 363.45kg.

In a follow-up operation on Saturday, November 14, the consignee, Kareem Issa, a.k.a. Ola, 35, was arrested when he came to take delivery at the premises of a logistics company in a grey Lexus 460 SUV, accompanied by two others.

A plumber by profession who lives on Lagos Island, he allegedly posed as a senior security officer, routinely blaring a siren fitted to his vehicle on visits to the logistics company to avoid attention.

On Tuesday, November 17, operatives on patrol along the Abuja-Kaduna expressway at Jere arrested a 35-year-old man, Lawali Muhammad, with 160 pieces of explosives bound for Zamfara State. The intended recipient, Aliyu Mohammed, 30, was arrested in a follow-up operation in Gusau the same day.

On the same axis, two suspects, Yusuf Magaji and Buhari Yusuf, 32, were arrested with 6,900 tablets of tramadol 225mg, 20,000 tablets of diazepam and 25,000 tablets of Exol-5.

Along the Zaria-Kano expressway at Gwargwaje, Zaria, operatives recovered 627,500 capsules of tramadol, weighing 21.50kg, from a Hummer bus whose driver abandoned it and fled on sighting the officers.

In Ogun State, a woman, Esther Ogundipe, was arrested on Thursday, November 19, with two locally made firearms and five live cartridges during a raid on a drug joint at Eleweron, Abeokuta.

Two days earlier, on Tuesday, November 17, two women, Balikis Ogunbiyi and Omobola Ajani, were arrested in a raid in Ilaro with 7.4 grams of cocaine, 638 grams of cannabis and 5.9 grams of methamphetamine.

Tonnes of cannabis in Osun, Ondo

In Osun State, a 43-year-old man, Francis Oduke, was arrested along the Ikire/Ibadan expressway, Ikire, with 359 bags of skunk weighing 4,627.7kg, concealed under a load of granite in a truck.

In neighbouring Ondo State, a Kano-bound truck carrying 93 bags of cannabis weighing 1,045kg was intercepted on Monday, November 16, along the Zango/Ado expressway, Akure.

The vehicle, loaded at Ogbese town, had been monitored following sustained intelligence gathering. Four suspects, Adamu Yerima, 19; Mohammed Mohammed, 19; Nura Mohammed, 25; and Usman Mohammed, were arrested.

Edo: Emmanuel Eze, 48, was arrested on Friday, November 20, with 11½ bags of cannabis weighing 156kg at Aduwawa community, Benin City.

Katsina: Abbas Bello, 39, was arrested on Tuesday, November 17, in the Gafai area with 148 blocks of cannabis weighing 72kg, hidden in the boot of his white Honda Accord.

Abia: On Wednesday, November 18, operatives raided the shop of Oluebube Innocent, 25, at Amankwa Street, Obingwa LGA, and recovered 2kg of cannabis from a hole dug into the floor and covered with ceramic tiles.

Rivers: Peter Sunday, 46, who is physically challenged, was arrested on Tuesday, November 17, with 300 grams of cannabis in a raid at Eneka.

Marwa: Cartels changing faces, not tactics

Commending officers of the MMIA, Kaduna, Ogun, Osun, Ondo, Edo, Katsina, Abia and Rivers commands, the NDLEA Chairman/Chief Executive Officer, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (Rtd), said the arrests of the golfer and the Kenyan woman, coming in the same period as that of the American basketballer, showed that “the cartels are changing faces but not their tactics”, according to Babafemi.

“The two cases show a trend in which international drug cartels now recruit sportsmen and other professionals as couriers, in the hope that their profiles will shield them from scrutiny,” Marwa said. “The NDLEA has a clear message for such syndicates: no profession, passport or travel class will provide cover for drug trafficking through Nigeria’s ports of entry.”

He urged officers at all ports of entry to remain vigilant and professional, and directed commands to balance drug supply reduction with demand reduction, especially War Against Drug Abuse (WADA) sensitisation campaigns in schools, workplaces, worship centres and communities.

Over the past week, commands continued WADA sensitisation activities. These included lectures to students and staff of Local Government Primary School, Ebute Ikorodu, Lagos; Government Girls Unity College, Birnin Kebbi; and Community Secondary School, Usa, Enugu Ezike. The Ondo State Command also paid an advocacy visit to the Deji of Akure, Oba Aladetoyinbo Ogunlade Adelusi, Odundun II.

The post NDLEA arrests South African golfer, Kenyan chef at Lagos airport over 50kg cannabis shipment appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Tinubu Approves ₦250m For Families Of Bayelsa Boat Accident Victims
description: President Bola Tinubu has approved ₦250 million in support for families of victims of the boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.Vice President Kashim Shettima announced the intervention during a condolence visit to Bayelsa, following the accident, which occurred on No
content:
President Bola Tinubu has approved ₦250 million in support for families of victims of the boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.

Vice President Kashim Shettima announced the intervention during a condolence visit to Bayelsa, following the accident, which occurred on November 20, 2026, around Oweikorogha community and claimed 29 lives.

The boat was conveying passengers from Ayama community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony when it capsized.

Speaking at the Bayelsa State Government House in Yenagoa, Shettima said he was in the state on the President’s directive to convey the Federal Government’s condolences and obtain further details about the incident.

He described the accident as a national tragedy, saying the country must not become accustomed to such incidents to the extent of losing its sense of compassion for affected families.

The Vice President also said the President had directed relevant federal agencies to work with the Bayelsa State Government in providing support to the victims and their families.

According to him, the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) has been instructed to provide assistance to those affected by the accident.

Shettima further disclosed that the President had directed the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy to ensure that appropriate safety measures were put in place to protect people travelling through riverine communities.

He added that the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) had also been directed to procure boats to support transportation in riverine areas.

Earlier, Governor Douye Diri said the death toll had risen to 29, while more than 51 survivors had been accounted for.

Diri explained that the final casualty figure had yet to be established because efforts were still ongoing to recover the capsized vessel. He said some passengers might still be trapped inside the boat.

The governor described the incident as avoidable, alleging that the boat was not fit for river travel and had operated from an unauthorised loading point.

He said the state government had taken responsibility for the medical bills and feeding of the survivors.

Diri also expressed appreciation to President Tinubu for the concern shown by the Presidency since the incident occurred, particularly the Vice President’s visit to the state.

He used the occasion to appeal for Federal Government support for the construction of more roads across Bayelsa, arguing that improved road access would reduce the dependence of some communities on water transportation.

Shettima, in his remarks, said the Governor had established a commission of inquiry to investigate the circumstances surrounding the accident, stressing that its findings must be implemented.

The Vice President also commended the state government’s response and called for stronger measures to protect people who depend on waterways for transportation.

The boat accident has renewed concerns about water transport safety in Bayelsa, where many riverine communities rely on boats to access neighbouring communities and other parts of the state.

The Federal Government’s announced interventions include financial support for bereaved families, assistance to survivors, and proposed measures to improve transportation safety in riverine areas.

The post Tinubu Approves ₦250m For Families Of Bayelsa Boat Accident Victims appeared first on Channels Television.

title: EPL: Fernandes breaks silence on alleged rift with ex-Man Utd boss
description:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has dismissed reports of a breakdown in his relationship with former manager Michael Carrick, insisting that his comments after their 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como were not intended as a criticism of his former boss.
Fernandes said there was no disagre
content:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has dismissed reports of a breakdown in his relationship with former manager Michael Carrick, insisting that his comments after their 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como were not intended as a criticism of his former boss.

Fernandes said there was no disagreement between them, explaining that Carrick understood his concerns and did not take offence at his post-match remarks.

The Portuguese midfielder made the clarification in an interview with Sky Sports on Sunday, days after his comments sparked speculation about tension between the pair.

PUNCH had earlier reported that Fernandes and Carrick appeared to disagree over Manchester United’s tactical approach following the defeat to Como, which intensified scrutiny of the former manager.

Speaking to TNT Sports after the match, Fernandes questioned the decision not to press Como aggressively, arguing that allowing the Italian side too much possession had helped them gain confidence and control the game.

“It’s a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, but sometimes when you give too much of the ball to these teams, they get confidence,” he said.

The comments came after Fernandes was left out of the starting line-up for the first Premier League game of the season, having last started a match from the bench on May 4, 2025, in a 4-3 defeat to Brentford.

He was subsequently omitted from the squad for the Premier League encounter against Bournemouth, but insisted the decision had nothing to do with his comments about the Como defeat.

Fernandes said Carrick personally informed him that he would not start against Bournemouth and explained that the decision was based on the team’s poor performances.

“The manager came to speak to me after that game, or before the Bournemouth game, to say, ‘Look, I’m not going to start you tomorrow’ and everything.

“There’s nothing to do with the words of Como; I know people will make it around that. I just want to tell you that we need to change something, I need to make a change, performances have not been great, so I just want you to know that there’s nothing to do with that,” he said.

The United captain added that he approached Carrick to clarify his remarks and ensure they were not misunderstood.

“I told him, ‘I think that you probably got our words in the wrong way, and you might be upset with me, and rightly so, if you got it in the way everyone is speaking about it’. And he said, ‘Bruno, I’m not; I just put you on the bench because I thought it was the best for the team,’” Fernandes recalled.

He said his return to the starting line-up in the following match further showed that there was no fallout between them.

United have since sacked Carrick and appointed former United States men’s national team coach Mauricio Pochettino as his successor.

Pochettino, who previously managed Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, has already made his expectations clear to the United players, according to Fernandes.

The midfielder described the Argentine as a positive but demanding manager who wants the club to succeed.

“He’s someone who likes to bring a very good energy to the team, someone very positive, very strong, strict; he said straight away that he won’t allow us to not give him what he demands from the team, from each player,” Fernandes said.

“He wants the club to succeed so much, he wants to win games, and that’s pretty clear and obvious by the way he and his staff speak and want us to improve.”

Fernandes also disclosed that he nearly joined Tottenham in 2019 when Pochettino was in charge, revealing that he held talks with the club’s board about a possible move.

He said the prospect of playing alongside Harry Kane, Dele Alli and Heung-Min Son had appealed to him.

“Obviously I was a very young player who was eager to come to the Premier League. They had Kane there, they had Dele Alli, Son; the chance of playing with those players in front was very attractive,” he said.

Fernandes joined Manchester United from Sporting Lisbon in January 2020 and has since established himself as one of the club’s key players.

He was named PFA Player of the Year in August after recording a league-record 21 assists last season.

Manchester United are currently 19th in the Premier League table with eight points from 10 matches, while Liverpool occupy fifth position with 18 points, 10 behind leaders Arsenal.

The post EPL: Fernandes breaks silence on alleged rift with ex-Man Utd boss appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Alex Ekwueme varsity, European Union launch agric sustainability project
description:
From Uchenna Inya, Abakaliki
Alex Ekwueme Federal University, Ndufu-Alike (AE-FUNAI), Ebonyi State, has launched a 12-month European Union-backed agricultural sustainability project.
The initiative is aimed at equipping farmers, processors and other food value chain actors with digital tools to meas
content:
From Uchenna Inya, Abakaliki

Alex Ekwueme Federal University, Ndufu-Alike (AE-FUNAI), Ebonyi State, has launched a 12-month European Union-backed agricultural sustainability project.

The initiative is aimed at equipping farmers, processors and other food value chain actors with digital tools to measure carbon emissions, reduce production costs and improve access to premium export markets.

The project, titled Enhancing Food Value Chain Sustainability through Digital Life Cycle Assessment Training (Digital LCA), is implemented under the STREAMING initiative funded by the European Union through the Horizon Europe programme, with emphasis on strengthening sustainable trade between Europe and Africa through innovation and technology.

Speaking at the inception workshop, the Vice-Chancellor of AE-FUNAI, Prof. Daniel Nwachukwu, represented by Prof. Robert Onyeneke, said Nigeria’s agricultural sector, despite employing millions and contributing significantly to food security, remained underperforming in export markets because of evolving sustainability requirements.

Nwachukwu said international buyers and regulators, particularly in Europe, increasingly demanded evidence of the environmental impact of food production, including carbon emissions, water and land use, post-harvest losses and product traceability, stressing the need for Nigerian producers to adapt to the changing requirements.

He said the project would develop Nigeria-adapted digital learning materials and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) calculators to enable farmers and food processors to measure the environmental impact of their activities, improve production efficiency and meet international market standards.

According to him, the initiative would test the digital tools through two pilot groups, including participants operating in areas with limited internet connectivity, before training at least 100 learners, with women accounting for a minimum of 40 per cent.

The Vice-Chancellor said the workshop was designed not merely to introduce the project but also to listen to stakeholders, identify challenges across agricultural value chains and jointly determine commodities requiring priority attention, while ensuring that participants’ data were protected during baseline assessments.

The Project Coordinator, Prof. Robert Onyeneke, said Nigeria needed to move beyond producing food primarily for domestic consumption to developing the capacity to generate sufficient surplus for international markets, noting that agricultural exports remained relatively low despite the sector’s importance to employment and livelihoods.

Onyeneke explained that LCA would enable farmers and processors to assess environmental impacts from production through processing, transportation and consumption, helping them to identify inefficient practices, reduce emissions, minimise waste and improve competitiveness.

He said the project would develop simplified digital calculators through which farmers could input information such as cultivated land area, harvest volumes, fertiliser usage and energy consumption to estimate their environmental footprints and improve business decisions.

The project coordinator added that the initiative would also help farmers to understand the actual costs of production, including labour, land preparation, inputs and transportation, to enable them to determine profitability, optimise production and avoid selling produce without accurately knowing their costs.

The Dean of the Faculty of Agriculture, Prof. Jane Munonye, described the initiative as a significant research opportunity, noting that its European Union backing would strengthen international collaboration, improve research capacity and open opportunities for publications in reputable scientific journals.

Munonye, who commended Onyeneke and his team for attracting research grants and partnerships, urged stakeholders to take advantage of the project to improve agricultural production, processing and market access, while promoting innovation and commercialisation.

The Deputy Director of Livestock in the Ministry of Agriculture, Mrs Chidinma Obi Okoye, also pledged the ministry’s technical support, emphasising the importance of value addition, standardisation, modern processing equipment and solar-powered drying technology to improve produce quality, reduce losses and create sustainable markets for farmers.

The post Alex Ekwueme varsity, European Union launch agric sustainability project appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Reps FCT committee celebrates chairman at 60
description:
Members of the House of Representatives Committee on the Federal Capital Territory have congratulated their chairman, Muktar Betara, on his 60th birthday.
Betara, a chieftain of the All Progressives Congress representing Biu/Bayo/Shani/Kwaya Kusar Federal Constituency of Borno State, was born on Nov
content:
Members of the House of Representatives Committee on the Federal Capital Territory have congratulated their chairman, Muktar Betara, on his 60th birthday.

Betara, a chieftain of the All Progressives Congress representing Biu/Bayo/Shani/Kwaya Kusar Federal Constituency of Borno State, was born on November 22, 1966, and chaired the House Committee on Appropriations in the 9th Assembly.

In a statement signed on Sunday by members of the committee, the lawmakers joined his family, friends, associates and well-wishers in celebrating what they called “decades of a life richly blessed, and in honouring a man whose leadership, courage, legislative ingenuity and commitment to public service continue to make a remarkable difference.”

The statement read in part, “As Chairman of our Committee, you have demonstrated exemplary leadership, uncommon dedication and an impressive capacity to build consensus, inspire confidence and deliver results.

“Your commitment to the work of the Committee and the development of the Federal Capital Territory reflects your deep understanding of public service and the responsibility entrusted to you.

“Your contributions to nation-building and your enduring commitment to the people of Biu, Bayo, Kwaya-Kusar and Shani Federal Constituency of Borno State have further distinguished your record of service.

“We are equally delighted to celebrate your well-deserved recognition as The Sun Newspaper’s House of Representatives Member of the Year, 2026.”

According to the committee members, “The prestigious honour is a fitting recognition” of Betara’s legislative contributions, outstanding leadership and the positive impact of his service.

At 60, the lawmakers said Betara stood as an inspiring example of purposeful leadership, resilience and service with distinction.

“We are proud to be associated with your leadership and privileged to serve alongside you.

“As you step into this new decade, we pray that Almighty Allah grants you renewed strength, sound health, greater wisdom and abundant grace.

“May the years ahead bring even greater accomplishments, fulfilment and opportunities to serve our nation and humanity.

“Happy 60th birthday, Distinguished Chairman! May your new chapter be even more rewarding and impactful,” the statement further read.

The post Reps FCT committee celebrates chairman at 60 appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Nigerian Navy commits warship, helicopter, interceptors to check piracy in Gulf of Guinea
description:
By Philip Nwosu
The Nigerian Navy has pledged to deploy a helicopter-capable Offshore Patrol Vessel and two fast interceptor boats to support joint maritime security operations in the Gulf of Guinea under the Combined Maritime Task Force (CMTF).
The commitment was announced by the Chief of the Naval
content:
By Philip Nwosu

The Nigerian Navy has pledged to deploy a helicopter-capable Offshore Patrol Vessel and two fast interceptor boats to support joint maritime security operations in the Gulf of Guinea under the Combined Maritime Task Force (CMTF).

The commitment was announced by the Chief of the Naval Staff, Vice Admiral Idi Abbas, as part of Nigeria’s contribution to strengthening regional efforts to combat maritime threats through shared military resources and coordinated operations.

Abbas disclosed this at the 10th Symposium of Heads of Navies and Coast Guards in the Gulf of Guinea, held in Libreville, Gabon, saying that the Nigerian Navy would also provide maritime domain awareness support through its Falcon Eye System, alongside other strategic capabilities aimed at enhancing the operational effectiveness of the regional task force.

The naval chief said the deployment of these assets was consistent with Nigeria’s commitment to transforming regional maritime security agreements into practical operational arrangements.

The Combined Maritime Task Force, inaugurated on June 1, 2026, by President Bola Tinubu, is designed to strengthen cooperation among African navies and coast guards in tackling shared maritime security challenges.

Speaking on the theme “Towards an Integrated Regional Naval Force: Which Capabilities Should Be Pooled?”, Abbas argued that the region could achieve better security outcomes by pooling available military resources rather than relying solely on individual national capabilities.

He identified joint maritime surveillance, intelligence sharing, combined patrols, pooled naval and air assets, and shared logistics as essential components of an effective regional security arrangement.

Beyond the provision of military platforms, the naval chief proposed that participating countries develop a time-bound operational roadmap within six months to establish clear responsibilities and deployment arrangements for the task force.

He said the proposed plan should specify the assets each country would contribute, operational deployment schedules, intelligence-sharing mechanisms and logistics support required to sustain joint missions.

According to him, such an arrangement would improve coordination, accountability and the ability of participating navies to respond collectively to emerging threats.

Abbas, however, cautioned that differences in national military capabilities, funding limitations and operational coordination could undermine the initiative if not properly addressed.

He therefore called for sustained political and military commitment, as well as an equitable sharing of responsibilities among participating countries.

The naval chief maintained that the effectiveness of regional maritime cooperation should not be judged by the number of agreements signed or institutions established, but by the ability of member countries to deploy their combined capabilities against common threats.

His presentation places the Nigerian Navy’s contribution to the CMTF within a broader regional effort to develop an integrated maritime security framework capable of protecting shipping routes and supporting economic activities across the Gulf of Guinea.

The proposed six-month operational roadmap, if adopted by participating countries, would provide a framework for translating the commitments made at the symposium into coordinated deployments and sustained maritime security operations.

The post Nigerian Navy commits warship, helicopter, interceptors to check piracy in Gulf of Guinea appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Nigerians need better living conditions, not name-calling, Oyo APM tells Tinubu

The party also described the president’s remark as
content:
The Allied Peoples’ Movement in Oyo State on Sunday slammed President Bola Tinubu for purportedly attacking the party during the All Progressives Congress rally held at Mapo Hall, in Ibadan, referring to his use of “Egbẹ́ Palẹmọ” against the party.

The party also described the president’s remark as desperate distractions from the mounting realities confronting Nigerians and the glaring failures of governance.

This was contained in a statement issued by the APM state Director of Communication/Spokesperson Campaign Council, Yinka Oladoyinbo, in Ibadan, the state capital.

The PUNCH reports that Tinubu had, on Saturday, in Ibadan, taken a swipe at the APM, whose presidential candidate for 2027 is Governor Seyi Makinde, deploying the Yoruba expression “Egbẹ́ Palẹmọ.”

He said, “We heard there is a certain group/faction called the ‘palẹmọ’ (Pack up) group. Don’t mind them; they are only waiting in vain; there is nowhere they are going.”

The remark, made in the home city of the Oyo governor, appeared to be a veiled reference to the APM, though the president did not mention the party or Makinde by name.

However, in a statement on Sunday, the APM said, “We consider the expression a curious choice of words from a President whose administration has become synonymous with economic hardship, public frustration, political manoeuvring and an increasingly desperate search for electoral validation._

“In Yoruba political parlance, ‘palẹmọ’ evokes the hurried gathering, packing or clearing away of belongings, sometimes suggestive of preparing to leave or carrying away what one can before departure.

“Mr President may wish to explain why such vocabulary comes so readily to him. As the saying goes, it takes a master of a craft to recognise the language of fellow practitioners. And when an accuser points one finger at another, the remaining four are invariably directed at himself.

“The APM will not be distracted by presidential name-calling. Nigerians are far more concerned about the cost of living, the purchasing power of their incomes, insecurity, unemployment, collapsing economic confidence and the daily struggle to survive than the linguistic theatrics of a campaign podium.”

The party also warned that traditional rulers, irrespective of their political affiliations, remain ” fathers to all.”

The APM said, among others, that it was “unimpressed by the President’s grandstanding” at the rally.

It said, “We are equally alarmed by the apparent attempt to draw revered traditional institutions into the APC’s partisan electoral machinery in the state. The presence and engagement of the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, and the Soun of Ogbomoso, Oba Ghandi Afolabi Olaoye, must not be misconstrued as political endorsements or electoral commitments by their communities.

“Our traditional rulers are custodians of culture, history, peace and communal identity. They are fathers to all, irrespective of political affiliation. Their palaces must remain places where the ruling party, the opposition, the undecided and the politically disenchanted can find counsel, mediation and a sense of belonging. They are not campaign surrogates, electoral assets or instruments for manufacturing political legitimacy.

“The electorate in Oyo State is politically conscious, discerning and increasingly intolerant of empty promises. Voters will judge political parties and candidates by performance, competence, credibility, economic relief, security and the quality of leadership they have experienced, not by the spectacle of campaign rallies or the proximity of politicians to royal stools.

“The APM is, therefore, unimpressed by the President’s grandstanding at Mapo Hall. Political arrogance, verbal assaults and carefully staged displays of influence will not erase the hardship Nigerians endure. Neither will the attempted appropriation of revered institutions conceal the fundamental question confronting this administration: what tangible improvement has it delivered to the lives of ordinary citizens that justifies another four years?”

Oladoyinbo noted that the people would have their say on January 16, 2027, adding that no amount of presidential bravado, royal proximity or political intimidation can substitute for the sovereign will of the electorate.

“The APM remains confident that Oyo voters will distinguish between political noise and credible leadership, between borrowed prestige and earned trust, and between the spectacle of power and the substance of governance,” the statement said.

The post Nigerians need better living conditions, not name-calling, Oyo APM tells Tinubu appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: UNICAL Alumni trains 1,000 graduating students in agribusiness
description:
From Aniekan Aniekan, Calabar
The University of Calabar (UNICAL) Alumni Association Worldwide has trained 1,000 final-year students in agribusiness, telling them bluntly that white-collar jobs are no longer guaranteed after graduation.
The training, tagged “agropreneurship”, is designed to equip gra
content:
From Aniekan Aniekan, Calabar

The University of Calabar (UNICAL) Alumni Association Worldwide has trained 1,000 final-year students in agribusiness, telling them bluntly that white-collar jobs are no longer guaranteed after graduation.

The training, tagged “agropreneurship”, is designed to equip graduating students with practical skills to start their own businesses and create employment, instead of depending solely on the increasingly competitive formal job market.

The National Vice-President I of the association, Mrs Chinyere Sani, said the initiative was designed to give students something to fall back on after graduation.

“Jobs are not guaranteed, so we want them to have something to fall back on after graduation.

“With the economy as it is, everybody is looking for a second means of income. This training will help them discover their interests and acquire skills to fend for themselves while waiting for opportunities in their respective professions,” she said.

She explained that the programme was not designed to give immediate cash or start-up capital, but to equip participants with the knowledge to identify and develop viable agricultural ventures.

Declaring the programme open, the Vice-Chancellor, represented by the Dean, Faculty of Agriculture, Prof. Ele Edebi, described agriculture as a major economic opportunity capable of addressing unemployment and creating wealth.

He cited egg production as an example, observing that demand for eggs in Calabar remained higher than supply, a gap that young graduates could fill through poultry farming.

Also speaking, the President of the UNICAL Alumni Association Worldwide, Mr Paul Ishiemomoh, said the programme was part of efforts to improve the employability and entrepreneurial capacity of graduates.

He said the quality of graduates should be measured not only by their certificates but also by their ability to secure employment or create businesses, and urged participants to apply the knowledge to establish viable businesses and eventually employ other graduates.

Some beneficiaries described the training as an opportunity to become employers of labour rather than wait endlessly for employment.

title: Leadership crisis: Fountain of Life members express hope for resolution
description:
Some members of The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos, have expressed concerns about the church’s leadership crisis, although others have voiced confidence that the disagreement will eventually be resolved.
Speaking with PUNCH Online after the church’s Sunday serviceSunday service, a member of
content:
Some members of The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos, have expressed concerns about the church’s leadership crisis, although others have voiced confidence that the disagreement will eventually be resolved.

Speaking with PUNCH Online after the church’s Sunday serviceSunday service, a member of two years, who identified herself simply as Deborah, expressed support for Odukoya, describing him as an open-minded leader who related well with members.

She suggested that some individuals were unhappy with his leadership and were looking for opportunities to challenge him, although she could not establish whether the opposition was coming from within or outside the church.

“I don’t know who, but I think there are some people looking for opportunities to attack,” she said.

She, however, maintained that members appreciated Odukoya’s leadership style, describing him as generous, approachable and receptive to both young and older members.

“Everybody wants him to continue being Senior Pastor. Ever since he has been leading the ministry, I don’t think he has done anything to jeopardise the house of God,” she said.

Another member, Martin, who said he was raised in the church, admitted that he did not know exactly what led to the leadership disagreement, noting that the developments happened quickly.

He, however, expressed optimism that the situation would eventually be resolved.

“Everything will be fine,” he said.

Reacting to the congregation’s chant of “We love you” when Odukoya mounted the pulpit during Sunday’s service, Martin said the gesture was not unusual, adding that members would have shown similar encouragement to another pastor.

Odukoya received a rousing welcome during the service, joining the choir in dancing during the praise session before making his way to the pulpit amid cheers from the congregation.

Meanwhile, attempts by PUNCH Online to obtain a response from church staff on the leadership dispute were unsuccessful, as those contacted declined to comment.

One staff member said, “Due to the situation of things, Pastor Jimmy isn’t in the position to speak now.”

The leadership dispute became public on November 17 when a faction of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that it no longer recognised Odukoya as Senior Pastor, citing a succession video reportedly recorded by the church’s late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, in December 2021.

The trustees named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as the church’s interim spiritual and administrative leader.

However, Odukoya and the church leadership rejected the decision, maintaining that his appointment in September 2023 was valid.

The Lagos State High Court subsequently issued an interim order restraining Odukoya from presenting himself as the church’s Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head.

The court also restrained him, either personally or through proxies, from interfering with or disrupting the church’s activities, governance and other business.

The matter was adjourned until December 1 for mention.

The post Leadership crisis: Fountain of Life members express hope for resolution appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: VIDEO: Tinubu joins family for special prayers in Lagos
description:
President Bola Tinubu on Sunday arrived at the Yoruba Tennis Club in Onikan, Lagos, for a special prayer session organised by members of his family.
Footage from the Nigerian Television Authority shows the presidential convoy, led by a black Cadillac bearing the national coat of arms, arriving under
content:
President Bola Tinubu on Sunday arrived at the Yoruba Tennis Club in Onikan, Lagos, for a special prayer session organised by members of his family.

Footage from the Nigerian Television Authority shows the presidential convoy, led by a black Cadillac bearing the national coat of arms, arriving under tight security.

Armed officers and aides escorted the President as he stepped out in traditional attire.

He was received by family members, associates and other guests before proceeding into the venue along a red carpet.

Inside the hall, decorated with red balloons and chandeliers, a large gathering of attendees in traditional white attire waited.

A banner with the inscription “The Tinubu Family of Lagos” was displayed on stage.

The President moved through the hall, exchanging greetings as the event began.

As he walked to his seat, the Master of Ceremonies was heard saying the prayer was organised for “his (Tinubu) re-election next year, Insha Allah.”

The event forms part of spiritual support for Tinubu’s re-election bid in the 2027 general elections.

It follows his attendance at an All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, the previous day.

At that rally, held at Mapo Hall, Tinubu endorsed the party’s governorship candidates for Oyo, Ogun and Lagos states and spoke on economic reforms and development plans for the South-West.

Tinubu had arrived in Lagos on Saturday afternoon after the Ibadan event.

He was received at the Presidential Wing of Murtala Muhammed International Airport by Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu; his Ogun State counterpart, Dapo Abiodun; the President’s Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila; former Governor of Ogun State Chief Segun Osoba; and other government officials, party leaders, and supporters.

Presidential spokesperson Bayo Onanuga confirmed that the short visit would centre on the family prayer before the President’s return to Abuja.

title: It Will Be Difficult To Stabilise What Tinubu Has Done If We Don’t Re-Elect Him — Wike
description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said that denying President Bola Tinubu a second term will amount to abandoning and undermining the positive effects of the various economic reforms and other policies his administration has started to implement.﻿Wike argued that
content:
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said that denying President Bola Tinubu a second term will amount to abandoning and undermining the positive effects of the various economic reforms and other policies his administration has started to implement.

Wike argued that though the removal of fuel subsidy came with initial difficulties, it would be in the best interest of Nigeria and its people for the President to complete the foundation he has laid for the country’s recovery and prosperity.

He spoke on Sunday during a thanksgiving and dedication service at St. Peter’s Anglican Church, Rumueprikom, his hometown in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State, where the Rainbow Coalition campaign council was dedicated ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Wike, who said the campaigns would begin on November 23, described Tinubu as a courageous leader who took difficult decisions to prevent Nigeria from collapsing.

“This country was on the verge of collapse, on the verge of collapse, but by the grace of God, He gave us somebody who is courageous,” the former governor said.

The minister cited the relative stability in the university system, saying lecturers’ strikes over unpaid entitlements, which previously disrupted academic calendars, are no longer a recurring problem under the Tinubu administration.

He also recalled the difficulties pensioners faced in securing their payments, arguing that the President’s decisions were necessary to address the country’s challenges.

Wike described the removal of the fuel subsidy as one such difficult decision, acknowledging it came with disadvantages but insisting the challenges were temporary.

“Now, in doing that, there must be some disadvantages.

“And that’s why they say these disadvantages will be temporarily seen. As he has laid his foundation, now it’s time for prosperity,” he said.

“If we don’t re-elect him, then it will be difficult to stabilise what he has done,” he said.

The minister called on Christians, Muslims and traditional worshippers to support the re-election bid, insisting that the campaign would not discriminate on religious grounds.

“I am not a native doctor, but I need their votes now. I need everybody’s votes because I know they are registered voters,” he added.

“The Muslims, I need their votes too. The Christians like you, we need your votes.”

Wike also defended the Tinubu administration against claims of religious imbalance in its appointments, saying Christians benefited more from the government than under previous administrations.

“Since Nigeria was created, we have never had the kind of appointments that are going on in this country now,” said the minister.

He further urged the congregation to participate actively in the forthcoming elections, warning that those who refuse to vote would have to live with the consequences of decisions made by others.

“If you don’t participate, and you have a bad leader, it will also affect you,” he added.

On the Rivers State governorship race, he urged the people to support the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, Kingsley Chinda, describing him as a son of the soil.

Speaking further, the minister said the dedication of the campaign council was in keeping with their tradition of committing political campaigns to God before setting out, expressing confidence that the exercise would be peaceful.

“Just as we have never had a crisis before, I believe we will also not have a crisis in this period,” Wike said.

The minister said he would continue to support the church.

As part of his support for the church, Wike announced, on behalf of the Rainbow Coalition, his friends and associates, a donation of ₦100 million.

He described the donation as their way of encouraging the church, urging religious leaders to also support them through prayers and the congregation through their votes.

Members of the Rainbow Coalition, including Chinda, Chairman of the PDP Board of Trustees, Senator Mao Ohuabunwa, Speaker of the Rivers State House of Assembly, Martin Amaewhule, and other political leaders, were present at the service.

The post It Will Be Difficult To Stabilise What Tinubu Has Done If We Don’t Re-Elect Him — Wike appeared first on Channels Television.

title: 2027: Ebonyi PDP, APC bicker over rainbow coalition
description:
From Uchenna Inya, Abakaliki
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ebonyi State are bickering over the rainbow coalition in next year’s general election.
While the APC dismissed the rainbow coalition as non-existent in the state, the PDP insisted that there ex
content:
From Uchenna Inya, Abakaliki

The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ebonyi State are bickering over the rainbow coalition in next year’s general election.

While the APC dismissed the rainbow coalition as non-existent in the state, the PDP insisted that there exists in the state a solid, strategic and broadly accepted political coalition involving multiple frontline political parties and stakeholders, and that the coalition has resolved to work together to provide the people of the state with a credible alternative to the APC-led administration, which it described as a failure.

Addressing journalists in Abakaliki, the state capital, at the weekend during its inaugural press briefing, the Director of Communication of the APC campaign council, Senator Emmanuel Onwe, said: “Sometime ago, somebody described the so-called rainbow coalition as a scam. I am not going so far as to describe any outfit as a scam, but to prove scam, you have to have a degree of legal requirements.

“All we will say is that there is no rainbow coalition in Ebonyi State. We had a meeting here with the Director-General of the campaign council and he was categorical in denouncing any rainbow coalition.

“The Governor has reiterated the same, disavowing any notion of rainbow coalition in Ebonyi State. Ebonyi State is APC. The entirety of the two political arms of government, the executive and the legislature, is APC.

“The 24 members of the state House of Assembly are APC. The entire state executive council members are APC. So, Ebonyi State has neither the time, nor the inclination, nor even the patience to discuss rainbow coalition or no rainbow coalition because it doesn’t exist in Ebonyi.”

But the PDP, in a statement signed by its Publicity Secretary, Darlington Onwe, said it was surprising that a figure of Senator Onwe’s intellectual standing would misconstrue what constitutes a coalition in modern political history, or deny its existence in the state, where it plainly exists, simply to defend the grossly failed record of the current APC-led administration in the state.

It urged Governor Francis Nwifuru to begin to prepare his handover note in good faith ahead of the May 29, 2027, inauguration.

“Political history, both globally and within Nigeria, is replete with successful examples of this exact principle. In fact, to wrest power from the then-ruling PDP at the national level in 2015, legacy political parties, namely the ACN, ANPP, CPC and a faction of APGA, merged in 2013 to form the APC, and were joined by a breakaway faction of the PDP itself.

“For the spokesperson of that same party to now deny the reality or validity of the existing coalition in Ebonyi State is a contradiction of the APC’s own political origin.

“For both official and public record purposes, there exists in Ebonyi State a solid, strategic and broadly accepted political coalition involving multiple frontline political parties and stakeholders.

“This coalition has resolved to work together to provide Ebonyi people a credible alternative to the already failed current APC-led administration under Governor Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru.

“Whether referred to as a ‘rainbow coalition’ or by any other nomenclature which naysayers may adopt, the reality on the ground is that this alliance of opposition forces is focused on rallying Ebonyi people to re-elect our President, Sen. Ahmed Bola Tinubu, and to also elect Dr Ifeanyi Chukwuma Odii as the next Governor of Ebonyi State.

“Most importantly, based on the feedback, public perception and citizens’ response, we urge Gov. Nwifuru, in good faith, to begin preparing his handover note, come what may, ahead of the May 29, 2027, inauguration.

“The Ebonyi PDP and its coalition partners remain committed to engaging Ebonyi people on concrete issues of development, accountability and good governance, confident that the collective resolve of the people will prevail at the polls in 2027,” the PDP stated.

The post 2027: Ebonyi PDP, APC bicker over rainbow coalition appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

By Daniel Abia



PORT HARCOURT — A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and close ally of its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, Chief Eze Chukwuemeka Eze, has dismissed Governor Si
content:
…Insists Rivers is nobody’s political inheritance, says APC must be punished for emergency rule

By Daniel Abia

PORT HARCOURT — A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and close ally of its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, Chief Eze Chukwuemeka Eze, has dismissed Governor Siminalayi Fubara’s pledge to deliver three million votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general election.

Eze described the governor’s assurance as an unrealistic political projection, insisting that Rivers State was not the political inheritance of any individual or group.

Fubara had, on November 7, during a Rainbow Coalition/APC presidential rally in Port Harcourt, assured Tinubu that the people of Rivers would deliver at least three million votes for him in the January 2027 presidential election.

Reacting to the pledge in a statement issued in Port Harcourt at the weekend, Eze described it as an “audacious exercise in political delusion, electoral deception and monumental grandstanding”.

He argued that the projection was unattainable and disconnected from the prevailing political realities in the state, alleging that the governor made the promise to massage the President’s ego and create an impression of widespread political acceptance.

The ADC chieftain said Tinubu’s reliance on political assurances from Fubara and the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, showed a misunderstanding of the political consciousness of Rivers people and their grievances over the political crisis that engulfed the state.

Eze recalled the declaration of a state of emergency in Rivers, the suspension of the governor, his deputy and members of the State House of Assembly, insisting that the people had neither forgotten nor forgiven the circumstances surrounding the intervention.

He said Rivers people were politically enlightened enough to distinguish genuine leadership from political manoeuvring and would not surrender their electoral choices to intimidation, patronage or political inducements.

“It is rather amusing that President Tinubu appears to have mistaken political silence for political acquiescence and the orchestrated jubilation at Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium for an irrevocable endorsement of his administration,” he said.

Eze also cautioned against interpreting the crowd at the APC rally as an indication of the President’s electoral strength in the state.

“Let nobody deceive the President with the political theatrics of Nyesom Wike, Governor Siminalayi Fubara and their respective political establishments.

“The crowd assembled at the stadium, regardless of its numerical appearance, cannot be substituted for the electorate. A rented or politically mobilised crowd, no matter how imposing, does not constitute an electoral mandate,” he said.

He further predicted that Tinubu would struggle to secure 100,000 genuine votes in Rivers in 2027, adding that even such a figure would not necessarily amount to an endorsement of his administration.

The ADC chieftain also accused the President and his political associates of assuming that they could influence the judiciary, security agencies and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to determine the outcome of the 2027 elections.

He warned that such assumptions could undermine democracy, stressing that the institutions were established by the Constitution and should not serve the interests of any political party or administration.

Eze said the Rivers political crisis had exposed the dangers of political arrogance, executive overreach and the subordination of constitutional democracy to personal political interests.

He added that Nigerians facing economic hardship and what he described as failed governance would use the ballot box to express their dissatisfaction and determine the country’s political future.

The ADC chieftain insisted that Rivers State was not the political property of any individual, warning that neither political alliances nor the influence of power brokers could guarantee electoral support.

He said the 2027 elections would ultimately be determined by voters, not political promises, rallies or claims of control over the electorate.

title: Atiku’s aide challenges Tinubu over prosperity promise
description:
A media aide to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Paul Ibe, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to provide evidence of economic improvements under his administration, saying Nigerians need tangible results rather than assurances of future prosperity.



Ibe made the remarks in a post on his X h
content:
A media aide to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Paul Ibe, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to provide evidence of economic improvements under his administration, saying Nigerians need tangible results rather than assurances of future prosperity.

Ibe made the remarks in a post on his X handle on Sunday while reacting to Tinubu’s message in Ibadan that Nigeria was on the path to prosperity.

He argued that Nigerians needed to see improvements in their living conditions, particularly in the cost of food, transportation, electricity and other essential services.

According to him, the President should explain the achievements of his administration and how its policies have translated into better living conditions for citizens, especially as he seeks another term in 2027.

Ibe questioned how long households would have to contend with rising living expenses, while workers struggle with increasing costs and businesses face energy-related challenges.

He maintained that government claims of economic progress should be assessed against the everyday experiences of Nigerians.

On the reported agreement to reopen a vehicle assembly plant, Ibe said productive investment was welcome but argued that its benefits should be measured by the actual resumption of operations, employment opportunities and wider economic impact.

He also acknowledged the importance of infrastructure development, while stressing that government should equally account for its impact on the livelihoods of citizens.

Ibe further questioned the emphasis on future generations in the President’s appeal for Nigerians to remain committed to the administration’s policies, saying the immediate needs of children and struggling households should also receive attention.

He called on the Federal Government to provide Nigerians with a clear account of the outcomes of the sacrifices associated with its policies, including the benefits recorded and when households could expect meaningful relief.

Reacting to Tinubu’s remarks about the opposition, Ibe said opposition parties had a legitimate role in scrutinising the administration’s performance, while citizens were entitled to consider alternative political positions.

He argued that public confidence in government should be strengthened through responses to citizens’ concerns and demonstrable improvements in their living conditions.

Ibe said the benefits of prosperity should be reflected in household purchasing power, workers’ wages, the survival of businesses and the security of communities.

He maintained that the administration should provide evidence of its achievements and address the economic and security concerns confronting Nigerians.

The post Atiku’s aide challenges Tinubu over prosperity promise appeared first on Vanguard News.

content:
President Bola Tinubu has said that he would continue to pursue reforms that would strengthen the capacity of the Nigeria Police Force, improve personnel welfare and create an enabling environment for effective policing services.

The president gave the assurance on Saturday during the passing out of the 8th Regular Cadets Course at the Nigeria Police Academy, Wudil, Kano State.

Represented by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume, the President noted that the success of these efforts would only depend on the personal commitment of the newly commissioned officers.

He assured that the present administration remained committed to building a police force that is adequately equipped, professionally trained, technologically enabled and sufficiently motivated to fulfil its constitutional responsibilities.

“The Federal Government will continue to pursue reforms and provide the necessary support to strengthen police capacity, improve personnel welfare and create an enabling environment for effective service policing.

“However, the success of these efforts will only depend on your personal commitment to excellence. The nation expects much from you, and you must never lose sight of the honour and responsibility that comes with wearing the uniform of the Nigeria Police Force,” Tinubu said.

He urged the officers to go out with courage, humility and an unshakable sense of duty.

“Let your service be defined by integrity, your leadership by compassion and your commitment to Nigeria by the highest standards of patriotism,” he urged.

Tinubu congratulated the graduating cadets on their successful completion of five years of intense academic, professional and physical training, noting that the achievement testifies to their discipline, resilience, determination and commitment to a noble cause.

“I also extend my sincere appreciation to your parents, guardians and families whose sacrifices and encouragement have contributed immensely to this milestone. I commend the leadership, management, academic staff, instructors and personnel of the Nigeria Police Academy for their dedication to moulding and preparing these young men and women for the enormous responsibilities ahead.

“You must understand that the uniform you are about to wear represents more than authority. It represents public trust, responsibility and a solemn obligation to protect every Nigerian, irrespective of ethnicity, religion, political affiliation or social standing. The true measure of your service will not be the rank you attain, but the lives you protect, the communities you secure and the confidence you inspire in the people you serve,” Tinubu said.

The President further charged the newly commissioned officers to uphold the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, respect the fundamental rights of citizens and discharge their duties with professionalism, fairness and accountability.

“Never allow the authority of your office to become an instrument of oppression, intimidation or personal enrichment. Be firm in enforcing the law, but always guided by justice, respect and respect for human dignity,” he said.

According to him, Nigeria is confronted by evolving security challenges that require a modern, intelligent, responsive and professionally equipped police force.

“You are graduating at a time when we are overhauling our policing structure by establishing state police. Wherever you find yourself, either at the state or federal level, your generation must be prepared to embrace innovation, leverage technology, strengthen intelligence-led policing and build meaningful partnerships with communities and other security agencies,” he stated.

In his address, the Commandant of the Academy, AIG Auwal Muhammad, described the day as one of celebrating discipline and readiness to sacrifice for the nation.

He commended the FG for the support it has been giving to the academy, stressing that the support had encouraged them to pursue higher standards in academic programmes and prepare the cadets to address the security challenges confronting the country.

A total of 845 Assistant Superintendents of Police were commissioned during the event, while awards were presented to some of them for their outstanding performances.

The PUNCH reports that Tinubu has received the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill establishing state police after all 36 state Houses of Assembly approved the proposed amendment, paving the way for its presidential assent.

The Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, announced the development in a statement on Wednesday, saying Tinubu would assent to the bill at a formal signing ceremony.

He said all 36 state Houses of Assembly had approved the bill, exceeding the constitutional requirement of at least 24 states, representing two-thirds of the 36 states, under Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution.

The allegation followed the circulation of a video on social media which appears to show the traditional
content:
The Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, has become a subject of controversy on X after a female tourist accused him of touching her inappropriately during a visit to his palace in Katsina State.

The allegation followed the circulation of a video on social media which appears to show the traditional ruler interacting with the tourist during her visit.

The woman, who identifies herself online as ‘beduina’, made the allegation in an Instagram post after completing a 30-day trip across different parts of Nigeria.

She said the incident occurred on Saturday, November 14, when she visited the Emir’s palace in Daura.

Recounting the encounter, the tourist said she was taken into an elegant room, where she sat with the traditional ruler and engaged in a conversation.

She alleged that the Emir held her hand and began playing with it before hugging and kissing her on the cheek.

According to her, the encounter took a disturbing turn when the traditional ruler allegedly touched her breasts.

“That was a shock for me. I told him ‘emir no, no, no, no’, ‘emir you cannot be touching’, but he was just laughing about it,” she wrote.

The tourist said she was particularly disturbed that the alleged incident happened inside a palace, despite having travelled through different parts of Nigeria without experiencing sexual assault in public spaces.

“I wasn’t sexually assaulted at any moment when walking through streets of Nigeria, even in busy crowded places, but to my shock I was assaulted in a palace by a traditional leader who should be behaving in exemplary and dignified way,” she said.

She described the experience as disgusting, adding that she had continued to relive the encounter in her thoughts.

The woman said the incident happened a week before she made the allegation public but explained that she waited until she had left Nigeria before speaking about it.

She also suggested that other women might have experienced similar treatment from the traditional ruler, although she did not provide evidence of such incidents.

“I suspect I wasn’t first woman he assaulted but probably first one with a proof recorded. I have meta glasses and quickly turned them on,” she added.

Her allegation has generated reactions on X, with some users expressing concern and demanding accountability.

As of the time of filing this report, neither the Daura Emirate Council nor the Katsina State Government had issued an official response to the allegation.

content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

A 70-year-old woman has survived after accidentally falling into a 60-foot-deep well at Oworonshoki, Kosofe Local Government Area of Lagos State.

The incident occurred in the early hours of Sunday at 37, Abiola Street, prompting a distress call to the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service.

Firefighters from the Oworonshoki Fire Station promptly responded to the call and successfully rescued the septuagenarian alive.

The rescue operation was concluded after the victim was stabilised and handed over to her family.

The Controller-General of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, Margaret Adeseye, who confirmed the incident, said the woman was responding to treatment as of press time.

title: Atiku’s aide faults Defence Ministry over Tinubu rally publicity
description:
A media aide to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Paul Ibe, has questioned the use of the Ministry of Defence’s official social media platforms to publicise a campaign rally for President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid.







Ibe, in a post on his X handle on Sunday, faulted the ministry fo
content:
A media aide to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Paul Ibe, has questioned the use of the Ministry of Defence’s official social media platforms to publicise a campaign rally for President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid.

Ibe, in a post on his X handle on Sunday, faulted the ministry for allegedly using its official Facebook page and X account to announce the rally and publicise Defence Minister, General Christopher Musa’s inspection of the venue ahead of the event.

He argued that the development raised concerns about the use of government communication platforms for partisan political activities.

According to him, while providing security for a presidential visit falls within the legitimate responsibilities of the ministry, using its official platforms to promote a re-election campaign compromises the institutional neutrality expected of public institutions.

Ibe noted that the Ministry of Defence was funded by taxpayers across different political affiliations and should, therefore, serve the interests of all Nigerians rather than those of a particular political party.

He said Nigerians facing insecurity deserved information about government efforts to protect their communities and support military personnel, rather than publicity for political campaigns.

He also questioned the confidence opposition parties and voters could have in the impartiality of state institutions if official government communication platforms were used to promote activities associated with the ruling party.

Ibe called on the Defence Minister to explain the publication, ensure the removal of what he described as partisan campaign publicity and maintain a clear distinction between official government responsibilities and party activities.

title: 2027: Atiku’s Support Groups dump ADC, endorse Obi, Kwankwaso
description:

The Coalition of Atiku Support Groups Initiative announced its decision during
content:
A coalition of support groups loyal to former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has explained its decision to endorse the presidential ambition of former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, ahead of the 2027 general election.

The Coalition of Atiku Support Groups Initiative announced its decision during a press conference in Abuja on Saturday, saying it had resolved to support the joint presidential ticket of Obi and former Kano State Governor, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso.

According to the coalition, its decision followed an assessment of the country’s political situation, the principle of regional power rotation and the need for opposition parties to unite against the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

The group said the current political circumstances favoured Obi, who is seeking the presidency under the platform of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC).

Explaining the reasons behind its endorsement, the coalition said it believed that supporting the Obi-Kwankwaso ticket would contribute to restructuring the opposition and strengthening efforts to challenge the ruling party.

In its statement, the group said: “The coalition of Atiku support groups has officially announced its decision to support the joint presidential ticket of Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso.

“The decisive resolution followed a comprehensive review of the current national political movement, regional power rotation principle and the imperative need to restructure the opposition to rescue Nigeria.”

The announcement represents a political development involving groups associated with Atiku, who is pursuing his presidential ambition under the African Democratic Congress (ADC).

However, the endorsement was announced by the support groups and should not be interpreted as a formal declaration by Atiku himself that he has withdrawn from the presidential race or endorsed Obi.

The development comes as opposition parties and political blocs continue discussions over possible cooperation ahead of the 2027 general election.

title: NAFDAC destroys N22.73bn fake, unsafe products, records 52 arrests
description:
… 821 seizures, 179 premises shut in eight monthsBy Chioma Obinna



The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has destroyed unwholesome products valued at approximately N22.73 billion, seized 821 products and secured 52 arrests in eight months as it intensified enfor
content:
… 821 seizures, 179 premises shut in eight months
By Chioma Obinna

The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has destroyed unwholesome products valued at approximately N22.73 billion, seized 821 products and secured 52 arrests in eight months as it intensified enforcement against unsafe and substandard regulated products.

The agency disclosed that it carried out 5,542 enforcement activities, including 213 raids, between January and August 2026, while 179 premises were shut and 221 sanctions imposed.

The figures formed part of major regulatory milestones presented by NAFDAC at the International Pharmaceutical Regulators Programme (IPRP) Management Committee Meeting in Prague, Czech Republic, held from November 18 to 19, 2026.

The agency also reported progress in local pharmaceutical manufacturing, disclosing that more than 70 per cent of finished pharmaceutical products covered by its 5+5 policy and Ceiling 36 are now being manufactured in Nigeria.

The development is expected to reduce dependence on imported medicines and strengthen the country’s medicine security.

In its regulatory update, NAFDAC said it had sustained its World Health Organisation (WHO) Maturity Level 3 status and was working towards attaining Maturity Level 4, the highest level of the WHO Global Benchmarking Tool.

It identified digital innovation as a critical component of the transition, citing the Integrated Regulatory Information Management System (IRIMS), Performance Management System (i-PMS), GMP Inspection (GMPi), Application and AI-assisted Technical Screening Tools (TST), and the revised Med Safety App.

The revised application is designed to strengthen the reporting of adverse drug reactions and substandard and falsified medical products.

NAFDAC also highlighted Nigeria’s growing influence in African pharmaceutical regulation, noting that it had emerged as a reference National Regulatory Authority, hosting regulatory authorities from Uganda, The Gambia, Mozambique and Côte d’Ivoire for technical capacity building and institutional benchmarking.

Another milestone was Nigeria’s ratification of the African Medicines Agency (AMA) Treaty, with the instruments of ratification deposited on October 25, 2026.

The agency said the achievements reflected the strategic leadership of its Director-General, Prof. Mojisola Christianah Adeyeye, and ongoing efforts to strengthen institutional capacity, promote science-based regulation and deepen international regulatory cooperation.

NAFDAC reaffirmed its commitment to protecting public health, strengthening Nigeria’s pharmaceutical industry and positioning the country as a leading regulatory authority in Africa.

title: Bayelsa boat tragedy: Atiku demands probe, overhaul of water transport safety
description:
By Luminous Jannamike



ABUJA – The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has called for an investigation into Friday’s fatal boat mishap in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, urging the Federal and State Governments to strengthen safety
content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has called for an investigation into Friday’s fatal boat mishap in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, urging the Federal and State Governments to strengthen safety measures on the nation’s waterways to prevent further loss of lives.

Atiku said the tragedy, which claimed several lives, highlighted the risks faced by millions of Nigerians who rely on boats for daily transportation, particularly in riverine communities, and called for urgent government action to protect them.

In a statement on Sunday, the Director of Media and Publicity of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Kola Ologbondiyan, described the incident as a heartbreaking tragedy that had plunged the affected communities into mourning.

He said the victims were travelling to honour a departed loved one when the accident occurred.

“What makes this tragedy even more painful is that these were ordinary Nigerians who set out in love and solidarity to honour a departed loved one, only to meet their own untimely deaths on the waters,” Ologbondiyan said.

“Bayelsa has lost fathers, mothers, children and breadwinners. No words can adequately capture the depth of grief now hanging over the affected communities.”

Ologbondiyan commended local divers, the Marine Police, the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) and other emergency responders for their efforts in the search and rescue operations.

He, however, called for a thorough investigation into the cause of the mishap and stricter enforcement of regulations against boat overloading, the use of unseaworthy vessels and other unsafe practices.

He said preventing similar accidents would require sustained government investment in safer water transportation.

“The Federal and State Governments must prioritise the provision of standard and well-maintained boats, adequate life jackets, functional jetties and properly trained boat operators across riverine communities,” he stressed.

“For millions of Nigerians in the Niger Delta and other riverine areas, water transportation is not a luxury; it is a daily necessity. Their safety must never be treated as an afterthought.”

He also urged the Federal Government, Bayelsa State Government and relevant humanitarian agencies to provide immediate assistance to survivors and bereaved families. Such assistance, he said, should include medical care, psychosocial support and financial help with the burial of victims.

Atiku commiserated with the bereaved families, the people of Ayama and Ukubie communities and the Bayelsa State Government, while praying for the repose of the deceased and the speedy recovery of those injured.

title: Nigeria has become a laughing stock because of dishonest leaders, Jonathan says
description:

Jonathan made the remarks on Saturday in Abuja while delivering the keynote address
content:
Former President Goodluck Jonathan has criticised Nigerian politicians over what he described as dishonesty in leadership, saying their conduct has damaged the country’s reputation before the international community.

Jonathan made the remarks on Saturday in Abuja while delivering the keynote address at the third edition of the Paul Alaje Colloquium, which focused on the theme, “The Brand Nigeria.”

The former president accused politicians of making promises they have no intention of fulfilling, arguing that the gap between their public assurances and actual conduct has contributed to Nigeria’s negative image.

According to him, the country, which was once respected internationally as a major nation, is now being ridiculed because of the actions of those entrusted with its leadership.

“Nigeria is a laughing stock because of dishonest leaders. We must reform our electoral credibility and a political culture that is more inclusive, rewards ideas, character and competence rather than money, patronage and sectional interests,” Jonathan said.

He warned that the country would continue to struggle to make meaningful progress if politicians persist in deceiving citizens and failing to live up to their responsibilities.

Jonathan also called for reforms in Nigeria’s electoral and political systems, stressing the need to strengthen internal democracy within political parties.

He maintained that the process of recruiting political leaders should prioritise integrity, competence and good ideas rather than financial influence, patronage or sectional considerations.

The former president’s comments come amid growing concerns over political leadership, public trust and the credibility of democratic institutions in Nigeria.
