title: PSG confirm Desire Doue ruled out for months with torn ACL
description:
Paris Saint-Germain star Desire Doue has suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee, the reigning French and European champions confirmed on Sunday.







Doue, 21, went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half of Saturday’s 3-2 Ligue 1 win at Nice and was stretchered
content:
Paris Saint-Germain star Desire Doue has suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee, the reigning French and European champions confirmed on Sunday.

Doue, 21, went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half of Saturday’s 3-2 Ligue 1 win at Nice and was stretchered off in tears.

The French international will undergo surgery before the end of the month, PSG added in a brief statement, without specifying the expected length of his absence, which is likely to be a matter of months.

Doue looked in agony as he clutched his right knee, and the match was stopped for five minutes to allow him to receive treatment before being carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium.

PSG have also lost Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee playing against Barcelona last month.

The Georgian winger is unlikely to return this season, and Doue looks set for a significant spell on the sidelines too.

“It is obviously a serious injury,” PSG coach Luis Enrique said on Saturday night.

The French international, who can play on the wing or in midfield, has been arguably PSG’s best player this season after playing a key role in their Champions League triumphs in each of the last two campaigns.

He has notably scored three goals in three Champions League appearances this season for PSG, who sold Bradley Barcola to Liverpool at the beginning of the campaign and have seen Ousmane Dembele struggle with his fitness recently.

title: Church not a political party — Bishop Mike Okonkwo
description:
By Olayinka Latona







The Fountain of Life Church today held its Sunday service despite reports of a court injunction against Pastor Jimmy Odukoya.







Addressing the crowded congregation, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya said he had not received any court injunction as reported, and stressed his unwaver
content:
By Olayinka Latona

The Fountain of Life Church today held its Sunday service despite reports of a court injunction against Pastor Jimmy Odukoya.

Addressing the crowded congregation, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya said he had not received any court injunction as reported, and stressed his unwavering love for the church. Members were said to have chanted “We love you” during the service.

Bishop Mike Okonkwo of The Redeemed Evangelical Ministry, one of the spiritual fathers to the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, ministered on the theme “The Glory of The Church.”

He charged members and ministers of the church to diligently keep the founder’s legacy and remain steadfast in Christ, reminding them of the advice he gave when the church founder died.

“The responsibility fell on us to talk to… The only honour we can do for the sacrifice, the process, pains and everything that the man of God who is highly celebrated in this country is that his legacy must continue,” Bishop Okonkwo said.

“And I told you that day that Fountain will never die. No matter the trial or temptation, this is a work that is solidly laid. The price has been paid; lives have been lost. There is no power of hell that would destroy this work. It will go from glory to glory.”

Acknowledging recent online attacks, he said: “For the past one or two weeks, we have been literally battered on social media. There is nothing that has not been said, both what is true and what is not true. Phone calls from far and near: ‘Bishop Mike, where are you?’ You can’t separate me from Fountain; it’s not possible, because it’s a covenant established by God Himself. What affects Fountain affects me. Don’t think that I am just aloof. I said to myself, ‘God, you just have to give us wisdom.’”

He added: “The day you fully understand the glory of God upon His church and what it takes to give birth to His church, then there is nothing from the gates of hell that will move you.”

Bishop Okonkwo warned that the church is not a political party but God’s house. “The church is not a human institution; it’s God’s house; it belongs to Him. Think of the price that He paid for the church. We should all know that we are not for Tolu, Jimmy or the Board of Trustees; none of them died for you,” he said. “The church is not a political party because Jesus Christ’s life was

involved. The church is not an ordinary thing. We must be careful that none of us is an instrument to destroy the church of Christ.”

He declared that God is interested in the church and that its best days are ahead. “God is interested in this church, in case you don’t know. What you have seen so far cannot be compared to what is coming, because everything that has to do with God is always progressive. This church is going to do seven more than what Pastor Taiwo left it,” he said.

“We must appreciate the predetermined plans of God concerning each and every one of us. You’re a vital, relevant, valued part of God’s global agenda for the human race worldwide… God values you, and that’s why it cost Him His life. You are called for glory and not shame. Fountainers, are you saying that Jesus did not factor in the challenges you will go through? Are you saying all the crises and gossip that are happening to you individually take God by surprise?”

He continued: “That is why I know without any form of doubt that whatever the devil does, he is already a failure. The story of the believer never ends in shame… Weeping may endure for a night… rejoice not over me, my enemies, when I fall…”

Bishop Okonkwo urged members to remain calm and trust God.

“Do you know the challenge of believers? When trials, temptations and difficulties come, we fall apart. We forget what God told us and we run helter-skelter and start doing what God warned us not to do, and we further harm the devil, when we should rather go to bed and chill,” he said. “If there was a time,

“Fountainers, that you needed to chill, this is the time. Chill; let God perfect what He has started. We are so used to seeing the wind blowing, the boisterous storm, the adversary like a roaring lion, and many times we analyse the devil. Who tells you to analyse the devil? You’re to cast the devil. Look up to God: when you look down, you experience defeat; when you look down, you experience discouragement; when you look around, you experience distractions; but when you look up, deliverance is guaranteed. Stop looking around, because those who observe lying vanities will forsake their own mercy.”

He declared: “I have come to tell you, the devil may have scored a number, but the final whistle is yet to come. The game is not over; you’re still in the will of God, still in His hands. God has not left His church. He has not left this church. Can I tell you? God will never leave this church. If anyone is saying that, tell him he is seeing wrongly. The glory of God remains in this house.”

“Rest assured that no matter what anyone says, that’s not your business; we will build this church together,” he said. He prayed that the voice and glory of the church would not diminish and further prayed for divine turnaround.

Earlier, one of the church ministers led the opening prayers and also urged the church not to join in the gossip but rather to remain steadfast in praying for the church. The church auditorium was filled to capacity, while the choir led the happy and joyful members in praise and worship sessions.

The post Church not a political party — Bishop Mike Okonkwo appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Women showed me shege before I met my wife -  Hafiz Oyetoro’
description:
Nollywood actor Hafiz Oyetoro has recounted how he faced repeated rejection from women before eventually meeting his wife, saying his reserved nature, appearance and financial struggles made it difficult for him to find a partner.



Oyetoro, popularly known as Saka, said he married late because he
content:
Nollywood actor Hafiz Oyetoro has recounted how he faced repeated rejection from women before eventually meeting his wife, saying his reserved nature, appearance and financial struggles made it difficult for him to find a partner.

Oyetoro, popularly known as Saka, said he married late because he lacked the confidence to approach women and often struggled to express his feelings when trying to woo them.

Oyetoro disclosed this during an interview on Agbaletu Podcast, conducted in Yoruba, where he narrated some of his unsuccessful attempts to woo women and how he eventually met his wife at 39 before marrying at 40.

“Actually, I married late because I am not very good at asking women out. I am very reserved, but the first woman I approached was laughing when I asked her out,” he said.

According to him, he initially misunderstood the woman’s reaction, believing she found him funny, but later realised she was mocking his appearance.

“She was laughing at my look derisively, but I thought she found me funny; the more effort I made to woo her, the harder she laughed. I was completely frustrated,” Oyetoro recounted.

He said the experience left him wondering whether he would ever find a woman willing to marry him.

“I said to myself, ‘Will I ever have a wife in my life?’” he added.

The actor also attributed some of the rejections he experienced to his financial situation at the time, describing himself as poor and saying his appearance made him less appealing to women.

“Ladies showed me shege; they didn’t look my way at all. Then, I was poor. If you saw me then, I looked like a refugee. My neck was long, my head was big,” he said.

Oyetoro recalled that some women openly questioned his suitability as a husband because of his appearance.

“Women would look at me and say, ‘Is this what I would marry?’” he said.

He further narrated how a woman he approached in Ife rejected him and subsequently complained to the person who introduced them, questioning why she had been linked with a man living with albinism.

“I once asked a lady out in Ife, and she rejected me and returned to the person who introduced me to her to blame the person for introducing a suitor living with albinism to her,” he said.

Oyetoro, however, said his confidence and ability to interact with women improved after completing his first degree, a development that eventually helped him find love.

“A lot happened, but by the time I finished my first degree, I had become outspoken; I could interact with ladies; I met my wife,” he said.

title: World Children’s Day: UNICEF urges greater investment in children
description:
As part of activities to commemorate World Children’s Day, the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has called for the inclusion of children’s voices in policy formulation and increased investment in their education, health and overall well-being.
The Chief of UNICEF’s Bauchi Field Office, Dr Nuz
content:
As part of activities to commemorate World Children’s Day, the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has called for the inclusion of children’s voices in policy formulation and increased investment in their education, health and overall well-being.

The Chief of UNICEF’s Bauchi Field Office, Dr Nuzhat Rafique, made the call on Saturday during the 2026 World Children’s Day celebration held at the New Banquet Hall of the Government House, Bauchi.

Represented by the office’s Education Specialist, Abdulrahman Ado, Rafique said children should be recognised as important members of society whose opinions and aspirations must influence decisions affecting their lives.

She said, “This year’s theme, ‘Choose a Future for Children,’ is both a call to action and a reminder that the future of our children depends largely on the choices we make today.

“World Children’s Day is more than just a celebration. It is an opportunity to reflect on our responsibilities towards children and to remind ourselves that children are not merely the leaders of tomorrow; they are important members of society today.

“Their voices matter, their opinions deserve to be heard, and their dreams and aspirations should influence the decisions that affect their lives.”

The UNICEF chief stressed the need to prioritise children’s development from pregnancy through the first 1,000 days of life, noting that adequate healthcare, nutrition and protection were essential for their growth.

She also identified poverty, insecurity, gender inequality, disability and geographical location as some of the barriers preventing children from accessing quality education.

“Every child deserves access to quality education, regardless of their background or circumstances,” she added.

Rafique further urged the government and other stakeholders to ensure that children were given opportunities to express their concerns, share their experiences and communicate their expectations.

“After all, decisions about children should not be made without children,” she said.

She explained that choosing a better future for children required deliberate investments in their health, nutrition, education, safety and protection.

“It means developing policies that put children first, allocating resources to essential services, strengthening our communities and ensuring that no child is left behind,” she said.

Rafique disclosed that the 2026 celebration also marked the commencement of activities towards UNICEF’s 80th anniversary, which would be commemorated on December 11.

She recalled that the organisation was established in 1946 with a commitment to protecting children irrespective of their nationality, background or circumstances.

According to her, children continue to face challenges associated with poverty, conflict, climate change, inequality and limited access to essential services, requiring renewed commitment and collective action.

She called on parents, teachers, communities, the private sector, government and development partners to work together to protect children’s rights and improve their living conditions.

Addressing the children, Rafique urged them to speak up, ask questions and express their expectations, assuring them that their voices and contributions mattered.

Also speaking, the Bauchi State Commissioner for Education, Abdulkadir Ibrahim, emphasised the importance of involving children in policy formulation, noting that they needed to understand decisions and policies affecting them.

He said the ministry was making efforts to provide a conducive learning environment in public schools in line with international best practices.

The commissioner commended UNICEF and other development partners for their continued interventions in the education sector, saying their contributions had helped improve basic education in the state.

PUNCH reports that World Children’s Day is celebrated annually on November 20.

It is observed worldwide to promote children’s rights, welfare, education, protection and participation in decisions affecting their lives.

The day was established by the United Nations and marks the adoption of the Declaration of the Rights of the Child in 1959 and the Convention on the Rights of the Child in 1989.

This year’s theme is “Choose a Future for Children”.

The post World Children’s Day: UNICEF urges greater investment in children appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: ABUAD warns students against cultism, cybercrime
description:
Varsity matriculates 2,442 students for 2026/2027 session



By Rotimi Ojomoyela



ADO-EKITI — Afe Babalola University, Ado-Ekiti (ABUAD), has warned newly admitted students against cultism, cybercrime, substance abuse and other social vices capable of undermining their education and future.
content:
Varsity matriculates 2,442 students for 2026/2027 session

By Rotimi Ojomoyela

ADO-EKITI — Afe Babalola University, Ado-Ekiti (ABUAD), has warned newly admitted students against cultism, cybercrime, substance abuse and other social vices capable of undermining their education and future.

The university also cautioned the students against examination malpractice, bullying and the irresponsible use of artificial intelligence, urging them to uphold discipline, integrity and academic excellence.

The Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Smaranda Olarinde, gave the warning at the institution’s 18th matriculation ceremony held over the weekend, where 2,442 students were formally admitted for the 2026/2027 academic session.

The figure comprises 2,089 regular undergraduate students, 77 Open and Distance Learning students and 276 part-time students.

Giving a breakdown of the undergraduate admissions, Olarinde said 306 students were admitted into the College of Social and Management Sciences, 307 into Sciences, 275 into Pharmacy, 684 into Medicine and Health Sciences, 171 into Law and 346 into Engineering.

Addressing the students, the vice-chancellor described their admission as an opportunity that required discipline, responsibility and commitment to academic excellence.

She urged them to be mindful of their associations, noting that their choice of friends could influence their habits, reputation, academic performance and future.

According to her, university education goes beyond obtaining certificates to include character formation, emotional maturity, leadership development and the acquisition of values needed to contribute meaningfully to society.

Olarinde urged the students to uphold the university’s philosophy of Labour, Service and Integrity, stressing that hard work, selfless service and honesty should guide their academic and professional pursuits.

She also cautioned against the misuse of artificial intelligence and other emerging digital technologies, warning students not to present machine-generated materials or another person’s intellectual work as their original research.

“The company you keep will influence your habits, attitude, reputation and ultimately your destiny. Surround yourselves with people who encourage learning, discipline, honesty and constructive ambition.

“Stay away from cultism, substance abuse, bullying, examination malpractice, cybercrime and every other form of misconduct that can destroy your future and bring disrepute to your family and this university.

“No momentary pleasure or misguided friendship is worth the sacrifice of your education, character or good name,” she said.

On the use of artificial intelligence, the vice-chancellor said the technology could support research, improve productivity and create new opportunities for learning, but should not replace independent thinking, genuine scholarship or personal integrity.

“Use digital tools responsibly. Do not present another person’s work, or material generated by a machine, as your own original effort in violation of academic rules.

“Remember that the value of your degree depends not only on the result you obtain but also on the knowledge and competence you genuinely possess,” Olarinde said.

The post ABUAD warns students against cultism, cybercrime appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: 2027: I Support Any Coalition In Favour Of Tinubu, APC Candidates – Umo Eno
description: Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, has declared support for any political coalition aimed at securing two million votes for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and ensuring the victory of All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the state ahead of the 2027 general elections.Eno made the declaration on
content:
Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, has declared support for any political coalition aimed at securing two million votes for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and ensuring the victory of All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the state ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Eno made the declaration on Saturday, November 21, during the monthly Government House prayer service at the Latter House Chapel, Government House, Uyo.

Governor Eno urged believers and supporters of his administration to intensify grassroots mobilisation through door-to-door campaigns, encouraging eligible voters to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and persuading the electorate to support continuity in governance.

He said his administration had given supporters sufficient reasons to canvass for its re-election, urging them to take the campaign message to their respective wards and polling units.

Highlighting some of his administration’s achievements, Eno disclosed that he inherited N111 billion in outstanding gratuity liabilities upon assumption of office, noting that N102 billion had been paid, with the remaining balance expected to be cleared before the end of his first term.

He also cited improvements in bursary payments to students, which he said had increased from N10,000 to N20,000 and N50,000, with plans to pay N200,000 and N250,000 in 2027.

Governor Eno acknowledged that his administration might not have directly impacted every individual, but said the peace maintained across the state remained a benefit shared by all residents.

He assured the people that Akwa Ibom would continue to progress, stressing the importance of electing leaders committed to sustaining development for present and future generations.

At the prayer service, Eno also announced the appointment of Mr Edwin James, who had voluntarily served as a cleaner at the Latter House Chapel for several years, as his Personal Assistant. He directed that the appointment be backdated to June 2023.

title: Atiku knocks defence ministry for promoting APC campaign rally on social media
description:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has questioned the use of the Federal Ministry of Defence’s official social media platforms to publicise the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally for President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid.
Atiku, through his Media Adviser, Paul Ibe, critic
content:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has questioned the use of the Federal Ministry of Defence’s official social media platforms to publicise the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally for President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid.

Atiku, through his Media Adviser, Paul Ibe, criticised the ministry in a statement on Sunday for using its official Facebook page and X handle to announce the rally and publicise the Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (retd.), inspecting the venue.

The rally was held on Saturday at Mapo Hall, Ibadan, Oyo State, where Tinubu canvassed support for his re-election and promised improved electricity supply.

On Saturday, the defence ministry, via its X handle, shared details of the minister’s inspection.

The ministry’s post, which includes photographs of the minister’s visit, reads, “Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (Rtd), OFR, Friday night conducted an on-the-spot inspection of the venue as part of strategic preparations ahead of the upcoming presidential campaign rally in the state.

“During the visit, General Musa toured the premises and surrounding perimeters to evaluate security readiness, crowd management logistics, and overall infrastructural preparedness. President Bola Tinubu GCFR, and key party officials would be on ground for the rally.”

The post had been deleted when our correspondent checked on Sunday afternoon.

PUNCH Online reports that both Musa and Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, are on the security team of the All Progressives Congress 2027 Presidential Campaign Council released in August 2026.

Questioning the ministry’s involvement in publicising the event, Atiku said the development raised concerns about the use of government communication platforms for partisan purposes.

“Why is the Ministry of Defence’s official Facebook page and X handle publicising an APC presidential campaign rally for Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid?” he asked.

He said the ministry’s post announced the rally and described Musa’s inspection of the venue as part of preparations for the event.

Atiku said providing security for a President’s visit was a legitimate responsibility of the ministry but argued that using its official platforms to publicise the President’s re-election campaign compromised the neutrality expected of public institutions.

“Providing security for a President’s visit is a legitimate responsibility. Turning the Ministry’s official platform into a publicity outlet for his re-election campaign compromises the institutional neutrality Nigerians should expect,” he said.

He added that the ministry was funded by taxpayers across political divides and should use its communication platforms to serve all Nigerians.

“The Ministry of Defence is funded by taxpayers of every political persuasion. Its platforms must serve all Nigerians,” he said.

Atiku said Nigerians facing insecurity deserved information about efforts to protect their communities and support security personnel, rather than publicity for a political campaign.

He also questioned the confidence opposition parties and voters could have in the impartiality of state institutions when an official defence platform publicised activities linked to the ruling party’s campaign.

The former Vice-President urged the minister to explain the publication, ensure that partisan campaign publicity was removed and maintain a clear distinction between official responsibilities and party activities.

The criticism followed a report by the Foundation for Investigative Journalism.

In its report published on Saturday, FIJ raised questions about the publication under Section 99(2) of the Electoral Act 2026, which states that “State apparatus including the media shall not be employed to the advantage or disadvantage of any political party or candidate at any election.”

The Ibadan rally was the seventh Tinubu had attended since his re-election campaign began in Kaduna on October 24.

The post Atiku knocks defence ministry for promoting APC campaign rally on social media appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NELFUND considers increase in N20,000 monthly student upkeep
description:
By Joseph Erunke







Millions of Nigerian students benefiting from the Federal Government’s student loan scheme may soon receive higher monthly upkeep allowances as the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, considers a review of the current N20,000 payment amid mounting pressure from rising livi
content:
By Joseph Erunke

Millions of Nigerian students benefiting from the Federal Government’s student loan scheme may soon receive higher monthly upkeep allowances as the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, considers a review of the current N20,000 payment amid mounting pressure from rising living costs.

The possibility of an increase emerged as NELFUND acknowledged that the existing allowance might require adjustment to better reflect the financial realities facing students struggling to meet the costs of feeding, transportation, accommodation and other basic necessities while pursuing their education.

The fund’s Managing Director, Akintunde Sawyer, disclosed this during an interview on Beyond the Headlines,a TVC news programme, where he said the monthly upkeep payment was under constant review.

Although he did not announce a new figure or a timeline for implementation, Sawyer signalled that an adjustment was being considered, raising expectations among students who have repeatedly complained that the current ₦20,000 monthly allowance is inadequate to survive on in the face of escalating prices.

“Are we considering it? Yes, of course. It’s under constant review,” he said.

The indication of a possible increase comes against the backdrop of growing concerns over the purchasing power of students, many of whom depend on the NELFUND intervention to cushion the financial burden of higher education.

With food prices, transportation fares, accommodation costs and other essential expenses continuing to weigh heavily on households, the N20,000 monthly upkeep has increasingly come under scrutiny over its capacity to provide meaningful relief to beneficiaries.

However, Sawyer said any decision to increase the allowance would have to be carefully weighed against the fund’s financial capacity and the need to sustain support for the growing number of students enrolled in the scheme.

He explained that while NELFUND was conscious of the need to improve students’ welfare, it could not make adjustments without considering the implications for the entire beneficiary population.

“What we need to do is plan it in such a way that it doesn’t put us in a situation where we can’t cater for the totality of the people that we need to cater for,” Sawyer said.

Beyond the proposed review by NELFUND, Sawyer disclosed that President Bola Tinubu was also considering an intervention aimed at providing students with more meaningful financial support to enable them to remain in school and successfully complete their academic programmes.

Although he did not disclose the nature, scope or financial details of the proposed presidential intervention, the NELFUND chief suggested that the government was exploring ways to improve the level of assistance available to students.

“I know the President certainly is looking at intervening in a way that helps the students have more meaningful sustenance so that they can get through their courses,” he said.

Sawyer further hinted that changes could be expected in the future, although he stopped short of making a definite commitment on when the review would be concluded or how much beneficiaries could receive if the allowance is increased.

“I suspect that if you watch this space, you’ll see some changes coming up in the future,” he added.

The proposed review is coming at a time when the Federal Government’s student loan programme is expanding rapidly, with millions of applications received from students seeking financial assistance to pursue tertiary education.

NELFUND’s figures indicate that the fund has disbursed ₦180.5 billion to students as upkeep allowances since the scheme commenced in May 2024, while another N194.7 billion has been paid to tertiary institutions to cover tuition fees.

The combined disbursement of approximately N375.2 billion underscores the growing scale of the intervention, which is designed to reduce financial barriers to tertiary education and prevent students from abandoning their studies because of economic hardship.

The fund has also recorded more than 2.5 million applications and about 1.6 million loan transactions across 320 beneficiary institutions, reflecting the increasing demand for financial assistance under the scheme.

Despite the growing reach of the programme, the adequacy of the monthly upkeep allowance remains a major concern, particularly for students who rely on it to meet their day-to-day needs without additional financial support from their families.

While Sawyer’s remarks offer hope of a possible adjustment, students will have to wait for the Federal Government and NELFUND to announce the details of any new arrangement, including the proposed amount, eligibility considerations and commencement date.

For now, the N20,000 monthly allowance remains in place, but the fund’s acknowledgment of a possible review, coupled with the President’s reported interest in a fresh intervention, suggests that the government may be considering a more substantial financial lifeline for students struggling to stay afloat.

The post NELFUND considers increase in N20,000 monthly student upkeep appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Gov Abiodun Condemns Attack On Segun Odegbami, Calls For Arrest Of Perpetrators
description: The Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has condemned the attack on Nigeria’s football legend and Ogun State Sports Ambassador, Chief Segun Odegbami, calling on the police to ensure that those responsible are apprehended and brought to justice.Odegbami, 74, was attacked by armed men at his resi
content:
The Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has condemned the attack on Nigeria’s football legend and Ogun State Sports Ambassador, Chief Segun Odegbami, calling on the police to ensure that those responsible are apprehended and brought to justice.

Odegbami, 74, was attacked by armed men at his residence in the Ibara GRA area of Abeokuta, Ogun State, around 2:30 a.m. on Friday, November 20, 2026.

The governor expressed deep concern over the incident, describing the attack on the former Super Eagles captain as unfortunate, unacceptable, and a threat to the safety of citizens.

Abiodun, however, thanked God that the assailants were unable to silence Chief Odegbami, noting that it was a matter of relief that the celebrated sports icon survived the attack.

” Odegbami, fondly known as ‘Mathematical’, remains an outstanding Nigerian whose contributions to the development of sports, particularly football, have earned him national and international recognition.”

The Governor noted that as Ogun State’s Sports Ambassador, Odegbami occupies a special place in the state’s sports development agenda, adding that his experience, influence and enduring commitment to the promotion of sports remain invaluable.

Abiodun urged the security agencies, particularly the police, to conduct a thorough investigation into the incident, track down the perpetrators, and ensure that they face the full weight of the law.

“No individual or group should take the law into their hands; any acts of violence and criminal intimidation would not be tolerated in Ogun State”

The governor also wished Chief Odegbami continued strength and good health, assuring him of the state government’s concern and support.

He reiterated his administration’s commitment to protecting lives and property and ensuring that Ogun State remains a peaceful and secure environment for residents and visitors

title: PHOTOS: Natasha donates patrol van, computers to Kogi police station
description:
The Senator representing Kogi Central, Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, has facilitated the provision of an additional patrol van and two computers to the Ihima Police Station in Okehi Local Government Area of Kogi State to strengthen security operations and improve policing in the area.
This was disclosed
content:
The Senator representing Kogi Central, Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, has facilitated the provision of an additional patrol van and two computers to the Ihima Police Station in Okehi Local Government Area of Kogi State to strengthen security operations and improve policing in the area.

This was disclosed in a statement issued by Akpoti-Uduaghan’s media aide, Mike Idoko, on Sunday.

She said the intervention is aimed at addressing some of the logistical and operational challenges confronting police officers, particularly in rural communities where difficult terrain and long distances often hamper patrols and emergency responses.

According to her, the additional patrol van is expected to improve the mobility of officers, expand security coverage and enable them to respond more promptly to distress calls across Ihima and neighbouring communities.

The two brand-new computers are also expected to strengthen the station’s administrative and operational capacity, particularly in record-keeping, crime reporting, documentation of complaints, case management and information retrieval for investigations.

Speaking on the intervention, Akpoti-Uduaghan said security agencies needed practical support and adequate equipment to discharge their responsibilities effectively.

She said, “Security is not something we should leave entirely to the men and women in uniform without providing them with the necessary tools to do their jobs. Our police officers need functional equipment, reliable transportation and the right working environment to respond effectively to the security needs of our communities.

“This additional patrol van will strengthen their mobility and enable them to reach more communities, while the computers will support proper documentation, record management and other essential police operations.

“My commitment is to continue supporting initiatives that improve the safety and wellbeing of our people. Every community deserves to feel protected, and our security agencies deserve the necessary support to deliver on their responsibilities.”

The lawmaker stressed that effective grassroots policing required adequate logistics, modern operational equipment and stronger collaboration between security agencies and the communities they serve.

She added that supporting security institutions remained an important part of her efforts to improve the safety and wellbeing of residents across Kogi Central.

The latest donation comes amid growing concerns over insecurity in parts of the country, with police formations, particularly those serving rural communities, facing the challenge of inadequate operational resources.

Residents of Ihima and neighbouring communities are expected to benefit from improved police visibility, faster emergency response and more efficient information management at the station.

title: ‘Don’t let your mouth kick people out of church’, Deeper Life fellowship warns bridal shower critics
description:
The Deeper Life Campus Fellowship at the University of Calgary, Canada, has cautioned church members against criticising a foreign bride and other members over a bridal shower organised ahead of her wedding.
The fellowship’s reaction followed criticism from some Deeper Life members, particularly in
content:
The Deeper Life Campus Fellowship at the University of Calgary, Canada, has cautioned church members against criticising a foreign bride and other members over a bridal shower organised ahead of her wedding.

The fellowship’s reaction followed criticism from some Deeper Life members, particularly in Nigeria, after videos of the bridal shower surfaced online.

A Nigerian man living in Canada recently married a woman identified as Michelle, who is from the Philippines.

Ahead of the wedding, some Deeper Life sisters in Canada organised a bridal shower to celebrate the bride-to-be.

Videos from the event showed the women holding balloons as they prepared to welcome Michelle into the venue before celebrating with her through various activities.

The event also featured trendy social media challenges, including the “I’m not the bride, I’m the bride’s friend” trend.

However, the videos attracted criticism from some Deeper Life members, who questioned the women’s appearance, particularly their use of braids, weaves and trousers, which they said were contrary to the church’s standards in Nigeria.

Some also questioned why the bridal shower was organised, claiming that such celebrations were not permitted for brides in Nigeria.

Responding to the backlash, the Deeper Life Campus Fellowship at the University of Calgary urged members to exercise restraint and avoid making comments that could discourage people from attending the church.

The fellowship explained that Michelle was not born into the church but attended because she appreciated its teachings.

“Just to know. Michelle wasn’t born into Deeper Life.

“I believe we have people who love coming to join us because we have the Word, which is one of the great reasons she loves attending Deeper Life.

“Probably with all this long talk going around, she may decide to never be a member.

“Don’t let your mouth kick people out of the church.

“Don’t be quick to judge,” the fellowship wrote.

It urged Christians to support one another through prayers rather than condemnation, citing Hebrews 12:12 and James 1:19.

“As a Christian we should be praying and holding one another’s hand. Heb 12:12.

“Be careful of what you say. Swift to hear and slow to speak James 1:19.

“Remember to read your Bible very well and look only unto Jesus. God bless you,” it added.

content:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has refuted claims of any disagreement with former manager Michael Carrick during the latter’s time at Old Trafford.

Fernandes stated that there was no breakdown in his relationship with his former boss after his comments following their 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League.

The Portuguese stated this in an interview with Sky Sports on Sunday,

PUNCH Online reported that Fernandes and Carrick appeared to disagree over the team’s tactical approach following their defeat to Como.

The loss raised fresh questions about Carrick’s future, with the ex-United boss facing scrutiny after a disappointing performance that left the travelling supporters frustrated.

Carrick later apologised to the 700 United fans who made the trip to watch the game.

Speaking to TNT Sports on Wednesday after the defeat, Fernandes questioned the decision not to press Como aggressively, suggesting that the approach allowed their opponents to grow in confidence and control the game.

“It’s a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, but sometimes when you give too much of the ball to these teams, they get confidence,” Fernandes said.

It was the first Premier League game of the season that Fernandes had started on the bench. He last started a game as a substitute on May 4, 2025, in a 4-3 defeat at Brentford.

He was later left out in the EPL game against Bournemouth, which he said was unrelated to his interview comments.

“The manager came to speak to me after that game, or before the Bournemouth game, to say, ‘Look, I’m not going to start you tomorrow’ and everything.

“There’s nothing to do with the words of Como; I know people will make it around that. I just want to tell you that we need to change something, I need to make a change, performances have not been great, so I just want you to know that there’s nothing to do with that,” Fernandes said.

Fernandes added that he went to meet Carrick to clear himself of any potential misunderstanding with his then boss.

Carrick later told him not to bother about it as he didn’t feel offended, saying the decision to leave him out of the team squad against Bournemouth was simply due to tactical reasons.

“I told him, ‘I think that you probably got our words in the wrong way, and you might be upset with me, and rightly so, if you got it in the way everyone is speaking about it’. And he said, ‘Bruno, I’m not; I just put you on the bench because I thought it was the best for the team,'” Fernandes narrated.

Fernandes said his return to the starting XI the following game was further evidence that there had been no fallout between the pair.

United later sacked Carrick and appointed former US men’s team coach Mauricio Pochettino.

The Argentine also had a spell in the Premier League where he coached Southampton and North London side Tottenham Hotspur before his eventual move to French giants Paris Saint-Germain.

On his views about the new manager, the Portuguese midfielder stated that Pochettino had made his demands clear to the United players from the outset.

He added that the manager and his staff want the team to succeed.

Fernandes said, “He’s someone who likes to bring a very good energy to the team, someone very positive, very strong, strict; he said straight away that he won’t allow us to not give him what he demands from the team, from each player,” Fernandes said.

“He wants the club to succeed so much, he wants to win games, and that’s pretty clear and obvious by the way he and his staff speak and want us to improve.”

The United captain also revealed that he almost joined Tottenham in 2019 when Pochettino was in charge at the club.

The midfielder confirmed he met with Tottenham’s board, who outlined how he could fit into the manager’s system, with the prospect of playing alongside Harry Kane, Dele Alli and Heung-Min Son proving attractive.

“Obviously I was a very young player who was eager to come to the Premier League. They had Kane there, they had Dele Alli, Son; the chance of playing with those players in front was very attractive,” he said.

Fernandes joined Manchester United from Sporting Lisbon in January 2020 and has established himself as one of the Premier League’s standout midfielders.

He was named PFA Player of the Year in August after recording a league-record 21 assists last season.

United currently sit on 19th with eight points from their first 10 EPL games. Liverpool have retained the fifth position with 18 points, exactly 10 points away from table leaders Arsenal.

The post EPL: Bruno Fernandes denies rift with ex-Man Utd boss Carrick appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: South-East APC leaders endorse Tinubu, back Uzodimma
description:
Leaders of the All Progressives Congress in the South-East geopolitical zone have backed President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027 and expressed support for the party’s leadership in the region under the watch of Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma.
The APC zonal leaders said that President Tinub
content:
Leaders of the All Progressives Congress in the South-East geopolitical zone have backed President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027 and expressed support for the party’s leadership in the region under the watch of Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma.

The APC zonal leaders said that President Tinubu had done a lot for the zone to warrant his re-election in the forthcoming presidential election, adding that recent attacks on Governor Uzodimma were mischievously aimed at discrediting efforts in this direction.

In a communiqué issued at the end of their zonal meeting on Saturday and signed by the Deputy National Chairman (South), Dr Benjamin Nwoye; National Treasurer, Chief Uguru Ofoke; and National Welfare Officer, Hon Donatus Nwankpa, among others, the APC stalwarts vowed to queue behind Uzodimma’s leadership of the party to actualise Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027.

The communiqué read, “The South East Zonal Executives of the All Progressives Congress (APC), having thoroughly deliberated on matters of urgent political and organisational importance affecting the Party in the zone, hereby issue this Communiqué in firm and unambiguous response to the deliberate circulation of AI-generated images, fabricated statements, and other forms of fake news targeted at His Excellency, Distinguished Senator Hope Uzodimma, Executive Governor of Imo State and the Leader of the APC in the South East Zone.

“We note with deep concern the growing trend of digital mischief, character assassination, and coordinated misinformation campaigns designed to undermine the hard-earned political progress of the APC in the South East. These reckless publications seek not only to impugn the integrity of our Leader but also to create artificial tension, sow seeds of distrust, and distract the Party from its core mandate of delivering good governance and consolidating the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR.

“We reaffirm, without any reservation whatsoever, our total, unalloyed, and unwavering support for, and absolute confidence in, His Excellency, Distinguished Senator Hope Uzodimma, Executive Governor of Imo State and Leader of the All Progressives Congress in the South East Zone.

“We publicly acknowledge and deeply appreciate the consistent, substantial, and sacrificial support he has continued to extend to the Party across the entire South East. This support has included significant financial contributions, logistical facilitation, strategic guidance, and personal mobilisation of party members and supporters, particularly during the recent Anambra Presidential Campaign Rally and other critical party programmes and activities throughout the zone. His leadership has remained a stabilising force and a major source of encouragement for APC structures in Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu, and Imo States.”

It added, “We state categorically, emphatically, and for the avoidance of all doubt, that the publications currently in circulation, including AI-generated images, purported statements, insinuations, and related fake news materials, are entirely false, fabricated, and malicious. No such information, statements, opinions, or insinuations emanated from Senator Hope Uzodimma, nor can they be linked in any remote or indirect manner to his person, office, or authorised representatives. These materials are deliberate fabrications manufactured by faceless individuals and groups whose sole intention is to mislead the public, create unnecessary controversy, and manufacture political tension where none exists.

“We are fully aware, and we place it on record, that these publications are ill-conceived, carefully orchestrated, and deliberately intended to sow discord, generate artificial discontent, and create a false impression of friction between our major benefactor in the South East Zone and the Federal Government. This mischievous campaign is particularly reprehensible when viewed against the clear and consistent record of unwavering support that Senator Hope Uzodimma continues to give to the All Progressives Congress, the policies of the Federal Government, and the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in the South East. The authors of these materials seek to undermine the growing political harmony and progress that the APC is recording in the zone.”

The post 2027: South-East APC leaders endorse Tinubu, back Uzodimma appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Why I put Man United contract talks on hold – Bruno Fernandes
description:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes on Sunday confirmed that he received a renewed contract offer from the club, but he has decided to put talks on hold and prioritise the team’s return to winning ways.
Fernandes further dismissed rumours that he demanded more money and years for the said cont
content:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes on Sunday confirmed that he received a renewed contract offer from the club, but he has decided to put talks on hold and prioritise the team’s return to winning ways.

Fernandes further dismissed rumours that he demanded more money and years for the said contract, saying he had always been loyal to United.

He stated this in an interview with Sky Sports on Sunday.

The 32-year-old Portuguese has been a central figure at Old Trafford since he arrived in 2020.

Fernandes, whose current contract expires at the end of the season, last signed his contract in August 2024.

He, however, noted that the club’s initial proposal was made in the summer when discussions first began over a new deal.

He said, “No, there are no negotiations ongoing, but I’ve seen people saying that he’s asked for more money; he’s asked for more years. If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here.

“I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

“Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave, and I always chose to be here. The thing is, I’ve always shown how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it’s time for me to move on, I will move on.

“I’m not going to be the player that I’ve seen many in this time at Manchester United. They’re going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract, and then we will see.”

The United captain, who expressed his continued readiness to continue playing for United, said he wouldn’t obstruct his move away from Manchester if the club decides to lay him off.

“In the moment the club says, ‘Bruno, it’s time to part ways’, I’m going to be the first one walking out the door.

“Yeah, the club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay. And as you said, there are no negotiations going on.

“We spoke about the contract at the end of last season; we came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to one side because I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for the club nor for me, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games,” he added.

Fernandes stated that he still aims to win the Premier League and Champions League with United.

“My aim will always be to win the Premier League and the Champions League within the club I am,” he said.

The attacking midfielder cautioned that simply qualifying for the Champions League should be the club’s target.

“I will never hide from that; I will never say, ‘ No.’ Our position at the moment needs to be to get top four.”

“They’ve been far too patient with us,” he said, commending the supporters for standing by the club despite going for some years without winning a league title.

The Red Devils will travel to Anfield on Sunday for their Premier League match against Liverpool.

United currently sit on 19th with eight points from their first 10 EPL games. Liverpool have retained the fifth position with 18 points, exactly 10 points away from table leaders Arsenal.

The post Why I put Man United contract talks on hold – Bruno Fernandes appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Nigerian sentenced to 24 months in US prison over COVID-19 relief fraud
description:
A Nigerian man, Chukwuebuka Arinze, has been sentenced to two years in prison in the United States for using another person’s identity to fraudulently apply for COVID-19 relief funds.



Arinze, 38, was convicted of aggravated identity theft after using a farmer’s Social Security number to submit an
content:
A Nigerian man, Chukwuebuka Arinze, has been sentenced to two years in prison in the United States for using another person’s identity to fraudulently apply for COVID-19 relief funds.

Arinze, 38, was convicted of aggravated identity theft after using a farmer’s Social Security number to submit an application under the US government’s Coronavirus Food Assistance Program.

He was sentenced on October 30, 2026, by US District Judge Robert Rossiter Jr. at a federal court in Omaha, Nebraska, according to the US Attorney’s Office for the District of Nebraska.

The Nigerian will also serve one year of supervised release after his imprisonment and face deportation from the United States, the statement said.

Prosecutors said Arinze, who was living outside the US at the time, sent an email to the Farm Service Agency office in Wayne, Nebraska, on September 28, 2020, seeking financial assistance under the programme.

The email, titled “CFAP Forms,” contained an application for the second phase of the Coronavirus Food Assistance Program, known as CFAP2, alongside an Automated Clearing House payment form.

Both documents were submitted in the name of a dairy farmer identified in court records as Victim 1 and contained the farmer’s Social Security number.

The US authorities said Arinze knowingly used the identification number belonging to the farmer without authorisation to validate the application.

He was later brought to the United States to face prosecution over the offence.

The Coronavirus Food Assistance Program was established by the US Department of Agriculture during the COVID-19 pandemic to support agricultural producers affected by declining sales and rising marketing costs.

The initiative was administered through the department’s Farm Service Agency and Agricultural Marketing Service.

Its first phase ran from May 26 to September 11, 2020, while the second phase, CFAP2, opened from September 21 to December 11 of the same year.

The programme allowed applicants to self-certify their eligibility without submitting evidence of pandemic-related business losses.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation investigated the case.

The post Nigerian sentenced to 24 months in US prison over COVID-19 relief fraud appeared first on Vanguard News.

The in
content:
By Jimoh Babatunde

The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) Deputy Governorship Candidate in Ogun State for the 2027 election, Hajia Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, has been installed as the first Akinkanju of Egbaland by the Alake and Paramount Ruler of Egbaland, Oba Adedotun Aremu Gbadebo, Okukenu IV.

The installation took place at the Alake Palace on Saturday as part of activities marking the monarch’s 21st coronation anniversary.

Sowunmi-Kolapo, who was previously honoured with the title of Iyalode of Ijemo, is also the Iya Sunnah of Egbaland and Ameerah of Ogun State.

According to the palace, the new title, the first of its kind, was conferred on her in recognition of her contributions to the development of Egbaland and her commitment to the community.

Oba Gbadebo urged her to remain committed to service, cultural preservation and the promotion of unity across Egbaland.

The ceremony attracted prominent personalities, including government officials, business leaders, traditional rulers and politicians.

The Ogun State PDP governorship candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, led other party leaders to celebrate with his running mate.

Speaking at the reception held at the Abeokuta Sports Club, Sowunmi-Kolapo expressed gratitude for the honour, particularly acknowledging the Alake for the recognition.

She also described the conferment as significant ahead of the 2027 governorship election, saying the people of Ogun State had spoken through the honour.

The deputy governorship candidate maintained that the forthcoming election should transcend party affiliations, insisting that the people must resist any alleged attempt to undermine the state’s interests.

“We are indigenes of Ogun State. We do not run from battles. It is in our DNA to always resist intimidation and protect our independence.

“I’m humbled by this gracious conferment of the title of the 1st Akinkanju of Egbaland on me by His Royal Majesty.

“I pray to justify the confidence reposed in me by our traditional rulers, our respected elders, who have continued to stand for our heritage, the people of Egbaland, and the people of Ogun State in general.

“Our father, the Alake of Egbaland, has spoken. Let us work hard to continue to have an Egba community that is first among others,” she said.

Also honoured at the ceremony was Senator Iyabo Obasanjo, who was installed as the first Iyaniwura of Egbaland by the Alake.

In his remarks, Adebutu congratulated his running mate and the other honourees, describing their recognition as well deserved.

He said Sowunmi-Kolapo’s elevation from Iyalode of Ijemo to Akinkanju of Egbaland reflected her years of service, loyalty, courage, motherly leadership and commitment to the unity and development of the Egba people.

Adebutu also congratulated Obasanjo on her installation as the first Iyaniwura of Egbaland, describing the honour as recognition of her distinguished public service and contributions to Egbaland and Nigeria.

He said the two traditional honours conferred by the Alake during his 21st coronation anniversary had further enriched the cultural heritage of Egbaland and brought pride to the PDP family in Ogun State.

title: NDLEA arrests South African golfer, Kenyan chef over drug trafficking
description:
Agency intercepts 160 explosives bound for Zamfara, seizes 4.6 tonnes of cannabis in Osun



By Kingsley Omonobi



The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arrested a 37-year-old South African professional golfer, Grobler Henlo, and a 25-year-old Kenyan chef, Abubakar Faiza Njambi, over
content:
Agency intercepts 160 explosives bound for Zamfara, seizes 4.6 tonnes of cannabis in Osun

By Kingsley Omonobi

The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arrested a 37-year-old South African professional golfer, Grobler Henlo, and a 25-year-old Kenyan chef, Abubakar Faiza Njambi, over an alleged attempt to smuggle 50.40 kilogrammes of Loud, a potent strain of cannabis, into Nigeria.

The suspects were arrested at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Ikeja, Lagos, following the interception of the illicit consignment.

The NDLEA spokesman, Femi Babafemi, said the golfer’s arrest came exactly one month before the agency intercepted an American professional basketball player, Greene Da’monte Khiree, at the same airport on November 11, 2026, over the importation of 33.95 kilogrammes of the same psychoactive substance.

According to the agency, Henlo arrived in Lagos from South Africa aboard a South African Airways flight on October 11 and was intercepted at the Terminal 2 arrival hall.

A search of two travelling boxes in his possession reportedly led to the discovery of 46 parcels of Loud weighing 50.40 kilogrammes.

Investigations revealed that although the boxes were in Henlo’s possession, they bore the luggage tags of his alleged accomplice, Njambi, who had collected two other boxes bearing his tags from the airport conveyor belt before leaving the airport.

The agency said the exchange of luggage tags was a deliberate attempt by the syndicate to frustrate the identification of ownership and enable each courier to deny the boxes bearing their respective names if intercepted.

During preliminary questioning, Henlo reportedly disclosed that he was recruited by a South African associate identified as Shanel, who linked him with other members of the syndicate whom he had never met physically.

He said a driver picked him up from his home in South Africa, handed him four travelling boxes and took him to the airport, where he was instructed to meet Njambi and exchange luggage tags.

The golfer reportedly said he was promised 5,000 South African rand upon successful delivery of the consignment.

Further examination revealed that tracking devices had been installed in the travelling boxes and on his mobile phone, a development the agency said was similar to what was discovered in the bags abandoned by the American basketball player a month later.

The NDLEA said the discovery showed how closely the cartels monitored their couriers and consignments.

It added that the passport biodata page of Njambi, recovered from Henlo’s phone, was used to profile her and place her on the agency’s watchlist.

She was subsequently arrested at the departure boarding gate of the Lagos airport on October 15 while attempting to board a South African Airways flight to Kenya.

The 25-year-old private chef reportedly told investigators that she was recruited through a man who was introduced to her by a friend in Kenya and promised $8,000 upon successful delivery of the consignment.

She said she travelled from Kenya to South Africa on October 4, stayed in a hotel for about a week and met Henlo at the airport on October 11, where he handed her two of the four boxes before they checked them in under their respective luggage tags.

On arrival in Lagos, she allegedly collected the two boxes bearing the golfer’s tags before a driver took her to a hotel in the Lekki area.

The claim tag for the two boxes bearing her name, which she reportedly abandoned at the airport, was recovered from her hand luggage. Both suspects subsequently identified each other during an identification parade.

Other seizures, arrests

In a separate operation at the import shed of the Lagos airport on November 13, NDLEA operatives intercepted a consolidated consignment that arrived from the United Kingdom aboard an Allied Air flight.

The agency said a freight agent, Sobowale Oladayo, was arrested when he presented himself to clear the shipment.

A search of the consignment led to the recovery of 10 parcels of synthetic cannabinoid weighing 10.10 kilogrammes, 27 packs of marshmallow weighing 318.80 kilogrammes and precursor chemicals comprising 11 containers of N,N-Dimethylformamide (DMF) weighing 18.90 kilogrammes, 10 containers of 5-Bromo-1-Pentane weighing 8.05 kilogrammes and seven containers of Potassium Carbonate weighing 7.60 kilogrammes.

The total gross weight of the recovered items was 363.45 kilogrammes.

In a follow-up operation on November 14, the agency arrested the consignee, identified as Kareem Issa, 35, also known as Ola, when he arrived to collect the shipment at a logistics company’s premises in a grey Lexus 460 SUV, accompanied by two other persons.

The NDLEA said Issa, a plumber by profession who lives on Lagos Island, allegedly presented himself as a senior security personnel.

Investigations reportedly showed that he routinely activated the siren fitted to his vehicle whenever he visited the logistics company to collect consignments, allegedly to portray himself as a security operative and avoid attention.

In Kaduna State, operatives on patrol along the Abuja-Kaduna Expressway at Jere on November 17 arrested a 35-year-old man, Lawali Muhammad, with 160 pieces of explosives allegedly being transported to Zamfara State.

The intended recipient, identified as Aliyu Mohammed, 30, was subsequently arrested in a follow-up operation in Gusau on the same day.

Also arrested along the Jere axis were two suspects, Yusuf Magaji and Buhari Yusuf, 32, with 6,900 tablets of tramadol 225mg, 20,000 tablets of diazepam and 25,000 tablets of Exol-5.

Similarly, operatives along the Zaria-Kano Expressway at Gwargwaje, Zaria, recovered 627,500 capsules of tramadol weighing 21.50 kilogrammes from a Hummer bus whose driver reportedly abandoned the vehicle and fled upon sighting the officers.

In Ogun State, a woman, Esther Ogundipe, was arrested on November 19 during a raid on a drug joint at Eleweran, Abeokuta, with two locally made firearms and five live cartridges.

Two days earlier, two other female suspects, Balikis Ogunbiyi and Omobola Ajani, were arrested during a raid in Ilaro with 7.4 grammes of cocaine, 638 grammes of cannabis and 5.9 grammes of methamphetamine.

In Osun State, a 43-year-old man, Francis Oduke, was arrested along the Ikire-Ibadan Expressway with 359 bags of skunk weighing 4,627.7 kilogrammes, concealed beneath a load of granite in a truck.

In neighbouring Ondo State, operatives intercepted a truck conveying 93 bags of cannabis weighing 1,045 kilogrammes to Kano State along the Zango-Ado Expressway, Akure, on November 16.

The agency said the interception followed intelligence gathering and surveillance of the vehicle, which was loaded in Ogbese town.

Four suspects, Adamu Yerima, 19; Mohammed Mohammed, 19; Nura Mohammed, 25; and Usman Mohammed, were arrested in connection with the seizure.

In Edo State, a 48-year-old man, Emmanuel Eze, was arrested on November 20 with 11 and a half bags of cannabis weighing 156 kilogrammes at Aduwawa community, Benin City.

In Katsina State, operatives arrested a 39-year-old man, Abbas Bello, in the Gafai area on November 17 with 148 blocks of cannabis weighing 72 kilogrammes concealed in the boot of his white Honda Accord car.

In Abia State, operatives on November 18 raided a shop belonging to a 25-year-old woman, Oluebube Innocent, at Amankwa Street, Obingwa Local Government Area, recovering two kilogrammes of cannabis concealed in a hole dug into the shop’s floor and covered with ceramic tiles.

The tiles were removed to recover the substance.

In Rivers State, a 46-year-old physically challenged man, Peter Sunday, was arrested with 300 grammes of cannabis during a raid in Eneka on November 17.

NDLEA intensifies anti-drug campaign

Meanwhile, the agency said its commands and formations across the country sustained their War Against Drug Abuse (WADA) sensitisation activities in schools, worship centres, workplaces and communities during the week.

The activities included enlightenment lectures for students and staff of Local Government Primary School, Ebute Ikorodu, Lagos; Government Girls Unity College, Birnin Kebbi; and Community Secondary School, Usa, Enugu Ezike.

The Ondo State Command also paid a WADA advocacy visit to the Deji of Akure Kingdom, Oba Aladetoyinbo Ogunlade Adelusi, Odundun II.

The Chairman/Chief Executive Officer of NDLEA, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), commended officers and men of the agency’s commands in Lagos, Kaduna, Ogun, Osun, Ondo, Edo, Katsina, Abia and Rivers states for the arrests and seizures.

Marwa said the arrests of the South African golfer and the Kenyan chef, coming within the same period as that of the American basketball player, indicated that international drug cartels were changing the profiles of their couriers but retaining their methods.

“The two cases show a trend in which international drug cartels now recruit sportsmen and other professionals as couriers, in the hope that their profiles will shield them from scrutiny.

“The NDLEA has a clear message for such syndicates: no profession, passport or travel class will provide cover for drug trafficking through Nigeria’s ports of entry,” he warned.

He urged officers at all ports of entry to remain vigilant and professional, while charging commands across the country to sustain efforts at reducing both drug supply and demand.

He particularly called for intensified WADA sensitisation campaigns in schools, workplaces, worship centres and communities.

The post NDLEA arrests South African golfer, Kenyan chef over drug trafficking appeared first on Vanguard News.

content:
A young man identified as Amaechi has been arrested by operatives of the Delta State Police Command for allegedly pushing his landlord during an altercation, leading to his death.

The police spokesperson, SP Bright Edafe, disclosed this in a video shared on X on Saturday.

According to Edafe, the suspect, who lives in the same compound with his brother, returned home late at night after the compound’s gate had been locked.

He said the compound had a rule requiring the gate to be locked by 10pm.

However, upon arriving and finding it locked, the suspect allegedly became angry and began banging on it, demanding that it be opened.

Edafe explained that the landlady subsequently threw the keys to someone inside the compound to open the gate.

He added that the suspect allegedly continued making a disturbance after gaining access to the compound, prompting the landlord to come out of his apartment to caution him.

During the ensuing confrontation, the suspect allegedly pushed the landlord, causing him to fall and hit his head against the tiled floor.

The landlord was subsequently rushed to a hospital but later died from his injuries.

However, the suspect, who appeared tearful in the video, denied pushing the deceased.

Sharing the video, Edafe called for greater restraint and anger management, warning against allowing anger to lead to irreversible consequences.

“One thing that you need as a man or as a woman is anger management. This young man came home late at night and had a quarrel with his landlord.

“He allegedly pushed him in anger, then landlord hit his head on the tiles and died. Cool your temper is not a slang. It’s a powerful message,” he wrote.

title: Nigerian jailed two years in US over identity theft, fraud
description:
A 38-year-old Nigerian, Chukwuebuka Arinze, has been sentenced to 24 months’ imprisonment in the United States for aggravated identity theft involving the use of a farmer’s Social Security number in an application for COVID-19 relief funds.
Arinze was sentenced on October 30, 2026, by US District Ju
content:
A 38-year-old Nigerian, Chukwuebuka Arinze, has been sentenced to 24 months’ imprisonment in the United States for aggravated identity theft involving the use of a farmer’s Social Security number in an application for COVID-19 relief funds.

Arinze was sentenced on October 30, 2026, by US District Judge Robert Rossiter Jr. in federal court in Omaha, Nebraska, according to a statement issued by the US Attorney’s Office for the District of Nebraska on Friday.

The statement, sighted by PUNCH Online on Sunday, said Arinze would serve a one-year term of supervised release after completing his prison sentence and would be removed from the US afterwards.

According to the statement, “Arinze committed the offence while living outside the US.

“On or about September 28, 2020, he sent an email with the subject line ‘CFAP Forms’ to the Farm Service Agency office in Wayne, Nebraska.”

The email contained an application for the second phase of the Coronavirus Food Assistance Program (CFAP2) and an Automated Clearing House form bearing the name of a dairy farmer identified as Victim 1.

The application contained the farmer’s Social Security number, which was used to validate the document.

The US Attorney’s Office said Arinze knew the number had been assigned to the farmer and that he was using it without lawful authority.

It added that Arinze was subsequently brought to the US to face charges.

The Coronavirus Food Assistance Program was introduced by the US Department of Agriculture in response to the COVID-19 pandemic to provide financial assistance to agricultural producers affected by falling sales and increased marketing costs.

The programme was administered through the department’s Farm Service Agency and Agricultural Marketing Service.

The first phase of the programme accepted applications between May 26 and September 11, 2020, while the second phase, CFAP2, ran from September 21 to December 11, 2020.

The statement said the programmes operated on a self-certification basis, meaning applicants were not required to provide documentation of pandemic-related losses to their businesses.

It added that the case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

title: ‘I’ve not been served’ – Jimmy Odukoya speaks on court injunction amid church crisis
description:
Pastor Jimmy Odukoya has said he has not been formally served with the court injunction restraining him from presenting himself as the Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos.







Odukoya made this known on Sunday while addressing the congregation during th
content:
Pastor Jimmy Odukoya has said he has not been formally served with the court injunction restraining him from presenting himself as the Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos.

Odukoya made this known on Sunday while addressing the congregation during the church’s service, saying he had only heard about the injunction but had yet to receive the court order.

“I heard that there was an injunction against me. I heard. I’ve not seen it. But I heard. But I’ve not been served. So, legally, I’ve not been served,” he said.

His remarks came shortly after the founder of The Redeemed Evangelical Mission, Bishop Mike Okonkwo, made a surprise appearance at the service and urged members not to take sides in the leadership dispute involving Odukoya and his sister, Tolu.

Thanking members for their continued support amid the controversy, Jimmy Odukoya said he appreciated their decision to attend the service despite the ongoing crisis.

“In spite of everything, you are still here,” he told the congregation.

He also reaffirmed his commitment to the church and its members, saying, “There is no Fountain without you. You are Fountain of Life. And as long as you are with me, I will continue to speak for you. I will continue to stand with you.”

Describing the service as the quickest, Odukoya joked that Okonkwo had already delivered the sermon, leaving him with little to add.

“Bishop has preached already. There is nothing to preach again,” he said, adding that he would finish speaking on time.

He subsequently asked the congregation if they wanted another dance, to which members reportedly responded in the affirmative.

Earlier, Okonkwo told the congregation that he was prompted by the Holy Spirit to visit the church and bless its members amid the leadership crisis.

“I have not slept since 1.30 am. The Holy Spirit said to me, son, go to the Fountain and bless them. That’s why I am here,” he said.

On Friday, Odukoya approached the Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging his reported removal as senior pastor and questioning the legality of decisions allegedly taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees.

The suit, instituted alongside the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church, named his sister, Tolu Odukoya, and seven other church leaders as respondents.

They include Pastors Rotimi Okpaise, Tobi Enuha, Gbenga Onabanjo, Fred Ohiani and Akin Osinbajo, as well as Biodun Balogun and Biodun Awosika.

Odukoya is challenging the validity of meetings held by some trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, and the decisions allegedly reached at those meetings.

He is also asking the court to determine whether the trustees could remove him as senior pastor without following the procedures stipulated in the church’s constitution.

The dispute became public on November 17 when a group identifying itself as members of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that Odukoya was no longer recognised as senior pastor, with immediate effect.

The group reportedly cited a review of the church’s constitution and succession instructions allegedly left by the late founder,

Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, who died in August 2023.

The trustees subsequently named Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader pending consultations and the establishment of a substantive leadership structure.

However, the church rejected the announcement, insisting that Jimmy Odukoya remained its duly appointed senior pastor and chairman of the Board of Trustees.

The disagreement took another turn on November 18 when the Lagos State High Court granted interim orders restraining Odukoya from presenting himself as the church’s senior pastor and spiritual head.

Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin also restrained him from interfering with or disrupting the church’s governance and administration.

The orders were granted ex parte, meaning they were made before Odukoya had an opportunity to respond to the application. The court, however, preserved his right to challenge the orders.

Meanwhile, the church postponed its 2026 Thanksgiving Service, which was scheduled for November 22, but announced that its regular Sunday worship service would hold at 9am.

The church also dismissed reports that its premises had been sealed, assuring members that services would continue.

The matter is expected to return to court on December 1.
