title: Chairman, Grace Ike, celebrates Betara at 60, hails his leadership, contributions
description:
The Chairman of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Council, Comrade Grace Ike, has congratulated the Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on the Federal Capital Territory, Rt. Hon. Muktar Aliyu Betara, OON, on his 60th birthday.
In her birthday mess
content:
The Chairman of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Council, Comrade Grace Ike, has congratulated the Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on the Federal Capital Territory, Rt. Hon. Muktar Aliyu Betara, OON, on his 60th birthday.

In her birthday message, Ike described Betara as a distinguished leader, a true democrat and a friend of the media, whose life has been marked by purposeful leadership, resilience, generosity and an unwavering commitment to public service.

She commended his contributions to the growth of democracy, the development of the Federal Capital Territory and the advancement of his constituents in Biu, Bayo, Kwaya-Kusur and Shani Federal Constituency.

According to her, Betara’s impact on governance and his commitment to the welfare of the people have continued to distinguish him as a leader whose contributions are worthy of recognition.

Ike also described his recognition as The Sun Newspaper’s House of Representatives Member of the Year 2026 as a fitting honour, noting that the award reflects his legislative excellence and people-centred leadership.

She further prayed for God’s continued blessings upon the lawmaker as he begins another decade of his life.

“As you step into this new decade, I pray that Almighty Allah grants you renewed strength, sound health, greater wisdom and abundant grace. May your years ahead be filled with even greater accomplishments and fulfilment,” she said.

The NUJ FCT chairman concluded by wishing Betara a happy 60th birthday, expressing hope that his new chapter would be even more impactful and rewarding.

title: Bayelsa boat tragedy: NEMA deploys technical team as death toll rises
description:
By Emem Idio, Yenagoa







The National Emergency Management Agency ,NEMA, said it has deployed a technical team to Bayelsa State to reinforce ongoing search and rescue operations following a boat accident that has now claimed 24 lives and still counting in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area.
content:
By Emem Idio, Yenagoa

The National Emergency Management Agency ,NEMA, said it has deployed a technical team to Bayelsa State to reinforce ongoing search and rescue operations following a boat accident that has now claimed 24 lives and still counting in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area.

The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, at the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities. The boat was conveying passengers from Ayama to Ukubie community for a burial ceremony when it capsized.

NEMA in a statement signed by Manzo Ezeki

of NEMA Press Unit, said 24 survivors had been rescued, while 24 bodies had been recovered as of Saturday, bringing the number of confirmed fatalities to 24. Search and rescue operations were still ongoing at the time of the announcement.

The agency disclosed that 19 of the survivors were taken to Ayama Clinic, while five others, who sustained varying degrees of injuries, were transferred to Family Care Hospital in Yenagoa for medical treatment.

The deployment of the technical team followed the earlier activation of NEMA’s South-South Zonal Directorate and the mobilisation of an emergency response team from its Port Harcourt Operations Office to the accident scene.

The agency said it is coordinating the rescue operation alongside the Bayelsa State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA), Nigerian Red Cross Society, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), local divers and other emergency responders.

Governor Douye Diri visited the scene of the accident, where he expressed grief over the loss of lives and condoled with the families of the victims.

He also commended the emergency agencies, security operatives, local divers and other responders for their intervention and continued efforts to locate possible survivors despite the difficult riverine terrain.

NEMA expressed sympathy with the Bayelsa State Government and the families affected by the tragedy, pledging to sustain its collaboration with relevant authorities to coordinate the rescue operation.

title: Police arrest two nephews over killing of 70-year-old uncle in Bauchi
description:
The Bauchi State Police Command has arrested two men for allegedly killing their 70-year-old paternal uncle, Sa’idu Malam, over allegations of witchcraft in Ningi Local Government Area of the state.
The suspects, identified as Dahiru Yakubu, aka Dangi, 30, and Musa Alhaji Yakubu, 22, were arrested o
content:
The Bauchi State Police Command has arrested two men for allegedly killing their 70-year-old paternal uncle, Sa’idu Malam, over allegations of witchcraft in Ningi Local Government Area of the state.

The suspects, identified as Dahiru Yakubu, aka Dangi, 30, and Musa Alhaji Yakubu, 22, were arrested on November 21, 2026, following an intelligence-led investigation into the murder.

The command’s Police Public Relations Officer, SP Nafiu Habib, disclosed this in a statement issued on Sunday.

According to Habib, the command received a distress call from a traditional ruler in Kyata village, Burra, on November 19, reporting that the victim’s lifeless body had been discovered beside a river.

He said the deceased, a resident of Jejin-Giwa, Kyata Ward, Burra, was found with marks of violence on his neck, hands and other parts of his body.

“On receipt of the report, police operatives attached to Burra Division swiftly mobilised to the scene. No exhibit was recovered at the scene at that time,” the statement read.

Habib said the victim’s remains were taken to the General Hospital, Burra, where a medical practitioner confirmed him dead before they were released to his relatives for burial in accordance with Islamic rites.

He said preliminary investigations revealed that the suspects were the deceased’s paternal nephews, being the children of his younger brother.

“During interrogation, the suspects confessed to the crime and claimed they attacked the deceased over an allegation of witchcraft. They alleged that the deceased had been bewitching their wives, and that whenever their wives conceived, the pregnancies were terminated as a result of the alleged bewitchment,” Habib stated.

The police spokesman added that a search conducted at the suspects’ shelter and premises led to the recovery of a blood-stained cutlass suspected to have been used in the crime.

He said the case remained under preliminary investigation and would soon be transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department, Bauchi, for discreet investigation and further necessary action.

Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police, Sani-Omolori Aliyu, commiserated with the deceased’s family and the Jejin-Giwa community over the incident, describing the killing as cruel and inhuman.

“The Commissioner of Police has assured that the Command will leave no stone unturned to ensure that justice is served,” the statement added.

The CP also warned members of the public against taking the law into their own hands over allegations or superstitious beliefs, urging them to report grievances to the police or other constituted authorities for proper investigation.

He stressed that “no allegation justifies murder” and reaffirmed the command’s commitment to protecting lives and property.

The post Police arrest two nephews over killing of 70-year-old uncle in Bauchi appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NDLEA arrests South African golfer, Kenyan chef over 50kg cannabis
description:
The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency has arrested a 37-year-old South African professional golfer, Grobler Henlo, and a 25-year-old Kenyan chef, Abubakar Njambi, over an alleged attempt to smuggle 50.40kg of a potent cannabis strain known as Loud into Nigeria.
The suspects were arrested at the M
content:
The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency has arrested a 37-year-old South African professional golfer, Grobler Henlo, and a 25-year-old Kenyan chef, Abubakar Njambi, over an alleged attempt to smuggle 50.40kg of a potent cannabis strain known as Loud into Nigeria.

The suspects were arrested at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Ikeja, Lagos, in October, according to a statement issued on Sunday by the NDLEA spokesperson, Femi Babafemi.

The agency said Henlo arrived in Lagos from South Africa aboard a South African Airways flight on October 11 and was intercepted at the Terminal 2 arrival hall.

A search of two travelling boxes in his possession reportedly led to the recovery of 46 parcels of Loud weighing 50.40kg.

The NDLEA said investigations revealed that although the boxes were with Henlo, they bore the luggage tags of Njambi, who had collected two other boxes bearing his tags from the airport conveyor belt and left.

“The swap of luggage tags was a deliberate ploy by the syndicate to frustrate the identification of ownership, so that each courier could deny the boxes bearing his or her name if intercepted.

“During preliminary interview, the golfer, who travelled in business class while his accomplice flew economy, said he was recruited by a South African associate identified as Shanel, who linked him with other members of the syndicate he never met in person.

“He said a driver picked him up from his home in South Africa, handed him four travelling boxes and took him to the airport, where he was instructed to meet the Kenyan lady and swap luggage tags with her. He claimed he was promised 5,000 South African rand upon successful delivery,” the statement read.

It added, “Further examination revealed that tracking devices had been installed on the traveling boxes as well as on his mobile phone, a feature also found in the bags abandoned by the American basketballer a month later, which shows how closely the cartels monitor their couriers and consignments.

“The passport biodata page of Abubakar Faiza Njambi, recovered from the golfer’s phone, was profiled and placed on the NDLEA watchlist, leading to her arrest at the departure boarding gate of the Lagos airport on Thursday 15th October 2026 as she attempted to board a South African Airways flight to return to Kenya.

“The 25-year-old private chef told NDLEA operatives she was recruited by a man adding that a friend in Kenya, persuaded her to accept the offer of US$8,000 upon successful delivery of the consignment.

“She said she left Kenya for South Africa on 4th October, stayed in a hotel for about a week, and met the golfer at the airport in South Africa on 11th October, where he handed her two of the four boxes before they checked them in under their respective luggage tags.

“She claimed that on arrival in Lagos, she collected the two boxes bearing the golfer’s tags, before a driver took her to a hotel in the Lekki area of Lagos.

“The claim tag of the two boxes bearing her name, which she abandoned at the airport, was recovered from her hand luggage, while both suspects identified each other during an identification parade.”

In a separate operation at the Lagos airport, NDLEA operatives on November 13 intercepted a consolidated consignment from the United Kingdom aboard an Allied Air flight.

The agency said the shipment contained 10 parcels of synthetic cannabinoids weighing 10.10kg, 27 packs of marshmallow weighing 318.80kg and precursor chemicals weighing a combined 34.55kg.

A freight agent, Sobowale Oladayo, was arrested when he presented himself to clear the consignment.

The consignee, identified as Kareem Issa, 35, also known as Ola, was arrested the following day when he arrived to collect the shipment at a logistics company’s premises in a grey Lexus 460 SUV.

The agency said Issa, a plumber who lives on Lagos Island, allegedly posed as a senior security official and routinely used a siren fitted to his vehicle when visiting the logistics company to collect consignments.

In Kaduna State, operatives arrested two men, Lawali Muhammad, 35, and Aliyu Mohammed, 30, in connection with 160 pieces of explosives intercepted along the Abuja-Kaduna Expressway at Jere on November 17. The intended recipient, Mohammed, was arrested in a follow-up operation in Gusau, Zamfara State, the agency said.

Two other suspects were arrested along the same route with 6,900 tablets of tramadol, 20,000 tablets of diazepam and 25,000 tablets of Exol-5.

NDLEA operatives also recovered 627,500 capsules of tramadol weighing 21.50kg from a Hummer bus along the Zaria-Kano Expressway. The driver reportedly abandoned the vehicle and fled.

In Ogun State, a woman, Esther Ogundipe, was arrested on November 19 during a raid on a suspected drug joint at Eleweran, Abeokuta, with two locally made firearms and five live cartridges.

Two other women were arrested in Ilaro on November 17 with 7.4g of cocaine, 638g of cannabis and 5.9g of methamphetamine.

In Osun State, a 43-year-old man, Francis Oduke, was arrested along the Ikire-Ibadan Expressway with 359 bags of skunk weighing 4,627.7kg, allegedly concealed beneath a load of granite in a truck.

In neighbouring Ondo State, operatives intercepted a truck carrying 93 bags of cannabis weighing 1,045kg and heading to Kano State. The seizure was made along the Zango-Ado Expressway, Akure, on November 16.

Four suspects, Adamu Yerima, 19; Mohammed Mohammed, 19; Nura Mohammed, 25; and Usman Mohammed, were arrested in connection with the seizure.

The agency also reported arrests and drug recoveries in Edo, Katsina, Abia and Rivers states.

In Edo, Emmanuel Eze, 48, was arrested with 11 and a half bags of cannabis weighing 156kg at Aduwawa community, Benin City, on November 20.

In Katsina, Abbas Bello, 39, was arrested in the Gafai area on November 17 with 148 blocks of cannabis weighing 72kg, allegedly concealed in the boot of his white Honda Accord.

In Abia, operatives recovered 2kg of cannabis from a hole beneath the tiled floor of a shop belonging to a 25-year-old woman, Oluebube Innocent, at Amankwa Street, Obingwa Local Government Area, on November 18.

In Rivers, a 46-year-old physically challenged man, Peter Sunday, was arrested with 300g of cannabis during a raid in Eneka on November 17.

The agency also said its commands and formations across the country continued to conduct its War Against Drug Abuse sensitisation activities in schools, worship centres, workplaces and communities.

The activities included lectures for students and staff of Local Government Primary School, Ebute Ikorodu, Lagos; Government Girls Unity College, Birnin Kebbi; and Community Secondary School, Usa, Enugu Ezike.

The Ondo State Command also paid an advocacy visit to the Deji of Akure, Oba Aladetoyinbo Ogunlade Adelusi.

Commending officers of the affected commands, the NDLEA Chairman, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), said the arrests of the South African golfer and Kenyan chef, coming within the same period as that of the American basketballer, showed that international drug cartels were changing their couriers but retaining their methods.

“The two cases show a trend in which international drug cartels now recruit sportsmen and other professionals as couriers, in the hope that their profiles will shield them from scrutiny. The NDLEA has a clear message for such syndicates: no profession, passport or travel class will provide cover for drug trafficking through Nigeria’s ports of entry”, Marwa warned.

He urged officers at all ports of entry to remain vigilant and professional, while charging personnel across all commands to sustain the balance between drug supply reduction and demand reduction efforts, particularly the War Against Drug Abuse sensitisation campaigns in schools, workplaces, worship centres and communities.

description:

The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) has set December 2026 as deadline for schools to ensure that, at least, 75 per cent of their teachers are professionally certified and licensed.



Dr. Ronke Soyombo, Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, disclosed this in an interview  the
content:
• ​​⁠‌‌​

The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) has set December 2026 as deadline for schools to ensure that, at least, 75 per cent of their teachers are professionally certified and licensed.

Dr. Ronke Soyombo, Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, disclosed this in an interview the Newsmen in Abuja on Sunday.

She said the measure was aimed at strengthening compliance with professional teaching standards.

Soyombo said schools would be required to meet the certification threshold to qualify to apply for the West African Examinations Council (WAEC) and National Examinations Council (NECO) examinations.

‘By December 2026, schools will be required to have at least 75 per cent of their teachers certified and licensed by TRCN to qualify to apply for WAEC and NECO examinations,’ she said.

Soyombo said the council had integrated its website with WAEC and NECO through an Application Programming Interface (API) to enable the examination bodies verify teachers’ professional status.

She said authorised officials of both examination bodies would be able to access the system using designated login credentials to determine schools’ compliance with the requirement.

The registrar said TRCN had commenced compliance monitoring, adding that it was engaging private school owners and administrators to encourage teachers to register for professional examinations and licensing.

She, however, expressed concern over the low level of compliance, noting that many teachers had passed the professional qualifying examination but failed to complete the licensing process.

‘Our position is that every practising teacher must be professionally licensed.

“Teaching without the required professional credentials would no longer be tolerated,” she said

Soyombo said the council was also implementing an Accelerated Teacher Professionalisation Pathway to enable teachers without professional teaching qualifications to acquire the necessary training.

She disclosed that during a recent teacher recruitment exercise in Nasarawa, TRCN personnel discovered that 250 applicants had presented fake certificates out of approximately 1,000 applicants.

She advised school owners to verify certificates presented by prospective employees, explaining that TRCN certificates carried QR codes that could be scanned to confirm their authenticity.

The registrar added that the council was taking action against impersonation and certificate fraud, disclosing that a suspect identified as Godfrey had been remanded in prison.

On improving service delivery, Soyombo said TRCN had established a six-member call centre to receive and address teachers’ complaints relating to registration, examinations and certification around the clock.

She said the council had also decentralised its operations into geographical regions, with designated personnel responsible for attending to complaints and ensuring quicker responses.

Soyombo explained that a monitoring system had been introduced to track applications awaiting verification, enabling her to identify delays and hold responsible officers accountable.

She said the council was also providing step-by-step assistance to applicants experiencing difficulties with digital processes, adding that incorrect or incomplete academic documents often delayed verification.

The registrar said the reforms were designed to strengthen accountability, eliminate fraudulent practices, improve professional standards and ensure that only qualified and licensed teachers practised in Nigerian schools.(

title: I have not been served court injunction — Jimmy Odukoya
description:
Pastor Jimmy Odukoya has said he has not been formally served with the court injunction restraining him from presenting himself as the Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos.
Odukoya disclosed this on Sunday while addressing the congregation during the church
content:
Pastor Jimmy Odukoya has said he has not been formally served with the court injunction restraining him from presenting himself as the Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos.

Odukoya disclosed this on Sunday while addressing the congregation during the church service, saying he had only heard about the court order but had not received it.

“I heard that there was an injunction against me. I heard. I’ve not seen it. But I heard. But I’ve not been served. So, legally, I’ve not been served,” he said.

His comment came shortly after the founder of The Redeemed Evangelical Mission, Bishop Mike Okonkwo, preached at the church and urged members not to take sides in the leadership dispute involving Odukoya and his sister, Tolu.

Odukoya also thanked members for standing by him despite the controversy, expressing appreciation for their continued presence at the service.

“In spite of everything, you are still here,” he told the congregation.

He further assured members of his commitment to the church, saying, “There is no Fountain without you. You are Fountain of Life. And as long as you are with me, I will continue to speak for you. I will continue to stand with you.”

Describing the service as the quickest, Odukoya joked that there was little left for him to preach after Okonkwo had delivered his sermon.

“Bishop has preached already. There is nothing to preach again,” he said, adding that he would finish speaking on time.

He subsequently asked the congregation if they wanted another dance, to which members reportedly responded in the affirmative.

Earlier, Okonkwo had made a surprise appearance at the church, saying he was prompted by the Holy Spirit to visit and bless the congregation amid the leadership crisis.

“I have not slept since 1.30 am. The Holy Spirit said to me, son, go to the Fountain and bless them. That’s why I am here,” he said.

Preaching on the topic, “The Glory of the Church”, Okonkwo urged members not to identify with either side in the dispute.

“You are not for Tolu or for Jimmy. You are for God. None of them died for you,” he said.

He also warned members against becoming instruments of division in the church, saying, “We must be careful so that none of us will be an instrument of destroying the church of Christ.”

The Lagos State High Court had issued an interim order restraining Odukoya from presenting himself as the church’s Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head.

The order, made by Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin on Wednesday, November 18, followed an application by the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church.

The court also restrained Odukoya, either personally or through proxies, from interfering with or disrupting the church’s activities, governance and other business.

The matter was adjourned until December 1 for mention.

title: Prioritise scholarships over student loans, ex-NANS president urges FG
description: Former President of the National Association of Nigerian Students, Chinonso Obasi, on Sunday questioned the Federal Government’s growing reliance on student loans to finance higher education, insisting that education should remain a public investment rather than a financial burden on young Nigerians
content:
Former President of the National Association of Nigerian Students, Chinonso Obasi, on Sunday questioned the Federal Government’s growing reliance on student loans to finance higher education, insisting that education should remain a public investment rather than a financial burden on young Nigerians.

Obasi, who expressed concern over the implications of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund for the economic future of graduates, urged President Bola Tinubu’s administration to strengthen public investment in education, expand scholarship opportunities and create an economy capable of providing employment for graduates.

In a statement released on the state of education, student loans and youth economic prospects in Nigeria, Obasi recalled that “during the 1976/1977 academic session, the Federal Government awarded 9,458 scholarships to Nigerians for undergraduate, technical and postgraduate studies.”

He said, “the intervention reflected an understanding that education was not merely a private investment but a national development responsibility.”

According to him, many beneficiaries of such opportunities subsequently became teachers, engineers, doctors, administrators, academics and other professionals who contributed significantly to national development.

He, however, expressed concern that the country’s approach to educational financing appeared to be changing, with students increasingly expected to assume financial responsibility for acquiring higher education.

Obasi asked whether “access to university education should become a financial obligation that follows young Nigerians from the classroom into adulthood.”

He particularly raised concerns about the economic realities confronting graduates “who might obtain loans to finance their education but encounter difficulties securing meaningful employment after graduation and the mandatory National Youth Service Corps programme.”

He noted that such graduates would be expected to compete for limited employment opportunities, navigate a difficult business environment and eventually meet the repayment obligations attached to their educational loans.

On NELFUND’s repayment arrangement, the former NANS president observed that the published terms provide for a 10 per cent deduction from the monthly salaries of employed beneficiaries, with repayment commencing two years after the completion of the NYSC programme for those who participate in it.

Obasi argued that education without corresponding employment opportunities, entrepreneurship support, industrial expansion and a functional economy could undermine the country’s investment in human capital.

He stressed that the existence of NELFUND should not be interpreted as a substitute for the government’s broader responsibility to adequately finance the education sector.

“The issue is not whether student loans should exist. They may serve as an additional financing option for students who need them. The issue is whether loans should become an increasingly important response to a problem that fundamentally requires stronger public investment, institutional accountability and economic planning,” he said.

He suggested that young Nigerians should graduate with the confidence that their education had opened doors to opportunities rather than the anxiety of unemployment and financial obligations.

“The country must avoid creating a generation that sees higher education primarily as a financial liability instead of an investment in personal development and national progress,” he said.

He maintained that the future of Nigeria could not be secured by transferring the cost of national development to young people who were yet to establish their economic independence.

“Our young people deserve an educational system that gives them not just certificates, but opportunity, dignity, economic independence and a genuine chance to contribute to national development,” he said.

Obasi urged the “Tinubu administration to rethink its educational financing priorities, invest more in universities and other institutions, expand scholarship opportunities and build an economy that rewards knowledge, skills and innovation.”

NELFUND was established by the Tinubu-led Federal Government to increase access to higher education.

The post Prioritise scholarships over student loans, ex-NANS president urges FG appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Cross River APC calls off Nov 26 campaign kick-off, sets new date
description:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Cross River State has cancelled its statewide campaign kick-off earlier scheduled for Thursday, November 26, leaving its campaign activities for the National Assembly and State House of Assembly elections temporarily uncertain.
The cancellation was announced on
content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Cross River State has cancelled its statewide campaign kick-off earlier scheduled for Thursday, November 26, leaving its campaign activities for the National Assembly and State House of Assembly elections temporarily uncertain.

The cancellation was announced on Saturday in a statement issued by the Director-General of the Cross River State APC Campaign Council, Prof. Stephen Odey.

The statement, released from the campaign secretariat at 42 Murtala Muhammed Highway, Calabar, informed party members and the public that the previously announced campaign itinerary had been cancelled.

According to the statement, a new date for the statewide campaign kick-off would be communicated in due course.

The party did not provide further details on the reason for the cancellation.

The Campaign Council, however, did not disclose the reason for the cancellation.

It apologised for any inconvenience the decision might have caused party leaders, stakeholders, candidates, supporters and members of the public.

Despite the cancellation, the council directed APC candidates contesting the National Assembly and State House of Assembly elections to continue their grassroots campaign activities.

It urged them to proceed with their respective ward-to-ward campaigns, visits, consultations, engagements with stakeholders and other approved campaign activities.

The directive suggests that the party intends to sustain grassroots mobilisation while arrangements are being made for a fresh date for the statewide campaign programme.

Odey thanked party members and the general public for their understanding and cooperation, assuring them that further information would be communicated in due course.

title: Tinubu pledges 50,000 hostel beds in federal tertiary institutions
description:
President Bola Tinubu has pledged to provide 50,000 additional hostel bed spaces across Federal tertiary institutions by the end of 2027 to address accommodation shortages in Nigerian universities.
He made the pledge during the commissioning of Block E of the College of Medicine Students’ Hostel, Un
content:
President Bola Tinubu has pledged to provide 50,000 additional hostel bed spaces across Federal tertiary institutions by the end of 2027 to address accommodation shortages in Nigerian universities.

He made the pledge during the commissioning of Block E of the College of Medicine Students’ Hostel, University of Ibadan, Ibadan, Oyo State, on Saturday.

The president, who was represented by the Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, said the project was part of the N400 billion Student Hostels Programme, to be implemented through the Tertiary Education Trust Fund and private-sector partnerships.

Tinubu said, “My administration will deliver 50,000 new bed spaces across federal tertiary institutions by the end of 2027, through our N400 billion Student Hostels Programme. Our purpose is to give more students safe, decent accommodation that supports their education.

“The newly commissioned facility would accommodate 192 medical and dental students in 48 rooms across four floors, with each room designed for four occupants. The rooms have private toilets, showers and kitchenettes, alongside four reading rooms.”

The president stressed that the college previously faced a shortage of 490 beds, representing 44.5 per cent of its accommodation requirement, following a 2020 directive by the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria requiring clinical students to reside within the University College Hospital premises.

He noted that the shortage exposed students to security challenges and affected the institution’s ability to utilise its admission quota fully.

Tinubu also said more than 36 universities had benefited from the Renewed Hope Energising Education Programme, with power installations ranging from 2.5 to 12 megawatts.

The president added that 20 Compressed Natural Gas conversion centres had been completed, while another 40 were expected by the end of 2028.

“Reliable power supports laboratories, libraries, hostels and the clinical facilities on which medical education depends,” he said.

Earlier, the university’s Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Peter Olapegba, described the commissioning as another milestone in efforts to improve accommodation for medical students.

He recalled that Blocks C and D, named after Philip Ozuah and T.Y. Danjuma, respectively, had also been commissioned as part of the initiative.

Olapegba thanked the Chagoury brothers — Gilbert and Ronald– for their contribution, saying, “Our expectation is that the improved learning environment will contribute to producing healthcare professionals distinguished by competence, integrity and a strong sense of national responsibility.”

In his address, the Provost, College of Medicine, Prof. Temidayo Ogundiran, said the college accounted for about one-third of the university’s institutional footprint, while its researchers generated approximately 80 per cent of the institution’s grant income.

The provost commended the Federal Government’s N110bn Special High Impact Intervention Project, launched in April 2025 to rehabilitate 18 medical schools across the six geopolitical zones through TETFund.

Ogundiran appealed for government support to construct a 1,000-seat student auditorium, expand the college’s administrative building and complete hostel Blocks A and B.

The varsity don also disclosed that the college spent about N18 million monthly on diesel and electricity bills, describing the cost as unsustainable.

“The college currently spends about N18m monthly on diesel and as payment to IBEDC for electric power supply. This expenditure is unsustainable and is placing severe pressure on our operations.”

Ogundiran urged the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, to facilitate the implementation of an approved solar hybrid mini-grid project for the university and UCH, as well as the installation of four 5MVA transformers.

“The ultimate measure of these investments will not be the number of buildings commissioned, but the quality of healthcare professionals, researchers and leaders whose lives they help shape,” the provost said.

The hostel, named the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu GCFR Block, was donated by the Chairman of Chagoury Group, Gilbert Chagoury, and his brother, Ronald Chagoury.

The post Tinubu pledges 50,000 hostel beds in federal tertiary institutions appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: TRCN uncovers 50 suspected impersonators in teachers’ exam
description:
The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria says it identified between 40 and 50 suspected examination impersonators during its recently concluded Professional Qualifying Examination.
The Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, Dr Ronke Soyombo, disclosed this in an interview with the News Agency of Nig
content:
The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria says it identified between 40 and 50 suspected examination impersonators during its recently concluded Professional Qualifying Examination.

The Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, Dr Ronke Soyombo, disclosed this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Sunday in Abuja.

Soyombo said the council identified the suspected impersonators through the introduction of candidates’ photographs into the examination process.

She described the innovation as a significant improvement in examination security and efforts to eliminate impersonation among candidates.

“For instance, in one state, we were able to identify approximately 40 to 50 individuals who were attempting to impersonate registered candidates,” she said.

The registrar, however, acknowledged that the examination encountered technical challenges, particularly poor internet connectivity in Ogun and Kaduna states.

She said the examination was conducted simultaneously across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, making 37 locations nationwide.

According to her, the exercise was successful in 35 locations, but inadequate bandwidth affected the stability of the examination platform in Ogun and Kaduna.

Soyombo explained that the council had initially secured a well-equipped Computer-Based Test centre in Ogun but encountered difficulties when the facility was declared unavailable.

She said TRCN had to secure an alternative centre within 24 hours, but its capacity was inadequate for approximately 1,000 candidates.

The registrar apologised to candidates affected by the challenges, promising that the council would communicate with them and address their concerns.

“We are always willing to acknowledge our shortcomings and take responsibility for addressing them,” she said.

On efforts to increase teacher registration, Soyombo said the council’s digital platform had significantly improved registration and examination participation.

She said applications increased from approximately 13,000 when she assumed office in May 2025 to 26,000 by November 2025.

She added that approximately 21,000 teachers sat for the November 2026 Professional Qualifying Examination nationwide.

Soyombo said the Federal Government had set a target of registering 75 per cent of teachers by the end of the year.

She also disclosed that the government had introduced a six-month Accelerated Teacher Professionalisation Pathway targeting 250,000 teachers, with the first cohort comprising 50,000 participants.

According to her, the programme combines four months of lectures with two months of supervised teaching practice, leading to a Postgraduate Diploma in Education (PGDE) qualification.

title: Don’t take sides, Bishop Okonkwo tells Fountain of Life Church members
description:
The founder of The Redeemed Evangelical Mission, Bishop Mike Okonkwo, on Sunday took the pulpit at The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos, where he urged members not to take sides in the ongoing leadership crisis involving Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and his sister, Tolu.
Okonkwo, who made a surprise
content:
The founder of The Redeemed Evangelical Mission, Bishop Mike Okonkwo, on Sunday took the pulpit at The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos, where he urged members not to take sides in the ongoing leadership crisis involving Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and his sister, Tolu.

Okonkwo, who made a surprise appearance at the church, said he was prompted by the Holy Spirit to visit and bless the congregation amid the controversy that has rocked the church in the past two weeks.

“I have not slept since 1.30 am. The Holy Spirit said to me, son, go to the Fountain and bless them. That’s why I am here,” he said.

Recalling the death of the church’s founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, Okonkwo described the period as traumatic, saying the late cleric’s legacy must be preserved.

.

He said, “And the only thing is that his legacy must continue. And I told you that day that Fountain will never die.”

The bishop, who said the church had been battered by social media discussions in the past one or two weeks, noted that he could not separate himself from the church because of the covenant he believed God had established.

“You can’t separate me from Fountain. It’s not possible. Because it is a covenant that God himself created by himself. So what happens to Fountain affects me,” he said.

Preaching on the topic, “The Glory of the Church”, Okonkwo urged members to remember that the church belonged to God and was not a human institution or political party.

He referenced biblical passages, including Jonah 2:8, 2 Corinthians 2:14, 1 Peter 1:18, Ephesians 1:7 and Colossians 1:14, to emphasise the price paid for the redemption of the church.

Addressing the leadership dispute, he told members not to identify with either of the two sides but to remain committed to God.

“You are not for Tolu or for Jimmy. You are for God. None of them died for you,” he said.

He also warned members against becoming instruments of division in the church.

“We must be careful so that none of us will be an instrument of destroying the church of Christ,” he said.

Okonkwo expressed confidence in the future of the church, saying its growth would continue despite the current challenges.

“Whatever you have seen so far is nothing compared to what is coming,” he said, adding that everything associated with God was progressive.

The appearance came minutes after Jimmy Odukoya received a rousing welcome from members at the church’s Sunday service, with his arrival triggering loud cheers that almost disrupted the praise session.

The leadership dispute became public on November 17 when a faction of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that it no longer recognised Jimmy as Senior Pastor, citing a succession video reportedly recorded by the late founder in December 2021.

The trustees named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader, a decision Jimmy and the church leadership rejected.

The dispute has also led to court proceedings, with the Lagos State High Court issuing an interim order restraining Jimmy from presenting himself as the church’s Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head. The matter was adjourned until December 1 for mention.

title: Otu pledges 10 million trees to save Agbokim Falls, boost eco-tourism
description:
From Aniekan Aniekan, Calabar
Cross River State Governor Bassey Otu has pledged to plant 10 million trees in two years to combat deforestation, erosion and landslides.
The governor made the pledge at the flag-off of the 2nd Agbokim Falls International Green Marathon and Eco-Tourism Festival in Etung
content:
From Aniekan Aniekan, Calabar

Cross River State Governor Bassey Otu has pledged to plant 10 million trees in two years to combat deforestation, erosion and landslides.

The governor made the pledge at the flag-off of the 2nd Agbokim Falls International Green Marathon and Eco-Tourism Festival in Etung Local Government Area of the state.

Governor Otu was represented by the Speaker of the House of Assembly, Elvert Ayambem, at the event, which had as its theme “Run for Nature, Tourism and Sustainable Development”.

He said Cross River experienced prolonged rainfall this year, partly due to deforestation and environmental degradation.

He described Agbokim Falls as a natural treasure with immense tourism and economic potential, and later led stakeholders in tree planting in the Agbokim community.

He also promised to sponsor outstanding athletes from the event to international competitions.

The Minister of State for Industry, Senator John Owan-Enoh, described the marathon as capable of turning Agbokim Falls into an international tourism brand.

He pledged stronger support for the 2027 edition to attract more participants and international recognition.

The Project Lead, Mr Emem Udim-Inyang, said tree planting was introduced to protect the Falls, warning that continued deforestation could affect the streams that feed it.

The Chairman of the Cross River Sports Commission, Mr Lawrence Etta, said the marathon was positioning Cross River as a sporting destination.

title: Tragedy as school building collapses in Abia, kills pupil
description:
Tragedy has struck Ehere Community Primary School in Obingwa Local Government Area of Abia State after a pupil, identified as Vincent Chiedozie Dum, reportedly died when a dilapidated school building collapsed on him last Friday.
Nine other pupils narrowly escaped death after fleeing the area before
content:
Tragedy has struck Ehere Community Primary School in Obingwa Local Government Area of Abia State after a pupil, identified as Vincent Chiedozie Dum, reportedly died when a dilapidated school building collapsed on him last Friday.

Nine other pupils narrowly escaped death after fleeing the area before the building gave way.

The deceased, who was in Primary Two, was reportedly beside the weakened structure to ease himself when the wall suddenly collapsed on him, trapping him underneath.

Principal of Ehere Community Senior Secondary School, Mr. Nwogu Chioma Allen,

said they have been warning the pupils and students about the dangers of going around the dilapidated buildings in the compound.

Nwogu stated the deceased pupil was rescued and taken to three hospitals who rejected for medical attention. However, he said the boy was later admitted at the Abia State University Teaching Hospital, ABSUTH, Aba.

He also disclosed that about 10 pupils and students were playing around the building when it suddenly collapsed and hit the victim while the pupils escaped.

The Principal said; “This place contains five institutions; the Ministry of Education, Primary Schools 1 and 2 and Ehere Community Junior and Senior Secondary Schools. We have a building here that is very weak. The building over the years, has lost its strength. You know children, they have been running around and we have been chasing them , telling them not to go around the building.

“Unfortunately, that afternoon, they were running around the place, up to 10 of them went , running around that building. My teachers were shouting to them, leave that area. Incidentally, the building fell on the boy, the other children were able to escape. The boy was taken to three hospitals for medical attention, but they all rejected him.”

He urged the state government to extend it’s school rehabilitation projects to the Ehere Community Primary and Secondary School.

“Some of the buildings here are weak. The government has been trying in the renovation of schools. We hope that our own school will be renovated to avert such situations.”

When Very Nigerian visited the school, it was observed that the dilapidated building has been sealed off.

title: ‘We love you’ – Fountain of Life congregation cheers Jimmy Odukoya during Sunday service
description:
Members of the Fountain of Life Church have publicly expressed their support for senior pastor Jimmy Odukoya during a Sunday service, welcoming him with loud cheers and chants of affection amid an ongoing legal dispute over his leadership of the church.
A video from the service showed Odukoya walkin
content:
Members of the Fountain of Life Church have publicly expressed their support for senior pastor Jimmy Odukoya during a Sunday service, welcoming him with loud cheers and chants of affection amid an ongoing legal dispute over his leadership of the church.

A video from the service showed Odukoya walking onto the stage to applause from members of the congregation, who repeatedly chanted, “We love you.”

The pastor responded warmly to the show of support, telling the congregation, “Fountain, I love you.”

He added, “We have a lot to talk about, but first of all, we have a pleasant surprise this morning, Bishop Mike decided to surprise us this morning. Please welcome to the stage Bishop Mike Okonkwo.”

The welcome came amid an ongoing leadership dispute at the church, which has seen rival positions emerge over Odukoya’s status as senior pastor.

On Friday, Odukoya approached the Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging his reported removal as senior pastor and questioning the legality of decisions allegedly taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees.

The suit, instituted alongside the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church, named his sister, Tolu Odukoya, and seven other church leaders as respondents.

They include Pastors Rotimi Okpaise, Tobi Enuha, Gbenga Onabanjo, Fred Ohiani and Akin Osinbajo, as well as Biodun Balogun and Biodun Awosika.

Odukoya is challenging the validity of meetings held by some trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, and the decisions allegedly reached at those meetings.

He is also asking the court to determine whether the trustees could remove him as senior pastor without following the procedures stipulated in the church’s constitution.

The dispute became public on November 17 when a group identifying itself as members of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that Odukoya was no longer recognised as senior pastor, with immediate effect.

The group reportedly cited a review of the church’s constitution and succession instructions allegedly left by the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, who died in August 2023.

The trustees subsequently named Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader pending consultations and the establishment of a substantive leadership structure.

However, the church rejected the announcement, insisting that Jimmy Odukoya remained its duly appointed senior pastor and chairman of the Board of Trustees.

The disagreement took another turn on November 18 when the Lagos State High Court granted interim orders restraining Odukoya from presenting himself as the church’s senior pastor and spiritual head.

Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin also restrained him from interfering with or disrupting the church’s governance and administration.

The orders were granted ex parte, meaning they were made before Odukoya had an opportunity to respond to the application. The court, however, preserved his right to challenge the orders.

title: Millions lost as fire razes goods at Yobe market
description:
A midnight fire outbreak has destroyed several shops and goods worth millions of naira at Potiskum Central Market in Yobe State, leaving traders with huge financial losses.
The incident reportedly occurred around 2:00 a.m. on Sunday, November 22, 2026, with the fire initially affecting the section o
content:
A midnight fire outbreak has destroyed several shops and goods worth millions of naira at Potiskum Central Market in Yobe State, leaving traders with huge financial losses.

The incident reportedly occurred around 2:00 a.m. on Sunday, November 22, 2026, with the fire initially affecting the section of the market occupied by traditional medicine dealers before spreading to nearby shops.

The outbreak reportedly took traders and residents around the market by surprise as the flames quickly spread across the affected area.

The intensity of the fire made it difficult for traders to rescue their goods and other valuable belongings, resulting in extensive damage to shops and merchandise.

The affected traders are now counting their losses following the destruction caused by the inferno.

Following the incident, traders and residents rushed to the scene in an attempt to rescue merchandise and prevent the fire from spreading to other parts of the market.

However, several shops and their contents had already been destroyed before effective intervention could be mounted.

The arrival of fire service personnel helped contain the inferno and prevent it from spreading to other densely populated sections of the market, thereby averting further destruction.

An eyewitness commended the firefighters for their timely intervention, saying their arrival helped prevent the fire from engulfing the entire market.

Although no casualties had been reported as of the time of filing this report, the destruction of goods and property has left affected traders facing significant financial losses.

The exact number of shops destroyed and the total value of merchandise lost were yet to be ascertained.

The Yobe State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA) is expected to assess the affected section to determine the extent of the damage, document the losses suffered by traders and establish the circumstances surrounding the outbreak.

The incident has renewed concerns over fire safety in commercial markets, particularly those with closely packed shops and large quantities of combustible materials.

For the affected traders, the immediate challenge is how to recover from the losses and rebuild their businesses following the destruction of their merchandise.

The post Millions lost as fire razes goods at Yobe market appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Tinubu congratulates NASFAT president on birthday
description:

The President described him as a renowned scholar, teacher and administrator of great repute.
Tinubu conveyed his congratulations in
content:
President Bola Tinubu has congratulated the President of the Nasrul-Lahi-L-Fatih Society of Nigeria, Ayodeji Abdulrauf, as he marks his birthday on November 23, 2026.

The President described him as a renowned scholar, teacher and administrator of great repute.

Tinubu conveyed his congratulations in a statement signed on Sunday by his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga.

The Nigerian leader joined Abdulrauf’s family, associates and NASFAT members worldwide in celebrating a leader he credited with making significant contributions to the propagation of Islam in Nigeria and beyond.

The President said, “Under his visionary leadership, NASFAT has helped considerably in fostering religious harmony, promoting community development and supporting the Federal Government’s socioeconomic empowerment initiatives.”

“I congratulate Alhaji Abdulrauf on his birthday and applaud his contributions to the Muslim community and numerous achievements as NASFAT President.”

“I wish him good health, continued grace of Allah and many more years of religious and community impact,” he added.

President Tinubu noted Abdulrauf’s commitment to providing religious and spiritual guidance to NASFAT members in Nigeria and across the world.

NASFAT, founded in Lagos in 1995, is one of Nigeria’s largest Islamic organisations, with chapters across the country and in the diaspora.

The society is known for combining Islamic scholarship with social welfare programmes, including education, healthcare and economic empowerment initiatives, and has grown into a significant voice in Nigeria’s Muslim community.

title: Cheers, jubilation as Jimmy Odukoya arrives church amid leadership crisis
description:
Members of The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos, on Sunday gave Pastor Jimmy Odukoya a rousing welcome as he arrived for the church service, amid the lingering leadership crisis threatening the congregation.
The congregation erupted in cheers as Odukoya made his entrance, generating so much e
content:
Members of The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos, on Sunday gave Pastor Jimmy Odukoya a rousing welcome as he arrived for the church service, amid the lingering leadership crisis threatening the congregation.

The congregation erupted in cheers as Odukoya made his entrance, generating so much excitement that the noise almost disrupted the ongoing praise session.

His appearance came days after the Lagos State High Court issued an interim order restraining him from presenting himself as the church’s Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head.

Despite the controversy surrounding the church’s leadership, the atmosphere within the premises appeared relatively calm before the service, with members going about their activities.

However, the heavy security presence around the church was a noticeable indication of the tension surrounding the dispute.

Before the service began, some worshippers were seen discussing the unfolding developments in pairs and small groups, while appearing cautious about their conversations in the presence of journalists, bloggers and other visitors.

The service opened with a prayer led by a minister identified as Pastor Ezeogwu, who declared, “The fowler’s snare has been broken,” drawing a loud “Amen” from the congregation.

In another part of the prayer, he urged members: “Do not allow us to join the column of gossips.”

The choir later led the congregation in praise songs, with its members dressed in colourful African-print outfits and jackets.

The warm reception for Odukoya came against the backdrop of public exchanges and disagreements that have characterised the church’s leadership crisis in recent days.

The Lagos State High Court, presided over by Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin, issued the interim order on Wednesday, November 18, following an application by the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church.

The court also restrained Odukoya, whether acting personally or through proxies, from interfering with or disrupting the church’s activities, governance and other business.

However, the certified true copy of the order did not direct the closure or sealing of the church premises.

The court adjourned the case until December 1 for mention, with the interim orders remaining in force pending further proceedings.

The dispute became public on November 17 when a faction of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that it no longer recognised Odukoya as Senior Pastor, citing a succession video reportedly recorded by the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, in December 2021.

The trustees subsequently named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as the church’s interim spiritual and administrative leader.

However, Jimmy Odukoya and the church leadership rejected the decision, insisting that his appointment as Senior Pastor in September 2023 was valid.

title: Video: ‘We love you’ – Fountain of Life Church members give Jimmy Odukoya rousing welcome
description:
Members of the Fountain of Life Church have welcomed their senior pastor, Jimmy Odukoya, with cheers and chants of affection during Sunday service, days after a dispute over his leadership of the church became a subject of litigation.







In a video from the service, Odukoya took the stage to app
content:
Members of the Fountain of Life Church have welcomed their senior pastor, Jimmy Odukoya, with cheers and chants of affection during Sunday service, days after a dispute over his leadership of the church became a subject of litigation.

In a video from the service, Odukoya took the stage to applause from the congregation, who repeatedly chanted, “We love you.”

Responding to the reception, he said, “Fountain, I love you.”

He added, “We have a lot to talk about, but first of all, we have a pleasant surprise this morning, Bishop Mike decided to surprise us this morning. Please welcome to the stage Bishop Mike Okonkwo.”

The welcome came amid an ongoing leadership dispute at the church, which has seen rival positions emerge over Odukoya’s status as senior pastor.

On Friday, Odukoya approached the Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging his reported removal as senior pastor and questioning the legality of decisions allegedly taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees.

The suit, instituted alongside the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church, named his sister, Tolu Odukoya, and seven other church leaders as respondents.

They include Pastors Rotimi Okpaise, Tobi Enuha, Gbenga Onabanjo, Fred Ohiani and Akin Osinbajo, as well as Biodun Balogun and Biodun Awosika.

Odukoya is challenging the validity of meetings held by some trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, and the decisions allegedly reached at those meetings.

He is also asking the court to determine whether the trustees could remove him as senior pastor without following the procedures stipulated in the church’s constitution.

The dispute became public on November 17 when a group identifying itself as members of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that Odukoya was no longer recognised as senior pastor, with immediate effect.

The group reportedly cited a review of the church’s constitution and succession instructions allegedly left by the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, who died in August 2023.

The trustees subsequently named Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader pending consultations and the

establishment of a substantive leadership structure.

However, the church rejected the announcement, insisting that Jimmy Odukoya remained its duly appointed senior pastor and chairman of the Board of Trustees.

The disagreement took another turn on November 18 when the Lagos State High Court granted interim orders restraining Odukoya from presenting himself as the church’s senior pastor and spiritual head.

Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin also restrained him from interfering with or disrupting the church’s governance and administration.

The orders were granted ex parte, meaning they were made before Odukoya had an opportunity to respond to the application. The court, however, preserved his right to challenge the orders.

Meanwhile, the church postponed its 2026 Thanksgiving Service, which was scheduled for November 22, but announced that its regular Sunday worship service would hold at 9am.

The church also dismissed reports that its premises had been sealed, assuring members that services would continue.

The matter is expected to return to court on December 1.

title: School building collapses, kills pupil in Abia
description:
By Ugochukwu Alaribe







UMUAHIA -Tragedy struck at Ehere Community Primary School, in Obingwa LGA, Abia State, last Friday, when a pupil, identified as Vincent Chiedozie Dum, was reportedly killed by a collapsed building at the school.



Nine other pupils escaped death as they fled before the c
content:
By Ugochukwu Alaribe

UMUAHIA -Tragedy struck at Ehere Community Primary School, in Obingwa LGA, Abia State, last Friday, when a pupil, identified as Vincent Chiedozie Dum, was reportedly killed by a collapsed building at the school.

Nine other pupils escaped death as they fled before the collapse of the building.

The deceased, a primary two pupil,was said to have gone to ease himself beside the dilapidated building when the wall suddenly collapsed on him.

Principal of Ehere Community Senior Secondary School, Mr. Nwogu Chioma Allen,
said they have been warning the pupils and students about the dangers of going around the dilapidated buildings in the compound.

Nwogu stated the deceased pupil was rescued and taken to three hospitals who rejected for medical attention. However, he said the boy was later admitted at the Abia State University Teaching Hospital, ABSUTH, Aba.

He also disclosed that about 10 pupils and students were playing around the building when it suddenly collapsed and hit the victim while the pupils escaped.

The Principal said; “This place contains five institutions; the Ministry of Education, Primary Schools 1 and 2 and Ehere Community Junior and Senior Secondary Schools. We have a building here that is very weak. The building over the years, has lost its strength. You know children, they have been running around and we have been chasing them , telling them not to go around the building.

“Unfortunately, that afternoon, they were running around the place, up to 10 of them went , running around that building. My teachers were shouting to them, leave that area. Incidentally, the building fell on the boy, the other children were able to escape. The boy was taken to three hospitals for medical attention, but they all rejected him.”

He urged the state government to extend it’s school rehabilitation projects to the Ehere Community Primary and Secondary School.

“Some of the buildings here are weak. The government has been trying in the renovation of schools. We hope that our own school will be renovated to avert such situations.”

When Vanguard visited the school, it was observed that the dilapidated building has been sealed off.

title: EFCC beat NSCDC on penalties to win 2026 CGF Cup
description:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission has emerged champions of the second edition of the CGF Cup 2026 after defeating the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps 5-3 on penalties in the final at the Moshood Abiola National Stadium, Abuja, on Saturday.
The match ended goalless after regulatio
content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission has emerged champions of the second edition of the CGF Cup 2026 after defeating the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps 5-3 on penalties in the final at the Moshood Abiola National Stadium, Abuja, on Saturday.

The match ended goalless after regulation time before EFCC triumphed in the penalty shootout to claim the title.

CGF Cup 2026, also called Comptroller-General Football Tournament, is the second edition of an inter-agency football competition in Nigeria organised by the Federal Fire Service for eight security, law enforcement, and emergency response agencies.

The outcome was announced in a statement signed by the FFS’ National Public Relations Officer and Head of Corporate Services, DCF Paul Abraham, on Saturday.

The Nigerian Air Force secured third position after defeating the Nigeria Correctional Service 3-1 in the third-place match.

Aminu Mohammed opened the scoring for the Air Force before Joseph Yakubu equalised for the Correctional Service. Haruna Yakubu then scored twice to give the Air Force victory.

The final kicked off at 3pm, with the Controller-General of the Federal Fire Service, Samuel Olumide, performing the ceremonial kick-off.

He was accompanied by the Deputy Controllers-General, Achi Okidi and Kehinde Ajasa; Assistant Controller-General GK Arogundade; Chairman of the AMAC Football Committee, Otunba Paul Oluwole; directors of sports from participating security agencies; and other dignitaries.

The statement said both finalists displayed determination, tactical discipline and sportsmanship in the closely contested encounter.

Following the final, Olumide presented individual awards to outstanding players and officials.

Achem Ezekiel of the Federal Fire Service won the top scorer award after netting two goals in 45 minutes, while Titus Ayuba of NSCDC was named the Most Valuable Player.

Eze Daniel of EFCC won the Best Goalkeeper award, while his team’s coach, Kabiru Sani, was named Best Coach.

EFCC finished as champions, NSCDC as runners-up and the Nigerian Air Force in third place.

The Federal Fire Service said the competition promoted unity, friendship and sportsmanship among security agencies, while strengthening inter-agency collaboration and institutional relationships.

title: Divorce crisis: How my wife left Government House — Kano gov
description:
Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, has narrated how his wife, Zainab, allegedly left the Government House and subsequently filed for divorce at an Abuja court.
Yusuf gave the account in an interview with the BBC Hausa service aired on Sunday, where he spoke about the breakdown of his marriage to Zaina
content:
Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, has narrated how his wife, Zainab, allegedly left the Government House and subsequently filed for divorce at an Abuja court.

Yusuf gave the account in an interview with the BBC Hausa service aired on Sunday, where he spoke about the breakdown of his marriage to Zainab, a niece of his former political mentor and ex-governor of Kano State, Rabiu Kwankwaso.

The governor said the couple had been married for about 20 years and had children together before the relationship deteriorated.

“This woman, Zainab, is the daughter of his (Kwankwaso’s) elder brother. He previously married her off to someone, though that marriage did not last long. After that, God brought us together, and I married her. We got married about 20 years ago, and we have children.

“Many things happened, to the point where her belongings were packed and she was taken away from my house, and through it all, I remained patient and did not speak out,” Yusuf said.

He added that he had assured their children that their mother would return home.

The governor, however, said she was surprised when she allegedly encouraged to take the matter to court in Abuja rather than Kano.

“Suddenly, she dragged me to court, a court in Abuja, not even in Kano,” he said.

Yusuf described the situation as unpleasant, adding that he had evidence and detailed information about how his wife was taken away but would not disclose the circumstances publicly.

Asked why he decided to speak about the matter, the governor denied politicising the family dispute.

“I am not the one who politicised it. If this was done to you, how would you feel?” he asked.

He further explained: “To have your wife’s belongings packed without your knowledge, for her to be taken away and kept elsewhere without your knowledge, taken to someone else’s house without your knowledge, and then suddenly you hear that she is the one who has sued you in court.”

The governor said the matter was still being examined and expressed hope that a resolution could be reached.

The interview comes amid the divorce proceedings between Yusuf and Zainab at the Upper Area Court in the Gudu District of Abuja.

The case, marked CV/97/26, was adjourned until December 15 after the Kano State Commissioner for Information, Sanusi Bature, who represented the governor, requested more time to brief his principal on the court processes.

Zainab reportedly filed the suit seeking the dissolution of their marriage, which began in 2006 and produced six children.

The marital crisis became public after Yusuf, while addressing pensioners at the Government House in Kano on November 16, acknowledged the development and likened his situation to a demotion from a corporal to a constable because he now had one wife.

He also said at the time that steps had been taken towards dissolving the marriage.

The dispute has attracted attention partly because of the political relationship between Yusuf and Kwankwaso, who was instrumental in his political rise.

Yusuf served as Kwankwaso’s personal assistant and later as Commissioner for Works during his second term as governor between 2011 and 2015.

However, their relationship deteriorated after Yusuf defected from the New Nigeria Peoples Party to the All Progressives Congress in January 2026.

Kwankwaso subsequently left the NNPP and joined the New Nigeria Democratic Congress, where he emerged as the running mate to its presidential candidate, Peter Obi.

title: Alcaraz to face Zverev for ATP Finals title
description:
Carlos Alcaraz rallied past Ben Shelton on Saturday to book his spot in the ATP Finals title match, where he will meet world number one Alexander Zverev as he bids to lift the trophy for the first time.
The world number three showed signs of vulnerability but fought through to beat the American 3-6,
content:
Carlos Alcaraz rallied past Ben Shelton on Saturday to book his spot in the ATP Finals title match, where he will meet world number one Alexander Zverev as he bids to lift the trophy for the first time.

The world number three showed signs of vulnerability but fought through to beat the American 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (7/1).

He will play Zverev in Sunday’s decider, after the two-time Finals champion beat Daniil Medvedev 7-6 (7/0), 6-4 in the other last-four match-up.

“It’s going to be a high-level match,” Zverev said.

“We had a practice before the tournament started; it was unbelievable. We played one set for one-and-a-half hours, so I hope it’s going to be similar tomorrow.

“I hope both of us are going to be at our best, and hopefully it’s going to be an entertaining match for everybody.”

Alcaraz lost to Italian Jannik Sinner in the season-ender’s showpiece match last year and will aim to go one better this time around in Turin.

He has been dealing with a left-thigh injury since Wednesday but, playing with his leg heavily strapped, he extended his winning streak to 13 matches, a run that includes title-winning campaigns in Vienna and Paris.

However, it was a hard-fought victory as the Spaniard struggled to play with his usual freedom before pulling through in just over two hours.

“I was a little bit frustrated at the beginning,” said the seven-time Grand Slam winner.

“But I’m just happy that I came back in the second set… and ended up playing good tennis.”

– ‘Excited for tomorrow’ –

Having dropped only 15 games across his three round-robin matches without once losing his own serve, Alcaraz was broken in his very first service game against Shelton.

The 23-year-old quickly fell behind 3-0 and was unable to claw his way back into the set.

In the second frame, Alcaraz upped his level, gaining the upper hand by breaking to lead 5-3 before levelling at one set all.

The deciding set remained tight, with neither player facing a break point, forcing the match into a tie-break.

Shelton faltered with two unforced errors, allowing the Spaniard to pull ahead 5-1, a deficit from which the American could not recover.

“I think the third set was even closer. I think he raised the level a little bit from the second set, myself as well,” said Alcaraz.

“Great points, great games, and just happy to play great tennis in the tie-break… I’m excited for tomorrow.”

Earlier in the month, Alcaraz beat Shelton in the Paris Masters final to win the title for the first time — a measure of revenge on the American who had ended his US Open title defence in September.

Alcaraz, who missed a chunk of the season with a wrist issue, will nonetheless be able to end his year on a high if he can next beat the man who took his French Open title during his injury-enforced absence.

In claiming that title in Paris, as well as the US Open crown, Zverev catapulted himself above Alcaraz and Sinner in the rankings to world No. 1.

In a repeat of the 2021 Finals title match, which the 29-year-old German also won, Zverev saw off Russian Medvedev in straight sets.

A tightly contested first frame rattled to a tie-break, which the two-time major winner raced through as Medvedev crumbled, failing to win a point.

The first break points of the match came in the seventh game of the second set, with Medvedev double-faulting to hand Zverev the advantage.

The big-serving Hamburg native, who is yet to drop a set, then served out the match to set up a final meeting between the tournament’s top two seeds.

The last meeting between Zverev and Alcaraz came in the semi-finals of the Australian Open in January, with the Spaniard winning in five sets en route to completing his career Grand Slam.

AFP

title: Ligue 1: PSG lose Doue to knee injury in 3-2 win at Nice
description:
Paris Saint-Germain star Desire Doue was stretchered off in tears after suffering what looked like a nasty knee injury as the reigning French and European champions beat Nice 3-2 in Ligue 1 on Saturday.
Doue went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half as he tried to control the ball, s
content:
Paris Saint-Germain star Desire Doue was stretchered off in tears after suffering what looked like a nasty knee injury as the reigning French and European champions beat Nice 3-2 in Ligue 1 on Saturday.

Doue went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half as he tried to control the ball, shortly after scoring to put PSG 2-1 ahead.

He looked in agony as he clutched his right knee, and the match was stopped for five minutes to allow Doue to receive treatment before being carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium.

PSG will now be dreading discovering the extent of the injury, having lost Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee playing against Barcelona last month.

The Georgian winger is unlikely to return this season, and Doue looks set for a significant spell on the sidelines too.

“We will need to wait until tomorrow for the test results, but it is obviously a serious injury,” PSG coach Luis Enrique told broadcaster Ligue 1+.

The 21-year-old French international, who can play on the wing or in midfield, has been arguably PSG’s best player this season after playing a key role in their Champions League triumphs in each of the last two campaigns.

He has notably scored three goals in three Champions League appearances this season for PSG, who sold Bradley Barcola to Liverpool at the beginning of the campaign and have seen Ousmane Dembele struggle with his fitness recently.

– ‘Not a problem’ –

“This is the life of a professional player at the very highest level,” added Luis Enrique. “You just have to accept it, and I am sure he will find a way to recover well and come back even stronger.”

Asked about the possibility of moving to sign a replacement in the January transfer window, the Spanish coach said PSG were “always open to possibilities.”

“We have players who can come in, and we will overcome this as a team. It is not a problem,” he added.

Earlier, Algerian international Mohamed Amoura had given Nice the lead only for Senny Mayulu to equalise with a penalty awarded after a VAR check following a handball in the home box.

Doue — who was wearing a mouthguard after one of his teeth became dislodged while playing for France against Italy during the international break — put PSG ahead a minute after that goal, turning in at the back post from an Achraf Hakimi assist for his sixth of the season in all competitions.

His replacement Ferran Torres scored PSG’s third in the 85th minute, controlling in the box before finishing on the turn for his eighth goal of the season — but his first in two months.

Ali Abdi pulled one back for Nice in stoppage time, but their run of three straight wins was ended as PSG made it 12 victories on the bounce.

Eight of those wins have come in Ligue 1, in which PSG are now five points clear at the top from Lille, who lost 1-0 at home to Lyon with Mads Bidstrup scoring the only goal.

Paris FC now have the chance to climb into second place and close the gap to PSG to three points by beating Angers on Sunday.

Lyon are up to fourth, while Brest moved into the top six after winning 1-0 at Strasbourg, as the home side lost in their first game since appointing Portugal’s Vitor Matos of Swansea City as coach.

Monaco needed a late Edan Diop equaliser to draw 1-1 at home to Auxerre as their winless run in Ligue 1 stretched to six games.

Lens drew 1-1 with Toulouse in their first match under new coach Didier Digard.

AFP
