title: WAEC, NECO: Schools must certify 75% of teachers by December — TRCN
description:
The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria has set December 2026 as the deadline for schools to ensure that at least 75 per cent of their teachers are professionally certified and licensed.
Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, Dr Ronke Soyombo, disclosed this in an interview with the News Agency of
content:
The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria has set December 2026 as the deadline for schools to ensure that at least 75 per cent of their teachers are professionally certified and licensed.

Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, Dr Ronke Soyombo, disclosed this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in Abuja on Sunday.

She said the measure was aimed at strengthening compliance with professional teaching standards.

Soyombo said schools would be required to meet the certification threshold to qualify to apply for the West African Examinations Council (WAEC) and National Examinations Council (NECO) examinations.

“By December 2026, schools will be required to have at least 75 per cent of their teachers certified and licensed by TRCN to qualify to apply for WAEC and NECO examinations,” she said.

Soyombo said the council had integrated its website with WAEC and NECO through an Application Programming Interface (API) to enable the examination bodies to verify teachers’ professional status.

She said authorised officials of both examination bodies would be able to access the system using designated login credentials to determine schools’ compliance with the requirement.

The registrar said TRCN had commenced compliance monitoring, adding that it was engaging private school owners and administrators to encourage teachers to register for professional examinations and licensing.

She, however, expressed concern over the low level of compliance, noting that many teachers had passed the professional qualifying examination but failed to complete the licensing process.

“Our position is that every practising teacher must be professionally licensed.

“Teaching without the required professional credentials would no longer be tolerated,” she said.

Soyombo said the council was also implementing an Accelerated Teacher Professionalisation Pathway to enable teachers without professional teaching qualifications to acquire the necessary training.

She disclosed that during a recent teacher recruitment exercise in Nasarawa State, TRCN personnel discovered that 250 applicants had presented fake certificates out of approximately 1,000 applicants.

She advised school owners to verify certificates presented by prospective employees, explaining that TRCN certificates carried QR codes that could be scanned to confirm their authenticity.

The registrar added that the council was taking action against impersonation and certificate fraud, disclosing that a suspect identified as Godfrey had been remanded in prison.

On improving service delivery, Soyombo said TRCN had established a six-member call centre to receive and address teachers’ complaints relating to registration, examinations and certification around the clock.

She said the council had also decentralised its operations into geographical regions, with designated personnel responsible for attending to complaints and ensuring quicker responses.

Soyombo explained that a monitoring system had been introduced to track applications awaiting verification, enabling her to identify delays and hold responsible officers accountable.

She said the council was also providing step-by-step assistance to applicants experiencing difficulties with digital processes, adding that incorrect or incomplete academic documents often delayed verification.

The registrar said the reforms were designed to strengthen accountability, eliminate fraudulent practices, improve professional standards and ensure that only qualified and licensed teachers practised in Nigerian schools.
NAN

The post WAEC, NECO: Schools must certify 75% of teachers by December — TRCN appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: First-Class degree not enough to make excellent teacher – TRCN
description:
The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) says possessing a first-class degree does not automatically make an individual an excellent teacher.







Dr. Ronke Soyombo, Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, stated this in an interview with  Newsmen on Sunday in Abuja.







Soyombo stressed
content:
The Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) says possessing a first-class degree does not automatically make an individual an excellent teacher.

Dr. Ronke Soyombo, Registrar/Chief Executive of TRCN, stated this in an interview with Newsmen on Sunday in Abuja.

Soyombo stressed the importance of professional competence adding that effective teaching required more than academic qualifications.

The registrar explained that teachers must demonstrate competence in five critical areas assessed through the Council’s professional qualifying examination.

She identified the areas as basic mathematics, foundational literacy, digital literacy, pedagogy, and safeguarding and child protection.

According to her, teachers must possess a sound understanding of basic mathematical concepts to effectively support children’s learning and development.

She described foundational literacy as equally important, noting that strong literacy skills enabled teachers to support learning across other subject areas.

The registrar said teachers must also understand today’s children, particularly those belonging to the Alpha Generation, and the technological environment in which they operate.

She identified digital literacy as the third major area of assessment, describing it as compulsory for teachers seeking to engage effectively with contemporary learners.

To illustrate the challenge, Soyombo recalled visiting an examination centre where she encountered an elderly teacher struggling with a computer mouse.

“I remember visiting an examination centre recently and meeting an elderly teacher who held a computer mouse and asked me, ‘Madam, what am I going to do with this?’” she said.

She said the encounter highlighted the extent of digital literacy challenges confronting some teachers and raised concerns about their preparedness for modern classrooms.

“How can teachers effectively engage children in today’s classrooms if they are not comfortable with basic technology?” she asked.

Soyombo, however, acknowledged the challenges and disclosed that several training programmes were being implemented to improve teachers’ digital competence.

On pedagogy, she said possessing excellent academic qualifications did not automatically translate into the ability to teach effectively.

“Having a first-class degree does not automatically make someone an excellent teacher,” she said.

She explained that academic qualifications alone could not guarantee that a teacher understood how to apply appropriate instructional methods to address different learning needs.

According to her, classrooms comprise learners with varying abilities, including average pupils, children requiring additional support, and gifted and talented learners.

She stressed that teachers must possess the pedagogical skills to effectively reach all categories of learners and ensure inclusive classroom experiences.

“This is why pedagogy is a critical component of our examination.

“Without sound pedagogical skills, a person cannot be considered a fully competent teacher,” she said.

The registrar identified safeguarding and child protection as the fifth critical area, emphasising the need to guarantee every child’s safety within the school environment.

She said teachers must understand safeguarding principles, child protection requirements and their professional responsibilities towards learners.

Soyombo said one positive development was the growing awareness among teachers that preparing for the TRCN examination involved more than simply passing a test.

She urged candidates preparing for the next examination scheduled for May, 2027, to explore the Council’s online resources and apply the knowledge gained in their classrooms.

“There is no point preparing for the next TRCN examination in May, 2027 without exploring the available resources and ensuring that the knowledge acquired improves children’s learning outcomes,” she said.

She emphasised that professional development should translate into measurable improvements in teaching quality and children’s educational experiences.

According to her, every agency within the education sector must remain conscious of the learning outcomes it seeks to achieve.

“For the education system to progress, every agency must remain conscious of the learning outcomes we want to achieve,” she said.

Soyombo maintained that improving professional standards was essential to the credibility and relevance of the Council, insisting that its mandate must produce tangible improvements

title: Arsenal Held By Newcastle Draw, Lose Raya To Injury
description: Arsenal missed the chance to open up an eight-point lead at the top of the Premier League after a stirring second-half fightback from Newcastle held the defending champions to a 2-2 draw on Saturday.The Gunners led through Eberechi Eze’s strike after a dominant first 45 minutes.But Mikel Artet
content:
Arsenal missed the chance to open up an eight-point lead at the top of the Premier League after a stirring second-half fightback from Newcastle held the defending champions to a 2-2 draw on Saturday.

The Gunners led through Eberechi Eze’s strike after a dominant first 45 minutes.

But Mikel Arteta’s men were suddenly headed for defeat when goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw provided a much-needed boost for under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle.

Noni Madueke salvaged a point for Arsenal and stretched their lead at the top over surprise package Brighton to six points.

However, the loss of influential goalkeeper David Raya to injury could provide a twist in the title race that many believed Arsenal would cruise.

Brighton can reduce the gap to three when they travel to Hull on Sunday.

“I think that we lost two points today,” said Arteta.

“We had some outstanding individual performances today for 70 minutes. But at this level, it requires 96 minutes, unless you score three or four goals and then you can allow yourself 15 or 20 minutes not to be at your best.

“That’s the next step this team has to make.”

Newcastle remain in the bottom half of the table with just one win in six games in all competitions.

Yet, Jaissle can point to his side’s second-half performance as a potential turning point after a difficult start to his reign at St. James’ Park.

“Second half, the momentum and the energy in the stadium, you get the feeling that a little bit more is possible,” said the German coach.

“We’re at the stage of the season where we need to be humble and realistic. A point against the best team in the Premier League is something we can build on.”

Madueke impresses

Arsenal move back six points clear of third-placed Manchester City, who they face next weekend, but missed the chance to put their foot down in the defence of their title.

Madueke continued his impressive form in the injury absence of Bukayo Saka and hit the post early on.

The opener arrived 12 minutes before the break when Kai Havertz pounced on a poor touch by Lewis Hall and brilliantly played in Eze to blast high past Lukas Hornicek.

Jaissle got the response he needed from his half-time team talk as Newcastle came out a completely different proposition after the break.

Arsenal also played a part in letting the home side back into the game and lifting the 50,000 crowd in doing so.

Martin Odegaard shanked his attempt at a long ball forward to allow William Osula to play in Barnes to level.

Suddenly an Arsenal side that had kept seven clean sheets in their opening 10 league games was on the rocks.

Thiaw bundled home a second for Newcastle just 13 minutes later after Dan Burn was left completely unmarked from a corner and his header was only parried by Raya.

That proved to be one of Raya’s final interventions as the Spaniard had to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Raya would be a massive miss if the Spaniard is sidelined for a significant spell.

But Arsenal regained their composure in time to salvage a point that keeps them well in the driving seat to retain the title.

Odegaard made amends for his earlier error by freeing Madueke down the right and he cut inside before his tame deflected shot found a way past Hornicek.

AFP

content:
…Traders count losses as inferno razes shops in Potiskum

By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman

A midnight fire outbreak has destroyed several shops and goods worth millions of naira at the Potiskum Central Market in Yobe State, leaving traders counting their losses.

The fire, which reportedly started at about 2:00 a.m. on Sunday, November 22, 2026, initially affected the section of the market occupied by traditional medicine dealers before spreading to adjoining shops.

The outbreak reportedly caught traders and residents around the market unawares, as the flames spread rapidly through the affected section, making it difficult to salvage goods and other valuables.

Following the incident, traders and residents rushed to the scene in an attempt to rescue merchandise and prevent the fire from spreading to other parts of the market.

However, several shops and their contents had already been destroyed before effective intervention could be mounted.

The arrival of fire service personnel helped contain the inferno and prevent it from spreading to other densely populated sections of the market, thereby averting further destruction.

An eyewitness commended the firefighters for their timely intervention, saying their arrival helped prevent the fire from engulfing the entire market.

Although no casualties had been reported as of the time of filing this report, the destruction of goods and property has left affected traders facing significant financial losses.

The exact number of shops destroyed and the total value of merchandise lost were yet to be ascertained.

The Yobe State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA) is expected to assess the affected section to determine the extent of the damage, document the losses suffered by traders and establish the circumstances surrounding the outbreak.

The incident has renewed concerns over fire safety in commercial markets, particularly those with closely packed shops and large quantities of combustible materials.

For the affected traders, the immediate challenge is how to recover from the losses and rebuild their businesses following the destruction of their merchandise.

The post Fire destroys goods worth millions in Yobe market appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Omo-Agege backs Obi, not Tinubu, says aide
description:
...Says APC circulating seven-month-old video to misrepresent senator’s position







Senator Ovie Omo-Agege has reaffirmed his support for Peter Obi as the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate for the 2027 general election, dismissing a video circulating on social media in wh
content:
...Says APC circulating seven-month-old video to misrepresent senator’s position

Senator Ovie Omo-Agege has reaffirmed his support for Peter Obi as the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate for the 2027 general election, dismissing a video circulating on social media in which he expressed support for President Bola Tinubu.

Omo-Agege’s position was contained in a statement issued on Saturday by his Special Adviser on Strategy and Communications, Godwin Anaughe, who accused the Delta State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and some officials of the state government of circulating an old video to misrepresent the senator’s political position.

The statement said the video, recorded in April 2026 at the Federal Polytechnic, Orogun, when Omo-Agege was still a member of the APC, showed him expressing support for Tinubu.

However, Anaughe described the circulation of the footage as misleading, arguing that it predated the senator’s defection from the APC to the NDC in May 2026.

According to the statement, Omo-Agege subsequently endorsed Obi at the NDC nomination convention on May 30, 2026, where he seconded the former Anambra State governor’s nomination as the party’s presidential candidate.

It added that the senator also declared his support for Obi during an appearance on Arise Television on June 3, 2026, describing him as his preferred presidential candidate for 2027.

The aide maintained that Omo-Agege had consistently expressed the same position since joining the NDC.

“For the record: Senator Omo-Agege is not endorsing President Tinubu for re-election. He is not going back to the APC. He is the NDC Senatorial candidate for Delta Central, and he stands solidly with Deltans and Nigerians in their resolve to make Peter Obi President in 2027,” the statement said.

Anaughe argued that a video recorded while Omo-Agege was still in the APC could not be used to establish his current political allegiance.

He accused those circulating the footage of deliberately ignoring the date it was recorded, insisting that the senator’s subsequent public declarations provided a clearer account of his present political position.

The statement also challenged the APC to focus on defending its performance in government rather than circulating old political footage.

It cited rising food prices, unemployment and declining public confidence as issues Nigerians expected political parties to address.

“If the APC wants to talk, it should talk about its record, not its video library,” Anaughe said.

He added that Omo-Agege remained focused on the 2027 elections and his support for what he described as a new Nigeria where opportunities would not depend on personal connections. The statement concluded with the slogan, “A New Nigeria Is Possible.”

content:
Church members erupted in cheers on Sunday as Pastor Jimmy Odukoya arrived for the service at The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos, with the excitement generating noise that almost disrupted the ongoing praise session.

His arrival came amid the leadership crisis rocking the church, following a court order restraining him from presenting himself as its Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head.

Before his arrival, the social media tension and drama of the past week did not appear to extend to the church premises, as the atmosphere was relatively calm and members went about their activities as though nothing had happened.

The heavy security presence around the premises was, however, one of the few indications that something might have happened.

Before the service began, church members were seen discussing the unfolding developments in pairs and small groups. They appeared more careful with their conversations, seemingly conscious that journalists, bloggers and other visitors could be present.

An opening prayer was led by a minister simply identified as Pastor Ezeogwu, while members settled down for the service.

“The fowler’s snare has been broken,” the minister prayed, drawing a thunderous “Amen” from the congregation.

In another part of the prayer, he said, “Do not allow us to join the column of gossips,” a remark that appeared to speak to the controversy surrounding the church’s leadership.

The choir later cheered the congregation with praise songs, dressed in African-print outfits and jackets of different colours.

The scene came amid the social media exchanges and public disagreement that have characterised the church’s leadership crisis in the past week.

The Lagos State High Court had issued an interim order restraining Odukoya from presenting himself as the Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of the church.

The order, made by Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin on Wednesday, November 18, followed an application by the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church.

The court also restrained Odukoya, either personally or through proxies, from interfering with or disrupting the church’s activities, governance and other business.

However, the certified true copy of the order did not direct the closure or sealing of the church premises.

The court adjourned the matter until December 1 for mention, while the interim orders remain subject to further proceedings.

title: Full list: FG announces 19 international job vacancies [How to apply]
description:
The Federal Government, FG has announced 19 international job vacancies for qualified Nigerians at the African Space Agency and the General Secretariat of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC).







The vacancies, announced by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, comprise five positions at the
content:
The Federal Government, FG has announced 19 international job vacancies for qualified Nigerians at the African Space Agency and the General Secretariat of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC).

The vacancies, announced by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, comprise five positions at the African Space Agency headquarters in Cairo, Egypt, and 14 positions at the OIC headquarters in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

The ministry disclosed this in two separate vacancy announcements dated Friday, November 20, 2026, signed by its spokesperson, Oluwafemi Adeniyi, and shared on its official Facebook page on Saturday.

According to the ministry, the African Space Agency is recruiting for five positions, with application deadlines of November 25 and December 10, 2026.

The positions include Director, Corporate Services (D-1); Director-General, African Space Agency (D-2); Head of Legal Affairs (Grade P-5); Senior Finance Officer (P3); and Senior Human Resources Officer (P3).

The ministry said interested and qualified Nigerians should visit the agency’s official website at https://africanspaceagency.org for details of the eligibility requirements and application procedures.

For the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, the ministry announced 14 vacancies across its departments and specialised units.

The positions include Director-General of Political Affairs; Director, Administration Department; Director, Information Department; Director, Conference Department; Director, Muslim Communities and Minorities; Director, African Affairs; and Director, European Affairs and International Organisations.

Others are Head of Human Resources (PP2); Professional Officer, Human Resources (PP2); Professional Officers, Administration Department (P2); Director, Peace, Security and Mediation Unit; Chief of HRC Office – IUT; Registrar – IUT; and Deputy Internal Auditor – IUT.

The ministry said the application deadlines for the OIC positions range from November 29 to December 24, 2026.

It urged interested and qualified Nigerians to visit the organisation’s official vacancy portal at https://www.oic-oci.org/en/vacancies for information on the specific requirements, application procedures and deadlines for each position.

How to apply

Interested Nigerians can apply through the following official platforms:

  1. African Space Agency: Visit https://africanspaceagency.org, navigate to the recruitment or careers section, and check the available positions, eligibility criteria and application instructions.
  2. Organisation of Islamic Cooperation: Visit https://www.oic-oci.org/en/vacancies, select the relevant vacancy and follow the stated application procedure.

Applicants are advised to review the requirements for their preferred positions and submit their applications before the respective deadlines.

description:
…Directs National Assembly, Assembly candidates to continue ward-to-ward campaigns







By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR







The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Cross River State has cancelled its statewide campaign kick-off scheduled for Thursday, November 26, throwing its campaign timetable for
content:
…Directs National Assembly, Assembly candidates to continue ward-to-ward campaigns

By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR

The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Cross River State has cancelled its statewide campaign kick-off scheduled for Thursday, November 26, throwing its campaign timetable for the National Assembly and State House of Assembly elections into temporary uncertainty.

The cancellation was announced in a statement issued on Saturday by the Director-General of the Cross River State APC Campaign Council, Prof. Stephen Odey, from the campaign secretariat at 42 Murtala Muhammed Highway, Calabar.

The statement said the campaign itinerary, which had earlier been released, had been cancelled, adding that a new date would be announced in due course.

The Campaign Council, however, did not disclose the reason for the cancellation.

It apologised for any inconvenience the decision might have caused party leaders, stakeholders, candidates, supporters and members of the public.

Despite the cancellation, the council directed APC candidates contesting the National Assembly and State House of Assembly elections to continue their grassroots campaign activities.

It urged them to proceed with their respective ward-to-ward campaigns, visits, consultations, engagements with stakeholders and other approved campaign activities.

The directive suggests that the party intends to sustain grassroots mobilisation while arrangements are being made for a fresh date for the statewide campaign programme.

Odey thanked party members and the general public for their understanding and cooperation, assuring them that further information would be communicated in due course.

title: Dickson mourns victims of Bayelsa boat mishap, seeks safety measures
description:
Former Governor of Bayelsa State, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, has commiserated with the families and friends of victims of the boat mishap along the Ayama/Oweikorogha waterways in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state.







Dickson, who disclosed this in a post on his X platform on S
content:
Former Governor of Bayelsa State, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, has commiserated with the families and friends of victims of the boat mishap along the Ayama/Oweikorogha waterways in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state.

Dickson, who disclosed this in a post on his X platform on Sunday, described the incident as unfortunate and expressed sadness over the loss of lives.

He also extended his condolences to the Bayelsa State Government and the people of the state over the tragedy.

The senator said he deliberately scaled down his engagements on Saturday as a mark of respect for those who lost their lives in the incident.

According to him, he reduced the number of visitors he attended to and cancelled some previously scheduled visits to reflect on the tragedy.

Dickson commended the relevant emergency response agencies and other individuals involved in the rescue operation for their swift response, urging them to sustain their efforts until the operation was successfully concluded.

He also called for stricter enforcement of maritime safety regulations and increased public awareness to prevent similar incidents.

The former governor stressed the need for continuous safety education for marine operators, security personnel and residents of Bayelsa State.

He further urged traditional institutions and the media to support efforts aimed at promoting maritime safety and ensuring compliance with relevant regulations.

Dickson reiterated his condolences to the bereaved families, praying that God would grant the deceased eternal rest and give their loved ones the strength to bear the loss.

title: Tinubu reiterates commitment to uninterrupted academic calendars
description:
President Bola Tinubu has reiterated his administration’s commitment to strengthening public tertiary institutions through infrastructure interventions, student financing and policies supporting uninterrupted academic calendars.







Tinubu said this during the grand finale of the 37th Convocation
content:
President Bola Tinubu has reiterated his administration’s commitment to strengthening public tertiary institutions through infrastructure interventions, student financing and policies supporting uninterrupted academic calendars.

Tinubu said this during the grand finale of the 37th Convocation ceremony of the Federal University of Technology, Akure (FUTA) on Saturday in Akure.

The ceremony featured conferment of postgraduate degrees on 1,173 graduands and the decoration of the scholars as Professors Emeriti.

The President, represented by Prof. Olatunde Ajagbonna of the National Universities Commission (NUC), said his administration recognised universities as vital to scientific, technological and economic progress.

“My administration recognises the critical role of universities in national development and has continued to support our tertiary institutions through interventions in infrastructure, equipment, research facilities, laboratories, lecture theatres and student accommodation.

“In furtherance of our commitment to student welfare, the Federal Government is also supporting the construction of 1,500-capacity hostel at FUTA in partnership with private sector organisations.

“In the education sector, I remain committed to ensuring that no Nigerian student is denied access to tertiary education on account of financial difficulties.

“The commitment informed the establishment of Nigerian Education Loan Fund(NELFUND) by my government, which provides financial assistance to eligible students in public tertiary institutions, including support for their upkeep,” he said.

Tinubu noted that economic reforms had yielded growth above four per cent in 2026 across oil and non-oil sectors, urging judicious use of federal interventions.

He urged the private sector and development partners to collaborate with FUTA in engineering, agriculture, healthcare, artificial intelligence and information technology to drive innovation and job creation.

In his goodwill message, Gov. Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo State, represented by Commissioner for Education, Science and Technology, Prof. Igbekele Ajibefun, congratulated the graduands and commended the vice-chancellor’s leadership.

Aiyedatiwa said the state government would continue to partner with and support FUTA in achieving its aspirations and advancing human capital development.

Earlier, FUTA Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Adenike Oladiji, said the event marked the fourth and final convocation of her tenure as the eighth substantive vice-chancellor since May 2022.

Oladiji said the university sustained a stable academic calendar and achieved NUC accreditation for its College of Health Sciences.

She said FUTA had no abandoned projects, reporting 21 completed projects and 24 ongoing projects, alongside agricultural expansion, a 5,000-layer poultry revamp and a revitalised feed-mill.

Giving a breakdown of the 1,173 postgraduate graduands, Oladiji said 641 received Master’s degree and 225 bagged Postgraduate Diploma.
She added that 173 earned Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degree, 131 graduated from the School of Professional Development, and three received Master of Philosophy (M.Phil) degree.

She announced that Prof. Felix Akinyosoye and Prof. Thomas Ofuya would be decorated as Professors Emeriti.

Prof. Akinyosoye was decorated as Professor Emeritus of Microbiology, Food Fermentation and Zymology, while Prof. Ofuya was decorated as Professor Emeritus of Crop Entomology.

Also speaking, Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the Governing Council, Dr Olugbenga Awe, congratulated the graduands and the two decorated Professors Emeriti.

Awe urged the graduands to approach their future with intellectual humility and apply their knowledge to improve institutions and solve societal challenges.

title: SERAP sues NDPC, INEC over AI manipulation of voters’ register
description: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project has sued the Nigeria Data Protection Commission and the Independent National Electoral Commission over alleged manipulation of the preliminary Register of Voters with artificial intelligence-generated photographs and possible breaches of voters’ p
content:
The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project has sued the Nigeria Data Protection Commission and the Independent National Electoral Commission over alleged manipulation of the preliminary Register of Voters with artificial intelligence-generated photographs and possible breaches of voters’ personal data.

SERAP said it filed the suit at the Federal High Court in Abuja last week, seeking an order compelling the data protection commission to independently investigate allegations of irregularities in the voters’ register.

The organisation disclosed this in a statement issued on Sunday by its Deputy Director, Kolawole Oluwadare.

In the suit, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/2863/2026, SERAP is asking the court “an order of mandamus to direct and compel the NDPC to obtain and examine relevant records, documents and electronic data held by INEC to establish the nature and extent of the reported irregularities and determine whether the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 has been violated.”

It is also seeking “an order of mandamus to direct and compel the NDPC to exercise its enforcement powers under the Act, including issuing corrective orders, imposing appropriate fines and sanctions, and facilitating remedies or compensation for voters affected by any established violations.”

The organisation said the alleged irregularities raised concerns about the security of Nigerians’ personal information and the reliability of the voters’ register ahead of the 2027 general elections.

It added that the accuracy of the register was essential to protecting voters’ personal data and their right to participate in public affairs.

“Nigerians should not have to worry that their personal information could be altered, manipulated or accessed without proper safeguards,” it said.

SERAP argued that INEC’s acknowledgement of questionable records and suspected AI-generated photographs made an independent investigation necessary.

“The public needs to know what happened, whether the law was breached and what measures are being taken to prevent a recurrence,” the organisation said.

It also urged the NDPC to conduct an independent forensic examination of INEC’s affected database and systems to establish whether personal data were unlawfully accessed or altered.

“The NDPC should exercise its statutory powers independently and without delay. Any investigation must establish the facts, protect affected voters and ensure that those responsible for any unlawful conduct are held accountable,” it said.

The suit, filed on behalf of SERAP by its lawyers, Oluwakemi Agunbiade, Kehinde Oyewumi, Andrew Nwankwo and Valentina Adegoke, also asks the court to compel the NDPC to determine whether the incidents constitute a personal data breach under Section 65 of the Nigeria Data Protection Act.

The organisation said the investigation should establish the number and geographical distribution of affected records, when and how they were created or altered, and the persons or institutions responsible.

It argued that the alleged irregularities could involve the unlawful alteration or processing of personal data, misuse of authorised access credentials and failures to protect information held by INEC.

SERAP further said any compromise of the voter database could undermine confidence in the electoral process and expose eligible voters to wrongful exclusion.

The suit also cited Section 37 of the Nigerian Constitution, which guarantees the right to privacy, as well as provisions of the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights and the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights on political participation.

The legal action follows INEC’s acknowledgement of suspected AI-generated photographs and questionable registration records in its preliminary Register of Voters.

In a statement issued on October 27, the commission said some questionable records were identified and flagged for further examination during the nationwide physical display of the register from October 9 to 15.

INEC said it had commenced a review and was taking corrective action, adding that the online publication did not reflect all its ongoing data-cleanup activities.

The commission also said it was examining the circumstances surrounding the suspicious photographs, including possible technical or procedural lapses.

On November 1, INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Lawrence Bayode, disclosed that its Automated Biometric Identification System had flagged 268 records for review over suspected AI-generated photographs and other irregularities.

The commission maintained that the preliminary register was not the final certified version and said it would complete its verification, adjudication and data-cleanup processes before certifying the final Register of Voters on December 15, 2026.

SERAP said an internal review by INEC could not replace an independent investigation by the data protection commission.

No date has been fixed for the hearing of the suit.

The post SERAP sues NDPC, INEC over AI manipulation of voters’ register appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Photos: Police take over Fountain of Life Church amid leadership crisis
description:
…As trustees, Jimmy Odukoya trade court actions, church postpones thanksgiving service







There was a heavy presence of police personnel at the headquarters of The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos, on Sunday, as the leadership crisis rocking the church deepened, leaving worshippers uncert
content:
…As trustees, Jimmy Odukoya trade court actions, church postpones thanksgiving service

There was a heavy presence of police personnel at the headquarters of The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos, on Sunday, as the leadership crisis rocking the church deepened, leaving worshippers uncertain about who would preside over the regular Sunday service.

The security presence came amid a bitter dispute between Senior Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and a group of church trustees over his continued leadership of the ministry founded by his late father, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya.

The disagreement has escalated into a legal battle, with both sides seeking judicial intervention over the control and administration of the church.

On Friday, Odukoya approached the Federal High Court in Lagos, challenging his reported removal as senior pastor and questioning the legality of decisions taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees.

The suit, instituted by Odukoya alongside the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church, named his sister, Tolu Odukoya, and seven other church leaders as respondents.

The respondents include Pastor Rotimi Okpaise, Pastor Tobi Enuha, Pastor Gbenga Onabanjo, Pastor Fred Ohiani, Pastor Akin Osinbajo, Biodun Balogun and Biodun Awosika.

In the court action, Odukoya is challenging the validity of meetings held by some trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, as well as the decisions allegedly taken at those meetings.

He is also asking the court to determine whether the trustees could remove him as senior pastor without following the procedures stipulated in the church’s constitution.

How the crisis started

The leadership dispute became public on November 17 when a group identifying itself as members of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that Odukoya was no longer recognised as the senior pastor, with immediate effect.

The trustees reportedly based their decision on a review of the church’s constitution and recorded succession instructions allegedly left by its late founder, Taiwo Odukoya, before his death in 2023.

They maintained that the decision was intended to give effect to the founder’s wishes and ensure compliance with the church’s governing provisions.

The group subsequently named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader pending consultations and the establishment of a substantive leadership structure.

However, the announcement immediately generated a counter-reaction from the church, which rejected the purported removal and described it as constitutionally invalid.

In a statement issued after the announcement, the church maintained that Jimmy Odukoya remained its duly appointed senior pastor and chairman of the Board of Trustees.

It argued that his appointment in September 2023 was unanimously approved by the recognised board and that no constitutionally valid decision had been taken to remove him.

The disagreement also extended to the control of the church’s communication channels, with the trustees alleging that individuals acting on Odukoya’s behalf had taken control of its official social media accounts without authorisation.

Court restrains Odukoya

The dispute took another turn on Wednesday, November 18, when the Lagos State High Court granted interim orders restraining Odukoya from holding himself out as the Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of the church.

Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin made the orders following an application by the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church.

The court also restrained Odukoya, whether acting personally or through proxies, from interfering with, disrupting or obstructing the church’s governance, administration and activities.

The orders were made ex parte, meaning they were granted before Odukoya had an opportunity to respond to the application.

However, the court preserved his right to challenge the orders or respond to the substantive claims.

The court did not order the closure of the church, suspend its worship services or appoint a replacement for Odukoya. The matter was adjourned until December 1 for mention.

Thanksgiving service postponed

Amid the unfolding dispute, the church announced the postponement of its much-anticipated 2026 Thanksgiving Service, which had been scheduled for Sunday, November 22.

In a notice published on its official social media platforms on Thursday, November 19, the church said a new date would be communicated in due course.

The postponement generated further uncertainty among members, particularly as reports circulated that police officers had sealed the church premises and directed workers to vacate the facility.

However, the church subsequently dismissed reports that its premises had been sealed.

In a message shared on its official social media account on Friday, it declared: “Don’t believe the noise; church is not sealed. See you in church on Sunday.”

It also announced that its regular Sunday service would hold at 9am, inviting members to attend physically or participate online.

Despite the clarification, a visit to the church premises on Sunday revealed a notable presence of security operatives, while access and activities at the facility appeared restricted.

Worshippers were nevertheless seen arriving and being ushered into the main auditorium for the regular service.

As of the time of filing this report, it was unclear who would lead the congregation or preside over the service.

Vanguard Newspaper

title: 2027: NEF raises alarm over political tension, warns against violence
description:
From Charity Nwakaudu, Abuja
The Northern Elders Forum (NEF) has warned politicians against inflammatory statements, threats and political intolerance ahead of the 2027 general elections, saying the trend could plunge the country into fresh violence and worsen insecurity.
The Forum urged political p
content:
From Charity Nwakaudu, Abuja

The Northern Elders Forum (NEF) has warned politicians against inflammatory statements, threats and political intolerance ahead of the 2027 general elections, saying the trend could plunge the country into fresh violence and worsen insecurity.

The Forum urged political parties, their candidates and supporters to embrace tolerance, restraint and peaceful conduct, warning that Nigeria’s fragile security situation could deteriorate if political hostilities were allowed to escalate.

In a statement by its spokesperson, Professor Abubakar Jika Jiddere, NEF expressed concern over growing hostility among political actors, describing the development as a threat to democratic stability.

The elders cautioned politicians against name-calling, intimidation, threats of retaliation, verbal and physical attacks, as well as hate speech capable of inflaming political tension.

“Political actors must immediately desist from name-calling, verbal and physical attacks, vilification, threats of retaliation, intimidation and other forms of political hostility,” the statement said.

The Forum also warned that the media must avoid amplifying provocative statements, hate speech and misinformation capable of deepening political divisions.

It called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), security agencies and other relevant institutions to discharge their constitutional responsibilities with fairness, transparency, independence and professionalism.

NEF expressed particular concern that rising political intolerance could further aggravate insecurity in Northern Nigeria, insisting that the region could not afford another round of violence.

“Let it be stated unequivocally that the North cannot afford any further escalation of insecurity or violence,” the Forum declared.

It also urged government authorities to exercise restraint and fairness in the discharge of their duties, warning against actions capable of triggering unnecessary confrontations or a breakdown of law and order.

On the role of security agencies, the elders stressed the need to respect citizens’ constitutional rights, particularly to peaceful assembly, while maintaining public order and protecting lives and property.

title: Kaduna Clerics, monarchs unite to keep girls in school, support young mothers
description:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo







Faith and traditional leaders in Kaduna State have pledged to collaborate with the Brain Builders Youth Development Initiative (BBYDI) to tackle barriers to girls’ education and facilitate the return of married girls, teenage mothers and those forced out of school by fi
content:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo

Faith and traditional leaders in Kaduna State have pledged to collaborate with the Brain Builders Youth Development Initiative (BBYDI) to tackle barriers to girls’ education and facilitate the return of married girls, teenage mothers and those forced out of school by financial difficulties.

The commitment was made at the inauguration of the Coalition of Faith and Traditional Leaders for Girls’ Education, organised by BBYDI under its Faith and Tradition for Girls’ Education Project, with support from the Malala Fund, at Asa Pyramid Hotel, Kaduna.

At the event, the organisation also unveiled an advocacy toolkit, including a local-language edition, a coalition charter and terms of reference to guide religious and traditional leaders in promoting girls’ education across communities.

The toolkit is designed to help religious and traditional leaders use sermons, congregational gatherings, traditional council meetings and community dialogues to sensitise parents and guardians on the importance of keeping their daughters in school.

The initiative is also expected to address challenges such as child marriage, poverty, insecurity and the stigma confronting girls who become pregnant or have children while still of school age.

Speaking at the inauguration, BBYDI Programme Director, Halimat Olufade, said consultations with faith and traditional leaders across the project’s 12 local government areas informed the formation of the coalition and the development of the advocacy materials.

She disclosed that the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) and Jama’atu Nasril Islam (JNI) had expressed willingness to deploy their churches, mosques and community platforms to encourage families to prioritise girls’ education.

According to her, particular attention would be given to married girls and young mothers who wish to return to school, stressing that marriage or motherhood should not permanently deprive girls of educational opportunities.

“No girl should have to abandon her education because she becomes a wife or a mother. No girl’s circumstances should permanently close the doors to learning,” Olufade said.

Governor Uba Sani, who commended BBYDI for the initiative, pledged the state government’s support and partnership.

The governor, represented by Mallam Abass Shehu, said the administration had provided conditional cash transfers to 46,572 girls to improve school attendance, retention and completion.

He added that the government had also constructed and renovated schools through the Adolescent Girls Initiative for Learning and Empowerment (AGILE) and the Reaching Out-of-School Children project.

Similarly, the Commissioner for Education, Abubakar Sani Sambo, commended the organisation and expressed the ministry’s readiness to work with the coalition.

Sambo urged members to use their influence to encourage parents to enrol their daughters in school, support their continued education and challenge cultural practices that undermine girls’ access to learning.

He also stressed the need to address the educational challenges facing girls with disabilities and those whose social circumstances make school attendance difficult.

The Emir of Zazzau, Ahmad Nuhu Bamalli, represented by the Makaman Malaman Zazzau, Sani Yusuf Magaji, also expressed support for the initiative, saying the emirate was willing to collaborate with BBYDI and other organisations on practical measures to expand girls’ access to education.

Magaji recalled historical efforts by the Zazzau Emirate to promote girls’ education, noting that a former emir, Jafaru Dan Isyaku, dedicated Babban Dodo Primary School as a girls’ boarding school and enrolled his daughter, Hajiya Talle.

He said district heads, ward heads and officials of the then Zaria Native Authority were also encouraged to enrol their daughters in primary schools.

In her remarks, the Director of the Gender Policy Unit at Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, Rahanatu Lawal, urged the coalition to involve girls and young women in designing programmes and policies affecting their education.

She said girls should be given opportunities to articulate the challenges they face, particularly regarding school safety,

retention and the support required to return to classrooms after dropping out.

Olufade said the coalition’s success would ultimately be determined by measurable improvements in girls’ education, including increased school retention and the number of girls who return to school and complete their education.

The post Kaduna Clerics, monarchs unite to keep girls in school, support young mothers appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: PSG star Doue in tears after suffering worrying knee injury against Nice
description:
Paris Saint-Germain star Desire Doue was stretchered off in tears after suffering what looked like a nasty knee injury as the reigning French and European champions beat Nice 3-2 in Ligue 1 on Saturday.



Doue went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half as he tried to control the ball
content:
Paris Saint-Germain star Desire Doue was stretchered off in tears after suffering what looked like a nasty knee injury as the reigning French and European champions beat Nice 3-2 in Ligue 1 on Saturday.

Doue went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half as he tried to control the ball, shortly after scoring to put PSG 2-1 ahead.

He looked in agony as he clutched his right knee, and the match was stopped for five minutes to allow Doue to receive treatment before being carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium.

PSG will now be dreading discovering the extent of the injury, having lost Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee playing against Barcelona last month.

The Georgian winger is unlikely to return this season, and Doue looks set for a significant spell on the sidelines too.

“We will need to wait until tomorrow for the test results, but it is obviously a serious injury,” PSG coach Luis Enrique told broadcaster Ligue 1+.

The 21-year-old French international, who can play on the wing or in midfield, has been arguably PSG’s best player this season after playing a key role in their Champions League triumphs in each of the last two campaigns.

He has notably scored three goals in three Champions League appearances this season for PSG, who sold Bradley Barcola to Liverpool at the beginning of the campaign and have seen Ousmane Dembele struggle with his fitness recently.

– ‘Not a problem’ –

“This is the life of a professional player at the very highest level,” added Luis Enrique. “You just have to accept it and I am sure he will find a way to recover well and come back even stronger.”

Asked about the possibility of moving to sign a replacement in the January transfer window, the Spanish coach said PSG were “always open to possibilities”.

“We have players who can come in and we will overcome this as a team. It is not a problem,” he added.

Earlier, Algerian international Mohamed Amoura had given Nice the lead only for Senny Mayulu to equalise with a penalty awarded after a VAR check following a handball in the home box.

Doue — who was wearing a mouthguard after one of his teeth became dislodged while playing for France against Italy during the international break — put PSG ahead a minute after that goal, turning in at the back post from an Achraf Hakimi assist for his sixth of the season in all competitions.

His replacement Ferran Torres scored PSG’s third in the 85th minute, controlling in the box before finishing on the turn for his eighth goal of the season — but first in two months.

Ali Abdi pulled one back for Nice in stoppage time, but their run of three straight wins was ended as PSG made it 12 victories on the bounce.

Eight of those wins have come in Ligue 1, in which PSG are now five points clear at the top from Lille, who lost 1-0 at home to Lyon with Mads Bidstrup scoring the only goal.

Paris FC now have the chance to climb into second place and close the gap to PSG to three points by beating Angers on Sunday.

Lyon are up to fourth, while Brest moved into the top six after winning 1-0 at Strasbourg, as the home side lost in their first game since appointing Portugal’s Vitor Matos of Swansea City as coach.

Monaco needed a late Edan Diop equaliser to draw 1-1 at home to Auxerre as their winless run in Ligue 1 stretched to six games.

Lens drew 1-1 with Toulouse in their first match under new coach Didier Digard.

The post PSG star Doue in tears after suffering worrying knee injury against Nice appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Messi should have been sent off for throwing ball at opponent – Columbus coach
description:
Columbus Crew coach, Laurent Courtois, has said Lionel Messi deserved a red card for throwing the ball at an opponent during Inter Miami’s 3-0 defeat in the Major League Soccer Cup playoffs on Saturday.
Messi lost his temper just before half-time when he hurled the ball into the face of Columbus for
content:
Columbus Crew coach, Laurent Courtois, has said Lionel Messi deserved a red card for throwing the ball at an opponent during Inter Miami’s 3-0 defeat in the Major League Soccer Cup playoffs on Saturday.

Messi lost his temper just before half-time when he hurled the ball into the face of Columbus forward Gonzalo Tapia during a throw-in, with Miami trailing 1-0.

The Argentine and Tapia were both shown yellow cards by referee Allen Chapman, but Courtois insisted after the match that Messi should have been sent off.

“Everybody knows that he deserved more than a yellow card,” Courtois said at a post-match press conference. “It’s just really sad.”

However, Chapman defended his decision to caution Messi, telling a pool reporter that the force used was negligible and did not amount to violent conduct.

“The force used was negligible and the offense did not reach the level of violent conduct,” he said.

Inter Miami were already down to 10 men when the incident occurred, having conceded an early penalty converted by Chilean forward Tapia.

The reigning MLS champions went on to suffer a 3-0 defeat at Nu Stadium, with Tapia scoring his second goal after Taha Habroune had doubled Columbus’ lead shortly after the break.

The result puts seventh-seeded Columbus, the 2023 champions, in a strong position to eliminate Messi and Inter Miami from the playoffs. They will advance with a victory in the second match of the best-of-three series in Ohio next Friday.

Miami coach Kily Gonzalez admitted that his side had failed to deliver the performance they expected.

“It was a game where nothing went right for us, and we effectively created their chances for them,” Gonzalez said.

“We didn’t produce the great performance we had hoped for. Everything went wrong, but we have to learn from it because next time, if we don’t win, we’re out,” he added.

“There’s no better challenge for us as a team than this. It’s a test of character, and I know my team has that character.”

In other MLS playoff matches on Saturday, Joaquin Valiente scored twice as Dallas defeated Portland 3-0 in their Western Conference series opener.

The 25-year-old Uruguayan midfielder scored in the 53rd and 55th minutes, while Samuel Sarver added a third goal in the fourth minute of stoppage time.

Dallas can secure qualification with a victory away to Portland next Saturday.

In the Eastern Conference, 19-year-old Peyton Miller scored once and provided an assist as New England defeated Philadelphia 2-0.

Miller’s 10th-minute effort deflected off Philadelphia defender Nathan Harriel before he sealed the victory in the 73rd minute from a Jack Harrison cross.

New England will advance to the Eastern Conference semi-finals with a win in the return fixture next Saturday.

The post Messi should have been sent off for throwing ball at opponent – Columbus coach appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: COP31 faces collapse threat as latest draft fails to mention fossil fuels
description:
The COP31 presidency proposed an eleventh-hour deal Sunday that again fails to mention fossil fuels — an omission that deepened a tense standoff at the UN climate talks.



The latest offering by summit co-hosts Turkey and Australia published deep into overtime leaves unresolved tensions over planet
content:
The COP31 presidency proposed an eleventh-hour deal Sunday that again fails to mention fossil fuels — an omission that deepened a tense standoff at the UN climate talks.

The latest offering by summit co-hosts Turkey and Australia published deep into overtime leaves unresolved tensions over planet-heating fossil fuels but retains a much-sought goal to electrify the global economy.

The proposal needs consensus approval from nearly 200 nations at a closing session Sunday but they have struggled to bridge differences during two weeks of grinding negotiations.

The European Union and other nations have pushed for strong language on transitioning away from fossil fuels, a call that has faced resistance from oil-rich Saudi Arabia.

An EU official told AFP the latest proposal was a “backwards” step, warning there was a “very real possibility” that COP31 ends with no deal.

“I am more pessimistic today than I was yesterday,” the official said on condition of anonymity.

“The situation is difficult, and the outcome is uncertain. The oil-producing countries are putting up a fierce fight,” a German official said.

A Saudi official declined to comment when approached by AFP.

Fossil fuels are a flashpoint at the climate talks and the summit comes against a difficult backdrop of soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran.

A draft deal unveiled earlier this week called for a faster phase out of fossil fuels but a second, pared-down version released Thursday stripped away all mentions of coal, oil and gas.

Threats of a walkout prompted Turkey and Australia to convene a hurried meeting between the European Union and Saudi Arabia in a bid to broker a compromise.

The latest text introduces a reference to a previous global deal in 2023 to shift the world away from fossil fuels — but stops short of naming them explicitly.

And it retains a contentious push to expand carbon capture and storage, a technology championed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised as costly and ineffective in cutting emissions.

“We are very disappointed with how the text looks,” the environment minister of Antigua and Barbuda, Michael Joseph, told AFP after leaving the COP31 presidency’s offices.

“I can’t honestly say that I’m okay with it passing” in its current state, Joseph said, adding that the draft was “quite silent” on fossil fuels.

– Goal to electrify –

The draft also calls for global efforts to boost the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035 and the expansion of “clean energy”.

The summit had been under pressure to show progress in tackling soaring greenhouse gas emissions in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal and Indonesia.

Facing blowback over fossil fuels, Turkey and Australia pointed to “electrification” as a way to cut heat-trapping emissions and bolster energy security.

This works by replacing technologies that burn fossil fuels directly — like diesel cars and gas heating — with electric alternatives.

But some nations had demanded an explicitly “clean” target to ensure the electrification push was powered by renewable energy and not fossil fuels.

Around one-third of global electricity is produced using coal and another fifth using fossil gas.

Attempts by Saudi Arabia, India and Kenya meanwhile to delay the next set of reports by the UN’s Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) have been another major source of friction at the talks.

The draft text “highlights the importance” of these reports for an upcoming stocktake of global carbon-cutting efforts in 2028.

Dozens of countries across Europe, Africa and the Pacific want these assessments by the global scientific authority on climate change published in time for that crucial stocktake.

Countries have also disagreed at COP31 over how to respond to the looming breach of the 1.5C warming target set under the Paris climate accord.

The latest draft expressed “deep concern” that global warming would cross 1.5C above pre-industrial levels in the next few years.

The talks also jammed over long-running complaints that rich nations are shirking their obligations to help developing nations confront climate change.

The removal of a $120 billion target for climate adaptation angered developing nations.

About 20 officers of the Medium Security Custodial Centre, Oke-Kura, in Ilorin, Kwara State, are being investigated over last Wednesday’s jailbreak by two condemned inmates.



Vanguard reliably gathered that among those now facing scrutiny are members of the armed s
content:
By Demola Akinyemi Ilorin

About 20 officers of the Medium Security Custodial Centre, Oke-Kura, in Ilorin, Kwara State, are being investigated over last Wednesday’s jailbreak by two condemned inmates.

Vanguard reliably gathered that among those now facing scrutiny are members of the armed squad and duty officers on round-the-clock supervision of inmates at the facility.

According to dependable sources (names withheld), probes indicate that last Wednesday’s jailbreak was a larger, coordinated effort involving seven inmates.

According to insider accounts, the inmates spent months secretly chiseling through the wall of their cell without prison management detecting it, pasting a poster over the opening to conceal the gradual breach.

On the morning of the escape, the convicts were said to have tied blankets to make a makeshift rope, throwing it to hook the broken bottles on the high perimeter fence.

“While the first two convicts successfully scaled the wall and fled, the rope snapped under the weight of the remaining five inmates, sending them falling back,” the source hinted.

Contacted,the Spokesperson of the state command, Adegbulugbe Phillips Olumide, however, could not confirm the development.

“I cannot confirm the report; those who came to investigate the incident returned to Abuja yesterday,so there’s no report on the outcome yet.”he said

Recall that the Controller General of Nigerian Correctional Service
Sylvester Nwakuche,who visited the scene on Thursday, attributed the escape of two condemned prison inmates to negligence, describing the incident as unfortunate and unacceptable.

Nwakuche also vowed that staff found guilty in the incident would be dealt with severely.

He, however, assured that a security dragnet has been spread across the state and the country and that the two escaped condemned criminals would be rearrested.

Meanwhile, the inmates identified as Shegun and Abraham, who reportedly escaped on Wednesday after breaking and scaling the wall of the custodial centre to ease their escape, have been declared wanted by the centre.

title: Messi deserved red card for throwing ball at opponent, says Columbus coach
description:
Columbus Crew coach Laurent Courtois said Lionel Messi should have been sent off after hurling a throw-in at an opponent as Inter Miami crashed to a 3-0 defeat in the MLS Cup playoffs on Saturday.



Messi’s frustration boiled over on the stroke of half-time when he aimed a forceful throw-in into th
content:
Columbus Crew coach Laurent Courtois said Lionel Messi should have been sent off after hurling a throw-in at an opponent as Inter Miami crashed to a 3-0 defeat in the MLS Cup playoffs on Saturday.

Messi’s frustration boiled over on the stroke of half-time when he aimed a forceful throw-in into the face of Columbus Crew forward Gonzalo Tapia with 10-man Miami trailing 1-0 at the time.

Messi and Tapia both were shown yellow cards for the incident by referee Allen Chapman, but Courtois said afterwards the Argentina superstar should have been given a red card.

“Everybody knows that he deserved more than a yellow card,” Courtois said in a post-game press conference when asked about the incident. “It’s just really sad.”

Referee Chapman later defended the decision to only show Messi a yellow.

“The force used was negligible and the offense did not reach the level of violent conduct,” Chapman told a pool reporter.

Inter Miami had already been reduced to 10 men when the incident occurred and were 1-0 down after Chile international Tapia’s early penalty.

Reigning MLS champions Miami went on to suffer a 3-0 defeat, with Tapia grabbing a second after a Taha Habroune strike just after half-time at Miami’s Nu Stadium.

The result means seventh seeds Columbus, the 2023 champions, can eliminate Messi and Miami from the playoffs with a victory in game two of the best-of-three series in Ohio next Friday.

“It was a game where nothing went right for us, and we effectively created their chances for them,” Miami coach Kily Gonzalez said afterwards.

“We didn’t produce the great performance we had hoped for. Everything went wrong, but we have to learn from it because next time, if we don’t win, we’re out,” he added.

“There’s no better challenge for us as a team than this. It’s a test of character, and I know my team has that character.”

In other MLS playoff action on Saturday, Joaquin Valiente scored two goals as host Dallas beat Portland 3-0 in their Western Conference series opener.

The 25-year-old Uruguayan midfielder scored in the 53rd and 55th minutes and Samuel Sarver added an insurance goal in the fourth minute of stoppage time for Dallas, who can advance by winning at Portland next Saturday.

US teen Peyton Miller scored one goal and set up another in New England’s 2-0 victory over visiting Philadelphia.

Miller’s 10th-minute shot deflected in off Philadelphia defender Nathan Harriel to make it 1-0 and the 19-year-old scored in the 73rd minute off a Jack Harrison cross to complete the scoring.

New England can advance to the MLS Eastern Conference semi-finals with a road victory next Saturday.

Vanguard News

title: Tinubu says economic sacrifices will yield prosperity
description:
President Bola Tinubu on Saturday in Ibadan said Nigerians’ sacrifices during a period of difficult economic reforms would soon give way to greater prosperity.



The President spoke at Samuel Ladoke Akintola Airport, where traditional rulers and political leaders from the South-West received him ah
content:
President Bola Tinubu on Saturday in Ibadan said Nigerians’ sacrifices during a period of difficult economic reforms would soon give way to greater prosperity.

The President spoke at Samuel Ladoke Akintola Airport, where traditional rulers and political leaders from the South-West received him ahead of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally at Mapo Hall.

This is contained in a statement by the Presidential Spokesperson, Mr Bayo Onanuga, on Saturday.

Addressing the traditional rulers, led by the Olubadan of Ibadan, Oba Rasheed Ladoja, Tinubu thanked them for their support and prayers for the nation.

“Stay the course for the sake of progress and prosperity of our country, for you, for your children and great-great-grandchildren. Our children will benefit from what we are doing,” he said.

Tinubu said an indicator of greater economic prospects for Oyo State was the recent agreement with Chinese bus manufacturer Yutong to reopen the old Leyland Automobile Bus Assembly plant.

He said the planned vehicle assembly would stimulate economic activity in the state.

The Olubadan commended the President for his administration’s willingness to address difficult issues, including establishing the state police.

He said Tinubu’s performance, particularly in infrastructure development, had become a major selling point for candidates seeking election on the APC platform.

The traditional ruler cited the Ibadan-Ife, Ibadan-Abeokuta and other road projects, saying the interventions had reduced travel time and improved connectivity across the state.

He expressed optimism that Tinubu would consolidate his achievements if given another term.

The Olubadan also said the traditional institution was interested in securing a constitutional role, urging the President to give the matter serious consideration.

At the rally, Tinubu called for a moment of silence in honour of those who died in the boat accident in Bayelsa.

He said Vice-President Kashim Shettima would visit the state to commiserate with the victims’ families and the affected community.

Tinubu thanked Oyo residents for their support in the 2023 elections, urging them to continue voting for the APC at all levels.

He acknowledged the contributions of prominent APC leaders and stakeholders in the South-West, including former Osun Governor, Chief Bisi Akande, Chief Segun Osoba and other party elders.

The President urged voters not to be distracted by opposition parties, accusing them of seeking to take away what Nigerians had worked hard to acquire.

“There is a party out there parading themselves. Please don’t mind them and don’t listen to them. They are only interested in clearing what you have. Vote for APC from top to bottom,” he said.

Tinubu also inspected 800 vehicles procured by the South-West Development Commission to strengthen the region’s security architecture.

In his remarks, Gov. Biodun Oyebanji of Ekiti, speaking on behalf of APC governors, urged South-West residents to unite behind Tinubu and other party candidates.

Oyebanji said the region had an important role in determining the presidential election outcome and urged voters to support Tinubu, Oyo APC governorship candidate Sen. Sarafadeen Ali and other party candidates.

Sen. Adams Oshiomhole recalled frequent strikes that disrupted academic sessions before Tinubu’s administration.

“For a long time now, a lecturer will teach you for two days, strike for three days. Is that not the truth? For four years, your academic calendar has not been interrupted,” he said.

Oshiomhole said Tinubu had deliberately prioritised university lecturers, adding that their salaries had been substantially increased.

He questioned how Gov. Seyi Makinde of Oyo State, the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), would alter the administration’s education policies under his proposed plan to reset Nigeria.

The event was attended by Vice-President Kashim Shettima; First Lady, Sen. Oluremi Tinubu; Senate President Godswill Akpabio; Deputy Senate President Barau Jibrin; Senate Majority Leader Opeyemi Bamidele; and governors of Ogun, Osun, Kwara, Imo, Ekiti and Ondo.

Also present were Minister of Power, Mr. Joseph Tegbe; Chairman of the Nigerian Revenue Service (NRS), Dr Zacch Adedeji; Oyo APC Chairman, Chief Moses Alake; among other dignitaries.

title: FG may raise N20,000 NELFUND student allowance — Official
description:
The Nigerian Education Loan Fund has indicated that students could receive an increase in their monthly upkeep allowance as the Federal Government considers ways to provide more financial support amid rising living costs.
The fund’s Managing Director, Akin Sawyer, disclosed this during an interview
content:
The Nigerian Education Loan Fund has indicated that students could receive an increase in their monthly upkeep allowance as the Federal Government considers ways to provide more financial support amid rising living costs.

The fund’s Managing Director, Akin Sawyer, disclosed this during an interview on Beyond the Headlines, hosted by Nifemi Oguntoye on TVC News on Friday.

NELFUND currently pays eligible students ₦20,000 monthly as upkeep allowance under the Federal Government’s student loan scheme. However, the amount has come under scrutiny as students contend with increasing costs of food, transportation, accommodation and other basic necessities.

Speaking on the possibility of reviewing the payment, Sawyer said the allowance remained under consideration, indicating that the fund was open to an adjustment.

“Are we considering it? Yes, of course. It’s under constant review,” he said.

He explained that although NELFUND recognised the need to provide students with more financial support, any decision to increase the allowance would have to take into account the fund’s capacity to sustain payments to all beneficiaries.

According to him, the fund must ensure that a possible increase does not undermine its ability to meet its obligations to the growing number of students benefiting from the scheme.

“What we need to do is plan it in such a way that it doesn’t put us in a situation where we can’t cater for the totality of the people that we need to cater for,” Sawyer said.

The NELFUND chief also disclosed that President Bola Tinubu was considering an intervention aimed at improving the financial support available to students, although he did not provide details of what the proposed intervention would entail.

He said the President was interested in ensuring that students had more meaningful financial support to help them complete their academic programmes.

“I know the President certainly is looking at intervening in a way that helps the students have more meaningful sustenance so that they can get through their courses,” he said.

While Sawyer did not announce a new allowance amount or give a specific date for its implementation, he suggested that changes could be expected in the future.

“I suspect that if you watch this space, you’ll see some changes coming up in the future,” he added.

The possible review comes as students continue to face pressure from the rising cost of living, with concerns over whether the existing ₦20,000 monthly payment can adequately cover their basic needs.

The upkeep allowance is one of the components of the Federal Government’s student loan scheme, which provides financial assistance to eligible students in public tertiary institutions for tuition and living expenses.

NELFUND’s figures show that it has disbursed ₦180.5bn to students as upkeep allowances since the scheme commenced in May 2024.

The fund also reported paying ₦194.7bn to tertiary institutions to cover tuition fees, bringing its total disbursements to approximately ₦375.2bn.

It has received more than 2.5 million applications and recorded about 1.6 million loan transactions across 320 beneficiary institutions.

The figures reflect the growing reach of the scheme, as NELFUND continues to provide financial assistance to students across public tertiary institutions.

However, despite the indication that an increase is being considered, Sawyer did not confirm the amount students could receive under a revised arrangement or when any adjustment would take effect.

The post FG may raise N20,000 NELFUND student allowance — Official appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Please, let Eze breathe
