content:
On his first day on the job, the trainee dialed the kitchen and shouted into the phone:

“Get me a cup of coffee, quickly!”

The voice from the other side responded:
“You fool, you’ve dialed the wrong extension! Do you know who you’re talking to?”

“No,” replied the trainee.

“It’s the Managing Director of the company, idiot!”

The trainee shouted back: “And do you know who You are talking to, you idiot?”

“No!” replied the Managing Director, indignantly.

“Thank God for that!” replied the trainee and slammed down the phone.

Wise men say silence is golden.

The one or two editors campaigning for the resignation of Eze Anaba as president of the Nigerian Guild of Editors, NGE on account of the fact that he is appointed into the governing council of the National Human Rights Commission, NHRC are not idiotic in the sense of trainee.

They are however, if the truth is to be said, an obstructive force engaging in digital harassment and reputation vandalism by spreading misinformation about the role and duties of the president of the NGE.

It is not in doubt that section 10 of the NGE amended constitution states that when a member of the Standing Committee (this is the elected executive committee) takes an appointment into an office that functions outside the mass media ecosystem, that member must his resign his or her position.

“In the event that a member of the Standing Committee accepts a political appointment and or a non-editorial position, the affected officer ceases to be a member of the Standing Committee.”

Constitutions are read, interpreted and applied in their letter and spirit.

There is, in my view, a clear distinction between taking a political appointment with office, pay and other perquisites and one in which one is appointed in representative capacity, on part-time basis and without a monthly salary.

One of those campaigners has cited the resignation of Chief Femi Adesina, OON as president, when he took an appointment as the Special Advisor, Media and Publicity to the President.

As special advisor media, Femi took office on a full time job, paid for by his new employer, which is the presidency.
In doing that job, he could not have combined it with his earlier post as the substantive managing director/editor-in-chief of the Sun newspaper in which he worked, otherwise a conflict of interest would have arisen.

But Femi’s resignation was itself not without a precedent.

When I served as the president, I did so for only a term and promptly called for elections to choose a new Standing Committee to replace me when I got appointed to a management position in the Aluminum Smelter Company of Nigeria, ALSCON, Ikot-Abasi, a PR job that was distinct from the journalistic standards that qualified me for the post of the NGE president.

In the present case of Eze Anaba, the current president of the Guild, he is the current daily editor of the Vanguard newspaper. He signs the paper five days a week. This is the organization that pays his wages.

His appointment as a member of the NHRC is not the first one in the council’s 30-year history.

When the first council was inaugurated in 1996, I, as the president of the NGE was sworn in as one of two members representing the media – the other member being Ray Ekpu, a high-standing journalist who at that time was the General Secretary of the Newspaper Proprietors Association of Nigeria, NPAN.

The NHRC then, and up until now, had been led by, and its membership populated by credible Nigerians representing various professions and law enforcement agencies, acting as an independent body, promoting, protecting and enforcing human rights as guaranteed under the Nigerian Constitution, the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights, the UN Charter, and other international treaties ratified by Nigeria.

As council members, no one was/is on a monthly salary but were/are paid sitting allowances which, by the standards of public service in the country, could barely pay for a decent hotel room and meals for the two-three days of meeting every three months.

Eze, like others who served in that position, is a representative of the media community. “Representative” as defined by the standard English dictionary “is a person chosen or appointed to act or speak for another person or group.”

In effect, no member-Eze inclusive – is there for himself but are all there in representative capacity.

It is inconceivable that a quasi-judicial institution which the NHRC is, could sit in judgment over human rights abuses- to which journalists are the primary and most frequent victims- without the media as represented by the NGE having a seat on the table.

As a matter of fact, it in the absence of credible institutions and leaders such as Eze on the table that the body’s reputation may become controversial, politicized and vulnerable to outside pressure.

When you remove the leaders of the media, you are, in all probability, going to have them replaced by men or women with poor human rights records who are more likely to work against the interests of journalists and other victims of human rights abuses.

In opening this discussion with the encounter of the trainee with his managing director, I have no intention of calling anyone an idiot.

There is a saying that when the right person speaks at the right time, even the biggest lie falls apart.

The NGE is faced with several challenges even as we are under an elected, democratic government, not least among which is the threat to the freedom of speech and of expression, the fulcrum on which rests the entire media ecosystem.

To focus on the prevailing challenges and the ones that lie ahead, the NGE can do without a distraction from an axis of malice, engaging in opportunistic obstructionism.

Let Eze Anaba, president of the NGE breathe.

Signed:

Garba Shehu, a former president of the NGE is currently a Director of the Peoples Daily and the Nigerian Local Government News

The post Please, let Eze breathe appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Church crisis: Jimmy Odukoya’s old birthday tribute to sister resurfaces
description:
Nigerians on social media have revisited a birthday tribute shared by Senior Pastor of the Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, to his sister, Pastor Caroline Odukoya, also addressed as Tolu Odukoya, amid their reported disagreement over the church’s leadership and succession.
Jimmy had celebrate
content:
Nigerians on social media have revisited a birthday tribute shared by Senior Pastor of the Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, to his sister, Pastor Caroline Odukoya, also addressed as Tolu Odukoya, amid their reported disagreement over the church’s leadership and succession.

Jimmy had celebrated Caroline on September 20, 2025, when she turned 40, describing her as the firstborn of the family and expressing affection for her.

In the birthday post shared on his X account, he wrote, “Caroline Toluwani Odukoya! First of her name! First born of the Clan! You are now officially Old SS!! Now you are 40, you won’t let us rest oh. Pictures don’t cut it, so here’s us being us. Love you, sis. 4O looks good on you!!!”

The post has resurfaced following the public disagreement involving the siblings and other members of the church’s Board of Trustees.

.

Several Nigerians reacting to the old post expressed hope that the family would resolve their differences and restore peace.

A user, Lamegh Nguher Jennifer (@IameghJ), wrote, “And now they’re in court fighting each other, God Abeg o.”

Another user, Ladi Ogunseye (@LadiSpeaks), urged the pastor to settle the disagreement, writing, “Don’t let the devil come between you both. Man up and settle the dispute/difference even if you have to compromise and beg her.”

Oluwatomilola (@IamTomieBlaq), in a reaction, prayed, “May God bring back the family.”

Another user, Naomi O (@TserunD), wrote, “Omo make devil leave this family alone abeg.”

Oyeyemi Ariyo-Osho (@oyeyemiariyo) also appealed for peace, writing, “Devil, leave this family alone!!!! Devil, leave this family alone!!!! Devil, leave this family alone!!!! @Toluwaniodukoya x @iamthatpj ni oruko Jesu, oju ma ti esu lori idile yin.”

A user identified as A Cactus is A Plant That Stands on (@…), criticised the church elders, writing, “Shame on all the church elders!”

Another user, Seyi (@ThonyBlack01), reacted, “See Wetin Una ruin fgs.”

Daniella (@UlokoDaniel…) expressed sadness over the resurfaced post, writing, “Gosh who brought this video back. I’m going to cry.”

Godfather Lagata (@HansLandaQ), whose account is labelled as a parody account, also reacted, questioning why people were surprised by the disagreement.

Sonia (@soniaezee) suggested that Caroline should have become the church’s head pastor, alleging that she was overlooked because she is a woman.

PUNCH Online had reported that Jimmy approached the Federal High Court in Lagos to challenge his purported removal as the church’s Senior Pastor and Chairman of its Board of Trustees.

He instituted the suit alongside the Incorporated Trustees of the Fountain of Life Church against eight defendants, including his sister, Pastor Tolu Odukoya, and other church leaders.

In the court processes, dated November 20, 2026, Jimmy challenged the validity of meetings held by some members of the Board of Trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, as well as decisions taken at the meetings.

He maintained that the meetings and resolutions, including the decision to remove him from office, violated the church’s constitution.

The pastor said he was appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees at an emergency meeting on September 14, 2023, and was subsequently installed that month.

The dispute became public on November 17, when some members of the church’s Board of Trustees announced his removal, citing disagreements over the church’s succession arrangement and other issues.

Jimmy and the church, however, rejected the removal, insisting that his appointment was valid and that the decision violated the church’s constitution.

The trustees later named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader.

The Lagos State High Court subsequently issued an interim order restraining Jimmy from presenting himself as the church’s Senior Pastor, a decision he is challenging at the Federal High Court.

The court had yet to determine the issues raised in the suit as of the time of filing this report.

The post Church crisis: Jimmy Odukoya’s old birthday tribute to sister resurfaces appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Abia-North 2027: Kalu bags multiple endorsements in Arochukwu, secures Philip Nto’s backing, 18-seater bus
description:
Kenneth Udeh from Umuahia


Former APC Senatorial aspirant says Kalu has no competitor, pledges political structures for his re-election
Senator receives 18-seater bus, bags fourth Senate Press Corps Award


With the 2027 general elections fast approaching, incumbent Abia North Senator, Orji Uzor Ka
content:
Kenneth Udeh from Umuahia

  • Former APC Senatorial aspirant says Kalu has no competitor, pledges political structures for his re-election
  • Senator receives 18-seater bus, bags fourth Senate Press Corps Award

With the 2027 general elections fast approaching, incumbent Abia North Senator, Orji Uzor Kalu, has received multiple endorsements from political leaders, traditional rulers and community stakeholders during his ongoing ward-to-ward tour of Arochukwu Local Government Area of Abia State.

Among those backing his re-election is former APC senatorial aspirant, Prof. Philip Nto, who has declared support for Kalu’s return to the Senate.

Nto, a former Abia State Commissioner for Finance and Economic Planning, declared that Kalu had no serious competitor in the forthcoming senatorial election, pledging to deploy his political structures, supporters and resources towards securing the senator’s re-election.

He also dismissed suggestions of disunity within the Abia APC, declaring that the party remained united ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Nto made the declaration on Saturday when he hosted Kalu and members of his entourage at his residence in Ututu, Arochukwu LGA, following the senator’s ward-to-ward engagements across the community.

The former commissioner, who accompanied Kalu throughout the tour, said his decision to support the senator was informed by his performance, political pedigree, grassroots connections and commitment to the collective interests of Abia North.

He expressed confidence in Kalu’s political experience and popularity, insisting that the former governor remained the candidate to beat in the forthcoming election.

Kalu, who represents Abia North Senatorial District and currently chairs the Senate Committee on the South East Development Commission (SEDC), commenced his Arochukwu tour with a courtesy visit to the palace of the Eze Aro, where he met members of the traditional ruler’s cabinet to formally announce his ward-to-ward engagements.

Accompanied by prominent philanthropist, Engr. Dr. Emeka Maduagwu, and the APC candidate for Arochukwu State Constituency, Prince Ike Okoroafor, among other party leaders, the senator said the exercise was designed to strengthen his relationship with constituents and identify areas requiring further development.

He highlighted his interventions across Arochukwu, including road construction and rehabilitation, the construction of over 20 schools, installation of streetlights, distribution of educational materials and overseas scholarship opportunities for indigenes.

Traditional ruler recalls Kalu’s relationship with Ututu

At the palace of His Royal Majesty, Eze Solomon Nwaizu Okereke, JP, Ezeoma I of Ezema Ututu, the traditional ruler recalled Kalu’s longstanding relationship with the community, particularly his appointment of several Ututu indigenes to positions of responsibility during his administration as governor of Abia State between 1999 and 2007.

The monarch described Kalu as a familiar figure whose relationship with the people extended beyond his years in the Senate.

He commended the senator for maintaining his connection with the community and expressed support for his continued representation, while appealing for additional developmental projects to improve the living conditions of residents.

Similarly, Princess Evelyn Nwankwo applauded Kalu’s representation, describing him as a longstanding friend of the Ututu people.

She expressed appreciation for his interventions over the years and pledged the community’s continued goodwill and support.

APC candidates endorse Kalu’s developmental record

The APC candidate for Arochukwu State Constituency, Prince Ike Okoroafor, commended Kalu for attracting developmental projects to the area, particularly in road infrastructure, educational facilities and other constituency interventions.

Describing the senator as one of their own, Okoroafor said his longstanding relationship with the Aro and Ututu people had further strengthened his connection with the communities.

Also speaking, the APC candidate for Arochukwu/Ohafia Federal Constituency, Chief Ikenna Nicholas Ukwa, pledged to collaborate with Kalu, if elected, to attract additional federal projects and development opportunities to the constituency.

Ukwa maintained that cooperation among elected representatives at the National Assembly would accelerate development and address infrastructure challenges confronting rural communities.

A community leader, Ohachi Victor, also declared support for Kalu’s re-election, insisting that Ututu stood firmly behind the senator.

Kalu receives 18-seater bus

Beyond the political endorsements, Kalu received an 18-seater bus donated by supporters at Obinkita, Arochukwu Ward 2, during the tour.

The presentation was coordinated by Engr. Emeka Maduagwu, who joined representatives of his foundation and other support groups in handing over the vehicle to the senator.

Expressing appreciation for the gesture, Kalu said: “I am deeply touched by this collective gesture of goodwill, solidarity and confidence in my representation. Your kindness and continued support mean a great deal to me, and I do not take them for granted.

“May God bless you all abundantly.”

At the various communities visited, including Amannagwu, Ugbo, Asaga, Obinkita and the five Ututu wards, Kalu interacted with residents, community leaders, women and youths, listening to their concerns and discussing opportunities for further development.

At Asaga, the senator reflected on his developmental interventions across the area, particularly road projects, school construction, streetlight installations, overseas scholarships and the distribution of educational materials.

He acknowledged that more work remained to be done, stressing the need to sustain the relationship between elected representatives and their constituents.

Addressing the people during the engagements, Kalu reiterated his commitment to purposeful representation and sustainable community development.

He said: “I have come to listen to our people, understand their priorities and deepen our partnership for progress and development.”

The former governor also emphasised that his ward-to-ward engagements were not merely political visits but opportunities to assess the needs of communities and identify areas requiring further legislative and developmental attention.

He assured constituents that their concerns would continue to receive attention, maintaining that effective representation required regular consultation and sustained engagement.

Kalu bags fourth Senate Press Corps Award

The Arochukwu tour comes shortly after Kalu received the 2026 Best Impactful Representation Award from the Senate Press Corps (SPC), in recognition of his contributions to constituency development, legislative representation and human empowerment.

The latest recognition brings to four the number of Senate Press Corps awards received by the former Abia governor since his election into the Senate in 2019.

The award further highlights his legislative and constituency development engagements over the years.

Kalu’s Arochukwu tour forms part of his ongoing ward-to-ward consultations across Abia North Senatorial District ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The engagements have provided an opportunity for the senator to reconnect with constituents, receive feedback on his representation and secure renewed commitments from political stakeholders and community leaders.

The endorsement by Nto, a former senatorial aspirant who has pledged to mobilise his political structures for Kalu’s re-election, emerged as one of the major political highlights of the Arochukwu tour.

title: Youth minister weds in Ondo
description:
Nigeria’s Minister of Youth Development, Ayodele Olawande, has married his partner, Stella Elegbe, in Akure, the Ondo State capital.
The white wedding ceremony took place on Saturday at the Christ Apostolic Church, Revival Centre, Akure, and was followed by a reception at the Dr Olusegun Mimiko Even
content:
Nigeria’s Minister of Youth Development, Ayodele Olawande, has married his partner, Stella Elegbe, in Akure, the Ondo State capital.

The white wedding ceremony took place on Saturday at the Christ Apostolic Church, Revival Centre, Akure, and was followed by a reception at the Dr Olusegun Mimiko Events Centre, popularly known as The Dome.

The wedding was the culmination of a series of ceremonies held by the couple over three days.

They had their marriage registry on Thursday, November 19, followed by their traditional engagement on Friday, November 20, before the church wedding on Saturday.

Family members, friends, political associates and government officials attended the ceremonies to celebrate the couple as they began their life together.

Among those who attended was Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, who was at the wedding reception.

The Lagos State Commissioner for Youth and Social Development, Mobolaji Ogunlende, also attended and said he represented Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, at the ceremony.

In a congratulatory message shared after the event, Ogunlende expressed the Lagos State Government’s goodwill towards the newly married couple, describing the occasion as an important milestone in the minister’s life.

He wrote, “Today, I had the honour of representing the Governor of Lagos State, Mr. Babajide Olusola Sanwo-Olu, at the Holy Matrimony ceremony of the Honourable Minister of Youth Development, Comrade Ayodele Olawande, and his beautiful bride in Akure, Ondo State.

“On behalf of the Governor and the people of Lagos State, I extend my heartfelt congratulations to the Honourable Minister and his wife on this beautiful milestone.

“May this union be blessed with enduring love, peace, understanding, joy and abundant blessings. May their home be filled with happiness, and may their journey together be one of lifelong companionship, grace and fulfilment.”

Also present at the wedding was the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Heineken Lokpobiri, who joined family members and friends to witness the exchange of marital vows.

Lokpobiri, in a message shared on X, celebrated Olawande and his wife, describing the occasion as the beginning of a new chapter in their lives. He also offered prayers for the couple, wishing them a marriage filled with love, companionship and God’s blessings.

He wrote, “I was delighted to join family and friends in witnessing the exchange of marital vows between the Honourable Minister of Youth Development, Hon. Ayodele Olawande, and his adorable wife, Mrs Stella Ifeoluwa Elegbe, as they embarked on a beautiful new chapter of their lives together.

“There is something truly beautiful about two people discovering themselves in love, choosing each other, and committing to a lifetime of shared joy, blessings, companionship and forever.

“Today, my friend and brother, the Honourable Minister, is that happy man, blessed with a wonderful woman to call his wife.

“I pray that God’s grace will continually abound in their home, that His blessings will never cease, and that every beautiful promise and blessing that comes with the gift of marriage will be theirs in abundance and beyond.”

Olawande currently serves as Nigeria’s Minister of Youth Development under President Bola Tinubu’s administration.

He is from Ondo State and has been involved in youth mobilisation and political activities before his appointment to the Federal Executive Council.

The wedding took place in his home state, with the couple’s civil, traditional and church ceremonies held in Akure.

The post Youth minister weds in Ondo appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Troops raid bandits’ hideout in Kogi, recover AK-47 rifles
description:
By Kingsley Omonobi



Troops of the Nigerian Army have dislodged suspected armed bandits from a hideout in Kogi State, recovering two AK-47 rifles, three magazines and 65 rounds of ammunition during an intelligence-led operation.







The operation, conducted on Saturday, November 21, 2026, targe
content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

Troops of the Nigerian Army have dislodged suspected armed bandits from a hideout in Kogi State, recovering two AK-47 rifles, three magazines and 65 rounds of ammunition during an intelligence-led operation.

The operation, conducted on Saturday, November 21, 2026, targeted suspected kidnappers operating in the Osara, Gada and Ohakiti forest areas of Okehi Local Government Area, following intelligence reports on their activities and hideouts.

In a statement, the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, said the operation was launched by troops deployed from Patrol Base Kabba in collaboration with other security personnel.

She said the operation was aimed at dismantling criminal hideouts linked to the recent spate of kidnappings along the Kabba–Okene Road and neighbouring communities.

According to the statement, troops encountered about six armed bandits at an abandoned settlement within the forest during the offensive, engaging them and forcing them to flee.

A subsequent search of the hideout led to the recovery of two AK-47 rifles, three magazines and 65 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition.

Other items recovered from the enclave included bags, torchlights, food supplies and a power bank believed to have been used by the fleeing suspects.

The Army said the operation underscored its determination to deny criminal elements freedom of action, dismantle their operational bases and restore security along vulnerable routes and communities in Kogi State.

It reaffirmed its commitment to sustaining intelligence-driven operations in collaboration with other security agencies to eliminate threats to lives and property.

The Army also urged members of the public to continue providing timely and credible information to security agencies to support ongoing efforts to identify and clear hideouts used by criminal elements across the country.

Benue State Governor, Hyacinth Alia, has met with key stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress in Abuja as part of efforts to reconcile and strengthen unity within the party in the state.
Alia disclosed this in a statement on Saturday, saying the meeting was convened by the North-Central Presid
content:
Benue State Governor, Hyacinth Alia, has met with key stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress in Abuja as part of efforts to reconcile and strengthen unity within the party in the state.

Alia disclosed this in a statement on Saturday, saying the meeting was convened by the North-Central Presidential Reconciliation Committee, chaired by former Katsina State Governor, Senator Ibrahim Shema.

The meeting, which lasted about two hours, was attended by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation,

; former Benue State Governor, Senator Gabriel Suswam; Senators Barnabas Gemade and Jack Gyado; and Elder Shango, among other party stakeholders.

The governor thanked Shema and members of the committee for bringing the party leaders together, noting that reconciliation required willingness among members to listen, speak frankly and work together despite their differences.

“I thank Sen. Shema and his committee for bringing us together. Reconciliation takes a willingness to listen, to speak frankly and to keep working together even where differences remain,” he said.

Alia reaffirmed his commitment to engaging with APC leaders and stakeholders to promote unity within the party, while ensuring that peace, security and development remained central to his administration.

“My commitment is clear. I will continue to engage with our leaders and stakeholders in the interest of a united APC, while keeping the peace, security and development of Benue State at the centre of my work,” he added.

He said the responsibility entrusted to the government by the people of Benue should guide the actions of political leaders and stakeholders.

“The people of Benue entrusted us with the responsibility to serve, and that responsibility must continue to guide us,” the governor said.

The meeting comes amid a prolonged leadership crisis in the Benue APC, which has divided the party into factions loyal to Alia and Akume. The disagreement, which dates back to shortly after Alia assumed office in 2023, has centred on control of the party’s structures and the influence of key stakeholders in the state.

The crisis has led to the emergence of parallel party executives, disagreements over party congresses and repeated reconciliation efforts. In November, Alia blamed the divisions on his refusal to allow some party chieftains access to state funds for personal interests, while Akume’s loyalists have accused the governor of sidelining established party leaders.

Previous peace efforts have also encountered disagreements, including a May reconciliation meeting over automatic tickets for elected APC officials.

title: George Washington’s hair sells for $4,000 at auction
description:
A framed lock of hair belonging to former United States President George Washington has been sold for $4,000 (£3,058) at an auction in the US.
As reported by the BBC, the historic item was sold on Saturday by Richmond Auctions, although the identity of the successful bidder has not been disclosed.
A
content:
A framed lock of hair belonging to former United States President George Washington has been sold for $4,000 (£3,058) at an auction in the US.

As reported by the BBC, the historic item was sold on Saturday by Richmond Auctions, although the identity of the successful bidder has not been disclosed.

According to the auction house, the hair originally belonged to John Gadsby, who hosted Washington for dinner in 1799, shortly before the former president died later that year.

Gadsby reportedly obtained the hair because of his friendship with Washington and preserved it as a historical keepsake.

The item was later acquired by collector John K. Lattimer from one of Gadsby’s descendants before eventually appearing at auction.

A 1928 statement by Gadsby’s granddaughter, Julia Ten Eyck McBlair, provided details about how her grandfather came into possession of the hair.

She recalled that the framed lock was displayed beneath Washington’s portrait in her family’s home in Washington City, where she had seen it throughout her life.

Gadsby also hosted Washington’s birthday celebrations in 1798 and 1799, according to Richmond Auctions.

However, Saturday’s sale was not the highest amount ever paid for Washington’s hair. In 2021, three strands believed to have been removed from him around the time of his death sold for nearly $`40,000.

Several locks of Washington’s hair have survived over the years, with at least 50 examples preserved in a collection at Mount Vernon, his former residence, which is now a museum.

According to Mount Vernon’s website, displaying locks of hair belonging to friends and loved ones was particularly popular among wealthy families during the 19th century.

Washington led American forces to victory against Britain during the American War of Independence and played a significant role in the drafting of the United States Constitution.

He became the country’s first president in 1789 and served two terms before leaving office in 1797.

Other historical items associated with Washington have also attracted considerable interest at auctions.

In July, a letter signed by Washington in 1776, requesting soldiers for the Continental Army to fight British forces, was sold for `$109,800.

title: Customs seize ₦3.52bn contraband in Ogun

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta



The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Ogun I Area Command, has intercepted contraband goods with a total Duty Paid Value (DPV) of ₦3.52 billion in a series of operations aimed at curbing smuggling, protecting pub
content:
…Recover cannabis, codeine syrup, 1.45m tablets, others

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Ogun I Area Command, has intercepted contraband goods with a total Duty Paid Value (DPV) of ₦3.52 billion in a series of operations aimed at curbing smuggling, protecting public health and safeguarding the nation’s economy.

The seized items include 6,037 wraps of cannabis, 20,500 bottles of codeine-containing cough syrup, more than 1.45 million tablets and capsules of various brands, foreign parboiled rice, petroleum products and vehicles.

The items were inspected and paraded by the Comptroller-General of Customs during a visit to the Command.

According to a statement issued on Saturday by the Command’s Public Relations Officer, Assistant Superintendent of Customs, Paul Gimba, the total value of the seized goods with available valuations stood at ₦3,517,838,700.

The statement said the seizures reflected the Command’s sustained efforts to combat smuggling and prevent the circulation of prohibited and potentially harmful products in the country.

A breakdown of the seizures showed that cannabis accounted for 6,037 wraps, valued at ₦1.268 billion, while 20,500 bottles of codeine-containing cough syrup had a DPV of ₦147.6 million.

The Command also intercepted 828,920 tablets of various brands, valued at ₦795.76 million, and 627,320 capsules worth ₦376.39 million.

Other pharmaceutical products seized included 2,850 ampoules of Enox 4000 injection, valued at ₦17.1 million, and 95 prostate pills worth ₦570,000.

The seizures further included 5,173 bags of 50kg foreign parboiled rice, valued at ₦455.22 million, and 1,067 used tyres worth ₦52.82 million.

In the petroleum products category, Customs intercepted 1,037 kegs of 25 litres of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), valued at ₦34.22 million, and 1,008 kegs of 25 litres of Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), worth ₦44.35 million.

Other seized items comprised 21 packages of walkie-talkies, 185 packages of sanitary pads and diapers valued at ₦18.13 million, 125 live cartridges and two trucks with a combined valuation of ₦144 million.

The Command also recorded seizures of several used vehicles, including a 2024 Toyota RAV4 and a Toyota Highlander valued at a combined ₦50 million; two Lexus vehicles worth ₦25 million; a 2000 Toyota Hilux valued at ₦11 million; a 2013 Toyota RAV4 worth ₦17 million; and a Toyota Sienna valued at ₦14.7 million.

Other vehicles intercepted were a 2010 Toyota Venza valued at ₦14.6 million, an Opel worth ₦7.3 million, a Mazda valued at ₦7.1 million and a 2012 Range Rover Sport worth ₦17.2 million.

The Customs Service said the interceptions underscored the Command’s determination to enforce relevant customs laws, prevent the importation and circulation of prohibited goods and protect Nigeria’s economic interests.

It added that the enforcement operations formed part of broader efforts to safeguard national security and public health while strengthening the country’s economic resilience.

The statement also highlighted the Service’s expanding role in national development, noting that its responsibilities extend beyond revenue generation and border enforcement to include community engagement, infrastructure support and trade facilitation.

It said the inspection and parade of the seized items, alongside the commissioning of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) projects, demonstrated the Service’s commitment to combining effective enforcement with initiatives that promote community development.

The post Customs seize ₦3.52bn contraband in Ogun appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: My mother regretted having me, wished I was aborted – Pastor Bolaji Idowu
description:
The Lead Pastor of Harvesters International Christian Centre, Bolaji Idowu, has recounted how his mother opposed his decision to become a pastor, telling him she regretted having him and would have aborted him had she known he would choose the ministry.
Idowu shared the experience in a video posted
content:
The Lead Pastor of Harvesters International Christian Centre, Bolaji Idowu, has recounted how his mother opposed his decision to become a pastor, telling him she regretted having him and would have aborted him had she known he would choose the ministry.

Idowu shared the experience in a video posted by Church Gist on X, recalling that his mother initially laughed when he told her he believed God had called him into ministry.

“She said God can never call you. She said, ‘Look at the whole family, who is the pastor in the family? God does not call us,’” he recalled.

According to the pastor, his mother’s opposition intensified when he returned to reaffirm his conviction about the calling.

“When I came back, and I confirmed God had called me, my mother said, ‘You are just lazy.’ I packed my things and left the house,” he said.

He further recalled that his mother predicted he would fail and expressed regret over his birth.

“My mother looked me in the eye and said, ‘You will fail. I regret having you as a child. If I knew this was your choice to be a pastor, I would have had an abortion.’”

Idowu shared the experience while preaching about divine mercy, describing his journey into ministry as a testimony of God’s intervention.

“I am a victim of mercy,” he said.

He also recounted an Instagram video he watched shortly before the engagement, featuring Pastor Dolapo Lawal, who spoke about starting a church in Atlanta that went six months without a single attendee.

According to Idowu, Lawal said he initially prayed for God to release him from the assignment rather than asking for the church to grow. However, he said God told him he was praying for the wrong thing and should ask for mercy instead.

Idowu said that, according to Lawal’s account, opportunities began opening for the ministry shortly after he changed his prayer.

The Harvesters pastor then drew on his own experience of rejection at home before eventually building his ministry.

content:
On Saturday, November 14, Otutochi ‘Tochi Wigwe, the eldest daughter of the late banking executive, Mr Herbert Wigwe, had the reception of her traditional wedding to Wilson Omogbale Aikhomu in a well-attended ceremony in Lagos.

The ceremony had in attendance dignitaries, including former Vice President Yemi Osinbajo, Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, Alhaji Aliko Dangote, Emir of Kano Muhammad Sanusi II, and Mrs. Toyin Saraki.

Singers Davido and Flavour serenaded guests with their music at the topnotch event.

The groom, a Lagos-based investment professional, is the Managing Partner and Chief Investment Officer of Zoya Admiralty. He is also the son of the late Rear Admiral Joseph Omozuwa Aikhomu and the nephew of former Chief of General Staff, Admiral Augustus Aikhomu.

Wilson was a close friend of Tochi’s late brother, Chizi.

Mrs Toyin Saraki said, at the occasion, that she had joy of joining Aigboje Aig-Imohkuede, the Chairman of Access Holdings who reportedly bankrolled the event, and his wife, Ofovwe, at the wedding reception.

She added that her dear friends, the late Herbert and Doreen Wigwe, and their beloved son, Chizi, were greatly missed and were with them in spirit throughout the day.

“They would have been immensely gladdened to see Tochi so radiant”, the former First Lady of Kwara State said.


“Tochi has shown remarkable grace and fortitude, and it was a privilege to witness her begins this new chapter beside Wilson, whose late father, Rear Admiral Joe Aikhomu, was likewise fondly remembered.

“May Almighty God keep and prosper your union, granting you abiding love, wisdom, peace and good health, and may your home be one of happiness and fulfillment for all the years to come”.

Earlier on November 5, 2026, Tochi tied the knot traditionally with Wilson in a private ceremony attended by family members and close friends.

The ceremony featured traditional marriage rites, including the payment of the bride price, signing of family documents and the formal handing over of the bride to her husband’s family at their Ikoyi residence.

Tochi’s aunt, in a social media tribute, shared details of the occasion.

She also reflected on the absence of Tochi’s parents and her elder brother, Chizi, who died in a helicopter crash in California on February 9, 2024.

Quoting Isaiah 61:3, the aunt described the occasion as “beauty for ashes”, expressing gratitude that Tochi was able to begin a new chapter of her life despite the family’s painful loss.

title: Kaduna traditional, faith leaders join forces to tackle barriers to girls’ education
description:
Faith and traditional leaders in Kaduna state have expressed readiness to work with Brain Builders Youth Development Initiative (BBYDI) to keep girls in school and help those whose education was interrupted by marriage, pregnancy or financial hardship return to the classroom.
The leaders declared th
content:
Faith and traditional leaders in Kaduna state have expressed readiness to work with Brain Builders Youth Development Initiative (BBYDI) to keep girls in school and help those whose education was interrupted by marriage, pregnancy or financial hardship return to the classroom.

The leaders declared their support at the inauguration of the Coalition of Faith and Traditional Leaders for Girls’ Education at the Asa Pyramid Hotel in Kaduna. The coalition was established under BBYDI’s Faith and Tradition for Girls’ Education Project, supported by Malala Fund.

BBYDI also launched an advocacy toolkit, available in a local-language edition, to help religious and traditional leaders speak with families about girls’ education in a language they understand. The organisation unveiled a coalition charter and terms of reference alongside the toolkit.

The toolkit is designed for use in sermons, congregational meetings, traditional council meetings and community dialogues. It gives leaders a resource for discussing why girls leave school, what families can do to keep their daughters enrolled and how communities can support girls who want to resume their education.

The coalition will address barriers such as child marriage, poverty, insecurity and stigma faced by girls who become pregnant or have children while of school age. The charter sets out the coalition’s shared commitments, while the terms of reference guide how members will work together.

Halimat Olufade, BBYDI’s programme director, said consultations with faith and traditional leaders across the project’s 12 local government areas informed the formation of the coalition and the development of the three documents.

Olufade said the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) and Jama’atu Nasril Islam (JNI) had expressed willingness to use their churches, mosques and community platforms to encourage families to prioritise girls’ education. She said the coalition would pay particular attention to married girls and young mothers who want to resume their studies.

“No girl should have to abandon her education because she becomes a wife or a mother. No girl’s circumstances should permanently close the doors to learning,” she said.

Uba Sani, governor of Kaduna, commended BBYDI for convening the coalition and pledged the state government’s support. The Governor was represented at the event by Mallam Abass Shehu

“The State Government pledges its full support and partnership,” Sani said in a goodwill message.

The governor said the state had provided conditional cash transfers to 46,572 girls to improve attendance, retention and completion. He said schools had also been built and renovated through the Adolescent Girls Initiative for Learning and Empowerment (AGILE) and the Reaching Out-of-School Children project.

Abubakar Sani Sambo, Kaduna’s commissioner for education, also commended BBYDI and said the ministry looked forward to working with the coalition. In his goodwill remarks, he urged members to use their platforms to encourage parents to enrol their daughters, support girls to remain in school and challenge practices that cut their education short.

Sambo said the involvement of religious and traditional leaders could strengthen collaboration between the ministry and community institutions. He also called for attention to the barriers faced by girls with disabilities and those whose social circumstances make it harder to attend school.

Ahmad Nuhu Bamalli, the Emir of Zazzau, commended BBYDI for its work on girls’ education in Kaduna, particularly in the Zazzau emirate. The Emir, who was represented by Sani Yusuf Magaji, the Makaman Malaman Zazzau, said the emirate was open to working with BBYDI and other organisations on practical proposals to expand girls’ access to education.

Magaji said the emirate council had been engaging parents, guardians, religious leaders and community groups on their role in helping girls access education. He recalled that Jafaru Dan Isyaku, a former emir, dedicated Babban Dodo Primary School to serve as a girls’ boarding school and enrolled his own daughter, Hajiya Talle.

He said district heads, ward heads and officials of the then Zaria Native Authority were also encouraged to enrol their daughters in primary school.

Rahanatu Lawal, director of the Gender Policy Unit at Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, urged the coalition to involve girls and young women in designing programmes and shaping the policies that affect them. She said girls should have a direct say in what would make schools safer and what support they need to return after dropping out.

Olufade said the coalition’s success would be measured by the changes for girls in the communities its members serve, including whether more girls stay in school and whether those who have dropped out can return and complete their education.

title: Ekiti govt disowns purported climate action award
description:
The Ekiti State Government has dissociated itself, Governor Biodun Oyebanji and his administration from a purported Best African Governor for Climate Action Award reportedly presented to the Governor.



According to a publication, the award was presented by the King’s College African Leadership Cen
content:
The Ekiti State Government has dissociated itself, Governor Biodun Oyebanji and his administration from a purported Best African Governor for Climate Action Award reportedly presented to the Governor.


According to a publication, the award was presented by the King’s College African Leadership Centre at its inaugural Climate Action Awards ceremony, held on the sidelines of COP 31 in Antalya, Türkiye, in collaboration with the Ondo State Oil Producing Areas Development Commission (OSOPADEC).


The Government, however, wishes to state categorically that Governor Oyebanji was neither aware of the purported award nor involved in its presentation. He did not attend the ceremony, nor authorise anyone to receive it on his behalf.


This disclaimer has become necessary to set the record straight and prevent members of the public from being misled by claims that are not only false but could also be part of a dubious publicity stunt.


Governor Oyebanji’s administration is guided by the principles of accountability, transparency and integrity. While the Governor has received several recognitions and awards from credible organisations and reputable institutions in acknowledgement of his contributions to governance and development, the Governor does not endorse or associate himself with questionable awards from organisations whose credibility and intentions are unclear.


Members of the public and the media are therefore urged to disregard the report and treat the purported award as unauthorised and unrecognised by the Governor and the Ekiti State Government.

title: Galatasaray set club record with 42-match unbeaten home run
description:
Galatasaray made history on Saturday by extending their unbeaten home run in the Süper Lig to 42 matches, the longest streak in the club’s history.
The Lions defeated Samsunspor 2-1 at the Başakşehir Fatih Terim Stadium, with goals from Lucas Torreira and Yunus Akgün securing the victory.
According
content:
Galatasaray made history on Saturday by extending their unbeaten home run in the Süper Lig to 42 matches, the longest streak in the club’s history.

The Lions defeated Samsunspor 2-1 at the Başakşehir Fatih Terim Stadium, with goals from Lucas Torreira and Yunus Akgün securing the victory.

According to a post obtained from the club’s X handle on Sunday, the result pushed Okan Buruk’s side to 31 points and kept them top of the table after 12 matchweeks.

The previous club record stood at 41 consecutive home games without defeat.

That mark, set between 2017 and 2019 during Fatih Terim’s tenure, was equalled in recent weeks and then broken with the win over Samsunspor. Galatasaray’s last home league defeat came in Matchweek 37 of the 2023-24 season, a 1-0 loss to Fenerbahçe. Since then, the team has recorded 34 wins and eight draws on home soil.

The match was staged at Başakşehir’s ground because of pitch maintenance work at RAMS Park. There was an extra layer of coincidence: the stadium bears Fatih Terim’s name, and it was Okan Buruk himself who, while coaching Başakşehir in 2019, ended Terim’s earlier 41-match home unbeaten run.

The victory also stretched Galatasaray’s winning streak across all competitions to seven matches.

Buruk’s side continue to chase a fifth successive Süper Lig title, maintaining strong form despite missing key players at times.

Club officials and fans celebrated the landmark achievement, with the official Galatasaray account highlighting “Winner” Okan Buruk and the Lions for delivering the longest home unbeaten sequence the club has ever known.

A new book by TheCable publisher, Simon Kolawole, has shed light on the breakdown of relations between former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and former Rivers State Governor Nyesom Wike ahead of the 2023 presidential election.

In excerpts from ‘Winning Formula: The Inside Story of Nigeria’s 2023 Presidential Election,’ made available to PUNCH Online on Sunday, Kolawole attributed the fallout to Atiku’s decision to choose former Delta State Governor Ifeanyi Okowa as his running mate despite reported assurances to Wike and a committee recommendation favouring him.

The author argued that Atiku’s remarks while announcing Okowa on June 16, 2022, further aggravated the disagreement by leaving Wike feeling humiliated.

He stated that Atiku announced Okowa as his running mate after the Peoples Democratic Party’s presidential primary. In his statement, he said he had consulted widely with party stakeholders and made his selection criteria clear.

He said his running mate must have “the potential to succeed me at a moment’s notice, that is, a president-in-waiting. In other words, the person must have the qualities to be president.”

Kolawole argued that the statement was an indirect slight against Wike, who had also sought the party’s vice-presidential ticket.

“By picking Okowa, he had virtually declared that Chief Nyesom Wike did not have presidential qualities. This was below the belt.

“And that was how a full-scale war broke out,” the author wrote.

The book said Wike, who felt hurt and humiliated, became determined to retaliate, while Atiku remained confident that he could win the election without the Rivers governor’s support.

Kolawole described the ensuing disagreement as a case of “mutually assured destruction”, noting that neither man eventually achieved his presidential ambition.

“Wike wanted a fight to the finish. Atiku was fully set for it. It was a case of mutually assured destruction (MAD).

“But rather than MAD being a deterrent doctrine as is the case with the world’s nuclear powers, it was the tonic for an all-out war between Atiku and Wike. Neither would end up as president or vice-president. The destruction was mutually assured,” the book stated.

The author also explained why Atiku was confident of winning the 2023 election despite the disagreement with Wike, citing his position as the leading northern candidate, his alliances in the South and the alleged support of some allies of former President Muhammadu Buhari.

Kolawole wrote that Atiku believed he had a strong chance of winning because “he was the strongest candidate from the north” and had “a considerably large coalition of allies in the south”.

The book also recounted a series of meetings between the two politicians and their associates in the weeks following the PDP presidential primary in May 2022.

One of the meetings took place at Wike’s residence in Guzape, Abuja, on May 30, 2022, after Atiku and the party’s National Chairman, Iyorchia Ayu, had paid a visit to former Sokoto State Governor Aminu Tambuwal.

Kolawole said Wike was unhappy that Atiku’s first visit after the primary was to Tambuwal, whose withdrawal from the contest had helped Atiku emerge as the party’s presidential candidate.

At the meeting in Wike’s residence, former Minister Adamu Maina Waziri represented Atiku’s camp, while former Ekiti State Governor Ayo Fayose and former Attorney-General of the Federation Mohammed Bello Adoke spoke on behalf of Wike’s camp.

Wike reportedly raised concerns about the PDP’s decision to field a northern presidential candidate despite an understanding among southern governors that power should shift to the South.

The two politicians later held a private discussion in Wike’s study, which they reportedly agreed would remain confidential.

According to Kolawole, Atiku expressed interest in working with Wike as his running mate during the meeting.

A bemused Wike reportedly asked, “In what capacity?” before Atiku responded, “as my running mate”.

Wike, however, reminded Atiku that he had already been told Okowa was the preferred choice.

“But I was told you already promised Okowa,” Wike was quoted as saying, while Atiku reportedly replied, “No, I have not promised anybody.”

The author said Wike’s mood improved following the exchange, and he promised to support the campaign with resources and grassroots mobilisation.

Kolawole wrote that Wike’s optimism was further encouraged by an arrangement for both men to travel in the same vehicle to the PDP national secretariat in Abuja for Atiku’s presentation with his certificate of return on June 1, 2022.

However, the arrangement was reportedly changed on the day of the event, with Wike informed that the governors would travel together in a bus while Atiku would ride separately. Wike subsequently found an excuse not to attend the ceremony.

The book stated that the development made Wike suspect that Atiku was changing his mind about choosing him as running mate.

Another meeting was arranged for June 8, 2022, during which Atiku reportedly told Wike that he would constitute a committee to assess prospective running mates and make a recommendation that would be binding on him.

Kolawole also detailed how the committee’s recommendation reportedly favoured Wike but did not translate into his selection.

“Adoke and Nwogu later briefed Wike on the discussions but encouraged him to still meet with Atiku before taking his next steps. Mallam Abdullahi Nyako, Atiku’s private secretary, put another meeting together on 8 June 2022, the day the APC announced the result of its own primary.

“At the meeting, Atiku explained to Wike that when he picked Mr Peter Obi as his running mate for the 2019 election, senior members of the PDP were unhappy and accused him of acting alone. This time, he said, he was going to constitute a committee that would assess all the prospective candidates and make a recommendation that would be binding on him.

“The 17-member committee, headed by Ambassador Umar Iliya Damagum, the party’s deputy national chairman, voted, and 13 of them, including Tambuwal, picked Wike. But Atiku still did not choose Wike, reportedly at the behest of the PDP elders from the north who did not have a high opinion of the governor,” the book stated.

The author said the decision to pick Okowa, despite the committee’s reported recommendation, further widened the rift between the two politicians.

He explained how the announcement of Okowa’s selection finally ended Wike’s hopes of joining Atiku’s ticket.

“As the announcement of the running mate drew closer, it was clear that Wike was not going to be the choice. Picking Okowa was one thing, but the framing of the announcement more than injured Wike’s ego.

“At this stage, Wike seemed to still be open to some form of accommodation in Atiku’s plans, but it was all a façade. He had lost the presidential primary and had also been overlooked in the choice of a running mate. It was all over,” the book stated.

Kolawole said Wike subsequently decided to stay away from Atiku’s campaign and work against his presidential ambition.

“He began to weigh his options and, by all accounts, decided to snub Atiku and shun the nationwide campaign. Not only would he shun the campaign; he would also work against Atiku with every ounce of energy in him and every kobo in his pocket,” the book stated.

The book, ‘Winning Formula: The Inside Story of Nigeria’s 2023 Presidential Election,’ published by CableBooks, is scheduled to go on sale on Monday, November 23, 2026.

The book description stated that it examined how Bola Tinubu outmanoeuvred former President Muhammadu Buhari, how Atiku and Wike undermined each other’s presidential ambitions, and how Peter Obi and the Obidient movement emerged as a political phenomenon.

It described the publication as “built on insider briefings, court filings and polling data, and told with the pace of a newsroom and the eye of a data analyst”.

The description further stated that the book explored “a story of naivety, cat-and-mouse games, cold calculations, and subterfuge”.

The post Revealed: How Atiku’s choice of Okowa triggered feud with Wike appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Otti disowns viral statement against campaign rallies, calls it fake
description:
By Steve Oko



Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has disowned a viral social media statement purportedly credited to him, describing it as fake and warning the public against spreading misinformation.







The statement, which circulated on X (formerly Twitter), quoted Otti as saying that incumbent
content:
By Steve Oko

Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has disowned a viral social media statement purportedly credited to him, describing it as fake and warning the public against spreading misinformation.

The statement, which circulated on X (formerly Twitter), quoted Otti as saying that incumbent governors who embark on campaigns have no business doing so if they have performed well, arguing that their achievements should speak for them and secure their re-election.

It also quoted the governor as saying he was not campaigning and that Abia residents should re-elect him only if they considered his performance satisfactory.

However, the governor, through his Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Ferdinand Ekeoma, on Friday, dismissed the statement and the X account that published it as fake.

Ekeoma, who signed the disclaimer, said Otti never made the statement and urged the public not to be misled by the publication.

He explained that, contrary to the impression created by the viral post, the governor was already campaigning and had been touring different parts of the state to interact with voters and obtain firsthand feedback, particularly from grassroots communities.

According to him, Otti considers campaigns a legitimate component of the electoral process and could not have disparaged politicians for engaging in them.

“The Governor believes that campaigns are legitimate parts of the electoral process and thus could not have dismissed it or cast aspersions on those campaigning,” Ekeoma said.

The state government urged members of the public to disregard the purported statement and the account responsible for circulating it, while calling on those behind the publication to immediately take it down and desist from misrepresenting the governor.

It also cautioned individuals using Otti’s popularity to generate online traffic to ensure that information published in his name is truthful, warning that deliberate misrepresentation could attract the attention of law enforcement agencies.

The disclaimer comes amid growing political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections, with social media increasingly serving as a platform for political messaging, claims and counterclaims.

Meanwhile, Vanguard investigations indicate that Otti currently faces no formidable challenger in the forthcoming governorship election.

title: Niger: Bandits kill village head, wife, worshippers in fresh attacks
description:
Armed men have killed a village head, his wife and several worshippers in separate attacks on two communities in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State.
The first incident occurred around 5am on Saturday in Lumman-Ba’are community, when residents had gathered for their early morning prayers.
The
content:
Armed men have killed a village head, his wife and several worshippers in separate attacks on two communities in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State.

The first incident occurred around 5am on Saturday in Lumman-Ba’are community, when residents had gathered for their early morning prayers.

The attackers reportedly opened fire on the worshippers, killing several people before setting the village head’s palace ablaze. Children were also reportedly among those killed, while other residents were abducted.

A source who spoke to Daily Trust said the village head and his wife were among those killed in the attack.

“Terrorists came and opened fire when the victims were observing their early morning prayers. They killed the village head and burnt down his palace. Some people were also kidnapped,” the source said.

The source put the number of casualties at 11, adding that several residents had fled their homes following the attack.

Another source confirmed that Lumman-Ba’are and Gadan Oli were targeted by heavily armed men, who reportedly shot at residents without regard for their age or gender.

“Lumman Ba’are and Gadan Oli communities were attacked by heavily armed terrorists. The attack was brutal attacks on the communities today. They shot at people indiscriminately regardless of age or gender, and setting houses on fire,” the source said.

The violence reportedly spread to Gada-Oli around 2pm on Saturday, when gunmen attacked residents while they were observing afternoon prayers. The number of people killed in the second incident was not immediately known.

The village head and his wife were reportedly buried at New Bussa, the headquarters of Borgu LGA.

Confirming the attack on Lumman-Ba’are, the spokesperson for the Niger State Police Command, SP Wasiu Abiodun, said five people were reportedly killed.

In a statement, Abiodun said the police received information about the invasion at about 5am on November 21.

“On 21/11/2026 at about 5am, report received indicated that suspected armed men invaded Lumma Ba’are village, Borgu LGA and attacked the community, while about five persons reportedly lost their lives during the attack,” he said.

The police spokesperson added that joint security teams had been sent to the area to track down the attackers.

“Joint security teams have been deployed to the location, efforts to apprehend the suspected perpetrators ongoing. Further development will be communicated,” Abiodun said.

The police confirmed the attack on Lumman-Ba’are but did not provide details about the reported assault on Gada-Oli.

title: High campaign costs, distrust hinder youths’ political ambitions – Report
description: Young Nigerians continue to face significant barriers to political participation and representation despite making up the majority of the country’s population, with high campaign costs, entrenched political structures and declining confidence in the electoral system limiting their access to elective
content:
Young Nigerians continue to face significant barriers to political participation and representation despite making up the majority of the country’s population, with high campaign costs, entrenched political structures and declining confidence in the electoral system limiting their access to elective positions.

A report by the BBC on Sunday, highlighted the challenges confronting young Nigerians seeking political offices, noting that the country’s political leadership remains dominated by older politicians despite its youthful population.

One of those seeking to change the situation is 38-year-old Abdulhadi Dalhatu, who is contesting for a seat in the Kano State House of Assembly ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Dalhatu believes young people deserve greater representation in government, arguing that they should have a stronger voice in decisions affecting their future.

“Younger people are the majority in this country and should be deciding the future,” he told the BBC.

However, Nigeria’s political history reflects the limited presence of young people in top elective positions.

Since the return to democratic rule in 1999, the country has continued to elect leaders considerably older than the majority of its population.

The situation is also evident in the National Assembly, where none of the 109 senators is below 40, while only 14 members of the 360-member House of Representatives fall within that age group.

The report identified financial constraints as one of the major obstacles preventing young Nigerians from participating actively in politics.

The high cost of nomination forms, campaign activities and internal party contests makes it difficult for aspiring young politicians without substantial financial resources to compete against established political figures.

Major political parties, including the All Progressives Congress, Peoples Democratic Party and African Democratic Congress, have reportedly fixed their presidential nomination fees at N100 million, placing the cost beyond the reach of many young aspirants.

Dalhatu disclosed that he had previously abandoned political ambitions because he could not raise enough money to finance his campaigns.

Another young politician, Fatima Zahra Umar, also noted that Nigerian politics was largely influenced by money, leaving many young people unable to secure influential elective positions.

Beyond financial challenges, the report identified political structures and cultural attitudes as additional factors limiting youth participation.

Political analyst Seun Ajayi argued that some young Nigerians lacked the determination to pursue major political positions, while others were content with occupying less influential roles in government.

The report also highlighted declining interest in electoral participation among young Nigerians, despite their significant involvement in political movements such as the 2020 #EndSARS protests and the Obidient movement during the 2023 general elections.

Although these movements demonstrated the ability of young people to mobilise around political issues, translating such enthusiasm into sustained electoral participation has remained a challenge.

According to the report, young people now account for 29 per cent of registered voters, compared with 40 per cent in 2023, despite an increase in the country’s overall registered voter population to more than 103 million.

The Independent National Electoral Commission has introduced initiatives, including appointing entertainment personalities as voter registration ambassadors, to encourage greater participation among young Nigerians ahead of the 2027 elections.

However, some young people remain sceptical about the electoral process, believing that their participation may not significantly change the country’s political leadership.

The report stressed that improving youth representation would require addressing financial barriers, strengthening political inclusion and encouraging young Nigerians to move beyond social media activism towards active participation in the electoral process.

As the 2027 general elections approach, the question of how to create more opportunities for younger Nigerians in politics remains an important issue in the country’s democratic development.

title: Abiodun demands arrest of Odegbami’s attackers
description:
Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has condemned the attack on former Super Eagles captain and the state’s Sports Ambassador, Segun Odegbami, urging the police to arrest and prosecute those responsible.
In a statement released on X by his media aide, Emmanuel Ojo, Abiodun expressed deep concern over
content:
Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has condemned the attack on former Super Eagles captain and the state’s Sports Ambassador, Segun Odegbami, urging the police to arrest and prosecute those responsible.

In a statement released on X by his media aide, Emmanuel Ojo, Abiodun expressed deep concern over the incident, describing the attack on the former Super Eagles captain as unfortunate, unacceptable, and a threat to the safety of citizens.

He also expressed relief that Odegbami survived the incident.

“Abiodun, however, thanked God that the assailants were unable to silence Chief Odegbami, noting that it was a matter of relief that the celebrated sports icon survived the attack,” the statement said.

The governor described the former international, popularly known as Mathematical, as an outstanding Nigerian whose contributions to sports, particularly football, had earned him national and international recognition.

He noted that Odegbami occupied a special place in the state’s sports development agenda as its Sports Ambassador.

“His experience, influence and enduring commitment to the promotion of sports remain invaluable,” the statement added.

Abiodun urged security agencies, particularly the police, to conduct a thorough investigation into the incident, track down the perpetrators and ensure that they faced the full weight of the law.

“Abiodun urged the security agencies, particularly the police, to conduct a thorough investigation into the incident, track down the perpetrators, and ensure that they face the full weight of the law.

“He stressed that no individual or group should take the law into their hands, warning that acts of violence and criminal intimidation would not be tolerated in Ogun State,” the statement concluded.

The governor also wished Odegbami continued strength and good health, assuring him of the state government’s concern and support.

He reiterated his administration’s commitment to protecting lives and property and ensuring that Ogun State remained a peaceful and secure environment for residents and visitors.

Odegbami, 74, survived an attack by three armed men at his residence in the Ibara Government Reservation Area, Abeokuta, in the early hours of Friday.

The football legend, in a message to a close associate, described the incident as an assassination attempt and the closest he had ever come to death.

He said the attackers broke down his door at about 2:30am, adding that he fought them with the assistance of his driver and domestic worker before they fled.

“Thank the Creator of the Universe for me. I survived an assassination attempt. This morning at 2:30am, three unknown persons came to the house to steal and kill. I fought back with the help of God.

“My driver and house boy joined me, and we fought them before they fled. It was the closest I have ever been face to face with death. They broke down my door to get to me. I have been to the hospital,” Odegbami said.

He sustained deep machete wounds during the struggle and was taken to an undisclosed hospital for treatment before being discharged.

The Ogun State Police Command confirmed the incident and said its Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, had visited Odegbami and ordered an investigation and manhunt for the attackers.

The command’s spokesperson, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, said, “The command is leaving no stone unturned in addressing the incident. The Commissioner of Police immediately ordered a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding it, with intensive efforts ongoing to identify and apprehend those responsible. We can also confirm that Chief Segun Odegbami has been discharged from the hospital.”

The police had yet to establish the motive for the attack as of the time of filing the report.

Odegbami played a key role in Nigeria’s victory at the 1980 Africa Cup of Nations, scoring three goals to finish as joint top scorer. He also helped Shooting Stars of Ibadan win the African Cup Winners’ Cup in 1976.

title: Tinubu doing fantastic job in sports development – Infantino

Infantino spoke at the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation
content:
FIFA President, Gianni Infantino, has praised President Bola Tinubu for investing in sports facilities and infrastructure, describing the efforts as evidence of Nigeria’s commitment to the development of its young population.

Infantino spoke at the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) in Abuja, where he commended the Federal Government for prioritising sports development.

He said the investments in sports infrastructure showed that Nigeria was looking towards the future and recognised the potential of its young people.

“He is doing, together with all of you, fantastic job here in Nigeria, showing that you are a country projected into the future,” Infantino said.

He added: “The investments done in sports facilities, infrastructure, show that you believe in your youth, in the young girls and the young boys of Nigeria.”

The FIFA president also congratulated the government and other stakeholders for their commitment to improving sports facilities and creating more opportunities for young Nigerians.

title: FG unveils 19 job opportunities for Nigerians abroad
description:
Nigerians seeking employment opportunities outside the country can apply for 19 advertised positions at two international organisations following a recruitment announcement by the Federal Government.
The openings are available at the African Space Agency, based in Cairo, Egypt, and the General Secre
content:
Nigerians seeking employment opportunities outside the country can apply for 19 advertised positions at two international organisations following a recruitment announcement by the Federal Government.

The openings are available at the African Space Agency, based in Cairo, Egypt, and the General Secretariat of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs publicised the recruitment exercise through two separate notices dated November 20, 2026. Both announcements were signed by the ministry’s spokesperson, Oluwafemi Adeniyi, and posted on its official Facebook page on Saturday.

Vacancies at the African Space Agency

The African Space Agency is seeking to fill five positions at its headquarters in Cairo.

The available roles and their respective application deadlines are:

– Director, Corporate Services (D-1): December 10, 2026.

– Director-General, African Space Agency (D-2): December 10, 2026.

– Head of Legal Affairs (Grade P-5): December 10, 2026.

– Senior Finance Officer (P3): November 25, 2026.

– Senior Human Resources Officer (P3): November 25, 2026.

Applicants can find information about the requirements and submission process on the agency’s website: [https://africanspaceagency.org](https://africanspaceagency.org).

Vacancies at the OIC General Secretariat

The second recruitment notice covers 14 positions at the OIC General Secretariat in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

The advertised roles are:

– Director-General of Political Affairs.

– Director, Administration Department.

– Director, Information Department.

– Director, Conference Department.

– Director, Muslim Communities and Minorities.

– Director, African Affairs.

– Director, European Affairs and International Organisations.

– Head of Human Resources (PP2).

– Professional Officer, Human Resources (PP2).

– Professional Officers, Administration Department (P2).

– Director, Peace, Security and Mediation Unit.

– Chief of HRC Office – IUT.

– Registrar – IUT.

– Deputy Internal Auditor – IUT.

According to the ministry, the closing dates for the OIC positions fall between November 29 and December 24, 2026.

Interested candidates have been advised to check the organisation’s vacancy portal, [https://www.oic-oci.org/en/vacancies](https://www.oic-oci.org/en/vacancies), for the specific deadlines, qualification requirements and instructions for submitting applications.

The Federal Government encouraged qualified Nigerians to consult the respective websites for full details before applying.

title: EPL: Alonso blames Chelsea’s 4-1 defeat on loss of belief
description:
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has attributed his side’s 4-1 defeat to Leeds United to a loss of confidence, mental fragility and their inability to respond positively to setbacks during the game.
The Blues suffered a disappointing defeat at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, despite taking the lead through
content:
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has attributed his side’s 4-1 defeat to Leeds United to a loss of confidence, mental fragility and their inability to respond positively to setbacks during the game.

The Blues suffered a disappointing defeat at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, despite taking the lead through Emmanuel Emegha in the 25th minute.

However, Leeds responded almost immediately, with Noah Okafor equalising three minutes later before Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted a penalty in the 53rd minute to put the visitors ahead.

Okafor added his second goal five minutes later, while Brenden Aaronson completed the emphatic victory with a stoppage-time strike.

Speaking to Bein Sport after the match, Alonso admitted that Chelsea lost control and momentum following Leeds’ equaliser and the early withdrawal of midfielder Moisés Caicedo through injury.

“What went wrong was after their equaliser, after the change with Moi, we lost completely the momentum,” Alonso said.

He explained that his players initially performed well, creating opportunities and dealing with Leeds’ pressing game, but struggled to maintain their confidence after conceding.

“From that moment, they started believing, we started not believing. After that, we never got the good feeling mentally in any moment, and we were not able to come out from the pressure,” he added.

The Spanish tactician also admitted that his team was going through a difficult period and needed to find solutions collectively to overcome their struggles.

“We are in a delicate moment, a fragile moment. I think that the team needs to find solutions. We need to find solutions together because we need to go through it,” he said.

On Caicedo’s injury, Alonso described the midfielder’s early substitution as a major setback but insisted that it was not the only reason behind the heavy defeat.

He also called on his players to improve their mentality and ability to compete when faced with difficult moments during matches.

Chelsea supporters expressed their frustration after the defeat, with many leaving Stamford Bridge before the final whistle.

Alonso apologised to the fans and urged them to continue believing in the team, promising that the players and coaching staff would work harder to turn the situation around.

The defeat leaves Chelsea needing to rebuild their confidence and consistency as Alonso looks for ways to address the team’s recent struggles.
