title: International breaks tough on top clubs – Mourinho
description:
José Mourinho has highlighted the challenges top European clubs face after international breaks, following Real Madrid’s hard-fought 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo on Saturday.
Football transfer expert Fabrizio Romano, shared the comments on X on Sunday, noting that several leading European clubs also
content:
José Mourinho has highlighted the challenges top European clubs face after international breaks, following Real Madrid’s hard-fought 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo on Saturday.

Football transfer expert Fabrizio Romano, shared the comments on X on Sunday, noting that several leading European clubs also struggled to secure victories after the international window.

“It’s never easy after the break. Look at the other teams that had many players with the national teams… you will notice that Arsenal didn’t win, City didn’t win, Chelsea didn’t win. Bayern didn’t win,” Mourinho said.

The Real Madrid manager made the remarks after his side came from behind to claim all three points at the Santiago Bernabéu, with a late winner sealing the victory.

Mourinho attributed his team’s difficult afternoon partly to the physical and mental demands of international duty, explaining that several players returned with limited time to recover and prepare for the fixture.

Some members of the squad reportedly returned only in the middle of the week, while others had to contend with long-distance travel and disrupted routines.

He contrasted his side’s situation with that of Celta Vigo, who had fewer players involved in international commitments and enjoyed more time to prepare collectively.

Despite the challenges, Mourinho praised his players for their determination and resilience in finding a way to secure victory.

Results involving other European heavyweights appeared to support his observation, with Arsenal drawing 2-2 against Newcastle United, Manchester City playing out a 1-1 draw with Fulham, and Chelsea suffering a 4-1 home defeat to Leeds United in the Premier League.

Bayern Munich also failed to record a victory in their corresponding fixture.

Mourinho has repeatedly raised concerns about the impact of international breaks on club football, particularly the risks of injuries, player fatigue and inadequate recovery time.

The Portuguese tactician has also expressed concerns about the demanding football calendar, which often leaves clubs with little preparation time before returning to domestic and European competitions.

His latest comments have once again brought attention to the difficulties managers face in maintaining team performance and consistency when key players return from international duty at different times and with varying levels of fitness.

The post International breaks tough on top clubs – Mourinho appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: I have moved on from APC, Obi is my candidate – Omo-Agege
description:
Former Deputy President of the Senate, Ovie Omo-Agege, has reaffirmed his support for Peter Obi ahead of the 2027 general elections, dismissing a viral video showing him endorsing President Bola Tinubu as outdated.
Omo-Agege, who is the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) senatorial candidate for Delt
content:
Former Deputy President of the Senate, Ovie Omo-Agege, has reaffirmed his support for Peter Obi ahead of the 2027 general elections, dismissing a viral video showing him endorsing President Bola Tinubu as outdated.

Omo-Agege, who is the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) senatorial candidate for Delta Central, said the footage was recorded in April 2026, when he was still a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC).

In a statement issued on Saturday by his Special Adviser on Strategy and Communications, Godwin Anaughe, the former lawmaker said the video was recorded during an event at the Federal Polytechnic, Orogun, and was now being circulated without regard to subsequent political developments.

He accused the Delta State APC and some officials of the state government of deliberately using the old footage to misrepresent his current political position.

“The clip is genuine. But it’s seven months old, and they are sharing it as if it were filmed this morning.

“A party confident in its record does not need to dress up an old video as breaking news. Only a desperate one does,” the statement read.

“The Delta State APC and some confused elements in the Delta State government are out of arguments, and their desperation is now on full display.”

Omo-Agege said he had consistently declared his support for Obi since joining the NDC in May and had not reversed his position.

He insisted that his political allegiance was now with the opposition party and that he remained committed to Obi’s presidential ambition.

“Nigerians don’t need a history lesson from the APC. They need answers. Food is expensive. Jobs are scarce. Hope is scarce. No recycled clip is going to change that, and none of it will put food on a single table,” he said.

“If the APC wants to talk, it should talk about its record, not its video library.”

The former deputy Senate president said he would not be “distracted or blackmailed with the past”, adding that his attention remained on the 2027 elections.

title: 2027: Who speaks for the North as ACF crisis deepens?
description:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo



As the 2027 general elections draw closer, an increasingly important question is emerging in Northern Nigeria: Who speaks for the North, and whose position represents the collective interests of the region?



The question has assumed greater significance amid the lingering
content:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo

As the 2027 general elections draw closer, an increasingly important question is emerging in Northern Nigeria: Who speaks for the North, and whose position represents the collective interests of the region?

The question has assumed greater significance amid the lingering leadership crisis in the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF), one of the North’s longstanding socio-political platforms, and growing disagreements among prominent Northern politicians, elder statesmen and interest groups over the direction the region should take in the next general elections.

For decades, the ACF provided an important platform for articulating Northern interests, engaging governments and promoting regional cohesion.

However, its current internal disagreements, involving its Board of Trustees and National Executive Committee, have raised questions about its ability to provide the kind of unified regional leadership expected of it at a critical political moment.

The dispute has reportedly degenerated into competing claims of authority, allegations of constitutional breaches and disagreements over the management of the organisation’s affairs.

The development may create an opening for other political and socio-cultural platforms to occupy the space traditionally associated with the ACF.

Indeed, the struggle over who represents Northern opinion became more apparent on Wednesday when the Arewa Emerging Elites Round Table challenged some prominent Northern figures over their criticism of President Bola Tinubu’s administration.

At a press conference in Kaduna, the group, through its chairman, Abubakar A. Kurawa, faulted Dr Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, Dr Usman Bugaje, former Minister Adamu Maina Waziri and former National Health Insurance Scheme Executive Secretary, Prof Usman Yusuf, for what it described as presenting partisan political positions as the collective position of Northern Nigeria.

In a briefing titled, Stop Hiding Naked Partisanship Behind the Sacred Robes of Arewa Eldership: You Do Not Speak for the North!, the organisation questioned the mandate under which the four personalities purportedly spoke for the region.

It argued that neither previous public offices nor political prominence automatically conferred the authority to determine the political direction of the 19 Northern states.

The group particularly questioned whether traditional rulers, religious leaders, youth organisations, professional associations, farmers, traders and ordinary citizens had been adequately consulted before positions were presented as representing the North.

It also challenged the former public office holders to demonstrate their contributions to regional development, insisting that discussions about Northern leadership should go beyond political rhetoric to measurable achievements.

Meanwhile, Murtala Mohammed, an Kaduna based critic, said the intervention has also brought another dimension to the debate: Whether those challenging the authority of established Northern voices are themselves speaking from a sufficiently broad regional mandate.

“The argument is significant because the four personalities criticised by the group are entitled, like other Nigerians, to express their political opinions and question government policies”, he said. “The more important distinction is between expressing personal or partisan positions and claiming to represent an entire region.”

Political realignments

The controversy comes against the background of increasing political realignments ahead of 2027.

While some Northern politicians and groups have expressed reservations about the Tinubu administration, others are advocating continuity and greater engagement with the Federal Government.

At the Kaduna Summit on Inclusivity, Good Governance and Sustainable Development organised by the Sir Ahmadu Bello Memorial Foundation on Wednesday, former Niger State Governor, Mu’azu Babangida Aliyu, endorsed Governor Uba Sani for a second term, citing his administration’s record in security, education, healthcare, agriculture and infrastructure.

The foundation’s Director-General, Abubakar Gambo Umar, also highlighted the importance of continuity and inclusive governance.

Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, represented by Deputy Speaker Ado Doguwa, called for accountability and constructive criticism while acknowledging continuing security challenges, particularly in Southern Kaduna.

Governor Uba Sani, however, went beyond the immediate Kaduna political debate, urging the foundation to mobilise Northern leaders towards developing a comprehensive regional development agenda.

He recalled the vision of the late Premier of Northern Nigeria, Sir Ahmadu Bello, for a united, peaceful and self-sufficient North, arguing that subsequent generations of leaders had departed from that vision.

His call raises an important question: Can Northern leaders agree on a common development agenda despite their differences over political parties, presidential succession and the 2027 elections?

Platforms

There are also other emerging platforms. The League of Northern Democrats, led by former Kano State Governor Ibrahim Shekarau, has been engaging the ACF, Northern Elders Forum and Middle Belt Forum on the possibility of building a common front around the region’s challenges.

Yet, the existence of several organisations does not necessarily translate into a coherent regional voice.

“The North’s problems extend beyond political representation. Insecurity, poverty, unemployment, educational backwardness, agricultural difficulties, infrastructure deficits and economic hardship require sustained engagement and measurable interventions,” said Murtala.

“Consequently, the question of who speaks for the North should not be reduced to who supports or opposes Tinubu, who wants power returned to the region or which political camp commands the loudest following.

“Neither should the North be treated as a politically homogeneous constituency whose millions of people must necessarily subscribe to one political position”.

The ACF crisis therefore presents an opportunity for serious introspection.

Its founding mission of promoting Northern unity and socio-economic advancement remains relevant, but rebuilding confidence in the organisation requires resolving its internal disagreements and restoring its institutional credibility.

Similarly, emerging Arewa groups must demonstrate inclusiveness, independence and accountability rather than simply becoming competing platforms for political interests.

Ultimately, Northern leadership ahead of 2027 should be measured not by the ability to mobilise endorsements, issue press statements or condemn political opponents, but by the capacity to develop a common agenda, build consensus across regional divides and hold governments accountable.

ACF speaks

Reacting, the National Publicity Secretary of the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF), Prof. Tukur Muhammad Baba, told Sunday Vanguard that differences of opinion within the forum were natural and should not be mistaken for a breakdown of unity or purpose.

He said such differences did not detract from the forum’s commitment to consultation, constructive engagement and advocacy on issues of common interest, including good governance in all its ramifications.

He explained that the ACF remained committed to holding elected officials accountable, promoting the fight against corruption and advocating policies that would advance the welfare of the people. Baba noted that the forum had consistently called on governments at all levels to intensify efforts to tackle insecurity, stressing that it had never relented in demanding decisive action against the persistent security challenges confronting the North.

Pundits argue that the North does not necessarily need one political voice, but needs credible institutions capable of accommodating different voices while agreeing on the fundamental interests of its people.

Until that happens, the question of who speaks for the North may remain one of the most contentious issues in the region’s politics ahead of 2027.

Vanguard News

title: China, Nigeria strengthen cultural ties through music
description:
Nigeria and China have stepped up cultural diplomacy through music and people-to-people exchanges, with the Chinese Cultural centre disclosing that it has organised more than 50 cultural activities in Nigeria since the beginning of 2026.
The China Cultural Centre Counsellor, Yang Jianxing, disclosed
content:
Nigeria and China have stepped up cultural diplomacy through music and people-to-people exchanges, with the Chinese Cultural centre disclosing that it has organised more than 50 cultural activities in Nigeria since the beginning of 2026.

The China Cultural Centre Counsellor, Yang Jianxing, disclosed this at the final of the 2026 Nigeria Chinese and English Singing Competition, on Saturday, where he described music as a powerful instrument for bridging cultural differences and strengthening bilateral relations.

Yang said the competition, which brought together Nigerian and Chinese participants, provided an opportunity for young people from both countries to showcase their talents, appreciate each other’s cultures and build lasting friendships.

“Music is a universal language of humanity and a bridge that connects different civilisations and brings people closer together. A song can transcend linguistic and national boundaries, conveying emotions, fostering mutual understanding and building lasting friendships,” he said.

He listed the cultural activities organised by the embassy and the China Cultural Centre in Nigeria to include the Happy Chinese New Year Temple Fair, Tea for Harmony: Yaji Cultural Salon and the China-Nigeria Food Festival.

According to him, the activities had created opportunities for citizens of both countries to interact, understand their respective cultures and strengthen bilateral friendship.

“These activities have created more opportunities for our two peoples to get to know each other and strengthen their friendship,” Yang said.

He added that the Chinese Embassy and the China Cultural Centre would continue collaborating with Nigerian institutions to organise more cultural programmes and deepen relations between the two countries.

Yang also described the competition as a practical demonstration of the Global Civilisation Initiative proposed by Chinese President Xi Jinping, which promotes respect for cultural diversity and stronger international exchanges.

He urged the contestants to sustain the spirit of friendship beyond the competition and contribute to advancing relations between both countries.

“I also hope that you will take this event as a new starting point and continue to make positive contributions, in your respective fields, to advancing the China-Nigeria comprehensive strategic partnership and bringing greater benefits to the peoples of our two countries,” he said.

Earlier, the Director-General of the China General Chamber of Commerce in Nigeria, Zhang Xinyu, thanked the Chinese Embassy for supporting the competition and commended the judges and organisers for their efforts.

He encouraged the contestants to relax, give their best performances and enjoy the opportunity to express themselves through music.

“Music knows no borders, and songs build bridges,” Zhang said, wishing the participants success.

Also speaking, the National President of the Society of Nigerian Artists, Muhammad Sulaiman, described the competition as more than a musical performance, saying it represented a meeting of hearts and an opportunity to strengthen understanding between the two countries.

He said the event demonstrated that people could build meaningful relationships despite differences in language, culture and geographical backgrounds.

Sulaiman expressed hope that the China Cultural Centre in Nigeria would sustain and expand its collaborations with Nigerian institutions.

He called for the spirit of unity demonstrated at the competition to be extended to communities and future generations, emphasising that music could promote understanding, friendship and peace.

“Because when we sing together, we heal together. We stand in the storm, we stand in all weather. We build a bridge that no wind can break. A bridge of music for friendship’s sake,” he said.

title: Why I’m teaming up with progressive allies in Oyo for Tinubu — Oduyoye, ex-Reps Chief Whip
description:
By Nnamdi Ojiego



Honourable Babatunde Oduyoye was the Chief Whip of the Alliance for Democracy in the House of Representatives where he represented Ibadan Nort-West /South-West Federal Constituency between 1999 and 2007. He had also served as Special Adviser on Political Matters to Governor Seyi
content:
By Nnamdi Ojiego

Honourable Babatunde Oduyoye was the Chief Whip of the Alliance for Democracy in the House of Representatives where he represented Ibadan Nort-West /South-West Federal Constituency between 1999 and 2007. He had also served as Special Adviser on Political Matters to Governor Seyi Makinde, as well as a member of Oyo State Advisory Council. He is one of the appointees that opened the recent gale of resignations from the government of Oyo State. In this interview, he speaks on why he left Makinde, why he is teaming up with other progressives to support the reelection of President Bola Tinubu and why the progressives need to undertake a rescue mission in Oyo State. Excerpts:  

Some time ago, you announced your resignation from Oyo State Advisory Council, thus opening the floodgates for the resignations of many others from Governor Seyi Makinde’s government. After the announcement, we didn’t hear much from you. What happened?

The Advisory Council is expected to advise the governor on the policy, politics, and administration. As of the time I resigned, I mentioned personal reasons, and it was to improve myself in certain areas. Apart from that, I had a feeling that the council had outlived its usefulness. Once you have a council that is not up and doing, or is doing the proper thing, and the governor is not recognising it, there was no need to sit in that council anymore. That is why, honorably, I resigned.

In the resignation letter, you said you had not joined any other party apart from the Alliance for Democracy (AD). And we know that the AD is no longer a registered political party. Can you give us an insight into your political direction going forward?

I was, at no point in time, a card-carrying member of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), neither did I attend any local government or state meeting. All my activities within the party were from the purview of my office, first as the Special Adviser on Strategy and Politics to the governor of Oyo State and later as member of Advisory Council. There were times I represented the governor outside the state, specifically in Edo and Kogi States. But there was never a time they called a meeting of leaders of the PDP in the southwestern part that they invited me. There was even a time I sent out an invitation on behalf of the governor for a meeting of the South-West chapter to hold in Ibadan and I remember a commissioner from Osun State then, raised the issue that why was a non-member of the PDP inviting them to a PDP meeting? However, what happened in 2019 was that as members of the AD, we joined hands with Seyi Makinde to assist him, with the likes of Tunde Tijani, Pastor Akinade Akanmu, who later emerged the Chairman of TESCOM and he also joined me in the Advisory Council.

What is next, going forward, now that the AD is no more? What should the people of Oyo expect from you after leaving the government of Makinde?

 Before I left the government of Makinde, my good friend and brother, I have been very close to a brother and friend too, in the person of Oloye Dotun Sanusi, Okanlomo Odua. And this was known to the government, and quite a few people, that we were pushing for him to the governorafter Seyi Makinde, because I believed he has all it takes to govern Oyo State. But the idea was not welcomed in some quarters. And apart from that, he is a very busy man. And it was surprising that an idea that has not even crystalised became toxic in some quarters even before it took off, as some people started ganging up against him. And as a member of the Advisory Council, we were given the responsibility of assisting the government to choose the would-be candidate of the governor’s party.

Governor Makinde wanted us, as the Advisory Council, to recommend. And we submitted quite a few names. And top of the list was the retired Commissioner of Police, Fatai Owoseni. The council unanimously endorsed Owoseni. Segun Ogunwuyi,then-Chief of Staff to the governor, came second. And some ofus were pressurizing that Nureni Adeniran should be number three, but the Chairman, Bolaji Ayorinde, and some other people pushed for Bimbo Adekanmbi as number three. Weeks after, we were told that what we recommended was turned upside down. The chairman submitted a report, we as a committee had the responsibility to submit a report. I have read contradictory newspaper reports. But I’m saying authoritatively, as a member who participated in the meetings, that Owoseni was unanimously endorsed by those who were present and by those who joined virtually on Zoom.

So that contributed to my resignation from the Advisory Council.  Because if we could come in, sit down for almost two days, do something, and at the end of the day, the final decision is that of the governor and our effort did not see the light of the day, that was why I abandoned it.  Let me add that some governors are beginning to add things that are strange to the practice of democracy these days. Democracy, as we know, and as it is practiced worldwide, I don’t think it is normal for a sitting governor to announce publicly that he has a preferred candidate. Two governors, the governor of Nasarawa and that of Oyo State brought that up in our political lexicon in the current political situation. For us to get the best in politics, we should provide a level-playing ground for all aspirants to be tested. And at the end of the day, an aspirant who emerges the candidate is bound to have the followership and everybody within thestate will key in to such a thing. But what we have is the reverse.  

You referred to Governor Makinde as your friend and brother. He is contesting to be president of Nigeria. Will you vote for him?

No.

And why would that be so?

 Well, when he wanted to be governor, and he has acknowledged this severally, he came to me, we discussed, and I was convinced. And he said it at my 60th birthday lecture at UI. From the moment I said yes, there was no looking back. There was a time I had an interview with some journalists when it was rumoured that he wanted to be the President of Nigeria, I cautioned then that he knew what to do. And not only that, I believed it was a thing he should discuss or maybe discussed with people close to him, but I was never part of such a discussion. So, why would I key into an agenda that I am unaware of?

And the same thing happened to the man he is supporting as governorship candidate. I have never met him. I was not part of the government of the late Senator Abiola Ajimobi. The responsibility and understanding I had with Makinde was for him to be elected as governor of Oyo and for him to do well in office. And it ends there.  

Your good friend and brother, Dotun Sanusi, has already declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election and Senator Sharafadeen Alli’s election as governor of Oyo State in 2027. Were you consulted?

 Yes. We are together. The first time Makinde contested election, we knocked Sanusi’s doors and he supported us without conditions. In 2023, when Makinde sought reelection, though Sanusi was initially reluctant, and he had a good basis to be reluctant because he gave all he had, as he normally does for elections, the only road leading to his resort, which the governor, on his own, promised to fix was left undone. The road is in bad shape as we speak. Though some people will claim that work had started, the pace it is being done is nothing to write home about. And then, Dotun Sanusi, on his own, has put in millions of naira through OYSTROMA to do that road. He partnered with OYSTROMA. And for the 2023 re-election of the governor, he connected over 20 communities to the national grid. 

That is why the first official function of Makinde, after winning the 2023 election, was the commissioning of the transformers Sanusi donated to the communities during the campaign. So, I am together with Dotun Sanusi. We consult, we collaborate, and we have made a lot of things work politically. So, I am with him.  

You are yet to formally declare for APC. What is happening?

Well, APC is an offshoot of the Alliance for Democracy. At a point in time, we had an internal crisis of two factions, the Akinfewa faction and the Baba Bisi Akande faction. Then I was close to Abdulkadri (then Chairman) because he ensured my re-election in 2003. So, I stayed with him. While working with Makinde, I was a member of AD, so, do I need to decamp from AD? Remember, I was never a card-carrying member of the PDP

So, we can say that you are progressing in progressivism. Is that so?

But my relationship with people is not based on political alliances. So, my tentacles and friends are all over APC. And the president is someone that is known to me. I have had the privilege of welcoming him in my house in 1998, after the D’Rovas AD primaries. He returned to my house before he went to his hotel. So, what I am saying is, I don’t need to make any public declaration about defection. I’ve remained a progressive since the start of the Fourth Republic.

Some people have said that the good works Makinde has done in Oyo could work against the APC in the January 16 and February 6 elections. Is that your reading as well?

I have made up my mind not to talk about the administration of Makinde concerning this coming election, but I make bold to say that each candidate, depending on his background and political party, will campaign, will speak to the people, and at the end of the day, the people’s opinion will determine who will win the election.

Dotun Sanusi is championing the campaign for President Tinubu in 2027 in Oyo. How sure is the president winning re-election and winning Oyo as he did in 2023?

 In 2023, President Bola Tinubu won Oyo and that was the first time the progressives would win the presidential election in the state. In 2027, the president is looking good because Pa Adebanjo, my respected leader of Afenifere, while he was alive, supported Peter Obi in 2023, for reasons of equity. He believed that the South-East had been denied the opportunity to govern Nigeria based on what happened during the Civil War. It still pervades the political scheme of things. And then, a lot of things happened in the 2023 election based on mutual understanding.

For example, President, Bola Tinubu, in no small measure too, assisted Governor Makinde in winning his re-election. I remember one of the gubernatorial candidates claimed he was thrown under the bus. What I’m trying to say is, I see the Yoruba people this time coming around to support their own. I will be working for the success of President Bola Tinubu in the elections. 

And I believe so many other people too. I listened attentively to an interview by a former governor of Lagos State, Raji Fasola, who was talking about flipping Lagos back. And I think with the Obafemi Quadri Hamzat going for election in Lagos, a lot of good things will happen. There was something that worked for Obi in the 2023 election.

The younger generation that doesn’t have the zeal anymore and the noise in the social media has waned. Because of the movement among the youths in 2023, most of our children across Yoruba land voted for Obi. But a lot of things have happened since then, but I believe they are now wiser. And that is why you don’t see that momentum again. It is no longer like a movement, which it was in 2023. So, I believe President Tinubu will have a resounding success at the polls in the South- West, and not only that the good infrastructural work he is undertaking will give him the votes across Nigeria.

So, we can say Tinubu’s re-election is almost a done deal?

I think he is looking good. And at the end of the day, he will succeed. Still, a lot must be done between now and the election time especially on the misconceptions regarding the removal of petrol subsidy and the promise of electricity. Nobody was talking about the caveat that was part of the statement on electricity. He said, “If I don’t provide electricity, don’t vote for me”. But there was a proviso there, that if there are good reasons. And I think with the performance in that industry now, and with the new man at the helms of affairs, and a lot of items that have been lying fallow at the Ports for 20 years, I believe I am in tandem with the Fashola’s views on that particular statement that the president made.

Do you see the 2027 governorship election in Oyo State as a two or three-horse race?

I know there are so many candidates in the race. I am projecting, as a political analyst, that there will be a coalition. And that coalition will turn it into a two-horse race. And whoever the coalition backs will most likely be the winner. From all available information, you can check out the role coalition played in 2019 and 2023. I am of the opinion and as an advocate of actualizing coalition, the coalition that worked in 2019, 2023, will still play a role in 2027, which ultimately will turn it into a two-horse race.

In 2023, a group was formed by you and some other stakeholders. It was called ‘Rescue Mission’. Are we likely going to see anything close this time?

At that time, somebody had to be rescued. And the mission succeeded in rescuing the person. But now, the aim is to rescue Oyo State and ensure that the state is on a path towards progress.

You said part of the reason you resigned from Makinde’s government was the way CP Fatai Owoseni (rtd) was treated. Now Owoseni has launched a group, Oyo Lagba Forum. Is that a political vehicle you are aware of?

 Well, talking about the CP, he is a fine gentleman, and an epitome of a disciplined police officer. I know so many young officers who are in the force today because of the way he conducted himself while in the police. Having said that, in the Advisory Council, I never personally pushed his candidacy. I was neutral, but a lot of powerful members of the council, for good reasons, implored members to support and recommend Owoseni. Some members reminded us of the agreement between the two dominant faiths, and the advantage he has, which politically, I believe, should not be permanent, but coming from Ibadan.

So, the Oyo Lagba Forum, I am part of it. I am an integral part of it, and I believe in the ideals, ethos, and norms of Oyo Lagba. It is a noble group and the emphasis of mentoring, which is absent in this part of the country, mentoring our young ones and having a lot of seminars, discussions, which I have been an advocate of through my annual birthday lectures. So, I am an integral part of Oyo Lagba. Though, at the initial stages, Owoseni is the face of Oyo Lagba. We wanted it like that. And with the respect that people have for him across the country, Oyo Lagba has been populated, and you cannot imagine how successful the membership has been.

So, I’m part and parcel, and fully involved in Oyo Lagba. Oyo Lagba will equally be playing a prominent role. We are already playing a role underground and when the time comes, or necessary resolutions have been passed, in tandem with the existing constitution of the group, pronouncements will be made very soon. 

Is it not getting late as the elections are coming so close?

Let me say this though I don’t have the authority to say it yet on behalf of Oyo Lagba, but I have an inkling that Oyo Lagba will be tending towards the noble and popular choice in Oyo State. I have a good feeling about that. I may not have their mandate yet, but the group, through some of the subsidiaries, are already putting up structures all over the places. So, time will tell.

Now, tell me, which candidate is the ‘noble and popular choice of Oyo State in 2027. I hope the people will understand this?

You can draw from the inference what I’ve been saying. I leave that to the progressives to deduce. I mean logical deductions.

Makinde has been campaigning seriously against President Bola Tinubu in the presidential race. Is there any hope for reconciliation?

Let me say clearly that Governor Seyi Makinde has a constitutional right, an inherent right, as enshrined in the Constitution, to contest for that highest position in this country. And we should equally recall that Governor Makinde, under the G5, worked closely, though, at the detriment of his own party.

The president equally reciprocated by supporting his re-election. And I think I listened to Governor Makinde in his last interview Arise TV. He has laid a pass. And that pass should be interpreted correctly. He said he would be willing to discuss with Minister Nyesom Wike.

title: Reps Committee members on FCT felicitate Hon Betara @ 60
description:
Members of the House of Representatives Committee on the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) have felicitated with their distinguished Chairman, Rt. Hon. Muktar Betara Aliyu, OON, as he marks his remarkable 60th birthday.
In a statement signed on Sunday by members of the Committee, the members joined fa
content:
Members of the House of Representatives Committee on the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) have felicitated with their distinguished Chairman, Rt. Hon. Muktar Betara Aliyu, OON, as he marks his remarkable 60th birthday.

In a statement signed on Sunday by members of the Committee, the members joined family, friends, associates and well-wishers in celebrating six decades of a life richly blessed, and in honouring a man whose leadership, courage, legislative ingenuity and commitment to public service continue to make a remarkable difference.

“As Chairman of our Committee, you have demonstrated exemplary leadership, uncommon dedication and an impressive capacity to build consensus, inspire confidence and deliver results.

Your commitment to the work of the Committee and the development of the Federal Capital Territory reflects your deep understanding of public service and the responsibility entrusted to you.”

“Your contributions to nation-building and your enduring commitment to the people of Biu, Bayo, Kwaya-Kusar and Shani Federal Constituency of Borno State have further distinguished your record of service.”

We are equally delighted to celebrate your well-deserved recognition as The Sun Newspaper’s House of Representatives Member of the Year, 2026.

This prestigious honour is a fitting recognition of your legislative contributions, outstanding leadership and the positive impact of your service.

At 60, you stand as an inspiring example of purposeful leadership, resilience and service with distinction.

We are proud to be associated with your leadership and privileged to serve alongside you.

They prayed Allah to grant him more wisdom, grace and renewed strength as he steps into a new decade of life

“As you step into this new decade, we pray that Almighty Allah grants you renewed strength, sound health, greater wisdom and abundant grace”

May the years ahead bring even greater accomplishments, fulfilment and opportunities to serve our nation and humanity.

Happy 60th Birthday, Distinguished Chairman! May your new chapter be even more rewarding and impactful.

Signed:
Members, House of Representatives Committee on the Federal Capital Territory (FCT)

title: We focus on things that matter to Edo; I’m ready to supervise execution of convicted kidnappers — Okpebholo
description:
By Ozioruva Aliu 



GOVERNOR Monday Okpebholo just celebrated his administration’s second year anniversary in Edo State. In this interview with some editors in his office in Benin-City, Okpebholo speaks about his administration’s commitment to good governance for the people and how he wants to leav
content:
By Ozioruva Aliu 

GOVERNOR Monday Okpebholo just celebrated his administration’s second year anniversary in Edo State. In this interview with some editors in his office in Benin-City, Okpebholo speaks about his administration’s commitment to good governance for the people and how he wants to leave the state among other issues.

How do you assess your administration so far?

Construction is ongoing all over the state. Road construction is ongoing. Schools are being constructed. Also construction is ongoing in the primary healthcare area, we are also doing marvelously well in that sector. There are many areas that have been neglected in the past where you can’t even remember that roads ever existed in some of these places but we are working there. I can remember vividly that when you were coming from Abuja, from Auchi, then Ewu to Ekpoma, that road was completely washed off. I spoke to the Minister of Works to please allow me do this work so that I could be reimbursed. He approved it and talked to Mr. President and Mr. President agreed that I should do it and then forward the bill, we are already on that road. I really don’t talk much because I know I am saving my energy to work. For me, talking is not the business, working is the business.

So I prefer doing the job than talking so that when you come you see. When they are crying, shouting on social media, it doesn’t bother me because the people that live in those areas know that work is ongoing. We are also working in the villages because there are also human beings there and they also contribute to the economy. If they don’t go to the farm, where will you see food to eat and when you don’t eat, there will be hostility. That is the truth and that is why I feel that everybody should be carried along. There are villages that you never think of, I will just go there and do my work. I don’t need any politician to lobby me. I don’t need any influencer to lobby me, all I need to do is just to do the will and the wish of the people.

Is it the policy of the state government now that your roads will be concrete pavement?

We are not only just doing the concrete pavement, one of the reasons we are doing it is because of the swampy nature of many of our areas. We are in the rainforest zone and we need to sustain the roads. We have carefully studied to see that without concrete pavement, we will have problems within a short time. We are preparing for the future so that by the time when this government leaves, the next government will come and concentrate on other areas so that development will spread.

Look, we are not only working on infrastructure, we are also working on security. We are trying to make Edo very safe, safer than we met it. When we came in, within a week I recorded about 11 people dead not in an accident, somebody will get into a shop and kill the person there, somebody will just see someone on the road and shoot him. Why? The killers were cultists. I remember when the BBC guys came here and asked: Do you fear them? I said “I don’t fear because I am working for the people and I want to save Edo people”.

Today, you can hardly hear somebody die as a result of cult issues because we took a stiff measure that when you kill, we go to your family house or your personal house or wherever you live, whether you left your hotel to that place, I will demolish that hotel. If you leave your father’s house to that place to kill, I will demolish your father’s house. So these are stiff measures we have taken that are really working for us and, to be honest with you, if not that we have done that, maybe you won’t be able to stay in Benin for two nights.

Today nightlife is back, business is booming at night, even supermarkets are beginning to open at night; in the next few weeks, it will be safer such that everywhere, at every corner of the state, there will be the police to watch everyone. They will be equipped even with motorbikes so that when somebody thinks he can run, then they will follow the person. Whether you take a bush path, they will follow you up. So we are prepared to secure the city. We are prepared to secure the state.

Are you ready for state police?

Yes, we are prepared. We were one of the first states to pass the bill; when others were talking, we said no, it is working for us and, right now, to be honest with you, even with our vigilantes, we already have state police because it is working for us. Edo is safe.

Remember there was this kidnapping that happened and within 24 hours which has never happened in Nigeria, we got the guys, so that is it. We are even prepared to go to other states when they take any of our citizens. We did it in Kogi, then something happened in Ogun, I called the governor, I said, “Please, I don’t want my person to stay with this kidnapper for more than five days”, and, as God would have it, he was able to get them out within a short time. So somebody has to be prudent with everything.

How are you managing the burden of debt servicing versus project implementation in the state?

Many times when I say I am rooting for Mr. President’s 2.5 million votes, people wonder why I am saying this. It is because of the evidence of what we are seeing today. The FAAC allocation has increased and our own internally generated revenue has also increased. So what we are doing is prudent spending. We focus on things that matter to the people and we are not interested in ourselves, so what matters to the people is what we spend money on.

Is there any plan to float an airline considering the traffic coming in and out of the state?

We are already on it. If you look at the newspapers a few days ago, there was widespread publication on Edo Air; so, very soon, you will see it.

There is the challenge of gully erosion in several places in the state. What is your government doing about this?

We have actually set up an ecological agency to handle such cases. We have to do our best to see who will secure our place for the teachers.

You recently employed some teachers, but there is still shortage of teachers in several schools. What are you doing about this?

We are still going to hire more teachers to be honest with you, because when we were growing up, if there were no teachers, we wouldn’t be where we are today. So, the education for the children is very key and that is one of the reasons when I came in I was so interested to see that we fixed our educational system.

There was EdoBEST but it was EdoBEST for Obaseki and not for Edo people. That is the truth and they just used that to take away Edo money because when I looked at the system called EdoBEST based on what I saw, it was just like a tablet and, first of all, before you could even use the tablet, there should be internet which is 3 or 4 5G but maybe the children were just buying little airtime and load on their phones to operate it. And the curriculum they were using was actually not our own curriculum. It was Kenya and I frowned at it and so I stopped it and some governors that were convinced to do it but didn’t know what it was all about now got in touch with me and asked me how I got out of it. In Edo, we are concentrating on a school access programme and, for me, that is the way to go because, first of all, you need classrooms for the children. They should have at least water in school, they should have toilets and they should also have teachers.

So once you have all these on ground children want to go there. Now in Edo State, many children don’t want to go to private schools, they want to come into government schools because the basic amenities for them are being provided and teachers are also there.

What is the situation of those recently sentenced to death for kidnapping?

I pray our brothers are not involved in kidnapping because I will sign the death warrant, even if it is my father, I will sign it. The truth is this, we just have to get some bad elements out of the system for the system to stand, and these people have been killing people. Just look at the way they were pushing that woman that day, supposing she died? Because of fear, people have gone through trauma.

Even our chief judge, if you see him, one of his fingers was cut off by kidnappers. I am just waiting, but a few days ago I asked my Attorney General “what happened? I am waiting for the paper”, and he said no, that they have appealed. We still follow them up on the appeal, we won’t just leave them to go like that, we’ll get to wherever they stop, we’ll take them from there, we will not spare anybody. If I see this paper today now I will sign it and I will even supervise the killing.

What are your plans to take the state from subsistence farming considering its potentials and your plans for the health sector?

 I remember when I met Mr. President in France, I was showing him in my phone what we have done with the primary health care, and he was so happy and very thankful to God for the time that we have stayed in office and what we have done in terms of health care. Apart from rebuilding the health care system, we are also providing free treatment for patients especially on malaria.

We are also doing a lot in the area of secondary healthcare, trying to source for equipment and build more facilities. I prefer practical governance. That is why when I came, I told the people I was going to provide them with practical governance which is what you are seeing. We have completed over 82 primary health care centres across local government areas, across all the communities. In agriculture, naturally Edo State is a home for food. Apart from the mechanization equipment that we are providing, we are also encouraging the people to go into farming.

The Commissioner for Agriculture yesterday sent me a design on producing our own rice. We have very big farms in Edo North and Edo Central. We have rice farm, we have corn farm, we have cassava farm, our rice farm is over 57 acres, we’re expanding, the corn farm to about 400 acres. So we are doing well in terms of agriculture. I am not talking about the private sector people who are coming in every day to ask for land for farming and they are doing well too. Presco is here, Okomu is there and there are many other private companies. We are also supporting our farmers.

What are you doing to make the local governments replicate what you are doing in the state in their localities?

 The first day I met Mr. President, he told me about local governments and he was so particular about them. He said that local government is the closest to the grassroots, which I believe is true. I can tell you that since I came into office, I have never had any JAC meeting with local governments, and I have never sent my Commissioner for Finance or anybody to tell them “Look, I need this money from you, let’s do this joint project together”. No, it has never happened. Ask any of the local government chairmen.

When we came in, they were all PDP, so you can ask the opposition whether we have done that. I have not done that and I don’t intend to touch their money. They are doing very well. Do you know that they task themselves? They build and renovate schools, even primary health centers across the 18 local governments and they are paying salaries. They are not owing anybody. So they are also doing other things. Like a few months ago, I commissioned earth moving equipment. So they are introducing maintenance agencies back to local governments. To me it is key. It reduces spending, they can also be focused. They can call their own maintenance agencies to where they are needed to work. The day I was sworn into office, the first thing that came to my mind was that I realised that out of four years a day is gone. So there is no time to waste. That is why you see what we are doing and we continue to do it. We are hungry to work.

In the face of all that you are doing, how do you feel when you go to bed for the day?

I feel satisfied that I have done my best and I just know that this is a task that I have to carry and I have to fulfill my promise to the people. When I went out to campaign to the people and tell them, “Look, when I win, I will do this”, they thought “when you win, you turn your back to them”. But I don’t know how I will feel turning my back at them.

Sometimes when I go around the city and they start giving me names like Okpe’s Baby, I feel like crying because I think I don’t deserve it; after all, I am using Edo money to work for them, it is the taxpayer’s money.

How were you able to navigate your administration especially considering your claim that your predecessor did not give you any hand over note?

First of all, let me tell you that winning an election is to me a privilege from God and also the people were expecting so much from me because of the trust they have reposed in me. I asked for the job. And my goal is to do the job. So whatever I am doing, I am here to serve. I am not here just because I want to be a fine boy. No, I want to serve the people. And that is my aim and that is my goal. I think it will be more honourable to me that when I leave government, I should be remembered for the things I did and not the amount of money I have.

When I was growing up, I kept hearing about Professor Ambrose Alli, now that I have grown up, I still see Alli’s sticker on vehicles. It is not Alli that printed those stickers but his fans; so, these are the things I want to be remembered for. By the time I am no longer in this world, people should still remember me and also put my sticker somewhere. 

Vanguard News

The post We focus on things that matter to Edo; I’m ready to supervise execution of convicted kidnappers — Okpebholo appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Group hails Nuhu Ribadu at 66, commends strategic coordination of Nigeria’s counter-terrorism effort
description:
The Citizens’ Safety & Security Network (CSSN) has congratulated Mallam Nuhu Ribadu on his 66th birthday, describing his stewardship as National Security Adviser as a defining period in Nigeria’s renewed campaign against terrorism, insurgency, and banditry.
In a statement issued by its Convener, Arc
content:
The Citizens’ Safety & Security Network (CSSN) has congratulated Mallam Nuhu Ribadu on his 66th birthday, describing his stewardship as National Security Adviser as a defining period in Nigeria’s renewed campaign against terrorism, insurgency, and banditry.

In a statement issued by its Convener, Arc. Timothy Danladi Usman, the group noted that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s appointment of Ribadu in 2023 marked a deliberate departure from the longstanding tradition of reserving the Office of the National Security Adviser almost exclusively for retired senior military officers.

The decision, CSSN said, reflected a strategic vision to bring intelligence expertise, policing experience, and economic-crime-fighting acumen to the apex of Nigeria’s security architecture at a time when terrorists and bandits increasingly relied on illicit funding, logistics networks, and cross-border alliances.

According to the statement, the past three years have witnessed a profound shift characterised by intelligence-driven precision, improved inter-agency harmony, deliberate disruption of criminal financing, and the pragmatic restoration of international partnerships.

The results, CSSN observed, include the neutralisation of thousands of terrorists and bandit elements, the elimination or capture of high-value leaders across multiple states, the near-decimation of large-scale crude oil theft in the Niger Delta, and a reinvigorated Nigeria–United States security partnership that has delivered significant operational gains.

The group highlighted several high-impact successes under Ribadu’s coordination. In May 2026, a precision joint operation with the United States Africa Command in the Lake Chad Basin neutralised Abu-Bilal al-Minuki (also known as Abu-Mainok), described as the global second-in-command and director of operations for ISIS.

In the Northwest, security forces systematically degraded bandit networks that had terrorised Zamfara, Katsina, Sokoto, and Kaduna States.

Notable figures eliminated include Kachalla Halilu Sububu (also referred to as Halilu Buzu) in a targeted operation in September 2024; Alti, the so-called “TikTok bandit commander,” in early 2026; Dan Karami in a joint military operation in April 2025; and multiple other Kachalla warlords and lieutenants whose camps in Shinkafi, Isa, and surrounding areas of Zamfara were dismantled in coordinated raids.

In the Northeast, CSSN noted continued degradation of ISWAP and residual Boko Haram networks, with senior commanders and hundreds of fighters neutralised in Borno and Yobe States.

Overall, public reports indicate that well over 13,000 terrorists, insurgents, and associated criminal elements have been neutralised since the new security strategy took firm root.

Perhaps the most transformative contribution, the group stated, has been the deliberate fostering of synergy across Nigeria’s security and intelligence agencies.

For years, inter-agency rivalry and siloed operations had produced duplicated efforts, intelligence hoarding, and, in some cases, botched missions.

Under the Office of the National Security Adviser, the Armed Forces, Nigeria Police Force, Department of State Services, National Intelligence Agency, and other stakeholders now operate with greater seamlessness through joint planning cells, shared intelligence platforms, and unified command structures.

The result, CSSN said, has been faster, better-informed, and more decisive operations.

Drawing on his tenure as pioneer Chairman of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission and his background as a police intelligence officer,

Ribadu has also applied forensic financial investigation techniques to disrupt the economic lifelines of terrorist and bandit groups. Extortion, kidnapping-for-ransom, illegal mining, and arms trafficking have been targeted through strengthened collaboration with financial regulators and international partners, complicating weapons procurement and eroding the incentive structures that once sustained prolonged violence.

On the diplomatic front, the group commended Ribadu’s low-key yet professional engagement with American officials, which helped rebuild trust after early concerns about the trajectory of Nigeria–United States relations.

This renewed partnership has already produced concrete dividends, most visibly in the May 2026 elimination of the senior ISIS figure in the Lake Chad region.

Beyond the traditional theatres of insurgency and banditry, CSSN pointed to decisive gains in the Niger Delta. Working with the military, specialised security contractors including Tantita Security Services, and relevant government agencies, the campaign against crude oil theft and illegal refining has reduced theft from levels that once exceeded 100,000 barrels per day to as low as 5,000–9,600 barrels per day in some periods.

This has contributed directly to the rebound in Nigeria’s crude oil production, which has climbed above 1.7 million barrels per day—the highest levels recorded in years—while restoring relative peace that enables communities and legitimate businesses to benefit from increased output.

The group commended President Tinubu for the courage and foresight to entrust security coordination to Mallam Nuhu Ribadu on the basis of results-oriented thinking rather than tradition.

It equally recognised Ribadu for his professional humility, tireless work ethic, and leadership style that combines intelligence expertise, financial acumen, diplomatic skill, and insistence on inter-agency unity.

While celebrating the substantial gains of the past three years, the group cautioned against complacency. Remnants of terrorist networks, surviving bandit groups, and emerging threats require sustained pressure so that every geopolitical zone—Northeast, Northwest, North-Central, Southwest, South-South, and Southeast—ultimately enjoys the same measure of security and normalcy that hard-won progress has begun to restore in key areas.

“Mallam Nuhu Ribadu must continue to build on these foundations by deepening intelligence capabilities, further strengthening inter-agency fusion, expanding regional and international cooperation, and ensuring that no part of Nigeria remains a sanctuary for terror or criminality,” the statement said.

On the occasion of his 66th birthday, the Citizens’ Safety & Security Network prays that God Almighty will grant Mallam Nuhu Ribadu many more years of sound health, wisdom, and strength in the service of God and country.

The group enjoins him to remain steadfast and upright in the discharge of his duties, and never to depart from the just path, integrity, competence, and love for the people that have defined his career and public service life.

Reaffirming its commitment, CSSN pledged continued support to the Office of the National Security Adviser in the collective effort to eradicate insurgency and restore lasting safety across the country.

Three years on, the group concluded, the trajectory is positive. With sustained focus, unity of purpose, and the support of all Nigerians, the vision of a Nigeria where every citizen can live, work, and travel in safety is increasingly within reach.

title: 2026 licensing round: How to bid for FG’s 40 oil, gas blocks
description:
The Federal Government has opened applications for its 2026 oil and gas licensing round, offering 40 petroleum blocks to companies interested in investing in Nigeria’s upstream petroleum sector.
The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission opened the registration portal on November 20, 2026
content:
The Federal Government has opened applications for its 2026 oil and gas licensing round, offering 40 petroleum blocks to companies interested in investing in Nigeria’s upstream petroleum sector.

The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission opened the registration portal on November 20, 2026, with interested companies given until January 15, 2027, to complete their registration and prequalification processes.

The 40 blocks are spread across three categories, comprising 17 onshore blocks, 14 shallow water blocks and nine deep offshore blocks.

The commission disclosed this in a statement issued by its Head of Corporate Communications and Media, Eniola Akinkuotu, on Saturday, urging prospective investors to visit the portal to access the full list of available blocks, bidding guidelines and frequently asked questions.

The statement read, “The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission wishes to inform the general public that the 2026 licensing round portal is now live. On offer are 40 oil and gas blocks across three terrains. The blocks are grouped as follows: Onshore (17), shallow water (14) and deep offshore (9). Interested bidders are urged to visit the site to view the full list of the 40 blocks, as well as the guidelines and frequently asked questions.”

According to the NUPRC, the licensing round will be conducted in five stages, beginning with registration and prequalification, followed by access to data, submission of technical and commercial bids, technical evaluation and a commercial conference.

According to the commission, the licensing round was first announced by its Chief Executive, Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, on October 6, 2026, following approval by President Bola Tinubu, who is also the Minister of Petroleum Resources.

How to apply for the oil and gas blocks

According to the NUPRC’s 2026 Licensing Round Guidelines and Frequently Asked Questions, applications are to be completed electronically through the official licensing round portal at br2026.nuprc.gov.ng.

Here are the steps interested companies are expected to follow.

1. Visit the official portal

Interested companies should visit the NUPRC’s licensing round portal at br2026.nuprc.gov.ng.

The website contains the full list of available blocks, bidding guidelines, frequently asked questions, prequalification criteria, maps and other relevant documents.

Applicants are advised to study the information provided before beginning the registration process.

2. Create an account and register

Companies seeking to participate must create an account on the portal and complete the electronic registration process.

Applicants are required to provide a valid work email address for verification and submit their corporate details, including their country of incorporation, registration number and address.

The registration process also requires companies to indicate whether they are applying independently or as part of a consortium.

3. Pay the registration fee

According to the NUPRC’s guidelines, applicants are required to pay a non-refundable registration fee of $`10,000.

The payment details are contained in Schedule F of the licensing round guidelines. The commission must receive value for the payment by the application deadline.

Companies are advised to follow the payment instructions on the portal and ensure that the transaction is completed early enough to avoid missing the deadline.

4. Upload the required documents

After registration, applicants must upload the documents required for prequalification.

The NUPRC’s requirements cover legal and corporate information, technical experience, financial capacity, and health, safety and environmental compliance.

For legal and corporate requirements, companies are expected to provide documents such as their certificate of incorporation, particulars of shareholders and directors, memorandum and articles of association, organisational chart and beneficial ownership declaration.

The beneficial ownership declaration must cover persons with at least five per cent control or interest in the company. Nigerian companies are also required to provide a letter of good standing from the Corporate Affairs Commission and valid tax clearance certificates covering the preceding three years or the period since incorporation.

For technical prequalification, applicants must demonstrate experience relevant to the terrain or category of block they intend to bid for.

Companies that do not independently possess the required experience may rely on a partnership, technical services agreement or support from a parent company, provided the relevant agreements and supporting documents are submitted.

For financial prequalification, applicants are expected to provide audited financial statements for the last three years, bank letters showing available funds or credit facilities, records of capital expenditure, or binding commitments for equity or financing.

The commission will assess whether applicants have the financial capacity to meet the minimum work programme and other financial obligations associated with the blocks.

Companies must also provide their health, safety and environmental policies and management system documents, as well as records of major accidents or enforcement actions within the preceding five years.

5. Apply as a consortium where necessary

Companies that do not independently meet all the requirements may participate through a consortium, subject to the conditions set out in the licensing guidelines.

A consortium must have at least two members and submit a consortium agreement identifying the lead member, the roles of participating companies and their respective interests.

The designated operator must hold at least a 30 per cent participating interest.

Each consortium member must satisfy the applicable legal requirements, while the operator is expected to meet the technical, financial and health, safety and environmental requirements.

6. Submit the application for prequalification

After completing the registration and uploading the required documents, companies must submit their applications through the portal before the deadline.

Applicants are advised to check their submissions carefully because applications cannot be changed after submission.

The commission will review the applications to determine whether the companies meet the requirements for participation in the licensing round.

According to the published timetable, the evaluation of registration documents is scheduled to take place between January 18 and February 1, 2027, with notifications to prequalified applicants expected on February 1.

Only companies that meet the prequalification requirements will proceed to the subsequent stages of the licensing exercise.

7. Access data on the available blocks

Companies that successfully pass prequalification will proceed to the data access stage.

At this stage, applicants are expected to obtain geological, seismic, well and other technical information needed to assess the blocks they intend to bid for.

According to the guidelines, applicants are required to obtain relevant data through the National Data Repository and accredited vendors, with evidence of purchase to be submitted as required.

Applicants seeking physical access to the data room are required to execute a confidentiality agreement. The guidelines also provide for a data prying fee of `$10,000 per session per block.

8. Submit technical and commercial bids

After reviewing the available data, prequalified companies can prepare and submit their technical and commercial bids.

The technical proposal is expected to contain the company’s work programme, assessment of the block’s exploration potential and proposed development concept.

Applicants must also demonstrate their capacity to undertake the proposed exploration and development activities in line with the commission’s requirements.

The bid submission stage is scheduled to run from February 2 to April 15, 2027.

A non-refundable bid application fee of $`25,000 is required for each bid. Applicants must also provide a bid guarantee in the form of a bank guarantee equivalent to five per cent of the signature bonus offered.

The guidelines limit each applicant to a maximum of two blocks, including interests held through affiliates and consortium arrangements.

9. Undergo technical evaluation

Following the submission of bids, the commission will assess the technical proposals to determine whether applicants meet the requirements for the blocks they seek to acquire.

The technical bid evaluation is scheduled to take place between April 16 and April 30, 2027.

The commission is expected to notify qualified companies on May 1, 2027, ahead of the commercial bid conference.

10. Participate in the commercial bid conference

The final bidding stage is the commercial bid conference, scheduled for May 7, 2027.

At this stage, technically qualified bidders will participate in the commercial process for the blocks.

Successful bidders will be announced alongside reserve bidders and will proceed towards the award of the relevant Petroleum Prospecting Licences, subject to the fulfilment of post-award conditions.

According to the guidelines, signature bonuses may range from $3m to $7m per block, depending on the asset. Successful bidders are required to pay the applicable signature bonus in full in US dollars before the grant of the licence.

Important dates and fees

The NUPRC’s 2026 licensing round has the following key dates and financial requirements:

Portal opening and registration: November 20, 2026.

Pre-bid conference: December 16, 2026, in Lagos.

Registration deadline: January 15, 2027, at 4:30pm WAT.

Evaluation of registration documents: January 18 to February 1, 2027.

Notification of prequalified applicants: February 1, 2027.

Data access, evaluation and bid submission: February 2 to April 15, 2027.

Technical bid evaluation: April 16 to April 30, 2027.

Notification of qualified companies: May 1, 2027.

Commercial bid conference: May 7, 2027.

Registration fee: `$10,000, non-refundable.

Bid application fee: $`25,000 per bid, non-refundable.

Physical data room access fee: `$10,000 per session per block.

Bid guarantee: Five per cent of the offered signature bonus.

Signature bonus: 7m per block.

The commission advised prospective investors to consult the full licensing round guidelines, frequently asked questions and prequalification criteria on its official portal, noting that the documents contain the detailed requirements governing the exercise.

The licensing round comes as Nigeria seeks to increase crude oil and gas production, attract investment into its petroleum industry and improve the country’s competitiveness in the global energy market.

It also follows the 2025 oil and gas licensing exercise, which offered 50 blocks and attracted interest from 143 companies. The exercise recorded 200 bids, with 31 companies emerging as successful bidders for 37 blocks, while 13 blocks did not receive bids.

The post 2026 licensing round: How to bid for FG’s 40 oil, gas blocks appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
