title: Why construction could become Africa’s key technology, investment opportunity
description:
By Jimoh Razaq



For years, Africa’s technology ecosystem has concentrated much of its entrepreneurial energy, investment capital and innovation around fintech, e-commerce, mobility, telecommunications and entertainment. These sectors have produced remarkable companies, attracted international inve
content:
By Jimoh Razaq

For years, Africa’s technology ecosystem has concentrated much of its entrepreneurial energy, investment capital and innovation around fintech, e-commerce, mobility, telecommunications and entertainment. These sectors have produced remarkable companies, attracted international investment and demonstrated that African businesses can build technology products capable of scaling across borders.

But there is another industry with enormous economic significance, deeply entrenched inefficiencies and a largely untapped opportunity for technological transformation: construction.

It is an industry that builds our homes, roads, hospitals, schools, factories, power infrastructure and cities. It employs millions of people, supports extensive manufacturing and distribution networks, moves significant volumes of capital and sits at the centre of economic development.

Yet much of its operational infrastructure remains fragmented, manual and inefficient.

While technology has transformed how people transfer money, order food, book transportation and access entertainment, the processes through which buildings and infrastructure are planned, financed, procured and delivered remain remarkably difficult to coordinate.

This is not simply an operational inconvenience. It is a massive economic opportunity.

The next generation of transformative African technology companies may emerge from solving the problems of the industries that physically build Africa.

The industry technology has overlooked

Construction is one of the world’s largest economic sectors. Global construction output was approximately $13 trillion in 2023, with projections suggesting it could reach $22 trillion by 2040.

Yet its productivity performance remains disappointing.

McKinsey’s 2024 research found that global construction productivity grew by approximately 0.4 per cent annually between 2000 and 2022, compared with around 2 per cent for the broader economy. This represents a productivity improvement of only about 10 per cent over more than two decades.

The implications are significant.

Projects experience delays. Budgets become unreliable. Material procurement remains fragmented. Labour productivity is difficult to measure. Project information is scattered across emails, spreadsheets, paper documents and messaging applications. Developers, contractors, consultants, suppliers, artisans and investors often operate without a shared information environment.

These challenges are particularly visible in emerging markets, where informal transactions, inconsistent data, financing constraints and infrastructure limitations compound existing industry inefficiencies.

Africa’s infrastructure ambitions make the opportunity even more important. The OECD’s Africa’s Development Dynamics 2025 estimates that investing approximately $155 billion annually in infrastructure could significantly accelerate the continent’s economic growth.

The question is not whether Africa needs more construction. It clearly does.

The question is whether the industry can deliver the volume of housing, infrastructure and commercial development required without fundamentally changing how it operates.

That is where technology founders should pay attention.

Construction is not just an engineering industry. It is a technology ecosystem waiting to be connected.

One of the biggest misconceptions about construction technology is that innovation is primarily about drones, robotics, 3D printing or sophisticated building design software.

Those technologies matter, but they represent only a fraction of the opportunity.

Construction is also an industry of financial transactions, procurement networks, logistics, labour coordination, data management, risk assessment, asset management and complex workflows.

Every construction project creates multiple interconnected problems that technology can solve.

Consider what happens when someone decides to build a house.

They need to verify land ownership, develop architectural and structural drawings, estimate project costs, secure financing, identify qualified professionals, procure materials, engage artisans, manage construction activities, monitor expenditure and verify completion.

Each stage involves multiple stakeholders, financial commitments and operational decisions.

In many African markets, these activities are still managed through disconnected systems.

There is an opportunity to build technology infrastructure that connects this entire process.

Opportunities that could redefine construction in Africa

AI-powered construction cost intelligence: One of the most persistent problems in construction is inaccurate project costing. Material prices fluctuate. Labour rates differ by location. Transportation costs change. Exchange-rate movements affect imported materials, while poor historical data makes reliable forecasting difficult.

An intelligent construction cost engine could combine material prices, labour rates, geographical information, historical project costs and market conditions to generate more reliable estimates.

Imagine a developer being able to estimate the cost of constructing a residential building in Lagos, Abuja, Ibadan or Accra using current market information rather than relying entirely on outdated rate books.

This is an opportunity for AI engineers, data scientists and construction professionals to build genuinely useful products.

Digital construction material marketplaces: The procurement of cement, reinforcement steel, roofing materials, electrical fittings, plumbing components and other construction products remains highly fragmented. Buyers frequently depend on personal contacts, multiple quotations and informal supplier relationships.

A verified digital marketplace could connect manufacturers, distributors, suppliers, contractors and developers through transparent pricing, product verification, digital payments and delivery tracking.

Beyond convenience, such a platform could improve price discovery, reduce procurement fraud and create a more accountable supply chain.

Save-To-Build financial technology: Millions of people want to build houses but cannot finance the entire project at once. Traditional construction financing is often inaccessible, while informal savings arrangements do not necessarily provide the structure or safeguards required for long-term building projects.

A Save-To-Build platform could allow individuals to accumulate funds towards clearly defined construction milestones. For example, a customer could save towards land documentation, architectural design, foundation construction, roofing and finishing.

Funds could be released against verified milestones, supported by appropriate financial safeguards and partnerships with regulated financial institutions.

This creates an opportunity to connect personal finance, construction delivery and financial inclusion.

AI-powered site supervision and project intelligence: Construction sites generate enormous amounts of information, but much of it is not systematically captured or analysed. Artificial intelligence, computer vision and mobile technology could help monitor construction progress, identify deviations from approved designs, track material consumption, record labour attendance and flag potential safety issues.

A project owner could receive a digital site performance report without having to depend exclusively on periodic manual updates.

The goal is not to replace professional site supervision or engineering judgement. It is to equip professionals with better information to make faster and more informed decisions.

5. Skilled labour and artisan marketplaces

Africa’s construction industry depends heavily on skilled and semi-skilled workers, many of whom operate within informal employment networks. Finding reliable masons, electricians, plumbers, tilers, welders, carpenters and other artisans can be difficult.

A structured digital marketplace could provide verified profiles, skills assessments, ratings, work histories, location-based discovery and protected payment arrangements.

Such platforms could also create opportunities for professional training, certification and workforce development.

Technology can help formalise an important part of the construction economy without excluding the people who already work within it.

Digital property development and off-plan sales platforms: Property developers frequently sell units before construction is completed. However, buyers may struggle to obtain reliable information about construction progress, payment schedules, contractual obligations and project delivery.

A digital off-plan platform could provide verified developer profiles, interactive property models, payment tracking, digital contracts and construction progress updates.

This would improve transparency and help restore confidence in property development markets.

Modular and industrialised construction technology: Construction technology should not be limited to software. There is a significant opportunity in developing prefabricated building systems, modular housing components, standardised structural elements and rapid-assembly construction solutions.

Combining digital design, manufacturing automation and efficient project logistics could reduce construction time, material waste and repetitive site activities.

This is particularly relevant to affordable housing, student accommodation, healthcare facilities and standardised institutional buildings.

Construction logistics and material tracking: Materials and equipment move continuously between manufacturers, warehouses, suppliers, transport operators and construction sites. Poor coordination leads to delayed deliveries, unnecessary transportation costs, material losses and idle equipment.

Internet of Things technology, QR codes, GPS tracking and logistics management software could provide greater visibility across the supply chain.

Developers could know what has been ordered, what has been dispatched, what has arrived and what has actually been consumed on site.

Digital building approvals and regulatory platforms: Building approval processes can involve several agencies, professional submissions, inspections and compliance requirements. Technology could help digitise application processing, document verification, inspection scheduling, permit tracking and regulatory records.

A properly integrated platform would improve transparency, reduce administrative delays and make compliance easier to monitor.

Governments could also benefit from better urban development data and more efficient building control.

AI-powered construction education and workforce development: Africa cannot build the infrastructure it needs without a skilled construction workforce. There is an opportunity to develop digital learning platforms for artisans, technicians, junior engineers, quantity surveyors, project managers and other construction professionals.

Artificial intelligence could personalise learning, provide technical explanations in accessible language and support practical training.

Local language support, including Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo and Pidgin, could make technical education more accessible to workers who may not benefit from conventional English-language training alone.

Land intelligence and title verification: Land ownership and title verification remain significant challenges in many African property markets. Technology platforms could integrate land registry records, survey information, ownership documentation, encumbrance checks and geographic information systems.

Where government data access and legal frameworks permit, secure verification APIs could help professionals, developers, investors and financial institutions conduct more reliable due diligence.

This could reduce information asymmetry and improve confidence in property transactions.

Digital estate and infrastructure planning: Housing developments require more than individual buildings. They require roads, drainage, electricity, water supply, waste management and other essential infrastructure.

Digital planning tools could integrate land surveys, topographical data, engineering designs, utility networks and development requirements to support more efficient estate planning.

AI-assisted design could help professionals evaluate alternative layouts, estimate infrastructure costs and identify potential planning constraints.

Integrated construction collaboration platforms: Perhaps one of the most important opportunities is the creation of a shared digital workspace for the entire construction value chain. Architects, engineers, quantity surveyors, contractors, developers, suppliers and clients need to work with the same project information.

A centralised collaboration platform could connect drawings, revisions, bills of quantities, procurement, contracts, schedules, budgets, site reports, payments and project performance.

Think of it as the digital operating system for a construction project.

Rather than managing every activity through disconnected applications, stakeholders could operate within a coordinated environment.

Why this opportunity is bigger than another startup trend

There is a temptation to approach construction technology as another opportunity to build an application, raise venture capital and pursue rapid user acquisition. That would be a mistake.

Construction technology requires a deeper understanding of the industry. A product that works in a conventional consumer technology environment may fail on a construction site if it does not account for procurement practices, professional responsibilities, contractual relationships, payment structures, regulatory requirements and the realities of field operations.

The most successful founders will not necessarily be those who write the best code. They will be those who understand the problems deeply enough to build technology that people are willing to use repeatedly.

This requires collaboration between technology founders and construction professionals. Software engineers need to understand construction workflows. Construction professionals need to become more comfortable with data, automation and digital systems. Investors need to understand that some construction technology products require longer adoption cycles but can eventually become deeply embedded in the industry.

There is also a need to build for Africa’s realities rather than simply importing solutions designed for different markets. Products must account for fragmented supply chains, mobile-first users, varying levels of digital literacy, unreliable connectivity in some locations, local payment systems, regulatory differences and the informal economy. Technology must simplify the industry, not make it more complicated.

The investment opportunity: from individual applications to industry infrastructure

The most interesting opportunities may not necessarily be standalone applications. They may be the platforms that become essential infrastructure for how the industry operates.

A material marketplace that becomes the primary procurement channel for thousands of contractors. A financial technology platform that manages construction savings, project financing and milestone payments. A project management system that becomes the standard operating environment for developers and contractors. A labour marketplace that connects millions of skilled workers with verified opportunities. An AI-powered construction intelligence platform that becomes an essential tool for estimating, planning and monitoring projects.

Each of these businesses could develop substantial commercial value if it achieves product-market fit, trusted distribution and sustainable unit economics.

They also create opportunities for interconnected ecosystems. For example, a construction cost platform can connect to a material marketplace. The marketplace can connect to financing. Financing can connect to project monitoring. Project monitoring can connect to procurement and payment verification.

This is how technology can move beyond isolated applications and become an operating layer for an entire industry.

The role of governments and institutional investors

The transformation of construction cannot be left to startups alone. Governments control important parts of the enabling environment, including land administration, building regulations, public procurement, infrastructure investment and access to official records.

They should create opportunities for responsible technology companies to participate in digitising these systems. Public agencies can support interoperable data standards, transparent procurement processes, digital building approval systems and reliable property information infrastructure.

Financial institutions and institutional investors also have a role to play. Construction technology companies may require patient capital, industry partnerships and access to real project environments to validate their solutions.

Venture capital firms should look beyond the familiar consumer technology categories and examine businesses that improve productivity across construction, infrastructure and industrial supply chains.

The OECD’s infrastructure investment analysis makes clear that Africa’s development ambitions require substantial capital mobilisation. Technology will be essential in improving how that capital is translated into productive assets.

Africa needs builders who understand both code and concrete

I believe we are approaching an important moment in the evolution of African technology. The continent has demonstrated that it can develop financial technology platforms, digital marketplaces and innovative consumer products.

The next opportunity is to apply that same entrepreneurial energy to the industries that underpin economic development. Construction is one of them. The opportunity is not simply to digitise paperwork or replace manual processes with mobile applications. It is to redesign how projects are financed, planned, procured, executed and managed.

It is to make construction more transparent, more productive, more predictable and more accessible. It is to use technology to reduce waste, improve project delivery, expand access to housing and accelerate infrastructure development.

This is also the thinking behind what we are developing with Ladaar: a connected construction technology ecosystem bringing together construction finance, professional services, procurement, project intelligence and workflow automation.

But the opportunity extends far beyond one company or one platform. Africa needs many more innovators willing to understand this industry and build solutions around its real problems.

The next generation of technology leaders should look beyond the sectors that have already attracted the most attention. They should look at the industries where inefficiencies are deepest, where the economic stakes are highest and where technology can produce tangible improvements in people’s lives.

Africa does not just need more technology companies. It needs technology companies that can help build Africa.

The next great African technology opportunity may not be another application for transferring money, ordering food or booking a ride. It may be the technology that helps us build a million homes, deliver infrastructure more efficiently, connect construction professionals, finance projects responsibly and create better cities.

The future of African technology will not be written by code alone. It will also be built with concrete, steel, data and innovation. And it is time the technology ecosystem paid attention.

Razaq is a construction and project management professional

The post Why construction could become Africa’s key technology, investment opportunity appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Four govs attend Adeboye’s crusade in Delta
description:
Four state governors on Saturday attended the grand finale of the ninth edition of the Festival of Champions, an outdoor outreach programme organised by the Redeemed Christian Church of God.
The governors were Sheriff Oborevwori (Delta), Douye Diri (Bayelsa), Biodun Oyebanji (Ekiti) and Monday Okpeb
content:
Four state governors on Saturday attended the grand finale of the ninth edition of the Festival of Champions, an outdoor outreach programme organised by the Redeemed Christian Church of God.

The governors were Sheriff Oborevwori (Delta), Douye Diri (Bayelsa), Biodun Oyebanji (Ekiti) and Monday Okpebholo (Edo).

The event, held at the Sports Field of Urhobo College, Effurun, Uvwie Local Government Area of Delta State, featured an all-night prayer and praise session that lasted into the early hours of Saturday.

Other prominent attendees included the Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele; the Speaker of the Delta State House of Assembly and Chairman of the Conference of Speakers of State Legislatures of Nigeria, Emomotimi Guwor; the Ovie of Agbarha-Warri Kingdom, His Royal Majesty, Kingsley Orereh Igbi II; and Esther Tonlagha, wife of Niger Delta industrialist, Matthew Tonlagha.

The General Overseer of the RCCG, Pastor Enoch Adeboye, who led the prayer sessions, urged worshippers to put their confidence in God, predicting miraculous breakthroughs for many before the end of the year.

Quoting extensively from the Scriptures, Adeboye declared, “Before you enter the New Year, you would have started singing a new song; you would have started making greater progress.

“From now on, we shall be singing a new song of joy. I will encourage you, therefore, if you believe, that before we enter the New Year, every obstacle before you would have vanished.”

He added, “I have good news for someone here tonight. Before the end of the year, miracles are coming your way. You will laugh last over your misfortunes. Every evil force hindering your progress, you will never hear from them again. You will sing a new song. Just confess your sins and come to God.”

The prayer and praise session featured performances by Nigerian and international gospel artistes, including Nathaniel Bassey, Muyiwa Olarewaju, Micah Stampley, Dunsin Oyekan, Mercy Chinwo, Chioma Jesus, Moses Bliss, Beejay Sax, Adeyinka Alaseyori, Lilian Nneji, Bidemi Olaoba, Bukola Bekes, Greatman Takit, Sounds of Salem, Tope Praise and South Africa’s Joyous Celebration.

Speaking earlier, the Pastor-in-Charge of RCCG Champions Cathedral and Region 70, Pastor Emmanuel Emefienim, who convened the crusade, said the annual programme had grown in attendance, popularity and impact since its inception nine years ago.

He described the Festival of Champions as an interdenominational outdoor outreach programme that brings Christians together to praise God, adding that the RCCG was privileged to host the event.

The post Four govs attend Adeboye’s crusade in Delta appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: The future of automobile technology: Embracing AI for business growth in Nigeria
description:
By Moses Stowe



The growing importance of technological innovation, professional development and sustainable business growth in Nigeria’s automobile industry took centre stage at the 2026 Nigeria Automobile Technicians Association (NATA), Lagos State Council Day, where Intercontinental Distillers
content:
By Moses Stowe

The growing importance of technological innovation, professional development and sustainable business growth in Nigeria’s automobile industry took centre stage at the 2026 Nigeria Automobile Technicians Association (NATA), Lagos State Council Day, where Intercontinental Distillers Limited (IDL), makers of Action Bitters, participated in an initiative recognising and supporting the contributions of automobile technicians to the nation’s economy.

Held under the theme, “Harnessing Artificial Intelligence (AI) to Transform and Develop the Business of Auto Technicians in Nigeria,” this year’s celebration provided an important platform for industry stakeholders, automobile professionals, corporate organisations and association leaders to examine emerging opportunities in the automotive sector and the need to equip technicians with the knowledge, skills and resources required to remain competitive in an increasingly technology-driven industry.

A major highlight of IDL’s participation was its support for the empowerment of automobile technicians through the provision of automobile tools. The initiative underscored the importance of practical support in strengthening the capacity of technicians, improving their operational efficiency and helping them deliver better services to customers. Beyond the recognition of their professional contributions, the gesture reflected the importance of providing tangible resources that can support the growth and sustainability of small businesses within the automobile value chain.

Speaking on the significance of the occasion, Celestine Anyanwu, Brand Manager, Wine and Bitters, IDL, acknowledged the invaluable contributions of automobile technicians to the nation’s economic and industrial development. He noted that their expertise, dedication and entrepreneurial spirit remain essential to the effective functioning of the transportation and automobile sectors.

He emphasised the importance of initiatives that recognise the efforts of professionals whose daily activities contribute to keeping businesses, individuals and transportation systems running. According to him, supporting the NATA community through the provision of relevant automobile tools represents a meaningful contribution towards professional development, business improvement and the advancement of the automobile servicing industry.

He further acknowledged the relevance of this year’s theme, noting that Artificial Intelligence presents emerging opportunities for automobile technicians to improve diagnostic processes, embrace modern automotive technologies and develop more efficient approaches to business operations. He encouraged industry stakeholders to continue supporting platforms that promote innovation, practical empowerment and sustainable professional growth.

One of the major highlights of the event was the presentation of the grand prize, a complete set of automobile tool kits, to Kazeem Oladeji, one of the beneficiaries of the empowerment initiative.

Expressing his appreciation, Oladeji described the award as a significant boost to his profession and business, noting that access to the right tools is essential to delivering quality automobile services. He commended Action Bitters and Intercontinental Distillers Limited for recognising the efforts of automobile technicians and extending support beyond mere celebration to practical empowerment.

In the address of the Chairman of NATA, Lagos State Council, Morufu Egberongbe, described the celebration as a significant milestone in the association’s collective journey towards the growth, recognition, empowerment and professional development of automobile technicians across Lagos State and Nigeria.

He reaffirmed the association’s commitment to promoting professionalism, unity, excellence and sustainable business development among its members, who operate across different segments of the automotive value chain. These include auto mechanics, auto electricians, panel beaters, spray painters, vulcanisers, auto air-conditioning technicians, diagnostic specialists, spare parts dealers and other related professionals.

Egberongbe explained that the choice of this year’s theme reflected NATA’s determination to embrace innovation and adequately prepare its members for the future of the automotive industry. He noted that Artificial Intelligence and other emerging technologies are creating new possibilities for vehicle diagnostics, maintenance, customer service and business management, making continuous learning and adaptation increasingly important.

The NATA chairman also expressed appreciation to corporate partners, sponsors and exhibitors for recognising the importance of the automobile technician community and supporting initiatives that promote innovation, capacity development and business growth. He described their contributions as investments in the future of the automotive industry and the thousands of businesses sustained by the sector.

He equally acknowledged government institutions, industry leaders, association executives, the planning committee and other stakeholders whose contributions helped make the celebration a success.

For IDL, its participation in the 2026 NATA Lagos State Council Day provided an opportunity to recognise a professional community whose contributions extend beyond automobile repairs to entrepreneurship, employment generation, technical expertise and economic development.

The provision of automobile tools also highlighted an important dimension of corporate engagement: the need to support professional communities with resources that address practical business needs. For automobile technicians, access to appropriate tools is essential to improving service delivery, adapting to changing vehicle technologies and maintaining the confidence of customers.

As Nigeria’s automotive landscape continues to evolve, the integration of Artificial Intelligence, digital diagnostic systems and modern vehicle maintenance solutions will increasingly shape the industry’s future. Platforms such as the NATA Lagos State Council Day therefore remain important in encouraging collaboration, knowledge exchange and stronger partnerships between professional associations and corporate stakeholders.

Ultimately, the 2026 celebration reinforced a shared vision of an automobile industry built on technical competence, innovation, professional recognition and economic empowerment. Through its participation and support for the initiative, IDL joined other stakeholders in recognising the importance of strengthening the capabilities of automobile technicians and creating opportunities for the continued development of their businesses.

The message was clear: the future of Nigeria’s automobile industry depends not only on technological advancement but also on empowering the skilled professionals who make the sector work.

The post The future of automobile technology: Embracing AI for business growth in Nigeria  appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Oando’s rising fortunes: How Wale Tinubu is rewriting growth story
description:
By Adebayo Adeoye



Jubril Adewale Tinubu, CON,  is not one to be easily satisfied with yesterday’s accomplishments. For the Oando Group Chief  Executive, every milestone appears to present another opportunity to raise the bar, test new possibilities and push the boundaries of what an indigenous en
content:
By Adebayo Adeoye

Jubril Adewale Tinubu, CON, is not one to be easily satisfied with yesterday’s accomplishments. For the Oando Group Chief Executive, every milestone appears to present another opportunity to raise the bar, test new possibilities and push the boundaries of what an indigenous energy company can achieve. That restless ambition is once again finding expression in Oando’s improving fortunes.

At Oando, the story has never been one of an overnight success. Rather, it is a tale of calculated risks, corporate reinvention and an unwavering belief in the possibilities of indigenous enterprise. Over the years, Tinubu has remained at the centre of the company’s evolution, steering its affairs through difficult economic seasons, industry uncertainties and the complex demands of a rapidly changing energy landscape.

Today, the signs of another promising chapter are becoming increasingly visible, as the indigenous energy company continues to record encouraging improvements in its operations, strengthening its position in an industry where survival and relevance are often determined by the ability to anticipate change and respond decisively. For Tinubu, who has spent considerable years building Oando into a recognisable name in Africa’s energy industry, the latest developments represent more than a corporate milestone. They reflect an enduring ambition to build an indigenous institution capable of competing beyond Nigeria’s shores and holding its own among established players in the global energy market.

One of the most encouraging aspects of Oando’s recent performance is the improvement in its operational efficiency. The company has continued to strengthen its production capacity, improve asset utilisation and address some of the operational challenges that have historically confronted the oil and gas industry. Its improving production profile suggests that the investments and management decisions taken over time are beginning to yield meaningful results.

But beyond increased production, the company’s efforts to reduce operating costs and improve facility reliability have equally attracted attention. In an industry where operational disruptions can quickly erode profitability, efficiency remains a critical ingredient for sustainable growth. Oando’s renewed focus on operational discipline therefore speaks to a management philosophy that recognises the importance of building a business on solid foundations rather than merely pursuing expansion for its own sake.

Indeed, Tinubu’s corporate journey has been defined by an appetite for ambitious decisions. His leadership at Oando has seen the company navigate major transitions, expand its interests and deepen its participation in Nigeria’s energy value chain.

The acquisition of additional upstream assets further underscored his belief that indigenous companies should not remain spectators in an industry that has for decades been dominated by international oil companies.

That ambition, however, comes with its own demands. The acquisition and development of oil and gas assets require substantial capital, careful financial management and the ability to balance immediate obligations with long-term business objectives. Oando is not insulated from these pressures, particularly as it continues to manage the financial commitments associated with its expansion strategy.

Nevertheless, the company’s improving operating performance offers reasons for optimism. Its ability to generate cash from operations while maintaining investments in drilling and other production-related activities demonstrates a determination to sustain its growth trajectory. Equally important is the company’s continuing effort to strengthen its financial position and manage its borrowing obligations.

For Tinubu, the task is clearly not simply to preserve what has already been built but to ensure that Oando remains relevant in an industry undergoing profound transformation. The global conversation around energy security, cleaner energy sources and sustainable development is changing the rules of engagement. Indigenous energy companies must therefore demonstrate not only financial resilience but also the capacity to adapt to emerging realities.

This is where the Oando story becomes particularly interesting. Tinubu has consistently projected the ambition of an African entrepreneur who believes that local businesses can rise above structural limitations and compete on a much bigger stage. His approach has been characterised by bold corporate moves, strategic partnerships and an understanding that the future belongs to companies willing to evolve.

Yet, beyond the boardroom calculations and corporate announcements, there is also the question of legacy. Building a successful company is one thing; establishing an institution that can withstand changing leadership, economic cycles and industry disruptions is another. It is a challenge that every ambitious business leader must eventually confront.

For now, Oando appears determined to keep its place in the unfolding energy narrative. Its improving operational fortunes provide fresh momentum, while Tinubu’s leadership continues to attract attention as the company pursues its broader ambitions.

Clearly, the Oando story is far from finished. And if the current momentum is anything to go by, Wale Tinubu is not ready to take his foot off the accelerator. In the competitive race for relevance in Africa’s energy industry, he appears determined to ensure that Oando is not merely present at the table but has a voice in deciding where the industry goes.

Adeoye Adebayo writes in from Lagos.

The post Oando’s rising fortunes: How Wale Tinubu is rewriting growth story  appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: 2027: Imperative of Peter Mbah’s second term in Enugu
description:
By Willy Eya



Politics apart, Enugu State Governor, Dr Peter Mbah deserves a second term in office. That is not contestable. Certainly, the governor’s achievements since assumption of office in 2023 will campaign for him ahead of the 2027 general elections. One good turn, they say, deserves anothe
content:
By Willy Eya

Politics apart, Enugu State Governor, Dr Peter Mbah deserves a second term in office. That is not contestable. Certainly, the governor’s achievements since assumption of office in 2023 will campaign for him ahead of the 2027 general elections. One good turn, they say, deserves another.

Mbah came in as an accomplished technocrat determined to reshape the public sector using his private sector background.He approaches governance with a structured blueprint rather than the usual, impromptu trial-and-error tactics by regular Nigerian politicians.

Every step the governor takes is intentional, hence, he links infrastructure directly to economic growth. His idea for instance is that fixing roads or investing heavily in security isn’t just for safety but a targeted prerequisite to open up the state for tourism, agriculture, and private sector investments.

He deliberately avoided slow, conventional governance steps and pushed instead for immediate macro-level structural adjustments from Day One.Mbah’s strength lies in translating private-sector efficiency into public-sector execution.This quality is evidenced by his courage to dismantle slow legacy systems—such as implementing the fully digitized Enugu Geographic Information Service (ENGIS) to fast-track land administration and heavily relying on data to drive executive decisions.

Unlike career politicians who rely on political patronage, the governor is largely a corporate technocrat whose leadership is rooted in rigorous planning.

From inception after his inauguration, he was clear in his road-map to radically change the story of Enugu State. His first major challenge was to end the Monday Sit-at-Home disruptions. For years, the illegal “sit-at-home” orders crippled the economy of the Southeast and his immediate and uncompromising ban on the orders from his first week in office is frequently cited as a defining test of his leadership.Despite initial hiccups, the administration restored normal business and economic activities on Mondays and Enugu State is better for it today.

In his cabinet appointments, Mbah consciously shifted the political culture of Enugu State by actively recruiting top-tier professionals from academia and the global private sector. He believes in inclusive and merit-based governance, hence, prioritized competence over partisan rewards. For him, governance is a serious business of service delivery, thus, he established a culture of accountability across state ministries.

Knowing the importance of security to his set goals, he was quick to establish the Command and Control Centre which deployed modern surveillance and security infrastructure, including an ultramodern command and control center, to improve safety across the state.

His administration has focused on a multi-faceted development framework aimed at growing the state’s economy from $4.4 billion to $30 billion. For many observers including this writer, that was a tall dream considering that hitherto, Enugu was largely a civil service state. He has proved pundits wrong as internal updates reveal a stark upward trajectory in the state’s fiscal performance, rising from ₦26 billion in 2022 to ₦181 billion in 2024, reaching ₦460 billion in 2025, and carrying an estimated projection of ₦871 billion for the 2026 fiscal year.

So, the imperative of a second term for the governor, is strengthened by his administration’s documented performance, structural transformation and repositioning of the state since 2023. As the 2027 general elections approach, the voters would not forget the need to institutionalize ongoing economic reforms, finalize massive infrastructure projects, and sustain human capital developments that have redefined Enugu’s developmental trajectory.

Across the state including the rural areas, there are visible projects and evidence of the administration’s commitment to improve public services. Governor Mbah’s ambitious vision to expand Enugu State’s economy from $4.4 billion to $30 billion and his obvious dogged determination to reposition Enugu State are his unique selling points.

Part of the projects that would speak for Governor Mbah’s second term include 260 Smart Green Schools, 260 primary healthcare centres, an international hospital intended to reduce medical tourism and the establishment of Enugu Air which has already commenced international flights. The State’s fiscal architecture had undergone significant reform through revenue automation, reforms at the Enugu State Internal Revenue Service, improved financial management, the Treasury Single Account, enterprise resource planning and broader institutional restructuring.

The administration has also ensured the sustenance of investments in youth empowerment, women development, technology, skills acquisition, social protection, tourism, environmental sustainability and community development.

So,most critical observers agree that Enugu is on an aggressive path to development, and disrupting the upward momentum in 2027 would stall the state’s economic trajectory.

It is then preposterous to imagine that people of the state will abandon Governor Mbah for a gamble with the opposition forces in next governorship election.

Though opponents and paid social media activists point to economic hardships and taxes as issues in the coming election but objective and critical observers agree that the revolutionary reforms by the Enugu State government are laying a foundation for enduring progress and development of the state.

It is not surprising that the governor’s supporters have moved away from the traditional political culture of treating a second term as an automatic entitlement but readily flaunt a data-backed scorecard to justify governance continuity.

On September 6, 2026, Governor Mbah unveiled a compendium of more than 10,000 milestones recorded in the first term of his administration. Among others, the compendium records over 1,521 kilometres of constructed and reconstructed roads, over 7,000 classrooms, 260 Type-2 Primary Healthcare Centres, Enugu Air, the New Enugu Smart City, and the revamp of moribund assets.

In an official manifesto performance review presented on October 29, 2026, Governor Mbah had noted that a second term is vital to deepen ongoing structural reforms and maximize completed projects rather than letting momentum stall. There is no doubt that re-electing him in the 2027 general elections would allow his administration to consolidate ongoing development projects, strengthen federal-state alignment, and expand economic opportunities.

Willy is a member, Public Communication, Enugu State APC Campaign Council

The post 2027: Imperative of Peter Mbah’s second term in Enugu appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Important caveats to prevent sudden death
description:
Stress and overwork rarely act in isolation. We saw in last week’s essay how hypertensive heart disease and related cardiovascular conditions lead to sudden, unexpected natural deaths. Stress accelerates the development of those conditions.
This week, we will examine how these factors subtly change
content:
Stress and overwork rarely act in isolation. We saw in last week’s essay how hypertensive heart disease and related cardiovascular conditions lead to sudden, unexpected natural deaths. Stress accelerates the development of those conditions.

This week, we will examine how these factors subtly change key structures within our blood vessels over time until they cause the catastrophic events which result.

Not every stressed or overworked person dies suddenly; individual factors like genetics, existing hypertension, diabetes, obesity, smoking, alcohol use, and access to proper healthcare matter greatly.

Reducing the risk involves addressing both the physiological effects of stress and the underlying cardiovascular vulnerabilities.

These can be obtained by regular blood-pressure and metabolic screening; blood-pressure control if you are hypertensive; prioritising sleep and rest. Other measures are stress-management techniques, including simple ones such as structured downtime, physical activity, or social support.

Avoidance of continuous overtime without recovery periods where possible is vital. Lastly, seek care for persistent symptoms rather than “pushing through” or invoking your faith.

In short, stress and overwork are widely recognised as important but modifiable contributors that raise blood pressure and can trigger fatal events in men who already carry high rates of undiagnosed hypertension and related risks.

Addressing economic and occupational pressures at a societal level, alongside individual health behaviour, must be part of the broader response. Therefore, you must conduct regular check-ups even when feeling well.

Eating healthier diets with less salt and processed food, and early detection of hypertension and related risks, are the most important preventive measures any individual can take.

While data quality on exact national rates is limited, due mostly to unreliable record-keeping, the figures available rely on hospital and autopsy series, surveys, and expert observation. The consistent finding across sources is that preventable cardiovascular events driven by hypertension and lifestyle factors are the core issue for sudden deaths in this demographic.

Alcohol is a recognised contributing risk factor for the sudden deaths discussed among men under 50 in Nigeria, primarily through its effects on blood pressure, heart rhythm, and overall cardiovascular health.

It is not usually the single dominant cause; hypertensive heart disease remains the leading finding in local autopsy series, but it amplifies existing risks, especially when combined with stress, overwork, poor diet, and undiagnosed hypertension.

Cardiologists discussing the rise in sudden “slump and die” cases routinely list excessive alcohol consumption among the lifestyle drivers of hypertension, alongside stress, smoking, obesity, and sedentary habits. Advice for prevention almost always includes limiting or avoiding excess alcohol.

Local studies support the blood-pressure link. For example, research on heavy consumers of traditional palm-wine liquor (“ozu”) found elevated blood-pressure parameters, particularly in middle-aged men. This is what alcohol does; excessive or regular heavy drinking is directly linked to hypertension.

It can cause both acute increases through sympathetic activation and chronic elevation. Reducing intake often lowers blood pressure in heavy drinkers. Nigerian clinicians note that a substantial proportion of patients with hypertension, heart failure, or serious heart disease in outpatient clinics report significant alcohol use together with smoking.

Binge drinking can provoke irregular heart rhythms including atrial fibrillation – “holiday heart syndrome” – and, less commonly, ventricular arrhythmias that can lead to cardiac arrest.

This risk is higher in people who already have structural heart disease or hypertension. Long-term heavy use can contribute to alcoholic cardiomyopathy, causing weakening and enlargement of the heart muscle, which increases the chance of heart failure and sudden cardiac death in the long term. It also interacts with other lifestyle factors like obesity, poorer sleep, and reduced exercise.

Alcohol can worsen metabolic problems, promote inflammation, and, in some cases of adulterated local spirits like methanol contamination, cause acute toxic deaths, though that is distinct from typical chronic effects.

Prevalence varies by region, age, and setting, but harmful patterns like heavy episodic drinking exist among adult men, even as some younger cohorts appear to drink less overall in recent surveys.

The volume consumed matters. Light or occasional drinking has weaker or inconsistent links to sudden cardiac death in some global studies, but heavy or binge patterns are clearly harmful for blood pressure and arrhythmia risk.

In a population with already high rates of undiagnosed hypertension, even moderate intake can be more problematic. Alcohol rarely acts alone. Its contribution is greatest when layered on top of hypertension, diabetes, obesity, smoking, chronic stress, and limited medical care.

Limiting alcohol, ideally avoiding excess or binge drinking, is one of the straightforward lifestyle measures recommended alongside blood-pressure screening and control, better sleep, stress management, and reduced salt and processed food consumption.

For men already under high economic or work pressure, substituting alcohol with healthier coping strategies can reduce one layer of cardiovascular strain.

In summary, alcohol contributes meaningfully by elevating blood pressure and raising the chance of acute rhythm disturbances or progressive heart damage, particularly in the high-risk environment of undiagnosed hypertension and lifestyle pressures common among Nigerian men under 50.

Reducing intake is a practical step that supports the broader prevention advice from physicians. Smoking, including cigarettes and even vaping, is another contributing risk factor for sudden deaths among men under 50 in Nigeria.

It accelerates cardiovascular damage and raises the likelihood of acute events in people who already have high rates of undiagnosed or poorly controlled hypertension. Smoking increases that risk by damaging blood vessels and promoting atherosclerosis. Nicotine and other toxins cause endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and plaque build-up in arteries.

This contributes to coronary artery disease, reduced blood flow to the heart, and higher chances of heart attack or cardiac arrest. This combination raises blood pressure and heart rate, causing temporary spikes in blood pressure.

So, chronic use supports the development or worsening of hypertension. It also promotes clotting and arrhythmias. Smoking makes blood more likely to clot and can trigger irregular heart rhythms that may lead to cardiac arrest.

These mechanisms are the dominant findings in Nigerian autopsies, and hypertensive heart disease and other risks such as stress, alcohol, obesity, and diabetes are the most likely combination of circumstances to cause sudden death in young Nigerian men.

Smoking is rarely the sole cause in the local pattern of sudden unexpected natural deaths, where hypertensive heart disease predominates over classic coronary atherosclerosis (unlike in many high-income countries).

Its impact is greatest when layered onto existing hypertension, diabetes, or other lifestyle pressures common in the demographic. Even so, it is one of the most actionable modifiable risks. Quitting reduces cardiovascular risk over time, with benefits beginning relatively soon after cessation.

So, avoiding or quitting smoking cigarettes, shisha, or vapes is a standard recommendation from doctors, alongside blood-pressure screening and control, limiting alcohol, managing stress, better diet, and regular activity.

For men under high work or economic pressure, eliminating smoking removes one major accelerator of the cardiovascular pathway that leads to many of these sudden deaths.

In short, smoking meaningfully heightens the risk of the hypertension-related and arrhythmic events that drive sudden deaths in this group. It is a preventable contributor that sits alongside the stress, overwork, and alcohol factors already discussed.

Questions and answers

Sunday Doctor, thank you for your essay about Ebola some months ago. I have followed your column for many years and remember how you were the first to warn Nigerians about that disease in 2014. This time around, the same thing happened. God bless you. Continue the good work, sir.                 +2347*******

Thank you very much for your comments and contribution. On both occasions, though, the speculated mode of entry into Nigeria did not happen as on the two occasions, diplomats were responsible each time for importing the virus.

Sunday Doctor, I don’t know what is happening to me, but I always feel nauseous and have thick phlegm in my mouth. I don’t know why I can’t keep my saliva down, and I know that I am not pregnant. What should I do because I brush my mouth almost to the point of vomiting?    0806*******

That is something that can happen occasionally depending on the state of your stomach. If you ate something not particularly in harmony with your stomach before the onset of these symptoms, a reaction like this is possible. So, to stop excessive secretion of saliva, you could try a medication like Buscopan over several days to gauge its effect.

 

Sunday Doctor, I appreciate your good work on this column. I am a 31-year-old single woman. I get tired easily. This has been going on for nearly a year. I have seen different doctors who recommended many different tests, but nothing has been found except malaria parasites on two occasions. I have done a Google search of my symptoms and also used ChatGPT, and although the information is so much, one thing

I haven’t done, which was suggested, is iron studies. Do you think I should do that too?                 0806*******

Good day to you. It is a good thing to be concerned about your situation. While there is no indication from your inquiry regarding which precise investigations you conducted, it is important to also consider hormonal studies in addition. Iron studies are unlikely to reveal anything of importance because it is expected that your doctors would have requested a full blood count on each occasion. That alone would have examined the nature, physical characteristics and numerical disposition of your red blood cells. Stool analysis, including for occult blood, is also important in case there is some lesion within your gastrointestinal tract that is responsible for some persistent blood loss that may not be visible.

Sunday Doctor. I am 53 years old. The last time I menstruated was five months ago, and I was happy about it because it has been behaving like that for the past 1 year. Then, in the past 8 days, my breasts became heavy and painful, and I started to experience spotting. Sometimes, the blood comes out when it is not expected, and I am now wearing a panty liner anytime I am leaving the house. Is this normal? What should I do? Thank you.      08038*******

To be clear, these events can happen. With the combination of your complaints, there is a probability that proper vaginal bleeding resembling your normal period could happen soon. That would likely provide you with some relief. You can use a mild pain reliever such as Paracetamol to deal with the breast discomfort, but this is not likely to be a serious event. However, if this happens to you up to 3 times in a row, you should see a gynaecologist. 

Sunday Doctor. When is the best time to deworm my twin five-year-old daughters? Should it be after they have eaten or before feeding? Thank you.                   0803*******

Worm expellers are better absorbed and more effective when taken on an empty stomach. The general advice is to be taken before breakfast. But in mass deworming campaigns, they are often administered to schoolchildren without following these recommendations.

Sunday Doctor, thanks for past help. My right eye doesn’t see as clearly as my left eye, even with glasses, when reading. Small water blocks it, but when I clean it, it clears a little. Besides, objects are smaller than in the left eye when one eye is closed. I have used several eye drops and yeast tablets, but no luck. I am a 70-year-old male.                     09039*******

Good day, sir. If your eyes see the same object at different sizes, that problem will not be resolved with the use of eye drops and yeast tablets. You should get a proper examination by an ophthalmologist, and a solution will be found.

Sunday Doctor, I think it is harmful for women to be taking contraceptive pills. It can be harmful in future, I think. What is your view?      0806*******

Every medication has got side effects, but that is particularly true of contraceptives especially when they are used for more than two years.

The post Important caveats to prevent sudden death appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Reps weigh bill on divorce over sex denial
description:
The House of Representatives is considering a bill seeking to make the denial of conjugal rights for at least three months an additional ground for divorce in the country.
The proposed amendment to the Matrimonial Causes Act, 2004, also seeks to recognise threats or infliction of grievous bodily har
content:
The House of Representatives is considering a bill seeking to make the denial of conjugal rights for at least three months an additional ground for divorce in the country.

The proposed amendment to the Matrimonial Causes Act, 2004, also seeks to recognise threats or infliction of grievous bodily harm, as well as emotional and psychological trauma, as grounds for seeking the dissolution of a marriage.

The bill, sponsored by the member representing Aguata Federal Constituency of Anambra State, Dominic Okafor, seeks to expand the circumstances under which a spouse can obtain matrimonial relief under Section 16 of the principal Act.

Titled “A Bill for an Act to Amend the Matrimonial Causes Act (MCA), Cap M7, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004, and for Matters Related Thereto,” the proposal was read for the first time on the floor of the House on Tuesday.

It is expected to proceed to a second reading, where lawmakers will debate its general principles before further legislative consideration.

Under one of the proposed provisions, a spouse who has “habitually and constantly denied or deprived” the petitioner of conjugal rights for a period of not less than three months could face divorce proceedings.

The bill also proposes that a respondent who, since the celebration of the marriage, has “inflicted or threatens to inflict grievous bodily harm” on the petitioner should be recognised as a ground for matrimonial relief.

Another provision seeks to recognise emotional and psychological trauma, allowing a petitioner to seek relief where the respondent has caused or continues to cause such trauma.

The proposed changes would expand the existing grounds for matrimonial relief to expressly address prolonged denial of marital intimacy, physical threats, and psychological harm.

However, the bill does not specify the evidentiary threshold courts would apply in determining claims of emotional and psychological trauma or prolonged denial of conjugal rights.

The Matrimonial Causes Act is Nigeria’s principal legislation governing divorce and other matrimonial proceedings. Under the existing law, a marriage may be dissolved where the court is satisfied that it has broken down irretrievably.

Among the grounds already recognised are wilful and persistent refusal to consummate a marriage, adultery, unreasonable behaviour, desertion, and prolonged separation.

The Act also provides for divorce where a respondent has, for at least two years, been a habitual drunkard or habitually intoxicated through excessive use of sedative, narcotic, or stimulating drugs.

It further recognises rape, sodomy, or bestiality committed by a respondent since the marriage as grounds for seeking dissolution.

If passed by the National Assembly and assented to by the President, the proposed amendment would add the three new provisions to the legal framework governing divorce in Nigeria.

title: I guarantee improved power supply – Tinubu
description:
President Bola Tinubu on Saturday promised improved electricity supply and announced an agreement to reopen the defunct Leyland factory in Ibadan, as South-West governors canvassed votes for his re-election.
Tinubu made the pledge at Mapo Hall, Ibadan, during the flag-off of the All Progressives Con
content:
President Bola Tinubu on Saturday promised improved electricity supply and announced an agreement to reopen the defunct Leyland factory in Ibadan, as South-West governors canvassed votes for his re-election.

Tinubu made the pledge at Mapo Hall, Ibadan, during the flag-off of the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign in Oyo State ahead of the January 16, 2027 election.

He said his administration had signed a memorandum of understanding with Yutong, a Chinese manufacturer of commercial vehicles, including electric buses, to revive the plant.

“For Oyo State, we have just signed a Memorandum of Understanding with a Chinese firm to reopen the Leyland factory in Ibadan.

“We are reopening it to produce public transport and automobile assembly. We will continue to bring industry. You will see it, and I guarantee you an improvement in electricity supply. Joseph Tegbe is really working hard with his team,” Tinubu said, referring to the Minister of Power.

The President endorsed the APC governorship candidates in Oyo, Ogun and Lagos states, raising their hands and urging residents to vote for them.

The Ibadan rally was the seventh Tinubu had attended since his re-election campaign began in Kaduna on October 24.

Vice-President Kashim Shettima, APC National Chairman Nentawe Yilwatda and the Director-General of the Tinubu Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, attended alongside governors and members of the National Assembly.

We will dance into Aso Rock – Adeleke

Speaking on behalf of the South-West governors, Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke urged residents to set aside their political differences and give Tinubu a second term to continue the projects his administration had started.

“I call on all of you from Oyo, Lagos, Ogun, Ekiti, Ondo and Osun to go all out and vote for Tinubu. I have said it before that all the work that the President has started must continue.

“Therefore, we must all come out on January 16 and vote for Tinubu. We will dance into Aso Rock,” Adeleke said.

Ekiti State Governor Abiodun Oyebanji, who spoke on behalf of the APC governors, said all 31 governors elected on the party’s platform backed Tinubu.

He said Adeleke and the governors of Anambra and Abia states, Chukwuma Soludo and Alex Otti, also supported the President.

Oyebanji urged South-West voters to back Tinubu and the APC governorship candidate in Oyo State, Sharafadeen Alli.

“Tinubu is our own. We Yorubas should not let this opportunity pass us by. We must ensure that we support our own and bring him back come January 16.

“Let us all come out and vote for Tinubu for the sake of our future. Let us also go all out and vote for Sharafadeen and all our Senate, House of Representatives and House of Assembly candidates,” he said.

Tegbe also urged Yoruba voters to back Tinubu and Shettima, saying the administration had laid the foundation for a prosperous Nigeria.

He called for support for the APC’s governorship and legislative candidates in Oyo.

Senate Leader Opeyemi Bamidele urged party members to campaign on the administration’s record and cautioned against splitting their votes.

“There is nothing like, ‘I will vote for APC as President and vote for another party for the Senate.’ We are to vote for all APC candidates. Let us all speak with one voice,” he said.

Oshiomhole tackles Makinde

Former Edo State Governor Adams Oshiomhole questioned what Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde meant by resetting Nigeria, asking whether he would reverse the student loan scheme, infrastructure projects linking Lagos to Calabar or the pay rise for university lecturers.

Oshiomhole said the loans were designed to help indigent students.

He also credited higher pay for lecturers with reducing disruptions to university calendars.

“Does Makinde want to reset this policy? Does he want the strikes to return? Does he want to reduce the salaries of lecturers?” he asked.

Oshiomhole added that if Makinde wanted to reset the country, the APC would “reset the people’s mind”.

Tinubu thanked Oyo residents for their support and asked for their votes in January.

He also acknowledged party elders, including Aremo Olusegun Osoba and Chief Bisi Akande.

“Our children must benefit from the hope of Nigeria. We must give them the right education and invest in agriculture,” he said.

Urging voters to reject the opposition, Tinubu said, “Don’t listen to those who call themselves the ‘Palermo’ party. They are going nowhere. Don’t vote for them.”

Shettima to visit Bayelsa

Tinubu had directed that the rally be held without much fanfare in honour of passengers who died in Friday’s boat accident in Ukubie, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.

He asked those at the rally to observe a minute’s silence and offered his condolences to the bereaved families.

“We will support the people of Bayelsa State. The Vice-President, Shettima, will go and condole with the families and the people of Bayelsa after this rally,” he said.

The post I guarantee improved power supply – Tinubu appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
