title: More specialist hospitals needed for children – APGA chieftain
description:
The shortage of specialised medical facilities for critically ill children in Nigeria requires urgent government attention, a House of Representatives candidate for Orumba Federal Constituency in Anambra State, Dr Odiraa Nwakwor, has said.
Nwakwor, the candidate of the All Progressives Grand Allianc
content:
The shortage of specialised medical facilities for critically ill children in Nigeria requires urgent government attention, a House of Representatives candidate for Orumba Federal Constituency in Anambra State, Dr Odiraa Nwakwor, has said.

Nwakwor, the candidate of the All Progressives Grand Alliance, said the country needed greater investment in secondary and tertiary healthcare services, particularly paediatric intensive care facilities.

He spoke at a fundraising ceremony in Lagos, where he unveiled his development agenda ahead of the elections.

The medical practitioner said his professional experience had shown him the challenges facing the country’s health system, including inadequate facilities for treating children with critical medical conditions.

He argued that preventive healthcare alone was insufficient without well-equipped specialist centres capable of managing life-threatening conditions.

According to him, the country’s paediatric intensive care infrastructure remains inadequate despite its large population, requiring urgent intervention from policymakers and other stakeholders.

Nwakwor said his decision to enter politics was driven by his desire to translate his professional experience and exposure into policies that would improve healthcare delivery and living standards for his constituents.

Beyond healthcare, he identified education, agriculture, erosion control, information and communications technology, and community development as priorities of his proposed legislative agenda.

On education, he said his commitment to the sector was shaped by his family background, noting that both his parents were teachers.

He described erosion control as another major development priority for Anambra State, saying several communities continued to face environmental threats from erosion.

Nwakwor said he would use his international connections to attract technical assistance and mobilise resources to tackle the problem.

On agriculture, he noted that Orumba North and Orumba South were predominantly agrarian communities, stressing the need to support farmers and strengthen farming to boost economic growth and improve livelihoods.

He also disclosed that he had set up an Orumba Consultative Council as part of his proposed approach to representation, though he did not give details of its structure and responsibilities.

Nwakwor expressed optimism about his grassroots support, linking the backing for his bid to his professional experience, international exposure, networks and commitment to community service.

Former Minister of Aviation, Osita Chidoka, urged friends and well-wishers at the event to support Nwakwor, citing the contributions he could make to the legislature.

Finidi George’s side drew 1-1 away to Kwara United in
content:
Rivers United will look to end a run of five league games without a win when they host Niger Tornadoes in Port Harcourt on Saturday.

The Pride of Rivers are ninth with 19 points from 12 games and have a game in hand over several teams above them.

Finidi George’s side drew 1-1 away to Kwara United in their last league outing, but they have one of the best defensive records in the league.

Tornadoes are 12th with 17 points from 13 games and have gone three matches without a win. They lost 2-1 at Bendel Insurance in Benin City, where John Taiwo scored the winner in the fifth minute of stoppage time.

They then let a lead slip in a 1-1 draw at home to Rangers, when substitute Waheed Adebayo equalised in the 78th minute after John Zakka had put them ahead.

Rivers will start as favourites at home, but Tornadoes have shown enough resilience to suggest they will not be easy opponents. Both teams are keen to arrest their slide.

title: Big Oly takes Afrobeats yacht parties to Los Angeles
description:
Entertainment entrepreneur Olaniyi Oladipo, popularly known as Big Oly, is expanding the reach of Afrobeats in the United States through premium music events and yacht parties in Los Angeles.
Oladipo, founder and Chief Executive Officer of LAY Events, said his interest in event promotion was driven
content:
Entertainment entrepreneur Olaniyi Oladipo, popularly known as Big Oly, is expanding the reach of Afrobeats in the United States through premium music events and yacht parties in Los Angeles.

Oladipo, founder and Chief Executive Officer of LAY Events, said his interest in event promotion was driven by a desire to create platforms where people from different cultural backgrounds could connect through African music.

In an interview with Society Plus, he explained that he ventured into entertainment after identifying an opportunity to organise Afrobeats events in premium venues, combining music with networking and social experiences.

“I wanted to create experiences where guests could dress up, network, celebrate, and enjoy world-class music in premium venues,” Oladipo said.

He identified an Afrobeats event hosted at Skybar, Mondrian Hotel, West Hollywood, as one of his most memorable experiences, recalling how hundreds of people from different cultural backgrounds gathered to enjoy African music.

According to him, the event reflected the growing acceptance of Afrobeats beyond the African community and demonstrated the importance of consistency and relationship-building in the entertainment business.

Oladipo also spoke about the growth of LAY Events, which started with events across Downtown Los Angeles and Hollywood before expanding to premium venues in West Hollywood.

He said the company’s yacht parties had become one of its signature offerings, combining music, luxury, networking and scenic views.

“What fuels me is seeing people from completely different backgrounds connect through African music. You’ll see Africans, Americans, Europeans, Caribbeans, and Latinos all singing the same songs together. That’s powerful,” Oladipo said.

Reflecting on the challenges of organising live events, he recalled an occasion when unexpected operational issues arose shortly before guests arrived.

He said his team responded by redistributing responsibilities, communicating with venue management and adjusting the programme to ensure the challenges did not affect the guests’ experience.

Oladipo noted that the experience reinforced the importance of staying calm, making quick decisions and maintaining effective communication during event production.

On partnerships, the entrepreneur said trust, professionalism, shared values and accountability were essential to successful collaborations.

He added that he prioritised working with DJs, photographers, venues, influencers, sponsors and artistes who were committed to delivering quality experiences rather than simply seeking publicity.

Speaking on his plans, Oladipo said LAY Events was expanding its portfolio to include themed entertainment experiences, premium nightlife events and larger yacht parties.

He also disclosed plans to take the brand beyond Los Angeles and establish its presence in major cities across the United States, while exploring partnerships with international brands.

Oladipo added that his ambition was to build a nationally recognised entertainment brand, noting that its success would be measured not only by attendance figures but also by its ability to unite different communities and promote Afrobeats.

The post Big Oly takes Afrobeats yacht parties to Los Angeles appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Shettima, Obasanjo, Mahama, Dangote celebrate Jim Ovia at 75
description:
Prominent Nigerians, business leaders and other dignitaries gathered in Lagos on Thursday to celebrate the 75th birthday of Zenith Bank founder, Jim Ovia.
The dinner, held at the Eko Convention Centre, Eko Hotels and Suites, Victoria Island, was themed “The Man, The Vision, and The Legacy,” in recog
content:
Prominent Nigerians, business leaders and other dignitaries gathered in Lagos on Thursday to celebrate the 75th birthday of Zenith Bank founder, Jim Ovia.

The dinner, held at the Eko Convention Centre, Eko Hotels and Suites, Victoria Island, was themed “The Man, The Vision, and The Legacy,” in recognition of Ovia’s contributions to the banking industry and business development in Nigeria and beyond.

Those who graced the occasion included Vice-President Kashim Shettima; former President Olusegun Obasanjo; Ghanaian President, John Dramani Mahama; Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu; businessman, Aliko Dangote; and Zenith Bank Group Managing Director, Adaora Umeoji, among other prominent personalities.

In her welcome remarks, Umeoji praised Ovia’s visionary leadership and commitment, which she said had transformed banking in Nigeria and across Africa.

She also acknowledged his investments in people, technology and customer service, noting that his leadership had inspired generations of banking professionals.

Speaking on the theme, Shettima described Ovia as a visionary entrepreneur whose contributions to national development extended beyond banking to education, philanthropy and human capital development.

He also described Ovia as his former boss and mentor, highlighting the importance of visionary leadership, strong institutions and trust in building sustainable businesses and contributing to national development.

“A bank is built with capital, technology, and sound judgment, but it survives through trust. Trust is a remarkable human investment: it takes years to earn, moments to lose, and constant attention to preserve,” he said.

The gathering also featured gospel singer Nathaniel Bassey among the entertainers at the celebration.

The highlight of the event was the cutting of the birthday cake by Ovia alongside Mahama, Shettima, Obasanjo, Dangote and other dignitaries.

The celebration brought together political leaders, business executives, associates and entertainment personalities to honour Ovia’s contributions to Nigeria’s banking industry, entrepreneurship and education.

title: Make Nollywood a Nigerian export, Mofe Duncan urges FG
description:
Actor and director, Mofe Duncan, has urged the Federal Government to recognise Nollywood as an export sector, saying the industry provides employment for thousands of Nigerians and contributes to the economy.
Speaking in an interview with Sunday Scoop, Duncan said the government needed to support th
content:
Actor and director, Mofe Duncan, has urged the Federal Government to recognise Nollywood as an export sector, saying the industry provides employment for thousands of Nigerians and contributes to the economy.

Speaking in an interview with Sunday Scoop, Duncan said the government needed to support the industry, noting that film production creates opportunities for people across different sectors, including actors, crew members and property owners.

“Nollywood is going in the right direction. I believe if the government sees us as an export, it will understand our value because Nollywood provides jobs for a lot of people.

“Landlords have houses sitting fallow, which we use as film sets. There are also crew members and actors who depend on the industry for their livelihoods. If the government can see acting as an export, it needs to help us so Nollywood can be an export for Nigeria. We provide work for a lot of people in terms of human capital,” he said.

Duncan also spoke about his growing interest in directing, revealing that he had taken a different direction in his career over the past three years.

“For the past three years, I have taken a different turn towards directing. We have to do more for the industry. We cannot do much if we are sitting on the bench as players. It is better to be a player-coach when you can dictate what happens. Tell your stories and shoot proper stories. It has been great. I have directed three films this year, which are coming out in February,” he said.

Reflecting on his journey in the entertainment industry, Duncan acknowledged that acting had earned him the recognition and fame he enjoys today but described directing as his new passion.

“Acting gave me everything I have in terms of the name, the fame and all that. I have always been a model. Directing is my new baby now,” he added.

On the challenges of directing in Nollywood, Duncan identified budget constraints as a major challenge, explaining that financial limitations sometimes prevent directors from achieving their creative vision.

“Directing in Nollywood is difficult. One is constrained by budget. There are things one wants to achieve, but one ends up facing constraints. If one isn’t the writer, it can be challenging. However, I have directed movies I have written because I also write,” he said.

title: Fountain of Life: Crisis deepens as  Jimmy sues sister, others
description:
The Senior Pastor of the Fountain of Life Church, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, has dragged his sister, Tolu Odukoya, and seven members of the church’s Board of Trustees before a Federal High Court in Lagos over his purported removal from office.
Jimmy, alongside the Incorporated Trustees of the Fountain of
content:
The Senior Pastor of the Fountain of Life Church, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, has dragged his sister, Tolu Odukoya, and seven members of the church’s Board of Trustees before a Federal High Court in Lagos over his purported removal from office.

Jimmy, alongside the Incorporated Trustees of the Fountain of Life Church, instituted the action against Tolu, Pastor Rotimi Okpaise, Pastor Tobi Enuha, Pastor Gbenga Onabanjo, Pastor Fred Ohiani, Pastor Akin Osinbajo, Biodun Balogun and Biodun Awosika.

The court processes, dated November 20, 2026, include an originating summons, a motion on notice and affidavits sworn to by Jimmy in support of the applications.

In the originating summons sighted by our correspondent on Saturday, the plaintiffs asked the court to determine whether meetings held by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, and the decisions taken at those meetings complied with the church’s constitution.

Jimmy said he was appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees at an emergency meeting of the board on September 14, 2023, and was subsequently installed later that month.

He said the church and its organs were governed by its constitution, amended by a special resolution dated January 16, 2003, and that the defendants were members of its Board of Trustees.

According to his affidavit, the disagreement began after a December 19, 2025, board meeting attended by Bishop Mike Okonkwo, at which the possibility of handing over the church’s administrative arm to the Associate Senior Pastor was discussed.

He said no resolution or final decision was reached at the meeting.

Jimmy said he subsequently convened a board meeting for January 5, 2026, but it could not hold because there was no quorum.

He added that some trustees later presented proposals to him, many of which he declined because, according to him, they were inconsistent with the church’s constitution.

The embattled pastor said the trustees subsequently sent him a letter dated January 7, 2026, requesting a response within three days, but he did not see it until after the deadline had elapsed.

Jimmy said he later directed the board secretary to schedule a meeting for January 30, 2026, after a board member requested a special meeting.

title: Oborevwori, Diri, governors attend Orodje’s 20th coronation anniversary
description:

The ceremony, held at Udogun Hall in the monarch’s palace in
content:
Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, on Saturday joined his Bayelsa State counterpart, Douye Diri, and other prominent Nigerians at the 20th coronation anniversary of the Orodje of Okpe Kingdom, Major General Felix Mujakperuo (retd.).

The ceremony, held at Udogun Hall in the monarch’s palace in Orerokpe, headquarters of Okpe Local Government Area of Delta State, attracted political leaders, traditional rulers, government officials and other dignitaries from within and outside the state.

The anniversary, themed “Two Decades of Peace and Progress in Okpe Kingdom,” marked 20 years of Mujakperuo’s reign, which began on July 29, 2006.

Oborevwori was accompanied by his wife, Deaconess Tobore Oborevwori, while Diri chaired the grand finale of the celebration. Also in attendance were Taraba State Governor, Agbu Kefas, and his Kogi State counterpart, Ahmed Usman Ododo.

Former Delta State governors, James Ibori and Senator Ifeanyi Okowa, were among the dignitaries, alongside the state’s Deputy Governor, Sir Monday Onyeme; the Olu of Warri, Ogiame Atuwatse III; and other first-class traditional rulers and monarchs from across Delta State and beyond.

Other government officials and political figures at the event included Senator Ede Dafinone; Speaker of the Delta State House of Assembly, Emomotimi Guwor; Deputy Speaker, Arthur Akpowowo; Secretary to the State Government, Dr Kingsley Emu; and Delta State All Progressives Congress Secretary, Chief Efe Uko.

Also present were Matthew Tonlagha and Mideno Bayagbon, among other prominent personalities.

Speaking at the event, Diri described traditional rulers as important partners in governance, noting that their roles were crucial to maintaining peace and stability in their communities.

Oborevwori, in his remarks, commended the monarch for his contributions to peace and development in Okpe Kingdom, while the Orodje expressed appreciation to the people and the state government for their support over the years.

The monarch also called on the people of Okpe Kingdom to preserve their cultural heritage, protect ancestral lands and encourage the younger generation to sustain the use of the Okpe language.

The ceremony also featured cultural dances and other side attractions.

content:
Gospel reggae artiste and songwriter, Ibrahim-David Gajere, popularly known as Ibi Dave, has recorded 10 new songs at a live concert in Gombe State, following his music tours of the United States and the United Kingdom.

The concert, held in October at All Saints Federal Low-Cost, Gombe, attracted more than 6,000 attendees, with several gospel artistes and entertainment personalities joining him on stage.

The 10 songs recorded at the event include Push It Up, Zion, Better Days, Pray, Karatu, Jah Grace, Thirsty, Miracles, Brighter Than the Sun and Testify.

Speaking with Sunday Scoop,  on the significance of the concert, Ibi Dave said the live recording offered him an opportunity to reconnect with his home audience while introducing them to his new gospel compositions.

“This concert is very special to me because it is an opportunity to share the new songs God has given me with the people. Recording these songs live in Gombe makes the experience even more meaningful,” he said.

The event featured guest performances by Minister Kaestrings, Rev. Silas Yako, Dave Azi, Mumaa Lucee and James Alkali, alongside other emerging gospel artistes.

The singer said the participation of fellow musicians underscored the importance of collaboration and unity in promoting gospel music.

“I am grateful to the artistes who joined me on this journey. Their presence and contributions made the concert memorable. Beyond recording the songs, we wanted to create an atmosphere of worship, fellowship and encouragement,” he added.

Ibi Dave, who hails from Filiya in Shongom Local Government Area of Gombe State, began his musical journey as a child when he joined his church choir.

His international exposure includes a musical tour of the US in April 2017 and subsequent tours of the UK in 2024, 2025 and 2026.

Reflecting on his journey, he said, “Music started for me in childhood when I joined the church choir. It has grown from that humble beginning into a ministry that has taken me to different places. I am grateful for every opportunity to use my music to inspire people and spread the gospel.”

The artiste is the lead performer and owner of No Pranks Music Band International, based in Gombe State. He has also received several awards in recognition of his contributions to gospel music.

His honours include the Exousia Award for Best Reggae and Best Collaboration with Solomon Lange in 2016, the Arewa Gospel Mega Awards in 2019, the National Gospel Merit Award in 2020, the Arewa Gospel Royal Ambassador Award in 2021 and the Africa Gospel Reggae Artist of the Year Award in 2024.

Beyond music, Ibi Dave is a certified accountant. He is married to Prisca Ibrahim, and they have three children.

title: Nigeria must end money politics to regain respect – Jonathan
description:
Former President Goodluck Jonathan has called for an overhaul of Nigeria’s political system to end the influence of money, patronage and ethnic considerations in leadership selection.
He warned that the practice was damaging the country’s international reputation.
Jonathan said restoring the country
content:
Former President Goodluck Jonathan has called for an overhaul of Nigeria’s political system to end the influence of money, patronage and ethnic considerations in leadership selection.

He warned that the practice was damaging the country’s international reputation.

Jonathan said restoring the country’s global standing would require credible elections, internal party democracy, accountable leadership and a political culture that prioritises competence over personal connections.

He made the call on Saturday in Abuja while delivering the keynote address at the third edition of the Paul Alaje Colloquium, themed “The Brand Nigeria.”

“We must reform our political and leadership recruitment processes. We must strengthen internal party democracy, electoral credibility and a political culture that is more inclusive, rewards ideas, character and competence rather than money, patronage and sectional interests,” Jonathan said.

The call came as Nigeria prepares for the 2027 general elections, amid longstanding concerns over vote-buying, the influence of money in party primaries and the use of political patronage in leadership selection.

Previous elections have drawn scrutiny over voter inducements, with the Independent National Electoral Commission and anti-corruption agencies repeatedly warning that electoral malpractice undermines democratic credibility.

The former President identified the growing preference for wealth, ethnicity and political connections in public appointments as one of the major factors undermining the country’s development and international credibility.

“The growing preference for money, patronage, ethnicity and personal connections over competence and merit in leadership recruitment and public appointments,” he said.

According to him, corruption, abuse of public office, impunity, insecurity and the weakening of public institutions have contributed to Nigeria’s declining global standing.

He also criticised the increasing celebration of wealth without adequate scrutiny of its source, alongside the normalisation of cybercrime, drug trafficking, cultism and other criminal activities.

“These developments have consequences beyond our borders. They undermine investor confidence, weaken international partnerships and diminish the respect attached to the Nigerian name,” Jonathan warned.

The ex-President also lamented that Nigeria, once respected for its diplomatic influence, economic potential and contributions to African liberation, was increasingly associated with corruption, unemployment, insecurity and economic difficulties.

“Today, we must honestly acknowledge that the image of our country has suffered considerable setbacks,” he said.

Jonathan expressed concern over the relatively weak international standing of the Nigerian passport, arguing that visa restrictions and limited travel opportunities reflected the challenges confronting the country’s reputation.

“A passport is more than a travel document; it is a symbol of national identity and the confidence other countries place in the nation that issues it,” he explained.

Nevertheless, he maintained that the country’s challenges should not overshadow the achievements of millions of Nigerians who continued to distinguish themselves internationally.

“Our problem is not a shortage of human potential. It is our failure to translate that potential consistently into effective institutions, responsible leadership and national progress,” he said.

The former President recalled the country’s contributions to peacekeeping operations in Liberia and Sierra Leone, the struggle against apartheid and the achievements of its professionals, athletes and creative industries.

He referenced the 2009 national rebranding campaign championed by the late Dora Akunyili under former President Umaru Musa Yar’Adua, which adopted the slogan, “Good People, Great Nation.”

Jonathan urged Nigeria to learn from Singapore, South Korea, Malaysia and India, particularly Singapore’s emphasis on meritocracy, institutional discipline, integrity and human capital development.

He called for greater investment in education, healthcare, agriculture, manufacturing, technology and infrastructure to build a productive economy capable of generating employment.

He also advocated stronger support for Nollywood, Afrobeats, literature, fashion and sports as instruments of cultural diplomacy and economic development.

“Restoring the Nigeria brand requires more than slogans and publicity campaigns. It requires a national commitment to changing the realities that shape our reputation,” he said.

Addressing young Nigerians, Jonathan urged them to uphold integrity, reject criminality and demand accountability from political leaders while accepting responsibility for their conduct.

In his opening address, the convener of the colloquium, Paul Alaje, warned that the country could not improve its international image through publicity without addressing institutional weaknesses and economic underperformance.

“We must stop confusing potential with progress. Potential is not prosperity. Resources are not development. Population is not automatically productivity. And international recognition is not national transformation,” Alaje said.

He argued that insecurity, corruption, policy inconsistency and weak institutions increased business costs, discouraged investment and accelerated capital and talent flight.

Alaje identified healthcare, governance and security, the creative economy, artificial intelligence and investment as five critical areas for strengthening Nigeria’s international competitiveness.

He urged policymakers to prioritise productivity, institutional trust, human development and support for businesses, while ensuring economic reforms translate into employment, purchasing power and improved living standards.

“We cannot market what we have not built. We cannot communicate our way out of institutional weaknesses. We cannot advertise our way into prosperity,” he said.

Alaje also praised Jonathan’s peaceful transfer of power in 2015, describing it as an important demonstration of democratic responsibility.

He called for a consistent national development vision that would survive changes in political administrations.

The post Nigeria must end money politics to regain respect – Jonathan appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

By Clare Nnabuike, Minna



Suspected terrorists have killed the village head of Lumma Ba’are community in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State, Mallam Bawa Muhammad, and five other residents in an attack that also left severa
content:
…Governor Bago deploys joint security team to affected community

By Clare Nnabuike, Minna

Suspected terrorists have killed the village head of Lumma Ba’are community in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State, Mallam Bawa Muhammad, and five other residents in an attack that also left several people abducted and houses burnt.

The attackers reportedly invaded the community at about 5:00 a.m. on Saturday, November 21, 2026, shortly after the Muslim call to prayer, forcing residents to flee into nearby bushes for safety.

Sources in the community alleged that the assailants beheaded the village head and burnt his body. They also reported that a newborn baby died after being left inside a house that was set ablaze during the attack.

Several residents were reportedly abducted, although the exact number of those taken away had yet to be established.

Some residents also alleged that individuals from the community had collaborated with the attackers. However, the claims had not been independently verified as of the time of filing this report.

The Niger State Police Command confirmed the attack, saying five people were killed and that joint security teams had been deployed to the area to apprehend the perpetrators.

The Police Public Relations Officer, Wasiu Abiodun, said in a statement that the incident was reported at about 5:00 a.m. on November 21.

“On 21/11/2026 at about 5am, report received indicated that suspected armed men invaded Lumma Ba’are village, Borgu LGA and attacked the community, while about five persons reportedly lost their lives during the attack.

“Joint security teams have been deployed to the location, efforts to apprehend the suspected perpetrators ongoing. Further development will be communicated,” Abiodun stated.

Also confirming the incident, the Niger State Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Obed Nuhu Nana, said five other persons sustained injuries and were evacuated to the General Hospital, New-Bussa, where they were receiving medical attention.

In a statement, Nana said the attack occurred amid lingering intercommunal tensions in the area, describing the incident as unfortunate and unacceptable.

“The Niger State Government condemns the attack on Lumma Ba’are community in Borgu Local Government Area, which claimed the lives of five persons, including the Village Head, Malam Bawa Muhammad.

“The attack, according to reports received, occurred at about 5:00 a.m. on Saturday, November 21, 2026, when suspected armed men invaded the community amid lingering intercommunal tensions and launched an assault on residents.

“Five other persons sustained injuries and were evacuated to the General Hospital, New-Bussa, where they are currently receiving medical attention. Some houses were also reportedly set ablaze during the incident,” the statement said.

The government extended its condolences to the families of the deceased and the entire community, while wishing the injured residents a speedy recovery.

Nana said joint security teams had been deployed to the affected community, with efforts being intensified to identify and apprehend those responsible.

He assured residents that Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago’s administration was working with relevant security agencies to prevent further attacks and restore peace to the area.

The government urged residents to remain calm, avoid taking the law into their hands and provide security agencies with credible information that could assist ongoing investigations.

It also reiterated its commitment to protecting lives and property across the state, irrespective of ethnic, religious or communal affiliations.

The post Terrorists kill Niger village head, five others, abduct residents appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Customs seize contraband worth N3.52bn in Ogun
description:
.recover cannabis, codeine syrup, others



By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta



The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Ogun I Area Command, has intercepted and seized contraband goods with a total Duty Paid Value (DPV) of ₦3.52 billion as part of intensified efforts to curb smuggling, protect public health
content:
.recover cannabis, codeine syrup, others

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Ogun I Area Command, has intercepted and seized contraband goods with a total Duty Paid Value (DPV) of ₦3.52 billion as part of intensified efforts to curb smuggling, protect public health and safeguard the nation’s economy.

The seizures, which include 6,037 wraps of cannabis, 20,500 bottles of codeine-containing cough syrup, more than 1.45 million tablets and capsules of various brands, foreign parboiled rice, petroleum products and vehicles, were inspected and paraded by the Comptroller-General of Customs during a visit to the Command.

According to a statement issued on Saturday, by the Public Relations Officer of Ogun I Area Command, Assistant Superintendent of Customs Paul Gimba, the total value of the seized items with available valuations stood at **₦3,517,838,700.

The statement said the seizures reflected the Command’s sustained efforts to combat smuggling and prevent the circulation of prohibited and potentially harmful products in the country.

A breakdown of the intercepted items showed that cannabis accounted for 6,037 wraps, valued at ₦1.268 billion, while 20,500 bottles of cough syrup containing codeine had a Duty Paid Value of ₦147.6 million.

The Command also intercepted 828,920 tablets of different brands valued at ₦795.76 million and 627,320 capsules worth ₦376.39 million. Other pharmaceutical products seized included 2,850 ampoules of Enox 4000 injection, valued at ₦17.1 million, and 95 prostate pills worth ₦570,000.

The seizures further included 5,173 bags of 50kg foreign parboiled rice, valued at ₦455.22 million, alongside 1,067 used tyres worth ₦52.82 million.

In the petroleum products category, Customs intercepted 1,037 kegs of 25 litres of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), valued at ₦34.22 million, and 1,008 kegs of 25 litres of Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), worth ₦44.35 million.

Other seized items comprised 21 packages of walkie-talkies, 185 packages of sanitary pads and diapers valued at ₦18.13 million, 125 live cartridges and two trucks with a combined valuation of ₦144 million.

The Command also recorded seizures of several used vehicles, including a 2024 Toyota RAV4 and Toyota Highlander valued at a combined ₦50 million; two Lexus vehicles worth ₦25 million; a 2000 Toyota Hilux valued at ₦11 million; a 2013 Toyota RAV4 worth ₦17 million; and a Toyota Sienna valued at ₦14.7 million.

Other vehicles intercepted were a 2010 Toyota Venza valued at ₦14.6 million, an Opel worth ₦7.3 million, a Mazda valued at ₦7.1 million and a 2012 Range Rover Sport worth ₦17.2 million.

The Customs Service said the interceptions underscored the Command’s determination to enforce relevant Customs laws, prevent the importation and circulation of prohibited goods and protect Nigeria’s economic interests.

It added that the enforcement operations were part of broader efforts to safeguard national security and public health while strengthening the country’s economic resilience.

The statement also highlighted the Service’s expanding role in national development, noting that its activities go beyond revenue generation and border enforcement to include community engagement, infrastructure support and trade facilitation.

According to the statement, the inspection and parade of the seizures, alongside the commissioning of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) projects, demonstrated the Service’s commitment to combining robust enforcement with initiatives that promote community development.

title: Rising profile of Tems, Asake and Nigerian artists’ Grammy journey
description:
By Ayo Onikoyi



The voices are getting louder everyday that Asake and Tems are the new King and Queen of Afrobeats respectively. And the Recording Academy confirmed it on November 16, 2026 when it announced the nominees for 2027 Grammy awards.



Asake appears just to be coming to his own with two
content:
By Ayo Onikoyi

The voices are getting louder everyday that Asake and Tems are the new King and Queen of Afrobeats respectively. And the Recording Academy confirmed it on November 16, 2026 when it announced the nominees for 2027 Grammy awards.

Asake appears just to be coming to his own with two nominations while Tems shatfers the roof with four Grammy nominations in one year.

Tems has emerged as Nigeria’s most successful representative in the latest nomination cycle, earning four nominations and further establishing herself as one of the most versatile Nigerian musicians on the international stage.

Her recognition in the R&B categories is particularly noteworthy. It demonstrates that her appeal extends beyond the African music market and that her songwriting and vocal abilities are attracting recognition in mainstream American music.

The nominations also build on an impressive Grammy history. Tems won her first Grammy in 2023 for her contribution to Future’s “Wait For U”, featuring Drake, which won Best Melodic Rap Performance. She subsequently won Best African Music Performance in 2025 for her reimagining of “Love Me JeJe”.

She has also received recognition for her contribution to Beyoncé’s Renaissance, Wizkid’s “Essence” and Rihanna’s “Lift Me Up”, from the Black Panther: Wakanda Forever soundtrack.

With two Grammy victories already to her credit, Tems is approaching the 2027 ceremony with an opportunity to increase her collection and further strengthen Nigeria’s presence in international R&B.

Asake on the other hand has not won any Grammy – yet. But he appears to be knocking on the door. The “Lonely at the Top” hitmaker has now received four Grammy Award nominations as of November 2026. His nominations are all in the Best African Music Performance category.

His flirting with the Recording Academy started in 2024 with his hit “Amapiano” with Olamide, followed by “MMS” with Wizkid in 2025. Once again, he has dragged Wizkid onto the Grammy ballot with their collaboration “Jogodo” and his own solo hit “Gratitude” in 2027

Six Nigerian stars earn 2027 Grammy nominations as Afrobeats expands global reach, with the country securing representation in Best African Music Performance, Best Global Music Album, Best Global Music Performance and Best R&B Song.

Joining Tems and Asake on the list are: Burna Boy with one nomination for Dia Dia with Shakira for Best Global Music Performance; Wizkid has one nomination too, for his collaboration with Asake on “Jogodo”; Ayra Starr has two nominations for Best Global Music Album with her hit “Starrgirl” and Best African Music Performance on the “Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?)” collaboration with Angélique Kidjo and Davido with one nomination as his album “Oriadé” earned a place in the Best Global Music Album category, where it will compete against projects by Tems, Ayra Starr, Anitta and Angélique Kidjo.

Nigerian artists Grammy journey

Nigerian artists have a rich history with the Recording Academy over the years. But the focus is on the current crop of Afrobeats singers who are making the country proud and leading the charge for Africa’s renaissance.

Burna Boy 

For Burna Boy, the 2027 nomination represents another opportunity to extend a Grammy legacy that has helped establish him as one of Africa’s most recognisable musical exports.

His collaboration with Colombian superstar Shakira on “Dai Dai” earned him a place in the Best Global Music Performance category, putting him in contention alongside other international acts.

His defining moment came in 2021 when Twice As Tall won Best Global Music Album, making him one of the Nigerian artistes to have secured the prestigious award.

He has since received nominations for Love, Damini, I Told Them…, “Last Last”, “City Boys”, “Alone” and “Higher”, among other recordings.

The new nomination takes his career tally to 14, according to the Recording Academy’s records, making him Nigeria’s most nominated artiste at the awards.

Tems

Tems has become the first Nigerian artist to win two Grammy Awards and has demonstrated an ability to compete across African music, global music, hip-hop and R&B categories. Her four nominations in 2027 further underline her growing international recognition.

She has received 12 nominations as of November 19, 2026. She is one of Africa’s most successful Grammy-winning female artists.

Wizkid 

Wizkid has won one Grammy Award and received seven nominations as of November 19, 2026. His latest nomination is for the 2027 Grammy Awards.

Davido

Davido has never won a Grammy Award. As of November 19, 2026, the Nigerian Afrobeats star has received six Grammy nominations across four consecutive editions of the awards, from 2024 to 2027.

title: ‘I Struggled To Come Out, Lost My Sister, Other Relatives,’ Bayelsa Boat Accident Survivor
description: A survivor of Friday’s boat accident in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has recounted how she struggled to escape from the capsized vessel, saying she lost several members of her family and neighbours in the tragedy.The woman, whose identity was not immediately disclos
content:
A survivor of Friday’s boat accident in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has recounted how she struggled to escape from the capsized vessel, saying she lost several members of her family and neighbours in the tragedy.

The woman, whose identity was not immediately disclosed, said her elder sister, her sister’s daughter-in-law and two children belonging to her relatives and neighbours were among those who died in the accident.

Recounting the incident, she said the boat suddenly capsized, trapping passengers beneath it.

“The boat just fell and pressed all of us. My elder sister’s son’s wife was lost. My elder sister was lost. Her son was also lost. One of my neighbours who followed us also lost her son. My neighbour herself was lost,” she said.

The survivor said she was the only person among those close to her who made it out alive, adding that she struggled to escape after the boat overturned.

“It’s only me that is safe. When I came out, somebody held me. I was drinking water. I was not able to come out. I struggled before I came out. Where we were standing, the boat broke from above and pressed us down,” she said.

Asked by the Bayelsa governor, Douye Diri, whether the bodies of her missing relatives and neighbours had been recovered, she replied in the negative.

Her account comes as the death toll from the accident has risen to 23, while 24 survivors are receiving treatment in hospitals.

The accident occurred near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw when a boat conveying mourners from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony capsized at about 11 a.m. on Friday.

The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident, saying preliminary findings indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways.

However, a survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger vessel, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings, raising concerns about possible breaches of waterway safety regulations.

President Bola Tinubu has expressed condolences to the families of the victims and directed relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery operations.

In a statement posted on his X account, Tinubu described the incident as tragic and said those who died did not deserve to lose their lives in such circumstances.

“Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation,” he said.

The President also directed that Saturday’s presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, be held without much fanfare in honour of the victims.

Meanwhile, Governor Diri has visited the scene of the accident and is expected to initiate an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the tragedy.

The state government has also warned boat operators against overloading, reckless navigation and travelling without life jackets, urging strict compliance with waterway safety regulations to prevent a recurrence.

The post ‘I Struggled To Come Out, Lost My Sister, Other Relatives,’ Bayelsa Boat Accident Survivor appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Can Enzo Maresca Win The Premier League In His First Season At Man City?
description: Six league titles. Ten years. A stand at the Etihad with his name on it. Good luck following that. Enzo Maresca has to, after Manchester City unveiled him as manager back in June 2026.Maresca at least knows his way around the training ground. Back in 2020-2021, he ran the Elite Development Squad and
content:
Six league titles. Ten years. A stand at the Etihad with his name on it. Good luck following that. Enzo Maresca has to, after Manchester City unveiled him as manager back in June 2026.

Maresca at least knows his way around the training ground. Back in 2020-2021, he ran the Elite Development Squad and won Premier League 2 with them. He returned in 2022 to work under Guardiola as an assistant, and that season ended with the treble. So this is spell number three, and he’s tied down until 2029.

Expectations at City don’t reset just because the man in the dugout has changed. City’s title odds have become some of the most debated in premier league online betting markets because bookmakers must weigh a campaign shaped as much by events off the pitch as on it.

A Flying Start, Then A Bump

The opening weeks went better than almost anyone expected. Maresca became the first manager in Premier League history to win his first seven games in charge of a new club. The football looked familiar too. City kept the ball and wore teams down, which is no surprise from a coach who learned so much from Guardiola. His Leicester and Chelsea sides played the same way.

City spent big to help him. Their summer outlay of around £460 million was a record for any club, and £125 million of it went on Enzo Fernández from Chelsea, a fee that matched the Premier League transfer record. Phil Foden signed a four-year extension. Rodri, one of the faces of the Guardiola years, left for Barcelona.

Maresca has won quickly before. He lifted the Championship title with Leicester in 2023-24. A year later at Chelsea, he won the Conference League and the Club World Cup and still finished fourth in the league.

Seven straight wins at the start of a season guarantee nothing, of course. Plenty of fast starters have slid down the Premier League table once the winter fixtures arrive. City soon lost three league games in a row, one of them a 1-0 home defeat to Brighton, who had never won away at City before. Then there are Arsenal. Mikel Arteta, another former Guardiola assistant, ended their 22-year wait for the title in 2025-26, helped along by a Premier League record for goals from corners.

The Fight Off the Pitch

The bigger problem might be off the pitch entirely. Early in the 2026-27 season, an independent commission found City guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules. It ruled that the club used “sham” contracts with commercial partners to inflate revenues and cut costs by more than £900 million between 2009 and 2018. City deny any wrongdoing and have appealed. If the verdict stands, they face a heavy sanction, and a big points deduction is one of the options on the table.

So Maresca could get everything right in the dugout and still watch the table get rewritten by lawyers. He says he trusts the club completely and expects the appeal to succeed. Keeping a dressing room focused while its future is in doubt is a different kind of test, and few managers have had to deal with anything like it.

City have been here before. The charges were first announced in February 2023, and a few months later they won the treble, with Maresca on the coaching staff.

History is on his side as well. Mourinho, Ancelotti, Pellegrini, Conte and Slot are among the few managers to win the Premier League in their first season at a club. Slot is the best comparison. He replaced Jürgen Klopp at Liverpool and won the league in 2024-25, his very first season, which showed that following a legend does not have to mean a year of transition.

On football alone, Maresca can do this. He has the players, he knows the system, and he knows the building. The early run proved City can still beat anyone, and title winners usually ride out a bad patch like the one that followed.

The real uncertainty is something he cannot control. All he can do is keep winning and leave City in the best possible position, whatever the appeal panel decides. If he pulls it off, it will be one of the most remarkable title wins the Premier League has seen.

The soldiers were sa
content:
Several soldiers are feared dead, while others sustained injuries following a road accident involving a military vehicle in Yobe State.

The incident reportedly occurred on Friday, November 20, at Garin Malam Adamu, near Buni Yadi, the headquarters of Gujba Local Government Area.

The soldiers were said to have been travelling from Buni Yadi to Damaturu, the state capital, when the accident happened.

Following the incident, the injured soldiers and other victims were reportedly evacuated to the Yobe State University Teaching Hospital in Damaturu for medical attention.

The exact number of casualties and the circumstances surrounding the accident have yet to be established.

Although the exact casualty figure remains unknown, preliminary accounts have linked the accident to the poor condition of a section of the road.

At the time of filing this report, military authorities had yet to officially confirm the incident or disclose the number of casualties.

title: Arsenal suffer double blow as Newcastle fight back to secure 2-2 draw
description:
Arsenal missed a golden opportunity to move eight points clear at the top of the Premier League after being held to a 2-2 draw by Newcastle United on Saturday.
The Gunners appeared firmly in control after a dominant first-half performance, with Eberechi Eze finding the back of the net to give Mikel
content:
Arsenal missed a golden opportunity to move eight points clear at the top of the Premier League after being held to a 2-2 draw by Newcastle United on Saturday.

The Gunners appeared firmly in control after a dominant first-half performance, with Eberechi Eze finding the back of the net to give Mikel Arteta’s side the lead.

However, Newcastle produced an impressive second-half comeback, turning the game around through goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw.

The comeback provided a much-needed boost for Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who had been under pressure following the club’s recent struggles.

Arsenal fought back to secure a draw but were unable to claim all three points, missing the opportunity to strengthen their position in the title race.

Noni Madueke salvaged a point for Arsenal and stretched their lead at the top over surprise package Brighton to six points.

However, the loss of influential goalkeeper David Raya to injury could provide a twist in the title race that many believed Arsenal would cruise.

Newcastle remain in the bottom half of the table with just one win in six games in all competitions.

Yet, Jaissle can point to his side’s second half performance as a potential turning point after a difficult start to his reign at St. James’ Park.

Arsenal move back six points clear of third-placed Manchester City, but missed the chance to put their foot down in the defence of their title.

Madueke continued his impressive form in the injury absence of Bukayo Saka and hit the post early on.

Former Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes was roundly booed on his first return to Tyneside since making a £75 million ($98 million) move to the Emirates Stadium In August.

The Brazilian nearly silenced his former faithful when he prodded just wide from a Madueke cross as Arsenal pressed for the opener.

It duly arrived 10 minutes before the break when Kai Havertz pounced on a poor touch by Lewis Hall and brilliantly played in Eze to blast high past Lukas Hornicek.

Jaissle got the response he needed from his half-time team talk as Newcastle came out a completely different proposition after the break.

Arsenal also played a part in letting the home side back into the game and lifting the 50,000 crowd in doing so.

Martin Odegaard shanked his attempt at a long ball forward to allow William Osula to play in Barnes to level.

Suddenly an Arsenal side that had kept seven clean sheets in their opening 10 league games was on the rocks.

Thiaw bundled home a second for Newcastle just 13 minutes later after Dan Burn was left completely unmarked from a corner and his header was only parried by Raya.

That proved to be one of Raya’s final interventions as the Spaniard had to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Raya would be a massive miss if the Spaniard is sidelined for a significant spell.

But Arsenal regained their composure in time to salvage a point that keeps them well in the driving seat to retain the title.

Odegaard made amends for his earlier error by freeing Madueke down the right and he cut inside before his tame deflected shot found a way past Hornicek.

title: Residents Killed As Bandits Attacks Niger State Community
description: Several people, including a village head and children under the age of five, have reportedly been killed in an early morning attack by suspected armed bandits on Luman Ba’are community in Shagunu Ward, Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State.The attack, which occurred on Saturday, also left
content:
Several people, including a village head and children under the age of five, have reportedly been killed in an early morning attack by suspected armed bandits on Luman Ba’are community in Shagunu Ward, Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State.

The attack, which occurred on Saturday, also left several houses, shops and motorcycles burnt, while an unspecified number of residents were abducted and taken to unknown destinations.

According to security sources in the area, the gunmen stormed the community at about 6:00 a.m., attacking residents and setting several buildings ablaze. Some of the victims were reportedly burnt to death.

The attackers were also said to have planted explosive devices along major roads and access routes leading to the community, apparently to prevent security operatives from gaining immediate access to the area.

In addition to the killings and destruction of property, the gunmen reportedly rustled an unspecified number of cattle belonging to residents before fleeing the community.

Luman Ba’are is also the home community of the Shagunu Ward Field Volunteer, who reportedly narrowly escaped death after engaging the attackers with his firearm in self-defence.

Meanwhile, the Niger State Police Command has confirmed the attack, although its initial casualty figure was lower than the number reported by local security sources.

In a statement issued on Saturday, the Police Public Relations Officer, SP Wasiu Abiodun, said the command received a report that suspected armed men invaded Lumma Ba’are village in Borgu Local Government Area at about 5:00 a.m. on November 21.

According to the police, about five people were killed in the attack.

The statement added that joint security teams had been deployed to the affected community, while efforts were ongoing to apprehend the suspected attackers.

The police assured residents that further developments would be communicated as investigations and security operations progressed.

The latest attack adds to growing security concerns in Borgu Local Government Area, which borders Kainji Lake National Park and has witnessed repeated incidents of banditry, mass abductions, cattle rustling and destruction of property.

title: Oborevwori to Diri: Delta stands with Bayelsa over Southern Ijaw boat tragedy
description:
From Joe Obukata Ogbodu, Warri
Delta State Governor, Rt Hon Sheriff Oborevwori, has commiserated with his Bayelsa State counterpart, Senator Douye Diri, over the boat mishap in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, which claimed lives and left several passengers missing.
The governor
content:
From Joe Obukata Ogbodu, Warri

Delta State Governor, Rt Hon Sheriff Oborevwori, has commiserated with his Bayelsa State counterpart, Senator Douye Diri, over the boat mishap in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, which claimed lives and left several passengers missing.

The governor said the tragedy was even more painful because the victims were travelling to attend a burial ceremony in Ukubie community when the boat capsized.

In a condolence message issued by his Chief Press Secretary, Sir Festus Ahon, Oborevwori extended his sympathies to the government and people of Bayelsa State, particularly the families of those who lost their loved ones.

He said the tragedy was a painful loss not only to the affected families but also to the people of Bayelsa State and the Niger Delta, assuring them of the solidarity and prayers of the government and people of Delta State.

Oborevwori said: “I am deeply saddened by the tragic boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State. On behalf of the government and people of Delta State, I extend my heartfelt condolences to my brother governor, Senator Douye Diri, the government and people of Bayelsa State, and, most importantly, the families who lost their loved ones.

“This is a painful tragedy, made even more distressing by the fact that the victims were travelling to attend a burial ceremony. No family should have to endure such a devastating loss under these circumstances.

“I pray that Almighty God grants the souls of the departed eternal rest and gives their families the strength and fortitude to bear this irreparable loss. I also wish those who sustained injuries a speedy and full recovery.”

The Delta governor also expressed concern for passengers still unaccounted for and urged the relevant authorities and rescue teams to sustain efforts to locate them.

At least four people, including two children, died after the boat conveying funeral guests from Ayama community to Ukubie capsized at about 11 a.m. on Friday, November 20, 2026, at the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities.

title: EPL: Arsenal held 2-2 by Newcastle, Raya suffers injury
description:
Arsenal were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw against Newcastle United in their Premier League clash at St James’ Park on Saturday.
The Gunners missed the opportunity to extend their lead at the top of the table to eight points after Newcastle staged a second-half comeback.
Arsenal dominated proceedi
content:
Arsenal were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw against Newcastle United in their Premier League clash at St James’ Park on Saturday.

The Gunners missed the opportunity to extend their lead at the top of the table to eight points after Newcastle staged a second-half comeback.

Arsenal dominated proceedings in the opening half and took the lead in the 33rd minute through Eberechi Eze, who finished off a fine pass from Kai Havertz.

However, Newcastle returned from the break with renewed determination and equalised in the 49th minute.

Harvey Barnes found the back of the net after William Osula capitalised on a mistake by Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard to set up the winger.

The hosts completed their turnaround in the 62nd minute when Malick Thiaw scored from close range following a corner kick.

Arsenal suffered another setback when goalkeeper David Raya was forced off with a shoulder injury after a collision with Osula.

The Spanish goalkeeper received treatment before being replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga in the 70th minute.

Mikel Arteta’s men eventually restored parity in the 78th minute through Noni Madueke, who finished a well-worked attacking move to make it 2-2.

Both teams pushed for a winner in the closing stages, but neither could find another goal.

The result takes Arsenal to 28 points, keeping them six points ahead of Brighton, who have a game in hand.

Arsenal will now turn their attention to their upcoming fixtures against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League, followed by Premier League encounters with Manchester City, Brentford and Tottenham.

The extent of Raya’s injury remains a concern for Arteta ahead of the demanding run of fixtures.

title: Kalu celebrates Mama Bernadette Ebri at 90, calls her a blessing to her family
description:
Ninety years is not small. Not in Nigeria. Not anywhere. So when Mama Bernadette Emah Ebri turned 90, people gathered to thank God for her life.
Senator Orji Uzor Kalu was one of those who did. He sent a short message to the family.
He said he was happy for Mama, and he prayed God would keep her str
content:
Ninety years is not small. Not in Nigeria. Not anywhere. So when Mama Bernadette Emah Ebri turned 90, people gathered to thank God for her life.

Senator Orji Uzor Kalu was one of those who did. He sent a short message to the family.

He said he was happy for Mama, and he prayed God would keep her strong, keep her healthy, and give her many more years in peace, surrounded by her children and grandchildren. Just simple. Just from the heart. Happy 90th birthday, Mama.

Mama is the mother of former Cross River State Governor, Dr Clement Ebri. The family celebrated her on Wednesday at their house along Clement Ebri Avenue, State Housing Estate, in Calabar. Family came. Friends came. Hundreds of people came to sit with her, pray with her and honour her.

Governor Bassey Otu also sent his own message. So did the Speaker of the Cross River State House of Assembly, Elvert Ayambem. They both talked about the same thing: that Mama is a woman of faith, a woman who gave her life to family and to education, and a woman who has lived well.

But it was Clement Ebri himself who said what touched many people most. He said Mama is not just his stepmother. To him, she is simply his mother. His beloved Mama Mkpani.

He remembered growing up with her in Umuahia in the mid-1960s. He remembered their Saturday market trips, and how she taught him to plan, to be responsible and to treat people well.

He remembered how she took him to secondary school in 1965 and kept writing him letters, just to stay close.

He said he never saw her quarrel with his father. Not once. That peace at home, he said, shaped him.

That is the kind of mother Mama is. Not loud. Not showy. Just present. Just steady.

The kind who shows up, who writes the letter, who walks the child to school, who keeps the house calm.

So when Senator Kalu says 90 years is God’s grace and mercy, he is not just saying a prayer. He is saying what everybody in Calabar saw that day: a woman who has lived long because she lived well, and a family that is still standing because she stood for them.

Happy 90th birthday, Mama Bernadette. May God keep you.

Rubby Obinna
November 12, 2026

title: 2027: Nto backs Orji Kalu’s re-election, says senator has no competitor, declares Abia APC united
description:
A former All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial aspirant for Abia North, Prof Philips Nto, has thrown his weight behind the re-election bid of Senator Orji Uzor Kalu, declaring that the former Abia State governor has no serious competitor in the race for the 2027 senatorial election.
Nto, a form
content:
A former All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial aspirant for Abia North, Prof Philips Nto, has thrown his weight behind the re-election bid of Senator Orji Uzor Kalu, declaring that the former Abia State governor has no serious competitor in the race for the 2027 senatorial election.

Nto, a former Commissioner for Finance and Economic Planning in Abia State, also declared that “the APC in the state remained united”, pledging to mobilise his political structures, supporters and resources towards Kalu’s re-election.

He made the declaration on Saturday when he hosted Kalu and members of his entourage at his residence in Ututu, Arochukwu Local Government Area, following the senator’s ward-to-ward tour of the clan.

The former senatorial aspirant, who accompanied Kalu throughout the tour, said his decision to support the senator was informed by Kalu’s performance and pedigree, and his commitment to party unity and the collective interests of Abia North.

He expressed confidence in Kalu’s political experience and grassroots connections, insisting that the senator remained the candidate to beat in Abia North.

The former commissioner further pledged to deploy his political network and resources towards mobilising support for Kalu across Ututu and other communities in Arochukwu Local Government Area.

Earlier, Kalu, who represents Abia North Senatorial District and chairs the Senate Committee on the South East Development Commission (SEDC), had toured Ututu Wards A, B, C, D and E, where he interacted with constituents on infrastructure, education, community development and other pressing needs.

The senator commenced his engagements with a courtesy visit to His Royal Majesty, Eze Solomon Nwaizu Okereke, JP, Ezeoma I of Ezema Ututu, who received him alongside other community leaders.

Welcoming the former governor, the traditional ruler recalled Kalu’s longstanding relationship with the people of Ututu, describing him as a “familiar figure whose association with the community extended beyond his years in the Senate”.

The monarch particularly recalled how Kalu appointed sons of Ututu to positions of responsibility during his administration as governor of Abia State between 1999 and 2007.

He commended the senator for maintaining his relationship with the community over the years and expressed support for his continued representation.

The traditional ruler, however, appealed to Kalu to facilitate additional developmental projects, particularly in areas requiring government intervention, to improve the living conditions of residents.

Also speaking during the tour, Princess Evelyn Nwankwo applauded Kalu’s representation of Abia North, describing him as a longstanding friend of the Ututu people.

She noted that the senator had maintained close ties with the community over the years and expressed appreciation for his developmental interventions.

Nwankwo pledged the community’s continued goodwill and support, expressing hope that the relationship would translate into further improvements in infrastructure and other essential services.

Similarly, the APC candidate for Arochukwu State Constituency, Prince Ike Okorafor, commended Kalu for attracting developmental projects to Arochukwu Local Government Area.

Okorafor said the senator had demonstrated his commitment to the area through interventions in road construction, educational infrastructure and other constituency projects.

He described Kalu as one of their own, noting that his longstanding relationship with the Aro and Ututu people had strengthened his connection with the communities.

In his remarks, the APC House of Representatives candidate for Arochukwu/Ohafia Federal Constituency, Chief Ikenna Nicholas Ukwa, pledged to collaborate with Kalu, if elected, to attract additional federal projects and development opportunities to the constituency.

Ukwa stressed that cooperation between elected representatives at the National Assembly would help address infrastructure deficits and other challenges confronting rural communities.

A community leader, Ohachi Victor, also expressed support for Kalu’s re-election, declaring that Ututu stood firmly behind the senator.

Addressing constituents during the tour, Kalu thanked the traditional ruler, community leaders, women, youths and other stakeholders for their reception and continued goodwill.

The former governor recalled his longstanding relationship with the people of Ututu, particularly the opportunities he provided for indigenes of the community to serve in his administration.

He also highlighted his constituency interventions across Arochukwu Local Government Area, including rural road construction and rehabilitation, classroom projects, solar-powered streetlights, educational materials and overseas scholarship opportunities.

Kalu explained that his ward-to-ward engagements were designed to provide an opportunity for direct interaction with constituents, assess their priorities and identify areas requiring further legislative and developmental attention.

He assured the people that their concerns would continue to receive attention, stressing that effective representation required regular consultation and sustained engagement with communities.

The tour concluded with a reception hosted by Nto at his residence, where Kalu and members of his entourage interacted with party stakeholders and community leaders.

Kalu expressed appreciation to his host for the hospitality and goodwill, while reiterating his commitment to strengthening his relationship with the people of Ututu and the wider Arochukwu Local Government Area.

The post 2027: Nto backs Orji Kalu’s re-election, says senator has no competitor, declares Abia APC united appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: EPL: Alonso reveals why Chelsea lost 4-1 to Leeds United
description:
Chelsea manager, Xabi Alonso, has attributed his side’s 4-1 defeat to Leeds United to a loss of confidence and mental weakness among his players.
The Blues suffered a disappointing defeat at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, extending their poor run of form in the Premier League.
Speaking after the match
content:
Chelsea manager, Xabi Alonso, has attributed his side’s 4-1 defeat to Leeds United to a loss of confidence and mental weakness among his players.

The Blues suffered a disappointing defeat at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, extending their poor run of form in the Premier League.

Speaking after the match, Alonso said Chelsea lost their momentum after conceding the equaliser, adding that his players struggled to recover mentally.

Emmanuel Emegha had given Chelsea the lead in the 25th minute, but Noah Okafor restored parity for Leeds three minutes later.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin put the visitors ahead from the penalty spot in the 53rd minute before Okafor scored his second goal five minutes later. Brenden Aaronson completed the victory with a stoppage-time goal.

Alonso admitted that his players were not strong enough to respond to the setback.

“We probably are in a fragile moment mentally. When we receive a punch, we don’t recover strongly enough. That was my feeling today,” he said.
The Spanish tactician added that Chelsea needed to work collectively to find solutions and improve their performances.

“We need to find solutions because there will be setbacks during any game. We need to be tougher and be able to go through those moments,” he added.

The defeat leaves Chelsea with three losses in their last four Premier League matches, increasing the pressure on Alonso.

The Blues will look to return to winning ways when they face Nottingham Forest in their next league fixture.

The post EPL: Alonso reveals why Chelsea lost 4-1 to Leeds United appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Nigerians can’t endure another Tinubu term, Obi is our hope – NDC chairman
description:
From Adesuwa Tsan, Abuja
The national chairman of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Senator Moses Zuwoghe, has urged Nigerians to vote out President Bola Tinubu in 2027, saying the country cannot afford another four years under an administration that has failed to address economic hardship, ins
content:
From Adesuwa Tsan, Abuja

The national chairman of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Senator Moses Zuwoghe, has urged Nigerians to vote out President Bola Tinubu in 2027, saying the country cannot afford another four years under an administration that has failed to address economic hardship, insecurity and the rising cost of living.

Moses declared that the presidential candidate of the NDC, Peter Obi, remained the only hope for Nigeria at this time, arguing that the country needed leadership capable of protecting lives, repositioning the economy and rebuilding national institutions.

He spoke at the celebration of his 57th birthday in Yenagoa, Bayelsa State, where he urged Nigerians to treat the 2027 presidential election as a referendum on the performance of the Tinubu administration.

The NDC chairman said a second-term mandate should be earned through tangible achievements rather than political sentiments, insisting that Nigerians must hold leaders accountable for their performance in office.

“Second-term election is a referendum. It is standing on the leg of your previous performance. If you have done well, they give you another mandate. If you have not done well, they ask you to go home,” he said.

Moses urged Nigerians to exercise their civic responsibility by voting out Tinubu, whom he accused of failing to provide the security, economic stability and policies needed to improve the living conditions of citizens.

He said the worsening hardship across the country made it imperative for voters to scrutinise the candidates seeking to succeed Tinubu, rather than allow religious considerations, party loyalty or political sentiments to determine their choices.

According to him, Nigerians should evaluate presidential candidates based on their records, competence and capacity to understand the country’s challenges and provide workable solutions.

The NDC chairman expressed confidence that Obi possessed the leadership qualities required to steer the country away from its present challenges, describing him as the country’s best option ahead of the 2027 election.

Stakeholders and party members who attended the birthday celebration, including members of the Bayelsa State House of Assembly, NDC candidates, religious leaders and associates, described Moses as a humble, loving and visionary leader whose commitment to service, good governance and human development had continued to inspire those around him.

The party had earlier felicitated Zuwoghe in a statement issued by its national publicity secretary, Osa Director, describing him as a leader of “wisdom, maturity and uncommon political dexterity”, adding that he had transformed the NDC into a national political force.

It described the party as one of the fastest-growing opposition platforms in Africa, attributing its growing profile to the chairman’s leadership and commitment to building a political alternative.

title: Death Toll In Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 23
description: The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 23, with 24 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals.The accident occurred when a boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie are
content:
The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 23, with 24 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals.

The accident occurred when a boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw.

The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, saying the boat was travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony on Friday, when it capsized at about 11 a.m.

A preliminary police report indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways.

Following the incident, rescue operations were launched, with several passengers rescued while others were initially reported missing. A survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger boat, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings, suggesting that this might have contributed to the accident.

President Bola Tinubu has expressed condolences to the families of the victims, describing the incident as tragic and directing relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery efforts.

In a statement posted on his X account, Tinubu said, “Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation.”

The President also directed that the presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, on Saturday, be held without much fanfare in honour of those who lost their lives.

“On behalf of the entire nation, I mourn those who lost their lives in the incident and sympathise with their families, the government and the people of Bayelsa State.

“I particularly mourn with Governor Douye Diri over this sad incident. I pray that God Almighty repose their souls and comfort their families,” he said.

Meanwhile, Governor Douye Diri has visited the scene of the accident and is expected to initiate a probe into the circumstances surrounding the tragedy.

The state government has also warned boat operators against overloading, reckless navigation and travelling without life jackets, stressing the need for strict compliance with waterway safety regulations.

It also emphasised the importance of enforcing safety measures to prevent a recurrence of such incidents.

The post Death Toll In Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 23 appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Tinubu cautions police against abuse, charges new cadets on professionalism
description:
From Desmond Mgboh, Kano
President Bola Tinubu has cautioned officers and men of the Nigeria Police Force against abusing the authority of their office.
The President gave the warning on Saturday at the passing-out parade of the 8th Regular Course cadets of the Nigeria Police Academy, Wudil, Kano St
content:
From Desmond Mgboh, Kano

President Bola Tinubu has cautioned officers and men of the Nigeria Police Force against abusing the authority of their office.

The President gave the warning on Saturday at the passing-out parade of the 8th Regular Course cadets of the Nigeria Police Academy, Wudil, Kano State.

Represented by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, Tinubu urged the new officers not to use the authority of their offices for oppression, intimidation or personal enrichment.

He said police uniforms represent public trust and responsibility, and charged the officers to protect all Nigerians irrespective of ethnicity, religion or political affiliation.

He further urged them to respect the Constitution, uphold citizens’ fundamental rights and preserve the rule of law in the discharge of their duties.

“Officers should uphold integrity, professionalism, discipline and respect for human rights in the discharge of their duties,” the President said.

Tinubu congratulated the 845 graduating cadets on completing their five-year academic and professional training, describing their achievement as a demonstration of resilience, discipline and commitment to national service.

He also commended their parents, as well as the management and instructors of the Academy, for their contributions to national service.

The President assured the officers of the Federal Government’s commitment to police reforms, improved personnel welfare, adequate equipment and professional training, including the proposed establishment of state police.

In his remarks, the Commandant of the Academy, AIG Auwal Musa, described the ceremony as the culmination of five years of academic development, discipline and professional training.

He expressed appreciation to the President for supporting the institution and for approving the establishment of another campus at Iperu, Ogun State, with take-off funding provided.
