title: Tinubu Urges Newly Commissioned Police Officers To Uphold Integrity, Professionalism
description: President Bola Tinubu has charged newly commissioned police officers to uphold professionalism, integrity, discipline and respect for the fundamental rights of citizens in the discharge of their duties.Tinubu gave the charge at the graduation ceremony of 845 cadets of Regular Course 8 of the Nigeria
content:
President Bola Tinubu has charged newly commissioned police officers to uphold professionalism, integrity, discipline and respect for the fundamental rights of citizens in the discharge of their duties.

Tinubu gave the charge at the graduation ceremony of 845 cadets of Regular Course 8 of the Nigeria Police Academy (POLAC).

The graduation is expected to boost the operational capacity of the Nigeria Police Force and strengthen efforts to address the country’s evolving security challenges.

The President, who was represented by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume, said the officers were graduating at a critical period when Nigeria was undertaking reforms in its policing structure, including moves towards the establishment of state police.

He urged the new officers to embrace modern policing approaches, leverage technology, strengthen intelligence-led operations and build meaningful partnerships with communities and other security agencies.

Tinubu emphasised that the police uniform represents public trust and responsibility, warning the officers against using their authority for oppression, intimidation or personal enrichment.

According to him, the true measure of their service would be the lives they protect, the communities they secure and the confidence they inspire among Nigerians.

The President also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to police reforms, improved personnel welfare, modern equipment, professional training and technological advancement to enhance effective service delivery.

Earlier, the Commandant of the Nigeria Police Academy, AIG Auwalu Musa Muhammad, expressed appreciation to the Federal Government for its continued support towards strengthening the institution.

He particularly acknowledged Tinubu’s approval for the establishment of another campus of the academy in Iperu, Ogun State, saying the initiative would expand police training capacity and address the country’s growing manpower requirements.

Muhammad said the expansion would complement the existing campus in Wudil, Kano State, while promoting higher standards of academic development, professional competence and institutional growth.

He also commended the reconstitution of the academy’s governing council, describing it as an important step towards strengthening institutional governance, accountability and strategic direction.

According to Very Nigerian, the suit, marked FHC/LAG/CS/1568/2026, was filed at the Federal High Court in Lagos.

title: Jimmy Odukoya sues sister, seven others over removal as senior pastor
description:
The Senior Pastor of the Fountain of Life Church, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, has approached the Federal High Court in Lagos to challenge his purported removal from office and the decisions taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees.
Odukoya, alongside the Incorporated Trustees of the Fountai
content:
The Senior Pastor of the Fountain of Life Church, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, has approached the Federal High Court in Lagos to challenge his purported removal from office and the decisions taken by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees.

Odukoya, alongside the Incorporated Trustees of the Fountain of Life Church, instituted the action against eight defendants, including Pastor Tolu Odukoya, Mr Biodun Balogun, Mr Biodun Awosika, Pastor Rotimi Okpaise, Pastor Tobi Enuha, Pastor Gbenga Onabanjo, Pastor Fred Ohiani and Pastor Akin Osinbajo.

The court processes, dated November 20, 2026, include an originating summons, a motion on notice and affidavits sworn to by Odukoya in support of the applications.

PUNCH Online sighted the originating summons and other court processes on Saturday.

In the originating summons, the plaintiffs are asking the court to determine whether meetings held by some members of the church’s Board of Trustees on January 22, February 28 and November 16, 2026, and the decisions taken at those meetings complied with the church’s constitution.

Odukoya said he was appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees at an emergency meeting of the board on September 14, 2023, and was subsequently installed in September of the same year.

He said the church and its organs were governed by its constitution, amended by a special resolution dated January 16, 2003, and that the defendants were members of its Board of Trustees.

According to his affidavit, the disagreement began after a December 19, 2025, meeting of the board, attended by Bishop Mike Okonkwo, at which the possibility of handing over the church’s administrative arm to the Associate Senior Pastor was discussed.

He said no resolution or final decision was reached at the meeting.

Odukoya said he subsequently convened a board meeting for January 5, 2026, but it could not hold because there was no quorum. He added that some trustees later presented proposals to him, many of which he declined because, according to him, they were inconsistent with the church’s constitution.

He said the trustees subsequently sent him a letter dated January 7, 2026, requesting a response within three days, but he did not see it until after the deadline had elapsed.

Odukoya said he later directed the board secretary to schedule a meeting for January 30, 2026, after a request for a special meeting was made by a board member.

However, he alleged that a separate notice for a meeting on January 22 was circulated by the fourth defendant and did not come from the board secretariat.

“I received the notice late in the evening of January 20, 2026, effectively giving me one day notice of the purported meeting,” he stated.

He said he declined to attend the meeting, but the defendants proceeded with it under the name of “concerned members of the Board”.

According to him, they “purportedly adopted a number of resolutions” which included separating the offices of Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees, suspending the board secretary and a church pastor, dissolving the church’s Executive Council and amending its constitution.

Odukoya said a series of conciliatory meetings followed but produced no meaningful result. He added that another meeting was held on February 9, 2026, where he reiterated his position on the disagreement.

He said he was subsequently invited to a meeting with Bishop Okonkwo and, following an understanding reached there, wrote to the concerned members of the board on February 13. The trustees replied on February 15, while he responded on February 20.

At the February 28 meeting, Odukoya alleged that some individuals convened a gathering which was neither a board meeting nor a meeting of the church council.

“Nonetheless, a vote was taken among those present, and I was purportedly removed as the Chairman of the Board,” he stated.

He said he responded to the purported removal in a letter dated March 2, 2026, addressed to the concerned trustees.

The pastor further alleged that the defendants caused an individual describing herself as an interim secretary to issue notices for board meetings, despite what he said was the failure to validly remove the substantive secretary in accordance with the church’s constitution.

Odukoya said the defendants later issued a notice for another board meeting scheduled for November 16, 2026, which he said was served on November 14.

He said he objected to what he described as the continued disregard for the church’s constitution in a letter dated November 15, but the meeting went ahead.

“The Defendants upon their meeting on November 16, 2026, wrote to me the letter dated November 17, 2026, which purports to remove me as the Senior Pastor and Chairman, Board of Trustees, upon some bogus facts,” he stated.

He maintained that the three disputed meetings and the decisions taken at them violated the church’s constitution.

“I know, by my knowledge of the provisions of the 1st Plaintiff’s Constitution, that the meetings on 22nd January, 2026, 28th February, 2026 and 16th November, 2026 held by the Defendants either amongst themselves or with other persons in attendance and all the decisions and resolutions emanating therefrom are in contravention of the constitution of the 1st Defendant,” he said.

In his application for urgent intervention, Odukoya also alleged that the defendants had plans to disrupt church meetings to prevent him from carrying out his duties.

“Despite their disregard for the constitution of the 1st Plaintiff, the Defendants have perfected the plan to violently disrupt any meeting of the 1st Plaintiff with a view to violently prevent me from performing my duties as the Senior Pastor of the church,” he stated.

He further alleged that the defendants were influential and had the capacity to use law enforcement agents to enforce what he described as illegal resolutions.

Odukoya said he feared that the dispute could disrupt church activities and lead to a breach of peace if the defendants were not restrained.

“Unless the Defendants are urgently restrained by an order of this Honourable Court, the Defendants will continue with their nefarious activities, wreaking havoc on the activities of the church which may lead to counter reactions by those opposed to them and which may result in a breach of peace,” he stated.

Explaining why he considered the matter urgent, he described himself as a public figure and an inspiration to young people.

“I am a clergy, a public figure and an inspiration to many young persons all over the world; a single public embarrassment and scandalous encounter would have irreparable effect on my personality, and this would definitely negatively affect those persons, especially the young ones, who, by the grace of God, look to me for guidance,” he said.

The pastor is asking the court to restrain the defendants from interfering with his functions and the management of the church’s affairs pending the determination of the dispute.

The court had yet to make a determination on the issues raised in the processes as of the time of filing this report.

The dispute became public on November 17, when some members of the church’s Board of Trustees announced Jimmy’s removal, citing a December 2021 video in which the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, reportedly named Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor and assigned Jimmy an administrative support role and leadership of the youth ministry.

The trustees also raised objections to Jimmy’s remarriage.

However, Jimmy and the church rejected the removal, insisting that his appointment in September 2023 was valid and that the decision violated the church’s constitution.

The trustees later named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise interim spiritual and administrative leader.

On November 18, the Lagos State High Court issued an interim order restraining Jimmy from presenting himself as the church’s senior pastor, a decision he is now challenging at the Federal High Court.

title: Bundesliga: Dortmund beat Gladbach to go top as Bayern drop points
description:
Felix Nmecha scored with 10 minutes remaining to send Borussia Dortmund to the top of the Bundesliga table with a 1-0 win at Borussia Moenchengladbach on Saturday.
Bayern Munich’s 1-1 home draw with Cologne on Friday opened up the door for the chasers but Dortmund had few opportunities until Nmecha’
content:
Felix Nmecha scored with 10 minutes remaining to send Borussia Dortmund to the top of the Bundesliga table with a 1-0 win at Borussia Moenchengladbach on Saturday.

Bayern Munich’s 1-1 home draw with Cologne on Friday opened up the door for the chasers but Dortmund had few opportunities until Nmecha’s late strike.

Dortmund are now outright first on 24 points, with Bayern and Freiburg, who won 1-0 at Elversberg, locked on 22 points.

Bayern also lost Harry Kane to injury in Friday’s draw, with the Ballon d’Or winner set to miss several months after undergoing surgery on his injured ankle earlier on Saturday.

Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck urged his teammates not to get too far ahead of themselves, despite overtaking Bayern.

“The season is only truly decided from March or April onwards. We need to be in the mix by then,” he told reporters.

Dortmund, who travel to Arsenal on Tuesday, knew victory would send them top but the 2024 Champions League finalists had few chances against a stubborn Gladbach.

Nmecha, who scored twice in Dortmund’s 2-1 win over Elversberg before the international break, looked most likely when his header forced a save from Daniel Batz.

With 17 minutes left, Marcel Sabitzer chipped a free-kick inches wide of the post.

Dortmund continued to push and Nmecha was on hand to knock a rebound through Batz’s fingers and help the visitors snare a crucial three points.

Igor Matanovic’s 68th-minute strike helped Freiburg break down promoted Elversberg and move level with Bayern.

Last season’s Europa League finalists Freiburg stay one point ahead of fourth-placed RB Leipzig, who romped to a 5-1 victory at Union Berlin.

Antonio Nusa, Romulo, Brajan Gruda, Rocco Reitz and Ridle Baku scored for Leipzig, who host Lens in the Champions League on Tuesday.

Gruda was particularly impressive with a goal and an assist, just days after impressing for Jurgen Klopp’s Germany with a goal and two assists versus the Netherlands on the other side of the German capital.

Elsewhere, Afonso Moreira broke his Bundesliga duck with a brace in Bayer Leverkusen’s 4-0 home win over Paderborn.

Moreira had failed to find the net since his summer move from Lyon but scored Leverkusen’s first two goals and laid on one for Ezequiel Fernandez.

Patrik Schick also got a goal to move level with Niclas Fuellkrug atop the league goalscoring charts with nine goals.

Jonathan Burkardt scored the only goal as Eintracht Frankfurt beat Hoffenheim at home.

Frankfurt goalkeeper Noah Atubolu saved a first-half Andrej Kramaric penalty to keep his remarkable spot-kick record alive.

Atubolu has saved seven out of the 11 penalties he has faced, which is the best save percentage in the Bundesliga’s 64-year history.

In Saturday’s late game, Stuttgart will hope to warm up for Wednesday’s trip to Inter Milan when they face strugglers Schalke away.

AFP

title: ‘Buhari rescued my business at its lowest point’ –  BUA chairman Abdul Samad Rabiu reveals
description: Chairman of BUA Group, Abdul Samad Rabiu, has revealed that he committed N500 million to the acquisition and distribution of the authorised biography of late former President Muhammadu Buhari because of the personal support he received from the former Nigerian leader during difficult periods of his
content:
Chairman of BUA Group, Abdul Samad Rabiu, has revealed that he committed N500 million to the acquisition and distribution of the authorised biography of late former President Muhammadu Buhari because of the personal support he received from the former Nigerian leader during difficult periods of his life.

Rabiu described Buhari as an “iroko tree” he leaned on during some of the most challenging moments of his life.

According to a statement issued on Saturday by the Muhammadu Buhari Foundation, the billionaire businessman made the remarks during the public presentation of the book titled Buhari: The Authorised Biography.

Rabiu, who was represented at the event by former Senator representing Zamfara North, Lawal Shuaibu, delivered a personal tribute in honour of the late former president, explaining the reason behind his financial commitment to the publication and distribution of the book.

The business tycoon drew on private memories, saying his relationship with Buhari spanned friendship, family ties, mentorship and moments of acute business adversity.

He said, “President Muhammadu Buhari was everything to me. He was a father, a mentor, a trusted friend and a pillar of strength to my family and me.”

He said the relationship prompted his N500m commitment to preserving the memory of the former president who passed away in July 2025 at a London medical facility.

Rabiu recalled one particularly difficult period when “disputes with government agencies threatened the survival of his business.”

At that point, he said, Buhari stood by him, resisted external pressure and insisted on acting according to what he considered just.

The reassurance, Rabiu said, moved him to tears.

“For that, I will remain eternally grateful to him. It is something I will never forget for as long as I live,” he stated.

He said “Buhari’s intervention had saved the business.”

Rabiu also described Buhari as a “cherished family friend” whose role in his life exceeded the formal boundaries of politics, government and commerce.

He recounted, “He was an iroko tree upon which I leaned when my strength was failing.”

Rabiu described Buhari as a man of integrity, humility and simplicity, who also prized loyalty, friendship and family.

“To the nation, he was a President and a statesman to me and my family, he was much more,” he stated.

According to the statement, the presentation was devoted to placing Buhari’s life before the judgement of history through the three-volume authorised biography written by Dr. Udu Yakubu.

Rabiu said the books deserved support because Buhari’s “life, service and legacy deserve to be remembered and celebrated for generations to come.”

He said his N500m acquisition commitment is based on his personal memory of Buhari as father figure, mentor, friend and protector.

It is also meant to preserve Buhari’s life and record through books intended to pass into homes, libraries, educational institutions and the wider national archive, said Rabiu.

title: Atiku advocates human capital revolution, AI-driven development as United Nigeria Airlines boss, Okonkwo hails his visionary investment in education
description:
From Billy Abel, Yola
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has called for a fundamental reorientation of Nigeria’s development priorities towards human capital investment, technological innovation and artificial intelligence, declaring that the country’s greatest national resource is its people, par
content:
From Billy Abel, Yola

Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has called for a fundamental reorientation of Nigeria’s development priorities towards human capital investment, technological innovation and artificial intelligence, declaring that the country’s greatest national resource is its people, particularly its young population.

Atiku, who spoke through his representative, former governor Rotimi Amaechi, at the 18th Founders’ Day celebration of the American University of Nigeria (AUN), Yola, on Saturday, November 21, 2026, argued that Nigeria’s future would depend largely on its ability to educate, equip, employ and empower its citizens to compete in an increasingly technology-driven global economy.

The event also featured a compelling Founders’ Day lecture by Professor Obiora Okonkwo, OFR, who paid glowing tribute to Atiku’s commitment to educational development, describing him as a visionary institution builder whose investment in AUN represents a profound commitment to the transformation of higher education and human development.

In his address titled ‘The Future We Choose: Human Capital, Artificial Intelligence, and Nigeria’s Renewal’, Atiku maintained that the country’s development challenge was not necessarily a shortage of talent but its failure to consistently develop and deploy the enormous human potential available to it.

He warned that Nigeria must make a deliberate choice between transforming its growing population into a productive, skilled and confident citizenry and allowing demographic expansion to deepen unemployment, insecurity, poverty and social frustration.

According to him, the quality of the country’s human capital, rather than the abundance of its natural resources, will ultimately determine its economic competitiveness and national prosperity.

He observed that the world was entering a new technological age defined by artificial intelligence, automation, robotics, biotechnology and digital networks, technologies that would fundamentally transform virtually every sector, including agriculture, medicine, education, journalism, banking, manufacturing, law and commerce.

While acknowledging the enormous opportunities these developments present, Atiku cautioned that technology could also widen inequality if access remained restricted to a privileged few or if young Africans remained consumers of technological products rather than becoming creators, innovators and problem-solvers.

He therefore called for an education system that prepares young Nigerians not merely to use emerging technologies but to understand, improve, regulate and apply them to address the country’s peculiar developmental challenges.

He stressed the need for Nigerian solutions to Nigerian problems, identifying opportunities for technological applications in agricultural productivity, education in underserved communities, public healthcare, electricity, clean water and the expansion of small businesses.

The former Vice President also advocated a fundamental shift in the philosophy of education, arguing that academic certificates alone were insufficient to prepare graduates for the demands of the contemporary world.

He identified five essential qualities that education must develop: strong foundational knowledge, practical competence, entrepreneurial confidence, ethical judgement and a sense of responsibility to society.

He further challenged universities to evolve beyond traditional institutions of teaching and examinations into centres of innovation, research, entrepreneurship, civic responsibility and economic transformation.

Atiku particularly emphasised AUN’s responsibility to its host region, noting that its location in north-eastern Nigeria placed it in a strategic position to demonstrate that academic excellence could flourish even in challenging environments.

He urged the university to strengthen its commitment to entrepreneurship, technology, research, community engagement and leadership development, while ensuring that talented students from disadvantaged backgrounds were not denied opportunities because of financial circumstances.

He also called for a renewed national compact involving government, the private sector, the diaspora, universities and citizens to strengthen human capital development.

Government, he said, must provide the enabling environment through reliable electricity, affordable connectivity, security, transparent regulation and sustained investment in education and research.

The private sector, in turn, must invest in skills development, internships, technology transfer and local innovation, while the diaspora should be mobilised as a reservoir of knowledge, mentorship, capital and international networks.

He challenged young people to become lifelong learners, embrace technological change and measure success not merely by personal income or positions attained but by the problems they solve, the people they uplift and the institutions they strengthen.

Okonkwo celebrates Atiku’s enduring investment in education

A major highlight of the celebration was the Founders’ Day lecture delivered by Professor Obiora Okonkwo, OFR, titled ‘Purposeful Education and the 21st-Century University: Leadership, Innovation and Social Responsibility’.

The lecture provided an important intellectual complement to Atiku’s address, examining the philosophical foundations of purposeful education and the responsibilities of contemporary universities in responding to the developmental challenges of Nigeria and Africa.

However, beyond its academic arguments, Okonkwo’s address offered a particularly significant appreciation of Atiku’s role in establishing and sustaining the American University of Nigeria.

He described the former Vice President as more than an education enthusiast, characterising him as a visionary and outstanding institution builder whose commitment to AUN transcended the conventional responsibilities of a university founder.

According to Okonkwo, the conception and execution of AUN reflected Atiku’s conviction that transforming university education in this part of the world required an extraordinary level of personal commitment.

He drew attention to the university’s non-profit character, the substantial annual financial support Atiku had provided for nearly two decades, the significant proportion of students benefiting from full scholarships and the relatively affordable fees charged by an institution offering international-standard teaching and infrastructure.

He also acknowledged Atiku’s continued willingness to support major initiatives designed to consolidate AUN’s position as a leading development-oriented university in Africa.

Okonkwo described such commitment as evidence that education, particularly higher education, was a transgenerational investment in national advancement and the cultivation of a more enlightened, productive and transformed society.

He said: “Your Excellency, Sir, thank you for demonstrating, in the most practical way, that education, particularly higher education, is a transgenerational investment, not just in national advancement but also in the cultivation of a more enlightened, productive and qualitatively transformed humanity.”

The professor also celebrated Atiku’s forthcoming 80th birthday on November 25, describing his contributions to humanity as invaluable and expressing gratitude for the opportunity to witness his impact.

Education must go beyond certificates, Okonkwo insists

Moving from the commendation of AUN’s founder to the broader responsibilities of higher education, Okonkwo argued that the fundamental purpose of education must extend beyond the acquisition of academic qualifications to the development of human and social capabilities.

He maintained that a university’s relevance should not be measured exclusively by the number of certificates awarded, research publications produced or institutional prestige accumulated, but also by the capabilities it develops, the problems it helps resolve and the opportunities it creates for society.

He warned against an educational culture that prioritises qualifications without sufficiently developing the capacity of graduates to think critically, solve problems, communicate effectively, collaborate and exercise sound judgement.

According to him, purposeful education should produce individuals who can think clearly, act competently, disagree intelligently, create value and recognise responsibilities beyond personal advancement.

He further argued that the international orientation of a university should not be separated from its national and regional development responsibilities.

Using AUN as an example, he maintained that global academic standards and local developmental relevance were complementary rather than competing objectives.

He explained that international exposure should provide access to global knowledge, comparative standards and research networks, while Nigeria’s developmental realities should determine the relevance and application of such knowledge.

In his assessment, a university that pursues international prestige without addressing local realities risks becoming an institution of display, while one that ignores global intellectual engagement risks becoming academically constrained.

Okonkwo also identified leadership, innovation, research, social responsibility, graduate employability, entrepreneurship, international partnerships and institutional sustainability as essential pillars of the 21st-century university.

He called for university leadership that goes beyond routine administration to embrace institutional stewardship, strategic vision, accountability and the ability to mobilise people and resources towards meaningful objectives.

He further advocated stronger research and innovation ecosystems that connect universities with local governments, schools, healthcare institutions, businesses, civil society organisations and communities.

Such relationships, he argued, would enable universities to translate knowledge into practical solutions and ensure that development became something institutions actively participated in rather than merely discussed in classrooms.

He equally stressed the importance of institutional resilience, financial discipline, environmental sustainability, transparent governance and continuity beyond the tenure of individual leaders.

Addressing students and graduates, Okonkwo challenged them to transform their education into a platform for invention, enterprise and productive engagement.

He urged them to move beyond simply understanding society’s problems to developing the imagination, competence and determination required to design and implement solutions.

AUN announces Medical School, records nearly 1,700 students

The university’s growth, community engagement and future expansion also featured prominently in the welcome address by its President, Dr DeWayne P. Frazier.

Reflecting on the institution’s journey, Frazier disclosed that the 2026 celebration marked 23 years since the groundbreaking of AUN, while acknowledging Atiku’s 80th birthday, which falls on November 25.

He said the university was established around a vision that education should be measured not merely by what students learn in classrooms but by the impact of that learning on their lives and the communities around them.

Frazier highlighted the importance of faculty mentorship, extracurricular activities, student leadership and community engagement as essential components of the university’s educational philosophy.

He particularly referred to AUN’s Feed and Read initiative, through which children in Yola receive meals and opportunities to develop their reading and basic mathematics skills with the assistance of student volunteers.

He disclosed that some of the Almajiri boys participating in the programme would receive full scholarships to study at AUN after completing their junior and senior secondary education, subject to the university’s selection arrangements.

One of the major announcements of the occasion was the appointment of Dr Abdullahi Alkali Abba as the founding Dean of AUN’s Medical School.

Frazier described the proposed medical school as an important opportunity to integrate teaching, research and community service around the healthcare needs of north-eastern Nigeria.

He explained that the initiative would enable the university to deepen research into infectious diseases, improve understanding of community health challenges and prepare future medical professionals to respond more effectively to the circumstances and needs of their patients.

The AUN President also announced that the university had attained a record enrolment of nearly 1,700 students, drawn from all 36 states of Nigeria and more than 20 countries.

He said the growing diversity of the student population reflected the founding vision of building an institution that was accessible to people from different backgrounds and nationalities.

Frazier expressed optimism that AUN’s greatest achievements were still ahead, pledging to sustain its commitment to academic excellence, community development and the preparation of graduates capable of making meaningful contributions to society.

A shared vision for Nigeria’s future

Taken together, the three addresses at the 18th Founders’ Day celebration presented a compelling argument about the relationship between education, leadership, innovation and national development.

While Atiku’s address placed human capital and technological preparedness at the centre of Nigeria’s national renewal, Okonkwo’s lecture examined the institutional and intellectual foundations required to translate education into meaningful social and economic progress.

Frazier’s address, meanwhile, demonstrated how AUN’s founding vision was being translated into practical initiatives through community engagement, student development, institutional expansion and the proposed establishment of a medical school.

The convergence of these perspectives reinforced the underlying philosophy of AUN as a Development University, an institution established to combine international academic standards with the practical demands of Nigeria’s and Africa’s development.

Twenty-three years after its groundbreaking, the university’s 18th Founders’ Day offered an opportunity not only to celebrate its history but also to renew the responsibilities associated with its founding vision.

For Atiku, the future Nigeria chooses will ultimately depend on the quality of its investment in people. For Okonkwo, the university must justify its existence through the knowledge it produces, the capabilities it develops and the problems it helps solve.

And for AUN, the challenge remains to turn that shared vision into an enduring institutional legacy.

The post Atiku advocates human capital revolution, AI-driven development as United Nigeria Airlines boss, Okonkwo hails his visionary investment in education appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

content:
The Traditional Ruler of Ogugu Ntu-egbenese Ancient Kingdom in Awgu Local Government Area of Enugu State, His Royal Highness, Igwe Aloysius Chidozie Ogbonna Jnr, who is also the Akajiofo Ntuegbenese and Isivumkpumenese, has commended Governor Peter Ndubuisi Mbah for recognising an illustrious son of Ntu-egbenese and one of the best from the clan, Senator Jim Ifeanyichukwu Nwobodo, following the governor’s pronouncement to rename the state’s university after him.

He described the decision as a welcome development and a worthy act of immortalising a leader whose hard work and contributions helped make Enugu a renowned Eastern business, social and entertainment hub.

In a congratulatory statement signed by the monarch and sent to newsmen in Enugu on Friday, he stated that Senator Nwobodo’s contributions to the development of the state, the South-East and Nigeria deserve such recognition.

Igwe Ogbonna noted that although some people might consider the recognition late, he believes that it has come at the right time, stressing that it is better to honour great leaders while they are alive and allow them to witness how much their contributions are appreciated. He added that history would remember Governor Mbah for taking this important step to celebrate one of Enugu’s distinguished sons.

The monarch further praised Governor Mbah for demonstrating political courage, historical consciousness and respect for the contributions of past leaders, while also noting that leadership is not only about initiating new projects but also about recognising those whose efforts laid the foundation for present-day achievements.

Akajiofo Ntuegbenese also expressed confidence that the governor would receive similar recognition and honour from future generations for his own contributions to the development of Enugu State.

He assured Governor Mbah of the massive support of the Ntu-egbenese clan, comprising over 30 communities spread across four Local Government Areas of Enugu State.

According to him, “the people of the clan appreciate the governor’s leadership and are prepared to continue supporting his administration and its development agenda. We want him to sustain his commitment to inclusive governance, fairness and the recognition of deserving sons and daughters of the state because the same will be reciprocated to him.”

title: NATO pledges to defend Poland after Russian missile incursion
description:
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte on Saturday pledged to defend Poland after Russian missiles landed in the country, with the alliance’s top decision-making body set to discuss the incident.
Warsaw said two Russian missiles hit its southeast on Friday, accusing the Kremlin of “intentional provocatio
content:
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte on Saturday pledged to defend Poland after Russian missiles landed in the country, with the alliance’s top decision-making body set to discuss the incident.

Warsaw said two Russian missiles hit its southeast on Friday, accusing the Kremlin of “intentional provocation” near where thousands of European troops are holding exercises.

Rutte, on a visit to Warsaw, said the alliance would determine what happened in the incident to identify any vulnerabilities, and pledged to defend Polish territory, in remarks to Polish media.

On Friday Rutte condemned what he said were “grave violations”, calling the incident “clearly dangerous”.

NATO’s main political decision-making body will discuss the incident in Brussels on Monday “as part of regular consultations among allies”, an alliance official told AFP.

Poland will be represented by its deputy defence minister, Pawel Zalewski, according to Polish public radio.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on Friday that Warsaw would ask NATO to strengthen its detection and surveillance systems over Poland, as Russia frequently launches waves of missiles and drones at western Ukraine, near the Polish border.

The Institute for the Study of War (ISW), a US think tank, said it believed Russia “intentionally fired missiles and drones into Polish airspace”.

The gesture was timed to coincide with exercises by the “Coalition of the Willing” taking place in Poland, the ISW said.

“Coalition of the Willing” refers to a group of Ukraine’s European backers who are prepared to send peacekeeping troops to the country.

AFP

title: Makinde’s image on campaign balloon stirs controversy at Tinubu’s Ibadan rally
description:
By Adeola Badru



The image of Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, displayed alongside those of President Bola Tinubu and other political figures on a balloon hoisted at the venue of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Ibadan on Saturday has stirred reactions, drawing a
content:
By Adeola Badru

The image of Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, displayed alongside those of President Bola Tinubu and other political figures on a balloon hoisted at the venue of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Ibadan on Saturday has stirred reactions, drawing attention to the governor’s political stance ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The balloon, which was hoisted at the rally ground around the historic Mapo Hall, featured the images of prominent political figures, including Makinde, who is not a member of the APC and has yet to publicly declare support for Tinubu’s re-election bid.

The development attracted attention at the campaign venue, where the President was expected to rally support for the APC and its candidates ahead of the 2027 elections.

Makinde, who is the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), has been at the centre of political discussions in Oyo State following his emergence as the party’s flag bearer.

His image on the balloon, therefore, raised questions about the message being conveyed by its display at an APC campaign rally, particularly as the political atmosphere in the state continues to intensify ahead of the next general election.

The circumstances surrounding the inclusion of the governor’s image on the balloon were not immediately clear as at the time of filing this report.

Meanwhile, President Tinubu has urged the people of Oyo State to sustain their support for the APC, declaring that continuity was essential for Nigeria’s progress, prosperity and development.

Tinubu, who spoke at the rally, promised increased investment in education, agriculture, industrialisation and electricity supply, while endorsing Senator Sharafadeen Alli as the APC’s governorship candidate in the state.

The President also announced plans to revive the old Leyland factory in Ibadan, saying his administration had signed an agreement with Chinese company Yutong to reopen the facility for the production of public transport vehicles and the establishment of an automobile assembly plant.

“For Oyo State, we have just signed an agreement with China’s Yutong to reopen the old Leyland factory in Ibadan. We are reopening it to produce public transport vehicles and establish an automobile assembly plant there. We will continue to bring industries. You will see progress and development,” Tinubu said.

He also assured residents of improved electricity supply, expressing confidence in the efforts of the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, and his team.

“You will see, and I guarantee you an improvement in electricity. Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe is really working hard with his team,” he said.

Tinubu urged the electorate to remain committed to the APC, reminding them of their support for the party in the previous election.

“You voted overwhelmingly for APC last time. You must stay the course. You must. For the sake of progress, prosperity of our country, development, for your children and our great-grandchildren,” he said.

The President added that the country must prioritise education and agriculture to create opportunities for younger generations.

“We must give them the right education, invest in agriculture,” he said.

He also took a swipe at opposition parties, describing them as “mediocre”, and urged the electorate not to be distracted by them.

Tinubu subsequently declared his support for Alli, urging the people of Oyo State to vote for him in the 2027 governorship election.

“I will show you the governorship candidate in Oyo State that you must vote for, and is Sen. Sharafadeen Alli,” he said.

The rally was preceded by the arrival of the President at the Ladoke Akintola Airport, Ibadan, where the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, and other traditional rulers received him.

The monarchs, drawn from the Ibadan, Ibarapa, Oyo, Ogbomoso and Oke-Ogun zones, reaffirmed their support for Tinubu’s re-election bid.

Welcoming the President on behalf of the Oyo State Council of Obas and Chiefs, Ladoja described Tinubu as the leader the monarchs had been waiting to receive.

“This is the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu that we have been waiting for,” the Olubadan said.

The monarch commended the President for infrastructure projects across the country, particularly in the South-West, including the Leyland Motor Assembly project, the Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode Road and the Ibadan-Oyo Road.

He, however, urged that ongoing projects be completed before fresh requests were made for additional ones.

Tinubu thanked the monarchs for their prayers and co-operation, urging them to encourage their subjects to participate in the forthcoming election.

The President also called for a minute’s silence in honour of those who lost their lives in a boat accident in Bayelsa State, expressing sympathy with the bereaved families.

Earlier, chaos had broken out at the rally venue as hoodlums clashed before the President’s arrival, with gunshots fired into the air.

The incident caused panic among supporters, who scampered for safety as the situation deteriorated.

Some of the hoodlums were seen dragging a firearm reportedly used by an unidentified man, while others hurled sticks and placards towards the media stand, disrupting activities at the venue.

The scuffle dispersed parts of the crowd and briefly disrupted preparations for the President’s arrival.

title: 2027: Tinubu throws weight behind Alli, Yayi, Hamzat at APC rally in Ibadan
description:
President Bola Tinubu on Saturday publicly declared his support for the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidates in Oyo, Ogun and Lagos states during the party’s campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State.
The President endorsed the candidates by raising their hands before party supporters a
content:
President Bola Tinubu on Saturday publicly declared his support for the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidates in Oyo, Ogun and Lagos states during the party’s campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State.

The President endorsed the candidates by raising their hands before party supporters at the rally held at Mapo Hall.

Addressing the crowd, Tinubu said, “The governor you will vote for, I will show you,” before raising the hand of Senator Sharafadeen Alli, the APC governorship candidate in Oyo State.

He also presented Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, as the party’s candidate for Ogun State, raising his hand in a show of support.

Tinubu subsequently raised the hand of Obafemi Hamzat, the APC governorship candidate in Lagos State, publicly endorsing the three aspirants ahead of the forthcoming governorship elections.
The President also raised the hand of Remi Oseni, the APC senatorial candidate for Oyo South.

The endorsements came as the ruling party intensified its campaign ahead of the 2027 general elections, with Tinubu using his visit to his home region to rally support for the party’s candidates.

The Ibadan event was the South-West leg of Tinubu’s re-election campaign and the seventh state rally he had attended since the exercise began in Kaduna on October 24.

Vice-President Kashim Shettima, APC governors, members of the National Assembly and other party leaders attended the rally.

The President had directed that the rally be held without much fanfare in honour of victims of a boat accident in Ukubie, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, on Friday.

In a statement announcing the directive, Tinubu said the decision was taken “in honour of the lives lost and in sympathy with the relatives and families of those involved in the disaster”.

The Oyo governorship contest is particularly significant for the APC as the party seeks to take control of the state from Governor Seyi Makinde, who is seeking the presidency under the Allied Peoples Movement.

Alli, who represents Oyo South in the Senate, was endorsed as the APC’s consensus governorship candidate in May following consultations among party leaders.

In Ogun, Adeola, who represents Ogun West in the Senate, is the APC’s governorship candidate, while Hamzat, the incumbent deputy governor of Lagos State, is the party’s flagbearer in the state.

Tinubu’s public show of support for the three candidates at the rally placed the party’s governorship contests alongside his own re-election campaign, as APC leaders seek to consolidate support across the South-West.

title: Camosunate not banned in Nigeria — NAFDAC
description:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control has dismissed claims circulating on social media that Camosunate, an antimalarial medicine, has been banned in Nigeria.
The agency said it had never banned Camosunate or medicines containing the artesunate-amodiaquine combination, urgi
content:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control has dismissed claims circulating on social media that Camosunate, an antimalarial medicine, has been banned in Nigeria.

The agency said it had never banned Camosunate or medicines containing the artesunate-amodiaquine combination, urging members of the public to disregard the reports.

NAFDAC made the clarification in a press release on Saturday which was signed by its Director-General, Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye.

“The Agency clarifies that it has never banned Camosunate or medicines containing the artesunate-amodiaquine combination,” the statement read.

It explained that some of the symptoms mentioned in the viral claims could be associated with known side effects of the medicine.

“Some of the symptoms reported in the viral claim may be associated with known side effects of Camosunate, including nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, headache, dizziness, drowsiness and loss of appetite,” it stated.

However, the agency said suspected adverse drug reactions should be reported for proper assessment rather than being circulated as claims of a ban.

“However, suspected adverse drug reactions should be reported to NAFDAC for proper assessment,” it added.

The regulatory agency encouraged members of the public and healthcare professionals to report suspected reactions through its Med Safety App, which is available for download on Android and iOS devices, or at the nearest NAFDAC office.

“Members of the public and healthcare professionals are encouraged to report suspected adverse drug reactions through the NAFDAC Med Safety App, available for download on Android and iOS devices, or at the nearest NAFDAC office,” the statement read.

NAFDAC also urged Nigerians to stop spreading the claim, particularly on social media, warning against the circulation of unverified information about the medicine.

“NAFDAC urges the public to stop circulating the false claim. Those who have already shared it are encouraged to disseminate this clarification through the same channels to help counter misinformation and prevent unnecessary public concern,” it stated.

The agency’s clarification comes amid the circulation of social media claims alleging that Camosunate had been banned in Nigeria because of reported adverse effects.

description:
African Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has condemned the attack on former Super Eagles captain, Segun Odegbami, at his residence in Abeokuta, Ogun State.
Atiku described the incident as disturbing, saying no Nigerian, irrespective of age, should feel unsafe in the comfor
content:
African Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has condemned the attack on former Super Eagles captain, Segun Odegbami, at his residence in Abeokuta, Ogun State.

Atiku described the incident as disturbing, saying no Nigerian, irrespective of age, should feel unsafe in the comfort of their home.

He made the remarks in a post on X on Saturday, where he also wished the former footballer a speedy and complete recovery and called on security authorities to apprehend those responsible for the attack.

“I was saddened to learn of the attack on Chief Segun Odegbami at his home in Abeokuta. Mathematical, as a generation of fans called him, gave Nigeria some of its proudest football memories.

“I wish him a swift and complete recovery, and I urge the authorities to find those responsible. No Nigerian, young or old, should feel unsafe in their own bedroom,” he wrote.

Odegbami, popularly known as Mathematical, reportedly escaped death after he was attacked with a machete at his residence in Abeokuta.

The former Green Eagles captain was said to have sustained injuries during the incident, which raised concerns about his safety.

Odegbami is one of Nigeria’s most celebrated footballers and played a leading role in the country’s victory at the 1980 Africa Cup of Nations, Nigeria’s first continental title.

He was also a key member of the national team that represented the country at the 1980 Olympic Games in Moscow and later became a prominent figure in sports administration and football development.

The attack has drawn attention to security concerns surrounding residents, with Atiku urging the authorities to ensure that those behind the incident are brought to justice.

title: REC confirms 2.8m registered voters in Edo
description:
By Ozioruva Aliu



BENIN CITY – THE Edo State Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC), Obo Effanga yest said that the state currently has 2.8 million registered voters.



According to him, the last registration exercise raised the figure adding that the final figure would be released after the recen
content:
By Ozioruva Aliu

BENIN CITY – THE Edo State Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC), Obo Effanga yest said that the state currently has 2.8 million registered voters.

According to him, the last registration exercise raised the figure adding that the final figure would be released after the recent clean up exercise by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

Giving an update on the Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) collection in Benin City, Effanga said a total of 23,401 cards had been collected across the state since distribution commenced on October 9.

He explained that the figure comprised 6,319 old PVCs, 5,128 newly produced cards and 11,954 PVCs relating to transfers.

Effanga noted, “The state currently has 2.8 million registered voters after the last registration exercise. However, the final figure would be released after the recent clean up exercise by the national body.”

The REC disclosed that PVCs for voters who registered during the first and second phases of the Continuous Voter Registration exercise were currently available for collection at INEC offices across the 18 local government areas of the state.

The Resident Commissioner said the commission was currently working towards ensuring a smooth electoral process.

Speaking on the mock accreditation exercise scheduled for November 28, the REC said the exercise would be conducted in 384 polling units across the state.

He said two polling units were selected from each of the 192 wards also known as registration areas for the mock exercise.

“The exercise would provide an opportunity to test the commission’s electoral technology and assess the readiness of its personnel ahead of the elections.

“The state office had submitted the list of proposed polling units to the commission’s headquarters for approval,” he added.

He said the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System would be deployed during the exercise to demonstrate how voters are accredited, how results are captured and how they are transmitted to the INEC Result Viewing Portal.

title: Man City Stumble Again In Fulham Draw
content:
Manchester City’s winless Premier League run extended to four games after failing to beat Fulham for the first time in 21 attempts on Saturday.

Arsenal can open up an eight-point lead at the top of the table with victory at Newcastle later as City’s title challenge wilts in the wake of a guilty verdict on widespread breaches of financial rules.

The club deny any wrongdoing but are likely to be hit with a severe points penalty, and possibly even relegation, unless they overturn the ruling on appeal.

After seven consecutive league wins to start Enzo Maresca’s reign, the off-field uncertainty appears to have derailed City’s quest to topple defending champions Arsenal.

Fulham had lost every meeting against City for the past 15 years but got their reward after striking early through Rodrigo Muniz.

The home side were furious that Erling Haaland’s equaliser before half-time was controversially ruled out as the Norwegian was deemed to have kicked the ball out of the grasp of Bernd Leno.

Elliot Anderson’s sweet strike saved City from a fourth consecutive defeat, but they were booed off after another disappointing display.

“Almost 80 percent of the goals we concede are in the first 20 minutes and it’s for sure something we need to improve,” said Maresca.

Bournemouth climbed into the Champions League places as their sensational run continued with a 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest.

Evanilson struck for the sixth consecutive league game and Justin Kluivert added a second as the Cherries’ winning run in all competitions stretched to nine games.

Tottenham are also marching up the table after a difficult start to the campaign.

Teenager Luca Williams-Barnett was the star of a 2-0 win over Ipswich as he netted on his first Premier League start before Dominic Solanke added a second to secure a fourth win in five for Roberto De Zerbi’s men.

Thomas Frank’s arrival at Crystal Palace failed to inspire a turnaround in the Eagles’ fortunes as they lost 3-2 at Coventry to remain bottom of the table.

Dwight McNeil’s late own goal gave the Sky Blues a vital victory in their quest for survival back in the top flight after four goals were shared in a thrilling first half.

Sunderland frustrated Aston Villa in a 0-0 draw that lifted the Black Cats above Manchester United in the relegation zone.

Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of United for the first time at Liverpool on Sunday with the Red Devils second bottom of the table.

title: Jonathan: Nigeria needs honest leaders to restore global respect
description:
…Ex-President condemns money-driven politics, primitive wealth accumulation



…Says democracy has standards, calls for investment in younger generation



By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief



Former President Goodluck Jonathan has called for purposeful, honest and visionary political leadership to r
content:
…Ex-President condemns money-driven politics, primitive wealth accumulation

…Says democracy has standards, calls for investment in younger generation

By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

Former President Goodluck Jonathan has called for purposeful, honest and visionary political leadership to rebuild Nigeria’s battered international image and restore the respect the country once commanded globally.

Jonathan, who spoke at the Paul Alaje Colloquium, themed “The Nigeria Brand”, in Abuja yesterday, said the country needed leaders who were deliberate about national development rather than personal wealth accumulation.

He lamented that the quality of politics currently practised in Nigeria was undermining democracy and threatening the country’s progress.

“Some of what goes on in our political space does not represent democracy. The brand of politics we are playing will set us backwards. Democracy has standards,” he said.

The former president criticised politicians who lacked knowledge of their parties’ manifestos, noting that many of the documents were prepared by hired consultants without any meaningful commitment from the candidates.

He urged political leaders to emulate the late Chief Obafemi Awolowo, whose clear vision and commitment to compulsory education transformed the old Western Region.

According to Jonathan, Awolowo’s education policy produced remarkable results, with the South-West at a point having more professors than the rest of Nigeria combined.

He challenged present-day leaders to abandon primitive accumulation of wealth and invest in the younger generation, stressing that leadership should be measured by the legacy left behind.

“Why will you stomach what you are supposed to invest in the younger generation at a time you know your time on earth is really not much?” he asked.

Speaking on the importance of a strong national identity, Jonathan said a country’s brand went beyond public relations, reflecting its character, leadership, institutions and development aspirations.

“A strong national brand attracts investment, tourism, international partnerships and opportunities for its citizens. It inspires patriotism at home and commands respect abroad.

“Therefore, discussing the Nigeria brand is not an exercise in public relations. It is a conversation about national character, leadership, development and the kind of country we want to leave to our children,” he said.

Jonathan recalled that Nigeria once enjoyed considerable international respect and influence but regretted that its reputation had suffered significant setbacks.

He identified insecurity, corruption, economic difficulties, unemployment, political instability and negative perceptions of public institutions as factors damaging the country’s image.

The former president particularly expressed concern over the limited international mobility associated with the Nigerian passport, which exposes citizens to considerable visa restrictions and difficulties travelling abroad.

However, he cautioned against equating the country’s challenges with the character of its people, maintaining that millions of Nigerians remained honest, industrious, talented and respected internationally.

He attributed the deterioration of Nigeria’s national identity partly to the erosion of societal values, where wealth was celebrated without questions about its source, while honesty, hard work and integrity received insufficient recognition.

Other factors, he said, included corruption, abuse of public office, impunity, weakened public institutions and insecurity, which had created doubts about the ability of the state to guarantee the safety of lives and property.

To reverse the trend, Jonathan called for stronger leadership and governance, insisting that public office must be treated as a position of trust.

He said merit, competence, transparency, accountability and the rule of law must become the guiding principles of public administration.

He also advocated reforms in political recruitment, stronger internal party democracy, credible elections and a political culture that rewards ideas, character and competence rather than money, patronage and sectional interests.

In his remarks, the convener of the colloquium, Dr. Paul Alaje, challenged Nigerians to examine the country’s international reputation by considering whether the world could trust Nigeria enough to invest in it and entrust its resources and future to its institutions.

He said the Nigeria brand was fundamentally about the country’s institutions and what they represented.

Alaje identified a troubling paradox in Nigeria’s development, noting that despite its enormous human capital and global achievements in music, film, literature, technology, medicine, finance, academia and engineering, the country continued to struggle with basic human development indicators.

He questioned how a country blessed with enormous human capital could struggle with human development, abundant agricultural potential yet find it difficult to feed its population, and a vibrant entrepreneurial spirit without an enabling business environment.

According to him, Nigeria must stop confusing potential with progress and deliberately address the structural challenges holding it back.

He cited China, India and South Africa as countries that had worked to change their international narratives, arguing that Nigeria could achieve similar results through deliberate policies and consistent implementation.

Alaje expressed concern over Nigeria’s poor life expectancy and widespread poverty, saying the country needed to become intentional about improving the living conditions of its citizens.

He called for policies that would encourage domestic production of goods for local consumption and export, while urging state governments to collaborate with the federal government and private-sector operators to expand electricity supply under the new electricity regulatory framework.

He also advocated productivity-enhancing policies in agriculture, more efficient transportation systems and increased investment in health and education as critical measures for raising living standards and rebuilding confidence in Nigeria.

The post Jonathan: Nigeria needs honest leaders to restore global respect appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Tankers Struck In Hormuz, As Iran Says Held Talks With Mediator Qatar
description: Two tankers were attacked on Saturday in the Strait of Hormuz, at the heart of the conflict between Iran and the United States, a maritime monitor said, as Tehran announced a visit from mediator Qatar.Negotiations between the US and Iran to end their war have stalled, months after it began with US-I
content:
Two tankers were attacked on Saturday in the Strait of Hormuz, at the heart of the conflict between Iran and the United States, a maritime monitor said, as Tehran announced a visit from mediator Qatar.

Negotiations between the US and Iran to end their war have stalled, months after it began with US-Israeli strikes on the Islamic Republic in late February.

The Strait of Hormuz has become the focus of the stalemated conflict, with Iran continuing in its efforts to blockade the waterway and targeting vessels that cross without its authorisation.

The US military, meanwhile, has been escorting ships through the strategic strait, which carried one-fifth of the world’s oil before the war, and maintains its own counterblockade of Iranian ports.

Iranian deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on Saturday that a Qatari delegation visited Tehran the previous evening and “held two hours of talks”, without providing details.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said: “The ongoing talks in the region must be given a chance, and the blockade must be lifted rationally.”

“Our position is clear: as long as Iran’s demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless,” he said, quoted by state television.

“At the same time, we have always affirmed our readiness for dialogue, just as we are ready to defend ourselves.”

Iran’s conditions have included ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the US counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

Shot Down Drone

On Saturday, British maritime agency UKMTO said: “A tanker transiting outbound in the Strait of Hormuz has been hit on the stern by an unknown projectile.”

“There are no reported casualties at this time,” it added, saying that another tanker was struck in its engine room.

Iran’s army on Saturday said a ship was on fire after hitting a mine in the strait.

“Before noon today, a violating oil tanker that had entered a restricted zone east of the Strait of Hormuz caught fire after striking a naval mine,” Iran’s army naval forces said in a statement carried by state TV.

The tanker “had its identification and navigation systems switched off, in defiance of issued warnings and maritime transit regulations”, it added.

In recent weeks, Tehran has made multiple announcements saying ships have caught fire in the strait, often claiming they struck mines.

But the US military recently said it had cleared all mines from the main routes through the waterway.

US Central Command, which oversees US military operations in the region, said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.

Iran said on Saturday it shot down a US drone over Qeshm Island in the strait, according to state TV.

American fighter jets struck an Iranian missile site on Qeshm last Tuesday, according to a US military official.

‘Clear Red Lines’

In August, Washington announced what it called an “economic asphyxiation” campaign on Iran aimed at curbing its trade and financial flows.

On Saturday, Gharibabadi said, according to Iran’s Tasnim news agency, that “we consider the economic blockade an act of war and we will take all necessary measures to lift it”.

“We have made this known to the other parties, including the mediators”, he added, saying “the United States was aware of this.”

In an interview published on Saturday by the state-run Iran Daily newspaper, Araghchi reiterated that Tehran would not allow its stockpiles of enriched uranium to leave the country.

The Iranian nuclear programme is one of the major issues in Iranian-American relations. Western nations accuse Iran of seeking a bomb, though Tehran insists the programme is entirely civilian in nature.

“I believe a solution can be found, but we have clear red lines: the material will not be taken out of the country,” Araghchi said.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, meanwhile, said US and Israeli strikes on Iran’s energy infrastructure had worsened energy problems ahead of winter.

“The attack on the country’s gas infrastructure has aggravated the situation, and we should therefore expect difficulties this winter,” he was quoted as saying by the ISNA news agency.

Mohammad Allahdad, head of Iran’s national electricity company, told state TV that the country will impose rolling power cuts from Sunday.

“Given the country’s fuel supply conditions, the electricity sector will be forced to impose distribution restrictions,” he said on Saturday.

description:
‎‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru‎‎ABUJA – PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu on Saturday, directed that the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, be held without the usual fanfare in honour of victims of the boat tragedy in Bayelsa State.



‎The President’s decision followed
content:
‎
‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
‎
‎ABUJA – PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu on Saturday, directed that the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, be held without the usual fanfare in honour of victims of the boat tragedy in Bayelsa State.

‎The President’s decision followed the capsizing of a passenger boat on Friday at Ukubie, near Oweikorogha Community, in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, leaving several people dead.

‎The victims were reportedly mourners travelling by boat to attend a funeral in the community when the vessel capsized.

‎President Tinubu in a statement by his spokesman, Bayo Onanuga expressed sadness over the unfortunate incident and directed that all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation.

‎The statement read: “I am deeply saddened by the tragic incident on Friday in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha Community, in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, where a boat carrying scores of people capsized, resulting in the loss of life.

‎”The deceased were said to be mourners travelling to attend a funeral in the community where the incident happened.

‎”Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation.

‎”I have also directed that our Presidential Campaign Rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, this Saturday, November 21, 2026, be observed without much fanfare in honour of the lives lost and in sympathy with the relatives and families of those involved in the disaster.

‎”On behalf of the entire nation, I mourn those who lost their lives in the incident and sympathise with their families, the government and the people of Bayelsa State.

‎”I particularly mourn with Governor Duoye Diri over this sad incident. I pray that God Almighty repose their souls and comfort their families.”

title: NDC defends Enugu governorship canddate’s manifesto
description:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress in Enugu State has dismissed criticism of its governorship manifesto, stating that no law requires cost estimates to be included.
Responding to an online report questioning the feasibility of Chinyeaka Ohaa’s “The Rescue Mission” manifesto, Ohaa’s spokesperson, Steve
content:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress in Enugu State has dismissed criticism of its governorship manifesto, stating that no law requires cost estimates to be included.

Responding to an online report questioning the feasibility of Chinyeaka Ohaa’s “The Rescue Mission” manifesto, Ohaa’s spokesperson, Steve Eboh, said in a rejoinder issued on Saturday that the 1999 Constitution, Electoral Act 2026 and INEC guidelines did not mandate cost breakdowns.

Ohaa is the governorship candidate of the NDC in the 2027 general election.

“It is generally not mandatory for a political party manifesto to include cost estimates,” Eboh said, adding: “Manifestos are primarily pre-election documents outlining a party’s ideology, goals, and proposed policies instead of formal budgets.”

He described the document as a directional blueprint, saying, “The manifesto establishes political priorities, governance philosophy, and measurable service targets, while exact Naira figures belong to the statutory annual budgeting process after assuming office.”

He noted: “Publishing fixed project costs without access to official state books… risks misleading voters with arbitrary numbers.”

Eboh outlined a Market Traders Recovery Fund for affected traders at Ogige, Garriki, Holy Ghost and Abakpa markets, as well as the Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium.

He said resource mobilisation would include blocking revenue leakages through digitised land records, reprioritising capital expenditure away from “white elephant projects in urban centres”, leveraging private investment in coal, natural gas and agro-industrial hubs, and transparent borrowing.

In a separate statement, the NDC accused the ruling All Progressives Congress and Governor Peter Mbah of impoverishing residents through “mandatory heavy financial pressure arising from multiple tax collections and high daily ticketing perpetrated by the Peter Mbah’s administration.”

“Enugu State residents have never had it so tough as we are experiencing it today. The pain is so excruciating,” Eboh said, noting increased costs despite higher federal allocations.

“One would have expected that more revenues from the federal government ought to have translated to lesser tax burden on the average Enugu person, but the reverse seems to be the case,” he added.

The party criticised what it described as “elitist” projects, including Hotel Presidential, Enugu International Hospital and Enugu Air, as well as Mbah’s unfulfilled 180-day potable water promise.

“Ndi Enugu, the die is cast. Our dear state is indeed in troubled times, and it will take a level-headed gentleman in the mould of Sir Chinyeaka Ohaa (ODALIJE)… to positively turn things around,” Eboh said.

The NDC candidate promised to abolish unjustified tolls, multiple taxation and arbitrary assessments, and implement a 12-month tax relief programme for small businesses through a Single Unified Business Assessment System.

He also promised to establish a Market Traders Recovery Committee within seven days of assuming office to facilitate compensation and provide alternative trading spaces for affected traders.

“A vote for Sir Chinyeaka Ohaa of the NDC as our governor on February 6, 2027 is a vote for visible economic emancipation of the good people of Enugu State,” Eboh concluded.

title: Enioluwa’s mother defends son over ‘lazy youths’ remark backlash
description:
The mother of social media influencer Enioluwa Adeoluwa, Dr Bolanle Adeoluwa, has defended her son following days of criticism over his remarks about Nigerian youths, insisting that he never described them as lazy.
Bola Adeoluwa made the clarification in an Instagram post on Saturday, saying an old
content:
The mother of social media influencer Enioluwa Adeoluwa, Dr Bolanle Adeoluwa, has defended her son following days of criticism over his remarks about Nigerian youths, insisting that he never described them as lazy.

Bola Adeoluwa made the clarification in an Instagram post on Saturday, saying an old video of her son speaking at a youth programme in Port Harcourt had been circulated with different interpretations and edited excerpts.

The controversy followed remarks Enioluwa made at the Emergence of Stars Youth Conference in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, where he urged young people to work harder and seek mentors, but drew criticism for suggesting that they no longer liked working and expected success to come easily.

The event was held on April 1, 2025, in Port Harcourt, Rivers State.

“Young people, we don’t like to work anymore because we think that things should come easily for us.

“We need to understand that you must work hard. You can’t give up easily. You are 20, and you say, ‘I’m tired of life’. Have you even seen life? What has life shown you, really? You’ve not seen anything,” he said

The influencer also encouraged young people to identify role models, even if they had never met them physically, citing American filmmaker Tyler Perry as his own mentor.

He said he studied Perry’s career trajectory to understand the steps that had contributed to his success.

Enioluwa also argued that academic success required consistent effort, saying, “If you read every night, you are going to finish with a first class. Simple and short.”

He added, “Life is not difficult. We’re overcomplicating it,” and said people needed to put in the work that would produce their desired results.

His comments attracted criticism from Nigerians who accused him of overlooking the economic realities confronting young people, including unemployment, low wages and the difficulty of making ends meet despite working hard.

Some critics argued that his remarks presented success as a straightforward reward for effort without acknowledging the barriers many young Nigerians face.

Enioluwa subsequently apologised in a post on X on November 17, saying he did not believe Nigerian youths were lazy.

“I do not believe that Nigerian youths are lazy. That has never been my belief, nor the message I intended to communicate. We are some of the most hardworking people I know,” he wrote.

He added that his words might have appeared to overlook his privileges and the challenges faced by young Nigerians.

“I sincerely apologise for any hurt my remarks may have caused,” he said, adding that young Nigerians worked hard despite economic difficulties and deserved opportunities to thrive.

Mother speaks out

Reacting to the controversy on Saturday, his mother said she had read different opinions, interpretations and edited videos relating to the speech, which she said was delivered over a year ago.

She also referred to screenshots circulating online concerning the allegation that her son had called Nigerian youths lazy.

“I am 100 per cent sure he would never do that considering the kind of nature he has and his contributions to the development of youths in Nigeria,” she wrote.

Describing herself as an academic, she urged people to verify information and preserve context before making judgments.

“As an academic, I believe strongly in the responsibility and importance to verify information, preserve context, and uphold integrity in public discourse. Even in emotionally charged situations,” she said.

She, however, acknowledged that her reaction was also shaped by her position as a mother.

“But beyond being an academic, I am a mother. I love my son dearly, and as a family we are incredibly proud of him. Our Eni. Kind, generous, simple and loving. His siblings love him dearly too,” she wrote.

Adeoluwa said the criticism had hurt her, although she recognised that public figures were subject to scrutiny.

“Does it hurt me as a mother? Certainly. But I understand that public life comes with its own responsibilities,” she added.

She also said the family was grounded in Christian values and had supported students with school fees.

“By the grace of God, we have collectively and individually paid school fees for students, and we still do,” she wrote.

She urged Nigerians to disagree without resorting to personal attacks, adding, “We can hold people accountable without being unkind, and we can disagree without losing our humanity.”

Adeoluwa is listed on the Federal University Oye-Ekiti’s academic staff portal as a Lecturer I in its Department of Mass Communication, under the Faculty of Communication and Media Studies.

Her official profile identifies her area of specialisation as communication and public relations. It also lists a PhD in Mass Communication from Afe Babalola University, obtained in 2025.

She has qualifications in education, mass communication, public relations, and industrial and labour relations, according to the university’s profile.

The post Enioluwa’s mother defends son over ‘lazy youths’ remark backlash appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
