title: Chelsea Humbled As Leeds Run Riot
description: Chelsea suffered an embarrassing 4-1 defeat against Leeds on Saturday as the Blues were beaten for the third time in their last four Premier League matches.Xabi Alonso’s side were ripped apart by rampant Leeds, who savoured their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years.Chelsea
content:
Chelsea suffered an embarrassing 4-1 defeat against Leeds on Saturday as the Blues were beaten for the third time in their last four Premier League matches.

Xabi Alonso’s side were ripped apart by rampant Leeds, who savoured their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years.

Chelsea scored six in a League Cup win against Leeds in September, but Daniel Farke’s men erased that painful result with a superb display on their return to West London.

Just 24 hours after NFL legend Tom Brady was linked with buying a minority stake in Chelsea, the seven-time Super Bowl winner might be thinking twice about his mooted investment.

Brady is believed to be friendly with Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali, who will have a big decision to make on Alonso’s future if results do not improve soon.

Chelsea are languishing in eighth place after a fifth defeat in their 11 league games under Alonso, who was hyped as the stabilising force the club needed after a turbulent period.

Alonso has been hampered by the absence of injured Brazilian striker Joao Pedro in recent weeks, and once again Chelsea struggled without their attacking talisman.

Making his full debut in Alonso’s latest bid to find a stand-in for Pedro, Emmanuel Emegha fired Chelsea ahead in the 25th minute.

Yet within three minutes they gifted an equaliser to Noah Okafor, who punished static defending to lash home.

Morgan Rogers conceded a penalty eight minutes into the second half, and Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted to put Leeds in front.

Swiss striker Okafor quickly made it three in the 58th minute and Brenden Aaronson got a fourth in stoppage time to leave Chelsea in turmoil.

Over a miserable five-match spell, the Blues have lost to Tottenham, Sunderland and Leeds, while also crashing out of the League Cup against Liverpool.

While it is too soon to suggest Alonso is in danger of the sack, the Spaniard has endured a disappointing start to his first spell as a Premier League manager.

Failing to beat struggling pair Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two games would undoubtedly turn the heat up on the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss.

title: NUPRC Opens 2026 Oil Licensing Round, Offers 40 Oil, Gas Blocks To Investors
description: The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) has opened its 2026 oil and gas licensing round, offering 40 blocks across onshore, shallow water and deep offshore terrains to prospective investors.The commission announced that the bidding portal went live on Friday, November 20, with
content:
The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) has opened its 2026 oil and gas licensing round, offering 40 blocks across onshore, shallow water and deep offshore terrains to prospective investors.

The commission announced that the bidding portal went live on Friday, November 20, with registration scheduled to close on January 15, 2027.

According to a statement signed by the NUPRC Head of Corporate Communications and Media, Eniola Akinkuotu, the blocks comprise 17 onshore, 14 shallow water and nine deep offshore assets.

The commission urged interested investors to visit the portal to access the complete list of available blocks, bidding guidelines and frequently asked questions.

It said the portal was designed to provide users with a seamless experience throughout the licensing process.

The 2026 licensing round will be conducted in five stages: registration and prequalification, access to data, submission of technical and commercial bids, technical evaluation, and the commercial conference.

The exercise was first announced on October 6, 2026, by the Commission Chief Executive, following approval by President Bola Tinubu, who also serves as Minister of Petroleum Resources.

The announcement was accompanied by statutory advertisements in local and international newspapers, in accordance with the provisions of the Petroleum Industry Act.

With the registration portal now open, the next major activity is the pre-bid conference scheduled to hold in Lagos on December 16, 2026.

The NUPRC said it would provide further information and updates on the licensing exercise through the bidding portal and its official social media platforms.

title: English village votes to ‘leave UK’ over migrant camp plan
description:
A small English village on Saturday voted to leave the UK in a symbolic poll protesting government plans to house hundreds of asylum seekers at a nearby former air force base.



The vote in Barnham follows a similar protest referendum in the village of Piddington in September, also over government
content:
A small English village on Saturday voted to leave the UK in a symbolic poll protesting government plans to house hundreds of asylum seekers at a nearby former air force base.

The vote in Barnham follows a similar protest referendum in the village of Piddington in September, also over government plans to move asylum seekers from hotels into former military accommodation.

Between 400 to 500 people were eligible to vote in the ballot which carried no legal weight, with 257 voting for independence, 16 against, and one spoilt ballot.

“There’s an issue with the sheer volume of people expected to be accommodated,” the chairwoman of the Barnham residents’ association, Helen Beck, told AFP earlier.

“Barnham is a small village. There will be nothing for the (lodged) people to do, nowhere to go.”

Under plans by Britain’s government, the base near the village in rural eastern England will be used to accommodate 931 migrants. The village has a population of 584.

Residents were asked whether they supported seeking a “crown dependency status” similar to that of Jersey, Guernsey and the Isle of Man.

Parish council chair John Bauer said this would allow the village to “retain loyalty to the crown” while removing itself from Home Office jurisdiction.

– Safety concern –

Residents in both Barnham and Piddington say they are also worried about locals’ safety, particularly that of women.

“We’ve been told they (the asylum seekers) are all males. We don’t know where they are from, their background,” Beck said.

“People are anxious about walking alone, walking their dog in darkness if an additional 900 men arrive in the area,” she said.

In the Piddington vote in September, 285 out of 312 votes were cast in favour of “pursuing self-determination”.

The government plans to house around 1,250 asylum seekers on a former defence ministry site close to Piddington village, all single men between 18 and 65.

Britain’s centre-left government, in power since July 2024, has vowed to end the use of hotels as migrant accommodation following a public outcry.

It plans to move all those currently in hotels — a policy inherited from the last Conservative government — to former military bases by 2029.

But Beck said that there were questions about whether military-style accommodation was suitable for people “fleeing a conflict or persecution”, adding that it was also “significantly more expensive than hotels”.

title: Man City stumble against Fulham; Leeds thrash Chelsea at Stamford Bridge
description:
Manchester City’s winless Premier League run extended to four games after failing to beat Fulham for the first time in 21 attempts on Saturday, as Leeds thrashed Chelsea 4-1 at Stamford Bridge.



Arsenal can open up an eight-point lead at the top of the table with victory at Newcastle later as City
content:
Manchester City’s winless Premier League run extended to four games after failing to beat Fulham for the first time in 21 attempts on Saturday, as Leeds thrashed Chelsea 4-1 at Stamford Bridge.

Arsenal can open up an eight-point lead at the top of the table with victory at Newcastle later as City’s title challenge wilts in the wake of a guilty verdict on widespread breaches of financial rules.

The club deny any wrongdoing but are likely to be hit with a severe points penalty, and possibly even relegation, unless they overturn the ruling on appeal.

After seven consecutive league wins to start Enzo Maresca’s reign, the off-field uncertainty appears to have derailed City’s quest to topple defending champions Arsenal.

Fulham had lost every meeting against City for the past 15 years but got their reward after striking early through Rodrigo Muniz.

The home side were furious that Erling Haaland’s equaliser before half-time was controversially ruled out as the Norwegian was deemed to have kicked the ball out of the grasp of Bernd Leno.

Elliot Anderson’s sweet strike saved City from a fourth consecutive defeat, but they were booed off after another disappointing display.

“Almost 80 percent of the goals we concede are in the first 20 minutes and it’s for sure something we need to improve,” said Maresca.

Leeds humble Chelsea

Leeds climbed into the top six after coming from behind to stun Chelsea.

Emmanuel Emegha’s first Chelsea goal opened the scoring, but the Blues have now lost four of their last five matches to put manager Xabi Alonso under scrutiny.

Noah Okafor quickly levelled for Leeds before Dominic Calvert-Lewin put the visitors in front from the penalty spot.

Okafor delivered a thumping finish into the top corner and Brenden Aaronson delivered the final blow in stoppage time as Leeds savoured a famous win at the home of one of their historic rivals.

Bournemouth climbed into the Champions League places as their sensational run continued with a 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest.

Evanilson struck for the sixth consecutive league game and Justin Kluivert added a second as the Cherries’ winning run in all competitions stretched to nine games.

Tottenham are also marching up the table after a difficult start to the campaign.

Teenager Luca Williams-Barnett was the star of a 2-0 win over Ipswich as he netted on his first Premier League start before Dominic Solanke added a second to secure a fourth win in five for Roberto De Zerbi’s men.

Thomas Frank’s arrival at Crystal Palace failed to inspire a turnaround in the Eagles’ fortunes as they lost 3-2 at Coventry to remain bottom of the table.

Dwight McNeil’s late own goal gave the Sky Blues a vital victory in their quest for survival back in the top flight after four goals were shared in a thrilling first half.

Sunderland frustrated Aston Villa in a 0-0 draw that lifted the Black Cats above Manchester United in the relegation zone.

Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of United for the first time at Liverpool on Sunday with the Red Devils second bottom of the table.

title: Nmecha Helps Dortmund Beat Gladbach To Top Bundesliga
description: Felix Nmecha scored with 10 minutes remaining to send Borussia Dortmund to the top of the Bundesliga table with a 1-0 win at Borussia Moenchengladbach on Saturday.Bayern Munich’s 1-1 home draw with Cologne on Friday opened up the door for the chasers but Dortmund had few opportunities until Nm
content:
Felix Nmecha scored with 10 minutes remaining to send Borussia Dortmund to the top of the Bundesliga table with a 1-0 win at Borussia Moenchengladbach on Saturday.

Bayern Munich’s 1-1 home draw with Cologne on Friday opened up the door for the chasers but Dortmund had few opportunities until Nmecha’s late strike.

Dortmund are now outright first on 24 points, with Bayern and Freiburg, who won 1-0 at Elversberg, locked on 22 points.

Bayern also lost Harry Kane to injury in Friday’s draw, with the Ballon d’Or winner set to miss several months after undergoing surgery on his injured ankle earlier on Saturday.

Dortmund, who travel to Arsenal on Tuesday, knew victory would send them top but the 2024 Champions League finalists had few chances against a stubborn Gladbach.

Nmecha, who scored twice in Dortmund’s 2-1 win over Elversberg before the international break, looked most likely when his header forced a save from Daniel Batz.

With 17 minutes left, Marcel Sabitzer chipped a free-kick inches wide of the post.

Dortmund continued to push and Nmecha was on hand to knock a rebound through Batz’s fingers and help the visitors snare a crucial three points.

Igor Matanovic’s 68th-minute strike helped Freiburg break down promoted Elversberg and move level with Bayern.

Last season’s Europa League finalists Freiburg stay one point ahead of fourth-placed RB Leipzig, who romped to a 5-1 victory at Union Berlin.

Antonio Nusa, Romulo, Brajan Gruda, Rocco Reitz and Ridle Baku scored for Leipzig, who host Lens in the Champions League on Tuesday.

Gruda was particularly impressive with a goal and an assist, just days after impressing for Jurgen Klopp’s Germany with a goal and two assists versus the Netherlands on the other side of the German capital.

Elsewhere, Afonso Moreira broke his Bundesliga duck with a brace in Bayer Leverkusen’s 4-0 home win over Paderborn.

Moreira had failed to find the net since his summer move from Lyon but scored Leverkusen’s first two goals and laid on one for Ezequiel Fernandez.

Patrik Schick also got a goal to move level with Niclas Fuellkrug atop the league goalscoring charts with nine goals.

Jonathan Burkardt scored the only goal as Eintracht Frankfurt beat Hoffenheim at home.

Frankfurt goalkeeper Noah Atubolu saved a first-half Andrej Kramaric penalty to keep his remarkable spot-kick record alive.

Atubolu has saved seven out of the 11 penalties he has faced, which is the best save percentage in the Bundesliga’s 64-year history.

In Saturday’s late game, Stuttgart will hope to warm up for Wednesday’s trip to Inter Milan when they face strugglers Schalke away.

The post Nmecha Helps Dortmund Beat Gladbach To Top Bundesliga appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Why I almost rejected Jonathan’s ministerial appointment — Chidoka
description:
From Okwe Obi, Abuja
A former Minister of Aviation, Osita Chidoka, has disclosed why he almost turned down former President Goodluck Jonathan’s ministerial appointment.
Chidoka said he insisted that his successor as corps marshal must come from the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), to ensure that th
content:
From Okwe Obi, Abuja

A former Minister of Aviation, Osita Chidoka, has disclosed why he almost turned down former President Goodluck Jonathan’s ministerial appointment.

Chidoka said he insisted that his successor as corps marshal must come from the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), to ensure that the gains recorded during his administration would not be swept under the carpet.

He spoke as a guest speaker at the reunion public lecture organised by the alumni of Senior Executive Course 41, 2019, of the National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies (NIPSS), Kuru, Jos, Plateau State, yesterday in Abuja.

The theme of the lecture was ‘Nigeria Development Challenges: Navigating Population Growth, Governance Gaps, Security Threats, Healthcare Financing and Technological Disruptions’.

“I almost turned down my appointment under President Goodluck Jonathan. I said, sir, you have to appoint someone from within. I insisted. I said, Mr President, you have to say it. He told me to give him the list.

“I have given you the list of the staff. I have shown you the best. I have shown you number one, number two. So, make a choice now. He said, I will go with number one. I said, okay.

“Thank you, sir. Announce it, sir. So, he went into the hall and announced it. Because I just couldn’t imagine how what we have done for seven years will go down like that.

“And that was it. These are the questions that shaped what we tried to build. And in 2013, we earned our ISO 9000 award certification, which was a quality management system.”

The former FRSC Corps Marshal questioned the efficacy of the policies churned out from NIPSS, owing to the rise of insecurity and bad governance in the country.

According to him, graduates of NIPSS must justify taxpayers’ money by ensuring that they come out with workable policies to address the multidimensional challenges bedevilling the country.

“So normally, around this November, seven years ago, you were packing your bags from Kuru. You carried along tens of researches, arguments, and the company of colleagues drawn from parts of Nigerian life you might otherwise never have encountered. So seven years is long enough for that experience to have produced something.

“And long enough for us to ask, what has happened? Your members have gone on to become important members in your organisations. Some have become chief executives.

“Some have become influential in different fields. But what you learned in Kuru, what did it impact in any of the places where you controlled? It will have been nice for people to know where to go.

“Because it is our federal resources that we spend every year in Kuru. It has a budget line. It is Nigeria’s premier policy institute.

“It is the place where we have decided that we will retain our manpower, the finest training, before they get to the top. That we will give them the finest training. They will see all the facets of our society.

“They will come from the army, the navy, the air force, the police, the civil service. And they will interact. So that when there is a crisis, when you are a permanent secretary, you can pick up the phone and call the DIG, who was your course mate.

“You can pick up the phone and call the Anambra State Head of Service, who was your course mate. It was intended, not just for a badge, but for an opportunity for the organisation to build people who can produce results in Nigeria.

“So I asked that question as someone who has spent much of his working life inside public institutions and now spends his time trying to build them outside government, which is not easy.

“So Nigeria’s central difficulty is not a shortage of ideas about development. We have produced plans, we have produced strategies and sectoral reforms for six decades.”

But the Secretary General of Senior Executive Course 41, Dr Goddy Nnadi, complained that most policies sent to government were not implemented, even after students went through a strenuous academic exercise to graduate.

“It has been an issue because you meet for one whole year, and it is a very strenuous course. You go through it, and you are able to write policy papers, and they are sent to government.

“Just about a week ago, the current set presented their own to our president, President Bola Tinubu, and they presented their report.

“We expect that it should be implemented. Every government will promise you that it will be implemented, but unfortunately, most of the time, they are not really implemented.

“That is really sad, and that is why this reunion is important, because every set now meets to ask questions, just like the guest speaker, who said, what are you doing to make sure that what you recommended, what you worked on, was implemented? Now, it’s for you to look at all the states of the federation.

“Which states are implementing what you recommended? If they are not, ask questions, and then we have people in almost every area, in the armed forces, the civil service, the private sector.

“We have the capacity to now ask the states, what are you doing about what we recommended? And that is why this is very important for us.”

Regardless of the seeming rejection of policies, he identified the state police law as one of the policies implemented by NIPSS.

“Some of them actually have been implemented. Like this state police that we are talking about was actually recommended by sect 40.

“Our own was on the primary healthcare in Nigeria, and it has been implemented by some states gradually, but not at the same speed that we want.

“That is why this reunion is important, because all we do as the set, you look at the topic that you discuss with the whole year, because it is a lot. You do the states, you visit at least two states.

“Every of the study groups, you go and do one in the north, and you do one in the south, and you prepare your papers. On all of them, eventually we culminate into the presidential report, which is presented to the government yearly,” he added.

title: EPL: Leeds thrash Chelsea 4-1, hand Alonso heavy defeat
description:
Leeds United stunned Chelsea with a 4-1 victory at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, handing manager Xabi Alonso another damaging Premier League setback.
The visitors recovered from conceding an early goal to score four times, with Noah Okafor netting twice, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin and substitute Bre
content:
Leeds United stunned Chelsea with a 4-1 victory at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, handing manager Xabi Alonso another damaging Premier League setback.

The visitors recovered from conceding an early goal to score four times, with Noah Okafor netting twice, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin and substitute Brenden Aaronson also found the net.

Chelsea took the lead in the 25th minute through Emmanuel Emegha, who marked his first start for the club by finishing Morgan Rogers’ pass.

However, Leeds responded three minutes later when Okafor fired past Emiliano Martinez after being set up by Calvert-Lewin to restore parity.

The visitors took the lead in the 53rd minute after referee Michael Oliver awarded them a penalty for handball against Morgan Rogers. The decision followed a VAR review after Jayden Bogle’s effort struck the Chelsea midfielder’s arm.

Calvert-Lewin stepped up and converted the spot kick, sending Martinez the wrong way to put Leeds 2-1 ahead.

Okafor extended the visitors’ advantage six minutes later, completing his brace after Chelsea failed to clear an Ethan Ampadu throw-in and the resulting ball fell into his path.

Chelsea attempted to recover by introducing Danny Welbeck and Pedro Neto, but Leeds maintained their advantage and continued to threaten on the counter.

Aaronson completed the emphatic victory in stoppage time, scoring in the 90th minute to make it 4-1 and seal Leeds’ first victory at Stamford Bridge since 1999.

The defeat compounds Chelsea’s difficulties under Alonso, who had been seeking a response after his side’s disappointing run before the international break.

Chelsea were also dealt an injury setback during the first half when midfielder Moises Caicedo was forced off and replaced by Jordan Henderson.

The result gives Leeds a significant boost in their attempt to move away from the lower half of the Premier League table, while Chelsea will be left to reflect on a damaging home defeat.

title: 2027 Elections: Tinubu Endorses Alli, Yayi, Hamzat
description: President Bola Tinubu has publicly endorsed the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidates in Oyo, Ogun and Lagos states ahead of the 2027 general elections.Tinubu endorsed the candidates on Saturday by raising their hands at the party’s presidential campaign rally held at Mapo Ha
content:
President Bola Tinubu has publicly endorsed the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidates in Oyo, Ogun and Lagos states ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Tinubu endorsed the candidates on Saturday by raising their hands at the party’s presidential campaign rally held at Mapo Hall in Ibadan, Oyo State.

Introducing the candidates, the President told supporters, “The governor you will vote for, I will show you,” before raising the hand of Senator Sharafadeen Alli, the APC governorship candidate in Oyo State.

He subsequently raised the hands of Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, the party’s candidate in Ogun State, and Obafemi Hamzat, its governorship candidate in Lagos State.

Tinubu also endorsed Remi Oseni, the APC senatorial candidate for Oyo South, by raising his hand at the rally.

The event marked the South-West leg of the President’s re-election campaign and the seventh state rally he had attended since the exercise began in Kaduna on October 24.

Vice-President Kashim Shettima, APC governors, members of the National Assembly and other party leaders attended the rally.

Tinubu, who arrived in Ibadan alongside his wife, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, said he was in the state to appreciate residents for their support during the 2023 presidential election.

He expressed confidence that they would vote for the APC again in 2027.

“I am just here to say thank you for standing with us. You gave us votes in 2023, and I am sure you will do the same in 2027,” he said.

The President, however, kept his speech brief and asked the audience to observe a minute’s silence in honour of victims of a boat accident in Ukubie, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, on Friday.

Tinubu had earlier directed that the Ibadan rally be held without much fanfare in honour of those who died in the incident and in sympathy with their families.

He also disclosed that he had met with traditional rulers in Oyo State, including the Olubadan of Ibadanland and the Soun of Ogbomoso, expressing confidence in their support.

The President further promised improved electricity supply and industrial development, announcing that his administration had signed an agreement with Chinese automobile manufacturer Yutong to reopen the defunct Leyland factory in Ibadan for the assembly of compressed natural gas (CNG) buses.

“We will bring industries and provide jobs for our youths,” he said.

The APC is seeking to take control of Oyo State from the incumbent administration of Governor Seyi Makinde, while Alli, who represents Oyo South in the Senate, emerged as the party’s consensus governorship candidate in May.

In Ogun State, Adeola, who represents Ogun West Senatorial District, is the APC’s governorship candidate, while Hamzat, the incumbent deputy governor of Lagos State, is flying the party’s flag in the 2027 governorship election.

The endorsements placed the three governorship contests alongside Tinubu’s re-election campaign as the APC seeks to strengthen its political presence across the South-West.

title: With better security, Nigerians may not need fences — Sowore
description:
African Action Congress presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, has said Nigerians may no longer need to build security fences around their homes if he becomes president.
He promised to tackle insecurity through technology-driven measures, including the deployment of drones and artificial intelligen
content:
African Action Congress presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, has said Nigerians may no longer need to build security fences around their homes if he becomes president.

He promised to tackle insecurity through technology-driven measures, including the deployment of drones and artificial intelligence.

He said his proposed approach to security would create an environment where Nigerians could move freely, cultivate their land and live without fear of attacks by criminals.

Sowore made the remarks while interacting with journalists in Asaba, Delta State, on Saturday, during his #RevolutionExpress campaign visit.

He said his administration would prioritise the use of technology to identify criminal elements and prevent attacks before they occurred, rather than rely on conventional security arrangements such as roadblocks.

“Full security means nobody will go hungry in our time because we make our land, you know, free to cultivate once again by providing security for everyone in the country.

“Security that is driven by technology, no more outside security of roadblocks. Drones, AI, to help us figure out where the criminals are, we bust them before they get to our people,” he said.

The AAC candidate said improved security and responsible leadership would also reduce the need for elaborate security barriers around residential buildings.

“So, if you vote right, you may not need fence in your houses anymore, except you will need it to decorate,” he added.

He said he had lived in a society for 20 years where even wealthy people did not surround their homes with fences, using the experience to illustrate the level of public safety he hoped to achieve in Nigeria.

Sowore also criticised the All Progressives Congress-led Federal Government, dismissing its reforms and accusing the ruling party of failing to develop a workable plan for the country.

Asked whether the APC’s reforms were working, he said, “APC, don’t be messing with me. APC is on its way out. There was no time they had any plan for the country. They lied to Nigerians in 2015 and their lives are caught up with that.”

He further accused the ruling party of hiring crowds for its political activities across the country, alleging that it continued to mislead Nigerians.

“That’s why they have to be hiring crowds, you know, all around the country and they keep lying,” he added.

Sowore arrived in Asaba on Thursday evening for a campaign stop and held a press conference upon arrival. His visit formed part of his political mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The latest promise is consistent with his previous advocacy for technology-driven security. In an earlier interview, the activist-turned-politician said he would make a drone his defence minister if elected president, arguing that Nigeria needed to embrace technology to improve its security operations.

He had also advocated the use of drones and modern surveillance systems to monitor criminal activities, gather intelligence and enable security agencies to respond to threats more effectively.

Sowore has also made proposals on education as part of his campaign promises. He recently pledged to scrap the Nigerian Education Loan Fund and introduce N100,000 grants per semester for students in tertiary institutions.

The presidential candidate has continued to make security, governance, education and economic reforms central to his campaign messaging ahead of the 2027 elections.

title: Tinubu’s achievements will give him victory in Edo – Shaibu
description:

‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru



‎ABUJA – FORMER Deputy Governor of Edo State and Director-General/CEO of National Institute for Sports, NIS, Rt. Hon. Philip Shaibu has said that the political wave that gave victory to the presidential candidate of the Labour
content:
.Says Obi’s 2023 wave won’t repeat itself 

‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

‎ABUJA – FORMER Deputy Governor of Edo State and Director-General/CEO of National Institute for Sports, NIS, Rt. Hon. Philip Shaibu has said that the political wave that gave victory to the presidential candidate of the Labour Party, in 2023 election in the state, Mr. Peter Obi, will not repeat itself in the 2027 polls.

‎Shaibu said President Bola Tinubu’s reforms and achievements would give victory.

‎Speaking exclusively to Sunday Vanguard, Shaibu, who was a former President of National Association of Nigerian Students, NANS, said no elections can be the same.

“From my experience so far in Nigerian politics—I have actively participated since 2023, beyond student union government elections and the politics of activism—my political career started mainly in 2023 in Edo State.

“Since then, from my little experience in active partisan politics, I know that no two elections are the same. Every election has its own dynamics, its own spirit, and its own issues that drive it. Edo is not different from the cyclical politics played in Nigeria.

‎”The 2023 election was a wave that we had never experienced in this country. That wave occurred because young Nigerians were interested in who became their president, and they were looking for an alternative.

‎”Even when the alternative they later got was not fully known to them, they simply wanted an alternative—someone they seemingly believed could be it, even though they did not have much information.

‎”They were persuaded and mobilised through the power of social media. Do not forget that the EndSARS protests created room for all that happened in 2023.

‎”But 2027 is a different ballgame. First, Asiwaju (President Tinubu) is now known to the people. He is known by the young people in this country, not only by partisan politicians in the state. He has now been president for over three years, and people understand what governance is.

‎”The person they thought was going to be a messiah—they have started seeing that he has more than one shoe that he claims to have. They have started seeing that the empire he has built is more than somebody owning a shoe.

‎”They have seen that the statistics they were reading, those statistics are all fallacy, they were all wrong. They were one of those home video acting to just convince people, but because people did not take time to check and that was why that wave.

‎”That wave cannot return in the next election, because even the young men and women—when you see the Tinubu support groups, you will see that it is dominated by these same young people who were part of that wave.

‎”So the politics of 2027 will be completely different from the politics of 2023, because we now know who President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is. We now know who the other opponents are. We have opponents, but we do not have an opposition. I can tell you that for the 2027 election, there are opponents, but there is no opposition.”

‎Asked why he said that there were opponents and no opposition, Shaibu said: “There are opponents who just need their names to appear on the ballot.

‎”When you have an opposition, you have a presidential candidate who carries weight and is a threat in every unit, in every ward, across the country. But what we have now are candidates who want their names on the ballot paper, yet already know they are only popular in a particular catchment area of the country.

‎”But we have a president who is known, who has agents and representatives in every unit in Nigeria, and that person is President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. The other candidates do not have that spread. So we have candidates, but no opposition. We have aspirants, but they are not an opposition. Unlike 2023, when we had both opposition and aspirants, in 2027 we only have aspirants.

“Do not forget that it is only in this country that people struggle to become aspirants so that, after the election, they can have a complementary title as a former presidential aspirant or former gubernatorial aspirant.”

‎

‎

title: Seplat Energy CEO tasks oil firm on responsible AI adoption to solve real problems
description:
From Joe Obukata Ogbodu, Warri
The Chief Executive Officer of Seplat Energy Plc, Engr Effiong Okon, has challenged African energy operators to stop talking about Artificial Intelligence (AI) and start using it to solve real operational problems.
Okon gave the charge while delivering the keynote addr
content:
From Joe Obukata Ogbodu, Warri

The Chief Executive Officer of Seplat Energy Plc, Engr Effiong Okon, has challenged African energy operators to stop talking about Artificial Intelligence (AI) and start using it to solve real operational problems.

Okon gave the charge while delivering the keynote address at the inaugural Digitalisation and AI in Energy West Africa conference in Lagos.

He said the relationship between energy and AI is a two-way relationship.

“There is no AI without energy, and as data centres and other digital infrastructure expand, the demand for reliable power will continue to grow. At the same time, AI gives the energy industry an opportunity to find more, decide faster and deliver sooner. For Nigeria, our gas resources will be important to powering that digital future,” Okon said.

Unlike many operators still at the talk stage, Okon gave a concrete example from Seplat’s operations at Sapele.

Using machine learning, Seplat improved permeability prediction accuracy from approximately 50-60 per cent to 80 per cent or better.

He also cited seismic reprocessing to improve subsurface imaging and planned ocean bottom node seismic acquisition to support more informed exploration decisions.

“The point is never the tool. It is the decision it changes. Digital is not a destination. Better uptime, safer operations, sharper reservoir decisions and faster production decisions are the destination,” he said.

Okon outlined three priorities for effective AI adoption: starting with a clear business problem rather than the technology, building strong data foundations and bringing employees along, saying AI should support engineers, not replace them.

“We must start with the problem we are trying to solve, build the right data foundations and bring our people along. AI should support engineers and strengthen their judgement, not replace the engineering discipline required to operate our assets safely,” he said.

In a separate session titled ‘What It Actually Took to Put AI into Production’, the General Manager, Information Technology, Seplat Energy, David Osemwegie, explained how Seplat achieved over 90 per cent adoption of Microsoft 365 Copilot.

Employees must complete basic activation training before receiving a Copilot licence, a simple rule that forced adoption.

Osemwegie also spoke on Seplat’s integration of the former ExxonMobil shallow-water asset, stressing strong data governance, business continuity and organisational alignment.

He said every AI use case at Seplat has a business product owner accountable for its roadmap and performance, while IT manages technical performance.

Seplat has also set up an AI Ethics, Risk and Compliance Committee, made up of legal, HR, finance and risk officials, to oversee responsible AI use.

Other industry leaders at the conference stressed linking digital investments to measurable outcomes, using digital twins, predictive maintenance and condition monitoring to reduce downtime and extend asset life.

The post Seplat Energy CEO tasks oil firm on responsible AI adoption to solve real problems appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Lagos APC, ADC trade words over alleged unpaid legal fees
description:
The Lagos State chapters of the All Progressives Congress and the African Democratic Congress have traded words over allegations that lawyers handling more than 200 cases involving the ADC have not been paid for their services since the party’s primaries in June.
While the APC questioned the ADC’s f
content:
The Lagos State chapters of the All Progressives Congress and the African Democratic Congress have traded words over allegations that lawyers handling more than 200 cases involving the ADC have not been paid for their services since the party’s primaries in June.

While the APC questioned the ADC’s financial management and accountability over the alleged outstanding fees, the opposition party accused the ruling party of meddling in its internal affairs and expressed concerns about its interest in cases involving the ADC.

The Lagos APC spokesman, Mogaji Seye Oladejo, raised the concerns in a statement on Saturday while reacting to reports that members of the Coalition of West African Journalists had expressed worries over the alleged unpaid legal fees.

Oladejo described the allegations as embarrassing, arguing that a political party aspiring to govern Nigeria should demonstrate financial discipline and the capacity to meet its organisational obligations.

He said the situation was particularly troubling because some of the lawyers reportedly affected were members of the ADC’s leadership structure.

According to him, the allegations followed earlier reports of unpaid salaries involving workers at the party’s national secretariat.

He said, “If the ADC cannot honour its financial commitments to lawyers engaged to defend its own political interests, what exactly is the basis of its confidence that it can responsibly manage the vastly more complex financial obligations of the Federal Republic of Nigeria?”

The APC spokesman also questioned how the opposition party could inspire public confidence while allegedly struggling to settle its internal financial obligations and manage its leadership disputes and legal battles.

He challenged the ADC National Chairman, Senator David Mark, and National Secretary, Rauf Aregbesola, to clarify whether the legal fees were outstanding, disclose the total amount involved and explain the arrangements for settling the affected lawyers.

“Nigerians deserve clear answers. Are the reported legal fees outstanding? What is the total liability? What arrangements have been made to settle the affected lawyers? And what safeguards exist to prevent a recurrence of these troubling allegations?” he asked.

However, responding to the allegations, the Lagos ADC Chairman, George Ashiru, accused the APC of concerning itself with the internal affairs of opposition parties instead of addressing its own challenges.

Speaking with PUNCH Online, Ashiru said the ruling party’s interest in the ADC’s affairs suggested an attempt to plant moles within the opposition party to obtain information for the APC.

He said, “APC should face its woes and not mind other party’s internal affairs. This interest in other party’s affairs suggests an interest in inserting moles within the ADC in order to feed the APC back.”

Ashiru also described the relationship between the ADC and its lawyers as a legal and business arrangement, questioning why the APC was speaking on behalf of unnamed lawyers.

“The business relationship between lawyers and the Party is purely a legal and business affair and the APC becoming a spokesperson for unnamed lawyers is in itself a worrying admission of their interest in the judicial processes,” he said.

The ADC chairman further expressed concern that the APC’s comments could suggest that it had some form of communication with the party’s legal representatives.

“Our hope is that the APC is not teleguiding the outcome of court cases by its own admission of having enough interest with court cases involving our party and therefore demonstrating they have some kind of communication with our legal representation,” he added.

He maintained that the ADC was not involved in any court dispute with the APC and questioned the ruling party’s interest in its ongoing cases.

“As far as I know the ADC is not in courts with the APC, so why exactly is the APC pretending to have interest in court cases involving the ADC, unless they have an insidious interest in subverting the judicial processes,” he said.

However, Ashiru later contacted PUNCH Online to clarify the party’s position, saying the ADC owed no lawyer for services rendered.

He said the party had confirmed that it had no outstanding legal fees, adding that its National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, had also stated the position.

Oladejo had urged the ADC to demonstrate transparency and accountability before seeking Nigerians’ mandate in the 2027 general elections, adding that the national treasury should not become a financial lifeline for a political organisation struggling to manage its affairs.

The APC statement did not provide documentary evidence of the alleged outstanding legal fees.

The post Lagos APC, ADC trade words over alleged unpaid legal fees appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: Former LP presidential candidate condemns attack on Tinubu praise singer
description:
From Idu Jude, Abuja
The former factional presidential candidate of the Labour Party (LP), Prince Kennedy Ahanotu, has strongly condemned the alleged physical attack on Dauda Kahutu, a popular Hausa musician and supporter of the All Progressives Congress (APC), widely known as Rarara, at the Nationa
content:
From Idu Jude, Abuja

The former factional presidential candidate of the Labour Party (LP), Prince Kennedy Ahanotu, has strongly condemned the alleged physical attack on Dauda Kahutu, a popular Hausa musician and supporter of the All Progressives Congress (APC), widely known as Rarara, at the National Mosque in Abuja.

Prince Ahanotu, who is also the convener of the Renewed Hope Alliance of Labour Party Youth Leaders (RHALY), said in a statement over the weekend that his group considers the incident deeply disturbing, particularly at a time when Nigeria needs greater political tolerance, national unity and respect for the fundamental rights of citizens, irrespective of their political affiliations.

Rarara, it will be recalled, was allegedly attacked by disenchanted members who felt his support for the ruling APC and President Tinubu was deceptive.

The statement further read in part: “It is particularly unfortunate that a place of worship, which should represent peace, brotherhood and mutual respect, became the scene of such an ugly confrontation.

“We must make it clear that supporting President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, who belongs to the APC, or expressing one’s political convictions is a fundamental democratic right. Nobody should be assaulted, threatened, intimidated or subjected to public humiliation for exercising that right.

“However, our restraint must never be mistaken for weakness.

“APC supporters across Nigeria are millions of citizens with the capacity, organisation and democratic strength to defend their political interests. They equally have the right to demand protection and justice when their members are attacked. But that strength must be demonstrated through lawful, peaceful and democratic engagement, not retaliatory violence.

“We therefore caution those who may be encouraging political intimidation to understand that Nigeria belongs to all of us. No political group has a monopoly on the streets, and no individual or organisation has the right to deny another Nigerian the freedom to support a political party or candidate of their choice.

“RHALY will not encourage its members or any APC supporter to take the law into their hands. Equally, we will not remain silent in the face of intimidation and attacks against citizens whose only offence is their political preference.

“We call on the performing Inspector-General of Police, the FCT Police Command and other relevant security agencies to thoroughly investigate this incident, identify those responsible and ensure that justice is served. We also urge the government to strengthen the protection of political actors, campaign supporters and ordinary citizens as the country approaches the 2027 general elections.

“We appeal to APC supporters, particularly our youths, to remain calm, vigilant and law-abiding. Do not allow anyone to provoke you into actions that could undermine our collective democratic aspirations.

“Our commitment to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope agenda remains firm. Our political conviction is not built on intimidation, and our determination cannot be weakened by violence.

“Nigeria must remain a country where political differences are settled through the ballot box, not through fists, threats or mob action.

“We demand justice for Rarara. We demand protection for every Nigerian. We demand an end to political intolerance.”

The post 2027: Former LP presidential candidate condemns attack on Tinubu praise singer appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Bauchi 2027: Leko defends wealth, dismisses allegations over properties outside state
description:
From Paul Orude, Bauchi
The All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Bogoro, Dass and Tafawa Balewa Federal Constituency, Hon Jafaru Gambo Leko, has dismissed allegations concerning his acquisition of properties outside Bauchi State, insisting that he has legitimate sources of income and an unb
content:
From Paul Orude, Bauchi

The All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Bogoro, Dass and Tafawa Balewa Federal Constituency, Hon Jafaru Gambo Leko, has dismissed allegations concerning his acquisition of properties outside Bauchi State, insisting that he has legitimate sources of income and an unblemished record.

Leko, who was elected to the House of Representatives in 2023 and is seeking re-election in 2027, said he was not intimidated by criticism of his personal wealth, and challenged those making the allegations to establish their claims.

He spoke on Saturday during the ongoing interview series organised by the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Bauchi State, where he also highlighted some of his legislative interventions and national policy initiatives.

Responding to allegations that he had acquired properties outside Bauchi State while attracting projects to other states, the lawmaker said he had nothing to hide, citing his 23 years of service as a civil servant as part of his background.

“Let him go and buy his own house. Is it his money? If it is alleged, let him go and look for money. I am not a thief. I have a record. I have an antecedent. I worked for 23 years,” Leko said.

He added that he was not afraid of anyone questioning his wealth, arguing that individuals should not begrudge others their financial achievements.

“If God has blessed me, even if you give me money to buy a voucher, I will buy a voucher and nobody can stop that,” he said.

Beyond defending his personal wealth, Leko used the interview to highlight what he described as his contributions to national economic policy through legislative motions, particularly on Nigeria’s trade and financial relationship with China.

He claimed that, shortly after his inauguration into the National Assembly in 2023, he moved a motion advocating the adoption of the Chinese yuan as a supplementary currency for Nigeria’s foreign exchange reserves and trade settlements.

According to him, the initiative followed research he conducted during a legislative visit to Rwanda, where he studied measures adopted by some African countries to strengthen their economies.

Leko said he observed that countries such as Rwanda and Tanzania were using the Chinese currency in some trade transactions and believed that Nigeria could benefit from a similar arrangement, given its extensive commercial relationship with China.

“When I went there, I was not only sitting down; I browsed through a lot of things in Rwanda. I saw what they were doing to improve their economy,” he said.

He claimed that he subsequently presented the motion on the floor of the House of Representatives and that the Federal Government, in collaboration with the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), adopted the yuan in December 2024 as an additional reserve and trade settlement currency alongside the United States dollar.

The lawmaker further attributed the relative stability of the exchange rate after the adoption to the inclusion of the yuan in Nigeria’s official reserves.

Leko also cited another motion concerning six houses reportedly forfeited by a former governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, arguing that such properties should be deployed for the benefit of ordinary Nigerians.

He said his position was informed by the constitutional responsibility of government to promote citizens’ welfare, particularly in the areas of shelter, food security and improved living conditions.

Referencing Section 16(2)(d) of the 1999 Constitution, Leko argued that government at all levels had an obligation to ensure the welfare of Nigerians.

He said he therefore advocated that the forfeited houses should be put to public use rather than left idle.

The lawmaker’s comments come as political activities gradually gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general elections, in which he will seek another mandate to represent Bogoro, Dass and Tafawa Balewa Federal Constituency.

His defence of his wealth and presentation of his legislative record formed part of a broader engagement with journalists on his public service and political ambitions.

title: World Children’s Day: 60 Lagos pupils benefit from educational support
description:
Sixty pupils in Lagos State have received scholarships, school kits and shopping vouchers under an educational support initiative by financial technology company PalmPay.
The pupils were recognised under the Young Stars initiative, implemented in partnership with the Lagos State Universal Basic Educ
content:
Sixty pupils in Lagos State have received scholarships, school kits and shopping vouchers under an educational support initiative by financial technology company PalmPay.

The pupils were recognised under the Young Stars initiative, implemented in partnership with the Lagos State Universal Basic Education Board (LASUBEB).

PalmPay revisited the beneficiaries as part of activities marking the 2026 World Children’s Day to assess their progress and find out how the support had impacted their education.

The follow-up visit also provided an opportunity to interact with the pupils and assess their academic development since receiving the assistance.

Speaking during the visit, the Chief Operating Officer of PalmPay Nigeria said the interaction with the children showed the importance of providing support for their education.

“Reconnecting with these children and seeing their progress is incredibly rewarding for the PalmPay team. Seeing their enthusiasm and renewed motivation to stay in school validates why initiatives like Young Stars matter,” the COO said.

The executive added that the programme was intended to encourage children to pursue their ambitions and remain committed to their education.

“Every child deserves the opportunity to dream, learn and build a future filled with possibilities. Through Young Stars, we wanted to do more than celebrate academic excellence; we wanted to remind these children that their dreams are valid and that they have people and organisations willing to support their journey,” the executive added.

The initiative also provided financial relief to parents by helping to cover some education-related expenses, including school fees and learning materials.

One of the beneficiaries had previously expressed his ambition to become a governor, reflecting the aspirations of some of the pupils recognised under the programme.

World Children’s Day, observed annually on November 20, highlights children’s rights, access to quality education and the need to provide an environment where every child can develop their potential.

The post World Children’s Day: 60 Lagos pupils benefit from educational support appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: 2027: You must stay the course for progress, Tinubu tells Oyo electorate
description:
By Adeola Badru



President Bola Tinubu has urged the people of Oyo State to sustain their support for the All Progressives Congress, APC, ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring that continuity was essential for Nigeria’s progress, prosperity and development.



Tinubu, who spoke at the APC
content:
By Adeola Badru

President Bola Tinubu has urged the people of Oyo State to sustain their support for the All Progressives Congress, APC, ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring that continuity was essential for Nigeria’s progress, prosperity and development.

Tinubu, who spoke at the APC presidential campaign rally held at the historic Mapo Hall in Ibadan on Saturday, called on the electorate to remain steadfast in their support for the party, while promising increased investment in education, agriculture, industrialisation and electricity supply.

The President also endorsed Senator Sharafadeen Alli as the APC’s governorship candidate in Oyo State, urging the electorate to vote for him in the forthcoming election.

He said the people of Oyo State had overwhelmingly supported the APC in the previous election and should not abandon the party, stressing that their continued backing would help secure a better future for their children and generations yet unborn.

The rally was preceded by the arrival of the President at the Ladoke Akintola Airport, Ibadan, where the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, and other members of the Oyo State Council of Obas and Chiefs received him.

Addressing the political gathering at Mapo Hall, Tinubu called on the electorate to sustain their loyalty to the APC, describing the party as their own political platform.

“I just want to say thank you. Thank you for all you have been doing and all the support you have given to APC. APC is our party. It’s your party. Is it clear?” he said.

The President reminded the electorate that they had overwhelmingly supported the APC in the previous election, urging them to remain committed to the party as the country prepares for another general election.

“You voted overwhelmingly for APC last time. You must stay the course. You must. For the sake of progress, prosperity of our country, development, for your children and our great-grandchildren,” the president said.

He stressed that the decisions being taken by the present generation must create opportunities for future generations to benefit from the country’s development.

“Our future children must benefit from the hope of Nigeria,” the President said.

He added that the country must prioritise education and agriculture to ensure that younger generations had the opportunity to thrive.

“We must give them the right education, invest in agriculture,” he said.

Bayelsa boat accident victims

Before addressing the political gathering, Tinubu called for a minute’s silence in honour of those who lost their lives in a boat accident in Bayelsa State.

The President expressed sympathy with the bereaved families and the people of the state, assuring them of the nation’s solidarity during their period of grief.

“To show respect and appreciate those who lost their lives when the boat capsized in Bayelsa State. We show solidarity and sympathy.

“Our condolences go to the people of Bayelsa State and the bereaved families. And we have one minute of silence,” he said.

The President also announced that his administration had signed an agreement with a Chinese company, U-Turn, to reopen the old Leyland factory in Ibadan, describing the initiative as part of efforts to revive industrial activities in Oyo State.

Tinubu said the factory would be reopened for the production of public transport vehicles and the establishment of automobile assembly plants, promising that his administration would continue to attract industries to the state.

“For Oyo State, we have just signed an agreement with China’s Yutong to reopen the old Leyland factory in Ibadan. We are reopening it to produce public transport vehicles and establish an automobile assembly plant there. We will continue to bring industries. You will see progress and development,” he added.

The announcement was also welcomed by Olubadan, who expressed appreciation to the President for infrastructure projects being undertaken across the country, particularly in the South-West.

The monarch specifically mentioned the Leyland Motor Assembly in Ibadan, the Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode Road and the Ibadan-Oyo Road, saying the projects would help address longstanding infrastructure challenges.

Tinubu also assured the people of Oyo State that electricity supply would improve, expressing confidence in the efforts of the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, and his team.

“You will see, and I guarantee you an improvement in electricity. Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe is really working hard with his team.”

Tinubu also used the occasion to recognise the contributions of APC elders and leaders, particularly those who had continued to support the party over the years.

He specifically mentioned former Ogun State Governor, Aremo Olusegun Osoba, and former Osun State Governor, Chief Bisi Akande, commending them and other party elders for their commitment to the APC.

“Now it is time to say thank you to all the elders, starting from Aremo Olusegun Osoba, Chief Bisi Akande, and others who have been holding the flag and supporting the party ever since. I salute sincerely,” he said.

The President also acknowledged traditional rulers in Oyo State, including the Olubadan of Ibadanland and the Soun of Ogbomoso, saying he had seen and spoken with them.

“I salute Olubadan. I’ve seen him. Soun of Ogbomosho and all the other obas. I’ve spoken with them. They will support you in every way possible,” he said.

He expressed confidence that the traditional rulers would continue to support the APC, saying he had interacted with them and believed they would assist the party in every way possible.

The President, however, took a swipe at opposition parties, dismissing their capacity and urging the electorate not to be distracted by them.

“And there is a party around that cannot hold anything, please don’t look at them, they are mediocre,” he said.

Tinubu subsequently declared his support for Senator Sharafadeen Alli as the APC’s governorship candidate in Oyo State, urging the electorate to vote for him in the 2027 election.

“I will show you the governorship candidate in Oyo State that you must vote for, and is Sen. Sharafadeen Alli,” the President said.

Olubadan

Earlier, the President was received at the Ladoke Akintola Airport, Ibadan, by the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, and scores of monarchs drawn from the various traditional councils across Oyo State.

The monarchs, who arrived at the airport at about 1.30pm, were drawn from Ibadan, Ibarapa, Oyo, Ogbomoso and Oke-Ogun zones I and II.

Their presence was to reaffirm the position of leading South-West monarchs at their recent meeting in Ibadan on Tinubu’s re-election.

Welcoming the President and his entourage on behalf of the Oyo State Council of Obas and Chiefs, the Olubadan, who is also the chairman of the council, described Tinubu as the leader the monarchs had been waiting to receive.

“This is the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu that we have been waiting for,” the Olubadan said.

The monarch contended that, just as a man’s gifts could make a way for him, so could the work of his hands.

He appreciated the President for the infrastructure development projects being undertaken nationwide, particularly in the South-West, describing them as works in progress.

Olubadan said the projects should be completed before fresh requests were made for additional ones.

He expressed gratitude to Tinubu for the Leyland Motor Assembly project in Ibadan, the Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode Road and the Ibadan-Oyo Road, among others.

According to him, many of the roads had previously fallen into a terrible state of disrepair, exposing commuters to untold suffering.

In his remarks, Tinubu thanked the monarchs for their prayers and co-operation, urging them to prevail on their subjects to come out en masse and vote in the forthcoming election.

The President stressed that mass participation in the election was important.

Other monarchs in attendance included the Soun of Ogbomoso, the Eleruwa of Eruwa, the Aseyin of Iseyin, the Okere of Saki, the Onpetu of Ijeru, the Olugbon of Orile-Igbon, the Onigboho of Igboho, the Alagere of Ago-Are, the Olokaka of Okaka, the Ona Onibode of Igboho, the Akibio of Ilora, the Olu of Fiditi and the Alajawa of Ajaawa.

Members of the Olubadan-in-Council were also present at the airport to receive the President.

Hoodlums clash

Meanwhile, chaos broke out at the APC presidential campaign rally in Ibadan on Saturday as hoodlums clashed at the campaign ground before the arrival of President Tinubu.

The incident, which occurred at the rally venue, involved multiple gunshots fired into the air as the crowd of APC supporters scampered for safety.

Our correspondent observed some of the hoodlums dragging the firearm shot by an unidentified man amid the chaos.

The brief scuffle reportedly escalated as some hoodlums hurled sticks and placards towards the media stand, dispersing the crowd.

The incident disrupted activities at the campaign ground before the President’s arrival, with supporters fleeing in different directions as the situation deteriorated.

title: FBI probes suspected hack of US crime database
description:
The Federal Bureau of Investigation is “investigating a suspected cyberattack on its National Crime Information Centre (NCIC), a nationwide database used by law enforcement agencies across the United States to share criminal justice information.”
The suspected intrusion was discovered in recent days
content:
The Federal Bureau of Investigation is “investigating a suspected cyberattack on its National Crime Information Centre (NCIC), a nationwide database used by law enforcement agencies across the United States to share criminal justice information.”

The suspected intrusion was discovered in recent days, with two people briefed on the investigation telling CNN that hackers apparently gained access to the system.

The development, reported by CNN on Friday, marks the second reported cyber intrusion involving FBI systems in recent months.

KCRA3 on Saturday reported that a former FBI cybercrime investigations official (name withheld) warned CNN that the concern was not “merely whether hackers accessed sensitive information, but whether they could compromise the accuracy of records used by police officers.

The NCIC serves as a central information-sharing platform for federal, state and local law enforcement agencies, providing access to records on outstanding warrants, wanted individuals, criminal histories and information used for background checks.

A former FBI official who previously led investigations into cybercriminal groups told CNN that the database was critical to day-to-day policing, as officers across the country rely on it to identify wanted fugitives and check outstanding warrants.

The former official also raised concerns about the possibility of hackers compromising the accuracy of information contained in the database, warning that incorrect records could affect decisions made by law enforcement officers.

The FBI did not immediately respond to requests for comment from CNN and Reuters.

The suspected breach comes amid growing concerns over cybersecurity vulnerabilities affecting US government institutions and critical infrastructure, following a series of technological disruptions involving banks, the National Security Agency and the Federal Aviation Administration’s air traffic control systems.

On Thursday, after FBI officials had reportedly learnt of the suspected intrusion, FBI Director Kash Patel appeared on Fox News to discuss the bureau’s cybersecurity efforts.

Patel promoted Operation Winter Shield, an initiative aimed at encouraging organisations to strengthen their digital security and protect critical infrastructure.

“Other administrations could have made these updates, but they didn’t,” he said, “We are staying ahead of the curve and making up for lost time.”

In a separate post on X on Friday, Patel said the FBI was taking the fight against cybercriminals around the world under President Donald Trump’s leadership.

“Through Operation Winter Shield, we’re going on offense against cyber threats, strengthening our nation’s defences, and working with our partners to protect American businesses, government systems, and critical infrastructure,” he wrote.

The latest suspected intrusion follows a September breach of an FBI recruitment website by the digital extortion group ShinyHunters, which reportedly exposed personal information belonging to current and former bureau employees.

The group claimed responsibility for that attack, which prompted an FBI investigation.

However, the “identity of those responsible for the latest suspected intrusion, the method used to access the NCIC and whether any information was stolen or altered remain unclear.”

title: CIPM urges HR professionals to drive public service reform
description:
The Chartered Institute of Personnel Management of Nigeria has urged human resource professionals in the public service to move beyond routine personnel administration and take a more strategic role in improving institutional performance, accountability and service delivery.
The institute said tradi
content:
The Chartered Institute of Personnel Management of Nigeria has urged human resource professionals in the public service to move beyond routine personnel administration and take a more strategic role in improving institutional performance, accountability and service delivery.

The institute said traditional personnel management practices were no longer sufficient to address the challenges facing public institutions, calling for greater emphasis on workforce productivity, employee development, ethical leadership and institutional efficiency.

CIPM disclosed this in a news release on Saturday, following its 74th Induction Ceremony in Lagos, where 134 professionals were admitted through its Executive and Practitioners’ routes.

The President and Chairman of the Governing Council of CIPM, Mallam Ahmed Gobir, said professional HR practice should translate into better decisions, stronger workplace values and improved contributions to organisations and society.

“The letters after your name, either ACIPM or MCIPM, must be supported by the values behind your decisions,” Gobir said.

He urged the inductees to challenge outdated administrative practices and promote employee development, performance management and institutional effectiveness, stressing that the public service should be driven by the needs of citizens.

“A government office can be fully staffed and still leave citizens underserved,” he said, adding that people seeking government services were the reason public institutions existed and should not be treated as interruptions to public servants’ work.

Gobir also described professional membership as a responsibility to uphold standards and strengthen the institute’s reputation through ethical conduct and sound decision-making.

Delivering the guest presentation, the Council Manager and Head of Administration at Agege Local Government, Mr Osikoya Adesina Sogo, called for a shift from routine personnel administration to strategic workforce management, identifying changes needed to improve public sector performance.

He advocated replacing reactive staff deployment with data-driven workforce planning, generic training with targeted skills development, and reactive disciplinary measures with stronger employee engagement and organisational culture.

Sogo also called for a shift from procedural compliance to stronger governance and ethical responsibility, noting that personnel decisions at the local government level had direct implications for service delivery.

He said staff deployment, training, personnel records and industrial relations influenced the quality of services provided by local authorities, urging HR professionals to balance performance standards with employee dignity, fairness and respect for due process.

The Vice President of CIPM, Mrs Chidinma Obiejesi, said human capital strategy was critical to public service transformation and called for stronger collaboration with the Lagos State Government to advance reforms in the state’s public sector.

The institute’s National Treasurer, Mr Adeyemi Ajayi, also urged the new members to contribute to its development through mentoring, coaching, continuous learning and participation in its professional activities.

A total of 134 professionals were inducted at the ceremony, comprising eight admitted through the Executive Route and 126 through the Practitioners’ Route.

CIPM said stronger public institutions depended on competent, ethical and professionally managed workforces, adding that the value of professional recognition should be reflected in practitioners’ contributions to their workplaces and society.

The post CIPM urges HR professionals to drive public service reform appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Rafael Nadal joins Real Madrid board
description:
Tennis legend Rafael Nadal has been elected to the board of directors of Spanish football club Real Madrid after receiving 99.5 per cent of votes at the club’s Extraordinary General Assembly.
The 22-time Grand Slam champion was ratified as a board member on Saturday during the assembly held at the b
content:
Tennis legend Rafael Nadal has been elected to the board of directors of Spanish football club Real Madrid after receiving 99.5 per cent of votes at the club’s Extraordinary General Assembly.

The 22-time Grand Slam champion was ratified as a board member on Saturday during the assembly held at the basketball pavilion of the club’s Ciudad Real Madrid training complex.

According to an announcement on Real Madrid’s website on Saturday, 1,704 of the 1,713 votes cast were in favour of Nadal’s appointment, with four against and five abstentions.

Nadal, who has been an honorary member of the club since 2011, received a standing ovation from the club’s representative members following the vote.

Reacting to his appointment, the 40-year-old Spaniard described the position as a major responsibility and expressed his desire to contribute to the club’s future.

“It is a great responsibility to be part of the Board of Directors of Real Madrid. This club is passed down from parents to children and unites people. For me, it connects me with family and friends to watch matches together. It’s an immense joy and a great satisfaction.

“I am very aware of the responsibility because Real Madrid is a global brand. It is an infinite responsibility, and I take it on with the hope of learning and contributing so that this club continues to be the best in the world,” he said.

Real Madrid president Florentino Pérez welcomed Nadal’s appointment, describing him as a sporting legend whose influence extended beyond his achievements on the tennis court.

Pérez said Nadal’s inclusion in the board represented more than the arrival of a celebrated athlete, adding that the tennis star wanted to share the responsibility of shaping the club’s future.

Nadal is one of the most successful tennis players in history, having won 22 Grand Slam singles titles, including a record 14 French Open championships.

He also won two Olympic gold medals, five Davis Cup titles with Spain and spent time as world number one during his career.

title: Tinubu arrives Lagos after Ibadan APC rally
description:
President Bola Tinubu arrived in Lagos on Saturday after attending the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State.
His aircraft landed at the Presidential Wing of the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Ikeja, at about 3pm, according to a statement by his Special
content:
President Bola Tinubu arrived in Lagos on Saturday after attending the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State.

His aircraft landed at the Presidential Wing of the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Ikeja, at about 3pm, according to a statement by his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga.

Tinubu was received by Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun, his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila, and former Ogun State Governor Segun Osoba.

Other government officials, party leaders and supporters were also at the airport to welcome him.

“While in Lagos on the short visit, President Tinubu is scheduled to attend a special prayer session organised in his honour by members of his family on Sunday, November 22,” the statement said.

He is expected to return to Abuja after the visit.

Earlier on Saturday, Tinubu attended the APC presidential campaign rally at Mapo Hall in Ibadan.

At the rally, he promised improved electricity supply in Oyo State and disclosed that his administration had reached an agreement with Chinese automobile manufacturer Yutong to revive the old Leyland factory in Ibadan for vehicle assembly.

He also urged residents to support the APC in the 2027 elections and publicly endorsed the party’s governorship candidates in Oyo, Ogun and Lagos states, as well as its Oyo South senatorial candidate.

The event was held without much fanfare following the President’s directive in honour of victims of the Bayelsa boat accident, with a minute’s silence observed for those who died.
