title: Tinubu unveils 50,000 new hostel bed spaces for federal varsities, commissions UI medical hostel
description:
President Bola Tinubu has promised to provide an additional 50,000 bed spaces in hostels across federal tertiary institutions by the end of 2027 to address accommodation challenges facing Nigerian students.
Tinubu made the pledge on Saturday during the inauguration of Block E of the College of Medic
content:
President Bola Tinubu has promised to provide an additional 50,000 bed spaces in hostels across federal tertiary institutions by the end of 2027 to address accommodation challenges facing Nigerian students.

Tinubu made the pledge on Saturday during the inauguration of Block E of the College of Medicine hostel at the University of Ibadan (UI), located at Alexander Brown Hall, University College Hospital.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the newly inaugurated hostel block was donated by the Chagoury family.

The President said the planned expansion of student accommodation was part of efforts to improve living conditions in federal tertiary institutions and ease the difficulties students face in securing affordable hostel spaces.

The initiative is expected to increase accommodation capacity and provide more students with access to suitable residential facilities within their institutions.

The President, represented by the Minister of Education, Dr Maruf Alausa, said that the 50,000 bed space hostels would be delivered through the ₦400 billion Student Hostels Programme, implemented via the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) and Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs).

He said the initiative was aimed at providing students with safe and decent accommodation to support their education.

“The accommodation shortage at the College of Medicine has become a critical challenge following the 2020 directive of the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN) requiring clinical students of medicine and dentistry to reside within the University College Hospital (UCH) premises for accreditation purposes.

“The college faced a shortfall of 490 bed spaces, representing 44.5 per cent of its accommodation requirement, leaving many students exposed to insecurity and difficulties attending essential clinical sessions,” the president said.

According to him, the shortage also prevented the college from fully utilising its annual admission quota for the Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) programme.

Tinubu said his administration was prioritising education funding and reforms through initiatives such as the Nigerian Education Sector Renewal Initiative, Nigeria Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), TETFund and the Student Venture Capital Grant.

He added that more than 36 universities had benefited from the Renewed Hope Energising Education Programme, with power installations ranging from 2.5 megawatts to 12 megawatts.

The President also said that the government had completed 20 compressed natural gas (CNG) conversion centres and maintenance facilities in some universities, with 40 additional facilities expected by the end of 2028.

Earlier, the Vice-Chancellor of UI, Prof. Peter Olapegba, said the inauguration of Block E marked another milestone in efforts to provide adequate accommodation for medical students and meet accreditation requirements.

Olapegba expressed appreciation to the benefactors, Ambassador Gilbert Ramez Chagoury and his brother, Ronald Chagoury, for their contribution to medical education.

“The hostel, named the Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu GCFR Block, provides accommodation for 192 medical and dental students in 48 rooms, with four students per room.

“The building also has four reading rooms, each measuring about 71 square metres, as well as rooms equipped with toilets, showers and kitchenettes,” Olapegba said.

The immediate past provost of the College of Medicine, Prof. Olayinka Omigbodun, said the hostel project was initiated to address the accommodation deficit that threatened the college’s ability to meet accreditation requirements.

Omigbodun, represented by Prof. Fatai Adeniyi, said the college required 1,101 bed spaces for clinical students but had only 611, resulting in a shortfall of about 500 beds.

She said the deficit had previously constrained the college’s ability to admit students up to its annual quota.

The Provost, College of Medicine, Prof. Temidayo Ogundiran, expressed appreciation to stakeholders and supporters who contributed to the realisation of the project.

According to him, the various contributions of the President Bola Tinubu-led administration had repositioned the education sector. (NAN)

The post Tinubu unveils 50,000 new hostel bed spaces for federal varsities, commissions UI medical hostel appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: ‘I Guarantee You Improvement In Electricity,’ Tinubu Tells Nigerians At Oyo Presidential Campaign Rally
description: President Bola Tinubu has assured Nigerians of improved electricity supply, promising to address the country’s persistent power challenges.The President gave the assurance on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign rally at Mapo Hall in Ibadan, Oyo State, ahead of the 2027
content:
President Bola Tinubu has assured Nigerians of improved electricity supply, promising to address the country’s persistent power challenges.

The President gave the assurance on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign rally at Mapo Hall in Ibadan, Oyo State, ahead of the 2027 general elections.

“We will continue to bring industry, you will see, and I guarantee you an improvement in electricity. Joseph Tegbe (Minister of Power) is working really hard with his team. You voted overwhelmingly for APC last time; you must stay the course for the sake of progress, prosperity of our country, development for the children and our great-grandchildren. Our future children must benefit from the hope of Nigeria. We must give them the right education and invest in Agriculture,” he said.

The President also announced plans to revive the defunct Leyland automobile factory in Ibadan through an agreement with Chinese bus manufacturer Yutong.

“For Oyo State, we have signed an agreement with Yutong of China to reopen the old Leyland factory in Ibadan. We are reopening it to produce public transport and automobile assembly plant there,” he said.

The agreement, signed on November 19, 2026, involves the Federal Government, through the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles (Pi-CNG & EV), Yutong and its local partner, YP Automobile.

Electricity Challenges

Tinubu’s latest assurance comes amid growing frustration among Nigerians over inadequate electricity supply, with households and businesses grappling with prolonged outages in different parts of the country.

The shortages have renewed questions about the effectiveness of the Band A, B and C electricity tariff classification, which links customers’ payments to the minimum hours of electricity supply they are expected to receive.

Customers on Band A, who are entitled to a minimum of 20 hours of electricity daily, have also complained about inadequate supply.

Intense heat has compounded the situation, leaving many residents struggling to cope without electricity to run fans and air conditioners.

Several Nigerians, including figures like Kate Henshaw and Cute Abiola, have expressed frustration over persistent power outages, lamenting that households have become “mini-factories” forced to generate their own electricity.

Meanwhile, rising petrol and diesel prices have made generator use increasingly expensive, while the cost of installing solar panels, batteries and inverters remains beyond the reach of many households and small businesses.

Minister of Power Tegbe recently attributed the prolonged blackouts to planned maintenance at the Egbin Power Station, gas supply shortages and vandalism of transmission infrastructure.

Tinubu’s 2023 Electricity Promise

The President’s latest assurance has also brought renewed attention to his 2023 campaign promise to tackle Nigeria’s electricity challenges and end estimated billing.

During his campaign, Tinubu told members of the Organised Private Sector in Lagos that Nigerians should hold him accountable if he failed to deliver on the promise.

“Whichever way, by all means necessary, you will have electricity, and you will not pay for estimated bills anymore. A promise made will be a promise kept. If I don’t keep the promise and I come for a second term, don’t vote for me, unless I give you adequate reasons why I couldn’t deliver,” he said.

The pledge returned to public discussion this week following comments by former Lagos State Governor and former Minister of Works, Babatunde Fashola, during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today.

Fashola argued that Tinubu did not specifically promise Nigerians 24-hour electricity during the 2023 campaign, saying his remarks had been taken out of context.

He explained that the President’s statement contained a qualification that voters should not re-elect him if he failed to deliver, unless he provided adequate reasons for the failure.

Fashola also urged Nigerians to assess the administration’s performance based on their personal experiences with electricity supply and the progress made in ending estimated billing.

His comments, however, attracted criticism from opposition figures and the campaign organisation of Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, who argued that the debate over the wording of Tinubu’s promise did not address the continuing power challenges facing Nigerians.

The post ‘I Guarantee You Improvement In Electricity,’ Tinubu Tells Nigerians At Oyo Presidential Campaign Rally appeared first on Channels Television.

title: EPL: Fulham hold Man City to 1-1 draw
description:
Manchester City ended their run of three consecutive Premier League defeats but were held to a 1-1 draw by Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday.
Elliot Anderson scored the equaliser for City in the second half after Rodrigo Muniz had given the visitors an early lead.
Fulham took the lead in the
content:
Manchester City ended their run of three consecutive Premier League defeats but were held to a 1-1 draw by Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday.

Elliot Anderson scored the equaliser for City in the second half after Rodrigo Muniz had given the visitors an early lead.

Fulham took the lead in the 16th minute when Muniz finished off a pass from former Manchester City winger Oscar Bobb, putting the visitors ahead.

City thought they had restored parity shortly afterwards through Erling Haaland, but the goal was disallowed after referee Thomas Bramall ruled that the striker had fouled Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno while attempting to score.

The decision stood after a VAR review, leaving the hosts frustrated.

Anderson levelled the scoring in the 57th minute with a powerful volley from the edge of the penalty area after Fulham failed to clear a corner.

The England international came close to scoring again as City pushed for a winner, but his effort went narrowly wide.

Fulham also threatened to reclaim the lead, with Muniz forcing a save from City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, while Calvin Bassey also came close.

Despite late pressure from both sides, neither team could find a winning goal as the match ended 1-1.

The result ended Fulham’s 20-match losing streak against Manchester City in all competitions.

City remain third in the Premier League table, five points behind leaders Arsenal, while Fulham extended their unbeaten run to five matches.

The post EPL: Fulham hold Man City to 1-1 draw appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: ‘Our Culture’: Deaf Nigerians Embrace Indigenous Sign Languages
description: With a quick flick of the wrist, Umaru Zayyanu conveys the phrase “I am a Nigerian”.But the 37-year-old is not speaking — or signing, rather — in the official sign language, Nigerian Sign Language (NSL). Instead, he’s using Hausa sign language.Such indigenous sign langu
content:
With a quick flick of the wrist, Umaru Zayyanu conveys the phrase “I am a Nigerian”.

But the 37-year-old is not speaking — or signing, rather — in the official sign language, Nigerian Sign Language (NSL). Instead, he’s using Hausa sign language.

Such indigenous sign languages abound in the country, where deaf people were communicating with each other long before the advent of formal sign language taught in deaf schools, in 1960.

Today, Nigeria, like many countries on the continent with limited education budgets, has a hard enough time placing children in dedicated schools for the deaf and hard of hearing.

And there’s even less attention paid to local sign languages used outside the school system — a serious disservice to the country’s linguistic diversity, Festus Zenda, who has worked on documentation projects with local deaf communities, told AFP.

“These indigenous signing systems should be studied, documented and preserved before changes in education, migration, technology and wider use of Nigerian Sign Language cause some of them to decline or disappear,” said Zenda, who has helped document the local sign language used by the Tiv ethnic group, in Benue state.

Displacement by formal signing

The working-class Abuja exurb of Zuba is a symphony of motorcycle horns, plantain hawkers’ shouts and the dull hum of construction work.

Another group adds their own, milder contributions: claps, muffled shouts of exclamation and the swish of rapid hand gestures as they chat in Hausa signs.

Nigerian sign languages, like their spoken counterparts, are sometimes confined to a small number of speakers in a country crowded with some 500 tongues and an unknown number of sign languages.

But Hausa sign language has become a lingua franca for deaf people across the north of the country.

“I cherish my culture, I cherish my indigenous sign language,” Sanni Lawal, who runs a laundry business in Zuba’s crowded market, told AFP through an interpreter. “I want it to expand everywhere.”

Nigeria traces its official sign language to Andrew Foster, an American who introduced formal deaf education across a swathe of African countries at the dawn of independence from colonial powers.

Many countries in the region today use an official sign language based on American Sign Language.

But in the decades since, some scholars argue indigenous signing has languished as governments have prioritised formal languages.

“People gather in the moonlight narrating their folklores in indigenous sign,” said Joshua Gyang, who has researched local languages with Nigeria’s deaf activist community.

Nevertheless, he warned they will “certainly perish” without preservation.

‘Our culture and identity’

The government doesn’t completely ignore local sign languages: politicians often bring Hausa signers to campaign stops to court deaf voters, Zuba residents told AFP.

The strategy makes sense: there’s no school there to teach formal sign language.

Under a USAID programme administered by Gallaudet University — the United States’ premier university for deaf and hard of hearing students, and Foster’s alma mater — researchers were providing training to deaf educators in Nigeria, which touched on local languages as well.

In a 2024 update, the university said their work sparked discussions around languages like Hausa sign language and whether they “deserve recognition and should be the medium of instruction in schools”.

The programme was shut down last year as Washington slashed foreign aid spending.

Nevertheless, Nigerian researchers and activists like Zenda, Zayyanu, Gyang and their colleague Taiwo Ajayi continue to document indigenous sign languages.

Even Nigerian sign language has its own local flair, Ajayi, a sign language interpreter, told AFP, noting the differences in the way signs are taught in school and the way people actually converse in the street.

For Hausa signers, their language has become a key part of “our culture and identity”, Zayyanu told AFP.

“Even before we go to school, we have our own language,” he said. “Instead of burying that one, why not develop it?”

The post ‘Our Culture’: Deaf Nigerians Embrace Indigenous Sign Languages appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Backlash trails defence ministry over publicity of Tinubu’s 2027 APC campaign rally
description:
The Ministry of Defence has faced criticism on social media after its official X account shared details of preparations for the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in support of President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid.
In a post published on Saturday, the ministry announ
content:
The Ministry of Defence has faced criticism on social media after its official X account shared details of preparations for the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in support of President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid.

In a post published on Saturday, the ministry announced that the rally was scheduled to take place at Mapo Hall in Ibadan, Oyo State, on November 21, 2026, with President Tinubu and other key APC officials expected to attend.

The ministry also disclosed that the Minister of Defence, retired General Christopher Musa, had visited the venue on Friday night to inspect security arrangements and other preparations ahead of the event.

The post attracted criticism from social media users, who questioned the ministry’s involvement in publicising activities linked to a political party’s campaign rally.

“Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (Rtd), OFR, Friday night conducted an on-the-spot inspection of the venue as part of strategic preparations ahead of the upcoming presidential campaign rally in the state,” the post reads.

“During the visit, General Musa toured the premises and surrounding perimeters to evaluate security readiness, crowd management logistics, and overall infrastructural preparedness. President Bola Tinubu GCFR, and key party officials would be on ground for the rally.”

The post, which was accompanied by photographs of the minister’s inspection, was followed by criticism from several Nigerians, who questioned the use of an official government platform to publicise the activities of a political party.

One of the critics, Kunle Adebajo, described the development as “political psychosis so deep it’s ridiculous even by Nigerian standards”.

Another X user, N6, questioned the ministry’s apparent involvement in partisan activities, asking, “How is the Ministry of Defence handle clearly being Partisan. Have you lost it?”

Similarly, a user identified as Dollarain2000 said, “Is this really the official handle of Nigeria’s Defence Ministry? Or the Security Directorate of the APC Presidential Campaign Council?” the user asked.

Another critic, Emmanuel Doji, expressed concern over what he described as the blurring of boundaries between government responsibilities and involvement in partisan political activities.

He wrote, “So what exactly is the meaning of this? The official Twitter handle of the Ministry of Defence is now publishing a political party’s campaign schedule and updates on preparations for its rally? Where exactly do we draw the line between government business and party politics?

“A whole Ministry of Defence is now a publicity arm of the APC. Will it also publish the activities and campaign schedules of other political parties? This is completely inappropriate and should be condemned. Government institutions should not be turned into platforms for partisan political activities. This is not how things should be done.”

Another user, Benjamin, wrote, “Defence handle of the nation doing this! No, no, no, no! This is preposterous! This is no more Democracy!”

Josephu_o also criticised the development, he wrote, “Imagine the Ministry of Defence, an institution funded by Nigerian taxpayers and entrusted with the security of over 200 million citizens, using its official platform to publicise a political party’s re-election rally.

“Is this a Ministry of Defence or an APC campaign publicity office? State institutions belong to Nigerians, not political parties,” the user added.

Another user, HonShield, questioned whether the ministry would extend the same publicity to opposition parties, asking, “Dear Ministry of Defence, will you also do this for other political parties? Do you now belong to the APC to be tweeting for their campaign? What’s going on in this country for God’s sake?”

The post Backlash trails defence ministry over publicity of Tinubu’s 2027 APC campaign rally appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: 2027: Reset your mind, align with people’s choice, Oshiomhole tells Makinde
description:
By Adeola Badru



Senator Adams Oshiomhole, former Governor of Edo State, has urged Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, to reconsider his political position ahead of the 2027 general elections, saying the country needed leaders committed
content:
By Adeola Badru

Senator Adams Oshiomhole, former Governor of Edo State, has urged Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, to reconsider his political position ahead of the 2027 general elections, saying the country needed leaders committed to sustaining progress.

Oshiomhole, who spoke in Ibadan on Saturday during President Bola Tinubu’s rally at the historic Mapo Hall, challenged Makinde to align himself with the wishes of the electorate, insisting that the governor must first reconsider his own position on Tinubu’s re-election bid.

The former Edo governor, who expressed support for Tinubu’s second-term ambition, described the forthcoming election as a decisive moment for Nigeria and questioned whether Makinde’s call for a reset was intended to reverse policies he said had benefited ordinary Nigerians.

“This coming election is a decisive factor. We have a leader, the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said.

Oshiomhole said he had questions for Makinde over his position on Tinubu’s continuation in office, particularly regarding the administration’s student loan scheme, infrastructure development, and improved welfare for university lecturers.

He asked whether Makinde’s opposition to the president’s re-election was connected to the federal government’s decision to provide financial assistance to students from poor backgrounds through the student loan scheme.

“Is Seyi Makinde angry because Tinubu is giving loans to the children of poor people in our universities? Is that what Makinde wants to reset?” he asked.

The senator also questioned whether the governor intended to reverse the federal government’s infrastructure projects, particularly the coastal highway linking Lagos to Calabar, which he said would improve connectivity and make movement easier for Nigerians.

“The President is creating massive infrastructure to connect Lagos to Calabar so that our people can move. Is that what Makinde wants to reset?” he said.

Oshiomhole further challenged Makinde’s position on the welfare of university lecturers, citing the University of Ibadan as an example of an institution that had previously experienced repeated disruptions to its academic calendar due to industrial action.

He recalled that university lecturers had, in the past, frequently embarked on strikes, disrupting academic activities and delaying students’ graduation.

“For this city has the most outstanding university in Africa, the University of Ibadan. For a long, long time, the lecturer will teach you for two days and then will go on strike for three days. Is that not true?” he said.

The former governor said the Tinubu administration had deliberately prioritized the welfare of university lecturers, whom he described as critical to developing the country’s future workforce.

He argued that improved remuneration for lecturers would strengthen the education sector, encourage qualified academics to remain in the profession, and ensure that students could complete their studies without repeated interruptions.

“I just want to deliver this message. Now, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has deliberately decided that those who make the manpower of tomorrow are the lecturers in our universities.”

“And he has increased their pay substantially so that for four years, your academic calendar has not been interrupted,” he said.

Oshiomhole asked whether Makinde intended to reverse the policy, allow strikes to return to the university system, or reduce lecturers’ salaries.

“Does Makinde want to reset this policy? Does he want the strike to return? Does he want to reduce the salaries of lecturers?” he asked.

He maintained that improved remuneration for university lecturers would encourage more intelligent minds to return to the teaching profession, which he described as one of the noblest professions.

“When you pay lecturers very well, intelligent minds will go back to the teaching profession, which is the most noble profession,” he said.

Oshiomhole, who repeatedly challenged Makinde’s call for a reset, urged the governor to reconsider his position and align himself with the aspirations of the electorate ahead of the 2027 elections.

He said Nigeria needed political leaders who would prioritize the country’s development and sustain policies aimed at improving the lives of citizens.

“When you go back, tell the man in Ibadan he is for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said.

The senator concluded by urging Makinde to reconsider his position before the election, stressing that the country’s progress should remain the priority of political leaders.

“The governor needs to reset his own mind before the election. We want Nigeria to progress. Thank you and God bless,” Oshiomhole said

The post 2027: Reset your mind, align with people’s choice, Oshiomhole tells Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Bayelsa boat mishap: more bodies recovered on river
description:
Bayelsa Govt, NDC mourn
___________________________________________________________________
From Femi Folaranmi, Yenagoa
Joint search and rescue efforts by the Bayelsa State government and security agencies have rescued more survivors and recovered more bodies after hundreds of people were feared mi
content:
Bayelsa Govt, NDC mourn

___________________________________________________________________

From Femi Folaranmi, Yenagoa

Joint search and rescue efforts by the Bayelsa State government and security agencies have rescued more survivors and recovered more bodies after hundreds of people were feared missing following a love boat mishap along the waterways of Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.

The love boat, which left Ayama carrying mourners to a burial in Ukubie in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area, had a mishap at a river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities.

Investigations revealed that the initial search and rescue efforts conducted by the police and security agencies rescued 24 passengers and recovered four bodies.

Nineteen of the 24 rescued victims were immediately taken to Ayama Hospital, while five in critical condition were taken to Family Care Hospital, Yenagoa, and the four passengers confirmed dead had their bodies deposited at the Federal Medical Centre (FMC).

On Saturday, six bodies were seen floating on the river, while search and rescue efforts recovered more bodies, including two children.

The Bayelsa State Government has stated that it is fully supporting the ongoing joint search and rescue operation and will continue to provide all necessary assistance to the divers, the police and other responders until the operation is concluded.

The Bayelsa State Commissioner for Information, Orientation and Strategy, Mrs Ebiuwou Koku-Obiyai, in a statement on behalf of the state government, condoled with the families of the deceased and assured them that the state government stands with them in their moment of grief.

It seized the opportunity to appeal again to boat operators and passengers across the state to strictly observe safety regulations.

‘Overloading, speeding, recklessness and travelling without life jackets must stop. No journey is worth a life. Operators must respect approved passenger capacity, ensure their boats are in good condition, and avoid night and bad weather travel.

‘The government will continue to work with relevant agencies, community leaders and transport unions to strengthen waterway safety and prevent a recurrence of such tragedies.’

The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Bayelsa State, in a statement by its chairman, Hon Dauprebo Ikuromo, has expressed deep sorrow over the boat mishap.

The party, while condoling with the victims and the families of the deceased, said the disaster should serve as a wake-up call for the government to address the persistent dangers associated with water transportation in the predominantly riverine state.

It noted that waterways remain the major means of transportation for several communities in Bayelsa, stressing that the safety of residents who depend on them for their daily activities and livelihoods must be treated as a priority.

The party stated that protecting lives on the waterways requires more than occasional appeals to boat operators and passengers to observe safety regulations.

It emphasised the need for sustained government commitment through effective regulation, routine safety inspections, functional emergency response systems, adequate life-saving equipment and accessible rescue services across the state’s waterways.

The NDC therefore called on the Bayelsa State Government, under Governor Douye Diri, to urgently formulate and implement a comprehensive maritime safety policy to strengthen water transportation, prevent avoidable accidents and protect lives.

The party maintained that the government must take proactive steps to ensure that residents of riverine communities can travel safely without being exposed to unnecessary risks.

Also mourning the victims of the boat mishap, the member of the House of Representatives representing the Southern Ijaw Federal Constituency, Hon Rodney Amabaiowei, commended Bayelsa State Governor, Senator Douye Diri, for his support and the provision of necessary healthcare and other assistance to the victims of the unfortunate incident.

According to him, the timely intervention demonstrates the importance of responsive leadership and government concern for the welfare of its citizens.

Amabaiowei noted that the boat tragedy has again reinforced the urgency of the motion he previously moved at the National Assembly, titled ‘Need to Tackle the Menace of Incessant Boat/Watercraft Mishaps on Our Coastlines and Waterways’.

He stated that the recurring loss of lives through boat mishaps, particularly in riverine communities such as his own, demands urgent and decisive action from relevant government agencies and maritime regulatory authorities.

‘I remain committed to advocating stronger maritime safety regulations, effective monitoring of watercraft operations, enforcement of passenger safety standards and improved safety infrastructure across our waterways to prevent further avoidable tragedies.

‘I appeal for sustained efforts to ensure that everyone involved in this unfortunate incident is accounted for and that adequate support is extended to the affected families.

‘I also urge boat operators to strictly adhere to maritime safety regulations, avoid overloading, ensure their boats are in good condition and provide functional life jackets for passengers. No journey is worth the loss of innocent lives.’

The post Bayelsa boat mishap: more bodies recovered on river appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Customs seize N3.52bn smuggled goods in Ogun
description:
The Nigeria Customs Service, Ogun 1 Area Command, Idiroko, says it “seized various smuggled goods, including 6,037 wraps of cannabis, with a Duty Paid Value of N3.52bn in October.”
The Acting Area Comptroller, Mr Abdulhamid Ahmed, disclosed this at a news conference on Saturday in Idiroko.
Ahmed sai
content:
The Nigeria Customs Service, Ogun 1 Area Command, Idiroko, says it “seized various smuggled goods, including 6,037 wraps of cannabis, with a Duty Paid Value of N3.52bn in October.”

The Acting Area Comptroller, Mr Abdulhamid Ahmed, disclosed this at a news conference on Saturday in Idiroko.

Ahmed said the seizures underscored the command’s commitment to enforcing customs laws, preventing the importation and circulation of prohibited and harmful products, and protecting the nation’s economic interests.

He said the seizures were made during coordinated operations by customs officers at “various smuggling flashpoints across the state.”

According to him, the “operations were intelligence-led and supported by improved enforcement strategies and collaboration with sister security agencies.”

He added that the collaboration helped officers track smugglers, intercept contraband and prevent the illicit goods from entering the country.

Ahmed listed the “seized items to include 20,500 bottles of cough syrup, 125 live cartridges, 828,920 tablets of various brands, 627,320 capsules, 95 pills of prostate medication and 4,000 Enox injections comprising 2,850 ampoules.

“Other seizures included 5,173 bags of foreign parboiled rice weighing 50kg each, 6,037 wraps of cannabis sativa, 1,067 used tyres, 1,037 25-litre kegs of Premium Motor Spirit and 185 packages of sanitary pads and diapers.”

He also listed “two trucks and several vehicles, including a 2024 Toyota RAV4, Toyota Highlander, two Lexus vehicles, a 2000 Toyota Hilux, 2013 Toyota RAV4, Toyota Sienna, 2010 Toyota Venza, Opel, Mazda and 2012 Range Rover Sport.”

The acting comptroller said the total DPV of the seized items with available valuations stood at N3.52bn.

He explained that some smugglers abandoned their consignments and fled into nearby bushes upon sighting approaching customs patrol teams.

Ahmed reiterated the command’s commitment to intensifying anti-smuggling operations to protect the nation’s economy and safeguard public health.

Earlier, the Comptroller-General of Customs, Mr Bashir Adeniyi, urged personnel to “sustain their efforts in combating smuggling activities across the borders.”

Adeniyi also “appealed to residents of border communities to collaborate with the service by providing useful intelligence” and “supporting campaigns against economic and cross-border crimes.”

The post Customs seize N3.52bn smuggled goods in Ogun appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Oyo rally: Tinubu assures Nigerians of improved electricity supply
description:
President Bola Tinubu has assured Nigerians of improved electricity supply, stressing that his administration is working round the clock to boost the power sector.



The president stated this on Saturday in Ibadan during the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign held at the historic Mapo
content:
President Bola Tinubu has assured Nigerians of improved electricity supply, stressing that his administration is working round the clock to boost the power sector.

The president stated this on Saturday in Ibadan during the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign held at the historic Mapo Hall.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the event also featured the formal presentation by President Tinubu of Sen. Sharafadeen Alli as the APC’s governorship candidate to the party’s supporters in Oyo State.

Tinubu commended Oyo State for the overwhelming votes delivered to him in the 2023 elections and urged the citizens to see the party as their own.

“For the sake of progress, development, your children’s future, and prosperity for our country, I urge you to stay the course.

“For our children and grandchildren to benefit from the hope of Nigeria, we must give them the right education and invest in agriculture.

“For Oyo State, we just signed an agreement with Yutong Automobile of China to reopen the old Leyland Automobile factory in Ibadan.

“This aims to start production of commercial vehicles and commence general automobile assembly plant.

“We will continue to bring in more industry, and, in addition, I guarantee you improvement in electricity supply,” he said.

The president, while commending the support of traditional rulers and leaders of the party in the state, urged supporters not to be deceived by other parties that allegedly come to dupe them.

Earlier, in separate goodwill messages, the governor of Ekiti State, Mr. Biodun Oyebanji, on behalf of the 31 progressive governors, and the Anambra and Osun governors, urged the electorate in Yoruba not to trade their votes.

This, he said, was necessary to let the president continue his reforms and good works, such as student loan initiatives, infrastructural development, and various transformational moves in other sectors.

Also, the Senate Leader, Sen. Opeyemi Bamidele, said that splitting the APC votes for different parties across different political offices in Oyo State would not profit the party maximally.

He stressed that votes for the presidential, governorship, and national and state assemblies should be for the APC.

Bamidele added that the achievements of the president in the last three years should be the template for the campaign.

Also, Sen. Adams Oshiomhole said that the coming election remained a decisive factor, as various initiatives and reforms of the president were already resetting Nigeria and should not be a campaign slogan for any other candidate.

NAN reports that the campaign was attended by both former and serving governors, their wives, members of the Senate and House of Representatives, and party leaders, among others. (NAN)

The post Oyo rally: Tinubu assures Nigerians of improved electricity supply appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: FG raises annual medical school admissions to 12,000 — Minister
description:
The Federal Government has increased annual admission into medical schools from 5,000 to 12,000 students, the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, has said.
Alausa, who stated this on the sidelines of the inauguration of a 192-bed hostel at the College of Medicine, University of Ibadan, on Saturd
content:
The Federal Government has increased annual admission into medical schools from 5,000 to 12,000 students, the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, has said.

Alausa, who stated this on the sidelines of the inauguration of a 192-bed hostel at the College of Medicine, University of Ibadan, on Saturday, said the government was targeting the enrolment of 20,000 students annually.

The minister said the increase in enrolment was part of efforts to address manpower shortages in the health sector amid the migration of Nigerian medical professionals abroad.

He said that since President Bola Tinubu assumed office, the government had increased annual nursing enrolment from about 28,000 to more than 130,000.

According to him, the country is making progress in producing more healthcare professionals.

Alausa, who represented Tinubu at the inauguration, said the administration was investing in infrastructure to expand the capacity of medical schools and other tertiary institutions to accommodate more students.

According to him, annual admission into medical schools has risen to about 12,000, from 5,000 students recorded before the administration began in May 2023.

“We decided that in four years, we will increase the number to 20,000 annually.

“Three years into it, we are enrolling about 12,000 medical students now across all our medical schools in the country, and by the end of 2028, we will meet our target of enrolling over 20,000 medical students,” he said.

Alausa said the government had also increased admission into dentistry, pharmacy, physiotherapy and other allied health programmes to strengthen the country’s healthcare workforce.

He said the expansion was being complemented by investments in infrastructure, including hostels, to support increased enrolment and improve the learning environment.

The minister added that the government was also investing in the education sector through the Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative.

“This include the construction and rehabilitation of schools, expansion of medical schools and re-equipping of engineering workshops,” the minister said.

Alausa said the administration had invested nearly N500bn in educational infrastructure, adding that the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) had also expanded access to tertiary education for students irrespective of their economic backgrounds.

He urged journalists to verify the figures on nursing and medical student enrolment through the relevant regulatory bodies, including the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria.

content:
Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky on Saturday reiterated his country’s determination to join NATO, following proposals to provide Kyiv with security guarantees similar to those of the military alliance.

“Of course Ukraine very much wants to be in NATO,” Zelensky told reporters, judging that membership of the alliance was one of the “most obvious security guarantees” for his country.

The issue of Ukraine joining NATO, ruled out by Washington since 2025, resurfaced in recent days during fresh talks to end the war nearly five years after Russia’s invasion.

At a meeting with Kyiv’s allies in Berlin on Thursday, US envoy Jared Kushner said Washington could be ready to grant Ukraine a security guarantee similar to that provided under Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty.

That clause – the cornerstone of NATO – states that an attack on one member is considered an attack on all allies.

On Friday, the French presidency said offering Kyiv “Article 5-type” protection would in practice amount to bringing Ukraine into the alliance.

The same day, two Russian missiles and a suspected drone landed in southeastern Poland, a NATO member bordering Ukraine.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte denounced violations of Polish airspace, calling them “clearly dangerous”.

title: Outrage as Defence Ministry publicises APC campaign rally
description:
By Ayobami Okerinde



The Ministry of Defence has come under criticism on social media after its official X account published details of preparations for the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in support of President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid.



In a post on Satur
content:
By Ayobami Okerinde

The Ministry of Defence has come under criticism on social media after its official X account published details of preparations for the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in support of President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid.

In a post on Saturday, it announced that the rally was scheduled to hold at Mapo Hall, Ibadan, Oyo State, on November 21, 2026, with Tinubu and key party officials expected to attend.

It also disclosed that the Minister of Defence, retired General Christopher Musa, had visited the venue on Friday night to assess security arrangements and other preparations ahead of the event.

“Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (Rtd), OFR, Friday night conducted an on-the-spot inspection of the venue as part of strategic preparations ahead of the upcoming presidential campaign rally in the state,” the post reads.

“During the visit, General Musa toured the premises and surrounding perimeters to evaluate security readiness, crowd management logistics, and overall infrastructural preparedness. President Bola Tinubu GCFR, and key party officials would be on ground for the rally.”

The post, which was accompanied by photographs of the minister’s inspection, was followed by criticism from several Nigerians, who questioned the use of an official government platform to publicise the activities of a political party.

One of the critics, Kunle Adebajo, described the development as “political psychosis so deep it’s ridiculous even by Nigerian standards”.

Another X user, N6, questioned the ministry’s apparent involvement in partisan activities, asking, “How is the Ministry of Defence handle clearly being Partisan. Have you lost it?”

Similarly, a user identified as Dollarain2000 said, “Is this really the official handle of Nigeria’s Defence Ministry? Or the Security Directorate of the APC Presidential Campaign Council?” the user asked.

Another critic, Emmanuel Doji, expressed concern over what he described as the blurring of boundaries between government responsibilities and involvement in partisan political activities.

He wrote, “So what exactly is the meaning of this? The official Twitter handle of the Ministry of Defence is now publishing a political party’s campaign schedule and updates on preparations for its rally? Where exactly do we draw the line between government business and party politics?

“A whole Ministry of Defence is now a publicity arm of the APC. Will it also publish the activities and campaign schedules of other political parties? This is completely inappropriate and should be condemned. Government institutions should not be turned into platforms for partisan political activities. This is not how things should be done.”

Another user, Benjamin, wrote, “Defence handle of the nation doing this! No, no, no, no! This is preposterous! This is no more Democracy!”

Josephu_o also criticised the development, he wrote, “Imagine the Ministry of Defence, an institution funded by Nigerian taxpayers and entrusted with the security of over 200 million citizens, using its official platform to publicise a political party’s re-election rally.

“Is this a Ministry of Defence or an APC campaign publicity office? State institutions belong to Nigerians, not political parties,” the user added.

Another user, HonShield, questioned whether the ministry would extend the same publicity to opposition parties, asking, “Dear Ministry of Defence, will you also do this for other political parties? Do you now belong to the APC to be tweeting for their campaign? What’s going on in this country for God’s sake?”

title: EPL: Anderson rescues Man City in 1-1 draw with Fulham
description:
Manchester City were held to a 1-1 draw by Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, extending their winless run in the Premier League to four matches.
Elliot Anderson scored in the second half to rescue a point for City after Rodrigo Muniz had given Fulham the lead in the first half.
The visitors t
content:
Manchester City were held to a 1-1 draw by Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, extending their winless run in the Premier League to four matches.

Elliot Anderson scored in the second half to rescue a point for City after Rodrigo Muniz had given Fulham the lead in the first half.

The visitors took the lead in the 16th minute when Muniz curled a right-footed effort into the top corner from inside the box following a pass from Oscar Bobb.

City thought they had equalised nine minutes later through Erling Haaland, who converted a rebound after Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno had saved his initial effort.

However, referee Thomas Bramall ruled out the goal for a foul on Leno, with the Video Assistant Referee confirming the decision after a review.

The decision frustrated Haaland, who protested against the call as City continued to search for an equaliser.

The hosts eventually drew level in the 57th minute when Anderson fired through a crowded penalty area to beat Leno, scoring his first Premier League goal since joining the club.

City pushed for a winner but Fulham held on to secure a point and leave the home supporters frustrated, with boos greeting the final whistle.

The result leaves City third in the Premier League table on 21 points, while Fulham remain 15th on 10 points.

City had entered the encounter after three consecutive league defeats, including losses to Nottingham Forest, Brighton and Aston Villa.

Fulham, meanwhile, extended their unbeaten run to five matches in all competitions, having drawn their previous league fixtures against Newcastle and Aston Villa.

The draw also ended City’s hopes of returning to winning ways after the international break.

title: Haaland in VAR controversy as Man City held by Fulham
description:
Erling Haaland was controversially denied a crucial goal as Manchester City’s spluttering Premier League title challenge suffered a fresh blow in a 1-1 draw against Fulham on Saturday.



Enzo Maresca’s side trailed to Rodrigo Muniz’s early opener at the Etihad Stadium before Haaland’s equaliser was
content:
Erling Haaland was controversially denied a crucial goal as Manchester City’s spluttering Premier League title challenge suffered a fresh blow in a 1-1 draw against Fulham on Saturday.

Enzo Maresca’s side trailed to Rodrigo Muniz’s early opener at the Etihad Stadium before Haaland’s equaliser was contentiously ruled out.

The City striker kicked the ball out of the grasp of Fulham keeper Bernd Leno on the goal-line.

But Leno barely had two hands on the ball when Haaland made contact, giving City reason to feel aggrieved with the decision.

Elliot Anderson saved City from a fourth successive league defeat as the England midfielder equalised in the second half with his first top-flight goal since signing from Nottingham Forest in the close-season.

But it was another frustrating afternoon for third-placed City, who could not find a winner and were booed off at full-time.

Leaders Arsenal can extend their lead over City to eight points if they win at Newcastle later on Saturday.

After making a blistering start to the season with seven successive league wins, City are winless in their last four top-flight matches.

It was the first time in 15 years and 21 games that City had failed to beat Fulham.

Still waiting to discover the result of their appeal against the guilty verdict over breaches of Premier League financial rules, City have looked increasingly distracted in recent weeks.

Maresca has claimed City are not bothered by the “noise” around the financial scandal, which is likely to include a huge points deduction if the appeal fails.

But his team’s lethargic performances of late suggest otherwise, with tricky tests against Napoli on Tuesday and Arsenal next weekend threatening to extend their slump.

– Slumping City –

City needed a fast start to ease their anxiety and Erling Haaland almost delivered it when his looping header was cleared off the line.

But Maresca has failed to fix the defensive problems that ailed City in their previous three games.

Fulham took full advantage of City’s flaws to snatch the lead with an incisive counter in the 16th minute.

Former City winger Oscar Bobb pounced on a wayward pass and accelerated down the right flank before picking out Muniz’s run into the penalty area.

With City’s defence in disarray, Muniz kept his composure to curl a fine finish into the top corner.

Maresca turned away in disgust and his frustration only increased when City were denied a leveller in the 26th minute.

Iliman Ndiaye’s cross reached Haaland inside the six-yard box but the Norway striker’s weak volley was saved by Leno.

Haaland’s momentum carried him into Leno and he kicked the ball over the line as the Fulham keeper struggled to get hold of it.

But Haaland’s celebrations were curtailed by VAR’s decision to disallow the goal for a foul on Leno.

Haaland squandered a golden opportunity to drag City level when he blazed wildly over from Phil Foden’s defence splitting pass.

Enduring one of his more profligate days, Haaland scuffed wastefully wide from Nico O’Reilly’s pass.

Out of sync for so long, City finally found some rhythm after the break and their pressure was rewarded in the 58th minute.

Fulham failed to clear a corner and Anderson pounced, drilling a fierce volley past Leno from the edge of the area.

Anderson was inches away from putting City ahead moments later with a low drive that fizzes just wide.

It was that kind of day for City, whose season is in danger of spiralling out of control before they even discover their appeal verdict.

title: One injured as fire guts Gombe residence
description:
One person has sustained injuries following a fire outbreak at a residence in the Federal Low-Cost area of Gombe State.
The Federal Fire Service, Gombe State Command, said the incident occurred in the early hours of Saturday along Savannah Clinic Street, adding that property worth about N3m was dest
content:
One person has sustained injuries following a fire outbreak at a residence in the Federal Low-Cost area of Gombe State.

The Federal Fire Service, Gombe State Command, said the incident occurred in the early hours of Saturday along Savannah Clinic Street, adding that property worth about N3m was destroyed.

In a statement issued on Saturday, the Command’s Public Relations Officer, ASF Muazu Musa, said the service received a distress call from the Gombe State Police Command’s Control Room at about 2:27am.

He said firefighters were immediately mobilised from the ATM Fire Station and arrived at the scene 11 minutes later.

“Upon arrival, the firefighters met an active fire outbreak at the residence. The crew immediately commenced firefighting operations and successfully extinguished the fire using one medium jet of water from the water tender, effectively preventing further spread and damage,” the statement said.

Musa disclosed that although one person sustained injuries and was receiving medical attention in hospital, no life was lost in the incident.

He added that preliminary assessment showed that property valued at approximately N3m was lost, while the timely intervention of the firefighters helped save property worth about N10m.

The statement further disclosed that the firefighting operation was led by DSF Mohammed Gambo, with FA Mustapha Abdullah serving as the driver of the service’s FFS 215 multipurpose water tender.

It said officers of the Nigeria Police Force, Gombe Division, led by Superintendent Inusa Jacob, were also at the scene to provide security and support during the operation.

According to the statement, the firefighters completed an inspection to ensure that the fire was completely extinguished and that there was no further threat before returning to their station at 3:54am.

The Command wished the injured victim a speedy recovery and reiterated its commitment to protecting lives and property through prompt emergency response and public fire safety awareness.

It urged residents to remain vigilant, observe basic fire safety measures and report fire incidents promptly to minimise casualties and property losses.

title: 2027: Tinubu takes swipe at Makinde, urges Oyo voters to choose APC
description:
By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja



President Bola Tinubu has told the people of Oyo State not to mind Governor Seyi Makinde, the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), and urged them to vote for the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) from top to bottom.



The president spoke on Sat
content:
By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has told the people of Oyo State not to mind Governor Seyi Makinde, the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), and urged them to vote for the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) from top to bottom.

The president spoke on Saturday at the APC presidential rally in Ibadan, the Oyo state capital.

Apparently referring to the governor, the president said, “There is a party out there parading themselves. Please don’t mind them and don’t listen to them. They are only interested in clearing what you have. Vote for APC from top to bottom.”

Tinubu said he would not speak at length. “I will not be able to speak much to you. I just want to greet you. This is our party. It is your party. Is that clear?

“You voted overwhelmingly for the APC last time. You must stay the course for the sake of progress, the prosperity of our country and the development of your children and great-grandchildren,” he said.

Before addressing the rally, the president asked the gathering to observe a minute of silence for the victims of the boat accident in Bayelsa State. “Our condolences go to the people of Bayelsa State and the bereaved families. May God grant the people of Bayelsa peace and happiness and prevent a recurrence of such an incident. We will support them,” he said.

Tinubu also announced an investment for Oyo State. “For your state, we have just signed an agreement with China’s Yutong to reopen the old Leyland factory in Ibadan. We are reopening it to produce public transport vehicles and establish an automobile assembly plant there. We will continue to bring industries. You will see progress and development,” he added.

Speaking on behalf of the APC governors, the governor of Ekiti State, Mr Biodun Oyebanji, urged the Yoruba to turn out for the President.

“We are appealing to the Yoruba people, particularly our sons and daughters, to come out and support the presidential candidate, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. On January 16, let us all come out and vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Senator Sarafadeen Ali of the APC. When the time comes, we will also support our candidates contesting for the Senate, House of Representatives and State House of Assembly.

“I appeal to the Yoruba people not to allow this opportunity to slip away. Let us stand together and ensure that our party succeeds in Nigeria,” Oyebanji said.

title: Movie producers plan Nollywood confab in Abuja
description:
From Fred Itua, Abuja
The Association of Movie Producers (AMP), Federal Capital Territory Chapter, has announced plans to host the Nollywood Film Conference and Awards, a national gathering aimed at exploring the strategic role of Nigeria’s film industry in promoting national security, peacebuilding
content:
From Fred Itua, Abuja

The Association of Movie Producers (AMP), Federal Capital Territory Chapter, has announced plans to host the Nollywood Film Conference and Awards, a national gathering aimed at exploring the strategic role of Nigeria’s film industry in promoting national security, peacebuilding, social cohesion and sustainable development.

The conference, scheduled for November 27, 2026 in Abuja, will be held under the theme, “Film for National Security and Sustainable Development,” with the sub-theme, “Harnessing Nollywood’s Creative Power for Peace, National Re-orientation and Sustainable Development.”

The Chairman of the Association of Movie Producers, FCT Chapter, Desmond Utomwen, made this known during an interview with journalists in Abuja, explaining that the conference would bring together filmmakers, government officials, security agencies, development organisations, investors, broadcasters and other stakeholders to explore opportunities for deploying cinema as an instrument of national transformation.

Utomwen said the initiative was informed by the growing recognition of film as a powerful medium for public enlightenment, behavioural change, social mobilisation and the promotion of responsible citizenship.

He observed that Nigeria’s security challenges require multidimensional approaches extending beyond conventional security operations to include strategic communication, youth empowerment, civic education, community engagement and national re-orientation.

According to him, Nollywood possesses enormous potential to complement these efforts through compelling storytelling that challenges harmful social practices, promotes tolerance and encourages peaceful coexistence.

“Every film carries the possibility of influencing how people see themselves, their neighbours and their country. Our responsibility as filmmakers is to recognise that influence and apply it with creativity, integrity and care. With this conference, we want to move the conversation towards practical partnerships. We want to examine how compelling Nigerian stories can support peace, strengthen public understanding, create livelihoods and help communities confront the pressures that threaten their security and wellbeing.” Utomwen stated.

He identified violent extremism, human trafficking, irregular migration, gender-based violence, drug abuse and youth involvement in criminal activities as critical issues that could be addressed through purposeful filmmaking.

Utomwen noted that cinema could also deepen public understanding of the experiences of security personnel, survivors of violence, internally displaced persons and communities affected by insecurity. The AMP-FCT Chairman further emphasised the relationship between national security and sustainable development, noting that a vibrant film industry could generate employment, stimulate entrepreneurship and contribute significantly to economic diversification.

He explained that Nollywood’s value chain provides opportunities across acting, directing, cinematography, screenwriting, animation, editing, sound engineering, costume design, logistics, hospitality and other production-related services.

According to him, the conference would examine film financing, production infrastructure, professional standards, technical capacity development, distribution, emerging technologies and institutional partnerships necessary to strengthen the industry’s contribution to national development.

Utomwen disclosed that the awards component would recognise outstanding contributions to filmmaking, celebrate professional excellence and encourage creativity, innovation and socially responsible storytelling. He stressed that collaboration between filmmakers and public institutions must respect artistic independence, factual accuracy, human dignity and professional ethics.

The AMP-FCT Chairman consequently called on government institutions, security agencies, corporate organisations, development partners, investors and industry practitioners to support and participate in the conference.

“Nollywood must be recognised beyond entertainment as a strategic contributor to national development, cultural diplomacy, economic empowerment and social transformation.

“Film can help a nation understand its challenges, imagine solutions and mobilise the will to act. This conference seeks to turn that potential into purposeful collaboration and lasting opportunities for Nigerians,” Utomwen declared.

The post Movie producers plan Nollywood confab in Abuja appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Diallo present as African football boss Motsepe reiterates support for Infantino
description:
African football supremo Patrice Motsepe said Saturday that all 54 members of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) support Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election as FIFA president.



Motsepe made the declaration in Abuja, where CAF is holding its ordinary general assembly and at which one of
content:
African football supremo Patrice Motsepe said Saturday that all 54 members of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) support Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election as FIFA president.

Motsepe made the declaration in Abuja, where CAF is holding its ordinary general assembly and at which one of Infantino’s two rivals, French football chief Philippe Diallo is present.

Former Japan Football Association president Kozo Tashima is the other candidate.

The trio will learn whether they have been successful on March 18 next year in Rabat — the winning candidate must obtain a majority of the 211 associations.

CAF’s support for Infantino comes hours after another of his steadfast supporters South American football’s governing body CONMEBOL gave him their “unanimous” backing.

CAF has been consistently behind Infantino — who is seeking a fourth and final term — even after the furore he stirred up in July with his shortlived FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Morocco is co-hosting the 2030 World Cup.

“Gianni, you have our support on behalf of the 54 nations in Africa to be our candidate,” Motsepe said.

“I have a report from all 54 member associations in Africa to say that we are unanimously supporting Gianni.”

Infantino has faced multiple calls to step down and lost the backing of European football’s governing body UEFA, whilst CONCACAF has also been strident in its criticism of the 56-year-old Swiss lawyer.

Motsepe though has been a vocal supporter and Infantino said such loyalty was reciprocal.

“You will always find, in me and in FIFA, a trusted partner,” Infantino told the assembly, announcing cash inflow of $25 million to each member of CAF, starting January 2027 for development projects.

On Wednesday, UEFA vice-president Laura McAllister told AFP that Diallo, a 63-year-old lawyer whose Senegalese-born father boxed for France at the 1960 Olympics in Rome, should not be seen as solely a European candidate.

“He is a francophone, which is an important asset in lots of CAF countries,” she said.

McAllister, who in 2023 became the first woman to be elected a vice-president of UEFA, noted though that confederations do not vote as a bloc.

“There is a soft space which Philippe can exploit and convince some federations within each confederation to support a reform agenda,” the 61-year-old said.

“There is a lot of discomfort around the behaviour of Gianni Infantino and a desire to challenge the concentration of power in his hands.

“This applies everywhere in world football. This is not about Europe, the same rules apply globally.”

title: I rejected deal that could have earned me three private jets – Frank Edwards
description:
Gospel singer Frank Edwards has revealed that he rejected an offer to remove the name of Jesus from his songs in exchange for international music distribution, saying accepting the deal could have earned him about three private jets.
Edwards said the offer came shortly after he travelled to South Af
content:
Gospel singer Frank Edwards has revealed that he rejected an offer to remove the name of Jesus from his songs in exchange for international music distribution, saying accepting the deal could have earned him about three private jets.

Edwards said the offer came shortly after he travelled to South Africa to shoot the music video for his song, ‘Beautiful’, at the early stage of his music career.

He disclosed this during a ministration at a concert, a video of which went viral on social media on Saturday where he recounted how some people offered to connect his music to a global audience on the condition that he replaced references to Jesus with God.

“I have also seen temptations that, if I had followed through, I probably would have had about three private jets by now.

“I’ve met people, I’ve seen people. Sir, I have been tempted. I have travelled, I have been tempted, and I’ve seen opportunities. These opportunities don’t look like you want to do evil. That’s why you have to be very careful,” he said.

The singer explained that the promoters argued that mentioning Jesus could offend some people and limit the reach of his music, while replacing the name with God would make his songs acceptable to a wider audience.

He recalled that they told him, “We can only distribute your music to a global audience if you remove Jesus and replace it with God because the name Jesus will offend many people. So, if you want to reach many people, you need to remove it and put God. It still means the same thing.”

Edwards said he initially struggled with the decision because he considered Jesus and God to be closely connected in the Christian faith, adding that the financial prospects attached to the offer were overwhelming.

He said he eventually became confused and decided to seek his mother’s advice.

According to him, his mother immediately rejected the proposal and instructed him to run away from the people making the offer.

“At some point, I really got confused because the offer was something else. Then, I called my mum.

“She didn’t even allow me to finish. My mum said, ‘We’ll go to school.’ When my mum calls you by your native name, just know that there’s a problem,” he recounted.

The singer said his mother, who was not physically with him in South Africa, instructed him to remove his slippers and run, a directive he obeyed.

He said the decision to heed her warning saved him from compromising his faith.

Edwards added that he later believed God promised to give him ten times what the promoters had offered if he refused to compromise.

“But when I did that, God said to me, ‘Because you did not fall for this temptation, whatever these people promised you, I’ll give you times ten of it,’” he said.

He further narrated how he eventually met a music personality who told him that he had all his songs on his phone and wanted to work with him.

According to Edwards, the encounter happened without him making any prior effort to contact the man.

“I met the man, and it was the man himself who told me, ‘Hey, I have all your songs on my phone.’ He said to me, ‘Anytime I see you, we have to do something together.’

“I said, ‘Eh? Me?’ And that was the beginning of it all,” he said.

The singer did not identify the promoters who made the initial offer during the ministration.

He also reflected on an earlier teaching from 2007, saying he had been told that a generation of gospel music ministers would emerge with an unconventional approach to music and face opposition but remain unstoppable.

“I said that a time is coming, you know, and by that time, I had released many albums. But God told me that a generation was coming that would be rugged, that would not understand religion. They were going to be crazy with their music. People would try to stop them, but they would be unstoppable,” he said.

content:
Gospel singer Frank Edwards has said he could have had about three private jets by now if he had given in to certain temptations he encountered during the early stages of his music career.

The gospel singer disclosed this during a ministration at a concert, where he recounted how some people offered to help distribute his music to a global audience on the condition that he replaced the name of Jesus with God in his songs.

He said the offer came shortly after he travelled to South Africa to shoot the music video for his song, Beautiful, but he rejected it after seeking his mother’s advice.

He disclosed this during a ministration at a concert, a video of which went viral on social media on Saturday where he recounted how some people offered to connect his music to a global audience on the condition that he replaced references to Jesus with God.

“I have also seen temptations that, if I had followed through, I probably would have had about three private jets by now.

“I’ve met people, I’ve seen people. Sir, I have been tempted. I have travelled, I have been tempted, and I’ve seen opportunities. These opportunities don’t look like you want to do evil. That’s why you have to be very careful,” he said.

The singer explained that the promoters argued that mentioning Jesus could offend some people and limit the reach of his music, while replacing the name with God would make his songs acceptable to a wider audience.

He recalled that they told him, “We can only distribute your music to a global audience if you remove Jesus and replace it with God because the name Jesus will offend many people. So, if you want to reach many people, you need to remove it and put God. It still means the same thing.”

Edwards said he initially struggled with the decision because he considered Jesus and God to be closely connected in the Christian faith, adding that the financial prospects attached to the offer were overwhelming.

He said he eventually became confused and decided to seek his mother’s advice.

According to him, his mother immediately rejected the proposal and instructed him to run away from the people making the offer.

“At some point, I really got confused because the offer was something else. Then, I called my mum.

“She didn’t even allow me to finish. My mum said, ‘We’ll go to school.’ When my mum calls you by your native name, just know that there’s a problem,” he recounted.

The singer said his mother, who was not physically with him in South Africa, instructed him to remove his slippers and run, a directive he obeyed.

He said the decision to heed her warning saved him from compromising his faith.

Edwards added that he later believed God promised to give him ten times what the promoters had offered if he refused to compromise.

“But when I did that, God said to me, ‘Because you did not fall for this temptation, whatever these people promised you, I’ll give you times ten of it,’” he said.

He further narrated how he eventually met a music personality who told him that he had all his songs on his phone and wanted to work with him.

According to Edwards, the encounter happened without him making any prior effort to contact the man.

“I met the man, and it was the man himself who told me, ‘Hey, I have all your songs on my phone.’ He said to me, ‘Anytime I see you, we have to do something together.’

“I said, ‘Eh? Me?’ And that was the beginning of it all,” he said.

The singer did not identify the promoters who made the initial offer during the ministration.

He also reflected on an earlier teaching from 2007, saying he had been told that a generation of gospel music ministers would emerge with an unconventional approach to music and face opposition but remain unstoppable.

“I said that a time is coming, you know, and by that time, I had released many albums. But God told me that a generation was coming that would be rugged, that would not understand religion. They were going to be crazy with their music. People would try to stop them, but they would be unstoppable,” he said.

The post I could have had three private jets if I yielded to temptation – Frank Edwards appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Tinubu inaugurates UI medical hostel, promises 50,000 bed spaces in federal varsities
description:
President Bola Tinubu has pledged to deliver additional 50,000 bed space hostels across federal tertiary institutions by the end of 2027 to tackle accommodation challenges confronting students



Tinubu made the pledge on Saturday at the inauguration of Block E of the College of Medicine hostel, Uni
content:
President Bola Tinubu has pledged to deliver additional 50,000 bed space hostels across federal tertiary institutions by the end of 2027 to tackle accommodation challenges confronting students

Tinubu made the pledge on Saturday at the inauguration of Block E of the College of Medicine hostel, University of Ibadan (UI), located at Alexander Brown Hall, University College Hospital.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the hostel block was donated by the Chagoury family.

The President, represented by the Minister of Education, Dr Maruf Alausa, said that the 50,000 bed space hostels would be delivered through the ₦400 billion Student Hostels Programme, implemented via the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) and Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs).

He said the initiative was aimed at providing students with safe and decent accommodation to support their education.

“The accommodation shortage at the College of Medicine has become a critical challenge following the 2020 directive of the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN) requiring clinical students of medicine and dentistry to reside within the University College Hospital (UCH) premises for accreditation purposes.

“The college faced a shortfall of 490 bed spaces, representing 44.5 per cent of its accommodation requirement, leaving many students exposed to insecurity and difficulties attending essential clinical sessions,” the president said.

According to him, the shortage also prevented the college from fully utilising its annual admission quota for the Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) programme.

Tinubu said his administration was prioritising education funding and reforms through initiatives such as the Nigerian Education Sector Renewal Initiative, Nigeria Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), TETFund and the Student Venture Capital Grant.

He added that more than 36 universities had benefited from the Renewed Hope Energising Education Programme, with power installations ranging from 2.5 megawatts to 12 megawatts.

The President also said that the government had completed 20 compressed natural gas (CNG) conversion centres and maintenance facilities in some universities, with 40 additional facilities expected by the end of 2028.

Earlier, the Vice-Chancellor of UI, Prof. Peter Olapegba, said the inauguration of Block E marked another milestone in efforts to provide adequate accommodation for medical students and meet accreditation requirements.

Olapegba expressed appreciation to the benefactors, Ambassador Gilbert Ramez Chagoury and his brother, Ronald Chagoury, for their contribution to medical education.

“The hostel, named the Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu GCFR Block, provides accommodation for 192 medical and dental students in 48 rooms, with four students per room.

“The building also has four reading rooms, each measuring about 71 square metres, as well as rooms equipped with toilets, showers and kitchenettes,” Olapegba said.

The immediate past provost of the College of Medicine, Prof. Olayinka Omigbodun, said the hostel project was initiated to address the accommodation deficit that threatened the college’s ability to meet accreditation requirements.

Omigbodun, represented by Prof. Fatai Adeniyi, said the college required 1,101 bed spaces for clinical students but had only 611, resulting in a shortfall of about 500 beds.

She said the deficit had previously constrained the college’s ability to admit students up to its annual quota.

The Provost, College of Medicine, Prof. Temidayo Ogundiran, expressed appreciation to stakeholders and supporters who contributed to the realisation of the project.

According to him, the various contributions of the President Bola Tinubu-led administration had repositioned the education sector. (NAN)

The post Tinubu inaugurates UI medical hostel, promises 50,000 bed spaces in federal varsities appeared first on Vanguard News.
