title: Minister gifts 200 Ondo youths sewing machines
description:
The Minister of Youth Development, Ayodele Olawande, has distributed industrial sewing machines to 200 youths in Ondo State as part of a planned empowerment programme targeting 1,000 beneficiaries.
Olawande said the initiative was designed to support young people with practical skills and help them
content:
The Minister of Youth Development, Ayodele Olawande, has distributed industrial sewing machines to 200 youths in Ondo State as part of a planned empowerment programme targeting 1,000 beneficiaries.

Olawande said the initiative was designed to support young people with practical skills and help them create employment opportunities for themselves.

The minister distributed the machines in Akure, the state capital, on Friday, describing the gesture as part of his wedding gifts to youths in the state.

He got married on Saturday.

“We started with 200, and we are still going further. I’m getting married, and I believe I should do that with impact,” he said.

He explained that the initiative was informed by the needs of fashion designers who require industrial sewing machines to run their businesses.

“I realised that many fashion designers need industrial sewing machines. So, within Akure metropolis and extending to other parts of Ondo State, we decided to embark on this initiative,” he said.

Olawande said the programme would be extended to other local government areas, including Ifedore, Ese-Odo and Owo, as the ministry works towards reaching its target of 1,000 beneficiaries.

“We intend to meet the target of 1,000 beneficiaries. We will also extend the initiative to people in other occupations, including bricklayers. I really want to target people who work with their hands,” he added.

The minister said the programme reflected his belief in skills acquisition and the need to support people with practical abilities.

He also linked the initiative to the Federal Government’s Renewed Hope Agenda, saying employment should not be limited to white-collar jobs.

“The President and all of us are preaching the same message, not every job has to be a white-collar job,” he said.

Olawande cited his experience learning photography as an example of how vocational skills could create opportunities, recalling that President Bola Tinubu had given him the opportunity to acquire the skill.

“For instance, if President Bola Ahmed Tinubu had not given me the opportunity to learn photography, I might not have become a photographer today,” he said.

One of the beneficiaries, Ayoluwa, thanked the minister, saying the sewing machine came at a time when her previous equipment had developed a fault.

“This is a very big testimony for me. Just last week, my sewing machine developed a fault that appeared almost impossible to repair. I was already considering buying a fairly used machine, but someone advised me against it,” she said.

Ayoluwa said she was surprised when a friend asked her to check her phone and she discovered that her name and address were on the list of beneficiaries.

“This means a lot to me because it has saved me from a lot of stress and financial challenges. I also want to thank the honourable minister,” she added.

The post Minister gifts 200 Ondo youths sewing machines appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Gen Ihejirika, others endorse Otti for 2nd term
description:
Former Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Azubuike Ihejirika (rtd), and other influential persons from Abia, under the aegis of the Alliance for Good Governance (AGG), have endorsed the re-election of Governor Alex Otti and have began mobilisation for this purpose.
The personalities drawn from
content:
Former Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Azubuike Ihejirika (rtd), and other influential persons from Abia, under the aegis of the Alliance for Good Governance (AGG), have endorsed the re-election of Governor Alex Otti and have began mobilisation for this purpose.

The personalities drawn from different political parties, made this known during a meeting held at the residence of Ken Ahia, SAN, in Umuasua, Isuikwuato Local Government Area.

The stakeholders resolved to work collectively to sustain the current administration’s development strides in Abia State.

Speaking, Lt General Ihejirika, said the stakeholders had put aside political affiliations to rally behind Governor Otti, whom he described as a leader whose performance had surpassed their expectations.

Ihejirika was of the view that the governor’s achievements in less than four years had provided sufficient motivation for their support, adding that their decision was based on performance rather than political sentiments.

“We understand that we are here irrespective of party affiliation to support our Governor, whose performance has exceeded our expectations.

“His performance has far exceeded our expectations of what a good governor could do in four years’ time. That is the motivating factor to support a leader who is doing well, no sentiments about it. We stand by him, morning, afternoon and night.” said Lt. Gen. Ihejirika.

The host, Ahia, SAN, said the meeting was convened to ensure that Abia remained united in support of Governor Otti, noting that the governor needed the cooperation of elected representatives and other political stakeholders to fully realise his vision for the state.

In a communique issued at the end of the meeting and read by the spokesman of AGG and former Secretary to the Abia State Government, Professor Mkpa Agu Mkpa, the stakeholders said they had resolved to work within the ambit of the law to ensure Governor Otti’s return in 2027 and sustain the gains of the present administration.

“As the general elections are around the corner, less than two months away, the Alliance for Good Governance considered it necessary to take a position on the future of Abia State”.

Prof Mkpa said as senior citizens and influential members of the state, the stakeholders would not want to witness a reversal of the progress made by the Otti administration.

“Even though we are apolitical, then we have sympathy for good governance. In our list, there are APC members, PDP members, AD members, these are people who want the perpetration of good governance in Abia State, and that good governance has been epitomised by Governor Alex Otti,” Prof. Mkpa said.

title: Hamzat seeks stronger public-private partnership to drive Lagos digital economy
description:
Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, has called for stronger collaboration among government, research institutions and the private sector to transform innovations into commercial products, create jobs and accelerate the state’s digital economy.
Hamzat said Lagos must move beyond fragmente
content:
Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, has called for stronger collaboration among government, research institutions and the private sector to transform innovations into commercial products, create jobs and accelerate the state’s digital economy.

Hamzat said Lagos must move beyond fragmented, government-funded research initiatives to build an integrated innovation ecosystem that connects research, funding, technology, industries and commercialisation.

He spoke at a private fintech town hall convened by MyCard Global in collaboration with the Fintech Association of Nigeria in Lagos.

The meeting, themed, “The Lagos Digital Economy Blueprint: Co-Authoring the Lagos Digital Economy Agenda,” brought together government officials, fintech executives, technology companies, investors and other stakeholders to explore ways of shaping the state’s digital economic future.

The deputy governor, a former Commissioner for Science and Technology, said the state had continued to support science-based research by providing platforms for young innovators to present their ideas for possible funding.

However, he stressed the need to strengthen the process of translating research outcomes into marketable products and services that could contribute meaningfully to economic growth.

According to him, building a sustainable innovation ecosystem requires deliberate collaboration among researchers, entrepreneurs, investors, government agencies and established industries.

Hamzat also identified reliable data as critical to effective governance, saying government must have accurate information about residents’ needs to ensure that policies, infrastructure and public investments deliver the desired results.

He said Lagos was working towards replacing disconnected programmes and individual initiatives with an integrated, data-driven governance system capable of supporting planning, research, innovation and economic development.

On digital infrastructure, Hamzat disclosed that the state was targeting an expansion of its fibre-optic network from the existing 2,400 kilometres to about 6,000 kilometres through partnerships with telecommunications companies and other private-sector players.

He said the expansion would improve connectivity across schools, public institutions and other facilities, enhance access to digital services and reduce the cost of doing business.

The deputy governor added that the government was connecting educational institutions and upgrading infrastructure to improve internet access, with the ultimate objective of ensuring that all public schools in the state were connected.

He further disclosed that the state was strengthening data governance and standardisation by developing common templates and operational standards for ministries, departments and agencies to facilitate seamless data exchange.

According to him, the proposed framework would enable government agencies to share information, improve institutional coordination and make decisions based on accurate and reliable data.

Hamzat urged fintech operators, technology companies, researchers and entrepreneurs to work with the government to identify challenges, develop innovative solutions and create opportunities for young people.

He described private-sector participation as indispensable to building a sustainable innovation ecosystem, adding that the government remained committed to supporting initiatives that would expand businesses, generate employment and strengthen Lagos’ position as a leading digital economy.

Speaking on the objective of the town hall, MyCard Global Executive Director, Aderemi Fagbemi, said the meeting was designed to deepen collaboration between government and private-sector players in shaping the state’s digital economy agenda.

She listed Flutterwave, Paystack, PiggyVest, Kuda, PalmPay, Mastercard, Visa, Oracle, Interswitch, OPay, Moniepoint, Paga and Meristem among the organisations represented at the meeting.

Fagbemi said the participating organisations were not merely building businesses but were also shaping the future of technology, payments, financial services and digital innovation.

She explained that the town hall provided an opportunity to bridge the gap between government policy and private-sector innovation while giving industry stakeholders a platform to contribute to the state’s digital development priorities.

Also speaking during a panel session, Flutterwave co-founder, Gbenga Agboola, called for predictable government policies and a stable regulatory environment to encourage business growth and attract investment.

Agboola said businesses required consistent regulations that would enable them to plan, invest and operate with confidence, warning that frequent policy changes could create uncertainty and undermine investor confidence.

He also advocated better coordination among regulatory agencies, particularly in licensing processes.

According to him, approvals obtained from one regulatory agency should facilitate the necessary processes with other relevant authorities, rather than subjecting businesses to repetitive and potentially cumbersome procedures.

The post Hamzat seeks stronger public-private partnership to drive Lagos digital economy appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

content:
…forces 26 terrorists, family members to surrender

The Armed Forces of Nigeria (AFN) have intensified offensives against terrorist networks, killing 21 ISWAP fighters, including senior commanders, and recording the surrender of 26 fighters and their family members in the Northeast.

The Director, Defence Media Operations, Maj.-Gen. Michael Onoja, disclosed this in a statement on ongoing military operations covering Nov. 13 to Nov. 19.

Onoja said precision air strikes conducted between Monday and Tuesday around Monguno and Arinna in the South Lake Chad area of Borno neutralised 21 ISWAP fighters and severely injured 10 others.

He said the first strike killed seven terrorists, including members of the group’s Improvised Explosive Device (IED) network, and incapacitated a key IED expert.

According to him, the second engagement at Arinna neutralised a member of ISWAP’s Shura Council, who served as its Provost Commander, a Qaid of Sabon Tumbu and 12 other fighters.

The director said the sustained military pressure also prompted 26 terrorists and their family members, comprising eight fighters and 18 family members, to surrender between Nov. 13 and Nov. 18.

He said the surrender took place in Bama, Dikwa, Gwoza, Kukawa and Monguno Local Government Areas of Borno.

Among those who surrendered were 12 women and children who fled Bula Daloye on Nov. 13, as well as a terrorist who surrendered along Gwoza-Pulka Road on Nov. 14.

“The latter reportedly handed over an AK-47 rifle, five magazines, 34 rounds of ammunition and two hand grenades,” he said.

Onoja said the surrendering terrorists cited intense military operations and internal clashes between rival factions as reasons for abandoning the group.

He added that troops also rescued four internally displaced persons who escaped from terrorist captivity at Zaha Village in the Mandara Mountains, Gwoza LGA, on Tuesday.

Onoja further disclosed that troops arrested suspected terrorist collaborators and logistics suppliers in Borno, Yobe and Kano, including individuals allegedly conveying combat materials and supplies to terrorist enclaves.

In the Northwest, he said the troops of Operation Fansan Yamma rescued three kidnapped victims along Anka-Gada Mayya Road in Zamfara on Nov. 12 and captured a vehicle belonging to the terrorists.

According to him, troops also neutralised one terrorist during an engagement at Aguba Village in Kajuru LGA of Kaduna on Nov. 14, recovering two fabricated rifles and a mobile phone.

Onoja said troops arrested a principal suspect in Ribah, whose confession reportedly led to the arrest of three other persons linked to an illegal supply network serving bandits along the Bena axis.

“In the North-Central, troops of Operation Enduring Peace recovered a PKT machine gun, three AK-47 rifles and three magazines surrendered by fleeing terrorists following sustained offensives around Odare Forest in Kanam LGA of Plateau.

“Troops of Operation Whirl Stroke also arrested suspected arms and logistics couriers in Taraba and Kogi, including individuals allegedly transporting weapons across the River Benue and River Niger corridors.

“In Niger State, troops arrested two suspected kidnappers at Warari Village in Rijau LGA while attempting to collect a N3.5 million ransom from a resident,” he said.

The director said troops of Operation Savannah Shield also recovered 12 rifles and rescued 10 kidnapped persons during the initial stage of negotiations with three prominent bandit leaders operating around Gbugbu Forest in Edu LGA of Kwara.

He added that four additional kidnapped victims were released to troops on Nov. 18 following further engagements.

He said troops subsequently intercepted four suspected terrorist logistics suppliers at Kanikoko in Kaiama Local Government Area.

According to him, troops recovered detonating cords, cartons of blasting explosives and fuses allegedly being conveyed to Sabon Fegi in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger.

Onoja said troops, in another operation at Kara’a Village in Mariga LGA of Niger on Tuesday, neutralised three terrorists and rescued three farmers abducted from Warari town.

He said troops of Operation Udo Ka discovered three command-detonated improvised explosive devices at an IPOB/ESN camp in Amankwu Village, Arochukwu LGA of Abia, alongside solar panels, a Biafran flag and other items.

“Troops also neutralised two suspected IPOB/ESN fighters during operations around Njaba in Mbaitoli LGA of Imo, recovering an AK-47 rifle, more than 110 rounds of ammunition and other items.

“In the South-South, troops of Operation Delta Safe uncovered seven illegal bunkering camps around Ndoni in Ogba/Egbema/Ndoni LGA of Rivers, with about 85,000 litres of stolen crude oil.

“They also discovered an illegal refining site at Apani Community in Ikwerre LGA, containing an estimated 2,100 litres of illegally refined products,” he added.

Onoja said troops, working with the police and local security groups, also arrested two suspected kidnappers at Iguelaba Community along the Delta-Edo boundary.

He said the Chief of Defence Staff, Gen. Olufemi Oluyede, commended troops and the Air Component for their resilience and sacrifices.

title: NAFDAC Set To Destroy N100bn Worth Of Fake, Banned Products In Ogun
description: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) said it will destroy fake and unregistered goods worth N100 billion uncovered at Ogwama Dumpsite, Ogere, Remo in Ogun State.A speech by the Agency’s Director-General, Prof. Christiana Adeyeye, at the destruction flag-off
content:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) said it will destroy fake and unregistered goods worth N100 billion uncovered at Ogwama Dumpsite, Ogere, Remo in Ogun State.

A speech by the Agency’s Director-General, Prof. Christiana Adeyeye, at the destruction flag-off of the products on Friday noted that the initiative is crucial to preventing the reintroduction of expired, fake, substandard, and falsified drugs into circulation.

“As the lead agency and chair of the Federal Task Force on Fake and Counterfeit Drugs and Unwholesome Processed Foods, NAFDAC is resolutely committed to ensuring that food, drugs, cosmetics, medical devices, chemicals, packaged water, and drinks are safe, wholesome, and effective for human consumption.

“There is no question that drugs are a critical aspect of NAFDAC’s mandate, and we have established strict guidelines governing the licensing, sale, and distribution of drug products.”

The products slated for destruction include expired, counterfeit, controlled, unregistered, and banned drugs, such as banned alcoholic beverages in sachets and PET bottles below 200ml, banned Analgin injection, expired Codeine cough syrups, Oxytocin injection, various types of counterfeit cosmetics and unwholesome food products.

“The estimated street value of these products being destroyed today stands at one hundred billion naira only.

“In some of our recent enforcement activities, operatives uncovered nefarious activities in a warehouse in Lagos meant for tools and hardware: illegally manufactured cosmetic products at the penthouse of the building, as well as several cartons of Augmentin and Ampicillin packets, leaflets, and other unregistered cosmetics.

“The Investigation and Enforcement officers uncovered a hub where fake, counterfeit popular brands of alcoholic beverages were being produced, and expired energy drinks were revalidated and stored.

“Officers promptly arrested the suspects, who will face the full wrath of the law. Also, in Lagos and Ogun states, officers coordinated the mop-up of over one hundred thousand cartons (100,000)of banned sachet and PET bottle alcoholic beverages from manufacturers, wholesalers and retailers.”

NAFDAC officers also uncovered a residential building used for manufacturing, producing, and selling large volumes of unauthorised and unregistered herbal mixtures to Nigerians.

Other products marked for destruction today include products mopped up from circulation during raids and expired products voluntarily handed over by compliant companies. The destruction of these products will undoubtedly eliminate the risk of their entry into the Nigerian Market.

“I want to sincerely and openly appreciate the collaboration with the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS). They handed over pharmaceutical products, including several cartons of Codeine cough syrup, CSC Cough syrup with codeine, which are being destroyed today.

She appreciated the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigerian Army, Department of State Services (DSS), Pharmacists Council of Nigeria (PCN), National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA), Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) and all stakeholders who united to achieve the feat.

“To community leaders, religious leaders, health practitioners, members of the press, and all Nigerians: it is imperative that you educate your families and wards about the dangers of patronizing quacks and unauthorized vendors.”

The Agency called on the public to actively participate in this fight against counterfeiting.

“We seek your continued cooperation in providing valuable information to help us prevent and ultimately eradicate unregistered, dangerous, and other violative products from our society. Together, we can protect the health and safety of all Nigerians.”

The post NAFDAC Set To Destroy N100bn Worth Of Fake, Banned Products In Ogun appeared first on Channels Television.

The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has destroyed fake, banned, expired, substandard and falsified products worth an estimated ₦100 billion in Ogun State.

The destruction exercise was carried out on Friday, 20 November 2026, at Ogwama Dumpsite, Ogere Remo, as part of the agency’s efforts to prevent unsafe and unregistered products from re-entering circulation.

Speaking at the flag-off of the exercise, NAFDAC’s Director-General, Mojisola Adeyeye, said the products included banned and unregistered medicines, alcoholic beverages in sachets and PET bottles below 200ml, banned Analgin injections, expired Codeine cough syrups, Oxytocin injections, counterfeit cosmetics and unwholesome food products.

She said the destruction was necessary to eliminate the risk of the products finding their way back into the Nigerian market.

“As the lead agency and chair of the Federal Task Force on Fake and Counterfeit Drugs and Unwholesome Processed Foods, NAFDAC is resolutely committed to ensuring that food, drugs, cosmetics, medical devices, chemicals, packaged water and drinks are safe, wholesome and effective for human consumption,” she said.

Adeyeye explained that the products were recovered during enforcement operations across the country. They also included items voluntarily surrendered by compliant companies and pharmaceutical products handed over to the agency by the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS).

She disclosed that NAFDAC operatives recently uncovered illegally manufactured cosmetics and unregistered pharmaceutical products in a warehouse in Lagos.

According to her, the facility, which was meant for tools and hardware, had a penthouse where cosmetic products were being manufactured. Officers also recovered several cartons of Augmentin and Ampicillin packets, leaflets and other unregistered cosmetics.

The agency also uncovered a facility where counterfeit versions of popular alcoholic beverage brands were being produced, while expired energy drinks were allegedly being revalidated and stored for distribution.

Adeyeye said the suspects arrested during the operations would face the full wrath of the law.

She added that NAFDAC officers, working with relevant authorities, had coordinated the removal of more than 100,000 cartons of banned alcoholic beverages in sachets and PET bottles from manufacturers, wholesalers and retailers in Lagos and Ogun states.

The Director-General further disclosed that officers uncovered a residential building being used to manufacture and sell large quantities of unauthorised and unregistered herbal mixtures.

Adeyeye commended the Nigeria Customs Service for its collaboration, particularly the handover of pharmaceutical products, including cartons of Codeine-containing cough syrups, which were among the items destroyed.

She also acknowledged the contributions of the Nigeria Police Force, Nigerian Army, Department of State Services, Pharmacists Council of Nigeria, National Drug Law Enforcement Agency and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, as well as other stakeholders.

The NAFDAC chief urged community and religious leaders, health practitioners, the media and members of the public to educate their families and communities about the dangers of patronising unlicensed vendors and unauthorised drug sellers.

She called on Nigerians to support the agency’s enforcement efforts by providing credible information about the production, sale and distribution of fake, unregistered and other violative products.

“We seek your continued cooperation in providing valuable information to help us prevent and ultimately eradicate unregistered, dangerous and other violative products from our society. Together, we can protect the health and safety of all Nigerians,” she said.

The post NAFDAC Destroys ₦100bn Worth Of Fake Drugs, Banned Products In Ogun appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Mexico captures drug kingpin on FBI’s most wanted list
description:
Mexico’s military announced on Saturday that it had captured the leader of a drug-trafficking group who was among the 10 most-wanted fugitives sought by US law enforcement.



Fausto Isidro Meza, alias “Chapo Isidro,” and two other leaders of his drug gang were captured during a special forces raid
content:
Mexico’s military announced on Saturday that it had captured the leader of a drug-trafficking group who was among the 10 most-wanted fugitives sought by US law enforcement.

Fausto Isidro Meza, alias “Chapo Isidro,” and two other leaders of his drug gang were captured during a special forces raid Friday night in Sinaloa state, the Mexican National Defense Secretariat announced on X.

A firefight ensued between the military and gang members in the town of Guasave, sparking panic in the surrounding area, including at a professional baseball game, local media reported.

“Chapo Isidro” is the alleged leader of the Beltran Leyva gang, which is allied with one of two rival factions in the powerful Sinaloa cartel, Mexico’s military said.

He was captured alongside his number two in the group and another man identified as a financial operator.

They were all transported by a Mexican Air Force aircraft to Mexico City “to be placed at the disposal of the competent prosecutorial authorities,” the military said.

Chapo Isidro faces criminal charges in both Mexico and the United States.

The FBI had placed him on its list of 10 most wanted fugitives and offered a $5 million reward for information leading to his arrest.

Giving his name as Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, the FBI bulletin says his group is responsible for importing “large quantities of heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl, and marijuana into the United States.”

title: 2027: Tinubu, First Lady arrive Ibadan for APC presidential campaign rally
description:
President Bola Tinubu and the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, have arrived in Ibadan, the Oyo State capital, for the South-West leg of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign.
The President is in the city to lead the party’s 2027 re-election campaign rally scheduled to hold at
content:
President Bola Tinubu and the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, have arrived in Ibadan, the Oyo State capital, for the South-West leg of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign.

The President is in the city to lead the party’s 2027 re-election campaign rally scheduled to hold at the historic Mapo Hall.

Their arrival came hours after Tinubu directed that the rally be conducted without much fanfare in honour of victims of Friday’s boat accident in Ukubie, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.

The directive followed reports that several people lost their lives after a boat carrying mourners travelling to attend a funeral capsized in the community.

Tinubu had also expressed sadness over the tragedy and directed relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful rescue and recovery operation.

In a statement on Saturday, Tinubu said, “I have also directed that our Presidential Campaign Rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, this Saturday, November 21, 2026, be observed without much fanfare in honour of the lives lost and in sympathy with the relatives and families of those involved in the disaster.”

The rally is attended by Vice President Kashim Shettima, APC governors, and the leadership of the National Assembly, led by Senate President Godswill Akpabio and House Speaker Tajudeen Abbas.

The Ibadan event is the seventh stop of Tinubu’s re-election campaign since it began in Kaduna on October 24, 2026.

title: FG increases medical student admission to 12,000, targets 20,000 annually — Alausa
description:
The Federal Government has increased annual admission into medical schools from 5,000 to 12,000 students, the Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, has said.



Alausa, who stated this on the sidelines of the inauguration of a 192-bed hostel at the College of Medicine, University of Ibadan (UI),
content:
The Federal Government has increased annual admission into medical schools from 5,000 to 12,000 students, the Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, has said.

Alausa, who stated this on the sidelines of the inauguration of a 192-bed hostel at the College of Medicine, University of Ibadan (UI), on Saturday, said that it targets enrollment of 20,000 students annually.

The minister said the increase in enrollment was part of efforts to address manpower shortages in the health sector amid the migration of Nigerian medical professionals abroad.

He said that the government, since President Bola Tinubu assumed office, had increased nursing enrollment from about 28,000 annually to more than 130,000.

According to him, the country is making progress in producing more healthcare professionals.

Alausa, who represented Tinubu at the inauguration, said the administration was investing in infrastructure to expand the capacity of medical schools and other tertiary institutions to accommodate more students.

According to him, annual admission into medical schools has risen to about 12,000, from 5,000 students recorded before the administration began in May 2023.

“We decided that in four years, we will increase the number to 20,000 annually.

“Three years into it, we are enrolling about 12,000 medical students now across all our medical schools in the country, and by the end of 2028, we will meet our target of enrolling over 20,000 medical students,” he said.

Alausa said the government had also increased admission into dentistry, pharmacy, physiotherapy, and other allied health programs to strengthen the country’s healthcare workforce.

He said the expansion was being complemented by investments in infrastructure, including hostels, to support increased enrollment and improve the learning environment.

The minister added that the government was also investing in the education sector through the Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative.

“This includes the construction and rehabilitation of schools, expansion of medical schools, and re-equipping of engineering workshops,” the minister said.

Alausa said the administration had invested nearly N500 billion in educational infrastructure, adding that the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) had also expanded access to tertiary education for students irrespective of their economic backgrounds.

He urged journalists to verify the figures on nursing and medical student enrollment through the relevant regulatory bodies, including the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria. (NAN)

title: Nigeria, CAF endorse Infantino for re-election as FIFA president
description:
Nigeria and the Confederation of African Football (CAF) have endorsed FIFA President Gianni Infantino for another term ahead of next year’s election scheduled to take place in Rabat, Morocco.
The endorsement was announced during the CAF Extraordinary Assembly in Abuja, where the Chairman of the Nati
content:
Nigeria and the Confederation of African Football (CAF) have endorsed FIFA President Gianni Infantino for another term ahead of next year’s election scheduled to take place in Rabat, Morocco.

The endorsement was announced during the CAF Extraordinary Assembly in Abuja, where the Chairman of the National Sports Commission (NSC), Shehu Dikko, reaffirmed Nigeria’s support for Infantino on behalf of the Federal Government.

Dikko disclosed that President Bola Tinubu had directed Nigeria to back Infantino’s re-election bid, citing his contributions to the development of football across the world, particularly in Africa.

The endorsement signals Nigeria’s support for Infantino as he seeks to continue leading the world football governing body beyond his current tenure.

“I must make it clear here that on behalf of the Federal Government and in regard to the resolution of all members of CAF, Nigeria’s family endorses Mr Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for re-election into CAF,” Dikko said.

He urged African football associations to unite behind Infantino, describing the endorsement as being in the continent’s collective interest.

Dikko, a former Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) executive committee member and league chairman, also defended Infantino’s leadership, saying his decisions had benefited football.

Read Also: Warri Stadium: Infantino sees global football potential in Delta
“I must tell you, Gianni’s decisions are very, very good for football. They are very apt for football. His main job is to develop football and bring revenues to football. He tries to do that,” he said.

Related News
CAF President Patrice Motsepe also declared the continent’s support for Infantino, saying the 54 African member associations were backing him for another term.

Motsepe said his experience working with Infantino over the past five years had convinced him of the FIFA president’s commitment to football development.

“Gianni, you have our support among the 54 member associations of CAF,” Motsepe said.

In response, Infantino pledged to continue prioritising football development in Africa, describing FIFA as a dependable partner for the continent.

He said the organisation would continue working to ensure that the aspirations of young footballers across Africa could be realised.

Infantino also reiterated plans to increase FIFA’s financial grants to member associations from $8 million to $25 million over a four-year cycle, a move that would significantly expand funding available for football development worldwide.

The post Nigeria, CAF endorse Infantino for re-election as FIFA president appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Military kills 21 ISWAP fighters, eight terrorists surrender
description:
The Armed Forces of Nigeria have intensified offensives against terrorist networks, killing 21 ISWAP fighters, including senior commanders, while recording the surrender of 26 fighters and their family members in the North-East.
The Director of Defence Media Operations, Maj. Gen. Michael Onoja, disc
content:
The Armed Forces of Nigeria have intensified offensives against terrorist networks, killing 21 ISWAP fighters, including senior commanders, while recording the surrender of 26 fighters and their family members in the North-East.

The Director of Defence Media Operations, Maj. Gen. Michael Onoja, disclosed this in a Saturday statement on ongoing military operations covering November 13 to 19.

Onoja said precision air strikes conducted between Monday and Tuesday around Monguno and Arinna in the South Lake Chad area of Borno State neutralised 21 ISWAP fighters and severely injured 10 others.

He said the first strike killed seven terrorists, including members of the group’s Improvised Explosive Device (IED) network, and incapacitated a key IED expert.

According to him, the second engagement at Arinna neutralised a member of ISWAP’s Shura Council, who served as its Provost Commander, a Qaid of Sabon Tumbu and 12 other fighters.

The director said sustained military pressure also prompted 26 terrorists and their family members, comprising eight fighters and 18 family members, to surrender between November 13 and 18.

He said the surrender took place in Bama, Dikwa, Gwoza, Kukawa and Monguno Local Government Areas of Borno State.

Among those who surrendered were 12 women and children who fled Bula Daloye on November 13, as well as a terrorist who surrendered along Gwoza-Pulka Road on November 14.

“The latter reportedly handed over an AK-47 rifle, five magazines, 34 rounds of ammunition and two hand grenades,” he said.

Onoja said the surrendering terrorists cited intense military operations and internal clashes between rival factions as reasons for abandoning the group.

He added that troops also rescued four internally displaced persons who escaped from terrorist captivity at Zaha Village in the Mandara Mountains, Gwoza LGA, on Tuesday.

Onoja further disclosed that troops arrested suspected terrorist collaborators and logistics suppliers in Borno, Yobe and Kano states, including individuals allegedly conveying combat materials and supplies to terrorist enclaves.

In the North-West, he said troops of Operation Fansan Yamma rescued three kidnapped victims along Anka-Gada Mayya Road in Zamfara State on November 12 and captured a vehicle belonging to the terrorists.

According to him, troops also neutralised one terrorist during an engagement at Aguba Village in Kajuru LGA of Kaduna State on November 14, recovering two fabricated rifles and a mobile phone.

Onoja said troops arrested a principal suspect in Ribah, whose confession reportedly led to the arrest of three other persons linked to an illegal supply network serving bandits along the Bena axis.

“In the North-Central, troops of Operation Enduring Peace recovered a PKT machine gun, three AK-47 rifles and three magazines surrendered by fleeing terrorists following sustained offensives around Odare Forest in Kanam LGA of Plateau.

“Troops of Operation Whirl Stroke also arrested suspected arms and logistics couriers in Taraba and Kogi, including individuals allegedly transporting weapons across the River Benue and River Niger corridors.

“In Niger State, troops arrested two suspected kidnappers at Warari Village in Rijau LGA while attempting to collect a N3.5 million ransom from a resident,” he said.

The director said troops of Operation Savannah Shield also recovered 12 rifles and rescued 10 kidnapped persons during the initial stage of negotiations with three prominent bandit leaders operating around Gbugbu Forest in Edu LGA of Kwara State.

He added that four additional kidnapped victims were released to troops on November 18 following further engagements.

He said troops subsequently intercepted four suspected terrorist logistics suppliers at Kanikoko in Kaiama Local Government Area.

According to him, troops recovered detonating cords, cartons of blasting explosives and fuses allegedly being conveyed to Sabon Fegi in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State.

Onoja said troops, in another operation at Kara’a Village in Mariga LGA of Niger State on Tuesday, neutralised three terrorists and rescued three farmers abducted from Warari town.

He said troops of Operation Udo Ka discovered three command-detonated improvised explosive devices at an IPOB/ESN camp in Amankwu Village, Arochukwu LGA of Abia State, alongside solar panels, a Biafran flag and other items.

“Troops also neutralised two suspected IPOB/ESN fighters during operations around Njaba in Mbaitoli LGA of Imo, recovering an AK-47 rifle, more than 110 rounds of ammunition and other items.

“In the South-South, troops of Operation Delta Safe uncovered seven illegal bunkering camps around Ndoni in Ogba/Egbema/Ndoni LGA of Rivers State, with about 85,000 litres of stolen crude oil.

“They also discovered an illegal refining site at Apani Community in Ikwerre LGA, containing an estimated 2,100 litres of illegally refined products,” he added.

Onoja said troops, working with the police and local security groups, also arrested two suspected kidnappers at Iguelaba Community along the Delta-Edo boundary.

He said the Chief of Defence Staff, Gen. Olufemi Oluyede, commended troops and the Air Component for their resilience and sacrifices.

According to him, the CDS also appreciated other security partners and called on communities, traditional rulers and stakeholders to provide timely information, reject collaboration with criminal networks and encourage terrorists and bandits to surrender.

He urged the media to sustain balanced coverage without compromising ongoing military operations.

The post Military kills 21 ISWAP fighters, eight terrorists surrender appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: NRS seeks simpler tax rules to boost creative economy
description:
The Nigeria Revenue Service has called for simpler, clearer and business-friendly tax rules to attract investment and unlock the potential of Nigeria’s creative economy.
The Service said the emergence of digital business models, intellectual property-driven enterprises and cross-border transactions
content:
The Nigeria Revenue Service has called for simpler, clearer and business-friendly tax rules to attract investment and unlock the potential of Nigeria’s creative economy.

The Service said the emergence of digital business models, intellectual property-driven enterprises and cross-border transactions required a tax system that creators, entrepreneurs and investors could easily understand and navigate.

The Executive Chairman of the NRS, Dr Zacch Adedeji, made the call at a high-level dialogue on taxation and investment in the creative economy during the Creative Africa Nexus event in Lagos.

According to a release shared with PUNCH Online on Saturday, he was represented by the Executive Director, People, Stakeholders and Communication, Obinna Ihedioha.

Adedeji described Nigeria’s creative economy as one of the country’s most promising economic assets, saying it had evolved beyond entertainment into a major economic enterprise capable of generating jobs, earning foreign exchange and attracting investment.

He said the development of digital platforms and emerging business models required a corresponding shift in tax administration to ensure that fiscal policies did not discourage innovation, investment or business expansion.

“Government needs sustainable revenue to invest in education, security, technology and infrastructure. But how we tax matters as much as what we collect. It shapes whether businesses start, whether investors come, and whether enterprises grow or stay small,” he said.

He said the new tax laws provided an opportunity to reset the system around clearer rules, fewer burdens for small businesses and an administration built on service, understanding and support.

Adedeji identified clarity, understanding and value as critical pillars of an effective tax system for the creative economy, adding that formalisation should give businesses access to finance, contracts, investment and larger markets.

The Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, Hannatu Musawa, also highlighted the sector’s importance to Nigeria’s economic diversification, describing it as an opportunity for job creation, wealth generation and youth empowerment.

She identified intellectual property protection, digital infrastructure and access to funding as priorities, noting that Nigeria could learn from countries such as South Korea, which had transformed its creative industries into major drivers of economic growth.

The Executive Director, Finance and Corporate Services, Muhammed L. Abubakar, said tax residency status and double taxation agreements between Nigeria and other countries were important considerations in determining the tax treatment of income earned abroad.

Similarly, the Executive Director, Policy and Compliance, Shettima Tamadi, said understanding the practical difficulties businesses encountered under existing rules was essential to making tax administration more efficient and responsive.

During a panel discussion, tax policy expert Simeon Onyegbula highlighted provisions in the tax framework that could support creative enterprises, including income tax relief for qualifying small companies, changes to minimum tax provisions and the recovery of Value Added Tax paid on qualifying business equipment.

Mustapha Akaje also explained provisions relating to the zero per cent Company Income Tax rate applicable to qualifying small companies.

Speaking on business formalisation, Kazeem Lawal said proper business registration and structures gave creative enterprises a distinct legal identity, improved record-keeping and strengthened their ability to attract investors and access local and international markets.

The NRS said it participated in CANEX through a high-level dialogue, an Investment and Tax Advisory Hub for creators and investors, and the Creative Economy Tax and Investment Initiative, which is designed to sustain engagement beyond the event.

In his closing remarks, Ihedioha said uncertainty was a major concern among creative entrepreneurs, stressing the need for clear, predictable and accessible tax rules.

“Uncertainty is a tax nobody collects but everybody pays,” he said, adding that creators and investors were more likely to formalise, invest and grow when their tax obligations were clear.

He said the Creative Economy Tax and Investment Initiative would provide a continuing framework for collaboration on tax education, business formalisation, investment facilitation and policy dialogue.

The post NRS seeks simpler tax rules to boost creative economy appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Kwara trains Arabic, Islamic teachers in modern teaching skills
description:
The Kwara State Government has trained teachers in Arabic and Islamic schools in modern teaching methods, digital and financial literacy, and peaceful coexistence as part of efforts to improve the quality of education in the state.
According to a statement issued on Saturday, the two-day capacity-bu
content:
The Kwara State Government has trained teachers in Arabic and Islamic schools in modern teaching methods, digital and financial literacy, and peaceful coexistence as part of efforts to improve the quality of education in the state.

According to a statement issued on Saturday, the two-day capacity-building workshop, organised by the Ministry of Education and Human Capital Development in collaboration with the Kwara State University of Education, Ilorin, and Nusret Educational and Cultural Company Ltd., was held from November 17 to 18, 2026, in Ilorin.

Speaking at the programme, Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq said his administration was committed to improving education across all sectors, including Arabic and Islamic schools, through infrastructure development and continuous teacher training.

He said, “We have invested not just in western-styled schools. We have also partnered with UBEC to extend infrastructure upgrades to many Arabic and Islamic schools.

“It is an ongoing effort. This is in the spirit of fairness, inclusion, and pragmatic engagement of every demography of our society.

“This workshop is particularly important as it focuses on strengthening pedagogical skills, digital and financial literacy, and peaceful coexistence. These are essential competencies for teachers in today’s changing world.”

He urged participants to apply the knowledge acquired during the training to improve classroom instruction and learning outcomes.

Earlier, the Commissioner for Education and Human Capital Development, Lawal Olohungbebe, said the workshop was informed by consultations with stakeholders in Arabic and Islamic education and a subsequent needs assessment conducted by the ministry.

Olohungbebe explained that the ministry convened a stakeholders’ engagement in May 2026 to identify challenges facing the sector and explore ways of improving its standards.

He said the findings of the assessment informed the choice of topics for the workshop, particularly contemporary teaching methods, digital and financial literacy, and peaceful coexistence.

According to the commissioner, “the training was designed to equip teachers with learner-centred instructional approaches, effective classroom management techniques, improved assessment methods and the ability to deploy digital resources in teaching.”

He added that the initiative was also aimed at promoting functional skills, tolerance and responsible citizenship among learners.

In her remarks, the Vice-Chancellor of the Kwara State University of Education, Prof. Medinat Salman, reaffirmed the institution’s commitment to teacher development, stressing that contemporary pedagogical approaches and digital competencies were essential to effective instructional delivery.

Similarly, the Managing Director of Nusret Educational and Cultural Company Ltd., Huseyin Selvi, said the partnership was intended to strengthen Islamic education and preserve cultural values by equipping teachers with relevant knowledge and modern instructional skills.

Goodwill messages were delivered by the Grand Kadi of the Kwara State Shariah Court of Appeal, Ilorin, Justice Abdulateef Kamaldeen; a former Grand Kadi, Justice Haroon Idris; the Imam Imale of Ilorin, Sheikh Abdulhameed; and Prof. Hamza Abdulraheem.

The speakers emphasised the need to strengthen Arabic and Islamic education through sustained investment in teachers’ professional development.

title: NDA decorates four newly promoted colonels
description:

Olatoye gave the charge on Friday during the decoration of the officers at the
content:
The Commandant of the Nigerian Defence Academy, Major General Oluyemi Olatoye, has urged four newly promoted colonels to uphold integrity, professionalism and discipline while embracing adaptive and authentic leadership.

Olatoye gave the charge on Friday during the decoration of the officers at the NDA Officers’ Mess, Afaka, on November 20, 2026.

The Major Academy Public Relations Officer, Njoka Irabor in a release shared Saturday disclosed this.

According to the release also shared on X, the officers promoted from lieutenant colonel to colonel are “AO Adewara, MJ Bent, CJ Nkemakolam and AA Lawal.”

The commandant said “elevation in rank went beyond recognition of past achievements, as it came with greater responsibilities, higher expectations and increased commitment to service.”

He described their promotions as a testament to their dedication, loyalty, consistency and commitment to the core values of the Armed Forces of Nigeria.

Olatoye also emphasised the importance of mentorship and the professional development of subordinates, urging the officers to provide guidance, offer constructive corrections and create opportunities for their subordinates to grow.

He further urged them to “remain worthy ambassadors of the NDA by upholding discipline, professionalism and excellence in the discharge of their duties.”

Speaking on behalf of the newly promoted officers, Colonel AO Adewara thanked the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, for finding them worthy of promotion.

He also appreciated the Commandant for his leadership, guidance and support, as well as the Academy’s principal staff officers, colleagues, families and well-wishers for their encouragement.

The ceremony ended with group photographs involving the newly promoted officers, the Commandant, principal staff officers, spouses and invited guests.

description: President Bola Tinubu has mourned those who lost their lives in Friday’s tragic incident in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha Community, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, where four persons, who were on their way to a funeral, lost their lives when a boat carrying scores of people c
content:
President Bola Tinubu has mourned those who lost their lives in Friday’s tragic incident in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha Community, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, where four persons, who were on their way to a funeral, lost their lives when a boat carrying scores of people capsized.

The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, saying the boat was travelling from Ayama community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony that is taking place on Friday, November 20, 2026, when it capsized at about 11 a.m.

A preliminary police report indicated that the boat developed a mechanical problem while navigating the waterways.

Tinubu, who was “deeply saddened” by the tragic incident, said he had directed relevant disaster rescue operations to the area.

“Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation.

“I have also directed that our Presidential Campaign Rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, this Saturday, November 21, 2026, be observed without much fanfare in honour of the lives lost and in sympathy with the relatives and families of those involved in the disaster.

“On behalf of the entire nation, I mourn those who lost their lives in the incident and sympathise with their families, the government and the people of Bayelsa State.

“I particularly mourn with Governor Duoye Diri over this sad incident.

“I pray that God Almighty repose their souls and comfort their families”, Tinubu said in a statement posted on his personnal handle, @officialABAT on Twitter.

As of Friday, some passengers were still missing, but others were rescued, while search and rescue operations continued for the missing people.

I am deeply saddened by the tragic incident on Friday in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha Community, in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, where a boat carrying scores of people capsized, resulting in the loss of life.

The deceased were said to be mourners travelling to attend a funeral in the community where the incident happened.

Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation.

I have also directed that our Presidential Campaign Rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, this Saturday, November 21, 2026, be observed without much fanfare in honour of the lives lost and in sympathy with the relatives and families of those involved in the disaster.

On behalf of the entire nation, I mourn those who lost their lives in the incident and sympathise with their families, the government and the people of Bayelsa State.

I particularly mourn with Governor Duoye Diri over this sad incident.

I pray that God Almighty repose their souls and comfort their families.

– PBAT

— Bola Ahmed Tinubu (@officialABAT) November 21, 2026

title: Nigeria endorses Infantino for another term as FIFA president
description:
Nigeria has declared its support for Gianni Infantino’s bid to retain the presidency of the world football governing body, FIFA, in the 2027 election.



The Chairman of the National Sports Commission, Shehu Dikko, announced the Federal Government’s endorsement on Saturday during the 48th Ordinary G
content:
Nigeria has declared its support for Gianni Infantino’s bid to retain the presidency of the world football governing body, FIFA, in the 2027 election.

The Chairman of the National Sports Commission, Shehu Dikko, announced the Federal Government’s endorsement on Saturday during the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football in Abuja.

Speaking on behalf of President Bola Tinubu, Dikko said Nigeria would back Infantino’s re-election and called on other African football associations to support his continued leadership.

“I must make it clear here on behalf of the Federal Government and in regard to the resolution of all the members of CAF that Nigeria firmly endorses Mr Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for the election.

“This is a direct message that was given to us by the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Federal Republic of Nigeria,” he said.

“We recognise Mr Gianni’s contribution to the advancement of football worldwide, particularly in Africa, and urge our fellow African member associations to stand firmly together in support of his continued leadership.

“This is in our collective interest,” he added.

The NSC chairman also praised Infantino’s administration, drawing on his experience in football management to argue that the FIFA president’s decisions had served the interests of the sport.

“Before I conclude, if I put my heart as a football person, Mr President, as a former member of the NFL Exco, Chairman of the League, member of the FIFA Seconders Committee, and founding member of the World League Forum, I must tell you, Gianni’s decisions are very, very good for football. They are very apt for football,” he said.

He maintained that Infantino’s central responsibility was to grow the game and generate more revenue, arguing that disagreements within football administration largely concerned how the funds were shared.

“His main job is to develop football and bring revenues to football. He tries to do that. The entire issue we are seeing across the world here today has nothing to do with bringing the revenues or the distribution. It’s all about distributing these revenues,” Dikko said.

Nigeria’s declaration came at the same gathering where CAF president Patrice Motsepe reiterated the continental body’s backing for Infantino’s re-election.

Infantino, who became FIFA president in 2016, is seeking another four-year term at the election scheduled to hold in Morocco in March 2027 with French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo and Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima set to challenge him.

title: CAF launches U-17 Women’s AFCON, invites countries to bid for hosting rights
description:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has approved the introduction of an Under-17 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations, creating a new continental competition for young female footballers across Africa.
The decision was reached during a meeting of the CAF Executive Committee held in Abuja, Nigeria,
content:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has approved the introduction of an Under-17 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations, creating a new continental competition for young female footballers across Africa.

The decision was reached during a meeting of the CAF Executive Committee held in Abuja, Nigeria, on Saturday.

The meeting was chaired by CAF President, Patrice Motsepe, who led discussions on the development of African football.

The announcement was contained in a statement published on CAF’s official website on Saturday.

The new competition is expected to provide a platform for young female footballers to showcase their talents and gain more opportunities to compete at the continental level.

“The new competition will provide more opportunities for young African female footballers to compete at international level, gain valuable experience and develop their talents,” CAF said.

The continental football governing body also approved the opening of the bidding process for member associations interested in hosting the inaugural tournament.

In a separate decision, CAF opened the bidding process for the hosting rights of the 2028 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations.

Interested member associations have three weeks to submit their bids to the CAF Secretariat.

The 2028 tournament is scheduled to take place in March and April of that year, while qualifying matches are expected to begin in April 2027.

The Executive Committee also discussed measures to improve refereeing standards across African football.

CAF said its president, Motsepe, emphasised the need to accelerate investment in referee development, training and performance.

The chairman of the CAF Referees Committee, Olivier Safari Kabene, presented initiatives including the CAF Elite Referees Project, whose first training course is scheduled for the final week of November 2026.

Another initiative, the Next Generation Referees programme, is expected to be launched shortly to develop upcoming match officials.

CAF also said work was continuing on a referees’ manual to establish guidelines and standards for more consistent officiating across its competitions.

CAF already organises the U-17 Africa Cup of Nations for male footballers, a competition whose history dates back to 1985 when it began as a qualifying tournament for the FIFA U-17 World Cup. Its first standalone finals were held in 1995, with Nigeria winning the title in 2001 and 2007.

The introduction of the women’s version comes shortly after Nigeria’s Flamingos won the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, becoming the first African country to claim the title.

They defeated Japan 2-1 in the final on November 7, with Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku scoring for the Nigerian side.

The post CAF launches U-17 Women’s AFCON, invites countries to bid for hosting rights appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: 2027: Tinubu endorses Alli, Yayi, Hamzat at Ibadan rally
description:

Tinubu, who spoke at the rally held at Mapo Hall, said, “The governor you will vote for, I
content:
President Bola Tinubu on Saturday publicly endorsed the All Progressives Congress governorship candidates in Oyo, Ogun and Lagos states, raising their hands at the party’s campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State.

Tinubu, who spoke at the rally held at Mapo Hall, said, “The governor you will vote for, I will show you,” before raising the hand of Senator Sharafadeen Alli, the APC governorship candidate in Oyo State.

He subsequently raised the hands of Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, the party’s candidate in Ogun State, and Obafemi Hamzat, its governorship candidate in Lagos State.

The President also raised the hand of Remi Oseni, the APC senatorial candidate for Oyo South.

The endorsements came as the ruling party intensified its campaign ahead of the 2027 general elections, with Tinubu using his visit to his home region to rally support for the party’s candidates.

The Ibadan event was the South-West leg of Tinubu’s re-election campaign and the seventh state rally he had attended since the exercise began in Kaduna on October 24.

Vice-President Kashim Shettima, APC governors, members of the National Assembly and other party leaders attended the rally.

The President had directed that the rally be held without much fanfare in honour of victims of a boat accident in Ukubie, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, on Friday.

In a statement announcing the directive, Tinubu said the decision was taken “in honour of the lives lost and in sympathy with the relatives and families of those involved in the disaster”.

The Oyo governorship contest is particularly significant for the APC as the party seeks to take control of the state from Governor Seyi Makinde, who is seeking the presidency under the Allied Peoples Movement.

Alli, who represents Oyo South in the Senate, was endorsed as the APC’s consensus governorship candidate in May following consultations among party leaders.

In Ogun, Adeola, who represents Ogun West in the Senate, is the APC’s governorship candidate, while Hamzat, the incumbent deputy governor of Lagos State, is the party’s flagbearer in the state.

Tinubu’s public show of support for the three candidates at the rally placed the party’s governorship contests alongside his own re-election campaign, as APC leaders seek to consolidate support across the South-West.

title: Bayelsa boat accident: Tinubu directs emergency agencies to launch rescue operation
description:
President Bola Tinubu has expressed sadness over a boat accident in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha community, in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, which reportedly claimed several lives on Friday.
The victims were reportedly mourners travelling to attend a funeral in the community when
content:
President Bola Tinubu has expressed sadness over a boat accident in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha community, in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, which reportedly claimed several lives on Friday.

The victims were reportedly mourners travelling to attend a funeral in the community when their boat capsized.

In a statement issued on Saturday by his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, the President said he was saddened by the tragic incident.

Tinubu also disclosed that he had directed relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful rescue and recovery operation.

The President’s directive is aimed at ensuring that necessary emergency efforts are coordinated to respond to the incident and assist those affected.

“Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation,” Tinubu said.

The President also directed that the presidential campaign rally scheduled to hold in Ibadan, Oyo State, on Saturday, November 21, be observed “without much fanfare” in honour of the victims and in sympathy with their families.

“On behalf of the entire nation, I mourn those who lost their lives in the incident and sympathise with their families, the government and the people of Bayelsa State.

“I particularly mourn with Governor Douye Diri over this sad incident.

“I pray that God Almighty repose their souls and comfort their families,” he added.

The All Progressives Congress had outlined a proposed nationwide campaign rally schedule covering the 36 states of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The proposed campaign kicked off in Kaduna on October 24, 2026, and will conclude with a grand rally in Lagos on January 9, 2027.

Oyo was outlined as one of the 12 states Tinubu is expected to join the rally in person and will be his fourth, after Kaduna, Port Harcourt and Jos.

Bayelsa boat tragedy

Very Nigerian initially reported that more than 30 people were feared dead, while about 300 others were reportedly missing after the boat, popularly known as a “Love Boat”, capsized near Oweikorogha while conveying mourners to Ukubie for a burial ceremony.

In a subsequent report, the Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed that four bodies, comprising two adults and two children, had been recovered, while 24 survivors were rescued. The police said preliminary investigations indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways.

The Bayelsa State Government subsequently warned boat operators against overloading, reckless navigation and travelling without life jackets following the accident.

It also said it was supporting the joint search and rescue operation.

Earlier in November, Very Nigerian reported that a police officer and a woman died in two separate waterway accidents in Brass and Sagbama LGAs. Seven passengers were rescued after a passenger boat travelling from Yenagoa to Akassa capsized.

title: 2027: PDP rejects Lukman’s opposition coalition, declares support for Rainbow alliance
description:
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has dismissed claims that it has joined the opposition Coalition for Democracy being promoted by former All Progressives Congress (APC) National Vice Chairman, Salihu Lukman.
The opposition party also announced that it would not participate in the coalition’s propo
content:
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has dismissed claims that it has joined the opposition Coalition for Democracy being promoted by former All Progressives Congress (APC) National Vice Chairman, Salihu Lukman.

The opposition party also announced that it would not participate in the coalition’s proposed summit scheduled for November 30.

The PDP said it had not entered into any alliance with the group, authorised anyone to represent it at the meeting or agreed to be bound by decisions taken in its name.

The party maintained that its only recognised coalition arrangement was the Rainbow Coalition, which it said was backed by its National Leader, Nyesom Wike.

The position was made known in a statement signed by the PDP National Publicity Secretary, Hon. Jungudo Haruna Mohammed.

Mohammed explained that individuals being presented as representatives of the PDP at the coalition were expelled members who no longer had the authority to speak or act on behalf of the party.

The party’s clarification comes amid efforts by opposition figures to build a broader political alliance ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Jungudo said the individuals’ claims to the party’s leadership and representation had suffered defeats at the Federal High Court, Court of Appeal and Supreme Court.

He added that the courts had issued orders restraining Kabiru Tanimu Turaki, SAN, and his associates from parading themselves as PDP leaders, while imposing financial penalties exceeding N100 million over alleged abuses of court processes and frivolous litigation.

Questioning Lukman’s continued engagement with the individuals, Jungudo said, “It is therefore astonishing that Mr Salihu Lukman, who ought to be sufficiently informed about the legal status and recognised leadership of the PDP, would continue to engage these individuals and use them as a basis for associating the party with his so-called Toronto Coalition.”

Describing the proposed arrangement as a political project built on misrepresentation, the PDP declared it ‘dead on arrival’, particularly because those being presented as its representatives lacked the authority to speak on its behalf.

The party also threatened legal action against Lukman, his associates and other promoters of the Coalition for Democracy if they continued to use its name and institutional identity in their political activities.

“The party will not hesitate to pursue appropriate legal action against any person or group that continues to unlawfully associate the PDP with this arrangement,” Jungudo warned.

Reiterating its position, the party said the Rainbow Coalition, in line with Wike’s political direction and directives, remained its only recognised coalition arrangement.

It consequently urged Nigerians, political stakeholders, members and supporters, as well as media organisations, to disregard reports linking its national headquarters at Wadata Plaza, Abuja, to the November 30 summit or any other political arrangement being promoted by Lukman and his associates.

“The PDP will not allow its identity to be hijacked, its institutional authority misrepresented or its political interests compromised by individuals who have no mandate to speak or act on its behalf,” Jungudo said.

The party maintained that it would not be bound by any resolution or commitment purportedly made in its name by the promoters of the coalition.

The Sultan was received at the Oba Akenzua II Airport by senior members of the Oba o
content:
The Sultan of Sokoto, His Eminence Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, has arrived in Benin City, Edo State, ahead of the 10th coronation anniversary of the Oba of Benin, Omo N’Oba N’Edo, Uku Akpolokpolo, Oba Ewuare II.

The Sultan was received at the Oba Akenzua II Airport by senior members of the Oba of Benin-in-Council upon his arrival on Friday.

He was accompanied by the Galadiman Gerin Sokoto, His Royal Highness Alhaji Aliyu Attahiru Galadanci, who led his entourage.

The aircraft conveying the Sultan landed in Benin City 25 minutes after departing the Samuel Ladoke Akintola International Airport, Ibadan, Oyo State, at 5:05 p.m. on Friday, November 20.

His visit is in connection with the celebration marking 10 years of the reign of Oba Ewuare II as the traditional ruler of the Benin Kingdom.

In a statement by Prince Bashir Adefaka on behalf of the Media Team of the Sultan of Sokoto, noted that the Sultan was received by senior members of the Oba of Benin-in-Council at the airport.

He was accompanied on the flight by the Galadiman Gerin Sokoto, His Royal Highness Alhaji Aliyu Attahiru Galadanci, and former Director-General, National Broadcasting Commission, NBC, Mallam Danladi Bako, Kogunan Sokoto.

The Sultan arrived Ibadan on a weeklong South-West working visit on Sunday, November 15, starting off his activities with participation in the 11th General Assembly of the Muslim Ummah of South West Nigeria, MUSWEN, as special guest of honour.

The Sultan also performed his duty as Chancellor of the University of Ibadan on Tuesday, November 17, supported by his Pro-Chancellor and Chairman Governing Council, Chief Bisi Akande, as well as the new Vice-Chancellor, Professor Peter Olamakinde Olapegba, among others.

On Wednesday, he travelled from his Ibadan to Saki to partake – as Chairman of the Day – in the official commissioning of the 500-seat Alhaji Azeez Adedokun Olowolagba Information and Communication Technology, ICT, Centre built and donated to the College of Nursing Sciences, Muslim Medical Foundation Saki, by Alhaji Mudasiru Adedokun Olowolagba, in memory of his late father.

On Thursday, the Sultan paid a courtesy call on the Aseyin of Iseyin, Oba Sefiu Olawale Adeyemi III (Ajirotutu I), who will be celebrating his third coronation anniversary on December 11. He also witnessed the award ceremony by the Iseyin Kingdom in honour of legal luminary and philanthropist, Barrister Ahmed Raji (SAN).

On Friday, the Sultan of Sokoto paid a courtesy visit to the palace of the Olubadan of Ibadan Land, where Oba Rashidi Ladoja, Arusa I, assisted by Olubadan-in-Council, received him. Both monarchs then proceeded to the Bodija Muslim Community Central Mosque, Ibadan, where they observed their Jumat service led by the Chief Imam, Sheikh Hakeem Ibrahim.

He the left for Benin City, where he was first received by members of the Oba of Benin-in-Council and then later by the royal host himself in his palace the same Friday night.

content:
Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has ordered a thorough and impartial investigation into an alleged shooting involving military personnel in Lawanti community, Akko Local Government Area of the state, which reportedly left three persons dead and 13 others injured.

The incident allegedly occurred following a confrontation between military personnel and residents over suspected theft of armoured cables.

In a statement issued on Saturday by the Director-General, Press Affairs, Government House, Gombe, Ismaila Uba Misilli, the governor described the incident as deeply distressing and extended his condolences to the families of the deceased, while wishing the injured victims a speedy recovery.

Preliminary reports indicated that three persons lost their lives, while 13 others sustained varying degrees of injuries and were receiving medical attention at different health facilities, including the Federal Teaching Hospital, Gombe.

Governor Yahaya condemned the incident and appealed to residents of Lawanti and neighbouring communities to remain calm, exercise restraint and avoid actions capable of escalating tensions or disrupting public peace.

As part of the government’s response, the governor dispatched a high-powered delegation led by the Secretary to the State Government to visit the affected community, assess the situation, commiserate with the victims’ families and engage relevant stakeholders towards restoring calm.

He also directed that the circumstances surrounding the incident be thoroughly investigated to establish the facts, determine the causes and ensure that appropriate measures are taken in accordance with the law.

The governor assured the affected families and residents that the state government would work closely with relevant security agencies and other authorities to address concerns arising from the incident.

He further pledged that the government would monitor the condition of the injured persons and provide necessary support, while calling on community leaders, traditional rulers, religious leaders and other stakeholders to support efforts to maintain peace.

Yahaya reiterated his administration’s commitment to protecting lives and property, stressing that no effort would be spared in ensuring justice, sustaining peace and preserving cordial relations between communities and security agencies.

He prayed for the repose of the souls of the deceased and the speedy recovery of those injured in the incident.

content:
Human rights lawyer, Pelumi Olajengbesi, has described Afrobeats star David Adeleke, popularly known as Davido, as one of the fine gifts to the present generation.

In a Facebook post on Saturday to celebrate the singer’s birthday, Olajengbesi, who was the campaign spokesman for the re-election of Davido’s uncle, Governor Ademola Adeleke of Osun State, applauded the greatness of the Adeleke family.

Olajengbesi said, “Happy Birthday Davido, thank you for who you are to everyone who meets you. You are one of the finest gifts to our generation. I am not just grateful to you and your family, I am indebted for life.

“I have seen men, I have seen great families, but I have not seen many like the Adelekes. Blessed by God, graced by men, strengthened by love, bound together by service, and united by a generosity of spirit that transcends generations.

“There is something extraordinary about a family whose greatness is measured not merely by wealth, influence or accomplishments, but by the number of lives they have touched, the doors they have opened and the hope they continue to inspire in others.

“I pray that the Almighty God continues to preserve you, enlarge your coast, strengthen your home and grant you greater accomplishments. May your light never grow dim, and may generations yet unborn find inspiration in the legacy you are building.”

Back in September, Davido endorsed the ambition of Olajengbesi to contest the Oriade-Obokun Federal Constituency seat in the 2027 general elections.

Davido had described Olajengbesi as his next project following the governor’s victory at the poll.

Olajengbesi is contesting against Wole Oke of the All Progressives Congress, who has occupied the seat for 24 years.

The lawyer has garnered support from the likes of popular singer Dapo Oyebanjo, aka D’banj; Spotlite Nation boss Moses Bliss; and Yoruba Nation campaigner Sunday Igboho, among others.

title: CAF introduces U-17 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations
