CAF an
content:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has approved the establishment of an Under-17 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations.

The decision was reached on Saturday during a meeting of the CAF Executive Committee in Abuja, Nigeria, under the leadership of the body’s president, Patrice Motsepe.

CAF announced the development in a statement published on its official website.

“The new competition will provide more opportunities for young African female footballers to compete at international level, gain valuable experience and develop their talents,” CAF said.

“This decision reflects CAF’s commitment to strengthening women’s football, particularly at youth level, and creating a stronger pathway for the next generation of African footballers.”

Following the approval, CAF also invited member associations interested in hosting the maiden edition to begin submitting their bids.

In a separate decision, the Executive Committee approved the commencement of the bidding process for the 2028 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations.

Interested member associations have three weeks to forward their hosting proposals to the CAF Secretariat.

The 2028 edition of the tournament is scheduled for March and April, while its qualifying campaign is expected to commence in April 2027.

The meeting also considered plans to strengthen refereeing across African football, with Motsepe stressing the importance of increased investment in the training, development and performance of match officials.

CAF Referees Committee chairman, Olivier Safari Kabene, presented several proposals, including the CAF Elite Referees Project, which is scheduled to hold its first training programme in the final week of November 2026.

The body also plans to introduce its Next Generation Referees programme to prepare emerging officials for future assignments.

CAF added that it was developing a referees’ manual to provide uniform guidelines and improve consistency in officiating across its competitions.

title: Nigeria backs Infantino’s FIFA re-election bid
description:
Nigeria has endorsed Gianni Infantino’s bid for another term as president of the world football governing body, FIFA.
The Chairman of the National Sports Commission, Shehu Dikko, announced the Federal Government’s position on Saturday at the ongoing 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederatio
content:
Nigeria has endorsed Gianni Infantino’s bid for another term as president of the world football governing body, FIFA.

The Chairman of the National Sports Commission, Shehu Dikko, announced the Federal Government’s position on Saturday at the ongoing 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football in Abuja.

Dikko, who delivered the message on behalf of President Bola Tinubu, said Nigeria was supporting Infantino’s candidacy and urged other African football associations to stand behind him.

He said, “I must make it clear here that on behalf of the Federal Government, and in regards to the resolution of the entire members of CAF, that Nigeria firmly endorses Mr Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for the election.

“This is a direct message that was given to us by the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.”

Dikko said the country recognised Infantino’s contribution to the development of football globally, particularly in Africa.

“We recognise Mr Gianni’s contribution to the advancement of football worldwide, particularly in Africa, and urge our fellow African member associations to stand firmly together in support of his continued leadership.

“This is in our collective interest,” he said.

The NSC chairman also defended Infantino’s leadership from the perspective of his experience in football administration, describing the FIFA president’s decisions as beneficial to the game.

“Before I conclude, if I put my heart as a football person, Mr President, as a former member of the NFL Exco, Chairman of the League, member of the FIFA Seconders Committee, founding member of the World League Forum, I must tell you, Gianni’s decisions are very, very good for football. They are very apt for football,” Dikko said.

He argued that Infantino’s responsibility was to develop the game and increase its revenue, adding that the debate surrounding football administration should be viewed in that context.

“His main job is to develop football and bring revenues to football. He tries to do that. The entire issue we are seeing across the world here today has nothing to do with bringing the revenues or the distribution. It’s all about distributing these revenues,” he said.

Nigeria’s endorsement came at the same assembly where CAF president Patrice Motsepe reaffirmed the continental body’s support for Infantino’s re-election.

According to Reuters, Motsepe said Infantino had the backing of CAF’s 54 member associations, citing his commitment to African football during his five years as the confederation’s president.

Infantino, who has led FIFA since 2016, is seeking another term in the election scheduled for March 2027 in Morocco.

He faces potential challengers including French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo and Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima.

title: Real Madrid will never be sold – Pérez
description:
Real Madrid president Florentino Pérez has ruled out the possibility of the Spanish football club being sold, insisting that its members will remain its sole owners while announcing plans to strengthen their ownership rights.
Pérez said the club’s ownership structure would not be handed over to exte
content:
Real Madrid president Florentino Pérez has ruled out the possibility of the Spanish football club being sold, insisting that its members will remain its sole owners while announcing plans to strengthen their ownership rights.

Pérez said the club’s ownership structure would not be handed over to external interests, dismissing suggestions that Real Madrid could eventually come under the control of investors or other individuals.

He spoke on Saturday during the opening address at the club’s 2026 Ordinary General Assembly of Delegate Members, according to a statement published on Real Madrid’s official website.

The president said the issue of ownership had generated misinformation during the club’s recent electoral campaign, prompting him to reaffirm its membership-based structure.

He said, “Many things were said: that we wanted to sell the club, that the members would cease to be the owners, that Real Madrid would fall into other hands. All false.

“So I want to take advantage of this Assembly to say it once again, here and in front of all of you, so that there is no doubt: Real Madrid is not for sale. It has never been considered for sale and it never will be.”

Pérez stressed that the club belonged to its members and would remain under their ownership.

“The club belongs to and will always belong to its members, and even more so than it does today,” he added.

He also explained why proposals to extend membership to family members of existing members could undermine the current ownership arrangement.

According to Pérez, Real Madrid has approximately 100,000 members, but opening membership to their family members could increase the figure to between 300,000 and 400,000, potentially reducing the influence of existing members.

“Those who accused us during the campaign of wanting to sell the club even suggested opening the door of Real Madrid to allow all family members of current members to become members themselves.

“Do the math with me: today we are about 100,000 members, and with such a measure, we could very quickly find ourselves with 300,000 or 400,000 new members, which would reduce the current members to a minimal part of the membership base. That would indeed be giving Real Madrid away to others, without any control,” the president stated.

The club president described members as custodians of its history and financial assets, saying they had a responsibility to preserve its heritage for future generations.

Perez noted, “Members are not only the owners of Real Madrid; they are above all its guardians. They are the ones who have defended its heritage and history for 124 years, and it is upon them that the responsibility falls to pass it on intact, and even greater, to future generations.”

He added that the club was working on reforms aimed at reinforcing members’ ownership status and protecting its long-term interests.

“And that is precisely what we aim for with the reform we are working on: to reinforce our ownership status, solidify the club for the long term, and safeguard the heritage we have built together since 1902.

“Because Real Madrid’s leadership must be eternal, safeguarded, and collective, and it must never depend solely on the strength of a Board of Directors or a president,” he added.

Pérez said the club’s members had reaffirmed their confidence in his leadership during the last presidential election, describing their support as a responsibility to protect Real Madrid’s institutional independence.

He also insisted that the club’s direction would continue to be determined by its members.

“The destiny of Real Madrid will only be decided by its members. It has always been this way, and it always will be,” Perez assured.

The president said the club was also working on a new Madridista loyalty programme designed to establish a direct relationship with supporters worldwide.

The proposed programme would recognise fans’ interactions with the club, including watching matches, buying jerseys, visiting the Santiago Bernabéu Stadium, following content on Real Madrid Play and participating in supporters’ club activities.

Pérez, however, clarified that the initiative would not affect the ownership rights of existing members.

“I want to make something very clear because I know it’s important for the members: this program does not change what it means to be a member of Real Madrid. The members are the sole owners of the club.

“We hold a unique and exclusive status that cannot be compared to any other form of connection with Real Madrid, and we will continue as owners, always occupying a role that is unparalleled,” he concluded.

He said the programme would also create new revenue opportunities for the club by allowing it to engage directly with millions of supporters without intermediaries.

title: ‘I’ll Be Back’: Bayern’s Kane Vows After Ankle Surgery
description: Bayern Munich’s star striker Harry Kane pledged to return for the “business end of the season” after undergoing surgery on his left ankle on Saturday.Kane limped off after 20 minutes of Bayern’s 1-1 home draw with Cologne in their Bundesliga match on Friday, the club confirmi
content:
Bayern Munich’s star striker Harry Kane pledged to return for the “business end of the season” after undergoing surgery on his left ankle on Saturday.

Kane limped off after 20 minutes of Bayern’s 1-1 home draw with Cologne in their Bundesliga match on Friday, the club confirming the England captain had torn a ligament in his ankle.

Bayern issued a statement Saturday saying the Ballon d’Or winner had “successfully undergone surgery” on his left ankle.

“The 33-year-old will now begin his rehabilitation program,” Bayern said, with the injury expected to keep Kane out for three to four months.

Kane posted a picture on social media from his hospital bed on Saturday, vowing to work his way back to fitness this season.

“The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027.

“I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season.”

Kane shared a quote from three-time Super Bowl-winning wide receiver Julian Edelman: “tough times don’t last, tough people do”, while thanking his supporters for their messages of support.

Kane has a history of ankle issues, although he has only missed a handful of games since moving to Bayern in 2023.

England coach Thomas Tuchel will be keeping a keen eye out on how England’s most-capped player’s rehabilitation progresses.

England play Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals in late March.

The injury comes at a difficult time for Bayern, who are currently missing several players, particularly up front.

Bayern are without Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and captain Manuel Neuer, while midfielder Jamal Musiala and coach Vincent Kompany both returned after long lay-offs on Friday.

AFP

title: Pérez renews call for probe into Barcelona’s payments to ex-refereeing chief
description:
Real Madrid president Florentino Pérez has vowed not to stop pursuing accountability in the Negreira case, accusing LaLiga and the Spanish Football Federation of failing to take appropriate action over payments made to a former senior refereeing official.
Pérez also disclosed that Real Madrid had re
content:
Real Madrid president Florentino Pérez has vowed not to stop pursuing accountability in the Negreira case, accusing LaLiga and the Spanish Football Federation of failing to take appropriate action over payments made to a former senior refereeing official.

Pérez also disclosed that Real Madrid had reported LaLiga president Javier Tebas to Spain’s Higher Sports Council over his remarks comparing the club’s communication to the propaganda machinery of Nazi Germany.

He made the remarks on Saturday during the opening address at Real Madrid’s 2026 Ordinary General Assembly of Delegate Members, according to a statement published on the club’s official website.

The Negreira case concerns payments made by Barcelona to José María Enríquez Negreira, former vice-president of the Spanish Football Federation’s Technical Committee of Referees.

In 2023, Spanish prosecutors charged Barcelona with corruption over the payments.

Two of the club’s former presidents, Josep Maria Bartomeu and Sandro Rosell are also facing the same charge.

Again on Saturday, Pérez described the matter as extraordinarily serious, alleging that Negreira received more than €8m from Barcelona over nearly two decades.

“What has happened is extraordinarily serious. The number two in Spanish refereeing, the vice president of the Technical Committee of Referees, received, over nearly two decades (as far as we know), more than 8 million euros from a club we all know.

“We are talking about payments to a key figure in the refereeing system: among other things, he was the one who informed referees about their promotions and demotions.”

The Real Madrid president also cited a statement Negreira allegedly made to tax authorities concerning the payments.

He stated, “I remind you of what Negreira himself declared to the tax authorities. He literally said the following: ‘What Football Club Barcelona wanted was to ensure that no decisions were made against them, that everything was neutral.’ Those were his words, not mine, and they are recorded in the judicial proceedings.”

Pérez said Real Madrid had submitted documentation and evidence to UEFA, adding that the European football governing body confirmed on October 1 that its ethics and disciplinary inspectors were examining the materials.

“It had to be Real Madrid, one of the aggrieved parties, that gathered all the information and filed the complaint with UEFA. We have provided extensive documentation and evidence about events of extraordinary seriousness, and on October 1, UEFA confirmed that their ethics and disciplinary inspectors are analyzing all that documentation.

“Our request is very clear: that it be rigorously investigated, that action be taken with the utmost urgency, and that justice be served. That the investigation reaches its conclusion and the consequences of all of this are addressed,” the president said.

He criticised LaLiga and the Royal Spanish Football Federation for what he described as their failure to pursue the matter, arguing that the two bodies had not taken the necessary steps to ensure the case was investigated by UEFA.

He noted, “LaLiga remains in absolute inaction, claiming it lacks authority. It is true that it joined the criminal case, but joining is not investigating: we have seen how it did not even ask questions during the judicial process interrogations, as if it were not present.

“In the face of such behavior, there are only two possible explanations: either it wants to hide that it had information and did nothing, or it is simply not fulfilling its responsibility. And neither of these is acceptable.”

The dispute has also deepened tensions between Real Madrid and the Spanish refereeing authorities.

Pérez alleged that the club had become a target of hostility since the case became public, while questioning the propriety of referees who had filed complaints against Real Madrid subsequently officiating its matches.

He said, “And on top of that, we have to endure a group of these referees filing complaints against Real Madrid. In other words, they file complaints against us and then are assigned to referee our team’s matches in La Liga. Can you imagine being judged in a court by a judge who has filed a complaint against you? Well, this is what is happening in our competition today.”

Pérez also criticised Tebas over a social media comparison involving the club and Joseph Goebbels, Nazi Germany’s propaganda minister.

“On October 16th, Mr. Tebas crossed all boundaries when he compared Real Madrid’s communication to the propaganda mechanisms exploited by Goebbels, the Minister of Propaganda for Nazi Germany.

“The propagandist of a regime that brought the world its greatest tragedy with over 6 million crimes,” the Real Madrid president declared.

He said Real Madrid had demanded Tebas’s immediate resignation and confirmed that the club had reported him to the Higher Sports Council.

“For this reason, Real Madrid demanded his immediate resignation, and I confirm to you that we have reported Mr. Tebas to the Higher Sports Council for these statements,” he included.

Pérez added that the council had independently asked the Administrative Court for Sport to examine whether Tebas’s remarks constituted a serious infraction.

He maintained that the courts and UEFA should determine the outcome of the Negreira case, insisting that his responsibility as Real Madrid president was to ensure that the allegations were thoroughly investigated.

“I want to be very precise: it is not my place to judge anyone. That will be done by the courts and UEFA, and I respect the timelines and procedures of justice.

“But it is my responsibility, as president of Real Madrid, to demand that these events be investigated thoroughly, as they directly affect the credibility of our competition.

“And I say to you very clearly that I will not stop until all responsibilities are clarified,” he concluded.

title: How we tackled kidnapping, armed robbery in Anambra – Obi
description:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Peter Obi, says his administration provided more than 600 patrol vehicles and billions of naira to communities in Anambra State as part of efforts to tackle insecurity during his tenure as governor.
Obi disclosed this on Saturday in the sixth i
content:
The Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Peter Obi, says his administration provided more than 600 patrol vehicles and billions of naira to communities in Anambra State as part of efforts to tackle insecurity during his tenure as governor.

Obi disclosed this on Saturday in the sixth instalment of his series, ‘Nigerians, Go and Verify’, titled ‘Securing Lives and Property: Partnership with Security Agencies’, in which he detailed the investments and measures introduced by his administration to combat armed robbery, kidnapping and other criminal activities.

He said his government prioritised security because development would be impossible without the protection of lives and property.

“No meaningful development can take place where lives and property are constantly under threat. Education, commerce, investment, and other productive activities can only flourish when people feel safe,” he said.

According to him, Anambra faced serious security challenges when he assumed office, including armed robbery, bank attacks and kidnapping, which had created an atmosphere of fear.

He said he personally approached the then Inspector-General of Police, Sunday Ehindero, in 2006 to seek urgent intervention.

“Following our appeal, the police authorities constituted a special team comprising experienced officers, including the late Haruna John, Alhaji Amusa Bello, and others, to confront the security challenges in the state,” Obi said.

The former Anambra governor said his administration subsequently provided more than 600 patrol vehicles to security agencies, including the police, Army, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Customs, Immigration, National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, Federal Road Safety Corps, Prisons, State Security Service, Navy and community vigilante organisations.

He said, “Accordingly, our administration, using funds from the security votes, provided over 600 patrol vehicles to various security agencies, including the Police, Army, Civil Defence, Customs, Immigration, NDLEA, Road Safety, Prisons, SSS, Navy, and community vigilante organisations.”

He added that the intervention extended beyond vehicles to include Armoured Personnel Carriers, armoured Hilux patrol vans, communication gadgets, repeater and linker stations, base stations, mobile radios, walkie-talkies and generators.

He said, “We also used the same security votes to provide financial support for their operations, including fuel, weekly allowances, and other essential needs of security personnel.”

On community policing, Obi said his administration provided billions of naira to the 177 communities in the state to strengthen security in their respective areas.

He said, “We paid particular attention to community security because we understood that effective policing must have a strong local presence. Again, using funds from the security votes, we provided billions of naira to the 177 communities in Anambra State to strengthen security in their respective areas.”

According to him, traditional rulers and town union presidents were directed to establish vigilante groups under police supervision, while the police provided uniforms for their identification.

He said the government also contributed to the payment of the vigilantes’ salaries.

Additionally, Obi said his administration distributed 250 patrol vehicles manufactured by Innoson Vehicle Manufacturing Company in Nnewi to communities across the state.

He said, “Additionally, we provided 250 patrol vehicles to communities across Anambra State. These vehicles were manufactured by Innoson Vehicle Manufacturing Company in Nnewi. Some towns received more than one, depending on their size and security needs. This initiative was also extended to universities and other large institutions in the state.”

He said markets in Onitsha and its environs also received security vehicles in March 2014 to protect traders and their businesses.

The beneficiaries included Bridge Head Market, Ogboefere Market, Building Materials Market, Ogidi, Onitsha Main Market, Marine Modern Market, Ogbaru Main Market, Ose Okwodu Market, Electronics Market and the Amalgamated Market Traders Association.

On sustainable funding, Obi said his administration established the Anambra State Security Trust Fund in December 2011, with a target of N2bn.

He said, “Consequently, in December 2011, we established the Anambra State Security Trust Fund, with a target of N2 billion. We also distributed N356 million to the presidents-general of the 177 communities for security and palliative measures in their respective areas.”

Defending the use of security votes, he said the funds were deployed to address security challenges and support other public priorities.

“It is important to explain that the security votes were not treated as money to be spent without accountability or consideration of public benefit,” he said.

He added that his administration used part of the funds to pay N1m each to first-class graduates from Anambra State.

Obi further said his government invested in security infrastructure, including police facilities, communication systems and operational facilities for the State Anti-Robbery Squad at Awkuzu.

He said, “We provided facilities for the SARS at Awkuzu, including a fortified perimeter fence and other protective infrastructure.”

He also disclosed that N200m was contributed towards the reconstruction of internal roads at the 302 Artillery Regiment in Onitsha, including an additional N100m presented to the Nigerian Army in June 2013.

According to him, “In June 2013, we presented another N100 million to the Nigerian Army, bringing our contribution towards the reconstruction of internal roads within the Onitsha military barracks to N200 million.”

He said the project was executed by Army engineers.

On the security of waterways, Obi said his administration supported the establishment of a permanent naval outpost at Odekpe in Ogbaru Local Government Area with N200m in October 2013.

He said, “In October 2013, we presented a cheque of N200 million to the Nigerian Navy at the groundbreaking ceremony. We also undertook to provide access roads to the facility.”

Obi said the then Chief of Naval Staff, Vice Admiral Joseph Ezeoba, had explained that the naval presence was necessary to protect inland waterways around Onitsha and secure commercial activities associated with the Onitsha River Port.

He added that naval operations had commenced, leading to the arrest of criminal elements and the impounding of vessels used for illegal activities, according to the naval authorities.

On the fight against kidnapping, the former governor said his administration introduced a policy of sealing and demolishing buildings used as hideouts or operational bases by kidnappers.

He said, “We understood that kidnapping had become an organised criminal enterprise. We therefore adopted a policy that any property established to facilitate kidnapping or used as a criminal hideout would be sealed and, where investigations established its connection with the crime, demolished in accordance with the applicable law.”

Giving an instance, Obi said he personally led security operatives in August 2012 to seal a hotel at Nkpor and two buildings at Nri in Anaocha Local Government Area after security investigations linked the premises to kidnapping activities.

content:
President Bola Tinubu and the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, have arrived in Ibadan, the Oyo State capital, for the South-West leg of the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign.

The President is in the city to lead the party’s 2027 re-election campaign rally, which is being held at the historic Mapo Hall.

His arrival came hours after he directed that the rally be observed without much fanfare in honour of victims of Friday’s boat accident in Ukubie, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.

In a statement on Saturday, Tinubu said, “I have also directed that our Presidential Campaign Rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, this Saturday, November 21, 2026, be observed without much fanfare in honour of the lives lost and in sympathy with the relatives and families of those involved in the disaster.”

The rally is attended by Vice President Kashim Shettima, APC governors, and the leadership of the National Assembly, led by Senate President Godswill Akpabio and House Speaker Tajudeen Abbas.

The Ibadan event is the seventh stop of Tinubu’s re-election campaign since it began in Kaduna on October 24, 2026.

title: Otti approves N670m for Ohafia electricity extension project
description:
Governor Alex Otti of Abia State said he has approved N670m for the Ohafia electricity extension project from the substation to the various communities in the area.
Governor Otti disclosed this at the Elu-Ohafia school field during a reception organized for him by the Ohafia Improvement Union.
The G
content:
Governor Alex Otti of Abia State said he has approved N670m for the Ohafia electricity extension project from the substation to the various communities in the area.

Governor Otti disclosed this at the Elu-Ohafia school field during a reception organized for him by the Ohafia Improvement Union.

The Governor said his administration had already resolved the issues affecting power supply in the area and had approved the extension of electricity from the substation to various communities as requested by the people.

He explained that he had initially planned to commission the Ebem power station during the visit but was prevented by damage to some electricity poles caused by a trailer, which disrupted power supply.

“So, what you can take for granted and go to sleep with is that there will be electricity here before the end of this month,” Gov. Otti assured

“We have been on the issue of electricity, and I can tell you that we have resolved the problem. We would have commissioned the Ebem power station today, but, as we always do, we don’t commission any project that has a little challenge.

“Even though it was not our fault that a trailer hit about three poles and disrupted power supply, there is already power in Ebem,” Otti said.

He disclosed that he had directed the Commissioner for Power and Public Utilities to ensure that the necessary arrangements were concluded for the commissioning of the power station, while also approving the extension of electricity beyond the substation to the various localities in Ohafia.

Otti reiterated his administration’s determination to develop Ohafia into a major urban centre, noting that the establishment of the Greater Ohafia Development Authority was a strategic step towards achieving the objective.

He promised the people that Collins Memorial College would be converted into a Smart School and directed that construction work should commence immediately.

Gov. Otti assured that a new and standard general hospital would soon be built in the area.

The Governor accepted the honorary citizenship of Ohafia offered by the people.

Welcoming the Governor, the President General, Ohafia Improvement Union, Chief Prince Kalu Emeri; the Committee Chairman, Chief Uduma Kalu Okoro; and the Chairman, Ohafia Traditional Rulers Council, Eze Oscar Kalu Osonwa, appreciated the Governor’s commitment to the development of Ohafia and the creation of the Greater Ohafia Development Authority, and requested that the distribution of power from the newly restored Ebem substation be extended to the other communities of Ohafia.

The people later presented him with 10 mini buses for his campaign and assured him of victory at the polls.

title: Tight Security As Tinubu Takes Re-Election Campaign To Oyo
description: President Tinubu arrived in Ibadan, Oyo State, at around 12:28 PM amidst tight security as he takes his 2027 re-election campaign to his geopolitical zone, the South-west.Already, Vice President Kashim Shettima had arrived ahead of President Tinubu to flag off the campaign. His aircraft arrived the
content:
President Tinubu arrived in Ibadan, Oyo State, at around 12:28 PM amidst tight security as he takes his 2027 re-election campaign to his geopolitical zone, the South-west.

Already, Vice President Kashim Shettima had arrived ahead of President Tinubu to flag off the campaign. His aircraft arrived the Ladoke Akintola Airport around 12:10 PM noon, into the hands of waiting dignitaries and security agents.

First-class traditional rulers expected to meet with the President include the Ooni of Ife, Olubadan of Ibadanland, Alake of Egbaland, Ewi of Ado Ekiti, Soun of Ogbomoso, Ataoja of Osogbo, Olu of Ilaro and Timi of Ede, among others.
After meeting with the monarchs, Tinubu will proceed to Mapo Hall, where he is expected to inaugurate security vehicles procured by the South-west Development Commission (SWDC) for the region.

The campaign rally, scheduled for 1 p.m., will thereafter commence, with the President leading other All Progressives Congress (APC) chieftains, including Vice President Kashim Shettima, 31 state governors, and the National Assembly leadership, represented by Senate President Godswill Akpabio and House Speaker Tajudeen Abbas.
Today’s rally will mark the seventh state Tinubu will be at his re-election campaign rally since the exercise commenced in Kaduna on October 24, 2026.

In the revised campaign timetable released earlier this week by the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Tinubu is scheduled to campaign in 19 of the 36 states of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

The President, who had earlier campaigned in Uyo, Port Harcourt, Dutse, Jos and Birnin Kebbi, is also scheduled to take the campaign train to 13 other cities between November 25, 2026, and January 13, 2027. They are Maiduguri, Enugu, Katsina, Kano, Jalingo, Abuja, Gusau, Owerri, Yola, Sokoto, Ilorin, Asaba and Lagos.

title: Kane vows to return stronger after ankle surgery
description:
Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has promised to return to action before the end of the season after undergoing successful surgery on his left ankle.
The England captain sustained the injury during Bayern’s 1-1 draw against Cologne in their Bundesliga encounter on Friday.
Kane was forced off after 2
content:
Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has promised to return to action before the end of the season after undergoing successful surgery on his left ankle.

The England captain sustained the injury during Bayern’s 1-1 draw against Cologne in their Bundesliga encounter on Friday.

Kane was forced off after 20 minutes of the match, with medical examinations later confirming that he had suffered a ligament tear in his left ankle.

Bayern announced on Saturday that the 33-year-old had successfully undergone surgery and would begin rehabilitation.

The club said Kane was expected to be sidelined for three to four months.

Reacting to the development, the striker shared a picture of himself on a hospital bed, expressing disappointment over the injury but insisting that he remained determined to return stronger.

“The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027.

“I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season,” he wrote.

Kane also shared a motivational quote from former American football star Julian Edelman, saying, “Tough times don’t last, tough people do.”

He thanked supporters for their messages and encouragement following the injury.

The setback comes at a difficult time for Bayern, who are already dealing with several injury concerns involving key players.

Meanwhile, England coach Thomas Tuchel will be monitoring Kane’s recovery ahead of the country’s Nations League quarter-final fixtures against Norway scheduled for late March.

The striker’s availability for the games will depend on his rehabilitation progress.

title: Tinubu orders low-key Ibadan rally after Bayelsa boat accident
description:
• Mourns victims of boat mishap carrying funeral mourners in Southern Ijaw
• Directs federal disaster agencies to coordinate rescue, recovery operations
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja
President Bola Tinubu has directed that Saturday’s All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally i
content:
• Mourns victims of boat mishap carrying funeral mourners in Southern Ijaw

• Directs federal disaster agencies to coordinate rescue, recovery operations

From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has directed that Saturday’s All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Ibadan, Oyo State, be held without much fanfare in honour of victims of the boat accident in Bayelsa State.

Tinubu said the decision was in sympathy with the families of those who lost their lives when a boat carrying scores of people capsized on Friday in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha Community, in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.

The President, who described the incident as tragic, disclosed that he had directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful rescue and recovery operation.

In a statement posted on his verified X handle, @officialABAT, Tinubu said the deceased were mourners travelling to attend a funeral in the community where the incident occurred.

“Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way,” he said.

The President expressed condolences to the bereaved families, the Bayelsa State Government and the people of the state, particularly Governor Douye Diri, over the incident.

“On behalf of the entire nation, I mourn those who lost their lives in the incident and sympathise with their families, the government and the people of Bayelsa State.

“I particularly mourn with Governor Duoye Diri over this sad incident,” he said.

Tinubu also prayed for the repose of the souls of the deceased and divine comfort for their families.

title: APC rally: Traders make brisk business in Ibadan, awaiting Tinubu’s arrival
description:
Traders, on Saturday, ahead of the arrival of President Bola Tinubu for the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign at the historic Mapo Hall in Ibadan, made brisk business.



Items which were majorly on sale were customised APC caps and T-shirts with different inscriptions, as well a
content:
Traders, on Saturday, ahead of the arrival of President Bola Tinubu for the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign at the historic Mapo Hall in Ibadan, made brisk business.

Items which were majorly on sale were customised APC caps and T-shirts with different inscriptions, as well as sachet/table water, soft drinks and snacks.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the venue of the rally and its neighbourhood, such as Beere, Oja-Oba and Idi-Arere, were filled by thousands of APC members and supporters who came to hear from the number one citizen of Nigeria.

Sellers of brooms, the symbol of the APC, also had a good business day, as did vendors selling kolanut and bitter kola.

Some of the traders who spoke with NAN expressed satisfaction with the sales already recorded even before the start of the programme and arrival of President Bola Tinubu.

Mrs Janet Yewande, a food vendor near the venue, said she hired an additional six people to cope with the high volume of people waiting to buy from her shop.

She said that the high influx of customers had not made her increase the price or reduce the quantity of food.

On her part, Miss Rasheedat Bolade said the extra sales being recorded in sachet water would go a long way in settling some pending bills and her school fees.

Bolade said her mother had earlier bought enough bags of sachet water in preparation for the business of the day, adding that this had been her usual practice and means of survival whenever a big event was to be held at the ancient Mapo Hall.

Also, Mr Akeem Ogunwale, who sold customised caps, also said that he had made the necessary preparations by printing more caps and T-shirts in anticipation of high sales.

Ogunwale said that he had sold not less than 60 customised caps and 12 T-shirts at the campaign ground.

A soft drink seller, Mrs Mercy Kingsley, said she had already sold 10 crates of soft drinks, noting that though many people preferred cold drinks due to the high intensity of the sun, they still went ahead to buy the ordinary ones due to high demand.

A attendee at the campaign rally, Mr Kolade Ayinde, said the long hours in the sun compelled him to drink up to three sachets of water, adding that many supporters did not mind the intensity of the sun due to their love for the president.

Ayinde said the presence of the traders was normal, as it met the needs of the party faithful, especially given the intensity of the sun.

NAN reports that the mammoth crowd in and around Mapo Hall was still awaiting the arrival of the president and his team as of the time of filing this report. (NAN)

title: CAF approves U-17 Women’s AFCON, opens hosting bids
description:
The Confederation of African Football has approved the introduction of an Under-17 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations, creating a new continental competition for young female footballers.
The decision was taken by the CAF Executive Committee, chaired by its president, Patrice Motsepe, at a meeting in Abu
content:
The Confederation of African Football has approved the introduction of an Under-17 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations, creating a new continental competition for young female footballers.

The decision was taken by the CAF Executive Committee, chaired by its president, Patrice Motsepe, at a meeting in Abuja, Nigeria, on Saturday.

This was contained in a statement published on CAF’s website on Saturday.

“The new competition will provide more opportunities for young African female footballers to compete at international level, gain valuable experience and develop their talents,” CAF said.

The continental football governing body also approved the opening of the bidding process for member associations interested in hosting the inaugural tournament.

In a separate decision, CAF opened the bidding process for the hosting rights of the 2028 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations.

Interested member associations have three weeks to submit their bids to the CAF Secretariat.

The 2028 tournament is scheduled to take place in March and April of that year, while qualifying matches are expected to begin in April 2027.

The Executive Committee also discussed measures to improve refereeing standards across African football.

CAF said its president, Motsepe, emphasised the need to accelerate investment in referee development, training and performance.

The chairman of the CAF Referees Committee, Olivier Safari Kabene, presented initiatives including the CAF Elite Referees Project, whose first training course is scheduled for the final week of November 2026.

Another initiative, the Next Generation Referees programme, is expected to be launched shortly to develop upcoming match officials.

CAF also said work was continuing on a referees’ manual to establish guidelines and standards for more consistent officiating across its competitions.

CAF already organises the U-17 Africa Cup of Nations for male footballers, a competition whose history dates back to 1985 when it began as a qualifying tournament for the FIFA U-17 World Cup. Its first standalone finals were held in 1995, with Nigeria winning the title in 2001 and 2007.

The introduction of the women’s version comes shortly after Nigeria’s Flamingos won the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, becoming the first African country to claim the title. They defeated Japan 2-1 in the final on November 7, with Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku scoring for the Nigerian side.

title: CSR: Customs CG commissions jetty, classrooms in Ogun community
description:
From Laide Raheem, Abeokuta
The Comptroller-General of Nigeria Customs Service, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi, has commissioned projects executed as part of the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) activities of the Ogun 1 Area Command of the Nigeria Customs Service in Ijofin Community, Ipokia Local Gover
content:
From Laide Raheem, Abeokuta

The Comptroller-General of Nigeria Customs Service, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi, has commissioned projects executed as part of the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) activities of the Ogun 1 Area Command of the Nigeria Customs Service in Ijofin Community, Ipokia Local Government Area of Ogun State.

Speaking at the commissioning ceremony of the projects, which include a newly constructed jetty, renovation of first Nigeria Custom Service office and renovation of two blocks of seven classrooms under the Customs Cares Initiative, Adeniyi said the progress of an institution must be measured not only by its operational achievements, but also by the positive difference it makes in the lives of the people and communities it serves.

He stated that Nigeria Customs Service occupies a strategic position in Nigeria’s economic and national security architecture, with responsibilities of revenue generation, trade facilitation and border security remaining central to national development.

According to him, the effectiveness and sustainability of these responsibilities are closely connected to the relationships the Service maintains with communities around its operational environments.

“Our borders are not merely geographical boundaries. They are also spaces where our people live, conduct their businesses, raise their families and pursue their aspirations. Consequently, effective border management must be accompanied by constructive engagement, mutual understanding and a genuine commitment to the welfare of host communities”, the Customs CG stated.

Adeniyi explained that this understanding informs the Service’s deliberate efforts to strengthen its CSR initiatives, expanding engagements beyond conventional customs operations to include practical interventions that address community needs and contribute to sustainable development.

He added hat the Customs Cares Initiative, which complements the Renewed Hope Agenda, reflects this commitment through interventions spanning education, healthcare, social investment, food security and the creative economy.

“We believe that a modern Customs administration must be responsible and responsive to the expectations of the people. The projects being commissioned today are a practical expression of this philosophy,” he said.

He described the newly constructed jetty as one of the important interventions being presented, noting that for a community such as Itokhine, where waterways play a significant role in local transportation and economic activities, the provision of functional infrastructure can contribute significantly to connectivity, mobility, inclusiveness and commercial activities.

“We expect this facility to support the movement of people and goods, improve access to water transportation and create better opportunities for economic integration. Beyond its immediate purpose, the jetty represents an investment in the everyday activities and livelihoods of the people,” he said.

He, however, stressed that infrastructure delivers its greatest value when properly maintained and responsibly utilised, and reiterated earlier calls by previous speakers for all to work together to ensure the facilities remain accessible, safe and beneficial to the people for whom they have been provided.

Of particular historical significance, Adeniyi said, is the renovation of the first Customs office in Nigeria, which he noted goes beyond the restoration of a physical structure and represents an important effort to preserve the institutional heritage of the Nigeria Customs Service.

“Every enduring institution must understand and appreciate its history. The structures, people and experiences that helped shape its development provide important lessons about its evolution, responsibilities and contributions to national life,” he said.

He said the historic Customs office is a reminder of the longstanding presence of customs administration in that part of Nigeria and its connection with the development of government administration and international commerce.

“By renovating this historic facility, we are preserving an important part of our institutional identity for present and future generations,” he said.

He added that the modern Nigeria Customs Service did not just emerge from nowhere, but has evolved through decades of service, institutional reforms and changing national and international responsibilities.

“As we embrace digitalisation, automation and modern government management systems, we cannot afford to lose sight of the foundations upon which this institution was built. Our history should remain a source of institutional pride, identity and aspiration,” he said.

Adeniyi described the renovation as an important legacy project and said he would be having discussions with the Customs Area Controller and members of the community on the best approach to maintaining the building and putting it to proper use.

On education, which he described as an investment in the future, Adeniyi expressed delight at seeing the pupils of Ijuvi Junior High School, which was renovated.

“I want to assure you that, from what we have witnessed today, these children have the potential to become the team leaders of tomorrow,” he said, while commending the pupils for their wonderful performance and their teachers.

He said the renovation of Ijuvi High School reflects another important dimension of the Service’s commitment to sustainable economic development, noting that education remains one of the strongest foundations for individual advancement and national transformation.

“We recognise that the quality of the learning environment has a direct bearing on the educational experiences of pupils and the ability of teachers to discharge their responsibilities effectively,” he said.

Addressing the pupils, he said: “I want you to see this intervention as a reminder that your future matters and that we care about your success.”

He said the facilities being provided and preserved will serve as an enduring legacy for present and future generations, and congratulated the benefiting communities while urging them to put the facilities to proper use.

In his remark, the acting Comptroller Federal Operations Unit, Zone A, Ikeja, DC O Afeni said urged beneficiaries of the project to use the facilities judiciously.

Afeni, who lauded effort of the Custom Comptroller General towards completion of the projects, called on the students to take their study serious and be a worthy ambassador of their community

Also, Chief Wasiu Olaniyan while speaking on behalf of the traditional rulers in attendance reiterated commitment of the traditional rulers towards emsuring good maintaince of the facilities.

He however reaffirmed support of the community to anti-smuggling.

title: WPRF 2026: Nigerian innovator wins $1,500 prize with AI-powered PR platform
description:
• Ubong Anietie-Udo clinches Global Alliance top award; Akinsanya Glory, Fathiu Bello win $1,000, $500 prizes respectively
• Neliaku, honoured as ‘Grand Commander’ of young professionals

A Nigerian communications innovator, Ubong Anietie-Udo, haswon the $1,500 star prize at the 2026 World Public Re
content:
• Ubong Anietie-Udo clinches Global Alliance top award; Akinsanya Glory, Fathiu Bello win $1,000, $500 prizes respectively

• Neliaku, honoured as ‘Grand Commander’ of young professionals

A Nigerian communications innovator, Ubong Anietie-Udo, haswon the $1,500 star prize at the 2026 World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) Youth Innovation Challenge with an artificial intelligence-powered platform designed to transform public relations practice.

Anietie-Udo, who works with Mo Eden Media Consult, emerged winner of the innovation challenge with Perceptor, an AI-powered, all-in-one communications tool designed to help public relations practitioners plan campaigns, create content, manage crises and reach target audiences more effectively.

The competition featured three finalists, with Akinsanya Glory emerging first runner-up with the Save Me safety application, while Fathiu Bello came third with Campaign Intelligence Nigeria.

While Anietie-Udo received the $1,500 Global Alliance President’s Prize, Glory won the $1,000 African Public Relations Association (APRA) President’s Prize, while Bello received the $500 Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR) President’s Prize.

The prizes were sponsored by the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management, APRA and NIPR.

Presenting his innovation before communications professionals at the forum, Anietie-Udo said Perceptor was developed in response to the growing challenge of information overload and the difficulty of securing public attention in an increasingly crowded digital space.

He explained that the platform would simplify the work of communications professionals by integrating several functions, including content planning, press release writing, campaign perception analysis, crisis management and media outreach.

According to him, Perceptor also provides media directories, recommends suitable media organisations for specific campaigns and helps practitioners localise their messages to reach intended audiences.

He described it as a one-stop communications platform that would eliminate the need for practitioners to move between multiple digital tools to execute routine professional tasks.

During the question-and-answer session, Anietie-Udo said the platform was also designed to address language barriers in communication, revealing that it had been simplified to accommodate Nigerian Pidgin, with plans to incorporate Hausa and Yoruba.

Asked what distinguished Perceptor from existing artificial intelligence platforms such as ChatGPT, he said the innovation was specifically designed for public relations and communications practitioners, offering industry-focused responses and integrated professional tools.

The second-place innovation, Save Me, presented by Akinsanya Glory, seeks to improve the safety of Nigerian students through instant emergency alerts, an artificial intelligence companion, voice-activated assistance and safety education.

The application is designed to support students before, during and after emergencies, including robbery, harassment and assault.

The developer said the team had built a prototype and was preparing to pilot it on selected campuses, with plans to partner student organisations, university managements and campus security departments.

The proposed business model offers students two months of free access before introducing a monthly subscription fee of N900.

The team also projected between 500 and 1,000 paying subscribers within its first year, with plans to expand to 10,000 users by the fifth year.

Responding to concerns about unreliable internet connectivity and power supply, the team admitted that the current version depended on electricity and internet access but said it planned to improve its capabilities.

It added that where a user’s phone went off, the application would transmit the person’s last known location to an emergency contact.

Bello, a final-year Mass Communication student of Lagos State University, presented Campaign Intelligence Nigeria, a platform designed to help organisations and campaign planners develop location-specific communication strategies.

He said the platform would provide information on the demographics, cultural backgrounds, religious considerations and media consumption habits of communities to help organisations deliver messages that resonate with their intended audiences.

Unlike generic artificial intelligence responses, Bello said the platform would rely on information supplied by people familiar with the communities being targeted.

He explained that the initiative would engage and pay local contributors to provide relevant community information for its database.

The audience, however, questioned the proposed data-gathering process, particularly how indigenous communities would be engaged and how the platform would ensure the accuracy and quality of information collected.

In a related development, the President of NIPR, Dr Ike Neliaku, was honoured by young professionals at the forum in recognition of his commitment to developing emerging communication practitioners.

The young professionals conferred on him the symbolic title of “Grand Commander” of young professionals and presented him with an award of recognition.

They also expressed appreciation to the NIPR leadership for providing a platform for young professionals and communication scholars to develop their skills and advance their careers.

The award presentation formed part of the concluding activities at the 2026 World Public Relations Forum in Abuja, which brought together communication professionals and stakeholders from across the world.

title: Severe Storm Destroys Thousands Of Homes, Kills Three In Brazil
description: A powerful storm with winds exceeding 100 kilometers per hour killed three people and destroyed around 5,000 homes Friday in southern Brazil, as authorities raced to rescue injured survivors and find more casualties in the wreckage.Rain and high winds battered Tupancireta early Friday, tearing up bu
content:
A powerful storm with winds exceeding 100 kilometers per hour killed three people and destroyed around 5,000 homes Friday in southern Brazil, as authorities raced to rescue injured survivors and find more casualties in the wreckage.

Rain and high winds battered Tupancireta early Friday, tearing up buildings and about 100 trees in the municipality that is home to 20,000 people.

“It’s something never seen before, a movie scene,” Tupancireta Mayor Gustavo Herter told local media.

“Our hospital was blocked by the trees around it, the access roads to the municipality were blocked with trees. The city is finished,” he said. The hospital’s roof was also destroyed and 11 patients had to be transferred.

The city was without electricity and water after the storm hit at around 3 am and lasted less than an hour, Herter said.

Three people were found dead, according to the state government of Rio Grande do Sul, where Tupancireta is located.

Another 32 municipalities also reported damage.

President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva ordered emergency teams be sent to the region in response to the storm.

“We know there was a party in the municipality where the roof of that structure ended up collapsing,” Luciano Boeira, state coordinator of civil defense, told Radio Gaucha.

Brazilian meteorologists said winds reached 114 kilometers per hour (70 miles per hour) during the storm.

Civil defense described the storm as a “supercell,” which often precedes a tornado with strong upward air currents, and has not ruled out the possibility that a tornado hit the city.

State officials have allocated about $330,000 in local currency to respond to the disaster.

Southern Brazil is frequently hit by tornadoes.

AFP

title: 2027: Inuwa flags off N24bn roads, says Gwamna will ensure completion
description: Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has flagged off the construction of two road projects covering approximately 23 kilometres in Balanga Local Government Area, assuring residents that the APC governorship candidate, Dr. Jamilu Ishyaku Gwamna, will ensure the completion of ongoing projects
content:
Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has flagged off the construction of two road projects covering approximately 23 kilometres in Balanga Local Government Area, assuring residents that the APC governorship candidate, Dr. Jamilu Ishyaku Gwamna, will ensure the completion of ongoing projects if elected in 2027.

The Governor performed the groundbreaking ceremonies on Tuesday, November 17, during the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign engagements across Balanga North, where the party’s campaign train received receptions from supporters, community leaders and stakeholders in Talasse, Bangu, Kulani-Degri, Gelengu and Swa.

The major project is the 18.9-kilometre Talasse-Bangu-Boka Bundi-Walalunguda Road, with a spur to Dalawaja, awarded to Datum Construction Limited at approximately N23.98 billion, with a completion period of 24 months.

The road will feature two major bridges and extend connectivity to communities bordering neighbouring Adamawa State, improving access to economic centres and essential services.

The Governor also flagged off the initial four-kilometre section of the Degri-Sikam-Nyuwar Road, covering the Degri-to-Sikam stretch. The project, also awarded to Datum Construction Limited, has an eight-month completion period, with 30 per cent of the contract sum already paid to facilitate the commencement of work.

Speaking at the campaign rally in Talasse, Inuwa Yahaya described his administration’s development interventions as visible and tangible, urging residents to acknowledge the projects executed across their communities.

“What we have done is physical, real and not abstract,” he said.

He called on the electorate to support APC candidates, including President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, governorship candidate Dr. Jamilu Ishyaku Gwamna and other party flag bearers, stressing that continuity in governance would ensure the completion of ongoing projects and sustain development programmes.

“We started with work and will finish our government with work and development. Another APC government under Jamilu Gwamna will continue from where we stop,” the Governor said.

He further described development as a continuous process, maintaining that his successor would build on the foundation laid by the present administration.

Responding, APC governorship candidate, Dr. Jamilu Ishyaku Gwamna, assured residents that his administration would sustain and expand the development initiatives of the Inuwa Yahaya government.

“Governor Inuwa has done a lot for you, and we pledge to sustain his legacy and build on it to achieve even more,” Gwamna said.

title: FG engages 6,500 artisans on Kano-Katsina-Maradi railway project
description:
The Federal Government has revealed that it has directly recruited, trained, and engaged more than 6,500 Nigerians in various construction and production activities on the ongoing Kano-Katsina-Maradi railway project.
The Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Transportation, Olufunso Adebiyi
content:
The Federal Government has revealed that it has directly recruited, trained, and engaged more than 6,500 Nigerians in various construction and production activities on the ongoing Kano-Katsina-Maradi railway project.

The Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Transportation, Olufunso Adebiyi, announced this on Friday, during an inspection tour of the project at the Kazaure construction site in Jigawa State.

Adebiyi highlighted that approximately 6,500 workers were currently engaged on the project, with only about 200 of them being expatriates. He explained that the locally recruited workers would be retained as staff after the completion of the project to ensure that Nigerians continue to operate and manage the railway infrastructure.

He also highlighted the contributions of the Federal University of Transportation, Daura, Katsina State, in providing specialised training and developing local manpower to strengthen the country’s railway sector.

The Permanent Secretary announced that the first phase of the project, covering the Kano-Dawanau to Katsina section, was scheduled for commissioning in December 2026, while construction would continue on the remaining sections linking Katsina to Jibia and Maradi in the Niger Republic.

Providing an update on the level of progress, Adebiyi disclosed that approximately 650,000 of the 800,000 concrete railway sleepers required for the project had already been manufactured at the construction yard.

He added that most of the materials needed to complete the project, including rail tracks and reinforcement materials, were already available at the site, while the formwork required for construction activities had also been completed.

According to him, workers were currently engaged in assembling and coupling railway tracks towards Maradi, adding that the new executive rail line was expected to be completed within 10 days.

Adebiyi described the Kano-Maradi railway project, which spans approximately 400 kilometres, as significantly larger than the Abuja-Kaduna and Kaduna-Kano railway corridors, which cover 189 kilometres and 203 kilometres respectively.

On cross-border operations, he disclosed that the Federal Government had resumed discussions with the Niger Republic’s Ministry of Transportation to address security, immigration and customs requirements.

According to the Permanent Secretary, the discussions were aimed at facilitating the movement of construction equipment, machinery and personnel between the two countries to ensure the timely completion of the remaining sections of the railway project.

Meanwhile, the Vice-Chancellor of the Federal University of Transportation, Daura, Professor Umar Adam Katsayal, commended the Permanent Secretary and his entourage for the inspection visit.

Katsayal expressed optimism that the visit would further strengthen the Ministry of Transportation’s support for the university.

He added that the engagement would also promote stronger collaboration between the university and companies involved in railway construction and the provision of critical railway infrastructure, particularly signalling and communication systems.

The post FG engages 6,500 artisans on Kano-Katsina-Maradi railway project appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: ‘I’ll be back’: vows Kane after ankle surgery
description:
Bayern Munich’s star striker Harry Kane pledged to return for the “business end of the season” after undergoing surgery on his left ankle on Saturday.



Kane limped off after 20 minutes of Bayern’s 1-1 home draw with Cologne in their Bundesliga match on Friday, the club confirming the England capta
content:
Bayern Munich’s star striker Harry Kane pledged to return for the “business end of the season” after undergoing surgery on his left ankle on Saturday.

Kane limped off after 20 minutes of Bayern’s 1-1 home draw with Cologne in their Bundesliga match on Friday, the club confirming the England captain had torn a ligament in his ankle.

Bayern issued a statement Saturday saying the Ballon d’Or winner had “successfully undergone surgery” on his left ankle.

“The 33-year-old will now begin his rehabilitation program,” Bayern said, with the injury expected to keep Kane out for three to four months.

Kane posted a picture on social media from his hospital bed on Saturday, vowing to work his way back to fitness this season.

“The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027.

“I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season.”

Kane shared a quote from three-time Super Bowl-winning wide receiver Julian Edelman: “tough times don’t last, tough people do”, while thanking his supporters for their messages of support.

Kane has a history of ankle issues although he has only missed a handful of games since moving to Bayern in 2023.

England coach Thomas Tuchel will be keeping a keen eye out on how England’s most capped player’s rehabilitation progresses.

England play Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals in late March.

The injury comes at a difficult time for Bayern, who are currently missing several players, particularly up front.

Bayern are without Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and captain Manuel Neuer, while midfielder Jamal Musiala and coach Vincent Kompany both returned after long lay-offs on Friday.

title: APC rally: Traders make brisk sales in Ibadan
description:
Traders on Saturday did brisk business ahead of the arrival of President Bola Tinubu for the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally at the historic Mapo Hall in Ibadan, Oyo State.
Items mainly on sale included customised APC caps and T-shirts bearing different inscriptions, as w
content:
Traders on Saturday did brisk business ahead of the arrival of President Bola Tinubu for the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally at the historic Mapo Hall in Ibadan, Oyo State.

Items mainly on sale included customised APC caps and T-shirts bearing different inscriptions, as well as sachet and bottled water, soft drinks and snacks.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the rally venue and its neighbourhoods, including Beere, Oja-Oba and Idi-Arere, were filled with thousands of APC members and supporters who came to hear from the President.

Sellers of brooms, the symbol of the APC, also recorded brisk sales, as did vendors of kolanuts and bitter kola.

Some of the traders who spoke with NAN expressed satisfaction with the sales recorded even before the start of the programme and the arrival of President Bola Tinubu.

Mrs Janet Yewande, a food vendor near the venue, said she had hired an additional six people to cope with the high volume of customers waiting to buy food from her shop.

She said the influx of customers had not made her increase her prices or reduce the quantity of food served.

Miss Rasheedat Bolade said the additional sales from sachet water would go a long way towards settling some pending bills and paying her school fees.

Bolade said her mother had bought enough bags of sachet water in preparation for the day’s business, adding that this had been her usual practice and means of survival whenever a major event was held at the historic Mapo Hall.

Also, Mr Akeem Ogunwale, a seller of customised caps, said he had made the necessary preparations by printing more caps and T-shirts in anticipation of high sales.

Ogunwale said he had sold no fewer than 60 customised caps and 12 T-shirts at the campaign ground.

A soft drink seller, Mrs Mercy Kingsley, said she had already sold 10 crates of soft drinks, noting that although many people preferred cold drinks because of the intense heat, some still bought drinks that were not chilled because of the high demand.

A participant at the campaign rally, Mr Kolade Ayinde, said the long hours spent in the sun had compelled him to drink up to three sachets of water, adding that many supporters did not mind the heat because of their support for the President.

Ayinde said the presence of traders was normal, as they catered to the needs of party supporters, especially given the intensity of the sun.

NAN reports that the large crowd in and around Mapo Hall was still awaiting the arrival of the President and his team as of the time of filing this report.

NAN

title: NAFDAC destroys N100bn fake, expired products in Ogun
description:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control says it has destroyed fake, banned, expired and substandard products worth N100bn.
The Director-General of NAFDAC, Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye, disclosed this in a statement issued on Friday, saying the products were destroyed at Ogwama Dum
content:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control says it has destroyed fake, banned, expired and substandard products worth N100bn.

The Director-General of NAFDAC, Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye, disclosed this in a statement issued on Friday, saying the products were destroyed at Ogwama Dumpsite, Ogere Remo, Ogun State.

Adeyeye said the exercise was crucial to preventing the reintroduction of expired, fake, substandard and falsified drugs into circulation.

She said the products destroyed included expired, counterfeit, controlled, unregistered and banned drugs, as well as alcoholic beverages in sachets and plastic bottles below 200ml.

Others included banned Analgin injection, expired Codeine cough syrups, Oxytocin injection, counterfeit cosmetics and unwholesome food products.

The NAFDAC boss said operatives had recently uncovered illegally manufactured cosmetics and unregistered pharmaceutical products in a warehouse in Lagos.

The Director-General said officers also discovered cartons of Augmentin and Ampicillin packets, leaflets and other unregistered cosmetics in the warehouse.

Adeyeye said the agency’s Investigation and Enforcement officers also uncovered a hub where counterfeit versions of popular alcoholic beverage brands were produced.

She added that expired energy drinks were revalidated and stored at the facility, while suspects were arrested to face the full wrath of the law.

According to her, NAFDAC officers in Lagos and Ogun coordinated the mop-up of more than 100,000 cartons of banned sachet and plastic-bottled alcoholic beverages.

The NAFDAC boss said the products were recovered from manufacturers, wholesalers and retailers during enforcement operations across the two states.

Adeyeye also disclosed that officers uncovered a residential building used for manufacturing and selling large volumes of unauthorised and registered herbal mixtures.

She said other products marked for destruction were recovered during raids, while some expired products were voluntarily handed over by compliant companies.

The Director-General said the destruction would eliminate the risk of the products re-entering the Nigerian market.

Adeyeye appreciated the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) for handing over pharmaceutical products, including several cartons of Codeine cough syrup, for destruction.

She also acknowledged the support of the Nigeria Police, Nigerian Army, Department of State Services, Pharmacists Council of Nigeria and National Drug Law Enforcement Agency.

The Director-General further appreciated the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps and other stakeholders supporting the fight against substandard and falsified medicines.

Adeyeye urged community and religious leaders, health practitioners, the media and Nigerians to educate their families on the dangers of patronising quacks and unauthorised medicine vendors.

She called for continued public cooperation and the provision of useful information to help prevent and eradicate unregistered, dangerous and other injurious products from society.

The NAFDAC boss said collective efforts were necessary to protect the health and safety of Nigerians.

(NAN)

title: Mexico arrests FBI most-wanted drug lord Chapo Isidro
description:
Mexican security forces have arrested notorious drug cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, popularly known as Chapo Isidro, during a military operation in Guasave, Sinaloa State.
The arrest took place on Friday, November 20, following an operation involving Mexican Army and National Guard special
content:
Mexican security forces have arrested notorious drug cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, popularly known as Chapo Isidro, during a military operation in Guasave, Sinaloa State.

The arrest took place on Friday, November 20, following an operation involving Mexican Army and National Guard special forces, with support from United States intelligence agencies, the New York Post reported on Saturday.

Meza Flores, “described by American authorities as a major drug trafficker, was reportedly arrested alongside two alleged associates identified as Germán N, also known as Serafín, and José N, who was said to be responsible for the organisation’s financial operations.”

The three suspects were subsequently flown to Mexico City.

The operation reportedly triggered violent confrontations between security forces and suspected cartel members, resulting in gunfire, road blockades and the burning of vehicles in parts of Sinaloa.

According to the New York Post, “gunshots also disrupted a baseball match in Guasave, forcing players and spectators to flee. The match was subsequently abandoned.”

Meza Flores’ arrest is considered a major development in the fight against drug trafficking, particularly because he was among the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s 10 most-wanted fugitives.

On February 4, 2025, the FBI added him to its Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list, accusing him of leading the Meza-Flores cartel, an organisation allegedly involved in trafficking fentanyl, cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine and marijuana into the United States.

The US government had also announced a reward of up to `$5m for information leading to his arrest and conviction.

In announcing his addition to the list, then FBI Acting Director, Brian Driscoll, accused the cartel leader of spending about 20 years trafficking illegal drugs into the United States.

Meza Flores was also accused by American authorities of involvement in kidnapping, extortion, torture and murder.

According to the FBI, he was first indicted on May 2, 2012, in the United States District Court for the District of Columbia. A superseding indictment returned on November 26, 2019, charged him with drug-trafficking offences and possession of firearms.

The FBI said the indictment alleged that he conspired to manufacture and distribute cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine and marijuana in the United States between 2005 and 2019.

The New York Post reported that “Meza Flores faces drug-trafficking and firearms-related allegations, as well as an extradition request from the United States.”

His organisation, also known as the Meza-Flores cartel, has been linked to the wider Sinaloa criminal network and has operated in the northern Mexican state.

The arrest comes amid renewed security operations against criminal organisations in Sinaloa, where suspected cartel members have repeatedly clashed with security forces.

Authorities reportedly deployed additional security personnel following the violence that erupted during Friday’s operation, while efforts were made to reopen affected roads and restore normal activities in the area.

According to PUNCH’s report, a fellow Mexican, Joaquín ‘El Chapo’ Guzmán was arrested on February 22, 2014, in Mazatlán, Sinaloa, Mexico.

He was subsequently rearrested on January 8, 2016, after escaping from prison in July 2015. He was extradited to the United States on January 19, 2017.

Fallen drug lord “El Chapo” was locked up in 2019 at the ADX federal maximum security prison in the US state of Colorado, where he will spend the rest of his days.
