title: Catholic Church in Nigeria has supported me spiritually, financially – Jude Nnam
description:
Renowned Nigerian composer, singer and music director, Dr Jude Nnam, has acknowledged the financial and spiritual support he has received from the Catholic Church in Nigeria during his ongoing medical treatment in India.







Nnam, who is currently recuperating, said the Catholic Bishops Conferenc
content:
Renowned Nigerian composer, singer and music director, Dr Jude Nnam, has acknowledged the financial and spiritual support he has received from the Catholic Church in Nigeria during his ongoing medical treatment in India.

Nnam, who is currently recuperating, said the Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria (CBCN) had been instrumental in supporting him throughout his medical journey, contrary to suggestions by some individuals that the Church had not done enough to assist him.

In a message of appreciation to friends and supporters on his Facebook page, the music director said he was getting better by the day through God’s grace, prayers and support from the Church and well-wishers.

Addressing concerns raised by some individuals over the need for the Catholic Church in Nigeria to assist with the financial burden of his treatment, Nnam said the Church had provided him with tremendous support.

He particularly expressed gratitude to the Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria for taking responsibility for his situation and providing both financial and spiritual assistance since his arrival in India.

Nnam also singled out the Secretary-General of the Catholic Secretariat of Nigeria, Rev. Fr. Michael Banjo, for his personal commitment and support.

According to him, Banjo visited him in India on behalf of the Bishops Conference, bringing gifts and blessings from the bishops, and spent an entire week with him.

He said the priest celebrated Mass for him daily throughout his stay before returning to Nigeria.

The composer further acknowledged the individual contributions of Catholic bishops and dioceses, noting that they had supported him through telephone calls, messages and financial contributions.

He also thanked friends and other well-wishers whose prayers and financial contributions had helped sustain him during the challenging period.

“Be rest assured that the Catholic Church in Nigeria has supported me in this journey in no small measure, and I remain grateful,” he said.

Nnam appealed for continued prayers for his recovery, expressing optimism that he would soon return to Nigeria and resume his musical and religious assignments.

“By the grace of God, I shall be back soon to continue the work of my Father and my Healer,” he said.

title: 2027: Tinubu must win all 18 Cross River LGs – Minister
description:
The Minister of State for Industry, Trade and Investment, John Enoh, has urged Cross River residents to secure President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, warning that the state risks losing its place in national decision-making if it fails to support the President.
Enoh said this on Friday in Ikom
content:
The Minister of State for Industry, Trade and Investment, John Enoh, has urged Cross River residents to secure President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, warning that the state risks losing its place in national decision-making if it fails to support the President.

Enoh said this on Friday in Ikom during the inauguration of the Tinubu/Shettima Project Beyond 2027, a support group mobilising for the President’s re-election in the northern part of Cross River State.

He challenged the group to improve on Tinubu’s performance in the 2023 presidential election, when the President won seven of the state’s 18 local government areas.

“In 2023, out of 18 local government areas, the President won seven. In 2027, we must leave here with a determination that Mr President is going to win 18 over 18 in Cross River. And that is possible,” he said.

The minister argued that the state needed to remain politically aligned with the ruling administration to retain its relevance in national affairs.

Enoh also compared Tinubu’s leadership to that of Singapore’s former Prime Minister, Lee Kuan Yew, whom he credited with transforming the Asian country through pragmatic leadership and good governance.

“I likened President Bola Tinubu to a one-time Prime Minister of Singapore, Lee Kuan Yew. Singapore became a top-notch country from nowhere because of the pragmatic leadership and good governance of that Prime Minister.

“Lee Kuan Yew did not look at politics the way a politician looks at the next election, but at the next generation. That is what President Bola Tinubu is doing. President Bola Tinubu is looking at the next generation, not the next election,” he said.

Defending the President’s economic policies, Enoh recalled the economic conditions Tinubu inherited when he assumed office in 2023.

He claimed that Nigeria’s net foreign reserves were below $1bn at the time, international transactions using Nigerian ATM cards were failing, and letters of credit could not be honoured.

According to him, Tinubu took difficult decisions on his first day in office out of concern for Nigerians and future generations.

“There is no doubt that those decisions may have affected us adversely because of the hardship people have had to go through. But like a bitter tablet that cures sickness, after that bitterness, you will get well. Three and a half years later, recovery has started and stability has set in,” he said.

Enoh said the administration’s next priority was to improve prosperity, Nigerians’ purchasing power and the cost of goods and services.

He also claimed that inflation had fallen to about 14 per cent from the high levels recorded when Tinubu assumed office, adding that the President was determined to reduce it to single digits.

“I am aware that there are market women here, people who go to market every day and experience the pain. Mr President is determined to take inflation to single digits,” he said.

The minister urged the support group to take the administration’s reform message to wards and communities across Cross River, insisting that the state could not afford to remain in opposition after the 2027 election.

title: 2027: We’re not joining your opposition coalition, PDP tells Lukman
description:
…Snubs November 30 summit, declares Wike’s Rainbow alliance its only coalition



By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja



The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has rejected claims that it has joined the opposition Coalition for Democracy being promoted by former National Vice Chairman of the All Progressives C
content:
…Snubs November 30 summit, declares Wike’s Rainbow alliance its only coalition

By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja

The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has rejected claims that it has joined the opposition Coalition for Democracy being promoted by former National Vice Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Salihu Lukman, declaring that it will not attend the coalition’s November 30 summit.

The party said it had not entered into any alliance with the coalition, authorised anyone to represent it at the summit or agreed to be bound by any decision taken in its name. It maintained that its only recognised coalition arrangement was the Rainbow Coalition, backed by its National Leader, Nyesom Wike.

The position was contained in a statement signed by the PDP National Publicity Secretary, Hon. Jungudo Haruna Mohammed, who said those being presented as the party’s representatives were expelled members with no authority to speak or act on its behalf.

Jungudo said the individuals’ claims to the party’s leadership and representation had suffered defeats at the Federal High Court, Court of Appeal and Supreme Court.

He added that the courts had issued orders restraining Kabiru Tanimu Turaki, SAN, and his associates from parading themselves as PDP leaders, while imposing financial penalties exceeding N100 million over alleged abuses of court processes and frivolous litigation.

Questioning Lukman’s continued engagement with the individuals, Jungudo said, “It is therefore astonishing that Mr Salihu Lukman, who ought to be sufficiently informed about the legal status and recognised leadership of the PDP, would continue to engage these individuals and use them as a basis for associating the party with his so-called Toronto Coalition.”

Describing the proposed arrangement as a political project built on misrepresentation, the PDP declared it ‘dead on arrival’, particularly because those being presented as its representatives lacked the authority to speak on its behalf.

The party also threatened legal action against Lukman, his associates and other promoters of the Coalition for Democracy if they continued to use its name and institutional identity in their political activities.

“The party will not hesitate to pursue appropriate legal action against any person or group that continues to unlawfully associate the PDP with this arrangement,” Jungudo warned.

Reiterating its position, the party said the Rainbow Coalition, in line with Wike’s political direction and directives, remained its only recognised coalition arrangement.

It consequently urged Nigerians, political stakeholders, members and supporters, as well as media organisations, to disregard reports linking its national headquarters at Wadata Plaza, Abuja, to the November 30 summit or any other political arrangement being promoted by Lukman and his associates.

“The PDP will not allow its identity to be hijacked, its institutional authority misrepresented or its political interests compromised by individuals who have no mandate to speak or act on its behalf,” Jungudo said.

The party maintained that it would not be bound by any resolution or commitment purportedly made in its name by the promoters of the coalition.

title: Open defecation: Lagos urges banks, eateries to open toilets to public
description:
The Lagos State Government has urged banks, eateries and filling stations to make their toilet facilities accessible to members of the public as part of efforts to improve access to safe and hygienic sanitation across the state.
The Special Adviser to the Governor on Environment, Olakunle Rotimi-Ako
content:
The Lagos State Government has urged banks, eateries and filling stations to make their toilet facilities accessible to members of the public as part of efforts to improve access to safe and hygienic sanitation across the state.

The Special Adviser to the Governor on Environment, Olakunle Rotimi-Akodu, made the appeal at the 2026 World Toilet Day celebration held at ASSBIFI House, Alausa.

The Director of Public Affairs, Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources, Kunle Adeshina, disclosed this in a statement on Saturday.

“He specifically encouraged commercial establishments, including banks, eateries and filling stations, to make their restroom facilities accessible to members of the public, noting that such partnerships would complement government efforts and expand access to decent toilet facilities in busy urban communities,” the statement read.

Speaking on the theme, ‘Sanitation and Gender Equality,’ Rotimi-Akodu said access to safe and hygienic toilets was not merely an infrastructure or environmental issue but a fundamental component of human dignity, personal security and social inclusion.

He noted that inadequate sanitation disproportionately affected women and girls, exposing them to insecurity, harassment and challenges associated with menstrual hygiene management.

The special adviser said the absence of safe, private and hygienic toilets in schools, workplaces, markets, transport terminals and healthcare facilities could undermine women’s confidence, school attendance, economic productivity and general well-being.

“Genuine gender equality cannot be achieved without addressing the structural inequalities that limit access to adequate sanitation,” he said.

Rotimi-Akodu disclosed that Lagos had more than 1,769 functional public toilet facilities, while the state government was constructing 200 public toilets and 80 bathrooms, alongside 100 urinals and 160 handwashing basins across its five divisions.

He said the facilities formed part of the government’s roadmap towards achieving an Open Defecation-Free Lagos.

The special adviser stressed that public toilets must meet standards of safety, accessibility, privacy, cleanliness and gender responsiveness, with special consideration for women, children, older persons and people living with disabilities.

title: Police Probe Alleged Attack On Edo NDC Secretariat, Invite Owan East Chairman
description: The Edo State Police Command has commenced an investigation into an alleged attack on the National Democratic Congress (NDC) Secretariat in Afuze, Owan East Local Government Area, by armed men suspected to be members of the Edo State Security Network.The incident reportedly occurred on Wednesday, No
content:
The Edo State Police Command has commenced an investigation into an alleged attack on the National Democratic Congress (NDC) Secretariat in Afuze, Owan East Local Government Area, by armed men suspected to be members of the Edo State Security Network.

The incident reportedly occurred on Wednesday, November 19, at about 4 p.m., when NDC political aspirants, Mariam Iseme and Professor Grant Eruhagan, were holding a meeting with other party members at the secretariat.

According to the Police Public Relations Officer, Edo State Command, ASP Eno Ikoedem, the armed men, dressed in security network uniforms and wielding guns and machetes, stormed the premises, destroyed political banners and other materials, and threatened to kill the occupants before fleeing upon sighting the police.

Ikoedem said the command had commenced efforts to identify, locate and apprehend those involved, adding that the Chairman of Owan East Local Government Area, Hon. Ernest Oyaole Aitalegbe, had also been invited to assist the ongoing investigation.

The Commissioner of Police, CP Patrick Daaor, warned politicians, aspirants, supporters and their loyalists against violence, intimidation, destruction of property and the use of thugs to advance political interests.

He stressed that the command would not tolerate political lawlessness, warning that anyone found sponsoring, perpetrating or aiding acts of violence would be arrested and prosecuted, irrespective of political affiliation or status.

The police commissioner urged political actors to desist from actions capable of disrupting public peace, assuring that the command would enforce the law without fear or favour.

title: Oyo allied health workers suspend strike, resume Monday
description:
The Nigerian Union of Allied Health Professionals, Oyo State Hospital Management Board (OYSHMB) chapter, has suspended its ongoing industrial action for two weeks.
The suspension takes effect from 11:59 p.m. on November 22, while work resumes on the morning of November 23, according to NAN on Saturd
content:
The Nigerian Union of Allied Health Professionals, Oyo State Hospital Management Board (OYSHMB) chapter, has suspended its ongoing industrial action for two weeks.

The suspension takes effect from 11:59 p.m. on November 22, while work resumes on the morning of November 23, according to NAN on Saturday.

The News Agency of Nigeria recalls that the allied health professionals embarked on an indefinite strike on October 28.

Among the union’s demands are the “payment of teaching allowance to members, implementation of skipping of CONHESS 10 as applicable to GL 11, and restoration of call duty allowance for dental therapists.”

Others include the “promotion of some Medical Laboratory Scientists and Radiographers who were denied promotion, and implementation of ward coat/lab coat allowance for members.”

The demands also include a review of the operational guidelines to accommodate members in management and other major committees in government hospitals across the state.

The decision was contained in an official communique issued after a meeting held on Thursday between the executive members of NUAHP OYSHMB and representatives of the Oyo State Government.

The communique, signed by the NUAHP OYSHMB Chairman, Olanrewaju Ajani; the General Secretary, Kayode Oyediran; and the Public Relations Officer, Olatunde Fatola, was made available to NAN on Saturday in Ibadan.

According to the communique, government representatives at the meeting included the Head of Service, the Commissioner for Establishment and Training, permanent secretaries, and representatives of OYSHMB and the State Ministry of Health (SMOH).

The union said government representatives appealed for the suspension of the ongoing industrial action, assuring it of concrete steps towards addressing its grievances and demands.

It said that, “after due consultation, deliberation and consideration of the government’s appeal, the union resolved to suspend the ongoing strike for an initial period of two weeks.”

The union said the” period would serve as an opportunity for the government to demonstrate its commitment through tangible actions towards resolving the issues raised.”

It added that, at the expiration of the two-week period, it would review the level of implementation and determine its next line of action.

(NAN)

title: AI-generated fake content threatens national security – Ex-FPRO
description:
A former Force Public Relations Officer, Olumuyiwa Adejobi, has warned that the misuse of artificial intelligence and social media to spread fake news poses a growing threat to Nigeria’s national security.
Adejobi, a Deputy Commissioner of Police in charge of Operations at the Delta State Police Com
content:
A former Force Public Relations Officer, Olumuyiwa Adejobi, has warned that the misuse of artificial intelligence and social media to spread fake news poses a growing threat to Nigeria’s national security.

Adejobi, a Deputy Commissioner of Police in charge of Operations at the Delta State Police Command, said fabricated images, videos, audio recordings and narratives could mislead the public, provoke hostility, incite violence and undermine confidence in public institutions.

He gave the warning in a statement titled, “The Palongo Dance of Social Media Palava,” issued in Lagos on Saturday, urging Nigerians to exercise caution and communicate responsibly on digital platforms.

The former police spokesperson expressed concern about the growing ability of artificial intelligence to make people appear to have said or done things they never did.

According to him, such fabricated content could have serious consequences for public safety and national security.

“Fabricated content can provoke hostility, incite violence, create panic and undermine public confidence in institutions,” he said.

Adejobi also blamed the monetisation of social media for encouraging some content creators to prioritise views, engagement and financial rewards over accuracy and responsibility.

He said some influencers resorted to sensational headlines, unverified allegations and provocative publications without considering the consequences for individuals, institutions and the country.

“Freedom of expression must be exercised responsibly and should not be used to fabricate information, destroy reputations, incite violence or deliberately mislead the public,” he said.

He urged Nigerians to verify information before believing, sharing or reposting it, describing fact-checking as a civic responsibility in the digital age.

Adejobi commended the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, for recently urging the public to remain vigilant against fake news and irresponsible information dissemination.

He also acknowledged the efforts of former Minister of Information and National Orientation, Lai Mohammed, and the incumbent minister, Mohammed Idris, in drawing attention to the dangers of misinformation and disinformation.

The former police spokesman called for sustained public enlightenment, strategic communication, institutional collaboration and appropriate regulatory measures to address the problem.

He, however, warned against allowing regulation to undermine constitutionally guaranteed freedoms, stressing that legitimate criticism and dissent must be distinguished from deliberate fabrication, impersonation and incitement.

Adejobi advocated a whole-of-society approach involving government institutions, security agencies, media organisations, technology companies, professional bodies, traditional and religious leaders, civil society groups and citizens.

Recalling his personal experience with misinformation and social media manipulation, he said false narratives could cause emotional and reputational damage that might take years to repair.

He warned that fabricated stories could be created within seconds, while the damage they caused could persist for years.

Adejobi urged Nigerians to promote digital literacy, ethical journalism, responsible content creation, fact-checking and constructive public engagement.

He said social media should serve as a platform for enlightenment, innovation, accountability, economic advancement and national development rather than hatred, hostility and destruction.

He also appealed to Nigerians not to “dance Palongo”, a Yoruba expression he said his grandmother used to describe an irregular and disorderly dance.

He urged citizens to reject digital recklessness and embrace truth, responsibility, civility and patriotism.

“Protect the country’s collective destiny from misinformation and manipulation. Nigeria is bigger than our individual interests, political affiliations, personal grievances and social media engagements,” he said.

NAN

title: The Governor, The Candidate And The Voter
description: Anambra puts the power of endorsements to the test, while opposition negotiations and election safeguards face approaching deadlines.On Thursday in Awka, Governor Chukwuma Soludo presented APGA’s flag to Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who received it on behalf of President Bola Tinubu.On Frid
content:
Anambra puts the power of endorsements to the test, while opposition negotiations and election safeguards face approaching deadlines.

On Thursday in Awka, Governor Chukwuma Soludo presented APGA’s flag to Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who received it on behalf of President Bola Tinubu.

On Friday, Peter Obi took his campaign through Onitsha, attracting supporters ahead of his town hall engagement.

Two neighbouring cities offered competing pictures of political strength.

In Awka, the message was partnership with the centre. In Onitsha, Obi demonstrated his continuing ability to mobilise in the state he once governed.

The electoral question lies between those pictures: how far can a governor’s endorsement move presidential votes, and how effectively can a candidate convert personal loyalty into turnout?

Anambra will help answer both.

Soludo’s Wager

APGA’s support gives Tinubu an organised partner outside the APC. Soludo is making an argument about the South-East’s place in national politics: that cooperation with the President offers a route to influence and development. The presentation reaffirmed APGA’s presidential alignment while the party continues pursuing its own interests in other elections.

For Tinubu, the opportunity lies in improving his reach through a political organisation rooted in the state.

For Soludo, the challenge is to persuade people who support his governorship to make the same choice in a presidential contest.

Those loyalties need not coincide. Voters can approve of a governor’s performance and prefer another presidential candidate. They can also reconsider a previous choice if a new alliance offers a convincing case.

The evidence will emerge through sustained mobilisation, local organisation and ultimately the ballot. A flag presentation establishes an endorsement. It cannot establish the electorate’s response.

Obi’s Home-State Test

Obi’s Onitsha road show supplies evidence of campaign activity and visible support. It does not, on its own, measure the balance of opinion across Anambra.

His task is to maintain that support while building sufficient reach elsewhere.

The home-state contest also brings his governing record into sharper focus. Obi has chosen to defend that record publicly; Soludo is advancing a different argument about Anambra’s political interests.

Voters deserve an exchange grounded in verifiable achievements, present needs and credible proposals. Claims that cooperation necessarily delivers prosperity or that popular enthusiasm guarantees victory require testing.

Anambra’s significance extends beyond its presidential tally. It offers a clear case study in the relationship between party machinery, a governor’s influence and a candidate’s personal following.

Opposition Unity Loses Another Week

The Coalition for Democracy has postponed its second summit from November 23 to November 30, citing member parties’ campaign schedules. The organisers say participating parties have agreed to suspend campaign activities on the new date so their leaders can attend.

The explanation is plausible. Presidential candidates have demanding itineraries.

The political cost is time.

Every week spent negotiating leaves less time to explain an agreement, reconcile local interests and organise around it. The postponement also illustrates the coalition’s central difficulty: its members are campaigning separately while trying to determine how they should cooperate.

That does not make the undertaking futile. Cooperation on electoral integrity, campaign freedoms and policy priorities could have value even without one presidential ticket.

But the summit’s eventual significance will depend on the obligations it creates. Who signs? Who is authorised to commit each party? What work begins immediately afterward?

For the ADC, NDC, APM, SDP, PRP and participating PDP representatives, attendance will be the first test. Implementation will be the more demanding one.

ADC: A Clearer INEC Position, an Unresolved Appeal

Fresh reporting provides an important update on INEC’s handling of the ADC leadership dispute.

National Commissioner Mohammed Haruna told The PUNCH that INEC had been served notice of the appeal and would await the appellate court’s decision before determining its next course of action. The rival Nafiu Gombe-led faction continues pressing for implementation of the Federal High Court judgment.

That reported administrative position offers greater clarity. It does not amount to an appellate victory for the Mark-led leadership.

A separate ruling today also requires precision. The Federal High Court rejected Atiku and the ADC’s application to amend their suit challenging Tinubu’s eligibility. The judge directed the parties to proceed with the substantive case. The ruling on the amendment should therefore not be described as a final determination of the underlying eligibility dispute.

For the ADC, the practical challenge remains sustaining a nationwide campaign while litigation demands attention and resources.

The Technology Debate Needs Answers

Atiku has asked INEC to permit independent scrutiny of its proposed use of artificial intelligence in processing polling-unit results. His petition seeks disclosure, audit arrangements and clear procedures for reviewing results flagged by the system.

The demand raises questions that deserve public answers. It does not establish that manipulation has occurred.

INEC should explain what the proposed technology does, where human decisions enter the process and how errors would be challenged and corrected.

The approaching November 28 mock exercise gives those explanations urgency. Public confidence would benefit from published test findings and an account of any corrective work required.

A successful demonstration should allow parties, observers and citizens to understand how the system behaves when something goes wrong, as well as when it works.

State Police: A Reform With Electoral Weight

Security reform has also advanced. Reporting this week says the state police constitutional alteration bill has been transmitted for presidential assent, while a separate operational framework remains necessary.

This is politically consequential because security is both a public demand and a question of institutional power.

Supporters see the prospect of policing closer to communities. Concerns about governors’ influence make safeguards central to the proposal’s credibility.

The campaign debate should examine funding, appointments, complaints, oversight and protection against partisan deployment. Passage of a reform and the creation of an effective service are distinct milestones.

What Changed This Week?

APC/Tinubu: The Anambra gathering reinforced the cross-party campaign strategy. Its value depends on whether APGA’s organisation and Soludo’s advocacy persuade additional presidential voters.

NDC/Obi-Kwankwaso: Friday’s Onitsha activity demonstrated mobilisation in Obi’s home state. National viability still depends on reach, organisation and turnout beyond familiar strongholds.

ADC/Atiku: INEC’s reported decision to await the appeal provides administrative clarity, while the underlying legal uncertainty continues.

APM/Makinde and other opposition partners: The revised summit date preserves the cooperation process but compresses the time available to implement any agreement.

The competitive position cannot responsibly be reduced to rally photographs, endorsements or partisan state-by-state predictions. No fresh, credible national polling reviewed for this edition establishes a decisive swing.

Recent local and off-cycle contests remain useful indicators when assessed alongside turnout, competitiveness and local circumstances. Their results should inform presidential analysis without becoming automatic forecasts.

Participation Must Carry Responsibility and Influence

At its South-South youth engagement this week, INEC urged young Nigerians to reject violence, manipulation, hate speech and misinformation. That is a relevant intervention as campaign tensions rise.

Political parties carry responsibilities too. They should give young members meaningful roles, protect volunteers and hold organisers accountable for misconduct.

The technology debate offers another opening. Young Nigerians with relevant expertise can contribute to independent observation, voter education and scrutiny of publicly disclosed systems.

Their economic questions remain equally pressing: access to work, education, affordable enterprise and reliable services. Those concerns need measurable answers from every campaign.

Youth Metre assessment: Campaign participation and institutional confidence deserve close attention; no verified age-specific evidence reviewed this week establishes a shift in candidate preference.

  • Any appellate ruling or formal INEC statement concerning the ADC.
  • Test procedures and public reporting arrangements for November 28.
  • Confirmation of authorised participants and commitments for the November 30 summit.
  • Evidence of local organisation following the Anambra campaign events.
  • The status of presidential assent and operational safeguards for state policing.

This week’s politics turns on the distance between an endorsement and a vote, an agreement and its implementation, a reform and its results.

The campaigns that close those gaps will have the strongest case to take to the electorate.

EDITORIAL NOTE

Political Signals is an independent weekly political analysis produced for Channels Television. It examines political developments, personalities and electoral trends without endorsement of any political party or candidate. Its assessments are based on publicly available evidence and may change as events and evidence develop.

title: Gov Soludo Approves N50,000 December Bonus For Anambra Workers
description: Anambra State Governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo, has approved an additional payment of fifty thousand naira for state civil servants as a December bonus. The payment, which will be reflected in workers’ December 2026 salaries, is part of the government’s efforts to support workers amid
content:
Anambra State Governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo, has approved an additional payment of fifty thousand naira for state civil servants as a December bonus. The payment, which will be reflected in workers’ December 2026 salaries, is part of the government’s efforts to support workers amid the current economic challenges.

The governor announced the approval during the 2026 Public Service Day celebration at the Jerome Udoji State Secretariat Complex in Awka.

Speaking at the event, Governor Soludo acknowledged that workers’ salaries were not enough to meet their needs under the prevailing economic conditions. He, however, assured them that his administration would only make financial commitments it could sustain.

He said, “The pay that we have all over is not enough; I clearly understand it. But there is one thing I also want to tell you, and that is I don’t play to the wind. Before we get into a commitment, we make sure that it is something that we will always honour.”

Beyond the financial bonus, the governor also approved three requests presented by the workers to improve conditions at the state secretariat.

They include the rehabilitation of roads within the complex, the establishment of an Information and Communication Technology Centre and the pruning of overgrown trees.

He also urged civil servants to consider the revenue base and financial capacity of individual states when comparing salaries and welfare packages.

Earlier, the Anambra State Head of Service, Mrs. Ngozi Iwouno, commended the governor for improving security across the state, saying civil servants could now report to work regularly without fear.

She noted that the disruption previously caused by Monday sit-at-home orders had been overcome, allowing workers to carry out their duties more consistently.

The celebration also featured the recognition of outstanding public servants and presentations to winners of the ministries’ novelty football competition.

title: Young Protesters Hit Streets Across Europe
description: Protesters rallied across Europe on Friday to vent anger over issues from high living costs to military spending and the climate crisis, ramping up pressure on political leaders they accuse of ignoring the concerns of young people.Demonstrators hit the streets in cities from Italy to Germany, Switze
content:
Protesters rallied across Europe on Friday to vent anger over issues from high living costs to military spending and the climate crisis, ramping up pressure on political leaders they accuse of ignoring the concerns of young people.

Demonstrators hit the streets in cities from Italy to Germany, Switzerland and Britain, many waving signs emblazoned with “fight for our future”, setting off flares and burning cardboard models of tanks.

The rallies, coordinated by a youth-led coalition of over 50 groups, are fuelled by grievances that vary from place to place, including Israel’s war in Gaza, high rents and deteriorating learning conditions at schools and universities.

But a common theme runs through them — a sense that governments across the continent are too busy with geopolitical crises and helping big business, and not investing enough in the well-being of younger generations.

Olivia Ferrario, an 18-year-old high school student at a protest in the Italian city of Milan, told AFP that young people were displaying their “dynamism and determination” by taking to the streets.

“If the government does not listen to us, we cannot remain silent,” she said at the demonstration that attracted tens of thousands of protesters.

Police deployed in large numbers due to fears of a repeat of the street violence that has marred recent major protests in France and other countries.

‘Lost So Much Hope’

In Switzerland, organisers claimed that more than 40,000 protesters had taken to the streets nationwide.

“Austerity is social violence,” read a banner in Lausanne, while another blared: “Be vegan, but eat the rich.”

The demonstrations were mostly peaceful. But a small number of people clashed with police after it ended, resulting in the deployment of tear gas and water cannon, the domestic Keystone-ATS news agency reported.

In Berlin, about 1,000 university students and school pupils protested over concerns including Germany’s rapid rearmament, which has stoked fears of a return to compulsory military service.

“I simply think it’s indefensible… to force someone to learn how to fight and kill, and then send them to war,” Helena Kossatz, 18, who finished high school last year, told AFP.

While Europe seeks to rearm in the face of a hostile Russia, organisers of the continent-wide protests say funds allocated to rearmament should be spent on education, youth policies and housing.

Several hundred protesters, some in school uniform, gathered at demonstrations in London outside parliament and in nearby Trafalgar Square, waving placards that said “save higher education” and “Fight for our futures not their wars”.

“I’ve lost so much hope,” Eliz, who had taken the day off from college and gave only one name, told AFP.

The 18-year-old said she was unsure whether she would go to university, “because of money. Because most jobs are getting taken over by AI. Everyone’s just kind of more depressed”.

There were scuffles between groups of right-wing and anti-fascist demonstrators, and AFP saw a handful of arrests.

Chants of “Palestine will live forever” rang out at the London protests, and Palestinian flags were on display at several of the demonstrations across Europe.

In Rome, high school students marched behind a banner that read: “We will take freedom if no one gives it to us — against the government, the war and the high cost of living.”

There were scuffles in the Italian capital, with some protesters throwing bottles and smoke bombs at police.

‘Dreadful’ Schools

Demonstrators called for more funding for education and railed against increased military spending during protests in the Spanish capital Madrid.

Gabriela Gimeno Serrano, a 16-year-old high school student, said there were 33 students in her class with just one teacher.

“Classrooms are very small, the facilities are in an absolutely dreadful state,” she told AFP, adding some schools were even plagued by rats and cockroaches.

Protests are set to extend into the weekend, with trade unions and housing associations calling for further demonstrations.

The protests come around the anniversary of the Yellow Vests movement in France, which rattled President Emmanuel Macron in 2018 and 2019. Demonstrations are planned there on Saturday.

The protests in European countries have in part been inspired by recent demonstrations in France, which have sometimes turned violent.

Those began when students demonstrated at high schools in mid-September to demand better learning conditions, fuelling a nationwide campaign against soaring prices, inadequate public services and police brutality.

AFP

The Sultan described the anniversary as a significant m
content:
The Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, has congratulated the Oba of Benin, Oba Ewuare II, on his 10th coronation anniversary, commending his leadership and commitment to cultural preservation, peacebuilding and national unity.

The Sultan described the anniversary as a significant milestone marking a decade of traditional leadership and dedication to the progress and well-being of the Benin Kingdom and its people.

In a statement issued on Saturday by Prince Bashir Adefaka, for the Sultan’s Media Team, Abubakar praised the monarch for upholding the cultural heritage, traditions and historical identity of the Benin Kingdom.

He also commended Oba Ewuare II for promoting peaceful coexistence, mutual respect and unity among Nigerians across ethnic, religious and cultural divides.

The Sultan noted that traditional institutions remained indispensable to national cohesion, the promotion of moral values, community development and peaceful coexistence, particularly at a time when Nigeria needed the collective wisdom and leadership of traditional rulers to address its challenges.

He said the Oba’s 10-year reign had reinforced the importance of traditional institutions as custodians of history, culture, values and the aspirations of their people.

According to him, the Benin monarch has also continued to serve as a rallying point for unity, stability and development.

Abubakar, who is physically present in Benin City for the anniversary celebration, expressed delight at being part of the historic occasion.

He said his presence demonstrated the enduring bonds of brotherhood, friendship and mutual respect among traditional rulers in Nigeria, irrespective of ethnic and regional differences.

The Sultan prayed for continued good health, wisdom, strength and long life for Oba Ewuare II, urging divine guidance for the monarch as he leads the Benin Kingdom towards greater peace, prosperity and development.

He also prayed for sustained peace and progress in the Benin Kingdom, Edo State and Nigeria.

title: IG appoints female AIG to oversee Bayelsa, Rivers
description:
The Nigeria Police Force has appointed Assistant Inspector-General of Police (AIG) Regina Udoette as the new Zonal Commander of Zone 16, comprising Bayelsa and Rivers states, making her the first female officer to occupy the position.
Udoette’s appointment followed the retirement of the immediate pa
content:
The Nigeria Police Force has appointed Assistant Inspector-General of Police (AIG) Regina Udoette as the new Zonal Commander of Zone 16, comprising Bayelsa and Rivers states, making her the first female officer to occupy the position.

Udoette’s appointment followed the retirement of the immediate past Zonal Commander, AIG Abubakar Zubairu.

The appointment was approved by the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Disu, who named the senior police officer to take over the leadership of the zone.

A Saturday statement issued by the Zonal Police Public Relations Officer, SP Gunn Emonena, said the new AIG was from Ifuho village in Ikot Ekpene Local Government Area of Akwa Ibom State.

According to the statement, Udoette was commissioned into the Nigeria Police Force as a Cadet Assistant Superintendent of Police in 1992.

She holds a Bachelor of Arts degree in Communication Arts and a master’s degree from the University of Uyo.

The statement described her as an experienced police officer who had served in various departments and capacities across different levels of the Nigeria Police Force.

Before her appointment as the Zonal Commander, she was the Commissioner of Police in charge of General Investigation at the Force Criminal Investigation Department (FCID), Enugu Annex.

The statement noted that her wealth of experience in policing would be brought to bear in the administration and security operations of the zone.

It said, “The Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, has appointed AIG Regina Cosmas Udoette to take over the mantle of leadership of Zone 16 following the retirement of AIG Abubakar Zubairu.”

On her professional background, the statement added that “the new AIG was commissioned into the Nigeria Police Force as a Cadet ASP in 1992.”

It further stated that “the first female AIG has served in various departments at different capacities, in all strata of the Force.”

Highlighting her most recent assignment, the statement said she “last served as Commissioner of Police in charge of General Investigation in FCID Enugu Annex.”

The zonal headquarters called on residents, community leaders and other stakeholders in Bayelsa and Rivers states to support the new commander in the discharge of her responsibilities.

It solicited “the co-operation and support of the good people of Bayelsa and Rivers State to enable her bring to bear her vast wealth of experience in policing.”

title: HURIWA mourns Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
description:
The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) has mourned the death of Vanguard Online Editor, Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, describing his passing at the age of 44 as a major loss to the journalism profession and Nigeria’s media industry.



Ajasa reportedly died following a brief illness.
content:
The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) has mourned the death of Vanguard Online Editor, Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, describing his passing at the age of 44 as a major loss to the journalism profession and Nigeria’s media industry.

Ajasa reportedly died following a brief illness.

In a condolence statement issued on Thursday, November 19, 2026, HURIWA’s National Coordinator, Comrade Emmanuel Nnadozie Onwubiko, said the journalist died at a time when his experience, creativity and digital expertise were still needed in the media industry.

The association described his death as particularly painful, noting that he belonged to a generation of journalists who successfully combined traditional journalistic values with the demands of digital journalism, online storytelling and editorial management.

HURIWA said Ajasa’s professional career began in photojournalism at National Mirror before he moved into editorial and digital leadership roles at Vanguard, TheNewsGuru and Pulse.

It described his career progression as a reflection of his dedication, versatility and commitment to the development of Nigerian journalism.

The association noted that his return to Vanguard in 2022 as Online Editor demonstrated the confidence reposed in his professional competence, experience and ability to contribute to newsroom development.

HURIWA extended its condolences to the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the Ajasa family, friends, colleagues and professional associates, urging them to draw strength from the positive impact he made during his lifetime.

The association also drew attention to the pressures and emotional demands of journalism, noting that media professionals often work under intense deadlines and challenging circumstances to keep the public informed.

While acknowledging that words might not adequately ease the pain of his loss, HURIWA urged the bereaved family to take solace in the legacy Ajasa left behind and the lives he touched through his professional and personal relationships.

The association prayed for the peaceful repose of his soul and asked God to grant his family, Vanguard management and the journalism community the strength to bear the loss.

The post HURIWA mourns Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: India probes suspected liquor poisoning as 11 die
description:
The Indian government has ordered an investigation into suspected illicit alcohol consumption that has killed at least 11 people and left hundreds hospitalised in Manipur State, northeast India.
The death toll and number of hospital admissions varied across reports by Indian media outlets on Saturda
content:
The Indian government has ordered an investigation into suspected illicit alcohol consumption that has killed at least 11 people and left hundreds hospitalised in Manipur State, northeast India.

The death toll and number of hospital admissions varied across reports by Indian media outlets on Saturday, with some reporting as many as 15 deaths and more than 300 people hospitalised.

The Indian Express reported that at least 11 people had died, while more than 300 were hospitalised in Imphal after consuming suspected spurious liquor in Chandel district.

The Times of India, however, reported 12 deaths and more than 180 hospitalisations, while India Today put the death toll at 15, with over 180 people hospitalised between November 18 and 20.

The Economic Times, citing the Press Trust of India, reported that 13 people had died by 9pm on Friday, while 346 patients had been admitted to hospitals over suspected methanol poisoning.

Manipur Chief Minister, Yumnam Khemchand Singh, said he visited Shija Hospital in Lamphelpat and Babina Hospital in Sajiwa on Friday to assess the condition of those receiving treatment.

In a post on X, the Chief Minister said, “Over 140 patients were admitted to Shija Hospital and over 41 patients at Babina Hospital. The death toll has touched 11 during the last 48 hours.”

He added that the patients were receiving medical evaluation and treatment under the supervision of doctors.

The Chief Minister also said a medical team led by a specialist in general medicine, alongside essential medicines, had been sent to Chandel district to strengthen the response.

He said, “I wished the patients a speedy and full recovery and extend my heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families of the deceased. The government will conduct an enquiry and the culprits will be punished.”

Meanwhile, the Chandel district administration said the exact cause of the deaths had not been medically and scientifically established and remained under investigation.

The Times of India quoted Chandel Superintendent of Police, Dharmendra Kumar, as saying that the liquor reportedly consumed by the victims was purchased from Sugnu in neighbouring Kakching district.

He was also quoted as saying there was “no known local brewing or manufacturing of traditional or local wine in Chandel district.”

The district administration issued a public health advisory warning residents against consuming locally brewed liquor or alcohol of doubtful origin.

India Today reported that the victims were mainly from five villages in the Chakpikarong subdivision of Chandel district.

The suspected poisoning has raised concerns over the circulation of illicit alcoholic drinks, although authorities have yet to confirm the precise substance responsible for the deaths.

title: US Agriculture Department, FBI Breached By Hackers
description: The US Agriculture Department and the FBI were breached by hackers in cyberattacks, US media reported on Friday, as concerns deepened over the recent spate of tech outages at key American institutions.The incidents were first reported by NBC News and CNN respectively, and it remained unclear whether
content:
The US Agriculture Department and the FBI were breached by hackers in cyberattacks, US media reported on Friday, as concerns deepened over the recent spate of tech outages at key American institutions.

The incidents were first reported by NBC News and CNN respectively, and it remained unclear whether they were related and who was responsible.

Major outages in recent weeks have disrupted travel, communications and e-commerce for countless users across the United States, even affecting a top-secret network at the National Security Agency.

US President Donald Trump has sought to calm the public and urged people to “relax”, while officials said the various outages were not linked to criminal activity.

The US Department of Agriculture (USDA) told employees that a system used to facilitate payments to farmers was targeted in a cyberattack, NBC reported on Friday, citing two former USDA officials.

The hackers may use the payments system as a backdoor to access more sensitive material, the former officials told NBC.

The USDA deals with “a bunch of scary biologic issues” and “if an adversary or a competitor were to have access to that same information… they could use our own research against us,” a former official was quoted as saying.

CNN said separately on Friday that the FBI was hacked for the second time since September.

The federal agency was investigating an intrusion of the National Crime Information Center (NCIC) by apparent hackers, CNN reported, citing two people briefed on the probe.

The NCIC has a nationwide criminal information database linking federal, state and local law enforcement and is used to share information on warrants and background checks.

“Every day, officers across the country rely on NCIC to identify wanted fugitives, check for outstanding warrants, and access information that can directly impact officer and public safety,” a former FBI official told CNN.

The former official expressed concerns that hackers “could compromise the accuracy of the information that officers rely on.”

AFP has contacted the FBI and USDA for comment.

The newly uncovered breaches at the FBI and USDA were described as hacks, which are different from outages like the ones that afflicted Microsoft Outlook and the Federal Aviation Administration.

In September, a hacking group known as ShinyHunters targeted sensitive employee personal data from an FBI jobs website.

The White House fired cybersecurity chief Sean Cairncross this week as criticism mounted over the string of major outages.

AFP

title: AI, fake news threaten Nigeria’s security – Ex-police PRO
description:
DCP Olumuyiwa Adejobi, a former Nigeria Police Force Public Relations Officer (FPRO), has warned that the misuse of social media and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to spread fake news threatens national security.



He gave the warning in a statement titled “The Palongo Dance of Social Media Palava”,
content:
DCP Olumuyiwa Adejobi, a former Nigeria Police Force Public Relations Officer (FPRO), has warned that the misuse of social media and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to spread fake news threatens national security.

He gave the warning in a statement titled “The Palongo Dance of Social Media Palava”, issued on Saturday in Lagos, urging Nigerians to communicate responsibly and exercise vigilance on digital platforms.

Adejobi, currently the Deputy Commissioner of Police in charge of Operations at the Delta State Police Command, described social media misuse as a growing threat to public order, national cohesion and security.

“Fabricated content can provoke hostility, incite violence, create panic and undermine public confidence in institutions,” he said.

The former FPRO expressed concern over the growing use of AI to generate fake images, videos, audio recordings and narratives capable of misleading the public.

According to him, the technology can make individuals appear to have said or done things they never did, with serious implications for public safety and national security.

Adejobi also blamed the monetisation of social media for encouraging some content creators to prioritise views, engagements and financial rewards over truth and responsibility.

“Some influencers resorted to sensational headlines, unverified allegations and provocative publications without considering their consequences for individuals, institutions and the country.

“Freedom of expression must be exercised responsibly and should not be used to fabricate information, destroy reputations, incite violence or deliberately mislead the public, ” he said.

He urged Nigerians to verify information before believing, sharing or reposting it, describing verification as a civic responsibility in the digital age.

The former spokesperson commended the Inspector-General of Police, Mr Olatunji Disu, for recently urging the public to remain vigilant against fake news and irresponsible information dissemination.

He also acknowledged the efforts of former Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mr Lai Mohammed, and the incumbent minister, Mr Mohammed Idris, in highlighting the dangers of misinformation and disinformation.

Adejobi called for sustained public enlightenment, strategic communication, institutional collaboration and appropriate regulatory measures to address the menace.

He, however, stressed the need to balance regulation with the protection of constitutionally guaranteed freedoms, noting that legitimate criticism and dissent must be distinguished from deliberate fabrication, impersonation and incitement.

The former image maker advocated a whole-of-society approach involving government institutions, security agencies, media organisations, technology companies, professional bodies, traditional and religious leaders, civil society groups and citizens.

Adejobi, who said he had personally experienced the consequences of misinformation and social media manipulation, said that false narratives could cause emotional and reputational damage that might take years to correct.

He warned that fabricated stories could be created within seconds, while the damage they caused could persist for years.

Adejobi urged Nigerians to promote digital literacy, ethical journalism, responsible content creation, fact-checking and constructive public engagement.

He said social media should serve as a platform for enlightenment, innovation, accountability, economic advancement and national development, rather than hatred, hostility and destruction.

Adejobi appealed to Nigerians not to “dance Palongo,” a Yoruba expression he said his grandmother used to describe an irregular and disorderly dance, urging citizens to reject digital recklessness and embrace truth, responsibility, civility and patriotism.

“Protect the country’s collective destiny from misinformation and manipulation, Nigeria is bigger than our individual interests, political affiliations, personal grievances and social media engagements,” he said. (NAN)

The post AI, fake news threaten Nigeria’s security – Ex-police PRO appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Fossil fuel row stalls COP31 climate deal
description:
The COP31 climate talks spilled into Saturday as countries raced to secure a deal after a draft text dropped all mention of fossil fuels, exposing deep divisions over how to tackle global warming.
Nearly 200 nations remained deadlocked after two weeks of grinding UN talks in Turkey, with negotiators
content:
The COP31 climate talks spilled into Saturday as countries raced to secure a deal after a draft text dropped all mention of fossil fuels, exposing deep divisions over how to tackle global warming.

Nearly 200 nations remained deadlocked after two weeks of grinding UN talks in Turkey, with negotiators working through the night after missing their scheduled Friday finish amid feuds over energy, science and finance.

Australia, which is presiding over the COP31 negotiations, raced against the clock to produce a third draft deal, with many delegates due to catch flights home.

“We are close to the finish line, but we are not there yet,” COP31 President Murat Kurum, who is Turkey’s environment minister, told an assembly late Friday that approved some technical matters.

Midway through his opening address, Kurum was forced to pause while a protester shouted “You are killing the future!” before being escorted from the hall.

Expectations of a major breakthrough have been low at COP31 as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran.

The summit follows a string of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal and Indonesia and unfolds as a super El Nino pattern amplifies the risk of further extreme weather.

A draft deal unveiled earlier this week called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels, a flashpoint at UN climate talks where producers such as Saudi Arabia have fiercely resisted such calls.

A second, pared-down draft released on Thursday stripped away all mentions of fossil fuels — sending negotiators rushing back to the bargaining table.

The European Union said the revised draft “risks turning this climate COP into a fossil summit”.

A dozen European and developing countries — from France to Panama and the Solomon Islands — released a letter Friday insisting that the deal include “a clear transition away from fossil fuels”.

Panama, which also signed the letter, threatened to walk away from the talks. The country’s environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, is a vocal critic of the climate negotiations, accusing a “petroleum mafia” of blocking progress.

Meanwhile, the OPEC oil cartel wrote on X that its head, Haitham Al Ghais, met Russian presidential climate envoy Ruslan Edelgeriev at COP31 to discuss “the importance of inclusive and balanced approaches across all multilateral environmental fora”.

• ‘Clean electrification’ –

Australia’s Climate Minister Chris Bowen, who shuttled between delegations to seek compromises, said Friday he would work “for as long as it takes, to get the job done”.

The draft “cover decision” proposes a target to electrify the global economy — a push to replace technologies that burn fossil fuels directly, like diesel cars and gas heating, with electric alternatives.

The goal is championed by COP31 hosts Turkey and Australia, who tout “electrification” as integral to tackling concerns over energy security and sluggish global progress in cutting heat-trapping emissions.

“Electrification is the key to transitioning away from fossil fuels,” said Bowen, who is chairing the negotiations.

The proposal calls for countries to boost the global share of final energy demand met by electricity to 35 percent by 2035.

But it does not specify that the additional electricity must come from renewables rather than coal or gas, spurring some countries to demand an explicitly “clean” target.

Some countries also rejected a proposal to ramp up carbon capture, dismissing it as a costly, unproven technology that could allow polluters to keep burning fossil fuels.

• $120 billion target –

Countries are sharply divided over a raft of other issues.

The timing of the next set of reports by the UN’s Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has been a major source of friction.

The latest draft expressed “deep concern” over the imminent breach of the 1.5C goal but dropped an earlier call to return warming below that threshold as soon as possible this century.

Negotiations are also deadlocked over long-running complaints by developing countries that rich nations are falling short in their obligations to help them confront climate change.

The removal of a $120 billion target for climate adaptation angered developing nations.

“We didn’t come here to beg,” said Ghana’s environment minister, Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings.

AFP

title: Why Nigeria is seeking stronger EU partnership to combat terrorism – Defence Minister
description:
Reveals Troops Intercepted Over 400 Starlinks Devices Linked to Terrorist Networks.



By: Kingsley Omonobi



The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (rtd), has reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to a comprehensive, whole-of-government strategy to combat terrorism, whil
content:
Reveals Troops Intercepted Over 400 Starlinks Devices Linked to Terrorist Networks.

By: Kingsley Omonobi

The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (rtd), has reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to a comprehensive, whole-of-government strategy to combat terrorism, while seeking stronger security cooperation with the European Union (EU).

Musa made this known at the third edition of the Schuman Security and Defence Forum held at the European Parliament in Brussels, Belgium, where he represented Nigeria.

Disclosing that the Armed Forces of Nigeria were deploying intelligence-led operations, advanced surveillance systems, unmanned aerial platforms and military artificial intelligence to weaken terrorist networks, the Minister told the gathering that troops of Operation Hadin Kai intercepted more than 400 Starlink communication devices linked to terrorist networks in the North-East in May 2026.

A statement issued by the Special Adviser on Media to the Minister, Leah Katung-Babatunde quoted the minister saying Nigeria was shifting from a predominantly military approach to a coordinated counterterrorism strategy involving intelligence gathering, law enforcement, community engagement and socio-economic interventions.

He explained that terrorism remained a complex security challenge fuelled by economic vulnerabilities, porous borders, local grievances and transnational organised crime.

The minister said the strategy, guided by Nigeria’s National Counter Terrorism Strategy (NACTEST), reflected the administration’s determination to address both the immediate threats posed by terrorist groups and the underlying factors sustaining insecurity.

Addressing the growing use of emerging technologies by violent extremist groups, Musa highlighted Nigeria’s efforts to counter the illicit deployment of drones, digital communication devices and satellite technologies.

He said the Armed Forces of Nigeria were deploying intelligence-led operations, advanced surveillance systems, unmanned aerial platforms and military artificial intelligence to weaken terrorist networks.

He particularly disclosed that troops of Operation Hadin Kai intercepted more than 400 Starlink communication devices linked to terrorist networks in the North-East in May 2026.

Musa also highlighted the Ministry of Defence’s efforts to promote indigenous defence innovation through research and partnerships with the private sector.

He called for stronger collaboration with the European Union in counter-drone technologies, digital forensics and satellite intelligence to enhance Nigeria’s capacity to respond to evolving security threats.

On the financial networks sustaining terrorism, the minister stressed the need to dismantle criminal economies, including kidnapping for ransom, illegal mining, cattle rustling and illicit arms trafficking.

He said the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU), National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC) and other security agencies were working together to trace illicit financial flows, prosecute criminal facilitators and strengthen border security to disrupt terrorist supply chains.

The Defence minister further reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to regional and international security cooperation through the Multinational Joint Task Force (MNJTF) in the Lake Chad Basin, the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), the African Union and the West Africa Police Information Systems (WAPIS)

He also emphasised that the Armed Forces remained committed to operating within the framework of national laws and international humanitarian law, with priority given to civilian protection and due process in the prosecution of suspects.

According to him, Nigeria also recognises the importance of rehabilitation and reintegration programmes for eligible former combatants through initiatives such as Operation Safe Corridor.

The Schuman Security and Defence Forum provides a platform for high-level discussions on international peace, security and defence among defence ministers of partner countries, European Union member states, representatives of international organisations and leading think tanks.

title: Sultan arrives Benin to honour Oba Ewuare II on 10th coronation anniversary
description:
The Sultan of Sokoto, His Eminence Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, has arrived Benin City, Edo State, ahead of the 10th coronation anniversary of the Oba of Benin, Omo N’Oba N’Edo, Uku Akpolokpolo, Oba Ewuare II, Oba of Benin.



The aircraft conveying the Sultan touched ground at the Oba Akenzua II
content:
The Sultan of Sokoto, His Eminence Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, has arrived Benin City, Edo State, ahead of the 10th coronation anniversary of the Oba of Benin, Omo N’Oba N’Edo, Uku Akpolokpolo, Oba Ewuare II, Oba of Benin.

The aircraft conveying the Sultan touched ground at the Oba Akenzua II Airport in the Edo State capital 25 minutes after departing the Samuel Ladoke Akintola International Airport, Ibadan, Oyo State, at 5:05 p.m. on Friday, November 20.

In a statement by Prince Bashir Adefaka on behalf of the Media Team of the Sultan of Sokoto, noted that the Sultan was received by senior members of the Oba of Benin-in-Council at the airport.

He was accompanied on the flight by the Galadiman Gerin Sokoto, His Royal Highness Alhaji Aliyu Attahiru Galadanci, and former Director-General, National Broadcasting Commission, NBC, Mallam Danladi Bako, Kogunan Sokoto.

The Sultan arrived Ibadan on a weeklong South-West working visit on Sunday, November 15, starting off his activities with participation in the 11th General Assembly of the Muslim Ummah of South West Nigeria, MUSWEN, as special guest of honour.

The Sultan also performed his duty as Chancellor of the University of Ibadan on Tuesday, November 17, supported by his Pro-Chancellor and Chairman Governing Council, Chief Bisi Akande, as well as the new Vice-Chancellor, Professor Peter Olamakinde Olapegba, among others.

On Wednesday, he travelled from his Ibadan to Saki to partake – as Chairman of the Day – in the official commissioning of the 500-seat Alhaji Azeez Adedokun Olowolagba Information and Communication Technology, ICT, Centre built and donated to the College of Nursing Sciences, Muslim Medical Foundation Saki, by Alhaji Mudasiru Adedokun Olowolagba, in memory of his late father.

On Thursday, the Sultan paid a courtesy call on the Aseyin of Iseyin, Oba Sefiu Olawale Adeyemi III (Ajirotutu I), who will be celebrating his third coronation anniversary on December 11. He also witnessed the award ceremony by the Iseyin Kingdom in honour of legal luminary and philanthropist, Barrister Ahmed Raji (SAN).

On Friday, the Sultan of Sokoto paid a courtesy visit to the palace of the Olubadan of Ibadan Land, where Oba Rashidi Ladoja, Arusa I, assisted by Olubadan-in-Council, received him. Both monarchs then proceeded to the Bodija Muslim Community Central Mosque, Ibadan, where they observed their Jumat service led by the Chief Imam, Sheikh Hakeem Ibrahim.

He the left for Benin City, where he was first received by members of the Oba of Benin-in-Council and then later by the royal host himself in his palace the same Friday night.

title: New LAWMA Chairman Unveils 60-Day Waste Evacuation Plan For Lagos
description: The Acting Managing Director of the Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA), Olajuwon Akinyemi, has unveiled a 60-day action plan focused on rapid waste evacuation, improved operational efficiency and institutional repositioning, as part of efforts to restore the Authority’s past glory.Akinye
content:
The Acting Managing Director of the Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA), Olajuwon Akinyemi, has unveiled a 60-day action plan focused on rapid waste evacuation, improved operational efficiency and institutional repositioning, as part of efforts to restore the Authority’s past glory.

Akinyemi announced the plan while addressing management and staff at a workers’ forum held at the Authority’s headquarters in Ijora-Olopa on Friday, where he was accompanied by the Acting Executive Director, Operations, Dr Olorunwa Tijani, and the Executive Director, Finance, Kunle Adebiyi.

He said that the immediate priority of the new management was to strengthen LAWMA’s operational capacity, particularly in waste evacuation, field monitoring and regulatory enforcement, while introducing strategic changes to improve service delivery across Lagos State.

Recalling his previous years of service in LAWMA and other government agencies, Akinyemi urged staff to demonstrate collective commitment, positive attitudes and renewed dedication to duty, stressing that repositioning the Authority would require the active participation of every member of staff.

“We are bringing in resilience and a new paradigm shift. It is a new wave in handling waste in Lagos. We already have the template to transform LAWMA positively. All we need to do is recreate, modernise and do better than in the past,” he stated.

As part of the 60-day action plan, he disclosed plans for proactive staff redeployment across the state’s three operational districts, taking into consideration personnel’s familiarity with different terrains and communities, to strengthen field monitoring, improve operational response and enhance service delivery.

He also announced plans to establish regional operational hubs across the state to decentralise waste management operations, strengthen supervision and bring interventions closer to communities, including those areas requiring urgent attention.

The Acting Managing Director further outlined plans to intensify community engagement and public enlightenment on proper waste sorting at source and responsible waste disposal, noting that traditional rulers, Community Development Association (CDA) leaders, market associations, artisans and other community stakeholders would be mobilised to support efforts to curb indiscriminate dumping.

He emphasised the need for stronger engagement with Private Sector Participation (PSP) operators and greater public compliance with approved waste collection tariffs, describing collaboration among the Authority, service providers and residents as essential to achieving a cleaner Lagos.

On staff welfare, Akinyemi assured employees of management’s commitment to their well-being, disclosing efforts to facilitate the procurement of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)-powered staff buses to ease transportation challenges.

Earlier, the Acting Executive Director, Operations, Dr Olorunwa Tijani, expressed delight at reuniting with the LAWMA family, assuring staff that the Authority’s operational framework would receive urgent attention and revitalisation to improve performance.

He stressed the need for a more effective operational structure and pledged his support for the new management’s drive to reposition the Authority and strengthen service delivery.

Also speaking, the Executive Director, Finance, Mr Kunle Adebiyi, expressed confidence in the capacity of the new leadership to reposition the Authority, pledging his support and commitment to teamwork.

Adebiyi emphasised the importance of prudent financial management, accountability and effective resource utilisation, noting that successful implementation of the 60-day action plan would require synergy among all staff, directorates, departments and units.

He urged employees to demonstrate professionalism, commitment and a shared sense of responsibility.

The Acting Managing Director, accompanied by the Acting Executive Director, Operations, and other management staff, subsequently embarked on a familiarisation tour of various departments within the Authority, interacting with employees to gain first-hand insight into their activities and operational challenges.

The victims were said to be mourners travelling to attend a funeral in the communit
content:
President Bola Tinubu has expressed sadness over the boat accident in Ukubie, near Oweikorogha community, in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, which reportedly claimed several lives on Friday.

The victims were said to be mourners travelling to attend a funeral in the community when the boat capsized.

In a statement issued on Saturday by his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, the President said he had directed relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful rescue and recovery operation.

“Those who lost their lives in the tragedy did not deserve to die that way. I have directed all relevant Federal Disaster Response agencies to work together to ensure a successful recovery and rescue operation,” Tinubu said.

The President also directed that the presidential campaign rally scheduled to hold in Ibadan, Oyo State, on Saturday, November 21, be observed “without much fanfare” in honour of the victims and in sympathy with their families.

“On behalf of the entire nation, I mourn those who lost their lives in the incident and sympathise with their families, the government and the people of Bayelsa State.

“I particularly mourn with Governor Douye Diri over this sad incident.

“I pray that God Almighty repose their souls and comfort their families,” he added.

title: South Korea records first cholera case in 10 years
description:
South Korea has confirmed its first cholera case in 10 years, with health authorities investigating a suspected locally acquired infection in the southeastern city of Changwon.
The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency announced the case on Friday, November 20, saying the patient had no histor
content:
South Korea has confirmed its first cholera case in 10 years, with health authorities investigating a suspected locally acquired infection in the southeastern city of Changwon.

The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency announced the case on Friday, November 20, saying the patient had no history of overseas travel in the preceding two months.

According to the agency, as reported by SBS World News, the patient visited a hospital emergency department in Changwon, South Gyeongsang Province, on November 6 after developing vomiting and diarrhoea.

The hospital suspected cholera and reported the case on November 9.

“Although the initial test returned negative on November 16, a retest of a sample collected before the patient received antibiotics confirmed the infection on November 18,” it said.

The agency said it “confirmed the presence of toxin-producing cholera bacteria early on November 19.

“The patient’s symptoms improved, and they were discharged on November 17.

“However, the patient remains under isolation management until two consecutive follow-up tests return negative results.”

The agency said it was conducting an epidemiological investigation and monitoring the patient’s contacts to establish the source of infection.

“This case is South Korea’s first since 2016, when three infections were reported. The country also experienced a larger outbreak in 2001, which sickened at least 162 people,” SBS reported.

Cholera is primarily transmitted through contaminated food or water and, in rare cases, through direct contact with an infected person’s faeces or vomit.

Severe cases can cause dehydration and shock, which may be fatal if treatment is delayed.

The health agency urged residents to drink safe water, eat thoroughly cooked food, wash their hands properly and wash or peel fruits and vegetables.

It also advised medical facilities to promptly test and report suspected cases.
