title: Countries race to secure COP31 deal after fossil fuel row
description:
The COP31 climate talks spilled into Saturday as countries raced to secure a deal after a draft text dropped all mention of fossil fuels, exposing deep divisions over how to tackle global warming.



Nearly 200 nations remained deadlocked after two weeks of grinding UN talks in Turkey, with negotiat
content:
The COP31 climate talks spilled into Saturday as countries raced to secure a deal after a draft text dropped all mention of fossil fuels, exposing deep divisions over how to tackle global warming.

Nearly 200 nations remained deadlocked after two weeks of grinding UN talks in Turkey, with negotiators working through the night after missing their scheduled Friday finish amid feuds over energy, science and finance.

Australia, which is presiding over the COP31 negotiations, raced against the clock to produce a third draft deal, with many delegates due to catch flights home.

“We are close to the finish line, but we are not there yet,” COP31 President Murat Kurum, who is Turkey’s environment minister, told an assembly late Friday that approved some technical matters.

Midway through his opening address, Kurum was forced to pause while a protester shouted “You are killing the future!” before being escorted from the hall.

Expectations of a major breakthrough have been low at COP31 as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran.

The summit follows a string of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal and Indonesia and unfolds as a super El Nino pattern amplifies the risk of further extreme weather.

A draft deal unveiled earlier this week called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels, a flashpoint at UN climate talks where producers such as Saudi Arabia have fiercely resisted such calls.

A second, pared-down draft released on Thursday stripped away all mentions of fossil fuels — sending negotiators rushing back to the bargaining table.

The European Union said the revised draft “risks turning this climate COP into a fossil summit”.

A dozen European and developing countries — from France to Panama and the Solomon Islands — released a letter Friday insisting that the deal include “a clear transition away from fossil fuels”.

Panama, which also signed the letter, threatened to walk away from the talks. The country’s environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, is a vocal critic of the climate negotiations, accusing a “petroleum mafia” of blocking progress.

Meanwhile, the OPEC oil cartel wrote on X that its head, Haitham Al Ghais, met Russian presidential climate envoy Ruslan Edelgeriev at COP31 to discuss “the importance of inclusive and balanced approaches across all multilateral environmental fora”.

– ‘Clean electrification’ –

Australia’s Climate Minister Chris Bowen, who shuttled between delegations to seek compromises, said Friday he would work “for as long as it takes, to get the job done”.

The draft “cover decision” proposes a target to electrify the global economy — a push to replace technologies that burn fossil fuels directly, like diesel cars and gas heating, with electric alternatives.

The goal is championed by COP31 hosts Turkey and Australia, who tout “electrification” as integral to tackling concerns over energy security and sluggish global progress in cutting heat-trapping emissions.

“Electrification is the key to transitioning away from fossil fuels,” said Bowen, who is chairing the negotiations.

The proposal calls for countries to boost the global share of final energy demand met by electricity to 35 percent by 2035.

But it does not specify that the additional electricity must come from renewables rather than coal or gas, spurring some countries to demand an explicitly “clean” target.

Some countries also rejected a proposal to ramp up carbon capture, dismissing it as a costly, unproven technology that could allow polluters to keep burning fossil fuels.

– $120 billion target –

Countries are sharply divided over a raft of other issues.

The timing of the next set of reports by the UN’s Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has been a major source of friction.

The latest draft expressed “deep concern” over the imminent breach of the 1.5C goal but dropped an earlier call to return warming below that threshold as soon as possible this century.

Negotiations are also deadlocked over long-running complaints by developing countries that rich nations are falling short in their obligations to help them confront climate change.

The removal of a $120 billion target for climate adaptation angered developing nations.

“We didn’t come here to beg,” said Ghana’s environment minister, Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings.

title: 11 Dead, Over 180 Hospitalised After Drinking Illicit Alcohol In India
description: At least 11 people have died, and more than 180 have been hospitalised after drinking suspected tainted alcohol in India’s northeastern state of Manipur.The victims fell ill after consuming the liquor, Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh said in a statement on Friday.“Over 180 patients
content:
At least 11 people have died, and more than 180 have been hospitalised after drinking suspected tainted alcohol in India’s northeastern state of Manipur.

The victims fell ill after consuming the liquor, Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh said in a statement on Friday.

“Over 180 patients have been admitted in the two hospitals so far, while the death toll has reached 11 in the last 48 hours,” the statement said.

He also ordered an enquiry into the incident, saying those responsible would be arrested and punished.

Deaths from illicit or adulterated alcohol are regularly reported in India, where cheap liquor sold outside regulated channels can contain methanol, a highly toxic industrial chemical.

In May, at least 15 people died after drinking methanol-laced illicit liquor in Pune and neighbouring Pimpri-Chinchwad in the western state of Maharashtra.

In August, 13 people died, and more than 60 were affected after consuming methanol-tainted liquor in Gujarat’s Bhavnagar district, according to local media reports.

Such liquor is widely consumed across India, where a bottle is sometimes sold for less than a dollar. If ingested, methanol can cause blindness, liver damage and death in larger concentrations.

AFP

title: Laws alone can’t protect Nigerian children – CJN
description:
The Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, has warned that legislation alone cannot protect Nigerian children from abuse, exploitation, neglect and other forms of violence, urging stronger enforcement of child protection laws.
She said the effectiveness of the Child Rights Act 2003 d
content:
The Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, has warned that legislation alone cannot protect Nigerian children from abuse, exploitation, neglect and other forms of violence, urging stronger enforcement of child protection laws.

She said the effectiveness of the Child Rights Act 2003 depended on how consistently its provisions were implemented to protect children in their daily lives.

The CJN spoke on Friday at the inaugural conference of the Nigerian Association of Family Court Judicial Officers, Magistrates and Other Practitioners, organised to commemorate the 2026 United Nations World Children’s Day in Abuja.

Represented by a Supreme Court Justice, Jummai Sanke, SAN, Kekere-Ekun said Nigeria had established an important legal framework for protecting children’s rights but needed coordinated action by relevant institutions to translate the provisions into practical safeguards.

“In Nigeria, the Child Rights Act 2003 provides an important legal framework for the protection and advancement of children’s rights. Its recognition of the best interests of the child as a primary consideration in all actions concerning children establishes a principle that must guide our laws, policies, institutions and decisions.

“However, the existence of legislation, important as it is, does not by itself guarantee the protection of children. The real measure of our commitment lies in how effectively these rights are respected, protected and enforced in the daily lives of children,” the CJN said.

She identified child abuse, neglect, sexual exploitation, trafficking, child labour, early and forced marriage, abandonment and denial of access to education and healthcare as persistent threats to children’s welfare.

The CJN said the judiciary had a significant responsibility to ensure that children appearing before courts as victims, witnesses or children in conflict with the law were treated with dignity, sensitivity and understanding.

She called for child-friendly judicial proceedings that protected children’s privacy, encouraged their participation and took account of their age, maturity and emotional circumstances.

“Where a child has come into conflict with the law, the emphasis should, where appropriate, be on rehabilitation and reintegration rather than measures that permanently undermine the child’s prospects,” she said.

Kekere-Ekun also called for more training for judicial officers in trauma-informed approaches, handling child witnesses, emerging forms of exploitation and the implications of digital technology.

She said child protection required collaboration among government institutions, law enforcement agencies, social welfare services, schools, healthcare providers, legislators, families and civil society organisations.

“A child who has suffered abuse should not have to navigate a fragmented system in search of help,” she said.

The CJN urged participants to identify practical solutions to child protection challenges and strengthen institutions to ensure that children’s rights guaranteed by law translated into meaningful protection.

She said the true measure of commitment to children’s rights would be seen in children protected from abuse, girls allowed to remain in school, children whose voices were heard in custody proceedings and young people given opportunities for rehabilitation.

The Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, also acknowledged gaps in the implementation of child protection laws, disclosing that the Federal Government was reviewing the Child Rights Act 2003 to address emerging challenges.

He said the review had culminated in a draft amendment bill scheduled for stakeholder validation on November 24, ahead of further steps towards its finalisation and enactment.

Fagbemi said the challenge confronting Nigeria was not the absence of laws but the failure to effectively implement them.

“The pressing challenge before us is not the absence of laws, but the gap in their implementation. Across the country, too many children still face realities that threaten their safety and stifle their potential.

“Bridging this gap demands sustained political will, coordinated institutional action, and a readiness to adapt our systems to the evolving vulnerabilities of our children,” he said.

The minister said the Federal Ministry of Justice was driving reforms to strengthen the country’s child justice system, adding that it had supported the development of Legal Aid Guidelines and Prosecutors’ Guidelines for Handling Cases of Children in Contact with the Law.

He said the guidelines were designed to guarantee quality legal representation and enforce child-sensitive prosecution standards nationwide.

Fagbemi also called for stronger safeguards against cyberbullying, digital exploitation, harmful online content and breaches of children’s privacy.

He urged stakeholders to ensure that the outcome of the conference went beyond communiqués and produced measurable improvements in courtrooms, policies and frontline services.

Earlier, the President of NAFCJOMP, Justice Eberechi Suzette Nyesom-Wike, said the association was committed to advancing children’s rights, protection and welfare through stronger family court practice and a child-sensitive administration of justice.

She said the association, registered with the Corporate Affairs Commission in January 2026, brought together judicial officers, magistrates, prosecutors, social welfare officers, advocates, law enforcement personnel and other child protection practitioners across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

Nyesom-Wike said the association’s mission was to promote children’s best interests by strengthening family court practice and supporting the effective administration of justice.

“Among other things, our objectives are to promote compliance with child protection laws by advocating for the implementation of policies related to child welfare, including education, healthcare, and social security.

“We seek to pursue the successful implementation of the Child Rights Act and laws of the sub-nationals, in ensuring that the Nigerian child suffers no detriment in any circumstance,” she said.

She said the association also sought to promote professional development and collaboration among family justice and child protection practitioners to ensure consistent standards in family and juvenile court practice.

Nyesom-Wike said NAFCJOMP, in collaboration with its partners, facilitated access to counselling, legal aid and medical support through a referral system.

“This reflects our conviction that protecting children requires not only sound laws and effective courts, but also coordinated support that meets children’s needs in practice,” she said.

She said the conference would provide an opportunity for stakeholders to strengthen their professional community, deepen collaboration across disciplines and develop practical approaches to challenges confronting children and families.

The Speaker of the Children’s Parliament, Miss Progress Umoh, also made a case for Nigerian children, while participants drawn from secondary schools across the Federal Capital Territory spoke on issues affecting their rights and welfare.

The conference, themed “My Day. My Rights. My Future,” brought together judicial officers, legal practitioners, policymakers, child protection professionals, civil society organisations and children to examine child protection, access to justice, rehabilitation and children’s participation in matters affecting them.

The post Laws alone can’t protect Nigerian children – CJN appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Ex S.African Deputy President, UN Women’s Chief Dies At 71
description: Tributes poured in on Saturday for South Africa’s former deputy president and head of UN Women, Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, who has died at the age of 71.Mlambo-Ngcuka passed away on Friday following complications from a medical procedure she underwent about two weeks ago, her family said in a sta
content:
Tributes poured in on Saturday for South Africa’s former deputy president and head of UN Women, Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, who has died at the age of 71.

Mlambo-Ngcuka passed away on Friday following complications from a medical procedure she underwent about two weeks ago, her family said in a statement carried by the state broadcaster, SABC.

Mlambo-Ngcuka was the first woman to serve as South Africa’s deputy president from 2005 to 2008, having previously worked as minerals and energy minister.

She was United Nations Under-Secretary-General and executive director of the United Nations’ agency for gender equality, UN Women, from 2013 to 2021.

“Our hearts are really, really sad and broken for having lost such a very dynamic woman leader in our country,” President Cyril Ramaphosa said.

“She truly flew the flag of women, not only women of South Africa and Africa, but women of the world,” he said.

In a statement of condolence on X, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres praised Mlambo-Ngcuka as a “lifelong champion of the rights & empowerment of women & girls”.

She “believed that gender equality is not a favour to be granted but a right to be claimed”, he said.

In an interview with SABC, UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed recalled Mlambo-Ngcuka’s interventions on behalf of women and girls in Afghanistan, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Nigeria.

“She pushed the limits and I think that that’s where we got a lot of the confidence to do the things that we do, following in her footsteps,” she said.

In a statement on X, Mohammed said Mlambo-Ngcuka “fought for women’s leadership till the end”, including by calling for a woman to succeed Guterres as secretary-general after his second term ends on December 31.

AFP

title: Army graduates 47 soldiers as military drivers in Plateau
description:
The Nigerian Army has graduated 47 soldiers as military drivers after completing a basic driving course at the Headquarters 3 Division in Jos, Plateau State.
The soldiers completed the Drivers Basic Course 2 of 2026, organised to improve their professional competence and strengthen the army’s operat
content:
The Nigerian Army has graduated 47 soldiers as military drivers after completing a basic driving course at the Headquarters 3 Division in Jos, Plateau State.

The soldiers completed the Drivers Basic Course 2 of 2026, organised to improve their professional competence and strengthen the army’s operational mobility.

The graduation ceremony was held at the 3 Division Auditorium, Maxwell Khobe Cantonment, Jos, with the General Officer Commanding 3 Division and Commander, Operation Enduring Peace, Major General W.M. Dangana, represented by the Commander, 53 Signals Brigade, Brigadier General P.A. Zipele.

According to a statement issued on Friday by the Acting Deputy Director, Army Public Relations, 3 Division, Lieutenant Colonel Olumide Victor Olukoya, the GOC commended the Supply and Transport Drivers Training Wing for its commitment to developing competent military drivers.

He emphasised the importance of transportation and logistics support to military operations, particularly in challenging terrains and demanding security environments.

The statement read, “Effective transportation and logistics support remain critical to operational success, particularly in the conduct of military operations across challenging terrains and demanding security environments.”

It added that the course was designed to equip the soldiers with the knowledge and practical skills required to operate military vehicles safely and professionally.

Charging the graduates to apply their training, the statement said, “Addressing the graduating soldiers, the GOC charged them to translate the knowledge and skills acquired during the course into practical performance in their respective units.”

It further stated that they were expected to demonstrate discipline, vigilance, responsibility and professionalism in their duties.

The statement added, “Safe driving practices and proper vehicle handling are essential to the protection of lives, military equipment and the successful execution of assigned missions.”

Earlier, the Commander, 73 Supply and Transport Brigade, Colonel O.C. Okungbure, described the graduation as another milestone in the division’s efforts to develop a skilled and professional workforce.

He said the training covered military driving procedures, traffic laws and safety precautions.

The statement read, “The course provided the 47 participants with essential driving competencies, including adherence to military driving procedures, traffic laws and safety precautions.”

It added that the training would “enhance operational mobility, improve logistics support and facilitate the effective movement of troops and equipment in both routine and operational environments.”

Okungbure urged the graduates to uphold the standards acquired during the course and remain worthy ambassadors of the Nigerian Army in their respective formations and units.

The ceremony featured a review of the course activities, presentation of certificates, and group photographs.

title: Kogi extends retirement age for health workers to 65
description:
The Kogi State Government has approved an extension of the retirement age for eligible skilled clinical health professionals in state-owned health institutions from 60 to 65 years, or from 35 to 40 years of service, whichever comes first.
A statement issued on Saturday by the state Commissioner for
content:
The Kogi State Government has approved an extension of the retirement age for eligible skilled clinical health professionals in state-owned health institutions from 60 to 65 years, or from 35 to 40 years of service, whichever comes first.

A statement issued on Saturday by the state Commissioner for Information, Kingsley Fanwo, said the approval was granted by the state Governor, Alhaji Ahmed Usman Ododo, as part of his administration’s deliberate efforts to improve the welfare of healthcare personnel, retain experienced professionals and ensure that the state continues to benefit from the expertise of skilled health workers while they are still active and capable of contributing meaningfully to healthcare delivery.

The commissioner said, “The decision reflects Governor Ododo’s recognition of the invaluable contributions of healthcare professionals to the well-being of citizens and the need to create an enabling environment that encourages them to remain in service and give their best.”

Fanwo disclosed that the governor conveyed the approval through the Office of the Head of Service for formal communication and implementation across the affected health institutions.

The State Head of Service, Hajiya Falilat Yusuf Musa, Esq., applauded the governor for the approval, describing it as a progressive workforce policy that recognises the value of experience, professional competence and the need to sustain critical manpower in the state’s healthcare system.

She said, “This is a commendable decision by His Excellency, Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo. It demonstrates his sensitivity to the needs of our healthcare professionals and his appreciation of the enormous contributions they make to the well-being of our people. Retaining experienced and competent personnel for longer years will strengthen our institutions, improve mentorship and ensure continuity in the delivery of essential services.”

According to the approved guidelines, the new retirement age applies to eligible skilled clinical health professionals in state-owned tertiary hospitals, general hospitals, cottage and comprehensive hospitals, primary healthcare centres and clinics.

The State Commissioner for Health, Dr Abdulazeez Adams Adeiza, also commended the governor for the approval, describing it as a timely intervention that would boost morale among health professionals and further strengthen the state’s capacity to deliver quality healthcare.

He said, “This approval is a major boost to the health sector in Kogi State. Experienced clinical professionals remain invaluable to our healthcare system, particularly in mentoring younger practitioners, handling complex cases and sustaining quality service. Governor Ododo has demonstrated a clear understanding of the importance of keeping our skilled health personnel in service while they remain physically fit, professionally competent and productive.”

The policy is expected to strengthen the state’s healthcare workforce by retaining experienced personnel, promoting continuity in service delivery and allowing younger health professionals to benefit from the wealth of knowledge and practical experience accumulated by senior colleagues.

The Commissioner for Health said the development was consistent with the Ododo administration’s commitment to improving healthcare infrastructure, personnel welfare and access to quality medical services across the state.

“The Ododo administration has continued to invest in healthcare development as part of its determination to build a responsive health system, improve citizens’ well-being and ensure that residents have access to quality and affordable medical services,” the commissioner noted.

title: Political Signals | Tracking The Opposition
description: The ADC faces two consequential court developments: an order changing its Adamawa governorship candidate and a procedural setback in its challenge to President Bola Tinubu’s eligibility.The NDC, meanwhile, demonstrated campaign mobilisation in Onitsha as police confirmed an investigation into
content:
The ADC faces two consequential court developments: an order changing its Adamawa governorship candidate and a procedural setback in its challenge to President Bola Tinubu’s eligibility.

The NDC, meanwhile, demonstrated campaign mobilisation in Onitsha as police confirmed an investigation into an attack on its Edo secretariat.

ADC: Court orders Suleiman’s restoration in Adamawa. On 20 November, Justice Obiora Egwuatu ordered INEC to restore Omar Suleiman as the party’s governorship candidate, overturning his replacement by Tukur Ribadu.

The court directed the ADC to forward Suleiman’s particulars and restrained Ribadu from presenting himself as its candidate.

Electoral implication: the judgment changes the basis on which the ADC must organise its state campaign, potentially requiring reconciliation between competing camps. It does not resolve the separate national leadership litigation.

Watch for INEC implementation, Ribadu’s response and any appeal or stay application.

Atiku’s eligibility challenge suffers a limited setback. Separately, Justice Inyang Ekwo rejected Atiku Abubakar and the ADC’s application to amend their suit against Tinubu’s 2027 eligibility.

The judge held that the amendments introduced new facts outside the constitutional filing period and directed the parties to proceed with the substantive case.

Analysis: this restricts the plaintiffs’ attempted expansion of their case; it is neither dismissal of the entire suit nor a determination of the underlying certificate allegation. Watch for substantive proceedings and any challenge to the amendment ruling.

NDC: Visible mobilisation in Onitsha. Peter Obi led a roadshow through Onitsha on 20 November ahead of a town hall engagement. Reporting and video documented supporters, traders and residents joining the procession.

Analysis: this provides evidence of active mobilisation in an important Anambra commercial centre. Crowd presence alone cannot establish statewide voting strength or national momentum. The next test is sustained ward organisation and polling agent preparation beyond major appearances.

Edo investigation raises campaign access concerns.

Police announced on 20 November that they were investigating the previous day’s reported attack on the NDC secretariat in Afuze and had invited Owan East council chairman Ernest Aitalegbe to assist.

Party members reported disruption and vandalism by armed men allegedly wearing Edo State Security Network uniforms.

Their identity and responsibility remain under investigation; the invitation does not establish culpability. Electoral implication: intimidation of local meetings could impede recruitment and organisation. Watch for arrests, findings and measures protecting lawful party activity.

APM: Electricity becomes a sharper campaign argument. Makinde’s campaign issued a statement on 20 November disputing the government’s defence of its electricity record and promoting improved supply reliability within three years.

This is a campaign commitment, not an independently validated delivery forecast.

Analysis: it gives the APM a household service issue on which to challenge the incumbent. Watch for financing, implementation milestones and measurable targets.

For PDP, SDP, PRP and Labour Party, no comparable new leadership or candidate status decision was verified in this reporting window. Recent rallies, endorsements and political predictions do not, without additional evidence, justify revising their assessed electoral prospects.

The post Political Signals | Tracking The Opposition appeared first on Channels Television.

description:

The 2-day mega event is scheduled to hold on Friday, November 27 and Saturday, November 28 at
content:
The Coalition of Entrepreneurs and Professionals (CEP) is set to host one of the biggest business gatherings in Lagos State – the CEP Conference and Trade Fair, tagged “Shop Lagos. Wear Lagos. Love Lagos.”

The 2-day mega event is scheduled to hold on Friday, November 27 and Saturday, November 28 at the LTV 8/ Radio Lagos Marque in Ikeja, Lagos.

The Conference and Trade Fair is designed to promote Made-in-Lagos products, empower local entrepreneurs, connect professionals, and celebrate the creativity, resilience, and enterprise that make Lagos the commercial capital of Nigeria and Africa.

Attendees will experience a rich blend of exhibitions, business masterclasses, networking sessions, product showcases, fashion, food, arts, and live entertainment – all proudly Made in Lagos.

CEP announced the event on Friday as the organisers formally unveiled the Conference and Trade Fair to the media, business community, and the public.

The briefing was chaired by the President of CEP, Dr. Adeniyi Ojikutu in company of members of the Coalition of Entrepreneurs and Professionals (CEP) and other key stakeholders.

Also in attendance were Mr. Dipo Ojikutu, Managing Director of Bigie Bids Limited, with his strategy team, alongside other meaningful Lagosians, entrepreneurs, professionals, and partners who have thrown their weight behind the vision of a stronger, self-reliant Lagos economy.

The event provided an opportunity for CEP leadership to outline the objectives of the event, the economic impact for Lagos entrepreneurs, and the strategic partnerships driving its success.

Addressing journalists, Dr. Ojikutu noted that the event is a deliberate intervention to connect Lagos entrepreneurs to markets, funding, visibility, and policy support, stressing that the future prosperity of Lagos depends on empowering its own business owners.

The event, he said, will be officially launched by the Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Dr. Kadiri Obafemi Hamzat (KOH), who will serve as the Chief Launcher.

Dr. Hamzat will speak on the impact of CEP in the strategic development of Lagos State and how the State intends to support professional entrepreneurs and small businesses for sustainable growth.

His keynote address will outline a bold vision for a Lagos where entrepreneurs are not just surviving but thriving – with access to funding, markets, infrastructure, and policies that work for business owners.

The event is proudly sponsored by Wema Bank, with LTV 8 and Radio Lagos as official media partners.

Bigie Bids Limited is also a key partner, having led the sponsorship drive for the event.

The conference and tradefair is positioned for participants to shop original Made-in-Lagos products directly from manufacturers and vendors; meet investors, buyers, and business partners; Learn from industry leaders and successful entrepreneurs; showcase their brands to thousands of visitors over 2 days and be part of the movement building the future of Lagos business

Speaking on the event, the President of CEP, Dr. Adeniyi Ojikutu, said that “Shop Lagos. Wear Lagos. Love Lagos.” is more than a trade fair. It is a celebration of Lagos enterprise and a call to action to support our own. When you buy Lagos, you grow Lagos.”

For vendors’ stands, sponsorship, and partnership, the organizers said that their doors are opened for various entrepreneurs to take advantage of the conference and trade fair like no other in Lagos State.

title: My son will get my nomination if Obi offers me ministerial job – Babachir Lawal
description:
Former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Babachir Lawal, has said he would nominate his 40-year-old son for a ministerial position if Peter Obi offers him an appointment after winning the 2027 presidential election.
Lawal, a chieftain of the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC), said he w
content:
Former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Babachir Lawal, has said he would nominate his 40-year-old son for a ministerial position if Peter Obi offers him an appointment after winning the 2027 presidential election.

Lawal, a chieftain of the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC), said he was no longer interested in holding public office, citing his age and claiming to have achieved his ambitions in life.

Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, the former SGF said he would prefer to return to farming rather than serve in an Obi-led administration.

He added that if the former Anambra State governor offered him a ministerial position, he would recommend his son for the role instead.

“Go back to my farm and watch Nigeria grow,” he said when asked what he would do if Obi won the presidency.

Explaining his position, Lawal said, “See, I keep telling you I’m 72 years old. I have a 40-year-old son. What is wrong if Peter says, ‘BD, give me, I’m going to make you Minister of Agric.’ I said, ‘Peter, instead give my son Minister of Agric.’ Is that wrong?

“In those days when we were young, that’s how things were done. When they approach you, ‘You are going to be this,’ you say, ‘No, I’m too old for this, there are young generation.’ Pick and give! It’s doable.”

He described himself as an elder statesman and suggested that having served as SGF under former President Muhammadu Buhari, ministerial appointment would be a demotion.

“I’m 72! Past 72. Yes, very. An elder statesman. And God has done well for me. I’ve achieved everything that I need to achieve,” he said.

Lawal said he was not in the party to seek political office but to support what he described as a good man capable of rescuing Nigerians from hardship.

He expressed confidence that Obi would win the 2027 presidential election, insisting that the circumstances surrounding the 2023 poll would not be repeated.

title: Funke Akindele backs IG’s directive on treating gunshot victims
description:
Nollywood actress and filmmaker, Funke Akindele, has backed the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu’s directive urging hospitals to treat gunshot victims immediately without demanding police reports.
Akindele expressed her support in a post on her X account on Saturday, while sharing a video
content:
Nollywood actress and filmmaker, Funke Akindele, has backed the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu’s directive urging hospitals to treat gunshot victims immediately without demanding police reports.

Akindele expressed her support in a post on her X account on Saturday, while sharing a video of the Nigeria Police Force’s message on the directive.

Addressing doctors and other healthcare workers, she urged them to begin treatment immediately whenever a gunshot victim was brought to their facilities, rather than insist on police documentation.

“To our doctors and health workers, the Inspector-General of Police has said it clearly.

“When someone comes to you with a gunshot wound, please begin treatment immediately. You don’t need to ask for a police report before you attend to them. Treat first. Save lives first,” she wrote.

She also encouraged members of the public to help injured persons get to hospitals, assuring them that the police had a responsibility to protect lives.

“To everyone watching, if you see someone who’s been shot, please don’t be afraid to help them get to a hospital.

“The duty of the police is to protect lives, and I commend the Nigeria Police Force for making that clear,” she added.

Akindele called on Nigerians to support efforts to save lives, saying, “Let’s help save lives. That’s what matters most.”

PUNCH Online had reported that IG Tunji Disu urged hospitals and medical personnel across the country to treat gunshot victims immediately without demanding police reports before providing medical attention. https://punchng.com/no-police-report-required-before-treating-gunshot-victims-ig/

“When a gunshot victim is brought to any hospital, the law does not require a police report before treatment,” he said.

He also appealed to doctors and healthcare workers to prioritise saving lives, while encouraging members of the public to assist injured persons in emergencies.

“To members of the public, if you see someone injured, do not hesitate to help. You will not be punished for helping,” Disu said.

He concluded with a call to hospitals and emergency responders: “Treat first, save lives.”

title: Justrite Expands South-West Footprint, Opens 40th And 41st Stores In Akure And Ibadan
description: Justrite Superstore has strengthened its presence in South-West Nigeria with the opening of its 40th and 41st stores in Akure, Ondo State, and Ibadan, Oyo State, respectively, reinforcing its position as a homegrown retail brand committed to bringing quality and affordable shopping closer to consume
content:
Justrite Superstore has strengthened its presence in South-West Nigeria with the opening of its 40th and 41st stores in Akure, Ondo State, and Ibadan, Oyo State, respectively, reinforcing its position as a homegrown retail brand committed to bringing quality and affordable shopping closer to consumers.

The two new outlets, located at Igbatoro Road, Akure, and Cocoa Mall, Dugbe, Ibadan, mark another significant milestone in the company’s expansion journey and its continued investment in the South-West region.

The openings reflect Justrite’s commitment to making authentic products accessible to more Nigerians while delivering quality, affordability and convenience under one roof. Through its growing retail network, the company continues to provide customers with a wide selection of everyday essentials, groceries, fresh produce, frozen foods, electronics, household items and other lifestyle products at competitive prices.

As consumers increasingly seek value for money without compromising on quality, Justrite remains focused on strengthening customer confidence by providing authentic products sourced through credible supply channels at affordable rates.

The expansion into Akure and Ibadan also reinforces the brand’s connection with the communities it serves, creating more opportunities for convenient shopping, improved access to essential goods and local economic participation.

With the opening of its 41st store, Justrite is not only expanding its physical footprint but also deepening its commitment to understanding and meeting the evolving needs of shoppers across the region.

title: Bayern’s Kane ruled out for months with ankle injury
description:
Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane will be sidelined for the next few months after suffering a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle during Friday’s 1–1 Bundesliga draw against FC Köln.
The German champions confirmed the injury in a statement published on their official website on Friday,
content:
Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane will be sidelined for the next few months after suffering a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle during Friday’s 1–1 Bundesliga draw against FC Köln.

The German champions confirmed the injury in a statement published on their official website on Friday, following an examination by the club’s medical department.

“Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in FC Bayern’s Bundesliga home match against 1. FC Köln on Friday evening. This was confirmed by an examination by FC Bayern’s medical department.

The 33-year-old will therefore be sidelined for the next few months,” the club said.

Kane sustained the injury during the encounter at the Allianz Arena and was substituted in the 20th minute, with Tom Bischof coming on to replace him.

The England captain had attempted to continue playing after picking up the injury but was eventually forced off.

Bayern manager Vincent Kompany expressed concern over the injuries suffered by Kane and French forward Michael Olise, who also failed to complete the match.

Speaking after the game, Kompany said the club would have to cope with the situation and find ways to secure results despite the absence of key players.

“We have other things to worry about, I must admit. Without complaining too much, we must accept what we’re in for and regain our strength so that we can get results in the next few matches despite the odds,” he said.

“It’s an extremely unusual situation at the moment. We need incredible performances from players who aren’t used to this pressure at FC Bayern. But that’s just how it is. We’ll all try to turn this situation into something positive. FC Bayern do that again and again, and that’s what we want to achieve now too.”

Bayern also confirmed that Olise suffered a bruise to the front of his foot and would receive treatment over the coming days.

The draw against Köln saw Bayern surrender points at home after Mikey Moore gave the visitors the lead in the 12th minute, before Nathaniel Brown equalised for the hosts in the 37th minute.

Kane’s injury is a major setback for the Munich side, who are scheduled to face French club Lille in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday.

The striker has been a key figure in Bayern’s attack, and his absence leaves Kompany with the task of reorganising his forward line for the coming fixtures.

Two weeks ago, the 33-year-old England captain signed a new contract that will keep him with the German champions until 2029.

On October 26, Kane won the 2026 men’s Ballon d’Or, at the 70th edition of the ceremony at the London Palladium, becoming the first Englishman to claim football’s most prestigious individual award since Michael Owen in 2001.

title: 2027: INEC REC seeks traditional rulers’ support for peaceful, secure elections in Benue
description:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi



The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Benue State, Mallam Aminu Idris, has called on traditional rulers in the state to promote a peaceful and secure environment before and during the 2027 general elections.



Idris m
content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Benue State, Mallam Aminu Idris, has called on traditional rulers in the state to promote a peaceful and secure environment before and during the 2027 general elections.

Idris made the appeal during a courtesy visit to the Tor Tiv and Chairman of the Benue State Council of Traditional Rulers, His Royal Majesty, Orcivirigh Prof. James Ayatse, on Friday, November 20, 2026, as part of the Commission’s stakeholder engagement ahead of the elections.

The REC also solicited the support of the traditional institution in encouraging eligible voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and strengthening collaboration with INEC to ensure successful conduct of the forthcoming polls.

According to a statement by the Public Affairs Officer of INEC in Benue State, Mrs. Peace Ogoyi, Idris described the visit as a vital step in the Commission’s preparations for the 2027 elections.

“He solicited the intervention and support of the royal father in three key areas: encouraging the collection of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), promoting a peaceful and secure environment before and during the elections, and providing further support to the Commission through sustained collaboration.”

Responding, the Tor Tiv welcomed the REC and his delegation, expressing appreciation for the visit and acknowledging the important role of traditional rulers in ensuring a conducive environment for electoral activities.

He noted that “traditional rulers, as fathers of the state, have a responsibility to receive electoral officials and ensure their safety and provision of a peaceful working environment.

Drawing from his experience in previous elections, including his service in various ad hoc capacities and as a State Returning Officer, Ayatse acknowledged the enormous responsibilities confronting the Commission.

He said the Traditional Council had consistently advocated peaceful political campaigns and a level playing field for all political parties.

The monarch further disclosed that traditional and religious leaders had organised prayers for peaceful elections and maintained constructive engagements with security agencies to strengthen peace and security across the state.

He assured the REC that the Council would continue to collaborate with relevant stakeholders to identify and address electoral security flashpoints ahead of the elections.

On the credibility of the electoral process, the Tor Tiv emphasised the need for INEC to uphold the will of the people, urging the Commission’s personnel to discharge their duties with neutrality, fairness and professionalism.

He also pledged the continued support of the “Benue State Council of Traditional Rulers towards the successful conduct of the 2027 general elections.”

On PVC collection, Prof Ayatse called for “stronger collaboration between Electoral Officers and traditional and religious leaders to intensify public sensitisation and encourage eligible voters to obtain their cards.”

He suggested that announcements be made at markets, community gatherings and places of worship, alongside sustained media advocacy, to reach more eligible voters.

According to him, PVC collection and participation in elections are shared responsibilities that require the collective efforts of all stakeholders.

The Tor Tiv offered prayers for peaceful, successful and outstanding elections in the state.

The Benue INEC Administrative Secretary, Mr. Shikfu Bewaran, appreciated the monarch for the warm reception accorded the INEC delegation, describing the Tor Tiv as not only a father to the state but also a traditional ruler with practical experience and a deep understanding of the electoral process.

The post 2027: INEC REC seeks traditional rulers’ support for peaceful, secure elections in Benue appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Obi best hope for Nigerians, NDC chairman Cleopas declares
description:
…Says 2027 poll must be referendum on Tinubu’s performance



By Emem Idio, Yenagoa



The National Chairman of the Nigeria Democratic Congress ,NDC, Senator Moses Cleopas, has described the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, as the best hope for Nigerians, urging the electorate to vote out
content:
…Says 2027 poll must be referendum on Tinubu’s performance

By Emem Idio, Yenagoa

The National Chairman of the Nigeria Democratic Congress ,NDC, Senator Moses Cleopas, has described the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, as the best hope for Nigerians, urging the electorate to vote out the President Bola Tinubu-led administration in the 2027 general election.

Cleopas said the country could not afford another four years under an administration that, in his assessment, had failed to address the worsening economic hardship, insecurity and rising cost of living.

He described the 2027 presidential election as an opportunity for Nigerians to determine the future direction of the country and hold the incumbent government accountable for its performance.

The former senator representing Bayelsa Central made the remarks on Friday in Yenagoa during a celebration marking his 57th birthday.

He said the election should serve as a referendum on the Tinubu administration, arguing that a second-term mandate must be earned through demonstrable performance rather than political sentiment.

“Second-term election is a referendum. It is standing on the leg of your previous performance. If you have done well, they give you another mandate. If you have not done well, they ask you to go home,” he said.

Cleopas said the impact of the economic crisis was being felt by families across the country, including his own, citing complaints from his wife and children about the rising cost of household upkeep and education.

He urged voters to assess the presidential candidates on the basis of competence, track record and their capacity to address the country’s problems, rather than party loyalty, religious considerations or financial inducements.

The NDC chairman expressed confidence that Obi would win the 2027 presidential election, insisting that his candidacy offered Nigerians a credible alternative to the present administration.

On insecurity, Cleopas condemned the persistent killings and abductions across the country, particularly attacks involving schoolchildren, accusing the government of failing in its fundamental responsibility to protect lives and property.

Recounting his experience in the Senate, he said lawmakers from different parts of northern Nigeria frequently reported killings in their constituencies, including the deaths of women and children.

He argued that insecurity should concern every Nigerian, irrespective of where attacks occurred, warning against the tendency to treat violence as a distant problem until it reaches one’s community.

Ahead of the 2027 elections, Cleopas accused some politicians of deploying money and public resources to weaken opposition parties and influence voters.

He specifically criticised an alleged plan by a political figure in Bayelsa to offer N50,000 per vote, describing the proposal as an affront to the electorate.

The former lawmaker warned public office holders against using government resources for partisan political activities, insisting that those entrusted with public funds must be held accountable for their use.

On the NDC’s prospects in Bayelsa, Cleopas expressed confidence that the party would make significant electoral gains, citing what he described as growing support among young people.

He, however, ruled out violence as a means of pursuing political power, urging the state government to guarantee the safety of opposition politicians and their supporters and ensure a level playing field for all parties.

“Violence is not part of constitutional democracy. It is alien to democracy. It is the responsibility of the ruling government to provide security,” he said.

Cleopas said opposition parties were entitled to equal protection under the law, disclosing that the NDC had adopted the practice of formally notifying security agencies and other relevant authorities ahead of its political activities.

He also accused the ruling party of deliberately organising rival political events in communities whenever the NDC scheduled campaigns or other political engagements, alleging that the tactic was intended to disrupt the opposition’s activities.

He called on Nigerians, regardless of political affiliation, to participate actively in the 2027 elections, mobilise their families and resist attempts to buy their votes.

The post Obi best hope for Nigerians, NDC chairman Cleopas declares appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Kano begins 20-year plan to end water shortages
description:
The Kano State Government has commenced the development of a 20-year Water Supply and Distribution Master Plan to guide investment and reforms aimed at ensuring sustainable access to potable water across urban and rural communities.
The Commissioner for Water Resources, Dr Dahiru Muhammad Hashim, di
content:
The Kano State Government has commenced the development of a 20-year Water Supply and Distribution Master Plan to guide investment and reforms aimed at ensuring sustainable access to potable water across urban and rural communities.

The Commissioner for Water Resources, Dr Dahiru Muhammad Hashim, disclosed this on Friday during a press conference in Kano.

He described the initiative as the second time such a long-term blueprint was being undertaken in the state’s history since the administration of the late Governor Audu Bako.

“This master plan is part of our broader efforts to address persistent water shortages, improve distribution infrastructure and ensure sustainable access to safe drinking water across the state,” Hashim said.

The commissioner said the government had recorded progress in restoring water supply to several communities in metropolitan Kano following the rehabilitation of the Challawa Water Treatment Plant and repairs to sections of the distribution network.

He disclosed that water pumped from Challawa Water Works had reached the Goron Dutse reservoirs, which have a capacity of 42.5 million litres, before being released into the distribution network.

Communities benefiting from the restoration include Goron Dutse, Gwammaja, Kwanar Dala, Jakara, Kofar Mazugal, Muskwani, Aikawa, Dukurawa, Kabara, Darma, Agadasawa, Kofar Wambai, Dukawa, Mandawari, Daneji, Fagge, Tudun Wada, Gama, Kofar Ruwa and Alfindiki, among others.

Hashim noted that some residents, including those in Alfindiki, had endured between two and three decades without running tap water.

“The restoration has brought relief to households and businesses that have suffered for decades without access to running water,” he said.

He stated that rehabilitation of the water facilities and distribution network was still ongoing, with more than 45 repair and replacement interventions already completed in different locations.

“The restoration of water pressure has exposed weaknesses in parts of the old distribution infrastructure, resulting in leakages and pipe bursts that require immediate attention,” Hashim said.

The commissioner added that rehabilitation work was continuing at the Tamburawa Water Treatment Plant and other facilities to increase the volume of treated water available for distribution.

He also announced the formal establishment of the Kano State Small Towns Water Supply Agency (KASSTOWA), with Engineer Sani Bala Danbatta appointed as Acting Managing Director and Aminu Mamman Yaro as Acting Deputy Managing Director.

Hashim urged residents to protect public water infrastructure and warned against unauthorised pipeline connections, vandalism and indiscriminate drilling around major water lines.

“Protecting water infrastructure is a shared responsibility. Residents must report burst pipes, leakages and suspected vandalism to the appropriate authorities,” he said.

The commissioner said the state government remained committed to improving access to safe and reliable drinking water across Kano.

content:
The Imo State Police Command has arrested a wanted serial armed robber, kidnapper and rapist, Olisamaka Umah, of Umuoma Irete, Owerri West Local Government Area of the state.

Force Public Relations Officer (FPRO), CSP Ani Iniedu disclosed this in a Friday statement.

The 29-year-old suspect was arrested by operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Unit, in synergy with Agwa Police Division, acting on credible intelligence.

“The suspect, who had been on the Command’s wanted list, confessed during interrogation to featuring prominently in several cases of kidnapping, armed robbery, and the rape of female victims.

“He has named fleeing gang members, whom operatives are actively tracking down to bring the entire syndicate to justice,” the statement reads in part.

Iniedu said the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Owerri is currently investigating the case.

The force spokesman further disclosed that the Kwara State Police Command has arrested four suspects linked to a robbery at Al-Hikmah University hostels.

He said operatives on stop-and-search duty at NASFAT Area, EiyeKorin, intercepted a commercial bus, leading to the arrest of 20-year-old Abdulahi Olamilekan, who jumped out and attempted to flee.

“A ringing phone found on him revealed a robbery at Al-Hikmah University hostels.

“Further investigations led to the arrest of three accomplices: Jimoh Abdulfatai (28), Abdulahi Bashir (29), and Tunji Abel,” the statement reads in part.

Iniedu said the four suspects, all ex-convicts, confessed to robbing the university hostels three times in the past.

He said police recovered two locally crafted pistols, one live cartridge, eight mobile phones, and a laptop.

“They have been positively identified by the victims,” Iniedu stated.

He added that the case is being investigated by the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Ilorin.

The post Wanted serial rapist nabbed in Imo appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Makinde Slams Fashola For Defending Tinubu’s ‘Failed’ Electricity Promise
description: The Allied Peoples Movement (APM), fielding the sitting Governor of Oyo State, Seyi Makinde, as its presidential candidate in the upcoming 2027 general election, has criticised former governor of Lagos State and Power, Works and Housing Minister, Babatunde Fashola, for defending what they described
content:
The Allied Peoples Movement (APM), fielding the sitting Governor of Oyo State, Seyi Makinde, as its presidential candidate in the upcoming 2027 general election, has criticised former governor of Lagos State and Power, Works and Housing Minister, Babatunde Fashola, for defending what they described as “worsening” electricity supply in the country.

The development came after Fashola appeared in a recent national television interview and defended President Bola Tinubu’s electricity reforms by claiming he never promised Nigerians 24-hour electricity.

Reacting to his stance, Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organization’s Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Ihediwa, in a signed statement on Friday, noted that Fashola’s “denial of the clear promise” by the President was not only “embarrassing but also shows how low All Progressives Congress (APC) leaders can descend to in the attempt to hoodwink Nigerians.”

Quoting President Tinubu’s words during the 2023 election campaigns, APM said; “For the avoidance of doubt, we will reproduce President Tinubu’s exact words:

“Whichever way, by all means necessary, you must have electricity. And you will not pay for estimated bill anymore. A promise made, will be a promise kept. If I don’t keep the promise and I come for a second term, don’t vote for me, unless I give you adequate reasons why I couldn’t deliver”, the statement read in part.

The party interpreted President Tinubu’s promise to mean: “You must have electricity” “You will not pay estimated bill anymore”. The question is, Has President Tinubu kept his promises?”

APM, however, alleged that since his assumption of office in 2023, President Tinubu’s electricity reforms have barely “moved a needle.”

“The President continues on empty boasts of electricity reforms and interventions in infrastructure, metering and market governance. What has been the result?

“Under President Tinubu’s ineffective watch Nigeria’s electricity crisis continue to worsen with Nigeria leading in worlds energy deficiency where estimated 86.8 million citizens still not having access to public electricity connection -the highest deficit globally-with no hope in sight given the consistent collapse of the national grid.

“In Fashola’s attempt to defend President Tinubu’s failed assertion that Nigerians “will not pay estimated bill anymore, he claimed that he does not have the numbers.

“Simple research would have shown him that according to the NERC, 4.70 million electricity customers in Nigeria remain without meters and are still exposed to estimated billing. Again, President Tinubu did not keep his promise.

“Fasola was quick to tell Nigerians that the President punctuated his promise with a caveat. So, what are the adequate reasons the administration has given for not keeping its promise. Tinubu apologists are always in a hurry to point to infrastructure constraints, legacy debts and the responsibilities of privately operated distribution companies. But these were the same reasons that existed before President Tinubu made the promise.

“President Tinubu has continued reforms, signed laws but we have little evidence that this has impacted availability of electricity for Nigerians.

“Our review of the NERC’s May 2025 Performance Improvement Plan order for the Transmission Company of Nigeria and the Nigerian Independent System Operator shows that only ₦1.7 billion had been disbursed for eight projects between January 2024 and January 2025.

“It also indicates that only 45% of approved funding for 2024 had reached the dedicated account while identifying other problems such as procurement-clearance delays and inadequate prioritisation as having delayed the project. in fact, the revised core portfolio fell from 142 projects to 50.

“In fact, instead of resolving the issues with the national grid, President Tinubu moved Aso Rock off the national grid and into a solar powered electricity system. We cannot find a better definition for cluelessness and lack of commitment to promise made.

“From all indications, the Tinubu administration is in above its head when it comes to solving electricity problems and no amount of defense for failure by Fashola or any other person for that matter, can turn on a light bulb.

“What is required is action. Nigeria’s problem is not simply generating electricity, or distribution, it requires a value chain approach and this is what the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) and its Presidential Candidate, Engr. Seyi Makinde offer with the RESET Nigeria Agenda.”

Makinde’s Campaign group noted that the Oyo State Governor, an Electrical Engineer, has already mapped out strategies to lift Nigeria from the current electricity crisis.

“In the Reset Nigeria Agenda, the electricity proposition is to improve the reliability and stability of supply within three years by connecting decisions, funding and accountability across the complete delivery chain.

“The Reset Agenda will move from creating new project lists to ensuring that projects are implemented.

“We therefore counsel former minister and other Fashola to stop ridiculing themselves but be courageous enough to accept President Tinubu’s manifest failures.

“Fashola should display statesmanship by supporting Engr. Makinde, whose RESET Agenda offers credible alternative to President Tinubu’s lethargic, clueless and ineffective government”, the party noted.

The post Makinde Slams Fashola For Defending Tinubu’s ‘Failed’ Electricity Promise appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Bayelsa boat tragedy: Govt warns operators against overloading
description:
The Bayelsa State Government has warned boat operators against overloading, reckless navigation and travelling without life jackets following a boat mishap that killed four people, including two children, in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state.
The government also urged operators to ens
content:
The Bayelsa State Government has warned boat operators against overloading, reckless navigation and travelling without life jackets following a boat mishap that killed four people, including two children, in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state.

The government also urged operators to ensure their boats were in good condition, respect approved passenger capacity and avoid travelling at night or during bad weather.

The state Commissioner for Information, Orientation and Strategy, Ebiuwou Koku-Obiyai, gave the warning in a statement on Saturday while reacting to the accident, which occurred along the waterway between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities.

The boat, which was conveying passengers from Ayama to Ukubie community, capsized at about 11am on Friday, leaving two adults and two children dead.

Koku-Obiyai said 24 passengers were rescued through the efforts of the Bayelsa State Police Command, local divers and other emergency responders.

She said 19 of the survivors were receiving treatment at Ayama Clinic, while five others who sustained injuries were taken to a hospital in Yenagoa for medical attention.

Appealing to boat operators and passengers to take safety precautions seriously, the commissioner said, “Overloading, speeding, recklessness and travelling without life jackets must stop. No journey is worth a life.”

She added, “Operators must respect approved passenger capacity, ensure their boats are in good condition, and avoid night and bad weather travels.”

On the rescue operation, Koku-Obiyai said the state government was providing support to ensure the exercise was concluded.

“Government is fully supporting the ongoing joint search and rescue operation and will continue to provide all necessary assistance to the divers, the police and other responders until the operation is concluded,” she said.

She commended the police, community divers and other responders for their efforts, saying their intervention led to the rescue of 24 passengers.

The commissioner also expressed condolences to the bereaved families and affected communities, including Ayama, Oweikorogha, Otuan and Ukubie.

“Our thoughts and prayers are with the families who lost their loved ones, and with those who are still receiving treatment,” she said.

The government said it would continue to work with relevant agencies, community leaders and transport unions to strengthen waterway safety and prevent a recurrence of such tragedies.

The post Bayelsa boat tragedy: Govt warns operators against overloading appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: EFCC case: ‘I’m most vilified; I shall be vindicated’– Yahaya Bello
description:
By Adegboyega Adeleye



Former Kogi State Governor Yahaya Bello has described himself as “the most transparent and the most vilified,” saying he expects to be vindicated over corruption allegations against him.



Bello spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, saying he would not co
content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Former Kogi State Governor Yahaya Bello has described himself as “the most transparent and the most vilified,” saying he expects to be vindicated over corruption allegations against him.

Bello spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, saying he would not comment on the EFCC case in detail because it was before the courts. He said Kogi State’s budgets, audited accounts, and records of performance were available online and challenged journalists and others to examine them and ask questions under the Freedom of Information Act.

“I’d rather decline to make a comment about EFCC on national television because we’re in court. However, from inception till date, all of our financials and budgets and the performance on the ground are online. We have our eight years’ budget, eight years’ final account, which we call an audited account, and the performance on the ground; we have them online,” he said.

Bello said he had experience managing public resources before becoming governor and was already financially established. He said he granted local governments financial autonomy after taking office and left the allegations for the courts to determine.

“I was never; I never assumed office as a poor man. I’m a man of my means before I assumed the office. God blessed me in my early age, and my children have been schooling in high-profile schools, both in Abuja and abroad. In any case, I don’t think I was a governor that time. The rest, I’ll leave it for them to prove it in court,” he said.

He added, “I am the most transparent and the most vilified. I’m the most transparent. I’m the most vilified. But at the end of the day, I shall be vindicated.”

Bello also said he had no regrets about his time as governor and accepted responsibility for what happened during his tenure, adding: “I gave my best.”

The EFCC is prosecuting Bello in two separate cases relating to alleged financial misconduct during his 2016–2024 governorship tenure.

The post EFCC case: ‘I’m most vilified; I shall be vindicated’– Yahaya Bello appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Army alerts Oyo residents as two-week military exercise begins Tuesday
description:
The Nigerian Army will on Tuesday begin a two-week field training exercise, code-named Exercise MUGUN BUGU V, in Old Oyo National Park, Oyo State.
The Acting Deputy Director, 2 Division, Army Public Relations, Lt. Col. Danjuma Jonah, disclosed this in a statement made available to newsmen on Friday
content:
The Nigerian Army will on Tuesday begin a two-week field training exercise, code-named Exercise MUGUN BUGU V, in Old Oyo National Park, Oyo State.

The Acting Deputy Director, 2 Division, Army Public Relations, Lt. Col. Danjuma Jonah, disclosed this in a statement made available to newsmen on Friday in Ibadan.

Jonah said the exercise would end on December 7, urging residents not to panic over the movement of troops and military equipment into the area.

He also advised farmers, herders, commuters and other residents around the park to remain calm if they heard gunshots and explosions.

According to him, the exercise forms part of the Army’s annual field training programme.

“The Nigerian Army reassures residents that necessary measures have been put in place to ensure the safety of lives and property throughout the exercise,” he said.

Recall that the General Officer Commanding, 2 Division, Nigerian Army, Maj. Gen. Auwalu Mahmuda, said the Old Oyo National Park had been taken over by the Army and converted into a training centre following the abduction and subsequent rescue of more than 40 schoolchildren and their teachers in Oriire Local Government Area of Oyo State.

Mahmuda disclosed this earlier in October when he said the Chief of Army Staff, Lt. Gen. Waidi Shuaibu, had directed the 2 Division to use the park as a training ground, adding that the Army had since taken over the facility.

content:
By Chancel Bomadi Sunday

The Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Delta South Senatorial District, Chief Adowei Freedom Binaebi, has pledged to prioritise the needs of riverine communities through inclusive representation if elected in the 2027 general elections.

Binaebi made the pledge on Thursday during a consultation visit to Bomadi, headquarters of Bomadi Local Government Area of Delta State.

He said his decision to contest the senatorial seat was informed by the need to give riverine communities a stronger voice in the National Assembly and ensure that their basic needs received adequate attention.

The candidate also promised to initiate youth capacity-building programmes aimed at equipping young people with relevant skills and addressing poverty in the area.

He appealed to the people of Bomadi to support his ambition, assuring them that he would not disappoint them if elected.

“From all indications, the people are suffering due to the mismanagement in governance, and I have resolved to contest in order to deliver my people from this plight.

“I will ensure inclusive representation for the people of the riverine communities when entrusted with the mandate, and I will never let them down,” he said.

Binaebi urged residents to vote for NDC candidates across elective positions in the 2027 elections, describing such support as necessary to enable the party fulfil its promises.

“I urge the people of Bomadi to cast their votes five over five for the NDC candidates in 2027, and we will honour and fulfil the mandate entrusted to us,” he added.

title: Sanwo-Olu targets 2,000 more homes before leaving office
description:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni



Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has pledged to deliver more than 2,000 additional housing units before the end of his tenure in 2027 as part of efforts to address the state’s housing deficit.







The governor made the commitment on Friday while commissioning two
content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has pledged to deliver more than 2,000 additional housing units before the end of his tenure in 2027 as part of efforts to address the state’s housing deficit.

The governor made the commitment on Friday while commissioning two residential estates comprising 294 housing units in the Ogombo and Ajah areas of Eti-Osa Local Government Area.

He also called for the speedy passage of the revised Lagos State Tenancy and Recovery of Premises Bill into law, while promising a four-lane expansion of Ogombo Road to improve access and ease traffic congestion in the area.

Sanwo-Olu disclosed that more than 2,000 housing units developed by the Ministry of Housing were ready for commissioning in Ibeshe, Sangotedo, Egan and Epe.

He added that other housing schemes being undertaken by the Lagos State Development and Property Corporation (LSDPC) were ongoing in Shogunro, Ogba, Apapa and Ogudu.

The governor said government alone could not meet the housing demands of Lagos, Nigeria’s commercial nerve centre, stressing that his administration was adopting a partnership model involving the provision of land, regulatory oversight and an enabling environment to attract private-sector investment.

The two commissioned projects are the 165-unit Treasure Estate at Ajiwe, Ogombo, developed by LSDPC in partnership with AKF Properties Limited, and the 129-unit Brooks Habitat at Abraham Adesanya, Ajah, facilitated by the Ministry of Housing in partnership with Brook Assets and Resources Limited.

Treasure Estate comprises two-bedroom terrace houses, three-bedroom flats and three-bedroom terrace houses, with facilities including a swimming pool, gymnasium, five-a-side football pitch, jogging tracks, water treatment plant and modern drainage systems.

Brooks Habitat, located on 2.3 hectares of land across 20 blocks, comprises 42 two-bedroom flats, 42 three-bedroom flats with service quarters and 45 three-bedroom terrace houses.

Its facilities include a clinic, gymnasium, solar-powered streetlights, paved access roads and dedicated security.

Addressing infrastructure needs in the rapidly developing Eti-Osa corridor, Sanwo-Olu pledged that Ogombo Road would be expanded into a four-lane carriageway, with improved drainage infrastructure.

He commended the developers, engineers and artisans involved in the projects, saying their contributions had helped deliver housing options across different income categories.

Earlier, the Commissioner for Housing, Moruf Akinderu-Fatai, urged the Lagos State House of Assembly to expedite the passage of the revised Lagos State Tenancy and Recovery of Premises Bill.

He said a sustainable housing framework required strong legislation to address unfair rental practices and protect the interests of both landlords and tenants.

Providing details of the Ogombo housing scheme, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of LSDPC, Ayodeji Joseph, disclosed that the two-bedroom terrace units were priced at N65 million.

He said prospective buyers could access mortgage facilities through the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN) and the Mortgage Refinancing and Infrastructure Fund.

Joseph added that four other housing projects within the axis were nearing completion.

In his response, the Majority Leader of the Lagos State House of Assembly, Noheem Adams, assured residents that the revised tenancy bill would be passed into law “very soon”.

He commended Sanwo-Olu for what he described as tangible housing and infrastructure development across Eti-Osa and other parts of the state.

The post Sanwo-Olu targets 2,000 more homes before leaving office appeared first on Vanguard News.
