title: CITN urges Nigerians to report unprofessional conduct of members
description:
…Inducts 2326 Associates
The Chartered Institute of Taxation of Nigeria (CITN) has urged Nigerians to report any member found engaging in unprofessional conduct, assuring that commensurate disciplinary measures would be taken against those found culpable to protect the integrity, credibility and sta
content:
…Inducts 2326 Associates

The Chartered Institute of Taxation of Nigeria (CITN) has urged Nigerians to report any member found engaging in unprofessional conduct, assuring that commensurate disciplinary measures would be taken against those found culpable to protect the integrity, credibility and standards of the tax profession.

Speaking at the 55th induction ceremony of the Institute which saw the admission of 2326 Associate members, the 17th President & Chairman in Council of the Institute, Mr. Innocent Ohagwa, while congratulating the new members, warned that a tax professional who is not tax compliant has no moral standing to teach compliance.

Ohagwa reminded the inductees that the Institute has raised the bar of competence and ethical standards and every member, particularly the practitioners must rise to meet it.

The tax professional explained that technical competence is now non-negotiable for recertification, saying, “ethical conduct has become the bedrock of trust. Professionalism is the new benchmark for relevance. And each of you, by choosing this path, has committed to uphold these values at the highest standards”

CITN Chief reminded tax professionals that Nigeria is at the implementation phase of far-reaching tax reforms and the role of the tax professional has never carried more weight than today. “It is imperative to note that our engagements with members and stakeholders, concerns have been raised about implementation challenges. I therefore urge all members, businesses and stakeholders to support the implementation and to stay constructive on the tax reform laws”

He advised members keep reading and learning, advise with integrity, and where necessary, collaborate with other professionals to exchange knowledge, share experiences and strengthen their skills.

The CITN Act, among other things, established an Investigating Panel and a Disciplinary Tribunal to deal with members, whether practitioners, administrators or others, who cross the red line by violating our code of ethics or acting contrary to professional standards.

“The general public, institutions, clients and members of the Institute are encouraged to report any instance of unprofessional conduct or behaviour unbecoming of a tax professional to the Institute. CITN will not waver or fail to investigate and deal with any matter that comes to its attention through public knowledge or observation, whether or not a formal report has been submitted”

He informed that being a member of CITN is a call to higher service. “You must uphold integrity, pursue excellence and ensure that you are always part of the solution and never otherwise” he added.

In welcome address, the Chairman, Membership and Professional Conduct Committee, Dr. Yemi Sanni, charged the tax professionals to uphold the highest level of professionalism, coupled with honesty and integrity.

“You are the first set of inductees to be admitted after a full year of the new tax regime. Since January, 2026, the comprehensive reforms —the consolidation and harmonisation of our tax laws, the new tax administration framework and the restructuring of our revenue institutions — have moved from paper into practice.

“Taxpayers are adjusting to new rules, tax authorities are building new systems, and many questions of interpretation are still being settled. This is precisely where the profession is most needed, and it is where you now have a seat at the table”

Sanni added that their success depends on competent and ethical professionals who would advise taxpayers correctly, help businesses comply, assist the authorities in administering the law fairly, and speak up constructively where refinements are needed.

“Your contributions will support government’s revenue mobilisation efforts, protect businesses, promote investment and strengthen public trust in the tax system. I must remind you that the practice of taxation is now increasingly digital. Electronic filing, e-invoicing, data matching and analytics are changing how tax is administered and how compliance is tested”

He advised that professional must be as comfortable with data and technology as with the provisions of the law, saying, “I urge you to embrace these tools early and to use them responsibly. You must adhere strictly to the institute’s Code of Conduct and continuously improve your skills through Mandatory Continuing Professional Development in order to remain relevant in today’s globalised, technologically driven and rapidly evolving business environment”

He emphasized the need to demonstrate competence, discipline and a high level of ethical conduct in the discharge of their professional responsibilities.

“Your certificate is a licence of trust. One unethical act can undo years of hard work, and it reflects not only on you but on every member of this Institute. The current tax regime demands a great deal from professionals in this field, and we must not be found wanting” he warned.

The post CITN urges Nigerians to report unprofessional conduct of members appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: NUC approves Oyinlola’s university in Osun
description:
The National Universities Commission has approved the establishment of Alolade Oyinlola University in Okuku, Osun State, founded by former Governor of the state, Prince Olagunsoye Oyinlola.
The approval was conveyed in a letter dated November 9, 2026, and signed by the NUC Executive Secretary, Prof.
content:
The National Universities Commission has approved the establishment of Alolade Oyinlola University in Okuku, Osun State, founded by former Governor of the state, Prince Olagunsoye Oyinlola.

The approval was conveyed in a letter dated November 9, 2026, and signed by the NUC Executive Secretary, Prof. Abdullahi Ribadu.

“The letter confirmed the Federal Executive Council’s approval for the issuance of a provisional licence to the institution following its fulfilment of statutory requirements,” the university said in a statement on Saturday.

Under the approval conditions, the university will operate under the academic and administrative mentorship of Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife, for five years.

“OAU will provide guidance on governance, staff recruitment, admissions, examinations, quality assurance, and institutional development, and will submit periodic reports to the NUC.

“The mentorship is also intended to support the university in developing its administrative systems, recruiting academic staff, and preparing to commence teaching activities,” the statement added.

The university said its academic development will be implemented in five phases.

The first phase will comprise the Faculties of Communication and Media Studies; Humanities, Management and Social Sciences; Basic Medical and Allied Health Sciences; Natural and Applied Sciences; and Science and Computing.

It will also include units for Basic Sciences, General Studies and Entrepreneurship.

The second phase will introduce the Faculty of Law and the School of Postgraduate Studies, while Environmental Sciences will follow in the third phase and Engineering and Technology in the fourth. The fifth phase will focus on consolidating the university’s academic development.

The NUC requires resource verification and regulatory approval before the university can commence academic activities. Any new faculty or academic programme must also receive prior approval from the commission.

The provisional licence is subject to a three-year probationary period, after which a statutory licence may be issued following a satisfactory assessment.

Members of the university’s Planning Committee include former NUC Executive Secretary Emeritus, Prof. Peter Okebukola; pioneer Vice-Chancellor of Osun State University, Prof. Sola Akinrinade; former Vice-Chancellor of OAU, Prof. Eyitope Ogunbodede; Dr Suleman Ramon-Yusuf; and former Deputy Vice-Chancellor for Academic, Research, Innovations and Partnerships at Osun State University, Prof. Anthony Kola-Olusanya.

Congratulating the institution on the approval, Ribadu expressed confidence in its potential contribution to higher education in the country.

“We look forward to the contribution of Alolade Oyinlola University, Okuku, Osun State, to the delivery of quality University education in Nigeria,” the letter stated.

Oyinlola, a retired Brigadier-General, is a member of a royal family of Okuku in Odo-Otin Local Government Area of Osun State.

He served as Military Administrator of Lagos State from 1993 to 1996 and as civilian Governor of Osun State from 2003 to 2010.

During his tenure as governor, he established Osun State University.

The new university is named after his late mother, Alolade Oyinlola.

Oyinlola also founded Alolade Oyinlola College of Health Sciences and Information Technology in Okuku in 2024.

The post NUC approves Oyinlola’s university in Osun appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

description:

The five-day training programme, which ended on Friday in Gombe,
content:
The Federal Government has trained retiring civil servants from the North-East zone on financial planning, investment decisions and retirement benefits management as part of efforts to prepare them for life after active public service.

The five-day training programme, which ended on Friday in Gombe, was organised by the Bureau of Public Service Reforms (BPSR) under its 2026 Pre-Retirement Training Programme for Retiring Officers of Federal Parastatals.

The programme seeks to equip public servants approaching retirement with practical knowledge and skills to manage their finances, health and personal affairs while exploring opportunities for productive engagement after leaving government service.

Speaking during the programme, the Director-General (DG) of BPSR, Dasuki Ibrahim Arabi, said the Federal Government had approved funding to train 660 retiring public servants drawn from 700 Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) across the country, with the exercise being conducted in two batches.

He explained that the initiative was designed to recognise officers who had dedicated between 30 and 35 years to public service while helping them make a smooth transition from active employment to retirement.

According to him, the training covers personal financial planning, budgeting, savings, investment decisions, wealth preservation and prudent management of retirement benefits.

Other areas include entrepreneurship, alternative sources of income, healthcare, psychological adjustment and pension administration.

He stressed that successful retirement required more than the payment of gratuity and pensions, urging participants to make informed financial decisions and develop sustainable sources of income.

The BPSR chief also encouraged retiring officers to embrace technology and learn how to use artificial intelligence, while exercising caution when accessing digital platforms and applications.

He advised participants to maintain contact with pension desk officers in their respective MDAs to obtain relevant information and assistance regarding their retirement entitlements.

He further called on government institutions to sustain their relationships with retired employees, stressing that retirement should not mark the end of their relevance or contributions to society.

The DG urged federal parastatals to institutionalise retirement-preparation mechanisms, maintain accurate personnel and pension records, process retirement documentation promptly and provide administrative support to retiring officers.

He described retired public servants as valuable national assets whose professional experience and institutional knowledge could continue to contribute to national development through mentorship, consultancy and community engagement.

The initiative forms part of the Federal Government’s broader public service reform and welfare agenda, which seeks to support public servants at every stage of their employment, including retirement.

title: Radda Flags Off ₦1.4bn Ingawa Hospital Upgrade, Commissions Road
description: Katsina State Governor, Malam Dikko Umaru Radda, has flagged off the comprehensive renovation and upgrade of Ingawa General Hospital at a cost of over ₦1.4 billion, reaffirming his administration’s commitment to strengthening healthcare infrastructure while mobilising support for the re-electi
content:
Katsina State Governor, Malam Dikko Umaru Radda, has flagged off the comprehensive renovation and upgrade of Ingawa General Hospital at a cost of over ₦1.4 billion, reaffirming his administration’s commitment to strengthening healthcare infrastructure while mobilising support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general elections.

The hospital project, awarded to an indigenous construction firm, will provide additional structures, modern medical facilities and state-of-the-art equipment aimed at transforming the hospital into a contemporary healthcare centre capable of serving Ingawa and neighbouring communities.

Speaking during the foundation-laying ceremony on Friday, Governor Radda also commissioned the newly completed 1.65-kilometre Ingawa township road, constructed by the Ingawa Local Government Council, describing it as a practical demonstration of the dividends of democracy.

He attributed the project’s success to the local government autonomy reforms introduced by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, saying direct allocation of funds to councils has empowered them to undertake projects that directly impact the lives of the people.

“Local government autonomy under President Tinubu has strengthened councils to receive funds directly and execute projects that meet the needs of their communities,” the Governor stated.

He commended the council leadership and stakeholders for completing the road project, expressing confidence that it would improve transportation, stimulate economic activities, and enhance the quality of life of residents.

Earlier, the Commissioner for Health, Alhaji Musa Adamu Funtua, disclosed that the hospital upgrade would include the construction of doctors’ quarters, an Accident and Emergency Unit, as well as the supply and installation of modern medical equipment.

He noted that the facility, which serves Ingawa and surrounding communities, had not witnessed any major renovation since the administration of the late President Umaru Musa Yar’Adua as Governor of Katsina State, and praised Governor Radda for responding to the healthcare needs of the people.

The Governor later addressed a massive Tinubu-Dikko-Jobe Campaign Rally in Ingawa, where he described the large turnout as a strong endorsement of President Tinubu’s leadership and the APC.

“Today, we have witnessed something extraordinary in Ingawa. You have demonstrated your happiness, love and appreciation for the legacy of our father, the late Engineer Mohammed Kanti Bello,” Governor Radda told the cheering crowd.

He appreciated the people for supporting the emergence of Hon. Mustapha Muhammad Kanti Bello as the APC candidate for the Kankia-Kusada-Ingawa Federal Constituency, expressing confidence in his ability to provide effective representation.

Governor Radda also praised Engr. Dr. Sani Magaji for his contributions to Ingawa’s development and announced that his administration would soon flag off road projects linking Ingawa and Kankia to improve connectivity and accelerate development.

He conveyed the appreciation of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima to the people of Ingawa for their continued loyalty and support.

Director-General of the Tinubu-Dikko-Jobe Campaign, Architect Ahmed Musa Dangiwa, described effective representation as one that attracts projects and opportunities to the people, urging voters to support APC candidates across all levels.

He observed that the opportunity to represent the Kankia-Kusada-Ingawa Federal Constituency had returned to Ingawa after previous representation by Kankia and Kusada, while also expressing confidence in the APC senatorial candidate for Katsina North, Malam Nasiru Hayatu.

Similarly, APC State Chairman, Dr. Bishir Gambo Saulawa, commended the people of Ingawa for the warm reception accorded to the campaign team and urged party members to sustain unity and peaceful coexistence.

The Speaker of the Katsina State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Nasiru Yahaya Daura, alongside other party stakeholders, also lauded Governor Radda’s development initiatives across the state.

At the palace of the District Head of Ingawa, Alhaji Tukur Suleiman Dambo II (Sarkin Fulanin Dambo), Governor Radda praised the longstanding unity among Ingawa, Kankia and Kusada, describing Ingawa as a community with deep personal significance.

“Whenever I visit this palace, I feel I have come home. My maternal grandparents hailed from this community,” he said.

The Governor commended political leaders who stepped aside to ensure consensus within the APC, describing their actions as evidence of maturity and commitment to party unity.

“The love you are showing Mustapha is recognition of the good name his late father earned. A legacy of integrity is more valuable than material possessions,” he added.

Reaffirming his role as Katsina State Coordinator of the Tinubu-Shettima Campaign, Governor Radda pledged to lead the APC campaign across Ingawa, Kankia and Kusada while seeking a second term alongside his deputy, Hon. Faruk Lawal Jobe.

Highlighting his administration’s achievements, the Governor cited the ongoing upgrade of Ingawa General Hospital and the completion of the 39-kilometre Ingawa-Shargalle Road within 11 months as evidence of his government’s commitment to delivering infrastructure and improving the welfare of citizens.

In his remarks, the District Head of Ingawa expressed appreciation for the Governor’s interventions in education, healthcare and road construction, describing the projects as visible evidence of responsive leadership.

He also commended the improved security situation in the state, noting that travelling between Kano and Katsina at night, once considered risky, had become significantly safer.

The traditional ruler assured Governor Radda of the community’s total support while appealing for the construction of a dam, rehabilitation of the Manomawa-Yaya Road and renovation of staff quarters at the Rural Boarding School in Ingawa.

The Chairman of Ingawa Local Government, Hon. Abubakar Idris 02, also thanked the Governor for his continued support and development projects, pledging sustained collaboration to advance the welfare of the people.

title: 11 dead, over 180 hospitalised after drinking alcohol
description:

The victims fell ill after consuming the liquor, Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh said in a statement on Friday.

content:
At least 11 people have died and more than 180 have been hospitalised after drinking suspected tainted alcohol in India’s northeastern state of Manipur.

The victims fell ill after consuming the liquor, Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh said in a statement on Friday.

“Over 180 patients have been admitted in the two hospitals so far, while the death toll has reached 11 in the last 48 hours,” the statement said.

He also ordered an enquiry into the incident, saying those responsible would be arrested and punished.

Deaths from illicit or adulterated alcohol are regularly reported in India, where cheap liquor sold outside regulated channels can contain methanol, a highly toxic industrial chemical.

In May, at least 15 people died after drinking methanol-laced illicit liquor in Pune and neighbouring Pimpri-Chinchwad in the western state of Maharashtra.

In August, 13 people died and more than 60 were affected after consuming methanol-tainted liquor in Gujarat’s Bhavnagar district, according to local media reports.

Such liquor is widely consumed across India, where a bottle is sometimes sold for less than a dollar. If ingested, methanol can cause blindness, liver damage and death in larger concentrations.

title: Four die, 24 rescued as Bayelsa burial boat capsizes
description:
Four persons, including two children, have died after a boat conveying passengers to a burial ceremony capsized in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State on Friday.







Twenty-four other passengers were rescued following the incident, which occurred at about 11am while the boat was
content:
Four persons, including two children, have died after a boat conveying passengers to a burial ceremony capsized in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State on Friday.

Twenty-four other passengers were rescued following the incident, which occurred at about 11am while the boat was travelling from Ayama community to Ukubie.

The Bayelsa State Police Command said preliminary findings indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways.

The police spokesperson, Musa Mohammed, disclosed this in a statement on Friday, alleging that some passengers had urged the operator to steer towards the riverbank after the fault developed, but he declined and continued the journey before the boat capsized.

Mohammed said the bodies of two adults and two children had been recovered and deposited at the mortuary of the Federal Medical Centre, Yenagoa.

He said 24 survivors were rescued, with 19 taken to Ayama Clinic, while five others who sustained injuries were transferred to Family Care Hospital in Yenagoa for treatment.

The police spokesperson disclosed that the boat operator, identified only as Omovie, had fled the scene, while the boat manager, identified as MV Bina, had been taken into custody for investigation.

He added that the police marine section had been deployed to reinforce search and rescue operations, while the Divisional Police Officer in Oporoma was coordinating efforts with local divers and other emergency responders.

Mohammed said investigations were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the tragedy, assuring that search and rescue operations would continue until everyone on board had been accounted for.

title: UNICEF raises alarm over 624,000 out-of-school children
description:
By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto



The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has raised concerns over the high number of out-of-school children in Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara states, disclosing that about 624,000 children have been identified as being outside the classroom across the three states.
content:
By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto

The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has raised concerns over the high number of out-of-school children in Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara states, disclosing that about 624,000 children have been identified as being outside the classroom across the three states.

The organisation said although about 68,000 children had benefited from interventions to return them to school, the scale of the challenge required urgent government action, increased investment and stronger community mobilisation.

UNICEF’s Chief of Field Office in Sokoto, Dr Michael Juma, made this known at a media briefing organised by the organisation’s Sokoto Field Office as part of activities marking the 2026 World Children’s Day.

He called for coordinated action by governments, media organisations, traditional institutions, religious leaders and community stakeholders to address challenges confronting children in the region.

Juma urged journalists across the three states to intensify public enlightenment, investigative reporting and advocacy to promote children’s rights, strengthen government accountability and ensure access to education, healthcare, nutrition and other essential services.

Describing the media as a critical partner in advancing children’s rights, he said journalists must go beyond reporting events to exposing gaps in service delivery and holding relevant authorities accountable.

“The media are important duty-bearers in advancing children’s rights. Journalists must provide balanced coverage that highlights development achievements while drawing attention to persistent gaps affecting the wellbeing of children,” he said.

He reaffirmed UNICEF’s commitment to strengthening collaboration with the governments of Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara, development partners, traditional and religious leaders, and grassroots organisations to guarantee children access to quality and inclusive education, healthcare, adequate nutrition, safe drinking water and social protection.

Providing an account of interventions undertaken through UNICEF’s partnerships with the three state governments, Juma disclosed that approximately 98,000 children had benefited from the Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL) programme, designed to improve foundational literacy and numeracy.

He said the organisation was also supporting teacher professional development, provision of instructional materials, accelerated basic education, integrated Qur’anic education and innovative learning opportunities, including radio-based education and the Nigeria Learning Passport.

According to him, the interventions are particularly targeted at children affected by insecurity, displacement and other emergencies.

On healthcare and immunisation, Juma disclosed that approximately 7.8 million children across the three states had been reached through measles-rubella vaccination, while more than five million children were vaccinated during the last concluded polio immunisation campaign.

He further said Kebbi State had recorded progress in malaria vaccination, with approximately 148,000 children receiving the first dose and 130,000 receiving the second dose.

He stressed that effective healthcare delivery and sustained immunisation campaigns remained essential to reducing preventable childhood deaths and improving children’s survival.

On malnutrition, the UNICEF official commended the Sokoto and Zamfara State Governments for committing approximately N100 million and N500 million respectively towards the procurement of Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food (RUTF), used in treating children suffering from severe acute malnutrition.

He also acknowledged the Kebbi State Government’s contribution of approximately N540 million towards free medical services for children.

Juma highlighted UNICEF-supported social health insurance interventions, which he said had expanded healthcare access to approximately 86,000 beneficiaries in Zamfara, 18,000 in Sokoto and 10,000 in Kebbi.

In the area of child protection, he said UNICEF had supported the development of child protection legislation, Family Court Rules and social protection policies aimed at strengthening the protection, rehabilitation and reintegration of vulnerable children, including those in conflict with the law.

He also highlighted the establishment of a Special Care Baby Unit in Sokoto, with similar interventions being advanced in Kebbi and Zamfara to improve medical attention for premature and low-birth-weight babies.

Despite the interventions, Juma acknowledged that significant challenges remained, particularly the large number of children still excluded from formal education.

He said the gap between the 624,000 children identified as out of school and the approximately 68,000 reached through re-enrolment efforts required urgent government intervention, increased funding and stronger community participation.

“Identifying these children is only the first step. The real challenge is ensuring that they return to school and remain there to acquire the knowledge and skills necessary for their future,” he said.

Addressing concerns over declining international development funding, Juma explained that the financial challenge was a global development issue and not peculiar to Nigeria.

He said UNICEF was intensifying its resource mobilisation strategies to sustain critical interventions and support state governments, assuring that education programmes across the three states had not been affected by the funding decline experienced earlier in the year.

On the difficulties of delivering services in remote and insecurity-affected communities, he said UNICEF was working through government structures, field facilitators and third-party monitoring arrangements to ensure that interventions reached vulnerable children and women.

He called for stronger coordination at ward and local government levels, stressing that protecting children’s rights was a collective responsibility that should not be left to UNICEF or government institutions alone.

“We need the active participation of government agencies, development partners, civil society organisations, traditional and religious leaders, community structures and parents. Journalists must also use their platforms to educate communities, generate demand for essential services and hold stakeholders accountable for their commitments to children,” he said.

As part of efforts to strengthen media participation, Juma invited journalists to join future field visits to document UNICEF-supported projects and independently assess their impact on vulnerable communities.

He also urged media organisations across the three states to support the December 5 to 11, 2026 polio immunisation campaign through public awareness, pre-campaign mobilisation and community engagement to encourage parents and caregivers to present eligible children for vaccination.

The briefing concluded with a renewed call for collective action as the world marks the 2026 World Children’s Day under the theme, “My Day. My Rights. My Future.”

UNICEF maintained that protecting children’s rights must go beyond policy declarations and public commitments to sustained investment, effective service delivery and measurable accountability, warning that the future of the region depended largely on the commitment of its leaders and communities to protect, educate and empower the next generation.

The post UNICEF raises alarm over 624,000 out-of-school children appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: NCoS releases names, photos of two fleeing death-row inmates in Kwara
description:
The Nigerian Correctional Service has released the identities and photographs of two death-row inmates who escaped from the Medium Security Custodial Centre, Oke-Kura, in Ilorin, Kwara State.
The Kwara State Command, in a public notice dated November 20, 2026, identified the escapees as “Segun Abrah
content:
The Nigerian Correctional Service has released the identities and photographs of two death-row inmates who escaped from the Medium Security Custodial Centre, Oke-Kura, in Ilorin, Kwara State.

The Kwara State Command, in a public notice dated November 20, 2026, identified the escapees as “Segun Abraham Nasiru, 38, and Oluwasegun Omoyajowo Ajiboye, 41.”

The notice, which was shared on the Service’s X handle on Saturday, contained photographs of the two inmates and details of their physical appearances and backgrounds to aid their identification and re-arrest.

According to the notice, Nasiru is a male inmate from Iloro Ekiti in Ijero Local Government Area of Ekiti State. He is 5.6 feet tall, has a light complexion and is of Yoruba origin.

Ajiboye, on the other hand, is from Lokoja in Kogi State. He is 6 feet tall, has a dark complexion and is of Okun origin.

“The Service solicits the cooperation of the general public in recapturing the fugitives. Anyone with useful information about their whereabouts should please contact the nearest Custodial Centre or Police Station,” the notice stated.

It provided the following telephone numbers for members of the public to report information: 08064756761 and 08075050006.

The Controller of Corrections, Kwara State Command, also assured the public that “no effort will be spared to recapture the fugitives,” adding that security had been strengthened across custodial facilities.

The escape was reported on Wednesday after the inmates allegedly broke through and scaled the perimeter wall of the Oke-Kura facility.

The PUNCH had reported that one of the escapees, identified as Abraham, was a repeat escapee who had previously fled from the Mandala Custodial Centre before he was rearrested and transferred to Oke-Kura.

Speaking to journalists at the facility on Thursday, the Controller-General of the Nigerian Correctional Service, Sylvester Mwakuche, acknowledged indications of negligence in the circumstances surrounding the escape.

He described the incident as unfortunate and unacceptable, warning that officers and inmates found culpable would face consequences.

“Naturally, they will face the music,” he said.

Mwakuche also said the Minister of Interior was displeased with the incident and that investigations would establish how the inmates escaped and determine those responsible.

The post NCoS releases names, photos of two fleeing death-row inmates in Kwara appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Morning recap: Petrol imports jump 47%, Odegbami survives machete attack, FG’s N100,000 grant, other stories
description:
Top headlines this morning include a 47 per cent rebound in petrol imports in October despite rising domestic refining, and former Super Eagles captain Segun Odegbami narrowly escaping death in a machete attack at his Abeokuta residence.
Meanwhile, families continue to agonise over 640 pupils and wo
content:
Top headlines this morning include a 47 per cent rebound in petrol imports in October despite rising domestic refining, and former Super Eagles captain Segun Odegbami narrowly escaping death in a machete attack at his Abeokuta residence.

Meanwhile, families continue to agonise over 640 pupils and worshippers still in captivity months after their abduction.

In another development, the Nigeria Customs Service has suspended training for 3,852 new recruits amid Federal Character Commission probes.

Also, mega churches face renewed scrutiny over succession plans following the Fountain of Life Church crisis.

The recap in full:

Petrol imports jump 47% despite local refining

Nigeria’s petrol imports rose by 47 per cent in October to 15 million litres per day, according to the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, reversing the previous month’s decline and highlighting continued reliance on foreign supplies even as domestic refining expands.

Domestic refineries supplied 31.9 million litres per day (up 12 per cent), accounting for about 68 per cent of the 46.9 million litres received daily.

Read the full story below: https://punchng.com/petrol-imports-jump-47-despite-local-refining/

Ex-Super Eagles captain Odegbami escapes death in machete attack

Former Super Eagles captain Segun Odegbami, 74, narrowly escaped death after armed men wielding machetes attacked him at his residence in Ibara GRA, Abeokuta, Ogun State, in the early hours of Friday.

The attackers overpowered his domestic staff and driver before assaulting him in his bedroom.

Read the full story below: https://punchng.com/ex-super-eagles-captain-odegbami-escapes-death-in-machete-attack/

Forgotten: Families agonise over pupils, worshippers still in captivity

No fewer than 640 Nigerians, including schoolchildren and worshippers, remain in captivity months after their abduction.

These include 78 schoolchildren abducted in Borno State (six months ago), 547 worshippers from a Niger State mosque attack (three months ago), and 15 schoolgirls taken in Rafi, Niger State, on October 31.

Read the full story below: https://punchng.com/forgotten-families-agonise-over-pupils-worshippers-still-in-captivity/

Customs suspend recruits’ training as FCC probes recruitment

The Nigeria Customs Service has temporarily suspended training for 3,852 newly recruited officers following concerns raised by the Federal Character Commission over alleged irregularities in the selection and invitation process.

Both agencies have agreed to further consultations to resolve the issues. The recruitment exercise had attracted over 573,000 applications.

Read the full story below: https://punchng.com/customs-suspend-recruits-training-as-fcc-probes-recruitment/

Mega churches face succession heat

The leadership crisis at the Fountain of Life Church, Lagos, involving Senior Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and the Board of Trustees, has sparked fresh scrutiny of succession arrangements in major Pentecostal churches, including Deeper Life, RCCG and Living Faith Church.

Comments by Pastor William Kumuyi, Pastor Enoch Adeboye and Bishop David Oyedepo on succession have resurfaced amid the controversy, which has led to a court order restraining Odukoya from acting as senior pastor.

Read the full story below: https://punchng.com/mega-churches-face-succession-heat/

EXPLAINER: How to apply for FG’s N100,000 family grant

The Federal Government’s Nigeria Family Strengthening and Development Programme is offering N100,000 cash support to vulnerable households.

Eligible applicants must be Nigerian citizens by birth, aged 18–65, with a valid NIN. Registration is via nfsp.ng/signup.

Beneficiaries will be selected based on poverty and vulnerability criteria and notified by SMS. The programme warns against fraudsters demanding payment for inclusion.

Read the full story below: https://punchng.com/explainer-how-to-apply-for-fgs-n100000-family-grant/

title: Amnesty kicks as Sharia court jails 19-yr-old teenager for insulting Kano Hisbah Board, commander
description:
Amnesty International has strongly condemned the sentencing by a Sharia court in Kano State of a 19-year-old TikTok user, Zainab Abubakar, to five months in prison and 10 strokes of cane for “insulting the state Hisbah Board and its Commander Aminu Ibrahim Daurawa.”
The court, which sat at the Shara
content:
Amnesty International has strongly condemned the sentencing by a Sharia court in Kano State of a 19-year-old TikTok user, Zainab Abubakar, to five months in prison and 10 strokes of cane for “insulting the state Hisbah Board and its Commander Aminu Ibrahim Daurawa.”

The court, which sat at the Sharada premises of the Kano State Hisbah Board headquarters, delivered the judgment on Wednesday, November 18.

“It is flabbergasting that someone can be made to appear before a court and stand trial, let alone serve a sentence and 10 strokes of cane for simply having expressed a strong opinion,” Amnesty said in a Friday statement.

The organisation described Zainab Abubakar’s trial and sentencing as the latest development in Kano authorities’ sustained and systematic repression against their youth.

“Five months in jail for ‘insulting the head of Hisbah’ is an outrageous sentence. It is also an indication of increasing lawless excesses of Hisbah targeting youth with less privileged backgrounds,” it said.

Amnesty stressed that the right to freely express one’s views, even if shocking or offensive, is protected by international human rights law, adding that no one should face punishment for freely speaking their minds.

It called on the authorities to quash Zainab Abubakar’s conviction and ensure her immediate and unconditional release.

By Benjamin Njoku



The highly anticipated Nollywood classic, “Issakaba Returns” stormed the domestic box office, recording a spectacular opening weekend gross of N47.8 million to become the highest-grossing debut ever for an action thriller.



The film, directed by popular filmmaker and producer,
content:
By Benjamin Njoku

The highly anticipated Nollywood classic, “Issakaba Returns” stormed the domestic box office, recording a spectacular opening weekend gross of N47.8 million to become the highest-grossing debut ever for an action thriller.

The film, directed by popular filmmaker and producer, Lancelot Oduwa Imasuen, premiered last Wednesday at Silverbird Cinemas, Victoria Island, Lagos.

Celebrating the feat, Lancelot, fondly called D’Guvnor, thanked everyone who showed up, bought tickets, filled the cinemas and embraced “Issakaba Returns” with so much love.

“To everyone who has supported this journey, shared the excitement, spread the word and made the opening weekend this remarkable, I do not take your love for granted.

“This is more than numbers. It is a testament to the love, nostalgia and connection you all have with this story.

“N47.8 million opening weekend gross, and this is only the beginning!

“Thank you for believing in us. Thank you for showing up. The love has been organic, and we feel every bit of it,” Lancelot said.

The premiere of “Issakaba Returns” was spectacular and memorable. The evening exploded into war songs, cultural dance and gyration as the film began its cinema run.

Long before the lights went down inside the cinema hall, the carnival had already begun outside. Drummers, dancers and chanting fans set the mood, recreating the fearless spirit of the Issakaba Boys who, 25 years ago, stood against evil in the South-East.

For the lead character, Sam Dede, the return is more than nostalgia. It is a message.

Speaking at the premiere, he said the evils the Issakaba Boys fought a quarter of a century ago, kidnapping, money rituals, human trafficking are still ravaging society today.

First released in 2001 and inspired by real-life vigilante movements, the original “Issakaba” became a cultural phenomenon.

title: Davido and Chioma: The love story continues
description:
By Benjamin Njoku



Afrobeats superstar Davido is known for flaunting his wife, Chioma Adeleke, on social media, displaying public affection and storming international show venues in her company.







It is no surprise, therefore, that the three-time Grammy nominee has taken their romance to the
content:
By Benjamin Njoku

Afrobeats superstar Davido is known for flaunting his wife, Chioma Adeleke, on social media, displaying public affection and storming international show venues in her company.

It is no surprise, therefore, that the three-time Grammy nominee has taken their romance to the studio, borrowing a leaf from the likes of Adekunle Gold and Simi, Banky W and Adesuwa Etomi, as well as Beyoncé and Jay-Z, who have all turned their love stories into music.

For Davido, Chioma has never just been his wife. She has been his muse from the very beginning.

Their love story in music started in 2018 with ‘Assurance’, the birthday gift Davido dedicated to Chioma when they were still dating. Chioma starred in the video, and the song became one of the most iconic love anthems in Afrobeats history.

She returned in 2020 for ‘1 Milli’, whose wedding-themed video further celebrated their relationship.

Nearly eight years after ‘Assurance’, ‘Already Falling’ brings that story full circle, from young lovers to husband and wife.

The song, the eighth track on Davido’s sixth studio album, “ORIADÉ”, was released on July 31, 2026. It blends English, Yoruba and Nigerian Pidgin, and reimagines Elvis Presley’s timeless classic ‘Can’t Help Falling in Love’ through an Afrobeats lens with background vocals by Peruzz

The official video, released on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, stars Chioma as his leading lady once again.

Directed by Meji Alabi, who also directed ‘Assurance, the video was filmed at the historic Château de Chanteloup, the estate of French cognac house Maison Martell in Cognac, France.

It blends French elegance with Nigerian style, with Davido arriving in a horse-drawn carriage, serenading Chioma in grand interiors, and later recreating a proposal scene by a lake at dusk, where he goes down on one knee to present her with a ring.

Though the couple wedded in a lavish Lagos ceremony in June 2024, the proposal scene is a cinematic metaphor for renewed commitment, not a new engagement.

Davido announced the release himself with the caption: “Already Falling. From us to you. Enjoy.”

Like other music stars, Davido is proving that a real-life love story can become a powerful artistic brand.

For fans, ‘Already Falling’ is more than a music video. It is a continuation of a story they have followed since 2018 ; from young lovers, to husband and wife, to parents, told in Davido’s most personal songs. And with Chioma by his side in the studio, on screen, and on tour, including their recent high-profile trip to Tanzania with Diamond Platnumz, the couple shows no signs of slowing down.

content:
Former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Babachir Lawal, has said the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, will defeat former Vice President Atiku Abubakar in Adamawa State in the 2027 general election.

Lawal made the prediction during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday.

Asked whether Obi could secure victory in northern Nigeria, the former SGF said the former Anambra State governor would win in Adamawa, despite the state being Atiku’s home state.

He further claimed that Atiku would finish third in the state in the 2027 presidential election.

He said: “Peter Obi will defeat Atiku in Adamawa State. Atiku will finish third. Let’s bet. I am ready to bet with anybody.”

According to him, Atiku’s time has passed in Adamawa, stating that the people of the state are tired of him and they want a new face.

The NDC chieftain said they have seen what Atiku did in ADC, and they will punish him at the ballot box.

The ex-SGF also said that Obi will equally get 25% in Kogi State, noting that Kogi people are suffering and they are looking for a man who will rescue them, and that man is Obi.

title: Amnesty demands release of youth detained for insulting Kano Hisbah Board on TikTok
description:
Amnesty International has called for the immediate and unconditional release of Muhammad Aliyu, a 20-year-old currently in prison and set to face what it described as a sham trial for allegedly insulting the Kano State Hisbah Board and its commander, Aminu Daurawa.
The rights group made the demand i
content:
Amnesty International has called for the immediate and unconditional release of Muhammad Aliyu, a 20-year-old currently in prison and set to face what it described as a sham trial for allegedly insulting the Kano State Hisbah Board and its commander, Aminu Daurawa.

The rights group made the demand in a statement shared on Facebook on Saturday.

According to Amnesty, Aliyu is one of three youths recently arrested by the Hisbah Board over allegations of using TikTok to abuse the board and its commander.

It described the court order remanding Aliyu as outrageous, heavy-handed and disproportionate.

The rights group said Aliyu was arrested at his shop at Hajj Camp on November 15 and detained until his arraignment before a Shariah court located within the premises of the Hisbah office.

Apart from being detained, he was also allegedly subjected to torture and other ill-treatment.

Amnesty said its findings show that the majority of victims of Hisbah excesses are poor and from the lower rung of society.

“Criticising public institutions or officials is not a criminal offence under international law, and no one should stand trial — let alone face imprisonment and strokes of cane — for just doing that,” the organisation said.

It called on Kano State authorities to end what it termed a travesty of justice without further delay by dropping all charges against Aliyu and ordering his immediate release.

title: Do women control their husbands?
description:
By Chioma Gabriel, Editor, Special Features







It is often said that women are a necessary evil, a desirable calamity and a domestic peril. It all depends on where one is standing.In traditional African societies, a woman’s place was said to be in the kitchen, from where she was expected to work
content:
By Chioma Gabriel, Editor, Special Features

It is often said that women are a necessary evil, a desirable calamity and a domestic peril. It all depends on where one is standing.
In traditional African societies, a woman’s place was said to be in the kitchen, from where she was expected to work her way into her husband’s heart through his stomach. Women were traditionally expected to be seen but not heard.

They were like shadows trailing their husbands, with little or no opportunity to express opinions on matters affecting the family and society. They were often regarded as acquired possessions whose primary responsibilities were to bear children and provide labour on the farms. They had little or no say in the scheme of things.


A similar pattern appears in some biblical accounts, where headcounts excluded women and children. When Jesus fed the 5,000 and the 4,000, the recorded figures referred to the men, with women and children excluded from the count.


In the early Christian community, Paul’s instruction required women to remain silent in church and ask their husbands questions at home. Although interpretations of this passage differ among Christian scholars, it has historically been cited to support restrictions on women’s public religious participation.


Despite these historical and cultural limitations, women have, in different ways, exercised considerable influence over men, including their husbands.

Biblical accounts


The Bible contains several accounts of women whose actions, decisions or influence significantly shaped the lives of men.
Eve persuaded Adam to eat the forbidden fruit after the serpent tempted her in the Garden of Eden.


Jezebel manipulated her husband, King Ahab, and orchestrated the murder of Naboth to acquire his vineyard.


Delilah used persistent pressure and deception to make Samson reveal the secret of his extraordinary strength.


Sapphira conspired with her husband, Ananias, to deceive the apostles about the proceeds from the sale of their property.
Michal helped David escape from King Saul but later confronted and despised him over his public dancing before God.


Bathsheba, working alongside the prophet Nathan, intervened to ensure that David fulfilled his promise that Solomon would succeed him as king.


Sarah persuaded Abraham to have a child through her maidservant, Hagar, and later demanded that Hagar and Ishmael be sent away.


Rebekah orchestrated a family deception by persuading her son Jacob to disguise himself as Esau and obtain Isaac’s blessing.
Herodias influenced her daughter to demand the head of John the Baptist from her husband, Herod Antipas.


Job’s wife, overwhelmed by their suffering, urged her husband to curse God and die.


Mary and Martha also demonstrated the emotional influence women could have. When their brother, Lazarus, died, their grief deeply moved Jesus, who wept before raising him from the dead.


There is also the account of a woman who anointed Jesus’ feet with her hair, although the biblical accounts differ on the identity of the woman. It is important not to confuse Mary Magdalene with Mary of Bethany or the unnamed woman in Luke’s account.
Not all these women controlled their husbands in the strict sense. Some influenced, persuaded, deceived, encouraged or challenged the men in their lives. Nevertheless, their stories demonstrate that women have never been entirely without influence, even in societies structured around male authority.

Did Queen Elizabeth 11 control her husband?


The marriage between Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip presents an interesting example of a reversal of traditional marital expectations.


Elizabeth’s relationship with Philip was largely a partnership shaped by an extraordinary reversal of conventional marital expectations. Philip had to accept that his wife was not only the Queen at home but also his sovereign in public life.
When Elizabeth ascended the throne in 1952, Philip suddenly became the husband of a reigning monarch. His position within the royal household changed significantly.


He had to accept that his wife outranked him in official protocol. At public ceremonies, he occupied a supporting position, observing the precedence attached to her office.


At her coronation in 1953, Philip knelt before Elizabeth and pledged allegiance to her. This was particularly significant because he was her husband, not merely a subordinate royal official.


He was not crowned king simply because he was married to the Queen. Instead, he became her royal consort, accompanying her on official engagements and supporting the monarchy.


Elizabeth’s position also shaped the royal arrangements surrounding their children and family. In 1957, she formally made Philip a Prince of the United Kingdom, recognising his position within the royal family. However, he did not acquire the constitutional authority of a king.


Despite Philip’s strong personality, Elizabeth remained the sovereign and the ultimate constitutional authority.


Perhaps the most interesting lesson from their marriage is that a man born into royalty had to spend more than seven decades accepting that his wife occupied a position above his in the constitutional hierarchy.


This, however, should not necessarily be interpreted as evidence that Elizabeth controlled Philip in their private relationship. It was primarily a consequence of her position as monarch.

Nigerian women who wielded power and influence


Nigeria’s history is replete with women who exercised considerable political, economic and traditional authority, even in societies where men dominated public life.


Queen Idia of the Benin Kingdom, in present-day Edo State, was the mother of Oba Esigie. She played a significant role in her son’s political and military success. Her influence was so considerable that the position of Iyoba, or Queen Mother, became an important institution in the Benin monarchy.


Omu Okwei of Osomari, in present-day Anambra State, was a wealthy businesswoman and influential traditional figure. Her commercial success gave her considerable economic and social authority, extending beyond her household into community affairs.
Madam Efunroye Tinubu of Abeokuta and Lagos was a powerful merchant and political figure. She wielded considerable influence in the affairs of Lagos and maintained relationships with powerful traditional rulers.


In Ibadan, Iyalode Efunsetan Aniwura was a wealthy trader and powerful female chief whose economic resources gave her considerable political influence. She was not simply a woman operating in her husband’s shadow but an authority in her own right.
These women demonstrated that female influence in traditional Nigerian society was not restricted to marriage or domestic relationships. Some wielded power independently through wealth, political connections, traditional institutions and personal achievements.


Their stories also challenge the assumption that women have always occupied powerless positions in African societies.
However, despite the influence of these historical figures and many contemporary women who hold sway in a male-dominated world, it would be inaccurate to conclude that Nigerian women systematically control their husbands.

Different strokes for different folks


Every marriage has its own power dynamics.


Behind the closed doors of many Nigerian homes, decisions are made, arguments are won and lost, compromises are reached and, sometimes, one partner quietly persuades the other to do things they would ordinarily not have considered.


While the husband may traditionally be regarded as the head of the family, it is not unusual to find a wife whose opinion carries considerable weight or whose approval is required before important decisions are taken.


In some homes, the man appears to wear the crown, but the woman holds the remote control.


This has fuelled an age-old argument: Do women really control their husbands? Is a woman who influences her husband’s decisions exercising wisdom, fulfilling her marital responsibilities or subtly taking over the leadership of the home? Where should the line be drawn between a wife’s influence and outright domination?


The debate becomes even more interesting when viewed against the background of biblical teachings, traditional African values and the changing realities of Nigerian marriages, where education, financial independence and evolving gender roles are steadily redefining relationships between husbands and wives.


A woman can influence her husband’s decisions without dominating him. She can manage the family finances without becoming a family dictator. She can disagree with her husband without disrespecting him, just as he can exercise leadership without becoming oppressive.


Marriage should not be an opportunity for one person to destroy the individuality of another. African traditions, too, contain examples of women whose wisdom, courage and contributions helped sustain powerful families and communities.


Perhaps the real question is not who controls the home but who contributes to making it work.


A marriage should not be a kingdom where one person reigns while the other lives as a subject. It should be a partnership in which two individuals, with different strengths and perspectives, work towards a common future.


The strongest husband is not necessarily the one whose wife never questions him, just as the strongest wife is not the one who always gets her way. The strongest marriage is one in which neither partner needs to dominate the other to feel respected.
That, perhaps, is the difference between having a spouse and having a true partner.

What people say


Taking this topic to the marketplace and engaging ordinary people in conversations about it proved quite interesting. Some respondents looked around, paused and carefully weighed their words before speaking. Clearly, the question of whether women control their husbands touches a sensitive nerve in many marriages.


Martina, a married mother of four, said it was not an easy subject to discuss but insisted that every woman exercised some measure of control over her husband.


“It is the bad kind of control that is worrisome. For instance, when my elder brother got married, there was something about his wife that put off every member of the family. She was not friendly with us, and one after another, we withdrew and left them alone.


“The way my brother, who was very close to us while we were growing up, suddenly stopped caring about us showed that something was wrong. I don’t think it was normal.


“He wedded her in the Catholic Church, but shortly afterwards, his wife opened a shrine in the family compound and brought the gods of her own family into ours. Before we knew what was happening, she started calling herself Ezenwanyi.


“Our brother, her husband, was her first convert. Before long, he was no longer the brother we knew. He did only what she told him to do, and our family home became a habitat for all manner of native doctors.


“Is that not control? We have stopped going home because there is no longer any trust. My brother now behaves like a zombie.”
Commenting on his sister-in-law, Kingsley said he had effectively lost his only brother after the latter got married.


“We were the only two children of our parents. I am the older one, and we were very close. When I relocated to the United States, I left my apartment and everything in it for my younger brother. I later came home for his wedding and stayed for a while to establish some businesses in Nigeria. I stayed with him.


“Because I was based overseas, I decided to use my old Nigerian residential address as my business address. My brother’s wife overheard us discussing the business and its location. She suddenly came out of the bedroom, shouting that her home address must not be used as my business address.


“It was the manner in which she spoke to me that baffled me. Ever since then, whenever I speak with my brother, it feels as though I am talking to a stranger.


“I am equally married, but my wife continues to maintain cordial relationships with my other relatives. I feel I have completely lost my brother. Anything I ask him now, he would say, let me ask my wife or let me discuss with my wife. He is my only brother and I can no longer confide in him.”


For Charles Ezealo, his experience with two marriages exposed the complicated relationship between marital influence and extended family expectations.


“I suffered considerable embarrassment after I got married. When I married my first wife, my mother would not allow her to join me in Lagos because she insisted that, having lost our father at a young age and struggled to train her children without assistance, my wife must first ‘marry’ her by coming to stay with her in the village for at least three weeks.


“My then wife, who was a medical doctor undergoing her housemanship, refused to accept the arrangement. She eventually divorced me.


“My mother subsequently arranged another marriage for me with a village girl from Imo State, whom she had personally selected and approved. She followed me to the UK.


“However, things changed when we got there. To cut a long story short, she is not even on speaking terms with my mother and has, on several occasions, opposed her visiting us in the UK. I have never seen anything like it but I think m mother deserved what she got.”


For Deacon Fredrick, marriage should be a win-win situation rather than an arrangement in which one partner dominates the other.
“Unfortunately, that is not always the case nowadays. I have encountered men who complain that their wives deny them conjugal rights until certain demands are met. Come to the Church, you hear all kinds of things as a marriage counsellor: He snores. She’s too fat. He has body odour. He’s a two-minutes man. All manner of things and people are getting divorced because of these.


“Some men also complain that their wives make financial demands beyond their capabilities and use such demands to create tension in their homes. A wise woman should build her home, not destroy it.


“But, mind you, not all women control their husbands. Healthy marriages are built on mutual respect, shared decisions and partnership rather than dominance.


“Controlling behaviour can occur in any relationship and is not exclusive to one gender. Either a wife or a husband can exhibit controlling tendencies. When a wife attempts to control or micromanage her husband, it may arise from particular relationship dynamics rather than inherent malice.”


For 52-year-old Odinaka, a businessman in Lagos, marriage has taught him that being the head of a household does not necessarily mean having the final word on every issue.


“I used to believe that whatever I said as the man of the house must stand. But experience has taught me otherwise. My wife understands certain aspects of family life better than I do, particularly finances and the children’s welfare. Sometimes, I may have an idea, but after listening to her arguments, I change my mind,” he said.


Although Emeka insists that his wife does not control him, he admits that she has considerable influence over his decisions.
His experience reflects a growing reality in many Nigerian households, where women are increasingly participating in decisions traditionally regarded as men’s responsibilities.


From choosing where the family lives to deciding how money is spent, determining the children’s education, making investment decisions and managing relationships with extended family members, women are playing increasingly influential roles.
For some men, however, this growing influence is interpreted as a threat to traditional masculinity.


In a society where many men were raised to believe that authority belongs exclusively to the husband, a wife who questions decisions, insists on being consulted or participates in managing family finances may quickly earn the label of a domineering woman.


Yet, some women argue that what men describe as control is often nothing more than participation.


“I am not controlling my husband. I simply refuse to be treated like a housemaid in my own home. If we are both contributing financially and raising the children together, why should only one person make decisions?” asked 43-year-old Awele, a civil servant in Lagos.


According to her, marriage should not be a military arrangement in which one person gives orders while the other obeys without question.


However, not all women exercise influence through open discussions. In some homes, control takes more subtle forms.
Some women determine how much money their husbands spend, monitor their movements, influence their friendships and decide which relatives deserve financial assistance. Others use emotional withdrawal, persistent arguments or threats to create pressure until their husbands surrender.


Interestingly, some men also exercise similar forms of control over their wives, using financial dependence, intimidation and cultural expectations to enforce obedience.


This suggests that the struggle for power in marriage is not exclusive to women.


Nigeria’s changing economic realities have also altered traditional household arrangements. With rising living costs, many families depend on the combined earnings of husband and wife to survive. Women who contribute substantially to rent, school fees, feeding and other household expenses increasingly demand a voice in family decisions.


However, financial contribution should not become a licence for domination, just as being a husband should not confer unlimited authority.


Ultimately, perhaps the more important question is not whether women control their husbands but whether either partner should have absolute control over the other.


A successful marriage should not be a competition for supremacy. It should be a partnership in which both individuals can express their opinions, disagree without fear and make decisions without intimidation.

title: Man arraigned for allegedly duping major general of N29.85m
description:
The Abuja Zonal Directorate of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) on Thursday, November 19, arraigned one Abdulkadir Ndaliman before Justice Chinyere E. Nwecheonwu of the Federal High Court, sitting in Kuje, Abuja, on a two-count charge bordering on obtaining by false pretence.
Ndal
content:
The Abuja Zonal Directorate of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) on Thursday, November 19, arraigned one Abdulkadir Ndaliman before Justice Chinyere E. Nwecheonwu of the Federal High Court, sitting in Kuje, Abuja, on a two-count charge bordering on obtaining by false pretence.

Ndaliman is accused of dishonestly converting to his personal use a total of N29.85 million entrusted to him by Major General Dagana Allu, being proceeds realised from the sale of a Toyota Corolla LE 2014 model.

Count one reads: “That you, Abdulkadir Ndaliman, sometimes in May 2026 at Abuja, within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court did dishonestly convert to your personal use the sum of N12,600,000.00 (Twelve Million, Six Hundred Thousand Naira) entrusted to you by Major General Dagana Allu being the proceeds realized from the sale of Toyota Corolla LE 2014 model and thereby committed an offence contrary to Section 311 of the Penal Code Act and punishable under Section 312 of the same Act.”

Count two reads: “That you, Abdulkadir Ndaliman, sometimes in July 2026 at Abuja, within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court did dishonestly convert to your personal use the sum of N17,250,000.00 (Seventeen Million, Two Hundred and Fifty Thousand Naira) entrusted to you by Major General Dagana Allu being the proceeds realized from the sale of Toyota Corolla LE 2014 model and thereby committed an offence contrary to Section 311 of the Penal Code Act and punishable under Section 312 of the same Act.”

The defendant pleaded not guilty to all the charges when they were read to him.

Following his plea, defence counsel, Muhammad Yakubu, moved an application for his bail, urging the court to grant his client bail pending the determination of the case.

Countering the request, prosecution counsel, Fatima Ado, initially urged the court to deny the defendant bail, citing the gravity of the offence, adding that the commission was ready to commence trial.

Justice Nwecheonwu granted the defendant bail in the sum of N5 million with one surety in like sum.

The surety must provide a verifiable residential address, a valid means of identification and evidence of a legitimate means of livelihood.

The matter was adjourned until February 1, 2027, for commencement of trial.

content:
Muslims are projected to overtake Christians as the world’s largest religious group by 2035, with Nigeria expected to rank among the countries with the largest populations of both religions by 2070.

This is according to two reports published by the Pew Research Center on November 18, 2026, examining projected changes in the global Christian and Muslim populations between 2020 and 2070.

The reports said the global Muslim population would grow faster than other religious groups, while Christianity would maintain a relatively stable share of the world’s population despite significant changes in its geographical distribution.

Pew projected that Muslims would increase by 80 per cent between 2020 and 2070, compared with an 11 per cent rise in the non-Muslim population.

“Muslims are the world’s fastest-growing religious group – a trend that’s expected to continue in the coming decades,” the report on the future of the global Muslim population stated.

Countries with the largest Muslim populations

In 2020, Indonesia had the world’s largest Muslim population, with 239 million followers, followed by Pakistan with 227 million and India with 213 million.

Bangladesh and Nigeria completed the top five, with 151 million and 120 million Muslims, respectively.

By 2070, Pakistan is projected to take the top position with 461 million Muslims, followed by India with 334 million and Nigeria with 282 million.

Indonesia is expected to drop to fourth place, with 274 million, while Bangladesh is projected to rank fifth with 218 million.

Top 10 countries with the largest Muslim populations

2020 estimates

  2. Pakistan
  3. India
  4. Bangladesh
  5. Nigeria
  6. Egypt
  7. Iran
  8. Turkey
  9. Sudan

2070 projections

  1. Pakistan

  4. Indonesia
  5. Bangladesh
  6. Egypt
  7. Ethiopia
  8. Sudan
  9. Turkey
  10. Afghanistan

Pew said Nigeria was expected to climb to third place globally by 2070, while Ethiopia and Afghanistan would enter the top 10.

It also projected that sub-Saharan Africa would account for 27 per cent of the world’s Muslim population by 2070, compared with 18 per cent in 2020.

Countries with the largest Christian populations

The United States had the world’s largest Christian population in 2020, with an estimated 217 million followers.

Brazil ranked second with 168 million, followed by Mexico with 113 million, the Philippines with 103 million and Russia with 102 million.

However, Pew projected that the Democratic Republic of the Congo would overtake the US by 2070, becoming the country with the largest Christian population, estimated at 299 million.

The US is projected to fall to second place with 174 million Christians, while Ethiopia would rank third with 150 million.

  7. Mexico
  8. Philippines
  9. Uganda
  10. Angola

Pew projected that several sub-Saharan African countries, including Nigeria, Tanzania, Uganda and Angola, would rise in the rankings by 2070.

The report said the number of Christians in sub-Saharan Africa would more than double, from 697 million in 2020 to 1.6 billion in 2070.

“By 2070, 54% of all Christians are expected to live on the African continent south of the Sahara Desert and its nearby islands, up from 31% in 2020,” it stated.

The projections also indicated that Christians would no longer constitute a majority in the United States and nine other countries by 2070.

Pew said the projections were based on demographic trends, including age distribution, fertility, mortality, migration and religious switching.

The research covered 201 countries and territories, representing 99.98 per cent of the world’s population.

title: Soludo approves N50,000 December bonus for Anambra workers
description:
By Vincent Ujumadu



Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has approved a N50,000 December bonus for civil servants in the state, with the payment expected to reflect in their December 2026 salaries.



The governor announced the bonus during the 2026 Civil Service Day celebration held at
content:
By Vincent Ujumadu

Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has approved a N50,000 December bonus for civil servants in the state, with the payment expected to reflect in their December 2026 salaries.

The governor announced the bonus during the 2026 Civil Service Day celebration held at the Jerome Udoji State Secretariat Complex in Awka, where he also approved measures to improve the working environment and productivity of civil servants.

Soludo acknowledged the economic challenges facing workers, admitting that their current salaries were inadequate amid prevailing economic conditions.

He, however, assured the workers that his administration would only make financial commitments it could realistically fulfil.

“I understand the situation and economic conditions, that we need to be able to do something. The pay that we have all over is not enough; I clearly understand it.

“But there is one thing I also want to tell you, and that is I don’t play to the wind. Before we get into a commitment, we make sure that it is something that we will always honour,” he said.

Addressing comparisons between Anambra’s salary structure and those of other states, the governor urged civil servants to consider the different revenue bases and economic capacities of state governments before making such assessments.

He stressed that sustainable governance and responsible financial management, rather than unfulfilled promises, remained the guiding principles of his administration.

Soludo also expressed appreciation to the workers for their support during last year’s governorship election, saying he was pleased that public servants overwhelmingly voted for his administration in recognition of its developmental efforts.

Responding to three major requests presented by the workers at the event, the governor immediately directed the rehabilitation of roads within the secretariat complex, approved the establishment of an Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Centre and authorised the pruning of overgrown trees across the premises.

Earlier, the Anambra State Head of Service, Barr. Ngozi Iwouno, commended Soludo for restoring security and normalcy across the state.

She said civil servants could now attend work regularly without fear, noting that the disruption previously caused by Monday sit-at-home orders had been overcome.

Iwouno said the improved security situation had restored confidence among workers and enabled them to discharge their duties more consistently.

title: EPL: Osimhen open to Manchester United move
description:
Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen is reportedly open to joining Manchester United following renewed interest from the Premier League club.
The Galatasaray forward is said to be keen on playing in the English Premier League before the end of his career and would consider a move to Old Trafford if a
content:
Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen is reportedly open to joining Manchester United following renewed interest from the Premier League club.

The Galatasaray forward is said to be keen on playing in the English Premier League before the end of his career and would consider a move to Old Trafford if an offer is made.

According to The Sun, Osimhen has been informed of Manchester United’s renewed interest and is pleased with the possibility of joining the English club.

Manchester United’s new manager, Mauricio Pochettino, is reportedly interested in signing an established striker as he seeks to strengthen the team’s attacking options.

Pochettino arrived at Old Trafford with Benjamin Sesko sidelined by a shin injury, while Joshua Zirkzee has struggled to establish himself as a regular goalscorer.

The report said Osimhen’s representatives are aware of United’s interest, although any potential transfer would depend on an agreement between the two clubs.

The 27-year-old is currently recovering from knee surgery and is expected to return to action before the end of December.

Osimhen joined Galatasaray permanently last year after spending the 2024/25 season on loan at the Turkish club from Napoli.

He remains under contract with Galatasaray until June 2029, meaning Manchester United would have to negotiate a transfer fee with the Turkish champions.

A January move could prove difficult, with Galatasaray reportedly valuing the Nigerian striker at between £80 million and £100 million.

A source close to Osimhen was quoted by The Sun as saying: “Of course the interest really flatters him, but he’s a loyal guy, so it will be up to United to move hard for him.

“Victor will score goals everywhere he goes, and he’s proven that, but it’s really up to the two clubs.”
