title: Enugu industrialist dies in road crash
description:
The Enugu State Government has confirmed the death of an industrialist and construction expert, High Chief Festus Oshaba-Onuh, in a road accident along the Enugu-Port Harcourt Expressway.
Oshaba-Onuh was the Chairman of FEROTEX Construction Company and Director of Finance of the Enugu State All Prog
content:
The Enugu State Government has confirmed the death of an industrialist and construction expert, High Chief Festus Oshaba-Onuh, in a road accident along the Enugu-Port Harcourt Expressway.

Oshaba-Onuh was the Chairman of FEROTEX Construction Company and Director of Finance of the Enugu State All Progressives Congress Campaign Council before his death.

Governor Peter Mbah announced his death in a condolence message on Friday, describing it as a “grievous loss” to the state and a “personal loss” to him.

“I received with a deep sense of grief the heartrending news of the death of our brother, Chief Festus Oshaba-Onuh, in a fatal road accident along the Enugu-Port Harcourt Expressway,” the governor said.

Mbah described the deceased as “a great son of whom we were so proud”, adding that he was “a distinguished player in the nation’s construction industry” who would be remembered for his “enchanting humility and kindheartedness”.

The governor also described Oshaba-Onuh as a philanthropist and patriot who believed in the vision of a new Enugu State and contributed to its infrastructural transformation.

“Therefore, this is a personal loss to me and Ndi
Enugu. We are all mourning,” he said, while extending his condolences to the deceased’s family and the people of Enugu Ezike and Igboeze North Local Government Area.

Also mourning the industrialist, the Chairman of Igbo Eze North Local Government Area, Chris Onyekachi Simon, described his death as “a devastating earthquake of unimaginable magnitude”.

In a separate condolence message, Simon described Oshaba-Onuh as “an exceptional road construction expert whose dedication to infrastructure development transformed communities and created lasting value”.

“Your remarkable contributions to road development and your commitment to the progress of our society will remain part of your enduring legacy,” he said.

The council chairman said the deceased would be greatly missed by his family, the Umuagama community, Igbo Eze North, the state government and the construction industry.

“Chief Festus Oshaba Onu, you were a rare personality whose place will be difficult to fill,” Simon added, praying that God would grant him eternal rest and give his family the strength to bear the loss.

title: Passengers fear proposed biometric checks may cause chaos at domestic airports
description:
By Dickson Omobola



Federal Government’s proposed mandatory biometric checks for domestic air passengers from January 1, 2027, have come under scrutiny less than five days after the plan was announced, with passengers and industry observers warning that the policy could make air travel more diffic
content:
By Dickson Omobola

Federal Government’s proposed mandatory biometric checks for domestic air passengers from January 1, 2027, have come under scrutiny less than five days after the plan was announced, with passengers and industry observers warning that the policy could make air travel more difficult.


They insisted that the plan appeared rushed and had not been properly thought through, particularly as the festive travel season would still be ongoing when the policy takes effect.


They also feared that its implementation could trigger a repeat of the chaos that followed the introduction of the Go Cashless payment system, which caused hours of gridlock at airports in Lagos and Abuja.


In March, the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, introduced an electronic payment system known as Go Cashless at the toll gate of two of the country’s busiest airports.


Its rollout left passengers travelling through the airports in Lagos and Abuja stranded for hours, triggering massive gridlock, missed flights and widespread frustration.


While some travellers abandoned their vehicles at airport entrances after encountering difficulties completing payments, others said they missed scheduled flights after spending hours trying to gain access to the airports.


The disruption prompted President Bola Tinubu to order the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr Festus Keyamo, to announce a suspension of the system on the fourth day of its implementation.


With the busy Yuletide travel period extending into January, passengers and industry observers fear that a similar situation could unfold at the Lagos airport, the country’s busiest, especially as Keyamo has given domestic airlines until December 31, 2026, to integrate their operations with the system that will facilitate the biometric checks.


Keyamo warned that airlines that fail to comply with the directive would not be allowed to board passengers from January 1, 2027.
Known as the Airport Passenger Verification System, v-PASS, the biometric identity verification system is linked to the National Identification Number, NIN, of Nigerians.


It is designed exclusively for domestic flights, with all passengers required to provide their NIN during check-in. Passengers are also expected to pay additional charges for the service.


Speaking during the unveiling of the system at the domestic terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos, Keyamo said: “I am giving the airlines till the end of December. I repeat it. From the 1st of January, no airline will be allowed to board their passengers if they don’t key into the v-PASS.”

X-raying v-PASS


Approved by the Federal Executive Council, FEC, v-PASS is a private-sector investment aimed at modernising airport operations through private-sector participation.


Managing Director of FAAN, Mrs Olubunmi Kuku, said the system is designed to provide passengers with a single digital identity that can be used at different stages of airport processing, from security access to boarding.


Passengers will enrol using their NIN. After registration, they will be able to enter the last four digits of their NIN at designated security access points.


At boarding gates, the identities of travellers will be verified through facial recognition, iris biometrics or QR codes displayed on boarding passes.

Concerns


Reacting to Keyamo’s announcement on X, formerly Twitter, a lawyer and frequent traveller, Dr Charles Omole, questioned how the system would accommodate foreigners and Nigerians travelling with foreign passports who do not have NINs.


He asked: “What happens to foreigners (Nigerians who travel in with foreign passports and pure non-Nigerians) who do not have a NIN? Does that mean they cannot fly on domestic flights?


“As Nigerians are allowed to fly into the country on expired passports, what happens to those who fly into the country that way (most do not yet have a NIN) but need a local flight to their final destination? Will they be stuck at the arrival airport?


“What happens to Nigerian children who do not have NIN? What happens to adult Nigerians who have not yet obtained a NIN but have other IDs? Is NIN now a compulsory requirement to fly in Nigeria? Is this backed by any law?


“These clarifications are important. A valid ID is the normal practice in most countries, not a national identification number. But your clarification will help us understand.”


Another passenger on X, Kelechi Nwachukwu, was particularly interested in the cost implications of the system, saying: “PPP arrangement? Surely, the private partners will recoup their investment. Nigerians are already paying so much for local flights. Hope the benefit outweighs the additional cost implication of flight fares.”

Rewarding cronies


Another user, Yagazilum, also expressed concern, saying: “I have my driver’s licence, passport and voter’s card all linked to NIN but there are still ticket racketeering and beggy-beggy at the airports. I guess this is another means of rewarding cronies with juicy contracts that add no value but rather create more problems, delays and avenues for extorting the public.”

Defence layers


For his part, aviation security expert, Group Captain John Ojikutu (retd), warned of the security implications of relying on a single service provider and the extent to which relevant aviation security agencies had been consulted.


He said: “Access into the Nigeria civil aviation security network cannot be restricted to only one service provider but must integrate them all. The NASC through the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, must set the standard. Aviation security membership mainly include the NCAA, government security agencies working in the airport and the representative of the Airline Operators of Nigeria, AON.


“Would the v-Pass exclude or include the Airlines boarding pass and the airport ODC? What are the inputs of the national aviation security committee, NCAA and the airport security committee in this new regulation for passengers facilitation?


“This is a job of national aviation security that must be networked and not for airport security alone otherwise while looking for default airline passengers, a non-passenger will pass through with his NIN and commit an unlawful act on aviation systems. NIN alone cannot deter unlawful act without intelligent information about passengers on watchlist or those on no-fly-list. The defence layers begin with shared intelligence from the NCAA with airlines and airport operators and others within the six defence layers.”


Dumping ground


An aviation stakeholder, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said: “For visitors who are here on holiday for a short period will have to obtain NIN to do their local flight. You should not turn Nigeria into a police country. What happens to students with their University ID cards and companies’ identity cards? Whenever there is a new technology that is not acceptable in the Western world, Nigeria is always the dumping ground. Our airports are already a difficult place to fly from, complex and expensive. I think we should focus on making life easier for an average citizen of this country.”


Air Peace boosts domestic operations


Nigeria’s largest carrier, Air Peace Limited, has expanded its domestic network with the introduction of daily flight connections from Asaba, Anambra, Benin, Enugu, Owerri, Ibadan, Port Harcourt and Warri to Kano.


The airline has also strengthened air connectivity between Lagos and Abuja by increasing flight frequencies to up to nine daily services.


The new connections from Asaba, Anambra, Benin, Enugu, Owerri, Ibadan, Port Harcourt and Warri to Kano took effect on November 20, 2026.


The airline’s spokesperson, Mr Efe Osifo-Whiskey, in a statement, said the development reflected Air Peace’s sustained drive towards network optimisation, capacity enhancement and service excellence, as it continues to consolidate its position in Nigeria’s aviation industry through strategic route expansion and increased flight frequencies.


He said: “Air Peace remains committed to providing safe, reliable and convenient air travel while continually expanding its operations to meet the evolving travel needs of passengers across Nigeria and beyond.”

The post Passengers fear proposed biometric checks may cause chaos at domestic airports appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: New LAWMA boss promises cleaner Lagos before Christmas
description:
The Lagos Waste Management Authority has set a 60-day deadline to clear illegal dumpsites and refuse heaps across the state, pledging to rid the metropolis of identified waste black spots before Christmas.
The Acting Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of LAWMA, Olajuwon Akinyemi, gave the
content:
The Lagos Waste Management Authority has set a 60-day deadline to clear illegal dumpsites and refuse heaps across the state, pledging to rid the metropolis of identified waste black spots before Christmas.

The Acting Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of LAWMA, Olajuwon Akinyemi, gave the assurance during a media briefing and stakeholders’ engagement on Friday.

During the meeting, Akinyemi unveiled plans to reposition the authority and address persistent waste management challenges in the state.

He said the agency would embark on an intensive clean-up operation within the next 30 to 60 days, adding that the exercise would involve the removal of refuse from illegal dumpsites and identified black spots across Lagos.

“In the next 30 to 60 days, we are going to ensure that all our staff cooperate with us to clean up the city and sustain it. We will ensure the removal of waste from every illegal dumpsite and black spot around the city.

“I can assure Lagosians that before Christmas, they will see that Lagos has found a new leaf. A new sheriff is in town to do wonders for Lagos waste management,” he said.

He said Lagos generated between 13,000 and 14,000 metric tonnes of waste daily, describing the volume as a major challenge for the densely populated state.

Akinyemi also called on residents to take responsibility for the waste they generated, stressing the need for household waste sorting and separation to reduce the volume of refuse taken to landfill sites.

He explained that recycling, reuse and reduction of waste were essential to addressing the state’s limited landfill capacity, adding that the authority could not achieve its objectives without the cooperation of residents.

On plans to decentralise waste management operations, Akinyemi said LAWMA would establish about 10 regional hubs across the state to bring its services closer to residents.

He said the proposed hubs would have offices headed by regional coordinators responsible for addressing waste management challenges in their respective areas.

According to him, the arrangement would address the challenges associated with managing distant communities from a central location.

“Take, for example, Ojo and Amuwo-Odofin down to Badagry; there is no office there. We are looking at creating regional hubs, about 10 of them, with offices and regional heads who understand what to do and can manage waste challenges in those areas.

“Take, for example, Ijede, Eredo and Agbowa, which are far from Ijora. We are taking waste management closer to the people. That is the next level we are looking at,” he said.

The LAWMA boss said the proposed restructuring would be pursued in collaboration with the Commissioner for the Environment, local governments and other relevant stakeholders, adding that the authority would focus on regulation and policy direction.

On concerns about the efficiency of Private Sector Participation operators, particularly the rising cost of waste evacuation, he said LAWMA would intensify engagement and public enlightenment to improve residents’ understanding of the operational challenges facing the operators.

He noted that the cost of acquiring specialised waste collection trucks had increased significantly, explaining that vehicles which previously cost between N5m and N10m now cost between N18m and N19m.

He added that the rising cost of diesel, which he put at between N1,800 and N2,000 per litre, had further increased the financial burden on the operators.

According to him, the authority would engage residents, Community Development Associations, Community Development Committees, market associations and local governments to encourage cooperation with PSP operators.

“We need to engage a lot. We need to do advocacy and enlightenment. Every waste generator should understand that he must be responsible for the waste he generates.

“Imagine if you are the one who invested in that business and want to break even, not to talk of recouping your investment. We strongly believe that Lagosians will understand when we engage them more,” he said.

He added that the authority would also work with the state government on the rehabilitation of landfill sites and the development of material recovery centres to strengthen waste processing and recycling.

Akinyemi said the new measures were aimed at improving service delivery and ensuring that waste management operations were more responsive to the needs of residents.

The post New LAWMA boss promises cleaner Lagos before Christmas appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Police probe attack on Edo NDC secretariat, invite LG chairman
description:
The Edo State Police Command has invited the Chairman of Owan East Local Government Area, Ernest Aitalegbe, over an alleged attack on the secretariat of the Nigeria Democratic Congress in Afuze, the headquarters of the council.
The command said the invitation was part of an ongoing investigation int
content:
The Edo State Police Command has invited the Chairman of Owan East Local Government Area, Ernest Aitalegbe, over an alleged attack on the secretariat of the Nigeria Democratic Congress in Afuze, the headquarters of the council.

The command said the invitation was part of an ongoing investigation into Thursday’s attack allegedly carried out by armed men suspected to be members of the Edo State Security Network.

The state Police Public Relations Officer, Eno Ikoedem, disclosed this in a statement on Friday.

According to the statement, two NDC political aspirants, Mariam Iseme and Grant Eruhagan, reported that they were holding a meeting with other party members at the secretariat around 4pm on Thursday when the attackers stormed the premises.

It added that the suspected assailants, dressed in uniforms of the Edo State Security Network and armed with guns and machetes, allegedly disrupted the meeting and vandalised party materials.

“The assailants destroyed political banners and other materials within the secretariat, while threatening to kill the occupants before fleeing upon sighting the police,” the statement read.

The police said they had commenced an investigation and were making efforts to identify and arrest those involved in the incident.

“The command has commenced investigation into the incident and is making concerted efforts to identify, locate and apprehend all persons involved in the attack,” Ikoedem said.

The statement added that the council chairman had also been invited to assist the investigation.

“The Local Government Chairman of Owan East Local Government Area, Hon. Ernest Oyaole Aitalegbe, has also been invited in connection with the incident to assist the ongoing investigation,” the statement added.

The state Commissioner of Police, Patrick Daaor, also warned politicians, political aspirants, supporters and their loyalists against resorting to violence, intimidation, destruction of property or the use of thugs to advance their political interests.

Daaor “strongly” warned political actors against actions capable of undermining public peace, stressing that the command would not spare anyone found culpable.

“Let it be known that the command will not tolerate any form of political lawlessness, and anyone found sponsoring, perpetrating or aiding acts of violence will be arrested and prosecuted, irrespective of political status, affiliation or influence.

“All political actors are therefore warned to desist from acts capable of disrupting public peace, as the command is fully prepared to enforce the law without fear or favour,” Ikoedem quoted the commissioner as saying.

The invitation followed an attack on the party’s secretariat on Thursday, November 19, by armed men suspected to be members of the Edo State Security Network.

title: 6.7 magnitude earthquake hits Peru
description:
A 6.7-magnitude earthquake struck central Peru on Friday, Peru’s Defense Ministry said, with preliminary reports indicating minor damage and no fatalities.



The earthquake occurred at 7:09 pm (0009 GMT Saturday), 30 kilometers (18 miles) northwest of the city of Junin, at a depth of 129 kilometers
content:
A 6.7-magnitude earthquake struck central Peru on Friday, Peru’s Defense Ministry said, with preliminary reports indicating minor damage and no fatalities.

The earthquake occurred at 7:09 pm (0009 GMT Saturday), 30 kilometers (18 miles) northwest of the city of Junin, at a depth of 129 kilometers.

The United States Geological Survey (USGS) also measured the quake to have a magnitude of 6.7, but estimated its depth to be only 108 kilometers.

Peru’s Defense Minister, Rafael Belaunde, reported that after the earthquake “minor damage was reported to homes in different parts of Junin, as well as interruptions of electricity service and restrictions on highway transit.”

Belaunde added that there had been “no harm to people or impacts to their bodies and health.”

AFP journalists in Lima saw hundreds of people evacuating buildings in the Miraflores district during the quake.

The earthquake was also felt in the capital Lima, as well as Ancash, Ica, Ucayali, Cerro de Pasco, Huanuco and Callao.

Peru’s National Emergency Operation Center (COEN) reported the quake was felt with moderate to strong intensity and that “monitoring continues in vulnerable areas.”

Hernando Tavera, the president of the Peruvian Geophysical Institute, told AFP: “The ground shaking was intense. We have no reports of damage at the moment, but there have been landslides and rockfalls on the hillsides.”

Peru is situated on the so-called Pacific Ring of Fire — an arc of intense seismic activity stretching from Japan through Southeast Asia and across the Pacific basin.

Seismologists say Peru experiences at least 400 earthquakes per year, three-quarters of which are so weak people do not feel them.

A 5.1-magnitude earthquake in the Junin region in July killed six people, injured 32 others and destroyed 52 homes.

title: ‘I needed N150,000 to start business’ – Betting turns lover to kidnapper
description:
*Stages girlfriend’s abduction, demands N500, 000 ransom *He took advantage of victim’s mental health challenges – Police



By Evelyn Usman 



A 28-year-old petty trader, Chibuike Emmanuel, has confessed to staging the abduction of his 22-year-old girlfriend, Chidinma Eke, after losing N100,000 be
content:
*Stages girlfriend’s abduction, demands N500, 000 ransom *He took advantage of victim’s mental health challenges – Police

By Evelyn Usman 

A 28-year-old petty trader, Chibuike Emmanuel, has confessed to staging the abduction of his 22-year-old girlfriend, Chidinma Eke, after losing N100,000 belonging to his mother, money meant for her business, to sports betting.

Emmanuel, arrested by operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Unit of the Lagos State Police Command, allegedly held the victim captive in a building in Mushin for about four days before fleeing with her to Okada, Edo State, when he realised security agencies were tracking his phone.

The police are also on the trail of another suspect, simply identified as Samuel, who has been named as an accomplice in the crime.

Police sources said the suspect took advantage of the victim’s mental health challenges, lured her into a romantic relationship and eventually abducted her, before demanding N500,000 ransom from her mother.

The ordeal, according to the police, began when the victim left home and became unreachable.

The Lagos State Police Command, narrating how the case unfolded, said: “Acting on a report lodged by one Mrs Nkechi Ake, whose daughter, Favour Chidinma Ake, aged 22 years, left home on October 28, 2026, and subsequently became unreachable, a strange telephone number contacted the family a day later, claiming that she had been kidnapped and demanded the sum of Five Hundred Thousand Naira (N500,000) as ransom for her release.

“About a week later, a photograph was sent to members of the family, claiming that the victim had been killed, with a further demand for money to be paid before her corpse could be released to the family. “Consequently, on November 18, 2026, operatives attached to this office, acting on intelligence, traced the suspect to Okada area of Edo State, where one Chibuike Emmanuel, male, aged 28 years, was arrested.

“Preliminary investigation revealed that the suspect allegedly lured the victim to their hideout and subsequently continued to demand ransom from her family members. Investigation is ongoing.”

Suspect speaks

The prime suspect, Emmanuel, a trader at Oyingbo Market, blamed his action on losing his mother’s business money to sports betting.

Explaining how he staged the victim’s kidnap, he said : I am from Anambra State. I am a trader at Oyingbo but I don’t have a shop of my own. Before, I was managing with my elder brother at our mother’s shop at the Oyingbo Market.

“I met Chidinma at my mother’s grocery shop. She was sent on an errand by her mother. It was even my mother that liked her first. I secretly exchanged contacts with her and we became friends.

“At the beginning, it was just a normal friendship. We just exchanged communication but we were not doing anything until I invited her to a friend’s birthday party in the Oyingbo area of Lagos State.

“On that day, I called her and she told me that she was in school. I told her to come and meet me so that we could attend the birthday party together. When she came, we both attended the party together till late in the night.

“Something happened at the birthday. She was just misbehaving. At a point, she left our table for another table and invited strangers to join our table and that almost caused a serious fight but we eventually settled everything before it could escalate.

“After the party, I told her that she should be going home and that it was late but she refused. She said that it was too late and that her mother would beat her. She said that she would sleep with me. Since the celebrant already got an apartment for himself to sleep after the party, we joined him and two other people to sleep at the apartment.

“After that day, her mother called me to come to their house and two days later, I went to see her. She asked me who I was to her daughter and I explained that I was her boyfriend and that I really liked her. It was very late in the night and she told me to go and come back for further discussion.

“About a week after, Chidinma came to my area again in Oyingbo. I took her to a nice joint, where I bought her some drinks and we stayed till very late. I told her to be going home and I saw her off to a very close distance from their house. I called her mother and told her that Chidinma was on her way home.

“Surprisingly, after about ten minutes, Chidinma called me and asked where I was. I told her and she came back to me that she didn’t want to go home again. We went to sleep at a cheap hotel in Oyingbo.

“After that, we went to Idi Oro in Mushin. By then, my brother had sent me away from my mother’s shop. He asked me not to sell for my mother again after I used one hundred thousand naira from the sales money for sports betting. I needed money to start up something on my own. That was how we came up with the plan to collect money from Chidinma’s mother.

“I needed just one hundred and fifty thousand naira to start up something and that was what I demanded from the mother. It was my friend Samuel that took us to Edo State. I met Samuel at Mile 12, where I was selling pineapple. “When we discovered that some people were tracking our phone number, we escaped to Edo State because we already told the mother that her daughter had been taken to Edo State.”

Victim’s mother speaks

Mother of the victim, Mrs Ngozi Ake, on her part said:  “From the first time that I saw him, I knew that he was not a responsible guy. My daughter is an out-patient at the Psychiatric Hospital in Yaba and now she has missed her appointment there twice. She has also not taken her drugs since she was in the custody of the suspects.

“There was a particular day that my daughter told me that she was going to school. Late in the night, she didn’t return home. I kept calling her number and she didn’t pick. I was very worried. The following day, she called me and said that she slept in one of her sisters’ place.

“When I called the sister, she confirmed that my daughter slept in her place. Unknown to me, she was only trying to protect her by lying to me.

“When that boy (the suspect) came to my place, I didn’t like what I saw. It was very late in the night and I told him to go and that we would talk later. When he was leaving our place, my daughter attempted to see him off and I told her not to go beyond my gate.

“I was surprised that thirty minutes later, my daughter was not back in the house. I was very angry. I immediately called that boy and warned him not to come near my daughter again. I also warned my daughter not to have anything with him again.

“After about a week, I got a call that somebody kidnapped my daughter and that the person brought her for prostitution in Edo and that my daughter refused to take part in prostitution. The caller demanded five hundred thousand naira, if I ever wanted my daughter to return.

“We quickly reported to the police who tracked the number to Mushin. We didn’t believe them. It was later they told us that my daughter had been taken to Edo. Initially I sent fifty thousand naira to them. When they got to Edo, I sent another one hundred and fifty thousand naira again.

“Right from the beginning, I could see that the boy was not responsible and I warned my daughter,” she said ruefully.

Vanguard News

title: Why obesity hits men harder than women – Study
description:
By Shola Ogundipe



Scientists have uncovered a hidden biological difference in the fat tissue of males and females that could help explain why obesity triggers different health consequences in men and women.



The discovery suggests that the battle against obesity may be playing out differently b
content:
By Shola Ogundipe

Scientists have uncovered a hidden biological difference in the fat tissue of males and females that could help explain why obesity triggers different health consequences in men and women.

The discovery suggests that the battle against obesity may be playing out differently beneath the skin, with immune cells living inside body fat either helping to protect against inflammation and metabolic disorders or making them worse, depending on biological sex.

Researchers at the University of California, Riverside, US, found that a group of immune cells known as eosinophils, traditionally associated with allergies and asthma, perform different functions in the fat tissue of male and female mice. While certain populations of these cells appear to protect against obesity-related inflammation, others may contribute to harmful metabolic changes.

The study, titled “Single-cell heterogeneity of adipose eosinophils is shaped by sex and RELMα and linked to macrophage communication networks in obesity”, was funded by the National Institutes of Health, the UCR School of Medicine and the California Institute for Regenerative Medicine.

The findings, published in the journal PNAS Nexus, challenge the longstanding assumption that eosinophils are largely similar in structure and function. They also raise questions about whether obesity treatments targeting the immune system should be designed differently for men and women.

Led by biomedical scientists Meera Nair and Adam Godzik, the study used high-resolution single-cell sequencing to examine how individual immune cells behave in fat tissue.

What emerged was an unexpected picture.

The researchers identified six distinct populations of eosinophils in adipose tissue, each with its own genetic activity and potentially different biological functions.

The discovery suggests that these cells are not simply passive occupants of body fat. Some may help maintain metabolic health, while others may contribute to the inflammatory processes associated with obesity.

“Eosinophils are more complex than we once thought,” said Nair, a professor of biomedical sciences at UCR’s School of Medicine. She explained that identifying and activating the biological pathways responsible for producing protective eosinophils could open new possibilities for improving metabolic health.

But perhaps the most striking finding was the difference between male and female mice. Female mice had a population of eosinophils that appeared to work more effectively with macrophages, another group of immune cells found in fat tissue. Their cooperation seemed to support a healthier environment within fat tissue and better metabolic function.

Male mice, however, showed a different response when exposed to a high-fat diet. They were more likely to develop eosinophil populations associated with inflammation, alongside weaker protective activity in their fat tissue.

In other words, the health implications of obesity may depend not just on how much fat the body stores, but also on the immune cells operating within that fat and how effectively they communicate with one another.

Rebecca E. Ruggiero-Ruff, a postdoctoral researcher in Nair’s laboratory and co-first author of the study, said the findings showed that counting eosinophils alone could not explain their influence on obesity. Their functional characteristics and interactions with neighbouring immune cells were equally important.

The researchers also identified a protein, RELM alpha, which could hold a key to understanding why some fat tissue is better protected against inflammation. Produced by macrophages, RELM alpha appeared to help maintain communication between macrophages and eosinophils in female mice. This interaction may explain, at least partly, why certain immune cell populations support healthier fat tissue.

The finding builds on earlier experiments by the same research group, which showed that administering RELM alpha to mice produced protective effects. Together, the results point to a possible role for the protein in regulating immune activity within fat tissue and influencing the body’s response to obesity.

For millions of people living with obesity, however, the discovery is not yet a treatment breakthrough. The experiments were conducted in mice, and although eosinophils have also been identified in the fat tissue of people with obesity, their precise functions in humans remain poorly understood.

Researchers say it is too early to establish whether the same protective mechanisms operate in men and women. That uncertainty is particularly important as scientists explore immune-based approaches to treating obesity and its complications.

Rather than treating all immune cells as though they perform the same function, future therapies could target specific cell populations and the communication pathways that influence inflammation and metabolic health.

For now, the central question remains whether the differences uncovered in mice also explain why obesity and its complications can affect men and women differently.

Vanguard News

title: Scientists uncover hidden inherited form of aggressive prostate cancer
description:
By Sola Ogundipe



A man could inherit a genetic mutation that silently puts him at risk of an aggressive form of prostate cancer, develop the disease in his 40s and discover it only after the cancer has spread beyond the prostate. Scientists say they have uncovered a previously unknown hereditary
content:
By Sola Ogundipe

A man could inherit a genetic mutation that silently puts him at risk of an aggressive form of prostate cancer, develop the disease in his 40s and discover it only after the cancer has spread beyond the prostate. Scientists say they have uncovered a previously unknown hereditary pathway that could help explain some of these devastating cases.

The discovery, by researchers at the University of British Columbia (UBC), Canada, has identified inherited mutations in a gene known as CDK12 as a potential cause of exceptionally aggressive prostate cancer, challenging the long-held belief that changes in the gene occur only within cancer cells during tumour development.

Although extremely rare, the finding could have far-reaching implications for families with a history of prostate cancer, particularly those in which men develop the disease unusually early or are diagnosed after it has spread.

In a study published in the journal Cancer Discovery, researchers analysed genetic data from more than 4,500 people with aggressive prostate cancer and identified five unrelated men carrying inherited CDK12 mutations.

The disturbing finding was that all five developed metastatic prostate cancer between the ages of 44 and 62. Metastatic cancer means the disease has spread beyond its original location, making treatment more challenging and reducing the prospects of a cure.

The researchers said the discovery offers an opportunity to identify unsuspecting family members carrying the same mutation before they develop cancer or, more importantly, before the disease reaches an advanced stage.

Dr. Alexander Wyatt, associate professor of urologic sciences at UBC’s Faculty of Medicine said: “What’s striking is that every patient we identified with this inherited mutation had already developed metastatic disease by the time they were diagnosed. The opportunity now is to identify these families earlier and give people the chance to benefit from enhanced screening, when there are still curative treatment options.”

Wyatt, who is also a senior research scientist at the Vancouver Prostate Centre and BC Cancer, said the availability of existing testing technology could accelerate the translation of the discovery into clinical practice.

“One of the most exciting aspects of this discovery is that we already have the technology needed to act on it. Adding CDK12 to existing genetic tests is relatively straightforward, which means this discovery could move from the research lab into clinical care much more quickly,” he said.

The findings add a new dimension to the growing understanding of hereditary cancers. While most cancers arise from genetic changes acquired during a person’s lifetime, an estimated five to 10 per cent are associated with inherited mutations that can be passed from parents to children.

BRCA1 and BRCA2 are among the best-known examples, CDK12 could now become another important gene in the search for families vulnerable to aggressive cancer.

For years, scientists believed that harmful CDK12 alterations were acquired spontaneously within cancer cells rather than inherited from parents. The new study challenges that assumption.

To establish whether the mutations were directly involved in causing the cancer, the researchers examined the tumours for a distinctive molecular pattern associated with the loss of CDK12 function.

They found a genetic fingerprint linking the inherited mutations to the development of the cancers, providing evidence that the mutations were not merely incidental findings.

Dr. Sofie Tolmeijer, a postdoctoral fellow in the Wyatt laboratory said: “The tumours provided us with a genetic signature that pointed directly back to CDK12. It gave us compelling evidence that these inherited mutations were playing a direct role in causing their cancer.

“While this mutation is extremely rare, the discovery could be lifesaving for the families who carry it,” Tolmeijer said.

Despite the potentially serious consequences, inherited CDK12 mutations remain exceptionally uncommon. They were identified in approximately one out of every 1,000 people with aggressive prostate cancer.

However, researchers estimate that hundreds of families worldwide could carry the mutation, making its identification important despite its rarity.

The most immediate implication of the discovery is the possibility of incorporating CDK12 into existing genetic testing panels for hereditary prostate cancer.

The researchers said the technology needed to detect CDK12 mutations is already available, meaning its inclusion in existing tests would not require the development of an entirely new diagnostic system.

For families affected, identifying one carrier could open the door to testing other relatives and determining who might also be at risk.

Beyond prostate cancer, the researchers also uncovered evidence suggesting that inherited CDK12 mutations may be associated with ovarian cancer, although the relationship remains to be established.

Some of the men identified in the study had relatives with a history of ovarian cancer. Researchers also identified another individual with ovarian cancer who carried an inherited CDK12 mutation.

Examination of that person’s tumour revealed the same distinctive genetic signature found in the prostate cancer cases.

The observation raises the possibility that CDK12 mutations could contribute to inherited cancer susceptibility beyond the prostate. However, further studies are needed to establish the extent of the risk and whether additional screening recommendations are justified.

The post Scientists uncover hidden inherited form of aggressive prostate cancer appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Delta: Six suspects in custody, no justice yet for Adeda?
description:
By Egufe Yafugborhi



From a workplace assault to justice in limbo, family grief and fears deepen 58 days after death of a Delta State Deputy Director.



Fifty-eight days after Unity Ekwevugbe Adeda died following a brutal workplace assault in Asaba, Delta State, six suspects remain in police cust
content:
By Egufe Yafugborhi

From a workplace assault to justice in limbo, family grief and fears deepen 58 days after death of a Delta State Deputy Director.

Fifty-eight days after Unity Ekwevugbe Adeda died following a brutal workplace assault in Asaba, Delta State, six suspects remain in police custody, but no charges have been filed and no autopsy conducted to establish precise medical cause of death.

For the Adeda family of Otovwodo, Ughelli, the prolonged wait for answers is deepening their grief and fears that those responsible for the death of their son could escape justice.

Adeda, a Level 16 Deputy Director in the Department of Examination and Standards, Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education, died on September 24, 2026, following a physical altercation at his workplace.

His death triggered protests by civil servants. It led to the constitution of an administrative panel of inquiry by the Delta State Government. The police also commenced separate criminal investigation.

But nearly two months after the incident, the family and concerned stakeholders are asking what progress has been made towards prosecution.

Six Suspects, No Charges

The police investigation, handled by the Homicide Section of the State Criminal Investigation Department, has resulted in six arrests, including Dr. Kingsley Ashibogwu, Commissioner for Secondary Education, and Mrs Clementine Ufuoma, Director of Basic and Secondary Education.

The arrests began with Lucky Adoh, an aide to the commissioner, shortly after the incident. Ashibogwu and three other suspects were subsequently taken into custody, bringing the number to five. Ufuoma, earlier declared wanted, later surrendered, increasing the number to six.

Despite the arrests, no formal charges have been announced.

Under the criminal justice process, the police are expected to conclude investigations, compile their findings and forward the duplicate case file to the Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP), Ministry of Justice, for legal advice. The DPP is expected to examine the evidence and determine whether a prima facie case exists to warrant formal charges.

However, the process has yet to reach that stage publicly, leaving questions about when the investigation will be concluded.

For Austine Aghomi, Coordinator, Journalists for Just Development of the Niger Delta, the silence of the police and the delay in providing meaningful updates are increasingly troubling.

He said: “But more concerning is the arrested progress on the part of the police. When will investigations be concluded?

“Can’t prosecution progress with a few other suspects still at large? Where is the autopsy to determine or confirm Adeda’s true cause of death after the assault?

“The police have not helped this case at all and it is just another test of integrity, seeing the police mum on this case for so long without offering meaningful updates.

“It’s like a conspiracy theory is building over this matter. Let there be justice for Adeda.”

The absence of an autopsy is another major concern. The deceased’s family has been pressing for the exercise to establish the medical cause of death and provide important forensic evidence for the investigation. No autopsy has yet been conducted.

Panel Report, White Paper Pending

While the criminal investigation continues, the Delta State Government has completed another aspect of its inquiry into the incident.

The eight-member administrative panel, chaired by the State Head of Service, Dr Charity Babigha-Ehime, was constituted on September 25 in consultation with organised labour. It was given two weeks to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident, particularly possible breaches of public service rules and civil service ethics.

Its deadline expired on October 9, but the government did not announce receipt of its report until November 16.

Receiving the report, Secretary to the State Government, Dr Kingsley Emu, explained that the panel encountered difficulties interviewing persons in police custody under stringent conditions, requiring his personal intervention to facilitate access.

Emu stated: “Today, on behalf of the state government, I received the report of the administrative panel of inquiry set up by the state government to investigate the altercation that happened in the Department of Examination and Standards, Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education.

“While a separate criminal investigation is being carried out by law enforcement agencies, the administrative panel’s primary focus was to examine the circumstances surrounding the participation of public servants and to uncover the extent of any breaches of public service rules and civil service ethics.

“The state government will thoroughly review the report and produce a comprehensive white paper to guide future administrative actions.”

But Aghomi said the announcement offered little reassurance without a definite timeline for releasing and implementing the white paper.

“The Emu acknowledgement of receipt of the panel report offers nothing meaningful to pursuit of justice in this case. This was a report that was nearly two months too late to be submitted.

“Announcing it makes no sense to the case. If anything, what is expected of government is to address when the white paper on the report will be released and implemented.

“That Emu was evasive of giving a clear timeline on that was deliberate. They probably want it to postdate electioneering campaigns so the people won’t use any disclosure for or against Governor Oborevwori. We probably won’t see that white paper this year,” he alleged.

The family had earlier rejected the panel’s composition, questioning the independence of an inquiry involving public servants without representation from the bereaved family or civil society organisations. Residents of Otovwodo also protested against the panel.

Family Fears Another Unresolved Murder

For the family, the delay in obtaining answers is compounding the pain of losing their son.

Oberhirhi Adeda, lawyer and Secretary to the Chief James Okpanovwe Adeda Family of Otovwodo, Ughelli, recently appealed for sustained media attention to the case, expressing fears that the perpetrators might escape justice if the necessary momentum was not maintained.

He said: “The entire Adeda family, like most Nigerians, have continued to be saddened by the brutal murder of our son, Mr Unity Adeda, who was until his brutal death, the Deputy Director in the Delta State Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education.

“Although investigation is ongoing, we the Adeda family are apparently afraid, and justifiably so too, that the perpetrators of the heinous crime may escape justice unless the required momentum is sustained on the matter.

“Our nation has records of so many unresolved murder cases where culprits walk the streets freely while leaving trails of agony with survivors of their victim. We do not want the case of our valued son to follow suit.”

The family acknowledged Governor Sheriff Oborevwori’s reported promise that everything would be done to ensure justice.

Oberhirhi added: “It is heartwarming that the Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, reportedly promised that everything would be done to ensure that justice is served.

“We pray that all those who are involved in the premature death of our valued son ‘Unity’, never know peace until the long hands of the law catches up with them.”

Accountability Beyond Politics

The case has also attracted political attention, with Chris Iyovwaye, Delta governorship candidate of the New Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), challenging Oborevwori to provide answers on Adeda’s death while demanding accountability over the November 7 violence at an NDC rally in Asaba.

Iyovwaye said: “Governor, you must also speak to Deltans about the death of Mr Unity Adeda. What has the investigation established about the circumstances of his death?

“What is the status of those arrested, including your Commissioner for Secondary Education? Have charges been filed?

“We demand a public update and the prosecution of anyone against whom the evidence supports charges, regardless of office.”

For the Adeda family, however, the overriding concern is not political exchanges but the conclusion of the investigation and prosecution of anyone found culpable.

Fifty-eight days after their son died, six arrests have produced no publicly announced charges, the autopsy remains outstanding, even as the family cares less about administrative panel’s outcome, having faulted its composition from the beggining.

The questions persist: When will the police conclude their investigation? When will the autopsy be conducted? When will the government release its white paper?

For a family still mourning, arrests and official assurances are not justice. Until the investigation produces concrete legal action and those found responsible face the law, the search for justice for Unity Adeda remains unfinished.

Vanguard News

The post Delta: Six suspects in custody, no justice yet for Adeda? appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: No roof for two masters, by Stephanie Shaakaa
description:
*Bloodline, Ballot Box, and the Bedroom: Lessons from Kano’s High Stakes Political Divorce



A marriage rarely belongs to two people alone. In northern Nigeria, where zumunci binds families through kinship, mutual obligations and family honour, marriage often carries expectations that extend far be
content:
*Bloodline, Ballot Box, and the Bedroom: Lessons from Kano’s High Stakes Political Divorce

A marriage rarely belongs to two people alone. In northern Nigeria, where zumunci binds families through kinship, mutual obligations and family honour, marriage often carries expectations that extend far beyond the couple. For twenty years, the union between Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf and Zainab Musa Kwankwaso appeared to demonstrate that bloodline and political loyalty could coexist under one roof. Today, that roof has given way.

The breakdown of the marriage between Governor Yusuf and Zainab, niece of his estranged political mentor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, and raised in the former governor’s household, is more than a headline from Government House. It raises an uncomfortable question: what happens when the political alliance connecting two families collapses, but the marriage binding them is left caught in its aftermath?

To understand the significance of this separation, one must understand how political trust is built in Kano. Political relationships are not always sustained by ambition and party loyalty alone. Sometimes, they are reinforced through family connections.

When Zainab and Abba Yusuf married on July 29, 2006, Yusuf was already deeply embedded in Kwankwaso’s political circle, having served as his personal and special assistant during Kwankwaso’s first tenure as governor and subsequently during his tenure as Minister of Defence. Zainab, raised in Kwankwaso’s household, was not simply marrying an ambitious politician. Their union connected two families whose fortunes were closely intertwined.

Over twenty years and six children, the marriage became one of the most personal bonds surrounding the Kwankwasiyya movement. Yusuf’s years of loyalty and proximity to Kwankwaso eventually culminated in his emergence as the latter’s preferred successor and his election as governor in 2023. The trusted lieutenant had become governor, with the backing of the political establishment that had shaped his career.

Yet there is a particular difficulty with marriages surrounded by powerful family and political networks. The expectations attached to them can become difficult to separate from the personal commitments of the couple. While everyone shares the same interests, the arrangement may appear harmonious. The real test comes when those interests begin to diverge.

That divergence became unmistakable in January 2026, when Governor Yusuf abandoned the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP), the platform on which he won office, and defected to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). The decision marked a decisive break with Kwankwaso, the political mentor who had nurtured his rise. With Kwankwaso pursuing a different political direction ahead of the 2027 elections, an alliance that once united two households became a bitter contest over Kano’s political future.

The timing of the marital separation has inevitably attracted attention. But timing is not proof of causation.

In her petition before the Upper Area Court in Gudu, Abuja, Zainab sought dissolution through khul’i, an Islamic legal procedure through which a wife may initiate divorce, ordinarily by returning her dowry or offering compensation. She cited an irretrievable breakdown of the marriage, pointing to a prolonged absence of mutual care, love, affection and emotional connection, and stated that reconciliation had failed.

These are the grounds stated in the petition. They must not be replaced with political explanations that have not been established by the court. Nevertheless, the political circumstances surrounding the separation provide an important context for understanding the wider family tensions.

When a protégé breaks with his benefactor, the consequences rarely remain confined to party offices and campaign rallies. Where marriage connects the two households, the rupture becomes harder to contain. A woman whose husband and father figure stand on opposing sides of a bitter political divide occupies a difficult position. It is not for outsiders to presume her feelings, but the circumstances illustrate the pressure competing loyalties can place on a family.

Reports that Zainab left the Kano Government House for her father’s residence before travelling to Abuja brought the domestic situation further into public attention.

On November 16, Governor Yusuf himself addressed the matter publicly. Speaking in Hausa to pensioners at the Government House, he compared having one wife remaining to being demoted from a corporal to a constable, confirmed that divorce papers had been issued and asked residents to pray for him as he prepared to marry again.

Whatever humour he intended, the remarks turned a twenty year marriage and its painful breakdown into public banter while court proceedings remained pending. Six children and two decades of shared history deserved greater restraint.

The significance of the Kano separation, however, extends beyond the political elite. Most Nigerians will never occupy a Government House or become entangled in a dispute between a governor and his political mentor. Yet the family pressures exposed by this episode are familiar in ordinary Nigerian homes.

Across our society, marriages are sometimes expected to serve purposes beyond the happiness of the people entering them. Parents seek to strengthen family alliances, secure financial stability, preserve social standing or satisfy expectations established by elders. Such arrangements may look attractive while everyone remains on the same side. But what happens when the interests that brought the families together begin to conflict?

When the architects behind a family arrangement fall out, the spouse caught in the middle may find ordinary conversations becoming loyalty tests. Visits home begin to look like taking sides. Silence is interpreted as betrayal. The individual is left negotiating between the bloodline that raised them and the partner with whom they have built a life.

This is the danger of allowing external loyalties to become the governing authority of a marriage. Family support should strengthen a home, not compete with the relationship at its centre

Whatever private circumstances brought the Yusuf marriage to this point, twenty years and six children represent a history that deserves dignity. A marriage may end, but its years of shared humanity should never be trivialised. Public office does not diminish the feelings or dignity of the other person in a marriage.

Ultimately, a lasting home requires a foundation that belongs to the couple themselves. Family connections may bring two households together, and politics may elevate their fortunes, but neither should dictate whether their marriage survives.

A person may marry into a family, but marriage should never become a lifelong contract to serve its political interests. No marriage should have to choose between two masters before it can remain a home.

Stephanie Shaakaa

shaakaastephanie@yahoo.com

08078600871

title: Infantino hails Warri Stadium, wants football in every community
description:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino has praised the renovated Warri City Stadium in Delta State, saying football development must extend beyond major stadiums to local communities.



Infantino spoke during a visit to Warri, where he attended the commissioning of the renovated stadium and upgraded sport
content:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino has praised the renovated Warri City Stadium in Delta State, saying football development must extend beyond major stadiums to local communities.

Infantino spoke during a visit to Warri, where he attended the commissioning of the renovated stadium and upgraded sporting facilities.

The FIFA president said football should be accessible to everyone, regardless of their location, adding that smaller stadiums play an important role in bringing the sport closer to communities.

“Yeah, that’s what football is about, isn’t it? It’s for everyone, everywhere,” Infantino told reporters in Warri yesterday.

“It’s big stadiums, it’s the World Cup, but it’s also smaller stadiums. It’s the proximity, and to be here in Warri for me is a fantastic occasion to showcase what we are about in FIFA, what we are about in football.”

Infantino also expressed appreciation for the warm reception he received in Nigeria and across Africa, attributing the relationship to years of collaboration and football development projects aimed at improving the lives of young people.

“Oh yes, I’m feeling so much the love of Africa, the love of Nigeria. This is based, of course, on many years of joint life together, of projects that we’ve put in place, of changing lives of girls and boys,” he said.

title: Obi shuts down Onitsha, visits his alma mater, CKC
description:
•Says Nigeria needs a president that has energy 



By Vincent Ujumadu 



Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi and members of his campaign team, shut down the commercial city of Onitsha on Friday as the party continued its town hall meetings and road shows.
content:
•Says Nigeria needs a president that has energy 

By Vincent Ujumadu 

Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi and members of his campaign team, shut down the commercial city of Onitsha on Friday as the party continued its town hall meetings and road shows.

Obi began with a visit to his alma mater, Christ the King College, CKC, in the heart of the city, where he reminded the students that the school has produced three governors and would soon produce the president of Nigeria.

The three governors produced by CKC are Dr Peter Odili of Rivers State, himself, Peter Obi and Chief Willie Obiano who succeeded him.

Addressing the students, Obi promised to improve the standard of education across the country if voted in as Nigeria’s president after the 2027 elections.

His convoy thereafter did a roadshow from Oguta Road through the popular Upper Iweka to the Head bridge and through Uga road to Modebe avenue to All Saints Cathedral where the town hall meeting took place.

Among those accompanying Obi during road show were Aisha Yusuf, Mama P, among others.

Traders at the drug market and building materials market lined the streets and danced to the NDC music.

The campaign train moved round all the major markets in Onitsha, with many enthusiastic traders closing their shops and headed to the venue of the town hall meeting.

Addressing the people at the town hall meeting, Obi said: “Kwankwaso and I have formed a team that will unite and secure Nigeria. We will secure Nigeria, fight corruption and use public money for public good.

“I assure Nigerians that from day one, they will be feeling good impact of their country. You will know that a new team is in charge.

We will ensure that a new Nigeria is possible and move the country from consumption to production.

“We will create jobs and employ our people.

We cannot continue with the present situation where our children don’t have jobs because that is not the way a country should be.

“We want a country where, when you are sick, you go to hospital and not to church. The Pope was sick and went to hospital and after the hospital he prayed.”

According to Obi, there will be functional health care center in every ward in Nigeria, adding , “We have promised to build 10,000 health care centers across the country.

Kwankwaso and I have said that from day one, we will start the building of ,40,000 school blocks. We will invest in education, in health and in critical areas Nigerians will be proud of”

He lamented that Nigeria currently generates only about 5,000 megawatts of electricity, saying “Kwankwaso and I are assuring Nigerians that our country will generate, transmit and distribute 10,000, megawatts.”

“I want all of you to take note of everything I say in this town hall meeting. We don’t want to make false promises. We are not going to tell Nigerians what we saw when we came in. We are seeing everything now and we are planning for it.”

I commend our party leaders who have shown that they are ready for the battle. Nigeria had suffered enough and our people have suffered enough.

To the voters he advised,: “I want all of you to know that you are contestants in the forthcoming elections, although you are doing it through those of us that are candidates. So, on that day, sacrifice it for Nigeria.

“While going to vote, carry your food, and after voting, stay there until they count and transmit the votes. Do not leave. That day should be a holiday for voting..

“You are all agents of the party. In the 2027 election, everybody is a party agent. Vote NDC for the president, Senate, House of Representatives for the first day and House of Assembly for the next one.

“Don’t be afraid of anybody that day. If anybody asks you to leave that polling station, tell him you won’t step out until the result is declared. That day should be set aside for people to defend their votes. Let nobody tell you stories; we are prepared and nobody will rig this election. We want to assure Nigerians that our commitment is total.”

Obi recalled that when President Tinubu came and removed fuel subsidy, prices of everything went beyond the reach of Nigerians and hunger and suffering became the order of the day.

“That is what we want to change so that Nigeria will be good. When the president came in , he said he won’t borrow because of the removal of fuel subsidy, but since then, we have not implemented 2024, 2025 budgets.

“Today, he has borrowed more money than all the previous governments put together. The question is, where is our money? For this, Tinubu must go. We want a government that is competent, has compassion and can care for the people; a government that has commitment and character.

“Above all, we want a government that has energy. Our current president has to go and rest because he is tired. This job requires energy and the person doing it must have energy. That is why we are begging him to go and rest.”

title: How Odegbami survived assassination attempt
description:
•Attackers inflict machete cut on him •NFF expressess shock •Police vow to bring perpetrators to justice



By Tony Ubani & James Ogunnaike



Former Super Eagles captain and Nigerian football legend, Chief Segun Odegbami, survived assassination yesterday when three armed men attacked him at his res
content:
•Attackers inflict machete cut on him •NFF expressess shock •Police vow to bring perpetrators to justice

By Tony Ubani & James Ogunnaike

Former Super Eagles captain and Nigerian football legend, Chief Segun Odegbami, survived assassination yesterday when three armed men attacked him at his residence in Ibara Government Reservation Area (GRA), Abeokuta, Ogun state inflicting deep machete wounds on him before they fled.

The attackers first overpowered his domestic staff and driver before making their way into his bedroom In his brief account which he posted on Sports platform, Chief Odegbami wrote: “Thank the Creator of the Universe for me, I survived an assassination attempt. This morning at 2:30 am. 3 unknown persons came to the house to steal and kill. I fought back with the help of God. My driver and house boy joined me, and we fought them before they fled. It was the closest I have ever been face to face with death. They broke down my door to get to me. I have been to the hospital Chief Segun Odegbami”.

The Nigeria Football Federation expressed shock over the attack even as the state Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, visited the 74 years old football icon to sympathise with him and reassure him of the command’s commitment to bring the perpetrators to justice.

During the attack, Odegbami, popularly known as ‘Mathematical’ during his illustrious playing career, reportedly put up stiff resistance when the armed men confronted him, resulting in a violent struggle.

However, the attackers eventually escaped after inflicting deep cuts on him, leaving him seriously injured.

A community resident, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the attackers arrived at the residence and initially demanded to see the former international but his domestic staff said he was not at home. The attackers reportedly became suspicious after noticing that the generator was running, suggesting that someone was inside the house. According to the resident, “the incident is unfortunate. The armed men struck in the early hours of Friday and first overpowered the domestic staff. They asked for Chief Segun Odegbami, but his staff denied that he was at home.

“But the generator was running at the time. So, the armed men believed he must be around and subjected the staff to severe beatings before making their way to Odegbami’s bedroom, where they attacked him.

“Not willing to succumb easily, Odegbami resisted his attackers. They eventually fled the scene, leaving him with deep machete cuts and bleeding heavily,” the source added.

The football legend was subsequently rushed to an undisclosed hospital for medical attention.

Residents of the community confirmed that the incident was promptly reported to the police. However, the motive behind the attack remained unknown as of the time the incident was reported.

Police vow to bring perpetrators to justice

Meanwhile, the Ogun State Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, has visited Odegbami to sympathise with him over the attack and reassure him of the command’s commitment to bringing the perpetrators to justice.

During the visit, Ojajuni expressed concern over the incident and wished the former Super Eagles captain a speedy and complete recovery. The commissioner also assured him that the police command was treating the matter with utmost seriousness, disclosing that he had ordered an immediate and thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack.

According to a statement made available to journalists by the command’s spokesperson, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, the commissioner said intensive investigative efforts were underway to identify and apprehend those responsible.

The statement partly reads, “the Commissioner of Police, Ogun State Command, CP Bode Ojajuni, has paid a visit to former Super Eagles captain and renowned sports administrator, Chief Segun Odegbami, to express the Command’s sympathy following the reported incident at his residence in Abeokuta.

“The Commissioner conveyed his concern and wished him continued recovery, reaffirming the Command’s commitment to protecting lives and property across the state.

“CP Ojajuni assured Chief Odegbami that the incident is receiving the Command’s utmost attention. He disclosed that he had ordered an immediate and thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident, while intensive investigative efforts are ongoing to identify and apprehend those responsible.

“He emphasised that the Command would leave no stone unturned in ensuring that the perpetrators are brought to justice.

“The Command confirms that Chief Odegbami has been discharged from the hospital and assures members of the public that all necessary steps are being taken to ensure a thorough investigation and appropriate action. Residents are encouraged to remain calm and provide credible information that could assist the investigation through established Police channels”.

Odegbami, one of Nigeria’s most celebrated football figures, is the proprietor of Eagles 7 Sports Radio 103.7 FM, based in Abeokuta.

NFF shocked by attack on Odegbami

Meanwhile, the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has expressed shock over the attack on former international and Nigerian football legend, Segun Odegbami, describing him as a national treasure whose contributions to the country remain invaluable.

Reacting to the incident, NFF Director of Communications, Ademola Olajire, said the federation was grateful that Odegbami survived the attack and called on the police to ensure that the perpetrators are brought to book.

“We’re shocked to hear this ugly news and are indeed grateful that Odegbami is alive,” Olajire said yesterday.

He also urged the security agencies to tighten security around the former Super Eagles captain to prevent a recurrence.

“Odegbami is a living legend who did his all to bring joy to the living rooms of Nigerians. Despite retiring from football, he is still in the forefront of efforts to ensure the good of the game,” Olajire added.

Nigerians were thrown into panic yesterday following reports that Odegbami had survived an attack by suspected armed assailants.

title: Tinubu’s re-election campaign backed by visible evidence, not just promises — Oshiomhole
description:
Sen. Adams Oshiomhole has said that President Bola Tinubu’s re-election campaign possess strong backing with evidence of work done in the first tenure and not just promises for the future.



Oshiomhole said this at the groundbreaking ceremony of the National Passport Booklet Manufacturing Centre on
content:
Sen. Adams Oshiomhole has said that President Bola Tinubu’s re-election campaign possess strong backing with evidence of work done in the first tenure and not just promises for the future.

Oshiomhole said this at the groundbreaking ceremony of the National Passport Booklet Manufacturing Centre on Friday in Abuja. Oshiomhole is the Chairman, Senate Committee on Interior.

According to Oshiomhole, the campaign by the incumbent president did not only focus on promises for the future but acknowledged his achievements, highlighting the passport manufacturing centre.

“For me, the real campaign is not about promising what we will do. It is about showing what President Tinubu is already doing through the Ministry of Interior, and in this case, the Nigeria Immigration Service,” he said.

He said that Tinubu possessed a “can do spirit” and believed that anything can be done before done anywhere in the world if the determination is there.

He maintained that he also seconded the president’s notion of the second tenure being the time to benefit the prosperity of the reforms and huge sacrifices made by Nigerians prior.

He likened the situation to the feeding of a stabilised patient who could not eat as much during treatment due to appetite, possible health complications and reactions.

“It is time to begin to give the patient all the milk, all the food, all of those nutrients needed, which had to be slowed down in the course of the surgery,” he said.

Oshiomhole described Tinubu as the “enabler in chief” who has dedicated his first tenure to enabling Ministries and agencies to rebuild the Nigeria of our dreams.

“No minister should complain about Mr President. It is easy to recognise his commitment to youth empowerment which is meant to bring energy, new vision and a commitment to using modern technology to refix and rebuild Nigeria.

“President Tinubu has taught us not to feel inferior as a people to any other nation because the truth and the fact is that we are not,” he said.

The senator commended the Interior Minister, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo for his aggression and hunger to break new grounds and generate new ideas that improve the travelling condition of Nigerians with the passport manufacturing centre.

“Tunji-Ojo is one of the youngest ministers and he has shown that it is not necessarily by age but by the quality of the brain, your capacity to think, to dream big and act even bigger,” he said.

Oshiomhole also said that the development would silence Nigerians in the Diaspora who used to lament about the dysfunctionality in Nigeria due to inability to renew their passports in order to visit family in Nigeria.

“Whether they were in America, Europe, or Asia, the Tunji-Ojo has dealt with the issues satisfactorily. My own grandchildren tell me the now have a Nigerian passport.

“These are real stories that speak of what is changing and that is the real meaning of renewed hope.

“If a man that couldn’t get a passport, even as a Nigerian is now celebrating, have you not renewed this hope in our country? That is the renewed hope agenda,” said the senator..

He also commended the NIS for its reforms and adoption of technology to curb long processes in travel documentations, highlighting that he has experienced it first hand.

“My last two trips outside, I came back and I was told to approach a machine. I put my passport on it, and it recognised me, opened and I passed.

“There were no long queues of questioning. The machine spoke to me, and I answered. That is the power of technology. That is the power of the initiative and the can-do spirit, which Tinubu has always spoken about,” he said.

He also urged the interior ministry to ensure that the construction of the centre is done in entirety by Nigerian workers in order to create opportunities for Nigerians.

“Let those electricians, bricklayers, technicians, masons, drivers and those who will supply this granite be Nigerian workers. And let them be paid decent wages because they are working for a decent agency that will not compromise the welfare of the Nigerian people,” he added.
