title: 2027: NYSC warns politicians against inducing corpers
description:
The National Youth Service Corps has warned politicians in Rivers State against offering food, water, drinks or other inducements to corps members who will serve as ad hoc staff of the Independent National Electoral Commission during the 2027 general elections.
According to the organization, corps m
content:
The National Youth Service Corps has warned politicians in Rivers State against offering food, water, drinks or other inducements to corps members who will serve as ad hoc staff of the Independent National Electoral Commission during the 2027 general elections.

According to the organization, corps members must be allowed to perform their electoral duties without interference, warning that anyone found accepting inducements from politicians would face appropriate sanctions.

The Rivers State Coordinator of the scheme, Moses Oleghe, gave the warning on Thursday while delivering his goodwill message at a state-level stakeholders’ meeting on the 2027 general elections at the INEC headquarters in Port Harcourt.

He urged politicians to desist from attempts to influence corps members, insisting that they must maintain their neutrality and integrity throughout the electoral process.

Oleghe also appealed to INEC to make adequate provisions for the welfare of corps members, including payment of allowances, transportation and other essential logistics, arguing that providing their entitlements would enable them to cater for their basic needs without depending on politicians.

He said, “We have to hold our corps members not to take anything from any politician. Don’t induce them. Allow them to do their work. It is a national assignment and they are committed to it.

“If INEC pays them their transport, they will not be hungry, so don’t bring food for them. Don’t bring water for them, don’t bring drinks for them.

“I can assure this gathering that if all of these are put in place, the corps members are well prepared to deliver on the mandate that they have been given.”

The NYSC coordinator, however, raised concerns over the treatment of corps members during previous elections, saying some had been stranded or abandoned by their Supervisory Presiding Officers in unsafe locations, thereby exposing them to danger.

He insisted that such experiences would not be tolerated during the 2027 elections, urging INEC to put adequate arrangements in place to protect corps members and ensure their welfare.

Oleghe said the NYSC had commenced sensitisation programmes in collaboration with INEC to prepare corps members for their responsibilities during the forthcoming elections.

He, however, stressed that the exercise would yield little result without proper planning and coordination among the electoral commission, security agencies and other stakeholders.

The NYSC boss urged the Resident Electoral Commissioner to ensure that corps members were trained by personnel with adequate knowledge of the electronic devices and other technologies to be deployed for the elections.

He also expressed concern over instances where corps members who had undergone training and reported at Registration Area Centres were replaced during deployment.

He said corps members who had made themselves available for training and deployment but were subsequently excluded should be paid their entitlements.

Oleghe further called on INEC to improve basic facilities at RAC centres, noting that corps members were often expected to remain at the centres from the afternoon before election day until the conclusion of voting and other electoral activities without adequate provisions.

He said facilities such as sleeping mats, drinking water, toilets, soap, tissue paper, electricity and security should be provided at the centres.

The coordinator also called for the early release of complete election materials, insisting that no corps member should leave a RAC centre for an assigned polling unit without all the materials required to discharge their duties.

title: CAF to revive Super Eagles AFCON hope
description:

Last year CAF president Patrice Motsepe said the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) will expand from 24 to 28 teams starti
content:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) will deliberate on the number of teams that will be at the next Africa Cup of Nations, which will be hosted by Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania.

Last year CAF president Patrice Motsepe said the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) will expand from 24 to 28 teams starting with the 2027 tournament, co-hosted by Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda from June 19 to July 17, 2027.

He also revealed that the tournament will run once in every four years. A plan that has been shelved but there has been no pronouncement on the number of teams that will be at the next tournament.

The fact that all three of the hosts are taking part in the qualifiers reducing the number of teams that will qualify from their groups to one rather than two, has further added fuel to the debate to stick with the plan of extending the teams to 28.

28 will mean half of the members of CAF taking part in the tournament, and if it is approved each group in the qualifiers will produce two teams which allows for fairness, but also play into the favour of Nigeria who are guaranteed of finishing second in their group behind current leaders Guinea-Bissau.

Already head coach of Guinea Paul Duarte has labelled the format of one team qualifying from their group as an injustice with his team currently second behind South Africa heading into the last round of games.

“With two more wins, it is obvious that if our group had the same rules as the others, with two teams qualifying, Guinea would already be qualified for AFCON 2027. Despite this injustice, we are not giving up. We will keep fighting for first place. Guinea deserves this qualification”, he lamented.

The post CAF to revive Super Eagles AFCON hope appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Cute Abiola Comedy Festival heads to London
description:
The Comedy Festival with Cute Abiola is set to expand beyond Nigeria, with London announced as the next destination for the event in March 2027.

content:
The Comedy Festival with Cute Abiola is set to expand beyond Nigeria, with London announced as the next destination for the event in March 2027.

The development follows successful editions held in Ilorin, Kwara State, on July 11, 2026, and Ibadan, Oyo State, on September 27, 2026.

The festival, produced by Ashipa Network and packaged by Khapy of Lagos, has attracted personalities from the comedy, music, filmmaking, streaming and digital content industries, positioning it as a growing platform for entertainment and cultural engagement.

Speaking on the planned expansion, Director of Ashipa Network, Kolawole Ashipa, said the success of the Ibadan edition motivated the decision to take the production to the United Kingdom.

He, however, clarified that the international expansion would not affect the festival’s planned tour of Nigerian cities, revealing that preparations were underway for editions in Osun, Ogun and Abuja.

“Our vision has always been to take this experience from one city to another, creating opportunities for entertainment, cultural exchange and economic engagement. While we continue our expansion across Nigeria, we also believe Nigerians in the diaspora deserve to experience what we are building back home,” Ashipa said.

He added that taking the festival to London would provide an opportunity to showcase Nigerian entertainment and creativity to a wider international audience.

Meanwhile, comedian Cute Abiola expressed appreciation to the Oyo State Government for its support and presence at the Ibadan edition.

He also acknowledged the contributions of celebrities, partners and other entertainment industry stakeholders who supported the event.

The previous editions featured more than 30 entertainment personalities each, including streamers Carter Efe, Peller and Trinity; musicians Skibii, Shoday, Rybeena, Segun Johnson and Danny S; as well as actors Femi Adebayo, Eniola Ajao, Kemity and Yemi Elesho.

Others included content creators Taaooma, Kidbaby, Kamo State and Ozain, alongside comedians Kenny Blaq, Baba Kamo, Alariya and Yunusa.

The organisers said the London edition was expected to create opportunities for corporate brands, investors and strategic partners while introducing the festival to Nigerians in the diaspora and other lovers of African entertainment in the United Kingdom.

For Ashipa Network and its packaging partner, Khapy of Lagos, the expansion represents an effort to build a sustainable entertainment brand that connects cities, promotes Nigerian creativity and creates opportunities within the global entertainment industry.

The organisers maintained that the festival would continue its Nigerian tour alongside its international expansion, with London scheduled as its next destination in March 2027.

title: Why INEC can’t finish voter register clean-up – Amupitan
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has said it will not be able to conduct a comprehensive clean-up of the national voters’ register before the 2027 general elections, citing time constraints and public resistance to its earlier plan to revalidate the register.
The commission’s chairman,
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has said it will not be able to conduct a comprehensive clean-up of the national voters’ register before the 2027 general elections, citing time constraints and public resistance to its earlier plan to revalidate the register.

The commission’s chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, disclosed this while appearing on a Bereke Family TV programme aired on Friday.

Amupitan said the commission had initially proposed a six-month exercise to remove deceased persons, underage voters, incomplete registrations and duplicate entries from the register but shelved the plan after opposition.

His explanation follows controversy over alleged irregularities in the preliminary voter register, particularly duplicate entries that drew criticism on social media.

Speaking during the programme, Amupitan said the commission had decided to postpone the comprehensive exercise until after the 2027 elections, although it was addressing cases of multiple registrations following public complaints.

According to him, the commission found that most complaints stemmed from the old register, which contained records dating back to 2011.

He said: “The complaint that came out on social media, those ones, majorly when we investigated further, we discovered it was the old register, the new one we have dealt with it. But the one that everybody is shouting about, complaining about duplication were mostly from the old register.

“In February, we decided that the foundation of a good election is a valid voters’ register. Let us do the validation because people who have already died were still in the register, and many names were doubled.

“We said the process would only take six months. Let us clean up so that people can come and update their details, but Nigerians said no. So, we said we would do it after the election.”

Amupitan said the commission had planned to use improved technology to detect irregularities that earlier registration systems missed.

He added that the proposed exercise was also meant to address incomplete registrations and underage entries, besides removing deceased persons.

Amupitan, however, said the commission could no longer carry out the entire exercise before the next general elections because of limited time.

He said INEC had instead returned to tackling duplicate entries, especially those flagged by the public.

Amupitan said some cases were particularly disturbing, with the same person appearing in the register with as many as five different photographs.

He said: “We cannot do everything now; we have no time to do it, but we can do duplications, those ones they are flagging.

“Some of the cases involve five pictures of the same person. It is very ridiculous, truly, and we cannot close our eyes to it. We are doing that right now to ensure that the register is clean.”

Amupitan also disclosed that the review had reduced the number of registered voters, adding that the commission would release the final register once the ongoing review ended.

He said INEC had initially scheduled December 15 for releasing the final register but was reviewing the timeline after widespread complaints.

The post Why INEC can’t finish voter register clean-up – Amupitan appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
Nollywood actor John Ekanem has taken the lead role in Time Bound, a supernatural thriller exploring themes of death, destiny, love, betrayal and second chances.

The film, according to a statement made available to Sunday Scoop, blends mystery, suspense and drama in a storyline centred on a man whose life takes an unexpected turn following a mysterious curse, an untimely death and an extraordinary second chance at life.

Driven by unsettling events and hidden secrets, the protagonist finds himself caught between destiny and survival as he struggles to reclaim his life and confront forces threatening his existence.

The statement described the film as an exploration of betrayal, human relationships and difficult choices that can alter the course of people’s lives.

Ekanem stars alongside Sonia Uche, Ichie Fuego and Blessing Onwukwe in the production, which explores the thin line between life and death and questions whether people can escape destinies beyond their control.

The film combines suspense, emotional twists and supernatural elements to sustain viewers’ interest as the mystery unfolds.

It also explores the cost of love and sacrifice, raising questions about whether a second chance at life is always a blessing.

Speaking in an interview with Saturday Beats, the actress stressed that filmmakers should pay attention to actor
content:
Popular actress Bimbo Ademoye has described fashion as an important part of filmmaking, saying costume choices contribute significantly to storytelling and the overall viewing experience.

Speaking in an interview with Saturday Beats, the actress stressed that filmmakers should pay attention to actors’ outfits, noting that costumes should communicate something about the characters and the stories being told.

“A storyline is very important. Picture quality is also very important. But the outfits one wears in a movie are important too. Even if one is wearing a rag, it should be able to tell a story. Even if they are pressing their phones, they are listening to the lines being delivered with their ears. As they are looking at the screen, they are also looking at what you are wearing and listening to what you are saying. So, make it worthwhile. Fashion and Nollywood are a match made in heaven,” she said.

Speaking about the fashion moments in her recent movie, My 30th Wedding, Ademoye said the looks were deliberately put together and required considerable effort.

“The fashion moments in the movie were intentional. I had sleepless nights putting that together. Was it intentional? Definitely,” the actress added.

On what aspiring professionals should do when faced with discouragement, the actress advised them to reassess their approach, identify their mistakes and remain persistent.

“If you are discouraged, as easy as it is to say keep going, I would say go back to the drawing board. Know what it is you are doing wrong, then you can start over and keep going. One day, you will definitely strike the diamond,” she said.

content:
Nollywood actress and humanitarian Sarah Martins has said she has never experienced sexual harassment while carrying out her street cooking and community feeding activities.

In an interview with Saturday Beats, Martins said no one had made inappropriate advances towards her during the outreaches.

“No, I have never experienced sexual harassment while carrying out my street cooking and community feeding activities. I have been blessed with the kind of audience I get. They respect the woman behind the project. I always get my due respect,” she said.

The actress also addressed the issue of encountering men who demanded sexual favours in exchange for sponsorship or professional opportunities.

“It has been exhausting sponsoring myself. I hardly get sponsorship offers, probably because I don’t reach out to people for assistance. I feel people should reach out to me themselves if they want to sponsor. But I have never gotten sponsorship that comes with sexual conditions,” she said.

Martins identified street bullies who demanded money from her while she cooked in public spaces as one of the challenges of her humanitarian work.

She explained that while some eventually withdrew their demands and joined the feeding activities, others made unreasonable demands and caused disturbances.

Beyond the challenges, the actress said she hoped to expand her community feeding initiative to reach more people across Nigeria.

Martins disclosed that her outreach had extended to Port Harcourt, where she claimed to have fed more than 1,000 people in two days.

She appealed to entertainers, including Davido and Burna Boy, as well as the government, to provide financial support for the initiative.

“My outreach needs support from the likes of Davido, Burna Boy, and the government entirely. I believe where there is no hunger, love answers,” she added.

The actress also advised young women, particularly those who are beautiful and curvy, not to allow public opinions about their appearance to distract them from their ambitions.

According to her, women should be recognised for their intelligence, achievements and contributions to society rather than judged solely by their physical appearance.

The post My street cooking outreach needs support from Davido, Burna Boy – Sarah Martins appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Mega churches face succession heat
description: The leadership crisis rocking the Fountain of Life Church, Lagos, has brought succession arrangements in some of the country’s biggest Pentecostal churches under fresh scrutiny, with renewed attention on statements by prominent clerics, including Pastor William Kumuyi, Pastor Enoch Adeboye and Bisho
content:
The leadership crisis rocking the Fountain of Life Church, Lagos, has brought succession arrangements in some of the country’s biggest Pentecostal churches under fresh scrutiny, with renewed attention on statements by prominent clerics, including Pastor William Kumuyi, Pastor Enoch Adeboye and Bishop David Oyedepo.

The controversy, which has pitted the church’s Senior Pastor, Jimmy Odukoya, against its Board of Trustees, has raised questions about how religious organisations choose successors.

While the Fountain of Life crisis has resulted in a court battle, conversations surrounding succession have extended to other major denominations, including the Deeper Christian Life Ministry, the Redeemed Christian Church of God and Living Faith Church Worldwide.

The dispute over the leadership of the Fountain of Life, founded by the late Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, intensified following the emergence of a video in which the cleric identified another pastor as his preferred successor.

The development prompted some Nigerians to revisit previous comments by leaders of other prominent ministries and question whether adequate arrangements exist to ensure smooth leadership transitions.

Kumuyi’s succession comments resurface

The General Superintendent of the Deeper Christian Life Ministry, Pastor William Kumuyi, came under renewed public attention following the circulation of a video in which he addressed questions about who would succeed him.

A strategy and transformational consultant, Ayo-Bankole Akintujoye, and an enterprise resource planning consultant, Oluwatobi Bamidele, were among those who drew attention to the cleric’s comments.

The two shared a video in which Kumuyi discussed succession.

Akintujoye wrote, “Pastor Kumuyi is an incredibly blessed man in his generation, but absolutely no leader at over 80 years old should be this afraid and rattled about a discussion on succession. Something is wrong somewhere.”

Bamidele, linking the remarks to the crisis at the Fountain of Life, wrote, “This Fountain of Life Church successor saga made me remember when Pastor Kumuyi said this about his successor.”

In the video, reportedly recorded during a Bible study programme in August 2025, Kumuyi maintained that the choice of his successor rested with God.

He was responding to comments attributed to a younger preacher in the church who stressed that there could be no leadership without a successor.

Kumuyi said he considered the repeated emphasis on succession inappropriate while he was still leading the ministry.

“The brother who taught the other Tuesday kept saying there is no leadership without a successor. He said it twice. I felt that was too much, more so since your father is still here. God will give a successor at His own time,” he said.

The cleric also warned church members against attempting to influence or dictate his decisions concerning leadership.

“You are not going to fight your shepherd, your pilot. I reject any member of the church, whether you are a worker, choir member, or security person, who tries to control me.

“Don’t try to kill my conviction. It will only make me resist you so that when you get to the other side, you won’t say I did not tell you. When the time comes, God will choose a man after His own heart. Don’t try to drive me away, even though I know you cannot,” he added.

Kumuyi later revealed the rotational leadership structure put in place at various levels of the church.

When Saturday PUNCH contacted a senior pastor in the church on the matter, he said, “We don’t discuss succession plans in Deeper Life when our father, Pastor Kumuyi, is still alive.”

Adeboye awaits divine direction

Similarly, previous remarks by the General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God, Pastor Enoch Adeboye, attracted attention in the wider conversation about succession.

Adeboye had stated in August 2018 that God had not revealed the identity of the person who would succeed him as the church’s General Overseer.

According to Tribune, the cleric made the disclosure during the church’s ministers’ conference at the Redemption Camp in Ogun State.

He addressed speculation over possible successors, including suggestions that he could hand over to Bishop David Oyedepo, Pastor Joe Olaiya or one of his spiritual sons.

“Some even said I would hand over to Bishop David Oyedepo, some said to Pastor Joe Olaiya because the two are very close to me and they do minister during our major events such as the conventions, Holy Ghost congresses and yet another quarter said one of my sons is the one succeeding me,” Adeboye said.

He explained that he was waiting for God to reveal the identity of his successor before making any announcement.

“So, let me say it loud and clear again that God has not told me who my successor is. What God had told me several years ago was that He would tell me who my successor would be at least five years before I would be called home, and as at this time, He had not told me anything as regards that, which means He is not ready to call me home in the next five years,” he added.

Oyedepo outlines succession procedure

The Presiding Bishop of Living Faith Church Worldwide, also known as Winners’ Chapel, Bishop David Oyedepo, publicly described a structured succession procedure for the ministry.

In a sermon reported by Daily Times Nigeria in June 2020, Oyedepo explained that the process was contained in The Mandate, a document he described as the church’s governing guide.

According to him, the presiding bishop is required to submit the names of three potential successors to the Council of Priests upon attaining the age of 70.

The nominees are subsequently examined by the church’s secretariat to determine whether they possess the required qualifications for the position.

Oyedepo explained that where none of the nominees meets the stipulated requirements, the list would be returned to the presiding bishop for another submission.

If the second set of nominees also fails to meet the requirements, the Council of Priests would take responsibility for the process, while the board would ratify the final decision.

He said the arrangement was designed to prevent uncertainty or confusion whenever a leader leaves office.

“It is a process, not that somebody dies and then we don’t know what to do,” Oyedepo said.

The bishop also cautioned against treating churches as personal or family property, warning that such an approach could undermine the purpose of the ministry.

Nigerians raise concerns

Beyond the comments by the religious leaders, the Fountain of Life controversy prompted some Nigerians to express concerns about the future leadership of churches established by prominent founders.

An X user, Adegbola John, described the crisis as a wake-up call for church founders and warned that similar challenges could emerge where succession arrangements were not clearly established.

John said he had repeatedly raised questions about what could happen at Deeper Life after Kumuyi’s departure.

He argued that many African political and religious leaders failed to plan adequately for leadership transitions because they were reluctant to relinquish power or publicly groom and endorse successors.

Drawing a comparison with the reluctance of some Africans to write wills before death, he said church founders often avoided succession conversations until circumstances made them unavoidable.

Another X user, Victor Abu, linked the Fountain of Life dispute to concerns about churches being treated as family businesses.

According to him, similar conflicts could emerge in other prominent Nigerian churches after their founders’ departure if leadership arrangements were not properly addressed.

Godswill Ikouwem, who directed his comments at Jimmy Odukoya, urged the pastor to allow the church’s leadership to be determined through spiritual guidance rather than family ties.

“Just because your dad, God bless his soul, was the founder doesn’t mean you must lead the church. Allow the Holy Spirit to take charge, and if the Holy Spirit is leading the church along a new leadership, just submit yourself to that leading. Don’t fight what God is doing in the now,” he wrote.

Another commentator, Oluwatosin Bukun-Joseph, expressed concern about the consequences of the dispute, warning that no church gathering could withstand the kind of turmoil he believed was developing within the congregation.

Fountain of Life crisis deepens

Meanwhile, the succession controversy at the Fountain of Life Church has continued to generate tension, with members expressing concerns over the future of the ministry amid the legal confrontation between Jimmy Odukoya and the Board of Trustees.

Saturday PUNCH gathered that the leadership disagreement, which dates back to 2023, had resulted in the departure of prominent figures. Pastor Kunle Areogun resigned his membership of the Board of Trustees, while Pastor Akin Osinbajo, a longstanding member, reportedly left the congregation.

The disagreement over the succession arrangement made by the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, escalated after Jimmy’s remarriage and the introduction of his new wife, Motunrayo.

A longstanding member of the church, who spoke with Saturday PUNCH on condition of anonymity, said the disagreement had divided the congregation and placed the reputation of the church at risk.

“Those of us who have been members for years are not happy. We love Jimmy, but doesn’t he need to step away from that position? I think he does. Some of these issues were probably part of the reasons Pastor Akin Osinbajo left the church recently; he was also a longstanding member,” she said.

Another member, who previously served in an official capacity in the church, said the prolonged controversy had left many worshippers disappointed.

The member expressed concern that more people could eventually leave the congregation if the disagreement remained unresolved.

“In fact, right now, I’m considering changing church because the drama is becoming too much in TFOLC,” the source said.

However, another insider familiar with the church’s activities disclosed that some stakeholders had begun efforts to secure Areogun’s return to help stabilise the ministry.

“Things are really getting messy and they (stakeholders) are trying to see how they will get Areogun back to the church for stability,” the insider said.

The source also claimed that the Overseer of the Citadel Global Community Church, formerly known as The Latter Rain Assembly, Pastor Tunde Bakare, had intervened in the matter.

According to the insider, Bakare was likely to make a public statement on the dispute in the coming days.

Jimmy, trustees battle in court

The confrontation between Jimmy and the trustees took a legal turn after a Lagos State High Court issued an order restraining him from parading himself as the senior pastor and spiritual head of the church.

Justice O. O. Adewunmi-Oshin granted the order on Wednesday in a suit instituted by the Incorporated Trustees of the church.

The trustees approached the court on the grounds that Jimmy had ceased to occupy the position following the appointment of a successor by his late father in accordance with the church’s constitution.

However, an insider disclosed that Jimmy was making moves to challenge the order, insisting that the Lagos State High Court lacked jurisdiction over the matter because the church was registered under Part F of the Companies and Allied Matters Act, 2020.

“The order will not stand; Jimmy will file an appeal. The Lagos State High Court does not have jurisdiction over the matter. I’m sure the order will be vacated,” the source said.

Following the court order, reports circulated that the church premises had been sealed.

But Jimmy, in a Facebook post on Friday, dismissed the reports and urged members to disregard them, maintaining that the premises remained open.

Although the church’s thanksgiving service scheduled for Sunday was postponed because of the crisis, the embattled pastor encouraged members to attend the regular Sunday service.

Saturday PUNCH also learnt that the disagreement extended to control of the church’s social media accounts.

Sources disclosed that the Board of Trustees attempted to take over the accounts but encountered resistance from Jimmy’s aides, who allegedly refused to release the login details.

Succession video, Jimmy’s response

The dispute in the church escalated on Tuesday when the Board of Trustees announced that it had withdrawn its recognition of Jimmy as the church’s senior pastor.

The trustees cited a recorded video instruction by the late Taiwo Odukoya, in which he reportedly identified Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor.

The video, said to have been recorded in December 2021, reportedly showed the late founder expressing his preference for Areogun to lead the ministry in the event of his death or incapacity.

Jimmy was assigned administrative and youth church responsibilities under the arrangement described in the recording.

According to the trustees, their examination of the video and relevant provisions of the church’s constitution established that the late founder had exercised his authority to determine succession and communicated his intentions before his death.

Consequently, the board declared that Jimmy was no longer recognised as the church’s senior pastor with immediate effect.

The trustees subsequently appointed Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as the interim spiritual and administrative leader pending further consultations and the establishment of a substantive leadership structure.

However, Jimmy presented a different account of the circumstances surrounding the video during an emergency workers’ meeting held on Wednesday.

Saturday PUNCH gathered that the pastor acknowledged the existence of the recording but explained that it was made when his father was preparing to undergo surgery in the United States.

According to Church Times, Jimmy explained that the late founder had been uncertain about surviving the operation when the recording was made.

He also disclosed that Taiwo’s elder brother, John Odukoya, was aware of the video.

Jimmy further claimed that after the operation was successful, his father instructed him to delete the recording because it was no longer valid.

He admitted that retaining the video had been a grave mistake on his part.

Commenting on the disagreement with the trustees, Jimmy said the board, which he identified as comprising Pastors Areogun and Rotimi, had presented seven demands to him.

He disclosed that he accepted four of the demands but rejected the remaining three.

Jimmy also claimed that Areogun resigned his membership of the Board of Trustees after being asked to do so.

According to him, Areogun had previously declined an offer from the late Taiwo Odukoya to succeed him.

The embattled pastor maintained that he would not step down as chairman of the Board of Trustees.

Instead, he said he had asked the trustees, including his elder sister, to resign from the board.

A source who attended the emergency workers’ meeting told Saturday PUNCH that some church workers had demanded to know the identities of the trustees.

According to the source, several workers expressed support for Jimmy during the meeting, while resentment towards the trustees appeared to be growing among some members.

“At the meeting, the church members were cheering Jimmy up; they were supporting him. You could see a growing resentment against the board members. They asked him to name the BoTs, but he was reluctant. He eventually mentioned Gbenga Onabanjo and Areogun, though he said the latter had resigned,” the insider said.

Jimmy absent from pulpit

During a visit to the church’s premises in the Ilupeju area of Lagos for its Thursday Showers service, Saturday PUNCH observed a sizeable turnout of worshippers despite the ongoing leadership dispute.

However, Jimmy was not seen presiding over the service, although he shared a livestream link to the programme on his social media platforms.

Another pastor, identified as Dipo Adeda-Osinloye, conducted the service.

Addressing the congregation, Adeda-Osinloye urged members to remain steadfast in their faith and expressed confidence that the church would survive the challenges confronting it.

He also warned that attempts to destabilise the church would fail.

“Nobody can bring this church down, no weapon of the enemy formed against us shall prosper, and when they gather because they do not gather for the sake of the Lord, they will scatter,” the pastor added.

When Saturday PUNCH approached a member of the church’s staff to request an interview with Jimmy, the official confirmed that he had been present but left shortly after the service.

Asked why Jimmy did not preside over the programme, the official explained that Thursday Showers was primarily a praise and worship session, unlike the church’s regular Sunday service.

The official added that the pastor would ordinarily remain available for counselling and meetings with members after the programme.

Members split over crisis

Despite concerns expressed by some members, others maintained that the controversy would not destabilise the church.

One member, who spoke with Saturday PUNCH on condition of anonymity, dismissed suggestions that Jimmy had been removed as the senior pastor.

According to the worshipper, Jimmy continued to perform his responsibilities while the church remained operational.

“Our senior pastor has not been removed. He is performing his functions as he should, and the church is moving forward,” the member said.

The source also questioned the legitimacy of the statement announcing Jimmy’s removal.

“It was not the church that issued the purported statement removing Pastor Jimmy. What is happening is just a minor distraction. The church will come out stronger,” the member added.

Meanwhile, Jimmy’s wife, Motunrayo, had earlier posted a series of cryptic messages on her Instagram story, which Saturday PUNCH sighted.

“Stay grounded. Stay kind. But don’t shrink just to make someone else more comfortable,” one of the messages read.

Another stated, “When someone is insecure, your confidence can feel like a threat. Not because you’re showing off, but because your growth confronts what they are avoiding.”

She also wrote, “Your happiness can look like arrogance to someone who is unhappy. Your success can look like bragging to someone who feels behind.”

The post Mega churches face succession heat appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

While the 78 schoolchildren abducted in Borno State have spent six months in their kidnappers’ den, 547 worshippers abducted in Niger State have
content:
No fewer than 640 Nigerians, including schoolchildren and worshippers, have remained in captivity months after their abduction, Saturday PUNCH can report.

While the 78 schoolchildren abducted in Borno State have spent six months in their kidnappers’ den, 547 worshippers abducted in Niger State have remained in captivity for three months. Also, 15 schoolgirls abducted in the Rafi area of Niger State on October 31 have yet to regain their freedom.

The Borno schoolchildren were abducted in two separate attacks in Askira-Uba Local Government Area on May 15 and June 29, 2026.

On May 15, armed insurgents stormed Mussa Primary and Junior Secondary School, abducting 42 pupils, including reportedly two-year-old children.

Six weeks later, bandits attacked Government Day Secondary School, Lassa, while students were sitting the National Examinations Council examinations, abducting 36 students and killing two teachers.

On August 21, terrorists suspected to be members of the Lakurawa group attacked Kpenya Mosque during Friday Juma’at prayers after raiding surrounding communities, including Gidan-Zana, Sabon Gida and Masaka, in the Dekara district of Borgu Local Government Area.

Initially, the police and local officials put the number of abductees at between 60 and 80. However, community leaders later compiled and published a list of 547 abducted men, women and children, according to Al Jazeera.

The terrorists later released footage showing hundreds of captives seated in a forested area, prompting President Bola Tinubu to order the victims’ rescue.

Similarly, bandits abducted 15 Islamiyya school pupils in Tungan-Bako village, Pandogari District, Rafi Local Government Area of Niger State, on October 31, 2026.

All the victims have remained in captivity, leaving their families in prolonged anguish and uncertainty over their whereabouts and possible release.

No contact with our abducted children

Speaking with Saturday PUNCH, a parent of one of the 78 abducted Borno schoolchildren, Bura Emmanuel, said there had been no contact with either the abductors or the children.

He said neither the government nor the abductors had provided any information about the children’s whereabouts.

Bura added that the parents had continued to wait, hoping the government would rescue their children.

“As of today, we have not heard anything. Not even the government is giving us any information. We just keep our hopes hanging, believing that our children will be rescued someday by the government,” he said.

Meanwhile, the Principal of Government Day Secondary School, Lassa, John Medugu, told Saturday PUNCH that the incident had affected the concentration of other students in the classroom.

“There is still trauma. The level of concentration of our students is very low because of fear,” he said.

Medugu, however, said he was unaware whether the state government had established contact with the students’ abductors.

“For now, I’m not aware of any form of communication at all. We are praying that the government will act fast to help in rescuing the abducted students and teachers,” the principal said.

Why rescue is delayed

However, the Managing Director of Beacon Security and Intelligence Limited, Kabir Adamu, attributed the delay in rescuing the victims to difficult terrain and the porosity of the country’s borders.

He also cited political considerations, explaining that an operation could result in casualties among the victims, a risk the government might be unwilling to take, especially with elections approaching.

Speaking with Saturday PUNCH on Friday, Adamu said, “The first challenge is the environment; it is a difficult one, with difficult terrain. There are ungoverned spaces where these criminal elements occupy. When they abduct, they take their victims to these ungoverned spaces. An example is the Mandara Mountains, and then you also have the Sambisa Forest, but in this instance, I think we are dealing with the Mandara Mountains.

“The second challenge is the porosity of the border. Army Joint Task Force is divided into four sectors; Niger was manning sector four, but because of the breakdown of the relationship between Nigeria and Niger, that border zone is open. So, it allows for cross-border movement of these criminal elements in and out of Nigeria and from other countries into Nigeria.

“When you add this to the first factor, you will now see that it is very difficult and maybe impossible for Nigerian security forces to completely dominate that space and prevent the criminal activities that are ongoing in those spaces.”

Adamu said the security forces might lack the specialised equipment needed to carry out the operation with minimal collateral damage.

“The third factor is the deficit of the special equipment needed by the security forces to carry out these types of operations with very little collateral damage. There are huge psychological and emotional attachments associated with dealing with children and women, and when you are carrying out such an operation, especially with deficit of equipment, and then the likelihood of collateral damage is high.

“So, no political leader will want to approve such an operation, especially around the election period,” he added.

The security expert also blamed the lack of sustained media and public attention on the abductions for the delay.

“The failure of the media and the public to sustain a campaign that would keep the issue on the front burner of national and international discourse has reduced the political incentive for the government to prioritise operations to secure their release.

“That is not to say the government is not interested in the release of the children, but that desire to do it speedily is not there,” he said.

However, a retired Brigadier General, Bashir Adewinbi, said the delay in rescuing the victims might be politically motivated, accusing some people of seeking to embarrass the government.

He alleged that the kidnappings had been turned into a campaign instrument against President Bola Tinubu’s administration.

Adewinbi said, “The delay in rescuing the victims may not be unconnected with politics. Kidnapping and terrorism are politically motivated, just to discredit the government.

“The people behind these kidnappings want to use it as a campaign tool. We don’t love ourselves in this country. These people can go to any length, and they can play games with anything, including human lives to achieve their aims.

“The security agencies are up to the task. They are doing their best, but they are doing it against so many odds. When you want to rescue, you must plan the operation with the aim of minimising casualties. But the terrorists will devise means to make sure that the rescue will be so difficult without casualties. It requires intelligence gathering, planning, and, if possible, negotiations.”

Efforts to get an update on the rescue operation from the spokesman for the Niger State Police Command, Wasiu Abiodun, were unsuccessful, as calls to his phone did not go through.

He had also yet to respond to a message sent to him as of the time of filing this report.

Similarly, several calls to the state Commissioner of Information and Orientation, Obed Nuhu, were unanswered, while he had yet to reply to a message sent to him.

The Borno State Commissioner of Information and Internal Security, Usman Tar, also did not answer calls or respond to a message seeking an update on the government’s efforts to rescue the children on Friday.

The state Police Public Relations Officer, Nahum Daso, also did not answer calls or respond to messages sent to his phone.

Efforts to get a comment from the Director of Media Operations at the Defence Headquarters, Maj. Gen. Michael Onoja, were also unsuccessful, as he neither answered calls nor responded to a message sent to him.

The post Forgotten: Families agonise over pupils, worshippers still in captivity appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Four mourners die in Bayelsa boat accident
description:
Four mourners, including two children, have died after a passenger boat conveying people to a burial ceremony capsized in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.
Twenty-four other passengers were rescued from the incident, which occurred at about 11am on Friday near the river junct
content:
Four mourners, including two children, have died after a passenger boat conveying people to a burial ceremony capsized in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.

Twenty-four other passengers were rescued from the incident, which occurred at about 11am on Friday near the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities.

The Bayelsa State Police Command said the boat was travelling from Ayama to Ukubie community when it reportedly developed a mechanical fault and capsized.

The Police Public Relations Officer, Musa Mohammed, disclosed this in a statement on Friday.

He said the bodies had been deposited at the mortuary of the Federal Medical Centre, Yenagoa.

According to him, 19 rescued passengers were taken to Ayama Clinic, while five others who sustained varying degrees of injuries were conveyed to Family Care Hospital, Yenagoa.

Other survivors had returned to their respective communities.

The police said the boat operator, identified simply as Omovie, fled the scene, while the boat manager, identified as MV Bina, was taken into custody for investigation.

Mohammed said preliminary investigations indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways.

He added that some passengers reportedly urged the operator to steer towards the riverbank after the fault developed, but he allegedly refused and continued sailing before the boat capsized.

“The circumstances surrounding the incident are being investigated,” the police spokesman said.

The Commissioner of Police, Ajao Adewale, was said to have directed the State Marine Police Section to join the search and rescue operation immediately after the incident.

Saturday PUNCH gathered that the Divisional Police Officer, Oporoma Division, was also coordinating efforts with local divers and other emergency responders to account for everyone on board.

The police said investigations would establish the circumstances surrounding the accident and determine possible liabilities.

Earlier accounts from the affected communities had suggested that more than 30 people were feared dead, with others reportedly missing.

 However, the figures could not be independently verified, while the police confirmed four deaths and 24 rescued passengers in its Friday statement.

A community source, who reportedly witnessed the loading of the boat at the jetty, said some passengers had expressed concerns about the number of people on board.

The source claimed that some passengers suggested stopping at Oweikorogha to reduce the number of people travelling because of alleged overcrowding, but the proposal was ignored.

The former Chairman of the Maritime Union Workers in Bayelsa State, Ipigansi Ogoniba, also confirmed receiving information about the incident but said he was yet to establish the actual number of casualties.

The Commissioner of Police expressed condolences to Governor Douye Diri and the families of the deceased, while wishing the injured survivors a speedy recovery.

The command warned boat operators against violating maritime safety regulations, particularly overloading and failure to provide life jackets.

It also urged passengers to ensure that life jackets were available and properly worn before embarking on water journeys.

title: FG begins $70m passport production centre in Abuja
description:
The Federal Government on Friday announced plans to produce six million passport booklets annually from a new $70m manufacturing facility in Abuja.
The plan also includes ambitions to scale output to 10 million booklets per year and position Nigeria as a passport supplier to other African countries
content:
The Federal Government on Friday announced plans to produce six million passport booklets annually from a new $70m manufacturing facility in Abuja.

The plan also includes ambitions to scale output to 10 million booklets per year and position Nigeria as a passport supplier to other African countries currently dependent on Europe and the Americas.

The Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, disclosed this at the groundbreaking ceremony for the National Passport Booklet Production Centre at the Nigeria Immigration Service headquarters in Abuja.

“The requirement of Nigeria is roughly between 1.8 to 2 million passports a year, but by May 2027, we will have the capacity for six million passports a year production, which we are going to scale to 10 million booklets a year,” Tunji-Ojo said.

He said the facility, developed with technology partner Iris Smart Technologies, was designed to meet ECOWAS travel document standards and could make Nigeria a continental exporter.

He said: “What we and our partners Aresmart are doing is to build a passport that will be able to service ECOWAS and even be able to export to other countries. All other countries in Africa, they are buying from Europe, from the Americas. But we believe Nigeria, being the giant of Africa, that is a market. Nigeria must lead.”

Tunji-Ojo said President Bola Tinubu would commission the facility in May 2027, adding that the project, sitting on 1.1 hectares of land and to be run entirely off-grid on solar power, was financed without government funds.

He said: “This project is about $70m without a dime from government.”

He noted that the initiative formed part of a broader plan since 2023 to domesticate the entire passport value chain, citing the completion of a centralised passport personalisation centre at NIS headquarters in September 2025 and an 8.3-petabyte AI-driven data centre.

He said Nigeria would become the first country in West Africa to manufacture e-passports domestically, joining South Africa, Ethiopia and Algeria as the only African countries with in-country passport manufacturing capacity, and the first to produce biometric e-passports.

He said: “In the whole of Africa, in the whole of West Africa, what we are doing today, by the time we deliver it in May, Nigeria will be the first country in West Africa to do it.”

He added that the original contract with Iris Smart Technologies dated to 2003, but President Tinubu inserted a “backward integration” condition requiring local manufacturing before the contract could continue.

Speaking at the event, the senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, who performed the groundbreaking, said the ceremony marked a shift from procurement to production, arguing that historic reliance on foreign passport printing reflected a failure of imagination rather than capacity.

The Senate Committee on Interior chairman said: “For the first time in Nigerian history, under the leadership of President Bola Tinubu, we are going to start to manufacture passport of the finest quality, right here in Abuja.”

Oshiomhole, a former president of the Nigeria Labour Congress and former governor of Edo State, said the project embodied his lifelong argument that production must be domestic, contrasting it with what he called the procurement mentality of earlier administrations.

“Rather than going to sign agreement in a foreign country to be producing Nigeria passport, today we will manufacture it here,” he said.

He also cited earlier passport reforms as evidence of change, noting that members of his family had benefited directly.

“Nigerians who used to cry and do all sorts of lamentations about the dysfunctionality of the Nigerian state, that they can’t even have their passport renewed, and therefore their plan to visit family at home was aborted by reason of the fact that the Nigerian passport has expired.

“We saw there whether they were in America, they were in Europe or they were in Asia. Within months of the honourable minister’s assumption of office, these issues were dealt with and dealt with satisfactorily, including my own grandchildren.

“They tell me, ‘Grandpa, now I have Nigeria passport.’ So these are not in the advert; they are real stories that speak to what is changing the real meaning of renewed hope,” he said.

The former governor praised Tunji-Ojo as one of the most consequential ministers in the Tinubu cabinet.

He also commended NIS Comptroller-General Kemi Nandap for her leadership, saying she had shown that women could break new ground in security agencies without affirmative allocation.

Breaking new ground in passport production

In her remarks, the NIS Comptroller-General, Kemi Nandap, said the ceremony marked not just the foundation of a building but the foundation of a more sovereign passport system.

She acknowledged years of booklet shortages that left students missing admissions and parents unable to travel, saying the lesson was that “a nation cannot run a dependable passport system without control over the critical parts of its own supply chain.”

She outlined three expected benefits of the manufacturing centre: enhancing security through national oversight of sensitive travel documents; strengthening supply chain resilience and local expertise in secure document production; and improving service delivery to Nigerians.

“History will not judge us by the promises we make at this groundbreaking ceremony, but by the institutions we build, the standards we uphold and the results we deliver,” she said.

Meanwhile, Acting Assistant Comptroller-General of Customs Doris Okonkwo, who represented Comptroller-General Bashir Adeniyi, congratulated the Immigration Service and said the project aligned with the government’s broader institutional modernisation agenda.

“This landmark project represents a strategic leap forward in strengthening Nigerian domestic passport production capacity, enhancing document security, and ensuring sustainable, self-reliant passport administration,” she said, adding that ending external reliance in passport booklet production would conserve foreign exchange and strengthen national security.

Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission Director-General Dr Jobson Ewanife cited the facility alongside recent concession signings and commissionings as evidence of momentum in the administration’s infrastructure drive.

He said: “What we are witnessing today is a product of the bold reform of His Excellency Mr. President.”

Ewanife added that the ICRC would monitor compliance with contractual obligations to ensure delivery to specification.

The post FG begins $70m passport production centre in Abuja appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: How I went from N3,000 roles to global recognition–Omowunmi Dada
description: Award-winning Nollywood actress Omowunmi Dada has carved out a niche as one of the industry’s most compelling talents, with an impressive body of work spanning stage, television, and film. A graduate of Creative Arts from the University of Lagos, Dada has earned recognition for her versatility, capt
content:
Award-winning Nollywood actress Omowunmi Dada has carved out a niche as one of the industry’s most compelling talents, with an impressive body of work spanning stage, television, and film. A graduate of Creative Arts from the University of Lagos, Dada has earned recognition for her versatility, captivating performances and commitment to telling meaningful African stories.

In a recent Appearance on Morayo Show, the actress reflects on her journey into Nollywood, the challenges of finding her feet in the industry, her international recognition and the importance of reclaiming the African woman’s narrative.

Enjoy!

How did your journey into Nollywood begin?

I studied Creative Arts at the University of Lagos, and right from my undergraduate days, I knew exactly what I wanted to do. I deliberately chose Creative Arts because I wanted to pursue acting. It wasn’t something I stumbled into or was persuaded to do. I knew what I wanted, so I went ahead and studied it.

My first stage production was Mori, in which I played Ario. One of the beautiful things about studying Creative Arts back then was that professionals were regularly invited to watch students’ performances.

During one of those productions, a man named Williams Eko saw me and expressed interest in having me feature in his play. He told me he would like me to be part of his production. That was how I moved from the academic environment into professional theatre.

While I was still in school, I began participating in professional theatre productions. Sometimes, I would tell my classmates that a particular class or test might not hold, and then head out for auditions. When I graduated in 2010, I was the best graduating student in my class. I subsequently worked with a media company for about a year, but I knew deep down that I wanted to return to acting.

How challenging was it finding your way back into the industry?

It wasn’t easy. Sometimes, auditions scheduled for 9 a.m. would find you at the venue as early as 7 a.m., only for you to discover that you were number 200 on the list. Even after waiting for hours, you might be told, “We’ll get back to you,” and never hear from them again. But I always reminded myself to give my best at every opportunity because you never know who is watching. I also believe in being audacious. If I want to meet someone or be part of a project, I ask. The worst they can say is ‘No’.

During the BlackBerry era, I reached out to a sound engineer, Valentine, whose production pictures I saw on his status. I told him I liked what he was working on and wanted to be involved. He initially said there was no substantial female role, except a walk-on character of a rape victim. I insisted he speak to the producer.

I eventually contacted the producer and asked several questions about the character because I wanted to understand her background and personality. My curiosity paid off. What was initially a one-scene role grew to three scenes, then six. The producer even developed a backstory for the character, and I eventually became the youngest sister of the film’s villain.

At the end of filming, I was offered just N3,000 because there was no budget for the role. I accepted because I was more interested in showcasing my talent and gaining the experience.

The short Nigerian film The Wages (2013) was written, produced, and directed by Walter Taylaur (under Waltbanger101 Productions. It went on to win Best Short Film at the AMVCA that year. His next call was for Married to the Game, an EbonyLife-commissioned series, where he offered me the lead female role. That was another breakthrough for me.

You recently starred at the 2026 BFI London Film Festival, where your work received international recognition. How would you describe the experience?

It was a beautiful and humbling experience. The film that took me to the BFI London Film Festival was The Secret Lives of Baba Segi’s Wives, adapted from the bestselling novel, in which I played the lead female role.

As a Theatre Arts student and film enthusiast, I had always dreamed of seeing my work screened at prestigious festivals such as Cannes, Sundance, Toronto and BFI. At BFI, we had two sold-out screenings, with audiences from diverse cultural backgrounds embracing a Yoruba-language film. Seeing people who were unfamiliar with our language and culture connect with the story was truly remarkable. Conversations about my character made the experience even more fulfilling.

At Film Africa, you spoke about the African woman reclaiming her narrative. Why is this important to you?

I grew up in a generation where women were rarely celebrated for their many achievements. Take Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti, for instance. People often remember her as the first woman to drive a car, overlooking her many other remarkable contributions. We must reclaim these stories and show the world how extraordinary African women are.

As an actor, my tool for social change is the stories I tell, the films I make and the characters I portray. I want the world to see African women as strong, vibrant and resilient. We break barriers, open doors for others and keep pushing until we achieve positive results.

Your position is particularly inspiring because many women are struggling with their own challenges and sometimes feel that the odds are against them. How important is it for women to share their stories and encourage one another?

I think it is very important. Every woman has a story, and many have had to overcome different challenges to get to where they are today. Sometimes, all someone needs is to hear another woman’s experience and realise that she, too, can overcome her circumstances. When women share their journeys, they inspire others to keep going.

We must continue to tell our stories, celebrate our achievements and encourage one another. Women are doing so much, and we need to ensure that their contributions are seen, heard and appreciated.

You were also part of the team behind the Guinness World Records attempt involving The Black Book. How did that historic initiative come about?

Nora approached me with a story about women, and I immediately bought into the idea. Interestingly, women’s stories often find their way to me, so I was excited to be part of it.

As we developed the film, we began exploring a distribution strategy beyond the usual cinema, YouTube or streaming platforms. We wanted something bigger, more iconic and globally significant.

Nora suggested a public screening. Inspired by Femi Adebayo’s community cinema initiative, we decided to take it a step further. When we discovered that the Guinness World Records record for simultaneous film viewing stood at 43,000 people, we thought, why not aim for 50,000?

It was ambitious, and we had no idea how we would pull it off, but I believed it was possible. We created awareness, and Nigerians showed up. We initially targeted 50,000 people, but 63,000 turned up, with 51,000 watching the film from beginning to end.

It was historic. Seeing thousands of Nigerians gather not for football or a concert, but to watch a film was remarkable. It was a massive win for Nollywood and Nigeria.

Beyond that project, what else are you working on, and what should your fans expect from you in the near future?

There are so many beautiful projects in the pipeline, but I don’t want to reveal too much just yet. We have an animation project coming out next year, alongside several exciting films from my production company, Signet Ring Studios. I’m also involved in projects as an actress. That’s all I can share for now.

You seem to be glowing from within. What is responsible for that?

It is the Lord’s doing, and it is marvellous in my sight. Let me tell you something: is life perfect? No, it isn’t. But when you know whose child you are, you are always encouraged because, no matter what happens, you know your Father has got you.

Honestly, that is what it is for me. God has got me. I am Jesus’ baby; I have the joy of the Lord, and that is it.

I am also very passionate about education, and I want to use this opportunity to inspire women. Never give up, and dream as big as you possibly can. That space you think you cannot dominate is one you can actually conquer. Everything you need is already within you.

When I started, the opportunities available to women in the industry were largely limited to acting, costume design and makeup. Today, we have female cinematographers, directors and producers. Women drive some of the biggest box-office successes, and women are also making remarkable strides in film distribution and other areas of the industry.

It wasn’t always like this. Women had to be audacious, speak their truth, and show the world what they were capable of.

Most importantly, whatever you do, strive for excellence. Let people say, “I have worked with this woman, and she is fantastic at her job.”

Be kind to everyone, and never forget that God loves you

The post How I went from N3,000 roles to global recognition–Omowunmi Dada appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Build systems, not just businesses, Wale Tinubu tells SMEs
description:
Oando Plc Group Chief Executive Wale Tinubu has urged Nigerian entrepreneurs to build businesses around strong systems, financial discipline and sound governance, warning that ambition alone cannot sustain growth or global competitiveness.
Tinubu said businesses must adopt structured operations, kee
content:
Oando Plc Group Chief Executive Wale Tinubu has urged Nigerian entrepreneurs to build businesses around strong systems, financial discipline and sound governance, warning that ambition alone cannot sustain growth or global competitiveness.

Tinubu said businesses must adopt structured operations, keep proper financial records and embrace long-term planning to grow from small enterprises into medium-sized, large and globally competitive organisations.

He spoke while delivering the keynote address at GROW Nigerian 2026, the National MSME Conference organised by the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria at the Ecobank Pan African Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos, according to a statement sent to Saturday PUNCH on Friday.

Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, SMEDAN Director-General Charles Odii, German Deputy Consul-General Katharina Ziegler and other business leaders, policymakers and development partners attended the conference.

Highlighting the role of small and medium-sized enterprises in the economy, Tinubu said they accounted for 96.9 per cent of businesses, 88 per cent of employment and 46 per cent of Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product.

He said the priority should be strengthening their capacity to scale beyond small businesses through deliberate decisions, consistency and disciplined execution.

“Nigerian giants are not built overnight. They are built through a series of bold decisions, executed with long-term commitment and persistence,” he said.

Drawing on Oando’s three-decade journey, Tinubu recounted how the company began with modest family contributions in a converted garage before moving into diesel trading and expanding into petroleum marketing, gas distribution and upstream oil and gas operations.

He linked the company’s growth to calculated risk-taking, reinvestment, reliability and quality, stressing that business opportunities require deliberate strategies and sustained execution.

On building businesses that attract investment, the Oando chief executive stressed the need for proper financial records, documented processes and audited accounts, saying they are vital for credibility and growth.

“One of the most important steps for an SME is to begin documenting its operations and processes, and to maintain audited financial statements. These are essential foundations for building a structured business and preparing it for growth,” he said.

Tinubu also named working capital management as vital to business survival, urging entrepreneurs to track their cash positions, receivables, liabilities and inventory.

He advised business owners seeking funding to explore different sources, including commercial banks, development finance institutions, fintechs, suppliers and joint venture partnerships.

“There is no single source of capital that is more important than another. Every source of financing, wherever it comes from, has a role to play in supporting business growth,” he said.

He also pointed to ambition, capability, competitiveness and endurance as key traits for building lasting enterprises, urging entrepreneurs to invest in their staff, pass on institutional knowledge and build systems that can be replicated as their businesses grow.

“The principles required to build a successful SME remain the same as those required to run a large enterprise. As you scale, the critical difference is your ability to replicate your systems, processes, and organisational DNA,” he added.

On operating conditions, Tinubu acknowledged government efforts to improve infrastructure but said businesses must prepare to handle policy shifts, delayed approvals and other operational hurdles.

He called for better electricity supply, logistics, port operations and ease of doing business, saying such reforms are crucial to helping small businesses grow into larger firms.

“These are areas that require commitment rather than significant financial resources. SMEs depend on improvements in logistics, port operations, and the ease of doing business to scale from small to medium-sized and ultimately large enterprises,” he said.

Looking back at Oando’s growth from a small trading firm into an integrated energy group, Tinubu said the company still relies on the entrepreneurial values that shaped its start.

“Even though we are a large conglomerate today, we still think like an SME. The principles that shaped our beginnings continue to inform how we build and grow the business,” he said.

The post Build systems, not just businesses, Wale Tinubu tells SMEs appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Fans divided over Brymo’s latest attack on Davido, Burna Boy, Wizkid
description:
Brymo’s latest remarks about Afrobeats stars Davido, Burna Boy and Wizkid have sparked debate among music fans, with some backing his views while others have faulted him for criticising the trio.
In a recent interview with Afromixx, Brymo, whose real name is Olawale Olofooro, questioned the criteria
content:
Brymo’s latest remarks about Afrobeats stars Davido, Burna Boy and Wizkid have sparked debate among music fans, with some backing his views while others have faulted him for criticising the trio.

In a recent interview with Afromixx, Brymo, whose real name is Olawale Olofooro, questioned the criteria for describing the trio as Afrobeats’ so-called ‘Big Three’.

He argued that commercial success and mainstream recognition should not give any artiste the impression that they own Afrobeats.

Brymo also questioned whether their recognition was based on songwriting, vocal performances, live performances or their willingness to speak up for themselves.

“My real problem with those so-called Big Three before is that they’ve forgotten that it’s called the mainstream.

“If you want to nail yourself down somewhere and say, ‘I’m the king, I’m the…’ Then go and create something. First of all, Afrobeats is not yours. Yours is a derivative of the real thing. So what’s Big Three? Big Three as what? As songwriting? As vocal performances? As live performances? As speaking up for yourself?” he queried.

The singer also appeared to take a swipe at one of the artistes over his dependence on family members, questioning his maturity and independence, although he did not mention any name.

“You get a woman pregnant, your father is on live TV defending you. You can’t be the biggest artiste in Nigeria. Your mum carries you around the whole world, you say you’re the biggest artiste in Nigeria? You’re not a man.”

Brymo, however, offered a different perspective on Wizkid, suggesting that the singer’s decision to live abroad was influenced by challenges in Nigeria.

“I know Wizkid for sure, and I know why he’s here out here. If things were really working out in Nigeria, he probably would be back home full-time, just like me.”

His comments have since generated mixed reactions among music lovers. While some supported his views, arguing that musical talent should be measured by songwriting, vocal ability and stage performances rather than popularity, others accused him of attacking successful artistes instead of concentrating on his career.

Supporting Brymo, an Instagram user wrote, “I don’t care about their lifestyles or life choices. That is their kettle of fish. Each one will pay for his actions or inactions. But when it comes to meaningful music, vocal power, lyrical expertise, and relatable cultural content, Brymo beats all the so-called Big 3 hands down! I listen to all four, but Olawale Olofooro is in a class of his own.”

Another commenter, @kingmaikudimufasa, described Brymo as underrated, while @emry_yx said, “Brymo is really good.”

However, another user, @VOsimhen144, defended the trio, highlighting their contributions to the industry and support for others.

According to the commenter, Burna Boy involves his family in his business, Davido is known for supporting others, while Wizkid also helps people despite keeping his activities private.

“The Big 3 are making us proud. Brymo should stop crying,” the user wrote.

Some fans also suggested that Brymo was using the controversy to promote his upcoming show in London.

An Instagram user, @adebayo_fejiro, wrote, “Wahala promo your show and leave Davido abeg. This format is old.”

Similarly, @zeyzey8747 asked, “But why is Wizkid’s name always on your lips?”

Another commenter, @Cyzzy2000, questioned why Brymo frequently criticised other artistes, urging him to concentrate on his music.

“I believe he is talented and should just focus on his craft. He makes beautiful soul music that people appreciate, has a niche to himself. Why all this unnecessary controversy and bad-mouthing?” the user queried.

Similarly, @Negroid001 suggested that the singer was seeking relevance.

The latest development comes months after Brymo urged established Afrobeats stars to make way for younger artistes, accusing some of them of dominating the industry through the ‘Big Three’ and ‘Big Four’ labels.

This is not the first time Brymo has attracted attention for his comments about prominent Nigerian artistes.

Two years ago, in an interview with Chude Jideonwo on #WithChude, he claimed that popular Nigerian artistes who believed they had made it in the industry were mistaken, arguing that most did not own their masters or music catalogues.

He also boasted that no Nigerian artiste, dead or alive, could command two hours of listening without interruption in the way he could.
