title: The Gambia Has 1.14 Million Registered Voters Ahead Of December 5 Election
description: Gambiaj.com – (BANJUL, THE GAMBIA) – The Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) has confirmed that The Gambia has 1,146,474 registered voters ahead of the December 5 presidential election, providing the most detailed breakdown yet of the electorate across the country’s 53 constituencies and individu
content:
Gambiaj.com – (BANJUL, THE GAMBIA) – The Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) has confirmed that The Gambia has 1,146,474 registered voters ahead of the December 5 presidential election, providing the most detailed breakdown yet of the electorate across the country’s 53 constituencies and individual polling locations.

In two documents released on Friday, November 20, the electoral body published the final 2026 registered-voter figures, including the number of polling centers and polling stations in each constituency.

The figures show that the electorate is spread across 730 polling centers, comprising 1,773 polling stations in the country’s seven administrative areas.

The release provides a more detailed picture of the geographical distribution of voters as political parties intensify their campaigns ahead of the presidential election.

Brikama And Kanifing Account For 56.5% Of Voters

The constituency-level figures reveal significant differences in the size of electorates across the country, with Kombo South emerging as the largest constituency, with 77,307 registered voters.

Other constituencies with large electorates include Busumbala, with 65,339 voters; Sanneh Mentereng, with 63,456; Old Yundum, with 62,494; and Serekunda West, with 51,522.

Brikama North has 45,807 registered voters, while Brikama South has 44,722 and Latrikunda Sabiji has 42,274.

At the administrative-area level, Brikama has the largest concentration of voters, with 437,020, representing approximately 38.1% of the national register.

Kanifing follows with 210,437 registered voters, accounting for about 18.4%.

Combined, the two administrative areas account for approximately 56.5% of all registered voters in The Gambia, highlighting the concentration of the electorate in the country’s most densely populated urban and peri-urban areas.

However, the distribution of registered voters does not necessarily indicate how constituencies or administrative areas will vote on election day.

Women Outnumber Men Across All Seven Administrative Areas

The IEC’s published registration statistics also provide a gender breakdown of registered voters across the seven administrative areas.

The figures show that women account for a higher proportion of registered voters than men in every administrative area.

Banjul has 52.53% female voters against 47.47% male voters, while Basse records the highest proportion of women, at 60.72%, compared with 39.28% men.

In Brikama, women represent 55.74% of registered voters, against 44.26% men. Janjanbureh records 57.67% women and 42.33% men.

Kanifing has 54.19% female voters and 45.81% male voters, while Kerewan records 56.54% women and 43.46% men.

In Mansakonko, women account for 54.05% of registered voters, compared with 45.95% men.

The figures suggest a consistent female majority across the country’s seven administrative areas. However, the IEC has not provided corresponding gender breakdowns for individual constituencies.

Age Breakdown Remains Unavailable

Despite the additional information, an important gap remains in understanding the demographic composition of the electorate, particularly the age distribution of registered voters.

The two documents released on Friday, as well as the IEC’s registration statistics, do not provide figures showing how many registered voters are aged between 18 and 25, those between 26 and 35, or the proportion of the electorate below 35.

The absence of age-related information also makes it difficult to establish how young voters are distributed across the country’s seven administrative areas and 53 constituencies.

It also leaves unanswered the question of how many registered voters will be voting for the first time.

Importantly, registration during the 2026 supplementary voter registration exercise does not necessarily mean that an individual is a first-time eligible voter, as some people may have qualified to vote in previous elections but only registered recently.

The publication of aggregated age statistics would therefore help provide a more comprehensive understanding of the electorate while protecting individual voter information.

Polling Centre Figures Provide Further Electoral Insight

The second IEC document provides a breakdown of registered voters at individual polling locations and polling streams, offering additional information about the distribution of voters within constituencies.

The data could help assess the number of polling streams serving different communities, variations in the size of polling-station electorates and the administrative demands facing election officials.

It could also help identify polling locations where large numbers of registered voters may require particular attention to queue management and election-day arrangements.

The IEC figures distinguish between 730 polling centers and 1,773 polling stations, two administrative categories that should not be used interchangeably.

The published figures represent the allocation of registered voters and do not indicate how many people will actually turn out to vote on December 5.

The release marks an important addition to publicly available electoral information ahead of the presidential election, allowing a more detailed examination of the country’s electoral geography.

However, the absence of age statistics and national totals for registered men and women means that a complete demographic picture of the electorate remains unavailable.

title: Expert seeks energy reforms
description:
A Lagos-based entrepreneur and public analyst, Ayotunde Bally, has called for reforms in access to credit, energy supply, and market operations to reduce the cost of doing business and ease poverty in Nigeria.
 Bally, in a statement made available to Saturday PUNCH on Friday, said affordable loans,
content:
A Lagos-based entrepreneur and public analyst, Ayotunde Bally, has called for reforms in access to credit, energy supply, and market operations to reduce the cost of doing business and ease poverty in Nigeria.

 Bally, in a statement made available to Saturday PUNCH on Friday, said affordable loans, lower energy costs, and an efficient market system were critical to improving household purchasing power, supporting businesses, and creating jobs.

“Nigeria’s greatest economic challenge is not simply that we are not producing enough wealth; it is because our economic system is failing to create a sustainable relationship between production, employment, income, and consumption,” he said.

Citing an International Monetary Fund estimate, Bally said about 63 per cent of Nigeria’s population was living in poverty in 2025, based on the national poverty line.

He said the figure reflected the difficulties many households faced in meeting basic needs, adding that the N70,000 statutory minimum wage highlighted the financial pressure on low-income earners.

Bally identified access to affordable credit as the first area requiring urgent reform, arguing that high borrowing costs and stringent collateral requirements limited the ability of individuals and businesses to expand.

“The first priority must be to fundamentally reform how individuals and businesses access credit in Nigeria,” he said. “Capital is the lifeblood of enterprise.”

He argued that financial institutions should place greater emphasis on borrowers’ repayment capacity and credit histories rather than relying heavily on conventional collateral requirements.

According to him, existing identification and financial systems, including the National Identification Number, Bank Verification Number, and licensed credit bureaus, could support a broader framework for assessing borrowers.

He urged the Federal Government to develop a national credit-enabling framework that would allow lenders to use verifiable economic information in evaluating loan applications.

On energy, the analyst called for electricity-sector reforms, greater competition, investment in domestic gas infrastructure, and improvements in fuel distribution to lower the cost of powering businesses.

He said reducing energy expenses would free up resources for production, innovation, employment, and business expansion.

Bally also called for a more efficient and competitive market system, urging the government to improve access to customers, strengthen distribution networks, simplify business regulations, and remove barriers that increase production and transportation costs.

He said economic performance should be assessed not only through gross domestic product growth and infrastructure spending, but also by the extent to which Nigerians could afford essential goods and services.

According to him, government policies should focus on improving real incomes, lowering the cost of basic commodities, and raising living standards, while directing scarce public resources towards projects with measurable economic and social benefits.

On implementation, Bally proposed a coordinated programme involving the Federal Ministry of Finance, the Central Bank of Nigeria, relevant energy institutions, development finance organisations, state governments, and the private sector.

He said the programme should prioritise affordable financing for small and medium-sized enterprises, lower energy costs, stronger credit facilities, and the removal of regulatory bottlenecks.

Bally proposed that clear targets be set within six months, with implementation beginning within the first year and measurable outcomes assessed over the following two to three years.

He added that regular public progress reports would be necessary to ensure accountability.

title: Imo police hunt man for killing girlfriend
description:
The Imo State Police Command has begun a manhunt for a man identified as Emmanuel Bright over the alleged murder of his girlfriend, known simply as Mmesoma, a hotel worker found dead in her room in Owerri.
The deceased, who reportedly worked and lived at Executive Garden Hotel on Okigwe Road, Owerri
content:
The Imo State Police Command has begun a manhunt for a man identified as Emmanuel Bright over the alleged murder of his girlfriend, known simply as Mmesoma, a hotel worker found dead in her room in Owerri.

The deceased, who reportedly worked and lived at Executive Garden Hotel on Okigwe Road, Owerri, was discovered dead on November 15 after Bright allegedly visited her at the facility.

Police said efforts were ongoing to find the suspect, with intelligence indicating he might still be in Owerri, the state capital.

The command’s spokesperson, Henry Okoye, confirmed the manhunt in an interview with Saturday PUNCH on Friday.

“The police are tracking him, and intelligence is showing that he is still in Owerri,” Okoye said.

Accounts attributed to hotel staff and eyewitnesses on Facebook stated that Mmesoma introduced Bright to the gateman on duty when he arrived at the hotel on Sunday, and he was allowed to follow her to her room.

The suspect allegedly left the premises a few hours later, and his departure reportedly raised no immediate suspicion until the deceased was found dead in her room.

Hotel staff reportedly raised the alarm after discovering the body, prompting contact with the police.

The circumstances surrounding the alleged killing, including the motive and whether there was an argument between the couple before the incident, remained unclear as of Wednesday.

There were also conflicting accounts on social media about the victim’s age and place of origin.

While some posts described her as a 17-year-old from Ihitte Uboma Local Government Area of Imo State, others identified her as being from Umuezeala in Ngor Okpala Local Government Area.

Saturday PUNCH could not independently verify her age, surname or place of origin, and police had not released her full identity as of the time of filing this report.

Questions have also been raised about whether closed-circuit television cameras were available at the hotel.

While a video circulating online claimed the facility had no CCTV cameras, another social media post alleged that footage of the incident existed, though neither claim could be independently verified.

Efforts by Saturday PUNCH to get the hotel management’s response to the allegations—including questions about its security arrangements and Mmesoma’s employment—were unsuccessful, as messages sent to the hotel’s official Facebook page had not received a response as of press time.

title: People sometimes forget celebrities are human too – Chuks Joseph
description:
Actor Chuks Joseph has urged fans to understand that celebrities are human beings with personal struggles and private lives, noting that being in the public eye does not mean they should always be available or accessible.
In an interview with Saturday Beats, Joseph said one of the unrealistic expect
content:
Actor Chuks Joseph has urged fans to understand that celebrities are human beings with personal struggles and private lives, noting that being in the public eye does not mean they should always be available or accessible.

In an interview with Saturday Beats, Joseph said one of the unrealistic expectations fans had of celebrities was the assumption that public figures were always happy, financially comfortable and willing to attend to people’s demands.

“People sometimes forget that celebrities are human beings too. They have private lives, personal struggles, bad days, and moments when one simply wants to be themselves without public attention.”

“There’s also this expectation that because someone is in the public eye, every aspect of their life should be open for public consumption. Also, there is the phenomenon that everyone on TV or in the public eye has some money stacked up somewhere and will readily send it to people because they are public figures,” he said.

Speaking about the financial realities of his acting career, Joseph admitted that although acting had been fulfilling, it was not always as lucrative as people imagined.

“Honestly, it has been both fulfilling and challenging. Acting allows me to express myself, tell stories, and connect with people in ways that are difficult to explain. Financially, I think it is an industry that requires a lot of patience, consistency, and the right opportunities. It is not always as glamorous as people imagine, but the fulfilment I get from doing what I love makes the journey worthwhile. I am still growing, and I believe the best is yet to come,” he said.

title: United Nigeria Airlines expands domestic flight routes
description:
United Nigeria Airlines is expanding its domestic network with the intreoduction of scheduled flights connecting Jos, the Plateau State capital, to Lagos, Kano and Owerri effective 24 November, 2026.
According to a statement from the airline, the new routes will provide Plateau residents with three
content:
United Nigeria Airlines is expanding its domestic network with the intreoduction of scheduled flights connecting Jos, the Plateau State capital, to Lagos, Kano and Owerri effective 24 November, 2026.

According to a statement from the airline, the new routes will provide Plateau residents with three additional air connections, while opening up opportunities for business, tourism, trade and social exchange.

The Lagos–Jos–Lagos route will operate four times weekly on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays, while Jos–Kano–Jos and Jos–Owerri–Jos will each run twice weekly.

Flights on the Jos–Kano route will operate on Tuesdays and Fridays, while the Jos–Owerri service is scheduled for Wednesdays and Sundays.

The airline added that owing to the temporary closure of Owerri Airport, the inaugural Jos–Owerri flight will take off on 29 November, five days after the commencement of the other services.

The expansion follows a Memorandum of Understanding signed on 9 November, between the Plateau State Government and United Nigeria Airlines at the office of the Commissioner for Transport, Jatau Gyang, in Jos.

UNA stressed that the agreement will see the airline introduce scheduled services on the Jos–Kano and Jos–Owerri routes, two connections the state had not previously enjoyed.

Speaking after the signing, Gyang described the partnership as a strategic step towards positioning Plateau as a leading destination for investment, tourism, commerce and economic development.

He commended the airline’s management for its confidence in the state’s economic vision, stressing that improved air connectivity would strengthen Plateau’s relationship with other parts of the country.

According to him, the Jos–Owerri route will provide easier access to the South-East and South-South, creating fresh opportunities for trade, investment, tourism and social interaction.

He said: “This route will make it easier for our people and those in neighbouring states to access the South-East and South-South. Beyond passenger movement, it will promote trade, investment, tourism and stronger social connections between our regions.”

On the Jos–Kano connection, the commissioner said the route would deepen Plateau’s economic ties with the North-West, a region he described as home to some of Nigeria’s major commercial and industrial centres.

He added that the connection would open up opportunities for business partnerships, commercial activities and greater economic cooperation.

Responding on behalf of the airline, its Managing Director, Mazi Osita Okonkwo, described the agreement as particularly significant because of its potential to connect three major geopolitical zones;  the South-East, South-West and North-Central.

He said Plateau remained a special and strategic destination for the airline, assuring residents that the company would deliver services consistent with its reputation.

Okonkwo said: “This is a strategic partnership, particularly because it creates a stronger connection between the South-East, South-West and North-Central regions. Plateau is a special state, and we are committed to delivering the standard of service for which United Nigeria Airlines is known.”

The post United Nigeria Airlines expands domestic flight routes appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Osimhen, Onyeka return to club training after injuries
description:
Super Eagles stars Victor Osimhen and Frank Onyeka have returned to training with their respective clubs as both players work their way back from injury setbacks.
Osimhen has resumed rehabilitation work in Istanbul following knee surgery, while Onyeka trained with Coventry City ahead of Saturday’s P
content:
Super Eagles stars Victor Osimhen and Frank Onyeka have returned to training with their respective clubs as both players work their way back from injury setbacks.

Osimhen has resumed rehabilitation work in Istanbul following knee surgery, while Onyeka trained with Coventry City ahead of Saturday’s Premier League clash against Crystal Palace.

Their return offers a boost to their clubs after both missed Nigeria’s November 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying double-header against Tanzania.

The 27-year-old Osimhen underwent an arthroscopic procedure on November 7 at Maslak Acıbadem Hospital in Istanbul to remove a loose fragment in his left knee, picked up in Galatasaray’s 2-0 Champions League victory over VfB Stuttgart on November 3.

While conflicting reports have emerged over whether he is back on the grass or doing individual work away from teammates, Turkish journalist Ali Naci Küçük noted his on-pitch return remains uncertain ahead of the Samsunspor league fixture and the November 24 Champions League tie against Aston Villa, making the November 30 Istanbul derby against Beşiktaş a more realistic target.

Meanwhile, Coventry City manager Frank Lampard confirmed on Thursday that Onyeka took part in training, though he stopped short of guaranteeing his availability for Saturday’s match at the Coventry Building Society Arena.

“Onyeka trained today, so we’ll see,” Lampard said.

Onyeka has missed Coventry’s last two league matches against Sunderland and Everton, as well as the recent 3-1 defeat at Everton before the international break, having made eight appearances across all competitions since making his move permanent from Brentford.

title: Funke Akindele’s resilience inspires me – TheRealFunke
description:
Content creator Tolani Arowolo, popularly known as TheRealFunke, has said Nollywood actress Funke Akindele’s resilience and consistency inspire her, particularly as they share the same first name.
Speaking in an interview with Saturday Beats, she described the actress as someone whose ability to rem
content:
Content creator Tolani Arowolo, popularly known as TheRealFunke, has said Nollywood actress Funke Akindele’s resilience and consistency inspire her, particularly as they share the same first name.

Speaking in an interview with Saturday Beats, she described the actress as someone whose ability to remain relevant in the entertainment industry deserves to be studied.

“I admire Funke Akindele so much. Her resilience needs to be studied. It inspires me. The way she keeps reinventing her brand and staying consistent inspires me to do more,” TheRealFunke said.

Addressing the relationship between social media influence and business revenue, she noted that having millions of followers did not automatically translate into millions of customers.

“Having millions of followers is not the same as having millions of customers. People can follow you because they enjoy your videos, your personality, or the things you do online. That does not automatically mean they need what you are selling. For me, the important thing is trust. People need to believe in you before they are comfortable spending their money on something you recommend or a product you sell. You cannot just wake up one day and start advertising everything because you have a large audience. People will notice when you are only interested in selling to them,” she said.

On balancing content creation with monetisation, TheRealFunke said she was careful not to turn every post into an advertisement.

“I try not to make everything about selling. People follow me for different reasons. Some enjoy my videos, some like my livestreams, some connect with my personality, and others know me through my business. I have to respect that.

“Being TheRealFunke is not just about having followers. It is also about the relationship I have built with the people who support me,” the content creator added.

title: LeBron, Sixers headline NBA weekend action
description:
LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers headline the NBA weekend when they host Tyler Herro and the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday.
The game starts at 7pm WAT and will be shown live on SportyTV. The Sixers lead the Eastern Conference with 13 wins and three losses, making them one of the league’s early
content:
LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers headline the NBA weekend when they host Tyler Herro and the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday.

The game starts at 7pm WAT and will be shown live on SportyTV. The Sixers lead the Eastern Conference with 13 wins and three losses, making them one of the league’s early pace-setters.

The 41-year-old James is playing his 24th NBA season, extending his own record for the most seasons in league history. The 22-time All-Star lines up alongside Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe, giving Philadelphia a strong blend of experience and star power.

Philadelphia are monitoring the availability of Jaylen Brown, who missed the last game against Orlando with a hamstring injury. Head coach Nick Nurse said Brown would be evaluated once the team returns from its road trip. Senegal’s Tacko Fall will hope for more court time after recording three blocks in 10 minutes against the Magic on Wednesday.

Saturday’s game is a rematch of Philadelphia’s 127-116 win over Milwaukee on October 24. Embiid had a triple-double of 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists in that game, while Brown scored 27 points. James missed that contest. Milwaukee, led by 2025 All-Star Herro, who is averaging 19.4 points per game, will be looking to end a 12-game losing streak.

On Sunday, the Detroit Pistons visit the Atlanta Hawks at 9:30pm WAT, live on ESPN. Detroit are 10-4 and have won four of their last five games, led by Cade Cunningham, who averages 25.8 points and 7.8 assists. Atlanta are 9-6 and arrive on a two-game winning streak, which includes a 117-112 away win over Oklahoma City. Nickeil Alexander-Walker leads the Hawks in scoring with 21.2 points per game, while Onyeka Okongwu, in his seventh season with the club, averages 15 points and 8.2 rebounds. Both teams also play in the Emirates NBA Cup tonight.

The post LeBron, Sixers headline NBA weekend action appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 36.3 million Nigerians face acute food crisis – Report
description:
About 36.3 million Nigerians face crisis or worse levels of food insecurity, according to a report by the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa.
The document, Food Security Monitor (Edition 74, October 2026), obtained by Saturday PUNCH on Friday, puts the figure at 36,289,939 people, the highest
content:
About 36.3 million Nigerians face crisis or worse levels of food insecurity, according to a report by the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa.

The document, Food Security Monitor (Edition 74, October 2026), obtained by Saturday PUNCH on Friday, puts the figure at 36,289,939 people, the highest number of any country in Africa covered in the report.

The report, supported by the United Kingdom government’s Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office, tracks food security and staple prices across East, Southern and West Africa.

According to the report, Nigerians facing food crisis represent 16.65 per cent of the analysed population, classified in Phase 3 or higher of the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification/Cadre Harmonisé scale.

The report said: “Nigeria continues to carry by far the largest absolute burden, with 36.29 million people facing Crisis or worse food insecurity, followed by South Sudan with 7.83 million.”

A Saturday PUNCH analysis of the report showed that Nigerians facing food crisis were about 7.1 million more than the combined 29.18 million recorded for the 13 other countries listed in the survey.

Nigeria accounted for about 55 per cent of the 65.5 million people counted across the table.

After South Sudan, the ranking included Uganda (2.94 million), Malawi (2.61 million), Kenya (2.55 million), Zimbabwe (2.50 million) and Niger (2.42 million).

The rest were Mozambique (1.84 million), Mali (1.56 million), Ghana (1.50 million), Côte d’Ivoire (1.33 million), Zambia (1.25 million), Tanzania (507,498) and Togo (332,147).

South Sudan had the highest incidence at 55 per cent, followed by Mozambique at 22 per cent and Nigeria at 16.65 per cent.

Uganda and Zimbabwe recorded 16 per cent each, while Kenya and Malawi had 14 per cent each.

In West Africa, Niger recorded nine per cent, Mali six per cent, Côte d’Ivoire and Togo five per cent each, and Ghana four per cent.

The report said the figures emphasised a difference between absolute and proportional burdens, with Nigeria carrying the largest number and South Sudan the highest incidence.

On the outlook, the report said Nigeria’s food security situation would remain “highly uneven” through January 2027.

It said Emergency (Phase 4) conditions would persist in inaccessible parts of Borno State, while conflict-affected areas of the North-West and North-Central would stay in Crisis as insecurity disrupted farming, harvesting, livelihoods and market access.

In other parts of the North-East, the report said harvests should bring temporary improvement from Crisis to Stressed (Phase 2), although many displaced and land-constrained households would remain in Crisis.

It added that high fuel and transport costs, and staple prices “well above the five-year average,” meant harvest gains were unlikely to substantially improve food access for poor and conflict-affected households.

The report also showed wide differences in food prices.

It noted that milled rice fell 9.1 per cent in October to N452.87 per kilogramme, and was 46.7 per cent lower than a year earlier, which the report attributed to good market supply.

White maize fell 5.8 per cent in the month to N333.10 per kg and was 12.7 per cent lower year-on-year.

However, white sorghum was 47 per cent higher than a year earlier at N486.23 per kg, while millet was up 23.3 per cent at N503.25 per kg.

Across West Africa, the report said food insecurity was expected to worsen into the 2027 lean season, particularly in conflict-affected parts of the central Sahel and northern Nigeria.

It named Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger and north-eastern Nigeria as the most severe cases, with humanitarian needs expected to peak between March and May 2027.

It said crop conditions were rated poor in conflict-affected parts of northern Nigeria, and that a very strong El Niño was compounding shocks across the continent.

The report follows similar data from the Cadre Harmonisé update for the June–August 2026 lean season, published on July 2.

The analysis said Nigeria accounted for nearly 66 per cent of the 54.8 million people in Crisis or worse across the Sahel, West Africa and Cameroon, followed by Chad (3.2 million), Cameroon (2.8 million) and Niger (2.4 million).

It also put about two million Nigerians in Emergency, with roughly 10,000 people in Catastrophe (Phase 5) in Borno State.

The earlier Cadre Harmonisé, presented in Abuja in late 2025, had put 27.2 million Nigerians in Crisis or worse between October and December 2025 and projected 34.7 million for June to August 2026.

The Food and Agriculture Organisation said the 36.3 million estimates represented a deterioration from 2025, when more than 30.6 million people were in Phase 3 or above.

The FAO also said over 3.7 million people were displaced nationwide as of early August 2026, about two-thirds of them in Borno.

The World Food Programme said in July that more than 17 million people in nine conflict-affected northern states were experiencing crisis, emergency or catastrophic hunger, and that it could support only 740,000 of 6.2 million food-insecure people in three North-East states, down from 1.3 million at the height of the 2025 lean season.

According to the National Bureau of Statistics, food inflation stood at 19.13 per cent year-on-year in October 2026, even as the food price index fell 0.75 per cent from September.

The post 36.3 million Nigerians face acute food crisis – Report appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Why listening matters in marriage
description:
Everyone wants to feel heard and understood, but in marriage this need carries special significance. Each spouse desires the reassurance that their thoughts, feelings, concerns, and aspirations are valued by the person with whom they share life’s journey.
Many marital difficulties arise not from a l
content:
Everyone wants to feel heard and understood, but in marriage this need carries special significance. Each spouse desires the reassurance that their thoughts, feelings, concerns, and aspirations are valued by the person with whom they share life’s journey.

Many marital difficulties arise not from a lack of love, but because of a lack of understanding. Great marriages flourish when both spouses know their voice matters.

By listening with patience, empathy, and genuine interest, couples cultivate a deeper emotional bond, creating a relationship where love is not only expressed but also truly understood.

To be fully present

Active listening is one of the clearest ways to communicate love and respect in marriage. It involves more than hearing what your spouse says; it means being fully present, listening with empathy and interest, and prioritising understanding before offering your opinion.

In the midst of life’s busy schedules, daily responsibilities, and endless distractions, couples can sometimes find themselves talking more and listening less. When your spouse stops feeling heard, he/she can begin to feel emotionally disconnected, even within the closeness of the marriage.

This is why active listening is such a powerful relationship habit. It helps couples stay connected, nurtures trust, and creates a safe space where both people feel seen and understood.

When your spouse confides in you, they are often seeking more than a conversation; they are seeking connection. They are inviting you into their world, sharing their joys, frustrations, fears, and hopes. In those moments, the greatest need is often not advice or solutions, but the comfort of knowing that the person they love is truly listening.

Creates emotional safety

Active listening is an expression of love. Spouses feel heard; they feel valued. When they feel understood, they feel loved. This is why active listening is such an essential part of a healthy marriage.

It creates emotional safety, builds trust, and encourages honest, meaningful connection. By taking the time to listen attentively and respond with empathy, you will be cultivating a relationship where you and your spouse feel supported, appreciated, and deeply connected.

Communicate with care

Strong marriages are built through countless everyday moments when spouses intentionally choose connection over distance.

Simple acts such as maintaining eye contact when your partner is speaking, listening without interrupting when they share a concern, acknowledging their feelings before offering advice, and giving them your full attention when they open their heart all communicate care and respect.

Though these habits may seem small, they send a powerful message of love, creating a deeper sense of understanding, trust, and emotional closeness that words alone cannot achieve.

Develop emotional validation

Many conflicts escalate because people feel the need to prove who is right. Yet in many situations, what a spouse truly desires is not correction but understanding. One of the most loving things you can do is to learn to validate each other’s feelings.

Validation does not mean agreeing with everything your spouse says; it simply means acknowledging their feelings and recognising that their experience is real to them.

Active listening is a powerful way of showing your spouse that their feelings matter. By listening with empathy and understanding, couples create emotional validation that builds trust, strengthens their bond, and contributes to a healthier, more satisfying marriage.

The post Why listening matters in marriage appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

description:

The artificial intelligence race just produced the biggest stock market debut in history.



Anthropic, the United States artificial intelligence
content:
–Claude maker raises $81.3bn in world’s largest IPO, overtakes SpaceX as investors rush for AI, despite $104bn loss
By Vera Anyagafu, with agency report

The artificial intelligence race just produced the biggest stock market debut in history.

Anthropic, the United States artificial intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot, on Wednesday priced its initial public offering at $83 per share, above its expected range of $70 to $78, valuing the company at about $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

The company sold 980 million shares, up from the 825 million originally planned, raising $81.34 billion and surpassing SpaceX’s $75 billion record to become the world’s largest IPO at initial pricing.

The offering is expected to close on Friday, November 20, subject to customary closing conditions, as demand became extraordinary.

One early investor said the original sale was oversubscribed by roughly ten times.

And reports put demand at close to $500 billion worth of shares, far above the offering size.

That demand brushed aside market jitters over AI stocks, the recent slide on Wall Street, and even the spy scandal that toppled Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang.

Anthropic is now the first major United States company specialising purely in AI development to go public.

It is also the only public US company focused entirely on AI, and it did it in just five years.

Founded in 2021 by seven former OpenAI employees, including siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, Anthropic did not exist until about five years ago.

In May, it raised $65 billion in its last private round, at a valuation of $965 billion. Six months later, it is worth $1.5 trillion.

That puts it roughly on par with Tesla, more valuable than Walmart and Samsung, and more than the combined market capitalisation of India’s top 10 companies, according to Indian banker Uday Kotak.

“Anthropic, an AI company known for Claude, listed at a valuation of $1.5 trillion. It did not exist till ∼5 years ago. This is more than the combined market cap of the top 10 Indian companies. Are we undervalued, or do we need to catch up in the new world? Or both?” Kotak wrote on X on Thursday.

But the total money raised is even bigger than the IPO alone.

Seven technology companies, AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron Technology, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC Partners, have separately agreed to invest a combined $26 billion in Anthropic through a private placement at the IPO price.

Together, the IPO and the private placement are set to raise a record $107 billion, above the $86 billion SpaceX raised in its listing.

The company is going public to finance its long-term commitments, estimated at around $900 billion, related to computing power and data centres. About $70 billion of computing bills are due in the next year alone.

Anthropic reported revenue of $33.2 billion in the first nine months of 2026, about 13 times the same stretch a year earlier. In the third quarter alone, revenue was about $17 billion, more than 12 times the year-earlier level, it reveals.

But for the same nine months, it reported a net loss of $104 billion, according to its IPO document, underscoring the financial demands of AI development.

Anthropic has already reported its first quarterly operating profit, but its prospectus warns that its computing commitments could strain its finances if growth slows.

At $83, Anthropic is valued at about 43 times trailing sales on a fully diluted basis, less than half SpaceX’s multiple at its June debut, but still leaving little room for error.

Earlier estimates had put Anthropic’s valuation as high as $2 trillion, but they fell as AI stocks slid on Wall Street in recent weeks. The tech-heavy Nasdaq has lost 12 per cent since its peak in October.

Its biggest rival, OpenAI, maker of ChatGPT, is expected to go public next year.

For now, though, the message from Wall Street is clear, investors still believe the AI boom is real, and they are willing to pay a record price to be part of it.

Korea presents roadmap for Nigeria’s Unified, citizen-centred digital government
By Vera Anyagafu

South Korea, through the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA), has handed over the final report of Nigeria’s e-Government Master Plan 2.0 (e-GMP 2.0) to the Federal Government for formal adoption.

The handover took place on Thursday in Abuja at the closing ceremony of KOICA’s project, ‘Building Foundations Towards Digital Governance in Nigeria (2022–2026)’, where KOICA Country Director, Mr Kim Eunsub, , presented the report to the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy.

The e-GMP 2.0 provides the strategic and implementation framework for Nigeria’s digital government transformation from 2026 to 2030. It was developed from May 2022 through consultations with relevant Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs), with technical expertise from South Korea. The plan consolidates the 25 initiatives under the first e-Government Master Plan into 10 strategic initiatives organised under five pillars: Integrated Digital Infrastructure, Sustainable Digital Government, Citizen-Centric Digital Service Transformation, Digital Governance and Institutional Reform, and Innovation, Partnerships and Digital Capacity. Presenting the document, Prof. Hung Kook Park, Project Manager from Sangmyung University in South Korea, outlined its development process, key achievements, critical success factors and roadmap for implementation.

The government says the plan is meant to move Nigeria from disconnected digital platforms towards an integrated, citizen-centred system. It is expected to provide common direction and standards for digital transformation across government, and to transform how institutions operate, exchange information and deliver services. A key outcome of the partnership is the soft launch of Nigeria’s first single-window Government Service Portal (GSP) in July 2026. KOICA’s 2022 to 2026 project also delivered 572 NIN registration devices and trained 2,276 Nigerian officials, according to reports on the handover. The Federal Government acknowledged at the ceremony that Nigeria is yet to fully realise its digital governance ambition, making formal adoption and implementation of the 2.0 plan the next critical step.

title: Glamour, style at The Sun Awards 2026
description: It was glamour, style, panache at the red carpet of The Sun Awards, which took place on Friday November 13 at the Eko Convention Centre, Eko Hotel, Victoria Island, Lagos. Guests –  men, women, young and old – came in their best to witness this yearly sought-after awards ceremony. Classic, timeless
content:
It was glamour, style, panache at the red carpet of The Sun Awards, which took place on Friday November 13 at the Eko Convention Centre, Eko Hotel, Victoria Island, Lagos. Guests –  men, women, young and old – came in their best to witness this yearly sought-after awards ceremony. Classic, timeless black in dresses and accessories, made their way into the event.  Long gowns, native attire, bright colours, all added to the beauty of the event.

Black dress

A lot of guests especially women, were seen in different styles of black. The black dress is a timeless wardrobe essential. Its neutral colour makes it a perfect canvas to pair with statement accessories, bold colours, soft pastels or metallic finishes. It flatters every body shape, suits every skin tone, and transitions seamlessly from daytime events to after-hour affairs.

Maxi dress

A maxi dress is one of the most versatile, elegant, and feminine pieces you can have in your wardrobe.  It transforms completely depending on how you style them to suit any occasion.  For a special event such as The Sun Awards, a long black dress never fails. Simply add a different touch with red, burgundy, or midnight blue tights, and complete the look with a cocktail shoe; A look that exudes sophistication, without the need for excessive sparkle or embellishment. 

Suited men

Some of the men came in suits. As it is with the suit, it adorns one’s personality and makes the person more noticeable. A suit is an outfit that makes any man’s confidence soar. The men in suit at the occasion looked well put together.

Native and traditional attires (Agbada/kaftan/Senator, Isi agu)

The male guests who wore traditional attires to the prestigious awards ceremony, also stood out.  Agbada, kaftan, senator styles, Isi agu, and so on, Nigerian native styles have always been about grandeur and dignity. Nigerian menswear continues to stand out, driven by bold new trends, rich textures, and colours that make a lasting impression.

Red cap

The Igbo red cap is a sacred symbol of authority, honour, and tradition in Igbo land, though it has increasingly crossed over into contemporary African fashion. The red cap is crafted for ceremonies, weddings, and cultural events.

Though it is worn by Igbo high chiefs, which symbolises authority; it also represents the entire institution of leadership, authority, and power in Igbo culture. Today, it has a become a fashion for men who want to make a style statement at big events.

title: FG seeks investors in creative economy
description:
The Federal Government is seeking greater private sector investment in Nigeria’s creative economy through cultural heritage, arts and tourism ahead of the 2026 National Festival of Arts and Culture in Enugu State.
The Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, Hannatu Musawa, said t
content:
The Federal Government is seeking greater private sector investment in Nigeria’s creative economy through cultural heritage, arts and tourism ahead of the 2026 National Festival of Arts and Culture in Enugu State.

The Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, Hannatu Musawa, said the festival would offer opportunities for investors, financial institutions, artisans and industry stakeholders to explore business prospects in the sector.

Musawa stated this on Friday in a statement by her Special Adviser on Media, Nneka Anibeze, ahead of the festival scheduled to hold from November 21 to 28.

She said the event would feature a colloquium with investors, financial institutions and creative industry stakeholders to examine financing options and unlock the economic potential of Nigeria’s cultural heritage.

According to her, the festival will also give artisans and entrepreneurs a platform to showcase products, connect with buyers and grow their businesses through a dedicated culture market.

The minister described Nigeria’s cultural diversity as a potential driver of national unity, social cohesion and economic growth, stressing the need to harness cultural resources for development.

She said the festival remained a key platform for bringing Nigerians together, promoting cultural heritage and projecting a positive image of the country.

Musawa explained that the decision to postpone the 2025 edition was taken to show solidarity with families and communities hit by insecurity across the country.

“Last year, we made the difficult but necessary decision to postpone NAFEST out of empathy, respect and solidarity with families and communities affected by insecurity across the country. It was more respectful and responsible to pause than to celebrate at a time when many citizens were grieving,” she said.

The minister said the festival would return with fresh opportunities to strengthen national integration and highlight Nigeria’s creative potential.

Themed “Connected Culture,” the eight-day festival is organised by the National Council for Arts and Culture in collaboration with the Enugu State Government.

Events will hold at the Enugu International Conference Centre and Michael Okpara Square, featuring cultural parades, traditional performances, exhibitions, indigenous games and competitions, including Jollof Wars, Dance-Off Naija and Sing-Off Naija.

The programme will also include creative industry workshops aimed at building capacity and expanding opportunities in the sector.

The Director-General of the NCAC, Obi Asika, urged Nigerians to take part, describing culture as a vital tool for national identity and economic opportunity.

“Our culture is our identity, our strength and our opportunity. NAFEST Enugu 2026 invites every Nigerian to celebrate who we are, showcase our creativity, and unlock the immense potential of our cultural heritage,” he said.

The National Festival of Arts and Culture is an annual initiative of the NCAC designed to promote Nigeria’s diverse cultural heritage, encourage cultural exchange and strengthen national integration.

Beyond preserving culture, the festival gives creatives, artisans and entrepreneurs a platform to display products, reach markets and contribute to the growing creative economy.

title: Men’s fertility and why sperm banking is gaining attention
description: For many men, fatherhood is something they assume can happen whenever they are ready. Unlike women, whose reproductive ageing is widely discussed, men often grow up believing that their ability to father children remains intact well into old age. While the assumption is understandable, it is not ent
content:
For many men, fatherhood is something they assume can happen whenever they are ready. Unlike women, whose reproductive ageing is widely discussed, men often grow up believing that their ability to father children remains intact well into old age. While the assumption is understandable, it is not entirely true.

A man may continue producing sperm throughout his adult life, but that does not mean his reproductive potential remains unchanged.

Ageing, illness, cancer treatment, exposure to workplace chemicals, excessive heat and certain lifestyle choices can gradually affect sperm quality, reduce fertility and increase the risks associated with fathering children later in life. This is where sperm banking, also known as sperm cryopreservation, is gaining attention.

The procedure involves collecting, testing and freezing sperm at very low temperatures, usually in liquid nitrogen, for possible use in future fertility treatment.

It allows a man to preserve sperm produced at a particular stage of his life rather than depend entirely on his reproductive health years later. The idea is simple. Preserve your reproductive options while you still have them.

For men who want children someday, those facing cancer treatment, or workers whose occupations expose them to potentially harmful substances, sperm banking offers an opportunity to take control of an aspect of their health that is often neglected.

Unlike women, who are born with a finite supply of eggs, men generally produce sperm continuously after puberty. This biological difference has helped reinforce the belief that male fertility has no meaningful age limit. However, sperm production does not make men immune to reproductive ageing.

As men grow older, changes can occur in semen volume, sperm concentration, motility and morphology. Sperm motility refers to the ability of sperm to move effectively, while morphology describes their shape and structure. These characteristics matter because sperm must travel through the female reproductive tract and successfully fertilise an egg.

There is also the issue of sperm DNA integrity. As men age, the likelihood of DNA damage and mutations in sperm can increase. This may affect reproductive outcomes even when a man can still achieve an erection, ejaculate normally and produce what appears to be a healthy semen sample.

Perhaps one of the strongest reasons for sperm banking is cancer. A cancer diagnosis can arrive when a man is still building his career, planning marriage or raising a young family.

Treatment may become the immediate priority, leaving little time to consider what life might look like after recovery. Yet chemotherapy, radiotherapy and certain surgical procedures can damage the reproductive system.

Some chemotherapy drugs destroy sperm-producing cells in the testes. Radiation involving the reproductive organs can also damage the cells responsible for sperm production.

Depending on the treatment, dosage and individual circumstances, the resulting infertility may be temporary or permanent. Men should not wait until chemotherapy begins. Cancer treatment can affect sperm quality and DNA integrity, sometimes after only one treatment. Where possible, sperm collection should take place before treatment starts.

Another reason sperm banking deserves attention is occupational exposure. Men working in agriculture, manufacturing, construction, petroleum operations, welding, chemical processing and other industrial environments may encounter substances or conditions capable of affecting reproductive health.

Pesticides, heavy metals, industrial solvents and certain chemicals have been associated with changes in sperm concentration, motility and morphology. Prolonged exposure to excessive heat may also interfere with normal sperm production because the testes require a temperature slightly below the body’s core temperature.

It does not mean that every man working in a farm, factory or industrial environment will become infertile. The degree of risk depends on the substance, intensity and duration of exposure, protective measures and individual health factors.

For some workers, sperm banking may be worth discussing with a reproductive specialist, particularly when exposure is substantial or prolonged and future fatherhood is important. It should not, however, replace workplace safety. Protective equipment, proper ventilation, exposure monitoring and occupational health regulations remain essential.

Freezing does not guarantee that every sperm cell will survive thawing. Some cells may lose viability, and the success of future treatment depends on several factors, including the original sperm quality, the woman’s reproductive health and the fertility procedure selected. The value of sperm banking becomes clearer when viewed across different stages of a man’s life.

In the medium term, stored sperm may become useful when a man is ready to settle down and start a family. This is particularly relevant to men whose fertility has declined following cancer treatment, serious illness or other medical interventions.

It may also provide an opportunity to use sperm collected at a younger age, although it cannot eliminate every reproductive risk associated with ageing or guarantee a successful pregnancy.

In the long term, sperm banking can preserve the possibility of biological fatherhood even when natural sperm production has become severely impaired or permanently stopped. For cancer survivors, it can be an important part of life after treatment. For men who have delayed parenthood, it offers another reproductive option as they grow older.

Properly frozen sperm can remain usable for many years, provided storage conditions are maintained. There is no simple biological expiry date that applies to every stored sample, although storage regulations, consent arrangements, clinic policies and costs must be considered.

More importantly, sperm banking should not be confused with sperm donation. The intention is to preserve a man’s own reproductive material for his potential future use, subject to appropriate consent and storage arrangements.

Ultimately, sperm banking is not about encouraging every man to freeze his sperm or creating anxiety about ageing. It is about recognising that male fertility is not unlimited and that some reproductive opportunities are easier to preserve before they are lost.

Men spend years planning their careers, finances, businesses and retirement. Yet many give little thought to preserving their ability to have children, but a man’s fertility deserves attention long before he actually needs it.

title: Can we be honest about Gen Z?
description:
A family friend (who is a university professor) contacted me recently to help out with the accommodation of one of his students who was said to be in town for ‘final-year clearance.’
He told me that she is about 21 years old and someone he is trying to help because “her family is poor.” It was not a
content:
A family friend (who is a university professor) contacted me recently to help out with the accommodation of one of his students who was said to be in town for ‘final-year clearance.’

He told me that she is about 21 years old and someone he is trying to help because “her family is poor.” It was not an easy favour for me to dispense (because she’s a total stranger whose way of life I don’t know), but my heart was becoming swayed because she was coming from someone that I have immense respect for.

Also, the fact that I am a mother made me keep imagining my own child in her shoes. I am a firm believer that the easiest way to ask for God’s grace over our own children is by being mindful of how we treat other people’s children.

So, I asked him to give the young lady my phone number and insisted that a phone conversation and a face-to-face meeting would have to happen first, as I believe that speaking with her and observing her for some minutes would enable me to make up my mind.

He did, and the young lady texted me on WhatsApp. I called her. From our conversation, I understood that she was actually done with the ‘clearance’ and just looking for somewhere to stay until the National Youth Service call-up.

Apparently, she does not find the house of the friend she was putting up with comfortable. I learned that it’s a family house and her friend’s parents are present.

Another thing I learned is that there’s a job she’s considering doing in the meantime. This aspect of the story was unknown to our mutual contact.

I was actually impressed by her job efforts until she got back to me later in the day to explain that meeting me the next day (Saturday), as scheduled, was no longer feasible. She postponed the meeting to Monday, even though I expected her to suggest Sunday as someone in dire need.

Monday came, and I didn’t hear from her all day until around 7 pm, when she contacted me via text to explain how busy she had been. She then asked if I was at home so she could be on her way.

I told her to revert to our mutual contact, as I had communicated my decision to him. The decision was that it was not convenient for me to take in someone whose duration of stay in my house was indefinite.

If she just needed accommodation for a week or two while in town, I could handle that. I also pointed out her mannerisms, which made it look like the meeting was dependent on her convenience, as if she was doing me a favour.

Well, if I expected “I am sorry. Thank you for the correction” or “That was not intentional,” it did not come. While communicating my observation to our mutual contact, I said to him, “Her body language is not some poor-girl behaviour but her-royal-highness.” He chuckled and then added, “Honestly, it’s a common Gen Z behaviour. We have lost standard courtesy and humility in them.”

This is actually the aspect of this Gen Z behavioural nightmare that I find more disturbing!

Are we now going to relax with a repulsive mannerism (from children who don’t know any better) as the new normal? How many of them even understand that ‘a Gen Z behaviour’ is rarely referred to in a positive light?

There is something painfully entitled, self-absorbed and not-humble about the Gen Z mindset. Even when your intervention is technically a lifeline to them, they still behave like they are doing you a favour!

An acquaintance who lives abroad shared his dating experience with me. According to him, he had just met the young lady, and their talks ‘flowed’ on the first day until the third day, when he asked for her pictures.

She explained that her ‘main phone,’ where her current pictures were saved, was with a phone repairer. He said that she harped on her ‘phone that has become difficult to repair’ for the next two days and then stopped picking up his calls. That was how that chapter was closed.

Sometimes, men who have honourable intentions for a relationship usually don’t have a principle of throwing money at the setting right away, especially those of them who have become ‘once bitten, twice shy.’

But knowing who he is, I can confidently say that the young lady just missed a man who could have effortlessly changed her life for good. He had actually begun to consider the fastest means of sending a phone down to her in Nigeria. And it was meant to be a surprise for her.

Rude impatience is another malady of Gen Z, and I shudder at their losses.

title: Obi vows to end kidnappings, corruption
description:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, has pledged to tackle kidnapping, corruption and unemployment, promising to generate 10,000 megawatts of electricity if elected president in 2027.
Obi, who made the pledge during a town hall meeting in Onitsha, Anambra State,
content:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, has pledged to tackle kidnapping, corruption and unemployment, promising to generate 10,000 megawatts of electricity if elected president in 2027.

Obi, who made the pledge during a town hall meeting in Onitsha, Anambra State, on Friday, said his proposed administration would prioritise security, education, healthcare and electricity, while moving the country from a consumption-driven economy to one based on production.

He said Nigerians had suffered enough under the current administration, promising that his partnership with his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, would unite the country and restore public confidence in governance.

“Kwankwaso and I have formed a team and that is the team that will unite Nigeria. We are not going to have a Nigeria where people will come and kidnap our schoolchildren.

“We will fight corruption, we want to use public money for public good, and from day one, you will feel it and you will know that a new team is in charge.

“We will move Nigeria from consumption to production, and our people will get jobs. We want a country where if you are sick, you go to hospital and not church,” he said.

The former Anambra governor also promised to establish functional primary healthcare centres in every ward across the country and build 50,000 primary school blocks as part of his proposed investment in education and healthcare.

On electricity, Obi said Nigeria’s current power generation, transmission and distribution capacity of about 4,000 megawatts was inadequate, promising that his administration would generate 10,000 megawatts.

“Today, Nigeria only generates, transmits and distributes 4,000 megawatts, but Kwankwaso and I will generate 10,000 megawatts of power.

“Everything we say here, please take note of it because we will do it. We will not give you excuses because we know that the country is already bad, and we will not tell you we didn’t know it was this bad,” he said.

Obi urged Nigerians to turn out for the January 16, 2027 election and defend their votes, asking supporters to remain at polling units until votes were counted and transmitted.

He said, “Nigerians have suffered enough, so all of you are contestants in this election through us. So go out there on that day, take it as a day of sacrifice for Nigeria.

“Carry your food to the polling unit on that day, vote, stay there for counting and transmitting and make sure there is no rigging. That day is now declared a public holiday for vote defence.”

The NDC candidate also criticised President Bola Tinubu’s borrowing record, accusing him of failing to fulfil his promise not to borrow after removing the petrol subsidy.

He said his campaign was seeking to change what he described as the failures of the present administration, adding that Nigeria needed an energetic president committed to addressing the country’s challenges.

Earlier, Obi led a road show through major parts of Onitsha, attracting large crowds as he moved from his residence in Onitsha GRA to the First Niger Bridge Head, Ochanja Market, Main Market, Ose Okwodu Market and other locations.

The procession ended at the Main Bowl of the Archbishop C.J. Patterson Building, All Saints Cathedral, venue of the town hall meeting.

Before the engagement, Obi visited his alma mater, Christ the King College, Onitsha, where he interacted with students and inspected a teachers’ residential building he said he and others had supported.

He said the project was intended to provide teachers with comfortable accommodation and improve the conditions under which they worked.

Obi reiterated his commitment to education, saying it would receive substantial investment if he became president.

“Education to me remains the tool for development. It is one investment that if I have the opportunity to serve Nigeria, everybody will visibly and measurably see our investment in education,” he said.

Also speaking, the senator representing Anambra Central, Victor Umeh, described Obi as the best candidate for the presidency, expressing confidence that the NDC would secure overwhelming support in the South-East and attract votes from the North through Kwankwaso.

The post Obi vows to end kidnappings, corruption appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Ex-ICAN chair to unveil memoir
description:
Former Chairman of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria, Lagos Mainland and District Society, Blessing Osakwe-Ogo, is set to document her journey from humble beginnings to professional leadership in an autobiography titled Blessed Beyond Limits.
The 12-chapter book, due to be unveiled o
content:
Former Chairman of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria, Lagos Mainland and District Society, Blessing Osakwe-Ogo, is set to document her journey from humble beginnings to professional leadership in an autobiography titled Blessed Beyond Limits.

The 12-chapter book, due to be unveiled on Sunday, November 22, 2026, at the ICAN Centre in the Amuwo area of Lagos, chronicles the personal and professional experiences that shaped her life, including the obstacles she overcame while building her career.

According to a statement sent to Saturday PUNCH on Friday by the author, the autobiography also explores aspects of Igbo culture, particularly life in Oguta before and after the Nigerian Civil War, offering a personal account of the social and cultural experiences that influenced her upbringing.

Osakwe-Ogo, who chaired the ICAN Lagos Mainland and District Society between 2017 and 2018, is currently National Chairperson of the Society of Women Accountants of Nigeria.

The book, according to the statement, reflects on her transition from modest beginnings to professional achievements, which she attributes to divine intervention, perseverance and the support she received along the way.

The unveiling will also serve as an occasion to mark her retirement from the federal civil service.

Renowned lawyer Charles Jaja will chair the event, while Fellow of Chartered Accountants Dr Fola Ogunsola is expected to deliver the keynote address.

Pastor Ituah Ighodalo of Trinity House Church is among the dignitaries expected at the ceremony, which will also draw professional leaders, business executives and other guests.

title: Sokoto-Badagry road: FG blames Ogun over unpaid compensation
description:
The Federal Government has blamed the Ogun State Government for the delay in paying compensation to residents whose properties were demolished along the Atan-Lusada axis of the Sokoto-Badagry road, saying it was not responsible for the demolitions.
Affected property owners and residents of Atan and
content:
The Federal Government has blamed the Ogun State Government for the delay in paying compensation to residents whose properties were demolished along the Atan-Lusada axis of the Sokoto-Badagry road, saying it was not responsible for the demolitions.

Affected property owners and residents of Atan and Lusada communities staged a peaceful protest on Tuesday over the alleged failure of the government to compensate them for properties demolished in July 2022 during the reconstruction of the Atan-Lusada-Agbara road.

According to the protesters, in a statement published by AMOKAZTv on Facebook, reports had circulated that the government had paid property owners, though they had yet to receive any compensation.

They lamented that their homes, shops, businesses and some religious centres were affected by the demolition exercise, leaving many families in hardship for more than four years.

The residents said they were not opposed to government infrastructure projects but insisted that development should be accompanied by fairness, justice and respect for citizens’ rights.

They called on the Federal Government, particularly the Minister of Works, to intervene and ensure all affected property owners receive compensation without further delay.

However, the officer in charge of the project and Senior Civil Engineer at the Federal Ministry of Works, Aliu Oyewande, said the Federal Government had paid those whose properties it demolished during the current road construction project.

Oyewande said a report had been prepared and affected property owners were asked to come forward for payment, adding that those who complied had received their compensation.

He said the demolitions in the Atan-Lusada area were carried out by the Ogun State Government during an earlier road construction project about 10 to 12 years ago.

“The Atan-Lusada area, we didn’t demolish any building there. It was the Ogun State Government. That road has been done almost 10 to 12 years ago. When we got there, we didn’t carry out any demolition there,” Oyewande said.

“The places we demolished were from after Atan towards Ilaro after the Atan junction, that is where we demolished.”

The official said residents who approached the Federal Government over compensation were told it was not responsible for the demolition of their properties.

He said the Federal Government had begun paying for properties affected by its own demolition exercise, which he claimed prompted residents whose properties were demolished earlier to demand compensation from it.

“They came before and we told them we were not responsible for the demolition of their buildings. We started this project last year; we couldn’t have been the one that demolished their properties. It was the Ogun State that did that road initially,” he said.

“The ones we are paying for were the ones we demolished. We told them to go and meet Ogun State, but because they saw that we started paying for the ones we demolished, that was when the agitation came up.”

The residents, however, maintained that their protest was not politically motivated, describing it as an appeal for justice and equal treatment.

They urged the relevant authorities to address the prolonged compensation delay and said they should not be forgotten because their properties were demolished for infrastructure development.

Efforts to reach the Ogun State Commissioner for Physical Planning and Urban Development, Olatunji Odunlami, for comment were unsuccessful, as calls and messages sent to his mobile phone got no response.

Also, the Special Adviser to the Ogun State Governor on Media and Strategy, Kayode Akinmade, neither answered calls nor replied to messages sent to him.

The post Sokoto-Badagry road: FG blames Ogun over unpaid compensation appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 3,000 runners set for Capital City Race
description:
The third edition of the Capital City Race will hold on Saturday, November 21, in Ikeja, Lagos, with 3,000 runners expected to take part in the 10-kilometre event.
The organisers have set aside at least N2m in cash prizes, but insist that promoting fitness, healthy living and recreational running ma
content:
The third edition of the Capital City Race will hold on Saturday, November 21, in Ikeja, Lagos, with 3,000 runners expected to take part in the 10-kilometre event.

The organisers have set aside at least N2m in cash prizes, but insist that promoting fitness, healthy living and recreational running matters more than the financial rewards.

The race convener, Dapo Ajayi, said at a press conference on Thursday at the Teslim Balogun Stadium, Lagos, that the event had grown steadily since it began in 2024. The first edition attracted about 1,000 runners, while 1,467 registered for the second edition in 2025. All slots for this year’s race have been filled.

The race starts at Ikeja City Mall and runs through Ikeja. Ajayi said the organisers were working with partners to improve the participants’ experience and make the event more accessible.

“We are happy with the steady progress and impact we are making. Very soon, Capital City Race may expand across other states,” he hinted.

The Director-General of the Lagos State Sports Commission, Lekan Fatodu, described the race as an important part of efforts to build a stronger culture of physical activity in the state. He said the rising number of road races and fitness events showed growing interest in healthier lifestyles among Lagos residents.

“What the competition does is to motivate them and push them to get on the road. We have realised that every single day, a lot of Lagosians want to step out to engage in outdoor activities related to healthy living, fitness and wellness,” Fatodu said.

He added that the government would keep supporting such initiatives because of their health and economic benefits, noting that businesses producing sports merchandise and selling healthy drinks also gain from the growing sports industry.

The co-convener, Folashade Falokun, said the growing number of running events in Lagos showed that more organisers were embracing fitness and longevity.

“We are encouraging fitness because we are encouraging longevity. People keep saying, ‘I am sick, I am feeling tired.’ When you keep fit, it is good for everybody. So, it is a win-win for all of us, for the runners and the organisers,” she said.

Falokun appealed to government institutions, businesses and corporate organisations to support initiatives that encourage mass participation in physical activity.

Three Crowns Milk and Pocari Sweat are among the sponsors of the 2026 race, and both brands said they were delighted to support a platform that promotes healthy living.

The race was conceived by sports and marketing consultant Ajayi to give Lagos a professionally organised 10-kilometre road race.

title: Edo voter register hits 2.8 million
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has put the number of registered voters in Edo State at 2.8 million following the conclusion of the Continuous Voter Registration exercise.
The Edo State Resident Electoral Commissioner, Obo Effanga, disclosed this on Friday, adding that the latest regis
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has put the number of registered voters in Edo State at 2.8 million following the conclusion of the Continuous Voter Registration exercise.

The Edo State Resident Electoral Commissioner, Obo Effanga, disclosed this on Friday, adding that the latest registration exercise had increased the state’s voter population.

He said the final figure would be announced after the commission’s national headquarters completed its clean-up exercise.

INEC had earlier announced that 131,165 new voters were registered in Edo during the Continuous Voter Registration exercise conducted between August 2025 and July 2026.

Providing an update on the collection of Permanent Voter Cards, Effanga said 23,401 PVCs had been collected across the state since distribution commenced on October 9.

He explained that the figure comprised 6,319 old PVCs, 5,128 newly produced cards and 11,954 PVCs relating to transfers.

Effanga said: “The state currently has 2.8 million registered voters after the last registration exercise. However, the final figure would be released after the recent clean-up exercise by the national body.”

The REC disclosed that PVCs belonging to voters who registered during the first and second phases of the Continuous Voter Registration exercise were available for collection at INEC offices across the state’s 18 local government areas.

He recalled that the first phase of the registration exercise lasted from August to December 2025, while the second phase took place between January and April 2026.

On preparations for the forthcoming elections, Effanga said the commission was working towards ensuring a smooth electoral process.

Speaking on the mock accreditation exercise scheduled for November 28, he said it would be conducted in 384 polling units across the state.

He explained that Edo had 192 registration areas, also known as wards, with two polling units selected from each registration area for the exercise.

According to him, the exercise would provide an opportunity to test the commission’s electoral technology and assess the preparedness of its personnel ahead of the elections.

He added that the state office had submitted the list of proposed polling units to INEC headquarters for approval.

Effanga said the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System would be deployed during the exercise to demonstrate voter accreditation, result capture and transmission to the INEC Result Viewing Portal.

On the recruitment of ad hoc personnel, the REC explained that INEC did not have sufficient permanent staff to conduct elections across the state’s 4,519 polling units, making the recruitment of temporary personnel necessary.

He said recruitment would commence after the closure of the application portal, following which the commission’s headquarters would process applicants’ details and forward the names to the respective states based on their preferred locations of service.

Successful applicants would subsequently be invited for screening and training before deployment, he added.

The REC identified Supervisory Presiding Officers and collation officers as other categories of ad hoc personnel required for the exercise.

He explained that Supervisory Presiding Officers were usually selected from among senior civil servants, particularly federal civil servants who met the required grade-level qualifications.

Addressing concerns over the safety of ad hoc personnel, particularly in view of previous incidents of electoral violence, Effanga said INEC was working with security agencies to ensure adequate protection for everyone involved in the electoral process.

He emphasised that security arrangements would cover not only election officials but also voters, journalists and other stakeholders participating in the exercise.

According to him, the commission had been holding regular meetings of the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security, with the latest meeting held on Tuesday.

He also disclosed that he would participate in a national summit on election security organised by the Office of the National Security Adviser in collaboration with INEC.

The REC, however, stressed that maintaining electoral security required the cooperation of all stakeholders, particularly politicians, whom he accused of sometimes encouraging violence through their actions and campaign rhetoric.

He said politicians must understand that elections were civil exercises and should not threaten or intimidate voters into supporting particular candidates.

Effanga condemned statements suggesting that people who refused to vote for certain candidates should not visit particular communities, describing such rhetoric as unacceptable.

On whether election personnel were covered by insurance in the event of injuries or other incidents during elections, the REC confirmed that the commission had insurance arrangements for those engaged in the electoral process.

He said the coverage included life insurance, adding that INEC had previously taken responsibility for the medical treatment and other necessary support of corps members injured while performing electoral duties.

The post Edo voter register hits 2.8 million appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
