title: Scrabble: Jimoh seeks govt investment after African triumph
description:
Nigeria’s number one Scrabble player, Abdulmumin Jimoh, has urged the Kogi State Government to invest in the development of the game following his emergence as African champion.
Jimoh won the individual title at the 16th African Scrabble Championship, held in Monrovia, Liberia, from October 22 to 25
content:
Nigeria’s number one Scrabble player, Abdulmumin Jimoh, has urged the Kogi State Government to invest in the development of the game following his emergence as African champion.

Jimoh won the individual title at the 16th African Scrabble Championship, held in Monrovia, Liberia, from October 22 to 25. He is the first player from Kogi State and the wider North Central region to achieve the feat.

In a statement signed by the spokesperson of the Nigeria Scrabble Federation, Maxwell Kumoye, Jimoh described the win as a landmark for Kogi State, Ebira land and the entire North Central. He appealed to Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo, former Governor Yahaya Bello, Senator Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, traditional rulers and other political leaders to recognise his achievement.

“I did not go there as Abdulmumin alone. I went there carrying Kogi on my chest,” Jimoh said.

He thanked the people of Kogi for their prayers and support, but stressed that his accomplishment deserved more attention, given the limited backing the sport receives.

Jimoh also highlighted the benefits of Scrabble, describing it as an effective tool for youth development and for keeping young people away from social vices. He said the game helps children improve their English language, mathematical skills, concentration, patience and critical thinking.

He challenged the state government to treat his success as an opportunity to invest in the next generation by introducing and strengthening Scrabble programmes in schools across Kogi Central, Kogi East and Kogi West.

“If Kogi can produce an African champion with little support, imagine what we can produce if our state stands behind us,” he said.

Jimoh expressed optimism that deliberate government intervention and grassroots investment would give more young people from the state the chance to excel at national, continental and international levels. His appeal comes amid growing calls for greater government recognition and financial support for Nigerian Scrabble players.

For the African champion, the ultimate reward would be for his breakthrough to become the foundation for producing many more champions from Kogi State and Ebira land.

“I am your son, and I will keep making Kogi proud,” he said.

title: Akpabio asks APC to shun violence
description:
Senate President Godswill Akpabio has cautioned members and support groups of the All Progressives Congress against being provoked into violence or retaliatory attacks on opposition supporters as campaign activities for the 2027 general elections gather pace.
Akpabio urged APC supporters to resist a
content:
Senate President Godswill Akpabio has cautioned members and support groups of the All Progressives Congress against being provoked into violence or retaliatory attacks on opposition supporters as campaign activities for the 2027 general elections gather pace.

Akpabio urged APC supporters to resist attempts by political opponents to instigate violence, insisting the ruling party was better placed to win the election through persuasion and its record in government.

He gave the advice in Abuja on Friday at the inauguration of the Tinubu Again Movement, a grassroots mobilisation platform convened by the Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, to mobilise more than 20 million votes for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027.

In a statement issued by his Special Assistant on Media and Communication, Anietie Ekong, Akpabio warned APC members against falling for what he described as opposition tactics to provoke violence and attract public sympathy ahead of the polls.

According to him, the ruling party should focus on winning votes rather than engaging in confrontations with opposition supporters.

“Please be careful. Don’t allow them to provoke you to violence. Because they know they are losing, they will sponsor some misguided youths to throw stones at you. If they throw stones at you, your target is to garner votes and defeat them.

“By January 16, 2027, they will know the difference between stones and votes. When you are certain of winning, you don’t deploy stones and violence as your weapons, but you persuade them with the monumental achievement of the APC administration,” he said.

Akpabio, who chaired the inauguration, urged members of the movement to take the achievements of the Tinubu administration to polling units, wards and local government areas to convince voters to support the President’s second-term bid.

He listed the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, the Sokoto-Badagry Highway and other road projects across the country among the administration’s achievements.

The Senate President also defended the removal of the petrol subsidy, saying the policy had increased allocations to state and local governments and enabled them to execute development projects without excessive borrowing.

He said Nigeria’s economy was close to collapse before Tinubu assumed office, adding that the administration’s economic reforms had helped stabilise the situation.

Akpabio also cited the Nigerian Education Loan Fund as an intervention that had widened access to higher education for indigent students, while describing the tax reforms as measures that had recalibrated the economy.

“Today the states are benefitting from the economic reforms. Many governors are executing projects without borrowing a dime because of the ingenuity of one man, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

“So, when you go out there to talk about how President Tinubu must be returned to office with over 20 million votes, say it with boldness because this President had stabilised and grown the economy and the indices are there for all to see,” he said.

He commended Matawalle for establishing the movement and urged other political appointees to follow his example by mobilising support for Tinubu’s re-election.

As part of the mobilisation drive, more than 1,000 vehicles were commissioned for distribution to the movement’s national, zonal and state coordinators. Grants and food items were also distributed to households across the country.

The inauguration was attended by the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas; APC National Chairman Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda; serving and former senators; ministers; women leaders and other party stakeholders.

title: Brighton coach blames Nigeria for Yohanna blow
description:
Brighton and Hove Albion manager Fabian Hürzeler has blamed Nigeria’s handling of Zadok Yohanna during international duty for the young winger’s latest injury setback ahead of Sunday’s Premier League clash against Semi Ajayi’s Hull City.
The setback rules Yohanna out of the weekend fixture after his
content:
Brighton and Hove Albion manager Fabian Hürzeler has blamed Nigeria’s handling of Zadok Yohanna during international duty for the young winger’s latest injury setback ahead of Sunday’s Premier League clash against Semi Ajayi’s Hull City.

The setback rules Yohanna out of the weekend fixture after his previous muscle problem flared up during Nigeria’s 2027 Africa U23 Cup of Nations qualifier against the Democratic Republic of Congo.

The 19-year-old was forced off in the first half of the first leg in Lubumbashi last Friday, which the Olympic Eagles lost 2-0, before returning to England and missing Tuesday’s 4-0 second-leg victory in Ikenne that sealed a 4-2 aggregate progression.

“Zadok, unfortunately, had a re-injury when he was in Nigeria under-23s,” Hürzeler said.

“Unfortunately, he wasn’t perfectly managed, and therefore he had a re-injury, which is very bad and very unlucky for Zadok.”

Having joined Brighton from Swedish club AIK in the summer on a five-year contract, Yohanna had only recently returned to senior training after more than two months out following early appearances against Aston Villa and Tromsø.

Hürzeler said the club would support him through recovery once more, though Brighton have not revealed the exact nature of the injury or a return timeline.

title: Nwobodo urges ESUT to prioritise innovation, research, good governance
description: By Alumona UkwuezeENUGU—-Former Governor of old Anambra State and former Minister of Sports, Chief (Dr.) Jim Ifeanyichukwu Nwobodo, has urged the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT) to prioritise research, technological innovation, entrepreneurship and good governance to enhance
content:
By Alumona Ukwueze
ENUGU—-Former Governor of old Anambra State and former Minister of Sports, Chief (Dr.) Jim Ifeanyichukwu Nwobodo, has urged the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT) to prioritise research, technological innovation, entrepreneurship and good governance to enhance its contribution to national development.

Nwobodo made the call while delivering the 3rd Distinguished Personality Lecture of ESUT during the university’s Special Convocation Ceremony at its permanent site at Ebe-ano City, Enugu State.

The lecture was titled, “From Vision to Legacy: Technology, Education, Leadership, Good Governance and the Responsibility of a New Generation.”

Nwobodo, who founded the Anambra State University of Science and Technology (ASUTECH) in 1980, said the establishment of the institution was a deliberate investment in the future, driven by the conviction that education, scientific knowledge, technological competence and visionary leadership were essential to societal progress.

He expressed satisfaction with the growth of the university, noting that the institution’s continued development more than four decades after its establishment demonstrated the enduring value of its founding vision.

According to him, the true measure of leadership goes beyond achievements recorded while in office to include the institutions established and the opportunities created for future generations.

Reflecting on his experience in public service, Nwobodo said governments and political office holders might come and go, but institutions founded on sound principles and sustained through responsible governance could endure for generations.

He stressed that visionary leadership required the courage to make difficult decisions and undertake initiatives whose benefits might extend beyond one’s tenure in public office.

On the future of ESUT, the former governor called for its transformation into a leading centre for research, innovation, entrepreneurship, technological development and practical solutions to societal challenges.

He said the university’s success should not be measured solely by student enrolment and graduation figures but also by the quality of its research, technological discoveries, entrepreneurial achievements and contributions to national development.

Nwobodo advocated increased investment in applied research, urging engineering students to develop solutions to energy and infrastructure challenges, agricultural scientists to improve food production, medical researchers to advance healthcare, and computer scientists to develop applications in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and digital technology.

He also called for stronger collaboration among students of management, law, economics and social sciences and their counterparts in science and engineering to translate research findings into commercially viable enterprises.

The former minister further urged the university to strengthen its partnerships with government, industries, investors, research institutions and alumni.

He specifically encouraged ESUT to establish or strengthen a dedicated centre for innovation and entrepreneurship where students, researchers and industry partners could transform promising ideas into products, businesses and practical solutions.

Nwobodo also underscored the importance of alumni participation in the university’s development, calling for stronger partnerships between the institution and its graduates through scholarships, research endowments, mentorship, industry partnerships, internships and support for entrepreneurship.

He said alumni who had distinguished themselves in business, industry, technology, academia and public service possessed valuable knowledge, professional networks and resources that could strengthen the university.

On technology and leadership, Nwobodo cautioned that technological competence must be accompanied by critical thinking, ethical judgment, responsible leadership and an understanding of society.

He noted that although artificial intelligence could process information at extraordinary speed, human beings must remain accountable for decisions made with its assistance.

“Technology determines what society is capable of doing. Leadership, values and governance determine how that capability is used,” he said.

He therefore urged universities to produce not only technologically competent graduates but also knowledgeable, innovative and ethical citizens capable of applying technology in the service of humanity.

Addressing the issue of good governance, Nwobodo said effective leadership required transparency, accountability, competence, fairness, respect for the rule of law and responsible management of public resources.

He maintained that public office was a position of trust that must be exercised in the public interest.

The former governor further stressed the need for continuity in institutional development, warning that when successive administrations abandoned the worthwhile initiatives of their predecessors, development became discontinuous and difficult to sustain.

He said institutions must be stronger than individuals and establish systems that preserve continuity, merit and accountability beyond changes in leadership.

Nwobodo noted that ASUTECH was established under an administration that eventually ended, but its educational vision endured because successive generations contributed to its development.

He urged the university community, particularly graduating students, to embrace leadership founded on integrity, responsibility, sound judgment and service to society.

The Governor of Enugu State, His Excellency, Dr. Peter Mbah praised Nwobodo’s vision and courage in leadership, especially for investing heavily in human capital development, taking the bold step to establish ESUT a few years after the civil war, not minding the enormity of the challenges involved.

“I have often wondered what it must have felt like to be governor in 1979. Nigeria had just returned to civilian government after thirteen years of military rule.

“The Civil War had ended less than a decade earlier, and the country was still dealing with its consequences. There was much to rebuild, and enormous pressure on the resources available to government.

“For many families, university education remained beyond their reach. And here was a young governor, who decided that his state should establish a university of science and technology.

“People questioned whether it could be done. Was there enough money? Could a state government sustain such an institution? Shouldn’t this be left to the federal government?,” the Governor said.

Earlier in his welcome address, the Vice Chancellor of ESUT, Professor Aloysius-Michaels Okolie, lauded the contribution of Senator Nwobodo, to the education sector, stating that “he dared to establish the first University of Technology in Nigeria.”

“Today, 46 years after, that seed had grown into a giant, producing thousands of scientists, engineers, doctors, managers and leaders serving Nigeria and humanity in various capacities. We are forever grateful, Sir.

“As the first civilian Executive Governor of old Anambra State (1979-1983), Senator Nwobodo broke all records of achievements and laid foundation of modern Anambra and Enugu States respectively. Your incredible footprints are still visible,” he said.

Equally, the Chairman of the Local Organizing Committee for the Lecture, Professor Okechukwu Oji, while welcoming guests at the event, stated that the Distinguished Personality Lecture Series was conceived by the University to bridge the gap between the town and gown and to address burning issues of public interest for the benefit of society.

He further stated that the Lecturer, Senator Nwobodo, given his wealth of knowledge and experience in leadership, politics and governance, as well as his God-given wisdom would do justice to the topic.

Honorary Doctorate Award for Leadership, Governance and Human Capital Development – Honoris Causa was conferred on Senator Nwobodo by ESUT during the lecture.

The lecture drew dignitaries including the Visitor to the University and Governor of Enugu State, Dr. Peter Mbah, ministers, commissioners and other critical stakeholders to ESUT.

The post Nwobodo urges ESUT to prioritise innovation, research, good governance appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: National anthem row: Youths ask Obi to apologise
description:
The Northern Youth Assembly has given the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, a 72-hour ultimatum to apologise over the singing of Nigeria’s former national anthem, Arise, O Compatriots, at a political gathering in Lagos.
Obi was also asked to clarify his position o
content:
The Northern Youth Assembly has given the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, a 72-hour ultimatum to apologise over the singing of Nigeria’s former national anthem, Arise, O Compatriots, at a political gathering in Lagos.

Obi was also asked to clarify his position on the officially adopted national anthem, Nigeria, We Hail Thee, and reaffirm his commitment to national unity and constitutional order.

The demands were contained in a statement issued by the assembly’s National Publicity Secretary, Adikwu Joshua, a copy of which was obtained by Saturday PUNCH on Friday.

The assembly expressed concern over the incident at the NDC town hall meeting in Lagos, where it alleged that some participants declined to sing the current national anthem and instead sang the former anthem.

It described the action as inappropriate, particularly at a gathering linked to a prominent political figure and presidential aspirant.

While acknowledging Nigerians’ constitutional rights to freedom of expression, peaceful assembly and political association, the group insisted that such freedoms should be exercised with respect for the country’s sovereignty and national symbols.

It argued that the national anthem represented Nigeria’s collective identity and should not be used as a political campaign tool or an instrument for airing grievances against the government.

The assembly maintained that national symbols should remain above partisan interests, ethnic affiliations and religious differences.

It also argued that Obi’s influence in the country’s political space placed a responsibility on him to promote national cohesion and responsible citizenship.

Consequently, the group demanded that Obi and others it claimed were directly involved in the incident issue a public apology within 72 hours of the statement.

It said the ultimatum was meant to give those involved an opportunity to show patriotism and respect for Nigerians.

The assembly warned that failure to receive a satisfactory response within the stipulated period could compel it to pursue further lawful action.

It, however, stressed that its position was not meant to suppress opposition or legitimate criticism of the Federal Government.

title: Barrow Promises To Transform Niani Into A Modern District If Re-Elected
description:
Gambiaj.com – (BANJUL, THE GAMBIA) – President Adama Barrow has promised to accelerate development in Niani, Central River Region North, pledging to transform the district through major infrastructure and social development projects if re-elected on December 5.
Addressing residents at a campaign ral
content:
Gambiaj.com – (BANJUL, THE GAMBIA) – President Adama Barrow has promised to accelerate development in Niani, Central River Region North, pledging to transform the district through major infrastructure and social development projects if re-elected on December 5.

Addressing residents at a campaign rally, Barrow urged voters to assess his administration’s development record in Kabada, arguing that the projects delivered there following his 2021 election victory demonstrated what his government could achieve.

He said his administration had constructed 12 roads connecting communities in Kabada, extended electricity and water supplies, built a school and a health center, and installed streetlights across the village.

Barrow pledged that Niani would benefit from even greater development interventions if residents renewed his mandate, promising to transform the district into a modern urban centre comparable to Dubai.

Government Highlights Development Projects In CRR North

The President’s promises come against the backdrop of several ongoing and completed projects in Central River Region North, particularly in healthcare, education, agriculture and infrastructure.

In the health sector, the Barrow administration says it has constructed new health posts in Kataba Omar, Buduck and Balaghar Jaloto, each equipped with an ambulance to improve access to emergency medical services.

Construction of the 56-bed Njau Hospital is reportedly 80 per cent complete, while community ambulances have also been provided to areas such as Njoben to bring essential healthcare services closer to residents.

In education and skills development, the Madina Lamin Kanteh Multi-Purpose Skills Center in Wassu has been completed and furnished. The facility is expected to provide vocational and practical training opportunities for young people in Daru Mbayen and across the region.

Focus On Agriculture And Rural Development

Agriculture also features prominently in the government’s development agenda for CRR North, with investments targeting farmers, particularly women, alongside improvements in agricultural storage and market infrastructure.

A 70-hectare solar-powered rice farming project is under development at Lamin Koto, expected to benefit 103 farmers, 90 of whom are women. The Bati Jaha garden has also been completed and currently serves 97 gardeners.

Other ongoing interventions include the construction of an agro-logistics center in Wassu and a seed storage facility in Niani Banni.

Women and youth gardening projects are also being developed in Kucha and Bakadaji as part of efforts to expand agricultural opportunities and support rural livelihoods.

Barrow is seeking another five-year mandate in the December 5 presidential election, with his campaign highlighting infrastructure expansion, improved access to basic services and agricultural investment as key achievements of his administration.

title: NAFDAC destroys N100bn fake drugs, banned items
description:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control on Friday destroyed fake, expired, banned, substandard and other unwholesome regulated products with an estimated street value of N100bn.
The items—which included counterfeit drugs, expired codeine cough syrups, banned alcoholic bevera
content:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control on Friday destroyed fake, expired, banned, substandard and other unwholesome regulated products with an estimated street value of N100bn.

The items—which included counterfeit drugs, expired codeine cough syrups, banned alcoholic beverages, unregistered cosmetics and unsafe food items—were destroyed at the Ogwama Dumpsite, Ogere Remo, Ogun State.

Speaking at the event, NAFDAC Director-General Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye said the exercise was meant to stop dangerous products from entering circulation and endangering public health.

She said the items included banned alcoholic drinks packaged in sachets and PET bottles below 200ml, banned Analgin injections, expired codeine cough syrups, Oxytocin injections, counterfeit cosmetics and unwholesome food products.

Adeyeye said the destruction formed part of the agency’s enforcement drive to rid the country of fake, falsified, expired and unauthorised products.

She disclosed that NAFDAC operatives had recently uncovered illegal manufacturing activities in a Lagos warehouse originally meant for tools and hardware.

“Investigators discovered illegally manufactured cosmetic products at the penthouse of the building, alongside cartons of Augmentin and Ampicillin packets, leaflets and other unregistered cosmetic products,” Adeyeye said.

“The agency also uncovered a facility allegedly used to manufacture counterfeit versions of popular alcoholic beverage brands, while expired energy drinks were reportedly being revalidated and stored for distribution,” she added.

Adeyeye said suspects arrested in connection with the operations would face prosecution.

She further disclosed that NAFDAC officers, working with relevant stakeholders in Lagos and Ogun states, had carried out a mop-up operation involving more than 100,000 cartons of banned sachet and PET-bottled alcoholic beverages from manufacturers, wholesalers and retailers.

“The agency also uncovered a residential building allegedly being used to manufacture and distribute large quantities of unauthorised and registered herbal mixtures,” she said.

The NAFDAC boss said other products destroyed during the exercise were seized in enforcement raids or voluntarily surrendered by companies complying with regulatory rules.

“The agency remained committed to regulating food, drugs, cosmetics, medical devices, chemicals, packaged water and drinks to ensure their safety and suitability for consumption,” she said.

Adeyeye commended the Nigeria Customs Service for handing over pharmaceutical products, including several cartons of codeine-containing cough syrups, for destruction.

She also acknowledged the support of the Nigeria Police Force, Nigerian Army, Department of State Services, Pharmacists Council of Nigeria, National Drug Law Enforcement Agency and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps.

Adeyeye urged community and religious leaders, health practitioners and members of the public to help educate Nigerians on the dangers of patronising unlicensed vendors and unauthorised drug outlets.

She called on Nigerians to provide useful information to the agency to help identify and eliminate counterfeit, unregistered and unsafe products from the market.

The post NAFDAC destroys N100bn fake drugs, banned items appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: World’s best Bassey not for sale – Arbeloa
description:
Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa has insisted that Super Eagles defender Calvin Bassey is not for sale amid growing transfer speculation linking him with a January move to Manchester United, PUNCH Sports Extra reports.
Arbeloa spoke ahead of Fulham’s trip to face Manchester City on Saturday, praisin
content:
Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa has insisted that Super Eagles defender Calvin Bassey is not for sale amid growing transfer speculation linking him with a January move to Manchester United, PUNCH Sports Extra reports.

Arbeloa spoke ahead of Fulham’s trip to face Manchester City on Saturday, praising the Nigerian centre-back and confirming that the club are in talks over a new contract.

“I’m going to be really clear: he is very, very important. He’s one of our captains, and from the first day that I arrived and I saw how good he is, I think he is one of the best centre-backs in the world,” Arbeloa said.

The 26-year-old defender has been linked with Manchester United under new head coach Mauricio Pochettino as the Old Trafford side look to tighten up a backline that has conceded 30 goals this season.

Bassey’s current deal runs out next summer, though Fulham hold an option to extend it by one year, and Arbeloa stressed that selling players in January is not on the agenda.

“We are talking with him, because we want to extend his contract. Like I say, he’s very important for us, and we are happy with him, and I think he’s happy with us,” Arbeloa added.

“Fulham is not a jail – everyone that is here is because they want to be here, because they are happy, because they feel important, because they feel loved.”

Since arriving from Ajax in July 2023, Bassey has started and captained Fulham in all 10 of their Premier League matches this season and made 12 appearances overall, with the Cottagers sitting 15th on 10 points as they prepare to face a Manchester City side that has won their last 20 meetings.

title: Odegbami narrates near-death experience after attack
description:
Former Super Eagles captain and renowned sports administrator, Segun Odegbami, has recounted his close brush with death after surviving an early-morning attack by three armed men at his residence in Abeokuta, Ogun State, on Friday, Saturday PUNCH reports.
In a message to a close associate, the 74-ye
content:
Former Super Eagles captain and renowned sports administrator, Segun Odegbami, has recounted his close brush with death after surviving an early-morning attack by three armed men at his residence in Abeokuta, Ogun State, on Friday, Saturday PUNCH reports.

In a message to a close associate, the 74-year-old football legend, popularly known as Mathematical, described the ordeal as an assassination attempt and the closest he had ever come to death, explaining how he fought off the assailants alongside his driver and domestic worker after they broke down his door at about 2:30am.

“Thank the Creator of the Universe for me. I survived an assassination attempt. This morning at 2:30am, three unknown persons came to the house to steal and kill. I fought back with the help of God. My driver and house boy joined me, and we fought them before they fled. It was the closest I have ever been face to face with death. They broke down my door to get to me. I have been to the hospital,” Odegbami said.

The proprietor of Eagles 7 Sports Radio 103.7 FM sustained deep machete wounds during the struggle inside his home in the Ibara Government Reservation Area, before he was rushed to an undisclosed hospital for treatment and subsequently discharged.

Neighbourhood accounts indicated that the intruders first overpowered Odegbami’s domestic staff and driver upon invading the compound, beating the workers severely after noticing a running generator despite claims that the former international was not at home.

“They immediately found their way to Odegbami’s bedroom and attacked him there. Not willing to succumb easily, Odegbami resisted his attackers. They eventually fled the scene, leaving him with deep machete cuts and bleeding heavily,” a resident said on condition of anonymity.

Confirming the incident and Odegbami’s discharge on Friday, Ogun State Police Command spokesperson DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi stated that Commissioner of Police Bode Ojajuni visited the football icon to sympathise with him and ordered an immediate manhunt to apprehend the culprits.

“The command is leaving no stone unturned in addressing the incident. The Commissioner of Police immediately ordered a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding it, with intensive efforts ongoing to identify and apprehend those responsible. We can also confirm that Chief Segun Odegbami has been discharged from the hospital,” Babaseyi said.

While the motive behind the attack had yet to be established as of the time of filing this report, the police appealed to residents to remain calm and provide credible information through established channels to aid the ongoing investigation.

Odegbami played a pivotal role in Nigeria’s squad that won the country’s first Africa Cup of Nations title on home soil in 1980, scoring three goals to finish as joint top scorer, and also helped Shooting Stars of Ibadan lift the African Cup Winners’ Cup in 1976.

title: Ekiti youths get grants to drive economy
description:
At least 60 youths in Ekiti State have received grants of N100,000 each, while 40 others secured internship opportunities with multinational organisations at a summit aimed at promoting youth entrepreneurship, wealth creation and economic development.
The beneficiaries emerged at the maiden Ekiti Yo
content:
At least 60 youths in Ekiti State have received grants of N100,000 each, while 40 others secured internship opportunities with multinational organisations at a summit aimed at promoting youth entrepreneurship, wealth creation and economic development.

The beneficiaries emerged at the maiden Ekiti Youth Summit, organised by Ekiti Like Minds in Ado Ekiti on Thursday, where speakers challenged young people to harness their intellectual abilities, creativity and entrepreneurial ideas to create jobs and contribute to the state’s economic growth.

Speakers urged youths to end dependence on politicians for short-term financial gains and instead position themselves as innovators, business founders, entrepreneurs and wealth creators.

Keynote speaker Mayowa Ekundayo, an agripreneur, who spoke on the theme “Beyond the Stereotype: Transforming Knowledge into Economic Prosperity,” said Ekiti had vast untapped economic opportunities that young people could harness to create wealth and drive development.

Ekundayo described the state as an investment haven, identifying agriculture, tourism, entertainment, technology, real estate, mining, manufacturing and the creative economy as sectors offering major opportunities for young entrepreneurs.

He, however, urged the state government to address infrastructure challenges, particularly electricity and transportation, while ensuring transparent access to grants and institutional support for entrepreneurs.

The Chairman of the Planning Committee for the summit, Tiwa Omope, said the event was designed to give young people a platform to take ownership of their future and contribute meaningfully to the state’s economic transformation.

Omope, who described the gathering as the beginning of a movement rather than a one-off event, said the summit would become an annual programme to inspire, connect and empower young people across Ekiti.

“The initiative is driven by the conviction that youths deserve more than political rhetoric. There is the need to create opportunities that will enable them to translate their potentials into measurable achievements,” he said.

Omope said Ekiti must move beyond its reputation as the Fountain of Knowledge by turning its pool of educated and intellectually gifted people into wealth creation, employment and sustainable enterprises.

The Senior Special Assistant to the President on Students Engagement, Sunday Asefon, urged young people in the state to embrace equity, believe in their potential and seize available opportunities to shape Ekiti’s future.

The post Ekiti youths get grants to drive economy appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Davido’s wedding shot me into limelight  — Cinematographer, Durode Akintante
description: The Chief Executive Officer of Duro Weddings and lifestyle cinematographer, Durode Akintante, speaks with DAMOLA ADEDIGBA about his journey into content creation, the wedding that brought his brand into the spotlight and the evolving business of wedding storytelling. He has 186,000 followers on Inst
content:
The Chief Executive Officer of Duro Weddings and lifestyle cinematographer, Durode Akintante, speaks with DAMOLA ADEDIGBA about his journey into content creation, the wedding that brought his brand into the spotlight and the evolving business of wedding storytelling. He has 186,000 followers on Instagram

Can you take us back to the beginning of Duro Weddings? What inspired you to start the brand?

Duro Weddings didn’t start as a wedding content page. It started with a guy who enjoyed making videos of his friends in school with his phone. There was always that one person in a class who liked taking pictures and keeping people’s throwback moments. I was that person. I would take pictures of people, keep them and show them the following semester.

So, documenting people has always been a part of me. Later, when I started attending House on the Rock in Asaba, Delta State, I joined the church media team. That was where my love for content creation really grew because I was constantly creating content for the church.

People began to know me as the person making sure the church was visible online. The creative content we produced also made people take an interest in the church’s social media platforms. Through that, I met some friends who were in the wedding industry.

It started with creating behind-the-scenes content for them whenever they had shows or weddings. At some point, they encouraged me to start doing it professionally, even if it meant charging a small fee.

At the time, I was also a civil servant, so balancing both became difficult because they were demanding. Eventually, when it became clear that content creation was the direction I wanted to take, I left the civil service to focus fully on it.

How would you describe the journey so far?

It has really been from school to church and then to weddings. Church, in particular, taught me resilience and confidence. When you are creating content in church, you have to move around the congregation and interact with different people, so it naturally builds confidence.

It also taught me speed. If you attend the first service, for instance, the content has to be ready before the second service. That experience helped develop the fast turnaround that later became part of the Duro Weddings brand.

Why did you choose wedding spaces for your content?

When I looked at the wedding content available online, I noticed that most of it focused on Lagos weddings. Being based in Asaba made me realise that weddings in the East were not getting enough visibility online.

That made me think, “Why not try something different?” The goal was to consistently document weddings in the East and give them the visibility they deserved.

Benin, for example, already had people documenting weddings, but the quality and consistency of the content were not quite where they are today. I also noticed that couples wanted their content delivered quickly. So, fast delivery became another gap we wanted to address.

With consistent content, good storytelling and a fast turnaround, the brand gradually started getting more bookings, including from Lagos. That was how Duro Weddings developed before eventually moving to Lagos.

Which events brought Duro Weddings into the spotlight?

There have been several events, and it feels more like a ladder because each one opened the door to the next. I remember the first wedding featured by BellaNaija on my page. It was an event in the East, and from there, things started moving upwards.

Then came Davido’s wedding, which was one of the major events that pushed the brand into the spotlight. That event alone brought about 30,000 followers, making it a significant turning point for Duro Weddings.

What makes Duro Weddings different from others?

I feel every brand has something unique that makes people connect with it, and that uniqueness can change over time. At the beginning, what stood out about Duro Weddings was the speed of our delivery. With time, people began to realise that Duro Weddings could connect with a couple’s story.

It is not just about capturing the outfits, makeup or beautiful locations. The goal is to go deeper into the couple’s love story and make people feel what brought them together. That is what we try to achieve. We want the videos and the overall experience to feel like real love because that is the foundation of the wedding in the first place.

How do you use lifestyle cinematography to tell a couple’s story?

The world has changed over time. In the past, wedding videography was more about taking your time to document almost everything.

Now, we are in the content age, where attention spans are shorter, and people want to be entertained while watching. So, it is important to make the content lively and introduce a lifestyle element into it.

Lifestyle cinematography allows the story to feel more natural, relatable and engaging, rather than simply documenting what happened at the wedding.

What is the biggest challenge you face when covering a wedding?

The biggest challenge is the number of content creators involved in weddings today. A bride may book one content creator, but by the time you get to the wedding, there could be several others covering the same event. Sometimes, it becomes overwhelming for the couple.

For instance, when there are fewer creators, the bride can trust you to properly capture her love story. But when there are too many people around her, she can begin to feel anxious, and the whole experience can start looking more like a fashion shoot than a wedding. We meet different people who have been booked for different aspects of the wedding, and sometimes managing all of that as a creator can be challenging.

What are some of the biggest mistakes couples make when choosing a wedding content creator?

There are different types of content creators, and many specialise in particular aspects of wedding content.

The mistake some couples make is booking a creator without first understanding what that person actually does. For example, a creator may be very good at showcasing bridal outfits, but the couple may expect that person to also capture the event highlights, the venue and the entire wedding experience.

So, before booking a content creator, couples need to study the person’s page and previous work. If you want to buy something, you look at what the brand has done before. The same thing applies here. Understanding a creator’s style beforehand helps couples know exactly what they are getting and prevents unnecessary pressure or disappointment on the wedding day.

How do you balance trends on TikTok and Instagram with creating timeless wedding memories that couples can still appreciate years later?

When creating wedding content, there are so many people to satisfy. There are the couple, the vendors, makeup artist, the stylist, planner, hairstylist and, of course, the audience watching online.

The goal, therefore, is to create content that different people can appreciate. For the bride, the focus may be on telling her story because that is something she will continue to value years later. At the same time, there can be fashion content for those interested in the looks and lifestyle content for people who enjoy that style.

So, it is really about finding a balance and making sure everybody gets to see themselves in the content. That way, the content can remain trendy while preserving the memories that matter.

We are in the age of AI. How do you embrace new technologies while maintaining creativity in your work?

AI can create things like birthday shoots, visuals and even entire productions. However, when it comes to real-life experiences, there is still a difference.

A wedding is an experience that happens live and cannot easily be recreated. AI cannot decide that a mother should suddenly cry or that a father should react in a particular way. Those spontaneous human moments are difficult to replicate.

Perhaps that may change in the future, but for now, the wedding space remains largely about real human experiences. Fashion shoots and visual concepts may be influenced by AI, but the actual wedding experience, with all its emotions and unexpected moments, cannot be completely replaced.

How do you manage the pressure of working on someone’s most important day?

When a couple books Duro Weddings, there is already a level of trust. They have seen the brand’s work and chosen it because they believe in what we do. That trust makes the process easier because it gives us creative freedom. We have been fortunate that most of our couples trust our creative direction.

From the consultation stage to the morning of the wedding and throughout the event, they give us the freedom to create. Knowing that they trust the brand makes it easier to relax, be creative and deliver the best possible work.

The Nigerian wedding industry has become expensive. How can couples get quality visual content without exceeding their budgets?

Couples need to do their research. It is similar to buying a phone. If you have the budget for an iPhone 15 Pro Max, you can go for it. But if that is beyond your budget, there are other options that can still meet your needs. The same thing applies to wedding content. Couples can research different creators and find those whose services fit their budgets. A wedding planner can also help with the research and recommend creators based on what the couple can afford.

However, if there is a particular brand whose work you genuinely love and you have the means to afford it, you can decide to go all out for that creator.

Ultimately, it comes down to understanding your budget, researching your options and choosing what works best for you.

As CEO, what has running Duro Weddings taught you about leadership, building a creative team and dealing with clients?

One thing running a team has taught me is that you have to treat it like a company.

When you work with people, you have to understand that their journey with you may not be permanent. It could be a three-month, six-month, one-year or two-year cycle. At some point, a team member may decide that it is time to leave and build something of their own. That can be a difficult reality to accept, but it is something you have to understand when working with people. You cannot always expect someone to remain with the company forever.

That is one of the biggest lessons leadership has taught me, both the hard way and the soft way. When it comes to clients, the experience has also taught me the importance of communication, trust and understanding what people expect from the brand.

Looking ahead, where do you see Duro Weddings in the next five years?

In the next five years, Duro Weddings should be a brand that not only caters to weddings in Nigeria but also covers weddings across Africa, Europe, America and other parts of the world.

The goal is to get to a point where the brand can experience and document different cultures, not just Nigerian culture.

More importantly, Duro Weddings should become a brand people can relate to. A brand where you watch the videos and think, “I want to get married.” A brand that makes people want to take themselves seriously, prepare for marriage and experience something beautiful of their own.

What should your audience and clients expect from the brand?

More amazing stories, more experiences and, ultimately, a brand that continues to expand across borders.

What advice do you have for upcoming content creators?

The best advice is not to take every piece of advice you receive. Sometimes, things are done a certain way simply because that is how everyone has always done them. But when you come into the industry, it does not mean you have to follow the same path.

Be that rebellious person who says, “I don’t want to do it the way everybody else does it. I want to try something different.” People thrive when they are different. So, be different, understand your craft and be daring enough to try new things.

The post Davido’s wedding shot me into limelight — Cinematographer, Durode Akintante appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Arsenal can win back-to-back titles – African China
description:
Veteran Nigerian artiste, Chinagorom Onuoha, popularly known as African China, reflects on the business evolution of Nigerian music, his favourite club, love for Osimhen and more in this interview with PETER AKINBO
Growing up, what sport did you enjoy?
Growing up, like most young kids across Nigeria
content:
Veteran Nigerian artiste, Chinagorom Onuoha, popularly known as African China, reflects on the business evolution of Nigerian music, his favourite club, love for Osimhen and more in this interview with PETER AKINBO

Growing up, what sport did you enjoy?

Growing up, like most young kids across Nigeria, I enjoyed and still enjoy football. I love playing football. I also represented my secondary school in a relay race once, but it obviously was not my calling, as I loved music a lot.

Did your parents ever discourage you from pursuing a career in sports?

They did not need to discourage me because I did not take up any sport as a career.

Were you passionate about football growing up?

I was back then, but not any more, even if I still play once in a while. I became a football lover in the late 1980s, watching Nigerian national teams.

What club do you support?

I support Arsenal.

What do you think of Arsenal’s season so far?

They have been doing well, but they lose games their fans least expect, just like the game against Brighton. I am happy now that we won that league last season, though, and I believe Arsenal stands a good chance of winning the EPL this season again if they can maintain a good league form. I see Liverpool and Manchester City losing more grounds.

If you could spend a day with any sportsperson, who would it be?

Currently, Victor Osimhen.

Who do you think is the Greatest Footballer of all Time?

That is a tough question, but if I am to pick one, I will take Pele.

If any of your children show an interest in sports, would you encourage them?

Of course, yes, it is the right thing to do.

Who do you think is the best African player of all time?

I know some will argue that I might be choosing him because he is Nigerian. Some will say he did not win much during his time playing, but I choose Austin ‘Jay-Jay’ Okocha any time, any day. To me, he is the most naturally skilled footballer I have ever seen.

You became known for songs that spoke directly about Nigerian crises and everyday realities. Looking back at what inspired those songs then, what was the goal?

Those songs were meant to call the attention of Nigerians to stop and reflect—it was more like a wake-up call. In *Crisis*, if you remember, I sang, *”Make we no let this country to fall inside well.” Back then, many people were just dancing to the rhythm without paying close attention to the deeper warning in the message.

What kind of songs do you find yourself listening to today?

Funny enough, I do not really follow many of the newer tracks on my own playlist. Many artists today rely heavily on street slang and lamba, and once that slang fades out, the song fades with it. Conscious music, on the other hand, grows with the listener because it is evergreen. There are still a few young artists who send me their songs, and I am blown away by their talent. Some tracks have great rhythm, though I personally still lean toward music with stronger lyrical substance.

Looking at the new generation of Nigerian artists, what is something they understand about the industry better than the older generation did?

They understand the business side of music, and I really applaud them for that. They took the business from point A to a much safer, more lucrative place. While technology and time naturally improved production, they really stepped up the business structure. When we started, we did it purely for the love of the craft—there was barely any money, just the joy of hearing people call your name on the street.

How much has the public perception of being a musician changed since your early days?

Tremendously. Back then, there was heavy stigma around being a musician; sensible families did not even want their children marrying one because society saw artistes as people without real jobs. Today, entertainment has become one of the highest-paying industries in the country, creating jobs for lawyers, personal assistants, managers, and stage managers, and musicians are respected. Even when we critique lyrics, we still applaud how far they have taken the business.

Looking back at your catalogue, which song gives you the most nostalgia?

Because I am the writer, all my songs give me nostalgia. For the fans, it is usually Crisis. That was my first song and the one that brought African China out—hearing that intro and feeling the crowd’s energy always brings back memories. And then Mr President, with the cock crowing; it was meant to be a wake-up call, just like a rooster crowing at dawn.

The post Arsenal can win back-to-back titles – African China appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Olalere urges NSC to replicate judo success in gymnastics
description: Chairperson of the Lagos State Gymnastics Association, Omowunmi Olalere, has urged the National Sports Commission to replicate the decisive intervention that produced a peaceful judo election by resolving lingering leadership and electoral disputes in the Gymnastics Federation of Nigeria, Saturday P
content:
Chairperson of the Lagos State Gymnastics Association, Omowunmi Olalere, has urged the National Sports Commission to replicate the decisive intervention that produced a peaceful judo election by resolving lingering leadership and electoral disputes in the Gymnastics Federation of Nigeria, Saturday PUNCH reports.

In a statement issued on Friday, Olalere congratulated the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, on his unanimous election as President of the Nigeria Judo Federation on Thursday, November 19, while calling on sports authorities to extend the same institutional commitment to gymnastics.

Disu, a third-dan black belt holder who began his judo career in 1986 and won silver at the 33rd US Open Judo Championship in July 2022, polled all 13 votes at the National Elective Congress in Abuja organised by the Sheriff Hammed-led Caretaker Committee.

Olalere described Disu’s emergence as a welcome milestone for Nigerian sports administration and an opportunity to strengthen judo’s institutional structure for greater national and international recognition, while commending NSC Chairman Shehu Dikko, Director-General Bukola Olopade and Hammed for delivering a credible transition.

“Special commendation goes to the Director General of the National Sports Commission, Bukola Olopade, for the leadership, determination and administrative commitment demonstrated in ensuring that the judo process was successfully concluded. This is the kind of purposeful intervention that gives stakeholders confidence in sports governance,” she stated.

Turning to gymnastics, Olalere stressed that the sport holds enormous potential for Nigeria across Olympic medal opportunities, early talent identification, youth development, international recognition, women and girls’ participation, grassroots and school sports, employment for coaches and judges, as well as sports tourism and investment.

“Having successfully navigated the judo process, I sincerely hope that the Commission will now turn its attention to the outstanding leadership and electoral issues in the Gymnastics Federation of Nigeria. Gymnastics deserves the same institutional commitment, fairness and decisive leadership,” she told our correspondent.

She warned that gymnastics does not need prolonged leadership disagreements, intimidation or division, appealing directly to Dikko and Olopade to conduct a transparent and legitimate election that puts athletes and the future of the sport ahead of individual interests.

“If we can successfully deliver judo, we can also deliver gymnastics. The ultimate beneficiaries must be Nigerian athletes, young talents and the future of our sports industry, not individual interests or positions,” Olalere added.

The post Olalere urges NSC to replicate judo success in gymnastics appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: TheCable founder set to release 2023 election book
description:
The founder of TheCable, Simon Kolawole, is set to release a new book chronicling the intrigues and political manoeuvres behind the 2023 presidential election.
The publishers, in a statement made available to Saturday PUNCH on Friday, said the 296-page book, titled Winning Formula: The Inside Story
content:
The founder of TheCable, Simon Kolawole, is set to release a new book chronicling the intrigues and political manoeuvres behind the 2023 presidential election.

The publishers, in a statement made available to Saturday PUNCH on Friday, said the 296-page book, titled Winning Formula: The Inside Story of Nigeria’s 2023 Presidential Election, would go on sale nationwide from Monday.

According to the publishers, the book draws on insider briefings, court filings and polling data to provide an account of the election and the events that preceded it.

Published by Cable Books and distributed by Rovingheights Bookstore, the book examines the political calculations, alliances and rivalries that shaped the election, which produced President Bola Tinubu as winner.

Kolawole said the book examined how Tinubu outmanoeuvred former President Muhammadu Buhari, how the rivalry between ex-Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and immediate past Rivers State governor Nyesom Wike affected their presidential ambitions, and how Peter Obi and the Obidient movement emerged as major forces in the election.

The author said the book also examined voting patterns that have determined presidential election winners since 1999, the controversy surrounding the Muslim-Muslim ticket and how former Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo lost out in the succession struggle.

Describing the book as a combination of political history, electoral analysis and behind-the-scenes accounts, Kolawole said it explored the political calculations and power struggles that shaped the outcome of the 2023 election.

“The 2023 presidential election was the most contested and the most controversial in a generation, four candidates polling over a million votes each, a technology glitch that froze the country in real time, and a thrilling court battle that generated global headlines as three candidates lay claim to victory,” he said.

“At the heart of the book, distributed nationwide by Rovingheights Bookstore, is a fascinating argument, in the Fourth Republic, no candidate has reached the presidency without building a competitive coalition across at least two of Nigeria’s three largest voting blocs the Hausa-Fulani, the Igbo, and the Yoruba as well as adding decisive support from a minority geo-political zone.”

title: Manufacturers, frozen food dealers groan as blackouts persist
description:
Manufacturers, cold-room operators and frozen food dealers are counting losses as persistent power outages force businesses to rely on generators, raising operating costs and threatening their survival.
Findings by Saturday PUNCH show that prolonged blackouts in parts of the country have compelled m
content:
Manufacturers, cold-room operators and frozen food dealers are counting losses as persistent power outages force businesses to rely on generators, raising operating costs and threatening their survival.

Findings by Saturday PUNCH show that prolonged blackouts in parts of the country have compelled many small and medium-scale enterprises to spend heavily on diesel and petrol to keep running.

Frozen food operators who spoke with Saturday PUNCH also lamented that inadequate electricity had caused the spoilage of goods worth millions of naira.

According to data obtained from nationalgrid.ng on Thursday evening, the country generated 257.2MW, representing an 89.1 per cent drop.

Businesses count losses

An official of a beverage manufacturing company in the Agbara industrial area of Ogun State, Femi Adeagbo, told Saturday PUNCH on condition of anonymity that persistent electricity disruptions had cut the company’s daily production capacity by about 40 per cent while sharply raising operating costs.

He said the Ibadan Electricity Distribution Company promised companies in the industrial zone between 20 and 22 hours of electricity daily, but they currently received less than 10 hours of supply.

He lamented that the situation had forced many companies to rely on gas-powered systems and diesel generators to keep production lines running.

He added that many companies along the axis were struggling to meet production targets because of unreliable electricity supply.

He explained that the disruptions had reduced his company’s daily output from an expected 10,000 cases of beverages to about 6,000 cases.

“It has had a major impact on our operations. No company can survive under the current state of Nigeria’s power system unless urgent steps are taken to address the challenges,” he said.

He disclosed that the company spent about N130m monthly on energy, while diesel expenditure alone stood at between N16m and N20m monthly for weekend operations.

“When we operate on gas from Monday to Friday and switch to diesel during the weekends, we spend between N8m and N10m on diesel weekly. That amounts to approximately N16m to N20m monthly on diesel for weekend operations alone.

“We have not even factored in what we would spend if we had to rely on diesel during the weekdays. The cost would certainly be much higher,” he added.

He said the added energy costs, equipment maintenance and lower production output had squeezed expected profit margins.

He added that the company was considering further diversification into solar energy to reduce reliance on the national grid, noting that some major manufacturers, including Nigerian Breweries and Seven-Up, were also exploring alternative energy sources.

A cold-room manager at Olomore Market, Abeokuta, Ogun State, Odedina Olaide, told Saturday PUNCH that operators had struggled to stay afloat since September when electricity supply worsened.

She said her business spent at least N218,400 daily on diesel to buy about 120 litres at N1,820 per litre.

She disclosed that the cold-room had spent more than N10m on diesel over the past two months, yet generators could not match the freezing achieved with regular electricity.

“The amount we spend on diesel daily is enormous, not to talk of the monthly cost. We buy at least 120 litres of diesel every day at the rate of N1,820 per litre,” she said.

“In the last two months, we have spent more than N10m on diesel to power our cold-room.

“Even if we run the generator for five hours, the frozen items will not be as properly frozen as they would be with one hour of electricity supply.”

She said the situation had also caused the loss of frozen food worth millions of naira, adding that some customers had returned goods because they could not preserve them properly with their refrigeration facilities.

She disclosed that the cold-room discarded frozen food worth N750,000 in September and another N550,000 in October because of inadequate power supply.

According to her, generators have failed to prevent further losses because they lack the capacity to freeze all items properly, while frozen products defrost faster when generators are switched off.

A frozen food dealer in Osogbo, Osun State, Bakare Ayodeji, also lamented that the situation had exposed businesses to heavy financial risks, especially when power failed for several consecutive hours.

“We cannot afford to leave our generators off because the goods in our cold-rooms will begin to defrost. At the same time, running generators continuously is becoming too expensive,” he said.

“We spend money buying fuel, servicing generators and repairing equipment. Even with all these expenses, we sometimes lose goods because the generators cannot maintain the required temperature. It is frustrating because we are spending more but making less profit.”

An operator of a poultry processing business in Ibadan, Oyo State, Somide Koya, said the cost of alternative power had become a major threat to the survival of small enterprises.

“We are practically working to buy fuel. Whatever profit we make goes back into keeping the business running. We cannot increase our prices every week because customers will stop patronising us,” he said.

“Unlike big companies, we don’t have enough capital to sustain this kind of expenditure. Some small businesses are already borrowing money to keep their operations running. If electricity supply does not improve, many operators may not survive.”

Another frozen food dealer, Badmos Suliat, decried the irregular power supply, saying it had hurt sales and discouraged bulk buying.

“Before now, customers could buy frozen chicken and fish in large quantities because they were confident that we could preserve them. But now, some of them prefer to buy small quantities because they are not sure we can keep the products frozen,” she said.

“Sometimes, we have to sell goods quickly at reduced prices when we notice that they are beginning to defrost. If we fail to do that, we risk losing the entire stock. It is a serious challenge because frozen food is not something you can keep without electricity.”

Power deficit threatens businesses

The Director-General of the Nigerian Association of Chambers of Commerce, Industry, Mines and Agriculture, Olusola Obadimu, warned that Nigeria would not achieve industrialisation with its current power generation capacity.

He said electricity generation of between 3,000 and 4,000 megawatts was grossly inadequate for a population of over 200 million people.

According to him, the country required at least 150,000 megawatts to industrialise, noting that South Africa, with a smaller population, generated significantly more electricity but still faced shortages.

“If we want to truly industrialise the country, we should be talking in the range of 150,000 megawatts. But because we are a domestic usage economy, people are just trying to solve their problems with whatever solar facility they can afford,” he said.

“It is a basic challenge for industry. Manufacturers are trying their best to cope, but at what price? They have to pass it on to the consumer. All these things have an inflationary effect on consumption.”

He said the country needed fundamental reforms across power generation, transmission and distribution, stressing that generated power must be effectively transmitted and distributed to consumers.

The immediate past President of the Nigerian Economic Society, Prof Adeola Adenikinju, said prolonged power outages had sharply raised operating costs for businesses, especially those relying on electricity for production and preservation.

He explained that grid electricity remained the cheapest option for most businesses, but poor supply had forced operators onto costlier alternatives such as diesel generators and solar systems.

According to him, the extra expenses would eventually push up prices of goods and services while cutting business profitability.

“If they are not careful, some of them may have to run at a loss. The prolonged outage must have impacted significantly on the bottom line of most of these businesses,” he said.

He estimated that businesses nationwide could be losing hundreds of millions, if not billions, of naira daily to poor electricity supply and generator operating costs.

He warned that small businesses already hit by inflation, high interest rates and weak consumer purchasing power were especially vulnerable.

“Some of them are already struggling to survive. When you layer power on it, they are just struggling to survive. They must be bleeding by now, particularly small-scale businesses that don’t have alternatives,” he said.

DisCos blame low tariffs

The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Association of Nigerian Electricity Distributors, Sunday Oduntan, said Nigeria needed more investment in power generation and distribution to tackle persistent supply shortfalls.

He said a country with an estimated population of 237 million people could not keep relying on power generation of about 5,500 megawatts.

Oduntan blamed part of the problem on energy theft and weak willingness by some consumers to pay for electricity, arguing that the sector needed sufficient revenue to sustain operations.

“No economy can grow in the dark. No economy can industrialise in the dark. Electricity is very essential to industrialisation.

“We just need to invest more, do more and bring in more foreign investors. Investors will not come if you cannot assure them of cost recovery,” he said.

The DisCos spokesperson noted that power sector improvements would take time, adding that the government and stakeholders needed to address challenges across generation, transmission and distribution.

He also urged state governments to use the amended Electricity Act 2023, which allows them to generate, transmit and distribute electricity within their jurisdictions.

According to him, only a few states, including Lagos, Abia and Enugu, have taken major steps towards developing their electricity markets.

Oduntan also defended cost-reflective electricity pricing, arguing that any gap between production cost and approved selling price must be borne by someone.

He said without adequate funding and cost recovery, electricity distribution companies would struggle to deliver reliable service.

title: There are boundaries I won’t cross – Lola Fany
description:

Speaking in an interview with Saturday Beats, she said, “I think one can be creative without doing everything for attention. Of course, I want my content to do well, but there are boundaries I
content:
Content creator and actress Lola Fany has revealed the boundaries she would not cross in creating content.

Speaking in an interview with Saturday Beats, she said, “I think one can be creative without doing everything for attention. Of course, I want my content to do well, but there are boundaries I won’t cross. Not every viral moment is worth it. I draw the line when something goes against my values or makes me uncomfortable.”

Fany also discussed how she handles male fans who mistake admiration for entitlement to her personal attention.

“Some people genuinely admire you, while others feel that because they support you, they’re entitled to your attention. And for me, those are two different things. I’m very appreciative of those that support me, but I also know that I can’t please everybody. If someone crosses the line, I don’t feel obligated to entertain them just to avoid hurting their feelings. I believe one can be nice to people and still stand one’s ground,” she said.

Fany also spoke about the inspiration behind her skit, ‘How to Keep a Man’, which generated more than 3,000 comments and several reshares on social media.

“Honestly, I’ve heard a lot of stories about traditional women who would go to any length to keep their men and impress their in-laws, so I found it quite interesting because, even though some people see it as being male-centred, others see it as a woman doing what she can to keep her home. So I felt, why not turn some of these things into comedy? That’s really where the idea came from.”

The post There are boundaries I won’t cross – Lola Fany appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Osimhen ready to listen to United offers
description:
Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen is ready to listen to offers from Manchester United after the Premier League club renewed their interest in signing him to bolster their struggling attack, PUNCH Sports Extra reports.
According to UK publication SunSport, the Galatasaray forward is flattered by th
content:
Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen is ready to listen to offers from Manchester United after the Premier League club renewed their interest in signing him to bolster their struggling attack, PUNCH Sports Extra reports.

According to UK publication SunSport, the Galatasaray forward is flattered by the fresh links to Old Trafford and remains keen on fulfilling his dream of playing in the English top flight.

The 27-year-old has been in prolific form for the Turkish champions this season, netting 10 goals in 11 appearances across all competitions after hitting 37 goals in his debut campaign and 22 last term.

His output dwarfs that of United’s current strikers, with Joshua Zirkzee scoring two goals in 10 games and Benjamin Sesko managing two in six, leaving the pair with just four goals combined from 16 outings.

A source close to the player confirmed his openness to a move while noting that Galatasaray’s stance will be decisive.

“Of course the interest really flatters him, but he’s a loyal guy, so it will be up to United to move hard for him. Victor will score goals everywhere he goes, and he’s proven that, but it’s really up to the two clubs,” the source said.

New United manager Mauricio Pochettino, who replaced Michael Carrick last week after the Red Devils won just one of their opening 10 league matches, is eager to sign an established centre-forward ahead of a difficult battle away from the relegation zone.

However, Osimhen is tied to Galatasaray until June 2029 on a reported £13m-a-year deal with no release clause, meaning United may have to meet a valuation of between £80m and £100m, or wait until next summer if a January transfer proves too difficult.

The post Osimhen ready to listen to United offers appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has pledged to improve on his first-term performance, assuring residents that he would not disappoint them during his second term.

Adeleke gave the assurance on Friday during a Jumu’at prayer at the Osogbo Central Mosque, marking the commencement of activities for his second-term inauguration scheduled for November 27.

The governor, who was represented by his deputy, Kola Adewusi, said his administration would continue to prioritise the welfare of residents, particularly workers and other vulnerable segments of the society.

According to a statement by his spokesperson, Olawale Rasheed, Adeleke recalled the struggles to sustain democracy in the state, pledging to keep the people’s interests at the centre of governance.

He commended residents for their steadfastness, perseverance and support during the electioneering period, describing Osun as a national symbol of people’s power and democratic participation.

“I won’t disappoint Osun people. I will deliver even more than my first term. I am hopeful our financial situation will soon improve with the expected resolution of the local government crisis. We will take good care of workers and all segments of the society,” he was quoted to have said.

Earlier, the Deputy Imam of the Osogbo Central Mosque, Sheikh Moruf Ishola, described the August 15 governorship election as unprecedented, saying its outcome defied political calculations.

Ishola urged Adeleke not to abandon God and the people, advising him to govern with the fear of God, fulfil his promises and prioritise public interests.

title: Adesanya targets UFC revival with greatest weapon
description:
Former two-time UFC middleweight champion, Israel Adesanya, says he will go back to using his mind, which he calls his greatest weapon, as he looks to end a four-fight losing streak.
Adesanya returns against Shara Magomedov in the main event of UFC Saudi Arabia at The Venue in Riyadh on Saturday, De
content:
Former two-time UFC middleweight champion, Israel Adesanya, says he will go back to using his mind, which he calls his greatest weapon, as he looks to end a four-fight losing streak.

Adesanya returns against Shara Magomedov in the main event of UFC Saudi Arabia at The Venue in Riyadh on Saturday, December 5. It is the first four-fight losing streak of his career, and he has not won since knocking out Alex Pereira in their April 2023 rematch. He then lost his title to Sean Strickland and suffered consecutive stoppage defeats to Dricus du Plessis, Nassourdine Imavov and Joe Pyfer.

The 37-year-old believes the slump began when he stopped fighting like himself. Speaking on his YouTube channel, he said he spent recent fights trying to prove he had knockout power, a response to critics from his kickboxing days who called him too skinny to hit hard.

“I wanted to prove through many fights that I could knock people out and that I had power because, earlier in my career during my kickboxing days, they said I was too skinny and didn’t have any power,” Adesanya said.

“But then I got into this thing where I wanted to get jacked and just flatline dudes to prove how rugged I am. I didn’t have to. My (thing) is stylebending — hit and not get hit.”

Adesanya was known throughout his reign for his fight IQ, his mid-fight adjustments and his ability to control opponents from range. That patient approach disappeared during the losing run, and he now questions why he felt the need to prove his toughness.

“I was trying to prove that I’m tough. I don’t need to prove that I’m tough, but I don’t really know why I thought that. I need to dive deeper into my psyche on this one. Did I let them get to me?” he said.

He added that he must be “the smartest guy in the game, the most cunning guy” again, and outthink opponents instead of matching their physicality. “I just need to outsmart these fools because I can beat them all — but not at being tough because a lot of them are built tough.”

“I’m tough when I need to be, but this (my mind) is my greatest weapon. I stopped using it and made the dumbest decisions in my fights. I don’t regret it, but I’ve learned from it,” Adesanya said.

The former champion has assembled a new team for this camp after spending almost his entire UFC career at City Kickboxing, and the change appears to have helped him enjoy training again. He also believes his close friend, Alexander Volkanovski, has shown that an older former champion can still turn back the clock.

Magomedov, nicknamed “Shara Bullet”, is a creative and dangerous striker who is likely to trade at range rather than build his game plan around wrestling. That should give Adesanya the chance to return to his preferred style in Riyadh.

The post Adesanya targets UFC revival with greatest weapon appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
