title: Four Nigerian students win award
description:
Four Nigerian students have earned global recognition after developing an innovative solution to water pollution by converting invasive water hyacinth into biodegradable packaging materials as alternatives to plastic bags.
The students, representing Destiny Christian Academy, Abuja, placed second in
content:
Four Nigerian students have earned global recognition after developing an innovative solution to water pollution by converting invasive water hyacinth into biodegradable packaging materials as alternatives to plastic bags.

The students, representing Destiny Christian Academy, Abuja, placed second in the Middle Division category of the Future Problem Solving World Solutions Challenge, an international academic competition involving schools from six continents, nine countries and 13 American states.

Their project, titled “Menace to Money: Wealth in Water Hyacinth”, proposed turning water hyacinth, which clogs waterways in Nigeria, into useful packaging materials while creating employment and income-generating opportunities for local communities.

The school’s administrator, Paul Onoja, disclosed the achievement while speaking with journalists in Abuja on Thursday, saying the institution was determined to win first place in future editions of the competition.

Onoja said the school scored over 93 per cent, narrowly missing the top spot despite competing against institutions from countries with access to advanced technology.

“You can imagine a school from Africa, where it is believed we are disadvantaged, proving to the world that we are not disadvantaged.

“The competition, as it is globally recognised, had given us the best platform to scale and compete amongst other leagues of institutions around the world,” he said.

He added that the school had identified areas requiring improvement and was already preparing for its next international outing.

“We are not preparing for second; we are preparing for the first position. I believe the second outing is going to be not just first position, but it’s going to be with a reasonable gap that even the person who will come next to us will not be close,” he said.

Onoja said the achievement reflected the institution’s commitment to academic excellence and the vision of its founders, the Senior Pastors of Dunamis International Gospel Centre, Dr Paul Enenche and his wife, Dr Becky Enenche, who established the school in 2005.

He said: “Like the Senior Pastor would always say, ‘You live ready.’ That is part of our principle. We live ready. You can call up any of our students for anything as he stands right now, and he will engage any competition globally.”

The administrator described the academy as an institution focused on developing children’s intellectual, spiritual, emotional and physical capacities to prepare them for life.

He disclosed that the school had participated consistently in international competitions, including events in South Africa, over the past four years.

Onoja added that the institution was preparing to represent Nigeria at a global robotics and engineering competition in Asia later this year.

The academy was represented in the competition by four students—Amos, Bamidele, Chukwura and Grace—who competed as the “DCA All-Stars”.

New Zealand’s Dilworth School placed first in the Middle Division category, while J. M. Robinson Middle School, North Carolina, United States, placed third.

The post Four Nigerian students win award appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: I turned nine-year university delay into  research, professional growth – AAU graduate
description:
After nine years at Ambrose Alli University, Success Owolabi graduated with a CGPA of 4.71/5.00 despite academic setbacks and personal loss. The first class graduate speaks with TEMITOPE ADETUNJI about his journey and academic achievement
What inspired you to study Medical Laboratory Science?
It was
content:
After nine years at Ambrose Alli University, Success Owolabi graduated with a CGPA of 4.71/5.00 despite academic setbacks and personal loss. The first class graduate speaks with TEMITOPE ADETUNJI about his journey and academic achievement

What inspired you to study Medical Laboratory Science?

It was inspired by my early fascination with medicine and the treatment of diseases. Growing up, I was exposed to the healthcare environment through my mother, who was a nurse. Watching her care for patients and contribute to their recovery naturally sparked my interest in the medical profession. She had always hoped I would become a medical doctor, but at the time, I was looking for a career in healthcare that would require a relatively shorter period of study. This led me to choose Medical Laboratory Science.

Interestingly, what I initially considered an alternative gradually became a passion of its own. I developed a deeper appreciation for the role of laboratory investigations in disease diagnosis, treatment monitoring and patient management. Although I had anticipated a shorter academic journey, I ended up spending nine years at the university.

Looking back, the journey was longer than I imagined, but it gave me the opportunity to grow, develop professionally and discover how much I genuinely love the science behind disease diagnosis.

In what year did you gain admission into Ambrose Alli University?

It was in 2017, but I officially resumed academic activities in January 2018.

Your university journey lasted nine years. What accounted for the extended period?

The extended duration was largely due to administrative and regulatory delays beyond our control. The university admitted students into the programme in numbers that significantly exceeded the approved admission quota. Consequently, the indexing process was delayed, affecting our eligibility and scheduling for the professional examinations.

Because of the large number of students involved, the indexing and professional examinations were eventually conducted in batches. This process took approximately three years, from 2023 to 2026, before we could complete the necessary professional requirements and proceed to induction.

How would you describe your experience as a student?

It was a deeply emotional and challenging experience. I would not necessarily say that delay is not denial because, over the years, I watched several opportunities pass me by simply because I could not move forward at the same pace as my peers. There were moments of uncertainty, frustration and discouragement when I wondered how much longer I would have to wait.

Navigating those years required tremendous resilience, patience and determination. I had to constantly find reasons to stay motivated, keep my ambitions alive and remind myself why I started in the first place. It was not always easy to maintain the same level of enthusiasm, especially when I watched my mates progress with their careers while I was still waiting to complete my professional journey.

Ultimately, the experience taught me that resilience is not always about being strong; sometimes, it is about finding the strength to keep going even when you are emotionally exhausted. It was a difficult chapter of my life, but one that shaped my character and strengthened my resolve.

What were some of the most difficult moments you experienced while pursuing your degree?

One of the most difficult moments was losing my mother just a few weeks before the commencement of my final semester in 2023. It was an incredibly painful period because I lost someone who meant so much to me, and I was suddenly faced with the challenge of navigating my final semester while grieving.

I had to sit for my final examinations barely three months after her burial. I resumed school a little late and had already missed the mid-semester test in a particular course, Molecular Biology and Biotechnology. At that point, I was still struggling emotionally because my worst fear had happened, and finding the strength to concentrate on academics was not easy.

However, I knew my mother would have wanted me to finish strong. I had to gather myself, confront the circumstances and keep moving. Before then, I was accustomed to studying for about eight hours daily, but I increased this to approximately 10 hours to make up for lost time and stay on track.

By God’s grace, I finished that semester with a perfect 5.00/5.00 GPA, my third perfect GPA during the programme. It remains one of my most memorable academic achievements, not just because of the grade, but also because of what I had to overcome to earn it.

You maintained an impressive academic record. What helped you remain consistent academically?

Maintaining academic consistency was not always easy, but I gradually discovered how to rekindle my motivation whenever I felt exhausted or discouraged.

One of the things that kept me going was reading the Campus Champion column in Saturday PUNCH. My dad was an ardent reader of the newspaper, and I vividly remember cutting out the Campus Champion pages from his stack of newspapers and keeping them in my travelling box before resuming in January 2018. I would read about other students’ academic achievements, their stories and successes. Whenever I felt weary, those stories reminded me of what was possible and reignited my desire to achieve something similar. Much later, I started following the column online.

I was also fortunate to have mentors, particularly Dammy, whom I looked up to from as early as my 100-level days. The guidance, encouragement and practical advice I received helped me navigate the academic demands of the programme and remain focused, even when things became difficult.

Beyond these, I learnt to be intentional about my studies and disciplined with my time. I understood that motivation could fluctuate, so I had to develop the discipline to keep going, even when the excitement was no longer there.

Looking back, it was a combination of personal determination, inspiration from other people’s achievements, mentorship and, above all, the grace of God that kept me going. I am grateful that it all worked out in the end.

How did you manage the pressure of academic work during periods of uncertainty and delay?

I managed the pressure by understanding myself, developing a study routine that worked for me and finding healthy ways to unwind. Whenever things became overwhelming, I listened to spiritual songs, prayed and joked around with friends. I also made time to relax. I doubt if a day passed without me watching a movie or doing something unrelated to academics to take my mind off studying.

By 300 level, I had become more strategic with my studies. Interestingly, I became less academically intensive during my first semesters in 300 level, deliberately allowing myself more time to rest and explore income-generating opportunities. However, I knew when to draw the line and refocus. I became particularly intentional about my academics during second semesters, when I committed myself more fully to studying.

During intensive preparation periods, I aimed for a minimum of eight hours of reading daily, although I did not necessarily achieve that every day. I had my cheat days, too, when I stayed away from books, went to the gym, attended parties or travelled. I understood the importance of balancing academic commitment with having a life outside school.

I also knew I did not have a photographic memory, so I sometimes had to read a topic five or six times before fully understanding it. Rather than become discouraged, I learnt to work with my learning pace and prepare accordingly. Interestingly, from 300 level through 500 level, I recorded a perfect 5.00/5.00 GPA in every second semester. That experience taught me that academic excellence is not necessarily about studying every waking hour, but about understanding yourself, managing your priorities and knowing when to give something your absolute best.

Did you ever consider giving up on your academic journey?

Honestly, giving up was never an option for me. Even though I did not necessarily feel the need to prove anything to anyone, I simply could not bring myself to let myself down or throw away the hard work I invested in over the years and semesters.

What does graduating with a CGPA of 4.71 out of 5.00 mean to you?

Graduating with a CGPA of 4.71/5.00 represents far more than an academic milestone to me. It is a testament to years of hard work, discipline, sacrifices and countless nights spent studying. I have come to understand that while some people are naturally gifted and grasp things effortlessly, others have to work four times as hard to achieve similar results. I belong to the latter category, and I am proud of the effort it took to get here. It certainly did not come by chance.

Beyond the academic achievement, it represents the contributions, encouragement and sacrifices of everyone who supported me along the way. My family, friends, mentors and everyone who stood by me at different stages of the journey all have a part in this achievement.

To me, it is not just a number on a transcript; it is a reminder that the years of effort were worthwhile and that I did not walk this journey alone. Above all, I am grateful to God for the strength and grace to see it through.

How did you feel after learning you emerged as the best graduating male student in your set and the second-best graduating student in your faculty?

It was an overwhelming feeling, and my induction remains one of the best days of my life. It felt like finally reaching the destination after embarking on a very long journey, during which I sometimes wondered if that day would ever come. Even as I walked into the hall, it still felt surreal, almost as though it would not happen after waiting so many years for it.

It was a rollercoaster of emotions because, alongside the excitement and gratitude, there was also a deep sense of missing someone who should have been there to witness and share that moment.

What year did you eventually graduate?

I completed my academic programme in May 2023, but my professional induction and oath-taking did not take place until October 28, 2026.

Who were the people that stood by you throughout your university journey?

My profound gratitude goes to my father, the Owokonirans and my older brother, Kingsley. I am equally grateful to Ife, Olamide, Kenny, Martins, Moses, Isobomuwa, SirmieD, Eghosa, Sammy, Sir Christian, Jane, AIJ, Iyobosa, Abby, Mavis, Obinna, Onazi, Bennycruz, Jennifer, Mudia, Dayo and Endurance.

I also want to appreciate my lecturers, Mr Ken and Madam Maureen, my HOD, Dr Sunny, my landlord and landlady, as well as Efosa, Halliday, Seunara and Bira.

Every single person mentioned here played a role in keeping me afloat. They pulled me through some of my lowest moments, stood by me through periods of uncertainty and ensured that I lacked nothing within their means.

I genuinely want them to know that I do not take their love, sacrifices and kindness for granted. My certificate may bear my name, but the journey was never mine alone.

What lessons did the nine-year experience teach you about navigating difficult circumstances?

Beyond teaching me perseverance, patience and resilience, the nine-year journey taught me one very important lesson: how to work while waiting. I realised that although I could not control the delays surrounding my academic and professional progression, I could control how I used the time available to me.

Rather than allow the waiting period to become unproductive, I invested in personal and professional development. I took online courses and earned five certifications. I also became actively involved in research, contributing to more than seven co-authored publications and publishing my own research as a first author.

Beyond research, I trained in professional writing and eventually built my own professional writing business.

Looking back, I would say the experience taught me that a delay does not have to translate into stagnation. Sometimes, while waiting for one door to open, you can equip yourself with the skills, knowledge and experience needed to walk through several others. Above all, I learnt to make progress even when my circumstances were not moving at the pace I desired.

Now that you have been inducted as a Medical Laboratory Scientist, what are your immediate plans and long-term career aspirations?

My immediate priority is to secure an internship placement where I can complete my compulsory one-year professional internship, gain further practical experience and strengthen my clinical competence as a Medical Laboratory Scientist, particularly in clinical microbiology.

In the long term, I aspire to become a leading researcher in infectious diseases and virology, contributing to research that advances disease prevention, diagnosis and treatment. I am particularly interested in infectious diseases, public health, and vaccinology, and I hope to secure a fully funded scholarship to pursue postgraduate studies and deepen my expertise in these fields.

Ultimately, I want to build a career that goes beyond clinical practice to include meaningful scientific contributions, research publications, and innovations that improve public health, particularly in infectious disease control and vaccine development.

The post I turned nine-year university delay into research, professional growth – AAU graduate appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Infantino inspects stadium projects in Warri City
description:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino has inspected the Warri City Stadium and the Hussey College mini-stadium in Delta State following his arrival at Osubi Airport in Warri on Friday morning ahead of their commissioning.
Infantino was received by Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and former Nigeria
content:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino has inspected the Warri City Stadium and the Hussey College mini-stadium in Delta State following his arrival at Osubi Airport in Warri on Friday morning ahead of their commissioning.

Infantino was received by Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and former Nigeria Football Federation president Amaju Pinnick, who also serves as Deputy Chairperson of the FIFA Men’s National Teams Competition Committee.

Oborevwori said the visit underscored peace in Delta State and expressed pride at hosting the FIFA chief alongside residents.

“To see the FIFA President is something that is very great to us. Delta is very peaceful; if it’s not, they won’t be here,” the governor said.

Infantino said the trip highlighted that football belongs to everyone, noting that the sport is about both major tournaments and smaller community facilities.

“That’s what football is about. It’s for everyone everywhere. It’s the big stadiums, it’s the World Cup, but it’s also the smaller stadiums, it’s the proximity,” he stated.

The FIFA president also praised Nigeria’s youth football achievements, pointing to the country’s U-17 girls’ team winning the World Cup in Morocco a couple of weeks ago in a final against Japan that he attended, and said such experiences help transform young lives across Nigeria and Africa.

title: WAVE Tools Journalists and Influencers to Track Hate Speech and Monitor Election Violence Against Women
description: Gambiaj.com – (BANJU, THE GAMBIA) – The Women’s Association for Women and Victim Empowerment (WAVE) has trained journalists and social media influencers to monitor and document violence against women in politics, hate speech, and misinformation ahead of The Gambia’s December 5 presidential election.
content:
Gambiaj.com – (BANJU, THE GAMBIA) – The Women’s Association for Women and Victim Empowerment (WAVE) has trained journalists and social media influencers to monitor and document violence against women in politics, hate speech, and misinformation ahead of The Gambia’s December 5 presidential election.

Held on Thursday, November 19, at the Baobab Hotel, the training focused on social media monitoring, tracking radio discussions and political rallies, and safely documenting incidents of gender-based political violence.

The initiative is supported by the Canada Fund for Local Initiatives (CFLI) under the theme, “Safe Politics for Women, Peaceful Elections.”

Speaking at the opening, WAVE Program Associate Essa Sanneh noted that women aspiring to political leadership continue to face systemic harassment, discrimination, and intimidation. He highlighted that these challenges increasingly include online attacks, character assassination, false information, and manipulated images.

Sanneh explained that the trained participants will serve as field and digital monitors throughout the election period, documenting incidents to help WAVE and its partners develop targeted responses and policy recommendations.

For Jankey Ceesay, a reporter with The Point newspaper, the training arrived at a critical moment as the country gears up for the polls.

“The training has equipped me with important skills in fact-checking, identifying misinformation and disinformation, and recognizing AI-generated content,” Ceesay said. “These are essential skills for journalists to produce accurate and credible reports.”

Awa Jallow, a reporter with West Coast Radio, emphasized the vital role of peace journalism, civic education, and responsible social media use during the campaign season.

She urged fellow journalists to use their platforms to condemn tribalism and hate speech, and to foster electoral tolerance rather than amplify misleading content.

“Everyone has the right to support and vote for their preferred candidate. As journalists, we have a responsibility to respect those rights and promote peaceful coexistence,” Jallow stated.

Participants concluded the session by describing the training as a timely boost to responsible journalism and peaceful political participation.

title: Organisers unveil judges for 7th BSMH edition
description:
Nigeria’s emerging digital innovators will have an opportunity to showcase their creativity, communication skills and problem-solving abilities before leading figures in business, public relations, broadcasting and entertainment at the seventh edition of Bodex Social Media Hangout (BSMH 7.0).
The or
content:
Nigeria’s emerging digital innovators will have an opportunity to showcase their creativity, communication skills and problem-solving abilities before leading figures in business, public relations, broadcasting and entertainment at the seventh edition of Bodex Social Media Hangout (BSMH 7.0).

The organisers have unveiled a five-member judging panel comprising Paul Onwuanibe, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Landmark Africa; Adetokunbo Modupe, Founder and Chief Consultant of TPT International; Tosin Adefeko, Founder of PodFest Naija and Chief Executive Officer of AT3 Resources; Omotunde Adebowale-David, popularly known as Lolo1; and veteran actor, Keppy Ekpenyong Bassey.

The event, scheduled for December 10, 2026, at the Distance Learning Institute (DLI) Hall, University of Lagos, Akoka, Lagos, is expected to attract more than 3,000 students from secondary and tertiary institutions.

The unveiling of the judges marks a major milestone in preparations for the event, which seeks to equip young Nigerians with the knowledge, confidence and skills required to navigate an increasingly digital world.

The panel brings together professionals with extensive experience across different sectors of the economy. Onwuanibe’s entrepreneurial background and experience in business development will provide insights into innovation and commercial viability, while Modupe’s expertise in strategic communications will offer a perspective on effective messaging, reputation management and brand positioning.

Adefeko brings experience in podcasting, media entrepreneurship and the growing creator economy, while Lolo1 and Ekpenyong are expected to contribute their knowledge of broadcasting, entertainment, performance and audience engagement.
Together, the judges will assess participating students on originality, critical thinking, presentation, communication and the practical relevance of their ideas.

Beyond the opportunity to interact with established industry professionals, participating students will compete for a total prize pool of ₦4.4 million.
The competition will be divided into secondary and tertiary institution categories, with ₦2.2 million allocated to each category. In both categories, the winning institution will receive ₦1 million, while the second and third-place winners will receive ₦700,000 and ₦500,000, respectively.

An outstanding individual presenter will also receive a brand-new smartphone in recognition of exceptional articulation, confidence and presentation skills.
The organisers said the competitions were designed to encourage students to develop innovative ideas capable of addressing contemporary challenges while promoting responsible social media use and meaningful digital participation.

Speaking on the unveiling of the judging panel, Bodex Hungbo, Founder of Bodex Media and Convener of Bodex Social Media Hangout, said the selection reflected the organisation’s commitment to creating meaningful opportunities for young people to learn from experienced professionals.

“Many young people have brilliant ideas but rarely get the opportunity to present them before people who understand their potential.

“Imagine a secondary school student defending an idea before the CEO of Landmark Africa, a respected PR industry leader, a podcasting entrepreneur and established entertainment personalities. That experience can build confidence, sharpen ambition and open a young person’s mind to possibilities they may never have considered,” she said.

Hungbo added that the initiative was designed to connect young people with professionals willing to share their knowledge, challenge their thinking and help them recognise the value of their ideas.

According to her, while the financial rewards remain important, the exposure, experience and confidence gained through participation could have a more lasting impact on the students.

Since its establishment in 2019, Bodex Social Media Hangout has reportedly empowered more than 10,000 young people, engaged over 200 educational institutions and featured more than 300 speakers and thought leaders.

The initiative has also generated over 100 million cumulative digital media impressions and recognised more than 200 individuals for using social media to promote positive causes and societal development.
The seventh edition, themed “Influence with Purpose: Shaping Africa’s Digital Future,” will feature digital media masterclasses, debates, quizzes, interactive discussions, games and raffle draws, alongside other educational activities.

Participating students will also receive certificates of participation.
Through these activities, the organisers aim to strengthen digital literacy, promote responsible online communication and encourage innovation among young Nigerians while creating opportunities for meaningful engagement between emerging talents and established industry professionals.

The post Organisers unveil judges for 7th BSMH edition appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Mayweather vs. Harrysong: Celebrity boxing, music, culture hit Lagos this Christmas
description:

content:
Boxing’s most famous family name enters the ring in Lagos this December.

The Showdown Experience will see Jeff Mayweather take on Nigerian music star Harrysong on Wednesday, 23 December 2026, at Oasis by Five Palms, Ligali Ayorinde, Victoria Island, Lagos.

The fight brings together two very different worlds. Mayweather is a former IBO world super featherweight champion, Floyd Mayweather Jr.’s uncle and a respected trainer of champions.

He brings decades of ring experience and the weight of a name known worldwide.

Harrysong, one of Nigeria’s best-known hitmakers, will trade the studio for the ring and defend home soil in front of his fans.

The night goes beyond the main event. The card also features a second boxing bout and a special performance by Ice King Ochacho.

It’s a night of music, cultural displays, comedy and celebrity boxing—and one of the standout events of Lagos’s Detty December season.

The build-up to fight night includes training camps on both sides of the Atlantic, a fight-week programme in Lagos, an open workout, and an official press conference and face-off on Saturday, 19 December.

The event is organised by The Showdown Experience Limited.

title: Peter Obi will sweep 2027 poll, what happened in 2023 won’t repeat itself – Babachir Lawal
description:
Former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Babachir Lawal, has expressed confidence that the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, will win the 2027 presidential election.
Lawal, an NDC chieftain, made the prediction during an interview on Chann
content:
Former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Babachir Lawal, has expressed confidence that the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, will win the 2027 presidential election.

Lawal, an NDC chieftain, made the prediction during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today programme on Friday, November 20.

He maintained that the political circumstances surrounding the 2023 presidential election would not be repeated in 2027, expressing confidence that Obi would emerge victorious in the next election.

The former SGF had previously argued that Obi was the actual winner of the 2023 presidential election, despite the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) declaring Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC) the winner.

Lawal also questioned the 2023 election outcome, arguing that Obi’s performance should have resulted in a runoff election.

Explaining why he believes the 2027 contest will be different, Lawal pointed to what he described as Obi’s personal qualities, including integrity, national outlook, business experience and consistency.

He argued that these qualities would help the former Anambra State governor attract support from Nigerians across different backgrounds.

Lawal also expressed doubts about the chances of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), arguing that he lacked sufficient ethnic support to secure victory.

On campaign strategy, the NDC chieftain said the party intended to prioritise town hall meetings and direct engagement with voters rather than relying mainly on conventional political rallies.

He further expressed confidence that Obi could make significant gains in several states, including Kogi, Benue and Plateau, while also defeating Atiku in Adamawa State.

Lawal’s comments come as political parties and their candidates intensify preparations for the 2027 general election, scheduled for January 16, 2027.

Obi contested the 2023 presidential election under the Labour Party and finished third behind Atiku and Tinubu. He is now seeking the presidency on the platform of the NDC.

The post Peter Obi will sweep 2027 poll, what happened in 2023 won’t repeat itself – Babachir Lawal appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Yahaya Bello speaks on alleged attempt to evade EFCC arrest
description:
Former Kogi State Governor Yahaya Bello has denied deliberately evading the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), saying he does not believe immigration or police authorities saw him crossing Nigeria’s borders.
Bello spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Fri
content:
Former Kogi State Governor Yahaya Bello has denied deliberately evading the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), saying he does not believe immigration or police authorities saw him crossing Nigeria’s borders.

Bello spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, where he responded to questions about the allegations against him and claims that he had attempted to avoid arrest by the anti-graft agency.

When asked about the alleged attempt to evade the EFCC, the former governor said he did not believe security agencies had witnessed him crossing the country’s borders.

“I don’t think the Nigerian immigration or Nigerian police saw me crossing the borders of this country,” he said.

During the interview, he was reminded that he had been in Kogi State and Abuja. However, Bello maintained that government authorities had the capacity to locate anyone, regardless of where the person might be.

He urged Nigerians to allow the legal process to run its course.

“Let’s allow the law to take its course,” he said.

Bello also rejected suggestions that he was corrupt, describing himself as one of the most transparent politicians in the country despite what he called attempts to vilify him.

“I am the most transparent and the most vilified. But at the end of the day, I shall be vindicated,” he said.

Responding to critics who accuse him of stealing public funds, the former governor challenged them to examine how resources were managed under his administration in Kogi State.

He also dismissed the accusations, saying, “Call me a thief, I pity you.”

Bello further maintained that he had been blessed by God and was capable of meeting his personal and family needs.

The former governor has been facing multiple EFCC cases over alleged financial misconduct during his administration between 2016 and 2024.

In one of the cases, the Federal Government accused him and two former state officials of involvement in an alleged ₦110.4bn money laundering scheme. The prosecution alleges that funds were diverted to acquire properties in Abuja and Dubai.

He is also facing a separate 19-count charge involving an alleged ₦80.2bn fraud and money laundering.

The post Yahaya Bello speaks on alleged attempt to evade EFCC arrest appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Grand Theft Auto VI Takes Record $3.8 bn On First day
description: “Grand Theft Auto VI” brought in $3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day, publisher Rockstar Games said Friday, calling it the biggest launch for any entertainment product in history.The figure, based on company estimates of worldwide sales through the end of Thursday, is nearly f
content:
“Grand Theft Auto VI” brought in $3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day, publisher Rockstar Games said Friday, calling it the biggest launch for any entertainment product in history.

The figure, based on company estimates of worldwide sales through the end of Thursday, is nearly five times the roughly $800 million that predecessor “Grand Theft Auto V” took in during its first 24 hours in 2013.

Rockstar, a label of New York-based Take-Two Interactive, said the game had sold 32.5 million units before release, a record across all platforms.

“We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world,” said Sam Houser, the studio’s founder and president.

The game came out Thursday on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. It launched first at midnight in New Zealand and then rolled out to each market as the clock reached midnight there.

The release generated more social media posts than this year’s World Cup, according to monitoring platform Visibrain.

Critics praised the game, which has a score of 99 on review aggregator Metacritic. Rockstar said that made it the highest-rated game ever.

In a review for The Verge, Andrew Webster wrote that “the game is so good that the outsize hype is the least interesting thing about it.”

This week the game received eight nominations for the Game Awards, which will be held December 10.

Rockstar spent more than eight years developing the title. It delayed the launch twice, first from autumn 2025 and then from May 2026.

The studio was also hit by a 2022 hack in which stolen gameplay footage was posted online.

The series has long been accused of glorifying violence and crime, since players can run over pedestrians, sell drugs and shoot at police.

No official release is currently planned in Russia, China, Lebanon or Qatar.

The post Grand Theft Auto VI Takes Record $3.8 bn On First day appeared first on Channels Television.

title: I’ll nominate my son if Obi offers me ministerial job – Babachir Lawal
description:
Former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Babachir Lawal, has said he would give his 40-year-old son a ministerial appointment if Peter Obi offered him one after winning the 2027 presidential election.
Lawal, a chieftain of the Nigerian Democratic Congress, said he was no longer interest
content:
Former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Babachir Lawal, has said he would give his 40-year-old son a ministerial appointment if Peter Obi offered him one after winning the 2027 presidential election.

Lawal, a chieftain of the Nigerian Democratic Congress, said he was no longer interested in serving in government, citing his age and saying he had achieved all he wanted in life.

Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, Lawal said he would rather return to his farm than take up a public office in an Obi-led administration.

“Go back to my farm and watch Nigeria grow,” he said when asked what he would do if Obi won the presidency.

Explaining his position, Lawal said, “See, I keep telling you I’m 72 years old. I have a 40-year-old son. What is wrong if Peter says, ‘BD, give me, I’m going to make you Minister of Agric.’ I said, ‘Peter, instead give my son Minister of Agric.’ Is that wrong?

“In those days when we were young, that’s how things were done. When they approach you, ‘You are going to be this,’ you say, ‘No, I’m too old for this, there are young generation.’ Pick and give! It’s doable.”

He described himself as an elder statesman and suggested that having served as SGF under former President Muhammadu Buhari, ministerial appointment would be a demotion.

“I’m 72! Past 72. Yes, very. An elder statesman. And God has done well for me. I’ve achieved everything that I need to achieve,” he said.

Lawal said he was not in the party to seek political office but to support what he described as a good man capable of rescuing Nigerians from hardship.

He expressed confidence that Obi would win the 2027 presidential election, insisting that the circumstances surrounding the 2023 poll would not be repeated.

The former SGF argued that the 2023 presidential election should have proceeded to a runoff, claiming that Obi secured the majority of votes but failed to meet the geographical spread requirement.

“Peter got the majority of votes; he didn’t get the spread. Bola Tinubu got the spread and came second. There should have been a runoff in that election,” he said.

Lawal predicted that Obi would win Kogi, Benue and Plateau states, as well as defeat former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress in his home state of Adamawa.

“I give it to you that Peter didn’t have more spread. This time, Peter will get the spread in Nigeria.

“Atiku will come third in Adamawa State this time around,” he added.

He also questioned Atiku’s chances in the election, arguing that the former vice-president would not have sufficient ethnic support to secure the presidency.

Comparing the NDC ticket with those of other political parties, Lawal described Obi and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, as a better option.

He disclosed that the party’s campaign strategy would prioritise town hall meetings, which he considered a more effective way of engaging voters.

According to him, Nigerians would support Obi because of his character and competence.

“First of all, he is incorruptible. Second, he is detribalised. Third, he is a businessman that understands market forces. And fourth, he is a man who sticks to his words,” Lawal said.

Asked whether Obi had made any promises to him, the former SGF replied, “No, he doesn’t need to.”

Lawal served as SGF under Buhari from 2015 to 2017. He joined the NDC in September 2026 after leaving the African Democratic Congress and declared his support for the Obi-Kwankwaso ticket.

Obi, a former governor of Anambra State, is the NDC’s presidential candidate for the 2027 election, with former Kano State Governor Kwankwaso as his running mate.

In the 2023 presidential election, Obi, who contested on the platform of the Labour Party, finished third with 6,101,533 votes, behind Atiku, who polled 6,984,520 votes, and President Bola Tinubu, who won with 8,794,726 votes.

title: Rema Releases Seven-Track EP ‘E-Mortal Boy’, Features Wizkid On First Collaboration
description: Nigerian Afrobeats star Rema has released a seven-track extended play (EP), ‘E-Mortal Boy,’ marking his first EP since ‘Ravage,’ released in 2023.The project, also stylised as EMB, arrived on Friday through Mavin Global Holdings and Jonzing World Entertainment, with distribut
content:
Nigerian Afrobeats star Rema has released a seven-track extended play (EP), ‘E-Mortal Boy,’ marking his first EP since ‘Ravage,’ released in 2023.

The project, also stylised as EMB, arrived on Friday through Mavin Global Holdings and Jonzing World Entertainment, with distribution involving Interscope/Universal Music Group.

The 22-minute project features a mix of previously released singles and five new songs, with its opening track, ‘Feel Alright’, featuring fellow Nigerian music star Wizkid.

The collaboration marks the first official musical outing between the two artistes, bringing together Wizkid, one of the leading figures in the global rise of Afrobeats, and Rema, who has emerged as one of the genre’s prominent contemporary voices.

‘Feel Alright’ is a record centred on romantic attraction and satisfying a lover’s desires. Produced by Thisizlondon and AoD, the song also credits both artistes as songwriters.

E-MORTAL BOY OUT NOW! https://t.co/h4CRrRmrQ0

— REMA (@heisrema) November 19, 2026

The collaboration has attracted attention as Rema’s first official track with any of Nigeria’s so-called Big Three, comprising Wizkid, Davido and Burna Boy.

Beyond the high-profile opening track, ‘E-Mortal Boy’ sees Rema continue his experimentation with different musical influences.

The EP includes ‘Oh No’ and ‘TEA’, which were released as singles in September and August 2026, respectively.

Other tracks include ‘Velvet’, and ‘TANZANIA’, featuring American producer BNYX. The latter draws on Bollywood-inspired sounds.

Rema also collaborates with French-Congolese singer Theodora on ‘SUGA’, a track with grunge influences, while the closing song, ‘Bang Bang’, features Nigerian-American singer Kah-Lo and producer Thisizlondon.

Tracklist . EMB Friday [Presave] https://t.co/EisJqq61aP

— REMA (@heisrema) November 17, 2026

Longtime collaborator Thisizlondon, who has worked with Rema on songs including ‘Calm Down’ and ‘Soundgasm’, also has production credits across the project.

The complete tracklist comprises ‘Feel Alright’ featuring Wizkid, ‘Oh No’, ‘Velvet’, ‘TANZANIA’ with BNYX, ‘TEA’, ‘SUGA’ featuring Theodora, and ‘Bang Bang’ featuring Kah-Lo and Thisizlondon.

The release follows Rema’s 2024 sophomore album, ‘HEIS,’ which earned a Grammy nomination.

With ‘E-Mortal Boy,’ the singer delivers a compact project that revisits his experimental approach to music while bringing together a range of collaborators. The Wizkid collaboration, however, has become the project’s most significant talking point, given the artistes’ influence on different generations of Nigerian music.

The post Rema Releases Seven-Track EP ‘E-Mortal Boy’, Features Wizkid On First Collaboration appeared first on Channels Television.

title: El-Rufai: I would have advised him to lie low, talk less – Yahaya Bello
description:
Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has said he would have advised former Kaduna State Governor, Nasir El-Rufai, to keep a low profile and avoid making public statements if they had maintained their previous level of communication.
Bello gave the advice during an interview on Channels Televisi
content:
Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has said he would have advised former Kaduna State Governor, Nasir El-Rufai, to keep a low profile and avoid making public statements if they had maintained their previous level of communication.

Bello gave the advice during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today, while speaking about his relationship with El-Rufai and the latter’s detention.

He disclosed that they had not communicated in more than four years, despite their close relationship while both served as governors.

Bello, however, said he continued to respect El-Rufai, describing him as an intelligent and idealistic politician who stands firmly by his convictions.

“El-Rufai is somebody I respect his intellect so much. I respect him. He’s very idealistic and he’s somebody that pursues whatever he believes in,” he said.

The former Kogi governor explained that differences could emerge between people without necessarily indicating that their relationship had broken down.

He said he would have offered El-Rufai several pieces of advice if they were still in regular contact, particularly concerning his political situation.

“If I had had contact with him, as we used to in the past, I would have advised him to lie low. I would have advised him to stay back in the house that he helped in building,” Bello said.

He added that he would have encouraged the former Kaduna governor to speak less and allow President Bola Tinubu to decide how to handle the situation.

“I would have advised him to talk less. I would have advised him to wait for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to see in his wisdom what he will do in every situation and every circumstance,” he said.

Despite their lack of communication, Bello expressed goodwill towards El-Rufai, saying he did not want the former governor to suffer political setbacks.

“But today, I wish him all the best, sincerely speaking, because he was part of this APC and I wouldn’t wish him to go down the drain,” he added.

Bello also noted that nobody was above mistakes, whether through their statements or actions, stressing that people continued to learn from their experiences throughout their lives.

He expressed hope that El-Rufai had learned how to manage political disagreements and other differences.

The former governors were members of the All Progressives Congress, although Bello did not disclose the specific circumstances that led to the loss of regular communication between them.

title: 2027: Sowore faults NELFUND, promises non-repayable grants
description:
By Dickson Omobola



African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore, Friday, faulted the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), saying he will abolish the scheme if elected.



Sowore promised to introduce N100,000 grants per semester for students, saying the scheme would prov
content:
By Dickson Omobola

African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore, Friday, faulted the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), saying he will abolish the scheme if elected.

Sowore promised to introduce N100,000 grants per semester for students, saying the scheme would provide financial support without requiring repayment.

He made the promise during a live session on his Facebook page, adding that students should not be burdened with debt while pursuing their education.

He said, “The NELFUND that this government has put in place. First, our party is going to abolish NELFUND. We will turn it into grants.”

He added that the policy would replace the existing student loan arrangement.

He said, “We are going to give N100,000 per semester, which is N20,000 more than what they are getting now. For two semesters, you get N200,000 so that you can focus on your studies.”

Sowore argued that Nigeria should avoid introducing a system that could leave graduates struggling with debt, particularly in a country where employment opportunities were limited.

Citing his experience in the United States, where he said he spent 20 years, the AAC candidate described student loans as a source of financial hardship for many graduates.

He said, “The biggest cause of depression in America is student loans. Where are you going to get the employment to pay back the loans? But the truth is that even the loans they are giving to them now, they are not paying back. So it just makes sense to turn it into grants.”

Sowore said a student completing a four-year program would receive a total of N400,000 under the proposed arrangement, assuming two semesters per year.

He described the amount as a reasonable investment in young Nigerians who would contribute decades of service to the country.

The former presidential candidate also proposed scholarships for students with outstanding academic abilities, saying beneficiaries could be sponsored to study abroad.

“Grants for anybody, whether… scholarships for people who show exemplary ability. We give you a scholarship; we send you abroad,” he said.

He advocated increased government investment in education, citing China’s support for students studying abroad as an example of how countries could develop their education systems.

Sowore blamed the decline in Nigeria’s education sector for several of the country’s challenges, arguing that investment in schools was essential to reducing poverty and developing human capital.

He recalled that during his childhood, free education and community efforts to ensure school attendance made education a priority.

The activist also cited the University College Hospital, Ibadan, as an example of Nigeria’s former standing in the health sector, saying members of foreign royal families previously travelled to the country for medical treatment.

He contrasted this with the present situation, where many Nigerians struggle to afford medical treatment abroad.

Sowore further recalled that Indian and Ghanaian teachers worked in Nigerian secondary schools in the 1980s, arguing that the country’s education system had since declined.

He maintained that increased public investment in education was necessary to reverse the trend and improve opportunities for future generations.

The post 2027: Sowore faults NELFUND, promises non-repayable grants appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Kogi 2027: Yahaya Bello says he will defeat Natasha Akpoti ‘overwhelmingly’
description:
Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has expressed confidence that he will defeat Senator Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan in the 2027 Kogi Central senatorial election, predicting an overwhelming victory.
Bello made the declaration during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he wa
content:
Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has expressed confidence that he will defeat Senator Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan in the 2027 Kogi Central senatorial election, predicting an overwhelming victory.

Bello made the declaration during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he was asked whether Akpoti-Uduaghan’s popularity and political activities posed a threat to his chances at the polls.

The former governor dismissed the possibility of a close contest, claiming that his political standing across Kogi State was far ahead of that of other politicians, including those from Kogi Central.

“Yahaya Bello and any other politician in Kogi State today, not even Kogi Central, let me say Kogi State, our polls are far apart when it comes to issue of contest,” he said.

Asked whether he remained popular despite being away from active political office for almost four years, Bello said his absence had further strengthened his popularity.

“That even added to my popularity,” he responded.

He also declined to directly compare himself with Akpoti-Uduaghan, saying he did not want to give undue recognition to other potential contestants.

“I can only equate any other person with maybe my third generation or fourth generation mentee politically, as far as this contest is concerned,” he said.

When asked if he was confident of winning the election, Bello replied, “Overwhelmingly.”

He attributed his confidence to what he described as the trust and loyalty of the people, claiming that his supporters were already campaigning for him without waiting for financial incentives.

According to him, the level of support became evident during his recent homecoming to Kogi State, when residents donated farm produce, food items and money to encourage him to represent them in the Senate.

Bello recalled a political tradition involving a former leader in the area, Elijah Abdul Kukuri Ujo Chere, whose supporters reportedly contributed food and money during election periods to encourage his political participation.

He said a similar show of support occurred during his own homecoming.

“As I speak now, I will not spend one dime in the campaign and election. And by the grace of God, you see me at the Red Chambers,” he said.

The former governor described himself as a political role model to people in Kogi State, particularly in Kogi Central, insisting that his record in office had earned their continued support.

“I am their political idol. I did not mislead them. I did not betray them. I did not fall their hands,” he said.

Bello also said he intended to remain in the All Progressives Congress and support President Bola Tinubu’s policies and programmes, which he claimed were being felt by people at the grassroots.

His remarks come as he prepares to challenge Akpoti-Uduaghan, the incumbent senator representing Kogi Central, for the senatorial seat in the 2027 election.

title: Ogun 2027: APC Gov Candidate Unveils Nine-Point Agenda For Development
description: The Ogun State All Progressives Congress governorship candidate, Solomon Adeola, has unveiled his Nine-Point Economic Development and Social Contract with the people of the state, tagged “Itesiwaju”, meaning “Moving Forward”.The blueprint, unveiled at the Cultural Centre in t
content:
The Ogun State All Progressives Congress governorship candidate, Solomon Adeola, has unveiled his Nine-Point Economic Development and Social Contract with the people of the state, tagged “Itesiwaju”, meaning “Moving Forward”.

The blueprint, unveiled at the Cultural Centre in the state capital, has critical infrastructure development, security, education and human capital development, agricultural transformation, job creation, among others, as critical components of the plan.

While seeking the support and understanding of residents of the state on the electoral task ahead, Adeola, also known as Yayi, said the action plans aim to bring more abundant life and shared prosperity to the state.

“Today, we are gathered to launch my Economic and Social Development Blueprint for the people of Ogun State, which I tagged ITESIWAJU. We are at the threshold of historical importance in the affairs of our dear state. In the democratic history of our state, this will be the first time that we are attempting to have a peaceful succession from one friendly administration to another, and it is our fervent wish and prayer that we succeed in this desirable venture,” he said.

” It is my firm belief that before we ask for a single vote from the people of Ogun State, we owe it as a duty to you to present our agenda for development of the state. My ITESIWAJU agenda took into consideration the inputs from my recently concluded interactions with stakeholders in all our 20 local governments. We sat with royal fathers, community leaders, women, youth, farmers, and traders.”

Adeola said he listened to the yearnings of Ogun people for development and built his agenda on your voices.

“This Agenda is a plan, not a performance. Read it as you would read a contract, because that is exactly what it is.

“Since 1976, Ogun State has been blessed with leaders who left indelible footprints of progress for our people: from the solid foundation laid by Chief Olabisi Onabanjo in infrastructure, education and hospitality industry; the bold rural development initiatives of Chief Olusegun Osoba that brought modernity to some of our villages; the policies of Otunba Gbenga Daniel that created some enduring institutions; the strides of Senator Ibikunle Amosun in some mega infrastructural projects; and at present the massive industrial transformation and mega projects under Prince Dapo Abiodun. It is all a story of progressive development in the interest of our state,” he added.

He commended the current administration of Governor Dapo Abiodun for the current developmental projects, which he said have placed the state as the first industrial destination of choice.

“And today, the baton is in the safe hands of our Governor, His Excellency, Prince Abiodun, CON. Your Excellency, you came not with slogans but with a compass: the ISEYA Development Agenda. You gave us the Gateway International Agro-Cargo Airport, pressed forward with the Kajola and Ijebu-Ode dry ports and the Gateway Deep Sea Port in the making, constructed more than 1,700 kilometres of roads, the highest of any administration so far, and delivered more than 7,000 housing units. Under your dutiful watch, our economy has grown to about ₦17 trillion, our revenue has more than doubled, and Ogun now stands as Number 5 in Nigeria for internally generated revenue.

“Your Excellency, ISEYA laid the foundation for economic growth. ITESIWAJU will build the foundation for more economic growth and prosperity for our people. Where ISEYA built infrastructure, we will connect such. Where ISEYA empowered our youth, we will turn their talent into great enterprise. Where ISEYA strengthened agriculture, we will carry it from the farm to the factory and to the world. History will be kind to you, because you have been kind to Ogun State,” the senator said.

“Governance is not a sprint; it is a relay race. Each leader must take the baton, run farther, and hand it to another for further development. To abandon good projects is to waste resources of the people and betray a trust. So, we will complete what is incomplete and ongoing, maintain what works, and reform what is failing. I am not coming to disrupt, but to deliver for the people. We are not reinventing Ogun State, but repositioning it for good, from Abeokuta to Ijebu, from Sagamu to Ado Odo Ota, and every community in between.

“Together, we have travelled the length and breadth of this State and what we see is that Ogun State stands at the cusp of greatness. With Lagos and the Atlantic Ocean to our south, the Republic of Benin to our west, three states to our north and east, there is no other state in this federation that sits at such an advantageous crossroads,” he added.

“Consider where we stand. Our ₦17 trillion economy, roughly $11 billion, is the size of the entire economy of the Republic of Togo. Our per capita income, at about $1,740, is already well above the Nigerian average of about $1,220. Lagos’s economy is about 3.7 times ours, yet its per capita income is only about 1.5 times ours. The gap between Ogun and Lagos is not in our people or our potential. It is in how well we plan, organise, and collect.”

“And yet, too many of our people still live in a State that works well for some and barely at all for others. The market woman in Ilaro whose stall closes at dusk for lack of power; the nurse in Sagamu managing thirty patients alone; the graduate in Abeokuta still searching for work years after graduation; and the farmer in Ijebu East who loses a third of his harvest for want of cold storage. These are not statistics to me. They are faces, names and conversations.”

The governorship candidate took the audience, which included Governor Abiodun, former governor Olusegun Osoba, captains of industry, members of the organized private sector, market women, and associations, on the journey of his vision and mission for the state if elected.

“My vision is to transform Ogun State where our natural and human resources are sustainably harnessed to unlock our economic and agro-industrial prowess, while ensuring inclusive governance and shared prosperity for our citizens in a vibrant and secure environment, while my mission is to transform Ogun State’s economy through strategic investments, infrastructure development, agricultural diversification, transparent governance, and quality education and health services, while fostering inclusive growth for sustainable prosperity,” he added.

The post Ogun 2027: APC Gov Candidate Unveils Nine-Point Agenda For Development appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Customs suspends recruits’ training amid FCC legal action over recruitment process
description:
The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has suspended ongoing training activities at its training colleges to allow for further consultations with the Federal Character Commission (FCC) over concerns surrounding its recruitment exercise.
The suspension was announced in a statement on Friday by Abdullahi M
content:
The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has suspended ongoing training activities at its training colleges to allow for further consultations with the Federal Character Commission (FCC) over concerns surrounding its recruitment exercise.

The suspension was announced in a statement on Friday by Abdullahi Maiwada, the NCS national spokesperson.

According to Maiwada, the decision was taken to create room for further discussions with the FCC “towards the amicable resolution of concerns raised in connection with ongoing recruitment exercise”.

He explained that the development followed engagements between the FCC and a delegation from the Customs Service.

Maiwada added that both institutions had reaffirmed their commitment to resolving the issues through constructive dialogue, mutual understanding and continued institutional collaboration.

The suspension is expected to allow both agencies to continue consultations towards resolving the concerns surrounding the recruitment process.

“In consideration of the concerns raised by the Commission and in line with the series of engagements, the Comptroller-General of Customs (CGC) Bashir Adewale Adeniyi MFR has reaffirmed the Service’s commitment to institutional collaboration and constructive engagement with relevant government institutions in the overall national interest,” the statement reads.

“Furthermore, the CGC acknowledged the critical role of FCC in promoting national unity, fairness and equitable representation in public service appointments, noting the importance of its constitutional mandate in strengthening inclusiveness and ensuring that the principles of federal character are upheld across the Federation.

“The NCS values its longstanding relationship with the FCC and remains confident that the ongoing dialogue will provide an opportunity to address the concerns raised in a mutually beneficial manner, while reinforcing the shared commitment of both institutions to fairness, national cohesion and effective public service delivery.

“The Service, under the leadership of the CGC and his management team, remains committed to upholding the highest standards of institutional accountability and transparency in the discharge of its responsibilities.”

The suspension comes days after the FCC filed criminal charges against NCS and Bashir Adeniyi, the agency’s comptroller-general, over alleged failure to provide information on its 2025 recruitment exercise.

The FCC instituted a four-count charge against NCS and Adeniyi at the federal high court in Abuja.

According to the charge sheet dated November 12, 2026, the FCC alleged that the customs CG “failed to furnish” requested information and records relating to the NSC’s 2025/2026 recruitment exercise.

BACK STORY

In July, NCS released the list of successful candidates in its recruitment exercise.

The service selected 3,852 candidates from 573,680 applications across three entry cadres; superintendent, inspectorate, and customs assistant.

Speaking about the list in August, Adeniyi said he was prepared to defend the selection on its merits.

He said the successful candidates were distributed equally across the 36 states of the federation.

In September, the NCS invited the successful candidates for physical screening and documentation at the Nigeria Customs Command and Staff College, Gwagwalada, Abuja.

Some of the candidates were subsequently invited for training.

However, allegations emerged that some applicants whose names appeared on the list of successful candidates had been screened out and replaced people who did not participate in the recruitment exercise.

In a statement released on October 19, NCS said it had acknowledged the complaints from applicants who participated in the recruitment exercise.

The agency said 397 applicants were screened out over issues relating to substance abuse, age, physical fitness, and documentation.

The NCS added that some candidates were rejected because of “identified irregularities in their selection process during the screening exercise”.

In October, the FCC called for the suspension of the NCS recruitment exercise over alleged violations of federal character principles.

The post Customs suspends recruits’ training amid FCC legal action over recruitment process appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Darkness looms as power generation for 220 million Nigerians drops to 900 megawatts
description:
Electricity allocation to Nigeria’s 11 distribution companies (DisCos) has dropped to a combined 948 megawatts, worsening concerns over the country’s persistent power supply crisis.
Checks conducted by Peoples Gazette on the Nigeria Grid website at about 3:15 p.m. on Friday showed that the 11 DisCos
content:
Electricity allocation to Nigeria’s 11 distribution companies (DisCos) has dropped to a combined 948 megawatts, worsening concerns over the country’s persistent power supply crisis.

Checks conducted by Peoples Gazette on the Nigeria Grid website at about 3:15 p.m. on Friday showed that the 11 DisCos received a total allocation of 948MW.

Ikeja Electricity Distribution Company received the highest allocation of 133MW, followed by Eko Disco with 132MW and Ibadan Disco with 119MW.

Benin Disco received 115MW, while Enugu Disco was allocated 110MW. Abuja Disco got 109MW, followed by Port Harcourt Disco with 104MW.

The remaining distribution companies received significantly lower allocations, with Yola Disco getting 37MW and Kano Disco receiving 31MW. Jos Disco and Kaduna Disco received 30MW and 28MW, respectively.

The development comes amid persistent challenges in Nigeria’s electricity sector, as power generation on the national grid continues to fluctuate.

Nigeria’s national grid reportedly collapsed twice within four days in January, with electricity generation plunging from 3,825MW to just 39MW within minutes.

A report by Peoples Gazette, citing data from the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO), also indicated that power generation at one point dropped to zero megawatts.

The latest allocation figures highlight the continuing pressure on electricity supply across the country, where millions of households and businesses depend on the national grid.

title: Peter Obi Will Win 2027 Election, What Happened In 2023 Won’t Repeat Itself — Babachir Lawal
description: A former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF) and chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Babachir Lawal, has reiterated that the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, will win the 2027 general election, insisting that the circumstances surrounding the 2023 pres
content:
A former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF) and chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Babachir Lawal, has reiterated that the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, will win the 2027 general election, insisting that the circumstances surrounding the 2023 presidential poll will not be repeated.

Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, Lawal predicted that Obi would emerge victorious, expressing the belief that the political dynamics of the next election would be different from those of 2023.

He also questioned the outcome of the 2023 presidential election, arguing that there should have been a runoff as Obi got the highest number of votes, a development he believes would have changed the political calculations surrounding the contest.

“Peter got the majority of votes; he didn’t get the spread. Bola Tinubu got the spread and came second. There should have been a runoff in that election,” he maintained.

The former SGF further projected that Obi would win Kogi, Benue and Plateau states, while defeating former Vice President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in his home state of Adamawa.

“I give it to you that Peter didn’t have more spread. This time, Peter will get the spread in Nigeria.

“Atiku will come third in Adamawa State this time around,” he added.

On the ADC candidate’s chances in the forthcoming election, Lawal argued that the former vice president would not have sufficient ethnic support to secure the presidency.

Comparing the NDC ticket with those of other political parties, he described it as a better option.

Lawal also disclosed that the party’s campaign strategy would prioritise town hall meetings, which he considers a more effective means of engaging voters.

He said Nigerians would look in the direction of Obi due to his character and competence.

“First of all, he is incorruptible. Second, he is detribalised. Third, he is a businessman that understands market forces. And fourth, he is a man who sticks to his words,” the NDC chieftain added.

Asked whether the former Anambra State governor made any promises to him, the former SGF said, “No, he doesn’t need to”.

The 72-year-old said he would go back to his 4,000 hectares of farmland where he produces cash crops and livestock, and watch Nigeria grow.

Asked whether he does not want to partake in Obi’s government if he wins, Babachir said, “I’m 72 years old. I have a 40-year-old son. What is wrong if Peter says, ‘I’m going to make you Minister of Agric,’ and I say Peter, instead, give my son Minister of Agric. Is that wrong? In those days when we were young, that’s how things were done.”

The post Peter Obi Will Win 2027 Election, What Happened In 2023 Won’t Repeat Itself — Babachir Lawal appeared first on Channels Television.

title: FG’s ₦100,000 Grant: Who can apply, How beneficiaries will be selected [Full Details]
description:
The Federal Government has outlined the eligibility conditions and registration process for its advertised ₦100,000 family grant under the Nigeria Family Strengthening and Development Programme (NFSP), an initiative said to target poor and vulnerable households across the country.
According to a sta
content:
The Federal Government has outlined the eligibility conditions and registration process for its advertised ₦100,000 family grant under the Nigeria Family Strengthening and Development Programme (NFSP), an initiative said to target poor and vulnerable households across the country.

According to a statement attributed to the programme’s management board, the intervention is designed to provide financial support to families struggling with economic hardship, rising food prices and the effects of ongoing economic reforms.

The programme is coordinated by the Hope for Indigenous Family Support Initiative’s Coordinating Office under the Federal Ministry of Youth Development.

However, the management board has clarified that meeting the basic registration requirements does not automatically guarantee payment, as beneficiaries are expected to undergo further verification and selection based on poverty and vulnerability criteria.

Who is eligible for the ₦100,000 grant?

The programme’s management board listed the following basic requirements for prospective applicants:

  1. Applicants must be Nigerian citizens by birth.
  2. They must possess a valid National Identification Number (NIN).
  3. They must be between 18 and 65 years old at the time of registration.

Applicants’ NIN details are expected to be verified through the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC).

The programme is specifically intended for poor and vulnerable households identified through social safety net systems and verified national identity records.

Therefore, meeting the age, citizenship and NIN requirements does not automatically qualify an applicant to receive the money.

How to apply for the ₦100,000 grant

The programme’s advertised registration portal is:

https://nfsp.ng/signup

Interested Nigerians are directed to visit the portal and provide the personal information requested on the registration page.

Applicants are expected to submit their details for verification and consideration under the programme’s selection process.

How beneficiaries will be selected

According to the management board, the selection process will involve identifying eligible households through social safety net systems, verifying their identity records and assessing their circumstances against established poverty and vulnerability criteria.

Beneficiaries are expected to be selected in phases across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones.

The programme will cover a limited number of households in each phase, meaning that not everyone who registers will receive payment immediately.

The board also stated that applicants who have not received a notification should not automatically assume they have been permanently excluded.

How successful applicants will receive the ₦100,000

The management board said selected beneficiaries would receive the money directly into the bank accounts submitted during registration.

Successful applicants are expected to receive SMS notifications from designated payment providers.

Recipients will then be required to follow the instructions in the messages and provide the necessary consent before the funds are credited to their accounts.

Warning against fraud

The programme’s management board has warned Nigerians against individuals or agents demanding money in exchange for registration, inclusion on the beneficiary list or guaranteed payment.

It advised applicants not to pay anyone who claims to have the ability to secure the grant on their behalf.

The board also urged Nigerians to avoid unofficial registration websites and rely on recognised communication channels for further information.

Prospective applicants should exercise caution and independently confirm the registration portal through recognised government channels before submitting sensitive personal information, including their NIN and banking details.

The post FG’s ₦100,000 Grant: Who can apply, How beneficiaries will be selected [Full Details] appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Waste crisis: Acting LAWMA MD resumes, reads riot act to staff
description:
.unveils 60-day action plan



​By Olasunkanmi Akoni



Amid mounting concerns over waste management across the metropolis, the newly appointed Acting Managing Director of the Lagos Waste Management Authority, LAWMA, Olajuwon Akinyemi, has assumed office with a stern warning to the workforce, readin
content:
.unveils 60-day action plan

​By Olasunkanmi Akoni

Amid mounting concerns over waste management across the metropolis, the newly appointed Acting Managing Director of the Lagos Waste Management Authority, LAWMA, Olajuwon Akinyemi, has assumed office with a stern warning to the workforce, reading the riot act against laxity.

Akinyemi, also unveiled a 60-day emergency action plan to clear backlogs and restore the agency’s past glory.

​Addressing management and staff at a tense workers’ forum held at LAWMA’s Ijora-Olopa headquarters on Friday, he made it clear that business as usual was over.

Accompanied by the Acting Executive Director, Operations, Dr. Olorunwa Tijani, and the Executive Director, Finance, Mr. Kunle Adebiyi, the new helmsman demanded total commitment, positive work ethics, and renewed dedication to duty from every personnel, warning that repositioning the agency requires uncompromising discipline and active participation from all ranks.

​”We are bringing in resilience and a new paradigm shift. It is a new wave in handling waste in Lagos.

“We already have the template to transform LAWMA positively. All we need to do is recreate, modernise and do better than in the past,” Akinyemi declared, signaling zero tolerance for operational inefficiencies.

​To back up his charge, Akinyemi rolled out a 60-day blueprint aimed at rapid waste evacuation, stricter regulatory enforcement, and aggressive field monitoring across Lagos State.

While giving key highlights of the emergency plan, the MD boss said personnel will be redeployed across the state’s three operational districts based on their familiarity with local terrains to sharpen field monitoring and speed up response times.

Hinting on decentralised operational hubs, Akinyemi added that the hubs will be established to decentralise waste management, tighten supervision, and bring rapid intervention closer to blackspots requiring urgent attention.

On ​indiscriminate dumping, he avowed the agency’s determination to intensify community sensitization on waste sorting at source, mobilizing traditional rulers, Community Development Association (CDA) leaders, market associations, and artisans to enforce responsible disposal habits.

Akinyemi, therefore, called for closer synergy with Private Sector Participation (PSP) operators and demanded stricter public compliance with approved waste collection tariffs to sustain operations.

​While reading the riot act on performance, the Acting MD also moved to boost morale, assuring workers that their welfare remains a top priority.

He revealed ongoing efforts to procure Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)-powered staff buses to cushion transportation challenges.

​Earlier, Tijani, reiterated the call for urgency, promising an immediate overhaul and revitalisation of LAWMA’s operational framework to boost field performance.

​Similarly, Adebiyi, warned that the success of the 60-day plan hinges on prudent financial management, strict accountability, and synergy across all directorates, urging staff to embrace professionalism and shared responsibility.

​Following the address, Akinyemi led the management team on an on-the-spot inspection tour of various departments at the headquarters to assess workflow and identify immediate operational bottlenecks.
