title: [VIDEO] I Would’ve Advised El-Rufai To Talk Less If I Had Had Contact With Him — Yahaya Bello
description: Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has said he would have advised former Kaduna State governor, Nasir El-Rufai, to speak less if he had had the opportunity to speak with him before his legal battle began.Bello, who spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Fri
content:
Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has said he would have advised former Kaduna State governor, Nasir El-Rufai, to speak less if he had had the opportunity to speak with him before his legal battle began.

Bello, who spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, said he would have urged El-Rufai to talk less, remain in the All Progressives Congress (APC) that he helped build, and wait to see what President Bola Tinubu would do.

He described El-Rufai as a respected and idealistic person who pursues whatever he believes in.

Bello said that though he does not wish him “to go down the drain,” the embattled former Kaduna governor must have learnt how to handle political differences.

El-Rufai is facing legal battles involving the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and the Department of State Services (DSS), alongside allegations of financial misconduct and unlawful phone interception.

In October, the Court of Appeal dismissed his appeal against the refusal of bail in the alleged financial misconduct case, upholding his continued detention by the ICPC.

In a separate DSS prosecution over alleged unlawful interception of National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu’s telephone communications, the Federal High Court on October 26 dismissed his no-case submission and ordered him to enter his defence, adjourning proceedings to November 25.

The Kaduna corruption trial, involving an alleged ₦8.68 billion CCTV contract, was adjourned to December 8, while a ₦1 billion fundamental rights suit against the ICPC, police and AGF is scheduled for judgment on December 2.

content:
From Fred Ezeh, Abuja

The Nigerian Association of Resident Doctors (NARD) has commended President Bola Tinubu over the payment of long-standing arrears owed to healthcare workers across the country, some of which had remained outstanding for more than seven years.

The association described the intervention as a significant step towards addressing persistent welfare challenges in the health sector, saying it had brought relief to healthcare professionals who had waited for years to receive their entitlements.

The NARD National President, Dr Ogar Idoko, gave the commendation during a media engagement in Abuja, where he expressed appreciation to the President for responding to concerns surrounding the unpaid allowances and other outstanding financial obligations to health workers.

Idoko said the payment had been positively received by healthcare workers, noting that the development demonstrated goodwill on the part of the Federal Government and a willingness to address issues affecting the welfare of medical professionals.

He said the association was particularly pleased that the government had taken steps to clear obligations that had lingered for several years, adding that the intervention would help strengthen confidence in ongoing engagements between healthcare professionals and the government.

According to him, the payment represents an important development in efforts to improve the working conditions of health workers and address welfare-related grievances that have continued to feature prominently in discussions about the country’s healthcare system.

The NARD president, however, stressed the need for sustained attention to the welfare of healthcare workers, noting that timely payment of entitlements and improved working conditions were essential to maintaining an effective and motivated health workforce.

He reaffirmed the association’s commitment to constructive engagement with the Federal Government, explaining that sustained dialogue and collaboration remained critical to resolving outstanding issues and achieving lasting reforms in the health sector.

Idoko also emphasised that NARD would continue to pursue actionable advocacy and partnership with relevant government institutions to promote policies and interventions capable of improving the welfare of resident doctors and other healthcare professionals.

He noted that strengthening the healthcare system required collective efforts from government, medical professionals and other stakeholders, particularly in addressing challenges affecting service delivery and the retention of skilled personnel.

The association maintained that improving the welfare of healthcare workers was not only a labour-related concern but also an important component of efforts to guarantee quality healthcare delivery to Nigerians.

It expressed optimism that the latest intervention would provide a foundation for deeper collaboration with the government on other issues affecting the medical profession and the broader health sector.

NARD reiterated its readiness to work with the Federal Government towards building a stronger healthcare system, improving the working environment for medical personnel and ensuring that the welfare concerns of resident doctors receive sustained attention.

description:
The Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) says it has restored all transmission lines that tripped during a grid disturbance on Friday.



The management of NISO said this in a statement in Abuja on Friday.



The ​‌‍‌​⁠‍⁠⁠‍‍⁠​⁠​​‌‍‌​system operator also said
content:
The Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) says it has restored all transmission lines that tripped during a grid disturbance on Friday.

The management of NISO said this in a statement in Abuja on Friday.

The ​‌‍‌​⁠‍⁠⁠‍‍⁠​⁠​​‌‍‌​system operator also said that the incident was not a system collapse.

It said that the disturbance resulted from the tripping of some transmission line, which caused load losses in parts of the country.

”NISO wishes to clarify that the grid disturbance experienced earlier today was not a system collapse.

“It resulted from the tripping of some transmission lines, which caused load losses in parts of the country.

”At 12:34 p.m., the Omotosho–Ikeja West transmission line tripped, resulting in a significant load drop within the Lagos Complex.

”Subsequently, at 12:50 p.m, the Ihovbor–Oshogbo transmission line tripped alongside the Benin–Egbin and Ihovbor–Ajaokuta transmission lines, resulting in load losses in some parts of the country,” it said.

The system operator said that prompt emergency response measures were activated by the relevant operational teams in coordination with TCN to stabilize the grid and restore affected transmission lines.

It said that all the affected lines had since been successfully restored to normal operation as of 2:49 p.m. on Friday.

It reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining grid stability, coordinating system operations, and ensuring the reliable and secure operation of the Nigerian electricity grid.

”The public is advised to rely on official communications from NISO for accurate information on developments within the national electricity grid,” it said. (NAN)

The post Transmission lines restored after grid disturbance – NISO appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Afenifere demands prosecution of sponsors of campaign violence
description:
…Raises alarm over rising attacks ahead of 2027 elections



By Adeola Badru



The pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Afenifere, has raised the alarm over increasing political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, calling for the arrest and prosecution of perpetrators and their sponso
content:
…Raises alarm over rising attacks ahead of 2027 elections

By Adeola Badru

The pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Afenifere, has raised the alarm over increasing political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, calling for the arrest and prosecution of perpetrators and their sponsors.

The organisation warned that the growing incidents of thuggery, intimidation and inflammatory political rhetoric posed a serious threat to the country’s democratic process.

Afenifere, in a statement issued on Friday by its National Publicity Secretary, Jare Ajayi, called on political parties, candidates, their sponsors and supporters to end violence and ensure that campaigns were conducted in accordance with the Constitution and the Electoral Act.

Ajayi expressed concern over reported attacks on political figures, campaign convoys and supporters in different parts of the country, warning that the growing atmosphere of hostility could undermine public confidence in the electoral process and endanger lives.

Among the incidents cited was the reported attack on the motorcade of President Bola Tinubu on Friday, November 13, shortly after he observed Jumu’ah prayers at the Central Mosque, Abuja.

According to the organisation, assailants threw stones and other dangerous objects at the departing presidential convoy, damaging several vehicles and injuring some security operatives.

Afenifere also condemned the attack on supporters of the Accord Party governorship candidate in Oyo State, Oriyomi Hamzat, around the Molete area of Ibadan, which reportedly resulted in the death of a 40-year-old supporter, Azeez Tajudeen.

It described the incident as particularly disturbing, saying the destruction of vehicles and loss of life highlighted the consequences of allowing political differences to degenerate into violence.

The organisation further listed the reported attack on the convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) vice-presidential candidate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, in Bichi, Kano State; the reported assault on the convoy of the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, in Calabar, Cross River State; and disruptions of political gatherings, particularly those of the APC and ADC in Sokoto, Kebbi and Lagos states.

It said the incidents reflected a disturbing pattern requiring urgent intervention by political leaders and security agencies.

Ajayi also recalled the warning by former President Goodluck Jonathan at the 2026 Goodluck Jonathan Foundation Peace Conference in Abuja, where he cautioned political leaders against running their parties like rival cult groups.

Jonathan had warned against recruiting and exploiting young Nigerians for political violence, saying such practices could plunge the country into avoidable crises.

Similarly, Senate President Godswill Akpabio had cautioned youths against allowing themselves to be used for political violence, warning that perpetrators could face serious criminal charges, including treasonable felony.

Afenifere also referenced concerns raised by former Head of State, General Abdulsalami Abubakar, and the National Peace Committee’s Co-convener, Most Rev. Matthew Kukah, over inflammatory political campaigns.

The interventions, it noted, followed reports of about 60 election-related incidents across the country within a month.

The organisation also recalled President Tinubu’s directive condemning political violence across party lines and insisting that the 2027 elections should be defined by ideas rather than hostility.

Highlighting the legal implications of electoral violence, Afenifere reminded political parties, candidates and their sponsors that recruiting, organising or financing political thugs constituted a criminal offence under Nigerian law.

It cited Section 227 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which prohibits political parties and associations from retaining, organising, training or equipping individuals or groups to use physical force or coercion in promoting political objectives.

It also referenced Section 78 of the Electoral Act, which, according to the organisation, prescribes fines of N5 million for a first offence and N7 million for subsequent offences by political parties, as well as N500,000 for every day the offence continues.

Individuals or groups who aid or abet such violations could also face a fine of N5 million, imprisonment for five years or both, it said.

Ajayi further cited Sections 92 and 93 of the Electoral Act, which criminalise political thuggery and the direct or indirect use or threat of force during election campaigns.

He said offenders could face up to 12 months’ imprisonment or a fine of N1 million, while political parties found culpable could also incur financial penalties.

“The provisions of the laws are quite clear. But impunity persists because sponsors of violence are rarely brought to book,” Ajayi said.

He urged political leaders to call their supporters to order, stressing that those seeking political offices had a responsibility to ensure peaceful campaigns.

The Afenifere spokesman also appealed to Nigerian youths not to allow themselves to be used as instruments of violence by politicians.

“Nigerian youths must refuse to be used as cannon fodders by desperate politicians whose own children are safely tucked away from harm,” he warned.

He urged political actors to respect the President’s position that the 2027 elections should be a democratic contest characterised by the exchange of ideas, peaceful participation and respect for the rights of Nigerians.

Afenifere further called on stakeholders to ensure that political parties and candidates enjoyed equal protection and freedom to campaign in every part of the country without harassment, intimidation or threats to their safety.

The organisation specifically challenged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), the Nigeria Police Force and the judiciary to move beyond public condemnations and take concrete action against electoral violence.

It demanded the prompt arrest and prosecution of those responsible for attacks, including individuals and groups financing or sponsoring them, as well as the disqualification of offenders where permitted by law.

Afenifere insisted that accountability should not end with the arrest of foot soldiers, but must extend to those who finance, organise and deploy political thugs.

It warned that failure to decisively address political violence could undermine the credibility of the 2027 elections and threaten Nigeria’s democratic stability beyond the polls.

title: Lagos diverts traffic in Ikeja for Saturday’s race
description:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni



The Lagos State Government has announced intermittent traffic diversions along major roads in Ikeja ahead of the third edition of the Capital City Race scheduled for Saturday, November 21, 2026.







The traffic management arrangement, according to the Commissioner for Tran
content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

The Lagos State Government has announced intermittent traffic diversions along major roads in Ikeja ahead of the third edition of the Capital City Race scheduled for Saturday, November 21, 2026.

The traffic management arrangement, according to the Commissioner for Transportation, Oluwaseun Osiyemi, will commence at 7 a.m. to ensure the smooth conduct of the 10-kilometre race.

Roads and corridors to be affected include Ikeja City Mall, Billings Way, Kudirat Abiola Way, Opebi Link Bridge, Adeniyi Jones, Oba Akran Road by the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital (LASUTH), and Archbishop Vining Memorial Church.

Osiyemi said personnel of the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA), Nigeria Police Force (NPF), Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) and Lagos State Neighbourhood Safety Corps (LNSC) would be deployed to junctions and intersections along the race route to manage traffic.

He explained that the diversions would be partial, with affected roads reopened intermittently to motorists as runners cleared each section of the route.

The commissioner, however, did not specify when the traffic restrictions would end and normal vehicular movement fully resume.

The state government appealed to motorists to cooperate with traffic management officials and exercise patience throughout the event to minimise inconvenience.

title: Obi woos Onitsha voters, promises jobs, better services
description:
…Says Nigeria needs energetic president



By Vincent Ujumadu



The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, on Friday drew a large crowd in Onitsha, Anambra State, as he led members of his campaign team on a roadshow and town hall meeting in the commercial city.
content:
…Says Nigeria needs energetic president

By Vincent Ujumadu

The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, on Friday drew a large crowd in Onitsha, Anambra State, as he led members of his campaign team on a roadshow and town hall meeting in the commercial city.

Obi began his visit with a stop at his alma mater, Christ the King College (CKC), Onitsha, where he told students that the institution had produced three state governors and could soon produce Nigeria’s president.

The three former governors he identified were Peter Odili of Rivers State, Obi himself and Willie Obiano, who succeeded him as governor of Anambra State.

Addressing the students, Obi promised to improve the standard of education across the country if elected president in the 2027 general elections.

His campaign train subsequently moved through Oguta Road, Upper Iweka, Head Bridge, Uga Road and Modebe Avenue before arriving at All Saints Cathedral, venue of the town hall meeting.

Among those who accompanied him during the roadshow were Aisha Yesufu and other members of his campaign team.

Traders at the drug market and building materials market lined the streets, dancing to campaign music, while several traders reportedly closed their shops to attend the town hall meeting.

Addressing supporters at the gathering, Obi said he and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, had formed a team committed to uniting the country, tackling insecurity and corruption, and ensuring that public resources were used for the benefit of Nigerians.

“Kwankwaso and I have formed a team that will unite and secure Nigeria. We will secure Nigeria, fight corruption and use public money for public good.

“I assure Nigerians that from day one, they will be feeling the good impact of their country. You will know that a new team is in charge,” he said.

He promised to move Nigeria from a consumption-driven economy to one centred on production, create employment opportunities and invest in critical sectors.

“We cannot continue with the present situation where our children don’t have jobs because that is not the way a country should be,” he said.

On healthcare, Obi advocated a system where Nigerians could access functional medical facilities without having to depend on religious institutions for treatment.

He pledged to establish functional primary healthcare centres in every ward and said his proposed administration would build 10,000 healthcare centres across the country.

He also promised that his administration would commence the construction of 40,000 classroom blocks from its first day in office, alongside increased investment in education and healthcare.

On electricity, the former Anambra governor expressed concern over Nigeria’s power generation capacity, which he put at about 5,000 megawatts.

He said his proposed administration would work towards generating, transmitting and distributing 10,000 megawatts of electricity.

Obi urged Nigerians to hold him and his running mate accountable for their campaign promises, insisting that they were not making promises without understanding the country’s challenges.

“We don’t want to make false promises. We are not going to tell Nigerians what we saw when we came in. We are seeing everything now and we are planning for it,” he said.

He also urged voters to actively participate in the 2027 elections and protect their votes by remaining at polling units until votes were counted and results transmitted.

“I want all of you to know that you are contestants in the forthcoming elections, although you are doing it through those of us that are candidates. So, on that day, sacrifice it for Nigeria,” he told the gathering.

He urged voters to remain at their polling units after casting their ballots, adding that they should not be intimidated into leaving before the conclusion of the counting and result-transmission processes.

Obi also called on supporters to vote for NDC candidates in the presidential, senatorial and House of Representatives elections, as well as the subsequent House of Assembly election.

On the economy, he criticised the Federal Government’s handling of the removal of petrol subsidy, arguing that the policy had contributed to rising living costs and worsening hardship.

He also questioned the government’s borrowing, alleging that it had accumulated more debt than previous administrations combined, while raising concerns about the implementation of successive national budgets.

“Today, he has borrowed more money than all the previous governments put together. The question is, where is our money?” he asked.

Obi called for a change of government in 2027, saying Nigeria needed leadership defined by competence, compassion, commitment and character.

He also questioned President Bola Tinubu’s capacity to sustain the demands of the presidency, arguing that the country needed an energetic leader.

“Above all, we want a government that has energy. Our current president has to go and rest because he is tired. This job requires energy and the person doing it must have energy. That is why we are begging him to go and rest,” he said.

The post Obi woos Onitsha voters, promises jobs, better services appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Oyedele urges banks to prioritise agricultural lending
description:
…Commissions Moniepoint Abuja branch



By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief



The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has urged banks and other financial institutions to make loans more affordable and accessible to businesses, particularly those operating in th
content:
…Commissions Moniepoint Abuja branch

By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has urged banks and other financial institutions to make loans more affordable and accessible to businesses, particularly those operating in the agricultural sector, to stimulate productivity and economic growth.

Oyedele made the call on Friday at the commissioning of the Abuja branch office of Moniepoint Microfinance Bank (MFB).

He said access to affordable financing remained a major challenge for small businesses, stressing that interest rates, fees, repayment periods and the time required to secure loans must be considered in determining the usefulness of credit facilities.

“We also must make business finance more affordable and more useful for many small businesses. The challenge is obtaining finance at a cost and on terms that they can sustain.

“Affordability involves the interest rates, the fees that we charge, the repayment period, and time spent securing even that facility itself. All of these decide whether financing helps a business or puts it under strain,” he said.

The minister said while the government had a responsibility to strengthen economic conditions to make financing more affordable, financial institutions must also contribute through efficient operations, improved risk assessment and transparent pricing.

He particularly emphasised the need for increased lending to agriculture, noting that every segment of the value chain required adequate financial support.

According to him, farmers need timely access to inputs and working capital, aggregators require funds to purchase produce, while processors need financing for equipment, storage and reliable supplies.

He added that transporters and traders also required financial support to move agricultural products efficiently to consumers.

Oyedele said appropriate financing for the sector would boost food production, reduce post-harvest losses, improve rural incomes and create employment opportunities.

He, however, cautioned that agricultural lending must reflect the realities of farming, including production cycles, weather conditions and market risks.

“Repayment schedules should follow production and harvest cycles. Lending decisions should recognise risks such as weather and market conditions, and partnerships with cooperatives, insurers, buyers and other credible participants can help lenders understand and manage them better,” he said.

The minister urged Moniepoint to deepen its engagement with agricultural businesses and develop practical partnerships to support viable enterprises.

On data protection, Oyedele called on financial institutions to strengthen safeguards around customers’ personal and financial information to protect them against fraud and other abuses.

He said public confidence in the financial system depended on customers being assured that their money was safe, their information was handled responsibly and the terms of financial products were clearly explained.

He also stressed the importance of customer education on protecting account credentials, identifying suspicious messages and reporting suspected fraud.

According to him, financial institutions must provide accessible complaint-resolution channels and ensure customers know who is handling their complaints and when to expect a response.

He said cooperation between financial institutions and regulators remained essential to sustaining confidence in the financial system as digital financial services expanded.

Oyedele commended Moniepoint for establishing its Abuja office, noting that the Federal Capital Territory provided a strategic location for serving businesses and communities across the North-Central and Northern regions.

“The location of this hub is significant. Abuja connects important commercial routes and provides a base for serving communities across North-Central and Northern Nigeria, including areas with substantial agricultural potential,” he said.

In his remarks, the Chief Executive Officer of Moniepoint, Tunde Olofin, described the financial institution as a bank of choice, attributing its growth to its digital banking services and innovative products.

He listed instant settlement for businesses and working capital loans among the products that had strengthened the bank’s appeal to customers.

Olofin said the opening of the Abuja branch marked an expansion of the bank’s services beyond digital channels, providing customers with physical locations where they could receive face-to-face support and interact with business relationship managers.

He said the bank planned to establish more branches in additional states to bring its services closer to customers.

Olofin reaffirmed the institution’s commitment to building what he described as financial happiness for every Nigerian.

Also speaking, the Managing Director of Shared Agent Network Expansion Facilities (SANEF) Limited, Uche Uzoebo, commended Moniepoint’s innovation and urged young Nigerians to contribute to national development.

She said Nigerians must take responsibility for building the country rather than expecting others to do so.

“I want to tell us Nigerians that we have to believe in ourselves. If we don’t build this place, nobody will build Nigeria for us,” she said.

title: Tinubu focused on next generation, not next election, Owan-Enoh says
description:
…Targets APC victory in all 18 Cross River LGAs



By Ike Uchechukwu, Calabar



The Minister of State for Industry, Senator John Owan-Enoh, has said President Bola Tinubu is focused on building a prosperous future for Nigerians rather than seeking victory at the next election.







Owan-Enoh stat
content:
…Targets APC victory in all 18 Cross River LGAs

By Ike Uchechukwu, Calabar

The Minister of State for Industry, Senator John Owan-Enoh, has said President Bola Tinubu is focused on building a prosperous future for Nigerians rather than seeking victory at the next election.

Owan-Enoh stated this on Friday at Ikom Township Stadium during the inauguration of the Cross River chapter of Project Beyond’s executive and polling unit structures for the Central and Northern Senatorial Districts of the state.

He described Tinubu as a pragmatic leader whose decisions were driven by long-term national development rather than immediate political considerations.

The minister likened the President’s leadership approach to that of Singapore’s founding Prime Minister, Lee Kuan Yew, whom he credited with transforming the Asian country into a global success story.

“That Prime Minister didn’t look at politics the same way a politician looks at the next election. That Prime Minister looked at the next generation.

“That is what President Bola Tinubu is doing,” he said.

Owan-Enoh acknowledged that the President’s economic reforms had subjected many Nigerians to hardship but described the sacrifices as temporary measures necessary for economic recovery.

He likened the reforms to bitter medicine that would eventually restore the country’s economic health.

“That tablet is bitter. But after that bitterness, you’ll get well,” he said.

According to him, Nigeria has begun experiencing economic recovery and stability after three and a half years of the administration’s policies.

He said the government’s next priority was to translate the gains into prosperity and improved purchasing power for Nigerians.

“Three and a half years later, recovery has started. Stability has set in, and I think for President Tinubu, the next concentration is prosperity.

“The next concentration is the power of your pocket,” he said.

The minister further claimed that inflation had declined to about 14 per cent, expressing optimism that it would continue to fall towards single digits.

He urged Cross River residents to support Tinubu’s re-election, arguing that the state needed to maintain its influence in national decision-making.

“You will need to sit at the table when decisions are taken for you to be able to put before that table what you want,” he said.

Owan-Enoh said securing the state’s political relevance required a strong electoral showing for the APC in the 2027 general elections.

Recalling the 2023 presidential election, he said Tinubu won in seven of Cross River’s 18 local government areas.

He, however, challenged party members to work towards securing victory in all 18 local government areas in the January 16, 2027 presidential election.

“In 2023, out of 18 local governments, the President won seven.

“In 2027, we must leave here with a determination and a resolve that, come January 16, 2027, Mr President is going to win 18 over 18 in Cross River, and that is possible,” he said.

content:
Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, on Friday attracted a large crowd in Onitsha, Anambra State, as he led his campaign team on a roadshow and town hall engagements ahead of the 2027 general elections. He began with a visit to his alma mater, Christ the King College (CKC), Onitsha, where he addressed students and said the school would produce Nigeria’s president in the future.

Stay At Polling Units To Protect Votes, Obi Urges Voters

Obi urged Nigerians to remain at polling units after voting to ensure their votes are counted and transmitted, declaring that nobody would be allowed to rig the 2027 general elections. Speaking at the town hall at All Saints Cathedral, Onitsha, he told supporters: “Sacrifice one day for Nigeria. That day of voting,” and to come with food and stay until votes are counted and transmitted.

Obi, Kwankwaso Pledge 10,000MW Power Supply

Obi promised that a government led by him and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, would generate, transmit, and distribute at least 10,000MW of electricity. He said Nigeria currently only generates, transmits, and distributes about 4,000MW, and that within their tenure Nigeria would reach at least 10,000MW.

Obi Promises 10,000 Health Centres, 40,000 Classrooms

Obi promised to establish 10,000 primary healthcare centres and build 40,000 primary school blocks across the country if elected president in 2027. He made the promises on Friday during the NDC town hall meeting at All Saints Cathedral, Onitsha.

Anambra Govt Says Obi Billboard Removed Over Signage Law, Not Politics

The Anambra State Government clarified that the campaign billboard belonging to Senator Victor Umeh, which featured Obi, was removed over an alleged violation of the state’s Signage Act, 2010, contrary to claims it was pulled down because of Obi’s identity. The state said although Umeh had paid the required signage fee, Obi had not complied with the payment requirement.

Don’t Attack Defectors, Obidient Coordinator Warns Supporters

The National Coordinator of the Global Obidient Movement, Dr Moses Paul, urged supporters not to insult or attack individuals who have left the group, saying political engagement should be guided by “respect and decency rather than bitterness”. He said the directive came from Obi, urging members to refrain from insulting, attacking, or making derogatory comments about those who decided to leave the movement.

The post The Obidient Pulse: Massive Crowd As Obi Returns To Onitsha, Visits CKC Alma Mater appeared first on Channels Television.

title: 2027: Our achievements will speak for us, Namadi tells voters
description:
…Says administration needs no fresh campaign promises



By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse



Jigawa State Governor and All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for the 2027 election, Malam Umar Namadi, has said his administration’s achievements in the last three years would serve as its campai
content:
…Says administration needs no fresh campaign promises

By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse

Jigawa State Governor and All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for the 2027 election, Malam Umar Namadi, has said his administration’s achievements in the last three years would serve as its campaign message, insisting that it does not need to make fresh promises to secure re-election.

Namadi stated this on Wednesday while addressing a large crowd of APC supporters during the flag-off of the party’s campaign in the South-West Senatorial District at Jahun Local Government Area of the state.

The governor said his administration had recorded achievements in agriculture, healthcare, education, electricity, job creation and other critical sectors, adding that its performance should be the basis for seeking another mandate.

“We are here not to make promises. What we have done in the last three years is enough for you to put your trust in us,” he said.

“Some other candidates will come to you making promises about what they will do, but for us, it is about what we have achieved in the last three years.”

He reiterated his commitment to improving infrastructure, connecting communities and making life easier for residents, assuring that his administration would sustain its development agenda if re-elected.

Namadi expressed satisfaction with the turnout of party members and supporters, describing it as a demonstration of confidence in the APC and its leadership.

He also highlighted development projects executed by the Jigawa State and Federal Governments across the senatorial district, assuring party members that the APC would reach every town and village to mobilise support for its candidates.

The governor reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to prioritising agriculture, education, healthcare, skills development, entrepreneurship and social welfare.

“We will continue to give priority to agriculture, education, healthcare, skills development, entrepreneurship and social welfare because these are critical areas for building a better future for our people,” he said.

On agricultural development, Namadi said his administration would sustain its partnership with the Federal Government to boost food production, strengthen food security and promote economic prosperity.

“Our partnership with the Federal Government in agriculture will continue to support food production, strengthen food security and promote economic prosperity in Jigawa State and across the country.

“We are determined to ensure that the benefits of these efforts reach our farmers, households and communities,” he added.

Namadi urged residents of the South-West Senatorial District to turn out in large numbers on January 16 and February 6, 2027, to vote for APC candidates, from President Bola Tinubu to candidates contesting seats in the State House of Assembly.

He also called for unity among party supporters, urging them to sustain what he described as the progress recorded under APC-led governments.

The post 2027: Our achievements will speak for us, Namadi tells voters appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Diri’s kinsmen declare support for Dickson, NDC
description:
By Henry Umoru



ABUJA — Political stakeholders and members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) from Kolokuma/Opokuma, the constituency of Bayelsa State Governor Douye Diri, have declared support for the party’s National Leader, Senator Seriake Dickson, and his political leadership.



The del
content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — Political stakeholders and members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) from Kolokuma/Opokuma, the constituency of Bayelsa State Governor Douye Diri, have declared support for the party’s National Leader, Senator Seriake Dickson, and his political leadership.

The delegation, comprising NDC candidates, stakeholders and party members from Kolokuma/Opokuma and Yenagoa Federal Constituency, made the declaration when they visited Dickson at his country home in Toru-Orua, Bayelsa State, to pay homage and demonstrate solidarity with him.

The development comes as Governor Diri, who hails from Kolokuma/Opokuma, has joined the All Progressives Congress (APC).

The delegation presented drinks, gifts and food items to Dickson in appreciation of his contributions to the people and his role in providing a political platform for their aspirations.

Speaking during the visit, the senator representing Bayelsa West said his political journey had been driven by a commitment to justice, equity, recognition, integration and freedom for oppressed people rather than personal ambition or material gains.

Dickson, who described himself as a politician motivated by a mission and a cause, said his political convictions were founded on the determination to fight for what was right, fair and beneficial to the people.

He maintained that his years in public service, including his tenure as governor and senator, had been guided by the collective interest of the people rather than personal enrichment.

In a statement signed by his spokesman, Steve Nwosu, the NDC leader said individual ambitions must always be subordinated to the general good, stressing that politics should be about service, responsibility, dignity and societal advancement.

He said these were the values the NDC intended to promote and institutionalise as it worked towards building a different political culture in Nigeria.

Dickson also acknowledged the historical significance of Kolokuma/Opokuma in the struggle for the emancipation and recognition of the Ijaw people, describing the area as a cradle of the Ijaw struggle.

He recalled that the importance he attached to the area informed his decision to establish the Ijaw National Academy there.

The former governor thanked the delegation for their solidarity and commitment to the NDC and the Niger Delta cause, describing the visit as a demonstration of shared values and a collective determination to advance the political and developmental aspirations of the region.

Speaking on behalf of the delegation, the member representing Kolokuma/Opokuma Constituency II in the Bayelsa State House of Assembly, Dr Fafi Wisdom, assured Dickson of the continued support of political stakeholders from the area.

Wisdom said the visit was organised to appreciate Dickson’s contributions to the development of Kolokuma and Yenagoa and reaffirm confidence in his leadership.

He particularly commended the NDC leader for providing opportunities for indigenes of the area to contest elective positions on the party’s platform despite prevailing political challenges.

He insisted that many people in Kolokuma remained appreciative of Dickson’s sacrifices, political investments and efforts to create opportunities for their people.

The lawmaker also expressed confidence in the NDC’s prospects in the forthcoming elections, declaring that the party had established a presence in Kolokuma/Opokuma.

He said its growing acceptance and expanding political structures were attracting attention among political opponents.

Wisdom further welcomed the entry of a prominent political figure popularly known as the German Machine into the NDC, describing the development as a boost to the party’s mobilisation and grassroots engagement.

He expressed optimism that the politician’s involvement would strengthen the party’s existing structures and attract more supporters ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Earlier, another delegation comprising NDC candidates from Bayelsa West also visited Dickson at his country home in Toru-Orua.

Led by Hon. Selekebina Saboh, the delegation presented drinks, gifts and food items to the senator in appreciation of his leadership and role in founding the NDC.

They described the party as a platform that had provided them with opportunities to pursue their political aspirations.

The post Diri’s kinsmen declare support for Dickson, NDC appeared first on Vanguard News.

The dire
content:
…Bans movement of timber after 7pm

By Dayo Johnson, Akure

The Ondo State Government has ordered the immediate removal and impoundment of timber stockpiled along roadsides across the 18 local government areas of the state following a fatal road accident that claimed three lives.

The directive also prohibits the movement of logs after 7pm, with the government warning that vehicles found violating the restriction would be impounded alongside their cargo.

The Senior Special Assistant to the Governor on Forestry, Bidemi Joshua Obayangban, announced the measures following the death of three persons in an auto crash at Ominla, along the Okitipupa–Ore Road.

Obayangban blamed the accident on the illegal stockpiling of timber along major roads, which he said narrowed roadways and obstructed motorists’ views.

In a statement, he commiserated with the families of the deceased and sympathised with others affected by the incident.

He said timber dealers, loaders and transporters had repeatedly been warned against leaving felled logs beside roads, noting that the practice posed serious dangers to motorists.

He also warned that loading and transporting timber at night endangered road users and provided cover for illegal logging and timber theft.

“Apart from the fact that these logs are illegal, they are actively causing road accidents and were the exact cause of the fatal crash that occurred on the Okitipupa–Ore Road,” he said.

According to him, stockpiling felled logs along roads and highways in the state is prohibited, while roadside and highway loading are also banned.

He added that vehicles must not load or transport logs after 7pm, warning that those found violating the directive would be impounded with their cargo.

“Logs already stockpiled along roads must be removed without delay,” he said.

Obayangban said the Government Task Force on Forestry would work with security agencies to enforce the directives across the state, warning that offenders would face the full weight of the law.

He also cautioned timber contractors, farmers and loggers against individuals or groups falsely presenting themselves as members of the forestry task force.

According to the statement, the only task force recognised by the state government and the Ministry of the Environment is the one constituted by the Senior Special Assistant on Forestry.

He said members of the task force carry identification cards bearing the SSA’s telephone number, which contractors and loggers can use to verify their identities.

Obayangban urged timber contractors, dealers, loaders and drivers to cooperate with the government, stressing that no business activity was worth endangering human lives.

He said the government was determined to keep highways across the state free from hazardous activities capable of causing fatal accidents and directed all forestry task forces to begin immediate clearance of roadside timber stockpiles.

The post Ondo orders removal of roadside logs after fatal crash appeared first on Vanguard News.

Launches ITESIWAJU Manifesto
______________________________________________________________________
From Laide Raheem, Abeokuta
The All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, on Friday promised that his administration would create 50,000
content:
Launches ITESIWAJU Manifesto

______________________________________________________________________

From Laide Raheem, Abeokuta

The All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, on Friday promised that his administration would create 50,000 jobs yearly, provide 200MW of power and launch between 50 and 100 CNG buses within the first 12 months, if elected governor in 2027.

Adeola made the promise while speaking at the formal launch of his ITESIWAJU Manifesto at the June 12 Cultural Centre, Abeokuta, the Ogun State capital. He also said his administration would construct no fewer than 2,500 kilometres of rural and urban roads across the state in four years, if given the mandate to lead Ogun.

The APC governorship candidate was addressing a gathering that included the National Leader of the APC and former governor of the state, Aremo Olusegun Osoba; Governor Dapo Abiodun; the State Chairman of the APC, Yemi Sanusi; and other party chieftains. He declared that the manifesto, titled “ITESIWAJU – Governance That Works For Everyone”, was a contract, not a campaign performance.

“This Agenda is a plan, not a performance. Read it as you would read a contract, because that is exactly what it is,” he said.

Adeola said the plan was built from his tour of all 20 local governments, where he met royal fathers, community leaders, women, youths, farmers and traders.

He described governance as a relay race, praising past leaders from Chief Olabisi Onabanjo to Chief Olusegun Osoba, Otunba Gbenga Daniel, Senator Ibikunle Amosun and Governor Dapo Abiodun.

He credited Abiodun’s ISEYA agenda with the Agro-Cargo Airport, dry ports, over 1,700km of roads, over 7,000 housing units and a ₦17 trillion economy.

“Where ISEYA built infrastructure, we will connect such to the world. Where ISEYA empowered our youth, we will turn their talent into great enterprise,” he said.

On his origins, Adeola traced his roots to Ago Isaga, Pahayi, Ilaro, and Kemta Odutolu, Abeokuta, crediting President Bola Tinubu as his political mentor.

As Senator for Ogun West, he said he had facilitated 1,015 projects across all 20 LGAs, and that his bill upgrading the Federal Polytechnic, Ilaro, to a Federal University of Technology was now law.

While introducing his running mate, Alhaja Kudirat Abiodun Adegunwa-Balogun, Adeola declared that his deputy was not a spare tyre but an important partner in governance.

He promised fiscal discipline through a Single Window Revenue Collection System, with no new taxes and no double taxation.

Within 30 days of taking office, he promised a Governor’s Delivery Unit, performance agreements for commissioners, a public dashboard tracking six indicators quarterly, and an annual State of Ogun Report.

“We will measure progress not by the ribbons we cut, but by the lives we change,” he said.

Adeola also assured the people of Ogun West, who have waited 50 years since 1976 to produce a governor, that their waiting had not been in vain.

“My roots are in Yewaland; my duty is to all of Ogun. I do not ask you to believe me. I ask you to hold me to this covenant,” Adeola concluded.

Earlier, in his welcome address, the Ogun APC State Chairman, Yemi Sanusi, said the event was meant to tell the people of the state about the next chapter of the government.

He commended Governor Abiodun for ensuring a hitch-free consensus arrangement that produced Senator Adeola, expressing confidence that the governorship candidate would continue to take Ogun to a higher pedestal.

In his remarks, Osoba expressed delight that the state would move further forward with Adeola at the helm of affairs.

Osoba urged the people of the state to vote massively for Senator Adeola as the next governor of Ogun so that he could continue the good work of the incumbent administration.

The post Ogun 2027: I’ll create 50,000 jobs yearly, launch 100 CNG buses within one year if elected governor – Adeola appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: FG backs Abuja aviation school as regional training hub
description:
Nigeria is targeting a reduction in its annual foreign aviation training expenditure as the Federal Government backs the development of Baze Aviation School into a regional training hub expected to attract pilots and other aviation professionals from across West and Central Africa.
The Minister of A
content:
Nigeria is targeting a reduction in its annual foreign aviation training expenditure as the Federal Government backs the development of Baze Aviation School into a regional training hub expected to attract pilots and other aviation professionals from across West and Central Africa.

The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, stated this on Friday, during a familiarisation and inspection tour of the aviation training facility in Bwari, Abuja, where he described the project as a major investment in local capacity development and the future of the aviation industry.

He noted that the facility would enable Nigeria to retain a significant portion of the money currently spent sending aviation personnel abroad for specialised training, while positioning the country as a destination for aviation education.

“We spend a lot of money every year sending our pilots and other aviation personnel to different parts of the world for training. With this facility, we expect that a significant part of that expenditure will be retained within Nigeria,” Keyamo said.

The minister noted that Nigerian airline captains and other aviation professionals currently travelled to countries such as South Africa and the United States for specialised training and simulator services, with airlines and employers bearing substantial costs.

He expressed optimism that the proposed simulator centre, equipped with facilities associated with major aircraft manufacturers such as Boeing and Airbus, would reduce the country’s dependence on foreign training institutions.

Beyond serving Nigerian aviation professionals, Keyamo said the institution was expected to attract trainees from neighbouring countries and become one of the leading aviation training centres in West and Central Africa.

He, however, warned government officials against frustrating the project through bureaucratic delays, assuring its promoters of the Federal Government’s support.

“Nobody should frustrate this project. No bureaucracy or official should keep your files or hide them somewhere, forcing you to run from one office to another. Don’t go around looking for anybody. Don’t even look for me. Let this project come to fruition,” he said.

Keyamo described the initiative as a national development project that should enjoy support irrespective of ethnic, religious or political differences. He urged the promoters to report any official attempting to obstruct its progress, promising to intervene within his supervisory and regulatory responsibilities.

Earlier, the founder of Baze University, Datti Baba-Ahmed, disclosed that the aviation school was being developed as a comprehensive aviation ecosystem, comprising a runway, hangars, terminal, academic facilities, accommodation and emergency response infrastructure.

He said the master plan included four hangars, a heliport, airside facilities, a runway safety area, an air traffic control building, airline management offices, aviation security facilities, a clinic and an emergency response centre.

The project would also accommodate original equipment manufacturers, with provisions for maintenance, repair and overhaul facilities, hotels and other hospitality services.

Giving an update on construction, Baba-Ahmed said the apron was being developed to cover 500 metres, with 155 metres already completed.

He added that work on the granular sub-base for the first 1,000 metres of the runway was about 95 per cent completed, while the remaining section of the initial kilometre was expected to be finished by the end of November.

According to him, the first phase of runway pavement construction would begin in December, followed by asphalt surfacing, after which the institution would seek approval from the aviation minister to commence flight training.

Baba-Ahmed said the first 1,000 metres of the runway was expected to be ready by January, providing capacity to accommodate virtually all categories of light aircraft.

He also disclosed that the school’s two Grand Caravan aircraft had arrived in Nigeria, adding that the aircraft and ongoing infrastructure development had generated interest among prospective trainees and parents seeking aviation careers for their children.

He said the institution was undertaking much of the construction itself to ensure quality, timely delivery and cost efficiency, while engaging specialised partners for technical aspects of the project.

The development has also generated expectations among host communities, with local leaders anticipating employment opportunities, improved economic activities and access to aviation careers for their children.

A representative of Gaba community and retired police officer, Mr Bulus Luka, said the institution would transform the economic and social fortunes of surrounding communities.

He expressed optimism that young people from Gaba, Nako and Tokolo villages could eventually become pilots and other aviation professionals through opportunities created by the school.

Luka said businesses had already begun springing up around the facility, adding that economic activities would increase as construction progressed and the institution commenced operations.

He, however, called for cooperation among traditional rulers and community leaders in the three communities to ensure residents maximised the benefits of the development.

The aviation school is expected to create a new training pathway for Nigerian and regional aviation professionals, while opening opportunities for investment, employment and the development of supporting aviation services.

The post FG backs Abuja aviation school as regional training hub appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2026 APEC Leaders’ Shenzhen Outlook: Building an Asia-Pacific community to prosper together
description: We, the Economic Leaders of APEC, gathered in Shenzhen, China, on 18 to 19 November 2026. Decades after APEC’s establishment, our sustained efforts have helped make our region a key engine of global growth and a champion of regional economic cooperation. Under the theme “Building an Asia-Pacific Com
content:
1. We, the Economic Leaders of APEC, gathered in Shenzhen, China, on 18 to 19 November 2026. Decades after APEC’s establishment, our sustained efforts have helped make our region a key engine of global growth and a champion of regional economic cooperation. Under the theme “Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together”, we have built on our work throughout the year with China’s APEC 2026 priorities “Openness, Innovation, Cooperation”, and advanced our shared objectives towards realising an open, dynamic, resilient and peaceful Asia-Pacific community, guided by the Putrajaya Vision 2040.
  2. The world today is changing rapidly, with new opportunities emerging alongside complex challenges. Technological breakthroughs are contributing to the economic growth, resilience and dynamism of our region. We endeavour to work together to maintain macroeconomic stability, promote productivity and dynamism, and boost economic growth for the benefit of all our people.
  3. APEC has long been at the forefront of regional economic cooperation, and its enduring role remains relevant in the current economic context. We reaffirm our commitment to APEC as the premier forum for regional economic cooperation, guided by its voluntary, non-binding and consensus-building principles, and to making APEC a more modern, efficient and effective incubator of ideas.

Trade and investment

  1. We underscore that supporting efforts to improve the trade and investment environment is important to our region. We reaffirm our commitments to strengthening supply chain resilience and deepening regional economic cooperation to build robust and resilient economies, contributing to the sustained economic growth and prosperity of our region.
  2. We will continue advancing economic integration in the Asia-Pacific region in a manner that is market-driven, including through the work on the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific (FTAAP) agenda. We recognise that the FTAAP agenda plays an important role in building economies’ capacity to participate in high-standard and comprehensive regional undertakings.
  3. We recognise the important role of digitalisation as a driver for innovation, productivity and economic growth across the region, and its benefit in facilitating trade. In this context, we welcome the APEC Trade Digitalization Cooperation Framework (2027–2030) to guide our efforts to foster a supportive policy environment, strengthen policy exchange and promote the use of digital technologies for trade digitalisation. We will continue to facilitate trade, including through measures to advance paperless trade and cross-border e-commerce. We are also committed to harnessing the benefits of emerging technologies for trade.
  4. Recognising the contribution of the services sector to economic growth and job creation, and the expanding role of digitally delivered services, we will continue to enhance the competitiveness of the APEC economies in the sector. We note the impacts of environmental and related challenges and encourage APEC economies to consider how capacity building and exchanges of experience can help meet their respective environmental and trade objectives. We also recognise APEC’s past and ongoing work to foster cooperation in advancing resilient business models. We acknowledge the positive contribution of the cultural and creative industries (CCIs) to economic growth, and affirm the importance of robust intellectual property protections. We are committed to enhancing the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights, as well as continued efforts to address challenges faced by innovators, creators and other right holders.

Connectivity

  1. We affirm that connectivity has served as a conduit for economic growth, facilitating the flow of goods, services, capital and people, including as supported by safe and resilient transport links. We appreciate the efforts made by APEC to advance regional connectivity over the past decade. Building on this progress, we endorse the APEC Connectivity Blueprint, through which we encourage economies to continue efforts towards achieving a seamlessly and comprehensively connected and integrated Asia-Pacific, by further strengthening the three pillars: physical, institutional and people-to-people. We will continue to advance connectivity to deliver tangible benefits for all. We will enhance cooperation on quality infrastructure development and investment. We also underscore the importance of investment, including through ex-ante investment in disaster risk reduction.
  2. In the face of supply chain challenges impacting our region, we reaffirm our commitment to maintaining resilient supply chains, particularly for essential goods. We recognise that it is in our mutual interest that our region remains interconnected and trade corridors remain open to facilitate trade flows, including energy supplies and other essential goods. We affirm our resolve to work together and with other trade partners to ensure trade continues to flow and critical infrastructure continues to support the viability and integrity of supply chains globally. We support efforts to enhance supply chain resilience, address chokepoints, and leverage existing platforms in APEC to advance supply chain connectivity and trade facilitation. We welcome the final review of Phase Three of the Supply Chain Connectivity Framework Action Plan (SCFAP III) (2022–2026). We also recognise the importance of transparency of measures that may affect trade or disrupt supply chains.
  3. We will continue cooperation to advance innovation and foster ICT resilience in the transport sector. We will continue to promote good regulatory practices, strengthen cooperation on standards and conformity assessment procedures, and pursue structural reform to improve the business environment. We will also foster practical exchange of experience on trade digitalisation, supply chains and trade facilitation, and advance the digitalisation of customs and trade-related procedures. We encourage business mobility through the APEC Business Travel Card, and welcome economies’ efforts to advance tourism facilitation and strengthen education, skills development and cultural exchanges.

Innovation

  1. We recognise that technology and innovation are profoundly reshaping our economies and rapidly driving economic growth in the Asia-Pacific region. We will leverage technological advancement to pursue innovation-driven and productivity-led growth, improve quality of life, and promote prosperity and opportunity for all our peoples. To this end, we support science, technology and innovation cooperation to foster a competitive, resilient and secure innovation ecosystem. We encourage the voluntary exchange of good practices to support the growth of local innovation ecosystems.
  2. We reaffirm our commitment to growing the digital economy and sharing the benefits of digital transformation with all our peoples. We encourage economies to advance digital connectivity and bridge digital divides across all segments of society and across regions between urban and rural areas, strengthen accessible and resilient digital infrastructure, promote digital transformation for economic growth, enhance digital literacy and skills, and promote the development of digital platforms. We encourage economies to address potential risks such as data breaches, online scams and deliberate misuse of digital and emerging technologies for malicious purposes, to strengthen and enhance the digital environment. We recognise the importance of respecting intellectual property rights in the development of digital and emerging technologies. We recognise the vital role of data in powering digital transformation. We will continue our cooperation on facilitating the flow of data across borders, strengthening business and consumer trust in digital transactions, and ensuring data protection and privacy.
  3. We underscore that digital and emerging technologies present transformative opportunities to boost productivity, efficiency, competitiveness, resilience and economic growth across the Asia-Pacific. We commend APEC’s efforts to advance discussions on digital and emerging technologies, including the APEC AI Initiative (2026–2030), and endorse the APEC Statement on Harnessing Digital and Emerging Technologies for Employment and Prosperity in the Asia-Pacific Region to continue this important work. We will support human-centric innovation, responsible approaches, and the adoption of digital and emerging technologies across all sectors of the economy for the benefit of all our peoples. We support driving the transformation of key sectors through digital and emerging technologies, harnessing them to improve public service delivery, including strengthening healthcare systems, fostering an enabling environment for businesses, promoting market-oriented and innovation-driven approaches, and empowering micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) with accessible digital tools. We will continue to invest in infrastructure related to digital and emerging technologies and advance data utilisation to fuel innovation.

Economic growth

  1. We recognise that the economic empowerment of all is an important way to boost productivity and innovation and strengthen participation in the economy. We emphasise the importance of preparing our workforce for the future of work to capture the benefits of technological advancement and respond to demographic changes in line with the APEC Collaborative Framework for Demographic Changes. We reaffirm our commitment to modernising human resources development through promoting high-quality, full, productive and decent employment, lifelong learning, vocational training, reskilling and upskilling, protecting the rights of workers and continuing efforts to promote international labour standards in the changing world of work, and optimising social security systems as appropriate.
  2. We emphasise the importance of credible and flexible fiscal, monetary and financial policy frameworks to manage shocks and maintain macroeconomic and financial stability. We note that global imbalances have persisted, creating risks to growth and stability. We recognise that global rebalancing is in our common interest and agree to strengthen communication and cooperation in this regard. We encourage fiscal policies to support households and promote financial access, opportunity and literacy for all, recognising that financial literacy is important to financial health and well-being.
  3. We seek to strengthen comprehensive security across all energy sectors and technologies and jointly address energy security challenges, ensuring uninterrupted, reliable and affordable access to energy to enable economic prosperity. We encourage strengthened energy security through cooperation on supply chain resilience, secure cross-border infrastructure interconnection and risk assessment. We recognise the benefits of timely restoration of critical energy infrastructure such as power plants, electric grids, submarine power cables and pipelines, and encourage the sharing of economies’ experiences on market mechanisms, emergency preparedness and response, and strategic reserve management. We recognise the importance of secure and uninterrupted energy flows and cooperation across the whole supply chain, including between producers and consumers in a mutually beneficial manner, as well as fostering energy cooperation in the region. We will promote universal access to high-quality energy that is secure, reliable, abundant, resilient and affordable, including for remote and rural areas. We encourage deepening voluntary cooperation on mutual enhancement between digital and emerging technologies and energy by supporting reliable, resilient and affordable energy for the development of digital and emerging technologies, while harnessing digital and emerging technologies to enhance energy systems that deliver benefits for all. We recognise that conventional and zero- and low-emission energy sources and technologies provide a foundation for energy security and strong and sustainable economic growth, and that each economy will choose an energy system mix consistent with its domestic priorities.
  4. We will work towards promoting open, fair, transparent, productive, resilient and innovative agri-food systems that benefit all. We will strengthen policy partnership on food security, boost agricultural productivity and efficiency, enhance the resilience of regional food systems and supply chains, including through innovation and digitalisation, promote the transformation of agri-food systems, advance food safety and nutrition for all, and prevent and reduce food loss and waste. We support science- and evidence-based, technology-enabled agriculture, including utilising tools such as digital and emerging technologies and advances in agricultural biotechnology. We reaffirm our commitment to strengthening economic opportunities in rural areas.
  5. We recognise the multiple values and contributions that forests provide for economic growth, biodiversity conservation, and the resilience and prosperity of communities across the Asia-Pacific region. We support cooperation on combating illegal logging and associated trade while promoting legally harvested forest products, sustainable forest management, and halting and reversing forest loss and degradation. We will also collaborate to improve the resilience of marine and coastal communities and promote the conservation and management of ocean resources, including by combating illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing and addressing the growing challenge of marine debris, while leveraging science- and technology-based approaches.
  6. We are committed to fostering an enabling business environment that supports the growth of MSMEs and start-ups through opportunities to become more competitive and innovative. We will promote greater access for MSMEs to capital, assets, skills training and digital tools, support MSMEs’ participation in value chains, and encourage economies to continue providing support for MSMEs’ capacity building. We encourage the development of accessible, easy-to-use and cost-effective products and solutions that help MSMEs boost productivity and efficiency, expand market participation, accelerate digital transformation and facilitate the transition of economic actors from the informal to the formal and global economies.
  7. We recognise the detrimental impact of corruption as a threat to economic growth, eroding public trust, harming trade and fair competition, diverting resources away from vital areas, and facilitating crimes, including organised crime. We resolve to promote growth and prosperity through effective anti-corruption and integrity measures, and continue our joint efforts to fight against corruption, including cross-border corruption, deny safe haven to corruption offenders, including people who benefit from corruption and illicit assets, and strengthen cooperation on asset recovery and return.
  8. As part of our collective endeavours to deepen regional cooperation across all fronts, we note the convening of the 2026 sectoral ministerial meetings for Women and the Economy, Trade, Tourism, Digital and AI, Forestry, Food Security, Small and Medium Enterprises, Energy, Transportation, Human Resources Development, and Finance, as well as other high-level events, including during the Digital Weeks. We commend the outcomes of the 37th APEC Ministerial Meeting as an important basis for future cooperation, including the adoption of the five-year review of the Aotearoa Plan of Action.
  9. Our business communities and other stakeholders bring creativity, dynamism and energy to APEC and remain vital partners in our work. We look forward to further strengthening multi-stakeholder engagement, as appropriate, including with the APEC Business Advisory Council (ABAC) and the Pacific Economic Cooperation Council (PECC).

  10. We extend our sincere gratitude to the People’s Republic of China and the people and city of Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, for their warm hospitality and thorough arrangements. We look forward to the upcoming APEC host years of Viet Nam (2027), Mexico (2028), Singapore (2030), Japan (2031), Chile (2032), Papua New Guinea (2033) and Peru (2034).

title: ‘I won’t disappoint you in my second term’ – Adeleke assures Osun people
description:
By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo



As the week-long activities to usher Governor Ademola Adeleke’s second term in office took off with Jumat service, the governor has vowed not to disappoint the people of the State.



Represented by the Deputy Governor, Prince Kola Adewusi, at the Oja Oba Central mosque
content:
By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo

As the week-long activities to usher Governor Ademola Adeleke’s second term in office took off with Jumat service, the governor has vowed not to disappoint the people of the State.

Represented by the Deputy Governor, Prince Kola Adewusi, at the Oja Oba Central mosque in Osogbo, the Governor recalled the struggles and battles for the sustenance of democracy in Osun State and vowed to continue to place the interest of the public at the heart of his administration.

A statement issued by his spokesperson, Olawale Rasheed, on Friday stated that the governor commended Osun people for their steadfastness, perseverance and persistent solidarity during the electioneering period, saying the state has become a national model, a symbol for people’s power as the foundation of democracy.

“I won’t disappoint Osun people. I will deliver even more than my first term. I am hopeful our financial situation will soon improve with the expected resolution of the local government crisis. We will take good care of workers and all segments of the society,” the governor was quoted as saying.

Earlier in his sermon, Sheikh Moruf Ishola described the recent Osun election as “unprecedented in many respects and a standout record for all students of democracy.

According to him, the Osun election that re-elected Governor Adeleke broke all records in terms of its dynamics and colours, adding that “the August 15 polls defied all calculations because almighty Allah ran it.

“That is why Mr Governor must not abandon God and the people. He must continue to govern with the fear of God, keep promises and serve only the interests of the people,” he submitted on behalf of the Chief Imam of Osogboland, Sheikh Musa Animasahun.

The prayer session was attended by the Secretary to the State Government, Hon. Teslim Igbalaye; Osun Central Accord Senatorial candidate, Hon. Ganiyu Olaoluwa; members of the state executive council; special advisers; and top government functionaries.

title: UNICEF, Lagos raise alarm over threats to children’s rights
description:
…As children demand free education, protection, greater say in policies



By Chioma Obinna



The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and the Lagos State Government have called for stronger protection of children’s rights, warning that their welfare and fundamental rights are increasingly under
content:
…As children demand free education, protection, greater say in policies

By Chioma Obinna

The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and the Lagos State Government have called for stronger protection of children’s rights, warning that their welfare and fundamental rights are increasingly under threat and require concrete government action.

The call was made on Friday during the commemoration of the 2026 World Children’s Day at the UNICEF Lagos Office, with the theme, “My Day. My Rights. My Future.”

UNICEF Chief of Field Office, Lagos, Celine Lafoucriere, said children’s rights were facing growing threats globally, stressing the need for governments and other stakeholders to guarantee every child access to education, healthcare, good nutrition, clean water, sanitation and social protection.

“Children’s rights are under pressure, they’re under threat, they’re being increasingly threatened throughout the world,” she said.

Lafoucriere said UNICEF was working closely with the Lagos State Government to ensure that children’s rights were respected and accessible to all, particularly the most vulnerable.

She emphasised the importance of social protection programmes, noting that the existence of rights did not automatically translate into access to basic necessities.

“Having a right is one thing, but it’s not going to put food on the table,” she said, explaining that social protection interventions could help vulnerable children access education, healthcare and adequate nutrition.

She added that Nigeria’s future depended largely on the attention and investment devoted to children today.

“The child is the future, and the future of Nigeria is today,” Lafoucriere declared.

The Lagos State Commissioner for Youth and Social Development, Mobolaji Ogunlende, said the government remained committed to promoting the welfare, protection and development of every child but acknowledged that it could not achieve the objective without the support of other stakeholders.

He urged parents, schools, communities, development partners and other stakeholders to work together to create an environment where every child felt safe, valued and heard.

“We must translate what we hear today into meaningful action and commitment,” he said.

Ogunlende assured the children that their contributions and concerns raised during the celebration would not end with the event but would inform government policies and practical interventions.

Also speaking, the Speaker of the Lagos State Children’s Parliament, Abdulsalam Anjola, called for greater involvement of children in decisions affecting their lives, insisting that their voices must be considered in the formulation of policies concerning them.

He said children were better positioned to communicate their experiences, particularly in cases involving abuse and other challenges.

Anjola also urged the government to increase investment in education and provide opportunities for out-of-school children.

“Education is the weapon that can instigate war,” he said, while calling for effective implementation of education policies to guarantee children access to opportunities to realise their potential.

He expressed optimism that investing in children would contribute to a safer Lagos, a better Nigeria and stronger communities.

A 14-year-old student of Ikeja Senior High School, Ishola Moyinoluwa, also called for greater protection of children’s rights, particularly access to basic and free education.

She said every child deserved the opportunity to be heard, educated and equipped for the future.

Moyinoluwa, whose artwork depicted a young boy dreaming of becoming an astronaut, said children’s aspirations could become reality through parental guidance and government support.

She urged parents to provide educational, moral and social guidance for their children, while calling on the government to establish platforms where young people could express their views on issues affecting their rights and future.

As part of the celebration, 80 children, divided into eight groups, participated in an art project titled, “80 Children, One Future,” through which they presented their visions of the Nigeria they hoped to see.

UNICEF urged adults to listen to children’s concerns and make practical commitments to address the challenges affecting them.

The Permanent Secretary, Lagos State Ministry of Youth and Social Development, Pharm. Toyin Oke-Osanyintolu, also encouraged children to speak out whenever their rights were threatened.

She urged them to believe in their dreams, declaring, “If you can dream it, you can do it.”

Oke-Osanyintolu commended UNICEF for its continued partnership with the Lagos State Government in advancing the welfare and development of children.

The post UNICEF, Lagos raise alarm over threats to children’s rights appeared first on Vanguard News.
