title: Ooni urges FG to revive, protect textile industry
description:
…Calls for prioritisation of Nigerian fabrics, investment in local production







By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo



The Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi, has called on the Federal Government to revive and protect Nigeria’s textile industry as part of efforts to strengthen the nation’s economic growth
content:
…Calls for prioritisation of Nigerian fabrics, investment in local production

By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo

The Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi, has called on the Federal Government to revive and protect Nigeria’s textile industry as part of efforts to strengthen the nation’s economic growth and development.

The monarch also urged textile unions to deploy all necessary measures to safeguard the industry and encourage the patronage of locally produced fabrics.

Oba Ogunwusi, represented by Olori Aderonke Adeyeye, made the call on Friday at the 38th Annual National Education Conference of the National Union of Textile, Garment and Tailoring Workers of Nigeria (NUTGTWN) and the Nigeria Textile, Garment and Tailoring Employers’ Association in Ile-Ife, Osun State.

Commending the unions for organising the conference to educate their members, the monarch said an informed labour union was essential to the survival of democracy and the development of the nation.

He said stakeholders must work together to restore the country’s textile industry, revive moribund mills and make locally manufactured fabrics a source of national pride.

“It is important for stakeholders to protect our industry. Let us prioritise our own fabrics. Let us revive our textile mills. Let us make Made in Nigeria a badge of pride, not an apology.

“We must honour labour. Every tailor, every cutter, every employer deserves dignity, fair pay and respect. Labour is not servitude; labour is nation-building.

“Let us raise a new generation. Teach them craft, teach them the business, teach them discipline. Do not let this knowledge die with us,” he said.

The Ooni further stressed that the survival of democracy was closely linked to economic prosperity, respect for workers and the protection of local industries.

“Democracy cannot stand on empty stomachs. It cannot stand where labour is not respected. It cannot stand where industry is allowed to die. A nation that abandons its artisans abandons its future,” he added.

Earlier, NUTGTWN President, Comrade Peter Godonu, urged the Federal Government to translate its commitment to industrialisation into concrete policies and investments capable of reviving the country’s struggling textile industry.

Godonu said Nigeria could no longer afford to celebrate the potential of its textile sector while factories remained closed, production capacity declined and imported products continued to dominate the domestic market.

He said the union would sustain its advocacy for policies that promote industrialisation, local production, decent work and the revival of the textile and garment industry.

“Our Union will therefore continue to intensify its advocacy and campaign for sustainable industrialisation, local production, decent work and the revival of the textile and garment industry.

“We remain available to partner with the Federal Government, state governments, employers and other stakeholders in developing and implementing practical solutions to these challenges,” he said.

The NUTGTWN president noted that Nigeria possessed several advantages that could support the rebuilding of a competitive textile and garment industry.

These, he said, included a large domestic market, cotton-growing potential, abundant labour, technical expertise, a vibrant fashion and garment-making industry, a youthful population and access to the wider African market through the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

He, however, said political will, policy consistency, investment and strategic coordination were necessary to harness these opportunities and restore the sector to productivity.

title: 2027: Obi urges Nigerians to defend their votes
description:
By Nwabueze Okonkwo



ONITSHA — Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged Nigerians to turn out en masse for the January 16, 2027 presidential election and defend their votes against electoral manipulation.



Obi made the call on Friday at the NDC town h
content:
By Nwabueze Okonkwo

ONITSHA — Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged Nigerians to turn out en masse for the January 16, 2027 presidential election and defend their votes against electoral manipulation.

Obi made the call on Friday at the NDC town hall meeting and presidential campaign rally held at All Saints Anglican Church Cathedral, Onitsha, Anambra State.

He said Nigerians should regard election day as an opportunity to make a sacrifice for the country by coming out to vote and remaining at polling centres to protect their ballots.

According to him, whoever emerges winner in a free, fair and transparent election should be supported by all Nigerians.

The former Anambra State governor, however, vowed to resist any attempt to manipulate the results in favour of any political party, saying he would not accept a repeat of what he described as irregularities that characterised the 2023 presidential election.

“We are going to match them fire for fire if they attempt to rig the election as usual, and we are going to block all loopholes to ensure that our votes count.

“The idea is for the right winner to emerge in a free and fair election. Nothing more, nothing less. Personally, I would like to win in a transparent election,” he said.

Obi also criticised the borrowing policy of the President Bola Tinubu administration, alleging that trillions of dollars had been borrowed between 2023 and 2026 without sufficient investment in productive sectors of the economy.

He warned that another four-year term for the administration after the 2027 election could worsen the country’s economic situation.

At the rally, Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central Senatorial District; NDC candidate for Idemili North/South Federal Constituency, Engr. Eric Anyamene; member representing Onitsha North II in the Anambra State House of Assembly, Hon. Pat Okafor; the party’s Anambra State Deputy Chairman, Barr. Chugbo Enwezor; and Chief Ikenna Victor Egbuna, SAN, expressed confidence that the party would win the presidential, National Assembly and state assembly elections in 2027.

title: 2027: Court sacks ADC governorship candidate in Adamawa
description:
The Federal High Court in Abuja on Friday ordered the removal of Tukur Ribadu as the 2027 Adamawa governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC).



Justice Obiora Egwuatu, in a judgment, held that Mr Omar Suleiman, who won the majority of the valid votes cast in the primary electio
content:
The Federal High Court in Abuja on Friday ordered the removal of Tukur Ribadu as the 2027 Adamawa governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC).

Justice Obiora Egwuatu, in a judgment, held that Mr Omar Suleiman, who won the majority of the valid votes cast in the primary election of the party, was unlawfully substituted by Ribadu.

Justice Egwuatu ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to immediately restore Suleiman as the rightful candidate of the party.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Suleiman, a cousin of former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Babachir Lawal, was said to have initially emerged as the ADC’s candidate in the Adamawa primary.

However, he was later replaced by Ribadu.

Dissatisfied, Suleiman filed a suit marked FHC/ABJ/C’S/1751/2026 before Justice Egwuatu to challenge his unlawful substitution.

He prayed the court to order the ADC to forward his name to the electoral umpire as a valid candidate of the party.

He also prayed the court to compel INEC to publish his name as the candidate of the party.

Delivering the judgment, Justice Egwuatu held that Suleiman could only be replaced as a candidate if he had formally and voluntarily withdrawn from the race or died.

He ruled that since Suleiman had neither withdrawn nor died, his replacement was illegal, null and void.

The judge consequently ordered INEC to immediately restore his name as the ADC governorship candidate for Adamawa State in the forthcoming governorship poll. (NAN)

title: Vandalism, illegal connections threaten Kano water supply
description:
Over 45 pipeline repairs completed, says commissioner



By Hadiza Yusuf



KANO — The Kano State Government has warned residents against vandalism, illegal connections and other activities capable of damaging public water infrastructure and disrupting the supply of drinking water across the state.
content:
Over 45 pipeline repairs completed, says commissioner

By Hadiza Yusuf

KANO — The Kano State Government has warned residents against vandalism, illegal connections and other activities capable of damaging public water infrastructure and disrupting the supply of drinking water across the state.

The Commissioner for Water Resources, Dr Dahiru Muhammad Hashim, gave the warning at a press conference in Kano on Friday while briefing journalists on the progress of ongoing rehabilitation of water facilities and restoration of supply to communities.

Hashim said the ministry had identified cases of unauthorised connections to water pipelines, vandalism, indiscriminate drilling around major water lines and improper handling of distribution valves.

He added that some water pipes had also been damaged by construction activities, refuse burning and other activities around drainage channels.

“We appeal to the general public to cooperate with the Ministry in protecting water infrastructure. Our assessment has identified cases of unauthorised tapping of pipelines, vandalism and damage to pipes crossing drainage channels,” he said.

The commissioner urged residents, contractors and those executing construction, road and drainage projects to consult relevant authorities before embarking on activities that could affect water pipelines.

He also called on residents to promptly report burst pipes, leakages, suspected vandalism and illegal connections to the appropriate authorities.

According to him, the restoration of water supply has exposed weaknesses in some old pipelines, many of which had remained without regular water flow for several years.

He explained that the return of water pressure to the distribution network had resulted in leakages and pipe bursts in some locations, necessitating urgent repairs and replacement of damaged infrastructure.

Hashim disclosed that the ministry had completed more than 45 repair and replacement interventions across different parts of the metropolis.

The affected areas include Goron Dutse, Jakara, Kofar Ruwa, Kurmi, Dukawa, Kofar Wambai, Fagge, Club Road, Tudun Wada, Gidan Zakka, Gabari, Koki, Mandawari and Sharada.

He said the interventions involved replacing damaged asbestos-cement pipes, fixing leaking PVC pipelines, installing valves and repairing faulty connections.

The commissioner further disclosed that water had been pumped from Challawa Water Works to the Goron Dutse reservoirs, which have a reported capacity of 42.5 million litres, before being released into the distribution network.

He listed communities that had received water to include Goron Dutse, Gwammaja, Jakara, Kofar Mazugal, Muskwani, Kofar Wambai, Mandawari, Fagge, Tudun Wada, Gama, Kofar Ruwa and Alfindiki, among others.

Hashim said the government was also working to improve access through the installation of public standpipes in communities where household water connections had yet to be fully restored.

“Protecting water facilities is a responsibility we all share, and the cooperation of residents is vital to sustaining the improvements made in restoring water supply across Kano,” he said.

title: I’m The Most Transparent, Vilified But I Shall Be Vindicated — Yahaya Bello
description: Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has expressed confidence that he will eventually be vindicated over the allegations of financial misconduct levelled against him by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC).He also described himself as the most transparent individual.“I am t
content:
Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has expressed confidence that he will eventually be vindicated over the allegations of financial misconduct levelled against him by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC).

He also described himself as the most transparent individual.

“I am the most transparent and the most vilified. But at the end of the day, I shall be vindicated,” Bello said on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday.

Bello, who has consistently denied wrongdoing, is facing multiple cases instituted by the anti-graft agency over alleged misappropriation of public funds during his eight-year tenure as governor of the state.

The EFCC Chairman, Ola Olukoyede, said in an interview with Channels Television in January 2026 that the commission had filed three cases against the former governor and fulfilled its mandate by investigating and prosecuting him.

According to Olukoyede, the responsibility for determining Bello’s guilt rests with the judiciary.

One of the cases involves a 16-count charge bordering on alleged criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving ₦110.4 billion.

Bello, who was the governor from 2016 to 2024, is standing trial alongside two former state government officials.

The Federal Government alleges that the defendants diverted state funds to acquire properties in highbrow areas of Abuja and Dubai, United Arab Emirates.

Bello is also facing a separate 19-count charge involving an alleged ₦80.2 billion fraud and money laundering before the Federal High Court in Abuja.

However, some prosecution witnesses have given evidence that has featured prominently in the proceedings.

In February 2026, an EFCC witness, Olomotane Egoro, told the Federal High Court that Bello’s name did not appear as a beneficiary, signatory, or party to transactions involving some companies allegedly awarded local government contracts in Kogi State.

Similarly, in March, another prosecution witness, Mahmoud Abdulazeez, maintained that Bello’s name was not linked to the transactions involving property documents tendered before the court.

In June 2026, the 17th prosecution witness, Shehu Bala, also told the court during cross-examination that Bello was not involved in the property transactions under examination.

Meanwhile, the EFCC secured a significant legal victory in August 2025 when the Court of Appeal in Lagos restored an interim forfeiture order covering 14 properties allegedly linked to the former governor.

The appellate court directed the EFCC to proceed with the final forfeiture proceedings, holding that properties suspected to be proceeds of unlawful activities could be investigated and preserved pending the determination of the case.

Despite the legal challenges, Bello, who is the senatorial candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) for Kogi Central in the 2027 general elections, has maintained his innocence and expressed confidence that the allegations against him will not stand the test of judicial scrutiny.

The cases remain before the courts, and no final determination of his guilt has been made.

title: Tinubu Must Stay group set to unveil presidential library, reform observatory
description:
By Omeiza Ajayi



ABUJA: The Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation TMS, popularly known as Tinubu Must Stay, has announced plans to establish a National Reform Documentation and Impact Observatory, a public digital policy archive and a possible future presidential library for Presid
content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: The Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation TMS, popularly known as Tinubu Must Stay, has announced plans to establish a National Reform Documentation and Impact Observatory, a public digital policy archive and a possible future presidential library for President Bola Tinubu.

Chairman of the Board of Trustees and National Coordinator of the group, Malam Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi, disclosed this on Friday during the commissioning of its National Secretariat in Abuja.

He said the records would start with Tinubu’s years as Governor of Lagos State between 1999 and 2007, then cover policy developments under successive administrations, his national political career and his presidency from 2023.

According to him, the archive would span public revenue administration, infrastructure, investment, education, economic management, digital transformation and institutional development. Students, researchers, historians, policymakers and ordinary citizens would be given access to original documents, implementation records, economic data and independent assessments.

Inuwa said the library, the observatory and the archive remained long-term aspirations that would need feasibility studies, sustainable funding, proper governance and professional archival standards.

“History serves future generations when it preserves evidence, not merely admiration,” he said.

He added that the documentation must make room for achievements, implementation difficulties, independent criticism and lessons learned.

The announcement came with a membership claim. Inuwa said the group, formally launched on October 1, 2026, had recorded 61,093 validated members within seven weeks across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

He said the group had representation in 730 of the country’s 774 local government areas, about 94 per cent geographical coverage. Its digital database also captures 4,750 wards and 22,584 polling units.

Inuwa said 65 per cent of members, roughly 40,000 people, were aged between 18 and 34, while the membership was 65 per cent men and 35 per cent women.

“The most remarkable feature of our membership is its youthful composition. This is not merely a demographic statistic. It places a profound responsibility upon our institution,” he said.

He said young Nigerians needed more than a seat in political conversations, naming quality education, employable skills, technology, finance and markets as what would turn the country’s demographic potential into prosperity. To that end, the group would run grassroots entrepreneurship workshops, digital skills training, mentorship programmes and policy dialogues.

“Today, we are not merely opening an office. We are opening a new chapter in our responsibility to Nigeria,” he said.

Inuwa said the secretariat would serve as a centre for research, civic engagement, youth empowerment and the documentation of policies and institutions shaping national development.

He insisted that the group intended to outlive the 2027 general elections, even though it openly backs the President’s Renewed Hope Agenda. He said it would encourage evidence-based assessment of government policies, including their implementation challenges and social consequences.

He acknowledged that the administration’s changes to petrol subsidies, foreign exchange management and fiscal policy had drawn mixed reactions, with some Nigerians seeing them as necessary to fix long-standing structural weaknesses and others worried about implementation and hardship in households.

“Reform is not an end in itself. Its purpose is to improve the lives of people,” he said.

On voter readiness, Inuwa said the group’s records showed that 81 per cent of respondents already held Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), 11 per cent had yet to collect theirs and six per cent were not registered to vote. The remaining two per cent, he said, required reconciliation.

He cautioned that large membership figures did not automatically translate into effective grassroots structures or measurable results.

“Our responsibility is to convert organisational reach into meaningful public value. We must move from membership registration to meaningful participation, from participation to capability, and from capability to opportunity,” he said.

Inuwa said the group would spend its first 90 days assessing operational capacity, developing programme standards and setting realistic targets before publishing measurable commitments. He stressed that it was independently established, with its own leadership, governance structures and membership system, despite its declared support for the President.

He urged the public to judge the organisation by its contributions to civic education, economic empowerment and sustainable development, not by membership figures or political declarations.

“A building can be completed with bricks, cement and steel. An institution must be built with integrity, competence, discipline, trust and a commitment to service,” he said.

Turning to the approaching elections, Inuwa expressed concern over reports of political intimidation, attacks on political gatherings and inflammatory public rhetoric. He condemned political thuggery and violence, irrespective of who was involved, and asked security agencies to investigate incidents impartially.

He called on political parties, civic organisations, the media and security institutions to promote peaceful participation, accurate information and respect for opposing views, and urged members to reject intimidation and misinformation.

“Political differences must never become a justification for violence. No political ambition is worth the life of an innocent Nigerian,” he warned.

The post Tinubu Must Stay group set to unveil presidential library, reform observatory appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Yahaya Bello denies imposing Ododo as Kogi governor
description:
Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has dismissed allegations that he installed Governor Usman Ododo as a political stooge.
Bello insisted that his successor was selected on merit and has demonstrated his ability to govern independently.
He said Ododo was chosen from among several contenders b
content:
Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has dismissed allegations that he installed Governor Usman Ododo as a political stooge.

Bello insisted that his successor was selected on merit and has demonstrated his ability to govern independently.

He said Ododo was chosen from among several contenders because he was considered the most qualified person to lead the state at the time, adding that the governor had continued to justify the confidence placed in him.

The former governor stated this in an interview with Channels Television on Friday.

He argued that political opponents were free to make allegations during election seasons but maintained that Ododo was now demonstrating his leadership capacity.

“During political seasons, anybody is free to say whatever they want. Without going too far, today, Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo, who has been called so many unprintable names, is proving that he is Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo, taking the lead from the front,” Bello said.

Explaining how the decision to support Ododo was reached, Bello said he refused to allow ethnic, religious or regional considerations to influence the choice of the party’s candidate.

According to him, several options were available, but Ododo stood out as the most suitable person for the position.

“You see, at that time, there were so many options available for us and the people of Kogi State, especially from our party first. But as the leader of the party and the state, at that time, I refused to allow sentiments of tribe, of religion, or where you come from, to influence my decision or our decision,” he said.

He added that the decision was collectively taken within their political circle after considering the qualifications of the aspirants.

“So collectively, as a member of a political family, we now decided that, look, Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo, though from the same Kogi Central, is more qualified.

“You suit this purpose now. And then, by the grace of God, the people of Kogi overwhelmingly voted him into office, and he’s doing excellently well now,” Bello said.

Asked whether he still considered Ododo the right person to lead Kogi, Bello maintained that his assessment had not changed.

“As at the time we chose him, he’s the best, and today, he is still the best to lead the state to the promised land,” he said.

Bello also expressed confidence that Ododo would secure a second term, predicting that voters would reward the governor for his performance.

Rejecting the suggestion that he had imposed Ododo on the people, the former governor insisted that the electorate made the final decision through the ballot.

“The people elected him, and 101%, I am very, very sure and very, very confident that the people will re-elect him again, when the time comes for his second term, because of his performance,” he said.

He further argued that Ododo’s record in public service, both as Auditor-General for Local Government and as governor, had strengthened his standing among residents.

“Even when he was in office then, as the Auditor General for local government, and now as the Executive Governor, his performance in less than three years has really sold him out to the people,” Bello added.

On his own eight-year tenure as governor, Bello said he had no regrets about his administration, although he was still reviewing his record in office.

Asked to identify his biggest regret, he responded, “Well, I have no regret whatsoever. I have no regret whatsoever. I take responsibility for everything that happened.”

He said he inherited a state that required firm leadership and believed his administration had provided the direction needed to move it forward.

“I met a state that was in need of leadership. Decisive leadership. And I provided it at that time,” he said.

Bello also insisted that he gave his best during his time in office, while acknowledging that the expectations of the people of Kogi remained high.

“Well, my people are so interesting that our best may never be enough, because we strive to always be ahead of others, especially knowing where we’re coming from,” he said.

He added that the circumstances confronting his administration were difficult, citing economic, political, social, and other challenges.

“If anything, considering the prevailing economic, political, physical, social, even spiritual situation at that time, we gave our best,” Bello said.

He maintained that his administration, which he described as the New Direction Administration, had rescued the state and placed it on a development path.

“We were able to rescue the state and put it on the path of proper development. We turned our administration then as New Direction Administration,” he said.

Bello also expressed satisfaction that Ododo, whom he described as one of his mentees, had continued from where his administration stopped.

“We provided that leadership, and thank God, from amongst, let’s say, my mentees, the current governor, is now leading the state from where we stopped in the right direction,” he said.

Ododo emerged as the All Progressives Congress candidate for the November 11, 2023 Kogi governorship election after serving as the state’s Auditor-General for Local Governments under Yahaya Bello.

His emergence as the party’s candidate attracted attention because he was widely regarded as Bello’s preferred successor.

Ododo went on to win the election with 446,237 votes, defeating his closest challenger, Murtala Ajaka of the Social Democratic Party, who polled 259,052 votes.

He was sworn in on January 27, 2024, succeeding Bello, who had completed two terms in office.

The relationship between the two politicians has remained a subject of public and political discussion, with critics questioning the extent of Bello’s influence over the incumbent governor.

In February 2026, for instance, a pressure group accused Ododo of being a puppet in his predecessor’s political affairs, an allegation that forms part of the wider debate over the governor’s independence.

title: 2027: APC leaders rally South-West support for Tinubu
description:
Leaders of the All Progressives Congress and the Presidential Campaign Council Support Group Directorate across the South-West on Friday intensified grassroots mobilisation for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The leaders spoke in their various remarks at
content:
Leaders of the All Progressives Congress and the Presidential Campaign Council Support Group Directorate across the South-West on Friday intensified grassroots mobilisation for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The leaders spoke in their various remarks at a town hall meeting held at Onirekere in Ibadan North-West Local Government Area of Oyo State.

Speaking at the event, the Director-General of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu Support Group and former Deputy Governor of Nasarawa State, Silas Agara, said, “The directorate deliberately shifted from traditional solidarity walks to interactive town hall sessions, following an earlier outing in Awka, Anambra State to directly engage citizens with verifiable facts.

“This gathering is designed to give all our people there the conducive environment to be able to state clearly, in clear terms, what Mr President has done in every state.

“So, let me appeal to our people in this region to support groups to ensure a massive voter turnout in January 2027 to return President Tinubu to Aso Villa.”

In his remarks, the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, said, “Roughly 80 million Nigerians, about 40 per cent of the population, lacked access to electricity when President Tinubu assumed office in 2023.”

Tegbe, who was represented by Rasheed Adegboyega, said, “The administration secured a $750 million publicly funded facility through the Rural Electrification Agency to catalyse an additional $1.1 billion in private sector investment for 1,120 isolated mini-grids and 250 interconnected mini-grids nationwide, alongside another $500 million earmarked for ongoing Ministry of Power projects.”

Tegbe added that eight federal universities, including the University of Ibadan, University College Hospital, University of Abuja and University of Maiduguri, were taken off the national grid under the second phase of the Energising Education Programme to relieve pressure on the decades-old grid.

He noted that comprehensive project compendiums across all six geopolitical zones had been distributed to support groups for door-to-door campaigns.

In a pointed comparison of local government funding in Oyo State across three administrations, former Commissioner for Local Government Affairs, Bimbo Kolade, revealed that monthly federal allocations to the state’s 33 councils had surged dramatically under Tinubu.

According to Kolade, “local governments in Oyo state received an average of N1.8 billion monthly under former Governor Christopher Alao-Akala and N2.4 billion monthly under former Governor Abiola Ajimobi, whereas monthly allocations under the current dispensation have risen to an average of N26 billion.”

Recalling past grassroots projects, Kolade noted that Alao-Akala executed five kilometres of road per local government, totalling 165 kilometres, while Ajimobi tarred 637 kilometres of asphalt roads and opened up earth roads totalling 1,033 kilometres across the councils.

Questioning the utilisation of the current N26bn monthly inflow in local councils such as Oriire and Egbeda, Kolade charged voters to back Tinubu’s second-term bid to entrench full local government autonomy.

On rail transportation, the Managing Director of the Nigerian Railway Corporation, Kayode Opeifa, described the Lagos-Ibadan standard-gauge rail as the most functional corridor in the country, noting that “frequency had increased since 2023 to twice daily from Thursday to Sunday and once daily from Monday to Wednesday, while container cargo operations at Moniya were boosting Oyo State’s economy.”

Opeifa revealed that plans were underway to extend passenger rail operations from Ibadan to Osogbo and Ado-Ekiti under a four-year South-West rail master plan in partnership with the South-West Development Commission, adding that a 50 per cent fare discount would soon be introduced for holiday travellers.

The Senior Special Assistant to the President on Media-Related Issues, Tunde Rahman, maintained that President Tinubu’s bold economic reforms saved the nation from total financial collapse, stabilised the naira and lifted Gross Domestic Product growth to about 4.2 per cent.

Rahman highlighted key social and infrastructure interventions, including the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, which provides a N20,000 monthly stipend to students; the clearance of N768bn in pension arrears; and major federal road contracts in Oyo State, such as the N276bn Ilorin-Ogbomoso highway, the N265bn Iseyin-Oyo-Ogbomoso road, as well as the Iwo township, Ibadan-Ijaye-Ago-Are, Iseyin-Okeho-Kishi, Ogbomoso-Igbeti and Ibadan-Abeokuta corridors.

In their separate remarks, Oyo State APC Chairman and former Deputy Governor, Moses Adeyemo, and the party’s governorship candidate, Senator Sharafadeen Alli, charged party faithful and residents to ensure their Permanent Voter Cards were ready, turn out en masse on election day and defend their votes at the polling units.

Alli also commended the developmental strides of the President, while an aide to the President, Sunday Dare, highlighted ongoing federal road interventions across 12 routes in Oyo State and emerging cargo rail opportunities between Omi Adio and Erunmu.

The post 2027: APC leaders rally South-West support for Tinubu appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: ICPC boss elected chairman of African asset recovery forum
description:
From Adanna Nnamani, Abuja
The Chairman of the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), Dr Musa Adamu Aliyu, has been elected Chairman of the African Asset Recovery Practitioners’ Forum (AARPF), in a move expected to strengthen continental efforts to trace, recover
content:
From Adanna Nnamani, Abuja

The Chairman of the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), Dr Musa Adamu Aliyu, has been elected Chairman of the African Asset Recovery Practitioners’ Forum (AARPF), in a move expected to strengthen continental efforts to trace, recover and repatriate stolen assets.

Aliyu was elected by members of the General Assembly at the first General Assembly of the forum, held in Abuja from November 17 to 20, 2026, under the theme “From Commitment to Action”.

The four-day meeting brought together delegates from all 55 member states of the African Union, as well as international partners, under the auspices of the African Union.

In his acceptance speech, Aliyu expressed appreciation for the confidence reposed in him, pledging to work with members of the steering council to deliver measurable results and advance institutional reforms.

He said his leadership would focus on ensuring that stolen assets belonging to African countries were traced, recovered and returned for the benefit of citizens.

Aliyu said the forum would be judged by its ability to deliver concrete results, including the enforcement of an amended charter, the presentation of a baseline compliance report, the training of practitioners, the development of model legal provisions and the establishment of an adequately equipped secretariat.

He said: “Let me be clear about how this council should be judged. Within the life of this work plan, this assembly is entitled to see an amended charter enforced, a baseline compliance report on its table, practitioners trained and placed, model provisions in the hands of members, and a secretariat equipped to sustain the work.

“I accept this promise on these terms, and I will account to this assembly against them. Africa’s stolen wealth must go home. With your support, this forum will help bring it home.”

The ICPC chairman said the operationalisation of the forum had strengthened his confidence that African countries could collectively overcome the challenges associated with tracing and repatriating illicit assets.

He recalled that efforts to establish the forum began in 2022, adding that member countries had since been working together to develop a coordinated approach to recovering stolen wealth.

Aliyu stressed that asset recovery should not be viewed merely as a punishment for corruption but as a means of restoring resources to communities deprived of basic infrastructure and social services.

“Every stolen asset belonging to African citizens represents a school not built, a clinic not equipped and a road not laid.

“Recovery is not an act of punishment alone; it is an act of restitution to our people. This forum exists so that no African practitioner has to pursue that restitution alone,” he said.

He identified institutional governance, the Kampala Voluntary Tool, capacity building, technical assistance and peer learning, the strengthening of legal and institutional frameworks, and cooperation as the strategic priorities that would guide the steering council.

On resource mobilisation, Aliyu announced that Nigeria would contribute $20,000 in 2027 under the Resource Mobilisation Initiative.

He also urged member countries to redeem at least half of their agreed annual contribution of $20,000, amounting to $10,000, on or before the end of May 2027.

The Vice Chairman of the forum, Marie-Rose Messy, expressed confidence that the new leadership would deliver on its mandate.

Messy, who is the Director of the Debt Recovery Agency in Cameroon, said her 35 years of experience would be deployed to support the committee’s work and advance the objectives of the forum.

Also speaking, the Chairperson of the African Union Advisory Board Against Corruption, Kwami Senanu, said the successful convening of the first General Assembly demonstrated what African countries could achieve through unity, shared responsibility and cooperation.

Senanu commended Nigeria for its support and consistent championing of the Common African Position on Asset Recovery, urging member states to translate existing commitments into practical actions and stronger institutional engagement.

The General Assembly, in its communiqué, called on African political leaders to demonstrate stronger political will by providing adequate funding for anti-corruption and asset recovery institutions, enacting relevant national laws and safeguarding the independence of agencies responsible for recovering stolen assets.

It said translating the Common African Position on Asset Recovery (CAPAR) from commitment to action required concrete support from political leaders across African Union member states.

The assembly also urged governments to facilitate mutual legal assistance requests, strengthen information sharing and ensure that recovered assets were managed transparently and used for the benefit of citizens.

It identified the challenges affecting asset recovery across the continent as including difficulties in tracing illicit assets, differences in national legal frameworks, delays in mutual legal assistance, and challenges in recognising and enforcing foreign confiscation orders.

The forum consequently called for stronger cross-border cooperation, harmonisation of national laws, joint investigations and faster processing of mutual legal assistance and extradition requests.

It also endorsed the CAPAR Monitoring Tool as a baseline compliance assessment mechanism and urged the African Union Advisory Board Against Corruption (AUABC) and the African Union Commission’s Political Affairs, Peace and Security Department to finalise the tool and its digital reporting platform to enable pilot implementation within six months.

The assembly further validated the forum’s 2027–2029 work plan and strategic priorities, while welcoming an agreement on an annual country contribution of $10,000, with the first payment due by May 2027.

content:
Former Super Eagles captain Segun Odegbami has sustained injuries after armed men attacked his residence in the Ibara Government Reservation Area (GRA) of Abeokuta, Ogun State.

Odegbami said three armed men invaded his home at about 2:30 am on Friday.

The 74-year-old football legend said he, alongside his driver and domestic staff, confronted the attackers during a struggle and eventually forced them to flee.

The incident left Odegbami injured following the confrontation.

Odegbami said “it was the closest I have ever been face to face with death” because “they broke down my door to get to me”.

Odegbami revealed that he has been to the hospital for treatment of the wound. The motive of the attack remains unknown.

Odegbami is a Nigerian football icon and was a key member of the Nigerian men’s national team side that won the country’s first-ever Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) title in 1980.

title: Trump urges Nvidia to give Jensen Huang ‘second chance’
description:
US President Donald Trump on Friday called for chip giant Nvidia to reinstate disgraced former CEO Jensen Huang after he resigned over extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.



“I would love to see him be back. You have one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world, an
content:
US President Donald Trump on Friday called for chip giant Nvidia to reinstate disgraced former CEO Jensen Huang after he resigned over extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

“I would love to see him be back. You have one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world, and where is he going to go?” Trump told reporters.

“I think that I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance.”

Huang resigned last week as chief of Nvidia, a company at the center of the AI revolution, after revelations of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy who may have funneled restricted chips to that country.

Reports of at least two further affairs emerged after that initial report, with US intelligence said to be aware of the possibility of the alleged Chinese espionage.

Trump defended Huang as “a good man” who “made some bad decisions.”

“I’d like to see Jensen make a big apology and go back because he created something with Blackwell,” he said, referring to the most advanced chips designed by Nvidia.

The US president also appeared to directly contradict his own treasury secretary, saying he had spoken to China’s President Xi Jinping about Huang during a summit earlier this week.

“I did discuss that with President Xi, and he said, ‘Oh, brilliant, brilliant! He’s a brilliant man,'” said Trump.

Earlier in the day, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Trump had not discussed Huang with Xi during the meeting in Shenzhen.

Trump advocated for Nvidia to take back Huang as their CEO “if they were smart.”

Huang has offered to return to the company, a move the chip giant’s board has rejected.

Board chair Harvey Jones said in an earnings call this week that “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.”

– ‘Must stay ahead’ –

Earlier, Bessent had spoken at length about the AI race with China in comments to US broadcaster CNBC.

Speaking about the Trump administration’s support for the domestic AI sector, Bessent stressed that the United States “must stay ahead” of China in that realm.

“Our best protection against the foreign SI and exploits by foreign actors is for our labs to maintain their substantial lead, and in effect, they are our shield against SI,” he said, using the government’s preferred SI, or “super intelligence.”

“There’s no turning back on this. What we have to do is make sure that our labs maintain their leads through their continued innovation, through their access to the best chips, and through smart policy.”

Bessent said Trump and Xi had agreed on certain guardrails on the use of AI in the military domain.

“President Trump and President Xi agreed that humans should always be involved in any military decisions that SI makes, and the SI should not be allowed to be autonomous for major military actions,” he said.

On the threat of AI-enabled cyberattacks, Bessent again stressed that the best defense his country had was to allow its AI companies “to continue at the frontier and to provide us with the best defense against these other models.”

title: WPRF 2026: Global Alliance president hails Tinubu, Nigeria for hosting ‘biggest, boldest, brightest’ forum
description:
• Says country has raised bar for future editions, lauds NIPR, government support
• As Neliaku says Abuja Declaration will deepen responsible communication worldwide
___________________________________________________________________________
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja
The president of the Gl
content:
• Says country has raised bar for future editions, lauds NIPR, government support

• As Neliaku says Abuja Declaration will deepen responsible communication worldwide

___________________________________________________________________________

From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

The president of the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management, Professor Justin Green, has applauded President Bola Tinubu and the Nigerian government for supporting and hosting what he described as the biggest, brightest and boldest World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) in the organisation’s history.

Green, who spoke at the closing ceremony of the 13th WPRF in Abuja, said the successful hosting of the global gathering in Nigeria had surpassed expectations, particularly after initial doubts about the possibility of bringing the event to the African continent.

He described the forum as a landmark achievement for the Global Alliance, saying its scale and execution had set a new benchmark for future editions.

“When we first said we wanted to bring it to the African continent, we got locked down. People didn’t think that would ever take place. We were told there was no way it would ever happen. But we made it happen,” he said.

Green specifically thanked President Tinubu for backing the project, as well as the Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, for his sustained support, saying the forum would not have been possible without the government’s commitment.

“I want to thank the government of Nigeria for really rowing in. I want to thank President Tinubu for getting right behind this project,” he said.

He also acknowledged the contributions of government agencies, including the State Security Services, Customs and Immigration, as well as the event partners, volunteers, service providers and other stakeholders who supported the conference.

Green commended the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR) for its extensive preparations, disclosing that about 21 to 23 teams worked across different areas to deliver the event after two years of planning.

He particularly praised the NIPR president, Ike Neliaku, for his leadership and commitment, joking that he had called him so frequently during preparations that Neliaku’s wife might have raised concerns.

The Global Alliance president said the forum’s legacy would extend beyond the conference, pointing to the establishment of a university dedicated to public relations and leadership in Nigeria as one of the remarkable outcomes of the gathering.

He said he never imagined that bringing the WPRF to Nigeria would coincide with the establishment of such an institution, describing it as evidence of the country’s recognition of the public relations and communication profession.

“Never in my wildest dreams would I have ever thought that Global Alliance would have brought a World Public Relations Forum to anywhere and have left a university dedicated to public relations and leadership,” he said.

Green also praised the forum’s commitment to diversity and inclusion, particularly the provision of sign language interpretation throughout the event to ensure participation by persons with disabilities.

In his closing remarks, Green urged public relations professionals, particularly young practitioners, to remain committed to the profession, describing it as demanding but rewarding.

He encouraged participants to enjoy their work, build meaningful careers and continue strengthening the global communication community.

Earlier, Neliaku announced that the Global Alliance had approved the integration of a Women’s Conference into future editions of the WPRF, making women’s participation and inclusion a central feature of the global gathering.

He described the decision as a significant step towards ensuring that women remain at the centre of the profession’s global conversations and leadership structures.

Neliaku also announced the induction of selected masters of ceremonies into a newly established College of MCs, following a selection process involving participants from different parts of the world.

He said the initiative had led to the introduction of a course on the art and science of compering events at the University of Public Relations and Leadership.

The NIPR president further disclosed that the Abuja Declaration, adopted at the forum, would serve as a global commitment to responsible communication, peace, development, persuasion, reason and the prevention of conflict.

He said the declaration would be deepened and promoted across the world as a framework for using communication to build peace and support development.

“The voice of the world, the voice of peace, the voice of development, the voice of non-violent communication, the voice of persuasion, the voice of reason,” he said.

The 13th World Public Relations Forum, which brought together communication professionals and leaders from across the world, ended with a celebration of Nigeria’s hosting and a call for the next host country to surpass the achievements of the Abuja edition.

title: Nasarawa attracts $2.3bn investments in seven years — Abdullahi
description:
Records 21 reforms, 11 PPP projects worth ₦93bn



By John Alechenu



ABUJA — Nasarawa State has attracted more than $2.3 billion in investments over the past seven years following reforms and institutional development aimed at making the state more competitive and investor-friendly.







The Man
content:
Records 21 reforms, 11 PPP projects worth ₦93bn

By John Alechenu

ABUJA — Nasarawa State has attracted more than $2.3 billion in investments over the past seven years following reforms and institutional development aimed at making the state more competitive and investor-friendly.

The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Nasarawa Investment and Development Agency, Ibrahim Abdullahi, disclosed this at the 13th World Public Relations Forum 2026 in Abuja.

Abdullahi said the investments cut across agriculture, solid minerals, retail, commercial activities, manufacturing, agro-processing and education.

He added that the state also implemented 11 public-private partnership (PPP) projects valued at about ₦93 billion within the period.

According to him, the achievements were the outcome of seven years of reforms and deliberate institution-building under Governor Abdullahi Sule, rather than publicity campaigns or political slogans.

Recounting the beginning of the process, Abdullahi said he was invited into the Nasarawa State public service seven years ago, when Governor Sule appointed him as economic adviser.

He said the assignment was to develop the state’s investment profile and position it as an attractive destination for investors.

He thanked the organisers of the forum for recognising Governor Sule with an honour presented a few days earlier.

Abdullahi said one of the first lessons from the assignment was the need to establish the necessary structures before embarking on investment promotion.

“So we could not go out and invite people to come to Nasarawa State without building any framework around it. That is to say that you cannot communicate something that is not there. You cannot communicate something that hasn’t been built. So, we put our heads down and began to build,” he said.

He explained that the state’s vision, as contained in the Nasarawa Economic Development Strategy, was to make it one of Nigeria’s most competitive states through improved and accelerated economic growth that would translate into better living conditions for residents.

Under the strategy, he said, the government implemented more than 21 reforms focused on improving the business environment and making the state attractive to investors.

He said the reforms were designed to guarantee a conducive business climate, competitive returns on investment and improved general welfare for residents.

According to him, the measures included the digitisation of revenue administration and improvements in the state’s fiscal and financial management framework.

Abdullahi said the reforms provided the foundation for the state to confidently promote its investment opportunities to local and international investors.

He noted that investors were attracted not by impressive speeches but by predictability, transparency, good returns and a government that honoured its commitments.

The investment agency chief said the experience offered important lessons to other state governments and public relations professionals, stressing that investment attraction should begin with building the necessary structures rather than merely branding a destination.

He also highlighted the importance of purpose in communication, saying communicators must be clear about the objectives they seek to achieve.

“Do I want to communicate to build or destroy? Once you have that conviction and a sense of purpose, it guides how you even communicate your message,” he said.

On reputation management, Abdullahi said credibility was essential to attracting and retaining investors, adding that reputation required deliberate efforts to establish and sustain.

“Your reputation is not just earned, you have to build it,” he said.

He identified courage and collaboration as other important ingredients for success, noting that people and institutions seeking meaningful progress must be willing to pursue new ideas and take bold decisions.

“There is no price tag for the best idea. Everywhere around the world, everyone who is succeeding has had to show a remarkable amount of zeal and courage,” he said.

Fund backs 31 projects, as FG expands university initiative to 20 institutions

By Uzoma Marvellous

The Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF) has supported the delivery of 25 operational Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) stations across the country in two years, with its investment portfolio expanding to 31 projects comprising 205 infrastructure assets.

The Executive Director of MDGIF, Mr Oluwole Adama, disclosed this during the commissioning of CNG refuelling facilities at the University of Lagos (UNILAG), University of Ibadan (UI), Federal University of Technology, Akure (FUTA) and Federal University Oye-Ekiti (FUOYE) on Thursday.

Adama said the achievements reflected the Federal Government’s efforts to deepen domestic gas utilisation, expand infrastructure and make natural gas more accessible to motorists and transport operators.

“In just two years, MDGIF has supported the delivery of 25 fully operational CNG stations nationwide, bringing cleaner, more affordable fuel closer to motorists and transport operators,” he said.

Established under Section 52 of the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA), the fund supports investments in midstream and downstream gas infrastructure.

Adama disclosed that the UNILAG facility was the 11th CNG station being commissioned in Lagos State, adding that nine additional university stations, mostly in Northern Nigeria, would be commissioned within weeks.

“Eleven stations in one state is a clear signal that CNG is no longer a promise for tomorrow. In Lagos, it is becoming part of everyday life,” he said.

Meanwhile, the Federal Government is expanding its university CNG initiative to 20 institutions, with 11 stations already commissioned under the programme.

The Chief Executive Officer of Femadec Energy Limited, Engr. Fola Akinnola, said the company planned to complete six additional stations before the end of 2026, while the remaining three would be commissioned early in 2027.

The programme began with facilities at the University of Abuja, Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife, and Federal University of Technology, Owerri.

Four other facilities were subsequently commissioned at the University of Uyo, University of Calabar, Federal University of Petroleum Resources, Effurun, and University of Nigeria, Enugu Campus.

Akinnola said the 20-campus initiative was designed to reduce transportation costs for students, lecturers and other university employees while promoting cleaner energy adoption.

“Campus communities are dynamic hubs of daily movement, where high transportation costs directly impact students, faculty and support staff alike. By systematically delivering this 20-campus network, we are providing immediate, practical relief—cutting campus transit fuel costs while significantly lowering carbon emissions,” he said.

He added that the facilities would also serve as practical training centres, exposing engineering and technical students to gas infrastructure management, vehicle conversion, maintenance and international safety standards.

“Each of these stations is designed as a living laboratory. Consistent with our commitment to technical capacity building, these facilities serve as hands-on training and conversion hubs,” he said.

The Minister of Education, Dr Maruf Tunji Alausa, said the programme, known as the Special Palliative Relief on University Transportation (Project SPROUT), was designed to address the high cost of commuting among students and university workers.

“Through the Special Palliative Relief on University Transportation, known as Project SPROUT, we are addressing one major concern students raise with us directly: the cost of getting to class,” Alausa said.

He explained that the initiative would cover 20 federal universities, beginning with a pilot phase involving one institution from each of the six geopolitical zones.

The minister urged university managements and transport operators to ensure that savings from the lower operating costs of CNG-powered vehicles translated into affordable fares and reliable campus shuttle services.

“The switch to CNG reduces running costs. I therefore urge university managements and transport operators to work together so that students share in those savings through affordable fares and dependable shuttle services,” he said.

Alausa also highlighted the employment and skills-development opportunities offered by the facilities, urging universities to expose students to vehicle conversion, equipment maintenance and station operations through supervised practical training.

He, however, stressed the importance of regular equipment maintenance, personnel training and compliance with safety regulations.

“Commercial operations must begin only after the required regulatory approvals are in place,” he cautioned.

Also speaking, the National President of the National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS), Comrade Akinteye Babatunde Afeez, said transportation remained one of the major daily expenses confronting students in tertiary institutions.

He noted that many students spent a significant portion of their upkeep on commuting, sometimes at the expense of other basic necessities.

Afeez said the success of the initiative should be measured by its direct impact on students through affordable fares, reliable transportation services and improved mobility within campuses.

“However, as an organisation whose primary responsibility is to protect and advance the interests of Nigerian students, we want to emphasise that the success of this programme must ultimately be measured by its direct impact on students,” he said.

title: FCT traders, artisans pledge Tinubu 200,000 votes
description:
Credit Wike’s roads, markets for endorsement



By Omeiza Ajayi



ABUJA — Traders, market women and artisans in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) have pledged to mobilise at least 200,000 votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general elections, citing infrastructure and market development p
content:
Credit Wike’s roads, markets for endorsement

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA — Traders, market women and artisans in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) have pledged to mobilise at least 200,000 votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general elections, citing infrastructure and market development projects executed under the FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike.

Chairman of the Amalgamation of Market Associations in the FCT, Chief Raphael Okorie, announced the pledge at a mini-rally in Abuja on Friday, saying the association had more than 300,000 members across the territory.

Okorie said the decision to support Tinubu’s re-election was based on what the group described as improvements in trading conditions and infrastructure across the FCT.

According to him, the decision to back the President “did not come easily or lightly”, but was informed by “what our eyes have seen and what our pockets have felt.”

The association consequently declared its “full and unreserved support” for Tinubu’s re-election bid.

“We are not politicians. We are people who wake up before dawn, open our shops, light our fires, and carry our wares to the market,” Okorie said.

He said the association would immediately commence grassroots mobilisation, urging members to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and participate in the election.

“We will go from person to person and house to house. We will make sure every member collects a permanent voter’s card, and we will make sure every member comes out to vote,” he said.

Okorie commended Wike for what he described as improvements in trading conditions through road construction, market development and the relocation of trading activities to designated areas.

He specifically mentioned roads in Gwagwalada, Dei Dei and Saburi, the Old Keffi Road linking Kado to Dei Dei, and the Kugbo International Market.

He also cited the relocation of the Apo Mechanics Village to Wassa as one of the initiatives aimed at improving trading and business activities in the territory.

“Let us speak about roads, because for a trader, a road is not a luxury. A road is life. These are not promises on paper. These are roads you can drive on and markets you can walk into,” he said.

The association chairman argued that improved roads and street lighting would enhance security by making communities more accessible and reducing hiding places for criminals.

“When roads are good, the area becomes safer. When streets are lit, when roads are open and busy, criminals lose their hiding places. A well-planned city is a safer city, and we feel the difference,” he added.

While acknowledging that traders still had concerns, Okorie said the FCT Minister had shown willingness to engage with their association and address their demands.

“He has promised regular interaction with traders, and we will hold him to that. But we are fair people, and fairness demands that we say plainly: this administration has done more for our markets and our trade than any we can remember,” he said.

Reaffirming the group’s commitment to Tinubu’s re-election, Okorie said the 200,000-vote target represented an expression of appreciation for the administration’s interventions in the FCT.

“We promise this nation and this city that we will deliver no fewer than 200,000 votes for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in the Federal Capital Territory.

“That is our gift to the President, and our word of honour to the Minister. We are repaying kindness with loyalty,” he said.

title: Christians were denied admission, jobs, promotions over names in Northern Nigeria – Balami makes case for Tinubu
description:
The National Director of Special Duties of the City Boy Movement, Isaac David Balami, has alleged that Christians in Northern Nigeria were previously denied university admission, employment and promotion in some instances because of their names.
Balami said the situation had created years of hardshi
content:
The National Director of Special Duties of the City Boy Movement, Isaac David Balami, has alleged that Christians in Northern Nigeria were previously denied university admission, employment and promotion in some instances because of their names.

Balami said the situation had created years of hardship for Christian communities in the region, arguing that citizens should not be discriminated against on the basis of their religious or ethnic backgrounds.

He made the remarks while addressing Christian and religious leaders in Abuja, where he called on the Church to become more actively involved in politics and national leadership.

On the sideline of the event, Balami said the country needed to confront uncomfortable truths about the experiences of Christian communities, particularly in Northern Nigeria.

“This is the moment of truth. These are times we should just stop lying to ourselves. Lies have brought this country to its knees. Lies have deceived us that people have endured what we have endured,” he said.

Recalling what he described as past experiences of religious discrimination, Balami said there was a time when certain names could prevent Christians from gaining admission into universities, securing employment or receiving promotions.

“There used to be a time in this country where with certain names, you can’t secure an admission into the university, gain employment or be promoted,” he said.

However, he argued that President Bola Tinubu had demonstrated a different approach to governance by treating Nigerians as citizens irrespective of their religious and ethnic identities.

“But President Tinubu came and said this must not continue. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is not taking us like that. He is taking us as Nigerians,” Balami added.

He urged Christian leaders to recognise the importance of political participation, saying the Church could no longer afford to remain detached from leadership and governance.

According to him, the early missionaries who introduced Christianity and formal education in many communities did not adequately prepare the Church for political leadership.

“The missionaries taught us everything but failed to teach us leadership. The Church abandoned leadership, hence Agbero took over leadership, and that has to change,” he said.

Balami said the Christian community needed to unite and take responsibility for shaping Nigeria’s political direction, particularly as the country approaches the 2027 general elections.

Quoting John 17:22, he stressed the importance of unity within the Body of Christ, arguing that disunity had weakened the Church’s ability to influence national affairs.

He also urged Christian and traditional leaders to mobilise support for Tinubu’s re-election, insisting that the administration had been fair to different ethnic nationalities.

Balami acknowledged that the impact of government reforms might not be felt immediately but urged Christians not to make what he described as the mistake of voting Tinubu out in 2027.

“We should not make a mistake as a Body of Christ to vote President Bola Tinubu out. We will regret it,” he said.

He maintained that his position was not motivated by personal benefits from the administration, claiming that he had neither received an appointment from the government nor secured a government contract.

The City Boy Movement director also called for an end to what he described as the practice of exploiting Middle Belt communities during elections and abandoning them when political appointments and opportunities are distributed.

He recalled that some political leaders received substantial support from Northern communities during the 2023 elections but failed to adequately recognise the region when it came to sharing political responsibilities.

Balami said Middle Belt leaders and younger generations were now determined to demand fairness, inclusion and equal opportunities in the country’s political system.

He cited recent engagements between prominent Middle Belt leaders, including General Theophilus Danjuma and former Speaker of the House of Representatives, Yakubu Dogara, with the President and other government officials, as part of efforts to address the region’s concerns.

He further called on wealthy Christians to extend their resources to less privileged members of society, insisting that believers should not concentrate wealth within their immediate families while others in their communities struggle.

“If God has blessed you, bless others. As believers, we should not be selfish. We should not wait for the government to do everything,” he said.

Using his community of Shaffa as an example, Balami urged affluent Nigerians to invest in education, welfare and opportunities for disadvantaged people.

He also appreciated Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, for sending a representative to the gathering and acknowledged the presence of the Esu Karu.

Balami’s remarks come amid growing political engagement by Middle Belt stakeholders ahead of the 2027 general elections, with calls for greater representation, inclusion and recognition of the region’s interests in national affairs.
