By James Ogunnaike



ABEOKUTA — The governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ogun State, Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, has unveiled a development blueprint featuring plans to generate more than 50,000
content:
Promises 50,000 annual jobs, 2,500km roads, 200MW additional power

By James Ogunnaike

ABEOKUTA — The governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ogun State, Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, has unveiled a development blueprint featuring plans to generate more than 50,000 formal jobs annually, construct and rehabilitate 2,500 kilometres of roads and provide an additional 200 megawatts of electricity if elected governor in 2027.

Adeola unveiled the blueprint, tagged ITESIWAJU: Governance That Works for Everyone, at its formal launch at the June 12 Cultural Centre, Abeokuta, on Friday.

The manifesto, which outlines his proposed development agenda up to 2031, is anchored on nine policy pillars covering infrastructure, tourism, education, security, healthcare, women and youth empowerment, agriculture, industrialisation and urban renewal.

Addressing political leaders, traditional rulers and other stakeholders at the event, the senator said the document was developed following consultations with communities across the state’s 20 local government areas.

He described the manifesto as a social contract with the people, urging residents to scrutinise its contents and hold him accountable for the commitments should he emerge governor.

“Today, I place that agenda, built on your voices, back in your hands. This agenda is a plan, not a performance. Read it as you would read a contract, because that is exactly what it is,” he said.

Adeola pledged to sustain and expand the infrastructure and economic development initiatives of Governor Dapo Abiodun’s administration, stressing that he would not abandon ongoing projects or policies yielding positive results.

He commended successive administrations in the state, including those of former governors Olabisi Onabanjo, Olusegun Osoba, Gbenga Daniel and Ibikunle Amosun, for their contributions to Ogun’s development.

He particularly acknowledged Abiodun’s ISEYA Development Agenda, citing the Gateway International Agro-Cargo Airport, proposed Kajola and Ijebu-Ode dry ports, planned Gateway Deep Sea Port, road construction and housing projects as investments capable of strengthening the state’s economy.

According to Adeola, Ogun’s economy is currently valued at approximately ₦17 trillion, while its internally generated revenue has increased significantly.

“ISEYA laid the foundation for economic growth. ITESIWAJU will build the foundation for more economic growth and prosperity for our people,” he said.

He described Ogun’s strategic location, bordering Lagos State, the Republic of Benin and other Nigerian states, as a major advantage for industrialisation, trade, logistics and regional economic integration.

The senator proposed positioning Ogun as the “New Jersey” to Lagos, arguing that improved transportation, reliable electricity, planned residential communities and an investor-friendly environment would enable the state to accommodate businesses and workers seeking opportunities around Lagos.

However, he acknowledged that the benefits of economic growth had yet to reach many households, citing unemployment, unreliable electricity, inadequate agricultural storage facilities and pressure on healthcare services.

On employment and empowerment, Adeola promised to establish a ₦10 billion Enterprise and Empowerment Fund to support 60,000 businesses owned by women and young people.

He also pledged to train 100,000 youths in digital skills, including coding, data analysis, graphic design and digital marketing, as well as another 100,000 women in practical and entrepreneurial skills.

The manifesto further proposes reserving at least 30 per cent of senior government appointments for women.

He promised to establish sports hubs, youth academies and an annual Ogun State Sports Festival to identify and develop sporting talents.

A social safety net would also be introduced to support 20,000 widows, elderly citizens, persons living with disabilities and low-income households.

On infrastructure, Adeola pledged to construct and rehabilitate 2,500 kilometres of roads by 2031, with emphasis on rural, urban and border communities.

He said the programme would improve connectivity between farming communities and markets, facilitate access to essential services and stimulate economic activities across the three senatorial districts.

On electricity, he identified an estimated 600-megawatt power deficit in the state and promised to address it initially through 200 megawatts of embedded and renewable energy generation.

The proposed projects include the Oke-Mosan Independent Power Project, renewable energy investments around Oyan Dam, power development around Ewekoro and solar mini-grids for underserved communities.

He also pledged to advance the development of the Gateway International Agro-Cargo Airport, Kajola and Ijebu-Ode dry ports, the proposed Gateway Deep Sea Port and Blue Marine Special Economic Zone in Ogun Waterside.

On transportation, Adeola promised to introduce between 50 and 100 compressed natural gas-powered buses within 12 months of assuming office.

The buses, he said, would operate along priority routes, including Abeokuta, Sango-Ota to Lagos, Mowe-Ibafo-Berger, Sagamu to Abeokuta and Sagamu to Lagos.

He also proposed establishing a Gateway Metropolitan Area Transport Authority to coordinate public transportation and introducing OgunRide, a regulated ride-hailing service covering cars, tricycles and licensed motorcycles.

“No one in Ogun State should wait under a tree for a bus again,” he said.

On industrialisation, the APC candidate promised to strengthen industrial estates, establish export-oriented industrial clusters and transform border communities such as Idiroko, Imeko and Ipokia into commercial and logistics centres.

He said his administration would introduce an Ogun State Local Content and Skills Development Law to encourage businesses operating in the state to employ and develop local talent without imposing additional taxes or levies.

He also promised to create 12,000 apprenticeship and internship opportunities by his fourth year in office, including placements in the energy, minerals and petroleum supply chain sectors.

On agriculture, Adeola said only about 30 per cent of Ogun’s estimated 1.2 million hectares of arable land was currently cultivated.

He promised to increase the proportion to 60 per cent through a programme tagged “Grow Ogun, Feed Nigeria”, which would focus on mechanisation, irrigation, improved extension services, agricultural financing and market access.

He also proposed developing cocoa production hubs in Ogun East, cashew hubs in Ogun West and oil palm hubs in Ogun Central, linking them to Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones.

In education, the senator pledged to rehabilitate 2,000 classrooms, construct 500 new educational facilities and train more than 35,000 public-school teachers.

He also set a target of achieving 95 per cent primary school completion through improved learning facilities, technology integration, curriculum modernisation and better teacher welfare.

On healthcare, he promised to equip and adequately staff primary healthcare centres across the state’s wards and establish a Centre of Medical Excellence in each senatorial district.

He further pledged to expand the Ilera D’ero health insurance programme to cover two million residents by 2031 and reduce maternal mortality to below 200 deaths per 100,000 live births.

On security, Adeola promised to strengthen the Amotekun Corps, reposition the State Security Trust Fund and establish a Joint Intelligence Fusion Centre.

He also proposed deploying CCTV surveillance and drones in major towns and border communities within three years, while preparing the state for a possible transition to state policing, subject to the necessary national legislation.

The APC candidate identified tourism and the creative economy as additional sources of revenue and employment, promising to develop 12 flagship tourism destinations to attract 500,000 visitors annually and generate a projected ₦15 billion in revenue by 2031.

Among the attractions he highlighted were Olumo Rock, Bilikisu Sungbo Grove, the Ojude Oba Festival, Lisabi Festival, Oronna Festival and the coastal attractions of Ogun Waterside.

He also proposed establishing an Ogun Film Village to promote film production, fashion, music and the state’s indigenous Adire textile industry.

On natural resources, Adeola promised to maximise opportunities in oil, gas and solid minerals, expressing optimism about prospective commercial oil production around Eba Island.

He said his administration would pursue the state’s constitutional entitlement to 13 per cent derivation when applicable and proposed establishing a naval base on Tongeji Island to strengthen maritime security.

He also identified gold, tantalite, kaolin, limestone and bitumen as mineral resources that should be processed locally to create employment and generate greater economic value.

Under urban renewal, the senator promised to attract ₦500 billion in private investment into urban development, identifying the Ota-Agbara, Mowe, Sagamu, Lagos-Ogun border, Sagamu-Ijebu and Abeokuta-Owode corridors as priority areas.

He also proposed preparing physical development master plans for all 20 local government areas and establishing physical planning offices in each council.

On environmental management, he pledged to strengthen the Ogun State Waste Management Agency, introduce performance-based contracts for private waste operators, establish waste-to-energy facilities and expand recycling programmes.

He also promised to eliminate open defecation by 2031.

Beyond the nine policy pillars, Adeola identified six strategic enablers for implementing the manifesto. They include fiscal discipline and revenue mobilisation, justice sector reform, legislative reform, civil service reform, optimisation of government assets and local government autonomy.

He proposed a Single Window Revenue Collection System to improve transparency, reduce revenue leakages and eliminate multiple taxation.

According to him, the state’s revenue increased by 136 per cent to ₦238.5 billion in 2025, while federal allocations still account for approximately 40 per cent of government expenditure.

He promised to expand the state’s revenue base without imposing additional taxes or double taxation on investors.

On justice administration, he proposed mobile courts, fast-track courts and electronic justice systems to reduce delays and improve access to justice.

He also pledged merit-based recruitment, improved pension administration, digital workflows and sustained implementation of the minimum wage in the civil service.

Adeola further promised to ensure that statutory allocations reach the 20 local government areas directly, fully and promptly, in accordance with constitutional provisions.

To ensure accountability, he pledged to establish a Governor’s Delivery Unit within 30 days of assuming office.

He said commissioners and heads of government agencies would sign performance agreements tied to specific targets, while a public performance dashboard would track progress quarterly.

The indicators would include secondary school completion, household electricity access, youth unemployment, maternal mortality, internally generated revenue as a proportion of total revenue and access to primary healthcare facilities within five kilometres.

He also promised that citizens would be able to report service delivery failures and receive responses within 21 working days.

An independent panel, he said, would assess government performance twice yearly, while an annual State of Ogun Report would be presented to the public.

“We will measure progress not by the ribbons we cut, but by the lives we change,” he said.

Adeola outlined four major economic and social targets for 2031, promising to increase per capita income from approximately $1,740 to $2,500, raise annual economic growth from about four per cent to between six and seven per cent, and increase revenue per resident from ₦39,600 to ₦66,000.

He also pledged to reduce the proportion of households living in multidimensional poverty from 68 per cent to below 45 per cent.

The senator acknowledged that some proposals, including state policing, the extension of Lagos rail lines into Ogun and the realisation of oil derivation benefits, would require cooperation with the Federal Government.

He nevertheless promised to pursue the necessary partnerships and keep residents informed about their progress.

Adeola urged residents to scrutinise the manifesto and hold him accountable for its implementation if elected, saying the document should serve as a basis for assessing his performance in 2028, 2029 and 2031.

“I do not ask you to believe me. I ask you to hold me to this covenant,” he said.

He added: “We are not coming to rule over you. We are coming to work beside you. We will listen closely. We will learn with humility. We will act with the fear of God and with decisive resolve.”

Beyond the nine policy pillars, Adeola identified six strategic enablers for implementing the manifesto. They include fiscal discipline and revenue mobilisation, justice sector reform, legislative reform, civil service reform, optimisation of government assets and local government autonomy.

He proposed a Single Window Revenue Collection System to improve transparency, reduce revenue leakages and eliminate multiple taxation.

According to him, the state’s revenue increased by 136 per cent to ₦238.5 billion in 2025, while federal allocations still account for approximately 40 per cent of government expenditure.

He promised to expand the state’s revenue base without imposing additional taxes or double taxation on investors.

On justice administration, he proposed mobile courts, fast-track courts and electronic justice systems to reduce delays and improve access to justice.

He also pledged merit-based recruitment, improved pension administration, digital workflows and sustained implementation of the minimum wage in the civil service.

Adeola further promised to ensure that statutory allocations reach the 20 local government areas directly, fully and promptly, in accordance with constitutional provisions.

To ensure accountability, he pledged to establish a Governor’s Delivery Unit within 30 days of assuming office.

He said commissioners and heads of government agencies would sign performance agreements tied to specific targets, while a public performance dashboard would track progress quarterly.

The indicators would include secondary school completion, household electricity access, youth unemployment, maternal mortality, internally generated revenue as a proportion of total revenue and access to primary healthcare facilities within five kilometres.

He also promised that citizens would be able to report service delivery failures and receive responses within 21 working days.

An independent panel, he said, would assess government performance twice yearly, while an annual State of Ogun Report would be presented to the public.

“We will measure progress not by the ribbons we cut, but by the lives we change,” he said.

Adeola outlined four major economic and social targets for 2031, promising to increase per capita income from approximately $1,740 to $2,500, raise annual economic growth from about four per cent to between six and seven per cent, and increase revenue per resident from ₦39,600 to ₦66,000.

He also pledged to reduce the proportion of households living in multidimensional poverty from 68 per cent to below 45 per cent.

The senator acknowledged that some proposals, including state policing, the extension of Lagos rail lines into Ogun and the realisation of oil derivation benefits, would require cooperation with the Federal Government.

He nevertheless promised to pursue the necessary partnerships and keep residents informed about their progress.

Adeola urged residents to scrutinise the manifesto and hold him accountable for its implementation if elected, saying the document should serve as a basis for assessing his performance in 2028, 2029 and 2031.

“I do not ask you to believe me. I ask you to hold me to this covenant,” he said.

He added: “We are not coming to rule over you. We are coming to work beside you. We will listen closely. We will learn with humility. We will act with the fear of God and with decisive resolve.”

title: Six killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza
description:
Israeli strikes killed six people in the Gaza Strip on Friday, the civil defence agency in the war-shattered territory told AFP, in the latest violence despite a ceasefire.
The Israeli military told AFP it had “targeted multiple military operatives” in several strikes, which came a day after the arm
content:
Israeli strikes killed six people in the Gaza Strip on Friday, the civil defence agency in the war-shattered territory told AFP, in the latest violence despite a ceasefire.

The Israeli military told AFP it had “targeted multiple military operatives” in several strikes, which came a day after the army said it had completed a rare ground incursion in the central Gaza Strip.

Israel and Hamas regularly accuse each other of violating the ceasefire that came into effect in October 2025, after two years of war triggered by the Palestinian Islamist movement’s unprecedented attack on Israel on October 7, 2023.

Mahmoud Bassal, the spokesman for Gaza’s civil defence agency, said that four Palestinians were killed and several others wounded in an Israeli airstrike southwest of Bureij refugee camp in the central Gaza Strip on Friday.

The nearby Al-Aqsa-Martyrs Hospital and Al-Awda Hospital each confirmed receiving two bodies following the strike.

The civil defence, a rescue force that operates under Hamas authority, also said one Palestinian was killed in an Israeli drone strike targeting a tent in the Al-Munasara camp for displaced people in Deir al-Balah.

A drone strike north of Nuseirat refugee camp, also in the central Gaza Strip killed another person, the civil defence said.

Al-Aqsa-Martyrs Hospital confirmed receiving two bodies following those strikes.

When asked by AFP, the Israeli military said: “Regarding these locations, we conducted several strikes targeting multiple military operatives”.

On Thursday, the military said it had completed a ground operation involving tanks in the central Gaza Strip that had begun the previous day.

It had targeted areas in a Hamas-controlled zone of central Gaza, beyond the so-called “Yellow Line” which separates areas under Israeli military and Hamas control following the ceasefire.

The military said the operation had been launched to “dismantle a terror tunnel” that posed a threat to troops.

More than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the start of the ceasefire, according to an AFP tally based on data from the Gaza health ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.

Over the same period, the Israeli military says seven of its soldiers have been killed, as well as one civilian contractor.

AFP

title: 18 countries visit Nigeria to study data protection framework – Olatunji
description:
From Adanna Nnamani, Abuja
The National Data Protection Commission (NDPC) says at least 18 countries have visited Nigeria in the last two years to study its data protection framework and learn from the country’s experience in regulating the sector.
The National Commissioner of the NDPC, Dr Vincent O
content:
From Adanna Nnamani, Abuja

The National Data Protection Commission (NDPC) says at least 18 countries have visited Nigeria in the last two years to study its data protection framework and learn from the country’s experience in regulating the sector.

The National Commissioner of the NDPC, Dr Vincent Olatunji, disclosed this on Friday in Abuja during a training programme organised for journalists by the commission.

Olatunji said Nigeria’s approach to data protection regulation had attracted international attention, particularly its Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model, which allows licensed Data Protection Compliance Organisations (DPCOs) to carry out compliance activities on behalf of the government.

He said the model had been recognised globally as unique and impactful, contributing significantly to the progress recorded in Nigeria’s data protection ecosystem.

According to him, Nigeria has also recorded more than 27,000 jobs in the data privacy ecosystem in less than three years, with the commission targeting the creation of about 500,000 jobs in the sector.

He said: “For this ecosystem, which is a sub-sector of the economic sector, we are saying that over 500,000 jobs are available in the data privacy ecosystem. And we are already pushing towards achieving that.

“If within the ecosystem we are doing over 27,000 jobs in less than three years, that is massive. That is very huge. But the target is to get to about 500,000 and even more.”

Olatunji also disclosed that Nigeria currently has more than 10,000 certified Data Protection Officers (DPOs), compared with fewer than 1,000 when the commission began its operations.

He said the growing demand for data protection professionals presented an opportunity for journalists to acquire additional skills and explore career opportunities without necessarily abandoning their profession.

The NDPC boss explained that journalists could become certified DPOs, conduct research and provide data protection services to organisations, including media establishments.

He urged participants to take the training seriously, noting that data protection was becoming an increasingly important global skill, with organisations across different sectors seeking qualified professionals.

Olatunji further said the commission was extending data privacy awareness and training to tertiary institutions to educate students about their rights and introduce them to emerging career opportunities.

He noted that about 94.7 per cent of data breaches in the United Kingdom were linked to a lack of qualified personnel in data privacy and protection, underscoring the global demand for professionals in the field.

On the commission’s regulatory approach, Olatunji said the NDPC prioritised compliance and remediation rather than imposing fines as a first response to violations.

He explained that the commission regarded organisations and other stakeholders as partners, adding that sanctions would be applied when operators crossed established legal boundaries.

According to him, the objective is to build a culture of compliance while ensuring that regulation supports economic growth and development rather than driving businesses out of operation.

He also said Nigeria’s data protection framework was attracting international partnerships, with countries including Egypt and Qatar expressing interest in collaborating with the commission.

Olatunji urged journalists to play a strategic role in promoting awareness of data protection rights and responsibilities, stressing that the effective protection of personal data was essential to Nigeria’s digital economy.

Earlier, the President of the Nigeria Information Technology Reporters Association (NITRA), Mr Blessing Olaifa, commended the commission for its partnership with the media and called for more opportunities for journalists to participate in its capacity-building programmes.

Olaifa said the training had exposed participants to data protection issues that journalists might previously have overlooked, particularly in the publication and republication of reports.

He also expressed interest in the opportunity for journalists to become certified Data Protection Officers, urging the commission to extend the initiative to more members of the association.

title: Nigeria to become world’s third-largest Muslim population by 2035 – Report
description:
Nigeria is projected to have the world’s third-largest Muslim population by 2035, behind Pakistan and India, as Islam is expected to record significant growth globally over the next decade.







The projection is contained in a report by the Pew Research Centre titled Future of World Religions, re
content:
Nigeria is projected to have the world’s third-largest Muslim population by 2035, behind Pakistan and India, as Islam is expected to record significant growth globally over the next decade.

The projection is contained in a report by the Pew Research Centre titled Future of World Religions, released on Wednesday.

According to the report, Muslims are expected to outnumber Christians globally by 2070 if current demographic trends continue, marking a significant shift in the religious composition of the world.

The report projects that the global Muslim population will exceed 3.6 billion by 2070, compared with just under three billion Christians.

It attributed the projected growth largely to differences in fertility rates, noting that Muslim women had an average of 3.1 children between 2020 and 2025, compared with 2.5 for Christian women and 1.6 for women belonging to other religious groups.

The report explained that a population requires an average of about 2.1 children per woman to maintain its size across generations.

Under the projections, Pakistan will have the world’s largest Muslim population by 2035, followed by India, Nigeria and Indonesia, which currently has the largest Muslim population.

The findings further indicated that four of the 10 countries with the largest Muslim populations by 2070 would be in Africa, namely Nigeria, Egypt, Ethiopia and Sudan.

The Pew Research Centre’s projections cover 201 countries and territories, accounting for 99.98 per cent of the world’s population.

It said the estimates were based on the assumption that existing trends in fertility, mortality and religious switching would continue, while acknowledging that developments such as wars, natural disasters and economic changes could alter the projections.

The report also projected significant changes in the global Christian population, particularly in the United States, which is expected to lose its Christian-majority status, although Christians would remain the country’s largest religious group.

It further predicted that the Democratic Republic of the Congo would overtake the United States as the country with the largest Christian population.

For centuries, Christianity has remained the world’s largest religion, but the latest projections point to a gradual shift in the global religious landscape, driven largely by population growth and demographic differences.

title: Four transmission lines trip in 16 minutes, disrupt power supply nationwide
description:
By Udeme Akpan, Energy Editor



Four major transmission lines tripped within 16 minutes on Friday, triggering significant electricity load losses in Lagos and other parts of the country.







The Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO), which disclosed this in a statement, ruled out a nationa
content:
By Udeme Akpan, Energy Editor

Four major transmission lines tripped within 16 minutes on Friday, triggering significant electricity load losses in Lagos and other parts of the country.

The Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO), which disclosed this in a statement, ruled out a national grid collapse, describing the incident as a transmission line disturbance.

According to the operator, the first incident occurred at 12:34 p.m. when the Omotosho–Ikeja West transmission line tripped, causing a significant load drop within the Lagos Complex.

At 12:50 p.m., three other lines – Ihovbor–Oshogbo, Benin–Egbin and Ihovbor–Ajaokuta – also tripped, resulting in further load losses across parts of the country.

Clarifying the incident, NISO said: “The grid disturbance experienced earlier today was not a system collapse, but a result from the tripping of some transmission lines, which caused load losses in parts of the country.”

The operator said its operational teams, working with the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN), immediately activated emergency measures to stabilise the grid and restore the affected lines.

It confirmed that all four lines had returned to normal operation by 2:49 p.m. on Friday.

NISO stated: “All the affected lines have since been successfully restored to normal operation as of 2:49pm today.”

The operator did not disclose the volume of electricity lost, the number of affected consumers or the specific causes of the transmission line trips.

title: Tinubu’s NYSC certificate: Court dismisses Atiku, ADC application
description: A Federal High Court in Abuja has dismissed an application by former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) seeking to amend their suit challenging President Bola Tinubu’s eligibility for the 2027 presidential election over his National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) dis
content:
A Federal High Court in Abuja has dismissed an application by former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) seeking to amend their suit challenging President Bola Tinubu’s eligibility for the 2027 presidential election over his National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) discharge certificate.

In a ruling on Friday, according to TheCable, Justice Inyang Ekwo held that the proposed amendments would introduce new facts and alter the substance of the original case.

The judge upheld the arguments by Tinubu, the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) that the applicants were attempting to introduce a fresh allegation of fraud after the defendants had responded to the original suit.

Ekwo noted that pre-election cases were sui generis, meaning they belonged to a special category of legal proceedings and were subject to strict timelines.

He added that litigants could not institute such actions and subsequently search for evidence to support their claims.

The judge also faulted the applicants for failing to challenge claims in the defendants’ counter-affidavits that the proposed amendments were intended to mislead the court.

“This is a time-bound suit, and the law makes it mandatory for all exhibits to be filed in court within 14 days of the occurrence of the event being challenged. Anything outside the prescribed 14 days is null and void and of no effect,” the judge held.

“I find no merit in this application to bring a fresh exhibit; it is hereby refused for being against the express provision of the law.

“I hereby make an order dismissing this application, and it is hereby dismissed,” he ruled.

The matter was adjourned until December 2 for hearing.

Atiku and the ADC had filed the substantive suit on August 14, seeking an order disqualifying Tinubu and the APC from the 2027 presidential election over an allegation that the NYSC discharge certificate submitted by the President to INEC was forged.

They also sought an order compelling the electoral commission to remove Tinubu’s name and the APC from the list of candidates and political parties for the election.

Following the defendants’ responses, Atiku and the ADC approached the court on September 10, seeking to amend their originating summons.

They said the proposed amendments were intended to correct errors in the description of INEC forms attached to their affidavit, provide clearer copies of exhibits, include particulars of the alleged fraud and incorporate Atiku’s written deposition.

However, Tinubu opposed the application, arguing that the proposed changes went beyond correcting errors and would introduce new facts, documents and reliefs.

He also contended that the original suit was statute-barred and that an incompetent originating process could not be amended.

The APC and INEC also opposed the application, arguing that the proposed amendments would introduce a new cause of action outside the 14-day constitutional period for filing pre-election cases.

Tinubu and the APC have denied submitting a forged certificate to INEC, maintaining that the NYSC has never disowned the discharge certificate.

title: 2027: Rivers ADC gov candidate promises 100,000 agric jobs
description:
The governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress in Rivers State, Gabriel Pidomson, has promised to create between 50,000 and 100,000 jobs in the state through agriculture if elected governor in 2027.
Pidomson said the plan would involve providing young people with farmland, start-up lo
content:
The governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress in Rivers State, Gabriel Pidomson, has promised to create between 50,000 and 100,000 jobs in the state through agriculture if elected governor in 2027.

Pidomson said the plan would involve providing young people with farmland, start-up loans, agricultural training and access to markets for their produce.

He spoke during a programme aired on Wazobia FM in Port Harcourt on Friday, monitored by our correspondent.

The governorship hopeful said the state had enough fertile land and water resources to support large-scale farming and reduce its dependence on imported food.

According to him, the agricultural programme would focus on fish, shrimp and crab farming in riverine communities, while cassava, maize, vegetables, rice, palm oil and poultry production would be developed in other parts of the state.

Pidomson, a former Secretary to the Rivers State Government, stated, “We will provide over 5,000 tractors for people to lease because the problem of farming in the state is that since people don’t have enough money, farmers can’t buy the tractors.

“However, if the government and private concerns invest in these tractors, they can be given out on lease for people to pay in instalments so that whenever one wants to clear his farm rather than use bare hands, one can hire the tractor with a small amount of money and use it to clear the land.

“Now we will have what is called green well core for young people. The fact is that we want to employ at least 50,00 to 100,000 young people.”

The plan, he said, also includes establishing agro-processing centres to turn farm produce such as cassava into garri and starch, as well as processed rice, palm oil, fish and poultry products for local consumption and export.

Pidomson further promised to establish what he described as the largest fish farm east of the Niger to boost production and create more jobs.

The state ADC governorship candidate expressed optimism that the agricultural programme would also develop rural communities, reduce migration to the city and create employment opportunities beyond Port Harcourt, the state capital.

He added, “We will establish the largest fish farm in the East of the Niger. It will be a mega fish estate that will have different types of fish to be located in the Kalabari axis of the state.

“With such an industry there, people will not need to come to Port Harcourt again.

“It means people who don’t have jobs and want to run to Port Harcourt for jobs and possibly add to the challenge of insecurity will now be going to work from their houses there.”

title: 2027: I wil build 40,000 Classrooms, establish 10,000 Healthcare Centres across Nigeria if elected – Obi vows
description:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has promised to establish 10,000 primary healthcare centres and construct 40,000 primary school blocks across Nigeria if elected president in the 2027 general election.
Obi said the proposed projects would expand access
content:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has promised to establish 10,000 primary healthcare centres and construct 40,000 primary school blocks across Nigeria if elected president in the 2027 general election.

Obi said the proposed projects would expand access to healthcare and education, particularly in rural communities and underserved areas across the country.

The former Anambra State governor made the promises on Friday during an NDC town hall meeting and homecoming event held at the Main Bowl of the Archbishop C.J. Patterson Building, All Saints Cathedral, Onitsha, Anambra State.

Speaking on his healthcare plans, Obi said his administration would ensure that every ward in Nigeria had access to a functional primary healthcare facility.

He noted that Nigeria has 8,809 wards but maintained that his proposed target would exceed that number, with plans to establish 10,000 primary healthcare centres.

“We will ensure that there’s a functional primary care in every ward in Nigeria. We have 8,809 wards, but we have promised Nigeria that we’ll do 10,000 primary care. That’s what we are going to do,” he said.

On education, the former governor expressed concern over the country’s out-of-school children crisis, citing an estimated 18 million children currently outside the classroom.

He pledged to construct 40,000 primary school blocks as part of efforts to improve access to basic education and reduce the number of children who are unable to attend school.

Obi said the impact of the proposed intervention would begin to become visible from the first day of his administration.

“What goes on, I have said, is that we have 18 million out-of-school children. From day one, people will see the reduction because we plan to do 40,000 primary school blocks. And we will do that,” he stated.

The NDC candidate added that his proposed administration would prioritise investment in education, healthcare and public safety, insisting that government resources must be directed towards improving the lives of ordinary Nigerians.

“What we are promising you is not a fake. We will invest in education. We will invest in health. We will invest in building that society that you’ll be proud of, that society that will care,” he said.

Obi’s appearance in Onitsha formed part of his political engagements ahead of the 2027 general election. The event followed a roadshow through parts of the commercial city and a visit to his former school, Christ the King College, Onitsha.

The former governor, who led Anambra State from 2006 to 2014, was the Labour Party’s presidential candidate in the 2023 election before joining the NDC to pursue his 2027 presidential ambition.

He is running with former Kano State Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso as his running mate.

The proposed healthcare and education projects form part of Obi’s campaign promises, although details of their funding, implementation timelines and delivery arrangements were not provided in the announcement.

title: Four Dead, Others Rescued As Passenger Boat Conveying Funeral Guests Capsizes In Bayelsa
description: At least four people, including two children, have died after a passenger boat capsized at the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.Some passengers were still missing at the time of filing this report, but others were rescue
content:
At least four people, including two children, have died after a passenger boat capsized at the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.

Some passengers were still missing at the time of filing this report, but others were rescued, while search and rescue operations continued for the missing people.

A survivor alleged that the wooden big boat popularly referred to as “love boat” was overfilled with passengers and their properties; hence, it could have led to the boat accident.

The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, saying the boat was travelling from Ayama community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony that is taking place on Friday, November 20, 2026, when it capsized at about 11 a.m.

The preliminary police report indicated that the boat developed a mechanical problem while navigating the waterways.

Nigeria’s Deadly Boat Accidents

Nigeria has recorded several deadly boat accidents in 2026, claiming dozens of lives and renewing concerns about safety on the country’s waterways.

On January 4, 24 people died after a canoe capsized in Adiyani village, Guri, Jigawa State.

Ten passengers were rescued, while 14 were initially reported missing.

On February 16, 14 people, including 13 women and a child, died when a boat carrying more than 100 passengers capsized in Kebbi State after a wedding celebration.

In July, six people died, and 15 were rescued after a canoe carrying about 40 passengers capsized in Jigawa.

August brought another major tragedy in Sokoto, where 46 people died and 16 were initially missing.

In September, eight died in a speedboat collision in Cross River, while four teenage girls died in another Jigawa accident.

title: Many feared dead as overloaded boat capsizes in Bayelsa
description:
By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa



Many passengers are feared dead after a cargo boat conveying more than 300 persons capsized in the riverine area of Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State on Friday.







The ill-fated vessel was reportedly travelling from Anyama Ijaw to Ukubie communi
content:
By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa

Many passengers are feared dead after a cargo boat conveying more than 300 persons capsized in the riverine area of Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State on Friday.

The ill-fated vessel was reportedly travelling from Anyama Ijaw to Ukubie community when the incident occurred between 12 noon and 1pm.

Preliminary reports indicated that the boat, which was allegedly overloaded with passengers travelling to attend a burial ceremony, capsized in the waterways between Oweikorogha and Angiama communities.

Eyewitness accounts suggested that the tragedy might have been averted, as some passengers reportedly advised the boat operator to stop at Oweikorogha to reduce the number of persons on board.

However, the advice was allegedly ignored, and the boat reportedly capsized shortly after leaving the community.

Although the actual casualty figure remained unknown as of the time of filing this report, fears were mounting that the death toll could be high, given the number of passengers on board.

The Chairman of the State Maritime Workers Union, Mr Ipigansi Igoniba, confirmed the incident to our correspondent but said details of the disaster were still sketchy.

“I cannot give the casualty figure right now. We have sent our members to the scene of the accident, and search and rescue efforts for the missing persons are ongoing,” Igoniba said.

Rescue operations were ongoing as efforts continued to establish the number of survivors and fatalities.

The incident has thrown the affected communities into mourning and renewed concerns over the dangers of overcrowding and unsafe transportation on Bayelsa’s waterways.

The post Many feared dead as overloaded boat capsizes in Bayelsa appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Tragedy as boat capsizes in Bayelsa, kills many
description:
No fewer than 30 people are feared dead after a wooden passenger boat travelling from Ayama to Ukubie community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State capsized during a journey for a burial ceremony.
A source said the boat was overloaded and overturned shortly after departing Oweiko
content:
No fewer than 30 people are feared dead after a wooden passenger boat travelling from Ayama to Ukubie community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State capsized during a journey for a burial ceremony.

A source said the boat was overloaded and overturned shortly after departing Oweikorogha community, despite passengers reportedly raising concerns about the large number of people on board.

Another source, however, described the vessel as a “love boat” carrying revellers who were enjoying a cruise along the river, dancing to loud music and drinking.

The incident has raised concerns over passenger safety and the dangers of overloading boats on Bayelsa’s waterways.

The exact number of casualties and the circumstances surrounding the tragedy are yet to be fully established.

The Nation gathered that some passengers had suggested that the boat made a stop at Oweikorogha to decongest the vessel due to the large number of people on board, but the plea was reportedly ignored.

But the Bayelsa Police Command in a statement by its image maker, Mr. Musa Mohammed, a Deputy Superintendent, who confirmed the incident, put the death toll at four, adding that the incident occurred yesterday at 11.00 a.m.

According to the statement, the boat mishap occurred at the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.

Mohammed said preliminary information indicated that the boat developed a mechanical problem while navigating the waterways.

The statement added that some passengers urged the boat operator to steer towards the riverbank but he ignored the pleas of the passengers.

It added that the Bayelsa Police, in synergy with local divers from the affected communities and other relevant responders, commenced search and rescue operations.

Part of the statement reads, “So far, four (4) bodies, comprising two adults and two children, have been recovered and deposited at the Federal Medical Centre (FMC) Mortuary, Yenagoa. Twenty-four (24) survivors have also been rescued, with nineteen (19) taken to Ayama Clinic and five (5), who sustained varying degrees of injuries, conveyed to Family Care Hospital, Yenagoa, for medical attention. Other passengers rescued from the incident have reportedly returned to their respective communities.”

The statement further stated that the boat operator simply identified as Omovie reportedly fled the scene, while the manager of the boat, identified as MV Bina, has been taken into custody.

title: Why I turned down Man United job – Conte
description:

content:
Ex-Chelsea coach Antonio Conte has defended his demanding coaching methods following discussions surrounding his failure to become Manchester United’s manager, insisting that his approach is built on hard work and winning.

The Italian tactician said he finds it strange that anyone could be afraid of his methodology, arguing that Manchester United need a strong approach to return to the level of success they enjoyed under former manager Sir Alex Ferguson.

Speaking to CronacheTweet on Friday, Conte said, “If anyone is frightened by my method, then they are frightened of winning, because that methodology leads to victory. That is my answer.”

Conte also expressed surprise at suggestions that his methods could be a problem for Manchester United, considering the club’s history and ambitions.

“Manchester United has such a significant history that I find it strange to imagine anyone could be afraid of an approach aimed at restoring the club to its true stature.

“They last won the league in 2013, under Ferguson. I have immense respect for Sir Alex Ferguson,” he said.

The former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur manager revealed that he had read Ferguson’s autobiography and was fortunate to spend time with the legendary Scottish manager at his home in London.

“I’ve read his book, and when I was in London, I was fortunate enough to visit his home and spend a day with him. He has an incredible passion for talking about football,” Conte added.

The 57-year-old further described some of the comments surrounding his potential appointment at Old Trafford as almost offensive to the club, insisting that a clear methodology is necessary to achieve major success.

“That is why I find certain remarks almost offensive toward United; it’s as if someone were placing a veto on the club’s return to its own history.

“A method is what’s needed to achieve major results. And if you’re suggesting that this method requires hard work, well, yes, it does. Everyone has to work hard, not just the players.”

The post Why I turned down Man United job – Conte appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

_________________________________________________________________________
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

content:
• Says digital transformation must eliminate delays, improve accountability, service delivery

_________________________________________________________________________

From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

President Bola Tinubu on Thursday directed Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) to take ownership of ongoing civil service reforms and translate them into measurable and sustainable results, insisting that the government must deliver faster, more efficient and responsive services to Nigerians.

According to a statement issued by the Director, Press and Public Relations, Eno Olotu, President Tinubu said the success of his administration’s reform agenda would depend largely on public institutions’ ability to move beyond policy pronouncements and deliver tangible improvements in governance and service delivery.

Tinubu, who spoke on Thursday in Abuja at the launch of the Public Sector Reform Playbook published by the Aig-Imoukhuede Foundation, said his administration remained committed to building a professional, digitally enabled and results-driven civil service.

Represented by the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, Olumuyiwa Abel, the President said digital transformation was already reshaping government operations through technology-driven processes designed to reduce delays, improve efficiency, strengthen transparency and enhance accountability.

He declared that “government must work better for Nigeria to work better,” charging public servants to embrace ongoing reforms as custodians of public trust and critical partners in translating government policies into concrete benefits for citizens.

The President said his administration had, since assuming office in May 2023, pursued far-reaching reforms to strengthen the economy, improve public finances and create a more conducive investment climate under the Renewed Hope Agenda.

He noted that achieving Nigeria’s ambition of building a self-reliant and prosperous economy by 2030 would require an efficient, responsive and innovative public sector.

Tinubu also urged stakeholders to rise above political differences and prioritise nation-building, stressing that strong institutions were essential to sustaining effective governance and service delivery beyond political cycles.

He called on MDAs to adopt the recommendations of the Playbook and ensure that their implementation produced measurable and lasting outcomes.

In her keynote address, a former Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, Dr Folasade Yemi-Esan, commended the Aig-Imoukhuede Foundation for its sustained commitment to improving public sector governance.

She described the Playbook as a practical resource for policymakers and reform practitioners, providing guidance on making reforms more accessible, actionable and effective.

The Chairman and Co-Founder of the Foundation, Aigboje Aig-Imoukhuede, said Nigeria was not short of reform ideas, policies or frameworks, but had struggled with sustaining implementation and translating reform ambitions into lasting results.

He said the Playbook was designed to help institutions identify priorities, strengthen implementation, promote accountability and measure performance.

The post Tinubu tasks MDAs to deliver measurable results from civil service reforms appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

…Mops up 100,000 cartons of banned alcoholic beverages



By Chioma Obinna



The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) on Friday destroyed fake, counterfeit, expired, banned and
content:
…Uncovers illegal cosmetic factory, counterfeit alcohol production hubs in Lagos, Ogun

…Mops up 100,000 cartons of banned alcoholic beverages

By Chioma Obinna

The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) on Friday destroyed fake, counterfeit, expired, banned and substandard drugs, alcoholic beverages, cosmetics and other regulated products worth N100 billion in Ogun State.

The destruction exercise, which took place at Ogwama Dumpsite, Ogere Remo, was aimed at preventing dangerous products from re-entering the Nigerian market and endangering public health.

Speaking at the flag-off ceremony, the Director-General of NAFDAC, Professor Christiana Mojisola Adeyeye, said the products included counterfeit, expired, controlled, unregistered and banned medicines, as well as unwholesome food products and cosmetics.

Among the products destroyed were banned alcoholic beverages packaged in sachets and PET bottles below 200ml, banned Analgin injection, expired Codeine cough syrups, Oxytocin injection and counterfeit cosmetics.

Adeyeye said: “The estimated street value of these products being destroyed today stands at one hundred billion naira only.”

She explained that the exercise was part of the agency’s sustained efforts to prevent expired, fake, substandard and falsified products from finding their way back into circulation.

The NAFDAC boss disclosed that recent enforcement operations had exposed several illegal manufacturing and distribution networks, particularly in Lagos and Ogun states.

According to her, operatives uncovered a warehouse in Lagos originally meant for tools and hardware, where illegal cosmetic products were being manufactured in the penthouse of the building.

She said officers also recovered several cartons of Augmentin and Ampicillin packets, leaflets and other unregistered cosmetics.

In another operation, NAFDAC investigators uncovered a production hub where counterfeit versions of popular alcoholic beverage brands were being manufactured, while expired energy drinks were allegedly being revalidated and stored for sale.

Adeyeye said suspects arrested in connection with the activities would face the full weight of the law.

She further disclosed that NAFDAC officers, in collaboration with relevant stakeholders, mopped up more than 100,000 cartons of banned sachet and small PET-bottle alcoholic beverages from manufacturers, wholesalers and retailers across Lagos and Ogun states.

The agency also uncovered a residential building allegedly converted into a production and distribution centre for unauthorised and registered herbal mixtures being sold in large quantities to Nigerians.

Adeyeye said other products destroyed included items seized during enforcement raids and expired products voluntarily surrendered by compliant companies.

She said the destruction would eliminate the possibility of the dangerous products being recycled or returned to the Nigerian market.

The NAFDAC director-general particularly commended the Nigeria Customs Service for handing over pharmaceutical products, including several cartons of Codeine cough syrup and CSC cough syrup containing codeine, for destruction.

She also acknowledged the support of the Nigeria Police Force, Nigerian Army, Department of State Services, Pharmacists Council of Nigeria, National Drug Law Enforcement Agency and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps.

Adeyeye urged community and religious leaders, health practitioners, the media and members of the public to intensify public education on the dangers of purchasing medicines and other regulated products from unauthorised vendors.

She said: “It is imperative that you educate your families and wards about the dangers of patronising quacks and unauthorised vendors.”

The NAFDAC boss called on Nigerians to provide useful information to the agency to help identify and eliminate counterfeit, unregistered and dangerous products from the market.

She reiterated that the agency remained committed to ensuring that food, drugs, cosmetics, medical devices, chemicals, packaged water and beverages available in Nigeria were safe, wholesome and effective.

The post NAFDAC destroys fake, expired drugs, drinks worth N100bn appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Obi pledges massive investment in education, healthcare
description:
By Chimaobi Nwaiwu

Obi, who made the pledge on Friday during a
content:
By Chimaobi Nwaiwu

NNEWI — Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has pledged massive investment in education and healthcare, improved electricity supply and an end to kidnapping if elected president in 2027.

Obi, who made the pledge on Friday during a visit to Onitsha, Anambra State, also said his proposed administration, with Rabiu Kwankwaso as his running mate, would prioritise national unity, job creation, security and the productive use of public resources.

The former Anambra State governor spoke during an inspection of a building being constructed for teachers of Christ the King College (CKC), Onitsha, his alma mater.

The building, which was already at the painting stage, is being funded by Obi and other contributors.

He said the project was aimed at providing teachers with a comfortable working environment and strengthening the quality of education.

“I am here to inspect the teacher’s house at CKC. This is my alma mater, and we are doing this to secure the pride of education and also give teachers the comfort they need to be able to impart knowledge on our children.

“I always come here to support what they do from time to time. I and others built this teacher’s house for the school. Education to me remains the tool for development. It is one investment that if I have the opportunity to serve Nigeria, everybody will visibly and measurably see our investment in education,” he said.

Obi recalled his interventions in schools during his tenure as governor, saying he believed education was central to societal development.

He added that teachers, security personnel and other workers needed decent accommodation to perform their duties effectively.

The NDC presidential candidate later attended a town hall meeting at C.J. Patterson Hall, All Saints Cathedral, Onitsha, where he addressed party supporters and outlined his proposed administration’s priorities.

He said his partnership with Kwankwaso was aimed at uniting the country and addressing its security and economic challenges.

“Kwankwaso and I have formed a team, and that is the team that will unite Nigeria.

“We are not going to have a Nigeria where people will come and kidnap our schoolchildren. We will fight corruption, we want to use public money for public good, and from day one, you will feel it and you will know that a new team is in charge,” Obi said.

He promised to move the country from consumption to production, create employment opportunities and strengthen primary healthcare delivery.

“We will move Nigeria from consumption to production, and our people will get jobs. We want a country where if you are sick, you go to hospital and not church.

“We will ensure a functional primary healthcare centre in every ward in Nigeria. We will build 50,000 primary school blocks. We will invest in education, healthcare and other sectors you will be proud of,” he said.

On electricity, Obi said his proposed administration would increase power generation from the approximately 4,000 megawatts he cited as the country’s current output to 10,000MW.

He urged Nigerians to participate actively in the electoral process, describing the 2027 election as an opportunity to demand accountable leadership.

Obi also called on voters to protect their votes by remaining at polling units during counting and transmission of results.

“Nigerians have suffered enough, so all of you are contestants in this election through us. So go out on that day, take it as a day of sacrifice for Nigeria. Carry your food to the polling unit on that day, vote, stay there for counting and transmitting and make sure there is no rigging. That day is now declared a public holiday for vote defence,” he said.

He also criticised the borrowing record of the President Bola Tinubu administration, arguing that the country’s resources should be deployed more effectively for public benefit.

Earlier, activist and prominent Obi supporter, Aisha Yesufu, drew attention at the gathering when she opened her address by singing the former national anthem.

Defending her action, Yesufu said the song was intended to encourage Nigerians to rise and defend their country, insisting that she had not violated any law.

She said the country was facing serious security challenges and called for greater national unity, particularly between the North and South-East.

Yesufu also urged Nigerians to mobilise for the NDC, announcing plans for supporters to wear blue on Mondays to identify with the party and embark on street campaigns on Saturdays.

Addressing Obi directly, she said the campaign belonged to Nigerians and called for concerted efforts to secure the release of abducted schoolchildren.

Responding to the controversy over the former national anthem, Obi said there was no law prohibiting anyone from singing it.

“We started this event with the new national anthem and prayers, so after that, anyone who wants to sing whatever song before speaking is free to do so, and there is nothing wrong with it,” he said.

The senator representing Anambra Central, Victor Umeh, who spoke on behalf of the party’s candidates, expressed confidence in the NDC’s electoral prospects.

Umeh described Obi’s campaign as a movement for national change and said the party expected substantial support from the South-East, while Kwankwaso would mobilise votes in the North.

The post Obi pledges massive investment in education, healthcare appeared first on Vanguard News.

From Aloysius Attah, Onitsha
Anambra State Governor Prof Chukwuma Soludo has rolled out an additional ₦50,000 flat payment for all state civil servants, to be reflected directly on their December 2026 payslips.
Soludo, who disclosed this at the 2026 Civil Service Day celebration held at the Jerome U
content:
From Aloysius Attah, Onitsha

Anambra State Governor Prof Chukwuma Soludo has rolled out an additional ₦50,000 flat payment for all state civil servants, to be reflected directly on their December 2026 payslips.

Soludo, who disclosed this at the 2026 Civil Service Day celebration held at the Jerome Udoji State Secretariat Complex in Awka, paired the financial boost with instant executive approvals to modernise the secretariat environment and enhance productivity.

Addressing demands comparing Anambra’s salary structure with that of other states, the governor delivered a candid lesson on fiscal federalism, reminding the workforce that states operate with vastly different economic capacities.

He urged workers to always weigh a state’s revenue and resource base before making inter-state wage comparisons, emphasising that sustainable governance, not empty promises, guided his administration.

“I understand the situation and economic conditions; we need to be able to do something. The pay that we have all over is not enough; I clearly understand it.

“But there is one thing I also tell you, and that is I don’t play to the wind. Before we get into a commitment, we make sure that it is something that we will always honour,” he said.

Soludo also thanked the workers for standing solidly behind his administration during the governorship election, expressing confidence that Anambra’s public servants overwhelmingly voted for and appreciated his government’s developmental strides.

Acting swiftly on three major appeals presented during the event, the governor issued immediate directives, including Secretariat Road Rehabilitation and ICT Centre Establishment, and granted instant approval for the pruning of overgrown trees across the secretariat complex.

Earlier, the Anambra State Head of Service, Barr Ngozi Iwouno, lauded Soludo for restoring security and normalcy across the state.

She noted that civil servants now reported to duty consistently without fear, having completely overcome the dread of the past Monday sit-at-home orders, before presenting the workforce’s appeals to the governor.

title: World Children’s Day: UNICEF, Lagos pledge action on children’s rights, welfare
description:
By Doris Obinna
The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and the Lagos State Government have pledged stronger action to protect children’s rights, improve their welfare and secure their future, with a commitment to translate their demands and aspirations into concrete policies and interventions.
content:
By Doris Obinna

The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and the Lagos State Government have pledged stronger action to protect children’s rights, improve their welfare and secure their future, with a commitment to translate their demands and aspirations into concrete policies and interventions.

The commitment was made on Friday in Lagos to mark the 2026 World Children’s Day organised by UNICEF in collaboration with the Lagos State Ministry of Youth and Social Development, with the theme “My Day. My Rights. My Future.”

The Commissioner for Youth and Social Development, Lagos State, Mr Mobolaji Ogunlende, reiterated that the government remained committed to the welfare, protection and development of every child but acknowledged that achieving this required stronger collaboration with parents, schools, communities and development partners.

Speaking on the theme “My Day, My Rights, My Future,” Ogunlende said children were not merely leaders of tomorrow but important voices in shaping society today, stressing that their opinions, rights and aspirations must be reflected in government policies.

He said the state government remained committed to promoting the welfare, protection and development of every child but acknowledged that government could not achieve this responsibility alone.

According to him, parents, schools, communities, development partners and other stakeholders must work together to create an environment where children feel safe, valued and heard.

Ogunlende said the children’s activities, particularly their artworks and conversations, provided an opportunity for government to understand their expectations and the kind of future they wanted.

He assured that the issues raised by the children would not end with the celebration but must translate into meaningful commitments and interventions.

“The future of every child in the state is important to the government. That is why we have the three pluses in the THEMES Plus Agenda, particularly the pillar on children’s rights and children’s future,” he said.

The commissioner described UNICEF as a critical development partner, noting that the ultimate beneficiaries of the collaboration were the children whose lives government and its partners were working to improve.

Earlier, the UNICEF Chief of Field Office, Lagos, Celine Lafoucriere, urged the Lagos State Government to ensure that every child, particularly the most vulnerable, enjoyed their fundamental rights, warning that children’s rights were increasingly under threat globally.

She identified education, healthcare, good nutrition, clean water, sanitation and social protection as essential rights that must be accessible to every child.

Lafoucriere said UNICEF was working closely with the Lagos State Government to ensure that no child was left behind, particularly those whose families lacked the resources to provide basic necessities.

She stressed that social protection was critical to bridging the gap between having rights and actually enjoying them, explaining that vulnerable children needed government support to access education, healthcare and adequate nutrition.

“Having a right is one thing, but it’s not going to put food on the table,” she said.

The UNICEF official challenged government and other adult stakeholders to move beyond listening to children’s demands and demonstrate their commitment through practical action.

“When our children paint the Nigeria they dream of, our job as adults is not to admire the picture. Our job is to build it,” she said.

She disclosed that commitments made by adults during the children’s gallery walk would be documented and followed up, insisting that promises to children must be measurable and kept.

The celebration featured 80 children divided into eight groups, who used paintings and other creative expressions to communicate their vision of the Nigeria they wanted.

The eight panels were subsequently brought together into a collective installation titled “80 Children, One Future.”

A member of the Lagos State Children’s Parliament and Young People’s Action Team, Rt. Hon. Abdulsalam Anjola, used the occasion to call on government to invest more in children’s education and involve them in decisions affecting their lives.

He said children who experienced abuse should be encouraged to speak for themselves, noting that their accounts could better convey the pain and trauma they endured.

Anjola also urged the government to provide educational opportunities for vulnerable children, including those living and working on the streets, stressing that investment in education would help build a safer Lagos and a better Nigeria.

Similarly, a 14-year-old student of Ikeja Senior High School, Ishola Moyinoluwa, urged government to create platforms where children could express their views and discuss issues affecting their rights and future.

She said every child deserved free basic education and the opportunity to pursue their dreams, explaining that her artwork, titled “My Dream, My Possibilities,” portrayed a young boy aspiring to become an astronaut.

In her closing remarks, the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Youth and Social Development, Mrs Toyin Oke-Osanyintolu, called on children to speak up against violations of their rights and remain confident in pursuing their aspirations.

She described children as the pride of Lagos State and urged them to take responsibility for contributing to the future they desired.

Oke-Osanyintolu appreciated UNICEF for its continued support to the state, expressing optimism about stronger collaboration to advance children’s welfare and protection.

She urged the children to believe in their abilities, declaring: “If you can dream it, you can do it.”

The post World Children’s Day: UNICEF, Lagos pledge action on children’s rights, welfare appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Police vow to arrest attackers of Segun Odegbami
description:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta



The Ogun State Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, has ordered an immediate investigation into the attack on former Super Eagles captain and sports administrator, Chief Segun Odegbami, assuring him that those responsible would be arrested and prosecuted.







Ojaj
content:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

The Ogun State Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, has ordered an immediate investigation into the attack on former Super Eagles captain and sports administrator, Chief Segun Odegbami, assuring him that those responsible would be arrested and prosecuted.

Ojajuni gave the assurance when he visited Odegbami at his residence in Abeokuta to express the sympathy of the Ogun State Police Command and reassure him of its commitment to protecting lives and property.

The Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, disclosed this in a statement made available to journalists on Friday.

During the visit, the commissioner expressed concern over the incident and wished the former football international a speedy recovery, assuring him that the command was treating the matter with the seriousness it deserved.

He said he had directed an immediate and comprehensive investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack and identify those responsible.

Ojajuni also assured Odegbami that the command would deploy all necessary investigative resources to apprehend the suspects and ensure they faced the full weight of the law.

The statement partly read: “The Commissioner of Police, Ogun State Command, CP Bode Ojajuni, has paid a visit to former Super Eagles captain and renowned sports administrator, Chief Segun Odegbami, to express the Command’s sympathy following the reported incident at his residence in Abeokuta.

“The Commissioner conveyed his concern and wished him continued recovery, reaffirming the Command’s commitment to protecting lives and property across the state.

“CP Ojajuni assured Chief Odegbami that the incident is receiving the Command’s utmost attention. He disclosed that he had ordered an immediate and thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident, while intensive investigative efforts are ongoing to identify and apprehend those responsible.”

The command further confirmed that Odegbami had been discharged from hospital and urged residents to remain calm and provide credible information that could assist the investigation through established police channels.

Odegbami, proprietor of Eagles 7 Sports Radio 103.7 FM, was reportedly attacked at about 2:30am on Friday at his residence in Ibara GRA, Abeokuta.

According to accounts from residents, three armed men allegedly stormed the football legend’s residence and attacked his domestic staff and driver before gaining access to his bedroom.

The attackers were said to have inflicted machete cuts on the former footballer during a struggle before fleeing the scene.

A resident, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the assailants initially demanded to know Odegbami’s whereabouts after overpowering members of his domestic staff.

The resident said the attackers reportedly suspected that he was at home because the generator was running at the time.

“They asked for Chief Segun Odegbami and his staff denied that he was at home. But the generator was on at that time. So, the armed men believed he must be at home and they handed severe beatings to the staff,” the resident said.

The source added that the assailants eventually located Odegbami’s bedroom, where he reportedly resisted them before they fled.

The motive for the attack had yet to be established as of the time of filing this report.

The post Police vow to arrest attackers of Segun Odegbami appeared first on Vanguard News.

Basiru noted that ending the subsidy regime had
content:
From Lateef Dada, Osogbo

The National Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Dr Ajibola Basiru, has warned Nigerians against falling for calls to reverse the fuel subsidy removal, cautioning that such a move would drag the country backward.

Basiru noted that ending the subsidy regime had been a major saving grace for the nation’s economy, enabling state governors to pay workers and pensioners promptly.

He made the remarks in Osogbo on Friday during a meeting with ward and local government coordinators of the Alubarika Movement from across Osun State.

Urging citizens to support President Bola Tinubu’s administration, Basiru asserted that critics campaigning for the reinstatement of the subsidy did not have the country’s best interests at heart.

“Today, because of the removal of the petroleum subsidy, states have the resources to pay workers’ salaries and pensions as and when due.

“Those calling for the reversal of this policy do not mean well for Nigeria. The only way the country can progress is to vote decisively for Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” Basiru said.

He tasked the coordinators with mobilising grassroots support for President Tinubu and all APC candidates vying for seats in the Senate, House of Representatives and State House of Assembly.

Highlighting the administration’s achievements in education, healthcare, security and infrastructure, Basiru noted that over 5,500 kilometres of roads were currently under construction or completed across the country.

He also pointed to the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), stating that it had enabled children from low-income families to pursue university education without financial strain, while academic strikes had been addressed to ensure uninterrupted tertiary education.

During the event, Basiru introduced the APC senatorial candidate for Osun Central, Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) Kunle Rasheed Adegoke, encouraging party members to work tirelessly for his victory alongside other APC flagbearers.

“I enjoin all of us to walk every street, knock on every door, visit every market, and canvass votes for APC candidates. With your dedication as canvassers and the commitment of those who believe in President Tinubu’s vision, we will celebrate victory on January 17, 2027,” Basiru said.

The report, titled Future of World Religions, examines anticipated changes i
content:
Nigeria is projected to have the world’s third-largest Muslim population by 2035, behind Pakistan and India.

This is according to a new report by the Pew Research Centre, which was posted on Monday and went viral on Friday.

The report, titled Future of World Religions, examines anticipated changes in the size and distribution of religious populations across 201 countries and territories.

The report read, “Pakistan is expected to record the highest number of Muslims by 2035, followed by India, Nigeria and Indonesia, which currently has the largest Muslim population.”

The projection comes amid expectations that Islam will continue to grow faster than Christianity, potentially becoming the world’s largest religion.

It said, “The global Muslim population is projected to increase by 80 per cent, exceeding 3.6 billion, while the number of Christians is expected to grow by 30 per cent to just below three billion.”

The report attributed much of the anticipated growth to differences in fertility rates among religious groups.

Between 2020 and 2025, Muslim women had an average of 3.1 children, compared with 2.5 among Christian women and 1.6 among women from other religious groups.

It explained that a population generally needs an average fertility rate of 2.1 children per woman to maintain its size across generations.
Pew said its projections cover 201 countries and territories, accounting for 99.98 per cent of the world’s population.

However, it cautioned that the estimates are based on the assumption that existing patterns of fertility, mortality and religious conversion will continue.

The Centre noted that unforeseen developments, including armed conflicts, natural disasters and economic changes, could affect the projected outcomes.

Looking further ahead, the report projected that Africa would account for four of the 10 countries with the largest Muslim populations by 2070.

Nigeria, Egypt, Ethiopia and Sudan were listed among the African countries expected to feature prominently in the ranking.
The report also forecast major changes in the global distribution of Christianity.

It projected that the United States would lose its Christian-majority status, although Christians would remain the country’s largest religious group.

The Democratic Republic of the Congo is also expected to overtake the United States as the country with the largest Christian population in the world.

The post Nigeria projected to have world’s third-largest Muslim population by 2035 — Report appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: LP condemns rising political violence ahead of 2027 polls

By John Alechenu, Abuja



The Labour Party (LP) has condemned the rising cases of politically motivated violence across the country ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that the trend poses a threat to democracy and national stability.
