content:
By John Alechenu, Abuja

The Labour Party (LP) has condemned the rising cases of politically motivated violence across the country ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that the trend poses a threat to democracy and national stability.

The party cautioned that failure to address the situation could derail the democratic process and plunge the country into an avoidable crisis.

The National Publicity Secretary of the party, Ken Asogwa, stated this in an interview with Vanguard in Abuja, where he appealed to political parties and their supporters to exercise restraint in their conduct and utterances.

Asogwa said the political atmosphere was already charged, warning that inflammatory statements and violent actions by political actors and their supporters could worsen tensions.

He said the Labour Party remained committed to peaceful, issue-based politics and would not be drawn into what he described as politics of bitterness, personal attacks and violence.

“For us in the Labour Party, all our candidates are bound by our code of ensuring issue-based campaigns devoid of personal attacks, insults and inflammatory rhetoric,” Asogwa said.

He maintained that elections should be contests of ideas, programmes and solutions to the challenges facing Nigerians rather than platforms for insults, intimidation and violence.

According to him, the party has directed its candidates at all levels to focus their campaigns on issues affecting the daily lives of citizens, including the economy, security, education, healthcare, employment and good governance.

“We need to first have a nation before we can contest for elective offices,” he said.

The LP spokesman stressed that no political ambition was worth the blood of any Nigerian, urging political leaders to put the country’s unity and stability above their individual ambitions.

He said leaders must recognise that Nigeria would remain one country after the elections, irrespective of their outcomes.

Asogwa also called on security agencies to be proactive, impartial and firm in dealing with individuals and groups promoting political violence, irrespective of their affiliations.

He urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), civil society organisations, the media and other stakeholders to support efforts to promote peace, tolerance and responsible political engagement ahead of the polls.

He said the Labour Party would continue to advocate peace, unity and issue-based campaigns as the country approaches the 2027 general elections.

According to him, democracy can only thrive in an atmosphere of peace, tolerance and respect for divergent views.

title: Power supply crashes to 781MW as four lines trip
description:
By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja



Electricity supply from the national grid plunged to 781 megawatts (MW) on Friday following the tripping of four transmission lines, the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) has disclosed.







Data obtained from the system operator showed that power generation, w
content:
By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja

Electricity supply from the national grid plunged to 781 megawatts (MW) on Friday following the tripping of four transmission lines, the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) has disclosed.

Data obtained from the system operator showed that power generation, which stood at 3,990MW at midnight, dropped to 3,935MW by 6am and 3,365MW by 11am before crashing to 781MW at 1pm.

The development left only eight power plants supplying electricity to the national grid as of 1pm, with Delta Power contributing 223MW, Odukpani National Integrated Power Project (NIPP) generating 182MW and Ihovbor NIPP supplying 168MW.

However, electricity supply recovered to 2,568MW by 5pm following emergency interventions by NISO and the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN).

In a statement on Friday, NISO attributed the sharp decline to the tripping of four transmission lines, clarifying that the incident was not a system-wide grid collapse.

The operator said the disturbance began at 12:34pm when the Omotosho-Ikeja West transmission line tripped, resulting in significant load losses within the Lagos Complex.

It added that the situation was compounded at 12:50pm by the tripping of the Ihovbor-Oshogbo, Benin-Egbin and Ihovbor-Ajaokuta transmission lines, disrupting electricity supply in some parts of the country.

According to NISO, emergency response measures were immediately activated by relevant operational teams in collaboration with TCN to stabilise the grid and restore the affected transmission lines.

The operator disclosed that all four affected lines had been successfully restored to normal operation as of 2:49pm on Friday.

“NISO wishes to reassure electricity consumers and the general public that the incident was a transmission line disturbance and not a system-wide collapse,” the statement said.

It reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining grid stability, coordinating system operations and ensuring the reliable and secure operation of the national electricity grid.

NISO also advised the public to rely on its official communications for accurate information on developments within the national grid.

title: The Other Black Gold: Nigeria’s Coffee Sector Wants A Shot
description: Richard Ali grew up with the aroma of coffee wafting through his house in central Nigeria as his father, an accountant, worked late into the night, drinking powdered, instant stuff from Maxwell House and Nescafé.It was not until years later, travelling on the other side of the continent, that
content:
Richard Ali grew up with the aroma of coffee wafting through his house in central Nigeria as his father, an accountant, worked late into the night, drinking powdered, instant stuff from Maxwell House and Nescafé.

It was not until years later, travelling on the other side of the continent, that Ali had a taste of “coffee, coffee — brewed coffee”.

“I have to bring this to Nigeria,” he thought, and he started looking into importing beans from Rwanda.

Ali later discovered he did not have to: coffee has been growing in Nigeria for more than 100 years.

A wave of entrepreneurs in Africa’s most populous country are turning towards the oil-producing nation’s other black gold — an uphill task in a place full of tea and instant coffee, and little sense of homegrown java as a daily staple or part of a wider cultural patrimony.

But roasters say they have found a market — and sense of national pride — to tap into, even if Nigeria’s beans are not well-known.

“We need to grow more coffee, whether for the domestic market, which is expanding, or the global market, which is now considering Nigerian coffee,” Ali, founder of Tigray Coffee, which launched in 2021, said over a cup of Nigerian brew, light with slightly chocolatey notes.

Agricultural Investments

In Ethiopia, hundreds of years of cultivation have bound coffee to local culture, while Uganda and Ivory Coast have become modern export powerhouses.

Nigeria produced 1,808 tonnes of beans in 2024, according to statistics from the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organisation — a paltry sum compared to Kenya’s 49,500 tonnes that same year.

The first seeds hit the ground in Nigeria in the 19th century, after coffee was introduced by British colonists.

The crop is notoriously fickle and can only grow in certain parts of the country.

But there has also been a dearth of investment in agriculture, critics say, as the government instead became over-reliant on the oil sector for revenues.

Experts have long called for a more diversified economy.

The government agrees, at least in principle: in May, agriculture minister Abubakar Kyari announced federal investments in coffee production in Ondo State, calling it “a powerful economic crop” that could create jobs and “boost rural livelihoods”.

‘Never Imported Coffee’

At the opening of a new cafe in Lagos last month, Princess Adeyinka Tekenah paired a local brew not with croissants, but puff-puff, a staple street food snack of fried dough.

“I have been in the business for 12 years, and I have never imported coffee,” the founder of Happy Coffee said.

While Tekenah has leaned into her local roots, the coffee industry has also been helped by a growing sense of cosmopolitanism in Nigeria’s cities, Ali said.

Hip cafes abound in the ritzy parts of Abuja, serving coffee sourced from around the world.

There is growing demand for “the cafe experience”, though not Nigerian coffee specifically, Ali cautioned — requiring efforts by domestic marketers “to situate Nigerian coffee within the larger specialty coffee conversation”.

Nigerian coffee culture is “non-existent, actually, which makes it quite exciting”, said Nnenna Samuila, founder of the Everything But Coffee brand.

“We can make it how we want,” Samuila, who went into business three years ago, told AFP.

In many cases, weak local production — hampered further by poor infrastructure and insecurity — cannot keep up: Samuila buys her coffee from neighbouring Cameroon as well as Ethiopia and Kenya.

The Cameroonian coffee may well be Nigerian anyhow: farmers are known to smuggle beans across the border when prices there rise, Ali said.

Frontier Market

Domestic economic headwinds and shifting regulations abroad are providing more challenges.

Economic reforms by President Bola Tinubu since 2023 have been hailed as long overdue by investors — but have also been likened to shock therapy, sending the country into a cost-of-living crisis.

Meanwhile, Ali needs to help his suppliers — smallholders, many farming informally held family plots — document their land, in order to comply with European anti-deforestation regulations.

Failure to do so could lock him out of his nascent European export market at a time when middle-class Nigerians, squeezed by inflation, have less money to spend on a mug of mud.

If investors see Nigeria as a frontier market, Ali considers local brew “a frontier origin coffee”.

“Everybody has heard of Brazilian, Colombian, Ethiopian,” he said.

“Why do we have to import coffee from wherever, when we have it here?”

AFP

The post The Other Black Gold: Nigeria’s Coffee Sector Wants A Shot appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Nwifuru reaffirms judicial independence, inaugurates court complex
description:
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki



Governor Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru of Ebonyi State has reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to judicial independence, stressing the need for an efficient justice system driven by technology and timely dispensation of justice.







Nwifuru stated this on Friday at t
content:
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

Governor Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru of Ebonyi State has reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to judicial independence, stressing the need for an efficient justice system driven by technology and timely dispensation of justice.

Nwifuru stated this on Friday at the State High Court, Abakaliki, during the special court session marking the commencement of the 2026/2027 Legal Year in the state.

The governor also inaugurated a Magistrate Court complex comprising six court halls and an exhibit hall, constructed under the administration of the Chief Judge of the state, Justice Elvis Ngene.

He advocated the adoption of technology-driven processes in the administration of justice, noting that an efficient justice system must be capable of resolving disputes promptly while minimising unnecessary expenditure of resources.

According to him, delays in the administration of justice undermine the effective use of resources, while technological innovations provide opportunities to improve judicial processes and enhance access to justice.

“A justice system that cannot resolve disputes timely wastes resources. Technology offers us the opportunity to resolve some of these things. Digital filings and digital transcriptions help.

“The significance goes beyond governance. It helps to transact with various registries without recourse to location,” he said.

Nwifuru explained that deploying digital technology in judicial administration would reduce the challenges associated with physical processes, improve efficiency and enable legal practitioners and litigants to interact with court registries more conveniently.

On judicial independence, the governor described the judiciary as a critical institution for sustaining constitutional democracy and checking possible excesses of the executive arm of government.

“An independent judiciary checkmates the government as well as its excesses. As a Governor, I recognise that the independence of the judiciary must be respected and allowed to perform its constitutional and professional mandate,” he stated.

He said his administration’s People’s Charter of Needs agenda had prioritised reforms in the justice sector, citing the introduction of electronic filing, establishment of a Moot Court, creation of the Office of the Public Defender and adoption of the Sexual Assault Bill as some of the initiatives.

The governor said the measures were aimed at strengthening institutional capacity, promoting access to justice and ensuring that the justice system remained responsive to the needs of the people.

Earlier, the Chief Judge of Ebonyi State, Justice Elvis Ngene, said the judiciary had recorded progress in several areas of judicial administration in the last year.

He identified the modernisation of judicial processes through technology, protection of judicial integrity, improvement of access to justice and appointment of qualified judicial officers as key areas of focus.

Ngene also listed official visits to correctional centres, regular human capital development, professional capacity building, infrastructural development and improvement of court facilities among the activities undertaken by the judiciary.

He emphasised that judicial integrity remained fundamental to the credibility and effectiveness of the justice system, urging judicial officers and other personnel to uphold the highest ethical standards.

The Chief Judge assured that the judiciary would sustain its investment in professional development and institutional reforms despite the financial constraints confronting the institution.

“As part of our efforts to promote this, we shall, notwithstanding the leanness of our resources, continue to encourage continuous legal education and professional learning, strengthen administrative competence, promote responsible use of technology and insist upon the highest ethical standards from every person entrusted with judicial responsibilities,” he said.

He added that the judiciary would continue to recognise the dedication of its workforce and prioritise measures to promote professionalism, institutional discipline and effective service delivery.

title: I won’t disappoint Osun people in my second term – Adeleke
description:
Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke on Friday assured the people of the state that he would not disappoint them but would do more during his second term in office.
The governor made the disclosure during Jumu’at prayers held at the Osogbo Central Mosque, where activities for his second-term inaugura
content:
Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke on Friday assured the people of the state that he would not disappoint them but would do more during his second term in office.

The governor made the disclosure during Jumu’at prayers held at the Osogbo Central Mosque, where activities for his second-term inauguration kicked off.

A statement signed by Adeleke’s spokesperson, Olawale Rasheed, stated that the governor was represented by his Deputy Governor, Kola Adewusi.

The governor recalled the struggles and battles for the sustenance of democracy in the state and vowed to continue to place the interests of the public at the heart of his administration.

Commending Osun people for their steadfastness, perseverance and persistent solidarity during the electioneering period, the governor said, “Osun has become a national model, a symbol for people’s power as the foundation of democracy.

“I won’t disappoint Osun people. I will deliver even more than my first term. I am hopeful our financial situation will soon improve with the expected resolution of the local government crisis. We will take good care of workers and all segments of the society.”

Earlier in his sermon, the Deputy Imam of the Osogbo Central Mosque, Sheikh Moruf Ishola, described the recent Osun election as “unprecedented in many respects and a standout record for all students of democracy.”

Ishola further said the Osun election that returned Adeleke broke all records in terms of its dynamics and colours, adding that “the August 15 polls defied all calculations because almighty Allah ran it.

“That is why Mr Governor must not abandon God and the people. He must continue to govern with the fear of God, keep promises and serve only the interests of the people.”

The prayer session was attended by the Secretary to the State Government, Teslim Igbalaiye; Osun Central Accord senatorial candidate, Ganiyu Olaoluwa; members of the state executive council; special advisers; and top government functionaries.

PUNCH Online earlier reported that the Osun State Government had said President Bola Tinubu, governors in the South-West and diplomats had been invited to the second-term inauguration of Adeleke.

The Secretary to the State Government, Teslim Igbalaiye, who chairs the inauguration committee, disclosed this while unveiling programmes lined up for the event at a press conference in Osogbo.

Igbalaiye said the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, several federal lawmakers, and the governor’s friends and associates from across the world had also been invited to the inauguration, scheduled to hold at the Osogbo Township Stadium on November 27.

title: How to know if FG selected you for N100,000 grant
description:
Applicants who registered for the Federal Government’s N100,000 cash support programme for vulnerable households have been advised to monitor their phones for text messages from designated payment providers to know if they have been selected.
The programme’s management board said successful applican
content:
Applicants who registered for the Federal Government’s N100,000 cash support programme for vulnerable households have been advised to monitor their phones for text messages from designated payment providers to know if they have been selected.

The programme’s management board said successful applicants would receive SMS notifications informing them of their selection and providing further instructions on how to access the financial support.

According to a statement signed by the management board and obtained by PUNCH Online on Friday, the notifications would be sent to the phone numbers obtained from the records used during the beneficiary selection process.

This means applicants should pay attention to the phone numbers associated with their registration details, as the designated payment providers are expected to communicate their selection through the numbers.

The board explained that the selection process would not happen at once, as beneficiaries would be identified and selected in phases across the country’s six geopolitical zones.

It said the exercise would involve identifying eligible households through the Social Safety Net Systems, validating their national identity records and assessing their poverty and vulnerability levels before determining those who would receive the financial support.

“The selection process involves identifying eligible households through the Social Safety Net Systems, using verified national identity records, assessing households based on poverty and vulnerability criteria, and selecting beneficiaries in phases across the six geopolitical zones,” the board stated.

The management board explained that beneficiaries would not be selected or paid simultaneously because the intervention would cover a limited number of households in each phase.

Consequently, applicants who registered for the programme on the website – nfsp.ng/signup may receive notifications at different times, depending on the phase in which their households are considered.

The board said the phased arrangement was part of the beneficiary selection process, which would be implemented across the six geopolitical zones.

It also cautioned applicants against concluding that they had been rejected simply because they had yet to receive a notification.

“If you have not received a notification, it does not necessarily mean you have been permanently excluded from the programme,” the board said.

The clarification means that the absence of an SMS should not automatically be interpreted as a final rejection, as the selection exercise is expected to continue in batches.

What happens after receiving an SMS?

The management board said applicants who receive selection notifications would be required to follow the instructions contained in the messages before their payments could be processed.

It explained that selected beneficiaries would receive the N100,000 through the bank accounts they submitted during registration.

“Selected beneficiaries will receive an SMS notification from their designated payment provider,” the board stated.

It further explained that the phone number used for the notification would be obtained from the records used during the beneficiary selection process.

Recipients are expected to follow the instructions in the message and provide the required consent before the money is credited to their submitted bank accounts.

This means receiving an SMS notification does not necessarily translate to an immediate credit alert, as selected beneficiaries must first comply with the instructions communicated by their designated payment providers and provide the required consent before the transfer is completed.

The management board’s published guidelines explain that selected beneficiaries will be contacted through SMS notifications from designated payment providers.

However, the board did not provide a separate USSD code or online beneficiary-status checker through which applicants can independently confirm their selection.

It also did not state that applicants who have yet to receive notifications should register again or submit another application.

Applicants are therefore advised to rely on official communications from the programme rather than individuals or websites claiming to offer instant confirmation of beneficiary status.

For enquiries and clarification, the programme provided the email address help@nfsp.ng and advised Nigerians to contact the Federal Ministry of Youth Development through its recognised communication channels.

Register for FG’s N100,000 family support grant here: nfsp.ng/signup

The post How to know if FG selected you for N100,000 grant appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Infantino inspects Warri Stadium, pledges FIFA support during visit
description:
By Adegboyega Adeleye







FIFA President Gianni Infantino has inspected the remodeled Warri City Stadium and pledged the world football body’s continued support for Nigerian football.



Infantino visited the Delta State facility on Friday with FIFA Secretary-General Mattias Grafström, ahead of i
content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

FIFA President Gianni Infantino has inspected the remodeled Warri City Stadium and pledged the world football body’s continued support for Nigerian football.

Infantino visited the Delta State facility on Friday with FIFA Secretary-General Mattias Grafström, ahead of its scheduled commissioning on Saturday. He was received at Osubi Airport by Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and former Nigeria Football Federation president Amaju Pinnick.

Infantino praised the Delta State Government’s investment, saying modern sports facilities could help develop young talent and expand opportunities for boys and girls. He also celebrated Nigeria’s football heritage, highlighting the country’s contribution to the global game.

“This stadium is fantastic. It has everything you can dream of. I just would love to wear some shorts and kick the ball,” he said, adding that he hoped to return and play there once the remaining work was completed.

The FIFA president also congratulated Nigeria’s U-17 women’s team, the Flamingos, on winning the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, describing their triumph as a source of pride.

“You will always count on FIFA and on the FIFA president as your not just partner, but your family member,” Infantino said.

Oborevwori said the inspection was an opportunity to assess the stadium’s readiness against international standards. In a post on X, the governor described the renovation as extensive and said the state remained committed to delivering world-class sports infrastructure.

He wrote: “It was a pleasure to welcome the President of FIFA, Gianni Infantino, to Osubi this morning. We thereafter proceeded to the Warri Stadium, where we inspected the facility to assess its readiness against international standards,”

“The transformation is extensive, and our commitment remains to deliver world-class sporting infrastructure that will position Delta State to compete on the global stage and emerge as a hub for sporting excellence. In the words of the FIFA President, Gianni Infantino: “This is fantastic!”

Earlier on Friday, Infantino inaugurated the Hussey College Sports Complex in Warri, a grassroots facility donated by the Brownhill Foundation with support from the Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board. During his visit, he also stressed the importance of bringing football closer to communities through local facilities.

Infantino’s visit to Warri is among several trips he has made to Nigeria since becoming FIFA president. He first came to the country in July 2016 for a two-day working visit to Abuja, where he met then-President Muhammadu Buhari, Nigerian football officials and presidents of African football associations.

He returned in February 2018 for the inaugural AITEO/CAF Football Awards in Lagos and a FIFA Executive Football Summit. In September 2021, he visited Lagos for the opening of the Aisha Buhari Cup and toured the renovated Moshood Abiola National Stadium in Abuja.

The post Infantino inspects Warri Stadium, pledges FIFA support during visit appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: FG backs efforts to develop Lassa fever vaccine in Nasarawa
description:
The Federal Government has pledged support for the Federal University Teaching Hospital, Lafia, Nasarawa State, in its efforts to develop a vaccine for Lassa fever, a disease that continues to claim lives in Nigeria.
The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Ali Pate, gave the
content:
The Federal Government has pledged support for the Federal University Teaching Hospital, Lafia, Nasarawa State, in its efforts to develop a vaccine for Lassa fever, a disease that continues to claim lives in Nigeria.

The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Ali Pate, gave the assurance during an inspection visit to the hospital’s Centre for Vaccine Research and Biotechnology on Friday, expressing confidence in the facility’s efforts to develop locally produced vaccines.

This is as the hospital restated its commitment to develop a vaccine for the disease.

The Director of the Centre for Vaccine Research and Biotechnology at FUTH Lafia, Prof. Mustapha Imam, disclosed this to journalists in Lafia, the Nasarawa State capital, when the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Ali Pate, paid an inspection visit to the facility on Friday.

According to Prof Imam, Lassa fever, which currently has no cure, has caused illness and claimed the lives of many Nigerians, including healthcare workers, hence the need to develop a vaccine to tackle the disease.

Imam lamented that despite the disease spreading to some West African countries, not much significant effort had been made to find a lasting solution to it.

He said, “We are talking about Lassa fever, which is primarily a Nigerian disease. Lassa fever started in Borno State. It still doesn’t have a cure.

“It has spread to some West African countries, but because it is not a Western disease, they don’t really care about finding a solution for it.

“So, we are working on it, trying to see if we can develop a vaccine. We are also working on dengue fever, which is also a problem in Nigeria and other African countries.”

Speaking on the minister’s inspection visit, the centre’s director expressed gratitude to Ali Pate for his commitment and support in ensuring that the centre had been able to deliver on its mandate since its establishment.

He noted that the minister’s visit would serve as an encouragement to the management and staff to do more, especially following his assurances of further support for the centre.

“We are really happy with the Minister’s visit because just like I have mentioned several times, this is like a baby center, and it requires all the support that it can get in terms of support, training, human capacity development, and more importantly, in terms of infrastructure.

“We are trying to fill a gap that critically exists in Nigeria. Most of the players in vaccine and drug research and development are usually in the later stages.

“So that means we need to wait for people in other countries to develop these drugs and we test them and use them. So now we are saying no to that. We don’t want to be in that trap. We want to discover the vaccines and develop them here in Nigeria,” he explained.

Earlier, the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Ali Pate, reiterated the Federal Government’s commitment to supporting the centre in developing vaccines locally and reducing Nigeria’s dependence on imported vaccines.

Our correspondent reports that the minister visited the centre while attending the 67th National Council on Health, held in Lafia, Nasarawa State.

Ali Pate said he was impressed by the facilities, the vision of the hospital’s Chief Medical Director, Dr Hassan Ikrama, and the commitment of staff to developing local vaccine production capacity.

He commended the Nasarawa State Government, the CMD and researchers from various institutions for collaborating to establish the centre and develop local solutions to Nigeria’s health challenges.

“They already have vaccine candidates that are in early stages but appear promising. So, the Federal Government will continue to support them to succeed.

“I am very impressed, and the Federal Government will continue to support this effort by bringing in partners, globally experienced partners, that can help build the human capital that this institution has,” he said.

Ali Pate stressed the importance of research that addresses local needs, saying it should be tailored to the country’s peculiar health challenges to deliver meaningful impact.

“Research is important, but it is even more important if it helps solve local problems, and it has to be contextualised, because the young men and women that I have seen here really have a lot of promise, and we will support them,” the minister added.

On his part, the Chief Medical Director of the Federal University Teaching Hospital, Lafia, Dr Ikrama Hassan, expressed appreciation to the minister for the visit, describing it as a significant boost to the hospital’s research and development efforts.

He said the hospital management remained committed to providing the necessary institutional support and a conducive environment for the research centre to achieve its mandate of advancing medical research, innovation and the development of solutions to pressing public health challenges.

Dr Hassan noted that strategic partnerships with relevant national and international institutions would be essential in strengthening the centre’s research capacity, facilitating knowledge exchange and ensuring that its activities aligned with global best practices.

He assured the minister that the hospital would continue to work closely with the centre’s leadership to translate research findings into practical healthcare interventions that would improve disease prevention, diagnosis and treatment, particularly in addressing infectious diseases affecting communities.

The CMD also expressed optimism that the minister’s engagement would open new opportunities for collaboration, capacity building, infrastructure development and greater visibility for the research centre.

The post FG backs efforts to develop Lassa fever vaccine in Nasarawa appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Some criticism of Man Utd has crossed the line – CEO
description:
Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has insisted that some of the criticism directed at the club’s hierarchy has gone too far, although he admits that supporters have every reason to be frustrated with the team’s performances.
Speaking in a rare interview with Sky Sports on Friday, Berrad
content:
Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has insisted that some of the criticism directed at the club’s hierarchy has gone too far, although he admits that supporters have every reason to be frustrated with the team’s performances.

Speaking in a rare interview with Sky Sports on Friday, Berrada acknowledged the anger among United supporters over the club’s disappointing position in the Premier League but maintained that criticism of the leadership should remain within reasonable limits.

“Being in this position comes naturally with the criticism and scrutiny we’re going to get. We accept it. Some of it is fair, some of it does cross the line,” he said.

Berrada also pointed to social media as a major contributor to the negative atmosphere surrounding the club, arguing that some individuals deliberately generate damaging stories to attract engagement and attention.

United’s director of football, Jason Wilcox, has come under particular pressure from supporters following questions over the club’s summer recruitment.

Minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe has also faced criticism, with fans regularly chanting against his involvement, while opposition to the Glazer family remains strong.

However, Berrada has defended the club’s transfer business, insisting that the additions of Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, alongside Marcus Rashford’s return from his loan spell at Barcelona, have improved the squad.

He admitted that United could have signed another defender but explained that the club was unwilling to spend heavily on players they were not convinced would improve the team.

Meanwhile, new head coach Mauricio Pochettino has expressed his desire to have greater involvement in the club’s football decisions, particularly future squad planning and recruitment.

Pochettino confirmed that he would take responsibility for selecting the starting XI and making substitutions but added that he wanted to be involved in the major decisions concerning the squad.

The comments highlight the challenges facing United’s leadership as the club attempts to rebuild its fortunes while dealing with growing pressure from supporters.

The post Some criticism of Man Utd has crossed the line – CEO appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
The son of Nigerian journalist Kemi Olunloyo, Olukayode Taiwo, has been arrested in Connecticut, United States, over allegations involving a firearm in Pennsylvania.

Olunloyo confirmed that Taiwo is her son in a statement shared on Friday, saying, “My son Olukayode Joshua Taiwo has been found by the US law enforcement team who declared him wanted. Thank you for all your prayers and concern.”

Taiwo was arrested on Thursday night by the US Marshals and Newington police after a search operation at Millyard at Meadows Commons Apartments on Pane Road in Newington, according to FOX 61 on Friday.

The arrest prompted authorities to order nearby apartment residents to remain indoors during the operation.

According to the police report, the US Marshals “was conducting an investigation into Olukayode Joshua Taiwo, 26, of Philadelphia.”

It added that he “was wanted out of Pennsylvania for charges related to an incident involving a firearm”.

The US Marshals, assisted by Newington police, responded to the apartment complex on Thursday evening to search for him.

“A shelter in place warning was issued to apartment residents, and the public was asked to avoid the area,” the report stated.

Law enforcement officers eventually located Taiwo at a nearby business, where he was arrested. He was taken into custody without incident, according to police.

Newington police arrested him as a fugitive from justice and held him on a $1m bond.

“He is scheduled to appear in court on Friday,” the report added.

It was not immediately clear when Taiwo would be returned to Pennsylvania to face the outstanding charges.

PUNCH had earlier reported that Philadelphia police were searching for him over the alleged abduction of a 23-year-old woman at gunpoint on November 2.

Investigators said he was also suspected of shooting at the same woman near her home on November 15.

title: US inmate takes over an hour to die by lethal injection
description:
A convicted murderer moaned and complained of excruciating pain as he was put to death by lethal injection in Texas in an execution that took more than an hour, witnesses said.
Reinaldo Dennes, 70, was executed at a state prison in Huntsville on Thursday evening for the 1996 murder of a diamond deal
content:
A convicted murderer moaned and complained of excruciating pain as he was put to death by lethal injection in Texas in an execution that took more than an hour, witnesses said.

Reinaldo Dennes, 70, was executed at a state prison in Huntsville on Thursday evening for the 1996 murder of a diamond dealer during a robbery.

Dennes was killed by the same drug — pentobarbital — that was used in the failed execution in Tennessee of another condemned murderer, Christa Pike, in September.

Pike survived the attempted execution. She was hospitalized in critical condition but has since been returned to prison.

Jeff Hood, Dennes’s spiritual adviser, who was in the execution chamber as he was being put to death, described it as a “botched” execution that took more than an hour.

“His chest is coming up like this, and he says ‘It’s not working, it’s not working,'” Hood told KHOU11. “There’s no question that this was a botched execution.

“To be able to scream out and describe the pain that you’re feeling, that’s not supposed to happen,” he said.

Michael Graczyk, a reporter with the US news agency The Associated Press who attended the execution, also said it was unusual.

Graczyk said he has witnessed nearly 500 executions by lethal injection and Dennes’s was “dramatically different.”

Dennes “moaned of excruciating pain” as he was injected with the lethal drugs, he said.

Amanda Hernandez, spokeswoman for the Texas Department of Criminal Justice (TDCJ), said there was initially some difficulty finding suitable veins for the IV needles that delivered the lethal drugs but denied the execution was botched.

“TDCJ denies any claim of the execution being ‘botched,'” Hernandez said. “The agency followed all of its protocols and the execution was successfully carried out.

“IVs were inserted into the most viable veins available, in the left foot and left side of the neck,” she said. “Dennes made allegations of pain in locations where there were no IVs established and prior to any drugs being administered.”

There have been 39 executions in the United States this year, all by lethal injection.

Support for the death penalty among Americans has fallen to its lowest level in 55 years, according to a recent poll.

Forty-nine percent of US adults are in favour of the death penalty for convicted murderers and 45 per cent are opposed, the Gallup poll found.

content:
By Elizabeth Adegbesan

The Naira today appreciated to N1,472 per dollar from N1,468 per dollar in the parallel market on Thursday.

Similarly, the naira depreciated to N1,394 per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, NFEM.

Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, showed that the indicative exchange rate for the official market rose to N1,394 per dollar from N1388 per dollar on Thursday, indicating N6 depreciation for the naira.

Consequently, the margin between the parallel and official markets narrowed to N78 per dollar from N80 per dollar on Thursday.

The value of interbank turnover in NFEM rose by 1.9 percent to $815.6 billion from $800.3 billion on Thursday.

title: Denmark expels Russian diplomat over attempt to kill Ukrainian rapper
description:
Denmark’s foreign minister on Friday said Moscow’s defence attache in Copenhagen would be expelled after Russia was suspected of being behind an attempted assassination of a Ukrainian rapper.



“We have just summoned the Russian ambassador to the ministry of foreign affairs and notified him of the
content:
Denmark’s foreign minister on Friday said Moscow’s defence attache in Copenhagen would be expelled after Russia was suspected of being behind an attempted assassination of a Ukrainian rapper.

“We have just summoned the Russian ambassador to the ministry of foreign affairs and notified him of the government’s decision to expel the Russian defence attache from Denmark” within seven days, Lars Lokke Rasmussen told a news conference.

“We are saying this very clearly: we have exposed you”, he said.

He also added Denmark was mulling suspending Schengen visas to Russians.

“We have launched work at the European level to further tighten the rules governing access of Russian nationals to Europe,” he said.

“We are now stepping up our efforts — towards a halt to all non-essential visas”.

“The strongest response Denmark can give is not to waver and to support Ukraine. And we fully intend to continue” supporting Ukraine, he said.

The announcements came after Danish intelligence said it suspected Russia of planning the assassination of a Ukrainian rapper during a concert in a Copenhagen suburb with the help of a Danish criminal gang.

Denmark’s public television DR identified the rapper as Kyivstoner, who holds both Ukrainian and American citizenship.

title: 2027 Election: ‘What President Tinubu is thinking about’
description:
…targets 18/18 victory for APC in Cross River



By Ike Uchechukwu – CALABAR



Minister of State for Industry, Sen. John Owan-Enoh, says President Bola Tinubu is focused on building a prosperous future for Nigerians rather than winning the next election.



Owan-Enoh stated this on Friday at Ikom T
content:
…targets 18/18 victory for APC in Cross River

By Ike Uchechukwu – CALABAR

Minister of State for Industry, Sen. John Owan-Enoh, says President Bola Tinubu is focused on building a prosperous future for Nigerians rather than winning the next election.

Owan-Enoh stated this on Friday at Ikom Township Stadium during the inauguration of the Cross River chapter of Project Beyond’s executive and polling unit structures for the Central and Northern Senatorial Districts of the state.

He described Tinubu as a pragmatic leader whose decisions were driven by long-term national development rather than immediate political considerations.

The minister likened Tinubu’s leadership approach to that of Singapore’s founding Prime Minister, Lee Kuan Yew, whom he credited with transforming the Asian country into a global success story.

“That Prime Minister didn’t look at politics the same way a politician looks at the next election. That Prime Minister looked at the next generation.

“That is what President Bola Tinubu is doing,” he said.

Owan-Enoh acknowledged that the President’s economic reforms had subjected many Nigerians to hardship but described the situation as temporary sacrifices necessary for economic recovery.

He likened the reforms to bitter medicine that would eventually restore the country’s economic health.

“That tablet is bitter. But after that bitterness, you’ll get well,” he said.

According to him, Nigeria has begun experiencing economic recovery and stability after three and a half years of the administration’s policies.

He said the administration’s next priority was to translate the gains into prosperity and improved purchasing power for Nigerians.

“Three and a half years later, recovery has started. Stability has set in, and I think for President Tinubu, the next concentration is prosperity.

“The next concentration is the power of your pocket,” he said.

The minister further said inflation had declined to about 14 per cent and expressed optimism that it would continue falling towards single digits.

He urged Cross River residents to support Tinubu’s re-election, saying the state needed to remain influential in national decision-making.

“You will need to sit at the table when decisions are taken for you to be able to put before that table what you want,” he said.

Owan-Enoh said securing the state’s political relevance required a strong electoral showing for the APC in 2027.

He recalled that Tinubu won seven of Cross River’s 18 local government areas in the 2023 presidential election.

He, however, challenged party members to work towards securing victory in all 18 local government areas in the Jan. 16, 2027 election.

“In 2023, out of 18 local governments, the President won seven.

“In 2027, we must leave here with a determination and a resolve that, come Jan. 16, 2027, Mr President is going to win 18 over 18 in Cross River, and that is possible,” he said

title: Infantino hails Delta’s investment in Warri stadium
description: ‎FIFA President, Gianni Infantino, on Friday applauded the Delta State Government’s investment in the remodelling of the Warri City Stadium, describing the transformation as a significant commitment to football development, just as he expressed optimism about the facility’s potential to host major f
content:
‎FIFA President, Gianni Infantino, on Friday applauded the Delta State Government’s investment in the remodelling of the Warri City Stadium, describing the transformation as a significant commitment to football development, just as he expressed optimism about the facility’s potential to host major football events.

‎Infantino, who spoke during an inspection visit to the remodelled stadium in Warri, where he was accompanied by FIFA Secretary-General, Mattias Grafström, commended Delta State Governor,  Sheriff Oborevwori, for the investment.

‎The FIFA President said he was delighted by the atmosphere and enthusiasm surrounding football in Delta State, noting that “Nigeria, particularly Delta, has a special place in the global football community because of its rich reservoir of talent and passion for the game”.

‎Infantino particularly praised the recent triumph of Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, describing the achievement as a source of pride not only for Nigeria but also for Africa and the global football community.

‎The FIFA chief described the investment in the Warri City Stadium as fantastic, noting that modern sporting infrastructure was essential to nurturing talent, expanding participation and creating opportunities for future generations of footballers.

‎Expressing his personal excitement about the facility, Infantino said he looked forward to returning to the stadium to play football once the remaining work had been completed.

‎He also paid tribute to Nigeria’s rich football heritage, acknowledging the contribution of Nigerian football legends and players to the global game. He observed that some of the world’s finest footballers have emerged from Nigeria, including Delta State, underscoring the state’s importance to the country’s football history.

‎”I feel so much the love of Africa, the love of Nigeria. I am very happy to be here. You can always count on FIFA. We are not just your partners; we are your family members,” he said.

‎ Oborevwori, in his remarks, expressed delight at hosting the FIFA President and Secretary-General, describing their visit as a significant endorsement of the state’s investment in sports infrastructure.

‎He also expressed appreciation to Warri’s football enthusiasts and assured them of exciting future developments for the city.

‎Earlier, Infantino had inaugurated the Hussey College Sports Complex in Warri, a facility donated by the Brownhill Foundation, with support from the Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board (NCDMB), as part of efforts to promote grassroots sports development and nurture emerging talents in Delta State.

‎Welcoming the FIFA President, Governor Oborevwori and other distinguished guests, former Nigeria Football Federation President, Amaju Melvin Pinnick, described Infantino as one of the most loved FIFA presidents, citing his passion for sports development, education and grassroots football.

‎The ceremony attracted an array of dignitaries, including the Olu of Warri, Ogiame Atuwatse III; the Orosuen of Okere-Urhobo Kingdom, Owhotemu II; the Ovie of Agbarha-Warri Kingdom, Kingsley Emakpo Orereh (Igbi II); Morris Ogheneochuko; top government officials, as well as old students of the college.

The post Infantino hails Delta’s investment in Warri stadium appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Four dead, 24 rescued in Bayelsa boat accident – Police
description:
The Bayelsa State Police Command has confirmed the recovery of four bodies and the rescue of 24 survivors following a boat mishap at the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state.
The incident occurred at about 11am on Friday when a
content:
The Bayelsa State Police Command has confirmed the recovery of four bodies and the rescue of 24 survivors following a boat mishap at the river junction between Oweikorogha and Otuan communities in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state.

The incident occurred at about 11am on Friday when a passenger boat conveying mourners from Ayama to Ukubie Community for a burial ceremony reportedly developed a mechanical fault and capsized.

The police said the recovered bodies comprised two adults and two children, while the injured survivors were taken to medical facilities for treatment.

In a statement issued on Friday, the state Police Public Relations Officer, Musa Mohammed, said 19 of the rescued passengers were taken to Ayama Clinic, while five others who sustained varying degrees of injuries were conveyed to Family Care Hospital, Yenagoa.

He said, “So far, four bodies, comprising two adults and two children, have been recovered and deposited at the Federal Medical Centre (FMC) Mortuary, Yenagoa.”

Mohammed added that other passengers rescued from the incident had reportedly returned to their respective communities.

According to the police, preliminary investigations indicated that the boat developed a mechanical problem while navigating the waterways.

Some passengers reportedly urged the operator to steer towards the riverbank after the mechanical problem developed, but he allegedly declined and continued sailing before the boat eventually capsized.

“The circumstances surrounding the incident are being investigated,” the police spokesman said.

He said the Commissioner of Police, Ajao Adewale, immediately directed the State Marine Police Section to proceed to the scene and reinforce the ongoing search and rescue operation.

The Divisional Police Officer, Oporoma Division, was also coordinating efforts with local divers and other emergency responders to ensure that everyone involved in the incident was accounted for.

The police disclosed that the boat operator, identified simply as Omovie, had reportedly fled the scene, while the boat manager, identified as MV Bina, had been taken into custody for investigation.

The police said the investigation would establish the circumstances surrounding the tragedy and determine possible liabilities.

The Commissioner of Police expressed condolences to Governor Douye Diri and the families of those who lost their loved ones, while wishing the injured survivors a speedy recovery.

The command also warned boat operators against violating maritime safety regulations, particularly overloading and failure to provide life jackets.

It urged passengers to insist on the availability and proper use of life jackets before embarking on water transportation.

Earlier reports from the affected communities had suggested that more than 30 persons were feared dead, with hundreds reportedly missing, although the figures could not be independently established.

A community source, who reportedly witnessed the loading of the boat at the jetty, said passengers had raised concerns about the large number of people on board.

The source said some passengers allegedly suggested that the boat should stop at Oweikorogha to reduce the number of people on board because of the overcrowding.

However, the suggestion was reportedly ignored, and the boat continued its journey before capsizing shortly afterwards.

Former Chairman of the Maritime Union Workers in Bayelsa State, Mr Ipigansi Ogoniba, also confirmed receiving information about the incident but said he was yet to establish the actual number of casualties.

The police figures of four recovered bodies and 24 rescued survivors were the confirmed figures contained in the command’s Friday statement, as search and rescue operations continued.

The post Four dead, 24 rescued in Bayelsa boat accident – Police appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: EFCC arraigns man over ₦29.85m car sale fraud
description:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission has arraigned one Abdulkadir Ndaliman over an alleged N29.85 million fraud involving the sale of a Toyota Corolla LE 2014 model.
Ndaliman was arraigned on Thursday, November 19, 2026, before Justice Chinyere E. Nwecheonwu of the Federal High Court sitting
content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission has arraigned one Abdulkadir Ndaliman over an alleged N29.85 million fraud involving the sale of a Toyota Corolla LE 2014 model.

Ndaliman was arraigned on Thursday, November 19, 2026, before Justice Chinyere E. Nwecheonwu of the Federal High Court sitting in Kuje, Abuja, by the EFCC’s Abuja Zonal Directorate.

He faces a two-count charge bordering on obtaining by false pretence and alleged dishonest conversion of funds entrusted to him by Major General Dagana Allu.

According to EFCC’s post on X on Friday, the first count, the defendant allegedly converted N12.6 million realised from the sale of the vehicle in May 2026 to his personal use.

The charge reads, “That you, Abdulkadir Ndaliman, sometimes in May 2026 at Abuja, within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court did dishonestly convert to your personal use the sum of N12,600,000.00 (Twelve Million, Six Hundred Thousand Naira) entrusted to you by Major General Dagana Allu being the proceeds realised from the sale of Toyota Corolla LE 2014 model.”

In the second count, he was accused of converting another N17.25 million from the same vehicle sale proceeds in July 2026.

The charge stated, “That you, Abdulkadir Ndaliman, sometimes in July 2026 at Abuja, within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court did dishonestly convert to your personal use the sum of N17,250,000.00 (Seventeen Million, Two Hundred and Fifty Thousand Naira) entrusted to you by Major General Dagana Allu being the proceeds realised from the sale of Toyota Corolla LE 2014 model.”

The alleged offences are said to be contrary to Section 311 of the Penal Code Act and punishable under Section 312 of the same Act.

Ndaliman, however, pleaded not guilty to the charges when they were read to him.

Following his plea, defence counsel, Muhammad Yakubu, applied for bail, urging the court to release his client pending the determination of the case.

Prosecution counsel, Fatima Ado, initially opposed the application, citing the gravity of the alleged offences and informing the court that the Commission was ready to commence trial.

In her ruling, Justice Nwecheonwu granted the defendant bail in the sum of N5 million with one surety in like sum.

The court directed that the surety must provide a verifiable residential address, a valid means of identification and evidence of a legitimate means of livelihood.

The matter was adjourned until February 1, 2027, for the commencement of trial.

The post EFCC arraigns man over ₦29.85m car sale fraud appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Kemi Olunloyo dismisses parenting criticism after son’s arrest

Nigerian journalist Kemi Olunloyo has defended her motherhood following the arrest of her son, Olukayode Joshua Taiwo, in the United States, saying she would not succumb to criticism over his upbringing.
Olunloyo stated this in a post shared on her social media page on Friday, in which she also conf
content:
Nigerian journalist Kemi Olunloyo has defended her motherhood following the arrest of her son, Olukayode Joshua Taiwo, in the United States, saying she would not succumb to criticism over his upbringing.

Olunloyo stated this in a post shared on her social media page on Friday, in which she also confirmed that her son had been found and thanked those who expressed concern and offered prayers.

“My son has been found,” she wrote.

“I will not succumb to negative comments mocking my motherhood without understanding the delinquency of fathers and toxic families,” she added.

The journalist said she single-handedly raised Taiwo in Canada and Nigeria without child support before sending him to Nigeria at the age of 18 to begin a new life.

She also cautioned against judging her personal life based on her journalism work, saying, “Do not associate my work in journalism investigating people or reporting entertainment news about celebrities with the journalist’s personal life.”

Olunloyo accused Taiwo’s father, Kehinde Taiwo, of taking his disability and COVID-19 benefits for years while they lived in Nigeria, alleging that he also collected tax refunds by including their son in his tax returns.

She further claimed that his father abandoned him when he was five years old, sending him to Nigeria in 2006.

Speaking about her son’s activities, Olunloyo said he worked with her on campaigns against gun violence and drug abuse in communities, schools and workplaces.

She added that he funded his Graphic Artist certificate with earnings from his music on Spotify and volunteered with the Toronto Police between 2007 and 2012.

The journalist said she would no longer provide updates on the case but planned to attend family therapy with her son.

“There will no longer be any updates on his case and plan to attend family therapy with him soon,” she said.

Taiwo, was arrested on Thursday night by the US Marshals and Newington police in Connecticut. He was wanted in Pennsylvania on charges related to an incident involving a firearm and was being held on a $1m bond as a fugitive from justice.

title: Stay at polling units to protect votes, Obi urges voters
description:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, has urged Nigerians to remain at polling units after voting to ensure their votes are counted and transmitted, declaring that nobody would be allowed to rig the 2027 general elections.
Obi said his supporters and other Nigeria
content:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, has urged Nigerians to remain at polling units after voting to ensure their votes are counted and transmitted, declaring that nobody would be allowed to rig the 2027 general elections.

Obi said his supporters and other Nigerians must take responsibility for protecting their votes by staying at polling units throughout the voting, counting and transmission processes.

He spoke on Friday at a town hall engagement organised by the NDC at the Main Bowl of the Archbishop C.J. Patterson Building, All Saints Cathedral, Onitsha, Anambra State, as part of his engagements ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Addressing supporters, the former Anambra State governor urged voters to make the election day a priority and prepare to spend the day at their polling units.

“Go out there on that day, sacrifice one day. Nigeria is asking for one thing. Sacrifice one day for Nigeria. That day of voting,” he said.

He advised voters to go to their polling units with food and other necessities, cast their ballots, and remain there until the votes were counted and transmitted.

“Carry your food. Carry everything. Go to a police station. Vote. Stay there. They count the votes. Transmit it,” Obi said.

He further urged voters not to leave their polling units after voting, describing them as agents responsible for protecting the electoral process.

“You are our agent. Don’t look at any party agent. You are the party agent. Everybody is a party agent,” he said.

Obi, who is seeking the presidency alongside his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, said the NDC was prepared for the election and would resist attempts to manipulate the outcome.

“We are prepared. Nobody will rig this election. Nobody will rig this election. We are prepared for it,” he declared.

The former governor also outlined his electricity target for the country if elected, promising that his administration would increase power generation, transmission and distribution to at least 10,000 megawatts.

“Today Nigeria only generates, transmits and distributes about 4,000 megawatts of electricity. Kwankwaso and I assure you that within our tenure, Nigeria will generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000 megawatts,” he said.

He cautioned against making promises that could not be fulfilled, adding, “Take note of everything I said here; we don’t want to make fake promises.”

title: Benue: Press Secretary tackles Agada, defends governor’s record
description:
APC leadership, insists governor has no rift with Akume
_____________________________________________________________________
From Scholastica Hir, Makurdi
The Chief Press Secretary to the Benue State Governor, Tersoo Kula, has strongly defended Governor Hyacinth Alia’s administration against critic
content:
APC leadership, insists governor has no rift with Akume

_____________________________________________________________________

From Scholastica Hir, Makurdi

The Chief Press Secretary to the Benue State Governor, Tersoo Kula, has strongly defended Governor Hyacinth Alia’s administration against criticisms by the erstwhile All Progressives Congress (APC) Chairman in the state, Mr Austin Agada, dismissing his allegations as laughable and disconnected from the realities of governance in Benue.

Kula, who spoke during an appearance on Arise News Television on Friday, was responding to various allegations and criticisms raised by Agada during an earlier interview on the same platform.

Responding to Agada’s position that Governor Alia had achieved nothing since assuming office in 2023, Kula said such a position showed that the former APC chairman was not on the ground and was therefore unaware of developments in the state, or lacked an understanding of development and of the challenges inherited by the present administration.

Kula disclosed that Governor Alia inherited local debts amounting to approximately N380 billion, alongside substantial outstanding obligations involving salaries, pensions and gratuities.

According to him, some categories of workers were owed between 10 and 20 months’ salaries, while employees of the Benue State University, now Rev. Fr. Moses Orshio Adasu University, Makurdi (MOAUM), had experienced salary delays of up to 18 months under the previous administration.

Kula further disclosed that the Alia administration had been able to repay approximately N100 billion of the inherited liabilities within three years, describing the feat as evidence of the governor’s commitment to restoring the state’s financial stability.

He said the situation had significantly improved, noting that retired civil servants now undergo approximately one month of documentation before commencing pension payments, describing these improvements as verifiable records of the administration’s efforts to address inherited liabilities and restore confidence in the public service.

Kula also highlighted the administration’s intervention in the welfare of staff of Benue State University, Makurdi, disclosing that Governor Alia had cleared the institution’s earned allowances, which had remained unpaid since 2018.

He said the development was another indication of the administration’s determination to address longstanding financial obligations and improve the welfare of workers in the state.

The governor’s spokesperson also highlighted the administration’s revenue performance, disclosing that Benue’s monthly Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) had increased to between N2.5 billion and N3.5 billion.

He contrasted the figure with the approximately N400 million to N600 million reportedly generated monthly under the immediate past administration. Kula said the improvement demonstrated the Alia administration’s efforts to strengthen the state’s revenue base, enhance fiscal capacity and reduce dependence on federal allocations, maintaining that the revenue figures were supported by official records.

On infrastructure, Kula said the Alia administration had made significant progress in reversing the deterioration of public infrastructure inherited in 2023, adding that approximately 500 kilometres of roads had been constructed across the state, while several roads in Makurdi were either completed or under construction.

He also cited the installation of streetlights and ongoing urban renewal projects as evidence of the administration’s determination to restore the outlook of the state capital, adding that the visible transformation of Makurdi and other parts of the state contradicted Agada’s claim that the government had recorded no achievements.

Addressing Agada’s allegation that Governor Alia imposed businessman Benjamin Omale as APC chairman in Benue without due process, Kula questioned the former chairman’s knowledge of the party’s current national activities, challenging Agada to disclose when he last attended a meeting of the party’s National Executive Committee (NEC), arguing that Omale’s participation in such meetings demonstrated his recognition within the national party structure.

Kula argued that the APC’s national leadership would not continue to recognise Omale’s participation if his emergence had not followed the required procedures.

He said Governor Alia was entitled to call on qualified individuals, irrespective of their professional backgrounds, to contribute to the development of the state.

Kula said Agada’s criticisms of Governor Alia were an attempt to divert attention from questions surrounding his own political record.

He described Governor Alia as an incorruptible leader who would not compromise his principles for political or financial interests.

He also rejected claims that Governor Alia was responsible for divisions within the APC and had deliberately alienated prominent political figures, including a former Minister of Justice, Chief Michael Aondoakaa, SAN, and a former governor, Samuel Ortom.

He challenged that both politicians had worked for Alia’s emergence as governor, recalling that Aondoakaa had challenged Alia’s election in court, while Ortom supported the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate, Titus Uba, against Alia during the 2023 governorship election.

On the alleged strained relationship between Governor Alia and the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator Dr George Akume, Kula insisted that there was no disagreement between the two leaders.

He described Akume as a respected political father, explaining that the governor had remained committed to carrying him along in the affairs of the party and government.

As evidence, Kula cited the inclusion of Akume in the APC campaign council, alongside several political associates of the SGF, describing the gesture as a demonstration of Alia’s commitment to inclusiveness and party unity.

He, however, expressed concern that some individuals identified with Akume’s political camp were making statements capable of creating unnecessary misunderstanding between the two leaders.

Kula maintained that Governor Alia remained focused on governance, reforms and the development of Benue State, insisting that his administration would not be distracted by what he described as politically motivated allegations.

title: CJN urges child-sensitive justice as AGF announces Child Rights Act amendment validation
description:
From Godwin Tsa, Abuja
The Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, has called on judicial officers and allied institutions to adopt a disciplined, coordinated and child-sensitive approach to cases involving minors.
Kekere-Ekun spoke on Friday in Abuja at the 2026 United Nations
content:
From Godwin Tsa, Abuja

The Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, has called on judicial officers and allied institutions to adopt a disciplined, coordinated and child-sensitive approach to cases involving minors.

Kekere-Ekun spoke on Friday in Abuja at the 2026 United Nations World Children’s Day conference at the Body of Benchers, Abuja. The theme was “My Day, My Rights: The Nigerian Child and the Justice System.”

The CJN, who was represented by Justice Jumai Sankey, urged the courts to close systemic gaps in handling cases of child neglect, abuse, trafficking and exploitation, stressing that the task is a collective responsibility.

She charged judges to exercise restraint and sensitivity, noting that children who enter the justice system “may be frightened, ashamed, hungry or vulnerable.” She also called for collaboration across institutions to protect minors, whether they appear as victims, witnesses, survivors or alleged offenders.

She further demanded inclusive access to justice, with fair and prompt remedies and tailored protections, including for children with disabilities and those from minority backgrounds.

“The existence of legislation, important as it is, does not by itself guarantee the protection of children,” the CJN said. “The real measure of our commitment lies in how effectively these rights are respected, protected and enforced in the daily lives of children.”

Acknowledging the Child Rights Act 2003 as the legal framework for child protection, she lamented that many children still suffer abuse, neglect, sexual exploitation, trafficking, child labour, early and forced marriage and abandonment.

Some, she said, are denied education and healthcare, while others face violence in the very environments where they should feel safest. She added that digital platforms have introduced new risks, including cyberbullying, online exploitation and exposure to harmful content.

She said children appearing in court “must be treated with dignity and understanding,” in proceedings that protect their privacy, encourage their participation and reflect their age and emotional circumstances.

For children in conflict with the law, she said the emphasis should, where appropriate, be on rehabilitation and reintegration rather than measures that permanently damage their prospects. She also urged judicial officers to deepen their understanding of child rights and child-sensitive adjudication.

The Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, announced that the Federal Ministry of Justice is coordinating a comprehensive review of the Child Rights Act 2003 to address emerging statutory gaps.

He said the process has produced a Draft Child Rights Act Amendment Bill, scheduled for stakeholder validation on November 24, 2026, ahead of its finalisation and enactment.

Fagbemi said the central challenge was “not the absence of laws, but the gap in their implementation.”

He disclosed that the Ministry supported the development of the Legal Aid Guidelines and the Prosecutors’ Guidelines for Handling Cases of Children in Contact with the Law, designed to guarantee quality legal representation and child-sensitive prosecution nationwide.

The AGF urged stakeholders to prioritise diversion, restorative justice and non-custodial measures where the law permits, insisting that justice for children in conflict with the law “must not be purely punitive.” He also called for updated legal safeguards against cyberbullying, digital exploitation and breaches of privacy.

Addressing delegates, he said: “Our outcomes must move beyond mere conference communiqués; they must drive measurable improvements in our courtrooms, policies and frontline services.” To the children present, he said: “Your voices matter, your rights are non-negotiable, and your dreams are valid.”

The First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, was represented by Dr Adedayo Benjamins-Laniyi, Director-General of the Maryam Babangida National Centre for Women Development. In her address, she said Nigeria took an important step by domesticating global child-rights principles through the Child Rights Act 2003.

She identified the plight of almajiri and out-of-school children, child labour and teenage pregnancy as persistent concerns, particularly because they deprive girls of education and protection. She urged the judiciary to ensure the Act is “upheld and strictly adhered to,” and called for protecting children from unregulated artificial intelligence technologies and social media addiction.

In her welcome address, the President of the Nigerian Association of Family Court Judicial Officers, Magistrates and Other Practitioners (NAFCJOMP), Justice Eberechi Nyesom-Wike, said the event was the association’s inaugural conference.

She is the wife of the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory.

She said NAFCJOMP was registered with the Corporate Affairs Commission in January 2026 after the CJN approved its formation. She thanked the CJN, saying that without that approval the association “would still have remained a dream.”

The association, she explained, brings together superior court judges, magistrates, directors of public prosecutions, social welfare officers, advocates, law enforcement personnel and other child-protection practitioners from the 36 states and the FCT. It also runs a referral system for counselling, legal aid and medical support.

She traced its origin to a 2017 national conference of family court judges and magistrates, organised by UNICEF and the Lagos State Judiciary.

At that conference, Justice Yetunde Idowu, then head of the Family Court division in Lagos, was elected president. Justice Nyesom-Wike was elected vice president. Justice Idowu has since died, and the gathering rose in tribute to her.

Justice Nyesom-Wike said the association intends to make the World Children’s Day conference an annual event.

title: Boat conveying mourners capsizes in Bayelsa, many feared missing
description:
What was meant to be a gathering of family members, friends and sympathisers to bid a loved one farewell has turned into a tragedy in Bayelsa State, following the capsizing of a passenger boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area.
The boat, popularly known a
content:
What was meant to be a gathering of family members, friends and sympathisers to bid a loved one farewell has turned into a tragedy in Bayelsa State, following the capsizing of a passenger boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area.

The boat, popularly known as a “Love Boat”, reportedly sank near Oweikorogha Community on Friday while conveying passengers to Ukubie Community for the burial ceremony.

More than 30 persons were feared dead, while about 300 others were reportedly missing, according to a community source who witnessed the loading of passengers at the departure jetty.

The incident has plunged families and residents of the affected communities into anxiety, with relatives waiting for information about the whereabouts of their loved ones.

The community source said the vessel was carrying a large number of passengers when it left the jetty and capsized shortly after passing Oweikorogha Community.

He disclosed that some passengers had reportedly expressed concern over the number of people aboard the vessel and suggested that it should stop at Oweikorogha to reduce the passenger load.

But the suggestion was allegedly not taken, and the boat continued its journey before the tragedy occurred.

The source said local divers, volunteers and other public-spirited individuals had joined efforts to search for survivors and recover missing passengers.

The scale of the reported casualties has also raised concerns about the challenges of emergency response in the riverine communities, where access to affected locations can be difficult and rescue operations depend heavily on available boats, divers and local volunteers.

For residents of Southern Ijaw, waterways are essential transportation routes connecting communities separated by rivers and creeks.

Consequently, boats are routinely used to transport residents attending burials, weddings, religious activities, political gatherings and other social events.

Burial ceremonies in Ijaw communities often attract relatives and sympathisers from different settlements, increasing the demand for water transportation.

The latest incident has therefore renewed concerns about the safety of passengers travelling on commercial and privately operated boats, particularly when large numbers of people are travelling for communal events.

Former Chairman of the Maritime Union Workers in Bayelsa State, Mr Ipigansi Ogoniba, confirmed receiving information about the accident but said he was yet to ascertain the actual number of casualties.

The Police Public Relations Officer in the state, DSP Musa Mohammed, also confirmed the incident, saying the Commissioner of Police had directed the Marine Police Unit and the Divisional Police Officer covering the area under Oporoma Division to join the rescue operation.

“The incident actually happened. The Commissioner of Police has detailed the Marine Police Unit as well as the Divisional Police Officer covering that area, in Oporoma Division, so they are on ground for the rescue operations,” he said.

On the reported figures of 30 deaths and 300 missing persons, Mohammed said he was still making efforts to establish the actual number of casualties.

As families continue to await information, the tragedy has raised fresh questions about passenger safety, the enforcement of boat capacity limits and the availability of life-saving equipment on vessels operating across Bayelsa waterways.

The actual number of passengers aboard the boat, the number rescued and the confirmed casualty figures were yet to be established as of the time of filing this report.

The post Boat conveying mourners capsizes in Bayelsa, many feared missing appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
