Former Labour Party presidential candidate Peter Obi on Friday received a rousing welcome from supporters in Onitsha, Anambra State, ahead of a political event scheduled for the commercial city.
The reception, which attracted a large crowd of supporters, brought parts of Oni
content:
From Adesuwa Tsan, Abuja

Former Labour Party presidential candidate Peter Obi on Friday received a rousing welcome from supporters in Onitsha, Anambra State, ahead of a political event scheduled for the commercial city.

The reception, which attracted a large crowd of supporters, brought parts of Onitsha to a standstill as residents and party loyalists turned out to welcome Obi on his homecoming visit.

A statement signed by the spokesperson of the Nigeria Democratic Congress National Campaign Council (NDC-NCC), Dr Constance Ikokwu, on Friday described the reception as a demonstration of the growing support for Obi and the party.

The council said the crowd comprised youths, women and elderly supporters, whose presence reflected what it described as the people’s faith in Obi’s political vision.

“This was not just a political gathering; it was a profound family reunion,” the statement said, adding that the reception underscored the bond between Obi and the people of Anambra.

It further described the turnout as evidence that the NDC’s ambition to rescue and rebuild the country was gaining momentum.

“We are profoundly humbled by this breathtaking reception. To the incredible people of Onitsha and across Anambra, thank you for standing tall, for believing, and for showing the world what hope looks like,” the council said.

The council urged supporters to stay tuned for further developments, adding that the reception marked the beginning of what it called a march towards a new dawn.

Obi, a former governor of Anambra State, is expected to attend an event in Onitsha later on Friday.

title: European leaders pledge €90bn support for Ukraine, tougher sanctions on Russia
description:
European leaders have pledged €90bn in military and financial assistance to Ukraine by the end of 2027 and vowed to impose tougher sanctions on Russia, including measures targeting its oil and gas revenues, cryptocurrency transactions and illicit financial flows.
The commitments were contained in a
content:
European leaders have pledged €90bn in military and financial assistance to Ukraine by the end of 2027 and vowed to impose tougher sanctions on Russia, including measures targeting its oil and gas revenues, cryptocurrency transactions and illicit financial flows.

The commitments were contained in a joint statement issued on Friday by the German Embassy in Nigeria, following a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing, Ukraine and the United States in Berlin.

The leaders of Germany, France, the United Kingdom and Ukraine reaffirmed their determination to sustain support for Kyiv and increase economic pressure on Moscow over its ongoing war against Ukraine.

They said the €90bn support package under the European Union’s Ukraine Support Loan would cover Ukraine’s financial needs well into 2027, providing both military and financial assistance.

The statement also reaffirmed NATO allies’ commitment to provide €70bn in military equipment, assistance and training to Ukraine in 2026, with at least equivalent levels of support planned for 2027.

The statement said they reaffirmed, “their commitment to fulfil in its entirety the pledge made by NATO Allies to provide 70 billion Euro in military equipment, assistance
and training for Ukraine in 2026 and at least equivalent levels in 2027.

“Under the European Union’s Ukraine Support Loan, 90 billion Euros will be
provided for military and financial assistance by the end of 2027, covering
Ukraine’s financial needs well into 2027”.

The leaders declared that Russia would not be able to outlast the coalition’s commitment to Ukraine, stressing that its resilience would be matched by sustained international assistance.

“Russia will not be able to outlast the steadfast support of the Coalition’s members and Ukraine’s resilience,” the statement said.

On economic measures, the leaders pledged to intensify sanctions and introduce broader measures to restrict Moscow’s ability to finance its military campaign.

They specifically agreed to pursue additional measures targeting Russian oil and gas revenues, cryptocurrency transactions and illicit financial flows, while disrupting the country’s military-industrial complex.

The coalition also pledged to strengthen efforts to obstruct Russia’s shadow fleet, which it said enables Moscow to circumvent existing sanctions.

The statement added that the leaders would work to safeguard maritime security by enforcing applicable international rules and standards established through the International Maritime Organization.

The renewed pressure on Russia comes amid growing concerns over its attacks on Ukrainian civilians and critical infrastructure.

The leaders condemned what they described as Russia’s systematic escalation of deliberate and indiscriminate missile and drone attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure.

They expressed condolences to families of victims and reiterated Ukraine’s right to defend itself against what they called Russia’s war of aggression.

The statement also argued that Moscow was paying an increasingly unsustainable price for the conflict, despite its continued attacks.

“Despite suffering record losses, Russia has made only minimal territorial gains this year and has failed to take a single strategically important town or city,” the leaders said.

They added that Russia’s escalating attacks on Ukrainian civilians could not compensate for its failures on the battlefield.

The leaders further condemned alleged Russian hybrid attacks in Europe, including sabotage, information operations and cyber-attacks, which they said were intended to weaken international support for Ukraine.

They insisted that such intimidation would not deter their commitment but instead strengthen their resolve to reinforce the defence of Ukraine, Europe and NATO.

On military assistance, the coalition identified strengthening Ukraine’s air defence capabilities, particularly systems capable of intercepting ballistic missiles, as a priority.

Ahead of winter, the leaders pledged to work with third countries to provide additional missile defence capabilities to protect civilians and critical infrastructure.

Beyond financial and military assistance, the statement outlined plans for legally binding security guarantees for Ukraine once a ceasefire takes effect.

The proposed guarantees, to be defensive in nature and closely coordinated with the United States, could include sustained military, financial and technical support to maintain Ukraine’s armed forces.

They could also involve Ukraine’s participation in a proposed US-led ceasefire monitoring and verification mechanism, alongside a European-led Multinational Force for Ukraine, supported by Washington.

The force would provide reassurance measures in the air, at sea and on land, while helping to rebuild Ukraine’s military capabilities.

The leaders also proposed a legally binding commitment, subject to national procedures, to take measures to restore peace and security if Russia launches another armed attack against Ukraine.

On diplomatic efforts to end the war, the coalition reaffirmed its commitment to a comprehensive, just and lasting peace, building on ongoing US diplomatic initiatives.

It commended Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s continued willingness to accept an immediate ceasefire and engage in meaningful negotiations.

The leaders also supported direct dialogue between Ukraine and Russia, with the participation of the United States and European countries.

They insisted that any peace agreement must respect Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, maintaining that international borders must not be altered through force.

“Ukraine’s sovereign right to choose its own security arrangements and alliances must be fully respected,” the statement said.

The leaders further maintained that Russia’s sovereign assets would remain frozen until Moscow ended its war of aggression and compensated Ukraine for the damage caused by the conflict.

They warned that negotiations on broader European security arrangements could not proceed while Russia continued its military aggression and violated international agreements, including the United Nations Charter, the Helsinki Final Act and the Paris Charter.

The statement also stressed that any negotiations involving the European Union and NATO would require the consent of their respective member states and allies.

As an immediate step towards ending hostilities, the leaders called on Russia to accept an energy ceasefire throughout the winter.

They also demanded a ceasefire arrangement in the Black Sea to guarantee safe passage and freedom of navigation, particularly to sustain food exports and protect global food security.

title: Police Recover Bodies Of Two Abducted Victims In Edo
description: The Edo State Police Command has recovered the bodies of two people abducted during a violent invasion of Utekun Community in Ovia North-East Local Government Area of the state.The victims, identified as Arebamen Osaighale Promise and Akugbe Sunday, were allegedly abducted on October 28, 2026.In a s
content:
The Edo State Police Command has recovered the bodies of two people abducted during a violent invasion of Utekun Community in Ovia North-East Local Government Area of the state.

The victims, identified as Arebamen Osaighale Promise and Akugbe Sunday, were allegedly abducted on October 28, 2026.

In a statement issued on Friday, the Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Eno Ikoedem, said preliminary investigations revealed that the prime suspect allegedly invaded the community with armed men and took the two victims to an unknown destination.

The statement disclosed that operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit (VCRU), acting on actionable intelligence, subsequently arrested six suspects in connection with the incident.

It added that investigations led to the discovery of the remains of Promise on October 29 in a shallow grave within the community.

The police said further investigations led to the recovery of the second victim, Sunday, in an unfinished building, with his hands and legs tied and his body lying in a pool of blood.

The remains of both victims have been evacuated and deposited in a morgue for preservation and autopsy, while investigations are ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the killings and apprehend other fleeing suspects.

The Commissioner of Police, Edo State Command, CP Patrick Daaor, condemned the incident and warned against the use of violence, intimidation, abduction and murder in resolving community leadership disputes.

He assured residents that the command would pursue everyone connected to the crime and ensure they face the full weight of the law.

The police commissioner also appealed to members of the public to remain calm and provide credible information that could assist ongoing investigations, reiterating the command’s commitment to protecting lives and property across the state.

title: ‘I find this disrespectful,’ Sola Allyson rebukes fan over comment
description:
Nigerian singer and songwriter, Sola Allyson, has rebuked a fan who told her that he loved her more than her husband, describing the comment as disrespectful and dishonourable.
The singer expressed her displeasure in a post on X on Friday while responding to a message from a fan identified as Anthon
content:
Nigerian singer and songwriter, Sola Allyson, has rebuked a fan who told her that he loved her more than her husband, describing the comment as disrespectful and dishonourable.

The singer expressed her displeasure in a post on X on Friday while responding to a message from a fan identified as Anthony with the X handle @omojay47).

The fan had praised Allyson for her music and described her as a blessing to his generation before making a remark comparing his affection for the singer with that of her husband.

“Your husband will think he loves you more than me.

“May the Lord continue to inspire you to create more inspiring songs for us. You are blessed and a blessing to my generation,” he wrote.

However, Allyson did not appear pleased with the comparison, telling the fan that although he might have intended to compliment her, his choice of words was inappropriate.

“Hmmm…

“I believe you wanted to sound very convincing and thought it would excite me but I find this a dishonourable, disrespectful thing to think, and then to say.

“It’s not an Omolúwabí thing to think or say. I do not ‘enjoy’ being ‘loved’ with these kind of words.

“Please don’t do it again. Thanks,” she replied.

The singer’s response made clear that she was uncomfortable with the suggestion that a fan’s affection for her could be compared with the love she receives from her husband.

Allyson, known for songs that draw on Yoruba language, culture and spirituality, has maintained a public connection with her audience through her music and social media presence.

title: Customs inaugurates jetty, rehabilitates 14 classrooms in Ogun
description: The Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Customs Service, Bashir Adeniyi, has reaffirmed the Service’s commitment to community development, historical preservation and improved public infrastructure, declaring that the success of the institution must be measured not only by its operational achievement
content:
The Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Customs Service, Bashir Adeniyi, has reaffirmed the Service’s commitment to community development, historical preservation and improved public infrastructure, declaring that the success of the institution must be measured not only by its operational achievements but also by its positive impact on the lives of Nigerians.

Adeniyi stated this on Friday during the inauguration of a newly constructed jetty, the renovation of what the Service described as Nigeria’s first Customs office, and the rehabilitation of 14 classrooms, among other Corporate Social Responsibility projects executed by the Ogun I Area Command under the Customs Cares Initiative in Ijofin, Ipokia Local Government Area of Ogun State.

The projects, according to the Customs boss, reflect the Service’s determination to extend its developmental responsibilities beyond revenue generation, trade facilitation and border security to addressing the social and economic needs of communities within its operational environment.

He said the interventions were informed by the understanding that effective border management must go hand in hand with constructive engagement, mutual understanding and a genuine commitment to the welfare of host communities.

Adeniyi said, “The Nigeria Customs Service occupies a strategic position in Nigeria’s economic and national security architecture. Our responsibilities of revenue generation, trade facilitation and border security remain central to national development.

“However, we recognise that the effectiveness and sustainability of these responsibilities are closely connected to the relationships we maintain with communities around our operational environments.

“Our borders are not merely geographical boundaries. They are also spaces where our people live, conduct their businesses, raise their families and pursue their aspirations. Consequently, effective border management must be accompanied by constructive engagement, mutual understanding and a genuine commitment to the welfare of host communities.”

The Comptroller-General said the Customs Cares Initiative was designed to strengthen the Service’s relationship with host communities through practical interventions in education, healthcare, social investment, food security and the creative economy.

He noted that the initiative complements President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda by translating the administration’s development aspirations into tangible projects that directly affect people’s lives.

“Through the vision of our administration, we are expanding the scope of our engagements beyond conventional customs operations to include practical interventions that address community needs and contribute to sustainable development. This is also what President Bola Ahmed Tinubu stands for through his Renewed Hope Agenda.

“Our Customs Cares Initiative, which complements the Renewed Hope Agenda, reflects this commitment through interventions spanning education, healthcare, social investment, food security and the creative economy,” he said.

Adeniyi described the newly constructed jetty as a significant intervention for the benefiting communities, particularly given the importance of waterways to transportation and commercial activities in the area.

He explained that the facility was expected to improve connectivity, facilitate the movement of people and goods, enhance access to water transportation and create opportunities for greater economic integration.

The Customs CG, however, stressed that the long-term benefits of the facility would depend on the commitment of the community and relevant stakeholders to its proper maintenance and utilisation.

On the renovation of the historic Customs office, Adeniyi described the project as more than the restoration of an old building, saying it represented an important effort to preserve the institutional heritage and identity of the Nigeria Customs Service.

According to him, the historic facility provides a link between the Service’s past and present, highlighting the longstanding presence of customs administration in the community and its relationship with the development of government administration and international commerce.

On the educational component of the CSR intervention, the Comptroller-General said the renovation of Ijuvi Junior High School underscored the Service’s recognition of education as a critical driver of sustainable economic development and national transformation.

In his remarks, the Acting Comptroller, Federal Operations Unit, Zone A, Ikeja, DC O. Afeni, urged beneficiaries of the projects to use the facilities judiciously.

Afeni, who lauded the efforts of the Comptroller-General towards the completion of the projects, called on the students to take their studies seriously and be worthy ambassadors of their community.

Also, Chief Wasiu Olaniyan, speaking on behalf of the traditional rulers in attendance, reiterated the traditional rulers’ commitment to ensuring the proper maintenance of the facilities.

title: Tinubu hails Jibrin’s economic diversification blueprint, says 572-page book enriches national discourse
description:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja
President Bola Tinubu has praised Abdulmumin Jibrin, a member of the House of Representatives, for his contribution to Nigeria’s economic policy discourse. Tinubu described Jibrin’s research on economic diversification and structural transformation as a valuable ad
content:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has praised Abdulmumin Jibrin, a member of the House of Representatives, for his contribution to Nigeria’s economic policy discourse. Tinubu described Jibrin’s research on economic diversification and structural transformation as a valuable addition to national knowledge.

Tinubu said Jibrin’s 572-page book, Economic Diversification and Structural Transformation in Nigeria: The Past, The Present, The Future, offered important insights into the country’s economic evolution and ongoing efforts to broaden its economic base.

The President gave the commendation on Thursday when he received the lawmaker at his residence in the State House, Abuja. Jibrin represents the Kiru/Bebeji Federal Constituency of Kano State.

Jibrin visited Tinubu to present copies of the book, which was officially launched on Tuesday at the State House Conference Centre.

According to a statement by the President’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, Tinubu commended the depth of research behind the publication. He noted that it documented Nigeria’s past attempts at economic diversification and the present administration’s efforts towards structural transformation.

The President also observed that Jibrin’s legislative experience, particularly in finance and appropriation, enriched the publication and strengthened its relevance to national economic conversations.

He said the book and the initiatives unveiled alongside it aligned with his administration’s commitment to documenting research-based knowledge for the benefit of Nigerians and the wider global community.

“These noble initiatives are in consonance with our commitment towards the documentation of researched knowledge for the benefit of citizens and humanity who seek to understand the nation’s continued effort at economic diversification,” Tinubu said.

He added that the initiatives were also consistent with his administration’s commitment to empowering citizens through access to relevant knowledge and skills for improved livelihoods and prosperity.

The book launch also featured the unveiling of Jibrin’s Global Centre for Policy Implementation and Sustainable Development and his foundation, marking his 50th birthday.

The Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, represented Tinubu at the launch.

Jibrin is currently Chairman of the House Committee on Housing and Habitat.

title: NFL legend Tom Brady in talks to buy Chelsea stake – Report
description:
Tom Brady is reportedly in talks to buy a stake in Premier League club Chelsea after the NFL legend recently sold his share in Birmingham City.
Brady’s decision to end his association with Championship leaders Birmingham was made with a view to his potential investment in Chelsea, according to a Gua
content:
Tom Brady is reportedly in talks to buy a stake in Premier League club Chelsea after the NFL legend recently sold his share in Birmingham City.

Brady’s decision to end his association with Championship leaders Birmingham was made with a view to his potential investment in Chelsea, according to a Guardian report on Friday.

The former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback is believed to be close to Behdad Eghbali, whose fund Clearlake Capital group owns 86.5 percent of the London club.

Chelsea, last crowned English champions in 2017, have so far declined to comment about Brady’s mooted interest.

Regarded as one of the NFL’s all-time greats after winning seven Super Bowl titles, Brady took a minority share in Birmingham in 2023 following a takeover by fellow American Tom Wagner’s Knighthead Capital.

The 49-year-old appeared in a television documentary about Birmingham, memorably meeting with then manager Wayne Rooney before admitting on camera that he was “a little worried about our head coach’s work ethic”.

Brady is also involved in the NFL’s Las Vegas Raiders as a minority shareholder and commentates on American football for the Fox network.

On the field, Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso said his side must deal with the absence of Joao Pedro as the Blues struggle for goals.

The injured Brazilian striker has not played since the 2-0 win over Everton on October 17 and will be unavailable again when Leeds visit Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

Pedro was a key part of Chelsea’s explosive attacking start to the campaign, scoring five times in seven games in all competitions.

Alonso’s men have netted only once in the Premier League from open play in the four games missed by Pedro, dropping to fifth place.

Having suffered two defeats in their last three games, Alonso said Chelsea’s other attacking stars, including Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers, Pedro Neto and Danny Welbeck, need to fill the void.

“It’s teamwork. For sure Joao is an important player but we need to deal with this time without him. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying,” Alonso told reporters on Friday.

“We need to deal with it. It’s not that I’m going to look for one explanation. I think that there are more explanations for one defeat than missing just one player.

“If we do more things right, we could compete better and win at Sunderland, but there are a few things that had to be done. We want Joao Pedro back but I don’t want to make a big thing out of that.”

AFP

title: Bayelsa: Hundreds of people feared missing in boat mishap
description:
From Femi Folaranmi, Yenagoa
Tragedy has struck in Bayelsa State as hundreds of people, including children, are feared missing after a makeshift boat carrying hundreds of people for a burial at Ukubie capsized between Oweirogha and Angiama communities, all in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area.
Acc
content:
From Femi Folaranmi, Yenagoa

Tragedy has struck in Bayelsa State as hundreds of people, including children, are feared missing after a makeshift boat carrying hundreds of people for a burial at Ukubie capsized between Oweirogha and Angiama communities, all in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area.

According to eyewitnesses, the boat, which was not a normal one, was built with planks in the form of a barge to accommodate more passengers.

Some of the passengers were said to have complained about the loud music from the DJ and the dancing by some of their fellow passengers, pleading that they should exercise caution as the boat was overloaded.

Investigations revealed that before the tragedy struck in Oweirogha waters, some passengers had suggested that the boat should stop at the Oweirogha jetty to offload some passengers.

It was gathered that the planks used to construct the boat broke and all the passengers fell into the water.

Those who could swim were able to reach the shore, while others who could not swim were seen in a viral video floating on the river, waiting for a rescue team.

“Unfortunately, that suggestion was not taken, and the tragedy occurred after the boat had passed Oweirogha community, heading to Ukubie,” a source said.

Another source said the number of those missing was over a hundred because the boat carried hundreds of passengers to the burial.

Mr Ipigansi Ogoniba, the State Chairman of the Maritime Union, who confirmed the incident, declined to comment on the number of casualties as it had not been ascertained.

“I cannot give the casualty figure right now. We have sent our team to the scene to conduct search and rescue of missing passengers,” he said.

The Bayelsa State Police Command also confirmed the incident and said it had dispatched a rescue team to the area.

The post Bayelsa: Hundreds of people feared missing in boat mishap appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Poland and allies say Russian missile a ‘provocation’ from Moscow
description:
Warsaw and its allies said Friday that a Russian missile landing in Poland was a “provocation” from Moscow as thousands of European troops were holding exercises nearby.



Poland said two Russian missiles hit its territory early on Friday, landing in southeastern Poland as drills were due to take p
content:
Warsaw and its allies said Friday that a Russian missile landing in Poland was a “provocation” from Moscow as thousands of European troops were holding exercises nearby.

Poland said two Russian missiles hit its territory early on Friday, landing in southeastern Poland as drills were due to take place.

Nobody was hurt, Poland said.

Authorities said one Kh-101 missile was confirmed to have landed in the eastern village of Nowy Lipowiec.

A second missile is suspected to have hit another location and a jet-powered drone a third.

The projectiles crossed into the NATO country as Russia pounded neighbouring Ukraine and thousands of European troops were holding unprecedented army drills in southeastern Poland.

Several European defence ministers were in Poland for the drills.

Prime Minister Donald Tusk said everything pointed to the fact that these were not accidental stray missiles.

“Three Russian objects violated Polish airspace. They fell on Polish land. One exploded. There is no destruction, no casualties,” he said, adding:

“This is not just my opinion but of our foreign partners and NATO: this does not look like a coincidence.”

He said he believed the incident was linked to the European drills.

“We are dealing with an intentional provocation,” he added.

He said the objects “fell close” to where “armies of the Coalition of the Willing” were training in Nowa Deba, southeastern Poland.

“Coalition of the Willing” refers to a group of Ukraine’s European backers who are prepared to send peacekeeping troops to the country.

Nowy Lipowiec, where the first missile fell, is a 1.5-hour drive from where the drills are taking place.

Just a day before the incident, US media outlet Fox News quoted Donald Trump as saying Russian leader Vladimir Putin “has been landing drones in Poland, and a couple of little missiles, by mistake”.

Tusk said on Friday that Poland would give the United States access to the missile debris.

“I don’t always agree with the interpretation of the US side on these incidents. We are cooperating with the Americans. They have access to the places, to the debris of the objects.”

The Kremlin has not yet commented.

The missiles flew in as Russian strikes killed at least eight people in Ukraine, a day after Putin met with Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

‘Putin seeks confrontation’

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the “incursion into Polish airspace is utterly unacceptable”, while the EU said it stood in “full solidarity” with the Poles.

Germany said the incident was “yet another example of Russia’s ongoing provocations” and that “rather than showing a willingness to negotiate, Putin… continues to seek confrontation”.

The French presidency called it a “serious incident”.

In Nowa Deba, European defence ministers condemned the incident as they watched several thousand troops hold the first exercise of a new multinational force in support of Kyiv.

“What has happened overnight is yet another example of Russian provocation designed to divide Europe,” the UK’s Wes Streeting said.

He added that: “The multinational force for Ukraine is ready to step forward when hostilities cease.”

French minister Catherine Vautrin expressed “solidarity” with Poland and saluted the drills, saying “nobody can break this determination of our unity.”

Tusk said NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte — who called the incident “clearly dangerous” — will be in Warsaw Saturday.

In Nowy Lipowiec, a local woman told Poland’s TVN broadcaster that her “whole house shook” at around 6:30 am (0530 GMT) when the missile hit.

Polish media quoted local official Andrzej Szarlip as saying that the missile fell “very close to buildings”, but that nobody was injured and “there was no material damage.”

A day earlier, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met allies in Berlin.

Poland is one of five countries Europe picked to represent it in future US-led talks on Ukraine.

Tusk said Friday’s incident showed “Poland needs to take part in the discussions of security in Ukraine and Europe, because we are most exposed to Russian aggression”.

Putin has called for a review of Europe’s security architecture and Moscow has recently refloated a 2021 demand that NATO pull back troops from Eastern Europe, including Poland.

In almost five years of Russia’s invasion, Poland — Ukraine’s western neighbour — has several times said stray projectiles have flown over or crashed on its territory.

Warsaw has been one of Ukraine’s main allies, becoming a transit route for the West to supply weapons to Ukraine and hosting more than a million Ukrainian refugees.

Vanguard News

title: Akpabio, Abbas, Matawalle pledge 20 million votes for Tinubu
description:
From Okwe Obi, Abuja
Ahead of the 2027 general polls, Senate President Godswill Akpabio; Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas; Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle; and National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Yilwadta Nantewa, have pledged to galvanise
content:
From Okwe Obi, Abuja

Ahead of the 2027 general polls, Senate President Godswill Akpabio; Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas; Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle; and National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Yilwadta Nantewa, have pledged to galvanise 20 million votes for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu through the Tinubu Again Movement (TAM).

They made the pledge at the unveiling of TAM in Abuja.

Akpabio noted that the achievements of President Tinubu were evident for naysayers to see and feel. He charged TAM ambassadors to ignore violence and to preach the good works of President Tinubu.

He said: “Now, all the stakeholders that are represented by the Director-General, I want you to know that you are only ambassadors of that. The country is gathered here today. Immediately after you step out of here, we are going to start the groundwork.

“We are going to be fishers of men and women. You are going to go from nook and cranny of our entire nation. Fish out the votes. You are already converted.

“So today, I want to ask that, why can’t you bring the 20 million votes? Twenty million votes are possible. They are possible. Once we are united as a group, this is what one man is able to do.

“The campaign is going down now. We are getting to the level where we are going to all the wards. Every support group will now have to move to the ward and unit.”

The Senate President claimed that money from subsidy and from other areas had been ploughed into meaningful projects.

“We used to have all sorts of exchange rates. Some people buy at 98 naira a dollar, go out there and sell at 300.

“The petrol price at 300 will go to the end user and sell at 650. And they will continue. They will go back to Sydney, make money, come back.

“At the end, people were buying plants without having a single stock. He stopped all that.

“For multiple exchange rates, he brought everything into one. And today, the tests are benefiting from the reform in the economic sector, in the financial sector,” he added.

The Speaker, Abbas, insisted that both appointed and elected members of the APC must inform the public of President Tinubu’s performance.

The lawmaker said: “It is the time that each and every one of us, most in our own little way, come out to support this government and to support this party.

“What Matawalle has done today is a typical example of a man who appreciates good leadership. It is not that he is the richest among the ministers. He is not the richest among the political appointees.

“He is not the richest among even members, elected members who are serving this government. But it is the will and determination and the passion to see that this government continue to succeed.”

The Minister of State for Defence added that the campaign flag-off was to energise “our executive from the national level down to the polling unit level for the task ahead as we approach 16th January 2027.

“The victory of TAM must double their effort and ensure that we deliver more than 20 million votes because we already projected 20 million votes, but we are determined to project more than that.

“The Tinubu Agenda Movement was conceived out of conviction of its founders and the supporters that the Renewed Hope Agenda of Mr President, Bola Tinubu, has made significant impact in various aspects, ranging from road and infrastructure, rail project, AKK gas project, student loan programme, agricultural support, empowerment programme and above all, the administration’s commitment to tackling insecurity and other economic problems across the country.”

title: EPL: Caicedo, Martinez fit for Chelsea’s Leeds clash
description:
Chelsea have received a timely fitness boost ahead of their Premier League clash against Leeds United, with Moises Caicedo and Emiliano Martinez both available for selection.
In his pre-match conference on Friday, Head coach Xabi Alonso confirmed that Caicedo is fit to start after having his minutes
content:
Chelsea have received a timely fitness boost ahead of their Premier League clash against Leeds United, with Moises Caicedo and Emiliano Martinez both available for selection.

In his pre-match conference on Friday, Head coach Xabi Alonso confirmed that Caicedo is fit to start after having his minutes carefully managed during Ecuador’s international fixtures.

The midfielder featured for his country during the break but was substituted at half-time in their most recent friendly.

Alonso said “Moises is ready to start. It was discussed after playing the first game he could save some minutes. That was good for him, and he’s fine.”

Martinez is also available after completing his international commitments with Argentina. Alonso explained that the decision to allow him more training time with his national team proved successful.

“He is in the squad and he is selectable,” the Chelsea boss confirmed.

Josh Acheampong is another positive addition, with Alonso giving the youngster the green light to return to action.

However, Chelsea will be without Joao Pedro, Maxence Lacroix and Jorrel Hato for Saturday’s encounter.

Pedro remains sidelined with a thigh problem, while Lacroix is recovering from a hamstring issue. Hato is also expected to spend more time out with a back problem.

Meanwhile, Reece James is making progress but still needs a few more weeks, while Jamie Gittens has returned to team training but will not yet be included in the matchday squad.

Chelsea will hope the availability of Caicedo, Martinez and Acheampong can help them return to winning ways against Leeds following their defeat to Sunderland.

title: Obi, Kwankwaso pledge 10,000MW power supply
description:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, has promised that a government led by him and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, would generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000MW of electricity.
Obi made the pledge on Friday at a town hall meeting in Onitsha, Anambr
content:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, has promised that a government led by him and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, would generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000MW of electricity.

Obi made the pledge on Friday at a town hall meeting in Onitsha, Anambra State, where he said the pair had assessed the country’s electricity challenges and were planning how to address them.

He said, “Today, Nigeria only generates, transmits and distributes about 4,000MW of electricity. Kwankwaso and I assure you that within our tenure, Nigeria will generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000MW.

“Take note of everything I said here, we don’t want to make fake promises. And we’re not going to go there and start telling you when we came in what we saw. We are seeing everything now, and we are planning for it.

“We’re not going to come in and tell you that, ‘oh, some people are still in charge.’ One person must be in charge.”

The pledge is one of the major promises being made by the Obi-Kwankwaso ticket ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election, in which they will face President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress and former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress, among other candidates.

Obi has repeatedly made the 10,000MW commitment during his campaign engagements.

In May, while accepting the NDC presidential ticket, he promised to achieve the target within four years if elected.

He repeated the pledge at a party town hall meeting in Enugu on October 29 and again in Lagos on November 12.

Data from the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission showed that grid-connected power plants generated an average of 4,022.40 megawatt-hours per hour in the second quarter of 2026.

The commission also reported that electricity distribution companies had metered 62 per cent of customers nationwide, while their average aggregate technical, commercial and collection losses stood at 36 per cent, against an allowed target of 16.92 per cent.

The Tinubu administration has also defended its record in the power sector, citing the Electricity Act 2023, investments in grid expansion and off-grid projects, and the Presidential Metering Initiative.

The Federal Ministry of Power said in July 2025 that installed generation capacity had increased from 13,000MW to 14,000MW under the administration, while peak generation had reached 5,801MW.

But the government has acknowledged continuing challenges. In September, Power Minister Joseph Tegbe said a review of the sector had identified constraints across gas supply, generation, transmission, distribution and market financing.

He also said electricity distribution companies’ commercial and collection losses and outstanding debts owed by government agencies were affecting the sector.

title: NEDC trains mechanics ahead of electric vehicle distribution in North-East
description:
The North-East Development Commission has begun training automobile technicians and other stakeholders on the use and maintenance of electric vehicles ahead of the planned distribution of 10,330 units across the region.
The training, held in Maiduguri, Borno State, brought together automobile techni
content:
The North-East Development Commission has begun training automobile technicians and other stakeholders on the use and maintenance of electric vehicles ahead of the planned distribution of 10,330 units across the region.

The training, held in Maiduguri, Borno State, brought together automobile technicians, members of road transport associations, police officers and officials of the Federal Road Safety Corps.

Speaking shortly after a stakeholders’ engagement and sensitisation workshop on electric vehicles on Friday, the consultant handling the programme, Umar Abatcha, said the NEDC planned to distribute 10,000 electric tricycles, 300 electric taxis and 30 electric buses to ease transportation difficulties in the region.

He said the workshop was organised to bring relevant stakeholders together and develop maintenance plans to protect the vehicles and ensure their durability.

“The workshop started in Taraba. It cuts across the six North-East states. The NEDC is planning to introduce 10,000 electric tricycles, 300 electric taxis, and 30 electric buses to cushion the hardship of transportation.

“This workshop is to unite all the stakeholders, to talk to them about the coming of the electric vehicles and how to protect and safeguard them for longer use. So, it is a combination of training and awareness programme,” he said.

Describing the vehicles as “cost-efficient and user-friendly,” Abatcha said they could cover up to 300 kilometres on a full charge.

“The e-vehicles are cost-efficient and user-friendly. This particular type is the first of its kind in the whole of the country. On one charge, the vehicles can travel 300 kilometres. They are not meant to travel long distances. The rural communities for now will only benefit from the tricycle,” he said.

Abatcha added that the commission would organise additional training for beneficiaries of the vehicles to equip them with the knowledge required for their long-term use and maintenance.

“They have been taught how to maintain the vehicles. This is not the only training we will be doing. NEDC will still organise another for the beneficiaries to enable them to understand how to use it in the long term,” he said.

Also speaking, the Secretary of the Road Transport Employers Association of Nigeria, Borno State chapter, Adamu Bulama, commended the initiative and pledged to extend the knowledge gained at the workshop to members of the association across the state.

“In our various meetings and for all our local governments and chapters, including the unit chairmen, the little experience we have here will also be passed down to others in the association,” he said.

Bulama said participants had also been briefed on how to operate the vehicles when they arrive, adding that beneficiaries would receive manuals to guide their use.

“We have been taught how we are going to use the e-vehicles when they arrive, and we are also made to understand that whoever is going to benefit from the vehicle, complete manuals will be given to them,” he said.NEDC trains mechanics ahead of electric vehicle distribution in North-East

content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA- THE President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio has urged support groups and members of the All Progressives Congress, APC, not to allow themselves to be provoked to carry out attacks or retaliate against members of the opposition as the party was better positioned to win in a free and fair election.

Senator Akpabio gave the charge in Abuja on Friday at the inauguration of “Tinubu Again Movement” a grassroots mobilization movement, convened by the Minister of State for Defence, Dr Bello Matawalle, aimed at securing more than 20 million votes for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in 2027.

In a statement signed by the Special Assistant on Media/Communication to the President of the Senate, Anietie Ekong, Akpabio urged the APC members and supporters not to be distracted by the antics of the opposition parties who aimed to attract sympathy by inciting violence in the run up to the election.

The President of the Senate said: “Please be careful. Don’t allow them to provoke you to violence. Because they know they are losing, they will sponsor some misguided youths to throw stones at you. If they throw stones at you, your target is to garner votes and defeat them.

“By January 16, 2027, they will know the difference between stones and votes. When you are certain of winning you don’t deploy stones and violence as your weapons but you persuade them with the monumental achievement of the APC administration.”

Akpabio charged the members of Tinubu Again Movement to carry the message of the Renewed Hope administration to their various polling units, wards and local government areas to sensitize the populace on the achievement of the administration of President Tinubu.

Akpabio who was the Chairman at the inauguration, reeled out some of the achievements of the administration to include, the Lagos – Calabar coastal highway, the Sokoto – Badagry highway, and other road infrastructure across the States.

He said the economy of the country had almost collapsed before the advent of rhe Tinubu administration and commended the administration for the courageous removal of fuel subsidy which he said had made more funds available to States and Local Governments to execute projects without resorting to borrowing.

According to him, the introduction of the Students Loan Fund had made it possible for indigent students to access education just as the tax reforms had recaliberated the economy, adding, “Today the States are benefitting from the economic reforms. Many Governors are executing projects without borrowing a dime because of the ingenuity of one man, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

“So when you go out there to talk about how President Tinubu must be returned to office with over 20 million votes, say it with boldness because this President had stabilized and grown the economy and the indices are there for all to see!”

Akpabio commended Dr Matawalle for the initiative in convening the Tinubu Again Movement and urged other political appointees to emulate him and in their own way mobilize the masses for the re-election of President Tinubu.

Over 1000 vehicles were commissioned to be distributed to National, Zonal and State coordinators of the Movement while grants and food items were also shared to households across the coutry.

The inauguration had in attendance the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Tajudeen Abbas, the National Chairman of the APC, Prof Nentawe Yilwatda, past and serving Senators, Ministers, Women Leaders and other stakeholders.

title: Three suspects arrested for luring rider with meal, stealing his tricycle in Borno
description:
The Borno State Police Command has arrested three suspects in connection with the alleged drugging of a tricycle rider and theft of his tricycle in Maiduguri, the state capital.
Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO) of the command, ASP Nahum Daso disclosed this in a statement issued on Friday.
Acco
content:
The Borno State Police Command has arrested three suspects in connection with the alleged drugging of a tricycle rider and theft of his tricycle in Maiduguri, the state capital.

Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO) of the command, ASP Nahum Daso disclosed this in a statement issued on Friday.

According to the police, at about 7:47 pm on November 13, one Mohammed Mohammed, a tricycle rider from Bolori II Ward, Maiduguri, picked up an unidentified male passenger.

The passenger subsequently invited him to join him for a meal at his residence at Moduganari New City area of Maiduguri, where one of his friends was also present.

Unknown to the unsuspecting rider, the suspects allegedly laced his food with a drug substance.

Shortly after consuming the meal, he became unconscious, and they stole his tricycle.

The command spokesman disclosed that upon receipt of the report, operatives of the command’s State Intelligence Department and Violent Crime Response Unit (Crack) swung into action and arrested the suspects.

During preliminary investigation, the suspects confessed that they intentionally laced the food, stole the tricycle and sold it to one Umar Abubakar aka Sanda.

Daso said the stolen tricycle has been successfully recovered, while all three suspects have been charged to court for prosecution.

The Borno State Police Command said it remains resolute in its commitment to protecting lives and property and ensuring that perpetrators of criminal activities are brought to justice.

Members of the public were urged to remain vigilant, avoid receiving edibles from strangers and promptly report suspicious activities to the nearest police station.

title: Osun CSOs demand law against indecent dressing
description:
Two Osun State-based civil society organisations, Dialogue 365 and Nigerians for Good Governance, have demanded laws stipulating minimum dress standards, especially for women in public places across the state.
They said the demand was prompted by the growing trend of scantily dressed women walking o
content:
Two Osun State-based civil society organisations, Dialogue 365 and Nigerians for Good Governance, have demanded laws stipulating minimum dress standards, especially for women in public places across the state.

They said the demand was prompted by the growing trend of scantily dressed women walking on streets and major roads in the state.

In a statement jointly signed by the conveners of the two groups, Waheed Saka and Wole Oladapo, respectively, and obtained in Osogbo on Friday, they argued that many young women were often found on streets and in public places without proper clothing.

The groups acknowledged the right of individuals to dress as they wished, provided they did not infringe on the rights of others.

However, the CSOs argued that appearing in public places in revealing dresses could also infringe on the rights of people who did not subscribe to such a way of life.

“We have in recent months observed the growing trend of people, especially ladies, appearing on streets in Osogbo in particular without being properly dressed.

“Many of those doing it move around major roads in Osogbo, the state capital, without wearing underwear. This is alien to our culture as Omoluabi.

“People are displeased and we cannot pretend not to observe this trend. Those involved are almost no longer covering their nakedness. The sense of decency associated with us as Omoluabi appears to be disappearing fast.

“We understand that people have the right to appear the way it is comfortable for them. But when your appearance is offensive to other people, you are also infringing on their rights.

“Curiously, the disturbing development has found its way into secondary schools in the state, where many female pupils who are expected to appear decent in class by wearing proper underwear are often found doing the opposite, with the excuse that they are not comfortable wearing underwear. There must be action to deal with this situation,” the groups said.

The groups subsequently urged the Osun State House of Assembly to enact laws stipulating minimum dress standards for women appearing in public places.

“Hiding behind excuses of excessive heat may not be tenable. Government should protect this society before more damage is done.

“There should be a law that will state the minimum dressing for women and even men appearing in public.

“The idea of walking around streets without underwear should not be allowed to gain more followers in the state,” the statement further read.

Commenting on the demand by the CSOs, the member representing Obokun State Constituency in the Osun State House of Assembly, Adewumi Adeyemi, said the concerns expressed by the groups were genuine.

Adeyemi, however, said enacting a law to regulate how people dress might not be the solution, adding that enforcing such a law would be difficult.

“Coming up with a law to check that trend may be challenging. How do we enforce it? Such a law can only be enforced in tertiary institutions and secondary schools where dress codes can be introduced. If a school says you must appear in a certain way, if you are displeased, you can leave and move elsewhere.

“But how do we enforce such a law on the streets? Are we going to ask those involved to leave Osun or Orita Sabo or wherever they live and go elsewhere?

“The constitution allows you to appear the way you want. But if CSOs are really interested in helping us in curbing this trend, enlightenment is important, not necessarily the law,” Adeyemi said.

The lawmaker also challenged the CSOs to organise visits to schools in the state to engage pupils and educate them about what he described as the negative aspects of indecent dressing.

He also emphasised parental influence, saying those involved might even be copying the act from their parents.

“I am a teen teacher. Sometimes, we observe that some of the things these teenagers are doing, they learn from their parents.

“These CSOs should go out and educate teachers, parents and others about this menace. I believe gradually, things will change. I share the concerns expressed by the CSOs. Things are getting bad,” Adeyemi said.

title: South-East needs security, dialogue, economic growth — Kigali varsity don
description: The Deputy Vice-Chancellor for Research, Innovation and Enterprise at the University of Kigali, Rwanda, Professor Ogechi Adeola, has outlined a seven-point agenda for the renewal of the South-East, urging leaders and stakeholders to address insecurity, promote inclusive dialogue and turn the region’
content:
The Deputy Vice-Chancellor for Research, Innovation and Enterprise at the University of Kigali, Rwanda, Professor Ogechi Adeola, has outlined a seven-point agenda for the renewal of the South-East, urging leaders and stakeholders to address insecurity, promote inclusive dialogue and turn the region’s human and economic resources into measurable development.

Adeola said the resilience of the Igbo people should not be celebrated as a substitute for addressing the conditions that make survival difficult, including insecurity, disrupted livelihoods and inadequate systems.

“We can’t keep praising the Igbo man for surviving what a system should have prevented,” she said.

She presented the agenda in her keynote address titled, “The Southeast Paradox: Olaudah Equiano, Igbo Identity and the Choice Between Conflict and Conversation,” at the 2026 International Conference of the Forum of South-East Academic Doctors, themed “Nigeria’s Southeast at a Crossroads: Conflict or Conversation,” on Friday. 

The seven priorities she outlined include safety and the rule of law, inclusive dialogue, economic and infrastructure coordination, youth development and innovation, cultural and historical preservation, the application of indigenous knowledge, and accountability through measurable results.

On security, Adeola called for an environment where people could travel, trade, learn and express themselves without fear, intimidation or harassment. She also stressed that violence and abuses should be investigated lawfully.

She linked security to the possibility of meaningful dialogue, arguing that people cannot freely participate in conversations about the region’s future when they are afraid to speak.

“Can there be real dialogue where people still fear to speak?” she asked.

She called for conversations that include women, young people, victims, residents and other communities, insisting that participation must result in clear commitments and follow-through rather than remain a symbolic exercise.

On economic development, Adeola urged the five South-East states to coordinate their efforts, particularly in addressing challenges that cut across state boundaries. She called for connected markets and infrastructure, shared projects and joint ventures that could strengthen regional commerce.

“The economic and security problems cross borders. So there should be coordination,” she said.

The professor also identified skills development, research, innovation and enterprise as essential to creating opportunities for young people. She called for practical investment in youth development and the renewal of systems such as the Igba Boyi apprenticeship model to strengthen skills transfer and entrepreneurship.

On cultural preservation, she urged stakeholders to document Igbo history, the experiences of older generations, community achievements and living cultural practices to ensure they are preserved for future generations.

“If you don’t write your history, somebody else has a pen,” she said.

She also warned about the need to protect the Igbo language and strengthen its representation in digital technologies, including artificial intelligence.

“If we do not do something this generation, this beautiful language would die,” she said.

Adeola further urged researchers to look inward and incorporate indigenous knowledge into research and development, citing traditional agricultural practices and other local expertise as resources that should be documented and applied to contemporary challenges.

“Let our research be more impactful… look inward and see what you can do for your people,” she said.

The final priority, accountability, focuses on ensuring that development plans produce results that can be assessed. Adeola called for clear baselines on security, access to opportunities and commercial activities, as well as regular reporting to determine whether interventions were improving people’s lives.

She emphasised that the region needed to move from discussions to practical action, with responsibilities assigned and progress monitored.

“Conversation is necessary, but we shouldn’t just talk. We should demand safety… inclusion… accountability,” she said.

Among the early steps discussed were convening forums, agreeing on shared priorities, publishing a transparent baseline assessment and piloting a locally supported market initiative within the first 10 days. These were presented as suggested actions for consideration, not as programmes that had already been approved or commenced.

Adeola said the region’s renewal would require collective responsibility, credible institutions, evidence-based advocacy and cooperation among stakeholders.

“We need our voice. We need the evidence. We need coalitions. We need institutions,” she said

title: Customs suspends training at colleges over recruitment dispute
description:
From Uche Usim
The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has suspended ongoing training activities at its two training colleges following concerns raised by the Federal Character Commission (FCC) over its recruitment exercise.
The Service said the suspension was temporary and intended to allow further consu
content:
From Uche Usim

The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has suspended ongoing training activities at its two training colleges following concerns raised by the Federal Character Commission (FCC) over its recruitment exercise.

The Service said the suspension was temporary and intended to allow further consultations with the commission to resolve the issues amicably.

In a statement on Friday, the NCS said the decision followed engagements between the commission and a delegation of the Service, during which both parties agreed to pursue constructive dialogue and mutual understanding.

The Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi, reiterated the Service’s commitment to working with relevant government institutions to resolve the concerns in the national interest.

Adeniyi also acknowledged the role of the FCC in promoting national unity, fairness and equitable representation in public service appointments.

He said the commission’s constitutional mandate was critical to ensuring that the principles of federal character were upheld across the country.

The Customs Service expressed confidence that the ongoing discussions would provide an opportunity to address the issues raised by the commission while strengthening the relationship between both institutions.

It added that it remained committed to transparency, accountability and constructive engagement with government agencies to promote public confidence and effective service delivery.

title: Russia pummels Ukraine, missile hits Poland, after Putin threat
description:
Moscow pounded Ukraine with massive strikes Friday, with Kyiv saying at least seven people were killed in the capital, while neighbouring Poland accused Moscow of “provocation” after two Russian missiles likely landed in the southeast corner of the NATO country.



Russia’s Vladimir Putin had vowed
content:
Moscow pounded Ukraine with massive strikes Friday, with Kyiv saying at least seven people were killed in the capital, while neighbouring Poland accused Moscow of “provocation” after two Russian missiles likely landed in the southeast corner of the NATO country.

Russia’s Vladimir Putin had vowed a “painful” response to Kyiv’s strikes on Moscow’s Crimea bridge after holding a summit with China’s Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump.

Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky called the night-time strikes one of Moscow’s largest of the nearly five-year war, denouncing what he said was Russian “terror”.

Zelensky, who met allies in Berlin Thursday, said Putin’s attempts to “redraw the world” with Xi and Trump had been a “failure”.

In China, Putin said he “shared responsibility” for global peace with Xi and Trump and issued a “declaration toward peace” that made no mention of Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine.

AFP journalists saw people hunkered down in Kyiv’s metro stations, which double as overnight air-raid shelters, sleeping on yoga mats, camping chairs and in pop-up tents.

Kateryna Liubychenko, 32, took her toddler down to try to get some sleep through the bombardment.

“It’s painful to have to stop our child from living,” she told AFP.

Two people were killed in Lviv, power was knocked out in swathes of the country and in Kyiv, three vital transport bridges were hit, officials said.

Explosions rang out through the night as Ukrainian officials reported more than 80 missiles and 400 drones were fired.

Three bridges that cross the Dnipro river were hit, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said, threatening yet more disruption to daily life in the city.

France requested a UN Security Council meeting over the strikes, saying “Russia will have to answer for its actions there”.

Poland decries ‘provocation’

In neighbouring Poland, authorities said one missile was confirmed to have landed in the eastern village of Nowy Lipowiec, with another missile and a jet-powered drone suspected to have hit two other locations.

Warsaw said no-one was hurt.

Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the weapons flying into Poland were deliberate.

“The provocation may have been linked with the fact that there are (military) exercises taking place on the territory of Poland,” Tusk told a televised press conference in Warsaw.

Thousands of European troops are taking part in military exercises in southeastern Poland.

“Nobody can say that this was an innocent coincidence,” Tusk said, adding he had informed NATO “straight away”.

Tusk said that NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte would be in Warsaw on Saturday and that he would inform him of the incident.

Poland is one of five countries Europe picked to represent it at future US-led talks on Ukraine.

Bridge retaliation

Russia, which has refused a ceasefire, has increased its strikes as temperatures dip in Ukraine, with many fearing this winter could be the worst of the war yet.

Kyiv’s state energy operator reported “significant damage” to the country’s energy infrastructure that had “seriously impacted the operation of the power grid”.

The Black Sea port city of Odesa was in a “critical” situation with a “widespread power outage”, it said — adding blackouts were also recorded in Kyiv and 10 other regions.

Russia’s military on Friday confirmed it had launched a “massive” attack with missiles and drones, saying they targeted military-industrial sites and transport infrastructure in several regions, including bridges in Kyiv.

The UN has reported rising civilian casualties this year as Russia intensifies its long-range strikes.

UNICEF on Friday said at least 114 children had been killed and 1,030 wounded in the first 10 months of 2026 — “a higher number of verified child casualties than in any of the past three years”.

“That is on average of more than three children killed or injured every single day,” the organisation said, warning of an “alarming escalation in violence affecting children in Ukraine”.

US-led talks on ending the fighting have so far shown little signs of progress, with Moscow having stuck to its hardline demands.

Putin has said a deal to end the war in Ukraine must be part of a wider agreement on European security.

Speaking in China on Thursday, he said any form of Ukraine-Europe military cooperation as part of that deal would be a “problem”.

title: ASUU Begins Indefinite Strike At Zamfara Varsity As Govt Inaugurates Salary Review Committee
description: The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Zamfara State University branch, has commenced an indefinite strike over the alleged failure of the state government to meet its demands on salary agreements and outstanding staff entitlements.The industrial action came as the Zamfara State Government
content:
The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Zamfara State University branch, has commenced an indefinite strike over the alleged failure of the state government to meet its demands on salary agreements and outstanding staff entitlements.

The industrial action came as the Zamfara State Government inaugurated a committee to review salary structures and address welfare concerns in state-owned tertiary institutions.

ASUU announced the strike after its congress held on Tuesday at the university’s temporary campus in Talata Mafara.

Speaking after the meeting, the Acting Chairman of the branch, Anas Dogo, accused the state government of failing to address issues affecting lecturers despite several appeals and engagements through established channels.

He said the decision followed the expiration of an ultimatum and a subsequent warning strike declared by the union, which he said did not receive any positive response from the government.

Dogo explained that the union could no longer guarantee the provision of academic services under the prevailing conditions.

He listed the union’s demands to include the implementation of the December 2025 Federal Government-ASUU salary agreement, payment of promotion arrears and other outstanding financial obligations owed to lecturers.

The ASUU leader said the union had held several meetings with the university’s governing council, management and other relevant stakeholders before deciding to embark on the indefinite strike.

He added that attempts to secure meetings with the Commissioner for Education, the Head of Service and the Secretary to the State Government were unsuccessful.

Meanwhile, the Zamfara State Government has inaugurated a committee to review the non-implementation of revised salary structures and other staff welfare issues in the state’s tertiary institutions.

The Secretary to the State Government, Abubakar Nakwada, who chairs the committee, inaugurated it and presided over its maiden meeting on Thursday in Gusau.

According to a statement issued by the Senior Special Assistant on Media to the SSG, Suleman Tudu, the committee is expected to examine relevant government circulars, determine the financial implications of outstanding obligations and consult stakeholders towards finding an amicable resolution.

Speaking at the inauguration, Nakwada reaffirmed Governor Dauda Lawal’s commitment to workers’ welfare, industrial harmony and the repositioning of tertiary education in the state.

He acknowledged that demands presented by the Forum of Zamfara State Tertiary Institutions (FOZASTI) and Zamfara State University over salaries, allowances and promotion benefits remained a concern to the government.

The SSG said the committee would approach the assignment with objectivity and sincerity, taking into consideration the interests of workers and the financial realities of the state.

He cited the increase in the state minimum wage from ₦7,000 to ₦70,000, clearance of gratuity arrears, and implementation of a new salary scale for healthcare workers as evidence of the administration’s commitment to workers’ welfare.

Nakwada appealed to aggrieved unions to give dialogue a chance and allow the committee to complete its assignment, warning that industrial action at this critical moment would hurt rather than help the education system.

Members of the committee include the commissioners for finance, education, science and technology, local government and chieftaincy affairs, and budget and planning.

Others are the special adviser on economic and financial matters, representatives of FOZASTI, the Nigeria Labour Congress in Zamfara State and Zamfara State University, while the permanent secretary of the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology will serve as secretary.

The government’s intervention is expected to provide a platform for addressing the outstanding welfare issues, although ASUU has already commenced its indefinite strike over the unresolved demands.

The post ASUU Begins Indefinite Strike At Zamfara Varsity As Govt Inaugurates Salary Review Committee appeared first on Channels Television.

title: 2027: Group drums up support for Tinubu, Ododo in Kogi
description:
A Northern support group, Arewa for Asiwaju, has urged residents of Kogi East Senatorial District to support President Bola Tinubu and Governor Ahmed Ododo, citing projects and government interventions under their administrations.
The State Coordinator of the group, Abdulkareem Mohammed, popularly k
content:
A Northern support group, Arewa for Asiwaju, has urged residents of Kogi East Senatorial District to support President Bola Tinubu and Governor Ahmed Ododo, citing projects and government interventions under their administrations.

The State Coordinator of the group, Abdulkareem Mohammed, popularly known as Asuku, disclosed this in a statement issued on Friday.

Mohammed said the group had embarked on a grassroots mobilisation tour of the district, engaging residents through town hall meetings, community visits and presentations on government projects.

He said residents needed to be adequately informed about government policies and achievements to enable them to make informed political decisions.

“Our mission is to bridge the information gap between the government and the people by taking information about government policies, interventions and achievements directly to the grassroots,” he said.

He urged residents to assess political leaders based on their performance, policies and contributions to community development rather than ethnic affiliations or campaign promises.

Asuku also called for unity and peaceful coexistence among residents, irrespective of their ethnic, religious and cultural backgrounds.

“We encourage residents to judge political leaders by their performance, policies and contributions to community development rather than ethnic affiliations or campaign rhetoric.

“Residents should also embrace unity and peaceful coexistence, irrespective of their ethnic, religious and cultural backgrounds,” he said.

The coordinator said the group was using projectors and other information and communication technology tools to showcase government projects and interventions rather than relying solely on political rallies and campaign speeches.

He disclosed that the mobilisation exercise had covered Dekina, Bassa, Ankpa and Olamaboro, with the delegation scheduled to extend its engagements to Idah and Ibaji.

He added that the Kogi outreach was part of the group’s wider mobilisation campaign for Tinubu’s re-election in 2027.

At a town hall meeting in Anyigba, Dekina Local Government Area, the group’s State Secretary, Dr Anthony Edogbo, presented selected achievements and interventions of the Tinubu and Ododo administrations.

The presentation highlighted infrastructure, security, the establishment of a military formation in Kogi State, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, scholarship opportunities, state bursary programmes, support for youth and student organisations, and the payment of workers’ salaries.

The meeting also featured the presentation of appointment letters to Hon. John Urah Ikani, who was named A4A Chairman in Dekina, and Prince Ishaq Okolo, who was appointed patron.

title: INEC picks 598 polling units for mock election exercise in Delta
description:
From Enweliku Kent, Asaba
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) will conduct a mock accreditation and result upload exercise in 598 polling units across the 25 local government areas of Delta State as part of its preparations for the 2027 general elections.
The exercise, scheduled for
content:
From Enweliku Kent, Asaba

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) will conduct a mock accreditation and result upload exercise in 598 polling units across the 25 local government areas of Delta State as part of its preparations for the 2027 general elections.

The exercise, scheduled for Saturday, November 28, 2026, is aimed at testing the functionality and reliability of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS), assessing election-day procedures and identifying potential operational challenges ahead of the polls.

The Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Delta State, Sir Etekamba Udo Umoren, disclosed this on Friday during a press briefing in Asaba.

Umoren said the simulation was part of INEC’s broader efforts to strengthen electoral processes and ensure credible, transparent, efficient and seamless elections in 2027.

He explained that the exercise would enable the Commission to evaluate BVAS performance under different environmental and operational conditions before its deployment for the general elections.

The REC emphasised that the exercise was strictly a simulation and not an actual election, adding that no winners or losers would be declared.

According to him, 598 polling units have been selected across the state’s 25 local government areas, with two polling units in each registration area designated for the exercise.

He said the polling units would open at 7:30 a.m., while voter accreditation would commence at 8:00 a.m. and end at 2:30 p.m.

Umoren noted that the selection was designed to ensure adequate geographical representation and provide an opportunity to assess the Commission’s operational capacity at the grassroots level.

The simulation will cover the testing of electoral technology and equipment, particularly BVAS, as well as procedures for voter accreditation, voting, result recording and transmission, alongside other election-day activities.

He added that any technical challenges encountered would be documented and addressed before the 2027 general elections.

On personnel readiness, the REC said the exercise would also assess electoral officials’ understanding of polling procedures, the handling of election materials, accreditation, voting, counting and result management.

He urged participating officials to demonstrate professionalism, discipline and neutrality while adhering strictly to established electoral guidelines.

The Commission will also use the exercise to evaluate its logistical arrangements, particularly the timely deployment of personnel, election materials, equipment and other essential resources to the designated polling units.

Umoren called on political parties, security agencies, media organisations, civil society groups, community leaders and other stakeholders to support the exercise by sensitising the public about its purpose and encouraging peaceful conduct in the selected polling units.

He specifically urged media organisations to ensure accurate and responsible reporting, stressing the need to educate residents that the exercise was solely intended to test electoral processes and did not constitute an actual election.

He assured residents that INEC would collaborate with relevant security agencies to maintain peace and order throughout the exercise. Political actors, community leaders, youths and members of the public were also urged to cooperate with electoral officials and avoid actions capable of disrupting the process.

The REC further disclosed that the Commission would closely monitor and evaluate the simulation to identify operational strengths, weaknesses and areas requiring improvement.

Feedback from electoral officials, observers, stakeholders and technical personnel would be analysed and used to improve operational procedures, enhance staff performance and strengthen logistical arrangements ahead of the 2027 elections.

Reaffirming INEC’s commitment to credible elections, Umoren said the Commission remained determined to deliver polls that were free, fair, transparent, inclusive and peaceful.

He described the forthcoming simulation as an important milestone in the Commission’s preparations for the 2027 general elections, noting that its success would depend largely on the cooperation and support of all stakeholders.

He urged the media to use the opportunity to educate residents on the importance of the exercise and its role in strengthening Nigeria’s electoral system, while reiterating INEC’s commitment to continuous improvement and stakeholder engagement to ensure that every eligible voter could exercise their franchise in a peaceful, secure and credible environment.

The post INEC picks 598 polling units for mock election exercise in Delta appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.
