title: Tinubu, Akpabio, Abbas attend Aliero’s daughter’s wedding in Abuja
description:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja
President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday joined an array of political leaders, governors and other prominent Nigerians at the wedding Fatiha of Senator Adamu Aliero’s daughter in Abuja.
The ceremony, held at the National Mosque, Abuja, attracted the President of the Sena
content:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday joined an array of political leaders, governors and other prominent Nigerians at the wedding Fatiha of Senator Adamu Aliero’s daughter in Abuja.

The ceremony, held at the National Mosque, Abuja, attracted the President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio; the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas; and the Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin.

Also in attendance were the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu; Kebbi State Governor, Nasir Idris; Kwara State Governor, AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq; and a former Bauchi State governor, Adamu Mu’azu.

Others included President Tinubu’s son, Yinka Tinubu; a former Zamfara State governor and Director-General of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council for the 2027 general elections, Senator Abdulaziz Yari; and the Etsu Nupe, Alhaji Yahaya Abubakar.

The wedding Fatiha brought together political associates, traditional rulers and other dignitaries to celebrate with the former Minister of the Federal Capital Territory and senator representing Kebbi Central.

Photographs from the ceremony showed Tinubu alongside Aliero and other political leaders at the mosque.

title: INEC begins distribution of 86,931 PVCs in Kogi
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission in Kogi State has announced the availability of 86,931 Permanent Voter Cards for residents who participated in the second phase of the Continuous Voter Registration exercise.
The Resident Electoral Commissioner in Kogi State, Dr Shehu L. Wahab, disclosed
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission in Kogi State has announced the availability of 86,931 Permanent Voter Cards for residents who participated in the second phase of the Continuous Voter Registration exercise.

The Resident Electoral Commissioner in Kogi State, Dr Shehu L. Wahab, disclosed this in a press release made available to journalists in Lokoja on Friday.

According to the commission, the second phase of the CVR exercise was conducted between January 5 and April 17, 2026.

INEC said the 86,931 PVCs produced for eligible registrants had been delivered to its offices across the 21 local government areas of the state and were ready for collection.

The commission advised registrants to visit the INEC office in the local government area where they completed their registration to collect their cards.

It said registrants were expected to come with their registration slips or printouts, or a valid means of identification where required.

INEC also clarified that PVCs from the first phase of the registration exercise were still available for collection.

The commission warned that PVCs would not be issued through proxies, stressing that registrants must personally collect their cards.

Collection is available at INEC local government offices from 9 am to 3 pm, Monday to Friday.

The commission further directed registrants to check the status of their PVCs and locate their collection centres through its CVR portal, cvr.inecnigeria.org.

INEC urged all voters who participated in the second phase of the CVR exercise to collect their PVCs without delay, noting that the cards were essential for participation in future elections.

The commission said timely collection would help ensure that no eligible voter was disenfranchised.

Wahab expressed appreciation to registrants for their patience during the production, verification, and distribution processes, assuring them that the commission remained committed to ensuring that every eligible voter obtained a PVC and was able to exercise their democratic right.

The post INEC begins distribution of 86,931 PVCs in Kogi appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Tinubu appoints former Lagos Commissioner Agboola Dabiri to National Assembly Service Commission
description:
President Bola Tinubu has approved the appointment of Agboola Lukman Dabiri as the South-West representative on the National Assembly Service Commission (NASC).
Dabiri replaces Taiwo Olukemi Oluwa, who resigned from the position on March 30, 2026, to pursue her ambition in the 2027 general elections
content:
President Bola Tinubu has approved the appointment of Agboola Lukman Dabiri as the South-West representative on the National Assembly Service Commission (NASC).

Dabiri replaces Taiwo Olukemi Oluwa, who resigned from the position on March 30, 2026, to pursue her ambition in the 2027 general elections.

Oluwa is seeking election to represent the Irewole/Isokan Federal Constituency of Osun State in the House of Representatives.

Before his new appointment, Dabiri served as the Commissioner for Youth and Social Development in Lagos State.

‎He also previously served as Mandate Secretary for Economic Planning, Revenue Generation and Public-Private Partnership in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).
‎
‎A statement by presidential spokesman, Bayo Onanuga said “The appointment is part of the President’s efforts to ensure effective representation and inclusivity in the National Assembly Service Commission.”

title: Nigeria’s cultural diversity can drive national unity, economic growth — Minister
description:
The Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, Hannatu Musawa, on Friday said Nigeria’s cultural diversity can serve as a catalyst for national unity, social cohesion and economic growth.
Musawa stated this in a statement released by her special adviser on media, Nneka Anibeze ahead
content:
The Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, Hannatu Musawa, on Friday said Nigeria’s cultural diversity can serve as a catalyst for national unity, social cohesion and economic growth.

Musawa stated this in a statement released by her special adviser on media, Nneka Anibeze ahead of the 2026 National Festival of Arts and Culture, scheduled to hold in Enugu State from November 21 to 28.

She said the festival remained an important platform for bringing Nigerians together, promoting the country’s cultural heritage and projecting a positive image of the nation.

The minister explained that the decision to postpone the 2025 edition was informed by the need to show solidarity with families and communities affected by insecurity across the country.

“Last year, we made the difficult but necessary decision to postpone NAFEST out of empathy, respect and solidarity with families and communities affected by insecurity across the country. It was more respectful and responsible to pause than to celebrate at a time when many citizens were grieving,” she said.

According to her, the festival will return bigger, with renewed opportunities to strengthen national integration and showcase Nigeria’s creative potential.

“Today, we return stronger. NAFEST has always played a powerful role in nation-building. It brings Nigerians together, strengthens social cohesion, and projects a different and more accurate picture of Nigeria, a picture of unity, inclusiveness, hospitality and national confidence,” Musawa added.

Themed ‘Connected Culture’, the eight-day festival is being organised by the National Council for Arts and Culture in collaboration with the Enugu State Government.

Activities will take place at the Enugu International Conference Centre and Michael Okpara Square, featuring cultural parades, traditional performances, exhibitions, indigenous games and competitions, including Jollof Wars, Dance-Off Naija and Sing-Off Naija.

The festival will also feature a culture market for artisans and entrepreneurs, creative industry workshops and a colloquium involving investors, financial institutions and industry stakeholders to explore opportunities for financing Nigeria’s creative economy.

The Director-General of the NCAC, Obi Asika, urged Nigerians to participate, describing culture as an important tool for national identity and economic opportunity.

“Our culture is our identity, our strength and our opportunity. NAFEST Enugu 2026 invites every Nigerian to celebrate who we are, showcase our creativity, and unlock the immense potential of our cultural heritage,” he said.

The National Festival of Arts and Culture is an annual initiative of the NCAC aimed at promoting Nigeria’s diverse cultural heritage, encouraging cultural exchange and strengthening national integration.

Beyond cultural preservation, the festival provides a platform for creatives, artisans and entrepreneurs to showcase their products, access markets and contribute to the country’s growing creative economy.

The post Nigeria’s cultural diversity can drive national unity, economic growth — Minister appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: EPL: Prove loyalty to Tottenham fans, De Zerbi tells Mudryk
description:
Roberto De Zerbi has challenged Mykhailo Mudryk to regain the support of angry Tottenham fans after the Ukraine winger’s admission that joining Arsenal would have been his “dream” move.
Mudryk recently said he came close to joining Arsenal just prior to his transfer from Shakhtar Donetsk to Chelsea
content:
Roberto De Zerbi has challenged Mykhailo Mudryk to regain the support of angry Tottenham fans after the Ukraine winger’s admission that joining Arsenal would have been his “dream” move.

Mudryk recently said he came close to joining Arsenal just prior to his transfer from Shakhtar Donetsk to Chelsea in 2023.

During an appearance on the ‘Guest of Gordon’ podcast, Mudryk described Premier League champions Arsenal as “the club I wanted to play for” and stated “moving to the Emirates Stadium was my dream”.

The 25-year-old eventually made it to north London, but with Tottenham not Arsenal, when he left Stamford Bridge in a season-long loan deal in September.

Mudryk’s desire to play for Tottenham’s bitter rivals inevitably sparked a frustrated response from supporters.

Tottenham boss De Zerbi admitted he could understand their anger and urged Mudryk to make amends on the pitch.

Ahead of Saturday’s Premier League home game against Ipswich, the Italian told reporters: “Yes, I can understand the fans (feeling) but Mudryk is a good guy and is a good player.

“He suffered a lot for the situation in the last couple of years. He has just one thing to do. Show on the pitch his qualities and show on the pitch that now he is playing for Tottenham.

“He has a big chance to play with us because Tottenham is a big club, he knows very well the coach, he knows very well the style of play and he knows I give him total confidence to show what he is.”

Mudryk will not be able to get back in the fans’ good books just yet.

He has played only 16 minutes for Tottenham due to an ankle injury and is still two to three weeks away from returning to training.

Asked if Tottenham could cancel his loan in January, De Zerbi ducked the issue.

“It is not my part, no? I am a coach and now we have to help him to recover in the best way because I believe he can be very important for us,” he said.

AFP

The post EPL: Prove loyalty to Tottenham fans, De Zerbi tells Mudryk appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Soludo approves ₦50,000 December bonus for Anambra workers
description:
Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has approved an additional flat payment of ₦50,000 for all state civil servants, to be reflected directly in their December 2026 payslips.
Soludo disclosed this at the 2026 Civil Service Day celebration held at the Jerome Udoji State Secretariat Complex
content:
Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has approved an additional flat payment of ₦50,000 for all state civil servants, to be reflected directly in their December 2026 payslips.

Soludo disclosed this at the 2026 Civil Service Day celebration held at the Jerome Udoji State Secretariat Complex in Awka on Friday.

He paired the financial boost with immediate executive approvals to modernise the secretariat environment and enhance productivity.

Addressing demands for comparisons between Anambra’s salary structure and those of other states, the governor offered a lesson on fiscal federalism, reminding the workforce that states operate with vastly different economic capacities.

He urged workers to consider a state’s revenue and resource base before making inter-state wage comparisons, emphasising that sustainable governance, rather than empty promises, guided his administration.

He said, “I understand the situation and economic conditions; we need to be able to do something. The pay that we have all over is not enough; I clearly understand it.

“But there is one thing I also tell you, and that is I don’t play to the wind. Before we get into a commitment, we make sure that it is something that we will always honour.”

Soludo also thanked the workers for supporting his administration during the governorship election, expressing confidence that Anambra’s public servants overwhelmingly voted for and appreciated his government’s developmental strides.

Acting on three major appeals presented during the event, the governor issued immediate directives on the rehabilitation of secretariat roads, the establishment of an ICT centre and the pruning of overgrown trees across the secretariat complex.

Earlier, the Anambra State Head of Service, Ngozi Iwouno, commended Soludo for restoring security and normalcy across the state.

Iwouno noted that civil servants now reported to work consistently without fear, having overcome the disruption caused by the past Monday sit-at-home orders, before presenting the workforce’s appeals to the governor.

The post Soludo approves ₦50,000 December bonus for Anambra workers appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Former Eagles captain, Segun Odegbami attacked at Ogun residence
description:
Former Super Eagles captain Segun Odegbami has reportedly been attacked and macheted by unidentified assailants at his residence in Abeokuta, Ogun State.
The 74-year-old football legend was attacked at about 2:30 am on Friday at his home in Ibara Government Reserved Area (GRA), Abeokuta.
According t
content:
Former Super Eagles captain Segun Odegbami has reportedly been attacked and macheted by unidentified assailants at his residence in Abeokuta, Ogun State.

The 74-year-old football legend was attacked at about 2:30 am on Friday at his home in Ibara Government Reserved Area (GRA), Abeokuta.

According to sources, the attackers, who were three in number, first overpowered Odegbami’s domestic staff and driver before forcing their way into his bedroom.

The incident has raised concerns over the safety of the former Nigerian international and the security situation in the area.

The assailants reportedly asked for Odegbami and beat up the staff after they denied that he was at home.

“The generator was on at that time. So, the armed men believed he must be at home and they handed severe beatings to the staff. They immediately found their way to Odegbami’s bedroom and attacked him there,” a resident who spoke on condition of anonymity said.

Odegbami who is the proprietor of Eagles 7 Sports Radio 103.7 FM, Abeokuta, was said to have resisted the attackers, leading to a scuffle, before they inflicted deep machete cuts on him and fled the scene.

He was rushed to an undisclosed hospital where he is currently receiving treatment.

Residents said the incident was promptly reported to the police.

The motive for the attack was yet to be established as of the time of filing this report.

When contacted, Ogun State Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, told Very Nigerian that a thorough investigation is underway with intensive efforts ongoing to identify and apprehend those responsible.

“The Command is leaving no stone unturned in addressing the incident. The Commissioner of Police immediately ordered a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding it, with intensive efforts ongoing to identify and apprehend those responsible.

“We can also confirm that Chief Segun Odegbami has been discharged from the hospital,” Babaseyi added.

The post Former Eagles captain, Segun Odegbami attacked at Ogun residence appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Customs suspend training for 3,852 recruits over Federal Character Commission concerns
description: The Nigeria Customs Service has suspended training activities for 3,852 newly recruited officers, nearly two years after it began the recruitment process, following concerns raised by the Federal Character Commission over alleged irregularities in the selection and invitation of successful candidate
content:
The Nigeria Customs Service has suspended training activities for 3,852 newly recruited officers, nearly two years after it began the recruitment process, following concerns raised by the Federal Character Commission over alleged irregularities in the selection and invitation of successful candidates.

The suspension, announced on Friday in a statement signed by the Deputy Comptroller of Customs and National Public Relations Officer, Abdullahi Maiwada, came after engagements between the management of the Customs Service and a delegation of the commission, with both institutions agreeing to further consultations to resolve the disagreement.

The statement read, “The Nigeria Customs Service has temporarily put on hold the ongoing training activities at its two training colleges to allow further consultations and dialogue with the Federal Character Commission towards the amicable resolution of concerns raised in connection with the ongoing recruitment exercise.

“The decision follows engagements between the Commission and a delegation of the NCS, during which both parties reaffirmed their commitment to resolving the issues through constructive dialogue, mutual understanding and continued institutional collaboration.”

Maiwada said the Service has suspended training activities at its two training colleges following concerns raised by the Federal Character Commission over the ongoing recruitment exercise.

He said the suspension is aimed at allowing the two agencies to resolve the disagreements surrounding the recruitment process through further consultations and dialogue.

The development comes amid questions over the selection of successful candidates, following complaints by applicants who alleged that they were excluded from the training exercise despite appearing on the published final recruitment lists.

The Service said both institutions had reaffirmed their commitment to resolving the issues through constructive dialogue, mutual understanding and continued institutional collaboration.

It stated that the Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi, had reiterated the agency’s commitment to working with relevant government institutions in the national interest.

The statement read, “In consideration of the concerns raised by the Commission and in line with the series of engagements, the Comptroller-General of Customs, CGC Bashir Adewale Adeniyi, MFR, has reaffirmed the Service’s commitment to institutional collaboration and constructive engagement with relevant government institutions in the overall national interest.

“Furthermore, the CGC acknowledged the critical role of FCC in promoting national unity, fairness and equitable representation in public service appointments, noting the importance of its constitutional mandate in strengthening inclusiveness and ensuring that the principles of federal character are upheld across the Federation.”

The Customs Service added that it valued its longstanding relationship with the commission and was confident that the ongoing discussions would provide an opportunity to address the concerns raised.

“The NCS values its longstanding relationship with the FCC and remains confident that the ongoing dialogue will provide an opportunity to address the concerns raised in a mutually beneficial manner, while reinforcing the shared commitment of both institutions to fairness, national cohesion and effective public service delivery,” it stated.

The Service also pledged to maintain transparency and accountability throughout the process, stressing that it would continue to engage relevant government institutions to strengthen public confidence in its operations.

The dispute comes against the backdrop of a recruitment exercise that began with a newspaper advertisement on December 27, 2024, when the Customs Service announced 3,927 vacancies across its Superintendent, Inspectorate and Customs Assistant cadres.

The exercise attracted more than 573,000 applications, with 286,697 candidates initially shortlisted for the next stage after the first round of documentary screening.

Following subsequent assessments, the Service published its final lists between July 28 and 30, 2026, announcing 3,852 successful candidates comprising 1,275 officers in the Superintendent Cadre, 367 in the Inspectorate Cadre and 2,210 in the Customs Assistant Cadre.

The training exercise subsequently commenced on October 9, 2026, with successful candidates reporting to the designated training colleges.

However, the recruitment process became contentious after some applicants complained that they had been excluded from training despite completing the required screening and documentation exercises and seeing their names on the published lists.

The Federal Character Commission subsequently raised concerns about the process, including allegations that some candidates whose names appeared on the final lists were not invited for training, while some individuals whose names were not published allegedly received invitations.

The commission also cited complaints from more than 500 applicants who claimed they had completed the necessary stages, including medical examinations, but were subsequently excluded.

In its position on the controversy, the FCC argued that the complaints required investigation to establish whether the recruitment process complied with the applicable federal character principles.

The commission called for the suspension of the training exercise pending an examination of the disputed recruitment process. It also said its 330th plenary session had resolved to suspend Customs recruitment activities indefinitely.

The latest decision by the Customs Service to put training activities on hold comes as both institutions seek an amicable resolution of the disagreement.

The controversy has placed renewed attention on the constitutional responsibility of federal institutions to ensure fairness and equitable representation in public appointments, particularly in recruitment exercises involving thousands of applicants from across the country.

The federal character principle is intended to prevent the concentration of public appointments and opportunities in a few states or sections of the country, while promoting national unity and balanced representation.

The Service, however, expressed confidence that continued engagement would produce a resolution that would protect the interests of both institutions and reinforce public confidence in the recruitment exercise.

The post Customs suspend training for 3,852 recruits over Federal Character Commission concerns appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Edo has 2.8 million registered voters — REC
description:
The Edo State Resident Electoral Commissioner, Obo Effanga, on Friday, said the state currently had 2.8 million registered voters following the latest Continuous Voter Registration exercise.
He said the final figure would be released after the Independent National Electoral Commission completed its
content:
The Edo State Resident Electoral Commissioner, Obo Effanga, on Friday, said the state currently had 2.8 million registered voters following the latest Continuous Voter Registration exercise.

He said the final figure would be released after the Independent National Electoral Commission completed its recent data clean-up exercise.

INEC had earlier announced that 131,165 new voters were registered during the Continuous Voter Registration exercise, which ran from August 2025 to July 2026.

Giving an update on the collection of Permanent Voter Cards, Effanga said 23,401 PVCs had been collected across the state since distribution began on October 9.

He said the figure comprised 6,319 old PVCs, 5,128 newly produced cards and 11,954 cards relating to voter transfers.

“The state currently has 2.8 million registered voters after the last registration exercise. However, the final figure would be released after the recent clean-up exercise by the national body,” Effanga said.

The REC disclosed that PVCs for voters who registered during the first and second phases of the CVR exercise were available for collection at INEC offices across the state’s 18 local government areas.

He recalled that the first phase of the registration exercise ran from August to December 2025, while the second phase took place between January and April 2026.

Effanga said the commission was working towards ensuring a smooth electoral process.

Speaking on the mock accreditation exercise scheduled for November 28, the REC said it would be conducted in 384 polling units across the state.

He explained that Edo had 192 registration areas, also known as wards, with two polling units selected from each for the exercise.

“The exercise would provide an opportunity to test the commission’s electoral technology and assess the readiness of its personnel ahead of the elections.

“The state office had submitted the list of proposed polling units to the commission’s headquarters for approval,” he added.

He said the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System would be deployed during the exercise to demonstrate how voters were accredited, how results were captured and how they were transmitted to the INEC Result Viewing Portal.

The REC explained that INEC did not have enough permanent staff to conduct elections across the state’s 4,519 polling units, making the recruitment of ad hoc personnel necessary.

He said recruitment would commence after the closure of the application portal, after which the commission’s headquarters would process applicants’ details and forward their names to the respective states based on their preferred locations of service.

Successful applicants would subsequently be invited for screening and training before deployment, he added.

Effanga identified supervisory presiding officers and collation officers as other categories of ad hoc personnel.

He explained that supervisory presiding officers were usually selected from among senior civil servants, particularly federal civil servants who met the required grade-level qualifications.

Responding to concerns about the safety of ad hoc staff, particularly in view of previous incidents of electoral violence, the REC said INEC was working with security agencies to ensure adequate protection for everyone involved in the electoral process.

He said the security arrangements would cover election officials, voters, journalists and other stakeholders.

According to him, the commission had been holding regular meetings of the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security, with the latest meeting held on Tuesday.

He added that he would participate in a national summit on election security organised by the Office of the National Security Adviser in collaboration with INEC.

However, Effanga said maintaining electoral security required the cooperation of all stakeholders, particularly politicians, whom he accused of sometimes encouraging violence through their actions and campaign rhetoric.

He said politicians should understand that elections were civil exercises and should not threaten or intimidate voters into supporting particular candidates.

The REC condemned statements suggesting that people who refused to vote for certain candidates should not visit particular communities, describing such rhetoric as unacceptable.

On whether election personnel were covered by insurance in the event of injuries or other incidents during elections, Effanga confirmed that the commission had insurance arrangements for those engaged in the electoral process.

He said the coverage included life insurance, adding that INEC had previously taken responsibility for the medical treatment and other necessary support for corps members injured while performing electoral duties.

The post Edo has 2.8 million registered voters — REC appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Police Probe Attack On NDC Secretariat In Edo, Invite Council Chairman
description: The Edo State Police Command has commenced an investigation into an attack on the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) secretariat in Afuze, Owan East Local Government Area, by armed men suspected to be members of the Edo State Security Network.The incident reportedly occurred on Wednesday, November 19
content:
The Edo State Police Command has commenced an investigation into an attack on the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) secretariat in Afuze, Owan East Local Government Area, by armed men suspected to be members of the Edo State Security Network.

The incident reportedly occurred on Wednesday, November 19, at about 4 p.m., when NDC political aspirants, Mrs. Mariam Iseme and Grant Eruhagan, were holding a meeting with other party members at the secretariat.

According to the Police Public Relations Officer, Edo State Command, ASP Eno Ikoedem, the armed men, dressed in security network uniforms and wielding guns and machetes, stormed the premises, destroyed political banners and other materials, and threatened to kill the occupants before fleeing upon sighting the police.

Ikoedem said the command had commenced efforts to identify, locate and apprehend those involved, adding that the Chairman of Owan East Local Government Area, Ernest Aitalegbe, had also been invited to assist the ongoing investigation.

The Commissioner of Police, CP Patrick Daaor, warned politicians, aspirants, supporters and their loyalists against violence, intimidation, destruction of property and the use of thugs to advance political interests.

He stressed that the command would not tolerate political lawlessness, warning that anyone found sponsoring, perpetrating, or aiding acts of violence would be arrested and prosecuted, irrespective of political affiliation or status.

The police commissioner urged political actors to desist from actions capable of disrupting public peace, assuring that the command would enforce the law without fear or favour.

title: France Probes 77-year-old Actor Depardieu, Author Houellebecq Over Alleged Gang Rape
description: French police are investigating allegations actor and convicted sex offender Gerard Depardieu and author Michel Houellebecq gang-raped and assaulted a woman on camera during a 2018 film shoot, two sources following the case said Friday.Depardieu, who has acted in more than 200 films and television s
content:
French police are investigating allegations actor and convicted sex offender Gerard Depardieu and author Michel Houellebecq gang-raped and assaulted a woman on camera during a 2018 film shoot, two sources following the case said Friday.

Depardieu, who has acted in more than 200 films and television series, is the highest-profile figure caught up in France’s response to the #MeToo movement.

The accusation is the latest in a flurry against the 77-year-old screen icon, who on Monday dropped his appeal against an 18-month suspended sentence for sexually assaulting two women during the filming of another movie in 2021.

Depardieu is to learn next week if he will stand trial for raping another actress, Charlotte Arnould, in 2018. A judge has ordered a trial, but Depardieu has rejected the allegations and appealed.

In the new case, the alleged abuse occurred in December 2018, during the shooting of “Thalasso”, a film starring the two men as versions of themselves.

Its director, Guillaume Nicloux, has been accused of complicity in the sexual abuse, one of the sources said.

The woman, an actor and dancer who was 32 at the time, told French investigative outlet Mediapart she was hired for a nude part but never given clear directions for the scene, which was not supposed to include any sex.

She said that during the filming, Houellebecq pulled her into a hotel room and onto a bed where he forcibly kissed her, then Depardieu digitally penetrated her while the author pinned her down.

Houellebecq also imposed an oral sexual act on her without her consent while the cameras were rolling, she told the publication, leaving her experiencing “profound humiliation” and “indescribable shame”.

The woman’s lawyer did not wish to respond to an AFP request for comment.

‘Not Simulated’

Depardieu’s attorneys did not immediately respond, nor did Houellebecq, who was contacted via his publisher.

The 70-year-old, who is among France’s most translated authors, is also under investigation for alleged incitement to discrimination in France over comments he made in 2022 about Muslims.

Last week, Mediapart and another outlet, Le Media, reported that another woman had accused Depardieu of groping her private parts when she appeared as an extra standing next to him during the filming of the 2013 movie “Turf”.

The casting director told Mediapart she had to crouch down between them to ensure he could no longer touch the woman in the final takes.

In April, Depardieu dropped legal action against public broadcaster France Télévisions over the editing of an investigative report aired in late 2023 in which he repeatedly made degrading and sexual remarks about women during a trip to North Korea.

In one of cinema’s most notorious scenes, Marlon Brando simulated anal rape of Maria Schneider in the 1972 film “Last Tango in Paris” without the director Bernardo Bertolucci informing her of the plan.

“Except that this time, it’s not simulated rape that the actor is denouncing,” Mediapart noted.

AFP

content:
‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
‎
‎ABUJA — PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has approved the appointment of Agboola Lukman Dabiri as Commissioner representing the South-West in the National Assembly Service Commission (NASC).
‎
‎Dabiri replaces Taiwo Olukemi Oluwa, who resigned her appointment on March 30, 2026, to contest in the 2027 General Elections for the Irewole/Isokan Federal Constituency of Osun State.
‎
‎Until his appointment, Dabiri served as Commissioner for Youth and Social Development in Lagos State.
‎
‎He also previously served as Mandate Secretary for Economic Planning, Revenue Generation and Public-Private Partnership in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).
‎
‎A statement by presidential spokesman, Bayo Onanuga said “The appointment is part of the President’s efforts to ensure effective representation and inclusivity in the National Assembly Service Commission.”
‎

title: Viral Video: Military uniforms found with bandits not from us – DHQ
description:
By Kingsley Omonobi



The Defence headquarters has denied supplying military camouflage uniforms allegedly found in the possession of suspected bandits in a viral social media video, insisting that the clothing did not originate from the Nigerian military.



Read Also: Viral Video: ‘We recovered 1
content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

The Defence headquarters has denied supplying military camouflage uniforms allegedly found in the possession of suspected bandits in a viral social media video, insisting that the clothing did not originate from the Nigerian military.

Read Also: Viral Video: ‘We recovered 12 AK-47 rifles, kidnap victims’ – Military defends engagement with bandits

The footage, circulating widely online, showed large quantities of woodland and desert camouflage uniforms spread on the ground, Several others were packed in sacks and allegedly held by suspected bandits.

Reacting to the video, the Director of Defence Media Operations, Maj. Gen. Michael Onoja ruled out the possibility that the uniforms were supplied by the military.

“That is not possible,” he said, when asked whether the clothing originated from the Nigerian military.

Onoja also dismissed suggestions that the uniforms might have been stolen from military supply vehicles attacked by bandits, saying no such incident had been reported.

“No such report has been made. It is not from the Nigerian military,” he added.

The video reportedly showed two different camouflage patterns, identified as woodland and desert designs, raising renewed concerns over the circulation of military clothing among criminal groups and unauthorised persons.

The development comes amid longstanding concerns about criminals, impersonating security personnel to perpetrate attacks, kidnappings and other crimes.

In February 2024, the Federal Government reiterated restrictions on the unauthorised use of military camouflage by civilians, warning against the misuse of security uniforms and equipment by criminal elements

Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle had stated that the restrictions were necessary to enable security agencies to distinguish legitimate personnel from impostors.

He noted that criminals had exploited military and other security agencies’ uniforms to deceive members of the public and facilitate criminal activities.

The government’s position was aimed at curbing impersonation, preventing the misuse of military uniforms and strengthening security operations across the country.

title: Federal Character Commission cancels 58 Staff recruitment in Kaduna
description:
The Federal Character Commission (FCC) has ordered the cancellation of the recruitment of 58 staff by the National Water Resources Institute (NWRI), Kaduna, over alleged violations of the Federal Character Principle.
The Commission directed the institute to commence a fresh recruitment exercise, cit
content:
The Federal Character Commission (FCC) has ordered the cancellation of the recruitment of 58 staff by the National Water Resources Institute (NWRI), Kaduna, over alleged violations of the Federal Character Principle.

The Commission directed the institute to commence a fresh recruitment exercise, citing failure to ensure equitable representation of states across the federation and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

In a statement issued on Friday, the FCC spokesperson, Ademola Lawrence, said the directive followed a review of a report submitted by the Commission’s monitoring officials, which established that the recruitment exercise did not comply with the prescribed Federal Character balancing index.

The Commission described the breach as a violation of the principles of fairness, equity and inclusiveness governing recruitment into public institutions.

It stressed that government agencies must ensure that employment opportunities reflect Nigeria’s diversity and do not create imbalances that undermine equitable representation.

“The Federal Character Principle, as enshrined in Section 14(3) of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended), is a constitutional requirement, not an administrative formality,” the statement said.

According to the commission, public institutions have a responsibility to ensure fairness and balanced representation in appointments, recruitment and the distribution of opportunities across the country.

Consequently, the FCC directed the National Water Resources Institute to cancel the entire exercise and begin the recruitment process afresh in strict compliance with the prescribed balancing index and other applicable requirements.

The commission maintained that it would not compromise its constitutional responsibility or overlook practices capable of undermining equitable representation in public institutions.

“Every qualified Nigerian deserves a fair opportunity to access public employment, irrespective of state of origin or geographical location,” it added.

The FCC reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring that fairness, equity and national inclusion are reflected in the recruitment practices of government institutions.

“Equity must be demonstrated in practice, not merely proclaimed in principle,” the Commission stated.

title: EPL: Arteta warns Arsenal players against leaking team news through FPL
description:
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has warned his players against inadvertently revealing sensitive team information through Fantasy Premier League (FPL), following an incident involving winger Christos Tzolis ahead of the club’s match against Liverpool.
The warning comes after Tzolis reportedly selected
content:
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has warned his players against inadvertently revealing sensitive team information through Fantasy Premier League (FPL), following an incident involving winger Christos Tzolis ahead of the club’s match against Liverpool.

The warning comes after Tzolis reportedly selected himself as captain in his Fantasy Premier League team before Arsenal’s encounter with Liverpool on November 1, despite having been sidelined for a month through injury.

As reported by BBC Sport on Friday, Arteta, speaking ahead of Saturday’s Premier League fixture against Newcastle United, disclosed that he had addressed the issue with his players and people close to the club to prevent further leaks of confidential team information.

“With Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well,” Arteta said.

“They’re constantly asking me about this as well, because they want to know. It’s a topic.”

Tzolis was subsequently named in Arsenal’s starting line-up at Anfield, making his first appearance since Greece’s Nations League draw with the Netherlands on October 1.

Arteta described the situation as a new challenge brought about by the growing popularity of fantasy football, stressing that the club would introduce measures to protect sensitive team information.

“This is the kind of thing that is happening in our society right now. It’s something new. We haven’t dealt with it before, and we need to put new things in place,” he said.

“Obviously, confidentiality is something critical because it’s about trust and about what you are trying to do, and that should be kept as a huge secret. We’ll take measures to make sure it doesn’t happen.”

The Spaniard also confirmed that Arsenal players are restricted from selecting themselves in their FPL teams, as the club seeks to prevent information about injuries and starting line-ups from becoming public before matches.

The development follows a similar incident involving Chelsea in October, when several FPL teams reportedly linked to club staff and players removed Brazilian striker Joao Pedro from their selections, raising speculation that he had sustained an injury.

The incidents have highlighted growing concerns among Premier League clubs over how fantasy football selections could unintentionally expose confidential information about team selection and player availability.

The post EPL: Arteta warns Arsenal players against leaking team news through FPL appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Nasarawa attracts $2.3bn investments in seven years – Official
description:
The Nasarawa State Government says it has attracted investments worth more than $2.3bn in seven years through business environment reforms, infrastructure development and public-private partnerships.
The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Nasarawa Investment and Development Agency,
content:
The Nasarawa State Government says it has attracted investments worth more than $2.3bn in seven years through business environment reforms, infrastructure development and public-private partnerships.

The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Nasarawa Investment and Development Agency, Ibrahim Abdullahi, disclosed this at the closing ceremony of the Global Alliance World Public Relations Forum in Abuja on Friday.

Abdullahi said the state had also implemented more than 21 reforms and facilitated 11 public-private partnership projects valued at about N93bn since Governor Abdullahi Sule assumed office in 2019.

He said Sule appointed him as economic adviser in 2019 with the responsibility of developing the state’s investment profile and creating an environment conducive to investment.

According to him, the state government focused on establishing institutional and economic structures to support investment before embarking on efforts to attract investors.

He said, “The first lesson from that very daunting task was to realise that you can’t give what you don’t have. So we could not go out and invite people to come to Nasarawa State without building any framework around it. You cannot communicate something that hasn’t been built. So, we put our heads down and began to build.

“Under the vision to make it one of the most competitive states in Nigeria, we focused on the enabling business environment. So, we implemented over 21 reforms, from digitising the revenue administration, improving the state’s fiscal and financial management framework, to ensuring that there is an institution that can back up these reforms and serve as a credible feedback mechanism between the investors, citizens and public service.

“We also implemented 11 public-private partnership projects worth about N93bn. Lastly, we also attracted investments worth over $2.3bn in seven years. These investments span across different sectors such as agriculture, solid minerals, retail, commercial, manufacturing, agro-processing and even education.”

The investments, according to Abdullahi, covered agriculture, solid minerals, retail, commercial activities, manufacturing, agro-processing and education.

He also spoke about the role of communication in building public institutions and sustaining economic development, urging public relations professionals to understand the objectives of the messages they convey.

Abdullahi said individuals and institutions needed to build and maintain their reputations to earn public trust.

“The second point is to say that your reputation matters much more than you can imagine. Your reputation is not just earned; you have to build it,” he said.

He also urged professionals to demonstrate courage, determination and solidarity in pursuing their ideas.

“The last message I wanted to communicate to you is that of courage and fraternity. There is no price tag for the best idea or for the next best idea,” he said.

The post Nasarawa attracts $2.3bn investments in seven years – Official appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Anthropic Falls More Than Nine Percent Day After Record IPO
description: Shares in Anthropic fell 9.5 percent in early trading Friday as the artificial intelligence company announced it had pocketed about $91.6 billion from its record-breaking initial public offering.The stock was changing hands at around $88 shortly after the opening bell in New York, down from Thursday
content:
Shares in Anthropic fell 9.5 percent in early trading Friday as the artificial intelligence company announced it had pocketed about $91.6 billion from its record-breaking initial public offering.

The stock was changing hands at around $88 shortly after the opening bell in New York, down from Thursday’s closing price of $97.17 but still above the $83 at which shares were priced in the IPO.

The pullback comes amid deep nervousness over AI stocks, which have swung sharply in recent weeks on fears of a bubble and doubts over whether the massive spending on the technology will pay off.

The shares had jumped 17 percent in their Nasdaq debut on Thursday despite a broad Wall Street sell-off, briefly valuing the maker of the Claude chatbot at about $2 trillion before closing at a valuation of about $1.75 trillion.

Nvidia, the chip giant at the center of the AI boom and an investor in Anthropic, has also been shaken by the resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang after an affair with a woman suspected by US intelligence to be a Chinese spy.

Anthropic said Friday that its underwriters had exercised in full their option to buy additional shares, lifting the total raised in the offering to about $93.5 billion.

About $1.9 billion of that went to existing shareholders who sold part of their stakes.

The final tally tops the $86 billion raised by Elon Musk’s SpaceX in its June listing, including its own additional shares, making Anthropic’s offering the largest IPO on record.

The company also raised about $26 billion by selling shares directly to a group of tech giants including Google, Microsoft and Nvidia, bringing the total haul from the listing to nearly $120 billion.

The listing, under the ticker “ANT,” made Anthropic the first of the leading AI model developers to go public, giving ordinary investors their first chance to bet directly on a stand-alone AI giant.

Founded in 2021 by siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei and several colleagues who left ChatGPT-maker OpenAI, the company has seen its revenue surge to $17 billion in the third quarter, up from $1.4 billion a year earlier.

Much of that comes from customers paying to use its models for computer coding, though its massive computing costs remain a major question for investors.

The company’s IPO filing warns that advanced AI systems could pose catastrophic or existential risks to society.

Critics accuse Anthropic of using its safety message as cover while it races to release ever more powerful technology.

title: Edo needs Tinubu’s second term to sustain development — Okpebholo
description:
Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, on Friday told party members, residents, and supporters that ongoing development in the state will continue only if the president stays in office.
Okpebholo stated this at the inauguration of the Edo State chapter of the PBAT Door-to-Door Campaign Moveme
content:
Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, on Friday told party members, residents, and supporters that ongoing development in the state will continue only if the president stays in office.

Okpebholo stated this at the inauguration of the Edo State chapter of the PBAT Door-to-Door Campaign Movement, a support group set up to canvass votes for the president’s re-election.

The governor said his administration’s achievements in the last two years were made possible by the backing Edo has received from the federal government.

“I am working because President Tinubu is behind me. For the work to continue, he must remain in office in 2027. A vote for Tinubu is a vote against kidnapping, cultism, and criminality in Edo State,” he said.

He promised the President 2.5 million votes from Edo State on January 16, 2027, and asked for the support and cooperation of voters across the state to meet the target.

“For me to continue to develop this state, President Tinubu must remain in Aso Rock,” the governor added.

He said the movement gives his team a platform to reach residents directly and explain the president’s record.

“Expect me in your neighborhood. I will visit you in your house and show you what our president has done in the last three and a half years,” he said.

The Grand Patron of the movement, High Chief Government Oweizide Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, represented by Engr. Kestin Pondi said the president had performed well and deserved another term to complete his development agenda.

Pondi disclosed that Tompolo had donated 25 campaign vehicles, along with speakers, generators, and amplifiers, for the re-election effort.

“We are in Edo State today to inaugurate the Edo chapter of the PBAT Door-to-Door Campaign Movement. The 25 vehicles will move from street to street and market to market to tell people what President Tinubu has done for Nigeria,” he said.

He admitted that times are hard but said the president is tackling the country’s challenges and gradually turning things around.

“Tinubu needs more time to complete the transformation he has started,” he said.

Pondi also said the President had stabilised the economy and the exchange rate, adding that Nigeria was now “on the threshold of growth.”

National Coordinator of the movement, Sunday Adekanbi, said the group was in Edo to inaugurate the chapter and begin house-to-house visits to assure residents that the president “means well” for the country.

He said Tinubu had confronted the fears of Nigerians and was working hard to change the country’s direction.

“The President is doing all he can to ensure Nigerians enjoy the dividends of democracy. The 36 state governors now have more money to work for their people, and investors are confident to invest in Nigeria,” Adekanbi said.

He urged Edo voters to turn out in large numbers for the president so that he could continue his development programmes for the state.

State Chairman of the Edo State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Mr Jarrett Tenebe said the party and the state government were working to deliver the 2.5 million votes promised the President.

“We are doing everything to give full support to the APC to win the general election. The President has given the South-South key appointments, and that is why we are throwing our weight behind him,” he said.

The mobilisation comes as political parties and support groups intensify preparations ahead of the 2027 general election, with the APC seeking to consolidate its position across the country and secure a second term for President Bola Tinubu.

Tinubu, who won the 2023 presidential election, is expected to face opposition from parties and political figures seeking to challenge his administration’s record on the economy, security and cost of living.

In Edo State, Okpebholo’s administration has aligned itself with the President, with the governor repeatedly acknowledging the Federal Government’s support for his development agenda. The APC also won the September 2024 governorship election in the state, ending the PDP’s eight-year hold on the Government House in Benin City.

The inauguration of the PBAT Door-to-Door Campaign Movement’s Edo chapter is part of efforts by Tinubu’s supporters to build grassroots support for his re-election bid through direct engagement with voters.

However, the governor’s pledge to deliver 2.5 million votes from Edo has set a major electoral target for the movement, which will have to persuade voters across the state’s 18 local government areas to support the President in 2027.

The post Edo needs Tinubu’s second term to sustain development — Okpebholo appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Galatasaray provides injury update on Osimhen, Leão, others
description:
Galatasaray have provided a fresh injury update on Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen and several other players, confirming that the Nigerian forward has started indoor training following arthroscopic surgery on his left knee last week.
In a post obtained from the club’s website on Friday, Galatasa
content:
Galatasaray have provided a fresh injury update on Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen and several other players, confirming that the Nigerian forward has started indoor training following arthroscopic surgery on his left knee last week.

In a post obtained from the club’s website on Friday, Galatasaray said Osimhen underwent the procedure last week and has now commenced rehabilitation under the supervision of the club’s physiotherapists after receiving medical treatment.

The club’s latest injury update also provided information on the recovery progress of Aleksey Batrakov, Davinson Sánchez, Roland Sallai, Ismail Jakobs, Uğurcan Çakır and Rafael Leão.

Batrakov, who sustained a blow to his right knee during Russia’s international match against Venezuela, returned to training with his teammates after receiving further treatment.

Colombia defender Sánchez has also resumed full training after suffering a left shoulder injury during his country’s encounter with Chile.

An MRI scan revealed a sprain involving the ligaments of his shoulder joint, accompanied by bleeding. However, following treatment, he successfully completed the full training session with the team.

Meanwhile, Hungary international Sallai has started treatment for a moderate left upper hamstring strain sustained during the warm-up before his country’s match against Northern Ireland.

MRI examinations confirmed a moderate muscle strain accompanied by bleeding.

Senegal defender Jakobs has also commenced treatment after experiencing pain in his left groin during shooting drills in training.

An MRI scan conducted at Acıbadem Hospital confirmed a moderate groin muscle strain with bleeding.

Goalkeeper Uğurcan Çakır, who experienced tightness in his right shoulder while on international duty, has returned to full training after receiving treatment.

The goalkeeper completed the full training sessions with his teammates on both days following his initial treatment.

Elsewhere, Portugal forward Leão is continuing his recovery programme at Aspetar in Doha, Qatar.

The forward will remain at the medical facility for 10 days under the supervision of his club’s physiotherapist as he follows an established treatment programme aimed at ensuring his full recovery.

The latest update shows that while some players have returned to full training, others, including Osimhen, remain under medical supervision as they continue their respective rehabilitation programmes.

title: Liverpool boss wary of Pochettino’s tactics ahead of Man Utd clash
description:
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola fears Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino will have an advantage over him on Sunday because he does not know the Argentinian’s preferred tactics with his new club.
Pochettino will be taking charge of United for the first time since leaving his role as USA natio
content:
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola fears Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino will have an advantage over him on Sunday because he does not know the Argentinian’s preferred tactics with his new club.

Pochettino will be taking charge of United for the first time since leaving his role as USA national team coach to replace the sacked Michael Carrick.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss has had limited time working with United’s players since arriving in Manchester this week.

That leaves Iraola guessing how Pochettino will deploy his team at Anfield.

“We’ve faced each other. Obviously he has a lot of Premier League games that we can look at, and we can look at games in the US, but they still have this small advantage,” Iraola told reporters on Friday.

“We don’t have references to prepare because they can go different ways that we don’t actually know.

“The staff have been working with them, so they are going to arrive well prepared. We don’t have the references that we have against other teams.”

Iraola will have to adapt on the fly and the Spaniard plans to switch up his game-plan if he is caught out by Pochettino’s tactics.

“Especially the beginning of the game will be important as we have to adapt to certain things and manage the situation as quick as possible,” he said.

“Every time there is a new manager you want to impress. It happens everywhere. But we have been focusing more on us, how we can improve.”

While Iraola would love to know Pochettino’s plans for his return to the Premier League, the Liverpool boss was quick to criticise the YouTube channel that used a drone to film part of a United training session this week.

“They were sending me the footage yesterday, but I think the important thing about this is that it shouldn’t be legal. It happened to Manchester United but it could happen to me in a training session in the future,” he said.

“It isn’t about the advantage, it is the fact that there is a reason we train behind closed doors because there are some things that you have to respect.”

Former Bournemouth boss Iraola will get his first taste of one of England’s fiercest rivalries when United arrive at Anfield.

Liverpool, who have not beaten United at home since 2023, sit in fourth place in the top-flight while their old foes are in the relegation zone after their worst start for 40 years.

“You don’t find bigger games than this honestly. I feel lucky to be here and privileged to be part of these games,” Iraola said.

“We have to acknowledge the importance of the game, and also a lot of ingredients, such as their new manager.

“It is important for us in lots of different ways because we want to improve our form at home and the first chance we have to do that is on Sunday.”

AFPx

The post Liverpool boss wary of Pochettino’s tactics ahead of Man Utd clash appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

“They were sending me the footage yesterday, but I think the important thing about this is that it shouldn’t be legal. It happened to Manchester United but it could happen to me in a training session in the future,” he said.

“It isn’t about the advantage, it is the fact that there is a reason we train behind closed doors because there are some things that you have to respect.”

Former Bournemouth boss Iraola will get his first taste of one of England’s fiercest rivalries when United arrive at Anfield.

Liverpool, who have not beaten United at home since 2023, sit in fourth place in the top-flight while their old foes are in the relegation zone after their worst start for 40 years.

“You don’t find bigger games than this honestly. I feel lucky to be here and privileged to be part of these games,” Iraola said.

“We have to acknowledge the importance of the game, and also a lot of ingredients, such as their new manager.

“It is important for us in lots of different ways because we want to improve our form at home and the first chance we have to do that is on Sunday.”

The post Liverpool Boss Iraola Admits Pochettino ‘Advantage’ in Man Utd Clash appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Canada jails two hockey players for sexually assaulting teenager
description:
Two young hockey players in Canada have each been sentenced to 40 months in prison for sexually assaulting a 17-year-old girl during an unwanted threesome at a Halloween party in Brampton, Ontario.
The two men, who were 18 at the time of the incident in 2023, were convicted of jointly sexually assau
content:
Two young hockey players in Canada have each been sentenced to 40 months in prison for sexually assaulting a 17-year-old girl during an unwanted threesome at a Halloween party in Brampton, Ontario.

The two men, who were 18 at the time of the incident in 2023, were convicted of jointly sexually assaulting the teenager at a private residence.

According to a report by the National Post on Friday, the victim’s identity and those of the offenders were protected, with the court identifying the men only by their initials.

In a sentencing decision delivered on November 3, Ontario Superior Court Justice J. Scott Cowan described the case as the joint sexual violation of a young girl by two youthful offenders who otherwise had excellent backgrounds.

The court heard that the teenager initially went into a bedroom with one of the men, where they engaged in consensual kissing before the encounter escalated.

The judge said he had significant reservations about whether she genuinely consented to the sexual activity that followed but was not satisfied beyond a reasonable doubt that a criminal offence had occurred during that initial encounter.

The situation changed when the second man joined them after receiving a telephone call from his friend, who told him, “It’s happening.”

The judge said the second man asked the teenager to perform oral sex on him, but the court was not satisfied beyond a reasonable doubt that the act constituted a criminal assault.

However, the court found that the criminal conduct began when the second man instructed his friend to “hit that from behind” while the teenager was performing oral s#x on him.

Cowan said the girl had not been consulted about the proposed sexual activity and had testified that she did not want to participate in a threesome.

The judge found that, despite her lack of consent, the men proceeded to subject her to simultaneous oral and vaginal penetration.

“For several minutes, the offenders alternated positions and each penetrated her orally and vaginally without her consent,” the judge said.

He added that the sexual activity was, at times, rough and degrading, noting that the teenager gagged and regurgitated during the encounter, while one of the men digitally scratched her inside her vagina and she sustained a visible bruise to her face.

The encounter ended “when one of the men asked whether she could continue and she responded that she could not.”

The judge also heard that other partygoers entered the bedroom after the incident and directed gendered and sexualised insults at the teenager while the two men did nothing to intervene.

Although Cowan described their failure to intervene as regrettable, he said he did not consider it an aggravating factor in sentencing.

The teenager promptly reported the assault and sought medical attention. Her facial bruise was photographed, while her testimony showed the psychological and emotional impact of the incident.

She told the court that the assault had affected every aspect of her identity and life, leaving her with feelings of powerlessness, depression, difficulty showing affection and vulnerability, and fears that the hurt might never end.

Both offenders had no previous criminal records and enjoyed the support of their families, friends and potential employers.

The judge also noted that both were skilled hockey players, adding that one had hoped to earn a living as an elite athlete before the offence and subsequent court proceedings derailed those ambitions.

The Crown had sought seven-year prison terms for both men, while their defence lawyers requested sentences at the lower end of the penitentiary range, citing their young ages and otherwise good backgrounds.

However, Cowan sentenced each of them to 40 months in prison, stressing that sentences for youthful first offenders should emphasise rehabilitation and, where necessary, individual deterrence.

He told the victim that the shorter sentences than those requested by the Crown did not diminish the suffering she had experienced or the profound effects of the offence.

The judge thanked her for putting her trust in the criminal justice system.

The two men will be eligible for full parole after serving one-third of their sentences, while they can qualify for day parole six months before then.

The post Canada jails two hockey players for sexually assaulting teenager appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Edo: Tinubu Must Remain In Office In 2027 For Work To Continue — Okpebholo
description: Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has said that the continued development of the state is tied to the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 elections, citing Federal Government support for his administration.The governor stated this on Friday during the inauguration of the Edo chapter
content:
Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has said that the continued development of the state is tied to the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 elections, citing Federal Government support for his administration.

The governor stated this on Friday during the inauguration of the Edo chapter of the PBAT Door-to-Door Campaign movement, a support group mobilising votes for the President’s second term.

Okpebholo said the achievements recorded by his administration in the last two years were made possible by the support of the Federal Government, insisting that Tinubu’s continued stay in office was critical to sustaining development in Edo.

“I am working because President Tinubu is behind me. For the work to continue, he must remain in office in 2027. A vote for Tinubu is a vote against kidnapping, cultism, and criminality in Edo State,” he said.

The governor pledged to deliver 2.5 million votes for Tinubu in Edo in the January 16, 2027 election, urging residents to support the target.

He said the door-to-door campaign would enable him to engage residents directly and explain the President’s achievements, promising to visit communities and households to canvass support.

The Grand Patron of the movement, Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, represented by Kestin Pondi, said the President deserved another term to complete his development agenda.

Pondi disclosed that Tompolo had donated 25 campaign vehicles, alongside speakers, generators and amplifiers, to support the mobilisation effort.

He said the vehicles would be deployed for grassroots campaigns across streets and markets to promote the President’s achievements, acknowledging the economic difficulties facing Nigerians but expressing confidence in the administration’s efforts to turn the situation around.

National Coordinator of the movement, Sunday Adekanbi, said the group was in Edo to inaugurate its chapter and commence house-to-house campaigns to convince residents of the President’s commitment to national development.

Adekanbi claimed that the Tinubu administration had improved economic stability, boosted investor confidence and increased allocations to state governments, urging Edo residents to support the President’s re-election.

The Edo State APC Chairman, Jarrett Tenebe, said the party and the state government were working to deliver the 2.5 million votes promised Tinubu, citing the President’s appointments and support for the South-South region as reasons for the party’s backing.

He assured the campaign movement of the party’s commitment to mobilising support for Tinubu and other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections.

The post Edo: Tinubu Must Remain In Office In 2027 For Work To Continue — Okpebholo appeared first on Channels Television.

title: JUST IN: NECO releases 2027 BECE guidelines, restricts registration to JSS 3 students
description:
The National Examinations Council (NECO) has released detailed guidelines for the registration of candidates for the 2027 Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE).
The Council announced the development in a circular shared on its official X handle on Friday.
The circular was addressed to all S
content:
The National Examinations Council (NECO) has released detailed guidelines for the registration of candidates for the 2027 Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE).

The Council announced the development in a circular shared on its official X handle on Friday.

The circular was addressed to all State Ministries of Education, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Education Secretariat, as well as principals and commandants of Junior Secondary Schools.

According to NECO, only students in their final year of Junior Secondary School (JSS 3) are eligible to register for the 2027 examination.

The Council issued the guidelines to provide information on the registration process and ensure that schools and relevant education authorities comply with the requirements for the examination.

“The examination is strictly for school-based candidates in Nigeria and overseas. Private candidates are not allowed,” NECO said

According to the council, schools must now mandatorily nominate prospective supervisors during the registration process, saying that registration cannot be completed without this step.

Every candidate will be issued a unique National Learners’ Identification Number (NLIN).

Possession of a valid National Identification Number (NIN) is compulsory for all candidates.

Transfer or admission of students into JSS 3 from other schools is prohibited.

NECO added that schools are required to correctly indicate candidates with special needs (including low vision, complete blindness, albinism, hearing impairment, and autism) during the offline bio-data entry. Official notification to NECO is required for candidates with autism.

“Schools must complete offline registration and validation before uploading data online. Candidates must verify their NIN, passport photograph, name, date of birth, gender, state of origin, local government area, and subjects. All corrections must be done offline. A signed Offline Validation List must be submitted to the NECO State Office,” NECO averred.

NECO warned that it will not be held responsible for registration errors made by schools. Double registration of candidates will not be entertained.

It, however, warned that any request for changes to passport photograph, name, date of birth, gender, subjects, state of origin, or LGA after online upload will attract a non-validation penalty of ₦10,000 per candidate.

“Change of passport photograph is only allowed before the end of the registration period, and only one change (name or photograph) is permitted.

“Schools must first be activated by their State Coordinator after submitting the required validation documents. All payments must be made into the NECO Treasury Single Account (TSA) via the Remita platform through the school’s NECO online portal. After successful payment and verification, a registration quota will be allocated to the school,” it added.

The Council advised schools paying in instalments to make the first payment for a minimum of 20 candidates. All payments are non-refundable.

NECO urged schools and education authorities to carefully study the guidelines and strictly comply with all procedures.

The post JUST IN: NECO releases 2027 BECE guidelines, restricts registration to JSS 3 students appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Ogun CP visits Odegbami after attack, vows to arrest attackers
description:
The Ogun State Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, has visited former Super Eagles captain and renowned sports administrator, Chief Segun Odegbami, following an attack at his residence in Abeokuta, assuring him that the perpetrators would be identified and brought to justice.
The visit was aimed a
content:
The Ogun State Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, has visited former Super Eagles captain and renowned sports administrator, Chief Segun Odegbami, following an attack at his residence in Abeokuta, assuring him that the perpetrators would be identified and brought to justice.

The visit was aimed at expressing the sympathy of the Ogun State Police Command over the incident and reassuring the former Nigerian international of the police’s commitment to protecting lives and property across the state.

The spokesperson for the state police command, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, disclosed this in a statement released on Friday.

During the visit, Ojajuni reportedly conveyed his concern over the incident and wished Odegbami continued recovery, while assuring him that the command was treating the matter with the seriousness it deserved.

The police commissioner disclosed that he had directed an immediate and comprehensive investigation into the incident to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack and identify those responsible.

He also assured the former football star that the command would deploy all necessary investigative resources to ensure that the perpetrators were apprehended and made to face the full weight of the law.

According to the police statement, Ojajuni reaffirmed the command’s determination to ensure that no stone was left unturned in the pursuit of justice.

The statement partly reads: “The Commissioner of Police, Ogun State Command, CP Bode Ojajuni, psc, FCSS, mnipr, has paid a visit to former Super Eagles captain and renowned sports administrator, Chief Segun Odegbami, to express the Command’s sympathy following the reported incident at his residence in Abeokuta.

“The Commissioner conveyed his concern and wished him continued recovery, reaffirming the Command’s commitment to protecting lives and property across the state.

“CP Ojajuni assured Chief Odegbami that the incident is receiving the Command’s utmost attention. He disclosed that he had ordered an immediate and thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident, while intensive investigative efforts are ongoing to identify and apprehend those responsible.

“He emphasised that the Command would leave no stone unturned in ensuring that the perpetrators are brought to justice.

“The Command confirms that Chief Odegbami has been discharged from the hospital and assures members of the public that all necessary steps are being taken to ensure a thorough investigation and appropriate action. Residents are encouraged to remain calm and provide credible information that could assist the investigation through established Police channels”.

Odegbami, who is the proprietor of Eagles 7 Sports Radio 103.7 FM, was reportedly attacked at about 2:30 am at his residence in Ibara GRA, Abeokuta.

Sources said the attackers, numbering three, arrived at the football legend’s home and first descended on his domestic staff and driver before invading his bedroom and inflicting deep machete cuts on him.

The post Ogun CP visits Odegbami after attack, vows to arrest attackers appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
