title: Osun federal health university appoints new VC
description:
The Governing Council of the Federal University of Health Sciences, Ila-Orangun, Osun State, has appointed a Professor of Public Health Entomology and Parasitology, Monsuru Adeleke, as the institution’s second Vice-Chancellor.
The announcement was made on Friday by the Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of
content:
The Governing Council of the Federal University of Health Sciences, Ila-Orangun, Osun State, has appointed a Professor of Public Health Entomology and Parasitology, Monsuru Adeleke, as the institution’s second Vice-Chancellor.

The announcement was made on Friday by the Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of Council, Prof. Wale Sulaiman, who addressed journalists on the university’s campus after a council meeting where the appointments were ratified.

Sulaiman said the university also appointed Dr Bolarinwa Feruke as Bursar, Dr Omowumi Ilori as Registrar and Prof. Elizabeth Adekanye as University Librarian.

He said Adeleke, who was the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Academic) before his appointment, and the other principal officers emerged after an extensive two-week selection process.

He said, “We advertised the minimum requirements for the principal officers. We had an extensive two-week selection process, interviews, interactions, and then final selections of the four principal officers, including the Vice-Chancellor of the Federal University of Health Sciences.

“For the Vice-Chancellorship, three finalists were scored over 100 marks. Prof. Kola Wahab scored 71.3 per cent, Prof. Musa Yakubu scored 72 per cent, while Prof. Monsuru Adebayo Adeleke scored 96.9 per cent to emerge as the winner.”

He commended the outgoing Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Akeem Lasisi, for his contributions to the development of the institution.

“Among the newly established federal universities of health sciences, the Ila-Orangun institution is the most advanced in terms of number of buildings, academic programmes and student enrolment. The outgoing Vice-Chancellor has done very well,” Sulaiman added.

In his remarks, Adeleke, an indigene of Igbo-Ora in Ibarapa Central Local Government Area of Oyo State, promised to govern without fear or favour and work towards building a smart campus.

He said the university would introduce innovative medical programmes, strengthen its research capacity and attract funding through grant-winning proposals, noting that the government alone could not fund education.

He said, “I am going to govern without any fear or favour. We are looking at a smart campus that is going to encompass everything. We want this university to serve as a differentiator. We are going to bring some innovative medical programmes to this university.

“We know that government alone cannot fund education. We need to think outside the box and bring innovative ways of getting the money that will be required to run this university effectively.

“The welfare of the staff will also be paramount. I am also going to make sure that nobody is denied their rightful entitlement as a staff member of this university. The same thing goes for the students. I am going to ensure that our students are attended to and their welfare is taken care of.”

The Federal Government appointed Lasisi as the pioneer Vice-Chancellor of the university in March 2022.

The post Osun federal health university appoints new VC appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: Opposition Coalition reschedules second summit to Nov 30
description:
The Coalition for Democracy, an alliance of six major opposition political parties in Nigeria, has postponed its second summit from Monday, November 23, to Monday, November 30, 2026.
The coalition said the decision was taken to accommodate the busy nationwide campaign schedules of its member parties
content:
The Coalition for Democracy, an alliance of six major opposition political parties in Nigeria, has postponed its second summit from Monday, November 23, to Monday, November 30, 2026.

The coalition said the decision was taken to accommodate the busy nationwide campaign schedules of its member parties ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The change of date was announced in a statement issued on Friday in Abuja by the Convener of the G100 and signatory on behalf of the coalition parties, Malam Salihu Moh. Lukman.

According to the statement, the coalition’s Central Leadership Committee approved the postponement following requests from some member parties.

The requests were reportedly made because their presidential candidates and campaign teams are currently engaged in intensive mobilisation activities across the country.

The coalition said the adjustment would allow the affected parties to manage their campaign commitments while preparing for the summit.

Explaining the rationale behind the postponement, the Committee emphasised that securing the physical presence of all key political actors outweighed holding the gathering on its previously announced date.

“It is more important that every party, every presidential candidate and every national chairman is in the room than that the Summit holds on its original date,” the Committee stated.

To guarantee full participation at the rescheduled event—earlier slated for the NAF Conference Centre in Abuja—all participating political parties have resolved to temporarily halt their electioneering activities across the federation on the new date.

“In consultation with key stakeholders, the Committee has agreed on 30 November to secure the widest possible participation. To make that commitment real, all member parties have agreed to suspend campaign activities nationwide on Monday, 30 November, so that their leadership can attend the Summit in full,” the statement read.

Describing the agreement to pause politicking as a deliberate demonstration of collective resolve, the coalition noted that safeguarding Nigeria’s democratic space supersedes individual partisan ambitions.

“That decision is itself a statement. Parties competing hard for votes are prepared to stand down their campaigns for a day, together, because the defence of Nigeria’s democratic space is bigger than any one campaign,” the Committee added.

At the November 30 gathering, opposition leaders are expected to finalise and formally sign the coalition’s common agreement—a Covenant for Democratic Renewal—while mapping out a coordinated strategy ahead of the January 16, 2027 elections.

“We will walk into that room united, and walk out of it committed,” the Committee assured.

While apologising to delegates, party leaders, and partners for any inconvenience caused by the rescheduling, the Committee confirmed that the previously communicated venue and accreditation arrangements remain unchanged. It said it would provide further updates to delegates and the media in due course.

Emerging from the inaugural G100 Opposition Summit held in Abuja on August 31, 2026, the Coalition for Democracy is spearheaded by six political parties: the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), and Social Democratic Party (SDP). The platform aims to foster opposition coordination, defend constitutional democracy, uphold the rule of law, and safeguard the credibility of the 2027 electoral process.

title: Babcock varsity matriculates 3,820, warns against drug abuse
description:
The President/Vice-Chancellor of Babcock University, Ilishan-Remo, Ogun State, Professor Afọlarin Ojewole, has charged newly admitted students to uphold discipline, integrity and academic excellence, warning them against drug abuse, examination malpractice, cultism and negative peer pressure.
Ojewol
content:
The President/Vice-Chancellor of Babcock University, Ilishan-Remo, Ogun State, Professor Afọlarin Ojewole, has charged newly admitted students to uphold discipline, integrity and academic excellence, warning them against drug abuse, examination malpractice, cultism and negative peer pressure.

Ojewole gave the charge on Friday during the university’s undergraduate matriculation ceremony held at the University Amphitheatre, Ilishan-Remo, where a total of 3,820 students, including 550 part-time students, were formally admitted into various first-degree programmes.

Addressing the matriculating students, the Vice-Chancellor described the ceremony as more than a formal university tradition, saying it represented a commitment to the institution’s values, academic responsibilities and broader mission of producing graduates equipped to contribute meaningfully to society.

He urged the students to make purposeful use of the opportunities available to them, noting that their eventual success would depend significantly on their commitment, diligence and willingness to embrace personal development.

Ojewole stated that the university’s educational philosophy went beyond the award of academic certificates to the development of individuals with sound knowledge, moral conviction, practical competence, leadership abilities and concern for humanity.

“At Babcock University, we believe education must go beyond the acquisition of certificates. We are interested in the whole person. We want you to graduate with strong academic knowledge, strong moral conviction and practical competence, leadership capability and genuine concern for the welfare of other people,” he stated.

He, however, reminded the students that providing opportunities was only one part of the university’s responsibility, insisting that they must take personal responsibility for maximising the resources available to them.

The Vice-Chancellor urged the matriculating students to attend lectures regularly, arrive early, respect lecturers and other members of the university community, participate actively in academic activities and develop the habit of reading beyond their lecture notes.

While charging the newly admitted students, Prof Ojewole said, “Please come to class. Come early. You have heard the saying that first class begins with a first class. So come prepared to learn. Respect your lecturer.

“Respect the rules. Respect your colleagues and every member of staff. Be punctual. Participate actively in academic activities. Ask probing questions. It’s okay to do so here in Babcock,”

He added, “Do not allow the desire for quick success to compromise your integrity. Reject examination malpractice, plagiarism, bullying, violence, cultism, drug use and every form of misconduct that undermines the values of this institution and the great values that you were brought up with.

“Don’t let no one deter you from your goal. Let no one make you stray from the path. Don’t let no one pump you up to do wrong. They may come to you with emotional manipulation. Please don’t listen.

“Your character is as important to us as your academic performance. Indeed, when the applause of graduation is over and the certificate is free, it is your character that will sustain you at the top and speak for you everywhere.”

Ojewole assured the students that the university had support structures, including pastors, chaplains, faculty members, advisers, counsellors and the Student Support Centre, to provide assistance and guidance.

He emphasised that students in need could seek help confidentially and would not be subjected to public embarrassment for opening up about their struggles, urging them not to suffer in silence.

Addressing parents and guardians, the Vice-Chancellor acknowledged their sacrifices, prayers, financial commitments and personal investments in securing admission for their children.

He thanked them for entrusting the university with the responsibility of educating and nurturing their wards, describing students’ success as a shared responsibility between the institution and their families.

Ojewole said the university remained committed to producing globally relevant, research-focused and data-driven graduates who would retain their Seventh-day Adventist identity and uphold high ethical standards.

The post Babcock varsity matriculates 3,820, warns against drug abuse appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: BREAKING: Court sacks Atiku’s ally Tukur Ribadu as Adamawa ADC guber candidate, orders INEC to restore Omar Suleiman candidacy
description: The Federal High Court in Abuja has sacked Hamman Tukur Modibbo Ribadu as the African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate for Adamawa State and directed the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to recognise Ambassador Omar Suleiman as the party’s rightful candidate for the 2
content:
The Federal High Court in Abuja has sacked Hamman Tukur Modibbo Ribadu as the African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate for Adamawa State and directed the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to recognise Ambassador Omar Suleiman as the party’s rightful candidate for the 2027 election.

The ruling followed a legal dispute over the party’s governorship ticket after Suleiman, who claimed to have won the ADC primary, was replaced by Ribadu.

Suleiman had challenged the substitution, insisting that he emerged victorious in the party’s primary election and that there was no legal basis for replacing him.

The court reportedly held that a candidate who had emerged from a primary election could not be substituted unless the candidate had formally withdrawn from the race or died.

On that basis, the court ordered INEC to restore Suleiman’s name as the ADC’s governorship candidate for Adamawa State.

The dispute had generated tension within the party, particularly following the emergence of Ribadu as the candidate listed by INEC.

Suleiman is a cousin of former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Babachir Lawal, who had also criticised the reported attempt to replace him.

The development is another twist in the ADC’s internal disagreements ahead of the 2027 general elections.

title: Tension as gunmen storm NDC secretariat, attack candidates, destroy party materials in Edo
description:
Armed men suspected to be members of the Edo State Security Network (ESSN) have attacked members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), including some of the party’s candidates in Edo State.
The Edo State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement issued on Friday by its Police Public R
content:
Armed men suspected to be members of the Edo State Security Network (ESSN) have attacked members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), including some of the party’s candidates in Edo State.

The Edo State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement issued on Friday by its Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Eno Ikoedem.

According to the police spokesperson, the NDC senatorial candidate for Edo North, Mrs Iseme Maria Oisamoje, and other party candidates were holding a meeting at the party’s secretariat when the armed men reportedly stormed the facility.

The attackers were said to have arrived with guns and machetes, disrupting the meeting and attacking members of the party.

According to the command’s spokesperson, the incident occurred on Thursday, November 19.

The PPRO also confirmed that the assailants “destroyed political banners and other materials within the Secretariat, while threatening to kill the occupants before fleeing upon sighting the Police”.

“The Command has commenced investigation into the incident and is making concerted efforts to identify, locate and apprehend all persons involved in the attack,” Ikoedem said.

She added that the Local Government Chairman of Owan East Local Government Area, Ernest Oyaole Aitalegbe, has been invited in connection with the incident to assist the ongoing investigation.

title: INEC makes 86,931 PVCs available for collection in Kogi
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has announced that 86,931 Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) are ready for collection by residents who participated in the second phase of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise in Kogi State.
The State Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC), D
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has announced that 86,931 Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) are ready for collection by residents who participated in the second phase of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise in Kogi State.

The State Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC), Dr. Shehu Wahab, disclosed this in a press statement made available to journalists in Lokoja on Friday.

According to the commission, the second phase of the CVR exercise was conducted between January 5 and April 17, 2026.

INEC said, “The 86,931 PVCs produced for eligible registrants have been delivered to our offices across the 21 Local Government Areas of the state and are now ready for collection.”

The commission urged all eligible registrants to visit the INEC office in the Local Government Area where they completed their registration to collect their Permanent Voter Cards.

The commission also emphasised the need for registrants to collect their cards to enable them to participate in future elections.

‎‎It said registrants are expected to come with their registration slips or printouts, or a valid means of identification where required.

‎‎INEC also clarified that PVCs from the first phase of the registration exercise are still available for collection.

‎‎”PVCs would not be issued through proxies, registrants must personally collect their cards. Collection is available at INEC LGA offices from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m., Monday to Friday.”

‎The commission further directed registrants to check the status of their PVCs and locate their collection centres through its CVR portal, cvr.inecnigeria.org.

‎‎INEC urged all voters who participated in the second phase of the CVR exercise to collect their PVCs without delay, noting that the cards are essential for participation in future elections.

‎‎The commission said timely collection would help ensure that no eligible voter is disenfranchised.

‎‎Wahab expressed appreciation to registrants for their patience during the production, verification and distribution processes, assuring that the commission remained committed to ensuring that every eligible voter obtains a PVC and is able to exercise their democratic right.

The post INEC makes 86,931 PVCs available for collection in Kogi appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Jigawa Shari’a judges warned against unnecessary detention
description:
The Acting Grand Kadi of the Jigawa State Shari’a Court of Appeal, Kadi Umar Nasir Ahmad, has cautioned Shari’a Court judges (Alkalis) against unnecessary remand of accused persons in civil cases, particularly those involving monetary claims.
The warning was given during an official tour of some Sha
content:
The Acting Grand Kadi of the Jigawa State Shari’a Court of Appeal, Kadi Umar Nasir Ahmad, has cautioned Shari’a Court judges (Alkalis) against unnecessary remand of accused persons in civil cases, particularly those involving monetary claims.

The warning was given during an official tour of some Shari’a Courts across the state as part of his familiarisation visits to assess their operational efficiency and engage staff on best practices.

In a statement made available to PUNCH correspondent in Dutse, the Jigawa State capital, on Thursday, the Director of Information and Protocol Matters of the Jigawa State Judicial Service Commission, Abbas Wangara, said the tour was aimed at strengthening the administration of justice across the state.

According to Wangara, the tour took the Acting Grand Kadi to Yalo Shari’a Court, Kaugama Shari’a Court, Madana Shari’a Court, Upper and Higher Shari’a Court Malam-Madori, Upper and Higher Shari’a Court Birniwa, Kirikasamma Shari’a Court, and Guri Shari’a Court.

Addressing the Alkalis, Kadi Ahmad charged them to desist from unnecessary remand of accused persons brought before them in civil suits.

Wangara said the Acting Grand Kadi specifically warned against remand in civil suits, particularly monetary claims, unless otherwise.

“He emphasised the need for judicious exercise of remand powers, warning that detaining accused persons in civil matters is contrary to the principles of justice,” Kadi Ahmad said.

The Acting Grand Kadi also drew the attention of court registrars and clerks to the importance of maintaining records of fines awarded through court decisions, while acknowledging that the judiciary was not a revenue-generating institution.

“He urged them to be prudent and transparent in the discharge of their official duties,” Wangara said.

Wangara further said Kadi Ahmad warned court staff to be more punctual, dedicated and hardworking to meet the yearnings and aspirations of litigants.

“He stressed that the Judiciary remains the last hope of the common man,” Wangara said.

Similarly, the Chief Registrar of the Shari’a Court of Appeal, Barr. Kabiru Abubakar Gumel, urged staff to update their records and other relevant documents to ensure the smooth running of their official duties.

“He urged them to avoid absenteeism without genuine reasons,” Wangara said.

The statement further read, “the tour showcased the commitment of the Jigawa State Shari’a Court of Appeal to ensuring effective and efficient administration of justice across the state.”

The Acting Grand Kadi was accompanied on the tour by the Chief Inspector of Shari’a Courts, Barr. Isma’il Sani; the Deputy Chief Inspector, Hadejia Zone, Barr. Isyak Mohd; and other principal officers of the Shari’a Court of Appeal.

title: My grandchildren couldn’t get passports before Tinubu’s reforms – Oshiomhole
description:
The Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, on Friday disclosed that his grandchildren were among Nigerians who had been unable to obtain Nigerian passports before recent reforms by the Ministry of Interior.
He said their eventual success in getting the documents was proof that the Renewed
content:
The Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, on Friday disclosed that his grandchildren were among Nigerians who had been unable to obtain Nigerian passports before recent reforms by the Ministry of Interior.

He said their eventual success in getting the documents was proof that the Renewed Hope Agenda was yielding tangible results.

Oshiomhole, who chairs the Senate Committee on Interior, spoke at the groundbreaking ceremony for the National Passport Booklet Production Centre at the Nigeria Immigration Service headquarters in Abuja.

He said, “They tell me, Grandpa, now I have Nigeria passport. So these are not in the advert; they are real stories that speak to what is changing, the real meaning of Renewed Hope.”

He recalled how Nigerians in the diaspora had been left stranded, unable to visit their families at home because their passports had expired and could not be renewed.

He credited the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, with resolving the crisis within months of assuming office.

“Within months of the honourable minister’s assumption of office, these issues were dealt with and dealt with satisfactorily,” Oshiomhole said, adding that the complaints had come from Nigerians in America, Europe and Asia.

He added, “If a man couldn’t get a passport, even as a Nigerian who wants to come home as a patriot, he couldn’t. He was being frustrated by the incompetence of the Nigerian state.

“And now that Nigeria is celebrating, has renewed his hope in our country, the Renewed Hope Agenda, I believe, is what is being translated here and now.”

The lawmaker also noted the significance of the new production centre as Nigeria’s first domestic passport booklet printing facility, saying the country would produce the booklets not only at the Abuja facility but also at additional locations.

The ceremony was attended by Tunji-Ojo, Oshiomhole and the Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Interior, Abdullahi Ahmed.

Also present were representatives of the Controller-General of Customs, the Controller-General of the Nigerian Correctional Service, the Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, the Director-General of the Federal Fire Service and senior officials of the NIS management team, among other dignitaries.

title: Court Rejects Atiku’s Bid to Tender Fresh Evidence In Suit Seeking Tinubu’s Disqualification
description: Justice Inyang Ekwo of the Federal High Court in Abuja has dismissed an application by former Vice President and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, to present fresh evidence in his suit seeking to prevent President Bola Tinubu from contesting the 2027 presi
content:
Justice Inyang Ekwo of the Federal High Court in Abuja has dismissed an application by former Vice President and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, to present fresh evidence in his suit seeking to prevent President Bola Tinubu from contesting the 2027 presidential election over allegations of forgery of his National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) discharge certificate.

The judge held that the time allowed by law to present evidence in a pre-election suit was 14 days, in line with Section 285(9) of the 1999 Constitution.

Justice Ekwo agreed with Tinubu and the other defendants that allowing Atiku to introduce fresh evidence would alter the nature of the original case and violate the provisions of the Constitution.

In his ruling on Atiku’s application to amend the originating summons in the suit against Tinubu, the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), the judge held that the former vice president attempted to mislead the court by claiming that the proposed amendment would not introduce fresh issues.

Justice Ekwo said that, after carefully examining the application, the court found that the ADC presidential candidate sought to substitute existing evidence with new evidence which, if allowed, would circumvent Section 285(9) of the Constitution, which requires such evidence to be presented within 14 days.

According to the judge, allowing Atiku to introduce fresh evidence through the back door would amount to a fundamental injustice against the defendants.

Meanwhile, following an agreement among the lawyers, the judge fixed December 2 for the hearing of the substantive suit.

Atiku had told the court that he needed to make substantial amendments to his case challenging Tinubu’s eligibility to participate in the 2027 presidential election.

In the main suit, Atiku and the ADC asked Justice Ekwo to disqualify Tinubu and the APC from the 2027 presidential election.

They challenged the authenticity of Tinubu’s NYSC discharge certificate submitted to INEC by the APC.

The plaintiffs, who sued the president, the APC and INEC as the first to third defendants, respectively, in an originating summons marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1888/2026, alleged that the APC submitted a forged NYSC discharge certificate belonging to the president to INEC.

They, therefore, asked the court to compel INEC to remove Tinubu’s name and that of the APC from the list of candidates and political parties for the presidential election.

However, Tinubu and the APC, in a joint counter-affidavit filed on September 9, urged the court to dismiss the suit in its entirety for being incompetent, arguing that the plaintiffs lacked the legal right to institute the case.

They denied submitting any forged certificate to INEC for either the 2023 or 2027 presidential elections.

The duo, through the APC’s Director of Legal Services, Sanusi Samaila, said they did not submit any Form CF001 to INEC for the 2023 or 2027 elections, as claimed by the plaintiffs.

They also maintained that the NYSC had never denied issuing the discharge certificate to the first defendant at the end of his service year.

They argued that it was settled law that the evidence required to establish that a certificate was forged was a disclaimer from the institution alleged to have issued it. They cited a previous Supreme Court decision in support of their argument.

They urged the court to uphold their preliminary objection and dismiss the suit.

INEC, in a preliminary objection filed on September 7 through its lawyer, Alex Izinyon, SAN, also challenged the competence of the suit because it was statute-barred, that the plaintiffs lacked locus standi, and that there was no reasonable cause of action and an abuse of court process.

The commission argued that the plaintiffs failed to comply with the mandatory written deposition requirement under Paragraph 7(1) of the Federal High Court Pre-Election Practice Directions (Amendment) 2026.

INEC also challenged the propriety of Reliefs 2 and 3 in Atiku and the ADC’s originating summons, urging the court to dismiss the suit.

Atiku and the ADC, however, filed a motion on notice on September 10, seeking to amend the suit.

The post Court Rejects Atiku’s Bid to Tender Fresh Evidence In Suit Seeking Tinubu’s Disqualification appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Fountain of Life Church dismisses closure claims, announces Sunday service
description:
The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos, has urged members and the public to disregard reports suggesting that its premises have been sealed, inviting worshippers to its Sunday service amid the ongoing leadership crisis involving Pastor Jimmy Odukoya.
The church, in a post shared on its official
content:
The Fountain of Life Church, Ilupeju, Lagos, has urged members and the public to disregard reports suggesting that its premises have been sealed, inviting worshippers to its Sunday service amid the ongoing leadership crisis involving Pastor Jimmy Odukoya.

The church, in a post shared on its official X account on Friday, said its Sunday service would hold at 9am, encouraging members to attend physically or participate online.

“Don’t believe the noise; church is not sealed, see you in church on Sunday,” the church wrote in its flyer.

In a separate message accompanying the post, it invited worshippers to its 9am service, saying, “Don’t believe the noise! Join us for service every Sunday at TFOLC. There’s a place for you, you can join us in person or online! 9AM WAT. We look forward to welcoming you!”

However, the development should be distinguished from the recent court proceedings, as the certified true copy of the court order did not direct the closure or sealing of the church premises.

PUNCH Online had reported that the Lagos State High Court restrained Jimmy Odukoya from holding himself out as the Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of the church, following an application by the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church.

Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin made the interim orders on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, in a suit filed by the church’s trustees.

The court also restrained Odukoya, whether acting personally or through proxies, from interfering with, disrupting or obstructing the church’s activities, governance and other business.

The orders were made ex parte, meaning they were granted without first hearing Odukoya’s response to the application.

The court, however, expressly preserved his right to apply to have the orders set aside or respond to the substantive claims after being served with the court processes.

The case was adjourned until December 1, 2026, for mention.

The leadership dispute became public on November 17 when a faction of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that Odukoya was no longer recognised as senior pastor, citing a succession video recorded by the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, in December 2021.

The trustees subsequently named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader.

However, Jimmy and the church leadership rejected the decision, insisting that his appointment as senior pastor in September 2023 was valid.

Meanwhile, the church had separately announced the postponement of its 2026 Thanksgiving Service, earlier scheduled for Sunday, November 22, saying a new date would be communicated.

The latest invitation to its regular Sunday service indicates that the church is still asking worshippers to attend its weekly gathering despite the controversy surrounding its leadership.

The post Fountain of Life Church dismisses closure claims, announces Sunday service appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: ‘That’s Not What’s Driving Me’: Tonye Cole Denies Trading Support For Future APC Governorship Ticket
description: Former Rivers State governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Tonye Cole, has denied that his decision to support the party’s political arrangement ahead of the 2027 elections was motivated by a promise of a future governorship ticket.Cole said his priority was to change t
content:
Former Rivers State governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Tonye Cole, has denied that his decision to support the party’s political arrangement ahead of the 2027 elections was motivated by a promise of a future governorship ticket.

Cole said his priority was to change the perception of Rivers State as a place associated with violence and political strongmen, arguing that peace and security were essential to attracting investment to the state.

He spoke on Friday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief, where he was asked whether he had been promised an opportunity to pursue his governorship ambition in the future.

“No, and that is not what is driving me,” he replied.

“What is driving me is that if you cannot bring peace and security and change the narrative of Rivers State, investment will not come to Rivers State. So the first aspect of it is that we must change the mindset of everyone that when they talk about Rivers State, violence, strongman, no gentlemen, loud, all of that tagline must change.

“If I cannot be the face of what the future of Rivers State politics should look like, then we have a problem,” he added.

Cole, who emerged as the APC governorship candidate in 2019 and 2023, withdrew from the party’s 2027 governorship race in May following consultations and efforts to reconcile rival factions within the state chapter.

He subsequently aligned with the Rainbow Coalition, a cross-party political arrangement led by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, which is backing President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid.

Explaining his decision to remain with the APC group that predated the current political arrangement, Cole said he wanted to ensure that members who had worked to build the party were not sidelined.

“For me, abandoning those who were in APC who worked was not the question. So I decided that I was going to stay with them so that they would have a voice. They cannot be removed, so I stayed there to represent the voice of the APC that built forth and kept Rivers State whole,” he said.

He added that the decision to bring different political interests together was informed by the need to prevent divisions that had previously weakened the APC in Rivers State.

‘No Differences With Wike’

Wike holds near-total control over the formal political institutions and party structures in Rivers State. There was intense, public friction and even a defamation lawsuit between Cole and the FCT minister before they reconciled to form the Rainbow Coalition.

Cole, speaking further, said he and Wike had put their past disagreements behind them and were now working towards a common political objective.

“I believe politics is about sacrifice. There is no politician who does not have scars. But you have to be looking at the future. So today, Nyesom Wike and I do not have any differences.

“What was in the past was in the past. We settled it towards the future. Now we have a common goal that the APC win the ballot in 2027,” he said.

The coalition, on October 27, unveiled its endorsed candidates for the 2027 elections at the Yakubu Gowon Stadium in Port Harcourt, with Kingsley Chinda emerging as its preferred governorship candidate under the APC.

Cole said the objective was to change the state’s political image and make it more attractive to investors.

“We want to remove that tagline that Rivers State is a violent state,” he added.

The post ‘That’s Not What’s Driving Me’: Tonye Cole Denies Trading Support For Future APC Governorship Ticket appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Stop recycling falsehoods against Tinubu, Lagos APC tells Pearse
description:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni



The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has slammed Dr. Adetokunbo Pearse over his recent series of interviews allegedly maligning and disparaging President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.



Lagos State APC Spokesman, Seye Oladejo, who made the remark, described th
content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has slammed Dr. Adetokunbo Pearse over his recent series of interviews allegedly maligning and disparaging President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

Lagos State APC Spokesman, Seye Oladejo, who made the remark, described the statement as “an obsessive campaign of calumny,” against the President.

The party said it would ordinarily have ignored the outbursts as a desperate attempt by a politically stranded individual to remain relevant, but added that the frequency, desperation and recycled nature of the allegations made it necessary to set the records straight.

“There is something particularly unfortunate about a man who appears incapable of moving beyond yesterday’s political arguments, even when the issues he continues to resurrect have been exhaustively examined, contested and addressed through established legal and judicial processes,” the party stated.

The APC said repetition does not transform an allegation into evidence, neither does the frequency with which a falsehood is circulated confer credibility upon it.

“The Nigerian public is not obliged to accept recycled accusations simply because they are delivered with theatrical confidence in television studios,” it said.

The party questioned how Pearse’s purported knowledge of the President’s academic history could be conclusive when, by his own account, he served at Chicago State University between 1985 and 1990, whereas President Tinubu’s academic records establish that he attended the institution between 1977 and 1979.

“How does a lecturer who arrived at an institution six years after a student’s graduation become the ultimate authority on whether that student ever attended the institution?” the party asked.

It described the discrepancy as not minor, saying “it goes to the very foundation of his latest claims,” adding that one would expect an academic of his purported standing to appreciate the importance of chronology, documentary evidence and elementary standards of verification.

The party noted that the Chicago State University controversy is not a matter left to speculation, as the university itself has repeatedly confirmed President Tinubu’s attendance and graduation in 1979.

It recalled that its Registrar, Caleb Westberg, also testified under oath in October 2023, confirming that the university’s official academic records showed that Bola Ahmed Tinubu graduated on June 22, 1979, with a degree in Business Administration.

“These were not whispers in political corridors or claims made by hired political communicators. They were official institutional records and sworn testimony produced in the course of proceedings initiated at the instance of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar,” the party said.

The APC said a responsible public commentator cannot conveniently ignore the university’s confirmation while presenting personal recollections, particularly recollections from a period several years after the President had left the institution, as conclusive evidence.

It added that the Nigerian electoral litigation over the President’s election has run its course, stressing that democracy cannot function on the principle that every concluded political and judicial contest must be endlessly reopened whenever an aggrieved partisan finds a new television platform from which to relitigate.

The party urged Pearse to invest his intellectual energy in issues that matter to Nigerians rather than remain imprisoned by a controversy he seems determined never to abandon.

“We sincerely hope he finds the courage to move on. After all, politics is ultimately about the future, and no one can successfully lead a people while permanently looking backwards,” it said.

“Enough of the manufactured outrage. Enough of the recycled allegations. Nigeria deserves better, and the road to 2027 will be determined by ideas, performance and the confidence of the electorate, not by the loudest purveyors of yesterday’s grievances,” APC stated.

The post Stop recycling falsehoods against Tinubu, Lagos APC tells Pearse appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Uche Nnaji: HURIWA accuses ICPC of political persecution, demands halt to prosecution
description:
… Alleges plot to weaken Mbah’s political challenger… Warns against weaponising anti-graft agencies ahead of 2027 elections



By Chioma Obinna



The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) on Friday accused the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC)
content:
… Alleges plot to weaken Mbah’s political challenger
… Warns against weaponising anti-graft agencies ahead of 2027 elections

By Chioma Obinna

The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) on Friday accused the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) of using its prosecution of former Minister of Science, Technology and Innovation, Uche Nnaji, to advance political interests in Enugu State, demanding an immediate halt to the case pending an independent review.

The rights group alleged that the continued prosecution of Nnaji, amid the controversy surrounding his academic qualifications, raises serious questions about the neutrality and independence of the anti-corruption agency, particularly as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general elections.

In a press statement signed by its National Coordinator, Comrade Emmanuel Nnadozie Onwubiko, HURIWA warned that criminal prosecution must not become an instrument for intimidating opposition figures, weakening political challengers or protecting incumbent office holders.

The association alleged that Nnaji’s prosecution increasingly bears the appearance of a political project designed to undermine one of the formidable challengers to Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah.

It claimed that the former minister remains one of the few politicians capable of mounting a serious challenge to Mbah’s political dominance, raising concerns that state institutions could be deployed to influence the state’s political landscape.

HURIWA said: “The ICPC must stop this prosecution if it cannot convincingly establish that the process is independent, evidence-driven and free from political considerations. Nigerians must not allow persecution to disguise itself as prosecution.”

The group maintained that while allegations against Nnaji should be subjected to lawful investigation and accountability, they must not provide a justification for selective deployment of state institutions against political actors.

It also recalled that Nnaji had approached the Federal High Court to compel the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, to release his academic transcript, noting that the controversy surrounding his academic records remained contentious.

According to HURIWA, the circumstances surrounding the investigation and prosecution require closer scrutiny to ensure that the anti-corruption agency is not acting on political considerations.

The association further accused the Federal Government of failing to prevent anti-corruption institutions from operating in ways that could intimidate perceived political opponents and distort the country’s multiparty democratic process.

Invoking the democratic principles underpinning the Electoral Act 2022, HURIWA argued that political competition must be free from intimidation, coercion and abuse of institutional power.

It specifically cited Sections 126 and 127 of the Act, which address electoral offences involving force, violence, restraint, voter influence and corrupt practices, arguing that public institutions must uphold the principles of free political participation.

The group warned that the use of criminal investigations and prosecutions to frustrate political opponents could create an atmosphere of fear and exclusion capable of undermining the credibility of the 2027 elections.

It therefore called on the ICPC to immediately suspend Nnaji’s prosecution pending an independent examination of the circumstances surrounding the case.

HURIWA also urged the Federal Government to rein in any institution found to be weaponising its investigative or prosecutorial powers against perceived political opponents.

The association warned that allowing anti-corruption agencies to become instruments of partisan political battles would erode public confidence in their operations, deepen political tensions in Enugu State and threaten democratic competition.

It stressed that the fight against corruption must be conducted without discrimination, insisting that no anti-corruption agency should become a tool for protecting incumbents or weakening their political challengers.

The group said the credibility of the ICPC depended on demonstrating that its actions were guided strictly by evidence, due process and the rule of law, rather than political interests.

The post Uche Nnaji: HURIWA accuses ICPC of political persecution, demands halt to prosecution appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: David Mark seeks renaming of FUT Minna after pioneer VC
description:
The National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress, David Mark, has called on the Niger State Government to rename the Federal University of Technology, Minna, after its late pioneer Vice-Chancellor, Professor Jonathan Ndagi.
Mark made the call on Thursday during a funeral service for Ndagi at
content:
The National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress, David Mark, has called on the Niger State Government to rename the Federal University of Technology, Minna, after its late pioneer Vice-Chancellor, Professor Jonathan Ndagi.

Mark made the call on Thursday during a funeral service for Ndagi at St Peter’s Anglican Church in Minna, the Niger State capital.

The former Senate President said the country had lost a great Nigerian but had not lost his legacies, adding that the proposal was in recognition of the late professor’s contributions to education and humanity.

He said Ndagi’s ideals would continue to endure, while the institutions he helped build would serve future generations.

“Professor Ndagi was a great educationist who contributed to ensure that the country prioritised education. Niger State deserves to name FUT Minna after the professor to keep his legacy alive,” he said.

Mark also commiserated with the Niger State Government, the people of the state and Nigerians over the death, describing the late educationist’s life as a lesson in service to humanity.

The funeral service was attended by hundreds of sympathisers, including the ADC governorship candidate in Niger State, Dr Mohammed Kpautagi, religious leaders and members of the academic community.

Ndagi was the pioneer Vice-Chancellor of FUT Minna, serving from 1983 to 1990. The university, established in 1983, is a Federal Government-owned institution specialising in science, engineering and technology education.

During his tenure, Ndagi oversaw the institution’s formative years. The university’s recent tribute to him also recalled his role in securing 10,800 hectares of land for its permanent campus at Gidan-Kwano.

Ndagi died on October 30, aged 96. He is survived by his children, including a former minister and a major general.

The university held a night of tributes in his honour at its Bosso campus on Wednesday, ahead of his burial.

title: Malaysia pledges long-term support for weightlifter who lost arm in crash
description:
Weightlifter Mohd Hafizuddin Roslin’s psychological recovery could take years, a senior Malaysian sports official said Friday, as the government rallied behind the injured athlete.
Hafizuddin’s right arm was amputated following a motorcycle accident in his native Malaysia on Monday night, ending the
content:
Weightlifter Mohd Hafizuddin Roslin’s psychological recovery could take years, a senior Malaysian sports official said Friday, as the government rallied behind the injured athlete.

Hafizuddin’s right arm was amputated following a motorcycle accident in his native Malaysia on Monday night, ending the 21-year-old’s promising career.

The National Sports Institute’s “psychology team will be with him from now on, according to his own pace”, Malaysia Sports Minister Taufiq Johari said.

“The process could take years and support will remain available for as long as he needs it,” Taufiq told the NST daily paper.

Hafizuddin won Commonwealth gold in the 88kg event in Glasgow in July and was a prospect for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.

Doctors amputated Hafizuddin’s arm above the elbow, local media reports said.

He remains in a stable condition in a hospital in Kuala Lumpur and was awaiting medical clearance to return home, Taufiq said.

The Malaysian government said it would also cover all his treatment and medical costs.

First Lady of Nigeria Oluremi Tinubu has called for stronger protection of children against the emerging dangers of unregulated artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and social media addiction, warning that their mental health and digital well-being must not be
content:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

First Lady of Nigeria Oluremi Tinubu has called for stronger protection of children against the emerging dangers of unregulated artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and social media addiction, warning that their mental health and digital well-being must not be neglected.

The First Lady said protecting children in a rapidly changing world must go beyond providing access to education and physical safety to addressing threats arising from their increasing exposure to digital technologies.

In her message to mark the 2026 World Children’s Day on Friday, themed “My Day. My Rights. My Future”, Mrs Tinubu stressed the need to create an environment where every child could learn, grow, live safely and fulfil their potential.

She noted that the responsibility to protect children must also extend to safeguarding them from the harmful effects of unregulated AI technologies and excessive social media use.

“In this rapidly changing world, the commitment to protect our children must include shielding them from the modern dangers of unregulated AI technologies and the harmful grip of social media addiction, ensuring their mental health and digital well-being are protected,” she said.

The First Lady urged Nigerians to remain committed to protecting all children, emphasising that their rights, safety and future must remain a collective responsibility.

“Let us ensure that every child is given the opportunity to learn, grow, live in safety and fulfil their potential,” she added.

title: EU And UK Eye ‘Reset’ Deal At Burnham’s Brussels Summit
description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and the EU’s top officials were set to announce deals to ease trade and youth mobility at a Brussels summit Friday, billed as a first step in a push to rebuild ties after Brexit.But in a potential spoiler for Burnham’s “reset”, Brussels said the
content:
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and the EU’s top officials were set to announce deals to ease trade and youth mobility at a Brussels summit Friday, billed as a first step in a push to rebuild ties after Brexit.

But in a potential spoiler for Burnham’s “reset”, Brussels said the deals coming into force would be conditional on reaching an agreement to cut university fees for EU students in Britain.

Since taking power this summer, the prime minister has smashed through the taboos in Britain’s toxic debate over relations with Europe — going as far as to float rejoining the bloc one day.

For now, the summit with EU chiefs Ursula von der Leyen and Antonio Costa will focus on much smaller steps to help turn the page a decade after the UK voted to leave — while Burnham saves for later the bigger decisions on what could come next.

“Britain and Europe share values, interests and a global neighbourhood. In a more dangerous world, we are stronger together. A closer partnership with Europe is good for working people, good for Britain and good for Europe,” a statement from Burnham said as he arrived in Brussels.

On the table in Brussels are three main agreements: a deal cutting red tape for food exports, another linking the two sides’ emissions-trading schemes and a third on a “youth experience scheme”.

Burnham argues those moves — which were in the pipeline long before he entered Downing Street — will help fix some of the damage Brexit inflicted.

British firms will export to Europe more easily again, and 100,000 under-30s from each side will be allowed to reside for up to three years in each other’s territory for work, study or travel.

But while the mood music at the meeting may be much improved, old habits still die hard.

Brussels and London wrangled ferociously down to the wire over the details.

One key sticking point was pinning London down to a future agreement on cutting fees for EU students at UK universities to the level paid by their British counterparts — with the EU making the other details entering into force contingent on striking a deal.

“We have not yet reached an agreement on tuition fees, and we have given ourselves six months to reach that agreement,” said an EU official, adding that the three core deals would be signed “in parallel” with those talks.

‘Tread Carefully’

The big question that the Brussels meeting won’t answer is what Burnham plans next.

“After the summit, we will initiate a discussion with our EU partners about options for our long-term relationship,” Burnham said earlier this week.

Having previously said he’d like to see Britain rejoin the EU in his lifetime, the former Manchester mayor has promised to lay out options that could range from leaving things as they are to entering the customs union or becoming a member again.

The strategy is in part because polls now regularly indicate most Britons regret Brexit and would vote to re-enter the bloc if a referendum were held tomorrow.

It is also reflective of Britain’s weak economy, damaged by Brexit, and how much the world has changed since 2016, with Europe firmly behind Ukraine in its war against Russian aggression.

Burnham hopes friendlier EU relations will help build a broad centre-left coalition to win the next general election, not anticipated until 2029.

But the strategy comes with huge risks, not least because his own party — never mind the country — is divided on how to proceed.

For now, the prime minister appears to have tempered his early urgency.

“I’m happy with closer ties, but he does need to tread carefully,” one Labour MP told AFP, speaking on condition of anonymity.

Burnham’s push leaves him open to accusations of Brexit betrayal from the opposition Conservatives and hard-right Reform UK party of Nigel Farage — who will give his own press conference in Brussels Friday.

In Brussels meanwhile, there is little expectation the UK will return to the fold any time soon.

“I doubt he’d take the risk of a major step that would be so radioactive,” said one senior EU diplomat.

“He’ll probably keep on trying to nibble away around the edges to improve ties — and we are open to having as close a relationship as possible.”

AFP

content:
American pop star Miley Cyrus is reportedly set to marry her fiancé, musician Maxx Morando, in Southern California this weekend.

According to a report by TMZ on Thursday, November 19, sources close to the couple confirmed plans for the wedding, although details surrounding the ceremony remain undisclosed.

Neither Cyrus nor Morando has publicly confirmed the reported wedding plans.

The marriage would be the second for the 33-year-old singer, who was previously married to Australian actor Liam Hemsworth.

Cyrus and Morando got engaged in 2025 after dating for about four years. The singer later revealed that Morando proposed during a trip to Japan, describing the experience as a surprise.

The couple recently attracted attention when Cyrus invited Morando onstage during her Hollywood Bowl performance in October to perform their song, Let’s Get Married.

Their relationship reportedly began in 2021 after they met on a blind date. They made their first public appearance together at the Gucci Love Parade fashion show in November of that year.

Cyrus married Hemsworth in December 2018 after dating for several years. However, the marriage ended in separation in August 2019, with their divorce finalised in January 2020.

title: UFC fighter Fiorot banned for three months over failed drug test
description:
French UFC flyweight fighter Manon Fiorot has been handed a three-month suspension for violating the promotion’s anti-doping policy after testing positive for a banned substance.
The UFC announced on Thursday that the 36-year-old had accepted the suspension following the detection of low levels of O
content:
French UFC flyweight fighter Manon Fiorot has been handed a three-month suspension for violating the promotion’s anti-doping policy after testing positive for a banned substance.

The UFC announced on Thursday that the 36-year-old had accepted the suspension following the detection of low levels of Ostarine in her sample.

Fiorot, who is ranked fourth in the UFC women’s flyweight division, tested positive on September 12, the same day she lost to Alexa Grasso in a title eliminator bout.

According to a statement from Combat Sports Anti-Doping (CSAD), Fiorot explained that her nutritionist had provided several dietary supplements that were new to her routine during fight week.

Tests conducted on the supplements reportedly revealed trace amounts of Ostarine, which is prohibited under the UFC’s anti-doping policy.

A second sample collected on October 16, before Fiorot was notified of the violation, returned negative results.

Ostarine is a selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) originally developed for potential medical applications, including helping patients with muscle-wasting conditions rebuild muscle.

The substance is prohibited at all times under the UFC’s anti-doping programme.

Fiorot initially faced a possible six-month suspension, but the UFC said her cooperation during the investigation contributed to a reduction in the punishment.

Her three-month suspension is scheduled to end on January 19, 2027.

The UFC’s anti-doping policy is administered by CSAD, while sample collection is conducted by Drug Free Sport.

title: Judges are not bullied by my administration, we respect judgements – Tinubu
description:
President Bola Tinubu has said his administration does not intimidate or bully judges, insisting that the government respects court judgments, including those it may find unfavourable.
The President spoke on Thursday at the launch of a six-volume book published to mark the 75th birthday and 50 years
content:
President Bola Tinubu has said his administration does not intimidate or bully judges, insisting that the government respects court judgments, including those it may find unfavourable.

The President spoke on Thursday at the launch of a six-volume book published to mark the 75th birthday and 50 years at the Bar of Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), Wole Olanipekun.

The event was held at the Body of Benchers Complex in Abuja.

Tinubu said his administration neither attacks nor denigrates the judiciary, warning that any government that intimidates judges undermines its own foundation.

He said the government remained committed to improving the welfare and working conditions of judicial officers, stressing that judges needed adequate financial support to discharge their responsibilities effectively.

“Our administration respects court judgments, even the ones we do not enjoy reading,” he said.

“We do not denigrate, attack or intimidate the judiciary. A government that bullies judges only weakens its own foundation.

“Instead, we continue to pursue initiatives that improve justice delivery for Nigerians and for everyone residing or doing business in our country. This is a personal commitment.

“We have also prioritised the welfare and service conditions of our judicial officers. Of course, we cannot ask our judges to hold the scale of justice steady while their own pockets are empty.”

The President said his administration had enacted the Judicial Office Holders (Salaries and Allowances, Etc.) Act, 2024, which increased the remuneration of judicial officers by 300 per cent as part of efforts to improve their welfare.

He said the measure was aimed at strengthening the judiciary and ensuring that judicial officers had the necessary support to deliver justice.

title: NCAC targets creative economy growth as NAFEST 2026 opens in Enugu
description:
By Chinenye Anuforo
The National Council for Arts and Culture (NCAC) has unveiled plans to use the 2026 National Festival of Arts and Culture (NAFEST) to promote Nigeria’s creative economy, develop young talents and create new opportunities for cultural entrepreneurs.
The eight-day festival, schedul
content:
By Chinenye Anuforo

The National Council for Arts and Culture (NCAC) has unveiled plans to use the 2026 National Festival of Arts and Culture (NAFEST) to promote Nigeria’s creative economy, develop young talents and create new opportunities for cultural entrepreneurs.

The eight-day festival, scheduled to hold from November 21 to 28 in Enugu, will feature cultural competitions, indigenous games, creative workshops, exhibitions, a daily Culture Market and national cultural showcases under the theme “Connected Culture”.

The festival, organised by the NCAC in collaboration with the Enugu State Government, is expected to bring together participating states, traditional institutions, artists, cultural enthusiasts, young creatives, entrepreneurs, policymakers and development partners.

Activities will centre on the Enugu International Conference Centre and Michael Okpara Square, with the programme designed to showcase Nigeria’s cultural diversity while exploring the economic potential of the country’s creative industries.

Speaking ahead of the festival, the Director-General of the NCAC, Obi Asika, urged Nigerians to attend the event, describing it as an opportunity to celebrate the country’s heritage, showcase talent and unlock opportunities in the creative sector.

“Our culture is our identity, our strength and our opportunity. NAFEST Enugu 2026 invites every Nigerian to celebrate who we are, showcase our creativity, and unlock the immense potential of our cultural heritage. Come to Enugu and be part of the experience,” he said.

A major highlight of the festival will be the Grand Cultural Parade and Procession of Participating States, featuring traditional costumes, indigenous music, dance and other cultural expressions.

Other activities will include Jollof Wars, Dance-Off Naija, Sing-Off Naija, Swag Show, Naija Home Makeover and the Culture Quiz, providing platforms for participants to demonstrate their culinary skills, artistic abilities, fashion creativity and cultural knowledge.

The festival will also showcase indigenous sporting and recreational traditions through traditional wrestling, Dambe, archery, Ayo and other traditional board games.

Children and young people will participate in storytelling, essay-writing competitions, arts and crafts activities and cultural knowledge contests, while eSports exhibitions, film screenings, fashion and music showcases, and indigenous craft demonstrations will also feature in the programme.

A major attraction throughout the eight days will be the NAFEST Culture Market, which will provide artisans, craftspeople, fashion designers, cultural entrepreneurs and small businesses with opportunities to display their products, engage customers and explore commercial partnerships.

The market will feature Nigerian arts and crafts, indigenous textiles, fashion, traditional accessories, cultural merchandise and locally made products, with the organisers expecting it to support local enterprises and promote Nigerian craftsmanship.

Beyond the cultural displays, the NCAC said the festival would focus on skills development and career advancement through its Career Centre and Creative Hustle workshops.

The Career Centre will provide young people, students, emerging professionals and aspiring creatives with opportunities to explore career pathways in the cultural and creative industries, gain industry insights and interact with experienced professionals.

The Creative Hustle workshops, on the other hand, will focus on the business of creativity, equipping emerging talents and entrepreneurs with knowledge on developing ideas, building sustainable creative enterprises, strengthening professional networks and turning creative skills into viable economic ventures.

The festival will also feature the NAFEST Colloquium, bringing together government representatives, development partners, financial institutions and creative industry leaders to discuss the future of Nigeria’s cultural and creative economy.

Discussions at the colloquium will focus on creative-sector financing, investment opportunities, policy support and stronger collaboration among federal and state governments and the private sector.

The NCAC said the engagements were intended to ensure that Nigerian creative talents were not only celebrated but also equipped with the knowledge, connections and opportunities required to build sustainable careers and businesses.

It added that the festival was also an opportunity for governments, investors, financial institutions and development partners to recognise and support the economic potential of Nigeria’s cultural and creative industries.

The council noted that, as Nigerian creativity gains increasing global recognition, there was a need to establish sustainable structures to support creative entrepreneurs, preserve indigenous knowledge and translate talent into viable economic opportunities.

For Enugu State, hosting the festival is expected to provide an opportunity to showcase its cultural heritage, hospitality and potential as a destination for tourism, investment and creative enterprise.

The festival will end with a grand closing ceremony featuring participating states, performers, dignitaries and festivalgoers, with outstanding performances and competition winners recognised.

The NCAC has encouraged residents of Enugu and neighbouring states, cultural organisations, schools, universities, creative communities and businesses to participate in the festival.

The event is supported by the Enugu State Government, British Council, GIZ, Bank of Industry, European Union, Techquest, Enugu Air and the South East Development Commission.

The post NCAC targets creative economy growth as NAFEST 2026 opens in Enugu appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Black teen charged for shooting identical twin to death in Washington DC
description:
A 16-year-old boy, Jamari Young, has been arrested and charged as an adult in the fatal shooting of his identical twin brother, Jabrell Young, inside their home in Washington, DC, United States.
The shooting occurred on October 25 but Jamari was taken into custody on Wednesday, November 18, by the U
content:
A 16-year-old boy, Jamari Young, has been arrested and charged as an adult in the fatal shooting of his identical twin brother, Jabrell Young, inside their home in Washington, DC, United States.

The shooting occurred on October 25 but Jamari was taken into custody on Wednesday, November 18, by the US Marshals Service, according to the Metropolitan Police Department.

He has been charged with second-degree murder while armed in the death of his twin brother.

On Thursday, a judge ordered him held without bond.

Police said officers responded at about 8:36 am on Sunday, October 25, to a report of a shooting at a home in the 200 block of 46th Street NE, in Northeast DC.

They found Jabrell unconscious and not breathing with an apparent gunshot wound.

He was pronounced dead at the scene.

Family members said he died in his mother’s arms in the basement of the home.

According to court documents, the brothers had been arguing after Jabrell allegedly went into Jamari’s room and touched his belongings.

A parent told police they found the twins tussling outside their adjacent basement bedrooms and tried to separate them when a gun went off.

The affidavit states that Jamari told his mother in the aftermath: “I didn’t mean to, it just went off. I didn’t mean to, I’m sorry ma.”

Police investigated the death as a homicide and launched a search for Jamari, who had left the house after the shooting.

Investigators recovered two .45-caliber shell casings inside the home but have yet to recover the weapon used in the killing.

Police also said a loaded 9mm pistol found wrapped in a blanket under a nearby parked car was linked to an unsolved fatal shooting in July, though it is not believed to be the murder weapon.

Family members have insisted the shooting was an accident.

The twins’ mother, Chantel Poe, and their aunt told reporters that the brothers were inseparable and that Jamari was terrified and did not intend to shoot his brother.

At Thursday’s hearing, Jamari’s defence lawyer argued for his release on personal recognisance, saying witnesses indicated the shooting was an accident and that he turned himself in.

Prosecutors countered that he did not surrender until nearly three weeks later.

The judge said he did not believe Jamari intended to kill his brother, but found probable cause for second-degree murder.

As she left the courtroom, Poe shouted to her son: “I love you. I’m here to support you.”

She later told reporters, “This is a lie. They are making it seem like this is not an accident. They paint a narrative that this was done malicious[ly]. And it was not.”

The post Black teen charged for shooting identical twin to death in Washington DC appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: ‎INEC releases 86,931 new PVCs for collection in Kogi
description:
‎By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja



‎‎The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Kogi State has announced the availability of 86,931 Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) for residents who participated in the second phase of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise.



‎The State Resident El
content:
‎By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja

‎‎The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Kogi State has announced the availability of 86,931 Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) for residents who participated in the second phase of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise.

‎The State Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) Dr. Shehu Wahab, made this known in a press statement made available to newsmen in Lokoja on Friday.

‎According to the commission, the second phase of the CVR exercise was conducted between January 5 and April 17, 2026.

‎‎INEC said, “The 86,931 PVCs produced for eligible registrants have been delivered to our offices across the 21 Local Government Areas of the state and are now ready for collection.”

‎‎The commission advised registrants to visit the INEC office in the Local Government Area where they completed their registration to collect their cards.

‎‎It said registrants are expected to come with their registration slips or printouts, or a valid means of identification where required.

‎‎INEC also clarified that PVCs from the first phase of the registration exercise are still available for collection.

‎‎”PVCs would not be issued through proxies, registrants must personally collect their cards. Collection is available at INEC LGA offices from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m., Monday to Friday.”

‎The commission further directed registrants to check the status of their PVCs and locate their collection centres through its CVR portal, cvr.inecnigeria.org.

‎‎INEC urged all voters who participated in the second phase of the CVR exercise to collect their PVCs without delay, noting that the cards are essential for participation in future elections.

‎‎The commission said timely collection would help ensure that no eligible voter is disenfranchised.

‎‎Wahab expressed appreciation to registrants for their patience during the production, verification and distribution processes, assuring that the commission remained committed to ensuring that every eligible voter obtains a PVC and is able to exercise their democratic right.

title: FG, Kaduna pledge support for young creatives, businesses
description:
The Federal Government and the Kaduna State Government have pledged stronger support for Nigeria’s creative industry, urging young people to turn their artistic talents into viable businesses capable of generating employment, attracting investment and boosting economic growth.
The Minister of Art, C
content:
The Federal Government and the Kaduna State Government have pledged stronger support for Nigeria’s creative industry, urging young people to turn their artistic talents into viable businesses capable of generating employment, attracting investment and boosting economic growth.

The Minister of Art, Culture and Creative Economy, Hannatu Musa Musawa, and Kaduna State Governor, Senator Uba Sani, made the commitment on Friday at the opening of the sixth edition of the Kaduna Fashion and Art Exhibition (KAFART), a three-day event in Kaduna.

Musawa, represented by the Curator of the National Gallery of Arts, Mrs Nana Hajara Tijjani, described the creative industry as a major economic asset that could contribute significantly to national development if properly harnessed.

She said the Federal Government, under President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, recognised arts, culture, innovation and creative enterprise as important instruments for economic diversification and employment generation.

The minister said, “Nigeria’s creative industry is more than a platform for artistic expression; it is a major economic opportunity. Our fashion designers, artists and cultural practitioners have the capacity to create jobs, attract investments and position the country competitively in the global economy.”

She urged governments at all levels, private sector operators and creative practitioners to strengthen partnerships to build an inclusive and sustainable creative industry.

According to her, “We must move beyond celebrating creativity to building an industry that provides opportunities, attracts investment and enables our talented young people to earn sustainable livelihoods from their skills.”

Musawa said emerging and established creatives needed access to finance, mentorship, professional training, markets and international networks to transform their talents into successful enterprises.

She described KAFART as an important platform for showcasing creative abilities, developing professional relationships and connecting practitioners with opportunities in the industry.

The minister urged participants to use the exhibition to establish partnerships and explore opportunities to promote Nigerian arts, fashion and cultural heritage beyond the country’s borders.

In his remarks, Sani pledged his administration’s continued support for the creative sector, particularly through vocational training, entrepreneurship, innovation and access to business opportunities.

Sani, represented by the Commissioner for Business, Innovation and Technology, Patience Fakai, said Kaduna was endowed with talented young people whose creative abilities could contribute significantly to the state’s economic development.

He said, “Our young people possess exceptional talents in fashion design, tailoring, painting, sculpture and other creative disciplines. We must provide them with the skills, mentorship, funding and platforms required to transform these talents into sustainable businesses.”

The governor described the creative economy as an emerging sector capable of generating employment, attracting investment and creating economic opportunities, particularly for young people and women.

He said his administration would continue to support vocational training and small and medium-sized enterprises through relevant government institutions.

Sani cited the Kaduna State Institute of Vocational Training and Skills Development as part of the government’s efforts to equip young people with practical skills in fashion design, carpentry, metalwork, hospitality, catering, interior design, welding and fabrication.

He urged the organisers of KAFART to strengthen collaboration with vocational institutions, noting that such partnerships would provide trainees with practical exposure, industry experience and employment opportunities.

The governor also said the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Technology would explore partnerships to support creative businesses through access to finance, mentorship, business development services, markets and professional networks.

He said KAFART’s international connections offered opportunities for cultural exchange and professional collaboration while promoting Kaduna as a destination for arts, culture and tourism.

On the theme, “To Have and to Hold,” Sani said the exhibition underscored the importance of preserving cultural heritage while embracing innovation and emerging opportunities.

Also speaking, the Technical Adviser to the Vice President on Women, Youth Engagement and Impact, Mrs Hauwa Liman, described the creative economy as an emerging source of wealth creation and employment.

She said Northern Nigeria had talented women and young people who needed platforms, financing and an enabling environment to translate their creativity into sustainable businesses.

The exhibition featured cultural performances, including a presentation by Mud Art Company titled “Anfara” and an indigenous leopard dance.

It also featured awards for outstanding creatives, with a N1m creative grant presented to Jessy Josh for embroidery, while Hassana Yusuf received the Queen Amina Embroidery Award.

Joshua Akubo received the Social Impact Award, while Liman was honoured with the Global Arewa Fashion Award.
