title: NCC seeks telecom VAS pricing benchmark to address industry disparities
description:
By Chinenye Anuforo
The Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) has commissioned a study to establish a cost-based pricing benchmark for value-added services (VAS) in the telecommunications industry, amid concerns over pricing disparities, revenue-sharing arrangements and consumer protection.
The s
content:
By Chinenye Anuforo

The Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) has commissioned a study to establish a cost-based pricing benchmark for value-added services (VAS) in the telecommunications industry, amid concerns over pricing disparities, revenue-sharing arrangements and consumer protection.

The study is expected to provide a common cost reference for operators and other players in the VAS value chain, while guiding future regulatory decisions on pricing and revenue distribution.

The Executive Vice-Chairman of the NCC, Dr Aminu Maida, disclosed this at a stakeholders’ consultative forum on the cost determination of value-added services in the Nigerian telecommunications industry in Lagos.

Maida, who was represented by the Head of the Competition and Tariff Unit at the commission, Omotayo Mohammed, said the exercise would provide an evidence-based assessment of costs across the VAS value chain.

He explained that value-added services had become an important part of the telecommunications ecosystem, supporting information, entertainment and financial applications beyond traditional voice and data services.

According to him, the commission introduced the VAS Aggregator Framework in 2017 and amended it in 2018 to improve connections between content providers and network operators, address market access challenges and strengthen revenue-sharing arrangements.

He said the commission had also introduced consumer protection measures, including the Do-Not-Disturb framework and short codes, to address unsolicited subscriptions and unauthorised deductions.

“Our objective is not to predetermine pricing outcomes, but to establish a credible and transparent cost basis that supports fair competition, efficient cost recovery, continued investment, innovation and consumer welfare,” Maida said.

He added that the study would identify inefficiencies and structural imbalances within the value chain rather than impose predetermined prices on industry players.

Maida urged telecommunications operators, aggregators, content providers and other stakeholders to cooperate with the consultants, Skyquest Concept Projects Ltd, by providing accurate and relevant information.

He warned that delayed, incomplete or inconsistent submissions could undermine the quality and reliability of the findings.

The NCC chief assured participants that commercially sensitive information provided during the exercise would remain confidential, noting that the consultants were contractually obligated to protect such data.

He also reminded operators of their obligations under Section 64 of the Nigerian Communications Act 2003, which empowers the commission to request relevant information and documents from industry players.

Also speaking, the Project Director, Skyquest Concept Projects Ltd, Olusegun Ekundayo, said Nigeria currently lacked a cost-based regulatory benchmark for VAS pricing and revenue-sharing arrangements.

He explained that existing agreements among mobile network operators, aggregators, VAS providers and content developers operated without a common cost reference, contributing to differences in service prices, quality and profit margins.

Ekundayo also identified billing transparency, unsolicited subscriptions and consumers’ difficulty in understanding charges for certain value-added services as challenges requiring attention.

He highlighted the growing economic importance of the sector, citing a global VAS market projection of $1.07 trillion in his presentation.

According to him, the study will examine developments in the Nigerian VAS market between 2017 and 2025, covering traditional services such as Short Message Service (SMS), Unstructured Supplementary Service Data (USSD), Interactive Voice Response (IVR) and web-based services.

The assessment will also cover emerging technologies and services, including artificial intelligence, fifth-generation (5G) networks, Internet of Things (IoT), Over-the-Top (OTT) services, cloud computing and application services.

The outcome is expected to provide the commission with a stronger basis for regulatory decisions aimed at improving pricing transparency, competition and consumer protection in Nigeria’s value-added services market.

title: WPRF 2026: Young PR professionals urged to build credibility through results, not age
description:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja
Young public relations professionals have been challenged to build reputations anchored on integrity, competence and measurable results, rather than rely on age, titles or self-proclaimed expertise to earn credibility.
The Chief Executive Officer of Dynasty Africa,
content:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

Young public relations professionals have been challenged to build reputations anchored on integrity, competence and measurable results, rather than rely on age, titles or self-proclaimed expertise to earn credibility.

The Chief Executive Officer of Dynasty Africa, Dayo Adedeji, gave the charge at the Global Youth Public Relations Summit, held as part of the World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) 2026 in Abuja, where he urged young Africans to abandon limiting perceptions and develop the capacity to build globally competitive businesses and influence.

Speaking on the theme “Be Someone Worth Believing”, Adedeji said credibility is established not by confidence or claims of excellence but by tangible achievements that demonstrate an individual’s value.

“If you want people to believe in you, your results do the explaining,” he said.

Drawing from his entrepreneurial journey, the Forbes Africa 30 Under 30 honouree explained how Dynasty Africa evolved from an influencer marketing agency five years ago into a full-service 360-degree marketing agency with operations and engagements across several African countries.

He said the company was recognised by Google in its second year as one of the African agencies with the largest influencer networks, before expanding into markets including Senegal, Côte d’Ivoire, Kenya, South Africa, Mozambique, Angola and Benin Republic.

According to him, the agency subsequently recorded more than 100 million impressions for its partners and clients and won a global Cannes Dolphins Award, marking what he described as a year of international recognition.

Adedeji said the transformation began when he stopped asking why anyone should believe in him and instead challenged himself with the question, “Why not me?”

He urged young professionals to adopt the same mindset, insisting that age should not determine the scale of ambition or achievement.

“There is no universally accepted age for great things. Success cannot be traced to age,” he said, citing the example of Colonel Harland Sanders, who founded the Kentucky Fried Chicken business in his 60s.

The marketing strategist also challenged young Africans to discard the perception that businesses and achievements originating from the continent are necessarily local, arguing that global relevance is driven more by ambition, quality and standards than by geographical location.

He cited the international success of African music and culture, Aliko Dangote’s business expansion and Nigeria’s hosting of the World Public Relations Forum for the first time as evidence of the continent’s growing global influence.

Adedeji said young professionals must learn to recognise opportunities within their immediate environments and build solutions capable of competing internationally.

He further stressed that personal perception influences ambition, decisions and, ultimately, the results people produce.

“Your sight shapes everything: your experience, your belief, your actions and your understanding,” he said, explaining that people must learn to see possibilities where others see limitations.

Earlier, the Chairman of the Youth Work Team and Special Adviser to the Anambra State Governor on Youth Reforms, Dr Nelson Omenugha, said the future of responsible communication rested significantly on the shoulders of young professionals and students.

Welcoming participants to the summit, Omenugha said the future of public relations would not be determined by technology alone but by the values, ethics, competence, courage and character of practitioners.

He noted that the growing influence of artificial intelligence, digital disruption and misinformation required young communication professionals to move beyond being consumers of change to becoming responsible creators, innovators and leaders.

“Technology can amplify our voices, but only integrity can give these voices credibility,” he said.

Omenugha urged participants not to wait for opportunities to be handed to them but to develop the competence and capacity to shape the future of the profession.

“To the PR students and young professionals here today, do not wait for the future to give you a seat at the table. Build competence, character and capacity to shape the table,” he said.

He also commended the President of the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR), Dr Ike Neliaku, for creating platforms to nurture emerging communication professionals.

He highlighted initiatives including the Young Professional Hub, the University of Communication and Leadership, unveiled during the forum, and a technology innovation challenge sponsored through the Global Alliance partnership with NIPR.

According to him, the initiatives represent long-term investments in building institutions, developing talent and creating opportunities for the next generation of communication practitioners.

The Global Youth Public Relations Summit brought together students, young professionals, industry leaders and communication practitioners from Nigeria and other countries to examine the future of responsible communication and prepare emerging professionals for leadership in the industry.

The post WPRF 2026: Young PR professionals urged to build credibility through results, not age appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: 2027: Tinubu may win only two states – Baba-Ahmed
description:
The National Chairman of the People’s Redemption Party, Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, has predicted that President Bola Tinubu will lose the 2027 presidential election if the exercise is free and fair.
Baba-Ahmed argued that widespread dissatisfaction with the administration could cost the ruling All Progressi
content:
The National Chairman of the People’s Redemption Party, Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, has predicted that President Bola Tinubu will lose the 2027 presidential election if the exercise is free and fair.

Baba-Ahmed argued that widespread dissatisfaction with the administration could cost the ruling All Progressives Congress its hold on power.

He also said the Tinubu government is concentrating more on retaining political power than addressing the country’s economic and security challenges.

He added that Nigerians were increasingly frustrated by the cost of living, insecurity and other difficulties confronting households.

Speaking in an interview with ARISE NEWS on Friday, the PRP chairman said his assessment was informed by his party’s interactions with ordinary Nigerians and their experiences under the current administration.

“If the elections are free and fair, President Tinubu, I repeat, will not win this election. Nigerians as a whole, not just Northwest, will reject him because he has not performed anywhere near what they expected.

“The Tinubu administration was more interested in just being in power than actually fixing problems in the country,” he said.

He maintained that the party’s position was based on direct engagement with citizens rather than assumptions about public opinion.

He stated, “We don’t just assume things. We mix with them. We don’t give them money. We don’t have the money that APC has to give them. So, we engage with them. We follow their lives. We follow their opinions. We are in touch with their sentiments.”

Baba-Ahmed also clarified that his earlier prediction about Tinubu’s electoral prospects was a nationwide assessment, not one restricted to the North-West or North-East.

“I said if the elections are credible, free and fair in 2027, President Tinubu is unlikely to win more than two states. I didn’t even say anything about the Northwest. I said in the country,” he said

The PRP chairman said his party had been involved in opposition coalition discussions from the beginning, describing the effort as an attempt to offer Nigerians an alternative to the APC ahead of the next general election.

“Our party has been part of the coalition from day one and we’re very proud of the role we have played. We have participated in all of it,” he stated.

He identified the Social Democratic Party, PRP, Peoples Democratic Party, Allied Peoples Movement, African Democratic Congress and Nigeria Democratic Congress as parties involved in the discussions. He added that more parties were expected to join before the end of November.

Baba-Ahmed said the coalition had set out two major objectives, the first being to work towards removing the APC from power.

He stated, “We have identified two fundamentals that we have to achieve. One is to work with Nigerians to make sure that we remove the APC administration from the neck of Nigerians. It is absolutely necessary that this administration does not come back.”

He expressed confidence that the opposition could defeat the ruling party in 2027 if it presented Nigerians with a credible alternative.

He said, “We are providing Nigerians a credible option to the APC, the most credible option to the APC. And we have a very comfortable expectation that we will win this election because Nigerians will reject from top to bottom. They will reject APC.”

On the political climate ahead of the election, Baba-Ahmed raised concerns about increasing violence and what he described as less visible restrictions on opposition parties’ ability to campaign.

“The escalating incidences of violence. Violence has now become a major factor in this politics. Not just overt violence, people beating opponents, people disrupting rallies and killing people. But the violence that is subtle.

“The antics of the APC closing the campaigning space for the opposition. You cannot mount billboards, you can’t have access to places to campaign,” he added.

He also rejected suggestions that northerners would be hypocritical if they withdrew their support for Tinubu after backing him in the 2023 presidential election.

According to him, voters who supported Tinubu in the last election had the same democratic right to change their minds based on their assessment of his performance.

He noted, “If the north elected Tinubu in 2023, it was the rights of northerners who felt that Tinubu was a better candidate than Obi and Atiku. And they have the same right now to reject Tinubu. There’s nothing hypocritical about this. That is what politics is all about.”

Baba-Ahmed linked the growing discontent in the North to worsening insecurity and the pressure of rising living costs, saying many families were struggling to meet basic needs.

He said, “There are towns, there are states where huge numbers, huge parts of the states in the north are under bandits or are vulnerable to bandit attack at any minute. Cost of living is impossible. You can’t pay school fees. You can’t take your children to the hospital. You can’t feed your family.”

He blamed the Tinubu administration for what he described as a deterioration in Nigerians’ living conditions.

He said, “Tinubu’s administration has destroyed lives and has made lives wretched. And this is why Nigerians are angry with him.”

Baba-Ahmed also defended his decision to criticise the president despite having served in his administration as special adviser on political matters. He said his departure followed concerns that the government was not giving sufficient attention to governance.

“I left the administration because I saw no evidence that President Tinubo’s administration was serious about governance,” he noted.

He said he had initially been part of the administration but left about a year to a year and a half after it began, having become convinced that its direction was wrong.

Baba-Ahmed said, “I was there when he started. I left a year into his administration, a year and a half into his administration, precisely because I saw the trajectory.”

He argued that the government’s public presentation of economic figures did not reflect the difficulties Nigerians were experiencing in their daily lives.

He added, “And rolling out statistics and figures and telling Nigerians we’re doing well, when in fact, life was becoming more and more impossible to deal with.”

The PRP chairman further criticised the state of the country inherited by Tinubu from his predecessor, former President Muhammadu Buhari, saying the current administration had made an already difficult situation worse.

He stated, “President Buhari handed over to Tinubu a country in a mess. And President Tinubu took it and made it considerably worse.”

Nigeria’s next general election is scheduled for 2027, with opposition parties facing the challenge of building a united front against the APC.

The coalition discussions involving the PRP, ADC, PDP, SDP, APM and NDC reflect efforts by opposition figures to coordinate their political activities and improve their chances of defeating the ruling party.

The debate over opposition unity comes against the background of the 2023 presidential election, in which Tinubu won on the APC platform while major opposition parties fielded separate candidates. Atiku Abubakar contested for the PDP, Peter Obi for the Labour Party and Rabiu Kwankwaso for the New Nigeria Peoples Party.

The post 2027: Tinubu may win only two states – Baba-Ahmed appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: ADC, NDC, PDP, others halt campaigns, sign common agreement Nov 30
description:
By Omeiza Ajayi



ABUJA: Member parties of the Coalition for Democracy, among them the African Democratic Congress ADC, the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC and a faction of the Peoples Democratic Party PDP among others will suspend campaign activities nationwide on Monday, 30th November 2026, to at
content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: Member parties of the Coalition for Democracy, among them the African Democratic Congress ADC, the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC and a faction of the Peoples Democratic Party PDP among others will suspend campaign activities nationwide on Monday, 30th November 2026, to attend the second summit of the coalition.

The decision was announced in a statement issued on Friday and signed by Salihu Moh. Lukman on behalf of the coalition parties.

According to him, concerned parties will sign a common agreement ahead of the January 16 presidential elections.

The summit had been scheduled for Monday, 23rd November 2026, but Linkman said member parties asked that it be rescheduled because their candidates and campaign teams are now deep into demanding programmes across the country.

“It is more important that every party, every presidential candidate and every national chairman is in the room than that the Summit holds on its original date,” the committee said.

The committee said the new date was agreed in consultation with key stakeholders to secure the widest possible participation. To make that commitment real, all member parties agreed to suspend campaign activities nationwide on the day, so that their leadership can attend in full.

“Parties competing hard for votes are prepared to stand down their campaigns for a day, together, because the defence of Nigeria’s democratic space is bigger than any one campaign,” it said.

According to the statement, the summit will finalise and sign the coalition’s common agreement and set the course for the work ahead of the 16 January 2027 elections.

The committee thanked member parties, delegates and partners for their understanding and regretted any inconvenience caused by the change. It said venue and accreditation details remain as communicated.

The coalition emerged from the G100 Opposition Summit held in Abuja on 31 August 2026. It is a multiparty platform pioneered by the ADC, the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), the NDC, the PDP, the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) and the Social Democratic Party (SDP).

The statement said it was established to give practical expression to the resolutions of that summit, and is committed to defending Nigeria’s constitutional democracy, protecting political pluralism, and ensuring free, fair, credible and competitive elections.

It described the coalition as a framework for opposition parties to coordinate their efforts, safeguard democratic institutions, uphold the rule of law, and protect the fundamental rights of Nigerians to freely choose their leaders.

“We will walk into that room united, and walk out of it committed,” the committee said.

title: 2027: Atiku’s camp demands probe into circulating ‘APC form’ linked to potential vote buying
description:
Paul Ibe, spokesman to ADC presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, has demand an immediate investigation of a circulating form linked to potential vote buying ahead of the 2027 general election.
He made the call in a Facebook post on Thursday.
Ibe said the form, purportedly issued in the name
content:
Paul Ibe, spokesman to ADC presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, has demand an immediate investigation of a circulating form linked to potential vote buying ahead of the 2027 general election.

He made the call in a Facebook post on Thursday.

Ibe said the form, purportedly issued in the name of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), combines polling-unit details and Voter Identification Numbers with National Identity Numbers (NINs), bank account details and Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs).

Its bank section, according to Ibe, says “complete only where payment is authorised.”

He warned that this bears the hallmarks of vote-buying ahead of the 2027 elections.

“Payment for what? Authorised by whom? From whose funds? And on what conditions?” Ibe queried.

He said the APC must establish whether the form is genuine and officially authorised, identify those distributing it, and explain precisely why such extensive personal and financial information is being collected.

“There are also allegations that applicants pay ₦1,000 for the form and another ₦500 on submission,” he stated.

Ibe said those allegations require investigation.

“Any arrangement linking promised payments to electoral support demands immediate scrutiny,” he argued.

Ibe cited Section 125(1)(c) of the Electoral Act 2026, which criminalises advancing money with the intention that it be used for electoral bribery, as well as knowingly reimbursing money spent on such bribery.

He noted that the penalty under subsection (1) is a maximum fine of ₦2 million, 12 months’ imprisonment, or both.

“Legitimate election expenses are exempted; disguising electoral bribery as ‘mobilisation’ would not make it lawful,” he added.

He linked the concerns to the reported promise by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, of ₦10 million to councillors who deliver their wards for President Bola Tinubu.

“Wike says the incentive is for political work. That explanation deserves scrutiny against the actual conditions and intended use of the money,” Ibe said.

He called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and relevant investigative agencies to establish the form’s origin, trace any associated payments, investigate the alleged charges, and determine whether electoral offences have occurred.

He also urged the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) to examine the collection and proposed use of the personal details.

Ibe said, “Nigerians deserve answers before their identities, financial information and electoral choices become instruments of political exploitation.

“The APC must seek a mandate through its record in government. Nigerians’ hardship must never become an opportunity to purchase their votes.”

The post 2027: Atiku’s camp demands probe into circulating ‘APC form’ linked to potential vote buying appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Why FIFA President Infantino is visiting Delta
description:
The arrival of FIFA President Gianni Infantino in Warri, Delta State on Friday has drawn attention to the city’s football heritage, grassroots sporting culture and ongoing efforts to upgrade its sporting facilities.
Beyond the inspection of the renovated Warri City Stadium, Infantino’s visit is also
content:
The arrival of FIFA President Gianni Infantino in Warri, Delta State on Friday has drawn attention to the city’s football heritage, grassroots sporting culture and ongoing efforts to upgrade its sporting facilities.

Beyond the inspection of the renovated Warri City Stadium, Infantino’s visit is also linked to his interest in grassroots football development and the history of Hussey College, an institution said to have produced several players for Nigeria’s senior national team.

Pinnick’s role in bringing Infantino to Warri

Former Nigeria Football Federation President and Deputy Chairperson of the FIFA Men’s Teams Competition Committee, Amaju Pinnick, had explained that Infantino’s visit was a reflection of his passion for grassroots football.

Speaking on the Morning Show, an Arise Television programme, on Tuesday, Pinnick said he had discussed Warri’s football history with the FIFA president and explained why the city deserved attention.

“On Saturday, by God’s grace, Gianni will arrive in Warri. Who will ever believe the president of FIFA will go to Warri, a subnational? Gianni loves grassroots football development,” he said.

Pinnick recalled that during one of their journeys from the airport, Infantino observed the number of people playing football along the road.

“The first time I picked him from the airport, as we were driving, he counted the number of people playing football, and I told him about Hussey College. This idea was also crystallised… He loves football, and he has seen everything,” he said.

The Hussey College connection

One of the places expected to feature prominently during the visit is Hussey College, Warri, an institution with a long history of producing football talents.

Pinnick drew attention to the school’s contribution to Nigerian football, claiming that it had produced 17 players who went on to represent the country with the Super Eagles.

“Hussey College produced 17 Super Eagles. Can you hear that? So, Gianni believes in these legends,” he said.

The school, founded in 1947, is among Warri’s historic educational institutions and has produced notable personalities across different fields.

The upgraded sporting facilities at the college are also part of efforts to provide opportunities for young people to develop their sporting abilities.

Among the former students associated with the national team are Clement Temile, Thompson Usiyan (Usiyen), Jossy Dombraye, Mike Obiku and Morten Owolo.

Why the Warri City Stadium matters

Infantino’s visit also brings attention to the Warri City Stadium, which the Delta State Government is rehabilitating under Governor Sheriff Oborevwori’s administration.

The 15,000-capacity facility is undergoing extensive improvements, including upgrades to its football pitch, athletics track, swimming pool, indoor sporting facilities, dressing rooms and other supporting infrastructure.

The project is intended to improve access to sporting facilities in Delta South and Central and strengthen the state’s capacity to host sporting competitions.

The state government has maintained that the project must meet the required standards before it is commissioned.

Infantino’s message about grassroots football

Speaking in an interview with Arise News in Warri, Infantino reiterated FIFA’s commitment to making football accessible to everyone, regardless of their location.

“Yeah, that’s what football is about, isn’t it? It’s for everyone, everywhere,” he said.

He explained that beyond major stadiums and the World Cup, smaller sporting facilities were equally important in bringing football closer to local communities.

“It’s big stadiums, it’s the World Cup, but it’s also smaller stadiums. It’s the proximity, and to be here in Warri for me is a fantastic occasion to showcase what we are about in FIFA, what we are about in football,” he said.

The FIFA president also expressed appreciation for the reception he received in Nigeria, citing the country’s recent victory at the Under-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco as an example of the opportunities football could create for young people.

Infantino said FIFA wanted to extend similar life-changing experiences to more girls and boys in Nigeria and across Africa.

Describing his experience in the country, he said he was happy to be in Nigeria and was encouraged by the warm reception.

“I’m very well, I’m very good, I’m here, I’m with family in Nigeria, in Africa, and we are working, we are continuing to work, we’ve been working a lot, and I’m just happy, I’m just enjoying and taking on all this positive energy here,” he said.

The post Why FIFA President Infantino is visiting Delta appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Trump vows to pursue nuclear arms deal despite challenges with China, Russia
description:
United States President Donald Trump has vowed to continue pursuing a nuclear arms control agreement involving China and Russia, despite admitting that securing the cooperation of the two countries would be difficult.
Trump spoke in a telephone interview with Reuters aboard his flight back to Washin
content:
United States President Donald Trump has vowed to continue pursuing a nuclear arms control agreement involving China and Russia, despite admitting that securing the cooperation of the two countries would be difficult.

Trump spoke in a telephone interview with Reuters aboard his flight back to Washington following discussions with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin at a trilateral summit in China.

He said establishing a three-way framework for nuclear arms control remained a major priority, arguing that reducing the world’s nuclear stockpiles was necessary despite the challenges involved in reaching an agreement.

“I love the concept of it but in terms of pure negotiation, it’s a very hard thing for me as a president to do,” Trump said.

“Because it should be done, but it’s hard to do psychologically,” he added.

China has been reluctant to participate in broader nuclear arms control negotiations even as it expands its nuclear arsenal.

The Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists estimated that China had about 410 nuclear warheads in 2023, compared with approximately 3,708 held by the United States. Russia’s nuclear stockpile was estimated at about 5,420 warheads as of March 2026.

The Pentagon has projected that China’s operational nuclear warheads could exceed 1,000 by 2030.

Trump said Xi supported the principle of reducing nuclear weapons but acknowledged that convincing countries with large arsenals to surrender a substantial portion of their stockpiles would be difficult.

He illustrated the challenge with a hypothetical situation in which a country possessing 4,000 nuclear warheads was asked to give up half of them.

Despite the difficulties, Trump maintained that discussions towards an agreement should continue.

Following the summit, a joint statement by Trump, Xi and Putin reaffirmed that a nuclear war could not be won and must never be fought.

The three leaders also expressed support for continued discussions aimed at reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.

title: Ogogo’s daughter Kira makes filmmaking debut with ‘Toriola’
description:
Shakirat Wunmi Taiwo, popularly known as Kira Ogogo, daughter of late Nollywood actor Taiwo Hassan, has made her debut as a filmmaker with the release of her first movie, Toriola.
The film, produced under Kira Ogogo Film Production, marks her entry into filmmaking months after the death of her fathe
content:
Shakirat Wunmi Taiwo, popularly known as Kira Ogogo, daughter of late Nollywood actor Taiwo Hassan, has made her debut as a filmmaker with the release of her first movie, Toriola.

The film, produced under Kira Ogogo Film Production, marks her entry into filmmaking months after the death of her father, who passed away in August 2026 following a battle with stage-four cancer.

Directed by veteran filmmaker Abbey Lanre, Toriola tells the story of a young woman whose ambition to build a peaceful and successful life is disrupted by deceit, jealousy and longstanding family secrets.

The plot follows her journey as she discovers that some of the people closest to her are responsible for the challenges threatening her future.

In honour of her father’s contributions to Yoruba cinema, Kira brought together established actors, family friends and emerging talents for the production.

The movie features veteran actor Yinka Quadri, Lanre Adediwura, Temitope Saliu Aremu, Azeez Ayinde Onifade and Oluwapelumi Aramide Kayode, popularly known as OAK.

Kira also features in the film under the acting credit Shaki, while her sister, Taiwo Halima Olamide, known as Lima Ogogo, is part of the cast.

The release comes weeks after Kira and her sister appealed to Nigerians and members of the entertainment industry to support their careers as they seek to sustain their father’s legacy.

In an appreciation video shared in October, the sisters thanked Nigerians and prominent personalities for their support following their father’s death.

They also urged fans who enjoyed Ogogo’s movies to extend the same support to their own productions.

With the release of Toriola, Kira takes her first major step into film production, following in the footsteps of her late father, who was a prominent figure in the Yoruba movie industry.

title: I nearly quit football after 18-month injury ordeal – Kulusevski
description:
Tottenham Hotspur and Sweden winger Dejan Kulusevski has revealed that he considered walking away from football during an 18-month injury nightmare that left him questioning his future in the game.
The 26-year-old admitted that his prolonged battle with a serious knee injury became so emotionally dr
content:
Tottenham Hotspur and Sweden winger Dejan Kulusevski has revealed that he considered walking away from football during an 18-month injury nightmare that left him questioning his future in the game.

The 26-year-old admitted that his prolonged battle with a serious knee injury became so emotionally draining that he eventually told his mother he no longer believed he could continue playing football.

In an interview with BBC Sport on Friday, the Swede was quoted as saying, “I told my mother. I sat with her and I told her: ‘Listen, I don’t think I can play any more,'” Kulusevski revealed in an emotional interview with Tottenham’s in-house media.

The Swedish international has not started a competitive match since May 11, 2025, when he suffered a serious right knee injury during Tottenham’s Premier League encounter against Crystal Palace.

Initially expected to spend only a few months on the sidelines, complications prolonged his recovery, forcing him to undergo multiple operations and miss the entire 2025-26 campaign, including the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Reflecting on the emotional impact of his absence, Kulusevski admitted that watching his teammates celebrate Tottenham’s Europa League triumph against Manchester United while he struggled with crutches was particularly painful.

“That was one of the hardest days of my life,” he said.

“It was so beautiful to see all the people happy, but for me I was going there with crutches. I couldn’t work.

“I couldn’t even go and get my medal because it was too slippy to go on that thing [platform].”

The former Juventus player also described the loneliness of watching his teammates enjoy their success while he remained sidelined.

“Seeing the team celebrating on the bus [outside Tottenham Hotspur Stadium] was probably one of the most difficult parts of this journey because you feel so alone.

“You feel like the whole world has forgotten about you and what you put in.”

Kulusevski’s recovery was further complicated by repeated setbacks, with the midfielder revealing that he was even offered a knee transplant as a possible treatment option, which he rejected.

“You get stressed because nothing works,” he added.

Another major disappointment came when Sweden manager Graham Potter informed him that he would not recover in time to represent his country at the 2026 World Cup.

Despite remaining hopeful of making the tournament, the news left him devastated.

“I just stared at the wall for three hours because I really believed I would do it,” he recalled.

His wife, Eldina Ahmic, also spoke about the difficulties of watching her husband endure such a challenging period, particularly as he missed Tottenham’s European triumph and every Premier League game during the following campaign.

Kulusevski has now made a full recovery and is closing in on his first Tottenham start since May 2025, offering a positive end to a difficult chapter in his career.

His story highlights the psychological challenges that accompany long-term injuries in professional football, with isolation, uncertainty and frustration often making rehabilitation as difficult mentally as it is physically.

For Kulusevski, the road back has been about more than recovering his fitness. It has been a fight to rediscover his confidence, belief and love for the game.

The post I nearly quit football after 18-month injury ordeal – Kulusevski appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Opposition coalition fixes November 30 for unity pact — Lukman
description:
The coalition of opposition political parties seeking to challenge President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election has shifted the date for the signing of its proposed agreement on democratic renewal to November 30.
This came amid continuing uncertainty over whether the parties can agree on
content:
The coalition of opposition political parties seeking to challenge President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election has shifted the date for the signing of its proposed agreement on democratic renewal to November 30.

This came amid continuing uncertainty over whether the parties can agree on a common presidential candidate.

Former Director General of the Progressives Governors Forum, Salihu Lukman, disclosed this during an interview on Arise TV.

Lukman explained that the date was moved by one week following consultations with political party leaders and presidential candidates who wanted more time to adjust their campaign schedules.

He said the coalition was working to ensure that party chairmen, presidential candidates and their running mates would be present at the Abuja gathering to formally endorse the agreement.

He described the planned signing as a significant step in the effort to bring opposition parties together, insisting that the process had moved beyond the initial stage of discussions and was now being driven by the participating political parties.

“One of the thing we want to be sure on that day is that all the party leadership and all the presidential candidates and the running will be in that hall. That is the first thing and while majority of them are ready.

“Others said they needed to adjust their campaign schedule. So we discuss and reach some compromise. So, it’s likely that some of them may not be there. We agree to shift it by one week to 30th November. We shift it to 30th November,” he said.

The coalition brings together six political parties and factions, including the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Allied Peoples Movement (APM), National Democratic Congress (NDC), a faction of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) associated with Tanimu Turaki, the People’s Redemption Party (PRP) and the Social Democratic Party (SDP).

According to Lukman, the parties are expected to sign a formal agreement committing them to cooperation, with details of possible joint campaigns and other forms of political collaboration to be worked out.

However, the most difficult issue confronting the coalition remains unresolved: whether the participating parties will eventually agree to support a single presidential candidate against Tinubu.

Lukman disclosed that the coalition had developed three major documents to provide the foundation for its proposed political cooperation.

They are a National Covenant for Democratic Renewal, a Framework for Opposition Unity and a National Reform Programme.

He stated, “So we spend the better part of the time from August to now trying to put the table and convince all of them to sit on the table.

“I think we have reached that agreement right and on the basis of that on that 30th November all of them will be there and the party chairman will sign a formal agreement committing to working together and what working together will entail will include a number of things that will be announced that very day which may include some joint campaigns. The detail will be worked out and will be announced on that very day.”

He explained that the covenant would establish the principles guiding the coalition, while the framework would provide mechanisms for managing disagreements among participating parties.

The third document, the National Reform Programme, would outline the minimum policy commitments expected of any government produced by the coalition.

Describing it as a collective manifesto, Lukman said the programme had been developed by examining the policy proposals of the different parties and identifying areas where they could reach common ground.

“The National Reform Programme is basically like the minimum undertaking that a government produced by the coalition will commit to,” he said.

He added that the documents would be made available to the media and the Nigerian public on November 30 for scrutiny.

Lukman insisted that the coalition was not asking participating parties to dissolve themselves or abandon their individual political identities.

Rather, the objective was to create a platform through which they could cooperate while retaining their structures and existing candidates.

Despite the progress claimed by the coalition, Lukman acknowledged that there was currently no agreed mechanism for selecting a common presidential candidate.

He said the organisers needed the direct involvement and consent of the presidential candidates before such an arrangement could be discussed conclusively.

“We are not asking any party to dissolve itself and stop existing. They will continue to exist,” he explained.

He also acknowledged that some parties were prepared to cooperate only on issues such as electoral credibility and the protection of votes, without necessarily agreeing to support another party’s presidential candidate.

“The issue is particularly sensitive given the competing ambitions of opposition figures, including former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State governor Peter Obi.

“The NDC, for instance, has indicated that any discussion about a common presidential candidate must take account of its preference for the Obi-Wan ticket,” he said.

Lukman said such differences would have to be addressed through further negotiations, describing the entire process as one of confidence-building.

He expressed concern that supporters of opposition parties were increasingly engaging in public attacks against one another rather than concentrating on challenging the ruling APC.

“One of the things that is so disturbing to us is a situation where people in opposition are fighting themselves and dissipating energy against themselves instead of facing a common enemy,” he said.

He warned that the APC would ultimately benefit if the opposition allowed its internal disagreements to undermine the coalition.

According to him, party leaders and presidential candidates must take responsibility for regulating the conduct of their supporters to prevent further divisions.

Lukman argued that the opposition’s failure to unite was a major factor in the outcome of the 2023 presidential election.

He recalled that opposition candidates collectively secured substantially more votes than the eventual winner, but failed to translate that support into electoral victory because they contested separately.

“Two opposition candidates, or even three combined, got more than 40 million votes. The winner of the election got eight million votes,” he said.

He argued that the figures demonstrated that the opposition had sufficient electoral strength to challenge the APC if its supporters and political structures could be coordinated.

“It was not even the APC that defeated the opposition; the opposition defeated itself,” he declared.

Lukman challenged opposition politicians to decide whether their ultimate objective was to win the presidency or simply participate in an election to satisfy their individual ambitions.

“Are they working to get their candidate to win the election and become president of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, or are they just going to the election to satisfy themselves and their candidates?” he asked.

He urged the opposition leaders to demonstrate statesmanship and place the national interest above personal political calculations.

Beyond the question of a common presidential candidate, Lukman identified electoral credibility as one of the most important areas of cooperation being negotiated.

He said the coalition’s first common national undertaking would be to protect the integrity of votes at every polling unit.

This could involve the joint deployment of polling agents by participating parties, particularly in areas where individual parties lack the resources to cover all polling units.

Lukman noted that some opposition parties did not have the capacity to deploy agents across Nigeria’s approximately 176,000 polling units.

He said the coalition intended to map the country, identify areas of electoral strength and pool the resources of participating parties to ensure adequate coverage.

“All the parties must come together and deploy their resources and get their agents together to protect the vote,” he said.

He argued that such cooperation would also help restore public confidence in the electoral process and encourage greater voter participation.

According to him, voter apathy remains a serious concern because many Nigerians believe their votes may not necessarily determine the eventual outcome of elections.

“When citizens now see parties coming together in the way we are trying to do, that will give them confidence to come out,” he said.

The coalition convenor also argued that Nigeria’s political system required fundamental reforms beyond simply replacing the ruling party.

He questioned the existing approach to zoning and power rotation, insisting that political arrangements should not be allowed to produce leaders who are unaccountable to citizens.

“The way this country is today, the democracy and the politics have been so bastardised that everything needs to be renegotiated,” he said.

He added that zoning arrangements that failed to guarantee accountable leadership had become a problem rather than a solution.

Lukman also called for stronger political parties, arguing that many of the country’s political organisations were not functioning in accordance with their own constitutions.

He warned against producing another president who would dominate the legislature and impose political leadership on the National Assembly.

“We don’t want to have another president produced by the coalition that will now come and bulldoze his way to impose leadership of the National Assembly and reduce the National Assembly to basically people singing choir for the president,” he said.

For him, the proposed coalition must, therefore, be about more than defeating Tinubu.

Although Lukman expressed satisfaction with the progress made, the timing of the proposed agreement presents a considerable challenge.

With the election approaching, the coalition still has to resolve disagreements over presidential ambitions, possible power-sharing arrangements, joint campaign structures and the practical details of electoral cooperation.

The November 30 meeting is therefore expected to be an important test of whether the opposition parties can translate their public commitment to unity into a workable political arrangement.

Lukman acknowledged that considerable work remained, but said the fact that party leaders were now sitting together was itself evidence of progress.

He maintained that the process had moved beyond the early scepticism that greeted the initiative, insisting that the participating parties had taken ownership of the negotiations.

The 2023 presidential election exposed the divisions within Nigeria’s opposition, as several major parties fielded separate candidates against the APC’s Bola Tinubu.

Tinubu won the election with 8,794,726 votes. Atiku Abubakar of the PDP came second with 6,984,520 votes, while Peter Obi of the Labour Party secured 6,101,533 votes. Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party polled 1,496,687 votes.

The three leading opposition candidates, Atiku, Obi and Kwankwaso, recorded a combined 14.58 million votes.

However, they contested separately and did not present a common presidential ticket.

The outcome has since fuelled calls for opposition parties to unite ahead of the 2027 election, with supporters of a coalition arguing that a common candidate could provide a stronger challenge to the ruling APC.

title: 2030: FG takes decisive action to end open defecation with Executive Order
description:
By Gabriel Ewepu



ABUJA – IN a renewed commitment, the Federal Government has unveiled a new Executive Order to accelerate Nigeria’s drive towards ending open defecation by 2030.



The unveiling of the Open Defecation Free Nigeria by 2030 and Other Related Matters Order, 2025 coincided with the c
content:
By Gabriel Ewepu

ABUJA – IN a renewed commitment, the Federal Government has unveiled a new Executive Order to accelerate Nigeria’s drive towards ending open defecation by 2030.

The unveiling of the Open Defecation Free Nigeria by 2030 and Other Related Matters Order, 2025 coincided with the commemoration of World Toilet Day and the seventh anniversary of the Clean Nigeria campaign in Abuja on Thursday.

Vice President Kashim Shettima, represented by the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Delivery and Coordination in the Office of the Vice President, Akubo Adegbe, described the Executive Order as a decisive step towards translating government commitments into measurable sanitation outcomes.

Shettima said the order marks a transition from fragmented interventions to stronger coordination, measurable results and sustainable national progress.

He called on state and local governments to strengthen accountability, increase sanitation financing and sustain community-led behavioural change

He disclosed that since the launch of the Clean Nigeria campaign in 2019, 185 of the country’s 774 local government areas have attained Open Defecation Free (ODF) status, while Jigawa and Katsina remain the only states certified as ODF nationwide.

While acknowledging the progress recorded, the Vice President warned that the country still had considerable ground to cover, urging states yet to achieve ODF status to establish monthly and quarterly targets and make their progress publicly available.

He also cautioned against a reversal of gains in communities already certified as open defecation-free, stressing the need for sustained monitoring and accountability to protect existing achievements.

According to him, Nigeria must prioritise sustainable financing, reliable data, stronger institutions, effective implementation and continuous behavioural change to achieve the 2030 target.

He also called on state and local governments to take ownership of the campaign by allocating adequate resources and strengthening sanitation institutions, while urging development partners, the private sector, traditional rulers, community leaders and civil society organisations to sustain their support.

Shettima, who chairs the Steering Committee of the Clean Nigeria Project, reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to working with subnational governments, noting that the National Economic Council would also be deployed to advance and sustain the national sanitation agenda.

Linking the campaign to this year’s World Toilet Day theme, “Sanitation and Gender Equality,” the Vice President highlighted the disproportionate burden poor sanitation places on women and girls.

He noted that inadequate access to safe and private sanitation facilities undermines their health, security, dignity, education and participation in economic and social activities.

He called for inclusive policies and investments that address the sanitation needs of women, girls, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable populations.

Meanwhile, the Minister of Water Resources and Sanitation, Engr Joseph Utsev, in his speech said the Clean Nigeria campaign had evolved beyond public awareness and mobilisation into a national platform for policy coordination, institutional engagement, community participation and performance monitoring.

Utsev highlighted the revised Clean Nigeria Strategy 2025–2030, which is structured around six strategic pillars, as well as the newly introduced Clean Nigeria Real Time Monitoring and Information System designed to improve data management, track implementation and strengthen accountability.

Reflecting on the campaign’s seven-year journey, the minister identified five critical lessons, including the need to translate political commitment into adequate financing and practical action, prevent communities from relapsing into open defecation, strengthen community ownership, adopt a multi-sectoral approach and ensure that reliable data informs planning and resource allocation.

The Minister of Youth Development, Ayodele Olawande, said the ministry was contributing to the campaign through youth mobilisation and community advocacy, disclosing that more than 1,000 youth volunteers had been trained to promote sanitation awareness and behavioural change.

He said pilot interventions were ongoing in Bauchi, Kaduna, Benue, Ebonyi and Oyo states, adding that young people also had an important role to play in promoting gender-responsive sanitation.

Olawande specifically emphasised menstrual hygiene education, access to safe and private toilet facilities and the need to eliminate the stigma associated with menstruation.

Goodwill messages were also delivered by the former Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, Didi Esther Walson-Jack, alongside representatives of civil society organisations, professional bodies and development partners, who reaffirmed the importance of collective action in achieving Nigeria’s 2030 open defecation elimination target.

The post 2030: FG takes decisive action to end open defecation with Executive Order appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Good night Olufemi Ajasa, you were more than a friend
description:
By Taiwo George



During the launch of the Converged Digital Newsroom of Media Trust Group, Alhaji Mohammed Idris, Minister of information and National Orientation, shared a personal story. While tracing the success story of the company, the Minister who was Special Guest at the occasion, narrated
content:
By Taiwo George

During the launch of the Converged Digital Newsroom of Media Trust Group, Alhaji Mohammed Idris, Minister of information and National Orientation, shared a personal story. While tracing the success story of the company, the Minister who was Special Guest at the occasion, narrated an encounter he had with Malam Kabir Yusuf, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Media Trust Group.

According to him, several decades ago, he and Media Trust Chairman had a sit-down session in Kaduna and Malam Yusuf told him about his dream of owning a successful media outfit, while he, the Minister, told Malam Kabiru of his own dream to be a Public Relations merchant. If there is anyone whom I shared my dream in this profession with, it was Olufemi. But because tomorrow is not promised to anyone, I unlike the Minister, would not have the opportunity to ever watch my late brother and colleague relieve a similar encounter in future. Kabi o osi!

Femi and I shared many things in common. We attended same institution, though while he was at the Communication School of the Lagos State University (LASU) in Anthony, I was at the main campus in Ojo. We got admitted the same year and graduated same year.

Our marital journey also has striking similarities. His wife and mine are both Mass Communicators. Our spouses were first colleagues before signing lifetime contract. While Femi met his wife at Uni, I met mine during the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) programme. At death, Femi was the Online Editor of Vanguard, I’m currently the Online Editor of Daily Trust. Both of us are not just proud sons of Lagos, but we share ancestral ties.

This is why it’s still quite difficult to come to terms with his sudden demise. A man of few words. He moved on whenever he made his point. Femi was never the one who would bore you with a conversation. Each time we spoke on phone, he went straight to the point. The few times the conversation dragged I said let me quickly make this final point, he would respond, “Oya na!”, and follow up with, “Take care!” whenever I summarized my point. Something unusual happened on the eve of his death. We usually compared notes on so many issues, particularly work. I came across an information which had to do with his workplace and forwarded same message to him via WhatsApp but it didn’t deliver. An online Editor being offline during that period?

I assumed he was in a place where network was bad, and would respond when he read the message until Monday morning when Victor Ogunyinka, our mutual friend, broke the news to me. I screamed and my wife who was coincidentally sleeping on the same couch Femi and his family sat when they attended the parlour party during my son’s third-year birthday, woke up. I told her what happened and she regained consciousness immediately. We went over a few memories with Femi and said prayers for the wife and kids he left behind.

Where do I start sharing the memories from? I remember when I was to relocate from Lagos to Abuja, Femi heard the news before I shared with him. Having moved to the capital city years before I did, I sought his advice on a number of issues, especially accommodation. He didn’t like the choice I eventually made but I convinced him. Weeks later when he hosted a get together for me and a few colleagues, he joked that I got there far behind schedule because of the distance but I protested saying it was because of work and we all laughed it over. On a journalists’ WhatsApp Forum where a link on his obituary was dropped, a colleague wrote, “What a fine man! God rest his soul.”

Talking about good looks, it’s common for people to command attraction in the early years of their youth but in the case of Femi, the charm improved as he aged. During the get together he organised for me upon relocation to Abuja, I almost didn’t recognize him. So cute and charming, I was like ’Abuja working well for you bro’, and he laughed asking which Ábuja? To prove that, he still didn’t lose his charm when Vanguard job took him back to Lagos.

Femi touched so many lives. He was always on the lookout for opportunities to make life better for colleagues. When he clocked 40 four years ago, one of his mentees told me we needed to find a way to celebrate him. He came up with the idea of surprise package which clicked and quickly we got Funsho, his wife, into the picture. Because the mentee was in Lagos, I was the one who coordinated things after which he got in touch with Funsho who the package was delivered to and she kept it till he returned from work. The next morning, Femi called, “Taiwoooooo!! You ehn! Thanks man! Thanks man.” The conversation ended.

Femi was a caring father who was involved in the lives of his children. As they made their way into the living room during the birthday, he watched them unlace their shoes and guided them to where they kept them. They also had chit chats that ended with smiles during the party. Not every father has such time in a busy era like this. Femi was a man who would praise you when the need arose and knock you if that’s what he felt you deserved. At a retreat organised three years ago, my boss asked me to get someone to review our brand, it was Femi who came through and he gave the team very practical and useful insights.

After the 2023 election, Femi called me saying, “Taiwooooo, superb coverage! You guys really tried. I followed the fantastic job your team did. Daily Trust was number two in terms of coverage.” To him a brand whose name I won’t deliberately mention (not Vanguard) was number one and he gave his reasons. Other times, Femi would argue Vanguard’s dominance of the digital terrain and irrespective of my point, he would say emphatically, ‘Vanguard is number one!” When my platform was the talk of town over a controversial story, Femi called and asked, “Taiwo, what did you guys do there? You want to set this country on fire? Take time o!”

The undeniable truth is that Femi loved his job and did it with passion. He gave his best to it and touched lives in the process. Every job has its challenges, but the aspect of the profession my late brother and I find ourselves in is no doubt demanding. It’s not a stroll in the park to manage the digital arm of a thriving newspaper. A decision taken within split seconds could ruin the brand’s hard-earned trust and you would be worse for it. The job is so jealous that at times, we cast headlines in the dream. I’ve lost the number of times an unexpected, unplanned activity disrupted a schedule planned for weeks or months.

As Online Editor, you have to stay alert to guide your team and ensure things go smoothly. A colleague shared a video of Femi with his laptop beside him on the hospital bed and I connected with that immediately. I’ve travelled that route before. I remember when I was trapped in the hospital for days but still couldn’t let go of my laptop. My older son fell ill so the mother rushed him to hospital and I joined them after work. As of the time I got there, my younger son had also started showing symptoms. The matron advised that he should be taken away immediately to prevent the situation from getting worse. The responsibility of taking care of him fell on me but as my wife walked out with my younger son, I signalled her to wait outside. I needed something from the car, my laptop.

Back to Femi, in that video, he said he was on drip and needed to rest before for a few hours before getting back to work. We’ve lost many colleagues recently. In August, it was Otunba Dotun Oladipo, who collapsed at work and gave up in the hospital. In September, it was Felix Onigbinde who also slipped into coma while on duty. Death is an inevitability for all mortals, that we know; but what about these untimely deaths? I think it’s high time we found a way to sort out work-life balance. Many questions racing through my mind over my friend’s demise.

Was it substandard treatment? Did he ignore warning signs? Was he too busy to take care of his health? Does this have spiritual undertone? What happened to Femi? We can’t question God. I never imagined not having Femi around in the next 30 years but such is life: here today, gone tomorrow. I’ve been following the drama trailing the death of gospel singer Olayemi Bayonle, better known as Toluwanisings, not knowing that death was lurking around the corner. Sleep well, my friend and brother. Ki Oluwa te e si afefe rere. Ishe owo re oni baje o. Your son will tell your story someday, good night.

The post Good night Olufemi Ajasa, you were more than a friend appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Ogogo’s daughter, Kira, releases debut film

As reported by PM News on Friday, the film, produced under Kira Ogogo Film Production, marks a major milestone in her cr
content:
Shakirat Wunmi Taiwo, popularly known as Kira Ogogo, daughter of late Nollywood actor Taiwo Hassan, has made her debut as a filmmaker with the release of her first movie, Toriola.

As reported by PM News on Friday, the film, produced under Kira Ogogo Film Production, marks a major milestone in her creative journey as she continues the legacy of her late father, who passed away in August 2026 after battling stage-four cancer.

Directed by veteran filmmaker Abbey Lanre,
Toriola tells the story of a young woman whose dreams of building a peaceful and successful life are shattered after she becomes entangled in deceit, jealousy and deep-rooted family secrets.

As the story unfolds, she discovers that the people closest to her are behind the challenges threatening her future.

In a tribute to her father’s longstanding contributions to Yoruba cinema, Kira assembled a cast of respected industry veterans, family friends and emerging talents to bring the project to life.

The movie features Nollywood icon Yinka Quadri, alongside Lanre Adediwura, Temitope Saliu Aremu, Azeez Ayinde Onifade, Oluwapelumi Aramide Kayode, popularly known as OAK, and Kira herself, who is credited as Shaki.

Her sister, Taiwo Halima Olamide, also known as Lima Ogogo, equally features in the production.l

The film’s release comes after the two sisters made an emotional appeal to Nigerians in an appreciation video shared in October, thanking the public and prominent personalities, including the First Lady, Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun and Senator Solomon Adeola, for their support following the loss of their father.

In the video, the sisters expressed gratitude for the love shown to their family during their period of grief and appealed to fans to extend the same support to their individual ventures in acting and filmmaking.

With Toriola, Kira Ogogo takes her first major step behind the camera, signalling a new chapter for the family in the Nigerian film industry.

The post Ogogo’s daughter, Kira, releases debut film appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Simon Kolawole reveals intrigues behind Tinubu’s 2023 victory in new book
description:
Veteran Nigerian journalist, Simon Kolawole, is set to release a book examining the political manoeuvres, rivalries and alliances that shaped the 2023 presidential election.
Kolawole is the founder of TheCable, an online newspaper launched in 2014.
The 296-page book, titled ‘Winning Formula: The Ins
content:
Veteran Nigerian journalist, Simon Kolawole, is set to release a book examining the political manoeuvres, rivalries and alliances that shaped the 2023 presidential election.

Kolawole is the founder of TheCable, an online newspaper launched in 2014.

The 296-page book, titled ‘Winning Formula: The Inside Story of Nigeria’s 2023 Presidential Election,’ will go on sale on Monday, November 23, according to a statement on Friday by its publishers, Cable Books.

In the book, Kolawole examines how President Bola Tinubu secured victory, the rivalry between former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and ex-Rivers State Governor Nyesom Wike, and the emergence of Peter Obi and the Obidient movement as major forces in the election.

Describing the book’s central themes, Kolawole said it would explain “how Bola Tinubu outmanoeuvred Muhammadu Buhari, how Atiku Abubakar and Nyesom Wike destroyed each other’s presidential ambition, how Peter Obi and the Obidient movement became a phenomenon — and how the winning formula that decided it all was hiding in plain sight.”

The author said the book drew on insider briefings, court filings and polling data to examine the election and the political calculations behind its outcome.

It also explores voting patterns in presidential elections since 1999, the controversy surrounding the Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket and how former Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo lost out in the succession contest ahead of the 2023 poll.

“This is a story of naivety, cat-and-mouse games, cold calculations — and subterfuge,” Kolawole said.

The 2023 presidential election had four candidates who each polled more than one million votes: Tinubu, Atiku, Obi and New Nigeria Peoples Party candidate Rabiu Kwankwaso.

The poll was also followed by controversy over delays in uploading presidential polling-unit results to the Independent National Electoral Commission’s Result Viewing Portal and legal challenges by candidates who disputed the outcome.

A central argument in the book is that no candidate has won Nigeria’s presidency in the Fourth Republic without building a competitive coalition across at least two of the country’s three largest voting blocs — Hausa-Fulani, Igbo and Yoruba — alongside support from a minority geopolitical zone.

The book combines political history, electoral analysis and accounts of events behind the scenes to explain how alliances and voting patterns influenced the outcome of the election.

It will be distributed nationwide by Rovingheights bookstore.

Kolawole began his journalism career at Complete Football magazine in 1993 and later worked with TheNews/TEMPO group and City People.

He joined THISDAY in 1997 and served as editor of the newspaper from 2007 to 2012.

In 2022, he published ‘Fellow Nigerians, It’s All Politics,’ a collection of essays on leadership, democracy and national development.

title: ‘There Are People Telling Tinubu Lies About Nigerians’ Support,’ Says Baba-Ahmed
description: The National Chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, has accused some political loyalists of misleading President Bola Tinubu about the level of public support for his administration.Baba-Ahmed, who once served under the Tinubu administration as Special Adviser on Politica
content:
The National Chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, has accused some political loyalists of misleading President Bola Tinubu about the level of public support for his administration.

Baba-Ahmed, who once served under the Tinubu administration as Special Adviser on Political Matters in the Office of the Vice President, said the president’s associates could be giving him a false impression of his popularity by relying on assurances from governors and party loyalists rather than listening to ordinary Nigerians.

He made the remarks on Friday during an appearance on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief programme.

The PRP chairman said his assessment of public sentiment was based on his grassroots political connections and familiarity with the administration, which he initially supported.

“I’m a politician. I lead a political party that is entirely grassroots-based. I have very strong organic links with the people. I followed the Tinubu administration from inception. Initially, I was even part of it,” he said.

Baba-Ahmed said he was familiar with the feelings of Nigerians and was not exaggerating the widespread dissatisfaction with the government.

He identified poverty, economic mismanagement, corruption and insecurity as some of the issues contributing to the growing distance between the administration and the people.

He also suggested that some political associates were giving Tinubu assurances about his chances of securing re-election in 2027 without adequately reflecting the mood of Nigerians.

“There are a lot of people who are telling President Tinubu lies if he thinks himself, and they think that the people are with them. Just look at wherever APC goes. People either chase them away or they trigger violence,” he said.

‘Bamayi’

Baba-Ahmed also described the ‘Bamayi’ chants directed at the president as an expression of widespread dissatisfaction, insisting that the sentiment was not restricted to young people or northern Nigerians.

“This Bamayi thing, it’s not just a slogan that young people throw at APC. It’s genuinely an organic element of the way Nigerians, not just northerners, Nigerians feel,” he added.

The ‘Bamayi’ chants, which translate to ‘we don’t want’ in Hausa, were heard on November 13 after Tinubu attended Friday prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in the Garki area of Abuja.

Some protesters reportedly threw stones at the president’s convoy and destroyed APC campaign posters, prompting security operatives to intervene.

The incident attracted reactions from political figures, including Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain Segun Sowunmi, who condemned the protesters’ actions.

Sowunmi, who is also a member of the APC campaign council, criticised the destruction of campaign posters and the use of violence during an appearance on Channels Television’s *Politics Today* on Monday.

He argued that Nigerians dissatisfied with a political candidate should express their opposition through the ballot box rather than resorting to violence.

Similarly, African Democratic Congress (ADC) chieftain Dele Momodu said Nigerians were rejecting Tinubu because they were experiencing the effects of his administration’s economic policies.

Momodu, the Deputy Director-General of Media and Communications of the ADC presidential campaign council, made the remarks on Thursday during an appearance on *Politics Today*.

He linked the growing public discontent to the hardship Nigerians had experienced since the removal of the petrol subsidy.

Tinubu, who assumed office in May 2023, is seeking re-election in 2027. He is expected to face opposition from Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC).

The post ‘There Are People Telling Tinubu Lies About Nigerians’ Support,’ Says Baba-Ahmed appeared first on Channels Television.

President of the Fédération Internationale de Football Association, Gianni Infantino, has arrived in Delta State to inspect the renovated Warri City Stadium ahead of its commissioning.

Infantino arrived in Osubi, Delta State, where he was received ahead of the inspection of the sporting facility.

His arrival was announced in a post on X on Friday by the Executive Assistant on New Media to the Delta State Governor, Dr Samuel Fadele, who wrote, “FIFA President is here in Osubi to inspect the renovated Warri City Stadium.”

Speaking in an interview with Arise News, Infantino reaffirmed FIFA’s commitment to making football accessible to everyone, everywhere, stressing the importance of smaller stadiums and grassroots sporting facilities.

“Yeah, that’s what football is about, isn’t it? It’s for everyone, everywhere,” he said.

He added that football was not limited to big stadiums and the World Cup but also involved smaller facilities that brought the game closer to communities.

“It’s big stadiums, it’s the World Cup, but it’s also smaller stadiums. It’s the proximity, and to be here in Warri for me is a fantastic occasion to showcase what we are about in FIFA, what we are about in football,” he said.

Infantino also expressed excitement about his reception in Nigeria, describing his visit as an opportunity to celebrate the country’s passion for football.

“Oh yes, I’m feeling so much the love of Africa, the love of Nigeria. This is based, of course, on many years of joint life together, of projects that we’ve put in place, of changing lives of girls and boys,” he said.

He cited Nigeria’s Under-17 women’s team’s recent World Cup victory in Morocco as an example of the life-changing opportunities football could offer young people.

He said he witnessed the team’s final against Japan, adding that the victory made Nigeria and the African continent proud.

Infantino said FIFA would continue working to extend such opportunities to more girls and boys in Nigeria and across Africa.
