title: Edo unveils compendium of laws to replace Bendel-era laws
description:
The Edo State Law Reform Commission has submitted a consolidated compilation of the state’s laws to the Chief Judge of Edo State, Justice Daniel Okungbowa, ending the state’s reliance on laws inherited from the defunct Bendel State.
Receiving the document, titled Compendium of Laws of Edo State 2026
content:
The Edo State Law Reform Commission has submitted a consolidated compilation of the state’s laws to the Chief Judge of Edo State, Justice Daniel Okungbowa, ending the state’s reliance on laws inherited from the defunct Bendel State.

Receiving the document, titled Compendium of Laws of Edo State 2026, from the commission’s chairman on Thursday, the Chief Judge said previous administrations had made efforts to reform the old Bendel State laws but were unsuccessful.

He expressed optimism that the consolidated laws had captured all relevant legislation in the state.

Okungbowa, who commended the commission for what he described as a job well done, said the reform of the old Bendel State laws was long overdue, describing the presentation as a historic event.

Earlier, the Chairman of the commission, Donald Osikhena-Boih, said the consolidated laws would make governance in the state seamless, adding that they would simplify the work of both the bench and the bar.

He said the consolidated laws would provide the legislature, judiciary and executive arms of government with an accessible and reliable legal framework for carrying out their day-to-day responsibilities.

He said, “On the part of the legislature, the lawmaking organ of government, when they have these laws on their shelves, before a bill is proposed, they will check whether the law exists, whether it has been in existence or whether it has been overtaken by events.

“That alone gives them law audit, law accuracy and law pragmatism to know what and how to go about the lawmaking of the state.”

On the executive arm, Osikhena-Boih said the consolidated laws would enable government officials to conduct proper legal audits before forwarding bills to the state House of Assembly.

The chairman further said the availability of the consolidated laws would eliminate the excuse by members of the public that they were unaware of what the law provided.

He explained that having the laws readily available would encourage citizens to familiarise themselves with relevant legislation and conduct themselves in accordance with the law.

Speaking on the judiciary, the commission’s chairman noted that one of the biggest challenges facing the bench had been accessing and determining the applicability of existing laws.

He added, “When the executive is making bills to be sent to the House of Assembly, they will go into the law audit, which is the Law Reform Commission, and particularly the law bank, to know which law is in existence with regard to what they try to cure that is considered to be a vacuum in the state.

“Then going to the judiciary, and of course you know very, very well that the most herculean task the judiciary, the bench, has always faced is getting the laws articulated, or rather making the law applicable.

“If you know that the laws are in place, you want to be careful and be orderly in society. You visit the law so that in the areas of your endeavour, you will not commit unnecessary infractions of the law.”

The post Edo unveils compendium of laws to replace Bendel-era laws appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: JUST-IN: FIFA President Gianni Infantino arrives in Warri for Stadium commissioning
description:
The President of the Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA), Gianni Infantino, has arrived in Warri, Delta State, ahead of the commissioning of two football facilities in the area.
Infantino arrived at Osubi Airport on Friday morning, where he was received by Delta State Governor,
content:
The President of the Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA), Gianni Infantino, has arrived in Warri, Delta State, ahead of the commissioning of two football facilities in the area.

Infantino arrived at Osubi Airport on Friday morning, where he was received by Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori.

His visit is expected to include the commissioning of the Warri City Stadium and the football pitch at Hussey College.

The visit is being seen as a boost to grassroots football development in the state, according to former Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) president and Deputy Chairperson of the FIFA Men’s Teams Competition Committee, Amaju Pinnick.

Speaking on Arise Television, Pinnick said Infantino’s decision to visit Warri demonstrated his interest in grassroots football and the development of the game beyond major cities.

“Who will ever believe the president of FIFA will go to Warri, a subnational? Gianni loves grassroots football development,” he said.

Pinnick recalled that during an earlier visit to Nigeria, Infantino observed people playing football while they were being driven from the airport.

He said he subsequently introduced the FIFA president to the history of Hussey College, which he noted had produced 17 players for the Super Eagles.

“The first time I picked him from the airport, as we were driving, he counted the number of people playing football, and I told him about Hussey College. This idea was also crystallised. He loves football, and he has seen everything,” Pinnick said.

He added that the institution’s contribution to Nigerian football was among the reasons the visit to Warri was significant.

“Hussey College produced 17 Super Eagles. Can you hear that? So, Gianni believes in these legends. I’m happy to say that Gianni will be going to the Warri City Stadium,” he added.

title: Naira slums to N1,400/$
description:
The naira weakened further against the United States dollar at the official foreign exchange market on Thursday, closing at N1,388/$ despite a significant increase in dollar transactions.
The latest depreciation represents a loss of N8.01, or 0.58 per cent, compared with the N1,379.99/$ recorded at
content:
The naira weakened further against the United States dollar at the official foreign exchange market on Thursday, closing at N1,388/$ despite a significant increase in dollar transactions.

The latest depreciation represents a loss of N8.01, or 0.58 per cent, compared with the N1,379.99/$ recorded at the close of trading on Wednesday.

Data published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) showed that the local currency traded at an intraday high of N1,397/$ and a low of N1,370/$ before settling at N1,388/$.

The decline occurred as foreign exchange turnover increased to $800.31 million across 184 transactions, compared with $502.88 million recorded in 148 transactions during the previous trading session.

The figures represent a 59.1 per cent increase in dollar transactions, suggesting stronger activity in the official market. However, the increased turnover did not prevent the naira from losing further value.

The depreciation also widened the gap between the official and parallel market exchange rates.

Currency dealers quoted the dollar at an average of N1,439 on Wednesday, while some parallel market rates reportedly reached N1,460. Based on Thursday’s official closing rate, the difference stood at N51 and N72 per dollar, respectively.

The latest decline extends the naira’s depreciation in November. The currency weakened from N1,346.01/$ on November 2 to N1,350.45/$ on November 5 and N1,353.50/$ on November 10.

It subsequently closed at N1,363/$ on November 17, before falling to N1,379.99/$ on November 18 and N1,388/$ on Thursday.

The pressure has coincided with a significant decline in foreign exchange inflows into the Nigerian economy.

A report by Coronation Merchant Bank’s research subsidiary showed that total foreign exchange inflows fell to $807.6 million last week from $2.48 billion in the preceding week.

This represented a 67.4 per cent decline and the lowest weekly inflow in at least five weeks.

Analysts have partly linked the naira’s weakness to reduced dollar supply, speculative demand and possible capital outflows ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Although the CBN has continued to provide foreign exchange to support liquidity in the market, the latest figures indicate that increased trading activity has not translated into sufficient stability for the local currency.

Nigeria’s external reserves have also recorded slower growth in recent weeks after rising steadily for several months.

Naira undervalued, may strengthen to N1,127/$ — Fasua

Meanwhile, the Special Adviser to the President on Economic Affairs, Dr Tope Fasua, has described the naira as undervalued, saying it could strengthen to N1,127 against the dollar if the country sustains reserve growth, improves foreign exchange supply and attracts productive investments.

Fasua said the International Monetary Fund had projected about three months earlier that the naira could trade at N1,127 to the dollar.

He argued that Nigeria needed to sustain its economic reforms and increase domestic production to support the currency.

He spoke on Thursday at the National Growth and Development Forum 2026 in Abuja.

“The IMF itself said about three months ago that the naira could be trading at N1,127 to the dollar. So the naira has now become undervalued,” he said.

Fasua also highlighted improvements in some economic indicators, saying Nigeria’s economy grew by 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, while inflation declined to 14.06 per cent in October from 20.9 per cent a year earlier.

He added that external reserves exceeded $55 billion in October, when the naira traded at N1,346 to the dollar at the end of the month.

However, the country’s gross external reserves have recently recorded a slight decline. Figures cited in the report showed that reserves fell from $54.76 billion to approximately $54.71 billion as of Wednesday.

The reserves had reportedly reached about $55.26 billion in October before falling below $55 billion on November 9.

Despite the recent decline, Nigeria’s external reserves remain above their level at the beginning of 2026.

Fasua maintained that a stronger currency must be supported by economic productivity rather than administrative measures.

“A stronger naira must be earned through a stronger economy. It cannot be legislated into existence,” he said.

Experts identify election spending, policy uncertainty as possible factors

The Chief Executive Officer of the Centre for the Promotion of Private Enterprise, Dr Muda Yusuf, identified increased political spending, uncertainty over economic reforms and speculative demand for foreign exchange as possible factors behind the naira’s recent depreciation.

Yusuf said demand for dollars could rise as political activities intensify ahead of the 2027 general elections, particularly in the parallel market, where some transactions involving cash are difficult to trace.

According to him, political spending could increase demand for physical foreign currency because some transactions may not pass through formal banking channels.

“You know that political spending and demand for dollars, especially cash, are likely to be much higher, putting pressure on the parallel market,” he said.

Yusuf also expressed concern that disagreements among political parties over the continuation of the government’s economic reforms could create uncertainty for investors.

He explained that concerns about a possible reversal of some policies after the elections might influence investment decisions and encourage capital outflows.

“We are having different perspectives now as to whether people believe in the reforms and whether they will reverse the reforms. Political parties are saying that they will reverse some of the reforms. That may also be creating some issues around political risk,” he said.

The economist warned that investors who were uncertain about Nigeria’s future policy direction could withdraw their investments.

“If you have political risk, then you have the risk of capital outflows. If you are not sure that the environment will remain as stable as it has been, the risk of capital outflows is also a possibility,” he added.

He further identified speculative demand as another possible factor, explaining that expectations of further depreciation could prompt individuals and businesses to purchase dollars in anticipation of higher exchange rates.

“People feel that the exchange rate may depreciate, and therefore they now begin to quickly buy up for speculative purposes,” Yusuf said.

Although he expressed concern about the recent movement, Yusuf said it was too early to conclude that the naira had entered another prolonged period of depreciation.

CBN’s reserve management also affects exchange rate — Okeke

Another economist, Dr Marcel Okeke, said the naira’s recent movements should be considered within the context of the CBN’s managed exchange rate system.

Okeke argued that Nigeria was no longer operating a completely floating exchange rate regime, as monetary authorities continued to intervene to manage movements in the foreign exchange market.

He explained that although the country’s external reserves had risen to about $55 billion, the funds could not be deployed entirely to defend the naira because they served several other economic purposes.

“External reserves have so many purposes. Because it is there, we cannot just take it and pump it into managing the exchange rate,” he said.

According to him, the size of a country’s reserves also influences international confidence in its economic strength and ability to meet external obligations.

Okeke added that some exchange rate fluctuations were normal under a managed system, provided they remained within acceptable limits and did not become excessively volatile.

He also identified election-related spending as a possible source of additional dollar demand, arguing that some politicians might prefer holding foreign currency because of its perceived value and acceptability.

He said increased political spending and currency conversions ahead of the 2027 elections could add further pressure to the foreign exchange market.

The post Naira slums to N1,400/$ appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: China, US, Russia Issue ‘Declaration Toward Peace’ After First Summit
description: China, the United States and Russia issued a “Declaration toward Peace” on Thursday after their leaders held an unprecedented summit, laying out common ambitions to overhaul the UN and keep the International Criminal Court in check.Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met in China
content:
China, the United States and Russia issued a “Declaration toward Peace” on Thursday after their leaders held an unprecedented summit, laying out common ambitions to overhaul the UN and keep the International Criminal Court in check.

Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met in China against a complex backdrop, with Russia’s years-long offensive in Ukraine grinding on, Trump bogged down in the Middle East and an ascendant China looking to strengthen its hand in East Asia.

“The three heads of state had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security,” a White House version of the statement said.

“We discussed the question of democracy. And what is democracy? It’s what? It’s the liberal order that certain circles put together and still now are trying to impose on the whole world,” Putin told a news conference in the southern city of Shenzhen.

The three men made opening remarks touching on weighty topics from nuclear weapons to the war in Ukraine as they met around a large, dark round table with a pink flower arrangement at its centre.

The discussion behind closed doors in Kylin Villa ended after an hour and 20 minutes.

Trump said the leaders were “making history”, while Putin said they wrote a new “page in the history of diplomacy”.

“The three countries share a common perspective on safeguarding world peace,” Xi said.

On his way home to Washington, Trump called into a meeting of European leaders to discuss Ukraine and update them on his three-way summit.

Not all of those European leaders were impressed: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the Trump-Xi-Putin talks a “photo op”, and French President Emmanuel Macron said it would not “lead to a reorganisation of the world”.

Trump said he would give a press conference on Friday about his “Great and Highly Consequential Trip” to China.

ICC, UN And Oil

In their joint statement, Trump, Xi and Putin “recognised that the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of State officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction”.

Putin is subject to an ICC arrest warrant, while Trump’s administration has vowed to dismantle the court “brick by brick”.

The leaders said they were “committed to reform the UN so that the UN can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security”.

The joint statement said the countries plan to boost supply and production of refined petroleum products, and reaffirmed the importance of “stable energy flows”.

The summit stoked fears that the three men want to divide the globe into spheres of influence, for example by making decisions impacting Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv or Europe.

But Trump said he wanted to make a deal on Ukraine “with Europe by his side”, accourding to special US envoy Jared Kushner.

‘Reducing Nuclear Risks’

Earlier Thursday, Trump and Putin held a meeting — their first since August 2025 — with the 80-year-old US president calling the Russian his “friend”.

Putin responded in English: “Nice to meet you.”

Trump and Xi then came together — their third time this year — for one-on-one discussions, with the US leader highlighting a “very special relationship”.

Putin, 74, and Xi, 73, held talks on Wednesday — their 50th meeting, the Chinese president said.

Beijing, Washington and Moscow previously gave different accounts of the agenda for the three-way meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, a forum of 21 economies around the Pacific Rim.

Washington initially signalled that Ukraine was off the table, before Trump said the war would feature. Xi does not view the conflict as China’s problem to solve.

Washington had also flagged up the Iran war and nuclear disarmament as topics of discussion, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February.

Beijing has long maintained that the United States and Russia must reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile.

The final statement said that the countries would “conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.”

– ‘Cheap violin’ –

Breaking with decades of diplomatic protocol, Xi met Trump at the airport, with the men briefly hugging before a red-carpet greeting complete with cheering children and a flyover.

Critics warned that the optics from the meeting would be damaging for the US president — but a fillip to Xi and Putin.

The meeting “gives Putin a platform to legitimise his war of aggression over Ukraine with seemingly little repercussions”, said Lyle Morris at the Asia Society Policy Institute.

“Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are playing Donald Trump like a cheap violin,” Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said.

The post China, US, Russia Issue ‘Declaration Toward Peace’ After First Summit appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Japan tightens permanent residency rules with language, integration checks
description:
Japan is introducing stricter requirements for foreign nationals seeking permanent residency, including a Japanese language proficiency standard of B1 or higher and an assessment of applicants’ understanding of the country’s laws, rules and social systems.
As reported by the Economic Times on Friday
content:
Japan is introducing stricter requirements for foreign nationals seeking permanent residency, including a Japanese language proficiency standard of B1 or higher and an assessment of applicants’ understanding of the country’s laws, rules and social systems.

As reported by the Economic Times on Friday, under the proposed framework, most applicants will be expected to demonstrate Japanese language skills equivalent to B1 level under the Reference Framework for Japanese Language Education, published by Japan’s Council for Cultural Affairs on October 12, 2021.

The requirement is intended to encourage foreign residents to integrate into Japanese society, communicate effectively, and manage everyday interactions within their communities.

However, five categories of applicants will be exempt from the standard language requirement.

They include highly skilled foreign professionals covered by specific classifications under Japan’s residence framework, qualifying family members of highly skilled professionals, and foreign nationals who have completed at least six cumulative years of primary or secondary education under Japan’s School Education Act.

Children born in Japan whose parent responsible for raising them has Japanese proficiency at B1 level or above will also qualify for an exemption.

The fifth category covers applicants granted individual exemptions by the Immigration Services Agency where applying the language requirement is considered unnecessary or inappropriate.

Understanding Japanese laws and social systems

Beyond language proficiency, applicants will also be assessed on their understanding of Japan’s laws, regulations and everyday systems.

The assessment will draw on the government’s Living and Working Guidebook, which provides foreign residents with information about living and working in the country.

Applicants who demonstrate limited understanding of these rules or show little willingness to learn about them could receive an unfavourable assessment.

The Commissioner of the Immigration Services Agency will determine the procedures for conducting this assessment.

Seven categories eligible for relaxed residency conditions

Separately, Japan’s immigration framework allows the Minister of Justice to grant permanent residency to certain categories of foreign nationals even when they do not satisfy all the standard eligibility requirements.

The seven categories are:

Spouses of Japanese citizens.
Children of Japanese citizens.
Spouses of permanent residents.
Children of permanent residents.
Spouses of special permanent residents.
Children of special permanent residents.
Individuals recognised as requiring international protection by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) or another recognised international organisation.

For individuals recognised under international protection frameworks, the financial self-sufficiency requirement may be waived, subject to additional conditions established by the Ministry of Justice.

Applicants in the other categories are generally still expected to demonstrate financial independence.

Exemptions do not guarantee approval

Despite the relaxed conditions available to certain groups, eligibility does not automatically translate into permanent residency approval.

Applicants must generally demonstrate good conduct, comply with Japanese laws and fulfil their financial obligations, including paying taxes and other public charges.

The Minister of Justice retains final authority to decide whether granting permanent residency serves Japan’s national interest.

The changes underline Japan’s emphasis on language ability, social integration, and compliance with national rules in its permanent residency assessment process.

The post Japan tightens permanent residency rules with language, integration checks appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
China raised concerns of judicial overreach after the International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, saying on Friday “such practices are not conducive” to a resolution.

Beijing’s statement comes after the top UN court determined Myanmar’s deadly 2017 crackdown on the mostly Muslim minority amounted to genocide.

China is a rare enduring partner for Myanmar after Min Aung Hlaing’s 2021 coup, which prompted Western nations to cut ties with the Southeast Asian nation.

“China is concerned about issues such as jurisdiction overreach and expanded interpretation, and believes that such practices are not conducive to the settlement of disputes,” foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told news briefing when asked about the ICJ ruling.

“The international community should make joint efforts in this direction to avoid complicating this issue,” he added.

One of the ICJ’s judges is Chinese, and voted in Myanmar’s favour on all but one count.

Asked whether Judge Xue Hanqin was acting on instructions from the Chinese government, Guo said the jurors “perform duties independently”.

Xue “expressed views based on international law and the facts of the case while drawing on professional experience… which also demonstrates a commitment to fulfilling duties”, he said.

The ruling was the first time in its 80-year history that the ICJ determined a state had committed genocide.

More than a million Rohingya live in Bangladesh, most having fled the brutal 2017 military crackdown in Myanmar.

The ICJ also ordered refugees be given safe passage home and awarded compensation, with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urging Myanmar to allow those exiled to return home.

AFP

title: EXPLAINER: How to apply for FG’s N100,000 family grant
description:
The Federal Government’s Nigeria Family Strengthening and Development Programme has outlined the eligibility requirements and application process for its N100,000 cash support for vulnerable households.
The programme, coordinated by the Hope for Indigenous Family Support Initiative’s Coordinating Of
content:
The Federal Government’s Nigeria Family Strengthening and Development Programme has outlined the eligibility requirements and application process for its N100,000 cash support for vulnerable households.

The programme, coordinated by the Hope for Indigenous Family Support Initiative’s Coordinating Office under the Federal Ministry of Youth Development, is designed to cushion the effects of economic hardship, rising food prices and economic reforms.

According to a statement by the programme’s management board sighted by PUNCH Online on Friday, the intervention was announced by the ministry on September 10, 2026, with selected beneficiaries expected to receive N100,000 in financial support.

The programme, known as the NFSP, is a cash transfer initiative targeting poor and vulnerable families across the country.

Who is eligible for the N100,000 grant?

The management board listed the eligibility requirements for prospective beneficiaries, saying applicants “must be a Nigerian citizen by birth”, have a valid National Identification Number and be between 18 and 65 years old at the time of registration.

It added that the NIN would be validated through the National Identity Management Commission.

The programme targets poor and vulnerable households identified through the Social Safety Net Systems and verified national identity records.

However, meeting the stated requirements does not automatically guarantee selection, as beneficiaries will be assessed based on poverty and vulnerability criteria.

How to apply for the grant

The management board identified the programme’s registration portal as nfsp.ng/signup, where interested individuals can submit their details for consideration.

It said the selection process would involve identifying eligible households through the Social Safety Net Systems, verifying their national identity records and assessing their circumstances against the programme’s poverty and vulnerability criteria.

“The selection process involves identifying eligible households through the Social Safety Net Systems, using verified national identity records, assessing households based on poverty and vulnerability criteria, and selecting beneficiaries in phases across the six geopolitical zones,” the board said.

It added that the programme would cover a limited number of households in each phase, meaning beneficiaries would not receive payments at the same time.

“If you have not received a notification, it does not necessarily mean you have been permanently excluded from the programme,” the board said.

How will beneficiaries receive the N100,000?

The board said payments would be made into the bank accounts submitted by selected beneficiaries.

“Selected beneficiaries will receive an SMS notification from their designated payment provider,” it said.

According to the statement, the phone number used for the notification would be obtained from the records used during the beneficiary selection process.

Recipients are expected to follow the instructions in the message and provide the required consent before the money is credited to their submitted bank accounts.

Warning against fraud

The management board warned Nigerians against paying individuals or agents who claim they can secure access to the grant or facilitate their inclusion on the beneficiary list.

It said, “Do not pay anyone to add your name to the beneficiary list.”

The board also cautioned applicants against paying anyone to release the N100,000 grant, stressing that only selected beneficiaries would receive official SMS notifications from approved payment providers.

It further advised Nigerians to avoid unofficial registration websites and rely on recognised communication channels for information about the intervention.

For enquiries and clarification, the statement provided the email address help@nfsp.ng and advised Nigerians to contact the Federal Ministry of Youth Development through its recognised communication channels.

The post EXPLAINER: How to apply for FG’s N100,000 family grant appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Vinicius battles to reclaim Real Madrid spot after Brazil revival
description:
Real Madrid have cut the gap on La Liga leaders Barcelona down to three points, without the help of Brazilian winger Vinicius Junior, who faces a fight to reclaim his place in the team.
Los Blancos have the chance to pull provisionally level with the Catalan giants on Saturday when they host Celta V
content:
Real Madrid have cut the gap on La Liga leaders Barcelona down to three points, without the help of Brazilian winger Vinicius Junior, who faces a fight to reclaim his place in the team.

Los Blancos have the chance to pull provisionally level with the Catalan giants on Saturday when they host Celta Vigo at the Bernabeu, with Vinicius in contention to play after serving a four-match domestic ban for hair-pulling.

In Vinicius’s absence, Jose Mourinho’s side beat champions Barca in the Clasico at Camp Nou, as well as scoring wins over Sevilla, Racing Santander and Valencia.

The forward started in Madrid’s Champions League victories over AEK Athens and RB Leipzig in that period but without finding the form which made him a vital player for Los Blancos over the past few years.

Vinicius, who joined Real Madrid from Flamengo in 2018, carved out a reputation as one of the most dangerous attackers in world football, helping his side win the Champions League in 2022 and 2024.

However, this season he has struggled badly for form, with his only Madrid goal coming in August against Real Sociedad.

In the interim period, Madrid’s record signing Yan Diomande has adapted well to his new club and has four goals in his last eight appearances, staking his claim for the left wing spot.

During the international break, Vinicius found some relief with Brazil, led by former Madrid coach Carlo Ancelotti.

The forward seemed unlocked, scoring five times in two friendlies against Japan and Singapore, which he hopes can be a platform to turn his domestic form around.

Vinicius admitted that this summer, during which he was heavily linked with a departure from Madrid before ultimately penning a new deal until 2032, he let his standards slip.

Brazil suffered a surprise round-of-16 elimination at the World Cup by Erling Haaland’s Norway, which took a toll.

“I don’t think I prepared myself as well as I could have after the World Cup because the impact of that tournament is very significant for all Brazilians… being knocked out so early was something we didn’t expect,” he told reporters this week.

“I used the holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in recent years.”

Vinicius said speculation on his future led to him feeling “overwhelmed” and he also highlighted the difficulty of staying at the peak of the game.

“I think only Cristiano Ronaldo and (Lionel) Messi have managed to do it for so many years, reaching the same numbers,” he added.

“I’m human, I make mistakes often, but I always try to improve.”

• Change of scene –

Vinicius’s only other goal this season came in the previous international break, for Brazil against Australia in a friendly.

Former Real Madrid player Predrag Mijatovic told Spanish radio station Cadena Ser that Vinicius seems happier playing for Brazil than his club side.

“I think last summer hurt Vinicius quite a bit because he had that doubt about whether to stay or not, whether to renew his contract or not, and he has more competition this year, right?” said Mijatovic.

“Diomande is performing well in this position, and now Mourinho is the one who has to make his own decisions.

“What’s clear is that Vini performs well when he’s happy, and I see him much happier playing with his national team than playing here.”

In previous campaigns, the Brazilian has saved his best form for the second half of the season.

“Last season, until December, I had only scored five goals. Then, I finished with more than 20 goals,” said Vinicius.

In each of the past five seasons, he has netted at least 22 times for Madrid.

On occasion Vinicius has faced criticism and whistles from the team’s own fans, but Mourinho has shown patience, while urging the most lethal version of the forward to return.

“The Vini who is at his best kills games — like he killed me in the past when I was with Benfica,” said the veteran Portuguese coach in September.

Mourinho will hope that Vinicius’s joy with Brazil can reignite his club form and bring back that killer instinct.

AFP

title: Resident doctors deny ultimatum, give FG four weeks for talks
description:
The Nigerian Association of Resident Doctors has clarified that it did not issue an ultimatum to the Federal Government over outstanding allowances and other welfare demands, but gave the government four weeks for further engagement.
The President of NARD, Dr Ogar Idoko, made the clarification durin
content:
The Nigerian Association of Resident Doctors has clarified that it did not issue an ultimatum to the Federal Government over outstanding allowances and other welfare demands, but gave the government four weeks for further engagement.

The President of NARD, Dr Ogar Idoko, made the clarification during an interview with Arise News, on Thursday.

Idoko said the association’s decision to allow further discussions followed progress recorded on some of its demands since the current leadership assumed office.

“We did not serve government any ultimatum. We just gave them four weeks so that we can go back to the drawing board and engage further with them,” he said.

He explained that although the association had previously issued ultimatums, its National Executive Council considered continued dialogue more appropriate in view of the progress made.

According to Arise News, NARD presented 17 demands at its Calabar Annual General Meeting, out of which between 13 and 14 had been addressed through engagements with the government.

“We decided to go the pathway of dialogue rather than confrontation,” Idoko said.

The association is seeking the payment of 14 months’ outstanding professional allowances and promotion arrears before Christmas.

Idoko said the Federal Government had paid four months of the 18 months’ outstanding professional allowances following an agreement reached at a tripartite meeting at the Presidential Villa.

He also disclosed that more than 400 doctors were yet to receive the 25 to 35 per cent upward review of their allowances because their names were omitted from the initial payment.

According to him, NARD had submitted the affected doctors’ details and expected the outstanding payments to be made after the completion of the November salary process.

The NARD president appealed to President Bola Tinubu to activate Article 17 of the National Constitution, as amended, to facilitate the payment of the outstanding allowances.

He insisted that the payments were not Christmas bonuses but existing entitlements owed to doctors.

“It is not a Christmas bonus. It is our due,” he said.

The association is expected to review the government’s response on December 20 and determine its next steps if the outstanding issues remain unresolved.

The clarification comes days after Idoko commended President Bola Tinubu over the Federal Government’s completion of the payment of the 2026 Medical Residency Training Fund, describing it as a “major achievement in addressing the welfare concerns of doctors”.

PUNCH Online had reported that Idoko made the remarks while reading a statement at a briefing at NARD’s secretariat in Abuja on Thursday, following the association’s Extraordinary National Executive Council meeting.

The association also praised the Federal Government for approving an upward review of the fund for 2027 and commencing payment of outstanding Professional Allowance Table arrears, with four of the 18 months owed to healthcare workers already paid.

title: Tinubu asked me to challenge governor’s impeachment – Olanipekun
description:
Chief Wole Olanipekun, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, has revealed that President Bola Tinubu personally urged him to assemble a legal team to challenge the impeachment of a state governor, warning that allowing such a removal could lead to the collapse of democracy.
Olanipekun said Tinubu called him
content:
Chief Wole Olanipekun, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, has revealed that President Bola Tinubu personally urged him to assemble a legal team to challenge the impeachment of a state governor, warning that allowing such a removal could lead to the collapse of democracy.

Olanipekun said Tinubu called him at home following the impeachment and directed him to mobilise lawyers to challenge the process, insisting that the country’s democratic system must be protected.

The senior lawyer made the disclosure on Thursday at the presentation of his six-volume book, Wole Olanipekun Through the Cases, which documents cases handled by his law firm, Wole Olanipekun & Co.

The event, held at the Body of Benchers Complex in Abuja, also marked his 75th birthday, 50 years at the Nigerian Bar and 35 years as a Senior Advocate of Nigeria.

Tinubu attended the ceremony, unveiled the books and conferred the Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger on him.

Olanipekun made the remarks while recounting his longstanding relationship with Tinubu and the President’s involvement in defending democratic institutions.

According to him, Tinubu contacted him after learning about the governor’s impeachment and asked whether he was aware that the President had accused him of being responsible for the governor’s removal.

He recalled that he was asleep when the call came and was surprised by the allegation.

Olanipekun said Tinubu told him, “Son, have you heard that the President said you have removed the governor of your state?”

He added, “He said, ‘What are you doing?’ I said, ‘I’m sleeping.’ He said, ‘There is no sleep for the wicked.’

“I said, ‘Am I a wicked person? How did I become a wicked person? Because somebody was impeached? Goodness me.’”

The senior lawyer said Tinubu subsequently instructed him to constitute a team to challenge the impeachment, warning that failure to resist such a development could undermine democracy.

He quoted the President as saying, “Please go and set up a team to fight it.

“This democracy will collapse if you allow governors to be removed that way.”

Olanipekun said he and other lawyers took up the challenge, describing the eventual Supreme Court decision as a significant moment in the country’s democratic history.

He said the apex court rejected the circumstances surrounding the governor’s removal, adding that the case demonstrated the importance of judicial intervention in protecting constitutional democracy.

“That was how it started,” he said.

Olanipekun, who was the Attorney-General of the old Ondo State, said Nigerians needed to understand that democracy went beyond elections and the transfer of political power.

He described democracy as a system built on public confidence, leadership and the protection of people’s rights.

“Democracy is the government of the people. It’s more than that. Far more than that.

“It is God. It is confidence. It is leadership,” he said.

The senior lawyer also recalled Tinubu’s involvement in challenging the dissolution of the National Assembly following the 1993 military coup led by the late General Sani Abacha.

He said Tinubu, alongside some other senators, approached him and the late G.O.K. Ajayi, SAN, at a meeting held at the residence of the late Senator Odi Adewumi on Agoro Doyin Street.

According to Olanipekun, the politicians briefed them to challenge the dissolution of the legislature in court.

He said, “At that nocturnal meeting at Agoro Doyin Street, in the residence of late Senator Odi Adewumi, you briefed my boss, one of my bosses in the profession, G.O.K. Ajayi, and myself that we should challenge the dissolution.

“We did file an action, but later withdrew it for exigencies of that time. Shortly thereafter, we didn’t see you because we couldn’t locate our clients and couldn’t be fighting any cause on behalf of a client that we don’t see, because you had disappeared. You had to travel; you had to leave.”

Olanipekun said Tinubu later returned and assigned him and other lawyers to work with senior lawyer Chi Williams on his legal matters.

He also recalled that Tinubu wrote him a letter in July 2003 after the conclusion of a legal case involving Mitchell Williams and Tinubu.

The senior lawyer said the letter contained commendations that humbled him and would be included in his memoirs.

“I’m not doing any campaign, but I’m talking as a lawyer. I’m talking of what I’ve seen.

“I’m not talking of what I’ve witnessed or what I’ve experienced. At first hand, I did not only work for you, Mr President, but you’ve always appreciated lawyers. This is very important to our profession,” he said.

Although Olanipekun did not mention the governor’s name or the state involved during his remarks, his account appears to relate to the 2006 impeachment crisis involving former Oyo State Governor, Senator Rashidi Ladoja.

In January 2006, 18 members of the Oyo State House of Assembly moved to impeach Ladoja and replace him with his deputy, Christopher Alao-Akala.

The impeachment was challenged in court, with Olanipekun among the lawyers involved in the legal battle.

The Court of Appeal nullified the removal, and the Supreme Court, on December 7, 2006, dismissed an appeal by the lawmakers who had sought to overturn the decision.

The apex court held that the impeachment process was unconstitutional.

title: Man dies after 10km race in Lagos
description:
A member of an Ikeja-based running community in Lagos, Roy Okeke, has died days after he reportedly became dizzy during a 10km race on Sunday.
The Team Active running community announced his death in a statement shared on its Instagram page on Thursday , expressing sadness over the loss of one of it
content:
A member of an Ikeja-based running community in Lagos, Roy Okeke, has died days after he reportedly became dizzy during a 10km race on Sunday.

The Team Active running community announced his death in a statement shared on its Instagram page on Thursday , expressing sadness over the loss of one of its members.

The group said what was meant to be a regular morning of fitness and community bonding turned tragic when Okeke became dizzy at about the 6km mark of the race.

“During the 10km dash organised by our sponsors on Sunday morning, while running alongside some of our members, he reportedly became dizzy at about the 6km mark,” the statement said.

According to the community, Okeke was immediately attended to and rushed to a hospital by ambulance.

“At the hospital, he experienced some seizures, but the doctors were able to stabilise him and bring him back to normal,” it added.

However, the group said he died on Tuesday despite the medical intervention.

“Sadly, despite these efforts, he eventually passed away on Tuesday,” the statement said.

Describing the deceased as an important member of the community, Team Active said his death had left members heartbroken.

“Team Active has always been more than just a running community. We are a family built on friendship, shared experiences, love and a passion for staying active. And today, we have lost one of our own,” it said.

The group extended its condolences to Okeke’s family, loved ones and others affected by his death.

“Our thoughts and prayers are with his family, loved ones and everyone who has been affected by this tragedy,” it said.

It also acknowledged the emotional impact of the incident on members who were present during the race.

“We also want to send our love and strength to the members who were present that morning and witnessed the unfortunate events,” the statement added.

As part of its mourning, the community announced the suspension of its scheduled runs for the following day and Saturday.

“In honour of our departed member and out of respect for this difficult moment, there will be no scheduled run tomorrow or on Saturday morning,” it said, adding that the decision was to give members time to “pause, reflect, mourn and stand together as a community.”

title: EPL: My ex-agent blocked dream move to Arsenal – Mudryk
description:
Tottenham Hotspur winger Mykhaylo Mudryk has claimed that his former agent failed to make his dream move to Arsenal happen before he eventually joined Chelsea in January 2023.
The Ukrainian winger has revealed that Arsenal were always his preferred destination, insisting that playing for the North L
content:
Tottenham Hotspur winger Mykhaylo Mudryk has claimed that his former agent failed to make his dream move to Arsenal happen before he eventually joined Chelsea in January 2023.

The Ukrainian winger has revealed that Arsenal were always his preferred destination, insisting that playing for the North London club and moving to the Emirates Stadium was his dream.

As reported by Fabrizio Romano on X, speaking on Guest of Gordon on Thursday, Mudryk opened up about his desire to join Arsenal and explained how his transfer situation unfolded behind the scenes.

“Before going to Chelsea, I wanted to join Arsenal. It’s no secret,” Mudryk said.

“Arsenal were the club I wanted to play for, and moving to the Emirates was my dream.”

However, the 25-year-old made a surprising allegation about his former agent, claiming that there were no genuine attempts to secure his desired move to Arsenal.

According to Mudryk, his former representative was more interested in making money through the negotiations than helping him join his preferred club.

“There weren’t even any attempts to make my dream come true and move to Arsenal. The attempts from my previous agent were only to earn more money,” he revealed.

Mudryk further explained that he was unaware of the alleged financial motivations at the time and only discovered the situation surrounding commissions and other financial arrangements later.

“But at the time, I didn’t know about it. I only understood about the commission and all the rest later on,” he added.

Arsenal were heavily linked with Mudryk during the January 2023 transfer window, but Chelsea eventually won the race for his signature, completing a deal with Shakhtar Donetsk worth an initial €70 million, potentially rising to €100 million with add-ons.

Mudryk’s latest comments have shed new light on the transfer saga, with the winger suggesting that joining Chelsea was not his original choice and that his dream of playing for Arsenal was never genuinely pursued by his former representative.

The post EPL: My ex-agent blocked dream move to Arsenal – Mudryk appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: ₦5bn libel suit: Court to rule on APC elders’ objection January 27
description:
The Ondo State High Court sitting in Akure has reserved ruling until January 27, 2027, on whether a preliminary objection in a N5bn libel suit against 35 All Progressives Congress elders should be heard separately or alongside the substantive case.
The suit was instituted by the state Commissioner f
content:
The Ondo State High Court sitting in Akure has reserved ruling until January 27, 2027, on whether a preliminary objection in a N5bn libel suit against 35 All Progressives Congress elders should be heard separately or alongside the substantive case.

The suit was instituted by the state Commissioner for Finance, Omowunmi Isaac, and Kunle Odide against the party elders in Owo Local Government Area over an allegedly libellous publication in a national newspaper in February.

The claimants are seeking N5bn in damages and an order directing the defendants to publish apologies to them in three national newspapers, among other reliefs.

The PUNCH had reported that the commissioner and Odide instituted the action against the 35 elders over the publication.

At the proceedings on Thursday, the first defendant, Kola Olawoye, SAN, asked the court to hear the defendants’ preliminary objection alongside the substantive suit to avoid wasting judicial time.

However, counsel for the claimants, Olaoluwa Imoru, opposed the application, arguing that the objection was a threshold issue that should be determined before the substantive trial.

Imoru said resolving the objection first would prevent the parties from spending time and resources on proceedings that could become unnecessary if the court eventually upheld it.

The presiding judge, Justice Yemi Fasanmi, adjourned the matter until January 27, 2027, for a ruling on the application.

Speaking with our correspondent after the proceedings, Olawoye said the case was scheduled for the hearing of the defendants’ preliminary objection, but they sought the court’s permission to defer it until the substantive suit so that both issues could be considered together and reflected in the final judgment.‎

‎”This is to safeguard against the wastage of precious judicial time on the preliminary objection. It is an issue of jurisdiction, which can be raised at any stage of the trial, even for the first time at the Supreme Court,” he said.

Olawoye, a former Ondo State Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, said the party elders remained willing to reconcile with the claimants but could not compel them to withdraw the suit.

“We, as elders and leaders of this party, are open 24 hours a day, seven days a week, to resolving issues and reconciling members of the party,” he said.

He added that the defendants had a responsibility to respond to the court action and could not avoid the proceedings because of the disagreement.

On his part, the claimants’ counsel, Imoru, maintained that the preliminary objection should be decided before the substantive case proceeds.

He said, “‎By its nature, a preliminary objection is an application through which a party argues that a case, as presently constituted, is not maintainable in law.
‎
“‎To that extent, we believe it is a threshold issue. As the name implies, a preliminary issue is something that should be addressed as quickly as possible, even before the parties begin dissipating energy on the trial and proceeding further with the case.
‎
“‎This is because, if a preliminary objection is upheld, whatever proceedings have taken place could amount to an exercise in futility. ‎That was our position. We believe it is better to address the issue now and take a decisive step on the preliminary objection before proceeding further with the substantive matter.”

The post ₦5bn libel suit: Court to rule on APC elders’ objection January 27 appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Atiku demands independent audit of INEC’s proposed AI system
description:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has called on the Independent National Electoral Commission to open its proposed Artificial Intelligence system to independent audit before deploying it to process results in the 2027 general elections.
 Atiku warned that the use of AI in election result manageme
content:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has called on the Independent National Electoral Commission to open its proposed Artificial Intelligence system to independent audit before deploying it to process results in the 2027 general elections.

 Atiku warned that the use of AI in election result management without adequate transparency and safeguards could undermine public confidence in the electoral process, particularly if algorithms were allowed to delay, reject or interfere with the transmission of polling unit results.

 He asked the electoral commission to disclose the technical and operational details of the system, including its source code, training data, discrepancy-detection criteria and the identities of its developers and third-party vendors.

 The former vice president made the demands in a petition addressed to the INEC Chairman on behalf of the African Democratic Congress and allied democratic stakeholders.

 In a statement issued on Thursday by the Director of Strategic Communication, African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said independent cybersecurity experts, representatives of political parties and civil society technologists should be granted access to the system for a comprehensive audit before the nationwide mock accreditation exercise scheduled for November 28, 2026.

 He expressed concern over INEC’s announced integration of AI and intelligent document processing into the process linking its Data Verification and Authentication System (DIVAS) with the INEC Result Viewing portal (IReV).

 According to him, Nigerians must be allowed to understand how the technology works and the extent of its influence on the handling of election results.

 “INEC cannot ask Nigerians to trust a system whose rules they are forbidden to see. If an algorithm can flag a polling unit result sheet, the public deserves to know what triggers that flag, who set the threshold, who can change it and what happens to the result afterward,” he said.

 Atiku cautioned that technical limitations could cause legitimate result sheets to be flagged or delayed, citing poor lighting, unfamiliar handwriting and worn-out paper as possible challenges that could affect the system’s ability to recognise uploaded documents.

 He argued that such technical difficulties should not become grounds for withholding valid election results, insisting that similar discrepancies must be treated consistently across polling units.

 The former presidential candidate also demanded that INEC establish and publicise a clear procedure for reviewing results flagged by the AI system.

 He said the commission must explain who would review such results, how decisions would be documented, how political parties would be notified and the mechanism available for promptly challenging erroneous assessments.

 Atiku maintained that AI should serve only as an administrative tool under human supervision and must not be empowered to delete, alter or permanently block election results.

 He further insisted that the commission must reaffirm the legal status of Form EC8A, the polling unit result sheet completed and signed by presiding officers and party agents.

 “The polling unit result sheet, Form EC8A, records what happened where the people voted. INEC must publicly reaffirm the legal status of the physical form completed and signed at the polling unit, and explain how it will resolve any conflict between that document and an AI assessment.

 “A machine’s verdict cannot be allowed to quietly displace the evidence witnessed by voters and party agents,” he added.

 The ADC presidential candidate also called for real-time monitoring access for political parties through a dedicated dashboard or observer interface to enable them to identify unusual patterns of result flagging, upload delays and blocked submissions during elections.

 He urged the National Assembly to summon INEC’s leadership and its Information and Communication Technology Directorate to explain the system’s design, safeguards and independent audit arrangements.

 Atiku also called on election observers and international partners to extend their monitoring activities beyond polling unit activities to include the digital handling and transmission of results.

 He advised voters to lawfully document results as announced and displayed at their polling units to provide a public record against which electronically uploaded results could be verified.

 The former vice president linked the demand for transparency to his campaign’s promise of an affordable life, arguing that Nigerians must be allowed to freely determine their political future without technological interference.

 “Voters must be free to accept or reject that promise at the ballot box. No hidden algorithm should stand between a struggling family’s vote and the change that family hopes to see,” he said.

 He urged INEC to address the concerns before public mistrust over the technology escalates into an electoral crisis.

 The demand comes amid growing attention to the role of technology in Nigeria’s electoral process, particularly following controversies surrounding the electronic transmission and public viewing of polling unit results in previous elections.

 INEC’s IReV portal was introduced to provide public access to scanned copies of polling unit result sheets, although its role is distinct from the statutory collation and declaration of election results.

 The proposed use of AI in processing election documents has raised questions about transparency, accountability, human intervention and the safeguards required to ensure that technological tools do not compromise the integrity of votes cast by Nigerians.

The post Atiku demands independent audit of INEC’s proposed AI system appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Provide evidence of doping allegations against Ukraine, Shevchenko tells Mudryk
description:
Ukraine football legend Andriy Shevchenko has challenged Mykhailo Mudryk to provide evidence to support his allegations against the Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF) over his doping ban.
Shevchenko, who is president of the UAF, responded after the Tottenham winger accused the football associat
content:
Ukraine football legend Andriy Shevchenko has challenged Mykhailo Mudryk to provide evidence to support his allegations against the Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF) over his doping ban.

Shevchenko, who is president of the UAF, responded after the Tottenham winger accused the football association of contributing to his 20-month absence from football following a positive test for the banned substance meldonium.

Mudryk, who joined Tottenham on a season-long loan from Chelsea, was suspended from November 2024 until July 2026 after testing positive for the substance.

The 25-year-old believes meldonium entered his system while he was on international duty and accused the UAF of mishandling his case, leaking information and delaying his return to football.

As reported by BBC Sport on Thursday, however, Shevchenko strongly rejected the allegations, describing them as a “baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally”.

He also made a serious allegation against Mudryk’s representatives, claiming they repeatedly approached the UAF to find an employee willing to accept responsibility for the presence of meldonium in the player’s doping sample.

“His representatives repeatedly approached the UAF with a proposal to find an employee who would falsely take responsibility for the meldonium found in his doping sample,” Shevchenko said.

“The UAF refused, as such a proposal contradicts the principles of our work.”
Shevchenko further maintained that investigations and audits conducted during the case had failed to establish when or where the banned substance entered Mudryk’s system.

He also defended the support provided to the winger during his time with the national team, insisting that officials respected Chelsea’s request not to administer any medication to the player while he was on international duty.

According to Shevchenko, national team head coach Serhiy Rebrov also approved Mudryk’s request to work with two personal specialists during training camps.

“Head coach Serhiy Rebrov also approved for Mykhailo to have two of his personal specialists work with him at the training camps,” he added.

“These were the exact people who monitored his regimen and recovery, and helped him with his daily routine.”

Shevchenko said the UAF completed the necessary checks and provided Mudryk’s representatives with the information they requested while maintaining contact with those handling the case.

He also expressed confidence in the professionalism of the national team staff, insisting that he had no reason to doubt their conduct.

The UAF president challenged Mudryk to produce evidence supporting his accusations and demanded a public apology if he could not substantiate them.

“If Mykhailo has evidence to back up his words, let him provide it. If no such evidence exists, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologise to the people whose honesty and professionalism he has called into question,” Shevchenko said.

BBC Sport reports that it has contacted Mudryk’s representatives for comment.

The post Provide evidence of doping allegations against Ukraine, Shevchenko tells Mudryk appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: Obi will defeat APC in Anambra despite Soludo’s backing — Dele Momodu
description:
A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress, Dele Momodu, has dismissed Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo’s prediction that President Bola Tinubu will win the 2027 presidential election, insisting that Nigeria Democratic candidate, Peter Obi, will defeat him in the state.
Momodu, the Deputy
content:
A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress, Dele Momodu, has dismissed Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo’s prediction that President Bola Tinubu will win the 2027 presidential election, insisting that Nigeria Democratic candidate, Peter Obi, will defeat him in the state.

Momodu, the Deputy Director-General of Media and Communications of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, said Obi would defeat Soludo “spectacularly” during the election.

“With due respect to Prof. (Soludo), he has joined those people I said were speaking like robots about Tinubu.

“I guarantee you that Peter Obi will disgrace him spectacularly during the election,” he said.

The former Peoples Democratic Party presidential aspirant made the remarks on Thursday while appearing on Channels Television’s Politics Today.

The comments came after Soludo handed over the All Progressives Grand Alliance flag to Vice-President Kashim Shettima as the party formally adopted President Bola Tinubu for the 2027 presidential election.

Asked whether Obi could win Anambra despite Soludo and former governor Chris Ngige supporting Tinubu, and whether he had seen the crowd at the All Progressives Congress rally in the state, Momodu dismissed the significance of the gathering.

“It’s good to see the crowd, but I am telling you they are beginning to nauseate Nigerians, and that is why Nigerians are shouting ‘bamayi, bamayi’,” he said.

He also claimed that criticism of Tinubu was growing, with leaders increasingly expressing dissatisfaction with the President.

Commenting on the APC’s campaign activities across the country, Momodu argued that the ruling party’s extensive mobilisation reflected its concerns about the outcome of the election.

“The only reason they are going everywhere feverishly is because they know they will lose the election. I am 66-plus. I have never seen this kind of campaign where the President is beginning to sound like an opposition leader,” he said.

Momodu also accused Tinubu of treating APC governors like “robots”, alleging that their public statements appeared coordinated.

“I monitored each of the governors. Let me tell you emphatically that they are being treated like robots. There is no question about it,” he said.

Soludo had earlier on Thursday declared that Tinubu did not need to rig the 2027 election because his administration’s performance would secure his re-election.

Speaking at an APC presidential campaign rally in Anambra State, the governor said the ruling party had a stronger nationwide presence than its opposition rivals.

“To our people, this election, to the best of our knowledge, is already won and lost. The President doesn’t need to rig the election. President Tinubu doesn’t need to rig the election.

“All over the country today, in every state of Nigeria, it is President Tinubu and Shettima’s ticket versus one other party. Whereas you have some other candidates who are strong in some parts of the country but don’t exist in others,” he said.

Obi, who contested the 2023 presidential election on the platform of the Labour Party, won Anambra State and finished third nationally with more than six million votes.

He is seeking the presidency again in 2027 on the platform of the NDC, where he is expected to face Tinubu of the APC, Atiku Abubakar of the ADC and Omoyele Sowore of the African Action Congress.

The post 2027: Obi will defeat APC in Anambra despite Soludo’s backing — Dele Momodu appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: INEC awaits appeal ruling as ADC factions clash
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has said its position on the leadership crisis rocking the African Democratic Congress will be guided by the outcome of the appeal pending before the Court of Appeal against the judgment nullifying the leadership of former Senate President David Mark.
Ho
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has said its position on the leadership crisis rocking the African Democratic Congress will be guided by the outcome of the appeal pending before the Court of Appeal against the judgment nullifying the leadership of former Senate President David Mark.

However, the Nafiu Bala Gombe-led faction has urged the commission to immediately comply with the subsisting judgment of the Federal High Court by recognising its leadership and removing the names of Mark and former Minister of Interior, Rauf Aregbesola, from its records.

INEC National Commissioner, Mohammed Haruna, disclosed the commission’s position to The PUNCH on Wednesday, saying it had been formally served notice of the appeal and would await the appellate court’s decision before determining its next course of action.

“The case is already in the Court of Appeal; they’ve already appealed. We’ve been served notice of the appeal, so we can’t pretend that we don’t know what is happening,” Haruna said.

He added, “So, that in itself serves in a way, as a kind of scale, so we’ll have to await the outcome of the Court of Appeal.”

However, counsel to Gombe, whose suit led to the judgment against the Mark-led leadership, insisted that INEC should comply with the subsisting court orders rather than await further correspondence from the commission.

One of Gombe’s lawyers, Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Haruna Musa, told The PUNCH that INEC had yet to respond to a letter written by the factional chairman.

Asked whether the commission had responded to the letter, Musa replied, “Not yet.” He, however, maintained that the commission was not required to respond to the letter but to implement the court’s directives.

“They don’t need to reply but to comply with the orders of the court,” he said.

Asked where Gombe was likely to operate from, amid allegations that the ADC national headquarters building belonged to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Musa said, “Ask him (Nafiu Bala), we have done our bit.”

Meanwhile, the Gombe-led Board of Trustees of the ADC has asked INEC to immediately enforce the November 5, 2026 judgment of the Federal High Court concerning the party’s leadership dispute.

The board also called on the commission to remove the names of Mark and Aregbesola from its records as the party’s leaders and delist candidates uploaded to its portal by the Mark-led leadership.

The BoT, in a statement issued by its Chairman, Chief Rufus Ikanmi, said the judgment delivered by Justice Peter Lifu in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, filed by Hon. Nafi’u Bala Gombe against the ADC and four others, remained valid and binding.

Ikanmi said, “The judgment of the Honourable Court is valid, binding, and subsisting. It has not been stayed, varied, or set aside by any superior court. INEC, as a statutory body bound by the rule of law, has a constitutional duty to give full effect to it without further delay.”

He urged the commission to recognise and deal only with the leadership headed by Gombe, which he said was affirmed by the court.

He specifically asked INEC to immediately remove the names of the Mark- and Aregbesola-led leadership from its records as leaders of the ADC and delist all candidates uploaded to its portal by the faction.

The board argued that the uploads were made in violation of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (as Amended), the Electoral Act 2022 and the party’s constitution.

It also urged former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and other persons allegedly acting with the Mark-led leadership to suspend campaign activities, rallies and public engagements organised in the name of the ADC pending compliance with the judgment.

“Any continued defiance of the judgment of the Federal High Court amounts to contempt of court and a direct assault on constitutional democracy and the rule of law,” Ikanmi said.

The board called on party members and supporters to remain calm and law-abiding, adding that it was committed to peace, unity and the constitutional order of the party.

The dispute followed a judgment of the Federal High Court in Abuja, which nullified the leadership of the ADC led by Mark and invalidated decisions taken under the caretaker committee, including the process that produced Atiku as the party’s presidential candidate for the 2027 general elections.

Justice Lifu declared the Mark-led Caretaker Committee illegal and nullified the process through which it conducted the party’s presidential primary.

The court also invalidated the emergence of Aregbesola as National Secretary, alongside the appointments of other national officers and the nominations of candidates presented by the party for the 2027 elections.

The judgment followed a suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, instituted by Gombe, a former Deputy National Chairman of the ADC (North-East), who challenged the process through which Mark and other members of the caretaker committee assumed control of the party.

Gombe argued that following the resignation of the former National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu, he was constitutionally entitled to take over the party’s leadership.

He consequently asked the court to invalidate the actions of the Mark-led leadership and restrain Mark and Aregbesola from parading themselves as National Chairman and National Secretary of the party, respectively.

Upholding Gombe’s case, Justice Lifu held that the emergence of the Mark-led leadership violated the ADC constitution, relevant provisions of the Electoral Act and the 1999 Constitution.

The judge also ordered INEC not to recognise or act on decisions taken at the party’s 99th National Executive Committee meeting held on July 27, 2025.

However, the Mark-led ADC has appealed the judgment and disclosed that it had filed an application for a stay of execution pending the hearing and determination of the appeal.

A report by Arise News on Thursday, citing a senior official of the commission, said the continued listing of the candidates was connected to a subsisting Notice of Appeal and an application for a Stay of Execution relating to the judgment.

The report added that the commission could not disregard the pending appellate proceedings while considering requests for recognition arising from the ruling.

Efforts to reach the Chief Press Secretary to the INEC Chairman, Dayo Oketola, for comments were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report.

The post INEC awaits appeal ruling as ADC factions clash appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: How Mobile Payments Are Changing the Online Casino Industry
description: Walk through any Lagos market, a Nairobi matatu terminus, or a Johannesburg taxi rank and you will see the same scene: fingers tapping phones, transfers flying, balances updating in seconds. Money in Africa moves through screens now, not queues. That shift has reshaped how people pay for everything,
content:
Walk through any Lagos market, a Nairobi matatu terminus, or a Johannesburg taxi rank and you will see the same scene: fingers tapping phones, transfers flying, balances updating in seconds. Money in Africa moves through screens now, not queues. That shift has reshaped how people pay for everything, including casino entertainment. Platforms like Rocketplay32.com sit right at this intersection, letting players fund accounts through the same mobile channels they use for daily business. The change goes deeper than convenience. It rewrites trust, speed, and access for an entire industry.

Key Facts section

  1. Global mobile payment transaction value passed $1.7 trillion in 2023, and analysts project it will cross $3.5 trillion by 2028.
  2. Mobile money accounts in Sub-Saharan Africa reached 856 million in 2023, according to the GSM Association’s State of the Industry Report.
  3. Nigeria’s instant payment system, NIP, processed 11.7 billion transactions in 2024, up from 9.7 billion in 2023, per the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System.
  4. Kenya’s M-Pesa moves roughly $300 million daily, and mobile wallets now handle over 80 percent of formal payment volume in the country.
  5. A Statista survey in 2024 found that 62 percent of online casino players prefer mobile wallets over cards for deposits.
  6. The global online gambling market hit $88.6 billion in 2024, and mobile devices generated more than 70 percent of that revenue, per Grand View Research figures.
  7. Industry forecasts for 2026 predict mobile wallets will account for over half of all online casino deposits worldwide.

Why the Punchng.com Newsroom Angle Matters

Punchng.com is a major Nigerian news website covering national and international current affairs. It publishes news on politics, business, finance, crime, sports, entertainment, technology, health, and education. That editorial mix explains why payment stories keep landing on its front page. A fintech launch in Lagos is business news. A fraud ring exploiting wallet loopholes is crime news. A central bank policy shift is politics and finance rolled into one. Casino payments sit inside every one of those beats. When Punchng.com reports on mobile money growth, it also reports, indirectly, on the infrastructure that powers online slots and table games. Readers who follow business and tech coverage already understand the rails. The casino industry simply rides them.

Speed Beats Everything in the Player Experience

Old payment methods punished players with waiting. Card deposits took minutes. Bank withdrawals took days. Mobile wallets collapse that timeline to seconds. A player funds an account, spins a jackpot round, and cashes out before the kettle boils. This immediacy changes behavior. Players deposit smaller amounts more often because friction has vanished. Operators see higher engagement and fewer abandoned transactions. A 2024 report from Worldpay found that mobile wallet payments in gaming carry a 23 percent higher completion rate than card payments. Fewer failed transactions mean happier players and steadier revenue. The whole loop rewards speed, and mobile money delivers it.

Trust Rests on Familiar Technology

Skeptical players worry about handing money to strangers online. Mobile payments solve that worry through familiarity. A Kenyan player trusts M-Pesa because they use it to pay school fees. A Nigerian player trusts their bank app because their salary lands there. When a casino accepts those same channels, it borrows that trust. The transaction feels like any other bill payment. This psychological shift matters enormously. Research from the Better Than Cash Alliance shows that people adopt digital payments faster when the interface matches tools they already use daily. Casino operators who ignore this pattern lose players to competitors who embrace it.

The Unbanked Market Finally Gets a Seat

Traditional online casinos demanded credit cards, and credit cards demand bank accounts. Millions of adults across Africa never had that access. Mobile money changed the math. A player with a registered SIM and a wallet can now join games that once excluded them. GSMA data shows Sub-Saharan Africa leads the world in mobile money adoption, with agent networks reaching rural areas far beyond bank branches. This expansion brings new players into the fold. It also forces operators to design bonuses and loyalty rewards around small, frequent deposits rather than large lump sums. The industry adapts because the market demands it.

Fraud and Security Keep the Industry Sharp

Every payment revolution carries risk. Mobile wallets attract SIM-swap scams, phishing, and social engineering attacks. Nigerian newspapers report these cases regularly, and the coverage keeps pressure on providers. The casino industry responds with tighter verification, transaction monitoring, and instant dispute channels. Payment providers invest in encryption and biometric checks. Players learn to guard PINs and confirm balances. This arms race never ends, but it produces a safer ecosystem over time. The same scrutiny that exposes weaknesses also drives the fixes.

Conclusion

Mobile payments did not just add a checkout option. They rewrote who can play, how fast money moves, and where trust comes from. The news cycle proves the point daily, linking finance, tech, and entertainment into one story. Players who want to experience the shift firsthand can explore platforms built for this moment. Speed, familiarity, and access now define the industry, and mobile money carries all three.

The post How Mobile Payments Are Changing the Online Casino Industry appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
