title: Reporters face rare phone restrictions on Air Force One
description:
Reporters travelling with US President Donald Trump were asked to surrender cell phones they had used in China in a rare security precaution as Air Force One prepared to leave Shenzhen on Thursday.
“A staffer collected a number of cellphones from poolers when we got on the plane and placed them in a
content:
Reporters travelling with US President Donald Trump were asked to surrender cell phones they had used in China in a rare security precaution as Air Force One prepared to leave Shenzhen on Thursday.

“A staffer collected a number of cellphones from poolers when we got on the plane and placed them in a Faraday bag, designed to block signal,” a White House pool reporter said in a note upon returning to the US.

“This was explained to us as being a necessary cybersecurity precaution against potential spying attempts,” the report added.

According to the separate video pool report, a presidential aide collected temporary “burner” phones used by White House staff during the China visit for disposal or data wiping.

Journalists were asked to place devices they had used in the country into signal-blocking bags until the aircraft landed in the United States.

The so-called Faraday bags are designed to shield electronic devices from wireless communications, reducing the risk of surveillance or data collection.

Burner phones are temporary devices used in place of regular cell phones to protect them from potential security threats.

The video pool report said many reporters and photographers had left their regular work and personal phones, laptops and smartwatches inside the protective bags before landing in China on Wednesday.

Those devices were not collected and could be used on the return flight, while journalists who had relied on their regular cell phones during the visit were left without them.

The phones were returned to the pool reporters upon Air Force One landing stateside.

The unusual precautions followed Trump’s meetings with world leaders in Shenzhen, including Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

PUNCH Online reported on Thursday that the three countries issued a “peace declaration” following an unprecedented leaders’ summit, almost five years into the Ukraine war and with Trump bogged down in Iran.

The statement, after Xi Jinping, Trump and Putin met in China, said that they wanted to reform the United Nations, to protect diplomatic immunity and boost supply and production of refined petroleum products.

“The three heads of state engaged in an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed themselves to upholding strategic stability and international security,” said the statement published by Chinese state media and the Kremlin, but not yet by the White House.

title: ‘He will lose the election’ – Kano fortune teller predicts Gov Yusuf’s fate ahead of 2027

content:
A self-proclaimed fortune teller identified as Malam Na Shuri Zaria has stirred reactions on social media after predicting that Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, would lose the 2027 governorship election.

In a video that has gone viral on social media, the fortune teller, who described himself as an expert in divination, repeatedly insisted that Governor Yusuf, popularly known as Abba Gida-Gida, would not win a second term in office.

His prediction has generated discussions across social media platforms, with users reacting to his claims about the governor’s political future.

‎”Wallahi, tallahi, billahil-ladhi la ilaha illa huwa, Abba Gida-Gida will not win the 2027 election,” he declared, repeating the oath three times.

‎He further claimed that other fortune tellers, regardless of where they lived, knew that the governor would lose the election.

‎”Every fortune teller, whether at home or in the courtyard, knows this. I swear he will lose the election,” he said.

‎Malam Na Shuri also offered to give a car to any fortune teller who disagreed with his prediction and believed Governor Yusuf would win a second term.

‎”Any fortune teller who thinks I am lying should come forward and let us agree. I swear I will give him a car if Abba wins re-election,” he added.

‎His prediction attracted reactions from supporters of the governor, including Senator Abdulrahman Kawu Sumaila, who represents Kano South Senatorial District.

‎The senator dismissed the claim, accusing the fortune teller of misleading the public and insisting that knowledge of the future belongs to Allah alone.

‎”You are lying. You do not know what will happen tomorrow. You are only deceiving people. This is the exclusive knowledge of Allah,” Sumaila said.

‎He also challenged the fortune teller to demonstrate his alleged powers by attempting to make him lose his sanity.

‎”Come and drive me mad if you have the power to do so. My name is Abdulrahman Kawu Sumaila. The Prophet Muhammad (SAW) warned against such practices more than 1,400 years ago,” he said.

‎The senator further challenged him to use his alleged spiritual powers to help tackle insecurity and banditry rather than make political predictions.

‎”If you can, use your powers to find a solution to banditry and insecurity,” he added.

‎As of the time of filing this report, Malam Na Shuri had not publicly responded to the senator’s challenge.

‎Another fortune teller links Abba’s electoral chances to marriage

‎In a related development, another self-acclaimed fortune teller, operating on Facebook under the name Kuliya Kabara, claimed on Tuesday that Governor Yusuf’s separation from Zainab Kwankwaso could affect his chances of winning the 2027 election.

‎The fortune teller advised the governor to make efforts to reconcile with his wife before the election, claiming that their marriage was connected to his political success.

‎He reportedly argued that the governor should not allow the separation to continue with the 2027 election approaching.

‎However, no evidence was provided to substantiate the claim linking the governor’s marriage to his electoral fortunes.

‎The development comes amid growing activity by self-acclaimed fortune tellers and traditional diviners on social media, where they increasingly make predictions and offer opinions on public affairs, particularly politics.

‎Their claims have continued to generate debate among social media users, with some challenging the credibility of their predictions.

title: Atiku urges INEC to open AI system to independent audit ahead of 2027 polls
description:
Atiku Abubakar, presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to publicly disclose any artificial intelligence (AI) system it intends to use in processing polling unit results ahead of the 2027 general elections.
A
content:
Atiku Abubakar, presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to publicly disclose any artificial intelligence (AI) system it intends to use in processing polling unit results ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Atiku also demanded that any such technology be subjected to independent scrutiny to ensure transparency and prevent possible interference with the electoral process.

In a statement issued on Thursday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, the former vice-president said Nigerians deserve to know whether an automated system would have the power to delay, reject or interfere with the transmission of election results before voting begins.

Atiku disclosed that he had written to the INEC chairman on behalf of his party and other democratic stakeholders, requesting full transparency regarding the commission’s planned use of artificial intelligence.

He said his demands include algorithmic transparency, an independent audit of the technology and clearly defined rules to ensure proper human oversight of any automated system used during the elections.

The call follows INEC’s announcement that it would integrate AI and intelligent document processing into the process linking its data verification and authentication system (DIVAS) with the INEC result viewing portal (IReV).

“If an algorithm can flag a polling unit result sheet, the public deserves to know what triggers that flag, who set the threshold, who can change it and what happens to the result afterward,” the statement reads.

The ADC candidate warned that result sheets could be flagged or delayed because of poor lighting, unfamiliar handwriting or worn paper, adding that such decisions could affect voters’ rights.

“Nor can INEC leave room for a system that treats errors in one area as harmless while treating similar errors elsewhere as grounds to delay results,” he said.

“Such decisions would affect real votes, cast by real people, whose rights cannot be made dependent on secret software settings.”

Atiku asked INEC to publish the system’s technical and operational framework, including the sources of its training data, the criteria for flagging discrepancies, and the identities of its developers and third-party vendors.

He also demanded that independent cybersecurity experts, political party technology representatives and civil society technologists be granted access to the source code, training data and decision logs to conduct a meaningful audit before the nationwide mock accreditation scheduled for November 28, 2026.

The former vice-president called on the commission to publish a clear procedure for handling result sheets flagged by the system, including who reviews them, how decisions are recorded, how political parties are notified and how errors can be promptly challenged.

He said AI must remain an administrative aid under human supervision and should not have the power to automatically delete, alter or permanently block a result.

“The polling unit result sheet, Form EC8A, records what happened where the people voted. INEC must publicly reaffirm the legal status of the physical form completed and signed at the polling unit and explain how it will resolve any conflict between that document and an AI assessment,” he said.

“A machine’s verdict cannot be allowed to quietly displace the evidence witnessed by voters and party agents.”

Atiku also demanded that political parties be granted real-time monitoring access through a dedicated dashboard or suitable observer interface to enable them to detect unusual patterns of flagging, delays or blocked uploads during elections.

He called on the national assembly to summon INEC’s leadership and ICT directorate to provide public explanations on the system’s design, safeguards and audit arrangements.

The former vice-president urged election observers and international partners to monitor the digital handling of results alongside events at polling units.

He added that voters should lawfully document results as announced and displayed at their polling units, providing a public record against which uploaded results can be checked.

title: EFCC presents 13 new evidence against ex-power minister Olu Agunloye over $6bn Mambilla project
description:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has submitted 13 additional pieces of evidence in the ongoing trial of former Minister of Power and Steel, Olu Agunloye, before the Federal Capital Territory High Court in Abuja.
Agunloye is standing trial on an amended seven-count charge bordering
content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has submitted 13 additional pieces of evidence in the ongoing trial of former Minister of Power and Steel, Olu Agunloye, before the Federal Capital Territory High Court in Abuja.

Agunloye is standing trial on an amended seven-count charge bordering on disobedience of presidential directives, receiving gratification and forgery.

The case is connected to the award of the $6 billion Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Project contract to Sunrise Power Transmission Company Limited by Agunloye during his time as minister between 2002 and 2003.

The EFCC is prosecuting the former minister over allegations linked to the controversial contract award.

At the resumed proceedings on Thursday, Abba Mohammed, prosecution counsel, told the court that the business of the day was the re-examination of Liyel Imoke, the sixth prosecution witness, who is a former minister of power and steel.

Mohammed said the prosecution had filed 13 additional proofs of evidence dated November 18, 2026, to address some salient issues in the trial.

“The documents attached are 13 proofs of evidence that relate to issues raised by the defence during cross examination,” Mohammed was quoted as saying in a statement issued by the EFCC.

“With your kind permission, My Lord, I am ready to proceed with the re-examination.”

Adeola Adedipe, the counsel to Agunloye, told the court that the documents were served on him on Wednesday.

Adedipe said he would not be prepared to proceed with the re-examination if the prosecution intended to rely on the documents.

Jude Onwuegbuzie, the presiding judge, asked the prosecution to proceed with the re-examination on other matters.

The judge said the defence should be given until the next adjourned date to enable Adedipe to study the documents.

During the re-examination, the prosecution showed Imoke “exhibits EFCC 3D and 3K”, which contain the minutes of the federal executive council (FEC) on May 21, 2003.

Mohammed asked Imoke to confirm whether the deliberations, conclusions and resolutions of the FEC meeting on that day regarding the memorandum submitted by the defendant were the same in form or shape.

Imoke responded that the exhibits were the same.

The judge adjourned the matter until November 26, 2026, for continuation of trial.

On November 11, Imoke told the court that FEC did not approve the $6 billion Mambilla power project contract awarded to Sunrise Power by Agunloye.

Imoke said the contract award was invalid because it had not been approved by the council.

He added that the May 21 meeting was the last FEC meeting before the cabinet was dissolved.

Key Facts

Fraud statistics tell a blunt story. These numbers show how much money and data sit exposed every day:

  1. Global payment fraud losses reached $48 billion in 2023, and analysts expect that figure to climb past $60 billion by 2027, per industry tracking cited by Statista.

Why Do Criminals Target Casino Accounts?

title: Jonathan’s sacrifice rare among politicians – LP chair
description:
The National Chairman of the Labour Party, Senator Nenadi Usman, on Friday questioned whether any presidential candidate ahead of the 2027 general election possesses the statesmanship, humility and commitment to national interest as demonstrated by former President Goodluck Jonathan.
She said Jonath
content:
The National Chairman of the Labour Party, Senator Nenadi Usman, on Friday questioned whether any presidential candidate ahead of the 2027 general election possesses the statesmanship, humility and commitment to national interest as demonstrated by former President Goodluck Jonathan.

She said Jonathan’s decision to sacrifice his personal political ambition to preserve Nigeria’s unity and democracy remained a rare demonstration of leadership that contemporary politicians should emulate.

Usman stated this in a birthday tribute to Jonathan, who turned 69, describing his love for the country, kindness and willingness to put national interest above personal ambition as defining qualities of his leadership.

The former finance minister, who described Jonathan as her boss and mentor, said his decision to prioritise peace over political considerations during his presidency raised questions about whether current presidential hopefuls would make similar sacrifices for the country.

“As Commander-in-Chief, you chose peace over political showmanship. And, as I have often wondered, given the enormity of the inflammatory rhetoric emanating from the camps of political actors today, one cannot help but ask whether any of the present-day presidential candidates would demonstrate the same statesmanship and make such enormous personal sacrifices in the overriding interest of our nation,” she said.

The LP chairman recalled Jonathan’s famous declaration that his ambition was not worth the blood of any Nigerian, saying the former President demonstrated his commitment to the principle when the opportunity arose.

She said, “It is this uncommon love for Nigeria that made you sacrifice your personal political ambition in the service of our nation. You famously told Nigerians that your ambition was not worth the blood of any Nigerian, and when the time came to practise what you preached, you lived up to that principle.

“As I have always maintained, the democracy we enjoy today is still standing because of the enormous sacrifices you made for our nation.”

Jonathan had explained that he conceded defeat to the late President Muhammadu Buhari in the 2015 presidential election without resistance because he regarded him as a statesman who loved God and Nigeria.

The LP chairman also praised Jonathan’s continued involvement in governance and democratic development after leaving office in 2015, particularly through the Goodluck Jonathan Foundation.

According to her, the former President has remained committed to promoting good governance and credible elections across Sub-Saharan Africa.

She further recalled Jonathan’s November 17 admonition to Nigerian politicians to demonstrate patriotism and exercise restraint in their public statements and actions ahead of the 2027 elections.

Usman urged political actors to heed the former President’s advice and avoid actions capable of undermining the country’s democratic process.

She said, “I continue to pray that our present-day political actors will see reason in your timely admonition, embrace peace and conduct themselves with the decency, decorum and restraint that our democracy demands as we approach the next elections.”

Usman wished Jonathan good health and a long life, saying Nigeria still had much to benefit from his experience and wisdom.

“Our nation still has so much to benefit from your wealth of experience, wisdom and, above all, your abundant milk of human kindness,” she added.

content:
Morning recap: ‘Bamayi’ chant sparks APC convoy attack, FG suspends Lagos-Ibadan bridge work, other stories

Saheed Oyelakin

Top headlines this morning include violence that erupted in Gombe after youths chanted the anti-APC slogan “Bamayi” at a party campaign convoy, leaving buses damaged and supporters injured.

The Federal Government has suspended pedestrian bridge construction on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway after a gridlock that stranded motorists for more than 20 hours.

Meanwhile, the Central Bank of Nigeria’s cash mop-up has more than doubled ahead of the 2027 elections while Lagos court has restrained Jimmy Odukoya from acting as senior pastor of the Fountain of Life Church.

The recap in full:

‘Bamayi’ chant sparks violence as suspected thugs attack APC convoy in Gombe

An anti-All Progressives Congress slogan, “Bamayi” (meaning rejection or lack of support), triggered a confrontation in Kwarge, Balanga Local Government Area of Gombe State.

The APC campaign convoy travelling from Cham to Bambam was attacked after youths emerged chanting the slogan.

Read the full story below: https://punchng.com/bamayi-chant-sparks-violence-as-suspected-thugs-attack-apc-convoy-in-gombe/

FG suspends Lagos-Ibadan bridge work after 20-hour

The Federal Government has suspended construction of a pedestrian bridge at the Aseese area of the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway after a diversion caused a traffic jam that lasted more than 20 hours from Wednesday afternoon into Thursday.

Motorists were stranded for hours, many abandoned their vehicles and trekked, while commercial operators hiked fares sharply.

Read the full story below: https://punchng.com/fg-suspends-lagos-ibadan-bridge-work-after-20-hour-gridlock/

CBN’s cash mop-up more than doubles ahead of 2027

The Central Bank of Nigeria withdrew more than N90tn from the financial system through Open Market Operations in the first 11 months of 2026, more than double the N40.9tn absorbed in 2025, as it seeks to contain excess liquidity and inflationary pressures ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Monetary Policy Committee members and analysts have warned that election-related spending could inject substantial funds into the economy and complicate disinflation efforts.

Read the full story below: https://punchng.com/cbns-cash-mop-up-more-than-doubles-ahead-of-2027/

ASUP strike rocks four S’West states

The Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics, Zone C, has directed all its chapters in state-owned polytechnics, colleges of technology and monotechnics in Ogun, Oyo, Osun and Ekiti states to embark on industrial action over the non-implementation of the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance and Earned Academic Allowance.

The strike took effect on Monday, November 16, after a 15-day ultimatum expired.

Read the full story below: https://punchng.com/asup-strike-rocks-four-swest-states/

Court restrains Jimmy Odukoya from acting as Fountain of Life pastor

The Lagos State High Court has restrained Jimmy Odukoya from holding himself out as the senior pastor and spiritual head of the Fountain of Life Church.

Justice O. O. Adewunmi-Oshin issued the order in a suit by the church’s Incorporated Trustees, who argued that he ceased to hold the position following the late founder Pastor Taiwo Odukoya’s appointment of a successor in line with the church’s constitution.

Read the full story below: https://punchng.com/court-restrains-jimmy-odukoya-from-acting-as-fountain-of-life-pastor/

Mob kills Osun accident survivor, police hunt suspects

Osun State Police have condemned jungle justice after a mob attacked and killed one of the occupants of a Toyota Camry involved in a fatal accident in Ilesa that claimed the lives of two pedestrians.

The vehicle was also set ablaze.

Read the full story below: https://punchng.com/mob-kills-osun-accident-survivor-police-hunt-suspects/

title: The weekend reset that makes your new week easier
description:
By Josephine Agbonkhese



There is something about the weekend that makes us realise just how much we have been carrying throughout the week. After days of juggling work, family responsibilities and other commitments, the weekend offers an opportunity to slow down, catch our breath and put a few th
content:
By Josephine Agbonkhese

There is something about the weekend that makes us realise just how much we have been carrying throughout the week. After days of juggling work, family responsibilities and other commitments, the weekend offers an opportunity to slow down, catch our breath and put a few things in order.

Beyond sleeping in, watching our favourite shows or catching up with friends, the weekend is also a good time to prepare for the days ahead. A few simple activities can make the transition into a new week less stressful and more manageable.

Tidy up your space

You do not need an elaborate cleaning exercise. Start with the areas you use most. Clear the kitchen counter, arrange the living room, put away scattered clothes and organise your workspace. A tidy environment can make it easier to concentrate and settle into your daily activities. It also feels good to start Monday without a pile of unfinished chores staring back at you.

Plan your outfits ahead

Save yourself the morning rush by deciding what to wear before the week begins. Check your calendar, consider your appointments and put together outfits that suit your activities. Iron your clothes, arrange your shoes and accessories, and ensure everything is ready. If you have children, preparing their school uniforms can also save valuable time. It is an opportunity to rediscover pieces in your wardrobe and experiment with new combinations.

Prepare a few meals

After a long day at work, deciding what to cook can become another chore. A little meal preparation over the weekend can help. Wash and portion vegetables, prepare a stew or soup, cook basic ingredients or simply plan your meals for the week. You do not have to prepare everything in advance. Knowing what you intend to eat can save time, reduce food waste and discourage expensive last-minute purchases.

Take a break from your screen

If your weekdays involve computers, messages and endless social media scrolling, use part of the weekend to disconnect. Put your phone aside for a few hours. Read a book, take a walk, spend time with family or enjoy a quiet moment without feeling the need to document it online. Constant notifications can make it difficult to switch off mentally. Spending some time away from screens allows you to be more present and enjoy other activities.

Review your finances

A weekend reset is a good opportunity to review your spending. Check your account balance, look through recent transactions and consider the expenses coming up during the week. Set aside money for transportation, groceries, school needs and other commitments. A simple spending plan can help prevent unnecessary financial pressure. It is not about denying yourself life’s pleasures but about knowing what you have and how best to manage it.

Make time for yourself

Between work, family and social obligations, personal time can easily become an afterthought. Dedicate part of your weekend to something you genuinely enjoy. Visit a favourite restaurant, get your hair or nails done, exercise, listen to music, watch a movie or catch up with a friend. You could also spend an afternoon doing absolutely nothing. Remember, rest is not a reward you must earn after completing every task. It is essential to maintaining your well-being.

Write down your priorities for the week

Before Monday arrives, take a few minutes to think about what you need to accomplish. Write down your important tasks, appointments and deadlines. Identify the three things that deserve your attention first. Having a written plan gives you a clearer sense of direction and makes it easier to approach your responsibilities one step at a time. It also helps you distinguish between what is urgent and what can wait.

Get enough sleep

Proper rest is perhaps the most underrated part of a weekend reset. Staying up late to squeeze in another movie or finish unfinished chores can leave you struggling on Monday morning. Maintain a regular bedtime, reduce late-night screen time and create a comfortable sleeping environment.

title: Three children orphaned in acid horror
description:
*Three Lives Left in the Shadows of Domestic Violence and Sickle Cell Struggles, after murder and suicideBy Adeola Badru



For three children in Akufo, Ido Local Government Area of Oyo State, life has become a painful journey into uncertainty. In one devastating episode, they lost both parents—the
content:
*Three Lives Left in the Shadows of Domestic Violence and Sickle Cell Struggles, after murder and suicide
By Adeola Badru

For three children in Akufo, Ido Local Government Area of Oyo State, life has become a painful journey into uncertainty. In one devastating episode, they lost both parents—the two people they should have been able to depend on for love, protection, education and survival.

Their tragedy is particularly heartbreaking because two of the surviving children reportedly battle recurrent sickle cell crises, requiring regular medication and medical attention. At a time when they need parental care more than ever, they have, instead, been left to confront grief, illness, financial hardship and an uncertain future.

Their story is not merely about the death of two parents. It is about a family reportedly torn apart by years of domestic violence, a marriage allegedly marked by repeated abuse and three innocent children left to bear the consequences of circumstances beyond their control.

The incident reportedly followed years of domestic violence. The husband, identified as 49-year-old Mr Lekan Adedeji, allegedly poured acid on his wife, 44-year-old, before ingesting the same corrosive substance. Both subsequently died.

The couple had been married for more than 25 years, but what should have been a lifetime of companionship was, according to the woman’s family, characterised by repeated physical abuse and disagreements over childbearing, even after the health implications of their genetic compatibility became known.

Speaking with Vanguard, Morufat Ashake, the deceased woman’s younger sister, who has taken custody of the children, recounted the painful circumstances surrounding the marriage and the events preceding the fatal attack.

She explained that the couple were unaware of their genotype status when they married. It was only after their first three children began experiencing recurrent illnesses that they discovered the medical implications of their genetic compatibility.

According to Ashake, Zainab eventually gave birth to six children, three of whom died from complications associated with sickle cell disorder.

The surviving children are Rashida Adedeji, 20, who is SS; Folawe Adedeji, 17, who is AS; and Folahanmi Adedeji, six, who is also AS. Rashida and the youngest child reportedly experience recurrent health crises and require consistent medical attention.

But the family’s medical challenges were not the only difficulties Zainab allegedly endured. Ashake said her sister suffered years of physical abuse from her husband, who reportedly continued insisting on having more children despite knowing the potential health implications.

Eventually, Zainab reportedly found the courage to leave the matrimonial home, hoping to escape the violence. She had been away for about three months before the incident.

Although members of the family had previously intervened and persuaded her to return, Ashake said her sister had reached a point where she could no longer endure the situation.

Sadly, the decision that should have marked the beginning of a safer chapter in Zainab’s life did not prevent the tragedy that followed.

A school fees invitation that ended in horror

Ashake traced the circumstances surrounding the fatal encounter to December last year, when Lekan allegedly contacted his estranged wife under the pretext of giving her money for their second daughter’s West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE) fees.

Believing the invitation concerned their daughter’s education, Zainab reportedly visited the house with Folawe and her youngest son, Folahanmi.

According to her account, Lekan instructed Folawe to take her younger brother outside. The teenager remained in the compound, sweeping, when she suddenly heard her mother’s screams coming from inside the house.

Alarmed, she attempted to open the door but was allegedly prevented from entering by her father.

She alleged that Lekan subsequently poured acid over Zainab’s body and attempted to force her to drink the corrosive substance.

Ashake further disclosed that before ingesting the substance, Lekan allegedly handed his mobile phone and the money intended for the children’s school fees to another person.

Both victims required urgent medical attention. Despite efforts to save Zainab’s life, she eventually succumbed to her injuries on January 23. The family reportedly spent more than N4 million attempting to secure treatment for her.

For the children, the incident meant losing their mother in particularly traumatic circumstances and subsequently being left without their father.

An ageing grandmother, three children and an uncertain future

Their maternal grandmother, 62-year-old Titilayo Ayoola, corroborated Ashake’s account, describing her daughter’s marriage as one marked by years of suffering.

Ayoola now faces the enormous responsibility of caring for three grandchildren who have lost both parents, including two who reportedly require regular medical attention.

At an age when she should ordinarily be enjoying some rest, she must now worry about medication, hospital bills, school fees and the emotional wellbeing of children struggling to comprehend their loss.

Her concern reflects the difficult reality confronting the family. Love and determination may provide emotional support, but the children also need sustained financial assistance, medical care, educational support and psychological counselling.

For Rashida, the eldest, the pain is compounded by uncertainty about what lies ahead.

Folawe, 17, who reportedly witnessed the events preceding her mother’s death, also described the family’s predicament.

Her experience is particularly distressing. At an age when she should be concentrating on her education and dreams, she is having to process a traumatic experience involving the violent loss of her mother.

Their youngest sibling, six-year-old Folahanmi, must also grow up without the daily presence of either parent.

The family previously lived in a four-bedroom flat built by Lekan in Akufo. However, the house that once accommodated the family has become associated with the violent incident that brought their marriage to a tragic end.

A tragedy that demands society’s attention

Beyond the immediate grief of the Adedeji family, the incident raises troubling questions about domestic violence and the protection available to victims seeking to escape abusive relationships.

Marriage should never become a prison in which one partner lives in perpetual fear of the other. Neither should leaving an abusive relationship expose a victim to further danger.

The family’s account also underscores the importance of genotype awareness, responsible family planning and access to proper medical counselling.

For the three surviving children, however, these lessons come amid a reality far more painful than any public discussion can capture.

They need help to continue their education, manage their medical conditions and recover from the emotional trauma of losing both parents.

Their grandmother and maternal aunt have assumed responsibility, but they cannot shoulder the burden alone.

Perhaps the cruelest dimension of this tragedy is that three children who had no control over their parents’ decisions, disagreements or relationship must now live with the consequences.

A mother is gone. A father is gone. Three children remain, carrying grief, medical challenges and questions that may never have satisfactory answers.

They did not choose the home into which they were born. They did not choose the circumstances that shaped their childhood. And they certainly did not choose to become orphans.

Yet, they must now find the strength to survive, heal, remain healthy and dream again.

For them, the tragedy is not over. It has only entered another chapter—one in which society must decide whether to look away or extend a helping hand.

Vanguard News

title: Nigeria, Russia move to ease trade, strengthen customs cooperation
description:
By Providence Ayanfeoluwa







The Nigeria Customs Service, NCS and Federal Customs Service of Russia have signed a cooperation agreement aimed at strengthening bilateral trade facilitation, intelligence sharing and customs enforcement, while exploring mutual recognition of their Authorised Econom
content:
By Providence Ayanfeoluwa

The Nigeria Customs Service, NCS and Federal Customs Service of Russia have signed a cooperation agreement aimed at strengthening bilateral trade facilitation, intelligence sharing and customs enforcement, while exploring mutual recognition of their Authorised Economic Operator, AEO programmes.

The service in a statement said the Agreement on Cooperation and Mutual Assistance in Customs Matters, CMAA provides a framework for collaboration in customs procedures, information exchange, financial integrity, border security and personnel capacity development.

Speaking, Comptroller-General of Customs, Adewale Adeniyi, who led the Nigerian delegation, described the agreement as a strategic instrument for safeguarding economic integrity, securing supply chains and strengthening trade governance.

He explained that the signing followed months of technical consultations, legal reviews and constructive engagements between both administrations.

Adeniyi explained that the NCS had accelerated its digital transformation through the adoption of electronic systems for customs declarations, payments and submission of supporting documents. According to him, the reforms demonstrate that revenue generation and trade facilitation can complement each other, in line with the World Customs Organisation’s SAFE Framework of Standards.

On the implementation of the agreement, the Customs boss identified cooperation between the two countries’ AEO programmes as a major priority.

He said both administrations would exchange experiences on their respective frameworks and operational procedures, with the long-term objective of achieving mutual recognition to facilitate the movement of cargo and reward compliant traders.

The two sides also explored arrangements for exchanging customs statistics and trade data to improve analysis of bilateral trade flows.

Adeniyi disclosed that Nigeria was participating in the World Customs Organisation’s data initiative. Russia’s Head of Customs, Valery Pikalyov, explained that his administration was authorised to collect and exchange customs statistics derived from declarations. Pikalyov expressed readiness to explore a dedicated data-sharing arrangement with Nigeria.

The agreement also provides for cooperation against customs offences, illicit financial flows, grey-market importations, tax evasion, counterfeit goods, narcotics and other prohibited or hazardous materials. It further establishes a framework for direct operational assistance, personnel training and the exchange of professional expertise between the two administrations.

title: US accuses Minnesota lawmaker-elect’s wife of illegal entry
description:
The United States Department of Homeland Security has alleged that the wife of newly elected Minnesota state lawmaker, Abdi Daisane, entered the country illegally in 2023 and has remained there without legal status.
DHS identified the woman as Ayan Ahmed Aidid, a 30-year-old Somali national, who it
content:
The United States Department of Homeland Security has alleged that the wife of newly elected Minnesota state lawmaker, Abdi Daisane, entered the country illegally in 2023 and has remained there without legal status.

DHS identified the woman as Ayan Ahmed Aidid, a 30-year-old Somali national, who it said crossed the US-Mexico border on foot on April 2, 2023.

In a statement shared on X on Thursday, the department said Aidid was apprehended by US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) agents but was subsequently released into the country by the administration of former President Joe Biden.

The statement was also shared by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), which said it would enforce immigration laws regardless of the political status or influence of those involved.

“Ayan Ahmed Aidid, the wife of newly elected Minnesota state lawmaker Abdi Daisane, is a 30-year-old Somali national who illegally crossed the southern border on April 2, 2023,” it said.

“Our nation’s immigration laws apply to EVERYONE, and the men and women of ICE will enforce them, regardless of political status or power,” the agency said.

“No one is above the law,” it added.

DHS further alleged that Aidid was released without proper vetting and had since remained in the country illegally.

The development comes weeks after Daisane, a member of the Democratic-Farmer-Labour Party, won election to represent Minnesota House District 14A, becoming the first Somali American elected to represent the St. Cloud area in the state legislature.

According to a report by US-based Alpha News, DHS confirmed Aidid’s immigration history to the outlet, which published the report on November 18.

The report said Aidid had previously spoken about her journey into the United States in a 2023 interview with BBC News Somali.

In the interview, she reportedly described climbing over the US-Mexico border fence to reunite with Daisane, saying, “I smuggled myself and jumped over the wall for my love.”

DHS also said she was apprehended about four miles west of the San Ysidro Port of Entry in California before being released.

However, Newsweek reported that it had not independently verified the department’s claims and that DHS did not provide supporting immigration records.

The publication said it contacted Daisane and Aidid for comment on Thursday, but had not received responses at the time of publication.

Daisane is scheduled to take his seat in the Minnesota House of Representatives in January 2027.

title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 20, 2026
description:
The Nigerian naira continued to face downward pressure against the United States dollar across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market on Friday, November 20, 2026, driven by tightening foreign exchange supply and rising end-of-year seasonal demand.



Offic
content:
The Nigerian naira continued to face downward pressure against the United States dollar across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market on Friday, November 20, 2026, driven by tightening foreign exchange supply and rising end-of-year seasonal demand.

Official Market Performance

Real-time interbank spot tracking at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market placed the US dollar at ₦1,352.54 during early morning trading on Friday, following an opening rate of ₦1,351.86 and an intraday peak of ₦1,355.31.

This early session trading follows Thursday’s official Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) volume-weighted benchmark, which saw the naira depreciate to a four-month low. According to official CBN data for the November 19 trading session, the NFEM weighted average rate settled at ₦1,376.58 per dollar, while the indicative closing rate rose to ₦1,388.00 per dollar from ₦1,379.99 recorded on Wednesday. Intraday interbank transactions on Thursday were conducted between a low of ₦1,370.00 and a high of ₦1,397.00 per dollar. Despite the depreciation, market liquidity improved significantly, with NFEM interbank turnover surging by 59.13 percent to $800.31 million across 184 deals, up from $502.88 million the previous day.

Parallel Market Rates

In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the local currency weakened further as Bureau de Change (BDC) operators and street dealers in Lagos and Abuja quoted the US dollar at a selling rate of up to ₦1,468 per dollar on Friday morning, following Thursday’s close between ₦1,461 and ₦1,468. Buying rates among informal currency dealers hovered between ₦1,445 and ₦1,458 depending on transaction volume and location.

With Thursday’s official closing benchmark at ₦1,388.00 and parallel market quotations reaching ₦1,468.00, the spread between the official and unofficial windows widened to ₦80.00 per dollar, compared to ₦70.01 recorded earlier in the week.

Market Drivers and Reserve Outlook

Since the end of October, when the naira closed at ₦1,346.00 in the official window and ₦1,373.00 in the parallel market, the currency has lost ₦42.00 and ₦95.00 in the respective segments. Meanwhile, Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $54.71 billion as of November 18, 2026, reflecting a moderation of $554 million from the October 27 peak of $55.26 billion.

Financial analysts note that the recent divergence between both windows is largely fueled by heightened festive import demand, corporate obligations, and reduced autonomous foreign exchange inflows rather than a structural depletion of the country’s external reserves.

title: Why we pulled down Umeh’s billboard — Anambra govt
description:
The Anambra State Government has dismissed claims that a billboard belonging to Senator Victor Umeh was pulled down because it carried the image of former Governor Peter Obi, calling the allegation false and misleading.



The government said the enforcement action stemmed from an alleged violation
content:
The Anambra State Government has dismissed claims that a billboard belonging to Senator Victor Umeh was pulled down because it carried the image of former Governor Peter Obi, calling the allegation false and misleading.

The government said the enforcement action stemmed from an alleged violation of the Anambra State Signage Act, 2010, rather than the identity or political affiliation of anyone featured on the billboard.

In a statement issued yesterday, the Commissioner for Information and Value Reformation, Dr Law Mefor, said that although Senator Umeh had paid the required signage fee, Peter Obi had not complied with the payment requirement.

Mefor alleged that the senator, instead of fully complying with the law, used the billboard to promote the presidential candidate of the New Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), thereby contravening the state’s signage regulations.

He stressed that the removal was carried out strictly in accordance with the law, which he noted was enacted during Peter Obi’s administration as governor of Anambra State.

“For the avoidance of doubt, the billboard was not pulled down because of Peter Obi’s image,” the commissioner stated.

The government further warned that any combined billboard campaign featuring candidates who had not fulfilled their signage obligations would face similar enforcement, regardless of their political party, status, or affiliation.

It maintained that the state’s outdoor advertising regulations would be guided by fairness, transparency, and even-handed application of the law.

Mefor urged the public to disregard what he described as a misleading narrative surrounding the incident, insisting that the government remained committed to due process and equal treatment in enforcing existing laws.

title: Why billboard featuring Peter Obi was removed – Anambra govt
description: The Anambra State Government has clarified that the campaign billboard belonging to Senator Victor Umeh, which featured the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, was removed over an alleged violation of the state’s Signage Act, 2010, contrary to claims that it was pul
content:
The Anambra State Government has clarified that the campaign billboard belonging to Senator Victor Umeh, which featured the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, was removed over an alleged violation of the state’s Signage Act, 2010, contrary to claims that it was pulled down because of Obi’s identity or political affiliation.

The state also dismissed claims that the billboard was removed because it bore Obi’s image, describing the allegation as false, misleading and a deliberate distortion of the facts.

In a statement issued on Thursday, the state Commissioner for Information and Value Reformation, Dr Law Mefor, said that although Umeh had paid the required signage fee, Obi had not complied with the payment requirement.

Mefor alleged that the senator, instead of ensuring full compliance with the law, used the billboard to promote the presidential candidate of the NDC, thereby contravening the state’s signage regulations.

He stressed that the removal was carried out strictly in accordance with the law, which he noted was enacted during Obi’s administration as governor of Anambra State.

The statement read, “The attention of the Anambra State Government has been drawn to claims in some quarters that Senator Victor Umeh’s billboard was pulled down because it bore the image of His Excellency, Mr. Peter Obi. This claim is false, misleading, and a deliberate distortion of the facts.

“For the avoidance of doubt, the billboard was not pulled down because of Peter Obi’s image.

“The fact is this: While Senator Victor Umeh has duly paid his signage fee, His Excellency, Mr. Peter Obi has not.

“Rather than ensure compliance, the Distinguished Senator decided to use his billboard to campaign for the NDC presidential candidate, in clear contravention of the Anambra State Signage Act, 2010, a law enacted by the Peter Obi administration itself.

“The enforcement action was therefore carried out strictly in accordance with the law, and not on account of any person, personality, or political affiliation.

“Let it also be emphasised that any combined billboard campaign involving a candidate or candidates yet to comply with the signage law will be met with similar enforcement, irrespective of party or status.”

Mefor said the Anambra State Government remained firmly committed to the fair, transparent and even-handed enforcement of all extant laws, without fear or favour.

“We will continue to uphold due process and ensure a level playing field for all in the regulation of outdoor advertising across the state.

“The public is therefore urged to disregard the misleading narrative and to be guided by the facts,” he said.

title: ESUT to be renamed after Jim Nwobodo – Mbah
description:
Governor of Enugu State, Dr. Peter Mbah, has unveiled plans to rename the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT) after a Second Republic Governor of old Anambra State, Senator Jim Nwobodo, subject to stakeholders engagement and legislative due process.







Mbah made this known du
content:
Governor of Enugu State, Dr. Peter Mbah, has unveiled plans to rename the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT) after a Second Republic Governor of old Anambra State, Senator Jim Nwobodo, subject to stakeholders engagement and legislative due process.

Mbah made this known during the 3rd Distinguished Personality Lecture of the university delivered by Nwobodo at the Barr. Peter Ndubuisi Mbah Multipurpose Auditorium, ESUT, Enugu, on Thursday.

He said the idea, which was first suggested by the ESUT Alumni Association, was in tandem with his thoughts, describing it as a fitting tribute to the elder statesman, who founded the institution in 1980.

The Governor emphasised that the brainchild of the ex-governor had played a critical role in the human capital development of not just Enugu State, but also the old Anambra State and Nigeria as a whole.

“Recently, representatives of the alumni of this university and its associated institutions came to see me.

“They asked that Enugu State University of Science and Technology be renamed in honour of Senator Jim Ifeanyichukwu Nwobodo.

“I told them that I support the proposal. I was particularly encouraged that the request came from the alumni who understand, through their own experience, what the university has meant to people’s lives.

“There is a legal process to follow. ESUT was established by law, and changing its name would require the appropriate legislative steps and engagement with relevant stakeholders.

“I intend to begin those engagements and work with the institutions concerned to advance the proposal through the proper process.

“Your Excellency, I hope that gives you some sense of the regard in which your contribution continues to be held.”

The Governor praised Nwobodo’s vision and courage in leadership, especially for investing heavily in human capital development, taking the bold step to establish ESUT a few years after the civil war, not minding the enormity of the challenges involved.

“I have often wondered what it must have felt like to be governor in 1979. Nigeria had just returned to civilian government after thirteen years of military rule.

“The Civil War had ended less than a decade earlier, and the country was still dealing with its consequences. There was much to rebuild, and enormous pressure on the resources available to government.

“For many families, university education remained beyond their reach. And here was a young governor, who decided that his state should establish a university of science and technology.

“People questioned whether it could be done. Was there enough money? Could a state government sustain such an institution? Shouldn’t this be left to the federal government?

“These were reasonable questions. I suspect some of them would have kept you awake at night.

“But for Jim Nwobodo, the fact that a problem is difficult does not mean we can afford to avoid it.

“In July 1980, Anambra State University of Technology was established. Forty-six years later, we are gathered in one of the institutions that grew from that decision. And generations of young people have gained opportunities that might otherwise have been beyond their reach,” he stated.

Mbah noted that beyond the establishment of ESUT, the Nwobodo Administration encouraged communities to build schools, with government providing teachers and other support.

“He also invested in industry, seeking to create employment and strengthen the state’s productive capacity.

“Some of those industries later fell into decline, and today we are working to bring a number of them back into use.

“The value of such decisions is ultimately found in people’s lives. A child who could attend school in their own community. A young person who became the first in their family to enter university. A household supported by employment in a local industry,” he stated.

He hailed generations of academics, administrators and staff, who have sustained ESUT through changing governments, difficult economic circumstances and the demands of educating successive generations.

“In this regard, I want to assure the university community that the Enugu State Government is committed to the full implementation of the Academic Staff Union of Universities’ agreement with the Federal Government.

“We are already speaking with legislators to firm up its inclusion in the budget for implementation as soon as possible,” he assured.

Meanwhile, a major highpoint of the event was the conferment of an Honorary Doctorate Degree in Leadership, Governance, and Human Capital Development on Nwobodo.

ESUT’s Vice Chancellor, Prof. Aloysius-Michaels Okolie, said it was in appreciation of the ex-governor’s huge contributions to the development of Enugu State, but also the entire old Anambra State, listing his many achievements.

Another highpoint was the unveiling of Senator Nwobodo’s iconic status and the commissioning of a newly constructed road, Dr. Peter Mbah Drive, by the Governor.

The post ESUT to be renamed after Jim Nwobodo – Mbah appeared first on Vanguard News.

description:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi



A farmer, identified as Mr Terkura Orvanya, has reportedly been macheted by suspected herdsmen following a disagreement over the grazing of cattle on his cultivated farm at Ikpakena village, Makurdi Local Government Area of Benue State.







Orvanya was said to have susta
content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi

A farmer, identified as Mr Terkura Orvanya, has reportedly been macheted by suspected herdsmen following a disagreement over the grazing of cattle on his cultivated farm at Ikpakena village, Makurdi Local Government Area of Benue State.

Orvanya was said to have sustained serious machete wounds while attempting to defend himself against one of the herders after challenging them for allowing their cattle to destroy his melon farm.

The incident was made public by Joseph Apahar, Media and Publicity Officer of IDP Benue State, in a social media post.

According to Apahar, two herders were grazing their cattle on Orvanya’s melon farm when the farmer arrived and asked them to remove the animals from his cultivated crops.

He alleged that the herders, despite being aware that the farm belonged to the farmer, showed no concern and refused to move the cattle away.

Apahar said trouble started when Orvanya attempted to chase the animals out of his farm, prompting one of the herders to allegedly draw a cutlass and attack him.

He said the farmer sustained machete wounds while attempting to shield himself from the attack, adding that Orvanya was receiving medical attention at a private hospital.

Expressing concern over the incident, Apahar lamented what he described as the increasing cases of herders allowing their cattle to destroy cultivated crops, particularly farms containing crops ready for harvest or already harvested.

He noted that such incidents were becoming increasingly common in the area, describing the development as a recurrence of the annual clashes between farmers and herders during harvest seasons after a period of relative peace.

Apahar appealed to security agencies to urgently intervene to protect farmers and their investments from further destruction.

“We are appealing to the security agencies to intervene urgently and help secure our crops before we are forced out of our villages, losing everything, and thereby reduced to nothing,” he said.

He stressed that farmers should be allowed to harvest their crops without intimidation or attacks, insisting that their lives and livelihoods must be protected.

“Our farmers deserve to harvest in peace. Our lives and livelihoods must be protected,” Apahar added.

Efforts to reach the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, for comments on the incident were unsuccessful, as he could not be reached at the time of filing this report.

The post Farmer allegedly macheted over grazing dispute in Benue appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: FG targets raw mineral export ban, revenue tops N100bn
description:
By Gabriel Ewepu







The Federal Government is pushing to end the export of unprocessed solid minerals as part of efforts to deepen local value addition, boost industrialisation and create jobs, even as revenue from the sector crossed N100 billion in 2026.







President Bola Tinubu stated this
content:
By Gabriel Ewepu

The Federal Government is pushing to end the export of unprocessed solid minerals as part of efforts to deepen local value addition, boost industrialisation and create jobs, even as revenue from the sector crossed N100 billion in 2026.

President Bola Tinubu stated this yesterday at the Nigeria Now! Investing in Energy, Infrastructure and Mining Summit in Abuja, themed, “United Nigeria, New Horizons, One Investment Destination.”

Tinubu said Nigeria was determined to move beyond exporting raw mineral resources, stressing the need for investment in processing and beneficiation to strengthen domestic industries.

“In mining, we’re equally determined to move beyond the export of unprocessed resources. Better geological information, transparent licensing, responsible exploration, and greater investment in beneficiation and processing must support Nigerian industries, skilled employment and meaningful benefits for host communities,” he said.

The President said the government was working to build integrated value chains that would enable Nigerian enterprises to participate more actively in the mining industry and expand domestic capabilities.

He urged investors to bring technology, finance and commercial expertise, assuring them of efforts to strengthen regulatory certainty and institutional support for sustainable returns.

Earlier, Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dr Dele Alake, said reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration had increased revenue from the sector from N6 billion annually before the administration to N100 billion in 2026.

“When I assumed office, the sector’s total annual revenue stood at just N6 billion. However, through reforms, the local value addition policy, the digitisation of mining processes, and efforts to sanitise operations within the sector, that figure increased from N6 billion to N38 billion by 2024.

“By 2025, it had risen to N70 billion. And just about a week ago, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) informed us that we had crossed the N100 billion mark this year,” Alake said.

He attributed the growth to reforms and efforts to sanitise mining operations, including the establishment of Mining Marshals, which he said had apprehended over 300 illegal operators and recovered more than 100 mining sites.

Meanwhile, Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Gboyega Oyetola, said revenue generated by agencies under his ministry rose from N700.79 billion in 2023 to N1.83 trillion in 2025.

He cited improvements in maritime security, port reforms and approval of Nigeria’s first National Policy on Marine and Blue Economy, while urging investors to explore opportunities in shipping, ports, shipbuilding, fisheries, aquaculture and logistics.

title: Tinubu reiterates commitment to respecting court judgments
description:
By Henry Ojelu



President Bola Tinubu, yesterday, reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to respecting court judgments.



He also conferred the Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger, GCON, Nigeria’s second-highest national honour, on renowned lawyer, Chief Wole Olanipekun, SAN.







Pre
content:
By Henry Ojelu

President Bola Tinubu, yesterday, reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to respecting court judgments.


He also conferred the Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger, GCON, Nigeria’s second-highest national honour, on renowned lawyer, Chief Wole Olanipekun, SAN.

President Tinubu at the launch of a six-volume book, Wole Olanipekun Through the Cases, organised to celebrate the senior lawyer’s 75th birthday, 50 years at the Bar and 35 years as an SAN, said: “Our administration respects court judgments, even the ones we do not enjoy reading. We do not denigrate, attack or intimidate the judiciary. A government that bullies its judges only weakens its own foundation.

“This administration passed the Judicial Officeholder Salary and Allowances Act 2024, reversing over 15 years of stagnation and delivering a 300 percent increase in the salaries of our Judicial Officers of the Superior Court of record.

“We are not yet at our desired designation. But significant work is in progress, and the brighter future is now in closer view. We will be there, my Lordship. Our administration respects court judgment, even the one we do not enjoy reading.
“We do not denigrate, attack or intimidate the judiciary,” President Tinubu reassured.

Tinubu urged stakeholders in the justice sector to promote Nigeria as a business-friendly destination, stressing that timely judgments could strengthen investor confidence.

“Every timely judgment is an advertisement for the Nigerian economy,” he said.

He congratulated Olanipekun on his professional milestones, noting that the senior lawyer had positively impacted Nigeria and humanity through his legal practice and mentorship.

Tinubu described Olanipekun as a phenomenal Nigerian and outstanding advocate who had upheld the traditions of excellence in the legal profession.

The President also acknowledged the lawyer’s decades of loyalty and friendship, disclosing that Olanipekun had led his legal team for decades.

“On a personal note, I celebrate decades of loyalty, friendship, commitment and reciprocity between Wole Olanipekun and I. He has led my legal team for decades. In politics, friends come and go. Wole came, and Wole stayed,” he said.


Tinubu said Olanipekun also led the legal teams that defended three of his predecessors when their election victories were challenged.

He said the senior lawyer had consequently served as lead counsel to four successive Nigerian presidents since 2007, describing the record as unprecedented.

“Presidents change. Parties change. The Lead Counsel remains,” he said.

President of the Senate Godswill Akpabio lauded President Tinubu for his commitment to justice, democracy, and national development.

He assured the President that the National Assembly will continue to support all legal instruments that will promote justice, democracy and the rule of law. He also commended Chief Olanipekun for his contributions to the legal profession.

Similarly, the Chief Justice of the Federation, Justice Kudirat Kere-Ekun, praised Wole Olanipekun for his immense contributions to the legal profession, believing that the publications being unveiled will further contribute to the intellectual depth, advocacy and enrichment of the nation’s jurisprudence.

The Attorney-General of the Federation and Justice Minister, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, also spoke glowingly of Olanipekun and recalled several times they collaborated in court. As a lawyer, you don’t want to be on the opposite side of Chief Olanipekun, he said.

Governor Biodun Oyebanji of Ekiti State eulogised Wole Olanipekun for enriching the legal profession, saying Ekiti State was proud of him.

Minister of the FCT, Nyesom Wike, also gave a goodwill message.

Chief Wole Olanipekun recalled his personal relationship with President Tinubu over the years and commended the President for his steadfastness, advocacy for democracy, and sacrifices. He revealed that at one such meeting, the President taught him the difference between legal and political jurisprudence.

In his keynote address titled “The Rule of Law As a Catalyst for Private Sector Growth”, Tony Elumelu said the rule of law was vital to private sector growth and attraction of foreign investment, as entrepreneurs and investors were concerned about the right application of law as well as fair and speedy arbitration.

According to him, trust is the currency that underpins economic activities and determines whether citizens cooperate with government, investors commit capital and businesses expand.

Oyedele said: “Trust is the one currency that sits beneath all the other currencies. When trust is strong, citizens cooperate, capital flows, businesses invest, and reforms get a fair hearing. When trust is weak, even sound policies meet suspicion, and every explanation sounds like an excuse.”

The minister said the economic consequences of negative narratives were often overlooked, adding that the country could lose investments and valuable human capital when its public image was dominated by stories of failure and hopelessness.


He cited damaging perceptions expressed in phrases such as “Nigeria is finished,” “Nigeria is a scam,” and “Nigeria happened to me,” warning that such narratives could influence investment decisions and undermine confidence in the country’s economic prospects.

Oyedele further explained that the cost was beyond reputational damage as, according to him, investors demand higher returns to compensate for perceived risks, postponement of expansion plans by businesses and seeking of opportunities elsewhere by talented Nigerians.

He, however, acknowledged that citizens had the right to expose government failures, demand accountability and draw attention to the difficulties they faced.

Responsible communication, he insisted, must not be confused with suppressing criticism, stressing that the country’s story must reflect both its challenges and progress.

“Government and businesses cannot rely on publicity to conceal poor performance or substitute communication for service delivery. We cannot communicate our way out of conflicts,” he said.

PR can’t cover bad leadership, global experts warn

Meanwhile, global public relations experts have warned governments and corporate organisations to stop using PR, propaganda or strategic messaging to hide leadership failures.

Trust, they said, could not be bought with publicity but earned through integrity, accountability and actions that match promises.

The warning came at a session on Ethical Leadership and Trust in a Divided World at the ongoing 2026 World Public Relations Forum, WPRF, organised in Abuja by the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management and the Nigeria Institute of Public Relations.

The panel featured the Alliance’s regional council chairs for Europe, Asia-Pacific, Africa, Middle East and South Asia, and North America, and moderated by Chimdi Neliaku, Chair of the NIPR Young Professionals Hub.

For Europe, Global Alliance Vice President and Chair of its European Regional Council, Silvia Arto, said ethical leadership was shown in personal conduct, not public declarations.

To me, ethical leadership is lead by example. It’s walk the talk. It’s integrity,” she said, adding that integrity meant doing what was right, even when nobody was watching.

From Asia-Pacific, the chair, Jaffri Osman, said effective leadership required more than intellectual intelligence, adding that motional and social intelligence matter just as much in building relationships across diverse communities.


“Trust is built by leaders who understand beyond IQ. They have to understand EQ and SQ,” he said.

Using Malaysia’s Sarawak region as an example of multicultural coexistence, Osman said professionals must understand local cultures, traditions and relationships to influence communities responsibly.

For Africa, Chair Ms Irene Lungu Chipili identified political messaging, democratic competition and misinformation as major threats to public confidence.

She questioned whether citizens could trust messages from political parties and governments, arguing that the credibility of the messenger was as important as the information.

From the Middle East and South Asia, Chair Serra Gorpe said accountability, transparency and stakeholder engagement were essential to institutional legitimacy.

“Legitimacy is accountability, transparency, stakeholder communication, engagement,” she said.

Gorpe called for stronger ethics education in universities, urging institutions to use regional case studies rather than relying predominantly on Western textbooks.

The post Tinubu reiterates commitment to respecting court judgments appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Dangote cement records 60% reduction in road traffic accidents
description: Dangote Cement Plc. has recorded a remarkable 60 per cent reduction in road traffic accidents, following the implementation of a comprehensive driver safety programme, underscoring the company’s unwavering commitment to protecting lives and promoting road safety across its transportation operations.
content:
Dangote Cement Plc. has recorded a remarkable 60 per cent reduction in road traffic accidents, following the implementation of a comprehensive driver safety programme, underscoring the company’s unwavering commitment to protecting lives and promoting road safety across its transportation operations.


The milestone was announced at the 2026 Customer Truck Scheme, CTS, Annual Driver Safety Award and Recognition Programme, where the company celebrated drivers who demonstrated exemplary safety performance and maintained accident-free records throughout the assessment period.


The achievement builds on an earlier 30 percent reduction in road traffic accidents recorded in 2023, following the introduction of the company’s Safety Improvement Plan.


As part of the initiative, approximately 3,000 drivers were trained in defensive driving techniques and safe road-use practices.
According to the company, the sustained decline in accidents reflects the effectiveness of continuous driver training, behavioural monitoring, corrective interventions, and the deliberate recognition of safe driving practices.


Speaking at the event on behalf of the Group Sales and Marketing Director, the National Sales Director of Dangote Cement Plc, Mr. Dolapo Ali, noted that the rapid expansion of the company’s transportation operations had made road safety a critical business priority.


He disclosed that the CTS fleet had grown significantly from 469 trucks in 2017 to over 2,500 trucks today, increasing the need for a more structured and proactive safety management approach.
“Our business has experienced tremendous growth over the years, and with that growth comes greater responsibility. As the number of trucks and drivers operating across our roads increases, so too does our exposure to road safety risks. Protecting lives and ensuring safe operations must therefore remain at the heart of our transport strategy,” he stated.
Ali explained that road traffic accidents peaked in 2021 and 2022, prompting the company to introduce its Safety Improvement Plan in early 2023.
A key component of the programme was an intensive defensive-driving training initiative through which approximately 3,000 drivers received professional safety training. The intervention delivered immediate results, with accident rates declining by 30 per cent in 2023 compared to the previous year, followed by a further 60 per cent reduction thereafter.
To strengthen compliance and encourage safer driving behaviour, Dangote Cement also deployed advanced telematics technology across its fleet operations. The system enables real-time monitoring of critical driving behaviours, including overspeeding, harsh braking, and aggressive acceleration.

title: Dollar scarcity, festive demand push Naira to N1,468/$
description: The naira yesterday continued its downward trend in both segments of the foreign exchange market, depreciating to N1,468 per dollar in the parallel market from N1,450 per dollar on Wednesday, as dwindling dollar supply and rising demand ahead of the festive season intensified pressure on the currenc
content:
The naira yesterday continued its downward trend in both segments of the foreign exchange market, depreciating to N1,468 per dollar in the parallel market from N1,450 per dollar on Wednesday, as dwindling dollar supply and rising demand ahead of the festive season intensified pressure on the currency.

Similarly, the naira weakened to N1,388 per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, NFEM, from N1,379.99 per dollar on Wednesday, representing a depreciation of N8.01.

Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, showed that the indicative exchange rate in the official market rose to N1,388 per dollar.

Consequently, the gap between the parallel and official markets widened to N80 per dollar from N70.01 per dollar on Wednesday.

Meanwhile, interbank turnover in the NFEM rose by 59.13 per cent to $800.3 million from $502.9 million recorded on Wednesday.

Vanguard analysis showed that the naira has depreciated by N95 in the parallel market since October 31, when it closed at N1,373 per dollar. Similarly, the currency has depreciated by N42 in the official market from N1,346 per dollar at the end of October.

The nation’s external reserves also declined to $54.71 billion on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, according to CBN data, representing a decline of $554 million from the peak of $55.264 billion recorded on October 27, 2026.

Commenting on the development, Chief Investment Officer of VNL Capital Asset Management, Dr. Ubah Jeremiah, said the naira’s weakness was driven more by tightening dollar supply and rising seasonal demand than by significant depletion of external reserves.

He said foreign exchange inflows had fallen sharply to about $807.6 million in the latest week from $2.48 billion previously, reducing dollar availability in the market.

“With fewer dollars coming in from autonomous sources, the market has leaned more heavily on CBN supply just as importers, businesses, and individuals step up purchases ahead of the festive season and year-end obligations,” he said.

Ubah also blamed diverging monetary policy positions between the CBN and the US Federal Reserve for reinforcing pressure on the naira, noting that higher US yields and a stronger dollar could weaken the attractiveness of naira assets and encourage portfolio outflows.

Meanwhile, parallel-market trader, Jubril Yinusa, attributed the depreciation to rising demand and limited dollar supply.

“The naira has recorded continuous depreciation this week due to the high demand as the festive season approaches and low supply. Importation demand is also contributing to the depreciation of the naira,” he said.

Another trader, Isa Dauda, said the festive season and the forthcoming election were also contributing to pressure on the currency.

He said some foreign investors were adopting a wait-and-see attitude ahead of the elections, further limiting foreign exchange inflows.

The post Dollar scarcity, festive demand push Naira to N1,468/$ appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: ‘He was a go-getter’ – Taiwo Obe, Providus Bank mourn Ajasa
description:
THE Chairman and founder of Journalism Clinic, Mr Taiwo Obe, has described the late Online Editor of Vanguard Newspapers, Mr Femi Ajasa, as a go-getter, regretting that his death has robbed journalism of one of its brightest young professionals.



Similarly, Providus Bank, one of Nigeria’s new-gene
content:
THE Chairman and founder of Journalism Clinic, Mr Taiwo Obe, has described the late Online Editor of Vanguard Newspapers, Mr Femi Ajasa, as a go-getter, regretting that his death has robbed journalism of one of its brightest young professionals.

Similarly, Providus Bank, one of Nigeria’s new-generation banks, has expressed sadness over Ajasa’s demise, saying his death is a loss not only to Vanguard but also to the media industry.

In a condolence letter by its Group Head, Brand and Corporate Communication, Dafe Ivwurie, the bank said: “We were deeply saddened to learn of the death of Olufemi Ajasa.

“By all accounts, he was an accomplished and highly respected digital journalist whose professionalism, dedication, and commitment to excellence contributed immensely to the growth and reputation of Vanguard’s digital media platforms. His passing at such a young age is a great loss not only to Vanguard but also to the Nigerian media industry.”

Meanwhile, Obe, who took to his Facebook page to mourn Ajasa, described him as one of the first journalists trained at his clinic.

He recounted the events that brought him close to the deceased and traced the history of their relationship until Ajasa’s death on Sunday.

Obe said: “Circa 1997, TaijoWonukabe Limited, which I co-founded about two years earlier, moved from its garage office graciously donated to us by the prolific columnist, late Pini Jason Onyegbadue, into a three-bedroom bungalow on Bassie Ogamba Street, off Adeniran Ogunsanya, in Surulere, Lagos.

“That property belonged to Madam Pemu, a relation of Sam Amuka-Pemu, the legendary journalist, Uncle Sam.

“One day, not long after we moved in, Uncle Sam showed up, to greet Madam Pemu, who lived in a separate bungalow on the same premises.

“I knew him then more by name than physical interactions. Either when he was leaving or as he alighted, I approached him, to introduce myself and after we exchanged pleasantries, he said: Money is good. See how you boys have changed this building.

“From that day till date, we became connected. Fast forward to circa 2015: I had founded The Journalism Clinic and converted and renamed the hall which was the finishing room of PrintPro Projects Limited – the printing subsidiary of TaijoWonukabe – to The Hub – the training room of The Journalism Clinic at Anifowose, around the corner from Bassie Ogamba.

“Uncle Sam visited one afternoon and declared ‘Vanguard will send people to all the training you will do here’.”

He kept his word and the first paid training we had in The Hub included three participants from Vanguard Online Desk and Olufemi Ajasa was one of them.

“A fine gentleman, two days ago, Vanguard reported his passing after a brief illness. Since that training, I had encountered Femi in various places and positions. He remained as respectful as ever; always go-getting and consistently impeccably-dressed. This really hit hard. Sùn re ò, Femooo,” he added.
