description: President Bola Tinubu in his determination to achieve the 40 percent fare-reduction target under the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme NACTP, as outlined in his renewed hope agenda 2.0, has welcomed plans by Yutong, the world’s largest bus manufacturer and a global leader in electric and CNG
content:
President Bola Tinubu in his determination to achieve the 40 percent fare-reduction target under the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme NACTP, as outlined in his renewed hope agenda 2.0, has welcomed plans by Yutong, the world’s largest bus manufacturer and a global leader in electric and CNG-powered buses, to establish a CNG bus assembly plant in Nigeria.

This followed his invitation to the Chinese automotive giant to support the expansion of affordable mass transportation across the country.

Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, Mr. Bayo Onanuga, in a statement, yesterday, noted that the investment would support the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme, NACTP, in collaboration with state governments, which targets transport fare reductions of approximately 40 percent on participating routes, in line with the President’s renewed hope agenda 2.0 for 2027–2031.

Under the agreement with the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles, Pi-CNG & EV, Yutong will supply an initial 300 CNG-powered buses, with the first 100 expected to arrive in Lagos by the end of December 2026.

Subsequent buses will be assembled in Nigeria through YP Automobiles Bus Assembly at the former Leyland Automotive plant in Ibadan, Oyo State, reviving local industrial capacity, reducing dependence on imported vehicles and creating employment opportunities for Nigerian engineers, technicians and other workers.

Yutong, which sold 49,518 buses globally in 2025, brings extensive experience in mass transit manufacturing, with operations across international markets and a track record of supporting local assembly and public transportation projects in several countries.

The President noted that the investment comes as CNG adoption continues to increase nationwide, supported by the expansion of refuelling infrastructure through Pi-CNG & EV, the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund, MDGIF, and private sector investors.

These interventions include deploying Mobile Refuelling Units (MRUs) and the President’s directive for 2,000 additional CNG refuelling infrastructure units nationwide, laying the foundation for a wider rollout of affordable commercial buses.

President Tinubu emphasises that reducing the daily cost of transportation for Nigerians remains the central objective of these investments.

The President notes that millions of Nigerians depend on commercial transportation to get to work, take their children to school, travel to markets and move goods between communities. For many households, transportation consumes a significant portion of their daily earnings.

He stresses that the lower operating costs of CNG-powered vehicles must translate into lower fares for passengers, allowing workers, traders and families to retain more of their income for food, education and other essential needs.

The President points to the approximately 40 percent fare-reduction target under the NACTP, as outlined in his renewed hope agenda 2.0, and reiterates his administration’s determination to work with state governments and transport operators to extend affordable CNG transportation to more routes nationwide.

He welcomed Yutong’s decision to establish local assembly capacity in Nigeria, noting that the investment would help sustain the supply of affordable commercial buses while facilitating technology transfer, creating skilled employment and strengthening the country’s automotive industry.

The post Tinubu moves to achieve 40% fares reduction under NACTP appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: FUT Babura appoints Hussaini new VC, beats six professors
description:
The Governing Council of the Federal University of Technology, Babura, Jigawa State, has appointed Professor Muhammad Auwal Hussaini as the institution’s new Vice-Chancellor.
 Hussaini emerged as the preferred candidate after defeating six other professors in the selection process.
 The Pro-Chancell
content:
The Governing Council of the Federal University of Technology, Babura, Jigawa State, has appointed Professor Muhammad Auwal Hussaini as the institution’s new Vice-Chancellor.

 Hussaini emerged as the preferred candidate after defeating six other professors in the selection process.

 The Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the Governing Council, Professor Onimawo Ignatius Akhakhia, announced the appointment on Wednesday while briefing journalists in Kano after the council’s meeting.

 The other contenders were Professors Bala Sidi Aliyu, Ibrahim Ali Muhammad Dabo, Babawuro Usman, Joel Manasseh, Mohammed Kabir Yakubu and Usman Haruna.

 Akhakhia described Hussaini’s emergence as a reflection of merit, hard work and commitment to the vision behind the establishment of the university.

 He said, “Professor Hussaini’s appointment is based purely on merit, hard work and his demonstrated commitment to the vision that informed the establishment of this university.”

 The new vice-chancellor is a Professor of Agronomy and an alumnus of Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, where he obtained his bachelor’s degree in Agriculture in 1988, a master’s degree in Agronomy in 1994 and a PhD in the same discipline in 2000.

 He began his academic career at ABU in 1990 before moving to Bayero University, Kano, where he served as Dean of the Faculty of Agriculture and pioneer Director of the Centre for Dryland Agriculture in 2012.

 He also served as Provost of Bilyaminu Usman College of Agriculture, Hadejia, between 2012 and 2014.

 Speaking on his plans for the institution, Hussaini pledged to work with the university management, staff and relevant government authorities to strengthen its mandate of providing science and technology education.

 He said, “By God’s grace, with the support of the staff, the university’s management and the government, we will ensure that the reason for establishing this university — to teach young people science, technology, skills and their practical applications — is fully realised.”

 Hussaini disclosed that the university commenced admission of students in the 2022/2023 academic session and currently has about 3,000 students, 400 staff members and 13 academic programmes.

 He said his administration would collaborate with the Federal Government, Jigawa State Government, the Ministry of Education and other stakeholders to position the institution for growth and achieve its founding objectives.

 The professor also expressed appreciation to the Jigawa State Governor, the Minister of Education, the governing council and the outgoing management team for their contributions to the development of the university.

 “We will continue to seek their support to ensure that whatever needs to be done for this university to progress and achieve its goals, God willing, we will do it,” he added.

 Hussaini’s appointment will take effect from January 27, 2027. ENDS.

The post FUT Babura appoints Hussaini new VC, beats six professors appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 14 arrested over $22.5m train cargo theft in US
description:
No fewer than 14 people have been arrested in the United States on federal charges over an alleged $22.5 million cargo theft conspiracy.
The defendants are accused of belonging to a theft ring that burgled at least 36 freight trains across Southern California, stealing merchandise including Nike sne
content:
No fewer than 14 people have been arrested in the United States on federal charges over an alleged $22.5 million cargo theft conspiracy.

The defendants are accused of belonging to a theft ring that burgled at least 36 freight trains across Southern California, stealing merchandise including Nike sneakers, Milwaukee tools and electronics.

The stolen merchandise was allegedly sold through black-market dealers and social media platforms.

According to a tweet on Thursday by the First Assistant US Attorney for the Central District of California, Bill Essayli, the syndicate is led by 21-year-old Nathan Angel, of East Los Angeles.

Essayli said the suspects allegedly stopped trains, removed cargo and transported the stolen goods to storage locations before selling them.

“This morning we arrested a train robbery crew. Nathan Daniel Angel, 21, of East Los Angeles, and 13 co-defendants have been federally charged with orchestrating a $`22.5 million cargo theft conspiracy.

“The indictment alleges the crew burglarised at least 36 freight trains across Southern California, stealing Nike sneakers, Milwaukee tools, electronics, and other merchandise for black-market resale.

“The defendants allegedly stopped trains by cutting air hoses, boarded rail cars, moved the goods to stash houses, and sold them via fence networks and social media,” his tweet partly read.

The official lamented the volume of damage caused by train robberies as they involve valuable goods.

He also stated that if convicted, the syndicate could face long sentences.

“Train robberies cause enormous economic damage because of the valuable cargo involved.

“These defendants face long federal prison sentences if convicted. All are presumed innocent until proven guilty,” he wrote.

According to a report by NBC Los Angeles on Thursday, the case was investigated by operatives of the Homeland Security Investigations and the Los Angeles Police Department Commercial Crimes Bureau, among other agencies.

Other members of the syndicate include Angel Sanchez, 24; Ruben Banuelos, 26; Fredy Marquina, 25; Carlos Martinez, 23; and Jorge Espinoza, 36, among others.

The report noted that Angel and the other defendants coordinated the thefts through Instagram.

“The defendants allegedly used trucks and vans to take burglars to rail lines in Pico Rivera, Fullerton and elsewhere in Southern California, where they boarded freight trains.

“Prosecutors allege some conspirators cut train air hoses to force emergency stops, then loaded stolen cargo into vehicles and transported it to stash houses, including residences in Los Angeles.

“The indictment alleges that some of the stolen merchandise was sold to an unnamed Los Angeles-based sneaker and streetwear resale company that was not an authorised Nike reseller,” it stated.

Prosecutors said, according to the report, that between May and October 2025, Marquina and Martinez allegedly sold thousands of pairs of stolen Nike sneakers and other goods to the company, receiving about $1.08m.

The charges carry maximum penalties ranging from five years in federal prison for conspiracy to life imprisonment for violence against railroad carriers, the report stated.

The post 14 arrested over $22.5m train cargo theft in US appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Barcelona thrash Servette 6-0 to top women’s Champions League
description:
A Claudia Pina hat-trick fired Barcelona top of the women’s Champions League table on Thursday in a 6-0 home thrashing of Servette, while Lyon earned an impressive 2-0 win at Arsenal to keep pace.
Barcelona and Arsenal both have 13 points from five of six league phase games, while Bayern Munich crui
content:
A Claudia Pina hat-trick fired Barcelona top of the women’s Champions League table on Thursday in a 6-0 home thrashing of Servette, while Lyon earned an impressive 2-0 win at Arsenal to keep pace.

Barcelona and Arsenal both have 13 points from five of six league phase games, while Bayern Munich cruised to a 4-0 victory over Austria Vienna and are level third on 11pts with Chelsea.

“I was just saying to my teammates that it was really important to finish first in the standings,” Pina told reporters.

“I don’t know if we can now switch off a little bit mentally but we’ve got a bit of calm.

“If we end up finishing top, even better, but it’s the Champions League, every match can be tricky,” she added.

Klara Buehl was named player of the match and she both opened the scoring and made an assist with Pernille Harder, Alara and Sophie Proost rounding out the comfortable win for the German champions.

Austria Vienna played with plenty of spirit but remain winless with only a point from five games as Bayern put on a display of firepower in the final third.

Despite the defeat, it was a memorable occasion for Austria Vienna, who showcased their progress in front of a record crowd for a women’s club football match in Austria with around 10,000 fans in attendance.

Roma took the lead twice at Benfica who battled back twice only to concede a late defeat when Roma’s Sofia Jahnukainen lost her marker late on for a superb winner making it 3-2 from a tight angle on 90+3.

Paris FC edged Danish side HB Koge 2-1, fighting back from going a goal down early thanks to midfielder Sheika Scott’s leveller on 35 minutes and the winner deep into second-half stoppage time from Celina Ould Hocine.

Veerle Buurman struck late as Chelsea edged Paris Saint-Germain 1-0 on Wednesday as English champions Manchester City and Spain’s Real Madrid earned vital wins to keep up with the early pace-setters after five rounds of matches.

AFP

title: CAF unveils 2027 AFCON logo
description:
The Confederation of African Football and the three host countries of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda, have unveiled the official logo for the tournament.
CAF announced the launch on Thursday, saying the new identity was inspired by the traditional East African shield, whi
content:
The Confederation of African Football and the three host countries of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda, have unveiled the official logo for the tournament.

CAF announced the launch on Thursday, saying the new identity was inspired by the traditional East African shield, which it described as a symbol of African heritage, identity and strength.

The logo was unveiled simultaneously in the three host nations at 1pm local time on November 19, 2026.

According to CAF, the design is built around the message: “Honouring Our Past, Celebrating Our Culture and Symbolising the Africa of Tomorrow.”

The football governing body said the shield was chosen because it represents identity, protection, pride and belonging, adding that it features in the national coats of arms of all three host countries.

At the centre of the logo is the silhouette of the AFCON trophy, topped by the outline of the African continent and bearing the CAF name.

CAF said the trophy’s position at the heart of the shield represents the tournament’s role in bringing together the continent’s cultures, identities and ambitions.

The design also incorporates colourful beadwork and geometric patterns inspired by East African craftsmanship, textiles and weaving.

The colours of the three countries are combined in the logo, with red and black at the top of the shield, green and yellow on either side of the trophy, and blue at its base.

The new visual identity also includes 12 shield patterns representing the individual identities of the three host nations.

Kenya’s design features bold horizontal bands, while Tanzania’s incorporates diagonal lines inspired by its national flag. Uganda’s pattern uses warm, layered colours and the country’s crested crane.

CAF said the designs would be displayed across stadiums, digital platforms and tournament activities.

The name PAMOJA, which means “Together” in Swahili, reflects the partnership between the three countries and the spirit of the competition.

The 2027 AFCON will be the first edition of the tournament to be jointly hosted by three countries.

It is scheduled to run from June 19 to July 17, 2027, with 24 teams expected to compete.

CAF said the logo launch came 212 days before the tournament’s opening match.

The post CAF unveils 2027 AFCON logo appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Police storm Kogi forest, rescue 15 kidnap victims
description:
The police have rescued 15 kidnapped victims during a joint security operation in Magaru Forest, Kakun-Kabba, Kogi State, following a fierce gun battle with their abductors.
The operation, conducted in the early hours of Wednesday, involved personnel of the Kogi State Police Command, the Nigerian Ar
content:
The police have rescued 15 kidnapped victims during a joint security operation in Magaru Forest, Kakun-Kabba, Kogi State, following a fierce gun battle with their abductors.

The operation, conducted in the early hours of Wednesday, involved personnel of the Kogi State Police Command, the Nigerian Army, Forest Guards, vigilante groups and other local security outfits.

The kidnappers reportedly engaged the security operatives in a gun battle as they advanced into the forest. However, the superior firepower of the joint team forced the criminals to retreat, with some sustaining gunshot injuries.

The Kogi State Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Saliu Oyiza Afusat, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday.

She said two other female victims, identified only as Joy and Nwakan, escaped from their abductors during the initial attack in which the victims were kidnapped.

According to the statement, the security team came under another ambush while evacuating the rescued victims from the forest.

However, the operatives repelled the attack and successfully brought all 15 victims out of the forest.

The rescued victims were subsequently debriefed and taken to St. John’s Catholic Hospital, Kabba, for medical attention after enduring physical and psychological distress during their captivity.

The police spokesperson said no suspects had been arrested, but actionable intelligence had been generated to track down the fleeing members of the kidnapping gang.

She added that investigations were ongoing to apprehend the suspects and identify their sponsors.

The Commissioner of Police, CP Naziru Bello Kankarofi, commended the participating security agencies and local security outfits for their collaboration, reiterating the command’s commitment to tackling kidnapping and other violent crimes in the state.

The command urged residents to provide credible, timely information to help security agencies fight criminal activities.

title: Army seeks Bauchi land for armour training as COAS leads combat exercise
description:
The Nigerian Army has conducted a combined-arms military exercise in Bauchi State as part of efforts to strengthen its operational capacity, while seeking additional land from the state government for the establishment of a dedicated Armour Corps training ground.
 The Chief of Army Staff, Lt-Gen. Wa
content:
The Nigerian Army has conducted a combined-arms military exercise in Bauchi State as part of efforts to strengthen its operational capacity, while seeking additional land from the state government for the establishment of a dedicated Armour Corps training ground.

 The Chief of Army Staff, Lt-Gen. Waidi Shaibu, made the request during a courtesy visit to Governor Bala Mohammed at the Government House, Bauchi, on Wednesday, a day after the Army conducted the fifth edition of Exercise MUGUN BUGU 2026 in Alkaleri Local Government Area.

 Shaibu said the proposed training facility had become necessary following the expansion of the Nigerian Army from eight to 12 divisions, which had increased the number of personnel requiring specialised and continuous training.

 He said, “Being an armour officer myself, I started my career here in Bauchi. The state is home to every armour officer, as many of us normally start our careers here before proceeding to other courses.

 “With the current expansion, many officers and soldiers have been coming to the corps for training, and the training continues throughout the year.

 “Being a training area generally, it also requires dedicated training grounds. We are therefore requesting a parcel of land that will be dedicated to the training of the Armour Corps.”

 Responding, Mohammed said the state government had approved the Army’s request, assuring that relevant military authorities would work with the government to identify a suitable location for the facility.

 The governor congratulated Shaibu on his appointment as Chief of Army Staff, describing his operational experience, particularly in the North-East theatre, as an important asset in tackling the country’s security challenges.

 He commended the Army and other security agencies for their sacrifices in maintaining peace and stability in Bauchi State.

 Mohammed said the relative peace in the state had enabled his administration to pursue infrastructure development, agricultural expansion and economic reforms.

 He said, “The relative peace and stability we enjoy today, which have enabled us to execute massive infrastructure development, agriculture and economic reforms, would not have been possible without the vigilance and synergy of the 33 Artillery Brigade, the Armour Corps and other security agencies.”

 The governor also commended President Bola Tinubu and the Army chief for approving the establishment of two additional Army battalions in the state.

 He said the deployment of personnel and logistics had enabled the new formations to become operational within a short period, adding that their presence would help address security vulnerabilities around border communities and forest corridors.

 However, Mohammed identified boundary disputes, kidnapping and illegal mining, particularly in border communities, as persistent security challenges requiring sustained collaboration among security agencies.

 He also pledged continued support for families of military personnel who died in the line of duty, saying their sacrifices deserved lasting recognition.

 Meanwhile, the Army conducted the fifth edition of Exercise MUGUN BUGU 2026, featuring a firepower demonstration, in Alkaleri on Tuesday.

 Speaking at the grand finale, Shaibu said the exercise was designed to improve the Army’s training standards and operational capabilities in response to evolving security threats.

 He explained that the exercise provided an opportunity to assess command and control, tactical decision-making, teamwork and the coordinated deployment of different combat capabilities under realistic field conditions.

 According to him, the exercise was also intended to bridge the gap between institutional military training and the practical demands of operations.

 He said, “One of the most important outcomes expected from Exercise MUGUN BUGU is enhancing our capacity to conduct effective command and combined-arms operations.

 “In contemporary military operations, the coordinated employment of infantry, armour, artillery, signals and other combat and combat support capabilities, sustained by effective command arrangements, cannot be overemphasised.”

 The Army chief stressed that no single arm could independently provide all the capabilities required for successful military operations, noting that effective coordination among the different arms and services remained critical.

 He said lessons learnt from the exercise would strengthen interoperability, operational precision and the Army’s capacity to conduct coordinated and decisive operations.

 Also speaking, the former Chief of Army Staff and Special Guest of Honour, Lt. Gen. Faruk Yahaya (retd.), called for the integration of emerging technologies into the Army’s training programmes, operational doctrines and capability development.

 Yahaya said the changing security environment, characterised by terrorism, insurgency, banditry and emerging technological threats, required continuous improvements in military preparedness.

 He said, “The threat of any army lies not merely in the sophistication of its weapons, but especially in the training, resilience of its personnel and their determination to accomplish assigned missions.”

 The former Army chief urged the military leadership to prioritise technological innovation, improved training methods and stronger command and control systems.

 He also called for closer collaboration among the Army, Navy, Air Force and other security agencies through joint planning, intelligence sharing and coordinated operations.

 Yahaya urged the Army to critically assess the observations and lessons from the exercise to improve future training programmes and operational effectiveness. ENDS…

title: Africa rejects Paris Agreement renegotiation at COP31
description:
Fifty-four African countries have rejected any attempt to renegotiate the Paris Agreement, warning that reopening the global climate pact, particularly its obligations, would undermine commitments already agreed by countries to address climate change.
 The African Group of Negotiators on Climate Cha
content:
Fifty-four African countries have rejected any attempt to renegotiate the Paris Agreement, warning that reopening the global climate pact, particularly its obligations, would undermine commitments already agreed by countries to address climate change.

 The African Group of Negotiators on Climate Change said any attempt to alter the agreement was a red line for the continent, insisting that developed countries must honour their existing obligations rather than seek to revise the framework governing global climate action.

 The position comes as negotiations at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference, known as COP31, in Antalya, Türkiye, enter their final hours, with African countries pushing for stronger commitments on climate finance, adaptation and support for vulnerable economies.

 Speaking at a press conference on the state of negotiations on Thursday, the AGN Chair, Nana Dr Antwi-Boasiako Amoah, said Africa would not accept any attempt to renegotiate the Paris Agreement, particularly provisions relating to the responsibilities of countries.

 He said, “There’s one message that I also want to put across, which is about renegotiating the Paris Agreement. I think this is something that is a big red line for the African continent.

 “Any attempt to renegotiate the Paris Agreement, especially when it comes to obligations, is something that the African continent rejects. We need to stay within the confines of the agreement because that is what we all have agreed in the past to do business with.”

 The chair’s remarks reflect growing concerns among developing countries that efforts to revisit existing climate commitments could weaken the obligations of developed nations to provide financial and other forms of support to countries bearing the brunt of climate change despite contributing relatively little to global greenhouse gas emissions.

 The dispute over climate finance has become one of the major sticking points at COP31, following changes to the proposed adaptation finance target in the latest draft decision released on November 19.

 The revised draft dropped an earlier proposal requiring adaptation finance for developing countries to reach at least $120bn annually by 2035.

 The figure had been based on tripling the $40bn annual adaptation finance commitment under the Glasgow Climate Pact, agreed at COP26 in 2021.

 Under that commitment, developed countries agreed to double adaptation finance from approximately $20bn provided in 2019 to $40bn annually by 2025.

 However, the latest draft no longer specifies the $120bn figure or identifies the $40bn Glasgow commitment as the baseline for calculating the proposed increase.

 Instead, paragraph 40 retains a commitment to at least triple adaptation finance by 2035, while paragraph 43 requests the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change Standing Committee on Finance to prepare a technical report identifying possible baselines. Paragraph 44 also proposes developing an implementation pathway for the target.

 The removal of the specific financial figure raises concerns about how the proposed increase will be measured, funded and implemented, particularly as developing countries seek assurances that climate finance commitments will translate into actual resources.

 African countries have repeatedly argued that such financing should be predictable, accessible and largely provided through grants or highly concessional instruments rather than commercial loans that could deepen their debt burdens.

 Addressing questions about the continent’s ability to implement its climate commitments amid limited financing, Amoah said Africa’s concerns were not simply about securing additional money but ensuring that the financial architecture delivered resources on affordable terms.

title: Jonathan reveals reason for conceding defeat to Buhari
description:
Former President Goodluck Jonathan has explained that he conceded defeat to the late President Muhammadu Buhari in the 2015 presidential election without resistance because he regarded him as a statesman who loved God and Nigeria.
Jonathan, who was represented by former Senate President Anyim Pius A
content:
Former President Goodluck Jonathan has explained that he conceded defeat to the late President Muhammadu Buhari in the 2015 presidential election without resistance because he regarded him as a statesman who loved God and Nigeria.

Jonathan, who was represented by former Senate President Anyim Pius Anyim, spoke on Thursday in Abuja at the public presentation of Muhammadu Buhari: The Authorised Biography, a three-volume work authored by Dr Udu Yakubu.

Anyim told the audience that Jonathan contacted him about two hours before the event to inform him of his inability to attend. He said the former president cancelled other engagements to ensure that he was properly represented at the ceremony.

He noted that many Nigerians continued to question why Jonathan conceded defeat in the 2015 presidential election, recalling that Buhari was widely recognised as the politician who defeated an incumbent president, while Jonathan earned a reputation as the African leader who peacefully relinquished power without controversy.

“President Buhari is renowned for being that politician who was able to unseat a sitting incumbent. President Goodluck is renowned for being that sitting African president who handed over power without any form of contention.

“It was easy for President Goodluck to say, ‘Look, this is a statesman that I know will love Nigeria.’ So there was no need for any form of contention. That is the story,” Anyim said.

He said Jonathan’s acceptance of the 2015 election results underscored the need to place national interest above party politics.

“When eventually Goodluck lost the election, there was no need for any form of opposition,” Anyim added.

Anyim described his relationship with Buhari as a father-and-son bond, saying their friendship endured despite belonging to different political parties.

He recalled that their closeness remained intact even after he joined the government while Buhari was in the opposition.

Jonathan, who was then the incumbent President and PDP presidential candidate, conceded defeat to Buhari of the opposition APC before the Independent National Electoral Commission announced the final results of the 2015 election.

title: Python Golf Club offers N30m purse for Pro-Am Classic
description:
Python Golf Club, Port Harcourt, has set aside a N30m prize purse for professional golfers competing at its 2026 Pro-Am Classic, which began on Wednesday.
The five-day tournament, scheduled to end on November 22, has attracted 120 professional golfers and 150 amateurs from Nigeria and other countrie
content:
Python Golf Club, Port Harcourt, has set aside a N30m prize purse for professional golfers competing at its 2026 Pro-Am Classic, which began on Wednesday.

The five-day tournament, scheduled to end on November 22, has attracted 120 professional golfers and 150 amateurs from Nigeria and other countries.

The competition brings professionals and amateur players together in a format designed to encourage interaction while providing an opportunity for golfers to compete for prizes.

Secretary of the planning committee, Loveday Demua, disclosed the prize money while speaking on behalf of the committee chairman, Leo Edochie.

“The purse money for the professionals for this event is N30m,” Demua said.

He added that more than 40 amateur golfers would also receive prizes, including golf sets, kits, one-year medical coverage and flight tickets.

The club’s captain, Johnbosco Ozigbu, said the tournament was organised to bring golfers together and promote the game, while giving participants the opportunity to enjoy the club’s facilities.

“We are bringing professionals from all over the world, mostly Nigeria, and all the amateurs to come and play, work on their mental health, swing well and win,” Ozigbu said.

The tournament is expected to feature players from across Africa and beyond, with organisers describing it as an opportunity to showcase the sport and strengthen the club’s profile.

The event follows the club’s hosting of the CIO Golf Championship earlier this month, which featured a separate N100m prize purse.

The Pro-Am Classic will conclude on Sunday, with amateur participants also competing for several incentives.

title: Pereira begs Barca to sign Bassey
description:
Former Fulham coach Javier Pereira has urged Barcelona to sign Nigerian defender Calvin Bassey, insisting that he has the physical profile that coach Hansi Flick lacks in big matches.
Pereira made the appeal in an interview with Marca on November 18. He said his former player would immediately impro
content:
Former Fulham coach Javier Pereira has urged Barcelona to sign Nigerian defender Calvin Bassey, insisting that he has the physical profile that coach Hansi Flick lacks in big matches.

Pereira made the appeal in an interview with Marca on November 18. He said his former player would immediately improve the Catalans, who are looking for a centre-back in the January transfer window. Barcelona have not been linked with the Fulham man.

Pereira said Barcelona have no centre-back like Bassey, who has “a different physical and athletic profile, something Flick is lacking in important matches”.

He praised the 26-year-old’s ability to play on a high defensive line, his aggression in the opposition half and his speed. Pereira also highlighted his ability to carry the ball past midfielders, saying that apart from Pau Cubarsi, Barcelona have no one with “the ability to break lines with his dribbling”.

Pereira argued that a move to Spain would suit Bassey better than a switch to Manchester United, citing his tactical maturity and positive body language.

Bassey is reportedly on a defensive shortlist of incoming United manager Mauricio Pochettino, whose side have conceded 19 goals in their first 10 Premier League matches.

Fulham are reportedly open to a sale and have placed a €55m price tag on him.

Bassey has played every minute of Fulham’s 10 league games this season under Álvaro Arbeloa.

title: Jonathan, Shettima, others pay tributes to Buhari
description: Vice-President Kashim Shettima, former President Goodluck Jonathan and ex-Nigerien President Mahamadou Issoufou paid glowing tributes to the late President Muhammadu Buhari, highlighting his patriotism and contributions to Nigeria and regional development at the public presentation of his authorised
content:
Vice-President Kashim Shettima, former President Goodluck Jonathan and ex-Nigerien President Mahamadou Issoufou paid glowing tributes to the late President Muhammadu Buhari, highlighting his patriotism and contributions to Nigeria and regional development at the public presentation of his authorised biography in Abuja.

Represented by his Special Adviser on General Duties, Dr Aliyu Modibbo Umar, Shettima spoke on Thursday at the public presentation of Muhammadu Buhari: The Authorised Biography, a three-volume work authored by Dr Udu Yakubu, in Abuja.

He said Buhari’s record of public service would continue to inspire future generations, stressing the importance of leaders leaving lasting legacies.

The Vice-President stated, “His Spartan lifestyle distinguished him in a world where too many seek public office to satisfy private appetites. There was something arresting about a man who could command so much and desire so little.”

Shettima recalled that Buhari taught him that a leader’s character determines the dignity and integrity of the office he occupies.

He continued, “I learnt so much from President Buhari as a leader, as a human being who was not drawn to worldly possessions, and as a patriot whose devotion to Nigeria endured beyond the offices he held.

“He taught me that the dignity of office depends upon the character of its occupant. He also taught me that a leader’s example continues to speak long after he is out of service.”

Shettima noted that Buhari’s political journey, from military leadership to democratic rule, attracted both significant public admiration and criticism of his policies and decisions.

Speaking while unveiling the book, former President Goodluck Jonathan explained that he conceded defeat to the late President Muhammadu Buhari in the 2015 presidential election without resistance because he regarded him as a statesman who loved God and Nigeria.

Jonathan, who was represented by former Senate President Anyim Pius Anyim, had contacted him about two hours before the event to inform him of his inability to attend.

He said the former president cancelled other engagements to ensure that he was properly represented at the ceremony.

Anyim noted that many Nigerians continued to question why Jonathan conceded defeat in the 2015 presidential election, recalling that Buhari was widely recognised as the politician who defeated an incumbent president, while Jonathan earned a reputation as the African leader who peacefully relinquished power without controversy.

“President Buhari is renowned for being that politician who was able to unseat a sitting incumbent. President Goodluck is renowned to be that sitting African president who handed over power without any form of contention.

“It was easy for President Goodluck to say, ‘Look, this is a statesman that I know that will love Nigeria.’ So there was no need for any form of contention. That is the story,” he said.

He said Jonathan’s acceptance of the 2015 election results underscored the need to place national interest above party politics.

“When eventually Goodluck lost the election, there was no need for any form of opposition,” he added.

Anyim described his personal relationship with Buhari as a father-and-son bond, saying their friendship endured despite belonging to different political parties.

He recalled that their closeness remained intact even after he joined the government while Buhari was in the opposition.

Jonathan, who was then the incumbent President and PDP presidential candidate, conceded defeat to Buhari of the opposition APC before the Independent National Electoral Commission announced the final results of the 2015 election.

Similarly, Issoufou, who chaired the occasion, described Buhari as a visionary leader and a close friend of Niger, recalling their collaboration on regional security, economic integration and efforts to strengthen relations between the two countries.

He said the three-volume biography would provide future generations with documented accounts of Buhari’s life, decisions and contributions to national and continental development.

Issoufou said Buhari’s commitment to constitutional order was evident. “He respected the constitutional principle of term limits and facilitated the alternation of power,” he said.

He recalled that Buhari made Niger his first foreign destination after assuming office on June 3, 2015, adding that he honoured the late Nigerian leader with the Grand Cross of the National Order of Niger in March 2021.

Issoufou, however, stressed that the biography should not be considered the definitive account of Buhari’s life and legacy.

He added, “None of us can claim to have the final word on Muhammadu Buhari. Nor should any biography pretend to do so.”

Former military Head of State, General Ibrahim Babangida (retd.), represented by former Inspector-General of Police Mohammed D. Abubakar, paid tribute to Buhari, describing him as a “comrade-in-arms”.

He stated, “Together, we travelled the path of training in the armed forces of our country. Together, we walked the trenches of danger for the common good. We forged our nation in peace and unity, and today, Nigeria is much better for it.”

Nasarawa State Governor, Abdullahi Sule, said Buhari’s honesty, patriotism and firm stance against corruption were among the qualities that distinguished him.

He said, “One thing that has been repeated over and over is his honesty, his love for Nigeria, and his uncompromising attitude when it comes to corruption.”

Also speaking, the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of BUA Group, Abdulsamad Isyaka Rabi’u, represented by Senator Lawal Shuaibu, described Buhari as a deeply important figure in his life.

Earlier, Chairman of the Biography Planning Committee, Engr. Suleiman Adamu, said the book chronicles the life of a man whose public career spanned over six decades of Nigeria’s history, from military service and the civil war to politics and eight years as an elected president.

Adamu stated, “There is, however, one fact about these volumes that deserves to be stated with particular emphasis. This biography was personally authorised by President Muhammadu Buhari.

“It was not a project conceived after his death. It was not an attempt to reconstruct his life when he was no longer available to speak for himself. President Buhari knew that the biography was being written. He gave his consent to it.

“He submitted himself to the process. He was interviewed repeatedly. He answered questions about the different stages of his life, including difficult and contested episodes. He assisted the author in reaching people, events and memories necessary for reconstructing the record. And he remained a participant in that process until his death.”

Author of the biography, Dr Udu Yakubu, said the three-volume work took more than two and a half years to complete, crediting former President Muhammadu Buhari for granting him access while he was alive.

Yakubu said Buhari personally authorised the project and participated in several interviews, answering questions about different stages of his life, although he did not always agree with the questions or provide the expected responses.

He also acknowledged Buhari’s nephew, Malam Mamman Daura, for helping him access relevant individuals and clarify events and timelines during the research.

The author said the biography should be open to public scrutiny and criticism, stressing that a work of such magnitude should not be shielded from critical examination.

The event was attended by former ministers who served under Buhari, alongside his friends and family members.

Buhari died on July 13, 2025, aged 82, after serving as Nigeria’s democratically elected President from 2015 to 2023.

The post Jonathan, Shettima, others pay tributes to Buhari appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Nigerian-Canadian crash victim’s family found after appeal
description:
The Airport Police Command says it has established contact with the family of Abraham Osakpolor, a Nigerian-Canadian who died after being hit by a vehicle along the Murtala Muhammed International Airport access road in Lagos.
The command disclosed this in a statement issued on Thursday by its Public
content:
The Airport Police Command says it has established contact with the family of Abraham Osakpolor, a Nigerian-Canadian who died after being hit by a vehicle along the Murtala Muhammed International Airport access road in Lagos.

The command disclosed this in a statement issued on Thursday by its Public Relations Officer, ASP Mohammed Adeola, following an earlier appeal to members of the public to help locate the deceased’s relatives.

“The command wishes to inform the general public that, following its earlier press release seeking assistance in identifying the family and friends of the late Abraham Safety Osakpolor, contact has now been successfully established with his family,” the statement said.

The command expressed appreciation to individuals, media organisations and members of the public who shared its earlier announcement, saying their cooperation helped achieve the outcome.

It quoted the Commissioner of Police, Airport Police Command, CP Olufunke Ogunbode, as reiterating the command’s commitment to maintaining a cordial relationship with the public.

“Effective policing thrives on mutual trust, cooperation and shared responsibility,” Ogunbode said, according to the statement.

The command had earlier appealed for help in locating Osakpolor’s family after he died in a road accident near the airport.

PUNCH Metro reported that the 58-year-old, who was born in Benin City, Edo State, was hit by a moving vehicle while walking along the expressway leading from the airport towards the Oshodi axis.

He was rushed to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead, and his remains were deposited in a morgue. The police also said the motorist involved in the accident had been apprehended and would be charged in court.

During an initial search, officers recovered a Nigerian passport and a mobile phone without a SIM card from his belongings. A Canadian passport was later discovered by mortuary attendants.

title: NAFDAC uncovers unregistered beverages, skin-lightening injections in Kano
description:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control has intercepted 17 cartons of suspected unregistered beverages, skin-lightening injections and anti-ageing injections at the Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport, Kano State.
NAFDAC disclosed this in a post on its X handle, seen by
content:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control has intercepted 17 cartons of suspected unregistered beverages, skin-lightening injections and anti-ageing injections at the Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport, Kano State.

NAFDAC disclosed this in a post on its X handle, seen by PUNCH Metro on Thursday.

The agency said the seizure was made through its Port Inspection Directorate following a joint examination of a consignment at the Skyway Aviation Handling Company shed at the airport.

According to NAFDAC, the products were discovered concealed in a 33-carton consignment declared as “personal effects” and brought into the country aboard an Ethiopian Airlines flight that arrived a day before the interception.

“The products were discovered concealed within a 33-carton consignment declared as ‘personal effects’ and transported aboard an Ethiopian Airlines flight that arrived the previous day.

“A physical examination revealed that the products bore no NAFDAC registration numbers, while the consignment lacked the requisite import documentation,” NAFDAC stated.

The agency added that the entire consignment had been placed on hold in the custody of the Nigeria Customs Service, while the importer was invited for questioning.

“The importer was subsequently invited for questioning, and a statement was obtained as part of the investigation,” it stated.

NAFDAC, however, said the products had yet to be confirmed as substandard or falsified, adding that their quality and authenticity remained unknown.

It stated that the interception was part of efforts to strengthen surveillance and enforcement at the nation’s entry points to prevent the unlawful importation and circulation of unregistered, substandard and falsified regulated products.

“NAFDAC continues to strengthen surveillance and enforcement at Nigeria’s entry points to prevent the unlawful importation and circulation of unregistered, substandard and falsified regulated products and protect public health,” it added.

title: How Yemi Tella’s lessons shaped Flamingos World Cup triumph – Busari
description: After guiding Nigeria’s Flamingos to a historic FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup triumph, head coach Akeem Busari speaks on the journey to global glory, the experiences that shaped his coaching philosophy and how he built a world-beating team in just seven months. He shares his thoughts with ABIODUN ADEW
content:
After guiding Nigeria’s Flamingos to a historic FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup triumph, head coach Akeem Busari speaks on the journey to global glory, the experiences that shaped his coaching philosophy and how he built a world-beating team in just seven months. He shares his thoughts with ABIODUN ADEWALE

Congratulations on leading Nigeria to the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup title and becoming the first African team to achieve that. How does the achievement make you feel, knowing the passion Nigerians have for football?

Football is a game of emotions, and we know Nigerians to be passionate. For us, representing over 200 million Nigerians at this level, we had to do our bit to show why we were saddled with that responsibility. We are happy, elated and proud that God has used us to put smiles on the faces of Nigerians and Africa as a whole. It is a source of pride for our names, our families and the integrity of the game.

Let’s go back to the days when nobody knew the name Akeem Busari. How did you put in the work over the years to obtain your coaching certificates, build your network and identify grassroots talents to shape your career as a coach?

Some people start in football and quickly move to the sidelines. For others, it may be a rare opportunity, while injuries also push some people into coaching. But the bottom line is perseverance and determination. Whenever an opportunity has not come, you just have to keep developing the talent God has given you and continue to improve yourself through coaching education in line with modern-day demands.

I started after my playing days and obtained my Advanced Diploma, the highest diploma at the National Institute for Sports. I got those certificates between 1999 and 2005. Aside from that, I have attended different courses, both online and physically. I became a CAF-licensed coach in 2016 and have since upgraded to a CAF A Licence.

I have represented Nigerian teams in the CAF Champions League, both male and female. I was with Enyimba during the Confederation Cup in 2022, and I was also with Bayelsa Queens, winning the President Federation Cup with them and taking them to the CAF Women’s Champions League. These are things I have been doing passionately, moving from one club to another. When the opportunity to lead the women’s U-17 team came in April, I had to look inward and identify players within the age bracket who could fit into the team. When we arrived at the numbers we needed for qualification, we played all our matches and won all five games at the WAFU B tournament, scoring a high number of goals.

The World Cup was another level of the game, and we were able to see maturity. Some of our opponents from Europe had players from big clubs and had global experience compared to some of our girls, who were still in school. But we are a gifted country when it comes to talent and capacity, and we were able to apply the basic methodology, which helped us.

At the World Cup, we lost our first game, which was quite difficult but understandable. However, we knew the team we had and believed we could come back. We analysed the games and changed our methodology individually, in pairs, in groups and in terms of team cohesion. That was what fostered the winning formula that took us to the final.

Nigeria had previously won bronze under coach Bankole Olowokere at the 2022 edition in India. How closely did you follow that campaign, and what lessons did you take from that achievement into your seven-month preparation for the tournament?

Coach Bankole is a colleague, and it was good for Nigeria to have been on the podium before. We watched the games they played last year, when they were knocked out in the second round. We saw why we lost to Italy, and it wasn’t because we were bad. We used that as a point of reference. We also picked games that we won and used them to learn. From there, we adopted a mindset that, against every team we played, nobody should score before us. And if they did, how would we respond? If you look at all the games, it was only Poland that scored before us, and that was the only game we lost. So, it was all about mentality. Immediately, we locked into that mindset; it helped us mentally. Even in training, we played with a high numerical advantage against the opposing team and told the players to play. That anxiety, tension and ability to cope with one another, when transferred to our matches against other teams, coupled with our physical ability as Africans, really helped us. We played against teams that had bigger players than ours, but it was a matter of mindset and approach.

What was the biggest challenge you faced during the seven-month preparation for the World Cup?

One of the biggest challenges was the headache of selection. We had some injury challenges, and those players were good enough to make the team. When about two or three of them, who could have added more depth to the team, sustained injuries and went for medical checks, we were told they would be out. We had to look inward, and today, we are celebrating all of us.

We saw the matches on television, but not what happened behind the scenes. What were some of the moments in the dressing room and at camp that helped turn the team into champions?

The first thing was discipline. If we scheduled any activity for 4 pm, everybody would be out and ready 10 minutes before then. Whenever we wanted to do match analysis, nobody was late, and everyone had to come with their roommates. We took it as a mission because we wanted to go back home with the trophy. Everyone was locked in. If there were any issues among the players, the captains would walk up to me and say, ‘Papa, this is what is happening, but don’t say I told you.’ I knew how to manage the situation. They are young players, and we had to ensure they did not lose confidence. We managed them physically and mentally and were even mindful of what we said to them.

How important was the support of your backroom staff to the team’s success?

I had two assistants, Coach Jegede and Coach Omoidiaghe, and Coach Kola Ige as the goalkeeper trainer. There was also Dr Oyinye, the physiotherapist, Charity, Rhoda, the kit manager, the team secretary and everyone else. They were fantastic. The moment I sent a programme, they set up the cones. We made decisions together, and it was a big family.

You have repeatedly emphasised the importance of grassroots football in your career. How did you identify and select the players who eventually formed the World Cup-winning squad?

The grassroots has been my main catchment area. I started from there and was in the setup for 14 years. Even when I moved to big teams, I had one or two grassroots players to work with. I normally produce players and even go as far as writing programmes for players who want to go on trials.

You were the technical director of Pacesetter Queens before your appointment as Flamingos coach. Given the team’s position in the NWFL at the time, some people questioned your credentials for the national team job. How did you handle those doubts, and what does the World Cup triumph say to those who underestimated you?

I was the technical director of Pacesetter Queens, and I joined the team a week after the start of the league. We were a youth team with players who did not have the experience of playing in the league. But we stuck with them, and people would have seen the level of coaching in that team. We gave teams like Edo Queens and Bayelsa Queens a run for their money. One thing Nigerians should understand is that it is about knowing the technical ability of a coach. It is about who the person is and their track record. Sometimes, you have the materials and things work well, but when you don’t have the materials, you also have to ask whether the coach can still achieve something.

Which coaches have had the greatest influence on your career, and whose methods did you draw from as you prepared the Flamingos for the World Cup?

My biggest mentor was the late coach Yemi Tella. I was in camp with him before the 2007 FIFA Men’s U-17 World Cup. That was where I gained experience in managing an U-17 team. I had been with the late Yemi Tella since 1997, even before I attended any coaching course, and he was the one who took me around when I was Lagos State head coach for the National Sports Festival in 2004 and 2005. When he was in camp with his U-17 players in 2007, I was offering technical assistance, and the experience I gathered there was a plus for me when I got the women’s U-17 job almost 19 years later. I think what I sowed is what I am reaping, and I just pray for God’s guidance moving forward.

Can you take us through your journey as a footballer and how injuries influenced your decision to become a coach?

When I was at CMS Grammar School in 1982, I played football for the school and hockey for Lagos State. In 1983, I played both football and hockey for the state, and in 1985, I represented Lagos State in football. That was when I was preparing to pursue further studies after completing my O’Level. In 1986, I sustained an injury to my left knee and could no longer play football as much, so I focused on hockey. I played a couple of club games in hockey, but I did not return to football until I ventured into coaching around 1993. I started with a youth team, and people used to tell me that what I had to offer was better than what some more experienced coaches were offering. So, it is just a gift, and when people see what you have, that pushes you to do more. That was what encouraged me to go to the NIS and become a CAF A-licensed coach, as well as an instructor for CAF and the NFF.

Coaching at the grassroots level is often driven by passion, with limited resources and little financial reward. Now that you and your players are receiving millions of naira in rewards, how significant is this moment for your career and personal life?

Sometimes, you don’t expect anything, and then it comes in multiple folds. I want to thank God for the players and everyone around us. I pray that bigger things will come our way. We cannot rest; we need to redouble our efforts and talents. As I always tell them, immediately you achieve one thing, you want to achieve two. The destination is higher than this, and with discipline, we will get there.

The post How Yemi Tella’s lessons shaped Flamingos World Cup triumph – Busari appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Nigeria records 941 road crash deaths in Q3 – FRSC
description:
Despite recording fewer road crashes and casualties in the third quarter of 2026, no fewer than 941 people died in road traffic accidents across Nigeria during the period, according to figures released by the Federal Road Safety Corps.
The figure represents a 12.6 per cent decline from the 1,077 dea
content:
Despite recording fewer road crashes and casualties in the third quarter of 2026, no fewer than 941 people died in road traffic accidents across Nigeria during the period, according to figures released by the Federal Road Safety Corps.

The figure represents a 12.6 per cent decline from the 1,077 deaths recorded in the corresponding period of 2025, while the number of crashes fell by 13.8 per cent from 2,434 to 2,098.

The FRSC also reported a 14.5 per cent reduction in road traffic injuries, from 6,856 in the third quarter of 2025 to 5,864 in the same period this year.

The figures, released by the Corps in a statement signed by its Corps Public Education Officer, Osondu Ohaeri, on Thursday, were presented at the end-of-year strategy session with commanding officers at the FRSC National Headquarters, Abuja.

Although the Corps described the performance as evidence of progress under its ongoing reforms, the figures show that the country still recorded an average of more than 10 deaths from road crashes every day during the three-month period.

The 2,098 crashes also amounted to about 23 incidents daily, while the 5,864 injuries underscored the continuing human cost of road accidents despite the reported improvement.

The FRSC said the reduction in crashes exceeded its 10 per cent target, attributing the performance to improved operational efficiency, preventive interventions, public enlightenment and enforcement.

However, the statement did not provide a breakdown of the crashes by state, identify the major causes of the accidents or indicate the categories of roads and vehicles responsible for the casualties. It also did not disclose how much of the reported improvement could be directly attributed to specific enforcement or technology interventions.

The figures were presented at the strategy session attended by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume, who reportedly commended the Corps’ performance under the leadership of its Corps Marshal, Shehu Mohammed.

Akume said the results demonstrated progress in the Federal Government’s efforts to improve institutional efficiency and protect lives and property under President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

But the persistent death toll presents a more sobering measure of the country’s road safety challenge, particularly as the FRSC prepares for increased highway traffic during the 2026 festive season.

Mohammed consequently directed commanding officers to intensify patrols along high-risk routes, improve traffic management and strengthen collaboration with other security and emergency-response agencies.

He also ordered the strategic positioning of ambulances, rescue teams and tow trucks, alongside sustained public enlightenment and improved personnel supervision.

The Corps Marshal warned against extortion, negligence and abuse of authority, charging commanding officers to take responsibility for the performance of their commands and ensure that available resources were properly deployed.

As part of its reforms, the FRSC also announced the completion of an upgraded Operations Monitoring and Control Centre at its national headquarters. The facility, commissioned by Akume, is expected to improve patrol monitoring, evidence management and coordination of operational responses.

According to the Corps, the centre will enable it to obtain, preserve and retrieve evidence against traffic offenders, while strengthening transparency and accountability in enforcement.

The FRSC said its road safety strategy was not limited to enforcement but also involved public education, intelligence gathering, technology and stakeholder collaboration.

It maintained that the ultimate measure of its performance should be the number of crashes prevented, injuries avoided and lives saved, rather than the volume of enforcement activities or personnel deployed.

The Corps expressed confidence that its reforms and improved operational capacity would sustain the reductions recorded, while acknowledging the need for further efforts to bring down road traffic casualties.

The post Nigeria records 941 road crash deaths in Q3 – FRSC appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: FG suspends Lagos-Ibadan bridge work after 20-hour gridlock
description:
The Federal Government has suspended the ongoing construction of a pedestrian bridge at the Aseese area of the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway following a gridlock that left motorists stranded for more than 20 hours.
The construction work, being carried out by the Federal Ministry of Works in collaboration
content:
The Federal Government has suspended the ongoing construction of a pedestrian bridge at the Aseese area of the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway following a gridlock that left motorists stranded for more than 20 hours.

The construction work, being carried out by the Federal Ministry of Works in collaboration with CBC Construction Company, was scheduled to run from Wednesday, November 18, to Sunday, November 22, to facilitate the installation of the pedestrian bridge.

The Ogun State Traffic Compliance and Enforcement Agency had earlier announced that the exercise would involve a temporary diversion of inbound Lagos-bound traffic towards the Lagos carriageway at Aseese, before motorists rejoined their normal route at a designated exit point opposite Christ Embassy.

However, the diversion triggered a prolonged traffic jam that began at about 2pm on Wednesday and lasted until about noon on Thursday.

Several motorists were stranded for hours, while many commuters trekked long distances to their destinations.

PUNCH Metro had reported that some commuters who boarded vehicles from Ibadan shortly after 11am did not arrive in Magboro until about 5.30pm. Another motorist lamented spending eight hours travelling from Mowe to Magboro.

Many frustrated motorists abandoned their vehicles and trekked several kilometres to their destinations.

Commercial motorcycle operators also took advantage of the situation to increase their fares, with one rider demanding as much asN6,000 from a passenger travelling from Mowe to Ibafo.

The gridlock was further worsened as some drivers resorted to driving against traffic to escape the congestion.

Lamenting the situation on Wednesday night, the Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Media and Communications, Sunday Dare, criticised the timing of the construction work.

Dare, in a post on his Facebook account, said the prolonged gridlock had left thousands of commuters stranded, with many forced to abandon their vehicles and trek to their destinations.

He questioned why the Chinese contractor handling the project chose to carry out the work during peak traffic hours instead of at night when vehicular movement was lighter.

Dare wrote, “Tonight – Lagos -Ibadan Expressway. I have been in a traffic gridlock for over five hours trying to get out of Lagos to Ibadan for multiple radio and television appearances ahead of the APC Presidential Rally coming up on Saturday in Ibadan.

“It beats me why a Chinese Contractor would choose the busiest hours of vehicular traffic to construct the bridge and road around this exit point. Stranded cars, thousands of people trekking to get home.

“What happened to doing construction work during the obituary hours when traffic is lean? This is unnecessary pain. It needs to be corrected.”

Other road users also took to social media to share their experiences.

A Facebook user, Adiatu Adeoye, wrote, “My truck spent 12hrs in the gridlock.”

Another user, Ojewale Adewale, lamented, “Got to Interchange from Abeokuta enroute Lagos by 3pm, I am just getting home now 9.59pm.”

Kemi Adewuyi also wrote, “I met the traffic yesterday afternoon on my way from work, still met it this morning on my way to work, it was terrible. Imagine paying N500 from car park C to Mowe bus stop this morning.”

Monitoring the situation on Thursday morning, our correspondent observed that the gridlock had persisted overnight and into the afternoon.

Some commuters also abandoned their journeys after commercial drivers increased their fares to as much as N3,000 from Mowe to Berger, compared with the usual fare of between N700 and N800.

Commercial motorcyclists also raised their fares to as much as N5,000 for the same journey.

However, at about noon on Thursday, traffic had eased and movement was restored along the affected section of the expressway.

Following the development, TRACE announced that the construction work has been suspended indefinitely.

The agency stated that the suspension followed the traffic challenges experienced along the corridor from Wednesday to Thursday morning.

TRACE spokesperson, Babatunde Akinbiyi, said the development necessitated a review of the traffic management arrangements surrounding the construction activities.

“Consequently, all motorists are hereby advised that the temporary traffic diversion associated with the pedestrian bridge construction is suspended, pending further directives from the relevant authorities.

“TRACE regrets the inconveniences, delays and discomfort this development may have caused motorists and other road users. We sincerely appreciate the patience, understanding and cooperation of the motoring public,” he stated.

Also, the acting Controller of the Federal Ministry of Works in Ogun State, Richard Adeleye, confirmed that the bridge work was suspended due to the traffic situation when contacted on Thursday.

“Yes, it was suspended due to the traffic situation,” Adeleye said in a telephone conversation with our correspondent.

Meanwhile, some road users called for the construction and rehabilitation of inner roads linking the expressway to provide alternative routes during traffic congestion.

A commuter, Kunle Adeleke, told our correspondent that functional inner roads would have provided alternative routes for motorists during the gridlock.

“If the inner roads are good, they would have served as the alternative routes for motorists during traffic situation. Ogun State Government should fix the inner roads and end this gridlock suffering every time,” he said.

Another commuter, Jamiu Akinsola, urged the Federal Government to monitor contractors handling projects along busy corridors to prevent a recurrence.

“Infrastructural development is good but the welfare of the people must be taking into consideration.

“The FG must call its contractors to order and inform them to put the wellbeing of the citizens first. We should be doing better than these at this stage of our national development,” he said.

The post FG suspends Lagos-Ibadan bridge work after 20-hour gridlock appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Osimhen ranks 5th among CIES’ most valuable strikers
description:
Galatasaray striker Victor Osimhen has been ranked fifth among the most valuable strikers playing outside Europe’s five major leagues, according to a study by the International Centre for Sports Studies.
The study ranked players by estimated transfer fees and placed the Nigerian at €53.7m. He is the
content:
Galatasaray striker Victor Osimhen has been ranked fifth among the most valuable strikers playing outside Europe’s five major leagues, according to a study by the International Centre for Sports Studies.

The study ranked players by estimated transfer fees and placed the Nigerian at €53.7m. He is the only player from the Turkish Süper Lig in the top five.

Club Brugge’s Nicolo Tresoldi leads the list at €67.8m, followed by Benfica’s Vangelis Pavlidis at €61.2m, Sporting Lisbon’s Luis Suarez at €57.6m and Palmeiras’ Jose Manuel Lopez at €54.8m.

The 27-year-old has scored 10 goals and provided three assists in 11 official matches this season, a direct contribution to 13 goals. He is reported to earn €21m annually from the Turkish champions.

Osimhen’s season has been disrupted by injury. He hurt his knee in Galatasaray’s 2-0 Champions League win over VfB Stuttgart on November 3 and later underwent successful surgery.

The injury ruled him out of Nigeria’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Tanzania.

Galatasaray vice president Mehmet Cibara has described the problem as a long-standing one and dismissed suggestions that the club’s pitch was responsible.

title: Obalende MTN bus park to open December, accommodate 1,000 buses — Wahab
description:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni



The Lagos State Government has said the ongoing redevelopment of the Obalende Bus Park, known as the Y’ello Bus Park, will be completed and ready for public use by the end of December 2026.







The facility, being developed by MTN Nigeria as part of its Corporate Social Re
content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

The Lagos State Government has said the ongoing redevelopment of the Obalende Bus Park, known as the Y’ello Bus Park, will be completed and ready for public use by the end of December 2026.

The facility, being developed by MTN Nigeria as part of its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiative, is designed to accommodate more than 1,000 buses.

Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, disclosed this during an inspection tour of the Obalende project and another MTN-sponsored under-bridge recreational park at Falomo, Ikoyi.

Wahab, who was accompanied by key government officials, including the Special Adviser to the Governor on Transportation, Sola Giwa; Special Adviser on Environment, Engr. Adekunle Akodu; General Manager of the Lagos State Parks and Gardens Agency (LASPARK), Adetoun Popoola; and Director of Drainage Services, Engr. Mahamood Adegbite, said the six-week completion window was agreed upon after consultations with stakeholders to resolve operational challenges.

He explained that the project was initially scheduled for completion within 21 weeks following an inspection of the area by Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu and his deputy as part of efforts to transform the previously degraded environment into a modern transport hub.

However, construction was delayed by logistical challenges involving existing transport operators conducting business at the site.

Wahab said the government had engaged the transport unions, contractors and the Special Adviser on Transportation to agree on temporarily relocating operators from the immediate construction area to enable the contractors to complete the work.

“Today was just to see how far they’ve gone. Thankfully, they had one or two logistics issues that had to do with the businesses that have been operating there, legacy things like the transport business.

“We had to engage the Special Adviser to the Governor on Transportation, the transport unions, and the contractors to see how we can give them a space for a maximum of six weeks—not shutting the place down 100 per cent, but moving them out of that immediate workspace to enable the contractors to complete it and hand it over to them to operate,” he said.

The upgraded facility is designed to accommodate approximately 1,000 buses and will feature dedicated parking and loading bays, sleeping facilities for drivers, modern toilet facilities and green areas.

The design also incorporates collapsible barriers along the perimeter to allow drainage maintenance teams access to the adjoining canal for regular cleaning and maintenance.

Addressing concerns about possible commercialisation of the facility and increases in transport fares, Giwa assured commuters and commercial transport operators that access to the terminal would be free.

“No, there’s no toll at all. It is for them; they are the ones using it. We are just making it a standard park that we will replicate all over the state as time goes on,” he said.

On the management of the facility after completion, Giwa said it would remain the property of the Lagos State Government under the supervision of the Ministry of Transportation.

He added that the government was working with transport unions to ensure effective utilisation of the facility and prevent its takeover by miscreants.

Giwa also warned commercial bus drivers against picking up passengers or parking along road corridors outside the designated terminal after its opening.

He said the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) would enforce compliance with traffic regulations.

“By the time we finish this place, there will be no need for us to have any bus on the road, and Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, LASTMA, will be on the ground to ensure they comply with all the rules and regulations of Lagos State.

“The laws are there. No one is above the law. We have provided the park for you, and if you come out of that park to obstruct traffic, definitely the law will take its course,” he warned.

Falomo under-bridge gets recreational park

Following the inspection at Obalende, the delegation visited the Falomo under-bridge, where MTN is also transforming a previously degraded space into a recreational park for public use.

Speaking at the site, LASPARK General Manager, Popoola, said the area, which was previously characterised by indiscriminate waste dumping and misuse, was being reclaimed as a relaxation centre for residents.

She said the facility would follow the model of the JJT Park in Alausa and remain open to the public free of charge for everyday recreational activities.

However, corporate organisations and other groups seeking to organise formal events or competitions at the venue would be required to pay a nominal maintenance fee, she added.

The Obalende project was formally handed over to MTN Nigeria by the Lagos State Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources on April 15, 2026, with an initial 21-week completion target.

The September 11 deadline was missed following delays attributed to heavy rainfall between June and August and operational challenges involving existing park management.

Construction resumed in mid-October, with clearing, foundation work and material deliveries, while interlocking pavement, curbing and fencing works were ongoing as of mid-November.

The wider redevelopment plan also includes electric vehicle charging points, more than 60 public toilet fixtures, a recycling drop-off station, kiosks and commercial spaces, solar lighting and tree planting.

Other components include a Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA) road camp for street sweepers and security personnel, improved lighting and CCTV facilities, as well as maintenance arrangements for the park and adjoining Macgregor Canal.

The post Obalende MTN bus park to open December, accommodate 1,000 buses — Wahab appeared first on Vanguard News.
