title: Northern leaders have failed region, need collective development agenda – Kaduna Gov
description:
Kaduna State Governor, Senator Uba Sani, has challenged past and present leaders of Northern Nigeria to accept responsibility for the region’s development challenges and evolve a common agenda to address its economic, security and social problems.
 He said northern leaders, including himself, had fa
content:
Kaduna State Governor, Senator Uba Sani, has challenged past and present leaders of Northern Nigeria to accept responsibility for the region’s development challenges and evolve a common agenda to address its economic, security and social problems.

 He said northern leaders, including himself, had failed the people and must be prepared to tell themselves the truth rather than exploit ethnic, religious and regional sentiments to seek political support.

 The governor made the call on Wednesday at a summit on Good Governance, Inclusivity and Sustainable Development organised by the Sir Ahmadu Bello Memorial Foundation in Kaduna.

 He urged the foundation to convene past and present leaders of northern extraction to develop a comprehensive regional development blueprint similar to the vision of the late Premier of Northern Nigeria, Sir Ahmadu Bello.

 Uba Sani said the late premier envisioned a united, peaceful and self-sufficient Northern Nigeria but lamented that subsequent generations of leaders had deviated from that vision.

 He said, “We must look ourselves in the mirror and tell ourselves some home truths. All of us, including myself, have failed the people of Northern Nigeria in one way or another.

 “We must come together, irrespective of our political affiliations, religious beliefs and ethnic backgrounds, to fashion out a collective agenda for the development of the North.”

 The governor also criticised politicians campaigning ahead of the 2027 general elections by appealing to regional sentiments without explaining their contributions to the development of the North while holding public offices.

 He said political leaders should be judged by their records in office and their ability to address the challenges confronting the people rather than where they come from.

 Uba Sani, however, attributed some of the achievements recorded by his administration to the support of President Bola Tinubu, whom he thanked for his interventions in Kaduna State.

 “I want to seize this opportunity to thank the President for all that he has done for Kaduna State in the last three and a half years,” he said.

 The governor recalled that he approached Tinubu over the completion of the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano highway, describing the road as a major gateway linking the northern and southern parts of the country.

 He said the President released billions of naira for the completion of the project, which had previously suffered delays.

 “Today, the road is almost 95 per cent completed,” he said.

 On the proposed Kaduna Light Rail project, Uba Sani said he and the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, had met with Tinubu to secure the President’s approval for the initiative.

 “I am happy to say that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, knowing the history of Kaduna, decided to approve $865m for the Kaduna Light Rail project. The contract has been signed.

 “By the grace of God, in the next two weeks, he will be coming to Kaduna to perform the groundbreaking. That will be the second light rail project in the whole of Nigeria,” he said.

 The governor also reeled out achievements of his administration since assuming office on May 29, 2023, including interventions in pensions, transportation, agriculture, education and security.

 He said his administration inherited pension liabilities of about N24bn but had paid more than N21bn to 9,683 state and local government retirees and families of deceased workers.

 On transportation, Uba Sani said 100 buses had been deployed under the state’s free Compressed Natural Gas bus service, adding that the scheme had recorded 5.2 million passenger trips and saved commuters more than N5bn.

 He said insecurity had previously prevented children in some communities from attending school and farmers from accessing their farmlands.

 According to him, the Kaduna Peace Model has enabled farmers to reclaim more than 500,000 hectares of previously inaccessible farmland.

 “There is no single school that has remained closed in Kaduna State due to insecurity at the moment,” he said.

 The governor further disclosed that his administration had increased the annual agricultural budgetary allocation from N1.48bn to more than N100bn to strengthen food production and support farmers.

 He said more than 69,000 smallholder farmers had received improved agricultural inputs, while over 1,400 truckloads of fertiliser had been distributed to more than 500,000 farmers across the state’s 23 local government areas.

 Uba Sani added that the government had facilitated access to more than 200 tractors through partnerships and enrolled over 100,000 farmers in crop insurance schemes.

 “We have also supported 5,000 livestock farmers with equipment and production inputs. Through the Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones and the Rural Access and Agricultural Marketing Project, we are linking farms to processors and markets, where better access can reduce losses and improve returns,” he said. ENDS…

The post Northern leaders have failed region, need collective development agenda – Kaduna Gov appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: IGP Disu emerges new president of Nigeria Judo Federation
description:
The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, has been unanimously elected President of the Nigeria Judo Federation at its National Elective Congress in Abuja on Thursday, November 19, The PUNCH reports.
The 13 eligible voters at the congress backed Disu, who is a third-dan black belt holder. The
content:
The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, has been unanimously elected President of the Nigeria Judo Federation at its National Elective Congress in Abuja on Thursday, November 19, The PUNCH reports.

The 13 eligible voters at the congress backed Disu, who is a third-dan black belt holder. The congress was organised by the Caretaker Committee led by Sheriff Hammed.

Disu began his judo career in 1986 and has won several medals since then. They include gold at the 1990 National Sports Festival, the Nigerian Police Games and various veterans’ championships. In July 2022, he won silver in the veterans’ -100kg category at the 33rd US Open Judo Championship. He has also served as Chairman of the Lagos State Judo Association and is the Patron of the Nigerian Police Judo Association.

In his acceptance speech, Disu called for reconciliation and unity in the judo community. “This is a very important day in my life. For the first time, I have both voted and been voted for in an election, and I am deeply honoured by the confidence reposed in me,” he said.

“There is no individual winner today. The real winner is judo because the sport is bigger than all of us. It is time for reconciliation and for us to reunite everyone who has been divided. Many people contributed to the growth of this sport, and we must bring them back into the fold.

“We will reach out to our great judokas, both within and outside the country, to foster reconciliation and strengthen our federation. I sincerely thank everyone for the trust and support you have shown me.”

Nwaobilor Ananaba was elected Vice President, while Emmanuel Ghahabo emerged as Second Vice President.

Other members of the new board are Catherine Ewa-Ekuta, Bassey Ekanem Ekwere (Paramilitary Representative), Ika Bassey Odo (Technical Representative), Ezeri Agahata (Athletes’ Representative), Chijioke Okechukwu (NAPHER-SD Representative), David Jesuorobo Osaghae (International Representative), Lawrence Ezeudu (South-East Representative), Osahon Eke (South-South Representative), Tokunbo Ajanaku (South-West Representative), Rosa Collins (NAWIS Representative), Salisu Mahmuda (North-West Representative) and Sunday Ewa (North-East Representative). Two more members are expected to be co-opted onto the board.

Hammed said the smooth election showed that Nigerian judo was on the right path.

“First, I want to congratulate the Nigeria Judo Federation family on the successful conduct of the election and the emergence of IGP Tunji Disu as President. As Chairman of the Caretaker Committee, I am proud that we have successfully fulfilled our mandate of facilitating a credible transition and restoring elected leadership to the federation,” he said.

“This is a new beginning for Nigerian judo. Our priority has always been the interest of the sport, not individuals. I commend all stakeholders for their cooperation and urge everyone to unite behind the new leadership as we work towards a stronger, more transparent and progressive Nigeria Judo Federation. The task now is to move forward together and take Nigerian judo to greater heights.”

Hammed also thanked the National Sports Commission, led by its Chairman, Shehu Dikko, and Director-General, Bukola Olopade, for helping to reposition the sport and strengthen its future development.

The post IGP Disu emerges new president of Nigeria Judo Federation appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: INEC tightens safeguards against  fake results, electoral manipulation
description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has tightened safeguards against electoral manipulation ahead of the 2027 general elections, introducing automated checks to detect over-voting and discrepancies in polling unit results before their transmission to its Result Viewing Portal (IReV)
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has tightened safeguards against electoral manipulation ahead of the 2027 general elections, introducing automated checks to detect over-voting and discrepancies in polling unit results before their transmission to its Result Viewing Portal (IReV).

The commission has also strengthened its result-uploading and validation procedures, removed more than 1.6 million invalid entries from the voter register and procured 57,000 additional Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices as part of measures to address irregularities that could undermine the credibility of the polls.

INEC Chairman, Joash Amupitan, who disclosed these measures at the 2026 Annual Lecture and Awards of the Association of Corporate Online Editors (ACOE) in Abuja yesterday, said polling unit figures entered on Form EC8A would undergo automated arithmetic consistency and over-voting checks before transmission to IReV.

Amupitan, represented by his Chief Press Secretary, Adebayo Oketola, said the commission was strengthening its electoral systems against manipulation, misinformation and operational lapses, while reaffirming its neutrality in the contest between the ruling party and opposition parties.

He warned that artificial intelligence-generated misinformation, synthetic voice cloning, manipulated videos and fabricated election results posed serious threats to public confidence and electoral security, urging the media and political parties to collaborate with INEC in protecting the integrity of the electoral process.

Speaking on the theme, “Roadmap to 2027: Strengthening Electoral Security Through Collaboration between INEC, the Media, and Political Parties for Credible and Hitch-Free Elections,” the chairman said the commission would not serve as an appendage of any political party, whether in government or opposition.

He maintained that institutional neutrality, compliance with electoral laws and transparent administration would guide INEC’s preparations and conduct of the elections.

According to him, the commission has reduced the number of voters assigned to each BVAS device from 1,250 to 850 to minimise accreditation delays, while making provisions for 232,658 registered voters with disabilities.

“INEC has reduced the number of voters assigned to each BVAS device from 1,250 to 850 to minimise accreditation delays.

“The commission has also made provisions for 232,658 persons with disabilities registered to vote.”

Amupitan explained that INEC had conducted four major off-cycle elections and 16 legislative by-elections since the current leadership assumed office in October 2025, noting that the exercises provided opportunities to identify operational weaknesses, assess logistics and improve electoral procedures ahead of the general elections.

He reiterated that the presidential and National Assembly elections would hold on January 16, 2027, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections were scheduled for February 6.

As part of its earlier announced preparations, INEC is scheduled to conduct a nationwide mock accreditation and electronic result transmission exercise on November 28 across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory to test its systems ahead of the polls.

On electoral security, Amupitan said the commission was collaborating with the Office of the National Security Adviser and the Nigeria Police Force through the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security, with arrangements being extended to state, local government and registration area levels to protect electoral personnel, materials and voters.

He cautioned political parties against campaign violence, intimidation and attacks on electoral officials and facilities, reminding them that the Electoral Act 2026 prescribed penalties for abusive campaign speeches, incitement and the deployment of private armed guards and masquerades at political rallies.

The INEC chairman urged political party leaders to restrain their supporters and pursue electoral grievances through lawful channels rather than resorting to violence.

Meanwhile, the commission has endorsed a voluntary Code of Conduct for independent tabulation and publication of election results, warning that unofficial tallies, projections and independently aggregated figures must not be presented as officially declared results.

Amupitan gave the endorsement at a stakeholders’ roundtable convened by Yiaga Africa in Abuja, where he said independent verification of election figures must complement electoral accountability without creating rival centres of statutory authority.

Represented by INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Lawrence Bayode, the chairman said the proposed code would strengthen transparency, promote responsible publication of electoral figures and protect public confidence during result collation.

“Independent verification should complement electoral accountability, not create competing centres of statutory authority.”

He outlined six guiding principles for the framework, including methodological integrity, accuracy, information integrity, data security, error accountability and voluntary compliance.

Yiaga Africa’s Executive Director, Samson Itodo, who disclosed the development in a statement on Thursday, said independent tabulation remained an important mechanism for citizens to scrutinise election outcomes and assess the credibility of the electoral process.

He, however, warned that differences in methodologies, data interpretation and publication standards could generate confusion during sensitive collation periods if organisations involved failed to adopt common safeguards.

According to him, the proposed code would establish minimum standards for independent tabulation, discourage premature declarations and ensure that published findings were supported by reliable verification.

Itodo said Yiaga Africa would lead further consultations to translate the agreed principles into a practical framework before the general elections.

Participants at the roundtable, including civil society organisations, political parties, election observers and media regulatory bodies, examined different independent tabulation models, including Yiaga Africa’s Processing Results Voter Tabulation, the Election Results Analysis Dashboard and aggregations from IReV.

They agreed that organisations publishing independently collated results must clearly disclose their methodologies, data sources and margins of error to prevent public misinterpretation.

The stakeholders also emphasised human verification, audit trails, data security and transparent error-correction procedures, while media representatives stressed the responsibility of journalists to verify electoral figures and distinguish independent projections from results officially declared by INEC.

Representatives of the National Broadcasting Commission, Broadcasting Organisations of Nigeria, Nigerian Press Council and Nigeria Union of Journalists attended the meeting.

The post INEC tightens safeguards against fake results, electoral manipulation appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Fidelity Bank names Chiedoziem Amuchie new CEO
description:
Fidelity Bank Plc has announced the appointment of Stanley Chiedoziem Amuchie as its substantive Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, effective January 1, 2027.
The appointment, which has received the approval of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), will see Amuchie succeed Nneka Onyeali-Ikp
content:
Fidelity Bank Plc has announced the appointment of Stanley Chiedoziem Amuchie as its substantive Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, effective January 1, 2027.

The appointment, which has received the approval of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), will see Amuchie succeed Nneka Onyeali-Ikpe, whose tenure ends on December 31, 2026.

Amuchie is currently an Executive Director and Chief Operations and Information Officer of the bank.

The Chairman of Fidelity Bank, Amaka Onwughalu, said the appointment reflected the board’s confidence in his leadership ability, industry experience and understanding of the bank’s business.

“We are delighted to confirm Stanley Amuchie as the substantive Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of Fidelity Bank. His appointment reflects the Board’s confidence in his leadership capabilities, strategic insight, extensive industry experience and deep understanding of the Bank’s business.

“We are confident that he will provide the leadership required to consolidate our achievements and drive the Bank’s next phase of growth,” she said.

Onwughalu also praised Onyeali-Ikpe for her contributions to the bank, describing her tenure as one marked by strategic vision, bold leadership and commitment to building a stronger institution.

“Under her stewardship, the Bank recorded significant milestones, strengthened its market position and expanded its strategic reach. We are deeply grateful for her dedication and the enduring legacy she leaves behind,” she said.

She added that the board would support the incoming CEO in driving innovation, operational efficiency and sustainable growth.

Amuchie brings more than 30 years of experience in the financial services industry, with expertise in leadership, financial management, strategy and institutional transformation.

He became Executive Director, Operations and Information Technology, at Fidelity Bank in January 2022, where he helped strengthen the bank’s operations and drive technology-led transformation.

Before joining Fidelity Bank, he worked at Zenith Bank Plc, where he held several senior positions, including Group Chief Financial Officer.

His professional achievements include playing a key role in Fidelity Bank’s acquisition of Union Bank UK, now known as FidBank UK, and contributing to the successful refinancing of the bank’s $400m Eurobond.

He also has experience in capital raising, treasury management, financial strategy and international business expansion.

Amuchie holds a First Class degree in Industrial Chemistry and a Master’s degree in Corporate Governance. He is a Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria and an Honorary Senior Member of the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria. He is also pursuing a PhD in Management of Technology and Innovation.

His appointment comes as Fidelity Bank seeks to strengthen its market position, expand its digital services and grow its presence in local and international markets.

The bank serves more than 14 million customers through digital channels and 255 business offices in Nigeria, as well as its United Kingdom subsidiary, FidBank UK Limited.

title: 2027: Anyone fighting Mbah is  fighting me, Jim Nwododo declares
description:
Second Republic governor of old Anambra State, Senator Jim Nwobodo, said Governor Peter Mbah of Enugu State has performed exceptionally in his first tenure in office, and deserves a second term, declaring that anyone fighting the governor is also fighting him.
Nwobodo, who said he was setting foot o
content:
Second Republic governor of old Anambra State, Senator Jim Nwobodo, said Governor Peter Mbah of Enugu State has performed exceptionally in his first tenure in office, and deserves a second term, declaring that anyone fighting the governor is also fighting him.

Nwobodo, who said he was setting foot on the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT) for the first time since he left office in 1983, was, however, in for a pleasant surprise as Governor Mbah announced plans to rename the university after the octogenarian, who founded the institution way back in 1980.

Nwobodo spoke at the 3rd Distinguished Personality Lecture of the ESUT delivered by him at the Peter Ndubuisi Mbah Multipurpose Auditorium, ESUT, Enugu, yesterday.

He said he had advised all the other candidates to shelve their ambitions in deference to excellence in governance as personified by Mbah.

“Anyone fighting Governor Peter Mbah is fighting me. He should be supported to complete his eight years in office. Others did their eight years, and nobody can deprive him of his complete tenure of two terms.

“Again, I want to make this message clear: Governor Mbah deserves to serve eight years because he is doing well as governor. I want to enjoin the good people of Enugu State to vote for Governor Mbah to complete the good work his administration is doing. He is the most qualified of all the candidates contesting for the office.

“I have received all the other candidates coming to me that they wanted to be governor. I asked them if Governor Mbah is doing well, and they said yes. Then I asked them, why are they now contesting since the governor is doing a good job.

“I told them the only candidate vying for governor in Enugu State, today, is Governor Peter Mbah. I know he is going to be re-elected,” he stated.

He commended the progress made by ESUT and other universities that grew from it, saying he took the step to establish the university, invest in scholarships and education to ensure that people of the old Anambra State had access to quality education after the civil war.

In his address, Governor Mbah said plans were afoot to rename ESUT after the elder statesman, but subject to legislative and other due process.

Mbah said the idea, which was first suggested by the ESUT alumni association, was in tandem with his thoughts as a befitting tribute to the elder statesman, who founded the institution, which has played a critical role in the human capital development of the old Anambra State and Nigeria.

“Recently, representatives of the alumni of this university and its associated institutions came to see me. They asked that Enugu State University of Science and Technology be renamed in honour of Senator Jim Ifeanyichukwu Nwobodo.

“I told them that I support the proposal. I was particularly encouraged that the request came from the alumni who understand, through their own experience, what the university has meant to people’s lives.

“There is a legal process to follow. ESUT was established by law, and changing its name would require the appropriate legislative steps and engagement with relevant stakeholders. I intend to begin those engagements and work with the institutions concerned to advance the proposal through the proper process.

“Your Excellency, I hope that gives you some sense of the regard in which your contribution continues to be held.”

The governor praised Nwobodo’s vision and courage in leadership, especially for investing heavily in human capital development, taking the bold step to establish ESUT a few years after the civil war, not minding the enormity of the challenges involved.

“I have often wondered what it must have felt like to be governor in 1979. Nigeria had just returned to civilian government after thirteen years of military rule. The Civil War had ended less than a decade earlier, and the country was still dealing with its consequences. There was much to rebuild, and enormous pressure on the resources available to the government.

“For many families, university education remained beyond their reach. And here was a young governor, who decided that his state should establish a university of science and technology.

“People questioned whether it could be done. Was there enough money? Could a state government sustain such an institution? Shouldn’t this be left to the federal government?

These were reasonable questions. I suspect some of them would have kept you awake at night.

“But for Jim Nwobodo, the fact that a problem is difficult does not mean we can afford to avoid it. In July 1980, Anambra State University of Technology was established. Forty-six years later, we are gathered in one of the institutions that grew from that decision. And generations of young people have gained opportunities that might otherwise have been beyond their reach,” he stated.

Mbah noted that beyond the establishment of ESUT, the Nwobodo administration encouraged communities to build schools, with the government providing teachers and other support.

“He also invested in industry, seeking to create employment and strengthen the state’s productive capacity. Some of those industries later fell into decline and, today, we are working to bring a number of them back into use.

“The value of such decisions is ultimately found in people’s lives. A child who could attend school in their own community. A young person who became the first in their family to enter university. A household supported by employment in a local industry,” he stated.

He hailed generations of academics, administrators and staff, who have sustained ESUT through changing governments, difficult economic circumstances, and the demands of educating successive generations.

“In this regard, I want to assure the university community that the Enugu State Government is committed to the full implementation of the Academic Staff Union of Universities’ agreement with the Federal Government.

“We are already speaking with legislators to firm up its inclusion in the budget for implementation as soon as possible,” he assured.

Meanwhile, a major highpoint of the event was the conferment of an Honorary Doctorate Degree in Leadership, Governance, and Human Capital Development on Nwobodo.

ESUT’s Vice Chancellor, Prof. Aloysius-Michaels Okolie, said it was in appreciation of the ex-governor’s huge contributions to the development of Enugu State, but also the entire old Anambra State, listing his many achievements.

Another highpoint was the unveiling of Senator Nwobodo’s iconic status and the commissioning of a newly constructed road, Peter Mbah Drive, by the governor.

title: Nigeria protests calls to ban citizens from South Africa
description:
• Fani-Kayode writes South African authorities, Nigerian Foreign Ministry
From Aidoghie Paulinus, Abuja
Nigeria has formally protested calls by an anti-immigrant group in South Africa for a ban on Nigerians entering the country, as the South African government distanced itself from the campaign and
content:
• Fani-Kayode writes South African authorities, Nigerian Foreign Ministry

From Aidoghie Paulinus, Abuja

Nigeria has formally protested calls by an anti-immigrant group in South Africa for a ban on Nigerians entering the country, as the South African government distanced itself from the campaign and rejected the blanket criminalisation of Nigerian nationals.

Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Olufemi Fani-Kayode, conveyed the country’s concerns to South Africa’s Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) following a protest in Pretoria by the March and March group, whose members accused Nigerians of involvement in drug trafficking and demanded restrictions on their entry into the country.

Fani-Kayode also communicated the development to Nigeria’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Abuja, while assuring Nigerians resident in South Africa that the mission was working with the host authorities to safeguard their welfare.

His Special Adviser on Media and Communications, Lizzy Okoji, confirmed the diplomatic communication to Daily Sun, although she declined to disclose its full contents.

“Ambassador Olufemi Fani-Kayode has formally expressed his concerns about these troubling sentiments in an official communication to the Director-General of DIRCO, the South African Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and communicated same to our Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Abuja,” Okoji said.

She urged Nigerians in South Africa to remain calm and take necessary precautions, stressing that the high commission was monitoring developments.

“We are studying the situation closely and will do all we can, in conjunction and collaboration with the South African authorities, to keep our citizens safe,” Fani-Kayode said.

The diplomatic intervention followed a protest march in Pretoria by members of March and March, who demanded that the South African government prohibit Nigerians from entering the country over allegations of drug-related crimes.

The protesters, led by Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma, marched through Sunnyside, a Pretoria suburb with a substantial Nigerian population, sometimes referred to as Little Lagos.

Ngobese-Zuma questioned the concentration of Nigerians in the area and challenged the community’s association with Lagos.

“I am being told here that we have entered Sunnyside, the home of Nigerians. I am inviting Nigerians to come out let’s talk to each other. We want to know who gave you this place and called it Nigeria. Who gave you permission to call this place Lagos or whatever you call it?” she said.

The group’s legal officer, Xolani Zuma, went further, demanding an outright ban on Nigerian nationals.

“The state must ban Nigerians from South Africa. They must ban Nigerians until they stop selling drugs to our people. The rest of Africa we are fine, but we do not want Nigerians in South Africa anymore, that is what we are saying,” Zuma declared.

However, the South African government rejected the group’s position, insisting that the protest did not reflect its policy towards Nigerians or other foreign nationals.

Spokesperson to South Africa’s Minister of International Relations and Cooperation, Phindile Kunene, told *Daily Sun* that although the country’s constitution guaranteed the right to protest, demonstrations must remain peaceful and unarmed.

“The actions of March and March do not represent the position of the South African government.

“We do not condone the wholesale characterisation of Nigerians or nationals of any other country through a criminal lens,” Kunene said.

She acknowledged that South Africa had previously raised concerns about the involvement of some Nigerian nationals in criminal activities, including drug-related offences and wire fraud.

According to her, Minister of International Relations and Cooperation, Ronald Lamola, raised the concerns during discussions with a high-level Nigerian government delegation in Abuja in July 2026.

Kunene, however, stressed that law enforcement must target individuals suspected of criminal conduct rather than subject entire national communities to suspicion or collective punishment.

She said measures against criminal activities should be evidence-based and directed at offenders, without profiling the broader law-abiding Nigerian population in South Africa.

“We are committed to strengthening bilateral relations between our two nations,” she stated.

The post Nigeria protests calls to ban citizens from South Africa appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Fresh crisis looms in varsities over unpaid salaries
description:
From Fred Ezeh, Abuja
A fresh industrial crisis is looming in public universities as the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) has demanded immediate payment of the outstanding three-and-a-half months’ salaries withheld during its 2022 strike, warning that further delay could disrupt the fragi
content:
From Fred Ezeh, Abuja

A fresh industrial crisis is looming in public universities as the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) has demanded immediate payment of the outstanding three-and-a-half months’ salaries withheld during its 2022 strike, warning that further delay could disrupt the fragile industrial peace in the university system.

The union accused the Federal Government of reneging on President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to resolve the dispute, lamenting that only four of the seven-and-a-half months’ salaries withheld under former President Muhammadu Buhari had been paid.

ASUU President, Chris Piwuna, raised the alarm in a statement issued in Abuja following the union’s National Executive Council (NEC) meeting held from November 13 to 14 at the University of Abuja.

Piwuna said the continued withholding of the salaries amounted to unjust punishment of lecturers who had made enormous sacrifices to recover the academic time lost during the 2022 industrial action.

He recalled that Tinubu, before assuming office in 2023, acknowledged that the prolonged strike could have been avoided if the government had addressed grievances arising from the poor implementation and failure to renegotiate the 2009 Federal Government-ASUU Agreement.

According to the union, the President had also indicated that clemency could provide a basis for resolving the withheld salaries, but efforts to secure payment had yielded no result.

ASUU alleged that the President’s Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila, and Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, had maintained that the government was unwilling to pay the outstanding arrears, while attempts to secure a direct audience with Tinubu had been unsuccessful.

The union faulted what it described as the selective application of the government’s “No Work, No Pay” policy, arguing that lecturers had endured delayed salary shortfalls, promotion arrears and third-party deductions without compensation.

It maintained that its members had forfeited annual and research leave and worked additional hours to enable students affected by the strike to complete their programmes, despite the personal and professional sacrifices involved.

ASUU insisted that its members were demanding legitimate entitlements rather than favours, rejecting what it described as the government’s strategy of prolonging negotiations without resolving outstanding grievances.

The union appealed to Tinubu to intervene personally and authorise the immediate release of the salaries in the interest of fairness, justice and industrial stability.

It warned that continued delay could undermine efforts to stabilise public universities and trigger renewed industrial disharmony.

“The struggle continues,” the union declared.

title: INEC must open AI system to independent audit –Atiku
description:
• Asks NASS to summon commission’s leadership
From Ndubuisi Orji, Abuja
Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has demanded an independent audit of the artificial intelligence (AI) system the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) plans to deploy i
content:
• Asks NASS to summon commission’s leadership

From Ndubuisi Orji, Abuja

Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has demanded an independent audit of the artificial intelligence (AI) system the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) plans to deploy in processing polling-unit results for the 2027 general elections, warning that undisclosed algorithms could delay, reject or interfere with valid election results.

Atiku, who called for access to the system’s source code, training data and decision logs, also urged the National Assembly to summon INEC’s leadership and Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Directorate to publicly explain its design, safeguards and arrangements for independent scrutiny.

In a statement by the Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, the former Vice President disclosed that he had written to INEC Chairman, Joash Amupitan, demanding algorithmic transparency, independent auditing and clear procedures for human oversight.

The demand followed INEC’s announcement that it would integrate AI and intelligent document processing into the process linking its Data Verification and Authentication System (DIVAS) with the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV).

Atiku insisted that the commission must disclose the criteria for flagging discrepancies, the identities of developers and third-party vendors, and the procedures for reviewing results rejected or delayed by the system.

“INEC cannot ask Nigerians to trust a system whose rules they are forbidden to see. If an algorithm can flag a polling unit result sheet, the public deserves to know what triggers that flag, who set the threshold, who can change it and what happens to the result afterward,” he said.

He warned that legitimate polling-unit results could be wrongly flagged because of poor image quality, unfamiliar handwriting or damaged result sheets, raising concerns about the possibility of arbitrary delays.

“The danger is plain. A valid result sheet photographed in poor light, bearing unfamiliar handwriting or produced on worn paper must not be held back because a machine fails to recognise it.

“Nor can INEC leave room for a system that treats errors in one area as harmless while treating similar errors elsewhere as grounds to delay results. Such decisions would affect real votes, cast by real people, whose rights cannot be made dependent on secret software settings,” he stated.

The ADC candidate demanded that independent cybersecurity experts, political party technology representatives and civil society technologists be granted access to the system for a comprehensive audit before the nationwide mock accreditation scheduled for November 28, 2026.

He also called for a dedicated monitoring dashboard through which political parties could track flagged results, transmission delays and blocked uploads in real time during elections.

According to him, INEC must publish procedures identifying who reviews flagged results, how decisions are documented, how political parties are notified and how errors can be challenged promptly.

Atiku further insisted that the commission clarify the legal status of physical polling-unit result sheets, particularly where an AI assessment conflicts with Form EC8A completed and signed at the polling unit.

“The polling unit result sheet, Form EC8A, records what happened where the people voted. INEC must publicly reaffirm the legal status of the physical form completed and signed at the polling unit, and explain how it will resolve any conflict between that document and an AI assessment.

“A machine’s verdict cannot be allowed to quietly displace the evidence witnessed by voters and party agents,” he said.

The former Vice President maintained that the credibility of the elections would depend partly on whether political parties and independent experts could scrutinise the technology before its deployment.

“INEC has an opportunity to answer these questions before mistrust hardens into a crisis. Open the system. Let independent experts test it. Publish the rules for correcting its mistakes. Guarantee that no valid vote will disappear behind a screen marked ‘flagged’,” he declared.

Atiku warned that Nigerians would not accept an electoral process in which results counted openly at polling units could subsequently be subjected to digital decisions whose rules remained hidden from voters and political parties.

“Nigerians will not accept an election in which they can watch the counting at their polling unit but cannot see what happens when their result enters INEC’s digital system,” he said.

title: Mob kills Osun accident survivor, police hunt suspects
description:
The Osun State Police Command has warned residents against engaging in jungle justice, urging them to instead allow the appropriate authorities to investigate and handle reported offences in accordance with the law.
The command made the warning known in a statement signed by its spokesperson, Abiodu
content:
The Osun State Police Command has warned residents against engaging in jungle justice, urging them to instead allow the appropriate authorities to investigate and handle reported offences in accordance with the law.

The command made the warning known in a statement signed by its spokesperson, Abiodun Ojelabi, on Thursday.

Ojelabi said the warning was in reaction to the killing of a man who was said to be travelling in a vehicle that was allegedly involved in an accident that killed two pedestrians in Ilesa, Osun State.

The PPRO said the deceased and others were in the vehicle that allegedly hit and killed two pedestrians identified as Silas Seun and Matthew Dada.

Ojelabi further said, “Osun State Police Command wishes to inform the public that on 18th November 2026, the Command received information about a fatal road traffic accident involving an unregistered Toyota Camry, a TVS motorcycle and two pedestrians, identified as Silas Seun (female) and Matthew Dada (male).

“The unfortunate incident resulted in the immediate death of the two pedestrians at the scene of the accident. The driver of the vehicle, one Favour Fabunmi, ‘M’, 23 years old, and the other occupants of the Toyota Camry were successfully rescued alive.

“However, in a disturbing turn of events, one of the rescued occupants was attacked and severely beaten by an angry mob.

“He was subsequently rushed to the hospital but was later confirmed dead. The vehicle was also set ablaze by the mob and completely burnt to ashes.”

Reacting further to the development, Ojelabi said the matter had been transferred to the command headquarters for a comprehensive investigation, adding that necessary legal procedures had also been initiated.

He also said the state Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Zungura, “strongly condemns the act of mob violence and warns members of the public against taking the law into their hands.

“Members of the public are therefore urged to resist the temptation to administer instant justice, irrespective of the circumstances, and allow the appropriate authorities to investigate and handle reported offences in accordance with the law.”

He said the CP assured the public that the command would leave no stone unturned “in identifying all individuals who participated in the mob action, and anyone found culpable would be arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law.”

He urged members of the public to remain calm, law-abiding and security-conscious, encouraging citizens to promptly report accidents and criminal incidents to the nearest police station rather than resorting to violence.

PUNCH Metro earlier reported that the command said it had commenced an investigation into the killing of Monica Mary, a student of Westland University, Iwo, who was allegedly stabbed to death by some unknown assailants.

title: ADC crisis deepens as BoT orders Atiku, others to halt campaigns
description:
• Demands removal of Mark, Aregbesola, delisting of candidates
From Charity Nwakaudu, Abuja
The leadership crisis rocking the African Democratic Congress (ADC) has taken a fresh turn, with the Board of Trustees (BoT) aligned with Nafiu Bala Gombe demanding that former Vice President Atiku Abubakar a
content:
• Demands removal of Mark, Aregbesola, delisting of candidates

From Charity Nwakaudu, Abuja

The leadership crisis rocking the African Democratic Congress (ADC) has taken a fresh turn, with the Board of Trustees (BoT) aligned with Nafiu Bala Gombe demanding that former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and other members of the David Mark-led faction immediately suspend all political campaigns, rallies and public engagements in the party’s name.

The board also asked the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to remove former Senate President David Mark and former Osun State Governor Rauf Aregbesola from its records as national leaders of the party and delist all candidates submitted by the disputed leadership for the 2027 general elections.

The demands, which could further deepen the opposition party’s internal crisis ahead of the January 16 presidential election, followed the November 5 judgment of the Federal High Court in Abuja invalidating the emergence of the Mark-led leadership and decisions taken under it.

In a statement issued yesterday, the board’s chairman, Rufus Ikanmi, insisted that the judgment delivered by Justice Peter Lifu in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025 remained valid and binding, having neither been stayed nor overturned by a superior court.

“The judgment of the Honourable Court is valid, binding and subsisting. It has not been stayed, varied or set aside by any superior court. INEC, as a statutory body bound by the rule of law, has a constitutional duty to give full effect to it without further delay,” Ikanmi said.

The board demanded that INEC recognise and deal exclusively with the leadership associated with Bala Gombe, maintaining that the continued recognition of Mark and Aregbesola amounted to disregard for the court’s decision.

It also called for the delisting of all candidates uploaded to the commission’s portal by the Mark-led leadership, alleging that their nominations violated the 1999 Constitution, as amended, the Electoral Act and the party’s constitution.

The board specifically called on Atiku and others associated with the disputed leadership to stop all campaigns and public engagements conducted in the ADC’s name until the judgment was complied with.

Ikanmi warned that continued disregard for the court’s decision would amount to contempt and an affront to constitutional democracy and the rule of law.

He appealed to party members and supporters to remain calm and law-abiding, assuring them that the board would pursue lawful measures to secure compliance with the judgment.

The latest development comes amid continuing legal efforts by the Mark-led ADC to overturn the November 5 judgment, which invalidated the leadership arrangement that produced the party’s national executive and the process through which Atiku emerged as its presidential candidate.

The ADC Presidential Campaign Council had earlier announced that it filed an appeal and an application for a stay of execution, urging INEC to refrain from taking steps that could prejudice the pending appellate proceedings.

Its Director of Strategic Communications, Phrank Shaibu, maintained that the party would challenge the judgment through the courts and continue its political activities.

The rival positions have left the party facing uncertainty over its national leadership and the status of its candidates as preparations intensify for the 2027 general elections.

 The incident occurred at about 5pm on
content:
An anti-All Progressives Congress slogan, “Bamayi”, reportedly triggered a violent confrontation between youths and APC supporters in Kwarge, Balanga Local Government Area of Gombe State, leaving five campaign buses damaged and several party supporters injured.

 The incident occurred at about 5pm on Wednesday when the APC campaign convoy was travelling from Cham to Bambam as part of its campaign tour of Balanga South ahead of the 2027 general elections.

 Arewa PUNCH gathered that trouble started when some youths reportedly emerged from their homes and began chanting “Bamayi” as the campaign convoy approached the community.

 “Bamayi” is a local expression meaning rejection, disagreement or lack of support.

 An eyewitness, who spoke on condition of anonymity for security reasons, said the situation became tense when the youths began chanting the slogan at the passing convoy.

 “The youths came out in large numbers and started chanting ‘Bamayi, Bamayi’ as the convoy was passing. The situation quickly became tense, and before long, there was a confrontation between them and some youths accompanying the campaign team,” the eyewitness said.

 Another source familiar with the incident said the confrontation escalated into an attack on the convoy, with some of the alleged attackers wielding clubs and cutlasses.

 The source added that five Gombe Line buses conveying APC supporters were damaged during the violence, while several party supporters sustained injuries.

 However, no death was recorded in the incident.

 The circumstances surrounding the confrontation and the identities of those responsible for the attack remained unclear as of the time of filing this report.

 Wednesday’s incident occurred on the second day of the APC campaign tour of Balanga, following the official flag-off of the party’s campaign at Bajoga, headquarters of Funakaye Local Government Area, on Saturday.

 Meanwhile, Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya has led APC candidates and other party leaders on visits to the palaces of the Polo of Daadiya, Abdulkadir-Abubakar Galadima, and the Ndu of Cham, James Chachi, to seek their support ahead of the 2027 elections.

 The campaign team also visited Jessu-Nyuwar, Kindiyo, Mwona and Bambam for the commissioning of Local Council Development Areas.

 Yahaya expressed confidence in the party’s electoral prospects, saying the state would record greater development with the calibre of candidates fielded by the APC.

 “Together, we will achieve more success for our dear state,” the governor said.

 The APC Deputy Chairman, Baba Abuja, also urged residents of Nyuwar to support the party at the polls, saying, “From top to bottom, you should vote APC.”

 Similarly, the APC candidate for Balanga South State Constituency, Melton Yahaya, commended the electorate and expressed confidence in the party’s victory.

The post ‘Bamayi’ chant sparks violence as suspected thugs attack APC convoy in Gombe appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Fake news, political interference threaten election coverage –Experts
description:
From Taiwo Ogunniyi, Ilorin
With the 2027 general elections approaching, media professionals have raised the alarm over the threat of fabricated press releases, manipulated videos, political interference and financial inducements to credible election coverage, warning that the growing spread of misi
content:
From Taiwo Ogunniyi, Ilorin

With the 2027 general elections approaching, media professionals have raised the alarm over the threat of fabricated press releases, manipulated videos, political interference and financial inducements to credible election coverage, warning that the growing spread of misinformation could mislead voters, undermine public confidence in the electoral process and erode the credibility of Nigerian journalism.

The warning came at the maiden Journalism and Media Conference in Ilorin, Kwara State, where Founder of The Journalism Academy, Mosunmola Ajibade; Chief Correspondent of The PUNCH, Dare Akogun; broadcast journalist and media entrepreneur, Joseph Chidiebere Emeribe and media professional, Rasheedat Oladotun-Iliyas, challenged journalists and media organisations to strengthen fact-checking, resist political and commercial pressures and refuse to sacrifice accuracy for the race to break news.

Speaking at the conference, themed, “The Future of Journalism: Truth vs Trends”, Oladotun-Iliyas specifically warned that the approaching elections could expose newsrooms to fabricated political statements, digitally manipulated videos and other misleading materials designed to influence public opinion, while Ajibade raised concerns over brown envelopes, intimidation and financial inducements capable of compromising editorial independence.

The speakers maintained that the combination of political manipulation, artificial intelligence-generated misinformation and the growing obsession with social media trends posed serious challenges to responsible journalism, stressing that only rigorous verification, investigative reporting and adherence to professional ethics could protect public trust during the elections.

In her opening address, Ajibade expressed concern over threats to journalists, political intimidation, unlawful detention, financial inducements and other pressures capable of undermining media independence.

She maintained that journalists must remain courageous, objective and committed to the truth despite the challenges confronting the profession, warning that allowing political or financial considerations to dictate editorial decisions would weaken the media’s capacity to hold public officials accountable.

“Journalism must remain relevant, courageous, independent, and committed to truth. It must never be silenced or compromised for personal, political, or financial interests,” she declared.

Ajibade also questioned whether journalism education in Nigerian institutions adequately prepared students for the realities of modern media practice, stressing the need to bridge the gap between classroom knowledge and professional experience.

She explained that The Journalism Academy, established on March 2, 2026, was designed to promote practical, inclusive and relevant media education through training, mentorship, career guidance and professional development.

According to her, the academy had extended its sensitisation activities to secondary schools, including Bishop Smith Memorial College and Saint Anthony, to expose students, particularly those in the arts, to career opportunities in journalism and the broader media industry.

Delivering the keynote address, Emeribe warned that increasing competition for online attention was encouraging sensationalism, clickbait headlines and the publication of unverified information at the expense of professional standards.

He argued that journalists did not have to choose between truth and trends, insisting that trending issues should only serve as channels for reaching audiences rather than determining editorial decisions.

“My central argument today is simple: the future of journalism does not require us to choose between truth and trends. It requires us to understand how to use trends without compromising the truth,” he said.

“Use trends as a vehicle, never as a compass. Trends can take you to your audience, but they must never determine your professional direction,” he added.

Emeribe identified the pressure to publish breaking stories, commercial interests, emotional reactions and the quest for online recognition as factors contributing to misinformation.

He noted that false information often travelled faster than corrections, observing that “falsehood sprints while correction walks.”

Citing the fatal accident near the main gate of the University of Ilorin on July 18, 2024, Emeribe recalled how conflicting reports about the number of casualties demonstrated the dangers of publishing unverified information, particularly during emergencies.

He also urged journalists to pay greater attention to community issues, including the Akerebiata Bridge collapse, flooding and persistent electricity challenges around Ilorin Technical College, Adunbarin, Irewolede and Afenifere.

According to him, stories affecting ordinary Nigerians should not be neglected simply because they do not attract national attention or generate online engagement.

“A collapsed bridge, a flooded community or a neighbourhood living without electricity may not always become a national trend. Yet, for the people affected, these are urgent realities that demand attention and accountability,” he said.

On technology, Emeribe encouraged journalists to embrace artificial intelligence for transcription, translation, data analysis and other newsroom activities but warned that human judgment and independent verification must remain central to journalism.

“AI can assist the journalist, but it cannot assume the journalist’s responsibility,” he stated.

He also identified financial dependence on politicians, government institutions and influential individuals as a threat to editorial independence, urging media organisations to explore sustainable revenue sources through subscriptions, digital publications, podcasts, newsletters, grants and partnerships.

“Dependence is the quiet enemy of independence,” he warned.

Similarly, Akogun called on journalists to strengthen investigative reporting as an instrument for exposing wrongdoing, promoting transparency and holding public officials accountable.

He said journalism must go beyond reporting official statements and breaking news to investigate public expenditure, monitor government projects and establish whether promises made by public officials translated into tangible benefits for citizens.

Using the abandoned Ilesha Baruba-Gwanara road project in Kwara State as an example, Akogun explained that sustained media scrutiny and follow-up reporting were essential to ensuring that public projects were completed.

He noted that the road remained abandoned for about eight years before its eventual completion by the present state administration.

“A road that exists only in a budget document is not development,” he said, urging journalists to investigate the relationship between budgetary allocations, contract awards and actual project delivery.

Drawing from his experience in environmental and investigative reporting, including concerns surrounding mining activities in Bani, Kwara State, Akogun urged journalists to investigate the environmental and social consequences of resource extraction.

He encouraged practitioners to make greater use of the Freedom of Information Act 2011, procurement documents, audit reports, financial records and other public information to uncover irregularities.

While acknowledging the usefulness of artificial intelligence, satellite imagery, geolocation and open-source intelligence in investigative journalism, he cautioned that such tools must complement rather than replace independent verification.

Akogun also called on media organisations to establish adequately funded investigative desks, improve journalists’ professional development and strengthen newsroom safety measures.

“Investigative journalism is not a licence to publish unverified allegations. It is a responsibility to establish facts in the public interest,” he said.

In her presentation, Oladotun-Iliyas stressed that accuracy and fact-checking must take precedence over the pressure to break news and generate online engagement.

Speaking on the topic, “Strengthening Trust in Contemporary Journalism: The Place of Fact-Checking, Public Interest Reporting, Solutions Journalism, Health Reporting and Gender”, she warned that competition between traditional media, bloggers, influencers and social media commentators was increasingly pushing some journalists towards speed at the expense of accuracy.

“Speed has become a competitor to accuracy. It now matters who tells the news first. And sometimes, in our desperation to be the first, we forget that our greatest responsibility is to be right,” she said.

She recalled her early professional experiences at ThisDay Newspapers in Lagos, where reports passed through several editorial stages involving reporters, proofreaders, sub-editors and news editors before publication.

She also recalled her experience at the Broadcasting House in Ikoyi, Lagos, where an experienced newsroom professional ensured that every word used in a report was properly justified.

Oladotun-Iliyas lamented that the growing reliance on social media statements and information from verified accounts had weakened independent verification in some newsrooms.

“A statement carrying the name and logo of a reputable organisation does not automatically become genuine. A video shared by thousands of people does not automatically become authentic,” she cautioned.

Citing previous controversies involving Nigerian media organisations, including the 2015 Nigerian Tribune report falsely attributed to Itse Sagay, the 2020 ThisDay report concerning Bishop David Oyedepo’s alleged visa denial and the April 2026 Daily Trust photograph controversy involving the Jilli Market airstrike, she warned that poor verification could damage media credibility and expose journalists to legal consequences.

Ahead of the 2027 general elections, Oladotun-Iliyas warned journalists to prepare for fabricated press releases, manipulated videos and misleading information designed to influence public opinion.

She called for continuous training in fact-checking, data journalism, digital security, investigative reporting and responsible artificial intelligence use, while urging professional bodies to strengthen ethical standards across the media industry.

She maintained that public trust remained journalism’s most valuable asset, citing Nobel Peace Prize laureate Maria Ressa’s observation that “without facts you cannot have truth, without truth you cannot have trust.”

Oladotun-Iliyas also urged journalists to focus more on public-interest issues, particularly healthcare, education, security, livelihoods, environmental protection and governance.

On health reporting, she called for increased investigative coverage of access to medical facilities, availability of medicines, staffing levels and the effectiveness of government health interventions.

She urged journalists to highlight the experiences of women travelling long distances to access maternal healthcare, children unable to obtain basic medical services and communities where primary healthcare centres existed only on paper.

She also advocated balanced gender reporting and solutions journalism, arguing that the media should not only expose societal problems but also highlight practical interventions that could improve people’s lives.

“Stories of solutions give communities ideas, encourage constructive public conversations and show policymakers what may be worth improving or replicating,” she said.

The speakers collectively stressed that the future of journalism would depend on the ability of practitioners to balance technological advancement with professional responsibility, protect editorial independence and remain accountable to the public.

They emphasised that journalists must resist political and commercial pressures, verify information before publication, correct mistakes transparently and continually develop their professional skills.

Emeribe, in particular, outlined seven commitments for emerging journalists, including verification before publication, responsible use of technology, protection of editorial independence, service to local communities and continuous professional development.

He maintained that the profession’s relevance would be determined by its commitment to truth rather than its ability to follow every online trend.

“The future of journalism does not belong to those who merely chase the trend. It belongs to those who understand the trend, master the tools, win the attention of the audience and, above all, never surrender the truth,” he said.

The conference, organised by The Journalism Academy at 12 Workspaces, Ilorin, brought together journalists, media practitioners, students and other stakeholders to examine the challenges and opportunities shaping contemporary journalism.

Participants called for stronger collaboration among media organisations, journalism educators and professional associations to build a credible, independent and sustainable media industry capable of strengthening democracy and holding public institutions accountable.

The post Fake news, political interference threaten election coverage –Experts appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Lagos arraigns suspects over monarch’s son, another’s murder
description:
The Lagos State Government on Thursday commenced the trial of four men accused of murdering Prince Akinloye Ademola and Sheriff Salami, with a police witness narrating how investigators arrested three of the suspects.
PUNCH Metro reports that Akinloye was the son of the Ajiran of Agungi, Oba Tijani
content:
The Lagos State Government on Thursday commenced the trial of four men accused of murdering Prince Akinloye Ademola and Sheriff Salami, with a police witness narrating how investigators arrested three of the suspects.

PUNCH Metro reports that Akinloye was the son of the Ajiran of Agungi, Oba Tijani Akinloye.

The trial commenced before Justice Tajudeen Muyideen of the Lagos State High Court, sitting in Igbosere, with the prosecution calling its first witness, Assistant Superintendent of Police Nosiru Isiaka, attached to Special Squad 1 of the Lagos State Police Command.

The defendants are Sefiu Fatai, aka Fabo; Yusuf Ismail, aka Bariga; Tajudeen Ahmed, aka Ahmed Ajiran; and Bode Ajose.

Led in evidence by the Lagos State Solicitor-General, Adebayo Haroun, ASP Isiaka testified about the investigation into the alleged killings and the circumstances surrounding the arrest of the defendants.

In his evidence-in-chief, the police witness narrated how his team initially arrested Fatai and Ismail before subsequent investigations led to the arrest of another suspect.

He also told the court how a technical team from the office of the Inspector-General of Police was involved in the arrest of one of the suspects in the Ajiran area of Ajah.

Isiaka further explained how information gathered during the investigation helped the police establish alleged links between the defendants and the killings.

However, as he was about to narrate how the investigation led to the arrest of another suspect, the witness’s testimony was interrupted by objections from the defence counsel, led by Olalekan Ojo, SAN.

Ojo challenged the manner in which the prosecution was leading the witness, arguing that the investigating police officer could not give evidence suggesting that he personally witnessed the circumstances surrounding the alleged killings when he was not at the scene.

The senior advocate maintained that the witness should restrict his testimony to facts within his personal knowledge and clearly distinguish between what he personally did or observed during the investigation and information obtained from other persons.

He argued that an investigating police officer’s account of information gathered during an investigation should not be presented as though the officer had direct knowledge of the events surrounding the alleged crime.

The other defence counsel also raised objections to aspects of the witness’s testimony, interrupting the prosecution’s examination.

The defence’s objections centred on the admissibility of the evidence and the distinction between the investigating officer’s personal knowledge and information obtained from other persons during police inquiries.

The prosecution was led by the Lagos State Solicitor-General, Haroun, while O. Ajanaku and R.O. Owolabi appeared for the defence. Ojo, SAN, and Gbenga Ojo also represented the third defendant, while M. Familola appeared for the fourth defendant.

Human rights lawyer Femi Falana, SAN, appeared alongside Abimbola Williams-Akinjide, SAN, as counsel holding a watching brief for the nominal complainant.

Following the proceedings, Justice Muyideen adjourned the case until November 25, 2026, for the continuation of the trial.

The post Lagos arraigns suspects over monarch’s son, another’s murder appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Saraki accuses Kwara gov of  summoning monarchs to scuttle visit
description: The Media Office of former Senate President Bukola Saraki has accused Kwara State Governor Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq of deliberately summoning traditional rulers from Kwara North Senatorial District to Ilorin, the state capital, to prevent them from being in their palaces during Saraki’s political visi
content:
The Media Office of former Senate President Bukola Saraki has accused Kwara State Governor Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq of deliberately summoning traditional rulers from Kwara North Senatorial District to Ilorin, the state capital, to prevent them from being in their palaces during Saraki’s political visit to the area.

The office described the alleged action as a desperate attempt by the governor to frustrate the former Senate president’s political engagements in Baruten Local Government Area, claiming that the growing acceptance of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) across the state had unsettled the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

In a statement, the media office alleged that traditional rulers from the district were compelled to undertake journeys lasting up to nine hours on deplorable roads to Ilorin, where they had remained without any clearly defined official assignment.

It claimed that the timing of the invitation, coming on the eve of Saraki’s visit, suggested a deliberate attempt to keep the monarchs away from their domains while the former Senate president engaged residents and political stakeholders.

“The royal fathers who have been compelled to embark on the tedious journey of about nine hours on bad roads from their respective towns to Ilorin have been in the state capital since yesterday without any specific assignment or any reason except that the state governor does not want them to be in their palaces during Saraki’s visits to Baruten Local Government Area for political engagement with the people,” the statement alleged.

The office accused Abdulrazaq of resorting to intimidation rather than addressing what it described as growing dissatisfaction with his administration, insisting that the alleged treatment of the traditional rulers demonstrated the government’s increasing political desperation.

“We consider this action another desperate and unproductive move by the governor, who is obviously confused about the best ways to respond to the widespread acceptance that the Peoples Democratic Party and its candidates are enjoying across the state.

“For a democratically elected governor to adopt this authoritarian method of coercing royal fathers and depriving them of the opportunity to listen to all sides of the political divide, it only demonstrates how unpopular the Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq administration has become,” it stated.

The media office further criticised the condition of roads linking communities in Kwara North to the state capital, accusing the governor of neglecting critical infrastructure while allegedly subjecting traditional rulers to unnecessary hardship.

According to the statement, compelling monarchs to travel long distances on bad roads instead of addressing the developmental challenges confronting their communities amounted to an advertisement of the administration’s failures.

It also questioned the competence of the governor’s political advisers and intelligence team, arguing that they had misread the purpose of Saraki’s ongoing consultations across the state.

The office maintained that the former Senate president was engaging directly with voters and stakeholders rather than seeking political endorsements from traditional rulers.

“If those teams are truly working and giving the governor good information and advice, he should have known that Saraki’s ongoing political engagement across the state is not with traditional rulers. He is engaging directly with the people and taking his messages to the voters. He is meeting with stakeholders and having useful exchanges of ideas,” the statement added.

It stressed that Saraki and the PDP recognised the nonpartisan position of traditional institutions and had no intention of turning royal palaces into political campaign grounds.

“Saraki and the PDP, out of respect to the royal fathers, do not turn palaces into campaign grounds. The PDP does not seek to turn our respected royal fathers into politicians,” it said, adding that traditional rulers remained fathers to all residents, irrespective of political affiliation.

The media office warned that the PDP had yet to commence its full electioneering campaign, predicting that the party’s popularity would become more evident when its campaigns formally began.

It accused the ruling APC of lacking clear programmes, a manifesto and fresh ideas, alleging that the administration had resorted to replicating initiatives associated with the opposition.

The office appealed to traditional rulers across the state to remain steadfast and resist being drawn into partisan political contests, describing the alleged inconvenience imposed on them as a reflection of the governor’s frustration over the changing political situation.

“These oppressive measures of the Kwara State governor can only bring temporary discomfort. They are the last acts of a drowning governor and his confused party in Kwara State. Their days are numbered,” the statement declared.

The post Saraki accuses Kwara gov of summoning monarchs to scuttle visit appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: APC plotting to rig polls in  Niger’s banditry-hit LGAs –SDP
description:
From John Adams, Minna
The Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Niger State has accused Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago and the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of plotting to exploit the worsening insecurity in seven local government areas to manipulate the 2027 general elections.
The party alleged
content:
From John Adams, Minna

The Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Niger State has accused Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago and the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of plotting to exploit the worsening insecurity in seven local government areas to manipulate the 2027 general elections.

The party alleged that the state government’s failure to contain banditry and other violent crimes in the affected communities was deliberate, claiming that the APC intended to take advantage of the possible disruption of voting to manufacture election results in its favour.

It identified Agwara, Mashegu, Shiroro, Rafi, Munya, Mariga and parts of Paikoro as areas allegedly being targeted for the planned electoral manipulation.

The SDP also accused the governor of diverting local government funds to finance his re-election campaign, alleging that billions of naira had been squandered on political mobilisation and patronage while development projects remained abandoned and insecurity continued to claim lives.

Spokesperson and Director of Contacts and Mobilisation for the SDP governorship candidate, Mohammed Ndarani Mohammed, Jonathan Vatsa, raised the allegations in a statement issued in Minna.

Vatsa, a former Commissioner for Information, Culture and Tourism in the state, claimed that the administration had deliberately failed to provide adequate support to security agencies despite the persistent killings and abductions in several communities.

“The government’s attitude towards addressing the security challenges in the state is deliberate. They are planning to write results from those areas because elections may not take place there.

“That is why the government has refused to address the situation despite the killings and abductions going on in the state.

“We have it on good authority that local government areas like Agwara, Mashegu, Shiroro, Rafi, Munya, Mariga and parts of Paikoro, where there are serious security challenges, are the places they want to use to rig elections,” he alleged.

Vatsa maintained that the opposition parties were aware of the alleged plot and would resist any attempt to manipulate the electoral process.

“Despite the enormous resources at its disposal, the government has refused to empower the security agencies in the state just because they want to use the situation to rig elections.

“Unfortunately for them, the opposition parties are very much aware of these plans, and we are prepared for them. We will resist any attempt to rig the forthcoming elections in the state,” he declared.

The SDP spokesperson expressed concern that the administration appeared more interested in securing political advantage than protecting communities devastated by banditry, accusing the government of attempting to turn the suffering of residents into an electoral opportunity.

“It is sad that the government wants to use the people’s nightmare to its electoral advantage.

“I, therefore, urge the people to be vigilant. If the government cannot help you to address the security challenges, you should not allow them to use your situation to their advantage,” he said.

Turning to the management of public resources, Vatsa alleged that the state government spent N10 billion on the flag-off of the governor’s re-election campaign last week, while ongoing projects across the state were starved of funds.

He further claimed that more than N10 billion had been expended on welfare packages and financial inducements to political groups visiting Government House, Minna, to declare support for the governor.

According to him, the administration’s spending priorities have left critical development projects abandoned, even as local government councils struggle to discharge their responsibilities.

Vatsa specifically accused Bago of withholding funds meant for local government councils and allegedly channelling the resources into political activities, leaving council chairmen without sufficient money to meet their operational obligations.

He argued that the alleged financial strangulation of the councils had contributed to the worsening security situation, as some local governments could no longer afford to fuel vehicles used by security personnel for routine patrols.

“These local governments cannot even afford to fuel security vehicles in the various councils for routine patrols,” he claimed.

“Any leader who has no respect for public funds, the implication is that the people suffer. That is exactly what is happening in the state under the APC administration.

“This is one administration that spends public funds with recklessness, yet the people expect development. It doesn’t work,” he added.

The former commissioner also criticised what he described as the governor’s extravagant political spending, citing the reported presentation of seven expensive vehicles and N700 million to Hausa musician Dauda Rarara as another example of alleged misuse of public resources.

He challenged residents to reject what he called the ruling party’s attempt to use public funds to secure electoral victory, urging them to adopt the approach of voters in the Osun State governorship election.

“The government has gathered the fuel subsidy money to buy the elections.

“You should collect their money and vote the government out. Any attempt to allow this current administration to return to office will spell doom for the state,” Vatsa warned.

The post APC plotting to rig polls in Niger’s banditry-hit LGAs –SDP appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.
