title: UNIZIK VC urges 19,522 graduands to uphold discipline, excellence
description:
By Nwabueze Okonkwo



ONITSHA – The Vice-Chancellor of Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Awka, Prof. Ugochukwu Bond Stanley Anyaehie, has urged the 2025 and 2026 graduating students of the institution to uphold its core values of discipline, excellence and self-reliance as they begin the next phase of the
content:
By Nwabueze Okonkwo

ONITSHA – The Vice-Chancellor of Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Awka, Prof. Ugochukwu Bond Stanley Anyaehie, has urged the 2025 and 2026 graduating students of the institution to uphold its core values of discipline, excellence and self-reliance as they begin the next phase of their lives.

Anyaehie gave the charge on Thursday in Awka while delivering his address at the university’s 20th and 21st combined convocation ceremonies.

He urged the graduands to become worthy ambassadors of the institution, named after Nigeria’s first President, Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe, popularly known as Zik of Africa.

Expounding on the university’s motto, the Vice-Chancellor said discipline required the graduands to make integrity, self-control and ethical conduct their guiding principles in an increasingly complex world.

On self-reliance, he advised them not to wait for opportunities to come their way but to embrace innovation, create value, build enterprises and develop solutions to real-life challenges.

He also urged them to pursue excellence and reject mediocrity, stressing that every task they undertook should reflect world-class standards.

Reflecting on his tenure as the institution’s seventh Vice-Chancellor, Anyaehie reaffirmed his commitment to scholarship, clinical integrity, effective higher education governance, staff development and institutional transformation.

He said his administration’s philosophy, “A Greater UNIZIK is Possible,” was not merely a slogan but a commitment to repositioning the university as a globally competitive centre of academic excellence, technological innovation and societal impact.

Presenting the convocation statistics, the Vice-Chancellor disclosed that a total of 19,522 graduands would receive various qualifications, comprising 16,260 first-degree recipients and 3,262 postgraduate graduands.

Of the first-degree recipients, 213 graduated with First Class Honours, 4,623 obtained Second Class Honours (Upper Division), 8,751 earned Second Class Honours (Lower Division), while 2,116 graduated with Third Class Honours and 71 obtained Pass degrees.

Another 486 students received unclassified degrees in Medical and Pharmaceutical Sciences.

The postgraduate category comprised 701 Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) recipients, 35 Master of Philosophy/Doctor of Philosophy (MPhil/PhD) recipients, 1,224 master’s degree recipients, 323 Postgraduate Diploma (PGD) recipients and 979 Postgraduate Diploma in Education (PGDE-NTI) recipients.

Highlighting his administration’s achievements, Anyaehie said institutional reforms had been implemented to strengthen academic standards, improve staff welfare, expand the university’s capacity and modernise its operations.

He also identified the full re-accreditation of the university’s Medical programme by the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN) as a major milestone in its academic and professional development.

In his remarks, the Chancellor of the university, His Royal Majesty, Da Jacob Gyang Buba, CON, Gbong Gwom Jos, acknowledged the presence of dignitaries and graduating students and extended greetings to President Bola Tinubu.

He paid tribute to the institution’s founding inspiration, Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe, describing his legacy as an enduring source of inspiration.

The Chancellor also appreciated the Federal Government, Federal Ministry of Education, National Universities Commission (NUC), benefactors and friends of the university for their financial, infrastructural and moral support.

Similarly, the Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the Governing Council, Barr. Monsur Olugbenga Kukoyi, congratulated the graduating students, describing the convocation as a celebration of perseverance, character and scholarship rather than merely a university tradition.

The post UNIZIK VC urges 19,522 graduands to uphold discipline, excellence appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Calabar power plant undergoes turbine overhaul amid blackouts
description:
As Nigerians battle prolonged power outages, the Calabar Generation Company, a subsidiary of the Niger Delta Power Holding Company Limited, has commenced a major maintenance exercise on its Turbine Unit 2 to improve operational efficiency, strengthen reliability and boost electricity generation.
Acc
content:
As Nigerians battle prolonged power outages, the Calabar Generation Company, a subsidiary of the Niger Delta Power Holding Company Limited, has commenced a major maintenance exercise on its Turbine Unit 2 to improve operational efficiency, strengthen reliability and boost electricity generation.

According to a statement by NDPHC, the exercise, being carried out in collaboration with the original equipment manufacturer, GE Vernova, “involves a comprehensive inspection of critical turbine components to assess their condition, identify potential deterioration and carry out necessary maintenance in line with OEM recommendations and international best practices.”

The Chief Operating Officer of the Calabar Power Plant, Bex Ayoade, said the exercise underscored the commitment of the management of NDPHC towards maintaining its power generation assets and maximising its contribution to national electricity generation.

Ayoade said the exercise would improve the turbine’s efficiency, reliability and operational lifespan, while providing opportunities for knowledge transfer and technical capacity development among NDPHC personnel.

He assured that stringent Health, Safety and Environment standards would be maintained throughout the exercise.

The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NDPHC, Jennifer Adighije, said the maintenance programme aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s drive to improve electricity supply and expand Nigeria’s productive capacity.

She said, “Maintaining the Calabar plant in optimal operating condition will strengthen NDPHC’s ability to deliver more electricity to the national grid, with direct benefits for Nigerian households, businesses and industries.”

Adighije noted that improved generation capacity would support economic activities, enhance productivity and contribute to better living standards for Nigerians.

She reaffirmed the company’s commitment to sustaining its power generation assets and ensuring that available capacity translated into reliable electricity supply.

The NDPHC chief executive stressed that “dependable power supply remains critical to reducing the burden on businesses, stimulating investment, creating jobs and supporting President Tinubu’s ambition of building a $1tn Nigerian economy.”

The post Calabar power plant undergoes turbine overhaul amid blackouts appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Coalition threatens sanctions over CSOs’ role in fraud trial
description: The Coalition of Civil Society Organisations on Human Rights, Democracy and Good Governance in Nigeria has threatened to investigate and sanction civil society groups accused of using advocacy platforms to interfere with judicial proceedings or disguise paid legal defence as independent civic engage
content:
The Coalition of Civil Society Organisations on Human Rights, Democracy and Good Governance in Nigeria has threatened to investigate and sanction civil society groups accused of using advocacy platforms to interfere with judicial proceedings or disguise paid legal defence as independent civic engagement.

The coalition said it would query any civil society organisation, community-based organisation, faith-based organisation or non-governmental organisation found promoting illegalities, obstructing justice or conducting media trials, warning that such activities could erode public confidence in the judiciary and compromise the credibility of the civil society sector.

Its Secretary, Peter Nwokolo, stated this at a press briefing in Abuja on Thursday, where the coalition addressed the involvement of civil society groups in the ongoing alleged $1.5m fraud case involving the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Ufoma Joseph Immanuel and Intermediate Investment Holdings Limited before the Special Offences Court, Ikeja, Lagos.

The coalition’s intervention comes amid public commentary surrounding the case, with Nwokolo alleging that some protests and public statements issued in the name of civil society were capable of exerting pressure on the court and undermining the right to a fair hearing.

He, however, did not identify the organisations allegedly involved in paid advocacy or provide evidence at the briefing to substantiate the allegation.

Nwokolo said, “The basic role of civil society organisations in the areas of justice, human rights, good governance and anti-corruption is to serve as an independent voice of the people by monitoring state power, promoting the rule of law and equal access to justice, and defending the fundamental rights and dignity of citizens.”

He added that organisations were expected to demand transparency and accountability in public governance, rather than become instruments for advancing the interests of individuals facing prosecution.

The coalition also warned against pronouncing individuals guilty before the courts had determined their cases, insisting that public advocacy must not displace established judicial procedures.

“An accusation is not a conviction. An investigation is not persecution. Every citizen invited by the courts or anti-corruption agencies must submit to due process, with full respect for the presumption of innocence and the right to a fair hearing,” Nwokolo said.

Giving its account of proceedings in the case, the coalition said it monitored the hearing on November 16, when the prosecution informed the court that it had written to the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital to authenticate a medical report submitted in support of the defendant’s bail application.

According to Nwokolo, the prosecution told the court that LASUTH’s response, dated July 22, 2026, indicated that the medical report did not originate from the hospital.

He said the court, on November 18, dismissed the fresh bail application, ordered an accelerated hearing, granted the defendant 30 days to engage new counsel and adjourned the case until January 25, 2027.

The coalition acknowledged that Immanuel had pleaded not guilty, stressing that it was not pronouncing on his guilt or innocence.

“The determination of guilt or innocence rests solely with the court,” Nwokolo said.

The coalition said it observed the proceedings alongside the Support for Civil Society Organisations Initiative, Centre for Leadership and Democratic Ethics, The People’s Care and Development Initiative, and Elorah Initiative Hub.

It also called on the National Leadership of Accredited Civil Society Organisations in Nigeria to examine the conduct of organisations allegedly using the civic space to obstruct judicial processes, engage in media trials or present paid legal representation as independent advocacy.

Nwokolo said the national leadership would query, investigate and, where necessary, sanction organisations found to have crossed those boundaries.

The coalition also drew attention to public statements issued in the name of the late Dr Tunji Braithwaite’s foundation concerning the case, asking the foundation to clarify whether the publications represented its official position.

It argued that where questions arose over the role of an organisation in a pending case, transparency was necessary, adding that legal arguments should be presented in court by properly briefed counsel and placed on the record.

The intervention raises questions about the boundaries between legitimate civil society advocacy, public criticism of law-enforcement agencies and attempts to influence judicial proceedings. While organisations have a responsibility not to obstruct justice or pronounce defendants guilty, scrutiny of prosecutions and defence of the rights of accused persons also form part of the civic space the coalition says it seeks to protect.

The coalition urged the judiciary to remain impartial, while calling on the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission and the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission to discharge their mandates professionally and avoid media trials.

It also asked the media not to promote narratives capable of undermining court proceedings and urged professional bodies to examine alleged conflicts arising from dual roles in line with the Rules of Professional Conduct.

“We will support no criminal, and we will oppose no innocent person. We stand with the law,” Nwokolo said.

The post Coalition threatens sanctions over CSOs’ role in fraud trial appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Kalu, NHIA DG seek investment in robotic healthcare
description:
The Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, and the Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority, Kelechi Ohiri, have called for sustained investment in Nigeria’s health sector to reduce medical tourism and improve access to specialised treatment.
 They made the
content:
The Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, and the Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority, Kelechi Ohiri, have called for sustained investment in Nigeria’s health sector to reduce medical tourism and improve access to specialised treatment.

 They made the call at the commissioning of a robotic surgery platform at Eleos Specialist Hospital, Abuja, the second of its kind in Northern Nigeria, according to a statement by the institution on Thursday.

 Kalu, represented by the Deputy Chairman of the House Committee on Health Institutions, Olumuyiwa Adedayo, said investment in modern medical technology was essential to strengthening the country’s healthcare infrastructure and enabling Nigerians to access advanced surgical procedures locally.

 He said, “The commissioning of this Robotic Surgery Platform demonstrates what private-sector investment, professional expertise and commitment to healthcare development can achieve. We must encourage more Nigerian investors to support modern medical facilities so that our people can access advanced surgical procedures without having to travel abroad.”

 Similarly, Ohiri, represented by his Senior Special Adviser, Chima Onoka, described the introduction of the technology as an important intervention in addressing medical tourism and retaining healthcare spending within the country.

 Onoka said, “Every year, billions of naira leave our shores as Nigerians travel abroad for complex urological and minimally invasive procedures. This capital flight deprives our local institutions of the resources needed to grow, while placing an unbearable financial burden on families who must pay for international travel, accommodation and foreign healthcare out of pocket.

 “By bringing this robotic platform to Abuja, Eleos Specialist Hospital is directly addressing this leak. We are shifting the narrative from capital flight to capital retention and positioning Nigeria as a hub for inbound medical tourism across West Africa.”

 He added that robotic-assisted surgery could offer benefits such as reduced blood loss, fewer postoperative complications in appropriate cases and shorter hospital stays, while urging policymakers to strengthen health insurance coverage to make advanced treatment accessible to more Nigerians.

 Earlier, the hospital’s Consultant Endourologist, Laparoscopic and Robotic Surgeon, Paul Ngwu, said the introduction of the platform was driven by the hospital’s commitment to bringing advanced surgical technology closer to Nigerian patients.

 He said the technology would strengthen the hospital’s capacity to perform complex urological and other selected procedures, adding that the facility would prioritise specialist training, patient safety and professional excellence.

 The Managing Director of the hospital, Victoria Ngwu, said the investment reflected the facility’s vision of providing Nigerians with advanced surgical services comparable to those available in leading medical centres globally.

 She added that the hospital would continue investing in skilled medical personnel, modern equipment and strategic partnerships to improve specialised healthcare delivery and reduce the need for Nigerians to seek treatment abroad.

 A former Nigerian Ambassador to Hungary, Eddy Onuoha, who disclosed that he had undergone robotic surgery at the hospital and recovered successfully, said the availability of the technology in Abuja could help change Nigerians’ preference for seeking treatment abroad.

 Robotic surgery is a form of minimally invasive surgery in which surgeons’ control specialised instruments through a computer-assisted system. The technology provides enhanced dexterity and visualisation, particularly during complex procedures.

 It is increasingly used in urology, including prostate, kidney and bladder surgeries. However, the technology does not operate independently or replace surgeons, who remain in control throughout the procedure.

title: Africa faults nations preaching fossil phase-out, pursuing oil deals
description:
The African Group of Negotiators on Climate Change has accused countries advocating a complete phase-out of fossil fuels of hypocrisy, alleging that some of them are simultaneously pursuing behind-the-scenes deals to secure petroleum supplies.
The group on Thursday said countries pushing for an end
content:
The African Group of Negotiators on Climate Change has accused countries advocating a complete phase-out of fossil fuels of hypocrisy, alleging that some of them are simultaneously pursuing behind-the-scenes deals to secure petroleum supplies.

The group on Thursday said countries pushing for an end to fossil fuel production and consumption must demonstrate consistency between their public climate commitments and private energy arrangements, warning that the conflicting positions were undermining trust in the global climate negotiations.

The African negotiators also insisted that the transition away from fossil fuels must reflect the continent’s economic realities, protect workers and farmers, and allow African countries to process and utilise their natural resources rather than impose additional development burdens on them.

The position comes as negotiations at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Türkiye, approach their conclusion, with disagreements over fossil fuels, climate finance and the pace of the global energy transition remaining major issues.

His remarks followed reports of a new trilateral declaration issued by China, the United States and Russia on Thursday after an unprecedented summit hosted by Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, attended by US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The declaration reportedly included commitments to pursue talks on nuclear risks, increase petroleum supplies and advance reforms of the United Nations.

The proposed cooperation on petroleum supplies was linked to efforts to strengthen global refined petroleum availability amid energy market pressures arising from the conflict involving Iran and disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz.

The reported agreement drew criticism at COP31 from the European Union’s Climate Chief, Wopke Hoekstra, who described the development as unfortunate and urged countries to invest in domestic clean energy to avoid repeating energy supply shocks.

But speaking during a press conference, the Chair of the African Group of Negotiators, Nana Dr Antwi-Boasiako Amoah, described the contradiction between countries’ climate rhetoric and their pursuit of petroleum supplies as hypocrisy in the global climate process.

Although he declined to comment specifically on the reported petroleum supply arrangement involving China, the United States and Russia, Amoah maintained that his criticism was directed at what he described as inconsistencies in countries’ overall approach to fossil fuel production and supply.

He said, “For China and U.S. issues, I don’t have information about it. But I’m just commenting on fossil service in total as parties. This is the hypocrisy in the whole process. And so at one point, you see some countries talking about taking fossil out completely, and the underground making deals to get fossils service in their pipelines. And that is the hypocrisy that we have in this whole process.

“So, if fossil service is something that we want to do away with as parties, let’s be honest to our commitments. Let’s stay with it head on, not to be going back doors to do certain things and later come back and make it look awkward in the face of the other people. That is hypocrisy.”

Amoah added that the continent’s participation in COP31 was guided by the need to protect multilateralism, secure the means to implement climate commitments and ensure that the transition was just and credible.

He said, “Our first point of call is the protection of multilateralism. Africa feels safe to be under multilateralism because this is the only place that we can function properly as a people. And therefore, any attempt, any plans to destroy this process is a red line for us as Africa.”

The post Africa faults nations preaching fossil phase-out, pursuing oil deals appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Ogun polytechnic students protest ASUP strike, seek Abiodun’s intervention
description:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta



ABEOKUTA — Students of state-owned polytechnics in Ogun State on Thursday protested at the Governor’s Office, Oke Mosan, Abeokuta, demanding Governor Dapo Abiodun’s urgent intervention to end the lingering industrial dispute between the state government and the Academ
content:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

ABEOKUTA — Students of state-owned polytechnics in Ogun State on Thursday protested at the Governor’s Office, Oke Mosan, Abeokuta, demanding Governor Dapo Abiodun’s urgent intervention to end the lingering industrial dispute between the state government and the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics (ASUP).

The protest, organised by hundreds of students under the aegis of the National Association of Polytechnic Students (NAPS), followed the expiration of two separate 48-hour ultimatums issued to the government without what the students described as concrete action towards resolving the dispute.

The strike, which has kept students out of classrooms for about 10 days, has disrupted academic activities across the six state-owned polytechnics.

Armed with placards bearing inscriptions such as “Gov. Dapo Abiodun, please end ASUP strike”, “Save Polytechnic Education Now”, “Our Lecturers Must Return to the Classroom” and “Attend to Our Lecturers’ Demands”, the protesters urged the governor to intervene personally and ensure an immediate resolution of the crisis.

Speaking during the demonstration, the Chairman of NAPS, Ogun State Liaison Council, Comrade Joshua Opatunmibi, said the students had exhausted available diplomatic channels and could no longer remain silent while their academic future was being jeopardised.

He explained that the protest was not intended to confront the state government but to draw attention to the hardship caused by the prolonged strike and demand decisive action.

Opatunmibi said the students had made several appeals to the government and issued two 48-hour ultimatums without the desired response.

He said: “On November 12, we issued a 48-hour ultimatum to the state government, appealing to Governor Dapo Abiodun to urgently intervene and bring an end to the ongoing ASUP strike.

“The 48 hours elapsed without any meaningful action from the government. Consequently, on Monday, we addressed another press conference, appealing to the government to come to our rescue because the strike had stalled our education. We also issued another 48-hour ultimatum.

“That ultimatum expired on Wednesday afternoon, but we were disappointed that nothing had been done to address our concerns. We are really unhappy. Does it mean that the government does not care about our plight?

“The closure of all the polytechnics in the state is seriously affecting us. We cannot continue to sit at home while our academic programmes and future plans are being put on hold.

“We are here to demonstrate that the voices of students matter. We are not fighting the government; we are simply demanding that the issues responsible for this strike be resolved.

“We cannot continue to put our future in jeopardy. We appeal to Governor Abiodun to please attend to the demands of our lecturers so that we can return to our respective institutions and complete our education.”

Also speaking, a NAPS member, Kolade Musbau, expressed disappointment over what he described as the government’s lack of urgency in resolving the dispute, saying students were bearing the brunt of the industrial action.

Musbau lamented that students who should be attending lectures and progressing with their academic programmes had been forced to remain at home, threatening their ability to complete their studies within the stipulated period.

He said: “The students are not happy that, instead of being in school, we are at home wasting valuable time because of this ASUP strike. Despite our repeated appeals, it appears that the government is not ready to do the needful.

“We have, therefore, been left with no option but to embark on this protest to draw the government’s attention to our plight and demand urgent intervention to end the strike.

“We are all eager to return to our respective institutions and complete our studies within the expected period. We appeal to Governor Abiodun to bring this strike to an end without further delay.”

Responding on behalf of the state government, the Permanent Secretary, Bureau of Cabinet and Special Services, Mr Dolamu Idowu-Agida, assured the protesters that the government was making efforts to resolve the disagreement with the lecturers.

Idowu-Agida disclosed that the government had held two meetings with relevant stakeholders to address the issues surrounding the industrial action.

He also revealed that approval had been granted for an increase in the monthly subvention to all state-owned polytechnics, expressing optimism that the strike would be called off within 48 hours.

He said: “I want to assure you that the state government has held meetings with relevant stakeholders on this matter twice. The government is seriously addressing your concerns.

“As of yesterday, approval had been granted for an increase in the subvention to all the polytechnics in the state.

“The issues raised by your lecturers are receiving serious consideration. I want to assure you that the matter will soon be resolved and your lecturers will return to the classrooms.

“Be rest assured that your lecturers should be back in the classrooms within the next 48 hours.”

It will be recalled that lecturers in the six state-owned polytechnics in Ogun State embarked on an indefinite strike last Wednesday following the expiration of a 15-day ultimatum issued to the state government to address their outstanding demands.

The industrial action followed the alleged non-implementation of the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance (CATA) and Earned Academic Allowance (EAA), as well as concerns over what the union described as inadequate funding of the institutions.

ASUP had also faulted the government’s continued payment of a monthly subvention of N5 million to some of the state-owned polytechnics, arguing that the amount had remained unchanged for more than a decade despite prevailing economic realities and rising operational costs.

Among its major demands, the union is seeking payment of outstanding CATA and EAA entitlements, as well as an immediate review and upward adjustment of the monthly subvention to N100 million for all state-owned polytechnics.

The union maintained that increased funding was necessary to meet the institutions’ operational needs, improve the quality of education and ensure effective delivery of academic programmes.

title: Trial of killers of Ademola, Salami begins in Lagos
description:
By Innocent Anaba



THE long-awaited trial of four persons accused of the alleged murder of Prince Akinloye Ademola and Sherriff Ishola Salami in the Ajiran area of Lagos State commenced yesterday, with the Lagos State prosecution opening its case before the court.



The trial began before Justice
content:
By Innocent Anaba

THE long-awaited trial of four persons accused of the alleged murder of Prince Akinloye Ademola and Sherriff Ishola Salami in the Ajiran area of Lagos State commenced yesterday, with the Lagos State prosecution opening its case before the court.


The trial began before Justice A. Muyideen of the Lagos State High Court sitting in Igbosere.Those standing trial are Sefiu Fatai, aka Fabo; Yusuf Ismail, aka Bariga; Tajudeen Ahmed, aka Ahmed Ajiran; and Bode Ajose.


The prosecution team was led by the Lagos State Solicitor-General, Mr Adebayo Haroon, while the defence counsel included Mr O. Ajanaku, Mr R. Owolabi, Mr Olalekan Ojo, SAN, and Mr Gbenga Ojo, who represented the third defendant. Mr M. Familola represented the fourth defendant.


The prosecution called its first witness, ASP Nosiru Isiaka, a police officer attached to Special Squad 1 of the Lagos State Police Command, who testified on the circumstances surrounding the investigation and eventual arrest of the defendants.


In his evidence-in-chief, ASP Isiaka narrated how the police initially arrested the first two suspects, Sefiu Fatai, aka Fabo, and Yusuf Ismail, aka Bariga, and how the third suspect was later arrested through the technical team from the Inspector-General of Police’s office in the Ajiran area of Ajah.
He further told the court how investigations eventually led to the arrest of the third defendant. He was about to narrate how the investigation led to the arrest of the fourth suspect, Mr Ahmed Tajudeen, when his testimony was interrupted by the defence counsel. The police witness, while recounting the investigative steps taken by his team, explained how information obtained during the investigation helped the police establish links between the four defendants and the alleged murder of the two victims.
However, proceedings were interrupted by objections from the defence counsel, Ojo, SAN, and the other three lawyers representing the defendants, who challenged the manner in which the prosecution witness was presenting his evidence.
Ojo, who is the leading counsel to the defendants, argued that the police Investigating Police Officer (IPO), being the first prosecution witness, could not give evidence.
in a manner suggesting that he personally witnessed the circumstances surrounding the killings when, in fact, he was only an investigating officer who was not present at the scene of the alleged crime.
He maintained that the witness must confine his testimony to facts within his personal knowledge and properly distinguish between what he personally did or observed during the investigation and information allegedly obtained from other persons in the course of police inquiries.
The objection interrupted the proceedings as the defence sought to ensure that the prosecution’s evidence remained within the boundaries of admissible evidence under the law.
Further hearing in the matter has been adjourned until November 25.

The post Trial of killers of Ademola, Salami begins in Lagos appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Customs to replace obsolete cargo tracking seals with 2,000 units
description:
The Nigeria Customs Service has concluded plans to upgrade its B’Odogwu Unified Customs Management System to address cargo clearance bottlenecks, strengthen tracking of goods in transit and improve revenue collection.
The resolutions followed a three-day review workshop, where the service and its te
content:
The Nigeria Customs Service has concluded plans to upgrade its B’Odogwu Unified Customs Management System to address cargo clearance bottlenecks, strengthen tracking of goods in transit and improve revenue collection.

The resolutions followed a three-day review workshop, where the service and its technology partners identified operational gaps and agreed on technical improvements to make the platform more efficient.

A major outcome of the meeting was the plan to replace 200 obsolete electronic cargo tracking seals with 2,000 newly procured units, alongside the integration of an upgraded Electronic Cargo Tracking System with the B’Odogwu platform.

The measures are expected to strengthen monitoring of bonded cargo, reduce the risk of diversion and improve the accountability of goods moving through Nigeria’s customs-controlled transit corridors.

The workshop, held between 9 and 11 November, 2026, was between the NCS management and officers, Trade Modernisation Project Limited and CB-XP representatives to assess the implementation of the system and agree on measures to address identified challenges.

In a statement issued by the service on Wednesday, the NCS said the discussions focused on improving the platform’s operational efficiency, strengthening customs processes and developing a roadmap for its future development.

The statement read, “The Nigeria Customs Service has concluded a three-day review of its B’Odogwu Unified Customs Management System in Lisbon, Portugal, with resolutions aimed at addressing operational challenges, accelerating cargo clearance, strengthening cargo tracking and improving revenue collection. The workshop, held from 9 to 11 November 2026 at the Corinthia Hotel, brought together NCS management and officers, Trade Modernisation Project Limited and CB-XP representatives to assess the system’s implementation and agree on technical and operational improvements.”

Speaking at the opening ceremony, the Deputy Comptroller-General of Customs in charge of ICT Modernisation, Oluyomi Adebakin, commended the Comptroller-General of Customs, Adewale Adeniyi, for his support for technological innovation and capacity development within the service.

The Managing Director of Trade Modernisation Project Limited, Jummai Umar-Ajijola, who represented the company’s Chairman, Saleh Ahmadu, said the B’Odogwu platform had attracted interest from the African Continental Free Trade Area Secretariat.

She said improvements to the system had contributed to higher revenue generation and strengthened the country’s revenue collection framework.

Umar-Ajijola said the review was an opportunity to assess the platform’s performance since its implementation and develop a clear direction for further improvements.

“We are to work to find a concrete plan not only to consolidate but to build a change roadmap going forward at the assessment of the three years so far,” she said.

She also commended the NCS Public Relations Unit for its consistent reporting on the project.

The workshop also identified several areas requiring improvements, including the automation of customs procedure code approvals and the processing of import, export, re-importation and transit declarations.

Participants also agreed on the need to harmonise procedure code nomenclature across customs operations to promote consistency, efficiency and accountability.

Under the proposed cargo tracking improvements, individual containers covered by relevant transit declarations will be monitored more effectively, while bond registration and validation processes will be strengthened.

title: CBN’s cash mop-up more than doubles ahead of 2027
description:
The Central Bank of Nigeria has intensified its liquidity mop-up operations, withdrawing more than N90tn from the financial system through Open Market Operations securities in the first 11 months of 2026, as it seeks to contain inflationary pressures ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The amount r
content:
The Central Bank of Nigeria has intensified its liquidity mop-up operations, withdrawing more than N90tn from the financial system through Open Market Operations securities in the first 11 months of 2026, as it seeks to contain inflationary pressures ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The amount represents a sharp increase from the N40.9tn withdrawn in 2025, reflecting the apex bank’s aggressive monetary tightening efforts to rein in excess liquidity and prevent renewed inflationary pressures amid concerns about election-related spending.

The increased liquidity withdrawal comes as policymakers warn that political spending ahead of the 2027 elections could inject substantial funds into the economy, potentially complicating the CBN’s efforts to sustain the disinflationary trend.

The CBN withdrew N50.23tn through liquidity mop-up operations in 2024, while its sales of OMO securities declined to N40.90tn in 2025, according to the apex bank’s 2025 Annual Report.

However, liquidity absorption has accelerated significantly this year. Data from CBN auctions, FMDQ and the Financial Market Dealers Association show that the apex bank withdrew more than N90tn through OMO operations between January and November. The figure, however, excludes OMO maturities for some months and may not reflect the net amount of liquidity absorbed during the period.

Monthly FMDA data show that the CBN withdrew N13.41tn in January and N6.3tn in February. The amount fell to N2.36tn in March before increasing to N4.48tn in April.

In May, the apex bank absorbed N5.42tn through two OMO auctions held on May 21 and 29, while its liquidity mop-up rose sharply to N13.96tn in June. The amount subsequently moderated to N7.18tn in July and N4.72tn in August.

September recorded the highest OMO allotment, with the CBN raising N17.5tn as it intensified efforts to contain excess liquidity in the banking system.

In October, the apex bank allotted N6.182tn in new OMO bills, while N9.051tn worth of existing securities matured, resulting in a net repayment of approximately N2.87tn before other adjustments, according to FMDA data.

The CBN subsequently withdrew N7.53tn through OMO auctions conducted on 3, 4 and 10 November.

Some sources cite CBN OMO sales at over N103tn so far this year, but The PUNCH relied on data from CBN auctions, FMDQ and the Financial Market Dealers Association.

The aggressive issuance comes as the CBN faces the challenge of maintaining monetary stability while preparing for potential liquidity pressures associated with the 2027 election cycle.

MPC members warn

Members of the Central Bank of Nigeria’s Monetary Policy Committee warned in late October that increased government spending ahead of the 2027 general elections could fuel inflation, weaken fiscal discipline and complicate efforts to maintain monetary stability.

The warnings came as Nigeria’s broad money supply rose to N146.60tn in September 2026, up N28.82tn from a year earlier, while credit to the government climbed by 63.09 per cent to N39.40tn.

The concerns were contained in personal statements issued by MPC members following the committee’s 307th meeting held on 21 and 22 September, 2026.

The members cautioned that election-related expenditure, alongside pressure from fuel, food and production costs, could slow the country’s progress in bringing inflation under control.

Deputy Governor of the CBN’s Corporate Services Directorate, Dr Muhammad Abdullahi, warned that election-related fiscal expansion could transmit inflationary pressure through transportation, energy and production costs.

“I recognise that election-related fiscal expansion and other incipient price pressures may propagate through transport, energy and production cost channels, amplifying economy-wide cost-push inflation,” he said.

Abdullahi called for closer coordination between fiscal and monetary authorities to prevent government measures from injecting additional liquidity into the economy and undermining price stability.

Another MPC member and Senior Fellow at the Brookings Institution, Dr Aloysius Ordu, urged the government to maintain fiscal discipline as political activities intensify.

“And as the election cycle approaches, stronger safeguards against fiscal slippage and pro-cyclical spending will be important,” Ordu said.

He noted that improved oil receipts were strengthening government finances but warned that converting foreign exchange earnings into domestic liquidity could complicate efforts to contain inflation.

Similarly, MPC member, Bandele Amoo, identified political activities and budget implementation as potential sources of renewed spending pressure.

“As global uncertainty remains elevated, domestic political activities may introduce new spending pressures, and supply-side vulnerabilities continue to pose risks to the inflation outlook,” Amoo said.

He expressed optimism that better coordination between the CBN and the Federal Ministry of Finance would help manage spending pressures, stressing that monetary policy decisions should remain guided by economic evidence and medium-term price stability.

Professor Murtala Sagagi acknowledged that election-related spending had historically put pressure on demand and prices but said existing monetary policy tools could help contain the risks.

He cited the CBN’s liquidity management instruments, its Cash Reserve Requirement and a memorandum of understanding on fiscal-monetary coordination between the CBN and the Federal Ministry of Finance.

CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, said the bank had analysed previous election cycles and developed scenarios to prepare for possible liquidity pressures.

“We are ready,” Cardoso said at a press briefing after the committee’s September meeting.

He said the bank would monitor currency in circulation, banking system liquidity, monetary aggregates and foreign exchange demand.

“We will proactively deploy any tools and instruments to mop up any excess liquidity,” the governor said, adding that the CBN would not allow itself to be caught unprepared.

World Bank warns

The World Bank warned in October that Nigeria’s consolidated fiscal deficit was expected to widen from 3.1 per cent of GDP in 2025 to 3.5 percent in 2026, despite higher oil revenues and increased government allocations.

In its Nigeria Development Update titled ‘Beyond the Federal Purse: How Higher Revenues Reshaped State Priorities’, the bank said stronger capital spending and pre-election spending would outweigh the gains from increased revenues.

“Despite the narrower federal fiscal deficit in H1 2026, stronger capital spending by states alongside rising federal personnel, interest, and pre-election spending is expected to widen the consolidated fiscal deficit from 3.1 percent of GDP in 2025 to 3.5 percent in 2026, outweighing stronger revenues,” the World Bank said.

The report said higher oil prices, following the conflict in the Middle East, had supported government revenues and improved the country’s external position, but existing oil sales and financing commitments had limited the fiscal benefits.

The bank warned that spending pressures are expected to increase later in the year, potentially reversing some of the fiscal gains.

Analysts wade in

Economists have attributed the CBN’s aggressive liquidity mop-up in 2026 to increased election-related spending and higher revenue allocations to state and local governments. They said the exercise reflects the apex bank’s efforts to prevent excess money in circulation from triggering fresh inflationary pressures.

In separate phone interviews with The PUNCH, the economists said rising government revenues, increased public sector deposits in commercial banks and political spending had contributed to the liquidity build-up, leaving the CBN with the task of absorbing surplus funds.

A Professor of Economics and Public Policy at the University of Uyo, Akpan Ekpo, said the CBN was seeking to control money supply to prevent excess liquidity from undermining price stability.

“With the election coming, there will be a lot of expenditures. So, the CBN has to mop it up because even inflation is not always a monetary phenomenon; it can also be a fiscal phenomenon,” Ekpo said.

He explained that the apex bank was concerned that excess cash in the financial system could translate into increased consumer spending and push up prices.

“I suspect the CBN wants to make sure that the liquidity in the system does not jack up the consumer price index,” he said.

However, Ekpo expressed doubts about the effectiveness of the intervention, arguing that the scale of spending expected ahead of the elections could undermine the CBN’s efforts.

“With the elections coming, I don’t think the CBN effort will bear much fruit,” he said.

Similarly, the Founder of the Centre for the Promotion of Private Enterprise, Dr Muda Yusuf, linked the liquidity expansion to increased government revenues and allocations to state and local governments, much of which he said remained within the banking system.

“The only source that I think could have been responsible for that is the high government revenue resulting from higher allocations to the state and local governments, most of which are also in the banks,” Yusuf said.

He noted that the CBN had introduced differentiated cash reserve requirements to limit the amount of public sector funds banks could deploy for lending. The apex bank imposes a 75 per cent Cash Reserve Ratio on public sector deposits outside the Treasury Single Account, compared with 45 per cent on regular deposits.

Despite these restrictions, Yusuf said public sector funds continued to contribute to overall liquidity in the financial system.

“The public sector liquidity is feeding into the financial system liquidity,” he said.

He also identified election-related expenditure as another source of pressure, noting that spending by political parties, candidates and government institutions involved in the electoral process could inject substantial amounts of money into the economy.

“Political spending from INEC, security agencies, political parties and, above all, the candidates themselves, all of those things are injecting a lot of liquidity into the system,” Yusuf said.

Also, the Managing Director of Highcap Securities Limited, Mr David Adonri, identified monetary operations, bank recapitalisation and government spending as factors that could have contributed to the liquidity build-up.

He explained that transactions involving Open Market Operations securities could influence the volume of funds available in the banking system, particularly when the CBN redeems previously issued instruments.

Adonri also noted that the reduction in banks’ holdings of certain securities could have left them with more funds to deploy, while the recapitalisation exercise increased the capital available to financial institutions.

He also linked the liquidity situation to political activities, arguing that increased expenditure by governments and politicians could add further pressure to the financial system.

According to him, when investors redeem government securities, the proceeds return to the banking system, potentially increasing available liquidity, particularly where the instruments carry high yields.

The post CBN’s cash mop-up more than doubles ahead of 2027 appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Opposition coalition pushes consensus candidate for 2027 polls
description:
An opposition political coalition, The Big Tent, has urged presidential candidates of opposition parties to unite and present a consensus candidate ahead of the January 16, 2027, presidential election.
 In a statement issued on Thursday in Abuja, the spokesman for the coalition, Toni Akeni, called o
content:
An opposition political coalition, The Big Tent, has urged presidential candidates of opposition parties to unite and present a consensus candidate ahead of the January 16, 2027, presidential election.

 In a statement issued on Thursday in Abuja, the spokesman for the coalition, Toni Akeni, called on opposition leaders to begin discussions on forming an inclusive cabinet-in-waiting to take over governance after the election.

 While assessing the political campaigns of various parties across the country, Akeni expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu and the ruling All Progressives Congress would lose the election, claiming that Nigerians were dissatisfied with the administration.

 “This is not guesswork. Since the history books of Nigeria were opened in 1914, since her independence in 1960 to the present, no sitting president and ruling party has made Nigerians suffer such mass hardship, misgovernance agony, ballot vengeance bitterness and red cards of eviction anger by Nigeria’s citizens as the Tinubu administration has managed to do,” he said.

 He claimed that public dissatisfaction with the APC was evident across the country, alleging that opposition parties were attracting larger crowds at their campaign rallies.

 “From north to south and east to west, the streets have spoken loud and clear. One thing is uppermost and dear. Legitimate voters’ verdict on the APC is damning and conclusive. They can’t wait for January 16, 2027, to boot the present ruling party out of power,” Akeni said.

 He further alleged that APC campaign rallies were poorly attended, while those of the Nigeria Democratic Congress and other opposition parties attracted large crowds.

 “Dissent against Tinubu’s APC is deafening on land and air. In homes, vehicles to work, offices, citizens’ discourses in the media, markets and malls,” he added.

 On the economy, Akeni accused the Tinubu administration of worsening poverty and accumulating unsustainable foreign debts, alleging that the government’s economic advisers were disconnected from the hardships facing Nigerians.

 He also criticised the administration’s handling of insecurity, accusing it of failing to protect communities affected by terrorist attacks and banditry.

 “For nearly three and a half years, Tinubu’s APC displayed incredible unconcern, dissociation and insensitivity to millions of Nigerians drenched in the calamities and agonies of daily killings, unrelenting bloodshed and literally hundreds of communities violently sacked by colonies of barefaced terrorists and bandits,” he said.

 Akeni also cited what he described as the growing number of internally displaced persons across the country, claiming that 3.7 million Nigerians were living in about 3,900 displacement camps.

 He called on opposition presidential hopefuls, including former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi, Donald Duke, Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, Peter Agada and Omoyele Sowore, to put aside personal ambitions and work towards selecting a consensus candidate.

 “Your Excellencies most valiant and noble: Abubakar Atiku, the blessed eldest opposition presidential candidate at age 79, Peter Obi, Donald Duke, Sheyi Makinde, Peter Agada, Omoyele Sowore and the others, the hour has come and indeed has long been overdue when you must hold hands – not as politicians but as statesmen, all pride and self-serving considerations gone – and walk together to that Green-White-Green Table to give Nigerians one consensus presidential candidate,” he said.

 According to him, a united opposition would provide an opportunity to present a candidate capable of leading a government focused on addressing the country’s challenges.

 He said the opposition leaders had an opportunity to make a lasting contribution to Nigeria’s political history by prioritising national interest over personal ambitions.

 “Legacy awaits you at that table. Nigerians have spoken. APC’s pestilence is broken. Their spell is over. Do the needful. History is waiting,” Akeni added.

The post Opposition coalition pushes consensus candidate for 2027 polls appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Lagos, Enugu, Ogun account for 54% of states’ IGR
description:
Lagos, Enugu and Ogun states jointly generated N2.36 trillion in Internally Generated Revenue in 2025, accounting for 54.4 per cent of the N4.34tn collected by the 35 states covered in BudgIT’s 2026 State of States report.
The remaining 32 states, many of which depend heavily on federal allocations,
content:
Lagos, Enugu and Ogun states jointly generated N2.36 trillion in Internally Generated Revenue in 2025, accounting for 54.4 per cent of the N4.34tn collected by the 35 states covered in BudgIT’s 2026 State of States report.

The remaining 32 states, many of which depend heavily on federal allocations, collectively generated N1.98tn, representing 45.6 per cent of the total revenue.

The report, titled From Allocation to Impact: Rethinking State Spending Priorities, highlights the significant revenue disparity between the three leading states and the remaining 32. An analysis of its figures revealed that IGR accounted for 59.6 per cent of the three states’ combined revenue of N3.96tn, compared with just 12.8 per cent of the N15.42tn generated collectively by the other 32 states.

Lagos alone raised N1.71tn, representing 39.5 per cent of the total, with its IGR rising 35.67 per cent from N1.26tn in 2024, accounting for 67.72 per cent of its recurrent revenue.

Its receipts from the Federation Account Allocation Committee were N816.48bn, or 30.47 per cent of its N2.68tn total revenue.

Enugu’s IGR rose 125.91 per cent, from N180.50bn to N407.76bn, and IGR made up 52.98 per cent of its total revenue. Ogun collected N238.50bn, representing 46.68 per cent of its N510.88bn total revenue.

BudgIT cautioned that the figures needed careful interpretation. Non-tax receipts accounted for 90.79 per cent of Enugu’s increase in IGR, while tax revenue made up only 11.68 per cent of its IGR.

BudgIT further noted that Ogun, despite its impressive IGR performance, placed 31st on the overall fiscal performance index. The state had a total debt of N538.92bn, the fourth largest among those assessed, while debt servicing consumed 17.11 per cent of its revenue. Lagos topped the index with 66.97 points, followed by Enugu with 65.45 points.

In contrast, the report showed that 30 of the 35 states generated less than 20 per cent of their total revenue internally. Federation Account allocations supplied the bulk of the money for most of them. The analysis showed that FAAC receipts made up 70.9 per cent of the combined total revenue of the 32 states outside the top three, compared with 32.3 per cent for Lagos, Enugu and Ogun.

BudgIT reported that 18 states depended on FAAC for at least 70 per cent of their total revenue. Bayelsa topped the list at 90.94 per cent, followed by Taraba at 90.29 per cent, Akwa Ibom at 89.12 per cent and Anambra at 86.47 per cent.

Yobe recorded the lowest IGR, at N13.35bn, representing 4.40 per cent of its total revenue. Sokoto’s IGR fell by 6.64 per cent to N20.58bn, while Osun’s slipped marginally by 0.25 per cent to N54.39bn.

Some states recorded sharp gains from low bases. Oyo’s IGR surged 112.79 per cent to N138.93bn, and Gombe’s IGR rose 111.28 per cent to N43.97bn. BudgIT warned against reading too much into such figures, saying, “percentage growth alone can be misleading.”

BudgIT said states should strengthen tax administration, reduce leakages, improve taxpayer services and broaden compliance through economic formalisation. It added that they must avoid placing excessive pressure on households and small enterprises already facing difficult economic conditions.

The organisation said tax reform must be tied to what citizens receive in return. BudgIT stated, “revenue reform must be linked to a credible social contract.”

It said citizens were more likely to accept tax obligations when they saw improvements in roads, healthcare, education, water and other public services.

BudgIT said higher collections did not by themselves amount to fiscal independence: “Fiscal independence is therefore not achieved merely when IGR rises.”

It noted that states achieved fiscal independence when they developed reliable, equitable and sustainable sources of public revenue.

BudgIT also stressed the quality of revenue over its size. “The quality of revenue matters as much as its quantity,” BudgIT stated.

Rivers State was excluded from the 11th edition because it produced no audited financial statement for 2025 and no budget implementation reports.

BudgIT disclosed that it changed its methodology this year, so year-on-year movements in rankings should not be read as direct improvements or declines.

The post Lagos, Enugu, Ogun account for 54% of states’ IGR appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Copyright abuse: REPRONIG takes advocacy campaign to South-West
description:
The Reproduction Rights Society of Nigeria has taken its national copyright advocacy campaign to the South-West, warning that the unauthorised reproduction of books, articles and creative works in tertiary institutions will no longer be tolerated.
The South-West Zonal Advocacy and Sensitisation Prog
content:
The Reproduction Rights Society of Nigeria has taken its national copyright advocacy campaign to the South-West, warning that the unauthorised reproduction of books, articles and creative works in tertiary institutions will no longer be tolerated.

The South-West Zonal Advocacy and Sensitisation Programme, held at the U.I Ventures Mini Hall, University of Ibadan, attracted authors, publishers, librarians, lecturers, artists and representatives of higher institutions across Ekiti, Lagos, Ogun, Ondo, Osun and Oyo states.

The programme, themed ‘Nigerian Copyright Law and the Role of REPRONIG,’ is the fifth in the ongoing nationwide campaign covering all six geopolitical zones. Previous editions have been held in North-Central, North-West, South-South and South-East, with the final edition for the North-East scheduled to hold in Maiduguri.

Speaking with journalists on the sidelines, Chairman, Board of REPRONIG, Mr Gbadega Adedapo, said the essence of the zonal advocacy was to bridge the gap between policy and the people meant to benefit from it.

“We collect rights of the authors from institutions — we license the institutions. Because if you have a programme but the communities that are supposed to benefit from that assignment are not fully aware, it shows that they may not even subscribe to it,” Adedapo said.

“So, this programme is about the fifth one in Nigeria and all the six geopolitical zones are almost covered. It’s a welcome development for writers. Imagine you have your published work in institutions but students are the ones enjoying it and you’re not benefitting from it. But now, there is an organisation ready to assist you, not a private business per se. Because we have the Nigerian Copyright Commission regulating our activities. And the board members of REPRONIG comprise the authors, publishers, artists, among others. So the stakeholders in that ecosystem are well represented.”

A board member of REPRONIG and current President of the Nigerian Publishers Association, Alhaji Lukman Dauda, said the programme was designed to confront the culture of indiscriminate photocopying in academic communities.

“The essence is to bring to the awareness of the general public and particularly, those people living within the academic communities to know what REPRONIG stands for, what’s capable of doing, the benefits derivable from its activities, especially to content creators — authors and other creators of original thinking,” Dauda said.

“What we are trying to do here is to ensure that people who have laboured to bring about something for the benefit of humanity don’t do that in vain, especially in the academic community where the common thing is for people’s works, especially published articles, to just be reproduced without any hindrance. Such things definitely affect the benefits derivable by the original owners, he added.

Dauda said invitations were sent to 77 public and private universities and polytechnics across the South-West, with each institution asked to nominate two representatives. However, despite repeated follow-ups, only about 30 institutions, representing 39 per cent, responded. At the time of the event, 60 participants had joined online, while 40 attended physically.

“By bringing this programme up throughout the six geopolitical zones of the country, and this is the fifth one, and another one will be happening next week in Maiduguri, the underpinning is to let the original owners of these creative works know that there’s an organisation that is fighting for their interest and that their labour will not be in vain going forward,” he said.

“So, we are trying everything possible to get institutions of higher learning licensed and then to be able to make contributions towards this unauthorised reproduction of people’s works. And whatever is generated from such efforts will be shared among the original owners that have taken the pain to register and upload their works on the platform of REPRONIG. That’s the major reason for this programme,” Dauda added.

Acting Executive Director of REPRONIG, Mr Tosin Akeredolu, explained the legal mandate of the organisation as the sole Collective Management Organisation for reprographic rights in Nigeria.

“The Reproduction Rights Society of Nigeria is the only collective management organisation in Nigeria that’s responsible for the administration and protection of secondary right in terms of reprography, that’s reproduction either through photocopy, through digital download, through scanning, through sharing on digital network and so forth,” Akeredolu said.

“By doing so, there’s a high tendency that the rights of those creators — authors, publishers, newspaper proprietors, artists, among others, might be infringed upon even without their permission. So, the government in its wisdom through the Nigerian Copyright Commission set up a body that’s licensed to monitor and also protect the rights of literary creators — right owners, right holders in the text and image-based sector. So, this sensitisation and awareness programme is for every stakeholder in the country to know their rights and to carry everybody along,” he added.

Deputy Director, Regulatory and Compliance Department, Nigerian Copyright Commission, Kunle Olatunji, who spoke on Nigerian Copyright Law and Reproduction Rights, said the Copyright Act 2022 had expanded protection into the digital space and now held Internet Service Providers accountable.

Speaking on the provisions, Olatunji noted, “The whole part of Copyright Act 2022 is devoted to copyright in the online environment. It also now has safeguards for tampering with any work in the online environment either by way of tampering with technological protection measures or removal of right management information.”

“It goes further to even make ISP responsible. And like I said earlier in my presentation, that provision is not only there, the Copyright Act now has the capacity to take down any infringing website wherever it is worldwide, and not just the work alone. For example, we are prosecuting the man behind NetNaija and that’s why you cannot see NetNaija anywhere. We are also prosecuting MovieBox online platform that distributes movies and what have you. So, if we can do that to those ones, then when it comes to the publishing industry, definitely the same rule will apply.”

On what ordinary Nigerians must do to avoid falling foul of the law, the NCC official was blunt: “Thou Shall Not Steal. Because if you used somebody’s work without permission, you’re essentially stealing.”

“So basically, we live in a country where the majority are not literate. Those of us who are literates pretend that we don’t see. That’s my experience for over 20 years in the industry.”

On Artificial Intelligence and intellectual property, Olatunji said AI had not altered the principle of authorship, explaining, “The protection of creatives in the realm of AI has not changed because copyright is essentially a human right, not a machine right. So, you cannot aggregate people’s works and do machine learning and start pushing it out. Each of those individuals whose works you’re dealing with under the cover of AI, they still have the original right. And the moment the commission discovers or we have a petition, we will go after you.”

He warned that penalties under the Copyright Act 2022 included asset forfeiture, fines, imprisonment or a combination, depending on the severity of the infringement.

Head of the Department of Library, Archival and Information Studies, University of Ibadan, Prof. Clement Akangbe, delivered his paper on Promoting Copyright Compliance in Libraries and Academic Institutions: The role of Librarians and Information Professionals.

The Director-General of the Nigerian Copyright Commission, Dr John Asein, was represented by Olatunji at the occasion.

Also in attendance were Managing Director of Stirling-Horden Publishers Limited, Prof. Tope Olaifa;  current Chairman of the Association of Nigerian Authors, Oyo State Chapter, Prof. Andrew Okwilagwe; Dr Philomena Nwoko; Mrs Yomi Ogunlari; and other participants.

The post Copyright abuse: REPRONIG takes advocacy campaign to South-West appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Checkers unveils BBNaija winner as brand ambassador
description:
Checkers Africa Limited, makers of Checkers Custard, has unveiled Big Brother Naija Season 11 winner, Temi Nkem, as its brand ambassador, highlighting family values, authenticity and her natural affinity with the product.
The company said Nkem’s genuine love for Checkers Custard during her 10-week s
content:
Checkers Africa Limited, makers of Checkers Custard, has unveiled Big Brother Naija Season 11 winner, Temi Nkem, as its brand ambassador, highlighting family values, authenticity and her natural affinity with the product.

The company said Nkem’s genuine love for Checkers Custard during her 10-week stay in the reality television show made her a natural fit for the brand, which has maintained its association with the programme.

The unveiling took place at the company’s office in Lagos on Monday, at a ceremony attended by its management, staff, media representatives, content creators and other guests.

Speaking at the event, the Chief Executive Officer of Checkers Africa Limited, Karan Checker, said the company had identified shared values and a natural connection between Nkem and the brand.

Checker said, “At Checkers Africa, we believe that great brands should be part of your daily experiences and happy moments of the people they serve. This is one of the reasons we have continued our support for Big Brother Naija. Beyond entertainment, the show celebrates talent, creativity, ambition, and the wonderful diversity of our people.”

He said the company followed Nkem’s journey on the show and noticed her frequent visits to the kitchen to prepare Checkers Custard.

“This made us look into a beautiful, interesting young lady and explore the potential for her representing the brand due to shared values and natural alignment. Somewhere along the way, she developed a very special relationship with Checkers Custard on the show. In fact, I think Temi visited the kitchen almost every day for Checkers Custard,” he said.

Checker added that the relationship stood out because Nkem’s preference for the product appeared genuine rather than a calculated promotional strategy.

“What made this even more beautiful was that her love for Checkers Custard was completely natural and genuine. For us, this was a wonderful connection between a young star and a brand loved by millions of Nigerian families,” he said.

He said the company expected the partnership to strengthen its connection with younger consumers, adding that Nkem’s personality and influence would bring fresh energy to the brand.

In her remarks, Nkem said she looked forward to joining the Checkers family, recalling how her affection for the product had developed during her time in the Big Brother house.

She said, “Honestly, inside the house, I loved Checkers so much. You guys saw every single time I was always in the kitchen. I didn’t know how to cook, but it was just the custard that I kind of just wanted to learn because it seemed very much easier.”

The brand ambassador said her repeated preparation of the product did not form part of any strategy to win the competition, stressing that she simply enjoyed eating it.

“My strategy was just to have fun. But at the same time, I made Checkers, it was fun for me. It wasn’t a strategy. I just liked custard and I enjoyed it,” she said.

Nkem also described the product as a family-friendly meal, saying it reminded her of the warmth and comfort associated with home.

“Family, I mean, Checkers custard is very homely. Honestly, you taste the warmth in your mouth because obviously it’s a warm meal,” she said.

She identified vanilla as her favourite flavour and promised to deepen her association with the brand through the partnership.

Also speaking, the Head of Marketing, Checkers Africa Limited, Timothy Ogundele, said the company did not intend to appoint every Big Brother Naija contestant who showed an interest in its product as an ambassador.

He said Nkem’s personality, discipline and alignment with the company’s family-oriented values had informed the decision.

“Not every custard lover in future Big Brother Naija shows would merit an automatic ambassadorial appointment. The reason this happened is that it really aligned. She is a providential ambassador, brand representative. It was never planned; it was never orchestrated,” Ogundele said.

He added, “Temi as a person in the house was, even though unapologetic, she was warm, witty, intelligent, and she exercised great restraint and a deep sense of discipline, which is, you know, we’re a family brand. So, the alignment is something that is beyond just love.”

The company said the partnership would involve television commercials, radio advertisements, outdoor branding and appearances by Nkem on behalf of Checkers Custard.

Checkers Africa Limited, which also produces Checkers Pap, Checkers Crunchy Peanuts and 3-in-1 Checkers ChocoTee, was an associate sponsor of the 11th edition of Big Brother Naija, marking its third sponsorship of the reality television show.

The post Checkers unveils BBNaija winner as brand ambassador appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Business leaders promote resilience, transformative leadership
description:
Top business leaders have urged Nigerians to embrace transformational and resilient leadership, stressing the need for individuals to make a positive difference in the lives of others, regardless of their positions in society.
They said effective leadership goes beyond holding positions of authority
content:
Top business leaders have urged Nigerians to embrace transformational and resilient leadership, stressing the need for individuals to make a positive difference in the lives of others, regardless of their positions in society.

They said effective leadership goes beyond holding positions of authority, noting that leaders must demonstrate integrity, inspire others, build capable teams and remain focused on creating lasting impact.

They spoke at the Business Leaders Live2Lead Conference, themed ‘Vision to Execution’, hosted by L’ecole Consulting in partnership with Maxwell Leadership in Lagos on Tuesday.

The Managing Partner of L’ecole Consulting, Mrs Evbusogie Osojie, said leadership required individuals to identify ways to improve the lives of people around them and build a legacy through service and positive transformation.

Osojie explained that she conceived the conference to expose Nigerians to global leadership insights, following her participation in the John Maxwell Leadership Conference held in Orlando, Florida, in September, which motivated her to create the platform.

She noted that the celebration of Maxwell Leadership’s 50 years of global influence had strengthened the commitment of leadership coaches to promote values centred on service, personal growth and transformation.

“His DNA includes things like serving people, making people better versions of themselves, equipping people, giving them tools to be better leaders, living by example, having a positive attitude as a leader, and finally, becoming a catalyst for change and transformation,” Osojie said.

She challenged Nigerians in positions of responsibility to assess the impact of their leadership on their communities, workplaces and society.

“Our duty as a leader is to know how to make a difference in the lives of people. My thought was, what am I doing today to make a difference in the lives of people in my world? What is my legacy?” she asked.

Osojie stressed that leadership development must begin with personal discipline and the ability to lead oneself before attempting to lead others.

She said, “A leader must be self-led. We talk about being a great leader, but that great leadership starts from you being a better version of yourself. People don’t follow leaders who don’t know where they’re going.”

The L’ecole Consulting managing partner added that leaders needed clear visions, strategies and the competence to manage people and resources to translate their ideas into tangible results.

Similarly, the President of the Nigeria-British Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Abimbola Olashore, said business leaders needed integrity, a clear vision and the ability to build cohesive teams to navigate disruptions.

He noted that businesses must understand their purpose and remain committed to solving customers’ problems, adding that strong leadership and team cohesion would help organisations withstand internal and external challenges.

“Leadership is a journey, and you must have very strong leadership traits for you to succeed in the long run. Leadership must be based on integrity, must be based on the vision, and your ability to share that vision with a team that will execute what the business is set up to do,” Olashore said.

He urged emerging business leaders to prepare for disruptions, stressing that organisations with strong teams and a clear understanding of their customers’ needs would remain resilient.

The Managing Director of Optimus Bank, Ademola Odeyemi, also emphasised authenticity, competence and accountability as essential qualities of effective leadership.

He said leaders must earn people’s trust by demonstrating integrity and surrounding themselves with individuals who possess the right knowledge, temperament and experience.

“The most important thing for a leader is to be authentic and to be real. If you’re authentic, you give the best, and you give what you have. You cannot give what you don’t have,” Odeyemi said.

He warned against appointing people to leadership positions based on political considerations rather than competence, arguing that organisations needed capable individuals to deliver results.

Odeyemi also called for greater accountability in the public sector, urging Nigerians to become more knowledgeable about economic issues to make informed electoral choices.

“Don’t teach politicians economics, teach the electorate economics. When you teach the electorate what they need to know, when there’s a lot of political education, people understand what they should ask for, what they should expect, then they will vote the right person in,” he said.

Speaking on the banking sector, Odeyemi commended the Central Bank of Nigeria’s reforms, particularly the recapitalisation exercise, saying the measures had helped restore public confidence and strengthen the industry’s financial position.

He said sustained reforms and stronger regulatory supervision would support the banking sector’s capacity to finance economic growth.

Meanwhile, the Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Sochitel Group, Jerry Ejikeme, described resilience as the ability of business leaders to remain focused and committed to their goals despite challenges.

He said his company’s nearly two decades of operations in Africa’s financial technology sector had reinforced the importance of consistency and innovation in business leadership.

“Resilient leadership means staying the course, staying focused. Sochitel will be 20 years next year, during which we’ve been innovating and providing services to banks around Africa,” Ejikeme said.

He expressed optimism about the future of business leadership in Nigeria, particularly the growing contribution of young entrepreneurs and technology-driven businesses.

Ejikeme said Nigerian youths had demonstrated remarkable capacity to innovate and compete globally despite the country’s infrastructure challenges.

“I’m very excited about the young leaders in Nigeria. I’m very excited about innovation in Nigeria because, despite the infrastructural deficit challenges, the young people have gone digital,” he said.

He added that the widespread adoption of mobile technology had created new opportunities for businesses, allowing Nigerians to transact and connect with the rest of the world more easily.

The Sochitel chief executive described Nigerian youths’ entrepreneurial drive as one of the strongest across Africa, adding that their growing participation in technology and innovation offered significant prospects for the country’s business future.
