title: Lagos admits unfinished projects at new varsity
description: The Lagos State Government has admitted that key infrastructure projects at the Lagos State University of Education remain incomplete, including two 750-seat auditoriums and the reclamation of swampy sections of its Oto/Ijanikin campus, as the institution graduated its first 2,486 students on Thursd
content:
The Lagos State Government has admitted that key infrastructure projects at the Lagos State University of Education remain incomplete, including two 750-seat auditoriums and the reclamation of swampy sections of its Oto/Ijanikin campus, as the institution graduated its first 2,486 students on Thursday.

Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu disclosed the outstanding projects at the university’s maiden convocation, nearly five years after he signed the law establishing the institution from the former Adeniran Ogunsanya College of Education and Michael Otedola College of Primary Education.

The governor, who is due to leave office on May 29, 2027, said his administration would complete what it could before handing over the remaining projects to its successor as unfinished work.

“The rest is not finished. Two auditoriums of 750 seats, one here and one at Epe, are not complete. Specialised teaching facilities are still needed. Much of the land on this campus still has to be drained and reclaimed. I will not pretend that the list is short,” Sanwo-Olu said.

His admission came as he commissioned the university’s Senate Building and disclosed that new lecture theatres and academic buildings had been constructed on its two campuses, while a new salary structure for staff had been introduced.

“In the months I have left, we will do what we can on that list. What we do not finish will be handed over, properly recorded, as work in progress,” he said.

The outstanding projects raise questions about the funding and completion timetable for infrastructure at the specialised university, particularly as it begins producing graduates and expands its student population.

Sanwo-Olu said the institution, established by a law he signed on February 2, 2022, had grown from two colleges without a university structure into an institution with more than 15,000 students, 49 full professors and 66 academic programmes that received full accreditation from the National Universities Commission in 2024.

He said 2,486 students graduated at the first convocation, while others received diplomas and certificates.

The governor explained that the conversion of the two colleges into a university was intended to address declining interest in teaching, which he attributed partly to the disparity in qualifications between prospective teachers and graduates pursuing other professions.

“A young person in Lagos who wanted to teach went to a college and came out with a certificate. A young person who wanted to do almost anything else went to a university and came out with a degree. Students and their parents drew their own conclusion, and enrolment suffered. Then we complained that our brightest young people no longer wanted to teach,” he said.

He added, “We decided to stop complaining and change the offer. A society shows what it thinks of its children by what it requires of the people who teach them. We decided that the person who teaches a six-year-old to read should be educated to the same level as the doctor who will treat that child, or the engineer who will build the road to her school.”

The institution was created by merging the former Adeniran Ogunsanya College of Education in Oto/Ijanikin and the Michael Otedola College of Primary Education in Epe, both of which had trained teachers for decades.

Sanwo-Olu said 3,300 pioneer students matriculated in 2023 after being selected from more than 8,000 applicants, despite the institution having no previous graduates whose qualifications prospective students could assess.

He said the university’s first graduating set included 84 first-class degree holders, with Blessed Mercy Olawunmi of the Department of Home Economics emerging as the best graduating student with a cumulative grade point average of 4.98.

The governor warned the university’s management against compromising academic standards, particularly as it builds its reputation as a new institution.

“Do not lower the standard for anyone. Not for a Governor. Not for a Visitor. That is the only way to honour a name on a wall,” he said, referring to the Senate Building named after him.

Sanwo-Olu also urged the pioneer graduates to protect the institution’s reputation, saying employers and parents would judge the value of its degrees by the performance of its first graduates.

“For the next ten years, you are its reputation. When an employer or a parent asks what a LASUED degree is worth, the answer will be the last LASUED graduate they met. Make sure it is a good answer,” he said.

He further argued that the growing use of artificial intelligence in education made professionally trained teachers more important, not less, because technology could not replace the human ability to identify and respond to a child’s emotional and learning difficulties.

“The machine will answer the child who asks. It will not notice the child who has stopped asking. It will not know that she is hungry, or afraid, or that she has decided school is not for people like her. Only a teacher sees that,” he said.

The governor acknowledged concerns about the remuneration of teachers, saying teaching was not the best-paid career graduates could pursue and that governments, including his administration, had a responsibility to narrow the gap.

He said the importance of the institution extended beyond Lagos, citing UNESCO’s estimate that sub-Saharan Africa would need an additional 15 million teachers by 2030.

Sanwo-Olu said the university was intended to strengthen the supply and quality of teachers for Lagos and provide an example for the country.

He recalled that the Lagos State House of Assembly passed the establishment bill on November 15, 2021, before he signed it into law in February 2022.

The governor said the institution’s development was the product of the work of the Assembly, the university’s governing council, management and staff, rather than his administration alone.

He is expected to hand over the institution’s visitorial role to his successor when he leaves office next May, saying the university must be able to function beyond the tenure of the government that established it.

title: Fraud threatens Nigeria’s economic growth, institute warns
description: The Chartered Institute of Forensics and Certified Fraud Investigators of Nigeria has warned that rising global fraud losses pose a serious threat to economic growth, good governance and institutional integrity, calling for stronger collaboration among governments, businesses and anti-corruption age
content:
The Chartered Institute of Forensics and Certified Fraud Investigators of Nigeria has warned that rising global fraud losses pose a serious threat to economic growth, good governance and institutional integrity, calling for stronger collaboration among governments, businesses and anti-corruption agencies to tackle the menace.

The institute said the estimated scale of global fraud losses had reached alarming proportions, comparable to the annual economic output of major economies, underscoring the need for coordinated national, regional and international responses.

The Founder and Chairman, Governing Council of CIFCFIN, Dr Iliyasu Gashinbaki, made the call during an international press conference in Abuja to flag off the 2026 International Fraud Awareness Week, themed “Fraud Losses Rival National GDP: A Threat to Governance in Nigeria and Africa.”

Gashinbaki urged governments, public institutions, private sector organisations, professionals and citizens to intensify collective efforts to combat fraud, strengthen accountability and safeguard national resources.

He said fraud should no longer be viewed “merely as financial misconduct but as a fundamental governance challenge capable of weakening public institutions, eroding investor confidence, undermining public trust and diverting critical resources from infrastructure, healthcare, education and other essential services.”

Highlighting the global significance of the campaign, Gashinbaki said the Association of Certified Fraud Examiners (ACFE), the world’s largest anti-fraud organisation, brings together professionals, governments, businesses and citizens across more than 140 countries to promote fraud prevention, detection and accountability.

He noted that CIFCFIN, as an international supporting organisation, was participating in the global initiative and leading activities to commemorate the awareness week in Nigeria.

its campaign, CIFCFIN unveiled a 13-point statement outlining priorities for combating fraud and strengthening governance.

The issues highlighted included the need to recognise fraud as a governance crisis rather than merely a financial problem, the risks posed by weak internal controls and inadequate oversight, the effects of fraud on the integrity of public institutions, the growing sophistication of cyber-enabled financial crimes and the vulnerability of public procurement systems to fraudulent practices.

The statement also highlighted the role of certified professionals in fraud prevention and investigation, while emphasising citizens’ rights and responsibilities in demanding transparency and accountability.

Gashinbaki said no single institution or government agency could effectively combat fraud in isolation.

“There is therefore the urgent need for stronger collaboration among anti-corruption agencies, financial institutions, professional bodies, regulatory authorities, private sector organisations and international partners,” he advised.

He also identified professional competence and ethical integrity as essential in the fight against financial crimes, noting that forensic accountants, certified fraud investigators, auditors, compliance officers and other relevant professionals played crucial roles in detecting irregularities, preserving evidence, supporting investigations and facilitating successful prosecutions.

He said their expertise could determine whether fraudulent activities were detected before substantial losses occurred or discovered only after significant damage had been done.

“It could also influence whether investigations produce credible evidence capable of withstanding judicial scrutiny,” Gashinbaki said.

The CIFCFIN founder urged governments, ministries, departments and agencies, financial institutions and private sector organisations to prioritise the engagement of appropriately qualified and certified professionals in fraud prevention, forensic investigations, compliance and related functions.

He reaffirmed the institute’s commitment to upholding rigorous professional and ethical standards among its members, saying a highly skilled and incorruptible professional workforce remained one of the strongest safeguards against financial crimes and institutional abuse.

As part of activities marking the 2026 International Fraud Awareness Week, CIFCFIN held public awareness campaigns, visited tertiary institutions and organised an advocacy street walk and other engagements to educate citizens, particularly young people, on the dangers of fraud and the importance of ethical conduct.

title: Tinubu confers GCON on Olanipekun
description:
President Bola Tinubu on Thursday conferred the country’s second-highest national honour, the Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger (GCON), on legal luminary Chief Wole Olanipekun, SAN.
 He described him as a phenomenon who had served as lead counsel to four successive presidents of the Federal
content:
President Bola Tinubu on Thursday conferred the country’s second-highest national honour, the Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger (GCON), on legal luminary Chief Wole Olanipekun, SAN.

 He described him as a phenomenon who had served as lead counsel to four successive presidents of the Federal Republic.

 The conferment was made at the public presentation of a six-volume publication authored by Olanipekun in Abuja, marking his 75th birthday, 50 years at the Bar and 35 years as a Senior Advocate of Nigeria.

 Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, revealed this in a statement he signed on Thursday titled, ‘President Tinubu Confers National Honour, GCON, on Wole Olanipekun at Public Presentation of His Books.’

 “As President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, I proudly celebrate Chief Wole Olanipekun, Senior Advocate of Nigeria, a phenomenon in Nigeria and an outstanding advocate who has fittingly stepped into the shoes of the acclaimed legends of the legal profession.

 “He did not merely fill those shoes but is walking with them into new territory,” the President said.

 Tinubu eulogised Olanipekun for his years of commitment, hard work, resilience, mentorship of younger generations and advancement of the legal profession, as well as his community development, scholarship and social empowerment work in Ekiti State and across Nigeria.

 Tinubu acknowledged a decades-long personal and professional bond with the celebrant, disclosing that Olanipekun had led his legal team for decades and had remained a constant presence through the most consequential chapters of his political life, some of which, he noted, are documented in the volumes presented to the public on Thursday.

 “On a personal note, I celebrate decades of loyalty, friendship, commitment and reciprocity between Wole Olanipekun and me.

 “He has led my legal team for decades. In politics, friends come and go, but Wole came and stayed,” the President said.

 He noted that Olanipekun had also led the legal teams that successfully defended three of his predecessors when their elections were challenged, making him the only lawyer in the country’s history to have served as lead counsel to four sitting presidents since 2007.

 Tinubu said, “Wole’s loyalty is not luck. It is trust, and it is kept at the highest level of our nation. I commend you as a worthy Nigerian.

 “This nation is very, very proud and honoured. As one of the finest advocates beyond the courtroom, I recently had cause to acknowledge your community development initiatives and philanthropic interventions across critical sectors in Ekiti State and Nigeria at large.”

 “We thank God for you. 50 years at the bar, and you are still raising the bar.

 “You have positively impacted Nigeria and humanity. You have mentored many, including myself. May God continue to spare your life, enrich you, protect you, strengthen your mind and enrich your intellectual inquisitiveness to do more for humanity the way we have been doing. Congratulations and happy birthday,” the President said.

 Tinubu used the occasion to reaffirm his administration’s commitment to judicial independence, describing a credible judiciary as not merely a constitutional requirement but an economic imperative.

 “The Rule of Law is a priority for our administration. This is not only because I am a constitutional democrat.

 “This is because of who we are as a nation, the giant of Africa. It is also because we firmly believe that a viable, trustworthy, competent, resourceful and independent judiciary is indispensable to the economic prosperity and to the rights and liberties of our citizens. Investors not only read our balance sheet, but they also read our judgments.

 “That is why we continue to support initiatives that present Nigeria as a destination and business-friendly country, one that respects the rights of all who live in the land and the sanctity of the law of every contract and that the new Nigeria contracts must be sacred, not seasonal,” the President said.

 He cited the Judicial Officeholder Salary and Allowances Act 2024 as evidence of that commitment, saying it reversed over 15 years of stagnation by delivering a 300 per cent increase in the salaries of superior court judges, while acknowledging that more remained to be done.

 “We are not yet at our desired designation. But significant work is in progress, and the brighter future is now in closer view. We will be there, my Lordship.

 “Our administration respects court judgments, even the ones we do not enjoy reading. We do not denigrate, attack or intimidate the judiciary,” the President reassured.

 Chairman of Heirs Holding, Tony Elumelu, delivering the keynote address titled ‘The Rule of Law as a Catalyst for Private Sector Growth,’ reinforced Tinubu’s message, arguing that the quality of a country’s judicial system was the primary condition for attracting and retaining investment, ahead of power supply, tax incentives or regulatory frameworks.

 “Capital goes where it is safe and stays where it is respected. Before power, before rules, before tax incentives, the first condition is a court judgment that is fair, impartial and timely. We know that justice delayed is justice denied,” Elumelu stated.

 Senate President Godswill Akpabio lauded Tinubu for his commitment to justice, democracy and national development, and assured him that the National Assembly would continue to support all legal instruments that promote justice, democracy and the rule of law.

 He also commended Olanipekun for his contributions to the legal profession.

 Chief Justice of the Federation, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, praised Olanipekun for his immense contributions to the legal profession, saying the six volumes being unveiled would “further contribute to the intellectual depth, advocacy and enrichment of the nation’s jurisprudence.”

 Meanwhile, Attorney-General of the Federation and Justice Minister Prince Lateef Fagbemi also paid tribute to the celebrant, recalling several occasions they had collaborated in court.

 “As a lawyer, you don’t want to be on the opposite side of Chief Olanipekun,” he said.

 Ekiti State Governor Biodun Oyebanji eulogised Olanipekun for enriching the legal profession, saying Ekiti State was proud of him. He also commended him for his contributions to the state in education, health, human capital development and mentoring of the younger generation.

 Minister of the FCT Nyesom Wike also delivered a goodwill message.

 For his part, Olanipekun recalled his personal relationship with Tinubu over the years, commending the President for his steadfastness, advocacy for democracy and sacrifices.

 He revealed that at one such meeting, the President had taught him the difference between legal and political jurisprudence.

 The event was attended by justices of the Supreme Court and the Court of Appeal, former chief justices of the federation, former governors, members of the Federal Executive Council, traditional rulers and the governor of Ondo State.

 Also present was Israel Adeniyi, the overall best graduating student at the 2026 Call to the Bar at the Nigerian Law School, who was introduced as a panellist to the audience.

The post Tinubu confers GCON on Olanipekun appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Reps seek separate pension board for police
description:
The House of Representatives is considering a bill to exempt the Nigeria Police Force from the Contributory Pension Scheme and establish a separate pension board to manage retirement benefits for serving and retired police personnel.
 The proposed legislation, titled “A Bill for an Act to Establish
content:
The House of Representatives is considering a bill to exempt the Nigeria Police Force from the Contributory Pension Scheme and establish a separate pension board to manage retirement benefits for serving and retired police personnel.

 The proposed legislation, titled “A Bill for an Act to Establish the Nigeria Police Pension Board, to Provide for a Special Pension Scheme for Officers, Inspectors, Rank and File of the Nigeria Police Force; and for Related Matters,” seeks to create a dedicated institutional framework for the administration of police pensions and gratuities.

 Sponsored by the member representing Oshodi-Isolo II Federal Constituency of Lagos State, Jesse Onuakalusi, the bill was introduced on the floor of the Green Chamber on Wednesday and now awaits a date in the coming weeks for the debate of its general principles.

 A copy of the bill, exclusively obtained by The PUNCH, shows that the proposed Nigeria Police Pension Board would assume responsibility for “managing the pensions, gratuities and other retirement benefits of all categories of police personnel, replacing the existing arrangement under the Contributory Pension Scheme established by the Pension Reform Act, 2014.”

 Specifically, Section 6 of the bill provides that “notwithstanding the provisions of the Pension Reform Act, 2014, the Nigeria Police Force shall, from the commencement of the proposed law, be exempted from the Contributory Pension Scheme.”

 It further provides for the transfer of the accrued rights and benefits of serving police officers under the existing scheme to the new board, in accordance with regulations to be issued by the Minister of Finance.

 The bill also gives the National Pension Commission “six months from the commencement of the Act to ensure the seamless transfer of all police pension assets and liabilities to the proposed board.”

 Upon completion of the transfer, the board would assume full responsibility for the administration of all police pension matters.

 Explaining the rationale for the proposed legislation, its explanatory memorandum states that the initiative is intended to address “the peculiar, hazardous and essential nature of policing duties in Nigeria.”

 It further states that the proposed special pension arrangement would ensure “timely, dignified and adequate post-service welfare for police personnel while providing a specialised management and investment framework for the sustainability of their retirement benefits.”

 The proposed board would be headquartered in Abuja and operate as a corporate body with perpetual succession, a common seal and the legal capacity to sue and be sued in its corporate name.

 Under Section 3, its governing board would be chaired by a retired senior police officer not below the rank of Deputy Inspector-General of Police.

 Other members would include “the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Police Affairs, a representative of the Police Service Commission, the Inspector-General of Police or his representative, and representatives of the Budget Office of the Federation and the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation.”

 The governing board would also include two representatives of retired police officers, one from the senior cadre and the other from the rank and file, as well as the Executive Secretary, who would serve as the chief executive officer.

 Members of the board would be appointed by the President on the recommendation of the Minister of Police Affairs.

 In terms of its responsibilities, the proposed board would formulate policies and guidelines for police pensions and gratuities, supervise pension fund management, authorise payments to eligible retirees and conduct periodic verification of pensioners.

 It would also be empowered to enter into contracts, acquire and dispose of property, employ personnel and collaborate with relevant government agencies to improve pension administration.

 On funding, the bill provides that the board’s resources would come from “annual budgetary allocations by the Federal Government, pension funds transferred from PenCom, investment income and grants or donations approved by the government.”

 It also provides for the establishment of a dedicated Police Pension Fund Account into which appropriated funds, transferred pension rights and contributions, investment proceeds and other lawful revenues would be paid.

 The fund would be applied to the payment of pensions, gratuities and other benefits, administrative and operational expenses, staff training and welfare, as well as procurement and logistics.

 To strengthen accountability, the proposed legislation requires the board to maintain proper financial records and subject its accounts to annual audits by the Auditor-General for the Federation or an external auditor approved by the Auditor-General.

 The audited accounts and reports would be submitted to the National Assembly not later than six months after the end of each financial year.

 The board would also be required to submit an annual report to the President and the National Assembly not later than June 30, detailing its activities during the preceding year and the financial position of the Police Pension Fund.

 The proposed management structure provides for an Executive Secretary, who would serve as the board’s chief executive and accounting officer.

 The Executive Secretary would be appointed by the President on the recommendation of the Minister of Police Affairs, subject to confirmation by the Senate, for a five-year term renewable once.

 The position would be open to a retired or serving police officer not below the rank of Assistant Inspector-General of Police, or a public administrator or pension management professional with at least 20 years of relevant experience.

 The bill further provides for seven core directorates covering finance and accounts, pension administration, human resources and administration, information and communication technology, investment and treasury management, legal services and board secretariat, as well as internal audit and compliance.

 To bring pension administration closer to retirees, the proposed board would establish zonal pension offices in the six geopolitical zones of the country. The offices would coordinate pension operations, facilitate retiree verification and enrolment, and submit periodic reports to the headquarters.

 The legislation also empowers the Minister of Police Affairs, on the recommendation of the board and with the President’s approval, to make regulations necessary for its implementation.

 If passed by the National Assembly and assented to by the President, the legislation would be cited as the Nigeria Police Pension Board (Establishment) Act, 2025.

 The proposal comes against the backdrop of longstanding concerns over the welfare and retirement conditions of police personnel, particularly the need for an effective pension arrangement that recognises the peculiar demands and risks associated with policing.

 By seeking a dedicated pension institution outside the existing contributory framework, the bill proposes a fundamental restructuring of how the retirement benefits of police officers are to be administered and funded in Nigeria.

title: FG, Chinese firm sign deal on CNG buses, assembly plant
description: The Federal Government has signed an agreement with China’s Yutong Bus Company and Nigerian partner YP Automobile to introduce compressed natural gas-powered buses and establish a local assembly plant, as part of efforts to reduce transportation costs and expand vehicle manufacturing in the country.
content:
The Federal Government has signed an agreement with China’s Yutong Bus Company and Nigerian partner YP Automobile to introduce compressed natural gas-powered buses and establish a local assembly plant, as part of efforts to reduce transportation costs and expand vehicle manufacturing in the country.

 The agreement, signed in Lagos on Thursday through the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles, includes a proposed project to assemble CNG buses in Nigeria, while Leyland Nigeria is expected to host the new assembly investment.

 The project is expected to create jobs in vehicle assembly, maintenance and the supply chain, while giving Nigerian workers access to technical skills and technology used in commercial vehicle manufacturing.

 Unlike arrangements that focus mainly on importing finished buses, the new partnership is intended to develop local capacity to assemble the vehicles, although details of the plant’s investment value, construction schedule and production commencement date were not disclosed at the signing.

 Executive Chairman of Pi-CNG & EV, Barr. Ismaeel Ahmed, said the agreement was designed to combine the deployment of CNG buses with local industrial development.

 “Not only are we now bringing in the buses in huge numbers, but they are going to set up an assembly plant so that our people will get jobs and we’ll have the transfer of technology to be able to do it ourselves and within country,” he said.

 Ahmed said the partnership involved YP Automobile, which he described as having operated in Nigeria’s mass commercial transport market for at least 15 years, and Yutong, one of China’s leading bus manufacturers.

 He said Nigeria had about 210 trillion cubic feet of proven natural gas reserves, arguing that the country could use the resource to reduce its reliance on petrol in the transportation sector.

 Through the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme, the government is seeking to expand access to cheaper public transportation using natural gas and electric vehicles.

 Ahmed said the latest agreement would support that objective while creating opportunities for local manufacturing.

 Chief Operating Officer of YP Automobile, Panagiotis Marris, said the partnership brought together Nigerian investors and Yutong, which he described as the world’s largest bus producer.

 He said the arrangement could help rebuild Nigeria’s automotive manufacturing capacity and restore technical expertise that had been lost over the years.

 “It’s a milestone in a sense that we’re reviving the Nigerian manufacturing auto industry, and we’ll create the know-how that we missed over the last 20 years,” Marris said.

 He added that high transportation costs remained an obstacle to economic development, while the adoption of CNG-powered buses could also help reduce the environmental impact of public transportation.

 Yutong Bus Company Account Manager, Damian Li, said the manufacturer had delivered more than 1,400 buses to Nigeria and understood the country’s transport market and operating requirements.

 He said the company planned to work with its Nigerian partners on the local assembly of 1,000 CNG buses, with the project expected to gradually increase domestic production capacity and develop a sustainable bus industry.

 “We plan to cooperate with the local partners and to start local bus assembly project of the thousand CNG buses,” Li said.

 Chairman of Leyland Nigeria, Yemi Idowu, said the company would host the proposed assembly investment, adding that the project would create employment opportunities beyond the factory.

title: Oil, gas operators seek credit reforms to unlock investment
description:
Oil and gas operators have called for a stronger and more credible credit management system to improve access to funding, unlock investment and boost energy supply across Nigeria.
 They made the call at the National Institute of Credit Administrators’ conference in Lagos, where industry stakeholders
content:
Oil and gas operators have called for a stronger and more credible credit management system to improve access to funding, unlock investment and boost energy supply across Nigeria.

 They made the call at the National Institute of Credit Administrators’ conference in Lagos, where industry stakeholders identified inadequate access to credit, trapped receivables, weak payment structures and poor creditworthiness as major obstacles to financing projects and expanding operations across the energy value chain.

 The discussions took place during a panel session themed ‘The Energy, Oil and Gas Credit Revolution: Unlocking the Cash, Credit and Confidence to Power Nigeria’s Energy Future’, moderated by the Chief Executive Officer of BlackGold Energy Limited, Dr Oladunni Owo.

 Speaking at the session, Owo described credit as the missing link between Nigeria’s enormous energy resources and the economic benefits they should generate.

 She said that although oil and gas remain critical to the country’s foreign exchange earnings, government revenue and industrial development, operators across the sector continued to struggle with access to working capital, while distributors battled trapped receivables and consumers faced rising energy costs.

 According to her, Nigeria did not lack energy resources but lacked an effective financial bridge to convert those resources into productive economic outcomes.

 She warned that without a reliable credit management system, lenders would remain reluctant to finance projects, investors would hesitate to commit funds, and operators would find it difficult to expand their businesses.

 Owo noted that the financing challenges facing the industry have implications beyond oil and gas companies, stressing that the availability of credit ultimately affected energy affordability, industrial productivity and the welfare of ordinary Nigerians.

 She recalled spending about 15 years seeking funding for a refinery project before the emergence of the Dangote Refinery, observing that the country’s fuel supply situation could have been considerably worse without the huge investment secured for the facility.

 Owo noted that the conference was a pilot initiative ahead of a much bigger national and international summit on energy, oil and gas credit management planned for 2027.

 Speaking on how operators could improve payment cycles and restore liquidity, the Chief Operating Officer of Emadeb Energy Group, Mr Sheriff Adeeyo, identified supply chain financing as one of the most effective mechanisms for unlocking capital within the industry.

 Adeeyo explained that conventional funding arrangements had become increasingly difficult for some operators, forcing companies to explore alternative financing structures and depend more on internally generated resources to sustain and expand their businesses.

 He cited supply chain financing initiatives involving major industry players, including Renaissance Africa Energy, as examples of how contractors and vendors could access financing through their contractual relationships with oil and gas companies.

 According to him, such arrangements enabled vendors and contractors to obtain funding from commercial banks and other financial institutions using verified contracts and business transactions as the basis for financing.

 Also speaking, the Group Executive Director, Operations, Masters Energy Group, Mr Felix Eribo, said the difficulty of accessing credit was not limited to the oil and gas industry but affected businesses across different sectors of the Nigerian economy.

 Drawing from research he conducted involving 41 microfinance banks in Nigeria as part of his Doctor of Business Administration thesis, Eribo said he encountered several promising business proposals that could not secure financing because the applicants were considered insufficiently creditworthy.

 He noted that even established oil and gas companies could be denied facilities when their credit ratings failed to meet the requirements of financial institutions.

title: Only 20% of Nigeria’s 30,000 PHCs functional, family physicians raise alarm
description:
By Matthew Johnson



The Society of Family Physicians of Nigeria, SOFPON, yesterday raised the alarm over the state of primary healthcare in the country, revealing that only about 20 per cent of more than 30,000 Primary Healthcare Centres ,PHCs, nationwide are fully functional.







Vice-Presiden
content:
By Matthew Johnson

The Society of Family Physicians of Nigeria, SOFPON, yesterday raised the alarm over the state of primary healthcare in the country, revealing that only about 20 per cent of more than 30,000 Primary Healthcare Centres ,PHCs, nationwide are fully functional.

Vice-President of SOFPON, Dr Ibrahim Yakubu, who disclosed this during a press conference themed, “Primary Health Care Without Family Physicians: Can Nigeria Afford the Gap?”, will also focus on “The Double Burden of Disease and the Cost of Fragmented Care” and “The Stressed Family Physician and Continuity of Care”. on November 19th 2026 ahead of the society’s 29th Annual General and Scientific Meeting ,AGSM, said the country’s primary healthcare system was facing a serious operational crisis.

He explained that the shortage of skilled medical personnel, poor funding and increasing migration of doctors were undermining access to quality healthcare, calling on the Federal Government and state governors to urgently integrate family physicians into the leadership of primary healthcare facilities.

Yakubu who said the majority of PHCs were unable to provide essential medical services due to structural decay, inadequate funding and shortage of skilled health professionals.

According to him, the conference will develop policy and clinical recommendations on integrating specialist services into primary healthcare, improving physician welfare and retention, and developing integrated care models for infectious and chronic diseases.

He described the situation was being worsened by the increasing migration of doctors, particularly frontline medical professionals, due to poor working conditions, inadequate equipment and weak welfare structures.

He said loss or sidelining of family physicians could further weaken the country’s healthcare delivery system, particularly at the grassroots where continuous and comprehensive medical care is required.

He further explained that family physicians were specially trained to manage patients holistically, coordinate treatment and address both infectious and chronic diseases at the primary healthcare level.

Yakubu said the country’s healthcare system was battling a double burden of disease, with communicable illnesses such as malaria, tuberculosis and cholera existing alongside rising cases of non-communicable diseases, including hypertension, diabetes, kidney diseases and cancer.

He warned that the absence of coordinated healthcare services was increasing treatment costs for families and making it difficult to manage patients with multiple health conditions.

He said the society also urged governments to move beyond constructing PHC buildings to adequately equipping existing facilities and providing sufficient funding and personnel to operate them.

Yakubu added that positioning family physicians at the centre of primary healthcare would promote early detection of chronic illnesses, reduce treatment costs and ensure continuity of care.

He said: “Data shows that only about 20 per cent of the over 30,000 PHC facilities across Nigeria are fully functional, with a vast majority unable to provide essential medical services.

“The rest suffer from structural decay, severe funding deficits that fall far below the 15 per cent Abuja Declaration target, and a devastating shortage of skilled medical professionals.

“When you remove the Family Physician, the specialist trained specifically to manage multi-dimensional, continuous, and holistic patient care from the community level, you create an unfillable gap.

“We are here today to tell the government and the public that Nigeria cannot afford this gap. Fragmented care is too expensive, too dangerous, and completely unsustainable,” he said.

“The society also raised concerns over the welfare of doctors, warning that excessive patient workloads, burnout, economic pressures and security threats were affecting the quality and continuity of healthcare delivery. A single family doctor in Nigeria today routinely consults for numbers of patients that far exceed international safety standards.

“Why does the stress of a doctor matter to the average Nigerian citizen? It matters because a stressed doctor is a direct threat to the continuity of care. If we want a healthy nation, we must care for the people who care for the sick. A broken doctor cannot heal a broken healthcare system.

“Against this backdrop, SOFPON called on the Federal Ministry of Health, state governors and health sector administrators to make the integration of certified family physicians into the administrative and clinical leadership of primary healthcare authorities mandatory.

“I further called for targeted rural allowances and improved security measures for doctors working in underserved and high-risk communities.” Yakubu said.

SOFPON said the issues would form part of discussions at the 29th AGSM, where family physicians, medical scholars and policymakers would examine strategies for strengthening primary healthcare delivery.

The post Only 20% of Nigeria’s 30,000 PHCs functional, family physicians raise alarm appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Tinubu woos Yutong, targets 40% fare cut
description:
President Bola Tinubu has secured a commitment from Yutong, the world’s largest bus manufacturer, to establish a compressed natural gas bus assembly plant in Nigeria.
 The first 100 buses are expected to arrive in Lagos before the end of December 2026.
 The Special Adviser to the President on Inform
content:
President Bola Tinubu has secured a commitment from Yutong, the world’s largest bus manufacturer, to establish a compressed natural gas bus assembly plant in Nigeria.

 The first 100 buses are expected to arrive in Lagos before the end of December 2026.

 The Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, disclosed the development in a statement he signed on Thursday, titled ‘President Tinubu Moves to Cut Transport Fares as World’s Largest Bus Manufacturer, Yutong, Sets Up Assembly Plant in Nigeria.’

 “The investment will support the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme in collaboration with State Governments, which targets transport fare reductions of approximately 40 per cent on participating routes, in line with the President’s Renewed Hope Agenda 2.0 for 2027–2031,” Onanuga said.

 Under the agreement with the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles, signed in Lagos on Thursday, Yutong will supply an initial 300 CNG-powered buses.

 “Subsequent buses will be assembled in Nigeria through YP Automobiles Bus Assembly at the former Leyland Automotive plant in Ibadan, Oyo State, reviving local industrial capacity, reducing dependence on imported vehicles and creating employment opportunities for Nigerian engineers, technicians and other workers,” the statement read.

 Tinubu had personally invited Yutong to Nigeria to support the programme, as committed in the All Progressives Congress’ Renewed Hope Agenda 2.0 for 2027–2031.

 Yutong sold 49,518 buses globally in 2025 and brings a track record of supporting local assembly and mass transit projects across multiple countries.

 “Millions of Nigerians depend on commercial transportation to get to work, take their children to school, travel to markets and move goods between communities. For many households, transportation consumes a significant portion of their daily earnings,” Tinubu said, stressing that the lower operating costs of CNG-powered vehicles must translate directly into lower passenger fares.

 He added, “The success of the CNG programme must ultimately be measured by how much Nigerians save on transportation.”

 The Federal Government said it had deployed Mobile Refuelling Units and directed the installation of 2,000 additional CNG refuelling points nationwide, supported by the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund and private sector investors.

 According to the Pi-CNG & EV initiative, there are currently 105 CNG refuelling stations across 24 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

 The President welcomed Yutong’s local assembly commitment as a vehicle for technology transfer, skilled job creation and the long-term strengthening of Nigeria’s automotive industry, noting that domesticating bus production would help sustain the supply of affordable commercial vehicles and reduce dependence on imports.

 Thursday’s announcement marks the fourth consecutive year of the Tinubu administration’s initiative of deploying transport palliatives during the yuletide season, during which there is a surge in intercity travel and a hike in fares.

 In December 2023, the administration approved a 50 per cent cut in road transport fares on 22 interstate routes and free train rides for 15 days over the Christmas and New Year period.

 The Federal Government said more than 163,000 travellers benefited from the scheme.

 In December 2024, it again announced free train services nationwide for the Christmas and New Year celebrations, extending the rail relief component of the initiative.

title: NGX sheds N30bn as bearish sentiment persists
description:
Equities on the Nigerian Exchange Limited edged lower on Thursday, as market capitalisation dipped by N30bn to N161.21tn from N161.24tn at the previous close.
The All-Share Index fell 0.02 per cent to close at 248,286.56 points, down from 248,329.65 points on Wednesday, extending the market’s downwa
content:
Equities on the Nigerian Exchange Limited edged lower on Thursday, as market capitalisation dipped by N30bn to N161.21tn from N161.24tn at the previous close.

The All-Share Index fell 0.02 per cent to close at 248,286.56 points, down from 248,329.65 points on Wednesday, extending the market’s downward trend from a weekly peak of 252,809.78 points recorded on Monday.

Trading activity closed with 372.01 million shares traded in 28,429 deals, while market breadth was negative, with 26 losers against 19 gainers.

Sovereign Trust Insurance Plc led the gainers’ chart, appreciating 9.96 per cent to close at N2.76 per share from N2.51. Critical Minerals Financing Corporation Plc followed closely with a 9.94 per cent gain to close at N3.87, while Chellarams Plc advanced 9.86 per cent to settle at N11.70.

Cornerstone Insurance Plc gained 9.64 per cent to close at N4.55, Regency Alliance Insurance Plc climbed 8.45 per cent to N0.77, while Caverton Offshore Support Group Plc rose 7.14 per cent to N4.50. Other notable advancers included Honeywell Flour Mill Plc, up 6.94 per cent to N38.50; Livingtrust Mortgage Bank Plc, which gained 6.76 per cent to N3.00; and Fidelity Bank Plc, which rose 3.91 per cent to end at N23.90.

Conversely, Royal Exchange Plc topped the losers’ table, shedding 6.00 per cent to close at N0.94 from N1.00. McNichols Consolidated Plc dropped 5.05 per cent to N4.70, while International Breweries Plc declined 4.50 per cent to N9.55.

Veritas Kapital Assurance Plc slipped 4.42 per cent to N1.08, Oando Plc lost 4.17 per cent to close at N34.50, United Bank for Africa Plc fell 3.38 per cent to N38.65, and Transnational Corporation Plc dropped 3.13 per cent to N31.00.

Sectoral performance was largely positive despite the overall market dip. The NGX Insurance Index led the sectors, rising to 1,087.76 points from 1,070.05 points; the NGX Growth Index advanced to 26,766.13 points from 26,697.67 points; and the NGX Industrial Index edged up to 11,727.12 points from 11,713.46 points.

Modest gains were also recorded in the NGX Banking Index, which closed at 2,345.06 points, and the NGX Pension Index, which ended at 12,358.44 points.

On the downside, the NGX Consumer Goods Index eased to 4,012.07 points from 4,024.03 points, while the NGX Oil and Gas Index slipped to 5,713.28 points from 5,720.07 points.

In the Exchange-Traded Fund segment, Vetiva Consumer Goods ETF led three gainers with a 6.25 per cent rise to N42.50, Stanbic IBTC ETF 30 gained 3.89 per cent to N935.00, and The SIAML Pension ETF 40 added 3.63 per cent to close at N1,498.49.

Meristem Value ETF paced nine decliners in the segment, falling 8.70 per cent to N126.00, while Meristem Growth ETF lost 7.23 per cent to N115.04 and Greenwich Alpha ETF fell 3.84 per cent to N624.99. Overall, Exchange-Traded Products recorded 594 deals involving 182,609 units, while the bond market remained muted, with seven deals involving 5,670 units and no price movements.

title: ProvidusUnity Bank named best workplace for women
description:
ProvidusUnity Bank has been named the Best Place to Work for Women in Nigeria at the 2026 Great Place to Work Awards.
The financial institution also emerged as the second-best workplace nationwide in the large corporate category, according to a statement issued by the bank on Wednesday.
According to
content:
ProvidusUnity Bank has been named the Best Place to Work for Women in Nigeria at the 2026 Great Place to Work Awards.

The financial institution also emerged as the second-best workplace nationwide in the large corporate category, according to a statement issued by the bank on Wednesday.

According to the organisers, the award recognises organisations that have demonstrated a commitment to creating workplace experiences where women can thrive, lead and realise their full potential. The dual recognition highlights the bank’s investment in building a culture anchored on diversity, inclusion, equal opportunity, employee well-being and professional growth.

The latest honours add to a string of workplace accolades recorded by the lender in recent years. In 2025, the bank was named the Best Workplace in Promoting a Fun and Friendly Culture, after winning the Best Workplace in Promoting Diversity, Equity and Inclusion award consecutively in 2023 and 2024.

Commenting on the recognition, the Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of ProvidusUnity Bank, Walter Akpani, described the award as a reflection of the bank’s enduring belief that great organisations are built by empowered people.

He said, “At ProvidusUnity Bank, we believe that when people are given the right environment, opportunities, and support, they are able to achieve extraordinary results. Being recognized as the Best Place to Work for Women in Nigeria is particularly meaningful because it validates our commitment to building a workplace where talent is valued, diversity is celebrated, and everyone has an equal opportunity to succeed. This recognition belongs to every member of the ProvidusUnity family who contributes daily to our culture of excellence.”

Also speaking on the milestone, the Group Head, Human Resources, Kingsley Ogirri, noted that the award reflects years of intentional efforts to build a workplace where inclusion goes beyond policy and becomes a lived experience.

“Creating a great workplace is not an event; it is a continuous journey. We have remained deliberate about nurturing an environment where our people feel respected, supported, heard, and inspired to perform at their best. This recognition affirms that our efforts to advance inclusion, promote gender equity, and promote a strong culture of belonging are making a meaningful impact. We are grateful to our employees whose trust and engagement make this achievement possible,” Ogirri stated.

The bank noted that, as it continues its growth trajectory, the recognition validates its position that a culture anchored on people, diversity and inclusion remains a critical driver of sustainable business success.

description:

The Regional bank announced that the facility would be provided through the Nigerian Export-Import Bank (NEXIM).



“The facility will f
content:
Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

The African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) is to finance export-oriented Nigerian Small and Medium -sized Enterprises (SMEs).

The Regional bank announced that the facility would be provided through the Nigerian Export-Import Bank (NEXIM).

“The facility will finance working capital and capital expenditure for export and intra-African trade activities, with eligible businesses in fashion, film, music, design and the wider creative industries among the intended beneficiaries,” Afreximbank said in a statement issued toay.

The facility reinforces Afreximbank’s broader commitment to expanding access to finance for African SMEs and exporters, including eligible businesses in the creative economy, the institution said.

It said the agreement was signed on behalf of Afreximbank by Mrs. Kanayo Awani, Executive Vice President, Intra-African Trade and Export Development, and on behalf of NEXIM by Mr. Abba Bello, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer , at the recent CANEX event in Lagos.

“Nigeria’s SMEs and export-oriented businesses need access to finance to expand production, invest in productive capacity and compete in new markets. This US$30 million facility will enable NEXIM to provide the working capital and investment financing required to support their growth and increase Nigeria’s exports across Africa and beyond,” Mrs. Awani was quoted as saying.

“By combining NEXIM’s export-finance capabilities with Afreximbank’s trade and development mandate, we can help more Nigerian enterprises build the capacity required to participate in regional and global value chains. Eligible creative businesses will also be able to benefit from the facility, supporting CANEX’s broader objective of connecting African talent and enterprise with appropriate finance and market opportunities,” she added.

Welcoming the partnership, Mr. Abba Bello, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NEXIM said,
“We are delighted to partner with Afreximbank to expand financing opportunities for Nigerian exporters. This US$30 million facility marks an important step in our efforts to help more businesses add value locally, fulfil export orders and reach new markets across Africa and beyond. SMEs operating across the export value chain, including eligible businesses in the creative industries, will also be able to access financing through this facility. We are particularly pleased that this partnership will help more Nigerian businesses strengthen their capacity to compete in regional and global markets, supporting our country’s economic diversification.”

The Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) is Afreximbank’s flagship programme for Africa’s creative and cultural industries. It supports the development of commercially sustainable, export-ready creative businesses through access to finance, skills, markets, commercial partnerships and policy support.

CANEX WKND 2026 took place from 5 to 8 November at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Cultural & Creative Arts in Lagos. Organised by Afreximbank, hosted by the Government of Nigeria and delivered in partnership with the African Union Commission and the AfCFTA Secretariat, it brought together creatives, investors, buyers and policymakers from Africa, the Caribbean and the diaspora.

NEXIM is Nigeria’s export credit agency and is owned equally by the Ministry of Finance Incorporated and the Central Bank of Nigeria.

title: Korea sees Nigeria as gateway for K-Beauty in Africa – Deputy Head of Mission, Tak Namgung
description:
By Nkiruka Nnorom



Tak Namgung is the Deputy Head of Mission at the Korean Embassy in Abuja. He spoke to journalists on the sidelines of the Korea-Nigeria joint seminar at the Nigerian Institute of International Affairs (NIIA), Lagos.







Let us start with K-beauty. Your Ambassador spoke briefl
content:
By Nkiruka Nnorom

Tak Namgung is the Deputy Head of Mission at the Korean Embassy in Abuja. He spoke to journalists on the sidelines of the Korea-Nigeria joint seminar at the Nigerian Institute of International Affairs (NIIA), Lagos.

Let us start with K-beauty. Your Ambassador spoke briefly about collaboration in that field. He said in the short term, K-beauty in Nigeria will mainly be about trade. What does that mean in practice?

In the short term, it is about trade and expanding the market here in Nigeria.


I recently spoke with fellow Korean diplomats who came to Lagos a month ago. They are based in Gabon, Senegal and Côte d’Ivoire. We share the same goal of promoting Korean beauty products. They told me they have a very strong chain — those trading in Gabon also have a network in Côte d’Ivoire, and a very strong branch in France. They are all connected.


As some of you mentioned, the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is important. When we see its full implementation, Nigeria will be a bridge, a gateway for all products.


After speaking with my colleagues, I felt I must work harder to have a stronger market presence here in Nigeria, because they see more productivity and more profit in our neighbouring, front-running countries.


That is what the Korean Embassy is doing right now. We know consumers deserve genuine products, without counterfeits. Proper registration will help them rely on local distributors. There are strong online customers. They are the ones in desperate need, so that they can have strong confidence in great products. And that opens the way for Korean manufacturers to come to Nigeria for production.

The Ambassador also spoke about shea butter. How does that fit in?

We spoke quite a lot about shea nuts. About 40 per cent of all shea nuts are produced here in Nigeria, but only about 1 per cent of the global shea market actually comes to Nigeria.


Nigeria is heading to fill that gap. NIIA serves as a wonderful platform for such conversations. It provides the intellectual discourse between the Korean Embassy, the Korean government, and Nigerian authorities that will eventually contribute to policy, and also to the business side, for Korean business persons to come.


There is a good example. As was said during the presentation, we will have Beauty West Africa in Lagos. There will be a Korean pavilion, and we will present K-beauty products.

What would Korea gain from this collaboration?

Today we held a seminar on cultural cooperation, in collaboration with NIIA. From here, we navigated the possible cultural collaboration.


According to the data, Nigeria’s creative economy accounts for about 2.3 per cent of the GDP. Nigeria also expects, by 2030, to create 2 million jobs from the creative economy. So it gives more opportunities for Korea as well.


Korea and Nigeria already have strong collaboration. For instance, we have had two joint dramas. One in 2024, titled My Sunshine, and this year, we also have My Alien Lover. That is the outcome of the collaboration between Korea and Nigeria. It is in Korean, English and Yoruba. So it shows a clear example of how our cultural collaboration is well maintained.

Can you tell us about Korea’s cultural success and what Nigeria can learn from it?

I would say Korea and Nigeria both have their unique cultures. It is about how both countries can have the opportunity to see each other. I am not saying this as a matter of capability or something. It is just a matter of time for Nigeria to flourish when it comes to cultural expansion.


But what I would like to point out is that we need collaboration. With its unique culture, Korea also has some platforms to make use of. And Nigeria has the core culture that needs to be promoted across the world.

What key steps is the Korean government taking to strengthen its cultural relationship with Nigeria?

I would like to highlight K-beauty as one of the potential collaboration points. This November, we will have a K-beauty showcase and conference here in Lagos. And in two weeks, we will also have Beauty West Africa, also held in Lagos. We will have a Korean pavilion.


So this is the first step we would like to take for Nigerians to enjoy Korean beauty products. But we also look forward to future collaboration in the near future because Nigeria has a large share in shea nut production. I also see it as an opportunity for potential collaboration in the field of cosmetics industry.

One of the presenters mentioned cultural exchange between Korean and Nigerian artists. Is this something you are looking at?

Yes. Fortunately, we do have a platform in place. We have the Korea Cultural Centre Nigeria, which was established in 2010. Now it is 2026, so it has been working for 16, 17 years.


We also have the Korean scholarship programme, which brings an average of 10 Nigerian university students and others to Korea. And we also have the KOICA scholarship programme. KOICA is Korea’s development agency. We also have scholarships through it.


With that human exchange, we expect — and the main point is — that they do not stay in Korea after graduation. They come back to Nigeria, and with affection for Korea, they come back to Nigeria and they become at the forefront in promoting cultural collaboration between the two countries.

There is a Korean cultural centre here in Abuja. Is there a Nigerian art/cultural centre in Korea? Is it possible to have one, just like we have one here?

I don’t think there is. It is at the discretion of the Nigerian authorities. But I think at least the conditions are already in place. Having an institution is important, but I would say the ambition I see here in Nigeria and also in Korea is already well in place.


For instance, as I said during my speech, we recently had in Seoul the Seoul Africa Festival. There was a Nigerian performer who has been inspired by both Korean and Nigerian culture. He had a mixture of K-pop and Afrobeats. So, it also shows a clear example of how our culture can be assimilated and appeal to the general public in the world.

The post Korea sees Nigeria as gateway for K-Beauty in Africa – Deputy Head of Mission, Tak Namgung appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Africa must be co-investor, not aid recipient, in proposed GECF gas bank — Expert
description:
By Nkiruka Nnorom



African countries must enter the proposed Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) gas bank as co-investors and strategic partners, rather than mere aid recipients, an energy policy expert has said.







Energy policy, markets and regulation consultant, Ifey Ikoneu, made the call
content:
By Nkiruka Nnorom

African countries must enter the proposed Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) gas bank as co-investors and strategic partners, rather than mere aid recipients, an energy policy expert has said.

Energy policy, markets and regulation consultant, Ifey Ikoneu, made the call at the conclusion of the Eighth Summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) in Moscow, while assessing key directions of Russian-African energy cooperation.

Assessing the initiative to create a gas bank, Ikoneu described it as very good, but warned that its success would depend directly on a balance of interests.

“It is important that this does not become just another multilateral investment institution where Africa’s interests are not put first,” she said.

According to her, African countries should act not merely as recipients of funds, but as co-investors and full participants in strategic decision-making.

Ikoneu said the bank should not only finance export infrastructure, but also the continent’s domestic needs, including electrification, petrochemicals, fertilizer production and industrial development, even given that many such projects are traditionally considered non-bankable.

For the new structure to work effectively, she said it would need transparency, protection from political interference and coordination with the African Development Bank, Afreximbank and Africa Finance Corporation.

She stressed that the continent’s domestic needs are extremely acute despite its wealth of energy resources with more than 600 million people in sub-Saharan Africa living without access to electricity.

In this context, she said the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline — a project long stalled due to financing problems — takes on particular significance.

Ikoenu noted that launching it requires a strong institutional framework among Nigeria, Niger and Algeria. At the same time, the pipeline should serve not only as an export channel to Europe but also as a driver of industrialisation for the participating countries.

This, according to her, applies especially to Niger, which is critically dependent on imported electricity and costly diesel generators. An infrastructure union, she said, will allow the three countries to collectively defend their interests on the export market, while giving Russia the opportunity to act as a strategic partner both in the construction itself and in training the necessary personnel.

Touching on the principle of technological neutrality enshrined in the GECF Moscow Declaration, the expert called for interpreting it as broadly as possible.

“This should mean not just a choice between imported technologies, but also the freedom to develop one’s own,” she said.

Ikoneu proposed creating a joint Russian-African research and innovation centre in the gas sector, expanding scholarship programmes for African students in Russia, and more actively involving women in the energy sector.

The main priority, she said, is investment in African specialists and institutions capable of building their own industrial competencies.

She emphasised the crucial role of the GECF as a platform for South-South cooperation among developing countries, saying that the Forum gives gas producers the opportunity to coordinate actions, ensure market transparency and shape fair pricing through long-term contracts.

“A fair global gas market is not only one that guarantees supplies to consumers, but also one where resource-owning countries have a fair opportunity to benefit from them,” she explained.

She warned that the value of such collective action by developing countries is especially high against the backdrop of current geopolitics.

As the expert warned, “sanctions against one country can hit commercial agreements with another state that is not involved in the sanctions confrontation at all,” she said.

title: NDC celebrates National Chairman Zuwoghe on birthday
description:
By Henry Umoru



ABUJA — The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has congratulated its National Chairman, Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe, on his birthday, crediting him with steering the party’s growth into a national political platform within a few months of its establishment.



In a birthday statem
content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has congratulated its National Chairman, Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe, on his birthday, crediting him with steering the party’s growth into a national political platform within a few months of its establishment.

In a birthday statement issued on Thursday and signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, the party praised Zuwoghe’s leadership, describing it as characterised by wisdom, maturity and political dexterity.

The NDC said his leadership had transformed the party into a national brand, which it described as one of the fastest-growing opposition parties in Africa.

The statement read: “The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) extends warm birthday wishes and heartfelt felicitations to our indefatigable National Chairman, Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe.

“In just a few months of its establishment, he has steered the ship of the NDC with wisdom, maturity, and uncommon political dexterity, transforming it into a national brand that is the envy of many — indeed, the biggest, strongest, and fastest-growing opposition party in Africa.”

The party further described the NDC as a “political Noah’s Ark” and a safe harbour for Nigerians seeking an alternative to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

It said: “He has made the NDC a political Noah’s Ark, a safe harbour for all patriots that will rescue Nigeria from the buccaneering government of the ruling and ruinous APC.”

The party wished the chairman long life, good health, greater wisdom, strength and prosperity, expressing hope that he would witness what it described as a new Nigeria under the NDC.

It concluded: “Happy Birthday, Mr. Chairman! Happy Birthday, our Leader! Happy Birthday, our Captain!”

title: Police rescue 15 kidnapped victims in Kogi forest
description:
By Boluwaji Obahopo



LOKOJA—THE Kogi State Police Command has rescued 15 kidnapped victims from a kidnappers’ den in Magaru Forest, Kakun-Kabba, following a fierce gun battle between security operatives and the abductors.



The victims, comprising men, women and children, were rescued in the earl
content:
By Boluwaji Obahopo

LOKOJA—THE Kogi State Police Command has rescued 15 kidnapped victims from a kidnappers’ den in Magaru Forest, Kakun-Kabba, following a fierce gun battle between security operatives and the abductors.


The victims, comprising men, women and children, were rescued in the early hours of Wednesday, November 18, during an intelligence-led joint security operation involving the police, military, forest guards and local security outfits.


The Commissioner of Police, Kogi State Command, Naziru Bello Kankarofi, disclosed this on Thursday while briefing journalists at the Police Headquarters in Lokoja.


Bello Kankarofi said the operation was carried out following his directive, adding that the joint security team stormed the forest and engaged the kidnappers in a fierce gun battle.
According to him, the superior firepower of the security operatives forced the criminals to retreat, with some of them sustaining varying degrees of gunshot injuries.
He said: “During the operation, the joint team advanced into the forest and engaged the kidnappers in a fierce gun battle. The superior firepower of the security operatives forced the criminals to retreat, with some sustaining varying degrees of gunshot injuries.” The rescued victims were identified as Okuma Terlum, 47; Ojo Deborah, 23; Samuel Danjuma, three; Faith Raphael, 21; Emmanuella Raphael, three; Donald Tor, 31; Joseph Jonathan, 20; Tergu Joseph, 15; Samuel Joseph, eight; Engr. Joseph Adebija, 58; Lois Abiodun, 50; Chuks Obiakor, 45; Ola Olufemi, 58; Ankpe Godwin, 23; and Kuhwa Solomon, 25.
The police commissioner disclosed that two other female victims, identified simply as Joy and Nwakan, escaped from their abductors during the initial encounter in which the victims were kidnapped.
He further revealed that the security team came under another ambush by members of the criminal gang while conveying the rescued victims out of the forest.
“However, the operatives successfully repelled the attack and brought all 15 victims out safely.”
The victims, who reportedly endured considerable physical and psychological distress during their captivity, were subsequently debriefed and taken to St. John’s Catholic Hospital, Kabba, for medical attention.
Although no arrests had been made as of the time of the briefing, the commissioner said actionable intelligence had been generated, while investigations were ongoing to track down the fleeing kidnappers and identify their sponsors.

The post Police rescue 15 kidnapped victims in Kogi forest appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: ‘Obi Will Disgrace Him Spectacularly In Anambra,’ Momodu Dismisses Soludo’s Victory Promise For Tinubu
description: A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Dele Momodu, has dismissed Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo’s prediction that President Bola Tinubu will win the 2027 presidential election, insisting that Peter Obi will defeat the President in the state.Momodu, the Deputy Director-G
content:
A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Dele Momodu, has dismissed Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo’s prediction that President Bola Tinubu will win the 2027 presidential election, insisting that Peter Obi will defeat the President in the state.

Momodu, the Deputy Director-General of Media and Communications of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, said Obi would defeat Soludo “spectacularly” during the election.

“With due respect to Prof. (Soludo), he has joined those people I said were speaking like robots about Tinubu.

“I guarantee you that Peter Obi will disgrace him spectacularly during the election,” he said.

The former Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) presidential aspirant made the remarks on Thursday while appearing on Channels Television’s Politics Today.

Asked whether Obi could win Anambra despite Soludo and former governor Chris Ngige supporting Tinubu, and whether he had seen the crowd at the APC rally in the state, Momodu dismissed the significance of the gathering.

“It’s good to see the crowd, but I am telling you they are beginning to nauseate Nigerians, and that is why Nigerians are shouting ‘bamayi, bamayi’,” he said.

He also claimed that criticism of Tinubu was growing, with leaders increasingly expressing their dissatisfaction with the president.

On the APC’s campaign activities across the country, Momodu argued that the ruling party’s extensive mobilisation reflected its concerns about the outcome of the election.

“The only reason they are going everywhere feverishly is because they know they will lose the election. I am 66-plus. I have never seen this kind of campaign where the President is beginning to sound like an opposition leader,” he said.

Momodu also accused Tinubu of treating APC governors like “robots,” alleging that their public statements appeared coordinated.

“I monitored each of the governors. Let me tell you emphatically that they are being treated like robots. There is no question about it,” he said.

Soludo had earlier on Thursday declared that Tinubu did not need to rig the 2027 election because his administration’s performance would secure his re-election.

“To our people, this election, to the best of our knowledge, is already won and lost. The President doesn’t need to rig the election. President Tinubu doesn’t need to rig the election.

“All over the country today, in every state of Nigeria, it is President Tinubu and Shetima’s ticket versus one other party. Whereas you have some other candidates who are strong in some parts of the country but don’t exist in others,” he said at an APC presidential campaign rally in Anambra State attended by top party chieftains.

Peter Obi, who contested the 2023 presidential election on the platform of the Labour Party, won Anambra State and finished third nationally with more than six million votes.

He is battling for the nation’s top job again in 2027 under the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), and this time he is up against main contestants like Tinubu of the APC, Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), and Omoyele Sowore of the African Action Congress (AAC).
