title: Investors need swift justice, not just incentives — Elumelu
description:
The Chairman of Heirs Holdings and Transcorp Group, Tony Elumelu, has urged President Bola Tinubu to prioritise judicial reforms, warning that delayed justice and weak enforcement of contracts could discourage investment despite government incentives and economic reforms.
Nigeria continues to face c
content:
The Chairman of Heirs Holdings and Transcorp Group, Tony Elumelu, has urged President Bola Tinubu to prioritise judicial reforms, warning that delayed justice and weak enforcement of contracts could discourage investment despite government incentives and economic reforms.

Nigeria continues to face challenges with delays in commercial litigation, contract enforcement and dispute resolution, which can discourage domestic and foreign investment.

According to the World Bank’s Business Ready 2025 report, Nigeria scored 63.48 out of 100 for its commercial dispute resolution regulatory framework, 24.50 for public services and 53.80 for operational efficiency.

The findings highlight weaknesses in judicial service delivery and the gap between legal provisions and their implementation, reinforcing concerns about the speed and effectiveness of commercial justice in Nigeria.

Elumelu said investors required fair, impartial and timely judicial decisions, alongside predictable regulations and protection of contractual agreements, to commit long-term capital to Nigeria.

He made the call on Thursday in Abuja while delivering the keynote address at the WOC Justice Summit, themed “The Rule of Law as a Catalyst for Private Sector Growth and Economic Transformation.”

“Before power, before roads, before tax incentives, the first condition is a court judgment that is fair, impartial and timely,” he said.

The businessman explained that investors assessed the reliability of a country’s judicial system before committing funds, warning that uncertainty over contracts and regulatory enforcement could trigger capital flight.

“Where any of them is in doubt, capital doesn’t argue. It leaves,” he warned.

Elumelu added, “I have said it in New York, London, Paris and I’ll say it in Abuja: capital goes where it’s safe and stays where it’s respected.”

According to him, the rule of law requires contracts to remain enforceable despite changes in government, while regulations must apply equally to businesses and their competitors.

He recalled that his acquisition of a struggling bank alongside other investors in 1997 depended partly on confidence that Nigerian law would protect the transaction.

Similarly, he said investments in Transcorp, electricity generation and the oil and gas sector involved assessing the country’s judicial system alongside its economic prospects.

“That is what the rule of law, properly working, delivers: justice that is routine, not heroic and justice that is not delayed,” he said.

Elumelu commended Tinubu’s economic reforms, including petrol subsidy removal, exchange-rate unification and the enactment of tax reform laws, describing them as necessary measures to address longstanding economic distortions.

He argued that the administration inherited an economy characterised by costly subsidies, multiple exchange rates that encouraged arbitrage and a tax system that disadvantaged compliant businesses.

Acknowledging the hardship caused by the reforms, he said, “I know the cost has been borne by ordinary Nigerians, and I know you know it too.”

He maintained that discretionary subsidy allocations, opaque foreign exchange arrangements and negotiated tax obligations undermined fair competition and economic growth.

Elumelu particularly emphasised the electricity sector, arguing that transparent regulation would attract investment, improve power supply and support industries, hospitals and educational institutions.

However, he insisted that judicial delays remained a major obstacle to private sector development.

“But justice is still being delayed. Justice is still being denied,” he said.

He urged the President to extend his reform agenda to the judiciary by deploying technology and introducing measurable performance indicators for case management and dispute resolution.

“That is the reform the private sector has been waiting for, and it is the reform that will outlast all of us,” he declared.

Elumelu also urged the administration to sustain its focus on electricity, arguing that improving investor confidence and capital inflows could accelerate economic transformation.

Speaking on Africa’s relationship with Europe, he rejected the continent’s continued dependence on exporting raw materials while importing finished products.

“Africa will not be Europe’s raw-material diversification strategy. We will be an equal partner and a creator of value,” he said.

He described Africapitalism as a development philosophy that places African businesses at the centre of economic transformation, supported by credible legal institutions.

The summit also celebrated the 75th birthday and 50-year legal career of Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Chief Wole Olanipekun.

Elumelu praised Olanipekun’s contributions to the legal profession, including his service as President of the Nigerian Bar Association, Chairman of the Body of Benchers and counsel to four successive Nigerian presidents in election disputes.

He also acknowledged the unveiling of six volumes of Wole Olanipekun Through the Cases, describing the publication as a record of significant legal disputes involving power, property, elections and liberty.

“Justice and prosperity are inseparable,” Elumelu concluded.

The post Investors need swift justice, not just incentives — Elumelu appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

The boy, a pupil of a nursery and primary school in the community, reportedly l
content:
By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR

The Cross River State Police Command has arrested five persons in connection with the disappearance of a five-year-old boy in Adim community, Biase Local Government Area of the state.

The boy, a pupil of a nursery and primary school in the community, reportedly left home for school on November 16, 2026, but has not returned since then.

The Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Sunday Eitokpah, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday.

According to the statement, the boy’s father reported the disappearance at about 10:30am on November 18, after efforts by the family to trace his son proved unsuccessful.

Following the report, police operatives visited the community and commenced investigations, which led to the arrest of five suspects.

The suspects have since been transferred to the Violence Crime Response Unit (VCRU) for further investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the boy’s disappearance and determine any possible involvement of the arrested persons.

The police, however, did not disclose the identities of the suspects or the missing child, or the circumstances that led to the arrests.

The Commissioner of Police, CP Ajo Geoffrey Ordue, has directed a thorough investigation into the incident and urged the relevant investigative units to intensify efforts to establish the child’s whereabouts.

The command appealed to residents of Adim and neighbouring communities to provide credible information that could assist in locating the missing boy.

Members of the public with useful information were advised to contact the Police Control Room on 0704 177 7060 or 0705 335 5415, or report to the nearest police station.

The command reassured the family and the public of its commitment to uncovering the circumstances surrounding the disappearance and ensuring that anyone found culpable is brought to justice.

The post Five arrested over disappearance of five-year-old boy in Cross River appeared first on Vanguard News.

content:
‎….Says never before has Nigeria seen top opposition figures defying partisanship to endorse candidate of another party

…I’m still in APC – Ngige

‎

‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

‎

‎ABUJA — THE Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima, has declared that the welfare and prosperity of the South-East region have been at the forefront of President Bola Tinubu’s agenda since his first day in office.

‎

‎He said targeted federal initiatives, critical infrastructure investments and inclusive governance remain central to uplifting the region and fostering lasting prosperity across all five South-Eastern states.

‎

‎Senator Shettima, who spoke on Thursday in Awka, Anambra State, while rallying support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally, noted that he was speaking in his capacity as a titled friend of the region.

‎

‎”So, I am speaking to you today as a titled friend of the Igbo, as the Enyi Ndigbo of Anambra State, as the Enyioma Ndigbo I of Abia State, and as the Aka Ekpuchi Ọnwa I of Ebonyi State.

‎

‎”I am here to assure you that your President, our leader, His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the Eze Udo of Igboland, has made the welfare and prosperity of the South-East a top priority since the very day he was sworn into office,” he declared.

‎

‎Acknowledging that no part of Nigeria could rival the enterprise of the South-East, VP Shettima said the geopolitical zone has proven again and again that the salvation of Nigeria rests on the promise to make the nation’s economy globally competitive.

‎

‎He pointed out that while the Tinubu administration has answered the “challenge in the most eloquent way possible,” it is proudly returning to the region to share the news that the economy is growing at an unprecedented pace after a series of difficult reforms.

‎

‎Senator Shettima appealed to the people of Anambra State to re-elect President Tinubu, basing his case not only on the effectiveness of the President’s reforms, which have brought higher federal allocations to the state, but also on the argument that the Presidency cannot be won merely by reciting phony statistics about developing nations.

‎

‎His words: “So, we have come to you today to seek your support to renew our mandate. This is not only because our reforms have made more money available to Anambra State, as they have to all South-East states and to all states of the federation.

‎

‎”The road to the Presidency cannot be paved with cramming bogus statistics about Bangladesh, like someone we all know. Anambra Kwenu, we must keep this unbeatable bond alive because there is no party that offers Ndigbo a more promising road to the Presidential Villa than the APC.”

‎

‎Stating that the performance of the Tinubu administration was clearly visible, the Vice President noted that the wave of opposition leaders endorsing the President was unprecedented.

‎

‎”I know you have seen our performance for yourselves, and your Governor has never failed to acknowledge it. Never before have we witnessed, on this scale, leading figures of opposition parties defying partisan conventions to endorse the President of another party for election. This is a remarkable moment in our political history, and we do not take it for granted,” he declared.

‎

‎The VP outlined the administration’s positive impact on the South-East, highlighting the rollout of Operation UDO KA, designed to ensure Mondays are as safe as any other day and to neutralise those destroying businesses in the region.

‎

‎He also noted the rehabilitation of the First Niger Bridge, alongside ongoing work on the Anambra access-road component of the Second Niger Bridge, the Enugu–Onitsha Expressway and the Onitsha–Owerri corridor.

‎

‎Senator Shettima described Anambra State as “the home of the political giants, intellectuals, industrialists and technocrats who have defined” Nigeria’s history, recalling that the first Nigerian President, Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe, an Igbo man from Anambra, “was an enduring reminder of what happens when we collaborate to form a unified front.”

‎

‎He described the state Governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo, as a quintessential embodiment of the late Azikiwe, saying he readily calls to mind the Zik of Africa.

‎

‎”He (Soludo) is, like Zik of blessed memory, an intellectual of encyclopaedic distinction. He is, like Zik, a pan-Nigerian advocate with practical insights into the nature of power. He is, like Zik, a scholar whose work preceded his entry into elected office.

‎

‎”These two men have shown us the possibility of an enduring bridge between the Igbo and the rest of Nigerians, and we shall honour what they have sacrificed to compel us to think beyond the confines of our ethnicities, our regions, our religions, our languages and our political affiliations,” he added.

‎

‎In his remarks, APC National Chairman, Professor Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda, while praising Governor Soludo for “making a smart decision to canvass for the winning team,” said he had come to Anambra State to present the best candidate to the people: the man who knows the way in education, the economy and infrastructure, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

‎

‎Urging the people to vote for the President for continued progress, he said President Tinubu cares about education and wants every Nigerian child to be educated. He added that gone are the days when a Nigerian child who aspired to go to school could not do so because there was no money.

‎

‎Also, Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Kalu, advocated a shift from sentimental politics to strategic cooperation to drive development in Anambra State and the wider South-East.

‎

‎He argued that the success of Igbo people in business and commerce stems from strategic thinking rather than sentiment, just as he suggested that political progress requires moving away from protest-based approaches and focusing instead on strategic alliances.

‎

‎For his part, the Governor of Imo State and Chairman of the Progressive Governors Forum (PGF), Senator Hope Uzodimma, commended Governor Soludo for his wise decision to support the President, noting that the Igbo have been at the forefront of development since the end of the civil war.

‎

‎While asking the people to vote wisely on Election Day, he urged them to visit the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), describing a vote for President Tinubu as a stand for unity, progress and further development.

‎

‎Former Governor of Anambra State and immediate past Minister of Labour and Employment, Senator Chris Ngige said that people should be free to choose their preferred candidate in 2027 election.

‎

‎Ngige, who said that he still remained a member of the APC but on sabbatical, however, called on the people of the state to vote APC in all positions.

‎

‎Wrapping up, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, called for a solid national coalition, urging South-East leaders to support President Tinubu in 2027.

‎

‎He charged the region to embrace the national political coalition and move into the mainstream, emphasising that achieving the Presidency requires broad cross-regional alliances rather than isolated regional efforts.

‎

‎Senator Yari cautioned against political narratives suggesting that a single-term presidency could be achieved without broad national consensus, stressing that sustainable political power is built through partnership and inclusion.

The post ‎South-East prosperity central to Tinubu’s agenda — Shettima appeared first on Vanguard News.

By Gabriel Ewepu



ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu on Thursday reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to ending the export of unprocessed solid minerals, saying Nigeria must develop local capacity to add value to its mineral resources.







Tinub
content:
…Sector generates over N100bn in 2026 — Alake

By Gabriel Ewepu

ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu on Thursday reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to ending the export of unprocessed solid minerals, saying Nigeria must develop local capacity to add value to its mineral resources.

Tinubu stated this in his presidential keynote address at the Nigeria Now! Investing in Energy, Infrastructure and Mining Summit in Abuja, with the theme, “United Nigeria, New Horizons, One Investment Destination”. The summit ends on November 20, 2026.

The President said the mining sector required improved geological information, transparent licensing, responsible exploration and increased investment in beneficiation and processing to support local industries, create skilled jobs and deliver benefits to host communities.

He said: “In mining, we’re equally determined to move beyond the export of unprocessed resources. Better geological information, transparent licensing, responsible exploration, and greater investment in beneficiation and processing must support Nigerian industries, skilled employment and meaningful benefits for host communities.

“Our mission is to build integrated value chains in which Nigerian enterprises participate and in which domestic capabilities grow.

“We invite investors to bring technology, finance and commercial enterprise while we continue to strengthen the regulatory certainty and institutional support needed for sustainable returns.

“Opportunities are substantial, but they must be converted into well-structured bankable projects rather than remaining prospects on paper. This is why Nigeria now must distinguish itself.”

Tinubu said the government was committed to creating an investment environment that would encourage private-sector participation and support the development of integrated value chains in the mining industry.

Earlier, the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dr Dele Alake, said reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration had increased revenue from the solid minerals sector to more than N100 billion in 2026.

Alake said the sector generated about N6 billion annually when he assumed office, but revenue rose to N38 billion in 2024 and N70 billion in 2025.

He said: “When I assumed office, the sector’s total annual revenue stood at just ₦6 billion. However, through reforms, the local value addition policy, the digitisation of mining processes, and efforts to sanitise operations within the sector, that figure increased from ₦6 billion to ₦38 billion by 2024.

“By 2025, it had risen to ₦70 billion. And just about a week ago, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) informed us that we had crossed the ₦100 billion mark this year.

“All of this has been achieved through reforms, deliberate initiatives, creativity, a sense of responsibility, and the public conscience to do what is right for the people and leave a lasting legacy.”

The minister also said the establishment of the Mining Marshals had strengthened efforts to tackle illegal mining.

According to him, more than 300 suspected illegal mining operators had been apprehended, while over 100 mining sites had been recovered from illegal operators and restored to their legitimate owners.

Alake, however, alleged that some operators affected by the enforcement activities were sponsoring moves to scrap the Mining Marshals.

“As I speak, there have been moves to scrap the Mining Marshals. These moves are sponsored by the operators whom the Mining Marshals have been deployed to bring to justice,” he said.

The minister also defended the removal of fuel subsidy, arguing that the use of savings from the policy had supported infrastructure development across the country’s six geopolitical zones. He criticised calls for the restoration of the subsidy.

Meanwhile, the Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Gboyega Oyetola, said the sector had recorded progress since the ministry was established in 2023.

Oyetola listed improvements in maritime security, port reforms and the approval of Nigeria’s first National Policy on Marine and Blue Economy among the developments recorded.

He disclosed that revenue generated by agencies under the ministry increased from N700.79 billion in 2023 to N1.83 trillion in 2025.

The minister urged investors to explore opportunities in ports, shipping, shipbuilding, fisheries, aquaculture, maritime tourism and logistics.

The post Tinubu vows to end export of unprocessed solid minerals appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: 2027: PDP insists on coalition to challenge Nwifuru in Ebonyi
description:
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki



ABAKALIKI — The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Ebonyi State has insisted that a coalition of political parties and interest groups exists to challenge the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led government of Governor Francis Nwifuru in the 2027 governorship election.
content:
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

ABAKALIKI — The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Ebonyi State has insisted that a coalition of political parties and interest groups exists to challenge the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led government of Governor Francis Nwifuru in the 2027 governorship election.

The party said the APC’s claim that it was not part of any coalition did not invalidate the existence of political groups working together to challenge the incumbent administration.

The media aide to the PDP governorship candidate, Dr Ifeanyichukwu Odii, Dr Jerry Uhuo, stated this while reacting to comments by the APC campaign spokesman, Senator Emmanuel Onwe, who had alleged that no coalition existed in Ebonyi State.

Uhuo accused Onwe of misunderstanding the concept of political coalition, explaining that it involved political interest groups coming together to pursue common objectives, including electoral victory.

“From all indications, Sen. Onwe appears not to understand what coalition means in the context of the current political engineering.

“Coalition is a coming together of political interest groups to work together for the interest of promoting a common interest and winning election.

“The fact that the Ebonyi APC claims non-membership of such a coalition does not mean that the coalition does not exist in Ebonyi. He admitted that any group could come together to form a coalition. That alone contradicts his original position,” he said.

Uhuo argued that the formation of a political coalition did not require the endorsement of a state government, insisting that political parties and interest groups were free to collaborate.

He added that the PDP and other political groups were already working together to challenge the APC-led administration in the state ahead of the 2027 elections.

“In the case of Ebonyi, the PDP and other political groups are already working together to dislodge the government of Governor Francis Nwifuru,” he stated.

title: Two death-row inmates escape Kwara prison
description:
Two inmates sentenced to death have escaped from the Oke-Kura Custodial Centre in Ilorin, Kwara State, after reportedly breaking through and scaling the facility’s perimeter wall.
The escapees, identified as Segun and Abraham, were said to have exploited security lapses at the correctional facility
content:
Two inmates sentenced to death have escaped from the Oke-Kura Custodial Centre in Ilorin, Kwara State, after reportedly breaking through and scaling the facility’s perimeter wall.

The escapees, identified as Segun and Abraham, were said to have exploited security lapses at the correctional facility to make their way out in the early hours of Wednesday, prompting the authorities to launch a manhunt for their recapture.

The PUNCH gathered that Abraham was reportedly a repeat escapee, having earlier fled from the Mandala Custodial Centre before he was rearrested and transferred to Oke-Kura, where he subsequently escaped again.

Following the incident, the custodial centre was placed under heightened security, with officers reportedly put on red alert to prevent further breaches and forestall any untoward development.

Reacting to the incident while addressing journalists at the facility in Ilorin on Thursday, the Controller-General of the Nigerian Correctional Service, Sylvester Mwakuche, admitted that there were indications of negligence in the circumstances surrounding the escape.

Mwakuche, who spoke on the need to establish the level of culpability of both officers and inmates, described the incident as unfortunate and unacceptable, promising that those found responsible would face disciplinary action.

He said, “Naturally, they will face the music.”

The Controller-General disclosed that the incident had attracted the displeasure of the Minister of Interior, adding that the President would equally be unhappy with the development, considering the Federal Government’s efforts to improve the welfare of correctional officers.

“The Honourable Minister is not happy. Mr President won’t be happy. Because the President of this great nation has done a lot for staff,” he said.

He listed improved salaries, regular promotions and the payment of outstanding promotional arrears among the measures taken to enhance the welfare of personnel, stressing that officers had been warned against conduct capable of undermining security in custodial facilities.

“I’ve admonished the staff. I’ve also admonished the inmates. And I know that it will not occur again,” Mwakuche added.

He, however, assured that efforts were underway to recapture the fleeing inmates, saying the authorities had spread their dragnet to ensure their rearrest.

The Controller-General also pledged that investigations would establish the circumstances that enabled the inmates to escape and ensure that anyone found culpable was appropriately sanctioned.

The post Two death-row inmates escape Kwara prison appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

content:
NO fewer than 14 persons reportedly lost their lives in a road accident involving a DAF truck conveying 35 cattle and several passengers along Kontagora Road in Niger State.


Zagazola Makama, a counter-insurgency publication, reported that the accident occurred around 11 a.m. on November 17 near Ibeto, as the truck, with registration number Lagos AZL 267 XH, travelled from Koko Local Government Area of Kebbi State to Lagos.


“Police sources said an unidentified vehicle travelling in the same direction reportedly attempted to overtake the truck but brushed against it, causing the driver to lose control before the vehicle fell,” Makama said.


“The truck driver and 13 other occupants reportedly died at the scene.


“Those identified among the deceased included Umar, 45, the driver, from Kaoje; Anas Suleiman, 25, and Sufiyanu Suleiman, 40, both from Koko; Salim Abu Dogo, 30; Abubakar Shehu, 45; Yahaya Abubakar, 30; and Manu, 35, all from Dankigari.
“Others were Rufai Umar, 25, from Bagudo; Faruk Tudu Kaoje, 20, from Kaoje; Umar Abubakar, 30, from Saradosa; Salisu Idry, 35, from Bagodo; and Abubakar Alhaji, 25, from Kaoje.”
Police sources told Makama that relatives identified the bodies, while those claimed by their families were released for burial in accordance with Islamic rites.
The publication added that two unidentified bodies had been deposited at the mortuary of Kontagora General Hospital. “The vehicle allegedly involved in the overtaking manoeuvre was later traced to Kaboji in Magama Local Government Area and taken to the Area Command Office,” Makama said.
“However, the driver of the vehicle reportedly fled and remains at large.”
According to the publication, the Niger State Police Command said investigation was ongoing to establish the full circumstances of the accident and apprehend the fleeing driver.

The post 14 killed as truck carrying passengers, cattle crashes in Niger appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: FG issues Executive Order to end open defecation by 2030
description:
By Gabriel Ewepu



ABUJA — The Federal Government has unveiled a new Executive Order to accelerate Nigeria’s efforts to eliminate open defecation by 2030, with state and local governments urged to strengthen sanitation financing, accountability and community mobilisation.







The Open Defecation
content:
By Gabriel Ewepu

ABUJA — The Federal Government has unveiled a new Executive Order to accelerate Nigeria’s efforts to eliminate open defecation by 2030, with state and local governments urged to strengthen sanitation financing, accountability and community mobilisation.

The Open Defecation Free Nigeria by 2030 and Other Related Matters Order, 2025, was unveiled on Thursday during the commemoration of World Toilet Day and the seventh anniversary of the Clean Nigeria campaign in Abuja.

Vice President Kashim Shettima, represented by the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Delivery and Coordination in the Office of the Vice President, Akubo Adegbe, described the Executive Order as a decisive step towards translating government commitments into measurable sanitation outcomes.

Shettima said the order marked a transition from fragmented interventions to stronger coordination, measurable results and sustainable national progress.

He disclosed that since the launch of the Clean Nigeria campaign in 2019, 185 of the country’s 774 local government areas had attained Open Defecation Free (ODF) status, while Jigawa and Katsina remained the only states certified as open defecation-free.

While acknowledging the progress recorded, the Vice President said Nigeria still had considerable ground to cover, urging states yet to achieve ODF status to establish monthly and quarterly targets and make their progress publicly available.

He also warned against a reversal of gains in communities already certified as open defecation-free, stressing the need for sustained monitoring and accountability to protect existing achievements.

According to him, achieving the 2030 target would require sustainable financing, reliable data, stronger institutions, effective implementation and continuous behavioural change.

Shettima called on state and local governments to take ownership of the campaign by allocating adequate resources and strengthening sanitation institutions.

He also urged development partners, the private sector, traditional rulers, community leaders and civil society organisations to sustain their support for the initiative.

The Vice President, who chairs the Steering Committee of the Clean Nigeria Project, reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to working with subnational governments, adding that the National Economic Council would also be deployed to advance and sustain the national sanitation agenda.

Linking the campaign to this year’s World Toilet Day theme, “Sanitation and Gender Equality”, Shettima highlighted the disproportionate burden poor sanitation places on women and girls.

He said inadequate access to safe and private sanitation facilities undermined their health, security, dignity, education and participation in economic and social activities.

He therefore called for inclusive policies and investments that address the sanitation needs of women, girls, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups.

Meanwhile, the Minister of Water Resources and Sanitation, Joseph Utsev, said the Clean Nigeria campaign had evolved beyond public awareness and mobilisation into a national platform for policy coordination, institutional engagement, community participation and performance monitoring.

Utsev highlighted the revised Clean Nigeria Strategy 2025–2030, which is structured around six strategic pillars, as well as the newly introduced Clean Nigeria Real Time Monitoring and Information System, designed to improve data management, track implementation and strengthen accountability.

Reflecting on the campaign’s seven-year journey, the minister identified five critical lessons, including the need to translate political commitment into adequate financing and practical action, prevent communities from relapsing into open defecation, strengthen community ownership, adopt a multi-sectoral approach and ensure reliable data informs planning and resource allocation.

Also speaking, the Minister of Youth Development, Ayodele Olawande, said his ministry was contributing to the campaign through youth mobilisation and community advocacy.

He disclosed that more than 1,000 youth volunteers had been trained to promote sanitation awareness and behavioural change.

Olawande said pilot interventions were ongoing in Bauchi, Kaduna, Benue, Ebonyi and Oyo states, adding that young people had an important role to play in promoting gender-responsive sanitation.

He specifically emphasised menstrual hygiene education, access to safe and private toilet facilities and the need to eliminate the stigma associated with menstruation.

Goodwill messages were also delivered by the former Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, Didi Esther Walson-Jack, alongside representatives of civil society organisations, professional bodies and development partners, who reaffirmed the importance of collective action in achieving Nigeria’s 2030 open defecation elimination target.

The post FG issues Executive Order to end open defecation by 2030 appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Shettima, Issoufou reflect on Buhari’s legacy at biography launch
description: ‎–Late ex-President demonstrated leadership defined by character, not power –VP‎–As Issoufou urges balanced assessment of Buhari’s achievements, controversies‎‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru‎‎ABUJA — THE Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima and former President of Niger Republic, Mahamadou Issoufou, yest
content:
‎–Late ex-President demonstrated leadership defined by character, not power –VP
‎–As Issoufou urges balanced assessment of Buhari’s achievements, controversies
‎
‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
‎
‎ABUJA — THE Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima and former President of Niger Republic, Mahamadou Issoufou, yesterday reflected on the legacy of the late former Nigerian leader, Muhammadu Buhari, describing his life and political career as an important chapter in Nigeria’s history that offers enduring lessons on leadership, character and public accountability.
‎
While Shettima said Buhari demonstrated that the true measure of leadership lies in personal character rather than the power and privileges of public office, Issoufou urged Nigerians to assess the former President’s legacy objectively, taking into account his achievements, decisions and controversies.
‎
‎The two leaders spoke at the public presentation of “Muhammadu Buhari: The Authorised Biography”, a three-volume account of the former President’s life and political career, held at the Nigerian Army Conference Centre and Suites, Abuja.
‎
‎The Vice President, who was represented by the Special Adviser to the President on General Duties, Office of the Vice President, Dr Aliyu Modibbo, said Buhari’s modest lifestyle, personal discipline and devotion to national service distinguished him from many political leaders.
‎
‎Speaking on the theme, “The Life We Leave to History”, the Vice President recalled lessons from his personal relationship with the late President, particularly his indifference to material possessions and commitment to Nigeria.
‎
‎”He taught me that the dignity of office depends upon the character of its occupant. He also taught me that a leader’s example continues to speak long after he is out of service,” Shettima said.
‎
‎He described Buhari’s Spartan lifestyle as remarkable in a political environment where public office is sometimes pursued to satisfy private interests.
‎
‎”His Spartan lifestyle distinguished him in a world where too many seek public office to satisfy private appetites. There was something arresting about a man who could command so much and desire so little,” he stated.
‎
‎Shettima noted that Buhari’s political journey, spanning military leadership and democratic governance, attracted both extraordinary public affection and strong criticism over his policies and decisions.
‎
‎He, however, said the former President’s enduring connection with millions of Nigerians reflected a distinctive leadership disposition that defied conventional political calculations.
‎
‎Beyond the tribute, the Vice President described the biography as an important contribution to historical documentation, institutional memory and public accountability.
‎
‎He urged serving public officials to preserve records of their decisions and explain the circumstances surrounding them, warning that failure to do so could leave future generations vulnerable to speculation and distorted accounts of national events.
‎
‎”The privilege of serving a nation includes the obligation of explanation. History becomes poorer whenever those who could have supplied its evidence leave it with unanswered questions,” he said.
‎
‎Shettima commended Buhari for authorising the biographical project during his lifetime and participating in the research, noting that his recollections, alongside interviews and documentary evidence, would enrich the historical record.
‎
‎In his remarks, Issoufou, who chaired the occasion, said the publication provided an opportunity to move beyond mourning and subject Buhari’s life and leadership to objective historical reflection.
‎
‎He described the three-volume work as a significant contribution to Nigeria’s historical record, particularly for younger generations who did not have personal encounters with the former President.
‎
‎”Today, in presenting these volumes, we move from mourning to historical reflection. Mourning belongs first to the family, friends and contemporaries. History belongs to everyone, including generations that never knew the man,” he said.
‎
‎Issoufou cautioned against presenting Buhari’s legacy in absolute terms, insisting that a fair historical assessment must accommodate both his accomplishments and shortcomings.
‎
‎”None of us can claim to have the final word on Muhammadu Buhari. Nor should any biography pretend to do so,” he added.
‎
‎Former Senate President Anyim Pius Anyim, who represented former President Goodluck Jonathan, also recalled Buhari’s commitment to personal relationships, describing it as an important aspect of his character that deserved recognition.
‎
‎Earlier, the author, Dr Udu Yakubu, said the three-volume biography was the culmination of more than two and a half years of research, interviews and documentation.
‎
‎He acknowledged Buhari’s cooperation throughout the process, noting that the former President granted him access to relevant information without compromising his independence as a researcher.
‎
‎”He gave the work the legitimacy of access without taking away my independence of judgement. I regret that he did not live to see these works completed, but the record now carries his voice,” Yakubu said.
‎
‎Reviewing the first volume, “Buhari: The Phenomenon”, Ambassador Dr Chijioke Wigwe described it as an authoritative account of the former President’s life, containing some of his final substantial recorded reflections.
‎
‎He traced Buhari’s journey from his upbringing in Daura, Katsina State, through his military career and appointment as Federal Commissioner for Petroleum Resources to his emergence as Head of State and eventual return to farming after leaving office.
‎
‎Wigwe observed that Buhari’s firm and uncompromising disposition shaped his leadership and influenced the circumstances surrounding his removal from power.
‎
‎He said the biography offered an opportunity to examine Buhari’s character and place in Nigeria’s history without sentiment or prejudice.
‎
‎”History must neither flatter nor condemn blindly but must examine dispassionately the human being whose life became part of the Nigerian story,” he said.
‎
‎Also reviewing the second and third volumes, The Presidency and “The Reckoning”, Ambassador Professor Tijjani Muhammad-Bande identified institutional discipline, accountability and national unity as defining features of Buhari’s leadership.
‎
‎He recalled the former President’s insistence that public funds spent on government projects must translate into tangible results, as well as his respect for institutional procedures and the constitutional tenure of public officeholders.
‎
‎Muhammad-Bande further described Buhari as a committed believer in Nigeria’s unity who opposed violent attempts to undermine the country’s territorial integrity.
‎
‎He said Buhari recognised the constitutional right to peaceful protest but maintained a firm position against taking up arms against the Nigerian state, regarding national unity as a responsibility that transcended ethnic, religious and political divisions.
‎
‎The three-volume biography examines Buhari’s personal background, military career, political journey and eight-year presidency, providing a historical account of a leader whose legacy continues to attract debate across Nigeria.

The post Shettima, Issoufou reflect on Buhari’s legacy at biography launch appeared first on Vanguard News.

content:

‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

‎ABUJA — ​PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has congratulated former President Goodluck Ebele Jonathan on his 69th birthday.
‎
‎​The President celebrated Dr Jonathan’s distinguished leadership and enduring contributions to Nigeria’s democratic development.
‎
‎​President Tinubu described Dr Jonathan as a patriot and statesman whose commitment to national unity, democratic governance, and Nigeria’s peaceful advancement remains an important part of the country’s political history.
‎
‎He ​acknowledged the former leader’s years of dedicated service to the nation—first as Deputy Governor and Governor of Bayelsa State, then as Vice President, and ultimately as President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.
‎
‎​President Tinubu also commended the former President’s continued engagement in promoting peace, democratic values, conflict resolution, and good governance across Africa and beyond, particularly through his international peacebuilding and mediation efforts.
‎
‎​As Dr Jonathan celebrates this special occasion, President Tinubu wished him continued good health, renewed strength, wisdom, and many more years of meaningful service to Nigeria, Africa, and humanity.

title: Tinubu targets 40% transport fare cut as Yutong plans Nigeria plant
description:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru



ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has welcomed plans by Yutong, the world’s largest bus manufacturer, to establish a bus assembly plant in Nigeria as part of efforts to reduce transportation costs and expand affordable mass transit across the country.



The proposed investment
content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has welcomed plans by Yutong, the world’s largest bus manufacturer, to establish a bus assembly plant in Nigeria as part of efforts to reduce transportation costs and expand affordable mass transit across the country.

The proposed investment is expected to support the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme (NACTP), which targets a reduction of about 40 per cent in transport fares on participating routes in collaboration with state governments.

Under an agreement with the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles (Pi-CNG & EV), Yutong will supply an initial 300 compressed natural gas (CNG)-powered buses, with the first batch of 100 expected to arrive in Lagos by the end of December 2026.

The remaining buses will be assembled locally through YP Automobiles Bus Assembly at the former Leyland Automotive plant in Ibadan, Oyo State.

The arrangement is expected to revive local automotive manufacturing capacity, reduce dependence on imported vehicles and create employment opportunities for Nigerian engineers, technicians and other workers.

Yutong, which sold 49,518 buses globally in 2025, has operations across several international markets and experience in supporting local assembly and public transportation projects.

According to a statement by the President’s spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, Tinubu said the investment came amid increasing adoption of CNG vehicles nationwide, supported by the expansion of refuelling infrastructure through Pi-CNG & EV, the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund and private sector investors.

The statement said the interventions included the deployment of Mobile Refuelling Units and the President’s directive for the provision of 1,000 additional CNG refuelling infrastructure units nationwide.

Tinubu said reducing the daily cost of transportation remained the central objective of the investments, noting that millions of Nigerians relied on commercial transport to commute to work, take their children to school, access markets and move goods.

He said transportation consumed a significant portion of the daily earnings of many households, stressing that the lower operating costs of CNG-powered vehicles must translate into reduced fares for passengers.

According to the statement, the President reiterated the approximately 40 per cent fare-reduction target under the NACTP, as outlined in his Renewed Hope Agenda 2.0 for 2027–2031.

He also pledged his administration’s commitment to working with state governments and transport operators to extend affordable CNG-powered transportation to more routes nationwide.

Tinubu welcomed Yutong’s decision to establish local assembly capacity, saying the investment would support the sustained supply of commercial buses, facilitate technology transfer, create skilled employment and strengthen Nigeria’s automotive industry.

He said the success of the CNG programme would ultimately be measured by the amount Nigerians saved on transportation.

The agreement between the parties is scheduled to be signed in Lagos on Thursday.

The post Tinubu targets 40% transport fare cut as Yutong plans Nigeria plant appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: 2027: Inuwa leads APC campaign train through Kaltungo West
description:
By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe



KALTUNGO — Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has led the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign train through the four wards in Kaltungo West constituency, with party leaders expressing confidence in the party’s victory in the 2027 general elections.



Thousan
content:
By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe

KALTUNGO — Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has led the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign train through the four wards in Kaltungo West constituency, with party leaders expressing confidence in the party’s victory in the 2027 general elections.

Thousands of party supporters, faithful and residents turned out to welcome the governor and other APC chieftains during the campaign rallies, which covered Kaltungo East, Kaltungo West, Toungo and Ture wards.

The rallies attracted large crowds of men, women and youths, with social and commercial activities temporarily disrupted as residents gathered to receive the campaign train.

The campaign provided an opportunity for APC candidates and leaders to highlight the achievements of the Inuwa Yahaya administration, showcase ongoing development projects and solicit support ahead of the 2027 elections.

Addressing supporters, Yahaya said his administration had demonstrated its commitment to improving the living conditions of residents through development projects across Kaltungo Local Government Area and other parts of the state.

He said the APC-led administration remained committed to people-oriented governance, infrastructure development and the provision of essential services.

The governor urged residents, particularly youths, to mobilise for the elections and vote for President Bola Tinubu and all APC candidates, stressing the need for continuity and consolidation of achievements at the federal and state levels.

The APC governorship candidate, Dr Jamil Isyaku Gwamna, described Kaltungo as a strategic constituency in the political development of Gombe State.

He urged residents to sustain their confidence in the APC and support its candidates before, during and after the elections.

Similarly, the APC senatorial candidate for Gombe South, Hon. Jerry Joseph Damara, said the administrations of Tinubu and Yahaya had initiated and executed projects with significant impacts across the senatorial district.

Damara appealed to the electorate to reciprocate the efforts of both administrations by voting for the APC, arguing that continued support would create opportunities for more development interventions.

The APC candidate for Kaltungo/Shongom Federal Constituency, Hon. Binta Bello, commended Yahaya for facilitating the establishment of federal institutions in Kaltungo and implementing projects aimed at improving the socio-economic well-being of residents.

She urged the electorate to support all APC candidates in the 2027 elections.

Also speaking, the APC candidate for Kaltungo East State Constituency, Gabriel Galadima, described Yahaya as a worthy ambassador of Kaltungo, saying the administration’s development interventions demonstrated its commitment to the area’s growth.

Earlier, the Chairman of Kaltungo Local Government Area, Hon. Silas Paris, commended the governor for attracting federal government presence to the area and facilitating improvements in infrastructure, education and healthcare delivery.

Paris assured the governor and the APC governorship candidate of the council’s readiness to mobilise support for the party, expressing confidence in its electoral prospects.

Former Senator Joshua Lidani and the Commissioner for Information and Strategy, Ambassador Moses Kyari Bolda, also expressed optimism about the APC’s chances in the 2027 elections.

They described the reception accorded the campaign train as evidence of the party’s acceptance in the constituency and pledged continued support for the governor and other party leaders.

The post 2027: Inuwa leads APC campaign train through Kaltungo West appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Enugu construction magnate, Festus Oshaba, reportedly dies in crash
description:
By Chinedu Adonu







Enugu-based industrialist and construction magnate, High Chief Festus Oshaba Onuh, popularly known as Ferotex, has reportedly died in a road accident along the Enugu-Port Harcourt Expressway.







Oshaba, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Ferorex Construction Company,
content:
By Chinedu Adonu

Enugu-based industrialist and construction magnate, High Chief Festus Oshaba Onuh, popularly known as Ferotex, has reportedly died in a road accident along the Enugu-Port Harcourt Expressway.

Oshaba, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Ferorex Construction Company, was reportedly returning to Enugu from Port Harcourt on Thursday when the accident occurred.

Sources said the vehicle conveying the businessman was involved in a collision with a truck, leaving it severely damaged.

A video circulating on social media showed the wreckage of the vehicle, with a person believed to have survived the crash heard crying.

A social media activist, Chininkem Ugwuanyi, also raised the alarm over the incident in a Facebook post.

Describing the reported death as a monumental loss, Ugwuanyi wrote: “Sun Set At Noon…

“The ghastly motor accident that killed Mambule, also known as Oshobaba, along Enugu/Port Harcourt Express Road this morning.

“The richest man from Nsukka zone was travelling back home to Enugu State this morning when this happened.

“This is a total loss for the whole world.”

However, details of the accident, including the number of casualties and the circumstances surrounding the collision, remained unclear as of the time of filing this report.

There was also no official confirmation of Oshaba’s reported death as of the time of filing this report.

The post Enugu construction magnate, Festus Oshaba, reportedly dies in crash appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: I told Peter Obi to support Atiku — Dele Momodu
description:
A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress, Dele Momodu, has disclosed that he advised the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, to support former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar ahead of the 2027 presidential election.
Momodu, however, said Obi rejected the suggest
content:
A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress, Dele Momodu, has disclosed that he advised the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, to support former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

Momodu, however, said Obi rejected the suggestion, insisting on running independently.

The publisher of Ovation International made this known on Thursday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he discussed the opposition’s chances in the 2027 election.

Asked whether he considered Atiku ahead of Obi in the presidential race, Momodu said there was no doubt about the former vice-president’s standing, describing him as a politician with national and international appeal.

“There is no question about that. I’ve told Obi to his face. He’s my friend, and I like him,” he said.

Momodu added, “I told him that he should support Atiku, but he said no, he will run it alone, and that’s okay. It’s a fair deal. I have nothing against him.

“Because Obi’s supporters think that the margin and the kind of support that Obi has is unassailable, and Atiku cannot even match it. In the coming days and weeks, we shall see.”

Momodu’s comments come as candidates intensify their campaigns ahead of the 2027 general election, with Atiku and Obi having previously been part of the same opposition coalition under the ADC.

The two politicians were among prominent opposition figures who adopted the ADC as their platform in July 2025, in a move aimed at building a coalition to challenge the ruling All Progressives Congress and President Bola Tinubu, who is seeking a second term.

Obi joined the ADC in December 2025, while Atiku had officially joined the party in November of the same year.

However, their stay in the party together was short-lived as Obi announced his departure from the ADC on May 3, 2026, citing internal crises, court cases and divisions within the party.

He subsequently joined the Nigeria Democratic Congress alongside former Kano State Governor, Rabiu Kwankwaso.

Atiku remained with the ADC and emerged as its presidential candidate for the 2027 election.

The relationship between Atiku and Obi also dates back to the 2019 presidential election, when Atiku, then the presidential candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party, chose Obi as his running mate.

Momodu had previously expressed support for a joint Atiku-Obi ticket in the 2027 election, arguing that their political experience and existing support bases could strengthen the opposition’s chances.

In April 2026, he said he would pair Atiku with Obi if given the opportunity, noting that the two politicians had worked together during the 2019 election.

The post I told Peter Obi to support Atiku — Dele Momodu appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

description: Social media personality Ademola Abiodun, popularly known as DJ Chicken, has appealed to President Bola Tinubu’s son, Seyi Tinubu, to forgive him over a social media publication interpreted as a threat to his life, offering to support the President’s political aspirations ahead of the 2027 election.
content:
Social media personality Ademola Abiodun, popularly known as DJ Chicken, has appealed to President Bola Tinubu’s son, Seyi Tinubu, to forgive him over a social media publication interpreted as a threat to his life, offering to support the President’s political aspirations ahead of the 2027 election.

The appeal was contained in a letter dated November 9, 2026, written by his lawyers, Whitehouse Legal, and addressed to Seyi, who is the patron of the City Boy Movement.

The letter, titled ‘Formal Representation and Appeal for Amicable Settlement, Reconciliation and Withdrawal of Further Prosecution Against Mr Ademola Abiodun (aka DJ Chicken)’, was signed by Rotimi Stephen and Adeniyi Falade, both of Whitehouse Legal.

Rotimi shared a copy of the letter on his Instagram page on Thursday.

In the letter, the lawyers said their client wanted to put the incident behind him and pursue an amicable resolution.

“Our Client has instructed us to communicate his sincere desire to put this unfortunate episode behind him and pursue an amicable resolution with Your Excellency,” the letter read.

The lawyers added that DJ Chicken “harbours no personal animosity, hostility or ill will” towards Seyi and had no intention of engaging in further conduct that could be considered antagonistic or disrespectful.

They said the content creator was also willing to redirect his social media influence towards youth mobilisation and the promotion of the President’s political aspirations.

“He has specifically indicated his commitment to supporting and campaigning for your father’s political aspirations through his social media platforms, using the visibility and audience he has cultivated over the years to encourage political participation and promote the Renewed Hope Agenda,” the lawyers stated.

The legal representatives said their client regretted the publication and was prepared to give an undertaking to demonstrate his commitment to responsible conduct.

“Our Client also uses this medium to tender an unreserved apology to Your Excellency and hereby gives an undertaking as may be considered appropriate to assure Your Excellency of his commitment to responsible conduct going forward,” they added.

The lawyers disclosed that the police and prosecuting authorities had indicated their readiness to consider withdrawing or discontinuing further proceedings if Seyi communicated that he had no further interest in pursuing the matter.

“From our engagements and understanding of the position communicated in relation to this matter, the police/prosecuting authorities have indicated their readiness to consider the withdrawal or discontinuance of further proceedings, provided there is a clear indication that Your Excellency, as the person directly concerned by the alleged publication, has no further interest in pursuing the matter and is favourably disposed towards an amicable settlement,” the letter read.

They explained that the outstanding issue was obtaining Seyi’s position on the proposed reconciliation, adding that his response would enable the relevant authorities to consider the necessary legal steps.

“For the avoidance of doubt, we recognise that the ultimate decision concerning the continuation or discontinuance of criminal proceedings rests with the appropriate prosecuting authority in accordance with the law and subject to the jurisdiction of the Honourable Court,” the lawyers stated.

They appealed to Seyi to communicate his willingness to settle the matter and facilitate the issuance of a formal letter conveying his position to the prosecuting authorities.

The lawyers also urged him to allow the leadership of the City Boy Movement to facilitate the communication, if necessary, ahead of the next court sitting.

According to the letter, the case had been adjourned until December 8, 2026, for a report of settlement.

Making a case for reconciliation, the lawyers said their client had already faced the consequences of the incident through his arrest, detention, arraignment and subsequent remand.

They added that the experience had made him appreciate the responsibilities associated with his influence as a social media personality.

“Our Client has also been made to appreciate the seriousness of public statements and the responsibilities that accompany the influence enjoyed by persons within the entertainment and social media industry,” they said.

The lawyers further argued that an amicable resolution would promote responsible public engagement and constructive youth participation.

“We respectfully submit that an opportunity for reconciliation at this stage would serve the broader interest of peace, responsible public engagement and constructive youth participation,” the letter added.

They, however, acknowledged that public figures were entitled to legal protection against threats and harassment, stressing that their appeal was not intended to undermine those rights.

PUNCH Online reports that DJ Chicken was arrested in July 2026 following a social media video in which he made comments about Seyi while discussing the 2027 presidential election.

He was subsequently arraigned before a Magistrate’s Court sitting in the Ogba area of Lagos State on a three-count charge bordering on alleged threat to life, offensive online publication, and conduct likely to cause a breach of the peace.

He pleaded not guilty to the charges, while the court granted him bail in the sum of N1m with two sureties in like sum. He was remanded at the Kirikiri Correctional Centre pending the perfection of his bail conditions.

He was later released after meeting the bail conditions. https://punchng.com/just-in-dj-chicken-released-from-detention/?amp

Following his release, DJ Chicken publicly thanked Seyi and the President, describing the President’s son as his “daddy” in a social media post. He also adopted Seyi’s photograph as his Instagram profile picture.

The post DJ Chicken apologises to Seyi Tinubu, pledges to campaign for Tinubu appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Court bars Jimmy Odukoya from posing as Senior Pastor of Fountain of Life Church
description:
The Lagos State High Court has issued an order restraining popular pastor and actor, Jimmy Odukoya, from presenting himself as the senior pastor of the Fountain of Life Church in Lagos.
The order was granted on Wednesday by Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin following a lawsuit filed by the incorporated tr
content:
The Lagos State High Court has issued an order restraining popular pastor and actor, Jimmy Odukoya, from presenting himself as the senior pastor of the Fountain of Life Church in Lagos.

The order was granted on Wednesday by Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin following a lawsuit filed by the incorporated trustees of the church.

The church, through its legal action, requested a “pre-emptive order of injunction” to stop Odukoya from parading himself as its senior pastor and spiritual head.

The court’s decision comes amid a legal dispute over the leadership of the Lagos-based church.

The church’s trustees argued that Jimmy “ceased to hold the office based on the appointment of a successor by the late Founder and Senior Pastor of the Church, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya”.

“A Pre-emptive Order of Injunction restraining the Respondent, whether acting personally or through any proxies in any alleged capacity as the Senior Pastor of the Church from interfering, disrupting, meddling with and or obstructing the activities, governance and any other business of the Church pending the Applicant’s full compliance with the High Court of Lagos State (Expeditious Disposal of Civil Cases) Practice Directions No. 2 of 2019 on Pre-action Protocol,” part of the suit reads.

The judge granted the order sought by the claimant.

Adewunmi-Oshin asked the claimant to serve the originating processes on the respondents.

“Leave is hereby granted to the Applicant to commence this action under the Pre-Action Protocol pursuant to Paragraph 4 of the High Court of Lagos State (Expeditious Disposal of Civil Cases) Practice Direction No. 2 of 2019,” she ruled

“The originating processes together with accompanying documents, shall be served on the Respondents forthwith.

“The Respondents shall file their Response in accordance with the timelines stipulated under the Practice Direction.

“This Order is made ex-parte and without prejudice to the right of the Respondents to apply to set it aside, or to respond fully to the substantive claims, upon being served.

“That the Respondent, whether acting personally or through any proxies is hereby restrained from holding himself out as the Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of the Fountain of Life Church (the “Church”) having ceased to hold the office based on the appointment of a successor by the late Founder and Senior Pastor of the Church, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution of the Church pending the Applicant’s full compliance with the High Court of Lagos State (Expeditious Disposal of Civil Cases) Practice Directions No. 2 of 2019 on Pre-action Protocol.”

The case was adjourned until December 1, 2026.

BACK STORY
On Tuesday, the church’s board of trustees removed Jimmy as senior pastor, saying his appointment was contrary to the wishes of his late father, Taiwo Odukoya, founder of the church.

The board of trustees said the decision followed a careful review of the church’s constitution and Taiwo’s recorded instructions before his death in 2023.

The board said it recently discovered a video recording of the late founder made in December 2021 in which Taiwo had left succession instructions.

The board said the video was not presented it before Jimmy’s appointment, which it described as wrongful.

Shortly after the board’s statement, Jimmy rejected his removal, saying it was not a constitutionally valid decision of the church’s board.

He said the board members behind the statement had been instructed since March 2026 to resign “on account of their repeated and flagrant violations of the Church’s Constitution and its founding principles and objectives”.

The board, however, maintained its position, insisting that Jimmy had ceased to be the church’s senior pastor.

The board said it had resolved to entrust the church’s interim spiritual and administrative leadership to Rotimi Okpaise, a pastor in the church.

Jimmy was named senior pastor in September 2023 following the death of his father, Taiwo.

The post Court bars Jimmy Odukoya from posing as Senior Pastor of Fountain of Life Church appeared first on Very Nigerian.

content:
A prominent Enugu businessman and Chief Executive Officer of Ferotex Group, Chief Festus Oshaba-Onuh, has reportedly died following a fatal road accident.

Oshaba-Onuh, popularly known as Ferotex or Oshobaba, was said to have died on Thursday morning in an accident along the Enugu-Port Harcourt Expressway.

The news of his reported death emerged after an Enugu-based social media influencer, Chijinkem Ugwuanyi, shared a video showing the scene of the accident on his Facebook page.

However, further details surrounding the circumstances of the crash and the businessman’s reported death had yet to be made public.

Ugwuanyi, while expressing grief over the incident, said the businessman was travelling back to Enugu State when the accident occurred.

Describing his death as a major loss, the influencer wrote: “Sun Set At Noon…

“The fatal motor accident that killed Oshaba-Onuh, also known as Oshobaba, along Enugu/Port Harcourt Express road this morning.

“The richest man from Nsukka zone was travelling back home to Enugu State this morning when this happened.

“This is a total loss for the whole world.”

Oshaba-Onuh was regarded as one of the prominent businessmen from the Nsukka area of Enugu State.

In January 2026, the billionaire buried his mother-in-law, the late Mrs Susan Oyibo Ugwu.

His death is expected to generate reactions from associates, business partners and residents of Enugu State.

title: S’West pensioners urge Tinubu to fulfil N25,000 monthly support
description:
The Nigeria Union of Pensioners, South-West Zone, on Thursday appealed to President Bola Tinubu to extend the N70,000 palliative payment to retirees and fulfil the Federal Government’s promise of N25,000 monthly support for vulnerable pensioners for three months.
The union also urged the President t
content:
The Nigeria Union of Pensioners, South-West Zone, on Thursday appealed to President Bola Tinubu to extend the N70,000 palliative payment to retirees and fulfil the Federal Government’s promise of N25,000 monthly support for vulnerable pensioners for three months.

The union also urged the President to intervene in the plight of pensioners in Oyo State-owned institutions, alleging that some retirees had not received their pensions since August 2026.

The demands were contained in a communique read by the Oyo State NUP Secretary, Olusegun Abatan, at the end of the union’s two-day meeting held in Ibadan, the state capital,

The union acknowledged the efforts of governors in the Southwest towards clearing outstanding gratuities and pension arrears but lamented that many retirees were still awaiting their entitlements, with some dating back to 2015 and 2016.

“We acknowledge the efforts of governments in the Southwest to address outstanding gratuities and pension arrears. However, many of our members are still waiting for their entitlements, some of which date back to 2015 and 2016. We appeal for more decisive action to ensure that all outstanding payments are cleared and pensioners can live with dignity,” the union said.

It particularly commended Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, and his Oyo State counterpart, Seyi Makinde, for their interventions in addressing pensioners’ welfare.

The union said Makinde committed N6 billion monthly to clearing gratuity arrears inherited from previous administrations and had promised to settle outstanding pension and gratuity liabilities by May 28, 2027.

It appealed to the governor to intervene in the plight of workers and pensioners in an Oyo State-owned institution, alleging that some workers were owed salaries while pensioners had not received payments since August.

The pensioners also expressed concern over outstanding gratuities in Lagos State, clarifying that the reported N13bn payment to retirees was largely for those under the Contributory Pension Scheme, while those under the Defined Benefit Scheme were yet to benefit from the arrangement.

The union recalled that the government promised vulnerable pensioners N25,000 monthly for three months during the 2024 minimum wage negotiations but had yet to fulfil the commitment.

It also faulted the exclusion of pensioners from the N70,000 palliative payment negotiated between the Federal Government and the Nigeria Labour Congress, urging Tinubu to extend the benefit to retirees.

“We appeal to Mr President to address the issue of the N25,000 for three months for vulnerable pensioners and also extend the N70,000 payment across the board to pensioners,” the union said.

The union further faulted a recent circular by the National Pension Commission reportedly fixing N52,500 as the minimum pension under the Contributory Pension Scheme, describing the arrangement as discriminatory against retirees under the Defined Benefit Scheme.

It argued that pensioners under the Public Service Defined Benefit Scheme, including those with federal entitlements, should also benefit from the minimum pension arrangement.

Illustrating what it described as the inadequacy of the amount, the union said a pensioner supporting a family of four would have just N13,125 per person monthly, questioning whether such an amount could meet basic needs amid rising living costs.

The pensioners also urged their members to avoid political violence ahead of forthcoming 2027 elections, stressing that the union was non-political, non-religious and non-ethnic.

Condemning the killings during the recent Osun State election, which it put at about 39, the union warned members against allowing politicians to use them to perpetrate violence.

“Take their money and vote your conscience. But don’t cause any harm. Don’t kill anybody because of anybody,” it advised.

The union said it would continue to engage with whichever government was in power while advocating improved welfare and the payment of outstanding entitlements to retirees.

The post S’West pensioners urge Tinubu to fulfil N25,000 monthly support appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Ogun students protest ASUP strike, seek gov’s intervention
description: Students of polytechnics across Ogun State on Thursday staged a peaceful protest, mounting fresh pressure on Governor Dapo Abiodun to urgently resolve the lingering industrial dispute between the state government and the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics, which has kept students away from their c
content:
Students of polytechnics across Ogun State on Thursday staged a peaceful protest, mounting fresh pressure on Governor Dapo Abiodun to urgently resolve the lingering industrial dispute between the state government and the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics, which has kept students away from their classrooms for about 10 days.

The protest, organised under the auspices of the National Association of Polytechnic Students, followed what the students described as the government’s failure to respond decisively to repeated appeals and ultimatums issued to secure the reopening of their institutions.

The students, who marched in their hundreds to the Governor’s Office, Oke Mosan, on Thursday, carried placards bearing various messages, including, “Gov Dapo Abiodun, Pls end ASUP strike”, “Gov Abiodun, save polytechnic education now”, “Our lecturers must return to classroom” and “Attend to our lecturers demand”, among others.

Speaking during the demonstration, the NAPS Chairman, Ogun State Liaison Council, Comrade Joshua Opatunmibi, popularly known as Lush, said the students had exhausted diplomatic channels and were no longer prepared to accept repeated assurances without corresponding action.

Opatunmibi maintained that the protest was not intended to create hostility between the students and the state government but to make their frustrations known and demand accountability over the prolonged disruption of their academic calendar.

The NAPS leader stressed that the continued closure of the institutions was taking a heavy toll on students, whose academic programmes and future plans had been put on hold, warning that the government must demonstrate the political will to bring the situation to an end.

He explained that, “On November 12th, we issued a 48 hours ultimatum to the government appealing for the quick intervention of the Gov Dapo Abiodun to help end the ongoing ASUP strike.

“The 48 hours elapsed and there was nothing done. So, on Monday again, we had another press conference and begged the government to come to our aid over this strike which has stalled our education and we gave another 48 hours ultimatum.

“The 48 hours expired yesterday, Wednesday afternoon. We are really not happy that the government has done nothing over our request. Is it that the government doesn’t care about our grievances or what? We are definitely not happy because this closure of all the polytechnics in the state is affecting us.

“So, we are here to show that our voice matters. It is not that we are fighting the government but we are saying that the matters involved should be resolved.

“We can’t continue to put our future in jeopardy, we call on Gov Abiodun to please attend to the demands of our lecturers so that we can all go back to our various schools to complete our education”.

Also speaking, Kolade Musbau, a NAPS member, decried the 10-day-old strike, saying that the students were unhappy that the government had not demonstrated serious commitment to ending the industrial action and allowing them to resume their studies.

Musbau said, “The students are not happy that when they are supposed to be in school they are at home wasting their time because of this ASUP strike and despite repeated appeal, it seems government is not ready to do the needful.

“So, we are left with no choice than to embark on this protest to draw government’s attention to our plight and demand urgent intervention to end this strike. We are all eager to go back to our schools and complete our studies within the record time. We hereby beg Gov Abiodun to please end this strike without further delay”.

Speaking on behalf of the state government, the Permanent Secretary, Bureau of Cabinet and Special Services, Mr Dolamu Idowu-Agida, assured the students that the government was already taking steps to resolve the disagreement between it and the lecturers.

Idowu-Agida disclosed that the government had held two meetings with relevant stakeholders as part of efforts to address the issues surrounding the strike. He added that approval had also been granted for an increase in subvention to all the polytechnics in the state, expressing hope that the strike would be called off within the next 48 hours.

He explained that, “I want to tell you that the State Government has held meetings with relevant stakeholders on this matter, twice. So government is seriously addressing your concerns. As at yesterday, approval has been granted for an increase of subvention to all polytechnics.

“The issue of your lecturers is being given serious consideration. I want to assure you. I want to assure you that very soon the matter will be resolved. And your lecturers will go back to classes. Be rest assured that your lecturers should be back to classrooms within the next 48 hours”.

It would be recalled that lecturers in the six state-owned polytechnics embarked on an indefinite strike last Wednesday following the expiration of the 15-day ultimatum given to the state government to address their concerns over the non-implementation of the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance and Earned Academic Allowance.

The union also lamented the inadequate funding of polytechnic education, saying the government had refused to review the N5m monthly subvention given to some of the state-owned polytechnics for more than a decade.

The union had, among other demands, urged the government to pay the outstanding CATA and EAA allowances and to “immediately review and increase the monthly subvention of all the state-owned polytechnics to ₦100 million to reflect current economic realities and the operational needs of these institutions”.

The post Ogun students protest ASUP strike, seek gov’s intervention appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
