title: Peter Obi cannot be more popular than Buhari – Shettima tells Igbos
description:
Vice-President Kashim Shettima has declared that former President Muhammadu Buhari was more popular than former Anambra State Governor and presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi.
Shettima made the statement on Thursday, November 19, 2026, during the All Progressiv
content:
Vice-President Kashim Shettima has declared that former President Muhammadu Buhari was more popular than former Anambra State Governor and presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi.

Shettima made the statement on Thursday, November 19, 2026, during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Awka, Anambra State, where he urged the people of the South-East to strengthen their political relationships with other regions of the country.

The Vice-President argued that Buhari’s political journey demonstrated that popularity within one region was not enough to secure victory in a Nigerian presidential election.

According to him, the former president contested the presidency in 2003, 2007 and 2011 but failed to win despite having a strong support base in Northern Nigeria.

He maintained that Buhari eventually won the 2015 presidential election after building political alliances across different regions.

“Peter Obi cannot be more popular than Muhammadu Buhari. Muhammadu Buhari tried to become President of Nigeria in 2003, he was already a former Head of State. He tried again in 2007, he lost.

“Again, he had a strong base of 15 million votes in Northern Nigeria. He tried again in 2011, he lost. Because having a strong base across the nation is what you need to win a presidential election in a country like Nigeria,” Shettima said.

The Vice-President also urged the Igbo people not to allow political disagreements to create divisions between them and other Nigerians, insisting that the South-East remained an important part of the country’s political and economic structure.

He claimed that approximately 17 million Igbo people lived in Northern Nigeria, while another 10 million resided in Lagos.

Shettima said the figures demonstrated the importance of building political relationships beyond the South-East, urging the people to take advantage of their widespread presence across the country.

“Don’t let anyone tell you that Igbos are not an essential component of the Nigerian configuration,” he said.

He further appealed to the people of the region to embrace political tolerance and make informed decisions ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The Vice-President also spoke about his personal relationship with the Igbo people, disclosing that some of his closest friends and aides were from the South-East.

He said he had maintained strong relationships with the region and had committed personal resources and time to issues affecting its people since becoming Vice-President.

Shettima also recalled the political alliance that brought the APC to power in 2015, urging the South-East to strengthen its participation in national politics.

His remarks come amid growing political realignments ahead of the 2027 general elections, with Peter Obi expected to be one of the major opposition figures challenging President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid.

The post Peter Obi cannot be more popular than Buhari – Shettima tells Igbos appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: 2027: Enenche speaks against imposing leaders on Nigerians
description:
Senior Pastor of Dunamis International Gospel Centre, Paul Enenche, has criticised the imposition of political leaders on Nigerians, insisting that anyone rejected by the people should not seek to remain in power.
The cleric made the remarks in a video shared on Thursday, November 19, as political a
content:
Senior Pastor of Dunamis International Gospel Centre, Paul Enenche, has criticised the imposition of political leaders on Nigerians, insisting that anyone rejected by the people should not seek to remain in power.

The cleric made the remarks in a video shared on Thursday, November 19, as political activities gradually build towards the 2027 general election.

Although he did not mention any politician by name, Enenche condemned leaders who allegedly use money and other means to force themselves on the electorate despite lacking public support.

He argued that leadership should reflect the wishes of the people rather than be secured through financial inducements or electoral manipulation.

“Is it not a shame? People say they don’t want you. You spend money to impose yourself on them,” he said.

“They don’t need you. They don’t want you. Clear out. Don’t contest at all,” the pastor added.

Enenche also warned individuals he described as architects of terrorism in Nigeria against seeking political leadership, saying they would not be allowed to rule the country under God’s watch.

The cleric further challenged fellow pastors and Nigerians who have remained silent over what he described as bad governance, arguing that refusing to speak against wrongdoing amounts to supporting it.

“If you are silent about evil, it means you are in agreement with that evil,” he said.

“Let people speak. Don’t be a coward anymore. Evil shall not rule our land,” he added.

His comments have drawn reactions from Nigerians on social media, with several users praising him for speaking out on the state of the country.

Some commenters also called on other religious leaders to publicly address issues of governance, while others argued that opposition parties needed to unite if they hoped to challenge the ruling party in 2027.

The post 2027: Enenche speaks against imposing leaders on Nigerians appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: 2027: People Are Rejecting Tinubu, They Can Feel The Pain — Dele Momodu
description: A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Dele Momodu, says Nigerians are rejecting President Bola Tinubu because they are feeling the adverse impact of his administration’s economic policies.Momodu, who is the Deputy Director-General of Media and Communications of the ADC presiden
content:
A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Dele Momodu, says Nigerians are rejecting President Bola Tinubu because they are feeling the adverse impact of his administration’s economic policies.

Momodu, who is the Deputy Director-General of Media and Communications of the ADC presidential campaign council, said the growing public discontent was a reflection of the hardship Nigerians have endured since the removal of the fuel subsidy.

The former Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) presidential aspirant made the remarks on Thursday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today.

Momodu said the government should have carefully considered the advantages and disadvantages of the policy before implementing it.

He likened the country’s economic situation to a patient who had been given an injection and remained in a coma for almost four years.

“That’s what is happening in Nigeria. And that is why you can see that everywhere Tinubu goes now, he is being rejected by the people. The people are not stupid; they are rejecting him because they can feel the pain,” he said.

The publisher accused the President of insensitivity to Nigerians’ economic hardship, citing excessive government spending, inadequate funding of critical sectors and the burden of subsidy removal.

“We’ve since discovered that this subsidy issue could have been better handled because, if you look at it, the people who are at fault are probably less than 1,000 people, and now you are punishing over 200 million Nigerians because of the sins of a few people.

“If he were sharing in the pain of the people, he would not be doing what he is doing, donating one billion, doing a budget to individuals, a budget in trillions, more than what you are paying the military, more than what you are using to service the health sector, more than what you are spending on the education of our children,” Momodu said.

Momodu accused the Tinubu administration of covertly reinstating fuel subsidies and dismissed positive economic assessments by the World Bank and IMF, arguing that they had not improved Nigerians’ living conditions.

“The world is praising us; the World Bank is praising us; the IMF is saying we are doing well. Whenever the IMF or World Bank is interested in your case, then something is wrong. You can see clearly that everything you can say is not affecting our people positively. Nigerians are suffering, and that’s just the truth,” he said.

Subsidy Removal, ‘Bamayi’

Tinubu announced the removal of the fuel subsidy during his inauguration on May 29, 2023, citing its growing cost to government finances.

Since that announcement, the policy, alongside the unification of the foreign exchange market, has contributed to higher petrol prices and increased living costs for Nigerians.

However, the President and some of his allies, including Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma and former Minister of Works and Housing Babatunde Fashola, have defended the decision, arguing that it prevented further pressure on public finances, improved revenue available to states and strengthened investor confidence.

Three years later, with the 2027 elections approaching, there has been public anger over economic hardship.

Some protesters reportedly threw stones at the President’s convoy recently and destroyed APC campaign posters, prompting security operatives to intervene.

The ADC has dismissed allegations that the opposition party is sponsoring the protests, maintaining that Nigerians are independently expressing their dissatisfaction with the administration.

title: Somalia expels UAE ambassador over internal interference
description:
Somalia on Thursday expelled the United Arab Emirates ambassador, accusing the Gulf nation of interfering in its internal affairs in a move blasted as “irresponsible” by Abu Dhabi.
Somalia and the UAE have quarrelled over several issues, including Abu Dhabi’s perceived support for Israel’s recogniti
content:
Somalia on Thursday expelled the United Arab Emirates ambassador, accusing the Gulf nation of interfering in its internal affairs in a move blasted as “irresponsible” by Abu Dhabi.

Somalia and the UAE have quarrelled over several issues, including Abu Dhabi’s perceived support for Israel’s recognition of the breakaway region of Somaliland.

“The Council instructed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation to recall Somalia’s ambassador to the UAE… and to notify the UAE ambassador to Somalia to leave the country within 72 hours,” Somalia’s Information Minister Abdulfatah Qasim said.

The expulsion followed a cabinet meeting at which the UAE was accused of “blatant aggression against Somalia.”

“The Somali government is taking a series of measures … to defend the country against UAE actions targeting its sovereignty, territorial integrity, national unity, internal security and independence,” Qasim said.

The UAE foreign ministry condemned the move in a statement. It “strongly denounced the escalatory and hostile approach by the Somali government towards the UAE.”

The expulsion reflected “irresponsible positions that undermine bilateral relations and weaken the foundations of cooperation between the two countries,” the statement added.

– Somaliland dispute –

On Tuesday, Somali President Hassan Mohamud criticised the UAE in a state of the nation address, accusing it of fuelling “political discord” in the Horn of Africa country.

“The UAE has provided political and financial support to certain regional states, enabling them to oppose the Federal Government,” Mohamud said.

“It has encouraged political discord and fuelled division among Somalis to undermine the authority of the state and make the country easier to control from outside,” he added.

In January, Somalia cancelled all agreements with the UAE after Israel’s recognition of Somaliland, and after the UAE allegedly helped a Yemeni separatist leader escape by boat and plane through Somali ports without consulting the government.

The UAE built and operates a large deep-water port and military base at Berbera in Somaliland and two others at Bosaso and Kismayo in other parts of Somalia.

Although the Somali government said the UAE would no longer be permitted to operate the ports, Somalia is deeply fragmented, and the FG has practically no control over the semi-autonomous states where the ports are located.

The UAE statement voiced “regret over the Somali government’s attempts to bring its internal power struggles into bilateral relations.”

In Sudan, the UAE is widely accused of arming the Rapid Support Forces paramilitaries, who have been fighting the regular military since 2023 and are accused of massacres against civilians.

The UAE has repeatedly denied the allegations.

AFP

title: 2027: INEC extends ad hoc staff recruitment to December 3
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has extended the deadline for the registration of ad hoc staff for the 2027 general election by two weeks.
The commission announced the extension in a statement issued on Thursday by the Chairman of its Information and Voter Education Committee, Mohammed
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has extended the deadline for the registration of ad hoc staff for the 2027 general election by two weeks.

The commission announced the extension in a statement issued on Thursday by the Chairman of its Information and Voter Education Committee, Mohammed Haruna.

INEC said the recruitment portal, which was initially scheduled to close on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, would now remain open until 11:59pm on Wednesday, December 3, 2026.

“The commission has extended the registration period by two weeks. The portal will now close at 11:59pm on Wednesday, 3rd December 2026,” the statement read.

The commission said the extension followed a review of the recruitment exercise and was intended “to give more eligible Nigerians the opportunity to apply and to ensure that the commission has an adequate pool of applicants for deployment across the country.”

INEC had opened the INEC Portal for Recruitment of Election Staff, known as INECPRES, at 8am on Friday, September 18, 2026, for the recruitment of personnel to support the conduct of the 2027 general election.

In an earlier notice, the commission said applications would be submitted through its online platform, accessible via its website and the dedicated INECPRES portal.

INEC urged interested Nigerians who had yet to apply to complete their registration before the new deadline.

“Persons who are yet to apply may do so through the dedicated portal: pres.inecnigeria.org, before the new deadline,” the statement said.

The commission also warned applicants against using unofficial websites or paying anyone to facilitate their recruitment.

“The public is further reminded that the application is free. No official of the commission or any other person is authorised to demand payment from any applicant,” it said.

INEC advised Nigerians to disregard any website, link or message claiming to be a recruitment portal of the commission other than its official platform.

title: Cash handouts alone can’t end poverty – Tinubu’s aide
description:
The Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Economic Affairs, Tope Fasua, has warned that distributing money to Nigerians without addressing underlying economic challenges will not provide a sustainable solution to poverty.
Fasua said the Federal Government must prioritise economic stability, pr
content:
The Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Economic Affairs, Tope Fasua, has warned that distributing money to Nigerians without addressing underlying economic challenges will not provide a sustainable solution to poverty.

Fasua said the Federal Government must prioritise economic stability, productivity, investment and job creation rather than depend excessively on cash handouts to address the country’s economic difficulties.

He spoke on Thursday in Abuja at the 2026 National Growth and Development Forum, themed “The Nigeria We Want: The Economy, Your Money, Our Future,” organised by Moneyline with Nancy on African Independent Television.

“If we only focus on sharing money, we’ll probably be digging a deeper hole from where we came from,” he said.

The presidential adviser acknowledged the hardship confronting Nigerians but maintained that sustainable improvements in living standards required a stable macroeconomic environment.

“If you don’t build a strong macro, you can’t go anywhere with the micro,” Fasua said.

He added, “People cannot hear anything if they are hungry.”

Fasua recalled the previous administration’s reliance on Ways and Means financing, which he estimated at between N30tn and N35tn, arguing that excessive monetary financing was not a sustainable economic strategy.

However, he acknowledged that the COVID-19 pandemic had complicated economic management under the previous administration.

Defending the Tinubu administration’s reforms, Fasua alleged that petrol subsidies previously cost Nigeria approximately $15bn annually, with substantial benefits accruing to powerful interests in the petroleum industry.

He also argued that exchange-rate reforms had reduced opportunities for arbitrage and improved access to foreign exchange for manufacturers and individuals.

According to him, the most difficult period of the reforms occurred between late 2023 and 2024, while subsequent developments indicated improving economic conditions.

“I think that the worst is over,” he declared.

Fasua cited Nigeria’s 4.43 per cent economic growth in the second quarter of 2026, moderating inflation and improvements in external reserves as evidence of progress.

Nevertheless, he acknowledged that poverty remained a major challenge requiring sustained attention.

He urged Nigerians to embrace entrepreneurship, arguing that the country’s infrastructure, agricultural, manufacturing, healthcare and technology challenges also presented opportunities for business development.

“Nigeria is not short of opportunity. We are sometimes short of the confidence, information, imagination, and determination to develop Nigeria,” he said.

The presidential adviser also stressed financial literacy, savings, investment and responsible borrowing, warning against spending beyond one’s income.

“A stronger Naira must be earned through a stronger economy. It cannot be legislated into existence,” he added.

His remark comes amid the Federal Government’s expansion of cash assistance programmes, with the World Bank reporting that N658.9bn had been disbursed to 10.46 million poor and vulnerable households as of September 2026.

Recently, the government also announced a N50,000 relief payment for selected vulnerable households under the National Emergency Relief and Stabilisation Intervention, generating widespread interest in payment alerts and eligibility.

Also speaking, the President of the Nigerian Economic Society, Dr Baba Musa, warned that improvements in macroeconomic indicators had yet to translate into adequate welfare gains for millions of Nigerians.

“Macroeconomic stability is necessary, but it is not yet shared prosperity. A stable exchange rate is not yet a full dinner table. Stability is the foundation; it is not the building,” Musa said.

He cited World Bank estimates indicating that about 63 per cent of Nigerians lived below the poverty line in 2025, while calling for agricultural productivity, affordable credit, job creation and stronger social protection.

Musa also urged political leaders to maintain fiscal discipline and policy continuity ahead of the 2027 elections.

Similarly, the President of Capital Market Academics of Nigeria, Prof. Uche Uwaleke, said economic reforms should be judged by their impact on employment, purchasing power and poverty reduction rather than macroeconomic indicators alone.

“The success of any economic reform must be measured not merely by improvements in GDP growth, foreign exchange stability, government revenue or external reserves, but by its capacity to create jobs, improve purchasing power, reduce poverty, expand opportunities and enhance the overall quality of life of citizens,” he said.

Uwaleke noted that the Nigerian capital market had recorded year-to-date returns exceeding 60 per cent, but stressed the need to make investment opportunities accessible to ordinary Nigerians through financial education, affordable products and stronger investor protection.

The Managing Director of the Bank of Agriculture, Ayodeji Sotinrin, also advocated productive financing rather than repeated distribution of free agricultural inputs.

He disclosed that the bank was implementing financing programmes covering smallholder farmers, mechanisation, improved seeds, irrigation and agricultural value chains.

“It’s not by giving them handouts because they’re on social media. It’s not by sharing free fertiliser. Give them tools to fish, and you teach them how to fish rather than you hand out fish to them,” he said.

Sotinrin explained that the bank was pursuing partnerships with cooperatives, financial institutions and state governments to provide sustainable agricultural financing.

Earlier, the Executive Producer of Moneyline with Nancy and the convener of the event, Nancy Iloh-Nnaji, said the forum was designed to bridge the gap between economic policymaking and public understanding.

“A policy is announced, a reform is introduced, but the people expected to benefit from it do not always understand what it means for them or how to take advantage of it,” she said.

She called for greater public awareness of development finance opportunities, financial literacy and investment risks, while warning Nigerians against fraudulent investment schemes and online impersonation.

The post Cash handouts alone can’t end poverty – Tinubu’s aide appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: ASUU demands immediate payment of withheld salaries
description:
The Academic Staff Union of Universities has demanded the immediate payment of the remaining three-and-a-half months’ withheld salaries of its members, warning that non-payment remains an undeserved punishment that could snowball into a bigger crisis for the Nigerian university system.
The demand wa
content:
The Academic Staff Union of Universities has demanded the immediate payment of the remaining three-and-a-half months’ withheld salaries of its members, warning that non-payment remains an undeserved punishment that could snowball into a bigger crisis for the Nigerian university system.

The demand was contained in a press release signed by the ASUU President, Prof. Chris Piwuna, titled “Why Our Withheld Salaries Must Be Paid Now” and issued in Jos on Thursday night.

According to the union, it has continually demanded payment of the withheld salaries since the twilight of the Buhari-led government, following the 2022 nationwide strike occasioned by the government’s failure to address issues arising from the poor implementation and non-renegotiation of the 2009 FGN-ASUU Agreement.

“Agitation in this respect has witnessed some twists and turns under the current administration led by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” the ASUU president said.

The union recalled President Tinubu’s involvement in the matter before his emergence as president on May 29, 2023.

“He, like some other friends of the Buhari government, had intervened in the matter. Candidate Tinubu agreed with ASUU that the crisis could have been averted if steps had been taken early enough to address the union’s grievances and pledged his commitment to preventing future occurrence if he emerged victorious in the then-upcoming presidential election. He alluded to the principle of ‘CLEMENCY’ as a solution to the problem of withheld salaries in critical labour matters such as the case of ASUU and the Federal Government,” the statement said.

ASUU said its members heaved a sigh of relief when Tinubu won the presidential election, with the expectation of a full release of the seven-and-a-half months’ salaries withheld under President Muhammadu Buhari.

“However, the hope raised through his pre-election intervention now seems to have been dashed. Three-and-a-half years down the line, only the arrears of four months have been paid!” the union said.

The union said its engagement with the President’s Chief of Staff, Rt. Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila, earlier in the administration, met with a brick wall.

“He categorically declared that government was not ready to pay the withheld salaries in full. Surprisingly, the Hon. Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, has continued to echo the Chief of Staff’s position on the matter, and all ASUU’s entreaties to have a direct audience with President Tinubu have been rebuffed,” ASUU said.

The union categorically restated its position that non-payment of the withheld salaries is an ill wind that blows nobody any good.

“Non-payment of the withheld salaries is an ill wind that blows nobody any good; it is an undeserved punishment for academics which could snowball into a bigger crisis for the Nigerian university system,” it said.

“Under both Presidents Buhari and Tinubu, our members’ rightful entitlements (salary shortfall, third-party deductions, promotion arrears, etc.) were delayed for months and years, for which no compensation for depreciated value and sundry losses were paid. When government ‘went on strike’ by withholding what is due to our members, we took our losses with equanimity and did not declare No Pay, No Work. Why then should government criminalise strike action through slavish enforcement of the so-called No Work, No Pay rule?”

ASUU said its members made enormous sacrifices to cover the lost grounds during the strike period to enable affected students to graduate and move on with their lives.

“At huge risks to their health, career progression and families, ASUU members forfeited their annual and research leaves, and doubled their efforts to regularise the academic calendar and stabilize the public university system. If the Tinubu government would not commend Nigerian academics for moderating their demands to guarantee industrial harmony in the universities, it should at least release what they are owed,” the statement said.

The union stressed that its members were not beggars.

“ASUU members are no beggars. Neither are they a conquered people or slaves. As free citizens, asking for what is due to us is not too much in a country that prides itself on a democratic pedestal. Our members cannot be cowed on account of platitudes. We reject the ‘No more ASUU strikes’ sloganeering and ‘Let’s keep them talking’ strategy. As scholars, we know our rights and we shall continue to demand for our dues – come rain, come shine. History teaches us that no government – no matter how powerful – has ever conquered a people of ideas for too long. The intellect prevails in the long run,” ASUU said.

The union disclosed that its National Executive Council (NEC), at its meeting of November 13 and 14, 2026, at the University of Abuja, called for the payment of the three-and-a-half months’ salaries without further delay in the spirit of fairness, equity, justice and respect for the worth of Nigerian academics.

“More specifically, NEC appealed to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to resist the temptation of punishing ASUU members for honoring him with the suspension of the 2022 nationwide strike over which about half of the unpaid salaries are still withheld under his watch,” the statement said.

The post ASUU demands immediate payment of withheld salaries appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Argentina mourns 16-year-old footballer who died after on-pitch collision
description:
Football fans, players and clubs in Argentina are mourning the death of 16-year-old Abel Nunez, who died two days after suffering a severe head injury during a youth football match.
Nunez sustained the injury on Friday while playing for his club, FC Ezeiza, against Muniz in a fifth-division youth co
content:
Football fans, players and clubs in Argentina are mourning the death of 16-year-old Abel Nunez, who died two days after suffering a severe head injury during a youth football match.

Nunez sustained the injury on Friday while playing for his club, FC Ezeiza, against Muniz in a fifth-division youth competition. He died on Sunday, according to reports in Argentine media.

Following the incident, FC Ezeiza announced that the teenager had suffered a serious head injury requiring surgery and appealed to supporters to join a prayer chain for his recovery.

His death has since drawn tributes from football clubs, teammates and members of the public, with many expressing sadness over the loss of a young player whose dream was to build a career in the sport.

In a statement, FC Ezeiza described Nunez as a member of its family and said his death had left the club devastated.

“With profound sorrow and immense sadness, we say goodbye to a young man who had his whole life ahead of him and who today leaves us with a void impossible to describe,” the club said.

It added that the teenager had been wearing the club’s shirt when he suffered the injury.

“Today football is in the background. We are overwhelmed by the pain of saying goodbye to a colleague, a young man full of dreams and hopes, who was part of our family.

“May you rest in peace. You will always be part of our family,” the statement added.

Nunez was born in 2008 and lived in Ezeiza, a city in the Greater Buenos Aires region. He played both football and futsal, according to details on his Facebook profile.

His futsal club, Nueva Estrella, also paid tribute to him and announced the suspension of its activities following his death.

“You will always be with us. Your memory will live forever in our hearts,” the club said.

Roman Corral, the father of Nunez’s best friend, said the teenager’s teammates were struggling to come to terms with the loss.

Speaking to Radio La Red, Corral recalled knowing Nunez since he was 12 and said the teenager had always dreamed of becoming a professional footballer.

“The boys are devastated; it’s something unnatural for them. At that age, you think you’re a superhero, and to lose your life like that, the way Abel lost his… I’ve known him since he was 12, when he started school with my son in first grade. His dream was to be a football player, just like my son,” he said.

Corral also appealed to the Argentine Football Association (AFA) to honour the teenager with a minute of silence, saying he deserved to be remembered as a footballer because he died while playing the sport.

“If anyone from the AFA is listening, please observe a minute of silence. He wanted to live as a footballer and he should be given a send-off as a footballer because he died on the pitch, doing what all Argentinians love, which is playing football,” he said.

The post Argentina mourns 16-year-old footballer who died after on-pitch collision appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

description: Yiaga Africa has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to publish comprehensive guidelines and the list of participating polling units for its nationwide mock accreditation and electronic results upload exercise scheduled for November 28.The organisation said timely access to in
content:
Yiaga Africa has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to publish comprehensive guidelines and the list of participating polling units for its nationwide mock accreditation and electronic results upload exercise scheduled for November 28.

The organisation said timely access to information about the exercise was necessary to enable citizens, political parties, civil society organisations, election observers, and the media to understand, participate in, and monitor the process.

In a statement signed by its Executive Director, Samson Itodo, Yiaga Africa welcomed INEC’s decision to conduct the exercise ahead of the 2027 general elections.

It said the exercise was consistent with sustained calls by citizens and civil society organisations for the commission to adequately test the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) before the elections.

“However, Yiaga Africa is concerned that, despite the importance of the exercise, the Commission is yet to make public comprehensive guidelines and a framework outlining how it will be conducted. The list of polling units where the exercise will take place is also yet to be made public.

“For an exercise of this significance, timely access to information is essential. Citizens and electoral stakeholders should have sufficient information and notice to understand, participate in, and observe the process,” the statement read in part.

Yiaga Africa said transparency in the exercise would be crucial to building public confidence in the electoral technologies that would be deployed for the 2027 elections.

It called on INEC to immediately publish a comprehensive framework outlining the scope, modalities and procedures for the exercise.

The organisation also urged the commission to release the complete list of participating polling units and other relevant locations early enough to give stakeholders sufficient time to prepare for the exercise.

Yiaga Africa further urged INEC to use the mock exercise as an opportunity to demonstrate transparency and responsiveness while allowing meaningful public scrutiny of BVAS and IReV.

Last week, INEC had announced November 28 as the date for the nationwide mock accreditation exercise to test its voter accreditation and electronic results transmission systems ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The commission’s chairman, Joash Amupitan, said the exercise would simulate the presidential election and take place across all states of the federation.

He said the exercise was part of measures to address technical challenges experienced during the 2023 general elections and strengthen the credibility of the 2027 polls.

The 2027 Presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections will be held on February 6.

The post Yiaga Africa Urges INEC To Publish Guidelines For Nov. 28 Mock Accreditation appeared first on Channels Television.

title: When Ndigbo Become President, It Must Be Eight Full Years — Oshiomhole
description: Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said the South-East should have a full eight-year presidential tenure when a candidate from the region eventually becomes Nigeria’s president.The former Edo State governor spoke on Thursday at an All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential
content:
Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said the South-East should have a full eight-year presidential tenure when a candidate from the region eventually becomes Nigeria’s president.

The former Edo State governor spoke on Thursday at an All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Anambra State, where he endorsed President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid.

“When Ndigbo will become president, it must be eight full years. No half-talk. It will be full talk by those with brains, with courage, and fill the gap,” he said.

Oshiomhole also praised Anambra State Governor Charles Soludo, a former governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), for his economic expertise and leadership.

He said Soludo understood the challenges facing Nigeria’s economy, particularly the disconnect between monetary and fiscal policies.

Earlier, Soludo declared that President Tinubu does not need to rig the 2027 presidential election to secure victory, arguing that the President’s performance will earn him another term.

“The President doesn’t need to rig the election. President Tinubu doesn’t need to rig the election. President Tinubu and Shettima, they are doing very well. They will win because they have done well,” the governor said.

Senator Oshiomhole’s comments on an eight-year presidential tenure for an eventual Igbo president come amid discussions about political power rotation and the South-East’s quest for the presidency.

Igbo Presidency, Obi’s Stance

Former Anambra State governor Peter Obi, who contested the 2023 presidential election, is seeking the nation’s top job again in 2027 under the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), with former Kano State Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso as his running mate.

Obi, a South-Easterner, finished third in the 2023 presidential election with 6,101,533 votes, and has pledged to serve only one four-year term if elected, promising to hand over power to the North in 2031.

He has argued that a single term would allow him to focus on governance without the distractions of seeking re-election.

He maintains that 48 months is enough time to tackle insecurity, fix the economy, and stabilise the country.

However, the pledge has drawn criticism from some South-East political leaders, who believe the region should not concede a full eight-year presidential tenure.

Former Imo State governor Rochas Okorocha described Obi’s proposal as a “four-year gamble”, arguing that the South-East should not settle for a single term when other regions have enjoyed eight years in office.

Minister of Works David Umahi also questioned why Obi would unilaterally settle for four years when other regions have served two terms of eight years

INEC has scheduled the presidential and National Assembly elections for January 16, 2027, with Bola Tinubu (APC), Atiku Abubakar (ADC), Obi (NDC) and Omoyele Sowore (AAC) among the contenders.

The post When Ndigbo Become President, It Must Be Eight Full Years — Oshiomhole appeared first on Channels Television.

title: 2027: NES warns against sacrificing economic gains for politics
description:
The Nigerian Economic Society has urged political parties, governments and other stakeholders to maintain fiscal discipline and policy continuity ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning against economic decisions that could undermine the gains of ongoing reforms.
The President of the society, D
content:
The Nigerian Economic Society has urged political parties, governments and other stakeholders to maintain fiscal discipline and policy continuity ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning against economic decisions that could undermine the gains of ongoing reforms.

The President of the society, Dr Baba Yusuf Musa, made the call on Thursday at the 2026 National Growth and Development Forum, organised by Moneyline with Nancy on African Independent Television in Abuja.

The warning comes as Nigeria prepares for the 2027 general elections, a period traditionally associated with increased political spending, campaign-related expenditure and pressure on public finances.

Previous election cycles have raised concerns about the diversion of public resources to political activities, expansionary government spending and the risk of fiscal decisions being driven by short-term electoral considerations rather than economic priorities.

The PUNCH recently reported that members of the Central Bank of Nigeria’s Monetary Policy Committee warned that increased government spending ahead of the 2027 general elections could fuel inflation, weaken fiscal discipline and complicate efforts to maintain monetary stability.

Speaking on the theme, “The Nigeria We Want: The Economy, Your Money, Our Future,” Musa said political considerations must not override sound economic management as the country approaches another election cycle.

“As we approach the 2027 elections, I appeal, respectfully but earnestly, to all stakeholders, across every party and every tier of government, to protect these hard-won gains through fiscal discipline and policy continuity. Sound economics should be the common ground on which all who aspire to lead this nation can stand,” he said.

The NES president warned that Nigeria’s development challenges required disciplined public finance, credible institutions and consistent implementation of economic policies.

“Debt is a financing instrument, not a development strategy,” he declared.

He added, “And every naira of public spending should answer three questions: What problem will it solve? Who will benefit? And how will we know it worked?”

Musa acknowledged the Federal Government’s economic reforms, including petrol subsidy removal, foreign exchange market unification, bank recapitalisation and tax reforms, describing them as difficult but necessary decisions.

He cited the country’s 4.43 per cent economic growth in the second quarter of 2026, October inflation of 14.06 per cent, external reserves of approximately $55bn and the reduction in the monetary policy rate from 26.5 to 23 per cent as signs of improving macroeconomic conditions.

However, he cautioned that these gains had yet to translate into meaningful improvements in the living conditions of many Nigerians.

“Macroeconomic stability is necessary, but it is not yet shared prosperity. A stable exchange rate is not yet a full dinner table. Stability is the foundation; it is not the building,” Musa stated.

Citing World Bank estimates, he said approximately 63 per cent of Nigerians lived below the poverty line in 2025, while food inflation, weak industrial growth and widespread informal employment remained major concerns.

He identified five priorities for sustainable development, including job-creating growth, affordable credit, domestic production, investment in human capital and disciplined public finance.

Musa also proposed a national development compact involving government, businesses, universities, the media and citizens, supported by measurable indicators covering household incomes, employment, education, healthcare, electricity and poverty reduction.

“We must replace the politics of short-term applause with the economics of long-term results,” he said.

Also speaking, the Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Economic Affairs, Tope Fasua, defended the administration’s reforms, arguing that sustainable improvements in household welfare depended on macroeconomic stability.

“If you don’t build a strong macro, you can’t go anywhere with the micro,” Fasua said.

He warned against excessive reliance on cash transfers and monetary financing, citing the previous administration’s Ways and Means advances.

The President of Capital Market Academics of Nigeria, Prof. Uche Uwaleke, similarly called for reforms that improve employment, purchasing power and poverty reduction.

He said the capital market had recorded year-to-date returns exceeding 60 per cent but stressed that investment opportunities must become more accessible to ordinary Nigerians.

The Managing Director of the Bank of Agriculture, Ayodeji Sotinrin, advocated affordable agricultural financing, mechanisation and improved seeds to raise productivity and strengthen food security.

Earlier, the forum’s convener and Executive Producer of Moneyline with Nancy, Nancy Illoh-Nnaji, emphasised the importance of financial literacy and public understanding of economic policies.

The post 2027: NES warns against sacrificing economic gains for politics appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: ADC crisis: BoT faction asks INEC to delist Mark, candidates
description:
The Nafiu Gombe-led Board of Trustees of the African Democratic Congress has asked the Independent National Electoral Commission to immediately enforce the November 5, 2026 judgment of the Federal High Court concerning the party’s leadership dispute.
The Board also called on INEC to remove the names
content:
The Nafiu Gombe-led Board of Trustees of the African Democratic Congress has asked the Independent National Electoral Commission to immediately enforce the November 5, 2026 judgment of the Federal High Court concerning the party’s leadership dispute.

The Board also called on INEC to remove the names of Senator David Mark and Rauf Aregbesola from its records as the party’s leaders and delist candidates uploaded to its portal by the Mark-led leadership.

The BoT, in a statement issued by its Chairman, Chief Rufus Ikanmi, said the judgment delivered by Justice Peter Lifu in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, filed by Hon. Nafi’u Bala Gombe against the ADC and four others, remained valid and binding.

Ikanmi said, “The judgment of the Honourable Court is valid, binding, and subsisting. It has not been stayed, varied, or set aside by any superior court. INEC, as a statutory body bound by the rule of law, has a constitutional duty to give full effect to it without further delay.”

He urged the commission to recognise and deal only with the leadership headed by Gombe, which he said was affirmed by the court.

He said, “Immediately remove the names of the Sen. David Mark and Rauf Aregbesola-led leadership from its records as leaders of the African Democratic Congress;

“Remove and delist all candidates uploaded to the INEC portal by the said leadership, as such uploads were done in clear violation of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (as Amended), Electoral Act 2022 and the party’s constitution.

“Recognise and deal only with the lawful leadership of the Party under the leadership of Hon Nafiu Bala Gombe, as affirmed by the Federal High Court.”

The BoT also urged former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and other persons allegedly acting with the Mark-led leadership to suspend campaign activities, rallies and public engagements organised in the name of the ADC pending compliance with the judgment.

“Any continued defiance of the judgment of the Federal High Court amounts to contempt of court and a direct assault on constitutional democracy and the rule of law,” Ikanmi said.

The board called on party members and supporters to remain calm and law-abiding, adding that it was committed to peace, unity and the constitutional order of the party.

On November 5, Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja nullified the leadership of the ADC led by former Senate President David Mark and invalidated decisions taken by the party under the leadership.

The court ruled in favour of Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former Deputy National Chairman of the party (North-East), who had challenged the emergence of Mark and other members of the interim National Working Committee following the resignation of former National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu.

However, the Mark-led ADC has appealed the judgement.

The party also disclosed that it had filed an application for a stay of execution of the judgment pending the hearing and determination of the appeal.

Efforts to get the the Chief Press Secretary to the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, Dayo Oketola were not successful as of the time of filling this report.

However, a report by Arise News on Thursday, citing a senior official of the commission, said the continued listing was connected to a subsisting Notice of Appeal and an application for a Stay of Execution relating to the judgment.

The report added that the commission could not disregard the pending appellate proceedings while considering requests for recognition arising from the ruling.

The post ADC crisis: BoT faction asks INEC to delist Mark, candidates appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Football needs personalities like Klopp – Guardiola
description:
Former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola has expressed his admiration for Jürgen Klopp, describing the German coach as one of the best figures in football and insisting that the game needs personalities like him.
Guardiola praised Klopp’s charisma, communication skills and influence on football,
content:
Former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola has expressed his admiration for Jürgen Klopp, describing the German coach as one of the best figures in football and insisting that the game needs personalities like him.

Guardiola praised Klopp’s charisma, communication skills and influence on football, saying he was delighted to hear that his former managerial rival had returned to coaching.

According to football transfer expert on X on Thursday, Guardiola said “Klopp is one of the best in football. I cannot even begin to describe how much I admire him,” Guardiola said, according to Bundesliga Magazine, via @iMiaSanMia.

“He is the kind of personality, the kind of coach, who makes our footballing world a better place. He has charisma and is an incredible communicator.”

The Spaniard also expressed confidence in Klopp’s ability to inspire the German national team and help restore the supporters’ pride in their country.

Guardiola believes Klopp’s football philosophy and leadership can bring renewed energy to the national side, although he admitted that winning major tournaments cannot be guaranteed.

“Jürgen will inspire the players to embrace his style of football, and things will get better again. Whether they win the next Euros or the World Cup, nobody can say.

“But I’m 100% convinced that German fans will once again be proud of their national team,” he added.

Guardiola and Klopp shared one of football’s most memorable managerial rivalries during their respective spells at Manchester City and Liverpool, competing for major honours in English football.

Despite their intense battles on the pitch, Guardiola’s latest comments underline the mutual respect between two influential figures in modern football.

The post Football needs personalities like Klopp – Guardiola appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Four convicted of sexually abusing woman drugged by husband in UK
description:
Four men have been found guilty of sexually abusing a woman whose husband secretly drugged her and advertised her to strangers on the internet over a 13-year period, in the first trial of its kind in the UK.
As reported by the BBC on Thursday, following a trial at Winchester Crown Court, a jury of e
content:
Four men have been found guilty of sexually abusing a woman whose husband secretly drugged her and advertised her to strangers on the internet over a 13-year period, in the first trial of its kind in the UK.

As reported by the BBC on Thursday, following a trial at Winchester Crown Court, a jury of eight men and four women convicted Norman Macksoni, 48, Richard Wilkins, 62, Connor Sanderson-Doyle, 32, and Mohammed Hassan, 38, of multiple sexual offences against Joanne Young.

The verdicts follow earlier guilty pleas from her ex-husband, Philip Young, 50, a former Conservative Swindon borough councillor.

He previously admitted to 56 charges—including 11 counts of rape, 11 of administering a substance with intent, and 14 of voyeurism—after using websites and apps such as Craigslist, Grindr, and Fab Swingers to invite men to his home in Swindon, Wiltshire, to abuse his wife without her knowledge.

The Convictions
Norman Macksoni, 48: Guilty of one count of rape.

Richard Wilkins, 62: Guilty of one count of rape and one count of assault by penetration.

Connor Sanderson-Doyle, 32: Guilty of one count of sexual assault by penetration and one count of sexual assault by touching.

Mohammed Hassan, 38: Guilty of one count of sexual assault by touching.

A sixth defendant, Dean Hamilton, 47, of Street in Somerset, admitted one charge of rape, one of assault by penetration, and two of sexual assault at an earlier hearing in February.

Judge Mr Justice Saini commended Joanne Young for showing “amazing bravery through these proceedings” and warned all defendants to expect lengthy jail terms when they are sentenced on 21 and 22 December.

Survivor Speaks Out
Joanne Young, who divorced Philip Young last year and waived her right to anonymity, wiped her eyes as she spoke on the steps outside the court.

“The person I trusted most in the world betrayed me in the most horrific way,” she said, adding that the abuse had “cost me my life as I knew it” and had a devastating impact on her and her children.

Addressing the actions of the co-defendants, she stated: “What happened to me was not the act of one man alone, others were invited to take part and they chose to. That choice makes them complicit in what was done to me and today’s verdicts recognise that.”

She urged the government to review the law of consent “as a priority” to ensure women are properly protected, while telling other survivors: “You can be believed and understood.”

Investigation and French Parallels
Specialist Crown Prosecution Service prosecutor James Foster said the case marked the first time a UK jury had been asked to consider organised, drug-facilitated sexual abuse orchestrated by a husband.

Police launched their investigation in 2023 after being alerted that Philip Young, whose most recent address was in Enfield, north London, had uploaded extreme pornographic images online.

Detectives found he had recorded 480 intimate images and videos of his wife across 200 separate occasions—mostly at their Swindon home—and posted images online at least 500 times.

During the inquiry, UK police sought expertise from French investigators who handled the case of Gisèle Pelicot, whose husband, Dominique Pelicot, was jailed for 20 years in France in 2024 for drugging her and recruiting dozens of men to abuse her.

Wiltshire Police confirmed they are still searching for another male suspect wanted in connection with alleged sexual offences against Joanne Young.

The force noted that organised drug-facilitated sexual assault may be significantly under-reported, as victims are often unaware they have been drugged or experience fragmented memories.

The post Four convicted of sexually abusing woman drugged by husband in UK appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: No capital needed to start business, QNET tells Nigerians
description:
…Promises job creation for Rivers residents
From Tony John, Port Harcourt
The General Manager of QNET, Ayokunmi Solesi, says Nigerians can start a legitimate business without initial capital through the company’s direct selling model, describing it as a major boost to small and medium enterprises an
content:
…Promises job creation for Rivers residents

From Tony John, Port Harcourt

The General Manager of QNET, Ayokunmi Solesi, says Nigerians can start a legitimate business without initial capital through the company’s direct selling model, describing it as a major boost to small and medium enterprises and the nation’s economy.

Solesi spoke on Thursday in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, during a media engagement ahead of the company’s EXPO ’26.

He said every nation that has thrived across the world has taken care of small and medium enterprises, noting that QNET falls under that category by providing business opportunities to people.

“We are providing business opportunity to people. We are saying to you that you do not need to have capital at the beginning of your business,” Solesi said.

“We are providing this business opportunity where you can buy the product at a good price and you can also sell the product, as long as you understand the benefit of the product and the consumers you are also selling it to.”

According to him, the impact goes beyond the company to individuals who will ultimately affect the economy of Nigeria as a whole.

On what stands QNET out from other wellness companies, Solesi said it is all about the product.

“It’s the product. It’s all about the product. Majority of our products already have a patent which is exclusive to us,” he said.

“You will realize that majority of our products also cannot be found anywhere else apart from our company. This is why in all the conversations we have had, we have talked about our wellness product, we have talked about our health product.”

He said the company is not only giving Nigerians good products already certified by the regulatory body, but also giving them business opportunities to sell the products in a legitimate way.

On affordability and access, Solesi said wellness products are generally not cheap, but QNET products offer value for money.

“Affordability is relative. Wellness product generally is not cheap. But I would say to you that in terms of the value itself, it is affordable,” he said.

He added that the products can be easily gotten online via http://QNET.net and delivered to customers’ doorsteps through DHL.

“And by the way, you also do not have to join the network to use our product. You can go online to buy the product directly and it is delivered to your doorstep through DHL. So, if you decide not to take the business opportunity, or you decide to use the product, you can still go on to our retail store to buy the product directly,” Solesi said.

Asked why the company, which has existed for 28 years, is just coming to Port Harcourt now, Solesi said QNET has actually been around in the city through people selling its products.

“We love Port Harcourt, so don’t think that Port Harcourt is the last. We have actually been around even in Port Harcourt. There are people that have been selling the product. But, we said that it is time for us to come to Port Harcourt to let Port Harcourt people know about the product,” he said.

“We want you all in Port Harcourt to understand and Rivers State to understand that QNET, as a company, has come to create opportunities for our youths, not just for our youths, for everyone in Port Harcourt. This is a business model that works. If you understand the product and how it works, you would understand that this is a fantastic opportunity.

“Yes, we have been existing for 28 years, but we have only been in Nigeria since 2022. So, it is a different thing entirely. So, it is just gradually we move across all the states.”

Ends.

The post No capital needed to start business, QNET tells Nigerians appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Tinubu hails Jonathan’s democratic legacy, peaceful concession as he turns 69
description:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja
President Bola Tinubu has described former President Goodluck Jonathan as a patriot and statesman whose contributions to Nigeria’s democratic development and national unity have left an enduring mark on the country’s political history.
Tinubu, who congratulated Jon
content:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has described former President Goodluck Jonathan as a patriot and statesman whose contributions to Nigeria’s democratic development and national unity have left an enduring mark on the country’s political history.

Tinubu, who congratulated Jonathan on his 69th birthday, November 20, also commended the former President for his continued efforts in promoting democracy, peacebuilding and conflict resolution across Africa and beyond.

The President said Jonathan’s commitment to democratic governance, national unity and Nigeria’s peaceful advancement remained significant to the country’s political history.

Tinubu, who congratulated Jonathan on his 69th birthday, November 20, also commended the former President for his continued efforts in promoting democracy, peacebuilding and conflict resolution across Africa and beyond.

The President said Jonathan’s commitment to democratic governance, national unity and Nigeria’s peaceful advancement remained significant to the country’s political history.

In a congratulatory message issued on Thursday by his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, Tinubu acknowledged Jonathan’s years of service to the country, from his early political career in Bayelsa State to the highest office in the land.

He recalled that Jonathan served as Deputy Governor and Governor of Bayelsa State, Vice President and eventually President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

Tinubu also praised the former President’s post-presidency engagements, particularly his international peacebuilding and mediation efforts, describing them as important contributions to democratic values and good governance.

Jonathan, who turns 69 on Friday, November 20, has remained active in peace and democratic initiatives across the continent since leaving office.

The President wished him continued good health, renewed strength, wisdom and many more years of meaningful service to Nigeria, Africa and humanity.

title: Akume charges FRSC to ensure crash-free Christmas, New Year travels
description: Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), George Akume, has charged the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) to prevent avoidable road crashes and fatalities during the Christmas and New Year festivities, insisting that Nigerians must be guaranteed safe journeys, free traffic flow and prompt
content:
Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), George Akume, has charged the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) to prevent avoidable road crashes and fatalities during the Christmas and New Year festivities, insisting that Nigerians must be guaranteed safe journeys, free traffic flow and prompt emergency response.

Akume gave the directive on Thursday in Abuja while declaring open the FRSC End-of-Year 2026 Corps Marshal Strategy Session with Commanding Officers, ahead of the anticipated increase in vehicular movement across the country during the festive season.

He directed the Corps to intensify intelligence-driven operations and pay particular attention to speeding, dangerous overtaking, overloading, impaired driving and driver fatigue, which remain major risks on Nigerian highways.

The SGF said the success of the Corps’ festive season operations would be measured not by activities or deployments but by tangible improvements in road safety.

“Ultimately, our success must be reflected in fewer crashes and fatalities, improved traffic flow, effective emergency response and greater public confidence,” he said.

Akume charged Zonal and Sector Commanders to take full responsibility for operations within their jurisdictions, ensuring that directives from the Corps leadership translate into visible results on the highways.

He said the strategy session, themed “Strengthening Operational Readiness and Effective Coordination for Seamless Traffic Management During the 2026 Festive Season,” must produce a practical operational plan, clear deployment arrangements, stronger inter-agency collaboration and measurable performance indicators.

The SGF warned that the festive period traditionally comes with increased movement of people and goods, heightening the risks of road crashes and traffic congestion.

He therefore urged the FRSC leadership to objectively assess its performance as the year winds down, acknowledge its achievements and address operational shortcomings.

Akume reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to strengthening institutions responsible for public safety, stressing that road safety remained a national priority requiring sustained government commitment and collective responsibility.

He said the administration of President Bola Tinubu, under the Renewed Hope Agenda, recognises safe and efficient transportation as critical to economic growth, national security and citizens’ well-being.

The SGF also urged the Corps to sustain its institutional reforms, manpower development and digital transformation initiatives while ensuring prudent, transparent and accountable management of public resources.
He stressed that professionalism, discipline, innovation and measurable results must define the Corps’ operations.

“Preventable crashes and unprofessional conduct must not undermine public confidence in the Corps,” he warned.

Akume assured Nigerians travelling for the Christmas and New Year celebrations that effective arrangements would be put in place to protect lives, reduce congestion and facilitate the safe movement of people and goods.

He, however, emphasised that the Federal Government’s continued support for the FRSC must be matched by professionalism, commitment and demonstrable improvements in operational performance.

The strategy session brought together the Corps Marshal, members of the management team, Zonal Commanding Officers, Commandants of Training Institutions, Sector Commanders and other senior officers of the Corps.

Akume commended the Corps Marshal for convening the meeting ahead of the festive season, describing it as an opportunity to review performance, identify operational gaps and strengthen road safety administration nationwide.

title: Zamfara Govt. inaugurates committee to review salary structure for tertiary institutions
description:
From John Bassey, Gusau
Zamfara State Government has inaugurated a committee to review and address the non-implementation of revised salary structures and other staff welfare issues in the state-owned tertiary institutions.
According to the statement signed by Suleman Ahmad Tudu, Senior Special Assi
content:
From John Bassey, Gusau

Zamfara State Government has inaugurated a committee to review and address the non-implementation of revised salary structures and other staff welfare issues in the state-owned tertiary institutions.

According to the statement signed by Suleman Ahmad Tudu, Senior Special Assistant (Media), Office of the Secretary to the Zamfara State Government and made available to Journalists on Thursday, the Secretary to the State Government and Chairman of the Committee, Malam Abubakar Mohammad Nakwada, inaugurated the committee and chaired its maiden meeting in Gusau, the state capital.

The committee is expected to examine relevant government circulars towards addressing all outstanding welfare concerns of staff in the institutions.

It will also determine financial implications and funding requirements involved, and consult relevant stakeholders to facilitate amicable resolution.

Speaking at the inauguration, Malam Nakwada reaffirmed the administration’s commitment to staff welfare, industrial harmony, and the repositioning of tertiary education in the state.

He further emphasized that Governor Lawal has proven to be workers-friendly, citing the upward review of the minimum wage from paltry N7,000 to N70,000, the clearing of the backlog of gratuities, implementing new salary scale for healthcare workers, and other welfare commitments of the current administration.

“This assignment is a clear demonstration of Governor Lawal’s commitment to the welfare of workers, industrial harmony, and the development of our tertiary institutions.

“The demands presented by the Forum of Zamfara State Tertiary Institutions (FOZASTI) and the Zamfara State University on salary, allowances and promotion benefits have been a source of concern. The government considers it necessary to address these issues holistically, fairly and sustainably.

“Our assignment must be guided by objectivity, sincerity, and the best interest of the State. We must listen to all parties, examine the facts and figures dispassionately, and come up with recommendations that are implementable, affordable and just.

“I assure the staff unions and management of our institutions that this Government is not unmindful of their plight. At the same time, we must also be mindful of the financial realities of the State.

“Our goal is to find a lasting solution that will guarantee industrial peace and improve the quality of education in Zamfara State,” the SSG stated.

Malam Nakwada further appealed for patience and understanding as the government works gradually but deliberately to address staff welfare concerns, stressing that while not all issues can be resolved at once, every legitimate demand is being given the attention it deserves.

He urged aggrieved unions to give dialogue a chance and allow the committee to complete its assignment, noting that industrial action at this critical moment would only hurt but not help the system.

Members of the Committee include Honourable Commissioners for Finance, Education, Science and Technology, Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, and Budget and Planning.

Other members are Special Adviser on Economic and Financial Matters, the Representatives of the Forum of Tertiary Institutions, the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Zamfara State Chapter, and Zamfara State University, while the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Education, Science and Technology, serves as Secretary.

The post Zamfara Govt. inaugurates committee to review salary structure for tertiary institutions appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Rivers promises new wage structure, urges ASUP to end strike
description:
The Rivers State Government says it has commenced the necessary processes for implementing the new wage structure for members of the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics.
The government urged the union to suspend its ongoing industrial action and return to the classrooms.
The government gave the ass
content:
The Rivers State Government says it has commenced the necessary processes for implementing the new wage structure for members of the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics.

The government urged the union to suspend its ongoing industrial action and return to the classrooms.

The government gave the assurance during a meeting with the leadership of ASUP in Rivers State led by the Secretary to the State Government, Dr Dagogo Wokoma, on Thursday.

Also at the meeting were the Commissioner for Education, Dr peters  Nwagor, and the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Education, Dr Mina Ikuru.

This was contained in a statement issued by Dr Juliana Masi, Head, Information and Public Relations Unit, Office of the Secretary to the State Government and sent to newsmen.

The meeting according to the statement focused on issues surrounding the ongoing strike and the implementation of the new wage structure for academic staff in the state’s polytechnics.

The government reaffirmed its commitment to addressing the concerns raised by the union, disclosing that the necessary administrative and financial processes for implementing the new wage structure were already underway.

While acknowledging the grievances of the union, the government appealed to its leadership to reconsider its position and call off the strike in the interest of students, parents and the overall development of the state’s education sector.

It stressed that sustained engagement and constructive dialogue remained the most effective means of resolving outstanding issues, assuring ASUP that the government was committed to fulfilling its obligations and maintaining a harmonious working relationship with academic staff.

The SSG urged members of the union to resume academic activities while discussions and implementation processes continued to prevent further disruption to the academic calendar.

“The Rivers State Government urges ASUP members to return to the classrooms while discussions and necessary implementation processes continue, to prevent further disruption to the academic calendar,” Wokoma said.

He reaffirmed governor Siminalayi Fubara’s commitment to workers’ welfare and the provision of a conducive environment for quality education across the state.

“Governor Siminalayi Fubara remains committed to the welfare of workers and the provision of a conducive environment for quality education across the state,” he added.

The ASUP delegation included Bariakwaadro Bere, Chairman of ASUP, Kenule Beeson Saro-Wiwa Polytechnic Bori Chapter; Destiny Obinna, Chairman of ASUP, Rivers State College of Health Science and Management; and Ezekiel Tamu-nodiepriye, Chairman of ASUP, Captain Elechi Amadi Polytechnic, Port Harcourt.

Recall that academic activities across Rivers State owned Polytechnics and Colleges of Education were disrupted as lecturers embarked on indefinite strike over their unpaid allowances.

The Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics had directed its branch chairman in the state to mobilise members for the strike of the state government fails to meet its demands.

The strike had entered the fourth day before the government intervention on Thursday.

title: Senate panel backs FCC lawsuit against Customs over recruitment
description:
The Senate Committee on Legislative Compliance has thrown its weight behind the Federal Character Commission’s decision to institute legal proceedings against the Nigeria Customs Service over alleged violations of the federal character principle in its 2025/2026 recruitment exercise.
The committee a
content:
The Senate Committee on Legislative Compliance has thrown its weight behind the Federal Character Commission’s decision to institute legal proceedings against the Nigeria Customs Service over alleged violations of the federal character principle in its 2025/2026 recruitment exercise.

The committee also urged the commission to extend its scrutiny to other ministries, departments and agencies of the Federal Government to ensure compliance with the Federal Character Commission Act.

The committee made its position known in a letter dated November 18, 2026, signed by its Chairman, Senator Garba Madoki, and addressed to the Chairman of the Federal Character Commission, and titled, ‘Commendation on the Federal Character Commission’s Action Against the Nigeria Customs Service for Non-Compliance with the Federal Character Principle in its Recruitment Exercise’.

In the letter, the committee commended the commission for taking legal action against the Customs Service over alleged non-compliance with the provisions of the Federal Character Commission Act.

“I write to commend the Federal Character Commission for its bold decision to institute legal proceedings against the Nigeria Customs Service over alleged non-compliance with the provisions of the Federal Character Commission Act in its 2025/2026 recruitment process,” the letter stated.

The committee described the action as a demonstration of the commission’s commitment to fairness, equity, inclusiveness and equal representation in the distribution of recruitment opportunities within the Federal Public Service.

“It is particularly encouraging that the Commission has taken concrete steps to enforce compliance with its statutory mandate, rather than allowing apparent violations of the Federal Character principle to go unchallenged,” it said.

The committee further assured the Commission of its support, citing its oversight responsibility to ensure compliance with legislation, resolutions and directives of the Senate.

“In view of the Committee’s oversight mandate, particularly as it relates to ensuring compliance with legislation, resolutions and directives of the Senate, the Committee wishes to assure the Commission of its full support in this important endeavour,” the letter added.

It also urged the commission to extend similar scrutiny to other government institutions where there might be violations of the Act, particularly in recruitment, appointments and other personnel-related processes.

“While commending the Commission for this initiative, the Committee wishes to encourage it to extend similar scrutiny to other Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) of the Federal Government where there may be instances of non-compliance with the provisions of the Federal Character Commission Act, particularly in their recruitment, appointments and other personnel-related processes,” it stated.

According to the committee, such action would strengthen enforcement of the law and ensure that no government agency is exempted from the principles of fairness and equitable representation.

The post Senate panel backs FCC lawsuit against Customs over recruitment appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: PSC appoints new police commissioners for Abia, Zamfara
description:
The Police Service Commission(PSC), has approved the appointment of police commissioners for Abia and Zamfara States.
PSC Head, Protocol and Public Relations Torty Njoku Kalu, Who made this known gave the names of the police commissioners as Sylvester Adaji Edogbanya for Abia state and Sirajo Lawal
content:
The Police Service Commission(PSC), has approved the appointment of police commissioners for Abia and Zamfara States.

PSC Head, Protocol and Public Relations Torty Njoku Kalu, Who made this known gave the names of the police commissioners as Sylvester Adaji Edogbanya for Abia state and Sirajo Lawal Salisu to Zamfara State.

CP Sylvester Adaji Edogbanya, is taking over from AIG Wilfred Olutokunbo following his promotion to a higher rank, while CP Sirajo Lawal Salisu, (CP, Zamfara State) is to take over from CP Ahmed M. Bello following his retirement from service.

Kalu, in a statement, said that The posting followed an interview session by Board Members of the Commission today at the Commission’s Corporate Headquarters, Abuja.

He said The session was presided over by Hon. Justice Paul Adamu Galumje, (rtd), who represented the Chairman of the Commission, DIG Hashimu Salihu Argungu (rtd), alongside other Board Members including DIG (Dr.) Taiwo Lakanu (rtd), and the Secretary to the Commission, Chief Onyemuche Nnamani.

CP Edogbanya attended the Cadet ASP Course 18, POLAC Wudil, Advanced/Junior Command Courses and TLCC at Staff College Jos, Simulation Course at AFCSC Jaji, SLCC at NIPS Abuja, and EIMC 15 at NISS Bwari.

He earlier served in Sokoto, Katsina, Akwa Ibom and Bauchi Commands, Police Colleges Maiduguri and Kaduna, as Pioneer Area Commander Itu-Ibiono, Area Commander Nnewi, DC DOPS Yobe and Zone 13, and DC ZCID Zones 6 and 8, before serving as CP CPTU, Staff College Jos.

CP Sirajo Lawal Salisu, who was Appointed Cadet ASP on 10th June 1994, holds a BA (Hons) English and a PGD in Public Policy and Administration, with courses including TLCC Jos, Professional Service Delivery, Lagos, and Squadron Commanders Combat Operation Courses at Ila Oragun and Ende Hills.

He previously served as PPRO Katsina, DPO Jibiya, Sabon Gari and Shasha, Area Commander Kaltingu, Commander 53 PMF Bama and 16 PMF Abeokuta, AC Intelligence PSFU Lagos, and Coordinator, FMIU, PSFU Lagos.

The PSC Chairman charged the new State CPs to demonstrate neutrality, diligence, and apply responsible policing with a human face in their new Commands, noting that humility is an asset.

The approval has been conveyed to the Inspector-General of Police in a letter signed by the Secretary to the Commission, Chief Onyemuche Nnamani, Esq, for further necessary action.

The post PSC appoints new police commissioners for Abia, Zamfara appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

His appointment will come to effect in January, 2027, when the tenure of the outgoing Vice Chancellor, Profes
content:
A Professor of Agronomy at Bayero University, Kano, Professor Muhammad Awwal Hussein, has emerged as the new Vice-Chancellor of the Federal University of Technology, Babura, in Jigawa State.

His appointment will come to effect in January, 2027, when the tenure of the outgoing Vice Chancellor, Professor Szbo Ibrahil Birnin Kudu will expire.

The Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the Governing Council, Professor Onimawo Ignatius Akhakhia, announced the decision of the council after a meeting of the Joint Council/Senate Selection Committee.

Accepting the appointment, Professor Hussein pledged to live up to the expectations of the University community and general public by consolidating the gains of the University in the last five years.

“I will mobilise resources, both human and material, to sustain the growth trajectory of the university, while praying to God to guide me to steer the affairs of the university to greater heights,” he declared.

Daily Sun reports that the incoming Vice-Chancellor is a graduate of Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, where he obtained his degree, his Masters and his PhD in 2000.

He started his academic career at ABU in 1990 before joining Bayero University, Kano, in 2004, where he was appointed the first Director of the Centre for Dryland Agriculture.
