content:
Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has revealed plans to invite President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to attend his second-term inauguration on November 27.

Outlining the schedule, the Chairman of the Inauguration Planning Committee and Secretary to the State Government, Hon. Teslim Igbalaye, disclosed on Thursday that the weeklong lineup of activities will commence on Friday, November 20, with a special Jumat prayer at the Central Mosque in Oja-Oba, Osogbo.

This, according to him, will be followed by an Inter-Faith Prayer Session on Saturday at the Government House open parking lot in Osogbo.

Igbalaye added that the grand finale of the Ademola Adeleke Victory Soccer Tournament will take place on Saturday afternoon, culminating in a Night of Praise and Worship at the Government House Banquet Hall, on Sunday.

On Monday, November 23, the benevolence outreach programme targeting orphanages and the less privileged will be rolled out across the state.

Activities will continue on Tuesday with the Osun Youth Summit, Innovation, and Enterprise event hosted at the Oasis Events Hall.

A statewide broadcast by Governor Adeleke will take place on Wednesday, preceding an inauguration lecture titled “Federalism Dilemma: Navigating Institutional Friction, Local Government Allocations, and Executive Overreach,” to be delivered by Senator Shehu Sani at the Aurora Event Hall, Osogbo.

The planning committee further stated that ceremonial parade rehearsals will take place on Thursday at the Osogbo City Stadium, alongside entertainment and reception events for government officials and labor unions at the Government House Banquet Hall.

According to Igbalaye, the weeklong inauguration program will officially conclude on Sunday with a Thanksgiving Service at the Cherubim and Seraphim Church in Oke-Gada, Ede.

He noted that several Senators, members of the House of Representatives, and members of the diplomatic corps have already confirmed their intention to attend the milestone event.

title: UK councillor stabbed, suspect arrested for attempted murder
description:
British police said on Thursday they had arrested a man after a local government representative was stabbed on the streets of the city of Bradford in northern England.
The 52-year-old councillor was found with serious injuries after the stabbing on a residential street on Thursday morning, West York
content:
British police said on Thursday they had arrested a man after a local government representative was stabbed on the streets of the city of Bradford in northern England.

The 52-year-old councillor was found with serious injuries after the stabbing on a residential street on Thursday morning, West Yorkshire Police said.

The man “was taken to hospital where his condition is described as serious but not life-threatening”, the police statement said.

A 32-year-old man suspected of the attack fled to a roof but was later brought down and charged with attempted murder.

Police said: “There is no information to suggest that this is a politically motivated incident at this time.”

The victim was named by the media as Councillor Ibrar Ali, a member of Your Bradford Independent group, which has 10 councillors, unpaid democratically elected representatives in local government.

Your Bradford Independent Group was supported in May elections by Your Party, a left-wing political party co-founded by veteran British socialist Jeremy Corbyn.

Ali was due to hold a meeting with locals on Saturday, which has been cancelled, according to the district council’s website.

Bradford has a population of around half a million and around 30 per cent of residents are Muslim.

The leader of Bradford’s council is from the hard-right anti-immigrant Reform party.

The head of the council’s Labour faction, Imran Khan, posted on Facebook that he was “horrified by this horrendous incident”.

AFP

title: Lagos moves to strengthen law against HIV stigma, discrimination
description:
By Lukman Olabiyi
Lagos State Government is working towards strengthening its legal framework to combat HIV-related stigma and discrimination, as part of efforts to remove barriers to prevention, testing and treatment of the disease.
The Chief Executive Officer of the Lagos State AIDS Control Agency
content:
By Lukman Olabiyi

Lagos State Government is working towards strengthening its legal framework to combat HIV-related stigma and discrimination, as part of efforts to remove barriers to prevention, testing and treatment of the disease.

The Chief Executive Officer of the Lagos State AIDS Control Agency (LSACA), Dr Folakemi Animashaun, disclosed this on Thursday at a media briefing at the Bagauda Kaltho Press Centre, Alausa, Ikeja, to flag off activities marking the 2026 World AIDS Day.

Animashaun said the state was working towards introducing a more effective legal framework to address emerging challenges associated with HIV and provide stronger protection for people living with the virus.

She explained that the existing legal framework being relied upon to address HIV-related discrimination originated in 2001, during the administration of President Bola Tinubu, then governor of Lagos State.

According to her, the proposed reforms are intended to bring the legal framework in line with contemporary realities and strengthen the protection of the rights and dignity of people living with HIV.

She identified stigma and discrimination as major obstacles to the state’s HIV response, noting that fear of being discriminated against could discourage people from undergoing HIV tests, disclosing their status or seeking medical attention.

The LSACA boss said the agency was collaborating with the State Gender and Human Rights Response Team and other relevant institutions to promote confidentiality, protect the dignity of people living with HIV and ensure appropriate responses to discriminatory practices.
She insisted that nobody should be denied healthcare or treated with indignity because of their HIV status.

Animashaun, who spoke on the theme, “Ending AIDS Starts with Access: Equity, Ownership and Sustainability,” said Lagos was also intensifying efforts to protect the gains recorded in the fight against HIV through increased domestic funding and stronger institutional capacity.

She disclosed that the state’s approved HIV budget allocation increased from approximately N791 million to N1.065 billion in 2026, representing an increase of about 35 per cent.
She said the state government had also procured antiretroviral medicines and that LSACA had commenced their distribution to people who depend on the drugs for treatment.

According to her, the intervention is designed to complement existing national and development-partner arrangements and strengthen the state’s capacity to ensure uninterrupted access to essential HIV medicines.

She, however, stressed that the success of the initiative would depend not merely on the procurement of medicines but also on effective forecasting, quality assurance, distribution and stock monitoring.

” The true measure of treatment security is not simply the purchase of medicines; it is whether the person who needs those medicines can obtain them consistently, without interruption,” she said.

The agency’s CEO further disclosed that Lagos was developing a 10-year HIV Response Transition and Sustainability Roadmap covering 2027 to 2036.

She said the roadmap would provide a framework for strengthening domestic financing, healthcare delivery, human resources, medicines and diagnostics, programme information, community participation and institutional accountability.

The roadmap, she added, was expected to be formally launched by Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu at the World AIDS Day Symposium scheduled for December 1, 2026, subject to the necessary approvals.

Providing an update on the state’s HIV response, Animashaun said consolidated programme records showed 387,558 HIV-negative test results and 7,584 HIV-positive results.

She clarified that the figures represented reported test results and should not be interpreted as the number of new HIV infections or necessarily as unique individuals.

She also disclosed that the maternal health programme recorded 156,122 new antenatal care clients and 156,109 HIV-negative test results among pregnant and breastfeeding women.
In community-based interventions, she said, 25,167 HIV tests were conducted among people aged 15 and above between January and October 2026, producing 1,166 positive results.

Animashaun said the figures underscored the importance of expanding access to testing and ensuring that people who test positive are promptly linked to treatment and sustained care.

She added that the agency was strengthening collaboration with healthcare institutions, development partners, community organisations and relevant government ministries and agencies to improve service delivery, programme coordination and accountability.

On prevention, she urged residents to obtain accurate information about HIV, know their status and take advantage of available preventive services, including condom use, HIV testing, pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP).

She also emphasised the importance of early diagnosis and consistent treatment, explaining that people living with HIV who take effective medication and maintain an undetectable viral load cannot transmit the virus sexually, a principle known as Undetectable = Untransmittable (U=U).

The post Lagos moves to strengthen law against HIV stigma, discrimination appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: NIBSS deepens drive for seamless cross-border payments to connect Africa’s markets
description:
By Chinenye Anuforo from Mauritius
The Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS) is deepening efforts to strengthen cross-border payment connectivity across Africa, supporting the adoption of multiple interoperable payment networks to facilitate seamless transactions, expand market access and unl
content:
By Chinenye Anuforo from Mauritius

The Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS) is deepening efforts to strengthen cross-border payment connectivity across Africa, supporting the adoption of multiple interoperable payment networks to facilitate seamless transactions, expand market access and unlock trade opportunities across the continent.

The organisation said Africa does not necessarily need to depend on a single regional payment infrastructure to achieve seamless cross-border payments, stressing that multiple national and regional payment systems could coexist and complement one another, provided they are interconnected.

Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NIBSS, Premier Oiwoh, stated this during an interview with journalists in Mauritius, Thursday, on the sidelines of the launch of the 2026 State of Inclusive Instant Payment Systems (SIIPS) in Africa Report, organised by the AfricaNenda Foundation in partnership with the World Bank and the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA).

Oiwoh urged African countries and payment infrastructure providers to move beyond prolonged discussions about integration and begin implementing practical solutions to connect existing payment systems across the continent.

He explained that existing regional arrangements, including the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS), could operate alongside other regional payment networks, noting that each system has its own settlement structures, operational arrangements and cost considerations.

“There is nothing wrong with having multiple payment systems. PAPSS is there and has its own costs, settlement arrangements and other structures. Other regions also have their own arrangements. Everybody should be allowed to pursue the system that works for them,” he said.

Describing the approach as a coalition of the willing, he argued that countries and regional blocs ready to advance payment integration should be encouraged to move forward rather than wait for a single continental arrangement to emerge.

He disclosed that some countries within the East African Community (EAC) had already developed integrated payment arrangements and were exploring connections with Nigeria.

According to him, connecting these systems to Nigeria’s payment infrastructure could provide access to a wider network of markets, including the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) region, through existing interoperability arrangements.

The NIBSS chief maintained that multiple payment rails would inevitably emerge across Africa, making interoperability more important than the pursuit of a single continental payment infrastructure.

“The bottom line is that there will be multiple rails on the continent, whether we like it or not. Anybody can choose the rails they want and decide how they want to connect.

“A single road does not lead to a market. You have multiple roads in and out of a market. That is how I see it,” he said.

He, however, stressed that stakeholders must prioritise practical implementation, observing that African countries and payment institutions had continued to discuss cross-border integration year after year without making sufficient progress.

He said payment switches and interoperability arrangements should become central priorities for stakeholders seeking to strengthen Africa’s financial ecosystem.

“At what point do we move to action? At what point do we say, let’s do this and move forward? For me, these are the things we should all focus on as payment switches and payment infrastructure providers,” he added.

Highlighting Nigeria’s experience, Oiwoh said the country had been among the pioneers of account-based instant payment systems and had continued to expand its capabilities beyond basic money transfers.

He explained that Nigeria’s payment infrastructure now supports additional functionalities, including direct debits, mandate creation and request-to-pay services, which are being integrated into a broader payment ecosystem.

According to him, the country’s experience and existing infrastructure could support faster integration with other African markets, particularly within West Africa, where countries share similarities in their financial and payment environments.

He expressed confidence that innovations developed within Nigeria could be deployed across the ECOWAS region more easily through regional collaboration than through separate bilateral engagements with individual countries.

The NIBSS chief urged African stakeholders to concentrate on building practical connections between existing systems rather than creating fragmented arrangements that could further complicate cross-border transactions.

He said the ultimate objective should be to enable Africans to make payments across countries with the same ease they experience when conducting domestic transactions, a development he noted would support cross-border trade, commerce and broader economic integration across the continent.

The post NIBSS deepens drive for seamless cross-border payments to connect Africa’s markets appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Trump, Putin, Xi agree to nuclear risk talks
description:
By Favour Ulebor



US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping have agreed to hold talks on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons following a trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China.







The agreement was containe
content:
By Favour Ulebor

US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping have agreed to hold talks on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons following a trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China.

The agreement was contained in a joint declaration issued by the White House on Thursday after the meeting, during which the three leaders discussed the international situation and pledged to promote strategic stability and international security.

The United States, Russia and China, which are permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, also committed to reforming the UN to enable it to respond more effectively to global challenges and strengthen its role in maintaining international peace and security.

The three countries further indicated plans to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products, while reaffirming the importance of stable energy flows.

The leaders also addressed issues relating to the immunity of state officials and the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Court (ICC), warning against what they described as the abuse of jurisdiction by the court and similar bodies.

Trump and Putin also expressed appreciation to China for hosting the trilateral summit.

The joint declaration read in part: “The three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.

“As permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, the United States, Russia, and China committed to reform the UN so that the UN can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security.

“The three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations. They reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows.

“The three heads of state recognised that the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of state officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction.”

title: Mob kills accident survivor after crash claims two lives in Osun

The mob also set the vehicle involved in the accident ablaze.
Reacting, the Osun State Police Command condemned the incident, warning residents against taking th
content:
An angry mob in Ilesa, Osun State, has beaten a survivor of a road accident to death after the crash claimed the lives of two pedestrians.

The mob also set the vehicle involved in the accident ablaze.

Reacting, the Osun State Police Command condemned the incident, warning residents against taking the law into their hands.

The police spokesperson, Abiodun Ojelabi, disclosed this in a statement obtained in Osogbo on Thursday.

Ojelabi said the accident, which occurred on Tuesday, involved an unregistered Toyota Camry, a TVS motorcycle and two pedestrians identified as Silas Seun and Matthew Dada.

According to him, the two pedestrians died at the scene, while the driver of the car, identified as 23-year-old Favour Fabunmi, and other occupants were rescued alive.

He said, “The unfortunate incident resulted in the immediate death of the two pedestrians at the scene of the accident. The driver of the vehicle, one Favour Fabunmi, ‘M’, 23 years old, and other occupants of the Toyota Camry were successfully rescued alive.

“However, in a disturbing turn of events, one of the rescued occupants was attacked and severely beaten by an angry mob. He was subsequently rushed to the hospital but was later confirmed dead. The vehicle was also set ablaze by the mob and completely burnt to ashes.”

Ojelabi said the case had been transferred to the command headquarters for a comprehensive investigation, adding that legal procedures had been initiated.

He quoted the Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Zungura, as saying he “strongly condemns the act of mob violence and warns members of the public against taking the law into their own hands.”

The CP urged residents to “resist the temptation to administer instant justice, irrespective of the circumstances, and allow the appropriate authorities to investigate and handle reported offences in accordance with the law.”

He also assured the public that the command would leave no stone unturned “in identifying all individuals who participated in the mob action, and anyone found culpable will be arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law.”

Ojelabi urged residents to remain calm and law-abiding, advising them to report accidents and criminal incidents to the nearest police station rather than resorting to violence.

The PUNCH had earlier reported that the police in Osun commenced an investigation into the killing of Monica Mary, a student of Westland University, Iwo, who was allegedly stabbed to death by unknown assailants.

The post Mob kills accident survivor after crash claims two lives in Osun appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: APC chieftain rejects Baba-Ahmed’s 2027 election prediction
description:
By Henry Umoru



ABUJA – A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Hon. Aminu Shehu Sharada, has faulted the National Chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Dr. Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, over his prediction that the ruling party could suffer significant losses in the 2027 general electi
content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA – A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Hon. Aminu Shehu Sharada, has faulted the National Chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Dr. Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, over his prediction that the ruling party could suffer significant losses in the 2027 general elections, particularly in northern Nigeria.

Sharada, in a statement he personally signed on Thursday, insisted that President Bola Tinubu enjoys political support in the North and would secure votes from the region in the 2027 presidential election.

He specifically rejected Baba-Ahmed’s projection that the APC would struggle to genuinely win even two or three states in northern Nigeria, describing the assessment as an underestimation of the political awareness, democratic maturity and independent judgment of voters in the region.

Baba-Ahmed had, in an interview, said it would be a miracle if the APC genuinely won two or three states in the North, citing what he described as public dissatisfaction with the ruling party at different levels.

“On the basis of the current disposition of the public towards APC at all levels, it will be a miracle if they genuinely win two or three states in the North,” he had said.

He also predicted possible APC losses across the South-East, South-South, parts of the South-West and North-Central.

However, Sharada argued that the political support enjoyed by Tinubu in northern Nigeria should not be dismissed on the basis of assumptions or projections by political commentators.

Defending the Tinubu administration’s record, the APC chieftain highlighted its economic reforms, infrastructure projects and interventions in education, healthcare, agriculture, housing and transportation.

He cited the removal of petrol subsidy, unification of the foreign exchange market and ongoing tax reforms as major policy decisions aimed at strengthening public finances and attracting investments.

He acknowledged that the reforms had generated considerable debate because of their immediate effects on household expenses, transportation costs and the general cost of living, but maintained that the administration considered them necessary for long-term economic stability.

On infrastructure, Sharada listed the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway and Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano Road among major projects being pursued by the Federal Government.

He also highlighted investments in railway modernisation, port improvements and electricity transmission.

In education, he pointed to the establishment of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), saying the initiative was designed to reduce financial barriers to higher education and improve access to tertiary education.

He also cited the Renewed Hope housing programme, healthcare interventions under the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative and the Presidential Compressed Natural Gas Initiative as part of the administration’s development agenda.

On agriculture, Sharada said government interventions involving fertilisers, improved seedlings, mechanisation, irrigation and access to agricultural financing were aimed at increasing food production and strengthening rural economies.

He also noted that Nigeria had recorded positive economic growth under the Tinubu administration, but acknowledged that such growth must translate into improved living conditions, affordable food, employment opportunities and increased purchasing power for ordinary Nigerians.

The APC chieftain maintained that the administration’s policies and development programmes deserved proper assessment rather than dismissal through political predictions.

He urged the ruling party to sustain engagement with citizens, address legitimate concerns and demonstrate the impact of its programmes across the country.

Reaffirming his confidence in Tinubu’s relationship with northern Nigeria, Sharada insisted that the region should not be written off ahead of the 2027 elections.

“Arewa stands with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. The North will stand with him and vote for him in 2027. No amount of political predictions or negative projections can take away the democratic right of the people to make their choice. The ballot box will ultimately speak,” he said.

The post APC chieftain rejects Baba-Ahmed’s 2027 election prediction appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Tinubu should grant interviews to Nigerian journalists, Akande says
description:
A former spokesman for ex-Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo, Laolu Akande, has urged President Bola Tinubu to grant interviews to Nigerian journalists, saying the local media should have the opportunity to hold the President accountable.







Akande made the call on Thursday while reacting to the contr
content:
A former spokesman for ex-Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo, Laolu Akande, has urged President Bola Tinubu to grant interviews to Nigerian journalists, saying the local media should have the opportunity to hold the President accountable.

Akande made the call on Thursday while reacting to the controversy surrounding Tinubu’s interview with American political strategist and lobbyist, Diana London.

He said he had no objection to the President granting an interview to a foreign journalist but questioned why Nigerian journalists had not been given similar opportunities to ask him questions on issues of national importance.

“I wish the President were also having interviews with Nigerian journalists. That’s my own main issue with this development.

“It’s not a bad thing that the President has chosen to have this interview; my worry is that he’s leaving out the Nigerian press. Why has he not made himself available for Nigerians to interrogate him?” he said.

On allegations that London received $4.5 million in connection with the engagement, Akande said the strategist had denied being paid as a lobbyist by the Federal Government for the interview.

He, however, called for greater transparency from the government to clarify the circumstances surrounding the engagement.

“As to the controversy whether this woman (Diana) was paid, the woman has denied that she was doing this as a paid lobbyist of the Federal Government. The ADC people are saying that there should be more clarity, there should be more transparency, yes.

“Let the Federal Government also give us more facts that this is not a paid-for interview. The most important thing is that Nigerians should be given the opportunity to interview Mr President,” Akande said.

The former presidential spokesman also recalled his experience in the Presidential Villa during the administration of ex-President Muhammadu Buhari, when Osinbajo served as Vice-President.

He said he considered it inappropriate for journalists invited to interview the President or Vice-President to demand payment for the opportunity.

“My own experience in the Villa, I wasn’t aware of any payment for an interview and I expressed this. When we were in the Villa, I considered it an insult to have an opportunity to interview the President and the Vice-President and be asking for money. The President of a country is the numero uno,” he said.

The controversy followed reports alleging that London received $4.5 million in connection with a lobbying arrangement involving the Nigerian government.

London, who heads London Global Strategies, has denied receiving $4.5 million from the Nigerian government or anyone else in the country.

She said she travelled to Nigeria to interview Tinubu for a documentary and to experience the country.

Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar also questioned whether the interview formed part of the reported $4.5 million lobbying arrangement.

Atiku cited United States filings identifying London as a consultant to DCI Group AZ, a firm engaged to work for Nigeria through Aster Legal.

He noted that the filings recorded a $4.5 million retainer paid to DCI Group but did not establish whether the presidential interview was covered by the arrangement.

He subsequently called on the Presidency to publish the lobbying agreement, disclose payments and invoices, and release the full, unedited recording of the interview.

The post Tinubu should grant interviews to Nigerian journalists, Akande says appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: ASUP begins strike in four South-West states over unpaid allowances
description: The Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics, Zone C, has directed all its chapters across state-owned polytechnics, colleges of technology, and monotechnics in Ogun, Oyo, Osun, and Ekiti states to embark on an industrial strike over the non-implementation of the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance an
content:
The Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics, Zone C, has directed all its chapters across state-owned polytechnics, colleges of technology, and monotechnics in Ogun, Oyo, Osun, and Ekiti states to embark on an industrial strike over the non-implementation of the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance and Earned Academic Allowance.

This was contained in a statement signed by the Zonal Executive Council of ASUP Zone C and read by its coordinator, Masopa, Adekunle Nurudeen, during a press conference held at the ASUP Secretariat, The Polytechnic, Ibadan, the Oyo State capital, on Thursday.

 The union lamented that while the Federal Government had commenced the payment of CATA and EAA to academic staff in Federal institutions on the CONPCASS salary structure, state governments in the zone—with the exception of Ondo State—had failed to follow suit.

Nurudeen stated that the strike action took effect on Monday, November 16, 2026, following the expiration of a 15-day ultimatum issued to state governments across the South-West zone.

According to the union, “The Federal Government concluded the renegotiation of the 2009/2010 agreement with ASUP in April 2026 under the Yayale Ahmed-led committee, birthing the 2025/2026 FGN/ASUP Agreement with an effective implementation date of January 1, 2026.

“It is on record and in the public domain that the Federal Government had commenced the implementation of CATA and EAA for members on the CONPCASS salary structure with reference to the effective date as contained in the agreement.

“However, our members in state-owned polytechnics and colleges of technology have not been considered after 10 months despite performing the same duties and facing the same economic hardship.

“We had written to all state governors on August 10, 2026, requesting the implementation of the agreement, and followed up with a reminder on September 21, 2026, to maintain industrial harmony.

“Following the lack of response, ASUP resolved at its 118th National Executive Council meeting held in Abuja between October 23 and 24, 2026, to issue a 15-day ultimatum to defaulting state governments, which elapsed on Tuesday, November 10, 2026.

“We are now directing all our chapters across state-owned polytechnics, colleges of technology, and monotechnics in Ogun, Oyo, Osun, and Ekiti states to embark on an industrial strike over the non-implementation of the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance and Earned Academic Allowance.”

While commending the Ondo State Government as the first and only state in the zone to implement the 2025/2026 agreement, ASUP criticised the governments of Ogun, Oyo, Osun, and Ekiti states for their silence.

“State governments should endeavour to treat our members in state-owned institutions appropriately, not as second-class citizens within the same national economy,” the union demanded.

ASUP Zone C listed its core demands to include the immediate implementation of CATA and EAA for academic staff in state-owned polytechnics, colleges of technology, and monotechnics across Ogun, Oyo, Osun, and Ekiti states, as well as the payment of accrued arrears from January 1, 2026, to date.

“Considering the unimpressive and demoralising conduct of the state governments of Ogun, Oyo, Osun, and Ekiti on the implementation of CATA and EAA, which has resulted in the non-implementation of these allowances, the Zonal Executive Council hereby reiterates the directive of the National Executive Council at the 118th NEC meeting; hence, we have directed all state chapters of ASUP to proceed on industrial strike effective from Monday, November 16, 2026,” the statement concluded.

The post ASUP begins strike in four South-West states over unpaid allowances appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: INEC warns youths against electoral violence, manipulation
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has urged young Nigerians to reject electoral violence, political manipulation, hate speech and misinformation ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The commission made the call during its South-South zonal engagement with youth organisations and other cr
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has urged young Nigerians to reject electoral violence, political manipulation, hate speech and misinformation ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The commission made the call during its South-South zonal engagement with youth organisations and other critical stakeholders, following an earlier engagement in the South-West.

According to a post on INEC’s X handle on Thursday, the engagement focused on strategies to promote peaceful participation, electoral integrity and credible elections, while encouraging young people to take greater responsibility for protecting Nigeria’s democratic process.

In his welcome address, the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Akwa Ibom State, Prof. Anugbum Onuacha, called on youths and other stakeholders to take ownership of the electoral process by actively participating in election planning and implementation.

He stressed that professionalism, transparency and stakeholder inclusion were essential to strengthening public confidence in elections.

Onuacha reaffirmed the commission’s neutrality, declaring that, “INEC has no political party and no candidates.”

He further noted that the commission remained committed to improving its electoral processes, stressing that, “No two elections are exactly the same.”

According to him, lessons learnt from previous electoral exercises would continue to guide the commission in improving subsequent elections.

In his goodwill message, the Akwa Ibom State Director of the National Orientation Agency (NOA), Mr. Mkpoutom U. Noa, commended INEC for organising the engagement, describing it as an important platform for addressing youth involvement in electoral violence.

He urged young Nigerians to understand the consequences of electoral offences and resist attempts by politicians to use them as instruments of violence.

“Youths must understand the consequences of electoral offences and avoid allowing themselves to be used as instruments of political violence,” he said.

Noa also expressed confidence in INEC’s commitment to improving the conduct of the 2027 elections, calling on young people to support efforts aimed at safeguarding the nation’s democratic process.

Similarly, the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC), through its Akwa Ibom State Coordinator, conveyed a goodwill message from its Director-General, Brigadier-General U. O. Ahmed, who commended the collaboration between INEC and the NYSC.

The message urged young Nigerians to embrace peace, demonstrate political maturity and take collective responsibility for protecting democracy.

It cautioned youths against allowing political differences, personal interests or financial inducements to turn them into agents of intimidation and electoral violence.

“Young Nigerians must not allow political differences, personal interests or financial inducements to turn them into agents of intimidation and electoral violence,” the message stated.

The engagement forms part of INEC’s efforts to strengthen youth participation, promote peaceful elections and encourage responsible civic behaviour ahead of the 2027 General Elections.

The post INEC warns youths against electoral violence, manipulation appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: FG doubles Gombe transmission capacity to 480MW
description:
The Federal Government has inaugurated electricity infrastructure projects in Gombe State, including a new substation in Billiri and upgraded transformers at the Gombe Transmission Substation, increasing the latter’s upstream transmission capacity to 480MW.
The projects were inaugurated on Thursday
content:
The Federal Government has inaugurated electricity infrastructure projects in Gombe State, including a new substation in Billiri and upgraded transformers at the Gombe Transmission Substation, increasing the latter’s upstream transmission capacity to 480MW.

The projects were inaugurated on Thursday by the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, who said they would strengthen electricity transmission and improve the capacity to meet growing demand in the state and neighbouring communities.

At the Gombe Transmission Substation, Tegbe said the installation of an additional 300MVA, 330/132kV transformer had doubled the station’s upstream transmission capacity from 300MVA to 600MVA, equivalent to 480MW.

He also said the replacement of an existing 30MVA, 132/33kV transformer with a 100MVA unit had increased the station’s downstream transformation capacity to 220MVA, equivalent to 176MW.

“The growing electricity demand exceeded the capacity of the existing infrastructure, resulting in suppressed demand. To address this, an additional 300MVA, 330/132kV transformer has been installed, doubling the upstream transmission capacity to 600MVA, equivalent to 480MW.

“Equally, the existing 30MVA transformer has been replaced with a 100MVA, 132/33kV transformer, increasing the downstream capacity to 220MVA, equivalent to 176MW,” the minister said.

According to Tegbe, the upgrades are expected to provide additional capacity for electricity consumers and accommodate more than 70,000 additional households.

The minister said the projects reflected President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to strengthening the national grid and addressing electricity supply challenges.

At Billiri, the government commissioned a new 2x60MVA, 132/33kV transmission substation with a combined transformation capacity of 120MVA, equivalent to approximately 96MW.

Funded by the World Bank and executed by Chris Ejik International Limited, the facility has six outgoing 33kV feeders and is connected to the existing Gombe-Savannah-Yola transmission line.

Tegbe said the substation would support agricultural activities, businesses and growing settlements in the area.

“The commercial exchanges, agricultural activities, small enterprises and growing settlements within this axis require electricity that is both accessible and dependable,” he said.

He added that the investment would extend the transmission network and give communities access to infrastructure needed to support economic activities.

The minister urged residents to protect the facilities against vandalism, warning that attacks on electricity infrastructure could disrupt businesses and household livelihoods.

Earlier, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Transmission Company of Nigeria, Sule Ahmed Abdulaziz, said the Billiri substation would strengthen the interface between transmission and distribution networks.

He said it would ease pressure on existing infrastructure and give the Jos Electricity Distribution Company greater flexibility to supply electricity to communities served by the facility.

Abdulaziz also urged the distribution company to increase its offtake of available electricity to ensure that residents and businesses benefit from the investment.

At the Gombe Transmission Substation, he said the reinforcement project was awarded to ISIN Electromechanical Industries Limited in June 2021 and completed in June 2026.

He explained that the contractor handled the design, manufacture, supply, testing, installation and commissioning of the transformers, as well as supporting structures and auxiliary equipment.

Abdulaziz said replacing transformers at an operational transmission station was technically demanding because electricity supply had to be maintained while the old equipment was removed and the new units installed.

Representing Governor Muhammadu Yahaya, the Commissioner for Energy Resources, Sanusi Ahmad, said the projects would strengthen the state’s electricity infrastructure and support economic expansion.

He said the state government had earlier commissioned two additional 33kV outgoing feeders in December 2023.

Ahmad also said the state was taking advantage of the Electricity Act 2023 through the implementation of the Gombe State Electricity Law 2025 and the establishment of the Gombe State Electricity Regulatory Commission.

“Our administration will continue to engage relevant Federal Government institutions, electricity market operators, private investors and development partners to explore opportunities that will further strengthen electricity supply across Gombe State,” he said.

The Mai Tangle, Danladi Sanusi, also commended the investment, describing the Billiri substation as a source of economic opportunity for the area.

He said improved electricity supply could stimulate businesses, attract investors, create jobs and improve healthcare and education.

The traditional ruler, however, urged the authorities to ensure proper maintenance and effective utilisation of the facilities to guarantee lasting benefits.

description:
President Bola Tinubu has conferred the Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger (GCON), Nigeria’s second-highest national honour, on renowned legal practitioner, Chief Wole Olanipekun, SAN.
The honour was announced on Thursday, November 19, 2026, during the launch of a six-volume publication title
content:
President Bola Tinubu has conferred the Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger (GCON), Nigeria’s second-highest national honour, on renowned legal practitioner, Chief Wole Olanipekun, SAN.

The honour was announced on Thursday, November 19, 2026, during the launch of a six-volume publication titled Wole Olanipekun Through the Cases in Abuja.

The book launch, held at the Body of Benchers Complex, formed part of activities marking the 75th birthday of the senior lawyer, which fell on November 18, as well as his 50 years at the Nigerian Bar and 35 years as a Senior Advocate of Nigeria.

Olanipekun is a former President of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) and currently serves as the Pro-Chancellor of the University of Lagos.

He previously received the national honour of Commander of the Order of the Federal Republic (CFR). The latest recognition elevates him to the GCON rank in acknowledgement of his contributions to the Nigerian legal profession and jurisprudence.

The ceremony was held as part of the WOC Justice Summit.

title: Two Inmates Escape From Kwara Correctional Centre, NCoS Begins Probe
description: Two condemned inmates have escaped from Oke-Kura Ilorin custodial centre, Kwara State.The inmates, identified as Segun and Abraham, reportedly escaped in the early hours of Wednesday after breaking and scaling the wall of the custodial centre.Abraham, it was learnt, had earlier escaped from Mandala
content:
Two condemned inmates have escaped from Oke-Kura Ilorin custodial centre, Kwara State.

The inmates, identified as Segun and Abraham, reportedly escaped in the early hours of Wednesday after breaking and scaling the wall of the custodial centre.

Abraham, it was learnt, had earlier escaped from Mandala custodial centre, but was later rearrested and kept at Oke-Kura custodial centre before the Wednesday escape.

A manhunt has, however, been launched by the Nigerian Correctional Service to rearrest the escaped inmates.

Oke-Kura custodial centre has also been placed under tight security following the latest incident as officers are on alert to forestall any unpleasant development.

Reacting to the development, on Thursday in Ilorin, the head of the Nigerian Correctional Service in the state, Sylvester Mwakuche, said that investigation so far showed some level of negligence, which he described as unfortunate and unacceptable, adding that the NCoS would get to the root of the matter.

“The Honourable Minister is not happy. Mr. President won’t be happy. Salaries are not being owed. Their welfare has been improved. Promotions have also been ongoing yearly, no backlogs.Promotional arrears paid. So I wouldn’t know the reason why such an unfortunate incident should happen,” he said.

“So what have you done to ensure that such things will not happen again? Well, naturally, this is a custodial facility. The correctional system is charged with the responsibility of safe custody. And we will always make sure that our inmates are treated well under humane conditions.

“And at the same time, we have to also drive our mandate that says we should keep them in safe custody. I’ve admonished the staff. I’ve also admonished the inmates. And I know that it will not occur again,” Mwakuche added.

title: Tinubu hails Jonathan at 69
description:
President Bola Tinubu on Thursday congratulated former President Goodluck Jonathan as he marks his 69th birthday on Friday, November 20.
Tinubu described the former Nigerian leader as “a patriot and statesman whose commitment to national unity, democratic governance and Nigeria’s peaceful advancemen
content:
President Bola Tinubu on Thursday congratulated former President Goodluck Jonathan as he marks his 69th birthday on Friday, November 20.

Tinubu described the former Nigerian leader as “a patriot and statesman whose commitment to national unity, democratic governance and Nigeria’s peaceful advancement remains an important part of the country’s political history.”

Tinubu conveyed his felicitations in a statement signed by his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga.

The president acknowledged Jonathan’s progression through successive tiers of elected office from Deputy Governor and Governor of Bayelsa State, through the Vice Presidency under the late President Umaru Musa Yar’Adua, to the presidency itself.

He also commended his continued engagement in peace, mediation, and democratic consolidation across Africa after leaving office.

“As Dr Jonathan celebrates this special occasion, President Tinubu wishes him continued good health, renewed strength, wisdom, and many more years of meaningful service to Nigeria, Africa, and humanity,” the statement read.

Born on November 20, 1957, in Ogbia, Bayelsa State, Jonathan rose through academic and administrative ranks, holding a doctorate in zoology from the University of Port Harcourt, before entering politics as deputy governor in 1999.

He became governor in 2005 following the impeachment of his principal, Diepreye Alamieyeseigha, and was elevated to the vice presidency in 2007 under Yar’Adua.

When Yar’Adua died in office in May 2010, Jonathan was sworn in as president, winning a full term in 2011 before his tenure ended after the 2015 general election.

Defeated by former General Muhammadu Buhari in the contest widely regarded as the most competitive in Nigeria’s post-military history, Jonathan reportedly placed a congratulatory phone call to Buhari before the final results were announced, conceding defeat.

Since leaving the Presidency, Jonathan has pursued an active career in conflict resolution and electoral mediation.

He has served as a special envoy of the Economic Community of West African States and led observer and mediation missions in Liberia, Senegal, and other West African states grappling with political instability.

His work through ECOWAS has included efforts to persuade military-led transitional governments in the Sahel, most notably Mali, to commit to credible electoral timelines.

Jonathan has also been a vocal advocate for the use of technology in electoral administration as a tool for improving the credibility of African elections.

The post Tinubu hails Jonathan at 69 appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Mbappe, Yamal, seven other footballers with €1bn release clauses
description:
Barcelona and Real Madrid have taken extraordinary measures to protect their most valuable players, reportedly inserting €1 billion release clauses into the contracts of several of their biggest stars.
The Spanish giants are using the enormous figures to discourage potential suitors, including wealt
content:
Barcelona and Real Madrid have taken extraordinary measures to protect their most valuable players, reportedly inserting €1 billion release clauses into the contracts of several of their biggest stars.

The Spanish giants are using the enormous figures to discourage potential suitors, including wealthy Saudi Pro League clubs, from attempting to lure their prized assets away.

Under Spanish football regulations, professional players must have release clauses in their contracts.

However, by setting the figures at €1 billion, Barcelona and Real Madrid have effectively made it extremely difficult for rival clubs to sign their stars without negotiating directly with them.

Some of the biggest names in world football are reportedly covered by these eye-watering clauses.

Here are nine players whose contracts are said to include a €1 billion release clause, according to Planet Football on Thursday.

1. Kylian Mbappe (Real Madrid)

Kylian Mbappe’s long-awaited arrival at Real Madrid in 2024 was one of the biggest moments in modern football.

The French superstar joined Los Blancos as a free agent after leaving Paris Saint-Germain, signing a five-year contract running until 2029.

According to Spanish outlet COPE, his deal reportedly includes a €1 billion release clause.

Given his status as one of the world’s leading footballers, Real Madrid are unlikely to consider selling him anytime soon.

2. Lamine Yamal (Barcelona)

Barcelona wasted little time protecting their most exciting young talent after Lamine Yamal broke into the first team.

The Spanish winger signed his first professional contract in 2023, when he was just 16, with the club reportedly including a €1 billion release clause.

His remarkable development has since established him as one of the best young players in world football.

Barcelona subsequently secured his future with a new contract running until 2031, making it clear that they view him as central to their long-term project.

3. Vinicius Junior (Real Madrid)

Vinicius Junior is another Real Madrid superstar reportedly protected by a €1 billion release clause.

The Brazilian forward signed a contract extension in 2022 that included the enormous figure.

Since then, he has developed into one of the most dangerous attackers in world football, playing a key role in Real Madrid’s domestic and European successes.

Despite occasional speculation about his future and reported interest from Saudi Arabia, the Spanish giants remain determined to keep him at the Santiago Bernabeu.

4. Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid)

Real Madrid secured Jude Bellingham’s signature from Borussia Dortmund in 2023 in a deal worth approximately €100 million.

The England international made an immediate impact in Spain, quickly becoming one of the club’s most important players.

His combination of creativity, goalscoring ability and physical strength has made him a major asset in Madrid’s midfield.

Bellingham, whose contract runs until 2029, reportedly has a €1 billion release clause designed to discourage potential buyers.5. Pedri (Barcelona)

5. Pedri (Barcelona)
Pedri became the first Barcelona player to receive a reported €1 billion release clause when he signed a contract extension in October 2021.

The Spanish midfielder has established himself as one of the finest playmakers in world football, thanks to his intelligence, technical ability and exceptional passing.

After overcoming several injury setbacks, he returned to top form under Hansi Flick and played a crucial role in Barcelona’s 2024-25 campaign.

The club further demonstrated its commitment to him by extending his contract until 2030 in January 2025.

6. Gavi (Barcelona)

Gavi followed Pedri’s example by signing a long-term contract extension with Barcelona, reportedly featuring a €1 billion release clause.

The Spanish midfielder, who came through the club’s famous La Masia academy, has become an important part of Barcelona’s future plans.

Although injuries and competition for places have affected his regular involvement, his energy, determination and technical quality make him a valuable member of the squad.

His contract runs until 2030.

7. Eduardo Camavinga (Real Madrid)

Eduardo Camavinga joined Real Madrid from Rennes in 2021 as one of Europe’s most promising young midfielders.

His versatility has made him an important option for the Spanish giants, with the Frenchman capable of playing in several midfield positions and even at left-back.

Following his impressive development, Madrid rewarded him with an improved contract in 2023, reportedly featuring a €1 billion release clause.

Although he still has areas of his game to develop, the club clearly sees him as an important part of its future.

8. Jules Kounde (Barcelona)

Jules Kounde joined Barcelona from Sevilla in 2022 and has since established himself as an important figure in the team’s defence.

The French international’s versatility, defensive discipline and ability to contribute going forward have made him a valuable player for the Catalan side.

Barcelona reportedly included a €1 billion release clause in his contract, which runs until 2030.

With several Premier League clubs having been linked with him, the enormous figure puts Barcelona in a strong negotiating position.

9. Rodrygo (Real Madrid)

Rodrygo completes the list of Real Madrid players reportedly protected by a €1 billion release clause.

The Brazilian forward signed a contract extension in 2023, keeping him at the club until 2028.

Since arriving from Santos, he has delivered several important performances, particularly in the Champions League, and developed into a valuable attacking option.

Despite occasional transfer speculation and competition for places in Madrid’s attack, the club has continued to value his contribution.

His reported €1 billion release clause makes any potential move away from the Bernabeu extremely difficult.

The post Mbappe, Yamal, seven other footballers with €1bn release clauses appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: APC, ADC clash over Katsina insecurity, governance
description:
The All Progressives Congress and the African Democratic Congress have traded accusations over political support, leadership credentials, and the performance of the Katsina State Government during separate campaign engagements in Kankia Local Government Area of the state.
While Governor Dikko Umaru
content:
The All Progressives Congress and the African Democratic Congress have traded accusations over political support, leadership credentials, and the performance of the Katsina State Government during separate campaign engagements in Kankia Local Government Area of the state.

While Governor Dikko Umaru Radda urged voters to reject what he described as irresponsible and disrespectful politicians and support APC candidates across all levels in the 2027 elections, the ADC governorship candidate, Senator Ahmed Babba Kaita, accused the ruling party of resorting to personal attacks because it lacked convincing achievements to present to the electorate.

Speaking during the APC campaign visit to Kankia on Thursday, Radda described the visit as a homecoming, expressing confidence that the people would support the party’s candidates in the forthcoming elections.

He said Kankia residents had benefited from several development projects facilitated by the former Minister of Housing and Urban Development, Architect Ahmed Musa Dangiwa.

“My visit to Kankia is a homecoming. It shows that Kankia people need good leaders. They are not in support of irresponsible and disrespectful persons.

“I believe that Kankia people have really benefited from a lot of projects brought by the former Minister of Housing and Urban Development, Architect Ahmed Musa Dangiwa. The people have assured and promised me that they will vote for the APC presidential candidate and other APC candidates from top to bottom,” the governor said.

Also speaking, the APC Deputy Chairman in Katsina State, Bala Abu Musawa, urged the people of Kankia to support a candidate from outside their locality, arguing that leadership should be determined by performance rather than place of origin.

He also questioned the ADC’s readiness for the 2027 elections, alleging that irregularities surrounding its governorship primary could affect the party’s chances.

Responding to the criticisms, Kaita dismissed the allegations against his character, insisting that those questioning his upbringing had no moral grounds to do so.

He accused APC campaigners of promoting individuals allegedly involved in drug-related activities while presenting themselves as champions of good conduct.

“Among all those talking about good character, I have not seen anyone who is more decent than me. If you are talking about good character, why would you promote someone involved in selling drugs?” he queried.

Kaita argued that the APC should have focused on assessing his record as a former senator representing the area rather than resorting to personal attacks.

He challenged the ruling party to ask Kankia residents whether his representation in the National Assembly was a success or failure.

The ADC candidate also criticised the state government’s handling of insecurity and the economic situation, questioning why political leaders were celebrating during campaigns when residents continued to face hardship.

He specifically alleged that Kankia General Hospital lacked essential medicines, despite the political activities of local government officials.

“At the Kankia hospital, where they went to tell people to vote for their candidate, there are no medicines. But the chairman keeps collecting money and producing posters. Who, then, is the irresponsible person between us?” he asked.

Kaita further alleged that government workers in the state had gone for about six months without receiving their salaries, while insecurity and economic hardship continued to affect residents.

On the suggestion that voting for the ADC in Katsina would amount to supporting former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Kaita dismissed the claim as an attempt to create confusion among voters.

He maintained that the ADC was determined to contest and win elections in Katsina State.

The former senator also alleged that the APC was relying on security personnel and financial inducements to facilitate its campaign activities across local government areas, claiming that some party officials were appealing to him to allow their campaign visits to proceed peacefully.

He said the ADC would concentrate on engaging voters rather than responding to what he described as baseless allegations.

The exchange highlights the growing political rivalry between the APC and ADC in Katsina State as political actors intensify consultations and mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The post 2027: APC, ADC clash over Katsina insecurity, governance appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: APGA officially adopts Tinubu as preferred presidential candidate
description:
The All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) has formally adopted President Bola Ahmed Tinubu as its preferred presidential candidate for the 2027 general election, pledging to mobilise support for his re-election across the country.
The decision was reaffirmed on Thursday, November 19, 2026, during t
content:
The All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) has formally adopted President Bola Ahmed Tinubu as its preferred presidential candidate for the 2027 general election, pledging to mobilise support for his re-election across the country.

The decision was reaffirmed on Thursday, November 19, 2026, during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally held at Alex Ekwueme Square in Awka, Anambra State.

Anambra State Governor and APGA National Leader, Professor Chukwuma Soludo, formally presented the party’s flag to Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who received it on behalf of President Tinubu.

Speaking at the event, Soludo said the decision followed consultations with the party’s leadership and was guided by its commitment to national unity, progressivism and cooperative federalism.

He explained that APGA had resolved to support Tinubu in the spirit of solidarity with the South, insisting that the region should be allowed to complete its presidential tenure before power returns to the North.

Soludo declared that members of APGA across the country would participate in campaigning and mobilising votes for the Tinubu-Shettima ticket ahead of the 2027 election.

The governor also urged Nigerians, particularly residents of the South-East, to embrace political engagement and build stronger relationships with the Federal Government rather than pursue political isolation.

He argued that greater cooperation between the region and the government at the centre would create opportunities for development and strengthen the South-East’s political influence.

The endorsement comes after APGA announced its decision to adopt Tinubu as its preferred presidential candidate during the inauguration of its national campaign in Awka on November 6.

At the earlier event, Soludo said APGA would not present its own presidential candidate for the 2027 election, explaining that the party had a history of supporting presidential candidates from other political platforms.

He also urged party members and supporters to work towards securing substantial votes for Tinubu, setting a target of at least 50 per cent of the votes in Anambra State.

The latest development further strengthens the political alliance between APGA and the ruling APC ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The post 2027: APGA officially adopts Tinubu as preferred presidential candidate appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Court restrains Jimmy Odukoya from parading as Fountain of Life senior pastor
description:
The Lagos State High Court has restrained Jimmy Odukoya from parading himself as the Senior Pastor and spiritual head of the Fountain of Life Church, Lagos.







Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin according to TheCable, granted the order on Wednesday following a suit instituted by the incorporated truste
content:
The Lagos State High Court has restrained Jimmy Odukoya from parading himself as the Senior Pastor and spiritual head of the Fountain of Life Church, Lagos.

Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin according to TheCable, granted the order on Wednesday following a suit instituted by the incorporated trustees of the church.

The trustees had sought a pre-emptive order of injunction restraining Odukoya from presenting himself as the church’s Senior Pastor and interfering with its activities, governance and other affairs.

They argued that Odukoya had ceased to hold the position following the appointment of a successor by the late founder and Senior Pastor of the church, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya.

In the suit, the trustees sought an order restraining Odukoya, whether acting personally or through proxies, from interfering with, disrupting, meddling with or obstructing the activities and governance of the church pending compliance with the High Court of Lagos State (Expeditious Disposal of Civil Cases) Practice Directions No. 2 of 2019 on pre-action protocol.

Granting the application, Justice Adewunmi-Oshin ruled: “Leave is hereby granted to the Applicant to commence this action under the Pre-Action Protocol pursuant to Paragraph 4 of the High Court of Lagos State (Expeditious Disposal of Civil Cases) Practice Direction No. 2 of 2019.”

The order followed the trustees’ application for judicial intervention in the leadership and administration of the church.

title: 2027: Atiku demands independent audit of INEC’s AI system
description:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has called on the Independent National Electoral Commission to subject its proposed Artificial Intelligence system to an independent audit before deploying it for processing results in the 2027 general elections.
Atiku said the use of AI in election result manage
content:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has called on the Independent National Electoral Commission to subject its proposed Artificial Intelligence system to an independent audit before deploying it for processing results in the 2027 general elections.

Atiku said the use of AI in election result management without adequate transparency and safeguards could undermine public confidence in the electoral process, particularly if algorithms were allowed to delay, reject or interfere with the transmission of polling unit results.

He asked the electoral commission to disclose the technical and operational details of the system, including its source code, training data, discrepancy-detection criteria and the identities of its developers and third-party vendors.

The former vice president made the demands in a petition addressed to the INEC Chairman on behalf of the African Democratic Congress and allied democratic stakeholders.

In a statement issued on Thursday by the Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said independent cybersecurity experts, political party representatives and civil society technologists should be granted access to the system for a comprehensive audit before the nationwide mock accreditation exercise scheduled for November 28, 2026.

He expressed concern over INEC’s announced integration of AI and intelligent document processing into the process linking its Data Verification and Authentication System with the INEC Result Viewing portal.

According to him, Nigerians should be informed about how the technology works and its role in election result management.

“INEC cannot ask Nigerians to trust a system whose rules they are forbidden to see. If an algorithm can flag a polling unit result sheet, the public deserves to know what triggers that flag, who set the threshold, who can change it and what happens to the result afterward,” he said.

Atiku said technical limitations, including poor lighting, unfamiliar handwriting and worn-out paper, could cause legitimate result sheets to be flagged or delayed.

He argued that such difficulties should not be grounds for withholding valid election results and called for discrepancies to be treated consistently across polling units.

The former presidential candidate also asked INEC to establish and publicise a procedure for reviewing results flagged by the AI system.

He said the commission should explain who would review such results, how decisions would be documented, how political parties would be notified and how erroneous assessments could be challenged.

Atiku said AI should serve only as an administrative tool under human supervision and should not be allowed to delete, alter or permanently block election results.

He also asked the commission to reaffirm the legal status of Form EC8A, the polling unit result sheet completed and signed by presiding officers and party agents.

“The polling unit result sheet, Form EC8A, records what happened where the people voted. INEC must publicly reaffirm the legal status of the physical form completed and signed at the polling unit, and explain how it will resolve any conflict between that document and an AI assessment.

“A machine’s verdict cannot be allowed to quietly displace the evidence witnessed by voters and party agents,” he added.

The ADC presidential candidate called for real-time monitoring access for political parties through a dedicated dashboard or observer interface to enable them to monitor result flagging, upload delays and blocked submissions during elections.

He urged the National Assembly to summon INEC’s leadership and its Information and Communication Technology Directorate to explain the system’s design, safeguards and independent audit arrangements.

Atiku also called on election observers and international partners to include the digital handling and transmission of results in their monitoring activities.

He advised voters to document results as announced and displayed at their polling units to provide records for comparison with electronically uploaded results.

The former vice president linked the demand for transparency to his campaign’s promise of an affordable life, saying Nigerians should be allowed to determine their political future without technological interference.

“Voters must be free to accept or reject that promise at the ballot box. No hidden algorithm should stand between a struggling family’s vote and the change that family hopes to see,” he said.

He urged INEC to address the concerns before public mistrust over the technology escalated into an electoral crisis.

INEC’s IReV portal provides public access to scanned copies of polling unit result sheets. The portal is distinct from the statutory process of collating and declaring election results.

The post 2027: Atiku demands independent audit of INEC’s AI system appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Don’t give terrorists undue publicity, ex-presidential spokesman urges media
description:
Former presidential spokesman, Femi Adesina, has urged Nigerian journalists and media organisations to exercise greater responsibility in their coverage of insecurity, warning that excessive publicity for terrorists and purveyors of ethnic and religious hatred could undermine national security.
Ades
content:
Former presidential spokesman, Femi Adesina, has urged Nigerian journalists and media organisations to exercise greater responsibility in their coverage of insecurity, warning that excessive publicity for terrorists and purveyors of ethnic and religious hatred could undermine national security.

Adesina, who served as Special Adviser on Media and Publicity to the late President Muhammadu Buhari, said the media must resist the temptation to amplify the activities and propaganda of terrorists while giving insufficient attention to the sacrifices and achievements of Nigeria’s security forces.

He made the call on Thursday while delivering a paper titled ‘Media, Conflict and National Security: The Journalist’s Role in a Changing Security Landscape’ at the second Nigeria Union of Journalists, Ogun State Broadcasting Corporation Annual Lecture, held at Iwe Iroyin Hall, NUJ Press Centre.

The former presidential spokesman said journalists had an enormous responsibility to ensure that their platforms promoted national development, mitigated conflict and strengthened public confidence in the country rather than creating fear, division and hopelessness.

He argued that although the media must hold governments accountable and report the country’s challenges truthfully, it should not allow negative narratives to overshadow genuine progress.

“I am not asking anybody to ignore the reality we live in and become propagandists for the government, no. Instead, we must be truthful and realistic. And reality is very different from the relentlessly negative messaging that the platforms of mass communication keep deliberately pushing day after day.

“Reality is about acknowledging the good, while also not ignoring the bad. Reality is about finding the right balance, and I would, in fact, like to argue that this should be done with a bias towards the positive.

“Nigeria has many challenges, many of which we have been dealing with for a long time, but we are also making progress in very important ways, and we must inspire ourselves with this progress as a way of convincing ourselves that even our most protracted challenges are not insurmountable,” Adesina said.

He expressed concern that media coverage of insecurity often gave disproportionate attention to terrorist activities, while the courage and sacrifices of members of the Nigerian Armed Forces and other security agencies received comparatively less prominence.

Adesina maintained that media organisations should not become platforms through which terrorists communicate threats, promote their causes or intimidate the population.

To reinforce his argument, he cited a 1985 speech by former British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher to the American Bar Association, in which she warned against providing terrorists with what she described as the “oxygen of publicity”.

“The media must resist the pervading belief that only bad news sells. Why is it that the activities of Boko Haram are usually amplified in the media, while no one gets to hear about the more frequent heroism of the gallant officers and men of the Nigerian Armed Forces?” he asked.

He also quoted Thatcher as saying:

“For newspapers and television, acts of terrorism inevitably make good copy and compelling viewing. The hijacker and the terrorist thrive on publicity: without it, their activities and their influence are sharply curtailed.

“There is a fearful progression, which the terrorists exploit to the full. They see how acts of violence and horror dominate the newspaper columns and television screens of the free world.

“They see how that coverage creates a natural wave of sympathy for the victims and pressure to end their plight, no matter what the consequence. And the terrorists exploit it. Violence and atrocity command attention. We must not play into their hands.”

Adesina said Thatcher had also urged media organisations to consider adopting a voluntary code of conduct to prevent the publication or broadcast of material capable of boosting terrorists’ morale or advancing their cause.

He said the warning remained relevant more than four decades later, particularly in an era when social media had made the dissemination of information faster and more difficult to regulate.

“Over forty years later, those words still ring very true. There is no justification for media houses and professionals of mass communication acting as spokespersons and loudspeakers for terrorists. If there is anything to be amplified, it must be the heroism of our law enforcement agents,” he said.

He, however, cautioned that responsible reporting of insecurity should not be confused with censorship or the suppression of legitimate criticism.

Adesina urged journalists to exercise sound editorial judgment, verify information and avoid publishing material that could unnecessarily heighten tensions, compromise security operations or encourage violence.

The former presidential spokesman also drew attention to the destructive consequences of irresponsible media practices, citing the 1994 Rwandan genocide, during which radio broadcasts played a significant role in inciting ethnic hatred and violence.

He identified Radio Rwanda, a government-owned station, and Radio Télévision des Mille Collines (RTLM), a privately owned broadcaster, as two media organisations whose broadcasts helped fuel the genocide, which claimed close to one million lives.

He noted that several broadcasters associated with the stations were subsequently prosecuted and convicted of genocide-related crimes.

Adesina reminded journalists that Nigeria’s future was a collective responsibility and that media professionals had an obligation to deploy their influence in the interest of national progress.

“You have a lot of power in your hands. Wield it with the utmost sense of care and responsibility, everywhere you find yourselves.

“Nigeria belongs to all of us, and we must make it work. When Nigeria works, it is for the benefit of all of us, including the present and future professionals of Mass Communication.

“You, of course, are the future of the profession in Nigeria, and you must look forward with hope and expectation, determined to do your best just as those before you have done theirs. So help you God,” he said.

He urged media practitioners, particularly younger journalists, to recognise the influence they wield and use it to strengthen national unity, promote responsible public discourse and contribute to building a more secure and prosperous Nigeria.

The post Don’t give terrorists undue publicity, ex-presidential spokesman urges media appeared first on Punch Newspapers.
