The command’s Police Public Relations Officer, Superintendent Ramhan Nansel, disc
content:
By Edwin Philip, Lafia

The Nasarawa State Police Command has arrested nine suspects over an armed robbery at student hostels in Keffi and rescued three kidnapped victims in Awe Local Government Area of the state.

The command’s Police Public Relations Officer, Superintendent Ramhan Nansel, disclosed this in a statement issued to journalists in Lafia on Thursday.

Nansel said the arrests followed a distress call reporting that suspected armed robbers had invaded student hostels behind Princess Sarah in Keffi and dispossessed occupants of their belongings.

He said operatives attached to the Angwan Lambu Division promptly mobilised to the scene but the suspects fled before their arrival.

Acting on intelligence, the police team reportedly trailed the suspects to a hotel on the outskirts of Keffi, where nine persons were arrested.

Items recovered from them included a cutlass, a long stick, eight mobile phones and substances suspected to be illicit drugs.

The police spokesman said investigations had commenced, adding that the suspects had been identified by their victims and were cooperating with investigators by providing useful information to establish their respective levels of involvement.

On the rescue operation in Awe, Nansel said three kidnapped victims were rescued in the Hunki axis, between Awe and Azara, following intelligence that armed bandits had abducted some persons and were holding them hostage in a forest.

According to him, the Commissioner of Police immediately mobilised operatives of the Violent Crimes Response Unit (VCRU) and other patrol teams to the area.

The operatives combed the forest and engaged the kidnappers, mounting pressure on them until they abandoned the victims and fled.

The rescued victims were identified as Habibu Samaika, 40, from Gulbin Dutsi, Ubi Local Government Area of Taraba State; Audi Abubakar, 40, from Shendam Local Government Area of Plateau State; and Shafiu Zakari, 19, from Azara in Awe Local Government Area of Nasarawa State.

Nansel said the victims were rescued unhurt and taken to Azara General Hospital for medical attention, where they were confirmed to be in stable condition.

He added that their relatives had been contacted and arrangements were being made to reunite them with their families after their discharge.

The Commissioner of Police, CP Sheikh Mohammed Danko, commended the operatives for their prompt response, courage and professionalism during the two operations.

Danko reassured residents of the command’s commitment to protecting lives and property, adding that intelligence-led operations, patrols and other security exercises would be sustained to dismantle criminal networks and their hideouts.

He urged residents to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements and criminal activities to the nearest police station, assuring them that information supplied would be treated with utmost confidentiality.

title: 2027: Atiku demands scrutiny of INEC’s AI system for processing election results
description:
By Luminous Jannamike



ABUJA — Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to open its proposed artificial intelligence system for processing election results to independent audit ahead of the 2027 general elections.







Atiku wants t
content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA — Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to open its proposed artificial intelligence system for processing election results to independent audit ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Atiku wants the commission to disclose how the technology works, who developed it and what safeguards are in place to prevent valid polling unit results from being flagged, delayed or excluded during electronic processing.

In a statement by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said he had petitioned the INEC Chairman on behalf of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, and allied democratic stakeholders, demanding algorithmic transparency, independent scrutiny and clear rules for human oversight.

The petition follows INEC’s announced integration of artificial intelligence and intelligent document processing into the process linking its Data Verification and Authentication System, DIVAS, with the INEC Result Viewing portal, IReV.

Warning against placing public confidence in an opaque technology, Atiku said: “INEC cannot ask Nigerians to trust a system whose rules they are forbidden to see. If an algorithm can flag a polling unit result sheet, the public deserves to know what triggers that flag, who set the threshold, who can change it and what happens to the result afterward.”

He demanded publication of the system’s technical and operational framework, including its training data sources, criteria for flagging discrepancies and the identities of its developers and third-party vendors.

He also wants independent cybersecurity experts, political party technology representatives and civil society technologists to have access to the source code, training data and decision logs for a comprehensive audit before the nationwide mock accreditation scheduled for November 28, 2026.

On the legal status of polling unit results, Atiku insisted that the physical Form EC8A, completed and signed at the polling unit, must remain the primary evidence of what transpired there, warning against allowing an algorithmic assessment to override it.

“The polling unit result sheet, Form EC8A, records what happened where the people voted. INEC must publicly reaffirm the legal status of the physical form completed and signed at the polling unit, and explain how it will resolve any conflict between that document and an AI assessment.

“A machine’s verdict cannot be allowed to quietly displace the evidence witnessed by voters and party agents,” he said.

Atiku also demanded a transparent procedure for reviewing flagged result sheets, including the officials responsible for such reviews, documentation of decisions, notification of political parties and mechanisms for promptly challenging errors.

He proposed real-time monitoring access for political parties through a dedicated dashboard or observer interface to enable them to identify unusual patterns of flagging, delays or blocked uploads during elections.

The former Vice President further urged the National Assembly to summon INEC’s leadership and Information and Communications Technology Directorate to publicly explain the system’s design, safeguards and audit arrangements.

He called on election observers and international partners to monitor the digital handling of results alongside activities at polling units, urging voters to lawfully document results as announced and displayed at their polling units for comparison with subsequently uploaded figures.

Linking the demand to his campaign’s political agenda, Atiku said the credibility of the electoral process was crucial to Nigerians’ ability to choose the government they wanted.

“Nigerians must be free to accept or reject that promise at the ballot box. No hidden algorithm should stand between a struggling family’s vote and the change that family hopes to see,” he said.

He urged INEC to open the system to independent testing, publish procedures for correcting errors and guarantee that no valid vote would disappear during electronic processing.

“Nigerians will not accept an election in which they can watch the counting at their polling unit but cannot see what happens when their result enters INEC’s digital system,” Atiku warned.

content:
By Nwabueze Okonkwo

ONITSHA – Vice-President Kashim Shettima has described Anambra State as a home of accomplished political leaders, citing Nigeria’s first President, Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe; former Vice-President, Dr. Alex Ekwueme; and the incumbent governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo.

Shettima made the observation on Thursday at a joint mega rally organised by the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and the All Progressives Congress (APC) under the banner of Progressives Working Together.

The Vice-President, who represented President Bola Tinubu at the rally, said he was not surprised that Soludo had embraced what he described as the visionary politics of national unity associated with Azikiwe and Ekwueme.

He commended the governor for what he described as his courage and political approach in the current political dispensation.

Shettima also assured Nigerians, particularly residents of Anambra State, that Tinubu’s administration would reposition the country if given another term in 2027.

In his remarks, Soludo said APGA and APC had unanimously endorsed Tinubu for a second term in office.

As part of the alliance, the governor handed over the APGA flag to the APC, describing the move as a demonstration of the parties’ commitment to working together.

Soludo further disclosed that elected APGA members in the state and National Assemblies would work with their APC counterparts in their respective legislative caucuses.

He said the arrangement was aimed at promoting cooperation, national unity and the indivisibility of Nigeria.

title: Police arrest suspected cultists over killing of BEDC worker in Delta
description:

The police said the victim was attacked by a
content:
The Delta State Police Command has arrested seven suspects in connection with the killing of a staff member of the Benin Electricity Distribution Company during a power disconnection exercise in Umunede, Ika North-East Local Government Area of the state.

The police said the victim was attacked by a group of youths armed with cutlasses, battle axes and daggers at Ileje Quarters, Umunede, on November 16, 2026.

The command disclosed this in a statement issued on Thursday by its Police Public Relations Officer, Bright Edafe.

According to the statement, the Umunede Divisional Police Headquarters received a report of the attack at about 1:15 pm on the day of the incident.

It said detectives were immediately deployed to the scene, adding that the victim, who sustained multiple stab wounds, was rushed to the General Hospital, Umunede, where he was confirmed dead.

The statement said, “Preliminary investigations led to the arrest of five suspects, namely Emmanuel Chinonso (30), Gift Francis (24), Jerry Nusi (20), Kelvin Ifeanyi (19) and Emmanuel Chinaza (24).”

It added that two other suspects, Michael Moses, 26, and Moses Egwuye, 35, were arrested on November 18.

The command said the two additional suspects were suspected members of the Aiye Confraternity, bringing the total number of suspects arrested in connection with the killing to seven.

“Manhunt to apprehend other suspects connected with the incident is ongoing,” the statement added.

The Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, Samuel Erale, condemned the killing and extended his condolences to the victim’s family, as well as the management and staff of BEDC.

The police commissioner also expressed concern over recurring attacks on BEDC personnel, warning against violence against individuals carrying out lawful duties.

“He sternly warns against attacks on persons discharging their lawful duties, emphasising that grievances must be addressed through lawful channels,” the statement said.

Erale assured the public that all those found culpable would be prosecuted, adding that the action would serve the interest of justice and deter others from committing similar offences.

title: Court restrains Jimmy Odukoya from acting as Fountain of Life senior pastor
description:
The Lagos State High Court has restrained Jimmy Odukoya from holding himself out as the senior pastor and spiritual head of the Fountain of Life Church, following a dispute over his position in the church.
Justice O. O. Adewunmi-Oshin issued the order on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, in a suit filed
content:
The Lagos State High Court has restrained Jimmy Odukoya from holding himself out as the senior pastor and spiritual head of the Fountain of Life Church, following a dispute over his position in the church.

Justice O. O. Adewunmi-Oshin issued the order on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, in a suit filed by the Incorporated Trustees of the Fountain of Life Church against Odukoya.

A certified true copy of the enrolled order obtained by PUNCH Online on Thursday showed the court’s directives.

The trustees had approached the court, arguing that Odukoya had ceased to hold the position following the appointment of a successor by the late founder of the church, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, in accordance with the church’s constitution.

In the enrolled order, the judge restrained Odukoya, whether acting personally or through proxies, from presenting himself as the church’s senior pastor and spiritual head.

The order stated that the defendant was restrained from holding himself out as the senior pastor, “having ceased to hold the office based on the appointment of a successor by the late Founder and Senior Pastor of the Church, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution of the Church”.

The court also restrained him from interfering with the church’s activities and governance.

It ordered that Odukoya, “whether acting personally or through any proxies in any alleged capacity as the Senior Pastor of the Church, is hereby restrained from interfering, disrupting, meddling with and/or obstructing the activities, governance and any other business of the Church”.

Both injunctions are to remain in force pending the trustees’ full compliance with the High Court of Lagos State (Expeditious Disposal of Civil Cases) Practice Directions No. 2 of 2019 on pre-action protocol.

The judge also granted the trustees leave to commence the action under the pre-action protocol, pursuant to Paragraph 4 of the practice direction.

The order was made ex parte, with the document stating that it was “without prejudice to the right of the Respondents to apply to set it aside, or to respond fully to the substantive claims, upon being served”.

It further directed that the originating processes, together with accompanying documents, be served on the defendant, who is to file his response in accordance with the timelines stipulated under the practice direction.

The suit was adjourned until December 1, 2026, for mention.

PUNCH Online gathered that the court document had been pasted at the church on Thursday.

The development is the latest in the leadership crisis that became public on November 17, when a group of the church’s trustees announced that Jimmy was no longer recognised as senior pastor, citing a review of the church’s constitution and a video containing succession instructions left by its late founder.

In the December 2021 recording, Taiwo Odukoya named Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor, while asking that Jimmy serve as Areogun’s administrative assistant and head of the church’s youth ministry.

The trustees said the recording was only made available to them in late December 2025 and was not presented when Jimmy was appointed senior pastor in September 2023.

However, Jimmy and the church rejected the removal announcement, describing it as constitutionally invalid and insisting that his appointment had been unanimously approved by the board in 2023.

They maintained that he remained the duly appointed senior pastor and chairman of the Board of Trustees.

The trustees subsequently reaffirmed their decision and appointed Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader pending consultations and the process of appointing a substantive leadership structure.

The dispute has also involved disagreements over Jimmy’s recent remarriage, which the trustees said raised concerns about the church’s teachings and the standards expected of its spiritual leadership.

The post Court restrains Jimmy Odukoya from acting as Fountain of Life senior pastor appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Gov Fubara Seeks Private Sector Participation In Rivers Tourism Development
description: Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, is wooing private investors to explore the state’s tourism potential, assuring them of improved infrastructure and government support to make tourism a viable investment destination.The governor gave the assurance during an inspection of ongoing road p
content:
Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, is wooing private investors to explore the state’s tourism potential, assuring them of improved infrastructure and government support to make tourism a viable investment destination.

The governor gave the assurance during an inspection of ongoing road projects at Ngo-Oyorokoto Beach in Andoni Local Government Area, where he expressed optimism that the facility would become a major tourist attraction and a hub for recreational activities.

Governor Fubara said the state government was committed to fulfilling its promise of transforming the beach into a tourism destination, recalling that the construction of the access road began before the declaration of the state of emergency in the state.

He acknowledged that the project subsequently attracted controversies over its progress and the contractor’s involvement but said the government has continued to monitor the work and fulfil its obligations.

According to him, construction of the access road to the beach is nearing completion, with only asphalting remaining.

“On the side of the beach, I think we are okay. What is just remaining is the asphalting of the road, and I can assure you that before December, or before the next beach party, the road will be asphalted,” he said.

The governor also inspected the road leading to the Oyorokoto fishing port, claimed to be the biggest fishing settlement in West Africa.

There, he identified a small culvert and approximately 100 metres of road as the outstanding work required to connect the settlement near the Atlantic Ocean.

He described the progress recorded as encouraging and urged prospective investors to take advantage of the improving facilities ahead of the next beach party.

“The extent of work that we have done as of today is better than what we had yesterday. Therefore, you have no fear in investing,” Fubara assured.

He also pledged to personally attend the forthcoming beach party, describing it as an opportunity to demonstrate the government’s commitment to supporting investors and promoting tourism.

“I, as the Governor, will be here to party with our investors,” he said.

title: Tinubu doesn’t need to rig 2027 election, Soludo says
description:
Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo, has declared that President Bola Tinubu does not need to rig the 2027 presidential election to secure re-election, expressing confidence that the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) would win the contest.







Soludo made the declaration on Thursday whil
content:
Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo, has declared that President Bola Tinubu does not need to rig the 2027 presidential election to secure re-election, expressing confidence that the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) would win the contest.

Soludo made the declaration on Thursday while speaking at a presidential campaign rally at Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka, where he argued that the APC had a stronger nationwide political presence than its opponents.

“This election, to the best of our knowledge, is already won and lost. The president doesn’t need to rig any election. President Tinubu doesn’t need to rig any election,” he said.

Explaining his position, the governor said the APC presidential ticket was facing opposition candidates whose political influence, according to him, was limited to certain parts of the country.

“All over the country today, in every state of Nigeria, it is President Tinubu and Shettima ticket versus one other party. Whereas you have some other candidates who are strong in some parts of the country but don’t exist in others.

“If you then take the totality of it all, do the arithmetic in your mind, this election is literally over,” Soludo said.

He also attributed his confidence to the performance of the Tinubu administration, arguing that the President and Vice-President Kashim Shettima deserved another term based on their record in office.

“President Tinubu, Shettima, they’re doing very well. They will win because they have done well,” he said.

The governor further argued that the APC had presented a stronger policy agenda than its opponents, claiming that no credible alternative had emerged ahead of the election.

“And let me put it on record, in terms of the agenda that they are pursuing, no candidate before 2023 presented a better manifesto, better agenda for Nigeria.

“And so far, less than two months to go, no candidate has presented a credible alternative. The Tinubu-Shettima ticket presidency is on course,” he said.

Soludo also defended the Federal Government’s handling of the economy and security, claiming that there was a consensus among people familiar with the economy, both locally and internationally, that the administration was moving in the right direction.

He cited the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), which provides financial support to eligible students, as one of the initiatives through which the administration was addressing the needs of Nigerians.

title: Tinubu confers GCON on Wole Olanipekun
description:
President Bola Tinubu has conferred the Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger (GCON), Nigeria’s second-highest national honour, on renowned lawyer and Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Chief Wole Olanipekun.







The honour was announced on Thursday by the President’s Special Adviser on Information
content:
President Bola Tinubu has conferred the Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger (GCON), Nigeria’s second-highest national honour, on renowned lawyer and Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Chief Wole Olanipekun.

The honour was announced on Thursday by the President’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, in a post on X.

Onanuga said Tinubu conferred the national honour on Olanipekun at the launch of a six-volume book celebrating his 75th birthday, 50 years at the Bar and 35 years as a Senior Advocate of Nigeria.

“President Tinubu confers Nigeria’s second-highest honour, the Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger, on Chief Wole Olanipekun,” Onanuga wrote.

He added that the honour was announced at the event organised to celebrate the legal icon’s professional and personal milestones.

Olanipekun was called to the Nigerian Bar in 1976 and elevated to the rank of Senior Advocate of Nigeria in 1991.

He served as President of the Nigerian Bar Association from 2002 to 2004 and has remained a prominent figure in Nigeria’s legal profession.

The GCON is Nigeria’s second-highest national honour, ranking below the Grand Commander of the Order of the Federal Republic (GCFR), traditionally reserved for the President and Vice-President.

title: JUST-IN: IGP Disu directs Hospitals to treat gunshot victims without Police report
description:
The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, has directed hospitals and healthcare workers across Nigeria to treat victims of gunshot injuries immediately without demanding police reports or clearance before providing medical attention.
Disu also assured Nigerians that they would not face
content:
The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, has directed hospitals and healthcare workers across Nigeria to treat victims of gunshot injuries immediately without demanding police reports or clearance before providing medical attention.

Disu also assured Nigerians that they would not face punishment for assisting injured persons, urging members of the public to help gunshot victims access medical facilities during emergencies.

The police chief gave the directive in a video message released by the Nigeria Police Force on Thursday, November 19, 2026, as part of efforts to prevent avoidable deaths caused by delays in accessing emergency medical care.

Addressing police officers, medical personnel and members of the public, Disu described the treatment of gunshot victims as a matter of life and death.

He emphasised that Nigerian law does not require a police report before hospitals can admit and treat anyone with gunshot wounds.

“When a gunshot victim is brought to any hospital, the law does not require a police report before treatment,” he said.

The IGP specifically appealed to doctors, nurses and other healthcare professionals to prioritise saving lives rather than allow administrative procedures to delay emergency treatment.

“To our doctors and healthcare workers, you are enjoined to treat gunshot victims immediately without waiting for a police report,” he stated.

Disu further explained that the responsibility of the police was to protect lives and ensure public safety, rather than create fear among citizens.

“Our duty is not to create fear, but to protect lives. We wish to reassure citizens of their safety at all times,” he added.

He also encouraged Nigerians to assist injured persons whenever they encounter them, assuring them that helping victims would not expose them to punishment.

“To members of the public, if you see someone injured, do not hesitate to help. You will not be punished for helping,” the police chief said.

The IGP urged police officers and medical practitioners to comply with the provisions of the law, stressing that every second counts when dealing with gunshot injuries.

He concluded his message with a call for immediate medical intervention, saying, “Treat first, save lives.”

The directive is backed by the Compulsory Treatment and Care for Victims of Gunshot Act, 2017, which mandates all public and private hospitals in Nigeria to provide immediate and adequate treatment to gunshot victims, regardless of whether they have obtained police reports or clearance.

The legislation also requires members of the public, including security personnel, to assist injured persons and ensure they are taken to the nearest hospital.

However, hospitals are required to notify the nearest police station within two hours of commencing treatment, allowing investigations into the circumstances surrounding the shooting to proceed without delaying medical attention.

The law also provides penalties for violations of its provisions, including situations where failure to perform statutory duties results in the unnecessary death of a gunshot victim.

The post JUST-IN: IGP Disu directs Hospitals to treat gunshot victims without Police report appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Obi can’t match Buhari’s popularity – Shettima
description: Vice-President Kashim Shettima has insisted that the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, cannot be more popular than former President Muhammadu Buhari, arguing that a presidential candidate in Nigeria needs strong regional alignment and a solid support base across t
content:
Vice-President Kashim Shettima has insisted that the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, cannot be more popular than former President Muhammadu Buhari, arguing that a presidential candidate in Nigeria needs strong regional alignment and a solid support base across the country to win an election.

Shettima also emphasised that the ultimate goal of ensuring strong regional alignment was to ensure that the South-East was firmly connected to the “national grid in the federation.”

The Vice-President stated this at Dr Alex Ekwueme Square in Awka on Thursday, where he led a presidential campaign rally for President Bola Tinubu alongside Anambra State Governor, Prof Chukwuma Soludo.

The rally, tagged “SoluTinubu 2027”, attracted a large crowd of party supporters drawn from the All Progressives Congress and the All Progressives Grand Alliance, who turned out in colourful party attire at the square.

Addressing the supporters, Shettima said, “Don’t let anyone tell you that Igbos are not an essential component of the Nigerian configuration. And I want to tell you, as someone who is close to this election, there are 17 million Igbos living in Northern Nigeria. There are 10 million Igbos living in Lagos alone.

“And I know that they have a lot of opportunities to come here. You have to reach out.

“Peter Obi cannot be more popular than Muhammadu Buhari. Muhammadu Buhari tried to become President of Nigeria in 2003—he was already a former head of state—he tried again in 2007, he lost.

“Again, he had a strong base of 15 million votes in Northern Nigeria. He tried again in 2011, he lost. Because having a strong base across the nation is what you need to win a presidential election in a country like Nigeria.

“I am telling you, let’s be honest with each other. Let’s talk to the people. Let’s make informed judgment, and Nigeria will be better for it.

“I have a confession to make: some of my best friends in this political dispensation are Igbo. And I want to tell you that I have grown up in the South-East, as a governor, and I call my brothers and sisters to remember that.

“That shows how much I love you guys. So pass it to your people that I love you. We are together; we have come a long way together. You are our brothers and sisters. When I became the Vice-President, I had to put in my life for two months, my resources, to fight for Igbo people.

“Two of my closest aides are Igbo people. To my brothers and sisters in action, let me tell you that I have human dignity, and I can come to you with a clear conscience. We are in this together. In 2015, we went out, one by one, and we won in Anambra.

“Next, I want to talk about our brothers and sisters in the South-East who are educated and capable. I have to be honest with you: we might have some challenges, don’t let anyone fool you. Anambra State is going to be a key state for us.

“Once again, I want to tell you on behalf of the President that we are committed to you. We won’t let you down. This is a massive and real partnership that we have.

“It’s a partnership that works, and it’s a partnership that will keep working. We are proud of you. We are proud of your achievements. You are the best, and we are proud of you.”

Shettima expressed delight at the mobilisation and support for Tinubu, assuring the people that the administration would deliver on its mandate if re-elected.

While acknowledging the constitutional right to freedom of association, he noted that voters could only be persuaded and not forced to support a candidate.

He also endorsed the push for regional alignment, emphasising that the ultimate goal was to ensure that the South-East was firmly connected to the “national grid in the federation” by mobilising votes for Tinubu at polling units, irrespective of party affiliations.

Earlier, the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu; Imo State Governor, Senator Hope Uzodimma; Minister of Works, Dave Umahi; former Anambra State Governor and APC chieftain, Senator Chris Ngige; and Senator Adams Oshiomhole, among others, echoed Soludo’s call for mainstream political integration and commended the governor for convening the cross-party mobilisation.

The post Obi can’t match Buhari’s popularity – Shettima appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Kwara South: APC candidate Adewoye confident of victory
description:
By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin



The All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial candidate for Kwara South in the 2027 general election, Prince Olalekan Adewoye, has expressed confidence in his ability to represent the people of the district effectively, saying his business experience and grassroots int
content:
By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin

The All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial candidate for Kwara South in the 2027 general election, Prince Olalekan Adewoye, has expressed confidence in his ability to represent the people of the district effectively, saying his business experience and grassroots interventions have prepared him for public service.

Adewoye said his conviction was anchored on more than three decades of experience in business, philanthropic activities and commitment to grassroots development.

Speaking in an interview with journalists, the industrialist said he was passionate about translating his private-sector experience into public service, despite not having previously held an elective position or served as a political appointee.

Addressing concerns about his lack of political experience and the challenge posed by established opposition politicians, Adewoye said he was confident of earning the support of voters.

“I am convinced of my capacity and believe I have what it takes to represent the people effectively,” he said.

He argued that voters should assess candidates based on their records, capacity and acceptability rather than previous political positions alone.

According to him, his years in business have equipped him with the ability to manage people from different backgrounds, create value and deploy resources efficiently.

He said these skills would be useful in legislative representation, particularly in ensuring that public resources and government programmes deliver tangible benefits to constituents.

Adewoye disclosed that before joining the senatorial race, he had been involved in philanthropic activities through a foundation established to address some of the social and economic challenges facing residents of Kwara South.

He identified healthcare, education and support for small businesses as critical areas requiring attention in the district.

He said the foundation had provided equipment to individuals seeking to establish or expand businesses, supported healthcare interventions, including health insurance for elderly people, and assisted artisans and other vulnerable groups.

According to him, the interventions were designed to promote self-reliance and economic independence rather than encourage beneficiaries to depend on periodic handouts.

“We should not simply tell young people to look for jobs. We must help them acquire the skills, resources and support they need to create value,” he said.

The APC candidate said his proposed representation would prioritise expanding economic opportunities for young people, traders, artisans and small business operators.

He also disclosed plans to establish a trust fund to bring together individuals and organisations willing to support entrepreneurs and other deserving residents of Kwara South.

He said the proposed initiative would operate under clear guidelines to ensure that assistance reached people with viable business ideas and genuine needs.

Adewoye further revealed that he had commenced a needs assessment across the senatorial district to identify pressing challenges and determine the priorities of the people.

He said the findings would form the basis of his legislative agenda if elected in 2027.

title: Group urges countries to match climate commitments with actions
description:
The African Group of Negotiators on Climate Change has accused countries advocating a complete phase-out of fossil fuels of hypocrisy, alleging that some of them are simultaneously pursuing behind-the-scenes deals to secure petroleum supplies.
The group on Thursday said countries pushing for an end
content:
The African Group of Negotiators on Climate Change has accused countries advocating a complete phase-out of fossil fuels of hypocrisy, alleging that some of them are simultaneously pursuing behind-the-scenes deals to secure petroleum supplies.

The group on Thursday said countries pushing for an end to fossil fuel production and consumption must demonstrate consistency between their public climate commitments and private energy arrangements, warning that the conflicting positions were undermining trust in the global climate negotiations.

The African negotiators also insisted that the transition away from fossil fuels must reflect the continent’s economic realities, protect workers and farmers, and allow African countries to process and utilise their natural resources rather than impose additional development burdens on them.

The position comes as negotiations at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Türkiye, approach their conclusion, with disagreements over fossil fuels, climate finance and the pace of the global energy transition remaining major issues.

His remarks followed reports of a new trilateral declaration issued by China, the United States and Russia on Thursday after an unprecedented summit hosted by Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, attended by US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The declaration reportedly included commitments to pursue talks on nuclear risks, increase petroleum supplies and advance reforms of the United Nations.

The proposed cooperation on petroleum supplies was linked to efforts to strengthen global refined petroleum availability amid energy market pressures arising from the conflict involving Iran and disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz.

The reported agreement drew criticism at COP31 from the European Union’s climate chief, Wopke Hoekstra, who described the development as unfortunate and urged countries to invest in domestic clean energy to avoid repeating energy supply shocks.

But speaking during a press conference, the Chair of the African Group of Negotiators, Nana Dr Antwi-Boasiako Amoah, described the contradiction between countries’ climate rhetoric and their pursuit of petroleum supplies as hypocrisy in the global climate process.

Although he declined to comment specifically on the reported petroleum supply arrangement involving China, the United States and Russia, Amoah maintained that his criticism was directed at what he described as inconsistencies in countries’ overall approach to fossil fuel production and supply.

He said, “For China and U.S. issues, I don’t have information about it. But I’m just commenting on fossil service in total as parties. This is the hypocrisy in the whole process. And so at one point, you see some countries talking about taking fossil out completely, and the underground making deals to get fossils service in their pipelines. And that is the hypocrisy that we have in this whole process.

“So if fossil service is something that we want to do away with as parties, let’s be honest to our commitments. Let’s stay with it head on, not to be going back doors to do certain things and later come back and make it look awkward in the face of the other people. That is hypocrisy.”

Amoah added that the continent’s participation in COP31 was guided by the need to protect multilateralism, secure the means to implement climate commitments and ensure that the transition was just and credible.

He said, “Our first point of call is the protection of multilateralism. Africa feels safe to be under multilateralism because this is the only place that we can function properly as a people. And therefore, any attempt, any plans to destroy this process is a red line for us as Africa.

“We also came to this COP with understanding that this COP would deliver for implementation. And in view of that, our slogan to the COP presidency is implementation meets means of implementation.”

He argued that countries responsible for providing climate finance must match their commitments with actual financial support, particularly for adaptation programmes in vulnerable developing countries.

“If the presidency is talking about implementation, it means that parties that have responsibility to deliver means of implementation must keep to the language of the COP presidency to deliver this on the ground. This is why and how climate finance is very important, especially adaptation finance,” he added.

The African group also called for a just transition that recognises the continent’s development priorities, including employment protection, local industrialisation and the use of its natural resources to support economic growth.

Amoah said any transition that placed an unfair burden on African countries would be rejected, stressing that the process must be designed around the continent’s specific circumstances.

He said, “We also came with understanding that this COP would deliver a just and credible transition. So any transition that is going to be burdensome to the African continent is rejected.

“And therefore, the just transition conversation might be situated within the African context where our farmers are protected, our workers are secured, African resources are given space to be processed and utilised within the continent, then also credible institutional structures are layered within the transitional process.”

The group further warned that the effects of rising global temperatures were disproportionately severe for Africa, making adaptation an urgent priority even as countries pursue emissions reductions.

According to Amoah, the implications of global warming and temperature overshoot must be assessed in relation to their effects on African economies and communities, rather than focusing exclusively on mitigation targets.

He said, “We are also saying that adaptation is very important because currently we are talking about overshoots of temperature. Even within this context of 1.5 or just above 1.5, we have implications.

“For Africa, 1.5 translates into 4 degrees, 4.5 degrees in southern geographical context in the African region, meaning that the overshoot is going to bring even much harsher conditions to the African continent.”

He explained that greenhouse gases remained in the atmosphere for extended periods, meaning that the consequences of excessive emissions would continue to affect countries and future generations long after the gases were released.

“Our understanding is that greenhouse gases have a much longer life within the atmosphere. Some gases can be out there for over 500 years, some 300 years.

“Even methane that is a short-lived pollutant can stay within the environment for at least 20 years. And so overshooting the temperature growth means that we are overshooting the impacts that affect our continent. And this is something that we want to see clearly articulated in any languages that is available in this space,” he said.

The Paris Agreement, adopted in 2015, established the international framework for limiting global warming to well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels while pursuing efforts to restrict the increase to 1.5 degrees Celsius.

However, negotiations over how quickly countries should move away from fossil fuels have remained contentious, particularly between developed economies and developing countries whose industrialisation, energy access and public revenues still depend significantly on oil, gas and coal.

African countries have consistently argued that a fair transition must recognise their limited historical contribution to global emissions, development needs and the need for adequate financial and technological support.

The continent has also maintained that climate action should create opportunities for local manufacturing, value addition and employment rather than restrict its ability to benefit from its natural resources.

title: Sanwo-Olu gives LASUED best graduate N5m, job
description:
By Elizabeth Osayande



Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has rewarded the overall best graduating student of the Lagos State University of Education (LASUED), Blessed Mercy Olawunmi, with N5 million and automatic employment.







The award was announced on Thursday, November 19, during t
content:
By Elizabeth Osayande

Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has rewarded the overall best graduating student of the Lagos State University of Education (LASUED), Blessed Mercy Olawunmi, with N5 million and automatic employment.

The award was announced on Thursday, November 19, during the institution’s maiden convocation ceremony held at its Oto/Ijanikin campus.

Olawunmi, of the Department of Home Economics, College of Vocational and Entrepreneurship Education, emerged top of the pioneering graduating class of 2,486 students, including 84 first-class graduates, with a Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 4.98.

Sanwo-Olu also announced a cash reward of N2.5 million each for the best graduating students from the university’s seven colleges.

Apart from the governor’s award, Olawunmi received N250,000 and a commemorative plaque from the university, while Oto-Awori Local Government presented her with N1 million.

The council chairman, Kareem Azeez Abiodun, also announced a reward of N500,000 each for the other best graduating students from the colleges.

Speaking at the ceremony, the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Bidemi Bilkis Lafiaji-Okuneye, thanked Sanwo-Olu for assenting to the law establishing the university in 2022.

She also commended the Governing Council, staff, students and other stakeholders for their contributions towards making the institution a source of pride.

However, she appealed to the governor to intervene in four areas requiring urgent attention: construction of a podcast and photojournalism studio, reconstruction of the perimeter fence, reclamation of swampy land at the main campus and completion of the 750-seat auditoriums at the Epe and Ijanikin campuses.

The Vice-Chancellor disclosed that more than 60 per cent of the main campus land was swampy, leaving the institution with limited space for expansion.

She said the university currently occupied only the dry portions of the land and was becoming increasingly cramped, adding that reclamation would provide room for future development.

She noted that a female hostel being constructed by the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) was already located on the site.

“Your Excellency, sir, these four appeals are strategic investments rather than isolated requests. A studio will enrich what we teach. Secure fencing will protect people who teach — our land. Reclaimed land will create room for all that we still hope to build. An auditorium will provide a gathering space in which scholarship, professional development, and public engagement can flourish,” she said.

Lafiaji-Okuneye also appreciated the Governing Council for its guidance and oversight, the Ministry of Tertiary Education for facilitating the university’s requests to the governor, and staff for sustaining the institution through its transition.

She urged the university community to preserve the academic stability achieved since its establishment, noting that the institution had maintained a stable academic calendar throughout its four years of existence.

“Our work, however, is not finished. Let us protect the academic stability we have worked so hard to establish. It is not easy to start in 2022, and we are convocating the first in November 2026. That means we have had a stable calendar for the four years,” she said.

She charged staff to uphold fairness in assessment, ethical standards in research, courtesy in administration, accountability in resource management and commitment to mentoring younger colleagues.

The Vice-Chancellor also congratulated parents and guardians for believing in the institution while its reputation was still being established.

She acknowledged the role of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), saying the scheme had helped students pay their tuition fees and provided them with monthly stipends.

In his remarks, Sanwo-Olu said he felt humbled to have signed the law establishing LASUED as a university.

He said his joy would be complete if the institution maintained its focus, resisted compromises and continued to set standards in quality teacher education.

The governor promised to consider the Vice-Chancellor’s requests, while assuring the university of continued government investment in infrastructure and learning facilities.

“Our administration will continue to provide the needed infrastructure and tools to ensure that we train the leaders of tomorrow… No matter how much AI you have or technology you use, a teacher’s name and their relevance cannot be taken away,” he said.

The Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the Governing Council, Mrs Sekinat Olusola Yusuf, urged the institution not to become complacent while celebrating its first convocation.

“May we be wise enough to celebrate this beginning without becoming complacent and bold enough to imagine the generations of educators, innovators, and responsible citizens who will yet pass through these gates. For a university worthy of its mission, its greatest achievements must always lie in the lives it transforms and the society it helps to improve,” she said.

Meanwhile, five of the six personalities scheduled for recognition at the ceremony received awards for their contributions to the establishment of LASUED as a university.

They included Sanwo-Olu; Speaker of the Lagos State House of Assembly, Mudashiru Obasa; former Lagos State Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Justice Moyosore Onigbanjo, SAN; Chairman of the House Committee on Tertiary Education, Owolabi Ibrahim Ajani; and former Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ibadan, Emeritus Prof. Olufemi Bamiro.

The post Sanwo-Olu gives LASUED best graduate N5m, job appeared first on Vanguard News.

Fubara gave the assur
content:
By Daniel Abia, Port Harcourt

Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, has expressed satisfaction with the progress of work on the Ngo-Atlantic Oyorokoto Beach Road in Andoni Local Government Area, urging prospective investors to explore the area’s tourism potential.

Fubara gave the assurance on Thursday during an inspection of the project, promising that the access road to the beach would be asphalted before December and ahead of the next Tourists Beach Party.

Speaking with journalists after the inspection, the governor said he visited the project site to assess the level of work, recalling that his administration had created an official access road to the beach before the declaration of a state of emergency in Rivers State.

He said the project experienced some delays during the period but that the state government had since resumed meeting its obligations to contractors to ensure the development of the area into a tourism destination.

“We’ve been following up and meeting our own side of the obligation to ensure that one of the promises that we made to our people that day — that we want to make this place a tourist centre — comes to reality. And that is one of the main reasons we came here to see what is happening and the extent of the job that has been done,” he said.

Fubara described the inspection as an opportunity to assess first-hand the progress made on the project.

He said work on the beach access road was largely satisfactory, adding that the major outstanding task was the asphalting of the road, which he assured would be completed before December or ahead of the next Tourists Beach Party.

The governor also disclosed that he inspected the other section of the road leading to the fishing ports, where he said only a culvert, measuring about 100 metres from the fishing centre, remained to be completed.

Fubara said the level of work recorded was significantly better than what was previously on ground.

He urged prospective investors to take advantage of the area’s tourism and commercial opportunities, assuring them that they had nothing to fear about investing in Rivers State.

title: 2027: Tinubu Doesn’t Need To Rig Any Election, He’ll Win Because He’s Done Well — Soludo
description: Anambra State Governor, Charles Soludo, has declared that President Bola Tinubu does not need to manipulate the 2027 presidential election to secure re-election, insisting that his performance in office will earn him victory.Soludo said the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential ticket of Tinu
content:
Anambra State Governor, Charles Soludo, has declared that President Bola Tinubu does not need to manipulate the 2027 presidential election to secure re-election, insisting that his performance in office will earn him victory.

Soludo said the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential ticket of Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima was already in a strong position ahead of the election, arguing that no opposition candidate had presented a credible alternative to the ruling party.

The governor spoke on Thursday at a 2027 presidential campaign rally in Anambra State attended by Shettima, Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council Abdul’aziz Yari, former Anambra State governor Chris Ngige and Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma, among other party chieftains.

“To our people, this election, to the best of our knowledge, is already won and lost. The President doesn’t need to rig the election. President Tinubu doesn’t need to rig the election

“All over the country today, in every state of Nigeria, it is President Tinubu and Shetima’s ticket versus one other party. Whereas you have some other candidates who are strong in some parts of the country but don’t exist in others.

“If you then take the totality of it all, do the arithmetic. This election is literally over. President Tinubu and Shettima, they are doing very well. They will win because they have done well,” he added.

Soludo also praised the Tinubu administration’s economic policies, security efforts and social intervention programmes, describing its agenda as superior to those presented by previous presidential candidates.

“We know that there is still work to be done. And that work to be done means moving now from stability, having rescued the economy from total collapse, now moving into the next phase of shared prosperity. But let’s not kid ourselves. You don’t change a winning team. The Tinubu-Shetima ticket is the winning team,” the governor said.

2027 Presidential Election

The 2027 presidential election, which is less than 60 days away, is expected to feature several prominent political figures, including Tinubu of the APC, Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), and Omoyele Sowore of the African Action Congress (AAC).

Tinubu, who is seeking a second four-year term, won the 2023 presidential election with 8,794,726 votes.

Atiku finished second with 6,984,520 votes, while Obi came third with 6,101,533 votes.

Following the 2023 election, both Atiku and Obi challenged Tinubu’s victory, citing alleged electoral irregularities, delays in uploading results, and problems with the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) result transmission portal.

However, the Presidential Election Petition Tribunal dismissed their petitions in September 2023, while the Supreme Court upheld Tinubu’s victory in October of the same year.

The opposition has also accused Tinubu and the APC of working towards establishing a one-party state, citing multiple defections by opposition politicians to the ruling party.

The President and the APC have rejected the allegations, insisting that Nigeria remains a multiparty democracy.

Meanwhile, parties like the NDC have taken a vocal stance against electoral manipulation and political intimidation.

INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan has pledged impartiality for the forthcoming elections, stating that his loyalty lies solely with the Nigerian Constitution and Electoral Act.

The post 2027: Tinubu Doesn’t Need To Rig Any Election, He’ll Win Because He’s Done Well — Soludo appeared first on Channels Television.

By Omeiza Ajayi



ABUJA: The All Progressives Grand Alliance APGA has presented its flag to President Bola Tinubu as its presidential candidate at the All Progressives Congress APC campaign rally in Awka, Anambra State.







APC National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, announced the alliance at
content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: The All Progressives Grand Alliance APGA has presented its flag to President Bola Tinubu as its presidential candidate at the All Progressives Congress APC campaign rally in Awka, Anambra State.

APC National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, announced the alliance at the rally held at Alex Ekwueme Square on Thursday. “The chairman of PDP is not here, but he is well in his spirit. The chairman of Accord is here. We are four in one. Four political parties supporting one candidate. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said.

Yilwatda then invited Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, to present the APGA flag, with Vice President Kashim Shettima receiving it on Tinubu’s behalf.

Soludo said the handover made the rally unlike any other. He said it was the first time APGA was presenting its flag to the Tinubu/Shettima ticket as its presidential candidate.

He also reminded the crowd that Anambra was where the ticket did worst in 2023. According to him, it recorded 5,111 votes, or 0.8 per cent. “Ndi Anambra, are we going to do far better than 2023? We will not be there again,” he said.

The governor said Ndigbo would lose from another round of political isolation. “Let us make this campaign a conversation, not an argument among ourselves. In a democracy, what leverage do we have other than our votes and having alliance with the rest of the country?There is work to be done, but you don’t change a winning team”, he said.

Soludo said power would move to the North in 2031 and that the South should first complete its eight years. He also said the contest was already decided. “This election, to the best of my knowledge, is already won and lost. No candidate before 2023 presented a better manifesto, better agenda for Nigeria. And so far, less than two months to go, no candidate has presented a credible alternative,” he said.

Yilwatda said the President had shown confidence in the Southeast by giving its sons key roles. He named the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, who he said is constructimg good roads.

He said even the opposition used those roads. “Even Peter Obi is using our roads. Atiku is using our roads. Those roads are constructed by your son, Umahi,” he said.

Yilwatda described Tinubu as the most experienced and formidable of the candidates, pointing to his record as Lagos State governor and at the centre. He said the President had stabilised the economy and fixed roads, power and education.

The Director General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Abdul’aziz Yari, urged Ndigbo to turn their economic weight into political influence. He cited the late President Muhammadu Buhari as proof that regional support alone does not win the presidency.

“Buhari used to have 12 states in Northern Nigeria. At any point in time, he would get those 12 states. But that did not make him become President of Nigeria. But when he got the South-West, he made it. Buhari lost in 2003, 2007 and 2011 before winning in 2015, when he had a friend who agreed to join hands with him”, he said.

Yari also told the Igbo that the economic strength of the Southeast should place them at the centre of national politics.
He urged them to turn out on January 16, 2027, and vote for Tinubu.

Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma, told the gathering that the Southeast had resolved to back Tinubu across party lines.

Uzodimma listed projects he credited to the APC-led federal government. These included the Second Niger Bridge, the completion or ongoing work on abandoned federal roads, a South East Development Commission, and loans for training young people.

He said APGA members had agreed to vote APC on January 16. He urged residents to collect their Permanent Voter Card (PVC) from the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and take the message to their polling units, wards and local governments.

title: Man accused of AI-assisted exam cheating found dead in Seoul
description:
A South Korean man suspected of using artificial intelligence (AI) to obtain a perfect score in the country’s law school entrance examination has been found dead at a motel in Seoul.







Lee Jin-woo was discovered at a motel in Cheonho-dong, Gangdong District, eastern Seoul, at about 1:12 p.m. on
content:
A South Korean man suspected of using artificial intelligence (AI) to obtain a perfect score in the country’s law school entrance examination has been found dead at a motel in Seoul.

Lee Jin-woo was discovered at a motel in Cheonho-dong, Gangdong District, eastern Seoul, at about 1:12 p.m. on Thursday, emergency authorities said.

According to Yonhap News TV, a note was also found at the scene, reportedly indicating that Lee was physically and mentally exhausted.

However, the note reportedly contained no admission of cheating or explanation of the allegations against him.

Authorities said they would examine the scene to establish the circumstances surrounding his death.

Lee had attracted public attention over allegations that he used AI to cheat in the Legal Education Eligibility Test (LEET), the examination required for admission into law schools in South Korea.

In an attempt to dispel the suspicions, he had announced plans to answer questions from the Korean language section of the 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test in real time on Thursday morning.

However, he failed to appear at the designated venue by 8:40 a.m., when the examination began.

Police launched a search after receiving a report at about 8:42 a.m. expressing concern over his whereabouts.

According to the police, Lee left his home on Wednesday and travelled to a lodging facility in Gwangjin District, eastern Seoul, before leaving on Thursday morning.

He reportedly took a taxi towards Songpa District, southern Seoul, between 8 a.m. and 9 a.m., before heading to Gangdong District, where his body was later discovered.

Lee had previously gained attention after revealing that he had scored between the sixth and eighth tiers in previous college entrance examinations, which use a nine-tier grading system, with higher numbers representing lower scores.

He said he later developed a better understanding of studying and reading comprehension, eventually gaining admission into Korea University’s Department of Political Science and International Relations in 2024 and Seoul National University’s School of Dentistry in 2026.

He also reportedly achieved a perfect score in the LEET while attending Seoul National University.

However, his academic achievements came under scrutiny following allegations of AI-assisted cheating in a national tax accountant certification examination.

Questions were subsequently raised over whether he had also used AI to cheat in the LEET and the college entrance examinations for the 2024 and 2026 academic years.

The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency said on Wednesday that it had assigned a criminal complaint against Lee, bordering on allegations of obstruction of business, obstruction of official duties and fraud, to its Provincial Special Detective Corps.

Following his death, police are expected to close the case without prosecution, as criminal proceedings cannot continue against a deceased suspect.

KoreaJoongAngDaily.com

title: Tinubu, South-West govs invited to Adeleke’s second-term inauguration
description:
The Osun State Government has said President Bola Tinubu, governors in the South-West, and diplomats have been invited to the second-term inauguration of Governor Ademola Adeleke.
The Secretary to the State Government, Teslim Igbalaiye, who chairs the inauguration committee, disclosed this on Thursd
content:
The Osun State Government has said President Bola Tinubu, governors in the South-West, and diplomats have been invited to the second-term inauguration of Governor Ademola Adeleke.

The Secretary to the State Government, Teslim Igbalaiye, who chairs the inauguration committee, disclosed this on Thursday while unveiling programmes lined up for the event at a press conference in Osogbo.

Igbalaiye said the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, several federal lawmakers, and the governor’s friends and associates from across the world had also been invited to the inauguration, scheduled to hold at the Osogbo Township Stadium on November 27.

He added that some dignitaries who were not formally invited had contacted the state government to express their interest in attending the ceremony.

“We have actually invited several dignitaries. We invited the President, Bola Tinubu. About 15 ambassadors contacted us and said they want to attend the inauguration. Senators, especially from the North, are coming for the inauguration.

“Also, members of the House of Representatives are coming. The Speaker of the House of Representatives: we are not certain yet if he will attend, but we invited him too. Five ministers have indicated interest in attending.

“A lot of dignitaries are coming into the state for the inauguration. South-West governors are coming. All of them want to associate with Imole,” Igbalaiye said.

Unveiling the activities lined up for the inauguration, the SSG said a Jumat service would hold on Friday at the Central Mosque, Oja Oba, Osogbo.

He said an interfaith prayer session would hold on Saturday at the open space in the parking lot of the Government House, Osogbo.

He added that the final of the Ademola Adeleke Victory Soccer Tournament would also take place on Saturday afternoon at the Fakunle Comprehensive High School playground in Osogbo.

According to him, a night of praise and worship would hold at the banquet hall of the Governor’s House, while government delegations would visit orphanage homes across the state to make donations.

The inauguration committee chairman also announced that an Osun Youth Summit on innovation and enterprise would be held as part of the activities.

He said Adeleke would also deliver a state broadcast to appreciate the people for their support.

Igbalaiye disclosed that the inauguration lecture would be delivered by Senator Shehu Sani, with the theme, ‘Federalism Dilemma: Navigating Institutional Friction, Local Government Allocations, and Executive Overreach.’

He solicited the cooperation of stakeholders, particularly the media, in ensuring adequate coverage of the activities.

Describing journalists as valued partners, he said, “Our valued partners to publish, broadcast and stream these activities to local and global audiences.”

The PUNCH earlier reported that Adeleke was re-elected in the August 15 Osun governorship election, defeating the APC candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, and 13 other contestants.

Adeleke was first elected governor for a four-year term on July 16, 2022.

title: AI giant Anthropic shares set to trade after record-breaking IPO
description:
Anthropic shares will begin trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday after the AI giant raised $81.3 billion in a record-breaking initial public offering, as hot demand brushed aside market jitters over the Nvidia spy scandal and fears of a tech bubble.
The company priced its shares at $83 on Wednesday, ab
content:
Anthropic shares will begin trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday after the AI giant raised $81.3 billion in a record-breaking initial public offering, as hot demand brushed aside market jitters over the Nvidia spy scandal and fears of a tech bubble.

The company priced its shares at $83 on Wednesday, above its expected range, and sold 980 million shares, about 956 million of them new shares and the rest from existing shareholders. Anthropic itself will receive about $79.4 billion.

The pricing values the maker of the Claude chatbot at about $1.5 trillion, including employee stock options and restricted shares.

The debut marks a milestone in the AI boom. A company founded five years ago by OpenAI defectors worried about AI safety has become the first of the leading model developers to list on Wall Street, at a valuation rivalling decades-old tech brands.

The listing, under the ticker “ANT,” gives ordinary investors their first chance to bet directly on a stand-alone AI giant.

“Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so, only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing,” chief executive Dario Amodei said at the Nasdaq in New York’s Times Square, underlining the company’s priority of promoting safe AI.

Newly listed shares do not start publicly trading at the opening bell. Nasdaq and the lead investment banks first gather buy and sell orders, a process that can take several hours for a large listing.

The offering surpasses the $75 billion that Elon Musk’s SpaceX raised in its June IPO at a valuation of $1.77 trillion. SpaceX’s total ultimately rose to $86 billion after its underwriters exercised an option to buy additional shares.

Anthropic has granted its underwriters an option to buy up to 147 million more shares, which would lift its total to about $93.5 billion.

“Demand seems to be outstripping supply of this newly publicly traded company,” Art Hogan of B. Riley Wealth Management told AFP.

“This may be the breath of fresh air that the tech trade needed to move beyond the fog of artificial intelligence that we’ve been living in for the last couple of weeks,” he added.

The strong demand comes even as AI stocks have swung sharply, with investors questioning whether heavy spending on the technology will pay off.

Nvidia, the chip giant at the centre of the AI investment boom and an investor in Anthropic and dozens of other AI companies, has been shaken by the resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang after a reported affair with a woman suspected by US intelligence to be a Chinese spy.

Earlier estimates had put Anthropic’s valuation as high as $2 trillion, but they fell as AI stocks slid on Wall Street in recent months.

Anthropic’s Claude models are among the most powerful in the world, hailed for their problem-solving potential but also feared for their capacity to destabilise societies and replace human workers.

The five-year-old company’s revenue has surged at a pace few US companies have ever matched, reaching $17 billion in the third quarter, up from $1.4 billion a year earlier. Much of that revenue comes from customers paying to use its AI models for computer coding.

Amodei and his sister Daniela, the company’s president, founded Anthropic with several colleagues in 2021 after leaving ChatGPT-maker OpenAI.

Threats to Americans

Anthropic’s IPO filing goes into extensive detail on the risks of the technology, reflecting the company’s focus on safety even as it builds ever more powerful models. It warns that advanced AI systems “could pose catastrophic or existential risks to society if not developed and deployed responsibly.”

US Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren criticised the listing on X, saying the company “fails to answer for the potential threats to Americans’ retirements and the entire financial system if this IPO goes awry.”

About a dozen protesters gathered outside the Nasdaq in New York’s Times Square on Thursday, chanting: “Why you doing IPO? This AI bubble’s about to blow!”

AFP

title: Fountain of Life Church postpones 2026 Thanksgiving service
description:
The Fountain of Life Church has postponed its 2026 Thanksgiving service, earlier scheduled for Sunday, November 22, amid an ongoing leadership crisis involving Senior Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and members of its Board of Trustees.







The Lagos-based church announced the postponement in a notice share
content:
The Fountain of Life Church has postponed its 2026 Thanksgiving service, earlier scheduled for Sunday, November 22, amid an ongoing leadership crisis involving Senior Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and members of its Board of Trustees.

The Lagos-based church announced the postponement in a notice shared on its official social media platforms on Thursday, November 19.

The notice read, “Please be informed that our Thanksgiving 2026 Service, previously scheduled for Sunday, November 22, has been postponed. A new date will be communicated in due course.”

The church did not give any reason for the decision or indicate when the service would be rescheduled.

The development comes amid a leadership dispute following an announcement by some members of the Board of Trustees withdrawing recognition of Odukoya as the church’s senior pastor with immediate effect.

The trustees reportedly based their decision on a review of the church’s constitution and a December 2021 video recording in which the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, outlined succession arrangements that identified another individual as his preferred successor, while assigning Jimmy Odukoya administrative and youth church responsibilities.

They also cited governance concerns and issues surrounding Odukoya’s recent remarriage.

However, Odukoya and representatives of the church rejected the announcement, describing it as constitutionally invalid and not a decision properly taken by the Board of Trustees.

They maintained that he remains the duly appointed senior pastor and chairman of the board, following his unanimous approval for the positions in September 2023 after his father’s death.

The trustees subsequently reaffirmed their position and appointed Pastor Rotimi Okpaise to provide interim spiritual and administrative leadership pending further consultations.

The crisis has also extended to the control of the church’s official social media accounts, with both sides reportedly disputing authority over the platforms.

Odukoya was notably absent from the church’s midweek service on Thursday as the leadership dispute continued.

The Thanksgiving service had attracted attention amid the unfolding crisis, with the postponement adding another development to the dispute over the church’s leadership and administration.

title: NSC Approves Postponement Of Enugu 2026 National Sports Festival To May 2027
description: The National Sports Commission (NSC) has approved the postponement of the 23rd National Sports Festival, tagged the ‘Coal City Games’, to May 2027.The decision followed a request by the Local Organising Committee, which tendered an unreserved apology for its inability to host the event a
content:
The National Sports Commission (NSC) has approved the postponement of the 23rd National Sports Festival, tagged the ‘Coal City Games’, to May 2027.

The decision followed a request by the Local Organising Committee, which tendered an unreserved apology for its inability to host the event as scheduled from November 28 to December 12, 2026.

The LOC said the games were postponed due to situations beyond the control of the Enugu State Government and pleaded with the NSC to accept the new proposed date.

Director General of the NSC, Bukola Olopade, said though the postponement was regrettable, the commission would intensify its interface with the Enugu State Government to ensure that when the festival holds in May next year, it would go down as the best ever organised games in the country’s history.

Commissioner for Youth and Sports and Chairman of the Local Organising Committee, Lloyd Ekweremadu, said the postponement was a temporary setback but assured all relevant stakeholders, especially participating states and the media, that the new date will only yield better-organised games next year.

“On behalf of the LOC and the Governor of Enugu State, Peter Mbah, we want to apologise to all the states who have been preparing for this festival, and we regret the inconveniences this has caused,” said Ekweremadu.

“Although the contractors handling the projects expressed confidence that the facilities would be completed within the expected timeframe, the Enugu State Ministry of Youth and Sports and the LOC, after a careful assessment, observed that the level of work remaining raised concerns about the readiness of the stadium and Awgu Games Village to meet the required standards before the commencement of the Games.”

“The Ministry and the LOC wish to clarify that other essential arrangements and facilities, including accommodation and related logistics, are ready for the hosting of the festival. However, the completion and full readiness of the Stadium and Awgu Games Village remain critical to the successful hosting of the event.”

He also expressed commitment to upholding the global best practice the National Sports Commission has set for the Games, especially concerning sporting facilities

“The National Sports Festival is our own Olympics, and we are committed to upholding the global best practice the National Sports Commission has set for the Games, especially with regard to sporting facilities.

“The LOC, on behalf of the Enugu State Government, also wants to use this medium to appreciate the leadership of the National Sports Commission, NSC, who are the owners of the Games, for their understanding, and we are assuring that we are committed to staging world-class Games when it holds in May next year,” he added.

By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo

Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has approved the appointment of Prince Adewumi Olusola Adeniyi of the Godo-dudu royal house as the new Owamiran of Esa-Oke.

The Commissioner for Information and Public Enlightenment, Kolapo Alimi, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday, saying the governor approved the appointment at the State Executive Council meeting.

The Owamiran stool became vacant following the death of Oba Akanbi Adediran, who hailed from the Aragadagbagun ruling house of Esa-Oke.

Following the development, the Godo-dudu royal house emerged as the next ruling house to produce a successor, while Prince Adeniyi’s candidature was subsequently ratified by the State Executive Council.

The state government congratulated the Oba-elect and wished him a peaceful reign as he assumes the responsibility of leading the ancient town of Esa-Oke.
