title: COP31: Africa rejects Paris Agreement renegotiation
description:
Fifty-four African countries have rejected any attempt to renegotiate the Paris Agreement, warning that reopening the global climate pact, particularly its obligations, would undermine commitments already agreed by countries to address climate change.
The African Group of Negotiators on Climate Chan
content:
Fifty-four African countries have rejected any attempt to renegotiate the Paris Agreement, warning that reopening the global climate pact, particularly its obligations, would undermine commitments already agreed by countries to address climate change.

The African Group of Negotiators on Climate Change said any attempt to alter the agreement was a red line for the continent, insisting that developed countries must honour their existing obligations rather than seek to revise the framework governing global climate action.

The position comes as negotiations at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, enter their final hours, with African countries pushing for stronger commitments on climate finance, adaptation and support for vulnerable economies.

Speaking at a press conference on the state of negotiations on Thursday, the AGN Chair, Nana Dr Antwi-Boasiako Amoah, said Africa would not accept any attempt to renegotiate the Paris Agreement, particularly provisions relating to the responsibilities of countries.

He said, “There’s one message that I also want to put across, which is about renegotiating the Paris Agreement. I think this is something that is a big red line for the African continent.

“Any attempt to renegotiate the Paris Agreement, especially when it comes to obligations, is something that the African continent rejects. We need to stay within the confines of the agreement because that is what we all have agreed in the past to do business with.”

The chair’s remarks reflect growing concerns among developing countries that efforts to revisit existing climate commitments could weaken the obligations of developed nations to provide financial and other forms of support to countries bearing the brunt of climate change despite contributing relatively little to global greenhouse gas emissions.

The dispute over climate finance has become one of the major sticking points at COP31, following changes to the proposed adaptation finance target in the latest draft decision released on November 19.

The revised draft dropped an earlier proposal requiring adaptation finance for developing countries to reach at least $120bn annually by 2035.

The figure had been based on tripling the $40bn annual adaptation finance commitment under the Glasgow Climate Pact, agreed at COP26 in 2021.

Under that commitment, developed countries agreed to double adaptation finance from approximately $20bn provided in 2019 to $40bn annually by 2025.

However, the latest draft no longer specifies the $120bn figure or identifies the $40bn Glasgow commitment as the baseline for calculating the proposed increase.

Instead, paragraph 40 retains a commitment to at least triple adaptation finance by 2035, while paragraph 43 requests the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change Standing Committee on Finance to prepare a technical report identifying possible baselines. Paragraph 44 also proposes developing an implementation pathway for the target.

The removal of the specific financial figure raises concerns about how the proposed increase will be measured, funded and implemented, particularly as developing countries seek assurances that climate finance commitments will translate into actual resources.

African countries have repeatedly argued that such financing should be predictable, accessible and largely provided through grants or highly concessional instruments rather than commercial loans that could deepen their debt burdens.

Addressing questions about the continent’s ability to implement its climate commitments amid limited financing, Amoah said Africa’s concerns were not simply about securing additional money but ensuring that the financial architecture delivered resources on affordable terms.

He said, “I think the last three questions you asked are important, because basically it comes back to the fact that how would you be able to implement your actions as Africa if you don’t have reliable means of implementation? And it comes back to the earlier question on debts and adaptation-related issues.

“We have been very vocal, not just talking, but also trying to make sure that the structures that deliver finance, that is, grants and highly concessional, from whichever platform we find ourselves. We are doing this in the Green Climate Fund; we’re trying to make sure that structures that are supporting implementation are right.”

He disclosed that the African Group had also been working to influence policies governing the next replenishment of the Green Climate Fund, particularly the distinction between contributions from traditional donors and financing from other sources.

According to him, the fund’s board recently delivered two policies that would guide the replenishment process next year, with African negotiators pushing to ensure that the different obligations attached to the two financing categories were properly recognised.

He said, “And the African group did a very stellar job to make sure that those two policies that are going to be adopted- one is for the contributors, the main contributors, and then the second policy is for other sources.

“We want to make sure that we don’t miss the two, because the two are not the same; the obligations are different. And so for us, it’s important to have highly concessional financial instruments in order to address our needs.”

Explaining the financial difficulties confronting African countries in accessing climate grants, the AGN chair gave an example of the additional resources countries were sometimes required to mobilise to secure relatively small amounts of grant funding.

He said, “And now I will give you an example. It’s an example that I love most, because I’ve been seeing it throughout today. If I take one dollar from GEF, a scammer, from South Africa, I need to put on the table seven dollars to be able to get one dollar grant.

“And so it means that I’m giving out seven dollars to be able to give one dollar. At the end of the day, I am even contributing more than what is being given to me.”

He rejected the perception that African countries were merely demanding financial assistance without making corresponding investments in climate action, arguing that the continent was reminding developed countries to fulfil commitments they had voluntarily accepted.

To demonstrate Africa’s contribution to climate implementation, Amoah cited four African projects recently approved by the Green Climate Fund, which he said received grants totalling about $300m.

He disclosed that the beneficiary countries mobilised an additional $4.2bn to support the implementation of the projects, arguing that the figures demonstrated the willingness of African governments to invest their own resources in climate action when adequate international support was available.

“Recently, four projects were approved by the GEF. They were African projects amounting to about $300m in grants.

“These countries mobilised $4.2bn to support the implementation. Because they want to see the progress of their people. And so it’s important to always look at it from that bigger picture,” he added.

The Paris Agreement, adopted in 2015 at COP21, provides the international framework for limiting global warming to well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels, while pursuing efforts to limit the increase to 1.5 degrees Celsius.

It also recognises the different national circumstances and capacities of countries, including the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities, which acknowledges that developed countries have greater historical responsibility for greenhouse gas emissions and stronger financial capacities.

With COP31 approaching its conclusion, the continent’s negotiators are seeking to ensure that the final decisions preserve existing commitments and provide a credible financing pathway for developing countries.

The post COP31: Africa rejects Paris Agreement renegotiation appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Anambra govt denies pulling down Umeh’s billboard over Obi
description:
The Anambra State Government has denied claims that it pulled down a billboard belonging to Senator Victor Umeh because it carried the image of former Governor Peter Obi.







The government described the claims as false and misleading, insisting that the billboard was removed over alleged non-com
content:
The Anambra State Government has denied claims that it pulled down a billboard belonging to Senator Victor Umeh because it carried the image of former Governor Peter Obi.

The government described the claims as false and misleading, insisting that the billboard was removed over alleged non-compliance with the state’s signage law.

The Commissioner for Information and Value Reformation, Law Mefor, stated this in a statement issued in Awka on Thursday.

Mefor explained that although Umeh had paid the required signage fee, Obi had not complied with the payment requirement.

He said the senator’s decision to use the billboard to campaign for the presidential candidate of the New Democratic Congress (NDC), which featured Obi, contravened the Anambra State Signage Act, 2010.

The commissioner said the enforcement action was therefore not connected to Obi’s image or political affiliation but was strictly based on compliance with the law.

“For the avoidance of doubt, the billboard was not pulled down because of Peter Obi’s image.

“The fact is this: While Senator Victor Umeh has duly paid his signage fee, His Excellency, Mr. Peter Obi has not. Rather than ensure compliance, the Distinguished Senator decided to use his billboard to campaign for the NDC presidential candidate, in clear contravention of the Anambra State Signage Act, 2010, a law enacted by the Peter Obi administration itself,” he said.

Mefor added that any combined billboard campaign involving candidates who had yet to comply with the signage law would attract similar enforcement, irrespective of their political parties or status.

He maintained that the state government remained committed to the fair and even-handed enforcement of existing laws and the regulation of outdoor advertising.

The commissioner urged the public to disregard what he described as the misleading narrative and be guided by the facts.

title: Road crashes fall 13.8%, deaths drop to 941 in Q3 2026 — FRSC
description:
By Favour Ulebor, Abuja



The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has reported a 13.8 per cent reduction in road traffic crashes across Nigeria in the third quarter of 2026, with fatalities dropping from 1,077 in the corresponding period of 2025 to 941.







The Corps also recorded a decline in the
content:
By Favour Ulebor, Abuja

The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has reported a 13.8 per cent reduction in road traffic crashes across Nigeria in the third quarter of 2026, with fatalities dropping from 1,077 in the corresponding period of 2025 to 941.

The Corps also recorded a decline in the number of people injured, from 6,856 to 5,864, representing a 14.5 per cent reduction.

The figures were disclosed in a statement on Thursday by the Corps Public Education Officer, Osondu Ohaeri, following the end-of-year strategy session with commanding officers at the FRSC headquarters in Abuja.

According to the statement, 2,098 road traffic crashes were recorded between July and September 2026, compared with 2,434 in the corresponding period of 2025.

The reduction of 336 crashes exceeded the Corps’ 10 per cent reduction target.

Similarly, the number of people injured dropped by 992, while fatalities declined by 136, representing a 12.6 per cent reduction.

The statement said, “A comparative assessment of the two periods shows that road traffic crashes declined from 2,434 in Q3 2025 to 2,098 in Q3 2026, representing 336 fewer crashes.

“Road traffic injuries also dropped significantly from 6,856 to 5,864, a reduction of 992, while recorded fatalities decreased from 1,077 to 941, representing 136 fewer deaths.”

The Corps attributed the improvement to enhanced patrol operations, crash prevention measures, public education and enforcement of traffic laws.

Ahead of the 2026 festive season, the Corps Marshal, Shehu Mohammed, directed commanding officers nationwide to intensify patrol operations along high-risk routes, improve traffic management and strengthen collaboration with other security and emergency response agencies.

He also ordered the strategic deployment of ambulances, rescue teams and tow trucks, while directing commands to sustain public awareness campaigns on safe driving.

“As the nation approaches the 2026 festive season, the Corps Marshal has directed Commanding Officers across the country to translate the gains recorded into more effective highway operations, with particular attention to strategic patrol deployment along high-risk corridors, improved traffic management, stronger collaboration with sister agencies, strategic positioning of ambulances, rescue teams and tow trucks, and sustained public enlightenment,” the statement added.

Mohammed also urged commanding officers to strengthen supervision, prioritise personnel welfare and enforce discipline, warning that the Corps would maintain zero tolerance for extortion, negligence and abuse of authority.

In his remarks, the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume, said the figures reflected progress made under the reforms introduced by the Corps Marshal, particularly the increased emphasis on technology and operational intelligence.

Akume charged FRSC commanders to ensure that Nigerians travelling during the Christmas and New Year celebrations enjoyed safer highways, smoother traffic flow and prompt emergency response.

He, however, warned that increased vehicular movement during the festive period could heighten the risk of road crashes.

He specifically directed the Corps to focus on addressing speeding, dangerous overtaking, overloading, impaired driving and driver fatigue.

The SGF urged zonal and sector commanders to develop practical operational plans for the festive season, with clear deployment arrangements, stronger coordination with relevant agencies and measurable performance targets.

“Ultimately, our success must be reflected in fewer crashes and fatalities, improved traffic flow, effective emergency response and greater public confidence,” he said.

Akume also called on the Corps to undertake a comprehensive review of its annual performance, address identified shortcomings and sustain investments in personnel training and digital systems.

He stressed the need for transparency and accountability in the management of public resources, warning that preventable crashes and unprofessional conduct could undermine public confidence in the Corps.

The SGF assured the FRSC of continued Federal Government support towards improving road safety, urging officers to demonstrate professionalism and deliver measurable results.

Akume also commissioned the upgraded Operations Monitoring and Control Centre at the FRSC headquarters.

The Corps said the facility would strengthen its capacity to monitor patrol operations, coordinate emergency responses and securely store and retrieve evidence of traffic offences.

title: 2027: Oborevwori seeks support, showcases Delta infrastructure projects
description:
Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, has highlighted his administration’s infrastructure projects, particularly the construction of the PTI and DSC flyovers, and urged residents to support the All Progressives Congress ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Oborevwori spoke on Wednesday during AP
content:
Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, has highlighted his administration’s infrastructure projects, particularly the construction of the PTI and DSC flyovers, and urged residents to support the All Progressives Congress ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Oborevwori spoke on Wednesday during APC campaign rallies in Warri South and Uvwie Local Government Areas of the state, according to a statement issued on Thursday by his Chief Press Secretary, Festus Ahon.

The governor also witnessed the defection of the Nigeria Democratic Congress House of Assembly candidate for Warri South Constituency II, Owin Ikuku, and the party’s vice chairman into the APC.

Speaking at the Uvwie rally, Oborevwori said the construction of the PTI and DSC flyovers had significantly reduced travel time and improved movement within the area.

“Anytime I pass through this route, it gives me joy. Three and a half years ago, travelling through here towards Bayelsa could take as long as three hours. Today, the story is different,” he said.

At the Warri rally, the governor attributed the state’s transformation to deliberate investments and his administration’s commitment to development, stressing that governance should be measured by projects that directly improve the lives of the people.

He also called for peaceful conduct during the forthcoming elections, insisting that political differences should not lead to violence.

“I am not a violent person. I don’t believe in violence. We must allow the people to exercise their democratic rights peacefully,” he said.

Oborevwori, who was accompanied by his wife, Deaconess Tobore Oborevwori, and other political leaders, urged eligible voters to turn out and exercise their civic responsibility, while appreciating residents for their support.

The Deputy Governor, Monday Onyeme, described Oborevwori as a performing leader, saying the large turnout at the rallies reflected the growing acceptance of the APC in the areas.

The state APC Chairman, Solomon Arenyeka, presented party flags to the party’s House of Assembly candidates for Warri South Constituencies I and II and formally received the defectors from the NDC.

At the Uvwie rally, Arenyeka also presented flags to the APC candidates for the House of Representatives, Ransom Onoyake, and the Uvwie State Constituency, Edafe Emakpor.

Similarly, the Director-General of the Delta APC Campaign Council, James Manager, commended the governor for what he described as the visible impact of his administration.

Manager listed road construction, bridge projects, market development and youth empowerment initiatives among the achievements of the Oborevwori administration.

The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, urged residents to support President Bola Tinubu and Oborevwori, cautioning against misinformation about their administrations.

Keyamo described the developments in Uvwie and other parts of Delta State as unprecedented, praising the governor for rehabilitating roads that had remained in deplorable condition for several years.

He assured Oborevwori that residents of Uvwie, Warri and other parts of the state would support his administration.

title: Police arrest nine over armed robbery, rescues kidnapped victims in Nasarawa
description: The Nasarawa State Police Command says it has recorded significant operational successes in its sustained efforts to combat criminal activities across the state, with the arrest of nine (9) suspects in connection with an armed robbery incident in Keffi Local Government Area and the successful rescue
content:
The Nasarawa State Police Command says it has recorded significant operational successes in its sustained efforts to combat criminal activities across the state, with the arrest of nine (9) suspects in connection with an armed robbery incident in Keffi Local Government Area and the successful rescue of three (3) kidnapped victims in Awe LGA of the state.

This was contained in a press statement made available to Journalists in Lafia on Thursday by the command’s Public Relations Officer, SP Ramhan Nansel.

According to him, Police operatives attached to Angwan Lambu Division arrested nine armed robbery suspects terrorising students’ general area in Keffi, following a distress call that some hoodlums invaded student hostels behind Princess Sarah, Keffi, and allegedly dispossessed occupants of their belongings.

The PPRO noted that upon receipt of the report, a patrol team promptly mobilised to the scene, but the suspects fled before the arrival of the operatives. While acting on available intelligence, the team trailed the fleeing suspects to a hotel on the outskirts of Keffi, where the nine (9) suspects were arrested.

Nansel said items recovered from the suspects include one cutlass, one long stick, eight mobile phones and substances suspected to be illicit drugs.

“Investigations have commenced, and the suspects have been identified by their victims. They are cooperating with the police by giving useful information to establish their respective levels of involvement,” he added.

In the press statement, the PPRO said in another development, on 18/11/2026 at about 0900hrs, the Command successfully rescued three (3) kidnapped victims in Hunki axis, an area between Awe and Azara in the Awe Local Government Area of the State.

He said this was based on credible information that armed bandits had abducted some persons and were holding them hostage in a forest at Hunki area.

“Upon receipt of the information, the Commissioner of Police immediately mobilised operatives of the Violent Crimes Response Unit and other patrol teams to the area; combed the forest and engaged the kidnappers. The teams mounted pressure on them which made them to abandon the victims which made them abandon the victims and flee.

“The three rescued victims are identified as: Habibu Samaika, male, aged 40, from Gulbin Dutsi, Ubi Local Government Area of Taraba State; Audi Abubakar, male, aged 40, from Shendam Local Government Area of Plateau State; and Shafiu Zakari, male, aged 19, from Azara, Awe Local Government Area of Nasarawa State.

“The victims were rescued unhurt and immediately conveyed to Azara General Hospital for medical attention, where they were confirmed to be in stable condition. Their relatives have been contacted, and arrangements are underway to reunite them with their families after their discharge,” he added.

The PPRO said the Commissioner of Police, Nasarawa State Command, CP Sheikh Mohammed Danko, commended the officers for their prompt response, courage and professionalism in the two operations.

“He reassured residents that the Command remains committed to protecting lives and property and will sustain its intelligence-led operations, patrols and exercises to dismantle criminals and their hideouts and bring perpetrators of crime to justice.

“He urged residents to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements and criminal activities to the nearest Police station, assuring them that all information received would be treated with utmost confidentiality.

“The Commissioner reiterates his commitment to ensuring the safety and security of all residents and will not relent in ensuring that criminal elements are sent out of the State,” the statement added.

The post Police arrest nine over armed robbery, rescues kidnapped victims in Nasarawa  appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Umahi urges South-East to vote massively for Tinubu
description:
Minister of Works, David Umahi, has urged the people of the South-East to vote massively for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general elections, saying such support would give the region greater confidence in negotiating for its interests at the national level.







Umahi made the appeal on Thurs
content:
Minister of Works, David Umahi, has urged the people of the South-East to vote massively for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general elections, saying such support would give the region greater confidence in negotiating for its interests at the national level.

Umahi made the appeal on Thursday at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Awka, Anambra State, where he argued that the Tinubu administration had significantly benefited the region, particularly in infrastructure development.

According to the minister, the South-East could no longer afford to remain on the sidelines of national affairs, adding that a massive vote for Tinubu would strengthen the region’s position at the national negotiation table.

“We cannot accept to be by the sideline. This president, this man of audacity, this man with rare courage, President Bola Tinubu, has integrated the people of the South-East. This president has cleansed our tears,” he said.

“Before now, we were not remembered. Before now, positions would be shared, and nothing tangible would come to the South-East.

“We need to vote massively for President Tinubu so that we can approach the negotiation table with boldness.”

Umahi maintained that the region was now benefiting from significant federal infrastructure investments, citing several ongoing and proposed road projects in Anambra State.

“Ndi Anambra State, let me tell you that the chunk of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s infrastructure projects resides here in Anambra State,” he said.

He cited the 108-kilometre Enugu-Onitsha highway project, saying 100 kilometres of the road was being constructed with concrete pavement.

According to him, 70 per cent of the concrete pavement section has been completed at a cost of N150 billion, while the remaining section, being constructed with asphalt, is valued at N202 billion.

He said the entire project was more than 85 per cent completed.

The minister also listed the 35-kilometre bypass of the Second Niger Bridge, valued at N175 billion, which he said included several bridges in Anambra.

Umahi further said Tinubu intervened when the First Niger Bridge developed problems, ensuring that the repairs were completed within two weeks.

He also identified the proposed 76-kilometre Upper-Nnewi dualisation project as another federal infrastructure intervention approved for the state, adding that procurement was ongoing.

Meanwhile, the APC had on October 13 rejigged its presidential campaign council, bringing in Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo, a member of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), alongside several other politicians from opposition parties.

The post Umahi urges South-East to vote massively for Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: JUST IN: NNPCL, MRS, other filling stations slash petrol prices following Dangote’s price cut
description:
The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL), MRS and other filling stations have further reduced their petrol pump prices following a recent reduction in the gantry price by Dangote Refinery.
A market survey conducted by Very Nigerian on Thursday showed that NNPCL had lowered its petrol
content:
The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL), MRS and other filling stations have further reduced their petrol pump prices following a recent reduction in the gantry price by Dangote Refinery.

A market survey conducted by Very Nigerian on Thursday showed that NNPCL had lowered its petrol price to N1,300 per litre from N1,325, representing a reduction of N25 per litre.

The new price has been introduced at NNPCL outlets along Kubwa Expressway and in Zones 4 and 6 in Abuja.

Similarly, MRS filling stations have reduced their petrol price by N34 per litre, bringing it down from N1,399 to N1,365 across their outlets in Abuja.

The latest adjustments come days after Dangote Refinery reduced its petrol gantry price, prompting further changes in pump prices across the country.

Also, Empire Energy and Ranoil filling stations adjusted their petrol pump prices to N1,385 per litre from N1,420.

This means that retail petrol prices in Abuja now range between N1,300 and N1,385 per litre.

Very Nigerian reports that the latest price reductions across filling stations followed Dangote Refinery’s decision to reduce its petrol gantry price to N1,159 per litre, while the price of imported petrol stood at N1,063 per litre.

The downward adjustment in domestic petrol prices comes as Brent and West Texas Intermediate, WTI, crude oil traded at $84 and $93 per barrel, respectively, at the time of filing this report.

Recall that on November 4, 2026, NNPCL reduced its petrol pump price to N1,325 per litre from between N1,370 and N1,405.

title: Man accused of AI cheating in South Korean exam found dead
description:
A 32-year-old South Korean man accused of using artificial intelligence to cheat in a law school entrance examination has been found dead at a motel in Seoul, amid a police investigation into the allegations.
The man, identified as Lee Jin-woo, was found at a motel near Cheonho Station at about 1:12
content:
A 32-year-old South Korean man accused of using artificial intelligence to cheat in a law school entrance examination has been found dead at a motel in Seoul, amid a police investigation into the allegations.

The man, identified as Lee Jin-woo, was found at a motel near Cheonho Station at about 1:12 pm on Wednesday, according to The Chosun Daily.

Police had been searching for Lee after receiving a report at 8:42 am expressing concern about his safety.

His discovery came hours after he failed to appear for a planned live-streamed test intended to address allegations that he had used AI to obtain a perfect score in this year’s Legal Education Eligibility Test, known as LEET.

Lee had reportedly promised to demonstrate his abilities by solving Korean-language questions from South Korea’s College Scholastic Ability Test in real time on YouTube at a private institute in Daechi-dong, Seoul.

The exercise was scheduled to begin at 8 am, but Lee did not arrive. His phone was also switched off.

The institute cancelled the exercise after he failed to show up by 8:35 am, when the examination papers were due to be distributed.

The institute reportedly said there was still a possibility that an accomplice inside an actual examination centre could relay questions to a candidate, even during a live verification exercise.

Police and fire officials visited Lee’s home in Bongcheon-dong, Gwanak-gu, after the institute raised concerns about his whereabouts, but found that he had not returned home since leaving on the evening of November 17.

Police subsequently traced his movements after confirming that he had checked out of a motel in Gwangjin-gu on Wednesday morning.

A packaging box that had contained a multi-purpose rope was reportedly found in the room he had occupied. Officers later tracked his movements towards the Achasan area and then Songpa-gu and Gangdong-gu before locating him at the motel near Cheonho Station.

A note allegedly written by Lee was also found at the scene. It reportedly contained the words, “My body and mind are exhausted,” but did not mention or apologise for the alleged examination cheating.

The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency said the cause of death would be established through an autopsy and other investigations.

“Once the death is finalised, the cause of death will be confirmed through the autopsy and other investigations,” the agency said.

However, the police investigation into the alleged AI-assisted cheating will continue despite Lee’s condition.

The Financial Crimes Investigation Unit of the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency’s Metropolitan Investigation Division said, “Despite the suspect’s death, we will continue the investigation to confirm the substantive truth related to this case.”

The post Man accused of AI cheating in South Korean exam found dead appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: ‎2027: APGA endorses Tinubu
description: ‎‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru‎‎ABUJA — Ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election, the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) on Thursday adopted President Bola Tinubu as its presidential candidate and handed him the party’s flag.‎‎Governor Charles Soludo and the party’s national chairman handed
content:
‎
‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
‎
‎ABUJA — Ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election, the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) on Thursday adopted President Bola Tinubu as its presidential candidate and handed him the party’s flag.
‎
‎Governor Charles Soludo and the party’s national chairman handed the flag to President Tinubu at an All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign event in Awka, Anambra State.
‎
‎Prof. Soludo said, “We resolved, in the spirit of one Nigeria, progressivism, cooperative federalism, unity and the progress of our indivisible, united Nigeria, to hand our flag to Prese
ent Tinubu.”
‎
‎He said all APGA members would canvass votes for President Tinubu.
‎He advocated political engagement and bridge-building rather than what he described as isolationism, saying this approach would ensure regional prosperity.
‎
‎Soludo said Ndigbo should adopt a political strategy that rejects political isolation and ethnic intolerance, noting that such attitudes limit political leverage and risk wasting productive years through internal conflict.
‎
‎He encouraged building bridges towards a united nation where all citizens could thrive, regardless of their location or ethnicity. He also asserted that the 2027 election was effectively decided in favour of the Tinubu/Shettima ticket.
‎
‎He claimed that no other presidential candidate had presented a credible alternative or a superior manifesto. He added that there was significant consensus on the administration’s approach to security and economic stability, which he credited with rescuing the economy from collapse.
‎
‎The governor described wasting political opportunities as a high-stakes mistake with significant long-term consequences. He stressed that solidarity with the Tinubu government was a means of securing future political influence in 2027.
‎
‎For his part, the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Kalu, advocated a shift from sentimental politics to strategic cooperation to drive development in Anambra State and the wider South-East.
‎
‎He argued that the success of Igbo people in business and commerce stems from strategic thinking rather than sentiment.
‎
‎He suggested that political progress requires moving away from protest-based approaches and focusing instead on strategic alliances.

title: Africa Records 71.4bn Transactions, $1.8trn Instant Payments In 2025 — Report
description: Africa’s instant payment systems processed 71.4 billion transactions worth $1.8 trillion in 2025, nearly three times the volume recorded in 2021, according to a new report by the AfricaNenda Foundation, the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa and the World Bank Group.The fifth editio
content:
Africa’s instant payment systems processed 71.4 billion transactions worth $1.8 trillion in 2025, nearly three times the volume recorded in 2021, according to a new report by the AfricaNenda Foundation, the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa and the World Bank Group.

The fifth edition of the State of Inclusive Instant Payment Systems in Africa (SIIPS) report, published on Thursday, highlighted the rapid expansion of digital payment infrastructure across the continent but warns that access alone has not translated into widespread everyday usage.

According to the report, 89 per cent of African adults live in countries with access to an instant payment system.

However, a survey of 1,403 digital payment users across 15 markets found that 55 per cent still use cash for about half of their transactions.

It also found that more than half of respondents had experienced payment problems, including delays and transfers to the wrong recipients, while one in three affected users never reported such incidents, largely because they did not know how to do so.

“Five years ago, our first report mapped 29 instant payment systems; today there are 39, and one in two African adults live in a country served by an inclusive instant payment system IIPS,” said Sabine F. Mensah, who is Deputy CEO of AfricaNenda Foundation and lead author of the report.

“The question has changed. It is no longer whether Africans can pay instantly, but whether they trust the system enough to stop reaching for cash. Our research shows that trust is won in seconds, through a payment that goes through instantly, with preventive safeguards such as recipient name validation, and a payment confirmation message received in real time. It is kept by getting timely resolution and people’s money back when something goes wrong.”

39 Instant Payment Systems

The report identified 39 live instant payment systems across Africa, comprising 35 domestic systems in 29 countries and four regional systems.

Overall, 43 African countries now have access to instant payment capabilities through domestic or regional platforms.

Four domestic systems were introduced in the past year in Liberia, Burundi, Guinea and Mauritania, while a new regional system now serves the eight countries of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU).

Another 17 countries have instant payment system projects underway.

Transaction volumes, according to the report, have grown by an average of 28 per cent annually since 2021, while the average transaction value has declined from $45 to $26, indicating increased use for smaller, everyday purchases.

Mobile money systems accounted for 73 per cent of all transaction volumes.

The report also identified instant payments, clear confirmation messages and recipient verification as the three major factors that build users’ confidence in digital transactions.

It noted that the handling of failed transactions also influences adoption, with 43 per cent of users who lost money reducing their use of digital payments, while those who received refunds often increased their usage.

Trust, Fraud Protection Challenges

On security, the report found that payment service providers are adopting artificial intelligence fraud prevention measures faster than instant payment system operators, while users largely perceive AI as a risk, particularly because of threats such as deepfakes.

It further observed that countries with operational instant payment systems record approximately seven percentage points higher active account usage.

According to the report, more inclusive instant payment systems also create opportunities to expand access to other financial services, including credit, through digital cash flow records.

“Africa has built inclusive instant payment infrastructure at remarkable speed, drawing on the talent of its own software engineers and designers,” said Robert Ochola, who is CEO of AfricaNenda Foundation.

“The next five years must be about making these systems affordable to use, safe and sustainable to run.”

The post Africa Records 71.4bn Transactions, $1.8trn Instant Payments In 2025 — Report appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Diaspora doctors seek medical missions to strengthen healthcare in Nigeria
description:
The Association of Nigerian Physicians in the Americas has called for a standardised framework for medical missions in Nigeria to ensure that diaspora interventions strengthen healthcare delivery beyond temporary medical relief.
The President of ANPA, Dr Gertie Chimeka-Anyanwoke, said medical missio
content:
The Association of Nigerian Physicians in the Americas has called for a standardised framework for medical missions in Nigeria to ensure that diaspora interventions strengthen healthcare delivery beyond temporary medical relief.

The President of ANPA, Dr Gertie Chimeka-Anyanwoke, said medical missions should be coordinated with state governments, ministries of health and healthcare facilities to enable visiting professionals to work with local medical teams and build their capacity to provide continuous care.

She made the call on Wednesday at the Redeemer’s Health Village in Mowe, Ogun State, during a global health roundtable involving healthcare leaders, health commissioners and other stakeholders.

Participants at the meeting discussed ways to improve healthcare delivery in Nigeria through diaspora engagement, emergency preparedness and technology.

Chimeka-Anyanwoke acknowledged the contributions of diaspora medical interventions to expanding access to healthcare services but stressed the need for structured partnerships that would enable local health workers to sustain the interventions after visiting professionals returned to their countries of residence.

She stated, “How can we in the diaspora contribute in ways that local partners value, that fit the communities you serve, and that continue after a mission ends? Chronic disease makes that question especially important. A screening event can identify high blood pressure, diabetes, or a possible cancer but what matters next is whether the person can access testing, treatment, medicines, and follow-up.

“The people and systems that make that continuity possible are already here. Our role should be to learn where support is most useful and work alongside those leading the care.

“We should measure success not only by how many people we reach during an outreach, but by whether patients remain connected to care and whether local teams have gained capacity they can continue to use.”

Also speaking, a former ANPA president, Dr Chinyere Anyaogu, said medical missions needed to move beyond occasional interventions and adopt a coordinated approach that would provide sustained support to healthcare facilities.

Anyaogu said, “What is crystallising is that we need to have a way whereby medical missions or diaspora interventions have a standardised process through the states to interface with healthcare facilities, so that it’s not incidental care.

“It is care that is interfaced with the on-ground teams so that they can sustain it after we’ve gone. They can have continuity.”

Anyaogu said working with local healthcare professionals would help visiting medical teams understand the country’s healthcare environment, operate within existing structures and identify areas requiring additional support.

She added that involving state ministries of health and healthcare commissions would improve coordination and ensure that knowledge acquired during medical missions translated into stronger local capacity.

According to her, diaspora doctors could contribute not only through direct patient care but also through training, skills transfer and other initiatives to improve healthcare delivery.

Anyaogu, an obstetrician and gynaecologist, said ANPA had sustained its commitment to healthcare collaboration, capacity building and advocacy through annual global outreach programmes and partnerships with other organisations.

She disclosed that the association, which had existed for more than 30 years, collaborated with organisations, including Rotary, to organise medical outreach programmes in Nigeria.

She said its relationships with state health authorities and other stakeholders had encouraged more diaspora medical professionals to participate in strengthening the country’s healthcare system.

“By doing that and building those relationships, we have more people who are able and willing to come back and participate in building a stronger healthcare system,” she stated.

Anyaogu said ANPA also prioritised capacity building through specialised training programmes aimed at improving the ability of Nigerian healthcare workers to manage emergencies.

She disclosed that the association conducted a Stop the Bleed training programme during its current mission to equip responders with skills to control severe bleeding in accident victims and other trauma patients before they reached hospitals.

According to her, about 12 trainers had been trained to subsequently train 200 participants in emergency bleeding controll, adding that approximately 15 healthcare workers received training in neonatal resuscitation to improve their ability to respond to newborns experiencing breathing difficulties or requiring respiratory support.

Anyaogu further disclosed that the association organised a menstrual hygiene skills camp where 40 girls were taught how to make reusable menstrual packs.

She said the initiatives highlighted the importance of combining medical outreach with practical training that could continue benefiting communities after visiting teams had left.

On emergency medical services, the former ANPA president called for stronger response infrastructure supported by technology.

She said technology could help identify hospitals equipped to receive emergency patients, warning that transferring critically ill people to facilities unable to manage their conditions could lead to dangerous delays.

She said, “There’s no point in having an emergency and then moving the patient to the hospital, only for the hospital to be unable to absorb the patient, and you go from hospital to hospital.

“Now we have technology. Perhaps there’s a way we can be smarter with that and even find a way to help relieve the hospitals of the turnover, thereby creating more capacity to absorb these emergencies.”

Also speaking, the immediate past National President of the Association of Nigerian Private Medical Practitioners, Dr Kayode Adesola, said Nigeria’s emergency medical response system was still developing and required sustained support to achieve its objectives.

Adesola called for increased investment, trained personnel and properly equipped emergency facilities, while urging greater public and private sector participation in strengthening the system.

Federal Government has existing policies aimed at making diaspora medical missions more coordinated and sustainable.

The National Diaspora Policy mandates the Federal Ministry of Health to implement national standards and guidelines for medical missions, identify healthcare needs and facilitate skills and knowledge transfer from Nigerian professionals abroad.

In July 2026, the ministry also launched the Nigerians in Diaspora Advanced Health Programme, a platform designed to connect Nigerian health professionals abroad with local healthcare institutions for specialist care, training, mentorship, and capacity building.

The post Diaspora doctors seek medical missions to strengthen healthcare in Nigeria appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Alex Ferguson greatest coach in football history — Pochettino
description:
Manchester United coach Mauricio Pochettino has paid a glowing tribute to legendary Manchester United manager Sir Alex Ferguson, describing him as the greatest coach in the history of sport.
The Argentine manager did not hesitate when sharing his opinion on Ferguson’s remarkable coaching legacy, hig
content:
Manchester United coach Mauricio Pochettino has paid a glowing tribute to legendary Manchester United manager Sir Alex Ferguson, describing him as the greatest coach in the history of sport.

The Argentine manager did not hesitate when sharing his opinion on Ferguson’s remarkable coaching legacy, highlighting the enormous respect he has for the former Manchester United boss.

As reported by Fabrizio Romano on X on Thursday, Pochettino was quoted as saying, “Sir Alex Ferguson is the best coach in the history of the sport, in my opinion,” Pochettino said.

Ferguson, who spent 26 years at Manchester United, built one of the most successful managerial legacies in football history, winning 13 Premier League titles and two UEFA Champions League trophies during his time at Old Trafford.

Pochettino also reflected on the privilege and responsibility that come with occupying a leadership position, explaining that the excitement of the role should provide the energy needed to embrace its challenges.

“Being here is an honour and a privilege. That is the responsibility that brings full energy in my body, because the excitement to be here is massive,” he explained.

The former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea manager also shared his philosophy on dealing with pressure, insisting that responsibility and expectations should motivate rather than overwhelm those carrying them.

“Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it’s too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back,” he added.

Pochettino further stressed the importance of allowing players the freedom to express their natural abilities, believing that talent flourishes when footballers feel connected to the game.

“When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent when you feel freedom,” he concluded.

His comments offer an insight into a coaching philosophy built around responsibility, positive energy and creative freedom, while his praise for Ferguson underlines the extraordinary influence the former Manchester United manager continues to have on football’s coaching generation.

The post Alex Ferguson greatest coach in football history — Pochettino appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: El Niño: Rising Climate Risks Deepen Economic Tensions
description: The El Niño weather phenomenon, expected to be exceptionally strong this year, is likely to exacerbate the disruptions to the global economy, with consequences including higher food and electricity prices.The naturally occurring warming of surface temperatures in the central and eastern equat
content:
The El Niño weather phenomenon, expected to be exceptionally strong this year, is likely to exacerbate the disruptions to the global economy, with consequences including higher food and electricity prices.

The naturally occurring warming of surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean has already altered wind and rainfall patterns around the world, resulting in devastating droughts and wildfires.

Combined with climate change as well as soaring prices for energy and other commodities from the US war against Iran, the potential for further damage is high.

“In general, you can say it’s an extreme negative supply shock,” Paolo Zanghieri, an economist at Generali Asset Management, told AFP.

Agriculture, trade and hydroelectric production are most immediately impacted by El Niño, which is expected to peak in December and last at least until next March — with repercussions felt for months beyond.

Oxford Economics estimates that if it is as strong as many experts warn, global GDP could be cut by 0.6 percent next year and a further 0.8 percent in 2028.

Inflation Pressures

Compromised harvests from excessive heat or rain are likely to send food costs higher, which will be especially painful for millions of people in developing countries, where food represents a much bigger share of household budgets.

“An El Niño characterised by a 2C rise in Pacific Ocean temperature could lift global food prices by up to 20 percent” by the first quarter of 2028, Zanghieri and his colleague Guillaume Tresca, an emerging markets strategist, wrote in a recent report.

That could lift overall US and eurozone inflation by 0.4 percentage points, but developing countries could see an additional 3.0 points in “a non-negligible, but temporary shock”, they wrote.

“Our vulnerability index suggests that South Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa face the greatest risks,” they added.

While a moderate food price shock can be offset by increased imports, existing stocks or product substitutions, Deutsche Bank analysts warn of more serious risks from a widespread crisis.

“A large shock propagating across multiple countries can’t be absorbed as easily, with second-round inflation effects likely to result,” they wrote in July.

For Simon Lacoume, an economist at the French export credit insurance group Coface, a drop in the corn harvest in Brazil, for example, would “percolate through the livestock farming and meat sectors”.

Droughts could also lower reservoir levels at hydroelectric plants, forcing countries to increase oil and gas imports at a time when prices are already high because of the Gulf conflict.

But the disruptions can also work the other way: Sri Lanka recently cancelled an electricity price hike after heavy El Nino rains helped fill reservoirs.

Hard To Measure

Droughts are also impacting global trade by forcing reduced traffic through the Panama Canal, after lower water storage forced authorities to restrict operations since September.

Recent rains have allowed increases, but the government has declared a nationwide emergency over the exceptionally strong El Niño.

Central banks are also wrestling with how to judge the fallout, worried about limiting inflation while not increasing interest rates to levels that could spark an economic downturn.

“The impact is very disparate and complicated to measure,” Tresca at Generali told AFP. “It depends on when a meteorological event hits during the planting cycle, for example.”

The Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) has urged governments to invest more in existing resilience plans for dealing with climate change.

But in most countries, the implementation of efforts to adapt agriculture and infrastructure remains insufficient.

“We don’t see the national adaptation plans actually resulting in actual mandates for different economic actors to take on these resilience investments,” said Catherine Gamper, Team Lead for climate change adaptation at the Paris-based agency.

And even when the will exists, many countries are also struggling to cut debt and deficit levels that have soared for a multitude of reasons in recent years.

“There is absolutely a public finance problem,” Gamper said.

AFP

The post El Niño: Rising Climate Risks Deepen Economic Tensions appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Anthony Joshua to meet newborn daughter for first time after Fury showdown
description:
British heavyweight boxer Anthony Joshua has revealed that he will meet his newborn daughter for the first time on December 12, a day after his scheduled fight against fellow British boxer Tyson Fury.
Joshua, who is currently undergoing a training camp in Marbella, Spain, ahead of the December 11 bo
content:
British heavyweight boxer Anthony Joshua has revealed that he will meet his newborn daughter for the first time on December 12, a day after his scheduled fight against fellow British boxer Tyson Fury.

Joshua, who is currently undergoing a training camp in Marbella, Spain, ahead of the December 11 bout, said his preparation for the fight had kept him away from his newborn child since her birth.

The 37-year-old made the disclosure during an interview with British newspaper *The Sun*, published on Wednesday.

He explained that although he had not met the baby in person, he had maintained contact with her and her mother, Nicole Osbourne, through video calls.

Joshua is expected to reunite with his daughter on December 12, immediately after fulfilling his boxing commitment against Fury.
He said the decision to remain in camp was a sacrifice he had made months before the baby’s arrival.

“I knew the sacrifice I had to make for this fight nine months ago, I made the commitment. We are on a mission. It’s not ideal but my little girl is in good hands. There’ll be many, many more birthdays I’ll be at, for sure.

“On December 12th, I’ll go and check in and rock her to sleep and let her hear my voice, and let her feel my heartbeat. The basic stuff,” he said.

The former world heavyweight champion said the situation had been difficult, but he was reassured that the baby was in good hands.

According to The Sun, the baby was born on Saturday, November 14, about three weeks before the scheduled fight. Joshua said the bout was initially expected to take place in mid-November, which would have allowed him to be present for the birth.

He also said the arrival of his daughter followed a difficult year, particularly the deaths of his close friends Sina Ghami and Latif Ayodele in a car crash in Nigeria last December.

“This past year has been incredibly tough, I realised how precious life is, and how short it can be. I’m just going to live my life by duty, and even having a baby girl was part of my duty,” he said.

He added that he wanted to “bring life in” after losing his friends.

Joshua, who already has an 11-year-old son, JJ, with Osbourne, described the newborn as a blessing and said he was looking forward to fatherhood again.

Ebikeme-Neme and his supporters are from Angalabiri community in Sa
content:
A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Bayelsa State, Clement Ebikeme-Neme, popularly known as Osama, has defected to the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) alongside his supporters ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Ebikeme-Neme and his supporters are from Angalabiri community in Sagbama Local Government Area of Bayelsa State.

The defectors were received by former Bayelsa State Governor and Senator representing Bayelsa West, Seriake Dickson, alongside other leaders of the NDC.

Dickson announced the development in a post on his verified X account, where he welcomed the former APC chieftain and his supporters into the opposition party.

“Yesterday, I received Mr Clement Ebikeme-Neme, alias Osama, who defected from the APC with all his supporters in Angalabiri community into the NDC,” the former governor stated.

He added that youth leaders of the party were present to welcome the new members.

Dickson also expressed appreciation to youths from Ayamasa community who presented him with gifts in recognition of his contributions to their community and the well-being of its residents.

The NDC chieftain described the party’s growing membership as evidence of its increasing grassroots support in Bayelsa State.

He further called on Nigerians to reject political intimidation, violence and propaganda, urging them to support what he described as the party’s efforts to provide an alternative political direction for the country.

The defection comes as political parties intensify efforts to strengthen their structures and attract influential grassroots mobilisers ahead of the 2027 general elections.

title: 2027: Radda warns Katsina voters against ‘irresponsible’ politicians
description:
Katsina State Governor, Dikko Radda, has urged voters in Kankia Local Government Area of the state to resist attempts by what he described as disrespectful and irresponsible politicians to lure them away from the All Progressives Congress.
Radda made the appeal on Thursday during a political rally i
content:
Katsina State Governor, Dikko Radda, has urged voters in Kankia Local Government Area of the state to resist attempts by what he described as disrespectful and irresponsible politicians to lure them away from the All Progressives Congress.

Radda made the appeal on Thursday during a political rally in the area, where he called on residents to support President Bola Tinubu, himself and other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections.

Describing his visit to Kankia as a homecoming, the governor said the people of the area had demonstrated their preference for responsible leadership through their support for APC-led administrations at the state and federal levels.

“My visit to Kankia is a homecoming. It shows that Kankia people need good leaders. They are not in support of irresponsible and disrespectful persons.

“Kankia has benefited from several development projects facilitated by the former Minister of Housing and Urban Development, Architect Ahmed Musa Dangiwa,” he said.

He added that residents had assured him of their commitment to voting for APC candidates at all levels in the forthcoming elections.

Earlier, the Katsina State APC Chairman, Dr Bishir Gambo Saulawa, thanked party supporters for the warm reception accorded to the campaign team and urged them to strengthen their commitment to the party.

“I challenge you all, the supporters, to ensure that the votes secured by the APC in the 2023 general elections are doubled in 2027,” he said, expressing optimism that the large turnout at the rally would translate into votes.

Also speaking, the Director-General of the Tinubu/Dikko 2027 Campaign Council in Katsina State and former Minister of Housing and Urban Development, Architect Ahmed Musa Dangiwa, who hails from the locality, said Kankia Local Government Area had benefited significantly from APC-led governments at both the state and federal levels.

Dangiwa said the area had received strategic political appointments, which he described as evidence of the confidence reposed in its people by the APC leadership.

He recalled that President Tinubu appointed him minister following a recommendation by Governor Radda, who had earlier appointed him Secretary to the State Government shortly after assuming office in 2023.

“I was personally appointed as minister by President Bola Tinubu after the governor of Katsina State recommended me. The governor had earlier, before my appointment as minister, appointed me as his SSG shortly after taking the oath of office in 2023.

“Nobody facilitated my appointment from outside; it was the governor. These and many other appointments given to Kankia people have greatly assisted our people so far,” he said.

Dangiwa urged residents to reciprocate the appointments and other benefits by voting for the APC in the forthcoming elections.

“All these appointments we are holding are far better than contesting under the platform of a crippled party. Please ensure that you vote for APC from top to bottom in the forthcoming elections,” he added.

Similarly, the Katsina State APC Deputy Chairman, Bala Abu, urged Kankia residents to support what he described as better leadership, saying the state had begun to witness positive results under Radda’s administration.

He also questioned the viability of the African Democratic Congress, alleging that irregularities surrounding its candidate selection process could affect the party’s chances in the forthcoming elections.

Abu cautioned voters against supporting the ADC candidate, claiming that doing so could amount to wasted votes if the party’s candidate failed to emerge victorious.

title: Tinubu has ended South-East marginalisation, says Umahi
description:
The Minister of Works, Senator Dave Umahi, has said President Bola Tinubu has ended the marginalisation of the South-East through increased political inclusion and infrastructure development, urging residents of the region to support his re-election bid.
Umahi made the appeal on Thursday during the
content:
The Minister of Works, Senator Dave Umahi, has said President Bola Tinubu has ended the marginalisation of the South-East through increased political inclusion and infrastructure development, urging residents of the region to support his re-election bid.

Umahi made the appeal on Thursday during the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Anambra State, where Tinubu was represented by Vice-President Kashim Shettima.

The former Ebonyi State governor said the South-East could no longer afford to remain on the sidelines of national politics, arguing that the region had benefited from the Tinubu administration.

“In the Southeast, in Anambra State, we cannot continue to stay by the side,” Umahi said.

He described Tinubu as a courageous leader who had integrated the South-East into national affairs, claiming that previous administrations had failed to give the region adequate recognition in political appointments and development projects.

“This President, this man of audacity, this man with real courage, President Bola Tinubu, he has integrated the people of Southeast,” he said.

“This President has cleansed our tears. Before now, we were not remembered. Before now, positions would not be shared, and nothing tangible will come to the Southeast,” Umahi added.

To support his position, the minister highlighted federal road projects in Anambra and other parts of the South-East, describing them as evidence of the administration’s commitment to infrastructure development in the region.

He cited the Enugu-Onitsha road project, saying 108 kilometres of the dual carriageway was under construction, with about 100 kilometres being executed using reinforced concrete pavement.

According to him, about 70 per cent of the concrete section had been completed, with N150bn committed to the project, while the remaining asphalt section was estimated to cost N202bn.

Umahi said the entire project was more than 85 per cent completed.

He also cited the 35-kilometre bypass of the Second Niger Bridge, valued at N175bn, which he said included multiple bridges in Anambra State.

The minister recalled the Federal Government’s intervention when the first Niger Bridge developed problems, saying Tinubu acted swiftly to ensure repairs.

“When the first Niger Bridge was giving trouble, the President marched out. And within two weeks, that project was fixed,” he said.

Umahi further disclosed that new road projects had been approved for the state, including a proposed 76-kilometre dualisation project, for which procurement was ongoing.

He urged residents of Anambra and other South-East states to consider the administration’s record in making their political decisions, insisting that the region should remain actively involved in national affairs.

“God is with us, and we will not be on the sideline again,” Umahi said.

title: Fountain of Life Church postpones thanksgiving service
description:
The Fountain of Life Church has postponed its 2026 Thanksgiving service, which was scheduled for Sunday, November 22.
The Lagos-based church announced the decision in a notice shared on its official social media platforms on Thursday, November 19.
The statement read, “Please be informed that our Tha
content:
The Fountain of Life Church has postponed its 2026 Thanksgiving service, which was scheduled for Sunday, November 22.

The Lagos-based church announced the decision in a notice shared on its official social media platforms on Thursday, November 19.

The statement read, “Please be informed that our Thanksgiving 2026 Service, previously scheduled for Sunday, November 22, has been postponed. A new date will be communicated in due course.”

No reason was given for the postponement, and the church did not indicate when the service would be rescheduled.

The announcement comes amid an ongoing leadership crisis at the church involving Senior Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and members of its Board of Trustees.

Earlier this week, a group of trustees announced that they had withdrawn recognition of Odukoya as senior pastor with immediate effect.

They cited a review of the church’s constitution and a December 2021 video recording in which the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, outlined succession arrangements that named another individual as preferred successor, while assigning Odukoya administrative and youth church roles.

The trustees also referenced governance concerns and issues surrounding Odukoya’s recent remarriage.

Odukoya and representatives of the church rejected the removal announcement, describing it as constitutionally invalid and not a proper decision of the Board of Trustees.

They maintained that he remains the duly appointed senior pastor and chairman of the board, a position unanimously approved in September 2023 following his father’s death.

The trustees later reaffirmed their position and appointed Pastor Rotimi Okpaise to provide interim spiritual and administrative leadership pending further consultations. Control of the church’s official social media accounts has also been disputed between the sides.

Odukoya was notably absent from the church’s midweek service on Thursday as the crisis continued.

The thanksgiving service had been expected to draw significant attention given the leadership questions.

The postponement of the Fountain of Life Church’s 2026 Thanksgiving Service comes amid an ongoing leadership dispute between Senior Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and members of the church’s Board of Trustees.

The crisis emerged after some trustees announced the withdrawal of their recognition of Odukoya as senior pastor, citing constitutional provisions, succession arrangements reportedly outlined by the late church founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, and other governance concerns.

The trustees referenced a December 2021 video in which the late founder allegedly identified another individual as his preferred successor while assigning Odukoya administrative and youth church responsibilities.

title: Tambuwal meets British envoy, seeks credible 2027 polls
description:
Former Sokoto State Governor and Senator representing Sokoto South, Aminu Tambuwal, has called for strong democratic institutions, respect for the rule of law and credible elections ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Tambuwal made the call on Tuesday during a meeting with the newly appointed Briti
content:
Former Sokoto State Governor and Senator representing Sokoto South, Aminu Tambuwal, has called for strong democratic institutions, respect for the rule of law and credible elections ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Tambuwal made the call on Tuesday during a meeting with the newly appointed British High Commissioner to Nigeria, Peter Vowles, at the British High Commission in Abuja.

The meeting focused on issues of mutual interest to Nigeria and the United Kingdom, particularly the country’s democratic process and preparations for the 2027 general elections.

In a statement shared on his X handle on Thursday, Tambuwal described the engagement as insightful, saying it provided an opportunity to discuss the longstanding relationship between Nigeria and the United Kingdom.

He said credible, transparent and peaceful elections remained essential to strengthening democracy in the country.

“I emphasised the need for strong institutions, respect for the rule of law and an electoral environment in which every eligible Nigerian can participate freely and confidently, knowing that their vote will count,” he stated.

The former Speaker of the House of Representatives stressed that electoral credibility was critical to democratic progress and public confidence in the electoral process.

Tambuwal also expressed his willingness to sustain constructive engagements with relevant international partners to advance shared interests and strengthen the longstanding relationship between Nigeria and the United Kingdom.

The meeting comes as political activities gradually gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general elections.

title: [VIDEO] Drama As Ngige Urges Residents To Vote For APC ‘From Top To Bottom’ At Anambra Presidential Rally
description: There was a mild drama at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Anambra State on Thursday when a former governor of the state, Chris Ngige, urged residents to vote for the APC in the 2027 presidential, National Assembly, and House of Assembly elections.The former Ministe
content:
There was a mild drama at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Anambra State on Thursday when a former governor of the state, Chris Ngige, urged residents to vote for the APC in the 2027 presidential, National Assembly, and House of Assembly elections.

The former Minister of Labour and Employment, who spoke in Igbo, said Anambra residents had one target.

“We will vote for the APC from top to bottom,” Ngige said, prompting reactions from participants at the rally, including Governor Charles Soludo of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), who stood beside him on stage and told his predecessor that the rally is a joint one.

The former governor, who said he was not surprised by the reactions, later told members of APGA to vote for candidates of their choice.

“Okay, members of APGA — freedom of choice — when you get to the polling booth, vote for the better place,” he said.

Ngige added that while people were free to choose between APGA and the APC, Anambra desires to be connected to the Federal Government at the centre and get it through the ruling party.

Earlier, the former minister said he remains a member of the APC, claiming that he brought the party to the South-East.

“I am still a member of the APC, bona fide member, because I brought APC to the South East — 2013/2014,” he said.

“The only thing is that I told people I am on sabbatical, but even if I am on sabbatical, my governor cannot be doing something, and the Vice President is coming physically, and the governor has called me to say we are here, and I would say I won’t come. No.”

Ngige said people should not be forced but persuaded to vote during the 2027 general election.

He also said those stopping people from campaigning are not doing so in the name of the APC.

“We don’t want that — destruction of vehicles, stoning of people. No! We don’t want that. We must emulate other people practising democracy,” the former Anambra governor said. “Democracy gives you the right of choice; even inside the same family, you must exercise that.”

content:
British heavyweight boxer Anthony Joshua has said he will meet his newborn daughter for the first time on December 12, a day after his scheduled fight against compatriot Tyson Fury.

Joshua, who is currently in Marbella, Spain, for a training camp ahead of the December 11 bout, said he had not been able to see the baby since her birth because of his commitment to the fight.

The 37-year-old disclosed this in an interview with British newspaper, The Sun, published on Wednesday, saying he had been keeping in touch with the newborn and her mother, Nicole Osbourne, through video calls.

He said the decision to remain in camp was a sacrifice he had made months before the baby’s arrival.

“I knew the sacrifice I had to make for this fight nine months ago, I made the commitment. We are on a mission. It’s not ideal but my little girl is in good hands. There’ll be many, many more birthdays I’ll be at, for sure.

“On December 12th, I’ll go and check in and rock her to sleep and let her hear my voice, and let her feel my heartbeat. The basic stuff,” he said.

The former world heavyweight champion said the situation had been difficult, but he was reassured that the baby was in good hands.

According to The Sun, the baby was born on Saturday, November 14, about three weeks before the scheduled fight. Joshua said the bout was initially expected to take place in mid-November, which would have allowed him to be present for the birth.

He also said the arrival of his daughter followed a difficult year, particularly the deaths of his close friends Sina Ghami and Latif Ayodele in a car crash in Nigeria last December.

“This past year has been incredibly tough, I realised how precious life is, and how short it can be. I’m just going to live my life by duty, and even having a baby girl was part of my duty,” he said.

He added that he wanted to “bring life in” after losing his friends.

Joshua, who already has an 11-year-old son, JJ, with Osbourne, described the newborn as a blessing and said he was looking forward to fatherhood again.

The December 11 contest against Fury is the long-awaited clash between the two British heavyweight rivals.

title: NAPTIP seals Abuja hotel linked to N1.8m newborn sale
description:
The National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons has sealed a hotel in Gwarinpa, Abuja, following investigations into the alleged illegal procurement and sale of a newborn baby for N1.8m.
NAPTIP disclosed this in a statement on Thursday, saying, “Preliminary findings indicate that a
content:
The National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons has sealed a hotel in Gwarinpa, Abuja, following investigations into the alleged illegal procurement and sale of a newborn baby for N1.8m.

NAPTIP disclosed this in a statement on Thursday, saying, “Preliminary findings indicate that a suspect allegedly lured a pregnant woman with a promise to purchase her unborn baby for N1.8 million after delivery, exploiting her vulnerable circumstances in the process.”

The agency said, “Following the delivery, the newborn baby was allegedly taken from the mother, while a sum of N300,000 was reportedly paid to her.”

It added that the hotel was allegedly used in connection with the incident, prompting it to seal the premises as part of its ongoing investigation and enforcement measures.

NAPTIP said it was working to “establish the full circumstances of the incident, trace the newborn baby, identify all persons connected to the alleged transaction and determine their respective roles.”

The agency described the case as particularly serious, citing the vulnerability of the mother and the need to establish the safety and whereabouts of the baby.

“Children are not commodities for sale, and anyone found culpable will be dealt with in accordance with the law,” it said.

NAPTIP also urged members of the public to report suspicious activities involving the sale or illegal procurement of children.

It appealed to the media to respect the privacy of the mother and baby while investigations continue.

The latest incident comes about three months after NAPTIP sealed a suspected illegal maternity facility in Elelenwo, Port Harcourt, Rivers State, over an alleged N13.5m baby sale involving three children.

PUNCH reported in August that the agency said a Liberian national residing in Belgium had allegedly taken custody of three children within about a month of arriving in Nigeria, despite having no evidence of pregnancy.

NAPTIP said investigations indicated that approximately N13.5m changed hands in connection with the transfer of the children. The agency also arrested the facility’s owner and a staff member in connection with the incident.
