title: Diana London: Tinubu should grant interviews to Nigerian journalists – Osinbajo’s ex-aide
description:
A former spokesman for ex-Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo, Laolu Akande, has described it as an insult for anyone invited to interview a sitting president or vice-president to demand payment for the engagement.
Akande stated this on Thursday while reacting to the controversy surrounding President Bola
content:
A former spokesman for ex-Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo, Laolu Akande, has described it as an insult for anyone invited to interview a sitting president or vice-president to demand payment for the engagement.

Akande stated this on Thursday while reacting to the controversy surrounding President Bola Tinubu’s interview with American political strategist and lobbyist, Diana London.

Reports had alleged that the Federal Government paid $4.5m in connection with the engagement, although the precise link between the interview and the reported lobbying arrangement remains unclear.

The former presidential spokesman, however, said his major concern was that Tinubu had not made himself available for interviews with Nigerian journalists when he featured on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily.

Akande said, “I wish the president were also having interviews with Nigerian journalists, that’s my own main issue with this development.

“It’s not a bad thing that the president has chosen to have this interview; my worry is that he’s leaving out the Nigerian press. Why has he not made himself available for Nigerians to interrogate him?

“As to the controversy whether this woman (Diana) was paid, the woman has denied that she was doing this as a paid lobbyist of the Federal Government. The ADC people are saying that there should be more clarity, there should be more transparency, yes.

“Let the Federal Government also give us more facts that this is not a paid for interview. The most important thing is that Nigerians should be given the opportunity to interview Mr President.

“My own experience in the Villa, I wasn’t aware of any payment for an interview and I expressed this. When we were in the Villa, I considered it an insult to have an opportunity to interview the president and the vice president and be asking for money, the president of a country is the numero uno.”

The controversy followed reports alleging that London received $4.5m in connection with a lobbying arrangement involving the Nigerian government.

However, London, who heads London Global Strategies, denied receiving the amount from the Nigerian government or anyone else in the country.

She said she travelled to Nigeria to interview Tinubu for a documentary and to experience the country.

The controversy also drew reactions from former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, who questioned whether the interview formed part of the reported $4.5m lobbying arrangement.

Atiku cited United States filings identifying London as a consultant to DCI Group AZ, a firm engaged to work for Nigeria through Aster Legal.

He noted that the filings recorded a $4.5m retainer paid to DCI Group but did not establish whether the presidential interview was covered by the arrangement.

He subsequently called on the Presidency to publish the lobbying agreement, disclose the payments and invoices, and release the full, unedited recording of the interview.

The post Diana London: Tinubu should grant interviews to Nigerian journalists – Osinbajo’s ex-aide appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Tinubu wouldn’t allow son marry Igbo woman if he hated Ndigbo – Shettima
description:
Vice-President Kashim Shettima has defended President Bola Tinubu against allegations of hostility towards the Igbo, saying the President would not have allowed his son, Seyi, to marry an Igbo woman if he disliked the ethnic group.
Shettima made the remark on Thursday at the All Progressives Congres
content:
Vice-President Kashim Shettima has defended President Bola Tinubu against allegations of hostility towards the Igbo, saying the President would not have allowed his son, Seyi, to marry an Igbo woman if he disliked the ethnic group.

Shettima made the remark on Thursday at the All Progressives Congress’ SoluTinubu 2027 campaign rally in Awka, Anambra State, where he appealed to the South-East to support Tinubu’s re-election bid.

“President Tinubu is a friend of Ndigbo. His son, Seyi, is married to a lady of Igbo extraction. If he hates the Igbo, he couldn’t have allowed his son to marry an Igbo lady,” he said.

The Vice-President added, “So we are essentially one people. The Igbos are an essential component of the Nigerian configuration.”

Seyi is married to Layal Jade Tinubu, a Nigerian-Lebanese entrepreneur and philanthropist.

She is of Lebanese and Nigerian descent, with her Nigerian maternal heritage linked to Anambra State.

The couple got married in August 2016, with their wedding celebrations held in Lagos and at Villa Erba, Lake Como, Italy. Their Italian wedding ceremony took place on August 10, 2016.

Layal studied Politics and African Studies at the School of Oriental and African Studies, University of London, and holds a master’s degree in Entrepreneurship and Business Management from the University of Surrey, United Kingdom.

She is the founder of Tots Toys, a children’s educational toy business, and co-founded the Noella Foundation with her husband. The couple have two children.

Seyi had also cited his marriage to an Igbo woman while campaigning for his father’s presidential ambition in Anambra State ahead of the 2023 general election.

During a visit to the state in January 2023, he appealed to residents and the wider South-East to vote for Tinubu, saying, “I am appealing to Ndi-Anambra and the Igbo region at large to vote for my father because I married an Igbo lady, Chinwe Layal.”

He was subsequently conferred with the chieftaincy title of Nwannedinamba by the traditional ruler of Mbaukwu Kingdom, Igwe Peter Anukwui, in Awka South Local Government Area of Anambra State.

Meanwhile, Shettima assured the South-East that the region could produce Nigeria’s president in the next political dispensation when power rotates to the South.

“And in the next dispensation, when power comes to the South, I can assure you that power will find its residence in the eastern region,” he said.

The rally was part of the APC’s efforts to strengthen its political support in the South-East ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

The post Tinubu wouldn’t allow son marry Igbo woman if he hated Ndigbo – Shettima appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Igbo presidency must be eight full years – Oshiomhole
description:
Senator Adams Oshiomhole has said any future Nigerian president of Igbo extraction must serve a full eight-year tenure, declaring that the South-East should not settle for a half-term presidency.
Oshiomhole stated this on Thursday at the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Anamb
content:
Senator Adams Oshiomhole has said any future Nigerian president of Igbo extraction must serve a full eight-year tenure, declaring that the South-East should not settle for a half-term presidency.

Oshiomhole stated this on Thursday at the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Anambra State, where he praised Governor Chukwuma Soludo’s administration and President Bola Tinubu’s policies on education and university funding.

“When Ndi Igbo will become president, it must be eight full years. No half cup. It will be full cup by those with brain, with courage, and fill the gaps,” the former Edo State governor said.

He also described Anambra as “the headquarters of intellectuals”, saying the state had historically produced prominent figures, including Nigeria’s first president, Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe.

“Historically, it has been so. You produce the Zik of Africa, not just Zik of Nigeria,” he said.

Oshiomhole, who spoke about growing up in a village without a hospital or school, praised Tinubu’s education initiatives, particularly the provision of financial support and loans for students.

He recalled having to travel several kilometres to attend primary school, saying he appreciated a President who recognised the difficulties faced by people from disadvantaged backgrounds.

“When I find a president who remembers people of my background, and say you shall not lack education; I will give you money. I will give you loan, which you can only pay when you get job,” he said.

The senator also praised the Federal Government’s handling of issues affecting universities, particularly the maintenance of academic calendars and improved remuneration for lecturers.

He said, “Now, for four years, there has been no strike. This is a threat to those who live on primary ownership of a public university, because the only reason people say they are children there is because of the integrity of academic calendar.”

He attributed the previous disruption of university education to what he described as poor leadership in Abuja, saying, “Because of poor brains in Abuja in the past, the best brains were leaving the university system.”

Oshiomhole said Tinubu was addressing the challenges confronting the university system and working to attract experienced academics back to the sector through improved remuneration.

“President Bola Tinubu is not only respecting that calendar by dealing with issues confronting us, but also ensuring that by proper remuneration, we bring back to academia the finest brains in our society,” he said.

He urged Anambra residents to support the President, expressing confidence that they would benefit from the investment they were being asked to make.

The rally was also attended by Soludo, who said Tinubu did not need to rig the 2027 presidential election to win a second term, claiming that the APC ticket was better positioned than those of opposition parties.

PUNCH reported that the governor argued that opposition candidates lacked nationwide reach compared with Tinubu and Vice-President Kashim Shettima. 

He also praised the administration’s economic and security policies and cited the Nigerian Education Loan Fund as one of its initiatives.

Soludo said, “This election, to the best of our knowledge, is already won and lost. The President doesn’t need to rig any election. President Tinubu doesn’t need to rig any election.”

Oshiomhole’s comments come amid debate over the South-East’s quest for the presidency and the proposed single-term arrangement involving former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi ahead of the 2027 election.

Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, has repeatedly pledged to serve only one four-year term if elected, saying the decision is intended to promote stability.

“I want to be a one-term president because of stability. I would not stay a day longer than four years, even with a gun to my head,” Obi said in an interview with News Central TV in May.

His running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, later confirmed that they signed separate agreements committing Obi to a single four-year tenure, after which the presidency would return to the North.

Kwankwaso said the arrangement provided that “after his term of four years (2027-2031), it comes back to the North.” Obi subsequently described the arrangement as an agreement that should be respected.

The post Igbo presidency must be eight full years – Oshiomhole appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: As deadly super El Niño looms, Kwali Council battles deforestation, high Cooking Gas costs
description:
By Oladosu Adebola Oluwaseun
​Addressing concerns over a University of Chicago prediction warning of extreme heat waves which could result in over 30,000 additional heat-related deaths annually an official from the Department of Environmental Services at the Kwali Area Council, Abuja, Obamila John,
content:
By Oladosu Adebola Oluwaseun

​Addressing concerns over a University of Chicago prediction warning of extreme heat waves which could result in over 30,000 additional heat-related deaths annually an official from the Department of Environmental Services at the Kwali Area Council, Abuja, Obamila John, has outlined local efforts to combat deforestation and environmental degradation.

​Responding to questions on how the council is protecting residents from the impacts of climate change, John noted that the department relies heavily on its forestry unit to regulate tree felling and promote reforestation across local communities.

​”According to environmental regulations, if you cut down one tree, you are supposed to plant at least ten replacements,” he explained. “If this law is properly implemented, we can reduce extreme heat to a minimum and protect the ozone layer.”

​However, John acknowledged that enforcing anti-deforestation laws remains difficult due to the high cost of alternative cooking fuels.

With liquefied petroleum gas (cooking gas) costing around ₦1,800 per kilogram, most rural households cannot afford it and continue to rely on firewood and charcoal for daily cooking.

​”It is very hard to tell people to abandon firewood when they cannot afford gas,” he noted, adding that the economic situation in the country has even driven the sale of charcoal from rural communities into major cities.

​To bridge this gap, the department conducts community sensitization campaigns, educating villagers on the dangers of indiscriminate tree felling and its link to extreme heat and environmental damage.

​John also pointed to rapid urbanization and infrastructure development as major drivers of tree loss in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Recalling his time living in Kuchigoro about 20 years ago, he described how the stretch from the community toward Area 1 was once lined with dense, shady trees including mango trees where residents could walk, rest, and eat fruit safely without fear.

​”Today, those trees have been cleared to make way for roads, residential buildings, and commercial structures,” he said. “Even designated green areas where people used to relax have been taken over and developed. While development is necessary, it is costing us our tree cover.”

​Emphasizing that environmental protection requires a collective effort, John noted that the crisis extends beyond the FCT to northern and eastern Nigeria, urging both residents and authorities to prioritize tree planting and preserve remaining green spaces.

The post As deadly super El Niño looms, Kwali Council battles deforestation, high Cooking Gas costs appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Tinubu doesn’t need to rig 2027 election; He has already won — Soludo
description:
Anambra State Governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo, has said President Bola Tinubu does not need to rig the 2027 presidential election to secure re-election, insisting that the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) is already in a strong position ahead of the poll.
Soludo made the remarks on Thursda
content:
Anambra State Governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo, has said President Bola Tinubu does not need to rig the 2027 presidential election to secure re-election, insisting that the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) is already in a strong position ahead of the poll.

Soludo made the remarks on Thursday during a presidential campaign rally at Alex Ekwueme Square in Awka, Anambra State.

According to the governor, the election is effectively decided in favour of the Tinubu-Shettima ticket, arguing that the opposition parties lack the nationwide political reach required to challenge the ruling party.

“This election, to the best of our knowledge, is already won and lost. The president doesn’t need to rig any election. President Tinubu doesn’t need to rig any election,” he said.

Explaining his position, Soludo argued that while some opposition candidates enjoyed considerable support in certain parts of the country, they lacked a comparable presence across other regions.

He said the APC ticket had a broader national reach, adding that an assessment of the political landscape showed Tinubu was well-positioned for another term.

The Anambra governor also attributed his confidence in the President’s re-election bid to the performance of the current administration.

“President Tinubu, Shettima, they’re doing very well. They will win because they have done well,” Soludo said.

He further argued that the Tinubu administration had presented a stronger policy agenda than its opponents, claiming that no presidential candidate had offered a credible alternative ahead of the election.

Soludo also defended the Federal Government’s handling of the economy and security, saying people familiar with the economy had acknowledged that the administration was moving in the right direction.

He cited the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), which provides financial support to students, as one of the initiatives introduced by the government.

The governor’s remarks came during a joint campaign rally organised by the APC and the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) in support of Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid.

At the event, Soludo also presented the APGA flag to Vice-President Kashim Shettima as the party formally adopted Tinubu for the presidential election.

The post Tinubu doesn’t need to rig 2027 election; He has already won — Soludo appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Pochettino calls for Man Utd to look beyond current struggles
description:
Mauricio Pochettino says it is a “mistake” to dwell on Manchester United’s current plight, insisting the focus should be on the club’s potential as he prepares for his first match in charge.



The Argentine takes his new team to bitter rivals Liverpool on Sunday — just days after ending his reign a
content:
Mauricio Pochettino says it is a “mistake” to dwell on Manchester United’s current plight, insisting the focus should be on the club’s potential as he prepares for his first match in charge.

The Argentine takes his new team to bitter rivals Liverpool on Sunday — just days after ending his reign as US coach.

United, who sacked Michael Carrick last week, are in the relegation zone after just one win in the Premier League this season.

Pochettino, speaking to in-house media in his first interview as United boss, said he wanted to free up his under-performing players.

“It’s a mistake to see the (current) situation,” he said. “We need to see the potential of this club. Of course, the circumstances are the circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances.

“But at the same time, we need to understand that it’s a game and, to connect with the game, we need to feel free.

“The players need to express their talent, we need to create the environment and the platform for them to perform. That is the most important thing and that is the priority.”

Pochettino will hold his first press conference as United manager on Friday.

The post Pochettino calls for Man Utd to look beyond current struggles appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Mimiko urges use of AI, digital technology for governance
description:
A former Governor of Ondo State, Dr Olusegun Mimiko, has called for the deployment of digital technology and artificial intelligence to strengthen participatory governance, improve service delivery and promote inclusive development in the country.
However, he warned against adopting digital systems
content:
A former Governor of Ondo State, Dr Olusegun Mimiko, has called for the deployment of digital technology and artificial intelligence to strengthen participatory governance, improve service delivery and promote inclusive development in the country.

However, he warned against adopting digital systems that could exclude vulnerable citizens from the development process.

Mimiko made the call on Thursday while delivering his remarks as chairman of the third Development Communication International Hybrid Conference and Workshop at Elizade University, Ilara-Mokin, Ondo State.

The conference was jointly organised by the Development Communication Research Association of Nigeria and the university’s Department of Mass Communication. It was themed, ‘Communicating Development and Citizen Participation in a Fast-Changing Digital and AI World.’

Recalling his administration’s governance model between 2009 and 2017, Mimiko highlighted the 3Is Initiative, which focused on infrastructure, institutions and industry, as an example of community-driven development.

He said, “Over 640 community-nominated projects were delivered in approximately eight years through a bottom-up process in which communities identified their needs while government provided the resources and institutional support.

“The ABIYE Safe Motherhood Programme and Kaadi Igbe Ayo (the Residency Smart Card) are other innovations that demonstrated the importance of citizen participation, accessible healthcare and reliable data in governance.”

Drawing parallels between the initiatives and national interventions such as the General Multipurpose Card and the National Social Register, Mimiko commended the Federal Government’s efforts to use digital identity systems and technology to improve service delivery.

He stressed the need for transparency, community-based verification and effective grievance mechanisms, noting that digital systems must not undermine human relationships or exclude people without access to electricity, internet connectivity and digital literacy.

The former governor urged governments to build resilience into digital transformation programmes by maintaining alternative channels for service delivery in the event of technological failures.

He also called for safeguards against data abuse, algorithmic bias and exclusion in the deployment of artificial intelligence, insisting that innovation should ultimately promote more responsive, participatory and accountable governance.

“Citizens must move beyond being passive recipients of government information to becoming active participants in shaping policies, monitoring implementation and demanding accountability,” he said.

The post Mimiko urges use of AI, digital technology for governance appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: No opposition coalition can stop APC in Kebbi – Gov Idris
description:
‎‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru‎‎‎Governor Nasir Idris was the National President of the Nigeria Union of Teachers and Deputy President of the Nigeria Labour Congress before his election in 2023. In this interview, he says his emergence was divine as becoming a Governor was not his initial plan.







He
content:
‎
‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
‎
‎
‎Governor Nasir Idris was the National President of the Nigeria Union of Teachers and Deputy President of the Nigeria Labour Congress before his election in 2023. In this interview, he says his emergence was divine as becoming a Governor was not his initial plan.

He says that his labour background is the reason his administration places paramount to workers welfare and he has approved implementation of ₦70, 000 transportation allowance to state workers and promises to be the first state to pay minimum wage when new one is agreed. Governor Idris says the APC will not allow the PDP to win presidential election in the state again.

He says the state has enjoyed tremendous support from President Tinubu. He vows that no coalition will unseat the APC in Kebbi

‎Excerpts:
‎
‎Coming from a labour background, having served as Deputy President of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and President of the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT), how has the transition from being a labour leader to becoming a politician and governor been? To what extent have the ideologies and experiences you acquired in the labour movement influenced your decisions and policies as governor?

‎As a labour person, even though I am now on the other side of the divide, there is no way I can forget the labour movement. It was the labour movement, particularly the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT), that made me what I am today. Therefore, I have no reason whatsoever not to appreciate these organisations and their leaders.
‎My ambition in life, throughout my journey in the labour movement, was to become the number one worker in Nigeria and the number one teacher in Nigeria. By the grace of God, I achieved both ambitions. God gave me the opportunity to subject myself to an election, and I emerged as President of the Nigeria Union of Teachers. I was also elected Deputy President of the Nigeria Labour Congress.


‎I also had the ambition of becoming the number one worker in Nigeria, and I was working towards that. A majority of the affiliate unions had endorsed me and agreed that, when the time came, they wanted me to lead the organisation. We were already working towards that ambition.


‎However, God had a different plan for me. What I was looking for was not what He had destined for me. He had a higher responsibility in mind.


‎I was sitting in my house when the opportunity to contest the governorship of Kebbi State came. At the time, the sitting governor had already indicated his preference for the then Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice to succeed him.


‎The governor invited us and told us that all of us were his brothers and that he had nothing against whoever emerged as his successor. However, he preferred the Commissioner for Justice to take over from him. He asked for my opinion.


‎I told His Excellency that I had accepted his position. I said I was not going to discuss it with anybody because, morally, he was the sitting governor and had the responsibility to decide whom he wanted to succeed him. I assured him that whoever he chose, I would support that person.


‎That was how events unfolded. I was even the person who led the delegation that went to submit the nomination form at the national secretariat of the All Progressives Congress (APC). The form was filled out in my house in Birnin Kebbi, and I personally led the delegation to submit it.


‎But God had already destined that position for me.


‎One day, I was sitting in my house when somebody called me and asked, “Are you Comrade Nasir Idris?”


‎I answered in the affirmative. He then asked whether I was not contesting the governorship election in Kebbi State. I told him I was not the one contesting, explaining that we were supporting the Commissioner for Justice.


‎He responded that the Commissioner had not told me that he was no longer interested in contesting. He advised me to go and purchase the nomination form because, based on his consultations, he believed the people loved me and wanted me to lead them.
‎The man ended the call without introducing himself. After about two or three minutes, I decided to call the number back and identify the caller. I tried searching for the number, including through Truecaller, but I could not find it.


‎That is how God works. I subsequently contacted the sitting governor and informed him that I had made up my mind to purchase the form and contest the governorship election.


‎That is why I always describe my emergence as governor as divine.


‎The journey was, however, very challenging. Many influential members of the APC had decided to leave the party and join the opposition PDP. They joined forces with a retired military general who had left the military only about five or six months earlier to venture into politics.


‎They mounted a campaign against me, questioning how a comrade and a teacher could govern a state. Some people believed that I could not preside over the affairs of a state because of my background as a labour leader and teacher.


‎That was where I became a little uncomfortable. I wondered why anybody would think that a teacher or a labour leader could not govern a state successfully.


‎But the workers and the masses stood by me. Teachers, market women, artisans, labourers, drivers, and ordinary people believed in me. I subjected myself to the electoral process, and the people expressed their preference.


‎The election was conducted in the 21 local government areas of Kebbi State, and I won in 18 of them. I was leading my opponent by 45,278 votes when the election was declared inconclusive.


‎Two weeks later, the supplementary election was conducted. Out of about 30,000 votes cast, I secured approximately 19,000 votes, and I was subsequently declared the winner.


‎Within 24 hours, my opponent took the matter to the tribunal, with the intention of taking away the mandate freely given to me by the people, including workers and teachers. By God’s grace, we won at the tribunal. The matter subsequently went to the Court of Appeal, where we also prevailed. Eventually, it was taken to the Supreme Court, and we won.


‎That was how God vindicated the people of Kebbi State and gave us the opportunity to lead them.


‎So, my background as a teacher and labour leader prepared me for the responsibility of governance. I had managed responsibilities at the local government, state, and national levels, as well as participated in regional and international labour engagements.


‎I had presided over the affairs of the Nigeria Union of Teachers, an organisation with a large membership of educated

professionals. I also had the opportunity to act as Deputy President of the NLC before I resigned to pursue my political ambition.
‎Honestly, when I became governor, I did not find it difficult to adapt to the responsibilities of governance because of the experience I had acquired over the years. God has helped me, and that is why, when I assumed office, I assured the people of Kebbi State that they had no cause to worry.


‎I was born in Birnin Kebbi, grew up there, worked there, and led teachers and workers in the state. Therefore, I understood their challenges and aspirations.


‎I made several promises during the electioneering campaign, and by God’s grace, I have fulfilled almost 90 per cent of them. I cannot claim to have fulfilled 100 per cent because no leader is perfect.


‎Before the election, I established a five-man committee to document every promise I made during our campaigns. Wherever I went, whenever I made a promise, the committee recorded it.


‎When we eventually formed the government, the committee submitted its report, reminding us of the promises made to the people in different local government areas.


‎For instance, I promised workers that I would provide a conducive working environment by bringing all government workers under one roof.


‎At the time, the existing secretariat could no longer accommodate all the workers. I assured them that I would construct a befitting secretariat that would bring them together, promote synergy and cooperation, and create a more conducive working environment.
‎Today, we have achieved that. Our new secretariat has a capacity of about 25,000, and workers are now accommodated in the same complex.


‎I also promised workers that I would address their welfare concerns, particularly the issue of the minimum wage.


‎At the time, workers in Kebbi State were receiving a minimum wage of ₦30,000. I told them they had nothing to lose by supporting me because I was one of them and understood their problems.


‎I assured them that they would not regret supporting my administration, and they stood by me.


‎Today, we have implemented a minimum wage of ₦75,000. We have also addressed the welfare concerns of teachers, including those who were previously not enjoying the minimum wage.


‎I told them that the era of treating teachers as second-class workers in Kebbi State was over. I am one of them, and I understand their challenges.


‎When we constituted committees to negotiate the minimum wage, organised labour presented its position, while the government also presented its own proposal through its committee. Eventually, both sides met and harmonised their positions.


‎The difference between the two proposals was just about ₦108 million. I told my government’s negotiating committee that, as a former labour leader, I had a responsibility to demonstrate leadership by example and ensure that workers received what was due to them.


‎I therefore directed that we should adopt labour’s proposal.


‎That was what we did to ensure industrial peace and harmony. Today, you hardly hear complaints from workers that they have been shortchanged. They are happy because they believe one of their own is in government and understands their concerns.
‎
‎
‎Kebbi is among the few states that have implemented a ₦75,000 minimum wage. However, considering the current economic realities and the declining purchasing power of workers’ salaries, there are still concerns about the hardship they face. Does your administration have any plans to provide additional interventions to cushion their economic difficulties before the next minimum wage negotiations are concluded?
‎
‎
‎I have just returned from a journey, and by God’s grace, I am aware of the intervention the Federal Government has approved for workers.
‎As a former labour leader, I believe something should also be done for workers in Kebbi State. I am returning to the state tomorrow, but because of this interview, I decided to ask you to come today before I depart.
‎I can assure you that workers in Kebbi State will not be left out.
‎
‎
‎Can you give us further clarification on the intervention?
‎
‎I have already constituted a committee, in writing, under the leadership of the Head of Service. The committee is working, and by God’s grace, when I return, I will communicate with the Head of Service.
‎
‎
‎The Federal Government has approved a ₦70,000 transport allowance for workers. Is Kebbi State prepared to implement the same amount, or possibly pay more?
‎
‎I have already made my position clear. Whenever the Federal Government increases workers’ salaries or approves an intervention for workers, Kebbi State will be among the first states to implement it.
‎We cannot shy away from the truth. I understand that the purchasing power of the minimum wage has been significantly eroded by the prevailing economic situation.
‎The President has done well by approving an additional ₦70,000 transport allowance to cushion the effects of the hardship being experienced by Nigerian workers.
‎Governors must also demonstrate responsibility by ensuring that appropriate measures are taken to reduce the hardship facing their workers.
‎So, yes, I can assure you that workers in Kebbi State will benefit from an additional intervention. That is why I have already constituted a committee. I do not want to pre-empt its recommendations, but definitely, workers in the state will see an improvement in their welfare, by God’s grace.
‎
‎
‎Beyond the implementation of the ₦75,000 minimum wage, what other concrete achievements has your administration recorded in improving the welfare and working conditions of workers in Kebbi State?
‎
‎I think I have mentioned some of them, particularly the implementation of the minimum wage and the construction of the new secretariat.


‎Let me also emphasise that my administration does not owe workers’ salaries. We do not owe pensions, gratuities, or other retirement benefits.


‎We have also implemented promotions and annual salary increments for workers.


‎We believe in prudent management and financial discipline. That is how we have been able to meet our obligations to workers despite the competing demands on government resources.


‎We have also taken steps to address unemployment, particularly among young graduates.


‎I know what it means for a young graduate to remain unemployed after completing his or her education. Having been a labour leader, I understand the implications of unemployment and the importance of creating opportunities for people.
‎That is why my administration has recruited 2,000 teachers and another 2,000 health workers, including doctors, nurses, pharmacists, and other health professionals.


‎We have also employed workers in other categories, including security personnel.


‎Beyond that, we have addressed the issue of casualisation in the state civil service. As a labour leader who fought against the casualisation of workers, I cannot become a governor and allow the same practice to thrive under my administration.
‎We have therefore absorbed many casual workers into the civil service.
‎
‎
‎Kebbi State was previously ranked among the states with relatively low internally generated revenue (IGR). However, there have been reports of improvements in the state’s revenue performance and ranking. How has your administration been able to achieve this?
‎
‎I do not entirely agree with some of those rankings. Sometimes, people sit down in Abuja and calculate figures without going to the actual places to establish what is happening.


‎However, I know that we have made efforts to improve our internally generated revenue.


‎When you talk about revenue generation, you must also talk about revenue leakages. We have worked hard to block those leakages and ensure that government revenue is properly accounted for.


‎That is why our internally generated revenue has increased.
‎
‎
‎Can you give us specific figures showing the state’s IGR before you assumed office and what it is currently generating?
‎
‎I would not want to give you figures that may not be entirely accurate. I do not want to quote figures that could turn out to be incorrect.
‎But I can assure you that there has been a significant improvement in what we generate now compared with what we were collecting before this administration came into office.
‎
‎
‎With the 2027 general election approaching, workers in Kebbi State would want to know what additional benefits they should expect if you are re-elected for a second term. What new welfare packages do you have in mind for them?
‎
‎By God’s grace, by 2027, we will also have a new minimum wage because the government has already put a committee in place to look into the issue.


‎Even if I do not introduce any entirely new package, I believe that sustaining the existing welfare arrangements is already a significant achievement.


‎For instance, workers want to be assured that when they retire, their gratuities and pensions will be paid.


‎Previously, some workers were paid only a percentage of their gratuities, such as 10, 15, or 20 per cent. But today, my administration pays 100 per cent of workers’ gratuities.


‎When a worker retires, we calculate the full entitlement and pay it.


‎We have also improved the pension payment arrangement. If a worker retires and his or her retirement falls within the applicable payment schedule, the person’s name is included for pension payment that month.


‎In the event of a worker’s death, the government also ensures that the family receives the appropriate benefits.
‎I believe that sustaining these arrangements is important. Workers must have confidence that the government will fulfil its obligations to them, even after retirement.


‎Beyond that, we are introducing additional welfare packages.


‎For instance, we have acquired about 155 housing units through the Federal Mortgage Bank, while another 250 housing units are currently under construction specifically for workers.


‎We also have about 75 existing housing units that we are renovating. All these houses are intended for workers.
‎The housing programme is particularly important because I understand the challenges workers face in securing decent and affordable accommodation.


‎Some of these houses are expected to be commissioned in December, and by 2027, we intend to introduce additional packages that will further improve workers’ welfare.


‎As a former labour leader, I understand what workers need, and we will continue to do everything possible to ensure that they enjoy the benefits of good governance.
‎
‎
‎With the 2027 general election approaching, how confident are you that the APC will retain Kebbi State, particularly given the political activities of opposition figures, including former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, who is also working towards the next election?
‎
‎By God’s grace, we are confident.


‎An election is something you can assess based on your performance and what you have done for the people. It is not simply about belonging to the APC or any other political party.


‎There is no administration that has introduced as many different packages and interventions for Nigerians as the present Federal Government under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.


‎Let me speak specifically about Kebbi State. I believe we have never had it so good in terms of development as we have under the present administration.


‎My philosophy of democracy is that governance must bring development projects to the doorsteps of the people.


‎Kebbi State has benefited tremendously from the infrastructure development taking place under President Tinubu’s administration.
‎For instance, there is an ongoing road construction project linking Yauri to Ngaski Local Government Area. The road is known as the Malando Road.


‎These are the kinds of development projects that people can see and appreciate.


‎By God’s grace, we believe that our performance, the support of the people, and the developmental projects we have delivered will speak for us when the time comes.
‎
‎
‎You have spoken about several federal infrastructure projects in Kebbi State. What has your administration done to attract federal government interventions, particularly in road construction, and how are these projects improving connectivity across the state?
‎
‎With the coming of this administration, when we went on our campaign tours, the people made several appeals to us concerning abandoned road projects. One of the major concerns they raised was the poor state of the roads and the hardship they were experiencing.


‎We subsequently met with Mr. President and drew his attention to these challenges. In particular, we discussed the abandoned road project and the reasons behind its delay. When we engaged the contractors, they explained that inadequate funding was responsible for the abandonment.


‎I personally took up the matter with Mr. President, and funding was subsequently made available to the company. Today, the contractor has returned to the site, and work has resumed.


‎There is another federal government road project linking Augie to Kangiwa and Kamba in Kamba Local Government Area. That road was originally awarded for construction during the administration of the late Alhaji Shehu Shagari in 1979, when he was governor of the old Sokoto State. Since then, successive administrations have done very little to address the condition of the road.
‎However, President Tinubu’s administration has awarded the contract, and the contractors are now working day and night to ensure its completion.


‎There is also the Koko–Zuru–Kala-Kala road project, which the Federal Government has awarded.


‎Another major road project is the Koko–Dawesulu–Zuru road, which is one of the worst roads in Kebbi State. My administration is currently handling its construction on behalf of the Federal Government.


‎I appealed to Mr. President to intervene because the contractor had been on site since February 2018 but had not constructed up to four kilometres of the road.


‎I requested that the contract be revoked and awarded to a reputable construction company capable of delivering the project, or that the responsibility be transferred to another competent contractor.


‎Following my appeal, the Federal Government permitted the Kebbi State Government to undertake the construction in line with federal government specifications. That is what we are doing.


‎The project is about 87 kilometres long, and we have divided the work among three construction companies: Abib Nigeria Limited, ZBCC, and JNIC. They are working day and night to ensure that the road is completed.


‎Previously, travelling from Koko to Zuru, particularly through the difficult sections of the road, could take about six and a half hours. The road was in a terrible condition.


‎Today, because of the work we are doing, the journey has been reduced to about two hours. By the time the project is completed, travelling from Koko to Zuru will take approximately one hour.


‎These are some of the infrastructure projects we have been able to attract and execute through our collaboration with the Federal Government.
‎
‎
‎Some Nigerians believe that the economic policies introduced by the present administration have brought more hardship than relief to the people. What is your response to such concerns?
‎
‎I believe that the only permanent thing in life is change.


‎If we are going through difficulties today and, as a result of the decisions we are taking, our children do not have to experience the same hardship tomorrow, then we have succeeded.


‎But if we continue to allow things to remain the way they are, all of us, including our children, will continue to suffer.
‎We must be prepared to make certain sacrifices today so that future generations can enjoy a better country.


‎I believe in these policies because, sometimes, previous governments may have lacked the courage to introduce certain reforms. Whenever a new policy is introduced, people are bound to feel its immediate impact, particularly when it involves changing an existing system.


‎However, every policy has its long-term objectives and benefits. At the end of the day, Nigerians will appreciate the results.
‎That is why President Tinubu has consistently appealed to Nigerians to remain patient and bear with the present challenges. I believe that, at the end of the tunnel, Nigerians will have reasons to smile.
‎
‎
‎How would you assess the performance of your administration in the health sector, particularly regarding the state health insurance scheme? How many people are currently benefiting from the programme?
‎
‎When I assumed office, I discovered that there were challenges with the health insurance scheme. However, we have made significant progress.


‎As I speak to you, about 300,000 people are benefiting from the Kebbi State health insurance scheme, known as KACHIMA. We are also planning to enrol an additional 50,000 people by early next year. By God’s grace, we will introduce that additional coverage.


‎In terms of healthcare infrastructure, I inherited several general hospitals that had not undergone meaningful renovation for many years, with some dating back to 1978.


‎When I came into office, I decided that we must address the situation. I therefore embarked on the comprehensive renovation of these hospitals.


‎I also established three additional general hospitals to address the needs of communities that had been demanding improved access to secondary healthcare services.


‎Out of the 33 general hospitals in the state, we are currently working on 27. Some have been completed and equipped, while equipment for others is ready and awaiting the completion of ongoing construction and renovation work.
‎We intend to address the remaining hospitals after completing the current phase.


‎We have also made significant interventions in primary healthcare. Kebbi State has 225 primary healthcare centres, and we are working on 175 of them. We are also equipping these facilities because we understand the challenges facing the health sector, particularly at the grassroots.


‎Unfortunately, some people have attempted to misrepresent the situation in our hospitals for political reasons.


‎At one point, an opposition candidate visited a hospital and presented images of an elderly man lying on a bed without a mattress or blanket, among other things, in an attempt to portray my administration negatively.


‎However, the hospital being presented was not in Kebbi State. It was in Kafur, Katsina State.


‎If you want to contest an election against me, that is your right. But you should subject yourself to the people and tell them what you have done for them. You should not resort to presenting misleading information about another state to discredit an administration.


‎I remember when I was invited to participate in a political debate. I was asked to come and explain what I intended to do for the people.


‎I told them that the issue should not simply be about what we intended to do in the future. We should also examine what we had already done.


‎Everybody who participated had attained significant positions in their respective fields. Some were generals in the Nigerian Army, while others had occupied important public offices.


‎I asked them: What have you done with the positions you have held? How many people have you employed? What projects have you attracted to your communities? What have you done to improve the lives of the people?


‎For instance, some of them had attained the rank of general in the Nigerian Army. How many people from their communities had they helped to secure recruitment into the military?


‎I am not interested in making promises alone. I can point to what I have done.


‎I can tell you the number of teachers and other workers I have helped secure employment. I can also take you to communities where we have executed projects.


‎Even in my own primary school in Birnin Kebbi, I have renovated and constructed several classrooms, provided electricity and water, cleaned up the environment, and supplied furniture.


‎I challenge those who are criticising my administration to identify a school they attended and show us whether they have provided even a single table and chair for that school.


‎I am putting that challenge on record.


‎I do not need to spend all my time telling people what I have done. The people of Kebbi State know my contributions before I became governor, and they can also assess my performance in office.
‎
‎
‎You spoke about the former Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, who was initially being considered as your party’s preferred successor to the former governor. We know that he has now left the APC. There have been allegations and counter-allegations from both camps, with some suggesting that he was forced out of the party, while others say he is unhappy with President Bola Tinubu. Is he actually angry with the President, and was he pushed out of the APC?
‎
‎
‎I do not want to go into that matter.


‎But if he has left the APC, is he not someone who benefited immensely from the APC?


‎Since Nigeria gained independence, has there been any Minister of Justice who has enjoyed the kind of opportunities and privileges he enjoyed while serving in that position?


‎I believe that is enough for people to reflect on.
‎
‎
‎Your earlier raised concerns about people sitting in Abuja and presenting inaccurate figures about Kebbi State without properly investigating the situation on the ground. As we approach the 2027 general election, there are also concerns about misinformation and fake news. Is this something that worries you, and what would you advise Nigerians, particularly the people of Kebbi State, about verifying information before accepting it?
‎
‎Fake news is a general problem in this country. Nobody can shy away from that reality.
‎However, I do not believe our people will simply accept fake news because they know what an administration has brought to the table.


‎You can be a minister, even the most powerful minister in the country, but if you have not attracted any meaningful project or development to the people of Kebbi State, what exactly are you asking them to judge you on?


‎Even if you are a minister, you should be able to use your position to attract development to your state.


‎For instance, the Federal High Court did not have its own permanent building in Kebbi State. It was operating from a temporary facility provided by the state government.


‎It was through my appeal to President Tinubu that the construction of a permanent Federal High Court building in Kebbi State commenced under this administration.


‎That is a practical example of what political leadership should be about.
‎People should therefore look beyond political propaganda and examine what those seeking their votes have actually done for them.
‎
‎
‎As the 2027 general election approaches, what is your message to the people of Kebbi State and Nigerians generally regarding your political ambition and support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s re-election?
‎
‎Our people know what we have done, particularly in the agricultural sector.
‎Kebbi State is the largest producer of rice in the country, and we have maintained that position.
‎In my first year in office, we procured 10,000 solar-powered water pumps and 25,000 CNG-powered water pumps for farmers. We also purchased tractors

title: Tinubu Moves To Cut Transport Fares As Yutong Sets Up Bus Assembly Plant In Nigeria
description: President Bola Tinubu has welcomed plans by Yutong, the world’s largest bus manufacturer and a global leader in electric and CNG-powered buses, to establish a CNG bus assembly plant in Nigeria, following his invitation to the Chinese automotive giant to support the expansion of affordable mass
content:
President Bola Tinubu has welcomed plans by Yutong, the world’s largest bus manufacturer and a global leader in electric and CNG-powered buses, to establish a CNG bus assembly plant in Nigeria, following his invitation to the Chinese automotive giant to support the expansion of affordable mass transportation across the country.

The development, revealed by Special Adviser to the President (Information and Strategy), Bayo Onanuga, in a statement on Thursday, noted that the investment will support the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme (NACTP) in collaboration with State Governments, which targets transport fare reductions of approximately 40 per cent on participating routes, in line with the President’s Renewed Hope Agenda 2.0 for 2027–2031.

Under the agreement with the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles (Pi-CNG & EV), Yutong will supply an initial 300 CNG-powered buses, with the first 100 expected to arrive in Lagos by the end of December 2026.

Subsequent buses will be assembled in Nigeria through YP Automobiles Bus Assembly at the former Leyland Automotive plant in Ibadan, Oyo State, reviving local industrial capacity, reducing dependence on imported vehicles and creating employment opportunities for Nigerian engineers, technicians and other workers.

Yutong, which sold 49,518 buses globally in 2025, brings extensive experience in mass transit manufacturing, with operations across international markets and a track record of supporting local assembly and public transportation projects in several countries.

The President noted that the investment comes as CNG adoption continues to increase nationwide, supported by the expansion of refuelling infrastructure through Pi-CNG & EV, the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF) and private sector investors.

These interventions include deploying Mobile Refuelling Units (MRUs) and the President’s directive for 2,000 additional CNG refuelling infrastructure units nationwide, laying the foundation for a wider rollout of affordable commercial buses.

President Tinubu emphasises that reducing the daily cost of transportation for Nigerians remains the central objective of these investments.

The President notes that millions of Nigerians depend on commercial transportation to get to work, take their children to school, travel to markets and move goods between communities. For many households, transportation consumes a significant portion of their daily earnings.

He stresses that the lower operating costs of CNG-powered vehicles must translate into lower fares for passengers, allowing workers, traders and families to retain more of their income for food, education and other essential needs.

The President points to the approximately 40 per cent fare-reduction target under the NACTP, as outlined in his Renewed Hope Agenda 2.0, and reiterates his administration’s determination to work with state governments and transport operators to extend affordable CNG transportation to more routes nationwide.

He welcomes Yutong’s decision to establish local assembly capacity in Nigeria, noting that the investment will help sustain the supply of affordable commercial buses while facilitating technology transfer, creating skilled employment and strengthening the country’s automotive industry.

President Tinubu reiterated that the success of the CNG programme must ultimately be measured by how much Nigerians save on transportation, and assured citizens of his administration’s continued commitment to reducing living costs through practical investments in infrastructure, manufacturing and affordable mass transit.

The agreement is scheduled to be signed in Lagos on Thursday, November 19, 2026.

The post Tinubu Moves To Cut Transport Fares As Yutong Sets Up Bus Assembly Plant In Nigeria appeared first on Channels Television.

This was contained in a statement signed by the state Commissioner for Information and Public Enlightenment, Kolapo Alimi, obta
content:
Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has approved the appointment of Prince Adewumi Olusola Adeniyi of the Godo-dudu royal house of Esa-Oke as the new Owamiran of Esa-Oke.

This was contained in a statement signed by the state Commissioner for Information and Public Enlightenment, Kolapo Alimi, obtained in Osogbo, Osun State, on Thursday.

Alimi said the approval followed the outcome of the state executive council meeting presided over by the governor.

The statement noted that the stool of Owa-Omiran of Esa-Oke became vacant after the death of Oba Akanbi Adediran from the Aragadagbagun ruling house of Esa-Oke.

Following this development, “with Godo-dudu as the next ruling house, Prince Adewumi Adeniyi’s candidature was subsequently ratified by the state executive council to fill the vacuum created by the death of the immediate Owamiran.”

The government congratulated and wished the new Oba-elect a peaceful reign as he directs the affairs of the ancient town of Esa-Oke in his new capacity as the approved Oba by the Osun State Executive Council.

The PUNCH earlier reported that Adeleke had directed the Ministry of Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs to probe the circumstances surrounding the reported appointment of a new king for Koka Ilase, leading to alleged two kings in one town.

“The ministry was instructed to review the situation and enforce due process of the law in respect of the chieftaincy law and tradition,” a statement signed by the spokesperson to the governor, Olawale Rasheed, stated.

title: Tinubu targets 40% transport fare cut, unveils 300 CNG buses
description:

content:
President Bola Tinubu has announced plans to reduce transport fares by approximately 40 per cent on participating routes between 2027 and 2031, as part of efforts to ease the cost of transportation for Nigerians.

Tinubu disclosed this in a statement on Thursday, saying preparations were underway to deliver on the commitment under his Reforms to Prosperity Agenda for 2027–2031.

“I know the burden of transport fares and how much less you have left for your family when you return home. It is a burden I am determined to ease,” the President said.

He also announced that Yutong, described as the world’s largest bus manufacturer, would establish a compressed natural gas bus assembly plant at the former Leyland automotive plant in Ibadan, Oyo State.

According to him, the company would supply an initial 300 buses for the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme under an agreement with the Presidential Initiative on CNG and Electric Vehicles.

“The first 100 are expected as early as next month. Subsequent buses will be assembled in Ibadan through YP Automobiles, creating jobs for our engineers, technicians and other workers,” he said.

Tinubu said the initiative was already producing results in at least 10 states and the Federal Capital Territory, citing reduced fares on some routes and free bus services in others.

He said a journey from Enugu to Nsukka, which previously cost as much as N4,000, now costs N1,600 on participating CNG buses.

“There are N50 bus rides in Borno and free CNG bus services in Kaduna. More Nigerians deserve to experience this,” he added.

The President also said state governments had increased their procurement of CNG buses, while private investors were expanding the country’s refuelling network.

He added that his earlier directive for 1,000 additional CNG refuelling infrastructure units nationwide would support the expansion.

Tinubu said Nigeria should maximise its natural gas resources to reduce transportation costs for workers, traders and families.

“Nigeria is blessed with abundant natural gas. We must put it to work for the woman going to the market, the young man going to work and the parent struggling with the cost of sending children to school,” he said.

He also defended the removal of the petrol subsidy, saying, “We cannot afford to return to the days when fraudulent subsidy claims enriched middlemen while ordinary Nigerians struggled.”

The President said he recognised the sacrifices Nigerians had made since the introduction of his economic reforms, adding that the government was focused on improving their living conditions.

“I want you to spend less getting to work, earn a decent living and return home with enough to give your family a better life. That is why we are doing this,” he said.

The latest announcement builds on the Federal Government’s ongoing deployment of CNG-powered buses under the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme.

In September, Tinubu said CNG buses deployed to Pacesetter Transport in Oyo had reduced the Lagos-Ibadan fare from about N8,000 to N3,200, while 100 buses in Enugu had cut the Enugu-Nsukka fare from N2,500 to N1,500. He also cited the deployment of 100 buses in Kaduna, which provided free transportation to about 3.2 million passengers in their first year.

The post Tinubu targets 40% transport fare cut, unveils 300 CNG buses appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: NDC campaign DG Abdulkarim accuses northern elites of entitlement

content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Director-General of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Presidential Campaign Council, Ibrahim Abdulkarim, has criticised what he described as a ‘sense of entitlement’ among some northern political elites, saying no candidate has the right to demand that others surrender their ambitions to Atiku Abubakar ahead of the 2027 elections.

Abdulkarim said this on Arise Television’s Prime Time on Wednesday while responding to allegations by African Democratic Congress (ADC) chieftain Hajiya Najaatu Mohammed that Rabiu Kwankwaso was a mole in the NDC working for President Bola Tinubu.

Dismissing the allegation as “their own imagination,” Abdulkarim criticised the way some politicians had approached the coalition-building process, calling some ADC politicians “lazy” because, in his view, they had not clearly agreed on the coalition’s purpose, presidential candidate or zoning arrangement before bringing people together.

“I think that’s their own imagination. You see, I used to term some of the people I see in ADC as lazy politicians. Right from time, even when they are constructing this coalition that they talk about, instead of them to find a way of doing what maybe APC have done before, put everything in black and white that we want to come for a coalition, and this coalition, this is the person that we want to be the president, or we are zoning this part of what we are going to do to this part of the country, at that time everybody that is coming into that coalition knows exactly why he is coming,” he said.

Abdulkarim said that setting out the terms in advance would make it clear why each politician was joining the coalition and prevent disputes over who should take which position as he questioned proposed plans to make Peter Obi Atiku’s running mate.

“Immediately we started this, and they started to say that Peter Obi is a vice presidential candidate to Atiku. So what kind of coalition is that?” he asked.

He also objected to what he described as an assumption that northern politicians should rally behind Atiku, saying Kwankwaso and other politicians had the right to choose whom to support and contest against.

“And the entitlement from the elite, I find it very, very annoying sometimes. You just decide the North, which North? You talk like you earned something that you just put in your pocket, that anytime you want it, you just play the card of the North, and then everybody just follows that. These people have the right to contest election. There is no right given to Atiku, for example, to say everybody must surrender his for him,” he said.

The NDC chieftain said Kwankwaso, who received about 1.5 million votes in the last presidential election, was entitled to decide where to go and whom to work with. He said Kwankwaso chose to work with Obi and had praised him as a decent politician.

“We have three people that participated in the last election and then, Kwankwaso had 1.5 million votes, and he’s entitled for him to choose where he wants to go to and who he will do a coalition with. And then he decided to pitch and work together with Mr Peter Obi, and he said recently, he has not seen a decent politician, somebody with high respect. He even regretted that, if he knows that this how this gentleman, Mr Peter Obi is, he will have followed him to be his vice presidential candidate in 2023,” he said.

He further criticised northern political elites who, he said, continued to appeal to regional loyalty despite the North’s record of political leadership and the hardship facing its communities.

“See, this kind of thinking that some of these elites have, more especially in the northern part of the country, like somebody is doing ‘Arewa for Peter Obi’, and then people feel that they are responsible. Us, the young people, we look at them as not just traitors or people because the North has been in this system. We’ve been ruling from IBB to Buhari, but look at where we are. Go and see our streets. Go and see our villages. Look at how we have been ravaged,” Abdulkarim said.

He urged voters to look beyond region, religion and tribe when assessing candidates, and to focus on integrity, accountability and whether public funds would be used for public benefit.

“But since somebody is still coming today, trying to play this northern card at this level, instead of us start thinking, how can we hire somebody, irrespective of where he’s coming from, irrespective of religion or tribe, somebody that we know he has this integrity, somebody that can make this public funds to be used for public good, somebody that can be accountable, somebody that we can call and sit him down and say, ‘Why are you doing what you are doing?’ But not people that are old and full of entitlement,” he said.

Abdulkarim added that he wanted leaders who were accessible and could be held accountable by Nigerians, rather than politicians he said were difficult to reach.

His response followed Najaatu’s allegation that Kwankwaso and Obi were “moles” working against Atiku. In an earlier interview on the same programme, Najaatu questioned whether Kwankwaso was genuinely in opposition, citing his comment that Tinubu was a better administrator than Atiku. She said she had expected him to argue that Obi would be a better administrator.

“There is a difference between being in opposition, in opposition, or in a latent way supporting the government that you are supposed to oppose. Let me tell you one thing that Kwankwaso once said recently. Kwankwaso came out to say that Tinubu is a better administrator than Atiku. I thought he should be saying that Peter Obi would be a better administrator,” Najaatu said.

title: VIDEO: South Africans protest Nigerians calling Pretoria community ‘Little Lagos’
description:
South African protesters have confronted Nigerians living in Pretoria’s Sunnyside neighbourhood, questioning their presence in the area and challenging its nickname, “Little Lagos”, during an anti-immigration demonstration led by the March and March movement.
In a video from the protest shared on so
content:
South African protesters have confronted Nigerians living in Pretoria’s Sunnyside neighbourhood, questioning their presence in the area and challenging its nickname, “Little Lagos”, during an anti-immigration demonstration led by the March and March movement.

In a video from the protest shared on social media on Wednesday, the movement’s leader, Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma, addressed Nigerians in the neighbourhood, asking who gave them permission to refer to the area as “Little Lagos”.

“I am being told here that we’ve entered Sunnyside, the home of Nigerians. I am inviting Nigerians to come out, let’s talk to each other. We want to know who gave you this place and called it Nigeria. Who gave you permission to call this place Lagos or whatever you call it?” she asked.

In a Facebook post on Thursday, Ngobese-Zuma further criticised Nigerians, making allegations about the country and its nationals.

“Their President is wanted for drug trafficking, their country is also a hub for drugs and some very delusional people think that Nigerians will contribute more than just drugs, prostitution, human trafficking and Jollofinas to our country?” she wrote.

The comments followed a protest organised by the March and March movement in Pretoria on Wednesday, November 18, against undocumented migration and South Africa’s immigration policies.

The demonstration began in Sunnyside, moved through Arcadia and proceeded towards the Department of Home Affairs in Hatfield, with protesters demanding stricter immigration controls and the deportation of undocumented foreign nationals.

The movement also called on the South African government to withdraw from the 1951 United Nations Refugee Convention and stop accepting new refugee applications. Some businesses along the protest route in Hatfield reportedly closed as demonstrators approached the Home Affairs offices.

Ngobese-Zuma had also argued that 95 per cent of asylum applications in the country were fraudulent, saying in an interview with eNCA that “if 95% of those applications are not real asylum seekers, then the problem is not with the Home Affairs departments. The problem is with the people that are applying.”

The latest protest comes amid renewed tensions between Nigeria and South Africa over xenophobic and Afrophobic attacks against Nigerians and other African nationals living in the country.

In September, the Federal Government said it had evacuated 1,821 Nigerians from South Africa following attacks and threats against foreign nationals. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs said it remained concerned about the persistent attacks and was pursuing diplomatic engagements with South African authorities to protect Nigerians in the country.

PUNCH had also reported that Nigeria’s Acting High Commissioner to South Africa, Ambassador Ajayi Alexander, said 98 Nigerians had died in mob and hate-related incidents in the country since 2022.

The tensions have also played out diplomatically in recent days following a disagreement between Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, and the South African Presidency over the omission of his speech from a livestream of the ceremony where he presented his letters of credence to President Cyril Ramaphosa on November 13.

South Africa subsequently summoned Fani-Kayode over his public comments on the incident, with its Department of International Relations and Cooperation expressing concern about his remarks and reminding him to use established diplomatic channels.

The Nigerian High Commission, however, said the meeting was cordial and that the envoy was neither reprimanded nor issued a warning.

The latest demonstration adds to concerns over the safety of Nigerians in South Africa and the strained relations between both countries.

title: Remi Tinubu seeks N70bn to complete National Library
description:
By Joseph Erunke, Abuja



The First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, has said an additional N70 billion is required to complete the National Library headquarters in Abuja, disclosing that her 65th birthday fundraising initiative has so far generated N25.6 billion for the project.
