content:
By Joseph Erunke, Abuja

The First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, has said an additional N70 billion is required to complete the National Library headquarters in Abuja, disclosing that her 65th birthday fundraising initiative has so far generated N25.6 billion for the project.

Tinubu made the disclosure on Thursday as construction work formally resumed on the long-abandoned National Library headquarters, a project conceived decades ago but stalled by funding challenges and repeated interruptions.

The First Lady launched the fundraising campaign in December 2025 to mark her 65th birthday. She said the contributions came from wealthy Nigerians, women’s groups and other individuals who shared her vision of a world-class national library.

While appreciating the donors, she acknowledged the challenge of raising the remaining funds, given the enormous resources required to complete the facility.

She, however, urged Nigerians to contribute to the project, saying even modest donations would make a difference.

“I have told the Minister that every contribution counts, even if it is just N10. Let everyone have an opportunity to say, ‘I contributed to the construction of the National Library’,” she said.

Tinubu said the National Library was not merely a government construction project but a national monument belonging to all Nigerians.

She urged students, individuals, organisations and other citizens to support the project, noting that collective participation would strengthen public ownership of the facility.

Explaining her personal attachment to the project, the First Lady said libraries played an important role in shaping her life and deepening her appreciation of education.

She recalled her years in the Senate, particularly during the 7th, 8th and 9th National Assemblies, when she consistently sought membership of the education committee because of her background as a teacher and passion for the sector.

Tinubu said she and President Bola Tinubu understood the struggles associated with humble beginnings and believed education remained one of the most potent instruments for breaking the cycle of poverty.

She recalled visiting the Qatar National Library in Doha in October 2025, where she saw how a modern library could serve beyond book storage to become a centre for research, technology, innovation, cultural preservation and lifelong learning.

The experience, she said, reinforced her determination to see Nigeria’s National Library transformed into a modern knowledge institution capable of serving generations.

She commended President Tinubu for renewing the government’s commitment to the project and urged contractors and consultants to deliver a world-class facility within the stipulated timeframe.

The Minister of Education, Dr Maruf Tunji Alausa, said the National Library headquarters, conceived and commenced in 2006, had suffered repeated setbacks before being abandoned for 16 years.

He said the project remained stalled until President Tinubu renewed the government’s commitment to its completion, describing the intervention as a demonstration of the administration’s resolve to prioritise education and human capital development.

Alausa said the National Library was a critical national asset for preserving Nigeria’s documentary heritage, providing access to knowledge and supporting research, education and national development.

He commended the First Lady for dedicating proceeds from her 65th birthday fundraising initiative to the project, describing the gesture as a personal celebration converted into an enduring public investment.

The minister assured Nigerians that the Federal Ministry of Education would work with the National Library management, contractors, consultants and relevant government agencies to ensure transparent oversight, quality execution and compliance with approved standards.

“The confidence invested in this project must be repaid through responsible and timely delivery,” he said.

Alausa charged the contractors and consultants to adhere strictly to project milestones, maintain rigorous supervision and promptly address challenges that could undermine delivery.

He said the completed facility would provide students with access to learning resources, support researchers, authors and publishers, and offer reliable information to policymakers and other stakeholders.

The minister also urged young Nigerians to cultivate reading habits, explore new ideas and harness knowledge to solve societal problems.

Providing an account of the project’s history, the National Librarian and Chief Executive Officer of the National Library of Nigeria, Professor Chinwe Veronica Nwakaego Anunobi, said efforts to establish a befitting headquarters began in 1981, when the institution engaged Odele International Associates to design the facility.

She said the construction contract was awarded to Reynolds Construction Company Nigeria Limited in March 2006 under former President Olusegun Obasanjo, with work commencing in April that year.

However, the project suffered major interruptions between 2008 and 2010 and again from August 2014, eventually grinding to a halt after reaching only 48 per cent completion.

Anunobi said the 11-storey complex, covering approximately 82,941 square metres, represented a significant national investment that had remained unrealised for too long.

She disclosed that construction resumed on October 21, 2026, following efforts by the Minister of Education, with work now being undertaken in phases.

The revised design, she said, incorporated modern facilities, including preservation and conservation laboratories, a digitisation laboratory, an innovation and research hub, and a children’s library.

According to her, the facilities would reposition the National Library as a centre for intellectual development, research, education, innovation, social engagement and economic advancement.

Anunobi also said the First Lady’s visit to the Qatar National Library, alongside education ministers, inspired a renewed vision for Nigeria’s National Library and culminated in the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding between Nigerian and Qatari library institutions in August 2026.

She said the agreement provided for knowledge and heritage sharing, exchange of expertise and collaboration in adopting international best practices in library management and development.

Describing the N25.6 billion raised by the First Lady as a major contribution towards Nigeria’s intellectual future, the National Librarian commended the President, Tinubu, Alausa and the Minister of State for Education, Professor Suwaiba Sa’idu Ahmad, for their roles in reviving the project.

She assured Nigerians that the National Library management was committed to delivering a world-class facility, stressing that the project was about more than completing a building.

According to her, it represents an effort to restore a national institution, preserve Nigeria’s intellectual heritage and safeguard knowledge for future generations.

N200,000 support for elderly, PWDs

In a related development, Tinubu announced plans to provide N200,000 each to elderly citizens and persons with disabilities across the country’s senatorial districts in December.

She said the initiative would cover 250 beneficiaries in each senatorial district, with the money intended to support small businesses or meet personal needs.

The First Lady said persons with disabilities would receive the support on December 3, in commemoration of the International Day of Persons with Disabilities, while elderly beneficiaries would be celebrated on December 17.

She described the initiative as part of her longstanding commitment to improving the welfare of vulnerable Nigerians.

Tinubu urged senators to work with her team to ensure effective implementation and encourage eligible beneficiaries to register through their respective senatorial representatives.

She said the programmes were being expanded to reach more Nigerians, acknowledging that the country’s large population required sustained efforts to extend support to different categories of vulnerable people.

The resumption of construction on the National Library headquarters offers an opportunity to complete an institution expected to serve as a major pillar of Nigeria’s educational, research and knowledge infrastructure after decades of delays.

title: Germany, France, Britain meet with Ukraine after Trump-Putin-Xi talks
description:
Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Berlin Thursday for a “Coalition of the Willing” summit where Kyiv’s allies were to signal steadfast support and push for a European role in any future peace talks.



The meeting – co-hosted by the leaders of Germany, France and Britain – was being
content:
Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Berlin Thursday for a “Coalition of the Willing” summit where Kyiv’s allies were to signal steadfast support and push for a European role in any future peace talks.

The meeting – co-hosted by the leaders of Germany, France and Britain – was being held shortly after unprecedented three-way talks in China between US President Donald Trump, Russia’s Vladimir Putin and China’s Xi Jinping.

The goal of the Berlin summit was to boost Europe’s role in any efforts to end the continent’s worst conflict since World War II, in a process so far dominated by Washington, Moscow and Kyiv.

Zelensky wrote on X that “we are doing everything we can to ensure that Europe’s presence in the negotiation process is fully represented”.

A so-called E5 core group – made up of Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Poland as well as EU officials – is expected to represent Europe in any potential peace negotiations.

US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff also arrived at the chancellery for the summit, expected to bring more than 25 European leaders as well as EU and NATO chiefs.

The US envoys were expected to face questions on the China talks, where the three presidents agreed a brief “peace declaration” that touched on “strategic stability” but made no mention of the war in Ukraine.

Putin, speaking later in China, said Russia had invited European officials, through diplomatic channels, to Moscow to discuss whether they should participate in US-led talks on ending the Ukraine war.

“We understand that discussing issues linked to security in Europe is pointless without the Europeans,” Putin told a press conference.

However, he also said Moscow could not accept any kind of military ties between Ukraine and Europe as part of a deal to end the war.

Billions needed for arms

Kushner wrote on X that he and Witkoff hoped “to further strengthen our close coordination with Ukraine and Europe, work toward a unified position on the key elements of a lasting peace, and to jointly prepare the agenda and proposed format for the next round of multilateral negotiations”.

He added that the talks would also explore how the coalition “can contribute to post-war security arrangements, including credible guarantees for Ukraine and a broader framework that strengthens European stability and reduces the risk of future conflict”.

Germany has emerged as the biggest provider of military aid to Ukraine since Trump scaled back US support and is also rapidly rebuilding its own military to deter a hostile Russia.

Merz has insisted that all 27 EU member states help finance Ukraine as it faces a 70-billion-euro ($77-billion) funding shortfall next year.

The European Union on Wednesday proposed members give Ukraine an extra 45-billion-euro loan to help plug the finance gap.

Russia has sought to link an end to the Ukraine war with a complete overhaul of the European security architecture that would push NATO further away from its borders.

Merz, speaking last week, dismissed that idea: “Russia wants to talk about questions of a European security architecture. We do not need to discuss that, it already exists.”

The Germany summit comes as the war enters its fifth gruelling winter, with Russian strikes hammering Ukraine’s energy and transport infrastructure.

Ukraine is in urgent need of interceptors, especially US-made Patriot missiles, at a time when the Middle East war has deepened a global shortage.

Ukraine has meanwhile targeted Russian oil facilities and again attacked the bridge connecting annexed Crimea to Russia on Thursday, the third time in a week the key transport artery had been targeted.

Putin, speaking in China after the trilateral summit, vowed that “we will respond to these attacks. Our response will be far more painful than Kyiv’s attack on the bridge.”

title: Tinubu doesn’t need to rig 2027 election – Soludo
description:
Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo, has said President Bola Tinubu does not need to rig the 2027 presidential election to secure a second term, declaring that the contest is effectively over in favour of the ruling All Progressives Congress.
Soludo made the prediction on Thursday while speaking
content:
Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo, has said President Bola Tinubu does not need to rig the 2027 presidential election to secure a second term, declaring that the contest is effectively over in favour of the ruling All Progressives Congress.

Soludo made the prediction on Thursday while speaking at a presidential campaign rally at Alex Ekwueme Square in Awka.

“This election, to the best of our knowledge, is already won and lost. The president doesn’t need to rig any election. President Tinubu doesn’t need to rig any election,” he said.

Explaining his position, the governor said the APC ticket was competing against opposition parties whose candidates, according to him, lacked nationwide reach.

“All over the country today, in every state of Nigeria, it is President Tinubu and Shettima ticket versus one other party. Whereas you have some other candidates who are strong in some parts of the country but don’t exist in others.

“If you then take the totality of it all, do the arithmetic in your mind, this election is literally over,” Soludo said.

He also attributed his prediction to the performance of the Tinubu administration, saying the President and his deputy would win because of their record in office.

“President Tinubu, Shettima, they’re doing very well. They will win because they have done well,” he said.

Soludo further argued that the APC had presented a stronger policy agenda than its opponents, adding that no credible alternative had emerged ahead of the election.

“And let me put it on record, in terms of the agenda that they are pursuing, no candidate before 2023 presented a better manifesto, better agenda for Nigeria.

“And so far, less than two months to go, no candidate has presented a credible alternative. The Tinubu-Shettima ticket presidency is on course,” he said.

The governor also defended the Federal Government’s handling of the economy and security, saying there was a “consensus, globally, internationally, nationally” among people familiar with the economy that the administration was moving in the right direction.

He cited the government’s support for students through the Nigerian Education Loan Fund as one of the initiatives benefiting Nigerians.

The INEC list of 18 presidential candidates for the January 16, 2027 election.

They include Tinubu of the APC; former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress; former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress; Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde of the Allied Peoples Movement; and former Cross River State Governor Donald Duke of the Peoples Redemption Party.

The other candidates are Adewole Adebayo of the Social Democratic Party; Sunday Okereke of the Labour Party; Omoyele Sowore of the African Action Congress; Sandy Onor of the Peoples Democratic Party; Rufai Omo-Aje of the Action Alliance; Abbas-Bin Aliyu of the Action Democratic Party; Kabiru Yusuf of the Allied Peoples Party; Sunday Adenuga of the Boot Party; Moses Adebisi of the Democratic Leadership Alliance; Ada Fredrick Okwori of the National Democratic Party; Nkem Esther Okereke of the National Rescue Movement; Peter Agada of the Young Progressives Party; and Daniel Nwanyanwu of the Zenith Labour Party.

title: Police recover NIWA vehicle stolen in Anambra, abandoned in Cross River
description:
The Cross River State Police Command has recovered a Toyota Hilux belonging to the National Inland Waterways Authority, reportedly stolen in Anambra State and tracked to Odukpani Local Government Area of Cross River State.
The vehicle, with registration number NIWA 19E-68-FG, was found abandoned aro
content:
The Cross River State Police Command has recovered a Toyota Hilux belonging to the National Inland Waterways Authority, reportedly stolen in Anambra State and tracked to Odukpani Local Government Area of Cross River State.

The vehicle, with registration number NIWA 19E-68-FG, was found abandoned around Uko-Ma Petrol Station, opposite Picolo Junction, near the Spaghetti Flyover in Odukpani.

The state Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Sunday Eitokpah, disclosed this in a statement made available to journalists on Thursday in Calabar.

According to the statement, the recovery followed a report received by the Odukpani Divisional Police Officer at about 11:30am on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, from a NIWA official in Calabar, who reported that the vehicle had been stolen in Anambra State and was being tracked to Cross River.

The statement read, “The Cross River State Police Command has recovered a Toyota Hilux belonging to the National Inland Waterways Authority (NIWA), with registration number NIWA 19E-68-FG, reportedly stolen in Anambra State and subsequently tracked to Odukpani LGA, Cross River State.

“The recovery underscores the command’s commitment to preventing crime, responding swiftly to credible intelligence and ensuring that Cross River State does not become a safe haven for criminal elements.”

The police spokesman said that, acting on the directive of the Commissioner of Police, CP Ajo Ordue, the DPO escalated the information, prompting the mobilisation of relevant operational units of the command.

“At about 3:00 p.m. the same day, the vehicle was tracked to the location where it was found abandoned. An individual suspected to be connected with the vehicle reportedly fled upon sighting the police,” statement read partly.

The recovered vehicle has been taken to the police station for safekeeping, while efforts are ongoing to identify and arrest the fleeing suspect, the statement added.

“Investigation has also commenced to establish the circumstances surrounding the theft and movement of the vehicle,” he said.

The Commissioner of Police commended the officers involved for their prompt response and coordination, reiterating the command’s resolve to tackle criminal activities through intelligence gathering, inter-divisional collaboration and proactive policing.

He warned criminal elements against using Cross River State as a hiding place or transit route, assuring residents that the command would continue to track down offenders and bring them to justice.

“The command urged members of the public to promptly report suspicious activities through its emergency numbers: 0704 177 7060 and 0705 335 5415,” he added.

The latest recovery comes amid other reports of vehicles stolen in neighbouring states and traced to Cross River.

On November 6, the state police command announced the recovery of a Lexus RX 330 allegedly stolen from a car wash in Enugu State and traced to Ugep in Yakurr Local Government Area. A 36-year-old suspect was arrested in connection with the incident.

Similarly, the Anambra State Police Command said in October that it had recovered a Toyota Highlander allegedly stolen in the state and traced to Calabar.

A suspect was also arrested in connection with the incident

title: Tiger Woods to design championship golf course in Northern Ireland
description:
Golf legend Tiger Woods is set to design a new championship links golf course in Northern Ireland, marking a major development for the country’s golf tourism industry.
Woods and his golf course architecture firm, TGR Design, have unveiled plans for Bellarena Golf Links, which will be built along the
content:
Golf legend Tiger Woods is set to design a new championship links golf course in Northern Ireland, marking a major development for the country’s golf tourism industry.

Woods and his golf course architecture firm, TGR Design, have unveiled plans for Bellarena Golf Links, which will be built along the spectacular Causeway Coast in the north-west of Northern Ireland.

The proposed course will be located approximately 20 miles west of Royal Portrush, a three-time host of The Open Championship.

The project will be Northern Ireland’s first new championship links course in more than a century and TGR Design’s first golf course development in Europe.

The 15-time major champion described the opportunity to create a course in one of the world’s most celebrated golfing destinations as a special experience.

As reported by BBC Sport on Thursday, Woods was quoted as saying, “Northern Ireland is home to some of the greatest links golf in the world, and building one on the Causeway Coast is a special opportunity for our team,” Woods said.

“We want Bellarena to feel as though it has always been part of this coastline, with a course that challenges the best players and is fun for everyone who plays it.”

The development is a partnership between Galgorm Collection and US-based Reef Destinations. Construction is expected to begin in 2027, subject to planning approval, with a target opening date of July 2029.

Galgorm Collection chief executive Colin Johnston described Woods’ involvement as a remarkable opportunity for the region.

“To have Tiger Woods and his company design a golf course in Northern Ireland is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity, it’s unbelievable,” Johnston said.

“It’s bringing together fantastic companies and partners and creating something that will benefit Northern Ireland for many years to come.”

Johnston said the location’s natural beauty was a major attraction, highlighting the views of Binevenagh Mountain, Lough Foyle and the Donegal hills.

“The backdrop of Binevenagh Mountain and the views over Lough Foyle and into the Donegal hills are just stunning,” he said.

Beyond its sporting appeal, the project is expected to strengthen tourism in Northern Ireland’s north-west by attracting more international golf visitors.

Johnston said golf tourism was already experiencing strong demand, making additional championship-level facilities important for the region.

“We know golf tourism is huge and we know it’s close to capacity,” he said.

“If we want to bring more people to this part of the world, we need to increase that capacity, and it needs to be at the elite level people expect when they come here.”

He added that Bellarena would complement established golfing destinations such as Royal Portrush and Royal County Down, while bringing more visitors to the region.

Unlike some of Northern Ireland’s exclusive championship venues, Bellarena is expected to operate as a non-member, pay-and-play course, giving visiting golfers greater access.

With Woods’ international profile, the spectacular coastal setting and the prospect of a new championship venue, Bellarena Golf Links is expected to become an important addition to Northern Ireland’s golfing landscape when it opens in 2029.

The post Tiger Woods to design championship golf course in Northern Ireland appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Why Bitcoin Price USD Now Shares Africa’s Crypto Stage
description: Bitcoin still supplies the number that many African crypto users check first. Yet the market around that number has changed. Chainalysis ranked African countries among the highest worldwide for grassroots adoption in September 2026. The country placed first for domestic peer-to-peer activity and fir
content:
Bitcoin still supplies the number that many African crypto users check first. Yet the market around that number has changed. Chainalysis ranked African countries among the highest worldwide for grassroots adoption in September 2026.

The country placed first for domestic peer-to-peer activity and first for cross-border flows. Those rankings point toward a crypto culture doing much more than waiting for Bitcoin to rise. Payments have grown in importance. Dollar-linked assets now handle a large share of transfers.

For someone in Lagos receiving money from abroad, the immediate concern may be conversion rather than investment performance. Bitcoin remains a major reference point, but it now shares attention with assets designed to hold a steadier dollar value.

Why Does the Dollar Quote Still Draw So Much Attention?

Global trading still gives Bitcoin much of its price in dollars. That affects Africans even when the money they spend starts as a different currency. Crypto exchanges provide spot markets and peer-to-peer routes where available, while users can also purchase through supported payment methods.

A Bitcoin USD price therefore offers a common reference before somebody works out the local cost and conversion route. The exchange figure isn’t the final amount leaving your account. Payment method and fees can alter that. So can the price available when the order reaches the market.

That distinction has become easier to understand as the naira has moved against the dollar. Reuters reported on October 8 that the currency was trading near 1,331 per dollar on the official market.

An African holder can therefore experience two price movements at once: Bitcoin changes against the dollar while the naira changes against that same currency. If you are keeping records, the local amount paid still deserves its own line rather than being reconstructed months later from a dollar chart.

Why Are Stablecoins Taking a Bigger Share?

Stablecoins now account for a substantial part of crypto activity across sub-Saharan Africa. Chainalysis estimated that they represented about 43% of the region’s total transaction volume in its 2024 geography report. The following year, sub-Saharan Africa received more than $205 billion in on-chain value between July 2024 and June 2025. That was an increase of about 52% from the previous 12 months.

The reason is broader than investment. Chainalysis found stablecoins being used in high-value transfers linked to trade between Africa and overseas markets. Merchant settlement also featured in its analysis.

A dollar-linked token offers a different proposition from Bitcoin because the user may care more about keeping a predictable dollar reference than gaining exposure to a changing market price. That can appeal to a business paying an overseas supplier or a household receiving money from abroad.

What Does This Tell Us About Africa’s Economy?

Digital assets are becoming part of a much wider change in how money moves across the continent. The IMF reported that mobile money accounts have grown faster than traditional deposit accounts across sub-Saharan Africa.

In several economies, they now outnumber conventional bank accounts. The share of remittances sent through digital channels also rose from 13% in 2019 to 46% in 2024.

Can Regulation Make Crypto Payments Easier to Understand?

Africa doesn’t have one regulatory model for digital assets. Ghana passed legislation covering virtual-asset services in 2025 and began a regulatory sandbox in March 2026. The Securities and Exchange Commission admitted businesses testing services that included virtual-asset exchanges and brokerage. Asset tokenisation also formed part of the programme.

Ghana’s authorities have also stressed that participation in supervised testing does not amount to unrestricted approval. The country’s framework requires licensing or registration for activities such as wallet provision and stablecoin issuance.

An IMF technical-assistance review published in September said Ghana had made progress toward global standards, while further rules were still needed in areas such as stablecoin arrangements and trading activity.

What Should African Users Compare Before Choosing an Asset?

Start with the job you want the asset to perform. Someone seeking long-term Bitcoin exposure faces a different decision from a freelancer who wants to receive a dollar-linked payment. Check the spread between buying and selling prices. Find the withdrawal cost before moving funds. If another wallet will hold the asset, establish who controls the private keys.

Currency conversion deserves the same attention. A dollar quotation can help you follow the global market, but it does not tell you what will reach a bank account or mobile-money wallet after conversion into local currency. Exchange rates vary across African economies. Access to dollars can vary as well.

Stablecoins reduce one form of price movement by targeting a reference such as the U.S. dollar, but they introduce issuer and redemption considerations. Bitcoin brings a different risk because its value can move much further. The IMF also warns that stablecoins remain unevenly regulated and can raise concerns about currency substitution in emerging markets.

For African users, the final comparison therefore needs a local layer. Check the rules in your country and the available cash-out routes. Then look at fees and custody. A service that works well for a user in Johannesburg may offer a different experience in Accra or Nairobi because the surrounding financial systems and regulations are different.

The post Why Bitcoin Price USD Now Shares Africa’s Crypto Stage appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Police Arrest Nine Suspected Robbers, Rescue Three Kidnapped Victims In Nasarawa
description: The Nasarawa State Police Command has arrested nine suspects over an armed robbery attack on student lodges in Keffi Local Government Area and rescued three kidnapped victims in Awe Local Government Area, Nasarawa State. The operations, according to a statement by the Police Public Relations Officer
content:
The Nasarawa State Police Command has arrested nine suspects over an armed robbery attack on student lodges in Keffi Local Government Area and rescued three kidnapped victims in Awe Local Government Area, Nasarawa State.

The operations, according to a statement by the Police Public Relations Officer, SP Ramhan Nansel, occurred as part of the Command’s sustained efforts to tackle criminal activities across the state.

The statement said the suspects were arrested by operatives of the Angwan Lambu Division following a distress call that armed hoodlums had invaded student hostels behind Princess Sarah in Keffi, dispossessing occupants of their valuables.

Although the suspects fled before the arrival of the police patrol team, operatives, acting on intelligence, trailed them to a hotel on the outskirts of Keffi, where nine persons were apprehended.

Items recovered from the suspects include a cutlass, a long stick, eight mobile phones and substances suspected to be illicit drugs.

The police said investigations had commenced, adding that the suspects had been identified by their victims and were providing useful information to establish their respective levels of involvement.

In a separate operation on November 18, 2026, police operatives rescued three kidnapped victims in the Hunki axis, between Awe and Azara in Awe Local Government Area.

The rescue followed credible intelligence that armed bandits had abducted some persons and were holding them hostage in a forest in the area.

According to the statement, the Commissioner of Police, CP Sheikh Mohammed Danko, immediately mobilised operatives of the Violent Crimes Response Unit (VCRU) and other patrol teams to the location.

The operatives reportedly combed the forest and mounted pressure on the kidnappers, forcing them to abandon their captives and flee.

The rescued victims were identified as 40-year-old Habibu Samaika from Ubi Local Government Area of Taraba State; 40-year-old Audi Abubakar from Shendam Local Government Area of Plateau State; and 19-year-old Shafiu Zakari from Azara in Awe Local Government Area of Nasarawa State.

The victims were rescued unhurt and taken to Azara General Hospital for medical attention, where they were confirmed to be in stable condition.

The police said their relatives had been contacted, while arrangements were being made to reunite them with their families following their discharge.

Commending the officers for their prompt response, courage and professionalism, CP Danko assured residents that the Command would sustain intelligence-led operations and patrols to dismantle criminal networks and bring perpetrators to justice.

He also urged members of the public to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements and criminal activities to the nearest police station, assuring them that all information received would be treated with utmost confidentiality.

The Commissioner reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to protecting lives and property across Nasarawa State.

The post Police Arrest Nine Suspected Robbers, Rescue Three Kidnapped Victims In Nasarawa appeared first on Channels Television.

title: Ebonyi gives shanty shop owners 15-day ultimatum to remove structures
description:
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki



The Ebonyi State Government has given owners and operators of shanty shops at Quarry Junction, Abakaliki, 15 days to dismantle and remove their structures over safety concerns.







The Commissioner for Capital City and Urban Planning, Chief Richard Ugo Idike, issued t
content:
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

The Ebonyi State Government has given owners and operators of shanty shops at Quarry Junction, Abakaliki, 15 days to dismantle and remove their structures over safety concerns.

The Commissioner for Capital City and Urban Planning, Chief Richard Ugo Idike, issued the directive during a routine inspection exercise aimed at ensuring compliance with urban planning regulations and protecting lives and property in the state capital.

Idike expressed concern that the makeshift shops were located directly beneath high-tension electricity lines, describing the situation as a serious threat to traders, customers and other members of the public.

He said the government’s intervention was necessary to prevent possible accidents, electrocution and loss of lives, stressing that commercial activities would not be allowed to continue in locations considered dangerous to public safety.

The commissioner directed all owners and occupants of the affected shops to dismantle their structures within 15 days, warning that failure to comply would attract enforcement action by the ministry.

He said the state government’s urban renewal and development agenda was not limited to creating a beautiful and well-organised capital city but also included ensuring that residents operated businesses in safe and approved locations.

Idike reiterated the ministry’s commitment to regular monitoring, inspection and enforcement of building and urban planning regulations across Abakaliki metropolis.

He urged residents, traders, property owners and developers to obtain the necessary government approvals before erecting structures or engaging in commercial activities.

The commissioner assured that the ministry would continue to take proactive measures to prevent avoidable disasters and promote orderly development across the state capital.

title: Treat gunshot victims first; police report can wait – IGP Disu to doctors
description:
By Enitan Abdultawab



The Inspector General of Police, Tunji Disu, has urged hospitals and healthcare workers across the country to treat gunshot victims immediately without demanding police reports, warning that delays could cost lives.



Disu also called on members of the public to assist injur
content:
By Enitan Abdultawab

The Inspector General of Police, Tunji Disu, has urged hospitals and healthcare workers across the country to treat gunshot victims immediately without demanding police reports, warning that delays could cost lives.

Disu also called on members of the public to assist injured persons in accessing medical attention, assuring them that they would not face punishment for helping victims.

The IGP made the appeal in a sensitisation message by the National Orientation Agency (NOA) in collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, shared by the police on its X account on Thursday.

Addressing Nigerians, police officers and medical personnel, Disu described the treatment of gunshot victims as a matter of life and death, stressing that no police documentation was required before emergency medical care could be provided.

“Fellow Nigerians, I am here to address a matter of life and death – the treatment of gunshot victims in our hospitals.

“To my fellow officers, to my medical personnel across the nation, and to every Nigerian listening, treating gunshot victims does not require a police report.

“When a gunshot victim is brought to any hospital, the law does not require a police report before treatment,” he said.

He urged doctors and other healthcare workers to prioritise saving lives rather than allow administrative procedures to delay emergency treatment.

“To our doctors and healthcare workers, you are enjoined to treat gunshot victims immediately without waiting for a police report. Our duty is not to create fear but to protect lives. We wish to reassure citizens of their safety at all times,” Disu added.

The police chief also appealed to Nigerians not to hesitate to help people who sustain gunshot injuries, emphasising that the law protects those who assist victims.

“To the members of the public, if you see someone injured, do not hesitate to help. You will not be punished for helping.

“Again, to my officers and medical personnel, please uphold the law because every second counts. Treat first, save lives,” he said.

In a related message accompanying the video, the Nigeria Police Force warned that refusing or delaying medical attention for gunshot victims was punishable under the Compulsory Treatment and Care for Victims of Gunshots Act, 2017.

According to the police, the legislation requires all public and private hospitals to provide immediate treatment to gunshot victims, regardless of whether they have police reports or clearance.

The police further warned that violations of the Act could attract imprisonment of up to 15 years and other penalties, depending on the offence.

The law provides that every hospital in Nigeria, whether public or private, must receive and provide immediate and adequate treatment to anyone with gunshot wounds, with or without police clearance.

It also places a responsibility on members of the public, including security personnel, to assist victims and ensure they are taken to the nearest hospital for treatment.

Under the Act, hospitals are required to notify the nearest police station within two hours of commencing treatment, allowing investigations into the circumstances surrounding the shooting to begin without delaying medical attention.

The legislation further protects volunteers and other helpers from unnecessary or embarrassing interrogation for their efforts to save the lives of gunshot victims.

The post Treat gunshot victims first; police report can wait – IGP Disu to doctors appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Burna Boy, Asake, Seyi Vibez feature on GTA VI soundtrack
description:
By Enitan Abdultawab



Nigerian music stars Burna Boy, Asake and Seyi Vibez have secured spots on the soundtrack of the highly anticipated video game, Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI).



The Nigerian artistes are among several international performers featured on the game’s soundtrack, which was recen
content:
By Enitan Abdultawab

Nigerian music stars Burna Boy, Asake and Seyi Vibez have secured spots on the soundtrack of the highly anticipated video game, Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI).

The Nigerian artistes are among several international performers featured on the game’s soundtrack, which was recently unveiled by Rockstar Games, the developer of the popular gaming franchise.

Some of their songs will feature on AfroBank FM, an in-game radio station dedicated to African music, including Afrobeats, amapiano, African classics and 3-step sounds.

Burna Boy is also set to co-host the station alongside British DJ and record producer Palms Trax, who appears in the game under the name Palmsy.

Among the Nigerian tracks featured on the station are Asake’s ‘Joha’ and ‘Giza’, a collaboration between Burna Boy and Seyi Vibez.

The station’s previewed playlist also includes ‘Gye Wani’ by Pat Thomas featuring Ebo Taylor, as well as ‘Shay’sana’ by DJ Lag and Robot Boii featuring Kamo Mphela.

Burna Boy also makes a separate contribution to the game’s official soundtrack with his song ‘Bigger’.

Other international artistes featured on the soundtrack include Travis Scott, Dua Lipa, Cardi B, Gunna, Young Thug, Kodak Black, Don Toliver, Zara Larsson, Camila Cabello and Lana Del Rey.

The development marks another international gaming appearance for Nigerian music, as Afrobeats continues to gain visibility across global entertainment platforms.

GTA VI is the latest instalment in Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto series, one of the world’s most popular video game franchises.

title: 2027: Court upholds Yahaya Bello’s APC senatorial candidacy
description:
The Federal High Court in Abuja has affirmed former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, as the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Kogi Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general election.
Justice Inyang Ekwo delivered the ruling on Thursday while dismissing a suit filed by Momoh Obaro
content:
The Federal High Court in Abuja has affirmed former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, as the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Kogi Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general election.

Justice Inyang Ekwo delivered the ruling on Thursday while dismissing a suit filed by Momoh Obaro, who challenged Bello’s emergence from the party’s May 18, 2026 primary election.

Obaro had claimed that he won the APC senatorial primary and questioned Bello’s emergence as the party’s candidate for the Kogi Central seat.

However, the judge dismissed the case for lacking merit and sufficient evidence.

Justice Ekwo also faulted the plaintiff for approaching the court without first exhausting the party’s internal dispute resolution mechanisms.

The ruling clears the way for Bello to retain his position as the APC’s candidate for the Kogi Central Senatorial District ahead of the 2027 elections.

‎The court held that there was no evidence before it to show that the aggrieved plaintiff exhausted the dispute resolution mechanisms of the party in the wake of the senatorial primary.

According to the judge, Obaro “bypassed” the Appeals Committee to seek redress in court.

‎Consequently, the court dismissed the suit for being “premature” owing to the plaintiff’s failure to fully exhaust the internal dispute resolution mechanism of the party.

‎Justice Ekwo said what could have triggered the jurisdiction of the court was if Obaro had approached the Appeals Committee of the APC to seek redress instead of rushing to the court, citing Section 15(3) of the APC Guidelines.

‎The court also faulted the plaintiff for submitting to the court a document that was not signed by the Chairman and Secretary of the Election Committee.

‎“In law, an unsigned document is of no value,” the judge said. “The documents are of dubious origin,” Justice Ekwo further noted, referring to the purported document indicating that the plaintiff clinched the Kogi Central senatorial ticket of the APC.

‎The judge further noted that whoever conducted the senatorial primary where Momoh Obaro emerged as winner of the May 18 primary only succeeded in “giving him false hope”.

‎The plaintiff, in his nomination form, took an oath that he would follow the internal dispute mechanism of the party and that he would not approach the courts to register his grievances before seeking redress within the party.

‎Justice Ekwo also indicated that the plaintiff had committed to support whoever emerged as winner of the senatorial primary. The judge said any person who takes an oath must abide by its terms.

‎One of the terms of the oath is not to institute a suit challenging the outcome of the primary without first dealing with the grievances internally.

The court indicated that the plaintiff’s failure to do so robbed it of jurisdiction to intervene in his case.

‎”This ultimately prompted the dismissal of the case for lacking merit and is hereby dismissed,” the judge declared.

The post 2027: Court upholds Yahaya Bello’s APC senatorial candidacy appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: FIFA unveils presidential candidates to challenge Infantino’s re-election
description:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino will face competition from French Football Federation President Philippe Diallo and Japanese football chief Kozo Tashima in his bid for another term.
The world football governing body announced the candidates in a statement issued on Thursday, PUNCH Online reports.
It
content:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino will face competition from French Football Federation President Philippe Diallo and Japanese football chief Kozo Tashima in his bid for another term.

The world football governing body announced the candidates in a statement issued on Thursday, PUNCH Online reports.

It stated that the election is scheduled for March 2027 and will mark the first time Infantino has faced an opponent since becoming FIFA president in 2016. He was re-elected unopposed in 2023.

FIFA added that the nominations had been forwarded to its electoral committee for review.

“The candidatures have been forwarded to the electoral committee for examination and for passing a decision on the admission of the candidates.

“Member associations will be notified of the names of the proposed and admitted candidates no later than 18 February 2027,” the statement read.

Former Switzerland defender Ramon Vega, who announced his intention to contest the election last month, was not included among the candidates named by FIFA on Thursday.

Diallo declared his intention to run on Monday, backed by European football associations represented on the UEFA executive committee and the FIFA Council.

Tashima, honorary president of the Japan Football Association, announced his ambition earlier this month and formally submitted his nomination on Wednesday.

Infantino has faced criticism and calls for his resignation following the controversy surrounding his proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise, an initiative reportedly aimed at selling stakes in the World Cup and other major competitions.

The proposal failed to materialise, but the FIFA president has maintained that he enjoys sufficient backing from member associations worldwide to secure another term.

Diallo, who became president of the French Football Federation in 2023, played a prominent role in the withdrawal of support for Infantino by France and other European associations over the controversy.

The post FIFA unveils presidential candidates to challenge Infantino’s re-election appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: UDUS medical academics threaten five-day warning strike
description:
By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto



The Nigerian Association of Medical and Dental Academics (NAMDA), Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto (UDUS)/Usmanu Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital (UDUTH) Chapter, has threatened to embark on a five-day warning strike over alleged irregularities in salary paymen
content:
By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto

The Nigerian Association of Medical and Dental Academics (NAMDA), Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto (UDUS)/Usmanu Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital (UDUTH) Chapter, has threatened to embark on a five-day warning strike over alleged irregularities in salary payments, partial implementation of professional allowances and outstanding promotion arrears owed to its members.

The association, at a press briefing in Sokoto on Thursday, said the unresolved welfare and remuneration issues had persisted despite several rounds of consultations, formal correspondence and peaceful engagements with the university management.

It warned that its members might be left with no option but to embark on an indefinite strike if the issues were not addressed.

Speaking at the briefing, presided over by Professor Usman Bello, NAMDA said its members had exercised considerable patience and goodwill through sustained dialogue with the relevant authorities, but expressed regret that the engagements had not produced the desired results.

The association said its concerns centred on the continued partial implementation of professional allowances under the revised Consolidated Medical Salary Structure (CONMESS), unexplained salary disparities among members on the same grade levels and steps, and the non-payment of promotion arrears covering 2017 to 2024.

It also alleged that some eligible members were excluded from the payment of 2025 and 2026 promotion arrears, describing the situation as an administrative and financial burden that had continued to affect the welfare and morale of medical academics.

According to the association, comparable institutions in both Northern and Southern Nigeria had fully implemented the revised CONMESS, a development it said had heightened concerns among its members over disparities in remuneration.

NAMDA recalled that it had pursued several avenues to resolve the dispute, including meetings with university authorities, submission of formal letters and supporting documents, and interventions by senior colleagues and elders.

However, it said those efforts had yet to yield the desired outcome.

The association also raised concerns over the migration of experienced medical professionals, including senior consultants and professors, to other countries in search of better working conditions.

It described the development, popularly known as “japa”, as a threat to medical education and healthcare delivery in the country.

“Mr President is aware of the ongoing exodus of highly experienced academic staff, including senior consultants and professors, to other countries, a trend popularly known as ‘japa’,” it said.

NAMDA added that the Federal Government’s decision to increase the admission quota for medical students had placed additional pressure on the declining number of medical teachers.

It warned that increasing student intake without corresponding investment in recruiting and retaining qualified medical lecturers could undermine the quality of medical education.

The association said medical teachers, under NAMDA, the Medical and Dental Consultants Association of Nigeria (MDCAN) and the Nigerian Medical Association (NMA), had continued to discharge their responsibilities despite the challenges.

“Despite these challenges, medical teachers have continued to impart knowledge and skills without compromising quality or professional standards,” it said.

NAMDA further disclosed that the Minister of Education had directed vice-chancellors to ensure the payment of outstanding arrears owed to medical teachers in compliance with a presidential directive.

It said several other universities had implemented the directive, but alleged that the management of UDUS had yet to act on it despite sustained engagements.

The association said its congress had consequently resolved to issue a 21-day ultimatum to the university management, effective November 3, 2026, demanding the resolution of all outstanding welfare and remuneration issues before the notice expires on November 24.

It warned that failure to address the concerns would trigger a five-day warning strike.

“Should these concerns remain unaddressed at the expiry of the notice on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, members shall commence a five-day warning strike from 12 midnight on Wednesday, November 25, 2026,” it stated.

The association added that it would review the situation after the warning strike, including the possibility of embarking on an indefinite industrial action if the dispute remained unresolved.

Despite the planned action, NAMDA appealed for urgent intervention and constructive engagement, saying it remained willing to work with the university management towards a lasting resolution in the interest of medical academics, students and patients who depend on the institution’s services.

The post UDUS medical academics threaten five-day warning strike appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: UK Asks YouTube To Remove Russell Brand’s Innocence Claim Video
description: The UK government has asked Google to remove a YouTube video in which jailed comedian Russell Brand protests his innocence, the justice ministry said Thursday, but the US tech giant has not yet complied.Brand, who was last week sentenced to 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assault against four
content:
The UK government has asked Google to remove a YouTube video in which jailed comedian Russell Brand protests his innocence, the justice ministry said Thursday, but the US tech giant has not yet complied.

Brand, who was last week sentenced to 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assault against four women, insisted he is innocent in a statement read out by his wife in the video uploaded Sunday to YouTube.

Laura Brand delivered his message, which was shared on their channel on the platform, prompting an immediate backlash from victims’ advocates, political leaders and others.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s spokesman called the video “clearly appalling” on Monday, and it is understood the Ministry of Justice subsequently submitted an official request to YouTube’s owner, Google, to remove it.

“It is only right that the government asks for content that is distressing for victims to be taken down, and we strongly believe YouTube should remove this content,” a ministry spokesman said in a statement to AFP.

“Removal ultimately depends on the platform’s own terms.”

As of 1100 GMT Thursday, the video remained accessible on the couple’s account, which has 6.6 million followers, and had been viewed more than 850,000 times.

The BBC reported Google had refused the request because it had determined its rules had not been broken.

In a brief statement, a spokeswoman for the company told AFP: “We’re aware of the new content and our teams are investigating.”

It said Google had suspended Brand’s channel from YouTube’s monetising partnerships programme in September 2023, and that the account had not been able to make money from its content on the platform since then.

The 51-year-old comedian and actor turned conservative religious guru was found guilty of rape and three sexual assaults earlier this month, and days later sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison.

Officials have noted that prisoners are banned from making statements that cause distress to victims, and speaking to the media is only permitted in exceptional circumstances.

Inmates cannot get around these rules by having someone else publish their comments, amid speculation that prison visits by Brand’s wife and communication between the couple could be restricted in the future.

Government minister Matthew Pennycook told the BBC that UK authorities “don’t have any power to mandate a removal of content”.

“That is up to Google,” he said.

“We’ve made a request in this instance because we feel very strongly that victims shouldn’t have to see this content.”

Brand’s accounts on Facebook and Instagram appear to be no longer available, and although his X account with 10 million followers can still be seen, there have been no posts since November 11.

AFP

title: NAFDAC Intercepts 17 Cartons Of Suspected Unregistered Beverages, Skin-Lightening Injections In Kano
description: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has intercepted 17 cartons of suspected unregistered beverages and skin-lightening and anti-ageing injections at the Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport in Kano State.The agency in a statement on Thursday said the products
content:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has intercepted 17 cartons of suspected unregistered beverages and skin-lightening and anti-ageing injections at the Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport in Kano State.

The agency in a statement on Thursday said the products were discovered concealed in a consignment of 33 cartons declared as “personal effects” and transported aboard an Ethiopian Airlines flight that arrived at the airport the previous day.

According to NAFDAC, the interception was carried out by its Port Inspection Directorate (PID) during a joint examination at the Skyway Aviation Handling Company Plc (SAHCO) Shed at the airport.

A physical examination of the consignment reportedly revealed that the suspected regulated products bore no NAFDAC registration numbers.

The agency also said the consignment was not accompanied by the requisite import documentation, raising regulatory concerns over the attempted importation.

Following the discovery, NAFDAC said the entire consignment was placed on hold in the custody of the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS).

NAFDAC said that the importer was subsequently invited for questioning, while a statement was obtained as part of the ongoing investigation.

It added that the intercepted products remained on hold pending further regulatory directives.

The agency, however, cautioned that the quality and authenticity of the products had not yet been established.

NAFDAC noted that the interception comes amid its efforts to strengthen surveillance and enforcement at Nigeria’s entry points to prevent the importation and circulation of unregistered, substandard and falsified regulated products.

The agency said it would continue to intensify monitoring activities to protect Nigerians from potentially harmful products and safeguard public health.

title: VeryDarkMan rushed to hospital In China over life-threatening sickness
description:
Nigerian social media activist Martins Vincent Otse, popularly known as VeryDarkMan (VDM), has been hospitalised in China after being diagnosed with what he described as life-threatening malaria.
The social media critic disclosed his health condition in a video shared on his Instagram page on Thursd
content:
Nigerian social media activist Martins Vincent Otse, popularly known as VeryDarkMan (VDM), has been hospitalised in China after being diagnosed with what he described as life-threatening malaria.

The social media critic disclosed his health condition in a video shared on his Instagram page on Thursday, November 19, 2026, while on a business trip to the Asian country.

VDM said his condition deteriorated despite attempts to manage the illness through self-medication, forcing him to seek medical attention after experiencing a serious health crisis.

According to him, the illness became severe on Wednesday night, leaving him fearing for his life before he was rushed to a hospital the following morning.

The activist disclosed that doctors attending to him had directed that he remain in the hospital under quarantine for between four and seven days.

In the caption accompanying the video, he described the experience as one of the most frightening moments of his life.

“This sickness almost took my life last night. This morning, I was rushed to the hospital and I will be in quarantine from today. I can’t leave,” he wrote.

He further revealed that he had never spent a night in a hospital throughout his 32 years, adding that the experience would mark his first extended hospital admission.

“In my whole 32 years of living, I have never slept in the hospital before, but this is going to keep me here for four to seven days straight,” he added.

VDM also expressed surprise at the severity of the malaria diagnosis, saying he had not previously heard of the condition being described as life-threatening.

The activist further noted that doctors informed him that the disease had caused several deaths among Nigerians.

His hospitalisation comes amid concerns over the dangers of self-medication, particularly when dealing with illnesses that require prompt medical attention.

Meanwhile, the development has attracted attention from his followers and supporters, many of whom have expressed concern and wished him a speedy recovery.

title: China, US, Russia issue ‘peace declaration’ after first summit
description:
China, the United States and Russia issued a “peace declaration” Thursday following an unprecedented leaders’ summit, almost five years into the Ukraine war and with Donald Trump bogged down in Iran.



The statement after Xi Jinping, Trump and Vladimir Putin met in China, said that they wanted to r
content:
China, the United States and Russia issued a “peace declaration” Thursday following an unprecedented leaders’ summit, almost five years into the Ukraine war and with Donald Trump bogged down in Iran.

The statement after Xi Jinping, Trump and Vladimir Putin met in China, said that they wanted to reform the United Nations, to protect diplomatic immunity and boost supply and production of refined petroleum products.

“The three heads of state engaged in an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed themselves to upholding strategic stability and international security,” said the statement published by Chinese state media and the Kremlin, but not yet by the White House.

The three-way meeting took place with Russia’s years-long offensive in Ukraine grinding on, mayhem in the Middle East in the wake of Trump’s attacks on Iran, and an ascendant China looking to strengthen its hand in East Asia.

“Our countries have many converging interests when it comes to resolving regional conflicts, including, of course, the conflict in Ukraine,” Putin said at the start of the meeting, adding they had a “shared responsibility for maintaining international peace and security”.

The three men made opening remarks touching on weighty topics from nuclear weapons to the war in Ukraine as they met around a large, dark round table with a pink flower arrangement at its centre.

The discussion behind closed doors in Kylin Villa in Shenzhen ended after an hour and 20 minutes.

Trump said the three men were “making history”, while Putin said they wrote a new “page in the history of diplomacy”.

“The three countries share a common perspective on safeguarding world peace,” Xi said.

ICC, UN and oil

In their joint statement, the leaders agreed that “the International Criminal Court and other similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction.”

Putin is subject to an ICC arrest warrant while Trump’s administration has vowed to dismantle the court “brick by brick”.

The leaders also “acknowledged the vital importance of the principle of state consent and the respect for (diplomatic) immunity enjoyed by state officials”, the statement said, adding that each country was “committed” to advancing the reform of the United Nations.

Putin said the discussion would also touch on food and energy security – both of which have been upended by conflicts in Iran and Ukraine.

The joint statement said the countries “plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products”, reaffirming “the importance of the stable flow of energy”.

The summit stoked fears that the three powerful men want to divide the globe into spheres of influence, for example by making decisions impacting Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv or Europe.

Earlier Thursday, Trump and Putin held a meeting — their first since August 2025 — with the 80-year-old US president calling the Russian his “friend”, who responded in English: “Nice to meet you.”

Trump and Xi then came together – for the third time this year – for one-on-one discussions, with the US leader highlighting their “very special relationship”.

Putin, 74, and Xi, 73, held talks on Wednesday – their 50th meeting, the Chinese president said.

‘Cheap violin’

Beijing, Washington and Moscow previously gave different accounts of the agenda for the three-way meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, a forum of 21 economies around the Pacific rim.

Washington initially signalled that Ukraine was off the table, before Trump said the war would feature. Xi does not view the conflict as China’s problem to solve.

Critics warned that the optics from the meeting would be damaging for the US president — but a fillip to Xi and Putin.

The meeting “gives Putin a platform to legitimise his war of aggression over Ukraine with seemingly little repercussions,” said Lyle Morris at the Asia Society Policy Institute.

“Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are playing Donald Trump like a cheap violin,” Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said.

Washington had also flagged up the Iran war and nuclear disarmament as topics of discussion, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February.

Beijing has long maintained that the United States and Russia must reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile.

The final statement said that the “three nations will engage in dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing nuclear proliferation”.

The extraordinary meeting preceded equally unusual scenes as the leaders arrived in the southern Chinese city for the talks.

Breaking with decades of diplomatic protocol, Xi received Trump at the airport, with the men briefly hugging before a red-carpet greeting complete with cheering children and an air force flyover.

Despite their differences, all the leaders – including Putin – posed for the APEC “family photo” on Thursday in special scarves.

Vanguard News

title: Microphone can kill like gun, Okonkwo warns PR professionals
description:
By John Alechenu







ABUJA — Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Prof. Obiora Okonkwo, has warned public relations professionals against irresponsible communication, saying that in the wrong hands, the microphone can become as destructive as a dangerous weapon.







Okonkwo gave the warning at
content:
By John Alechenu

ABUJA — Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Prof. Obiora Okonkwo, has warned public relations professionals against irresponsible communication, saying that in the wrong hands, the microphone can become as destructive as a dangerous weapon.

Okonkwo gave the warning at the 13th World Public Relations Forum 2026 in Abuja, where he drew lessons from historical events, Nigeria’s recent elections, the COVID-19 pandemic and his experience in the aviation industry.

He cited the 1994 Rwandan genocide as one of the most tragic examples of the destructive potential of irresponsible communication, recalling how the radio station, RTLM, became an instrument for promoting ethnic hatred, dehumanisation and incitement to violence.

He said the broadcasts helped create an atmosphere in which neighbours were turned against one another, adding that the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda subsequently established the criminal responsibility of media figures for their roles in inciting genocide.

“The lesson is clear: communication is not always an innocent exercise. In the hands of irresponsible actors, the microphone can become as destructive as a dangerous weapon,” he said.

Okonkwo identified Nigeria’s 2023 general elections as a more recent illustration of the dangers of irresponsible communication, noting that while social media platforms facilitated political mobilisation, they also enabled the circulation of unverified claims, fabricated results and divisive ethnic and political narratives.

He also recalled that during the COVID-19 pandemic, the World Health Organisation identified an infodemic, describing it as an overwhelming volume of information, including false and misleading content, capable of confusing populations and undermining confidence in public health institutions.

“These examples demonstrate that irresponsible communication can threaten not only democratic stability, but also human lives,” he said.

Drawing from his experience in the Nigerian aviation industry, Okonkwo stressed the importance of truthful communication in managing corporate reputation.

According to him, timely, factual and transparent communication can prevent speculation, correct misinformation and sustain stakeholder confidence, while evasive statements can turn operational difficulties into reputational crises.

“I have come to appreciate that truthfulness is not the enemy of reputation management. It is its most sustainable foundation,” he said.

Also speaking at the forum, Director-General of the National Orientation Agency (NOA), Lanre Issa-Onilu, challenged public relations professionals to examine the relationship between national image-building and the actual conduct of institutions and citizens.

He posed questions on whether Nigeria could be promoted as an investment destination while investors continued to encounter unnecessary bureaucracy, or whether national unity could be projected while citizens perceived discrimination and prejudice.

Issa-Onilu said the President Bola Tinubu-led administration had, in three years, embarked on reforms covering the economy, infrastructure, business conduct, education, healthcare and strategic communication with citizens.

He, however, questioned whether the reforms could be sustained without a corresponding improvement in the country’s national character.

“We can introduce the best tax system, but it will fail if officials are dishonest. We can construct excellent roads, but they will not last if contractors compromise standards and road users disregard regulations.

“That is why character reform is fundamental to national development. Policies do not implement themselves. People implement them, and their values influence the results,” he said.

In a message to the forum, Nobel Laureate, Prof. Wole Soyinka, said the gathering provided an opportunity to reaffirm the strategic importance of public relations in shaping perceptions, building trust and strengthening institutions.

Soyinka, who won the 1986 Nobel Prize in Literature, said the profession carried greater responsibility at a time of technological disruption and growing demands for transparency and accountability.

He commended the Global Alliance, the African Public Relations Association (APRA), the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR) and other partners for bringing the conversation to Africa.

He expressed hope that the forum would strengthen collaboration and contribute to the advancement of the public relations profession.

The post Microphone can kill like gun, Okonkwo warns PR professionals appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Pay presidential campaign fee to feature Obi on billboard, Soludo’s aide tells Umeh
description:
An aide to Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo, Izuchukwu Adichie has told Senator Victor Umeh to pay the required presidential campaign permit fee if he wants to feature Peter Obi on his campaign billboard, following the removal of the billboard by state officials.
Adichie, the Senior Special A
content:
An aide to Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo, Izuchukwu Adichie has told Senator Victor Umeh to pay the required presidential campaign permit fee if he wants to feature Peter Obi on his campaign billboard, following the removal of the billboard by state officials.

Adichie, the Senior Special Assistant on New Media to Soludo, made the remark following the dismantling of a campaign billboard featuring Umeh and Obi by officials of the Anambra State Signage and Advertisement Agency.

The billboard promoted Umeh’s senatorial ambition alongside Obi, who is seeking the presidency in the 2027 general election on the platform of the NDC.

Reacting to the development in a Facebook post on Thursday, Adichie said Umeh should pay the applicable fee for featuring a presidential candidate on his campaign material.

“If Senator Victor Umeh wants to put Peter Obi’s face on his billboard, let him pay Peter Obi’s rate as well. Peter Obi is running for president. ANSAA needs money!” he wrote.

The development followed reports that Umeh had paid the agency’s ₦20m senatorial campaign permit fee but did not obtain a separate permit for Obi’s presidential campaign.

Under the agency’s campaign fee structure for the 2027 general elections, presidential candidates are required to pay ₦50m, while senatorial candidates are to pay ₦20m.

Other categories include ₦5m for House of Representatives candidates, ₦1.5m for state House of Assembly candidates and ₦2.5m for local government chairmanship candidates.

The Anambra State Commissioner for Information, Law Mefor, had defended the agency’s action, saying it was based on compliance with the state’s signage regulations and not an attempt to target Obi.

The government maintained that Umeh’s payment covered his senatorial campaign and did not extend to the promotion of another candidate seeking the presidency.

Umeh, a former national chairman of the All Progressives Grand Alliance, is a long-time political ally of Obi and has previously criticised Soludo over his position on the former Anambra governor’s presidential ambition.

The senator had warned Soludo against undermining Obi’s 2027 presidential bid, insisting that the governor should not work against the political aspiration of his former predecessor.

Soludo and his party, APGA, have adopted President Bola Tinubu as their preferred candidate for the 2027 presidential election.

Obi contested the 2023 presidential election on the platform of the Labour Party before moving to the NDC, under which he is seeking the presidency again.

content:
FIFA has announced French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo and former Japan Football Association chief Kohzo Tashima as challengers to Gianni Infantino in the race for its presidency.

The global football governing body confirmed the candidates in a statement released on Thursday.

The presidential election is scheduled to take place at FIFA’s 77th Congress on March 18, 2027.

The contest will mark the first time Infantino faces opposition in a presidential election since he secured unopposed victories in 2019 and 2023.

Infantino’s planned fourth-term bid has come amid criticism over his abandoned proposal to sell certain World Cup stakes to private investors. The move reportedly cost him the backing of UEFA and several other influential football confederations.

PHILIPPE DIALLO

Philippe Diallo, who heads the French Football Federation, is among the candidates seeking to challenge Infantino for the FIFA presidency.
The 63-year-old Diallo, who announced his candidacy on Monday, is backed by UEFA member associations, while Tashima represents the far-east Asian voting bloc and has also served on FIFA’s executive council.

However, Infantino continues to enjoy massive support from member associations in Africa and the Middle East.

FIFA said the candidacies will be examined by the body’s electoral committee before a final decision is made on whether to admit them.
