title: Middle Belt youth leader rejects Tinubu’s 2027 endorsement, backs Obi
description:
By Golok Nanmwa



JOS — The National Youth Leader of the Middle Belt Forum (MBF), Emmanuel Zopmal, has rejected the purported endorsement of President Bola Tinubu for re-election in 2027 by some Middle Belt leaders, declaring support for the presidential ambition of the Nigeria Democratic Congress
content:
By Golok Nanmwa

JOS — The National Youth Leader of the Middle Belt Forum (MBF), Emmanuel Zopmal, has rejected the purported endorsement of President Bola Tinubu for re-election in 2027 by some Middle Belt leaders, declaring support for the presidential ambition of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso.

Zopmal, who is also the North-Central Coordinator of The Big-Tent Coalition, stated this on Thursday while addressing journalists in Jos, Plateau State, where he presented the position of the Middle Belt youth leadership on the political future of the region.

He faulted the reported endorsement, alleging that it did not reflect the collective position of the people because critical stakeholders, including community leaders, traditional institutions, youths and women, were not consulted before the visit to the President.

“There was no due consultation with Middle Belt communities, elders, traditional institutions, youths and women who feel and live the terrible experiences in our various communities before the purported endorsement of President Tinubu for the 2027 re-election bid,” he said.

Zopmal described the reported endorsement as insensitive to the security and economic challenges confronting communities across the region and the country.

He cited insecurity, economic hardship, inflation, rising borrowings and poverty as issues that should have informed any political position taken in the name of the Middle Belt.

The MBF youth leader also questioned the leadership and administrative structure of the forum, alleging that it had operated without a General Assembly, elections, constitutional processes and accountability for eight years.

He called for the organisation to return to democratic principles and provide clearer direction for the Middle Belt struggle.

He also criticised the immediate past President of the forum, Dr Pogu Bitrus, over what he described as a lack of broad-based consultations in the organisation’s activities.

“We believe that no individual or group should assume the authority to speak for the entire Middle Belt without the consent and participation of the people and the various structures of the Forum,” he said.

On the recent visit by some Middle Belt leaders to Tinubu, which involved elder statesman and retired General Theophilus Danjuma, Zopmal alleged that the exercise was influenced by the political interests of some individuals.

He expressed concern that the outcome of the meeting could be wrongly associated with Danjuma’s position without the wider consent of the people.

Zopmal further argued that the Middle Belt Forum should remain non-partisan, questioning why representatives of opposition parties from the region were excluded from the engagement.

“Middle Belt Forum is not a partisan platform. We have Middle Belters who are national chairmen of other major opposition political parties. Why were they not involved in the visit, while the APC National Chairman was in attendance?” he queried.

He also dismissed reports suggesting that a Middle Belt candidate could be considered for the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential ticket in 2031, saying such assurances were not sufficient grounds for supporting Tinubu’s re-election.

“Middle Belt people should not be persuaded to support a political project on the basis of promises about what may happen in 2031. Our immediate concerns are security, economic empowerment, justice and the welfare of our people,” he said.

Appealing to Danjuma to reconsider the reported endorsement, Zopmal said the region needed concrete commitments on security and development rather than political assurances.

“We want to appeal to our father, Gen. T.Y. Danjuma, to reconsider the purported endorsement. The future of the Middle Belt is too important to be determined without the involvement of the people,” he stated.

He also accused the Federal Government of failing to do enough to address the plight of communities affected by violent attacks, particularly the resettlement of internally displaced persons (IDPs) and restoration of livelihoods.

“None of our grabbed community lands has been recovered. No IDPs have been resettled to their ancestral homeland,” he alleged.

He further claimed that there was no sustainable government programme to rebuild affected communities or a clear plan to enable residents return to their farms without fear.

Zopmal also criticised the President’s handling of security challenges in Plateau State, particularly the Palm Sunday attack, arguing that affected communities required more visible government intervention.

He said Plateau and other Middle Belt communities deserved sustained government attention, protection and concrete measures to address the consequences of violent attacks.

Declaring support for Obi and Kwankwaso ahead of the 2027 presidential election, Zopmal said his coalition would mobilise voters across the region for the NDC candidates.

“Peter Obi is the only presidential candidate who has consistently identified with the Middle Belt struggle, visited troubled communities and supported families affected by violent attacks. We believe his engagement with the region reflects the values of justice, fairness and equity,” he said.

He called on youths and women across the region to participate actively in the electoral process, vote according to their conscience and resist inducements.

He also urged them to defend their votes and ensure their voices count in the democratic process.

Zopmal said the Middle Belt struggle remained anchored on justice, fairness and equity, adding that the coalition would continue to mobilise support for what it described as a more inclusive and accountable Nigeria.

The post Middle Belt youth leader rejects Tinubu’s 2027 endorsement, backs Obi appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: FIFA Chief Infantino Faces Challenge From France’s Diallo, Japan’s Tashima
description: French football chief Philippe Diallo and veteran Japanese official Kozo Tashima were on Thursday confirmed by FIFA as the challengers to incumbent Gianni Infantino in next year’s presidential election.Infantino has faced criticism over his aborted plan to allow private investment into the Wor
content:
French football chief Philippe Diallo and veteran Japanese official Kozo Tashima were on Thursday confirmed by FIFA as the challengers to incumbent Gianni Infantino in next year’s presidential election.

Infantino has faced criticism over his aborted plan to allow private investment into the World Cup, but he retains considerable support for his bid to win re-election next March.

French Football Federation president Diallo will represent UEFA, the European confederation which has been the most vocal in its criticism of Infantino.

Tashima is a former head of the Japan Football Association and has served on the FIFA Council.

FIFA said the candidacies will be examined by the body’s electoral committee before a final decision is made on whether to admit them.

Ramon Vega, the Swiss former Tottenham defender who had expressed a desire to run against Infantino, was not included among the candidates.

Diallo has indicated he would like to hold talks with Tashima, with a view to “joining forces” to unseat Infantino.

The 68-year-old Japanese official, who has said he wants to make FIFA a “more trusted organisation”, said he was open to talks but was cautious about the steps after that.

“It’s clear we need to talk,” Tashima told French sports daily L’Equipe on Wednesday. “But we must consider one thing: is the mere fact that our programmes are similar enough for us to decide to work together, or unite? Or should we think tactically, asking what the most effective strategy would be to defeat Infantino?”

In opposing Infantino, Tashima is going against his own confederation after the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) announced last month that it would support the 56-year-old Swiss for re-election.

Infantino also has the backing of the Confederation of African Football (CAF), while South American governing body CONMEBOL, is largely supportive.

Under his rule, FIFA’s profits have skyrocketed, and so have the amounts that member federations receive.

AFP

title: ‘Nigerians must go’ – Anti-migrant protesters demand entry ban in South Africa
description:
Members of the anti-migrant group, March and March, staged a protest in Pretoria, South Africa, on Wednesday, demanding that Nigerians be banned from entering the country.
The demonstrators, led by the group’s leader, Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma, challenged Nigerian immigrants living in Sunnyside, a suburb
content:
Members of the anti-migrant group, March and March, staged a protest in Pretoria, South Africa, on Wednesday, demanding that Nigerians be banned from entering the country.

The demonstrators, led by the group’s leader, Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma, challenged Nigerian immigrants living in Sunnyside, a suburb of Pretoria, to explain why the area is popularly known as “Little Lagos”.

Ngobese-Zuma questioned how the neighbourhood acquired the nickname, calling on Nigerians living in the area to come forward and explain their presence.

“I’m being told here that we’ve entered Sunnyside, the home of Nigerians. I’m inviting Nigerians to come out let’s talk to each other. We want to know who gave you this place and called it Nigeria. Who gave you permission to call this place Lagos or whatever you call it?” Ngobese-Zuma asked.

The protest reflects renewed tensions surrounding immigration and the presence of foreign nationals in South Africa, particularly Nigerians living in areas with significant immigrant communities.

“Who called you here and gave you permission to call our country Lagos?”

Xolani Zuma, March and March legal representative, called for an entry ban on Nigerians.

“The state must ban Nigerians from South Africa. They must ban Nigerians until they stop selling drugs to our people. The rest of Africa we are fine, but we do not want Nigerians in South Africa anymore, that is what we are saying,” Zuma said.

Ngobese-Zuma also demanded South Africa’s withdrawal from the 1951 Convention relating to the status of refugees.

The core principle of the 1951 UN Convention is non-refoulement, which asserts that a refugee should not be returned to a country where they face serious threats to their life or freedom.

Ngobese-Zuma described the treaty as “not sustainable and not feasible”, saying migrants place additional pressure on public resources and fuel frustration among South African citizens.

She said the demonstrators were marching to the Home Office to place their demands.

The protests follow a period of heightened diplomatic tensions between Nigeria and South Africa.

Just last week, the Nigerian high commission and South African presidency traded words over the exclusion of Femi Fani-Kayode’s speech during his presentation of credentials as high commissioner.

The high commissioner described the omission as disrespectful to Nigeria but said the incident had been put behind following President Cyril Ramaphosa’s intervention, and an invitation from the department of international relations and cooperation (DIRCO) over the row.

Fani-Kayode said from the time he arrived in South Africa, he began to look into some of the issues that concern the Nigerian community.

He described those responsible for xenophobic attacks in South Africa as a “tiny minority”, saying they do not represent the majority of South Africans, whom he characterised as decent and accommodating people.

Over 1,500 Nigerians were repatriated from South Africa this year over xenophobic attacks that left at least four Nigerians dead.

Fani-Kayode has said Nigeria will not sever ties with South Africa but warned that patience was growing thin within the corridors of power.

title: Video: Fresh protest hits South Africa as demonstrators demand ban on Nigerians
description:
By Ayobami Okerinde



A fresh anti-Nigerian protest has erupted in South Africa, with demonstrators in Pretoria demanding that the government close its borders to Nigerian nationals and prohibit their entry into the country.



The demonstration, organised by the March and March movement on Wednesd
content:
By Ayobami Okerinde

A fresh anti-Nigerian protest has erupted in South Africa, with demonstrators in Pretoria demanding that the government close its borders to Nigerian nationals and prohibit their entry into the country.

The demonstration, organised by the March and March movement on Wednesday, saw protesters accuse Nigerians of involvement in drug trafficking and worsening social problems in South African communities.

In a video shared by South African broadcaster, Newzroom Afrika, the group’s leader, Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma, was seen leading demonstrators through Sunnyside, a Pretoria suburb with a sizeable Nigerian population, popularly nicknamed ‘Little Lagos’.

Addressing Nigerians in the neighbourhood, Ngobese-Zuma questioned how the area acquired the nickname and challenged residents to explain their presence in the community.

“I am being told here that we’ve entered Sunnyside, the home of Nigerians. I am inviting Nigerians to come out, let’s talk to each other. We want to know who gave you this place and called it Nigeria. Who gave you permission to call this place Lagos or whatever you call it?” she said.

She also described the presence of migrants in the country as unsustainable, alleging that they were putting pressure on public resources and contributing to the difficulties faced by South African citizens.

The group’s legal representative, Xolani Zuma, also called for a blanket ban on Nigerians entering South Africa, accusing them of selling drugs to South Africans.

“The state must ban Nigerians from South Africa. They must ban Nigerians until they stop selling drugs to our people. The rest of Africa, we are fine, but we do not want Nigerians in South Africa anymore. That is what we are saying,” he said.

Speaking in another video, Ngobese-Zuma urged the South African government to withdraw from the 1951 United Nations Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees, arguing that its obligations under the agreement were no longer sustainable.

“We need to get out of it, it’s not sustainable or feasible,” she said.

title: Saudi Arabia agrees to five-year labour reforms — ITUC-Africa
description:
By Victor Ahiuma-Young



The African Regional Organisation of the International Trade Union Confederation (ITUC-Africa) has welcomed a landmark labour rights agreement with Saudi Arabia, describing it as a major breakthrough in efforts to protect migrant workers, particularly thousands of Africans
content:
By Victor Ahiuma-Young

The African Regional Organisation of the International Trade Union Confederation (ITUC-Africa) has welcomed a landmark labour rights agreement with Saudi Arabia, describing it as a major breakthrough in efforts to protect migrant workers, particularly thousands of Africans working in the Kingdom.

The agreement, signed on November 18, 2026, provides a framework for five years of engagement and technical cooperation aimed at addressing longstanding labour rights violations, including forced labour, wage abuses, discrimination and poor working conditions affecting migrant workers.

ITUC-Africa General Secretary, Akhator Joel Odigie, who disclosed this in a statement, said the agreement demonstrated the importance of international solidarity and sustained advocacy in securing workers’ rights.

He said the framework offered an opportunity to improve the welfare and protection of migrant workers through reforms covering fair recruitment, wage protection, access to justice, social protection, occupational safety and health, as well as the rights of domestic workers.

The organisation attributed the development to sustained trade union advocacy and international pressure, recalling that it spearheaded an Article 26 complaint under the Constitution of the International Labour Organisation (ILO) in June 2025, with the support of the International Trade Union Confederation (ITUC).

The complaint, submitted by workers’ delegates to the ILO Governing Body, called for stronger action by the Saudi government to protect migrant workers against exploitation and other forms of abuse.

Odigie said the process initiated by the complaint had culminated in the agreement, describing it as evidence of the importance of trade union solidarity, sustained advocacy and international accountability.

He commended the ITUC, Building and Wood Workers’ International (BWI), the International Domestic Workers Federation (IDWF) and other partners for their contributions to efforts to defend migrant workers’ rights.

However, ITUC-Africa cautioned that the agreement must translate into tangible improvements in workers’ lives rather than remain a formal commitment.

It noted that stronger guarantees for freedom of association and effective worker representation were not adequately captured in the framework.

The organisation stressed that the five-year workplan and monitoring arrangements must ensure measurable progress, particularly in protecting workers from exploitation and ensuring the payment of wages and other entitlements.

“The true measure of this agreement will not be its signatures, but whether workers are safer, wages are paid, rights are respected and justice is accessible,” Odigie said.

ITUC-Africa also called on African governments to strengthen recruitment oversight, improve consular protection for their citizens abroad and establish enforceable bilateral labour agreements with Saudi Arabia.

It urged the Saudi government to demonstrate genuine commitment to the agreement through credible reforms and effective enforcement, insisting that migrant workers and their representatives must have meaningful roles in the implementation process.

The organisation reaffirmed its commitment to supporting the implementation of the framework and ensuring that African migrant workers benefit from the promised reforms.

It maintained that sustained monitoring, accountability and continued dialogue would be necessary to ensure that the agreement delivers lasting improvements in labour conditions and protects the rights and dignity of migrant workers.

The post Saudi Arabia agrees to five-year labour reforms — ITUC-Africa appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: EPL: Pochettino vows to make Man Utd ‘brave’ against Liverpool
description:
New Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has promised to make the club competitive again, insisting his side will approach Sunday’s Premier League clash against Liverpool at Anfield without fear.
Pochettino made the promise in his first interview after taking charge of the Old Trafford c
content:
New Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has promised to make the club competitive again, insisting his side will approach Sunday’s Premier League clash against Liverpool at Anfield without fear.

Pochettino made the promise in his first interview after taking charge of the Old Trafford club on Wednesday, saying he was eager to begin work despite arriving just hours after leaving his position as manager of the United States national team.

In the video interview posted on the club’s YouTube page on Thursday, the Argentine described his appointment as a privilege and a huge responsibility, adding that he was determined to prepare the team for the difficult trip to Anfield.

“It’s an opportunity, and it’s a privilege to be head coach of Manchester United, and I think we cannot waste time. We need to be ready to compete on Sunday,” he said.

He added, “We need to be ready and prepare everything to be sure that we are going to compete in the best condition at Anfield.”

Pochettino acknowledged the challenge of taking over at United but said his immediate priority was to create an environment where players could express themselves and perform without being overwhelmed by pressure.

“We need to see the potential of this club. Of course, circumstances are circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances.

“But at the same time, we need to understand that it’s a game. The players need to express their talent, and we need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform,” he said.

The former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea manager said he wanted to establish a strong team culture built around unity, trust and shared responsibility.

“The culture, to create the culture, is the most important. To have the culture, create the habits and the principles. We need to look forward and find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us close to winning every single game,” he said.

He also called for unity among the players, coaching staff, club management and supporters, saying everyone must work together to restore the club’s winning mentality.

“We need to be united because, in the end, we are Manchester United. We need to create our own philosophy and have genuine and very natural leadership,” Pochettino said.

On his assessment of the squad, the 54-year-old said he was satisfied with the players available and would focus on helping them fulfil their potential.

“We need to love the players that we have. We need to support the players and provide all the tools for their performance,” he said.

Turning to Sunday’s meeting with Liverpool, Pochettino acknowledged the significance of the fixture but insisted United would travel to Anfield with the ambition of securing victory.

“I know very well what that game means and how important it is. I think we know very well that it’s going to be a tough game, but at the same time, we believe in our way.

“We are going to go there, to Anfield, with the idea to win, be brave and be Manchester United,” he said.

He added that his players must approach the encounter with confidence and without fear, despite facing a strong Liverpool side.

“We need to make sure that we are brave and we are protagonists, and go there with no fear and challenge a very good team like Liverpool,” he said.

Pochettino also recalled his admiration for United, dating back to the club’s dramatic 2-1 victory over Bayern Munich in the 1999 Champions League final in Barcelona.

He said he watched the match while playing for Espanyol and was impressed by the team’s performance and late comeback.

“That was an amazing game, and then what happened in the end, it’s impossible not to emphasise that team,” he said.

The coach also spoke of his admiration for former United manager Sir Alex Ferguson, whom he described as the best coach in the history of the sport.

Pochettino said he wanted to help supporters regain the feeling of watching a team capable of winning consistently, adding that the responsibility for delivering that ambition rested with him and his players.

“We are here to try to do everything to recover that feeling about winning and be in a place that you deserve to be,” he said.

The post EPL: Pochettino vows to make Man Utd ‘brave’ against Liverpool appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: WPRF 2026: Green celebrates Davido’s sacrifice, hails him as Africa’s ambassador
description:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja
President and Chief Executive Officer of the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management Justin Green, has praised Nigerian Afrobeats superstar, David Adeleke, popularly known as Davido, for cutting short his stay in the United States to retur
content:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

President and Chief Executive Officer of the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management Justin Green, has praised Nigerian Afrobeats superstar, David Adeleke, popularly known as Davido, for cutting short his stay in the United States to return to Nigeria and perform at the international conference.

Green who is also the global host of the World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) Abuja 2026, described the singer’s decision as an exceptional demonstration of patriotism and ambassadorial spirit, saying his global influence and commitment to projecting a positive image of Nigeria and Africa made him a worthy ambassador of the continent.

Davido thrilled delegates, dignitaries and other guests with a live performance at the forum, bringing Afrobeats energy to the international gathering Wednesday night and adding entertainment to the celebration of African identity and culture.

Green spoke on the fourth day of the forum, tagged African Day, with the theme, “Africa, the Voice of the World: Communication for Peace, Democracy and Development”.

The conference is jointly organised by the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management, the African Public Relations Association (APRA), the continental host, and the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR), the national host.

Recounting how Davido agreed to perform at the international gathering, Green said he had publicly appealed to the singer during a television interview ahead of the conference, expressing his desire to have him perform at the event.

He said the television presenters laughed off the suggestion, believing it was impossible to secure the international music star’s participation.

However, Green said the appeal eventually reached Davido, who was in New York at the time.

According to him, during a visit to the Nigeria Customs Service, he was handed a telephone and informed that someone wanted to speak with him. To his surprise, it was Davido calling from New York.

Green said the singer, who was woken at about 5am because of the time difference, immediately asked which day he was expected to perform.

He said Davido subsequently changed his travel plans, returned to Nigeria and flew from Lagos to Abuja, arriving the previous night before heading straight to the conference.

“He was supposed to still be in New York. He agreed to fly back. He flew back, and he flew from Lagos to here. And he agreed to do it. And he landed last night, came straight here to do it,” Green said.

Commending the gesture, Green said Davido’s willingness to sacrifice his personal schedule to support the conference reflected the Nigerian spirit and his commitment to contributing to the country’s international image.

“That is the type of Nigerian spirit that we keep talking about. He wanted to contribute in a way to make this event and to show the world,” he said.

Green described Davido as a huge ambassador not only for Nigeria but for the entire African continent, noting that the singer’s international achievements and the image he projects wherever he goes have made him an influential voice for Africa globally.

“Everywhere he goes, he puts out a great image of Africa. And what he has achieved worldwide is enormous. And he’s a great, great ambassador for the African continent,” he said.

The African Day celebrations also featured a colourful parade by 54 children representing the 54 African countries, each carrying the flag of a country to showcase the continent’s diversity, identity and unity.

The forum’s Head of Protocol and member of the National Planning Committee, Aisha Gambari, said the children were demonstrating the pride Africans have in their continent, while urging participants to celebrate their shared African identity.

The parade, which featured the playing of the Global Alliance anthem, formed part of activities marking African Day and reinforced the forum’s focus on projecting Africa’s voice, heritage and identity to the world.

The WPRF Abuja 2026 has brought together public relations practitioners, policymakers, business leaders and other stakeholders from across the world to examine the role of strategic communication in advancing peace, democracy and development.

title: Super Eagles must improve or miss 2027 AFCON – Jo Bonfere
description:
Former Super Eagles coach, Jo Bonfrere, has warned that Nigeria could miss out on the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations if the team fails to improve its performance in the remaining qualifying matches.



Bonfrere gave the warning following Nigeria’s goalless draw against Tanzania’s Taifa Stars in Zanzibar
content:
Former Super Eagles coach, Jo Bonfrere, has warned that Nigeria could miss out on the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations if the team fails to improve its performance in the remaining qualifying matches.

Bonfrere gave the warning following Nigeria’s goalless draw against Tanzania’s Taifa Stars in Zanzibar on Tuesday, a result he described as a setback to the country’s qualification campaign.

The result left the three-time African champions second in Group L with seven points from four matches, three points behind leaders Guinea-Bissau, who defeated Madagascar 2-0 in Bissau.

With only group winners guaranteed qualification for the tournament, the former coach said Nigeria must win their remaining fixtures to avoid putting their AFCON hopes in jeopardy.

Speaking to Complete Sports, Bonfrere said the Super Eagles missed an opportunity to close the gap on Guinea-Bissau with a victory in Zanzibar.

“It’s a poor result for the Super Eagles,” he said.

“The Super Eagles should have done better. A win would have bridged the gap with Guinea-Bissau. But with this result, they will have to work hard in their two remaining games or risk seeing their 2027 AFCON ambition fade,” the 80-year-old said.

Bonfrere, who led Nigeria’s U-23 team to football gold at the 1996 Olympic Games in Atlanta, Georgia, also expressed concern over the team’s scoring record in the qualifiers.

Nigeria have scored five goals and conceded the same number in four Group L matches, a record the Dutch tactician said was below expectations, considering the quality of players available to the country.

He argued that the Super Eagles should be scoring more goals, given that several members of the squad feature for top European clubs.

“You score goals, you win games. If you don’t score, you don’t win. The Super Eagles have good players in top European teams. They have more experience than any other team in Africa. So, they must score goals,” he said.

Comparing Nigeria’s performance with that of Guinea-Bissau, Bonfrere noted that the group leaders had scored eight goals and conceded just one in their four matches.

“You said Guinea-Bissau have scored eight goals and conceded one. That’s good for them. That’s what the Super Eagles should be doing, and even more, because Nigeria have quality players,” he added.

Nigeria will return to action in March 2027 when they travel to face Madagascar in their Matchday Five encounter, while Guinea-Bissau host Tanzania.

The Super Eagles will then conclude their qualifying campaign against Guinea-Bissau at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, on March 28.

Both fixtures are crucial to Nigeria’s chances of securing a place at the 2027 AFCON.

The post Super Eagles must improve or miss 2027 AFCON – Jo Bonfere appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: Police arrest four over robbery at Kwara varsity hostels
description:
The Kwara State Police Command has arrested four suspected armed robbers in connection with attacks on student hostels at Al-Hikmah University in the Adewole area of Ilorin.
The arrests followed a stop-and-search operation by operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit in the NASFAT area of Eyenko
content:
The Kwara State Police Command has arrested four suspected armed robbers in connection with attacks on student hostels at Al-Hikmah University in the Adewole area of Ilorin.

The arrests followed a stop-and-search operation by operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit in the NASFAT area of Eyenkorin.

During the search, eight mobile phones and a laptop suspected to have been stolen were recovered.

The Police Public Relations Officer, Adetoun Ejire-Adeyemi, disclosed this in a statement issued on Thursday, a copy of which was obtained by The PUNCH in Ilorin.

According to the statement, the operation began at about 6am on November 15, 2026, when VCRU operatives intercepted a commercial bus travelling to Ibadan during a routine patrol.

It reads, “A search of the vehicle led to the recovery of eight mobile phones and a laptop from two passengers who could not satisfactorily explain how they came into possession of the items.

“The two passengers, identified as Abdulahi Olamilekan, 20, and Jimoh Abdulfatai, 28, from the Apete area of Ibadan, Oyo State, were subsequently arrested after one of them allegedly attempted to escape during questioning.

“However, the investigation took a different turn when an officer answered an incoming call on one of the recovered phones.

“The caller reported that four armed men had robbed students at Al-Hikmah University hostels in the Adewole area of Ilorin overnight.”

The police said six students affected by the robbery subsequently gave statements to investigators, while the two arrested passengers allegedly admitted participating in the attack.

The suspects told investigators that the firearm used during the operation was in the possession of their accomplices.

“Acting on information obtained during the investigation, VCRU personnel arrested Abdulahi Bashir, 29, and Tunji Abel, 26, at separate locations in Ilorin,” the statement added.

The police said two locally made pistols and one cartridge were recovered during the subsequent operation that led to the arrest of the two additional suspects.

It added that the suspects arrested in Ilorin admitted involvement in two previous robberies at the university hostels and also provided accounts of other robbery incidents within the state.

“Investigators are verifying those accounts,” the statement said, adding that all four suspects remained in police custody.

The Commissioner of Police, Ojo Adekimi, assured residents of the command’s commitment to protecting lives and property.

He also reiterated the command’s resolve to strengthen public confidence through professional policing and closer cooperation with communities, in line with the vision of the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu.

The latest incident is not the first reported robbery involving students of the university.

In April 2019, two Al-Hikmah University students reportedly told the police that a man armed with a knife broke into their hostel in Ilorin, stole two mobile phones and threatened them.

A suspect was subsequently arrested and remanded by a court.

title: Unionism not a licence for irresponsibility, Wike’s aide slams UniAbuja staff
description:
…Says varsity used only 1,426.67 hectares in 38 yrs



By Omeiza Ajayi



ABUJA: Lere Olayinka, Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media to the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has told staff of the University of Abuja that “unionism and activism
content:
…Says varsity used only 1,426.67 hectares in 38 yrs

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: Lere Olayinka, Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media to the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has told staff of the University of Abuja that “unionism and activism should not be a licence for reckless advertisement of irresponsible behaviour” as they agitate over the reduction of the institution’s land from 11,824.04 hectares to 4,685 hectares.

In a statement on Thursday in Abuja, Olayinka described the utterances of the union leaders, especially the chairman of the Academic Staff Union of Universities ASUU at the university, Professor Sylvanus Ugoh, as unbecoming of people operating in an academic environment.

Olayinka said after existing for 38 years, the university had used a fraction of its land.

“Most importantly, after existing for 38 years, UNIABUJA has only utilized 1,426.67 hectares of land, with 49.56 hectares used for staff quarters. What then is the need for over 11,000 hectares of land when less than 1,500 hectares was utilized in 38 years?” he asked.

He dismissed the claim by the Joint Action Committee (JAC), which is seeking a reversal of the reduction, that the Minister forged the 2016 report of the Joint Committee of the Federal Capital Territory Administration (FCTA) and UNIABUJA on Land and Sundry Issues. The committee was set up by the then FCT Minister, Mohamed Musa Bello.

Olayinka called the allegation recklessness and irresponsibility taken too far.

“It is therefore strange that supposed academia will hide under an unknown Joint Action Committee to insult the person of the FCT Minister and accuse him of forging official documents of the government arising from a committee duly set up by his predecessor,” he said.

He added that apart from the 2016 committee, another one was set up on December 17, 2020, following the university management’s visit to the FCT Minister on October 13, 2020.

According to him, part of the recommendations of the December 2020 committee read: “Based on the recommended size of 100Ha for a University Campus stipulated by the National University Commission and considering that the University has held the title of about 11,608.33Ha for over thirty (30) years, a total of about 1,922.66Ha should be left to the University while the remaining part of the land should be designed and detailed by URP (Urban and Regional Planning) Department for compatible land use like Institution and Research Districts.”

The recommendation went on: “This will solve the issues of continuous and unabated village expansion which will save the FCTA the unending trouble of village encroachments and the cost of removing them.”

Olayinka said the issues the university presented to the 2016 committee included the issuance of Certificate of Occupancy for its main and mini campuses and its properties in Kado and Jahi districts. Others were Area Council layout within its campuses, indigenous and illegal settlements within the main campus land, and re-issuance of the title document of the mini campus, which got burnt during the 1994 students uprising.

He said the December 2020 committee, which visited the university and other settlements within the over 11,000 hectares, “found that 805.7 hectares of the land had been occupied by villages while the Nigerian Army Welfare Limited Guarantee Housing Estate occupied 9.91 hectares.”

“Also, about 500 hectares had already been approved for a main sewage treatment plant,” he said.

On the Minister’s powers, Olayinka said: “In exercising his powers under the Land Use Act No. 6 of 1978, Capital. L5, Laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 2004, the FCT Minister does not even require any committee report. It is also not the duty of any workers union to be involved in the allocation of land to a university by the government, most importantly, a university owned by the government.

“Government established a university, gave land to it and later saw the need to reduce the land to what it opined can be better managed and utilized by the university, workers unions with primary responsibility of welfare of its members are protesting. What exactly is their business? Were they consulted before the university was established and the land allocated in the first place? Of what effect is land occupied by university to its workers and students?

“The university is owned by the government. The land is owned by the government. The meddlesome interlopers acting under this Joint Action Committee are workers and students employed or admitted by the university. When did it become the responsibility of an employee to fight an employer for choosing to reduce the land occupied by his own establishment?

“Meanwhile, some of these union leaders have their children in private universities in Nigeria. How many of those private universities are built on more than 100 hectares of land?” he asked.

While insisting that the protest was misplaced, he described as funny and strange a situation where university union leaders protest over land issues when other universities in the world are already operating virtually.

“And if the land is so needed by the university, why did it allocate part of it to individuals and corporate organization, including the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission?” he queried.

The post Unionism not a licence for irresponsibility, Wike’s aide slams UniAbuja staff appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: 2027: ADC Leaders are lazy, entitled politicians – NDC campaign DG
description:
The Director-General of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) National Campaign Council, Ibrahim Abdulkareem, has described some leaders of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) as lazy and entitled politicians over their handling of opposition coalition talks ahead of the 2027 general elections.
Ab
content:
The Director-General of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) National Campaign Council, Ibrahim Abdulkareem, has described some leaders of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) as lazy and entitled politicians over their handling of opposition coalition talks ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Abdulkareem accused the ADC leadership of failing to establish clear arrangements on power-sharing, zoning and the choice of a presidential candidate before inviting other politicians to join the proposed coalition.

He made the remarks on Wednesday while appearing on Prime Time, a programme on Arise Television.

The NDC chieftain argued that the ADC should have adopted the approach used by the All Progressives Congress (APC) during its formation in 2013 by agreeing on key political arrangements and documenting them before bringing other politicians into the alliance.

According to him, the failure to establish such agreements from the beginning has created disagreements over who should emerge as the coalition’s presidential candidate and how political positions should be distributed.

“I used to term some of the people I see in ADC as lazy politicians,” Abdulkareem said.

He questioned why the ADC began inviting politicians into its coalition without first deciding its leadership structure, presidential candidate and zoning arrangements.

The NDC campaign director also criticised suggestions that former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi should accept a vice-presidential position under former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar.

He described the proposal as an indication of the disagreements arising from the absence of clearly defined terms within the coalition.

“Immediately we started this thing, they started to say Peter Obi is a vice-presidential candidate to Atiku. What kind of coalition is that? The entitlement from the elite, I find it very annoying sometimes,” he said.

Abdulkareem further faulted what he described as attempts by some northern political figures to determine the direction of the opposition coalition based on regional considerations.

He questioned the argument that the North should automatically retain the presidency, citing the country’s political history under former military Head of State Ibrahim Babangida and former President Muhammadu Buhari.

“You just decide the North. Which North? You talk like you own something. There is no right given to Atiku, for example, to say everybody must surrender,” he stated.

He argued that Nigeria’s political leadership should be determined by considerations such as integrity, accountability and the ability to manage public resources effectively, rather than ethnic, religious or regional affiliations.

The NDC chieftain also criticised established politicians who, according to him, believe their political experience or influence entitles them to leadership positions despite the country’s development challenges.

Meanwhile, Abdulkareem clarified that the NDC was not opposed to an opposition coalition ahead of the 2027 elections but insisted that such an arrangement must be properly structured.

He maintained that opposition parties and politicians could work together without necessarily adopting the ADC as their political platform.

He also suggested that the NDC could provide an alternative platform for opposition collaboration, mentioning the possibility of a joint presidential ticket involving Peter Obi and former Kano State Governor Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso.

His comments come amid ongoing political realignments among opposition figures seeking to challenge President Bola Tinubu and the ruling APC in the 2027 general elections.

The post 2027: ADC Leaders are lazy, entitled politicians – NDC campaign DG appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: AI being run in a ‘mediaeval’ way –  UN
description:
Artificial intelligence is being governed in an almost mediaeval fashion, the UN rights chief warned Thursday, with power concentrated in the hands of a few tech barons.



Speaking at the RightsX summit in Geneva, Volker Turk said that while the story of AI sounded futuristic, underneath it was an
content:
Artificial intelligence is being governed in an almost mediaeval fashion, the UN rights chief warned Thursday, with power concentrated in the hands of a few tech barons.

Speaking at the RightsX summit in Geneva, Volker Turk said that while the story of AI sounded futuristic, underneath it was an age-old narrative of power.

“A handful of men still control much of the world’s AI computing power, data and infrastructure. And we still have no common rules to pace or steer AI development,” he said.

Turk said there was a glaring democratic deficit when five technology companies owned more than 70 percent of global AI computing capacity.

“We have the technology of the future governed in an almost mediaeval way: by a select few, with virtually no checks, no balances, no participation, and no accountability,” he said.

“History has taught us: with this kind of power, the rights and freedoms of ordinary people are the first to suffer.”

Reiterating his call for rights-centred AI regulation, the UN high commissioner for human rights said the technology was increasingly controlling people’s lives.

And this, he warned, was often happening without their knowledge, and could distort public debate in “subtle, insidious ways”.

Meanwhile biased algorithms could reproduce injustice on an industrial scale, he cautioned.

– ‘Civilisational collapse’ –

“Our transport, food and healthcare are increasingly digitised. We may not be far from the day when AI can cut off the critical infrastructure of entire communities or countries, either on its own or in the wrong hands,” Turk warned.

“When people discuss the chances of civilisational collapse because of AI, we need to ask: who decides what chances we take?”

He voiced optimism that people would ultimately challenge unchecked power, with the democratic deficit turning into a deficit of trust.

He cited young people already stepping offline to regain greater control of their lives.

Turk said AI’s benefits should be shared equitably, which would require goodwill from technology companies, but also regulation and accountability.

He said he had written to frontier AI companies urging them to introduce effective safeguards “before it is too late”.

Turk noted that a bottle of milk could not make it to a shop without layers of testing, rules and regulations.

So for AI, “it’s a no-brainer that you need some form of regulation”, given its potential for harm, Turk said.

As for how models are trained, he suggested giving the Universal Declaration of Human Rights “as the task to AI”.

title: Court Dismisses Suit Challenging Emergence Of Abubakar Bawa As Taraba APC Chairman
description: A Federal High Court sitting in Jalingo, Taraba State Capital, has dismissed the suit filed by Alhaji Abdulhadi Haruna Lau against the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Taraba State Chairman of the party, Alhaji Abubakar Bawa, challenging the APC Congress in Taraba State conducted on March 3,
content:
A Federal High Court sitting in Jalingo, Taraba State Capital, has dismissed the suit filed by Alhaji Abdulhadi Haruna Lau against the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Taraba State Chairman of the party, Alhaji Abubakar Bawa, challenging the APC Congress in Taraba State conducted on March 3, 2026.

The court, presided over by Justice Mashkur Salisu in his ruling after hearing the arguments presented by the parties involved, upheld the preliminary objections raised by the respondents.

The court held that the plaintiff did not exhaust all internal dispute resolution mechanisms of the party before approaching the court, as required by the party’s constitution.

The court further held that the plaintiff was not an up-to-date member of the party in terms of payment of party dues, and therefore lacked the locus standi to institute the suit.

The court also held that it lacked jurisdiction to entertain the matter by virtue of Section 83(5) of the APC Constitution.

Having upheld the preliminary objections, the judge noted that he could have stopped there. However, in line with the directive of the Supreme Court that trial courts should also determine the substantive suit, he proceeded to deliver judgment on the merits of the case.

In the substantive suit, the court found in favour of the defendants on all issues and dismissed the case in its entirety.

The court awarded the sum of N1 million each in favour of the 1st Defendant, the APC, and the 2nd Defendant, Alhaji Abubakar Bawa, as costs.

Reacting to the judgement, the Taraba State APC chairman, Abubakar Bawa, described the judgment as the will of the people of the state, insisting that the court has done the right thing at the right time.

He appealed to the appellant to reconsider his stand of going to the appeal court and consider the unity of the party for its progress.

title: ‘Ban Nigerians from our country’: South African protesters issue fresh demand
description:
A group of anti-immigrant protesters in South Africa has called on the government to ban Nigerians from entering the country, accusing them of contributing to drug-related problems.
The demonstrators, led by the March and March group, staged a protest in Pretoria on Wednesday, where they demanded th
content:
A group of anti-immigrant protesters in South Africa has called on the government to ban Nigerians from entering the country, accusing them of contributing to drug-related problems.

The demonstrators, led by the March and March group, staged a protest in Pretoria on Wednesday, where they demanded that Nigerian immigrants be barred from the country.

The group’s leader, Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma, also questioned the growing Nigerian presence in Sunnyside, a suburb of Pretoria often referred to as “Little Lagos” because of its Nigerian community.

She challenged Nigerians living in the area to explain why it had acquired the nickname.

“I’m being told here that we’ve entered Sunnyside, the home of Nigerians. I’m inviting Nigerians to come out let’s talk to each other.

“We want to know who gave you this place and called it Nigeria. Who gave you permission to call this place Lagos or whatever you call it?” she said.

The group’s legal representative, Xolani Zuma, called on the South African government to stop Nigerians from entering the country.

“The state must ban Nigerians from South Africa. They must ban Nigerians until they stop selling drugs to our people.

“The rest of Africa we are fine, but we do not want Nigerians in South Africa anymore, that is what we are saying,” he said.

The protesters also want South Africa to withdraw from the 1951 United Nations Convention relating to the Status of Refugees.

Ngobese-Zuma described the agreement as “not sustainable and not feasible”, arguing that migrants put pressure on public resources and contribute to frustration among South African citizens.

She said the protesters were heading to the Home Office to present their demands.

The demonstration comes amid fresh diplomatic tension between Nigeria and South Africa following a disagreement over the exclusion of a speech by Nigeria’s High Commissioner, Femi Fani-Kayode, during his presentation of credentials.

Fani-Kayode had described the omission as disrespectful to Nigeria. However, he later said the issue had been resolved after the intervention of South African President Cyril Ramaphosa and an invitation from the Department of International Relations and Cooperation.

Since assuming office, the Nigerian envoy has said he has been looking into issues affecting Nigerians living in South Africa.

He has also described those responsible for xenophobic attacks as a small minority, insisting that they do not represent the majority of South Africans.

More than 1,500 Nigerians have reportedly been repatriated from South Africa this year following xenophobic attacks that left at least four Nigerians dead.

Although Fani-Kayode has ruled out Nigeria severing diplomatic relations with South Africa, he warned that patience within the Nigerian government was running thin.

The post ‘Ban Nigerians from our country’: South African protesters issue fresh demand appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

As reported by football transfer expert Fabrizio Romano on X on Thursday, speaking on the Ukrainian podcast Guest of Gordon, the winger said Alonso was direct with him before he j
content:
Mykhailo Mudryk has revealed that Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso personally told him to leave the club on loan this summer.

As reported by football transfer expert Fabrizio Romano on X on Thursday, speaking on the Ukrainian podcast Guest of Gordon, the winger said Alonso was direct with him before he joined Tottenham.

“Xabi Alonso told me straight to my face: ‘You’d better go, play, get some game time, and then come back to Chelsea,’” Mudryk explained. “Xabi also added: ‘I’m counting on you.’”

Mudryk returned to Chelsea in the summer after serving a doping ban. Alonso, who had just taken charge, felt the Ukrainian needed regular minutes to rebuild after a long absence from competitive football.

Several Premier League clubs showed interest, including Brighton, Brentford and Leeds. Mudryk ultimately chose Tottenham on Deadline Day, reuniting with former Shakhtar Donetsk coach Roberto De Zerbi.

He has made only one appearance so far for Spurs after suffering an ankle injury in training. He is expected to return to action this weekend.

title: Ohaji youths block Owerri-Port Harcourt highway over bad roads
description:
By Chidi Nkwopara



OWERRI — Vehicular traffic on the busy Owerri-Port Harcourt federal highway was brought to a halt for several hours on Wednesday as youths from Ohaji communities in Imo State protested against the deplorable condition of roads in the area.







The protesters, who blocked the
content:
By Chidi Nkwopara

OWERRI — Vehicular traffic on the busy Owerri-Port Harcourt federal highway was brought to a halt for several hours on Wednesday as youths from Ohaji communities in Imo State protested against the deplorable condition of roads in the area.

The protesters, who blocked the highway before 7am, demanded urgent government intervention to rehabilitate and reconstruct roads across Ohaji, lamenting that years of neglect had subjected residents to hardship.

Although the demonstration was largely peaceful, with no reported destruction of property, the protesters expressed anger over what they described as repeated government neglect and unfulfilled promises.

One of the protesters, who identified himself simply as Uche, said the blockade was intended to draw the government’s attention to the poor state of roads in their communities.

“We decided to block this road before 7am today (yesterday), so that government will know that we are not happy.

“We have been suffering untold hardship in our different communities as a result of the extremely bad roads in the entire Ohaji.

“All the past attempts made to draw government’s attention to the roads in our area failed woefully. All we got in response were unfulfilled promises,” he said.

Uche described Ohaji and Egbema as major contributors to Imo State’s economy because of their oil deposits, lamenting that poor road infrastructure had undermined the economic potential of the area.

Another protester, Sunday Nwali, said residents felt abandoned by the government despite the economic contributions of their communities.

He called on the government to declare a state of emergency on roads in Ohaji and immediately commence rehabilitation or reconstruction work.

“We want the government to, as a matter of utmost urgency, not only declare a state of emergency on all the roads in Ohaji, but also commence rehabilitation or reconstruction work on our roads.

“We cannot understand why our roads have remained hopeless, while some other parts of the state are enjoying good roads. Are taxes not collected from our people?” he asked.

Nwali, who described residents as predominantly farmers, said the poor road network had made it difficult to transport agricultural produce to urban markets because of high transportation costs.

He expressed hope that the protest would prompt the government to address their demands.

When contacted, the Imo State Police Command’s Public Relations Officer, Henry Okoye, confirmed the protest.

He said the police had engaged the protesters, who agreed to reopen the highway.

“The Imo State Police Command is on top of the situation. We have engaged with the protesters, and they have agreed to reopen the road,” Okoye said.

The post Ohaji youths block Owerri-Port Harcourt highway over bad roads appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: N100m Housing Loans: What Nigerians need to know about Tinubu’s mortgage scheme
description:
President Bola Tinubu has announced that eligible Nigerians can access mortgage loans of up to N100 million, with repayment periods of up to 20 years, under the Federal Government’s housing finance initiative.
The programme is aimed at expanding access to affordable housing and addressing Nigeria’s
content:
President Bola Tinubu has announced that eligible Nigerians can access mortgage loans of up to N100 million, with repayment periods of up to 20 years, under the Federal Government’s housing finance initiative.

The programme is aimed at expanding access to affordable housing and addressing Nigeria’s housing deficit, estimated at about 15 million units.

According to details published by Daily Trust, the facility operates under the N1 trillion MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund (MREIF), which provides long-term mortgage financing at a fixed annual interest rate of 9.75 per cent.

Beneficiaries are required to make an initial deposit of 10 per cent of the property’s value, while the remaining balance can be repaid over a period of up to 20 years.

Tinubu announced the initiative in a statement on his verified X account on Tuesday, explaining that it was designed to make homeownership more accessible to Nigerians who cannot afford to pay for houses outright.

Using a N10 million property as an example, the President said a prospective homeowner would be required to pay an initial deposit of N1 million, with monthly repayments of approximately N85,400 over 20 years.

He disclosed that more than 2,300 Nigerians across 27 states had accessed a combined N160 billion in mortgage financing through MREIF.

Tinubu said the scheme was intended to address the challenges Nigerians face in securing affordable accommodation and long-term housing finance.

He added that eligible citizens could apply regardless of their location or social status, stressing that access to the programme should not depend on political or personal connections.

“You should not need to know a minister, a governor or anybody in the Presidential Villa to apply and benefit from these opportunities,” he said.

The President also identified the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN) as another source of housing finance, saying eligible Nigerians could access loans of up to N50 million at an interest rate of six per cent, with repayment periods extending to 30 years.

He further explained that contributors to the Contributory Pension Scheme could use up to 25 per cent of their Retirement Savings Account funds towards an initial mortgage deposit, subject to applicable regulations.

Married applicants may also apply jointly with their spouses to improve their eligibility for higher loan amounts.

For Nigerians unable to afford mortgage financing, Tinubu said the government was implementing other housing interventions through the Family Homes Fund and the Renewed Hope Social Housing Programme.

He said the Family Homes Fund had delivered more than 53 social housing units for vulnerable and underserved households, while the Renewed Hope Social Housing Programme was targeting 77,400 affordable homes across the country.

The President also disclosed that 100 free houses had been provided to widows in Kaduna State, while another 50 were delivered to wives of fallen military personnel in Ibadan, Oyo State.

Additionally, more than 15,000 housing units are under construction under the Renewed Hope Cities and Estates Programme.

Reacting to the initiative, real estate expert, ESV Olufemi Oyedele, said the MREIF scheme had been available to Nigerians since 2025 at an interest rate of 9.75 per cent.

He said the initiative was first announced in December 2024 and could help qualified Nigerians become homeowners rather than remain tenants throughout their lives.

Oyedele added that the N1 trillion fund had the potential to ease the country’s housing challenges if more eligible Nigerians accessed the facility.

The post N100m Housing Loans: What Nigerians need to know about Tinubu’s mortgage scheme appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Diallo, Tashima challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency
description:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino is set to face his first electoral challenge after the global football governing body announced two candidates seeking to contest his bid for a fourth term in office.
The candidates are Philippe Diallo, president of the French Football Federation, and Kohzo Tashima, f
content:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino is set to face his first electoral challenge after the global football governing body announced two candidates seeking to contest his bid for a fourth term in office.

The candidates are Philippe Diallo, president of the French Football Federation, and Kohzo Tashima, former head of the Japan Football Association.

FIFA announced their candidacies in a statement on Thursday, ahead of its 77th Congress scheduled for March 18, 2027, when the election will take place.

Infantino, who has been FIFA president since 2016, was returned unopposed in the 2019 and 2023 elections.

Diallo, 63, announced his intention to contest the presidency on Monday and has the backing of UEFA member associations, while Tashima is expected to draw support from the East Asian voting bloc. He has also served on FIFA’s executive council.

Infantino, however, continues to enjoy strong support among member associations in Africa and the Middle East.

His leadership has faced criticism over an abandoned proposal to sell certain World Cup stakes to private investors, a move that reportedly cost him the support of UEFA and several influential football confederations.

FIFA said the electoral committee would examine the candidates’ submissions before deciding whether to approve their participation in the election.

The 2027 contest will therefore be the first time Infantino faces opposition in his bid to retain the FIFA presidency since securing re-election unopposed in 2019 and 2023.

The post Diallo, Tashima challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: My late father appeared to me, urged me to stand firm – Jimmy Odukoya
description:
The embattled Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, has revealed how his late father, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, appeared to him in a dream during the church’s leadership crisis, urging him not to give in to pressure from members of the Board of Trustees (BoT).
Jimmy disclosed this
content:
The embattled Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, has revealed how his late father, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, appeared to him in a dream during the church’s leadership crisis, urging him not to give in to pressure from members of the Board of Trustees (BoT).

Jimmy disclosed this on Wednesday while addressing about 300 church workers at the church auditorium, where he gave his account of the prolonged disagreement between him and some members of the board.

According to Church Times, which reported the meeting, Jimmy arrived at the church premises in a convoy of about five vehicles, accompanied by security personnel, and addressed the workers at about 6.45pm.

The former Nollywood actor said he turned to fasting and prayers during the crisis, seeking divine direction on how to handle the dispute.

“I took to fasting and praying, asking God to speak to me on the matter. I gave God two options: to speak to me in a dream and to send someone I did not know to give me clarity on the matter.

“In the course of the fasting and prayers, my late father appeared to me in a dream. The message I got from the dream was that I should not succumb to the threats of the Board of Trustees. He told me that they would try to throw dirt on me, but that I would overcome.

“Not long after the dream, I met a pastor who told me that if I did not sack the Board of Trustees, they would continue to give me problems,” he said.

Jimmy said the two experiences strengthened his resolve to stand his ground and subsequently ask members of the board, including his elder sister, to resign.

He, however, said he pleaded with his sister that she could be reconsidered for membership after the church had been given a fresh start, but his sisters rejected the proposal while the board maintained its position.

Explaining the origin of the leadership crisis, Jimmy said disagreements began about a year after he assumed leadership of the church, following concerns raised about his administration.

He claimed that the board later asked him to relinquish his position as chairman while retaining his role as Senior Pastor, a proposal he rejected because he considered it an attempt to undermine his authority.

He also alleged that his two sisters supported the board’s position, claiming that one of them, Tolu, had approached him and asked him to step aside as chairman to enable her to take over the position.

The disagreement reportedly escalated despite the intervention of Bishop Mike Okonkwo, who appealed to Jimmy to relinquish the board chairmanship.

The leadership crisis deepened after some members of the board, following a November 16 meeting, withdrew recognition of Jimmy as Senior Pastor and announced Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader.

The trustees based their decision partly on a video recorded in December 2021 in which the late founder reportedly named Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor, with Jimmy designated as Areogun’s administrative assistant and head of the youth church.

They alleged that the recording was not presented when they considered the succession arrangement that led to Jimmy’s appointment in September 2023, weeks after his father’s death in August of the same year.

The trustees also cited concerns about Jimmy’s remarriage and the public blessing of his marriage, which they said conflicted with the church’s teachings and standards for spiritual leadership.

However, Jimmy’s camp rejected the purported removal, describing it as unconstitutional and insisting that he remained the church’s duly appointed Senior Pastor and chairman of the BoT.

It maintained that his appointment was unanimously approved in September 2023 and alleged that the trustees behind the removal announcement had been asked to resign in March 2026 over alleged violations of the church’s constitution.

The post My late father appeared to me, urged me to stand firm – Jimmy Odukoya appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Kogi Police free 15 kidnap victims after gunfight with terrorists in forest hideout
description:
The Kogi State Police Command has rescued 15 kidnapped victims, including men, women and children, from a kidnappers’ hideout in Magaru Forest, Kakun-Kabba, following a fierce gun battle with the abductors.
The victims were freed in the early hours of Wednesday, November 18, during an intelligence-l
content:
The Kogi State Police Command has rescued 15 kidnapped victims, including men, women and children, from a kidnappers’ hideout in Magaru Forest, Kakun-Kabba, following a fierce gun battle with the abductors.

The victims were freed in the early hours of Wednesday, November 18, during an intelligence-led joint security operation involving police officers, military personnel, forest guards and local security operatives.

The Commissioner of Police in the state, CP Naziru Bello Kankarofi, disclosed this on Thursday while addressing journalists at the Police Headquarters in Lokoja.

Bello Kankarofi said the operation was carried out on his directive, explaining that the security team stormed the forest and engaged the kidnappers in a fierce gun battle before successfully rescuing the victims.

According to him, the superior firepower of the security operatives forced the criminals to retreat, with some of them sustaining varying degrees of gunshot injuries.

He said, “During the operation, the joint team advanced into the forest and engaged the kidnappers in a fierce gun battle. The superior firepower of the security operatives forced the criminals to retreat, with some sustaining varying degrees of gunshot injuries.”

The rescued victims were identified as Okuma Terlum, 47; Ojo Deborah, 23; Samuel Danjuma, three; Faith Raphael, 21; Emmanuella Raphael, three; Donald Tor, 31; Joseph Jonathan, 20; Tergu Joseph, 15; Samuel Joseph, eight; Engr. Joseph Adebija, 58; Lois Abiodun, 50; Chuks Obiakor, 45; Ola Olufemi, 58; Ankpe Godwin, 23; and Kuhwa Solomon, 25.

The police commissioner also disclosed that two other female victims, identified simply as Joy and Nwakan, escaped from their abductors during the initial encounter in which the victims were taken captive.

He further revealed that the security team came under another ambush by members of the criminal gang while conveying the rescued victims out of the forest.

However, he said the operatives successfully repelled the attack and brought all 15 victims out safely.

The victims, who reportedly endured considerable physical and psychological distress during their captivity, were subsequently debriefed and taken to St. John’s Catholic Hospital, Kabba, for medical attention.

Although no arrests had been made as of the time of the briefing, the commissioner said actionable intelligence had been generated, while investigations were ongoing to track down the fleeing kidnappers and identify their sponsors.

He commended the participating security agencies and local security outfits for their courage, resilience and collaboration, assuring residents of the command’s commitment to sustaining coordinated operations against kidnapping and other violent crimes.

The operation involved personnel of the Kabba Area Command, Kabba ‘A’ Division, Iyara Division, Ekerin-Adde Division, Ayetoro-Gbede Division, Violent Crime Response Unit, 70 Police Mobile Force, the Nigerian Army’s 251 Tank Battalion, Forest Guards, Kogi State Vigilante Services, Agbekoya and Kabba Security Outfit.

The commissioner appealed to members of the public to continue providing credible and timely information to security agencies to support efforts to combat criminal activities across the state.

The post Kogi Police free 15 kidnap victims after gunfight with terrorists in forest hideout appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Plateau APC declares support for Tinubu, Mutfwang, rejects Rainbow Coalition
description:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Plateau State has ruled out the possibility of forming a Rainbow Coalition ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring its commitment to securing the re-election of President Bola Tinubu, Governor Caleb Mutfwang and other party candidates.
The state APC Chai
content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Plateau State has ruled out the possibility of forming a Rainbow Coalition ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring its commitment to securing the re-election of President Bola Tinubu, Governor Caleb Mutfwang and other party candidates.

The state APC Chairman, Rufus Bature, said the party was focused on strengthening its political structure and ensuring victory for its candidates in the forthcoming elections.

Bature also warned that the party would not tolerate any form of anti-party activities among its members, stressing that those found guilty would face disciplinary action in line with the APC constitution.

He maintained that no individual was bigger than the party, adding that every member was expected to respect and abide by its rules and regulations.

The APC chairman spoke when the Director-General of the Bola Tinubu/Caleb Mutfwang Campaign Council, Joe Ari, led members of the council on a visit to the party’s state secretariat in Jos.

Bature said the party and the campaign council had learnt from past mistakes and were determined to strengthen their collaboration ahead of the elections.

He said, “It is time to campaign. The last time we went through this, we had hiccups here and there because there was no spirit between the party and the campaign organisation.

“But this time around, we have gone through this and we have seen the mistakes we made, and now I think it is time to correct such mistakes.”

He stressed the need for sustained collaboration between the party and the campaign council, particularly at the grassroots, to ensure effective mobilisation across polling units and local government areas.

“There is every need that this synergy that we are trying to establish be continued so that we take the party to the grassroots.

“We cannot just sit down and say we are a campaign council when we know that there are issues at the grassroots.

“These campaign councils should be reflected in our work, in our polling units and in our local governments so that there is synergy in what we are doing,” he said.

On alleged anti-party activities, Bature said the party was aware of members working against its interests and would take appropriate action in accordance with its constitution.

“The party is aware of certain individuals that are doing anti-party activities. We are governed by laws. We are here as members of the State Executive Committee because the constitution has provided for us to be here. And the constitution has also provided for us to guide us in what activities we are doing.

“Therefore, at the appropriate time, the party will work on those individuals it feels, or has found wanting in one way or the other,” he said.

He added that all members must respect the party’s rules, insisting that nobody was above the organisation.

“We must be governed by laws and we must respect the laws that have created us as a body. Nobody is bigger than the party. All of us are under the party and we are subject to the rules and obligations of the party,” he said.

Dismissing the possibility of a Rainbow Coalition, Bature said the APC would not identify with any political arrangement that did not support the party’s candidates.

“We do not believe in any Rainbow Coalition. You can call it rain gun or whatever, but we do not know that one.

“We do not know any Rainbow. Any APC member that does not do 5.5 is an incipient child of APC. If you are a son of your father and you know that it is APC that gave birth to you, you have to do APC. Any Rainbow Coalition that does not do APC is not part of us,” he said.

Earlier, Ari said the campaign council had developed an action plan for the 2027 general elections, which had been presented to its principals and approved for implementation.

He called on the APC leadership to enforce party discipline, particularly against members involved in anti-party activities, stressing that unity and cooperation were essential to securing victory for the party’s candidates.

The campaign council director-general said the council was committed to working with the party leadership to mobilise support for APC candidates, from the presidential election to the State House of Assembly contests.

The post Plateau APC declares support for Tinubu, Mutfwang, rejects Rainbow Coalition appeared first on Very Nigerian.
