title: Why I regret keeping my father’s successor video – Jimmy Odukoya
description: The Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, has explained why he kept a 2021 video in which his late father, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, identified Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor, despite allegedly being instructed to delete the recording after recovering from surgery
content:
The Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, has explained why he kept a 2021 video in which his late father, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, identified Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor, despite allegedly being instructed to delete the recording after recovering from surgery.

Jimmy gave the explanation on Wednesday while addressing church workers amid the ongoing leadership crisis that has divided the church’s leadership.

The crisis reportedly followed a decision by a faction of the church’s Board of Trustees to withdraw its recognition of Jimmy as the Senior Pastor.

According to Church Times, which reported that its correspondent attended the meeting, Jimmy addressed approximately 300 church workers, explaining his decision to retain the video and the circumstances surrounding the controversy.

Jimmy said the video was recorded in 2021 when his father was preparing to undergo surgery in the United States and feared he might not survive the procedure.

He said, “That was when he asked me to record him where he made the statements about succession. I was the one who recorded the video,” adding that his father’s elder brother, Pastor John Odukoya, was also aware of the recording.

Explaining what happened after the operation, Church Times quoted him as saying, “He said, however, that after the surgery turned out successful, his father asked him to delete the video as it was no longer valid. Rather than delete the video, Jimmy kept it, admitting that it was a grave mistake on his part.”

The publication further reported that he said, “He added that only a handful of people were privy to the video, including his sisters, whom he alleged released it to the public.”

Giving further insight into the leadership dispute, Jimmy said the disagreement with the board started about a year after he assumed office, when members allegedly asked him to relinquish his position as Chairman of the Board of Trustees and concentrate on his pastoral responsibilities.

According to Church Times, he said, “That was a hard pill for him to swallow. He said he sensed that what the board wanted to do was to control him, insisting that he would not allow that to happen.”

The report also quoted him as alleging that his sister, Pastor Tolu Odukoya-Ijogun, had approached him and asked him to step down so she could become the board’s chairman.

Jimmy said the dispute was taken before the General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God, Pastor Enoch Adeboye, following interventions by Bishop Mike Okonkwo.

Recounting the meeting, he said, “When we got to Pastor Adeboye, I was there, and I watched every board member lie against me to my face.”

According to the report, Adeboye allowed him to explain his side of the disagreement before advising the parties to resolve their differences. He also reportedly reminded Jimmy that he had been called to preach the gospel and not to be chairman of the board, warning that if they failed to resolve the disagreement, “it will not be goodbye, it will be bye-bye.”

Related News
He further stated that the board, which included Pastors Kunle Areogun and Rotimi Okpaise, presented him with a seven-point demand, but he only agreed to four of the conditions.

On allegations of financial misconduct, Jimmy denied claims that he embezzled N250m donated to the church for a project.

According to Church Times, he told the workers that the money remained intact, explaining that the project had been delayed because of the economic situation and rising costs, which made its execution difficult.

The report added that he said he had restricted access to church funds and argued that if there had been financial wrongdoing, members of the accounts department would also be culpable.

Jimmy maintained that he remained the Senior Pastor of the church, although he expressed uncertainty about how the next Sunday service would proceed. He also said an advertised church programme would not hold because he did not want the crisis to escalate.

The development comes after a faction of the church’s Board of Trustees announced on Tuesday, November 17, that it had withdrawn recognition of Jimmy as Senior Pastor with immediate effect and appointed Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader.

The faction cited a December 2021 succession video in which Taiwo named Areogun as his preferred successor.

In the recording, the late founder said, “In case of my demise, which I don’t expect to happen soon, or a situation where I cannot write or talk, please, the next pastor of the church should be Kunle Areogun.”

He also designated Jimmy as Areogun’s immediate administrative assistant and head of the youth church.

PUNCH Online had reported that the trustees claimed they only became aware of the video in late December 2025, more than two years after Taiwo’s death, and that it was not presented during Jimmy’s appointment in September 2023.

However, a statement from Jimmy’s camp rejected the board faction’s decision as constitutionally invalid, insisting that he remained the duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees.

Taiwo founded The Fountain of Life Church in 1992 with his first wife, Pastor Bimbo Odukoya. Following his death on August 7, 2023, Jimmy was announced as Senior Pastor in September and formally installed on September 30, 2023, while his sister, Tolu, was named Associate Senior Pastor.

The competing claims have left the church embroiled in a leadership crisis, with both factions insisting on the legitimacy of their positions.

The post Why I regret keeping my father’s successor video – Jimmy Odukoya appeared first on Very Nigerian.

title: Diana London Denies $4.5m Payment For Tinubu Interview, Says 'Smear Campaign Can't Change The Facts'
description: The American strategist says the Nigerian government never paid her for her interview with President Tinubu, after Atiku Abubakar cited US filings linking her to a firm on a $4.5m retainer.
source: Mindnewsng (from statements on X and Atiku media office)
content:
American political strategist Diana London has denied receiving $4.5 million from the Nigerian government in connection with her interview with President Bola Tinubu, calling the allegation a smear campaign.

London responded on X on Wednesday night, three days after the interview was recorded at the Presidential Villa in Abuja.

What she said

“I unequivocally deny the claim that Nigeria’s government nor anyone else in Nigeria paid me $4.5 million,” she wrote. “I went to Nigeria to interview President Tinubu @officialABAT for parts of a documentary and see Nigeria for myself.”

She added: “This SMEAR CAMPAIGN can make noise, but can’t change the facts or stop me from speaking the truth.”

That is the first direct answer from London since the payment claim began circulating. It does not address the specific documents Atiku Abubakar cited, and it does not explain why her earlier posts about the trip were deleted.

What Atiku is asking

Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar opened the issue on Wednesday through a statement released by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu. He asked the Presidency to explain whether the interview was connected to a lobbying engagement between Abuja and a United States firm.

Atiku said the US filings list London as a consultant to DCI Group AZ, a firm reportedly retained by the Nigerian government through Aster Legal, and that those filings show a $4.5 million retainer.

He wants four things made public:

  • The contract itself, and the details of the payment.
  • The complete, unedited recording of the interview.
  • The identity of whoever approved the reported payment.
  • The source of the money, and whether taxpayers’ funds were used.

His argument is simple: Nigerians are entitled to know whether the Villa interview was an independent media engagement or a publicity exercise paid for by the government.

The posts that disappeared

The controversy grew because of what London published before the denial. She wrote posts praising security cooperation between Nigeria and the United States under Tinubu and President Donald Trump, describing Nigeria as America’s greatest ally in Africa and suggesting the partnership could strengthen trade.

She also acknowledged working with people involved in improving relations between Abuja and the Trump administration. Those posts were later deleted, and the comment section of her X account was restricted after Nigerian users flooded it.

Deleting the posts did not quiet the story. It sharpened it — because the posts were the clearest public evidence of the very relationship Atiku is asking the Presidency to explain.

What the Presidency has said

Nothing, publicly. As of Thursday, the Presidency had not answered Atiku’s questions or said whether the interview was connected to the reported lobbying arrangement.

That silence is now the story as much as the money. A one-paragraph statement — either confirming or denying a government contract with DCI Group AZ — would end the speculation. Instead the government has left a denial from a private American consultant as the only official-sounding word on the matter.

Why it lands in Nigeria now

The interview was not an isolated media booking. It came in the middle of a sensitive stretch in Nigeria–US relations: Washington redesignated Nigeria a Country of Particular Concern over religious violence, American officials have been watching the run-up to the 2027 election, and security cooperation has become a bargaining chip between the two governments.

In that environment, an interview granted to an American strategist who is simultaneously reported to be on a lobbying retainer raises an obvious question about where journalism ends and public relations begins. The answer matters well beyond this one interview.

What happens next

Three things will settle it. Atiku has demanded the unedited recording — if it is released, the public can judge the interview on its content. The US lobbying filings are public documents and can be read directly. And the Presidency can either confirm or deny the contract.

Until at least one of those happens, the claim and the denial will both stand, and Nigerians will be left weighing a strategist’s word against her own deleted posts.

Source: statements by Diana London on X and by Atiku Abubakar’s media office; US lobbying filings cited by the former vice-president.

title: Aketi Bowl IV: NAFA unveils ‘Raised Here’ theme as NSSFFL season 5 reaches national championship
description: The Nigeria American Football Association (NAFA), in partnership with the Nigeria School Sports Federation (NSSF), has unveiled plans for Aketi Bowl IV, the national championship concluding the fifth season of the Nigeria Secondary School Flag Football League (NSSFFL), with a renewed commitment to p
content:
The Nigeria American Football Association (NAFA), in partnership with the Nigeria School Sports Federation (NSSF), has unveiled plans for Aketi Bowl IV, the national championship concluding the fifth season of the Nigeria Secondary School Flag Football League (NSSFFL), with a renewed commitment to promoting youth development and expanding the reach of flag football across Nigeria.

The championship, themed “RAISED HERE,” is scheduled to hold in Abuja from November 17 to 20, 2026, following preliminary competitions conducted across 18 states between October 20 and 30.

Aketi Bowl IV marks the fourth edition of the national championship, while NSSFFL Season 5 represents the fifth season of the secondary school league. The two milestones reflect the continued development of the competition and NAFA’s efforts to establish a sustainable pathway for young Nigerians to discover and develop their sporting talents.

Explaining the significance of this year’s theme, NAFA said “RAISED HERE” celebrates the schools, families, coaches, teachers and communities that contribute to shaping young athletes long before they reach the national championship stage.

According to the organisers, the theme recognises that sporting talent does not develop in isolation but requires encouragement, opportunities, guidance and a supportive environment.

As participating teams prepare to converge on Abuja, they will be representing not only their respective schools but also the communities and states that have supported their development throughout the season.

The organisers noted that the championship would provide an opportunity to celebrate the collective efforts behind every athlete’s journey, while highlighting the values of discipline, teamwork, leadership, confidence, communication and resilience that flag football promotes among young people.

Speaking on the vision behind the championship, NAFA’s leadership is expected to emphasise that the association’s commitment extends beyond organising sporting competitions to creating opportunities for young people to participate in structured sporting activities and develop valuable life skills.

The association also seeks to strengthen the relationship between school sports and youth development by providing secondary school students with a competitive platform through which they can showcase their abilities, build confidence and represent their institutions at national level.

NSSFFL Season 5 has provided a structured competition pathway, allowing participating schools to progress through preliminary state-level contests for the opportunity to qualify for the national championship.

The preliminary stage, which took place across 18 states from October 20 to 30, culminated in the qualification of teams expected to compete for national honours in Abuja.

The championship will feature both boys’ and girls’ categories, reinforcing the league’s commitment to providing opportunities for young athletes across both groups to participate, compete and develop their sporting potential.

Organisers say the national competition will also offer a platform for schools and communities to demonstrate the progress made in developing flag football at the grassroots level.

While the competition will provide an opportunity for emerging talents to demonstrate their abilities, NAFA is also using the league to promote broader values associated with sports, including inclusion, teamwork, discipline and leadership.

The association has acknowledged the contributions of athletes, teachers, coaches, school administrators, officials, parents, volunteers, partners and supporters whose commitment has helped sustain the league through its fifth season.

Their involvement, according to the organisers, underscores the importance of collective support in building a successful school sports programme and creating an environment where young athletes can thrive.

The media briefing is also expected to provide journalists with comprehensive information about the championship’s qualification process, participating states and schools, competition categories, fixtures, match schedules and other organisational arrangements.

The organisers have emphasised the importance of accurate reporting, urging media representatives to use the correct championship identity, Aketi Bowl IV, the national championship of NSSFFL Season 5, in all coverage and official references.

They have also encouraged journalists to look beyond match results and capture the personal stories, school experiences and community contributions that have shaped the participating athletes.

With Aketi Bowl IV approaching, NAFA hopes to build greater awareness of flag football, attract stronger institutional support and create more opportunities for young Nigerians through school sports.

The championship represents another significant step in the association’s efforts to establish flag football as a growing sporting discipline in Nigeria while connecting athletic participation with education, personal development and community engagement.

Under the theme “RAISED HERE,” Aketi Bowl IV seeks to tell a broader story: one of young athletes whose talents have been nurtured by their schools and communities and who now have the opportunity to showcase their abilities on the national stage.

The post Aketi Bowl IV: NAFA unveils ‘Raised Here’ theme as NSSFFL season 5 reaches national championship appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Ecuadorian footballer banned for eight years after throwing stone at referee
description:
An Ecuadorian footballer, Jhon Perlaza, has been banned from all football-related activities for eight years after throwing a stone at an assistant referee during a third-tier league match.
The incident occurred in October when Perlaza’s side, Club Ciudad de Yantzaza, faced Club Rio Aguarico FC.
Acc
content:
An Ecuadorian footballer, Jhon Perlaza, has been banned from all football-related activities for eight years after throwing a stone at an assistant referee during a third-tier league match.

The incident occurred in October when Perlaza’s side, Club Ciudad de Yantzaza, faced Club Rio Aguarico FC.

According to the Ecuadorian Football Federation (FEF) on Thursday, the player threw the stone from his team’s dugout in the 96th minute, striking assistant referee Lenin Giovanni Ojeda Nunez in the face.

A video of the incident circulating on social media shows Perlaza standing up in the dugout and throwing the object towards the official, who immediately fell to the ground while holding his face.

The match was subsequently abandoned as the injured referee received medical attention.

The FEF confirmed that Nunez suffered serious facial injuries that required surgery and a 60-day recovery period.

Following a disciplinary investigation, the federation found Perlaza responsible for physically assaulting a match official and handed him an eight-year suspension, which will run until October 19, 2034.

The FEF also announced plans to request that FIFA extend the suspension worldwide, potentially preventing the player from participating in football activities outside Ecuador.

In addition to Perlaza’s punishment, Club Ciudad de Yantzaza was fined $2,000 and ordered to pay $4,369 in medical expenses incurred by the injured referee.

Meanwhile, Yantzaza confirmed that Perlaza had been dismissed from the club following the incident.

In a statement released on October 20, three days after the match, the club apologised to the refereeing team and supporters, stressing its opposition to violence in football.

The club said it had immediately removed the player after identifying him as the person responsible for the incident.

It also reaffirmed its commitment to respect, peaceful coexistence and fair play, condemning all forms of verbal and physical aggression inside and outside sporting venues.

The post Ecuadorian footballer banned for eight years after throwing stone at referee appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Otti presents N1.23tn 2027 budget to Abia Assembly
description:
Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has presented a proposed budget of N1.23tn for the 2027 fiscal year to the state House of Assembly for consideration and approval.
Presenting the appropriation bill before the Speaker and members of the 8th Assembly on Thursday, Otti described the proposal as an ambit
content:
Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has presented a proposed budget of N1.23tn for the 2027 fiscal year to the state House of Assembly for consideration and approval.

Presenting the appropriation bill before the Speaker and members of the 8th Assembly on Thursday, Otti described the proposal as an ambitious but realistic plan to sustain the state’s development drive.

“Today, when I come to this hallowed assembly to lay the draft of the 2027 Appropriation Bill for the next fiscal year, a total budget estimate of N1.23 trillion shall be tabled before this Honourable House for consideration,” Otti said.

He said N647.23bn was expected from internal and external revenue sources, including internally generated revenue, statutory allocations from the Federation Account Allocation Committee, Value Added Tax and other federal revenue sources, as well as capital receipts.

The governor said the remaining N552.67bn would be raised through concessional loans and dedicated to infrastructure projects with regenerative value.

“The balance of N552.67 billion shall be sourced through concessional loans and committed strictly to infrastructure projects with regenerative value,” he stated.

Otti put the state’s projected internally generated revenue for 2027 at N199.8bn, saying the amount, if realised, would cover 180 per cent of recurrent expenditure.

“The projected IGR output for the coming fiscal year is estimated at N199.8 billion, and if achieved as projected, will be enough to cover 180% of our recurrent expenditure, which puts us in a good fiscal position,” he said.

He added that the proposed budget represented an 80 per cent increase over the current year’s budget and a 648 per cent rise in IGR compared with 2023.

The governor said 80 per cent of the proposed expenditure would go to capital projects, while the remaining 20 per cent would cover recurrent spending.

“We are devoting 80% of the entire budget, that is N960 billion in absolute numbers, to capital expenditure, leaving the remaining 20% for recurrent expenditure,” Otti said.

He said the administration had prioritised human capital development, with 35 per cent of the proposed budget earmarked for education and health.

According to him, education would receive 20 per cent, while the health sector would get 15 per cent of the total budget.

“This necessitates the commitment of 35% of the 2027 fiscal outlay to the education and health sectors, with basic, secondary and tertiary education receiving 20%, while the health sector gets 15%,” he stated.

On sectoral allocations, Otti said 55 per cent of the proposed budget would go to the economic sector, covering agriculture, works, transportation, petroleum and solid mineral development, power and public utilities, among other areas.

He listed other areas under the sector to include the Greater Aba Development Authority, land administration, arts, culture and the creative economy, digital capacity development, infrastructure and support for small and medium-scale enterprises.

The governor said 7.2 per cent of the budget was allocated to the social sector, covering education, health, environmental protection, sports development, local government and chieftaincy affairs, poverty alleviation, social protection and women’s affairs.

He added that the administrative sector, including law and justice, would receive 5.1 per cent of the proposed expenditure, with N17.3bn earmarked for it.

Describing the proposal as both ambitious and achievable, Otti said the state had demonstrated the capacity to sustain its development plans.

“The proposed budget is as realistic as it is aspirational, reflecting the magnitude of our ambition,” Otti said.

“The ship has since left the harbour, and we have demonstrated sufficient capacity and resilience to weather the storms that lie ahead. The job now is to keep our focus, maintain the course and stay committed to the project,” he added.

He said the proposal was prepared with contributions from stakeholders, including business leaders, development partners, civil society organisations, community leaders and traditional rulers.

“We have painstakingly aggregated the views of our people to put together a realistic and responsive budget that promises to further expand the sea of opportunities for everyone while protecting vulnerable individuals and households,” he stated.

Otti thanked the lawmakers for their support and urged them to scrutinise the proposal to ensure it reflected the aspirations of residents.

“The expectation is that, as you have done in the last three years, you will meticulously study and critique the bill, which I shall shortly lay before you, to ensure that it reflects in its entirety the collective aspirations of our people,” he said.

He expressed optimism that the Assembly would pass the bill before the end of the year, saying its timely passage would provide clarity for investors and development institutions seeking opportunities in the state.

Responding, the Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. Emmanuel Emeruwa, said the increased budget proposal indicated progress in the state.

He assured the governor that the lawmakers would examine the estimates and ensure their speedy passage before the end of 2026.

The proposed N1.23tn budget represents another increase in Abia State’s annual spending plan under Otti’s administration.

In December 2024, the governor signed the N750.28bn 2025 budget into law, with 82 per cent allocated to capital expenditure and 18 per cent to recurrent spending.

In November 2025, Otti presented a N1.016tn proposal for the 2026 fiscal year, representing a 13 per cent increase over the 2025 budget.

The proposal allocated N811.8bn, or 80 per cent, to capital projects and N204.4bn to recurrent expenditure. It was subsequently signed into law on December 29, 2025.

The post Otti presents N1.23tn 2027 budget to Abia Assembly appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027 Election: Court Affirms Yahaya Bello As APC Senatorial Candidate For Kogi Central
description: Justice Inyang Ekwo of the Federal High Court in Abuja has affirmed the former Governor of Kogi State, Yahaya Bello, as the APC Candidate for Kogi Senatorial.Delivering Judgement, Justice Ekwo dismissed the suit filed by Momoh  Obaro challenging the emergence of former Kogi State Governor Yahaya Bel
content:
Justice Inyang Ekwo of the Federal High Court in Abuja has affirmed the former Governor of Kogi State, Yahaya Bello, as the APC Candidate for Kogi Senatorial.

Delivering Judgement, Justice Ekwo dismissed the suit filed by Momoh Obaro challenging the emergence of former Kogi State Governor Yahaya Bello as winner of the May 2026 Kogi Central Senatorial District primary election.

The judge held that the Plaintiff failed to exhaust the internal dispute resolution mechanisms of his political party before approaching the court for redress.

Justice Ekwo further ruled that the documentary exhibits tendered by the Plaintiff were unsigned and therefore lacked probative value.

In his pronouncement, Justice Ekwo noted that part of the binding undertaking sworn to by the Plaintiff upon joining the party and participating in the primary election was not to institute any court action without first exhausting internal party remedies.

According to the party’s guidelines, an aggrieved member must utilise every domestic channel within the party structure before seeking judicial intervention.

While acknowledging that the Plaintiff complied in part by lodging a petition before the Appeal Committee, the court observed that he failed to take the mandatory next step of escalating his grievance to the National Working Committee (NWC).

Citing Paragraph 15(3) of the party’s Constitution—which stipulates that an aggrieved member shall appeal before both the Appeal Committee and the NWC—Justice Ekwo found no evidence that the Plaintiff completed these internal processes.

By rushing straight to court without approaching the NWC, the Plaintiff bypassed a mandatory condition precedent. Consequently, I resolve this issue in favour of the 1st Defendant (INEC) and the 2nd Defendant (Yahaya Bello),” the court held.

Justice Ekwo subsequently dismissed the suit for lacking in merit and ordered parties to bear their respective costs.

title: Canada Opens New Permanent Residence Route For 14 Rural Communities, Applications Start January 1, 2027
description: Canada's Rural Community Immigration Program opens on January 1, 2027, offering permanent residence to skilled workers who take jobs in 14 small communities. Here are the towns, the six requirements, the language scores and the exact settlement funds you must show.
content:
Canada will open a new permanent residence route for small towns on January 1, 2027, and it is aimed at workers who are willing to settle outside Toronto, Vancouver and Montreal. The Rural Community Immigration Program (RCIP) gives permanent residence to skilled foreigners who take a job with a designated employer in one of 14 participating rural communities.

It replaces the Rural and Northern Immigration Pilot (RNIP), which IRCC now lists as closed. Unlike the Express Entry system, the RCIP does not run on a points ranking. The gatekeepers are the employer that hires you and the community that recommends you — and both must act before Ottawa looks at your file.

The 14 communities

IRCC published the full list of participating rural communities, with boundary maps for each so applicants can see exactly which area qualifies:

  • Pictou County — Nova Scotia
  • North Bay and Area — Ontario
  • Sudbury — Ontario
  • Timmins — Ontario
  • Sault Ste. Marie — Ontario
  • Thunder Bay — Ontario
  • Steinbach — Manitoba
  • Altona/Rhineland — Manitoba
  • Brandon — Manitoba
  • Moose Jaw — Saskatchewan
  • Claresholm — Alberta
  • West Kootenay — British Columbia
  • North Okanagan Shuswap — British Columbia
  • Peace Liard — British Columbia

A separate Francophone Community Immigration Pilot runs alongside it for French speakers, with six communities: the Acadian Peninsula in New Brunswick, Sudbury, Timmins and the Superior East Region in Ontario, St. Pierre Jolys in Manitoba and Kelowna in British Columbia.

The six things you must have

  1. A job offer from an employer that the community has designated to hire foreign workers.
  2. A recommendation certificate issued by that community.
  3. One year of related work experience — 1,560 hours in the past three years.
  4. A language test from an approved agency (details below).
  5. Education — a Canadian credential, or a foreign one assessed as equivalent.
  6. Proof of settlement funds for yourself and every family member, whether or not they travel with you.

The work experience must be related to the job you are offered, and the language and education documents have to be in place before the community will look at your file. IRCC says language results must be less than two years old when you apply.

Language: the scores are lower than Express Entry

The minimum score depends on the type of job, not on your age or degree:

Job offer level (NOC TEER)Minimum language score
TEER 0 or 1 (management, professional)CLB 6
TEER 2 or 3 (technical, trades, supervisors)CLB 5
TEER 4 or 5 (entry-level, labour)CLB 4

Approved English tests are CELPIP-General, IELTS General Training and PTE Core. For French, IRCC accepts TEF Canada and TCF Canada. You need the minimum score in all four abilities — reading, writing, listening and speaking — not an average.

For comparison, a Federal Skilled Worker application through Express Entry normally needs CLB 7. The RCIP opens at CLB 4 for entry-level jobs, which puts the program within reach of applicants who have been shut out of Express Entry by the language threshold.

Settlement funds: the exact amounts

You must show the money is available when you apply and again when the visa is issued. Bank statements, bank drafts, cheques and money orders are all accepted:

Family membersSettlement funds (CAD)
1$10,507
2$13,080
3$16,080
4$19,524
5$22,143
6$24,975
7$27,806
Each extra person after 7+$2,831

The count includes your spouse or partner and all dependent children, even if they are Canadian citizens or are not moving with you.

There is one exemption: if you are already working in Canada on a valid work permit, you do not need to show proof of funds.

Why it matters for Nigerians

Canada remains one of the most requested destinations for Nigerian professionals, but the main Express Entry draws have stayed brutally competitive, and the Provincial Nominee Programs are oversubscribed. The RCIP is a different door: it is decided by a small town that cannot fill a vacancy, not by a points cut-off.

That also means the jobs on offer reflect what those towns actually need — healthcare support workers, trades, transport, food processing, childcare and hospitality — rather than the white-collar roles most Nigerian applicants target. Applicants who are flexible about the type of work and the size of the town have a realistic path; those waiting for an office job in Toronto do not.

What to do before January 1

  1. Book the language test now. CELPIP, IELTS and PTE slots fill weeks ahead, and the result is valid for two years.
  2. Start the educational credential assessment. It is the slowest document in the pack.
  3. Check the community list against your trade or profession, and look at each community’s own website for its priority sectors and designated employers.
  4. Have the settlement funds sitting in a bank account in your name, not in a friend’s account.

IRCC also lists an optional work permit for candidates in the program, which allows a worker to start the job while the permanent residence file is still in process.

Bottom line

The Rural Community Immigration Program opens on January 1, 2027, in 14 communities across six provinces. It asks for one year of work experience, a language score as low as CLB 4, an assessed qualification and CAD $10,507 for a single applicant — but none of it matters without a job offer from a designated employer and a recommendation from the community.

Source: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), Rural Community Immigration Program pages, updated 9 November 2026.

title: Second private robotic surgery platform in northern Nigeria unveiled in Abuja
description:
…NHIA, Reps hail investment, say it will reduce medical tourism
Eleos Specialist Hospital, Abuja, has commissioned a robotic surgery platform, the second of its kind in Northern Nigeria, in a development expected to strengthen specialised healthcare delivery and reduce Nigerians’ dependence on forei
content:
…NHIA, Reps hail investment, say it will reduce medical tourism

Eleos Specialist Hospital, Abuja, has commissioned a robotic surgery platform, the second of its kind in Northern Nigeria, in a development expected to strengthen specialised healthcare delivery and reduce Nigerians’ dependence on foreign medical services.

The facility is expected to expand access to advanced surgical procedures, particularly in urology, while positioning Nigeria as a potential destination for medical treatment in the West African sub-region.

It’s also expected to support selected complex procedures, particularly in urology, complementing the hospital’s existing services in prostate surgery, kidney and urinary tract stone treatment, and other specialised urological conditions.

The Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA), Dr Kelechi Ohiri, who spoke through his representative, Prof. Chima Ariel Onoka, at the commissioning ceremony, in Abuja, on Wednesday, described the investment as a significant contribution to the country’s healthcare development.

Onoka, Senior Special Adviser to the NHIA boss and Professor of Public Health and Health Systems Economics, said the introduction of robotic-assisted surgery would strengthen Nigeria’s capacity to undertake complex medical procedures locally and reduce the financial burden associated with seeking treatment abroad.

He noted that Nigeria had lost billions of naira annually to medical tourism, particularly as patients travelled overseas for specialised urological and minimally invasive procedures.

According to him, the new facility would help reverse the trend by retaining healthcare resources within the country and potentially attracting patients from other West African countries.

He said robotic-assisted surgery could offer clinical and economic benefits, including reduced blood loss, fewer postoperative complications in appropriate cases and shorter hospital stays, enabling patients to recover faster and return to productive activities.

Onoka, however, called on policymakers to strengthen health insurance coverage and introduce innovative healthcare financing mechanisms to ensure that advanced medical services were accessible beyond high-income earners.

He also stressed the importance of training Nigerian surgeons, nurses and biomedical engineers to operate and sustain the technology.

Similarly, the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Dr. Benjamin Kalu, represented by the Deputy Chairman of the House Committee on Health Institutions, Hon. Olumuyiwa Adesola Samuel Adedayo, commended the hospital for investing in modern medical technology.

Kalu described the commissioning as an important milestone in efforts to modernise Nigeria’s healthcare infrastructure, urging more private investors to support the development of specialised medical facilities.

He said stronger collaboration between government, private investors and healthcare professionals was necessary to improve access to advanced treatment and make Nigeria a destination for specialised medical services.

Earlier, the hospital’s Medical Director and Chief Robotic Surgeon, Dr. Paul Ngwu, said the investment was driven by the desire to bring modern surgical technology closer to Nigerian patients.

He explained that robotic-assisted surgery offered surgeons enhanced precision, improved visualisation and greater control during selected complex procedures.

Ngwu said the hospital would prioritise patient safety, specialist training and professional excellence in deploying the technology.

The Managing Director of the hospital, Dr. Victoria Ngwu, described the commissioning as a landmark achievement, saying the facility reflected the hospital’s commitment to providing specialised healthcare services comparable to international standards.

Also speaking, former Nigerian Ambassador to Hungary, Ambassador Eddy Onuoha, who disclosed that he underwent robotic surgery at the hospital after initially being referred from abroad, described his successful recovery as evidence that Nigerians could access advanced treatment locally.

He urged Nigerians to reconsider the automatic preference for overseas medical treatment.

The post Second private robotic surgery platform in northern Nigeria unveiled in Abuja appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: 2027: Atiku can’t win 25m northern votes when son backs Tinubu – APC chieftain
description:
A member of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council’s Media Directorate, Obafemi George, has questioned former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s claim to strong support in the North ahead of the 2027 presidential election, citing his son’s defection to the ruling party.
George argu
content:
A member of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council’s Media Directorate, Obafemi George, has questioned former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s claim to strong support in the North ahead of the 2027 presidential election, citing his son’s defection to the ruling party.

George argued that Atiku’s inability to convince his son, Abba Atiku Abubakar, to support his presidential ambition raised questions about his appeal among millions of voters in the region.

Speaking during an interview on Arise Television on Thursday, George said it was doubtful that Atiku could secure the support of about 25 million voters in the North-West when his own son had joined the APC and was campaigning for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election.

He said, “Vice President Atiku Abubakar is boasting that the North-West and North-East would vote for him when his own biological son left his party, moved to the APC and is campaigning for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

“So, if Atiku Abubakar cannot even convince his own biological son of his capacity to lead Nigeria, you now think that 25 million voters in the North-West will believe him?”

Abba, one of Atiku’s sons, defected from the Peoples Democratic Party to the APC in January 2026 and declared support for Tinubu’s second-term ambition.

He also renamed his political organisation, formerly known as the Haske Atiku Organisation, the Haske Bola Tinubu Organisation, and directed its members to join the APC and work for the President’s re-election.

George also questioned the loyalty of members of the African Democratic Congress, citing the political affiliation of the daughter of the party’s National Chairman, David Mark.

He claimed that Mark’s daughter, Odon Odon, who is an aspirant for the Otukpo/Ogbadibo/Ohimini Federal Constituency seat in Benue State, was seeking election on the APC platform.

He said, “Secondly, the chairman of the ADC, Senator David Mark, his own biological daughter in Benue, Odon Odon, is contesting in the Otukpo/Ogbadibo/Ohimini Federal Constituency as an aspirant member.

“Guess what? From which political party? APC.

“So, if the chairman of a party cannot convince his own daughter to stay with his party, why should Nigerians believe that they have a plan?”

The APC chieftain urged Nigerians not to be swayed by politicians’ claims about their electoral strength, arguing that political leaders could assess their chances of winning elections.

“See, don’t get deceived by politicians. A politician knows whether he’s going to lose an election or he’s going to win an election.

“So there’s no pathway for them,” he added.

While defending Tinubu’s re-election bid, George described the President as the candidate best equipped to provide a lasting foundation for Nigeria’s development, comparing the task of nation-building to constructing a skyscraper.

He said his 25 years of experience in the real estate sector had taught him that the foundation of a high-rise building was too important to be entrusted to an inexperienced contractor.

According to him, several skyscrapers around the Ozumba Mbadiwe, Bourdillon and Kingsway Road areas of Lagos were built by different owners and contractors but had their foundations constructed by the same company.

He said the arrangement illustrated the importance of having the right leadership and experience to build a country as complex as Nigeria.

George said Tinubu had demonstrated the capacity to lay a foundation for the country’s development through reforms in security, education, the economy, infrastructure and healthcare.

“In this 2027 election, there is only one candidate who has the track record, who has the capacity, who has the audacity to lay the kind of foundation that will sustain Nigeria for the next 40, 50 years. And that candidate is President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said.

Tinubu is seeking re-election in the January 16, 2027 presidential election, while Atiku is the presidential candidate of the ADC.

The post 2027: Atiku can’t win 25m northern votes when son backs Tinubu – APC chieftain appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Two men convicted of sexually assaulting 14-year-old girl on UK train
description:
The Inner London Crown Court has found two Afghan nationals guilty of sexually assaulting a 14-year-old girl on a train in Kent.
Baryalai Rahimi, 25, of Southall, west London, and his friend, Mirebadurahman Sadat, 29, of Cricklewood, northwest London, were both convicted by the court. However, only
content:
The Inner London Crown Court has found two Afghan nationals guilty of sexually assaulting a 14-year-old girl on a train in Kent.

Baryalai Rahimi, 25, of Southall, west London, and his friend, Mirebadurahman Sadat, 29, of Cricklewood, northwest London, were both convicted by the court. However, only Rahimi was charged with rape.

According to a statement by the British Transport Police on Wednesday, the convictions follow a comprehensive investigation led by its detectives from its Major, Serious and Organised Crime team.

The police account noted that the duo subjected the teenage girl to a “heinous and prolonged” sex attack on a train into London.

The jurors were informed that Rahimi and Sadat approached the girl at Sturry station near Canterbury, Kent, where they all boarded a London-bound train at 3 pm.

While on board, evidence showed that Rahimi was the first to “force himself upon her and sexually assault her.”

The police said Rahimi took the girl into one of the train’s toilets and “raped her.

Afterwards, his friend, Sadat, also sexually assaulted her.

“A short while later, Rahimi walked down the carriage and left the girl alone with Sadat –he too then subjected her to a sustained sexual assault,” the police said.

The statement noted that throughout the attack, the girl “told both men ‘no’ but was ignored. She also told them she was 14 years old.”

Upon the train’s arrival at London Bridge, the men followed the girl onto a train to Peterborough before Rahimi got off at St Pancras, and Sadat at Finsbury Park.

“The victim engaged with police at Peterborough station and bravely told officers what they did to her” the statement said.

It added that after the victim’s account, the BTP detectives launched an urgent probe to hunt down both men.

On February 10, detectives arrested Rahimi and Sadat in West London, using the victim’s account and CCTV footage.

“A file including forensic evidence, phone data and CCTV mapping was submitted to the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), and detectives were authorised to charge the pair.

“After a two-week trial at Inner London Crown Court, a jury found the men, who are both Afghan nationals, guilty on nine counts.

“Baryalai Rahimi, 25, of Southall, west London, was found guilty of rape, sexual assault, and three counts of sexual activity with a child.

“Mirebadurahman Sadat, 29, of Cricklewood, northwest London, was found guilty of assault by penetration, sexual activity with a child, and two counts of causing a person to engage in sexual activity,” read the statement.

The duo will be sentenced at the same court on December 18, 2026.

BTP Detective Constable, Gemma Littlewood, lamented the attack, saying both men, described as “two dangerous predators,” have caused “irreparable harm to a child.

“They deliberately targeted her travelling alone, then conspired together so Rahimi could rape her and Sadat could sexually assault her.

“They knew her age, they knew she was vulnerable, and they heard her say no, but none of that stopped them from subjecting her to a heinous and prolonged attack.”

The detective further appreciated the victim for her “exceptional courage” in reporting the incident.

He noted that the police operatives are committed to “tackling sexual violence against women and girls.”

“To report something to us, text 61016, or call 999 in an emergency,” he urged the public.

The post Two men convicted of sexually assaulting 14-year-old girl on UK train appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: I’m very healthy, says Kompany after health scare
description:
Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany has declared himself “very healthy” as he prepares to return to the dugout on Friday following his recent hospitalisation over a health scare.
The 40-year-old former Manchester City captain was taken to hospital last month after falling ill while watching Bayern
content:
Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany has declared himself “very healthy” as he prepares to return to the dugout on Friday following his recent hospitalisation over a health scare.

The 40-year-old former Manchester City captain was taken to hospital last month after falling ill while watching Bayern Munich’s second team train.

He was subsequently diagnosed with meningeal irritation, an inflammation of the protective membrane surrounding the brain and spinal cord.

Speaking at a news conference on Thursday, Kompany expressed gratitude to the club, medical personnel, players, coaches and supporters for their encouragement and support during his recovery.

“It was very intense. At the time, it was a new experience. Looking back, everything went perfectly. I received support right away, from the club and the doctors. I’m very grateful,” he said.

The Belgian tactician said medical examinations returned positive results, assuring supporters that he had recovered fully and was feeling well ahead of his return.

“You try to stay calm and wait until you have the results. It was a positive process, all the tests were positive.

“I have to say, I’m very healthy. We did a lot of tests, and they all came back fine. In those quiet moments, you also try to learn.

“Now I feel very good again and I’m happy to be back with the team,” he added.

During Kompany’s absence, his assistant, Aaron Danks, took charge of the team, guiding Bayern to four victories and one draw.

Kompany also acknowledged the support he received from fellow coaches across the football community, including those he had previously competed against.

“I’d also like to thank the coaching community. We’re always competing, but almost every coach has reached out to me, even if we’ve played against each other and perhaps argued as well. That’s a beautiful thing,” he said.

Bayern Munich, who have England captain Harry Kane in impressive form, currently sit at the top of the Bundesliga standings, level on points with Borussia Dortmund.

The defending German champions are scheduled to face Cologne on Friday following the conclusion of the two-week international break, with Kompany expected to return to the touchline.

The post I’m very healthy, says Kompany after health scare appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: US monitors trial of Egyptian Christian convert facing death penalty
description:
The United States Department of State said it is closely monitoring the trial of an Egyptian man who converted from Islam to Christianity and could face the death penalty after prosecutors requested the maximum punishment against him, Fox News reports on Tuesday.
The case involves Said Mansour Rezk
content:
The United States Department of State said it is closely monitoring the trial of an Egyptian man who converted from Islam to Christianity and could face the death penalty after prosecutors requested the maximum punishment against him, Fox News reports on Tuesday.

The case involves Said Mansour Rezk Abdelrazek, whose prosecution has drawn international attention over concerns that his religious conversion and expression of Christian beliefs are being treated as criminal offences.

A State Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital that the US was following the proceedings and urged the Egyptian government to protect the religious rights of its citizens.

“We are monitoring his trial closely. Religious freedom is a fundamental human value, and we encourage the Egyptian government to protect the religious freedom rights of all its citizens,” the spokesperson said.

According to Fox News, Abdelrazek’s lawyer, Said Fayez, said prosecutors requested the maximum penalty during a hearing in early November. The punishment could be execution or 25 years in prison.

The lawyer’s office said the prosecution had concluded its arguments and asked the court to impose the maximum sentence available under the law.

Abdelrazek’s defence is expected to present its closing arguments on December 8.

The 30-year-old was arrested at his home in Cairo on July 15, 2025, according to Amnesty International. He was held for nine months before being referred to trial before the Terrorism Circuit of the First Criminal Court in Badr.

The charges against him include joining a banned terrorist organisation, contempt for Islam, inciting unrest and spreading false information.

However, Coptic Solidarity, an advocacy organisation representing Egyptian Christians and other religious minorities, said the allegations had not been established in court.

Its spokeswoman, Lindsay Rodriguez, told Fox News that the case raised concerns about religious freedom and the fairness of the trial.

“These remain prosecution allegations, not findings of guilt,” she said.

Rodriguez added that the organisation was concerned about reports of religious remarks attributed to the presiding judge during the November 3 hearing, saying they raised questions about whether Abdelrazek could receive an impartial trial.

“Peaceful religious conversion and expression must not be treated as terrorism or national-security offences,” she said.

She urged the United States, the European Union and Australia to use the December 8 hearing to press Egypt on religious freedom and fair-trial standards.

Abdelrazek’s fiancée, Sophia, an Australian-Egyptian citizen who declined to disclose her surname over security concerns, has also been campaigning for his release.

“I am pleading for them to release him,” she told Fox News.

Amnesty International said Abdelrazek’s prosecution stemmed from his conversion and religious beliefs and called on Egyptian authorities to release him.

The rights organisation also raised concerns about his treatment in detention and his access to legal representation.

Fox News reported that it contacted Egypt’s Embassy in Washington and its Foreign Ministry for comments but did not receive a response.

Egypt has an estimated population of 120 million people, with Coptic Christians accounting for about 10 per cent of the population.

The post US monitors trial of Egyptian Christian convert facing death penalty appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: UDUS medical lecturers threaten strike over unpaid allowances
description:
Medical lecturers at the Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto, have threatened to embark on a five-day warning strike from November 25 over the alleged failure of the university management to implement revised professional allowances and pay outstanding promotion arrears.
The Nigerian Association of
content:
Medical lecturers at the Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto, have threatened to embark on a five-day warning strike from November 25 over the alleged failure of the university management to implement revised professional allowances and pay outstanding promotion arrears.

The Nigerian Association of Medical and Dental Academics, UDUS/UDUTH Chapter, issued the warning during a press conference held at the Nigeria Union of Journalists Press Centre in Sokoto on Thursday.

The association warned that its members might proceed on an indefinite strike if the outstanding issues were not addressed after the warning strike.

The lecturers’ grievances include the partial implementation of professional allowances under the revised Consolidated Medical Salary Structure, irregularities in salary payments and non-payment of promotion arrears owed to members promoted between 2017 and 2024.

They also complained about the exclusion of some eligible members from the 2025 and 2026 promotion arrears already paid.

Addressing journalists in a statement signed by the Chairman of NAMDA, UDUS/UDUTH Chapter, Prof. Usman Bello, and its Acting Secretary, Dr Lukman O. Ajiboye, the association said the challenges had persisted despite several engagements with the university management.

“The remuneration challenges facing our members have persisted for a considerable period, notwithstanding sustained dialogue, consultations and peaceful engagement by the Association,” it said.

NAMDA said previous efforts to resolve the issues, including meetings with university authorities, formal correspondence, submission of supporting documents and the intervention of respected senior colleagues, had yet to produce the desired results.

It expressed concern that medical academics in comparable institutions across Northern and Southern Nigeria were already enjoying the full benefits of the revised CONMESS while members of the association at UDUS continued to experience disparities.

The association also alleged that some members on the same CONMESS level and step received different salaries.

It said the situation was particularly troubling given the increasing migration of experienced medical academics, including senior consultants and professors, to other countries.

“Mr President is also aware of the ongoing exodus of highly experienced academic staff, including senior consultants and professors, to other countries, a trend popularly known as ‘japa’,” the association stated.

NAMDA noted that while the Federal Government had directed an increase in the admission of medical students to address the shortage of doctors caused by migration, the number of medical teachers had continued to decline.

It said medical teachers, represented by NAMDA, the Medical and Dental Consultants’ Association of Nigeria (MDCAN) and their parent body, the Nigerian Medical Association (NMA), had continued to make sacrifices to sustain the quality of medical education.

“Despite these challenges, medical teachers have continued to make sacrifices to impart knowledge and skills without compromising quality or standards,” it said.

The association further disclosed that the Minister of Education had directed vice-chancellors to pay outstanding arrears owed to medical teachers in compliance with a presidential directive.

It, however, lamented that the directive had yet to be implemented by the management of UDUS despite several engagements.

“Several sister universities have since complied. Despite sustained engagement, both formal and informal, this directive is yet to be implemented by the management of our university,” NAMDA said.

The association said the failure to resolve the issues had left its members with little option but to consider a comprehensive strike.

However, it said its congress had opted for a five-day warning strike as a first step out of respect for President Bola Tinubu and the Minister of Education, while allowing the university management additional time to implement the directive.

According to the resolutions of its emergency general meeting held on November 2, the association issued a 21-day notice to the university management, effective November 3, to address the outstanding concerns.

It said the warning strike would commence at 12 am on Wednesday, November 25, if the issues remained unresolved by Tuesday, November 24.

NAMDA added that its congress would review the situation after the warning strike, including the possibility of an indefinite industrial action.

“Congress would thereafter review the situation, including the possibility of an indefinite strike, an outcome we sincerely hope to avoid,” it stated.

The association, however, reaffirmed its willingness to work with the university management towards resolving the dispute, stressing that the welfare of its members, the interest of students and the quality of healthcare services remained important.

It said, “Congress wishes to reaffirm the Association’s commitment and its readiness to work closely with Management towards a prompt and lasting resolution of these matters, in the interest of our members, our students and the patients we serve.”UDUS medical lecturers threaten five-day strike over unpaid allowances

title: UPDATED: Court upholds Yahaya Bello’s emergence as APC senatorial candidate
description:
The Federal High Court in Abuja has affirmed former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, as the All Progressives Congress candidate for the Kogi Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general election.
Justice Inyang Ekwo, in a judgment on Thursday, dismissed the suit filed by Momoh Yusuf Obaro, who
content:
The Federal High Court in Abuja has affirmed former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, as the All Progressives Congress candidate for the Kogi Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general election.

Justice Inyang Ekwo, in a judgment on Thursday, dismissed the suit filed by Momoh Yusuf Obaro, who challenged Bello’s emergence as the winner of the party’s May 18, 2026, senatorial primary.

The judge held that Obaro failed to exhaust the party’s internal dispute resolution mechanisms before approaching the court and did not provide credible evidence to establish his claim.

The suit, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1085/2026, was instituted by Obaro, who sought a declaration that he was the authentic winner of the APC senatorial primary in Kogi Central.

Justice Ekwo held that the plaintiff failed to comply with the party’s constitution, which required aggrieved members to seek redress through the party’s Appeal Committee and the National Working Committee before approaching the court.

The judge noted that although Obaro had submitted a petition to the Appeal Committee, there was no evidence that he subsequently appealed to the NWC as required by the party’s constitution.

Citing Paragraph 15(3) of the party’s Constitution, which stipulates that an aggrieved member shall appeal before both the Appeal Committee and the NWC, Justice Ekwo held that he found no evidence that the plaintiff completed these internal processes.

“By rushing straight to court without approaching the NWC, the Plaintiff bypassed a mandatory condition precedent. Consequently, I resolve this issue in favour of the 1st Defendant (INEC) and the 2nd Defendant (Yahaya Bello),” the court declared.

He held that the failure to exhaust the prescribed internal remedies constituted a breach of a mandatory condition precedent to instituting the action.

The court also faulted the documents tendered by Obaro to establish his alleged victory in the primary, noting that they were not signed by the chairman or secretary of the electoral committee that conducted the exercise.

Justice Ekwo said the documents lacked probative value and described them as being of dubious origin.

The judge observed that the plaintiff ought to have consulted his counsel before presenting the documents to the court, adding that whoever supplied them had misled him and given him false hope.

“Take it that the Plaintiff is not a lawyer, but he should have taken a step to consult his lawyer before dumping these documents on the court. These unsigned documents submitted by the Plaintiff are of dubious origin,” Justice Ekwo stated.

“In law, an unsigned document is of no value. The documents are of dubious origin,” he added.

The trial judge further noted that Obaro had undertaken, in his party membership and nomination documents, to abide by the party’s internal dispute resolution procedures and refrain from instituting court proceedings before exhausting those channels.

Justice Ekwo held that the plaintiff was bound by the undertaking and could not disregard the party’s prescribed procedures.

Consequently, the court dismissed the suit for lacking merit and ordered the parties to bear their respective costs.

Reacting to the judgment, counsel for Bello, Paul Daudu, SAN, described the verdict as sound and well-reasoned.

Daudu said the judgment had upheld the sanctity of the law and the democratic process, adding that Bello’s emergence as the party’s candidate was the product of an overwhelming endorsement by party members.

“We commend the learned trial Judge for his erudite and painstaking judgment, which has upheld the sanctity of the law and the democratic process.

“The dismissal of this suit comes as no surprise, as the plaintiff merely embarked on a speculative voyage—seeking from the bench a victory he failed to secure from the electorate.

“Our candidate’s triumph at the primary election was the product of an overwhelming endorsement by the people, and we are gratified that the court has given judicial validation to that clear mandate,” he said.

The post UPDATED: Court upholds Yahaya Bello’s emergence as APC senatorial candidate appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: 2027: SDP’s Adamu promises free education, electricity for small businesses in Nasarawa
description:
The Nasarawa State governorship candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), former Inspector-General of Police, Abubakar Adamu, has promised to introduce free education in public primary and secondary schools and remove electricity bills for small-scale businesses if elected in 2027.



Adamu sa
content:
The Nasarawa State governorship candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), former Inspector-General of Police, Abubakar Adamu, has promised to introduce free education in public primary and secondary schools and remove electricity bills for small-scale businesses if elected in 2027.

Adamu said the proposed interventions were aimed at reducing the financial pressure on ordinary families and business owners struggling to meet basic expenses.

He made the promises on Wednesday, November 18, while addressing supporters and residents of Gade community in Karu Local Government Area of the state.

The former police chief said his administration would ensure that parents no longer had to struggle to pay school fees for their children.

“We do not see any reason why a family, whether it is a boy or a girl, should have children in primary or secondary school and still struggle to pay school fees,” he said.

“Government is supposed to take responsibility for that. Therefore, our administration will end the suffering associated with paying school fees by providing free education across primary and secondary schools.”

He also pledged to remove electricity bills for small-scale business operators, arguing that the cost of power had become an additional burden for people trying to earn a living.

“Insha Allah, our administration will remove the burden of electricity bills on small-scale businesses,” he said.

On security, Adamu promised to deploy his experience as a former police chief to address insecurity in the state, particularly the challenges confronting farmers.

He said the situation had prevented many residents from accessing their farmlands and earning a livelihood.

“We are also aware that insecurity has become a major challenge. Many people can no longer go to their farms because of insecurity. If elected, we will deploy our experience to ensure that citizens enjoy the security they deserve,” he said.

Adamu also criticised the administration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the state, asking residents to assess its performance before deciding whether to support it for another term.

He warned that re-electing the ruling party would mean another eight years of hardship for residents.

The SDP candidate said his decision to seek the governorship was driven by the need to improve the living conditions of ordinary people.

He further asked Gade residents to nominate three representatives for his campaign council, saying they would serve as a link between the community and his team and monitor the fulfilment of promises made to them.

content:

title: Oyo trains healthcare workers to tackle childhood illnesses, prevent deaths
description:
The Oyo State Primary Health Care Board has begun a nine-day training programme to strengthen healthcare workers’ capacity to manage common childhood illnesses and reduce preventable deaths among children in the state.
The training themed ‘Training of Trainers and Facilitating Skills Course on Integ
content:
The Oyo State Primary Health Care Board has begun a nine-day training programme to strengthen healthcare workers’ capacity to manage common childhood illnesses and reduce preventable deaths among children in the state.

The training themed ‘Training of Trainers and Facilitating Skills Course on Integrated Management of Childhood Illness’ is holding at Plaza De Aruna Hotel, Eleekara, Oyo.

The programme is designed to equip healthcare workers with the knowledge and practical skills to identify childhood illnesses early, administer appropriate treatment PHCN and refer children requiring specialised care.

The Commissioner for Information, Dotun Oyelade, disclosed this in a statement made available to journalists in Ibadan on Thursday.

Speaking at the opening ceremony, the Executive Secretary of the board, Dr Muideen Olatunji, represented by the Director of Disease Control and Immunisation, Dr Festus Mustapha, reaffirmed the board’s commitment to improving child health and strengthening primary healthcare delivery.

“Healthcare workers must be well equipped to recognise early signs of illness in children and respond appropriately,” he said.

He added that timely diagnosis and treatment could prevent complications and save lives.

He explained that the Integrated Management of Childhood Illness strategy provides a comprehensive approach to treating common childhood conditions, noting that its effective implementation would improve the quality of care provided at health facilities across the state.

Olatunji urged participants to engage actively in the training and apply the knowledge acquired in their daily duties, stressing that the programme’s success would depend largely on how effectively the skills were put into practice.

The State IMCI Programme Officer, Mrs Adepeju Mosunmade, also stressed the importance of adhering to the programme’s guidelines when assessing and treating sick children.

She said proper assessment, accurate classification of illnesses and appropriate treatment were essential to preventing complications and childhood deaths.

Mosunmade highlighted the need for healthcare workers to identify danger signs in children, communicate effectively with caregivers, maintain accurate records and ensure the rational use of medicines while providing timely, evidence-based and compassionate care.

She also explained that the training-of-trainers component was designed to enable participants to transfer the knowledge and skills acquired to other healthcare workers, extending the programme’s reach to more health facilities and communities.

The nine-day course features classroom sessions, practical demonstrations, case studies, group exercises, clinical simulations and facilitation techniques to equip participants with clinical knowledge and the teaching skills required to train others.

The training covers the management of common childhood illnesses, including malaria, pneumonia, diarrhoea and malnutrition, with emphasis on early detection, appropriate treatment, caregiver counselling, follow-up and referral in line with established guidelines.

According to the organisers, the programme is expected to strengthen participants’ ability to manage childhood illnesses, provide quality care and train other healthcare workers on the effective implementation of the IMCI strategy in their facilities.

The board reiterated its commitment to continuous capacity building for healthcare workers, describing it as essential to strengthening primary healthcare services and improving children’s health outcomes across the state.

“The initiative reflects the board’s ongoing efforts to reduce preventable childhood deaths, improve access to quality healthcare and ensuring that every child receives timely and appropriate medical attention, regardless of location,” the statement said.

The post Oyo trains healthcare workers to tackle childhood illnesses, prevent deaths appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

French football chief Philippe Diallo and veteran Japanese official Kozo Tashima were on Thursday confirmed by FIFA as the challengers to incumbent Gianni Infantino in next year’s presidential election.



Infantino has faced criticism over his aborted plan to allow private investment into the World
content:
French football chief Philippe Diallo and veteran Japanese official Kozo Tashima were on Thursday confirmed by FIFA as the challengers to incumbent Gianni Infantino in next year’s presidential election.

Infantino has faced criticism over his aborted plan to allow private investment into the World Cup, but he retains considerable support for his bid to win re-election next March.

French Football Federation president Diallo will represent UEFA, the European confederation which has been the most vocal in its criticism of Infantino.

Tashima is a former head of the Japan Football Association and has served on the FIFA Council.

FIFA said the candidacies will be examined by the body’s electoral committee before a final decision is made on whether to admit them.

Ramon Vega, the Swiss former Tottenham defender who had expressed a desire to run against Infantino, was not included among the candidates.

title: INEC backs code for independent tabulation of 2027 election results
description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has endorsed a voluntary Code of Conduct for independent tabulation and publication of election results ahead of 2027.



INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, gave the backing at a stakeholders’ roundtable convened by Yiaga Africa in Abuja.



The
content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has endorsed a voluntary Code of Conduct for independent tabulation and publication of election results ahead of 2027.

INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, gave the backing at a stakeholders’ roundtable convened by Yiaga Africa in Abuja.

The Executive Director of Yiaga Africa, Samson Itodo, states this in a statement he signed on Thursday in Abuja.

According to Itodo, Amupitan, who was represented by INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Dr Lawrence Bayode, said the code would strengthen transparency and public confidence.

He warned that independently aggregated figures, projections and partial tallies must never be presented as official election results.

“Independent verification should complement electoral accountability, not create competing centres of statutory authority,” the INEC boss stated.

Amupitan outlined six guiding principles for the framework, including methodological integrity, accuracy, information integrity, data security, error accountability and voluntary compliance.

Itodo said independent tabulation helps citizens to scrutinise election outcomes and assess credibility.

The Yiaga Africa boss noted that differing methodologies and publication standards could cause confusion during sensitive collation periods if left uncoordinated.

He stressed that a common code would establish minimum standards, curb premature declarations and ensure findings are backed by reliable verification.

Itodo said Yiaga Africa was expected to lead further engagements to translate the agreed principles into a practical framework before the 2027 general elections.

Participants at the forum included civil society groups, political parties, election observers, the National Broadcasting Commission and the Broadcasting Organisations of Nigeria.

Also in attendance were representatives of the Nigerian Press Council (NPC) and the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ).

Stakeholders examined different tabulation models, including Yiaga Africa’s Processing Results Voter Tabulation (PRVT) and Election Results Analysis Dashboard (ERAD), alongside INEC’s Result Viewing Portal (IReV) aggregations.

They agreed that organisations must clearly disclose their methodologies, data sources and margins of error to prevent public misinterpretation.

A technical session also highlighted the need for human verification, audit trails, data security and transparent error-correction procedures.

Media stakeholders emphasised the duty of journalists to verify figures and clearly distinguish independent tallies from official results declared by INEC. (NAN)

The post INEC backs code for independent tabulation of 2027 election results appeared first on Vanguard News.
