title: Why I chose South Africa posting over Europe — Fani-Kayode
description:
Nigeria’s Ambassador to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has said he appealed to President Bola Tinubu to be posted to South Africa after he was initially assigned to a European country.
Fani-Kayode disclosed this during a dinner and reception organised in his honour by members of the Nigerian High C
content:
Nigeria’s Ambassador to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, has said he appealed to President Bola Tinubu to be posted to South Africa after he was initially assigned to a European country.

Fani-Kayode disclosed this during a dinner and reception organised in his honour by members of the Nigerian High Commission, Nigerian Consular Office and diplomatic community in Pretoria, following the presentation of his letters of credence to South African President Cyril Ramaphosa on November 13.

He shared a video of his speech on X on Wednesday.

Explaining his decision, he said, “I was initially posted to a European country, and I made an appeal to our president that I’d prefer to go to South Africa, which he graciously, you know, agreed to. That’s why I find myself here.”

He said he had started examining issues affecting Nigerians in South Africa from the time he received approval to take up the posting.

“From the time I was accepted and I was given the agrément to come to South Africa, that’s when I started looking into some of the things that were going on here which touched and concerned members of our community,” he said.

Fani-Kayode added, “I am here first and foremost to protect the interests of members of the Nigerian community in South Africa.”

He explained that he considered his remarks important because of the growing dissatisfaction among some Nigerian political and business leaders over developments involving the Nigerian community in South Africa.

“The feeling that is being enunciated by a number of our leaders, particularly those in the Nigerian Senate and the Nigerian House of Assembly, and a number of other leaders from the private sector, about South Africa, are not that good,” he said.

“Some have called for a complete break in diplomatic ties, which the Federal Government and the President has resisted. Some have called for sanctions,” he added.

The ambassador also said he believed Nigeria and South Africa had an important role to play in the development of the African continent, urging both countries not to allow disagreements to undermine their relationship.

“It is important we recognise the fact that together, South Africa and Nigeria can actually help to move Sub-Saharan and Africa in general forward,” he said.

“We must not allow any division. We must not allow any misunderstanding. We must not allow even any slight to pull us apart.”

He described Nigeria as a country of about 250 million people, with a rich history and resilient population, saying he had been sent by Tinubu to represent its government and citizens.

He also spoke warmly about his host country, describing South Africans as “equally resilient, hardworking, decent, civilised, with an equally rich history and heritage as we have”.

Fani-Kayode said both countries had experienced difficult periods but could work together to advance the continent.

“What’s important is this: it is important we recognise the fact that together, South Africa and Nigeria can actually help to move Sub-Saharan and Africa in general forward,” he said.

This comes at a time of renewed tension between Abuja and Pretoria over the treatment of Nigerians living in the country.

A fresh wave of anti-immigrant violence in 2026, including attacks linked to xenophobic and Afrophobic sentiments, heightened concerns in Nigeria.

The Federal Government condemned the attacks and pressed South Africa to take action to protect Nigerians and other African nationals.

Fani-Kayode’s diplomatic assignment has also got off to a rocky start following a dispute over the livestream of the ceremony at which he presented his letters of credence to President Cyril Ramaphosa on November 13.

The envoy alleged that the South African Presidency deliberately excluded his introduction, the Nigerian delegation and his speech from the broadcast, claiming that the livestream was interrupted during his presentation and resumed after he had finished.

He said he raised the matter directly with Ramaphosa, who questioned the officials responsible and directed them to address it.

The complaint triggered a public exchange between Fani-Kayode and South African presidential spokesperson Vincent Magwenya.

Magwenya disputed the envoy’s account, saying Ramaphosa had referred him to the South African Broadcasting Corporation’s acting political and foreign editor, Sophie Mokoena, to address the broadcast issue.

He also described Fani-Kayode’s handling of the complaint as “grossly inappropriate”. The South African Presidency later released a separate video of the Nigerian envoy’s speech.

The disagreement was subsequently taken up at a meeting between Fani-Kayode and South Africa’s Director-General of International Relations and Cooperation, Zane Dangor, on November 17.

South African officials reportedly expressed concern about the envoy’s public comments and reminded him that Article 41 of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations requires diplomats to conduct official business through the receiving country’s established diplomatic channels. Fani-Kayode later described the meeting as cordial and constructive.

The post Why I chose South Africa posting over Europe — Fani-Kayode appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Kalu, NHIA boss seek investment to curb medical tourism
description:
The Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, and the Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority, Dr Kelechi Ohiri, have called for sustained investment in Nigeria’s health sector to reduce medical tourism and improve access to specialised treatment.
They made t
content:
The Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, and the Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority, Dr Kelechi Ohiri, have called for sustained investment in Nigeria’s health sector to reduce medical tourism and improve access to specialised treatment.

They made the call at the inauguration of a robotic surgery platform at Eleos Specialist Hospital, Abuja, the second of its kind in Northern Nigeria, according to a statement by the institution on Thursday.

Kalu, represented by the Deputy Chairman of the House Committee on Health Institutions, Olumuyiwa Adedayo, said investment in modern medical technology was essential to strengthening the country’s healthcare infrastructure and enabling Nigerians to access advanced surgical procedures locally.

He said, “The commissioning of this Robotic Surgery Platform demonstrates what private-sector investment, professional expertise and commitment to healthcare development can achieve.

“We must encourage more Nigerian investors to support modern medical facilities so that our people can access advanced surgical procedures without having to travel abroad.”

Similarly, Ohiri, represented by his Senior Special Adviser, Prof Chima Onoka, described the introduction of the technology as an important intervention in addressing medical tourism and retaining healthcare spending within the country.

Onoka said Nigeria lost billions of naira annually as patients travelled abroad for complex urological and minimally invasive procedures.

He said, “Every year, billions of naira leave our shores as Nigerians travel abroad for complex urologic and minimally invasive procedures.

“This capital flight deprives our local institutions of the resources needed to grow, while placing an unbearable financial burden on families who must pay for international travel, accommodation and foreign healthcare out-of-pocket.

“By bringing this robotic platform to Abuja, Eleos Specialist Hospital is directly addressing this leak. We are shifting the narrative from capital flight to capital retention and positioning Nigeria as a hub for inbound medical tourism across West Africa.”

He added that robotic-assisted surgery could offer benefits such as reduced blood loss, fewer postoperative complications in appropriate cases and shorter hospital stays, while urging policymakers to strengthen health insurance coverage to make advanced treatment accessible to more Nigerians.

He added that robotic-assisted surgery could offer benefits such as reduced blood loss, fewer postoperative complications in appropriate cases and shorter hospital stays, while urging policymakers to strengthen health insurance coverage to make advanced treatment accessible to more Nigerians.

Earlier, the hospital’s Consultant Endourologist, Laparoscopic and Robotic Surgeon, Dr Paul Ngwu, said the introduction of the platform was driven by the hospital’s commitment to bringing advanced surgical technology closer to Nigerian patients.

He said the technology would strengthen the hospital’s capacity to perform complex urological and other selected procedures, adding that the facility would prioritise specialist training, patient safety and professional excellence.

The Managing Director of the hospital, Dr Victoria Ngwu, said the investment reflected the facility’s vision of providing Nigerians with advanced surgical services comparable to those available in leading medical centres globally.

She added that the hospital would continue investing in skilled medical personnel, modern equipment and strategic partnerships to improve specialised healthcare delivery and reduce the need for Nigerians to seek treatment abroad.

A former Nigerian Ambassador to Hungary, Eddy Onuoha, who disclosed that he had undergone robotic surgery at the hospital and recovered successfully, said the availability of the technology in Abuja could help change Nigerians’ preference for seeking treatment abroad.

Robotic surgery is a form of minimally invasive surgery in which surgeons control specialised instruments through a computer-assisted system.

The technology provides enhanced dexterity and visualisation, particularly during complex procedures.

It is increasingly used in urology, including prostate, kidney and bladder surgeries. However, the technology does not operate independently or replace surgeons, who remain in control throughout the procedure.

title: Businesses risk tax losses, disruptions over e-invoicing knowledge gaps
description:
…Afri Invoice bridges compliance gaps with free masterclass series
Nigerian businesses risk financial losses, tax complications and operational disruptions due to inadequate understanding of the Federal Government’s electronic invoicing requirements, even as the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) intensi
content:
…Afri Invoice bridges compliance gaps with free masterclass series

Nigerian businesses risk financial losses, tax complications and operational disruptions due to inadequate understanding of the Federal Government’s electronic invoicing requirements, even as the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) intensifies efforts to migrate taxpayers to digital invoicing.

Industry observations by Afri Invoice showed that many businesses, particularly medium-sized and growing enterprises, are yet to fully understand the technical requirements of the new system, with some mistaking registration on the tax authority’s platform for complete compliance readiness.

The company warned that the knowledge gap could expose businesses to avoidable compliance difficulties, delays in invoice processing and potential disruptions to their financial and supply chain operations as the NRS expands the implementation of its electronic invoicing mandate.

To address the challenge, Afri Invoice has launched a free 2026 Masterclass Series aimed at educating business owners, accountants, finance professionals and tax practitioners on the technical and operational requirements of electronic invoicing.

Under the NRS framework, businesses are expected to move away from paper-based and static PDF invoices to structured, machine-readable electronic invoices that can be validated in real time through the Merchant Buyer Solution (MBS) platform.

However, Afri Invoice said many organisations still struggle to understand how their existing Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and accounting software can connect with the tax authority’s infrastructure.

The company identified Application Programming Interface (API) connectivity, Invoice Reference Numbers (IRN), Cryptographic Stamp Identifiers (CSID) and the role of accredited intermediary service providers in invoice transmission as some of the areas creating confusion among businesses.

The knowledge gap could also have direct financial implications, particularly as the recovery of input Value Added Tax (VAT) is tied to receiving validated electronic invoices from suppliers under the new framework.

Afri Invoice, which operates as an e-invoicing Access Point Provider and System Integrator accredited by the NRS, said its masterclass initiative was designed to translate the technical requirements of the new tax administration system into practical guidance that businesses can understand and implement.

The first two sessions, held in September and October, focused on foundational electronic invoicing processes and the integration of ERP and accounting software with the e-invoicing infrastructure.

The final session of the 2026 series is scheduled for Saturday, November 28.

Speaking on the initiative, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Afri Invoice, Mark Odenore, said the major challenge confronting businesses was not necessarily resistance to the new regulatory requirements but a lack of understanding of how to implement them.

“E-invoicing should not be something Nigerian business owners and accountants are afraid of or confused about. Businesses need to understand what is changing, what it means for their operations, and how they can prepare.

“Moving beyond simply hearing about e-invoicing to understanding how invoicing, accounting software, ERP systems, and digital compliance fit together is essential before compliance deadlines become an operational disruption,” he said.

With the NRS expected to extend the compliance phases to medium-sized and smaller taxpayers through 2027 and 2028, the company stressed the need for businesses to begin aligning their systems and processes ahead of their respective deadlines.

It added that sustained stakeholder education and early technical preparation would be critical to ensuring a smooth transition to electronic invoicing and strengthening digital tax administration in Nigeria.

The post Businesses risk tax losses, disruptions over e-invoicing knowledge gaps appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Prince Harry says would rejoin military to fight Russia if needed
description:
Britain’s Prince Harry said he would “sign up again” to serve in the military and fight against Russia if needed, in an interview from Ukraine with The Telegraph aired Thursday.



“I think there’s a lot that the whole world can learn from Ukraine,” the prince said during an unannounced visit to the
content:
Britain’s Prince Harry said he would “sign up again” to serve in the military and fight against Russia if needed, in an interview from Ukraine with The Telegraph aired Thursday.

“I think there’s a lot that the whole world can learn from Ukraine,” the prince said during an unannounced visit to the western city of Lviv over the weekend.

“If asked to sign up again, if the need is there, then I will 100% be there to serve my country alongside my fellow veterans and service personnel.”

Harry, a former British army officer and the younger son of King Charles III, made his fourth visit to Ukraine since Russia’s 2022 invasion to meet wounded veterans and medics.

The prince is also the founder of the Invictus Games for wounded veterans and met athletes hoping to represent Ukraine at next year’s games in the British city of Birmingham.

“Just because there’s not drones, bullets, and rockets flying at us, that doesn’t mean that we’re not at war,” he told the British daily’s “Ukraine: The Latest” podcast.

“I feel very confident that Europe has a united front, and it would be fantastic to have more American support for that as well,” he added.

Earlier on his weekend visit to Lviv he told wounded veterans and medics specialising in war injuries: “You’re going to win the war”.

He repeated that sentiment on the podcast, insisting that “Ukraine are winning” and “there is no version where Russia is making any more advances”.

The 42-year-old prince has previously spoken about being moved by witnessing death and life-changing injuries while on deployment in Afghanistan, and launched the Invictus Games in 2014 when he was still in the British army.

Harry, his wife Meghan and their two children moved back to the UK earlier this year from California amid an enduring rift with the royal family and his brother and heir-to-the-throne Prince William.

But the Sussex couple have launched themselves back into public life since their surprise return, carrying out engagements and visiting the EU parliament last week for an event about the dangers children face online.

Despite their busy schedule, Meghan has been keeping a relatively low profile since her estranged father was charged in the US for the alleged possession of child sexual abuse images.

title: I wrote UTME eight times before gaining admission – Kwara education commissioner
description:
The Kwara State Commissioner for Education and Human Capital Development, Dr Lawal Olohungbebe, has revealed that he sat for the Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) eight times before eventually gaining admission into the University of Maiduguri.
Olohungbebe disclosed this while recoun
content:
The Kwara State Commissioner for Education and Human Capital Development, Dr Lawal Olohungbebe, has revealed that he sat for the Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) eight times before eventually gaining admission into the University of Maiduguri.

Olohungbebe disclosed this while recounting his academic journey in a video obtained from the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board’s X handle on Thursday, which he said spanned eight years, from 1997 to 2005, before he finally secured admission into the university.

Reflecting on his experience, the commissioner said his repeated attempts did not stop him from pursuing his educational ambitions, adding that he has risen to become the Kwara State Commissioner for Education and Chairman of Commissioners of Education in Nigeria.

“I wrote UTME eight times before I passed. From 1997 to 2005, and to God be the glory, I’m the commissioner today and the chairman of all commissioners of education in Nigeria,” he said.

The commissioner also cautioned prospective university students against accepting admission offers outside the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board’s (JAMB) Central Admissions Processing System (CAPS), insisting that the platform remains the recognised channel for confirming admission offers.

“Anything that falls out of CAPS, forget about it, it’s not going to happen. It is only JAMB, through CAPS, that can offer you admission that you can be rest assured that yes, you have admission. Anything outside that, forget about it, it’s not going to work,” Olohungbebe stated.

Speaking about his academic qualifications, he disclosed that he gained admission into the University of Maiduguri, where he studied Sociology and Anthropology.

He subsequently studied Social Work and Community Development at Ladoke Akintola University of Technology before proceeding to obtain a Bachelor of Laws (LLB) degree. He also earned a PhD in Community Development and Adult Education from Bayero University, Kano.

Olohungbebe’s account highlights his prolonged struggle to gain university admission and his subsequent academic progression, which he described as a journey that eventually led him into public service.

His experience also serves as a reminder to prospective students that setbacks in the pursuit of education do not necessarily mean the end of their academic ambitions.

title: Anthony Joshua Welcomes Baby Girl, Says 'I Can't Believe I'm A Girl Dad'
description: Anthony Joshua has announced the birth of his daughter, his second child with former childhood sweetheart Nicole Osbourne - three weeks before his heavyweight fight with Tyson Fury in Cardiff.
content:
Anthony Joshua has become a father again – and this time he is a "girl dad". The British heavyweight announced that he and his former childhood sweetheart, Nicole Osbourne, have welcomed a baby girl, three weeks before he steps into the ring with Tyson Fury in Cardiff.

The 37-year-old broke the news in an interview published on 18 November 2026, and the timing caught almost everyone off guard: he had kept the pregnancy entirely out of the public eye while preparing for the biggest domestic fight of his career.

"I can't believe I'm a girl dad"

"It's been amazing, a big blessing, and I can't believe I'm a girl dad. I didn't want to find the sex out during the pregnancy."

Joshua said he deliberately asked not to be told the baby's sex. When he found out it was a girl, his whole plan for fatherhood changed on the spot.

"I love boys but as soon as I found out we had a little girl I said, 'No more FIFA, no more motorbiking, no more PlayStation!'"

He went further, describing the kind of father he intends to be:

"I'm going to do it all, so you might see me with some eyeshadow on, some nail polish on, drinking some tea in a doll's playhouse and just trying to do the right thing by her. I will change nappies – I've gotta go through all that stinky bum time again!"

The mother, and the name

The baby is Joshua's second child with Nicole Osbourne. The pair are not in a romantic relationship, but they came together to extend their family. Their son, Joseph Bayley Temiloluwa Prince Joshua, is 11 and has been kept largely out of the public eye.

Joshua said the baby girl does not have a name yet – but she already has one from her father.

"We haven't given her a name yet, but she's my Princess."

He also spoke about what raising a daughter means to him personally:

"Now I've got a daughter, I will get an insight and a bit more understanding of what it means to be a woman, and how I can be supportive. My daughter will give me a first-hand experience of the power of a woman – I've spoken to all the women in my family, and it's amazing the amount of support that women give each other."

Why the news lands hard

The announcement comes 11 months after the car crash in Nigeria that killed two of Joshua's closest friends and left him injured. He has spoken since about wanting another child to "give back to the world" – a line that reads differently now that the baby is here.

It also lands in the middle of a fight camp. Joshua faces Tyson Fury on Friday, 11 December 2026 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff – a bout British boxing has chased for years, and one that will define the final chapter of both careers.

What it means for the Fury fight

Nothing, technically. A newborn does not change a jab. But fighters have long spoken about how fatherhood reshapes the way they approach the sport – less risk-taking, more purpose. Joshua, who has spent most of the past year rebuilding after the crash, now has a second reason to walk out of that ring on his feet.

Whether it sharpens him or softens him is the question Cardiff will answer on 11 December.

Bottom line: Anthony Joshua is a father again – a daughter, still unnamed, already called "Princess" – and he will fight Tyson Fury three weeks after her birth. The heavyweight division's biggest storyline just got a human one attached to it.

title: Lumumba faults African leaders seeking medical treatment abroad
description:
Renowned Kenyan scholar and Pan-Africanist, Prof. Patrick Lumumba, has urged African leaders to reduce dependence on foreign expertise and develop indigenous capacity to execute projects in healthcare, infrastructure, agriculture and other critical sectors.
Lumumba said the continued reliance on for
content:
Renowned Kenyan scholar and Pan-Africanist, Prof. Patrick Lumumba, has urged African leaders to reduce dependence on foreign expertise and develop indigenous capacity to execute projects in healthcare, infrastructure, agriculture and other critical sectors.

Lumumba said the continued reliance on foreign countries, despite the availability of trained African professionals and local resources, was reinforcing neo-colonialism and undermining the continent’s development.

He spoke on Thursday in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, while delivering the keynote address at the maiden Pan-African Awakening Conference organised by the Social Engagement and Reorientation Initiative.

The scholar called for a change in mindset among African leaders, saying the continent must develop home-grown solutions to bridge the technological and economic gap between it and developed countries.

“They teach us engineering, but largely, when we want to do our roads, we still call the Chinese to do them for us,” he said.

Lumumba also criticised the practice of African leaders seeking medical treatment abroad despite the training and qualifications of healthcare professionals on the continent.

“Why is it that we train our doctors in universities, complete with PhDs and other specialisations, but even our ministers for health in African countries, when they are sick, they don’t go to hospitals in Abuja, or in Nairobi, or in Senegal? They are in London, and in Paris, and in Germany.

“Even our presidents don’t trust our ministries of health, yet they have allocations for them. Why is it?” he asked.

He also faulted the continent’s dependence on imported goods despite its capacity to produce raw materials and manufacture finished products.

“We produce what we do not consume, and consume what we do not produce,” he said.

“Why is it that our cows produce milk, and when we want butter, we still go to the Netherlands? Why is it that we produce cotton, but once we have produced cotton, we are still importing bedsheets from Vietnam and China?

“Why is it that we have leather, and we have skin, and you sell it in Kano, and in Kaduna, and in other places, but when we want bags for our ladies, we still go to Italy to get Gucci and Dolce & Gabbana?” he added.

Lumumba urged African countries to learn from the development experiences of nations such as China, India and South Korea, but adapt the lessons to their local circumstances.

“We can learn from the Indians. We can learn from the Caucasians. We can learn from the Chinese. We can learn from the Koreans, but once we have done so, let us give it an African flavour. Because when we give it an African flavour, that is when it becomes African,” he said.

He disclosed that 22 African and Caribbean countries had united to establish a common front aimed at changing what he described as the negative and colonial mindset of leaders across the continent.

The scholar also urged Nigeria to take the lead in the campaign against neo-colonialism, citing its human and natural resources.

He called on Nigerian youths to rise above ethnic and religious divisions and embrace citizenship as a basis for national development.

“You know, this Nigeria, one out of every five Africans is Nigerian. If you want to know how great this Nigeria could be, travel the world. Go to Costa Rica, you’ll find Nigerian doctors, Nigerian businessmen. Go to Saint Kitts and Nevis, go to Tonga, go to Europe, go to the United States of America.

“You are Nigerians. You are the ones who are going to change Nigeria. And you can only change Nigeria if you are a Nigerian citizen, not if you are a tribalist and an idiot. So be citizens,” Lumumba said.

He commended the Akwa Ibom State Government for its efforts to develop infrastructure, particularly roads, saying the state’s progress demonstrated what could be achieved through investment in local development.

“Akwa Ibom has some of the best roads in the continent of Africa, and I have travelled Africa. At least, when you look at the roads in Akwa Ibom, it tells you what can be done.

“You know, Akwa Ibom has oil. You know, Akwa Ibom has a GDP that is larger than a number of African countries. So when Nigeria tells me, ‘Our economy is improving, we are now 500 billion,’ I don’t even clap my hands. Nigeria should be talking two trillion, then I’ll begin to clap my hands,” he said.

Earlier, the Founder and Executive Director of the Social Engagement and Reorientation Initiative, Engr. Ekemini Amos, said the organisation was established to raise a new generation of Nigerian youths from different ethnic backgrounds but united by a common purpose of contributing to national and continental development.

“This gathering is not just another conference! This is the resurrection of a cause! The cause of African liberation was buried with Nkrumah! It was buried with Sankara! It was buried with Murtala Muhammed! For many years, we buried it with our silence, with our japa syndrome, with our love for foreign things! But today, in Uyo, we are resurrecting that cause!” Amos said.

He urged stakeholders to partner with the organisation in building a better future for Africa and supporting its mentorship initiatives, including the Youth Membership Hub for people aged 18 to 35 and the Nation Builders Club for secondary school students aged 10 to 18.

The highlight of the conference was the unveiling of the SERI Mentorship Programme, the organisation’s flagship initiative. Lumumba, who serves as its Chief Adviser and Grand Patron, performed the unveiling.

Lumumba and his wife were also decorated with the titles Akwa Ujo Africa, meaning the biggest voice in Africa, and Mkpouto Africa, meaning the jewel of Africa, respectively.

The post Lumumba faults African leaders seeking medical treatment abroad appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: I disobeyed my father’s order to delete succession video – Jimmy Odukoya
description:
The Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, has admitted disobeying his late father, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, by retaining a succession video he was instructed to delete after the founder’s successful surgery in 2021.



Odukoya described his decision to keep the recording as a gra
content:
The Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, has admitted disobeying his late father, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, by retaining a succession video he was instructed to delete after the founder’s successful surgery in 2021.

Odukoya described his decision to keep the recording as a grave mistake while addressing about 300 church workers on Wednesday, against the backdrop of the ongoing leadership crisis at the church.

He explained that his father requested the recording before travelling to the United States for surgery because he feared he might not survive the procedure.

According to Church Times, which reported details of the meeting, Odukoya said he personally recorded the message in which Taiwo identified Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor.

However, following his successful operation, the late founder reportedly asked him to erase the recording, saying the circumstances that prompted its creation no longer applied.

Rather than comply, Jimmy kept the video, a decision he now acknowledges was wrong.

He also claimed that only a few people, including his sisters, knew about the recording, alleging that they were responsible for making it public.

The video has become central to the leadership dispute at the church, with a faction of its Board of Trustees relying on its contents to withdraw recognition of Jimmy as Senior Pastor.

The faction announced on November 17 that it had appointed Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader, citing Taiwo’s instruction that Areogun should succeed him.

In the recording, the late founder said Areogun should take over if he died or became unable to communicate, while assigning Jimmy the roles of Areogun’s administrative assistant and head of the youth church.

Jimmy, however, has rejected the board faction’s decision, insisting that he remains the church’s legitimate Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees.

He told the workers that the disagreement with the board began about a year after he assumed office, when members allegedly asked him to relinquish his position as board chairman and concentrate on pastoral responsibilities.

He also alleged that his sister, Pastor Tolu Odukoya-Ijogun, approached him to step aside to allow her to become board chairman.

The disagreement was reportedly taken to the General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God, Pastor Enoch Adeboye, after Bishop Mike Okonkwo intervened.

Jimmy further denied allegations that he misappropriated N250m donated to the church for a project, maintaining that the money remained intact and that economic challenges had delayed the project.

He said he had restricted access to church funds and dismissed claims of financial misconduct.

Although he maintained that he remained Senior Pastor, Jimmy expressed uncertainty about the conduct of the next Sunday service and said an advertised church programme would not hold to prevent further escalation of the dispute.

The post I disobeyed my father’s order to delete succession video – Jimmy Odukoya appeared first on Vanguard News.

title: 2027: Yul Edochie backs Tinubu’s re-election bid
description:
Nollywood actor, Yul Edochie, has declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, endorsing the joint ticket of the President and Vice-President Kashim Shettima ahead of the 2027 general election.
Edochie made his position known in a post on his Instagram page following a recent road t
content:
Nollywood actor, Yul Edochie, has declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, endorsing the joint ticket of the President and Vice-President Kashim Shettima ahead of the 2027 general election.

Edochie made his position known in a post on his Instagram page following a recent road trip to Enugu, where he commended the Tinubu administration for what he described as improvements to road infrastructure in the South-East.

The actor listed the Niger Bridge, Umunya-Enugu Expressway and Enugu-Port Harcourt Expressway among the roads he said had been repaired or were undergoing rehabilitation.

He also praised the installation of streetlights along the Umunya-Enugu route, claiming that about 90 per cent of federal roads in the South-East had been fixed, with more projects ongoing.

Commending the administration, Edochie wrote, “Kudos to the President Bola Tinubu-led administration.”

He subsequently declared his political preference ahead of the next presidential election, stating, “2027, TINUBU/SHETTIMA or nothing.”

The actor’s declaration comes as political activities gradually gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general election.

title: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Launches Worldwide To Near-Perfect Reviews
description: Gamers around the world got their first taste of “Grand Theft Auto VI” on Wednesday, as critics heaped praise on one of the most anticipated video game releases ever.The latest installment of the crime franchise comes 13 years after the last full edition broke sales records and became on
content:
Gamers around the world got their first taste of “Grand Theft Auto VI” on Wednesday, as critics heaped praise on one of the most anticipated video game releases ever.

The latest installment of the crime franchise comes 13 years after the last full edition broke sales records and became one of the most profitable entertainment products of all time.

The series lets players live out gangster fantasies, smash up cars and fight whoever they choose in a fictionalized US city populated by lowlifes, sex workers and thugs.

“GTA VI” launched first in New Zealand at midnight local time (1100 GMT Wednesday) and is rolling out around the world as each market reaches midnight.

New Zealander Luke Starik was among the first to play, and his character did not last long. “Wasted already. First one, didn’t survive long,” he told AFP, laughing.

“This is one of the big things in my life…I’ve been playing GTA for such a long time,” Riley Fennel, an Australian student visiting Tokyo, told AFP.

Review aggregator Metacritic gave the game a score of 99 out of 100.

A 42-year-old gamer wrote on a German-language Reddit forum that he had taken time off work to play all night. By 1:20 am, he was already in bed with a headache, still blown away by the game.

“Thirteen years ago, with a game like this, I’d have played until six in the morning,” the gamer wrote.

In the game’s official Reddit forum, people raved about improved interactive elements, such as being able to push a stranded ski jet back in the water.

“This is amazing!” one person wrote.

Analytics firm Omdia estimates “GTA VI” could generate $3.2 billion in sales by the end of the year for studio Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two Interactive.

PlayStation briefly reported connection issues on its status page before services were restored.

‘Taylor Swift of games’

In a review for The Verge titled “GTA VI does something impossible — it lives up to the hype,” Andrew Webster wrote that “the game is so good that the outsize hype is the least interesting thing about it.”

Social media users praised the graphics.

“There’s one moment, no spoilers, where the light hits behind one of the characters just right, and I swore I was looking at a real human,” wrote Reddit user No_Strike9652.

Before the release, Joost van Dreunen, a professor at New York University’s Stern School of Business, told AFP the game was an “outlier” in the entertainment industry.

“This is the Taylor Swift of video games,” he said.

“The reach of the game is such that it will lead to a downstream effect on engagement on other entertainment services,” such as streaming platforms, said Omdia analyst James McWhirter.

Many fans have taken time off to explore the fictional state of Leonida, which is modeled on Florida.

“I’m going to take four days off,” said Dmytro Shkambara, a 27-year-old Ukrainian player living in Berlin, who said he had been planning his first session “for a very long time.”

Human resources platform Remote said it had seen a 32 percent increase in leave requests worldwide for November 19.

Billed as bigger, better and more realistic than its predecessors, “GTA VI” follows a Bonnie-and-Clyde-style couple trying to survive in Vice City, a crime-ridden city modeled on Miami.

The game received eight nominations on Tuesday for the Game Awards, the US ceremony honoring the year’s best video games, which takes place on December 10.

Subversion and controversy

Rockstar spent more than eight years developing the game.

The studio delayed the launch twice after a 2022 hack in which stolen gameplay footage was posted online, and it was hit by another round of leaks last summer.

The series has long been accused of glorifying violence and crime. It has also become a pop culture symbol of subversion, known for mocking the flaws of American society.

Players can run over pedestrians, sell drugs and shoot at police.

“It’s a series that is famous for being always over the top in terms of its representation of violence and different forms of abuse or harassment, for its representations of gender,” said Paolo Ruffino, a lecturer in digital cultures at King’s College London.

“I don’t expect to see necessarily major controversies unless there is something completely new,” he added.

No official release is currently planned in Russia, China, Lebanon or Qatar.

The post ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Launches Worldwide To Near-Perfect Reviews appeared first on Channels Television.

title: I Will Rejoin Military To Fight Russia If Needed — Prince Harry
description: Britain’s Prince Harry said he would “sign up again” to serve in the military and fight against Russia if needed, in an interview from Ukraine with The Telegraph aired Thursday.“I think there’s a lot that the whole world can learn from Ukraine,” the prince said du
content:
Britain’s Prince Harry said he would “sign up again” to serve in the military and fight against Russia if needed, in an interview from Ukraine with The Telegraph aired Thursday.

“I think there’s a lot that the whole world can learn from Ukraine,” the prince said during an unannounced visit to the western city of Lviv over the weekend.

“If asked to sign up again, if the need is there, then I will 100% be there to serve my country alongside my fellow veterans and service personnel.”

Harry, a former British army officer and the younger son of King Charles III, made his fourth visit to Ukraine since Russia’s 2022 invasion to meet wounded veterans and medics.

The prince is also the founder of the Invictus Games for wounded veterans and met athletes hoping to represent Ukraine at next year’s games in the British city of Birmingham.

“Just because there’s not drones, bullets, and rockets flying at us, that doesn’t mean that we’re not at war,” he told the British daily’s “Ukraine: The Latest” podcast.

“I feel very confident that Europe has a united front, and it would be fantastic to have more American support for that as well,” he added.

Earlier on his weekend visit to Lviv, he told wounded veterans and medics specialising in war injuries: “You’re going to win the war”.

He repeated that sentiment on the podcast, insisting that “Ukraine are winning” and “there is no version where Russia is making any more advances”.

The 42-year-old prince has previously spoken about being moved by witnessing death and life-changing injuries while on deployment in Afghanistan, and launched the Invictus Games in 2014 when he was still in the British army.

Harry, his wife Meghan and their two children moved back to the UK earlier this year from California amid an enduring rift with the royal family and his brother and heir-to-the-throne Prince William.

But the Sussex couple have launched themselves back into public life since their surprise return, carrying out engagements and visiting the EU parliament last week for an event about the dangers children face online.

Despite their busy schedule, Meghan has been keeping a relatively low profile since her estranged father was charged in the US for the alleged possession of child sexual abuse images.

AFP

title: Bayelsa CP seeks joint action against gender-based violence
description:
The Commissioner of Police in Bayelsa State, Ajao Adewale, has called for stronger collaboration among government agencies, traditional rulers, civil society organisations and other stakeholders to tackle gender-based violence and protect women and girls in the state.
Adewale made the call on Wednes
content:
The Commissioner of Police in Bayelsa State, Ajao Adewale, has called for stronger collaboration among government agencies, traditional rulers, civil society organisations and other stakeholders to tackle gender-based violence and protect women and girls in the state.

Adewale made the call on Wednesday during a one-day stakeholders’ workshop on Gender-Based Violence organised by the Bayelsa State Police Command through the Gender Unit of the State Criminal Investigation Department at the Command Officers’ Mess, Yenagoa.

The workshop, which had the theme, “Together, We Can Stop Gender-Based Crimes in Bayelsa State,” brought together representatives of the Ministry of Women, Children Affairs and Social Development, the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons, the International Federation of Women Lawyers, civil society organisations, traditional rulers and non-governmental organisations.

The police commissioner described gender-based violence as a serious violation of human rights and a threat to the wellbeing of families and society, insisting that its prevention should not be left to the police alone.

He said, ” Gender-based violence constitutes a grave violation of human rights and our collective humanity. The abuse or destruction of a woman’s dignity undermines the foundation of our families and society.”

Adewale, who cited the popular saying, “If you educate a woman, you educate a nation,” often attributed to Dr James Emman Kwegyir Aggrey, stressed the importance of protecting women as key contributors to societal development.

He added, ” A crime against a woman is a crime against humanity. We must therefore work together to ensure that women and girls are protected from every form of violence, abuse and exploitation.”

The CP reaffirmed the command’s commitment to the prevention, investigation and prosecution of gender-based crimes, assuring victims and survivors of professional handling of their cases.

According to him, victims and survivors would be treated with dignity, compassion and professionalism, while efforts would be sustained to ensure that perpetrators are brought to justice.

He urged members of the public to break the culture of silence surrounding sexual and gender-based violence, reject harmful traditional practices and promote respect, equality and responsible behaviour.

“The fight against gender-based violence requires the collective responsibility of all stakeholders. We must reject harmful practices, break the culture of silence and encourage victims to speak out and seek justice,” he said.

Adewale further challenged participants to translate the resolutions and recommendations of the workshop into practical measures, stronger partnerships and sustained public enlightenment.

He said the ultimate objective was to create a safer environment where women and girls could live, learn and thrive without fear of violence, abuse or exploitation.

The workshop featured lectures, presentations and deliberations on strategies for preventing and responding to sexual and gender-based violence in Bayelsa State.

The Director of Women Affairs in the state Ministry of Women, Children Affairs and Social Development, Mrs Atotu Yemi Nyinawemi, representatives of NAPTIP and FIDA, among others, attended the event.

The post Bayelsa CP seeks joint action against gender-based violence appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

The Airport Police Command said it has finally established contact with the family of Abraham Safety Osakpolor, a Nigerian and Canadian passport holder who was killed in a road accident after arrival in Lagos on Friday, November 13.
Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO) of the command, ASP Mohammed
content:
The Airport Police Command said it has finally established contact with the family of Abraham Safety Osakpolor, a Nigerian and Canadian passport holder who was killed in a road accident after arrival in Lagos on Friday, November 13.

Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO) of the command, ASP Mohammed Adeola disclosed this in a Thursday statement in
Ikeja, Lagos.

In an earlier statement on Wednesday, the command had sought the public’s assistance to locate the victim’s family and friends after efforts to do so internally proved abortive.

Thursday’s statement reads, “The Airport Police Command wishes to inform the general public that following its earlier press release seeking assistance in identifying the family and friends of late Abraham Safety Osakpolor, contact has now been successfully established with his family.

“The Command expresses its appreciation to every individual, media organisation and well-meaning member of the public who shared, reposted and helped cascade the earlier announcement across various platforms. Your collective efforts and cooperation made this positive outcome possible.”

The Commissioner of Police, Airport Police Command, CP Olufunke Ogunbode, while noting that effective policing thrives on mutual trust, cooperation and shared responsibility reiterated the command’s commitment to sustaining a cordial and productive relationship with the public.

title: 2027: IPC urges journalists to shun sensational reporting
description:
Barely two months before the 2027 general elections, the International Press Centre has cautioned journalists against sensational reporting, warning that such practices could undermine the country’s democracy.
Speaking in Yola on Wednesday during a training session for over 30 journalists in Adamawa
content:
Barely two months before the 2027 general elections, the International Press Centre has cautioned journalists against sensational reporting, warning that such practices could undermine the country’s democracy.

Speaking in Yola on Wednesday during a training session for over 30 journalists in Adamawa State on election coverage, the Executive Director of IPC, Lanre Arogundade, urged Nigerian journalists to uphold professionalism, fairness and balanced reporting before, during and after the 2027 general elections.

Arogundade, who was represented by the Programme Manager, Mrs Stella Nwofia, said the training was coming at a crucial time as the general elections approached.

He said, “The media had a crucial role to play in providing credible, inclusive and public-interest information before, during and after elections.”

He called on media practitioners to change their approach to reporting political campaigns and party activities by focusing attention on issues that directly affected women, citizens and their expectations of their leaders.

He said, “The media played a critical role in shaping citizens’ opinions on elections. Most people vote based on the media reports they read or listen to before elections.”

He also emphasised the need to ensure that women, youths, persons with disabilities and other underrepresented groups were prominently featured in media reports.

Delivering a paper titled, “2027 General Election in the Context of Democratic and Accountability Reporting: Scanning the Electoral Environment and Reporting Citizens’ Priority Concerns,” Dr Shadrach Idi of the Department of Communication, Taraba State University, said journalists should focus on politicians’ campaign promises to hold them accountable.

He said reporting citizens’ priority concerns should be the hallmark of journalism, adding that such an approach would bring to the fore the challenges facing people in rural communities.

Also speaking, Dr Olusola Oludira, in a presentation titled, “Integrating Fact-Checking for Democratic and Accountability Reporting,” urged journalists to verify information presented to them before publishing reports.

He said misinformation, disinformation and malinformation were among the tools politicians used during election campaigns.

Oludira described data as a vital tool for journalists to report facts rather than fiction.

The post 2027: IPC urges journalists to shun sensational reporting appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Why I kept video showing my father naming his successor – Jimmy Odukoya
description:
The embattled Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, has revealed why he retained a video in which his late father, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, named Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor, admitting that keeping the recording was a grave mistake.
Jimmy made the disclosure o
content:
The embattled Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, Jimmy Odukoya, has revealed why he retained a video in which his late father, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, named Pastor Kunle Areogun as his preferred successor, admitting that keeping the recording was a grave mistake.

Jimmy made the disclosure on Wednesday while addressing about 300 church workers amid the leadership crisis rocking the church, according to Church Times.

He said the video was recorded in 2021 when his father was preparing for surgery in the United States and feared he might not survive the procedure.

“That was when he asked me to record him where he made the statements about succession. I was the one who recorded the video,” Jimmy said, adding that his father’s elder brother, Pastor John Odukoya, was also aware of the recording.

He explained that his father later asked him to delete the video after the surgery was successful, but he retained it.

According to Church Times, Jimmy admitted that keeping the recording was a grave mistake, saying his father had considered it no longer valid after recovering from the operation.

He further alleged that only a handful of people knew about the video, including his sisters, whom he accused of releasing it to the public.

Giving an account of the disagreement with the church’s Board of Trustees (BoT), Jimmy said the crisis began about a year after he assumed office, when members allegedly asked him to relinquish his position as chairman and concentrate on his pastoral responsibilities.

“That was a hard pill for him to swallow. He said he sensed that what the board wanted to do was to control him, insisting that he would not allow that to happen,” Church Times quoted him as saying.

The report also quoted Jimmy as alleging that his sister, Pastor Tolu Odukoya-Ijogun, approached him and asked him to step down to enable her to become the board’s chairman.

He said the dispute was taken to the General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God, Pastor Enoch Adeboye, following interventions by Bishop Mike Okonkwo.

Recounting the meeting, Jimmy said: “When we got to Pastor Adeboye, I was there, and I watched every board member lie against me to my face.”

According to the report, Adeboye allowed him to explain his side before advising the parties to resolve their differences.

The cleric reportedly reminded Jimmy that his calling was to preach the gospel, not to serve as board chairman.

Adeboye also warned that if the parties failed to resolve the disagreement, “it will not be goodbye, it will be bye-bye.”

Jimmy said the board, which included Pastors Kunle Areogun and Rotimi Okpaise, presented him with a seven-point demand, but he accepted only four of the conditions.

On allegations of financial misconduct, he denied embezzling N250m donated to the church for a project, insisting that the money remained intact.

According to Church Times, he told the workers that the project had been delayed by the prevailing economic situation and rising costs, which made its execution difficult.

He also reportedly said he had restricted access to church funds and argued that if there had been financial wrongdoing, members of the accounts department would also be culpable.

Jimmy maintained that he remained the church’s Senior Pastor, although he expressed uncertainty about how the next Sunday service would proceed. He also said an advertised church programme would not hold because he did not want the crisis to escalate.

The development followed the decision of a faction of the church’s BoT on November 17 to withdraw recognition of Jimmy as Senior Pastor and appoint Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader.

The faction cited a December 2021 video in which Taiwo named Areogun as his preferred successor.

In the recording, the late founder said: “In case of my demise, which I don’t expect to happen soon, or a situation where I cannot write or talk, please, the next pastor of the church should be Kunle Areogun.”

He also designated Jimmy as Areogun’s immediate administrative assistant and head of the youth church.

The trustees claimed they only became aware of the video in late December 2025, more than two years after Taiwo’s death, and that it was not presented during Jimmy’s appointment in September 2023.

However, a statement from Jimmy’s camp rejected the board faction’s decision as constitutionally invalid, insisting that he remained the duly appointed Senior Pastor and chairman of the BoT.

Taiwo founded The Fountain of Life Church in 1992 with his first wife, Pastor Bimbo Odukoya. Following his death on August 7, 2023,

Jimmy was announced as Senior Pastor in September and formally installed on September 30, 2023, while Tolu was named Associate Senior Pastor.

The post Why I kept video showing my father naming his successor – Jimmy Odukoya appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: AI can help Nigerian farmers beat climate uncertainty – Expert
description:
…Urges African governments to invest in climate data, local language technology
As unpredictable rainfall, prolonged dry spells and recurrent flooding threaten agricultural productivity across Africa, a Microsoft artificial intelligence (AI) expert has called for greater deployment of technology to
content:
…Urges African governments to invest in climate data, local language technology

As unpredictable rainfall, prolonged dry spells and recurrent flooding threaten agricultural productivity across Africa, a Microsoft artificial intelligence (AI) expert has called for greater deployment of technology to help farmers anticipate climate risks, improve planting decisions and protect their livelihoods.

The expert, Dr Girmaw Abebe Tadesse, said artificial intelligence could play a critical role in strengthening Africa’s food security by translating weather forecasts and climate data into practical information that farmers and governments could use to prepare for changing weather conditions.

He, however, stressed that improving the accuracy of weather predictions alone would not address the continent’s agricultural challenges unless farmers could access timely, reliable and locally relevant information to guide their decisions.

Tadesse, who leads Microsoft’s AI for Good Lab in Nairobi and is a member of the United Nations Independent International Scientific Panel on AI, made the case in an article examining how AI could help African countries navigate growing climate uncertainty.

He noted that for millions of farmers across the continent, the timing of rainfall could determine whether a planting season produces a successful harvest or results in significant financial losses.

According to him, planting too early could expose seeds to failure when expected rains do not arrive, while late planting could prevent crops from reaching maturity before the end of the rainy season.

He said these uncertainties were becoming more pronounced in countries such as Nigeria, where changing rainfall patterns, extended dry spells and flooding were disrupting agricultural seasons and threatening the livelihoods of farming households.

With governments and development partners meeting for the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), Tadesse argued that attention should extend beyond improving weather forecasting to ensuring that climate intelligence reaches farmers and public institutions in ways that support timely decisions.

He identified Probabilistic Bias Correction, a machine learning approach developed by Microsoft Research, as one of the technologies that could improve the reliability of existing weather forecasts by correcting recurring errors in weather models.

More reliable forecasts, he explained, could help farmers determine when to plant, anticipate dry spells and make better decisions about the allocation of agricultural inputs.

However, he warned that climate information must be adapted to local realities, including soil conditions, crop varieties, water availability, production costs and farmers’ existing knowledge.

He pointed to Nigeria’s Digital Climate Advisory Services initiative, involving the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet) and MTN Nigeria, as an example of efforts to make location-specific weather information accessible to farmers through mobile communication channels.

The initiative is designed to provide weather guidance that can support decisions around planting, irrigation and harvesting.

He also highlighted the role of digital agricultural platforms, citing Farmcrowdy, a Nigerian agritech company that developed a platform connecting farmers with financing and agricultural support.

Although not specifically an AI-based weather forecasting platform, the initiative demonstrates how digital technology can help address some of the financial and operational challenges confronting smallholder farmers.

On agricultural insurance and climate-risk management, Tadesse cited efforts involving Pula, Leadway Assurance, Bayer Foundation and government partners to strengthen the resilience of approximately 250,000 smallholder farmers across eight states in Nigeria through data-driven agricultural insurance and risk management.

He said such interventions demonstrated that climate intelligence would deliver greater value when connected to services that enable farmers to act on available information, including access to financing, agricultural inputs and insurance.

Beyond forecasting and financial support, the Microsoft expert identified language accessibility as another major challenge limiting the adoption of digital agricultural services across Africa.

He explained that connectivity costs, limited digital literacy, language barriers and inadequate agricultural extension services could prevent farmers from benefiting from even the most sophisticated technology.

To address this, he highlighted LINGUA Africa, an initiative supported by Microsoft’s AI for Good Lab and partners, which is advancing the development of artificial intelligence tools that reflect Africa’s linguistic diversity.

In Nigeria, projects such as AgroLingua Africa are exploring how AI can deliver agricultural information in local languages, including Hausa, Yoruba and Igbo, while HausaNLP’s DialectBridge is working to improve AI capabilities across regional Hausa dialects.

According to him, delivering agricultural advice in languages farmers understand is essential to ensuring that technology serves their needs.

He maintained that farmers, researchers and agricultural extension workers must remain central to the development and deployment of AI solutions, noting that local knowledge and experience were critical to effective agricultural decision-making.

He also warned that fragmented agricultural records, inadequate technical capacity in public institutions and poor coordination among agencies responsible for agriculture, meteorology and disaster management could limit the impact of AI-driven interventions.

Against this backdrop, he urged African governments and development partners to prioritise investment in agricultural data systems as essential infrastructure for climate adaptation.

He said such investments should cover the integration of agricultural and climate databases, affordable internet connectivity, responsible data-sharing arrangements and continuous training for government analysts and agricultural extension workers.

He further stressed the importance of national ownership of data systems to ensure that investments remain sustainable beyond individual development projects.

While acknowledging that artificial intelligence could not prevent droughts, replace irrigation infrastructure or eliminate the financial pressures facing farmers, Tadesse said the technology could significantly improve how farmers and governments anticipate and respond to climate-related risks.

He argued that Africa’s agricultural future would depend not merely on the ability to predict rainfall but on whether farmers and governments could translate such predictions into practical decisions before climate risks become crises.

The post AI can help Nigerian farmers beat climate uncertainty – Expert appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: 2027: Shari’ah Council warns politicians against violence, hate speech
description:
…urges Nigerians to obtain PVCs, participate in elections
The Supreme Council for Shari’ah in Nigeria (SCSN) has cautioned politicians and their supporters against engaging in activities capable of triggering violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that no political ambition is worth t
content:
…urges Nigerians to obtain PVCs, participate in elections

The Supreme Council for Shari’ah in Nigeria (SCSN) has cautioned politicians and their supporters against engaging in activities capable of triggering violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that no political ambition is worth the blood of any Nigerian.

The Council also called on Nigerians, irrespective of their religious, ethnic, political and regional affiliations, to embrace peace, tolerance and patriotism, stressing that the preservation of the country’s unity and stability should take precedence over political interests.

In a press statement issued on Wednesday and signed by its Secretary-General, Prof. Ahmad Bello Dogarawa, the Council described elections as a constitutional process through which citizens exercise their democratic rights, rather than a war between political opponents.

It warned that political differences must never be allowed to justify hatred, violence, intimidation, destruction of property or the loss of innocent lives.

The Council, therefore, urged eligible Nigerians to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), ensure that their voter registration details were in order and participate actively in the electoral process by voting for candidates and political parties of their choice.

It cautioned citizens against surrendering their democratic responsibilities to apathy, intimidation, inducement or political manipulation, noting that every eligible Nigerian had a legitimate stake in determining the country’s leadership and future direction.

The SCSN equally urged political parties, candidates, campaign organisations and supporters to conduct their electioneering activities with decorum, restraint and respect for the rights and dignity of others.

It insisted that political campaigns must be issue-based and peaceful, without inflammatory rhetoric, religious incitement, ethnic profiling, hate speech, threats and personal attacks.

The Council also called on political leaders to demonstrate responsible leadership by restraining their supporters and discouraging pre- and post-election violence, thuggery, intimidation and the use of political enforcers to undermine the democratic process.

On the role of security agencies, the Council urged them to discharge their constitutional and statutory responsibilities impartially and professionally.

It said government must guarantee a secure and fair political environment where political parties and candidates could freely organise, campaign, assemble and communicate their programmes without intimidation or discrimination.

It further urged security agencies to remain neutral, resist political manipulation and provide adequate protection for voters, electoral officials, observers and election materials throughout the electoral process.

On election days, the Council urged Nigerians to respect electoral procedures and cooperate with relevant authorities, while condemning vote buying, voter suppression, ballot snatching and electoral intimidation.

It also appealed to political parties and their supporters to accept credible electoral outcomes and channel legitimate grievances through constitutional and judicial processes rather than resorting to violence and lawlessness.

Reiterating that Nigeria’s peace and stability were non-negotiable, the Council said political power was temporary and public offices should be regarded as positions of trust and responsibility.

It also called on religious leaders, traditional rulers, community leaders, civil society organisations and the media to intensify public enlightenment, promote tolerance and discourage messages capable of triggering political or communal violence.

The Council emphasised that religious and traditional institutions should serve as platforms for peace, reconciliation and responsible citizenship, rather than instruments of political division.

The post 2027: Shari’ah Council warns politicians against violence, hate speech appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

title: Create jobs, tackle national challenges, Crawford varsity VC urges graduates
description:
The Vice-Chancellor of Crawford University, Ogun State, Prof. Solomon Makinde, has urged graduating students to embrace entrepreneurship and create jobs rather than depend solely on paid employment.
Makinde gave the charge on Wednesday at the institution’s 18th convocation ceremony in Igbesa, where
content:
The Vice-Chancellor of Crawford University, Ogun State, Prof. Solomon Makinde, has urged graduating students to embrace entrepreneurship and create jobs rather than depend solely on paid employment.

Makinde gave the charge on Wednesday at the institution’s 18th convocation ceremony in Igbesa, where 630 students, comprising 528 undergraduates and 102 postgraduate students, graduated with various degrees and postgraduate diplomas.

Addressing the graduands, whom the university described as the Unicorn Class of 2025/2026, the vice-chancellor said they were entering a world being reshaped by artificial intelligence, digital innovation, economic changes and evolving professional demands.

He said academic qualifications alone would not be enough to succeed in the changing environment, urging the graduates to develop critical thinking, problem-solving, communication and adaptability skills.

Presenting five charges to the graduands, Makinde urged them to uphold the university’s philosophy of knowledge with godliness, pursue excellence, develop entrepreneurial mindsets, demonstrate responsible leadership and maintain relationships with their alma mater.

He said, “Let Knowledge with Godliness remain your enduring compass. Never allow the pursuit of material success to diminish your commitment to truth, integrity, humility and godly living.

“Knowledge without character can become destructive, while achievement without integrity is unsustainable. Let your lives demonstrate that intellectual excellence and spiritual depth reinforce one another.

“Do not define your future exclusively by the availability of paid employment. Develop an entrepreneurial mindset, identify societal problems, create solutions and contribute to employment generation and national development. Nigeria and the wider world need graduates who can transform challenges into opportunities.”

He also urged them to embrace continuous learning and use technology responsibly.

Giving a breakdown of the undergraduate results, Makinde said 54 graduands earned First Class degrees, 233 obtained Second Class Upper Division, 191 graduated with Second Class Lower Division, while 50 received Third Class degrees.

The postgraduate category comprised 57 Master of Science graduates, seven Master of Business Administration graduates, 21 Postgraduate Diploma recipients and 17 Doctor of Philosophy graduates.

He said the number of doctoral graduates reflected the university’s efforts to strengthen its postgraduate research culture and develop advanced human capital.

The best graduating students in the undergraduate category were Anthony Eromonsele Ibazebo of Computer Science and Technology and Chiamaka Jasmine Njoku of Biochemistry, who both finished with a cumulative grade point average of 4.92.

In the School of Part-Time Studies, Perpetua Ndidiamaka Uzoma of Physics with Electronics emerged as the best graduating student with a CGPA of 4.96.

The vice-chancellor also announced that the university had secured approval from the National Universities Commission for six new undergraduate programmes under its proposed College of Allied Health Sciences.

The programmes are Nursing Science, Medical Laboratory Science, Physiotherapy, Radiography, Public Health and Community Health.

Meanwhile, the convocation lecturer, Dr Alban Igwe, Director-General of the Dangerous Goods Academy, Lagos, urged the university to build an internationally connected institution that combines global academic standards with practical solutions to local and African challenges.

Delivering a lecture titled, “The Future of Crawford University: Globalizing the Locals and Localizing the Globals,” Igwe said the institution’s growth would depend on its ability to preserve its local identity while connecting its academic programmes, research and graduates to international opportunities.

He argued that globalisation should not mean abandoning local realities, while local relevance should not become an excuse for academic isolation.

“My proposition is uncompromising: Crawford’s future will not be secured by choosing between local relevance and global excellence. It must master both. It must be deeply rooted in its locality and confidently connected to the world—local in identity, global in standard, African in purpose, international in reach,” he said.

Igwe also urged the university to leverage its location in Igbesa and the surrounding industrial and commercial environment, particularly its proximity to major trade and logistics networks.

The post Create jobs, tackle national challenges, Crawford varsity VC urges graduates appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

title: Police locate family of Nigerian-Canadian killed in Lagos crash
description:
The Airport Police Command says it has established contact with the family of Abraham Safety Osakpolor, a Nigerian-Canadian who died after being hit by a vehicle along the Murtala Muhammed International Airport access road in Lagos.
The command disclosed this in a statement issued on Thursday by its
content:
The Airport Police Command says it has established contact with the family of Abraham Safety Osakpolor, a Nigerian-Canadian who died after being hit by a vehicle along the Murtala Muhammed International Airport access road in Lagos.

The command disclosed this in a statement issued on Thursday by its Public Relations Officer, ASP Mohammed Adeola, following an earlier appeal for members of the public to help locate the deceased’s relatives.

“The Command wishes to inform the general public that following its earlier press release seeking assistance in identifying the family and friends of late Abraham Safety Osakpolor, contact has now been successfully established with his family,” the statement said.

The command expressed appreciation to individuals, media organisations and members of the public who shared its earlier announcement, saying their cooperation helped achieve the outcome.

It quoted the Commissioner of Police, Airport Police Command, CP Olufunke Ogunbode, as reiterating the command’s commitment to maintaining a cordial relationship with the public.

“Effective policing thrives on mutual trust, cooperation and shared responsibility,” Ogunbode said, according to the statement.

The command had earlier appealed for help in locating Osakpolor’s family after he died in a road accident near the airport.

PUNCH Online reported that the 58-year-old, who was born in Benin City, Edo State, was hit by a moving vehicle while walking along the expressway leading from the airport towards the Oshodi axis.

He was rushed to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead, while his remains were deposited in a morgue. The police also said the motorist involved in the accident was apprehended and would be charged in court.

During an initial search, officers recovered a Nigerian passport and a mobile phone without a SIM card from his belongings. A Canadian passport was later discovered by mortuary attendants.

The post Police locate family of Nigerian-Canadian killed in Lagos crash appeared first on Punch Newspapers.

Tinubu, who described Malik as a brilliant courtro
content:
President Bola Tinubu has commended Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), Aikhunegbe Malik, for his contributions to the legal profession and his role in the legal team that represented him in the proceedings arising from the 2023 presidential election.

Tinubu, who described Malik as a brilliant courtroom advocate and arbitrator, said the legal practitioner distinguished himself during the election litigation.

The President gave the commendation in a birthday message to Malik, who turns a year older on Thursday, November 19, 2026.

According to a statement issued by his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, Tinubu praised Malik’s professional accomplishments and described his career as reflective of a generation of Nigerian lawyers whose experience cuts across public service, private legal practice, advocacy, arbitration, election disputes and professional leadership.

“He was one of the lawyers who represented me in the proceedings arising from the 2023 presidential election. He shone brilliantly in that team,” the President said.

Tinubu described Malik’s elevation to the Inner Bar as an important milestone in a career devoted to the practice and development of law.

The President wished the legal practitioner long life, robust health and continued impact in his profession and society.

Malik, who has over two decades of legal practice experience, is the founding and principal partner of A.A. Malik & Co., a law firm headquartered in Abuja.

He was conferred with the prestigious rank of Senior Advocate of Nigeria in September 2019.

title: Tinubu’s aide experiences motorists’ ordeal in five-hour Lagos-Ibadan gridlock
description:
President Bola Tinubu’s Special Adviser on Media and Communications, Sunday Dare, has experienced the frustration faced by motorists on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway after spending more than five hours trapped in traffic while travelling to Ibadan, Oyo State.
Dare, who lamented the situation in a Face
content:
President Bola Tinubu’s Special Adviser on Media and Communications, Sunday Dare, has experienced the frustration faced by motorists on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway after spending more than five hours trapped in traffic while travelling to Ibadan, Oyo State.

Dare, who lamented the situation in a Facebook post on Wednesday night, said thousands of travellers were stranded by the heavy congestion, with some forced to abandon their vehicles and trek long distances to reach their destinations.

His experience brought him face to face with the difficulties commuters endure on the busy highway, particularly when road construction disrupts movement.

The presidential aide blamed the timing of the ongoing construction, questioning why the Chinese contractor handling the project chose to carry out the work during peak traffic hours instead of at night when fewer vehicles use the road.

“It beats me why a Chinese Contractor would choose the busiest hours of vehicular traffic to construct the bridge and road around this exit point. Stranded cars, thousands of people trekking to get home,” he wrote.

He further called for a change in the construction schedule to reduce the hardship faced by road users.

“What happened to doing construction work during the obituary hours when traffic is lean? This is unnecessary pain. It needs to be corrected,” Dare added.

The gridlock followed the resumption of construction work on a pedestrian bridge around the Aseese section of the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway on Wednesday.

The activity disrupted traffic in both directions, leaving motorists travelling along the route caught in prolonged congestion.
